##### 13. Solution plan
**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.payment`, module `schema`. Base `/api/recovery/payment/v1`, schema and login `rwb_payment`, topic `rwb.payment.events.v1`, queue `rwb-payment` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, on the service's own Flyway sequence (DP-15).

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The legacy marker this slice replaces is one schema with one login and one `V0001` baseline (DP-01, DP-15): the split is the new work §R6 records. The monolith name `recovery.proceeds` is marker text only: it stays as built and is neither the target nor a read path. The other seven DPs are carried by the key and their runtime work sits with the stories that write and read the table: the record with the row and the outbox row (DP-03), the ACE payment through the owner's contract or the service's view (DP-05), the lists and parameters through their contracts (DP-06, DP-07) in one hop with a 2 s timeout (DP-11), the topic names from the library (DP-14) and SCR-28 through the gateway-bff route (DP-19). This story creates a table, so none of them adds a call of its own. It adds no build edge either: the six platform contracts are the service baseline and are traced in section 18 rather than in an H row (GAP-2540; ASM-4198).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `V<seq>__rwb_p8_e1001_payment_schema.sql` | Flyway migration | Creates `proceeds` with its key, its two indexes and the 7 standard columns; writes no row, creates no view and no grant |
| `PaymentFieldDeclaration` | Build artefact and test fixture | The field-row declaration of `proceeds`; the source the conformance test compares against and hands to the one seed |
| `PaymentDictionaryConformanceTest` | Test (pipeline) | Compares `information_schema.columns` with the declaration in both directions, ignoring the 7 standard columns |
| `PaymentSchemaBoundaryTest` | Test (pipeline) | Fails on another schema name, on a grant to another login and on a foreign key that leaves the schema |
| `PaymentIndexPlanTest`, `PaymentGrantFixture` | Test and fixture | Assert the two read paths' plans with the SIT rule set, and the refusals of AC6 through a login with grants on `rwb_payment` only |

**Database and migrations.** One transaction creates `proceeds` and nothing else: `id` uuid primary key, `case_id` uuid not null, `treatment_id` uuid, `account_payment_id` uuid, `source` varchar(12) not null, `amount` numeric(18,2) not null, `received_date` date not null, `matched_to` varchar(15) not null, `posting_ref` varchar(40), plus the 7 standard columns. No check constraint holds a list value (BR3, AC11). Three columns are values, so the three relationships of TSD P8 T3.3 become references by value (BR5). The indexes are `proceeds (matched_to, received_date)` for the unmatched and matched list of a business date and `proceeds (case_id, received_date DESC)` for the receipts of a case and the daily reconciliation; their names and the column order beyond the leading column are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2536; ASM-4194). No constraint, index or default names `public` or another `rwb_*` schema (BR1, BR8).

**Migrations in order** (forward only). 1. The service baseline: schema, login, the template's standard columns and the library objects (RWB-PLT-NF06-DB; RWB-PLT-E1027-CON), already applied. 2. This story: `V<seq>__rwb_p8_e1001_payment_schema.sql`, `proceeds` with its key and indexes and nothing else. 3. The service's own stories: the matching stories that write receipts, the contract and operation stories, and the settlement, auction, fees, ALS booking, ledger post and reconciliation stories; this story neither creates nor depends on them.

**Configuration and reference data.** The schema name comes from the deployment configuration of `rwb-payment` (RWB-PLT-E1044-CON); the legacy `recoverySchema` parameter stays the baseline's and is not read here. `LOV-MATCH` and `LOV-PROCEEDS-SRC` are read through the reference-data contract of `rwb-case` with the version in force (DP-07), never stored as a check constraint or a Java enum, which is why a new value needs no migration (AC11). No value the business may change is written in this story's code or migration.

**Build steps**

1. Write the migration from TSD P8 T3.1 and T3.0 with the schema from configuration; run it on an empty container that holds `rwb_payment` and no other `rwb_*` schema, and prove one table, its key and its two indexes (AC1, AC2).
2. Write `PaymentFieldDeclaration` and `PaymentDictionaryConformanceTest`; prove the test fails on an extra column and on a changed physical type (AC3).
3. Prove the rollback and the skip: a copy that fails on the unmatched-list index leaves no table and no successful version (AC4); a second run changes nothing (AC5).
4. Prove the boundary: the migration names `rwb_payment` only, creates no view and no grant, and a read of `rwb_case.recovery_case`, of `rwb_source_data.sys_fields` and of `recovery.v_ace_payment` through the service login is refused (AC6).
5. Hand the declaration to the one seed (RWB-P1-E1001-APP) and record the handover in the Change Register, writing no row of `rwb_source_data` (AC9; GAP-2537); prove no row is written (AC7); write `PaymentIndexPlanTest` and prove it fails when an index is dropped (AC8); confirm the DP13 row through the reference-data fake (AC10); and prove that a new list value needs no build (AC11).

**Feature switch.** None of its own: a migration is not behind a flag, the table either exists at the version or the pipeline has not applied it (BR6, BR7). The matching switches belong to the service's own stories.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass; the migration runs clean in DEV and SIT; `rwb_payment` holds exactly `proceeds` with its key, its two indexes and no row; the declaration is matched; the boundary test reports nothing outside `rwb_payment`; and the read paths use their indexes.

##### 14. Validation and messages
| ID | When | Message | Where it is produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| insufficient_privilege | A login without a grant on `rwb_payment`, or a read of `rwb_case`, `rwb_source_data` or a `recovery.v_ace_*` view through this login | The database's own refusal | PostgreSQL, asserted by AC6 |
| None (pipeline log) | A statement fails, a column has no declaration row, a row has no column or another physical type, a statement or grant names another schema, or a read path has no index | The stage fails and names the statement and its line, "{table}.{column} has no data dictionary entry", "{fieldId} physical type {expected} expected, {found} found", the schema found, or the read path and its plan | The pipeline, the conformance test, the boundary test and the plan check (AC3, AC4, AC6, AC8) |
| None | A receipt is matched, refused or left unmatched | MSG-P1-001, MSG-P8-001, MSG-P8-002, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-003 and MSG-GEN-001 are the matching and operation stories' (FSD P8 A2.1, A2.2; RWB-P8-E2008-APP); this story makes the store answer and produces no message | Not this story |

Every error that reaches a caller is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId`, `detail` and `instance`; the IDs are the service's later stories', because this story provides no operation. Its own failures stop the pipeline, and the log line carries the statement, the table or the Field ID. No message or log line carries a personal value.

##### 17. Guardrails
- No business value in code: the sources, the match values, the Field IDs and the lengths are specification or list values, and the lists arrive through DP-07 with a version, so a new value needs no migration (BR3, AC11).
- No personal data anywhere: the table holds references, a source, an amount, a date, a match value and a posting reference; every fixture, log line and prompt is synthetic (BR9).
- No cross-schema read and no cross-schema key (DP-01): every statement names `rwb_payment` and no constraint or index points at `public` or another service's schema (BR1, BR5).
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `v_ace_*` views: this service holds no grant on the 30 views and this story reads no ACE data (DP-05, ADR-010; BR8).
- The baseline is never rewritten: the monolith's `V0001`, its 92 tables, its dictionary and its 14 catalog rows keep their version and rows, and this story adds a line rather than editing an applied version (BR7; AC9). It never drops a table in PROD and is forward only (BR6).
- One writer per row and no invented money fact: this story writes no row, so no receipt, match or posting reference can be seeded (BR4, BR10), and no ledger column is copied (BR11).
- One hop and a 2 s timeout on every call to another service, and none at run time here (DP-11); the declaration cannot drift from the dictionary because the conformance test compares both directions (BR2, AC3); and one base and one topic — `/api/recovery/payment/v1` and `rwb.payment.events.v1` with `rwb-payment` in namespace `rwb-recovery` — with no monolith base and no other service's base declared as this service's own.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: RWB-E1-001 is realigned. The built migration and its 92-table estate are kept, and this wave-1 integration story proves that the estate now spans the 19 per-service `rwb_*` schemas while the dictionary, the data product catalog and the read paths still work end to end against the real services. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **test lead of the integration harness (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **a wave-1 integration run that proves the 92 tables of the 14 data products resolve one owning `rwb_*` schema each across the 19 services, and that the data dictionary, the data product catalog and the read paths still work end to end against the real services**, so that **the schema split of RWB-E1-001 is accepted with evidence before wave 1 leaves integration, and no later wave builds on a table estate that only works in a single recovery schema**.

##### 2. Business rationale

RWB-E1-001 put 92 tables (the 88 Workbench tables and the four extension tables of DF-EXT-001 to DF-EXT-049), 122 `sys_objects` rows and 1,366 `sys_fields` rows into one recovery schema with the read model `v_data_dictionary` and the catalog `data_product`. That estate is built and stays built. What changes is where it lives: each of the 19 services now writes its own schema `rwb_<name>` with its own login and its own Flyway sequence (DP-01, DP-02, DP-15), and no service reads another service's tables (DP-11: a contract, one hop, 2 s timeout). The split is delivered by RWB-PLT-NF06-DB and the per-service DB stories; this story does not build it.

What nothing else proves is that the estate still behaves as one dictionary and one catalog after the split. The dictionary is a read model over `sys_objects`, `sys_fields` and `data_product`, which the Ownership Map keeps together in rwb-source-data; the catalog is a versioned data load that enters through the rwb-case reference-data contract (DP-07), is applied by the rwb-source-data handler, is authorised by rwb-access (DP-06 to DP-07 boundary) and leaves one hash-chained entry in the rwb-decision ledger (DP-03). Three services, one transaction each, no shared table. If the wiring or the naming drifts, it fails here, in SIT, with a named assertion — before a case officer reads a case through a contract that no longer matches the dictionary.

The measure this run serves is the one the legacy story serves: the ACE batch is complete when the Workbench reads it on 99 percent of days, and every read and every freshness stamp is resolved against this dictionary and this catalog. The run is part of the integration harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG and follows its topology, its run lock and its report.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The nine wave-1 services are deployed to SIT from their own pipelines, each with its own schema and login, and each schema carries its own Flyway baseline (DP-15, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON).
- The migrated SIT data set exists: the 14 `data_product` seed rows, the 122 `sys_objects` rows and the 1,366 `sys_fields` rows, carried from the built RWB-E1-001 migration and replayed into the owning schema by the per-service DB stories.
- The 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views exist in the ACE database and are readable by the rwb-source-data login only (DP-05).
- The reference data administrator (RW-REFADM) holds Reference data C in SIT, and a reader login may query the dictionary read model of rwb-source-data.
- The catalog load file for the 14 data products exists as a fixture, with table code `data_product`, the three legacy system-of-record strings and synthetic owner user IDs for SIT.
- The integration harness holds its run lock, its Kafka topics and its Temporal namespace `rwb-recovery` in SIT.
- No build dependency and no contract dependency: the run executes against the deployed services, their real contracts and their real schemas. Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: takes the SIT run lock, reads `/health` on the nine wave-1 services and records each service's Flyway version and schema name.
2. Harness: reads `information_schema.tables` for the 19 `rwb_*` schemas and builds the table-to-schema resolution for the 92 tables of the estate.
3. Harness: compares the resolution with the estate list of the legacy story and fails on a missing table, a duplicated table name in two schemas, or one of the twenty tables that left the estate.
4. Harness: queries the dictionary read model `v_data_dictionary` in rwb-source-data for entity `v_ace_account` and field `days_past_due`, and for entity `account_ext` and field `dispute_open`, and records the owning schema and owning service beside every row.
5. Harness: posts the catalog fixture to rwb-case on `POST /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads` with table code `data_product`, valid from 2026-11-30, as the reference data administrator.
6. rwb-case: asks rwb-access on `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` for Reference data C with the caller's role and scope before it accepts the load.
7. rwb-case: forwards the accepted load to rwb-source-data; `DataProductCatalogHandler.validate` refuses or accepts the whole file and writes nothing.
8. rwb-source-data: `DataProductCatalogHandler.apply` writes the 14 rows of DP01 to DP14 in one transaction in `rwb_source_data` and returns the row count; the service writes its local decision record in the same transaction and publishes `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` through its outbox.
9. rwb-decision: appends one entry to the central ledger from `rwb.decision-record.v1`; the harness reads it back on `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log`.
10. Harness: reads the dictionary again and asserts the 14 rows, the three system-of-record strings of DP01, DP03 and DP06 and their refresh cycles.
11. Harness: posts the same catalog file a second time and asserts that nothing is written and that the ledger holds exactly one entry for the load.
12. Harness: exercises the read paths on the migrated SIT data through the owners' contracts: `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/accounts/{id}` and `GET /api/recovery/payment/v1/cases/{caseId}/payments`.
13. Harness: runs the boundary test over the 19 schemas, every foreign key, every grant and every view definition.
14. Harness: publishes the run report, releases the lock and hands the report to the wave-1 exit review.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A table of the estate sits in no schema, in two schemas, or a table that left the estate is found | The run fails and names each table and schema pair | None (run report) | AC12 |
| X2 | A service cannot reach another service, or a call exceeds the 2 s budget | The step fails and the report names the caller, the callee, the operation and the elapsed time | None (run report) | AC13, AC14 |
| X3 | The catalog row names no system of record, two systems, a bare source name, or no owner user ID | The whole load is refused; the run asserts the refusal and the message | MSG-P1-003 | AC7 |
| X4 | The catalog file does not hold exactly the 14 products DP01 to DP14 | The whole load is refused | MSG-P1-004 | AC3 |
| X5 | A catalog row names an owner role or a refresh cycle outside its list | The whole load is refused | MSG-P1-007 | AC3 |
| X6 | The same catalog file is posted again | Nothing is written, the answer is the repeat message, and the ledger keeps one entry | MSG-P1-011 | AC15 |
| X7 | A caller without Reference data C posts the load | rwb-access refuses, rwb-case answers 403 and the refusal is in the access log | MSG-P4-002 | AC13 |
| X8 | A cross-schema foreign key, a read of another service's table, or a second reader of the ACE views is found | The boundary test fails and names the constraint, the query or the grant | None (run report) | AC14 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency and no contract dependency; it runs against the deployed wave-1 services in SIT and their real contracts |
| Negotiable | The fixtures, the assertion order and the report shape are settled inside the harness; the 92 tables, the 14 products and the three system-of-record strings are fixed by the legacy story and are not changed here |
| Valuable | It is the only place where the split estate is seen as one dictionary, one catalog and one set of read paths across services |
| Estimable | One suite, four fixtures, one boundary test, one run order and one report |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the wave-1 services already deployed |
| Testable | One assertion per criterion; a failing assertion names the service, the schema and the object |

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every table column and every view column in the recovery estate has exactly one row in the data dictionary, with its BR Field ID, types, source system and meaning | Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary; sys_fields |
| BR2 | Workbench data is held in the 14 data products DP01 to DP14 | REQ-RDF-001; sys_objects.data_product |
| BR3 | Each data product has exactly one system of record, written "ACE (ingested from X)" for source data, "Recovery Workbench" for Workbench records, or, where the product holds both, one sentence that names ACE with its sources and the Recovery Workbench; and one named owner | REQ-RDF-001; D-RCV-35 U1 |
| BR4 | The catalog values are a versioned data load, changed without a code release; a load with an exception is refused in full | Principle 1; DT02; CTL-08 |
| BR5 | Where a product is fed by several sources (DP06, DP07, DP13), its one system of record names ACE and every source it ingests; a bare source name is refused because no source reaches the Workbench except through ACE | D-RCV-35; ADR-010 |
| BR8 | The recovery estate holds no copy of source data. No constraint references a table in schema public, and a link to an ACE record is a varchar(255) business key with no foreign key | D-RCV-35 U4; ADR-010; Data Tier Map section 1 |
| BR10 | Each of the 92 tables has exactly one owning `rwb_*` schema and exactly one writing login; a table name appears in one schema only, and the dictionary read model names the owning schema and the owning service of every object | DP-01; Arch v5 slides 20, 41 and 45 |
| BR11 | Services talk to each other by contract, not by table: no cross-schema foreign key, no read of another service's tables, one hop with a 2 s timeout, and the boundary test fails the build on any violation | DP-01, DP-11; ADR-014, ADR-020; Arch v5 slide 45 |
| BR12 | Every service writes its decision record locally in the same transaction as its state change and publishes it through its outbox to `rwb.decision-record.v1`; the inbox dedupes, so one load leaves one ledger entry and a repeated load leaves none | DP-03, DP-09; ADR-015, ADR-022; Temporal and Drools design slide 16 |

BR6, BR7 and BR9 of the legacy story are not re-proven here: BR6 (schema names from parameters, one migration per story) belongs to RWB-PLT-NF06-DB and the per-service DB stories, BR7 (personal fields flagged in the dictionary) belongs to the dictionary and masking stories, and BR9 (the baseline seeds the dictionary before the views exist) belongs to RWB-P1-E1064-APP and the view story. The IDs and their texts are unchanged in the legacy story, and the copied test cases keep their legacy Covers values, so a row still names BR6, BR7 or BR9 where the legacy named it; the run proves the part of that rule in scope and the owning story proves the rest.

##### 9. State transitions

None for case status: this story changes no `recovery_case` row and takes no business decision. The states the run asserts are:

| From | To | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| Service baseline not applied | Service baseline applied | Each service's Flyway baseline runs in its own schema before the run |
| Catalog version none | Catalog version 2026-11-30 in force | The 14 rows are applied in one transaction and the version becomes current |
| Catalog version 2026-11-30 in force | Catalog version 2026-11-30 in force (no change) | The same file is posted again; nothing is written and the answer is MSG-P1-011 |
| Ledger without the load | Ledger with one entry for the load | `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` is consumed once; a repeated load adds no entry |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-TRIBE, integration and test roles | Start a run, read the report, change a fixture through a reviewed pull request |
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | Posts the catalog load (Reference data C) |
| RW-DATASTEW, data steward and data product owner | Confirms the catalog version as its owner (Reference data U); cannot load it |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Books the SIT slot, restores the migrated data set after the run |
| Role without Reference data C | Refused with MSG-P4-002 on the catalog load, asserted as an expected refusal |

No approval level from the delegation of authority applies; the run takes no business decision.

##### 11. Data

Table per owning schema, from the Ownership Map only. Every read of another service's data in this story is read through the owner's contract; the dictionary is read through the owner's read model.

| Schema | Service | Tables of the estate in this schema | Read in this run |
|---|---|---|---|
| rwb_source_data | P1 rwb-source-data | data_product, sys_objects, sys_fields, sys_field_version, data_contract, data_product_access, data_product_load, party_ext, contact_point_ext, account_ext, valuation_ext, interaction, efs_ledger_outcome, reconciliation_result, dp_treatment, dp_guarantee_claim | Read through the owner's contract; the dictionary read model `v_data_dictionary` is read as published by the owner |
| rwb_case | P3 rwb-case | recovery_case, case_account, case_party, case_entry_exclusion, queue, queue_member, queue_measure, task, timer, assignment, parameter_catalog, parameter_value, reference_row, reference_version, lov_value | Read through the owner's contract; the load enters through `POST /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads` |
| rwb_decision | P7 rwb-decision | decision_log_entry, approval, rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row, rule_test_case | Read through the owner's contract on `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` |
| rwb_access | P4 rwb-access | role, permission, delegation_limit, masking_rule, role_conflict | Called on `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise`; no table read |
| rwb_payment | P8 rwb-payment | the proceeds, matching, fee and booking tables of the module | Read through the owner's contract on the case payments operation |
| the other fourteen schemas | P2, P5, P6, P9, P10, S1 to S9 | their own tables of the 92 | Not read here; each is asserted to exist and to belong to one owner only |

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-REF-070 to DF-REF-079 | data_product | all 10 fields | Read 14 rows; written only by the owner's handler through the load |
| DF-REF-087 to DF-REF-093 | sys_objects | all 7 fields | Read 122 rows |
| DF-REF-094 to DF-REF-110 | sys_fields | all 17 fields | Read 1,366 rows |
| DF-EXT-001 to DF-EXT-049 | party_ext, contact_point_ext, account_ext, valuation_ext | all 49 fields | Read, through the dictionary |
| DF-CAS, DF-WRK, DF-TRT, DF-LEG, DF-PRT, DF-SAL, DF-INT, DF-DOC, DF-DEC, DF-FIN, DF-REF, DF-OPS, DF-RPT and DF-AGT prefixes | the 85 other Workbench tables | 979 fields | Read as object and field rows of the dictionary; no row of these tables is read |
| DF-ACE-018 | v_ace_account.days_past_due | one field | Read through the dictionary read model |
| DF-EXT-028 | account_ext.dispute_open | one field | Read through the dictionary read model |

The 92 tables hold 1,062 fields and the 30 views add 304, so the dictionary holds 122 objects and 1,366 fields; the run asserts those counts once, from the dictionary, not from the tables.

The dictionary carries 122 `sys_objects` rows: 98 name a data product and 24 carry none, the 13 OPS objects, the 8 AGT objects and the 3 RPT objects. Which `rwb_*` schema owns each of those 24 operational objects is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0333; ASM-0427). The run therefore asserts the owning schema of the 92 tables and of every object that names a data product, and records the 24 as a list to be resolved by the DB stories; it does not fail on them.

##### 12. Contract

This is an integration story: it publishes nothing and consumes the real contracts.

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None (integration story; no operation is published).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

Owner from the Ownership Map; base per service (DP-13).

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the run |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads` | P3 rwb-case | The catalog load with table code `data_product`; the entry point of AC13 |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | Reference data C check for the caller, called by rwb-case; granted and refused answers |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` | P7 rwb-decision | The one ledger entry of the load and the absence of a second one |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/accounts/{id}` | P1 rwb-source-data | A read path over the extension tables after the split |
| GET | `/api/recovery/payment/v1/cases/{caseId}/payments` | P8 rwb-payment | A read path of a wave-2 service over the same case, on the migrated data |

Every call goes to the owner's base, one hop, with a 2 s timeout, and none of them names another service's schema.

###### 12.3 Events published

None (no business event is produced by this story; the events asserted are in 12.4).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

The run consumes and asserts the events of the services it exercises; it produces none.

| Event | Topic | Owner | What the run asserts |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` | `rwb.source-data.events.v1` | P1 | The business date and the freshness summary arrive once per business date, with the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope and no personal data |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 | One message per load with the rule and version reference, the final call and the decided time, keyed so the ledger keeps the order |
| any message on `rwb.source-data.events.v1` | `rwb.source-data.events.v1` | P1 | The topic name, the record key and the envelope of the owner's topic are the ones the wave-1 services subscribe to; the retry and `.dlt` topics exist |

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| AceIngestCheck | Workflow, started by `AceDataReady` | `rwb-source-data` | Business date in; freshness and completeness summary out; the run reads its result before it loads the catalog |
| the ledger consumer of `rwb.decision-record.v1` | Consumer inside the service, not a workflow of this story | `rwb-decision` | One append per decision message, deduped through the inbox; the run asserts the entry, not the implementation |

No workflow is started by the harness itself; the harness observes the two queues it depends on.

|---|---|---|---|
| Chain check | 02:00, `rwb-decision` (JOB-14) | P7 | The run reads the last chain-check result and asserts that it covers the ledger entry the load produced; it never starts the schedule |

None.

None — the ITG run replaces every contract fake with the real service.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverable.** The wave-1 estate and catalog suite of the integration harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG, folder `itg/wave1`, package `<ACE base package>.recovery.itg.wave1`. It is not deployed as a service.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| EstateResolutionTest | Test | Reads `information_schema` for the 19 schemas and resolves every one of the 92 tables to one schema; fails on a missing table, a duplicated name or a table that left the estate |
| DictionaryContractTest | Test | Queries the dictionary read model for the two legacy rows and for the owning schema and service of every object; asserts the 122 objects and 1,366 fields once |
| CatalogLoadJourney | Test | Posts the fixture to rwb-case, follows the authorise answer, the handler result, the local decision record, the published event and the ledger entry |
| CatalogRepeatTest | Test | Posts the same file again and asserts MSG-P1-011, no write and one ledger entry |
| BoundaryTest | Test | Reads every foreign key, grant and view definition of the 19 schemas; fails the build on a cross-schema foreign key, a write grant outside the owner, a table read across services or a second reader of `recovery.v_ace_*` |
| RunReport | Service | Publishes the report per assertion with the service, the schema and the object named |

**Fixtures**

| Fixture | Content |
|---|---|
| catalog-2026-11-30.csv | The 14 rows DP01 to DP14 of the legacy seed table, the three system-of-record strings of DP01, DP03 and DP06, the refresh cycles DAILY, ON_CHANGE and WEEKLY, expected by 08:00, as it changes and MON 08:00, synthetic SIT owner user IDs |
| catalog-two-systems.csv | DP06 with "ACE (ingested from CCMS); SVAF" and DP11 without an owner user ID, for AC7 |
| catalog-bare-source.csv | DP06 with a bare "CCMS", for the legacy refusal |
| estate-92.csv | The estate list: the 88 Workbench tables, the four extension tables and the 20 tables that left |

**Migrated SIT data.** The migrated data set of the wave-1 DB stories: the 14 `data_product` seed rows, the 122 `sys_objects` rows and the 1,366 `sys_fields` rows, each in its owning schema, plus a case with one account and one payment for the two read paths. The harness owns no data; it restores the set after the run.

**Topology.** All nine wave-1 services plus rwb-payment run in SIT from their own pipelines, with their own schemas, logins, topics and task queues, and their real contracts. No WireMock, no stub, no seed injected into a table by the harness: a write happens only through an owner's operation, so the run proves the operations and not the tables.

**Boundary test.** One query against `information_schema` and `pg_constraint` per schema plus the view definitions of `pg_views`, and one grant review of `information_schema.role_table_grants`. The single cross-schema read allowed is the read-only grant on the rwb-source-data dictionary read model: it is the published dictionary, not a business table, and it is the one exception DP-01 accepts for a read model.

**Run order.** Lock, health and Flyway versions, estate resolution, dictionary rows, catalog journey, ledger assertion, repeat, read paths, boundary, report, unlock. The run stops at the first failed stage and the report names the stage.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON (held by the service stories) |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON (held by the service stories) |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON (held by the service stories) |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON (held by the service stories) |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON (held by the service stories) |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON (held by the platform edge story) |

The story carries no H and no C dependency: DP-03, DP-06, DP-07, DP-14, DP-15 and DP-19 resolve to contract work inside the service stories, and this run only observes their result. DP-11 resolves to the one-hop rule the boundary test asserts.

**Build steps**

1. Write the estate list fixture and EstateResolutionTest; prove it fails on a table in two schemas and on a table that left the estate.
2. Write the schema version and health step of the run.
3. Write DictionaryContractTest for the two legacy rows and for the owning schema and service of every object.
4. Write CatalogLoadJourney and prove it fails when the rwb-access answer is refused.
5. Add the ledger assertion and the local decision-record assertion.
6. Write CatalogRepeatTest and move it inside the journey so one run proves AC13 and AC15 in order.
7. Write BoundaryTest and prove it fails on a planted cross-schema foreign key, a planted cross-schema select and a second `recovery.v_ace_*` reader.
8. Add the run to the wave-1 exit gate and run it on the wave-1 build.

**Done when.** Every assertion of section 16 passes on the wave-1 build in SIT, the report names the 19 schemas and the 92 tables, the catalog load and the repeat are proven in one run, the boundary test passes with no exception beyond the dictionary read model, and the 24 operational objects of section 11 are recorded for the DB stories.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-003 | Catalog row with no system of record, more than one, a bare source name, or no owner | {product} must name one system of record, written ACE (ingested from X) or Recovery Workbench, or both where the product holds both, and one named owner. |
| MSG-P1-004 | Catalog file without exactly DP01 to DP14 | The catalog must hold the 14 data products DP01 to DP14. Missing: {products}. |
| MSG-P1-007 | Catalog value outside its list | Row {row}: {field} must be one of {values}. |
| MSG-P1-011 | Same catalog file loaded again | The {source} load for {date} is already complete or running. It was not run again. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without Reference data C | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The run asserts these texts as the services return them; it never restates them in a fixture. The report findings are for the release team and are not part of the message standard.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story. The report is read by the wave-1 exit review. The dictionary is read through the owner's read model and the catalog screen and the dictionary endpoint belong to other stories; nothing is rendered here and no screen state is asserted.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code or in a fixture beyond the legacy seed: the product names, definitions, systems of record, owners and refresh cycles are read from the catalog load, and the fixture copies the legacy seed table.
- No personal data in logs, reports, events or prompts: the run uses the masked SIT data set and the report holds table, schema, operation and message identifiers only.
- No read of another service's table: the run reads through the owners' contracts, and the one read model it reads is the published dictionary (DP-01, DP-11).
- The run never writes a table directly: a write happens only through the owner's operation, so a broken operation cannot be hidden by a seed.
- The boundary test is never relaxed per environment; a violation is fixed in the service that caused it.
- The run never touches UAT or production and never starts a Schedule.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-002 for rwb-source-data. The story keeps the case-list build behaviour of the legacy story and moves the builder from the JOB-04 Spring Batch step and its Quartz chain into the Temporal workflow `CaseListBuildWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-source-data`, reads the case through the rwb-case case query contract and ACE data through P1's own views, writes `case_list_row` in schema `rwb_source_data`, and drops the extract file, the outbound file adapter and the Power BI data set under DP-17. Gaps GAP-0485 to GAP-0487 and their assumptions are carried in §12, §13 and §16. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR)**, I want **one case list with case number, account, product, stage, status, owner, queue, route, total balance and days past due for every account at 90 days past due or more, built from the open cases and the ACE account view on each ACE business date and available in Power BI**, so that **every recovery team works from one list that is dated to the ACE batch it was built from**.

The legacy story built the list as one Spring Batch step of JOB-04, chained by Quartz after JOB-03, joined in process to `CaseQueryApi` and the `recovery.v_ace_*` views, and published it as a CSV extract through the outbound file adapter to the data lake for a Power BI data set. D-RCV-60 keeps the behaviour and moves the ownership:

- **The builder becomes a workflow.** One `CaseListBuildWorkflow` per business date on task queue `rwb-source-data` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, started by `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` (published by RWB-P1-E1015-APP) and started again, only when no run for that date is open, by the `DailyCaseList` Schedule at 07:15 Asia/Bangkok (DP-10; Arch v5 slides 44 and 12). The two activities are `listEligibleAccounts`, which reads the case through the rwb-case case query contract, and `snapshot(page)`, which reads P1's own released rows and serves them in pages (Arch v5 slide 15).
- **Case data arrives by contract, not in process.** The `CaseQueryApi` java interface of RWB-E1-018 becomes the rwb-case case query and allocation contracts, called one hop with a 2 s timeout and faked from Day 1 (DP-11; C RWB-P3-E1018-CON, C RWB-P3-E1020-CON).
- **ACE data stays read-only through P1's own views.** `v_ace_account`, `v_ace_efs_action` and `v_ace_batch_status` are read by P1 only, in schema `recovery`, with no copy and no foreign key (DP-01, DP-05, DP-02).
- **The rows live in P1's own schema.** `case_list_row` is created in `rwb_source_data` by RWB-P1-E1001-APP and written here on the service's own Flyway sequence (DP-01, DP-15). The row is the daily published projection; the case list API and screen stay with rwb-case.
- **DP-17 removes the publish path.** There is no data lake, no extract file, no outbound file adapter and no Power BI data set. The released rows are read by rwb-case for the SCR-02 case list screen and by rwb-reporting for its measures, both through P1's case-list contract: `GET /case-list/dates/{businessDate}` for the released status and row count, `GET /case-list/rows` for paged rows in the section 11 column order, and `snapshot(page)` for a caller inside the namespace.
- **Names.** REST base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`, topic `rwb.source-data.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-source-data`, namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.sourcedata` (DP-13, DP-14).

##### 2. Business rationale

Each recovery team keeps its own list of accounts today, and the lists do not agree with each other or with the source. This story builds one case list each business date from the open cases and `v_ace_account`, with the account number, balance and days past due read live from ACE rather than copied. The count is checked daily against ACE by REC-01 in RWB-P1-E1011-APP, and a business key with no ACE row is listed by REC-05. It meets REQ-RDF-007 and serves the measure "case list built and released by 07:30 on 99 percent of days" (FSD P1 v3 A2.18).

**What D-RCV-60 changes.** The list, its columns, its date and its 07:15 wait are unchanged. What changes is where the list is built, who owns the row and how a reader reaches it. Built in an event-started workflow it starts the moment the ACE batch is stamped ready instead of waiting for a Quartz chain, and it can be replayed for a business date by the platform administrator through the rerun operation (DP-10, DP-11). Owned by `rwb-source-data` it sits with the only login that may read ACE, so the balance, days past due and last contact stay read-only view reads (DP-05, ADR-010). Read by contract instead of by a lake file, the released rows reach rwb-case and rwb-reporting without a second copy and without a nightly file window (DP-17).

**Why the released status survives the lake.** Publishing was never only a file transfer: it was the point at which a reconciled list became readable by a team. That gate stays. `publish_status` still moves from PENDING to HELD or RELEASED under RWB-P1-E1011-APP, the case-list date operation still answers the released status and the row count, and a date that is HELD is not served to rwb-case or rwb-reporting. What disappears is the transfer, the retry, the exception queue task and the 07:30 data set refresh, because there is no lake to transfer to (GAP-0485).

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P1-E1001-APP is done: `case_list_row` exists in `rwb_source_data` with the columns of section 11 and the unique key on `(business_date, case_id, account_key)`.
- RWB-P1-E1069-APP is done: the Section A views exist, including `v_ace_account`, `v_ace_efs_action` and `v_ace_batch_status`, on P1's own Flyway sequence (DP-05). `v_ace_batch_status` is a Section B view, so the freshness line and the gate stay behind their flags until RWB-ACE-001 lands (DL43).
- RWB-P1-E1015-APP is done: it stamps `data_product_load` and publishes `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1`; the daily completeness gate holds the build until the ALS batch for the business date is COMPLETED.
- RWB-PLT-E1071-CON is in place: the Temporal workflow kit and the Schedule registration, on namespace `rwb-recovery` (DP-10).
- RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON are in place: the parameters and reference-data client libraries, the topic naming library, the per-service Flyway sequence and the gateway-bff composite route (DP-06, DP-07, DP-14, DP-15, DP-19).
- The rwb-case case query, allocation, parameter and reference-data contracts are published and faked (C RWB-P3-E1018-CON, C RWB-P3-E1020-CON, C RWB-P3-E1042-CON, C RWB-P3-E1043-CON).
- Parameters are loaded through the rwb-case parameter contract: `case.entry.dpd` 90 (DL16), `recon.caselist.tolerance.pct` 0.00 (assumed, DL25), `caselist.allocation.wait.until` 07:15.
- The service login `rwb_source_data` holds SELECT on the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views and no privilege on `public` or on any other `rwb_*` schema (DP-02).

##### 4. Flow

1. `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` arrives on `rwb.source-data.events.v1` for the business date, or the `DailyCaseList` Schedule fires at 07:15 Asia/Bangkok when the event has not arrived.
2. `CaseListBuildWorkflow` starts with workflow ID = business date; a second start for a date whose run is RUNNING returns MSG-P1-011 and starts nothing.
3. System: reads the business date and completion time of the ALS batch from `v_ace_batch_status` (source_system ALS, is_complete true) and asks the freshness stamp of DP01.
4. Activity `listEligibleAccounts`: reads the open case accounts for the business date from the rwb-case case query contract, each with its `case_id`, `case_no`, product group, stage, status, owner, queue, team, route and `account_key` (DP-11).
5. System: joins each `account_key` to `v_ace_account` for the account number (`account_code`), total balance and days past due, for the business date in `data_as_of` (DP-05).
6. System: reads the latest contact and action code per `account_key` from `v_ace_efs_action`.
7. System: reads the allocation state for the date from the rwb-case allocation contract and sets the check ALLOCATION_COMPLETE YES or NO.
8. System: replaces the `case_list_row` rows for the business date in one transaction, each with the refresh time and publish status PENDING, and counts the rows below the entry threshold.
9. RWB-P1-E1011-APP: the reconciliation compares the list with `v_ace_account` and sets the publish status of the date to HELD or RELEASED.
10. Reader: rwb-case for SCR-02 and rwb-reporting for its measures read the released date through `GET /case-list/dates/{businessDate}` and `GET /case-list/rows`, or call `snapshot(page)` inside the namespace; a HELD date answers its status and no rows.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A source the case list reads is not COMPLETED at the cut-off | The daily completeness gate of RWB-P1-E1015-APP holds the workflow; no `case_list_row` is written; the last released date stays the one that is served; the data steward and team managers are alerted | MSG-P1-001 | AC5 (RWB-ITG-E1002-ITG) |
| X2 | The allocation step has not completed by 07:15 | The list is built with the owner and queue as they are; the check ALLOCATION_COMPLETE is NO on the run | None (shown on the run record) | AC6 |
| X3 | The workflow runs again for the same business date | The rows for that date are replaced; no duplicate rows; the refresh time is the time of the rerun | None | AC7 |
| X4 | The rwb-case case query contract raises an error | The transaction rolls back; the run status is FAILED; the previous rows stay; the platform administrator restarts through the rerun operation | None (alert to the platform administrator) | AC8 |
| X5 | The publish step's transfer to the lake fails after the adapter retries | No longer reachable: there is no lake, no adapter and no transfer (DP-17). The check PUBLISHED is retained as history and answers YES when the date is RELEASED; see the Target reading of AC9 | None | AC9 |
| X6 | A case account has no `v_ace_account` row for the business date | The row is written with empty balance and days past due; REC-05 lists the key for the data steward and the ACE team; the case and the link are unchanged | None (REC-05) | AC10 (RWB-ITG-E1002-ITG) |
| X7 | A role without Platform administration R lists the case-list runs | 403 with the problem envelope and the guard-library refusal | MSG-P4-002 | AC11 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Reads cases only through the rwb-case contracts and ACE only through P1's own views; the readers of the list are other services that call this contract |
| Negotiable | The entry threshold, the tolerance and the wait time are parameters read by contract; the workflow and schedule names are fixed here under GAP-0487 |
| Valuable | One list for every team, with owner and queue, dated to the ACE batch, replacing the team files |
| Estimable | One workflow, two activities, one table, one contract, four fakes |
| Small | Can be finished in two weeks or less with its tests, once RWB-P1-E1069-APP and RWB-P1-E1015-APP are in |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one automated test on synthetic cases and a contract fake |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Case list v1 with case ID, owner and queue

  Background:
    Given the business date is 2026-11-30 and v_ace_batch_status shows ALS COMPLETED for 2026-11-30
    Given the parameters case.entry.dpd = 90 and recon.caselist.tolerance.pct = 0.00 are in force

  Scenario: AC2 Columns present (legacy RWB-E1-002 AC2)
    Given the case list for 2026-11-30 is built
    When the extract file for 2026-11-30 is written
    Then each row holds case number, account number, product, stage, status, owner, queue, route, total balance and days past due, in that order
    Then each row also holds team, business date and refresh time
    Then the Power BI data set "Case list v1" offers filters on team, queue and product
    Then the row for case "RW-2026-000123" shows account "ACC0000123", product "MORTGAGE", status "ASSIGNED", queue "MTG-BKK-CO", total balance 1,250,000.00 and days past due 96, the values of v_ace_account for that account_key

  Scenario: AC6 Allocation not finished (legacy RWB-E1-002 AC6)
    Given JOB-03 for 2026-11-30 has not completed at 07:15
    Given the rwb-case allocation contract mock returns ALLOCATION_COMPLETE NO for 2026-11-30
    When the case list step starts at 07:15
    Then the system builds the list with the owner and queue as they are at 07:15
    Then the run record shows check ALLOCATION_COMPLETE NO
    Then the report shows "Owners and queues may be incomplete for 30 Nov 2026"

  Scenario: AC7 Run repeated for the same date (legacy RWB-E1-002 AC7)
    Given the case list for 2026-11-30 holds 28,156 rows
    When the platform administrator restarts the step for 2026-11-30
    Then case_list_row still holds 28,156 rows for 2026-11-30 and no case account appears twice
    Then the refresh time is the time of the rerun

  Scenario: AC8 Case interface error (legacy RWB-E1-002 AC8)
    Given CaseQueryApi raises an error after 12,000 accounts are read
    Given the rwb-case case query contract mock raises an error after 12,000 accounts
    When the case list step runs
    Then the system writes no case_list_row for 2026-11-30
    Then the run status is FAILED
    Then the rows for 2026-11-27 are unchanged

  Scenario: AC9 Transfer to the lake fails (legacy RWB-E1-002 AC9)
    Given the outbound file adapter fails all its retries for the 2026-11-30 extract file
    When the publish step runs with publish_status "RELEASED"
    Then the run shows COMPLETED with check PUBLISHED NO
    Then the transfer is in the exception queue with a task for the platform administrator

  Scenario: AC11 Case list access refused (legacy RWB-E1-002 AC11)
    Given user "u-owner-01" holds RW-CASEOWN and not Platform administration R
    When the user calls GET /admin/jobs?type=JOB-04
    Then the system refuses the call with status 403 and MSG-P4-002
```

**Target reading.** Every Given, When and Then above is the legacy line, value for value, with its origin tag. The only additions are the two mock `Given` lines, on AC6 for the rwb-case allocation contract and on AC8 for the rwb-case case query contract; no legacy line is changed or dropped. What changes is where each assertion runs:

- **AC2.** The ten columns, the three extra fields and the row values are the `case_list_row` columns DF-RPT-001 to DF-RPT-019 in `rwb_source_data`, in the order the operation `GET /case-list/rows` returns them. The legacy extract file and the Power BI data set are removed by DP-17 (GAP-0485, ASM-0677): the filters on team, queue and product are query parameters of `GET /case-list/rows`, and the data set refresh line is read as the refresh time and business date the date operation answers. Case "RW-2026-000123" is the P3 case query fake fixture and account "ACC0000123" the `v_ace_account` fixture, so every legacy value is asserted unchanged.
- **AC6.** The 07:15 wait is the `DailyCaseList` Schedule time in Asia/Bangkok; the allocation mock answers ALLOCATION_COMPLETE NO for 2026-11-30, so the workflow still builds the list and still records the check.
- **AC7.** The restart is `POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun` (API-P1-002) with an Idempotency-Key, which starts `CaseListBuildWorkflow` again for the same business date; the rows are replaced in one transaction and the count 28,156 is unchanged.
- **AC8.** The failing call is the rwb-case case query contract, which is one hop from the workflow activity; the rollback, the FAILED status and the unchanged 2026-11-27 rows are unchanged in substance.
- **AC9.** Kept as history. There is no outbound file adapter and no lake in the target (DP-17), so the transfer cannot fail: PUBLISHED answers YES when the date is RELEASED and NO when it is HELD, and the exception queue task for a failed transfer has no target. The criterion is not deleted because the check it names was a real control; it is explained in GAP-0485 and ASM-0677 and is not re-implemented.
- **AC11.** The legacy call keeps its path and parameter as written; the target operation is API-P1-001 `GET /admin/jobs` with the filter parameter `jobCode`, and the 403 with MSG-P4-002 now comes from the guard library of rwb-access, so the refusal is identical in every service.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The case list holds one row per open case and linked account for the business date | REQ-RDF-007; DL17 |
| BR2 | Account number, total balance and days past due come from `v_ace_account` by `account_key` for the ACE business date in `data_as_of`; the Workbench holds no copy | D-RCV-35 U4; ADR-010 |
| BR3 | The list is built only when the daily completeness gate of RWB-P1-E1015-APP reports the sources the case list reads COMPLETE for the business date | BR-P1-014-4; MSG-P1-001 |
| BR4 | The count of accounts at or above the entry threshold is compared with `v_ace_account` by REC-01 of RWB-P1-E1011-APP; this story builds the list and records the rows below the threshold, it does not pass or fail a count | CTL-01; REC-01; `case.entry.dpd` (DL16) |
| BR5 | The list carries the business date and the refresh time on every row | REQ-RDF-009; FEAT-RDF-18 |
| BR6 | A repeated run for the same business date replaces that date's rows | R-UNI-40 |
| BR7 | A transfer that fails after the retry limit goes to the exception queue with a task for the owner | R-UNI-34; REQ-DRI-007; no transfer exists in the target (DP-17) |
| BR8 | Case data is read only through the rwb-case contracts. ACE data is read only through `recovery.v_ace_*` views | ADR-002; DT08; ADR-010 |
| BR9 | Last contact and action code come from `v_ace_efs_action` by `account_key`, taking the row with the latest `contact_at` | RWB-E1-069; Data Tier Map |
| BR10 | A case account with no ACE row is written with empty amounts and listed by REC-05; it is never deleted and the case is never changed by this story | BR-P1-011-3 |

Where each rule lives in the target: BR1, BR5 and BR6 are answered by the table `case_list_row` in `rwb_source_data` and its unique key. BR2, BR8 and BR9 are answered by the SELECT-only login on the three views and by the boundary rule of RWB-P1-E1069-DB. BR3 and BR4 are answered by the freshness gate of RWB-P1-E1015-APP and the reconciliation of RWB-P1-E1011-APP, both unchanged. BR7 keeps its text as history: with DP-17 there is no file to fail, and the exception queue task of the legacy publish step has no target. BR10 is answered by the empty-amount row and the REC-05 break list.

##### 9. State transitions

The story does not change a case status. It writes the `case_list_row` rows of the business date and moves the run state of `CaseListBuildWorkflow`, and it writes `publish_status` as PENDING only; RWB-P1-E1011-APP moves it to HELD or RELEASED.

| From | To | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| Date absent | Rows written, publish_status PENDING | `CaseListBuildWorkflow` completes for the business date |
| Rows written, PENDING | Rows written, PENDING (replaced) | The workflow is started again for the same date; the rows are replaced and the bucket count is unchanged |
| Run RUNNING | Run COMPLETED | Both activities complete and the transaction commits |
| Run RUNNING | Run FAILED | The case query contract fails; the transaction rolls back and no row of that date changes |
| publish_status PENDING | publish_status HELD or RELEASED | REC-01 and REC-02 of RWB-P1-E1011-APP, outside this story |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| `rwb_source_data` login, the service identity | Runs the workflow and both activities; writes `case_list_row`; reads the three views |
| rwb-case, the case service | Serves the case query, allocation, parameter and reference-data contracts |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Lists the runs (Platform administration R) and restarts a run (Platform administration U) |
| RW-DATASTEW, RW-COE, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-SECADM | List the runs (Platform administration R) |
| RW-BIANAL, reporting and BI analyst | Reads the released dates and rows through the case-list contract (Reporting R); the data set is no longer built from a lake file |
| RW-TEAMMGR, RW-CASEOWN, RW-PHONECOL | Read the case list on SCR-02 and on the reporting screens; row-level security by team follows RWB-P1-E1016-APP |

No approval level from the delegation of authority applies. Every "who" is a role code held as data in rwb-access and reached through its authorise contract (DP-08 is not in this story's pattern set; the guard library is used by the platform, not built here).

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and the Data Dictionary. `case_list_row` is P1's table in `rwb_source_data`; the cross-reference `case_id` is an identifier held without a foreign key, and `account_key` stays a varchar(255) business key with no foreign key to ACE (DP-01, TSD P1 v3 T3.9). The exact column widths of the paged row answer and the maximum page size are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0486; ASM-0678).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-source-data (P1); base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`. The four operations and their answer shapes are fixed here (GAP-0486; ASM-0678) because no source document gives them.

| ID | Method | Path | Shape | Access |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| API-P1-001 | GET | `/admin/jobs` | `Job[]` filtered by `jobCode`, `status`, `from`, `to`; each `Job` carries the business date, the status and the checks ROWS_BELOW_ENTRY, ALLOCATION_COMPLETE and PUBLISHED | Platform administration R |
| API-P1-002 | POST | `/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun` | `Job`; requires the Idempotency-Key header; 409 when the date is not complete in `v_ace_batch_status` or a run for it is open | Platform administration U |
| — | GET | `/case-list/dates/{businessDate}` | The business date, the `publish_status`, the row count and `refreshed_at` | Reporting R |
| — | GET | `/case-list/rows` | Paged rows in the section 11 column order, filtered by `businessDate`, `team`, `queue` and `product`; a HELD date answers its status and no rows | Reporting R |

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases?businessDate=2026-11-30` | P3 rwb-case | The open case accounts with case number, product group, stage, status, owner, queue, team, route and `account_key`; faked (RWB-P3-E1018-CON) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/cases?businessDate=2026-11-30` | P3 rwb-case | The owner and queue as they stand and the allocation state for the date; faked (RWB-P3-E1020-CON) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/parameters/{key}` | P3 rwb-case | `case.entry.dpd`, `recon.caselist.tolerance.pct` and `caselist.allocation.wait.until` with the version in force; faked (RWB-P3-E1042-CON) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/reference-data/{lovCode}` | P3 rwb-case | LOV-PUBLISH-STATUS, LOV-PRODUCT and LOV-CASE-STATUS; faked (RWB-P3-E1043-CON) |

Every call is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a circuit breaker and a bulkhead (DP-11). No call is made to rwb-integration: the outbound file adapter of RWB-P2-E1007-CON is a contract dependency only, retained because the legacy publish step named it and because its removal is the DP-17 gap (GAP-0485).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. This story publishes no business event. `publish_status` becoming RELEASED is a state of the row, not an event; the readers ask the date operation. `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` and `rwb.source-data.AceDataLate.v1` on `rwb.source-data.events.v1` belong to RWB-P1-E1015-APP (DP-14).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Starts |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` | `rwb.source-data.events.v1` | P1 (RWB-P1-E1015-APP) | `CaseListBuildWorkflow` for the business date; the payload is IDs, codes, dates and counts only |

The consumer dedupes through `processed_event` in `rwb_source_data` (DP-09 library, created by this service's DB story).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| CaseListBuildWorkflow | Workflow, one per business date, workflow ID = business date | `rwb-source-data` | Input schema (business date, source, trigger), run record shape, search attributes BusinessDate and PublishStatus; no case data and no personal data in the payload |
| listEligibleAccounts | Activity | `rwb-source-data` | Business date in; `CaseAccountRow[]` out, one per open case account, from the rwb-case case query contract and the allocation contract |
| snapshot(page) | Activity | `rwb-source-data` | Business date and page in; the page of released `case_list_row` rows in the §11 column order out; idempotent, read only, served to rwb-case for SCR-02 and to rwb-reporting for its measures |

The activity and workflow interfaces are published in the contract jar of `rwb-source-data`; a caller imports the interface and calls the owner's task queue (Arch v5 slide 11).

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Schedule | Cadence | Documented fields | Legacy reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| DailyCaseList | Daily at 07:15 Asia/Bangkok, with `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` as the primary trigger | Schedule ID `DailyCaseList`, cadence `0 15 7 * * *` in `Asia/Bangkok`, overlap policy SKIP, catch-up window one business date, business date input | JOB-04 case list step and the `caselist.allocation.wait.until` wait of 07:15 |

The Schedule name, its 07:15 fallback and the workflow name are not given by Arch v5 or by TSD P1 (GAP-0487; ASM-0679); the 07:15 value is the legacy wait kept unchanged.

| Table | Schema | Owner (Ownership Map) | This story |
|---|---|---|---|
| case_list_row | rwb_source_data | P1 | Read, replace the rows of one business date, write `publish_status` PENDING |
| data_product_load | rwb_source_data | P1 | Read only; the stamp is written by RWB-P1-E1015-APP |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | rwb_source_data | PLT library | Created in this schema; the inbox dedupes AceDataReady and the idempotency table stores the rerun response |

No other table is named and no table of another service is read (DP-01).

| Fake | Serves | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-case case query fake (RWB-P3-E1018-CON) | `GET /cases` | Every run and the AC8 error; the fixture carries case "RW-2026-000123" and account "ACC0000123" |

The four fakes are the only contract partners of this story; the rwb-integration outbound adapter of RWB-P2-E1007-CON is declared as a dependency but never called, because the file path it served is removed (DP-17).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.sourcedata.caselist`, with the published workflow and activity types in `...sourcedata.caselist.api`. REST base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`, schema and login `rwb_source_data`, topic `rwb.source-data.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-source-data` in namespace `rwb-recovery`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `CaseListBuildWorkflow` | Workflow (Temporal) | One run per business date: gate, `listEligibleAccounts`, join the views, replace the rows, record the checks; replay safe and idempotent on the business date |
| `ListEligibleAccountsActivity` | Activity | Calls the rwb-case case query and allocation contracts; returns one row per open case account; writes nothing |
| `SnapshotActivity` | Activity | Reads `case_list_row` of the released date and returns the page in the §11 column order for rwb-case and rwb-reporting |
| `CaseListRowRepository` | Repository | Deletes and inserts the rows of one business date in one transaction; no statement names another schema |
| `LastContactReader` | Service | Reads the latest `v_ace_efs_action` row per `account_key` |
| `CaseListContract` | Controller | API-P1-001, API-P1-002, the date operation and the paged-rows operation |
| `DailyCaseListRegistrar` | Component (workflow kit) | Registers or updates the Schedule; fails the release if the namespace rejects it |

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-02 | `recovery_svc` login | One login per service | none |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting | none; gap if the story needs lake data |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Build steps**

1. Write `CaseListRowRepository` against a container database in `rwb_source_data`; test the replace of one date's rows and the unchanged 2026-11-27 rows when the transaction fails (AC7, AC8).
2. Write `ListEligibleAccountsActivity` against the four contract fakes; prove that a contract error after 12,000 accounts fails the run and writes nothing (AC8).
3. Write the join to `v_ace_account` and `v_ace_efs_action` and the empty-amount row for a case account with no ACE row (AC10 fixture, proven in RWB-ITG-E1002-ITG).
4. Write the ALLOCATION_COMPLETE check from the allocation fake and the 07:15 wait from `caselist.allocation.wait.until` (AC6).
5. Write `SnapshotActivity` and the two read operations; prove the column order, the filters and that a HELD date answers no rows (AC2).
6. Write the workflow and its dedupe on the business date, and the rerun operation with the Idempotency-Key rule (AC7).
7. Register `DailyCaseList` at 07:15 Asia/Bangkok with overlap policy SKIP and prove the event trigger and the Schedule start the same workflow once (GAP-0487).
8. Add MSG-P1-001, MSG-P1-011 and MSG-P4-002 to the message table; the texts are the legacy ones.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p1.case-list`, from the platform flag library. Off: the workflow is not started and the date operation answers the last released date.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass in DEV and SIT, `CaseListBuildWorkflow` builds 28,156 rows for a synthetic business date through the four fakes, the date and rows operations serve the released date to rwb-case and rwb-reporting, and no file, adapter or lake path exists in the deployment.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-001 | The ACE batch for the business date is not complete, list not built | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |
| MSG-P1-011 | A second start while a run for the date is running or complete | The {source} load for {date} is already complete or running. It was not run again. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The IDs and texts are the legacy ones, character for character. MSG-P4-002 is now raised by the guard library of rwb-access, so the refusal is identical in every service.

##### 15. Screens and states

No Workbench screen is built in this story. The team manager reads the case list on SCR-02 Case list (Loading; empty; list; filtered), which rwb-case builds through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), and the reporting screens of rwb-reporting read the same released rows. The composite route and the screen field list belong to the edge and rwb-case stories; this story serves the two read operations and the `snapshot(page)` activity behind them. The filters are team, queue and product, and the header line shows the business date and the refresh time of the released date.

The 11 legacy TC IDs, their Covers and their Data are kept in legacy order and character for character, so a row still names AC1, AC3, AC4, AC5 or AC10 where the legacy named it: those five criteria sit with RWB-ITG-E1002-ITG, which runs them end to end against the real contracts. The legacy Level "System" maps to "End to end" and "Access" maps to "Component", because the access test now exercises the guard library in one component. The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the entry threshold, the tolerance and the wait time are parameters read through the rwb-case parameter contract, never constants (DP-06).
- No personal data in events, workflow inputs or logs: the workflow payload holds the business date and the source; the run record holds counts; `case_list_row` holds no customer name, identity number or contact value.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `recovery.v_ace_*` views: the three views are read by the `rwb_source_data` login and by no other login (DP-02, DP-05).
- No cross-schema read and no cross-schema key: every statement names `rwb_source_data`; `case_id` is an identifier and `account_key` a varchar(255) business key, both without a foreign key (DP-01).
- One hop and a 2 s timeout on every call to rwb-case, with a circuit breaker and a bulkhead per downstream (DP-11).
- The workflow is idempotent on the business date: a second start for an open or complete date starts nothing and answers MSG-P1-011.
- No file, no lake path, no adapter and no data set is created or referenced at run time (DP-17).
- No production payload is copied into a fixture; every fixture is synthetic.
