Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR)**, I want **one case list served by rwb-case with the case ID, the owner and the queue on every row, for every open case and its linked accounts, dated to the ACE business date it was built from**, so that **every recovery team works from one list that carries the same owner, the same queue and the same account position as ACE**.

Service facts: schema `rwb_case`, REST base `/api/recovery/case/v1`, topic `rwb.case.events.v1` with event names `rwb.case.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`, epic `RWB-SVC-P3` (DP-14 naming rule).

- The legacy story was a nightly batch step of the P1 data engine: it joined the open cases to `v_ace_account`, wrote `case_list_row`, reconciled the count and pushed an extract file to the data lake for a Power BI data set. This story is that list as a read of its owner: `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases` (API-P3-001), page by page, with the scope, the filters and the header `X-Data-As-Of`.
- Three owners replace the one module: the case, its account link and the queue are `rwb_case` rows of this service (DP-01); the account number, balance, days past due, last contact, action code and data as of are `rwb-source-data`'s, read through its contract one hop with a mock (DP-05, DP-11); the composite route and the screen-model merge are `gateway-bff`'s (DP-19).
- The list is no longer a file: `case_list_row`, its unique key, the lake path, the outbound adapter and the "Case list v1" data set are removed (DP-17), the daily trigger becomes the Schedule `rwb-case-caselist-daily` (DP-10), and reporting reads the events of this service in `rwb-reporting`.
- It is a Day-1 story in lane L-P3-B with no build dependency, built against the `rwb_case` baseline schema and the fakes; the eleven legacy criteria are reworked into eleven new ones (ASM-3676) and the eleven legacy test cases are kept.

##### 2. Business rationale

Each recovery team keeps its own list of accounts today, and the lists do not agree with each other or with the source. This story makes one list, served by the service that owns the case row, with the owner and the queue on every row and the account position read from the owner of ACE data rather than copied, so a manager who filters by queue sees the same owner and the same balance as the officer who opens the case.

The ownership split is the point: the case row has one owner (`rwb_case`) and the account has another (`rwb-source-data`), and neither keeps a copy of the other's value (DP-01, DP-05) — a nightly copy is what made the legacy list disagree with ACE. The freshness line is not decoration either: the list states the business date it was built from and the time it answered, so a late ALS batch shows as a stale date (AC5) rather than as a plausible but wrong list (BR3, BR5). Three rules carry the rest: a case with no owner or queue is listed with blank cells and never guessed (AC6, BR7); an account key the source answer does not hold is listed with empty amounts and goes to REC-05 (AC10, BR7); and a read stays a read — no case row, no assignment, no event and no file (BR10).

##### 3. Preconditions

| Precondition | What it gives this story |
|---|---|
| The `rwb_case` baseline schema exists with its login | `recovery_case`, `case_account`, `queue` and the standard record columns in schema `rwb_case`, one login for the service (DP-01, DP-02); the seed and fixtures of section 12.8 stand in for production rows until RWB-P3-E1018-APP fills them |
| The parameters are in force | `case.entry.dpd` 90 (DL16), `recon.caselist.tolerance.pct` 0.00 (assumed, DL25) and `caselist.allocation.wait.until` 07:15, read as parameter rows with their version through the rwb-case parameters contract (DP-06) |
| The reference data is in force | LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-STAGE, LOV-CASE-STATUS and LOV-ROUTE as reference rows with their version, through the rwb-case reference-data contract (DP-07) |
| The rwb-source-data contract answers the freshness and the account reads | `RWB-P1-E1015-CON` publishes the freshness resource and the account read this story consumes; it is built against its fake and never blocks (DP-05, DP-11; GAP-2228) |
| The workflow kit is installed | The Schedule and the workflow of 12.5 and 12.6 run through `RWB-PLT-E1071-CON` (DP-10) |
| The composite route exists | gateway-bff serves SCR-02 and merges the answer of this service and of rwb-source-data into the screen model (DP-19; `RWB-PLT-N001-CON`) |
| The caller holds a role with the Case record right R | The right, the scope and its default are declared on the operation and answered by the guard library, which holds no permission row of its own |
| The feature flag `rwb.p1.case-list` is on | Off, `GET /cases` answers 404 and the Schedule is paused (ASM-3682) |

The platform contracts the DP rows name are baselines pulled by the rwb-case platform stories; this story declares no build, contract, integration or external dependency of its own (ASM-3681).

##### 4. Flow

1. Team manager: opens SCR-02 Case list through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19); the screen shows the Loading state.
2. gateway-bff: calls `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases` with page 0 and size 50, one hop, no chaining.
3. rwb-case: the guard checks the declared Case record right R and the caller's scope, per object and per request; a role without the right is a 403 and nothing is read.
4. `CaseListQueryService`: applies the scope and the filters and reads `recovery_case`, `case_account` and `queue` in `rwb_case` only (DP-01); the page is ordered by team, queue, then case number.
5. rwb-case: asks the rwb-source-data contract twice for one page — the ALS freshness answer, and the account keys of the page — each one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker (DP-05, DP-11).
6. `CaseListRowMapper`: builds one row per open case with case ID, case number, product group, stage, status, owner, queue, team, route, entry date and its account keys, then the account number, total balance, days past due, last contact, action code and data as of from the source answer; an account key the answer does not hold leaves blank cells and is listed for REC-05, never guessed (AC10).
7. `CaseListRowMapper`: stamps the row's refresh time and the page's `X-Data-As-Of` from the freshness answer, and flags the page stale when the ALS batch for the date is not complete (AC3, AC5).
8. rwb-case: answers `CasePage` with `page`, `size`, `total` and the header; the read holds no lock beyond its statement and writes nothing.
9. Screen: the ten columns, the filters on team, queue and product and the refresh line; a row opens the case record of RWB-P3-E1023-APP, which is a separate route.
10. 07:15, or the configured wait time: the Schedule `rwb-case-caselist-daily` starts `CaseListDayOpen` for the business date; it reads the freshness answer once and raises MSG-P1-001 to the team manager group when the batch is late (AC5). It writes no row and changes no page content.
11. No extract file is written, no lake path is called and no report data set is refreshed by this service (DP-17; AC9).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The ALS batch for the business date is not complete | Rows carry the last complete ACE date and are marked stale; no row claims the missing date; the day-open run alerts the team manager group | MSG-P1-001 | AC5 |
| X2 | A case has no owner or no queue at the wait time | Blank owner and blank queue cells, the case is still listed, the page shows the incomplete line | None (shown on the page) | AC6 |
| X3 | A linked account key is absent from the source answer | Empty account number, balance and days past due for that row; the key is listed for REC-05; the case and the link are unchanged | None (REC-05) | AC10 |
| X4 | The rwb-source-data contract answers an error or passes 2 s | 503 with no partial page; the read is retried once with jitter; no row carries a half-filled account column | MSG-GEN-006 | AC8 |
| X5 | The same page is read twice for the same business date | The same rows in the same order, no duplicate case, the refresh time of the second read | None | AC7 |
| X6 | A caller holds no Case record right | 403, no row and no column read | MSG-P4-002 | AC11 |
| X7 | A filter value is outside its list | 422 before any case is read; the list stays as it is | MSG-GEN-007 | AC11 |
| X8 | The page size is outside 1 to 200 | 422 before any case is read | MSG-GEN-002 | AC1 |

X6 and X7 answer with a status on purpose: a value outside its list is a caller error, and a missing right is a refusal with a status — neither returns an empty page, because an empty page reads as "no work" and hides a permission problem.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Reads only `rwb_case` rows and builds against the fakes of the source-data, access and workflow contracts, so neither rwb-source-data nor rwb-access needs to exist in the development environment |
| Negotiable | Page bounds, the wait time and the list values are parameter and reference rows; the row shape and the freshness rule are fixed |
| Valuable | One list per team with owner, queue and account position, dated to the ACE batch it came from, replacing the team files and one nightly extract |
| Estimable | One query operation, one row mapper, two downstream reads, one Schedule and one workflow |
| Small | Fits in two weeks: query, mapper, page, two fakes, one Schedule |
| Testable | Every criterion has a test case in section 16; the refusals and the stale page are contract tests and the columns are component tests |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Case list v1 with case ID, owner and queue

  Background:
    Given the rwb-source-data contract mock returns 28,140 accounts at 90 days past due or more with dataAsOf 2026-11-30
    Given the parameters case.entry.dpd = 90 and recon.caselist.tolerance.pct = 0.00 are in force
    Given the rwb_case seed holds open cases with their linked account keys

  Scenario: AC1 One row per open case with its case ID, owner and queue (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given rwb_case holds 28,119 open cases and 28,156 linked account keys
    Given 37 of the linked accounts are below 90 days past due
    When a caller reads GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases with page 0 and size 200
    Then the page holds total 28,119 and each case appears once
    Then every row carries its case ID, case number, owner user ID, queue code and team code
    Then the 37 accounts below 90 days past due appear on the account list of their case and add no case row

  Scenario: AC2 Columns present (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given case "RW-2026-000123" links account "ACC0000123"
    Given the rwb-source-data contract mock returns account "ACC0000123" with account number "ACC0000123", product "MORTGAGE", total balance 1,250,000.00 and days past due 96 for 2026-11-30
    When the case list is read
    Then the row shows case number "RW-2026-000123", account number "ACC0000123", product "MORTGAGE", status "ASSIGNED", queue "MTG-BKK-CO", total balance 1,250,000.00 and days past due 96
    Then each row also holds team, business date and refresh time
    Then the page offers filters on team, queue and product
    Then the account values are the source answer for that account key and rwb-case holds no copy of them

  Scenario: AC3 Daily refresh (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the ALS batch for 2026-11-30 completed at 05:40 and the allocation for 2026-11-30 completed at 06:52
    When the case list is read and answers at 07:12 on 2026-12-01
    Then every row carries refresh time 2026-12-01 07:12
    Then the header X-Data-As-Of is 2026-11-30
    Then the refresh line reads "Refreshed 1 Dec 2026 07:12, data as of 30 Nov 2026"

  Scenario: AC4 Last contact from the EFS history through the owner (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rwb-source-data contract mock returns for account "ACC0000123" last contact 2026-11-30 15:42 with action code "PTP"
    When the row of case "RW-2026-000123" is read
    Then the row shows last contact 2026-11-30 15:42 and action code "PTP"
    Then rwb-case holds neither the contact time nor the action code

  Scenario: AC5 ACE batch not complete (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rwb-source-data contract mock returns freshness for ALS with no COMPLETED row for 2026-11-30
    When the case list is read at 08:00
    Then the rows carry the last complete business date 2026-11-27 in X-Data-As-Of and are marked stale
    Then no row claims business date 2026-11-30
    Then the team manager group receives MSG-P1-001 "DP01 Account and arrears is from 2026-11-27. Today's ACE batch has not arrived."

  Scenario: AC6 Allocation not finished (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given case "RW-2026-000456" has no owner and no queue at 07:15
    When the case list is read
    Then the row of "RW-2026-000456" shows a blank owner and a blank queue and is still listed
    Then the page shows "Owners and queues may be incomplete for 30 Nov 2026"

  Scenario: AC7 Same page read twice (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the list for 2026-11-30 returned 28,119 rows on the first read
    When the same read is made again for 2026-11-30
    Then the page holds total 28,119 again and no case appears twice
    Then the refresh time is the time of the second read

  Scenario: AC8 Source contract error (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rwb-source-data contract mock answers an error after the accounts of 40 rows are read
    When the case list is read
    Then the response is 503 with no partial page and no row carries a half-filled account column
    Then the read is retried once with jitter and the second answer is served

  Scenario: AC9 No extract file and no data lake (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the case list for 2026-11-30 is served
    When the read completes
    Then no extract file is written and no lake path or lake credential is called
    Then the reporting read model is built by rwb-reporting from the events of rwb.case.events.v1

  Scenario: AC10 Case account without an ACE account row (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given case "RW-2026-000456" links account key "ACC0000456", which the rwb-source-data contract does not return for 2026-11-30
    When the case list is read
    Then the row for "ACC0000456" has an empty account number, total balance and days past due
    Then REC-05 of RWB-P1-E1011 lists "case_account.account_key ACC0000456" as an orphan for the data steward and the ACE team

  Scenario: AC11 Case list access refused (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given user "u-owner-01" holds the Case record right R with scope Own and case "RW-2026-000123" is owned by "u-owner-02"

```

Every scenario is tagged `(new, D-RCV-60)`: this story owns no legacy criterion identifier, and the eleven legacy criteria AC1 to AC11 of RWB-E1-002 are reworked into these eleven, keeping the legacy values, the legacy columns and the legacy test cases (ASM-3676). Each cross-service Given carries the rwb-source-data mock and every value the legacy story attributes to ACE.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The list holds one row per open case for the business date, with its linked account keys; a linked account below the entry threshold adds no case row | REQ-RDF-007; DL17 (one case per customer per product, accounts linked) |
| BR2 | Account number, total balance, days past due, last contact, action code and data as of come from rwb-source-data by account key for the ACE business date; the Workbench holds no copy | D-RCV-35 U4; ADR-010; DP-05 |
| BR3 | The list is served only with the freshness answer of the owner of ACE data; a date that is not complete is marked stale and never presented as complete | BR-P1-014-4; MSG-P1-001 |
| BR4 | The count of accounts at or above the entry threshold is compared with the ACE count by REC-01 of RWB-P1-E1011; this story serves the rows and passes or fails no count | CTL-01; REC-01; parameter case.entry.dpd (DL16) |
| BR5 | Every row carries the business date and the refresh time, and the page carries the same date in `X-Data-As-Of` | REQ-RDF-009 (freshness); FEAT-RDF-18 |
| BR6 | The same request on unchanged data returns the same rows in the same order; no read writes or replaces a row, so a repeated read is safe | R-UNI-40 read as idempotence of a read |
| BR7 | An account key the source answer does not hold is listed with empty amounts and goes to REC-05; it is never deleted and the case is never changed by this story | BR-P1-011-3; REQ-DRI-007 |
| BR8 | Case data is read only from the rows of this service, and ACE data only through the rwb-source-data contract; no other schema is named | ADR-002; DT08; ADR-010 |
| BR9 | Last contact and action code come from the source answer for the account key, taking the row with the latest `contact_at` | RWB-E1-069; OpenAPI `GET /cases` |
| BR10 | No extract file, no data-lake transfer, no Power BI data set and no event from this service; reporting reads the case events of the owner topic | DP-17; AC9 |

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story changes no case status and writes no row: it reads `recovery_case`, `case_account` and `queue`, and it changes the run state of nothing. The only states it exposes are the case statuses of LOV-CASE-STATUS and the stage codes of LOV-STAGE as rows in force; a filter value outside its list is refused before a case is read (AC11). The Schedule run of 12.5 has Temporal execution states only — RUNNING, COMPLETED, FAILED — and no case state.

| Who | What they may do in this story |

| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | Reads the list for every queue of the team (Case record R, Team scope) |

| SY-CASEWF, case workflow identity | Runs the Schedule's workflow and its activities |
| No approval applies | The story takes no decision and records none |

The role names are read from rwb-access by the guard; no name of a person appears anywhere and the owner is a staff user reference only.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/case/v1`; owner rwb-case (P3).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/cases` | One page of the open cases in the caller's scope, each row carrying case ID, case number, product group, stage, status, owner, queue, team, route, entry date, its account keys and the account columns of the legacy list, with `X-Data-As-Of` | Case record R, scope applied per object | Read only: the same request on unchanged data returns the same rows in the same order (BR6) |

Query: `product`, `stage`, `status`, `owner`, `queue`, `caseNo`, `ageFrom`, `ageTo`, `route`, `page`, `size` (1 to 200), `sort`. The response is `CasePage`: `items` of `CaseListRow`, `page`, `size`, `total`. `CaseListRow` adds to the `Case` schema of API-P3-001 the elements `caseId`, `accountKeys`, `accountNumber`, `totalBalance`, `daysPastDue`, `lastContactAt`, `lastActionCode`, `dataAsOf`, `refreshedAt` and `stale`, all of which are the legacy columns of the case list. `refreshedAt` is the time the read answered and `dataAsOf` the ACE business date of the freshness answer, also carried in `X-Data-As-Of` with the stale flag (ASM-3678). The schema names and the problem body are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2228; ASM-3677).

Errors: 401 no session (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Case record right (MSG-P4-002); 422 a filter value outside its list (MSG-GEN-007) or a page size outside its bounds (MSG-GEN-002); 503 the store is down or the source-data contract does not answer inside its budget (MSG-GEN-006).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

One hop, no chaining; 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). Both rows are the rwb-source-data contract of RWB-P1-E1015-CON.

| Method | Path | Service | Used for | Timeout |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/accounts/{accountKey}` | rwb-source-data (P1) | Account number, total balance, days past due, data as of and the latest contact and action code of one account key; called for the keys of the page, or with the key list where the contract publishes its batch form | One hop, 2 s, breaker, retry once with jitter |
| GET | `/data-products/freshness` | rwb-source-data (P1) | The ALS business date, its completion time and the stale flag behind `X-Data-As-Of` and the refresh line | One hop, 2 s, breaker |

The account path is the one Architecture v5 slide 10 names for the case screen, and the freshness resource is RWB-P1-E1015-CON's; whether one call carries the page's key list or one call is made per key is a contract fact of that baseline (GAP-2228; ASM-3677). The parameters and the reference rows are in-process library reads of this same service and are not rows of this table (DP-06, DP-07).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The read writes no outbox row and publishes no event. The topic `rwb.case.events.v1` with the names `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1`, `rwb.case.CaseAllocated.v1`, `rwb.case.CaseAllocationFailed.v1`, `rwb.case.CaseTransferred.v1`, `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1`, `rwb.case.TimerBreached.v1` and the signal `rwb.case.CaseEvent.v1` belongs to the stories that own the case, allocation, transfer, state and timer behaviour under DP-14; this story adds none and the owner topic is named only as the service baseline (BR10).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The page is read from the rows per request, so a case that moves is seen on the next read; no inbox row is written and no subscription is added. `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` and `rwb.source-data.AceDataLate.v1` are the trigger of the case creation and the freshness of this list, and the freshness answer of 12.2 carries the date this page states rather than a stored event.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Item | Type | Name | Queue | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb-case-caselist-daily` → `CaseListDayOpen`, workflow ID `case-list-{businessDate}` | Workflow | `CaseListDayOpen` | `rwb-case` | Opens the list day for one business date: reads the freshness answer once, and raises the stale alert when the ALS batch is late (AC5) |
| Freshness read | Activity | `readFreshness` | `rwb-case` | The one call of 12.2 to the freshness resource, logged by id and business date only |
| Stale alert | Activity | `raiseStaleListAlert` | `rwb-case` | MSG-P1-001 to the team manager group when the date is stale |

The workflow is deterministic and holds no clock read and no I/O; the fixed workflow ID makes a repeated start of the same business date a no-op (TSD T2.4 convention, read for `rwb-case`).

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Schedule | Workflow | Cron | Zone | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb-case-caselist-daily` | `CaseListDayOpen` | `0 15 7 * * ?` from the parameter `caselist.allocation.wait.until` | Asia/Bangkok | Overlap policy SKIP; a manual trigger is Platform administration U; the list itself stays a read, so the Schedule changes no row |

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Schema | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|---|
| `recovery_case` | rwb_case | rwb-case (P3) | The case row behind every list row: case number, product group, status, stage, route, owner, queue, team and entry date |
| `case_account` | rwb_case | rwb-case (P3) | The account keys of the case and the primary flag that orders the account columns |
| `queue` | rwb_case | rwb-case (P3) | The queue code and team of the owner and queue columns and of the filter values |
| `parameter_catalog`, `parameter_value` | rwb_case | rwb-case (P3) | The threshold, the tolerance, the wait time and the page bounds, read in process (DP-06) |
| `reference_row`, `reference_version`, `lov_value` | rwb_case | rwb-case (P3) | The four lists of values in force (DP-07) |

No other table is named. `case_list_row` is removed with the data lake (DP-17) and is not read here; `assignment` and `queue_member` are this service's and are not read, because the list needs the current owner on the case row; no `rwb_access` or `rwb_source_data` table is read (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 1 provided, 2 consumed | `GET /cases` provided; the account read and the freshness read of rwb-source-data consumed; one hop, 2 s, breaker, one retry with jitter |
| Kafka | None | No event published and none consumed (12.3, 12.4) |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`, module `caselist`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case.caselist`; front end `src/modules/recovery/case/caselist`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_case`; the list reads `recovery_case`, `case_account` and `queue` of this service only | none |
| DP-02 | `recovery_svc` login | One login per service; the `rwb_case` login holds grants on `rwb_case` only | none |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | The account, contact and batch columns are read through the rwb-source-data contract, not from a view | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library: threshold, tolerance, wait time, page bounds | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case: the four lists in force | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | The Quartz chain step becomes the Schedule `rwb-case-caselist-daily` through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | The legacy `CaseQueryApi` and the ACE-view join become REST calls of the rwb-source-data contract with a mock, one hop, 2 s | none (C from the legacy dependency RWB-E1-069) |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.case.events.v1` and `rwb.case.<Event>.v1` from the naming library; this story publishes nothing | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in `rwb_case`: the list indexes land here | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed: no data lake; `case_list_row`, the extract file and the Power BI data set go, and reporting reads events | none; gap GAP-2228 |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route for SCR-02 | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-09 is not applied: the read publishes nothing. The platform CON rows above are library baselines of the service, and the four dependency rows of the metadata table stay None as the story's WP fixes them (ASM-3681).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| CaseListController | Controller | `GET /cases`; the filter and page validation; the problem responses with their message ids |
| CaseListQueryService | Service | Scope and filter predicate over `recovery_case`, `case_account` and `queue`; the stable order; the page envelope |
| CaseListRowMapper | Component | One row per case with the legacy columns, the account keys, the blanks of AC10 and the stale flag of AC5 |
| SourceDataClient | Client | The two reads of 12.2, one hop, 2 s, breaker, one retry with jitter (DP-05, DP-11) |
| AccessCheckClient | Client | The declared Case record right and the caller's scope, cached per request |
| CaseAndWorkflowRepository | Repository | Paged query on the three tables of 12.7 in `rwb_case` |
| CaseListDayOpen | Workflow | The day-open workflow of 12.5, with its two activities |
| CaseListPage | React component | SCR-02: columns, filters, refresh line, Loading, list, stale and refused states |

**Database and migrations**

- Reads `recovery_case`, `case_account` and `queue`; no row is written and no foreign key points out of `rwb_case`.
- `V012_1__case_list_index.sql` in the rwb-case Flyway sequence after the V0001 baseline (DP-15; RWB-PLT-E1044-CON): `ix_case_list_team_queue` on `recovery_case (team_code, queue_id, status)` and `ix_case_account_key` on `case_account (account_key)`. If RWB-P3-E2033-APP already lands an index on the same columns, that one is used and this migration is not created.
- The legacy key `uk_case_list_row UNIQUE (business_date)` and its replacement `UNIQUE (business_date, case_id, account_key)` are dropped with the table, which now belongs to nobody (GAP-2228; ASM-3680).

**Configuration and reference data**

- `case.entry.dpd` 90, `recon.caselist.tolerance.pct` 0.00, `caselist.allocation.wait.until` 07:15 and the page bounds 1 to 200 are parameter rows with the version in force (DL16, DL25; ASM-3679); no value is a constant.
- The lists come through the reference-data contract (DP-07); the labels follow the label standard (DL10).
- The feature flag keeps the legacy name `rwb.p1.case-list` (ASM-3682). Off: `GET /cases` answers 404 and the Schedule is paused.

**Build steps**

1. `CaseListController` and `CaseListRowMapper` against the fakes, with the 401, 403, 422 and 503 bodies; AC1, AC2.
2. `CaseListQueryService` and `CaseAndWorkflowRepository` with the scope predicate, the filters and the stable order; AC1, AC7, AC11.
3. `SourceDataClient` with the two reads, the blanks of AC10 and the stale flag of AC5; AC3, AC4, AC5, AC8, AC10.
4. `CaseListPage` with the ten columns, the filters and the five states; AC2, AC6.
5. `CaseListDayOpen`, its two activities and the Schedule wiring in the workflow kit test environment; AC5.
6. The removal check of AC9 and the 2 s check on 26,500 cases at the 95th percentile.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p1.case-list`. Off: no list and no Schedule.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass; the list answers in under 2 s at the 95th percentile on 26,500 cases in SIT; no query of this story names a schema other than `rwb_case`; no extract file, lake call or report refresh exists in the build; and AC5 is seen in the test server of the workflow kit.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Where it is produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-001 | The ACE batch for the business date is not complete | DP01 Account and arrears is from 2026-11-27. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. | rwb-source-data freshness answer, surfaced here and by `raiseStaleListAlert` |
| MSG-P4-001 | No valid session | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2228; ASM-3677) | The guard, surfaced here |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | The guard, surfaced here |
| MSG-GEN-007 | A filter value is outside its list | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2228; ASM-3677) | This story, before a case is read |
| MSG-GEN-002 | A page size is outside its bounds | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2228; ASM-3677) | This story, before a case is read |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The source-data contract does not answer | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2228; ASM-3677) | This story, on the 503 of X4 |

The texts of MSG-P1-001, MSG-P4-002 and the two owner lines are copied from the legacy story character for character and no identifier is renumbered. The refusal order is fixed: the session, the right, the filter values, the page bounds, then the cases, then the source reads; a request refused at any of the first four steps reads nothing.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the threshold, the tolerance, the wait time, the page bounds and the lists are parameter and reference rows with the version in force (BR5; DP-06, DP-07).
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts: a row carries the case number, codes, dates, amounts and a staff user reference, never a customer name, identity number, address or contact value; the test data is synthetic.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: no view, no `v_ace_*` name and no foreign key into ACE in this service (DP-05).
- No read of another service's tables, and no other schema named by a query or a view of this story (DP-01).
- One hop at a time: rwb-case calls rwb-source-data and returns; it never calls a service that calls another (ADR-020).
- A refusal is a refusal: a role without the right is a 403 and never a thinner row or an empty page.
- No event, no workflow payload with personal data, and no file: the Schedule's history carries the business date and case identifiers only (BR10).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-002 for rwb-source-data. This story deploys the case-list capability: the api and worker deployments of `rwb-source-data`, the Temporal worker for `CaseListBuildWorkflow` with its KEDA scaling, the `DailyCaseList` Schedule registration at 07:15 Asia/Bangkok, the configuration of the three parameters by contract, the read path of rwb-case and rwb-reporting, the dashboards, the MSG-P1-001 and PUBLISHED NO alerts, the runbook and the capacity. It deploys no lake credential, no file adapter and no data set (DP-17; GAP-0485, ASM-0677). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform engineer**, I want **rwb-source-data deployed from the service template with its api and worker deployments, its Flyway migration job, its probes, its Temporal worker and KEDA scaling on the `rwb-source-data` task queue, the `DailyCaseList` Schedule registered at 07:15 Asia/Bangkok, the three case-list parameters read from the rwb-case parameter contract, the read path that serves the released case list to rwb-case and rwb-reporting, the dashboards and the MSG-P1-001 and PUBLISHED NO alerts, the runbook and the capacity plan**, so that **the case list of every business date is built, released and read predictably in every environment, and an operator can see and act on a late batch, a failed run or a date that never released without reading code or a lake file**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story depends on a Quartz chain, one shared schema, an outbound file adapter and a Power BI refresh at 07:30. In the target a service is a Helm release built by one pipeline with its own schema, login, topic, queue and Schedules (DP-02, DP-10, DP-15), and the list is read by contract instead of by a lake file (DP-17). Deployment is therefore part of the capability: an unregistered Schedule means a business date with no list when the ACE event is late, a worker without KEDA means a backlog that misses the 07:30 measure, and an alert that fires only on an exception misses a date that is HELD by reconciliation and never releases. This story makes the run observable and repeatable so the app story can be proven in SIT and the on-call rota can operate it.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template, chart skeleton and pipeline are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-LIB), and the Temporal workflow kit with namespace `rwb-recovery` is in place (RWB-PLT-WF, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON).
- The Kafka event platform provisions topics with a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON).
- The ACE database administrator has created schema `rwb_source_data` and the login, with SELECT on the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views and no grant on any other schema (DP-02, DP-05).
- The platform error envelope, the message catalogue and the alert routing are in force, so an alert can carry a message ID.
- The three environments DEV, SIT and UAT exist with the parameter scope of LOV-ENVIRONMENT.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. The pipeline builds one image and one chart version from one commit, runs the unit, component and contract tests, scans the image and the dependencies, and publishes the chart.
2. The chart deploys the api deployment and the worker deployment with the `rwb_source_data` login reference, the pre-deploy migration job and the probes; the migration job runs on the per-service Flyway sequence before the rollout is marked ready.
3. The provisioning step creates the consumer group for `rwb.source-data.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` paths and registers the Temporal task queue `rwb-source-data` in namespace `rwb-recovery`.
4. The Schedule registration step creates or updates `DailyCaseList` at 07:15 Asia/Bangkok with overlap policy SKIP and the catch-up window, and checks that `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` starts the same workflow for the business date (GAP-0487).
5. The configuration step wires the three parameters through the rwb-case parameter contract and the reference lists through the reference-data contract; no parameter value is written into a values file.
6. The dashboards are published: runs started and finished, rows written, rows below entry, allocation complete, publish status by date, run duration, activity retries, consumer lag.
7. The alerts are wired to MSG-P1-001 and to the PUBLISHED NO check, and to the runbook entries.
8. A smoke step starts `CaseListBuildWorkflow` for a synthetic business date in a test namespace against the four fakes and checks the run record, the released date and the probes.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The migration job fails | The deployment stays unready and the pipeline stops; no traffic to the new version | None | AC1 |
| X2 | The readiness probe fails after the start-up window | The pod is removed from the service and the pipeline marks the release failed | None | AC3 |
| X3 | The task queue is not registered or the worker build ID is not on the version set | The release fails; a case list would otherwise never be built | None | AC4 |
| X4 | The Schedule registration is rejected by the namespace | The release fails | None | AC5 |
| X5 | A run waits for a complete ALS batch | The alert carries MSG-P1-001 with the product and the last completed date, and the batch-gate runbook entry | MSG-P1-001 | AC6 |
| X6 | A date is reconciled but never released | The alert carries the PUBLISHED NO check with the business date and opens a ticket for the data steward | None (check PUBLISHED NO) | AC6 |
| X7 | A run fails on the case query contract | The failed-run alert carries the run ID and the contract name, and the runbook entry restarts through the rerun operation | None | AC6 |
| X8 | A role without Platform administration R lists the runs | The refused-read count is visible on the dashboard only and never pages the on-call rota | MSG-P4-002 | AC6 |
| X9 | A lake credential, a file adapter or a data set is found in the chart or the values | The pipeline fails the release on the DP-17 guard | None | AC1 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the chart skeleton, the platform topic provisioning and the workflow kit; no application code is built here |
| Negotiable | Replica counts, resource sizes and alert thresholds are environment values, not story decisions |
| Valuable | Makes the case-list run deployable, observable and repeatable in every environment, and removes the lake dependency from the release |
| Estimable | One chart, one pipeline stage, one migration job, two deployments, two probes, one provisioning step, one Schedule registration, six dashboard panels, four alert rules and five runbook entries |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the runbook and the capacity plan |
| Testable | Every criterion tests an artefact: the chart renders, the probes answer, the queue is registered, the Schedule fires, the alerts fire on a synthetic metric |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Deployment of the rwb-source-data case-list capability

  Background:
    Given the service template chart and the platform pipeline are in force
    Given the target environment is SIT

  Scenario: AC1 The chart deploys the api and worker with no lake artefact (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rwb-source-data Helm chart and its values files
    When the chart is rendered for DEV, SIT and UAT
    Then each render succeeds with the chart version and the image digest pinned
    Then the release declares the api deployment and the worker deployment, the pre-deploy migration job and the platform secret references
    Then the migration job runs the per-service Flyway sequence in schema rwb_source_data before the rollout is marked ready
    Then the release declares no lake credential, no file adapter, no outbound mount and no data-set job
    Then no replica count, resource size, Schedule cadence or parameter value is hard-coded in the template

  Scenario: AC2 The pipeline builds, tests and promotes one artefact (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a commit on the main line
    When the pipeline runs
    Then it builds one image and one chart version from the same commit
    Then it runs the unit, component and contract tests and fails the build on a contract drift
    Then it scans the image and the dependencies and fails on a critical finding
    Then it promotes the same artefact through DEV, SIT and UAT without a rebuild

  Scenario: AC3 Readiness and liveness probes answer (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a running pod of the api and of the worker
    When the readiness probe is called before the migration job and the start-up window complete
    Then the pod is not marked ready
    When the readiness and liveness endpoints are called after start-up
    Then both answer healthy without a database write
    Then a failing dependency, including the ACE views or the rwb-case contract, is reported as not ready and never as live-and-broken

  Scenario: AC4 The Temporal worker, the task queue and KEDA scaling are in place (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the provisioning step and the worker deployment
    When a synthetic backlog is queued on rwb-source-data in namespace rwb-recovery
    Then the worker polls only its own task queue with the release build ID on the version set
    Then KEDA scales the worker on backlog and returns to the minimum when the backlog clears
    Then CaseListBuildWorkflow, listEligibleAccounts and snapshot(page) are registered by the same worker
    Then the consumer group of rwb.source-data.events.v1 is configured with the retry topic, the .dlt topic and the inbox dedupe

  Scenario: AC5 The DailyCaseList Schedule is registered and fires once per business date (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the Schedule registration step
    When it runs
    Then DailyCaseList is registered at 07:15 Asia/Bangkok with overlap policy SKIP and the one-business-date catch-up window
    Then a synthetic business date starts one run through the Schedule and one through rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1, and only one run exists for that date
    Then a second start for a running or complete date starts nothing and answers MSG-P1-011
    Then the run record carries rows written, rows below entry, allocation complete and publish status

  Scenario: AC6 Dashboards, alerts and the runbook cover the legacy controls (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published dashboard and the runbook
    When a synthetic run is replayed with a late batch, a failed case query call and a date held by reconciliation
    Then each condition raises the alert that carries MSG-P1-001 for the late batch, the run ID for the failure and the PUBLISHED NO check for the held date, with the legacy text where a message exists
    Then the refused-read count carries MSG-P4-002 and does not page the on-call rota
    Then every alert links one runbook entry with the check, the owner role and the recovery step
    Then the dashboard shows the publish status of every date of the last 30 days

  Scenario: AC7 The read path serves the released list to rwb-case and rwb-reporting (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a released business date and a held business date
    When rwb-case reads the date operation for SCR-02 and rwb-reporting reads the paged rows for its measures, both through the gateway-bff composite route
    Then the released date answers its row count and its rows in the 19-column order within the 2 s budget
    Then the held date answers its status and no rows
    Then no reader is given a file path, a lake location or a data-set name
    Then the route target and the health check of the two read operations are registered and answer

  Scenario: AC8 The capacity plan covers the peak business date (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the capacity plan of the service
    When it is checked against the peak figures of the case-list run
    Then it states the rows of a peak date, the pages served to rwb-case and rwb-reporting, the worker maximum and the database connection cap of the login
    Then the plan keeps the run inside the 07:30 measure with the worker at its maximum and the migration job idle
    Then the plan records no lake throughput and no file window, because both are removed
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One service, one schema, one login: the release uses the `rwb_source_data` login reference and no other service's credential | DP-02; Arch v5 slide 29 |
| BR2 | The migration is a per-service Flyway sequence in schema `rwb_source_data` and runs before the rollout is ready | DP-15; RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| BR3 | Every topic has a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic, and the consumer dedupes through the inbox | DP-09; Arch v5 slide 11 |
| BR4 | A Temporal Schedule uses overlap policy SKIP with a catch-up window, and the event-started workflow takes the business date as its input | DP-10; Arch v5 slide 44 |
| BR5 | No environment value is hard-coded: replica counts, resource sizes, thresholds, cadences and the three parameters come from values files and contracts | DP-06; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR6 | An alert carries a message ID where one exists, the agreed text, and links one runbook entry | Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR7 | A refused read is counted on the dashboard and never pages the on-call rota | MSG-P4-002 |
| BR8 | The service writes only schema `rwb_source_data` and reads ACE only through the `recovery.v_ace_*` views | DP-01, DP-05 |
| BR9 | The release carries no lake credential, file adapter or data-set job; a chart that does fails the DP-17 guard | DP-17; GAP-0485 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | Chart published | The image, the chart and the migration job pass the pipeline | Deploying |
| Deploying | Migration job complete and probes healthy | The schema is at the expected version, the worker has polled and both probes answer | Ready |
| Ready | Release superseded | A new chart version is promoted | Rolling |
| Rolling | All pods on the new version | The old ReplicaSet drains and the worker build ID is on the version set | Ready |
| Ready | Migration job failed or the Schedule rejected | The schema is not at the expected version or the namespace refused the Schedule | Failed |
| Failed | Rollback | The previous chart version is redeployed; the Schedule is re-registered from the previous release | Ready |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |

| DevOps engineer | Owns the chart, the values files, the pipeline stages, the provisioning and Schedule registration steps, the dashboards, the alerts and the runbook |
| Platform administrator | Owns the `rwb-recovery` namespace, the topic provisioning and the Schedule registration rights |
| ACE database administrator | Owns the `rwb_source_data` schema, the login, its grants and the migration job approval |
| Release manager | Approves the promotion of one artefact through the environments |
| On-call operator | Runs the runbook entries and opens an incident when the PUBLISHED NO check or MSG-P1-001 persists |
| RW-PLATADM | Reads and reruns the case list in the running service, not in the cluster |

The per-service login name used by the chart is the fixed name `rwb_source_data` (DP-02); the chart references it through a secret reference and never a literal password.

There is no lake path, no extract file and no data-set refresh time to document (DP-17; GAP-0485).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

The deployment exposes the four operations of the contract baseline behind gateway-bff: `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs`, `POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun`, `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/case-list/dates/{businessDate}` and `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/case-list/rows`. Owner rwb-source-data (P1). The probes are cluster-internal and are not part of the API surface.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Deployment need |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases` | P3 rwb-case | The open case accounts; 2 s client budget (DP-11) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/cases` | P3 rwb-case | Allocation state, owner and queue |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/parameters/{key}` | P3 rwb-case | The three case-list parameters with their version |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/reference-data/{lovCode}` | P3 rwb-case | LOV-PUBLISH-STATUS, LOV-PRODUCT and LOV-CASE-STATUS |

No operation of rwb-integration is consumed: the outbound file adapter of RWB-P2-E1007-CON is not deployed, because the publish path it served is removed (DP-17).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-02 | `recovery_svc` login | One login per service | none |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting | none; gap if the story needs lake data |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Artefacts**

| Artefact | Content |
|---|---|
| `helm/rwb-source-data/` | Chart with the api deployment, the worker deployment, the service, the migration job, the config map, the secret references, the probes and the Schedule registration hook |
| `helm/rwb-source-data/values-dev.yaml`, `values-sit.yaml`, `values-uat.yaml` | Image digest, replicas, resources, probe timings, log level, feature switches, environment name |
| Pipeline stage | Build, unit and contract tests, image and dependency scan, chart publish, promote the same artefact |
| Provisioning step | Consumer group and retry path for `rwb.source-data.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-source-data` in namespace `rwb-recovery` |
| Schedule registration | DailyCaseList at 07:15 Asia/Bangkok with overlap policy SKIP and the catch-up window; idempotent create or update |
| KEDA scaling | Worker scaled on the task-queue backlog with a minimum and a maximum from the values file |
| Dashboards | Six panels: run counts, run duration, rows written and below entry, publish status by date, activity retries, consumer lag |
| Alerts | Four rules: MSG-P1-001, PUBLISHED NO, failed run, refused read |
| Runbook | Five entries: late ACE batch, failed case query call, held date never released, Schedule not fired, migration failure |

**Probes.** Readiness answers healthy only when the migration is at the expected schema version, the consumer is running, the worker has polled and the last view read answered; liveness answers healthy when the process is up and its internal loop is responsive. Neither probe writes to the database. Exact paths and timings are values.

**Migration job.** Runs the per-service Flyway sequence for schema `rwb_source_data` with the `rwb_source_data` login as a pre-deploy job with a backoff limit; a failed job blocks the rollout and the release.

**Alert mapping carried over from the legacy story.**

| Message ID or check | Condition | Alert | Route |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-001 | The workflow waits for a complete ALS batch | Batch-gate alert with the product and the last completed date | Platform on-call, ticket |
| PUBLISHED NO | A date is reconciled but not released | Publish alert with the business date, the publish status and the run ID | Data steward, ticket |
| None (run failure) | A run fails on the case query contract or on the views | Failed-run alert with the run ID and the contract or view name | Platform on-call, page |
| MSG-P1-011 | A second start for a running or complete date | Counted on the dashboard and in the run log | No page |
| MSG-P4-002 | Read without Reporting R | Refused-read count on the dashboard | No page |

**Capacity.** The plan states, per environment, the rows of a peak date, the pages served to rwb-case and rwb-reporting, the worker minimum and maximum, the PgBouncer connection cap of the login and the run duration at maximum. The target is the legacy measure: the list built and released by 07:30 on 99 percent of days. No lake throughput and no file window appear in the plan, because both are removed (DP-17).

**Done when.** The chart renders in all three environments, the pipeline promotes one artefact, the probes answer, the queue and the consumer group are verified by a test, KEDA scales on backlog, `DailyCaseList` is registered and fires once per business date, the four alerts fire on synthetic metrics, the capacity plan is reviewed and the five runbook entries are accepted by the on-call rota.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-001 | The workflow waits for a complete ALS batch | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |
| MSG-P1-011 | A second start for a running or complete date | The {source} load for {date} is already complete or running. It was not run again. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Read without Reporting R | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story; the deployment adds the alert routing and the runbook link, never a new wording. The PUBLISHED NO and failed-run conditions have no message ID in the legacy story and keep none.

##### 15. Screens and states

The deployment serves the SCR-02 Case list screen of rwb-case (Loading; empty; list; filtered) and the reporting screens of rwb-reporting, both through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The operator-facing surfaces of this story are the pipeline run view, the release view, the dashboards and the runbook. This story registers the route target and the health check of the two case-list read operations only; the screen field list and the composite route specification belong to the edge and rwb-case stories.

The legacy Level "System" maps to "NFR" for the deployment checks, and "Access" to "Component".

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a values file: the entry threshold, the tolerance and the wait time are parameters read through the rwb-case contract, never deployment values (DP-06).
- No personal data in logs, dashboard series, alert payloads or the runbook: run counts, IDs, dates and durations only.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `recovery.v_ace_*` views: the release holds SELECT on the 30 views and no grant on `public` (DP-02, DP-05).
- No cross-schema read and no cross-schema key: the migration job writes `rwb_source_data` only and never touches another schema (DP-01).
- Every topic has a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic, and the consumer dedupes through the inbox (DP-09).
- The release pins the image digest and the chart version; a rebuild between environments is not allowed.
- No secret is written into a values file, a chart template, a dashboard or the runbook; all secrets come from the platform secret store.
- No lake credential, file adapter or data-set job is deployed, and the DP-17 guard fails a release that carries one.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: RWB-E1-002 is split and reworked as the wave-1 integration story RWB-ITG-E1002-ITG, which proves the case list end to end across rwb-case, rwb-source-data, rwb-integration, rwb-reporting and the gateway-bff composite route for SCR-02, with the removed data lake replaced by the delivery of the daily extract to rwb-reporting. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **squad member (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **the case list proved end to end on the real wave-1 services — the open cases and their owner and queue read from rwb-case through its published contract, the daily `case_list_row` rows built and replaced in one transaction in rwb-source-data by the JOB-04 reconciliation workflow started by `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1`, the daily extract delivered to rwb-reporting by the `deliverFile` activity of rwb-integration instead of the removed data lake, and SCR-02 served in one hop by the gateway-bff composite route**, so that **the one list every team works from is dated to the ACE batch it was built from and is proven against the services that will run it, not against a fake**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story RWB-E1-002 built one case list each business date from the open cases through the P3 in-process interface `CaseQueryApi`, joined it to the ACE account view and published it to Power BI through a file on the data lake (INT-19). In Arch v5 the single recovery schema and the in-process call are gone: rwb-case publishes a REST contract under `/api/recovery/case/v1`, rwb-source-data is the only service that reads the thirty `recovery.v_ace_*` views (DP-05), and the data lake and its Power BI connection are removed (DP-17; ADR-018). The list is still needed — it is the one list every team works from and the measure "case list built and released by 07:30 on 99 percent of days" still applies — so the behaviour has to be proved somewhere on the real services, and that is this story.

The chain the story proves is short and has one owner per step. rwb-source-data consumes `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` on `rwb.source-data.events.v1` and starts its reconciliation workflow on task queue `rwb-source-data` (DP-10, DP-14); the workflow reads the open case accounts through the rwb-case contract, one hop with a 2 s timeout (DP-11), and writes the `case_list_row` rows of the business date in schema `rwb_source_data` in one transaction, reading no table of schema `rwb_case` (DP-01, DP-02). When the date is released, rwb-source-data calls the rwb-integration activity `deliverFile` on queue `rwb-integration`; rwb-integration records the file run and publishes `rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1`, and rwb-reporting consumes the delivery into its own projection, so reporting is fed by events and delivered files and never by a lake (DP-17). SCR-02 is served by the gateway-bff composite route, one hop, on the rwb-case base (DP-19).

The parameters and reference data the run reads are the rwb-case contracts (DP-06, DP-07), the topic and event names come from the naming library (DP-14), the schema objects arrive through the P1 Flyway sequence (DP-15) and the account and arrears facts come from the ACE views read by rwb-source-data alone (DP-05). What no source states is the target read operation by which rwb-case serves the list that rwb-source-data builds, and how the daily extract reaches rwb-reporting once the data lake is removed: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0335; ASM-0429). The story proves the two operations that exist today and records the choice as an assumption, so a change of operation is one contract edit and one test change.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P3-E1018-APP is done: rwb-case creates the case, the case account link and the number, `recovery_case`, `case_account` and `case_party` exist in schema `rwb_case`, and `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases` and `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` answer from it.
- RWB-P3-E1020-APP is done: the morning allocation sets the owner and the queue on each case and publishes `rwb.case.CaseAllocated.v1`, so the list has an owner and a queue to show.
- RWB-P1-E1002-APP is done: the `case_list_row` table, its unique key on business date, case and account, the case list step of the reconciliation workflow, the extract writer and the call to `deliverFile` exist in rwb-source-data, and `rwb_source_data` is migrated by the P1 Flyway sequence.
- RWB-P2-E1007-APP is done: the rwb-integration `deliverFile` activity, the `interface_config`, `file_run` and `outbound_item` objects, the manifest and the `rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1` and `rwb.integration.FileFailed.v1` events exist on queue `rwb-integration`.
- RWB-P3-E1002-APP is done: the case list read operations of rwb-case, including `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/cases`, are published and answer with the owner, the queue, the stage, the status, the route and the refresh fields.
- rwb-reporting consumes `rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1` and `rwb.reporting.events.v1` is available, so the delivered extract lands in a projection in schema `rwb_reporting`.
- The gateway-bff composite route for SCR-02 is deployed in SIT (DP-19, RWB-PLT-N001-CON), with the 2 s per-call timeout and no call chain deeper than one hop.
- An SIT data set holds open cases and a masked ACE account view for a business date, with at least the 28,156 rows of the legacy fixture available to the run.
- The parameters `case.entry.dpd` = 90, `recon.caselist.tolerance.pct` = 0.00 and `caselist.allocation.wait.until` = 07:15 are in force through the rwb-case parameters contract, owned by RW-COE.
- Every service is the real SIT service behind its own login: no contract fake stands in for a service in this suite.
- No build dependency: the story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7) and waits only for the integration dependencies above.

##### 4. Flow

1. Test fixture: publishes `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` for source ALS and business date 2026-11-30 on `rwb.source-data.events.v1`, with the CloudEvents envelope and one event id.
2. rwb-source-data: the consumer deduplicates through its inbox `processed_event` and starts the reconciliation workflow for 2026-11-30 on task queue `rwb-source-data`, as an event-started workflow and not from a shared scheduler (DP-10).
3. rwb-source-data: the case list step of the workflow reads the open case accounts of the business date through `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases`, one hop on the rwb-case base with a 2 s timeout (DP-11), and reads the queue cut through `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/cases` for each queue it needs.
4. rwb-source-data: joins each `account_key` to the ACE account view for the account number, the total balance and the days past due of `data_as_of`, and reads the latest contact and action code per `account_key` from the EFS action view. Both views are read in rwb-source-data only (DP-05), never through another service.
5. rwb-source-data: replaces the `case_list_row` rows of 2026-11-30 in one transaction in schema `rwb_source_data`, each with `refreshed_at` and `publish_status` PENDING, and records the run checks ROWS_BELOW_ENTRY, ALLOCATION_COMPLETE and PUBLISHED.
6. rwb-source-data: the reconciliation step of RWB-P1-E1011-APP compares the count with the ACE view and sets `publish_status` HELD or RELEASED for the date.
7. rwb-source-data: the publish step calls the rwb-integration activity `deliverFile` on queue `rwb-integration` with the manifest of the 2026-11-30 extract — fileId, batchId, sha256 and record count — only when `publish_status` is RELEASED.
8. rwb-integration: records the file run and the outbound item in schema `rwb_integration`, delivers the file to the rwb-reporting target and publishes `rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1` on `rwb.integration.events.v1`, or `rwb.integration.FileFailed.v1` when the retries are exhausted.
9. rwb-reporting: consumes the delivery through its inbox and writes the delivered extract into its own projection in schema `rwb_reporting`; no data lake path and no lake copy is read or written anywhere in the chain.
10. gateway-bff: the SCR-02 composite route calls `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/cases` and `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases`, one hop each, and merges the answers into the screen model with the refresh line.
11. Assertions: the suite reads `case_list_row` through the rwb-source-data contract projection, the rwb-integration file run through its operations endpoint, the reporting projection through the rwb-reporting contract, and the SCR-02 route answer; it reads no table directly other than the SIT fixture checks of RWB-P1-E1002-APP.
12. Replay fixture: republishes the same AceDataReady event id and asserts one run and one set of rows for the business date.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A source the case list reads is not complete at the cut-off | The daily completeness gate holds the case list step; no `case_list_row` is written for the date; the last released extract stays in rwb-reporting and the data steward and team managers are alerted | MSG-P1-001 | AC5 |
| X2 | The allocation step has not completed by 07:15 | The list is built with the owner and the queue as they are and the run check ALLOCATION_COMPLETE is NO | None (shown on the run) | AC1 |
| X3 | The same AceDataReady event is delivered twice | The inbox drops the second delivery, no second run starts and the rows of the date are unchanged | MSG-P1-011 | AC15 |
| X4 | The rwb-case contract raises an error after 12,000 accounts are read | The transaction rolls back, no `case_list_row` is written for the date, the run status is FAILED and the platform administrator restarts the workflow from Temporal | None (alert to the platform administrator) | AC1 |
| X5 | `deliverFile` fails all its retries | rwb-integration publishes `rwb.integration.FileFailed.v1`, the run shows COMPLETED with check PUBLISHED NO and the transfer is in the exception queue with a task for the platform administrator | None (R-UNI-34) | AC13 |
| X6 | A case account has no ACE account row for the business date | The row is written with empty account number, total balance and days past due; REC-05 lists the key for the data steward and the ACE team; the case and the link are unchanged | None (REC-05) | AC10 |
| X7 | The gateway-bff route cannot reach rwb-case inside the budget | The route answers with the platform error envelope and the screen shows SCR-02 in its error state; no partial screen is composed | None (DP-11, DP-19) | AC14 |
| X8 | A role without the right lists the JOB-04 runs | 403 with the error envelope | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-002-11-ITG |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Proves the cross-service behaviour of the five real services of the chain; needs no other screen or route and no build work of its own |
| Negotiable | The business date, the queue and the case used by the fixture are data; the operations are fixed by the published contracts |
| Valuable | The list that every team works from is proved on the services that will run it, with no data lake and no fake in the chain |
| Estimable | One suite, five service fixtures, one event publisher, four assertions and one absence assertion |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the fixtures and the report |
| Testable | Every criterion is one assertion on a real-service answer, a row, an event or a route response |

```gherkin
Feature: Case list v1 with case ID, owner and queue, proved on the real wave-1 services

  Background:
    Given the business date is 2026-11-30
    Given rwb-source-data publishes rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1 for source ALS and business date 2026-11-30
    Given the parameters case.entry.dpd = 90 and recon.caselist.tolerance.pct = 0.00 are in force through the rwb-case parameters contract
    Given rwb-case, rwb-source-data, rwb-integration and rwb-reporting are the real SIT services behind their own logins and no contract fake stands in for a service

  Scenario: AC1 List built and reconciled (legacy RWB-E1-002 AC1)

    When the case list step of JOB-04 runs

    Then REC-01 of RWB-E1-011 compares 28,119 with 28,119 and is PASS
    Then the run record shows 37 rows below 90 days past due

  Scenario: AC3 Daily refresh (legacy RWB-E1-002 AC3)
    Given the ALS batch for 2026-11-30 completed at 05:40 and JOB-03 completed at 06:52
    When the case list step runs and completes at 07:12

  Scenario: AC4 Last contact from EFS through ACE (legacy RWB-E1-002 AC4)
    Given v_ace_efs_action holds an action "PTP" for an account of case "RW-2026-000123" with contact_at 2026-11-30 15:42
    When the case list step runs

  Scenario: AC5 ACE batch not complete (legacy RWB-E1-002 AC5)
    Given v_ace_batch_status shows no COMPLETED ALS row for 2026-11-30 at 08:00
    When the DP01 cut-off passes and JOB-04 is triggered
    Then the daily completeness gate holds the step and no case_list_row for 2026-11-30 is written
    Then the lake keeps the extract file for 2026-11-27

  Scenario: AC10 Case account without an ACE account row (legacy RWB-E1-002 AC10)
    Given case "RW-2026-000456" links account_key "ACC0000456", which has no v_ace_account row for 2026-11-30
    When the case list step runs
    Then the row for "ACC0000456" has an empty account number, total balance and days past due
    Then REC-05 of RWB-E1-011 lists "case_account.account_key ACC0000456" as an orphan for the data steward and the ACE team
    Then the case and its case_account link are unchanged

  Scenario: AC12 JOB-04 runs as an event-started workflow and reads the list through the rwb-case contract (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1 for business date 2026-11-30 is on rwb.source-data.events.v1
    When rwb-source-data consumes it and starts its reconciliation workflow on queue rwb-source-data
    Then the workflow reads the open case accounts of 2026-11-30 through GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases on the rwb-case base /api/recovery/case/v1, one hop with a 2 s timeout
    Then it reads the queue cut through GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/cases for queue MTG-BKK-CO
    Then it writes the case_list_row rows of 2026-11-30 into schema rwb_source_data in one transaction, each with publish_status PENDING
    Then no statement of the run reads a table of schema rwb_case, and the run reads no ACE view outside rwb-source-data

  Scenario: AC13 The daily extract is delivered to rwb-reporting and no data lake path exists (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the reconciliation step sets publish_status RELEASED for 2026-11-30
    When the publish step calls the rwb-integration activity deliverFile on queue rwb-integration with the manifest of the 2026-11-30 extract
    Then rwb-integration records the file run and the outbound item in schema rwb_integration and publishes rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1 with the fileId, the batchId, the sha256 and the record count
    Then rwb-reporting consumes the delivery and holds the extract in its own projection in schema rwb_reporting
    Then no data lake path, no lake copy and no Power BI data set connection exists in the chain
    When deliverFile fails all its retries
    Then rwb-integration publishes rwb.integration.FileFailed.v1 and the run shows COMPLETED with check PUBLISHED NO

  Scenario: AC14 gateway-bff serves SCR-02 in one hop from the rwb-case contract (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the browser calls the gateway-bff composite route of SCR-02 for queue MTG-BKK-CO
    When the route resolves the screen model
    Then it calls GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/cases and GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases on the rwb-case base, one hop each, with a 2 s timeout and no call chain deeper than one
    Then the answer carries case number, account number, product, stage, status, owner, queue, route, total balance and days past due with refresh time 2026-12-01 07:12 and data as of 2026-11-30
    Then the browser calls no rwb-source-data base and the case_list_row projection of schema rwb_source_data is not exposed as a browser route

  Scenario: AC15 The same AceDataReady event delivered twice produces one run and one set of rows (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1 for 2026-11-30 was consumed and its run completed
    When the same event id is delivered again
    Then the inbox row in processed_event deduplicates it and no second reconciliation workflow is started for 2026-11-30
    Then case_list_row still holds 28,156 rows for 2026-11-30 and no case account appears twice
    Then the refresh time stays the time of the first completed run
```

The five legacy criteria are carried unchanged, including their lake and Power BI wording, because they are the legacy proof; the removed data lake is replaced by the delivery of 12.3 and 12.4 to rwb-reporting, and AC12 to AC15 prove that replacement on the real services.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The case list holds one row per open case and linked account for the business date | REQ-RDF-007; DL17 (one case per customer per product, accounts linked) |
| BR2 | Account number, total balance and days past due come from `v_ace_account` by `account_key` for the ACE business date in `data_as_of`; the Workbench holds no copy | D-RCV-35 U4; ADR-010 |
| BR3 | The list is built only when the daily completeness gate of RWB-E1-015 reports the sources the case list reads COMPLETE for the business date | BR-P1-014-4; MSG-P1-001 |
| BR4 | The count of accounts at or above the entry threshold is compared with `v_ace_account` by REC-01 of RWB-E1-011; this step builds the list and records the rows below the threshold, it does not pass or fail a count | CTL-01; REC-01; parameter case.entry.dpd (DL16) |
| BR5 | The list carries the business date and the refresh time on every row | REQ-RDF-009 (freshness); FEAT-RDF-18 |
| BR6 | A repeated step for the same business date replaces that date's rows | R-UNI-40 |
| BR7 | A file that fails after the retry limit goes to the exception queue with a task for the owner | R-UNI-34; REQ-DRI-007 |
| BR8 | Case data is read only through the P3 published interface. ACE data is read only through `recovery.v_ace_*` views | ADR-002; DT08; ADR-010 |
| BR9 | Last contact and action code come from `v_ace_efs_action` by `account_key`, taking the row with the latest `contact_at` | RWB-E1-069; Data Tier Map |
| BR10 | A case account with no ACE row is written with empty amounts and listed by REC-05; it is never deleted and the case is never changed by this story | BR-P1-011-3 |
| BR11 | Every call in the chain is one hop between two services with a 2 s timeout and a published contract: the browser reaches gateway-bff, gateway-bff reaches rwb-case, rwb-source-data reaches rwb-case and rwb-integration by contract and activity. No service reads another service's tables and no call chain is deeper than one | DP-01; DP-11; ADR-020; Arch v5 slide 11 |
| BR12 | There is no data lake and no lake copy. Reporting is fed by events into rwb-reporting and by files delivered through `deliverFile`, and no step of the list writes to a lake path | DP-17; ADR-018; Arch v5 slide 37 |

##### 9. State transitions

None for a case status. The run states this story exercises are the reconciliation workflow of the case list step in rwb-source-data (RUNNING to COMPLETED or FAILED, with the run checks ROWS_BELOW_ENTRY, ALLOCATION_COMPLETE and PUBLISHED), the `deliverFile` activity of rwb-integration (STARTED to COMPLETED or FAILED, with the file run state it writes in schema `rwb_integration`), and the `case_list_row.publish_status` of the business date, written PENDING by this step and moved to HELD or RELEASED by the reconciliation step of RWB-P1-E1011-APP. No case status is changed by any step of the chain.

| rwb-source-data service identity (the rwb-source-data login, DP-02) | Consumes AceDataReady, runs the reconciliation workflow and the case list step, reads the ACE views, writes `case_list_row` and the run record in schema `rwb_source_data`, calls `deliverFile` |
| rwb-case service identity (the rwb-case login, DP-02) | Serves the case list read operations under `/api/recovery/case/v1` within the caller's scope |

| gateway-bff, platform edge | Owns the SCR-02 composite route, the 2 s timeout and the session check |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Lists the reconciliation runs and restarts a FAILED workflow from Temporal |

No approval level from the delegation of authority applies: the story takes no business decision.
