The case fields are read only through the rwb-case contract and are never copied into another schema as a foreign key; `case_list_row` is P1's dated projection for the business date and holds business keys only; the ACE views are read only by rwb-source-data (DP-01, DP-05). The reporting projection the delivered extract lands in is owned by rwb-reporting in schema `rwb_reporting`; its field list is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0335; ASM-0429), so this story asserts the delivery and the file metadata, not the projection's columns. Field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. This story builds and runs integration tests and publishes no operation; every operation in the chain is provided by its owner service.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Base | Use in the suite | Budget |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases` | P3 rwb-case | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | The open case accounts of the business date, read by the JOB-04 case list step; the case-number search used by AC1 | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/cases` | P3 rwb-case | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | The queue cut for queue MTG-BKK-CO, used by the queue part of the list and by SCR-02 (AC12, AC14) | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/freshness` | P1 rwb-source-data | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` | The business-date freshness and the ACE batch completeness the gate reads (AC5) | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |

The target read operation by which rwb-case serves the case list that rwb-source-data builds is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0335; ASM-0429); the suite asserts the two published reads above and changes with one contract edit if the agreed operation differs. The browser reaches none of these bases directly: it calls the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | When | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1` | `rwb.integration.events.v1` | P2 rwb-integration | The daily extract of the business date is delivered to rwb-reporting (AC13) | fileId, batchId, sha256, record count, target, deliveredAt |
| `rwb.integration.FileFailed.v1` | `rwb.integration.events.v1` | P2 rwb-integration | Every retry of the delivery fails (AC13) | fileId, batchId, failureCode, attempt count, failedAt |

The suite publishes no event of its own; it asserts these two on the wire and asserts that rwb-reporting consumes the delivery into its own projection. No personal data is carried, and the projection is fed by events and delivered files only, never by a lake (DP-17).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Consumer | Asserted behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` | `rwb.source-data.events.v1` | P1 rwb-source-data | rwb-source-data inbox and reconciliation workflow; rwb-case DailyCaseRun | Starts the case list step for 2026-11-30; a duplicate is dropped by `processed_event` (AC12, AC15) |
| `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1` | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 rwb-case | rwb-source-data and rwb-reporting | A new open case is on the list of the next business date |
| `rwb.case.CaseAllocated.v1` | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 rwb-case | rwb-source-data and rwb-reporting | The owner and the queue on the list are the allocated ones (AC1, AC12) |

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Owner | Use in the suite |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DailyCaseRun | Workflow | `rwb-case` | P3 rwb-case | Started by AceDataReady; creates and allocates the cases the list reads (AC1, AC12) |
| ReconciliationWorkflow (JOB-04) with the case list step | Workflow, event-started by AceDataReady | `rwb-source-data` | P1 rwb-source-data | Builds and replaces the `case_list_row` rows of the business date in one transaction (AC1, AC12, AC15) |
| deliverFile | Activity | `rwb-integration` | P2 rwb-integration | Delivers the daily extract to rwb-reporting and publishes FileDelivered or FileFailed (AC13) |

The workflow ID of the case list run is keyed by the business date, so a second delivery of the same date resolves to the same run and the same rows (BR6, AC15).

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Schedule or trigger | Cadence | Owner | Legacy reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| JOB-04 case list step | Event trigger: `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` for the business date, with the step chained after the allocation step and a wait until 07:15 at the latest | P1 rwb-source-data | JOB-04 Daily reconciliation |
| Reporting refresh | Daily 07:30, after the delivery of the business date | P9 rwb-reporting | The 07:30 data set refresh of the legacy story |

No shared scheduler table and no Quartz job is used: the trigger is the event and the refresh is a Temporal Schedule in its owning service (DP-10).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. This story owns no table and writes no schema of its own (DP-01). The tables in the chain are owned as follows and are read or written only by their owner: `case_list_row`, the run record and `processed_event` in schema `rwb_source_data` (P1); `recovery_case`, `case_account`, `queue` and `case_party` in schema `rwb_case` (P3); `interface_config`, `file_run` and `outbound_item` in schema `rwb_integration` (P2); the projection and `processed_event` in schema `rwb_reporting` (P9).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

None. The suite runs against the deployed SIT services and their published contracts; contract fakes are not used at this level, because the point of the story is that the real cross-service behaviour is proved (R5.4 class I).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | In this story |
|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 3 consumed: the two rwb-case reads and the rwb-source-data freshness read, every call one hop with a 2 s timeout, the browser only through gateway-bff |
| Kafka | 0 published by this story; 2 asserted from rwb-integration (FileDelivered, FileFailed); 3 consumed by the services (AceDataReady, CaseCreated, CaseAllocated) |
| Temporal | 2 workflows and 1 activity observed: DailyCaseRun on queue `rwb-case`, ReconciliationWorkflow on queue `rwb-source-data`, deliverFile on queue `rwb-integration` |
| File | 1 delivered file per business date, through `deliverFile` with a manifest of fileId, batchId, sha256 and record count; no lake transfer |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `integration/recovery/wave1/caselist` in the ACE repository, package `<ACE base package>.recovery.itg.wave1.caselist`. Not part of a deployed service.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Wave1Topology fixture | Configuration | Names the real SIT endpoints, logins and task queues of rwb-case, rwb-source-data, rwb-integration, rwb-reporting and gateway-bff; fails the suite when a fake endpoint is configured |
| AceDataReadyPublisher | Test fixture | Publishes `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` for the business date with a fixed event id, and republishes the same id for AC15 |
| CaseListAssertion | Test service | Reads `case_list_row` of the business date through the rwb-source-data contract and asserts the counts of AC1, the refresh of AC3, the contact of AC4 and the orphan of AC10 |
| RunAssertion | Test service | Asserts the run record, the checks ROWS_BELOW_ENTRY, ALLOCATION_COMPLETE and PUBLISHED, and the absence of a `rwb_case` table reference in the run (AC5, AC12) |
| DeliveryAssertion | Test service | Asserts the rwb-integration file run, `rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1`, the failure event and the absence of a lake path (AC13) |
| RouteAssertion | Test service | Calls the gateway-bff SCR-02 composite route, asserts one hop per call, the 2 s timeout and the merged screen model (AC14) |
| DedupeAssertion | Test service | Asserts one inbox row, one run and one set of rows after the replay (AC15) |
| SuiteReport | Service | Publishes the result with the build ID, the data set version and the service versions |

**Real-service topology.** rwb-case (P3, schema `rwb_case`, base `/api/recovery/case/v1`, queue `rwb-case`, `rwb.case.events.v1`); rwb-source-data (P1, schema `rwb_source_data`, base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`, queue `rwb-source-data`, `rwb.source-data.events.v1`); rwb-integration (P2, schema `rwb_integration`, base `/api/recovery/integration/v1`, queue `rwb-integration`, `rwb.integration.events.v1`); rwb-reporting (P9, schema `rwb_reporting`, base `/api/recovery/reporting/v1`, queue `rwb-reporting`, `rwb.reporting.events.v1`); gateway-bff for SCR-02. Every service is reached behind its own login (DP-02) and no service reads another service's schema (DP-01).

**Fixtures**

|---|---|
| Business date run | Business date 2026-11-30, ALS batch complete at 05:40, allocation complete at 06:52, case list step complete at 07:12, 28,140 accounts in the ACE view, 21 exclusions, 28,156 rows |
| Case rows | Case RW-2026-000123, account ACC0000123, product MORTGAGE, status ASSIGNED, queue MTG-BKK-CO, total balance 1,250,000.00, days past due 96 |
| Contact row | EFS action PTP for an account of case RW-2026-000123 with contact_at 2026-11-30 15:42 |
| Orphan row | Case RW-2026-000456 with account_key ACC0000456 and no ACE account row for 2026-11-30 |
| Late batch | No COMPLETED ALS row for 2026-11-30 at 08:00 |
| Delivery failure | The rwb-integration target forced to fail all its retries |

Every fixture value is the legacy value carried unchanged; no new business value is invented.

The DP dependencies resolve to the platform and service contract stories of the owning services and stay with their implementation stories; this story carries no H, C or X dependency and carries the I dependencies above (§R5.4 class I, allowed on an ITG story only).

**Run order**

1. Check the topology: every endpoint, login and task queue is the real SIT one and no fake endpoint is configured.
2. Publish AceDataReady for 2026-11-30 and wait for the reconciliation run to start on queue `rwb-source-data`; assert the run ID is keyed by the business date (AC12).
3. Wait for the case list step and assert the run record and the checks; assert no `rwb_case` statement in the run (AC1, AC5, AC12).
4. Assert the rows of 2026-11-30: 28,156 rows, the refresh time, the contact row and the orphan row (AC1, AC3, AC4, AC10).
5. Assert the reconciliation result and `publish_status` of the date, then trigger the publish step and assert the `deliverFile` call, the file run, `rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1` and the reporting projection (AC13).
6. Force the delivery failure and assert `rwb.integration.FileFailed.v1` and PUBLISHED NO (AC13).
7. Call the gateway-bff SCR-02 route and assert the merged answer, the one hop and the 2 s timeout (AC14).
8. Republish the same AceDataReady event id and assert one inbox row, one run and one set of rows (AC15).
9. Assert the absence: no data lake path, no lake copy and no Power BI data set connection is configured or called (AC13).
10. Publish the suite report with the build ID, the data set version and the service versions.

**Configuration.** The business date, the queue, the case, the counts and the service versions sit in the fixture files; the pass limits are the legacy values of the criteria. Nothing business-specific is coded in a test method.

**Done when.** Every test of section 16 passes in SIT against the real wave-1 services, the replay proves one run and one set of rows, the delivery reaches the rwb-reporting projection with no lake path anywhere in the run log, and the report is attached to the wave-1 integration record.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-001 | The ACE batch for the business date is not complete and the list is not built | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |
| MSG-P1-011 | A second delivery or trigger while a run for the date is running or complete | The {source} load for {date} is already complete or running. It was not run again. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right lists the JOB-04 runs | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The message texts are the legacy texts, carried unchanged. The suite's own report lines — the run ID, the row count, the file id and the route timing — are for the integration record and are not part of the message standard.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen is built in this story. The screen the suite exercises end to end is SCR-02 Case list in its four states — Loading, empty, list and filtered — served by the gateway-bff composite route on the rwb-case base, one hop per call with a 2 s timeout, and showing the ten columns of the list with the refresh line "Refreshed 1 Dec 2026 07:12, data as of 30 Nov 2026". The route composes the answer from the owner's contract only: the browser calls no rwb-source-data base and the `case_list_row` projection is not exposed to it. The route specification and the field-level masking of customer fields are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0335; ASM-0429); the screen build itself is RWB-P3-E1002-APP.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the entry threshold, the tolerance, the wait time, the counts and the queue are fixture data and parameters, never constants in a test method.
- No personal data in logs, reports, events, workflow payloads or prompts: the run reads `account_key` and `case_no` only, the extract carries no customer name, identity number or contact value, and the report holds counts, ids and timings.
- No read of another service's tables: the case is read through the rwb-case contract, the ACE views through rwb-source-data only, and the assertions use the owner's contract (DP-01, DP-05).
- One hop and one timeout: every call is a contract call with a 2 s timeout and no chain deeper than one; a deeper chain fails the route assertion (DP-11, DP-19).
- No data lake: the suite fails when a lake path, a lake copy or a lake client is configured in any service of the chain (DP-17).
- The suite never runs against UAT or production and writes only the rows of its own business date through the services; the SIT data set is restored after the run.
- Every service is real in this suite. A fake endpoint, a stub base or a mocked consumer fails the topology check before any load is generated.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-002 for rwb-source-data. This story publishes the contract baseline of the case list: the four REST operations and their answer shapes, the consumed event, the workflow, activity and Schedule contracts, the nine contract tables and the four rwb-case fakes. The case-list operations and their answer shapes, the workflow and schedule names and the 07:15 fallback are fixed here under GAP-0486, GAP-0487 and ASM-0678, ASM-0679, and the removal of the lake, the extract file and the Power BI data set is recorded under GAP-0485 and ASM-0677. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of rwb-source-data for the case list: an OpenAPI 3.1 document for `GET /admin/jobs`, `POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun`, `GET /case-list/dates/{businessDate}` and `GET /case-list/rows`, an AsyncAPI document for the consumed `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1`, the typed workflow and activity interfaces of `CaseListBuildWorkflow`, `listEligibleAccounts` and `snapshot(page)`, the `DailyCaseList` Schedule declaration, the error envelope, the Idempotency-Key rule, the versioning rule, the nine contract tables of section 12 and the four rwb-case fakes**, so that **the app, operations and test stories of this legacy key build against a fixed, testable contract on Day 1 without waiting for rwb-source-data, rwb-case, rwb-integration or the reporting team to be built**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST and one hop with a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020), and the Temporal contract jar is the same rule for workflow steps (Arch v5 slide 11). This legacy key spans four stories in three disciplines: the build, this contract, the deployment and the end-to-end integration. They can only run in parallel if the answer shapes are fixed once. Two of the shapes are fixed nowhere in the source material — the case-list date and rows operations do not appear in Arch v5 or in TSD P1, and neither do the workflow and Schedule names — so read as written the build story would invent them privately and every reader would invent a different answer. This story writes them down, fakes the four rwb-case contracts the build reads, and states the DP-17 removal in the contract itself so that no consuming team plans a lake file that will never exist (GAP-0485, GAP-0486, GAP-0487).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the document, topic and event names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- The platform error envelope, the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope and the idempotency library are the platform baseline; this document narrows them but never redefines them (DP-09, DP-11).
- The workflow kit and the namespace `rwb-recovery` are available for the typed activity and Schedule declarations (RWB-PLT-E1071-CON).
- The operations and the tables are taken from the Ownership Map only: `case_list_row` is P1's, the case list API and screen are P3's, and a document never declares another service's path.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 document for the four operations, with the shared components used across the rwb-source-data surface.
2. Agree and write the answer shapes of `/case-list/dates/{businessDate}` and `/case-list/rows`, including the column order, the filters and the HELD behaviour.
3. Draft the AsyncAPI document for the consumed `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` with the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope and the payload fields.
4. Write the typed workflow and activity interfaces and the `DailyCaseList` Schedule declaration into the contract jar.
5. Agree the error envelope and map each condition to MSG-P1-001, MSG-P1-011 or MSG-P4-002.
6. State the Idempotency-Key rule for the rerun POST and the versioning rule for REST and for the activity jar.
7. Publish the nine contract tables and the four rwb-case fakes.
8. Add the contract tests and tag the baseline for RWB-P1-E1002-APP, RWB-P1-E1002-OPS and RWB-ITG-E1002-ITG.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A request body or query fails schema validation | 400 with the error envelope and the failing pointer | None (contract code) | AC3 |
| X2 | The rerun POST omits the Idempotency-Key header | 400 with the error envelope naming the header | None (contract code) | AC4 |
| X3 | The same Idempotency-Key is replayed with a different body | 422 with the error envelope; the stored response is not overwritten | None (contract code) | AC4 |
| X4 | A reader asks a date that is PENDING or HELD | 200 with the status and no rows | None | AC1 |
| X5 | A fake drifts from the document | The contract test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC7 |
| X6 | A field-level definition is missing from the source material | The field is marked with the placeholder and the gap is carried | None | AC2 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the workflow kit and the Ownership Map only |
| Negotiable | Field-level detail of the row answer is settled with rwb-case and rwb-reporting; the named operations, the shapes and the rules are fixed here |
| Valuable | Unblocks the build, operations and integration stories of this legacy key on Day 1 |
| Estimable | Two documents, one contract jar, two rules, nine contract tables, four fakes and seven contract tests |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion tests an artefact, never a business outcome |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Case-list contract baseline for rwb-source-data

  Background:
    Given the service naming rule of the platform library is in force
    Given the base of rwb-source-data is /api/recovery/source-data/v1

  Scenario: AC1 The OpenAPI 3.1 document describes the four case-list operations (new, D-RCV-60)

    When it is validated against the OpenAPI 3.1 schema
    Then it validates with no error
    Then it declares GET /admin/jobs with the filters jobCode, status, from and to and the checks ROWS_BELOW_ENTRY, ALLOCATION_COMPLETE and PUBLISHED on every Job
    Then it declares POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun with the Idempotency-Key header and the 409 condition for a date that is not complete or a run that is open
    Then it declares GET /case-list/dates/{businessDate} answering the business date, the publish_status, the row count and refreshed_at
    Then it declares GET /case-list/rows with the filters businessDate, team, queue, product and page, and the row in the 19-column order DF-RPT-001 to DF-RPT-019

  Scenario: AC2 The event contract names one consumed event and none published (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the AsyncAPI document of rwb-source-data is published
    When it is validated against the AsyncAPI 3 schema
    Then it declares the topic rwb.source-data.events.v1 and the consumed rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1
    Then the payload carries eventId, occurredAt, schemaVersion, sourceSystem, businessDate, status and completedAt and no personal data field
    Then every message uses the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope with the attributes id, source, type, specversion, time, subject and datacontenttype
    Then the document declares no published rwb-source-data event for this capability

  Scenario: AC3 The error envelope is one shape and the message IDs are fixed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the error envelope component of the document
    When a 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 or 503 response is produced
    Then the body carries the code, the message, the messageId, the traceId and the field list
    Then the messageId is MSG-P1-001, MSG-P1-011, MSG-P4-002 or a contract code, with the legacy text where the message already existed
    Then the response carries the problem media type and the trace identifier

  Scenario: AC4 The rerun POST requires an Idempotency-Key (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rerun operation of the document
    When the request omits the Idempotency-Key header
    Then the service answers 400 with the error envelope
    When the same key is sent twice for the same business date
    Then the second call returns the stored response and starts no second run

  Scenario: AC5 The versioning rule covers REST and the activity jar (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the document declares major version 1 in the path
    When a caller uses an unsupported major version
    Then the service answers 404 with the error envelope and the served major versions
    Then the activity and workflow interfaces are versioned in the contract jar with a compatible change rule, and an incompatible change needs a new interface package
    Then the consumed event schema is versioned in the registry with BACKWARD compatibility

  Scenario: AC6 The workflow, activity and Schedule contracts are declared (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the contract jar and the Schedule declaration
    When they are reviewed against Arch v5 slides 12, 15 and 44
    Then CaseListBuildWorkflow is declared with workflow ID = business date, the run record shape and the search attributes BusinessDate and PublishStatus
    Then listEligibleAccounts is declared with the business date in and the case-account rows out, and snapshot(page) with the business date and page in and the released rows out
    Then DailyCaseList is declared at 07:15 Asia/Bangkok with overlap policy SKIP, the catch-up window and AceDataReady as the primary trigger
    Then no activity payload carries a case payload or a personal data field

  Scenario: AC7 The nine contract tables are complete and the fakes match them (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the contract section of this story
    When the nine sub-tables are reviewed
    Then each of 12.1 to 12.9 is present and names its owner from the Ownership Map
    Then the four rwb-case fakes answer the paths and payloads of 12.2
    Then the contract tests compare the fakes with the document and fail on any drift
    Then the document states that no file, no lake path and no data set is part of the contract
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One REST base per service: `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`; a document never declares another service's path | DP-13; Arch v5 slide 41 |
| BR2 | The service topic is `rwb.source-data.events.v1` with event names `rwb.source-data.<Event>.v1`, retry and `.dlt` topics | DP-14; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR3 | Every consumed event carries the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, is keyed by caseId where a case exists and carries no personal data | Arch v5 slides 42 and 43; DP-09 |
| BR4 | Every POST declares the Idempotency-Key header and stores its response | Arch v5 slide 11; DP-09 |
| BR5 | Error responses use one envelope and one message ID per condition; business message texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story | Arch v5 platform baseline; Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR6 | A schema change is additive within a major version; a breaking change is a new major version or a new interface package | Arch v5 slide 42; DP-11 |
| BR7 | The document lists only operations and tables owned by rwb-source-data; a consumed operation is described as consumed, never as provided | Ownership Map v1 |
| BR8 | The contract carries no file, lake or data-set artefact: the publish path is removed by DP-17 | DP-17; GAP-0485 |
| BR9 | No business value is fixed in the contract: the threshold, the tolerance and the wait time stay parameters read by contract | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Case list date | `businessDate`, `publishStatus` (PENDING, HELD, RELEASED), `rowCount`, `refreshedAt` |
| Case list row | The 19 fields DF-RPT-001 to DF-RPT-019 in order: `id`, `businessDate`, `caseId`, `caseNo`, `accountKey`, `accountNo`, `productGroup`, `stageCode`, `status`, `ownerReference`, `queueCode`, `teamCode`, `routeCode`, `totalBalance`, `daysPastDue`, `refreshedAt`, `lastContactAt`, `lastActionCode`, `publishStatus` |
| Job | `jobId`, `jobCode` (JOB-04), `businessDate`, `status`, `startedAt`, `finishedAt` and the checks ROWS_BELOW_ENTRY, ALLOCATION_COMPLETE, PUBLISHED |
| Consumed event | `eventId`, `occurredAt`, `schemaVersion`, `sourceSystem`, `businessDate`, `status`, `completedAt` |
| Activity payloads | Business date, page number and page size only; no case payload in workflow code or payloads |

The maximum page size, the sort key and the exact JSON types of the row answer are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0486; ASM-0678); this story fixes the field names and the column order and leaves the field-level detail to the baseline review.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-source-data (P1); base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`.

| ID | Method | Path | Documented shape | Access |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| API-P1-001 | GET | `/admin/jobs` | `Job[]` filtered by `jobCode`, `status`, `from`, `to` | Platform administration R |
| API-P1-002 | POST | `/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun` | `Job`; Idempotency-Key required; 409 for a date not complete or a run open | Platform administration U |
| — | GET | `/case-list/dates/{businessDate}` | CaseListDate; 404 for a date with no run | Reporting R |
| — | GET | `/case-list/rows` | CaseListRowPage in the 19-column order, filtered by `businessDate`, `team`, `queue`, `product`, `page` | Reporting R |

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases` | P3 rwb-case | Open case accounts for the business date; faked |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/cases` | P3 rwb-case | Allocation state, owner and queue; faked |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/parameters/{key}` | P3 rwb-case | `case.entry.dpd`, `recon.caselist.tolerance.pct`, `caselist.allocation.wait.until`; faked |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/reference-data/{lovCode}` | P3 rwb-case | LOV-PUBLISH-STATUS, LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-CASE-STATUS; faked |

No operation of rwb-integration is consumed. RWB-P2-E1007-CON is named in this baseline only because the legacy publish step used its outbound file adapter and that step is removed (DP-17, GAP-0485): the adapter is documented as removed, never as consumed.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. This capability publishes no event. `AceDataReady` and `AceDataLate` on `rwb.source-data.events.v1` are produced by RWB-P1-E1015-APP; the release of a case-list date is a state of the row, read through the date operation.

| snapshot(page) | Activity | `rwb-source-data` | Business date and page in; released rows out in the 19-column order; read only, idempotent |

The name and time are fixed here because no source gives them (GAP-0487; ASM-0679).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** `openapi/rwb-source-data-v1.yaml` (OpenAPI 3.1), `asyncapi/rwb-source-data-v1.yaml` (AsyncAPI 3), `contract/rwb-source-data-activities.jar` (typed workflow and activity interfaces plus the Schedule declaration), `contract/error-envelope.yaml`, the idempotency and versioning rules in the contract README, and the four WireMock mappings.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-02 | `recovery_svc` login | One login per service | none |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting | none; gap if the story needs lake data |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Build steps**

1. OpenAPI 3.1 skeleton with the base path, the security scheme, the error responses and the shared components; schema lint in the pipeline.
2. The four operations with the shapes of section 11 and the 19-column order; the date operation and the HELD behaviour (GAP-0486).
3. AsyncAPI 3 document with the consumed event, the CloudEvents envelope and the registry versioning rule.
4. Contract jar: the workflow and activity interfaces and the Schedule declaration at 07:15 Asia/Bangkok (GAP-0487).
5. Error envelope and the message-ID mapping, business texts copied unchanged.
6. Idempotency-Key rule and the versioning rule for REST and for the jar.
7. The four fakes and their fixtures; the drift test.
8. Baseline tag and the consumer sign-off note.

**Done when.** The OpenAPI, AsyncAPI and jar validate in the pipeline, the seven contract tests pass, the four fakes answer every consumed path, the document states the DP-17 removal, and the build, operations and integration stories have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-001 | The ACE batch for the business date is not complete, list not built | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |
| MSG-P1-011 | A second start while a run for the date is running or complete | The {source} load for {date} is already complete or running. It was not run again. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The IDs and the texts are the legacy ones, character for character; the baseline adds the routing into the error envelope, never a new wording.

##### 15. Screens and states

The contract serves the SCR-02 Case list of rwb-case (Loading; empty; list; filtered), reached through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), and the reporting screens of rwb-reporting. This baseline fixes the source-data side of the merge only: the date operation, the paged rows and the `snapshot(page)` activity. The composite route specification and the screen field list belong to the edge and rwb-case stories; the fact that a HELD date shows its status and no rows is part of this contract.

The 11 legacy TC IDs are kept in legacy order and character for character, with new Covers, because the contract baseline proves the same conditions as artefacts rather than as business outcomes: a row still named AC2 or AC6 of the legacy story where the legacy named it. The legacy Level "System" maps to "Contract" or "Component" for the same reason.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the threshold, the tolerance and the wait time stay parameters read by contract, never constants (DP-06).
- No personal data in an event schema, an example, a workflow payload or a fake: IDs, codes, dates, counts and amounts only.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `recovery.v_ace_*` views: the baseline names no ACE object and no `public` table, and the views are read by the `rwb_source_data` login alone (DP-05).
- No cross-schema read and no cross-schema key: the contract names `case_list_row` in `rwb_source_data` only, and `caseId` and `accountKey` are identifiers without a foreign key (DP-01).
- One REST base and one topic per service; a document that names another service's base or topic fails the review (DP-13, DP-14).
- Every example in the document and every fixture is synthetic; no production payload is copied into a schema or a fake.
- The error envelope, the CloudEvents envelope and the naming rule come from the platform library; this story narrows them but never redefines them.

| REQ-RDF-009 | Every screen and API that shows source data shows its business date and freshness status | `refreshedAt` and `businessDate` in the date and row answers | TC-E1-002-02 |

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-007 for rwb-integration. The legacy story had no published contract: one module held the adapter, the scheduler, the tables and the exception queue, its "published interfaces" were three Java interfaces in one package and its two endpoints sat under the monolith base. This story fixes the contract of the outbound-file capability of rwb-integration on `/api/recovery/integration/v1`, the AsyncAPI document of `rwb.integration.events.v1` with `FileDelivered` and `FileFailed`, the `deliverFile(manifest)` and `receiveFile` activity contract on queue `rwb-integration`, one error envelope, the Idempotency-Key rule, the versioning rule and the contract fakes, so that the app, infrastructure, operations and test stories of this key can start on Day 1. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the rwb-integration outbound-file capability fixed as a contract: the four admin operations of the exception queue on the service base, the two events `FileDelivered` and `FileFailed` on `rwb.integration.events.v1` with the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, the `deliverFile(manifest)` and `receiveFile` activities on queue `rwb-integration` with the manifest of a claim-check file, one error envelope, the Idempotency-Key rule on every POST, the versioning and compatibility rule, the nine contract tables and the fakes of every consumed service**, so that **every team of this key builds on Day 1 against one agreed, testable shape and no team waits for another service, or for the app story, to exist**.

The legacy story described a pattern in prose and three Java interfaces inside one package. That was enough while one module owned the adapter, the retry schedule, the tables and the screen. Across a service boundary it is not: the requesting service has to know what `deliverFile` accepts and returns, the operations team has to know what the exception queue reads, the app story has to know what a delivery row means, the test stories have to know what a fake may answer, and the reporting and debt-sale teams have to know that their files travel on the same contract. This document is that answer, and it is deliberately narrow: it declares the four admin operations, two events, two provided activities, one manifest, one envelope and nine fakes, and it declares nothing that belongs to another service.

The contract also fixes the seams the split creates, and says so where a source is silent. The manifest of `deliverFile` is the claim-check manifest of Architecture v5 slide 11 — fileId, batchId, sha256, record count — widened with the interface, the business date, the case IDs, the idempotency key, the claim-check link and the requesting service; its exact payload is Not specified in the source documents, so it is fixed here and carried as a gap row (GAP-0648; ASM-1078). Whether `deliverFile` returns when the item is PENDING or when the file is acknowledged is fixed the same way: it returns the item reference and the status, and the requesting service learns the outcome from `FileDelivered` or `FileFailed`. Both are the kind of seam that costs a week per team if it stays unwritten.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling rule (DP-11, ADR-020) and the event contract is the platform rule (DP-09, DP-14). Both only pay off if the seams are written once. Here the seams are small and load-bearing: four admin operations, two events, two activities, one manifest, five consumed services and nine fakes. The business values behind them are already fixed by the legacy story — the retry intervals, the attempt limit, the exception queue, the owner task, the resend — so what is left is shape, and shape is what unblocks parallel work.

If the shape is agreed and faked on Day 1, four teams move at once. The app story builds the builder, the sender, the retry policy, the inbox and the four operations against the fakes; the infrastructure story provisions the endpoints, the keys and the staging area to the manifest and the budgets of this document; the operations story provisions the topic, the queue, the windows and the alerts against the events and the states declared here; the test and integration stories read one event shape and one state list. Without it, each team invents its own manifest, the delivery states diverge between the sender and the screen, and the one property the business asked for — that a failed file is found on the day it fails and reaches a named owner — depends on which service was written first.

The contract also states what this service does not own and does not do. Only rwb-source-data reads the thirty `recovery.v_ace_*` views, so no element of this contract is an ACE read (DP-05; ASM-1071). `debt_sale_account` is rwb-debtsale's, so the INT-25 tape rows travel in the manifest and are never read here (DP-01; ASM-1072). There is no data lake, so no element names a lake target (DP-17; ASM-1073). There is no inbound adapter, so `receiveFile` is published for completeness and called by no wave-1 flow (BR9). And the two Airflow windows are not Schedules of this service (ASM-1074).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the REST base, the topic, the event names and the task queue follow the platform rule and not a local choice (DP-13, DP-14).
- The CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, the JSON Schema registry with BACKWARD compatibility, the platform error envelope and the message catalogue are the platform baseline (DP-09); this document narrows them where it must and says so.
- The outbox and inbox library contract is available (RWB-PLT-TE006-CON): `outbox_event`, `processed_event`, `outbox_delivery`, `idempotency_key`, the retry topics and the `.dlt` topic are its elements and are reused, not redefined.
- The Temporal workflow kit contract is available (RWB-PLT-E1071-CON): the typed activity and workflow interfaces, the task queue naming, the retry and heartbeat policy, the codec and the build ID rule (DP-10).
- The owners' contracts are as published: the rwb-source-data freshness, customer and account operations (RWB-P1-E1015-CON and the P1 stories), the rwb-comms notice read (RWB-P6-E1007-APP), the rwb-document store and read (RWB-P5-E1007-APP), the rwb-case case action (RWB-P3-E1007-APP) and the rwb-access authorise operation (RWB-P4-E1037-CON). This story consumes them and fakes them; it defines none of them.
- The reference-data contract of rwb-case carries the lists this contract names (RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-P3-E1043-CON; DP-07).
- The decision-record library contract is available (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON; DP-03).
- The gateway-bff composite route that serves SCR-09 is published (RWB-PLT-N001-CON; DP-19).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the provided operations: the four admin paths on `/api/recovery/integration/v1`, their query parameters, their response types, their rights and their idempotency.
2. Draft the error envelope: one RFC 9457 problem-details body, the status codes of the four operations, and the message identifier each code carries.
3. Draft the AsyncAPI document of `rwb.integration.events.v1`: `FileDelivered` and `FileFailed`, their CloudEvents attributes, their key, their payload elements and the rule that neither carries personal data or file content.
4. Draft the activity contract: `deliverFile(manifest)` and `receiveFile` on queue `rwb-integration`, the manifest element list, the return element, the typed failures and the retry classification.
5. Draft the consumed contracts as this service sees them: the five owner operations, their placeholders where no source names a path or a field, and the degradation rule for a 4xx and a 5xx.
6. State the tables and their ownership, including that the outbox, inbox and idempotency objects are library objects created in `rwb_integration` and that no ACE view and no other service's table is named.
7. State the versioning and compatibility rule: `/v1` in the path, additive change only within a version, a breaking change in a new version, BACKWARD compatibility in the registry.
8. Publish the nine fakes and the drift test that compares each fake with this document.
9. Tag the baseline and hand it to the app, infrastructure, operations and test stories of this key.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A provided operation is called without a session or without a Recovery role | The envelope answers 401 before any read | MSG-P4-001 | AC1 |
| X2 | A provided operation is called by a role without the Platform administration right | The envelope answers 403 and nothing changes | MSG-P4-002 | AC1 |
| X3 | A resend names an unknown item or delivery | The envelope answers 404 | MSG-P4-003 | AC1 |
| X4 | A resend names an item or delivery that is not in EXCEPTION, or whose version changed | The envelope answers 409 and nothing changes | MSG-GEN-004 | AC1 |
| X5 | A message on `rwb.integration.events.v1` misses a CloudEvents attribute or carries a type other than the two | The contract test fails the producer, and at run time the consumer routes the message to `.dlt` with an alert | None | AC2 |
| X6 | An event payload would carry a name, an address, an identity number or file content | The schema refuses the field and the contract test fails the build | None | AC2 |
| X7 | A fake drifts from this document, or the app calls a path this document does not declare | The contract test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC5 |
| X8 | A consumed contract removes, renames or retypes an element this document declares | The contract returns to review with the owner of that operation and the stories of this key are re-baselined | None | AC4 |
| X9 | A field-level detail of a consumed operation is missing from the source material | The element carries the placeholder of §R9, one gap row and one assumption row, and the fake is written to the assumed shape | None | AC4, AC5 |
| X10 | A code path or a migration of this service reaches another schema, an ACE view or a foreign key | The architecture boundary test fails the build | None | AC6 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; uses the platform envelopes, the library contracts and the owners' published operations, and declares none of theirs as its own |
| Negotiable | Field-level detail of the consumed operations is settled with their owners; the manifest, the two events, the four operations and the state list are fixed by this realignment |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app, infrastructure, operations and test stories of this key on Day 1 and gives rwb-comms, rwb-payment, rwb-debtsale and rwb-reporting one file contract to call |
| Estimable | Four provided operations, two events, two activities, five consumed services, nine tables and nine fakes |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact — the OpenAPI document, the AsyncAPI document, the activity contract, the fake, this file — and never against a business outcome |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Contract baseline of the outbound-file capability for rwb-integration

  Background:
    Given the service naming rule and the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope of the platform library are in force
    Given the outbox, inbox and idempotency library contract of RWB-PLT-TE006-CON is in force
    Given the service base is /api/recovery/integration/v1, the topic is rwb.integration.events.v1 and the task queue is rwb-integration

  Scenario: AC1 The four admin operations and the one error envelope are published (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the OpenAPI 3.1 document of this contract
    When the four operations are reviewed
    Then the operations are GET /admin/outbound-items, POST /admin/outbound-items/{itemId}/resend, GET /admin/outbox/deliveries and POST /admin/outbox/deliveries/{deliveryId}/resend on the base
    Then each operation names its right as Platform administration R or U and states that the scope is applied
    Then both POST operations require the Idempotency-Key header and answer 409 on an item or delivery not in EXCEPTION
    Then every error is one RFC 9457 problem-details body carrying the status, the code, the message identifier and the trace id
    Then the document declares no fifth path, no other base and no path of another service

  Scenario: AC2 The topic carries FileDelivered and FileFailed and nothing else (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the AsyncAPI document of rwb.integration.events.v1
    When the two event types are validated
    Then the types are rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1 and rwb.integration.FileFailed.v1
    Then each message carries the CloudEvents 1.0 attributes id, source, type, specversion, time, subject and datacontenttype in binary mode
    Then each message is keyed by the case ID and its payload carries fileId, interfaceId, businessDate and the facts of the event only
    Then no payload element can carry a name, an address, an identity number or file content
    Then an eighth type and a message without the envelope are refused by the contract test and routed to .dlt at run time

  Scenario: AC3 The deliverFile and receiveFile activity contract carries the claim-check manifest (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the activity contract of this document
    When deliverFile and receiveFile are reviewed
    Then both are activities on the task queue rwb-integration and on no other queue
    Then the deliverFile input carries fileId, batchId, sha256, recordCount, interfaceId, businessDate, caseIds, idempotencyKey, the claim-check link and the requesting service
    Then the deliverFile output carries the item reference and the item status, and the outcome arrives as FileDelivered or FileFailed
    Then receiveFile is published for completeness and no wave-1 flow calls it
    Then a typed failure distinguishes a non-retryable refusal from a retryable failure, and no activity input carries file content
    Then the exact manifest payload is the assumed shape of GAP-0648 and is re-confirmed at the contract review

  Scenario: AC4 The nine contract tables are complete and attributed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the contract section of this story
    When the nine sub-tables are reviewed
    Then each of 12.1 to 12.9 is present and names its owner from the Ownership Map
    Then 12.7 names interface_config, outbound_item and job_catalog as P2 tables and the four library objects created in rwb_integration
    Then no ACE view, no recovery schema table and no other service's table is named as an object of this service
    Then 12.2 names the five consumed services and no operation of theirs appears as provided
    Then 12.6 registers no Temporal Schedule for the two file windows

  Scenario: AC5 The nine fakes answer every declared path and drift fails the build (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the nine fakes of 12.8
    When each fake is compared with the element it serves
    Then every consumed path and payload is answered with the shape of this document
    Then every error answer named in this document, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 503, is reachable in a fake
    Then the withheld file, the failed transfer and the duplicate event are reproducible from the fakes alone
    Then a drift between a fake and this document fails the contract test and blocks the merge

  Scenario: AC6 Versioning, compatibility and the boundary are fixed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published contract and the code and migrations of this key
    When the compatibility and boundary checks run
    Then the version is in the path as /v1 and a breaking change requires a new version
    Then an additive change within the version keeps the schema subject BACKWARD compatible
    Then the boundary test finds no statement on an ACE view, no cross-schema read, no foreign key out of rwb_integration and no SFTP call outside the transport component
    Then no element of this contract names a data lake, a lake file or a lake delivery
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One REST base and one topic per service: this contract declares `/api/recovery/integration/v1` and `rwb.integration.events.v1` and never declares another service's path or topic as its own | DP-13; DP-14; Arch v5 slide 41 |
| BR2 | The two events are `rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1` and `rwb.integration.FileFailed.v1` on `rwb.integration.events.v1`, keyed by case ID and carried with the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope; no other type is published | Arch v5 slides 16, 41 and 43; DP-09 |
| BR3 | The four admin operations are the exception queue surface of this service, on the paths of the TSD P2 v3 appendix and the Ownership Map; the naming of Architecture v5 slide 16 (`/interface-runs`) is superseded | TSD P2 v3 T-A.1 API-P2-001 to API-P2-004; Ownership Map; GAP-0648; ASM-1076 |
| BR4 | Every POST carries the Idempotency-Key header and stores its response for 24 hours; a repeat returns the stored response and changes nothing | Arch v5 slide 11; TSD P2 v3 T3.1 `idempotency_key` |
| BR5 | Every error is one RFC 9457 problem-details body; a resend of an item or delivery not in EXCEPTION, or a changed version, is 409 | Arch v5 slide 11; TSD P2 v3 T-A.2 |
| BR6 | `deliverFile(manifest)` and `receiveFile` are activities on queue `rwb-integration` in namespace `rwb-recovery`; the manifest is a claim-check manifest with fileId, batchId, sha256 and the record count, widened with the interface, the business date, the case IDs, the idempotency key, the claim-check link and the requesting service | Arch v5 slides 11 and 16; DP-10; GAP-0648; ASM-1078 |
| BR7 | Only rwb-source-data reads the `recovery.v_ace_*` views; no element of this contract is an ACE read and `rwb_integration` holds no grant on the recovery schema | Arch v5 slides 8, 9 and 29; ADR-010; DP-05; ASM-1071 |
| BR8 | `debt_sale_account` is rwb-debtsale's and is never read by this service: the INT-25 tape rows travel in the `deliverFile` manifest | Ownership Map; DP-01; FSD P2 v3 A1.5; ASM-1072 |
| BR9 | There is no inbound adapter: `receiveFile` is published for completeness, no wave-1 flow calls it, and `interface_config` holds outbound rows only | D-RCV-35 U1; ADR-010; FSD P2 v3 A1.6 |
| BR10 | There is no data lake: no element names a lake target, and the reporting extract of INT-19 is a `deliverFile` request to rwb-reporting while the decision and outcome feed of INT-20 is continuous Kafka ingest in rwb-decision | DP-17; Arch v5 slides 37 and 44; ASM-1073 |
| BR11 | The retry counts, intervals, owner role, alert role and lists are `interface_config` rows and reference-data rows with the version in force; no element of the contract fixes a value | DP-07; DP-09; TSD P2 v3 T3.1 and T3.2 |
| BR12 | No personal data in an event, a command, an activity input or a fake: identifiers, codes, counts and hashes only, and the claim-check link instead of the file | Arch v5 slide 11; CTL-11; DP-09 |
| BR13 | The version is in the path, an additive change is allowed within it and a breaking change needs a new version; the registry subject is BACKWARD compatible, and the subject name and the compatibility level are platform values | Arch v5 slide 11; DP-13; DP-14; ASM-1080 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The four operations, the two events, the two activities, the nine sub-tables and the nine fakes are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | The app, infrastructure, operations and test stories accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A field, an error code or a fake is added without removing one | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change to a provided operation or an event | A path, an element or a type is removed, renamed or retyped | New version |
| Baselined | Breaking change to a consumed operation | An owner removes, renames or retypes an element this contract declares | In review, with that owner |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |

The runtime states the contract fixes for the item are PENDING, SENT, RETRY, EXCEPTION and ACKNOWLEDGED, and for the delivery PENDING, RETRYING, DELIVERED and EXCEPTION; they are declared in 12.1 and 12.7 and are not states of this document (TSD P2 v3 T3.2 and T4).

| Who | What they may do in this story |

| Tech lead of rwb-integration | Owns this document and the nine fakes; tags the baseline |
| Solution architect | Approves a breaking change to a provided operation, to an event or to the manifest |
| The rwb-source-data owner | Owns the freshness, customer and account operations and signs off the shapes this contract consumes |

The deployment identity that calls the owners' contracts is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0648; ASM-1070); the document names it "the rwb-integration login (DP-02)" and leaves the name to the operations story.

##### 11. Data

The contract declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Outbound item | id, interfaceId, idempotencyKey, payloadRef, caseIds, attemptCount, nextAttemptAt, status, lastError, ownerRole (`outbound_item`) |
| Interface row | interfaceId, direction, transport, inboundPath (outbound folder), filePattern, dataProduct, maxAttempts, retryIntervalsMin, ownerRole, alertRole, validFrom, validTo (`interface_config`) |
| Delivery record | eventId, consumer, status, attemptCount, nextAttemptAt, lastErrorCode, deliveredAt, taskId (`outbox_delivery`) |
| Outbox event | eventType, schemaVersion, caseId, caseSeq, idempotencyKey, payload, actorRef, occurredAt (`outbox_event`) |
| Inbox record | consumer, idempotencyKey, eventId, hitCount, lastSeenAt (`processed_event`) |
| Idempotency record | idempotencyKey, endpoint, requestHash, response (`idempotency_key`) |
| File manifest | fileId, batchId, sha256, recordCount, interfaceId, businessDate, caseIds, idempotencyKey, claim-check link, requesting service |
| Item status list | PENDING, SENT, RETRY, EXCEPTION, ACKNOWLEDGED (LOV-OUTBOUND-STATUS) |
| Delivery status list | PENDING, RETRYING, DELIVERED, EXCEPTION (LOV-OUTBOX-DELIVERY) |
| Decision-record element | decision code, the action (deliver, exception, resend), the item or delivery reference and the freshness, written by the library on `rwb.decision-record.v1` |

The physical names, lengths and required flags are those of the TSD P2 Integration v3 T3.1 and the BR field IDs DF-OPS-136 to DF-OPS-148 and DF-OPS-168 to DF-OPS-206. The JSON field names of the four responses and the shape of the problem body are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0648; ASM-1082) and are fixed here; the query parameters of the two list operations are those of TSD P2 v3 T-A.2.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/integration/v1`; owner rwb-integration (P2). Four operations.

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/admin/outbound-items` | Lists outbound items by status, interface, from and to; response `OutboundItem[]` of id, interfaceId, status, attemptCount, lastError, caseCount, ownerRole, updatedAt | Platform administration R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| POST | `/admin/outbound-items/{itemId}/resend` | Sends an item in EXCEPTION again: status PENDING, attempt count 0, written to the ACE audit log with the user and the time; response `OutboundItem` | Platform administration U, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header; 409 when not in EXCEPTION or the version changed |
| GET | `/admin/outbox/deliveries` | Lists outbox deliveries by status, consumer, eventType, from, to, page and size; response `OutboxDeliveryPage` | Platform administration R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| POST | `/admin/outbox/deliveries/{deliveryId}/resend` | Sends a delivery in EXCEPTION again: status PENDING, attempt count 0; response `OutboxDelivery` | Platform administration U, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header; 409 when not in EXCEPTION |

Errors, one RFC 9457 body for all four: 401 no session or no Recovery role (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Platform administration right (MSG-P4-002); 404 unknown item or delivery (MSG-P4-003); 409 not in EXCEPTION or a changed version (MSG-GEN-004); 422 a malformed query; 503 the store or a consumed contract is unavailable (MSG-GEN-006). The four paths are API-P2-001 to API-P2-004 of TSD P2 Integration v3 T-A.1 and the Ownership Map rows owned by P2, re-based on the service base by DP-13. Architecture v5 slide 16 names `GET /interface-runs` and `POST /interface-runs/{id}/retry` instead; that naming is superseded and recorded (GAP-0648; ASM-1076). A later slice narrows the consumer filter of the delivery read and does not re-declare these paths.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/freshness` | P1 rwb-source-data | Whether the ACE batch of the business date is complete; faked with COMPLETE, FAILED at 05:20 and one slow answer |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/customers/{id}` | P1 rwb-source-data | The addressee facts by person key and contact key; faked with one hit, one miss and masking applied by the owner |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/accounts/{id}` | P1 rwb-source-data | The account facts of the INT-25 tape; faked with the 120 synthetic keys of the request |
| GET | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0648; ASM-1081) | P6 rwb-comms | The notice facts behind INT-14: notice ID, sent date, person key and document ID; faked with 85 notices and one 404 |
| POST | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents` | P5 rwb-document | Stores the built file and returns the upload link and the document ID |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{id}` | P5 rwb-document | Follows the claim-check link of a stored file; faked with one hit and one 404 |
| POST | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/actions` | P3 rwb-case | The route-state change and the one owner task; faked with the two route states and the task |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | The Platform administration R and U check, cached per session |
| POST (ACE Common path) | INT-22 audit and PII logging | ACE Common | The resend record and the personal-data access events |

Every operation is one hop with a 2 s client budget and a breaker per downstream, one GET retry with jitter and no retry on a 4xx (DP-11, ADR-020). The notice read is named by its legacy purpose only — `notice.sent_date` and `notice.person_key` (DF-LEG-019, DF-LEG-030) and `document.storage_ref` (DF-DOC-006) — because Architecture v5 slide 14 gives no notice-fact read to P6 and the legacy story built the file from the notice table in process; its path, query and field names are fixed in the rwb-comms contract (GAP-0648; ASM-1081). `debt_sale_account` appears in no consumed operation: the INT-25 rows travel in the manifest (BR8).

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event type | Topic | Key | Payload elements |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1` | `rwb.integration.events.v1` | caseId | fileId, interfaceId, businessDate, documentId, sha256, recordCount, requesting service |
| `rwb.integration.FileFailed.v1` | `rwb.integration.events.v1` | caseId | fileId, interfaceId, businessDate, attemptCount, lastError code, caseIds, ownerRole |

Both are written to `outbox_event` in the same transaction as the item state change and relayed with the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope in binary mode, retry topics 1 minute, 10 minutes and 1 hour, then `.dlt` with an alert (DP-09; Arch v5 slides 9 and 11). The schema version is carried in `outbox_event.schema_version`; the registry subject is BACKWARD compatible. The shared event `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` is published by the local decision-record library when an item moves to EXCEPTION or is resent; its schema belongs to RWB-P7-E1027-CON and is not restated here (DP-03).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event type | Topic | Owner | Consumer contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` | `rwb.source-data.events.v1` | P1 | CloudEvents 1.0, key the source and the business date; releases a held request after a failed batch; inbox dedupe on the key; no outbox delivery of its own |

This service is called as a task and not as an event listener for its work (Arch v5 slide 16, "events (none: called as a task)"), so `AceDataReady` is the only subscription. `AceDataLate` is P1's alert to the platform and to the gateway banner and is not consumed here. The requesting flows — a notice, a posting file, a buyer tape, a reporting extract — arrive through `deliverFile` and never as an event of this service.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `deliverFile(manifest)` | Activity, provided by P2, called by the requesting services | `rwb-integration` | Input: the manifest of BR6. Output: the item reference and the item status. Typed failures: `FreshnessHold`, `ManifestRefused`, `TargetUnavailable` |
| `receiveFile` | Activity, provided by P2 | `rwb-integration` | The published inbound counterpart; input and output are declared for completeness and no wave-1 flow calls it (BR9) |
| `OutboundFileWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per interface and business date, workflow ID `<interfaceId>:<businessDate>` | `rwb-integration` | Input: the manifest and the item reference. Output: the last item status |
| `buildOutboundFile` | Activity | `rwb-integration` | Input: the manifest and the item. Output: the file reference, the record count and the sha256 |
| `storeOutboundFile` | Activity | `rwb-integration` | Input: the file reference and the manifest. Output: the document ID and the claim-check link |
| `sendFileOverMft` | Activity | `rwb-integration` | Input: the document ID, the interface and the endpoint reference. Output: the attempt result; idempotent on the fileId |
| `parkItemInException` | Activity | `rwb-integration` | Input: the item, the failure class and the attempt count. Output: status EXCEPTION, `FileFailed` in the outbox and the owner task reference |

The retry policy is the workflow kit's: initial interval 1 s, back-off 2, maximum 3 attempts per activity, with a 4xx of a consumed contract classified as non-retryable and a 5xx or a timeout as retryable (DP-10). The file-level retry ladder is not the activity retry: it is the `max_attempts` and `retry_intervals_min` of the interface row, applied by `OutboundFileWorkflow` as timers (BR11). That `deliverFile` returns at PENDING and lets the workflow carry the ladder is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0648; ASM-1078).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. This contract registers no Temporal Schedule. The WIN window at 16:00 and the debt-buyer window per lot are opened by the bank's Airflow, which calls the requesting services and never a `rwb_*` schema (Arch v5 slides 16, 32 and 44; ASM-1074). The outbox relay runs every minute as a platform interval of the library and is not a Schedule of this contract (DP-09). The retry ladder is a workflow timer, not a Schedule (BR11). The exact trigger contract of the two windows is Not specified in the source documents and belongs to RWB-P2-E1007-OPS.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| `interface_config` | P2 (rwb_integration) | The outbound interface rows, by version, with direction OUTBOUND only |
| `outbound_item` | P2 (rwb_integration) | One outbound file, its status, attempt count, next attempt, last error, case IDs and manifest reference |
| `job_catalog` | P2 (rwb_integration) | The job catalog read; this contract writes no row in it and the loading of the JOB-10 and JOB-11 rows is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0648; ASM-1079) |
| `outbox_event` | PLT library, created in `rwb_integration` | The event written in the same transaction as the state change |
| `outbox_delivery` | PLT library, created in `rwb_integration` | One delivery per event and consumer, its attempts and its task |
| `processed_event` | PLT library, created in `rwb_integration` | The inbox: consumer, key, CloudEvents id, hit count |
| `idempotency_key` | PLT library, created in `rwb_integration` | The stored response of the two POST operations, kept 24 hours |
| `decision_record` | PLT library, created in `rwb_integration` | The local decision record of an exception and of a resend (DP-03) |

No other table is named. `notice` is rwb-comms's, `document` is rwb-document's, `debt_sale_account` is rwb-debtsale's, `recovery_case` and `task` are rwb-case's and `role` is rwb-access's; none appears here as an object of this service (DP-01). The thirty `recovery.v_ace_*` views are rwb-source-data's read surface and this schema holds no grant on `recovery` (BR7). `interface_run` and `interface_signoff` do not exist in the target (FSD P2 v3 A1.6; TSD P2 v3 T3.1).

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |

| rwb-source-data WireMock | Freshness COMPLETE and FAILED at 05:20 for 2026-11-10, one slow answer; addressee and address for the 85 synthetic notices; account facts for the 120 synthetic keys | App story, contract tests |
| rwb-comms WireMock | The 85 approved notices of 2026-11-10 with person key, sent date and document ID; one 404 | App story, AC5 |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 4 provided, 9 consumed | The four admin operations provided; the P1 freshness, customer and account reads, the P6 notice read, the P5 store and read, the P3 case action, the P4 authorise and the ACE Common audit path consumed; one hop, 2 s timeout |
| Kafka | 2 published, 1 consumed | `FileDelivered` and `FileFailed` on `rwb.integration.events.v1`; `AceDataReady` consumed with inbox dedupe; `DecisionRecorded` published by the library |
| Temporal | 1 workflow, 6 activities | `OutboundFileWorkflow` with four step activities and the provided `deliverFile` and `receiveFile` on queue `rwb-integration` |
| File | 2 party interfaces, 1 reporting delivery | INT-14 WIN and INT-25 buyer tape over MFT/SFTP with PGP; INT-19 delivered to rwb-reporting through `deliverFile`; no data lake and no lake element anywhere in the contract |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** `contract/outbound-admin.yaml` (OpenAPI 3.1 of the four admin operations, the problem envelope and the idempotency rule), `contract/integration-events.yaml` (AsyncAPI 3 of `rwb.integration.events.v1` with the CloudEvents envelope, the two types and their payloads), `contract/outbound-activities.yaml` (the `deliverFile` and `receiveFile` activity contract, the manifest, the return and the typed failures), `contract/outbound-consumed.yaml` (the five owner operations as consumed, with the notice-read placeholder), `contract/outbound-tables.md` (the ownership statement of 12.7), and the nine WireMock mapping sets.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_integration`; no other schema is read | none |
| DP-02 | `recovery_svc` login | One login per service, named by the operations story | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | ACE facts through the rwb-source-data contract; no view is read here | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case; the lists stay rows | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library, CloudEvents, the service topic, retry and `.dlt` | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Typed activity and workflow contract on the service queue; timers instead of a scheduler | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with a fake; one hop; 2 s timeout | none |
| DP-16 | `recovery.integration.adapter` | The rwb-integration contract: activities, events, admin operations, manifest | C RWB-P2-E1007-CON |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed; no lake element in any document | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route for SCR-09 | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Build steps**

1. Write the OpenAPI document: the four operations, their query parameters, their response types, their rights, the Idempotency-Key rule, the 409 and the one problem body.
2. Write the AsyncAPI document: the two types, the envelope, the key, the payloads, the retry topics, the `.dlt` rule and the schema subject.
3. Write the activity contract: the two activities, the manifest of BR6, the return element, the typed failures and the retry classification.
4. Write the consumed contracts: the five owner operations, the notice-read placeholder and the 4xx and 5xx degradation rule.
5. Write the table ownership statement and the explicit absence of any ACE view, recovery table, lake element and inbound adapter.
6. Write the versioning and compatibility rule and the drift test between each fake and this document.
7. Build the nine fakes and their fixtures with synthetic keys only.
8. Add the six contract tests of section 16.
9. Tag the baseline and collect the sign-off of the app, infrastructure, operations and test stories.

**Done when.** The five contract files validate in the pipeline, the six contract tests pass, the nine fakes answer every consumed path and every declared error, and the stories of this key have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-001 | An outbound file is held because the ACE batch is not complete | {product} is from {date}. Today's data is not yet complete. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | A resend on an item or delivery not in EXCEPTION, or on a changed version | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-GEN-005 | A resend is accepted | Saved. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A consumed contract is unavailable, so the attempt is retried | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P2-001 | An outbound item moves to the exception queue | The {interface} file {file} was not sent after {count} attempts. It is in the exception queue. |
| MSG-P4-001 | A call without a session | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the Platform administration right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | A resend or a list names an unknown item or delivery | This record was not found. |

The texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story, except MSG-P1-001, which uses the FSD P2 Integration v3 wording because the FSD outranks the story master under R-PREC (ASM-1075). The contract adds no message of its own; a message identifier is carried on every error of the envelope, and a code without an identifier in the source set keeps the §R9 placeholder until the Error and Message Standard names it.

##### 15. Screens and states

None in this story. The four provided operations serve SCR-09 Exception queue, whose fields, states and masking belong to RWB-P2-E1007-APP and whose route is RWB-PLT-N001-CON. The contract fixes only the states a screen may show — PENDING, SENT, RETRY, EXCEPTION and ACKNOWLEDGED for an item, PENDING, RETRYING, DELIVERED and EXCEPTION for a delivery — and the resend action with its 409. The held-file and failed-file alerts are alert rules over the held-item series and over `FileFailed`, owned by RWB-P2-E1007-OPS; the legacy alert names `rwb.integration.outbound.held` and `rwb.integration.outbound.failed` are not event names of the target (GAP-0648; ASM-1077).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the attempts, the intervals, the owner role, the alert role and the lists are `interface_config` rows and reference-data rows with the version in force.
- No personal data in an event, a command, an activity input or a fake: identifiers, codes, counts and hashes only, and the claim-check link instead of the file.
- The contract names only rwb-integration's own operations, events and activities as provided; the five consumed services are consumed and are never restated as this service's.
- One REST base, one topic and one task queue per service; a document that names another service's base as provided, or a topic outside `rwb.<short>.events.v1`, fails the review (DP-13, DP-14).
- No ACE view, no recovery table and no lake element appears as an object of this service, and `rwb_integration` holds no grant on `recovery` (DP-01, DP-05, DP-17).
- The envelope, the registry, the inbox, the retry topics and the `.dlt` rule come from the platform library; this story narrows them and never redefines them.
- Every example and fixture is synthetic; no production payload, address or event is copied into a schema or a fake.
- The version stays in the path and a breaking change needs a new version; the compatibility check runs in every build.
