##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case.fileoutcome`, module `fileoutcome`, in the service root `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`; the boundary rule is added to the test source tree of the service.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_case`; never read another service's tables; the case and the task are this service's rows | none |
| DP-02 | `recovery_svc` login | One login per service: the rwb-case login holds `rwb_case` only | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`; one entry per case per outcome, written first | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | ACE facts only through rwb-source-data's contract; this slice reads no view at all, and the boundary rule refuses one | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case and the client library: the route-state codes and the task code and due date rule | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library, CloudEvents 1.0, the owner's topic, retry topics and `.dlt`; the inbox is the only guard against a second application | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | No job and no Schedule: the build window and the sender are rwb-integration's Temporal path, the due date of the task is data, and the listener runs on the `rwb-case` worker of the kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock, one hop, 2 s timeout; the legacy published interfaces `CaseEvents` and `TaskApi` become internal services of the listener | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-16 | `recovery.integration.adapter` | The rwb-integration contract: the two outcomes and the admin item read | C RWB-P2-E1007-CON |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake); no lake target, no lake file, no lake row and no outbound extract; reporting is from events into rwb-reporting | none; gap if the story needed lake data |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route for the exception queue and the case screens | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**This is a secondary slice: the metadata H row is None and this story adds no build dependency of its own.** The platform contracts behind DP-03, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10 and DP-19 arrive with the `rwb_case` baseline and the platform epics, so they are not repeated in the metadata rows (GAP-0739; ASM-1340). DP-10 resolves to a prohibition (no `Schedule`, no job, no timer in this package), DP-05 to a prohibition enforced by the boundary rule, DP-01 to "the case and the task are this service's and no other schema is named", DP-17 to "no lake element and no outbound extract anywhere in the package", and DP-11 to the one-hop budget of the item read plus the conversion of the legacy in-process interfaces into internal services of the listener (GAP-0739; ASM-1339). The one contract dependency, `RWB-P2-E1007-CON` of DP-16, never blocks a build (§R5.4): the Kafka stubs and the admin-read fake of 12.8 stand in for rwb-integration on Day 1.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `FileOutcomeListener` | Listener | Consumes the two outcomes, validates the envelope, checks the inbox and drives the case-side steps in the order of section 4 |
| `InboxGuard` | Component | Inserts into `processed_event`; on conflict increments the hit count and drops the message |
| `ItemStatusReader` | Client | `GET /api/recovery/integration/v1/admin/outbound-items`, one hop, 2 s, breaker per downstream |
| `RouteStateResolver` | Service | Maps the item status to the target route state, and the `FileDelivered` outcome to the state to resume, from the reference rows in force |
| `CaseRouteStateWriter` | Repository | Writes `recovery_case.route_state` per case in the transaction of the outcome; skips a closed case |
| `OwnerTaskRaiser` | Service | Adds one open `task` for the case set with the task code, element type, owner role and due date of the reference rows in force |
| `FileOutcomeRecordWriter` | Service | Writes the decision-record entry first in the transaction through the DP-03 library |
| `FileOutcomeBoundaryRule` | ArchUnit rule in the test source | BND-6 over the module map: no `rwb_integration`, no `public`, no `v_ace_*` view, no lake path, no file and no SFTP class |

**Database and migrations.** None. This story creates no table, adds no column and writes no migration: `recovery_case`, `task`, `reference_row` and `reference_version` are the `rwb_case` baseline, and `processed_event` is created in `rwb_case` by the platform library migration. The service connects with its own login (DP-02), holding grants on `rwb_case` only.

**Configuration and reference data**

- The route-state codes for the retry and the exception route state, and the resume-path convention: reference rows of rwb-case at the version in force; no code value is written in code.
- The task reference row of the outbound-file failure task: its task code, element type, owner-role rule and due date rule, read at the version in force. The values are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0739; ASM-1338).
- The interface, its attempts, its intervals and its owner and alert roles stay in the interface row of rwb-integration and are never copied into this service; the item read answers them for the case at hand.
- The feature switch is `rwb.case.file-outcome`, read as a flag of the platform flag library (§R3 default rulings): off means the listener drops the outcomes with an alert and no state moves.

**Build steps**

1. `InboxGuard` over `processed_event` with the duplicate and the concurrent-worker cases; tests for AC4.
2. `ItemStatusReader` with the 503, the empty and the timeout paths and the breaker; tests for AC6.
3. `RouteStateResolver` over the reference rows, with a fixture set for RETRY, EXCEPTION and delivered; tests for AC1, AC3 and AC8.
4. `CaseRouteStateWriter` with one transaction per outcome, the closed-case skip and the case status left untouched; tests for AC1, AC2 and X10.
5. `OwnerTaskRaiser` with the task code, the owner role and the due date of the rows in force; tests for AC2 and AC8.
6. `FileOutcomeRecordWriter` written first in the transaction, with the stopped-chain path; tests for AC5.
7. `FileOutcomeListener` wiring the six steps in the order of section 4; the contract-fake run of the whole path.
8. `FileOutcomeBoundaryRule` and the module map, with fixture classes on `rwb_integration.outbound_item`, `public.customer`, `recovery.v_ace_account`, a lake path and an SFTP session; tests for AC7.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.case.file-outcome`, read as a flag of the platform flag library.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, each case of a failed file moves once, one task exists per case set at the retry limit, a delivered file restores the state held on the entry, a redelivery writes nothing, the build is green and red on the five boundary fixtures, and a session as the rwb-case login holds no privilege on `rwb_integration`, on `public` or on any `rwb_*` schema but its own.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Where it is produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written, so no route state and no task is changed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | This story, in `FileOutcomeRecordWriter` |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The rwb-integration admin read is unavailable, or a reference row is not in force, and the outcome is retried | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. | This story, on the item read and the reference read |
| MSG-P4-001 | The caller holds no Workbench role when reading the task list or the case | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. | rwb-access, surfaced here |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right reads a task list or a case it does not hold | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | rwb-access, surfaced here |
| MSG-P2-001 | Produced by rwb-integration when its item moves to the exception queue; read here as the reference of the task description, never produced | The {interface} file {file} was not sent after {count} attempts. It is in the exception queue. | rwb-integration, read here |
| MSG-GEN-004 | A reader acts on a case whose version changed | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. | This story, on the case read |
| Build log | A class names `rwb_integration`, `public`, a `v_ace_*` view, a lake path or a file | Boundary rule BND-6 broken: {class} names {object}. A case class names no other schema, no ACE view, no lake and no file. | This story, in the pipeline |

For MSG-P4-002 in this story, {action} names the action the role tried, for example "read the task list of another role", and never a row of a case. No new `MSG-` identifier is introduced by this story, and no identifier is renumbered by the realignment. The task description text and the alert text are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0739; ASM-1338) and are owned by RWB-P2-E1007-OPS through the alert role of the interface row. The refusal order is fixed: session, then right, then the case, and only then is a row read or a state moved.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen is built by this story. The exception queue is SCR-09, served by the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19): it reads the failed items from rwb-integration through that service's admin operation and shows them with the interface, the attempt count, the last error and the case count, and this story supplies the other half — the route state of each case and the open owner task. The case record view and the timeline show the route state and the task without a screen of this story. The route path, the screen-model field list and the visual layout are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0739; ASM-1338) and belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON and the designer.

| Screen | State | What the reader sees through the owner's contract |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-09 Exception queue | Retry | The item in RETRY on the rwb-integration read, and the case in route state RETRY_QUEUE with one entry and no task |
| SCR-09 Exception queue | Exception | The item in EXCEPTION with `MSG-P2-001`, the case in route state EXCEPTION_QUEUE and one open task for RW-PLATADM |
| SCR-09 Exception queue | Restored | The case back in the state it held, one entry with the action delivered, and the task unchanged |
| SCR-09 Exception queue | Repeated | The same view as the first outcome, with the inbox hit count raised and no second entry and no second task |
| Case record view and timeline | Delivery state | The route state of the case and the owner task, with the interface, the business date and the attempt count of each entry |

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the route-state codes, the task code, the due date rule, the owner and alert roles, the attempts, the intervals and the feature switch are rows and parameters read at run time.
- No personal data in events, logs, workflow inputs, decisions, tests or prompts: the entry carries identifiers, codes, counts and dates, and no file content is ever logged.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `v_ace_*` views — and this package reads neither: a class that names a view or `public` fails the build.
- No cross-schema read and no cross-schema key: `rwb_case` holds no foreign key into another schema and no copy of an item, an interface row or a delivery row; the item is read through the rwb-integration admin operation only (DP-01).
- No file access and no outbound extract: the package opens no file, no SFTP session and no lake path, and hands no bytes to anyone (DP-16, DP-17).
- The record comes first: a state move that cannot be recorded is not made, and an outcome that cannot be recorded fails the listener rather than being dropped (R-UNI-39).
- One hop, no chaining: the item read never calls a downstream of a downstream, and the breaker and bulkhead are per downstream.
- The case status is not moved by a file outcome, and no case event is published for it; a story that changes `recovery_case.status` here has left this slice.
- No new table, no column, no migration, no workflow and no `Schedule`: a story that adds one of them has left this slice.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-007 for the rwb-comms producer side of the INT-14 outbound notice file. The legacy single adapter module, its `recovery_svc` identity, its in-process reads of the `recovery.v_ace_*` views, its Quartz jobs JOB-10, JOB-11, JOB-13 and JOB-15 and its two data-lake deliveries are replaced by one service with its own login, one build-and-hand-off capability against the published contract `RWB-P2-E1007-CON`, and the removal of the lake interfaces INT-19 and INT-20. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform administrator (RW-PLATADM)**, I want **the notices rwb-comms holds for a business date written into the INT-14 WIN letter file from the service's own `notice` and `template` rows, the file offered as a claim-check object and handed to rwb-integration through the published contract `RWB-P2-E1007-CON`, with the run state readable on SCR-44 and the addressee never entering `rwb_comms`**, so that **every notice leaves for WIN on one path, the transport, the retry schedule and the exception queue belong to the service that owns them, and no statement of rwb-comms reads another service's table or an ACE view**.

This document is the rwb-comms slice of legacy key RWB-E1-007. The same legacy key has the primary slice in rwb-integration (`RWB-P2-E1007-APP`, which owns `interface_config`, `outbound_item`, the SFTP transport, the retry ladder, the exception queue and the `FileDelivered` and `FileFailed` events), an infrastructure and a deployment slice of that service, and the integration story `RWB-ITG-E1007-ITG` which proves the whole journey on the real wave-1 services. This story owns only the producer side: the record set, the file, the hand-off and the run state.

The legacy story held the adapter, the five tables, the scheduler and the exception queue in one module, ran as the shared `recovery_svc` identity, read `recovery.v_ace_contact`, `recovery.v_ace_account` and `recovery.v_ace_batch_status` in process and wrote two lake files. Under D-RCV-60 the producer side is one service, one schema `rwb_comms`, one login, one task queue `rwb-comms` and no table of another owner. rwb-comms builds the record set from its own rows, writes the file behind a claim-check reference, calls the rwb-integration hand-off, publishes the existing notice event, and reads the outcome the owner announces. The lake interfaces INT-19 and INT-20 are removed and are not rebuilt here.

It serves REQ-DRI-006, REQ-DRI-007 and REQ-DRI-008, and it serves the FSD P6 measure "notices with proof of delivery, 100 percent" by making the outbound file of the business date a single, repeatable run.

##### 2. Business rationale

The Workbench loads no source data; ACE ingests every source and the Workbench only sends (D-RCV-35 U1). What remains of the legacy key on this side is the producer of one file: the WIN registered-mail notice file of the business date (INT-14, JOB-10). The legacy rationale, the four outbound interfaces and the one adapter pattern are unchanged in intent; the owner of each fact is what moved. The notice rows and the template version are rwb-comms's own; the interface row, the item, the transport, the retry intervals, the exception queue and the delivery events are rwb-integration's; the addressee and contact token is read by rwb-source-data and never stored here; the list values and the eligible notice state are reference data of rwb-case; the letter behind `notice.document_id` and the claim-check object are rwb-document's.

Three legacy statements are retired rather than restated, because no source gives them a target. The inbound file load, its checks, its run record and its sign-off are ACE ingestion (RWB-ACE-001), and P2 has no inbound adapter. The INT-19 reporting extract and the INT-20 decision-log copy are lake interfaces; DP-17 removes the lake, reporting is fed by events into rwb-reporting, and the decision ledger is fed by the shared decision-record topic. And the legacy Quartz rows are gone: JOB-10 is a file window of the bank scheduler plus the dispatch Schedule of the service, and JOB-11 is the platform outbox relay of DP-09. The removals are recorded as GAP-1163 with ASM-2110 and GAP-1165 with ASM-2112.

What the business asked for is unchanged. A notice of the business date still leaves in one file; a repeated run still adds nothing; a file that cannot be handed over is still reported with the same message; and a caller without the right is still refused with the same text. What changed is that every one of those seams is now a one-hop contract call with a 2 s budget, a breaker and a fake, so the story is buildable on Day 1 against `RWB-P2-E1007-CON` alone.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P2-E1007-CON is published: the `deliverFile(manifest)` activity contract on queue `rwb-integration` with the manifest and its return element, the `rwb.integration.events.v1` AsyncAPI document with `FileDelivered` and `FileFailed`, the read that returns the INT-14 interface row in force, the error envelope and the fakes.
- The INT-14 interface configuration row is loaded by the reference data administrator (RW-REFADM) at version "IF-2026.11" with direction OUTBOUND, max attempts 3 and retry intervals 5, 15 and 45 minutes; it is a row of rwb-integration and is read through the contract only, never as a table (DP-01).
- The notices of the business date exist in `rwb_comms`: RWB-P6-E1052-APP generates them and RWB-P6-E1046-APP holds the template and merge-field catalog; the dispatch columns `dispatch_file_id` and `dispatch_attempts` are in `notice` (DF-LEG-033, DF-LEG-034).
- The reference-data contract of rwb-case carries the eligible state set plus LOV-NOTICE, LOV-SENT-TYPE and LOV-DELIVERY with the version in force, so no list value is written in code; that contract (RWB-P3-E1043-CON) is not in this story's contract list (GAP-1161; ASM-2108).
- The platform libraries that DP-03, DP-09, DP-10 and DP-19 add are live: the local decision-record library (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON), the outbox, inbox and idempotency library with CloudEvents (RWB-PLT-TE006-CON), the workflow kit with task queue `rwb-comms` in namespace `rwb-recovery` (RWB-PLT-E1071-CON) and the gateway-bff composite route (RWB-PLT-N001-CON). None of the four is in this story's build list, which is empty, so the story builds against their fakes until they publish (GAP-1161; ASM-2108).
- The addressee and address token of a notice is read through the rwb-source-data contract by `notice.party_id`; the rwb-source-data contract is not in this story's contract list and its element names are not named in the source documents (GAP-1162; ASM-2109).
- The claim-check object store that holds the built file, and the operation that accepts it and returns its reference, are not named in the source documents (GAP-1164; ASM-2111); the payload reference is the `payload_ref` element of the rwb-integration manifest (DF-OPS-171).
- The WIN edge in SIT is the stub of 12.8: an SFTP folder and an acknowledgment record reached by rwb-integration, with no real WIN connection and no production data.
- The service runs as its own login on schema `rwb_comms` (DP-02); it holds no grant on `recovery`, no grant on another `rwb_*` schema and no `v_ace_*` grant.

##### 4. Flow

1. The dispatch Schedule of rwb-comms starts the dispatch run for the business date at 16:00 Asia/Bangkok on task queue `rwb-comms` in namespace `rwb-recovery` (JOB-10); the bank Airflow file window opens the cross-system edge in the same window.
2. `NoticeFileRunWorkflow` starts with workflow ID `INT-14:<businessDate>` and asks the rwb-integration contract for the INT-14 interface row in force: the file pattern, the record layout and the record count rule (12.2).
3. `selectFileRecords` reads the eligible set from `rwb_comms` only: notices of the business date in the eligible state, with a resolved template version, that carry no file reference for that date; the eligible state and the lists come from the rwb-case reference-data contract with their version.
4. `renderNoticeFile` builds the INT-14 record set and its trailer from those rows and from the template version in force; where a rule decides the eligible set, the outcome is written through the local decision-record library before the record set is fixed (DP-03).
5. The addressee and address of each record are requested as a token through the rwb-source-data contract, by `notice.party_id`, inside the build only; no name, address or contact value is stored in `rwb_comms`, put on the manifest or logged.
6. `storeNoticeFile` stores the built file behind a claim-check reference in the object store and returns that reference; the file content never travels on a message, a workflow input or a log.
7. `handoffFile` calls `deliverFile(manifest)` on queue `rwb-integration` with the interface ID `INT-14`, the business date, the idempotency key `INT-14:<businessDate>`, the claim-check payload reference, the record count, the notice IDs, the case IDs and the requesting service; one hop, 2 s timeout, one retry with jitter and a breaker.
8. The run records the item reference and its status in the answer, sets `dispatch_file_id` to that reference and increments `dispatch_attempts` on each notice it wrote, and writes `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1` to its outbox in the same transaction (DP-09).
9. rwb-integration owns everything after the hand-off: the `outbound_item` row, the SFTP transfer with PGP, the retry intervals, the exception queue, the owner task and the two events. This service never opens a session to WIN and never writes an item.
10. When rwb-integration announces `rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1` or `rwb.integration.FileFailed.v1`, the inbox of `rwb_comms` dedupes it on the event ID and the run records the delivered or failed state with the attempt count and the last error code; no notice state changes on either event, because the acknowledgment that sets a notice Sent belongs to RWB-P6-E1055-APP.
11. A repeated run on the same business date rebuilds nothing for a notice that already carries the file reference and hands the same file over under the same idempotency key, so no second item and no second file exist.
12. The platform administrator reads the run state on SCR-44 through the gateway-bff composite route with `GET /file-runs/{businessDate}`; a data-quality break of the run is shown on SCR-45.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | rwb-integration does not answer the hand-off inside 2 s, or its breaker is open | The run records the hand-off as not accepted, no notice changes state, nothing is retried by this service and the next run of the business date hands the same file over under the same key | MSG-GEN-006 | AC4 |
| X2 | rwb-integration reports the file in its exception queue after the last attempt | The run shows the failed state with the attempt count and the error code, and names the owner's message; the resend belongs to the owner and is not built here | MSG-P2-001 | AC4, AC8 |
| X3 | The run is repeated on the same business date | No notice is written into a second file; the file reference and the attempt count move once; the owner answers with the first item | None | AC3 |
| X4 | A notice carries a template code that resolves to no template row, or a notice type outside LOV-NOTICE | The notice is left out of the record set and counted on the run; the rest of the file is written and handed over | None | AC5 |
| X5 | The answer of the source-data contract carries the stale marker of the business date | The record set is not built from a partial answer; the run is held and names the product and its date | MSG-P1-001 | TC-E1-007-04 |
| X6 | The same `FileDelivered` or `FileFailed` event arrives twice | The inbox ignores the repeat, counts the hit and no run state moves a second time (R-UNI-40) | None | AC3 |
| X7 | A caller without the right reads or reruns a run | Refused at the edge before any read or write; nothing changes | MSG-P4-002 | AC8, TC-E1-007-10 |
| X8 | A run, a component or a statement reaches an ACE view, another `rwb_*` schema, an SFTP client or the file system | The grant refuses the statement and the architecture boundary test fails the build; nothing is released | None (pipeline log) | AC2, AC6 |
| X9 | A read names a business date with no run | The answer is 404 and no record is read | MSG-P4-003 | AC8 |
| X10 | The decision record cannot be written where a rule decided the eligible set | Nothing is written into the file and the run stops with an incident | MSG-P7-003 | BR10 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Starts on Day 1 against `RWB-P2-E1007-CON` and its fakes; the reference data, the source-data token, the outbox library, the workflow kit and the edge route are fakes until their stories publish (GAP-1161; ASM-2108) |
| Negotiable | The file pattern, the layout, the attempts and the intervals are the owner's interface row; the object store and its operation are open; the story fixes only the producer behaviour |
| Valuable | The notice file of the business date leaves on one path, a repeated run adds nothing, and the addressee never enters this service |
| Estimable | One workflow, four activities, two read operations, three consumed contracts, one event and ten test cases |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests, as the secondary slice of the legacy key |
| Testable | Each criterion runs against the contract fakes with synthetic notices; the access row is a component test and the retired inbound checks are NFR rows |

The eight criteria are new work under D-RCV-60 and test only the producer deliverable of this story. They assert nothing that belongs to the rwb-integration slice: the item table, the transport, the retry intervals, the exception queue, the resend and the owner task are owned by `RWB-P2-E1007-APP` and its contract. The legacy criteria AC1 to AC7 of RWB-E1-007 are owned by the P2 slice (AC1, AC2, AC3, AC5, AC6, AC7) and by `RWB-ITG-E1007-ITG` (AC4), and no legacy line is restated here.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The INT-14 record set is built from this service's own `notice` and `template` rows for the business date; the eligible state, the list values, the file pattern and the layout are data with a version, never code | legacy BR1, BR8; INT-14; JOB-10; DP-07 |
| BR2 | The only path to WIN is the rwb-integration contract; no SFTP client, no file-system client and no direct WIN call exist in rwb-comms | legacy BR1; DP-16; REQ-DRI-006; ADR-010 |
| BR3 | `interface_config` and `outbound_item` belong to rwb-integration, and this service creates, reads and writes neither; the item reference is all the run holds | Ownership Map; legacy BR10; DP-01 |
| BR4 | The addressee and the contact value are read by rwb-source-data and never enter `rwb_comms`; they are used inside the file build as the token the owner's contract returns, are never logged and are not put on an event | legacy BR10; CTL-11; DP-05 |
| BR5 | A repeated run on one business date adds no second item and no second file, because the hand-off carries one idempotency key per interface and business date | legacy section 12, JOB-10 ("a second run adds nothing"); R-UNI-40 |
| BR6 | A downstream that fails is retried by its owner, and this service never advances a notice on a call that failed; the run reports only the state it learned | legacy BR5; R-UNI-33; DP-11 |
| BR7 | There is no data lake: the reporting extract INT-19 and the decision-log copy INT-20 are not built, and reporting is fed by events into rwb-reporting | DP-17; Architecture v5 slides 2, 37 and 44 |
| BR8 | JOB-10 is the dispatch Schedule of this service and JOB-11 is the platform outbox relay; no Quartz row and no job table entry is written | Architecture v5 slide 44; DP-10 |
| BR9 | A notice with a template code that resolves to no template row, or a notice type outside LOV-NOTICE, is left out of the file and counted; a partial record set is never handed over as complete | legacy section 5, X8; FSD P6 A2.2 AC-EXC-P6-002-02 (the held notice is not in the WIN file) |
| BR10 | The decision is never recorded after the effect: where a rule decides the eligible set, the record is written first through the local decision-record library, and a failed write stops the run | DP-03; MSG-P7-003; FSD P6 A2.2 AC-EXC-P6-002-03 |
| R-UNI-33 | A downstream system that fails is retried, and the state of the record is not advanced until the retry succeeds | legacy BR5; INT-14 error handling |
| R-UNI-34 | A retried call that passes its limit leaves the record in the exception queue with the reason, and the queue is reviewed by the owning team | legacy BR6; INT-14 error handling |
| R-UNI-40 | The same event or the same source row twice produces one effect, and the repeat is counted | legacy BR7 |

##### 9. State transitions

This story moves the dispatch fields of the notice and the state of its own file run. It moves no notice lifecycle state: the move to Sent is the acknowledgment of RWB-P6-E1055-APP and the move to Delivered is its proof of delivery.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Notice in the eligible state with no file reference for the date | The run writes the notice into the record set | The template version resolves and the eligible state is current | The notice keeps its state, `dispatch_file_id` is set and `dispatch_attempts` is incremented |
| Notice with a file reference for an earlier date | A later run writes it again | The notice is still in the eligible state | `dispatch_file_id` moves to the new file and `dispatch_attempts` is incremented |
| Notice with a file reference for the same date | The run is repeated on that date | The same business date | Unchanged: no second reference and no second file |
| Notice left out of the record set | The run finds no resolvable template version | The reference is unknown | Unchanged, and counted on the run as not buildable |
| Run without an item reference | `deliverFile` answers with an item reference | The hand-off is accepted | The run holds the reference and its status, and the notices carry it |
| Run without an item reference | `deliverFile` does not answer inside 2 s | The breaker is open or the call times out | The run records the hand-off as not accepted; the next run retries the same key |
| Run with an item reference | `rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1` is consumed | The envelope names interface INT-14 and the business date | The run records the delivered state and the attempt count; no notice state changes |
| Run with an item reference | `rwb.integration.FileFailed.v1` is consumed | The envelope names interface INT-14 and the business date | The run records the failed state, the attempt count and the error code; no notice state changes |

The item status the run reports is the owner's list (`PENDING`, `SENT`, `RETRY`, `EXCEPTION`, `ACKNOWLEDGED`, LOV-OUTBOUND-STATUS of the rwb-integration interface row) and is never re-derived here. This service writes no run table (GAP-1166; ASM-2113): the run is read from the dispatch fields of its own notices, the workflow run and the status the owner returns.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| rwb-comms service identity | Builds the record set, stores the file, calls the hand-off, writes the dispatch fields and the outbox row, and reads the run state; it holds no grant on another schema and no `v_ace_*` grant |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Documents R and Litigation absent (TSD P6 T6.1): reads the run state on SCR-44 and reruns the producer run of a business date |
| RW-DATASTEW, data steward | Documents R: reads the run state and receives the held-file and failed-file alerts |
| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer | Litigation CRUA: reads the notice and its file reference on the case; no right on the run operations |
| RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-COE | Documents R: read the run state |
| rwb-integration service identity | Answers the interface row, creates and owns the item, transports and retries the file, and announces the two events |
| rwb-case, rwb-source-data and rwb-document service identities | Serve the reference data, the addressee token and the claim-check store; they take no decision in this story |

The right on the two run operations is enforced at the edge for the screen path (DP-19); a local guard on the operation itself is not named in the source documents, and DP-08 is not in this story's pattern list (GAP-1166; ASM-2113). A refusal keeps MSG-P4-002 and changes nothing.

Field IDs are those of the legacy story, the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary, the TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 and the TSD P2 Integration v3 T3.1. No new table and no new column is created: the dispatch columns `dispatch_file_id` (DF-LEG-033) and `dispatch_attempts` (DF-LEG-034) arrive with the `notice` table of RWB-P6-E1052-APP and this story writes them only. `outbox_event`, `processed_event` and `idempotency_key` are platform library objects created in `rwb_comms` (DP-09). No row of `interface_config`, `outbound_item`, `document`, `party_ext` or `contact_point_ext` is copied into `rwb_comms`, no foreign key leaves the schema, and `notice.dispatch_file_id` is an identifier and not a foreign key across schemas (DP-01).

**No personal data.** The rows this story reads carry identifiers, dates, a code and a counter. The addressee, the address and the contact value are read by rwb-source-data and used inside the file build as a token; they are never stored in `rwb_comms`, never logged, never put on the manifest beyond the claim-check reference and never put on an event. The file content is never logged, only its name, its record count and its hash.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-comms (P6); base `/api/recovery/comms/v1`.

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/file-runs/{businessDate}` | Read the run state of the business date: interface `INT-14`, the record count, the notice count, the item reference, the item status the owner reports, the attempt count, the last error code and the delivered or failed state | Documents R, enforced at the edge (DP-19) | Not applicable |
| POST | `/file-runs/{businessDate}/retry` | Rerun the producer run of the business date: rebuild the record set and hand the same file over under the same idempotency key; it resends no item and changes no item state, because the resend of an exception item is the owner's operation | Documents U, enforced at the edge (DP-19) | `Idempotency-Key` header required; 409 with MSG-GEN-004 when the run is already accepted and the version changed; 404 with MSG-P4-003 for a business date with no run |

The two paths are this story's design on the service base, because no source names them: the TSD P6 Communications v2 appendix T-A carries no run operation and the interface monitor is SCR-44 of the operations surface (GAP-1166; ASM-2113). Errors: 401 no session; 403 no right (MSG-P4-002); 404 unknown business date (MSG-P4-003); 409 a changed version (MSG-GEN-004); 503 a store or a consumed contract unavailable (MSG-GEN-006). The response field names are fixed in the P2 contract story only for the item it returns, and the run answer is this service's own.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Temporal activity | `deliverFile(manifest)` on queue `rwb-integration` | P2 rwb-integration (RWB-P2-E1007-CON) | The only path to WIN: the manifest carries the interface ID, the business date, the idempotency key, the claim-check payload reference, the record count, the notice IDs, the case IDs and the requesting service, and the answer returns the item reference and its status |
| GET | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1164; ASM-2111) | P2 rwb-integration | The `INT-14` interface row in force: the file pattern, the record layout and the record count rule, read through the contract and never as a table |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/customers/{customerId}` | P1 rwb-source-data (contract not in this story's list, GAP-1162; ASM-2109) | The addressee and address token of each record, by `notice.party_id`, inside the file build only |
| The LOV read of the rwb-case reference-data contract | P3 rwb-case (contract not in this story's list, GAP-1161; ASM-2108) | The eligible state set, LOV-NOTICE, LOV-SENT-TYPE and LOV-DELIVERY by version, so no list value is in code |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, one GET retry with jitter and a breaker per downstream (DP-11, ADR-020). No row is composed into another: this service never calls a service that calls a third one, and the hand-off is the only call that leaves the service with a file.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Key | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1` (EV-14) | `rwb.comms.events.v1` | caseId | notice ID, case ID, business date, the file reference, the dispatch attempt count, and the sent date, barcode and sent type the notice carries (empty on the first run, because they arrive with the acknowledgment of RWB-P6-E1055-APP). No addressee, no address, no contact value |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | caseId | decision record reference, rule code, rule version, final call, decided at; written through the local decision-record library where a rule decides the eligible set |

No new event name is added: the file-run fact travels on the existing `NoticeDispatched` event of the service, whose envelope and field names are fixed by the service's event contract and never re-declared here. Both rows are written to the outbox in the same transaction as the dispatch-field change and relayed with the CloudEvents envelope (DP-09).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Handler use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1` | `rwb.integration.events.v1` | P2 rwb-integration | The run records the delivered state, the item reference and the attempt count; no notice state changes |
| `rwb.integration.FileFailed.v1` | `rwb.integration.events.v1` | P2 rwb-integration | The run records the failed state, the attempt count and the error code and shows MSG-P2-001; no notice state changes and no task is raised here |

Both events name the requesting service as their consumer (Architecture v5 slide 43), so this service consumes them and nothing else. Each is deduped through the inbox of schema `rwb_comms` on its event ID; a repeat produces no second effect and is counted (R-UNI-40). The hand-off request itself is an activity, not an event (Architecture v5 slide 16, "events (none: called as a task)").

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NoticeFileRunWorkflow` | Workflow from the kit template, one execution per interface and business date, workflow ID `INT-14:<businessDate>` | `rwb-comms` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Owns the run: the interface row, the eligible set, the file, the hand-off, the outcome and the events |
| `selectFileRecords` | Activity | `rwb-comms` | Reads the eligible notices of the business date from `rwb_comms` and resolves their template version |
| `renderNoticeFile` | Activity | `rwb-comms` | Builds the INT-14 record set and its trailer in the layout of the interface row, with the addressee token |
| `storeNoticeFile` | Activity, calls the claim-check object store | `rwb-comms` | Stores the built file and returns its claim-check reference (GAP-1164; ASM-2111) |
| `handoffFile` | Activity calling `deliverFile` on `rwb-integration` | `rwb-integration` | One hop, 2 s timeout; returns the item reference and status, or no answer |
| `recordFileRun` | Activity | `rwb-comms` | Writes the dispatch fields of the notices, the outbox rows and the state the run reports |

The workflow is idempotent by interface and business date: a retried run writes no notice into a second file, does not rebuild a record that already carries the reference, and does not re-send an accepted file.

###### 12.6 Schedules

One Schedule starts the work of this story; it is registered by the dispatch story of the service, because the run it starts is the dispatch run.

| Schedule | Cron | Overlap | Catch-up | What it starts |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| The dispatch Schedule of rwb-comms, registered by RWB-P6-E1055-APP (RWB-PLT-E1071-CON) | 16:00 Asia/Bangkok, daily | SKIP | Catch-up window of the workflow kit | The dispatch run whose file build and hand-off are this story |

The cross-system edge of JOB-10 is the bank Airflow file window, owned by the platform and by rwb-integration (Architecture v5 slide 44, "Airflow file window + workers"). This story registers no Schedule of its own, no Quartz row, no job table entry and no Control-M job, and JOB-11 is the platform outbox relay of DP-09 (BR8).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| notice | P6 (rwb_comms) | The notice rows of the record set and their dispatch fields `dispatch_file_id` and `dispatch_attempts` |
| template | P6 (rwb_comms) | The template version in force behind each record, read only |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_comms` | The outbox, inbox and idempotency objects of the published event, the two consumed events and the retry operation (DP-09) |

Not owned and never read as a table: `interface_config` and `outbound_item` (P2), `document` (P5), `party_ext` and `contact_point_ext` (P1), `recovery_case` and `task` (P3), `decision_log_entry` (P7). No `v_ace_*` view is read here and no ACE table is read here: every ACE fact arrives through the rwb-source-data contract (DP-01, DP-05).

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-integration contract fake (RWB-P2-E1007-CON) | The `INT-14` interface row in force with direction OUTBOUND, max attempts 3 and intervals 5, 15 and 45 minutes; `deliverFile` returning item reference `OB-0001` in status `PENDING` for 2026-11-30; `ACKNOWLEDGED` after the transfer; `EXCEPTION` with an error code after three attempts; no answer beyond 2 s; the acknowledgment record carrying sent date 30112026, barcode `RR123456789TH` and sent type `NPL` for contract `CT-77001` | AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC8 |
| rwb-case reference-data fake | The eligible state set `GENERATED`; LOV-NOTICE (`DEMAND`, `RECALL`, `STATUTORY_SALE_NOTICE`, `GUARANTOR_NOTICE`), LOV-SENT-TYPE (`BEFORE_NPL`, `NPL`) and LOV-DELIVERY (`DELIVERED`, `REFUSED`, `UNDELIVERABLE`, `PENDING`) at their version; no template for code `DEMAND-OLD` | AC1, AC5 |

The fakes are test-only and are replaced by the real services in SIT; the drift between a fake and the baseline is a build failure in the P2 contract.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 provided, 3 consumed | The run read and the rerun on `/api/recovery/comms/v1`; the interface row on rwb-integration, the addressee token on rwb-source-data and the LOV read on rwb-case; one hop and 2 s each |
| Kafka | 2 published, 2 consumed | `NoticeDispatched` and `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.comms.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1`; `FileDelivered` and `FileFailed` on `rwb.integration.events.v1` |
| Temporal | 1 workflow, 5 activities | `NoticeFileRunWorkflow` on `rwb-comms` with the four build steps, and the hand-off activity that calls `deliverFile` on `rwb-integration` |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.comms`, module `outboundfile`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.comms.outboundfile`. The legacy folder `src/main/java/recovery/integration/adapter` and the legacy package `recovery.integration.adapter` are not carried over: the transport and the adapter boundary are rwb-integration's, and this service holds the producer only.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-02 | `recovery_svc` login | One login per service | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-16 | `recovery.integration.adapter` | rwb-integration contract | C RWB-P2-E1007-CON |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting | none; gap if the story needs lake data |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-05 applies only as a prohibition: this service reads no ACE view and holds no `v_ace_*` grant, so the addressee, the address and the batch completeness arrive through the rwb-source-data contract. DP-16 applies as "the only path to WIN is `deliverFile`", and DP-17 as "no lake file, no lake copy and no lake delivery row".

**Dependencies the table adds and the plan lists do not hold.** The patterns above add six H rows and one C row: `RWB-PLT-E1027-CON` (DP-03), `RWB-PLT-E1043-CON` with `RWB-P3-E1043-CON` (DP-07), `RWB-PLT-TE006-CON` (DP-09), `RWB-PLT-E1071-CON` (DP-10) and `RWB-PLT-N001-CON` (DP-19). This story's plan lists hold `Depends on (build)` None and `Contract dependencies` `RWB-P2-E1007-CON` only, so none of them is in the metadata table. The story keeps the plan's lists as they are, builds against the contract fakes until those stories publish, and records the absence as GAP-1161 with ASM-2108.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| FileRunController | Controller | The run read and the rerun on `/api/recovery/comms/v1`, with the problem mapping for 401, 403, 404, 409 and 503 |
| NoticeFileRunWorkflow | Workflow | The run of section 4: the interface row, the eligible set, the file, the hand-off, the outcome and the events |
| EligibleSetSelector | Service | The eligible notices of the business date from `rwb_comms` only, with the eligible state and the lists read as reference data |
| NoticeFileWriter | Service | The INT-14 record set and its trailer in the layout of the interface row, with the addressee token read at build time |
| ClaimCheckWriter | Client | Stores the built file behind a claim-check reference; holds no file-system path and no SFTP setting |
| IntegrationHandoffClient | Client | The `deliverFile` call on queue `rwb-integration`, one hop and 2 s, with the breaker and the retry boundary |
| FileOutcomeListener | Listener | The inbox-deduped handlers of `FileDelivered` and `FileFailed`, and the run state they record |
| NoticeDispatchedPublisher | Service | Writes the outbox row of `NoticeDispatched` in the same transaction as the dispatch-field change |
| FileRunReader | Service | The run answer from the dispatch fields, the workflow run and the status the owner reports |
| BoundaryRuleTest | Test | No SFTP client, no file-system client, no lake client and no statement outside `rwb_comms` |

**Database and migrations.** No new table and no new column. `notice`, `template`, `merge_field` and the library objects live in `rwb_comms`; the dispatch columns and their indexes arrive with the `notice` table of RWB-P6-E1052-APP, and this story adds no Flyway file of its own. `interface_config` and `outbound_item` are not created here.

**Configuration and reference data.** `rwb.comms.filerun.eligible-states` = `GENERATED`; `rwb.comms.filerun.interface-id` = `INT-14`; `rwb.comms.filerun.idempotency-prefix` = `INT-14:`. All three are reference data read with their version through the rwb-case reference-data contract and owned by the platform administrator, and none is compiled into the service. The file pattern, the layout, the attempts and the intervals are the owner's interface row and are never copied into a value file.

**Build steps**

1. Build `EligibleSetSelector` over `rwb_comms` with the reference-data read and the resolved template version; test AC1 and AC5.
2. Build `NoticeFileWriter` with the layout of the interface row, the trailer and the addressee token; test AC1 and AC7.
3. Build `ClaimCheckWriter` against the store stub and record the returned reference; test AC1.
4. Build `IntegrationHandoffClient` with the manifest, the 2 s budget, the breaker and the no-answer path; test AC2 and AC4.
5. Build `NoticeFileRunWorkflow` with workflow ID `INT-14:<businessDate>`, the idempotency rule and the repeated-run path; test AC3.
6. Build `FileOutcomeListener` with the inbox dedupe and the two run states; test AC3 and AC8.
7. Build `NoticeDispatchedPublisher` in the same transaction as the dispatch-field change, and the decision record where a rule decides; test AC3 and AC6.
8. Build `FileRunController`, the right check at the edge and the 409 and 404 paths; test AC8 and TC-E1-007-10.
9. Add the boundary test for the lake, the SFTP client, the file system and the foreign schema; test AC2 and AC6.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.comms.win-file-v1`, read as a flag of the platform library; off means no record set is built and no file is handed over.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, the contract tests of `RWB-P2-E1007-CON` stay green, the boundary test runs in the pipeline, and a SIT week shows one file per business date, no notice in a second file of the same date, one item per file created by rwb-integration, no addressee value stored here and no lake interface of this key.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-001 | The record set is held because the answer of the source data carries the stale marker of the business date | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The hand-off does not answer inside 2 s, or the breaker is open, or the claim-check store is unavailable | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P2-001 | rwb-integration reports the file in its exception queue after the last attempt | The {interface} file {file} was not sent after {count} attempts. It is in the exception queue. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | A rerun names a run whose record changed | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-GEN-005 | A rerun is accepted | Saved. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right reads or reruns a run | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | A read or a rerun names a business date with no run | This record was not found. |

The seven texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story RWB-E1-007 section 14; no identifier is renumbered. `MSG-P2-001` is authored by rwb-integration and is displayed on the run state here, never raised by this service, because the exception queue is the owner's.

##### 15. Screens and states

| Screen | State | What the user does |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-44 Interface and job monitor | Loading | Sees the placeholder while the gateway-bff composite route answers |
| SCR-44 Interface and job monitor | List | Sees the run of the business date with interface `INT-14`, the record count, the item reference, the item status and the attempt count |
| SCR-44 Interface and job monitor | Held | Sees the run held with MSG-P1-001 naming the product and its date |
| SCR-44 Interface and job monitor | Not accepted | Sees that rwb-integration did not accept the hand-off, with MSG-GEN-006 |
| SCR-44 Interface and job monitor | Failed | Sees the failed state with the attempt count, the last error code and MSG-P2-001 |
| SCR-44 Interface and job monitor | Rerun | Reruns the producer run, reads MSG-GEN-005 and sees no second file |
| SCR-44 Interface and job monitor | Refused | A role without the right reads MSG-P4-002 and nothing changes |
| SCR-45 Data quality | Breaks | Sees the notices left out of the record set and counted, and the held run of the business date |

Both screens are reached through the gateway-bff composite route at the edge and read this service once per operation (DP-19); the route path, the screen-model field list and the merge order belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON, and the full interface and job monitor of the programme belongs to the platform and operations stories, not here.

| TC-E1-007-01 | AC1, AC6 | End to end | 85 notices of 2026-11-30; one `INT-14` interface row with direction OUTBOUND; the boundary test for the lake, the inbound path and the SFTP client |

The ten legacy identifiers are kept in the order of the source list. Legacy levels map System to End to end, Access to Component and Resilience to NFR. `TC-E1-007-05` and `TC-E1-007-06` are the retired inbound-load cases: their behaviour is ACE ingestion, the ACE batch record and the EV-27 `AceDataLate` alert, so they run as NFR checks on the retired path and assert only that no inbound adapter, no inbound folder, no file check of DQ-057 or DQ-059 and no `interface_run` row exists here (GAP-1165; ASM-2112). The real cross-service journey of the file is proven by `RWB-ITG-E1007-ITG`, and the item, transport, retry and resend cases are run by `RWB-P2-E1007-APP`. The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the eligible state, the interface ID, the file pattern, the layout, the attempts, the intervals and the list values are data with a version; no role, list value, state name or count appears in Java.
- No personal data in events, logs, workflow inputs or tests: the addressee, the address and the contact value never enter `rwb_comms` and are never logged; file content is never logged, only its name, its record count and its hash.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: the addressee and the batch completeness arrive through rwb-source-data, and this service holds no `v_ace_*` grant and no grant on the `recovery` schema (DP-05).
- No read of another service's tables and no cross-schema join: `interface_config`, `outbound_item`, `document`, `party_ext` and `contact_point_ext` are reached only through their owners' contracts (DP-01).
- Files move only through rwb-integration: no component opens an SFTP session, reads a folder or calls WIN, and the boundary test fails the build on any such call (DP-16, REQ-DRI-006).
- No data lake and no lake delivery row: INT-19 and INT-20 have no target, and no adapter of this key writes them (DP-17).
- One hop and a 2 s budget per consumed call, with one GET retry with jitter and a breaker per downstream; no call chain.
- Every published event is written to the outbox in the same transaction as the dispatch-field change and carries IDs and facts only; every consumed event is deduped through the inbox (DP-09).

##### 19. Out of scope

- The item, the transport, the retry schedule, the exception queue, the owner task, the resend and the two events: `RWB-P2-E1007-APP` and `RWB-P2-E1007-CON`; the MFT/SFTP endpoints, the PGP keys, the firewall and the staging area: `RWB-P2-E1007-INF`.
- The real cross-service journey of the file with all services live: `RWB-ITG-E1007-ITG`.
- The inbound source ingestion, its schedules, its checks and the ACE team sign-off, which replace the retired inbound load of this legacy key: RWB-ACE-001.
- The record-level checks, the reconciliation and the stale marker of the data products: RWB-P1-E1011-APP and RWB-P1-E1015-CON.
- The dispatch run itself, the WIN acknowledgment, the sent fields and the proof of delivery: `RWB-P6-E1055-APP` and its contract; notice generation and the template catalog: RWB-P6-E1052-APP and RWB-P6-E1046-APP.
- The run books, the alerts and the full SCR-44 interface and job monitor: RWB-E1-056 and the platform and operations stories.
- The Scheduled jobs and the shared tables they used: JOB-10 is the file window and the service's dispatch Schedule, JOB-11 is the platform relay, and no Quartz row or job table entry is written.
- The data lake: the reporting extract INT-19 and the decision-log copy INT-20 are removed and are not rebuilt; reporting comes from events into rwb-reporting and the decision ledger from the shared decision-record topic.
- The stored letter, the claim-check store's own retention and custody: rwb-document (P5) and its stories; this story follows the contract reference only.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: this is the P5 slice of legacy RWB-E1-007, split (rework). The legacy story's adapter, its `recovery_svc` identity, its SFTP session, its retry ladder and its exception queue stay in `rwb-integration` (RWB-P2-E1007-APP); this slice takes only the document-hub side of the same outbound path — the store of the built file, its claim-check reference, its retention class and the read back — in `rwb-document` with schema `rwb_document`, REST base `/api/recovery/document/v1`, topic `rwb.document.events.v1` with `DocumentStored` only, task queue `rwb-document` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document`. The legacy data-lake statements of JOB-13 and JOB-15 are retired (DP-17). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform administrator (RW-PLATADM)**, I want **the file that rwb-integration has built for an outbound interface to be stored once in the document hub with its manifest, its claim-check reference and the retention class of its type, served back to the flow that owns it through the claim-check link, and announced by one `DocumentStored` event**, so that **every outbound file of the Workbench is held in one place under write-once storage, is found again by its document ID, and never travels as content on a Kafka message or in a workflow payload**.

Inside `rwb-document` this is the document-hub side of the one outbound-file path of legacy RWB-E1-007:

- Service `rwb-document`, schema `rwb_document`, REST base `/api/recovery/document/v1`, topic `rwb.document.events.v1` with the event name `rwb.document.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document`.
- Three operations carry the outbound path: `POST /api/recovery/document/v1/documents` takes the built file and its manifest and returns the document ID, the storage reference, the SHA-256, the state, the retention class and the claim-check link; `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}` and `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/content` serve the metadata and the file back to its owner and to the requesting flow.
- rwb-document accepts the file that rwb-integration has built — the `deliverFile(manifest)` path of RWB-P2-E1007-CON — stores it through the platform storage product RWB-PLT-TE012-APP in Azure Blob with WORM, keeps the claim-check reference (`storage_ref`) and the manifest facts (`fileId`, `batchId`, `sha256`, record count), and applies the retention class of the document type in force. It publishes `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` to its outbox in the store transaction and consumes nothing.
- The claim-check link is a SAS link for one file, valid 15 minutes (Arch v5 slide 11). No file bytes and no personal value travel in an event, a workflow input or a log.
- There is no adapter of its own in this slice, no SFTP call, no file-system call and no inbound path: rwb-integration builds, sends and retries the file (RWB-P2-E1007-APP), and this slice stores and serves it.
- There is no data lake: INT-19 and INT-20 carry no lake target; the reporting extract is delivered to rwb-reporting through `deliverFile` and the decision and outcome feed is continuous Kafka ingest in rwb-decision (DP-17).
- The database login is one per service (DP-02). Its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1027; ASM-1959); this story uses the phrase "the rwb-document login (DP-02)" and never a shared login.

This slice owns no legacy acceptance criterion: AC1 to AC7 of RWB-E1-007 belong to RWB-P2-E1007-APP, which builds, sends, retries and escalates the file. The six criteria of section 7 are new under D-RCV-60 and test only the document-hub side stated here (GAP-1027; ASM-1951).

##### 2. Business rationale

The outbound file is the largest payload on the outbound path: the WIN registered-mail notice file (INT-14), the debt-buyer data tape (INT-25), the reporting extract that is now delivered to rwb-reporting (legacy INT-19) and the decision and outcome feed that is continuous Kafka ingest in rwb-decision (legacy INT-20). Only one of those is a message-sized fact; the rest are files of many megabytes. The claim-check keeps the bytes off the bus, WORM keeps a legal file from being altered after it is stored, and the retention class of the type fixes how long the evidence is kept. The P5 measure of this path is therefore the document hub's own storage and read, not the transport: a file that is stored once, found by its document ID and read back with the same SHA-256.

The behaviour the business asked for is unchanged; only the seams moved. A file that cannot be built because today's ACE batch is not complete is still held by rwb-integration; a transfer that fails is still retried on the same three attempts and the same 5, 15 and 45 minute intervals; the case still moves to `RETRY_QUEUE` and then `EXCEPTION_QUEUE` and the owner still gets one task. What this slice adds is the place where the built file rests, and it is deliberately narrow: one store, one read pair, one event, no adapter.

Seven realignment changes:

1. One service, one schema: the store and the index move to `rwb_document` (DP-01), and no `recovery` table and no other `rwb_*` schema is read by this slice.
2. One login: the shared `recovery_svc` identity becomes the rwb-document login (DP-02); its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1027; ASM-1959).
3. The claim-check replaces the in-process file hand-off: rwb-integration passes a manifest and follows a SAS link for one file, valid 15 minutes, instead of a file path on a shared folder (Arch v5 slides 8 and 11; ASM-1956).
4. WORM through the platform storage product: the file is written to `rwb-docs-legal` when its type is write-once and to `rwb-docs` otherwise, at `{container}/{caseId}/{documentId}/v1`, through RWB-PLT-TE012-APP (ASM-1957).
5. The document type table is the source of the retention class and the write-once flag: version `DOCTYPE-2026.11` in force, never a value typed in code or taken from the caller.
6. The event is the announcement: `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` is written to the outbox in the store transaction (DP-09) and carries IDs and facts only. No lake copy and no lake row exist (DP-17).
7. The two file statements of the legacy scheduler are retired, not restated: JOB-13 (decision log copy to the lake) is continuous Kafka ingest in rwb-decision and JOB-15 (reporting extract to the lake) is a `deliverFile` request to rwb-reporting (Arch v5 slide 44; DP-17).

##### 3. Preconditions

| Precondition | What it gives this story |
|---|---|
| RWB-P2-E1007-CON | The published contract of the requesting side: the `deliverFile(manifest)` activity with the claim-check manifest (`fileId`, `batchId`, `sha256`, `recordCount`, `interfaceId`, `businessDate`, `caseIds`, `idempotencyKey`, the claim-check link and the requesting service), the OpenAPI shape of the store request, and the `FileDelivered` and `FileFailed` schemas on the rwb-integration topic `rwb.integration.events.v1`. No P2 operation is called by this slice: the contract is what the store request and the manifest must accept |
| RWB-P5-E1024-APP | The store contract of the document hub: `POST /documents`, the Document shape, the error envelope with `messageId`, the `Idempotency-Key` rule and the `copyPending` activity of `DocumentIntakeWorkflow`. This slice builds and tests against it as a fake and lists it in no H dependency (GAP-1027; ASM-1955) |
| RWB-P3-E1018-CON (consumed, not in C) | `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` on `rwb-case`, one hop with a 2 s timeout, so the scope check of the store never reads a case table (DP-11). It is not listed in this slice's contract dependencies in the story JSON (GAP-1027; ASM-1958) |
| RWB-PLT-TE012-APP (no X dependency listed) | The platform storage product: the Blob containers `rwb-docs`, `rwb-docs-legal` and `rwb-quarantine`, the managed identity and the WORM policy. The story JSON lists no external dependency for this slice (GAP-1027; ASM-1957) |

Business preconditions carried from the legacy story, unchanged in value:

- The interface configuration version "IF-2026.11" is in force, with interface rows INT-14 (WIN registered mail), INT-19 (reporting extract), INT-20 (decision and outcome feed) and INT-25 (debt-buyer data tape), each with direction OUTBOUND, max attempts 3 and retry intervals 5, 15 and 45 minutes. This slice reads no interface row: the interface ID and the business date arrive in the store request (DF-OPS-137 to DF-OPS-148 are read through the P2 contract, and no `rwb_integration` row is read by SQL).
- The document type table version "DOCTYPE-2026.11" is in force, with the six types DEMAND_LETTER, COURT_NOTICE, APPRAISAL_REPORT, TITLE_DEED, SETTLEMENT_AGREEMENT and GUARANTOR_NOTICE, each with its retention class and its write-once flag.
- The storage containers `rwb-docs`, `rwb-docs-legal` and `rwb-quarantine` exist in each environment with their immutability policy.
- The rwb-document login (DP-02) holds its grant on `rwb_document` only; the name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1027; ASM-1959).
- The feature flag `rwb.document.outbound-store` is on in the environment; its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1027; ASM-1959).
- The outbound file's document type row and its retention class are data rows of `document_type`. Which type code an outbound interface file is stored under, and therefore which retention class it carries, is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1027; ASM-1954).

The store story of the same lane, RWB-P5-E1024-APP, is earlier in the lane but is not an H dependency in this slice's JSON. This slice therefore tests against the store fake of RWB-P5-E1024-APP and adds no build dependency of its own (GAP-1027; ASM-1955).

##### 4. Flow

1. rwb-integration (`OutboundFileWorkflow`, after `buildOutboundFile`) stores the built file with `POST /api/recovery/document/v1/documents`, a multipart request carrying the file, the document type, the source `GENERATED`, the case ID the request anchors, the interface ID, the business date and the manifest (`fileId`, `batchId`, `sha256`, `recordCount`, the case IDs and the requesting service), with the `Idempotency-Key` header of the `deliverFile` request.
2. `OutboundFileStoreService`: reads the case through the `rwb-case` contract `GET /cases/{caseId}` (one hop, 2 s timeout) and refuses the store when the case is not found or not in scope, so no case table of another service is read (DP-01, DP-11).
3. `DocumentTypeReader`: reads the type row of `document_type` in the version in force (`valid_from` and `valid_to`) and takes the allowed size and file-type rules of the document hub from `document_hub_parameter`, plus the retention class and the write-once flag of the type. Neither value is taken from the caller.
4. `OutboundFileStoreService`: checks the file content signature against the allowed types (PDF, JPG, PNG) and the size against the limit of 25 MB; refuses a file that fails either check before any row is written (X2, X3).
5. `StorageClient`: generates the document ID, then calls the platform storage product RWB-PLT-TE012-APP, which writes the file to `rwb-docs-legal` when the type is write-once and to `rwb-docs` otherwise, at `{container}/{caseId}/{documentId}/v1`. The path is deterministic, so a repeat of the same request writes the same path and the product answers it idempotently; a failed or refused write ends the store here, before any database row.
6. `OutboundFileStoreService`, one transaction in `rwb_document` after the accepted write: inserts the `document` row with source `GENERATED`, `storage_ref`, `content_sha256` from the manifest, `doc_version` 1 and state `STORED`, and writes the `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` row to the outbox (DP-09). The legacy decision record of the store is the DOCATT record of RWB-P5-E1024-APP's library, written in the same transaction (DP-03). A failure here leaves the row and the event absent and the blob unreferenced.
7. `OutboundFileStoreController`: answers the store with the document ID, the storage reference, the SHA-256, the state `STORED`, the retention class and a SAS link for one file valid 15 minutes (ASM-1956).
8. A repeat of the same `Idempotency-Key` returns the document stored by the first call, with no second row and no second event (X5).
9. The requesting flow, or the owner of the case, follows the claim-check with `GET /documents/{documentId}` for the metadata and `GET /documents/{documentId}/content` for the file; the content read returns the same SHA-256 as the manifest, and each read is written to the PII access log by the ACE common module, never by this package.
10. The outbox relay (JOB-11, the platform relay of DP-09) publishes `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` on `rwb.document.events.v1` once per committed store, keyed by `caseId`, with IDs and facts only and no file content.

The case ID the store request anchors is `document.case_id`, which the schema requires; an outbound batch file covers 85 notices on 85 cases, and which case anchors the document row is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1027; ASM-1953). The case IDs of the file travel in the manifest and in the `DocumentStored` payload is only the anchor case.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The document type of the file is not in `document_type` in force, or its retention class cannot be resolved from the type row | The store is refused with 422 before any row, any upload and any outbox row; nothing is stored | MSG-P5-006 | AC4 |
| X2 | The file content is not PDF, JPG or PNG | The store is refused with 415; nothing is written to a container or to a table | MSG-P5-001 | None (inherited from RWB-P5-E1024-APP AC6) |
| X3 | The file is larger than the size limit in force (25 MB, from `document_hub_parameter`) | The store is refused with 413; nothing is stored | MSG-P5-017 | AC4 |
| X4 | The platform storage product RWB-PLT-TE012-APP does not answer, or refuses the write | The store is refused with 503 before the database transaction opens; no document row and no outbox row exist; the retry belongs to the caller (RWB-P2-E1007-APP), which retries the attempt on the intervals of `interface_config` | MSG-GEN-006 naming "Document storage" | AC5 |
| X5 | The same `Idempotency-Key` is presented again | The document stored by the first call is returned; one `document` row and one `DocumentStored` event exist for it | None | AC3 |
| X6 | Two store requests for the same interface, business date and manifest arrive at the same time | One holds the unique key and the other is answered with 409; exactly one row exists | MSG-GEN-004 | AC3 |
| X7 | A read names a document ID that does not exist | 404, with a not-found message whose ID is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1027; ASM-1953) | None (message ID not specified) | None |
| X8 | The claim-check link is used after its lifetime | The link is refused with 403 by the storage product and the reader asks for a new one with `GET /documents/{documentId}`; no second file and no stored copy is created | MSG-P4-002 | AC2 |
| X9 | The `rwb-case` contract does not answer within 2 s, or its breaker is open | The store is refused with 503 before any row; the breaker shields the case service; the retry belongs to the caller | MSG-GEN-006 | AC2, AC5 |
| X10 | A statement of this slice reads a table of another service, a `recovery` table or another `rwb_*` schema | The grant refuses the statement and the architecture boundary test fails the build; the case and the interface facts arrive through their contracts | None (pipeline log) | AC1, AC6 |

The legacy copy-failure path that leaves the row `COPY_PENDING` and retries it on the next intake run (FSD P5 AC-EXC-P5-001-03) is RWB-P5-E1024-APP's `copyPending` activity, not this slice's: X4 is the store refused before any row is left behind, and the caller's retry is the outbound retry ladder of rwb-integration (ASM-1955).

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds on Day 1 against the published rwb-integration contract, the store fake of RWB-P5-E1024-APP, the `rwb-case` contract fake and the storage stub; no in-lane story is waited for |
| Negotiable | The type code of an outbound file, its retention class, the size limit, the container names, the 15-minute window and the interface facts are data rows or properties; the story fixes only the behaviour |
| Valuable | Every outbound file of the Workbench rests once in the document hub under write-once storage and is found and read again by its document ID |
| Estimable | One service slice, three operations, one store transaction, one event, two readers and six criteria |
| Small | One squad, one iteration with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion of section 7 is one automated test against the fakes; the ten legacy cases of section 16 stay with the path |
