###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 new provided, 2 consumed | `POST /api/recovery/document/v1/documents` on rwb-document and `GET /api/recovery/integration/v1/admin/outbound-items` on rwb-integration; one hop, 2 s timeout |
| Kafka | 0 published by this story, 2 consumed | `FileDelivered` and `FileFailed` on `rwb.integration.events.v1` with the inbox dedupe; the decision-record library publishes `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` |
| Temporal | 0 workflows, 2 activities provided, 1 activity consumed | `buildAccessReviewFile` and `requestFileDelivery` on queue `rwb-access`; `deliverFile` on queue `rwb-integration`; the JOB-18 workflow is RWB-P4-AD008-APP's |
| File | 1 delivered file per review cycle | One staging file and one stored document behind the claim-check manifest handed to rwb-integration; no SFTP class, no second copy and no data lake in this package |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access.review`, module `review`, in the service root `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`. The outcome listener sits beside it in `...access.review.event`, and the boundary rule is added to the test source tree of the service.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_access`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-02 | `recovery_svc` login | One login per service | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | ACE facts only through rwb-source-data's contract; this service reads no view | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library, CloudEvents, the owner's topic, retry and `.dlt` | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal activity contract on the service queue through the workflow kit; the Schedule is AD008's | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST and activity contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-16 | `recovery.integration.adapter` | The rwb-integration contract: the `deliverFile` activity, the two events and the admin read | C RWB-P2-E1007-CON |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake); no lake target, no lake file and no lake delivery row | none; gap if the story needed lake data |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**This is a secondary slice: the metadata H row is None and this story adds no build dependency of its own.** The platform contracts behind DP-03, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10 and DP-19 arrive with the `rwb_access` baseline and RWB-P4-E1037-CON, and the one contract dependency, `RWB-P2-E1007-CON` of DP-16, never blocks a build (§R5.4): the activity fake, the admin read fake and the Kafka stubs of 12.8 stand in for rwb-integration on Day 1. DP-05 resolves to a prohibition (no `v_ace_*` view is read here and the boundary rule enforces it), DP-01 to "the four tables and the records are this service's and no other schema is named", DP-17 to "no lake element anywhere in the package", and DP-11 to the inbound budget of the two consumed operations and the one hop of the `deliverFile` call. DP-19 is the route that renders the delivery outcome on the administration screens, which this story does not build.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `AccessReviewRequestAuthoriser` | Service | Resolves the starter identity and the R letter in `REFERENCE_DATA` from `role` and `permission` at the matrix version in force before any extract is read |
| `AccessReviewExtractReader` | Repository | Reads `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule`, `delegation_limit` and the local access entries at the versions in force; reads no other schema |
| `AccessReviewFileBuilder` | Service | Writes the one staging file, computes the sha256 and the record count, takes the file name from the interface row |
| `AccessReviewManifest` | Value | The manifest of BR7: file name, sha256, record count, business date, interface, requesting service and idempotency key |
| `DocumentStoreClient` | Client | `POST /api/recovery/document/v1/documents` on rwb-document, one hop, 2 s; returns the document ID |
| `DeliveryRequestClient` | Client | The one `deliverFile(manifest)` call on task queue `rwb-integration`, typed failures mapped |
| `RequestKeyStore` | Service | Reads and writes the `idempotency_key` object created in `rwb_access`, so one request exists per business date |
| `DeliveryOutcomeListener` | Listener | Consumes `FileDelivered` and `FileFailed`, dedupes in `processed_event`, writes the outcome entry, raises the failure alert |
| `ItemStatusReader` | Client | `GET /api/recovery/integration/v1/admin/outbound-items`, one hop, 2 s |
| `ReviewRecordWriter` | Service | Writes the request and outcome entries through the DP-03 library, first in the transaction; a failed write fails the activity |
| `buildAccessReviewFile`, `requestFileDelivery` | Activities | The two typed activities on queue `rwb-access` |
| `ReviewBoundaryRule` | ArchUnit rule in the test source | BND-6 over the module map: no `v_ace_*` view, no `public` table, no data lake path, no SFTP class and no second file copy |

**Database and migrations.** None. This story creates no table, adds no column and writes no migration: the four tables, `role_conflict` and the library objects are the `rwb_access` baseline and DP-09, and the verdicts of `masking_rule` are another P4 story's rows. The request and outcome entries are rows of the decision-record library in `rwb_access`, and the two library objects (`processed_event`, `idempotency_key`) are created there by the platform library migration.

**Configuration and reference data**

- The interface row of the access-review file: direction OUTBOUND, its `file_pattern`, `data_product`, `owner_role` and `alert_role`, loaded by RW-REFADM at the version in force. Its interface ID and its pattern are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0981; ASM-1717).
- The extract layout and the recipient of the file: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0981; ASM-1717). The layout is declared with the interface row and never in code, and this story fixes only the manifest.
- Lists LOV-CAPABILITY, LOV-ROLE and LOV-SCOPE come from the reference-data contract at the version in force (DP-07); the capability area of the right check, `REFERENCE_DATA`, is one of their values.
- The feature switch is `rwb.access.access-review-file`, read as a parameter: off means `buildAccessReviewFile` refuses and no file, no document and no request exist.
- The login is the rwb-access login (DP-02): Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0981; ASM-1716).

**Build steps**

1. `AccessReviewRequestAuthoriser` with the R-letter check in `REFERENCE_DATA` ordered before every read; tests for AC6.
2. `AccessReviewExtractReader` over the four tables and the access records, with a fixture set that names no ACE view and no other schema; tests for AC2 and the reading half of AC7.
3. `AccessReviewFileBuilder` and `AccessReviewManifest` with the sha256, the record count and the file name from the interface row; tests for AC2.
4. `DocumentStoreClient` with the one store call and the 503 path; tests for AC2 and X3.
5. `RequestKeyStore` and the one-request-per-date path, including the second run of the same date; tests for AC1.
6. `DeliveryRequestClient` and the two activities with the typed failures and the one-hop call on queue `rwb-integration`; tests for AC3.
7. `DeliveryOutcomeListener` with the inbox dedupe, the two entry shapes and the failure alert; tests for AC4, AC5 and AC8.
8. `ItemStatusReader` against the admin-read fake; the read half of AC3.
9. `ReviewBoundaryRule` and the module map with a fixture class on `recovery.v_ace_customer`, the same class on `public.customer`, a class naming a lake path and a class opening an SFTP session; tests for AC7.
10. A contract-fake run of the whole path, so the story builds before RWB-P4-AD008-APP and rwb-integration are live.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.access.access-review-file`, read as a parameter; off refuses the build of the extract and leaves the boundary rules and the right check in force.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, one request exists per review date under the key, one document is stored and one `deliverFile` call is made per cycle, each outcome writes one entry and a redelivery writes none, the build is green and red on the four boundary fixtures, and a session as the rwb-access login holds no privilege on any of the 30 views and none in `public`.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | The token holds no Workbench role | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The starter's roles carry no R letter in capability area `REFERENCE_DATA` | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written, so the request is not made | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | rwb-document or the `deliverFile` activity is unavailable and the step is retried | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P2-001 | Produced by rwb-integration when its item moves to the exception queue; read here, never produced | The {interface} file {file} was not sent after {count} attempts. It is in the exception queue. |
| Build log | A class names a `v_ace_*` view, a `public` table, a lake path or an SFTP session | Boundary rule BND-6 broken: {class} names {object}. A recovery class names no ACE view, no public table, no lake and no SFTP endpoint. |
| Alert | A `FileFailed` outcome is consumed for a request of this cycle | The {interface} access-review file for {businessDate} was not delivered: {lastError}. |

For MSG-P4-002 in this story, {action} names the action the role tried, for example "request the access-review file", and never a row of the extract. The alert text and its identifier are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0981; ASM-1717) and are owned by RWB-P2-E1007-OPS through the alert role of the interface row; the delivery itself is never re-sent from here. No new `MSG-` identifier is introduced by this story.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen is built by this story. The delivery outcome is read on the administration screens served by the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) — SCR-43 Roles and access for the review rows and the versions they were built from, and the interface and job monitor for the file state — and those screens, their fields and their states belong to their own stories. This story supplies the request entry, the outcome entry and the item status the screens read, and it renders nothing: the review file is a file, not a screen, and its layout and recipient are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0981; ASM-1717).

| State | What the reader sees through the owner's contract |
|---|---|
| Requested | One request entry for the business date and the item in PENDING on the rwb-integration admin read |
| Delivered | One outcome entry with action `delivered`, the document ID, the sha256 and the record count |
| Failed | One outcome entry with action `failed`, the attempt count and the last error code, and the item in the rwb-integration exception queue with its owner task |
| Repeated | The same view as the first outcome, with the inbox hit count raised and no second entry |

| TC-E1-007-07 | AC4, AC8, BR12, BR15 | Component | One `FileDelivered` and one `FileFailed`, each sent twice with the same CloudEvents id; hit count 2 and no second entry |
| TC-E1-007-08 | AC1, BR8 | Component | Two runs for the same review date; one document, one `deliverFile` call and one request entry |
| TC-E1-007-09 | None here (the resend and the exception-queue surface are RWB-P2-E1007-APP's and RWB-P2-E1007-CON's) | Integration | The resend fixture of the rwb-integration admin fake; this story only re-reads the item status, and the resend changes nothing here |
| TC-E1-007-05 | None (retired with the inbound file load; the behaviour is ACE ingestion and EV-27 AceDataLate) | End to end | The legacy inbound case "file missing at the cut-off"; carried as a reference row only and not run by this story |
| TC-E1-007-06 | None (retired with the inbound file load; the behaviour is ACE ingestion) | End to end | The legacy inbound case "same file delivered twice"; carried as a reference row only and not run by this story |

The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID. Legacy levels map System to End to end, Access to Component and Resilience to NFR. Every legacy test case of this key is listed above with the slice of the behaviour this story answers: TC-E1-007-10 answers the access refusal on the request that this service now owns; TC-E1-007-01 answers the one-pattern rule at the requester boundary, the pattern itself being RWB-P2-E1007-APP's; TC-E1-007-02 answers the ACE boundary as a prohibition, because this service reads no view at all; TC-E1-007-03, TC-E1-007-04 and TC-E1-007-09 answer the retry ladder, the held request and the resend, which are rwb-integration's and are run by RWB-P2-E1007-APP and RWB-ITG-E1007-ITG; TC-E1-007-07 and TC-E1-007-08 answer the duplicate outcome and the single request, which this slice does own; and TC-E1-007-05 and TC-E1-007-06 stay as retired legacy IDs. The `-ITG` copies of these cases are not here — they belong to RWB-ITG-E1007-ITG, which proves the file path across the real services.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the interface ID, the file pattern, the layout, the data product, the owner and alert roles, the review date, the matrix, masking and limit versions and the feature switch are rows and parameters read at run time.
- No personal data in events, logs, workflow inputs, manifests, tests or prompts: the manifest carries a file name, a sha256, a count and a date, and the entries carry identifiers, codes and counts; file content is never logged.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `v_ace_*` views — and this service reads neither: a class that names a view fails the build, and the masking rows name a field ID only.
- No cross-schema read and no cross-schema key: `rwb_access` holds no foreign key into another schema and no copy of an item, a document or a case row; `outbound_item`, `interface_config` and `outbox_delivery` are reached only through the rwb-integration admin operation (DP-01).
- No SFTP class, no file-system transport and no second copy of the bytes in this package: the only transport of the bytes is rwb-document and the only transport to the party is rwb-integration's transport component (DP-16).
- No data lake: no lake path, no lake file, no lake delivery row and no lake element in any document of this story (DP-17).
- One request per business date under one key; a second request for the same date is a defect even when it is harmless.
- The record comes first: a request that cannot be recorded is not made, and an outcome that cannot be recorded fails the listener rather than being dropped (R-UNI-39).
- One hop, no chaining: the two activities never call a downstream of a downstream, and the breaker and bulkhead are per downstream.
- No new table, no migration and no `Schedule`: a story that adds one of them has left this slice.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-007 for rwb-integration. The legacy story assumed the SFTP outbound folders existed in DEV and SIT with credentials in the key store, and it assumed one identity with SELECT on the ACE views. On the infrastructure side this story replaces both assumptions with provisioned resources: two MFT/SFTP egress endpoints with exchanged PGP keys, the key-store layout for the credentials and certificates, the firewall and DNS rules, the file staging area and the claim-check storage, the size and timeout budgets, the no-inbound-listener rule, the network zones and the observability hooks the transfer emits. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As an **infrastructure engineer**, I want **the outbound egress of rwb-integration provisioned as infrastructure — the WIN endpoint (INT-14) and the debt-buyer endpoint (INT-25) over MFT/SFTP with exchanged PGP keys, the credentials and certificates in the key store behind workload identity with a rotation runbook, the firewall and DNS rules that admit the named receivers only, the file staging area and the claim-check storage, the enforced file-size and transfer-timeout budgets, no inbound listener and no inbound folder, the network zones and the observability hooks of the transfer**, so that **the app and operations stories of this key can send a real file over a real endpoint from Day 1, with nothing listening inward and no secret or partner credential in code, configuration or a values file**.

The legacy story had one paragraph for this work: "the SFTP outbound folders exist in DEV and SIT, with credentials in the key store (NFR-052)" and "the recovery service identity holds its Entra ID managed identity in each environment and SELECT on `recovery.v_ace_*` only". Both statements are wrong under D-RCV-60 in a way that matters. The views are read only by rwb-source-data (ADR-010), so no grant and no network path to ACE is provisioned for this service here; and the outbound path leaves the cluster through an MFT/SFTP endpoint with a PGP key per receiver (Arch v5 slides 7, 8 and 11), not through a folder that happens to exist. This story provisions the endpoint, the key, the route, the staging area and the budgets, and it proves that nothing listens inward.

The story is also where the split is enforced at the network layer. No inbound listener, no inbound folder, no pickup rule and no sign-off exist, because the Workbench loads no source data (D-RCV-35 U1; BR9 of the app story); the `receiveFile` activity is published in the contract and called by no flow. And no data-lake route, endpoint or landing container is provisioned, because the data lake is removed (DP-17): the reporting extract leaves as a `deliverFile` call to rwb-reporting and the decision feed is Kafka inside the cluster.

##### 2. Business rationale

Two files leave the bank on this path: the WIN registered-mail notice file daily at 16:00 (INT-14) and the debt-buyer data tape per awarded lot (INT-25), both over MFT/SFTP with PGP for a party outside the bank (Arch v5 slides 8, 11, 16 and 32). Neither can leave without a provisioned endpoint, an exchanged key, a routed network and a place to stage the file while the claim-check link is valid. Zero trust requires that every one of them is reachable only over a private path, by an identity, with the key in the key store and never in configuration (Arch v5 slide 35; NFR-052, NFR-053).

The prices of not doing this on Day 1 are concrete. An endpoint created ad hoc in SIT cannot be promoted, so the release date slips by a change request per environment. A credential copied into a values file becomes a security finding, and rotating it becomes a rebuild. A staging area that is shared with the document store breaks the claim-check rule, because a second service could read a file it is not entitled to. A missing size budget turns a malformed file into a transfer that hangs until the SFTP server closes it, and the retry ladder burns its three attempts on a cause that is not a transfer failure. Each of these is prevented by a provisioned value, not by code.

The two windows are the bank's, not this story's: the bank Airflow opens the WIN window at 16:00 and the debt-buyer window per lot, and rwb-integration still builds and sends the files (Arch v5 slides 16, 32 and 44). This story therefore provisions the transport and the route and registers no Schedule; the deployment, the alerts and the windows belong to RWB-P2-E1007-OPS.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The platform subscription, the resource group and the network (virtual network, subnets, private DNS zones) of the environment are available.
- The AKS cluster of the ACE platform is reachable from the rwb-recovery namespace, with the workload identity of rwb-integration registered, so access is bound to an identity and not to a shared credential.
- The platform key store of the environment exists with its access policy (RWB-PLT-N012-INF provisions the standard Blob, key store and MFT/SFTP resources; this story consumes them for the two outbound interfaces).
- The rwb-document claim-check store exists and issues a SAS link for one file for 15 minutes with a manifest of fileId, batchId, sha256 and record count (Arch v5 slide 11).
- The bank MFT team has named the receiver-side contact and the key-exchange procedure for WIN and for the debt-buyer buyers, and the endpoint hosts and ports are known to the network team.
- The contract of this key is published (RWB-P2-E1007-CON): the manifest, the two events and the two activities fix what a transfer carries and what it reports.
- No build dependency and no contract dependency in the plan of this key; this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7). The two values it needs from the contract are read from RWB-P2-E1007-CON when it is published and do not block the provisioning.

##### 4. Flow

1. List the two outbound interfaces and what each needs: the WIN endpoint (INT-14) and the debt-buyer endpoint (INT-25) per awarded lot, the PGP key of each receiver, the file pattern of each interface row and the staging location.
2. Provision the MFT/SFTP egress endpoints in each environment, one per receiver, with the account, the folder, the permissions and the transfer mode fixed by the interface row of `interface_config`.
3. Exchange the PGP keys with each receiver, record the key identifier and the fingerprint against the endpoint, and confirm the receiver's public key and the bank's key pair.
4. Put the credentials, the private keys and the certificates in the key store of the environment and bind each entry to the rwb-integration workload identity; write a rotation runbook for the credential, the certificate and the PGP key.
5. Apply the network rules: egress only to the named receiver ranges and ports, private DNS for the endpoint names, no public inbound rule on any of them, and TLS on the cluster side.
6. Provision the file staging area of the environment and confirm that the claim-check rule holds: one file per link, 15 minutes, manifest with fileId, batchId, sha256 and record count, and no file content in a queue.
7. Set the enforced budgets as environment values: the maximum file size, the transfer timeout, the connection and read timeouts, the concurrent transfer limit and the retry classification of a timeout as a transfer failure.
8. Confirm that nothing listens inward: no inbound listener, no inbound port, no inbound folder and no pickup or sign-off rule on either endpoint.
9. Wire the observability hooks: the endpoint health, the transfer attempt, the byte count, the checksum result, the failure class and the OpenTelemetry trace context, with no file name carrying personal data.
10. Hand the endpoint references, the key identifiers, the staging path and the budgets to the app and operations stories and run the four tests of section 16.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A receiver's PGP key does not match the key used to encrypt the file | The transfer is refused before any clear file leaves the bank and the attempt fails as a transfer failure | MSG-P2-E1007-INF-03 | AC2, AC5 |
| X2 | A credential or certificate has expired or is rotated out | The transfer fails closed, the endpoint health reports not ready and the rotation runbook restores the version; no clear-text fallback exists | MSG-P2-E1007-INF-02 | AC2 |
| X3 | A connection is attempted from outside the allow-list, or inward to the endpoint | The network rule refuses the connection before authentication; the refusal is logged and no listener answers | None | AC3, AC6 |
| X4 | The file exceeds the maximum size, or the transfer exceeds the timeout | The transfer is aborted and counted as a transfer failure, so it follows the retry ladder of the app story; the file is never truncated and never sent twice | MSG-P2-E1007-INF-03 | AC6 |
| X5 | The claim-check link has expired when the transfer starts | The request is refused with 403 and no partial read; the attempt fails and the next attempt asks rwb-document for a new link | MSG-P2-E1007-INF-04 | AC4 |
| X6 | The staging area holds a file whose sha256 does not match the manifest | The transfer is refused and the failure is reported with the checksum mismatch, never with a partial file | MSG-P2-E1007-INF-03 | AC4 |
| X7 | A second interface is configured against the same endpoint with a different key or folder | The configuration check fails the change, because one endpoint answers one receiver and one key | None | AC1 |
| X8 | A values file, a script or a runbook carries a secret | The secret scan fails the change and the value is moved to the key store | None | AC2 |

Message identifiers MSG-P2-E1007-INF-01 to MSG-P2-E1007-INF-04 are the infrastructure validation messages of section 14; the business messages of the app story are unchanged and the file failure signal itself is `FileFailed` on `rwb.integration.events.v1`.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Provisions two endpoints, the keys, the routes, the staging area and the budgets; no application code and no dependency on a service build |
| Negotiable | Endpoint hosts, ports, folders, key identifiers, firewall ranges, staging names, the size limit and the timeouts are environment values settled with the MFT and network teams; the resource types and their rules are fixed by the architecture |
| Valuable | Gives the app and operations stories a real endpoint, a real key and a real route on Day 1, with nothing listening inward and no secret in configuration |
| Estimable | Two endpoints, one key-store layout, one network rule set, one staging area, one budget set, one rotation runbook and four test areas |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the runbook and the tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against a provisioned resource, a refused connection, a refused transfer or a scan, never against a business outcome |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Outbound egress for rwb-integration

  Background:
    Given the platform subscription, the resource group and the private network of the environment are in place
    Given the two outbound interfaces are INT-14 WIN registered mail and INT-25 debt buyer tape
    Given the target environment is SIT

  Scenario: AC1 The two egress endpoints exist and nothing listens inward (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the MFT/SFTP resources of the environment
    Then the WIN endpoint for INT-14 exists with its account, folder and transfer mode
    Then the debt-buyer endpoint for INT-25 exists and serves one awarded lot per transfer
    Then each endpoint is bound to exactly one receiver and one key
    Then no inbound listener, inbound port, inbound folder or pickup rule exists on either endpoint
    Then the service holds no grant on the recovery schema and no network route to an ACE view
    Then no data-lake target and no lake landing container is provisioned

  Scenario: AC2 The keys and the credentials live in the key store and rotate under a runbook (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the key store of the environment
    Then the credentials, the private keys and the certificates of both endpoints are held there and bound to the rwb-integration workload identity
    Then each PGP key is recorded with its identifier and fingerprint and matches the receiver's key
    Then a secret scan of the configuration, the scripts and the values finds no secret
    When a credential or a certificate reaches its rotation point
    Then the rotation runbook stages the new version, switches the endpoint and retires the previous version
    Then a transfer with an expired credential fails closed and no clear-text fallback is used

  Scenario: AC3 The route to each receiver is private and allow-listed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the network rules of the environment
    Then egress is admitted to the named receiver ranges and ports only
    Then the endpoint names resolve through private DNS
    Then traffic in transit uses TLS on the cluster side
    Then no public inbound rule exists on either endpoint
    When a connection arrives from outside the allow-list
    Then it is refused before authentication and logged

  Scenario: AC4 The staging area and the claim-check storage hold one file per link (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the file staging area of the environment
    Then a built file is staged with its manifest of fileId, batchId, sha256 and record count
    Then the claim-check link answers one file for 15 minutes and no other
    When the link is used after 15 minutes
    Then the request is refused with 403 and MSG-P2-E1007-INF-04
    Then a staged file whose sha256 does not match the manifest is refused with MSG-P2-E1007-INF-03
    Then no file content is placed on a queue, a topic or a workflow input

  Scenario: AC5 The transfer emits its observability hooks with the trace context (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the observability configuration of the environment
    When one file is transferred and one transfer fails
    Then the endpoint health, the transfer attempt, the byte count, the checksum result and the failure class are emitted
    Then each signal carries the environment, the interface ID and the OpenTelemetry trace context
    Then no signal carries a file content, an address or an identity number
    Then the failed transfer is visible before the app story raises FileFailed

  Scenario: AC6 The size and timeout budgets are enforced as environment values (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the budget set of the environment
    Then the maximum file size, the transfer timeout, the connection and read timeouts and the concurrent transfer limit are set as values and not in code
    Then a file above the maximum size is refused and counted as a transfer failure
    Then a transfer that exceeds the timeout is aborted and counted as a transfer failure
    Then the exact values are not in the source documents and are carried as GAP-0649 until the MFT team sets them
    Then the retry ladder of the interface row is the only retry and the infrastructure adds none
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The two outbound interfaces leave the bank over MFT/SFTP with PGP: INT-14 WIN registered mail daily at 16:00 and INT-25 debt buyers per awarded lot | Arch v5 slides 8, 11, 16 and 32 |
| BR2 | One endpoint answers one receiver and one key; the credentials, private keys and certificates live in the key store and are never in code, configuration, a values file or a runbook | NFR-052; Arch v5 slide 35; legacy RWB-E1-007 precondition |
| BR3 | Nothing listens inward: no inbound listener, no inbound port, no inbound folder and no pickup or sign-off rule, because rwb-integration has no inbound adapter | D-RCV-35 U1; ADR-010; FSD P2 v3 A1.6; app story BR9 |
| BR4 | Every endpoint is reachable only over a private route, with private DNS and an allow-list limited to the named receivers | Arch v5 slide 35; zero trust |
| BR5 | A file is staged with its manifest and its sha256, the claim-check link answers one file for 15 minutes, and no file content travels on a message | Arch v5 slide 11 |
| BR6 | The file-size limit, the transfer timeout and the concurrency limit are environment values, enforced by the transport, and a violation is a transfer failure that follows the interface retry ladder | Arch v5 slide 11; ASM-1083 |
| BR7 | No ACE grant and no ACE network path is provisioned for this service: only rwb-source-data reads the thirty `recovery.v_ace_*` views | Arch v5 slides 8, 9 and 29; ADR-010; DP-05 |
| BR8 | No data-lake endpoint, route or landing container is provisioned, because the data lake is removed | DP-17; Arch v5 slides 2 and 37 |
| BR9 | The observability of the transfer carries counts, identifiers, the interface, the environment and the trace context only, never a file content, an address or an identity number | ADR-023; CTL-11 |
| BR10 | This story provisions transport and route only: it registers no Schedule, holds no business value and builds no file | Arch v5 slides 16, 32 and 44; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |

##### 9. State transitions

Endpoint lifecycle.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Requested | Provisioning approved | The receiver, the folder, the key and the route are known | Provisioned |
| Provisioned | Key exchanged and access bound | The PGP key matches the receiver and the workload identity is bound | In use |
| In use | Rotation started | The credential, the certificate or the key reaches its rotation point | Rotating |
| Rotating | Previous version retired | No staged file and no running workflow depends on the earlier version | In use |
| In use | Endpoint suspended | The receiver asks for a stop or a security event is open | Suspended |
| Suspended | Endpoint resumed | The cause is cleared and the route is re-checked | In use |
| In use | Decommission approved | The interface is retired and no staged file remains | Retired |

File row.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Staged | Manifest written | fileId, batchId, sha256 and record count are recorded by the app story | Ready to transfer |
| Ready to transfer | Transfer started | The claim-check link is valid and the endpoint is in use | Transferring |
| Transferring | Transfer completed | The bytes arrive and the receiver confirms | Delivered to receiver |
| Transferring | Size, timeout, checksum or key check failed | Any budget or key check fails | Failed |
| Failed | Operator retry | The cause is cleared and the next attempt starts from the retry ladder | Transferring |
| Delivered to receiver | Link expired | The 15 minutes elapse | Cleared |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| SCB IT infrastructure | Owns the story, the two endpoints, the network rules, the staging area and the two runbooks |
| Bank MFT team | Owns the MFT service, the receiver agreements, the key ceremony and the transfer logs; this story records the key identifier and the fingerprint |
| Platform team | Owns the key store, the workload identity binding and the private DNS zone |
| Security | Owns the access policy, the rotation requirement and the secret scan; approves a relaxation of the allow-list |
| rwb-integration owner | Consumes the endpoint references, the key identifiers and the budgets; owns the file build and the retry ladder |
| rwb-document owner | Issues the claim-check link and owns the claim-check store |
| Data steward | Confirms that no file name, manifest or log line carries personal data |
| Audit (RW-AUDIT) | Reads the transfer trail and the key-rotation trail |

The endpoint names, the accounts, the folders, the key identifiers, the receiver ranges, the staging names, the file-size limit, the timeouts and the rotation period are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0649; ASM-1083, ASM-1084).

| Budgets | Maximum file size, transfer timeout, connection and read timeouts, concurrent transfer limit, all as environment values; a violation is a transfer failure | Arch v5 slide 11; GAP-0649 |
| Observability hooks | Endpoint health, transfer attempt, byte count, checksum result, failure class and the OpenTelemetry trace context; no file content and no personal data | ADR-023 |
| Absent by design | No inbound listener, no inbound folder, no pickup rule, no sign-off, no ACE grant, no ACE network route, no data-lake endpoint | D-RCV-35 U1; ADR-010; DP-17 |

The names, numbers and addresses of the table above are environment values of the resource files in section 13; they are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0649; ASM-1083) and this story fixes only their shape and the rule that no value is written in code.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. The infrastructure calls no service operation; the app story's transport calls rwb-document and rwb-source-data at run time and the endpoint references of this story are injected into the chart by RWB-P2-E1007-OPS.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. `rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1` and `rwb.integration.FileFailed.v1` are published by the app story on `rwb.integration.events.v1`; this story emits no event and holds no outbox.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The only subscription of the service is `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` and it belongs to the app story.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. No workflow, no activity and no task queue is registered by this story; `deliverFile(manifest)` and `receiveFile` are the app story's and run on queue `rwb-integration`.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The WIN window at 16:00 and the debt-buyer window per lot belong to the bank Airflow and the container of the release to RWB-P2-E1007-OPS; this story registers no Schedule and no timer.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. `interface_config`, `outbound_item` and `job_catalog` are the app story's tables in `rwb_integration` and this story creates no table, no column and no grant; it provisions no ACE view, because only rwb-source-data reads them (DP-05).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

None. The endpoint test uses a receiver stub on the MFT/SFTP side, which is a test double of the infrastructure and not a contract fake; the contract fakes of the consumed services are RWB-P2-E1007-CON's.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | None | No operation is provided or consumed by the infrastructure |
| Kafka | None | No topic is produced or consumed; the two events belong to the app story |
| Temporal | None | No workflow and no activity; the codec and the mTLS material come from the platform |
| File | 2 outbound interfaces | INT-14 WIN registered mail and INT-25 debt buyer tape over MFT/SFTP with PGP; one file per 15-minute SAS link with its manifest; no inbound interface and no data lake |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** `infra/mft/endpoints.yaml` (the two endpoints, their accounts, their folders, the file patterns and the transfer mode), `infra/security/keys.yaml` (the key-store entries, the workload identity bindings, the PGP key identifiers and fingerprints), `infra/network/rules.yaml` (the private DNS records, the egress allow-list, the TLS settings and the absence of a public inbound rule), `infra/storage/staging.yaml` (the staging area, its access rule and its clearing rule), `infra/mft/budgets.yaml` (the size and timeout set of BR6), `runbooks/key-rotation.md` (credential, certificate and PGP rotation, version retention, break-glass) and `runbooks/file-transfer.md` (staging, manifest, checksum, failure and re-delivery).

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | The staging area and the key store hold no table copy and no ACE row; the schema `rwb_integration` is not touched | none |
| DP-02 | `recovery_svc` login | One login and one workload identity per service; the credential of rwb-integration is its own and lives in the key store | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | No decision record is written by the infrastructure; the library of the app story publishes it | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON (of the app story) |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | No ACE grant and no route to an ACE view is provisioned for this service | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | The file patterns and the folders come from the `interface_config` rows and never from a resource file | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON (of the app story) |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | No topic, no outbox and no inbox is provisioned here; the platform chart does it | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON (of the app story) |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | No Schedule and no worker is provisioned here; the two windows are the bank's | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON (of the app story) |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | No REST call is made by the infrastructure; the 2 s budget is a value of the app story's client | none |
| DP-16 | `recovery.integration.adapter` | The endpoint serves the rwb-integration contract; it declares no path and no operation of its own | C RWB-P2-E1007-CON |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | No lake endpoint, route or landing container is provisioned | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | No screen and no route is provisioned for the infrastructure; SCR-09 is the edge's | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON (of the app story) |

The H dependencies of the table are the app story's and are not carried by this story, whose plan holds no build dependency; they are listed to show where each pattern resolves.

**Build steps**

1. Write the endpoint inventory: the two interfaces, their receiver, their account, their folder, their file pattern and their transfer mode.
2. Provision the two endpoints in each environment and bind each to one receiver and one key.
3. Exchange the PGP keys, record the identifier and the fingerprint, and confirm the receiver's key.
4. Place the credentials, the private keys and the certificates in the key store and bind them to the rwb-integration workload identity.
5. Apply the private DNS records, the egress allow-list and the TLS settings of the environment, and run the public-access scan that proves no inbound rule answers on either endpoint.
6. Provision the staging area and the claim-check storage rule with the 15-minute single-file link, its access rule and its clearing rule.
7. Set the size and timeout budgets as environment values and classify a violation as a transfer failure.
8. Wire the observability hooks and the endpoint health signal with the trace context and no personal data.
9. Publish the two runbooks and hand the endpoint references, the key identifiers, the staging path and the budgets to the app and operations stories.

**Configuration.** The endpoint host, port, account, folder, key identifier, receiver range, staging name, maximum file size, transfer timeout, connection and read timeouts and concurrency limit are values of the environment files. None of them is in code, and none is in a values file that is committed with a secret (NFR-052).

**Done when.** Both endpoints are provisioned in the environment, no public inbound rule answers on either, a PGP transfer completes with a verified sha256, a mismatched key and an oversized file are refused with the documented message, the staging area clears after the link expires, a secret scan finds nothing, and both runbooks are reviewed by the security and on-call roles.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P2-E1007-INF-01 | An endpoint is requested with no receiver, no key or a second receiver on one endpoint | This endpoint needs one receiver and one key. |
| MSG-P2-E1007-INF-02 | A credential, a certificate or a PGP key has expired or is rotated out | The endpoint credential has expired. Follow the rotation runbook. |
| MSG-P2-E1007-INF-03 | The size, timeout, checksum or PGP check fails | The file could not be transferred: the integrity check failed. |
| MSG-P2-E1007-INF-04 | The claim-check link has expired | This link has expired. Ask for a new link to the document. |

The four messages are the infrastructure texts of this story and are new; no legacy business message is renumbered or reworded by them. A refused transfer is reported to the operator through the transfer hooks of AC5 and, at run time, through `FileFailed` of the app story.

##### 15. Screens and states

None — the infrastructure has no screen of its own. The transfer status is read by the app story's SCR-09 Exception queue and by the dashboards of RWB-P2-E1007-OPS; the endpoint health signal of AC5 is what the operations story alerts on.

| TC ID | Covers | Level | Data |
|---|---|---|---|
| TC-P2-E1007-INF-01 | AC1 | Integration | Both endpoints provisioned in SIT; a second receiver on one endpoint refused; no inbound listener, no inbound folder and no ACE route found |
| TC-P2-E1007-INF-02 | AC2 | NFR | Keys and certificates in the key store with a workload identity binding; a secret scan clean; a rotation cycled; an expired credential fails closed |
| TC-P2-E1007-INF-03 | AC3 | NFR | Egress admitted to the named ranges only; a connection from outside refused and logged; private DNS resolves; no public inbound rule |

| TC-P2-E1007-INF-05 | AC5 | Integration | One successful and one failed transfer; every hook emitted with the environment, the interface and the trace context; no personal data in any signal |
| TC-P2-E1007-INF-06 | AC6 | NFR | A file above the maximum size and a transfer past the timeout are refused as transfer failures; no infrastructure retry is added |

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a resource file: the file patterns, the folders, the attempt limits and the retry intervals stay `interface_config` rows, never a literal in the infrastructure.
- No personal data in a file name, a manifest, a log, a trace attribute or an alert: identifiers, counts and hashes only.
- No secret in code, configuration, a values file, a script or a runbook; every credential is read with the workload identity (NFR-052, BR2).
- Nothing listens inward: no inbound listener, no inbound port, no inbound folder and no pickup rule on either endpoint (BR3).
- No ACE grant and no ACE network path for this service; only rwb-source-data reads the views (BR7).
- No data-lake endpoint, route or landing container (BR8).
- The private route and the allow-list are mandatory on both endpoints; a public inbound rule is a release blocker.
- Every transfer is PGP protected and every receipt is checked against the manifest and the sha256 (BR5).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-007 for rwb-integration. The legacy story assumed a shared Quartz scheduler that ran JOB-10, JOB-11, JOB-13 and JOB-15, a shared database that held every table, and an exception queue that an operator could see by opening the database. This story deploys the outbound-file capability of rwb-integration: one chart and values, the Flyway baseline of `rwb_integration`, the topic and the task queue with retry and `.dlt`, the two Airflow file windows that are not Schedules, the held and failed file alerts, the dashboards and the runbook. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform engineer**, I want **the rwb-integration outbound-file capability deployed as one Helm release with its values files, its per-service Flyway baseline in `rwb_integration`, its topic and task queue with retry and `.dlt`, its worker scaling on the queue backlog, the WIN 16:00 and per-lot buyer windows carried by the bank Airflow and not by a Schedule, the held-file and failed-file alerts, the dashboards and the runbook**, so that **an operator can see a file that was held or that stopped moving, resend it, and prove that nothing was lost between an outbound request and a party outside the bank without reading code or opening a database**.

The legacy story ran the adapter behind a shared Quartz scheduler and a shared schema: JOB-10 built the WIN file at 16:00, JOB-11 sent due items every minute, and JOB-13 and JOB-15 copied two files to a data lake. In the target that picture splits in three. JOB-10's window is opened by the bank's Airflow, which calls the requesting service and never a `rwb_*` schema; the file is still built and sent by rwb-integration (Arch v5 slides 16, 32 and 44). JOB-11 is the platform outbox relay that runs every minute in every service. JOB-13 and JOB-15 are removed with the data lake: the reporting extract is a `deliverFile` request from rwb-reporting and the decision and outcome feed is continuous Kafka ingest in rwb-decision (DP-17). What is left for this story is a deployment, a topic, a queue, two windows it does not own, four alert rules and a runbook.

Deployment is also where the split is enforced operationally. The release carries the rwb-integration login only, migrates `rwb_integration` only, publishes on its own topic only and subscribes to `rwb.source-data.events.v1` only. It provisions no ACE grant, no view and no data-lake route: an operator cannot reach an ACE fact or a lake file from this deployment, because neither exists in it (DP-01, DP-02, DP-05, DP-17). The observability follows ADR-023 per service: six series, four alerts and five runbook entries, each alert carrying a message identifier and one runbook entry.

##### 2. Business rationale

The business measure of this legacy key is "outbound items in the exception queue over one day: zero". A deployment is what makes that measure visible: a held file, a parked item, a retry that keeps failing and a topic that falls behind are all failures that no unit test can see, and all of them are silent unless the release emits them. The busiest hour of this service is 16:00, when the letter window opens and rwb-comms requests the WIN file; the buyer tape arrives per awarded lot and can land at any hour (Arch v5 slides 32 and 33). Both are visible only if the queue, the items and the events are instrumented.

The split changes what an operator does. In the legacy story the operator opened the exception queue in the same database and restarted the Quartz job. In the target the operator reads SCR-09 through the edge, resends an item or a delivery through the admin operation, and checks three things: that the worker polls `rwb-integration`, that the item's next attempt is in the future and moving, and that `FileDelivered` or `FileFailed` reached the requesting service. The runbook is written for that sequence, and the alerts are wired to it, because the difference between a busy hour and an incident is whether the operator has to guess which of the three failed.

The story also carries the retirement explicitly. No Schedule is registered for the two windows, no lake target is provisioned, and no inbound consumer exists: the deployment would fail its own checks if it created one, because the topic list, the migration target and the queue subscription are all fixed by the release checklist (BR1, BR2, BR12).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template, the chart skeleton and the pipeline are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-LIB).
- The Kafka event platform provides `rwb.integration.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and the ACLs of this service's principals (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON; DP-09, DP-14).
- The Temporal workflow kit and the namespace `rwb-recovery` exist, with worker versioning, the build ID provider and the payload codec (RWB-PLT-WF, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON; DP-10).
- The per-service Flyway sequence and the migration conventions of `rwb_integration` are published (RWB-PLT-E1044-CON; DP-15).
- The platform error envelope and the message catalogue are in force, so an alert can carry a message identifier.
- The three environments DEV, SIT and UAT exist and the production namespace exists for the release date; the feature flag `rwb.integration.file-adapters` exists in the platform flag library.
- The two MFT/SFTP endpoints, the keys and the staging area exist in each environment (RWB-P2-E1007-INF).
- The gateway-bff composite route for SCR-09 is published (RWB-PLT-N001-CON; DP-19).
- The bank Airflow owns the WIN window at 16:00 and the debt-buyer window per lot and calls the services through their APIs only (Arch v5 slides 16, 32 and 44; ASM-1074).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7). The baseline it deploys is RWB-P2-E1007-APP's and the values it injects are RWB-P2-E1007-INF's; both are declared before the release and neither blocks the chart work.

##### 4. Flow

1. The pipeline builds the service image and the contract jar, runs the unit, component and contract tests, scans the image and the dependencies, and publishes one chart version.
2. The chart deploys the API deployment and the worker deployment with the rwb-integration login, the namespace `rwb-recovery`, the task queue `rwb-integration`, the codec, the build ID of the release and the endpoint references of RWB-P2-E1007-INF.
3. The worker scaling step enables KEDA on the queue backlog of `rwb-integration`, so the back grows with the 16:00 window and the per-lot buyer tape and the front stays at its fixed replica count.
4. The migration step applies the `rwb_integration` sequence of the release, starting with the V0001 baseline of the three P2 tables and the library objects, and refuses to run when the target schema is not `rwb_integration`.
5. The topic step creates or verifies `rwb.integration.events.v1` with its partitions, its replication factor, its retention, its retry topics at 1 minute, 10 minutes and 1 hour and its `.dlt` topic, and records the ACL of the producer and of the requesting services' consumer groups.
6. The window step confirms that the WIN window at 16:00 and the debt-buyer window per lot are opened by the bank Airflow, that the deployment registers no Schedule for either, and that the interface row of each environment holds the file pattern and the folder.
7. The flag step sets `rwb.integration.file-adapters` from the values of the environment.
8. The dashboards are published with the six series and the environment, release and build ID as dimensions.
9. The four alerts are wired to their message identifiers and to their runbook entries: MSG-P2-001 for a parked item, `FileFailed` for a failed file, the held-item series for a held file, and the identifier the Error and Message Standard has yet to name for the topic lag, carried as Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0650; ASM-1085).
10. A smoke step in DEV requests one synthetic INT-14 file for a synthetic business date, follows it to ACKNOWLEDGED against the MFT stub, forces one transfer failure to EXCEPTION with `FileFailed`, resends it through the admin operation, and confirms that no second file exists and that the environment is restored.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The chart render or the migration job fails | The deployment stays unready and the pipeline stops; no traffic, no offset and no migration is left half applied | None | AC1 |
| X2 | The migration step is pointed at a schema other than `rwb_integration` | The step refuses and the release stops | None | AC1 |
| X3 | A consumer group of `rwb.integration.events.v1` lags past its threshold | The lag series rises and the lag alert fires; the runbook entry names the group, the topic and the partition | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0650; ASM-1085) | AC2, AC4 |
| X4 | The feature flag is off in an environment | No worker is deployed, the queue holds no poller and `deliverFile` refuses, so no item and no file exist | None | AC1 |
| X5 | A transfer fails on its last allowed attempt | The item is EXCEPTION, `FileFailed` is published and the failed-file alert fires with MSG-P2-001 | MSG-P2-001 | AC4, AC6 |
| X6 | The ACE batch of the business date is not complete, so the request is held | No item and no file exist; the held-file alert fires on the held-item series and the runbook names the freshness check | MSG-P1-001 | AC4 |
| X7 | The 16:00 window or a per-lot buyer window does not start | The window check fails the smoke run and the runbook entry names the Airflow DAG and the requesting service | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0650; ASM-1086) | AC3, AC6 |
| X8 | A dashboard series is missing, or an alert carries no message identifier or no runbook link | The observability check fails the release | None | AC5, AC6 |
| X9 | A new build is promoted while items are in RETRY | The workflow of each item replays on the new build from its history; the dashboards show both build IDs | None | AC1, AC5 |
| X10 | The MFT/SFTP endpoint is unreachable | The attempts fail, the retry ladder of the interface row runs out, the item is EXCEPTION and the alert fires; nothing is lost and nothing is duplicated | MSG-GEN-006 | AC4 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the chart skeleton, the workflow kit, the topic provisioning, the migration conventions and the flag library; no application code is built here |
| Negotiable | Replica counts, resource sizes, lag and alert thresholds, intervals and consumer quotas are environment values |
| Valuable | Makes the outbound path observable, resendable and provable at the 16:00 window and per buyer lot before the release date |
| Estimable | One chart, one migration step, one topic, one queue, two windows it does not own, six series, four alerts and five runbook entries |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the runbook |
| Testable | Every criterion tests an artefact: the chart renders, the migration refuses a foreign schema, the groups hold offsets, an alert fires on a synthetic metric, the windows start, the smoke run passes |
