```gherkin
    Then the dashboards show items by status, attempts per item, the age of the oldest EXCEPTION item, files delivered and failed per interface, requests held by the freshness check, and consumer lag by group and partition
    Then each series carries the environment, the release and the build ID as dimensions
    Then a held file, a parked item and a lagging group are visible on the dashboards before any alert is read

  Scenario: AC6 The runbook and the smoke run cover the operational failures (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published runbook and the smoke run of the release
    When a held file, a parked item, a stuck retry, an unreachable endpoint and a lagging group are simulated
    Then each condition maps to one runbook entry with the check, the owner role and the recovery step
    Then the smoke run delivers one synthetic INT-14 file to the MFT stub, parks one item in EXCEPTION with FileFailed and resends it with MSG-GEN-005
    Then the smoke run ends with one file per interface and business date, no duplicate file and the environment restored
    Then no threshold and no interval is hard-coded and no secret appears in a values file, a dashboard or the runbook
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One login, one task queue and one schema per service: the release carries the rwb-integration login, polls `rwb-integration` only and migrates `rwb_integration` only | Arch v5 slide 41; DP-02; DP-15 |
| BR2 | The release publishes on `rwb.integration.events.v1` and on `rwb.decision-record.v1` only, and subscribes to `rwb.source-data.events.v1` only | Arch v5 slides 16, 42 and 43; DP-09; DP-14 |
| BR3 | The two file windows belong to the bank Airflow, which opens them and calls the service APIs only; the deployment registers no Schedule for them | Arch v5 slides 16, 32 and 44; ASM-1074 |
| BR4 | JOB-11 is the platform outbox relay on its one-minute interval and is deployed with the library, not as a job of this service | Arch v5 slide 44; DP-09 |
| BR5 | There is no data-lake target, no lake route and no lake delivery row: the reporting extract is a `deliverFile` request and the decision feed is Kafka ingest in rwb-decision | DP-17; Arch v5 slides 37 and 44 |
| BR6 | Every alert carries a message identifier and the agreed text and links one runbook entry | Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR7 | No environment value is hard-coded: replicas, resources, thresholds, intervals, quotas and the flag come from values files and parameters | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR8 | Dashboard series, alert payloads and the runbook carry counts, identifiers, interface codes, business dates and build IDs only, never an address, an identity number or a file content | ADR-023; CTL-11 |
| BR9 | The release exposes the four admin operations through the chart and its ingress and declares no path of its own; SCR-09 is reached through the gateway-bff composite route | DP-19; TSD P2 v3 T-A.1 |
| BR10 | A failing release never replaces a working one: the previous build stays in force until the new build passes its tests and its smoke run | DP-10 |
| BR11 | An exhausted item is never deleted: it is EXCEPTION with a task for the owner role, and a resend sets PENDING with attempt count 0 | Legacy AC7; TSD P2 v3 T4 |
| BR12 | The deployment provisions no ACE grant, no view and no inbound consumer, because there is no inbound adapter and only rwb-source-data reads the ACE views | D-RCV-35 U1; ADR-010; DP-05 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | Chart published | The image, the chart and the contract tests pass | Deploying |
| Deploying | Migration applied and worker registered | The `rwb_integration` sequence applied and the worker polls `rwb-integration` | Ready |
| Ready | Release superseded | A new chart version passes its tests | Rolling |
| Rolling | All workers on the new build | The old build drains its open workflows | Ready |
| Ready | Flag off | `rwb.integration.file-adapters` is turned off in the environment | Not deployed |
| Ready | Smoke run failed | The window check, the delivery or the resend step of the smoke run fails | Blocked |
| Blocked | Previous build restored | The previous chart is redeployed or a later build passes the smoke run | Ready |

The item states PENDING, SENT, RETRY, EXCEPTION and ACKNOWLEDGED and the delivery states PENDING, RETRYING, DELIVERED and EXCEPTION are the app story's runtime and are not states of this deployment.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| DevOps engineer | Owns the chart, the values files, the pipeline stages, the migration step, the dashboards and the runbook |
| Platform administrator | Owns the `rwb-recovery` namespace, the topic ACLs, the consumer quotas, the flag library and the resend of an item or a delivery |
| Platform event owner | Owns `rwb.integration.events.v1`, its retry and `.dlt` topics, its schema subject and its retention |
| Bank Airflow owner | Owns the DAGs that open the WIN window at 16:00 and the debt-buyer window per lot and that call the service APIs only |
| Release manager | Approves the promotion of one artefact and may block it on a failing smoke run |
| On-call operator | Runs the five runbook entries and opens an incident when a held file, a parked item or a lag persists |
| MFT team | Owns the endpoint, the key and the receiver agreement that the values point to |
| RW-AUDIT | Reads the items, the deliveries, the resend record and the run summaries |

The worker runs as the rwb-integration service identity (DP-02), carried by the chart as a secret reference and never as a literal. The login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0650; ASM-1070).

##### 11. Data

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Deployment values | Image digest, chart version, replica counts for the API and the worker, resource requests and limits, probe paths and timings, log level, namespace, task queue, build ID, feature switch, KEDA backlog threshold |
| Task queue | `rwb-integration` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, polled by the worker of this service only |
| Topic | `rwb.integration.events.v1` with its partitions, replication factor, retention and key, its retry topics at 1 minute, 10 minutes and 1 hour and its `.dlt` topic; `rwb.decision-record.v1` published by the library; `rwb.source-data.events.v1` the only subscription |
| Schema | `rwb_integration`, migrated by its own per-service Flyway sequence from the V0001 baseline of `interface_config`, `outbound_item` and `job_catalog` plus the four library objects |
| Interface rows | The INT-14, INT-19, INT-20 and INT-25 rows with direction OUTBOUND, max attempts 3 and retry intervals 5, 15 and 45 minutes, loaded as reference data by RW-REFADM |
| Endpoint values | The WIN and debt-buyer endpoint references, the key identifiers and the staging path of RWB-P2-E1007-INF, injected as values and never as literals |
| Dashboard series | Items by status, attempts per item, the age of the oldest EXCEPTION item, files delivered and failed per interface, requests held by the freshness check, consumer lag by group and partition; dimensions environment, release, build ID |
| Runbook entries | Held file, parked item, stuck retry, unreachable endpoint, lagging group; each with the check, the owner role and the recovery step |
| Alerts | Four rules and one runbook entry each: MSG-P2-001 for a parked item, `FileFailed` for a failed file, the held-item series for a held file, and the identifier placeholder of GAP-0650 for the lag alert |
| Secrets | The rwb-integration login secret, the Kafka client credential, the Temporal mTLS material and the MFT credential reference, all from the platform secret store |
| Test data | One synthetic INT-14 request for a synthetic business date, one forced transfer failure and one resend; synthetic keys only |

The deployment topology (cluster names, node pools, replica counts, resource sizes, zone spread, ingress class and probe timings) belongs to each environment and is set by the platform team in its values file; the chart exposes every one of them as a value and this story fixes only their names and the rule that they are never hard-coded.

**Probes.** Readiness answers healthy only after the worker has polled `rwb-integration` once and the API has answered its health path; liveness answers healthy when the process is up and its internal loop is responsive. Neither probe writes to the database or commits an offset, and a failing dependency is reported as not ready, never as live-and-broken.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None from this story. The four admin operations — `GET /api/recovery/integration/v1/admin/outbound-items`, `POST /api/recovery/integration/v1/admin/outbound-items/{itemId}/resend`, `GET /api/recovery/integration/v1/admin/outbox/deliveries` and `POST /api/recovery/integration/v1/admin/outbox/deliveries/{deliveryId}/resend` — are declared by RWB-P2-E1007-CON and implemented by RWB-P2-E1007-APP; this deployment exposes them through the chart and its ingress and declares no path of its own. The probes are cluster-internal and are not part of the API surface.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None from the deployment. The worker calls the rwb-source-data, rwb-comms, rwb-document, rwb-case and rwb-access contracts at run time as the app story's client; the chart carries no REST client of its own and no outbound call at start-up beyond the Temporal frontend, the Kafka brokers and the MFT endpoint.

###### 12.3 Events published

None of its own. `rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1` and `rwb.integration.FileFailed.v1` are published by the app story on `rwb.integration.events.v1`; `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` is published by the local decision-record library through the relay when an item moves to EXCEPTION or is resent (DP-03, DP-09).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event type | Topic | Deployment element |
|---|---|---|
| `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` | `rwb.source-data.events.v1` | The worker group with the inbox, the retry topic and the `.dlt` routing; releases a held request |

The topic and its retry and `.dlt` topics are provisioned by the platform event epic; this deployment configures the group, the inbox, the offsets and the relay that hands an event to the worker.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Deployment element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `OutboundFileWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per interface and business date | `rwb-integration` | Registered by the worker of this release, with the build ID and worker versioning |
| `deliverFile(manifest)` and `receiveFile` | Provided activities | `rwb-integration` | Registered by the same worker; `receiveFile` is called by no flow |
| buildOutboundFile, storeOutboundFile, sendFileOverMft, parkItemInException | Activities | `rwb-integration` | Registered with the kit's retry policy; the file-level ladder is the interface row, not the activity retry |
| Outbox relay | Platform relay | not a worker | Deployed with the library; publishes `rwb.integration.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1` on its one-minute interval (JOB-11) |

**Build ID and versioning.** The build ID is the one supplied by the workflow kit for the release commit; worker versioning is enabled and a new build takes new workflows while the old build drains. The build ID format and the versioning policy are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0650; ASM-1085).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The deployment registers no Temporal Schedule. The WIN window at 16:00 and the debt-buyer window per lot are opened by the bank Airflow, which calls the requesting services and never a `rwb_*` schema (Arch v5 slides 16, 32 and 44; BR3). The outbox relay runs on the platform's one-minute interval (BR4), and JOB-13 and JOB-15 are removed with the data lake (BR5). The exact trigger contract of the two windows is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0650; ASM-1086).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Deployment element |
|---|---|---|
| `interface_config` | P2 (rwb_integration) | Created by the V0001 baseline; the interface rows are loaded as reference data, never as a chart value |
| `outbound_item` | P2 (rwb_integration) | Created by the V0001 baseline; read by the worker, the sender and the exception queue |
| `job_catalog` | P2 (rwb_integration) | Created by the V0001 baseline; the loading of the JOB-10 and JOB-11 rows is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0650; ASM-1079) |
| `outbox_event` | PLT library, created in rwb_integration | Created by the library migration in the same schema; written by the app story |
| `outbox_delivery` | PLT library, created in rwb_integration | Created by the library migration; read by the relay and the delivery read |
| `processed_event` | PLT library, created in rwb_integration | Created by the library migration; the inbox of the consumed event |
| `idempotency_key` | PLT library, created in rwb_integration | Created by the library migration; the stored response of the two POST operations |
| `decision_record` | PLT library, created in rwb_integration | Created by the library migration; published to `rwb.decision-record.v1` |

The release applies the `rwb_integration` migration of this key and no other: no ACE view, no other service's table and no lake object is created, altered or read (DP-01, DP-05, DP-15, DP-17).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

None. No fake is deployed. The MFT endpoint of the smoke run is the infrastructure stub of RWB-P2-E1007-INF, and the contract fakes of the consumed services are in-process test doubles of the app story and of RWB-P2-E1007-CON.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 0 consumed by the deployment | The four admin operations are the app story's; the probes are cluster-internal |
| Kafka | 0 published, 1 type consumed through 1 group | `rwb.integration.events.v1` provisioned with retry and `.dlt`; `rwb.source-data.events.v1` the only subscription; `rwb.decision-record.v1` published by the library |
| Temporal | 1 workflow, 6 activities, 0 Schedules | Worker on `rwb-integration` with a pinned build ID, worker versioning and KEDA scaling |
| File | 2 interfaces | INT-14 WIN and INT-25 buyer tape through the endpoint values of RWB-P2-E1007-INF; no data lake and no inbound folder |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | The release migrates `rwb_integration` only and reads no other schema | none |
| DP-02 | `recovery_svc` login | One login per service, carried as a secret reference | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | The local record library is deployed with the relay and publishes to `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | No ACE grant, no view and no route in this release | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | The interface rows and the lists stay reference data; no chart value carries them | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | The topic with its retry and `.dlt` topics, the inbox and the relay | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | The worker, the task queue and worker versioning from the kit; no Schedule and no Quartz job | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | The release declares no REST path and no client of its own | none |
| DP-16 | `recovery.integration.adapter` | The release exposes the rwb-integration contract and adds no path of its own | C RWB-P2-E1007-CON |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | No lake target, route or delivery row is deployed; JOB-13 and JOB-15 are gone | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | The ingress registers the service base for the gateway-bff edge; no screen is deployed | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Artefacts**

| Artefact | Content |
|---|---|
| `helm/rwb-integration/` overlay | API deployment, worker deployment, config map, secret references, probes, task queue, namespace, build ID, KEDA rule and flag |
| `helm/rwb-integration/values-dev.yaml`, `values-sit.yaml`, `values-uat.yaml` | Image digest, replicas, resources, probe timings, log level, flag value, build ID, consumer group name, intervals, endpoint references (ASM-1085) |
| Pipeline stage | Build, unit and contract tests, image and dependency scan, chart publish, migration step, topic step, window check, smoke run, promotion |
| Migration step | The `rwb_integration` sequence from the V0001 baseline; a target schema other than `rwb_integration` is refused |
| Topic step | `rwb.integration.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics, the producer ACL and the consumer ACLs of the requesting services |
| Window step | Confirms the two Airflow windows and that no Schedule is registered for either |
| Dashboards | The six series of section 11 with the three dimensions |
| Alerts | Four rules, each with a message identifier or its placeholder and one runbook entry |
| Runbook | Five entries: held file, parked item, stuck retry, unreachable endpoint, lagging group |

**Alert mapping**

| Message ID | Condition | Alert | Route |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-001 | A request is held because the ACE batch of the business date is not complete | Held-file alert naming the interface, the business date and the source date | Platform on-call and the data steward, ticket |
| MSG-P2-001 | An item moved to EXCEPTION after its last allowed attempt | Failed-file alert naming the interface, the business date, the attempt count and the build ID, with the count of items in EXCEPTION | Platform on-call, page |
| Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0650; ASM-1085) | The consumer group of `rwb.integration.events.v1` or of `rwb.source-data.events.v1` lags past its threshold | Lag alert naming the group, the topic, the partition and the lag | Platform on-call, page in the 16:00 window, else ticket |
| Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0650; ASM-1086) | A file window did not start, or the endpoint refused every connection | Window and endpoint alert naming the interface, the window and the endpoint health | Platform on-call and the MFT team, ticket |

**Retry and offsets.** The file-level retry ladder is the `max_attempts` and `retry_intervals_min` of the interface row, applied by `OutboundFileWorkflow` as timers; the activity retry is the kit's three attempts with back-off and never multiplies the ladder. The deployment adds no retry of its own. Offsets are committed after the inbox row is marked, so a crash replays the `AceDataReady` handling and the inbox makes the replay harmless (DP-09).

**Rollback.** A release that fails the smoke run is not promoted. A release already promoted is rolled back by redeploying the previous chart version with its own build ID, which keeps the old build serving its open workflows until they finish; items in RETRY are replayed from their history and the inbox makes the replay harmless. No data repair is needed, because the release writes no row of its own and the migration is additive.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.integration.file-adapters`. On: the worker polls `rwb-integration`, `deliverFile` accepts a request and the file path runs. Off: no worker, no item and no file; the flag is not a way to stop a running ladder, which is what the exception queue and the resend are for.

**Done when.** The chart renders for DEV, SIT and UAT with a pinned digest and the build ID, the migration step refuses a foreign schema, the topic and its retry and `.dlt` topics exist with their ACLs, the two windows are confirmed as Airflow's with no Schedule registered, the smoke run delivers one file, parks one item and resends it, the six series and the four alerts are published with their identifiers or placeholders and their runbook links, and the five runbook entries are reviewed by the on-call rota.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-001 | A request is held because the ACE batch is not complete | {product} is from {date}. Today's data is not yet complete. |
| MSG-P2-001 | An item is in the exception queue after its last allowed attempt | The {interface} file {file} was not sent after {count} attempts. It is in the exception queue. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The endpoint is unreachable and the attempt is retried | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-GEN-005 | A resend is accepted in the smoke run | Saved. |
| Identifier pending | The consumer group lags past its threshold | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0650; ASM-1085) |
| Identifier pending | A file window did not start, or the endpoint refused every connection | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0650; ASM-1086) |

MSG-P1-001 uses the FSD P2 Integration v3 wording, which outranks the story master under R-PREC (ASM-1075). The other business texts are the legacy ones and are unchanged. The lag alert and the window alert have no identifier in the source set, so both carry the placeholder until the Error and Message Standard names them. An alert payload names counts, interface codes, business dates, attempt counts, group names and the build ID only, never an address, an identity number or a file content.

##### 15. Screens and states

The deployment has no screen of its own. Its operator-facing surfaces are the pipeline run view, the release view, the dashboards, SCR-09 Exception queue through the gateway-bff composite route, and the runbook. SCR-09 is served by the app story and the route of RWB-PLT-N001-CON; the deployment only registers the ingress path. The Temporal Web UI stays behind Entra ID: RW-PLATADM operates and RW-AUDIT reads, and payloads are decoded only through the codec server under break-glass. SCR-44 Interface and job monitor is not used for this service, because the release registers no job of its own and the relay is a platform interval.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a values file: the file patterns, the attempt limits, the retry intervals, the owner role and the alert role are `interface_config` and reference-data rows, never a deployment value.
- No personal data in logs, dashboard series, alert payloads, the runbook or the workflow history: counts, identifiers, interface codes, business dates and build IDs only, and payloads stay encrypted.
- One login, one task queue and one schema per service: the release carries the rwb-integration login, polls `rwb-integration` and migrates `rwb_integration` only (DP-02, DP-15).
- The release deploys no ACE grant, no view, no inbound consumer and no lake object (DP-05, DP-17, BR12).
- The topic and its retry and `.dlt` topics exist with their ACLs before the worker starts (DP-09, BR2).
- No item is ever deleted: an exhausted item is EXCEPTION with a task for the owner role, and a resend sets PENDING with attempt count 0 (BR11).
- The release pins the image digest, the chart version and the build ID; a rebuild between environments is not allowed, and a failing smoke run never replaces a working build.
- No secret is written into a values file, a chart template, a dashboard or the runbook; all secrets come from the platform secret store (NFR-052).

##### 19. Out of scope

- The build of the outbound path, the retry policy, the inbox, the four admin operations and the workflow (RWB-P2-E1007-APP).
- The contract documents, the manifest, the event schemas and the fakes (RWB-P2-E1007-CON); this story only deploys and gates them.
- The MFT/SFTP endpoints, the PGP keys, the key store, the network rules, the staging area and the budgets (RWB-P2-E1007-INF).
- The Temporal cluster, the namespace, worker versioning and the codec server as platform components (RWB-PLT-WF, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON).
- The topic provisioning, the schema registry and the `.dlt` retention as platform components (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON); this story configures the ACLs and the group.
- The bank Airflow DAGs themselves and their ownership (bank platform team, for discussion); this story confirms the windows and registers no Schedule.
- The real cross-service journey of the path with all services live (RWB-ITG-E1007-ITG).
- The exact cluster topology, node pools, replica counts, lag thresholds and probe timings, which are set per environment by the platform team (GAP-0650).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: RWB-E1-007 is split (rework) and this integration story proves the one outbound-file path end to end across the real wave-1 services — rwb-comms requests, rwb-integration executes `deliverFile`, rwb-source-data answers every source-data read, rwb-document stores the file, rwb-case takes the route-state change and the owner task and rwb-access authorises. It builds and executes the integration tests and publishes no operation of its own. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform administrator (RW-PLATADM)**, I want **the one outbound-file path proved end to end against the real wave-1 services, from the requesting notice in rwb-comms through the `deliverFile` activity on queue `rwb-integration`, the source-data reads that leave one hop to rwb-source-data, the claim-check store in rwb-document, the delivery to WIN and to a debt buyer, and the retry, exception-queue and owner-task path into rwb-case, with the right check in rwb-access on the resend**, so that **every outbound file of every later wave is proved once, on the real services, before it is copied**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story fixed one adapter pattern for every outbound file, built from `recovery.v_ace_*`, retried on intervals held as data and raised to an exception queue with a named owner. In the target that pattern is no longer one process reading an ACE table: rwb-comms requests the WIN letters file, rwb-payment the posting file and rwb-debtsale the buyer tape, rwb-integration executes one activity `deliverFile(manifest)` on queue `rwb-integration`, rwb-source-data is the only service that reads the thirty `recovery.v_ace_*` views, rwb-document holds the bytes behind a claim-check link and rwb-case carries the route state and the task (DP-01, DP-05, DP-09, DP-16, DP-17). Every one of those edges fails in a way no single-service suite can see: a second file built for one request, a read that reaches an ACE view from the wrong service, a retry that duplicates a file, a task raised for nobody because the event and the action disagreed.

This story is the end-to-end proof of that path on the wave-1 services, and it is the reference the later ITG stories copy. It exercises REQ-DRI-006 (no direct call to a system of record), REQ-DRI-007 (every outbound file logged, retried and raised to an owner) and REQ-DRI-008 (data from other systems only through ACE ingestion and the ACE views, read by rwb-source-data alone), and it holds the FSD P2 measure "outbound items in the exception queue over one day: zero". It also proves DP-17 for this legacy key: no inbound adapter, no data lake, INT-19 and INT-20 carry no lake target, the reporting extract goes to rwb-reporting through `deliverFile` and the decision and outcome feed is continuous Kafka ingest in rwb-decision.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P2-E1007-APP is done in SIT: `deliverFile(manifest)` and `receiveFile` are published in the activity contract on queue `rwb-integration`, and the exception-queue read, the resend and the outbox-delivery read exist on base `/api/recovery/integration/v1`.
- RWB-P2-E1007-CON is published: the activity contract jar, the AsyncAPI document of `rwb.integration.events.v1` with `FileDelivered` and `FileFailed`, the error envelope, the Idempotency-Key rule and the contract fakes. This story runs against the real services, so the fakes are not used here.
- RWB-P6-E1007-APP is done: rwb-comms requests the WIN letters file for a business date and publishes `rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1`.
- RWB-P1-E1001-APP, RWB-P1-E1069-APP and RWB-P1-E1015-APP are done: rwb-source-data answers `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/customers/{id}`, `/accounts/{id}` and `/freshness` behind its own views, and it is the only service with a read grant on `recovery.v_ace_*`.
- RWB-P5-E1007-APP is done: rwb-document accepts a stored file on `POST /api/recovery/document/v1/documents` and returns the upload link and the document ID.
- RWB-P3-E1007-APP is done: rwb-case consumes `rwb.integration.FileFailed.v1`, moves the route state and raises the owner task through the case contract.
- RWB-P4-E1007-APP is done: rwb-access answers the authorise check on `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` for the right on the exception-queue screen.
- The interface configuration version "IF-2026.11" is loaded for interfaces INT-14 (WIN registered mail, daily outbound file), INT-19 (reporting extract), INT-20 (decision and outcome feed) and INT-25 (debt buyer tape), each with direction OUTBOUND, max attempts 3 and retry intervals 5, 15 and 45 minutes. The reference-data administrator (RW-REFADM) loads the rows.
- The bank Airflow frame opens the WIN file window at 16:00 and the debt-buyer window per lot, and calls the services through their APIs only. The exact trigger contract of the two windows is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0334; ASM-0428), so the harness opens the window by calling the requesting service the way the Airflow task does and records the call in the run log.
- The `deliverFile(manifest)` payload and the claim-check handoff between rwb-integration and rwb-document are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0334; ASM-0428); the manifest of section 12.5 is used until the P2 contract review fixes it.
- SIT holds the run fixtures of section 13: 85 approved notices for business date 2026-11-10, the synthetic INT-25 tape of 120 accounts, one ALS batch at status FAILED at 05:20 for 2026-11-10, and the event key EV-10:TRT-0001:v1.
- The run uses the per-service logins of the wave-1 services (DP-02); no service login is shared.
- No build dependency and no contract dependency: the eight integration dependencies are on the real services. Day 1.

##### 4. Flow

1. Bank Airflow: at 16:00 opens the WIN file window and calls rwb-comms for the business date's approved notices, the way the Airflow task does; the harness records the call in the run log.
2. rwb-comms: publishes `rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1` on `rwb.comms.events.v1` for the 85 approved notices of 2026-11-10, then calls the rwb-integration activity `deliverFile(manifest)` on queue `rwb-integration` with the interface ID "INT-14", the business date, the idempotency key and the case IDs.
3. rwb-integration: reads the interface configuration row in force for "INT-14" — target, transport, attempts, retry intervals, owner role and alert role — from `interface_config` in its own schema `rwb_integration`.
4. rwb-integration: asks rwb-source-data `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/freshness` for the business date; the answer says whether the ACE batch of 2026-11-10 is complete and which source date the data carries (AC4, AC13). One hop, 2 s timeout.
5. rwb-integration: builds the file from its own `outbound_item` and from the notice references it was given, and reads the addressee and account facts it needs with `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/customers/{id}` and `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/accounts/{id}`, one hop each, 2 s timeout. No statement of the build reads `recovery.v_ace_*`.
6. rwb-integration: writes one `outbound_item` for "INT-14" and 2026-11-10 under the unique idempotency key, in status PENDING, then calls rwb-document `POST /api/recovery/document/v1/documents` and stores the built file `WIN_NOTICE_20261110.txt`; `outbound_item` holds the document ID and the claim-check manifest (fileId, batchId, sha256, record count 85). No file content travels on a message.
7. rwb-integration: sends the file to WIN over MFT/SFTP with PGP, sets the item SENT, and writes the `outbox_delivery` rows of the events it raises; on the acknowledgment file the item moves to ACKNOWLEDGED.
8. rwb-integration: publishes `rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1` on `rwb.integration.events.v1` with key the case ID and the requesting service in the payload; the requesting service acknowledges it once through its inbox. Nothing else in the run builds, sends or stores a file for that business date.
9. rwb-integration: on a failed transfer raises the next attempt from the retry intervals in the row — attempt 2 five minutes after attempt 1 and attempt 3 fifteen minutes after attempt 2 — and keeps the item in RETRY while an attempt is outstanding.
10. rwb-integration: after the last allowed attempt sets the item EXCEPTION, writes `rwb.integration.FileFailed.v1` to its outbox in the same transaction, and shows the item in the exception queue with MSG-P2-001.
11. rwb-case: consumes `rwb.integration.FileFailed.v1` through its inbox once, moves the route state of each case on the file to EXCEPTION_QUEUE — RETRY_QUEUE after a first failure — and raises one open task for role RW-PLATADM for the case set, through the rwb-case contract.
12. rwb-access: answers the authorise check when the platform administrator opens the exception queue and when the resend is called; a role without the right is refused with MSG-P4-002 and nothing changes.
13. rwb-integration: on the resend returns the item to PENDING with attempt count 0, answers MSG-GEN-005, and writes the resend to the access audit trail with the role and the time.
14. rwb-reporting: when its extract falls due for the business date, calls `deliverFile(manifest)` for "INT-19" with its own base and receives `rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1` back; no file goes to a data lake and no lake copy is written.
15. rwb-decision: ingests the decision and outcome feed continuously from `rwb.decision-record.v1`; no "INT-20" file is produced and no lake delivery row exists (DP-17).
16. The harness: compares the run against the expected counts — one outbound_item per interface and business date, 85 cases on the WIN file, 120 accounts on the INT-25 tape, one FileDelivered or FileFailed per item, one task per case set, zero duplicate files — and publishes the run report with the boundary result.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The ACE batch for the file's business date is not complete | rwb-source-data answers the freshness check with the source date; no file is built and no outbound_item is written; the request waits for the next window after AceDataReady | MSG-P1-001 | AC4 |
| X2 | The outbound transfer fails on an attempt | The item waits for the next attempt from the retry intervals in the row; the cases of the file move to route state RETRY_QUEUE after the first failure | MSG-GEN-006 | TC-E1-007-03-ITG |
| X3 | The retry limit of 3 attempts is reached | The item moves to EXCEPTION, `rwb.integration.FileFailed.v1` is published, each case moves to EXCEPTION_QUEUE and one task goes to role RW-PLATADM | MSG-P2-001 | AC14 |
| X4 | The same requesting event arrives twice with the same key | The inbox of rwb-integration drops the second one, the hit is counted and no second file is built (R-UNI-40) | None | TC-E1-007-05-ITG |
| X5 | Two worker instances pick the same due item | Only one holds the row lock; the other skips it, so the file is sent once and the attempt count is 1 | None | TC-E1-007-06-ITG |
| X6 | A platform administrator resends an item from the exception queue | The item returns to PENDING with attempt count 0, the sender picks it up in its next pass and no duplicate file exists | MSG-GEN-005 | AC14 |
| X7 | A role without the right lists or resends exception items | Refused by rwb-access; nothing changes | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-007-10-ITG |
| X8 | A service other than rwb-source-data attempts a read of `recovery.v_ace_*` | The statement fails at the database grant and the boundary check of the run fails | None (run log) | AC13 |
| X9 | The stored file is missing in rwb-document when the manifest is followed | The attempt fails as a transfer failure; the claim-check link is never rebuilt from a partial file; the item follows the retry path | MSG-GEN-006 | AC12, AC14 |
| X10 | rwb-source-data does not answer inside the REST budget | One hop, 2 s timeout, no retry other than one GET retry with jitter; the attempt fails and is retried, never built from a partial answer | None | AC13 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Runs against the real wave-1 services already in SIT; it builds no operation and waits for no contract. The eight integration dependencies are the services it exercises |
| Negotiable | The fixtures, the window call and the expected counts are harness configuration; the business values are the legacy ones and are not changed |
| Valuable | The one outbound path of every later wave is proved on the real services once, including the retry, the exception queue and the owner task |
| Estimable | One harness, one fixture set, one boundary check, one run report; no production code |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the fixture set |
| Testable | Every owned criterion has a test case in section 16; the last four are the new end-to-end ones |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Integration adapters for outbound files, end to end

  Background:
    Given the interface configuration version "IF-2026.11" is in force
    Given interface "INT-14" WIN outbound has direction "OUTBOUND", max attempts 3 and retry intervals 5, 15 and 45 minutes
    Given interface "INT-14" has owner role "RW-PLATADM"
    Given the business date is 2026-11-10
    Given every service in the run is the real wave-1 service on its own base /api/recovery/<short>/v1

  Scenario: AC4 Outbound file held while the ACE batch is not complete (legacy RWB-E1-007 AC4)
    Given v_ace_batch_status shows the ALS batch for 2026-11-10 with status "FAILED" at 05:20
    Given the WIN notice file for 2026-11-10 is due at 16:00
    When JOB-10 reaches its build step
    Then no file is built and no outbound_item is written
    Then the request is held with the reason "DP01 Account and arrears is from 2026-11-07"
    Then the platform administrator receives MSG-P1-001 "DP01 Account and arrears is from 2026-11-07. Today's ACE batch has not arrived."
    Then the file is built by the next JOB-10 run after EV-26 for 2026-11-10

  Scenario: AC12 A WIN request produces one outbound item and one stored file (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given 85 approved notices for business date 2026-11-10 are in rwb-comms and it publishes rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1
    When rwb-comms calls the rwb-integration deliverFile(manifest) activity on queue "rwb-integration" for "INT-14"
    Then exactly one outbound_item exists for "INT-14" and 2026-11-10, in status "PENDING"
    Then the built file "WIN_NOTICE_20261110.txt" is stored in rwb-document and the outbound_item holds its document ID
    Then the claim-check manifest carries fileId, batchId, sha256 and record count 85, and no file content travels on a message
    Then rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1 is published on rwb.integration.events.v1 with key the case ID and the requesting service in the payload
    Then the requesting service acknowledges it once, and the outbound_item moves to "SENT" and then "ACKNOWLEDGED" when the acknowledgment file arrives

  Scenario: AC13 Source data for the build is one hop to rwb-source-data (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the file build needs the addressee and the account facts of the business date
    When deliverFile builds the file
    Then each source-data read is one REST call to rwb-source-data: GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/customers/{id}, GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/accounts/{id} and GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/freshness
    Then every call has a 2 s timeout, one GET retry with jitter and no call chain
    Then no service outside rwb-source-data reads recovery.v_ace_* and the boundary check of the run finds no such read
    Then the ACE business date on the outbound_item is the one rwb-source-data reports, 2026-11-10

  Scenario: AC14 The retry limit, the exception queue and the owner task (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given outbound_item "OB-0002" for the 85 cases of the file is due
    Given the transfer fails on attempts 1, 2 and 3
    When the third attempt fails
    Then the item status is "EXCEPTION" and the item shows in SCR-09 with message MSG-P2-001
    Then rwb.integration.FileFailed.v1 is published on rwb.integration.events.v1 for the requesting service
    Then the rwb-case contract raises one open task with owner role "RW-PLATADM" for the case set of the file, and each case is in route state "EXCEPTION_QUEUE"
    Then the outbox holds one FileFailed row and the inbox of rwb-case processes it once, so a redelivery writes no second file and no second task
    Then a platform administrator resends the item, the response carries MSG-GEN-005, the item returns to "PENDING" with attempt count 0, and no duplicate file exists

  Scenario: AC15 No inbound adapter and no data lake (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given every interface configuration row of version "IF-2026.11", including "INT-14", "INT-19", "INT-20" and "INT-25"
    Then every row has direction "OUTBOUND" and the load refuses a row with direction "INBOUND"
    Then no inbound folder is read and the receiveFile activity is called by no flow in the run
    Then "INT-19" and "INT-20" name no data lake target: the reporting extract is delivered through deliverFile(manifest) to rwb-reporting and the decision and outcome feed is continuous Kafka ingest in rwb-decision
    Then no file is sent to a data lake, no lake copy is written, and no JOB-13 file exists
    Then the debt buyer tape "INT-25" is delivered through the same deliverFile path, per lot, encrypted
```

The legacy criteria this story does not own (AC1, AC2, AC3, AC5, AC6, AC7) are owned by RWB-P2-E1007-APP and are re-exercised only inside the end-to-end run of section 13, never restated here.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every outbound file goes through the one adapter; no component calls a target system directly | ADR-010; REQ-DRI-006; legacy RWB-E1-007 BR1 |
| BR2 | An outbound file reads ACE data only by business key, through the owner's contract, and never writes to ACE | D-RCV-35 U4; ADR-010; BR-P2-001-ACE; legacy RWB-E1-007 BR2 |
| BR3 | An outbound file is built only when the ACE batch for its business date is complete | VR-P2-001-1; legacy RWB-E1-007 BR3 |
| BR4 | An outbound file is sent again on the intervals in its configuration row; after the last failure a task goes to the owning role | ifspec INT-14; interface_config.max_attempts; legacy RWB-E1-007 BR4 |
| BR5 | A system that is unavailable queues the action and retries | R-UNI-33, R-UNI-35, R-UNI-36; legacy RWB-E1-007 BR5 |
| BR6 | An item that fails after the retry limit moves to the exception queue with a task for the owner | R-UNI-34; REQ-DRI-007; legacy RWB-E1-007 BR6 |
| BR7 | An event with a key already processed by the consumer is ignored and the hit is counted | R-UNI-40; events.txt Rules sheet, Duplicates; legacy RWB-E1-007 BR7 |
| BR8 | Retry counts, intervals, folders, patterns and owners are data rows, never code | Principle 1; DT02; legacy RWB-E1-007 BR8 |
| BR9 | rwb-integration has no inbound adapter: no file is picked up, checked or signed off in the Workbench, and `interface_config` holds outbound rows only | D-RCV-35 U1; ADR-010; legacy RWB-E1-007 BR9 |
| BR10 | An outbound item carries case IDs and business keys, never an address, a name or an identity number; the file itself is held in rwb-document behind the claim-check link | CTL-11; Guardrails; legacy RWB-E1-007 BR10 |
| BR11 | Between services the file path is contract-only: rwb-integration reads source data only through the rwb-source-data REST contract, one hop and 2 s, and no service outside rwb-source-data reads `recovery.v_ace_*`; no service reads another service's tables and no file content travels on a Kafka message | DP-01; DP-05; DP-11; DP-16; ADR-010; Architecture v5 slides 9, 10 and 11 |
| BR12 | There is no data lake: the reporting extract is delivered to rwb-reporting through `deliverFile` (legacy JOB-15) and the decision and outcome feed is continuous Kafka ingest in rwb-decision (legacy JOB-13); INT-19 and INT-20 carry no lake target | DP-17; Architecture v5 slides 37 and 44 |

##### 9. State transitions

`outbound_item.status` as exercised end to end:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | `deliverFile(manifest)` accepted | The freshness check passes and the idempotency key is new | PENDING |
| PENDING | First transfer fails | The transport raises a failure | RETRY |
| RETRY | A later attempt is sent | The retry interval in the row has elapsed | SENT |
| RETRY | Attempt count equals `max_attempts` (3) | The third attempt fails | EXCEPTION |
| SENT | The acknowledgment file arrives | The target confirms the file | ACKNOWLEDGED |
| EXCEPTION | Platform administrator resends | The right check passes and the item version matches | PENDING |

`recovery_case.route_state` in rwb-case, as exercised by the events this story publishes:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| ANY_ACTIVE | SYSTEM_UNAVAILABLE | First failed attempt of an outbound file for the case | RETRY_QUEUE |
| RETRY_QUEUE | RETRY_SUCCEEDED | A later attempt is sent | RESUME_STATE |
| RETRY_QUEUE | RETRY_LIMIT_REACHED | Attempt count equals max attempts | EXCEPTION_QUEUE |

The case status (`recovery_case.status`) does not change and this story writes no case row: rwb-case moves the route state when it consumes `rwb.integration.FileFailed.v1`. This story writes no row through any owner either; every assertion is made on the owner's contract answer and on the events on the topic. The run also exercises `outbox_delivery.status` in rwb-integration and the inbox row in `processed_event` of every consumer, through those services' own logs and admin reads.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| rwb-integration service identity (its own login, DP-02) | Builds, stores, sends and retries the file; writes its own `outbound_item`, `outbox_event` and `outbox_delivery` rows; publishes `FileDelivered` and `FileFailed` |
| rwb-source-data service identity | Answers the freshness, customer and account reads; the only identity with a read grant on `recovery.v_ace_*` |
| rwb-document service identity | Stores the built file and returns the upload link and the document ID |
| rwb-case service identity | Consumes `FileFailed`, moves the route state and raises the owner task |
| rwb-access service identity | Answers the authorise check for the exception-queue read and the resend |
| rwb-reporting service identity | Requests the reporting extract through `deliverFile` and receives `FileDelivered` |
| rwb-decision service identity | Ingests the decision and outcome feed continuously |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Lists exception items, resends one, reads the run state (Platform administration, U) |
| RW-DATASTEW, data steward | Receives the held-file and failed-file alert; reads run state (Platform administration, R) |
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | Loads a new interface configuration version; holds no right on the exception queue |
| RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-COE, RW-SECADM | Read run state and exception items (Platform administration, R) |
| The integration lead and the QA role | Own the harness, the fixtures and the run report; take no business decision |

Field IDs are those of the legacy story and the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary. The five integration tables sit in schema `rwb_integration`; `processed_event`, `outbox_event` and `outbox_delivery` are PLT library objects created in that schema (DP-09). This story owns no table and writes none: it reads them through the rwb-integration admin operations and asserts on the contract answers. The source-data fields the build needs — `contact_key`, `person_key`, `account_key`, `account_code`, `business_date`, `is_complete` (DF-ACE-001, DF-ACE-002, DF-ACE-076, DF-ACE-077, DF-ACE-179, DF-ACE-186) — are read only through the rwb-source-data contract, never from a view by this story or by rwb-integration.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. This story builds and executes integration tests and publishes no operation; the operations of the path belong to RWB-P2-E1007-CON and RWB-P2-E1007-APP.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

Every call is one hop on the owner's per-service base, with a 2 s timeout and a circuit breaker per downstream (DP-11, DP-13).

| Method | Path | Owner | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/integration/v1/admin/outbound-items` | P2 rwb-integration | List items by status and interface for the exception-queue assertions of AC14 |
| POST | `/api/recovery/integration/v1/admin/outbound-items/{itemId}/resend` | P2 rwb-integration | Resend an item in EXCEPTION (AC14, MSG-GEN-005) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/integration/v1/admin/outbox/deliveries` | P2 rwb-integration | Outbox delivery state of `FileDelivered` and `FileFailed` |
| POST | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents` | P5 rwb-document | Store the built file and take the upload link and document ID (AC12) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{id}` | P5 rwb-document | Follow the claim-check link to the stored file (AC12) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/customers/{id}` | P1 rwb-source-data | Customer facts of the file build (AC13) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/accounts/{id}` | P1 rwb-source-data | Account facts of the file build (AC13) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/freshness` | P1 rwb-source-data | ACE batch completeness for the business date (AC4, AC13) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/actions` | P3 rwb-case | Route-state change and owner task on the case set of the file (AC14) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | Right check on the exception-queue read and the resend (X7) |

A service never calls another service's base inside a business step: the file steps run as Temporal activities on the owner's queue (DP-10, DP-16), and the requests of section 12.4 are events. The connection matrix of Architecture v5 slide 13 shows no cell for the rwb-integration read of rwb-source-data or for the `FileFailed` listen edge of rwb-case; the matrix cell is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0338; ASM-0432) and is treated as incomplete, so the reads follow slides 12 and 15 and DP-11.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Key | Payload (IDs and facts only) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1` | `rwb.integration.events.v1` | P2 | caseId | fileId, interfaceId, businessDate, documentId, sha256, recordCount, requesting service |
| `rwb.integration.FileFailed.v1` | `rwb.integration.events.v1` | P2 | caseId | fileId, interfaceId, businessDate, attemptCount, lastError code, caseIds, ownerRole |

Both are written to the outbox in the same transaction as the item state change and relayed with the CloudEvents envelope; no personal data and no file content is carried (DP-09). This story asserts on the topic and on the outbox rows; it publishes nothing itself.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

These are the requesting flows the run exercises, and the events the path reacts to.

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Handler in the run |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1` | `rwb.comms.events.v1` | P6 | rwb-comms then requests `deliverFile` for INT-14; the run starts here (AC12) |
| `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` | `rwb.source-data.events.v1` | P1 | Releases a held request and starts the next window after a failed batch (AC4) |
| `rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1` | `rwb.payment.events.v1` | P8 | rwb-payment requests `deliverFile` for its posting file, the second requesting flow of the same path (X2) |
| `rwb.debtsale.LotAwarded.v1` | `rwb.debtsale.events.v1` | S6 | rwb-debtsale requests `deliverFile` for the INT-25 buyer tape, per lot (AC15) |

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `deliverFile(manifest)` | Activity, provided by P2 and called by the requesting services | `rwb-integration` | Builds, stores, sends and retries one outbound file; one item per interface and business date. The manifest carries fileId, batchId, sha256 and record count, and the claim-check link; its exact payload is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0334; ASM-0428) |
| `receiveFile` | Activity, provided by P2 | `rwb-integration` | The published inbound activity of the P2 contract; wave 1 exercises no inbound call and the run asserts that no flow calls it (BR9, AC15) |

The claim-check handoff is a manifest plus a SAS link valid 15 minutes for one file (Architecture v5 slide 11); the exact handoff is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0334; ASM-0428), and the assumption holds until the P2 contract review.

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Window or timer | When | Owner of the trigger | Legacy reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| WIN file window | Daily 16:00 | Bank Airflow opens the window; rwb-comms requests and rwb-integration executes | JOB-10; Architecture v5 slides 16 and 44 |
| Debt-buyer file window | Per lot, when the lot is awarded | Bank Airflow opens the window; rwb-debtsale requests | JOB-10; Architecture v5 slide 16 (buyer files per lot) |
| Retry timers | Attempt 2 five minutes and attempt 3 fifteen minutes after the previous attempt, up to 45 minutes | The `deliverFile` retry timer, from `interface_config.retry_intervals_min` | ifspec INT-14; legacy AC3 |

The exact trigger contract of the two windows is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0334; ASM-0428); the harness opens them the way the Airflow task does and records the call. No service-side cron opens a file window.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The path's tables — `interface_config`, `outbound_item`, `processed_event`, `outbox_event` and `outbox_delivery` in `rwb_integration` — are owned by P2 rwb-integration with the PLT library for the outbox, inbox and idempotency objects (DP-01, DP-09). This story owns no schema and reads those rows only through the owner's admin operations.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

None. The run uses the real wave-1 services and their published contracts; the contract fakes of RWB-P2-E1007-CON are replaced by the services themselves at this level.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 10 consumed | Admin reads and resend on rwb-integration; store and read on rwb-document; freshness, customer and account reads on rwb-source-data; case action on rwb-case; authorise on rwb-access; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 2 published by the path, 4 consumed by the run | `FileDelivered` and `FileFailed` on `rwb.integration.events.v1` asserted; `NoticeGenerated`, `AceDataReady`, `ProceedsMatched` and `LotAwarded` drive the requesting flows |
| Temporal | 2 activities | `deliverFile(manifest)` and `receiveFile` on queue `rwb-integration` |
| File | 2 interfaces | INT-14 WIN registered mail daily outbound file and INT-25 debt buyer tape per lot; claim-check to Blob through rwb-document and MFT/SFTP with PGP to the party; no data lake |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `test/integration/recovery` in the ACE repository, package `<ACE base package>.recovery.itg.files`. Not part of any deployed service.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-02 | `recovery_svc` login | One login per service | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-16 | `recovery.integration.adapter` | rwb-integration contract | C RWB-P2-E1007-CON |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting | none; gap if the story needs lake data |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The DP dependencies stay with the service implementation stories; this story carries only the eight integration dependencies on the real services and no H, C or X dependency. DP-03 resolves to "the decision and outcome feed is read from `rwb.decision-record.v1`", DP-19 to "SCR-09 is reached through the gateway-bff composite route at the edge", and DP-17 to "no lake row, no lake target, no lake delivery".

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| FilePathRun | Test suite | The ordered end-to-end run of section 4; one run lock per environment |
| RequestingFlowDriver | Fixture | Drives rwb-comms, rwb-payment and rwb-debtsale to request the file, the way their own flows do |
| WindowDriver | Fixture | Opens the WIN window at 16:00 and the debt-buyer window per lot the way the Airflow task does, and records the call |
| AceBatchFixture | Fixture | Sets the ACE batch of the business date to COMPLETE or FAILED at 05:20 behind rwb-source-data, never in a view read by another service |
| ItemAssertions | Assertions | One item per interface and business date, the state chain, the attempt count, the retry intervals, the exception queue |
| DocumentAssertions | Assertions | The stored file, the document ID and the manifest (fileId, batchId, sha256, record count) |
| CasePathAssertions | Assertions | Route state RETRY_QUEUE and EXCEPTION_QUEUE, one open task with owner role RW-PLATADM per case set |
| BoundaryCheck | Check | Fails the run on any `recovery.v_ace_*` read outside rwb-source-data, any cross-schema read, any call chain and any inbound folder read |
| RunReport | Publisher | Publishes the run report with the counts, the boundary result and the fixture versions |

**Fixtures**

- 85 approved notices for business date 2026-11-10 with `person_key` and `contact_key`, and the WIN file expected as `WIN_NOTICE_20261110.txt`.
- The synthetic INT-25 tape of 120 accounts from `debt_sale_account` and the account facts answered by rwb-source-data.
- The ALS batch for 2026-11-10 at status FAILED at 05:20 for AC4, and the same batch COMPLETE for the other criteria.
- Outbound items OB-0001 (due, two workers) and OB-0002 (in EXCEPTION after 3 attempts).
- The event key EV-10:TRT-0001:v1 sent twice.
- Interface configuration version "IF-2026.11" for INT-14, INT-19, INT-20 and INT-25, plus one INBOUND row used only to prove that the load refuses it.
- Synthetic keys only; no name, address or identity number anywhere in the fixtures.

**Real-service topology of the run**

| Node | Part in the run |
|---|---|
| gateway-bff | The staff entry to SCR-09 and to the resend, one hop per call |
| rwb-comms (P6) | Publishes `NoticeGenerated` and requests `deliverFile` for INT-14 |
| rwb-integration (P2) | Executes `deliverFile` and `receiveFile` on queue `rwb-integration`; owns `interface_config`, `outbound_item` and the outbox |
| rwb-source-data (P1) | Answers freshness, customer and account reads; the only reader of `recovery.v_ace_*` |
| rwb-document (P5) | Stores the file and returns the claim-check link |
| rwb-case (P3) | Consumes `FileFailed`, moves the route state and raises the owner task |
| rwb-access (P4) | Answers the authorise check |
| rwb-reporting (P9) | Requests the reporting extract and receives `FileDelivered` |
| rwb-decision (P7) | Ingests the decision and outcome feed continuously |
| Kafka, Temporal, Airflow frame, Blob, MFT/SFTP with PGP | Shared platform parts; the party at the SFTP edge is a stub, the only stub in the run |

**Run order**

1. Reset the wave-1 schemas in the environment and load interface configuration version "IF-2026.11", including the refused INBOUND row.
2. Start the wave-1 services and the shared platform parts; wait for every health check.
3. Load the fixtures of this section, then set the ACE batch for 2026-11-10 to FAILED at 05:20 and run the held-file criterion (AC4).
4. Set the batch to COMPLETE and raise `AceDataReady`; open the WIN window and run AC12: one item, one stored file, one `FileDelivered`, item SENT then ACKNOWLEDGED.
5. Run AC13: capture every source-data call of the build, assert one hop, 2 s timeout, no chain and the reported business date.
6. Run the retry and exception criteria: three failed attempts, EXCEPTION, `FileFailed`, the route states, the owner task, the single inbox action, then the resend (AC14).
7. Run the duplicate-event and two-worker criteria on the same path (TC-E1-007-05-ITG, TC-E1-007-06-ITG) and the access refusal (TC-E1-007-10-ITG).
8. Open the debt-buyer window per lot, run the INT-25 tape and the reporting extract, and run AC15: no inbound adapter, no inbound folder, no lake target, continuous ingest in rwb-decision.
9. Run the boundary check, publish the run report and restore the environment.

**Configuration.** The fixtures, the window call and the expected counts sit in `test/integration/recovery/config`; the interface rows, the attempts and the retry intervals are data in `interface_config`, never in the harness.

**Done when.** The fourteen test cases of section 16 pass in one run, the boundary check finds no `recovery.v_ace_*` read outside rwb-source-data and no call chain, the run report shows one item per interface and business date with zero unexplained exception items, and the run is repeated once green on the same build to prove it is repeatable.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-001 | An outbound file is held because the ACE batch is not complete | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | An outbound transfer fails and is queued for retry | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P2-001 | An outbound item moves to the exception queue | The {interface} file {file} was not sent after {count} attempts. It is in the exception queue. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | A resend on an item whose version changed | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-GEN-005 | A resend is accepted | Saved. |
| MSG-P4-001 | A call without a session | Your session has ended. Sign in again. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right calls the screen or the resend | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | A resend names an unknown item | This record was not found. |

Every message is the legacy wording of RWB-E1-007 and is asserted unchanged in the run; the run adds no message of its own and its report text is for the release team only.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-09 Exception queue (E1) is exercised end to end through the gateway-bff composite route: Loading and list, where the platform administrator sees the failed outbound items with the interface, the attempt count, the last error and the case count; empty, when no item is in EXCEPTION; filtered, on interface INT-14 and on the business date; the resend action, which answers MSG-GEN-005 and returns the item to PENDING; and the refusal for a role without the right, which answers MSG-P4-002 and changes nothing. The run asserts the list content from the rwb-integration admin read and not from the screen, because the screen is the edge's own story; the screen fields and the composite route specification are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0334; ASM-0428). The full SCR-44 interface and job monitor is out of scope (section 19).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the interface rows, the attempts, the retry intervals, the owner role and every fixture count are data or configuration.
- No personal data in logs, events, workflow inputs, fixtures or the run report: synthetic keys only, and file contents are never logged — names, counts and hashes only.
- ACE data only through the rwb-source-data contract; a `recovery.v_ace_*` read outside rwb-source-data is a defect and fails the boundary check of the run.
- No read of another service's tables and no cross-schema join: every assertion is made through the owner's published operation or on the topic.
- One hop, 2 s timeout, no call chain; the run fails when a call chain or an unbounded timeout is observed.
- No file content on a Kafka message or in a workflow payload: the claim-check link and the manifest only.
- No inbound adapter, no inbound folder, no sign-off and no interface row with direction INBOUND; no data lake and no lake delivery row.
- The run never touches UAT or production data, and the environment is restored after the run.

##### 1. Story

As a **contract owner of rwb-decision**, I want **the published baseline of the central decision ledger — the two read operations on `/api/recovery/decision/v1`, the `DecisionLogEntry` and `DecisionLogPage` shapes field for field, the error envelope and its message identifiers, the `DecisionRecorded` envelope the ledger ingests, the tables the ledger owns, and a fake for each of them**, so that **the ledger implementation, the query API, the strict-mode waiters and rwb-reporting can build on Day 1 against one frozen description of what a decision entry is**.

This is the contract slice of legacy RWB-E1-008. It publishes no code and no row: it fixes the description that `RWB-P7-E1008-APP` implements, that `RWB-P7-E2005-APP` extends with filters, and that every service's record already satisfies on the shared topic. It owns **no legacy acceptance criterion**: AC1 to AC8 of RWB-E1-008 stay with `RWB-P7-E1008-APP`, and every criterion in section 7 is new (D-RCV-60) and tests only the published baseline.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story described its contract inside itself: two read paths on the monolith base (`decision-log` and `decision-log/{entryId}`), one response shape, four error codes, and a published Java interface for the writer. Under Architecture v5 the same description has three different readers on Day 1 and none of them can wait for the others:

- the **ledger implementation** of this service, which must know what an entry looks like before it can chain one (DP-03);
- the **strict-mode waiters** — debt transfer, write-off posting, auction sale, title transfer — which wait for the ledger to confirm a record before a point of no return (Architecture v5 slide 28), and which must know the shape they read back;
- **rwb-reporting** and the query API of Epic 2, which read the ledger rather than the events (ADR-018) and need the page shape and the paging rule before they can write an extract.

The contract is also where three architecture facts become binding rather than advisory. **The base is the service's**, `/api/recovery/decision/v1` (DP-13), so the monolith base disappears with no compatibility path. **The record comes from the shared topic**, `rwb.decision-record.v1`, with the `DecisionRecorded` envelope of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, so the ledger's input is a CloudEvents message and not an in-process call (DP-03). And **the table belongs to `rwb_decision`** (Ownership Map, `decision_log_entry`, P7), so no other service reads it and the cases and limits it names arrive as identifiers (DP-01).

Two points are published as the working read because no source closes them, and both are recorded: the Ownership Map gives P7 the two `GET` paths and **no append operation**, so the baseline declares no write path and the ingest of the shared topic stays the only writer (GAP-1224; ASM-2188); and Architecture v5 slide 14 names the ledger read `GET /decisions?caseId=` while the Ownership Map names `GET /decision-log` — the Ownership Map wins under the source precedence of Template and Rules §R3 (GAP-1230; ASM-2194).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service name, schema, base, topic, event-name, task-queue and package conventions of Template and Rules §R4 are fixed: `rwb-decision`, `rwb_decision`, `/api/recovery/decision/v1`, `rwb.decision.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics, `rwb.decision.<Event>.v1`, `rwb-decision`, `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision`.
- The entry fields are the ones fixed by TSD P7 v2 T3.1 (`DF-DEC-001` to `DF-DEC-031`) and by the physical schema: `id`, `case_id`, `decision_code`, `rule_id`, `rule_version`, `model_version`, `agent_version`, `inputs_ref`, `recommendation`, `approver_user_id`, `approval_level`, `final_call`, `override_reason`, `actions`, `outcome`, `decided_at`, `prev_hash`, `entry_hash`, `chain_seq`, `corrects_entry_id`, `actor_user_id`, `idempotency_key`.
- The decision codes and approval levels are rows in force of the rwb-case reference contract, `LOV-DECISION` and `LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL` (DP-07); the contract names them and carries no list of its own.
- The `DecisionRecorded` envelope is the one published by RWB-PLT-E1027-CON on the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`; this contract consumes it and restates only the fields the ledger stores.
- The `decision_log_entry` owner is P7 and the schema is `rwb_decision` under the Ownership Map rulings; the library objects `outbox_event`, `processed_event` and `idempotency_key` are PLT objects created in that schema by the DB story of this key.
- The paging parameters, their defaults and their maximum, and the full error body of the two reads, are Not specified in the source documents: the baseline publishes them as the working read (GAP-1229; ASM-2193).
- No build dependency and no approval stop: a CON story has no build dependency, is Day 1 by rule and groups in `CG-W1` (Template and Rules §R5.7); it is released at status Draft (realignment v1).

##### 4. Flow

1. The contract author fixes the two operations: method, path under `/api/recovery/decision/v1`, purpose, authorisation, paging and the error set, with owner `rwb-decision`.
2. The author fixes `DecisionLogEntry`: every field of the entry with its type, its field identifier and whether it may be absent, in the order of TSD P7 v2 T3.1.
3. The author fixes `DecisionLogPage`: the entries, the paging block and the ordering rule — `chain_seq` ascending, always.
4. The author fixes the error envelope: RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` with the message identifier, and the four cases of the legacy contract (401, 403 MSG-P4-002, 404 MSG-P4-003, 503 MSG-GEN-006).
5. The author fixes the consumed `DecisionRecorded` envelope: the CloudEvents attribute set, `ce_type` `rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1`, the key rule, the payload fields the ledger stores, and the dedupe key (`ce_id` into `idempotency_key` and `processed_event`).
6. The author fixes the owned tables: `decision_log_entry` in `rwb_decision`, plus the three library objects created there, and states explicitly what the ledger does not own.
7. The author writes the versioning rule: major version 1, a backward-compatible change versus a breaking change with a new major version, and the pinning rule for consumers.
8. The fake set is generated from the same examples: the ledger read fake, the `DecisionRecorded` fake, the reference fake, the authorise fake, the case fake and the seal target fake.
9. The contract test runs the fakes against the document on every change, and the drift test of each consumer fails the build on any difference from sections 12 and 13.
10. The baseline is published at v1 and every consumer pins it.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A published path is not under `/api/recovery/decision/v1`, or an append operation is invented | The lint fails the build; the base is the service's and the ledger has no write path | None | AC1 |
| X2 | A published shape drops a field, renames one or changes a type against TSD P7 v2 T3.1 | The schema validation fails the build; the field identifiers are the source | None | AC2 |
| X3 | An error is published without a message identifier, or with a status the legacy contract does not have | The validation fails the build; the four cases and their identifiers are fixed | None | AC3 |
| X4 | The `ce_type`, the key rule or a payload field of `DecisionRecorded` differs from RWB-PLT-E1027-CON | The envelope validation fails the build; the shared envelope is not redefined here | None | AC4 |
| X5 | A table of another owner is named as the ledger's, or a cross-schema key is published | The boundary check fails the build; the owned list is fixed | None | AC5 |
| X6 | A breaking change is made to a path, a field or the envelope | The change raises major version 2 and a new `ce_type`; v1 is never edited in place | None | AC7 |
| X7 | A value the consumers need is named by no source — the paging defaults, the maximum page size or the error body | The value is published as the working read of the assumption and the gap stays open | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1229; ASM-2193) | Section 3 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Publishes a document and a fake set; builds against nothing, reads no business data and starts on Day 1 |
| Negotiable | The paging defaults and the fixture set are open until v1 is frozen; the paths, the shapes, the error identifiers and the envelope are fixed |
| Valuable | Unblocks the ledger implementation, the query API, the strict-mode waiters and rwb-reporting on Day 1 |
| Estimable | Two operations, two shapes, one error envelope, one consumed envelope, one owned-table list and six fakes |
| Small | One sprint for the document, the fakes and the lint rules |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one lint, schema or fake assertion in section 16 |

