The eight criteria above are new and test only this deliverable: the local append-only hash-chained store, the verifier and the `DECISION_LOG` right. The legacy criteria of RWB-E1-008 belong to the other slices: the central store and the response shape of the two decision reads to RWB-P7-E1008-APP, the schema objects and the grants of `rwb_decision` to RWB-P7-E1008-DB, the access-event writers, the entry shape and break-glass to RWB-P4-E1039-APP, and the run across services to RWB-ITG-E1008-ITG. No legacy criterion text is copied into this story.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every decision writes one entry holding the seven field groups: inputs, versions, recommendation, approver, final call, actions and outcome | REQ-DRI-001; DF-DEC-004 to DF-DEC-015 |
| BR2 | A stored entry is never updated and never deleted; a correction is a new entry that names the entry it corrects | REQ-DRI-002; R-UNI-24; `tr_declog_append_only`; ADR-009 |
| BR3 | Entries form one chain in `chain_seq` order; `prev_hash` is the `entry_hash` of the entry before, and 64 zeros for the first | REQ-DRI-003; DF-DEC-017, DF-DEC-018 |
| BR4 | `entry_hash` is the SHA-256, in lower-case hexadecimal, of the canonical form: the entry's fields except `entry_hash` and the standard columns, as JSON with keys in alphabetical order, UTF-8, no spaces, timestamps in ISO 8601 UTC with microseconds, numbers as strings and empty fields as null; one implementation serves the store and the verifier | Legacy RWB-E1-008 BR4; ADR-009 |
| BR5 | The append is the last statement of the caller's transaction, so the action and its entry commit or roll back together | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; CTL-06 |
| BR6 | The verifier runs on every append and behind the local access-log read, and a break raises an incident and is reported to Compliance with MSG-P7-008; the daily Schedule, its 15-minute bound and the daily seal stay with `rwb-decision` | NFR-035; REQ-DRI-003; DP-10 |
| BR7 | Retention of entries follows the bank retention schedule; this story deletes nothing | DL26 |
| BR8 | The store is the local library object of DP-03 in schema `rwb_access`, written by the owner and read by the owner only; no service reads another service's store | DP-01; DP-03; Architecture v5 slides 20 and 28 |
| BR9 | `DECISION_LOG` R is required on the local access-log read and on the authorise answer that `rwb-decision` takes before it returns a central entry; the scope is applied through the entry's case, a missing right answers 403 MSG-P4-002 and an out-of-scope entry answers 404 MSG-P4-003 | FSD P4 A2.26 VR-P4-026-1; TSD P4 T6.1 and T6.2; ASM-1726 |
| BR10 | The right is resolved from the `permission` and `role` rows at the matrix version in force, with default deny; no role code, area code, letter or matrix version is written in Java | FSD P4 A2.4; TSD P4 T3.1 (`permission`); DP-07 |
| BR11 | No job, topic, table, interface or file copies this store or the central ledger to a data lake; reporting reads the shared topic | DP-17; Architecture v5 slide 37 |
| BR12 | This service reads no ACE table and no `v_ace_*` view: boundary rule BND-6 fails the build on a view name or a `public` table, and the rwb-access login holds no privilege on either | ADR-010; DP-01; DP-05 |
| BR13 | A failed append leaves nothing behind: the caller's transaction rolls back, the state change does not happen, the `chain_seq` is not consumed and the caller shows MSG-P7-003 | Legacy RWB-E1-008 AC7; R-UNI-39 |
| BR14 | No Temporal Schedule and no workflow sits in this story: DP-10 is carried by the 02:00 chain check of `rwb-decision` (JOB-14) | DP-10; Architecture v5 slide 44 |

##### 9. State transitions

`rwb-access` holds no case state machine of its own (TSD P4 T4). This story changes no case, task, role or permission status. The states it owns and observes are the states of a stored entry, of the chain and of a read.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| No entry | An append by a decision path of this service | The chain lock is held and the last entry verifies | Entry appended with the next `chain_seq` and the last `entry_hash` as `prev_hash` |
| No entry | An append by a decision path of this service | The canonical form of the last entry does not verify | No entry; the append is refused, an incident is raised and MSG-P7-008 is sent |
| Entry appended | The caller's transaction commits | None | Entry and state change are durable together |
| Entry appended | The caller's transaction rolls back | None | No entry; the `chain_seq` is not consumed |
| A stored entry is wrong | A correction is appended | `corrects_entry_id` names the corrected entry | A second entry exists; the first keeps its value and its position |
| Chain | The verifier runs on a write or on a read | Every hash and every link match | Chain unbroken, head named |
| Chain | The verifier runs on a write or on a read | A hash or a link does not match | Chain broken at the first failing entry; incident raised, MSG-P7-008 sent |
| Read request | The caller's roles are resolved | `DECISION_LOG` R is held and the entry's case is in scope | Entries returned with the verified head |
| Read request | The caller's roles are resolved | R is absent | 403 with MSG-P4-002 and one AC-DENY entry |
| Read request | The caller's roles are resolved | R is held and the entry's case is out of scope | 404 with MSG-P4-003 |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| rwb-access service identity (the rwb-access login, DP-02) | Appends entries, holds the chain lock, runs the verifier, resolves the right and writes the refusal entry |
| Every decision path of `rwb-access` (access events of RWB-P4-E1039-APP, the DoA lookup of RWB-P4-E2013-APP, administrative changes of RWB-P4-E1037-APP) | Writes through the store only; no path writes `decision_record` directly |
| RW-AUDIT Internal audit | Reads the local entries under `DECISION_LOG` R (FSD P4 A2.26.3.3) |
| RW-COMPLY Compliance and PDPA officer | Reads the local entries; receives the break report MSG-P7-008 |
| RW-COE Center of excellence analyst | Reads the local entries under `DECISION_LOG` R |
| Every bank role holding `DECISION_LOG` R | Reads the entries inside its scope, and no entry outside it |
| RW-PLATADM Platform administrator | Receives the incident on a break or on a failed append |
| `rwb-decision` (P7) | Takes the authorise answer for area `DECISION_LOG` before returning a central entry; owns the ledger, the ingest and JOB-14 |
| No role | May update or delete an entry, and no role reads an entry outside its scope |

The letters each role holds in `DECISION_LOG` are rows of the permission matrix, not values of this story, and they are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0984; ASM-1726). The refusal shape is 403 or 404 with an RFC 9457 problem response and `messageId` set; the unauthenticated shape is 401 with MSG-P4-001.

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Table in `rwb_access` | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | `decision_record` | all entry fields, including decision code, case reference, inputs reference, recommendation, approver, approval level, final call, actions, outcome and decided at | Write (append), read |
| DF-DEC-028 | `decision_record` | `chain_seq` | Write, read |
| DF-DEC-029 | `decision_record` | `corrects_entry_id` | Write, read |
| DF-DEC-030 | `decision_record` | `actor_user_id` | Write, read |
| DF-DEC-017, DF-DEC-018 | `decision_record` | `prev_hash`, `entry_hash` | Write, read |
| DF-REF-040 to DF-REF-044 | `permission` | `role_id`, `capability_area`, `letters`, `matrix_version`; the `DECISION_LOG` R letter and the version in force | Read |
| DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-039 | `role` | `role_code`, `role_class`, `default_scope`; the scope of an entry's test | Read |
| DF-REF-159 to DF-REF-184 | `reference_version`, `reference_row` of `rwb-case` | `LOV-CAPABILITY` with `DECISION_LOG`, at the version in force | Read through the reference-data contract (DP-07) |
| (outbox) | outbox library table in `rwb_access` | the row of each appended entry, written by the library | Write through the library |
| (inbox) | `processed_event` | none: this story consumes no event | None |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018, DF-DEC-028 to DF-DEC-030 | `decision_log_entry` of `rwb_decision` | none | Not read and not written: the central ledger is P7's |

No row of `case`, `document`, `assignment` or `rule_package` is read, and no foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01). The case reference in an entry is a value the writer recorded, not a join, and it is used for the scope test only. No ACE row and no view column is read or copied: the store holds IDs, codes, references, hashes and times only (BR12).

The column set beyond the five columns this story names, their physical types and the canonical form of the entry are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0984; ASM-1725); the story takes the entry fields from DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 and fixes the canonical form in BR4. Field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None new. The two operations this slice serves the store and the right behind are the ones the Work Package fixes, and this story adds no path, no query parameter and no response field:

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log` | The local access log of `rwb_access`, answered from the chain of this story and verified before it is returned | `DECISION_LOG` R, scope applied through the entry's case | Not applicable, read only |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | The authorise answer for area `DECISION_LOG`, right R and a case reference, taken by `rwb-decision` before it returns a central entry | Any authenticated caller; the answer repeats the caller's own right | Idempotent by identity, area, right and case within the cache window |

Errors on both operations: 401 no Workbench role (MSG-P4-001), 403 no `DECISION_LOG` R (MSG-P4-002), 404 entry of a case outside the caller's scope (MSG-P4-003), 503 the store cannot be written or the chain does not verify (MSG-P7-003). The request and answer field names of both operations are published by RWB-P4-E1037-CON and RWB-P4-AD007-CON; this story changes neither schema. That `DECISION_LOG` R, rather than the `PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION` R that TSD P4 API-P4-008 names for this path, governs the local read in this slice is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0984; ASM-1726).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. The caller's identity arrives in the session, the right is resolved from the rows of this service, and the reference list reaches it through the client library of `rwb-case` (DP-07). The one hop and the 2 s budget of DP-11 apply to the inbound calls only.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Key | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | PLT library, published for each append; consumed by P7 and P9 | `entryId` | the hash-chained entry: entry ID, case reference, decision code, rule ID, rule version, inputs reference, recommendation, approver reference, approval level, final call, actions, outcome, decided at, `prev_hash`, `entry_hash` |

CloudEvents 1.0 envelope in binary mode, IDs and references only, no personal data. The library publishes it; this story adds no topic and no event type of its own, and it publishes no `rwb.access.<Event>.v1` message, because the events of this service are `AccessPolicyChanged` and `DoaLimitChanged` (Architecture v5 slides 14 and 43) and they belong to RWB-P4-E1037-APP.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. `rwb-access` is a reference-data owner in Architecture v5 slide 14 (events: none), and the chain of this story is read from its own schema.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The append, the verifier and the right answer are synchronous work in the caller's thread. `rwb-access` registers no activity on queue `rwb-access` in this story, and the six-monthly access review list (JOB-18) belongs to RWB-P4-AD008-APP.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Temporal Schedule and no Quartz job sits in this story: DP-10 is carried by `rwb-decision`, where the chain check of the central ledger runs at 02:00 as JOB-14 (RWB-P7-E1008-OPS). This slice starts no workflow and registers no Schedule.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access.record`, module `record`, in the service root `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`. The migration sits in the per-service Flyway sequence of the service.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting | none; a gap if the story needs lake data |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

This is a secondary slice: it adds no new build dependency of its own, and the metadata rows "Depends on (build)" and "Contract dependencies" stay exactly as this Work Package fixes them. The H dependencies of DP-03, DP-07, DP-15 and DP-19 arrive with the platform contract libraries and with the baseline of this service (RWB-P4-E1037-APP and its contract story), and DP-10 adds no dependency here at all because this story starts no Schedule: the only chain check of the estate is P7's JOB-14. DP-01 and DP-17 apply as prohibitions: this service reads no other schema, and no element of the build copies the store to a data lake.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `V1008_1__decision_record.sql` | Migration | Creates `decision_record` in `rwb_access` with the five named columns and the entry fields, the trigger `tr_declog_append_only`, the two indexes and the grants; no update and no delete grant is issued |
| `DecisionRecordRepository` | Repository | Inserts one row and reads a range in `chain_seq` order; the class exposes no update method and no delete method |
| `CanonicalEntryForm` | Service | Builds the canonical JSON of BR4; the one implementation used by the store and by the verifier |
| `DecisionRecordStore` | Service | Takes the chain lock, reads the head, sets `chain_seq` and `prev_hash`, hashes, inserts and releases the lock |
| `HashChainVerifier` | Service | Recomputes a range in `chain_seq` order in batches and reports count, head `chain_seq`, head `entry_hash` and the first break |
| `ChainBreakReporter` | Service | Raises the incident and sends MSG-P7-008 to RW-COMPLY on a break |
| `AccessLogChainReader` | Service | Answers the range of the local access-log read with the verified head in the `chain` field |
| `DecisionLogRightResolver` | Service | Resolves `DECISION_LOG` R from `permission` and `role` at the matrix version in force, applies the scope through the entry's case, and answers 403 or 404 |
| `DecisionRecordEntry` | Entity | Maps `decision_record`; immutable, with no setter |
| `record-modules.yaml` | Rule table | The package name and the allowed source object list of boundary rule BND-6, which is empty for this service |

**Database and migrations**

- Migration `V1008_1__decision_record.sql`, in the `rwb-access` sequence of DP-15, creates `decision_record` in schema `rwb_access` with the entry fields of DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 and the five named columns `chain_seq` (bigint, not null, unique), `prev_hash` (char(64), not null), `entry_hash` (char(64), not null), `corrects_entry_id` (uuid, references `decision_record` (id)) and `actor_user_id` (uuid); it adds the index `ix_declog_actor_time` on (`actor_user_id`, `decided_at`) and the index `ix_declog_chain` on (`chain_seq`).
- The same migration creates the function that refuses a change and the trigger `tr_declog_append_only` on UPDATE and DELETE, and it revokes UPDATE and DELETE on `decision_record` from the service role.
- The column set beyond the five named columns, their physical types and the choice of a database trigger over a rule are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0984; ASM-1725); the types above follow the legacy physical schema of the key and are confirmed with the DB story of this service.
- No table of another service is created, altered or read, and no foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01). The copy of the same objects in `rwb_decision` is RWB-P7-E1008-DB's and is not touched here.
- An applied Flyway version is never edited; a change is a new version with a later number.

**Configuration and reference data**

- The chain key of the advisory lock is configuration, per service, and never the key of the central ledger.
- The genesis value is 64 zeros, held as configuration rather than as a literal in code; the canonical form of BR4 is the one implementation of `CanonicalEntryForm`.
- The capability area `DECISION_LOG` and the letters of each role are rows of `permission` and of `LOV-CAPABILITY`, read through DP-07 at the version in force; no area code, role code or letter is a constant (BR10).
- The feature switch is `rwb.access.decision-record`, read as a parameter; off means the append path is closed and the service answers its own message rather than writing an unrecorded decision.
- The login is the rwb-access login (DP-02): Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0984; ASM-1725).

**Build steps**

1. The migration with the table, the trigger, the indexes and the grants, and a fixture that attempts an UPDATE and a DELETE through the service login and as the schema owner; tests for AC1.
2. `CanonicalEntryForm` with golden vectors (a fixed entry to a fixed hash) checked into the test resources, and a fixture that changes one character of the canonical form.
3. `DecisionRecordStore` with the chain lock, the genesis case, the consecutive `chain_seq` and the parallel appends; tests for AC2.
4. `HashChainVerifier` on the write path and on the read path, with the break at `chain_seq` 51 and the refused append after a break; tests for AC2.
5. The correction path with `corrects_entry_id` and the read order; tests for AC3.
6. `DecisionLogRightResolver` and `AccessLogChainReader` behind the two operations, with the scope test through the entry's case; tests for AC4, AC5 and AC6.
7. `ChainBreakReporter` on the ACE incident and notification paths, with MSG-P7-008.
8. The lake-copy guardrail test and boundary rule BND-6 with two fixture classes; tests for AC7 and AC8.
9. A contract-fake run of the whole path, so the story builds before the library contract and the central read contract are published.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.access.decision-record`, read as a parameter. Off closes the append path and fails the guardrail tests; it never allows an unrecorded write.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the golden hash vectors give the same result on the build server and on a developer machine, `decision_record` exists in `rwb_access` with the trigger and the grants and no update or delete path, the verifier names the first break on the tampered chain, the local read answers under `DECISION_LOG` R with 403 and 404 as specified, the lake-copy scan finds nothing, and the build is green and red on the two fixtures of the boundary rule.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Where it is produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | The caller has no session | Your session has ended. Sign in again to continue. | This story, on both operations |
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller holds no `DECISION_LOG` R | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | This story, on both operations; one AC-DENY entry |
| MSG-P4-003 | The entry belongs to a case outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. | This story, on both operations |
| MSG-P7-003 | The store cannot be written, or the chain does not verify | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | This story, on both operations |
| MSG-P7-008 | The verifier finds a break | The decision log check for {date} found a break at entry {entryId}. Entries from that entry on cannot be relied on until Compliance reviews them. | This story, on a break found on a write or on a read; P7 uses the same text on its 02:00 check |
| Build log | A class names a `v_ace_*` view or a `public` table | Boundary rule BND-6 broken: {class} names {object}. A recovery class names no ACE view and no public table. | This story, in the build |

For MSG-P4-002, {action} names the action the caller tried — "read the access log" or "read a decision record" — and never a case fact or an entry value. The five message texts are copied unchanged from RWB-E1-008 and from the P4 access messages of the legacy model; this story writes no new text. Every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set and `instance` naming the request.

| SCR-43 Roles and access, access-log panel | Chain broken | The first failing entry is named and no entry from that point is shown as verified; the incident reference is with RW-COMPLY |
| SCR-43 Roles and access, access-log panel | Refused | 403 with MSG-P4-002 for a role without R; 404 with MSG-P4-003 for an entry outside the scope |

The field list of the composite route and the rendering of the panel belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON and to the screen work of the epic, not here.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the chain key, the feature switch, the genesis value and the retention class are configuration; the capability area and the letters are rows of `permission` and of the reference list, read with the matrix version in force.
- No personal data in the store, in the event, in logs, in workflow inputs or in tests: the entry holds IDs, codes, references, hashes and times only, and every fixture is synthetic.
- One canonical form and one hash implementation for writing and verifying (BR4); a second implementation would make a real break indistinguishable from a hash mismatch.
- No update and no delete path: no repository method, no database grant, no endpoint and no trigger path exists for either, and the tests assert the refusal rather than rely on a review.
- A correction is a new entry and never an edit; the corrected entry keeps its value, its `chain_seq` and its `entry_hash`.
- The store is the owner's own schema object (DP-01, DP-03): no service reads another service's `decision_record`, and the central ledger is P7's.
- No ACE data and no `public` table: a class that names a view fails the build, and the login holds no privilege on either (BR12).
- No copy of the log leaves the database (BR11, DP-17); the lake-copy guardrail is a regression test, not a one-off check.
- No Schedule and no workflow in this story (BR14): DP-10 is P7's JOB-14, and an extra chain check in this service would double the incident path.
- One migration per story in the service's own Flyway sequence (DP-15); an applied version is never edited.

##### 1. Story

As an **ACE database engineer**, I want **the central decision ledger created in schema `rwb_decision` on the per-service Flyway sequence — `decision_log_entry` with its thirty columns, its chain columns, its keys and its indexes, the append-only enforcement of a missing UPDATE and DELETE grant plus the trigger `tr_declog_append_only` and the function `refuse_change`, the three library objects of the event platform, the grants of the `rwb-decision` login and a tested rollback — **so that** the ledger of legacy RWB-E1-008 can hold every entry of every service immutably in its own schema, no other service can reach it, and a change made outside the service is impossible or detectable.

This is the database slice of RWB-E1-008. It delivers, in schema `rwb_decision`:

- the migration that creates `decision_log_entry` after the V0001 baseline, with the twenty-two columns and physical types of the legacy `Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v6.sql` and of TSD P7 v2 T3.1 (DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-031) plus the seven standard record columns;
- the **append-only guarantee** in its three parts: no UPDATE and no DELETE grant for the service login, the trigger `tr_declog_append_only BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON decision_log_entry FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION refuse_change()`, and the owner separated from the service it serves so that the trigger is the owner's own guard;
- the **hash-chain columns** `chain_seq bigint NOT NULL`, `prev_hash char(64) NOT NULL` and `entry_hash char(64) NOT NULL`, with the unique key on `chain_seq` that makes a chain position single, and the unique key on `idempotency_key` that makes a record single;
- the **indexes** the two reads and the verifier need: the primary key on `id`, the unique `chain_seq`, `ix_declog_case_time` on `(case_id, decided_at)`, the legacy `ix_declog_actor_time` on `(actor_user_id, decided_at)`, the legacy `ix_declog_rule` on `(rule_id, rule_version)`, `ix_decision_log_entry_case_id` and `ix_decision_log_entry_corrects_entry_id`;
- the **three library objects** `outbox_event`, `processed_event` and `idempotency_key` created from the event platform template in this schema, because every service writes its own outbox and inbox in its own schema;
- the **grants and the login** of the service (DP-02, DP-15), whose name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1232; ASM-2196);
- the explicit statement that the schema holds **no foreign key, no view and no grant that names another schema**: `case_id` is a plain uuid and not a key into `rwb_case` (DP-01), and `delegation_limit`, `parameter_catalog`, `reference_row`, `approval` and `rule_*` are not created here.

The eight legacy acceptance criteria stay with `RWB-P7-E1008-APP`; every criterion in section 7 is new (D-RCV-60) and tests only the schema deliverable.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story added one migration, `V_E1_008__declog_chain.sql`, to a single `recovery` schema of 92 tables with one shared login, and it relied on `decision_log_entry` having been created by RWB-E1-001. Two of its three guarantees were database statements — the missing grant and the trigger — and the third was code. After the split the table moves to `rwb_decision` (Ownership Map, `decision_log_entry`, P7; Architecture v5 slide 41), and the same three guarantees must survive the move intact, because they are the reason Audit can rely on the log at all (REQ-DRI-002, CTL-06, ADR-009 and ADR-022).

The append-only pair is deliberately two mechanisms and not one. A grant alone is defeated by the owner of the table, and a trigger alone is defeated by anyone who may disable it; together they cover the two roles that could change a row (legacy AC1 tests both in one scenario, and the chain check of AC4 covers the third route, a change made with the trigger disabled). This story therefore creates the table under a schema owner that the service never uses to write, grants the service login INSERT and SELECT only, and installs `refuse_change` as the owner's guard.

The chain columns are the contract with the algorithm. `char(64)` is fixed by DF-DEC-017 and DF-DEC-018 and by the DDL of the legacy schema; the unique key on `chain_seq` is what makes "the entry before" unambiguous in a parallel append, and the unique key on `idempotency_key` is what makes a repeated envelope a repeat and not a second decision. The index set is the legacy set plus the two the two reads add, so the query by case and date and the query by actor and date are both indexed and the verifier's sequential walk is a primary-key scan.

Three deltas are the schema's own statement of the target. `case_id` loses its foreign key: a key into `rwb_case` would be a cross-schema key, which DP-01 forbids and the boundary test fails, so the case is an identifier and its existence is checked over P3's contract. The three library objects exist here and not in `rwb_integration`, because the outbox and the inbox are the producer's and the consumer's own. And no data-lake object, no watermark and no partition table appears: the copy is retired (DP-17) and the ledger keeps its chain and its daily seal instead.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The V0001 baseline of `rwb_decision` exists on the per-service Flyway sequence from RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and the platform DB work: the schema, the `flyway_schema_history` table and the standard record columns of TSD P7 v2 T3.0 (`is_active`, `state`, `version`, `created_at`, `created_by`, `updated_at`, `updated_by`).
- The ACE database and the per-service login policy are in place; the login of `rwb-decision` is created by the platform DB work and its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1232; ASM-2196).
- The ownership map is the only source of table ownership: `decision_log_entry`, `approval`, `rule_package`, `rule_package_version`, `rule_row` and `rule_test_case` are P7 and in `rwb_decision`; `delegation_limit` is P4 and in `rwb_access`; `parameter_catalog`, `parameter_value`, `reference_row`, `reference_version` and `lov_value` are P3 and in `rwb_case`; the ACE views are P1's.
- The column set, the types and the constraints are the legacy physical schema's, character for character, and the field identifiers are TSD P7 v2 T3.1's (DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-031).
- The trigger body is the legacy one: `RAISE EXCEPTION '% is append only: % refused', TG_TABLE_NAME, TG_OP`, which is what makes the message read `decision_log_entry is append only` in AC1.
- The three library objects follow the template of the event platform (RWB-PLT-TE006-CON); their column set is not restated here and is not fixed by any source of this read set (GAP-1232; ASM-2196).
- No approval is required to run a Draft migration on a development database; the migration is released to SIT only after the checks of section 16 pass.

##### 4. Flow

1. The ACE database engineer checks out the `rwb-decision` migration folder and confirms the highest applied version on the sequence (the V0001 baseline).
2. The engineer adds this story's migration after that version, with a guard that refuses to run before the baseline.
3. The engineer creates `decision_log_entry` with the twenty-two columns of section 13 and the seven standard record columns, in the order of the physical schema.
4. The engineer adds the keys: primary key on `id`, unique `uk_decision_log_entry (entry_hash, chain_seq, idempotency_key)`, unique `uk_decision_log_entry_chain_seq (chain_seq)`, unique `uk_decision_log_entry_idempotency_key (idempotency_key)`.
5. The engineer adds the indexes: `ix_decision_log_entry_case_id`, `ix_decision_log_entry_corrects_entry_id`, `ix_declog_case_time (case_id, decided_at)`, `ix_declog_actor_time (actor_user_id, decided_at)` and `ix_declog_rule (rule_id, rule_version)`.
6. The engineer creates the function `refuse_change()` and the trigger `tr_declog_append_only` on `decision_log_entry` only; the interaction ledger's trigger of the same function is P1's and is not created here.
7. The engineer applies the event platform's template for `outbox_event`, `processed_event` and `idempotency_key` in `rwb_decision`, unchanged.
8. The engineer writes the grant script for the `rwb-decision` login: usage on the schema, `SELECT, INSERT` on `decision_log_entry`, `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE` on the three library objects, and usage on the sequences those objects own; no UPDATE and no DELETE on the ledger, and nothing to any other login.
9. The engineer writes the rollback: the undo per migration in reverse order, with the ledger rows preserved where a later change only adds an object.
10. The pipeline applies the baseline and this story's migrations to an empty schema and then to a copy of the SIT schema, and runs the catalogue checks: keys, indexes, trigger, function, grants, and a scan for any foreign key, view, synonym or grant that names another schema or `public`.
11. The check that the ledger has no UPDATE and no DELETE grant for the service login and no write path through a view is a catalogue query: any hit fails the build (BR2).
12. The append-only pair is exercised: an UPDATE and a DELETE as the service login fail on the grant, and the same two as the schema owner fail with `decision_log_entry is append only: UPDATE refused`.
13. The rollback is exercised on a copy: the schema returns to its pre-migration shape and the library objects are dropped last.
14. The migration is recorded in the release notes of the sequence with its version and its checksum.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message |
|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A migration runs before the V0001 baseline | Flyway refuses with an unresolved baseline and nothing is applied | Pipeline error, no message id |
| X2 | `decision_log_entry` already exists in the sequence | The repeatable guard refuses to re-create it and the migration is marked as already applied | Pipeline error, no message id |
| X3 | A foreign key, view, synonym or grant names another schema or `public` | The catalogue check fails the build; the object is removed and the value is read over a contract instead | Check finding, no message id |
| X4 | The grant script grants UPDATE or DELETE on `decision_log_entry` | The grant check fails the build; the ledger is append only (BR2) | Check finding, no message id |
| X5 | The trigger `tr_declog_append_only` is missing or disabled on a fresh apply | The object check fails the build; the trigger is part of the migration | Check finding, no message id |
| X6 | The grant script runs before the login exists | The script fails on the missing role; the platform DB story creates the login first | Database error, no message id |
| X7 | `case_id` carries a foreign key into `rwb_case`, or `delegation_limit` is created here | The boundary and ownership checks fail the build; both are other owners' | Check finding, no message id |
| X8 | A column is needed but no field identifier exists | The column is not invented: it carries the placeholder and the gap is raised | GAP-1232 |
| X9 | The rollback would drop `decision_log_entry` and lose the chain | The rollback drops only what this migration added and keeps the table and its rows | Review finding, no message id |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | One migration, one trigger, one grant script and a rollback on the service's own sequence; nothing to build against |
| Negotiable | Constraint and index names follow the platform naming library; the column set is fixed by the field identifiers and the legacy physical schema |
| Valuable | The ledger has a schema that is granted, indexed, append-only three ways and reversible, and no other service can reach it |
| Estimable | One table, one function and one trigger, five indexes, one grant script, three library objects, one rollback |
| Small | Days, not weeks, with the catalogue checks |
| Testable | Every criterion is a catalogue query or a pipeline run in section 16 |

These criteria are new and test the database artefacts only: no legacy acceptance criterion is repeated, and every physical value — table, column, type, constraint name, index name, trigger name, function name, migration name and the refusal message — is the legacy or technical-specification value, character for character.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The ledger row carries the seven field groups of REQ-DRI-001 with the field identifiers and physical types of TSD P7 v2 T3.1 | REQ-DRI-001; DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-031 |
| BR2 | A stored entry is never updated or deleted: the service login has no UPDATE and no DELETE grant, and the trigger `tr_declog_append_only` refuses both for the schema owner | REQ-DRI-002; R-UNI-24; legacy AC1; ADR-009 |
| BR3 | `chain_seq` is unique and `prev_hash` is the `entry_hash` of the entry before, 64 zeros for the first; `entry_hash` and `prev_hash` are 64 characters | REQ-DRI-003; DF-DEC-017, DF-DEC-018, DF-DEC-028 |
| BR4 | A repeated `idempotency_key` is refused by a unique key, so a repeated envelope cannot become a second entry | R-UNI-40; DF-DEC-031 |
| BR5 | Each service's objects live in its own schema under its own login; one login per service | DP-01, DP-02, DP-15; Architecture v5 slide 29 |
| BR6 | No foreign key, view or grant crosses a schema boundary: `case_id` is an identifier and the case exists in P3's contract | DP-01; Architecture v5 slide 29 |
| BR7 | Every service writes its own outbox and inbox in its own schema, so the three library objects are created here | Ownership Map ruling on `outbox_event`, `processed_event` and `idempotency_key`; Architecture v5 slides 11 and 20 |
| BR8 | No business value is fixed by a constraint: the decision codes, approval levels and limits are rows of other owners, and no check constraint carries them | DP-07; Principle 1 |
| BR9 | The retention class is a property of the bank schedule and not of the schema; no row is deleted by a job of this story | DL26; BR2 |

##### 9. State transitions

None in the runtime sense: a table has no state machine, and a stored entry has no states. The states this story moves through are the migration states of the service's Flyway history — pending, applied, failed, undone — and the row-level columns the schema exposes are the standard ones of TSD P7 v2 T3.0. The ingest states of an envelope and the chain-check states of a business date are the app story's and leave no additional column here.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Absent | Migration applied | The baseline is present and the objects do not exist | Applied (table, trigger, function, indexes, library objects, grants) |
| Applied | Migration fails part way | A statement fails | Failed (rolled back, the pod does not become ready) |
| Applied | Rollback run on a copy | The reverse order is followed | Undone (the library objects, the trigger, the function, then the table) |
| Applied | A second pipeline run | Nothing is pending | Applied (no change, no new checksum) |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The ACE database engineer (any team, per U3) | Writes and runs the migration, the trigger, the grant script and the rollback |
| The service owner of rwb-decision | Approves a destructive change; none is planned here |
| The platform DB owner (RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, the platform DB story) | Owns the sequence, the baseline, the login policy and the connection pool per login |
| RW-PLATADM Platform administrator | Reads the migration runs on the job monitor; the ledger itself is not theirs to change |
| RW-AUDIT Internal audit | Reads ledger rows through the service's two operations, never through SQL |
| The schema owner | Owns the objects and is refused an update or a delete by its own trigger |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A schema change is not a credit decision |

The grantee is named only as the `rwb-decision` login (DP-02); its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1232; ASM-2196). No personal name and no credential appears in a migration, a script or a run book.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Sequencing.** The service's Flyway sequence is owned by RWB-PLT-E1044-CON. The V0001 baseline creates the schema, the history table and the standard columns. This story adds the next versions after the baseline:

| Version | File | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| V0001 | baseline, from the platform DB story | Schema `rwb_decision`, history table, standard columns |
| next after the baseline | `..._decision_log_entry.sql` | Creates `decision_log_entry` with its columns, keys and indexes |
| next after that | `..._declog_append_only.sql` | Creates the function `refuse_change()` and the trigger `tr_declog_append_only` |
| next after that | `..._event_library_objects.sql` | Creates `outbox_event`, `processed_event` and `idempotency_key` from the event platform template |
| next after that | `..._decision_grants.sql` | Usage on the schema, the ledger grants and the library grants for the `rwb-decision` login |

The legacy migration name `V_E1_008__declog_chain.sql` is recorded as the source of the chain columns; the monolith name and number are not reused on the service sequence. The exact version numbers are assigned by the sequence owner at build time; the order above is fixed by this story.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables. The table and the three library objects live in `rwb_decision` | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`. The library writes its record into the service's own tables, which the writer stories own | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON (carried by the writer's story; named here) |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case. `lov_value` and the reference tables are never created or read here | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit. The chain check is a Schedule and writes no table of this story | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1`. The schema name follows the same short name: `rwb_decision` under `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema. This story adds four migrations after the baseline and reuses no monolith name | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON (the sequence owner; named here) |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting. No lake object, watermark or partition exists | none; gap if the story needs lake data |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route. No screen reads this schema; the edge reads the two operations | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |

The patterns **not claimed** here are DP-02 (one login per service — delivered by the platform DB work and used, not designed, here), DP-04, DP-05, DP-06, DP-08, DP-09 (the library objects are applied from the template and the platform contract is not a dependency of this story), DP-11, DP-12, DP-14, DP-16, DP-18 and DP-20.

**Table definition.** `decision_log_entry` — `id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()`, `case_id uuid`, `decision_code varchar(8) NOT NULL`, `rule_id varchar(20)`, `rule_version varchar(20)`, `model_version varchar(40)`, `agent_version varchar(40)`, `inputs_ref varchar(400) NOT NULL`, `recommendation jsonb`, `approver_user_id uuid`, `approval_level varchar(4)`, `final_call varchar(40) NOT NULL`, `override_reason varchar(1000)`, `actions jsonb`, `outcome jsonb`, `decided_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()`, `prev_hash char(64) NOT NULL`, `entry_hash char(64) NOT NULL`, `chain_seq bigint NOT NULL`, `corrects_entry_id uuid`, `actor_user_id uuid`, `idempotency_key varchar(80)`, plus `is_active boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true`, `state varchar(40)`, `version integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1`, `created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()`, `created_by uuid`, `updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()`, `updated_by uuid`. The three unique constraints are `UNIQUE (entry_hash, chain_seq, idempotency_key)`, `UNIQUE (chain_seq)` and `UNIQUE (idempotency_key)`.

**Append-only enforcement.** `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION refuse_change() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN RAISE EXCEPTION '% is append only: % refused', TG_TABLE_NAME, TG_OP; END; $$;` and `CREATE TRIGGER tr_declog_append_only BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON decision_log_entry FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION refuse_change();`. The function is created once in `rwb_decision`; the interaction ledger's trigger of the same function is P1's and is not this story's. The service login receives `SELECT, INSERT` and nothing else on the table, which is the first half of AC1; the trigger is the second half, and the chain check of the app story is the third.

**No cross-schema key.** `case_id` is a uuid and carries no foreign key, although the legacy schema declared `fk_decision_log_entry_case_id` to `recovery_case` and TSD P7 v2 T3.3 declares the relationship: in the target the case is P3's row in another schema, so the key would cross a boundary that DP-01 forbids and the boundary test fails. The case is verified through P3's contract on the read (GAP-1231; ASM-2195). `corrects_entry_id` names an entry of the same table and keeps its self-reference at the application level, not as a database key, for the same reason the chain is advisory-locked rather than key-enforced.

**No business value in a constraint.** The decision codes, the approval levels and the rule identifiers are values of a list or a rule package of another owner. No check constraint carries them: a new code must be a data change, not a migration (BR8). The one check the legacy story added — `ck_declog_case (case_id IS NOT NULL OR decision_code LIKE 'AC-%')` — is kept as a business-free structural rule: an entry either names a case or is an access event, and an access event is any code that starts with `AC-`.

**Library objects.** `outbox_event`, `processed_event` and `idempotency_key` are created in `rwb_decision` from the template published by the event platform (RWB-PLT-TE006-CON) and are not modified here.

**Grants.** `GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA rwb_decision TO <the rwb-decision login>`; `GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON decision_log_entry TO <the rwb-decision login>`; `GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key TO <the rwb-decision login>`; usage on the sequences those objects own. No UPDATE and no DELETE on the ledger, no grant to a shared login, no grant to another service's login, and no grant on `rwb_case`, `rwb_access` or an ACE schema. The grantee name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1232; ASM-2196).

**Rollback.** Per migration, in reverse order: the grant script is reversed by revoking the grants it made; the library objects, then the trigger and the function, then the table are dropped. A ledger row inserted between the two runs keeps its `id` and `chain_seq` where the rollback only reverses an added object, so a later re-apply never rewrites a chain position (BR9). The rollback is exercised on a copy of the SIT schema and recorded in the run book.

**Done when.** The migrations apply twice without a change, the catalogue checks pass, the append-only pair is proven for the login and for the owner, no cross-schema object exists, the rollback returns the schema to its pre-migration shape, and the tests in section 16 pass.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| Database error, no message id | A migration runs before the baseline or finds an object already present | The migration fails and nothing is applied; the pipeline stops |
| Database error, no message id | A grant script runs before the login exists | The script fails on the missing role; the platform DB story creates the login first |
| Check finding, no message id | A foreign key, view or grant names another schema or `public` | The pipeline check fails the build; the object is removed |
| Check finding, no message id | The ledger carries an UPDATE or a DELETE grant, or the trigger is absent | The pipeline check fails the build |
| `decision_log_entry is append only: UPDATE refused` | An UPDATE is attempted by the schema owner | Raised by `refuse_change`; the attempt is written to the ACE audit and SOC log by the caller |
| `decision_log_entry is append only: DELETE refused` | A DELETE is attempted by the schema owner | Raised by `refuse_change`; the same audit path |
| MSG-P7-009 | A record reaches the database with a required field empty | The decision record was refused: {field} is missing or not valid. Raised by the application, not by a database constraint |
| MSG-P7-003 | The ingest cannot insert the row | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. Raised by the application |

The database enforces what does not change: keys, uniqueness, the chain position, the refusal of an update and a delete, and the schema boundary. The business checks — a known decision code, a rule ID with its version, a final call in force — stay in the application, so a business person can change them without a migration.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen. The result of a migration is visible in the release pipeline and in the service's Flyway history: pending, applied, failed, undone, each with a version and a checksum. The table exposes the standard record columns of section 9 and no state of its own; the audit screens read entries through the two operations of the service and never through SQL.

##### 1. Story

As a **DevOps engineer of the platform**, I want **the `rwb-decision` service deployed with Flyway running on start in `rwb_decision` under the service's own login, a drift gate before SIT, UAT and PROD, the ingest consumer and the 02:00 chain check running with their alerts, an append-only verification job that proves the grant and the trigger are still in place, a backup and restore procedure that is safe for a ledger nothing may change, and a run book for each failure**, so that **the ledger is deployed, watched, proven immutable and recoverable without a hand ever touching a row**.

This is the deployment slice of legacy RWB-E1-008. It delivers:

- the **pipeline** of the service on the golden template — build, unit and contract tests, image, the migration stage, the API deployment and the worker deployment on the same task queue (ADR-021; Architecture v5 slide 33);
- **Flyway on service start** in `rwb_decision` with the service's own login from the key store, the service's own history table and the two-instance lock, so a start applies exactly the pending migrations of this service (DP-15);
- the **drift gate** before SIT, UAT and PROD: the migrations applied to a clean container and compared with the target schema through a read-only account, and the deployment stopped on a difference;
- the **configuration and the secrets**: the consumer group and its retry and dead-letter topics, the chain algorithm parameters, the 15-minute notice budget, the notification group, the seal target, and every credential as a key-store reference (NFR-052);
- the **ingest consumer and the chain-check job** as operational objects: the consumer lag monitor against the 5-minute completeness target of BR10, the 02:00 Schedule, the incident route and the Compliance notice;
- the **append-only verification job** that queries the catalogue for a missing trigger, a missing function and any UPDATE or DELETE grant on `decision_log_entry`, and fails an alert when one is found (BR2 of the DB story, AC1 of the app story);
- the **backup and restore** of an append-only ledger: point-in-time recovery, a restore into an isolated environment, the chain re-verified from the first entry to the last after the restore, and the seal files in immutable storage used as the external reference of the last hash;
- the **run book**: one entry per failure — a failed migration, a lagging consumer, a dead-lettered envelope, a chain break, a missing seal, a drift finding and a restore.

The eight legacy acceptance criteria stay with `RWB-P7-E1008-APP`; every criterion in section 7 is new (D-RCV-60) and tests only the deployment deliverable.

##### 2. Business rationale

A ledger that nothing may change is only as trustworthy as the deployment that surrounds it. Three failure modes are specific to this story and none of them is a code defect:

- **A migration applied by the wrong principal.** The append-only guarantee is a grant plus a trigger. If the pipeline applies migrations as the service login, or if a later migration is run by hand with an owner that grants too much, the first half of the guarantee is gone and nothing notices: the table still looks right, the inserts still work, and an UPDATE simply succeeds. The run-at-start rule with the migration account from the key store, and the verification job of this story, are what keep the pair intact (ADR-021; NFR-052).
- **A silent gap in the ingest.** The ledger is complete only if the consumer keeps up: Architecture v5 slide 28 sets a 5-minute completeness target and an alert for a missing record. A consumer that is down, a dead-lettered envelope that nobody reads, or a lag that grows overnight produces exactly the failure the legacy story was written to prevent — a decision that happened and was never recorded.
- **A restore that quietly rewrites the past.** A restore is the one operation that can produce a ledger which is internally consistent and yet wrong: a point-in-time restore to before the last entries, a restored copy with the trigger missing, or a restore that is then "repaired" by an update. The chain makes the first detectable and the seal in immutable storage makes it provable; the run book makes the second and the third forbidden.

The deployment is also the place where three target facts become operational. The base of the service is `/api/recovery/decision/v1` behind gateway-bff (DP-13, DP-19), so the route a smoke test calls is the gateway's and not a pod's. The ingest is a Kafka consumer on the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03), so its health is measured in lag and dead letters and not in HTTP 200. And there is no data-lake copy (DP-17), so the nightly job that used to ship partitions is replaced by the 02:00 chain check and its seal — the same JOB-14 id, a different mechanism (DP-10; Architecture v5 slide 44).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service is built from the platform template and deployed by the golden pipeline: an API deployment and a worker deployment on the same task queue, on the platform's Helm chart (RWB-PLT-TPL; Architecture v5 slide 33).
- Schema `rwb_decision`, its `flyway_schema_history` table and the `decision_log_entry` objects exist on the per-service Flyway sequence of RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and from RWB-P7-E1008-DB (DP-15).
- The migration account, the read-only drift account and the runtime account of `rwb-decision` are entries in the key store (NFR-052); their names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1232; ASM-2196).
- The shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` exists with its retry topic and its `.dlt` on the Kafka platform of RWB-PLT-EVT; the consumer group of the ingest is this story's to configure, and its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1233; ASM-2197).
- The workflow kit and the `rwb-recovery` namespace are live (RWB-PLT-E1071-CON), so the 02:00 Schedule runs on the `rwb-decision` queue.
- The gateway route of RWB-PLT-N001-CON exists, so the smoke test calls the two reads through gateway-bff and not a pod.
- The 5-minute completeness target, the 15-minute notice budget and the 02:00 run time are the architecture's; the alert thresholds, the dashboard panel set, the RPO and the RTO are Not specified in the source documents and are set as the working read (GAP-1233; ASM-2197), (GAP-1234; ASM-2198).
- No build dependency: the story has no build dependency and is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Pipeline: build the service image from the template, run the unit tests and the contract tests against the published baseline and its fakes, and publish the image.
2. Pipeline: run the migration stage — apply every pending migration of `rwb_decision` to a clean container with the migration account read from the key store.
3. Pipeline: run the drift gate before the deployment to SIT, UAT and PROD — compare the object list produced by the migrations with the target schema through the read-only account, and stop the deployment on a difference.
4. Deployment: on service start, Flyway reads the migration account from the key store, applies each pending migration once in version order and writes the checksum to the service's own history table; a second instance that starts at the same moment waits for the Flyway lock and finds nothing pending.
5. Deployment: the API pods become ready only after the migrations and after the ingest consumer has joined its group; a readiness gate holds traffic until both are true.
6. Runtime: the ingest consumer reads `rwb.decision-record.v1` with the retry topic and the `.dlt`; the consumer lag is exported and compared with the 5-minute completeness target; a dead-lettered envelope raises an alert with its `ce_id`, its `ce_type` and its reason.
7. Runtime: at 02:00 the Schedule `decision-log-chain-check` starts `DecisionChainCheckWorkflow` on the `rwb-decision` queue; the run writes one seal file per verified business date to immutable storage and raises an incident and the Compliance notice on a break.
8. Runtime: the append-only verification job runs on a schedule and queries the catalogue: the trigger `tr_declog_append_only` exists and is enabled, the function `refuse_change` exists, and no login other than the schema owner holds UPDATE or DELETE on `decision_log_entry`; a hit raises an alert and is a P2 incident.
9. Runtime: the dashboards show the ingest lag, the entries per hour, the dead-letter count, the last chain-check result, the last seal for each business date, the drift gate result of the last deployment and the append-only verification result.
10. Backup: the schema is covered by the ACE database backup policy with point-in-time recovery; the seal files are kept in immutable storage with their own retention.
11. Restore: a restore is run into an isolated environment, to a point in time after the last verified seal; after the restore the chain is re-verified from the first entry to the last, the append-only verification job runs, and only then is the restored copy accepted; a restore that fails either check is not promoted.
12. Run book: each failure of section 5 has one entry in the run book with its symptom, its first check, its recovery step and the record it leaves.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A pending migration fails at service start | The transaction rolls back, the history records the failure, the pod does not become ready and the deployment stops | MSG-P3-016 | AC1 |
| X2 | The drift gate finds an object the migrations do not produce | The deployment stops before it starts and the object is named | MSG-P3-016 | AC2 |
| X3 | The migration account or the read-only account cannot be read from the key store | The pod does not start; the failure is logged without the secret | None | AC3 |
| X4 | The ingest lag passes the 5-minute completeness target | An alert names the group, the topic, the partition and the lag; the run book's first check is the consumer and the dead-letter topic | A missing-record alert | AC4 |
| X5 | An envelope is dead-lettered | The alert carries `ce_id`, `ce_type` and the reason; the run book steps are the replay and the incident | MSG-P7-009 where the body was refused | AC4 |
| X6 | The chain check finds a break | An incident is raised and MSG-P7-008 goes to Compliance within 15 minutes; the seal of that date is not written | MSG-P7-008 | AC5 |
| X7 | The append-only verification job finds a missing trigger, a missing function or a grant | The alert is raised as a P2 incident and the grant or the trigger is restored by the DB story's migration; no row is touched | None | AC6 |
| X8 | A restore is run | The chain is re-verified and the append-only job is run before the copy is accepted; a failure stops the promotion | MSG-P7-008 on a break | AC7 |
| X9 | Two instances of the service start together | One applies the migrations, the other waits for the lock and finds nothing pending | None | AC1 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the template, the chart, the schema and login, the Kafka platform, the workflow kit, the gateway route and the ACE backup policy |
| Negotiable | The dashboard panels, the alert thresholds and the run-book wording are settled with the operations team; the rules of section 8 are fixed |
| Valuable | The ledger is deployed, watched and restored without an operation that can change a row, and a silent gap is impossible |
| Estimable | One pipeline, one drift gate, one consumer and one Schedule in production, one verification job, one restore procedure, one run book |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion runs in a pipeline, in a container or in a restore exercise in section 16 |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: deployment of the central decision ledger

  Background:
    Given the service schema is rwb_decision and the baseline version is V0001
    Given the migration account and the read-only drift account are secret references in the key store
    Given the ledger is written only by the ingest of rwb.decision-record.v1 and read on /api/recovery/decision/v1

  Scenario: AC1 Start applies the pending migrations once, with the two-instance lock (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a service with two pending migrations in SIT
    When the service starts twice, the second instance starting while the first is still migrating
    Then both migrate in version order and the history records them with their checksums
    Then the second instance waits for the Flyway lock, finds nothing pending and becomes ready
    Then a migration that fails rolls back, the history records the failure and the pod does not become ready

  Scenario: AC2 The drift gate runs before SIT, UAT and PROD (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the migration stage of the pipeline
    When a column has been added by hand to rwb_decision, or an index has been dropped
    Then the gate fails with MSG-P3-016, names the object and stops the deployment in SIT, UAT and PROD
    Then in DEV the gate reports the same difference and the deployment continues
    Then the gate compares the object list of the migrations with the target through the read-only account and never writes

  Scenario: AC3 The accounts are secret references and none is in a file (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the migration, read-only and runtime accounts of the service in the key store
    When the pipeline and the pod read them
    Then each account is a secret reference and never a value in a pipeline file, a chart value, an image layer, a log or a prompt
    Then a scan of the pipeline files, the chart, the image and the startup log finds no credential
    Then the runtime login of the ingest is the service login and holds no UPDATE and no DELETE on decision_log_entry

  Scenario: AC4 The ingest is monitored and a gap is alerted (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the consumer group of the ingest on rwb.decision-record.v1 with its retry topic and its .dlt
    When the lag passes the 5-minute completeness target, or an envelope is dead-lettered
    Then an alert names the group, the topic, the partition, the lag or the ce_id and the reason
    Then the run book entry for the case is linked from the alert and states the replay step
    Then the dead-letter count, the entries per hour and the lag appear on the dashboard of the service

  Scenario: AC5 The chain check runs at 02:00 and its failure reaches Compliance (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the Schedule decision-log-chain-check at 02:00 on the rwb-decision queue
    When the run verifies a clean range
    Then one seal file for the business date is written to immutable storage with the count, the last chain_seq and the last entry_hash
    When the run finds a break
    Then an incident is raised and MSG-P7-008 reaches the Compliance and PDPA officer group within 15 minutes of the run start
    Then no seal is written for that business date, and the missing seal is itself an alert

  Scenario: AC6 The append-only verification job proves the guarantee in place (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the scheduled verification job
    When it queries the catalogue of rwb_decision
    Then it passes only when tr_declog_append_only exists and is enabled, refuse_change exists and no login other than the schema owner holds UPDATE or DELETE on decision_log_entry
    When the trigger is dropped or disabled, or an UPDATE grant is added
    Then the job fails with the object named and raises a P2 incident
    Then the recovery step is the DB story's migration and no row of the ledger is updated

  Scenario: AC7 A restore of the ledger is verified before it is accepted (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a point-in-time restore of the ACE database into an isolated environment, to a time after the last verified seal
    When the restore completes
    Then the chain is re-verified from the first entry to the last and every seal file of immutable storage matches the last chain_seq and entry_hash of its date
    Then the append-only verification job passes on the restored copy
    Then a restored copy that fails either check is not promoted, and no UPDATE and no DELETE is run on it to make it pass

  Scenario: AC8 The run book covers every failure of this story (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the run book of the service
    When it is reviewed against the exception paths X1 to X9
    Then each path has one entry with its symptom, its first check, its recovery step and the record it leaves
    Then no entry instructs an update or a delete on decision_log_entry, and every entry that needs one escalates to the DB story instead
```

These criteria are new and test the deployment artefacts only: no legacy acceptance criterion is repeated, and every identifier, time, topic and target is the architecture's or the technical specification's value, character for character.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Flyway runs on service start in every environment and applies each pending migration of this service once, under the service's own login from the key store | ADR-021; DP-15; RWB-PLT-E1044-OPS |
| BR2 | The drift gate runs before every deployment to SIT, UAT and PROD and stops it on a difference; DEV reports and continues | RWB-PLT-E1044-OPS BR3; ADR-021 |
| BR3 | Every credential is a key-store reference and no credential appears in a file, an image, a log or a prompt | NFR-052 |
| BR4 | The ingest keeps up with the shared topic: the lag against the 5-minute completeness target and the dead-letter count are alerted, not merely graphed | Architecture v5 slide 28 (BR10 of the app story) |
| BR5 | The chain check runs at 02:00 as a Schedule of this service and a break reaches Compliance within 15 minutes; a date that did not verify is not sealed | Architecture v5 slide 44 (JOB-14); NFR-035 |
| BR6 | The append-only guarantee is verified in place on a schedule: the trigger, the function and the absence of an UPDATE and DELETE grant | REQ-DRI-002; the DB story's BR2 |
| BR7 | A restore is verified by the chain and by the seals before it is accepted, and no UPDATE or DELETE is ever run on the ledger to make a check pass | REQ-DRI-002; REQ-DRI-003; DP-17's "no repair by hand" |
| BR8 | There is no data-lake copy, no watermark job and no partition step; the 02:00 run and its seal replace the legacy 01:00 copy | DP-17; ADR-018; Architecture v5 slide 44 |
| BR9 | The two reads are reached through gateway-bff and never from a pod, so a smoke test proves the route and not only the container | DP-19; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR10 | Retention follows the bank schedule for the ledger and its own class for the seal files; no job of this story deletes a ledger row | DL26; the DB story's BR9 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | Deployment starts | The drift gate passes | Migrating |
| Migrating | All pending versions applied | The history records every checksum | Starting |
| Starting | The ingest joins its group and the API is ready | The readiness gate is satisfied | Serving |
| Migrating | A version fails | A statement or a validation fails | Failed (rolled back, the pod not ready) |
| Serving | The lag passes the target, or an envelope is dead-lettered | The alert rule fires | Degraded (alerted, catching up) |
| Degraded | The lag returns inside the target | The group catches up | Serving |
| Serving | The 02:00 run verifies the range | Every hash and link matches | Sealed for the business date |
| Serving | The 02:00 run finds a break | The first mismatch is named | Broken (incident, no seal) |
| Serving | The verification job finds a grant or a trigger missing | The catalogue query hits | Guard lost (P2 incident, restored by migration) |
| Broken, Guard lost, or a data loss | Restore into an isolated environment | After the last verified seal | Restored (chain and seals verified before promotion) |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| DevOps engineer of the platform | Owns the pipeline, the drift gate, the chart values, the dashboards, the alerts and the run book |
| RW-PLATADM Platform administrator | Reads the deployment and the job runs; reruns a failed migration job after the fix is a new version |
| The pipeline migration account of the service | Applies the migrations of `rwb_decision` with the service's login from the key store |
| The runtime login of the service | Ingests the shared topic and reads the ledger; never updates and never deletes a ledger row (DP-02) |
| Key store administrator | Owns the secret entries and their rotation; not a Workbench role |
| RW-COMPLY Compliance and PDPA officer | Receives the break notice; takes no operational action in this story |
| RW-AUDIT Internal audit | Reads the ledger through the two operations and the run records; no direct SQL |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A deployment is not a credit decision |

No personal name, no e-mail address and no credential appears in a pipeline file, a chart value, a dashboard, a run book or a test.

##### 11. Data

No business field. The deployment writes run records — one per migration run, one per chain-check run, one per verification job run, each with the service, the schema, the version, the checksum, the counts, the start and end time and a status — to the P1 job view and to the platform's logs. It reads the catalogue of `rwb_decision`, the consumer offsets of the ingest, the sandbox seal files and the key store references. It writes no row of `decision_log_entry` and no business row of any kind.

The alert thresholds, the dashboard panel set, the seal file layout and the retention class of a run record are the working read of the assumptions (GAP-1233; ASM-2197), (GAP-1234; ASM-2198); the times, the topic, the target and the message identifiers are the architecture's values.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** The pipeline of the service on the golden template, the chart values that read the three accounts from the key store and set `RWB_SCHEMA=rwb_decision` per environment, the start configuration (`spring.flyway.baseline-on-migrate=false`, `clean-disabled=true`, validation on start, out-of-order off, the lock on), the drift gate stage, the consumer configuration with its retry and `.dlt`, the 02:00 Schedule and the verification job, the dashboard, the eight alerts, the restore procedure and the run book.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables. The deployment touches `rwb_decision` only | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`. The deployment operates the subscription of the ledger | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON (carried by the app story; named here) |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case. The deployment changes no reference value | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit. The 02:00 run is a Schedule of this service, not a Quartz row | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON (carried by the app story; named here) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1`. The smoke test calls the decision base through the gateway | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema. The run at start applies this service's sequence and no other | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON (the sequence owner; named here) |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting. No copy job, no watermark and no partition step exists in the pipeline | none; gap if the story needs lake data |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route. The smoke test goes through the gateway | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON (carried by the app story; named here) |

The patterns **not claimed** here are DP-02 (the login is created by the platform DB work and used here), DP-04, DP-05, DP-06, DP-08, DP-09 (the library objects and the relay are the app and DB stories'), DP-11, DP-12, DP-14, DP-16, DP-18 and DP-20.

**Configuration and secrets.** Non-secret configuration: the consumer group and its topic, the retry topic and the `.dlt`, the verifier batch size of 1,000, the completeness target of 5 minutes, the notice budget of 15 minutes, the genesis hash of 64 zeros, the Schedule cron of `0 0 2 * * *`, the seal target and the notification group. Secrets, all as key-store references: the migration account, the read-only drift account and the runtime account of the service. The consumer group name, the seal target path and the alert thresholds are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1233; ASM-2197).

**Alerts.** One per failure mode: a failed migration; a drift finding; a consumer lag past the target; a dead-lettered envelope; a failed chain-check run; a missing seal for a business date; an append-only verification hit; a restore verification failure. Each alert links its run book entry and carries no personal data — an envelope is named by its `ce_id`, never by a customer reference.

**Backup and restore of an append-only ledger.** The schema is covered by the ACE backup policy with point-in-time recovery; the seal files live in immutable storage under their own retention, so the last verified `chain_seq` and `entry_hash` of a date exist outside the database. A restore is always run into an isolated environment first, to a point in time after the last verified seal; the chain is re-verified end to end, the seals are compared, the append-only verification job runs, and only then is the copy promoted. A restored copy that fails is not repaired by a statement: it is restored again, or the gap is recorded. The RPO, the RTO and the retention of a restore exercise are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1234; ASM-2198).

**Run book entries.** (1) A failed migration: the version, the checksum and the statement; the fix is a new version. (2) A drift finding: the object, and the migration that should produce it. (3) A lag: the consumer, the partition, the last offset and the dead-letter count. (4) A dead-lettered envelope: the `ce_id`, the reason, and the replay after the fix. (5) A chain break: the first `chain_seq` and entry ID, the incident, the Compliance notice and the quarantine of the range from that entry on. (6) A missing seal: the run and the night. (7) An append-only hit: the grant or the trigger and the migration that restores it. (8) A restore: the point in time, the seal compared and the two checks. (9) A gateway-only failure: the route, the two reads and the pod health behind it.

**Done when.** The eight criteria of section 7 pass in SIT, the drift gate stops a drifted SIT, UAT and PROD deployment and passes it in DEV, two instances start together inside the connection cap, a break reaches Compliance inside 15 minutes, the verification job catches a dropped trigger and a widened grant, and a restore is verified by the chain and the seals before promotion.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-016 | Drift found, checksum mismatch, a refused clean or undo, or a failed migration | Schema check failed in {schema}: {object}. The deployment was stopped. |
| MSG-P7-008 | The chain check finds a break | The decision log check for {date} found a break at entry {entryId}. Entries from that entry on cannot be relied on until Compliance reviews them. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The ingest cannot write an entry and the envelope is retried | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A caller without Decision log R runs the smoke read | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| An operational alert, no message id | Lag, dead letter, missing seal or append-only hit | Raised to the platform queue with the object named; no business user sees it |

MSG-P3-016 is the message of the migration work of RWB-E1-044, carried unchanged; MSG-P7-008 and MSG-P7-003 are the ledger's and are relayed, not rewritten. Thai text for each message follows DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

No new business screen. The service's dashboard shows the ingest lag against the 5-minute target, the entries per hour, the dead-letter count, the last chain-check result, the last seal for each business date, the last drift gate result and the last append-only verification result; SCR-44 Interface and job monitor shows the three run records. The operational states of a deployment and of a business date are the ones in section 9 — Serving, Degraded, Sealed, Broken, Guard lost and Restored — and none of them is a business state of a case.

##### 17. Guardrails

- One schema and one login per service: the run and the subscription use the `rwb-decision` login and touch no other schema (DP-01, DP-02).
- No credential in a pipeline file, a chart value, an image layer, a log or a prompt; every account is a key-store reference (BR3).
- No clean and no undo in PROD; a fix is a new version through the pipeline (BR2).
- No statement on a ledger row from a pipeline, a run book or an alert response; the only recovery is a migration or a restore, and a restore is verified before promotion (BR7).
- No data-lake job, no watermark and no partition step (BR8, DP-17); the 02:00 run and its seal are the only nightly work.
- No personal data in an alert, a dashboard, a run record or a seal file: an envelope is named by `ce_id`, a run by its business date.
- The smoke test goes through gateway-bff and never to a pod (BR9).
- No business value in the configuration beyond the values the architecture fixes; the thresholds and the cron of the verification job are configuration and not code.
