##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-02 | `recovery_svc` login | One login per service | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting | none; gap if the story needs lake data |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-10 is the deployment pattern of this story: a shared Quartz step becomes an event-started workflow with one worker and a KEDA rule. DP-17 is a removal that the release proves: no extract job, no lake target, no report refresh. DP-19 is registered only as the route target of the admin surface that calls 12.1.

**Artefacts**

| Artefact | Content |
|---|---|
| `helm/rwb-source-data/` | Chart with the api and worker deployments, service, migration job, config map, secret references and probes |
| `values-dev.yaml`, `values-sit.yaml`, `values-uat.yaml` | Image digest, replica ranges, resources, probe timings, log level, scaling thresholds, feature switches |
| Pipeline stage | Build, unit, component and contract tests, image and dependency scan, chart publish, promotion of one artefact |
| Worker registration | Task queue `rwb-source-data` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, build ID of the release, KEDA rule on queue backlog and consumer lag |
| Provisioning step | Consumer group for `rwb.source-data.events.v1` with retry and `.dlt`, inbox table check |
| Rerun binding | `POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun` starts `ReconciliationWorkflow` for the business date; no Schedule |
| Dashboards | Rows written, variance, tolerance, publish state, orphan count, run duration, rows per run, worker count and backlog |
| Alerts | Two rules, each with a message ID and one runbook entry |
| Runbook | Five entries: held publish, failed run, batch not complete, worker not polling, migration failure |

**Probes.** Readiness answers healthy only when the migration is at the expected schema version, the worker has polled the queue and the consumer is joined; liveness answers healthy when the process is up and its loop responds. Neither probe writes to the database. Exact paths and timings are values.

**Migration job.** Runs the per-service Flyway sequence for schema `rwb_source_data` with the `rwb_source_data` login, as a pre-deploy job with a backoff limit; a failed job blocks the rollout and the release.

**Alert mapping carried over from the legacy story.**

| Message ID | Condition | Alert | Route |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-012 | A product breaks the tolerance and the case list is held | Hold alert with product, business date, variance and percent | Data steward and platform on-call, ticket |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A view or the store is unavailable during the run | Failed-run alert naming the system and the business date | Platform on-call, page |

MSG-P1-001 is carried as the third signal of the runbook entry for a date the batch record does not show complete; it is raised by the completeness gate of RWB-P1-E1015-APP and is not a new alert of this story.

**Done when.** The chart renders in the three environments, the pipeline promotes one artefact, the migration job and both probes pass, the worker registers and scales on a synthetic backlog, the consumer group has its retry and `.dlt` topics, the rerun starts one run per date, the parameter check refuses a missing parameter, the two alerts fire on synthetic metrics and the five runbook entries are reviewed by the on-call rota.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-012 | A product breaks the tolerance and the publish is held | The case list for {date} does not reconcile to ACE for {product}: a difference of {variance} accounts, {pct} percent. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The batch for the date is not complete | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A view or the store is unavailable during the run | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A rerun by a role without Platform administration U | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story; the deployment adds the alert routing and the runbook link, never a new wording.

##### 15. Screens and states

The deployment serves no screen of its own. The admin result list is rendered through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) and the operator-facing surfaces of this story are the pipeline run view, the release view, the dashboard and the runbook. The states an operator sees are Ready, Rolling and Failed at the release, and PASS, BREAK and NOT_RUN with the publish RELEASED or HELD at the run. No Power BI report and no lake refresh exists.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code or in a values file: the tolerance, the entry threshold and the waiting periods are parameters of the catalog, never a deployment value.
- No personal data in events, workflow inputs or logs and none in a dashboard series, an alert payload or the runbook: business dates, product groups, counts, amounts and durations only.
- One login per service: the chart carries the `rwb_source_data` login reference and no other service's credential (DP-02).
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `recovery.v_ace_*` views: the release grants the login SELECT on the views and nothing in `public` (DP-01, DP-05).
- No cross-schema read and no cross-schema key: the migration job touches schema `rwb_source_data` only (DP-01).
- Every consumer group has a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic, and the consumer dedupes through the inbox (DP-09).
- No lake path: no extract job, no lake target and no report refresh in the release (DP-17).
- No secret is written into a values file, a chart template, a dashboard or the runbook; every secret comes from the platform secret store.

- The platform topic provisioning implementation, the Temporal cluster and KEDA itself (platform epics RWB-PLT-EVT and RWB-PLT-WF).
- The exact cluster topology, node pools, replica counts, resource sizes, probe timings and scaling thresholds (GAP-0497).
- The jobs and case-list operations and the `DailyCaseList` Schedule (RWB-P1-E1002-CON and RWB-P1-E1002-OPS).
- The lake extract job, the Power BI data set and the 07:30 refresh, which the target removes (DP-17).
- The dashboards and alerts of the sibling slices RWB-P3-E1011-APP, RWB-S5-E1011-APP and RWB-P6-E1011-APP.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: RWB-E1-011 is split and reworked as the integration story RWB-ITG-E1011-ITG, the end-to-end proof of JOB-04 across rwb-source-data, rwb-case, rwb-asset, rwb-comms, rwb-integration and rwb-reporting, with the data lake removed. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **test engineer in the release squad (RW-TRIBE), with the data steward (RW-DATASTEW) as the reader of the result**, I want **the five daily reconciliations REC-01 to REC-05 of JOB-04 proved end to end in SIT against the real wave-1 services — started by the AceDataReady event on the rwb-source-data workflow, reading its own ACE views, taking open case accounts and exclusions from rwb-case, asset keys from rwb-asset and notice person keys from rwb-comms over one-hop contracts, writing the results in rwb_source_data, setting the case-list publish status through the rwb-case contract, and delivering the reconciliation and data quality extracts to rwb-reporting through rwb-integration**, so that **each wave-1 release shows whether today's case list and its links can be trusted before the release date**.

##### 2. Business rationale

No one can say today whether the recovery teams' lists cover every account at 90 days past due, so missing accounts are found late or not at all. The legacy capability runs five reconciliations every business date — the account count by product against `v_ace_account` (REC-01), the balance by product (REC-02), approved treatments against `v_ace_plan` (REC-03), payments against proceeds (REC-04), and every business key on a Workbench table against the view that holds it (REC-05) — holds the publish of the case list when a product is outside the tolerance, and publishes the result with the data quality measures.

In the target the capability is spread over the real services, so the legacy story alone cannot prove it: JOB-04 is an event-triggered workflow in rwb-source-data (Arch v5 slide 44), the checks read the ACE views through the owner that holds them (DP-05), the open case accounts and the exclusions come from rwb-case, the asset keys from rwb-asset and the notice person keys from rwb-comms over one-hop REST contracts with a 2 s timeout (DP-11), and the two extracts reach rwb-reporting as delivered files through rwb-integration because the data lake is removed (DP-17, ADR-018). This story builds that integration harness, runs it against the real services instead of the contract fakes, and holds the wave-1 release on its result. It meets REQ-RDF-007, REQ-RDF-008 and REQ-CWC-004, applies control CTL-01, and serves the accuracy measure "reconciliation breaks cleared within one day, 100 percent".

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P1-E1011-APP is done: the JOB-04 reconciliation workflow and its activities run on task queue `rwb-source-data`, the results are written in `rwb_source_data`, and the job listing reads them per check and product group.
- RWB-P3-E1011-APP is done: the exclusion resource of the case contract, the open case accounts, and the case-list publish status gate.
- RWB-S5-E1011-APP is done: the asset keys of the business date are published on the rwb-asset contract. RWB-P6-E1011-APP is done: the notice person keys are published on the rwb-comms contract.
- The wave-1 services are deployed in SIT in one environment: rwb-source-data, rwb-case, rwb-asset, rwb-comms, rwb-integration and rwb-reporting, each on its own base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1`, each on its own schema and login (DP-01, DP-02), with the SIT Kafka topics and the Temporal namespace `rwb-recovery` reachable.
- rwb-source-data publishes `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` for the SIT business date, so the reconciliation workflow can be started by the event rather than by a scheduler.
- The SIT data set carries the synthetic fixture values of the legacy criteria: MORTGAGE 12,256, HIRE_PURCHASE 12,960 and SSME 2,903 accounts at 90 days past due or more; the 12 SSME account keys of the break fixture; case "RW-2026-000140" with person_key "P0099881"; and the parameter `recon.tolerance.pct` 0.00 in force for REC-01 and REC-02.
- The reporting report "Reconciliation and data quality" exists in SIT with its 07:30 refresh, and SCR-45 Data quality is reachable read-only.
- No data lake path is provisioned in SIT: the legacy INT-19 outbound adapter and the lake copy of the case list are not installed (DP-17).
- Which service runs REC-03 (treatments) and REC-04 (payments) in the target, and how the two extracts reach reporting once the lake is removed, is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0336; ASM-0430).
- No build dependency: the four integration dependencies are the real services, and the story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. rwb-source-data completes the ALS ingest for business date 2026-11-30, its `AceIngestCheck` workflow confirms freshness over `recovery.v_ace_*`, and it publishes `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` with source ALS and the business date on `rwb.source-data.events.v1`.
2. The reconciliation workflow starts on task queue `rwb-source-data` from that event, one run per business date, and takes the business date of the event as the date of every check.
3. It reads `v_ace_batch_status` through the ACE views it owns, confirms the ALS batch is complete for the date, and reads `recon.tolerance.pct`, `recon.treatment.days`, `recon.payment.days` and `case.entry.dpd` through the parameters contract (DP-06).
4. REC-01 and REC-02: for each product group it counts and sums `v_ace_account` rows at or above the entry threshold with `data_as_of` equal to the business date, subtracts the accounts excluded at entry, and compares the result with `case_list_row`.
5. Exclusions: it calls the exclusion operation that the rwb-case contract publishes — its exact path is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0337; ASM-0431) — on rwb-case, one hop with a 2 s timeout; the exclusion rows carry the reason code, the rule ID and the package version, and an excluded account is explained and never a break.
6. Open case accounts: it calls `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases` and the account link read of the case contract on rwb-case, one hop with a 2 s timeout, never a table of `rwb_case`.
7. REC-03 and REC-04: treatments and payments are checked against `v_ace_plan` and `v_ace_payment`. In wave 1 the owning services are not in the environment, so both checks report NOT_RUN with their reason; the not-run grade and its reason are the legacy BR10 values and no new business value is introduced.
8. REC-05: every `account_key`, `person_key`, `asset_key`, `payment_code` and `contact_key` on a Workbench table is resolved to its view row. The asset keys come from `GET /api/recovery/asset/v1/assets` on rwb-asset and the notice person keys from `GET /api/recovery/comms/v1/cases/{caseId}/notices` on rwb-comms, one call per case in the run, each one hop with a 2 s timeout; an orphan is listed for the data steward and changes no row.
9. It computes the variance and the variance percent per check and product group, compares them with the tolerance, and writes one `reconciliation_result` row per check and product group in one transaction, unique on rec_code, business_date and product_group.
10. Publish gate: it calls the case-list publish contract of rwb-case, which sets the publish status of the business date to RELEASED when every REC-01 and REC-02 result is PASS and to HELD when any is BREAK, and it alerts the data steward, the platform administrator and the team managers with MSG-P1-012 on a break.
11. Extracts: it writes the reconciliation extract and the data quality extract and asks rwb-integration for a delivery; rwb-integration runs the `deliverFile` activity on task queue `rwb-integration`, records the file run in `rwb_integration`, and publishes `rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1` for each file.
12. rwb-reporting reads the two delivered files and the business events of the date and builds the report; at 07:30 the report shows each product as green, red or not run, the variance, the break rows, the referential completeness and the quality measures.
13. The harness: publishes the event, waits for the workflow, asserts the results and the publish status, reads the two files from the outbound item record, reads the report, and records one verdict per test case.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A product's variance is above the tolerance | Result BREAK; red on the report; publish held; break rows listed; alert | MSG-P1-012 | AC2, AC15 |
| X2 | The variance equals the tolerance | Result PASS | None | AC3 |
| X3 | The ACE batch for the business date is not COMPLETED | No reconciliation result for the date; the report shows not run with the reason; the publish stays held | MSG-P1-001 | AC4 |
| X4 | The run repeats for the same date after a fix | The date's results are replaced; the publish is released when every REC-01 and REC-02 result passes | None | AC15 |
| X5 | The same event is delivered twice | One row per check, product group and date; no second run and no second row | None | AC12 |
| X6 | A business key has no ACE row | REC-05 is BREAK with the orphan count and the key is listed; no Workbench row changes | None | AC7 |
| X7 | A view or a store returns an error during the run | No result is written for the date; the run is FAILED with the system named | MSG-GEN-006 | TC-E1-011-09-ITG |
| X8 | A role without Platform administration R lists the break rows | 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-011-07-ITG |
| X9 | A cross-service read exceeds the 2 s budget | The step fails as a timeout, no result is written for the date, and the rerun writes every row | MSG-GEN-006 | AC13 |
| X10 | A file delivery fails | rwb-integration publishes `rwb.integration.FileFailed.v1`; the run records the failed file run; the delivery is retried from the outbound item | None | AC14 |
| X11 | REC-03 or REC-04 has no owning service in the environment | The check reports NOT_RUN with its reason; the report shows not run; the archive of the day records no PASS for that check | None | AC12 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Proves behaviour that already exists in the four integration dependencies; builds no product capability and changes no case |
| Negotiable | The fixture values, the file names and the harness settings are configuration; the checks, the tolerance rule and the publish gate are fixed by the legacy story |
| Valuable | A release cannot claim the wave-1 reconciliation works until the real services pass the run together, which no single service story can show |
| Estimable | One harness, one event driver, six read checks, two extract checks, one publish check |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its test cases |
| Testable | Every criterion is one automated test against the real SIT services, with the failure path recorded |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Reconciliation and data quality report across the wave-1 services

  Background:
    Given the business date is 2026-11-30 and v_ace_batch_status shows ALS COMPLETED for 2026-11-30
    Given the parameter recon.tolerance.pct = 0.00 is in force for REC-01 and REC-02
    Given the ACE views are read by rwb-source-data, the owner of the view contract

  Scenario: AC1 Variance under limit (legacy RWB-E1-011 AC1)
    Given the v_ace_account accounts at 90 days past due or more less the exclusions are MORTGAGE 12,256, HIRE_PURCHASE 12,960 and SSME 2,903
    Given the case list rows at 90 days past due or more are MORTGAGE 12,256, HIRE_PURCHASE 12,960 and SSME 2,903, with equal balance sums
    Given no restructure plan is overdue in v_ace_plan, no payment of the date is unmatched, and every business key resolves to its view
    When the reconciliation step of JOB-04 runs
    Then the system writes fifteen reconciliation_result rows, REC-01 to REC-05 for each of the three product groups, each with variance 0 and result PASS
    Then the system sets the publish status of the case list for 2026-11-30 to RELEASED
    Then the report after the 07:30 refresh shows all three products green

  Scenario: AC2 Variance over limit (legacy RWB-E1-011 AC2)
    Given v_ace_account holds 2,903 SSME accounts at 90 days past due or more less the exclusions
    Given the case list holds 2,891 SSME rows at 90 days past due or more, a variance of 12 accounts, 0.41 percent
    When the reconciliation step runs
    Then the REC-01 result for SSME is BREAK with variance 12 and variance percent 0.41
    Then the 12 account keys are on the break list for the data steward, with their days past due from v_ace_account
    Then the system sets the case list publish for 2026-11-30 to HELD and the lake keeps the case list of 2026-11-27
    Then the data steward, platform administrator and team manager groups receive MSG-P1-012 "The case list for 2026-11-30 does not reconcile to ACE for SSME: a difference of 12 accounts, 0.41 percent."
    Then the report shows SSME red with the 12 break rows, and MORTGAGE and HIRE_PURCHASE green

  Scenario: AC3 Variance equal to the tolerance (legacy RWB-E1-011 AC3)
    Given the parameter recon.tolerance.pct for REC-01 is changed by a reference load to 0.10 from 2026-11-30
    Given the MORTGAGE variance is 0.10 percent and the SSME variance is 0.11 percent
    When the reconciliation step runs
    Then the MORTGAGE result is PASS and the SSME result is BREAK

  Scenario: AC4 ACE batch not complete (legacy RWB-E1-011 AC4)
    Given v_ace_batch_status shows no COMPLETED ALS row for 2026-11-30 at 08:00
    When the DP01 cut-off passes and JOB-04 is triggered
    Then the daily completeness gate holds JOB-04 and the system writes no reconciliation_result for 2026-11-30
    Then the case list publish for 2026-11-30 stays HELD
    Then the report shows every product as not run with the reason "DP01 is from 2026-11-27"

  Scenario: AC7 Business key without an ACE row (legacy RWB-E1-011 AC7)
    Given case_party on case "RW-2026-000140" carries person_key "P0099881", which has no row in v_ace_customer
    When the REC-05 step runs
    Then the REC-05 result for the product group of the case is BREAK with 1 orphan
    Then "case_party.person_key P0099881" is on the break list for the data steward and the ACE team
    Then the case and its case_party row are unchanged

  Scenario: AC12 JOB-04 starts on AceDataReady and writes one result per check and product group (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given rwb-source-data publishes rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1 for source ALS and business date 2026-11-30
    When the reconciliation workflow starts
    Then it is an event-started workflow on task queue rwb-source-data, one run for the business date
    Then it uses the business date of the event for every check and never a mix of two business dates
    Then it computes REC-01 to REC-05 and writes one reconciliation_result row per check and product group in one transaction, REC-01 to REC-05 for each of the three product groups
    Then reconciliation_result holds unique rec_code, business_date and product_group, so a second delivery of the event writes no second row
    Then REC-03 and REC-04 report NOT_RUN with their reason until rwb-treatment and rwb-payment land in wave 2, using the not-run grade and the reason of legacy BR10 and no new status value

  Scenario: AC13 Every cross-service read is one hop on the owner's contract (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the reconciliation workflow is running for 2026-11-30
    When it needs the open case accounts and the exclusions of the date
    Then it calls rwb-case on GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases and on the exclusion operation of the case contract, whose exact path is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0337; ASM-0431)
    When it needs the asset keys and the notice person keys for REC-05
    Then it calls rwb-asset on GET /api/recovery/asset/v1/assets and rwb-comms on GET /api/recovery/comms/v1/cases/{caseId}/notices for the cases in the run
    Then every call is one hop with a 2 s timeout and no call is chained through a second service
    Then no service reads a table of rwb_source_data
    Then a read that exceeds the 2 s budget fails the step and the date is rerun

  Scenario: AC14 The two extracts reach rwb-reporting and no data lake path exists (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the reconciliation run for 2026-11-30 has finished with its results
    When the workflow publishes the reconciliation extract and the data quality extract
    Then rwb-integration delivers both files through the deliverFile activity on task queue rwb-integration
    Then rwb-integration records the file run in rwb_integration and publishes rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1 for each file
    Then rwb-reporting reads both delivered files and builds the report of the date from them
    Then no data lake path, no INT-19 adapter and no lake copy of the case list exists in the environment

  Scenario: AC15 A REC-01 or REC-02 break holds the publish and a passing rerun releases it (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the REC-01 result for SSME is BREAK with variance 12 and variance percent 0.41
    When the workflow sets the publish status of the case list for 2026-11-30
    Then the status is set by the rwb-case case-list publish contract call and reads HELD
    Then the reconciliation extract carries the 12 break rows and MSG-P1-012 is sent to the data steward, platform administrator and team manager groups
    When the rerun for 2026-11-30 replaces the results and every REC-01 and REC-02 result is PASS
    Then the same contract call sets the publish status to RELEASED
    Then the case list of 2026-11-30 is the one that rwb-reporting reports for the date
```

The five scenarios AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4 and AC7 are the legacy proof of RWB-E1-011 and are kept word for word; the data lake they name is removed (DP-17) and the target delivery is proved by AC14, and the wave-1 run reports REC-03 and REC-04 as NOT_RUN per AC12 until rwb-treatment and rwb-payment land, so the fifteen PASS rows of AC1 are recorded when they do. No scenario uses a contract mock: the run is against the real service contracts.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Accounts at or above the entry threshold in `v_ace_account` for the business date are compared with open recovery cases and the case list rows, by count per product group, every business date | REC-01; CTL-01; REQ-RDF-007 |
| BR2 | Balances in `v_ace_account` are compared with the balances on the case list rows, by sum per product group | REC-02 |
| BR3 | An approved restructure treatment whose plan is not booked in `v_ace_plan` two business days after approval is a break | REC-03; parameter recon.treatment.days |
| BR4 | A payment in `v_ace_payment` with no proceeds matched to its `payment_code` one business day after the payment date stays on the exception list and counts as a break | REC-04; parameter recon.payment.days |
| BR5 | Every `account_key`, `person_key`, `asset_key`, `payment_code` and `contact_key` on a Workbench table must resolve to a row in `v_ace_account`, `v_ace_customer`, `v_ace_asset`, `v_ace_payment` or `v_ace_contact`; zero orphans, and every one is listed | REC-05; REQ-RDF-007 |
| BR6 | A result is a break when the variance percent is above the tolerance; REC-03 and REC-04 use their waiting periods and a zero tolerance | Parameter recon.tolerance.pct, 0.00 assumed (DL25) |
| BR7 | A break in REC-01 or REC-02 holds the publish of the case list for the business date and lists the break rows for the data steward | FEAT-RDF-13; REC-01 "Break list to the data steward" |
| BR8 | Accounts excluded at entry are explained and do not count as breaks | REC-01 "zero unexplained"; REQ-CWC-004 |
| BR9 | No reconciliation runs until the daily completeness gate reports COMPLETE for the sources the reconciliation reads on the business date | BR-P1-014-4; MSG-P1-001 |
| BR10 | Report grades: green, every reconciliation for the product passed; red, at least one break; not run, the reconciliation did not run, with the reason | FEAT-RDF-12 |
| BR11 | A repeated run for the same date replaces that date's results | R-UNI-40 |
| BR12 | The reconciliation reads ACE for the business date of the ACE batch it was started by, and never a mix of two business dates | BR-P1-011-2 |
| BR13 | A REC-05 orphan never deletes or changes a Workbench record; it is listed for the data steward and, where the row is missing in ACE, for the ACE team | BR-P1-011-3 |
| BR14 | Every cross-service read is one hop on the owner's contract with a 2 s timeout; the reconciliation reads open case accounts and exclusions from rwb-case, asset keys from rwb-asset and notice person keys from rwb-comms, and reads no other service's tables | DP-01; DP-11; ADR-020 |
| BR15 | There is no data lake: the reporting read model is fed by the business events and by the files rwb-integration delivers, so a lake copy of the case list or of an extract is neither written nor read | DP-17; ADR-018; Arch v5 slides 37 and 44 (JOB-15) |

##### 9. State transitions

None for a case status. This story changes no case. It proves the status of `reconciliation_result` (PASS, BREAK or NOT_RUN, with NOT_RUN and its reason as legacy BR10 defines them) and of `case_list_row.publish_status` (HELD or RELEASED) for the business date.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| rwb-source-data service identity (the rwb-source-data login, DP-02) | Runs the reconciliation workflow, writes `reconciliation_result`, sets the publish status through the rwb-case contract, and asks rwb-integration for the delivery |
| rwb-case, rwb-asset and rwb-comms service identities | Answer the one-hop reads of the run; no write in this story |
| rwb-integration service identity | Runs `deliverFile`, records the file run and publishes the file events |
| RW-TRIBE, release squad and test engineers | Publish the SIT event, run the harness, read the verdicts |
| RW-DATASTEW, data steward and data product owner | Reads the results and the break rows (Platform administration R); signs the daily reconciliation to ACE |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Reads the results, restarts the run for a business date (Platform administration U) |
| RW-COE, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-SECADM | Read the results and the break rows (Platform administration R) |
| RW-TEAMMGR, RW-BIANAL and other report readers | Read the report (Reporting R); RW-BIANAL builds it (Reporting CRUD) |
| ACE team | Reads the orphan list for a key that has no ACE row |

The per-service login names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0337; ASM-0431); the story names them "the rwb-<short> login (DP-02)".

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary. The harness reads and writes nothing directly: every field above is read through the owning service's contract or through the rwb-source-data views and job listing (DP-01, DP-05). `case_list_row` is P1's daily published projection and the case-list API and the publish gate stay with P3 under the Ownership Map ruling; `publish_status` is therefore set by the rwb-case contract call and never written by the harness.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. This story builds and runs an integration harness and publishes no REST operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the run | Budget |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/freshness` | P1 rwb-source-data | Batch completeness of the business date before the run | One hop, 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs?type=JOB-04` | P1 rwb-source-data | Run record: REC-01 to REC-05 with PASS, BREAK or NOT_RUN per product group and the publish status | One hop, 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases` | P3 rwb-case | Open case accounts and the case list of the date | One hop, 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/exclusions?businessDate={businessDate}` | P3 rwb-case | Accounts excluded at entry, for REC-01; this is the operation the rwb-case contract of RWB-P3-E1011-APP must publish, because its exact path is not named in the Ownership Map or the Architecture extract | One hop, 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/asset/v1/assets` | S5 rwb-asset | Asset keys for REC-05 | One hop, 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/comms/v1/cases/{caseId}/notices` | P6 rwb-comms | Notice person keys for REC-05, one call per case in the run | One hop, 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/integration/v1/admin/outbound-items` | P2 rwb-integration | The two delivered files and their file runs | One hop, 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/reporting/v1/reports/{reportId}` | P9 rwb-reporting | The report of the date, read only | One hop, 2 s |

The workflow itself performs the reads of rows 3 to 6 inside its activities; the harness calls them in the same way and fails the run when one of them exceeds the budget. The exact exclusion operation of the case contract is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0337; ASM-0431); the path above is the one the P3 E1011 contract must publish.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Asserted in the run |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1` | `rwb.integration.events.v1` | P2 rwb-integration | One per extract, with the file reference, the business date and the requesting service |
| `rwb.integration.FileFailed.v1` | `rwb.integration.events.v1` | P2 rwb-integration | Asserted on the forced failure path only |

Both are published by rwb-integration, not by the harness; the story asserts them, and every event carries IDs, references and facts only (DP-09).

| Name | Type | Task queue | Asserted in the run |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reconciliation workflow (JOB-04) | Workflow, started by AceDataReady | `rwb-source-data` | One run per business date, the event's business date used for every check, one transaction for the results |

| Schedule or trigger | Cadence | Asserted in the run |
|---|---|---|
| AceDataReady trigger | On the ACE batch of the business date, with a Temporal Schedule fallback and overlap policy SKIP | The event starts the workflow once per business date; a redelivered event starts no second run |
| Reporting refresh | Daily at 07:30, owned by rwb-reporting | The report of the date is rebuilt after the extract delivery and shows the grades of the run |

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The harness owns no table (DP-01); `reconciliation_result` and `case_list_row` belong to rwb-source-data, `case_entry_exclusion` to rwb-case, and the harness reads every one of them through the owning contract.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

None. The run replaces the contract fakes with the deployed SIT services; a fake used anywhere in the run fails the story.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | In this story |
|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 8 consumed; every call one hop on the owner's base with a 2 s timeout |
| Kafka | 0 published, 3 consumed and 2 asserted; the harness publishes AceDataReady for the SIT date and asserts the two rwb-integration file events |
| Temporal | 1 workflow and its check activities on `rwb-source-data`; `deliverFile` on `rwb-integration` |
| File | 2 files delivered, the reconciliation extract and the data quality extract, read back through the outbound item record |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `itg/reconciliation` in the ACE repository, package `<ACE base package>.recovery.itg.reconciliation`. Not part of a deployed service; it runs in the SIT release pipeline.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-02 | `recovery_svc` login | One login per service | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting | none; gap if the story needs lake data |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The story carries no H, C, I or X dependency beyond the four integration dependencies, because the harness builds nothing: DP-03 resolves to reading decision records the services write, DP-06 and DP-07 to reading parameters and reference data through the deployed contracts, DP-10 to observing the workflow that RWB-P1-E1011-APP owns, DP-14 to asserting the names, DP-15 to reading the schemas of the DB stories, DP-17 to asserting that no lake path exists, and DP-19 to reading the report and SCR-45 read-only through gateway-bff. The H dependencies of these patterns stay with the implementation stories of the owning services.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| EventDriver | Test harness | Publishes `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` for the SIT business date through the SIT topic and waits for the workflow to complete |
| WorkflowProbe | Test harness | Asserts one run per business date on queue `rwb-source-data`, the workflow type and the business date input |
| ContractProbe | Test harness | Calls the eight consumed operations on the owner's base with the 2 s budget, and records status, time and body |
| ResultAssertion | Test harness | Compares the run record and the result read model with the expected grades, variances and row count of the fixture |
| ExtractAssertion | Test harness | Reads the two extracts from the outbound item record and compares the rows with the run |
| PublishAssertion | Test harness | Asserts HELD on the break run and RELEASED on the passing rerun |
| FixtureLoader | Test harness | Loads the synthetic SIT fixture values of the legacy criteria; holds no production data |
| ReportProbe | Test harness | Reads the report of the date, and SCR-45 read-only, through gateway-bff |

**Topology and fixtures**

- One SIT environment: the six wave-1 services, one ACE SIT database with one schema and one login per service (DP-01, DP-02), the SIT Kafka topics, the Temporal namespace `rwb-recovery` with one task queue per service, and no data lake (DP-17).
- Synthetic fixtures only: MORTGAGE 12,256, HIRE_PURCHASE 12,960 and SSME 2,903 accounts at 90 days past due or more with equal balance sums for AC1; 2,891 SSME case list rows and the 12 missing account keys for AC2; the tolerance 0.10 load for AC3; no COMPLETED ALS row for AC4; case "RW-2026-000140" with person_key "P0099881" absent from `v_ace_customer` for AC7; 2,903 SSME accounts against 2,891 rows for AC15.
- The fixture loader seeds only through the SIT data set and the SIT topics; it never writes a service table and never calls a production endpoint.

**Run order**

1. FixtureLoader loads the fixture set and the parameters of the date.
2. ContractProbe confirms that the six wave-1 services answer on their own base and that no service reads another schema.
3. EventDriver publishes AceDataReady for 2026-11-30; WorkflowProbe registers the run and its start type.
4. The run completes; ResultAssertion reads the run record and asserts the row count and the grades of REC-01 to REC-05.
5. PublishAssertion reads HELD on the break fixture and asserts the MSG-P1-012 alert of the break.
6. ExtractAssertion reads the reconciliation extract and the data quality extract from the outbound item record and compares them with the run.
7. rwb-integration publishes `rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1` for both files; the assertion records the two deliveries.
8. ReportProbe reads the report of the date after the 07:30 refresh and SCR-45 read-only.
9. The missing accounts are created, the run is repeated, and PublishAssertion asserts RELEASED with every REC-01 and REC-02 result PASS.
10. The harness writes one verdict per test case of section 16 and fails the release stage on any FAIL.

**Build steps**

1. EventDriver and WorkflowProbe with the SIT topic, the inbox dedupe assertion and the one-run-per-date assertion; tests for AC12.
2. ContractProbe over the eight operations with the 2 s budget and the timeout path; tests for AC13.
3. ResultAssertion for the fifteen-row, unique-key and NOT_RUN behaviour of the run record; tests for AC12 and AC1.
4. FixtureLoader with the legacy fixture values of section 13 and the parameter loads of AC3; no production value.
5. PublishAssertion with the HELD, RELEASED and alert assertions; tests for AC15 and AC2.
6. ExtractAssertion with the two extracts and the outbound item record; tests for AC14.
7. ReportProbe with the report and SCR-45 reads, and the no-lake-path assertion.
8. Add the stage to the release pipeline before the wave-1 exit and run it once on the wave-1 build.

**Done when.** The thirteen test cases of section 16 pass against the SIT wave-1 services, the run shows fifteen `reconciliation_result` rows with their grades, both extracts are read in rwb-reporting, the publish status reads HELD on the break and RELEASED after the rerun, and no data lake path exists in the environment.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |

| MSG-P1-012 | A product breaks the tolerance | The case list for {date} does not reconcile to ACE for {product}: a difference of {variance} accounts, {pct} percent. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The ACE batch is not complete; reconciliation not run | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A view, a contract call or the store is unavailable during the run | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The harness verdicts are for the release team and are not part of the message standard; the business messages above are the legacy texts, copied unchanged.

##### 15. Screens and states

No Workbench screen is built in this story. Two existing surfaces are exercised read-only through gateway-bff (DP-19): the reporting report "Reconciliation and data quality", read after the 07:30 refresh in the state of the run (green, red or not run per product, with the break rows and the referential completeness), and SCR-45 Data quality, read in its list state to confirm the same breaks are visible to the data steward. The harness changes no screen state and takes no screenshot.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the tolerance, the waiting periods, the threshold, the fixture values and the file names are configuration and the SIT data set; the release stage compares them with the parameter values in force.
- No personal data in logs, reports, tests or prompts: break rows carry account keys, account numbers and business keys only, and the fixtures are synthetic.
- No read of another service's tables: every cross-service field comes through the owner's contract, one hop with a 2 s timeout (DP-01, DP-11), and the harness asserts that no service reads a table of `rwb_source_data`.
- ACE data only through rwb-source-data, which owns the `recovery.v_ace_*` views (DP-05); no other service and no harness process opens an ACE view.
- No data lake path: no INT-19 adapter, no INT-20 extract and no lake copy of the case list is installed or read (DP-17).
- The harness runs in SIT only; it never points at UAT or production and never writes a service table.
- A held case list is never released by hand in this story; the rerun through the publish gate is the only release path.
- A failing verdict is never added to an exception list; a limit that must change is changed in the service story that owns it.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-011 for rwb-source-data. The reconciliation is published as one resource on `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`, with a typed workflow and activity contract on task queue `rwb-source-data` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and one consumed event, `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` (DP-10, DP-11, DP-14). The two lake extracts and the Power BI data set are removed, and rwb-reporting reads the results through this contract (DP-17; GAP-0495; ASM-0687). The path, the result element names and the workflow name are fixed here (GAP-0497; ASM-0689). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of rwb-source-data for the reconciliation resource: an OpenAPI 3.1 document for the two result reads, an AsyncAPI fragment for the consumed `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1`, the typed workflow and activity interfaces of `ReconciliationWorkflow` and `reconciliation`, the published interface `ReconciliationQuery`, the result and break-row schemas with their field IDs, the error envelope, the Idempotency-Key rule of the rerun, the nine contract tables of section 12 and the four contract fakes**, so that **the app, operations and test stories of this legacy key, and rwb-reporting, build against a fixed, testable contract on Day 1 without waiting for the reconciliation to be built**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020), and an event-started workflow is the replacement for the shared Quartz job (DP-10, ADR-016). The legacy story had no interface at all: the report read two CSV files in the lake and the job record in the shared job table, so every reader was coupled to a file layout and to a scheduler console. In the target the same figures are a resource with a version, a filter and an error body, and the run is a workflow with an input and an output schema.

The baseline matters on Day 1 because three parties move at once: the app story builds the activity against the same result shape, the operations story binds the rerun and the alerts to the same operation names, and rwb-reporting builds its dashboard against the two reads instead of the lake (DP-17). A change to an element name is then a contract change caught by a contract test, not a report that silently returns nothing.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the base path, the topic and the event names follow the platform rule (DP-13, DP-14).
- The workflow kit and the `rwb-recovery` namespace exist (RWB-PLT-WF, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON), so the workflow and activity contract is declared against the kit's version and build ID.
- The outbox, inbox and idempotency library is the reference for the table names and columns of the inbox and the stored rerun response (RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, DP-09).
- The platform error envelope, the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope and the message catalogue are the baseline; where this document narrows them it says so.
- The operations and their owners are read from the Ownership Map only: API-P1-003 belongs to this story, and API-P1-001 and API-P1-002 belong to the jobs and case-list contract (RWB-P1-E1002-CON).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 document on base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` for the two result reads, with the shared components of the service.
2. Draft the AsyncAPI fragment for the consumed `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1`, with the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope and the fields the run needs.
3. Declare the `ReconciliationQuery` interface and the workflow and activity contract of `ReconciliationWorkflow` and `reconciliation` on task queue `rwb-source-data`, with the input, the output and the retry policy.
4. Fix the result and break-row schemas against the field IDs of `reconciliation_result` and the break list, with no personal data field.
5. Agree the error envelope, the message mapping and the Idempotency-Key rule of the rerun that starts this workflow.
6. Publish the nine contract tables of section 12 and the four fakes.
7. Add the contract tests: schema validation, envelope validation, error mapping, workflow input validation, idempotent replay and version negotiation.
8. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-P1-E1011-APP, RWB-P1-E1011-OPS, RWB-P1-E1002-CON and rwb-reporting.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A query or path element fails schema validation on the read | 400 with the error envelope and the failing element | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |
| X2 | The caller reads without Platform administration R | 403 with the error envelope; nothing is returned | MSG-P4-002 | AC1 |
| X3 | A result id does not exist for the date range | 404 with the error envelope; no empty row is invented | None (the envelope carries the code and no message ID is fixed) | AC1 |
| X4 | The rerun POST arrives twice with the same key and body | The stored response is returned and the workflow is started once | None | AC6 |
| X5 | The rerun POST names a date the batch record does not show complete | 409 with the error envelope and the date | MSG-P1-001 | AC6 |
| X6 | A workflow input omits the business date | The workflow is not started; the caller sees the contract error | None | AC3 |
| X7 | A fake drifts from the document | The contract test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC7 |
| X8 | A value is missing from the source material | The element is marked with the placeholder and one gap row is carried | None | AC2 |

X1 to X3 are the read paths of API-P1-003; X4 to X6 are the run paths of the rerun and the workflow; X7 keeps the fakes honest. No message identifier is invented here: MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P1-001, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-GEN-006 come from the platform catalogue and the legacy story, and the 404 read carries the error envelope with no message ID of its own.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the Ownership Map and the workflow kit only |
| Negotiable | Element names inside the result are settled with rwb-reporting; the path, the operations, the event, the workflow name and the rules are fixed |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app, operations and test stories of this key and the rwb-reporting dashboard on Day 1 |
| Estimable | Two documents, one interface, one workflow contract, two schemas, nine contract tables and four fakes |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against an artefact, not against a business outcome |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Reconciliation contract baseline for rwb-source-data

  Background:
    Given the service naming rule of the platform library is in force
    Given the reconciliation resource is owned by rwb-source-data (P1) and its results are read by rwb-reporting

  Scenario: AC1 The two result reads are described and validate (new, D-RCV-60)

    Then it declares the base /api/recovery/source-data/v1
    Then it declares GET /admin/reconciliation/results with the filters recCode, product, result, from and to, and GET /admin/reconciliation/results/{resultId}, both owned by rwb-source-data
    Then every operation names Platform administration R and its error responses 401, 403, 404 and 503

  Scenario: AC2 The result and break-row schemas carry the field IDs and no personal data (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the result schema of the document
    When it is compared with reconciliation_result
    Then every property maps to a field ID of DF-OPS-118 to DF-OPS-129
    Then the break-row schema carries the table, the column and the business key, and the account key with its days past due, and no name, address, identity number or contact point
    Then a result row carries recCode, businessDate, productGroup, sourceCount, workbenchCount, sourceAmount, workbenchAmount, varianceCount, variancePct, tolerancePct and result

  Scenario: AC3 ReconciliationWorkflow and reconciliation are published as a typed contract (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the workflow contract of the document
    When it is reviewed against the workflow kit
    Then it declares ReconciliationWorkflow on task queue rwb-source-data in namespace rwb-recovery with workflow ID recon-{businessDate}
    Then it declares the activity reconciliation with the business date and the source system as input and the run summary as output
    Then the run summary carries the six result rows of the date, the orphan count and the publish state
    Then a missing business date fails validation and starts no workflow

  Scenario: AC4 The AceDataReady intake is fixed with its envelope, key and dedupe (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the AsyncAPI fragment of the document
    When a consumed message is validated
    Then it is rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1 on topic rwb.source-data.events.v1
    Then it uses the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope with id, source, type, specversion, time, subject and datacontenttype
    Then it carries sourceSystem, businessDate, status and completedAt and no personal data
    Then the inbox dedupes on the event id and the workflow starts once per business date and event

  Scenario: AC5 The consumed rwb-case elements are fixed and faked (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the three consumed elements of the document
    When each is read against its owner's published contract
    Then the case query operation returns the excluded accounts for a business date with product group, account key and reason code
    Then the parameter read returns recon.tolerance.pct and case.entry.dpd for the business date
    Then the reference-data read returns LOV-PRODUCT and LOV-REC-RESULT with their versions
    Then no ACE view and no rwb_case table is named in the document

  Scenario: AC6 The error envelope, the message mapping and the rerun rule are fixed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the error components of the document
    When a 400, 401, 403, 404, 409 or 503 response is produced
    Then the body carries the code, the message, the messageId, the traceId and the field list
    Then MSG-P1-012, MSG-P1-001, MSG-GEN-006 and MSG-P4-002 keep their legacy text
    Then the rerun of POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun requires the Idempotency-Key header and starts ReconciliationWorkflow for the business date
    Then a replay with the same key returns the stored response and a date that is not complete is refused with 409

  Scenario: AC7 The nine contract tables are complete, the fakes match them and no lake element exists (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the contract section of this story
    When the nine sub-tables are reviewed
    Then each of 12.1 to 12.9 is present and names its owner from the Ownership Map
    Then the four fakes answer the paths and payloads of 12.2 and 12.4
    Then the contract tests compare each fake with the document and fail on any drift
    Then no extract, no lake target and no Power BI data set appears in any schema, path or fake
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One REST base per service: `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`; the document declares no other service's path | DP-13; Arch v5 slide 41 notes |
| BR2 | Event names are `rwb.<short>.<Event>.v1` on `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; this resource consumes one event and publishes none | DP-14; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR3 | Every event carries the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope and no personal data | Arch v5 slide 42 notes; DP-09 |
| BR4 | Every POST declares the Idempotency-Key header and stores its response; the rerun is the only POST this resource relies on | DP-09; TSD P1 v3 T-A.2 |
| BR5 | Error responses use one envelope and one message ID per condition; the legacy texts are copied unchanged | Arch v5 platform baseline; Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR6 | A schema change is additive within major version 1; a breaking change is a new major version | Arch v5 slide 42 notes |
| BR7 | The document lists only operations owned by rwb-source-data; the case query, the parameters and the reference data are described as consumed | Ownership Map v1 |
| BR8 | No business value is fixed in the contract: the tolerance, the entry threshold and the waiting periods stay parameters | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17; DP-06 |
| BR9 | No lake element exists in the contract: the result is read, never extracted (DP-17) | Arch v5 slides 2 and 37; DP-17 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The two reads, the workflow contract and the event are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | The app, operations and test stories and rwb-reporting accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | An element is added within major version 1 | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | An element is removed, renamed or retyped, or the workflow name changes | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Tech lead of rwb-source-data | Owns the document, the AsyncAPI fragment, the workflow contract and the fakes; tags the baseline |
| Solution architect | Approves a breaking change and a new major version |
| rwb-reporting owner and the app, operations and test teams | Review and sign off the parts they consume |
| Platform workflow owner | Owns the workflow kit, the namespace and the worker versioning rule the contract reuses |
| Data steward | Confirms that no personal data field is declared in the event or in a break row |

The per-service login named in the security scheme is `rwb_source_data` (DP-02; Architecture v5 slide 29); the document names it as a security scheme and carries no credential.

##### 11. Data

The contract declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Result resource | `resultId`, `recCode`, `businessDate`, `productGroup`, `sourceCount`, `workbenchCount`, `sourceAmount`, `workbenchAmount`, `varianceCount`, `variancePct`, `tolerancePct`, `result`, from `reconciliation_result` fields DF-OPS-118 to DF-OPS-129 |
| Break row resource | `recCode`, `businessDate`, `productGroup`, `objectName`, `fieldName`, `businessKey`, `daysPastDue` where the key is an account, and `reasonCode`; no personal field |
| Workflow input | `businessDate`, `sourceSystem`, `eventId` |
| Run summary | The rows of the date, the orphan count and the publish state RELEASED or HELD |
| Event payload | `sourceSystem`, `businessDate`, `status`, `completedAt`; no personal data |

The names `resultId`, `recCode`, `productGroup` and the element list above are fixed by this story because no source gives a path, a result shape or a workflow name (GAP-0497; ASM-0689); the field IDs are the fixed part and an element may be renamed only through the versioning rule.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-source-data (P1); base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`; access Platform administration R with scope applied.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/admin/reconciliation/results` | Result page filtered by `recCode`, `product`, `result`, `from` and `to` | Platform administration R |
| GET | `/admin/reconciliation/results/{resultId}` | One result row with its break rows | Platform administration R |

API-P1-003 is the identifier of the first operation (TSD P1 v3 T-A.1); the second is the single-row read the contract needs and its identifier is not fixed by any source (GAP-0497). `GET /admin/jobs` (API-P1-001) and `POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun` (API-P1-002) belong to RWB-P1-E1002-CON; this document references them as consumed and documents no shape of theirs beyond the Idempotency-Key rule.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | the case query operation of the rwb-case contract | P3 rwb-case | Excluded accounts for a business date, faked |
| GET | the parameter read of the rwb-case contract | P3 rwb-case | `recon.tolerance.pct`, `case.entry.dpd`, faked |
| GET | the reference-data read of the rwb-case contract | P3 rwb-case | `LOV-PRODUCT` and `LOV-REC-RESULT`, faked |
| POST | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun` | P1, RWB-P1-E1002-CON | The run trigger this resource is bound to, documented by its own story |

The three rwb-case elements are one hop each with a 2 s timeout and a breaker (DP-11). The document names no path of the case query beyond the contract's own operation id, because the rwb-case baseline owns the path and this story must not restate it (DP-11; BR7).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. `rwb.source-data.events.v1` carries `AceDataReady` and `AceDataLate`, and both belong to RWB-P1-E1013-APP; the reconciliation publishes no fact of its own and writes no outbox row.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Consumer contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` | `rwb.source-data.events.v1` | P1 | `sourceSystem`, `businessDate`, `status`, `completedAt`; starts `ReconciliationWorkflow` after the case list step; inbox dedupe on the event id |

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ReconciliationWorkflow` | Workflow, one run per business date, workflow ID `recon-{businessDate}` | `rwb-source-data` | Input and output schemas; retry policy; search attributes `BusinessDate`, `RecSource` |
| `reconciliation` | Activity | `rwb-source-data` | Business date and source system in; run summary out; one transaction for the rows and the publish state |
| `ReconciliationQuery` | Published interface | — | The typed read the reporting projection and the admin surface call: results by date range and filter, and one result by id; one implementation behind 12.1 |

The interface name is fixed here and no source gives one (GAP-0497; ASM-0689). It is a Java type inside the service and not a shared library across services: the cross-service path is REST (DP-11).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The workflow is event-started; the only daily start of the service is the `DailyCaseList` Schedule of RWB-P1-E1002-CON, which this resource does not register or own (DP-10; Architecture v5 slide 44).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| `reconciliation_result` | P1 (`rwb_source_data`) | The result resource, unique on `(rec_code, business_date, product_group)` |
| `case_list_row` | P1 (`rwb_source_data`) | Read for the two count checks; `publish_status` written for the date |
| `data_product_load` | P1 (`rwb_source_data`) | Read for the completeness gate of the date |
| `outbox_event`, `processed_event`, `idempotency_key` | PLT library, created in `rwb_source_data` | Inbox dedupe of the consumed event and the stored rerun response |

No other table is named in the contract, no `rwb_case`, `rwb_treatment` or `rwb_payment` table is read, and no foreign key leaves the schema (DP-01).

| RWB-P3-E1042-CON fake | `recon.tolerance.pct` 0.00 and 0.10, `case.entry.dpd` 90, `recon.treatment.days` 2, `recon.payment.days` 1 | App story, contract tests |

| View fixture | The eight views of RWB-P1-E1069-APP with a batch row and a failing `v_ace_account` stub | App story, contract tests |

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 provided, 3 consumed plus the rerun binding | Result reads; case query, parameters and reference data; one hop, 2 s |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** `openapi/rwb-source-data-reconciliation-v1.yaml` (OpenAPI 3.1), `asyncapi/rwb-source-data-acedataready-v1.yaml` (AsyncAPI 3 fragment), `contract/reconciliation-workflow.yaml` with the workflow, the activity and the `ReconciliationQuery` interface, `contract/error-envelope.yaml`, the idempotency and versioning rules in the contract README, and the four WireMock mappings.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-02 | `recovery_svc` login | One login per service | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting | none; gap if the story needs lake data |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-11 is the pattern this baseline delivers: the published interface of the legacy story is replaced by an OpenAPI document, a workflow contract and one typed query interface behind them. DP-17 is used as a removal, and the contract test of AC7 enforces it. DP-03 and DP-19 are named in the contract only where a run record and the admin surface consume it; the baseline builds neither.

**Build steps**

1. OpenAPI skeleton with the base path, the security scheme, the error responses and the shared components; schema lint in the pipeline.
2. The two result reads and their schemas, with the field IDs and the break rows.
3. AsyncAPI fragment for the consumed event, with the CloudEvents envelope and the dedupe rule.
4. The workflow contract: `ReconciliationWorkflow`, `reconciliation`, the run summary and the retry policy.
5. The `ReconciliationQuery` interface and its documented answer shapes.
6. Error envelope and message mapping, with the legacy texts copied unchanged.
7. The Idempotency-Key rule of the rerun and the versioning rule.
8. The four fakes and the stub fixtures.
9. The contract tests; a drift between a fake and the document fails the build.
10. Baseline tag and the consumer sign-off note.

**Done when.** The OpenAPI and AsyncAPI artefacts validate in the pipeline, the workflow contract is accepted by the workflow kit owner, the contract tests pass, the four fakes answer every consumed element and the app, operations and test stories and rwb-reporting have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-012 | A product breaks the tolerance | The case list for {date} does not reconcile to ACE for {product}: a difference of {variance} accounts, {pct} percent. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The batch for the date is not complete | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A read without Platform administration R | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required query or path element is missing | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A downstream is unavailable | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |

The message IDs are contract elements and the texts are the agreed texts, copied unchanged from the legacy story and the platform catalogue; no new wording is introduced. A 404 read carries the error envelope and no message ID of its own.

##### 15. Screens and states

The contract serves the admin result list rendered through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) and the rwb-reporting dashboard that reads the same operations. The screen field list and the composite route specification belong to the platform edge story and to rwb-reporting; this story fixes only the case of the merge, which is the result row and its break rows. No Power BI report is in scope.

This story owns no legacy acceptance criterion, so the nine rows are the legacy test cases of RWB-E1-011 listed against the new criteria they exercise: their IDs, their order and their data are kept, and the Covers column names this story's own criteria only where the legacy case tests the contract's artefact. The legacy criteria themselves are owned by RWB-P1-E1011-APP and the sibling slices and proven end to end in RWB-ITG-E1011-ITG. The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code or in the contract: the tolerance, the entry threshold and the waiting periods stay parameters, and the product groups and the result list stay reference data.
- No personal data in events, workflow inputs or logs and none in an event schema, an example or a fake: the event carries a source system, a date, a status and a time, and a break row carries business keys and account keys only.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `recovery.v_ace_*` views: the document names no ACE table and no `rwb_*` schema other than `rwb_source_data`.
- No cross-schema read and no cross-schema key: the contract names only P1's tables, and no element of it is a foreign key into another schema (DP-01).
- One REST base, one topic, one task queue per service; a document that names another service's base, topic or queue fails the review (DP-13, DP-14).
- No lake element: an extract, a lake target or a Power BI data set in the document fails AC7 (DP-17).
- Every example is synthetic; no production payload is copied into a schema or a fake.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: contract baseline of the baseline-measures capability of rwb-reporting, split from RWB-E1-013. It fixes the two reads on `/api/recovery/reporting/v1` (DP-13) with the definitions read that RWB-P3-E1013-APP consumes, the columns of DF-RPT-031 to DF-RPT-058 in the three tables, the six closed lists, the five consumed rows of rwb-case and rwb-source-data, the decision-record element of DP-03, the 01:30 Schedule of DP-10, the rights of TSD P9 T6.1, the error envelope, the fakes and the absence tests. The data lake, the INT-19 extract and the trailer are removed (DP-17); the plan's C row does not carry the two rwb-source-data rows; and no source gives the path of the definitions read or the approver's type (GAP-2566, GAP-2567, GAP-2569, GAP-2570, GAP-2571, GAP-2572; ASM-4232, ASM-4233, ASM-4235, ASM-4236, ASM-4237, ASM-4238). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead of rwb-reporting**, I want **the published contract baseline of the baseline-measures capability — the two reads on `/api/recovery/reporting/v1`, the three tables' columns and their closed lists, the five consumed rows of rwb-case and rwb-source-data, the decision-record element, the Schedule of the 01:30 run, the rights, the error envelope and the fakes**, so that **RWB-P9-E1013-APP, RWB-P3-E1013-APP, RWB-P1-E1013-APP, the wave 1 harness and the deployment story build against one fixed, testable surface on Day 1 and a measure column, a list value, a consumed row or a read shape can never drift between the four services without a failing build**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). The legacy story of RWB-E1-013 crossed three boundaries at once inside one module: the definitions, the case and payment facts, and the lake extract. The target splits them, and each boundary is now a contract another team builds against: rwb-case serves the facts, RWB-P3-E1013-APP owns them; rwb-source-data serves the payments and the gate, RWB-P1-E1013-APP owns them; rwb-reporting owns the definitions, the snapshot and the publish, and serves the catalog that rwb-case needs so that a band version cannot retire a band a definition still uses.

The baseline also fixes the naming the checks require: schema `rwb_reporting`, login `rwb_reporting`, base `/api/recovery/reporting/v1`, topic `rwb.reporting.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics, task queue `rwb-reporting` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.reporting` (Template and Rules §R4; context pack P9). It records that this service holds no `v_ace_*` grant and no grant on `rwb_case`, so DP-05 is declared as a prohibition and the ACE data is consumed on the owner's contract only.

Four points are carried as gaps and assumptions rather than decided quietly: the plan's C row is None while the app story consumes five rows (GAP-2567), the Ownership Map gives this service no event while the wave 1 harness names `rwb.reporting.ReportPublished.v1` (GAP-2569), no source gives the path or the shape of the definitions read that rwb-case consumes (GAP-2572), and the legacy story assigns the measures read to Epic 2 while the Ownership Map gives the operation to this service (GAP-2570).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the base, the topic, the queue and the event names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- The platform error envelope, the paging and filter convention and the `Idempotency-Key` rule are the platform baseline (Architecture v5 slide 11); where this document narrows them it says so.
- The ownership of the objects is taken from the Ownership Map only: `measure_definition`, `measure_snapshot` and `measure_publish` are P9's; `recovery_case`, `queue`, `case_account` and the reference rows are P3's; every `v_ace_*` view is P1's; `decision_log_entry` is P7's.
- RWB-P3-E1013-APP, RWB-P3-E1018-CON, RWB-P3-E1043-CON and RWB-P1-E1013-APP publish the five rows this baseline consumes, with their fakes. The two rwb-source-data rows are not in this story's contract-dependency row, which is None, and the absence is recorded (GAP-2567; ASM-4233).
- The decision-record library of DP-03 and the workflow kit of DP-10 are platform work, named here and built elsewhere.
- The three tables are declared by this baseline and created by the app story's migration; this story creates no table, no column and no migration.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 document of rwb-reporting for this capability: the two reads with their query parameters, the answer elements, the paging, the rights and the error responses.
2. Fix the three elements of the tables: the definition columns of DF-RPT-031 to DF-RPT-040, the snapshot columns of DF-RPT-041 to DF-RPT-052 and the publish columns of DF-RPT-053 to DF-RPT-058, with their types, their required flags and the list each of them is declared against.
3. Fix the consumed rows: the case-facts read of RWB-P3-E1013-APP, the case-record read of RWB-P3-E1018-CON, the reference-list read of RWB-P3-E1043-CON, the payments read and the freshness read of RWB-P1-E1013-APP, marking every field the sources do not give with the placeholder.
4. Record the decision-record element of DP-03, written before the snapshot rows commit, and the Schedule element of DP-10 with its 01:30 time, its catch-up policy and its no-overlap rule.
5. Record the closed vocabulary of the six lists, the rights of the two reads, the naming baseline and the rule that no measure code, formula, unit or band is a constant of the code.
6. Publish the contract tables of section 12 and the six fakes of 12.8.
7. Add the contract tests: schema validation, the additive rule, the vocabulary, the shapes, the error envelope, the absence of a `v_ace_*` read and of a `recovery_case` property, the absence of a published and of a consumed event, the drift between a fake and the document, and the absence of a lake path.
8. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-P9-E1013-APP, RWB-P3-E1013-APP, RWB-P1-E1013-APP, RWB-P9-E1013-OPS and the wave 1 harness.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A response or a request body fails schema validation | The build fails on the schema lint; a deployed service answers 400 or 500 with the error envelope | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1, AC4 |
| X2 | A property is renamed or removed within major version 1 | The contract test fails; the change needs a new major version | None | AC1, AC2 |
| X3 | A contract fake drifts from the document | The drift test fails the build and the merge is blocked | None | AC6 |
| X4 | A consumed row has a field list the sources do not give | The row carries the placeholder, the gap and the assumption, and the fake is derived from the published document | None | AC3, AC5 |
| X5 | A value outside one of the six closed lists appears in the document or in an example | The vocabulary test fails the build | None | AC2 |
| X6 | The document declares another service's operation as provided, a `v_ace_*` view, a `recovery_case` property or a rule row | The review fails the baseline; the boundary test fails the build | None | AC3 |
| X7 | The document declares an event of this service, a consumed event, a second topic or a lake path | The absence test fails the build | None | AC5 |
| X8 | The rights of a read are not the ones TSD P9 T-A.1 and T6.1 declare | The access test fails the build | MSG-P4-002 | AC4 |
| X9 | The document types `approved_by` as a string while TSD P9 T3.1 types it `uuid`, or the reverse | The baseline carries the TSD type, and the legacy approver reference is carried as a comment on the element | None | AC2, §11 |

X1 to X4 and X6 to X8 are the paths of a contract baseline carried from the platform convention, X5 is the closed vocabulary and X9 is the one type conflict the sources give (GAP-2571; ASM-4237).

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the Ownership Map, the FSD P9 and TSD P9 appendices and the published rows of rwb-case and rwb-source-data only |
| Negotiable | The element names beyond the ones the sources give, the example values and the fake fixtures are settled in the baseline review; the two reads, the tables, the lists, the base, the topic, the queue and the schema are fixed by the target architecture |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app story, the P3 facts story, the P1 payments story, the deployment story and the wave 1 harness on Day 1 |
| Estimable | One OpenAPI document, nine contract tables, six fakes and six new contract tests |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |
