**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-013 for rwb-reporting. It deploys the measures capability of the service from the template with its own login and its per-service migration for the three tables and the frozen-row trigger, registers the 01:30 run of JOB-15 once as a Temporal Schedule and no Quartz row, publishes the panels for the run, the gate, the publish state and the freshness stamp, wires the alerts to the message IDs of the feature within the 15-minute target, and publishes the run books for a held run, a stale product, a refused rerun and a failed run. It declares no topic, no consumer group, no lake path and no outbound extract (GAP-2566, GAP-2573, GAP-2574, GAP-2575; ASM-4232, ASM-4239, ASM-4240, ASM-4241). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform engineer**, I want **the measures capability of rwb-reporting deployed from the service template with its own login, its migration for the three tables and the frozen-row trigger, its 01:30 Schedule registered once, the panels for the run, the gate answer, the publish state and the freshness stamp, the alerts wired to MSG-P9-001, MSG-P9-003, MSG-P1-001, MSG-GEN-006 and MSG-P7-003 within the 15-minute target, and the run books for a held run, a stale product, a refused rerun, a failed run and a slow read**, so that **an operator finds a held publish or a late ACE batch before the working day without reading code, and no release can quietly restore the data lake, a Quartz trigger, a second Schedule or a second source of truth for the baseline**.

This story deploys an existing capability. It adds no topic, no consumer group, no endpoint and no measure: the three tables are rows of `rwb_reporting`, the run is the Schedule of DP-10, the facts and the gate are read on the P3 and P1 contracts, and SCR-44 is reached through the gateway-bff route.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story had one module, one Quartz row and one operator, and its failure signals were a run record nobody watched outside office hours: a baseline that published twice, a definition loaded without a formula and a lake that did not answer were all found at month end. In the target the measures are a service with its own release, its own login, its own Schedule and its own alerting (DP-02, ADR-023), and the operational question changes from "did the job run" to four separate questions: did the run start, is it waiting for the gate, did it publish or hold, and is the value of a date explained by its definition version (NFR-067, NFR-068).

Two failures are separated on purpose. A **failed** run is an incident of this service and pages the owner role of the catalogue row. A **held** run is a signal about a source: it pages nobody, it raises MSG-GEN-006 or MSG-P1-001 to the data steward and the operations channel, and the run book says in one line that no Workbench action will make the ACE batch arrive. Deployment is part of the capability because a chart that carries a second credential, a release that re-adds a lake egress path, or a Schedule registered twice would break the guardrails the story set was built on (DP-17, DP-10).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template, the chart skeleton and the pipeline are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-LIB).
- The observability stack of the platform is available (RWB-PLT-OBS, ADR-023): metrics, traces and logs with one trace across the composite route and the service.
- The workflow kit is available (RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, DP-10) and namespace `rwb-recovery` exists with queue `rwb-reporting`, so the Schedule of the run can be registered and polled.
- The Kafka event platform is available (RWB-PLT-EVT); `rwb.reporting.events.v1` and its retry and `.dlt` topics exist by the naming rule, and this release publishes to none of them and subscribes to none.
- RWB-P9-E1013-CON is published, so the smoke profile and the drift test run against the two reads, the reference-load element and the six fakes of that baseline.
- RWB-PLT-E1056-OPS loads the catalogue baseline with `owner_role`, `expected_minutes`, `alert_after_minutes` and `runbook_path` for JOB-15, so every alert and every run-book link resolves to an owner without a code change. The threshold values have no source and are values-file entries (GAP-2574; ASM-4240).
- The three environments DEV, SIT and UAT exist with their platform session, their database endpoint and their Temporal endpoint.
- The three tables of the capability are created by the app story's migration, and this release runs the same per-service sequence before the deployment is marked ready (DP-15; GAP-2575; ASM-4241).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. The pipeline builds one image and one chart version from the same commit, runs the unit, component and contract tests, scans the image and the dependencies, and publishes the chart.
2. The chart deploys rwb-reporting with the rwb-reporting login, the pre-deploy migration job that runs the per-service Flyway sequence in `rwb_reporting` — the three tables, their unique keys and the trigger that refuses an UPDATE or a DELETE of a frozen row — and the readiness and liveness probes of the api deployment.
3. The worker deployment polls queue `rwb-reporting` in namespace `rwb-recovery` with the build ID of the release, so the workflow of the 01:30 run is available before the first tick.
4. The provisioning step registers the Schedule of JOB-15 once, at 01:30 Asia/Bangkok, one run per business date, catch-up of one missed run, no overlapping execution, and asserts that no Quartz trigger, no shared job table and no second Schedule of this job exists.
5. The provisioning step asserts that the release declares no topic, no consumer group, no event and no lake path: no INT-19 or INT-20 client, no extract writer, no trailer builder, no outbound batch and no route to a data store outside the cluster (DP-17).
6. The dashboards are published: runs by business date with their state, duration against `expected_minutes`, the gate answer by product, the publish state and the hold reason, the freshness stamp lag, the frozen row count, the refused rerun count, and the read latency and error rate of the two operations.
7. The alerts are wired to the message IDs of section 14 and to the run-book entries of section 13; each threshold and each channel is a values-file entry and each owner role comes from the catalogue row of JOB-15.
8. A smoke step in the SIT profile calls the two reads through gateway-bff for a synthetic business date, reruns JOB-15 for the baseline date and asserts that the frozen rows are unchanged and the run record carries MSG-P9-001, and asserts that a forced record failure leaves no snapshot row behind.
9. The run books are published and reviewed with the on-call rota: a held run for a stale product, a refused rerun of a frozen date, a failed run, a slow or failed read, and a publish that stays held after two runs.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The migration job fails, or the frozen-row trigger is missing after it | The deployment stays unready and the pipeline stops; no traffic reaches the new version | None | AC1 |
| X2 | A release declares a topic, a consumer group, an event or a Schedule of its own | The provisioning assertion fails the release | None | AC3 |
| X3 | A release adds a lake path, an extract writer, a trailer or an outbound batch | The boundary assertion fails the release | None | AC3, AC6 |
| X4 | A run fails | The failed-run alert fires within the 15-minute target to the owner role of the catalogue row | None | AC5 |
| X5 | A run waits because the gate answer is HOLD | The wait panel rises, MSG-P1-001 is raised to the data steward and the operations channel, and no page is sent | MSG-P1-001 | AC5 |
| X6 | A publish stays held after two runs | The hold panel rises with the reason, MSG-GEN-006 follows the run book entry | MSG-GEN-006 | AC4, AC5 |
| X7 | A rerun of the baseline date is refused | The refused-rerun count rises and the run book entry explains the frozen rule | MSG-P9-001 | AC6 |
| X8 | A measure is listed with no definition in force | The run record names it, the panel counts it and the entry names the loader | MSG-P9-003 | AC4, AC5 |
| X9 | A read is slow or fails | The read latency and error-rate alerts fire; the composite route is checked before the service | None | AC4, AC5 |
| X10 | The smoke step cannot see the second run after a rerun, or sees a changed frozen row | The release stops; the run log, the Schedule history and the trigger are checked | None | AC6 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the chart skeleton, the platform provisioning, the observability stack and the published contract baseline; builds no application code and no measure |
| Negotiable | Replica counts, resource sizes, retention, thresholds and channel names are environment values, not story decisions |
| Valuable | Turns the measures into an operated capability with an owner, a signal and a run book for each of its five failures |
| Estimable | One chart, one pipeline stage, one migration job, one Schedule registration, two probes, eight panels, six alert rules and five run-book entries |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the run books |
| Testable | Every criterion tests an artefact: the chart renders, the assertions pass, the panels carry data, an alert fires on a synthetic metric, a run-book entry resolves |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Deployment of the baseline measures of rwb-reporting

  Background:
    Given the service template chart and the platform pipeline are in force
    Given the target environment is SIT

  Scenario: AC1 The chart and values deploy rwb-reporting with its own login and its migration with the frozen-row trigger (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rwb-reporting Helm chart and its values-dev.yaml, values-sit.yaml and values-uat.yaml
    When the chart is rendered for DEV, SIT and UAT
    Then each render succeeds with the chart version and the image digest pinned
    Then the release declares the rwb-reporting login reference and no other service's credential and no ACE credential
    Then the migration job runs the per-service Flyway sequence in schema rwb_reporting and creates measure_definition, measure_snapshot and measure_publish with their unique keys, the publish row keyed on business_date, and the trigger that refuses an UPDATE or a DELETE where frozen = true
    Then the migration is idempotent and a second run of it changes nothing
    Then the api deployment answers its readiness and liveness probes on the health operation of the template, and the worker deployment polls queue rwb-reporting in namespace rwb-recovery
    Then no replica count, resource size, timeout or threshold is hard-coded in the template

  Scenario: AC2 The pipeline promotes one artefact and runs the contract tests (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a commit on the main line
    When the pipeline runs
    Then it builds one image and one chart version from the same commit
    Then it runs the unit and component tests of RWB-P9-E1013-APP and the contract tests of RWB-P9-E1013-CON and fails the build on a drift between a fake and the document
    Then it scans the image and the dependencies and fails on a critical finding
    Then it promotes the same artefact through DEV, SIT and UAT without a rebuild

  Scenario: AC3 The Schedule is registered once and the release carries no topic, no consumer group and no lake path (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the provisioning step of rwb-reporting for the measures capability
    When it runs against the environment
    Then exactly one Schedule exists for the run of JOB-15, at 01:30 Asia/Bangkok, one run per business date, catch-up of one missed run and no overlapping execution, registered on queue rwb-reporting in namespace rwb-recovery
    Then the release declares no Quartz trigger, no shared job table and no second Schedule for the same job, and the assertion fails the release when a second one appears
    Then the release declares no topic of its own, no consumer group and no event, and rwb.reporting.events.v1 keeps the partitions, the retention and the retry and .dlt topics of the platform
    Then the assertion fails the release when the chart carries an INT-19 or INT-20 client, an extract writer, a trailer builder, an outbound batch or any path to a data store outside the cluster
    Then no release adds a credential or a job name that can start or rerun an ACE batch or read an ACE table

  Scenario: AC4 The eight panels show the five operational questions (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published dashboard of rwb-reporting
    When it is opened for a business date
    Then it shows the runs of that date with their state, rerun and complete, and the duration of each against its expected_minutes from the catalogue
    Then it shows the gate answer by product with the date of the product and the count of products in HOLD
    Then it shows the publish state of the date with its hold reason and the lag of its freshness stamp
    Then it shows the frozen row count of the baseline date and the count of refused reruns
    Then it shows the runs that wrote no value for a measure with no definition in force, and the read latency and error rate of the two operations
    Then every panel reads an identifier, a code, a date, a count or a duration and no customer field

  Scenario: AC5 The alerts fire to the catalogue owner within the 15-minute target (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the alert rules of the capability and their values-file thresholds
    When a synthetic metric crosses each rule
    Then a failed run alerts the owner_role of its catalogue row within 15 minutes of the failure
    Then a run in its waiting state past its cut-off raises MSG-P1-001 to the data steward and the operations channel and pages nobody
    Then a publish held for two runs raises MSG-GEN-006 with its reason and links the run-book entry
    Then a measure with no definition in force raises MSG-P9-003 and links the loader run book
    Then a read error or a latency above its threshold alerts the platform administrator role
    Then every threshold is a values-file entry and no threshold, owner or channel is written in the chart or the code

  Scenario: AC6 The run books and the smoke profile prove the frozen baseline and the absent lake (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the run books of section 13 and the SIT smoke profile
    When the smoke step runs through gateway-bff
    Then it reads the measures and the definitions of a synthetic business date on the two operations of the baseline
    Then it reruns JOB-15 for the baseline date and receives MSG-P9-001, and the frozen rows of measure_snapshot are unchanged and the trigger refuses a direct UPDATE of one of them
    Then a forced record failure leaves no snapshot row, no publish state and no baseline flag behind
    Then the smoke profile and the release manifest name no data lake, no INT-19 extract, no trailer and no outbound batch
    Then each of the five run-book entries names its message ID, its first check, its owner role and its escalation
```

These six criteria are new for the deployment of the capability and test artefacts only; they restate no business outcome owned by RWB-P9-E1013-APP and copy no criterion of the legacy story. The wave 1 harness RWB-ITG-E1013-ITG consumes the deployed capability and copies none of these criteria.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One login per service and no ACE credential in the release; grants on `rwb_reporting` only | DP-02; RWB-PLT-TPL |
| BR2 | The per-service Flyway sequence owns the schema objects the release needs, and no other service's schema is touched; the frozen-row trigger is part of the release and an absent trigger fails it | DP-15; ADR-021; legacy BR2 |
| BR3 | The run is one Schedule of this service and no Quartz row, no shared job table and no second Schedule of the same job | DP-10; ADR-016; GAP-2573 |
| BR4 | The release declares no topic, no consumer group and no event; the topic of the service stays as the platform provisioned it | DP-09, DP-14; GAP-2569 |
| BR5 | No release adds a lake path, an extract writer, a trailer or an outbound batch, and no release adds a path that reads an ACE table | DP-17; ADR-018; GAP-2566 |
| BR6 | A failed run alerts its catalogue owner role within 15 minutes; a held run raises its message and pages nobody | NFR-068; RWB-P9-E1013-APP BR8 |
| BR7 | Every threshold, channel and owner is a values-file or catalogue entry, never code | NFR-067; Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 (s17) |
| BR8 | One artefact is promoted through the three environments without a rebuild | ADR-023; Template and Rules §R8 |
| BR9 | The panels, the alerts and the run books read identifiers, codes, dates, counts and durations only; no personal data reaches a panel, a log line or a trace | Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 (s17) |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | Pipeline run | The pipeline and the boundary assertions pass | Deployed to DEV |
| Deployed to DEV | Promotion | The smoke profile passes | Deployed to SIT |
| Deployed to SIT | Promotion | The smoke profile, the panels and one alert per rule pass | Deployed to UAT |
| Deployed | A run fails or waits | The alert rule fires | Alerted, run book entry opened |
| Alerted | Run book completed | The run completes after the gate answers COMPLETE, or the cause is cleared | Recovered, the alert closes |
| Deployed | A release declares a topic, a consumer group, an event, a second Schedule or a lake path | The assertion fails | Release refused; the previous version keeps running |
| Deployed | The Schedule is registered a second time | The provisioning step refuses the second registration | Unchanged, one Schedule |

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None by this story. It deploys the two reads and the reference-load element of RWB-P9-E1013-CON — `GET /api/recovery/reporting/v1/reports/measures`, `GET /api/recovery/reporting/v1/measure-definitions` and the reference-load element of table `measure_definition` — and declares no operation of its own. The composite route is the platform's (RWB-PLT-N001-CON, DP-19).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None consumed by this story at run time. The smoke profile calls the two reads through gateway-bff, and the P3 and P1 fakes of RWB-P9-E1013-CON stand behind them in SIT.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The service topic `rwb.reporting.events.v1` exists by the naming rule with its retry and `.dlt` topics, and this release publishes nothing and declares no producer of its own. The event question that the wave 1 harness raises is recorded in the contract baseline of this key and not resolved here (GAP-2569; ASM-4235).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The release declares no consumer group and binds no subscription; the run starts on its Schedule and reads its sources on the two contracts.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None new. The worker deployment polls queue `rwb-reporting` in namespace `rwb-recovery` with the build ID of the release, so `MeasureRunWorkflow` and its `measureRun` activity of RWB-P9-E1013-APP are available before the first tick of the Schedule.

###### 12.6 Schedules

One, registered by this story: the run of JOB-15 at 01:30 Asia/Bangkok for the previous business date, one run per date, catch-up of one missed run and no overlapping execution, on `rwb-reporting` in namespace `rwb-recovery` (DP-10). The registration is idempotent and a second one is refused; no Quartz row and no shared job table is deployed. The Airflow chain of Architecture v5 slide 9 is not wired to this run, and the one trigger that exists is the Schedule (GAP-2573; ASM-4239).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| measure_definition | P9 (`rwb_reporting`) | Deployed and migrated here; written by the app story's load |
| measure_snapshot | P9 (`rwb_reporting`) | Deployed and migrated here, with the unique key and the frozen-row trigger |
| measure_publish | P9 (`rwb_reporting`) | Deployed and migrated here, keyed on the business date |
| Flyway history of the service | P9 (`rwb_reporting`) | The per-service migration record of this release |

No table of rwb-case, rwb-source-data or rwb-decision is touched, and the release holds no `v_ace_*` grant (DP-01, DP-05).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Environment | Use |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-case case-facts fake | SIT and UAT smoke only | Gives the run a business date of facts to compute from |
| rwb-source-data payments and freshness fake | SIT and UAT smoke only | A gate answer COMPLETE and a HOLD with a stale product |
| gateway-bff composite route fake | SIT only | The merged SCR-44 answer with the run of the baseline date |
| Frozen-row seed | SIT and UAT smoke only | Proves the refused rerun, MSG-P9-001 and the trigger |
| Forced record failure switch | SIT only | Proves that a failed record leaves no snapshot row and no publish state |

The fakes never run in production: in the production environment every answer is the real one, and a missing answer is shown as unknown rather than faked.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 reads deployed, 1 element deployed, none declared here | The measures read, the definitions read and the reference-load element of RWB-P9-E1013-CON |
| Kafka | None | No topic, producer or consumer group declared by this release |
| Temporal | 1 worker on `rwb-reporting` and 1 Schedule | The run of JOB-15 at 01:30 and the workflow of the app story |
| File | None | No file path is deployed; the lake, INT-19 and its extract are removed (DP-17) |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** The Helm chart with its three values files, the pipeline stage, the pre-deploy migration job, the Schedule registration and its idempotency assertion, the eight panels, the six alert rules, the five run-book entries and the SIT smoke profile.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_reporting`; never read another service's tables | none; the release asserts no cross-schema grant |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | none for the deployment; the library object is present and untouched |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none; the release asserts no ACE read path |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | none for the deployment; the lists are read at run time by the app |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | one Schedule registered; no Quartz row |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none; the smoke profile uses the fakes |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/reporting/v1` | none; the smoke profile uses the per-service base |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | the migration job, replayed from the app story |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting | none; the release asserts no lake egress (GAP-2566) |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | none for the deployment; the route is RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Chart and values | Deployment artefact | api and worker deployments, the login reference, probes, resources and thresholds per environment |
| Migration job | Pre-deploy job | Replays the per-service Flyway sequence, the three tables, their keys and the frozen-row trigger, and fails the release when the trigger is absent |
| Schedule registration | Provisioning step | Registers the 01:30 run once and refuses a second registration |
| Boundary assertion | Pipeline step | Fails a release that declares a topic, a consumer group, an event, a second Schedule or a lake path |
| Dashboard set | Observability artefact | The eight panels of AC4 |
| Alert rules | Observability artefact | The six rules of AC5, each with a values threshold and a catalogue owner |
| Run books | Operations artefact | The five entries below |
| Smoke profile | Test artefact | The SIT journey of AC6 through the composite route |

**Run-book entries.** (1) A publish is held for a stale product: read the gate answer and the product date, raise MSG-P1-001 to the data steward, and take no Workbench action on the ACE batch. (2) A rerun of the baseline date is refused: read the frozen date and MSG-P9-001, confirm the rows, and do not attempt a write around the trigger. (3) A run failed: read its failed step and message ID, fix the cause, rerun from SCR-44 and confirm the run record. (4) A measure was not published: read MSG-P9-003, confirm the definition version in force, and hand the row to the reference data administrator. (5) A read is slow or fails: check the composite route, then the service health, then the database session.

**Build steps**

1. Chart and values with the login reference, the probes and the pinned image digest; tests for AC1.
2. The pre-deploy migration job, the three tables, their keys and the frozen trigger, with the trigger assertion; a failed or missing trigger stops the release.
3. The Schedule registration and its idempotency assertion, including the refusal of a second Schedule and the absence of a Quartz row (AC3).
4. The boundary assertion of AC3, including the lake, the INT-19 extract, the trailer, the event and the consumer group.
5. The eight panels of AC4 and the six alert rules of AC5, each threshold from the values file and each owner from the catalogue.
6. The five run-book entries with their message IDs, first checks and escalation.
7. The SIT smoke profile through the composite route, with the refused rerun and the forced record failure (AC6).
8. The alert rehearsal: one synthetic metric per rule, with its owner and its channel recorded.

**Done when.** The chart renders in the three environments, the migration creates the three tables and the trigger and is idempotent, exactly one Schedule exists and a second is refused, the boundary assertion passes on the release and fails on a deliberate breach, the eight panels carry data for a synthetic business date, each of the six alerts fires in the rehearsal, and the smoke profile proves the refused rerun with the frozen rows unchanged and the absent lake.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P9-001 | A rerun of the baseline date is refused, and the panel and the run book show it | The baseline for {date} is frozen. It cannot be published again. |
| MSG-P9-003 | A measure listed for a run has no definition in force | {measure} has no approved definition. It is not published. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The gate answer for a business date is HOLD and a run waits | {product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A publish stays held with its reason | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The run record cannot be written and the run changes nothing | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A definition row is invalid and the load is refused | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role lacks Reporting R or Reference data C | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story and FSD P9; no threshold, channel or owner name is written here. The alert thresholds and the channel names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2574; ASM-4240) and are values-file entries; the 15-minute target of a failed run comes from NFR-068.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the chart or the code: the measure codes, the formulas, the units, the baseline date, job names, cadences, expected durations, alert minutes, owners and thresholds are rows of the catalogue, of the definitions or of the values files.
- No personal data in a panel, a log line, a trace or a run book: identifiers, codes, dates, counts and durations only.
- One login for the service and no ACE credential; no grant on another `rwb_*` schema and no `v_ace_*` grant (DP-01, DP-02, DP-05).
- No release adds a lake path, an INT-19 extract, a trailer or an outbound batch (DP-17).
- Exactly one Schedule for the run, no Quartz row and no shared job table; a second registration is refused (DP-10).
- No topic, consumer group or event is declared by this release; the service topic stays as the platform provisioned it (DP-14).
- Every threshold, channel and owner is a values-file or catalogue entry, and the assertion of AC3 and AC5 fails a release that writes one in the chart.
- The frozen-row trigger is part of the release: a migration that creates the tables without it fails the release (BR2).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: integration slice of RWB-E1-013 for RWB-ITG-W1. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **QA integration engineer**, I want **the baseline measures of RWB-E1-013 proven end to end across rwb-case (P3), rwb-source-data (P1) and rwb-reporting (P9) on their published contracts — the synthetic case set and the ACE batch of business date 2026-11-27 seeded through rwb-case and rwb-source-data, the measure definition of version MD-2026.11 in force, the 01:30 JOB-15 run publishing the baseline, the baseline frozen, and the daily gate holding the publication when the ALS batch of that date is not COMPLETE**, so that **the cross-service criteria no single service can prove are signed off before wave 1 exits**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Measures are counted by hand at month end today and each team counts a case differently, so the baseline is only worth having if the chain that produces it is proven on the services that will run it. RWB-E1-013 owns REQ-RDF-012 and the frozen baseline of business date 2026-11-27.

This integration slice owns two of the eight legacy acceptance criteria: **AC2 Baseline published** and **AC6 Batch of the baseline date not complete**. The other six sit with the sibling app stories: **RWB-P9-E1013-APP** owns AC1 (the definition file of 6 rows and the version in force), AC4 (a definition without a formula refused in full), AC5 (the baseline published twice), AC7 (the publish held when the delivery path does not answer) and AC8 (a measure with no definition in force); **RWB-P3-E1013-APP** owns the case-fact side the baseline is counted from — route, stage, queue, entry date and stage clock start of the 120 synthetic cases; **RWB-P1-E1013-APP** owns the ACE view contract, the payments since entry and the freshness and gate side that AC2 and AC6 read through. **RWB-P3-E1018-APP** is the case creation of JOB-02 that fills the synthetic set.

None of the two owned criteria can be signed off inside one service. AC2 needs a case set that rwb-case created, a COMPLETED ALS row that rwb-source-data reads from the ACE views, a definition that rwb-reporting holds in force, a 01:30 run that reads the case facts through the P3 contract and the payments through the P1 contract, and a snapshot that is written once and frozen. AC6 needs the same chain with the gate answering HOLD, no baseline row written and the run record naming the stale product and date. A fake proves the arithmetic of a calculator; it cannot prove that a case created through rwb-case reaches a measure through two contracts, or that a missing ACE batch stops the publication.

The target changes the last hop only. **DP-17 removes the data lake**: there is no INT-19 extract to a lake. rwb-reporting projects the facts from its events and from the P1 snapshot activity and publishes on `rwb.reporting.events.v1` with ReportPublished, and **rwb-integration delivers the regulatory extract**. The measure values, the definition version, the baseline date and the gate are unchanged; the suite therefore asserts the same AC2 and AC6 values and the v5 publication path in place of the lake step (GAP-0339; ASM-0433).

Service contracts are not faked in this story. Every call and every event is made to the real service, on the real base and the real topic, in SIT; the only fakes are the ACE batch fixture and the Airflow trigger that stands in for the bank scheduler.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P3-E1018-APP is done: case creation writes the case record and the case facts of JOB-02 through the rwb-case path, and `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases` answers them.
- RWB-P9-E1013-APP is done: measure_definition, measure_snapshot, the definition load, the measures Schedule, the publication on `rwb.reporting.events.v1` and `GET /api/recovery/reporting/v1/reports/measures` exist in rwb_reporting.
- RWB-P3-E1013-APP is done: the case facts of route, stage, queue, entry date and stage clock start are served on the P3 contract for a business date.
- RWB-P1-E1013-APP is done: the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views, the ACE batch record, the payments since entry, the freshness and the readiness trigger are served by rwb-source-data.
- Each owner has published its contract: the OpenAPI document of P1, P3 and P9 and the AsyncAPI document of the three consumed topics.
- The harness **RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG** is available and its synthetic data set is loaded: the 120 open cases of business date 2026-11-27 with 60 Mortgage, 45 Hire purchase and 15 SSME, the payments since entry that total 4,350,000.00 THB, and the ACE batch rows of the fixture dates.
- SIT is in place: namespace `rwb-recovery`, the task queues `rwb-case`, `rwb-source-data` and `rwb-reporting`, the topics `rwb.source-data.events.v1`, `rwb.case.events.v1` and `rwb.reporting.events.v1` with their retry and `.dlt` topics, and the schema registry with BACKWARD compatibility.
- The six definitions of version MD-2026.11 are approved and can be loaded through the P9 path; the baseline date is configured on rwb-reporting as 2026-11-27.
- No production data and no production namespace: the suite runs on synthetic data in SIT only.
- Release 30 November 2026 is tentative, and a date is never a blocker for this story.
- No build dependency: the story is Day 1 under Template and Rules §R5.7, and the four integration dependencies never block a build.
- The v5 publication path replaces the INT-19 lake step; the exact composition of the fixture files is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0339; ASM-0433).

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: runs the preflight of section 13 — the four services answer their health and contract check, the three topics and their retry and `.dlt` topics exist, the schema registry holds the three event versions, the three task queues are registered in `rwb-recovery`, and the JOB-15 Schedule is present; a missing element stops the run before any test.
2. Harness: seeds the synthetic case set of business date 2026-11-27 through the rwb-case creation path, and seeds the ACE batch rows of the fixture dates through the W1J01 ACE batch fixture, so that the batch record answers a COMPLETED ALS row for 2026-11-27.
3. Harness: loads the measure definition of version MD-2026.11 with the 6 rows through the P9 measure-definition path published by RWB-P9-E1013-APP, and reads the version in force back through `GET /api/recovery/reporting/v1/reports/measures`.
4. Harness: triggers the readiness signal with `POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/business-days/2026-11-27/ready` through the Airflow trigger stub, and waits for one `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` on `rwb.source-data.events.v1`.
5. System: rwb-source-data publishes AceDataReady, rwb-case starts DailyCaseRun for JOB-02 and the cases of the date exist, and rwb-case publishes `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1` on `rwb.case.events.v1` which rwb-reporting projects.
6. Harness: asserts the daily gate and the case facts on the contracts only — `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness` for the gate and `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases` for the 120 cases of 2026-11-27, and never reads a service table.
7. Harness: triggers the JOB-15 measures run once for 01:30 on 2026-11-28 through the P9 run path, waits for the workflow to complete, and collects the `rwb.reporting.ReportPublished.v1` events of the run from `rwb.reporting.events.v1`.
8. Harness: asserts AC2 through `GET /api/recovery/reporting/v1/reports/measures` — the rows of business date 2026-11-27 carry definition version MD-2026.11, the baseline flag and the frozen flag; CASES_BY_ROUTE is 120 cases of which 60 are Mortgage; REALIZED_RECOVERY equals the synthetic payments since entry of 4,350,000.00 THB, read through `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/payments?accountId={accountId}` and summed by the harness.
9. Harness: asserts AC6 on a second synthetic set with no COMPLETED ALS row for business date 2026-11-27 — the gate answers HOLD, the run writes no baseline row for the date, the run record carries MSG-P1-001 naming "DP03 Case" and 2026-11-26, and the baseline appears at the first JOB-15 run after the ALS batch of 2026-11-27 is COMPLETED.
10. Harness: writes the evidence report of AC2 and AC6 with the payload references, the measure values and the run identifiers, resets the synthetic set to its fixture state for a repeatable rerun, and publishes the evidence to the wave 1 exit gate.

The suite never writes another service's table and never calls another service through a service: every assertion is made on a contract response or on an event, and every write it needs is a call to the owner's own path.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A published contract of P1, P3 or P9 differs from the version the suite was built against (contract drift) | The preflight fails on the contract check, the suite names the service, the operation and the differing element, and no test runs | None | AC2, AC6 |
| X2 | No `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` arrives after the readiness call | The harness waits out the configured window, records the missing event and fails; DailyCaseRun is not started and the case facts of the date are absent | None | AC2, AC6 |
| X3 | No measure definition is in force for a measure of the configuration | rwb-reporting publishes no value for that measure and lists it in the run record | MSG-P9-003 | AC2 |
| X4 | JOB-15 runs a second time for business date 2026-11-27 | The frozen baseline rows are unchanged and the run record shows the refusal naming 2026-11-27 | MSG-P9-001 | AC2 |
| X5 | The daily gate answers HOLD because the ALS batch of the business date is not COMPLETE | No baseline row is written for the date, the run record names the stale product and date, and the baseline is published by the first run after the batch is COMPLETED | MSG-P1-001 | AC6 |
| X6 | A consumed event lands on the `.dlt` topic | The harness names the event id, the topic and the failure, and fails the criterion that expected the event | None | AC2 |
| X7 | A fixture of the synthetic data set is missing or not idempotent | The preflight stops the run before any test and names the missing fixture file; the suite is never run on a partial set | None | AC2, AC6 |
| X8 | The suite looks for an INT-19 data-lake assertion or a Power BI refresh | The step does not exist: the suite asserts the v5 path instead — ReportPublished on `rwb.reporting.events.v1` and the regulatory extract delivered through rwb-integration | None | AC6 (GAP-0339; ASM-0433) |

X1 to X7 are the failure modes of the chain the two owned criteria assert. X8 is the record that the legacy lake step is not part of the wave 1 suite (DP-17).

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | A test project of its own; it needs the four integration services, the three topics and the Schedule, and it owns no schema, no table and no operation |
| Negotiable | Fixture size, wait windows, retry counts and report layout are configuration; the measure values, the definition version, the baseline date, the message IDs and the run order are fixed by the legacy story |
| Valuable | Proves across services what no single service story can prove: a baseline published once and frozen, and a gate that stops the publication |
| Estimable | One suite, two feature files, four fixture groups, two runs (published, held) and one evidence report |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the report |
| Testable | Every criterion is asserted on an observable: a contract response, an event, a run record or a measure value |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Baseline measures, proven across rwb-case, rwb-source-data and rwb-reporting

  Background:
    Given the synthetic case set for business date 2026-11-27 holds 120 open cases: 60 Mortgage, 45 Hire purchase and 15 SSME
    Given age bands are "0-90", "91-180", "181-365", "366-730" and "over 730" days since entry
    Given all wave 1 services are deployed in SIT with their published contracts
    Given the synthetic data set of the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG is loaded

  Scenario: AC2 Baseline published (legacy RWB-E1-013 AC2)
    Given v_ace_batch_status holds a COMPLETED ALS row for business date 2026-11-27
    When JOB-15 runs at 01:30 on 2026-11-28
    Then measure_snapshot holds rows for business date 2026-11-27 marked baseline and frozen with definition version "MD-2026.11"
    Then "CASES_BY_ROUTE" totals 120 cases, of which 60 are Mortgage
    Then "REALIZED_RECOVERY" equals the sum of synthetic payments since entry, 4,350,000.00 THB

  Scenario: AC6 Batch of the baseline date not complete (legacy RWB-E1-013 AC6)
    Given v_ace_batch_status holds no COMPLETED ALS row for business date 2026-11-27
    When JOB-15 runs at 01:30 on 2026-11-28
    Then the system writes no baseline rows for 2026-11-27
    Then the run record shows MSG-P1-001 naming "DP03 Case" and 2026-11-26
    Then the system publishes the baseline by the first JOB-15 run after the ALS batch for 2026-11-27 is COMPLETED
```

**Target reading.** The views named in the criteria (`v_ace_batch_status`) are read only by rwb-source-data, and the suite asserts them through the P1 contract of RWB-P1-E1013-APP, never by a query of its own. `measure_snapshot` is asserted through `GET /api/recovery/reporting/v1/reports/measures` on the P9 contract of RWB-P9-E1013-APP. The legacy INT-19 step of the data lake is replaced: rwb-reporting publishes on `rwb.reporting.events.v1` and rwb-integration delivers the regulatory extract (GAP-0339; ASM-0433). The measure values, the definition version, the baseline date and the gate are copied unchanged from RWB-E1-013.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Each measure is published only under a definition in force that names its data product, formula, unit and approver | RWB-E1-013 BR1; REQ-RDF-012; Principle 1 |
| BR2 | The baseline is the snapshot of the configured baseline business date and is frozen once written | RWB-E1-013 BR2; REQ-RDF-012; FEAT-RPT-01 |
| BR3 | Measures are computed from Workbench records read through the owning modules, never from a separate count | RWB-E1-013 BR3; NFR-065 |
| BR4 | A measure is computed only from a COMPLETED ACE batch; stale data is not published as the baseline | RWB-E1-013 BR4; CTL-02; MSG-P1-001 rule |
| BR5 | The extract to the data lake holds the publish and alerts on failure, and runs again in the next window | RWB-E1-013 BR5; INT-19 error handling |
| BR6 | Age bands are a reference list | RWB-E1-013 BR6; Principle 1 |
| BR7 | A definition load with any invalid row is refused in full | RWB-E1-013 BR7; refdata.txt change process, step 3 |
| BR8 | The suite reads and writes no schema of its own and never reads another service's tables: every assertion is made on a contract response or an event, and every write it needs is a call to the owner's own path | DP-01, DP-05, DP-11 |
| BR9 | Every call is one hop to the owning service on its own base, with a 2 s client budget; a call that exceeds it fails the criterion and is reported | DP-11, DP-13 |
| BR10 | One event type per owner topic in the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, keyed caseId, carrying IDs and facts only and no personal data field | ADR-015; Arch v5 slide 42 and slide 43 notes |
| BR11 | The suite runs on synthetic data in SIT only and never points at production data or a production namespace | ADR-018; this story |
| BR12 | No business value in the test code: the measure codes, the definition version, the baseline date, the age bands and the expected totals come from the legacy acceptance criteria and the fixture files | RWB-E1-013 section 17; this story |

BR5 is read with BR10 of RWB-P9-E1013-APP and with DP-17: the publish and the hold stay, the destination is the v5 path — rwb-reporting publishes ReportPublished and rwb-integration delivers the regulatory extract — and no lake assertion is part of the wave 1 suite (GAP-0339; ASM-0433).

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It sets the baseline flag and the frozen flag on measure_snapshot rows, and the JOB-15 run status (running, complete, failed, held).

The states the suite observes on the services:

| Item | States |
|---|---|
| Measure run (JOB-15) | Scheduled; Running; Complete; Failed; Held |
| `measure_snapshot` baseline flag | Not baseline; baseline, set once for the configured baseline business date |
| `measure_snapshot` frozen flag | Not frozen; frozen, never changed after the baseline write |
| Daily gate | COMPLETE; HOLD when no COMPLETED ALS row exists for the business date |
| Case set of the business date | Created through JOB-02 for the date, or absent |
| Harness run | Not started; running; passed; failed with the failing criterion and the service named |

The suite observes these states and drives none of them; a state it cannot reach is a failed criterion, not a skipped one.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| QA integration engineer | Owns the suite, the fixtures, the run order and the evidence report; runs it in SIT only |
| Service owner of rwb-case (P3) | Owns the case creation, the case facts and their contract the suite calls |
| Service owner of rwb-source-data (P1) | Owns the ACE views, the readiness trigger, the freshness and gate, the payments and the reconciliation |
| Service owner of rwb-reporting (P9) | Owns the measure definition, the snapshot, the baseline and frozen flags, the measures Schedule, the publication and the extract |
| Data steward | Reads the run record, the freshness and the published measures; confirms the definition version in force |
| Platform administrator | May rerun JOB-15 and read the run record; owns the SIT namespace, the queues and the topics |
| Reporting and BI analyst | Reads the published baseline; does not run the suite and changes no definition |
| Operations | Receives the alert of a failed or held run |
| No role | May read a service table, edit a published measure or change a frozen row |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary and are copied from RWB-E1-013. Every element above is synthetic for this suite: 120 synthetic cases of business date 2026-11-27, synthetic payments since entry totalling 4,350,000.00 THB, a synthetic ACE batch row, and the definition rows of version MD-2026.11 approved as TRB-0001. ##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The suite provides no REST operation. P2 rwb-integration's reserved names `/api/recovery/integration/v1`, `rwb.integration.events.v1`, `rwb-integration` and `rwb_integration` are not used, and the suite writes no rwb_integration table.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/business-days/{date}/ready` | P1 rwb-source-data | Airflow-style readiness trigger for the business date, 2 s budget |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness` | P1 rwb-source-data | Daily gate for the business date, 2 s budget |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/payments?accountId={accountId}` | P1 rwb-source-data | Realized recovery of the synthetic set for wave 1, 2 s budget |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases` | P3 rwb-case | Case facts of the synthetic set for the business date, 2 s budget |
| GET | `/api/recovery/reporting/v1/reports/measures` | P9 rwb-reporting | Published measures, baseline and frozen flags, definition version, 2 s budget |

Every call is one hop to the owning service on its own base (DP-11, DP-13) with the 2 s client budget. The suite never calls a service through another service and never reads a view or a table of its own.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The suite publishes no event. Every event asserted in this story is produced by a service and is listed in 12.4.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` | `rwb.source-data.events.v1` | P1 rwb-source-data | Starts DailyCaseRun in rwb-case (JOB-02); the suite waits for it after the readiness call |
| `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1` | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 rwb-case | Projected into rwb-reporting; the suite counts the cases of the business date |
| `rwb.reporting.ReportPublished.v1` | `rwb.reporting.events.v1` | P9 rwb-reporting | Marks the extract ready for rwb-integration; the suite takes it as the evidence that the run published |

All three are consumed in the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, keyed caseId, with the inbox dedupe of the consumer and the retry and `.dlt` topics of the owner (ADR-015; Arch v5 slides 42 and 43). The suite asserts on IDs and facts only and writes no payload of its own.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| CaseWorkflow | Workflow | `rwb-case` | Parent per case; the suite observes the case record and the facts it carries |
| DailyCaseRun | Workflow, started by Schedule and by AceDataReady | `rwb-case` | Runs JOB-02 case creation for the business date; the suite waits for its result through the case read |
| listEligibleAccounts | Activity | `rwb-source-data` | Accounts eligible for the business date, the input of the case set |
| snapshot(page) | Activity | `rwb-source-data` | Paged snapshot of the facts rwb-reporting measures from |
| buildRegulatoryExtract | Activity | `rwb-reporting` | Builds the regulatory extract that rwb-integration delivers |

All five are registered by the owning services (RWB-P3-E1013-APP, RWB-P3-E1018-APP, RWB-P1-E1013-APP, RWB-P9-E1013-APP); this story drives them through their own triggers and reads their result on a contract, and it adds no workflow of its own.

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Schedule | Cadence | Registration | Legacy reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| JOB-15 measures | Daily at 01:30, Airflow trigger, no data lake | Registered by the rwb-reporting release and triggered once by the harness through the P9 run path with the same input the cadence uses | JOB-15 Reporting extract |
| JOB-02 case creation | Airflow: ACE data ready | AceDataReady starts DailyCaseRun in rwb-case; the harness drives it with the readiness call | JOB-02 Case creation |
| JOB-04 reconciliation | Airflow: ACE data ready | Event-started workflow in rwb-source-data; the harness observes its freshness result | JOB-04 Reconciliation |

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The suite owns no table and never reads another service's schema (DP-01). The tables it exercises belong to `rwb_case`, `rwb_source_data` and `rwb_reporting` and are listed in section 11 with their owners.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

External stubs only, and no service contract fake:

| Stub | Stands in for | Note |
|---|---|---|
| ACE batch fixture (W1J01) | The ACE batch record the views read | Synthetic rows only, including the COMPLETED ALS row of 2026-11-27 and its absence for the held run |
| Airflow trigger stub | The bank scheduler | Calls `POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/business-days/{date}/ready` and the P9 run path; it holds no business rule |
| Azurite Blob | The regulatory extract storage | Receives the extract delivered through rwb-integration; the suite asserts the delivery, not a lake |

The three services, their topics, their queues and their Schedules are real. No contract of P1, P3 or P9 is faked.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Provided | Consumed | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 | 5 | Readiness trigger, freshness and gate, payments, case facts, published measures; one hop, 2 s (DP-11, DP-13) |
| Kafka | 0 published | 3 event types | AceDataReady, CaseCreated, ReportPublished on the three owner topics, key caseId |
| Temporal | None | 2 workflows, 3 activities | CaseWorkflow, DailyCaseRun; listEligibleAccounts, snapshot(page), buildRegulatoryExtract |
| File | None | 1 | The regulatory extract delivered through rwb-integration |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** One JUnit and Testcontainers suite in the W1J01 harness, `integration/recovery-w1/baseline-measures`, with the two feature files of section 7, the four fixture groups below, the evidence report writer and the wave-gate publisher. The suite reuses the W1J01 environment, topic and queue helpers rather than a second harness. No service code and no schema change is part of this story.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| SuiteRunner | Runner | Reads the environment, runs the preflight, orders the two runs, writes the report and the exit code |
| Preflight | Component | Checks the four services, the three topics with retry and `.dlt`, the schema registry versions, the three task queues and the JOB-15 Schedule |
| CaseSetSeeder | Component | Seeds the 120 synthetic cases of 2026-11-27 through the rwb-case creation path and the P1 readiness trigger, and asserts the case facts on the P3 contract |
| MeasureDefinitionSeeder | Component | Loads the 6 rows of version MD-2026.11 through the P9 path published by RWB-P9-E1013-APP and reads the version in force back |
| GateProbe | Component | Calls the freshness and gate operation and asserts COMPLETE for the published run and HOLD for the held run |
| MeasuresProbe | Component | Reads the published measures, the baseline and frozen flags and the definition version on the P9 contract |
| PaymentsProbe | Component | Reads the payments of the synthetic set on the P1 contract and sums them for the REALIZED_RECOVERY comparison |
| EventProbe | Component | Consumes the three owner topics and asserts one event per fact, the key, the envelope and the move to `.dlt` on failure |
| ReportWriter | Component | One row per criterion and per test case, with the evidence references |
| GatePublisher | Component | Publishes the evidence report to the wave 1 exit gate |

**Database.** None of its own. The suite reads nothing directly: every value is taken from a contract response or an event, and every write is a call to the owner's own path.

**Configuration and reference data**

- The service list, the five operations, the three topics with their retry and `.dlt` topics, the three task queues and the namespace `rwb-recovery`, all as configuration.
- The measure codes of the six definitions, the definition version MD-2026.11, the baseline business date 2026-11-27 and the age bands, read from the legacy criteria and the fixture files.
- The fixture dates: the baseline date 2026-11-27, the run date 2026-11-28, the held-run date and its first successful run after the batch.
- The 2 s client budget, the wait windows and the retry counts, as configuration.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting | none; gap if the story needs lake data |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

This ITG story adds no build dependency: the H dependencies of DP-03, DP-07, DP-10, DP-15 and DP-19 stay with the service, platform and operations stories whose behaviour the suite proves, and the I list names the four services it exercises without ever blocking a build (Template and Rules §R5.4 and §R5.7). The DP-17 gap is GAP-0339.

**Fixtures**

| Fixture | Content | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| Synthetic case set | 120 open cases of business date 2026-11-27: 60 Mortgage, 45 Hire purchase and 15 SSME, with route, stage, queue, entry date and stage clock start | AC2, AC6, TC-E1-013-02-ITG, TC-E1-013-06-ITG |
| ACE batch fixture | The COMPLETED ALS row of 2026-11-27 for the published run, and its absence for the held run | AC2, AC6 |
| Payments fixture | The synthetic payments since entry totalling 4,350,000.00 THB | AC2 |
| Measure definition fixture | The 6 rows of version MD-2026.11 approved as TRB-0001 | AC2, AC6 |
| Held-run set | The 2026-11-27 set with no COMPLETED ALS row, and the same set after the batch is COMPLETED | AC6 |
| Environment config | Services, operations, topics, queues, schedules and wait windows | All |

**Build steps**

1. Add the suite to the W1J01 harness and read the environment configuration, reusing its topic, queue and report helpers.
2. Write the preflight: the four services, the five operations, the three topics with retry and `.dlt`, the schema versions and the JOB-15 Schedule.
3. Write the case-set seeder and the readiness call, and assert the case facts of 2026-11-27 on the P3 contract.
4. Write the measure-definition seeder through the P9 path and assert version MD-2026.11 in force.
5. Write the gate and payments probes, and the REALIZED_RECOVERY comparison against the synthetic sum.
6. Write the measures probe and the AC2 assertions: roll-up of 120 cases with 60 Mortgage, baseline and frozen flags, definition version.
7. Write the AC6 run: gate HOLD, no baseline row, MSG-P1-001 on the run record, publication at the first run after the batch.
8. Write the report writer, the repeatable reset of the synthetic set and the wave-gate publisher; run the suite twice to prove the fixture is idempotent.

**Done when.** The nine test cases of section 16 pass with their `-ITG` copies on the real services in SIT, AC2 shows the 120 cases with 60 Mortgage and REALIZED_RECOVERY of 4,350,000.00 THB with the baseline and frozen flags set at version MD-2026.11, AC6 shows no baseline row, the HOLD gate and MSG-P1-001 naming "DP03 Case" and 2026-11-26, and the evidence report is published to the wave 1 exit gate.

No screen is written by this story and the suite renders nothing: the five operations are called directly and are the only reader surface it uses. The states the suite observes on the services are the measure-run, flag, gate and harness states of section 9.

##### 17. Guardrails

- Synthetic data only: the 120 cases of 2026-11-27, the synthetic payments of 4,350,000.00 THB and the ACE batch fixture; no production data and no production namespace.
- No personal data in events, logs or fixtures: case IDs, codes, counts and amounts only, and no field marked personal in sys_fields.
- No cross-service table read: every assertion is a contract response or an event, and every write is a call to the owner's own path (DP-01, DP-05).
- No business value in the test code: the measure codes, the definition version, the baseline date, the age bands and the expected totals come from the legacy acceptance criteria and the fixture files (BR12).
- CloudEvents 1.0 on the owner topics, key caseId, IDs and facts only, with the registry's BACKWARD compatibility and the inbox dedupe of the consumer (ADR-015, BR10).
- One hop and a 2 s budget on every call; a service is never called through another service and a timeout fails the criterion instead of being retried into a pass (DP-11, BR9).
- No production access of any kind; the suite refuses an environment that is not SIT.
- Clean-up and idempotent fixtures: the synthetic set is reset to its fixture state after a run, and a second run on the same set gives the same result.
- The lake assertion stays out: the suite asserts the v5 publication and the rwb-integration delivery, and it fails if a lake step is added back (DP-17, GAP-0339).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-015 for rwb-source-data. The freshness capability publishes a contract for the first time: three operations on `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`, the typed interfaces `FreshnessQuery` and `DailyCompletenessGate`, the two events `AceDataReady` and `AceDataLate` on `rwb.source-data.events.v1` under a CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, the `AceIngestCheckWorkflow` activity contract and the one cut-off Schedule per data product (DP-09, DP-10, DP-11, DP-14). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of rwb-source-data for freshness: an OpenAPI 3.1 document for `GET /data-products/freshness`, `GET /freshness` and `POST /business-days/{date}/ready`, the typed `FreshnessQuery` and `DailyCompletenessGate` interfaces in a contract jar, an AsyncAPI 3 document for `AceDataReady` and `AceDataLate` under a CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, the `AceIngestCheckWorkflow` activity contract, the declaration of one cut-off Schedule per data product, the nine contract tables of section 12 and the contract fakes for rwb-decision, rwb-case and the platform**, so that **rwb-case, rwb-payment, rwb-deviation, rwb-writeoff, rwb-decision, the alerts and the gateway-bff banner build against a fixed, testable contract on Day 1 without waiting for the freshness code to be written**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST and one hop with a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020), and the freshness capability is the one read that four services and one screen depend on before anything else can run: rwb-case starts `DailyCaseRun` on `AceDataReady`, rwb-payment starts payment matching on the same event, rwb-deviation and rwb-writeoff follow it, rwb-decision writes the freshness of every input into its own snapshot, and the stale banner reaches gateway-bff on `AceDataLate` (Arch v5 slide 43, rows 26 and 27). If the shapes, the envelope and the activity contract are agreed once and faked, the app, operations and test stories of this legacy key, and the four consuming services, build in parallel; a change in any of them is caught in a contract test rather than in an integration window.

The baseline also fixes the naming the checks enforce: schema `rwb_source_data`, REST base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`, topic `rwb.source-data.events.v1`, event names `rwb.source-data.<Event>.v1`, task queue `rwb-source-data` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.sourcedata` (DP-13, DP-14; Arch v5 slides 29, 41 and 43).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the document, topic and event names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- The outbox, inbox and idempotency library is available as a reference for the table names and the envelope (RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, DP-09).
- The workflow kit is available, with its Schedule registration and its typed activity contract convention (RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, DP-10).
- The platform RFC 9457 problem body and the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope are the platform baseline; where this document narrows them it does so explicitly.
- The operations and their owners are taken from the Ownership Map only; rwb-source-data never documents an operation owned by another service.
- The event payload and the envelope attributes are fixed by GAP-0493 with ASM-0685; the Schedule names and per-product cut-offs by GAP-0494 with ASM-0686; the source/load time mapping by GAP-0492 with ASM-0684.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 document for the three operations with the shared components, the security scheme and the error responses of every code.
2. Draft the typed interfaces `FreshnessQuery` and `DailyCompletenessGate` and the `FreshnessStamp` record in the contract jar, with their nullability and their timeout budget.
3. Draft the AsyncAPI 3 document for `rwb.source-data.events.v1`: the two event types, the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope and the seven payload fields.
4. Draft the `AceIngestCheckWorkflow` contract: the input schema, the mode, the workflow ID rule and the five activity inputs and outputs.
5. Declare the one cut-off Schedule per source-fed data product, with its cadence source, its overlap policy and its catch-up window.
6. State the versioning rule for the REST surface, the event schemas and the activity contract.
7. Publish the nine contract tables of section 12 and the six fakes.
8. Add the contract tests: schema validation, envelope validation, error mapping, idempotency replay on the Airflow signal and drift between a fake and the document.
9. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-P1-E1015-APP, RWB-P1-E1015-OPS and every consuming service.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A response body fails schema validation | 400 with the problem body and the failing pointer | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |
| X2 | A caller asks for a major version the service does not serve | 404 with the problem body and the served major versions | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |
| X3 | An interface signature changes without a new major version | The contract test fails and the merge is blocked | None (pipeline log) | AC2 |
| X4 | A consumer cannot deserialise an event | The registry validation fails the build; the event schema is not published | None (pipeline log) | AC3 |
| X5 | A declared Schedule has no data source for its cadence | The registration check fails the build, because a cadence in code would be a business value there | None (pipeline log) | AC4 |
| X6 | A contract fake drifts from the document | The contract test fails and the merge is blocked | None (pipeline log) | AC5 |
| X7 | A field-level definition is missing from the source material | The field is marked with the placeholder and the row of section 12 carries it | None | AC6 |
| X8 | The Airflow signal is replayed with the same business date | The stored answer is returned; no second gate run and no second event | None | AC1 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the workflow kit and the Ownership Map only |
| Negotiable | Field-level detail of the payload and the response bodies is settled with the consumers; the named operations, events, interfaces and rules are fixed by the target architecture |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app, operations and test stories of this legacy key on Day 1, and the four consuming services and rwb-decision |
| Estimable | Two documents, one contract jar, one AsyncAPI file, one workflow contract, nine contract tables, six fakes and six contract tests |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One REST base per service: `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`; a document never declares another service's path | DP-13; Arch v5 slide 41 notes |
| BR2 | Event names are `rwb.<short>.<Event>.v1` on the topic `rwb.<short>.events.v1`, with retry and `.dlt` topics | DP-14; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR3 | Every event carries the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, is keyed by the source system and the business date, and carries no personal data | Arch v5 slides 42 and 43 notes; DP-09 |
| BR4 | Every POST declares the Idempotency-Key header and stores its response | Arch v5 slide 11; DP-09 |
| BR5 | Error responses use one envelope and one message ID per condition; business message texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story | Arch v5 platform baseline; Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR6 | A schema change is additive within a major version; a breaking change is a new major version, for the REST surface, the events and the activity contract | Arch v5 slide 11 notes |
| BR7 | The document lists only operations owned by rwb-source-data; a consumed path is described as consumed, never as provided | Ownership Map v1 |
| BR8 | No business value is fixed in the contract: the expected-by times, the refresh cycles and the product-to-source map stay data rows, and a cadence is never a literal | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17; DP-10 |

| From | Event | Condition | To |

| In review | Consumer sign-off | The app, operations and test stories, rwb-case, rwb-payment, rwb-deviation, rwb-writeoff and rwb-decision accept the baseline and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A field is added within major version 1 | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A field or an activity signature is removed, renamed or retyped | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |

The per-service login name behind the document's security scheme is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0493; ASM-0685); the document names it "the rwb_source_data login (DP-02)".

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Freshness stamp resource | `productCode`, `productName`, `businessDate`, `sourceExtractedAt`, `loadedAt`, `status` (LOADED or STALE), `staleSince`, taken from `data_product_load` fields DF-OPS-001 to DF-OPS-009 and `data_product` fields DF-REF-071 to DF-REF-078 |
| ACE batch resource | `sourceSystem`, `businessDate`, `startedAt`, `completedAt`, `status`, `recordCount`, `feedVersion`, `isComplete`, `ageDays`, from `v_ace_batch_status` fields DF-ACE-178 to DF-ACE-186 |
| Gate result | `businessDate`, the result COMPLETE or HOLD, the product and source that hold it, and the time read |
| Event payloads | `eventId`, `occurredAt`, `schemaVersion`, `sourceSystem`, `businessDate`, `status`, `completedAt`; no name, address, identity number or contact point |
| Workflow inputs | `sourceSystem`, `businessDate`, `observedStatus`, `mode`; no personal data and no ACE fact beyond those four |

The exact JSON field names of the two freshness responses and the detail texts of the problem body are fixed here and confirmed with the consumers; the source/load time mapping behind `sourceExtractedAt` and `loadedAt` is the one ruled in GAP-0492 with ASM-0684, and the envelope attributes by GAP-0493 with ASM-0685.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-source-data (P1); base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/data-products/freshness` | `DataProductFreshness[]`; query product (DP01 to DP14, optional) and asOf (optional) | Case record R |
| GET | `/freshness` | The architecture alias: query businessDate; answers the ACE batch rows with `sourceSystem`, `businessDate`, `startedAt`, `completedAt`, `status`, `recordCount`, `feedVersion`, `isComplete` and `ageDays` | Case record R |
| POST | `/business-days/{date}/ready` | The Airflow signal of Arch v5 slide 15: no body, Idempotency-Key required, answers the gate result COMPLETE or HOLD with product and source | Server to server, workload identity |

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | Role, scope and right check before a stamp is returned, faked |

No other operation is consumed at run time: ACE is read through the views, not over REST (DP-05).

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Schema |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` (EV-26) | `rwb.source-data.events.v1` | P1 | eventId, occurredAt, schemaVersion, sourceSystem, businessDate, status, completedAt; CloudEvents 1.0 envelope |
| `rwb.source-data.AceDataLate.v1` (EV-27) | `rwb.source-data.events.v1` | P1 | The same seven fields, with the status of the latest batch row |

Consumers of AceDataReady are rwb-case, rwb-payment, rwb-deviation and rwb-writeoff; consumers of AceDataLate are the alerts and the gateway-bff banner (Arch v5 slide 43, rows 26 and 27). `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` is the shared ledger event of the library and is not published by this capability (DP-03).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Consumer contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | None | None | The capability polls `v_ace_batch_status`; the architecture's IN line states that Airflow calls the ready signal and that the fallback polls the ACE batch record (Arch v5 slide 15) |

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| AceIngestCheckWorkflow | Workflow, one run per source system and business date, workflow ID from both | `rwb-source-data` | Input schema sourceSystem, businessDate, observedStatus, mode; the signal and query surface |
| stampProducts, markStale | Activities | `rwb-source-data` | Product-to-source map and batch row in; stamps and one outbox row out |
| publishAceDataReady, publishAceDataLate | Activities (event library) | `rwb-source-data` | The envelope and the payload of 12.3 |
| checkDailyCompleteness | Activity | `rwb-source-data` | Business date and products in; COMPLETE, or HOLD with product and source out |

The two published interfaces travel with the workflow contract in the same jar: `FreshnessQuery` (`stampFor`, `stampForRow`, `stampsFor`) and `DailyCompletenessGate` (`check`).

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Schedule | Cadence | Documented fields | Legacy reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| One cut-off check per source-fed data product (DP01, DP02, DP05, DP06, DP07, DP11, DP13) | At `data_product.expected_by` in Asia/Bangkok: 08:00 daily, MON 08:00 weekly, as data rows | Schedule ID, the product code, the overlap policy SKIP, the catch-up window, the mode input | The legacy Quartz trigger per product |

The Schedule names and the per-product expected-by values beyond 08:00 and MON 08:00 are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0494; ASM-0686); the contract fixes one Schedule per product and that the cadence is read from the data row.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| data_product_load | P1 (rwb_source_data) | The freshness stamp resource of 12.1 and of the two events |
| data_product | P1 (rwb_source_data) | The product name, refresh cycle and expected-by behind the stamp and the Schedules |
| outbox_event, processed_event | PLT library, created in rwb_source_data | The outbox of the two events and the inbox of the listener (DP-09) |
| decision_log_entry | P7 (rwb_decision) | **Named as P7's and never read**; the inputs snapshot reaches this capability only through `FreshnessQuery` (DP-01, DP-03) |
