The deployment topology detail (cluster names, node pools, replica counts, resource sizes, zone spread, ingress class, the exact probe timings and the KEDA thresholds) is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0490; ASM-0682); the chart exposes them as values and this story fixes only their names and the rule that they are not hard-coded.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

The deployment exposes the two retention-run operations of the contract baseline behind the service's own route: `POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/retention-runs` and `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/retention-runs/{runId}`. Owner rwb-source-data (P1). The probes are cluster-internal and are not part of the API surface.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Interface | Path | Owner | Deployment need |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CaseHoldQuery` | Published interface, no REST path | P3 rwb-case | The legal-hold answer at run time; one hop, 2 s budget (DP-11) |
| Container put and get | The write-once container of RWB-PLT-TE012-APP under `retention/` | RWB-PLT-TE012-APP | The archive and its manifest, and the read-back check |
| Reference-data client library | `/api/recovery/case/v1` reference data | P3 rwb-case | The values a rule set may use; loaded at start-up (DP-07) |

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The topic `rwb.source-data.events.v1` is provisioned for the service by the platform for its other events (`AceDataReady`, `AceDataLate`, owned by RWB-P1-E1013-APP); this release publishes no message for the retention action and creates no topic of its own.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The retention run is started by the rwb-document Schedule through the contract call, so no consumer group and no retry topic is created for this capability.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Deployment element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `RetentionRunWorkflow` | Workflow, one run per run date and rule version | `rwb-source-data` | Worker deployment with the build ID of the release |
| `validateRules`, `selectRows(page)`, `archiveTable`, `verifyManifest`, `deleteArchivedRows`, `recordRun` | Activities | `rwb-source-data` | Registered by the same worker; KEDA scales on queue backlog |
| `casesOnLegalHold`, `caseNumbers` | Activities wrapping the interface | `rwb-source-data` | Registered by the same worker; mTLS to the Temporal frontend |

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. JOB-17 (retention, monthly, first Sunday) is a Temporal Schedule of rwb-document on queue `rwb-document` (Architecture v5 slides 16 and 44; ASM-0076), and this release fails its own check if a Schedule for the retention action appears in a namespace it deploys.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Deployment element |
|---|---|---|
| `interaction`, `case_list_row`, `reconciliation_result`, `data_product_load`, `party_ext`, `contact_point_ext`, `account_ext`, `valuation_ext` | P1 (`rwb_source_data`) | Created by the per-service Flyway sequence; the purge-setting migration is the version that follows |
| `data_product`, `sys_objects`, `sys_fields` | P1 (`rwb_source_data`) | Created by the same sequence; read by the run's validation |
| `retention_rule`, `retention_action` | P5 (`rwb_document`) | Not created, not mounted and not read by this release |
| `decision_log_entry` | P7 (`rwb_decision`) | Not created and never touched; the database keeps its unconditional refusal |

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Deployment use |
|---|---|
| rwb-case `CaseHoldQuery` fake | Runs in the pipeline and in the SIT smoke profile, so a release can prove a run without rwb-case |
| Write-once container stub (Azurite in the lower environments) | Proves the mount, the manifest and the write refusal path before the real container is granted |
| rwb-source-data retention-run fake of RWB-P1-E1017-CON | Lets the P5 side be tested against the deployed route in SIT |

The fakes are test-only workloads; they are not deployed into UAT or production.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 provided, 1 interface consumed in the deployment path | The run start and the run record; the legal-hold answer; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | None for this capability | The topic exists for the service's other events; no message and no consumer group is added here |
| Temporal | 1 workflow, 8 activities, no Schedule | `RetentionRunWorkflow` on `rwb-source-data` in `rwb-recovery`; KEDA scaling on backlog |
| File | 1 container prefix | `retention/` in the write-once container, with a manifest and an immutability policy |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-10 is used here in its second form only: the worker runs a workflow that another service's Schedule starts, and this release registers no Schedule of its own. DP-15 covers the migration job and the purge-setting version it must apply. DP-19 is declared for the administration surface that reads a run and is built by another story.

**Artefacts**

| Artefact | Content |
|---|---|
| `helm/rwb-source-data/` | Chart with the api and worker deployments, service, migration job, config map, secret references, probes, container volume and the KEDA scaler |
| `helm/rwb-source-data/values-dev.yaml`, `values-sit.yaml`, `values-uat.yaml` | Image digest, replicas, resources, probe timings, log level, feature switches, batch size, container name, KEDA thresholds |
| Pipeline stage | Build, unit, component and contract tests, image and dependency scan, chart publish, promote the same artefact |
| Provisioning step | Task queue `rwb-source-data` in namespace `rwb-recovery`; the topic is the platform's and is not recreated |
| Container step | Mount, credential scope on the `retention/` prefix, immutability check and the smoke write and read-back |
| Dashboards | Run counts, rows per table, run duration, container write failures, refused rule sets, held cases |
| Alerts | Three rules, each with a message ID and one runbook entry |
| Runbook | Six entries: refused rule set, unreachable container, failed delete, duplicate start, failed migration, probe failure |
| Capacity note | Archive volume of the eight tables per month, container growth, workflow history retention |

**Probes.** Readiness answers healthy only when the migration is at the expected schema version, the Temporal worker has polled `rwb-source-data` and the container mount answers; liveness answers healthy when the process is up and its internal loop is responsive. Neither probe writes to the database or to the container.

**Migration job.** Runs the per-service Flyway sequence for schema `rwb_source_data` with the service login, as a pre-deploy job with a backoff limit, and applies the purge-setting migration of RWB-P1-E1017-APP; a failed job blocks the rollout and the release.

**Alert mapping carried over from the legacy story.**

| Message ID | Condition | Alert | Route |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-020 | A retention run completes | Summary alert with the counts per product and table, the rule version and the held cases | Compliance mailbox and dashboard, no page |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The archive container is unavailable or refuses a write | Container alert with the system name and the run id | Platform on-call, ticket; page only when it persists past the retry window |
| MSG-P2-006 | A start is posted while a run for that date is active | Duplicate-start counter and operator alert with the job name | Platform on-call, no page on the first occurrence |
| MSG-P1-002 | A rule set is refused in full at a check | Refused-rule-set alert naming the check and the table | Business on-call and Compliance, page |
| MSG-P4-002 | A caller without the run right | Refused-call count on the dashboard | No page |

**Done when.** The chart renders in all three environments, the pipeline promotes one artefact, the probes answer, the queue is registered and KEDA scales, the container mount and the smoke write pass, the three alerts fire on synthetic metrics, the runbook entries are reviewed by the on-call rota and the capacity note is accepted.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-020 | Retention run summary to Compliance | {count} rows of {product} were archived under rule {rule} version {version}. {held} cases on legal hold were kept. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | Archive container unavailable | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P2-006 | A start while the run is active | {job} is already running. Wait for it to finish before you rerun it. |
| MSG-P1-002 | A rule set refused at a check | The {source} load for {date} was refused: {check}. The previous load is still in use. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A caller without the right on the run surface | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story; the deployment adds the alert routing and the runbook link, never a new wording. Thai text follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

The deployment serves the two contract operations and no screen of its own. The operator-facing surfaces of this story are the pipeline run view, the release view, the queue and scaler view, the dashboards and the runbook. Compliance reads a run in the running service through `GET /retention-runs/{runId}`, which the platform administration surface of another P1 story exposes, and the retention classes show on SCR-47 Personal data from Epic 8. The gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) is not on this path.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a values file: the months, the tables, the age-basis fields and the end action are data in the run request, never a deployment value.
- No personal data in logs, dashboard series, alert payloads or the runbook: counts, table names, case numbers, run ids and hashes only.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `recovery.v_ace_*` views: this release mounts no ACE object and reads no view.
- No cross-schema read and no cross-schema key: the migration job and the run touch only `rwb_source_data`, and the legal hold comes over the rwb-case interface.
- One login per service and one container credential per service; the chart carries secret references and no literal credential (DP-02).
- The release pins the image digest and the chart version; a rebuild between environments is not allowed.
- The container is write-once: a wrong archive is a new object at a new run date, never an overwrite, and no operator is granted a bypass of the immutability policy.
- No Schedule is created for the retention action in a namespace this release owns: JOB-17 stays with rwb-document (ASM-0076).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: integration slice of RWB-E1-017 for RWB-ITG-W1. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **QA integration engineer**, I want **the end-to-end proof of the RWB-E1-017 retention rule across rwb-document (P5, the owner), rwb-case (P3, legal hold), rwb-decision (P7, decision log excluded) and rwb-source-data (P1, the interaction ledger)**, so that **the archive, the legal hold and the decision-log exclusion are proved on real services before wave 1 exits**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story runs JOB-17 inside P1 over the interaction table and a retention_rule copy held in the recovery schema. The Ownership Map ruling ASM-0076 moves retention to P5 rwb-document (Architecture v5 slides 16, 41 and 44) and P1 drops its retention_rule copy; the interaction ledger stays with P1 rwb-source-data under the default ruling and DP-18. The decision log is never archived by this job, and its entries stay in P7 rwb-decision. The archive is a write-once Blob container with a manifest, not a data lake: the data lake and its Power BI feed are removed (DP-17, ADR-018).

The target split for the legacy key is therefore: P5 rwb-document owns the retention rule, the retention action, the run and the document archive; P1 rwb-source-data owns the interaction ledger and applies the rule to its own schema; P3 rwb-case owns the case, the case number and the legal hold; P7 rwb-decision owns the decision log, which the rule may never name. This story is the integration proof across those four owners.

No service contract is faked. The suite exercises the published wave 1 contracts of the four services, the shared Temporal namespace and a real write-once container; the only stubs are the external ones named in section 12.8. Where the sources do not name the cross-service trigger for the P1 interaction rows, the run-status surface of the P5 retention run or the fixture composition, the suite asserts through the owners' contracts and records the open point as GAP-0342 and ASM-0436.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P5-E1017-APP is done: the retention rule and retention action tables, the Schedule-started retention run and the archive writer are in SIT.
- RWB-P1-E1017-APP is done: the interaction ledger is owned by rwb-source-data and holds no retention_rule copy.
- RWB-P7-E1017-APP is done: the decision log is readable through the rwb-decision contract and is excluded from every retention load.
- The published contracts of P1 rwb-source-data, P3 rwb-case, P5 rwb-document and P7 rwb-decision are deployed under /api/recovery/<short>/v1.
- The harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG is available with its synthetic documents, cases and interaction rows.
- The environment is SIT, Temporal namespace rwb-recovery, with a write-once Blob container (Azurite in the lower environment).
- No production data is used, and no production connection is opened.
- The release date 30 November 2026 is tentative; a date is not a condition of this story.

##### 4. Flow

1. QA integration engineer: seeds the synthetic documents, cases and interaction rows of the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG; no production data is used.
2. Harness: stores the synthetic document through DocumentIntakeWorkflow on queue rwb-document and waits for rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1.
3. Harness: loads the retention rule version through the retention load path delivered by RWB-P5-E1017-APP; the load is validated in full before it is stored (the path is not named in the source documents; see GAP-0342).
4. Harness: sets the legal hold of one synthetic case through POST /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/legal-hold and reads the case back through GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}.
5. Harness: moves the business date with the clock control and lets the monthly retention Schedule fire; the run starts on the rwb-document task queue.
6. Harness: follows the run through Temporal visibility and reads the run record through the P5 contract; the rule version in force and the record class are recorded on the run.
7. Harness: asserts the archive manifest in the write-once container, the live document through GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}, the case documents through GET /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents, the hold report through the P3 case contract and the unchanged decision log through GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log.
8. Harness: repeats the run on the same run date and asserts that the archive holds one copy of the set.
9. Harness: posts the negative cases — a load that names the decision log, a load value outside the allowed range, a rerun while the run is active and a rerun by a role without the platform administration right — and records every message and status.
10. Harness: writes the evidence report, clears the legal hold and removes the synthetic fixtures.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A retention load names the decision log | The load is refused in full; the rule version in force stays in use; the decision log entries of rwb-decision are unchanged | MSG-P1-002 | AC4 |
| X2 | The archive container refuses writes | No live record is deleted; the run ends FAILED; the alert is raised; the rerun is taken from the job monitor | MSG-GEN-006 | AC5 |
| X3 | A retention load carries a value outside the allowed range | The load is refused in full; the previous rule version stays in force | MSG-GEN-002 | AC7 |
| X4 | A rerun is posted while the retention run is active | Status 409; the active run completes unchanged | MSG-P2-006 | AC9 |
| X5 | A role without the platform administration right posts a rerun | Status 403; no run starts | MSG-P4-002 | AC10 |
| X6 | A consumed contract call exceeds the 2 s timeout or returns a server error | The step is retried under the run policy; the evidence report records the call and the response; no archive or delete is asserted on unverified data | None | AC1, AC2 |
| X7 | The P3 legal-hold call fails before the run starts | The run does not start; the harness records the failed precondition and stops the scenario | None | AC3 |
| X8 | The synthetic fixture set does not match the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG expectations | The suite fails as a fixture fault and names the mismatched element; no service defect is raised | None | AC1, AC6 |
| X9 | The clock control cannot move the business date | The suite fails as a harness fault; the run date is unchanged and no archive assertion is made | None | AC2, AC8 |
| X10 | The archive manifest assertion finds an unexpected object in the container | The suite fails and names the object; the live record is not treated as archived | None | AC2, AC6 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | The suite is its own module and reuses the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG; it needs the three APP stories and the published contracts of P1, P3, P5 and P7, not their source code |
| Negotiable | Periods, record classes, the archive location and the fixture sizes are data rows of the harness; the story fixes the assertions and the call set |
| Valuable | The retention rule, the archive, the legal hold and the decision-log exclusion are proved on real services before wave 1 exits |
| Estimable | One suite module, one fixture pack, one run-date clock, one manifest assertion and one evidence report |
| Small | Ten scenarios over four services and one Schedule; no service code and no schema change |
| Testable | Every scenario asserts a contract response, a run state, a manifest entry or a message; all data is synthetic |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Retention and archive rule for the data store, end-to-end across wave 1 services

  Background:
    Given the wave 1 services rwb-source-data, rwb-document, rwb-case and rwb-decision are deployed in SIT with their published contracts
    Given the RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG synthetic data set is loaded and no production data is used
    Given a retention rule version is in force on the business date

  Scenario: AC1 The retention run is owned by rwb-document (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the retention rule in force names a record class held by rwb-document
    When the monthly retention Schedule fires
    Then the rwb-document retention run starts on the service's own task queue
    Then the run records the rule version in force and the record class
    Then no service reads or writes another service's schema

  Scenario: AC2 A record past its retention age is archived and removed from the live store (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a synthetic record older than the retention age in force
    When the retention run completes
    Then the archive manifest lists the record under the run date and record class
    Then the live store no longer returns the record
    Then the run record counts the archived row under the rule version

  Scenario: AC3 A case on legal hold is not archived (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a synthetic case under legal hold with a record older than the retention age in force
    When the retention run completes
    Then the record stays in the live store
    Then the hold report lists the case
    Then the summary alert names the number of cases kept on legal hold

  Scenario: AC4 The decision log is never archived (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a retention load that names the decision log
    When the load is validated
    Then the load is refused in full with MSG-P1-002 and the check names the decision log
    Then the rule version in force stays in use
    Then the decision log entries of rwb-decision are unchanged

  Scenario: AC5 An archive failure leaves the live record and ends FAILED (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the archive container refuses writes
    When the retention run ends
    Then no live record is deleted
    Then the run ends FAILED with MSG-GEN-006 for the archive container

  Scenario: AC6 A repeat run does not duplicate the archive (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the retention run archived a set of records on the run date
    When the same run is repeated on the same date
    Then the archive holds one copy of the set
    Then the run records no second archive of the same record

  Scenario: AC7 A retention rule outside the allowed range is refused (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a retention load with a value outside the allowed range
    When the load is validated
    Then the load is refused in full with MSG-GEN-002 naming the field and the allowed range
    Then the rule version in force stays in use

  Scenario: AC8 A record exactly at its retention age stays (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a synthetic record exactly at the retention age in force
    When the retention run completes
    Then the record stays in the live store
    Then the run record counts it as kept

  Scenario: AC9 A rerun while the retention run is active is refused (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the retention run is active
    When a platform administrator posts a rerun
    Then the service refuses the rerun with status 409 and MSG-P2-006
    Then the active run completes unchanged

  Scenario: AC10 A role without the job right is refused (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a user holds a role without the platform administration right
    When the user posts a rerun of the retention run
    Then the service refuses the call with status 403 and MSG-P4-002
    Then no run starts
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Each data product and table has one retention rule in force, held as a versioned data row | RWB-E1-017 BR1 |
| BR2 | A row older than its retention period on its age-basis field is archived and removed from the live store | RWB-E1-017 BR2 |
| BR3 | A legal hold keeps every row of the case, overriding the retention rule | RWB-E1-017 BR3 |
| BR4 | A row is removed only after its archive copy is written and checked | RWB-E1-017 BR4 |
| BR5 | The decision log is not archived by this job; its retention is set by Compliance | RWB-E1-017 BR5 |
| BR6 | A retention load with an exception is refused in full | RWB-E1-017 BR6 |
| BR7 | A new version applies from its valid-from date; earlier runs keep their recorded version | RWB-E1-017 BR7 |
| BR8 | P5 rwb-document owns the retention rule and the retention action; no other service holds a copy of the rule table | ASM-0076; Architecture v5 slides 16, 41 and 44 |
| BR9 | Each owning service applies the rule to its own schema; the suite asserts through the owner's contract and never queries another service's table | DP-01; ASM-0076 |
| BR10 | The interaction ledger stays with P1 rwb-source-data, the case and the legal hold stay with P3 rwb-case and the decision log stays with P7 rwb-decision; each is read only through its own API | Ownership Map; ASM-0076 |
| BR11 | Every cross-service call in the suite is one hop with a 2 s timeout | ADR-020 |
| BR12 | No personal data in the run record, the archive manifest assertion, the evidence report or the fixtures; identifiers and counts only | RWB-E1-017 section 17; ADR-015 |

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It changes the JOB-17 run status (Running, Complete, Failed) and the retention rule version in force.

| Object | State | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Retention run | Running | The Schedule-started run is active on the rwb-document task queue |
| Retention run | Complete | The archive is written, the manifest is checked, the live rows are removed and the run record is written |
| Retention run | Failed | The archive write or the manifest check failed; no live row is deleted and the alert is raised |
| Retention rule version | In force | The approved version whose valid-from date covers the run date |
| Retention rule version | Superseded | Replaced by a later approved version; earlier runs keep the version they recorded |
| Case legal hold | On | Every record of the case is kept and the case is listed in the hold report |
| Case legal hold | Off | Set by P3 rwb-case when the hold is cleared; the record follows the rule again |

The suite sets and clears the hold through the P3 contract; it does not change the case status.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The suite provides no REST operation. The names reserved for P2 rwb-integration — /api/recovery/integration/v1, rwb.integration.events.v1, rwb-integration and rwb_integration — are not used, and no rwb_integration table is written.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method and path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|
| GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId} | P5 rwb-document | Read the live document and its record class before and after the run |
| GET /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents | P5 rwb-document | Read the documents of a case and their archive state |
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId} | P3 rwb-case | Read the legal hold flag and the case number |
| POST /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/legal-hold | P3 rwb-case | Set and clear the legal hold |
| GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log | P7 rwb-decision | Prove the decision log is unchanged |
| GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs | P1 rwb-source-data | Optional run evidence for the interaction path |

Every call is one hop with a 2 s timeout (ADR-020, DP-11).

None. The suite publishes no event.

|---|---|---|---|
| rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1 | rwb.document.events.v1 | P5 rwb-document | The synthetic document is stored; the suite waits for it before the run |

No event is produced by the suite.

The run reads only the rwb_document schema. No workflow, activity or the suite reads another service's schema.

None. The suite owns no table and never reads another service's schema (DP-01).

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Suite module for RWB-ITG-W1, reusing harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG | Integration suite | Runs the ten scenarios against SIT and holds no service code |
| Fixture pack | Test data | Synthetic documents, cases and interaction rows for the record classes under test |
| Run-date clock control | Harness control | Moves the business date and restores it after the scenario |
| Archive manifest assertion | Assertion | Reads the write-once container and checks the manifest entry per run date and record class |
| Evidence report | Report | Records per scenario the run id, the run state, the contract responses, the counts and the messages |

Decoupling patterns applied (Template and Rules v1 §R5.5):

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added | Where it sits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | recovery.<table>, "recovery schema" | Owner's schema rwb_<name>; never read another service's tables | none | The suite asserts through contracts only; each of P1, P3, P5 and P7 writes its own schema |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic rwb.decision-record.v1 | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON | On the P1, P5 and P7 APP stories; not a build dependency of this suite |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON | On the APP stories; the suite only reads the case through the P3 contract |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON | On RWB-P5-E1017-APP; the suite observes the Schedule-started run |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) | The six consumed REST operations of section 12.2 |
| DP-13 | /api/recovery/v1 | /api/recovery/<short>/v1 | none | Every consumed path in section 12.2 |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON | On the APP stories; the suite changes no schema |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON | Not used by this suite; no screen is in scope |

The dependency-added column records the build dependency of the owning story. This story has no build dependency: an ITG story waits on no build of its own, and its I dependencies are the APP stories listed in the metadata table.

Build steps:

1. Create the suite module next to harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG and wire it to the SIT endpoints of P1, P3, P5 and P7.
2. Build the fixture pack: synthetic documents, cases and interaction rows, with the record class and legal hold as data rows.
3. Add the run-date clock control and the restore step.
4. Implement the ten scenarios of section 7 in TC order and assert only through the contracts of section 12.2, the events of section 12.4 and Temporal visibility.
5. Add the archive manifest assertion for the write-once container, including the write-refusal scenario.
6. Add the negative loads, the rerun while active and the role without the right, and assert the exact messages and statuses.
7. Write the evidence report with the run id, the rule version in force, the counts, the hold report and the decision-log comparison.
8. Run the suite in SIT against the wave 1 release candidate and keep the report with the wave exit evidence.

Done when: all ten test cases pass in SIT against the published wave 1 contracts, the evidence report is attached to the wave exit pack, and no service code or schema was changed by this story.

##### 17. Guardrails

- Synthetic data only; the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG loads the fixtures and no production data is read, copied or connected to.
- No personal data in the run record, the archive manifest assertion, the logs, the evidence report or the fixtures: identifiers and counts only.
- No cross-service table read: every assertion goes through the owner's contract, and the suite owns no table.
- No business value in test code: periods, record classes and the archive location are data rows or properties.
- No live row is deleted before the archive copy is checked, and the suite never deletes a live row itself.
- One hop and a 2 s timeout on every call (ADR-020).
- No production access of any kind from the suite or its configuration.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-018 for rwb-case. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of rwb-case for the case resource: an OpenAPI 3.1 document for the case operations, an AsyncAPI document with the six event schemas under a CloudEvents envelope, the error envelope, the Idempotency-Key rule on every POST, the versioning rule, the contract tables of section 12 and the contract fakes for rwb-source-data, rwb-access and rwb-decision**, so that **every consuming team and the app, operations and test stories of this legacy key can build against a fixed, testable contract on Day 1 without waiting for rwb-case to be built**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST and one hop with a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). rwb-case publishes sixteen REST operations and six event types; the case-creation capability of RWB-E1-018 needs four of those operations, two event types it publishes and two it consumes. If the field-level contract is agreed once and faked, the app story builds in parallel with rwb-source-data, rwb-access and rwb-decision, and a change in any of them is caught in a contract test rather than in an integration window. The baseline also fixes the naming that the checks require: schema rwb_case, REST base `/api/recovery/case/v1`, topic `rwb.case.events.v1`, event names `rwb.case.<Event>.v1`, task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the document, topic and event names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- The outbox, inbox and idempotency library is available as a reference for the table names and columns (RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, DP-09).
- The platform error envelope and the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope are the platform baseline; where this document narrows them it does so explicitly.
- The operations and their owners are taken from the Ownership Map only; rwb-case never documents an operation owned by another service.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 document for the four case operations the capability needs, with the shared components used across the sixteen rwb-case operations.
2. Draft the AsyncAPI document for `rwb.case.events.v1` with the six event types and the shared CloudEvents 1.0 envelope.
3. Agree the error envelope and map each HTTP status to its message ID.
4. State the Idempotency-Key rule for every POST and the stored-response behaviour.
5. State the versioning rule for the REST surface and for the event schemas.
6. Publish the contract tables of section 12 (nine sub-tables) and the three contract fakes.
7. Add the contract tests: schema validation, envelope validation, error mapping, idempotency replay and version negotiation.
8. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-P3-E1018-APP, RWB-P3-E1018-OPS and every consuming service.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A request body fails schema validation | 400 with the error envelope and the failing pointer | MSG-P3-030 | AC3 |
| X2 | A required header is missing on a POST | 400 with the error envelope naming the header | MSG-P3-031 | AC4 |
| X3 | The same Idempotency-Key is replayed with a different body | 422 with the error envelope; the stored response is not overwritten | MSG-P3-032 | AC4 |
| X4 | A caller asks for a major version the service does not serve | 404 with the error envelope and the served major versions | MSG-P3-033 | AC5 |
| X5 | A consumer cannot deserialise an event | The schema registry validation fails the build; the event is not published | None | AC2 |
| X6 | A contract fake drifts from the document | The contract test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC6 |
| X7 | A field-level definition is missing from the source material | The field is marked with the placeholder and one gap row is carried | None | AC1 |

Message IDs MSG-P3-030 to MSG-P3-033 are the contract-level codes of this baseline; the business messages MSG-P1-001, MSG-P3-025, MSG-P3-027, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003 and MSG-P7-003 keep their text from the legacy story and are carried unchanged in the error envelope mapping.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes and the Ownership Map only |
| Negotiable | Field-level detail is settled with the consumers; the named operations, events, envelope and rules are fixed by the target architecture |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app, operations and test stories of this legacy key on Day 1 and every consumer of the case resource |
| Estimable | Two documents, one error envelope, two rules, nine contract tables, three fakes and six contract tests |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Case resource contract baseline for rwb-case

  Background:
    Given the service naming rule of the platform library is in force
    Given the six rwb-case event types are CaseCreated, CaseAllocated, CaseAllocationFailed, CaseTransferred, CaseStateChanged and TimerBreached

  Scenario: AC1 The OpenAPI 3.1 document describes the case operations (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the OpenAPI 3.1 document of rwb-case is published
    When it is validated against the OpenAPI 3.1 schema
    Then it validates with no error
    Then it declares the base /api/recovery/case/v1
    Then it declares GET /cases, GET /cases/{caseId}, GET /cases/{caseId}/accounts and GET /cases/{caseId}/parties with the owner rwb-case
    Then every operation names its security right and its error responses 401, 403, 404 and 503

  Scenario: AC2 The AsyncAPI document carries the six event schemas (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the AsyncAPI document of rwb-case is published
    When it is validated against the AsyncAPI 3 schema
    Then it declares the topic rwb.case.events.v1
    Then it declares the six event types rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1, rwb.case.CaseAllocated.v1, rwb.case.CaseAllocationFailed.v1, rwb.case.CaseTransferred.v1, rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1 and rwb.case.TimerBreached.v1
    Then every message uses the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope with the attributes id, source, type, specversion, time, subject and datacontenttype
    Then every message carries IDs and facts only and no personal data field

  Scenario: AC3 The error envelope is one shape for every failure (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the error envelope component of the document
    When a 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 or 503 response is produced
    Then the body carries the code, the message, the messageId, the traceId and the field list
    Then the messageId is one of the contract or business message IDs and the text is the agreed text
    Then the response carries the problem media type and the trace identifier

  Scenario: AC4 Every POST requires an Idempotency-Key (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a POST operation in the document
    When the request omits the Idempotency-Key header
    Then the service answers 400 with the error envelope and MSG-P3-031
    When the same key is sent twice with the same body
    Then the second call returns the stored response and no second state change
    When the same key is sent with a different body
    Then the service answers 422 with the error envelope and MSG-P3-032

  Scenario: AC5 The versioning rule is stated and enforced (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the document declares major version 1 in the path
    When a caller uses an unsupported major version
    Then the service answers 404 with the error envelope and the served major versions
    Then the event schemas are versioned in the registry with BACKWARD compatibility and the event name carries the schema version
    Then a breaking change to a published schema requires a new major version

  Scenario: AC6 The nine contract tables are complete and the fakes match them (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the contract section of this story
    When the nine sub-tables are reviewed
    Then each of 12.1 to 12.9 is present and names its owner from the Ownership Map
    Then the three contract fakes answer the paths and payloads of 12.2
    Then the contract tests compare the fakes with the document and fail on any drift
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One REST base per service: `/api/recovery/case/v1`; a document never declares another service's path | DP-13; Arch v5 slide 41 notes |
| BR2 | Event names are `rwb.<short>.<Event>.v1` on the topic `rwb.<short>.events.v1`, with retry and `.dlt` topics | DP-14; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR3 | Every event carries the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, is keyed by caseId and carries no personal data | Arch v5 slides 42 and 43 notes; DP-09 |
| BR4 | Every POST declares the Idempotency-Key header and stores its response | Arch v5 slide 11; DP-09 |
| BR5 | Error responses use one envelope and one message ID per condition; business message texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story | Arch v5 platform baseline; Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR6 | A schema change is additive within a major version; a breaking change is a new major version | Arch v5 slide 42 notes (BACKWARD compatibility) |
| BR7 | The document lists only operations owned by rwb-case; a consumed operation is described as consumed, never as provided | Ownership Map v1 |
| BR8 | No business value is fixed in the contract: the threshold, the exclusion reasons and the bands stay data | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |

| Draft | Review opened | The four case operations and the six events are described | In review |

| Baselined | Additive change | A field is added within major version 1 | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A field is removed, renamed or retyped | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Case account resource | `id`, `caseId`, `accountKey`, `isPrimary`, `linkedFrom`, `linkedTo`, from `case_account` fields DF-CAS-024 to DF-CAS-029 |
| Case party resource | `id`, `caseId`, `personKey`, `partyRole`, `roleFrom`, `roleTo`, from `case_party` fields DF-CAS-030 to DF-CAS-035 |
| Exclusion resource | `accountKey`, `businessDate`, `reasonCode`, `ruleId`, `ruleVersion`, from `case_entry_exclusion` fields DF-CAS-056 to DF-CAS-061 |
| Event payloads | IDs, codes, dates and amounts only; no name, address, identity number or contact point |

The exact field-level schema of the new case resource (types, lengths, required flags per property and the page and sort parameters) is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0676; ASM-1223); this story fixes the field names above and leaves the field-level detail to the baseline review.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-case (P3); base `/api/recovery/case/v1`.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/cases` | CasePage with the case-number search and the paging parameters (GAP-0676) | Case record R |
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}` | Case | Case record R |
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}/accounts` | CaseAccount[] | Case record R |
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}/parties` | CaseParty[] | Case record R |

The full rwb-case surface of sixteen operations is published in the service API file; this baseline documents the four operations the case-creation capability needs and keeps the shared components reusable for the rest.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/accounts/{id}` | P1 rwb-source-data | Account and arrears fields, faked |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/customers/{id}` | P1 rwb-source-data | Customer row and extension flags, faked |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/freshness` | P1 rwb-source-data | Batch completeness for the business date, faked |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-models/{n}/{v}` | P7 rwb-decision | Package model and checksum, faked |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | Role, scope and right check, faked |

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Schema |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1` | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 | caseId, caseNo, productGroup, accounts, businessDate |
| `rwb.case.CaseAllocated.v1` | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 | caseId, caseNo, queueCode, ownerReference, allocationRuleId, packageVersion |
| `rwb.case.CaseAllocationFailed.v1` | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 | caseId, caseNo, queueCode, reasonCode, allocationRuleId, packageVersion |
| `rwb.case.CaseTransferred.v1` | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 | caseId, caseNo, transferReasonCode, fromReference, toReference |
| `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 | caseId, caseNo, fromStatus, toStatus, ruleId, packageVersion, decidedAt |
| `rwb.case.TimerBreached.v1` | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 | caseId, caseNo, timerId, timerType, expiresAt |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 | decision record reference, ruleId, ruleVersion, finalCall, decidedAt |

The six `rwb.case.*` types are the rwb-case event contract; DecisionRecorded is the shared ledger event the local decision-record library publishes (DP-03).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Consumer contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` | `rwb.source-data.events.v1` | P1 | Business date, source ALS, freshness summary; starts DailyCaseRun |
| `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` | `rwb.decision.events.v1` | P7 | Package code, version label, checksum, valid-from date; refreshes the KieBase cache |

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| CaseWorkflow | Workflow, parent, one per case, workflow ID = case ID | `rwb-case` | Input and signal schemas, search attributes CaseId, Stage, ProductGroup, QueueCode |
| DailyCaseRun | Workflow, started by AceDataReady with a daily Schedule fallback | `rwb-case` | Input schema (business date, source), run record shape |
| allocate, transfer, rebalance | Activities | `rwb-case` | Input and output schemas |

**Build steps**

1. OpenAPI 3.1 skeleton with the base path, the security scheme, the error responses and the shared components; schema lint in the pipeline.
2. The four case operations and their resources, with the field names of section 11; the field-level detail is agreed under GAP-0676.
3. AsyncAPI 3 document with `rwb.case.events.v1`, the six event types, the CloudEvents envelope and the registry versioning rule.
4. Error envelope and the message-ID mapping, business texts copied unchanged.
5. Idempotency-Key rule and the stored-response behaviour, and the versioning rule.
6. The three contract fakes and the stub fixtures.
7. The six contract tests; a drift between a fake and the document fails the build.
8. Baseline tag and the consumer sign-off note.

**Done when.** The OpenAPI and AsyncAPI documents validate in the pipeline, the six contract tests pass, the three fakes answer every consumed path and the app, operations and test stories have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-030 | A request body or query fails schema validation | The request could not be read: {detail}. |
| MSG-P3-031 | A required header is missing on a POST | The request is missing {header}. |
| MSG-P3-032 | An Idempotency-Key is replayed with a different body | This request was already sent with different content. |
| MSG-P3-033 | An unsupported major version is requested | This version of the service is not available. |
| MSG-P1-001 | DailyCaseRun waiting for a complete ALS batch | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |
| MSG-P3-025 | Yearly case number range used up | Case numbers for {year} are used up. New cases are on hold until the range is extended. |
| MSG-P3-027 | No ENTRY or EXCLUSION version is in force on the business date | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Read without Case record R | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | Case outside the reader's scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Decision record write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The message IDs are contract elements; the text is the agreed text taken from the legacy story where the message already existed.

##### 15. Screens and states

The contract serves the two screens of the case-creation capability: SCR-02 Case list (Loading; empty; list; filtered) and SCR-03 Case record (Loading; read only). The gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) calls the case operations and the rwb-source-data operations in parallel and merges the answers. The composite route specification, the screen field list and the masking of customer fields are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0674; ASM-1221); the OpenAPI document fixes the case side of the merge only.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the threshold, the exclusion reasons, the exposure bands and the status list stay data in the parameters, the reference tables and the rule packages.
- No personal data in an event schema, an example or a fake: IDs, codes, dates and amounts only.
- The contract names only rwb-case tables and only operations owned by rwb-case; no other service's table is read or documented as provided (DP-01).
- One REST base and one topic per service; a document that names another service's base or topic fails the review (DP-13, DP-14).
- Every example in the document is synthetic; no production payload is copied into a schema or a fake.
- The error envelope, the CloudEvents envelope and the naming rule come from the platform library; this story narrows them but never redefines them.

##### 1. Story

As a **product owner**, I want **every account at 90 days past due or more that rwb-source-data publishes from the ACE account view, and that no exclusion rule blocks, placed on one recovery case per customer and product inside rwb-case, with a case number in the form RW-YYYY-NNNNNN issued from a per-service sequence at creation and never reused, a status and its linked accounts and parties held in the rwb_case schema, created by the DailyCaseRun workflow on AceDataReady for the business date**, so that **every team, letter and document refers to one case ID held by one owner service**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Recovery teams keep their own lists today, so one account can be on several trackers under different references, and some accounts at 90 days past due have no owner at all (control CTL-01 answers this audit finding). In the target, ACE ingests the ALS account, the SCBPDM customer and the EFS collections history, and rwb-source-data publishes the thirty `recovery.v_ace_*` views through its contract; rwb-case never reads an ACE view or another service's tables (DP-01, DP-05). This story creates the case by rule when the ACE batch for the business date is complete, blocks an excluded account with a logged reason, and gives the case a number that every later document carries.

Under D-RCV-36 the entry and exclusion rules are the Drools packages ENTRY and EXCLUSION. In the target the governance of a package (authoring, tests, four-eyes approval, effective dating) is central in rwb-decision (P7), the version in force is fetched by rwb-case through `GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}` and executed by the embedded Drools kit inside an activity (DP-04), so a rule change needs no release and every decision names the rule ID and the package version. It meets REQ-CWC-001 to REQ-CWC-005 and REQ-CWC-016, and supports reconciliation REC-01 (accounts at 90 days past due against open cases, zero unexplained) and REC-05 (every business key on a P3 table resolves to its source row).

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P3-E1018-CON is published: the case resource schemas, the six `rwb.case.events.v1` event schemas with the CloudEvents envelope, the error envelope, the Idempotency-Key rule and the contract fakes.
- RWB-PLT-E1044-CON is published: the per-service Flyway sequence and migration conventions (DP-15). The rwb_case tables `recovery_case`, `case_account`, `case_party` and `case_entry_exclusion` exist before this story runs its own migrations.
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published: the local decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03). RWB-P7-E1027-CON publishes the central ledger contract behind it.
- RWB-PLT-E1072-CON is published: the embedded Drools kit, with one KieBase per package version, first-match semantics and the `NoPackageInForce` outcome (DP-04).
- RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-P3-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON are published: the parameters contract and the reference-data contract, both owned by rwb-case, with the client library (DP-06, DP-07).
- RWB-PLT-TE006-CON is published: the outbox and inbox library with CloudEvents (DP-09). RWB-PLT-E1047-CON is published: the topic and event naming library (DP-14). RWB-PLT-E1071-CON is published: the Temporal workflow kit in namespace `rwb-recovery` (DP-10).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the gateway-bff composite route that serves the case screen (DP-19), also recorded under GAP-0674.
- RWB-P3-E1073-APP is done: package ENTRY version "ENTRY-2026.11" and package EXCLUSION version "EXCL-2026.11" are approved by RW-RISK, who is not the author, and are in force from 2026-11-30, each with at least 50 passing scenarios. The EXCLUSION rows carry reason codes DECEASED, FRAUD, BANKRUPTCY, ACTIVE_PLAN and OPEN_DISPUTE (REQ-CWC-004).
- Parameter `case.entry.dpd` = 90 is in force in `parameter_value` (DL16), owned by RW-COE.
- The exposure band table LOV-EXPOSURE, the status list LOV-CASE-STATUS and LOV-PRODUCT are held in the rwb-case reference tables `lov_value`, `reference_row` and `reference_version` (DP-07).
- The daily case run is switched on only when the ACE batch of the business date is complete and rwb-source-data has raised AceDataReady (EV-26).
- The login is the rwb-case login (DP-02): Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0675; ASM-1222).

##### 4. Flow

1. rwb-source-data: the ALS batch for business date 2026-12-01 completes, its `AceIngestCheck` workflow confirms freshness over the `recovery.v_ace_*` views, and it publishes AceDataReady (EV-26) for source ALS and business date 2026-12-01 on `rwb.source-data.events.v1`.
2. rwb-case: the case router consumes the event through its inbox (one action per event), calls `signalWithStart` and starts DailyCaseRun on task queue `rwb-case` for that business date; the inbound ID is read through the rwb-source-data contract, never from an ACE view.
3. DailyCaseRun: reads parameter `case.entry.dpd` through the parameters contract of rwb-case, with the version in force.
4. DailyCaseRun: reads the eligible accounts from the rwb-source-data contract activity `listEligibleAccounts(businessDate)`: `account_key`, `account_code`, `product_group`, `region_code`, `days_past_due`, `total_balance`, `tdr_flag`, `data_as_of`. An account that already has an open `case_account` row (`linked_to` is null) is skipped.
5. DailyCaseRun: for each account asks rwb-source-data for the BORROWER `person_key` and its customer row; an account whose borrower key has no customer row is not grouped and gets no case.
6. EvaluateRules activity: the embedded Drools kit evaluates package EXCLUSION on the facts built from the account and customer rows and the extension flags; an excluded account gets a `case_entry_exclusion` row with the reason code, the rule ID and the package version, and no case. The package version is the one in force on the business date and is verified against the checksum returned by rwb-decision.
7. EvaluateRules activity: package ENTRY is evaluated on `days_past_due`, the product group and the entry threshold; an account the package does not match gets no case and is counted as not entered; the ENTER rule ID and package version are carried to the decision record.
8. Grouping: the remaining accounts are grouped by the borrower `person_key` and the product group read from the account row; an existing open case for the same pair receives a new `case_account` row with the `account_key` instead of a new case.
9. Case number: the per-service sequence for the entry year in `rwb_case` is drawn and formatted RW-2026-000123; a number is never reused, including for a closed case.
10. RecordAndApply activity: in one rwb_case transaction the service writes `recovery_case` with status NEW, the primary customer key, `dpd_at_entry`, `total_outstanding_at_entry` and the exposure band, the `case_account` rows with `account_key` and `is_primary`, the BORROWER `case_party` row with `person_key`, and CaseCreated (EV-01) in the outbox. The primary account is the linked account with the highest `total_balance` on the business date; a tie breaks on the lowest `account_key`.
11. RecordAndApply activity: as the last step before commit, the local decision-record library writes decision code "D6", final call "CASE_CREATED", the ENTRY rule ID and package version and the ALS business date, and publishes DecisionRecorded on `rwb.decision-record.v1` through the outbox; a failed write rolls the whole transaction back, so no number is consumed by a visible case.
12. DailyCaseRun: records the counts (accounts read, excluded, not entered, linked, created, failed) on the run record and starts the next step, the morning allocation (JOB-03, carried by RWB-P3-E1020-APP).
13. CaseWorkflow is started once per case with the workflow ID equal to the case ID, on task queue `rwb-case`, and takes the case from entry to closure.
14. Case owner: opens the case through gateway-bff, which calls `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` and `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/accounts` on rwb-case and, in parallel, rwb-source-data for the account and customer fields, then merges the two answers into the screen model.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The account matches an EXCLUSION rule | No case; `case_entry_exclusion` row with reason code, rule ID and package version | None | AC2, AC6 |
| X2 | The borrower already has an open case for the same product group | The account is linked to that case by `account_key`; no new case | None | AC3 |
| X3 | Days past due is 89 in the account row of the business date | No case; the account is read again on the next complete ALS batch | None | AC7 |
| X4 | DailyCaseRun runs again for the same business date | No duplicate case, link or number; the inbox drops the second event and the run skips a linked account | None | AC8 |
| X5 | The ALS batch for the business date is not complete | DailyCaseRun does not start; no case from an incomplete day; it starts when AceDataReady is raised for the date | MSG-P1-001 | AC9 |
| X6 | The decision record write fails | The case is not created and no number is consumed by a visible case; the account is retried in the next run | MSG-P7-003 | AC10 |
| X7 | The yearly number range RW-2026-999999 is used | Creation stops for the year's remaining accounts; an incident is raised | MSG-P3-025 | AC11 |
| X8 | The same borrower has a mortgage and a hire purchase account at 90 days past due | Two cases, one per product group | None | AC12 |
| X9 | A business key on a case or in the intake has no row in the source contract | The intake creates no case or party link from the missing row; an existing link is unchanged; REC-05 lists the key for the data steward and the ACE team; the key is read again on the next complete batch | None | AC13 |
| X10 | A role without Case record R reads a case | Refused with 403 by the rwb-access authorise check behind the endpoint | MSG-P4-002 | AC14 |
| X11 | No EXCLUSION version is in force on the business date | DailyCaseRun creates no case for the date; the run record carries MSG-P3-027 for the package-in-force check; the accounts are held for the next run | MSG-P3-027 | AC15 |
| X12 | rwb-source-data does not answer inside the REST budget | One hop, 2 s timeout (DP-11); the account is left for the next run and counted as failed, never created from a partial record | None | AC9, AC10 |

```gherkin
    Then the exclusion record for A-5005 holds reason "OPEN_DISPUTE" and rule ID "EXCL-006"

  Scenario: AC7 The entry threshold boundary (legacy RWB-E1-018 AC7)
    Given v_ace_account holds account A-5006 at days_past_due 89 and account A-5007 at days_past_due 90, both with no exclusion
    Given the rwb-decision contract mock returns package code "ENTRY" with version "ENTRY-2026.11"
    When the entry rule runs
    Then the system creates a case for A-5007
    Then the system creates no case for A-5006

  Scenario: AC8 A repeated run creates nothing new (legacy RWB-E1-018 AC8)
    Given JOB-02 has created case RW-2026-000125 for account A-5008 on 2026-12-01
    When JOB-02 runs again for 2026-12-01
    Then account A-5008 has one case link
    Then the system issues no case number in the second run

  Scenario: AC10 The decision log write fails (legacy RWB-E1-018 AC10)
    Given the decision log store is unavailable
    When the entry rule runs for account A-5009
    Then no case exists for A-5009
    Then the job record lists A-5009 as failed with MSG-P7-003
    Then the system takes A-5009 again in the next run

  Scenario: AC11 The yearly number range is used up (legacy RWB-E1-018 AC11)
    Given the last case number issued in 2026 is RW-2026-999999
    When account A-5010 qualifies for a new case on 2026-12-30
    Then the system creates no case for A-5010
    Then the job record carries MSG-P3-025 with year 2026
    Then the system raises an incident to the platform administrator

  Scenario: AC12 Two products give two cases (legacy RWB-E1-018 AC12)
    Given v_ace_account holds mortgage account A-5011 and hire purchase account A-5012 for borrower P-0103, both at days_past_due 91
    Given the rwb-source-data contract mock returns mortgage account A-5011 and hire purchase account A-5012 for borrower P-0103
    When the entry rule runs
    Then two cases exist for P-0103, one with product group "MORTGAGE" and one with "HIRE_PURCHASE"

  Scenario: AC14 A role without Case record R is refused (legacy RWB-E1-018 AC14)
    Given user "U-5001" holds RW-REFADM, which has no Case record right
    Given the rwb-access contract mock returns no Case record right for role "RW-REFADM"
    When "U-5001" calls GET /cases/{caseId} for case RW-2026-000123
    Then the system refuses the call with status 403 and MSG-P4-002
    Then the system writes one AC-DENY event with area "CASE_RECORD" and right "R"
```

AC1, AC9, AC13 and AC15 are cited in the flow and the exception table but are owned by the integration story RWB-ITG-E1018-ITG of this legacy key, where the real cross-service behaviour and the batch gate are proved; the eleven criteria above are the ones this story owns.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | An account enters recovery when `days_past_due` for the ACE business date is at or above the entry threshold and package ENTRY returns ENTER | Parameter case.entry.dpd = 90; package ENTRY; DL16; DF-ACE-018 |
| BR2 | One case per borrower `person_key` and product group, with every qualifying account linked by `account_key` | DL17; REQ-CWC-003 |
| BR3 | An account matching an EXCLUSION rule gets no case; the reason, rule ID and package version are recorded in `case_entry_exclusion` | Package EXCLUSION; REQ-CWC-004 |
| BR4 | The case number is RW, the entry year and a six-digit number from the per-service yearly sequence; it is issued once and never reused, including after closure | `recovery_case.case_no` (DF-CAS-002); the unique key on the case number |
| BR5 | A new case has status NEW and no owner until allocation | casemodel.txt Case status "New" |
| BR6 | Status values are read from the reference list, not from code; a new list value is accepted with its version in force | LOV-CASE-STATUS; DP-07 |
| BR7 | No case is created before the ACE batch for the business date is complete; a late or failed batch is carried by AceDataLate and the case is created on the next complete batch | CTL-02; DailyCaseRun "No cases from an incomplete day" |
| BR8 | Every case creation writes its decision record, with the ENTRY rule ID and package version, in the same transaction as the case rows and the outbox row; a failed write rolls the creation back | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; REQ-CWC-016 |
| BR9 | The exposure band is set from the total outstanding at entry using the band table in force | `recovery_case.exposure_band` (DF-CAS-015); LOV-EXPOSURE |
| BR10 | A case created on bad data is canceled by rule, never deleted | R-UNI-16 (Epic 2 handling) |
| BR11 | The case links to its source by business key (`primary_customer_id`, `account_key`, `person_key`) with no foreign key across services. A key with no source row is listed by REC-05 and never invented from a partial record | DP-01; D-RCV-35 U4; ADR-010; REC-05 |
| BR12 | The primary account is the linked account with the highest `total_balance` on the business date; a tie breaks on the lowest `account_key` | `case_account.is_primary` (DF-CAS-027); Data Tier Map section 5 |
| BR13 | Entry and exclusion decisions come only from the embedded Drools kit on packages ENTRY and EXCLUSION, using the version in force. A version not in force holds creation with MSG-P3-027 and is never a default decision | R-UNI-41; D-RCV-36 T3, T5; DP-04 |
| BR14 | The package version is fetched from rwb-decision, its checksum is verified before the KieBase is used, and a version is never edited in place | D-RCV-36 T4; DP-04 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | AceDataReady (EV-26), package ENTRY returns ENTER | `days_past_due` at or above 90 for the complete ALS business date, package EXCLUSION returns no match, no open case for the borrower and product group | New |
| New | CaseWorkflow started with the case ID | The case rows, the party link and the CaseCreated outbox row commit together | Active |
| New | Allocation rule matched | Handled by RWB-P3-E1020-APP | Assigned |

`WAITING_COURT` is a list value added to LOV-CASE-STATUS by a list load with valid from 2027-01-01 (AC5); it is accepted as data through the reference-data contract and needs no code change.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| rwb-case service identity (the rwb-case login, DP-02) | Runs DailyCaseRun; reads the eligible accounts, the customer rows and the extension flags from rwb-source-data; creates the case, the account links, the party link, the exclusion rows and the decision record |
| ACE batch record through rwb-source-data | Raises AceDataReady (EV-26); no case write in this story |
| Drools evaluator (SY-RULES identity) | Evaluates the ENTRY and EXCLUSION packages through the embedded kit (Rules and parameters R) |
| Decision-record library identity | Writes the local decision record and its outbox row (Decision log C) |
| RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-PHONECOL and every role with Case record R | Read the case and its accounts through the endpoints, within their scope |
| RW-COE | Owns the ENTRY and EXCLUSION packages and the threshold parameter; loads the packages through RWB-P3-E1073-APP and the parameter through the parameters contract |
| RW-RISK | Approves a package version; the author cannot approve |
| Platform administrator | Extends the yearly number range when MSG-P3-025 is raised |
| RW-REFADM | Has no Case record right; refused on the read endpoints |

The per-service login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0675; ASM-1222); the story names it "the rwb-case login (DP-02)" until it is agreed.

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity in rwb_case | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023 | recovery_case | all fields | Write |
| DF-CAS-024 to DF-CAS-029 | case_account | all fields | Write |
| DF-CAS-030 to DF-CAS-035 | case_party | all fields | Write |
| DF-CAS-056 to DF-CAS-061 | case_entry_exclusion | all fields, including rule_id and rule_version | Write |
| DF-CAS-002 | recovery_case | case_no (RW-YYYY-NNNNNN) | Write |
| DF-REF-132 to DF-REF-158 | parameter_catalog, parameter_value | `case.entry.dpd` and its version in force | Read |
| DF-REF-159 to DF-REF-184 | reference_version, reference_row | LOV-CASE-STATUS, LOV-EXPOSURE, LOV-PRODUCT versions | Read |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision record (local library) | all fields | Write |

Source fields are read only through the rwb-source-data contract: `account_key`, `account_code`, `product_group`, `branch_code`, `days_past_due`, `total_balance`, `tdr_flag`, `data_as_of`, `person_key`, `deceased_flag`, the BORROWER relation and the borrower's relation type (DF-ACE-001, DF-ACE-002, DF-ACE-010, DF-ACE-012, DF-ACE-018, DF-ACE-020, DF-ACE-031, DF-ACE-036, DF-ACE-056, DF-ACE-061, DF-ACE-084, DF-ACE-085, DF-ACE-086), and the extension flags `dispute_open`, `deceased_override`, `bankruptcy` and `fraud_flag` (DF-EXT-001, DF-EXT-003, DF-EXT-004, DF-EXT-005, DF-EXT-027, DF-EXT-028). No copy of a source row is written into rwb_case.

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8. `case_entry_exclusion.rule_id` holds the Drools rule name and `case_entry_exclusion.rule_version` holds the package version label (D-RCV-36 T5); both are inside DF-CAS-056 to DF-CAS-061, so no field ID is added. rwb-case reads no rule row; the package is fetched as a model from rwb-decision.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/case/v1`; owner rwb-case (P3).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/cases` | List cases in the caller's scope, including the case-number search used by AC4 | Case record R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}` | Read one case with status, entry date, exposure band and totals | Case record R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}/accounts` | Read the linked accounts with the primary flag and link dates | Case record R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}/parties` | Read the parties on the case, masked by role | Case record R, scope applied | Not applicable |

Response fields per the case CON story: case `id`, `caseNo`, `productGroup`, `primaryPersonKey`, `status`, `entryDate`, `dpdAtEntry`, `exposureBand`, `totalOutstandingAtEntry`, `deviationOpen`, `legalHold`; account `id`, `caseId`, `accountKey`, `isPrimary`, `linkedFrom`, `linkedTo`. Errors: 401 no session (MSG-P4-001), 403 no Case record R (MSG-P4-002), 404 not found or out of scope (MSG-P4-003), 503 store down.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Service | Used for | Timeout |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/accounts/{id}` | rwb-source-data (P1) | Account and arrears fields of the business date | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/customers/{id}` | rwb-source-data (P1) | Customer row, deceased flag and extension flags | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/freshness` | rwb-source-data (P1) | ACE batch completeness for the business date (AC9) | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-models/{n}/{v}` | rwb-decision (P7) | Package model, checksum and version label (DP-04) | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | rwb-access (P4) | Role, scope and right check before a read (AC14) | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |

The eligible-account list is read as the rwb-source-data activity `listEligibleAccounts(businessDate)` in the workflow, not as a REST call.

| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 | caseId | decision code "D6", final call "CASE_CREATED", rule ID, rule version, business date, record reference |

Both are written to the outbox in the same transaction as the state change and relayed with the CloudEvents envelope; no personal data is carried (DP-09).

| Name | Type | Task queue | Purpose |

| rebalance | Activity | `rwb-case` | Rebalances a queue (owned by RWB-P3-E1020-APP) |
| EvaluateRules | Activity (workflow kit) | `rwb-case` | Calls the embedded Drools kit with a package code, facts and the business date |
| RecordAndApply | Activity (workflow kit) | `rwb-case` | Writes the decision record, the state change and the outbox rows in one transaction |

| Schedule | Cadence | Trigger | Legacy reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| DailyCaseRun | Daily, when the ALS batch for the business date completes, with a daily fallback | AceDataReady (EV-26) plus a Temporal Schedule with overlap policy SKIP and a catch-up window | JOB-02 Case creation |
| Allocation step inside DailyCaseRun | After case creation, by 07:00 | DailyCaseRun step | JOB-03 Morning allocation (RWB-P3-E1020-APP) |
