The seven criteria are new and test only the deliverable in the title: the case-creation entry of the ledger, its refusals, its repeat rule, its read and its chain answer. The legacy criteria of RWB-E1-018 are owned elsewhere: AC1, AC3, AC4, AC7, AC8, AC11, AC12 and AC15 are created, numbered and held by rwb-case (RWB-P3-E1018-APP); the ACE read behind them is rwb-source-data (RWB-P1-E1018-APP); AC14 is the access decision of rwb-access (RWB-P4-E1018-APP); the document binding is rwb-document (RWB-P5-E1018-APP).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One case creation writes one entry: "D6", "CASE_CREATED", the ENTER rule ID, the version label and the ALS business date; a run that creates no case appends no entry | Legacy flow step 11 and BR8; REQ-CWC-016; FSD P7 AC-P7-002-01 |
| BR2 | The rule ID and its version label travel together; a record with one and not the other is refused with MSG-P7-009 naming the field | FSD P7 AC-EXC-P7-002-01; BR-P7-003 |
| BR3 | The decision code is a value of LOV-DECISION read through DP-07 with the version in force; a code outside the list is refused and no code is a constant of the code | TSD P7 T3.1 DF-DEC-003; FSD P7 AC-EXC-P7-002-05; principle 1 |
| BR4 | The profile accepts a version label only when `rule_package_version` holds it for package ENTRY; a label that is not held is refused, and no default and no label in force is substituted | Legacy BR13; R-UNI-41; Arch v5 slide 27 |
| BR5 | The ledger is append-only and hash-chained: `prev_hash` is the `entry_hash` of the entry before it, the first is 64 zeros, no entry is updated or deleted, and a refused record uses no `chain_seq` | FSD P7 AC-P7-001-01 and AC-ALT-P7-001-01; RWB-P7-E1008-APP |
| BR6 | The append is the seal: it writes no further record and publishes no event | Arch v5 slide 28; ADR-022 |
| BR7 | The entry carries `decided_at`, the producing service identity, and an inputs reference that names the ALS business date; no case attribute is copied | TSD P7 T3.1 DF-DEC-008, DF-DEC-016, DF-DEC-030; legacy flow step 11 |
| BR8 | A repeat of the event ID appends nothing, answers the first entry ID and moves the repeat count by one | Legacy AC8; FSD P7 AC-EXC-P7-002-03; R-UNI-40 |
| BR9 | An entry that does not match the chain is answered with `chainVerified` false and the MSG-P7-012 warning, an incident is raised, and the stored row is untouched | FSD P7 AC-P7-001-01; TSD P7 NFR-035 |
| BR10 | A store that cannot be appended or read blocks the case creation: nothing is committed, no entry is invented, MSG-P7-003 is answered and the record waits in the producer's outbox | Principle 5; FSD P7 VR-P7-001-2 and AC-EXC-P7-001-01 |
| BR11 | The case reference is a business key: no foreign key to `rwb_case`, no case attribute column in `rwb_decision`, no `rwb_case` table read, and a reference with no case row is kept as it arrived | D-RCV-35 U4; ADR-010; legacy BR11; DP-01 |
| BR12 | The read applies Decision log R and the caller's scope before any entry value is answered, and a refusal answers no case attribute | TSD P7 T6.1 and T6.2; legacy AC14 |

How the rules hold: `CaseCreationRecordProfile` executes BR1 to BR4 before any append, reading LOV-DECISION through DP-07 and the registry hold from its own schema, and answering MSG-P7-009 with the field. The appender and the append-only trigger of RWB-P7-E1008-APP execute BR5 and BR7 in one transaction with the next `chain_seq`. BR6 is the shape of the append. BR8 is the inbox row on the event ID. BR9 is `CreationEntryChainCheck` on the answered entry. BR10 is the caller's transaction and its outbox. BR11 is the schema, and BR12 is the controller guard and the scope filter it reads from the template cache.

##### 9. State transitions

This story owns no case state and no rule-version state machine; it owns the admission of a case-creation record and the answer for one entry.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| (none) | `DecisionRecorded` (EV-08) for a case creation | The record passes the profile and its event ID is new | One `decision_log_entry` row appended at the next `chain_seq` |
| (none) | the same event ID arrives again | The inbox holds the event ID | No row appended; the first entry ID is answered; the repeat count moves by one |
| (none) | half a rule reference, a label the registry does not hold, or a code outside LOV-DECISION | A profile check fails | No row; MSG-P7-009 naming the field; `chain_seq` not used |
| (none) | the store is unavailable | The append or the read cannot run | No row; MSG-P7-003; the producer's outbox retries |

A version state is read here and changed only by the registry stories: a label is acceptable when the registry holds it, and this story makes no state move of its own.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The rwb-decision service identity (the per-service login of DP-02) | Consumes the record, applies the profile, calls the appender and answers the case-creation read; holds no grant on `rwb_case` |
| RW-RISK, RW-AUDIT and every role with Decision log R (RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-RESTRUCT, RW-LITOFF and the other RW roles of TSD P7 T6.1) | Read the creation entry of a case in scope with its rule ID, rule version, inputs reference, hash and `chainVerified`; the approval of a version is RW-RISK's in RWB-P7-E1073-APP, not here |
| SY-CASEWF, case workflow module | Produces the record of a case creation on its own contract (Decision log C), which this service consumes; it writes no ledger row |
| SY-RULES, Drools evaluator | Evaluates ENTRY and EXCLUSION in rwb-case and stamps the rule ID and version on the record (DP-04); it evaluates nothing in this service |
| The registry owner of RWB-P7-E1073-APP | Holds and moves the version labels the profile tests against; this story reads them and changes none |
| A caller whose role holds no Decision log R | Refused with MSG-P4-002 on the read; the legacy refusal of the case read under Case record R is RWB-P4-E1018-APP's |

No person is named anywhere: the actors are roles, service identities and the caller of a contract.

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-DEC-001 | decision_log_entry | id | Write |
| DF-DEC-002 | decision_log_entry | case_id (the case reference, a business key) | Write; read; indexed, no foreign key |
| DF-DEC-003, DF-DEC-012 | decision_log_entry | decision_code ("D6", LOV-DECISION), final_call ("CASE_CREATED") | Write; read |
| DF-DEC-004, DF-DEC-005 | decision_log_entry | rule_id (the ENTER rule ID), rule_version ("ENTRY-2026.11") | Write; read |
| DF-DEC-008, DF-DEC-016 | decision_log_entry | inputs_ref (carries the ALS business date 2026-12-01), decided_at | Write; read |
| DF-DEC-017, DF-DEC-018, DF-DEC-028 | decision_log_entry | prev_hash, entry_hash, chain_seq | Write; read |
| DF-DEC-030, DF-DEC-031 | decision_log_entry | actor_user_id (the producing service identity), idempotency_key (the event ID) | Write; read |
| DF-REF-275 | rule_package | package_code ("ENTRY") | Read |
| DF-REF-281, DF-REF-282 | rule_package_version | version_label, status | Read |
| DF-REF-297 | rule_row | drools_rule_name (the rule ID, for example "EXCL-004") | Read, for the label the record cites |

Field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 and TSD P7 v2 T3.1. `decision_log_entry` is P7's in `rwb_decision`, and no other service reads it (DP-01). The TSD still models `case_id` as a uuid in a relationship with `recovery_case` and gives the row no business-date column, so in the target the case reference is an indexed business key with no foreign key and the ALS business date travels inside `inputs_ref` (GAP-2435; ASM-4044). `DF-DEC-006` and `DF-DEC-007` stay empty on a case-creation entry: a creation reads no model and no agent. The literal value of the ENTER rule ID of package ENTRY is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2436; ASM-4045); the entry carries the rule ID the published record carried. No case row, no ACE row and no `v_ace_*` view is read or copied here.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner `rwb-decision` (P7); base `/api/recovery/decision/v1`. The path is API-P7-006 of TSD P7 v2 T-A.1, which RWB-P7-E2005-APP delivers as the audit query. This story provides the `finalCall=CASE_CREATED` filter on that path and the case-creation profile fields of the answer, and it owns neither the screen nor the export. The filter parameter and the profile field list are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2434; ASM-4043).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/decision-log?caseId={caseId}&finalCall=CASE_CREATED` | Answer the case-creation entry of one case with `entryId`, `caseRef`, `decisionCode`, `finalCall`, `ruleId`, `ruleVersion`, `inputsRef`, `decidedAt`, `actorUserId`, `prevHash`, `entryHash`, `chainSeq` and `chainVerified`; 200 | Decision log R, scope applied | Not applicable, read only |

Errors: 401 no session; 403 the role lacks Decision log R (MSG-P4-002) or the case is outside the scope (MSG-P4-003); 404 no case-creation entry for the case; 503 the store is unavailable (MSG-P7-003). The answer is a page of `DecisionLogPage` of TSD P7 T-A.2 with the filter applied, and `chainVerified` is added per entry as FSD P3 AC-EXC-P3-037-01 requires. The search by case, rule, approver and date, the saved filters, the export and the audit population read are RWB-P7-E2005-APP's.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 rwb-case, on RWB-P3-E1043-CON | LOV-DECISION with the value "D6" and its version in force, for the decision-code check of the profile (DP-07); faked, one hop, 2 s (DP-11) |

This is the only operation this story calls. The scope filter is the cached permission decision the service template holds from rwb-access, so no case read is made; RWB-P3-E1018-CON defines the case ID value the record cites and supplies its fake, and it is not called at run time.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The append of a ledger entry writes no further record and publishes no event, because the ledger is the seal (BR6). The events of this service belong to other stories: `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` (EV-30, RWB-P7-E1073-APP) and the records of the writer (RWB-P7-E1027-APP).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Producer | Key | What this story does with it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | rwb-case, when it creates a case | entryId, with the event ID and idempotency key held by the inbox | Applies `CaseCreationRecordProfile` and hands a passing record to the appender of RWB-P7-E1008-APP; a record for another decision is that story's to append, and a repeat appends nothing (DP-03, DP-09) |

The payload is the record shape of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and the fields of TSD P7 T3.1, mapped one to one with no added field. No event carries a name, an e-mail address, a mobile number, an account number or any other personal value.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The ingest is a Kafka listener with an inbox and a dead-letter topic, not a workflow; the read is synchronous REST; the chain check is `CreationEntryChainCheck` on the answered entry, not an activity. The promote workflow of JOB-20 is RWB-P7-E1073-APP's, and the evaluation of ENTRY and EXCLUSION is an activity in rwb-case (DP-04).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The three jobs of this service belong to other stories: JOB-13, the continuous ingest, is RWB-P7-E1008-APP's; JOB-14, the 02:00 chain check, is RWB-P7-E1008-APP's; JOB-20, the 00:01 promotion, is RWB-P7-E1073-APP's. The legacy JOB-02, the case-creation job that raises the record, becomes the event-started workflow of rwb-case (DP-10).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|
| `decision_log_entry` | P7 (`rwb_decision`) | The creation entry: appended through the baseline of RWB-P7-E1008-APP and read by the profile read |
| `rule_package`, `rule_package_version` | P7 (`rwb_decision`) | The package row of ENTRY and the version label and state that answer whether a cited label is held |
| `rule_row` | P7 (`rwb_decision`) | The rule ID a label carries, read only to name the rule the record cites |
| `outbox_event`, `processed_event`, `idempotency_key` | PLT library, created in `rwb_decision` | The inbox of `DecisionRecorded` and the idempotency rows of the ingest (DP-09) |

Not owned and not read: every `rwb_case` table (no foreign key, no read, BR11), every `v_ace_*` view (DP-05; this service reads no ACE data), `approval` and `delegation_limit` (P7, but the stories of RWB-P7-E2013-APP), `rule_test_case` (RWB-P7-E1073-APP writes it) and the retired data-lake copies (DP-17). No foreign key crosses a schema.

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-case reference-data and contract fake | RWB-P3-E1043-CON and RWB-P3-E1018-CON | LOV-DECISION with "D6" and its version in force, without "D99"; the synthetic case `RW-2026-000123` for borrower `P-0101` and account `A-5001` |
| decision-record topic fixture | RWB-PLT-E1027-CON | The creation record of `RW-2026-000123`; a record of `RW-2026-000124` with the rule ID and no label; a record with code "D99"; a record of `RW-2026-000125` citing "ENTRY-2026.12"; a repeat of event `EV-7f3a-0001` |
| ledger and registry fixtures | RWB-P7-E1008-APP and RWB-P7-E1073-APP | The append at the next `chain_seq`, the append-only refusal, the 64-zero first `prev_hash`, a forced append failure and the entry at `chain_seq` 230 changed with the trigger disabled; "ENTRY-2026.11" of ENTRY in force, and no "ENTRY-2026.12" until AC3 loads it |

Each fake is replaced by the real contract or the real library as its story lands, without a change to the scenarios. All values are the legacy story's synthetic keys, package codes, version labels and states.

| REST | Provided 1, consumed 1 | The case-creation filter of the ledger read; the LOV-DECISION list read, one hop and 2 s |
| Kafka | Consumed 1 event type, published 0 | `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` from rwb-case; the append publishes nothing |

| File | None | This story reads and writes no file |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision`, module `creation`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision.creation`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or the recovery schema | Owner's schema `rwb_decision`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-02 | `recovery_svc` login | One login per service | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.decision.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

This is a secondary slice with no owned legacy acceptance criterion of a build story: it adds no build dependency of its own (metadata "Depends on (build)" is None; GAP-2437; ASM-4046) and builds against the baseline of RWB-P7-E1008-APP, the record library of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and the registry rows of RWB-P7-E1073-APP. DP-01 and DP-02 are the target shape itself. DP-03 is the record shape this profile reads. DP-04 applies as a prohibition plus one reference: the packages are versioned by rwb-decision and evaluated in rwb-case with the kit of RWB-PLT-E1072-CON, and the profile only asks whether a label is held. DP-05 is a prohibition, because this service reads no ACE view. DP-06 adds nothing here, since the only tunable is an observability setting. DP-07 is the LOV-DECISION read. DP-09 is the inbox of the ingest. DP-10 is recorded and not built: the legacy JOB-02 becomes rwb-case's event-started workflow, and this service's schedules belong to the two stories named in 12.6. DP-11 is the list read. DP-13, DP-14 and DP-15 are the base, the names and the migration `V1018_2__case_creation_profile.sql`. DP-19 is the composite route behind SCR-38.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| CaseCreationRecordProfile | Service | Applies BR1 to BR4 to a `CASE_CREATED` record before any append and answers the field of a refusal |
| RegistryHoldRepository | Repository | Answers whether `rule_package_version` holds a label for package ENTRY, and the rule ID behind it; reads only `rwb_decision` |
| CaseCreationLogController | Controller | Serves the `finalCall=CASE_CREATED` filter of the ledger read with the Decision log R guard, the scope filter and the problem mapping |
| CreationEntryChainCheck | Service | Recomputes the hash of the answered entry, sets `chainVerified`, answers MSG-P7-012 on a break and raises the Compliance incident |
| ReferenceDataClient | Client | The LOV-DECISION read of 12.2, one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker |

**Database and migrations.** Writes `decision_log_entry` and the library objects in `rwb_decision` through the baseline of RWB-P7-E1008-APP; reads `rule_package`, `rule_package_version` and `rule_row` in the same schema; reads no other schema and holds no foreign key into another schema. One migration in the per-service Flyway sequence of DP-15, `V1018_2__case_creation_profile.sql`, adds the partial index on `(case_id, final_call)` that serves the creation read; it adds no column, no constraint across schemas and no seed row.

**Configuration and reference data.** No business value is configured here: the decision code comes from LOV-DECISION with its version, the final call from the record shape, the version labels and rule IDs from the registry, and the case reference from the record. Two settings only: the base of the rwb-case reference-data contract and the `rwb-decision` service identity of DP-02. The feature switch `rwb.p7.creation.profile` holds the profile off in an environment where the registry is not yet loaded: the ledger stays readable, no creation entry is admitted, and the records wait in the producers' outboxes.

**Build steps**

1. `RegistryHoldRepository` over `rule_package`, `rule_package_version` and `rule_row` in `rwb_decision`; tests for AC3.
2. `CaseCreationRecordProfile` with the five checks and the refusals naming the field, including the LOV-DECISION read; tests for AC1, AC2 and AC3.
3. The ingest hook into the listener of RWB-P7-E1008-APP with the inbox dedupe and the first-entry-ID answer; test for AC4.
4. `CaseCreationLogController` with the `finalCall` filter, the guard, the scope filter, the 404 and the 503; tests for AC1, AC5 and AC6.
5. `CreationEntryChainCheck` with the recomputation, the `chainVerified` flag, the MSG-P7-012 warning and the Compliance incident; test for AC7.
6. The privacy test: the topic fixture, the entry and the answer hold IDs, codes, labels, dates and hashes only, and no name, e-mail address, mobile number, national identity number or account number.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass; a SIT week shows one entry per case creation with "D6", "CASE_CREATED", the ENTER rule ID and "ENTRY-2026.11"; no case attribute column in `rwb_decision`; no foreign key to `rwb_case`; a label the registry does not hold refused with the field named; one entry on a repeated event; and a chain break reported with MSG-P7-012 while the stored row is unchanged.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-009 | Half a rule reference, a version label the registry does not hold, or a decision code outside LOV-DECISION | The message text is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2433; ASM-4042); the detail names the field, "ruleId", "ruleVersion" or "decisionCode" |
| MSG-P7-012 | An answered entry does not match the chain | The warning text is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2433; ASM-4042); the warning names the entry's `chainSeq` |
| MSG-P7-003 | The ledger store is unavailable for an append or a read | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller's role holds no Decision log R | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The entry's case sits outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. |

Every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set, `detail` carrying the text with its placeholders filled, and `instance` naming the request. For MSG-P4-002 the {action} value names the action the caller tried, "read the decision log of this case", and never a case fact. A refusal never echoes the rule ID, the version label or the case reference of another tenant's case.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-38 Decision log query shows the entries with their decision code, rule ID, rule version, final call, actor, decided time and `chainVerified`, and the decision list of a case shows the same entries for one case, both through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). This slice fixes only what the read answers for a case creation and the MSG-P7-012 warning on a row that does not verify. The screen, its filters, its saved searches, its export and its loading, empty and filtered states are RWB-P7-E2005-APP's, first in Epic 2. The creation entry has no screen of its own inside this service: the reader who wants the basis of a case sees it on that query, and the case owner sees the same entry on the case decision list of SCR-03, which rwb-case and rwb-decision serve through the composite route.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the decision code is a value of LOV-DECISION read with its version, the final call is a value of the record shape, and the version labels and rule IDs are registry rows; the case reference is a value of the record.
- No personal data in events, workflow inputs, logs, tests or answers. The record, the entry and the answer carry IDs, codes, labels, dates and hashes only; no name, address, identity number or account number is logged, and a refused record is logged with the case reference and the field only.
- No cross-schema read (DP-01), and ACE data only through the owner's contract or `v_ace_*` views, which this service reads neither (DP-05): `rwb_decision` reads no `rwb_case` table, holds no foreign key into another schema and holds no case attribute column.
- The ledger is append-only and the chain is checked on read into the answer only: this service has no update and no delete path on `decision_log_entry`, and a read never rewrites an entry, never renumbers a `chain_seq` and never deletes a row to satisfy a scope.
- One evaluator decides every ENTRY and EXCLUSION outcome and it is not here: the profile asks whether a label is held and never evaluates a rule, and a version that is not held is a refusal rather than a default.
- The partial index of the migration is the only schema change this story makes, and no topic, event or queue name is typed in code (DP-14).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-018 for rwb-case. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform engineer**, I want **rwb-case deployed as one service from the service template, with its Helm chart and values, its Flyway migration job, its readiness and liveness probes, its topic and queue provisioning with retry and dead-letter topics, the DailyCaseRun schedule registration, the case-creation dashboards and the runbook, and the legacy batch alerts mapped to the new signals**, so that **the case-creation capability of RWB-E1-018 runs predictably in every environment and an operator can see and act on a failed or late run without reading code**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story depends on a Quartz job, a shared schema and an in-line scheduler. In the target, a service is a Helm release built by one pipeline, with its own schema, login, topic, queue and Schedules (DP-02, DP-10, DP-15). Deployment is therefore part of the capability: an unregistered schedule or a topic without a dead-letter path silently loses case creations, and an alert that only fires on a job exception does not catch a run held by a missing rule package. This story makes the case-creation run observable and repeatable, so the app story can be proven in SIT and the on-call rota can operate it.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template, chart skeleton and pipeline are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-LIB).
- The Temporal workflow kit and the `rwb-recovery` namespace are available (RWB-PLT-WF, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON).
- The Kafka event platform provisions topics with a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON).
- The platform error envelope and the message catalogue are in force, so an alert can carry a message ID.
- The three environments DEV, SIT and UAT exist with the parameter scope of LOV-ENVIRONMENT.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. The pipeline builds the service image, runs the unit and contract tests, scans the image and the dependencies, and publishes the Helm chart version.
2. The chart deploys the service with its own login, its schema migration job and its probes; the migration job runs before the deployment is marked ready.
3. The provisioning step creates `rwb.case.events.v1` with its retry topic and `.dlt` topic, and the Temporal task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery`.
4. The Schedule registration step creates or updates DailyCaseRun with the overlap policy and the catch-up window, and checks that AceDataReady starts the same workflow for the business date.
5. The dashboards are published: run counts, created, excluded, not entered, linked, failed; run duration; event lag; decision-record lag.
6. The alerts are wired to the message IDs of section 14 and to the runbook entries.
7. A smoke step posts a synthetic business date to the DailyCaseRun trigger in a test namespace and checks that the run record and the probe answer are healthy.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The migration job fails | The deployment stays unready and the pipeline stops; no traffic to the new version | None | AC1 |
| X2 | The readiness probe fails after the start-up window | The pod is removed from the service and the pipeline marks the release failed | None | AC3 |
| X3 | The topic is missing its retry or `.dlt` topic | The provisioning step fails the release; the relay refuses to start | None | AC4 |
| X4 | The Schedule registration is rejected by the namespace | The release fails; a case creation would otherwise never start | None | AC5 |
| X5 | A run waits for a complete ALS batch | The alert carries MSG-P1-001 and the runbook entry for the batch gate | MSG-P1-001 | AC6 |
| X6 | The decision-record write fails during a run | The alert carries MSG-P7-003 and the failed-account count | MSG-P7-003 | AC6 |
| X7 | No rule package version is in force | The alert carries MSG-P3-027 and names the package code | MSG-P3-027 | AC6 |
| X8 | The yearly number range is used up | The alert carries MSG-P3-025 and opens an incident | MSG-P3-025 | AC6 |
| X9 | A role without Case record R is refused | The access-denied signal is counted, not alerted as an incident | MSG-P4-002 | AC6 |
| X10 | A case is outside the reader's scope | The out-of-scope count is visible on the dashboard only | MSG-P4-003 | AC6 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the chart skeleton, the platform topic provisioning and the workflow kit; no application code is built here |
| Negotiable | Replica counts, resource sizes and alert thresholds are environment values, not story decisions |
| Valuable | Makes the case-creation run deployable, observable and repeatable in every environment |
| Estimable | One chart, one pipeline stage, one migration job, two probes, one provisioning step, one schedule registration, four dashboards panels and seven alert rules |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the runbook |
| Testable | Every criterion tests an artefact: the chart renders, the probes answer, the topics exist, the schedule is registered, the alerts fire on a synthetic metric |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Deployment of the rwb-case case-creation capability

  Background:
    Given the service template chart and the platform pipeline are in force
    Given the target environment is SIT

  Scenario: AC1 The Helm chart and values deploy rwb-case (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rwb-case Helm chart and its values files
    When the chart is rendered for DEV, SIT and UAT
    Then each render succeeds with the chart version and the image digest pinned
    Then the release declares the rwb-case login and no other service's credential
    Then the migration job runs the per-service Flyway sequence in schema rwb_case before the deployment is marked ready
    Then no replica count, resource size or schedule cadence is hard-coded in the template

  Scenario: AC2 The pipeline builds, tests and promotes one artefact (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a commit on the main line
    When the pipeline runs
    Then it builds one image and one chart version from the same commit
    Then it runs the unit, component and contract tests and fails the build on a contract drift
    Then it scans the image and the dependencies and fails on a critical finding
    Then it promotes the same artefact through DEV, SIT and UAT without a rebuild

  Scenario: AC3 Readiness and liveness probes answer (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a running rwb-case pod
    When the readiness probe is called before the migration job and the start-up window complete
    Then the pod is not marked ready
    When the readiness and liveness endpoints are called after start-up
    Then both answer healthy without a database write
    Then a failing dependency is reported as not ready and never as live-and-broken

  Scenario: AC4 Topics and the task queue are provisioned with retry and dead-letter paths (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the provisioning step for rwb-case
    When it runs against the environment
    Then the topic rwb.case.events.v1 exists with its retry topic and its .dlt topic
    Then the shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1 is consumed as provided by the platform and is not recreated
    Then the Temporal task queue rwb-case is registered in namespace rwb-recovery
    Then the outbox relay and the consumer are configured with the retry topic and the .dlt topic

  Scenario: AC5 The DailyCaseRun schedule is registered and fires (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the Schedule registration step
    When it runs
    Then DailyCaseRun is registered with the daily cadence, the overlap policy SKIP and the catch-up window
    Then a synthetic business date starts one run and a second start for the same business date starts nothing
    Then the run record carries the counts accounts read, excluded, not entered, linked, created and failed

  Scenario: AC6 Dashboards and the runbook cover the legacy alerts (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published dashboard and the runbook
    When a synthetic run is replayed with a late batch, a failed decision record, a missing package version and an exhausted number range
    Then each condition raises the alert that carries MSG-P1-001, MSG-P7-003, MSG-P3-027 and MSG-P3-025 with the legacy text
    Then the refused-read and out-of-scope counts carry MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P4-003 and do not page the on-call rota
    Then every alert links one runbook entry with the check, the owner role and the recovery step
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One service, one schema, one login: the release uses the rwb-case login and no other service's credential | DP-02; Arch v5 slide 41 notes |
| BR2 | The migration is a per-service Flyway sequence in schema rwb_case and runs before the deployment is ready | DP-15; RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| BR3 | Every topic has a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic; a consumer never acknowledges an event it could not process | DP-09; Arch v5 slide 42 notes |
| BR4 | A Temporal Schedule uses overlap policy SKIP with a catch-up window, and an event-started workflow takes the business date as its input | DP-10; Arch v5 slide 44 notes |
| BR5 | No environment value is hard-coded: replica counts, resource sizes, thresholds and cadences come from values files and parameters | DP-06; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR6 | An alert carries a message ID and the agreed text, and links one runbook entry | Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR7 | A refused read and an out-of-scope read are counted on the dashboard and never page the on-call rota | MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003 |
| BR8 | The service writes only schema rwb_case and reads no other service's tables | DP-01 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | Chart published | The image, the chart and the migration job pass the pipeline | Deploying |
| Deploying | Migration job complete and probes healthy | The schema is at the expected version and both probes answer | Ready |
| Ready | Release superseded | A new chart version is promoted | Rolling |
| Rolling | All pods on the new version | The old ReplicaSet drains | Ready |
| Ready | Migration job failed | The schema is not at the expected version | Failed |
| Failed | Rollback | The previous chart version is redeployed and the migration is reversed by its own script | Ready |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |

| DevOps engineer | Owns the chart, the values files, the pipeline stages, the provisioning and schedule registration steps, the dashboards and the runbook |
| Platform administrator | Owns the `rwb-recovery` namespace, the topic provisioning and the Schedule registration rights |
| ACE database administrator | Owns the rwb_case schema, the login and its grants, and approves the migration job |
| Release manager | Approves the promotion of one artefact through the environments |
| On-call operator | Runs the runbook entries and opens an incident when MSG-P3-025 or MSG-P7-003 persists |
| RW-PLATADM | Reads and operates the case-creation run in the running service, not in the cluster |

The per-service login name used by the chart is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0675; ASM-1222); the chart references "the rwb-case login (DP-02)" through a secret reference and never a literal name.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

The deployment exposes the four case operations of the contract baseline behind gateway-bff: `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases`, `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}`, `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/accounts` and `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/parties`. Owner rwb-case (P3). The probes are cluster-internal and are not part of the API surface.

| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | Access check before a read |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-models/{n}/{v}` | P7 rwb-decision | Package model and checksum |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-02 | `recovery_svc` login | One login per service | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Artefacts**

| Artefact | Content |
|---|---|
| `helm/rwb-case/` | Chart with deployment, service, migration job, config map, secret references, probes and the Schedule registration hook |
| `helm/rwb-case/values-dev.yaml`, `values-sit.yaml`, `values-uat.yaml` | Image digest, replicas, resources, probe timings, log level, feature switches, environment name |
| Pipeline stage | Build, unit and contract tests, image and dependency scan, chart publish, promote the same artefact |
| Provisioning step | Topic `rwb.case.events.v1` with retry and `.dlt`, consumer groups, task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery` |
| Schedule registration | DailyCaseRun with cadence, overlap policy SKIP and catch-up window; idempotent create or update |
| Dashboards | Run counts, run duration, event lag, decision-record lag, refused and out-of-scope reads |
| Alerts | Seven rules, each with a message ID and one runbook entry |
| Runbook | Six entries: batch gate, decision record failure, package not in force, number range exhausted, migration failure, probe failure |

**Probes.** Readiness answers healthy only when the migration is at the expected schema version, the outbox relay is running and the Temporal worker has polled; liveness answers healthy when the process is up and its internal loop is responsive. Neither probe writes to the database. Exact paths and timings are values (GAP-0677).

**Migration job.** Runs the per-service Flyway sequence for schema rwb_case with the rwb-case login, as a pre-deploy job with a backoff limit; a failed job blocks the rollout and the release.

**Alert mapping carried over from the legacy story.**

| Message ID | Condition | Alert | Route |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-001 | DailyCaseRun waiting for a complete ALS batch | Batch gate alert with product and date fields | Platform on-call, ticket |
| MSG-P7-003 | Decision record write failed for an account | Failed-account alert with the count and the run ID | Platform on-call, page |
| MSG-P3-027 | No ENTRY or EXCLUSION version is in force | Package-in-force alert naming the package code | Business on-call (RW-COE), page |
| MSG-P3-025 | Yearly case number range used up | Number-range alert with the year and an incident | Platform administrator, incident |
| MSG-P4-002 | Read without Case record R | Refused-read count on the dashboard | No page |
| MSG-P4-003 | Case outside the reader's scope | Out-of-scope count on the dashboard | No page |

The WP line lists the number-range message as MVG-P3-025; the message ID in the legacy story and in the message catalogue is MSG-P3-025, which is the ID used above.

**Done when.** The chart renders in all three environments, the pipeline promotes one artefact, the probes answer, the topic and queue provisioning is verified by a test, the Schedule is registered and fires once per business date, the six alerts fire on synthetic metrics and the runbook entries are reviewed by the on-call rota.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-001 | DailyCaseRun waiting for a complete ALS batch | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |
| MSG-P3-027 | No ENTRY or EXCLUSION version is in force on the business date | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Decision record write failed for an account | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P3-025 | Yearly case number range used up | Case numbers for {year} are used up. New cases are on hold until the range is extended. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Read without Case record R | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | Case outside the reader's scope | This case is not in your scope. |

The texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story; the deployment adds the alert routing and the runbook link, never a new wording.

##### 15. Screens and states

The deployment serves the two screens of the capability: SCR-02 Case list (Loading; empty; list; filtered) and SCR-03 Case record (Loading; read only), behind the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The operator-facing surfaces of this story are the pipeline run view, the release view, the dashboard and the runbook. The composite route specification and the screen field list are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0674; ASM-1221); the deployment only registers the route target and the health check of the case endpoints.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a values file: the entry threshold, the exclusion reasons, the bands and the status list are parameters and reference data, never a deployment value.
- No personal data in logs, dashboard series, alert payloads or the runbook: run counts, IDs and durations only.
- One login per service; the chart carries the rwb-case login reference and no other service's credential (DP-02).
- The service writes only schema rwb_case; the migration job never touches another schema (DP-01).
- Every topic has a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic, and the consumer dedupes through the inbox (DP-09).
- The release pins the image digest and the chart version; a rebuild between environments is not allowed.
- No secret is written into a values file, a chart template, a dashboard or the runbook; all secrets come from the platform secret store.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: integration slice of RWB-E1-018 for RWB-ITG-W1. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **QA integration engineer**, I want **the end-to-end proof of the RWB-E1-018 case creation and case record across rwb-source-data (P1), rwb-case (P3), rwb-access (P4), rwb-document (P5) and rwb-decision (P7)**, so that **the batch gate, the case-created event, the missing-view-row path and the package-in-force refusal are proved on real services before wave 1 exits**.

##### 2. Business rationale

RWB-E1-018 creates one recovery case per customer and product at 90 days past due, and every later team, letter and document refers to that case number. The component copy of the behaviour already exists: RWB-P3-E1018-APP owns the legacy criteria AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC10, AC11, AC12 and AC14 in rwb-case, against the published contracts of the services it needs. This integration story owns the four criteria that a single service cannot prove: AC1 (the case is created at the threshold and the creation is announced), AC9 (nothing is created before the ALS batch for the business date is complete), AC13 (a business key with no view row is listed and never invented) and AC15 (no EXCLUSION package in force holds creation for the whole date).

The batch gate is a fact about rwb-source-data, not about rwb-case: the readiness signal, the freshness stamp and the AceDataReady event are produced by the source-data owner, and rwb-case only reacts to them. The case-created fact is a cross-service fact in the same way: the case row commits in rwb-case, the event leaves on the owner's topic and the decision is recorded in the central ledger of rwb-decision, and an assertion on any one of those three alone would pass while the other two were wrong. A missing view row is found by the source-data data quality check, while the link that must not be invented lives in rwb-case. None of the four can be proved inside one service.

The target delta is named in GAP-0343 and ASM-0437. The legacy AC1 publishes the in-process `caseCreated` and the legacy section 12 writes the decision log inside P3; in the target the creation publishes `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1` on `rwb.case.events.v1` (CloudEvents, key caseId) and the decision is recorded in rwb-decision through the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03), asserted through the P7 contract. REC-05, the check that every key resolves to its ACE view row, is a data-quality exception owned by rwb-source-data, so the harness reads its output rather than a P3 table. No service contract is faked in this story: the eight integration dependencies are the real services on their published contracts, and a fake would defeat the purpose of the run.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P1-E1001-APP is done: the recovery tables for the data products, the ACE view contract and the freshness of the ALS data product are in place in rwb_source_data.
- RWB-P1-E1016-APP is done: the ACE source query and its boundary are published, so the account, customer and relation facts are read by the owner and exposed through the P1 contract.
- RWB-P1-E1069-APP is done: the data products, their freshness and the readiness call for a business date are published.
- RWB-P3-E1018-APP is done: case creation exists in rwb-case, with the gate on the readiness signal, the one-case-per-customer-and-product rule, the number issuance and the case read operations.
- RWB-P5-E1018-APP is done: the case document links are created and read through the rwb-document contract.
- RWB-P1-E1018-APP is done: the intake and the reconciliation that produce the missing-key list for the data steward are published.
- RWB-P4-E1018-APP is done: the Case record right and its refusal are enforced by rwb-access.
- RWB-P7-E1018-APP is done: the rule-package version list, the rollback and the central decision ledger are published, and the ENTRY and EXCLUSION packages are loaded and approved.
- The published contracts of P1, P3, P4, P5 and P7 are versioned in the registry, and the harness consumes only those contracts.
- The harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG is available with its synthetic ALS batch and its synthetic case set.
- The SIT environment is available with the Temporal namespace `rwb-recovery`, the topics of the wave-1 services with their retry and `.dlt` topics, the schema registry and the rule packages of the run.
- No production data is read, copied or connected to; every account, customer, person, account key and case number used by the run is synthetic.
- The release date 30 November 2026 is tentative and is copied unchanged.

##### 4. Flow

1. QA integration engineer: seeds the ACE batch rows for the business date and the synthetic accounts, customers and relations of the RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG set through the harness; no service schema is opened and no production row is used.
2. Harness: publishes the readiness signal for the business date by calling `POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/business-days/{date}/ready`, in the same way the Airflow readiness stub does.
3. Harness: consumes `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` on `rwb.source-data.events.v1` and confirms that the DailyCaseRun workflow started on queue `rwb-case` for that business date.
4. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness` and confirms that the ALS data product for the business date is fresh before any case is asserted.
5. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases` with the case-number search, then `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` and `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/accounts`; it asserts status "NEW", no stage code, the entry date, the primary person key and the account link with `is_primary` true.
6. Harness: consumes `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1` on `rwb.case.events.v1` and asserts the CloudEvents envelope, the key caseId, case number RW-2026-000123, product group, accounts and business date, and that no personal data field is present.
7. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` for the case and asserts one record with decision code "D6", final call "CASE_CREATED", the ENTRY rule ID, the package version "ENTRY-2026.11" and the ALS business date; it also consumes `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` for the same creation.
8. Harness, AC9: seeds a second business date 2026-12-02 whose batch row is at status "RUNNING", runs the cut-off check, asserts that no case exists for that date and that the job monitor shows MSG-P1-001, then publishes readiness for 2026-12-02 and asserts that the cases appear.
9. Harness, AC13: takes the synthetic row of account A-5013 and person P-0105 out of the source set through the P1 data set, runs the next intake, asserts that no case and no party link is created, that the existing links of case RW-2026-000126 are unchanged, and that the reconciliation output lists both keys for the data steward.
10. Harness, AC15: reads `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-packages/EXCLUSION/versions`, rolls the EXCLUSION package back with `POST /api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/rollback`, publishes readiness for a new date, asserts that no case is created and that the job record carries MSG-P3-027 with package code "EXCLUSION", then promotes "EXCL-2026.11" again, asserts that creation resumes, and cleans up the synthetic set.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The ALS batch for the business date is still RUNNING at the cut-off | DailyCaseRun does not start for that date, no case is created and the job monitor shows the waiting line for the data product and the date | MSG-P1-001 | AC9 |
| X2 | No EXCLUSION package version is in force on the business date | Creation is held for the whole date, no case exists and the job record names the package-in-force check with the package code | MSG-P3-027 | AC15 |
| X3 | A business key on a case link or in the intake has no row in the source view | No case and no party link is created from the missing row, the existing link is unchanged, and the reconciliation output lists the key | None | AC13 |
| X4 | AceDataReady is delivered twice for the same business date | The consumer inbox ignores the second delivery, the run creates no second case or link, and every account shows one case link | None | AC1, TC-E1-018-08-ITG |
| X5 | The yearly case number range is used up | No case is created for the account, the job record carries the range line with the year and an incident goes to the platform administrator | MSG-P3-025 | TC-E1-018-11-ITG, owned by RWB-P3-E1018-APP |
| X6 | The decision of the creation cannot be recorded | No case exists for the account, the run reports the account as failed and the account is taken again in the next run | MSG-P7-003 | TC-E1-018-10-ITG, owned by RWB-P3-E1018-APP |
| X7 | A consumed contract drifts from the published one (path, field, status or event schema) | The preflight fails on the contract test and the run stops before any assertion; the drift is reported against the owning service and no fake is put in its place | None | Preflight, AC1 |
| X8 | The W1J01 synthetic set, or the ACE batch fixture in it, is missing or does not match the run | The run fails as a fixture fault and names the missing element; no production value is substituted | None | AC1, AC9 |
| X9 | No earlier EXCLUSION version can be rolled back to, or the rollback is refused | The rollback step fails and the run stops; the version in force is reported and creation is not asserted | MSG-P3-027 | AC15 |
| X10 | A suite step tries to read a service schema directly | The step does not exist: the suite is built with no client for a service schema, and the pipeline scan fails any change that adds one | None | Section 17 |

X1 to X3 and X9 are the legacy exception paths carried onto the real services; X4 to X8 are the cross-service failures that only appear when the run leaves one service; X10 is the guardrail of section 17 in testable form.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | The suite is a module of its own and reuses the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG; it needs the eight integration dependencies and the published contracts of P1, P3, P4, P5 and P7, not their source code, and it owns no schema and no table |
| Negotiable | The fixture composition, the poll interval, the cut-off time and the report layout are configuration; the gate behaviour, the message IDs, the case number and the package versions are fixed by the legacy story |
| Valuable | Proves across services what no single service story can prove: the batch gate, one case per customer and product, one CaseCreated event per creation, one decision record in the central ledger, the missing-view-row path and the package-in-force refusal |
| Estimable | One suite module, one fixture builder, four contract probes, one gate control, one rollback step and one report |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the report |
| Testable | Every criterion is asserted on an observable: a REST response, a Kafka event, a workflow result, a ledger record or a data-quality list |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Case ID issuance and case record v1, proven across the wave 1 services

  Background:
    Given parameter "case.entry.dpd" is 90
    Given package ENTRY version "ENTRY-2026.11" is in force
    Given package EXCLUSION version "EXCL-2026.11" is in force
    Given the business date is 2026-12-01
    Given v_ace_batch_status holds the ALS batch for 2026-12-01 with status "COMPLETED" and is_complete true
    Given all involved services are deployed in SIT with published contracts
    Given the RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG synthetic set is loaded

  Scenario: AC1 Case created at 90 days past due (legacy RWB-E1-018 AC1)
    Given v_ace_account holds account A-5001 with product_category "HIRE_PURCHASE", days_past_due 90 and data_as_of 2026-12-01, with no exclusion
    Given v_ace_ca_relation holds person_key P-0101 on account A-5001 as "BORROWER" and v_ace_customer holds P-0101
    Given the last case number issued in 2026 is RW-2026-000122
    When AceDataReady is raised for ALS and 2026-12-01 and JOB-02 runs
    Then case RW-2026-000123 exists with status "NEW", no stage code, entry date 2026-12-01 and primary_person_key P-0101
    Then case_account holds account_key A-5001 on that case with is_primary true
    Then case_party holds person_key P-0101 as "BORROWER"
    Then the system publishes caseCreated with case number RW-2026-000123

  Scenario: AC9 No cases before the ALS batch is complete (legacy RWB-E1-018 AC9)
    Given v_ace_batch_status shows the ALS batch for 2026-12-02 with status "RUNNING" at the 09:00 cut-off
    When the morning check runs
    Then JOB-02 does not start for 2026-12-02
    Then the job monitor shows MSG-P1-001 for "DP01 Account and arrears" with date 2026-12-01
    Then JOB-02 starts for 2026-12-02 when AceDataReady is raised for ALS and 2026-12-02

  Scenario: AC13 A key with no view row is listed, never invented (legacy RWB-E1-018 AC13)
    Given case RW-2026-000126 links account_key A-5013 and person_key P-0105
    Given v_ace_account has no row for A-5013 on 2026-12-01 and v_ace_customer has no row for P-0105
    When JOB-02 runs for 2026-12-01 and the intake reads the case links
    Then the system creates no case and no party link from a missing view row
    Then case RW-2026-000126 keeps its existing links unchanged
    Then REC-05 lists account_key A-5013 and person_key P-0105 for the data steward and the ACE team
    Then both keys are read again on the next complete ALS batch

  Scenario: AC15 No EXCLUSION package in force holds creation (legacy RWB-E1-018 AC15)
    Given no EXCLUSION version is in force on 2026-12-01
    When AceDataReady is raised for ALS and 2026-12-01 and JOB-02 runs
    Then the system creates no case for 2026-12-01
    Then the job record carries MSG-P3-027 for the package in force check with package code "EXCLUSION"
    Then the accounts are taken again when an EXCLUSION version is in force
```

**Target reading.** The source views are read only by rwb-source-data and are asserted here through the P1 contract and its freshness stamp; the suite opens no view and no service schema. The case-created event is the Kafka event `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1` on `rwb.case.events.v1` in the CloudEvents envelope, key caseId, not the in-process `caseCreated` of the legacy criterion. The decision record of a creation is asserted through the P7 contract on `rwb.decision-record.v1` and the P7 decision-log read; the EXCLUSION rollback of AC15 is the P7 admin path, which is the one-call rollback of the rule design. No service table is read and no value is invented (GAP-0343; ASM-0437).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | An account enters recovery when `days_past_due` in `v_ace_account` for the ACE business date is at or above the entry threshold and package ENTRY returns ENTER | Parameter case.entry.dpd = 90; package ENTRY; DL16; DF-ACE-018 |
| BR2 | One case per borrower `person_key` and product group, with every qualifying account linked by `account_key` | DL17; REQ-CWC-003 |
| BR3 | An account matching an EXCLUSION rule gets no case; the reason, rule ID and package version are recorded in `case_entry_exclusion` | Package EXCLUSION; REQ-CWC-004 |
| BR4 | The case number is RW, the entry year and a six-digit number from a yearly sequence; it is issued once and never reused | recovery_case.case_no (DF-CAS-002); uk_recovery_case |
| BR5 | A new case has status NEW and no owner until allocation | casemodel.txt Case status "New" |
| BR6 | Status values are read from the list, not from code | LOV-CASE-STATUS; Principle 1 |
| BR7 | No case is created before the ALS batch for the business date is COMPLETED in `v_ace_batch_status`. A late or failed batch raises AceDataLate (EV-27), and the case is created on the next complete batch | CTL-02; JOB-02 "No cases from an incomplete day"; RWB-E1-015 |
| BR8 | Every case creation writes its decision log entry, with the ENTRY rule ID and package version, in the same transaction; a failed write rolls the creation back | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; REQ-CWC-016 |
| BR9 | Exposure band is set from the total outstanding at entry using the band table in force | recovery_case.exposure_band (DF-CAS-015); LOV-EXPOSURE |
| BR10 | A case created on bad data is canceled by rule, never deleted | R-UNI-16 (Epic 2 handling) |
| BR11 | The case links to ACE by business key (`primary_person_key`, `account_key`, `person_key`) with no foreign key. A key with no view row is listed by REC-05 and never invented from a partial record | D-RCV-35 U4; ADR-010; REC-05 |
| BR12 | The primary account is the linked account with the highest `total_balance` on the business date; a tie breaks on the lowest `account_key` | case_account.is_primary (DF-CAS-027); Data Tier Map section 5 |
| BR13 | Entry and exclusion decisions come only from `RuleEvaluator` on packages ENTRY and EXCLUSION. A version not in force holds creation with MSG-P3-027 and is never a default decision | R-UNI-41; D-RCV-36 T3, T5 |
| BR14 | One case per customer and product across the real services: the case is created once in rwb-case, the account link is created once per `account_key`, and a repeated readiness signal for the same business date adds no case and no link | DP-09; REQ-CWC-003; Arch v5 slide 42 (inbox dedupe, key caseId) |
| BR15 | Event first, never a table copy: the creation commits in rwb-case with its outbox row and leaves as `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1` on `rwb.case.events.v1`; the decision leaves as `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; the suite reads no copy of either | ADR-015; DP-03; DP-09 |
| BR16 | No cross-service table read: the suite and every service read another service's data through its contract only, and the source views stay behind rwb-source-data | DP-01; DP-05; ADR-020 |
| BR17 | One hop and two seconds: every REST call of the run goes to the owning service, behind gateway-bff where a screen is involved, with the 2 s client budget and no service-to-service chain | ADR-020; DP-11; DP-19 |
| BR18 | No personal data in events, logs, workflow history or fixtures: the run carries account keys, person keys, case numbers, rule IDs, package versions and business dates only | Guardrail of RWB-E1-018; Arch v5 slide 42 notes |

##### 9. State transitions

The legacy case states of RWB-E1-018:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | AceDataReady (EV-26), package ENTRY returns ENTER | `days_past_due` at or above 90 in `v_ace_account` for the completed ALS business date, package EXCLUSION returns no match, no open case for the borrower and product group | New |
| New | Allocation rule matched | Handled by RWB-E1-020 | Assigned |

The states the run observes across the services:

| Item | States |
|---|---|
| Batch gate | Waiting (the batch is not complete and MSG-P1-001 is shown), Ready (the readiness signal is received and the data product is fresh), Held (no EXCLUSION version is in force and MSG-P3-027 is shown) |
| DailyCaseRun | Not started, started by AceDataReady, waiting at the gate, completed with the run counts, held for the whole business date |
| Case | NEW at creation with no stage code; Assigned belongs to RWB-E1-020 and is out of scope |
| Rule package version | LOADED, APPROVED, IN_FORCE, SUPERSEDED, ROLLED_BACK, REFUSED |
| Suite run | Not started, running, passed, failed with the failing test case named |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| QA integration engineer | Owns the suite module, the fixtures, the clock and gate control, the rollback step and the evidence report |
| Service owner of rwb-source-data | Owns the readiness call, the freshness read, the AceDataReady event and the reconciliation that lists a missing key |
| Service owner of rwb-case | Owns case creation, the DailyCaseRun workflow, the case read operations and the publication of `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1` |
| Service owner of rwb-access | Owns the Case record right and its refusal on the case reads |
| Service owner of rwb-document | Owns the case document links that the run reads back after a creation |
| Service owner of rwb-decision | Owns the version list, the rollback, the central ledger and the RulePackageInForce event |
| Data steward | Receives the missing-key list of REC-05 and decides the data correction |
| Platform administrator | Receives the incident when the yearly number range is used up and when the gate is held for a whole date |
| Every case role holding Case record R | Reads the case and its accounts inside its scope; no write in this story |
| No role | Reads a service schema directly, or takes production data into the run |

The exact fixture composition - the row count of the synthetic ACE batch rows, the exact synthetic case set and the keys of the removed view row - is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0343; ASM-0437).
