**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the rwb-decision slice of RWB-E1-020, keeping the ALLOCATION and ASSIGNMENT packages in the rule registry, serving a version only while it is in force, and collecting the allocation record of every morning run in the central ledger. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR), an internal auditor (RW-AUDIT) and the owning service itself**, I want **every allocation and assignment decision of a morning run recorded in rwb-decision as one ledger entry per case and business date, carrying the ALLOCATION rule ID and package version and the ASSIGNMENT rule ID and package version with the queue and owner identifiers, and the compiled models of the two packages served only while their version is in force and only with a matching SHA-256**, so that **every case that was queued and given an owner can be explained the same day from its record, and no run can cite a rule version that rwb-decision never promoted**.

Inside `rwb-decision` this is the registry and record half of the allocation engine:

- Service `rwb-decision`, schema `rwb_decision`, REST base `/api/recovery/decision/v1`, topic `rwb.decision.events.v1` with event names `rwb.decision.<Event>.v1`, task queue `rwb-decision` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision`.
- The record: `rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1` arrives on the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`, key caseId, and is consumed idempotently into `decision_log_entry`: one entry per case and business date, final call "OWNER_ASSIGNED" when the case was queued and given an owner and "RULE_GAP" when no rule matched it (legacy AC5, AC6).
- The values: rule ID "ALLOC-014" with version "ALLOC-2026.11" in `rule_id` and `rule_version`; assignment rule ID "ASSIGN-007" with version "ASSIGN-2026.11", the queue identifier and the owner identifier in the actions payload. No product group, region, band, amount or case number: identifiers only.
- The read: `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId=...&ruleId=ALLOC-014&from=...&to=...` explains every allocation of a date, with the result of the chain check on each item.
- The registry: the two packages and their row sets live in `rule_package`, `rule_package_version`, `rule_row` and `rule_test_case`; JOB-20 promotes the version whose date has arrived, and the compiled model is served to the owning service only while in force and only with a matching SHA-256.
- No rule is evaluated here: the KieBase, the first-match evaluation and the 300 ms budget stay in the owning service (DP-04), and a version not in force is never a default allocation.

The legacy facts are unchanged: first match wins, the rule ID is the row name, ALLOC-014 sends a MORTGAGE case in BKK to queue MTG-BKK-CO, and the entry cannot be altered once written.

##### 2. Business rationale

Legacy RWB-E1-020 promised that every new case is queued and given an owner by rule on the morning it arrives, with the rule ID and package version on the decision log entry, so any allocation can be explained afterwards. In the target that promise has two halves in two services: the allocation, the owner choice and the case update stay with rwb-case; the proof of it, and the authority of the rules it cites, are this service's.

Both mechanisms changed, and each fails silently. The log is no longer one table written by one writer: each service writes a local record in its own transaction and announces it on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and rwb-decision collects it (ADR-022, DP-03). Rules are no longer read from one shared schema: governance is central here and evaluation is local in the service that owns the model, which fetches a version and verifies its checksum before it swaps it (DP-04, ADR-017). A run can now finish with no ledger entry and no error, or cite a version this service never promoted, and every case still looks allocated.

This story puts the two guarantees back: one entry per case and business date in `decision_log_entry`, carrying both rule identities and the queue and owner identifiers, append only and hash-chained, so the allocations of a date are one read; and one promoted version per package, announced to the owning services, with a model served only while in force and only with a matching SHA-256.

This is the secondary slice of legacy RWB-E1-020. The run, the two evaluations, the assignment methods, the cap, the owner choice, the overflow and exception queues and the case update stay with rwb-case (RWB-P3-E1020-APP); the deviation handler queue with rwb-deviation; the rerun right with rwb-access. It answers REQ-CWC-016, supports REQ-CWC-007, REQ-CWC-008 and REQ-CWC-009 on the record side, and serves NFR-033 and control CTL-03.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P3-E1020-CON is published: the rwb-case allocation contract, with the case read `GET /cases/{caseId}` and the queue read `GET /queues`, their error envelope, the not-found answer and its fake (DP-11). This service reads the case number and the queue code through it at display time and stores neither.
- The `rwb_decision` baseline is in place from the service template: the schema, the six tables of this service, the outbox and inbox objects of DP-09, the base, the topic, the task queue and the chart.
- `decision_log_entry` exists with `chain_seq`, `prev_hash`, `entry_hash` and `corrects_entry_id`, the chain lock, the canonical form and the append-only trigger, and the service role holds INSERT and SELECT with no UPDATE or DELETE grant (RWB-P7-E1008-APP).
- The record contract of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published: the record shape, the envelope on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, the idempotency key and the transaction rule, with its fake. How the business date travels in that envelope, and the field names of the queue and owner identifiers in the actions payload, are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2441; ASM-4049).
- The two versions are loaded, tested and approved: ALLOCATION "ALLOC-2026.11" and ASSIGNMENT "ASSIGN-2026.11", each with its workbook, generated DRL, SHA-256, valid-from date of 2026-11-30 and an approver holding RW-RISK who is not the author (RWB-P7-E1073-APP). This story reads, promotes and serves those rows; it loads none of them.
- The version-state list and LOV-DECISION are in force and are read as reference data through the contract of DP-07; no list value is written in this service's code.
- The workflow kit, the namespace `rwb-recovery` and the task queue `rwb-decision` are provisioned, so JOB-20 can run as a Temporal Schedule (DP-10).
- The synthetic facts of the tests: case RW-2026-000201 with product group MORTGAGE, region BKK and band B2 in queue MTG-BKK-CO of team MTG-BKK with owner U-03; and case RW-2026-000204 with product group SSME and region NE3, which matches no rule. The business date is 2026-12-01.
- Readers hold Decision log R and an owning service holds a model-owner service identity (TSD P7 T6.1). The authorisation decision is the cached permission decision the service template holds from rwb-access; DP-08 is not in this slice's pattern set, so this story adds no guard of its own.

##### 4. Flow

1. Morning run: the JOB-03 step of DailyCaseRun in rwb-case evaluates ALLOCATION and then ASSIGNMENT locally, gives case RW-2026-000201 queue MTG-BKK-CO and owner U-03, and writes its record with the case change and the outbox row in one transaction (RWB-P3-E1020-APP).
2. The record leaves as `rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, key caseId, carrying the decision code, the final call, the rule ID, the rule version, the inputs reference, the actions payload and the actor.
3. rwb-decision: `AllocationRecordIngest` consumes it through the inbox, deduplicating on the event identifier and again on the case and business date.
4. rwb-decision: `AllocationRecordValidator` applies the refusals of this slice and checks the fields an entry cannot be written without: the inputs reference, the final call and the decided time.
5. rwb-decision: `LedgerAppender` appends one `decision_log_entry`: the decision code the record carries and final call "OWNER_ASSIGNED", `rule_id` "ALLOC-014", `rule_version` "ALLOC-2026.11", the inputs reference, the decided time, the actor, and an actions payload holding "ASSIGN-007", "ASSIGN-2026.11", the queue identifier and the owner identifier. The chain columns come from the ledger's chain.
6. rwb-decision: a case that matched no rule arrives with final call "RULE_GAP", no rule ID and no rule version, and is appended the same way; the exception queue and the case status are rwb-case's and are recorded here as identifiers at most.
7. rwb-decision: a repeat of the same case and business date appends nothing, answers the first entry's id and adds one to the repeat count for R-UNI-40.
8. Any time: `AllocationDecisionReader` answers the decision-log query with the entries of the date, their rule and version, their final call and, per entry, the result of the recomputed hash chain.
9. 00:01 daily: JOB-20 finds every version whose valid-from date has arrived and whose state is APPROVED, sets it in force, supersedes the version it replaces, writes its own record in the same transaction and publishes `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1`; on that announcement and on a cache miss an owning service asks for the compiled model, which is served only if the version is in force and the recomputed checksum matches.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A record carries a rule ID and an empty rule version | Refused; nothing appended; the refusal is logged with the case ID and the missing field and one incident is raised | MSG-P7-009 with "ruleVersion" | AC5 |
| X2 | A record carries a decision code that is not in LOV-DECISION | Refused as X1, naming the decision code field; nothing appended | MSG-P7-009 with "decisionCode" | AC5 |
| X3 | The same record arrives twice, or the morning run for the date is repeated | One entry for the case and the business date; the first entry's id is answered and the repeat is counted | None | AC3 |
| X4 | The ledger store is unavailable | The append is refused and the read answers with no partial page; the records wait in the producers' outboxes, so none is lost, and the ingest catches up | MSG-P7-003 | TC-E1-020-15 |
| X5 | A model is asked for under a version that is not in force | Refused; no model body; the answer names the package code, the version label and its state | None | AC6 |
| X6 | The recomputed SHA-256 of the stored artifact differs from the recorded one | Refused; no model body; one incident for the version, and the version in force keeps serving | None | AC6 |
| X7 | The chain does not hold for an entry on the page | The entry is returned with the check result false, a warning names it on the page and one incident goes to the Compliance queue; the entry is never hidden | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2442; ASM-4050) | AC4 |
| X8 | A record carries a decision code of another point in a case's life, for example CASE_CREATED | Not this slice's mapping: the ledger's own ingest appends it (RWB-P7-E1027-APP) and this story adds no entry and no refusal | None | None |

A package version that is not in force is never a default allocation: where nothing is servable the owning service stops its run with NoPackageInForce and MSG-P3-027 before it touches a case, and this service never hands out an older, a superseded or an unchecked version to fill the gap.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against the published rwb-case contract and its fake (RWB-P3-E1020-CON), the envelope of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, the `rwb_decision` baseline and the registry rows of RWB-P7-E1073-APP; it calls no rule engine and no other service at run time |
| Negotiable | Nothing business is fixed: the rule IDs, versions, queue codes, caps and methods are rows of the two packages; this story fixes the record and the serving rules |
| Valuable | One read explains every allocation of a date, and no service can fetch a version that was not promoted or does not match its checksum |
| Estimable | One consumer, one validator, one appender, one reader, one model service and one short Schedule workflow |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests, as a secondary slice of the legacy key |
| Testable | Every criterion in section 7 is one automated test against the record fixture and the registry fixture, with the synthetic cases the legacy story fixes |

The six criteria above are new and test only this deliverable: the allocation record in the central ledger, its refusals, its read, and the two packages held and served only while in force. The legacy criteria are owned elsewhere: AC1 to AC9 and AC11 to AC13 are the run and the case update of rwb-case (RWB-P3-E1020-APP); AC10 is the wait on case creation, proved across services by RWB-ITG-E1020-ITG; the deviation branch is rwb-deviation's; the rerun right is rwb-access's. The legacy test cases this story answers are listed in section 16.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every allocation of a morning run is recorded once in the central ledger, one entry per case and business date, with final call "OWNER_ASSIGNED" when the case was queued and given an owner and "RULE_GAP" when no rule matched it | REQ-CWC-016; FSD P7 AC-P7-002-01; legacy AC5, AC6, BR9 |
| BR2 | The entry carries the ALLOCATION rule ID and version in `rule_id` and `rule_version`, and the ASSIGNMENT rule ID and version with the queue identifier and the owner identifier in the actions payload. First match wins and the rule ID is the row name | REQ-CWC-016; CTL-03; legacy BR1 and BR9. The FSD P7 names the same row "ALLOC-MTG-BKK-01" (GAP-2440; ASM-4048) |
| BR3 | A record with a rule ID and no rule version, or with a decision code outside LOV-DECISION, is refused and nothing is appended; the refusal names the field | FSD P7 AC-EXC-P7-002-01 and AC-EXC-P7-002-05; MSG-P7-009 |
| BR4 | An entry is append only and hash-chained: nothing updates or deletes it, and the chain is the record of the order of decisions | FSD P7 AC-P7-001-01; DF-DEC-017, DF-DEC-018, DF-DEC-028; legacy BR7 |
| BR5 | The read names the rule and its version for every allocation of a date, and a break in the chain is shown on the page, never hidden and never dropped, and reported to Compliance the same day | REQ-CWC-016; NFR-033; NFR-035; FSD P7 AC-BG-P7-006-01 |
| BR6 | A decision whose record cannot be written does not proceed, and a read against an unavailable ledger answers with no partial page | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; CTL-06; FSD P7 AC-EXC-P7-002-07; MSG-P7-003 |
| BR7 | An allocation is recorded at most once for a case and a business date: a repeated event or a repeated run gives one entry and the repeat is counted | R-UNI-40; FSD P7 AC-EXC-P7-002-03; legacy AC8 and BR8 |
| BR8 | A model is served only while its version is in force, and only when the recomputed SHA-256 of the stored artifact matches the recorded one | DP-04; ADR-017; RWB-P7-E1073-APP |
| BR9 | No rule is evaluated in rwb-decision: the KieBase, the first-match evaluation and the 300 ms budget stay in the owning service, which keeps its last good model when a new one is refused | DP-04; ADR-017; legacy BR1 and guardrail "one evaluator" |
| BR10 | JOB-20 promotes a version at 00:01 on its valid-from date, supersedes the earlier one and announces the promotion; a version not in force is never a default allocation | REQ-CWC-008; DP-10; FSD P7 AC-P7-007-01 and AC-ALT-P7-007-02 |

How the rules hold in `rwb-decision`: BR1 and BR7 run in the ingest and in the unique key on the case and the business date, so a second delivery finds the first entry and changes nothing. BR2 runs in the mapper, which copies the rule identity as it arrives and derives nothing from a case attribute. BR3 runs before any append, so a refused record leaves the ledger as it was. BR4 runs in the schema, where the append-only trigger refuses an UPDATE and a DELETE. BR5 runs in the reader, which recomputes each hash and compares it with the link before it. BR8 and BR9 run in `RuleModelService` and in what it does not hold: it reads a state and a checksum, serves bytes, and contains no evaluator, working memory or agenda. BR10 runs in `VersionPromotionService` under JOB-20, which moves a state and publishes an event and evaluates nothing.

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | an accepted record for a case and a business date | No entry exists for the pair | One `decision_log_entry` at the next `chain_seq`, final call "OWNER_ASSIGNED" or "RULE_GAP" |
| Appended | the same case and business date again | The idempotency key repeats | No change; the first entry id is answered and the repeat counted |
| APPROVED | JOB-20 at 00:01 on the valid-from date | The version passed its load checks and its approver is not its author | In force; the version in force before it is superseded |
| In force | a model fetch | The recomputed checksum matches the recorded one | Served, unchanged |
| In force | a model fetch | The checksum does not match | Refused, no model body, an incident raised; the state is unchanged |
| LOADED, APPROVED, superseded, rolled back or refused | a model fetch | The version is not in force | Refused, the state named in the answer; no model body |

The case state machine is not this service's: rwb-case owns the case status, queue, owner and stage (TSD P7 T4, "No case state machine of its own"), and this slice changes no case state. The load, the checks, the approval and the rollback that move a version between its states are RWB-P7-E1073-APP; this story owns the promotion at 00:01 and the refusal of anything not in force.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| rwb-decision service identity (SY-DECLOG) | Appends the ledger entry, serves the two models, promotes a version under the Schedule and publishes the announcement |
| SY-CASEWF, case workflow module | Writes the allocation record in its own schema and transaction and announces it; holds no grant on `rwb_decision` |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager; RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Read the ledger for their team or their own cases (Decision log R, scope applied) |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit; RW-COMPLY, Compliance and PDPA officer | Read the ledger with its chain state (Decision log R) |
| RW-RISK, risk and model risk officer | Approves each version through RWB-P7-E1073-APP; this story records the approval and promotes on its date |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Operates JOB-20, reads the promotion result and the incidents of a refused fetch |
| rwb-case (P3) | Owns the case, queue, owner and the rule row behind the decision; this service holds their identifiers and reads their codes at display |

The authorisation decision is the cached permission decision the service template holds from rwb-access; DP-08 is not in this slice's pattern set, so this story adds no guard and no access entry. The refusal shapes are 403 with MSG-P4-002 for a role that holds no Decision log right and 503 with MSG-P7-003 when the ledger cannot be read. The role codes above are rows of the role model in `rwb_access` (TSD P7 T6.1) and are not fixed in code.

| DF-DEC-001 | decision_log_entry | id | Write |
| DF-DEC-002 | decision_log_entry | case_id (a value from the record, with no foreign key into `rwb_case`) | Write |
| DF-DEC-003 | decision_log_entry | decision_code (a value of LOV-DECISION carried by the record) | Write |
| DF-DEC-004, DF-DEC-005 | decision_log_entry | rule_id ("ALLOC-014"), rule_version ("ALLOC-2026.11") | Write |
| DF-DEC-008, DF-DEC-016, DF-DEC-030 | decision_log_entry | inputs_ref, decided_at, actor_user_id | Write |

| DF-DEC-014 | decision_log_entry | actions ("ASSIGN-007", "ASSIGN-2026.11", queue identifier, owner identifier) | Write |
| DF-DEC-017, DF-DEC-018, DF-DEC-028 | decision_log_entry | prev_hash, entry_hash, chain_seq | Write |

Field IDs are those in the Technical Specification P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1 and the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary. `decision_log_entry.case_id` is the only case value in `rwb_decision`: no case number, product group, region, band, amount, queue code or owner name column exists, and no foreign key points into another schema (DP-01). The physical columns of `rule_package_version` and the payload a compiled artifact is served in are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2439; ASM-4047): the sources fix what a version stores, not its physical form.

##### 12. Contract

The base is `/api/recovery/decision/v1` (DP-13), the topic is `rwb.decision.events.v1` (DP-14), the queue is `rwb-decision` and the schema is `rwb_decision`.

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

| Method | Path | Purpose | Authorization |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/decision-log` | Search the ledger for the allocations of a case, a rule or a date: query `caseId`, `ruleId`, `from`, `to`, `page`, `size`; each item carries `chainVerified`, the result of its chain check, and the page names an entry that fails it | Decision log, right R, scope applied |
| GET | `/rule-models/{packageCode}/{version}` | Serve one compiled model version with its SHA-256 to the owning service that holds the package | A model-owner service identity, under the rule-package contract |

API-P7-006 of the TSD appendix T-A is the decision-log query and carries the same four filters. The model-serving operation is Not specified in the source documents as a provided operation of the Ownership Map, which lists 19 operations without it (GAP-2443; ASM-4051). This story fills the query with the allocation read on the path the ledger story declares and adds no third path: the entry read `GET /decision-log/{entryId}` and the audit export stay with RWB-P7-E1027-APP and legacy RWB-E2-005.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Service | Used for | Timeout |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | rwb-case (P3), under RWB-P3-E1020-CON | The case number shown beside an entry on the page, read at display time | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/queues` | rwb-case (P3), under RWB-P3-E1020-CON | The queue code and team shown for a queue identifier in the actions payload | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |

| Event | Topic | Key | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|
| rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1 | `rwb.decision.events.v1` | The package code | Package code, version label, in force at and the version's SHA-256; identifiers and facts only |

| Event | Topic | From | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1 | `rwb.decision-record.v1` (shared) | The owning services; the allocations of this story from rwb-case | The append of `decision_log_entry`: decision code, final call, rule ID and version, inputs reference, actions and actor |

Consumed through an inbox that deduplicates on the event identifier and again on the case and business date, with the retry and dead-letter topics of DP-09. The envelope is the one RWB-PLT-E1027-CON fixes; how the business date and the queue and owner identifiers are carried in it is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2441; ASM-4049).

| PromoteDueVersions | Activity | `rwb-decision` | Sets APPROVED versions whose valid-from date has arrived in force, supersedes the version each replaces, and writes the record and the outbox row in one transaction |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision`, modules `allocationrecord` and `rulemodel`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| AllocationRecordIngest | Consumer | Consumes the record through the inbox, deduplicates on the event and on the case and business date, and hands it to the validator |
| AllocationRecordValidator | Service | The refusals and the required fields, before any append |
| LedgerAppender | Service | Maps the record to one `decision_log_entry`, appends it with `chain_seq`, `prev_hash` and `entry_hash` in one transaction, and answers the first entry id on a repeat |
| AllocationDecisionReader | Service | The allocation read with the chain result per item, the warning on a broken link, and the case number and queue code taken from the rwb-case contract |
| RuleModelService | Service | Serves a compiled version only when it is in force and its recomputed SHA-256 matches; serves no evaluator |
| VersionPromotionService | Service | Under JOB-20, promotes the versions due, supersedes the earlier one, writes the record and the outbox row, and publishes the announcement with the package code as the key |

**Database and migrations**

- Writes `decision_log_entry` (append only) and the version state at 00:01; writes no case, queue or owner value.
- Reads `rule_package`, `rule_package_version`, `rule_row` and their catalog projection.
- Index on `(case_id, rule_id, decided_at)` for the read, and a unique key on the idempotency key of the case and business date.
- Per-service migration of DP-15: `V1020_1__allocation_record.sql` adds the two indexes and no column carrying a case attribute. The tables arrive with the baseline and the registry stories; no row is seeded here.

**Configuration and reference data**

- No business value is configured: the package codes, rule IDs, versions, queue codes and caps are rows of the two packages and values of rwb-case; parameters and lists come through DP-06 and DP-07 and none is written in Java.
- Two settings only: the 00:01 time of the Schedule and the two package codes this service holds in the registry.

**Build steps**

1. `AllocationRecordIngest` and `AllocationRecordValidator` against the fixture, with the accepted, the RULE_GAP, the duplicate, the two refusals and the foreign decision code; tests for AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC5.
2. `LedgerAppender` with `chain_seq`, the hashes and the repeat path; tests for AC1 and AC3.
3. `AllocationDecisionReader` with the filters, the chain result and the warning on a broken link; test for AC4.
4. `RuleModelService` with the state check and the checksum comparison, and a schema assertion that `rwb_decision` holds no case attribute column; test for AC6.
5. `VersionPromotionService` and the JOB-20 Schedule, with the record, the outbox row and the event in one transaction, then the display path with the case number and queue code taken from the contract fake; tests for AC1 and AC6.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

This is a secondary slice: it adds no build dependency of its own (metadata "Depends on (build)" = None) and builds against the `rwb_decision` baseline, the registry rows and the RWB-P3-E1020-CON fake. The platform H rows and the C rows of the table are the dependencies the patterns add; they are held by the platform and contract stories and are not repeated in the metadata rows, which name the one contract dependency of the legacy key. DP-01, DP-13 and DP-15 are the target shape itself. DP-03 is the record path: the local record of the owning service, the shared topic and the ledger here, with no shared table and no call into rwb-case. DP-04 is the point of this slice: governance central here, evaluation local there, so this service holds no KieBase and serves bytes and states. DP-05, DP-06 and DP-07 are prohibitions: no ACE view is read, and no parameter or list value is written in this service's code. DP-09, DP-10, DP-11 and DP-14 are the mechanism: the inbox dedupe and the keyed announcement, the 00:01 Schedule with no Quartz row, one 2 s hop for the display read, and `rwb.decision.events.v1` supplied by the naming library. DP-19 is the gateway-bff composite route behind the decision log page.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the contract tests of RWB-P3-E1020-CON and RWB-PLT-E1027-CON stay green, and a SIT week shows one entry per case and business date with both rule identities, a repeated run adding none, a page that names a broken link and hides no entry, and no model served for a version not in force or with a mismatched checksum.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-009 | A record is refused for a missing or invalid field | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2442; ASM-4050); the answer is a refusal that names the field |
| MSG-P7-003 | The ledger cannot take the append or answer the read | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller's role holds no Decision log right for the action | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P3-027 | No version of a package is in force at the owning service | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |

MSG-P7-009 is written to the service log and the incident and is never shown to a customer; its {field} value is "ruleVersion" or "decisionCode", and its text is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2442; ASM-4050). A broken chain on a page carries a warning naming the entry, with the same gap. For MSG-P4-002 the {action} value is "read the decision log". For MSG-P3-027 the {check} value is "package in force" and the {detail} names the package code only. Every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` and `detail` filled; the reads answer 401 without a session, 403 for a role without the right and 503 with MSG-P7-003 when the ledger cannot be read, and a refused model names the package code, the version label and its state without a model body.

##### 15. Screens and states

No new screen. The allocation view of SCR-38 Decision log query shows, for one case or one business date, the rule ID and version, the final call, the assignment rule ID and version, the queue, the owner, the decided time and the chain result; the case number and queue code beside them are read from the rwb-case contract at display time. Its states are Loading, Results, Empty ("No decisions match this search.") and Error with MSG-P7-003; a broken link puts a warning at the top and leaves the entry in place. The screen itself, its filters beyond the four query parameters, its paging and its export are legacy RWB-E2-005's, served by the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), which calls this service for the entries and rwb-case for the case header.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the rule IDs, versions, queue codes, caps and methods are rows of the two packages and values of rwb-case. No rule form, prefix, queue code or cap appears in this service's Java.
- No personal data in events, workflow inputs, logs or tests. The entry carries a case identifier, a queue identifier, an owner user identifier and a rule identity; no name, address, identity number or account number is written or logged. Test data uses synthetic keys (`RW-2026-000201`, `MTG-BKK-CO`, `U-03`, `ALLOC-014`).
- No cross-schema read (DP-01): `rwb_decision` reads no `rwb_case` table and no table of another service, and holds no foreign key into one.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `v_ace_*` views, and this service reads neither: the case and queue facts behind a decision stay with rwb-case.
- The record is the owning service's and the entry is this service's: no service writes another's schema, and the append is never done twice for one case and business date.
- An entry is never corrected in place: a correction is a new entry naming the one it corrects, and the append-only trigger refuses an UPDATE and a DELETE.
- No rule engine in this service: no KieBase, no working memory and no evaluation on this queue, so the 300 ms budget of an evaluation is never spent here.
- The announcement is keyed by the package code, the consumed record by the case ID, and no topic name is typed in code (DP-09, DP-14).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the deviation slice of RWB-E1-020 is realigned onto rwb-deviation (S8, service wave 2, business wave 1). The legacy key allocates every new case by rule; its exception X4 sends a case with an open deviation to the deviation handler queue with no case owner. In the target the deviation, its handler queue and its named owner are this service's, while the case, the queue, the assignment and the timers stay with rwb-case, so this slice builds the placement answer the morning allocation needs: the handler queue code from the parameter `allocation.deviation.queue.code`, the handler by code from the DEV package (R-DEV-01, R-DEV-03 to R-DEV-06, R-DEV-21), the decision record before the row (DP-03), `DeviationRaised` from the outbox (DP-09, DP-14) and the stage outcome the parent applies. The two operations stay on `/api/recovery/deviation/v1` (DP-13) and the two screens behind the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The case owns no queue column, so no migration adds one; the plan gives this key no CON story of its own, and the boundary shape, the handler roster and the assignment method are not published (GAP-3072, GAP-3073; ASM-5230 to ASM-5234). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR)**, I want **a new case that carries an open deviation to be sent to the deviation handler queue with one named handler instead of being given a case owner by the morning allocation**, so that **every case at 90 days past due that no case owner may work has one handler, one queue and one recorded reason from its first day**.

This story owns:

- the deviation half of the legacy exception X4: the handler queue code of a case with an open deviation, and the named handler of that deviation by code (R-DEV-01, R-DEV-03 to R-DEV-06, R-DEV-21);
- the handler choice for the codes X2 to X7 and for an unmapped code, which RWB-S8-E7001-APP does not build;
- the `deviation` row's `handler_user_id` and `state` in `rwb_deviation`, its decision record written before the change (DP-03), and its `DeviationRaised` row in the outbox (EV-06);
- the placement answer returned to rwb-case as the stage outcome of `DeviationWorkflow`, the child of the case, on task queue `rwb-deviation` in namespace `rwb-recovery`;
- the read-only deviation queue slice of SCR-08 and the queue and owner columns of SCR-02 behind the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19);
- the idempotency of the placement per case and business date, and the one migration that indexes the two reads it needs.

It does not own: the case of record, its queue, its assignment, its timers and the morning run JOB-03 (rwb-case, P3); the X1 raise and outcome journey (RWB-S8-E7001-APP); the DEV rule rows, their versions and the central ledger (rwb-decision, P7); the roles, the rights and the reference values (rwb-access P4, rwb-case P3); the contact stop, the evidence pack and the notices (X1 to X3 flows, P5 and P6); and the schema, deployment and observability of this service (the DB, INF and OPS stories of this legacy key).

##### 2. Business rationale

The objective and the measure do not move: deviations closed within the service level, measured on the decision log and the Workbench records and reviewed monthly (FSD S8 A2.4.1). The service-side requirement is REQ-DVH-003, "Each deviation code routes to its named owner, and a code with no owner routes to the team manager and is recorded as unmapped" (FSD S8 Requirements served).

The legacy problem is that a case can be owned by nobody: the allocation engine of RWB-E1-020 places every new case in a queue and gives it an owner by rule before 07:00, but a case that already carries a deviation cannot be worked by a case owner, and the legacy path is one monolith method that reads `deviation_open`, reads the queue table and writes both the case and the deviation (RWB-E1-020 sections 3, 4 and 5 X4).

D-RCV-60 changes who owns each fact, not what the team manager gets:

- **The deviation and its handler are this service's.** `deviation` is the one table the Ownership Map gives S8, its `handler_user_id` and its `state` are its columns, and the DEV package is evaluated inside this service by its own embedded kit (context pack ownership rows; TSD S8 T0.2, T3.1; DP-01, DP-04).
- **The case, the queue and the owner are rwb-case's.** `recovery_case`, `queue`, `queue_member` and `assignment` are P3's, and the S8 row of the connection matrix names Temporal and events to P3 and never REST, so the diversion is answered as a child-workflow outcome and this story writes no case, queue or assignment row (Architecture v5 slides 8 and 13; ASM-5230).
- **The handler queue code is a parameter, not a constant.** "DEV-HANDLER" is the value the legacy section 3 says is assumed under DL23, and in the target the code is read from `allocation.deviation.queue.code` through the parameters contract of rwb-case (DP-06; ASM-5232).
- **The decision is recorded first**, in the same transaction as the deviation change and before the event leaves: that is what TSD S8 T2 states and what the legacy decision-log rules require (DP-03).
- **The event leaves from the outbox** on `rwb.deviation.events.v1`, with rwb-case, rwb-comms and rwb-treatment as its listeners (TSD S8 T5.2.1; ASM-5234).

No business value moves: the deviation codes, the raised-by values, the handler roles, the state names and the queue code stay rule rows or reference data read with their version, never a constant of the code.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service baseline is in place: `rwb-deviation`, schema `rwb_deviation`, base `/api/recovery/deviation/v1`, topic `rwb.deviation.events.v1` with `.retry` and `.dlt`, task queue `rwb-deviation` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.deviation`, gateway-bff for its screens (context pack service row; TSD S8 T0.1).
- The plan gives this key H = None, C = `RWB-P3-E1020-CON` only, so the two published operations of the service and the platform contracts behind the DP rows are preconditions already in place rather than in-lane build dependencies (GAP-3073; ASM-5233).
- `RWB-P3-E1020-CON` is published with its fake: the case element the parent presents (case reference, product group, region, exposure band, business date, the open deviation reference and code) and the stage outcome it accepts. The element names of both shapes are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3072; ASM-5230).
- rwb-case starts `DeviationWorkflow` on `rwb-deviation` as the child of `CaseWorkflow`, with parent close policy ABANDON and continue-as-new; the case router of P3 forwards the case and never calls this service over REST (TSD S8 T5.2.1; Architecture v5 slide 13).
- `deviation` exists in `rwb_deviation` from the DB story of this service with the fields DF-CAS-036 to DF-CAS-045 and the standard record columns of TSD S8 T3.0; this story adds no column (DP-15).
- The DEV rule package is in force at its version with R-DEV-01, R-DEV-03, R-DEV-04, R-DEV-05, R-DEV-06 and R-DEV-21; it is authored, tested and approved in rwb-decision and loaded here, and this service evaluates it with its embedded kit (DP-04; TSD S8 T2).
- The parameter `allocation.deviation.queue.code` holds "DEV-HANDLER", the value DL23 assumes, read through the parameters contract of rwb-case (DP-06; RWB-E1-020 sections 3 and 4; ASM-5232).
- The lists LOV-DEVIATION (X1 to X7), LOV-RAISED-BY (SCREENING_AGENT, RULE, OFFICER, CUSTOMER_CONTACT) and LOV-DEV-OUTCOME (RETURNED, RE_ROUTED, CASE_ENDED) are read through the reference-data contract of rwb-case (DP-07; TSD S8 T3.2).
- The queue and its members are P3's rows: the handler candidates of a queue arrive on the P3 contract, and this service keeps no copy of a queue, a member or a cap (GAP-3072; ASM-5231).
- The service runs as its own login on `rwb_deviation` and holds no grant on another `rwb_*` schema and no `v_ace_*` grant, so a statement on `rwb_case` fails the boundary test (DP-01, DP-02).
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft contract baseline; the contract is tagged when its tests pass.

##### 4. Flow

1. The morning allocation of rwb-case reaches a NEW case for business date 2026-12-01 and starts `DeviationWorkflow` on queue `rwb-deviation` as the child of `CaseWorkflow`, with the case element of `RWB-P3-E1020-CON`; the run itself stays JOB-03 of P3 (RWB-E1-020 sections 3 and 4; ASM-5230).
2. The workflow reads the case's open deviation from its own rows: a row whose `cleared_at` is empty and whose `state` is not RESUMED, DEV_REJECTED or CASE_ENDED. With no open deviation it answers NO_DEVIATION and ends, and nothing is written (AC4).
3. `evaluateHandlerRules` loads the DEV package version in force and evaluates R-DEV-01 for the open code: the deviation is flagged, the stage clock pauses and the prescription clock keeps running. It then evaluates the code rule: R-DEV-03 for X2 and X3, R-DEV-04 for X4, R-DEV-05 for X5, R-DEV-06 for X6 and X7, and R-DEV-21 where the code is outside X1 to X7 or the code has no owner (Business Rules and Routing Logic v4).
4. The handler queue code is read from the parameter `allocation.deviation.queue.code` through the parameters contract of rwb-case; "DEV-HANDLER" is the value in force and no queue code is written in code (DP-06; ASM-5232).
5. `assignHandler` picks the handler the fired rule names from the members the P3 contract lists for that queue, taking the handler with the fewest open deviations in this service's own rows; no cap is applied, because no source publishes a handler cap (GAP-3072; ASM-5231).
6. `recordAndApplyPlacement` writes one decision record through the local library before any change: case reference, deviation reference, code, rule ID with the package version, the queue code, the handler reference, the inputs reference and the decided-at time (DP-03; TSD S8 T2).
7. In the same `rwb_deviation` transaction the activity updates the row: `handler_user_id`, `state` = DEV_WITH_OWNER, `version`, `updated_at` and `updated_by`, and writes the outbox row for `DeviationRaised` with identifiers, the code, the queue code, the rule ID and version and no personal data (DP-09).
8. The workflow returns the stage outcome to the parent: the deviation reference, the queue code, the handler reference, the rule IDs with their versions and PLACE_DEVIATION_QUEUE. The parent places the case in the queue, keeps status NEW, sets no case owner and pauses the stage clock (R-DEV-01; ASM-5230).
9. A repeat presentation for the same case and business date answers the placement already recorded, writes nothing, publishes no second event and counts the repeat (R-UNI-40).
10. SCR-08 Deviation queue shows the open deviation with its type, its handler and its age, and SCR-02 Case list shows the case in the handler queue with no owner; both are composed by gateway-bff and neither writes anything (DP-19).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The decision record cannot be written | Nothing changes: no handler, no state move and no event, the case is not diverted, and the step answers a failure | MSG-P7-003 | AC5 |
| X2 | No DEV package version is in force at the run | The step holds before any case is placed, the run of that case is reported and the case keeps status NEW | MSG-P3-027 | AC5 |
| X3 | The parameter `allocation.deviation.queue.code` has no value, or names a queue the P3 contract does not list | The placement holds, the handler is not assigned and the case is not diverted; the parameter and the missing queue are named | None (platform 503 envelope) | AC3 |
| X4 | The P3 contract does not answer inside 2 s or its breaker is open | The placement holds, the handler is not assigned and the case stays NEW with no queue and no owner | None (platform 503 envelope) | AC1 |
| X5 | The case's open deviation is already in DEV_WITH_OWNER with a handler | The existing handler is answered and nothing is rewritten; the placement is not repeated | None | AC7 |
| X6 | The code is outside X1 to X7, or the code has no owner | R-DEV-21 assigns the case owner's team manager and records the code as unmapped | None | AC6 |
| X7 | A repeat presentation for the same case and business date | The recorded placement is answered, the repeat is counted and no second row, record or event leaves | None | AC7 |
| X8 | A component, a statement or a test reaches a `v_ace_*` view, a `rwb_case` row or another service's schema | The grant refuses the statement and the boundary test fails the build | None (pipeline log) | Section 17, BR5, BR6 |

X1 to X4 are the paths the target call types and the container add; X6 is the unmapped-code path the FSD requires; X5 and X7 are the idempotency of the placement; X8 is the DP-01 and DP-05 boundary. The legacy per-case paths of the allocation itself — overflow, exception queue, repeated run, a case that is not NEW — are RWB-P3-E1020-APP's.

| Independent | Starts on Day 1 against `RWB-P3-E1020-CON`, the DEV package fixture, the decision-record stub, the outbox relay stub and the parameters and reference-data fakes, on its own schema, and needs no live P1, P3 or P7 |
| Negotiable | The activity names, the shape of the placement answer and the tie-break of two handlers with the same load are this story's choice; the rules, the state names, the queue code source and the `deviation` fields are fixed |
| Valuable | A case that already carries a deviation is diverted on the morning it arrives, with one handler, one queue, one recorded decision and no case owner |
| Estimable | One workflow branch, two activities, one event publication, two reads, one migration and the boundary and failure tests |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests on the fakes |
| Testable | Every path runs on synthetic cases through the contract fakes, plus the forced record failure and the missing-parameter path |

AC1 to AC7 are the criteria this story owns, and every one of them is new under D-RCV-60 because this slice owns no legacy acceptance criterion: the plan gives the one criterion of the legacy key that covers the diversion, AC7 of RWB-E1-020, to RWB-P3-E1020-APP, and this story proves the deviation half of it. The case number, the zone suffix of AC3 and the codes X2 to X7 are synthetic test data except the codes, which are the LOV-DEVIATION values of TSD S8 T3.2; no business value is invented, because the queue code comes from the parameter, the handler from the rule and the state from the DEV package.

##### 8. Business rules

| Rule | Route set | Codes | From state | Event | Condition | Action | To state | Owner | Systems | Timer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-DEV-01 | Deviations | X1 to X7 | ANY_STATE | DEVIATION_FLAGGED | deviation_code in (X1..X7) | Pause the stage clock, keep the prescription clock running, route to the named owner | DEV_FLAGGED | Workbench | Workbench, the Workbench document hub | same day |
| R-DEV-03 | Deviations | X1 to X7 | DEV_FLAGGED | OWNER_ASSIGNED | deviation_code in (X2,X3) | Assign to the specialist; Legal joins X3 for the estate claim | DEV_WITH_OWNER | Specialist, Legal | Workbench | None |
| R-DEV-04 | Deviations | X1 to X7 | DEV_FLAGGED | OWNER_ASSIGNED | deviation_code = X4 | Assign to the fraud team and refer to Aric | DEV_WITH_OWNER | Fraud team | Aric, Workbench | None |
| R-DEV-05 | Deviations | X1 to X7 | DEV_FLAGGED | OWNER_ASSIGNED | deviation_code = X5 | Assign to Legal; file with the official receiver or the LED before the deadline | DEV_WITH_OWNER | Legal | LIT, Workbench | deadline driven |
| R-DEV-06 | Deviations | X1 to X7 | DEV_FLAGGED | OWNER_ASSIGNED | deviation_code in (X6,X7) | Agent handles within policy; a person approves an insurance claim | DEV_WITH_OWNER | Agent, case owner | Workbench | None |
| R-DEV-21 | Deviations | X1 to X7 | DEV_FLAGGED | OWNER_ASSIGNED | deviation_code is not one of X1 to X7, or no owner is set for the code | Assign to the case owner's team manager and log the unmapped code | DEV_WITH_OWNER | Team manager | Workbench | same day |

The six rows are the rows of Business Rules and Routing Logic v4, copied character for character; their states are the DEVIATION states of TSD S8 T4 and their rule IDs are the ones the DEV package carries, never a constant of the code. R-DEV-02 is RWB-S8-E7001-APP's (the X1 complaint officer) and R-DEV-07 to R-DEV-20 and R-DEV-22 are the outcome and escalation rules of the other stories of this service; this story places a deviation, it does not resolve one.

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A case that carries an open deviation is never given a case owner by the morning allocation: it is answered with the handler queue code and one handler, and the case keeps status NEW | RWB-E1-020 AC7, section 5 X4; R-DEV-01; REQ-DVH-003 |
| BR2 | The decision is recorded before the deviation row changes, with the rule ID and the package version in force; a failed write changes nothing, diverts nothing and answers MSG-P7-003 | DP-03; TSD S8 T2; legacy BR7 |
| BR3 | The handler queue code is read from the parameter `allocation.deviation.queue.code` at every placement; no queue code, no handler role and no state name is written in code | DP-06; RWB-E1-020 section 3; TSD S8 T3.2; BR-S8-004 |
| BR4 | The handler is the owner the fired rule names for the code, and a code outside X1 to X7 or a code with no owner follows R-DEV-21 and is recorded as unmapped | R-DEV-03 to R-DEV-06, R-DEV-21; FSD S8 A2.4.3.1; REQ-DVH-003 |
| BR5 | `deviation` is this service's: no `recovery_case`, `queue`, `queue_member`, `assignment` or `timer` row is read or written, and the case facts arrive on the P3 contract | Context pack ownership rows; TSD S8 T0.2; DP-01 |
| BR6 | ACE data is never read here: the party facts a screening needs are rwb-source-data's, and this slice reads no `v_ace_*` view and no ACE table | DP-05; TSD S8 T0.4 |
| BR7 | The placement is answered once per case and business date; a second presentation answers the recorded placement and counts the repeat | R-UNI-40; legacy BR8 |
| BR8 | One `DeviationRaised` per placement, published from the outbox in the transaction of the row, with identifiers, the code, the queue code and the rule version and no personal data | DP-09, DP-14; TSD S8 T5.2.1, T5.3 |
| BR9 | The service identity that runs the placement holds the Case record letters of TSD S8 T6.1 and a person needs Case record right U for the raise; a caller without it is refused 403 | TSD S8 T6.1, T6.2; legacy section 10 |

##### 9. State transitions

The case state, its queue, its assignment and its two clocks are rwb-case's and this story does not change them: the step returns the placement and the parent applies it (BR5). This story owns the `deviation.state` of the record it writes, over the 9 DEVIATION states of TSD S8 T4.

| From (`deviation.state`) | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| No row | - | The case has no open deviation | Unchanged; the answer is NO_DEVIATION and nothing is written (AC4) |
| DEV_FLAGGED | DEVIATION_FLAGGED | The open code is X1 to X7 | DEV_FLAGGED on R-DEV-01 |
| DEV_FLAGGED | OWNER_ASSIGNED | The code rule names an owner: X2 or X3 (R-DEV-03), X4 (R-DEV-04), X5 (R-DEV-05), X6 or X7 (R-DEV-06) | DEV_WITH_OWNER |
| DEV_FLAGGED | OWNER_ASSIGNED | The code is outside X1 to X7, or no owner is set for it | DEV_WITH_OWNER with the team manager and the code recorded as unmapped (R-DEV-21) |
| DEV_WITH_OWNER | OWNER_ASSIGNED | A handler is already set | Unchanged; the existing handler is answered and nothing is rewritten (X5) |

| Step execution | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Waiting | The parent presents a case for a business date | The DEV package version in force is loaded | Evaluating |
| Evaluating | R-DEV-01 and one code rule fire | The parameter and the handler candidates are available | Applying |
| Applying | The decision record, the row update and the outbox row commit | The transaction commits | Answered, placement returned to the parent |
| Applying | The record write or the transaction fails | X1, X2 | Waiting, nothing changed, MSG-P7-003 or MSG-P3-027 |
| Answered | The same case and business date arrive again | X7 | Unchanged, the recorded placement is answered and the repeat is counted |

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Hardship and vulnerability specialist (RW-SPECIAL) | Holds RU on the case record (TSD S8 T6.1) and is the handler R-DEV-03 names for X2 and X3 |
| Fraud investigator (RW-FRAUD) | Holds RU and is the handler R-DEV-04 names for X4 |
| Legal counsel (RW-LEGAL) | Holds R, joins X3 for the estate claim on R-DEV-03 and is the handler R-DEV-05 names for X5 |
| Complaint officer (RW-COMPLAIN) | Holds RU and is the X1 handler of R-DEV-02, which stays with RWB-S8-E7001-APP |
| Case owner (RW-CASEOWN) | Holds CRU and is the "case owner" whose team manager R-DEV-21 names, and the owner the agent works with on R-DEV-06 |
| Team manager (RW-TEAMMGR) | Holds R, receives the X3, X4, X5, X6, X7 and unmapped placements as the named owner where the rule names a team, and reads SCR-08 |
| SY-CASEWF, case workflow module | Presents the case as the parent workflow and applies the placement; it writes no deviation row |
| SY-RULES, rules component | Evaluates the DEV package version in force and returns the rule ID with its output (R-DEV-01, R-DEV-03 to R-DEV-06, R-DEV-21) |
| rwb-access (P4) | Owns the roles and the rights of TSD S8 T6.1 that the guard checks |
| rwb-decision (P7) | Owns the DEV package, its rows and their versions, and the central ledger; this service only evaluates and records |

No delegated authority limit applies: a placement takes no credit decision and approves nothing, and the only approval in the module is the insurance claim of X3, which is not this story's. The database login is per service (DP-02) and its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3073; ASM-5233).

| DF-CAS-038, DF-CAS-041, DF-CAS-043 | `deviation` | S8, `rwb_deviation` | **Read**: the code, the paused state and the contact stop of the open deviation the placement is about |

| None: library table | `outbox_event`, `idempotency_key`, `processed_event` | Platform library in `rwb_deviation` | The `DeviationRaised` row, the placement key with its answer and the inbox of the parent's presentation |

The placement writes no new column: the handler queue is not a column of `deviation` (TSD S8 T3.1), because the queue belongs to the case and to the parameter, and the row carries only the handler and the state (`handler_user_id`, `state`). The codes and the lists are the LOV-DEVIATION, LOV-RAISED-BY and LOV-DEV-OUTCOME values of TSD S8 T3.2, read at their version through DP-07. No personal value enters `rwb_deviation`, the record, the event or a log: `case_id` and `handler_user_id` are references to other services' facts, and no customer name, contact value or address is copied.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None new in this story. The two operations the Ownership Map gives rwb-deviation stay exactly as the service baseline publishes them on base `/api/recovery/deviation/v1` (DP-13), and this story adds no path, no element and no status:

| ID | Method | Path | What this story decides behind it |
|---|---|---|---|
| API-S8-001 | POST | `/cases/{caseId}/deviations` | The handler queue code and the handler of a raise for the codes X2 to X7 and for an unmapped code, through the same engine the parent calls; the X1 raise stays RWB-S8-E7001-APP's. Case record U, `Idempotency-Key` |
| API-S8-002 | PATCH | `/deviations/{deviationId}` | Nothing: the outcome path is RWB-S8-E7001-APP's and the other code stories'. Case record U |

Both keep the error set 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404, 409, 422 and 503 of TSD S8 T-A.2, each in the platform problem envelope. The morning entry of the allocation is not a REST call: rwb-case starts the child workflow (12.5), because the S8 row of the connection matrix names Temporal and events to P3 and never REST (ASM-5230).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None for this slice. The case and its open deviation arrive on the Temporal boundary defined by `RWB-P3-E1020-CON`, and the queue and its members travel in the same element, so no hop is added and the one-hop 2 s rule of DP-11 is untouched. The element names of the case input and of the stage outcome are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3072; ASM-5230). The P1 party-flag read and the P10 agent run of TSD S8 T5.2.2 are the screening stories' and are not consumed here.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Data | Consumers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DeviationRaised` (EV-06, `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1`) | `rwb.deviation.events.v1`, with `.retry` and `.dlt` | Case reference, deviation reference, code, raised-at, the queue code, the rule ID and version; CloudEvents 1.0, key `caseId`; no personal data | rwb-case, rwb-comms, rwb-treatment (TSD S8 T5.2.1) |
| `DecisionRecorded` (EV-08, `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1`) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | The placement record of DP-03, relayed by the library | rwb-decision, for the central ledger (DP-03) |

`DeviationCleared` (EV-07) is not published by this story: nothing is cleared at a placement, and the clear path is RWB-S8-E7001-APP's. The pairing of the id EV-06 with the name `DeviationRaised` is taken from TSD S8 T0.2 and T5.2.1 (ASM-5234).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The case is presented by its parent as a child workflow, not as an event, so this slice subscribes to nothing; the `CaseCreated` (EV-01), `AceDataReady` (EV-26) and `AgentRunCompleted` (EV-28) subscriptions of TSD S8 T5.2.2 belong to the screening and agent-run stories of this service.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Queue | Element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DeviationWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per case, started by rwb-case as the child of `CaseWorkflow`, parent close policy ABANDON, continues-as-new | `rwb-deviation` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Hosts the handler-placement branch; its input carries the case element of `RWB-P3-E1020-CON` and its result is the stage outcome the parent applies |
| `evaluateHandlerRules` | Activity, the EvaluateRules step | `rwb-deviation` | The case, the open deviation and the business date in; the rule ID, the package version, the queue code and the handler out |
| `recordAndApplyPlacement` | Activity, the RecordAndApply step | `rwb-deviation` | The decision in; the decision record, the row update, the outbox row and the stage outcome out, one transaction |

The stage outcome carries the case reference, the deviation reference, the queue code, the handler reference, the rule IDs with their versions and PLACE_DEVIATION_QUEUE or NO_DEVIATION; the parent places the case and pauses its own clock (ASM-5230). The names of the outcome element and of its fields are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3072; ASM-5230).

None. The Ownership Map gives S8 no job, and the morning allocation stays JOB-03 of rwb-case: this story starts no Schedule, reads no Quartz row and declares no batch table (context pack ownership rows; DP-10).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.deviation`, module `deviation/handler-placement`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.deviation.placement`.

**Pattern application** (R5.5)

| DP | Legacy marker | Pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_deviation`; never read another service's tables | None |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | None |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | None |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/deviation/v1` | None |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.deviation.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in `rwb_deviation` | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

What each DP means for this slice:

- DP-01 is the reason the queue, the members and the case facts arrive on the P3 contract: `recovery_case`, `queue`, `queue_member` and `assignment` are P3's and no statement of this story names them.
- DP-03 is the placement record: the deviation's decision is written before the row and before the event, in the same transaction.
- DP-04 is the DEV package: the rule rows and their version are governed in rwb-decision and evaluated here by the service's own kit, which is why the kit row and the P7 registry row appear here and not in the metadata, whose C row carries `RWB-P3-E1020-CON` alone (GAP-3073; ASM-5233).
- DP-05 is recorded because the legacy key reads ACE data (`v_ace_batch_status`) for its batch gate: the gate is P1's in the target and the case arrives from a run that has already passed it, so this service reads no view.
- DP-06 is the handler queue code and DP-07 the three lists; both are read on the P3 contracts with their version, and a new value moves the case with no deployment.
- DP-09 and DP-14 are the single event of the placement on the one topic of the service, with the retry and `.dlt` topics of the naming rule.
- DP-10 is the workflow kit behind the child and DP-11 the one-hop rule that keeps the boundary a Temporal call rather than a second REST hop.
- DP-13 moves the base of the two operations, DP-15 puts the one migration in the `rwb_deviation` sequence, and DP-19 puts SCR-08 and SCR-02 behind the composite route.
- DP-02 and DP-08 are the service's own patterns in TSD S8 T0.3 and are already in place at the baseline; the plan's pattern set for this key does not carry them (ASM-5233).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| DeviationWorkflow (placement branch) | Workflow | Receives the case from the parent, runs the two activities and returns the stage outcome |
| HandlerQueueRule | Service | Reads `allocation.deviation.queue.code` and answers the queue code of a placement, with no value in code |
| HandlerAssignmentEngine | Service | Applies the fired code rule, reads the queue members on the P3 contract and picks the handler with the fewest open deviations |
| OpenDeviationQuery | Service | Reads the case's open deviation from `deviation` and answers NONE, OPEN or ALREADY_ASSIGNED |
| PlacementRecordWriter | Service | Writes the decision record, the row update and the two outbox rows in one transaction (DP-03, DP-09) |
| HandlerPlacementRepository | Repository | `deviation`, the decision record, the outbox, the inbox and the idempotency key in `rwb_deviation`; no foreign table |
| PlacementController | Controller | The placement element of the two published operations, behind the service's DeviationHandlingController; validation and problem responses |

**Database and migrations.** One migration in the per-service Flyway sequence of DP-15: `V1020_1__placement_indexes.sql` adds `ix_deviation_case_state` on `deviation (case_id, state)` and `ix_deviation_handler_state` on `deviation (handler_user_id, state)`, so the open-deviation read and the handler load are index reads. No column is added: the queue code is not a column of `deviation`, and no business value is written in the migration.

**Configuration and reference data.** The parameter `allocation.deviation.queue.code` through DP-06 and the three lists through DP-07; the queues and their members from P3; the DEV package version from P7. The value "DEV-HANDLER" is the DL23 assumed value and lives in the parameter row, never in the code (ASM-5232).

**Build steps.** (1) Wire the placement branch of `DeviationWorkflow` and the two activities on `rwb-deviation`. (2) `OpenDeviationQuery` against `deviation`, with the four answers. (3) `HandlerQueueRule` over the parameters contract and `HandlerAssignmentEngine` over the members of the P3 contract and the open-deviation count. (4) `PlacementRecordWriter` with the record first, the row update, the two outbox rows and the idempotency key in one transaction. (5) The stage outcome and its PLACE_DEVIATION_QUEUE and NO_DEVIATION values. (6) The placement element of the two published operations. (7) The migration and its index tests. (8) Prove AC1 to AC7 on the fakes.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.s8.handler-placement`. Off: a presentation answers NO_DEVIATION and the case is allocated by the rules of rwb-case as if this service had not been called; no row, no record and no event are written. It needs no schema rollback and blocks no raise.

**Done when.** AC1 to AC7 pass at component level on the fakes; a placement writes one record, one row update and one event; a forced record failure leaves nothing changed; a repeat writes nothing; the boundary test shows no `v_ace_*` read and no `rwb_case` statement; and SCR-08 answers through the gateway-bff route.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written before the change (X1) | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P3-027 | No DEV package version is in force at the presentation (X2) | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A caller without Case record right U raises a deviation (BR9) | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The data product behind the case facts is stale (VR-S8-004-1) | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |

The four messages are the legacy and FSD S8 wording, copied unchanged; the placement itself adds no new message, and the overflow, exception and deviation counts of the morning summary stay with the allocation's own MSG-P3-011 and MSG-P3-012 in rwb-case. The Thai text follows DL10.

Both screens are the edge contract's (DP-19) and the composite route also calls rwb-case for the case, its owner and its timers; this story fixes only its own answers and builds no screen of its own. ##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the deviation codes, the handler roles, the state names and the handler queue code are rule rows, list values or parameter rows read at their version (BR3, BR4).
- No personal data in the row, the decision record, an event, a workflow input, a log or a prompt: case and handler references, codes, instants and a rule version only (NFR-039, NFR-040).
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: no `v_ace_*` view, no ACE table, no other service's schema and no copy of a party flag (DP-01, DP-05).
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; this story adds no second topic and no Schedule (DP-13, DP-14, DP-10).
- The decision record is written before the change and in its transaction; a failure rolls the row back and diverts nothing (DP-03).
- The placement is idempotent per case and business date, and the repeat counter is the only effect of a second presentation (BR7).
- The queue, the members and the caps stay with rwb-case: this story answers a queue code and a handler and never moves a case, assigns a case owner or pauses a clock itself (BR5).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-020 for rwb-case. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform administrator (RW-PLATADM)**, I want **the allocation worker of rwb-case, its DailyCaseRun schedule, its topic with retry and dead-letter topics, its metrics, its alerts, its runbook and its feature-flag rollout deployed as code**, so that **the morning allocation runs by itself by 07:00 with no Quartz table, no manual start and no silent failure**.

This is the deployment slice of legacy RWB-E1-020 in rwb-case. It delivers, all through the platform Helm chart and the service pipeline:

- the **worker deployment** of rwb-case that polls task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and scales on backlog;
- the **DailyCaseRun** Temporal Schedule registration, and the event-started run that `AceDataReady` triggers; the legacy job name **JOB-03 Morning allocation** is kept in the runbook, the dashboards and the alerts, and the legacy Quartz trigger is gone;
- the **topic provisioning** of `rwb.case.events.v1` with its retry topics (1 min, 10 min, 1 h) and its `.dlt`, the ACLs for the consumers, and the producer side of `rwb.decision-record.v1`;
- the **allocation metrics and alerts**: cases read, assigned, overflow, exception, failed, skipped, the four family messages, the stuck-run alert and the dead-letter alert;
- the **runbook** for the morning run, carrying the legacy RWB-E1-056 job monitoring content;
- the **feature-flag rollout** of `rwb.case.allocation`, with the flag as data in the platform library.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story depended on a Quartz job on a shared scheduler and on a job monitor that a person had to read. Nothing was deployed per service and nothing scaled on load. In the target the allocation engine is one worker of one service, with its own task queue, its own topic and its own dashboards, so the morning run either finishes by 07:00 or raises an alarm that names the run, the case count and the reason.

The cost of a silent failure is high: if the morning allocation does not run, every new case stays NEW with no queue and no owner, and the service level of the whole book starts to slip on the first day. The alerts and the runbook are therefore part of the story, not an afterthought.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The rwb-case service is created from the service template with its Helm chart, its golden pipeline and its `api` and `worker` deployments (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-LIB).
- Schema `rwb_case` and the service login exist (RWB-PLT-DB); the per-service login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0684; ASM-1231), so the chart takes it from a Key Vault reference and never from a value in the repository.
- The Temporal cluster is at 1.30 or later, namespace `rwb-recovery` exists and task queue `rwb-case` is agreed (RWB-PLT-WF).
- The Kafka platform accepts the topic definitions of the service (RWB-PLT-EVT); Azure Event Hubs Premium is the fallback.
- The workflow kit is available for the Schedule and the event-started workflow (RWB-PLT-E1071-CON), and the outbox and inbox library for the producer side (RWB-PLT-TE006-CON).
- The feature-flag library is available (platform library), and the contract of 12.1 is published (RWB-P3-E1020-CON).
- The build of the allocation engine can be absent: this story deploys and wires, and the flag keeps the path closed until the build story is accepted.

##### 4. Flow

1. **Chart and values.** The worker deployment, the service account, the Key Vault references, the resource requests and limits, the horizontal autoscaling on task-queue backlog, the pod disruption budget, the readiness and liveness probes, the OpenTelemetry exporter and the log format are set in the Helm values of the service.
2. **Database access.** The chart mounts the service login and connection pool from Key Vault; the Flyway migration of the allocation columns runs as a pre-deploy job in the rwb-case sequence (DP-15). No schema outside `rwb_case` is granted.
3. **Temporal.** The worker connects to namespace `rwb-recovery` and polls only `rwb-case`; the payload codec keys come from Key Vault; the build ID is published to the worker versioning record so a new build takes new runs while the old drains.
4. **Schedules.** The DailyCaseRun Schedule is created by the deployment, idempotently, with overlap policy SKIP, a catch-up window and the business-date input; the JOB-06 rebalancing Schedule at 06:30 is registered on the same queue. The exact schedule expression of the date-based run is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0686; ASM-1233), so it is a value in the chart and not a constant in code.
5. **Kafka.** The topic `rwb.case.events.v1` is created with the platform defaults (12 partitions, replication factor 3, 7-day retention, key caseId, CloudEvents binary mode), with `rwb.case.events.v1.retry.1m`, `.retry.10m`, `.retry.1h` and `rwb.case.events.v1.dlt`; ACLs allow rwb-case to produce, and the documented consumers to read; the producer side of `rwb.decision-record.v1` is granted.
6. **Observability.** Counters and histograms for cases read, assigned, overflow, exception, failed and skipped; a timer for the run duration; a gauge for the last successful run per business date; counters for the four message identifiers and for the dead-letter topic; one trace from the event to the transaction, with the case number as an attribute and no personal data.
7. **Alerts.** Alert on: no successful DailyCaseRun for the current business date by the agreed deadline; a run with any FAILED_LOG case; a non-empty dead-letter topic; `NoPackageInForce` raised by the activity; the workflow stuck for longer than the agreed window; the schedule not registered after a deployment. Thresholds live in the chart values and are reviewed with the service owner.
8. **Runbook.** One page: what the run is, when it runs, how to see the run in the Temporal UI, how to see the counts, how to retry a business date, how to check the rule model version, how to re-drive the dead-letter topic, whom to call for the rule package and for the database. The legacy RWB-E1-056 job monitoring content is carried into it, including the JOB-03 entry and the MSG-P1-001 waiting state.
9. **Rollout.** The flag `rwb.case.allocation` is created off, switched on in DEV, then SIT, then UAT, then PROD, each step after the alerts are proven by a forced failure in that environment; the legacy flag name `rwb.p3.allocation` is retired.
10. **Rollback.** Turn the flag off: DailyCaseRun stops and cases stay NEW, as in the legacy behaviour. The Schedule is paused, not deleted, so the run can be resumed without a deployment.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | The worker cannot reach the Temporal frontend | The pod fails readiness and is restarted; runs stay on the queue and are not lost | None | AC1 |
| D2 | The schedule is missing after a deployment | The deployment fails its post-deploy check; an alert fires; the schedule is recreated idempotently | None | AC2 |
| D3 | A message fails three retries | It lands on the dead-letter topic and the alert fires with the case number | None | AC3 |
| D4 | The dead-letter topic has messages | The alert fires; the runbook re-drive step is used after the fix | None | AC3, AC4 |
| D5 | The connection pool or the login secret is unavailable | The pod does not start; the pre-deploy check stops the release | None | AC1 |
| D6 | `NoPackageInForce` is raised by the activity | The run stops at once and the alert fires; the last good model is kept | MSG-P3-027 | AC4 |
| D7 | The run has not finished by the deadline | The alert fires with the business date and the cases still NEW | MSG-P1-001 where the cause is a late batch | AC4 |
| D8 | The flag is switched off during a run | The run in flight completes; no new run starts | None | AC5 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs only the platform pieces of wave 0, the service template chart, the contract of RWB-P3-E1020-CON and the naming of rwb-case; no engine code |
| Negotiable | Replica counts, resource sizes and alert thresholds are values; the schedule, the topic names, the metric names and the runbook steps are fixed |
| Valuable | Turns a person-read job monitor into an alarm that names the run, and removes the shared Quartz dependency from the morning chain |
| Estimable | One chart, one schedule registration, six topics, one dashboard, six alerts, one runbook |
| Small | Two weeks or less including the environment rollout |
| Testable | Five criteria, each with an NFR-level test in section 16 |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Deployment of the allocation worker and the DailyCaseRun schedule

  Background:
    Given the rwb-case service chart of the template and the golden pipeline
    Given namespace rwb-recovery, task queue rwb-case and topic rwb.case.events.v1
```
