    Given the chart values of rwb-case for the environment
    When the release is installed in that environment
    Then the worker deployment polls only task queue rwb-case in namespace rwb-recovery and runs under the rwb-case login taken from a Key Vault reference
    Then the deployment sets resource requests and limits, a readiness probe, a liveness probe, a pod disruption budget and a horizontal autoscaler bound to the task-queue backlog
    Then the worker publishes its build ID for worker versioning and reads its payload codec keys from Key Vault
    Then the pre-deploy job applies the rwb-case Flyway sequence and fails the release if the schema grant reaches any schema other than rwb_case
    Then the deployment exports traces and metrics through OpenTelemetry and logs without personal data

  Scenario: AC2 The DailyCaseRun schedule is registered and is idempotent (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the deployment of the worker has completed
    When the post-deploy check runs twice
    Then exactly one DailyCaseRun Schedule exists for rwb-case, with overlap policy SKIP, a catch-up window and the business date as input
    Then the JOB-06 rebalancing Schedule at 06:30 Asia/Bangkok is registered on the same queue
    Then a second deployment does not create a duplicate schedule and does not reset the last run
    Then an `AceDataReady` event for the same business date starts nothing new while the run for that date exists

  Scenario: AC3 The topic, the retry topics and the dead-letter topic are provisioned (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the topic definitions of the service
    When the topic provisioning runs
    Then rwb.case.events.v1 exists with 12 partitions, replication factor 3, 7-day retention, key caseId, CloudEvents binary mode, and rwb.case.events.v1.retry.1m, rwb.case.events.v1.retry.10m, rwb.case.events.v1.retry.1h and rwb.case.events.v1.dlt exist with the same settings
    Then the ACLs let rwb-case produce on its topic and on rwb.decision-record.v1 and let the documented consumers read, and let no other principal write
    Then a message that fails three retries lands on the dead-letter topic and no message is lost
    Then the consumer side dedupes through its inbox table and a duplicate delivery changes nothing

  Scenario: AC4 The allocation metrics and alerts are live (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the dashboards and the alert rules of the service
    When the morning run completes, and when a run is forced to fail
    Then the dashboard shows cases read, assigned, overflow, exception, failed and skipped for the business date, the run duration and the last successful run
    Then an alert fires when no run has succeeded for the current business date by the agreed deadline, when any case ends FAILED_LOG, when the dead-letter topic is not empty, when NoPackageInForce is raised, and when the run is stuck past the agreed window
    Then every alert names the service, the environment, the business date and the run, and links to the runbook
    Then no metric, log line or trace attribute carries personal data

  Scenario: AC5 The runbook and the feature-flag rollout are in place (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the runbook and the feature flag of the service
    When the release is promoted from DEV to SIT, UAT and PROD
    Then rwb.case.allocation exists in the platform flag library, off by default, and is the only switch that starts or stops DailyCaseRun
    Then each environment proves the alerts with a forced failure before the flag is switched on
    Then switching the flag off pauses the schedule, starts no new run and leaves cases NEW, and switching it on resumes the schedule without a deployment
    Then the runbook carries the JOB-03 entry and the MSG-P1-001 waiting state from legacy RWB-E1-056, and the steps to retry a business date, re-drive the dead-letter topic and check the rule model version
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | No value in the chart that a business person may change: the schedule expression, the deadline, the alert thresholds, the replica bounds and the topic names are values, not constants | Principle 1; DP-06 |
| BR2 | The worker polls only its own task queue and writes only its own schema; no grant reaches another schema | DP-01; Arch v5 slide 11 |
| BR3 | Secrets come from Key Vault by reference; no credential is written in the repository or in a values file | Arch v5 slide 8 |
| BR4 | The topic follows the platform standard: 12 partitions, replication factor 3, 7-day retention, key caseId, CloudEvents binary mode, retry at 1 min, 10 min and 1 h, then the dead-letter topic with an alert | Arch v5 slide 9 |
| BR5 | The Schedule uses overlap policy SKIP and a catch-up window, and a duplicate `AceDataReady` starts nothing new | DP-10; Arch v5 slide 44 |
| BR6 | With the flag off, DailyCaseRun does not run and cases stay NEW; the schedule is paused, not deleted | Legacy `rwb.p3.allocation`; DP-06 |
| BR7 | Every alert is actionable and names the run; an alert without a runbook step is not accepted | Arch v5 slide 35; JOB-21 |
| BR8 | No personal data in metrics, logs or trace attributes: the case number is the identifier | Arch v5 slide 11; PDPA |
| BR9 | The legacy job name JOB-03 and the legacy message identifiers stay in the runbook and the dashboards after the Quartz trigger is removed | Template §R6; legacy RWB-E1-020 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | Release installed | Chart and values valid, pre-deploy migration passed | Deployed, flag off |
| Deployed, flag off | Flag switched on | Alerts proven in the environment | Live, schedule active |
| Live | Flag switched off | Rollback decided | Paused, schedule paused |
| Live | Run started | Schedule fired or `AceDataReady` received | Run in progress |
| Run in progress | Run finished | Every selected case handled | Run succeeded or run failed, alert raised |

The case states are unchanged by this story; it only controls whether the run that moves them is deployed, active or paused.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** Service chart and environment values; the schedule registration job; the topic and ACL definitions; the dashboard and the six alert rules; the runbook page; the feature-flag definition and the rollout record per environment.

**Build steps**

1. Extend the service chart with the worker deployment, the autoscaler, the probes, the disruption budget and the Key Vault references.
2. Add the pre-deploy migration job and the boundary check on the schema grant.
3. Add the schedule registration as an idempotent post-deploy job for DailyCaseRun and the JOB-06 schedule.
4. Add the topic, retry and dead-letter provisioning and the ACLs to the environment pipeline.
5. Add the dashboard, the metrics and the six alert rules, each with a runbook link.
6. Write the runbook page from the legacy RWB-E1-056 monitoring content and the new run.
7. Roll the flag through DEV, SIT, UAT and PROD, forcing a failure in each environment to prove the alerts.
8. Record the rollout and the rollback rehearsal in the environment log.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.case.allocation` in the platform flag library, off by default, dated for removal once the run has been stable for a full business cycle. The legacy flag `rwb.p3.allocation` is retired.

**Done when.** The release installs in every environment from the pipeline; the schedule exists exactly once after two deployments; the topics and ACLs are as in AC3; the six alerts fire in the forced-failure test and name the run; the runbook is published and reviewed; the flag rollout record is complete.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-011 | Allocation summary, case in overflow | {count} new cases are waiting in the overflow queue for {team}. Every owner is at the caseload cap. |
| MSG-P3-012 | Allocation summary, no rule matched | {count} new cases matched no allocation rule and are in the exception queue. |
| MSG-P3-013 | Decision record write failed for a case | The case was not allocated because the decision could not be recorded. It will be tried again in the next run. |
| MSG-P3-027 | No package version is in force | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The run is waiting because the ACE batch has not completed | {product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived. |

The alert text of each rule is written in the chart values and names the service, the environment, the business date and the run; the message identifiers above stay on the dashboard and in the runbook so the operations team sees the same wording as the screens.

##### 15. Screens and states

The run monitor replaces the legacy job monitor tile of JOB-03. Its states are: Not scheduled, Scheduled, Waiting for the business date (with MSG-P1-001), Run in progress (with cases read so far), Run succeeded (with counts), Run failed (with the reason and the link to the runbook), Paused by flag. The case screens are unchanged: SCR-02 Case list and SCR-09 Exception queue read the result of the run through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).

##### 17. Guardrails

- **G1 No business value in the chart.** The schedule expression, the deadline, the thresholds, the replica bounds and the topic settings are values with a documented default.
- **G2 No credential in the repository.** Every secret is a Key Vault reference.
- **G3 No cross-schema grant.** The pre-deploy check fails the release if the login can read or write any schema other than `rwb_case`.
- **G4 No personal data in telemetry.** Metrics, logs and trace attributes carry the case number only.
- **G5 Every alert has a runbook step** and names the run, the environment and the business date.
- **G6 The schedule is paused, never deleted,** so a rollback needs no deployment.
- **G7 No shared Quartz table.** The legacy trigger of JOB-03 is removed; nothing in this story writes the ACE shared scheduler tables.

##### 1. Story

As a **QA integration engineer**, I want **the end-to-end proof of the RWB-E1-020 allocation and assignment engine across rwb-case (the JOB-03 step of DailyCaseRun, the two package evaluations, the case commit with its outbox row and the allocation events), rwb-decision (the package registry with its checksum and the central decision ledger), rwb-access (the Platform administration right that guards a rerun) and rwb-deviation (the deviation event that sends a case to the deviation handler queue)**, so that **every new case is queued and owned by rule before 07:00, at most once per business date, with its decision record in the central ledger, and the wait on case creation is proved on the real services before wave 1 exits**.

##### 2. Business rationale

RWB-E1-020 places every new recovery case in a queue and gives it an owner by the ALLOCATION and ASSIGNMENT rule packages on the morning the case arrives, so that no case at 90 days past due waits with no owner and nobody allocates by hand. The component copy of the behaviour already exists: RWB-P3-E1020-APP owns the legacy criteria AC1 to AC9 and AC11 to AC13 in rwb-case, against the published contracts of the services it needs. This integration story owns the one criterion a single service cannot prove: AC10, the run waits for case creation. The fact AC10 turns on is not produced inside the allocating step at all — the JOB-02 step of the same run must have completed for the business date, and the readiness signal that starts the run belongs to rwb-source-data — so an assertion made inside rwb-case alone would pass while the gate itself was wrong.

The rest of what this story proves is cross-service in the same way. The rule packages are governed in rwb-decision and only evaluated locally, so a suite that read a local table would never notice an unapproved or unchecksummed version reaching the run. The decision record of an allocation commits in rwb-case but is collected into the central ledger of rwb-decision within five minutes (ADR-022), and an assertion on the local record alone would pass while the ledger stayed empty. The allocation facts leave as `rwb.case.CaseAllocated.v1` and `rwb.case.CaseAllocationFailed.v1` on the owner's topic, and a case with an open deviation is diverted on the event of rwb-deviation rather than on a flag read from another service's table. None of those can be proved inside one service.

The legacy story runs JOB-03 as a Quartz job (D-RCV-36 T2), writes the decision log entry through a published interface of the case module, and reads the target queue, the cap and the rule rows from the monolith schema. The target delta is the mechanism and the delivery path, not the behaviour. DP-10 makes JOB-03 a step of DailyCaseRun in rwb-case, started by AceDataReady for the business date and complete by 07:00, with no Quartz table and no second timer (Arch v5 slide 44). DP-04 makes rwb-decision the registry: each version carries its SHA-256, the service fetches both packages, verifies the checksum and evaluates its own copy inside the EvaluateRules activity, so no shared rule server sits on the hot path. DP-03 splits the record: the local record commits in `rwb_case` with the case change in one transaction and leaves as `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` for the ledger of rwb-decision. DP-09 and DP-14 keep the announcement on `rwb.case.events.v1` in the CloudEvents envelope, key caseId, IDs and facts only. DP-13 renames the base to `/api/recovery/<short>/v1`, DP-05 keeps the ACE views behind rwb-source-data, DP-06 and DP-07 read the parameters and the lists as data through the rwb-case contracts, DP-01 keeps `recovery_case`, `queue`, `queue_member`, `assignment` and the local record in `rwb_case`, DP-15 gives each service its own Flyway sequence, and DP-19 puts any screen behind gateway-bff.

No service contract is faked in this story: the four integration dependencies are the real services on their published contracts, and a fake would defeat the purpose of the run. What the sources do not fix is the surface the suite reads the JOB-03 run through — the catalogue read and the rerun belong to the rwb-source-data job catalogue while the run itself is a workflow step of rwb-case — and it is recorded as GAP-0345 with ASM-0439. The legacy values stay as they are: packages "ALLOC-2026.11" and "ASSIGN-2026.11", queues "MTG-BKK-CO", "MTG-BKK-OVF", "RWB-EXC" and "DEV-HANDLER", the cap of 150, the business date 2026-12-01 and the criterion of 07:00. Release 30 November 2026 is tentative and is never a condition of this story.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P3-E1020-APP is done: the JOB-03 step of DailyCaseRun, the two `RuleEvaluator` calls for ALLOCATION and ASSIGNMENT, the assignment engine with its cap and round-robin cursor, the idempotency of the business date, the allocation summary and the allocation case reads are in SIT on rwb-case.
- RWB-P7-E1020-APP is done: the package versions of ALLOCATION and ASSIGNMENT with their checksums, the rule-package version list, the rollback and the central decision ledger are published by rwb-decision.
- RWB-P4-E1020-APP is done: the Platform administration right U and its refusal on the administrative operations are enforced by rwb-access.
- RWB-S8-E1020-APP is done: `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1` leaves rwb-deviation on `rwb.deviation.events.v1` for the case that is screened, and the deviation flag is observable through the owners' contracts.
- The published contracts of P3, P4, P7 and S8 are versioned in the registry, and the harness consumes only those contracts; the suite opens no service schema.
- The harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG is available with its synthetic case set, its synthetic queues and members and its caps for business date 2026-12-01.
- SIT is in place: the Temporal namespace `rwb-recovery`, the task queues `rwb-case`, `rwb-decision`, `rwb-access` and `rwb-deviation`, and the topics `rwb.case.events.v1`, `rwb.decision-record.v1`, `rwb.decision.events.v1` and `rwb.deviation.events.v1` with their retry and `.dlt` topics, plus the schema registry.
- The agreed test-only fault switch on the decision-record library of rwb-case can fail the record write for one case (AC20) and for every case of a run (TC-E1-020-15-ITG), and its use is agreed with the rwb-case owner.
- No production data is read, copied or connected to; every case number, owner id, queue code, product group and region used by the run is synthetic.
- This story has no build dependency, so it is ready on Day 1 under Template and Rules §R5.7. The release date 30 November 2026 is tentative and is copied unchanged.

##### 4. Flow

1. QA integration engineer: records the package evidence through `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/approvals` and `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions` for ALLOCATION and ASSIGNMENT — the version in force from 2026-11-30, the approver role RW-RISK and the SHA-256 of each version — then seeds the synthetic cases, queues, members and caps of the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG for business date 2026-12-01; no production data is used.
2. Harness: waits on `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` on `rwb.decision.events.v1` for the promotion of "ALLOC-2026.11" and "ASSIGN-2026.11" by the JOB-20 promote at 00:01, so that both packages are in force before any case is asserted.
3. Harness: publishes the readiness signal for 2026-12-01 through the P1 readiness operation and confirms that DailyCaseRun started on queue `rwb-case` for that business date, with the JOB-02 step before the JOB-03 step.
4. System: the JOB-02 step creates the new cases with status NEW, product group, region and exposure band; the JOB-03 step then selects every NEW case whose `last_allocation_date` is before the business date and allocates it through the two packages.
5. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases` for the cases of 2026-12-01 and then `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` for each one, asserting status "ASSIGNED", the queue, the team, the owner and the ALLOCATION package version on the case record.
6. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues` for the queue codes, the method, the cap of 150 and the overflow queue of "MTG-BKK-CO", then `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/cases` for "MTG-BKK-OVF", "RWB-EXC" and "DEV-HANDLER" and reconciles every count of the run with the case reads and the two summary lines MSG-P3-011 and MSG-P3-012.
7. Harness: consumes `rwb.case.CaseAllocated.v1` and `rwb.case.CaseAllocationFailed.v1` on `rwb.case.events.v1` and asserts the CloudEvents envelope, the key caseId, the case number, the queue code and the absence of any personal data field.
8. Harness: waits on `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` for every allocation, reads `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` and measures the elapsed collection of each record against the five-minute target, asserting exactly one record per allocation with rule ID and package version.
9. Harness: moves the clock past 07:00 on a business date whose ALS batch row is not COMPLETE in `v_ace_batch_status`, reads the job catalogue through `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs` and asserts that the JOB-03 step has not started, that the monitor line carries MSG-P1-001 and that every NEW case keeps no queue and no owner (AC10).
10. Harness: runs the remaining controls — the rerun of the same business date through `POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs/JOB-03/rerun`, the rerun by an identity without Platform administration U, the rollback of the ALLOCATION version and its promote back for the held date, the deviation event of S8, and the forced record failure of AC20 — records every status, message and count, proves from the call set of the run that no service schema and no Quartz table was read, then writes the evidence report, removes the synthetic fixtures and restores the clock and the packages.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The JOB-02 step has not completed for the business date | The JOB-03 step does not start for that date, no case is allocated, and the run shows the waiting line for the predecessor step | MSG-P1-001 | AC10 |
| X2 | No ALLOCATION or ASSIGNMENT version is in force on the business date | The run is refused before any case is touched, the whole business date is held, every case keeps status "NEW" and the run record names the package code | MSG-P3-027 | AC16 |
| X3 | A package version is fetched with a checksum that does not match the one held by rwb-decision | The version is refused, the run stops before the first allocation, and the evidence report names the package and the version | None | AC12 |
| X4 | A case has an open deviation, raised on `rwb.deviation.events.v1` | The case goes to the deviation handler queue "DEV-HANDLER" with no case owner and status "NEW", and no CaseAllocated event leaves for it | None | AC15 |
| X5 | Every owner of the target queue is at the cap of 150 | The case goes to the overflow queue named by the ASSIGNMENT row, keeps status "NEW", and is counted in the summary | MSG-P3-011 | AC18 |
| X6 | No ALLOCATION rule matches the case | The case goes to the exception queue "RWB-EXC", the rule gap is recorded, and `rwb.case.CaseAllocationFailed.v1` leaves with reason "NO_ROW_MATCHED" | MSG-P3-012 | AC14, AC18 |
| X7 | The decision record of one case cannot be written | That case is not allocated and stays "NEW" with no queue and no owner, the rest of the run continues, and the run record names the case | MSG-P3-013 | AC20 |
| X8 | The same business date is run again | The cases already allocated for the date are skipped, so no second assignment and no second ledger entry exists | None | AC17 |
| X9 | A second rerun reaches a case the first run still holds | The case row lock stops the second worker, and each case is allocated once; a rerun of a run still in flight is refused as a conflict | MSG-GEN-004 | AC17, TC-E1-020-11-ITG |
| X10 | An identity without Platform administration U reruns the JOB-03 step | The call is refused with status 403, no run starts and no case is allocated | MSG-P4-002 | AC19, TC-E1-020-14-ITG |
| X11 | A consumed contract drifts from the published one (path, field, status or event schema) | The preflight fails on the contract test and the run stops before any assertion; the drift is reported against the owning service and no fake is put in its place | None | Preflight, AC11 |
| X12 | The W1J01 synthetic set or the agreed fault switch is missing or does not match the run | The run fails as a fixture fault and names the missing element; no production value is substituted | None | AC19, AC20 |

X1 to X10 are the exception paths of the legacy story read on the wave 1 services; X11 and X12 are the failures that only appear when the run leaves one service or loses its fixture, so that a timeout or a fixture fault never becomes a pass.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | The suite is its own module and reuses the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG; it needs the four integration dependencies and the published contracts of P3, P4, P7 and S8, not their source code, and it owns no schema and no table |
| Negotiable | The fixture composition, the poll interval, the wait window and the report layout are configuration; the gate behaviour, the message IDs, the package versions, the queue codes and the cap are fixed by the legacy story |
| Valuable | Proves across services what no single service story can prove: the wait on case creation, the governed package with its checksum, one ledger record per allocation within five minutes, the allocation events, the deviation diversion, the held date and the idempotency of a rerun |
| Estimable | One suite module, one fixture builder, four contract probes, one clock and gate control, one package rollback step and one evidence report |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the report; eleven scenarios over four services, four topics and four consumed operations of the run |
| Testable | Every criterion is asserted on an observable: a REST response, a Kafka event, a workflow result, a ledger record or a run count |

    Given package ALLOCATION "ALLOC-2026.11" and package ASSIGNMENT "ASSIGN-2026.11" are in force and were announced by rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1
    Given each version carries its SHA-256 in rwb-decision

    Given case RW-2026-000205 is allocated to U-02 in queue "MTG-BKK-CO"

    Then no rwb.case.CaseAllocated.v1 leaves for the case

  Scenario: AC16 No version in force holds the whole business date (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given no ALLOCATION version is in force on 2026-12-01
    When the JOB-03 step runs for 2026-12-01
    Then no case is allocated for the date and every case keeps status "NEW" with no queue and no owner
    Then the run record carries MSG-P3-027 for the package in force check with package code "ALLOCATION"
    Then no rwb.case.CaseAllocated.v1 and no ledger record exists for the date

  Scenario: AC17 A rerun of the same business date has no further effect (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the JOB-03 step has allocated case RW-2026-000201 to U-03 on 2026-12-01
    When the JOB-03 step for 2026-12-01 is started again through POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs/JOB-03/rerun
    Then case RW-2026-000201 keeps owner U-03 and its one assignment record
    Then exactly one ledger record exists for the case and no second rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 leaves
    Then the run record shows 1 case skipped as already allocated

  Scenario: AC18 The overflow and exception counts reconcile with the case reads (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given U-01, U-02 and U-03 each hold 150 open cases in queue "MTG-BKK-CO"
    Given case RW-2026-000203 is placed in queue "MTG-BKK-CO" and case RW-2026-000204 matches no allocation rule
    When the JOB-03 step completes for 2026-12-01
    Then the cases read in queue "MTG-BKK-OVF" through GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues and /queues/{queueId}/cases equal the overflow count of the run
    Then the cases read in queue "RWB-EXC" equal the exception count of the run
    Then the summary for team "MTG-BKK" carries MSG-P3-011 with the overflow count and MSG-P3-012 with the exception count

  Scenario: AC19 A role without Platform administration U is refused the rerun (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a test identity holds RW-CASEOWN and no Platform administration right U
    When the identity calls POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs/JOB-03/rerun for 2026-12-01
    Then the call returns status 403 with MSG-P4-002
    Then no run starts, no case is allocated and no ledger record is written by the attempt

  Scenario: AC20 A failed record leaves that one case new and the run continues (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the decision-record write fails for case RW-2026-000207 through the agreed test-only fault switch
    When the JOB-03 step allocates the cases of 2026-12-01
    Then case RW-2026-000207 keeps status "NEW" with no queue and no owner
    Then the other cases of the run are allocated and each has one record in GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log
    Then the run record carries MSG-P3-013 for case RW-2026-000207
```

**Target reading.** Against the monolith, DP-10 replaces the Quartz trigger of JOB-03 with a step of DailyCaseRun in rwb-case, started by AceDataReady for the business date and finished by 07:00, with no Quartz table and no shared scheduler; DP-04 makes rwb-decision the registry, so the suite waits for the JOB-20 promote, fetches each version with its SHA-256 and lets the service evaluate its own copy inside the EvaluateRules activity; DP-03 keeps the record local to the transaction of the case change and collects it into the central ledger of rwb-decision as `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` within five minutes; and DP-09 keeps the announcement of an allocation on `rwb.case.events.v1`, where the case commits with its outbox row and the suite reads the event rather than a table copy. DP-01, DP-05, DP-06, DP-07, DP-11, DP-13, DP-14, DP-15 and DP-19 change the schema, view, parameter, list, call, path, topic, migration and screen surfaces of the same behaviour. What the sources leave open — the surface the suite reads the JOB-03 run through, given that the job catalogue belongs to rwb-source-data and the run to rwb-case — is recorded as GAP-0345 and ASM-0439, and no value is invented in its place.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A case is allocated by the first rule of package ALLOCATION, in row order, whose product group, region and exposure band match the case; a column value of "any" matches every value | Package ALLOCATION; D-RCV-36 T5; DL24; REQ-CWC-008 |
| BR2 | The owner is chosen by the ASSIGNMENT rule for the queue, whose outputs hold the method — ROUND_ROBIN, LOWEST_LOAD, NAMED_OWNER or SKILL — and the cap | Package ASSIGNMENT; queue.assignment_method (DF-WRK-006); LOV-ASSIGN |
| BR3 | An owner at or above the queue's caseload cap is skipped; open cases are the cases in the queue owned by the person with a status other than CLOSED | queue.capacity_cap (DF-WRK-007); DL23 |
| BR4 | A case that cannot be given an owner goes to the overflow queue named in the ASSIGNMENT row; a row with no overflow queue sends it to the exception queue with reason "NO_OVERFLOW_QUEUE" | queue.overflow_queue_id (DF-WRK-008) |
| BR5 | A case that matches no rule goes to the exception queue and the gap is logged; R-UNI-41 handles the case once a person decides | R-UNI-41; FEAT-CWC-09 |
| BR6 | A case with an open deviation goes to the deviation handler queue "DEV-HANDLER" with no case owner | R-DEV-01 |
| BR7 | A decision that cannot be recorded does not proceed: no case change commits without its decision record | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; CTL-06 |
| BR8 | A case is allocated at most once per business date, so a repeated run of the date adds no assignment and no ledger record | R-UNI-40; events.txt rule "Duplicates" |
| BR9 | Each allocation records the ALLOCATION rule ID and package version on the decision record and the ASSIGNMENT rule ID and package version on the assignment row | REQ-CWC-016; CTL-03; D-RCV-36 T5 |
| BR10 | The ALLOCATION package always has a default row as its last row; the check is at load and is not repeated at run time | REQ-CWC-008; D-RCV-36 T5 |
| BR11 | JOB-03 is the allocation step of DailyCaseRun in rwb-case, after the JOB-02 step of the same run and complete by 07:00; it is not a Quartz job and holds no schedule of its own | Arch v5 slide 44 (JOB-03 DailyCaseRun step); DP-10 |
| BR12 | Both packages are fetched from rwb-decision with their package version, their valid-from date and their SHA-256, the checksum is verified, and the evaluation runs inside the service's activity on its own copy of the model, never against a shared rule server and never against `drl_source` | DP-04; Drools design slide 15; D-RCV-36 T3, T6 |
| BR13 | The decision record commits in `rwb_case` in the same transaction as the case change and leaves as `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1`; rwb-decision collects it into the central ledger within five minutes and answers it through the decision-log read | DP-03; ADR-022; REQ-CWC-016 |
| BR14 | An allocation leaves as `rwb.case.CaseAllocated.v1` and a rule gap as `rwb.case.CaseAllocationFailed.v1` on `rwb.case.events.v1` in the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, key caseId, with IDs and facts only and no personal data | DP-09; DP-14; ADR-015; Arch v5 slide 42 rows 02 and 03 |
| BR15 | An open deviation is taken from the deviation event of rwb-deviation, not from a read of the deviation schema, and it diverts the case to the deviation handler queue with no owner | R-DEV-01; DP-01 |
| BR16 | A version not in force holds the whole business date with MSG-P3-027 and touches no case; it is a run-level refusal, not a per-case failure, and it is never replaced by a default decision | R-UNI-41; D-RCV-36 T5 |
| BR17 | Every cross-service call of the run is one hop to the owning service with the 2 s client budget, and no service is called through another service | ADR-020; DP-11; DP-13 |
| BR18 | The counts of the run — read, assigned, overflow, exception, failed — reconcile with the queue reads through the case contract and with the two summary lines MSG-P3-011 and MSG-P3-012 | RWB-E1-020 section 4 steps 8 and 9; CTL-03 |

##### 9. State transitions

The legacy case states of RWB-E1-020, observed through the case contract:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| New | Allocation rule matched | ALLOCATION rule matched and the ASSIGNMENT rule gives an owner below the cap | Assigned |
| New | Allocation rule matched | ALLOCATION rule matched and every owner at the cap | New, in the overflow queue |
| New | Allocation rule matched | No ALLOCATION rule matched | New, in the exception queue |
| New | DeviationRaised (R-DEV-01) | deviation_open = true | New, in the deviation handler queue |

The states the run observes across the services:

| Item | States |
|---|---|
| DailyCaseRun | Not started, started by AceDataReady, waiting at the JOB-02 step, running the JOB-03 step, completed with the run counts, held for the whole business date |
| Case | New, Assigned; the case is never written by the suite, and the queue and the owner are read back through the case contract |
| Rule package version | LOADED, APPROVED, IN_FORCE, SUPERSEDED, ROLLED_BACK, REFUSED |
| Decision record | Recorded locally in `rwb_case`, published as DecisionRecorded, collected in the ledger of rwb-decision |
| Suite run | Not started, running, passed, failed with the failing test case named |

##### 10. Authority

| QA integration engineer | Owns the suite module, the fixtures, the clock and gate control, the package rollback step and the evidence report |
| Service owner of rwb-case | Owns the JOB-03 step, the two package evaluations, the assignment engine, the case commit with its outbox row and the allocation events |
| Service owner of rwb-decision | Owns the package versions, the checksum, the promote at 00:01, the rollback and the central decision ledger |
| Service owner of rwb-access | Owns the Platform administration right U and its refusal on the administrative operations |
| Service owner of rwb-deviation | Owns the deviation screening and the DeviationRaised event that diverts a case |
| RW-TEAMMGR team manager | Receives MSG-P3-011 and MSG-P3-012 and reads the queues in team scope |
| RW-PLATADM platform administrator | Reruns the JOB-03 step through the job catalogue (Platform administration U) and reads the run record |
| RW-CASEOWN case owner | Reads the cases given to them and may not rerun the run |
| No role | Reads a service schema directly, or takes production data into the run |

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The suite provides no REST operation. The names reserved for P2 rwb-integration — `/api/recovery/integration/v1`, `rwb.integration.events.v1`, `rwb-integration` and `rwb_integration` — are recorded but unused, and no `rwb_integration` table is written.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method and path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases | P3 rwb-case | The cases of business date 2026-12-01 with status "NEW" before the run and their queue and owner after it |
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId} | P3 rwb-case | One case: status, queue, team, owner, the ALLOCATION package version and `last_allocation_date` |
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues | P3 rwb-case | The queue codes, team, method, cap of 150 and overflow queue, and the queue id of "MTG-BKK-OVF", "RWB-EXC" and "DEV-HANDLER" |
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/cases | P3 rwb-case | The cases of a queue, for the overflow, exception and deviation counts of AC18 and the no-owner assertion of AC15 |
| GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs | P1 rwb-source-data, job catalogue | The job catalogue and the state of the JOB-02 and JOB-03 steps on the monitor, including the waiting line of MSG-P1-001 |
| POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs/JOB-03/rerun | P1 rwb-source-data, job catalogue | The rerun of the same business date for AC17, and the refused attempt of AC19 |
| GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log | P7 rwb-decision | Exactly one record per allocation, with the ALLOCATION rule ID and package version, and the elapsed collection against five minutes |
| GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions | P7 rwb-decision | The version in force of ALLOCATION and ASSIGNMENT, its valid-from date and its SHA-256, for AC12 and AC16 |
| GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/approvals | P7 rwb-decision | The approval evidence of each version: the approver role RW-RISK, who is not the author |
| POST /api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/rollback | P7 rwb-decision | AC16: the one-call rollback that removes the ALLOCATION version from force for the held date, and the promote back |

Every call is one hop to the owning service on its own base with the 2 s client budget (ADR-020, DP-11, DP-13); the suite calls no service through another service and writes nothing through these paths except the rerun and the rollback. The job catalogue read and the rerun are x-module P1 in the API specification, while the JOB-03 run itself is registered by rwb-case as a step of DailyCaseRun, so the suite reads the run through the catalogue and asserts the step through the workflow; the surface that shows the JOB-03 step of a workflow run and the exact rerun façade at the nominal time are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0345; ASM-0439).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The suite publishes no business event; it observes the events of the owning services, listed in 12.4.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | What the suite asserts |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.case.CaseAllocated.v1` | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 rwb-case | Exactly one event per allocation, key caseId, case number, queue code and the ALLOCATION rule ID with its package version; CloudEvents 1.0 and no personal data field |
| `rwb.case.CaseAllocationFailed.v1` | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 rwb-case | One event for a case that matched no rule, with reason "NO_ROW_MATCHED"; the assertion of AC14 on the platform |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 rwb-decision, with the record written by each producing service | The record of each allocation reaches the central ledger; rule ID "ALLOC-014" and package version "ALLOC-2026.11", collected within five minutes |
| `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` | `rwb.decision.events.v1` | P7 rwb-decision | The JOB-20 promote at 00:01 puts "ALLOC-2026.11" and "ASSIGN-2026.11" in force before the run, and the promote back after the rollback of AC16 |
| `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1` | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` | S8 rwb-deviation | The open deviation of case RW-2026-000206 that diverts it to "DEV-HANDLER" with no owner in AC15 |

The envelope is CloudEvents 1.0 and a consumer dedupes on the event ID through its inbox (ADR-015, DP-09). The payload of each event is the owner's published schema; the event and ledger assertions replace the in-process `caseAllocated` call and the local decision log of the legacy criterion.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| CaseWorkflow | Workflow, one per case | `rwb-case` | Holds the case from entry to closure; the suite asserts the state the allocation put it in through the case read and takes no part in the order of its steps |
| DailyCaseRun | Workflow, started by AceDataReady and by its Schedule | `rwb-case` | Runs the JOB-02 step and then the JOB-03 step for the business date; its output is the run result that AC11 and AC13 are read against |
| EvaluateRules | Activity | `rwb-case` | Input package code, facts and business date; fetches the version from rwb-decision, verifies the checksum and returns package code, package version, rule ID and outputs (DP-04) |
| RecordAndApply | Activity | `rwb-case` | Writes the decision record, the case change, the assignment and the outbox rows in one transaction and fails as one unit (DP-03, DP-09) |

All four are registered by RWB-P3-E1020-APP on task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery` (Arch v5 slides 13 and 14; Drools design slide 13). The suite starts no workflow of its own: it observes DailyCaseRun and CaseWorkflow through the case contract, the run result and the topics, and it triggers the step only through the readiness signal and the rerun of the job catalogue.

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Schedule or start | Cadence | Registration | Legacy reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| JOB-02 case creation | Event-started: AceDataReady for the business date starts DailyCaseRun | Registered by the rwb-case release | JOB-02 Case creation |
| JOB-03 Morning allocation | A step of DailyCaseRun, after the JOB-02 step and by 07:00; not a Schedule of its own | Runs in rwb-case, not a Schedule | JOB-03 Morning allocation (Arch v5 slide 44) |
| JOB-20 rule promote | Temporal Schedule at 00:01, overlap policy SKIP, catch-up window; publishes RulePackageInForce | Registered by the rwb-decision release | JOB-20 Rule promote |

The suite starts no Schedule, moves no Schedule and waits for no Schedule of its own. It moves its own test clock past 07:00 for AC10, triggers the JOB-03 step through the readiness signal and the rerun of section 12.2, and takes the JOB-20 promote as an observed event.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The suite owns no table and never reads another service's schema (DP-01). The tables it exercises — `recovery_case`, `queue`, `queue_member`, `assignment` and the local decision record in `rwb_case`, the package versions and the ledger in `rwb_decision` — are listed in section 11 with their owners and are read only through the contracts of 12.2 and the events of 12.4.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

None for a service contract. No published contract of P3, P4, P7 or S8 is faked: a run that needs such a fake fails the preflight. The only stubs are external to the nineteen services:

| Stub | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Synthetic case, queue, member and cap fixture (RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG) | Stands in for the ACE ingestion and the case set that the bank's Airflow and the case service produce, outside the nineteen services |
| Synthetic ALS batch rows | Stand in for the batch record of the source system, so that the gate of AC10 can be held and released without a production row |
| Mock Entra sign-in | Gives the run its synthetic test identities, including the identity of RW-CASEOWN for AC19, as the platform demo sign-in does |
| Agreed test-only fault switch on the decision-record library of rwb-case | Stands in for a store that fails one record write (AC20) and every record write (TC-E1-020-15-ITG); its exact scope and reset are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0345; ASM-0439) |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Provided | Consumed | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 | 10 | Three case reads, the queue read and the queue-case read, the job catalogue read and the rerun, the decision-log read, the version list, the approvals read and the rollback; one hop, 2 s (DP-11, DP-13) |
| Kafka | None | 5 event types | `rwb.case.CaseAllocated.v1`, `rwb.case.CaseAllocationFailed.v1` on `rwb.case.events.v1`; `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1`; `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1`; `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1`; CloudEvents 1.0, key caseId |
| Temporal | None | 2 workflows and 2 activities observed | DailyCaseRun and CaseWorkflow, with the EvaluateRules and RecordAndApply activities, all on `rwb-case`; the JOB-02, JOB-03 and JOB-20 starts of 12.6 are observed, never started by the suite |
| File | None | None | No file in this story |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** One suite module that reuses the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG: a fixture builder for the synthetic case set, the queues, the members and the caps, a clock and gate control for the JOB-02 wait, a set of contract probes across P3, P4, P7 and S8, a package rollback and promote-back step, and an evidence report with one verdict per test case. No service code and no schema change: the suite builds nothing that a service owns.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| SuiteRunner | Test harness | Preflight against the published contracts, run order, report and exit code |
| CaseFixtureDriver | Test harness | Seeds the synthetic NEW cases of 2026-12-01, the queues "MTG-BKK-CO", "MTG-BKK-OVF", "RWB-EXC" and "DEV-HANDLER" and the members U-01, U-02 and U-03 with their loads, through the W1J01 set |
| GateControl | Test harness | Holds and releases the JOB-02 step for the business date and moves the clock past 07:00, so the wait of AC10 is proved rather than assumed |
| CaseProbe | Test harness | Calls the four case operations and asserts status, queue, team, owner, package version and the counts of overflow, exception and deviation |
| PackageProbe | Test harness | Reads the version list and the approvals, waits for RulePackageInForce, and asserts the checksum of AC12 and the held date of AC16 |
| LedgerProbe | Test harness | Consumes DecisionRecorded, reads the decision log and measures each collection against five minutes |
| EventProbe | Test harness | Consumes CaseAllocated, CaseAllocationFailed and DeviationRaised, and asserts the envelope, the key, the count per case and the absence of a personal data field |
| RerunStep | Test harness | Calls the job-catalogue rerun for AC17 and the refused rerun of AC19, then asserts the counts and the ledger entry count |
| RecordFaultStep | Test harness | Drives the agreed test-only fault switch for one case (AC20) and for every case (TC-E1-020-15-ITG) |
| ReportWriter | Test harness | One row per test case, with the evidence and the elapsed time, and the cleanup record |

**Database.** None of its own. The suite writes no service table and no schema object, and it holds no client for a service schema.

**Configuration and reference data**

- The SIT endpoints of P3, P4, P7 and S8, the topic names, the task queues, the namespace `rwb-recovery` and the schema-registry address, all as configuration.
- The synthetic case numbers RW-2026-000201 to RW-2026-000209, the owners U-01, U-02 and U-03 with the loads of 120, 95, 140, 149 and 150, the queues "MTG-BKK-CO", "MTG-BKK-OVF", "RWB-EXC" and "DEV-HANDLER", the cap of 150 and the business date 2026-12-01.
- The package codes ALLOCATION and ASSIGNMENT with the versions "ALLOC-2026.11" and "ASSIGN-2026.11", read through the P7 contracts and never written in the suite code.
- The rule ID "ALLOC-014" and the assignment rule ID "ASSIGN-007", taken from the package answer and never computed by the suite.
- The parameters and lists through the P3 contracts (DP-06, DP-07): `allocation.exception.queue.code`, `allocation.deviation.queue.code`, LOV-ASSIGN and LOV-CASE-STATUS.
- The 2 s client budget, the poll interval, the 07:00 cut-off and the five-minute collection target.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |

The H and C entries of the table belong to the owning APP stories — RWB-P3-E1020-APP for the step, the evaluations and the local record, RWB-P7-E1020-APP for the registry and the ledger — and this ITG story carries no H, no C and no X of its own. Its I list is the four services whose behaviour the run exercises, and an integration story never becomes a build dependency of another story (Template and Rules §R5.4, §R5.7).

**Build steps**

1. Create the suite module next to harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG, wire it to the SIT endpoints of P3, P4, P7 and S8, the four topics and the task queues, and write the preflight: the four services answer, the topics and their retry and `.dlt` topics exist, the queues are registered in `rwb-recovery` and both packages are in force.
2. Build CaseFixtureDriver and the W1J01 fixtures for the NEW cases, the queues, the members and the caps; hold the ALS batch row and prove that no case is created and no case is allocated before the readiness signal.
3. Build GateControl and AC10: the held JOB-02 step, the clock past 07:00, the catalogue read with MSG-P1-001, and every NEW case with no queue and no owner; then release the step and assert that the same cases are allocated.
4. Build the CaseProbe assertions of AC11 and AC18: the JOB-03 step after the JOB-02 step in the history of DailyCaseRun, no Quartz row for JOB-03, and the overflow and exception counts reconciled with the queue reads and MSG-P3-011 and MSG-P3-012.
5. Build PackageProbe for AC12 and AC16: the version list with its SHA-256 and valid-from date, the approvals read, the RulePackageInForce wait, the refusal of a mismatched checksum, and the rollback of the ALLOCATION version with the promote back.
6. Build LedgerProbe and AC13: exactly one ledger record per allocation with "ALLOC-014" and "ALLOC-2026.11", and the elapsed collection measured against five minutes.
7. Build EventProbe for AC14 and AC15: the CloudEvents envelope, the key, one CaseAllocated per allocation, one CaseAllocationFailed with "NO_ROW_MATCHED", and the DeviationRaised event that diverts RW-2026-000206 to "DEV-HANDLER" with no owner.
8. Build RerunStep and RecordFaultStep for AC17, AC19 and AC20, with the refused rerun of RW-CASEOWN, the single assignment and single ledger record of a repeated date, and the one case left NEW by a failed record write while the rest of the run continues.
9. Build ReportWriter, the cleanup of the synthetic set and the evidence report; run the whole suite twice to prove that a repeated run adds no assignment and no ledger entry.

**Done when.** The fifteen test cases of section 16 pass on the real services in SIT, AC10 and the ten new criteria are signed off against the contracts, exactly one `rwb.case.CaseAllocated.v1` and one ledger record exist per allocation inside five minutes, the held date carries MSG-P3-027 and no case, the repeated date adds no assignment and no ledger entry, no service schema and no Quartz table was read, the synthetic set is restored and the packages are back in force, and the evidence report names every criterion with its observable.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-011 | Allocation summary, case in overflow | {count} new cases are waiting in the overflow queue for {team}. Every owner is at the caseload cap. |
| MSG-P3-012 | Allocation summary, no rule matched | {count} new cases matched no allocation rule and are in the exception queue. |
| MSG-P3-013 | Decision record write failed for a case | The case was not allocated because the decision could not be recorded. It will be tried again in the next run. |
| MSG-P3-027 | No ALLOCATION or ASSIGNMENT version is in force at the run | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The JOB-03 step waits because the ALS batch has not completed | {product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right reruns the run | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | A rerun is asked while the first run still holds the date | The action is already in progress. Try again when it has finished. |

The seven texts are copied unchanged from RWB-E1-020 and this story adds no message ID. For MSG-P3-027 the {check} value is "package in force" and the {detail} names the package code only. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen is built or tested by this story. SCR-02 Case list (states Loading; list; filtered) shows the queue, the owner and the status of each case after the run, and the suite reads the same facts through `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` behind the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). SCR-09 Exception queue (list) shows the cases placed in "RWB-EXC" and the suite asserts the same cases and the count of MSG-P3-012 through the queue read. The team manager receives the allocation summary after each run, which the suite asserts on MSG-P3-011 and MSG-P3-012. Queue screens come in Epic 2 (SCR-07) and are out of scope.

##### 17. Guardrails

- Synthetic data only: the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG loads every case number, owner id, queue, member, cap and batch row, and no production data is read, copied or connected to; the suite refuses to start against an environment that is not SIT.
- No personal data in events, logs, workflow history, fixtures or the report: case numbers, queue codes, owner ids, rule IDs, package versions and business dates only.
- No cross-service table read: every fact is read through a contract of 12.2 or an event of 12.4, the ACE views stay behind rwb-source-data (DP-01, DP-05), and the suite ships with no client for a service schema and none for the Quartz tables.
- No business value in the test code: the cap of 150, the queue codes, the method, the rule IDs, the product groups and the regions are the packages, the queues and the parameters in force, read through the P3 and P7 contracts (DP-04, DP-06, DP-07).
- One evaluator and one copy: ALLOCATION and ASSIGNMENT are evaluated only inside the EvaluateRules activity of the owning service on a checksum-verified copy of the package, and the suite never reads `drl_source`, a workbook or a rule row directly.
- No package state is left changed: a version rolled back for AC16 is promoted back in the same run, and the evidence report records the state before and after.
- CloudEvents 1.0 with IDs and facts only on every asserted event, one allocation event per case, and the consumer inbox as the only dedupe.
- One hop and a 2 s budget on every REST call, and a timeout is never retried into a pass (ADR-020, DP-11).
- Clean-up in the same run: the synthetic cases, the business dates, the held batch row, the fault switch and the started workflows are removed or restored, and the report records what was cleaned.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-021 for rwb-case. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **consumer of the case service (any service or the gateway-bff)**, I want **one published, versioned contract for moving a case between queues, teams and owners, with its events, its reason and rule-result shapes and its error envelope**, so that **every caller and every consumer builds against a fixed shape on Day 1, before the transfer capability is built**.

This story is the contract baseline of the transfer capability of `rwb-case`:

- REST base `/api/recovery/case/v1`, OpenAPI 3.1.
- Topic `rwb.case.events.v1`, event names `rwb.case.<Event>.v1`, AsyncAPI 3.0, CloudEvents 1.0.
- Temporal task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery`.
- Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`.
- Schema `rwb_case`, owned by P3, with the per-service login of DP-02. The login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0688; ASM-1235) and is referred to as "the rwb-case login (DP-02)".

It carries no business logic. It fixes the artifacts that RWB-P3-E1021-APP and RWB-P3-E1021-OPS build and deploy, and it publishes the fake that the other services build against.

##### 2. Business rationale

The monolith published a Java interface (`TransferService`) and a shared decision log; nothing outside the module could be built against it without the module. In the target, the transfer is called over REST by the gateway and by nothing else, and observed over Kafka by `rwb-reporting`. Without a published contract on Day 1, the five sibling slices of this legacy key (rwb-access, rwb-decision, rwb-document, rwb-deviation and the wave-1 integration harness) and the gateway route would each guess a shape, and the transfer request, response, error codes and authorization that REQ-CWC-010 requires to stay unchanged would drift.

The contract also fixes the two things that changed under D-RCV-60: the reason list is read as reference data of `rwb-case` (DP-07) and the rule answer is the `RuleResult` shape of the embedded Drools kit (DP-04), not a local rule table. Both appear in the document as named components, so a consumer can see where a value comes from without reading a table (DP-01).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The Template and Rules v1 service facts are in force: schema `rwb_case`, REST base `/api/recovery/case/v1`, topic `rwb.case.events.v1`, queue `rwb-case`, package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`.
- The ownership map confirms P3 owns `POST /cases/{caseId}/transfer`, `POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-hold`, `GET /me/tasks` and `PATCH /tasks/{taskId}`, and the tables `recovery_case`, `assignment`, `queue`, `queue_member`, `task`.
- The legacy request, response, error codes and authorization of the manual transfer are the baseline and do not change (BR11 of RWB-E1-021).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 and sits in contract group `CG-W1` (Template and Rules §R5.7 rule 1).

##### 4. Flow

1. Write the OpenAPI 3.1 document for the transfer operation and the two task operations, with the schemas `TransferRequest`, `Assignment`, `LegalHoldRequest`, `Case`, `Task`, `TaskPage` and the error envelope.
2. Write the AsyncAPI 3.0 document for `rwb.case.events.v1` with `CaseTransferred` and `CaseStateChanged`, the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, the key and the headers.
3. Write the named schemas `TransferReason`, `RuleResult` and `DecisionRecordRef`, and reference them from the operation and the events.
4. Publish the error envelope: RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId`, `detail`, `instance` and `traceId`.
5. State the versioning rule: path version `v1` at the base, additive change only inside `v1`, breaking change is a new path version, deprecation announced in the document.
6. Publish the fake: a contract server generated from the document, with deterministic examples for 200, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503, and a Kafka stub that emits one CaseTransferred and one CaseStateChanged.
7. Run the contract tests of section 16 against the fake and publish the document in the service contract catalogue.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Situation | What the contract does |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | A caller sends an unknown field in `TransferRequest` | The schema sets `additionalProperties: false`; the request is refused with the error envelope and the 422 example |
| C2 | A caller omits `Idempotency-Key` on the POST | The header is declared required; the 400 example names the missing header; the document states the behaviour |
| C3 | A consumer sends an event without the CloudEvents envelope | The AsyncAPI document marks the envelope required and the schema refuses a bare payload |
| C4 | A producer adds a field to CaseTransferred | Allowed as an additive change inside `v1`; the consumer schema keeps `additionalProperties: true` and ignores unknown fields |
| C5 | A breaking change is needed | A new path version is published; `v1` stays served until its announced retirement date; the change is never made in place |
| C6 | A caller sends a transfer reason that is not in the list | The enum is a reference to LOV-TRANSFER-REASON; the 422 example shows MSG-P3-001; the list itself is read at run time, not frozen into the client |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Day 1; no build dependency, no service code |
| Negotiable | Field names follow the legacy request and response; the descriptions and examples are reviewable |
| Valuable | Five sibling slices and the gateway build against it without waiting for the capability |
| Estimable | Three documents, six schemas, one fake, six contract tests |
| Small | One sprint-week for one pair |
| Testable | Every artifact has a contract test in section 16 |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Transfer rules and engine v1 - contract baseline

  Background:
    Given the contract baseline of rwb-case version 1 is published
    Given the service facts of Template and Rules v1: base /api/recovery/case/v1 and topic rwb.case.events.v1

  Scenario: AC1 OpenAPI 3.1 document for the transfer operation (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the OpenAPI 3.1 document of rwb-case version 1
    When the path /cases/{caseId}/transfer is read
    Then it declares POST with the operation ID of the transfer, the request body TransferRequest and the response 200 Assignment
    Then it declares 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 with the error envelope and a named messageId for each
    Then it declares the Idempotency-Key header as required and the Authorization bearer scheme
    Then a document validator reports no error against OpenAPI 3.1

  Scenario: AC2 Task operations and the transfer context (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the same OpenAPI 3.1 document
    When the paths /me/tasks and /tasks/{taskId} are read
    Then GET /me/tasks answers TaskPage and PATCH /tasks/{taskId} answers Task
    Then the Task schema carries the caseId, queueCode, ownerUserId and the transfer reason code of the case
    Then every operation declares its authorisation right (Case record R for the read, Case record U for the update)

  Scenario: AC3 AsyncAPI document for the two events (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the AsyncAPI 3.0 document of rwb.case.events.v1
    When the messages CaseTransferred and CaseStateChanged are read
    Then each message name follows rwb.case.<Event>.v1
    Then the envelope is CloudEvents 1.0 with the key caseId and the source rwb-case
    Then the CaseTransferred payload carries caseId, fromOwner, toOwner, reasonCode and ruleId
    Then no payload carries a party name, a national identifier or a contact detail

  Scenario: AC4 Transfer reason and rule-result shapes (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the named schemas of the document
    When TransferReason, RuleResult and DecisionRecordRef are read
    Then TransferReason is a string that references LOV-TRANSFER-REASON and its values come from the reference-data contract, not from the document
    Then RuleResult carries packageCode, packageVersion, ruleId and outputs and is marked as the answer of the embedded Drools kit
    Then DecisionRecordRef carries the decision record ID and the hash link, and never the inputs

  Scenario: AC5 Error envelope, idempotency and versioning (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the document components Error and Problem
    When a 422 response example is read
    Then it is an RFC 9457 problem response with type, title, status, detail, instance, messageId and traceId
    Then messageId holds a MSG- identifier and never free text
    When the Idempotency-Key behaviour and the versioning rule are read
    Then a repeat with the same key returns the first response and creates no second assignment
    Then the versioning rule states v1 in the path, additive-only change inside v1 and a new path version for a breaking change

  Scenario: AC6 The nine contract tables of section 12 (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the contract story of RWB-E1-021
    When section 12 is read
    Then each of the nine sub-tables is present and either carries rows or states None
    Then every operation and table owner named in it is the owner recorded in the ownership map
    Then the fake described in 12.8 is published with the document in the same release
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The manual transfer keeps its endpoint, request, response, errors and authorization; the contract copies them unchanged | REQ-CWC-010; BR11 of RWB-E1-021 |
| BR2 | The transfer reason is a coded value from LOV-TRANSFER-REASON, referenced and not frozen into the document | LOV-TRANSFER-REASON; REQ-WKM-003 |
| BR3 | CaseTransferred carries caseId, fromOwner, toOwner, reasonCode and ruleId, and no personal data | EV-04; section 12.3 |
| BR4 | A repeat of the POST with the same Idempotency-Key returns the first response | Architecture v5 slide 11; TSD P3 API-P3-006 |
| BR5 | The path version sits in the base; a breaking change is a new version and never an in-place change | DP-13; Template and Rules §R5.5 |
| BR6 | The document names no table of another service and no rule table; the rule answer is a `RuleResult` | DP-01; DP-04; D-RCV-36 T5 |
| BR7 | Topic and event names come from the naming rule and are not typed by a consumer | DP-14 |

**Build steps**

1. Draft `TransferRequest`, `Assignment`, `LegalHoldRequest` and `Case` from the legacy request and response, field for field.
2. Add the two task operations and their schemas.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-001 | Manual transfer without a reason | Choose a reason for the transfer. |
| MSG-P3-002 | Target owner at the cap | {owner} is at the caseload cap. Choose another owner or the team queue. |
| MSG-P3-005 | Move not allowed from the status | This case cannot move to {state} from {current}. |
| MSG-P3-011 | Target queue full, case in overflow | {count} new cases are waiting in the overflow queue for {team}. Every owner is at the caseload cap. |
| MSG-P3-027 | No TRANSFER version is in force for a rule trigger | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | Second transfer on a changed record | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Decision log write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

Each identifier is bound to one HTTP status in the document: MSG-P4-002 to 403, MSG-P3-005 and MSG-GEN-004 to 409, MSG-P3-001, MSG-P3-002 and MSG-P3-011 to 422, MSG-P7-003 to 503, and MSG-P3-027 to the non-retryable error of the activity, not to a caller response.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the document that belongs to reference data: the reason list is referenced, not enumerated.
- No personal data in any example, in any event payload or in any response: examples use case numbers, user identifiers and codes only.
- No table of another service is named as a source; the rule answer is a `RuleResult`, never a rule table (DP-01, DP-04).
- The manual transfer keeps its request, response, errors and authorization (BR11 of RWB-E1-021).
- The document is versioned and never edited in place: a breaking change is a new path version.
- The fake is generated from the document, so a drift between document and fake fails the pipeline.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-021 for rwb-case. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR)**, I want **cases moved between queues and roles by the TRANSFER rule package on stage change, route decided, timer expired, deviation raised or cleared, approval needed, document received, payment missed, or a manual request with a reason**, so that **hand-offs between teams run without email**.

Inside `rwb-case` this is the transfer capability of the case service:

- Service `rwb-case`, schema `rwb_case`, REST base `/api/recovery/case/v1`, topic `rwb.case.events.v1` with event names `rwb.case.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`.
- The transfer runs as the `transfer` activity of `CaseWorkflow`, reached by the case router from a Kafka event or by the manual REST call `POST /cases/{caseId}/transfer`.
- The TRANSFER rule package is evaluated locally through the embedded Drools kit (DP-04); the package and its versions are authored, approved and promoted in `rwb-decision` (RWB-P3-E1073-APP) and fetched as a model, never read as a table of another service.
- The database login used by the capability is the per-service login of DP-02. Its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0688; ASM-1235); this story uses the phrase "the rwb-case login (DP-02)" and never the shared monolith login.

The legacy behaviour is unchanged: the same endpoint, request, response, errors and authorization; the same eight triggers; the same TRANSFER package code; the same reason list; the same decision record content.

##### 2. Business rationale

A case changes hands between the TDR, litigation, NPA and debt sale teams by email today, and the case can wait between teams with nobody holding it. This story moves the case by rule when one of eight triggers fires, picks the owner in the receiving queue, ends the old assignment and records the rule ID and package version, and gives the team manager a programmatic transfer with a coded reason before the Epic 2 screens. It meets REQ-CWC-010 and REQ-CWC-016.

Under D-RCV-36 (16 November 2026) the transfer rules are package TRANSFER, evaluated with first-match semantics (T5); the eight triggers arrive as one `TransferTrigger` fact. The manual transfer API does not change; it keeps its endpoint, request, response, errors and authorization. A rule change is a package version loaded and approved through RWB-E1-073, not a release.

The realignment changes the mechanism, not the business rule:

1. The in-process `RuleEvaluator` call of the monolith becomes the embedded Drools kit of DP-04. The kit caches one KieBase per package version, verifies the checksum, refuses a checksum mismatch, and is called only inside the Temporal activity so a replay reuses the recorded answer (the Temporal and Drools design, slide 14).
2. The decision log write becomes the local decision-record library of DP-03 written in the same transaction as the state change, hash-chained to the previous record and published on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; `rwb-decision` collects it into the central ledger within 5 minutes. The legacy decision log store of another module is no longer written directly.
3. The trigger listener becomes the case router (Kafka consumer with the inbox of DP-09) that calls `signalWithStart` on `CaseWorkflow` and forwards the trigger to the running stage child. `TimerDue` is no longer a Kafka event: the durable timer inside `CaseWorkflow` raises the same trigger inside the workflow (the timer ruling in the Ownership Map; RWB-P3-E1028-CON provides the timer contract).
4. Reference data (the transfer reason list, the queue and team lists) is read through `rwb-case`'s own reference-data contract of DP-07, never from a foreign table.

Business preconditions carried from RWB-E1-021:

- Package TRANSFER version "TRF-2026.11" is in force, and each row holds trigger event, condition, target queue code and row order (D-RCV-36 T5).
- The transfer reason list LOV-TRANSFER-REASON holds R01 Capacity, R02 Customer deceased, R03 Skill, R04 Owner absent, R05 Legal referral and R06 Wrong queue (DL23), loaded through RWB-E1-043 and read through the reference-data contract.
- Manual transfer callers hold Queue and allocation U (RW-TEAMMGR, RW-CAPACITY). Hold and release callers hold Case record U (for example RW-LITOFF acting on a Legal instruction).
- The case router is running on queue `rwb-case` and the `transfer` activity is deployed by RWB-P3-E1021-OPS.

##### 4. Flow

Automated path (one Kafka event, the four steps of the workflow model):

1. Event source: another service writes its fact to its own outbox and publishes it — CaseStateChanged for a stage change, RouteDecided for a route decided (legacy trigger ROUTE_APPROVED), DeviationRaised, DeviationCleared, ApprovalRequested, DocumentStored or PaymentMissed. A timer expiry is raised inside `CaseWorkflow` by its durable timer. Each event names the case; no payload carries personal data.
2. Case router: the Kafka consumer of `rwb-case` reads the event into the inbox of DP-09, deduplicates by event ID (R-UNI-40), and calls `signalWithStart` on `CaseWorkflow` with workflow ID equal to the case ID.
3. `CaseWorkflow` forwards the trigger to the running stage child, or handles it itself when no stage child is open; the trigger is one `TransferTrigger` fact built from the event code and the case snapshot.
4. `EvaluateRules` activity: the embedded Drools kit evaluates package TRANSFER for the fact and the business date and returns the first matching rule in row order (T5) with its rule ID and package version. No match means no transfer and no decision record.
5. `transfer` activity: skips an automated transfer when `legal_hold` is true (R-UNI-20) and writes the skip to the log with the rule ID R-UNI-20.
6. `transfer` activity: locks the case by its version, picks the owner in the target queue with the assignment engine, and checks the move is allowed from the case status.
7. `RecordAndApply`, one transaction in `rwb_case`: ends the open assignment, writes the new assignment with reason TRANSFER and the rule ID, updates queue, team and owner, writes the decision record (rule ID, package version, from and to queue and owner, trigger, hash link), and writes the outbox rows for `rwb.case.CaseTransferred.v1` (EV-04) and the decision record.
8. The outbox relay publishes `rwb.case.CaseTransferred.v1` to `rwb.case.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1` to the shared topic; `rwb-decision` collects the record into the central ledger within 5 minutes.
9. Team manager: calls `POST /cases/{caseId}/transfer` with reason code MANUAL, transfer reason R03 and a target owner or queue; steps 6 and 7 run with reason MANUAL and step 7 writes the decision record with the caller, the reason and the target, and no rule ID. `Idempotency-Key` is required and a repeat with the same key returns the first response.
10. Litigation officer: calls `POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-hold` with action place or lift; the case goes to On hold or back to the status it paused in, and `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` is published.

The decision record is written before the change takes effect and in the same transaction, so a failure leaves both unchanged (R-UNI-39).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Two transfers reach the same case in the same second | First commits; second refused on the version check and logged as rejected | MSG-GEN-004 | AC3 |
| X2 | Manual transfer without a transfer reason | Refused with 422; nothing changes | MSG-P3-001 | AC6 |
| X3 | Named target owner at the caseload cap | Refused with 422; nothing changes | MSG-P3-002 | AC7 |
| X4 | Transfer of a closed case | Refused with 409 | MSG-P3-005 | AC8 |
| X5 | Decision record write fails | Refused with 503 for a manual call; the activity is retried for a rule transfer; nothing changes | MSG-P7-003 | AC9 |
| X6 | Rule trigger arrives while legal_hold is true | No automated transfer; the skip is logged | None | AC10 |
| X7 | The same event arrives twice | Second ignored by the inbox; one transfer | None | AC11 |
| X8 | No owner below the cap in the target queue | Case placed in the target queue's overflow queue with no owner; team manager told | MSG-P3-011 | AC12 |
| X9 | Hold placed on a case already on hold | Refused with 409 | MSG-P3-005 | AC13 |
| X10 | No TRANSFER rule matches the event | No transfer; no decision record | None | AC14 |
| X11 | A role without Queue and allocation U calls the transfer | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-E1-021-15 |

A TRANSFER version not in force is refused by the embedded Drools kit before the case is touched (NoPackageInForce, MSG-P3-027). The error is non-retryable in the activity retry policy: the event stays on the inbound topic for redelivery once a version is in force, and no case moves. It is not a per-case exception path.

Two more target-service paths:

- A stale version at commit (zero rows updated) is MSG-GEN-004 and the second transfer is recorded with final call TRANSFER_REJECTED, as in the legacy behaviour.
- Who may override a transfer that a rule or the cap check has refused is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0689; ASM-1236). This story provides no override path: a refused transfer changes nothing and the caller may retry with another target.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds on the assignment engine (RWB-P3-E1020-APP), the workflow kit, the Drools kit, the decision-record library, the reference-data contract and the contract of this key; no screen |
| Negotiable | Trigger rows, target queues and the reason list are data |
| Valuable | Removes email hand-offs between the six recovery teams |
| Estimable | One case router path, one activity, one package, two endpoints |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Every criterion has a test case in section 16 |
