AC4 (Eight triggers) is not owned by this story. The eight triggers stay covered by BR2 and are exercised by TC-E1-021-04, which this story keeps in section 16 because the legacy test set for the key is carried in full by the build story.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A case moves by the first TRANSFER rule, in row order, whose trigger and condition match. First match follows D-RCV-36 T5 | Package TRANSFER; REQ-CWC-010 |
| BR2 | The eight triggers are stage change, route decided, timer expired, deviation raised, deviation cleared, approval needed, document received and payment missed. They arrive as one TransferTrigger fact with an event code; a manual request is a separate call with a caller-supplied reason | REQ-CWC-010; events EV-05, EV-06, EV-07, EV-09, EV-12, EV-16, EV-18; D-RCV-36 T5 |
| BR3 | A manual transfer needs a transfer reason from the list | LOV-TRANSFER-REASON (assumed); REQ-WKM-003; VR-P3-010-1 |
| BR4 | A transfer to an owner at the cap is refused | queue.capacity_cap; VR-P3-010-2 |
| BR5 | A case is in exactly one queue with one open assignment | REQ-CWC-005 |
| BR6 | No automated transfer while a legal hold is in force | R-UNI-20 |
| BR7 | Lifting a hold returns the case to the status it paused in | R-UNI-21; casemodel.txt status transitions |
| BR8 | An event with the same ID is processed once | R-UNI-40 |
| BR9 | Every rule transfer is logged with the rule ID and package version, and every manual transfer with its caller and reason, before it takes effect | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; REQ-CWC-016; D-RCV-36 T5 |
| BR10 | A transfer keeps the case status and the clocks | R-UNI-18 (same principle for reallocation) |
| BR11 | The manual transfer API is unchanged: endpoint, request, response, errors and authorization stay as they are | REQ-CWC-010 |
| BR12 | A TRANSFER version not in force leaves the trigger event unprocessed and moves no case; it is never a default transfer | R-UNI-41; D-RCV-36 T5 |

Target-service statements that make the rules hold in `rwb-case`:

- BR1 is executed by the embedded Drools kit inside the `EvaluateRules` activity; the row order is the salience in the package, and no trigger list, row order or target queue is written in code (D-RCV-36 T3, T5).
- BR9 is executed by the decision-record library of DP-03 in the same transaction as the state change (one `RecordAndApply` activity), so the record and the change commit together or not at all.
- BR3 and BR4 read the reason list and the queue cap through `rwb-case`'s own contract of DP-07 and `rwb_case.queue.capacity_cap`; no business value is typed in code (BR-P3-010).
- BR8 is executed by the inbox of DP-09 (`rwb_case.processed_event`) and by `Idempotency-Key` on the POST.
- BR11 is the reason the transfer request, response, error codes and authorization are copied unchanged into RWB-P3-E1021-CON.

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| New, Assigned, In progress, any Waiting | LEGAL_HOLD_PLACED (R-UNI-20) | Placed through the legal-hold endpoint | On hold |
| On hold | LEGAL_HOLD_LIFTED (R-UNI-21) | Lifted through the legal-hold endpoint | The status it paused in |

A rule or manual transfer changes the queue, the team and the owner, not the status. `status_before_hold` holds the status the case paused in.

Workflow states of the capability itself:

| From | Event | To |
|---|---|---|
| CaseWorkflow running, no transfer pending | a trigger event or a manual call arrives | `EvaluateRules` scheduled as an activity |
| `EvaluateRules` done with a rule | rule ID and package version returned | `transfer` activity scheduled |
| `transfer` done | queue, team, owner and assignment changed | `RecordAndApply` scheduled |
| `RecordAndApply` committed | decision record and outbox rows written | waiting on the next durable timer or signal |
| `evaluate` or `transfer` raised NoPackageInForce or a refusal | error recorded with its message ID | waiting; the case is unchanged |
| Stage ends or 28 days pass | Continue-As-New | CaseWorkflow continues with a new run and the same workflow ID |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-TEAMMGR | Transfers and reassigns cases in team scope (Queue and allocation U) |
| RW-CAPACITY | Transfers cases (Queue and allocation U) |
| RW-LITOFF and other roles with Case record U | Place and lift a legal hold on a Legal or court instruction (Case record U) |
| RW-CASEOWN | Reads the case; may not transfer (Queue and allocation R) |
| SY-RULES | Evaluates package TRANSFER through the embedded Drools kit, inside the activity |
| SY-CASEWF | Carries out rule transfers (Queue and allocation CRU) |
| SY-DECLOG | Writes the decision records and publishes them on the shared topic |

The authorisation decision is taken by `rwb-access` (Recovery roles as data, scope, masking and DoA in `rwb_access`) and is consumed as the cached permission decision the service holds. This story adds no REST operation consumption and no guard of its own for it: the refusal shape is 403 with MSG-P4-002, as in the legacy endpoint. Where the legacy guard is replaced by the shared guard library is RWB-P3-E1019-APP (DP-08); this story inherits it.

Who may override a transfer that has been refused is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0689; ASM-1236).

The database login is per service (DP-02). Its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0688; ASM-1235); the story refers to "the rwb-case login (DP-02)".

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`, module `case/transfer`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| CaseRouter | Kafka consumer with inbox | Reads the trigger events, deduplicates by event ID, calls `signalWithStart` on `CaseWorkflow` |
| TransferTrigger | Fact record | event code, case number, stage, route, deviation state, legal hold |
| TransferActivity | Temporal activity | Hold check, `EvaluateRules` call through the kit, version lock, owner choice, assignment swap, record and outbox in one transaction |
| TransferService | Service | The shared logic behind the activity and the manual call |
| TransferController | Controller | `POST /cases/{caseId}/transfer` and `POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-hold`, with the access check and `Idempotency-Key` |
| LegalHoldService | Service | Place and lift with `status_before_hold`, publish CaseStateChanged |
| CaseRepository | Repository | `recovery_case`, `assignment`, `queue`, `queue_member`, `timer`; no foreign table |
| RuleModelClient | Kit client | Fetches the TRANSFER model of the version in force, verifies the checksum, hands it to the KieBase registry |

**Database**

- Writes `recovery_case` (queue_id, team_code, owner_user_id, status, legal_hold, status_before_hold, rule_version, version), `assignment` (end the open row, insert the new row with transfer_reason_code), the inbox `processed_event` and the outbox.
- Update with `WHERE id = ? AND version = ?`; zero rows updated means the version changed (MSG-GEN-004).
- Constraint: partial unique index `ux_assignment_open_case ON assignment (case_id) WHERE ended_at IS NULL AND task_id IS NULL`.
- Migration in this story, in the per-service Flyway sequence of DP-15: `V1021_1__transfer.sql` adds `recovery_case.status_before_hold`, `assignment.transfer_reason_code`, the partial unique index and `processed_event` (event_id uuid primary key, consumer varchar(60), processed_at).

**Configuration and reference data**

- Package TRANSFER version "TRF-2026.11", loaded by RW-COE and approved by RW-RISK through RWB-E1-073 (RWB-P3-E1073-APP); the running version is a row in `rwb-decision`, not in this schema.
- LOV-TRANSFER-REASON (R01 to R06; DL23) through the reference-data contract of DP-07.
- Queues and members from RWB-E1-019 data, read from `rwb_case`.
- Feature flag `rwb.p3.transfer`. Off: no rule transfers, the manual endpoints return 404 and the activity is not registered.

**Build steps**

1. `TransferTrigger` and the `EvaluateRules` call through the kit, with unit tests for each trigger (BR2), no match (AC14) and a version not in force (BR12).
2. `transfer` activity with version lock, hold check and assignment swap; tests AC1, AC3, AC10, AC12.
3. Case router with the inbox and `signalWithStart`; test AC11.
4. Manual path with reason and cap validation; tests AC2, AC6, AC7, AC8.
5. `LegalHoldService` place and lift; tests AC5, AC13.
6. Decision record as the last step of the same transaction, including the rejected transfer, and the outbox rows; test AC9.
7. Controller endpoints with the access check and `Idempotency-Key`; access test.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The single legacy interface the DP-11 row replaces is the in-process `RuleEvaluator` call; the transfer activity is the mockable boundary and the package is fetched as a model. DP-04's contract dependency RWB-P7-E1073-CON is carried by the platform kit's own contract (H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON) in this story's dependency list; the build-time C dependency recorded on the story is the decision contract RWB-P7-E1027-CON.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, each of the eight triggers moves a case in SIT, every rule transfer decision record names the TRANSFER rule ID and package version, every manual transfer record names the caller and reason, and `rwb.case.CaseTransferred.v1` is on the topic once per transfer with no personal data.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-001 | Manual transfer without a reason | Choose a reason for the transfer. |
| MSG-P3-002 | Target owner at the cap | {owner} is at the caseload cap. Choose another owner or the team queue. |
| MSG-P3-005 | Move not allowed from the status | This case cannot move to {state} from {current}. |
| MSG-P3-011 | Target queue full, case in overflow | {count} new cases are waiting in the overflow queue for {team}. Every owner is at the caseload cap. |
| MSG-P3-027 | No TRANSFER version is in force for a rule trigger | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | Second transfer on a changed record | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Decision log write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

For MSG-P3-027 the {check} value is "package in force" and the {detail} names the package code only.

Delivery shape: every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set to the ID above, `detail` carrying the text with its placeholders filled, and `instance` naming the request. The manual path answers 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503; the rule path never answers a caller, it records the error on the activity and lets the retry policy act.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story. The case record view (SCR-02 Case list and SCR-03 Case record) shows the new queue, owner and the hold banner through the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19 (RWB-PLT-N001-CON) and the read operations of RWB-P3-E1023-APP. The transfer screen SCR-05 comes in Epic 2 (RWB-E2-012).

States this story makes visible: the case status and queue and owner after a transfer; the hold banner while `legal_hold` is true; the overflow marker when the case sits in the overflow queue with no owner.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: triggers, target queues and the reason list are data in the TRANSFER package and the list; BR-P3-010.
- No personal data in logs, tests, workflow history, event payloads or prompts; the workflow payload codec of the kit encrypts every payload.
- No read of another service's tables (DP-01): the trigger events arrive through Kafka, the rule package arrives as a model, the reason list arrives through the reference-data contract.
- One evaluator: TRANSFER is evaluated only through the embedded Drools kit and only inside an activity; no trigger list, row order or target queue is written in code (D-RCV-36 T3, T5).
- The manual transfer API keeps its request, response, errors and authorization (BR11).
- A transfer never resets the stage clock or the prescription date (BR10).
- The transfer is idempotent twice over: `Idempotency-Key` on the POST and the inbox on the event.
- The feature flag `rwb.p3.transfer` removes the capability without a rollback of the schema.
- JOB-03 and JOB-05 are legacy references; the transfer is event-started and the timer is durable inside the workflow, so no case wait moves to a new scheduler in this story.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the transfer-record and TRANSFER-model slice of RWB-E1-021 moved into rwb-decision, so that every transfer of a case, rule-driven or manual, is explained from one append-only ledger entry that names the rule and its version or the caller and the coded reason, while the transfer engine itself stays with rwb-case. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR), a litigation officer (RW-LITOFF) and the central ledger itself**, I want **every transfer of a case, rule-driven or manual, held in one decision log entry that names the rule ID and rule version that moved it or the caller and coded reason that moved it, the trigger event and the queues and owners it moved between, that refuses a record which claims a rule and no version, and that serves the compiled TRANSFER model it cites with its checksum and its row order**, so that **any transfer of any case is explained from the ledger alone, a manual transfer is as traceable as a rule transfer, and no entry exists that cannot be reproduced**.

Inside `rwb-decision` this is the transfer-record slice of the decision log and the model side of the rule registry:

- Service `rwb-decision`, schema `rwb_decision`, REST base `/api/recovery/decision/v1`, topic `rwb.decision.events.v1` with event names `rwb.decision.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-decision` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision`.
- The transfer record is written by rwb-case in its own transaction and published as DecisionRecorded (EV-08) on the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`; this service consumes it idempotently into `decision_log_entry` and never asks rwb-case to wait for the ledger.
- The TRANSFER version "TRF-2026.11" is served from `rule_package_version` and `rule_row` of this schema, with its checksum and its row order TRF-001 to TRF-009. The model is evaluated only in rwb-case (DP-04, TSD P7 T4).

The legacy facts are unchanged: eight triggers, first match in row order, the rule ID and package version on every rule transfer, and the caller and coded reason on every manual transfer (legacy AC1 to AC4, BR1, BR2, BR9). A transfer changes the queue, the team and the owner, never the status.

##### 2. Business rationale

A case changes hands between the TDR, litigation, NPA and debt sale teams by email today. Legacy RWB-E1-021 moved the case by rule, and the email hand-off became a rule row. The remaining question in an audit is the one this story answers: why is the case in this queue with this owner, and who put it there. A rule ID with no version answers nothing; a manual transfer with no caller and no reason answers less.

The transfer engine is only as good as its ledger. rwb-decision is where every service's record meets:

1. One entry per transfer, written from the DecisionRecorded event rwb-case publishes, with the rule ID and the package version that fired, the trigger event code and the queues and owners on both sides.
2. A manual transfer held to the same standard: the caller, the coded reason and no rule ID, and a schema check that refuses a claimed rule with no version rather than storing a record nobody can reproduce.

This story is the rwb-decision part of legacy RWB-E1-021. The transfer engine, the eight-trigger listener, the queue and owner choice, the legal hold and the two endpoints stay with rwb-case (RWB-P3-E1021-APP) and its contract RWB-P3-E1021-CON; the ledger store, its trigger and the chain verifier stay with RWB-P7-E1008-APP; the record library every service writes with stays with RWB-P7-E1027-APP; authoring, the scenarios, the four eyes, the approval and the rollback stay with RWB-P7-E1073-APP. This slice delivers the records, their refusals, the read and the model read, nothing else. It meets REQ-CWC-010, REQ-CWC-016 and REQ-WKM-003, and supports REQ-CWC-005: the ledger holds the completed and the refused transfer of a case, so the one queue it ended in is provable after the fact.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The `rwb_decision` baseline is in place from RWB-P7-E1008-APP: the `decision_log_entry` table with its required columns, the append-only trigger, the hash chain and the chain verifier, plus the service-template baseline (schema, login, base, topic, queue, chart). This story adds no table of its own.
- RWB-P3-E1021-CON is published: the rwb-case transfer contract fixes the transfer request and answer and the shape of the DecisionRecorded record a transfer publishes, and it carries the fake this story builds against (DP-11).
- The record library of RWB-P7-E1027-APP is in every service from the template (DP-03), so rwb-case writes its local record and publishes EV-08 without this story.
- Package TRANSFER version "TRF-2026.11" is loaded and approved by RW-RISK, who is not its author, and is in force from 2026-11-30, with the nine rows TRF-001 to TRF-009 and at least 50 passing scenarios (legacy section 3, D-RCV-36 T5, Temporal and Drools slide 15).
- The reference-data contract of DP-07 is in force for the decision code list; the values of LOV-DECISION are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1323; ASM-2336).
- The synthetic facts the tests use: case RW-2026-000301 in queue "TDR-BKK-CO" with owner U-21, queue "LIT-BKK-OFF" of team "LIT-BKK" with owner U-31, route "R4", transfer reason "R03", record version 7, and event "EVT-88120" (legacy AC1, AC2, AC3, AC11).

##### 4. Flow

1. rwb-case carries out the transfer and, in the same transaction in its own schema, writes the transfer record and a DecisionRecorded row to its outbox; the relay publishes it on `rwb.decision-record.v1` with the case ID as the key (EV-08, CloudEvents 1.0, DP-09). The transfer never waits for this service.
2. This service's consumer reads the event once per event ID: the inbox drops a duplicate, so a redelivery never appends a second entry (R-UNI-40).
3. The validator reads the decision code, the final call, the rule ID, the rule version and the payload. The decision code is checked against LOV-DECISION. A rule ID with an empty rule version is refused before any append. A record with final call CASE_TRANSFERRED and no rule version, model version or agent version at all is refused naming "versions" (FSD AC-ALT-P7-008-01).
4. The ledger appends one `decision_log_entry` in `rwb_decision`: id, case_id, decision_code, rule_id, rule_version, inputs_ref (the trigger event code), final_call, actions (the from and to queue and the from and to owner), decided_at, actor_user_id, chain_seq, prev_hash and entry_hash. The entry hash is the SHA-256 of the entry's canonical form and prev_hash is the entry hash before it; the first entry's prev_hash is 64 zeros.
5. A rule-driven transfer arrives with final call "CASE_TRANSFERRED", rule ID "TRF-007", rule version "TRF-2026.11", the trigger event code and from "TDR-BKK-CO"/U-21 to "LIT-BKK-OFF"/U-31. No name, account number, amount or document text is copied into the entry.
6. A second transfer refused on a changed record arrives with final call "TRANSFER_REJECTED", the same rule ID "TRF-007" and the same rule version "TRF-2026.11", and the same from and to values as the transfer that committed. The ledger then holds one CASE_TRANSFERRED and one TRANSFER_REJECTED for the case, which is how the one queue the case ended in stays provable (REQ-CWC-005).
7. A manual transfer arrives with final call "CASE_TRANSFERRED", the caller as actor_user_id, the reason "R03" in the payload, and no rule ID and no rule version. It passes the schema check because a rule version is required only when a rule ID is claimed.
8. The entry commits before the inbound coordinate commits, and the record is acknowledged within 5 minutes of the transfer (Temporal and Drools slide 31). A failed append commits neither, so a half entry never exists.
9. The read: `GET /decision-log` filters by case, rule and period and answers the page with `chainVerified` on each entry; `GET /decision-log/{entryId}` answers one entry with its rule, version, inputs reference and both hashes.
10. The registry: `GET /rule-models/{packageCode}/{version}` serves the compiled TRANSFER model "TRF-2026.11" with its SHA-256 and its rows in row order; JOB-20, a Temporal Schedule at 00:01 in queue `rwb-decision`, promotes a version and publishes `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` (EV-30).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A record names rule ID "TRF-007" with an empty rule version | Refused before any append; nothing is stored and the refusal names the field | MSG-P7-009 naming "ruleVersion" | AC4 |
| X2 | A record carries decision code "D99", outside LOV-DECISION | Refused before any append; nothing is stored and the refusal names the field | MSG-P7-009 naming "decisionCode" | AC4 |
| X3 | A record carries final call "CASE_TRANSFERRED" with no rule version, model version or agent version | Refused; the refusal names "versions"; the transfer in the same transaction is rolled back by the writer | MSG-P7-009 naming "versions" | AC4 |
| X4 | The same event ID arrives a second time | One entry; the first entry ID is returned and the repeat is counted as an idempotency hit | None | AC1 |
| X5 | A manual call repeats with the same Idempotency-Key | One entry; the first entry ID is returned | None | AC3 |
| X6 | The ledger store is unavailable | Nothing is appended, the coordinate is not committed and the record stays on the topic; the caller that waits on the seal is refused | MSG-P7-003 (GAP-1323; ASM-2336) | AC7 |
| X7 | A version whose state is LOADED, APPROVED, SUPERSEDED, ROLLED_BACK or REFUSED is asked for | Refused rather than served; the client keeps the model it holds | MSG-P7-009 naming the version state | AC6 |
| X8 | The stored checksum does not match the compiled model | Refused and reported; the model is not served and no client swaps it in | MSG-P7-009 naming the checksum | AC6 |
| X9 | An entry fails the chain on a read | The page answers with `chainVerified` false on that entry and the warning | MSG-P7-012 | AC5 |

A record refused at X1, X2 or X3 is not retried: it is a defect in the calling service's record, and that service's own transaction rolls back with it. A record that fails on an unavailable store (X6) is different and is re-read, because the transfer already happened in rwb-case's schema.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against the `rwb_decision` baseline of RWB-P7-E1008-APP, the RWB-P3-E1021-CON fake and the TRANSFER version already in force; it calls no other service at run time |
| Negotiable | Nothing business is fixed here: the rule rows, the reason list and the decision code list are data, and the policy is the package's |
| Valuable | One place where any transfer of any case is explained, and a ledger that refuses a record nobody could reproduce |
| Estimable | One consumer, one validator, one append, one read, one model read, one Schedule |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests, as a secondary slice of the legacy key |
| Testable | Every criterion in section 7 is one automated test against the event fake, the store fixture and the package fixture |

```gherkin
    Given the ledger store is unavailable
    When a DecisionRecorded event for case "RW-2026-000309" with transfer reason "R03" arrives on "rwb.decision-record.v1"
    Then the record is refused with 503 and MSG-P7-003
    Then no decision_log_entry is appended and no chain_seq is used
    Then the inbound coordinate is not committed, the record stays on the topic and the entry is appended when the store returns
```

The seven criteria above are new and test only this deliverable: the transfer records of the central ledger, their refusals, the read that explains them, the model read and the promotion event. The legacy criteria of RWB-E1-021 are owned elsewhere: AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC10 and AC12 of the legacy story are the transfer engine and the queue and owner choice of rwb-case (RWB-P3-E1021-APP); AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9 and AC13 are its request validation and the legal hold; the access refusal stays with rwb-access (RWB-P4-E1021-APP); AC14 is the no-match path of rwb-case, which writes no record and therefore sends nothing here.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every transfer, rule-driven or manual, has exactly one decision log entry, appended when the transfer records it and never dropped; the ledger holds the completed and the refused transfer of a case, so the queue the case ended in stays provable | REQ-CWC-016; REQ-CWC-005; FSD P7 A2.2; principle 5 |
| BR2 | A rule transfer entry names the rule ID and the package version that fired; a manual entry names the caller and the coded transfer reason and names no rule ID | REQ-CWC-010; REQ-WKM-003; legacy BR2, BR9 |
| BR3 | A record that claims a rule ID must name its rule version; a claimed rule with no version is refused before any append and the refusal names the field | FSD P7 AC-EXC-P7-008-01; legacy BR9 |
| BR4 | A decision code outside LOV-DECISION is refused before any append and the refusal names the field | FSD P7 AC-EXC-P7-008-05; TSD P7 T3.1 (DF-DEC-003) |
| BR5 | The ledger is append only and hash chained: prev_hash is the entry_hash of chain_seq minus one, the first prev_hash is 64 zeros, and each entry_hash is the SHA-256 of the entry's canonical form | FSD P7 AC-ALT-P7-001-01; TSD P7 T3.1; Temporal and Drools slide 16 |
| BR6 | An event with the same event ID, and a manual call with the same Idempotency-Key, each give one entry, and the repeat returns the first entry ID | R-UNI-40; FSD P7 AC-EXC-P7-008-03; legacy BR8 |
| BR7 | The read answers every transfer of a case in a period, by case, rule and version, with chainVerified on each entry, and a break is reported on the page rather than hidden | API-P7-006; FSD P7 AC-BG-P7-002-01; NFR-035; TSD P7 T6.1 |
| BR8 | A package version is served only when its state is IN_FORCE and its checksum matches the compiled model; no rule is evaluated in this service, and a version not in force is never a default | Temporal and Drools slide 15; DP-04; TSD P7 T4 |
| BR9 | The ledger blocks rather than drops: when the store cannot be written nothing is appended, the coordinate is not committed and the record stays on the topic, so the history never has a silent gap | R-UNI-39; FSD P7 VR-P7-008-2 (MSG-P7-003); Temporal and Drools slide 28 |

How the rules hold in `rwb-decision`:

- BR1 and BR2 are executed by `TransferRecordConsumer` and `LedgerAppend`: the entry is built from the event only, and the actor, the rule ID, the rule version and the reason come from fields of the event, never from a lookup in another schema.
- BR3, BR4 and BR8 are executed before a byte is stored: `TransferRecordValidator` refuses a bad record in the same consumer call, and `RuleModelReader` reads the version state and the checksum and refuses before it serves.
- BR5, BR6 and BR7 are executed by the store and the read: the append-only trigger and the chain columns are the store story's, the inbox and the unique idempotency key (`DF-DEC-031`) hold the repeat, and `DecisionLogQuery` answers the stored hash with its verified flag.
- BR9 is executed by the commit order: the append and the inbound coordinate are one transaction, so a failure leaves both out.

##### 9. State transitions

The case state machine is not this service's (TSD P7 T4: "No case state machine of its own"). This slice changes no case state; it records what rwb-case did.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| none | DecisionRecorded arrives | The event ID is unseen, the decision code is in LOV-DECISION, a claimed rule ID carries its version and the required fields are present | Appended at chain_seq n+1 with final_call CASE_TRANSFERRED or TRANSFER_REJECTED |
| none | DecisionRecorded arrives | The schema check fails | Nothing appended, no chain_seq used, MSG-P7-009; the record is not retried |
| appended | the same event ID or Idempotency-Key arrives again | The idempotency key matches an existing entry | No second row; the first entry ID is returned |

The package version moves through its own states, and only one of them is served:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| none | a workload is uploaded and passes the load checks | Compile, schema, overlap, unreachable row, default row, at least 50 scenarios and the dry run pass | LOADED |
| LOADED | RW-RISK approves | The approver is not the author | APPROVED |
| APPROVED | JOB-20 at 00:01 on the valid-from date | The version is approved and its valid-from date has arrived | IN_FORCE, and RulePackageInForce is published |
| IN_FORCE | a later version is promoted, or a rollback | The later version reaches its valid-from date, or RW-RISK calls rollback once | SUPERSEDED, or ROLLED_BACK with the earlier version back IN_FORCE |
| LOADED, APPROVED | a load check fails | Any check fails | REFUSED |

Only IN_FORCE is served on `/rule-models/{packageCode}/{version}`; the other five states answer a refusal (AC6).

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| rwb-decision service identity (the rwb-decision login, DP-02) | Consumes DecisionRecorded, appends the entry, serves the model read and publishes RulePackageInForce; holds no grant on another schema |
| SY-CASEWF and SY-RULES | C on the decision log (TSD P7 T6.1): fetch the model and write their own record before this service collects it |
| RW-TEAMMGR, RW-LITOFF, RW-RISK, RW-COE, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-CASEOWN and every role with Decision log R | Read the entries of a case in their scope, with `chainVerified` |
| RW-COE and RW-RISK | Author a package version, and approve one that is not their own (the authoring story) |
| rwb-case (P3) | Owns the transfer, the trigger, the queue and owner choice and the record it publishes; this service reads none of its tables |

The authorisation decision is the cached permission decision from rwb-access that the service template's guard already holds; DP-08 is not in this slice's pattern set, so this story adds no guard of its own. The refusals are 403 with MSG-P4-002 for a role without the right, 404 with the not-found answer for an entry that does not exist, and 503 with MSG-P7-003 when the ledger cannot be read or written. The role codes are rows of the role model in `rwb_access` (TSD P7 T6.1) and are not fixed in code.

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Table in rwb_decision | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-DEC-001 | decision_log_entry | id | Write |
| DF-DEC-002 | decision_log_entry | case_id (the case the transfer moved) | Write |
| DF-DEC-003 | decision_log_entry | decision_code | Write; checked against LOV-DECISION |
| DF-DEC-004 | decision_log_entry | rule_id | Write (empty on a manual transfer) |
| DF-DEC-005 | decision_log_entry | rule_version (the package version label) | Write (empty on a manual transfer; refused when rule_id is set and it is empty) |
| DF-DEC-008 | decision_log_entry | inputs_ref (the trigger event code of the eight) | Write |
| DF-DEC-012 | decision_log_entry | final_call | Write (CASE_TRANSFERRED or TRANSFER_REJECTED) |
| DF-DEC-014 | decision_log_entry | actions (from and to queue, from and to owner, the reason on a manual transfer) | Write; the field names inside the JSONB are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1323; ASM-2336) |
| DF-DEC-016 | decision_log_entry | decided_at | Write (the time of the transfer, not of the ingest) |
| DF-DEC-017, DF-DEC-018, DF-DEC-028 | decision_log_entry | prev_hash, entry_hash, chain_seq | Write |
| DF-DEC-030 | decision_log_entry | actor_user_id | Write (SY-CASEWF on a rule transfer, the caller on a manual transfer) |
| DF-DEC-031 | decision_log_entry | idempotency_key (the event ID, or the Idempotency-Key of a manual call) | Write |
| DF-REF-279 to DF-REF-295 | rule_package_version | id, version_label, status, checksum, valid_from, author, approver and the rest of the version row | Read |
| DF-REF-002, DF-REF-003, DF-REF-006, DF-REF-007, DF-REF-052 to DF-REF-054 | rule_row | rule_id, rule_version, event_code, condition_expr, rule_table, row_order, target_queue_code | Read |

Field IDs are those in the Technical Specification P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1 and the API Specification v4 rule-package schemas. `decision_log_entry` is the only table this slice writes. No customer name, account number, amount, document text or free text reason is held in the entry: the manual reason is a list value ("R03") and the transfer detail is identifiers only.

##### 12. Contract

Base `/api/recovery/decision/v1`, owner rwb-decision (P7), schema `rwb_decision`, topic `rwb.decision.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-decision`.

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

| Method | Path | API ID | Access | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/decision-log` | API-P7-006 | Decision log R | Search by case, rule, rule version, approver and period; `caseId`, `caseIds`, `decision`, `ruleId`, `ruleVersion`, `approver`, `from`, `to`, `page`, `size` (1 to 500) and `text/csv` export; each entry carries `chainVerified` and the page carries MSG-P7-012 on a break |
| GET | `/decision-log/{entryId}` | API-P7-007 | Decision log R | One entry with its rule ID, rule version, inputs reference, final call and both hashes |
| GET | `/rule-models/{packageCode}/{version}` | none in API Specification v4 (Arch v5 slide 14: `GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}`) | C on the decision log for the owning service identity (SY-RULES, SY-CASEWF) | The compiled TRANSFER model with its SHA-256 and its rows in row order; the full path decorator and response shape are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1323; ASM-2336) |

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. The transfer record arrives as an event, not as a call, and this service calls no other service at run time. The decision code list is resolved by the writer story through the reference-data contract of DP-07, and the model rows are read from this service's own schema.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Key | When | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` | `rwb.decision.events.v1` | packageCode | JOB-20 at 00:01, or a rollback | EV-30; the owning service takes the package code and the version label from it, fetches the model on 12.1 and verifies the checksum |

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Producer | Key | Handling |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DecisionRecorded (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | every service; for a transfer, rwb-case (P3) | caseId | CloudEvents 1.0; inbox deduplication on the event ID; one `decision_log_entry` per event; acknowledged within 5 minutes; a schema failure is refused and not retried, a store failure is re-read |

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The ingestion is a Kafka consumer and the promotion is a Schedule; this story starts no workflow and runs no activity, and it holds no case state. `ApprovalWorkflow` is the approval story's.

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Job | Time | Queue | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| JOB-20 Rule promote | 00:01 | `rwb-decision` | Promotes an approved version whose valid-from date has arrived, sets it IN_FORCE, supersedes the version it replaces and publishes `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` (DP-10) |

| Table | Owner | Note |

| `decision_log_entry` | P7 (rwb_decision) | The append-only, hash-chained ledger row; this slice appends and reads it |
| `rule_package_version` | P7 (rwb_decision) | One row per uploaded version of the package TRANSFER, with its label, state, checksum, valid-from, author and approver; read here |
| `rule_row` | P7 (rwb_decision) | The parsed catalogue, TRF-001 to TRF-009, with event code, condition, row order and target queue; read here |
| inbox and processed-event objects | PLT library, created in `rwb_decision` | The inbox that drops a duplicate event and the coordinate this slice commits with the entry |

| package fixture (RWB-P7-E1073-APP data) | `rule_package_version` and `rule_row` | "TRF-2026.11" IN_FORCE with checksum `SHA-256-TRF-2026-11` and nine rows TRF-001 to TRF-009; a version in state LOADED; a checksum that does not match |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision`, module `transferrecord`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision.transferrecord`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| TransferRecordConsumer | Kafka consumer | Reads DecisionRecorded once per event ID, takes the decision code, final call, rule ID, rule version, actor and payload, and calls the validator; commits the inbound coordinate with the entry |
| TransferRecordValidator | Service | Checks the decision code against LOV-DECISION, requires a rule version when a rule ID is claimed, requires the version group on a completed transfer, and refuses with MSG-P7-009 before any append |
| LedgerAppend | Service | Appends the entry with chain_seq, prev_hash and entry_hash in one transaction, holds the idempotency key and returns the first entry ID on a repeat |
| DecisionLogQuery | Service | The read by case, rule, version and period, with `chainVerified` per entry and MSG-P7-012 on a break |
| RuleModelReader | Service | Serves the compiled model with its checksum and row order, refuses a state other than IN_FORCE and a checksum that does not match |
| TransferRecordController | Controller | The three reads of 12.1 with the access check and the problem response |

**Database and migrations**

- Appends `decision_log_entry`; reads `rule_package_version`, `rule_row` and `rule_package`; writes no other schema.
- Index `(case_id, rule_id, decided_at)` on `decision_log_entry`, which serves the read of AC5 and the period filter of the screen.
- Migration in this story, in the per-service Flyway sequence of DP-15: `V1021_1__transfer_record.sql` adds that index and nothing else. The table, its required columns, the append-only trigger and the chain are the store story's, and no row is seeded here: the TRANSFER version and its nine rows arrive through the authoring story.

**Configuration and reference data**

- No business value is configured here: the rule rows, the target queues, the condition "R4" and the reason "R03" are data of the package and of the reason list; the decision codes are the LOV-DECISION list.
- Two settings only: the rwb-case transfer contract base (the fake in a build, the service in a run) and the rwb-decision login (DP-02), named by the DB story of this service. The 5-minute acknowledgement target and the commit order are configuration of the consumer, not code branches.

**Build steps**

1. `TransferRecordConsumer` and `TransferRecordValidator` against the event fake, with the completed transfer, the refused transfer and the manual transfer; tests for AC1, AC2 and AC3.
2. The refusals of BR3, BR4 and BR9 before any append, and the assertion that a refused record uses no chain_seq; tests for AC4 and AC7.
3. `LedgerAppend` with the idempotency key and the repeat path; tests for AC1 and AC3.
4. `DecisionLogQuery` with the period and rule filters, `chainVerified` and MSG-P7-012; test for AC5.
5. `RuleModelReader` with the IN_FORCE state and the checksum check, and `RulePromotionSchedule` with a shortened schedule in SIT; test for AC6.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_decision`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

This is a secondary slice with no owned legacy acceptance criteria of a build story: it adds no new build dependency of its own (metadata "Depends on (build)" = None) and builds against the `rwb_decision` baseline and the RWB-P3-E1021-CON fake. Read one by one:

- DP-01, DP-02 and DP-13 are the target shape itself: the schema `rwb_decision`, the rwb-decision login and the base `/api/recovery/decision/v1`, with no new dependency.
- DP-03, DP-09 and DP-14 are the live patterns of the record: DecisionRecorded arrives on `rwb.decision-record.v1` through the inbox, RulePackageInForce leaves through the outbox, and both names come from the naming library.
- DP-04 applies divided: the registry half is here (the version, its checksum and its rows are served) and the evaluation half is rwb-case's; this service holds no KieBase, which is what lets the record and the row that fired be read side by side.
- DP-05, DP-07 and DP-10 are statements of what is not done here (no ACE view, no list value in code, no Quartz job), DP-11 is the record crossing as a published event with the model read as a one-hop 2 s contract, DP-15 is `V1021_1__transfer_record.sql`, and DP-19 is the composite route behind the decision log page and SCR-03.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the contract tests of RWB-P3-E1021-CON stay green, and a SIT week shows every transfer of every case in the ledger with its rule ID and version or its caller and reason, no entry for a record that failed the schema, one entry per event on a redelivery, the model read answering IN_FORCE only, and a break on the read visible as MSG-P7-012 rather than hidden.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-009 | A record fails the ledger schema: a rule ID with no rule version (names "ruleVersion"), a decision code outside LOV-DECISION (names "decisionCode"), a completed transfer with no version at all (names "versions"), or a version that is not IN_FORCE or whose checksum does not match (names the state or the checksum) | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1323; ASM-2336) |
| MSG-P7-003 | The ledger store cannot be written or read | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P7-012 | An entry on the page fails the chain | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1323; ASM-2336) |
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller's role holds no Decision log R, or no Decision log C for the model read | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The message text of MSG-P7-009 and of MSG-P7-012 is not given in the P7 sources, which name only the field each one names and the entry each one names; the two IDs and the field they name are the contract until the message catalogue fixes the sentences. Every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set to the ID above, `detail` carrying the text with its placeholders filled, and `instance` naming the request. The read answers 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404 for an entry that does not exist, and 503 with MSG-P7-003. For MSG-P4-002 the {action} value names the action the caller tried - "read this decision log" or "hold this rule model" - and never a case fact.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen of its own in this story. The read plane is what the screens use: the decision log page reads `GET /decision-log` by case and period and shows, for each transfer, the rule ID, the rule version, the from and to queue and owner, the final call and the chain flag; the decision tab of SCR-03 Case record shows the same entries for one case, beside the case header read from rwb-case. Both are served by the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), one hop to rwb-decision and one to rwb-case. The states this story makes visible are three: an entry that verifies (`chainVerified` true), an entry that does not (false, with MSG-P7-012 on the page and no silent pass), and the refusal when a reader's role holds no right (403 with MSG-P4-002). The page layout, its filters, its loading and empty states and its export belong to the decision-log screen story; the case number shown beside an entry is read from the rwb-case contract at display time and is never stored in `rwb_decision`.

The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID. The legacy level System maps to End to end, Access to Component and Resilience to NFR. Every legacy test case of RWB-E1-021 is listed above with the slice of the behaviour this story answers; the -ITG copies belong to the integration slice RWB-ITG-E1021-ITG and are not rows of this table.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the rule rows, the target queues, the condition "R4", the reason "R03" and the decision codes are data of the package and the lists, read at run time. No queue code, rule ID or reason code appears in this service's Java.
- No personal data in events, workflow inputs, logs or tests. This slice writes case IDs, queue codes, owner IDs, rule IDs, versions and hashes only; no name, address, identity number, account number or free-text reason is held or logged. Test data uses synthetic keys (`RW-2026-000301`, U-21, U-31, `TDR-BKK-CO`, `LIT-BKK-OFF`).
- No cross-schema read (DP-01): `rwb_decision` reads no `rwb_case` table and no table of another service; the transfer arrives as an event and the case is never queried.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `v_ace_*` views, and this service reads no view (DP-05): no customer or account fact enters the ledger.
- One evaluator, and it is not this one: TRANSFER is evaluated only in rwb-case (DP-04), and this service serves the model and records the answer. The ledger is append only: no code path updates or deletes a `decision_log_entry`, and a correction is a new entry with `corrects_entry_id`.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the deviation-triggered half of RWB-E1-021 is realigned onto rwb-deviation (S8). The engine moves into the service that raises the trigger: the `TransferTrigger` fact is built from `DeviationRaised` and `DeviationCleared` in `DeviationWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-deviation`, the TRANSFER package is evaluated by the service's embedded Drools kit with first match in row order (DP-04), the decision record is written before the move through the local library (DP-03), and the queue, team and owner move is requested from rwb-case on its published contract (DP-11; C RWB-P3-E1021-CON) because `recovery_case`, `queue` and `assignment` are P3's tables and the Ownership Map gives S8 only `deviation` (DP-01). The manual transfer endpoint, the legal-hold endpoint and the assignment swap stay with the primary slice of this legacy key in rwb-case. The two Operations of this service move onto `/api/recovery/deviation/v1` (DP-13), the read-only case screens are reached through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), and the events leave on `rwb.deviation.events.v1` (DP-09, DP-14). The plan's build list is empty although the DP table adds platform contract rows, and the business epic keeps wave 1 over the service wave 2 (GAP-3074; GAP-3075; ASM-5235; ASM-5236). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR)**, I want **the TRANSFER rule package evaluated inside rwb-deviation when a deviation is raised or cleared, so that the case moves to the queue and the owner the rule names, with the rule ID and the package version recorded before the move**.

This story owns:

- the `TransferTrigger` fact of the legacy story (event code, case number, stage, route, deviation state, legal hold) built from `DeviationRaised` and `DeviationCleared` and from the case trigger events this service subscribes to;
- the TRANSFER package evaluated by the service's **embedded Drools kit**, first match in row order, with the version in force read from rwb-decision (DP-04); a package with no version in force throws `NoPackageInForce` and moves no case;
- the legal-hold and idempotency checks that stand in front of the move (R-UNI-20, R-UNI-40);
- the transfer request to rwb-case that ends the open assignment, writes the new one with reason TRANSFER and the rule ID, and updates queue, team and owner (DP-11; C RWB-P3-E1021-CON);
- the decision record of every rule transfer and of every refused transfer, written in the caller's transaction **before** the case changes (DP-03);
- the `deviation` columns this move touches, `handler_user_id` and `state`, in `rwb_deviation` (DP-01);
- the outbox relay of `DeviationRaised` and `DeviationCleared` on `rwb.deviation.events.v1` (DP-09, DP-14);
- the transfer reason list read on the reference-data contract of rwb-case (DP-07) and the case facts read on the rwb-source-data contract (DP-05);
- the two operations of this service on `/api/recovery/deviation/v1` as the raise and clear paths that fire the trigger (DP-13), and the read-only SCR-02 and SCR-03 slices behind the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19);
- the per-service Flyway sequence of `rwb_deviation` for the story's own schema need, with no shared `recovery` migration (DP-15).

It does not own: the manual transfer endpoint and its `MANUAL` reason path, the legal-hold place and lift, the assignment swap itself and the `CaseTransferred` publication (the primary slice of RWB-E1-021 in rwb-case, P3); the `recovery_case`, `queue`, `assignment`, `timer` and `decision_log_entry` tables (P3 and P7); the TRANSFER package rows, their authoring, their approval and their version (rwb-decision, P7); the roles, the capability rights and the authorise operation (rwb-access, P4); and the contract surface with its fakes and its error envelope (RWB-P3-E1021-CON and the CON story of this service).

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy objective stands unchanged: a case changes hands without email, is held by one owner, and the rule that moved it is recorded with its version (RWB-E1-021 §2; REQ-CWC-010, REQ-CWC-016, REQ-WKM-003, REQ-CWC-005).

D-RCV-60 changes where the engine sits, not what the team manager gets:

- **The trigger is raised here, so the first evaluation runs here.** `DeviationRaised` and `DeviationCleared` are this service's own events (EV-06, EV-07 in the Ownership Map), and the deviation is flagged, routed and cleared in `DeviationWorkflow` on queue `rwb-deviation` (context pack; TSD S8 T4). Evaluating the TRANSFER rows for those two triggers in the service that owns the deviation removes a hop and the outbox wait that the monolith needed.
- **The case stays with rwb-case.** The S8 row of the connection matrix names REST and events to P3 and no shape beyond it; `recovery_case`, `queue` and `assignment` are P3's, and the plan gives this slice one class C dependency, `RWB-P3-E1021-CON`, which publishes the transfer request this story builds against (DP-11).
- **The rules are rwb-decision's.** The rule package registry is P7's by the default ruling and the package registry row is P7's in the Ownership Map; this service carries the **embedded** Drools kit and never owns a rule row (DP-04; ADR-017).
- **The decision is recorded first.** That is the monolith's own rule (BR9 of the legacy story, TSD S8 T2) and it survives the split unchanged: a failed record writes nothing and moves nothing (DP-03).
- **No data lake, no second truth.** The events carry identifiers, the code, the contact-stop flag and the rule version only, and rwb-reporting builds its read model from them (DP-09; ADR-018).

Wave is the one point where the two sources disagree: business epic EP01 places the story in wave 1 and the service sits in wave 2. The W-MAP wave is kept, as §R5.6 requires, and the conflict is recorded once for this service and this business epic (GAP-3074; ASM-5235).

##### 3. Preconditions

- `RWB-P3-E1021-CON` is published and tagged: the transfer request shape, the queue and assignment shapes it answers with, the version-check error, the capacity error, the error set and the fake are baselined and handed to this story.
- The platform contract stories the DP table names are published with their stubs: the local decision record and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03), the embedded Drools kit and the package reader (DP-04), the reference-data client (DP-07), the outbox and inbox library (DP-09), the workflow kit (DP-10), the topic-naming library (DP-14), the per-service Flyway baseline (DP-15) and the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The plan carries no build dependency on this key, so the story starts on Day 1 against those baselines and the fakes; the rows are tracked, not blocking (GAP-3075; ASM-5236).
- `deviation` exists in `rwb_deviation` with the columns of DF-CAS-036 to DF-CAS-045 and the standard record columns of TSD S8 T3.0, created by the DB story of this service; this story adds no table and no column.
- The TRANSFER package is in force at a version authored, tested and approved in rwb-decision (P7) with at least 50 passing scenarios, and each row holds trigger event, condition, target queue code and row order (legacy §3; D-RCV-36 T5, carried into the package registry of P7).
- The transfer reason list `LOV-TRANSFER-REASON` with R01 Capacity, R02 Customer deceased, R03 Skill, R04 Owner absent, R05 Legal referral and R06 Wrong queue is readable on the reference-data contract of rwb-case (DL23; DP-07).
- The case trigger events arrive on the subscription the connection matrix gives S8 to P3; the event names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3079; ASM-5240).
- The data product behind the case facts carries today's business date, or shows its date as stale and holds the step (VR-S8-001-1; MSG-P1-001).
- The service runs as its own login on `rwb_deviation`, holds no grant on another `rwb_*` schema and no `v_ace_*` grant, so a statement on `rwb_case` is refused by the database and fails the boundary test (DP-01, DP-05).

##### 4. Flow

1. A deviation is raised on a case for one of X1 to X7, or an open deviation is cleared, through `POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations` or `PATCH /deviations/{deviationId}` on `/api/recovery/deviation/v1` (DP-13).
2. `DeviationWorkflow` receives the signal on queue `rwb-deviation` and builds one `TransferTrigger`: event code (`DeviationRaised` or `DeviationCleared`), case number, stage code, route code, deviation state and the legal-hold flag.
3. The same signal path carries the case triggers of the subscription: a stage change or a route decision, a timer due, an approval request, a document stored or a payment missed, each with its own event code (legacy BR2; EV-05, EV-09, EV-12, EV-16, EV-18).
4. `evaluateTransferRules` loads the TRANSFER package version in force through the embedded kit and evaluates the fact; the first row in row order whose trigger and condition match wins and returns its rule ID and the package version (DP-04; legacy BR1, T5). No match means no transfer and no decision record entry.
5. A package with no version in force raises `NoPackageInForce` before the case is touched; the trigger stays in the outbox and is retried when a version is in force, and no default transfer ever runs (legacy BR12, R-UNI-41; MSG-P3-027).
6. The workflow skips an automated transfer while `legal_hold` is true and records the skip with R-UNI-20 (legacy BR6; R-DEV-01 keeps the legal clock running).
7. `requestCaseTransfer` calls rwb-case with the target queue code, the chosen owner, reason TRANSFER, the rule ID and the package version, and the trigger event ID as the idempotency evidence. One hop, 2 s, a breaker, and no retry inside the step (DP-11).
8. rwb-case locks the case by its version, picks the owner in the target queue with its assignment engine and a `LOWEST_LOAD` method, checks that the move is allowed from the case status, and in one transaction ends the open assignment, writes the new one with `transfer_reason_code`, updates queue, team and owner, and publishes `CaseTransferred` (the primary slice; legacy §4 steps 5 and 6).
9. A version conflict answers MSG-GEN-004 and the transfer is refused; an owner at the cap answers MSG-P3-002 and a queue with every owner at the cap places the case in the overflow queue with no owner and tells the team manager with MSG-P3-011 (legacy X1, X3, X8).
10. `recordAndApplyTransfer` writes, in one `rwb_deviation` transaction and as the last step before commit, the decision record with the rule ID, the package version, the from and to queue and owner and the trigger; a refused transfer is recorded with final call `TRANSFER_REJECTED` (legacy BR9; DP-03).
11. In the same transaction the activity moves the `deviation` row: `handler_user_id` becomes the owner the rule names and `state` moves to DEV_WITH_OWNER, or back to RESUMED when the trigger was the clear; the outbox row for `DeviationRaised` or `DeviationCleared` is written there (DP-09).
12. A repeated event ID is ignored and counted as an idempotency hit, and a repeated call with the same `Idempotency-Key` answers the response it already gave (R-UNI-40).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Two triggers reach the same case in the same second | First commits; second refused on the version check, recorded as `TRANSFER_REJECTED`, and the case ends in exactly one queue | MSG-GEN-004 | AC4, TC-E1-021-03 |
| X2 | No TRANSFER version is in force for the trigger | `NoPackageInForce` before the case is touched; the trigger stays in the outbox for retry; no default transfer | MSG-P3-027 | AC3, TC-E1-021-14 |
| X3 | A trigger arrives while `legal_hold` is true | No automated transfer; the skip is recorded with R-UNI-20 and nothing changes | None | AC5, TC-E1-021-10 |
| X4 | The same event ID arrives twice | Second ignored and counted; one transfer | None | Flow step 12, TC-E1-021-11 |
| X5 | No TRANSFER rule matches the trigger | No transfer and no decision record entry; the deviation stays where it is | None | AC8, TC-E1-021-14 |
| X6 | The named target owner is at the caseload cap | The request is refused with the owner named and nothing changes | MSG-P3-002 | AC6, TC-E1-021-07 |
| X7 | No owner below the cap in the target queue | The case is placed in the target queue's overflow queue with no owner and the team manager is told with the count | MSG-P3-011 | AC6, TC-E1-021-12 |
| X8 | The decision record cannot be written | Nothing changes: no transfer request, no `deviation` change and no event | MSG-P7-003 | AC7, TC-E1-021-09, TC-E1-021-16 |
| X9 | The caller lacks the Case record right on the raise or the outcome that fires the trigger | 403 before any change and before any decision record | MSG-P4-002 | AC9, TC-E1-021-15 |
| X10 | A statement, a test or a component reaches a `rwb_case` row, a `v_ace_*` view or another service's schema | The grant refuses the statement and the boundary test fails the build | None (pipeline log) | Section 17 |

X1, X3, X4, X5, X6, X7, X8 and X9 restate the legacy exception rows X1, X6, X7, X10, X3, X8, X5 and X11 for this slice, and X2 is the package-not-in-force path the legacy story states below its own table. X10 is the DP-01 and DP-05 boundary. The legacy rows that belong to the primary slice — a manual transfer without a reason (MSG-P3-001) and a hold on a case already on hold — are not restated here, and the closed case is answered by rwb-case inside the transfer request.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds on Day 1 against `RWB-P3-E1021-CON` and its fake, the platform stubs of DP-03, DP-04, DP-07, DP-09 and DP-19, and a synthetic `deviation` row; no live P3, P4 or P7 is needed |
| Negotiable | The activity names, the shape of the transfer request this service sends and the decision code per outcome are this story's choice; the rules, the messages, the package, the target queues and the `deviation` columns are fixed |
| Valuable | A deviation that changes who holds the case moves it at once, to the queue and owner the rule names, with the rule and its version recorded before the case changes |
| Estimable | One workflow branch, three activities, one package evaluation, one request to rwb-case, two event relays, the decision record and the schema sequence |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests on the fakes and the access and failure tests |
| Testable | Every path runs on synthetic cases through the contract fakes, plus the forced record failure and the boundary test |

The nine criteria are new: this slice owns no legacy criterion, because the split gives the criteria of RWB-E1-021 to the primary slice in rwb-case (`acs` is empty on this slice), and each criterion here tests only the deliverable of the title — the engine, the request it sends and the record it keeps. Every business value in the scenarios — the package version, the rule IDs, the queues, the owner IDs, the cap of 150, the reason list, the message IDs — is copied character for character from RWB-E1-021 §7, §5 and §14; no value is invented.

##### 8. Business rules

| Rule | Route set | Codes | From state | Event | Condition | Action | To state | Owner | Systems | Timer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-DEV-01 | Deviations | X1 to X7 | ANY_STATE | DEVIATION_FLAGGED | deviation_code in (X1..X7) | Pause the stage clock, keep the prescription clock running, route to the named owner | DEV_FLAGGED | Workbench | Workbench | Same day |
| R-DEV-02 | Deviations | X1 | DEV_FLAGGED | OWNER_ASSIGNED | deviation_code = X1 | Assign to the complaint officer | DEV_WITH_OWNER | Complaint officer | Workbench | None |
| R-DEV-03 | Deviations | X2, X3 | DEV_FLAGGED | OWNER_ASSIGNED | deviation_code in (X2,X3) | Assign to the specialist; Legal joins X3 for the estate claim | DEV_WITH_OWNER | Hardship and vulnerability specialist | Workbench | None |
| R-DEV-18 | Deviations | X1 to X7 | DEV_RESOLVED | CLOCK_RESUMED | Any | Resume the stage clock and return the case | RESUMED | Previous owner | Workbench | None |

The four rows are copied character for character from FSD S8 A2.2.3.1, A2.4.3.1 and the DEVIATION machine of TSD S8 T4. R-DEV-04 to R-DEV-06 assign X4 to X7 to their named owners; their text is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3078; ASM-5239). The owner column is a business role, not a service.

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A case moves by the first TRANSFER row, in row order, whose trigger and condition match the `TransferTrigger`; the rule ID and the package version are returned and recorded | Legacy BR1; D-RCV-36 T5 |
| BR2 | The trigger is the one event code the fact carries: a deviation raised or cleared here, or a case trigger of the subscription forwarded to this child | Legacy BR2; R-DEV-01 |
| BR3 | The package is read from rwb-decision and evaluated by the embedded kit of this service; no rule row, row order or target queue is written in code | DP-04; ADR-017; legacy §17 |
| BR4 | No automated transfer while a legal hold is in force, and the skip is recorded | R-UNI-20; legacy BR6 |
| BR5 | Every transfer, applied or refused, is recorded with the rule ID and the package version before it takes effect; a failed record changes nothing and answers MSG-P7-003 | Legacy BR9; DP-03; TSD S8 T2 |
| BR6 | A version not in force leaves the trigger in the outbox, moves no case and is never a default transfer | R-UNI-41; legacy BR12 |
| BR7 | An event with the same ID is processed once, and an `Idempotency-Key` answers the response it already gave | R-UNI-40; legacy BR8 |
| BR8 | The move itself is rwb-case's: this service requests it on the owner's contract and writes no `recovery_case`, `queue` or `assignment` row | DP-01, DP-11; context pack ownership rows |
| BR9 | A transfer keeps the case status and both clocks: it moves the queue, the team and the owner only | Legacy BR10; R-UNI-18 |
| BR10 | No person name, contact value, address or identity number enters the deviation row, the decision record, a log, a workflow input or an event | Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 s17 |

##### 9. State transitions

This story moves the `deviation` record of the case and requests a move of the case; it never writes the case state.

| From (`deviation.state`) | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| No row, or DEV_FLAGGED | OWNER_ASSIGNED | R-DEV-02 or R-DEV-03 fires for the code, and the transfer request is accepted | DEV_WITH_OWNER, `handler_user_id` = the owner the rule names |
| DEV_WITH_OWNER | DEVIATION_RESOLVED | The clear path fires and R-DEV-18 applies | RESUMED with `cleared_at` written |
| Any | OWNER_ASSIGNED | The transfer is refused on the version check, the cap or the record | Unchanged, with the refusal recorded |

| Step execution | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Waiting | A deviation or case trigger arrives | The package version in force is loaded | Evaluating |
| Evaluating | A TRANSFER row matches | The legal-hold check passes | Requesting |
| Evaluating | No row matches, or no version in force | X2, X5 | Waiting, nothing changed, no record |
| Requesting | rwb-case accepts the move | The decision record is written | Applying |
| Requesting | rwb-case refuses on the version check or the cap, or the record write fails | X1, X6, X8 | Waiting, the refusal recorded, nothing else changed |
| Applying | The `deviation` update and the outbox row commit | The transaction commits | Waiting for the next trigger |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Team manager (RW-TEAMMGR) | Holds R on the case record (TSD S8 T6.1) and is the role the legacy story serves; receives the overflow notice of MSG-P3-011 |
| Complaint officer, Hardship and vulnerability specialist, Fraud investigator, Legal counsel | Are the named owners R-DEV-02 and R-DEV-03 route X1 to X3 to, and hold RU or R on the case record (FSD S8 A2.4.3.3; TSD S8 T6.1) |
| Case owner (RW-CASEOWN) | Holds CRU and raises or clears the deviation that fires the trigger |
| The rules component of this service (embedded kit) | Evaluates the TRANSFER package; it holds no right of its own and writes nothing |
| rwb-case (P3) | Owns the case, its assignment, its queue and its version check, and executes the move on this story's request |
| rwb-decision (P7) | Owns the TRANSFER package, its rows, their version and their approval; this story only evaluates the version in force |
| rwb-access (P4) | Owns the roles and the capability rights checked on the two operations |
| Solution architect | Confirms the transfer request shape and the event subscription (GAP-3076; GAP-3079) |

The legacy story named `RuleEvaluator` as the one evaluator; after the split the evaluator is the embedded kit of each service and the package registry stays in rwb-decision, which is ADR-017. No delegated-authority limit applies: a transfer takes no credit decision.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-deviation (S8); base `/api/recovery/deviation/v1` (DP-13). These are the two operations the Ownership Map gives this service; this story adds none.

| Method | Path | Shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/cases/{caseId}/deviations` | `DeviationRequest` in, `Deviation` out (API-S8-001) | Case record, right U, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header |
| PATCH | `/deviations/{deviationId}` | `DeviationOutcome` in, `Deviation` out (API-S8-002) | Case record, right U, scope applied | Not applicable |

Both answer 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404, 409, 422 and 503 in the platform error envelope; the shapes and the exact status list are the CON story's of this service. The POST is the raise path and the PATCH is the clear path that fire the trigger.

| Operation | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|
| The transfer request that ends the open assignment and writes the new one; operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3076; ASM-5237) | P3 rwb-case, contract `RWB-P3-E1021-CON` | The move of the case with reason TRANSFER, the rule ID, the package version and the trigger event ID; answers the assignment or a refusal |
| The queue, capacity and owner selection read; operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3076; ASM-5237) | P3 rwb-case | The target queue, its team, its cap, its overflow queue and the member with the lowest load |
| The reference-data read of `LOV-TRANSFER-REASON` (DP-07); operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3076; ASM-5237) | P3 rwb-case | The six reason codes R01 to R06 with their version |
| The package and rule-in-force read (DP-04); operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3076; ASM-5237) | P7 rwb-decision | The TRANSFER package in force with its version and its rows |
| The authorise call; operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3076; ASM-5237) | P4 rwb-access | The Case record right on the two operations |
| The case-facts read (DP-05); operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3076; ASM-5237) | P1 rwb-source-data | The case facts the trigger is built from, with their freshness stamp |

All six are one hop with a 2 s budget and a breaker, and none retries inside the step (DP-11, ADR-020). Only the first is a row of the plan's C list, which holds `RWB-P3-E1021-CON` alone.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** The trigger branch of `DeviationWorkflow`, the three activities, the TRANSFER package evaluation against the version in force, the legal-hold and idempotency checks, the one-hop transfer request to rwb-case, the decision record writer, the `deviation` update with its outbox row, the two event relays, and the per-service Flyway sequence of `rwb_deviation`.

**Pattern application** (§R5.5)

| DP | Legacy marker | Pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>`, "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_deviation`; no other service's table is read | None |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H `RWB-PLT-E1027-CON` |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H `RWB-PLT-E1072-CON`; C `RWB-P7-E1073-CON` |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract | None |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H `RWB-PLT-E1043-CON`; C `RWB-P3-E1043-CON` |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library, owner topic, CloudEvents | H `RWB-PLT-TE006-CON` |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H `RWB-PLT-E1071-CON` |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | None (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/deviation/v1` | None |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` and `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` through the naming library | H `RWB-PLT-E1047-CON` |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in `rwb_deviation` | H `RWB-PLT-E1044-CON` |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H `RWB-PLT-N001-CON` |

The eight H rows the table adds are platform contract rows; the plan's build list for this key is empty and therefore stays empty in the metadata, and the rows are tracked as platform dependencies (GAP-3075; ASM-5236). DP-11 keeps the one class C dependency the plan gives, `RWB-P3-E1021-CON`; DP-04 and DP-07 also add a C row each, which the metadata does not carry.

**Build steps.** (1) Wire the trigger branch and the three activities on `rwb-deviation`. (2) Load the TRANSFER package version through the embedded kit and evaluate the `TransferTrigger`, first match in row order. (3) Add the legal-hold and event-ID checks and the `NoPackageInForce` path. (4) Send the transfer request to rwb-case with the rule ID, the version and the trigger event ID, and map its refusals. (5) Write the decision record first, then the `deviation` update and the outbox row, in one transaction. (6) Relay `DeviationRaised` and `DeviationCleared`. (7) Fold the story's schema need into the per-service Flyway sequence, with no shared `recovery` migration. (8) Prove AC1 to AC9 on the fakes and run the boundary test.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.s8.transfer`. Off: no rule transfer runs, the trigger stays in the outbox, and the two operations keep working without firing the engine.

**Done when.** AC1 to AC9 pass at component and contract level on the fakes, every transfer and every refusal leaves one decision record with its rule ID and the package version, the repeat test writes once and publishes once, and the boundary test shows no `rwb_case` statement and no `v_ace_*` read.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-001 | A manual transfer without a reason (the primary slice's path, named for traceability) | Choose a reason for the transfer. |
| MSG-P3-002 | Target owner at the cap | {owner} is at the caseload cap. Choose another owner or the team queue. |
| MSG-P3-005 | Move not allowed from the status | This case cannot move to {state} from {current}. |
| MSG-P3-011 | Target queue full, case in overflow | {count} new cases are waiting in the overflow queue for {team}. Every owner is at the caseload cap. |
| MSG-P3-027 | No TRANSFER version is in force for a trigger | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | Second transfer on a changed record | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Decision record write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The data product behind the case facts is stale | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |

The text is RWB-E1-021 §14 and FSD S8 A2.1.3.1, copied unchanged; no message is reworded and none is added. For MSG-P3-027 the {check} value is "package in force" and the {detail} names the package code only.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the trigger rows, the target queues, the row order, the reason list and the caps are package rows, reference data or rwb-case facts, read with their version.
- No personal data in the `deviation` row, the decision record, an event, a workflow input, a log or a prompt: identifiers, codes, instants and a rule version only.
- ACE data and case data only through the owner's contract: no `v_ace_*` view, no `rwb_case` statement, no document blob and no other service's schema (DP-01, DP-05, DP-11).
- One evaluator per service and one package registry: TRANSFER is evaluated only through the embedded kit against the version in force from rwb-decision, and no trigger list or target queue is written in code (DP-04; ADR-017).
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; this story adds no second topic and no Schedule (DP-13, DP-14).
- The decision record is written before the move and in its transaction; a failure rolls the row back, and a transfer never resets the stage clock or the prescription date.

- The contract surface: the OpenAPI and AsyncAPI documents, the `deviation` element, the lists, the envelopes, the error set and the fakes (the CON stories of this service and of P3).
- The TRANSFER package rows, their authoring, approval, promotion and rollback in rwb-decision, and the DEV transfer rows themselves (GAP-3078).
- The other six deviation codes and their flows (X2 to X7), the screening agent, the low-confidence review, two deviations on one case, the contact-breach path and the override review — each is its own story of this service.
- The case of record, its status, its route state, its timers and its queues (rwb-case, P3); the notices (rwb-comms, P6); the roles and reference data (rwb-access, P4).
- The schema, migration, login, deployment, observability and pipeline of `rwb_deviation` beyond this story's own Flyway sequence (the DB, INF and OPS stories of this legacy key).
- Any change to a legacy file, to a master or to built Epic 1 code.
