    Given every role, group and test user of the fixture is synthetic

    Then each operation is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a circuit breaker per downstream and an error as an RFC 9457 problem detail
    Then the two paths are stated at the base of the service because Architecture v5 slide 14 names the operations and the Ownership Map has no path row: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0776; ASM-1403)

  Scenario: AC2 The authorise answer carries the decision and the versions the session resolved (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a session resolved under matrix version "PM-2026.11" with role "RW-CASEOWN"
    When the guard asks for area "PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION" and right "R"
    Then the answer is REFUSED, because the Platform administration letter of "RW-CASEOWN" is "-"
    Then the answer carries matrix version "PM-2026.11", conflict version "SOD-2026.11" and the reason code NO_RIGHT
    When the guard asks for the area "DOCUMENTS" and right "R" for a session holding "RW-LITOFF" and "RW-LEGAL"
    Then the answer is ALLOWED with the letters "CRUA" as the union of "CRU" and "CRUA"

  Scenario: AC3 The permission answer and the scope of the caller are published (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a session resolved to "RW-CASEOWN" with default scope "OWN" and a team code and a region code read through the rwb-case contract
    When the caller reads GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/permissions
    Then the answer holds the role code "RW-CASEOWN", its name and default scope, and the letters of each capability area the session holds
    Then the answer holds the scope type "OWN" with the team and region codes, matrix version "PM-2026.11", conflict version "SOD-2026.11" and the resolution time
    Then the answer holds no token, no session reference of a store this service owns and no personal value

  Scenario: AC4 The refusal vocabulary and the recorded fact are fixed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a session that resolved with role "RW-PHONECOL" and the letter "-" in Platform administration
    When the guard asks for area "PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION" and right "R"
    Then the caller receives 403 with MSG-P4-002 and the action it names
    Then the recorded fact holds the user reference, area "PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION", right "R", result "REFUSED" and reason code NO_RIGHT
    Then a token without a second factor, a session with no role and a conflicting pair are refused with MSG-P4-005, MSG-P4-001 and MSG-P4-006 respectively
    Then the conflict refusal names both roles of the pair and carries reason code ROLE_CONFLICT
    Then no message id is invented and every one used is the legacy id of this key

  Scenario: AC5 The negative statements of the contract are published (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published contract document
    When a consumer asks it for a session, a token, a password, an event or a delegation limit
    Then the document has no such operation, no such field and no such event: this service publishes none of them and consumes none
    Then GET /api/recovery/access/v1/doa-limits is named as the delegation-of-authority story's of this service and is not published here
    Then the maintenance of the role-to-group mapping is named as RWB-P4-AD001-CON, and the mapping rows themselves are role.entra_group data of this service
    Then role, permission and role_conflict are named only, as the tables of this service created by RWB-P4-E1022-DB
    Then a document that adds a session table, a token or a password field is refused at review

  Scenario: AC6 The fakes and the contract test of every consuming service (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the five published fakes: session, role fixture, reference data, roles and teams, and access entry
    When the contract test of a consuming service runs against the published document and its fakes
    Then the fakes answer an ALLOWED decision, a REFUSED decision with NO_RIGHT, a conflict refusal, a 503 and the permission answer of AC3
    Then a consumer that omits the area or the right declaration fails its own test with the operation named

These criteria are new and test only the contract deliverable. No legacy acceptance criterion is copied: legacy AC2, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8 and AC9 are carried by RWB-P4-E1022-APP, and legacy AC1 and legacy AC3 by RWB-ITG-E1022-ITG.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A capability area and a right are checked before the caller's handler runs, and a refused action changes nothing | permission.letters (DF-REF-043); REQ-ACA-010; CTL-09 |
| BR2 | Deny by default: an answer that cannot be given is a refusal, never an allow, and no failed answer is cached | Architecture v5 slides 10 and 29; REQ-ACA-002 |
| BR3 | The answer carries the matrix version and the conflict version the session resolved, and the session keeps them until it ends | Legacy BR7; Admin and access model, section 4.2 |
| BR4 | A role pair listed in the conflict table may not be held in one session, and the refusal names the pair | Legacy BR5; separation of duty version SOD-2026.11 |
| BR5 | A service identity is resolved and checked on the same contract as a person | Legacy BR6; REQ-ACA-010; NFR-051 |
| BR6 | Group names, roles, letters, scopes and conflicts are data rows with a version; none is a constant of the contract or of the code | Legacy BR8; Principle 1; DT02 |
| BR7 | The contract holds no session, no token and no password, and the identity boundary is ACE Common's through gateway-bff | ADR-010; Architecture v5 slide 35 |
| BR8 | The contract publishes no event and consumes none; the policy events belong to the stories that load a policy version | Architecture v5 slide 14; DP-14 |
| BR9 | The contract answers the authorise and permission questions only: the delegation limits and the masking policies are the operations of their own stories | Architecture v5 slide 14; ownership map |
| BR10 | The role-to-group mapping is maintained under RWB-P4-AD001-CON, and the mapping rows are role.entra_group data of this service | Ownership Map (role, P4); Template and Rules §R7 |
| BR11 | The service owns its tables and its schema; the contract names the tables of this service and reads no table of another service | DP-01, DP-02; Architecture v5 slide 29 |
| BR12 | A published version is never edited in place; a breaking change is a new major version with a migration note and a new pin | Architecture v5 slides 11 and 38 |

##### 9. State transitions

The contract fixes the states of a decision and the lifecycle of the contract version; it holds no case status and no stored object of its own.

| Object | From | Event | To | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Contract version | 1 | A backward-compatible change to a payload, an attribute or a fake | Version 1, minor change | The pinned consumers build unchanged |
| Contract version | 1 | A breaking change to an operation, an answer or the vocabulary | Version 2 with a migration note | A consumer moves only by changing the pin and passing its contract test |
| Access decision | UNCHECKED | The letters of the area hold the right the caller declares | ALLOWED | The caller's handler runs |
| Access decision | UNCHECKED | The letters do not hold the right, or the area holds no row | REFUSED | 403 with MSG-P4-002 and reason code NO_RIGHT |
| Access decision | UNCHECKED | The answer cannot be given | FAIL_CLOSED | 503 with no business data and nothing cached |
| Session resolution | UNRESOLVED | The claims carry a second factor, a mapped active role and no conflicting pair | RESOLVED | The role set, the scope and the two versions are answered |
| Session resolution | UNRESOLVED | No second factor, no mapped role, or a conflicting pair | REFUSED | MSG-P4-005, MSG-P4-001 or MSG-P4-006, and the reason code on the fact |

A REFUSED or FAIL_CLOSED decision is never cached by the contract's own means: the contract stores nothing, and a cache is the consumer's with its own time to live (DP-08, RWB-PLT-E1037-CON).

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The contract owner of rwb-access (any team, per U3) | Owns the document, the two operations, the vocabulary, the fakes and the versioning of the contract |
| The service template owner | Pins exactly one version of the contract in the template and moves the pin with the build as the gate |
| The consuming squads of the 19 services and gateway-bff | Compile and test against the published document and its fakes, and raise a change request instead of a local override |
| RW-SECADM Security administrator | Owns the role-to-group mapping rows and their maintenance contract RWB-P4-AD001-CON; receives the conflict incident |
| RW-REFADM Reference data administrator | Loads an approved role or matrix version; the contract reads it and never writes it |
| RW-CASEOWN, RW-PHONECOL, RW-LITOFF, RW-LEGAL, RW-SECADM and SY-RULES | Hold the roles whose answers the criteria exercise |
| No approval level of the delegation of authority applies | The contract publishes no delegation limit and takes no credit decision |

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-REF-034, DF-REF-035, DF-REF-036 | role (P4 rwb-access) | id, role_code, role_name | Named only: carried in the two answers |
| DF-REF-037, DF-REF-038 | role (P4 rwb-access) | role_class, default_scope | Named only: class and the source of the scope type |
| DF-REF-039 | role (P4 rwb-access) | entra_group | Named only: the mapping row the resolution reads; the maintenance contract is RWB-P4-AD001-CON |
| DF-REF-040 to DF-REF-044 | permission (P4 rwb-access) | id, role_id, capability_area, letters, matrix_version | Named only: the letters and the version the answers carry |
| DF-REF-205 to DF-REF-211 | role_conflict (P4 rwb-access) | id, role_code, conflicts_with, reason, conflict_version, valid_from, valid_to | Named only: the conflict version and the pairs the refusal names |
| DF-REF-016 to DF-REF-026, DF-REF-055 to DF-REF-062 | delegation_limit (P4 rwb-access) | the limit fields | **Not published here**: `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/doa-limits` belongs to the delegation-of-authority story of this service |
| Session claim (no field ID) | The verified claims of gateway-bff | the `groups` claim, the `amr` claim, the user reference | Named only: the input of the resolution, never stored by this service |
| No data of its own | The contract | None | The contract stores nothing, caches nothing and owns no schema |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary. Every row is named and none is written by the contract: the tables are created by RWB-P4-E1022-DB and written by the role and matrix stories of this service (DP-01). A contract that carried a value, a table or a token would break the identity boundary of ADR-010, so the shapes are published without one.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

| Method and path | Request | Answer | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise | The role codes of the resolved session, the scope type with the team and region codes, the capability area, the right, and the delegation band key of the action where the action needs one | The decision ALLOWED or REFUSED, the area and right asked, the matrix version, the conflict version and, on a refusal, the reason code and the message id | 400 malformed; 401 MSG-P4-001 or MSG-P4-005; 403 MSG-P4-002; 422 an assertion no area or right; 503 fail closed |
| GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/permissions | None | The role codes with their names and default scopes, the letters of each capability area, the scope type with the team and region codes, the matrix version, the conflict version and the resolution time | 401 MSG-P4-001 or MSG-P4-005; 503 fail closed |

Both paths are published under the base of §R4 and DP-13. Architecture v5 slide 14 names the operations `authorise` and `me/permissions` and the Ownership Map has no path row for them: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0776; ASM-1403). The request and answer fields are stated by this contract and stay open until the freeze: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0776; ASM-1404).

The contract does **not** publish `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/doa-limits`: that read belongs to the delegation-of-authority story of this service, RWB-P4-E1038-APP. It does not publish `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/masking-policies` either, which is the masking story's. The two legacy reads `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/roles` and `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` are the role-to-permission contract's, RWB-P4-E1037-CON, and are not republished here.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method and path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode} | P3 rwb-case | The values of `LOV-ROLE-CLASS`, `LOV-CAPABILITY` and `LOV-SCOPE` in force, through the reference-data contract behind RWB-PLT-E1043-CON (DP-07) |
| The roles-and-teams read of the rwb-case contract | P3 rwb-case | The team and region codes a TEAM or REGION scope names, through RWB-P3-E1019-CON |
| ACE Common sign-in, group-to-role (INT-21) | ACE Common, through gateway-bff | The verified claims the resolution reads; the service never calls Entra ID directly and holds no token |

Each call is one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream (DP-11, ADR-020). This contract story has no build dependency on them: it names them and the app story calls them.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. This service publishes no event on this contract. `AccessPolicyChanged` and `DoaLimitChanged` on `rwb.access.events.v1` are published by the stories that load a policy version, not by the sign-on contract.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The resolution holds no cache, so there is nothing for this contract to invalidate; the cache with its time to live and its refresh is the consumer's, published by RWB-PLT-E1037-CON.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The contract defines no workflow and no activity; the resolution and the check are synchronous request handling.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The six-monthly access review list (JOB-18) is a Schedule of this service and belongs to the access-review story.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None created here. The contract reads the tables of this service — `role`, `permission` and `role_conflict`, all P4 and all in `rwb_access` — which RWB-P4-E1022-DB creates and the role and matrix stories write. `delegation_limit` and `masking_rule` are P4's as well and are the other stories' operations. `lov_value` is P3's and is read through the reference-data contract (DP-07). No table of another service is named in a statement of this story.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| Session fake | The verified claims of gateway-bff behind RWB-PLT-N001-CON | A token with `amr` holding `mfa`, one with `pwd` only, a workload token for SY-RULES, a set with an unmapped group, and an expired session (AC1, AC3, AC4) |
| Role fixture | The `role`, `permission` and `role_conflict` rows of `PM-2026.11` and `SOD-2026.11` | RW-CASEOWN with scope OWN and `-` in Platform administration; RW-PHONECOL with `-`; RW-LITOFF CRU and RW-LEGAL CRUA in Documents; RW-SECADM with any business role (AC2, AC4) |
| Reference-data fake | `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | The values in force, an unreachable answer and a malformed answer (AC3) |
| Roles-and-teams fake | The rwb-case roles-and-teams read | The team and region codes of a TEAM or REGION scope (AC3) |
| Access-entry fake | The writer of RWB-P4-E1039-APP | A recorder of the user reference, the area, the right, the result and the reason code, and a switch that fails the write (AC4) |

The five fakes are published with the contract so that a consuming service needs no running rwb-access to build or test (AC6).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary (REST, Kafka, Temporal, File)

| Call type | Provided | Consumed | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 | 2 | The authorise and permission answers are provided; the rwb-case reference read and the team read are named as the app story's |
| Kafka | 0 | 0 | No event on this contract |
| Temporal | 0 | 0 | No workflow, activity or Schedule |
| File | 0 | 0 | No file is read or written |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** The OpenAPI 3.1 document and the generated client and server shapes for the two operations, published as one versioned contract artefact of the service, with the fakes and their fixtures as resources of the same artefact. The implementation is RWB-P4-E1022-APP's, in `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`; the published shapes sit in `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access.api`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables. The contract names `role`, `permission` and `role_conflict` as `rwb_access` tables and owns none of them | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`. The refusal and sign-in facts are recorded by the writer of RWB-P4-E1039-APP, which this contract names and does not build | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case. The classes, the areas and the scopes are named by the contract and read through it at run time | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library. This story is the contract of the authorise answer that the guard library calls | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout. The three in-process interfaces of the legacy story become two REST operations and one named fact writer | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1`. Both operations sit at `/api/recovery/access/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema. The contract adds no migration and states that the schema is RWB-P4-E1022-DB's | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route. The contract fixes the 401, 403 and 503 answers the route renders and the session line it shows | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |

The H and C dependencies named in the last column belong to RWB-P4-E1022-APP and to the consuming stories; this contract story has no build dependency of its own, which is why its H, C, I and X rows read None.

**Hardware and software change.** The `recovery.access.signin` package's published Java interfaces — `AccessCheck.check`, `SessionResolver.resolve` and `AccessEventPublisher.publish` — are replaced by two REST operations with a published document, a mock and a contract test in every consumer's build. The roles, the letters and the conflict pairs leave the monolith's single schema and stay in `rwb_access`; the reference values and the team codes are asked of rwb-case one hop away. The contract adds no schema, no topic, no queue, no Schedule and no bucket, so no new hardware is implied: the document is published to the artefact registry and the operations run in the service's existing pods on the existing AKS cluster.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| OpenAPI 3.1 document | Document | The two operations, their shapes, their errors and their examples (AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4) |
| Error vocabulary | Document | 401 with MSG-P4-001 or MSG-P4-005, 403 with MSG-P4-002, the conflict refusal with MSG-P4-006, 503 with no business data, and the refusal fact with its reason code (AC4) |
| Negative statements | Document | No event, no session, no token, no password, no delegation limit, no mapping maintenance, named with the story that owns each (AC5) |
| Fakes and fixtures | Test asset | The five fakes of section 12.8 and the synthetic rows they answer from (AC6) |
| Contract test | Test asset | The test a consuming service runs against the document and the fakes, including the drift test on the version pin (AC6) |

**Build steps**

1. Write the two operations in the OpenAPI document with their examples, and run the contract test of a sample consumer against the generated client (AC1).
2. Write the authorise answer and the permission answer with the version labels and the scope, and prove them against the role fixture (AC2, AC3).
3. Write the error vocabulary with the four message ids and the reason codes, and prove each refusal path with a consumer test (AC4).
4. Write the negative statements and check that the document has no session, token, password, event or delegation-limit surface (AC5).
5. Publish the five fakes and wire the contract and drift tests into the build of a consuming service; test the ALLOWED, REFUSED, conflict, 503 and permission answers (AC6).
6. Publish the document with the nine tables of section 12, record its version and its compatibility rule, and hand the pin to the service template.

**Done when.** The six criteria pass as contract tests, the five fakes are published with the document, the nine tables of section 12 name their owner from the Ownership Map, and RWB-P4-E1022-APP and the guard library of RWB-PLT-E1037-APP build and pass their tests against the published document.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | A session with no Workbench role | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-P4-002 | An action outside the role's permission | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-005 | Token without a second factor (new) | Sign in again with your second factor. The Workbench needs multi-factor authentication. |
| MSG-P4-006 | Conflicting role pair at sign-in (new) | Your roles {role} and {otherRole} cannot be held together. Access is refused and the security administrator has been told. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | ACE sign-in service unavailable | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |

The message ids and the wording are copied unchanged from RWB-E1-022, and the Thai text of each follows DL10; the contract adds no message of its own. The 503 fail-closed answer carries no message id and no business data: one RFC 9457 problem detail with the trace identifier and the operation.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen of its own. The contract fixes what a screen receives: 401 with MSG-P4-001 or MSG-P4-005 on the access request page, 403 with MSG-P4-002 where a menu entry is absent or an action refused, the conflict refusal with MSG-P4-006 naming the pair, and the role and scope line the edge renders at the top of every page. Those are gateway-bff composite screens under RWB-PLT-N001-CON; SCR-43 Roles and access and SCR-47 Personal data arrive in Epic 8 and are out of scope.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: roles, groups, letters, scopes, versions and message ids are data rows or message-catalogue entries, never constants of the document or of the code.
- No personal data in a payload, a fixture or a log; the two answers carry identifiers, codes and version labels only.
- No session, token, password or local account in the contract: the session is gateway-bff's in its Redis store, and the identity boundary is ADR-010's.
- No event on this contract: the policy events belong to their own stories, and the refusal fact goes through the decision-record library.
- Deny by default and fail closed, with no business data in the 503 answer.
- The contract names the tables of this service only; a consumer that reads a P4 table directly fails its boundary test.
- A published version is never edited in place; a breaking change is a new major version with a migration note and a new pin.
- No place name, no person name and no credential anywhere: the fixture is synthetic and the users are references.

##### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN) and the service identities the Workbench calls (SY-RULES)**, I want **my Entra ID sign-in and its second factor turned inside rwb-access into a resolved set of roles, scope and policy versions, every call checked against that set before the handler runs, and an unmapped, inactive or conflicting group refused at the door**, so that **access is controlled from the first release, every service reads one authority instead of a copy of the roles, and nobody holds a Workbench password or a local account**.

This is the application slice of legacy RWB-E1-022 for rwb-access, and it is the authority half of that key. The legacy story resolved the session, checked the right and wrote the sign-in fact in one process against one schema; D-RCV-60 keeps the behaviour and separates the ownership:

- **This story, rwb-access (P4), schema `rwb_access`:** the session resolver over the verified claims, the group-to-role mapping on the active `role` rows, the conflict check over `role_conflict`, the letter union over `permission`, the two answers the rest of the platform uses — `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` and `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/permissions` — and the refusal facts with their reason codes (DP-01, DP-08).
- **Not this story, the contract of the same key:** RWB-P4-E1022-CON publishes the two operations, their shapes, their error vocabulary and their fakes. This story implements them and adds no path.
- **Not this story, the schema of the same key:** RWB-P4-E1022-DB creates `role`, `permission` and `role_conflict` in `rwb_access`, the library objects and the login. This story reads `permission` and writes none of the three tables at run time.
- **Not this story, legacy AC1 and legacy AC3:** the SSO sign-in across the edge and the "no group at all" refusal are carried by **RWB-ITG-E1022-ITG**, which owns those two criteria and their end-to-end form. This story owns legacy AC2, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8 and AC9.
- **Not this story, the lead time:** there is no Workbench password, no local account, no session table and no token store in the service. Staff sign-in is ACE Common (Entra ID, MFA) at the shared gateway-bff, and the session lives in the Redis store of gateway-bff (RWB-PLT-N006-INF; ADR-010).
- **Service naming:** base `/api/recovery/access/v1` (DP-13), schema `rwb_access`, topic `rwb.access.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-access` in namespace `rwb-recovery` (not used here), Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`.
- **Events:** this story publishes no event and consumes none. A policy change is published by the story that loads a policy version, not by the resolver that reads it.

##### 2. Business rationale

Access to recovery data today is granted system by system, and the bank cannot show who could see a case on a given date. The legacy story made Entra ID group membership the only way to hold a Workbench role: one group per role per environment, granted through the bank IAM, read at each sign-in and turned into a session with roles, scope and the permission matrix version in force. That answer is still right, and the realignment makes it narrower and stronger by moving the resolution into the service that owns the roles.

There is one change of substance and it is the point of the split. In the monolith the resolver read `role`, `permission` and `role_conflict` in the same connection, kept a `SessionContext` object for the life of the process session, and every module called `AccessCheck` in the same JVM. In the 19-service target the roles are read by **every** service and by gateway-bff, each of which must authorise its own object (Architecture v5 slide 10), while the tables stay with one owner (DP-01). So the resolution becomes an answer of rwb-access over two published operations, and the session itself belongs to the shared edge: gateway-bff holds it in Redis, P4 holds no session table, and what travels is identifiers and version labels, never a token and never business data (ADR-010; slide 35). Three sentences of the architecture are what this story must make true: each service authorises the object itself with cached permission data from rwb-access and a 2 s timeout (slide 10); the access owner publishes `authorise` and `me/permissions` and writes `AccessPolicyChanged` when a policy version changes (slide 14); personal data stays in the owning service and never travels in an event, a workflow payload or a log (slides 11 and 35).

The negative side is fixed as tightly as the positive one. An unmapped or inactive group gives no role; a conflicting pair refuses the session; the matrix and conflict versions a session resolved stay with it until it ends; a service identity is checked exactly like a person; and no value the resolver needs — a letter, a scope, a group name, a conflict pair — is written in code (legacy BR1 to BR8, kept unchanged). It meets REQ-ACA-001, REQ-ACA-002 and REQ-ACA-010 and supports control CTL-09 (access by role and scope). The measure is unchanged from the legacy story, the access test set of section 16 passing for every role with real users at the release (DL39: administration roles at Epic 1), and additionally the guard of every consuming service passing its contract test against these two answers.

**The division is fixed and is the same in every story of this legacy key.** The seven criteria of this story — legacy AC2, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8 and AC9 — are carried here word for word with their origin tag; legacy AC1 (SSO sign-in end to end) and legacy AC3 (not in any group) are **not** this story's; they are carried by RWB-ITG-E1022-ITG, and this story copies no part of them as a scenario of its own.

Where the sources do not fix a value this story must build on, it carries the placeholder: the home of the resolved version labels now that P4 keeps no session table, the target of the incident that a conflicting pair raises, and the operation that returns a person's team and region codes for the scope line — Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0775; ASM-1398), (GAP-0775; ASM-1399) and (GAP-0775; ASM-1401).

- RWB-P4-E1022-DB has created `role` (DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-039), `permission` (DF-REF-040 to DF-REF-044) and `role_conflict` (DF-REF-205 to DF-REF-211) in `rwb_access`, with the partial index on `role.entra_group` where `is_active` (DP-15; tracked as the external dependency of the same key).

Those two legacy reads are that contract's and are not republished here; this story answers the two operations of its own contract only.

- RWB-PLT-E1043-CON is published and RWB-P3-E1043-CON is the contract behind it (H, C): `LOV-ROLE-CLASS`, `LOV-CAPABILITY` and `LOV-SCOPE` are read with the version in force through the reference-data contract (DP-07). `LOV-SCOPE` holds OWN, TEAM, REGION and ALL; `LOV-CAPABILITY` holds the 14 areas, including PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION.
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published (H): the gateway-bff route contract. gateway-bff is the only entry for staff, it holds the session in its Redis store, and it hands the verified claims to this service (DP-19; RWB-PLT-N006-INF).
- RWB-PLT-E1044-CON is published (H): the per-service Flyway sequence. This story writes no migration; the schema is RWB-P4-E1022-DB's.

- The role rows of the environment are loaded by the role story of this service, and each environment's row carries that environment's group name in `role.entra_group`, for example `RWB-SIT-RW-CASEOWN` in SIT (legacy precondition, names DL40). The mapping rows are `role.entra_group` data of this service; their maintenance contract is RWB-P4-AD001-CON.
- RWB-P3-E1019-CON is published (C): the roles, teams and queues contract of rwb-case, from which the team and region codes of a TEAM or REGION scope are read. This story builds against its fake from Day 1 (DP-11) and copies no team row into `rwb_access`.
- The ACE Common sign-in is configured for the Workbench application in Entra ID (INT-21), with the bank conditional access policy that requires a second factor. The verified claims reach this service from gateway-bff, never directly from the browser.
- The test users, groups, roles and matrix rows of this story are synthetic; no production entitlement, person or credential is read, written or logged.
- No approval is required to build against a Draft contract: the contract is Draft (realignment v1) and the shapes are frozen when the consuming services pass their contract tests.

##### 4. Flow

1. The person opens the Workbench in the ACE front end. gateway-bff redirects to Entra ID through ACE Common sign-in; the person signs in with password and second factor, and Entra ID returns an OpenID Connect token with the `groups` claim and the `amr` claim.
2. gateway-bff verifies the token, stores the session in its Redis store with the identifiers and the version labels it is given, and calls this service for the resolution. The token and the session never reach this service's database (ADR-010).
3. `SessionResolver` checks that the `amr` claim contains `mfa`. Without it the session is refused and nothing is resolved (legacy X3, AC4).
4. `SessionResolver` maps each value of the `groups` claim to an active `role` row on `role.entra_group`, through the partial index on the column. A group with no active row is ignored and its name is carried on the sign-in fact, as a group name only and never as a person's attribute (legacy X6, AC8; GAP-0775; ASM-1400).
5. `SessionResolver` reads `role_conflict` at the conflict version in force and refuses the session where the resolved set holds both halves of a pair. The refusal names the pair and raises the incident (legacy X4, AC6).
6. `SessionResolver` resolves the session: the user reference, the role codes with their names and default scopes, the matrix version in force, the conflict version in force, the scope type and the team and region codes read through the rwb-case contract. The version labels are what the session keeps until it ends (legacy X7, AC9; ASM-1398).
7. The resolved identifiers and version labels are handed back to gateway-bff for its session record; this service writes no session row and no token anywhere.
8. gateway-bff renders the first screen with one line naming the roles and the scope, for example "Case owner. Scope: own cases.", and a menu holding only the screens whose capability area has R for at least one role. That rendering is the edge's and its contract is RWB-PLT-N001-CON; this story supplies the answer it renders.
9. The person, or another service on the person's behalf, calls an endpoint. The guard of that service calls `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` with the role set, the scope, the capability area and the right the endpoint declares, one hop, 2 s timeout, breaker per downstream.
10. `AccessCheckService` unions the letters of the session's roles in that area and answers ALLOWED or REFUSED. A refusal is 403 with MSG-P4-002 and the refusal fact carries the user reference, the area, the right and the result; the handler of the caller never runs.
11. A service identity is resolved and checked exactly like a person: its group maps to its non-human role row and its call is refused on the same rule as a human call (legacy X5, AC7).
12. A caller reads its own set on `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/permissions`: the roles, the letters per area, the scope, the matrix version and the conflict version it is being checked against.
13. Every sign-in and every refusal is passed to the access-entry writer of RWB-P4-E1039-APP with its reason code — NO_ROLE, NO_MFA, ROLE_CONFLICT or NO_RIGHT — and that writer records it locally and publishes it to `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03; ASM-1402).
14. The reference-data contract of rwb-case is unreachable, times out or answers malformed: the resolution fails closed with 503, nothing is cached, and no letter is assumed. The call is counted as a fail-closed resolution.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A role without the right calls an endpoint, for example the admin API | Refused with 403 before the handler runs; the refusal fact carries the area and the right | MSG-P4-002 | AC2 |
| X2 | The person is in no Workbench group | Session refused with 401; the access request page shows the message and no data. Carried by RWB-ITG-E1022-ITG, not by this story | MSG-P4-001 | legacy AC3 (RWB-ITG-E1022-ITG) |
| X3 | The token has no second factor in the `amr` claim | Session refused with 401; the refusal is recorded with reason NO_MFA | MSG-P4-005 | AC4 |
| X4 | The groups give a role pair listed in the conflict table version in force | Session refused with MSG-P4-006 naming the pair; the incident is raised; the refusal is recorded with reason ROLE_CONFLICT | MSG-P4-006 | AC6 |
| X5 | A service identity calls an area its role does not hold | Refused with 403, exactly as for a person, with the identity reference on the refusal fact | MSG-P4-002 | AC7 |
| X6 | A group maps to no active role row, or to an inactive one | The group is ignored and its name is written on the sign-in fact; if no group maps, the no-role path applies | None on the ignored group | AC8 |
| X7 | A new matrix version takes effect while a session is open | The open session keeps the version it resolved; the next session resolves the new one | None | AC9 |
| X8 | The verified claims arrive after the session has ended, or with no session reference | Refused with 401 and no resolution; the service resolves nothing for a session the edge does not hold | MSG-P4-001 | AC2 |
| X9 | The reference-data contract of rwb-case is unreachable, times out or answers malformed | The resolution fails closed with 503; no letter and no scope is assumed, nothing is cached, and the failure carries no business data | None | AC9 |
| X10 | The `permission` rows of the matrix version in force hold no row for an area | The area answers with no letter for every role, so every action in it is refused | MSG-P4-002 | AC2 |

No exception path of this story changes a case, a task or a queue: this service answers roles, scope and rights, and the case state machine is rwb-case's. X2 remains the property of RWB-ITG-E1022-ITG and appears here only so that the table of the legacy story is not silently narrowed.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against its own contract, the guard library contract, the reference-data fake and the rwb-case team contract fake; no other service has to be finished first |
| Negotiable | The role roster, the group names, the letters, the conflict pairs and the versions are data rows; the story fixes the resolution, the two answers and the refusal rules only |
| Valuable | Every service and the edge get one authority for who may do what, and a person with an unmapped, inactive or conflicting group is stopped at the door |
| Estimable | One resolver, one check service, two answers, one conflict check, one refusal path and the fixtures |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests, with the schema and the contract built by the sibling stories of the same key |
| Testable | Every criterion in section 7 is one automated test over synthetic role rows, a session fake and a reference-data fake |

    Given the role conflict table says RW-SECADM may not hold any business role
    When the user signs in
    Then the system refuses the session with message MSG-P4-006 naming "RW-SECADM" and "RW-CASEOWN"
    Then the system raises an incident to the security administrator queue
    Then the system writes one refusal event with reason "ROLE_CONFLICT"

  Scenario: AC7 A service identity is checked like a person (legacy RWB-E1-022 AC7)
    Given the gateway-bff session contract mock returns the verified workload claims of managed identity "SY-RULES" in group "RWB-SIT-SY-RULES"
    When it calls GET /admin/roles
    Then the system refuses the call with status 403 and message MSG-P4-002
    Then the system writes one refusal event with user "SY-RULES"

  Scenario: AC8 An unmapped or inactive group gives no role (legacy RWB-E1-022 AC8)
    Given the gateway-bff session contract mock returns the verified claims of test user "U-1008" in groups "RWB-SIT-RW-CASEOWN" and "RWB-SIT-LEGACY01"
    Given no active role row has entra_group "RWB-SIT-LEGACY01"
    When the user signs in
    Then the session holds only "RW-CASEOWN"
    Then the system writes the unmapped group name on the sign-in event

  Scenario: AC9 An open session keeps the versions it resolved (legacy RWB-E1-022 AC9)
    Given test user "U-1009" signed in at 09:00 on 1 December 2026 under matrix version "PM-2026.11"
    Given matrix version "PM-2026.12" takes effect at 10:00 on 1 December 2026 and removes R in Reporting from RW-CASEOWN
    When the user calls GET /reports/measures at 10:30 in the same session
    Then the system checks the call against "PM-2026.11" and allowed
    Then after the user signs in again at 11:00 the same call is refused with MSG-P4-002
```

These seven criteria are the legacy criteria of RWB-E1-022 unchanged, each tagged with its origin. The first Given of each is the boundary a service test has to fake — the verified claims that gateway-bff hands over, or the reference values that rwb-case supplies — and every value the legacy line carries is kept. Legacy AC1 and legacy AC3 are not scenarios of this story: they are carried by RWB-ITG-E1022-ITG.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Membership of the Entra ID group mapped to a role is the only way to hold the role. The Workbench holds no password and no local account | role.entra_group (DF-REF-039); DT07; Admin and access model, section 4.2 |
| BR2 | A session is refused unless the token carries a second factor | NFR-049; FEAT-ACA-02 |
| BR3 | No role inherits from another. A person with two roles holds the union of both roles' letters | permission.letters (DF-REF-043) |
| BR4 | A capability area with no letter for any of the session's roles refuses every action in that area | Permission matrix; CTL-09 |
| BR5 | A role pair listed in the role conflict table may not be held in one session | Separation of duty sheet, roles.txt; role conflict table (new) |
| BR6 | A service identity holds a role in the same table and is checked the same way as a person | REQ-ACA-010; NFR-051 |
| BR7 | A session keeps the matrix and conflict versions it resolved at sign-in until it ends | Admin and access model, section 4.2 |
| BR8 | Group names, roles, letters and conflicts are data rows with a version; none is written in code | Principle 1; DT02 |
| BR9 | The answer is one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream, and a reference contract that cannot be reached refuses the resolution instead of assuming a value | Architecture v5 slides 10 and 11; DP-11 |
| BR10 | An unmapped or inactive group gives no role, and the group name is written on the sign-in fact as a name only, never as a person's attribute | Legacy X6 and BR1; Architecture v5 slide 35 |
| BR11 | The service holds no session, no token and no local account, and a fact it records carries an identifier, an area, a right and a reason code, never a name, a contact value or a credential | ADR-010; Architecture v5 slides 11 and 35 |
| BR12 | The role rows, the letters and the conflict pairs are read in `rwb_access`; the reference values are read through the rwb-case contract and the team codes through the roles-and-teams contract, and nothing is copied | DP-01, DP-07; ownership map |

##### 9. State transitions

No case status changes in this story. It resolves a session with the states RESOLVED and REFUSED, and it records the refusal reason as a value of the fact:

| Object | From | Event | To | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Session resolution | UNRESOLVED | The `amr` claim holds `mfa`, at least one group maps to an active role row and no conflicting pair is held | RESOLVED | The role set, the scope and the matrix and conflict versions are answered and kept for the session |
| Session resolution | UNRESOLVED | The `amr` claim holds no `mfa` | REFUSED (NO_MFA) | 401 with MSG-P4-005; no role is resolved |
| Session resolution | UNRESOLVED | No group maps to an active role row | REFUSED (NO_ROLE) | 401 with MSG-P4-001; carried by RWB-ITG-E1022-ITG |
| Session resolution | UNRESOLVED | The resolved set holds both halves of a conflicting pair | REFUSED (ROLE_CONFLICT) | MSG-P4-006 naming the pair, the incident raised, no role answered |
| Access decision | UNCHECKED | The letter of the area holds the right the endpoint declares | ALLOWED | The caller's handler runs |
| Access decision | UNCHECKED | The letter of the area does not hold the right, or the area has no row | REFUSED (NO_RIGHT) | 403 with MSG-P4-002; the caller's handler does not run |
| Access decision | UNCHECKED | The reference contract cannot be reached, times out or answers malformed | FAIL_CLOSED | 503; nothing is assumed and nothing is cached |
| Resolved version | PM-2026.11 | A new matrix version takes effect while the session is open | PM-2026.11 until the session ends | The open session keeps its labels; the next resolution reads PM-2026.12 |

A REFUSED resolution is final for that token: a second attempt needs a new sign-in, and the resolver holds nothing of the first attempt.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Line manager (bank IAM, level 4) | Requests a Workbench role for a team member in the bank IAM, naming the person, the role and the reason. May not approve the request they raised |
| Role owner (bank IAM, level 2), the head of the unit whose staff hold the role | Approves or rejects each grant of a role they own after checking the separation of duty table |
| Access administrator (bank IAM, level 3), Chief Debt Recovery Management Office (assumed, DL01) | Adds the person to the Entra ID group of the approved role in each environment requested. Approves no grant |
| Application owner (level 1), Tribe Lead of the Collections and Recovery Tribe (assumed, DL02) | Approves the roles table and each group to role mapping |
| RW-SECADM Security administrator | Maintains the Entra ID groups and the IAM link (DL40); owns the role-to-group mapping rows and their maintenance contract RWB-P4-AD001-CON; receives the conflict incident in AC6 |
| RW-REFADM Reference data administrator | Loads an approved role or group mapping version. Approves none |
| RW-CASEOWN and every bank role | Signs in and uses the screens of the role |
| RW-PHONECOL Phone collector | Signs in; refused on Platform administration (AC2) |
| SY-RULES and the other service identities | Act under their managed identity and their own role row, checked exactly as a person |
| RW-COE, RW-DATASTEW, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-PLATADM, RW-SECADM | Read the role catalogue on the contract of RWB-P4-E1037-CON (Platform administration R) |
| The ACE DB team and the platform edge team | Own the schema, the login and the session store; this story writes none of them |

The four administration levels act in the bank IAM, not in the Workbench. If the bank chooses central administration (DL01), level 3 moves to the central IAM team and nothing in this build changes.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

| Method and path | Published by | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|
| POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise | RWB-P4-E1022-CON | The guard of a consuming service and the edge ask whether a session may take the action, in the area and with the right the endpoint declares |
| GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/permissions | RWB-P4-E1022-CON | A caller reads the roles, the letters per capability area, the scope and the matrix and conflict versions its own session is checked against |

The two paths sit at the base of §R4 and DP-13, because Architecture v5 slide 14 names the operations and the Ownership Map has no path row for either; the derivation of the base is the contract's, and its open point is stated in RWB-P4-E1022-CON section 12.1. The legacy reads `GET /admin/roles` and `GET /me/session` are not republished here: the catalogue and the session line belong to the role-to-permission contract RWB-P4-E1037-CON, and AC2 and AC7 exercise the refusal before the handler rather than the catalogue itself.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method and path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode} | P3 rwb-case | The values of `LOV-ROLE-CLASS`, `LOV-CAPABILITY` and `LOV-SCOPE` in force, read through the reference-data contract behind RWB-PLT-E1043-CON (DP-07; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON) |
| The roles-and-teams read of the rwb-case contract | P3 rwb-case | The team and region codes of a TEAM or REGION scope, read through RWB-P3-E1019-CON and its fake (DP-11; C RWB-P3-E1019-CON) |
| ACE Common sign-in, group-to-role (INT-21) | ACE Common, through gateway-bff | The verified claims and the group-to-role read of the sign-in; the service never calls Entra ID directly and holds no token |

Every call is one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream (DP-11; ADR-020). The team and region read is the one operation the sources do not name: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0775; ASM-1401).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. This story publishes no event and owns no topic. The policy events `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` and `rwb.access.DoALimitChanged.v1` on `rwb.access.events.v1` are published by the stories that load a policy version, not by the resolver.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The resolver holds no cache of a policy version, so there is nothing to invalidate: every answer is read at the version in force at the moment of the call.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The resolution, the check and the two answers are synchronous request handling in this service; no workflow, activity or task queue is used, and the task queue `rwb-access` is not started by this story.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The six-monthly access review list (JOB-18) is a Schedule of this service and belongs to the access-review story, not to the resolver.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner (ownership map) | This story |
|---|---|---|
| role | P4 | Read only. Created by RWB-P4-E1022-DB, written by the role story RWB-P4-E1019-APP |
| permission | P4 | Read only. Created by RWB-P4-E1022-DB, written by RWB-P4-E1037-APP |
| role_conflict | P4 | Read only. Created by RWB-P4-E1022-DB, written by the role story RWB-P4-E1019-APP |
| lov_value | P3 | Not read by SQL: the values are read through the reference-data contract of rwb-case (DP-07) |
| queue, queue_member | P3 | Not read: the team and region codes come through the rwb-case contract, never from its tables (DP-01) |

No table of another service is named in a statement of this story, and the boundary test of the service fails on a cross-schema reference.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access` for the implementation, with the published shapes of the two operations in `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access.api`. The front end is not part of this service: the shell, the session line and the menu filter are gateway-bff's composite route (DP-19; RWB-PLT-N001-CON).

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables. `role`, `permission` and `role_conflict` are `rwb_access` tables and this story reads them in its own schema | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`. The sign-in and refusal facts are recorded locally by the access-entry writer of RWB-P4-E1039-APP; the dependency is carried here | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case. The role classes, the capability areas and the scope codes are read with the version in force and copied nowhere | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library. This story is the authorise answer that the guard library calls, and the two are tested against each other's fakes | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout. The rwb-case reference read and the team read each get their own breaker | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1`. The two operations are published at `/api/recovery/access/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema. This story writes no migration; the schema is RWB-P4-E1022-DB's on that sequence | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route. The one-line roles and scope banner, the menu filter and the access request page are the edge's, not this service's | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Hardware and software change.** The monolith's `SessionResolver`, `AccessCheckService`, `AccessCheckInterceptor` and `AccessEventPublisher` inside `recovery.access.signin` become one service that answers two published operations, and the `SessionContext` object of the monolith becomes an answer plus the version labels the shared edge keeps in its Redis session record. The roles, the letters and the conflict pairs leave the monolith's single schema and stay in `rwb_access`; the reference values and the team codes are asked of rwb-case one hop away and are copied nowhere. No new hardware is implied: the service runs on the existing AKS cluster, the Redis session store is part of gateway-bff (RWB-PLT-N006-INF), and the resolver adds no database, no topic, no Schedule and no bucket.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `AccessDecisionController` | Controller | Serves the two operations of section 12.1 and maps a refusal to an RFC 9457 problem detail with its message id (BR9) |
| `SessionResolver` | Service | Checks the `amr` claim, maps groups to active role rows on `role.entra_group`, applies the conflict check and resolves the role set, the scope and the version labels (BR1, BR2, BR5, BR7) |
| `AccessCheckService` | Service | Unions the letters of the session's roles in the area and answers ALLOWED or REFUSED with the area and the right (BR3, BR4) |
| `AccessCheckInterceptor` | Service | Reads the `x-capability` area and right declared on each endpoint of this service and refuses before the handler runs; an endpoint with no declaration fails the build (BR4, BR9) |
| `PolicyVersionSnapshot` | Value type | The role set, the scope type, the team and region codes, the matrix version and the conflict version of one resolution; what the edge keeps and what the answer carries (BR7) |
| `RoleConflict` | Entity | Maps `role_conflict` and answers whether two role codes of the resolved set form a pair at the version in force (BR5) |
| `AccessRepository` | Repository | Reads `role` on the partial index of `entra_group` where active, `permission` and `role_conflict` in `rwb_access`; writes nothing (BR12) |
| `AccessEntryClient` | Service | Passes the sign-in and refusal facts with their reason code to the writer of RWB-P4-E1039-APP (BR11) |
| `FailClosedPolicy` | Component | The 2 s timeout, the breaker and the 503 mapping of the reference read, with no assumed letter and nothing cached (BR9) |

**Configuration.** `rwb.access.required-amr=mfa` (legacy) and the timeout and breaker settings, read through the parameters client (DP-06 is not in this story's pattern set, so the two values are configuration of the service template). Group names, roles, letters, scopes and conflicts are never constants: they are rows. The scope line wording follows the labels of DL10.

**Build steps**

1. Implement `SessionResolver` over the session fake: the `amr` check and the group mapping on active rows through the partial index; test AC4 and AC8, including the inactive row and the group name on the sign-in fact.
2. Implement the conflict check over `role_conflict` at the version in force and the refusal with the pair named; test AC6, with a pair that is not a conflict at the version in force allowed.
3. Implement the letter union and `AccessCheckService`; test AC5 with CRU and CRUA in Documents and the dash in Platform administration, and test BR4 for an area with no row.
4. Implement the resolution snapshot: the role set, the scope, the team and region codes from the roles-and-teams fake, the matrix and conflict versions; test AC9 with `PM-2026.11` and `PM-2026.12` one hour apart.
5. Implement the two answers of section 12.1 against the shapes of RWB-P4-E1022-CON, and the contract test that compares them with the published document.
6. Implement `AccessCheckInterceptor` and the declared area and right; the contract test that every operation of this service declares one, and the refusal of AC2 and AC7 before the handler.
7. Implement `AccessEntryClient` over the fake of RWB-P4-E1039-APP and the reason codes NO_ROLE, NO_MFA, ROLE_CONFLICT and NO_RIGHT; test one refusal of each kind (AC2, AC4, AC6, AC7).
8. Wire the fail-closed path of the reference read and the team read: unreachable, timeout at 2 s and malformed each answer 503 with nothing cached and no business data in the body (BR9).
9. Prove that no statement of the package names a table of another schema, no log line carries a claim value, and no session, token or password column exists in `rwb_access` (BR11, BR12).

**Feature flag.** `rwb.access.sso-roles` (legacy). Off, the resolver refuses every resolution with 503 rather than answering from a stale set, so a switch-off never opens an unchecked path.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, a test user per Epic 1 administration role resolves with MFA in SIT, the contract test finds no endpoint of this service without a declared area and right, and the guard library of RWB-PLT-E1037-APP passes its contract test against the two answers.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | Sign-in with no Workbench role | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-P4-002 | An action outside the role's permission | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-005 | Token without a second factor (new) | Sign in again with your second factor. The Workbench needs multi-factor authentication. |
| MSG-P4-006 | Conflicting role pair at sign-in (new) | Your roles {role} and {otherRole} cannot be held together. Access is refused and the security administrator has been told. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | ACE sign-in service unavailable | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |

The message ids and the wording are copied unchanged from RWB-E1-022, and the Thai text of each follows DL10; the proposed Thai for the two new messages is in the additions file of the legacy story. MSG-P4-001 appears here because the no-role path is a reason code of this service even though its end-to-end criterion is RWB-ITG-E1022-ITG's. The 503 fail-closed answer carries no message id and no business data: one RFC 9457 problem detail with the trace identifier and the operation.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen of this story. What a person sees is the edge's rendering of the answers: the one-line roles and scope at the top of every page, the menu with only the entries whose capability area the session can read, and the access request page with MSG-P4-001 and no data. Those are gateway-bff composite screens under RWB-PLT-N001-CON, and the legacy `SessionBanner` and `AccessRequestPage` components are not built in this service. Epic 1 has no business screens (DL39); RW-CASEOWN test users exist in SIT and UAT only, and the full administration screens SCR-43 and SCR-47 arrive in Epic 8.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: group names, roles, letters, scopes and conflicts are read from tables with their version.
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts: a sign-in or refusal fact carries the Entra ID object reference, never the person's name or e-mail, and a claim value is never logged.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or a `v_ace_*` view read by the data owner; this service reads no ACE view and no table in `public`.
- No read of another service's tables: the reference values and the team codes arrive over the rwb-case contract, one hop, never by SQL (DP-01).
- No local password, local account, session table, token or role cache that outlives the session (ADR-010).
- Every endpoint of this service declares its capability area and right; an endpoint without one fails the contract test.
- Deny by default and fail closed: an unreachable or malformed reference read refuses the resolution and assumes no letter.
- No place name, no person name and no credential in a fixture or a runbook; every role, group and user of the tests is synthetic.

##### 1. Story

As an **ACE database engineer**, I want **the role, permission and conflict tables of this key created on the per-service Flyway sequence in schema `rwb_access`, with the library objects the event platform needs in that schema, the login and grants of the service, a tested rollback, and an explicit statement that the schema holds no session, no password, no token and no local account**, so that **the sign-on story has a schema that is correct, granted, reversible and confined to the service's own schema, and nobody looks for a Workbench credential that does not exist**.

This is the database story of legacy RWB-E1-022. It delivers, in schema `rwb_access`:

- the migration that creates `role`, `permission` and `role_conflict` after the V0001 baseline, on the per-service sequence (DP-15);
- the keys and indexes this key's sign-in needs: the primary keys, the unique role code, the partial index on `role.entra_group` where `is_active` that the resolution reads on every sign-in, the unique key on `permission` per role, area and matrix version, and the unique key on the conflict pair per conflict version;
- the three library objects `outbox_event`, `processed_event` and `idempotency_key` created in this schema from the template of the event platform, because every service writes its own outbox and inbox in its own schema (DP-09's library, applied per service);
- the grant script for the rwb-access login (DP-02), whose name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0777; ASM-1405);
- the rollback: the undo of each migration, in reverse order, with the role and matrix rows preserved where a later migration only added a column;
- the explicit statement, in the migration and in the tests, that the schema holds **no session table, no password column, no token column and no local account row**: staff sign-in is ACE Common through gateway-bff, with the session in the gateway's Redis store (RWB-PLT-N006-INF; ADR-010);
- the statement that the ACE group facts behind a mapping row are read through the P1 contract or `RWB-P1-E1069-APP`, never from a table or view of the ACE schema and never from `public.*`.

`role` is written by the role story of this service, `permission` by the permission-matrix story, and this key's sign-in reads all three. This story creates the objects and the grants and writes no business row at run time.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story added one migration, `V_E1_022__role_conflict.sql`, to a single recovery schema of 92 tables with one shared login, and it relied on `role` and `permission` having been created by RWB-E1-001. After the split every service owns its schema, its migrations and its login, so the three tables that decide who may see a case cannot be changed by another service's release, and no other service can read them: the roles are read over the published contract of this key, one hop away (DP-01, DP-08; Architecture v5 slides 10 and 29).

Three details make the schema a design statement and not only plumbing. The partial index on `role.entra_group` where the row is active is what makes the resolution a lookup on a small index at every sign-in, and it is the legacy index kept exactly. The absence of a session table, a password column and a token column is not an omission: the target has no Workbench credential at all, the identity is ACE Common's and the session is gateway-bff's, so a schema that grew one would be the one place where the architecture could quietly be undone (ADR-010; Architecture v5 slide 35). And the three library objects must exist in this schema before the service can publish any event or consume one idempotently, which is why the event platform's template is applied here and not left to a story that owns no schema.

Where no source fixes a value this story depends on, it carries the placeholder: the name of the rwb-access login, the source of the ACE group facts behind a mapping row, and the column set of the three library objects — Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0777; ASM-1405), (GAP-0777; ASM-1406) and (GAP-0777; ASM-1407).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The V0001 baseline of `rwb_access` exists on the per-service Flyway sequence, from RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and RWB-PLT-NF06-DB: the schema, the `flyway_schema_history` table and the standard record columns of TSD P4 v3 T3.0 (`is_active`, `state`, `version`, `created_at`, `created_by`, `updated_at`, `updated_by`).
- The ACE database and the per-service login policy are in place; the login of rwb-access is created by the platform DB work and its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0777; ASM-1405).
- The ownership map is the only source of table ownership: `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule`, `role_conflict` and `delegation_limit` are P4 and in `rwb_access`; `lov_value`, `reference_row` and `reference_version` are P3 and in `rwb_case`; the ACE views are P1's. This story creates no object of another service.
- The field identifiers are fixed by TSD P4 v3 T3.1: DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-039 for `role`, DF-REF-040 to DF-REF-044 for `permission`, DF-REF-205 to DF-REF-211 for `role_conflict`.
- The legacy physical statements are the source of the objects: the `role` columns with `entra_group varchar(120)` and the partial index `ix_role_entra_group` on `(entra_group)` where `is_active`; the `permission` columns with `letters varchar(5)` and `matrix_version`; and `role_conflict` with `id uuid, role_code varchar(20), conflicts_with varchar(30), reason varchar(200), conflict_version varchar(20), valid_from date, valid_to date` plus the standard columns.
- The three library objects follow the template of the event platform (RWB-PLT-TE006-CON). Their column set is not restated here and is not fixed by any source of this read set (GAP-0777; ASM-1407).
- The ACE group facts behind a mapping row — `v_ace_iam_group.entra_group` in FSD P4 v3 — are read through the P1 contract or `RWB-P1-E1069-APP`. No object of this schema reads an ACE schema, the `recovery` schema or `public`.
- No approval is required to run a Draft migration on a development database; the migration is released to SIT only after the tests in section 16 pass.

##### 4. Flow

1. The ACE database engineer checks out the rwb-access migration folder and confirms the highest applied version on the sequence (the V0001 baseline).
2. The engineer adds the migration for this story after that version, with a repeatable check that the objects it creates do not already exist in the sequence.
3. The engineer creates `role`, `permission` and `role_conflict` with their columns from DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-039, DF-REF-040 to DF-REF-044 and DF-REF-205 to DF-REF-211, plus the standard record columns.
4. The engineer adds the keys and indexes: the primary key on each table, the unique role code, the partial index on `entra_group` where `is_active`, the unique key on `permission` per role, area and matrix version, and the unique key on the conflict pair per conflict version.
5. The engineer applies the event platform's template for `outbox_event`, `processed_event` and `idempotency_key` in `rwb_access`, unchanged: this schema is the producer's and the consumer's own, so the outbox and the inbox live here (DP-09's library, per service).
6. The engineer writes the grant script for the rwb-access login, scoped to schema `rwb_access` and to the six tables of this key, plus the sequence usage the tables need.
7. The engineer writes the rollback: the undo per migration, in reverse order, with data preservation for `role` and `permission` where a later change only adds a column.
8. The pipeline applies the baseline and this story's migrations to an empty schema, then to a copy of the SIT schema, and runs the schema checks: keys, indexes, grants, and a scan for any foreign key, synonym, view or grant that names another schema or `public`.
9. The check that no session, password, token or local-account column exists is a catalogue query over the schema: any hit fails the build (ADR-010).
10. The rollback is exercised on a copy: the schema returns to its pre-migration shape, and the role and matrix rows that were loaded between the two runs keep their identifiers.
11. The migration is recorded in the release notes of the sequence, with its version number and its checksum.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message |
|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A migration runs before the V0001 baseline | Flyway refuses with an unresolved baseline and nothing is applied | Pipeline error, no message id |
| X2 | `role`, `permission` or `role_conflict` already exists in the sequence | The repeatable check refuses to re-create it; the migration is marked as already applied | Pipeline error, no message id |
| X3 | A foreign key, view, synonym or grant names another schema or `public` | The catalogue check fails the build; the object is removed and the value is read over a contract instead | Check finding, no message id |
| X4 | The grant script runs before the login exists | The script fails on the missing role; the platform DB story creates the login first | Database error, no message id |
| X5 | The grant script grants to a shared or legacy login | The review rejects the script: one login per service (DP-02) | Review finding, no message id |
| X6 | A session, password, token or local-account column appears in the schema | The catalogue check fails the build and the column is removed: the identity and the session are not this schema's (ADR-010) | Check finding, no message id |
| X7 | The rollback would drop `role` and lose the role identifiers the matrix rows point at | The rollback drops only what the migration added and keeps the table and its rows | Review finding, no message id |
| X8 | A column is needed but no field identifier exists | The column is not invented: it carries the placeholder and the gap is raised | GAP-0777 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Three migrations, one grant script and a rollback, on the service's own sequence; nothing to build against |
| Negotiable | Constraint and index names follow the platform naming library; the column set is fixed by the field identifiers and the legacy statements |
| Valuable | The sign-on story, the role story and the matrix story have a schema that is granted, indexed, reversible and free of any credential |
| Estimable | Six tables, five indexes and keys, one grant script, one rollback |
| Small | Days, not weeks, with the schema checks |
| Testable | Every criterion is a catalogue query or a pipeline run in section 16 |

    Given the migration for permission

    Then a unique key exists on role_id, capability_area and matrix_version
    Then letters is varchar(5) and matrix_version is varchar(20) and both are NOT NULL

  Scenario: AC4 role_conflict is created with its columns and its version key (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the migration for role_conflict, the legacy V_E1_022__role_conflict.sql of RWB-E1-022
    When it is applied
    Then role_conflict has id, role_code, conflicts_with, reason, conflict_version, valid_from and valid_to of DF-REF-205 to DF-REF-211 plus the standard record columns
    Then the primary key is on id and a unique key exists on role_code, conflicts_with and conflict_version
    Then conflicts_with is varchar(30), because it holds a role code or the class value ANY_BUSINESS_ROLE or ANY_OTHER_ROLE, and no check constraint carries those values
    Then valid_from is NOT NULL and valid_to is nullable

  Scenario: AC5 The three library objects exist in rwb_access from the event platform template (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the event platform template published by RWB-PLT-TE006-CON
    When this story's migration for the library objects is applied
    Then outbox_event, processed_event and idempotency_key exist in schema rwb_access
    Then each object is created from the template unchanged, with no column renamed, added or dropped in this story
    Then the three objects carry their own keys and no foreign key into role, permission or role_conflict
    Then no other schema holds this service's outbox or inbox row

  Scenario: AC6 The schema holds no session, password, token or local account, and no object names another schema (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the applied schema
    When the catalogue query for columns, foreign keys, views, synonyms and grants runs
    Then no table, column or row holds a session, a password, a token or a local account, because staff sign-in is ACE Common through gateway-bff and the session lives in the gateway's Redis store (RWB-PLT-N006-INF; ADR-010)
    Then no foreign key, view, synonym or grant in rwb_access names rwb_case, the recovery schema, an ACE schema or public
    Then the ACE group facts behind a mapping row are read through the P1 contract or RWB-P1-E1069-APP and never by SQL from this schema
    Then the only grantee of the six tables is the rwb-access login

  Scenario: AC7 The grants and the rollback are complete and safe (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the grant script and the rollback of this story
    When the grant script runs and then the rollback runs on a copy
    Then the rwb-access login has usage on the schema and select, insert, update and delete on role, permission, role_conflict, outbox_event, processed_event and idempotency_key
    Then no other login holds a grant on those tables, and no grant on rwb_case or on an ACE schema is present
    Then the rollback drops the library objects, then role_conflict, then permission, then role, in reverse order
    Then a role row loaded between the two runs keeps its id and role_code where the rollback only reverses an added object
```

These criteria are new and test the database artefacts only: no legacy acceptance criterion is repeated, and every physical value — table, column, field identifier, index definition and the legacy migration name — is the legacy or technical-specification value, character for character.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Membership of the Entra ID group mapped to a role is the only way to hold the role, so the mapping is a column of `role` and its lookup is indexed | role.entra_group (DF-REF-039); Legacy BR1; DT07 |
| BR2 | One role has one letter set per capability area at a matrix version, and no role inherits from another | permission.letters (DF-REF-043); DF-REF-044; Legacy BR3 |
| BR3 | A role pair listed as a conflict may not be held in one session, and the pair is versioned by the conflict version and its valid from date | role_conflict (DF-REF-205 to DF-REF-211); Legacy BR5 |
| BR4 | Group names, roles, letters, conflicts and versions are rows; no database check constraint carries a business value | Legacy BR8; Principle 1; DT02 |
| BR5 | Each service's objects live in its own schema under its own login; one login per service | DP-01, DP-02, DP-15; Architecture v5 slide 29 |
| BR6 | The schema holds no session, no password, no token and no local account; the identity is ACE Common's and the session is the gateway's | ADR-010; Architecture v5 slide 35 |
| BR7 | Every service writes its own outbox and inbox in its own schema, so the three library objects are created here | Ownership Map ruling on outbox_event, processed_event and idempotency_key; Architecture v5 slides 11 and 20 |
| BR8 | The ACE group facts are read through the owner's contract and never by SQL from this schema, and no object names `public` | DP-01; DP-05's boundary rule; FSD P4 v3 A2.1 |
| BR9 | A role, a permission row and a conflict pair keep their identifiers across a rollback, so a later migration never rewrites a key | Legacy BR3; version applies whole or not at all |

##### 9. State transitions

None in the runtime sense: a table has no state machine. The states this story moves through are the migration states of the service's Flyway history — pending, applied, failed, undone — and the row-level states the schema exposes are the standard record columns of TSD P4 v3 T3.0: `is_active` and `state` on every row, plus the validity window of a conflict pair (`valid_from`, `valid_to`). The sign-on states of a session — RESOLVED and REFUSED — are the app story's and leave no row here, because the schema holds no session.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The ACE database engineer (any team, per U3) | Writes and runs the migrations, the grant script and the rollback |
| The service owner of rwb-access | Approves a destructive change; none is planned here |
| The platform DB owner (RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, RWB-PLT-NF06-DB, RWB-PLT-N011-DB) | Owns the sequence, the baseline, the login policy and the connection pool per login |
| RW-SECADM Security administrator | Owns the role-to-group mapping rows the schema stores, under RWB-P4-AD001-CON; loads none of them here |
| RW-REFADM Reference data administrator | Loads an approved role or matrix version through the service's operations, never through SQL |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A schema change is not a credit decision |

The grantee is named only as the rwb-access login (DP-02); its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0777; ASM-1405). No personal name and no credential appears in a migration, a script or a runbook.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. This is a database story and publishes no operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None by this story. The values the tables carry arrive through the service's own operations, and the ACE group facts arrive through the P1 contract.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The outbox object is created here so that the service can publish later; this story writes no event row and publishes nothing.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The inbox object is created here so that the service can consume idempotently later; this story consumes nothing.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The migration runs in the release pipeline, not on a Temporal Schedule.
