| permission | P4 | Created | PK on id; foreign key role_id to role; unique on role_id, capability_area, matrix_version |
| role_conflict | P4 | Created | PK on id; unique on role_code, conflicts_with, conflict_version; index on valid_from |
| outbox_event | PLT (library object, created in this schema) | Created from the event platform template | The template's keys, unchanged |
| processed_event | PLT (library object, created in this schema) | Created from the event platform template | The template's keys, unchanged |
| idempotency_key | PLT (library object, created in this schema) | Created from the event platform template | The template's keys, unchanged |
| masking_rule, delegation_limit | P4 | Not touched | Their own stories' migrations |
| lov_value, reference_row, reference_version | P3 | Not touched and not referenced | No key, no view and no grant names `rwb_case` |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Sequencing.** The service's Flyway sequence is owned by RWB-PLT-E1044-CON. The V0001 baseline creates the schema, the history table and the standard columns. This story adds the next versions after the baseline:

| Version | File | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| V0001 | baseline, from the platform DB story | Schema `rwb_access`, history table, standard columns |
| next after the baseline | `..._role_permission_conflict.sql` | Creates `role`, `permission` and `role_conflict` with their keys and indexes |
| next after that | `..._event_library_objects.sql` | Creates `outbox_event`, `processed_event` and `idempotency_key` from the event platform template |
| next after that | `..._access_grants.sql` | Usage on the schema and the table grants for the rwb-access login |

The legacy migration name `V_E1_022__role_conflict.sql` is recorded as the source of the `role_conflict` object; the monolith name and number are not reused on the service sequence. The exact version numbers are assigned by the sequence owner at build time; the order above is fixed by this story.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables. The three business tables and the three library objects live in `rwb_access` | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`. The library writes its record into this schema's own tables, which the writer of RWB-P4-E1039-APP owns | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON (carried by the writer's story; named here) |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case. `lov_value` is never created or read here: the values arrive over the contract | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library. The tables this story creates are the data that answer the guard, and no other service reads them | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout. The schema holds no call; the answers are the app story's | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1`. The schema name follows the same short name: `rwb_access` under `/api/recovery/access/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema. This story adds three migrations after the baseline and reuses no monolith name | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON (the sequence owner; named here) |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route. No screen reads this schema; the edge reads the answers of the app story | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |

**Table definitions**

`role` — `id` uuid NOT NULL, `role_code` varchar(20) NOT NULL, `role_name` varchar(80) NOT NULL, `role_class` varchar(15) NOT NULL, `default_scope` varchar(8) NOT NULL, `entra_group` varchar(120) NULL, plus the standard record columns of TSD P4 v3 T3.0. Primary key `(id)`; unique `(role_code)`; partial index `ix_role_entra_group` on `(entra_group)` where `is_active`.

`permission` — `id` uuid NOT NULL, `role_id` uuid NOT NULL, `capability_area` varchar(30) NOT NULL, `letters` varchar(5) NOT NULL, `matrix_version` varchar(20) NOT NULL, plus the standard record columns. Primary key `(id)`; foreign key `role_id` to `role(id)`; unique `(role_id, capability_area, matrix_version)`.

`role_conflict` — `id` uuid NOT NULL, `role_code` varchar(20) NOT NULL, `conflicts_with` varchar(30) NOT NULL, `reason` varchar(200) NOT NULL, `conflict_version` varchar(20) NOT NULL, `valid_from` date NOT NULL, `valid_to` date NULL, plus the standard record columns. Primary key `(id)`; unique `(role_code, conflicts_with, conflict_version)`; index on `(valid_from)`.

**No business value in a constraint.** `role_class`, `default_scope`, the letters and the two class values of `conflicts_with` are values of a list or of a matrix row. No check constraint carries them: a new area, a new letter set or a new class value must be a data change, not a migration (BR4). The application validates against `LOV-ROLE-CLASS`, `LOV-CAPABILITY` and `LOV-SCOPE` read over the reference-data contract.

**Library objects.** `outbox_event`, `processed_event` and `idempotency_key` are created in `rwb_access` from the template published by the event platform (RWB-PLT-TE006-CON) and are not modified here. Every service writes its own outbox and inbox in its own schema, so this is the only place where this service's events and inbox rows can live (Ownership Map ruling; ASM-1407).

**No session, password, token or local account.** The migration creates no session table, no password column, no token column and no local-account row, and the catalogue check of AC6 fails the build if one appears. Staff sign-in is ACE Common through gateway-bff, the session is in the gateway's Redis store (RWB-PLT-N006-INF), and there is no token store in the target (ADR-010; Architecture v5 slide 35).

**Grants.** `GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA rwb_access TO <the rwb-access login>`; `GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON role, permission, role_conflict, outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key TO <the rwb-access login>`; usage on the sequences those tables own. No grant to a shared login, no grant to another service's login, and no grant on `rwb_case` or on an ACE schema. The grantee name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0777; ASM-1405); the other migrations of the same service grant to the same login.

**Rollback.** Per migration, in reverse order: the grant script is reversed by revoking the grants it made; the library objects, then `role_conflict`, then `permission`, then `role` are dropped. A role row loaded between the two runs keeps its `id` and `role_code` where the rollback only reverses an added object, so a later matrix load is never orphaned (BR9). The rollback is exercised on a copy of the SIT schema and recorded in the runbook.

**Done when.** The migrations apply twice without a change, the catalogue checks pass, the grants are exactly as above, no session, password or token column exists, the rollback returns the schema to its pre-migration shape, and the tests in section 16 pass.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| Database error, no message id | A migration runs before the baseline or finds an object already present | The migration fails and nothing is applied; the pipeline stops |
| Database error, no message id | A grant script runs before the login exists | The script fails on the missing role; the platform DB story creates the login first |
| Check finding, no message id | A foreign key, view or grant names another schema or `public` | The pipeline check fails the build; the object is removed |
| Check finding, no message id | A session, password, token or local-account column appears | The pipeline check fails the build; the column is removed |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A role or matrix load reaches the database with a NOT NULL column empty | Enter {field}. Raised by the application, not by a database constraint |
| MSG-P1-002 | A matrix load names a role code the reference list does not know | The value you chose is not in the list. Raised by the application from the reference-data contract |

The business checks a reader might expect as database constraints are deliberately in the application: the class, area and scope values come from the reference contract (DP-07), and the letters are checked by the loading story, so a business person can change them without a migration. The database enforces what does not change: keys, uniqueness, dates and the schema boundary.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen. The result of a migration is visible in the release pipeline and in the service's Flyway history: pending, applied, failed, undone, each with a version and a checksum. The tables expose the standard record columns and the validity window of a conflict pair listed in section 9; nothing here is shown to a user directly, and the administration screens SCR-43 and SCR-47 in Epic 8 read the tables through the service's operations, never through SQL.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a constraint: the class, area and scope values and the letters are application and reference data, read over their contracts (DP-07).
- No personal data in a migration, a script, a test fixture or a runbook: a role, a group name and a matrix version are identifiers, and a user appears as a reference only.
- No session, password, token or local account in the schema, by design and by catalogue check (ADR-010).
- No read of another schema, no key into another schema and no grant that names one: `rwb_access` objects reference `rwb_access` objects only (DP-01).
- The ACE group facts come through the P1 contract or `RWB-P1-E1069-APP`; no view, synonym or statement in this schema names an ACE schema or `public`.
- One login per service: the rwb-access login is the only grantee, and its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0777; ASM-1405).
- The sequence is per service and linear: no monolith migration name is reused and no object is created twice (DP-15).
- The library objects are applied from the published template and never edited in this story, so a change to the outbox shape is one change in one place.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: integration slice of RWB-E1-022 for RWB-ITG-W1. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **QA integration engineer**, I want **the end-to-end proof that one Entra sign-in through the ACE common module yields one short-lived user JWT that gateway-bff carries to rwb-access (P4), rwb-case (P3) and rwb-source-data (P1) on the same session**, so that **the group-to-role mapping held as one data row in rwb-access, the scope taken from the P3 queue membership, the refusal of a service identity at a service boundary, the refusal event on the audit path, the version pinned by the open session, the authorise answer that expires with the session and the Redis-only session record are proved on the real wave 1 services before the wave exits**.

##### 2. Business rationale

RWB-E1-022 puts one sign-in in front of the whole Workbench: an Entra ID group per role per environment, granted through the bank IAM, read at each sign-in and turned into a session that carries the roles, the scope, the permission matrix version in force and the separation-of-duty version in force. Under the legacy design the SessionResolver lives in the P4 module, maps the `groups` claim against `role.entra_group` in the recovery schema, checks the `role_conflict` table, unions the letters of `permission` per capability area, and every controller of the monolith asks the in-process AccessCheck before its handler. The component copy of that behaviour sits in RWB-P4-E1022-APP, which owns the seven legacy criteria AC2, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8 and AC9 against the published contracts of the services it needs.

This integration story owns the two legacy criteria that no single service can prove, AC1 (one sign-in gives a session with roles, scope and matrix version, and the same session answers the session line and the menu) and AC3 (an identity in no Workbench group is refused everywhere at once), and it adds the eight cross-service criteria AC10 to AC17. Each of the ten is a statement about two owners at once. The session of AC1 is minted by the ACE common module, stored by gateway-bff, resolved by rwb-access and honoured by every other owner: asserted inside one service, it passes while the next service accepts a token whose session was never resolved. The refusal of AC3 is a fact about the edge and about every owner base at the same moment: a service that lets the token through to its own handler makes the criterion fail while the P4 story still passes.

The target moves the source of the facts, never the behaviour. Roles, permissions, conflicts, the delegation-of-approval table and the access log belong to rwb-access in `rwb_access` (DP-01, DP-08), so no service holds a role row and no service holds a copy of the group-to-role mapping. The session itself belongs to the edge: gateway-bff exchanges the browser's opaque session cookie for a short-lived user JWT from ACE common sign-in and keeps the session in its Redis store with no business data (DP-19; Arch v5 slide 20). Each call is one hop from the edge to the owner it needs, in parallel for a composite screen, with the 2 s budget and a breaker per owner (DP-11), and every path moves from the single `/api/recovery/v1` base to `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` (DP-13). The scope line is no longer a value read from a role row in the caller's own module: it is answered from the P3 queue-membership contract (DP-07), the same rows that decide which cases a person may open, so the session's scope and the case read cannot drift. Group names and the capability-area and scope lists are reference data read through the P3 reference-data contract (DP-07), the refusal is recorded locally by the owner that refuses it and collected in the central ledger (DP-03), each service migrates its own schema on its own Flyway sequence (DP-15), and the sign-in and refusal facts leave each service as an event and never as a personal value.

One point is not fixed by the sources and is carried as one gap and one assumption. Arch v5 slide 20 says gateway-bff turns the ACE common sign-in into a session and a short-lived user JWT, and the legacy story puts the `amr` check inside the service's SessionResolver, but no source says which claims the user JWT carries or where the multi-factor gate sits in the target. This story reads the gate at the edge, before any owner is called, and has rwb-access repeat the check when it resolves the session; the claim set is asserted by shape only, never by a value. That reading is GAP-0347 and ASM-0441. Release 30 November 2026 stays tentative, and a date is never a condition of this story.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P4-E1022-APP is done: the role, permission and role-conflict tables are in force in `rwb_access`, and `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session`, `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/roles`, `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` and `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log` answer on the P4 base.
- RWB-P3-E1019-APP is done: the queue and membership rows in force answer through the rwb-case contract, including the membership of a person, which the scope line of the session is read from.
- RWB-P1-E1001-APP is done: the 14 data products and their tables are in place, and the freshness read answers the business date of each data product, so a case read in the run is served from data in force.
- The permission matrix version PM-2026.11 is in force from 30 November 2026, and separation of duty version SOD-2026.11 is in force, both loaded as data in `rwb_access`.
- Role RW-CASEOWN carries `entra_group` RWB-SIT-RW-CASEOWN and default scope OWN in SIT; the roles of the run, RW-PHONECOL, RW-LITOFF, RW-LEGAL and RW-SECADM, carry their own `entra_group` rows, and the service identity SY-RULES carries RWB-SIT-SY-RULES.
- The ACE common module sign-in is configured for the Workbench application in Entra ID with the bank conditional access policy that requires a second factor, and rwb-access reaches it for sign-in and group-to-role as its only external call.
- gateway-bff is in front of every owner base in SIT, holds its Redis session store, and carries the short-lived user JWT of the ACE common module to the owner of each call.
- The published contracts of P1, P3 and P4 are versioned in the registry, and the run consumes only those contracts.
- The harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG is available with its synthetic identities U-1001 to U-1009, their group membership and the synthetic cases of the run.
- No production data is read, copied or connected to; every identity, group, role, case and business date the run uses is synthetic.
- The release date 30 November 2026 is tentative and is copied unchanged.

##### 4. Flow

1. QA integration engineer: loads the synthetic identity set of the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG - U-1001 in RWB-SIT-RW-CASEOWN, U-1002 in RW-PHONECOL only, U-1003 with no group whose name starts RWB-SIT-, U-1004 in RWB-SIT-RW-CASEOWN with a token whose `amr` claim holds `pwd` only, U-1005 in RWB-SIT-RW-LITOFF and RWB-SIT-RW-LEGAL, U-1006 in RWB-SIT-RW-SECADM and RWB-SIT-RW-CASEOWN, U-1008 in RWB-SIT-RW-CASEOWN and the unmapped RWB-SIT-LEGACY01, U-1009 for the two matrix versions, and the managed identity SY-RULES in RWB-SIT-SY-RULES; no service schema is opened and no production row is used.
2. Harness: opens the Workbench through gateway-bff as U-1001 and signs in once at the ACE common module with password and second factor.
3. ACE common module: returns the OpenID Connect token with the `groups` claim and the `amr` claim; gateway-bff records the one sign-in and exchanges it for a short-lived user JWT.
4. Gateway-bff: refuses the token at the edge when its `amr` claim does not contain `mfa`, with MSG-P4-005, before any owner is called (AC17).
5. Gateway-bff: calls `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` on the P4 base with the user JWT and stores the session record it receives in its Redis store, keyed by the session ID it issued.
6. rwb-access: checks the `amr` claim again, maps each group of the `groups` claim to an active `role` row by `entra_group`, ignores a group with no active row, checks the resulting role set against the role conflict version in force, reads the scope line from the P3 queue membership, and answers the session record: identity reference, roles with their default scope, matrix version, conflict version and scope line.
7. Harness: asserts the session record on `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` and the role list in force on `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/roles`, both on the same user JWT (AC10).
8. Harness: calls `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` on the P3 base with the same user JWT for the case of U-1001 and for the case of another officer, and reads `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness` to separate "not in scope" from "no data" (AC12).
9. Harness: signs in as U-1003 and as U-1002 and asserts the refusals of AC3 and AC2 across every owner base, the refusal events on the ACE audit and SOC path, and the two records of `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log` (AC14).
10. Harness: signs in as SY-RULES and asserts that the service identity is refused at the P4 boundary with the same message and the same reason code as the person of AC2 (AC13).
11. Harness: moves matrix version PM-2026.12 into force at 10:00 on 1 December 2026 in an open session of U-1009 signed in at 09:00 under PM-2026.11, checks the P4 and P3 boundaries at 10:30, signs in again at 11:00 and checks both again (AC15).
12. Harness: inspects the Redis session record of a valid session for the fields it holds and for the business values it does not hold, and the Redis store after the session ends for an authorise answer left behind (AC16, AC17).
13. Harness: proves from the recorded call set that no owner called the ACE common module for a second sign-in of the same session, that no call passed through another service, and that no fake stood in for a P1, P3 or P4 contract; then writes the evidence report and removes the synthetic identities.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A role without the right calls an endpoint, for example the admin API | Refused with 403 at the owner that declares the capability area and right; the refusal is written to the access event stream and the access log | MSG-P4-002 | AC13, AC14, TC-E1-022-02-ITG |
| X2 | The identity is in no Workbench group | Refused with 401 at the edge and at every owner base; the access request page shows the message and no data | MSG-P4-001 | AC3, AC14 |
| X3 | The token has no second factor in the `amr` claim | Refused with 401 at the edge before any owner is called; the refusal is logged | MSG-P4-005 | AC17, TC-E1-022-04-ITG |
| X4 | The groups give a role pair listed in the role conflict table | Session refused; an incident is raised to the security administrator; the refusal is logged | MSG-P4-006 | TC-E1-022-06-ITG, regression for RWB-P4-E1022-APP |
| X5 | A service identity calls an area its role does not hold | Refused with 403 at the service boundary, exactly as for a person, with the same reason code | MSG-P4-002 | AC13 |
| X6 | A group maps to no active role row | The group is ignored at rwb-access; if no other group maps, X2 applies | MSG-P4-001 | AC11, TC-E1-022-08-ITG |
| X7 | A new matrix version takes effect while a session is open | The open session keeps the version it resolved at the edge and at every owner; the next session uses the new one | None | AC15 |
| X8 | The ACE sign-in service does not answer | The sign-in fails with the general message and no session is created; no owner is called | MSG-GEN-006 | Section 17 |
| X9 | A cached authorise answer outlives its session | The answer is dropped with the session and the next call asks the owner again | None | AC16 |
| X10 | A consumed contract drifts from the published one, or the synthetic identity set does not match the run | The preflight fails on the contract test or on the identity check and the run stops before any assertion; no fake is put in place of a service contract | None | Section 17 |

X1 to X7 are the exception paths of the legacy story read on the wave 1 services; X4 is the legacy path whose criterion belongs to RWB-P4-E1022-APP and is run here as regression evidence; X8 to X10 are the suite's own failure modes, so that a missing answer never becomes a pass.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | The suite is a module of its own and reuses the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG; it needs the three integration dependencies and the published contracts of P1, P3 and P4, not their source code, and it owns no schema and no table |
| Negotiable | The identity count, the poll interval, the retry of the suite and the report layout are configuration; the groups, roles, scopes, versions, messages and reason codes are fixed by the legacy story and read as data |
| Valuable | Proves across services what one service cannot prove: one sign-in for every boundary, the mapping held once, the scope from the queue membership, the same refusal for a service identity, the refusal event, the version pinned by the session, the cache that dies with it, and the session that lives only at the edge |
| Estimable | One suite module, one identity pack, eight probes, one Redis inspection and one evidence report |
| Small | Seventeen scenarios over three services and two topics, with no service code and no schema change |
| Testable | Every criterion asserts a response, a status, a message, a reason code, a record, a field of the Redis record or the absence of a value, and every identity is synthetic |

```gherkin
    Then the P3 case read and the P1 freshness read answer from their own contracts and hold no group name and no mapping row

    Then GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId} answers case one on the same JWT

    When SY-RULES calls GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/roles

    Then POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise answers the same reason code "NO_RIGHT" for SY-RULES and for U-1002

    Given matrix version "PM-2026.12" takes effect at 10:00 on 1 December 2026 and rwb-access publishes AccessPolicyChanged on rwb.access.events.v1
    When GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/roles and GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId} are called at 10:30 in the same session
    Then rwb-access and rwb-case both answer under "PM-2026.11" and the open session keeps the version it resolved
    Then after U-1009 signs in again at 11:00 both boundaries answer under "PM-2026.12"
    Then no owner re-resolved the version of the open session

  Scenario: AC16 The cached authorise answer dies with the session (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the authorise answer for U-1001 is cached for the session, as the P4 contract allows
    When rwb-access publishes AccessPolicyChanged and the answer for the area of the cached call changes
    Then the open session keeps the answer it resolved and every call inside it receives the same answer
    Then after the session ends, or idles past its idle limit, the next call re-asks POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise and receives the new answer
    Then the Redis store holds no authorise answer after the session ends

  Scenario: AC17 The session lives only at the edge and the MFA gate is at the edge (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given test user "U-1004" is in group "RWB-SIT-RW-CASEOWN" and the token's amr claim holds "pwd" and not "mfa"
    When the token reaches gateway-bff
    Then the gateway refuses the session with status 401 and message MSG-P4-005 before any owner is called
    Then the recorded call set holds no P4, P3 or P1 call for that token
    Then the Redis session record of a valid session holds the session ID, the identity reference, the resolved roles, the two versions and the scope line, and no case, account, person or document value
```

**Target reading.** In the monolith one SessionResolver inside the P4 module reads `recovery.role`, `recovery.permission` and `recovery.role_conflict` and every controller asks the in-process AccessCheck. In the target the role, permission, conflict, delegation and access-log rows live in `rwb_access` only (DP-01, DP-08), each service signs in with its own login (DP-15 keeps its own migration sequence), the session is minted at the ACE common module, stored in the gateway Redis store and carried to every owner as one short-lived user JWT with one hop per call and a 2 s budget (DP-19, DP-11), the authorise answer is the published contract of rwb-access cached per session, the scope line is answered from the P3 queue membership and the lists from the P3 reference-data contract (DP-07), the refusal is recorded locally by the owner that refuses it and collected in the central ledger (DP-03), and the legacy `/api/recovery/v1` base moves to `/api/recovery/access/v1/`, `/api/recovery/case/v1/` and `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/` (DP-13). The claims of the short-lived user JWT and the split of the multi-factor gate between the edge and rwb-access are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0347; ASM-0441), so the suite asserts them by shape and never by a value.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Membership of the Entra ID group mapped to a role is the only way to hold the role. The Workbench holds no password and no local account | role.entra_group (DF-REF-039); DT07; Admin and access model, section 4.2 |
| BR2 | A session is refused unless the token carries a second factor | NFR-049; FEAT-ACA-02 |
| BR3 | No role inherits from another. A person with two roles holds the union of both roles' letters | permission.letters (DF-REF-043) |
| BR4 | A capability area with no letter for any of the session's roles refuses every action in that area | Permission matrix; CTL-09 |
| BR5 | A role pair listed in the role conflict table may not be held in one session | Separation of duty sheet, roles.txt; role_conflict table |
| BR6 | A service identity holds a role in the same table and is checked the same way as a person | REQ-ACA-010; NFR-051 |
| BR7 | A session keeps the matrix and conflict versions it resolved at sign-in until it ends | Admin and access model, section 4.2 |
| BR8 | Group names, roles, letters and conflicts are data rows with a version; none is written in code | Principle 1; DT02 |
| BR9 | The role, permission, conflict, delegation and access-log rows live in `rwb_access` only, and no service holds a role row or a copy of the group-to-role mapping | DP-01; DP-08; ownership map (role, permission, role_conflict, delegation_limit) |
| BR10 | One sign-in per session: the ACE common module mints the short-lived user JWT once, gateway-bff carries it to every owner, and no owner signs in again for the same session | Arch v5 slide 20; DP-19 |
| BR11 | The session record lives in the gateway Redis store and holds no business data: identity reference, roles, versions and scope line only | Arch v5 slide 20; DP-19 |
| BR12 | The multi-factor gate sits at the edge before any owner is called, and rwb-access repeats the check when it resolves the session; a token without `mfa` in its `amr` claim creates no session | BR2; ASM-0441 |
| BR13 | The scope line of the session is answered from the P3 queue membership; the scope of a role and the membership of a person cannot drift apart because there is one source | DP-07; BR7; REQ-ACA-009 |
| BR14 | The authorise answer is cached per session only, and the cache dies with the session | Arch v5 slide 14 (`authorise (cached)`); DP-08 |
| BR15 | A refusal carries a reason code - NO_ROLE, NO_MFA, ROLE_CONFLICT or NO_RIGHT - from the owner that refuses it, and the event of the refusal carries the Entra ID object reference and no personal value | RWB-E1-022 build step 5; guardrail of RWB-E1-022; DP-03 |
| BR16 | Every endpoint declares its capability area and right, and the contract test fails on an endpoint without one | RWB-E1-022 guardrail; DP-08 |
| BR17 | Each service signs in with its own login and migrates its own schema; the suite owns no schema and runs no migration | DP-02; DP-15; ADR-021 |
| BR18 | No service schema is opened by the suite and no published service contract is faked; a run that needs either fails the preflight | DP-01; section 17 |

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story changes no case status and no record; it creates a session with the states Resolved and Refused, and the session ends at sign-out or at its idle limit.

The states the run observes across the services:

| Item | States |
|---|---|
| Session at the edge | Created (gateway record and user JWT), Valid, Ended (sign-out or idle limit) |
| Session resolution at rwb-access | Resolved (roles, scope, matrix version, conflict version, scope line), Refused (reason code) |
| Refusal reason | NO_ROLE, NO_MFA, ROLE_CONFLICT, NO_RIGHT |
| Authorise answer | Cached for the session, Re-asked after the session ends |
| Suite run | Not started, running, passed, failed with the failing test case named |

The request, approval and grant of a role run in the bank IAM and are outside this story.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The suite provides no REST operation. The names reserved for P2 rwb-integration - the base `/api/recovery/integration/v1`, the topic `rwb.integration.events.v1`, the task queue `rwb-integration` and the schema `rwb_integration` - are recorded as reserved and are not used, and no `rwb_integration` table is written.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use | Budget |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` | P4 rwb-access | AC1, AC10, AC12, AC15: the session record after one sign-in - identity reference, roles with their default scope, matrix version, conflict version and scope line | 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/roles` | P4 rwb-access | AC10, AC11, AC13, AC15: the role list in force with `entra_group`, and the refusal of a role without Platform administration R | 2 s |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | AC13, AC16: the authorise answer for a role, a scope and a duty limit, cached per session; the published authorise contract of rwb-access on Arch v5 slide 14 | 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log` | P4 rwb-access | AC13, AC14: one record per refused call with the identity and the reason code | 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | AC12, AC15: the case of the session holder, the 404 outside the scope, and the version pinned by the open session | 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness` | P1 rwb-source-data | AC12: the data product behind the case, so a 404 is the scope answer and not a missing data product | 2 s |

Every call is one hop to the owning service on its own base (DP-11, DP-13) with the 2 s client budget behind gateway-bff, and the suite calls no service through another service. The session read, the role read and the access-log read are P4 operations in the ownership map, and the case read is a P3 operation there; the authorise operation is named for rwb-access on Arch v5 slide 14 (`POST /authorise`, `GET /me/permissions`, `GET /doa-limits`, `/masking-policies`), so the path shown is that operation on the P4 base of DP-13 and is a derivation of two sources, not a new contract.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The suite publishes no business event.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | What the suite asserts |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` | `rwb.access.events.v1` | P4 rwb-access (observed as produced) | AC15: the version announcement that follows the matrix version in force; the open session keeps its version and the next session resolves the new one at two services |
| `rwb.access.DoaLimitChanged.v1` | `rwb.access.events.v1` | P4 rwb-access (observed as produced) | AC16: a duty-limit announcement while a session is open changes neither the cached authorise answer nor the session record; the values of the duty table themselves belong to RWB-P4-E1022-APP |

The suite asserts no other event. The local decision record of a refusal is written by the owner that refuses it and collected in the central ledger in rwb-decision (DP-03), and that record belongs to RWB-P4-E1022-APP; this story asserts the refusal on the audit path and in the access log instead. No event carries a case, an account or a person value.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The sign-in, the session resolution, the authorise check and the refusal are synchronous service steps; this story starts no workflow, observes no workflow and asserts no activity, and no case workflow is on the path of a sign-in.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The six-monthly access review list of rwb-access (JOB-18, a Schedule in the owning service) is not asserted by this story and belongs to RWB-P4-E1022-APP; the suite starts no schedule and moves only the matrix version of AC15 with its own clock control.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The suite owns no table and never reads another service's schema (DP-01). The tables it exercises are listed in section 11 with their owners: `role`, `permission` and `role_conflict` in `rwb_access`, the queue and membership rows in `rwb_case`, and the data products of `rwb_source_data`.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

None for a service contract. The only stub is external to the nineteen services:

| Stub | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Mock Entra sign-in with its synthetic groups | Gives the run its synthetic identities U-1001 to U-1009, the managed identity SY-RULES and their group membership, with the `groups` and `amr` claims, as the platform demo sign-in does |

No published service contract is faked: the run needs the real P1, P3 and P4 services on their published contracts, and a run that needs a fake for any of them fails the preflight.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Provided | Consumed | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 | 6 operations | The session read, the role read, the authorise call, the access-log read, the case read and the freshness read; one hop each, 2 s budget (DP-11, DP-13, DP-19) |
| Kafka | None | 2 event types | `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` and `rwb.access.DoaLimitChanged.v1` on `rwb.access.events.v1`; CloudEvents 1.0 (DP-14) |
| Temporal | None | None | No workflow and no activity in this story |
| File | None | None | No file in this story |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** One suite module that reuses the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG: an identity pack for the synthetic people, the managed identity and their groups; a version and clock control for the matrix version of AC15; eight probes; a Redis inspection; and an evidence report with one verdict per test case. No service code and no schema change.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| SuiteRunner | Test harness | Preflight against the published contracts of P1, P3 and P4 and against the identity pack, run order, report and exit code |
| IdentityDriver | Test harness | Drives the mock Entra sign-in for U-1001 to U-1009 and SY-RULES, counts the sign-ins, and sets the `groups` and `amr` claims of each token |
| SessionProbe | Test harness | The session record of AC1 and AC10 on `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session`, the role list on `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/roles`, and the one-sign-in count |
| MappingProbe | Test harness | The mapped and the unmapped group of AC11, and the assertion that no service other than rwb-access decides a role |
| ScopeProbe | Test harness | The scope line of AC12 from the P3 queue membership, the case in scope and the 404 outside it, with the freshness read that separates the two |
| IdentityBoundaryProbe | Test harness | The refusal of SY-RULES at the P4 boundary of AC13 with the same message and the same reason code as U-1002 |
| RefusalEventProbe | Test harness | The two refusal events of AC14 on the ACE audit and SOC path, their Entra ID object reference and the absence of a personal value, and the two access-log records |
| VersionProbe | Test harness | The two matrix versions of AC15 across the P4 and P3 boundaries at 09:00, 10:00, 10:30 and 11:00 |
| CacheProbe | Test harness | The cached authorise answer of AC16 and its disappearance with the session |
| EdgeGateProbe | Test harness | The `amr` gate of AC17 at the edge, the empty owner call set for that token, and the fields held and not held by the Redis record |
| ReportWriter | Test harness | One row per test case with its evidence and elapsed time, and the cleanup record |

**Database.** None of its own. The suite writes no service table and no schema object, and it holds no client for a service schema and no client for a `v_ace_*` view.

**Configuration and reference data**

- The SIT endpoints of P1, P3 and P4 behind gateway-bff, the topic name, the schema-registry address, the Redis inspection endpoint of the gateway and the gateway idle limit, all as configuration.
- The synthetic identities U-1001 to U-1009, the managed identity SY-RULES and their groups RWB-SIT-RW-CASEOWN, RWB-SIT-RW-LITOFF, RWB-SIT-RW-LEGAL, RWB-SIT-RW-SECADM, RWB-SIT-SY-RULES and RWB-SIT-LEGACY01, with no production identity.
- The role rows of the run, RW-CASEOWN, RW-PHONECOL, RW-LITOFF, RW-LEGAL and RW-SECADM, read through the P4 role read and never written in the suite code.
- Permission matrix versions PM-2026.11 and PM-2026.12 and separation of duty version SOD-2026.11, with their effective times, read through the P4 session record and the announcement topic.
- The capability-area and scope lists, LOV-CAPABILITY and LOV-SCOPE, read through the P3 reference-data contract (DP-07) and not typed in the suite.
- The 2 s client budget, the retry of the suite and the poll interval of the announcement topic.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-01 and DP-08 carry the role, permission, conflict and access-log facts behind one owner; DP-07 carries the scope line and the two lists, which are reference data of rwb-case; DP-11 and DP-19 carry the one hop from the edge and the 2 s budget; DP-13 carries the base of every path; DP-03 applies to the refusal, which the refusing owner records locally and which is collected in the central ledger, and the suite asserts it on the access log and the audit path rather than in a table; DP-15 keeps one migration sequence per service and one schema per owner. The H and C entries of the table belong to the service, platform and operations stories that own them: this ITG story carries no H, C or X entry of its own, and an integration story never becomes a build dependency of another story (Template and Rules section R5.4 and R5.7). The I list names the three service builds whose behaviour the run exercises.

**Build steps**

1. Create the suite module next to harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG and wire it to the SIT endpoints, the topic and the gateway Redis inspection, with the contract preflight that fails on any drift.
2. Build IdentityDriver and the identity pack; assert that each synthetic identity signs in and that each group membership is the one the criteria name, before any assertion is made.
3. Build SessionProbe and prove the one sign-in of AC10: the session record, the role read and one sign-in count at the ACE common module.
4. Build MappingProbe for AC11 and assert that the mapping is one row in `rwb_access`, that the unmapped group is ignored, and that the P3 and P1 responses hold no group name.
5. Build ScopeProbe for AC12: the scope line from the P3 queue membership, the case in scope, the 404 outside it and the freshness read behind the case.
6. Build IdentityBoundaryProbe and RefusalEventProbe; assert the same refusal for SY-RULES and for U-1002, the two reason codes, the two audit events with the Entra ID object reference, and the two access-log records.
7. Build VersionProbe for AC15 and CacheProbe for AC16 with the clock control; assert the version pinned by the open session at two services and the answer re-asked after the session ends.
8. Build EdgeGateProbe for AC17: the refusal at the edge with MSG-P4-005, the empty owner call set, and the fields held and not held by the Redis record.
9. Build ReportWriter and the cleanup; run the whole suite twice to prove that a repeated sign-in of the same identity opens a second session and leaves no answer of the first behind.

**Done when.** The ten test cases of section 16 pass on the real services in SIT, the two criteria this story owns (AC1 and AC3) and the eight cross-service criteria (AC10 to AC17) are signed off against the contracts, the gateway Redis store holds no authorise answer after a session ends and no business value during one, no service table and no view was opened by the suite, the synthetic identities are removed, and the evidence report names every criterion with its observable.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | Sign-in with no Workbench role | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-P4-002 | An action outside the role's permission | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-005 | Token without a second factor | Sign in again with your second factor. The Workbench needs multi-factor authentication. |
| MSG-P4-006 | Conflicting role pair at sign-in | Your roles {role} and {otherRole} cannot be held together. Access is refused and the security administrator has been told. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | ACE sign-in service unavailable | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |

The five texts are copied unchanged from RWB-E1-022 and this story adds no message ID. The messages are rendered by the service or the edge that refuses the call and passed through gateway-bff unchanged, so the suite asserts the ID and the text on the response it receives.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen is built by this story. The ACE front end shell is served through gateway-bff (DP-19): it shows the session line from `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` at the top of every page, hides the menu entries whose capability area the session cannot read, and shows no Administration menu for RW-CASEOWN. A person with no role sees the access request page with MSG-P4-001 and no data. A token without a second factor never reaches a page, because the gate is at the edge. Epic 1 has no business screens in this story, and the screen states the run observes are the session line, the filtered menu, the access request page and the refusal banner of the owner that refused the call.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No local password and no local account: the only credential is the ACE common module sign-in with a second factor, and the Workbench holds no secret of its own (DP-19; BR1).
- No role cache that outlives the session: the authorise answer is cached per session and dies with it, and the Redis store holds no answer after the session ends (DP-08).
- No copy of the group-to-role mapping in any service but rwb-access: no service holds a role row, a group name or a mapping table (DP-01; BR9).
- No personal data in events, logs or fixtures: a refusal carries the Entra ID object reference, the reason code and the area and right, and never a name, an e-mail or a case, account or person value (DP-03; BR15).
- Every endpoint declares its capability area and right, and the contract test fails on an endpoint without one (BR16).
- The identity number and every personal field stay behind the owners; this story reads no personal field at all.
- No business value in code: the roles, the groups, the letters, the versions and the lists are read as data through the P3 and P4 contracts.
- Synthetic identities only: the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG supplies every identity, and the run refuses any environment that is not SIT.
- One hop and a 2 s budget on every call, with no service called through another service and no owner signing in again for the same session (ADR-020; DP-11).
- Clean-up in the same run: the synthetic identities and the moved version are removed or restored, and the report records what was cleaned.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-023 for rwb-case. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As **TechX (any team may pick up this story)**, I want **one OpenAPI 3.1 document for the read-only case record operations of rwb-case, with the composed response schemas, the read-only rule, the masking and scope hooks, the error envelope, the version and the nine contract tables**, so that **rwb-case, gateway-bff, rwb-access, rwb-source-data and every later consumer build the case record view against one published read contract on Day 1**.

The document covers the five read operations the view needs: `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}`, `/accounts`, `/parties`, `/timeline` and `/timers`. It is the baseline for the contract fake that RWB-P3-E1023-APP builds against; it starts no build dependency.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the engineering standard (ADR-020, DP-11). The case record view is a composite: gateway-bff calls rwb-case and rwb-source-data in parallel and merges the answers. Unless the read shape, the field masking markers, the scope behaviour and the error envelope are fixed before the screen work starts, each caller invents its own shape and the merge in gateway-bff breaks at every change.

This story fixes that shape on Day 1: the operations, the response schema that composes the case, account, party, timeline and timer blocks, the read-only rule, the masking and scope hooks, the error envelope, the version and the nine tables of §12. It also fixes the fakes for rwb-source-data, rwb-access and the masking contract so the screen story and the vehicle tests can run without the live services.

The contract carries no business value of its own: every label, mask rule, timeout and page size comes from the owning service or from a parameter, so a change is data, not a new version of the contract.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service naming of Template and Rules §R4 is fixed for rwb-case: schema `rwb_case`, REST base `/api/recovery/case/v1`, topic `rwb.case.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`.
- The legacy contract of RWB-E1-023 §12 and the endpoint inventory API-P3-002, API-P3-003, API-P3-004, API-P3-005 and API-P3-013 of TSD P3 v3 Appendix T-A are the source of the operation list.
- The table ownership of `_work/msr/plan/ownership.json` is accepted: rwb-case owns `rwb_case`; rwb-source-data owns the interaction ledger and the ACE views.
- The rwb-case login (DP-02) will exist with SELECT on schema `rwb_case`. The login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0692; ASM-1239).
- The masking contract of rwb-access is published as C RWB-P4-E1039-CON. The exact shape of the field masking contract is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0694; ASM-1241).
- The platform contract RWB-PLT-N001-CON will publish the gateway-bff composite route. The exact route specification is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0693; ASM-1240).
- The timeline page size and the interaction read operation are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0695; ASM-1242).
- No build dependency. Day 1.

##### 4. Flow

1. TechX: takes the operation list from §12.1 and the legacy contract, and names each operation with an `operationId` in the service package.
2. TechX: writes the response schemas for the case block, the account block, the party block with its contact points, the timeline page and the timer block, and one composed schema that holds all five blocks for the composite route.
3. TechX: marks every personal field with its masking hook (masked or clear source, personal-data flag) and every operation with its scope hook (Case record R, scope applied).
4. TechX: writes the error envelope once and references it from every operation with the status codes 401, 403, 404 and 503 and the MSG codes of §14.
5. TechX: fixes the version `v1` in the path, the media type, the identifier format and the read-only rule, then runs the OpenAPI 3.1 linter and the review checklist.
6. TechX: generates the contract fake from the document and publishes it, with the fakes for rwb-source-data, rwb-access and rwb-document, to RWB-P3-E1023-APP and to gateway-bff.
7. TechX: records the consumer acknowledgements of gateway-bff, rwb-access and rwb-source-data against the document checksum.
8. Every consumer: builds against the fake; a change to the document is a new version and a new checksum.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A request or response field has no source value | The document carries the placeholder Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0692; ASM-1239) for the login name, (GAP-0693; ASM-1240) for the composite route, (GAP-0694; ASM-1241) for the masking shape and (GAP-0695; ASM-1242) for the ledger read and paging; no value is invented | None | AC1, AC4 |
| X2 | The document declares a write operation on a read path | The linter fails and the document is not published | None | AC3 |
| X3 | The document fails OpenAPI 3.1 validation | The document is not published and the checksum is not issued | None | AC1 |
| X4 | A consumer builds against a superseded checksum | The consumer fails the compatibility check against the published checksum | None | AC5 |
| X5 | The rwb-access masking contract changes shape after publication | A new version of the document is raised and the masking hook is re-pointed; the screen story is not changed in place | None | AC4 |
| X6 | The gateway-bff composite route is published with a different merge shape | The contract keeps the five read operations and adds the route mapping; the difference is recorded as GAP-0693 | None | AC2, AC5 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency and no table; it fixes the shape other stories build against |
| Negotiable | Schema names and block order are design choices; no business value is fixed here |
| Valuable | One published read contract removes the guesswork from the screen, the edge and the masking work |
| Estimable | One document, five operations, one composed schema, one error envelope, four fakes |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its contract tests |
| Testable | The document itself is the test object; every criterion is checked by a linter or a contract test |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Case record read contract v1

  Background:
    Given the contract baseline of rwb-case read-only case record operations under /api/recovery/case/v1

  Scenario: AC1 The OpenAPI 3.1 document for the five read operations (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the OpenAPI 3.1 document is generated from the contract baseline
    When the document is validated with an OpenAPI 3.1 validator and the contract linter
    Then it validates with no error
    Then it declares GET operations for /cases/{caseId}, /cases/{caseId}/accounts, /cases/{caseId}/parties, /cases/{caseId}/timeline and /cases/{caseId}/timers
    Then every operation carries an operationId, a summary, the 200 response, the error responses and the Case record R security requirement

  Scenario: AC2 The composed response schema (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the document is published
    When a consumer resolves the composed case record schema
    Then it holds a case block with the header fields, an accounts array, a parties array with the contact points, a timeline page and a timers array
    Then each block names its owning service and the business date it carries
    Then the composed schema is the one gateway-bff uses for the SCR-03 screen model

  Scenario: AC3 The read-only rule (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the document is published
    When every path and operation in the document is listed
    Then the five read paths carry GET only
    Then the document declares no POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE operation on a case record path
    Then the transfer, legal-hold, task and placement operations are absent from this document

  Scenario: AC4 The masking and scope hooks (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the document is published
    When every personal field of the party and contact blocks is inspected
    Then each one names its masked source and its personal-data flag
    Then each operation states the Case record R right and the scope filter
    Then a field whose masking rule is unavailable is described as Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0694; ASM-1241)

  Scenario: AC5 The error envelope, version and fakes (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the document is published with version v1 in the path
    When a caller sends a request outside the caller's scope or without the right
    Then the documented answer is 404 with MSG-P4-003 and 403 with MSG-P4-002 in the same error envelope
    Then the envelope carries a code, a message and a trace identifier and is shared by every operation
    Then the fakes for rwb-source-data, rwb-access and the masking contract are generated from the same document and published with its checksum

  Scenario: AC6 The nine contract tables (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the document is published
    When its §12 tables are compared with the service facts
    Then tables 12.1 to 12.9 are all present and none is empty
    Then the schema, REST base, topic and task queue match Template and Rules §R4 for rwb-case
    Then every table named in 12.7 is owned by P3 in the ownership map
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| CB1 | The document follows OpenAPI 3.1 and the service naming of Template and Rules §R4: base `/api/recovery/case/v1`, schema `rwb_case`, topic `rwb.case.events.v1`, queue `rwb-case`, package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case` | R4; ADR-020 |
| CB2 | The five read operations are the only operations in this document; every other rwb-case operation belongs to its own story | §12.1; BR11 of RWB-P3-E1023-APP |
| CB3 | Every personal field names its masked source and its personal-data flag, and every operation states its right and its scope | RWB-P4-E1039-CON; DP-08 |
| CB4 | One error envelope serves every operation, with the MSG codes of §14 and the status codes 401, 403, 404 and 503 | TSD P3 v3 T2.1; §14 |
| CB5 | The version sits in the path; a change is a new version and a new checksum, never an edit in place | ADR-020; R8.2 of the Template and Rules |
| CB6 | Every value that a source does not give is a placeholder with its gap and assumption, never an invented value | Template and Rules §R9; GAP-0695; ASM-1242 |

##### 9. State transitions

None. A contract has versions, not case state. This story changes no case status and writes no row.

##### 10. Authority

| rwb-case service owner (P3) | Owns the document as the service contract; approves the operation set |
| rwb-access owner (P4) | Owns the masking contract and the access-log hook that the document references |
| rwb-source-data owner (P1) | Owns the customer, account, freshness and interaction operations the document consumes |
| gateway-bff owner (RWB-PLT-N001-CON) | Owns the composite route and acknowledges the composed schema |
| Solution architect | Approves the read-only rule and the versioning rule |
| Test and QA lead | Runs the contract tests and the consumer compatibility check |

##### 11. Data

The document fixes shapes, not values. The schemas carry these fields, with the field IDs of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v7:

| Block | Fields | Table or contract behind it | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| case | case_no, product_group, status, stage_code, route_code, owner_user_id, queue_id, entry_date, prescription_date, deviation_open, legal_hold | recovery_case, queue | P3 |
| accounts | account_key, is_primary, accountNo, daysPastDue, totalBalance, dataAsOf | case_account plus the rwb-source-data account contract | P3 for the link, P1 for the facts |
| parties | person_key, party_role, displayName, customerNo, idNo or idNoLast4, category, contacts with contactType, contactKey, contactValue, dataAsOf | case_party plus the rwb-source-data customer and contact contract | P3 for the link, P1 for the facts |
| timeline | occurredAt, channel, contactResult, sourceSystem, actionCode, actionCodeName, contactAt, promiseStatus, page, size | the rwb-source-data interaction read; paging Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0695; ASM-1242) | P1 |
| timers | timer type, started_at, expires_at, warn_at, paused, status | timer | P3 |

No row is read or written by this story. The response shapes copy the field names of the legacy contract of RWB-E1-023 §12 unchanged, and the field IDs of section 11 of that story.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** The document is held with the service contract of rwb-case, under Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`; it is the input to the code generator of the platform contract library.

| Composed schema | case, accounts, parties, timeline and timers in one screen model for gateway-bff |
| Contract linter rules | Read-only rule, operationId naming, personal-field flags, the nine tables present |
| Fakes | The rwb-case read fake plus the four fakes of 12.8 |
| Checksum register | The published document with its checksum and the consumer acknowledgements |

**Pattern application**

As a CON story it carries no build dependency: the H rows above are the pattern rows of the vehicle, recorded here for the trace, and they are taken by the APP story that builds.

**Build steps**

1. Fix the operation list and the operationIds from 12.1; check the legacy contract for every request and response field.
2. Write the five block schemas and the composed schema; check every field name against section 11.
3. Add the masking hook to every personal field and the scope hook to every operation.
4. Write the error envelope once and reference it from every operation with the MSG codes.
5. Fix version v1, the media type, the identifier format and the read-only rule.
6. Run the OpenAPI 3.1 validator and the contract linter; a write operation on a read path fails the build.
7. Generate the fakes of 12.8 and publish them with the checksum.
8. Collect the gateway-bff, rwb-access and rwb-source-data acknowledgements.

**Done when.** The document validates, the linter passes, the fakes are published with the checksum and the three consumer acknowledgements are recorded.

**Contract tests.** Schema validity and compatibility with the previous checksum, the read-only rule, the error envelope on all four status codes, the masking flags on every personal field and the completeness of the nine tables.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | No session or an expired session | You are not signed in. Sign in to continue. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | Case outside the scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P3-023 | A section cannot be shown | {section} cannot be shown now. The rest of the case is shown. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The access record cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

Validation rules the document must satisfy: OpenAPI 3.1 valid; every operation has an operationId in the service namespace; every path is under `/api/recovery/case/v1`; no write method on a case record path; every personal field carries a personal-data flag and a masked source; every operation declares 401, 403, 404 and 503 with the shared envelope; the envelope carries a code, a message and a trace identifier. The envelope body shape follows the problem response of TSD P3 v3 T2.1 and its field names are fixed by this document, not by a caller.

##### 15. Screens and states

None. This story delivers no screen. It fixes the data the SCR-03 screen consumes in each state: Loading (the composed schema with empty blocks), Read only (the five blocks with their business dates), On hold (the hold flag and the prescription date in the case block), Stale input (the business date and batch state per block, so the stale banner can be driven), Error (the shared envelope with the MSG code for the section that failed). The screen itself is built by RWB-P3-E1023-APP and served as the gateway-bff composite route.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the document: labels, mask rules, timeouts and page sizes are named as sources, never fixed here.
- No personal data in the document examples: every example party is synthetic and no example carries a clear identity number or contact value.
- No PII in events, workflow inputs or logs, and none in the contract examples.
- rwb-case reads only schema `rwb_case`; the document declares no foreign table and no cross-schema read (DP-01).
- ACE data is declared only through the rwb-source-data contract, never as a view or a table of rwb-case (DP-05).
- The interaction ledger is declared through its owner's read, never as a table (DP-18).
- The document states Case record R and the scope on every operation; a hook that hides the scope fails the linter (DP-08).
- No write operation on a case record path in this document.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-023 for rwb-case. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **one read-only screen per case with the case ID, accounts, arrears, owner, queue, stage, status, contact history and documents, read live through the owner of each fact with the business date of each**, so that **I stop searching files and systems to understand a case**.

The screen is SCR-03, delivered as a gateway-bff composite route (DP-19, H RWB-PLT-N001-CON). gateway-bff calls rwb-case `GET /cases/{caseId}` and, in parallel, rwb-source-data for the customer and account parts, then merges the answers into the screen model. rwb-case serves the case block, the account and party links, the timeline and the timers from its own schema `rwb_case`; it reads no other service's tables and no ACE view (DP-01). The customer, account, contact and collections history facts arrive through the rwb-source-data contract (DP-05), and the interaction ledger belongs to rwb-source-data (DP-18). Masking is applied by the rwb-access policy (DP-08, C RWB-P4-E1037-CON), with the personal-field read shaped by C RWB-P4-E1039-CON.

##### 2. Business rationale

A case owner opens EFS, ALS, shared drives and team spreadsheets today to answer one question about a case. Under D-RCV-35 the Workbench holds no copy of the account, the customer or the contact point: the screen reads the ACE views by `account_key` and `person_key` through rwb-source-data, which is the only reader of `v_ace_account`, `v_ace_customer`, `v_ace_contact` and `v_ace_efs_action`. The identity number is already masked inside `v_ace_customer` (`id_no_masked` and `id_no_last4`) and the contact values are masked by role through the rwb-access masking policy, so no clear personal value is copied into a Workbench table or a screen cache.

This story puts the case, its accounts and arrears, its parties and contacts, its contact history and its documents on SCR-03, each section showing the ACE business date behind it, and writes every view of personal data to the access log through the rwb-access access-log contract. It meets REQ-OCC-007, REQ-RDF-009, REQ-ACA-005, REQ-ACA-006 and REQ-ACA-009. The read is the first screen of the service, so it also fixes the read shape the whole service reuses: one hop per owner, a 2 s budget, a composite route at the edge and no chained call.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P3-E1018-APP is done: cases exist in schema `rwb_case` with `account_key` links on case_account and `person_key` links on case_party.
- RWB-P3-E1023-CON is done: the OpenAPI 3.1 document and the fakes for the read-only case record operations, through which this story builds.
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is done: the gateway-bff composite route that serves SCR-03. The exact route specification (path, merge rules, timeout ownership) is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0693; ASM-1240).
- RWB-PLT-E1037-CON and C RWB-P4-E1037-CON are done: the authorise, masking-policy and access-log contracts of rwb-access are published with their fakes (DP-08).
- C RWB-P4-E1039-CON is published: the customer and account read contract that also carries the masking contract for personal fields. The exact shape of the field masking contract is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0694; ASM-1241).
- The published rwb-source-data contract serves `GET /customers/{id}`, `GET /accounts/{id}`, `GET /freshness` and the interaction read, with its fake. The timeline page size and the interaction read operation are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0695; ASM-1242).
- RWB-P3-E1018-APP cases carry the case header fields this view shows: case number, product group, status, stage, route, owner, queue, entry date and prescription date.
- RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1042-CON (parameters), RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON (reference data), RWB-PLT-E1047-CON (event and topic naming), RWB-PLT-E1044-CON (Flyway sequence) and RWB-PLT-E1027-CON (decision record) are done.
- The rwb-case login (DP-02) holds SELECT on schema `rwb_case` and no privilege on any other schema. The login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0692; ASM-1239).
- The user holds a role with Case record R in rwb-access and the case is in the user's scope.
- Personal data access is recorded through the rwb-access access-log contract, which also sends the PII access record to PII Kafka through the ACE common module.
- `v_ace_batch_status` is a Section B view, so the freshness line reaches the screen through rwb-source-data and the stale banner stays behind its flag until RWB-ACE-001 lands (DL43).

##### 4. Flow

1. Case owner: opens a case from SCR-02 Case list; the gateway-bff composite route shows SCR-03 in the Loading state.
2. gateway-bff: checks the session in Redis, takes the short-lived JWT through ACE Common sign-in and checks the coarse permission.
3. gateway-bff: calls rwb-case `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` and, in parallel, rwb-source-data `GET /customers/{id}` and `GET /accounts/{id}`; the document panel is one further hop to rwb-document `GET /cases/{id}/documents`.
4. rwb-case CaseRecordController: checks Case record R and the scope through the cached rwb-access `POST /authorise`; out of scope returns 404.
5. rwb-case CaseRecordQueryService: reads the header from recovery_case and the links from case_account and case_party, plus queue, timers and the reference labels, all inside schema `rwb_case` (DP-01).
6. rwb-case SourceDataClient: calls the rwb-source-data contract for the account facts by `account_key`, the customer and contact facts by `person_key` and the collections history from `v_ace_efs_action`; every row carries the ACE business date from `data_as_of` and the freshness contract.
7. rwb-case TimelineComposer: merges the rwb-case state changes and the Workbench entries read from the rwb-source-data interaction read (DP-18) into one contact history ordered by time, each row carrying its source system.
8. rwb-case MaskingApplier: asks rwb-access `GET /masking-policies` for the caller's role, fills each personal field from the masked or the clear column through the guard library, and publishes one AC-READ access record with the field IDs read and their masked flags. A read whose record cannot be written returns nothing.
9. rwb-document (P5): returns the document list for the case through its endpoint.
10. gateway-bff: merges the three answers into the screen model and returns it.
11. CaseRecordPage: shows the header (case number, product, status, stage, route, owner, queue, entry date, prescription date, deviation and hold flags), then Accounts, Parties with their contact points, Contact history and Documents, each with its ACE business date (read only state).
12. CaseRecordPage: shows the stale banner with MSG-P1-001 on any section whose ACE batch is not COMPLETE for the latest business date, and no Workbench load or job status anywhere.
13. CaseRecordPage: shows the on hold banner with MSG-P3-004 when the case is on hold.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The ACE batch behind a section is not COMPLETE for the latest business date | Section shows with its business date and the stale banner | MSG-P1-001 | AC4 |
| X2 | The case is outside the user's scope | 404; nothing shows | MSG-P4-003 | AC5 |
| X3 | The document hub does not answer | Documents section shows the section message; the rest shows | MSG-P3-023 | AC6 |
| X4 | The access record cannot be written | The read is refused; no case data and no personal field shows | MSG-P7-003 | AC7 |
| X5 | The role may not see a personal field in clear | The field shows from the masked column of the view, through the masking policy | None | AC8 |
| X6 | The case is on hold | On hold banner with the prescription date | MSG-P3-004 | AC9 |
| X7 | The case has no documents and no contact history | Each section shows its empty sentence | MSG-P3-024 | AC10 |
| X8 | A role without Case record R opens the view | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-E1-023-11 |
| X9 | A case link holds an `account_key` that the account contract does not return | The Accounts row shows the key with empty values; REC-05 lists it; the rest shows | None | AC12 |
| X10 | rwb-source-data does not answer within the 2 s budget | The Accounts and Parties sections show MSG-P3-023; the header, timeline and documents show | MSG-P3-023 | AC6 pattern, new in D-RCV-60 |
| X11 | The gateway-bff composite route merge fails | The screen shows the section message for the part that failed; no partial case data with a missing scope check is shown | MSG-P3-023 | AC6 pattern, new in D-RCV-60 |

```gherkin
    Given v_ace_contact holds a mobile for P-7001 with contact_key "PHONE:88421" and contact_value "0812345678"
    Given the rwb-source-data contract mock returns person_key P-7001 with category "RETAIL", id_no_masked "XXXXXXXXX4821" and the mobile for P-7001 with contact_key "PHONE:88421"
    When the view opens
    Then the Parties section shows the borrower with role "BORROWER", category "RETAIL" and business date 2026-12-02
    Then the borrower's contact points show from v_ace_contact with their contact_type and usage_code
    Then the contact history shows the v_ace_efs_action entries with action code, time and promise status

  Scenario: AC5 Case outside the scope (legacy RWB-E1-023 AC5)
    Given case RW-2026-000702 belongs to team "LIT-BKK" and U-81 has scope Own
    Given the rwb-access contract mock returns scope Own for U-81
    When U-81 opens case RW-2026-000702
    Then the response is 404 with MSG-P4-003
    Then no case data shows

  Scenario: AC6 Document hub unavailable (legacy RWB-E1-023 AC6)
    Given the document hub does not answer within 3 seconds
    When U-81 opens the view
    Then the Documents section shows MSG-P3-023 for "Documents"
    Then the header, accounts, parties and contact history show

  Scenario: AC7 The access event cannot be written (legacy RWB-E1-023 AC7)
    Given the access event stream rejects every write
    Given the rwb-access contract mock rejects every AC-READ access record write
    When U-81 opens the view
    Then the call returns status 503 with MSG-P7-003 and no case data
    Then no personal field shows

  Scenario: AC8 Masking by role (legacy RWB-E1-023 AC8)
    Given phone collector U-82 holds no masking rule that lets RW-PHONECOL see DF-ACE-078 in clear
    Given the case is in U-82's scope
    Given the rwb-access contract mock returns the masking policy for RW-PHONECOL with DF-ACE-078 masked and DF-ACE-079 clear
    When U-82 opens the view
    Then the identity shows "XXXXXXXXX4821" from v_ace_customer.id_no_masked
    Then the phone shows "XXXXXX5678" from v_ace_contact.contact_value_masked
    Then the access log holds the read with user U-82, the field IDs and the masked flags

  Scenario: AC9 Case on hold (legacy RWB-E1-023 AC9)
    Given case RW-2026-000701 has status "ON_HOLD" for deviation X1 with prescription date 2028-03-15
    When U-81 opens the view
    Then the on hold banner shows MSG-P3-004 with "X1" and 2028-03-15

  Scenario: AC10 No documents and no contact history (legacy RWB-E1-023 AC10)
    Given case RW-2026-000703 has no documents and no contact history
    Given the rwb-source-data contract mock returns no interaction for case RW-2026-000703
    When its owner opens the view
    Then the Documents and Contact history sections each show MSG-P3-024
```

The Background, and every Given and Then line above, are copied unchanged from legacy RWB-E1-023. In the target the view facts reach rwb-case through the rwb-source-data contract, so `v_ace_account`, `v_ace_customer`, `v_ace_contact`, `v_ace_efs_action` and `v_ace_batch_status` are named as the system of record behind that contract, and rwb-case reads none of them directly (DP-01, DP-05). AC4, AC11 and AC12 of the legacy story are not owned here.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every section shows the ACE business date behind it: rwb-case takes the case dates from schema `rwb_case` and the accounts, parties, contact history and freshness dates from the rwb-source-data contract; no Workbench load date is used | REQ-RDF-009; VR-P3-001-1; DP-05 |
| BR2 | A section whose ACE batch is not COMPLETE for the latest business date shows the stale banner | MSG-P1-001; screens.txt Common states "Stale input"; the rwb-source-data freshness operation |
| BR3 | A personal field shows from the masked column unless the masking rule in force lets the role see it in clear; the identity number is never in clear because the customer contract exposes `id_no_masked` and `id_no_last4` only | REQ-ACA-005; CTL-11; DL26; DF-ACE-073, DF-ACE-074; DP-08 |
| BR4 | Every read of personal data is written to the access log of rwb-access; a read whose record cannot be written returns no data | REQ-ACA-006; legacy RWB-E1-039 BR2; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| BR5 | Only cases in the caller's scope open; others return 404 | CTL-09; REQ-ACA-009 |
| BR6 | The view has no edit control in Epic 1 | SCR-03 "E1 read only" |
| BR7 | The view loads in under 2 seconds with 50 documents | NFR-009 |
| BR8 | Account, customer, contact and collections history data are read live through the rwb-source-data contract by business key; the Workbench holds no copy and shows no Workbench load status | D-RCV-35 U1 and U4; ADR-010; DP-05 |
| BR9 | A case link with no view row shows the business key with empty values and is listed by REC-05; it is never deleted or rewritten | REC-05; Data Tier Map section 5 |
| BR10 | The contact history merges the ACE EFS entries and the Workbench interaction ledger in one time order, each row naming its source system; the ledger belongs to rwb-source-data | E1-068; interaction.source_system (DF-INT-013); DP-18 |
| BR11 | The read path carries no write operation: the OpenAPI document of RWB-P3-E1023-CON declares GET operations on the five read paths only | D-RCV-60; DP-19; ADR-020 |
| BR12 | rwb-case reads only schema `rwb_case`; another service's facts arrive through its published contract and never through a table read | D-RCV-60; DP-01; DP-11 |
| BR13 | The timeline page size and the interaction read operation come from the rwb-source-data contract; the value is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0695; ASM-1242) | D-RCV-60; DP-18 |

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It reads the case and shows its status, its stage, its timers and its hold flag. The events that move a case are published by other rwb-case stories on topic `rwb.case.events.v1`; this story consumes none of them.
