The field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v7 and the DF-ACE-* are the `recovery.v_ace_*` fields of Physical Schema v6, which is why they are named here and read by P1 only (DP-05). The one row this service writes is the AC-READ record and it holds identifiers, field IDs and masked flags, no value (BR12). The lists this page shows are reference data of rwb-case - LOV-ACTION-CODE, LOV-CONTACT-RESULT, LOV-CHANNEL, LOV-CONTACT-TYPE, LOV-PARTY-ROLE and LOV-DEVIATION - read at their version (DP-07; ASM-5250).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-deviation (S8); base `/api/recovery/deviation/v1` (DP-13). The five paths are the legacy paths of RWB-E1-023 section 12 with the base moved; every one is a read and none writes a table except the AC-READ record (DP-03).

| Method | Path | Shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}` | Case header: case no, product, status, stage, route, owner, queue, entry date, prescription date, deviation and legal hold flags, each with the business date of its answer | Case record R, scope applied | Not applicable; a read |
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}/accounts` | CaseAccount[]: account key, account code, days past due, total balance, `dataAsOf` | Case record R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}/parties` | CasePartyView[]: person key, party role, display name, customer no, identity masked or last four, category, contacts[] with type, key, value by role and `dataAsOf` | Case record R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}/contact-history` | ContactHistoryPage: the EFS entries and the ledger entries, one time order, each with its `sourceSystem`; query from, to, page, size | Case record R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}/documents` | DocumentPage: type, source, version, page and size; answered by P5 | Documents R, scope applied | Not applicable |

Every operation answers 400, 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404 with MSG-P4-003, 422 and 503 with MSG-P7-003, each in the platform error envelope; the exact shapes and status list are RWB-P3-E1023-CON's. The Ownership Map gives S8 two write operations and no read, so these five reads are recorded as a conflict (GAP-3082; ASM-5243).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|
| The case header, link, queue, parameter and list read of rwb-case; operation names Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3081; ASM-5247) | P3 rwb-case | The header fields, the two hold flags, the links, the queue, `caserecord.section.timeout.ms` and the six lists; baselined by RWB-P3-E1023-CON |
| The account, party and contact read of rwb-source-data; operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3081; ASM-5246) | P1 rwb-source-data | The accounts, the parties with their contact points and the identity mask, each with its `dataAsOf` and its freshness answer |
| The contact-history read of rwb-source-data (ledger owner, DP-18); operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3081; ASM-5246) | P1 rwb-source-data | The EFS entries and the ledger entries, one time order, each with its source system |
| The document list read of rwb-document; operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3081; ASM-5247) | P5 rwb-document | The document list of the case with its type, source and version |
| The authorise and mask read of rwb-access; operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3081; ASM-5249) | P4 rwb-access | The capability right, the scope and the masking rule of the caller, and the accept of the AC-READ record |

Every call is one hop with a 2 s budget and a breaker, and none retries inside the section; the case-record contract is the one C row of this slice (DP-11, ADR-020).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. A read publishes no business event: the AC-READ access record is written locally through the library of DP-03 and relayed by rwb-decision on the shared `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and this service's own topic `rwb.deviation.events.v1` carries the two events of its write stories, not this one (DP-14 applied as naming only; ASM-5245).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. Every section is read when the page is opened, so a stale answer is answered with its own stamp and MSG-P1-001 rather than kept fresh by a subscription (BR1, BR2). The deviation block reads its own table; no other service's event changes it.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The page is a synchronous read with no workflow, no activity and no timer; the `deviation` rows it reads are written by `DeviationWorkflow` on `rwb-deviation`, which belongs to the write stories of this service.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The Ownership Map gives S8 no job, and this story declares no Schedule, no Quartz row and no shared job table.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `deviation` | S8, `rwb_deviation` | Read only: the open codes, the raise facts, the contact stop, the handler, the return point and the state |
| `decision_record` | Platform library in `rwb_deviation` | Written: one AC-READ record per read, before the answer (DP-03) |

`recovery_case`, `case_account`, `case_party`, `queue`, `timer`, `interaction`, `document`, `rule_row` and every `v_ace_*` view are other owners' and are named only; no foreign key leaves `rwb_deviation` and `deviation` carries no column of another service's fact (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-case case-record fake (`RWB-P3-E1023-CON`) | The header of a synthetic case with its queue, owner, status, entry and prescription dates, its links, its parameters and its six lists; an out-of-scope team; a case on hold; a link with no answer | AC1, AC2, AC5, AC9, AC12 |
| rwb-source-data data-product fake | Accounts, parties with contacts and the contact history with fresh stamps; a stale stamp; an account with no answer; an empty contact history | AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC10, AC11, AC12 |
| rwb-document list fake | 50 documents; an empty list; no answer inside 3 s | AC1, AC6, AC10 |
| rwb-access authorise and mask fake | A right and a scope; a refusal; a masking rule per role; the accept of the AC-READ record | AC5, AC8, TC-E1-023-11 |
| Local decision-record stub (`RWB-PLT-E1027-CON`) | A healthy chain; a rejected AC-READ write | AC7 |
| gateway-bff composite route fake | The assembled SCR-03 for a synthetic case | AC1 to AC12 |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 5 provided, 5 consumed | The five reads on `/api/recovery/deviation/v1`; the rwb-case, rwb-source-data (two), rwb-document and rwb-access calls; one hop, 2 s, 3 s for the document section |
| Kafka | None | No business event published or consumed; the AC-READ record rides the library's `rwb.decision-record.v1` |
| Temporal | None | A synchronous read; no workflow, activity or Schedule |
| File | None | No file is read, built or delivered by this story |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** The five read handlers on the target base, `CaseRecordViewGuard`, `CaseRecordViewService`, `CaseSectionReader`, `DeviationBlockReader`, `MaskingApplier` with the AC-READ writer, the six section components with their badges and banners, and the failure, access and boundary tests.

**Pattern application** (§R5.5)

| DP | Legacy marker | Pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>`, "recovery schema" | Own schema `rwb_deviation`; no other service's table is read | None |
| DP-02 | `recovery_svc` login | One login per service | None |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H `RWB-PLT-E1027-CON` (not in the empty build row, ASM-5244) |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | ACE facts through rwb-source-data's contract | None |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H `RWB-PLT-E1042-CON`; C `RWB-P3-E1042-CON` |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H `RWB-PLT-E1043-CON`; C `RWB-P3-E1043-CON` |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library | H `RWB-PLT-E1037-CON`; C `RWB-P4-E1037-CON` |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock, one hop, 2 s | C from the legacy dependency (`RWB-P3-E1023-CON`) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/deviation/v1` | None |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topics | Topic `rwb.deviation.events.v1`; naming library | H `RWB-PLT-E1047-CON` (naming only, ASM-5245) |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway in `rwb_deviation` | H `RWB-PLT-E1044-CON` |
| DP-18 | Interaction ledger | Ledger owned by rwb-source-data | None |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H `RWB-PLT-N001-CON` |

**Build steps.** (1) Wire the guard and the five read handlers on the target base. (2) Read the header, links, queue, parameters and lists from rwb-case on its contract, the accounts, parties and contact history from rwb-source-data with their stamps and freshness answers, the documents from rwb-document, and the deviation block from `deviation`. (3) Apply the masks and the scope and write the AC-READ record before the answer. (4) Build the six section components with their badges and the stale, on hold and empty banners. (5) Prove AC1 to AC12, the access refusal, the forced record failure and the boundary test; the section timeout, the masks and the lists are parameters and reference data (DP-06, DP-07; ASM-5250).

**Done when.** AC1 to AC12 pass at component and contract level on the fakes, NFR-009 holds in SIT, the boundary test shows no `v_ace_*` read and no `rwb_case` statement, and a refused AC-READ write returns 503 with MSG-P7-003 and no data.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-001 | A section's answer is not fresh for the latest business date (X1) | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |
| MSG-P3-004 | The case is on hold (X6) | This case is on hold for {deviation}. The prescription date is still {date}. |
| MSG-P3-024 | A section has nothing to show (X7) | Nothing is recorded in {section} yet. |
| MSG-P3-023 | A section cannot be shown (X3) | {section} cannot be shown now. The rest of the case is shown. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks the right (X8) | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The case is outside the scope (X2) | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The AC-READ record cannot be written (X4) | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The wording is the legacy and FSD wording, copied unchanged; no message is reworded and none is added. The legacy "decision log store" of MSG-P7-003 is read here as the local AC-READ record, which is why the message is not reworded (DP-03; ASM-5245).

##### 15. Screens and states

| Screen | States | What this story answers |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-03 Case record | Loading: skeleton rows per section. Read only: fields without edit controls; the header, the deviation block and five sections, each with the business date of its answer. On hold: the banner with the code and the prescription date. Stale input: MSG-P1-001 above the section. Error: MSG-P3-023 in the section that failed, and MSG-P3-024 in an empty one | The five reads of section 12.1 and the deviation block behind the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) |

The screen shows no Workbench load, job or file status, and no edit control (BR6). The composite route also calls rwb-case for the case list and the timers of SCR-02 and SCR-04; this story fixes only its own answers (ASM-5243).

The thirteen ids are the legacy cases of RWB-E1-023, kept in their legacy order; the two that read two services at once are carried at Contract level and their end-to-end half belongs to the wave 1 harness. The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same id.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the section timeout, the masks, the labels and the six lists are parameters and reference data read at their version (DP-06, DP-07).
- No personal data in `rwb_deviation`, the AC-READ record, a log, a screen cache or a prompt; test parties are synthetic and the application log holds case numbers only.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: no `v_ace_*` view, no ACE table and no other service's schema is read here, and a statement that tries is refused by the grant and fails the boundary test (DP-01, DP-02, DP-05).
- The page holds no copy of a source record; the identity number is masked inside the P1 answer and the contact values are masked at the API by role (BR3, BR8).
- A personal field is never shown when the AC-READ record cannot be written (BR4).
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; this story adds no second base and no new topic (DP-13, DP-14).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: integration slice of RWB-E1-023 for RWB-ITG-W1. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **QA integration engineer**, I want **the end-to-end proof of the RWB-E1-023 read-only case record view composed by gateway-bff from rwb-case (P3), rwb-source-data (P1), rwb-document (P5), rwb-access (P4) and rwb-deviation (S8)**, so that **the freshness stamp of every section, the no-copy boundary, a case link with no ACE row, the masking position, the access record, the merged contact history and the degraded document section are proved on the real wave 1 services before the wave exits**.

##### 2. Business rationale

RWB-E1-023 puts one read-only screen per case in front of the case owner: case number, accounts and arrears, parties and contacts, contact history, documents, each section carrying the ACE business date behind it. Under the legacy design the screen read `v_ace_account`, `v_ace_customer`, `v_ace_contact` and `v_ace_efs_action` inside the P3 module, merged the EFS entries with the Workbench interaction ledger in one time order, masked each personal field by the caller's role and wrote one AC-READ access record per open. The component copy of that behaviour sits in RWB-P3-E1023-APP, which owns the legacy criteria AC1, AC2, AC3, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9 and AC10 against the published contracts of the services it needs.

This integration story owns the three criteria that no single service can prove: AC4 (a section whose ACE batch is not complete shows its earlier business date and the stale banner, with no Workbench load date anywhere), AC11 (the Accounts section follows the newest ACE batch and no Workbench table holds the earlier balance) and AC12 (an `account_key` on a case link with no view row shows with empty values, the rest of the case still shows, and the key is listed for the data steward and the ACE team). Each of the three is a statement about two owners at once: the staleness and the freshness stamp are facts about the P1 data product, the no-copy rule is a fact about the boundary between P1 and P3, and the missing view row is found by the P1 reconciliation while the link that must not be invented is the P3 case link. Asserted inside one service, each of them passes while the other side is wrong.

The target moves the source of the facts, never the behaviour. Only rwb-source-data reads the ACE views (DP-05, DP-01), so account, customer, contact and EFS facts and the business date of each data product reach the screen through the P1 contract and its freshness read. The interaction ledger belongs to rwb-source-data under the default ruling (DP-18), so the contact history is the P1 ledger merged with the case entries of rwb-case in one time order, each row naming its own source system. Documents belong to rwb-document and are read on the P5 contract. The masking rule and the access log belong to rwb-access (DP-08), so the question of which field is clear is answered by P4 and the personal value itself never leaves the owner. The screen is composed by gateway-bff with the owner calls in parallel, one hop each, inside the 2 s budget and with a breaker per service (DP-19, DP-11), and the paths become `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` (DP-13). The section budget, the labels and the list values are data read through the P3 parameter and reference-data contracts (DP-06, DP-07), the topic names follow `rwb.<short>.events.v1` (DP-14), each schema is migrated by its own service (DP-15), and each service signs in with its own login (DP-02).

Three points are not fixed by the sources and are carried as one gap and one assumption. The ownership map holds `POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations` and `PATCH /deviations/{deviationId}` for rwb-deviation but no read of the deviations of a case, and Arch v5 puts rwb-deviation in wave 2 while this wave 1 story lists RWB-S8-E1023-APP as an integration dependency, so the read path of AC18 is read from Arch v5 slides 15 and 41 and the service is assumed present in SIT. The fixture composition of the run is the RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG set and is not itemised in any source. Both are recorded in GAP-0348 and ASM-0442. Release 30 November 2026 stays tentative, and a date is never a condition of this story.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P3-E1023-APP is done: the case record reads, the section composition, the scope check, the masking call and the refusal when the access record cannot be written are in SIT on rwb-case.
- RWB-P1-E1069-APP is done: the ACE view contract, the account, customer, contact and EFS facts by business key, and the freshness stamp of each data product are published on base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`.
- RWB-P1-E1068-APP is done: the interaction ledger is readable by case through the P1 contract, with `occurred_at`, `channel`, `contact_result` and `source_system`.
- RWB-P5-E1024-APP is done: the documents of a case are readable through the rwb-document contract on base `/api/recovery/document/v1`.
- RWB-P4-E1023-APP is done: the masking rules by role are in force and name the view field IDs, and the answer carries the clear or masked position of each field.
- RWB-P4-E1039-APP is done: the access log records one AC-READ entry per read with the field IDs and their masked flags, and the log is readable on `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log`.
- RWB-S8-E1023-APP is done: the deviation of a case and its prescription date are readable through the rwb-deviation contract for AC18.
- The published contracts of P1, P3, P4, P5 and S8 are versioned in the registry, and the run consumes only those contracts.
- The harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG is available with its synthetic accounts, parties, contacts, case links, documents, ledger entries, batch rows and masking rules.
- SIT is in place with gateway-bff in front of every owner base, the namespace `rwb-recovery`, the topic `rwb.source-data.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics, and the schema registry.
- rwb-deviation is a wave 2 service in Arch v5 slide 41 and this story lists it as an integration dependency; the run therefore needs its contract in SIT. That reading is the assumption ASM-0442 and the point is in GAP-0348.
- No production data is read, copied or connected to; every account, person, contact value, case number and document used by the run is synthetic.
- The release date 30 November 2026 is tentative and is copied unchanged.

##### 4. Flow

1. QA integration engineer: seeds the synthetic set for case RW-2026-000701 through the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG — account A-7001 at 97 days past due with THB 206,175.00 and data as of 2026-12-02, person P-7001 with the masked identity and one mobile contact, the link to A-7010 with no view row, 50 documents, 120 ledger entries, and the batch rows for 2026-12-02 and 2026-12-03; no service schema is opened and no production row is used.
2. Harness: signs in through gateway-bff as U-81 holding RW-CASEOWN with Case record R and scope Own, and reads `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/permissions` for the masking position of the role.
3. Harness: opens SCR-03 for RW-2026-000701 through the gateway-bff composite route and records the call set and the elapsed time of each owner call.
4. Gateway-bff: calls the P3 header read, the P3 accounts read, the P3 parties read, the P1 interactions read, the P5 documents read, the P1 freshness read and the S8 deviation read in parallel, one hop each, inside the 2 s budget and with the breaker of each owner.
5. Harness: asserts the header (case number, product, status "IN_PROGRESS", stage, route, owner U-81, queue "TDR-BKK-CO", entry date, prescription date, deviation and hold flags) and the five sections, each with the business date of its own data product read from the P1 freshness contract.
6. Harness: asserts the Accounts section for A-7001 at 97 days past due and THB 206,175.00 with business date 2026-12-02, and that no response holds a load date, a job status or a batch run of a service.
7. Harness, AC4: sets the batch state so that no COMPLETED ALS row exists for 2026-12-03, opens the view and asserts that the Accounts section keeps business date 2026-12-02, that the stale banner shows MSG-P1-001 for "DP01 Account and arrears" with date 2026-12-02, and that no Workbench load or job status shows.
8. Harness, AC11: moves the ALS batch of 2026-12-03 to THB 210,000.00 for A-7001, opens the view again and asserts that the Accounts section shows THB 210,000.00 with business date 2026-12-03, and that no service holds the earlier balance for the case: the case read, the accounts read and the P1 contract are the only sources and none of them returns 206,175.00 for that date.
9. Harness, AC12: reads the case link A-7010 with no view row, opens the view and asserts that the Accounts section shows A-7010 with empty balance and days past due, that the other four sections show, and that the P1 reconciliation output lists A-7010 for the data steward and the ACE team.
10. Harness: asserts the contact history as one time order of 120 entries with the source system on each row and no duplicate, the masking outcome for U-82 under a clear rule and under no clear rule, the one AC-READ record in the P4 access log with the field IDs and their masked flags, the refused read when that record cannot be written, the deviation flags of AC18 without a copy in the P3 response, the document-hub timeout path, and the refusal of a role without Case record R at the first owner call.
11. Harness: proves from the call set of the run that no service schema and no view was opened, that no call passed through another service, and that no fake stood in for a P1, P3, P4, P5 or S8 contract; then writes the evidence report, removes the synthetic set and restores the batch state.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The ACE batch behind a section is not complete for the latest business date | The section shows with its own business date and the stale banner | MSG-P1-001 | AC4 |
| X2 | The case is outside the caller's scope | The scope answer of the P4 contract refuses the case and the screen returns 404 with nothing shown | MSG-P4-003 | TC-E1-023-05-ITG, regression for RWB-P3-E1023-APP |
| X3 | The document hub does not answer inside the 2 s budget | The Documents section shows the section message, the breaker opens for that owner, and the other sections show | MSG-P3-023 | AC19 |
| X4 | The access record cannot be written | The authorise call is refused, the read returns no case data and no personal field shows | MSG-P7-003 | AC15 |
| X5 | The role may not see a personal field in clear | The field shows from the masked field of the owner and the access record carries the masked flag | None | AC16 |
| X6 | The case is on hold | The on-hold banner shows the deviation and the prescription date read from the S8 contract | MSG-P3-004 | AC18 |
| X7 | The case has no documents and no contact history | Each section shows its empty sentence | MSG-P3-024 | TC-E1-023-10-ITG, regression for RWB-P3-E1023-APP |
| X8 | A role without Case record R opens the view | The first owner call, the P4 authorise check, refuses with 403 and no other owner is called | MSG-P4-002 | AC20 |
| X9 | A case link holds an `account_key` that the view does not return | The Accounts row shows the key with empty values, REC-05 lists it, and the rest of the case shows | None | AC12 |
| X10 | A consumed call exceeds the 2 s budget or returns a server error | The call is retried once under the suite policy, the breaker of that owner is recorded, and no assertion is made on data that was not read | None | AC13 |
| X11 | A consumed contract drifts from the published one, or the synthetic set does not match the run | The preflight fails on the contract test or on the fixture check and the run stops before any assertion; no fake is put in place of a service contract | None | AC13, section 17 |

X1, X3, X4, X5, X6 and X9 are the exception paths of the legacy story read on the wave 1 services; X2, X7 and X8 are the legacy paths whose criteria belong to RWB-P3-E1023-APP and are run here as regression evidence; X10 and X11 are the suite's own failure modes, so that a timeout never becomes a pass.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | The suite is a module of its own and reuses the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG; it needs the seven integration dependencies and the published contracts of P1, P3, P4, P5 and S8, not their source code, and it owns no schema and no table |
| Negotiable | The fixture sizes, the poll interval, the retry of the suite and the report layout are configuration; the criteria, the message IDs, the keys and the values are fixed by the legacy story |
| Valuable | Proves across services what no single service can prove: the freshness stamp of each section, the no-copy boundary, the missing view row, the masking position, the access record, the merged contact history and the degraded section |
| Estimable | One suite module, one fixture pack, eight probes, one composed-route assertion and one evidence report |
| Small | Eleven scenarios over five services, one composed route and one topic, with no service code and no schema change |
| Testable | Every criterion asserts a contract response, a record, a message, a status or the absence of a value, and every value is synthetic |

**Target reading.** In the monolith the P3 module reads `recovery.v_ace_*` itself, merges the EFS rows with its own ledger and writes the access event from inside the case module. In the target only rwb-source-data reads the views and serves the account, customer, contact and EFS facts and the business date of each data product (DP-05, DP-01), the interaction ledger is P1's (DP-18), the documents are P5's, the masking rule and the access log are P4's (DP-08), the screen is composed by gateway-bff with the owner calls in parallel and a breaker per owner (DP-19, DP-11), and every path moves to `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` (DP-13). `v_ace_batch_status` and `v_ace_account.data_as_of` of AC4, the earlier balance of AC11 and the missing row of AC12 are therefore asserted through the P1 freshness read and the P1 reconciliation output, never by opening a view; the deviation of AC18 is read from the S8 contract and never copied into rwb-case. No value is invented and no service table is read (GAP-0348; ASM-0442).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every section shows the business date of the data product behind it, read from the P1 freshness contract; no Workbench load date is used | REQ-RDF-009; VR-P3-001-1; DP-05 |
| BR2 | A section whose data product is not complete for the latest business date shows the stale banner | MSG-P1-001; screens.txt Common states "Stale input"; the P1 freshness stamp |
| BR3 | A personal field shows in clear only when the masking rule in force lets the caller's role see it; the identity number is never in clear because the owner exposes the masked identity and the last four digits only | REQ-ACA-005; CTL-11; DL26; DF-ACE-073, DF-ACE-074 |
| BR4 | Every read of personal data writes one AC-READ record with the field IDs and their masked flags; a read whose record cannot be written returns no data | REQ-ACA-006; RWB-E1-039 BR2; DP-08 |
| BR5 | Only cases in the caller's scope open; others return 404, and the refusal is the answer of the P4 authorise contract | CTL-09; REQ-ACA-009 |
| BR6 | The view has no edit control in Epic 1 | SCR-03 "E1 read only" |
| BR7 | The view loads in under 2 seconds with 50 documents | NFR-009 |
| BR8 | Account, customer, contact and collections history data are read live by business key through the owner's contract; no service holds a copy and no service shows its own load status | D-RCV-35 U1 and U4; ADR-010; DP-01; DP-05 |
| BR9 | A case link with no view row shows the business key with empty values and is listed by REC-05; it is never deleted or rewritten | REC-05; Data Tier Map section 5 |
| BR10 | The contact history merges the P1 ledger and the P3 case entries in one time order, each row naming its source system | E1-068; interaction.source_system (DF-INT-013); DP-18 |
| BR11 | The screen is composed by gateway-bff with one hop per owner, the owner calls in parallel, a 2 s budget and a breaker per owner; no owner calls another owner for this screen | ADR-020; DP-11; DP-19; Arch v5 slide 20 |
| BR12 | The deviation and hold flags of the header and the on-hold banner are read from the S8 contract; rwb-case keeps the flag, never a copy of the deviation or its prescription date | Arch v5 slide 15; DP-01 |
| BR13 | The section budget, the labels and the list values on the screen are data read through the P3 parameter and reference-data contracts, never code | DP-06; DP-07; Principle 1 |
| BR14 | Topic names follow `rwb.<short>.events.v1` and every service signs in with its own login; there is no shared login and no legacy topic prefix | DP-14; DP-02; Arch v5 slide 41 |
| BR15 | Each service migrates its own schema on its own Flyway sequence; the suite owns no schema and runs no migration | DP-15; ADR-021 |
| BR16 | A section that fails shows its own message and the rest of the case shows; a failure is never turned into a blank screen and never into a pass | SCR-03 Error; MSG-P3-023 |
| BR17 | No personal data in the suite's fixtures, events, logs or report: account keys, person keys, case numbers, document IDs, field IDs and business dates only, and the clear contact value of AC16 is read from the owner inside the run only | Guardrail of RWB-E1-023; Arch v5 slide 42 notes |
| BR18 | No service schema is opened by the suite and no published service contract is faked; a run that needs either fails the preflight | DP-01; section 17 |

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story changes no case status and no record; it reads the case and shows its status.

The states the run observes across the services:

| Item | States |
|---|---|
| Screen section | Loading (skeleton rows), Shown with its business date, Stale (MSG-P1-001 above the section), Section message (MSG-P3-023 or MSG-P3-024) |
| Case status as read | "IN_PROGRESS", "ON_HOLD" with the deviation and the prescription date from the S8 contract |
| Access record | Written (AC-READ with the field IDs and masked flags), Refused (no data returned, MSG-P7-003) |
| Masking position of a field | Clear (the rule in force allows the role), Masked (the masked field of the owner) |
| Suite run | Not started, running, passed, failed with the failing test case named |

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The suite provides no REST operation. The reserved P2 names - the base `/api/recovery/integration/v1`, the topic `rwb.integration.events.v1`, the queue `rwb-integration` and the schema `rwb_integration` - are unused, and no `rwb_integration` table is written.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use | Budget |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | Header of the case: case number, product, status, stage, route, owner, queue, entry date, prescription date, deviation and hold flags; the case entries of the contact history | 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/accounts` | P3 rwb-case | Accounts section: `account_key`, `is_primary` and the account facts the owner reads from P1 by business key; AC2, AC11, AC12 | 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/parties` | P3 rwb-case | Parties section: `person_key`, `party_role` and the contacts by role; AC3 | 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions` | P1 rwb-source-data (owner per the Ownership Map; API Specification v4 lists x-module P3 and the ruling puts the ledger in P1, ASM-0038) | The ledger half of the contact history with `occurred_at`, `channel`, `contact_result` and `source_system`; AC17 | 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents` | P5 rwb-document | Documents section and its section message when the owner does not answer; AC19 | 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness` | P1 rwb-source-data | The business date of every section and the stale banner; AC4, AC11, AC14 | 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/deviation/v1/deviations?caseId={caseId}` | S8 rwb-deviation | The deviation and the prescription date behind the header and the on-hold banner; AC18 | 2 s |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | Case record R and the scope at the first owner call, and the refusal of a role without the right; AC20 | 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/me/permissions` | P4 rwb-access | The masking position of the caller's role for the fields of the view; AC16 | 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log` | P4 rwb-access | The one AC-READ record of the open with the field IDs and their masked flags; AC15 | 2 s |

Every call is one hop to the owning service on its own base (DP-11, DP-13) with the 2 s client budget behind gateway-bff; the suite calls no service through another service. The deviation read follows Arch v5 slide 15 (`GET /deviations`) and the S8 base of slide 41, because the ownership map carries only the POST and PATCH rows for the resource (GAP-0348; ASM-0442).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The suite publishes no business event.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | What the suite asserts |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.source-data.AceDataLate.v1` | `rwb.source-data.events.v1` | P1 rwb-source-data | No late event is published for a section whose freshness stamp reads complete, so the banner of AC4 and the stamp of AC14 agree; CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, business date and data product code, no personal data field |

The suite asserts no other event: every other fact it proves is a synchronous answer of an owner's contract or a record of the P4 access log, and the events of the same behaviour are asserted by the owning service stories RWB-P3-E1023-APP, RWB-P5-E1024-APP and RWB-S8-E1023-APP.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The view is a REST composition and this story starts no workflow, observes no workflow and asserts no activity; the case workflow of rwb-case is not on the read path of SCR-03.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The suite starts no schedule and moves no clock.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The suite owns no table and never reads another service's schema (DP-01). Every fact it asserts is read through a contract of 12.2 or 12.4.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

None for a service contract. The only stubs are external to the nineteen services:

| Stub | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Synthetic party, account and contact fixture (RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG) | Stands in for the ACE ingestion and the ACE rows behind the P1 contract, outside the nineteen services |

No published service contract is faked: the run needs the real P1, P3, P4, P5 and S8 services on their published contracts, and a run that needs a fake for any of them fails the preflight.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** One suite module that reuses the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG: a fixture pack for the synthetic case, accounts, parties, contacts, documents, ledger entries, batch rows and masking rules; a batch-state control; eight probes; a composed-route assertion; and an evidence report with one verdict per test case. No service code and no schema change.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| SuiteRunner | Test harness | Preflight against the published contracts and the fixture set, run order, report and exit code |
| FixtureDriver | Test harness | Seeds and removes the synthetic case RW-2026-000701, A-7001, A-7010, P-7001, the 50 documents, the 120 ledger entries, the batch rows for 2026-12-02 and 2026-12-03 and the masking rules |
| CompositeRouteProbe | Test harness | Opens SCR-03 through gateway-bff, records the call set and the elapsed time of each owner call, and proves the parallel composition and the one-hop rule of AC13 |
| AccountsProbe | Test harness | The Accounts section of AC2, AC11 and AC12 on A-7001 and A-7010 through the P1 and P3 contracts |
| FreshnessProbe | Test harness | The business date of every section from the P1 freshness read, the stale banner of AC4, the absent Workbench load date and the AceDataLate agreement of AC14 |
| MissingKeyProbe | Test harness | Takes A-7010 out of the view and reads the P1 reconciliation output for the REC-05 list of AC12 |
| MaskingProbe | Test harness | The P4 masking position and the clear and masked outcomes of AC16, including the assertion that the clear value never leaves the owner |
| AccessLogProbe | Test harness | The one AC-READ record of AC15 and the refused path, and the refusal of AC20 at the first owner call |
| ContactHistoryProbe | Test harness | The merged time order of AC17, the source system on each row and the absence of a duplicate |
| DeviationProbe | Test harness | The header flags and the on-hold banner of AC18 from the S8 contract, and the absence of a copy in the P3 response |
| DocumentHubProbe | Test harness | The timeout, the breaker and the section message of AC19 |
| ReportWriter | Test harness | One row per test case with its evidence and elapsed time, and the cleanup record |

**Database.** None of its own. The suite writes no service table and no schema object, and it holds no client for a service schema.

**Configuration and reference data**

- The SIT endpoints of P1, P3, P4, P5 and S8 behind gateway-bff, the topic name, the schema-registry address and the namespace `rwb-recovery`, all as configuration.
- The synthetic keys and values of the W1J01 set, the business dates 2026-12-02 and 2026-12-03, and the case number RW-2026-000701.
- The section budget, the labels and the list values read through the P3 parameter and reference-data contracts (DP-06, DP-07), including LOV-ACTION-CODE, LOV-CONTACT-RESULT, LOV-CHANNEL, LOV-CONTACT-TYPE and LOV-PARTY-ROLE; the legacy `caserecord.section.timeout.ms` gives way to the 2 s client budget of DP-11 and is read, not written, where the screen still needs it.
- The masking rules of RW-CASEOWN and RW-PHONECOL, read through the P4 contract and never written in the suite code.
- The 2 s client budget, the retry of the suite and the poll interval.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-02 | `recovery_svc` login | One login per service | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-18 | Interaction ledger | Ledger owned by rwb-source-data (default ruling) | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-01, DP-05 and DP-18 carry the source facts and the ledger behind the owners; DP-08 carries the authorise answer and the masking position; DP-11 and DP-19 carry the composed route and the 2 s budget; DP-13 and DP-14 carry the base and the topic names; DP-03 applies to the refused read, whose refusal is recorded by the owner in its local decision record and collected in the central ledger, and the suite asserts it through the P4 access log rather than through a table; DP-06 and DP-07 carry the section budget, the labels and the list values; DP-02 and DP-15 keep one login and one migration sequence per service. The H and C entries of the table belong to the service, platform and operations stories that own them: this ITG story carries no H, C or X entry of its own, and an integration story never becomes a build dependency of another story (Template and Rules §R5.4, §R5.7). The I list names the seven services whose behaviour the run exercises.

**Fixtures**

| Fixture | Content | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| Case set | Case RW-2026-000701 with status "IN_PROGRESS", queue "TDR-BKK-CO", owner U-81, entry date 2026-11-30 and 2 accounts, seeded through the W1J01 set | AC13 to AC20 |
| Account facts | A-7001 at 97 days past due with THB 206,175.00 and data as of 2026-12-02; the 2026-12-03 batch at THB 210,000.00 | AC11, AC14 |
| Missing key | The link to A-7010 with no row in the account view | AC12 |
| Party and contact facts | P-7001 with the masked identity XXXXXXXXX4821 and one mobile, its clear form 0812345678 and its masked form XXXXXX5678 | AC16 |
| Documents and ledger | 50 documents on the case and 120 ledger entries with their source systems | AC13, AC17 |
| Batch state | The 2026-12-02 rows complete for ALS, SCBPDM and EFS, and no COMPLETED ALS row for 2026-12-03 | AC4, AC11, AC14 |
| Deviation | Deviation X1 on the case with prescription date 2028-03-15 | AC18 |
| Masking rules | The rule set of RW-CASEOWN and RW-PHONECOL, with and without the clear position for DF-ACE-078 | AC15, AC16 |

**Build steps**

1. Create the suite module next to harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG and wire it to the SIT endpoints, the topic and the namespace, with the contract preflight that fails on any drift.
2. Build FixtureDriver and the fixture pack; assert that the case, its accounts, its parties, its documents and its ledger entries read back through the owners before any assertion is made.
3. Build CompositeRouteProbe and prove the parallel composition, the one-hop rule and the 2 s budget of AC13 from the recorded call set.
4. Build AccountsProbe and FreshnessProbe; assert A-7001 at 97 days past due with THB 206,175.00 and business date 2026-12-02, the absent Workbench load date, and the stale banner of AC4.
5. Build the AC11 step: move the batch, re-read the case, assert THB 210,000.00 with business date 2026-12-03 and prove that no response of the run returns the earlier balance.
6. Build MissingKeyProbe for AC12 and read the P1 reconciliation output for the REC-05 list.
7. Build MaskingProbe and AccessLogProbe; assert the clear and masked outcomes of AC16, the one AC-READ record of AC15 and the refused read of the same scenario, and the refusal of AC20 at the first owner call.
8. Build ContactHistoryProbe and DeviationProbe; assert the merged time order of AC17 and the S8 flags of AC18 with no copy in the P3 response.
9. Build DocumentHubProbe for AC19, ReportWriter and the cleanup; run the whole suite twice to prove that a repeated open adds no second AC-READ record and no duplicate entry.

**Done when.** The thirteen test cases of section 16 pass on the real services in SIT, the three criteria this story owns (AC4, AC11, AC12) and the eight cross-service criteria (AC13 to AC20) are signed off against the contracts, the access log holds exactly one AC-READ record per open of the run, no service table and no view was opened, the synthetic set is removed, and the evidence report names every criterion with its observable.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-001 | A section's data product is not complete for the latest business date | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |
| MSG-P3-004 | Case on hold | This case is on hold for {deviation}. The prescription date is still {date}. |
| MSG-P3-024 | A section has nothing to show | Nothing is recorded in {section} yet. |
| MSG-P3-023 | A section cannot be shown | {section} cannot be shown now. The rest of the case is shown. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | Case outside the scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The access record cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The seven texts are copied unchanged from RWB-E1-023 and this story adds no message ID. The messages are rendered by the owning service and passed through gateway-bff unchanged, so the suite asserts the ID and the text on the composed response.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-03 Case record, composed by gateway-bff (DP-19) from the P3, P1, P5 and S8 reads. Loading: skeleton rows per section. Read only: fields without edit controls; the header and the five sections, each with the business date of its own data product read from the P1 freshness contract. On hold: the banner with the deviation and the prescription date from the S8 contract. Stale input: MSG-P1-001 above the section whose data product is not complete. Error: MSG-P3-023 in the section that failed, with the breaker of that owner open for the next call. The screen shows no Workbench load, job or file status, and no section shows a copy of a record it does not own.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No copy of an ACE record in any Workbench table, cache or screen state: the account, customer, contact and collection facts are read by the owner on every open and are held nowhere (DP-01, DP-05).
- No clear personal value in a cache or a log: the identity number is shown only in its masked form from the owner, and the clear contact value of AC16 exists inside the run only and is asserted absent from every response, cache and log.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or the `v_ace_*` views, and those views only through rwb-source-data; the suite ships with no client for a service schema and no client for a view.
- The identity number is masked in the view itself, so no role and no path can return it in clear.
- No business value in code: the section budget, the labels, the list values and the masking rules are read through the P3 and P4 contracts.
- No personal data in the suite's fixtures, topic payloads, logs or report: keys, case numbers, document IDs, field IDs and business dates only.
- Synthetic data only: the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG loads every account, person, contact, document and batch row, and the run refuses any environment that is not SIT.
- One hop and a 2 s budget on every call, with a breaker per owner and no service called through another service (ADR-020; DP-11; DP-19).
- Clean-up in the same run: the synthetic set and the moved batch state are removed or restored, and the report records what was cleaned.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the store and index moved into `rwb-document` with the schema `rwb_document`, the topic `rwb.document.events.v1`, the REST base `/api/recovery/document/v1` and the `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` template of the target service. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **litigation officer (RW-LITOFF)**, I want **every document stored against its case with its type, date, source and extracted fields, legal types held in a write-once container, and every version kept**, so that **I find a document by case ID, type and date, and a legal document cannot be changed after it is stored**.

Inside `rwb-document` this is the store and index capability of the document service:

- Service `rwb-document`, schema `rwb_document`, REST base `/api/recovery/document/v1`, topic `rwb.document.events.v1` with event names `rwb.document.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document`.
- The store is the only writer of the document tables. It writes `document`, `document_field` and the document-hub parameter rows, reads the document type table of RWB-P5-E1025-APP, and writes the decision record (DP-03) and the outbox row (DP-09) in the same transaction as the document row.
- The file goes to Azure Blob with WORM through the platform storage product RWB-PLT-TE012-APP (the X dependency), never through a local file write: containers `rwb-docs` (standard), `rwb-docs-legal` (write-once) and `rwb-quarantine` (intake holds), reached by managed identity at `{container}/{caseId}/{documentId}/v1`. This service never overwrites a blob; every version is a new blob path. The storage account and the immutability policy of the containers are RWB-PLT-TE012-APP's and are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1031; ASM-1979).
- The case is read through the `GET /cases/{caseId}` contract of `rwb-case` (RWB-P3-E1018-CON, a C dependency, DP-11, one hop, 2 s timeout), never from a case table of another service and never from a `rwb_case` copy.
- The decision is recorded through the local decision-record library of DP-03 (H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON; the central ledger contract of `rwb-decision` is RWB-P7-E1027-CON) in the same transaction as the document row and the outbox row, with decision code DOCATT and final call STORED; a failed record means nothing is stored (MSG-P7-003, R-UNI-39).
- Parameters `INTAKE_ALLOWED_TYPES` and `INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB` are read through the parameters contract and client library of `rwb-case` (DP-06, H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, C RWB-P3-E1042-CON). The document-hub rows they resolve to live in `document_hub_parameter` in `rwb_document`, which the Ownership Map gives to P5.
- Reference lists LOV-RETENTION, LOV-REVIEW, LOV-DOC-TYPE and LOV-DOC-SOURCE are read through the reference-data contract of `rwb-case` (DP-07, H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, C RWB-P3-E1043-CON); no list value is typed in code.
- The database login is one per service (DP-02). Its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1030; ASM-1978); this story uses the phrase "the rwb-document login (DP-02)" and never a shared login.

The legacy behaviour is carried unchanged in intent and values: the same user story, rationale, preconditions, flow, exception paths, business rules, messages, authority, data fields, twelve acceptance criteria and fourteen test cases, adapted to the target service's schema, topic, API base and workflow template.

##### 2. Business rationale

Recovery documents are held today in folders, shared drives and with couriers; originals go missing and evidence is rebuilt for each audit (FSD P5 A1.3). This story builds the store and the index that every other document story writes to: one document record in the Workbench document hub per file, the file in blob storage, legal types write-once (DT06, ADR-007, control CTL-12). It meets REQ-DCM-001, REQ-DCM-002, REQ-DCM-003 and REQ-DCM-008. The module measure is fields extracted without review (FSD P5 A2.1.1), which can only be counted once every document is indexed against its case.

The realignment changes the mechanics, not the business rule:

1. One schema, one topic, one API base: `rwb_document`, `rwb.document.events.v1` and `/api/recovery/document/v1` (DP-01, DP-13). No table of another service is read and no monolith table name survives.
2. The case arrives through the `rwb-case` contract `GET /cases/{caseId}` with a mock and a 2 s timeout (DP-11), so the store builds against a published shape and never against a `rwb_case` table.
3. The decision log write becomes the local decision-record library of DP-03, written in the same transaction as the row and the outbox row and published on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; `rwb-decision` collects it into the central ledger.
4. The parameters come from the parameters contract and client library of `rwb-case` (DP-06); the document-hub parameter rows themselves stay in `rwb_document`, which is P5's own store for them. The reference lists come from the reference-data contract (DP-07).
5. The document type table of RWB-P5-E1025-APP is a P5 table read locally in the version in force (`valid_from` and `valid_to`), with no contract hop: the write-once flag, the retention class and the field list of a type are never taken from the caller.
6. The retry of a pending copy becomes the `copyPending` activity of the `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` template of the workflow kit (DP-10), not a Quartz job step.
7. The file is written to Blob WORM through the platform storage product RWB-PLT-TE012-APP; this service holds the reference and the hash, never a copy of the bytes in its own store.
8. The store reads reach the case documents screen through the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19 (RWB-PLT-N001-CON); the migration is one step in the per-service Flyway sequence (DP-15).

Business preconditions carried from RWB-E1-024:

- Document type table version DOCTYPE-2026.11 is in force with the six types, the write-once flag and the retention class of each type (RWB-P5-E1025-APP).
- Document hub parameters loaded: `INTAKE_ALLOWED_TYPES` = PDF, JPG, PNG; `INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB` = 25, assumed (DL11). RWB-E1-053 and RWB-E1-057 read the same parameters through the same contract.
- The caller is the upload path (RWB-P5-E1026-APP, user with Documents C) or the intake (SY-OCR). A reader holds Documents R with the case in scope.
- The feature flag `rwb.document.store` is on. The legacy flag name `rwb.dochub.store` is retired with the monolith.

The storage account name and the immutability policy of the containers are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1031; ASM-1979). The database login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1030; ASM-1978).

##### 4. Flow

1. Caller: calls the store command with the case ID, the document type, the source, the file reference in the intake container, its SHA-256 hash and any extracted fields. The upload path reaches it through `POST /documents`, which returns the upload link; the intake path reaches it through the same store command (12.1).
2. `DocumentStoreService`: reads the case through the `rwb-case` contract `GET /cases/{caseId}` (DP-11, one hop, 2 s timeout) and refuses the call if the case does not exist or the contract does not answer.
3. `DocumentStoreService`: reads the type row from `document_type` in the version in force (`valid_from` and `valid_to`): `write_once`, `retention_class` and the field list (RWB-P5-E1025-APP).
4. `DocumentStoreService`: checks the file type by its content signature and the file size against `INTAKE_ALLOWED_TYPES` and `INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB`, read through the parameters contract and client library (DP-06).
5. `DocumentStoreService`: looks for an active document on the case with the same type and hash; if one exists it returns it and stops, with no second row, entry or event.
6. `DocumentStoreService`, one transaction in `rwb_document`: writes the decision record (decision code DOCATT, final call STORED) through the decision-record library of DP-03, inserts the `document` row with `doc_version` 1 and state COPY_PENDING, inserts the `document_field` rows, and writes the `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` row to the outbox. A failed record aborts the transaction: nothing is stored and MSG-P7-003 is returned.
7. `copyPending` activity of `DocumentIntakeWorkflow`, after commit: calls the storage product RWB-PLT-TE012-APP, which writes the file to `rwb-docs-legal` when `write_once` is true and to `rwb-docs` otherwise, at `{container}/{caseId}/{documentId}/v1`; the service sets `storage_ref` and state STORED. A failure leaves the row COPY_PENDING for the next run.
8. User with Documents R: opens the document from the case documents screen (SCR-30) through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19); `GET /documents/{documentId}` returns the metadata, the extracted fields and the version list; `GET /documents/{documentId}/content` returns the file. The ACE common module writes each read to the PII access log, never this package.
9. User with Documents U: adds a version with `POST /documents/{documentId}/versions`; the service inserts a new `document` row with `doc_version` n+1 and `previous_version_id` set to the current row, and marks the earlier row `is_active` = false. The earlier version stays readable, and its blob path is untouched.
10. Outbox relay: publishes `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` to `rwb.document.events.v1` and the decision record to `rwb.decision-record.v1`; the event is published once per committed store, keyed by caseId, and carries no personal data.

The decision record is written before the change takes effect and in the same transaction as the document row and the outbox row, so a failure leaves all three unchanged (R-UNI-39).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Delete or content replace of a write-once document, through the service or directly on the container | Refused; the file and the row are unchanged; an audit event DOCUMENT_CHANGE_REFUSED is written for each attempt | MSG-P5-002 | AC2 |
| X2 | Document type not in the type table in force | Refused with 422; nothing stored | MSG-P5-006 | AC5 |
| X3 | File content is not PDF, JPG or PNG | Refused with 415; nothing stored | MSG-P5-001 | AC6 |
| X4 | File above `INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB` | Refused with 413; nothing stored | MSG-P5-017 | AC7 |
| X5 | The same file is stored again on the same case with the same type | The existing document is returned; no second row, entry or event | None | AC8 |
| X6 | Two users add a version to the same document at the same time | The first succeeds; the second gets 409; one new version exists | MSG-GEN-004 | AC9 |
| X7 | A version is added to a document that is not the latest version | Refused with 409 | MSG-P5-025 | AC10 |
| X8 | The copy to the container fails after commit | The row stays COPY_PENDING; the copy is retried by the `copyPending` activity of `DocumentIntakeWorkflow`; content reads return 503 until it is stored | MSG-GEN-006 | AC11 |
| X9 | The reader's role scope does not include the case | Refused with 403; nothing is returned | MSG-P4-003 | AC12 |
| X10 | The caller's role lacks the Documents right | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-024-13 (Access) |
| X11 | The decision record write fails | Nothing is stored; incident raised (R-UNI-39) | MSG-P7-003 | TC-E1-024-14 (Principle 5) |
| X12 | The `rwb-case` contract does not answer within 2 s, or the breaker is open | Refused with 503; nothing is stored; the circuit breaker shields the case service | MSG-GEN-006 | TC-E1-024-11 (target path) |
| X13 | The outbox relay is down when the store commits | The row, the fields, the decision record and the outbox row are committed; the event is published by the relay when it recovers, once, with no duplicate store | None | TC-E1-024-08 (target path) |

Two target-service notes:

- A store refused at the contract read (X12) is not retried by the caller's `Idempotency-Key`; a repeat of the same key after the case service recovers returns one stored document, because the duplicate check of step 5 runs before the insert.
- The legacy `delete` and `replaceContent` methods are not REST operations in the target (12.1). The refusal of AC2 is executed against the store command and against the container, and the audit event `DOCUMENT_CHANGE_REFUSED` is written by the store service.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the type table (RWB-P5-E1025-APP), the containers (RWB-PLT-TE012-APP), the case contract (RWB-P3-E1018-CON), the decision-record library and the outbox library, all earlier or contract work |
| Negotiable | File types, size limit, write-once flag and retention class are data rows or parameters; the story fixes the behaviour |
| Valuable | Every later document path (upload, OCR intake, generation) stores through this one capability |
| Estimable | One service, four public operations plus one internal store command, one detail panel, one migration |
| Small | Fits within two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test case in section 16 |

```gherkin
    Then the system refuses the call with 415 and MSG-P5-001
    Then the system writes nothing to the containers or the tables

  Scenario: AC7 Size limit boundary (legacy RWB-E1-024 AC7)
    Given two PDF files for case "RW-2026-000123" of 26,214,400 bytes and 26,214,401 bytes
    When each is stored
    Then the system stores the file of 26,214,400 bytes
    Then the system refuses the file of 26,214,401 bytes with 413 and MSG-P5-017 showing 25 MB

  Scenario: AC8 The same file stored twice (legacy RWB-E1-024 AC8)
    Given the court notice from AC1 is stored on case "RW-2026-000123"
    Given the rwb-decision contract mock returns the central ledger reference for decision code "DOCATT"
    When the same file with the same hash and type is stored again on that case
    Then the system returns the existing document ID
    Then the case still holds one court notice row, one decision log entry and one DocumentStored event for it

  Scenario: AC9 Two versions added at the same time (legacy RWB-E1-024 AC9)
    Given the appraisal report at doc_version 2
    When two users add a new version at the same time
    Then one request returns 200 with doc_version 3
    Then the other returns 409 with MSG-GEN-004
    Then exactly one row with doc_version 3 exists

  Scenario: AC10 Version on a superseded document (legacy RWB-E1-024 AC10)
    Given the appraisal report version 1 is inactive
    When a user adds a new version to version 1
    Then the system refuses the request with 409 and MSG-P5-025
    Then the system writes no new row

  Scenario: AC11 The storage copy fails (legacy RWB-E1-024 AC11)
    Given container "rwb-docs" refuses writes
    When an appraisal report is stored for case "RW-2026-000123"
    Then the system writes the document row with state "COPY_PENDING"
    Then GET content returns 503 with MSG-GEN-006 naming "Document storage"
    Then when the container accepts writes again the next document intake run copies the file and sets state "STORED"

  Scenario: AC12 Case outside the reader's scope (legacy RWB-E1-024 AC12)
    Given a phone collector with scope OWN who does not own case "RW-2026-000123"
    When the phone collector requests the court notice from AC1
    Then the system refuses the request with 403 and MSG-P4-003
    Then no metadata or content is returned
```

Every Given, When and Then line above is the legacy line unchanged. The cross-service part is mocked by the added Background Given on the `rwb-case` contract and by the `rwb-decision` contract Given in AC1 and AC8. In AC11 the "next document intake run" is the `copyPending` activity of `DocumentIntakeWorkflow`, whose 15-minute Schedule belongs to RWB-P5-E1049-APP (12.6).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every document is held against one case, with type, source, stored date and extracted fields | REQ-DCM-001; document.case_id is mandatory |
| BR2 | The document hub is the system of record; the file is held only in the hub containers | DT06; DL27; REQ-DCM-002 |
| BR3 | The write-once flag and the retention class come from the document type table version in force, never from the caller | Document type table (New); principle 1; DT02 |
| BR4 | A write-once document is never deleted or changed; a change is a new version | CTL-12; REQ-DCM-003; NFR-029 |
| BR5 | File types and the size limit are parameters | Document hub parameter table (New); DL11 |
| BR6 | A store with the same case, type and hash returns the existing document | R-UNI-40; events.txt rule Duplicates |
| BR7 | Only the latest version of a document takes a new version | FEAT-DCM-20 |
| BR8 | A store that cannot be written to the decision log does not proceed | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; CTL-06 |
| BR9 | Every read checks role, capability area and scope, and is written to the access log | CTL-09; REQ-ACA-006 |

Target-service statements that make the rules hold in `rwb-document`:

- BR1, BR2 and BR6 are executed in `rwb_document` only: `document` and `document_field` are the index, `storage_ref` points at the WORM blob, and the duplicate check is the unique partial index `uk_document_case_type_hash` plus the pre-insert read of step 5. No foreign schema is read (DP-01); the case arrives through `GET /cases/{caseId}` of RWB-P3-E1018-CON.
- BR3 and BR5 read the type row and the two parameters from the version in force; the type table is P5's own table and the parameters arrive through the `rwb-case` parameters contract (DP-06). Neither the write-once flag, the retention class, the size limit nor the allowed types is written in code.
- BR4 is executed by the store refusing every content change on a write-once document, by the blob path being immutable per version, and by the container's own WORM policy at RWB-PLT-TE012-APP.
- BR7 is executed by the latest-version rule on `doc_version` and `is_active`, with `version` as the optimistic lock.
- BR8 is executed by the decision-record library of DP-03 inside the store transaction: the record, the row, the fields and the outbox row commit together or not at all (R-UNI-39).
- BR9 is executed by the authorisation decision the service template's guard holds and by the ACE common module's PII access log for every read; this package writes no access-log entry.
- DP-07 keeps the four lists in reference data; DP-15 puts the store migration in the per-service Flyway sequence as one step in `rwb_document`; DP-09 puts the event in the outbox inside the same transaction.

##### 9. State transitions

No case state machine in this story: the store changes no case status. It sets the document record state (standard column state) and the active flag:

| From | Event | To |
|---|---|---|
| (no row) | store commits with the decision record and the outbox row | `document.state` = COPY_PENDING |
| COPY_PENDING | the `copyPending` activity stores the file and sets `storage_ref` | STORED |
| COPY_PENDING | the copy fails | COPY_PENDING (retried by the next intake run) |
| STORED, `is_active` = true | a new version is added to the latest version | `is_active` = false on the earlier row; the new row is COPY_PENDING then STORED |

A write-once document has no transition out of STORED: no delete, no content replace, no overwrite of its blob path.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| SY-OCR, OCR and extraction pipeline | Stores documents through the store command (Documents C) |
| RW-CASEOWN, RW-LITOFF, RW-RESTRUCT and the other roles with Documents C | Store through the upload path of RWB-P5-E1026-APP |
| Roles with Documents U (for example RW-CASEOWN, RW-LITOFF, RW-LEGAL, RW-COMPLY) | Add a new version |
| Roles with Documents R (for example RW-TEAMMGR, RW-AUDIT, RW-PHONECOL) | Read metadata and content inside their scope |
| SY-DECLOG, decision record writer | Writes the DOCATT record |
| SY-DOCUMENT, the rwb-document service identity | Runs the copy after commit and writes the audit event for a refused change |
| Nobody | Deletes or changes a write-once document |

The authorisation decision is taken by `rwb-access` (Recovery roles as data, scope, masking and DoA in `rwb_access`) and consumed as the cached permission decision the service holds. This story adds no operation and no guard of its own for it: the refusal shape is 403 with MSG-P4-002 or MSG-P4-003, as in the legacy endpoints. Where the legacy guard is replaced by the shared guard library (DP-08) is another story's deliverable; this story inherits it.

The database login is per service (DP-02). Its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1030; ASM-1978); the story refers to "the rwb-document login (DP-02)".

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Table in `rwb_document` | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-DOC-001 to DF-DOC-011 | `document` | id, case_id, party_id, document_type, source, storage_ref, classification_confidence, review_status, retention_class, write_once, doc_version | Write |
| DF-DOC-025 | `document` | previous_version_id | Write |
| DF-DOC-026 | `document` | content_sha256 | Write |
| Standard column | `document` | state, is_active, version | Write |
| DF-DOC-012 to DF-DOC-017 | `document_field` | id, document_id, field_name, field_value, confidence, confirmed_by | Write |
| DF-REF-219 | `document_type` | doc_type_code | Read |
| DF-REF-222 | `document_type` | write_once | Read |
| DF-REF-223 | `document_type` | retention_class | Read |
| DF-REF-229 | `document_type` | table_version | Read |
| DF-REF-245 | `document_hub_parameter` | param_code | Read |
| DF-REF-246 | `document_hub_parameter` | param_value | Read |
| DF-CAS-001 | `rwb-case` case, through the contract | id | Read |
| DF-CAS-002 | `rwb-case` case, through the contract | case_no | Read |
| (decision record) | decision-record library table in `rwb_document` | chain_seq, inputsRef, ruleId, finalCall, decidedAt, prev_hash, entry_hash | Write |
| (inbox) | `processed_event` | event_id, consumer, processed_at | Write |
| (outbox) | outbox library table in `rwb_document` | the row for DocumentStored and the decision record | Write |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary and the TSD P5 T3.1 table. No `rwb_case` row is copied and no ACE view is read by this service: DF-CAS-001 and DF-CAS-002 arrive inside the `rwb-case` contract answer, and DP-01 forbids a foreign-schema read. Personal data never enters the event payload, the workflow input, the decision record or the log; extracted field values in logs are replaced by the field name.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

| Operation | Path | Owner | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents` | P5 | Creates the document in COPY_PENDING with its metadata and returns the upload link for the file; `Idempotency-Key` required. The exact request and response field names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1032; ASM-1980) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/store` | P5 | The store command the upload and intake paths call: case contract read, type row, signature and size, duplicate check, decision record, row, fields and outbox in one transaction. Internal operation, service identity only. Field names as above |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}` | P5 | Metadata, extracted fields and the version list; Documents right R with scope applied |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/content` | P5 | The file of that version as `application/octet-stream`; 503 while the state is COPY_PENDING |
| POST | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/versions` | P5 | Adds a version to the latest version only; multipart file and reason; `Idempotency-Key` required |

The five operations are carried into the `rwb-document` contract stories; this story builds them. The response body of a document read and of a version is the Document shape of the TSD P5 T-A.2 (id, caseId, partyId, documentType, source, storageRef, classificationConfidence, reviewStatus, retentionClass, writeOnce, docVersion), extended with storedAt, previousVersionId, versions and fields. Errors follow RFC 9457 with `messageId`.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Path | Owner | Story | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 | RWB-P3-E1018-CON | The case exists and is in the caller's scope; one hop, 2 s timeout, breaker per downstream (DP-11) |

The two parameters and the four reference lists are not REST operations of this story: they are read through the `rwb-case` parameters and reference-data client libraries of DP-06 and DP-07, which wrap the contracts RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON. The file is written through the storage product RWB-PLT-TE012-APP, which is not a REST contract of another service; it appears in 12.9 as File.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Key | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` (EV-16) | `rwb.document.events.v1` | P5 | caseId | documentId, caseId, documentType, source, storedAt |
| decision record | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | PLT library, consumed by P7 | caseId | the hash-chained record with decision code DOCATT and final call STORED |

CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, binary mode; no personal data in either payload. The event is written to the outbox in the store transaction, so it exists exactly when the document row exists; the trigger guarantees the consumers rely on (once per store, order per case, no duplicate) rest on the outbox relay and the consumer inbox of DP-09, and the transfer trigger that reacts to DocumentStored in this service is stated by RWB-P5-E1021-APP.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. This story consumes no Kafka event. `DocumentFieldsExtracted` is published by the extraction path (RWB-P5-E1050-APP and RWB-P5-E1053-APP), not by this story, and DocumentStored is consumed by `rwb-case` and `rwb-agent`.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Kind | Queue | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` | Workflow, from the L3 workflow kit template "Document intake" | `rwb-document` | OCR, classify, extract; registered by RWB-P5-E1049-APP, which owns the workflow |
| `copyPending` | Activity | `rwb-document` | Contributed by this story: copies a COPY_PENDING document to its container after commit and sets `storage_ref` and state STORED |

###### 12.6 Schedules

None in this story. The 15-minute document-intake Schedule (legacy JOB-12) belongs to RWB-P5-E1049-APP; this story contributes only the `copyPending` activity that the Schedule-started workflow calls.
