##### 1. Story

As a **QA integration engineer**, I want **the end-to-end proof of the RWB-E1-026 attach and search screen across rwb-document (P5, the owner of the document), rwb-case (P3, the parameter and reference-data owner) and the gateway-bff composite route for SCR-30**, so that **the upload, the case document list, the type-and-date search and the checklist are proved on the real services and through the one composite route the screen uses before wave 1 exits**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy screen is a case record view tab that calls the document endpoints and the case record view directly: upload with a type, list of every document on the case, search by type and stored date, and a checklist placeholder showing which of the six agreed types are present. Those facts matter to the case owner, and the legacy criteria that test the behaviour inside the document hub stay where they belong: AC1 to AC11 of RWB-E1-026 are owned by RWB-P5-E1026-APP and are not copied here. This integration story owns the ten criteria that no single service can prove, because in the target the screen is not a direct caller.

In the target architecture SCR-30 is a gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) over the P5 document contract and the P3 parameter and queue-measure contracts: the screen makes one call, gateway-bff composes it from the document list of P5 and the parameter, reference-data and case reads of P3, and the browser calls no service directly. The upload path is proved on the P5 contract, the parameters and the list values come from the P3 contracts (DP-06, DP-07), the decision record of a store is written by the local decision-record library (DP-03), and the document, its versions, its metadata and its stored file are owned by P5 rwb-document in `rwb_document` (DP-01). A test of the screen inside one service would pass while the composite, the parameter source or the storage ownership were wrong, and that is exactly what this story prevents.

No service contract is faked. The suite exercises the published wave 1 contracts of P5 rwb-document and P3 rwb-case, the composite route of gateway-bff and a real Blob container; the only stubs are the external ones named in section 12.8. The composite path, its aggregation shape and the source behind the malware scan are not published in the Ownership Map, so the suite asserts the composite response and the scan result only, and the open point is recorded as GAP-0351 and ASM-0445. The release date 30 November 2026 is copied unchanged and is tentative.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P5-E1026-APP is done: the upload, the case document list, the document read, the document content read, the duplicate response, the idempotency handling and the checklist operation are in SIT, and `rwb_document` is the only writer of the document tables.
- RWB-P3-E1045-APP is done: the parameter contract publishes `INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB` = 25 and `INTAKE_ALLOWED_TYPES` = PDF, JPG, PNG, and the document type and source lists are readable as reference data through the P3 contract.
- RWB-P3-E1030-APP is done: the case read and the queue-measure read of the case record view are published, so gateway-bff composes SCR-30 from real answers.
- The gateway-bff composite route for SCR-30 is deployed in SIT with its session and coarse-permission check (DP-19).
- The published contracts of P5 rwb-document and P3 rwb-case are versioned in the registry, and the suite consumes only those contracts.
- The harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG is available with its synthetic case set, its 50-document case and its six document types.
- The environment is SIT, the topics of the wave 1 services are live with their retry and `.dlt` topics, and a Blob container with an intake and a quarantine path is available (Azurite in the lower environment).
- Feature flag `rwb.dochub.casedocs` is on.
- No production data is used and no production connection is opened; every case number, user identity, document and file is synthetic.
- The release date 30 November 2026 is tentative; a date is not a condition of this story.

##### 4. Flow

1. QA integration engineer: seeds the synthetic case set of the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG — case RW-2026-000123 with 50 documents, of which 12 are `COURT_NOTICE` and 4 were stored in October 2026, and 1 is `APPRAISAL_REPORT` — and signs in as the synthetic identity that holds RW-CASEOWN for that case; no production data is used.
2. Harness: calls the gateway-bff composite route for SCR-30 for case RW-2026-000123 and asserts that the response carries the document list that P5 publishes for the case, in the same order and with the same count.
3. Harness: uploads `court-notice-0007.pdf` of 2 MB with type `COURT_NOTICE` and source `UPLOAD` through `POST /api/recovery/document/v1/documents`, and asserts 201, the source and doc_version 1.
4. Harness: waits for `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` on `rwb.document.events.v1` and reads the list again through the composite; the new document is at the top within 5 seconds of submit.
5. Harness: searches type `COURT_NOTICE` from 1 October 2026 to 31 October 2026 and asserts the 4 October court notices, newest first, with count 4.
6. Harness: reads the checklist for the case and asserts the six agreed types with the present counts.
7. Harness: posts the negative uploads — no type, the EICAR file, the same file twice, the double submit with the same Idempotency-Key and the two files at the size boundary — and records every status and message.
8. Harness: posts the inverted date range and the empty search, and asserts the refusal and the empty sentence.
9. Harness: calls the composite with an identity whose scope excludes the case and asserts the 403 and that no document name is shown.
10. Harness: writes the evidence report with one verdict per test case, removes the synthetic documents and the quarantined file, and records the cleanup.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Upload with no document type | Refused by the owning service with 422; the composite passes the refusal through; nothing stored | MSG-GEN-001 | AC4 |
| X2 | The file fails the malware scan | Refused with 422; the file is held in quarantine; no document row exists | MSG-P5-016 | AC5 |
| X3 | The file type is not allowed | Refused with 415; nothing stored | MSG-P5-001 | TC-E1-026-06-ITG (regression) |
| X4 | The same file and type is already on the case | The existing document is returned and highlighted; no second document | MSG-P5-024 | AC6 |
| X5 | The submit is sent twice with the same Idempotency-Key | One document and one decision record; the second call returns the first result | None | AC7 |
| X6 | Date from is after date to | The owning service refuses the range, the composite passes the refusal through and no search runs | MSG-GEN-003 | AC8 |
| X7 | Search matches nothing | Empty state with the sentence and the clear filter action | None | AC8 |
| X8 | Case is outside the user's scope | Refused with 403 and no document name is shown | MSG-P4-003 | AC9 |
| X9 | Role without Documents C uploads | Refused with 403; the Upload action is not shown | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-026-12-ITG |
| X10 | The decision record write fails during the store | Nothing is stored; the dialog shows the message | MSG-P7-003 | TC-E1-026-13-ITG |
| X11 | A consumed contract drifts from the published one (path, field, status, list or event schema) | The preflight fails on the contract test and the run stops before any assertion; the drift is reported against the owning service and no fake is put in its place | None | Preflight; AC1, AC3 |
| X12 | The gateway-bff composite route for SCR-30 is missing or returns a server error | The run fails as a deployment fault and names the route; no upload and no search is asserted through a direct service call in its place | None | AC1, AC2, AC3 |
| X13 | The W1J01 synthetic set, its 50-document case or its six types do not match the run | The run fails as a fixture fault and names the mismatched element; no production value and no invented document is substituted | None | AC2, AC3 |
| X14 | A consumed call exceeds the 2 s budget | The call is recorded as a budget breach, the assertion is not written from a partial answer, and the evidence report names the operation and the elapsed time | None | AC1, AC2, AC9 |
| X15 | A suite step tries to read a service schema directly | The step does not exist: the suite ships with no client for a service schema, and the pipeline scan fails any change that adds one | None | Section 17 |

X1 to X10 are the legacy exception paths carried onto the real services; X11 to X15 are the cross-service failures that appear only when the run leaves one service.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | The suite is a module of its own and reuses the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG; it needs the three integration dependencies and the published contracts of P5 and P3 plus the composite route, not their source code, and it owns no schema and no table |
| Negotiable | The fixture composition, the poll interval and the report layout are configuration; the case number, the type list, the messages, the size limit and the 5 second expectation are fixed by the legacy story and the parameter contract |
| Valuable | Proves across services what no single service story can prove: the composite composition, the stored document at the top of the list, the type-and-date search, the checklist counts, the parameter-driven size limit and the scope refusal at the edge |
| Estimable | One suite module, one fixture pack, eight contract probes, one size-boundary pair and one report |
| Small | Ten scenarios over two services and one composite route; no service code and no schema change |
| Testable | Every criterion asserts a contract response, a composite field, a count, an exact message or a container state; all data is synthetic |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Attach and search screen, proven across the wave 1 services and the SCR-30 composite route

  Background:
    Given document type table version "DOCTYPE-2026.11" is in force
    Given user "TEST-CO-01" holds RW-CASEOWN and owns case "RW-2026-000123"
    Given the wave 1 services rwb-document and rwb-case are deployed in SIT behind gateway-bff
    Given the RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG synthetic set is loaded and no production data is used

  Scenario: AC1 The composite returns the P5 list and a new upload shows at the top (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the gateway-bff composite route for SCR-30 serves case "RW-2026-000123"
    When "TEST-CO-01" opens the Documents tab of the case
    Then the composite returns the document list that P5 publishes for the case, with the same items and count
    When "TEST-CO-01" uploads "court-notice-0007.pdf" of 2 MB with type "COURT_NOTICE"
    Then the P5 response is 201 with source "UPLOAD" and doc_version 1
    Then the document shows at the top of the composite list within 5 seconds of submit

  Scenario: AC2 Type-and-date search returns exactly the October court notices (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given case "RW-2026-000123" holds 50 documents of which 12 are "COURT_NOTICE"
    Given 4 of the court notices were stored between 1 October 2026 and 31 October 2026
    When "TEST-CO-01" searches type "COURT_NOTICE" from 1 October 2026 to 31 October 2026
    Then exactly the 4 court notices stored in October return, newest first
    Then the result count reads 4

  Scenario: AC3 The checklist lists the six agreed types with their present counts (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given case "RW-2026-000123" holds 12 court notices and 1 appraisal report and no other agreed type
    When the Documents tab opens through the composite route
    Then the checklist lists the six agreed types of the type table in force
    Then COURT_NOTICE shows present with 12 and APPRAISAL_REPORT shows present with 1
    Then DEMAND_LETTER, TITLE_DEED, SETTLEMENT_AGREEMENT and GUARANTOR_NOTICE show not present

  Scenario: AC4 An upload without a document type is refused and nothing is stored (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given "TEST-CO-01" picks "scan-0009.pdf" and no document type
    When "TEST-CO-01" submits the upload through the composite route
    Then the P5 response is 422 with MSG-GEN-001 naming "Document type"
    Then the composite shows the refusal and the system stores no document

  Scenario: AC5 A file that fails the malware scan is refused and quarantined (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a test file "eicar-0001.pdf" holding the EICAR test signature
    When "TEST-CO-01" uploads it with type "COURT_NOTICE"
    Then the P5 response is 422 with MSG-P5-016
    Then the file is held in the quarantine container and no document row exists for the case

  Scenario: AC6 A repeated upload of the same file and type returns the existing document (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given "court-notice-0007.pdf" is stored on case "RW-2026-000123" as "COURT_NOTICE"
    When "TEST-CO-01" uploads the same file with the same type
    Then the response is 200 with the existing document and MSG-P5-024
    Then the case still holds one copy of that court notice and the composite shows it once

  Scenario: AC7 A double submit returns one document and one decision record (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given "TEST-CO-01" submits "appraisal-0003.pdf" with Idempotency-Key "TEST-TOKEN-0001"
    When the same request with Idempotency-Key "TEST-TOKEN-0001" arrives a second time within 1 second
    Then both responses carry the same document ID
    Then one document row and one decision record exist for it, written by the local decision-record library

  Scenario: AC8 The date filters are validated and an empty search shows the empty state (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given case "RW-2026-000123" holds no document of type "TITLE_DEED"
    When "TEST-CO-01" searches from 31 October 2026 to 1 October 2026
    Then the owning service refuses the range with MSG-GEN-003 and the composite passes the refusal through
    Then no search is run for the inverted range
    When "TEST-CO-01" searches type "TITLE_DEED" from 1 October 2026 to 31 October 2026
    Then the composite returns no item and the screen shows "No documents match this search."

  Scenario: AC9 A case outside the caller's scope is refused and shows no document name (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given user "TEST-CO-02" holds RW-CASEOWN with scope OWN and does not own case "RW-2026-000123"
    When "TEST-CO-02" opens the Documents tab of that case through the composite route
    Then the call returns 403 with MSG-P4-003
    Then the system shows no document name

  Scenario: AC10 The size limit comes from the parameter contract and holds at the exact byte (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the P3 parameter contract publishes INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB as 25
    When "TEST-CO-01" uploads a file of 26,214,400 bytes with type "COURT_NOTICE"
    Then the response is 201 and the document is stored
    When "TEST-CO-01" uploads a file of 26,214,401 bytes with type "COURT_NOTICE"
    Then the response is 413 with MSG-P5-017 and the system stores no document
```

**Target reading.** These ten criteria are new and belong to this story alone; the legacy AC1 to AC11 of RWB-E1-026 stay with RWB-P5-E1026-APP and are regression evidence here. The screen is proved through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) and the upload through the P5 contract (DP-11, DP-13); the parameters and the list values are read through the P3 contracts (DP-06, DP-07); the decision record is the local library write (DP-03); the document tables are P5's alone (DP-01). The composite path, its aggregation shape and the source behind the malware scan are not published in the Ownership Map, so the suite asserts the composite response and the scan result only (GAP-0351; ASM-0445).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A user upload carries a document type from the type table in force and source UPLOAD | RWB-E1-026 BR1; REQ-DCM-001; LOV-DOC-SOURCE |
| BR2 | Every upload is scanned for malware before it is stored | RWB-E1-026 BR2; REQ-DCM-010 |
| BR3 | The list and the search show only cases in the user's scope | RWB-E1-026 BR3; CTL-09 |
| BR4 | The date filter applies to the stored date of the document | RWB-E1-026 BR4; FSD P5 A2.5; REQ-DCM-008 |
| BR5 | The checklist lists the types of the type table in force; the required items per case type come in RWB-E1-040 | RWB-E1-026 BR5; REQ-DCM-011 |
| BR6 | A repeated upload with the same file, type and case returns the existing document | RWB-E1-026 BR6; R-UNI-40 |
| BR7 | A store that cannot be written to the decision record does not proceed | RWB-E1-026 BR7; Principle 5; R-UNI-39 |
| BR8 | P5 rwb-document owns the document, its versions, its metadata and its stored file in `rwb_document`; no other service writes a document table | DP-01; Ownership Map (document, document_type, document_checklist_item, document_custody) |
| BR9 | P3 rwb-case owns the parameter contract and the reference data that the screen reads: the size limit, the allowed types, the document types and the source list | DP-06; DP-07; Ownership Map (parameter_catalog, parameter_value, lov_value) |
| BR10 | gateway-bff composes SCR-30 in one composite route over the P5 and P3 contracts; the screen calls no service directly and the composite makes one hop per owner with a 2 s budget | DP-19; ADR-020; Architecture v5 slide 20 |
| BR11 | No cross-schema read: the suite and gateway-bff read every fact through the owner's contract, never through a table or a view of another service | DP-01; ADR-020 |
| BR12 | The size limit and the allowed file types are read from the P3 parameter contract in force, never from code; the front end size check does not replace the service check | DP-06; RWB-E1-026 section 17 |
| BR13 | The decision record of a store is written by the local decision-record library (DP-03), and a failed write stores no document | DP-03; RWB-E1-026 BR7 |
| BR14 | No personal data in the composite response, the evidence report, the fixtures or the logs: document IDs, types, dates, counts and case numbers only | RWB-E1-026 section 17; ADR-015 |

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story changes no case status. The document record it creates follows the states of RWB-P5-E1026-APP, and the suite observes them through the P5 contract.

| Object | State | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Document record | COPY_PENDING | The row exists and the file copy is not yet confirmed |
| Document record | STORED | The file is stored and the document is returned by the list and the read |
| Document record | QUARANTINED | The scan found a threat; no document row is created and the file is held in the quarantine container |
| Checklist item | Present | The count of stored documents of that type is at least one |
| Checklist item | Not present | No stored document of that type on the case |
| Suite run | Not started, running, passed, failed with the failing test case named | The evidence report per test case |

| Who | What they may do in this story |

| QA integration engineer | Owns the suite module, the fixture pack, the size-boundary pair and the evidence report |
| Service owner of rwb-document | Owns the document, its versions, the metadata, the stored file, the checklist operation and the scan integration |
| Service owner of rwb-case | Owns the parameter contract, the reference data, the case read and the queue measures the composite composes |
| Platform owner of gateway-bff | Owns the composite route for SCR-30, the session in Redis and the coarse-permission check |
| Case owner (RW-CASEOWN) | Uploads, lists and searches inside the scope of the own case, as the synthetic test identity |
| Roles with Documents R (for example RW-TEAMMGR, RW-AUDIT) | List, search and open documents inside their scope; no upload |
| Partner roles PT-AGENCY, PT-LAWFIRM, PT-VALUER, PT-AUCTION | No access in this story; partners reach the Workbench only through the external gateway (DL03) |
| No role | Reads a service schema directly, or takes production data into the run |

The document tables are P5's alone, the parameter and reference-data tables are P3's, and the composite shape and the scan source are the open point named above.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The suite provides no REST operation. The names reserved for P2 rwb-integration — the base `/api/recovery/integration/v1`, the topic `rwb.integration.events.v1`, the queue `rwb-integration` and the schema `rwb_integration` — are not used, and no `rwb_integration` table is written.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method and path | Owner | Use | Budget |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/recovery/document/v1/documents` | P5 rwb-document | Upload with type, source UPLOAD and an Idempotency-Key; the store, the duplicate answer and the size and type refusals | 2 s |
| `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents` | P5 rwb-document | The case document list, the type-and-date search and the result count | 2 s |
| `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}` | P5 rwb-document | The stored document: source, doc_version, stored date and content hash | 2 s |
| `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/content` | P5 rwb-document | The stored file of the uploaded court notice, read back for the content assertion | 2 s |
| `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The case the composite composes: case number, status and scope check | 2 s |
| `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | P3 rwb-case | The parameter in force: `INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB` = 25 and `INTAKE_ALLOWED_TYPES` (DP-06) | 2 s |
| `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/cases` | P3 rwb-case | The queue measures of RWB-P3-E1030-APP that the case record view shows next to the tab | 2 s |
| gateway-bff composite route for SCR-30 | gateway-bff (platform edge) | The one call the screen makes: the document list, the checklist, the case and the parameters composed into the SCR-30 model (DP-19); the path and the aggregation shape are not published (GAP-0351; ASM-0445) | 2 s |

Every call is one hop to the owning service, or to gateway-bff, on its own base (DP-11, DP-13, DP-19) with the 2 s client budget; the suite calls no service through another service.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The suite publishes no event.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Producer | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` | `rwb.document.events.v1` | P5 rwb-document | The upload is stored; the suite waits for it before it reads the top of the list and the stored document |

The envelope is CloudEvents 1.0, the key is the document ID, and the payload carries identifiers, types and dates only; the suite asserts no personal data field.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Workflow or activity | Owner | Task queue | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| DocumentIntakeWorkflow | P5 rwb-document | `rwb-document` | The store path of the uploaded file: intake, classification and the scan step before the document row is confirmed |

The scan step inside the intake is not named in the Ownership Map, so the suite asserts the scan by its result only — the 422 with MSG-P5-016 and the quarantined file with no document row — and never by an internal path (GAP-0351; ASM-0445). The suite starts no workflow of its own.

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Job | Name | When | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| JOB-12 | Document intake | Every 15 min, event plus KEDA workers | P5 rwb-document | Used only to place the synthetic documents of the case set; not the path of a user upload |

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The suite owns no table and never reads another service's schema (DP-01). The document tables are P5's, the parameter and reference-data tables are P3's, and every fact is read through a contract of 12.2, 12.4 or 12.5.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

External stubs only:

| Stub | Use |

| EICAR test file | The file that the scan must refuse; a test signature, not a real threat |
| RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG synthetic case set | Case RW-2026-000123 with 50 documents, 12 court notices, 4 in October 2026, 1 appraisal report and the six agreed types |
| Blob container (Azurite in the lower environment) | The intake path, the stored file and the quarantine path |
| Mock Entra sign-in | Synthetic test identities for the case owner, the reader and the out-of-scope user |

No service contract is faked: every P5 and P3 call and the gateway-bff composite go to the real deployment in SIT.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** One suite module that reuses the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG: a fixture pack for the 50-document case and the six types, a composite probe for SCR-30, a document probe for the P5 upload and search, a parameter probe for the size limit, a scan probe that asserts the result only, and an evidence report with one verdict per test case. No service code and no schema change.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| SuiteRunner | Test harness | Preflight against the published contracts and the composite route, run order, report and exit code |
| FixtureDriver | Test harness | Seeds the W1J01 case set, the 50-document case and the six types through the P5 and P3 published paths |
| CompositeProbe | Test harness | Calls the SCR-30 composite route and asserts the list, the checklist, the case and the parameter parts against the owners' answers |
| DocumentProbe | Test harness | Uploads, lists, searches and reads the document through the P5 contract, including the duplicate, the inverted range and the empty state |
| ParameterProbe | Test harness | Reads `INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB` and `INTAKE_ALLOWED_TYPES` through the P3 parameter contract and drives the 26,214,400 and 26,214,401 byte uploads |
| ScanProbe | Test harness | Uploads the EICAR file and asserts the 422, MSG-P5-016, the quarantined object and the absence of a document row, without an internal path |
| EventProbe | Test harness | Consumes `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` and asserts the envelope, the key and the absence of a personal data field |
| ReportWriter | Test harness | One row per test case with the evidence and the elapsed time, and the cleanup record |

**Database.** None of its own. The suite writes no service table and no schema object (DP-01).

**Configuration and reference data**

- The SIT endpoints of P5 and P3, the composite route of gateway-bff, the topic name, the queue name and the namespace `rwb-recovery`, all as configuration.
- The synthetic case number RW-2026-000123, the user identities, the 50-document case, the 2 MB court notice and the two size-boundary files.
- The size limit and the allowed types, read through the P3 parameter contract and never written in the suite code (DP-06, AC10).
- The six agreed types and the source list, read through the P3 reference-data contract (DP-07).
- The 2 s client budget, the 5 second list expectation and the poll interval of the run.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added | Where it sits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none | The document tables stay in `rwb_document` (P5) and the suite asserts through the P5 contract; no suite step opens a schema |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON | The store writes its record through the local library; AC7 asserts one record for the double submit |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON | The size limit and the allowed types are read through `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters`; AC10 |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON | The six document types and the source list are read through the P3 reference-data contract; AC3 |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The one call the screen makes; every screen assertion of section 15 goes through the SCR-30 composite route |

The dependency-added column records the build dependency of the owning story. This story has no build dependency: an ITG story waits on no build of its own. It carries no H, C or X dependency, and its I dependencies are the three APP stories RWB-P3-E1045-APP, RWB-P3-E1030-APP and RWB-P5-E1026-APP listed in the metadata table.

**Fixtures**

| Fixture | Content | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| Document case set | Case RW-2026-000123 with 50 documents, 12 `COURT_NOTICE` of which 4 stored in October 2026, 1 `APPRAISAL_REPORT` and the other four types absent | AC2, AC3, AC8 |
| Upload file | `court-notice-0007.pdf` of 2 MB with type `COURT_NOTICE` and source `UPLOAD` | AC1, AC6 |
| Scan file | `eicar-0001.pdf` holding the EICAR test signature | AC5 |
| Size pair | A file of 26,214,400 bytes and a file of 26,214,401 bytes | AC10 |
| Idempotency pair | Two submissions of `appraisal-0003.pdf` with the same Idempotency-Key | AC7 |

**Build steps**

1. Create the suite module next to harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG and wire it to the SIT endpoints of P5 and P3, the composite route, the topic and the queue, with the contract preflight that fails on any drift (X11, X12).
2. Build FixtureDriver and the document case set, and assert that the composite list matches the P5 list for the same case.
3. Build CompositeProbe for the list, the checklist, the case and the parameter parts of the SCR-30 answer, and assert that the composite adds no document that P5 does not publish.
4. Build DocumentProbe for the upload, the 5 second top-of-list expectation, the type-and-date search, the duplicate, the inverted range and the empty state.
5. Build ParameterProbe and the size-boundary pair, reading the limit through the P3 parameter contract and never from code.
6. Build ScanProbe for the EICAR file and assert the 422, MSG-P5-016, the quarantined object and the absence of a document row, with no internal scan path.
7. Build EventProbe and ReportWriter, including the cleanup of the synthetic documents and the quarantined file.
8. Run the suite twice in SIT against the wave 1 release candidate so that a repeated run adds no document and no decision record.

**Done when.** The thirteen test cases of section 16 pass in SIT against the published wave 1 contracts and the SCR-30 composite route, the ten criteria of section 7 are signed off, a 2 MB upload shows at the top of the composite list within 5 seconds, no service table was read, the synthetic set is cleaned up, and the evidence report names every criterion with its observable.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | Upload with no document type | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-003 | Date from after date to | {field} cannot be before {other}. |
| MSG-P5-001 | File type not allowed | This file type cannot be stored. Use PDF, JPG or PNG. |
| MSG-P5-016 | Malware found | This file was not stored because the malware scan found a threat. It is held in quarantine. |
| MSG-P5-017 | File above the size limit | This file is larger than {size} MB and cannot be stored. |
| MSG-P5-024 | Same file already on the case | This file is already on the case as {document}. |
| MSG-P5-006 | Type not in the table | {value} is not a document type in force. Choose a type from the list. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | Case outside the scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Decision record write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The message IDs and wording are copied unchanged from RWB-E1-026 and this story adds no message ID. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-30 Case documents, reached from SCR-03 Case record, served by the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The suite asserts each state through the composite and the same facts through the P5 and P3 contracts.

| State | What the user sees and does | What the suite asserts |
|---|---|---|
| Loading | Skeleton rows while the list and the checklist load | The composite returns one answer carrying the list, the checklist, the case and the parameters; no partial answer is asserted |
| list | Documents with type, stored date, source, version and the write-once label; the search bar with type and date range; the checklist with the six types | The composite list matches the P5 list and the P5 read of the document; the checklist counts match the P5 counts; the date range narrows to the 4 October court notices |
| upload | The upload dialog with the file, the document type and the size limit; errors from section 14 next to the field | The P5 upload response, the duplicate answer, the size refusal and the empty-type refusal, and the composite showing the same message |
| Empty | "No documents match this search." with the action "Clear the search" (common state) | The composite returns no item and the sentence is shown for a type with no document |
| Error | The message from section 14 at the top | The 403, the 415, the 422 and the 413 of sections 5 and 14 carried through the composite unchanged |

The Upload action shows only to roles with Documents C. A missing composite route is a deployment fault and is never replaced by a direct service call in the suite (X12).

##### 17. Guardrails

- Synthetic data only: the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG loads every case number, user identity, document and file, and no production data is read, copied or connected to.
- No personal data in the composite response, the events, the logs, the evidence report or the fixtures: document IDs, types, dates, counts and case numbers only.
- No cross-service table read: every fact is read through a contract, and the suite ships with no client for a service schema (DP-01).
- No business value in test code: the size limit, the allowed types, the six document types and the source list are the parameter and the reference data in force, read through the P3 contracts (DP-06, DP-07).
- The front end size check does not replace the service check, and the suite asserts both answers on the same upload.
- The scan is asserted by its result only; no internal scan path is assumed (GAP-0351).
- One hop and a 2 s budget on every call, with no service called through another service (ADR-020).
- No production access and no production namespace: the run is pinned to SIT and refuses to start against any other environment.
- Clean-up in the same run: the synthetic documents, the quarantined file and the fixture rows are removed in a controlled order, and the report records what was cleaned.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform contract owner**, I want **the published contract of the local decision-record library — the interfaces and exceptions, the record shape, the DDL template of `decision_record` that every service applies in its own schema, the `DecisionRecorded` envelope on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, the transaction and idempotency rules, the versioning rule and the fakes — instead of the monolith's one `decision_log_entry` table in the shared `recovery` schema**, so that **all 19 services can write their records from Day 1 against one frozen contract while the central ledger stays P7's**.

##### 2. Business rationale

In the monolith the decision log was one table, `decision_log_entry`, in the single `recovery` schema, and the writer was one published interface inside the same process (legacy sections 11 and 12). Architecture v5 changes both facts in one move. Slide 20 states what every service does from the service template and the shared libraries — it writes its own decision records locally, in "Own schema: business tables + outbox + inbox + decision_record", and publishes `DecisionRecorded` to `rwb.decision-record.v1` — and slide 28 adds that the record is written with the change in one transaction, chained to the one before, and collected centrally by rwb-decision within 5 minutes. ADR-022 records the decision: a local decision record plus a central ledger.

**The division of the legacy key is fixed.** This WP delivers the **local decision-record library** and its contract. The **central ledger** — the `rwb_decision` store, the continuous ingest (JOB-13), the chain check (JOB-14) at 02:00 and the reads `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` and `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log/{entryId}` — is **RWB-P7-E1027-APP**, and the **end-to-end proof** is **RWB-ITG-E1027-ITG**. The legacy acceptance criteria **AC1 to AC7 stay with RWB-P7-E1027-APP** and are not copied here: every criterion in section 7 is new (D-RCV-60) and tests only the contract deliverable in this title.

The contract has to exist before the code does, for three reasons. The record shape is the only thing that makes the chain check of P7 possible at all: if one service writes a different column set, the ledger cannot recompute an entry hash, and Audit cannot search one place for every decision. The transaction rule is the whole point of the local write: a library that opened its own transaction would let an action commit without its record, which is exactly what REQ-DRI-005 forbids, so `MANDATORY` is part of the contract and not a coding convention. And the envelope has to be fixed for a shared topic: all 19 services publish to `rwb.decision-record.v1`, so the type name, the key and the payload shape are the only thing that keeps the ingest simple and the ordering per case intact.

The contract also fixes what the library does not do. It does not write the central ledger, does not raise a case event or a task, does not copy to a data lake (the legacy RWB-E1-014 copy is retired, DP-17), and does not write another service's table. The table it declares is a library object owned by PLT and created in each service's own schema, and `decision_log_entry` is named only as the P7 ledger that is not this contract's.

The fake is the Day-1 unblocker: every service can build and test its record write, its refusal path and its outbox call before a single other service exists, and P7 can build its ingest against the same envelope (Template and Rules §R5.4 class C).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The local record is the caller's: Architecture v5 slides 20 and 28 fix that each service writes its own record in its own schema and publishes `DecisionRecorded`, and that the central ledger is P7's.
- The shared topic name is fixed by Template and Rules §R4 as `rwb.decision-record.v1`; the event name follows the §R4 naming rule as `rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1` and the topic keeps its shared name (ASM-2444).
- The ledger owner is fixed: `decision_log_entry` is P7's under the Ownership Map ruling on `decision_log_entry` (owner P7) and Architecture v5 slide 41.
- The record columns are the ones the Temporal and Drools Design slide 16 names — `chain_seq`, `inputsRef`, `ruleId`, `ruleVersion`, `recommendation`, `approverUserId`, `approvalLevel`, `finalCall`, `actions`, `outcome`, `decidedAt`, `prev_hash`, `entry_hash` — with the case, the decision code, the actor and the idempotency key of the legacy story.
- The decision codes and approval levels are values in force in the target owner's data, read through the parameters and reference-data contracts of rwb-case; the contract refers to them and holds no list of its own.
- The outbox contract of RWB-PLT-TE006-CON exists, so the contract can name the publisher it uses without redeclaring it.
- The per-service Flyway conventions of RWB-PLT-E1044-CON exist, so the DDL template is a template and not one shared migration.
- The message identifiers `MSG-P7-009` and `MSG-P7-003` are kept unchanged from the legacy build; no published message catalogue defines their entry format, so that entry is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1403; ASM-2443).
- The full column set of the local table, the entry-hash algorithm and the exact payload schema beyond the fields named in section 12.3 have no published specification and are published here as the working read (GAP-1403; ASM-2443).
- No build dependency and no approval stop: a CON story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7) and is published at status Draft (realignment v1).

##### 4. Flow

1. The contract author fixes the three interfaces — `DecisionRecordWriter`, `DecisionRecord` and `DecisionRecordEntryRef` — with their signatures, the two exceptions and the `MANDATORY` transaction rule.
2. The author fixes the record shape as the seven field groups of section 12.2, with the access-event exception for the subject and the version group, and one worked example that uses the legacy values only.
3. The author writes the DDL template of `decision_record`: the columns, the unique keys, the chain columns, the append-only trigger and the index, as one template each service applies in its own schema.
4. The author writes the `DecisionRecorded` envelope section: CloudEvents 1.0 binary mode, the attribute set, `ce_type` `rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1`, the key rule, the payload fields and the rule that the payload carries identifiers and facts only.
5. The author writes the transaction and idempotency rules: the call joins the caller's transaction, opens none, throws before any write, returns the first entry reference for a repeated key and counts the repeat.
6. The author writes the versioning rule: major version 1, a backward-compatible change versus a new major version with a new `ce_type`, and the pinning rule for consuming services.
7. The lint and schema steps run: the interfaces compared against the legacy published interface, the DDL applied twice in throwaway schemas, the example scanned for personal data, and the envelope validated against one accepted and one refused schema.
8. The fake set is generated: a writer fake, a chain fixture, an outbox fake, a registry fake and a P7 ledger fake, all answering from the same example set.
9. The contract test runs the fakes against the document on every change and fails the build on any drift.
10. The document and the fakes are published at v1; RWB-PLT-E1027-APP and every consuming service pin the version.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A published signature opens its own transaction, or performs a write when no transaction is open | The contract lint fails the build; the `MANDATORY` rule and the throw-before-write rule are fixed | None | AC1 |
| X2 | A record shape published without the version group, or without the access-event exception | The schema validation fails the build; the seven field groups are all required and the exception is declared | None | AC2 |
| X3 | A service applies the DDL template in another service's schema, or hand-writes the table | The boundary and drift checks fail the build; the template creates the table in the applying schema only | None | AC3 |
| X4 | The envelope is published with a type other than `rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1`, or with no key | The envelope validation fails the build; the type and the key rule are fixed | None | AC4 |
| X5 | A breaking change is made to an interface, a column, the key rule or the envelope | The change raises major version 2 and a new `ce_type`; v1 is never edited in place and stays readable | None | AC5 |
| X6 | A consuming service ships without the drift test, or a schema change breaks a consumer | The registry refuses the change and the drift test fails the build | None | AC6 |
| X7 | A value the consumers need is named by no source — the full column set, the hash algorithm, the payload schema or the incident route | The value is published as the working read of the assumption, and the gap stays open | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1403; ASM-2443) | Section 3 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Publishes a document, a DDL template and fakes; builds against nothing, reads no business data and starts on Day 1 |
| Negotiable | Column widths, the hash algorithm and the fixture set are open until v1 is frozen; the interfaces, the seven field groups, the key rule and the versioning rule are fixed |
| Valuable | Unblocks all 19 services and the P7 ingest on Day 1 and keeps one shared decision table out of every service plan |
| Estimable | Three interfaces, one record shape, one DDL template, one envelope, two rules and five fakes |
| Small | One sprint for the document, the template, the fakes and the lint rules |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one lint, schema or fake assertion in section 16 |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: local decision-record library contract

  Background:
    Given the platform library contract document is published with major version 1
    Given the 19 services have one schema and one login each
    Given the contract declares no REST base, no topic and no queue of its own

  Scenario: AC1 The interfaces, the MANDATORY transaction rule and the exceptions are published (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the interface section of the contract document
    When it is validated and linted
    Then it publishes DecisionRecordWriter.record(DecisionRecord) returning DecisionRecordEntryRef, annotated with propagation MANDATORY
    Then DecisionRecordEntryRef carries entryId, chainSeq, entryHash and repeated
    Then the write declares DecisionLogRecordInvalidException with messageId MSG-P7-009 and field, and DecisionLogUnavailableException with messageId MSG-P7-003, and no other thrown type
    Then a call with no open transaction throws IllegalTransactionStateException before any write
    Then no interface method opens, commits or rolls back a transaction and no method calls another service

  Scenario: AC2 The record shape carries the seven field groups with the access-event exception (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the record-shape section of the document and its worked example
    When the schema is validated
    Then the shape carries the decision code, the subject case, the version group, the inputs reference, the recommendation and final call, the approver with an approval level, and the actor with the decided-at time
    Then the version group requires at least one of rule version, model version and agent version, and a rule ID requires its rule version
    Then an access event carries no case and requires no subject group, and every other group stays required
    Then the example uses only the legacy values, with decision code D6, final call OWNER_ASSIGNED, rule ALLOC-MTG-BKK-01 of ALLOC-2026.11 and case RW-2026-000123

  Scenario: AC3 The DDL template creates decision_record in each service's own schema (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the DDL template of the contract
    When it is applied twice, in two throwaway schemas, through each service's own Flyway sequence
    Then it creates decision_record in the applying schema only, with the chain columns chain_seq, prev_hash and entry_hash
    Then it declares the unique key on idempotency_key and the unique key on chain_seq
    Then it installs the append-only rule that refuses an update and a delete
    Then it declares no foreign key and no reference to another service's schema
    Then a hand-written table that drifts from the template fails the drift test

  Scenario: AC4 The DecisionRecorded envelope is fixed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the envelope section of the document
    When one record is validated against it
    Then the event is rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1 published on the shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1 in CloudEvents 1.0 binary mode with ce_specversion 1.0, ce_id, ce_type, ce_source, ce_subject, ce_time and the trace header
    Then the record key is caseId where the record has a case, and the entry id where it does not
    Then the payload carries the entry id, the case where there is one, the decision code, the final call, the rule ID, the rule version, the chain sequence, the entry hash and the actor reference
    Then the payload carries no personal data and no free text beyond the legacy fields
    Then the registry holds one accepted schema version and refuses a body that does not match it

  Scenario: AC5 Versioning separates a compatible change from a new major version (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the versioning section of the document
    When a change is proposed to a published element
    Then a backward-compatible change keeps major version 1 and the ce_type version, and is accepted by the registry in BACKWARD mode
    Then a breaking change raises major version 2 and a new ce_type, and v1 is never edited in place
    Then a consuming service pins a published version and raises a change request rather than a private variant

  Scenario: AC6 The fake answers the document and every consuming service runs the drift test (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the fake set generated from the document
    When the contract test runs the writer fake, the chain fixture, the outbox fake, the registry fake and the P7 ledger fake
    Then the writer fake returns an entry reference with chain sequence and entry hash, refuses with MSG-P7-009 and the field name, and repeats a key with repeated true
    Then the chain fixture answers a first record and a second record linked to the first, and refuses an update
    Then the outbox fake records the event in the caller's transaction and answers absent after a rollback
    Then the drift test of every consuming service fails on any difference from section 12 and section 13
```

These criteria are new and test only the contract deliverable: no legacy acceptance criterion is repeated here — **AC1 to AC7 of RWB-E1-027 stay with RWB-P7-E1027-APP** — and every identifier comes from the legacy story, Architecture v5 or the Temporal and Drools Design, character for character.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The library publishes three interfaces and nothing else, and the write is declared with propagation MANDATORY so that it joins the caller's transaction and opens none | RWB-E1-027 section 12; ADR-022; Architecture v5 slide 28 |
| BR2 | The record carries the seven field groups; the subject case and the version group are not required for an access event, and every other group is required for every record | RWB-E1-027 BR2, BR3, BR4; DF-DEC-002 to DF-DEC-016 |
| BR3 | The table is a library object owned by PLT and created in each service's own schema by the DDL template, append-only, with the chain columns and the unique idempotency key | DP-01; DP-15; Architecture v5 slide 20; Ownership Map |
| BR4 | `DecisionRecorded` is published on the shared topic in CloudEvents 1.0 binary mode with the type and the key rule of section 12.3 | DP-09; ADR-015; Architecture v5 slides 20, 22 and 42 |
| BR5 | A refused record names the field with MSG-P7-009; a failed append raises with MSG-P7-003 and the caller's transaction rolls back | R-UNI-39; REQ-DRI-005; RWB-E1-027 sections 4 and 14 |
| BR6 | The same idempotency key gives one record, the first entry reference and a counted repeat | R-UNI-40; RWB-E1-027 BR6 |
| BR7 | A published version is never edited: a backward-compatible change stays in major version 1 and a breaking change raises major version 2 with a new `ce_type` | Template and Rules §R7.2; §R5.4 class C |
| BR8 | The ledger stays P7's: `decision_log_entry` in `rwb_decision` is named only, and no consumer of this contract reads or writes it directly | DP-01; Ownership Map row `decision_log_entry`; Architecture v5 slide 41 |
| BR9 | The contract writes no data-lake copy and no reporting copy; the legacy copy RWB-E1-014 is retired and its dependencies are dropped | DP-17; ADR-018; Template and Rules §R6 |
| BR10 | The message identifiers MSG-P7-009 and MSG-P7-003 are kept unchanged although the store moved, so every record and report that cites them stays readable | ASM-2443 |

##### 9. State transitions

None in this story: a document has no runtime state. Two vocabularies are fixed here and the implementation behind them is specified in RWB-PLT-E1027-APP section 9.

| Object | State | Meaning in the contract |
|---|---|---|
| Decision record | Unwritten | The caller has opened the transaction and not yet called the library |
| Decision record | Validated | The seven field groups passed and the idempotency key is new |
| Decision record | Written in the transaction | The row is appended with its chain link and is visible inside the caller's transaction |
| Decision record | Committed | The caller committed; the action, the row and the outbox row are stored together |
| Decision record | Refused | A field group failed; nothing is stored and the field is named |
| Decision record | Repeated | The key already existed; the first entry reference is returned and the repeat counted |
| DecisionRecorded | Published | The caller's outbox relay published the event on the shared topic |
| DecisionRecorded | Absent | The caller's transaction rolled back; no event exists |
| Contract version | v1 | The published version every consuming service pins |
| Contract version | v2 | Raised by a breaking change, with a new `ce_type`; v1 stays readable and is never edited |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The contract author (any team, per U3) | Writes and versions the document, the DDL template, the envelope section and the fakes |
| The platform owner of the library | Approves a breaking change and freezes a version |
| The service teams of the 19 services | Consume the contract, pin the version, raise a change request rather than a private variant |
| The rwb-decision owner (P7) | Confirms the ledger side: the ingest, the chain check and the two read operations that this contract announces to |
| The rwb-case owner (P3) | Confirms the parameters and reference-data operations the decision code and approval-level lists are read from |
| RW-PLATADM | Receives the incident that the implementation raises when a record cannot be written |
| RW-AUDIT, RW-COE | Audit the records through the P7 ledger, not through this contract |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A library contract is a technical artefact, not a credit decision |

No personal name, no email address and no credential appears in the document, the template, an example or a fake. Where a caller or an operator must be named, the example uses a role code or a user identifier only.

##### 11. Data

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Business data published | None. The document publishes signatures, the record shape, codes, status values and message identifiers; no customer, account or case value appears |
| Record shape published | The seven field groups of section 12.2 and the chain columns, with one worked example from the legacy story |
| Personal data | None. The actor is a reference such as `SY-CASEWF` or a user identifier, never a name; no account number, national identifier or document content appears |
| Tables published | `decision_record` only, as a DDL template applied in each service's own schema; the central `decision_log_entry` is P7's and is named only |
| Field identifiers | The record fields carry the legacy identifiers DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018, DF-DEC-030 and DF-DEC-031; the list values carry DF-REF-028 and DF-REF-029 |
| Retention | The table is append-only in each service's schema and keeps every record; the retention period of a local record is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1403; ASM-2443) |

The record shape is the one place where a rule value could leak into the contract, so the document fixes that a record carries codes and identifiers, the rule ID and the version label, and never the DRL, the payload of a rule evaluation or a personal field.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None — the library is in process and publishes Java interfaces, a DDL template and an envelope, not an OpenAPI document. The two ledger reads belong to P7 rwb-decision under `/api/recovery/decision/v1` and are named in section 19, not declared here.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None — the library joins the caller's transaction and calls no service. The decision code and approval-level lists reach it through the parameters and reference-data client libraries, whose REST consumption belongs to RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and RWB-PLT-E1043-CON.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Key | Payload carries | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1 | rwb.decision-record.v1 (shared topic) | `caseId` where the record has a case; the entry id where it does not | entry id, case ID where there is one, decision code, final call, rule ID, rule version, chain sequence, entry hash, actor reference | Announces every record to the P7 central ledger and to rwb-reporting; written to the caller's outbox in the same transaction |

| Envelope element | Value |
|---|---|
| Mode | CloudEvents 1.0, binary mode |
| ce_specversion | 1.0 |
| ce_type | rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1 |
| ce_source | The producing service |
| ce_subject | The case ID where there is one, the entry id where there is not |
| ce_id and traceparent | The event identifier and the W3C trace context of the caller |
| Payload | Identifiers and facts only; no personal data and no free text beyond the legacy fields |

The event name follows the §R4 naming rule while the topic keeps the shared name `rwb.decision-record.v1` (ASM-2444). The key rule for a record with no case, the exact payload schema beyond the fields listed and the `ce_subject` format are Not specified in the source documents and are published as the working read (GAP-1403; ASM-2443).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None — the library consumes no event. The chain check of P7 reads the table through its own contract and is not a subscription of this library.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None — the contract defines no workflow and no activity. The library is called from inside the caller's own activity on the caller's own task queue, and a workflow class never calls it, so a replay reuses the recorded decision (DP-10).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None — the legacy JOB-14 chain check is a P7 Schedule at 02:00 and is named in section 19 as out of scope; this contract declares no Schedule (RWB-P7-E1027-APP).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| decision_record | PLT | Contract shape of the local record: the seven field groups, the chain columns `chain_seq`, `prev_hash` and `entry_hash`, the unique key on `idempotency_key` and the append-only rule. Each service applies the template in its own schema |

The table is a library object owned by PLT and created in each service's own schema through that service's own Flyway sequence and login; the contract does not create a schema, a login or a table in another service's schema and declares no foreign key across a service boundary (DP-01, DP-15). The central `decision_log_entry` is P7's, lives in `rwb_decision` and is named here only: this contract neither creates it nor writes it, and no consumer of the contract reads it directly (BR8).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Answers |
|---|---|---|
| Writer fake | `DecisionRecordWriter`, `DecisionRecord` and `DecisionRecordEntryRef` | An accepted record with chain sequence and entry hash; a refusal with MSG-P7-009 and the field name; a repeated key with `repeated` true; a call with no transaction throwing IllegalTransactionStateException |
| Chain fixture | The chain columns and the append-only rule | A first record with chain sequence one and no `prev_hash`; a second linked to the first; a refused update and a refused delete |
| Outbox fake | `OutboxWriter` of RWB-PLT-TE006-CON | An event recorded in the caller's transaction, and absent after a rollback |
| Registry fake | The schema registry | BACKWARD mode with one accepted and one refused `DecisionRecorded` body |
| P7 ledger fake | The contract of RWB-P7-E1027-CON | One ledger entry per event, with the entry id, the chain sequence and the 5-minute completeness boundary |

The fakes answer from the same example set as the document, so a change to the contract shows up as a contract-test failure in a consuming service rather than as a surprise at run time.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Provided | Consumed | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| REST | 0: the contract publishes interfaces, a template and an envelope | 0 | The two client libraries consume the rwb-case operations |
| Kafka | 1 event type fixed by the contract, published by the caller through its outbox | 0 | AsyncAPI 3.0, CloudEvents 1.0 binary mode, key `caseId` or entry id on the shared topic |
| Temporal | 0 | 0 | No workflow, no activity and no Schedule; the caller's activity calls the library |
| File | 0 | 0 | No file crosses the contract |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Shared library contract artefact of the platform: the three interfaces in `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.platform.api`, the record type and the entry reference with them, the DDL template as a resource, and the envelope and versioning rules in the contract document. The implementation is RWB-PLT-E1027-APP. The artefact coordinates and the publication channel are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1403; ASM-2443).

**Interface surface**

| Interface | Signature | Returns or throws |
|---|---|---|
| `DecisionRecordWriter` | `DecisionRecordEntryRef record(DecisionRecord record)` annotated `@Transactional(propagation = Propagation.MANDATORY)` | The entry reference; throws `DecisionLogRecordInvalidException` (MSG-P7-009, field) and `DecisionLogUnavailableException` (MSG-P7-003) |
| `DecisionRecord` | The seven field groups: idempotencyKey, caseId, decisionCode, ruleId, ruleVersion, modelVersion, agentVersion, inputsRef, recommendation, approverUserId, approvalLevel, finalCall, actions, outcome, actorUserRef, decidedAt | The record the caller assembles from values it already holds |
| `DecisionRecordEntryRef` | `entryId`, `chainSeq`, `entryHash`, `repeated` | The first entry reference of an idempotency key |

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables. The contract declares the table in the applying schema only | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`. This story is the contract of that library | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library; the decision code per event is a parameter read as a value in force | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case; the decision code and approval-level lists are reference rows | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents. The contract fixes the `DecisionRecorded` envelope the caller's outbox carries | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit; the contract states the library is called in an activity and the chain check stays a P7 Schedule | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout; the record is handed in process inside the caller's transaction and the ledger is reached through its contract | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1`; the contract adds no path and the ledger reads stay under the decision base | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema; the DDL template is applied by each service's own sequence | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting. The legacy lake copy of the decision log is retired and the contract declares no copy | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route; the ledger view for a screen is out of scope here | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |

**Hardware and software change.** The contract moves the decision record from one `decision_log_entry` table in the monolith's `recovery` schema to a template that every service applies in its own schema, fixes the record inside the caller's transaction with `MANDATORY`, fixes the chain columns per schema, and fixes one envelope on one shared topic for all 19 producers. Governance and the central log stay in rwb-decision. No new hardware is implied: the template is applied by each service's own Flyway run in the existing ACE PostgreSQL server, and the events use the Kafka platform ACE already runs.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `DecisionRecordWriter` | Published interface | The one write method, its `MANDATORY` rule and its two exceptions (BR1, BR5) |
| `DecisionRecord` and `DecisionRecordEntryRef` | Published types | The seven field groups and the entry reference (BR1, BR2) |
| DecisionRecordDdlTemplate | Resource | The `decision_record` DDL: columns, keys, chain columns and append-only rule (BR3) |
| EnvelopeSpecification | Document | The CloudEvents 1.0 binary-mode attribute set, the `ce_type`, the key rule and the payload fields (BR4) |
| VersioningSpecification | Document | Major version 1, the compatible versus breaking rule and the pinning rule (BR7) |
| Fake set and fixtures | Test asset | The writer, chain, outbox, registry and ledger fakes used by every consuming service (AC6) |

**Build steps**

1. Write the three interfaces, the record type and the entry reference, taken from the legacy published interface; lint the `MANDATORY` rule and the throw-before-write rule (AC1).
2. Write the record-shape section with the seven field groups, the access-event exception and the legacy example (AC2).
3. Write the DDL template and apply it twice in two throwaway schemas; assert the chain columns, the unique keys, the append-only rule and the absence of a cross-schema key (AC3).
4. Write the envelope section and validate one record against the registry fake; assert the type, the key and the payload fields (AC4).
5. Write the transaction and idempotency rules into the interface documentation; test the repeated key and the missing transaction on the writer fake (AC1, AC6).
6. Write the versioning section with the compatible and breaking examples (AC5).
7. Generate the fake set and write the drift test; wire it into the build of every consuming service (AC6).
8. Publish v1 and record the pinned version of RWB-PLT-E1027-APP and of each consuming service.

**Done when.** The document and the template validate, the two throwaway applications prove the reusability, the fake set answers every criterion including the refusal, the repeat and the absent event, the drift test is green on the build of this story and on the build of RWB-PLT-E1027-APP, and v1 is published with the pinned versions recorded.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Published as |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-009 | A record is refused for a missing or invalid field (written to the service log and the incident, not shown to customers) | The decision record was refused: {field} is missing or not valid. | `DecisionLogRecordInvalidException`, messageId MSG-P7-009, with `field` |
| MSG-P7-003 | The record cannot be written and the action is not taken | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | `DecisionLogUnavailableException`, messageId MSG-P7-003 |
| MSG-P3-013 | Allocation not made because the write failed (shown by the allocation summary of the caller) | The case was not allocated because the decision could not be recorded. It will be tried again in the next run. | Named only; the caller owns the display |

The three texts are copied unchanged from RWB-E1-027 and this contract adds no message ID. The field names are `versions`, `ruleVersion` and `decisionCode` for the three refusals of the legacy criteria. The published catalogue entry format for MSG-P7-009 and MSG-P7-003 is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1403; ASM-2443). Thai text follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story, and the contract declares none: the library has no user interface and answers inside the caller's transaction. The ledger view and the decision-log screens are reached through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) and belong to RWB-P7-E1027-APP; a refused record appears as an incident, not as a screen error.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the decision codes and approval levels are values in force in the owner's data, and the only values this document fixes are the legacy example values.
- No personal data in a schema, an example, a fake or a log: the actor is a reference, the subject is a case or document identifier, and the scan fails the build otherwise.
- No cross-schema reference in the DDL template and no foreign key across services; the boundary test fails the build.
- No write path to `decision_record` other than the library, no update path at all, and the architecture test is part of the contract test of every consuming service.
- No REST surface and no topic of the library's own: the shared topic belongs to the event platform and the ledger reads to P7.
- The library writes no ledger row, raises no case event and no task, and writes no data-lake or reporting copy.
- A published version is never edited in place: a breaking change raises major version 2 with a new `ce_type` and a migration note.
