**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: integration slice of RWB-E1-030 for RWB-ITG-W1. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **QA integration engineer**, I want **the end-to-end proof of the RWB-E1-030 daily rebalancing and queue measures across P3 rwb-case (the JOB-06 Schedule, assignment, queue_measure, decision records), P7 rwb-decision (the central ledger) and P9 rwb-reporting (the published measures), with P1 rwb-source-data serving the job catalogue**, so that **rebalancing, reconciliation and measures are proved on the real wave 1 services before the wave exits**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story moves work left in overflow or without an owner each morning, takes owners above the cap back inside it (R-UNI-19), and takes one snapshot per queue at one time: depth, unassigned, age in days from the entry date, owner spread and SERVICE_LEVEL timers EXPIRED. It runs JOB-06 on Quartz at 06:30, copies the snapshot to the data lake by JOB-15, and publishes the interface `recovery.casewf.rebalance.QueueMeasureService`, which P9 reads for Power BI (RWB-E1-030 sections 4 and 12). Every move is logged with the decision record written before it takes effect, and the measures publish only when every queue depth reconciles to the case list with zero difference.

The target changes the mechanism and the delivery path, not the behaviour. DP-10 replaces Quartz with a Temporal Schedule in rwb-case (Arch v5 slide 44, JOB-06 at 06:30, overlap SKIP, catch-up window), so the run belongs to the service that owns the cases and the ACE shared Quartz tables are no longer used. DP-03 makes each move write a local decision record in rwb_case in the same transaction as the assignment change and publish `DecisionRecorded` to `rwb.decision-record.v1`, collected by P7 rwb-decision within five minutes (ADR-022). DP-17 removes the data lake: the measures reach P9 rwb-reporting as a projection from events, JOB-13 ingests the decision records continuously and JOB-15 is an Airflow trigger with no lake copy. DP-13 and DP-14 rename the base to `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` and the topic to `rwb.<short>.events.v1`. DP-01 keeps `queue_measure` in `rwb_case`, where the case and the assignment live.

The target split of the legacy key is therefore: RWB-P3-E1030-APP owns the Schedule, the assignment and cap logic, the hold checks, the snapshot and its reconciliation, the breach alert and the local decision record; RWB-P7-E1030-APP owns the central ledger and its collection of `rwb.decision-record.v1`. This integration story owns no legacy acceptance criterion: legacy AC1 to AC10 sit at component level with those two app stories, and the scenarios of section 7 are the integration proof that the same behaviour holds when the three services and the two topics are wired together in SIT. One consumed operation needs a word here. The job catalogue of P1 rwb-source-data — `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs` and `POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs/JOB-06/rerun` — is a CON-level platform contract with no APP story in this lane, so it is not in the integration dependency list, and the measure read of P9 rwb-reporting is the wave 1 reporting projection of the same legacy measures, not an APP story of this legacy key.

Where the sources do not fix the details the suite needs, the suite asserts through the owners' contracts and records the open point: the Schedule identifier and the exact rerun façade at the nominal run time (GAP-0354; ASM-0448), the event that marks a measure as published (GAP-0354; ASM-0449), and the scope of the test-only fault switch on the decision-record library (GAP-0354; ASM-0450). Release 30 November 2026 stays tentative, and a date is never a condition of this story.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P3-E1030-APP is done: the JOB-06 Schedule, the assignment and cap logic, the hold checks, the one-transaction move with its decision record, `queue_measure`, the snapshot reconciliation and the breach alert are in SIT on rwb-case.
- RWB-P7-E1030-APP is done: the central ledger collects `rwb.decision-record.v1` idempotently and the ledger query answers by case, decision code and date.
- The published contracts of P3 rwb-case, P7 rwb-decision and P9 rwb-reporting, and the P1 rwb-source-data job catalogue, are deployed under their per-service bases behind gateway-bff, and the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG is available with its synthetic cases, queues, members and caps for business date 2026-12-02.
- The capacity caps are loaded as data rows (DL23), with the queue method LOWEST_LOAD of queue TDR-BKK-CO a configuration row and not code, and the queue and member reference data and the measure definitions are read through the P3 parameters and reference-data contracts with the codes sent as data.
- SIT is in place: namespace `rwb-recovery`, the task queues `rwb-case`, `rwb-decision` and `rwb-reporting`, and the topics `rwb.case.events.v1`, `rwb.decision-record.v1` and `rwb.reporting.events.v1` with their retry and `.dlt` topics, and the clock control of the harness can move the nominal Schedule time to 06:30 on 2026-12-02 and restore it afterwards.
- The agreed test-only fault switch on the P3 decision-record library can fail the record write for one case (AC6) and for every move (AC11), and it is agreed with the service owner.
- No production data is used and no production connection is opened; the suite refuses an environment that is not SIT, and release 30 November 2026 is tentative.
- This story has no build dependency, so it is ready on Day 1 under Template and Rules §R5.7; the Schedule identifier in SIT and the exact rerun façade at the nominal run time are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0354; ASM-0448).

##### 4. Flow

1. QA integration engineer: seeds the synthetic cases, queues, members and caps of the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG for business date 2026-12-02, with cap 150 on TDR-BKK-CO, members U-61 and U-62 at 140 and 144 open cases and 12 cases with no owner; no production data is used.
2. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues` and `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/cases` before the run, records the queue depth, the unassigned count and the owner spread, and moves the clock to 06:30 on business date 2026-12-02 so the JOB-06 Schedule fires.
3. System: rwb-case assigns the unassigned cases and moves the newest cases off owners above the cap, skipping cases with `deviation_open` or `legal_hold` true, with reason REBALANCE, writing the assignment and the local decision record in one transaction.
4. Harness: reads the queues and their cases after the run, reads `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` for each moved case and asserts the new owner with the same status and stage, and reads `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers` for case RW-2026-000501 to take the expired service-level timer as the breach the next snapshot must count.
5. Harness: waits on `rwb.case.CaseTransferred.v1` on `rwb.case.events.v1` for one event per move and on `rwb.case.TimerBreached.v1` for the breach, and asserts the CloudEvents envelope and the case ID key.
6. Harness: waits on `rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` for every move, reads `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` and measures the elapsed collection of each record against the five-minute target.
7. Harness: takes the snapshot at 2026-12-02 06:52, reads `GET /api/recovery/reporting/v1/reports/measures` for the business date and reconciles every queue depth to `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases` at the snapshot time, with zero difference.
8. Harness: triggers a rerun through `POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs/JOB-06/rerun` and asserts that no case moves and no decision record is written on the same business date.
9. Harness: runs the negative cases — no member with capacity, no cap, held cases and the owner exactly at the cap, a failed record for one case, every record failing, a snapshot depth that differs from the case list, and a caller without Platform administration U — records every status, message and count, proves from the call set of the run that no lake endpoint is called, then writes the evidence report, removes the synthetic fixtures and restores the clock.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | No member of the queue has capacity | The cases keep no owner and are counted in the run summary | MSG-P3-011 | AC4 |
| X2 | No capacity cap is loaded for the queue | The queue is reported and no case in it is moved | None | AC5 |
| X3 | The local decision record write fails for one case | That case stays with its owner, the run continues for the other cases, and the run record names the case that stayed | MSG-P7-003 | AC6 |
| X4 | JOB-06 runs again on the same business date | An already balanced queue gives no further move and no further record | None | AC7 |
| X5 | A case has an open deviation or a legal hold | The case is not moved and the next newest case is taken instead | None | AC8 |
| X6 | The snapshot depth differs from the case count at the same time | The snapshot is held, nothing is published for the date, and the break is listed for the data steward | MSG-P3-029 | AC9 |
| X7 | An owner holds exactly the cap | No case is moved off that owner | None | AC8 |
| X8 | A role without Platform administration U reruns JOB-06 | Refused with status 403, no run starts and no case moves | MSG-P4-002 | AC10 |
| X9 | The decision record write fails for every move of the run | Nothing moves, no partial run is left and every case of the run is reported | MSG-P7-003 | AC11 |
| X10 | A consumed call exceeds the 2 s timeout or returns a server error | The call is retried once under the suite policy and the evidence report records it; no assertion is made on data that was not read | None | AC1, AC2 |
| X11 | The fixture set does not match the harness expectations, or the clock control cannot move the nominal Schedule time | The suite fails as a harness fault and names the element; no service defect is raised | None | AC1, AC3 |

X1 to X9 are the exception paths of the legacy story read on the wave 1 services; X10 and X11 are the suite's own failure modes, so that a timeout never becomes a pass and a fixture or clock fault is reported as a harness fault rather than as a service defect.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | The suite is its own module and reuses the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG; it needs the two APP stories and the published contracts of P1, P3, P7 and P9, not their source code |
| Negotiable | The fixture sizes, the clock control, the wait windows and the rerun façade are properties of the harness; the story fixes the assertions, the values and the call set |
| Valuable | Rebalancing, the ledger and the measures are proved on the real services, and the five-minute collection and the reconciliation are measured rather than assumed, before wave 1 exits |
| Estimable | One suite module, one fixture pack, one clock control, two assertions (reconciliation and ledger completeness) and one evidence report |
| Small | Eleven scenarios over four services, three topics and one Schedule; no service code and no schema change |
| Testable | Every scenario asserts a contract response, an event, a status, a message or a count; all data is synthetic |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Daily rebalancing and queue measures, end-to-end across wave 1 services

  Background:
    Given the wave 1 services rwb-case, rwb-decision and rwb-reporting are deployed in SIT with their published contracts behind gateway-bff
    Given the RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG synthetic cases, queues, members and caps are loaded and no production data is used
    Given the business date is 2026-12-02

  Scenario: AC1 The 06:30 Schedule rebalances through the case contract (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given queue "TDR-BKK-CO" uses "LOWEST_LOAD" with cap 150
    Given 12 cases with no owner
    Given members U-61 and U-62 hold 140 and 144 open cases
    When the JOB-06 Schedule fires at 06:30
    Then the 12 cases are assigned, 8 to U-61 and 4 to U-62, by lowest load with ties going to the member first in the queue list
    Then each case read through GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId} shows its new owner with the same status and stage
    Then one CaseTransferred event is published on rwb.case.events.v1 for each move

  Scenario: AC2 The measures reconcile and reach reporting without a lake (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the snapshot is taken at 2026-12-02 06:52
    When the queue measures are published
    Then GET /api/recovery/reporting/v1/reports/measures for 2026-12-02 shows for every queue a depth equal to the case count of that queue at 06:52
    Then "TDR-BKK-CO" shows depth 296, unassigned 0 and an average age of 41 days
    Then no lake endpoint is called and the measures reach rwb-reporting only through its published topic (DP-17)

  Scenario: AC3 A service-level breach reaches the team manager (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given case RW-2026-000501 in "TDR-BKK-CO" passes its service level
    When the timer check raises the breach
    Then the team manager of "TDR-BKK" receives MSG-P3-028 with count 1 and queue "TDR-BKK-CO"
    Then the next snapshot shows 1 breach for that queue

  Scenario: AC4 No member has capacity (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given every member of "TDR-BKK-CO" holds 150 open cases and 5 cases have no owner
    When JOB-06 runs
    Then the 5 cases keep no owner
    Then the team manager receives MSG-P3-011 with count 5

  Scenario: AC5 No cap loaded (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given queue "WO-BKK-CO" has no capacity cap
    When JOB-06 runs
    Then no case in "WO-BKK-CO" is moved
    Then the snapshot still reports "WO-BKK-CO"

  Scenario: AC6 A failed decision record stops that case only (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given owner U-63 holds 153 open cases and the local decision record write fails for the second of the 3 newest cases
    When JOB-06 runs
    Then 2 cases move off U-63 and 1 stays
    Then the job record lists the case that stayed with MSG-P7-003
    Then each moved case has one entry in GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log within five minutes

  Scenario: AC7 A repeated run (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given JOB-06 has balanced "TDR-BKK-CO" on 2026-12-02
    When JOB-06 runs again on the same business date
    Then no case is moved
    Then no decision record is written

  Scenario: AC8 Held cases and the cap edge (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given owner U-64 holds 152 open cases and the 2 newest have deviation_open = true
    When JOB-06 runs
    Then those 2 cases stay with U-64 and the next 2 newest are moved
    Then owner U-65 holding exactly 150 open cases loses no case

  Scenario: AC9 A count difference holds the snapshot (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the snapshot depth for "DIL-BKK-CO" is 88 and the case count at the same time is 87
    When the snapshot is checked
    Then it is not published
    Then the data steward receives MSG-P3-029 with check "queue depth against case list"

  Scenario: AC10 A role without the right cannot rerun (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given test user "U-7101" holds RW-CASEOWN
    When the user calls POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs/JOB-06/rerun
    Then the call returns status 403 with MSG-P4-002
    Then no run starts and no case moves

  Scenario: AC11 Every record failing means nothing moves (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the local decision record write is switched to fail for every move by the agreed test-only fault switch
    When JOB-06 runs
    Then no assignment changes and no partial run is left
    Then no decision record exists for the business date
    Then each case is reported with MSG-P7-003
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Cases with no owner are assigned by the queue's method within the cap | queue.assignment_method, queue.capacity_cap; FEAT-CWC-17 |
| BR2 | An owner above the cap loses the newest cases until inside the cap | R-UNI-19 |
| BR3 | Cases with an open deviation or a legal hold are not moved | R-UNI-20; R-DEV-01 |
| BR4 | A queue with no cap is reported and not rebalanced | DL23 |
| BR5 | A move keeps the case status and the clocks | R-UNI-18 |
| BR6 | Measures publish only when queue depths reconcile to the case list with zero difference | DL25; REC-01 |
| BR7 | Every move is logged before it takes effect | Principle 5; R-UNI-39 |
| BR8 | A breach raises an alert to the escalation role; the case does not move | R-UNI-30 |
| BR9 | JOB-06 is a Temporal Schedule in rwb-case at 06:30 with overlap SKIP and catch-up, replacing Quartz | DP-10; Arch v5 slide 44 |
| BR10 | Each move writes its local decision record in rwb_case in the same transaction and publishes DecisionRecorded, and P7 collects it within five minutes | DP-03; ADR-022 |
| BR11 | Queue measures reach rwb-reporting as a projection from events, and a measure publishes only when reconciled with zero difference, with no data lake | DP-17; DL25 |
| BR12 | Every cross-service call is one hop with a 2 s timeout | ADR-020; DP-11 |

##### 9. State transitions

None for the case status. This story does not change a case status. It observes the owner of a case and its assignment moving with reason REBALANCE, and the state of a measure snapshot moving from TAKEN to PUBLISHED or to HELD, all of them read through the owners' contracts and the owner topics and none of them changed directly.

| Object | State | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Assignment (rwb_case) | Moved to a new owner | The old assignment ends and a new one is written with reason REBALANCE in the same transaction as the local decision record; `recovery_case.owner_user_id` names the new owner, read through `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}`, and the case status, the stage and the clocks are unchanged (R-UNI-18) |
| Measure snapshot (rwb_case) | TAKEN | One snapshot per queue at one time: depth, unassigned, average age in days from the entry date, owner spread and expired SERVICE_LEVEL timers |
| Measure snapshot (rwb_case) | PUBLISHED | Every queue depth reconciles to the case list with zero difference; the measures are projected into rwb-reporting and published for the business date |
| Measure snapshot (rwb_case) | HELD | At least one queue differs from the case list at the same time; nothing is published for the date and the data steward receives MSG-P3-029 |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary, copied from RWB-E1-030. The legacy story writes these tables in the monolith. In the target `queue_measure`, `assignment`, `recovery_case` and `timer` stay in `rwb_case` (DP-01), the local decision record is written in `rwb_case` and collected into the ledger of `rwb_decision` (DP-03), and the measures are a projection in `rwb_reporting` (DP-17). The suite reads every one of them only through the contracts of section 12.2, or through an event of section 12.4, and writes no schema of its own and no row of another service.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The suite provides no REST operation. The names reserved for P2 rwb-integration — `/api/recovery/integration/v1`, `rwb.integration.events.v1`, `rwb-integration` and `rwb_integration` — are not used, and no rwb_integration table is written.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method and path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues | P3 rwb-case | Read the queues, their method, their cap and the team before and after the run |
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/cases | P3 rwb-case | Read the cases of a queue with their owner and assignment time before and after the run |
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases | P3 rwb-case | Read the case list of the business date for the reconciliation of every queue depth at the snapshot time |
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId} | P3 rwb-case | Read one moved case: the new owner with the same status and stage |
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers | P3 rwb-case | Read the expired service-level timer of the breach case |
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters | P3 rwb-case | Read the parameters and the queue reference data as rows, not as code |
| GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs and POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs/JOB-06/rerun | P1 rwb-source-data, job catalogue | Read the job catalogue and trigger one rerun of JOB-06; the exact façade is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0354; ASM-0448) |
| GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log | P7 rwb-decision | Confirm the collection of every decision record of the run and measure the elapsed time against five minutes |
| GET /api/recovery/reporting/v1/reports/measures | P9 rwb-reporting | Read the published measures of business date 2026-12-02 for the reconciliation and the breach count |

Every call is one hop to the owning service on its own base with a 2 s timeout (ADR-020, DP-11, DP-13); the P1 job catalogue is a CON-level platform contract with no APP story in this lane, and it is consumed here for the catalogue read and the rerun.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The suite publishes no event. Every event asserted in this story is produced by a service and is listed in 12.4.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Producer | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| rwb.case.CaseTransferred.v1 | rwb.case.events.v1 | P3 rwb-case | One event per move; the suite counts the moves of the run against it |
| rwb.case.TimerBreached.v1 | rwb.case.events.v1 | P3 rwb-case | The breach the next snapshot must count for the queue |
| rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1 | rwb.decision-record.v1 | every service, with the ledger owned by P7 rwb-decision | The record of each move; the suite measures the collection against the five-minute target |
| rwb.reporting.ReportPublished.v1 | rwb.reporting.events.v1 | P9 rwb-reporting | Marks the measures of the business date as published; whether P9 signals one event per measure or per snapshot is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0354; ASM-0449) |

All four are consumed in the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, keyed caseId, with the inbox dedupe of the consumer and the retry and `.dlt` topics of the owner (ADR-015; Arch v5 slides 42 and 43). The suite asserts on IDs and facts only and writes no payload of its own.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| CaseWorkflow | Workflow, parent per case | rwb-case | Holds the case; the suite observes its record through the case read and takes no part in its order of steps |
| DailyCaseRun | Workflow started by AceDataReady and by its Schedule | rwb-case | Runs JOB-03 as a step, so the business date is allocated before the JOB-06 run |
| JOB-06 Schedule | Temporal Schedule | rwb-case | Fires the rebalancing at 06:30 with overlap SKIP and the platform catch-up window; the suite moves the test clock to the nominal time |
| allocate, transfer, rebalance | Activities | rwb-case | Read the queue and the members, choose the owner, write the assignment and the local decision record in one transaction |

All four are registered by RWB-P3-E1030-APP; this story starts the Schedule only through its nominal time and the rerun, and it adds no workflow and no activity of its own.

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Schedule | Cadence | Registration | Legacy reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| JOB-06 Daily rebalancing | Daily at 06:30, overlap SKIP, catch-up window per platform default | Registered by the rwb-case release on task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery`; the Schedule identifier in SIT is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0354; ASM-0448) | JOB-06 Rebalancing (Arch v5 slide 44) |
| JOB-03 Morning allocation | A step of DailyCaseRun, started by AceDataReady, after 02 and by 07:00 | Runs in rwb-case, not a Schedule of its own | JOB-03 Morning allocation (Arch v5 slide 44) |

The suite starts no Schedule, moves no Schedule and waits for no Schedule of its own. It moves its own test clock to 06:30 on 2026-12-02 so the nominal fire time is reached, and for the rerun cases it calls the job-catalogue rerun of section 12.2. The exact rerun façade at the nominal run time is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0354; ASM-0448).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The suite owns no table and never reads another service's schema (DP-01). The tables it exercises belong to `rwb_case`, `rwb_decision` and `rwb_reporting` and are listed in section 11 with their owners.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

None. No service contract is faked: every call in section 12.2 and every event in 12.4 is made to the real SIT service and the real topic. Two interventions are agreed, and they are the only ones in a running service:

| Intervention | Stands in for | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Test-only fault switch on the P3 decision-record library | A record write that fails | Fails one case in AC6 and every move in AC11; its exact scope and reset are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0354; ASM-0450) |
| Clock control | The passage of time to 06:30 | Moves the nominal Schedule fire time for the business date and is restored after the run; it changes no business rule |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Provided by the suite | Consumed by the suite |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 | 9 |
| Kafka | 0 | 4 |
| Temporal | 0 | 1 observed (the JOB-06 Schedule) |
| File | 0 | 0 |

##### 13. Solution plan

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Suite module for RWB-ITG-W1, reusing harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG | Integration suite | Runs the eleven scenarios against SIT and holds no service code |
| Fixture pack | Test data | Synthetic cases, queues, members and caps for business date 2026-12-02, with the caps loaded as data rows (DL23) |
| Clock control | Harness control | Moves the nominal Schedule time to 06:30, holds the snapshot time at 06:52 and restores both after the run |
| Reconciliation assertion | Assertion | Compares every queue depth of the P9 measures with the case list of the P3 contract at the snapshot time and fails on any difference |
| Ledger completeness assertion | Assertion | Polls the P7 decision log until the record of each move appears and measures the elapsed time against the five-minute target |
| Evidence report | Report | Records per scenario the queue, the owner, the case, the event ids, the statuses, the messages and the elapsed ledger time |

Decoupling patterns applied (Template and Rules v1 §R5.5):

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added | Where it sits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none | `queue_measure`, `assignment`, `recovery_case` and `timer` stay in `rwb_case`; the ledger is in `rwb_decision`; the suite asserts through contracts only |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON | On RWB-P3-E1030-APP, which writes the local record and publishes it; not a build dependency of this suite, which only waits for the ledger entry |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON | On the APP stories for the queue methods and the measure definitions; the suite sends and reads the codes as data |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON | On RWB-P3-E1030-APP and RWB-P7-E1030-APP for CaseTransferred, TimerBreached and DecisionRecorded; the suite consumes the topics only |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON | On RWB-P3-E1030-APP, which registers the JOB-06 Schedule; the suite moves the clock and triggers one rerun |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) | The nine consumed REST operations of section 12.2 |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none | Every consumed path in section 12.2 |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON | On RWB-P3-E1030-APP for `rwb.case.events.v1`; the suite asserts the topic name and publishes nothing |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON | On RWB-P3-E1030-APP and RWB-P7-E1030-APP for their own sequences; the suite owns no schema |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting | none; gap if the story needs lake data | The lake step of JOB-15 is absent; AC2 asserts that no lake endpoint is called and that the measures arrive as a projection |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The suite enters through gateway-bff; no screen is in scope, and the case list is read through the P3 contract |

The H and C dependencies in the table above belong to the owning APP stories: they record what the services the suite proves had to build, not what the suite waits for. This story's H, C and X lists are exactly the metadata rows — no H, no C and no X — and its I list is the two integration dependencies RWB-P3-E1030-APP and RWB-P7-E1030-APP. An ITG story builds against published contracts and blocks no build of its own (Template and Rules §R5.4 and §R5.7).

Build steps:

1. Create the suite module next to harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG, wire it to the SIT endpoints of P1, P3, P7 and P9 through gateway-bff, and write the preflight: the four services answer, the three topics and their retry and `.dlt` topics exist, the three task queues are registered in `rwb-recovery` and the JOB-06 Schedule is present.
2. Build the fixture pack: synthetic cases, queues, members and caps for 2026-12-02, with the caps read as data rows through the P3 parameters and reference contracts, and add the clock control with its restore step.
3. Implement AC1: the clock at 06:30, the queues read before and after, the 8 and 4 assignment, the same status and stage on the case read, and one CaseTransferred event per move.
4. Implement AC2: the snapshot at 06:52, the measures read for the business date, the depth 296, unassigned 0 and average age 41 days of TDR-BKK-CO, the reconciliation to the case list and the proof that no lake endpoint is called.
5. Implement AC3: case RW-2026-000501, its expired timer, MSG-P3-028 with count 1 and the breach count of the next snapshot.
6. Implement AC4, AC5, AC7 and AC8: no member with capacity, no cap, the repeated run, the held cases and the owner exactly at the cap, with the exact counts and messages.
7. Implement AC6 and AC11 through the agreed test-only fault switch on the P3 decision-record library, and the ledger completeness assertion that measures each collection against five minutes.
8. Implement AC9 and AC10, prove over the call set that no lake endpoint is called, write the evidence report, remove the fixtures, restore the clock and run the suite in SIT against the wave 1 release candidate.

Done when: all twelve test cases pass in SIT against the published wave 1 contracts of P1, P3, P7 and P9, the 06:30 Schedule moves the cases by the queue method with one record per move, every queue measure of 2026-12-02 reconciles to the case list and reaches rwb-reporting with no lake call, every decision record is collected inside the five-minute target, the evidence report is published to the wave 1 exit gate, and no service code or schema was changed by this story apart from the agreed test-only fault switch.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-011 | Cases left without an owner | {count} new cases are waiting in the overflow queue for {team}. Every owner is at the caseload cap. |
| MSG-P3-028 | Service level breach alert | {count} cases in {queue} are past their service level. |
| MSG-P3-029 | Snapshot does not reconcile | The queue measures for {date} were not published: {check}. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Decision log write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The reconciliation and collection result is reported as one line of the evidence report and carries no message ID: {collected} of {expected} queue measures of business date {date} were reconciled and published, the slowest in {seconds} seconds. The message IDs and wording are copied from RWB-E1-030. No new message ID is added by this story. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen is built or tested by this story. SCR-02 Case list (filtered) shows the new owner after a move, and the suite reads the same owner through `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}`. SCR-09 Exception queue (list) shows the cases left without an owner behind MSG-P3-011, which the suite asserts on the message and the count. The Power BI queue page is built by RW-BIANAL from the P9 measures read in section 12.2, not by this story. SCR-07 team queues and the steering dashboard come in Epic 2 and are out of scope.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: caps, queue methods and measure definitions are data rows read through the parameters and reference contracts (DL23, DL25).
- No personal data in the snapshot, the alerts, the events, the logs, the evidence or the fixtures; the snapshot holds counts and ages only.
- No cross-service table read and no schema change: every assertion is a contract response or an event, every write is a call to the owner's own path (DP-01), and the only change in a running service is the agreed test-only fault switch of section 12.8.
- One hop and a 2 s timeout on every call (ADR-020, DP-11), and a timeout is never retried into a pass.
- The harness clock is the test input and the durable timers inside CaseWorkflow are the service's own; the suite moves only its own, and it never starts, moves or stops the Schedule, because the rerun goes through the owner's job catalogue.
- Synthetic data only, loaded by the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG and reset to its fixture state after a run, with no production access of any kind from the suite or its configuration; the suite refuses an environment that is not SIT.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-031 and published as the rwb-case contract baseline of the case list and its export. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract of the rwb-case case list and its export - `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases` with the queue, team and status filters and the queue and owner columns, and `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/export` with its row limit, its access-log entry and its masked workbook - together with the row and page shape, the filter set and the AND rule, the stable order, the error envelope and its message codes, the right each answer requires, the 2 s one-hop budget, the nine contract tables and the contract fakes**, so that **the app, test and gateway stories build on Day 1 against a fixed, testable contract, and a column, a filter or a refusal can never drift between rwb-case, the composite route and the screen**.

The legacy key is split with rework, not moved: the two operations keep their behaviour, their filters, their messages and their values, and this story adds the contract form of them. The owner is rwb-case, the base is its own, and the right, the scope, the masking rules and the access log are consumed from rwb-access and never republished here (DP-08, DP-11).

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). The case list is the most-read surface of rwb-case, and the route merges its answers with those of other services (DP-19). Four things drift silently without a contract: the row fields and the blank owner of AC7, the filter set with the team filter the legacy flow uses, the paging and order that make "page 2" mean the same to two readers, and the order between the access-log entry and the file.

The baseline also fixes the naming the checks require: schema `rwb_case`, REST base `/api/recovery/case/v1`, topic `rwb.case.events.v1` with event names `rwb.case.<Event>.v1`, task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`. It records that the two answers are reads, that no operation of this contract writes, and that the only write on the export path is the access-log entry of rwb-access (DP-09 not applied).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the document, the base path and the schema name follow the platform rule and not a local choice.
- The platform error envelope and the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope are the platform baseline (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON); this document narrows the first for its two operations and publishes no event schema.
- The parameters contract of rwb-case (RWB-P3-E1042-CON, DP-06) and its reference-data contract (RWB-P3-E1043-CON, DP-07) are published, so `caselist.export.maxrows` and LOV-CASE-STATUS and LOV-TEAM are declared as data and never as values in this document.
- The rwb-access authorise and access-log contracts (RWB-P4-E1037-CON, RWB-P4-E1039-CON) are the consumed answers; this document names them and republishes nothing of them (DP-08, DP-11).
- The Ownership Map gives `GET /cases` and `GET /cases/export` to P3 rwb-case; this document declares no other service's operation as provided.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. The contract author writes the OpenAPI 3.1 document `caselist.yaml` for the two read operations, one tag `Case list`.
2. The author fixes the row shape `CaseListRow` from the legacy `Case` fields, with `ownerUserId` optional and `queueCode` and `queueName` beside `queueId`.
3. The author fixes the filter set `queue`, `team`, `status`, `owner`, `product`, `stage` and the AND rule, and states the team filter as an additive optional parameter (ASM-3624).
4. The author fixes paging `page` and `size` with `total`, the default and maximum size read as parameter rows, and the order that ends on the case number.
5. The author fixes the export: the same filters without paging, the spreadsheet content type, the 422 above the row limit and the 503 when the access-log entry cannot be written, and states that the entry precedes the file.
6. The author records the two consumed operations of rwb-access with their use, the 2 s budget and the message ids of the 403 and the 503, and the masking rule that travels in the authorise answer.
7. The lint, schema and example steps run; the fake is generated from the document and answers every operation and every example of section 14.
8. The document and the fake are published; RWB-P3-E1031-APP, RWB-P3-E2033-APP, RWB-P3-E2011-APP, the gateway-bff stories and RWB-ITG-E1031-ITG pin the version.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message |
|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | An operation is published without a 4xx error envelope | The lint step fails the build and the document is not published | Lint finding, no message id |
| X2 | A path is published outside `/api/recovery/case/v1` | The lint step fails the build; the monolith base is never republished | Lint finding, no message id |
| X3 | The row schema adds a field no source defines | The field is not invented: the example carries the placeholder and the gap row is cited | GAP-2209 |
| X4 | An example carries a personal name, an account number or an identity number | The review step rejects the example; only user references and case numbers appear | Review finding |
| X5 | A filter is published without its list in force | The lint step fails: every enumerated value names its LOV or its parameter row | Lint finding, no message id |
| X6 | A consumer needs a filter or a column the legacy story does not fix | The change is raised as a request against v2; v1 is not edited in place | Review finding |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Publishes a document and a fake; builds nothing and depends on no build |
| Negotiable | Field order, example values and the detail layout of the problem body are open until the version is frozen |
| Valuable | The app, the queue views, the gateway and the integration harness start on Day 1 against one document and one fake |
| Estimable | Two operations, one row schema, one page envelope, four message ids, nine tables, one fake |
| Small | One sprint for the document, the fake and the contract test |
| Testable | Each criterion is a schema, lint or fake assertion in section 16 |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: rwb-case contract baseline for the case list and its export

  Background:
    Given the rwb-case base path is /api/recovery/case/v1 and the schema is rwb_case
    Given the contract version is v1

  Scenario: AC1 The case-list operation is published with its owner (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the OpenAPI 3.1 document for the Case list tag
    When it is validated and linted
    Then it declares GET /cases and GET /cases/export under /api/recovery/case/v1
    Then every operation names rwb-case (P3) as its owner and declares no operation of rwb-access
    Then GET /cases answers 200, 401, 403, 422 and 503

  Scenario: AC2 The row shape and the owner column are fixed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the schema CaseListRow
    When it is compared with the DF-CAS fields published in section 11 and with DF-WRK-001 to DF-WRK-004
    Then it carries caseNo, productGroup, status, stageCode, queueId, queueCode, queueName, ownerUserId, teamCode, regionCode and entryDate
    Then ownerUserId is optional, so a case with no owner is one row with the field absent and never a missing row
    Then no field carries a customer name, an identity number, an address or an account number

  Scenario: AC3 The filter set and the AND rule are published (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the parameters of GET /cases and GET /cases/export
    When the document is validated
    Then both operations carry queue, team, status, owner, product and stage
    Then the team parameter is optional and additive on GET /cases, as the legacy flow and the export operation state it
    Then every enumerated filter names its list in force: LOV-CASE-STATUS for status, the queues in force for queue, LOV-PRODUCT for product, LOV-STAGE for stage
    Then the description states that the filters combine with AND inside the caller's scope

  Scenario: AC4 Paging and the stable order are fixed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the page and size parameters of GET /cases
    When the document is validated
    Then the response envelope carries items, page, size and total
    Then the default and maximum size are named as parameter rows and not as numbers in the schema
    Then the order is stated and ends on the case number, so a walk of pages neither repeats nor skips a case
    Then no cursor token is published, because no source gives one

  Scenario: AC5 The export contract and its refusals are fixed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the operation GET /cases/export
    When it is validated and linted
    Then it takes the same filters without page and size
    Then it answers 200 with the spreadsheet content type, one row per matching case and the columns masked for the caller's role
    Then it answers 422 above caselist.export.maxrows and 503 when the access-log entry cannot be written, and in both cases no file is produced
    Then the description states that the access-log entry AC-EXPT is written before the workbook is built

  Scenario: AC6 The right, the scope and the error envelope are published (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the problem schema shared by both operations
    When the error examples are validated
    Then the envelope carries type, title, status, detail, instance and an errors list with field
    Then the examples carry MSG-P4-002 on 403, MSG-P3-021 on 422, MSG-P7-003 on 503 and MSG-P3-020 as the empty page text
    Then every operation requires the Case record right R and states that the scope is applied

  Scenario: AC7 The two consumed answers and the 2 s budget are recorded (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the consumed operations of section 12.2
    When the document is reviewed
    Then the authorise answer of rwb-access is named with the right, the scope and the masking rules it returns
    Then the access-log write of rwb-access is named with the AC-EXPT fields of the legacy story
    Then both are one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker, and no operation of this document chains a call

  Scenario: AC8 The nine contract tables and the fakes agree (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the nine tables of section 12 and the published document
    When the contract test runs
    Then every table and index named in section 12 sits in rwb_case with its P3 owner
    Then the fake answers every operation and every example, including the 403, 422 and 503 of section 14
    Then a breaking change raises v2 and deprecates v1 instead of editing it
```

These criteria are new and test only the contract baseline: no legacy acceptance criterion is repeated here, and every business value in the examples comes from the legacy story or the technical specification character for character. The legacy criteria AC1 to AC8 are owned and proved by RWB-P3-E1031-APP against this document.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The contract publishes rwb-case resources only; the right, the scope, the masking rules and the access log are rwb-access | DP-08; ownership map |
| BR2 | The list holds only cases inside the caller's scope (Own, Team, Region, All) and the filters combine with AND | Legacy BR1, BR2; REQ-ACA-009 |
| BR3 | The export is refused above `caselist.export.maxrows` before anything is written | Legacy BR5; DL11 |
| BR4 | The access-log entry is written before the workbook is built, and a failure of the entry produces no file | Legacy BR3; REQ-ACA-006 |
| BR5 | Export columns follow the masking rules for the caller's role, which arrive in the authorise answer | Legacy BR4; REQ-ACA-005; DL26 |
| BR6 | The order of a page is total and ends on the case number | Legacy AC1 and AC7; paging |
| BR7 | A case with no owner is a row with `ownerUserId` absent, never a row hidden | Legacy AC7 |
| BR8 | Both operations are reads: no POST, no event, no workflow, no lock, and the export declares no Idempotency-Key because it stores nothing of its own | Legacy section 9; DP-09 not applied |
| BR9 | Every value a business person may change is a parameter or reference row with its version in force | Legacy BR5; DP-06, DP-07 |

##### 9. State transitions

None in this story: a document has no runtime state. The states the document exposes are the case statuses of LOV-CASE-STATUS in the `status` filter and in the row, and the case and queue transitions themselves belong to RWB-P3-E1020-APP and RWB-P3-E1021-APP. This document fixes only the HTTP status that accompanies each refusal: 401 no session, 403 no Case record right, 422 a value outside its list or an export above its limit, 503 the store or the access log unavailable.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The contract author (any team, per U3) | Writes and versions the document and the fake |
| The service owner of rwb-case | Approves a breaking change and a version freeze |
| The consumer teams (app, queue views, gateway, integration harness) | Read the document, pin a version, raise a change request |
| rwb-access (P4) | Owns the authorise and access-log contracts this document consumes and never republishes |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A contract is a technical artefact, not a credit decision |

Role names appear in the examples as role codes only, resolved by rwb-access at run time (DP-08). No personal name, no email address and no credential appears in the document or an example; an owner appears as a staff user reference, and the display name is not published (GAP-2209; ASM-3630).

##### 11. Data

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Field identifiers published | DF-CAS-001, DF-CAS-002, DF-CAS-003, DF-CAS-005, DF-CAS-006, DF-CAS-009, DF-CAS-010, DF-CAS-011, DF-CAS-012, DF-CAS-013 (recovery_case); DF-WRK-001 to DF-WRK-004 (queue) |
| Field identifiers referenced, not published | The parameter rows behind `caselist.export.maxrows` and the reference rows behind LOV-CASE-STATUS and LOV-TEAM: read in process through RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON, never joined in SQL and never republished as values |
| Field identifiers with no source | The display name of an owner, the page-size default and maximum as parameter keys, and the parameter field identifiers themselves: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2209; ASM-3630) |
| Personal data in examples | None. Owners appear as staff user references (U-71, U-11) and cases as case numbers (RW-2026-000601) |
| Values in examples | 64 cases in "DIL-BKK-CO", 20 in "DIL-BKK-OVF", 51 filtered cases, 10,000 and 10,001 rows, 10,000 as the limit, all copied from the legacy story |

The document carries no value that no source holds. Where a consumer needs a field or a key that neither the legacy story nor the technical specification defines, the schema carries the placeholder text and the change waits for the gap to close; this is a draft baseline, so a new version can add the field without breaking a consumer.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/case/v1`; owner rwb-case (P3).

| Operation | Document | Request | Responses | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases | caselist.yaml | Query: queue (uuid), team, status, owner, product, stage, page, size, sort | 200 CaseListPage (items, page, size, total); 401 MSG-P4-001; 403 MSG-P4-002; 422 a value outside its list; 503 | P3 |
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/export | caselist.yaml | The same query without page and size | 200 application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet; 401 MSG-P4-001; 403 MSG-P4-002; 422 MSG-P3-021 above the row limit; 503 MSG-P7-003 access log unavailable | P3 |

`CaseListRow` carries `caseNo`, `productGroup`, `status`, `stageCode`, `queueId`, `queueCode`, `queueName`, `ownerUserId` (optional), `teamCode`, `regionCode` and `entryDate`. `queueCode` and `queueName` are joined from `queue` for the column and the filter labels; `regionCode` is published because the scope of BR2 needs it. The exact name of the envelope, of the row schema and of the sort token, and the page-size keys, are this story's proposal (GAP-2209; ASM-3630). The team parameter is additive and optional on `GET /cases` (ASM-3624).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Provider | Why this document needs it | Pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise | rwb-access (P4) | The 403 example, the scope rule of BR2, and the masking rules of BR5 arrive in this answer, cached per request | DP-08, DP-11 |
| POST /api/recovery/access/v1/access-events | rwb-access (P4) | The 503 example and the ordering rule of BR4: the AC-EXPT entry with the user, the time, the filters and the row count, written before the file | DP-11 |

Both are one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker; no operation of this document calls a service that calls another (ADR-020). The parameter and reference reads of DP-06 and DP-07 are in-process library reads of rwb-case and are not rows of this table.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. No operation of this document publishes an event and the export writes no outbox row. `rwb.case.events.v1` and the names `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1`, `rwb.case.CaseAllocated.v1`, `rwb.case.CaseTransferred.v1`, `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` and `rwb.case.TimerBreached.v1` are contracted by the stories that own their behaviour under DP-14; the access event AC-EXPT is not a Kafka event but the rwb-access call of 12.2.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The list is read from the rows per request and no projection or inbox row stands behind it, so this contract declares no subscription and no event schema.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. Neither operation starts, signals or reads a workflow. `CaseWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery` is the case lifecycle and is declared by the stories that own it; this document names the task queue only as the service's naming baseline.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Temporal Schedule and no batch window belongs to these operations: the list is read on request and the export is officer-driven.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Schema | Key and indexes to publish in the baseline file | Owner | Rows exposed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| recovery_case | rwb_case | PK id; unique case_no; ix_case_status_queue (status, queue_id); ix_case_owner_status (owner_user_id, status); ix_case_team_status (team_code, status) | P3 | GET /cases, read only |
| queue | rwb_case | PK id; unique queue_code; team_code | P3 | queueCode, queueName and the queue filter values |
| parameter_catalog, parameter_value | rwb_case | PK id; unique parameter key per environment; version in force | P3 | caselist.export.maxrows and the page-size bounds, through DP-06 |
| reference_row, reference_version | rwb_case | PK id; version_id to reference_version; unique table code and version number | P3 | LOV-CASE-STATUS and LOV-TEAM, through DP-07 |
| lov_value | rwb_case | PK id; unique list code and value code | P3 | The list values of the filter pickers |

The tables arrive on the per-service Flyway sequence after the V0001 baseline (DP-15; RWB-PLT-E1044-CON); `ix_case_team_status` is the index the legacy story asked for and it is published here as part of this legacy key (ASM-3631). This document adds no table outside `rwb_case` and no reference to a table in `rwb_access`.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-case case-list fake (this story) | The two operations, the row and page shape and the problem bodies | RWB-P3-E1031-APP, RWB-P3-E2033-APP, RWB-P3-E2011-APP, gateway-bff stories, RWB-ITG-E1031-ITG |
| rwb-access authorise fake (P4) | POST /authorise | The 403 example, the scope example and the masking rules of the app story |
| rwb-access access-log fake (P4) | The AC-EXPT write | The 503 example and the export tests |
| gateway-bff route stub | The SCR-02 composite route (DP-19) | The screen assertions of the app story |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Provided | Consumed | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 operations under `/api/recovery/case/v1` | 2 operations, both to rwb-access | OpenAPI 3.1, one hop, 2 s timeout, a breaker per downstream |
| Kafka | 0 | 0 | No event schema is published by this document |
| Temporal | 0 | 0 | Declared by the stories that own the workflows |
| File | 1 (the xlsx of the export in the response) | 0 | No claim-check store and nothing written to Blob |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** `caselist.yaml` (OpenAPI 3.1, tag `Case list`, the schemas `CaseListRow` and `CaseListPage` and the shared problem schema); `schema-baseline.sql` with the five table groups of section 12 (for reference only, the executable migration belongs to the DB work); the contract fake; the contract test.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_case`; the document names no other service's tables | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library: the export limit and the page bounds are parameter rows, not schema constants | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case: every enumerated filter names its list in force | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library; the 403 and the scope rule are consumed, never republished | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with a mock, one hop, 2 s timeout: the two rwb-access answers | none (C from the legacy dependencies RWB-P4-E1037-CON and RWB-P4-E1039-CON) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.case.events.v1` and `rwb.case.<Event>.v1`; naming library, no channel published | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in `rwb_case`; the baseline file names the tables and the three indexes | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route for SCR-02 | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

This is a CON story: it documents the patterns of the legacy key and adds no build dependency of its own, so it is Day 1. DP-11 is the row that matters here, because the legacy in-process `AccessEventPublisher` is exactly the call that becomes a REST answer with a fake.

**Build steps**

1. Write `caselist.yaml` with the two operations, the `CaseListRow` and `CaseListPage` schemas and the shared problem schema.
2. Fix the filter set with the enumerated values and their lists in force, and the additive team parameter of BR2 and AC3.
3. Fix paging, the page-size parameters and the order that ends on the case number; declare no cursor.
4. Fix the export: content type, the row limit of BR3, the 422 and 503 of AC5 and the ordering rule of BR4.
5. Add the examples of section 14 with the four message ids and synthetic data only.
6. Write `schema-baseline.sql` from section 12 and cross-check every column against DF-CAS and DF-WRK identifiers.
7. Generate the fake and the contract test; wire both into the build of RWB-P3-E1031-APP and into a nightly run with RWB-P3-E2033-APP and RWB-ITG-E1031-ITG.
8. Publish v1 to the contract registry and notify the consumers.

**Done when.** The document validates, the lint rules pass, the fake answers every operation and every example, and the contract test runs green on the build of this story.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Published as |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-020 | No case meets the filters | No cases match these filters. Change a filter to see more. | 200 with an empty page; the text is the screen's empty state |
| MSG-P3-021 | The export is above its row limit | The export holds at most {max} rows. Narrow the filters and try again. | 422 with the errors list naming the limit |
| MSG-P7-003 | The access-log entry cannot be written at export | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | 503, and no file |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role does not hold the Case record right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | 403 |
| MSG-P4-001 | No valid session | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2209; ASM-3630) | 401 |

The identified texts and identifiers are the legacy ones and no identifier is renumbered. Request validation is published as schema constraints where a source defines the value (queue as a uuid, status from LOV-CASE-STATUS, product from LOV-PRODUCT, stage from LOV-STAGE, page and size bounded by their parameter rows) and as the placeholder where no source does (the filter labels, the sort token and the page-token shape - GAP-2209; ASM-3630).

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story: it publishes the answers a screen binds to. The states the answers expose are the seven of SCR-02 in RWB-P3-E1031-APP - Loading, List, Filtered, Empty, Export refused, Export failed and Refused - and each is produced by a status of section 12.1: 200 for List and Filtered, 200 with an empty page for Empty, 403 for Refused, 422 for Export refused and 503 for Export failed. The route path, the screen model and the layout belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON and the designer (DL31).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a schema as a constant: the export limit and the page bounds are published as parameter-row references and every enumerated filter names its list (DP-06, DP-07).
- No personal data in examples, events or logs: an owner is a staff user reference and a case is a case number; no name, identity number, address or account number appears.
- No cross-schema reference: the document names `rwb_case` tables only and consumes the rwb-access answers without republishing them (DP-01, DP-08).
- One hop and a 2 s timeout for every consumed operation; a timeout is published as 503 and never as a stale answer.
- The base path is `/api/recovery/case/v1` and the monolith base is never republished (DP-13).
- The export cannot be made without its access-log entry, and the document says so in the operation description (BR4).
- The document is versioned: a breaking change raises v2 and deprecates v1 rather than editing v1 in place.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-031 and reworked for rwb-case. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR)**, I want **the queue and owner columns on the case list, with filters by queue, team and status and an export to Excel**, so that **I see my queues and who owns each case without a new screen**.

Inside `rwb-case` this is the case-list and export slice of legacy RWB-E1-031. Service facts: schema `rwb_case`, REST base `/api/recovery/case/v1`, topic `rwb.case.events.v1` with event names `rwb.case.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`, epic `RWB-SVC-P3` (DP-13, DP-14).

- The slice delivers two operations on the owner's own rows: `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases` with the queue, team and status filters and the queue and owner columns on every row, and `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/export` with the row limit, the access-log entry that precedes the file and the workbook masked by role.
- What the legacy story called the module's own code is now three owners. The right, the scope and the access log are `rwb-access`'s (DP-08, DP-11); the display name of an owner is resolved at the edge; the composite route is `gateway-bff`'s (DP-19). The case, the queue and their columns are this service's and are read from `rwb_case` only (DP-01).
- The wider case list with ageing and the queue views are RWB-P3-E2033-APP and RWB-P3-E2011-APP; this story adds the queue and owner columns, the three filters and the export those two stories re-use. The journey with every service live is RWB-ITG-E1031-ITG.
- All eight legacy criteria are this story's (AC1 to AC8), with legacy test cases TC-E1-031-01 to TC-E1-031-09. The contract form of the two operations is RWB-P3-E1031-CON, which is a build dependency because the row shape it fixes is what the screen binds to.

The story writes no case, queue or assignment row and changes no case status. It reads `recovery_case` and `queue` in `rwb_case`, and it writes exactly one row that is not its own: the access-log entry in `rwb-access`, made through that service's contract before any file is built.

##### 2. Business rationale

Today a team manager asks each collector for their list to know who holds which case. With allocation by rule (RWB-P3-E1020-APP), every case has a queue and an owner; this story shows both on the case list, filters by queue, team and status inside the manager's scope, and exports the filtered list with the export written to the access log for PDPA. It meets REQ-CWC-007 (the result of allocation is visible) and REQ-ACA-009 (a user sees only the cases their scope allows).

The facts the screen shows are the owner's: the case row, its queue and its owner are `rwb_case` rows, so the list is served by the service that holds them and no copy can show a manager a different queue or owner (DP-01). The scope is not a filter this service owns; it is the answer of the rwb-access authorise contract, cached for the request (DP-08), and a role without the Case record right is refused rather than shown an empty page, because an empty page reads as "no work" and hides a permission problem.

Three rules do the visible work: filters combine with AND, so a queue filter and a team filter narrow and never widen (BR2); an export is written to the access log before the file is made, and no file is made when the entry cannot be written (BR3), which is the PDPA control the legacy story fixed; and the export holds at most `caselist.export.maxrows` rows with the columns masked for the caller's role (BR4, BR5), so an export can never be a wider read than a screen.

##### 3. Preconditions

| Precondition | What it gives this story |
|---|---|
| RWB-P3-E1020-APP is done | Cases carry `queue_id`, `team_code` and `owner_user_id`, so the queue column and the owner column are populated and an unassigned case is the exception it should be (it waits for this story in lane L-P3-F) |
| RWB-P3-E1031-CON is published and baselined | The two operations, the row and page shape, the filter set, the paging order and the problem body this story is tested against. It is an H dependency of the same service and the first thing this story builds against |
| RWB-P4-E1039-CON is published | The access-log write operation and its error answer, used by AC2 and AC5 (contract dependency; the build uses its fake and never blocks) |
| RWB-P4-E1037-CON is published | The authorise answer with the Case record right R, the caller's scope and the masking rules of the role, cached per request (contract dependency) |
| The platform contracts the DP rows name are published | RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-E1037-CON, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON; they are pulled by the rwb-case baseline stories and add no work of their own here |
| The parameters in force hold the export limit | `caselist.export.maxrows` = 10,000, the legacy value under DL11, read as a parameter row with the version in force through the rwb-case parameters contract (DP-06; ASM-3628) |
| The reference data in force holds the lists | LOV-CASE-STATUS and LOV-TEAM as reference rows with the version in force, and the queues as `queue` rows of this service (DP-07) |
| The user holds a role with the Case record right R | The team manager's default scope is Team; the right and the scope are answered by rwb-access and cached per request by the guard library |
| The feature flag `rwb.p3.caselistqueue` is on | Off, the list hides the queue and owner columns and the export (ASM-3629) |

##### 4. Flow

1. Team manager: opens SCR-02 Case list through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19); the screen shows the Loading state.
2. gateway-bff: calls `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases` on rwb-case with page 0 and size 50, one hop.
3. rwb-case: `AccessCheckClient` asks the rwb-access authorise contract for the Case record right R and the caller's scope, cached for the request; a role without the right is a 403 and nothing is read (DP-08).
4. `CaseQueryService` applies the caller's scope and returns one page; `CaseListPage` shows each row with case number, product, status, stage, queue, owner and entry date (list state).
5. Team manager: picks queue "DIL-BKK-CO", team "DIL-BKK" and status "ASSIGNED"; the page calls `GET /cases` with the three filters (filtered state).
6. `CaseQueryService` combines the filters with AND inside the scope and returns only the cases that meet every filter, with the total.
7. Team manager: chooses Export; `ExportButton` calls `GET /cases/export` with the filters shown and without page and size.
8. `CaseExportService`: counts the matching rows against `caselist.export.maxrows`; above the limit it refuses with MSG-P3-021 and builds nothing (AC4).
9. `AccessEventClient`: writes the access event AC-EXPT through the rwb-access contract with the user, the time, the filters and the row count, before the workbook is built; if the entry cannot be written, no file is made (AC5, MSG-P7-003).
10. `CaseExportService`: builds the xlsx with the columns masked for the caller's role; the browser downloads "Case list 20261202 1.xlsx" (AC2, AC8).

Nothing in steps 1 to 10 writes a case, a queue or an assignment, publishes an event, starts a workflow or takes a lock for the length of a page.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | No case meets the filters | Empty state with a plain sentence | MSG-P3-020 | AC3 |
| X2 | The filtered list holds more rows than the export limit | Export refused; the user narrows the filter | MSG-P3-021 | AC4 |
| X3 | The access log cannot be written | Export not made | MSG-P7-003 | AC5 |
| X4 | A filter names a queue outside the caller's scope | Only in-scope cases return; an out-of-scope queue returns none | MSG-P3-020 | AC6 |
| X5 | A case has no owner | Owner cell is blank; the case is still listed | None | AC7 |
| X6 | Exactly 10,000 rows | Export allowed | None | AC8 |
| X7 | A role without Case record R opens the list | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-031-09 |

X4 and X7 answer differently on purpose: a queue outside the scope is an empty page inside a permitted read, and a role without the right is a refusal with a status. A consumer that reads the second as the first hides a permission problem.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Reads the queue, team and owner fields RWB-P3-E1020-APP fills; builds against RWB-P3-E1031-CON and the rwb-access fakes, so neither rwb-access nor the edge needs to exist in the development environment |
| Negotiable | Column order and the export row limit are configurable; the three filters, the AND rule and the access-log ordering are fixed |
| Valuable | Team managers see ownership on one screen and take a masked extract of exactly what they see |
| Estimable | Two query parameters, one export operation, two clients, one screen change |
| Small | Fits under one week: two operations, one query, one export writer, one page of screen support |
| Testable | Every criterion has a test case in section 16; the refusals are contract tests and the screen states are component tests |

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The list holds only cases inside the caller's scope (Own, Team, Region, All) | REQ-ACA-009; CTL-09; LOV-SCOPE |
| BR2 | Filters combine with AND, and the queue, team and status filters narrow inside the scope | FSD A2.19; legacy section 4 step 4 |
| BR3 | Every export is written to the access log before the file is made | REQ-ACA-006; CTL-11 |
| BR4 | Export columns follow the masking rules for the caller's role | REQ-ACA-005; DL26 |
| BR5 | An export holds at most the configured number of rows | Parameter caselist.export.maxrows = 10,000 (assumed; DL11) |
| BR6 | A screen responds in under 2 seconds | NFR-008 |
| BR7 | A case with no owner is listed with a blank owner cell, never hidden and never filled by guess | Legacy AC7 |
| BR8 | Nothing is published and no case row is written: the two operations are reads, and the only row written is the access-log entry of rwb-access | DP-09 not applied; legacy section 9 |

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It reads queue, owner and status only. The states the screen exposes are the case statuses of LOV-CASE-STATUS (NEW, ASSIGNED, IN_PROGRESS, WAITING_CUSTOMER, WAITING_PARTNER, WAITING_APPROVAL, ON_HOLD, CLOSED) as rows in force, and a filter value outside that list is refused before a case is read (RWB-P3-E1031-CON AC6).

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-TEAMMGR | Lists, filters and exports cases in team scope (Case record R) |
| RW-CASEOWN | Lists and exports their own cases (Case record R, scope Own) |
| Every role with Case record R | Lists cases in its scope |
| RW-REFADM, RW-SECADM | No Case record right; refused |
| RW-COMPLY | Reads the access log entries for exports |

The right, the scope and its default are answered by rwb-access and held nowhere in rwb-case (DP-08). Role names appear as role codes only; no personal name, address or credential appears in this story, and the owner is a staff user reference (U-71 style) with no name beside it (GAP-2208; ASM-3625).
