No row is written, so no field is marked Write.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/case/v1`; owner rwb-case (P3).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/cases` | One page of the cases in the caller's scope with the filters queue, team, status, owner, product and stage; each row carries case number, product group, status, stage code, queue, owner, team and entry date | Case record R, scope applied through the rwb-access authorise contract | Read only: the same request on unchanged data returns the same rows in the same order |
| GET | `/cases/export` | The same filters without page and size, answered as an xlsx masked by role, after the access-log entry AC-EXPT and after the row-limit check | Case record R, scope applied | Not applicable on the data; each export is a new access-log entry, and the entry is written before the file |

The request carries the legacy query parameters `queue` (uuid), `status`, `owner`, `product`, `stage`, `page`, `size` and `sort`, with `team` added by this story (BR2; GAP-2208; ASM-3624). The response is the legacy `CasePage`: `items` with `caseNo`, `productGroup`, `status`, `stageCode`, `queueId`, `ownerUserId`, `teamCode`, `regionCode` and `entryDate`, plus `page`, `size` and `total`; `queueCode` and `queueName` are joined from `queue` for the column and the filter labels, and `regionCode` is the field the region scope of BR1 is decided on. The exact spelling of the row, the envelope and the problem body is the one RWB-P3-E1031-CON freezes (GAP-2209; ASM-3630).

Errors: 401 no session or no Recovery role (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Case record right (MSG-P4-002); 422 a filter value outside its list or an export above the row limit (MSG-P3-021); 503 the store is down or the access log cannot be written (MSG-P7-003).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

One hop, no chaining; 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020).

| Method | Path | Service | Used for | Timeout |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | rwb-access (P4) | The Case record right R, the caller's scope with its default, and the masking rules of the role, cached per request by the guard library (DP-08; RWB-P4-E1037-CON) | One hop, 2 s, cached per request |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/access-events` | rwb-access (P4) | The access-log entry AC-EXPT with the user, the time, the filters and the row count, written before the workbook is built (DP-11; RWB-P4-E1039-CON) | One hop, 2 s, no retry on the export path |

The masking rules travel in the authorise answer and are applied by this service when it builds the columns; rwb-case holds no copy of a masking row (GAP-2208; ASM-3627). The parameter and reference reads of DP-06 and DP-07 are in-process library reads of this same service and not cross-service calls, so they are not rows of this table.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The two operations are reads: no outbox row is written and no event is published. `rwb.case.events.v1` and the names `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1`, `rwb.case.CaseAllocated.v1`, `rwb.case.CaseTransferred.v1`, `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` and `rwb.case.TimerBreached.v1` belong to the stories that own the case, allocation, transfer, state and timer behaviour under DP-14, and this story adds none to them. The access event AC-EXPT is not a Kafka event: it is the rwb-access contract call of 12.2.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The list is read from the rows per request, so a case that moves is seen on the next read rather than through a projection, and no inbox row is written. `rwb.case.CaseAllocated.v1` and `rwb.case.CaseTransferred.v1` are the events that change the queue and the owner this screen shows; the screen does not subscribe to them and needs no cache.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. Both operations answer inside the request: no workflow, no activity, no signal and no timer. `CaseWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-case` is the case lifecycle and is not started, signalled or read by this story.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The legacy story had no job and the target adds none: the list is read on request and the export is officer-driven, so no Temporal Schedule, no timer and no batch window belongs to this story.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Schema | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|---|
| `recovery_case` | rwb_case | rwb-case (P3) | The case row behind every list row: number, product group, status, stage, owner, queue, team, region and entry date |
| `queue` | rwb_case | rwb-case (P3) | The queue code and name of the column and of the queue filter values |
| `parameter_catalog`, `parameter_value` | rwb_case | rwb-case (P3) | `caselist.export.maxrows` with the version in force, read through the contracts of this service and never joined in SQL |
| `reference_row`, `reference_version` | rwb_case | rwb-case (P3) | LOV-CASE-STATUS and LOV-TEAM with the version in force |
| `lov_value` | rwb_case | rwb-case (P3) | The list values served by the reference-data contract to the filter pickers |

No other table is named. `assignment` and `queue_member` are this service's and are not read here: the list needs the current owner on the case row, not the assignment history. No table of `rwb_access` is read and no `recovery` or other `rwb_*` schema is named (DP-01, DP-08).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-access authorise fake | The P4 contract of DP-08 | Granting Case record R with scope Team for `DIL-BKK` and scope All for AC4 and AC8; refusing a role with no Case record right with MSG-P4-002; returning the masking rules of the role |
| rwb-access access-log fake | RWB-P4-E1039-CON through DP-11 | Accepting the AC-EXPT entry of AC2 and AC8; answering unavailable for AC5, so no file is made |
| RWB-P3-E1031-CON fake | The two operations of 12.1 | The row, the page envelope, the 403, 422 and 503 problem bodies, for the contract test of this story |
| gateway-bff route stub | The edge route of RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The SCR-02 route and the merged screen model (DP-19) |
| rwb-case seed set and fixtures | This story's own test data | 64 cases in `DIL-BKK-CO`, 20 in `DIL-BKK-OVF`, 51 filtered cases, 10,000 and 10,001 case sets, case `RW-2026-000601` with no owner, one queue of another team, and the parameter row `caselist.export.maxrows` 10,000 |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 provided, 2 consumed | `GET /cases` and `GET /cases/export` provided; the rwb-access authorise and access-log operations consumed; one hop, 2 s, breaker, cache per request |
| Kafka | None | No event published and none consumed (12.3, 12.4) |
| Temporal | None | No workflow and no activity (12.5) |
| File | 1 | The xlsx of the export, returned in the response; nothing is written to Blob and no claim-check store is used |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`, module `caselist`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case.caselist`; front end `src/modules/recovery/case/caselist`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_case`; the list and the export read `recovery_case` and `queue` of this service only and never another service's tables | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and its client library: the export row limit is a parameter row | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case: LOV-CASE-STATUS and LOV-TEAM with the version in force | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library, cached per request, on both operations | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | The legacy `AccessEventPublisher` becomes the access-log operation of rwb-access, called with a mock one hop and a 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency RWB-P4-E1039-CON) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.case.events.v1` and `rwb.case.<Event>.v1`; naming library; this story publishes nothing | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in schema `rwb_case`: the team index the legacy story asked for arrives here | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route for SCR-02 | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| CaseListController | Controller | `GET /cases` with the team filter; `GET /cases/export`; problem responses with their message ids |
| CaseQueryService | Service | Builds the scoped query with the AND filters; joins `queue` for the code and the name |
| CaseExportService | Service | Row count against the limit, the access-log entry first, then the xlsx with masked columns |
| AccessEventClient | Client | The AC-EXPT entry through the rwb-access access-log contract (DP-11) |
| AccessCheckClient | Client | The Case record right R, the scope and the masking rules through the authorise contract (DP-08) |
| CaseAndWorkflowRepository | Repository | Paged query on `recovery_case` and `queue` in `rwb_case` |
| CaseRowMapper | Component | The row of 12.1, with the blank owner of AC7 |
| CaseListPage | React component | SCR-02 with the queue and owner columns and the states Loading, empty, list, filtered |
| CaseListFilters | React component | Queue, team and status pickers from the queues and the lists in force |
| ExportButton | React component | Calls the export and shows MSG-P3-021 or MSG-P7-003 |

**Database and migrations**

- Reads `recovery_case` and `queue` only; uses `ix_case_status_queue` (status, queue_id) and `ix_case_owner_status` where they already exist.
- Adds `ix_case_team_status` on `recovery_case (team_code, status)` as `V031_1__case_team_index.sql` in the rwb-case Flyway sequence after the V0001 baseline (DP-15; RWB-PLT-E1044-CON). If the case-list story RWB-P3-E2033-APP already lands an index on the same two columns, that index is used and this migration is not created.
- The service connects with its own login (DP-02), holding grants on `rwb_case` only and no grant on a `recovery` or another `rwb_*` schema. The login name is not fixed by any source read here (GAP-2208; ASM-3628).

**Configuration and reference data**

- `caselist.export.maxrows` = 10,000 as a parameter row with the version in force, never a constant (DL11; ASM-3628). The page size default 50 and maximum 200 are the parameter rows RWB-P3-E2011-APP declares and are re-used, not re-declared.
- Queues come from `queue`; LOV-CASE-STATUS, LOV-TEAM and the filter labels come through the rwb-case reference-data contract (DP-07); the labels "Export" and "Owner user ID" follow the label standard (DL10).
- The feature flag keeps the legacy name `rwb.p3.caselistqueue` (ASM-3629).

**Build steps**

1. `CaseListController` and `CaseRowMapper` against the fake of RWB-P3-E1031-CON and the rwb-access stub, with the problem bodies; AC1, AC3.
2. `CaseQueryService` and `CaseAndWorkflowRepository` with the scope predicate and the AND filters, team included; AC1, AC6, AC7.
3. `CaseListPage` and `CaseListFilters` with the Loading, list, filtered and empty states; AC1, AC3, AC7.
4. `AccessEventClient` and `CaseExportService` with the limit check and the access-log entry ahead of the workbook; AC2, AC4, AC5, AC8.
5. The export response, the masked columns and the file name "Case list YYYYMMDD 1.xlsx"; AC2, AC8.
6. The access test, the 2 second check on 26,500 cases, and the contract test of RWB-P3-E1031-CON.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.caselistqueue`. Off: the list hides the queue and owner columns and the export.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass; the list answers in under 2 seconds on 26,500 cases at the 95th percentile in SIT (NFR-008); the export is refused with 422 and no file above 10,000 rows; no file is made when the access-log entry fails; the contract test of RWB-P3-E1031-CON is green; and no query of this story names a schema other than `rwb_case`.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Where it is produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-020 | No case meets the filters | No cases match these filters. Change a filter to see more. | This story, on the list empty state |
| MSG-P3-021 | Export above the row limit | The export holds at most {max} rows. Narrow the filters and try again. | This story, on the export path, before the file |
| MSG-P7-003 | Access log unavailable at export | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | rwb-access through the access-log contract, surfaced here |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | rwb-access through the authorise contract, surfaced here |
| MSG-P4-001 | No valid session | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2208; ASM-3626) | rwb-access, surfaced here |

The four identified texts are copied from the legacy story character for character and no identifier is renumbered. The refusal order is fixed: the session, then the right, then the filter values, then the row count, then the access-log entry, and only then a row is read or a file is built; a request refused at any of those steps reads nothing and writes nothing.

##### 15. Screens and states

| Screen | State | What this story supplies |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-02 Case list | Loading | Skeleton rows while the operation answers |
| SCR-02 Case list | List | Columns case number, product, status, stage, queue, owner, entry date; a blank owner cell for AC7 |
| SCR-02 Case list | Filtered | The chosen queue, team and status shown above the list with a clear control; Export uses the filters shown |
| SCR-02 Case list | Empty | MSG-P3-020 when no case matches |
| SCR-02 Case list | Export refused | MSG-P3-021 naming the maximum of 10,000 rows, and no file |
| SCR-02 Case list | Export failed | MSG-P7-003 when the access-log entry cannot be written, and no file |
| SCR-02 Case list | Refused | MSG-P4-002 on a role without the Case record right |

The screen is SCR-02 and is served by the gateway-bff composite route, which calls rwb-case once and merges the answer into the case screen model, one hop (DP-19). The owner cell shows the owner user reference as the case row holds it; the display name is not this service's to resolve (GAP-2208; ASM-3625). The route path, the screen-model field list and the visual layout belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON and the designer (DL31).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the export row limit, the lists and the queues are parameter and reference rows read with the version in force (BR5; DP-06, DP-07).
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts: a row carries the case number, codes, dates and a staff user reference, never a customer name, identity number, address or account number; test data is synthetic.
- No read of another service's tables: the case and the queue are `rwb_case` rows, and the right, the scope, the masking rules and the access log come through the rwb-access contracts (DP-01, DP-08, DP-11).
- The export is never made when its access-log entry cannot be written, and the entry is written before the file is built (BR3).
- One hop only: the service calls rwb-access and returns, and never calls a service that calls another (ADR-020).
- A refusal is a refusal: a role without the right is a 403 with MSG-P4-002 and never a thinner row or an empty page.
- No event, no workflow and no lock: both operations are reads and the only row written is rwb-access's.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: integration slice of RWB-E1-031 for RWB-ITG-W1. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **QA integration engineer**, I want **the end-to-end proof of the RWB-E1-031 case list with queue and owner, the queue, team and status filters and the Excel export across P3 rwb-case (the list, export and row limit) and P4 rwb-access (the right, the masking and the export access entry)**, so that **scope, masking and the export audit are proved on the real wave 1 services before the wave exits**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story adds the queue and owner columns to SCR-02 Case list, filters the list by queue, team and status inside the caller's scope, and writes the export to the access log through the P4 `AccessEventPublisher` before the file is made. In the 19-service target the same behaviour is served from the owning services: the list and the export stay on P3 rwb-case under `/api/recovery/case/v1` (DP-13); the row limit, the queues and the status lists are data read through the P3 parameters and reference-data contracts (DP-06, DP-07); the access guard and the access log are P4 rwb-access's (DP-08), and the masking rules are P4's, applied over the P1 rwb-source-data masked view columns before any value reaches a response or a file; the screen itself is reached through gateway-bff (DP-19) but is not built or tested here.

The target split for the legacy key is therefore: P3 rwb-case owns the case list query, the queue, team and status filters, the export endpoint and the row limit, and reads the case and queue rows from its own schema (DP-01); P4 rwb-access owns the right check on Case record R, the masking policy for the role and the export access entry with its read path. This story is the integration proof across those two owners. This ITG story owns no legacy acceptance criterion: legacy AC1 to AC8 sit at component level with RWB-P3-E1031-APP, and the access criterion sits with RWB-P3-E1031-APP and RWB-P4-E1039-APP. The ten scenarios of section 7 are the integration proof, and they are all new in D-RCV-60.

No service contract is faked: the suite exercises the published wave 1 contracts of P3 and P4 through gateway-bff. Where the sources do not name the exact access entry and its read path, the masking source used for the export columns, or the home of the row limit and the list rows, the suite asserts through the owners' contracts and records the open point as Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0355; ASM-0451), with its two companions ASM-0452 for the masking source and ASM-0453 for the parameter and list home.

The measure is unchanged from the legacy story: a user sees only the cases their scope allows (REQ-ACA-009), every case carries a queue and an owner visible on the list (REQ-CWC-007), the export holds at most the configured rows, and the list answers in under 2 seconds (NFR-008). The story meets REQ-ACA-005, REQ-ACA-006 and REQ-ACA-009 and supports controls CTL-09 and CTL-11.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P3-E1031-APP is done: the case list, the queue, team and status filters, the export endpoint and the row limit are in SIT on P3 rwb-case.
- RWB-P4-E1039-APP is done: the right check on Case record R, the masking policy for the role and the access log with its write and read are in SIT on P4 rwb-access.
- The published contracts of P3 rwb-case and P4 rwb-access are deployed under their own per-service bases behind gateway-bff.
- The harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG is available with synthetic cases, teams, queues and users.
- The parameter `caselist.export.maxrows` is 10,000 (assumed; DL11), loaded as a data row through the P3 parameters contract.
- The queues and the status lists are loaded as data rows: queue "DIL-BKK-CO", "DIL-BKK-OVF" and "LIT-BKK-OFF", and status "ASSIGNED" and "WAITING_PARTNER".
- The test users U-71 holding RW-TEAMMGR with scope Team, U-7102 holding RW-REFADM, and the scope All users of AC4 and AC8 exist in SIT.
- No production data is used, and no production connection is opened.
- The release date 30 November 2026 is tentative; a date is not a condition of this story.
- This story has no build dependency, so it is ready on Day 1.

##### 4. Flow

1. QA integration engineer: seeds 64 cases in queue "DIL-BKK-CO", 20 in queue "DIL-BKK-OVF" and one case in queue "LIT-BKK-OFF" of team "LIT-BKK" through the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG; no production data is used.
2. Harness: signs in as test user U-71 holding RW-TEAMMGR with scope Team and reads the session through GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/permissions.
3. Harness: calls GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases with page 0 and size 50 and checks each row for case number, product, status, stage, queue, owner and entry date.
4. Harness: filters by queue "DIL-BKK-CO", then by team "DIL-BKK" and status "ASSIGNED", and records the total of each filtered list.
5. Harness: reads GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues and asserts the three queues with their team codes.
6. Harness: calls GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/export on the filtered list and reads the xlsx row count and its header row.
7. Harness: reads GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log and finds the export entry with user U-71, the time, the filters and the row count, and asserts that its write time precedes the file time.
8. Harness: runs the negative cases — no match, 10,001 rows, the access log switched to fail, the out-of-scope queue "LIT-BKK-OFF", the case with no owner, exactly 10,000 rows and the role without Case record R — and records every status, message and entry.
9. Harness: reads GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters and asserts `caselist.export.maxrows` is 10000.
10. Harness: proves the 2 s budget over 20 calls of GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases with page 0 and size 50 on 26,500 synthetic cases in scope, writes the evidence report and removes the fixtures.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | No case meets the filters | The list returns an empty page with total 0 and the empty state is shown | MSG-P3-020 | AC3, AC6 |
| X2 | The filtered list holds more rows than the export limit | The export is refused with 422 and no file is made; the user narrows the filter | MSG-P3-021 | AC4 |
| X3 | The access entry cannot be written | The export returns no file; the refusal is raised before the xlsx is built | MSG-P7-003 | AC5 |
| X4 | A filter names a queue outside the caller's scope | Only in-scope cases return; the out-of-scope queue returns none | MSG-P3-020 | AC6 |
| X5 | A case has no owner | The owner cell is blank and the case is still listed | None | AC7 |
| X6 | The filtered list holds exactly 10,000 rows | The export is allowed and the file holds 10,000 rows | None | AC8 |
| X7 | A role without Case record R calls the list | The call is refused with 403 and no row returns | MSG-P4-002 | AC9 |
| X8 | The list exceeds the 2 s budget | The call is recorded as a breach against NFR-008; the suite reports the percentile and asserts nothing about the data | None | AC10 |
| X9 | A consumed call exceeds its 2 s timeout or returns a server error | The call is retried once under the suite policy; the evidence report records the call and the response; no assertion is made on unverified data | None | AC1, AC2, AC10 |
| X10 | The fixture set does not match the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG expectations | The suite fails as a harness fault and names the missing element; no service defect is raised | None | AC1, AC10 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | The suite is its own module and reuses the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG; it needs the two APP stories and the published contracts of P3 and P4, not their source code |
| Negotiable | The row limit, the queues, the status lists, the fixture sizes and the exact fault-switch mechanism are data rows or harness properties; the story fixes the assertions and the call set |
| Valuable | Scope, masking and the export audit are proved on the real wave 1 services, and the 2 s budget is measured rather than assumed, before the wave exits |
| Estimable | One suite module, one fixture pack of 26,500 cases, one export reader, one access-log assertion, one 2 s sampler and one evidence report |
| Small | Ten scenarios over two services; no service code and no schema change |
| Testable | Every scenario asserts a contract response, a row count, a status or a message; all data is synthetic |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Queue and owner on the case list with filters, end-to-end across wave 1 services

  Background:
    Given the wave 1 services rwb-case and rwb-access are deployed in SIT with their published contracts behind gateway-bff
    Given the RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG synthetic cases, teams, queues and users are loaded and no production data is used
    Given team "DIL-BKK" has 64 cases in queue "DIL-BKK-CO" and 20 in "DIL-BKK-OVF"

  Scenario: AC1 Filter by queue (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given test user "U-71" of team "DIL-BKK" with scope Team
    When "U-71" filters by queue "DIL-BKK-CO"
    Then 64 cases return through GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases, each with its owner and status
    Then no case from another queue shows

  Scenario: AC2 Export with its access entry (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the list filtered by queue "DIL-BKK-CO" and status "ASSIGNED" holds 51 cases
    When "U-71" calls GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/export
    Then an Excel file with 51 rows downloads
    Then GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log holds one export entry with user "U-71", the time, the filters and 51 rows, written before the file

  Scenario: AC3 No case meets the filters (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given test user "U-71" of team "DIL-BKK" with scope Team
    When "U-71" filters by queue "DIL-BKK-CO" and status "WAITING_PARTNER" and no case matches
    Then the list shows the empty state with MSG-P3-020

  Scenario: AC4 Export above the limit (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given parameter "caselist.export.maxrows" is 10000
    Given a filtered list holds 10,001 cases for a user with scope All
    When the user exports
    Then no file is made
    Then MSG-P3-021 shows with maximum 10000

  Scenario: AC5 The access log is unavailable (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the P4 access-log write is switched to fail by the agreed test-only fault switch
    When "U-71" exports a list of 51 cases

    When "U-71" filters by that queue
    Then the case shows with a blank owner value

  Scenario: AC8 Export at the limit (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a filtered list of exactly 10,000 cases for a user with scope All
    When the user exports
    Then a file with 10,000 rows downloads

  Scenario: AC9 A role without Case record R is refused (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given test user "U-7102" holds RW-REFADM

    Then the call returns status 403 with MSG-P4-002

  Scenario: AC10 The list meets the 2 second budget (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given 26,500 synthetic cases in scope
    When the suite calls GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases with page 0 and size 50 twenty times
    Then the 95th percentile response time is under 2 seconds (NFR-008)
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The list holds only cases inside the caller's scope (Own, Team, Region, All) | RWB-E1-031 BR1; REQ-ACA-009; CTL-09; LOV-SCOPE |
| BR2 | Filters combine with AND | RWB-E1-031 BR2; FSD A2.19 |
| BR3 | Every export is written to the access log before the file is made | RWB-E1-031 BR3; REQ-ACA-006; CTL-11 |
| BR4 | Export columns follow the masking rules for the caller's role | RWB-E1-031 BR4; REQ-ACA-005; DL26 |
| BR5 | An export holds at most the configured number of rows | RWB-E1-031 BR5; parameter caselist.export.maxrows = 10,000 (assumed; DL11) |
| BR6 | A screen responds in under 2 seconds | RWB-E1-031 BR6; NFR-008 |
| BR7 | Masking is applied from the P4 rules over the P1 masked view columns before any value reaches a response or the file | REQ-ACA-005; DL26; DP-08 |
| BR8 | The row limit, the queues and the status lists are data rows read through the P3 contracts | DP-06; DP-07 |
| BR9 | Owner display names come from the ACE user directory in the common module and are synthetic in SIT, and every call is one hop with a 2 s timeout | ADR-020; DP-11 |

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story changes no case status; it reads queue, owner and status only. The screen's Loading, empty, list and filtered states are observations of one read, not transitions.

| Observation | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Loading | The screen waits for the page of GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases; the suite reads the same page and adds nothing |
| Empty | The page holds no item and total 0, and MSG-P3-020 is shown; AC3 and AC6 read this state |
| List | Rows carry case number, product, status, stage, queue, owner and entry date; AC1 and AC7 read this state |
| Filtered | The chosen queue, team and status are applied and the total reflects them; AC1, AC2 and AC8 read this state |

The suite reads these observations through the owner's contract; it changes none of them directly.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-TEAMMGR | Lists, filters and exports cases in team scope (Case record R) |
| RW-CASEOWN | Lists and exports their own cases (Case record R, scope Own) |
| Every role with Case record R | Lists cases in its scope |
| RW-REFADM, RW-SECADM | No Case record right; refused |
| RW-COMPLY | Reads the access log entries for exports |
| QA integration engineer | Runs the suite, seeds the synthetic fixtures, reads the evidence report |

No other role is in scope for this story.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The suite provides no REST operation. The names reserved for P2 rwb-integration — `/api/recovery/integration/v1`, `rwb.integration.events.v1`, `rwb-integration` and `rwb_integration` — are not used, and no rwb_integration table is written.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method and path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases | P3 rwb-case | The scoped and filtered list with queue and owner; AC1, AC3, AC6, AC7, AC9, AC10 |
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/export | P3 rwb-case | The xlsx of the filtered list; AC2, AC4, AC5, AC8 |
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues | P3 rwb-case | The queue rows used by the queue filter |
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId} | P3 rwb-case | One case row, to confirm the blank owner of case RW-2026-000601 |
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters | P3 rwb-case | The row limit caselist.export.maxrows as a data row |
| GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log | P4 rwb-access | The export entry with user, time, filters and row count; AC2, AC5 |
| GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/permissions | P4 rwb-access | The right and the masking position of the caller's role |

Every call is one hop with a 2 s timeout (ADR-020, DP-11).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The suite publishes no event.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The suite consumes no topic in this story: the list and the export are synchronous REST reads. No legacy `rwb.p3.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic name appears anywhere in the run (DP-14).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. No workflow, activity or Nexus operation is started or awaited by this story.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The list and the export are on demand; no Schedule, workflow or activity runs for them.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The suite owns no table and never reads another service's schema (DP-01). The rows behind the assertions are recovery_case and queue in rwb_case (P3), and role and masking_rule in rwb_access (P4); each is read only through its owner's contract.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

None. Every call in section 12.2 goes to the real SIT service; no service contract is faked. AC5 uses the agreed test-only fault switch on the P4 access-log write, and it is the only intervention in a running service. The synthetic xlsx is checked by row count and header row only, and its masked columns are checked through the header names.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Provided by the suite | Consumed by the suite |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 | 7 |
| Kafka | 0 | 0 |
| Temporal | 0 | 0 |
| File | 0 | 0 |

The xlsx arrives in the body of the export response; it is not a claim-check file call, so the file column stays at zero.

##### 13. Solution plan

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Suite module for RWB-ITG-W1, reusing harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG | Integration suite | Runs the ten scenarios against SIT and holds no service code |
| Fixture pack | Test data | 26,500 synthetic cases across teams and queues, the queues and status lists, and the test users U-71, U-7102 and the scope All users |
| Export reader | Assertion | Opens the xlsx of the response, reads the header row and the row count, and asserts the masked columns and the absence of a customer name and an identity number |
| Access-log assertion | Assertion | Reads GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log and matches the export entry on user, time, filters and row count, and on its write time preceding the file |
| 2 s sampler | Assertion | Calls GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases with page 0 and size 50 twenty times and reports the 95th percentile against 2 seconds |
| Evidence report | Report | Records per scenario the total, the file row count, the access entry, the statuses, the messages and the percentile |

Decoupling patterns applied (Template and Rules v1 §R5.5):

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added | Where it sits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | recovery.<table>, "recovery schema" | Owner's schema rwb_<name>; never read another service's tables | none | P3 rwb-case reads recovery_case and queue in rwb_case; the suite asserts through contracts only |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON | On RWB-P3-E1031-APP for the row limit; the suite reads the same row as data through GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON | On RWB-P3-E1031-APP for the queues and the status lists; the suite sends the codes as data |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON | On RWB-P3-E1031-APP for the right check and on RWB-P4-E1039-APP for the masking and the access log; the suite asserts the refusal of AC9 and the entry of AC2 |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) | The seven consumed REST operations of section 12.2 |
| DP-13 | /api/recovery/v1 | /api/recovery/<short>/v1 | none | Every consumed path in section 12.2 |
| DP-14 | rwb.p<n>. or rwb.casewf. topic names | rwb.<short>.events.v1; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON | The suite consumes no topic, and no legacy topic name appears in the run |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON | On RWB-P3-E1031-APP for the case and queue rows; the suite owns no table and runs no migration |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The suite enters through gateway-bff; no screen is in scope and none is tested |

The dependency-added column records the build dependency of the owning story. The H, C, I and X lists of this story are exactly those of the metadata table: no H, no C, no X, and the two I dependencies RWB-P4-E1039-APP and RWB-P3-E1031-APP. An ITG story waits on no build of its own.

Build steps:

1. Create the suite module next to harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG and wire it to the SIT endpoints of P3 rwb-case and P4 rwb-access through gateway-bff.
2. Build the fixture pack: 26,500 synthetic cases across teams and queues, the queues "DIL-BKK-CO", "DIL-BKK-OVF" and "LIT-BKK-OFF", the status lists, and the users U-71, U-7102 and the scope All users, with `caselist.export.maxrows` read as a data row.
3. Implement AC1, AC3, AC6 and AC7: the scoped and filtered list, the empty state, the out-of-scope queue and the blank owner.
4. Implement AC2, AC4, AC5 and AC8 with the export reader and the access-log assertion: the 51-row file and its entry, the refusal above 10,001 rows, the fault-switch refusal with no entry, and the 10,000-row file.
5. Implement AC9: the refused call of the RW-REFADM user with status 403 and MSG-P4-002.
6. Implement AC10: the 2 s sampler over 20 calls on 26,500 synthetic cases and the 95th percentile report.
7. Prove BR4 and BR7 over the header row and a value read of the export, write the evidence report, run the suite in SIT against the wave 1 release candidate and remove the fixtures.

Done when: all ten test cases pass in SIT against the published wave 1 contracts of P3 and P4, the export entry is found for every successful export and for none of the refused ones, the 95th percentile of the list is under 2 seconds on 26,500 cases, and no service code or schema was changed by this story apart from the agreed test-only fault switch.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-020 | No case meets the filters | No cases match these filters. Change a filter to see more. |
| MSG-P3-021 | Export above the row limit | The export holds at most {max} rows. Narrow the filters and try again. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Access log unavailable at export | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

A successful export carries no message: the response is the file itself, and its proof is the access entry of AC2.

The message IDs and wording are copied from RWB-E1-031 section 14. No new message ID is added by this story. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-02 Case list, reached through gateway-bff. Loading: skeleton rows. Empty: MSG-P3-020. List: columns case number, product, status, stage, queue, owner, entry date. Filtered: the chosen queue, team and status show above the list with a clear control, and Export uses the filters shown.

The suite does not build or test the screen; it reads the same rows through GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases and the same file through GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/export. The export file name is "Case list 20261202 1.xlsx".

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the row limit, the queues and the status lists are data rows read through the P3 contracts.
- No personal data in logs, tests, evidence or prompts: the export applies masking by role and holds no customer name and no identity number; only field IDs and masking positions are asserted.
- No cross-service table read: every assertion goes through the owner's contract, and the suite owns no table. Owner display names come from the ACE user directory interface.
- One hop and a 2 s timeout on every call (ADR-020).
- The export is never made when its access entry cannot be written; the refusal is raised before the file is built.
- Synthetic data only, loaded by the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG; the scope All users of AC4 and AC8 hold no production right.
- No production access of any kind from the suite or its configuration.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the contract baseline of the intake-match API of `rwb-document` is split out of legacy RWB-E1-032 and published on base `/api/recovery/document/v1` with the topic `rwb.document.events.v1`, the four operations, the four shapes, the five match outcomes, the error envelope, the event schema, the fakes and the drift test. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the intake-match API of `rwb-document` — the list, read, content and resolve operations on base `/api/recovery/document/v1` with the `IntakeItem`, `IntakeItemPage`, `Document` and `IntakeAttachRequest` shapes, the five match outcomes and their status codes with the `match_status`, `review_status`, `candidate_case_ids` and classification fields, the error envelope with every message ID of section 14 and its HTTP status, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the `rwb.document.DocumentAttached.v1` schema with no personal data, the decision-record position and the fakes with their drift test**, so that **the app story of this legacy key, the review screen, the store inside the same service and the wave 1 integration harness build against a fixed, testable contract on Day 1, and a renamed field, a different held-status list or an attach answered with the wrong status can never drift between two builds without a failing test**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). Legacy RWB-E1-032 carries its four endpoints in a section 12 of prose, with an in-process `CaseDirectory` and a `DocumentStore` interface beside them, and it leaves the consumer to infer the exact shapes. Under the target architecture the parts most likely to drift silently are exactly the ones this baseline fixes:

- a field renamed in `IntakeItem` or `IntakeItemPage`, so the Unmatched list on SCR-31 renders without its candidates or its OCR pages;
- a different list of held statuses in the query default, so an item in CONFLICT or NO_TYPE disappears from the reviewer's queue;
- `match_status` widened to the values of another list, so `rwb-case` and `rwb-agent`, which read the attach event, see a value they cannot interpret;
- an attach answered 200 where the legacy contract answers 201, or a concurrent attach answered 409 without `MSG-GEN-004`;
- a `version` that is not the optimistic lock, so two reviewers both attach the same item;
- the attach event changed, or a personal value put into it, so a consumer cannot read it and a data steward cannot approve it.

The baseline fixes the names the checks require: schema `rwb_document`, REST base `/api/recovery/document/v1`, topic `rwb.document.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics, task queue `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document`. It makes the C dependencies of the app story explicit - the P3 parameters contract `RWB-P3-E1042-CON` and the P3 reference-data contract `RWB-P3-E1043-CON` - and it records that the two `rwb-case` reads, the case by number and the open cases by account, are consumed and faked although the plan lists them in no C row (`ASM-1758`).

It also records the naming conflict the sources carry. The legacy story publishes `POST /intake-items/{intakeItemId}/attach` with the Documents right C and a `201 Document` answer; TSD P5 API-P5-013 names `POST /intake-items/{intakeItemId}/resolve` with the right U and an `IntakeResolution` answer; Arch v5 slide 42 lists two events for this service and neither is called `DocumentAttached`. The baseline declares the TSD path and the legacy answer shape, keeps the Documents right C on the chosen case, and records the losers as `GAP-0991` with `ASM-1755` and `ASM-1759`. Nothing else is guessed: the field-level names this key does not settle carry the placeholder `Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0992; ASM-1755)`.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the operation, topic, event and queue names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- The platform error envelope, the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, the `Idempotency-Key` rule and the retry and `.dlt` topic convention are the platform baseline (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON); where this document narrows them it does so explicitly.
- TSD P5 appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2 are in force for API-P5-010, API-P5-011, API-P5-012 and API-P5-013, and TSD P5 T3.1 and T3.2 are in force for the `document`, `document_intake` and `document_text` definitions and the seven-value LOV-INTAKE-MATCH list.
- The Ownership Map is the only source of owners: `document`, `document_intake`, `document_text`, `document_type` and `document_hub_parameter` are P5's in `rwb_document`; `recovery_case`, `case_account`, `lov_value`, `parameter_catalog` and `reference_row` are P3's; `decision_log_entry` is P7's; the ACE views are P1's.
- The classification and extraction baselines are published (RWB-P5-E1050-CON, RWB-P5-E1053-CON), so the fields `predicted_type`, `classification_confidence`, `type_candidates`, `classifier_version`, `review_reason`, `case_no` and `account_no` have one owner document each.
- The store baseline of this service (RWB-P5-E1024-APP) is in force, so the `Document` answer of the resolve operation is the store's shape and not a second one.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7; `ASM-1753`), so its four H, C, I and X columns are empty and every dependant builds against the published baseline and its fakes.
- The release date 30 November 2026 is the legacy one and is tentative (`ASM-1756`), and the story carries Status Draft (realignment v1) because no approval of the realigned story is recorded (`ASM-1757`).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 document of `rwb-document` with the four intake operations, the four resources of section 11 and the error responses of section 14, on the single base `/api/recovery/document/v1`.
2. Fix the list operation: the `matchStatus` default of the five held values, `page`, `size` with its default 50, the oldest-first order and the scope filter that keeps only items whose candidates are in the caller's scope, plus the items with no candidate for scope ALL.
3. Fix the `IntakeItem` and `IntakeItemPage` shapes, so the screen reads one answer with the item, its OCR pages, its type candidates and its candidate cases, and the page carries its own paging fields.
4. Fix the `Document` and `IntakeAttachRequest` shapes, so the resolve operation answers exactly what the store returns and the optimistic lock travels in the request rather than in a header.
5. Fix the five match outcomes, their status values and the fields that carry them, together with the seven values of LOV-INTAKE-MATCH and the five values of LOV-INTAKE-REVIEW.
6. Map every failure to the error envelope and a message ID, status by status, and carry the naming conflict and the missing C row as a gap and an assumption.
7. Record the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the stored answer of a repeat and the `version` lock of the resolve operation.
8. Declare the event position: `rwb.document.DocumentAttached.v1` on `rwb.document.events.v1` with its seven payload fields and no personal data, the record on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and no third event of this key.
9. Publish the seven fakes, the drift test and the baseline tag, then hand the baseline to RWB-P5-E1032-APP, RWB-P5-E1026-APP, the store story and the wave 1 harness.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A response body fails schema validation | The build fails on the schema lint; a deployed service answers 500 with the error envelope | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |
| X2 | A field is renamed, removed or retyped within major version 1 | The contract test fails; the change needs a corrected document or a new major version | None | AC2, AC3 |
| X3 | The list of held statuses differs between the query default and the coverage rule | The contract test fails: the default carries NO_MATCH, MULTIPLE, CONFLICT, CASE_CLOSED and NO_TYPE and nothing else | None | AC4 |
| X4 | An outcome is answered with a status outside the declared set, or `match_status` carries a value outside LOV-INTAKE-MATCH | The contract test fails on the enum and on the status of the operation | None | AC4, AC5 |
| X5 | An error carries no `messageId`, or a message ID with the wrong status | The contract test fails on the error envelope and on the status mapping of section 14 | MSG-GEN-004 | AC5 |
| X6 | A repeat of the same `Idempotency-Key` creates a second document, or the `version` is not the lock | The contract test fails, and the concurrency case answers two 201 where it must answer one 201 and one 409 | MSG-GEN-004 | AC6 |
| X7 | The event payload changes, an eighth field is added, or a personal value appears in it | The AsyncAPI schema test and the no-personal-data test fail | None | AC7 |
| X8 | A fake drifts from the document | The drift test fails the build and the merge is blocked | None | AC8 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Criterion | Verdict | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Independent | Pass | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, TSD P5 T-A and T3, the Ownership Map and the two P5 baselines only |
| Negotiable | Pass | The field-level names are settled with the consumers; the operations, the held-status list, the status mapping, the event schema and the idempotency rule are fixed by the target architecture and the legacy section 12 |
| Valuable | Pass | Unblocks RWB-P5-E1032-APP, the review screen and the wave 1 harness on Day 1 |
| Estimable | Pass | One document, four resources, four operations, four consumed rows, nine contract tables and seven fakes |
| Small | Pass | Fits one sprint with its contract tests |
| Testable | Pass | Every criterion in section 7 is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

The eight criteria are new for the contract baseline and test the artefact only; they restate no business outcome owned by RWB-P5-E1032-APP. The legacy AC1 to AC15 are owned by RWB-P5-E1032-APP, and the wave 1 harness RWB-ITG-E1032-ITG consumes this baseline and copies none of these criteria.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One REST base per service: `/api/recovery/document/v1` on every declared operation | DP-01; Template and Rules §R4; Arch v5 slide 41 notes |
| BR2 | One topic per service: `rwb.document.events.v1`, with the retry and `.dlt` topics of the platform convention | DP-09; Arch v5 slides 16 and 42 |
| BR3 | A change inside major version 1 is additive; a removed, renamed or retyped property and a narrowed required set are a new major version | Architecture v5 slide 42 notes (BACKWARD compatibility) |
| BR4 | The document declares only tables of `rwb_document` and only operations owned by `rwb-document`; a consumed operation is described as consumed and faked, never as provided | Ownership Map; DP-01 |
| BR5 | The event names of this service follow `rwb.document.<Event>.v1` on its own topic, and the baseline declares one event and one record and no third event | Arch v5 slides 16 and 42; DP-09; DP-14 |
| BR6 | No business value is fixed in the contract: the patterns, the threshold, the type list, the decision code, the review labels and the paging defaults are parameters, reference rows or document defaults | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17; RWB-E1-032 section 17 |
| BR7 | No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: identifiers, codes, versions, confidences, dates and page text of synthetic documents only, and no customer name, address or national ID number in any payload | Arch v5 slide 11; RWB-E1-032 section 17 |
| BR8 | No OCR text and no file byte in the event or the decision record: the payload carries the item ID and the match method, and the text stays behind the read operation with masking and the access log | DP-09; RWB-E1-032 section 17 |
| BR9 | Every consumed row states one hop, a 2 s timeout, a GET retry once with jitter and a breaker per downstream, and a failed read maps to MSG-GEN-006 naming the system that failed | DP-11, ADR-020; Arch v5 slide 11 |
| BR10 | Every error uses one envelope and one message ID per condition; the message texts are copied unchanged from legacy RWB-E1-032 section 14 | Architecture v5 platform baseline; Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR11 | A POST requires `Idempotency-Key` and stores its answer; a GET declares none; the resolve operation carries the optimistic lock in the body as `version` | Architecture v5 slide 11; DP-09; legacy AC15 |
| BR12 | The contract declares no case state and no document state machine beyond the values the fields may take; a transition belongs to the app story that performs it | RWB-E1-032 section 9; RWB-P5-E1032-APP owns the match transitions |

##### 9. State transitions

| Baseline state | Event | Condition | Next state |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The four operations, the four resources, the four consumed rows and the event schema are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | RWB-P5-E1032-APP, the review screen, the store owner and the wave 1 harness accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A property is added within major version 1, for example an optional `reviewReason` on the page item | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A property is removed, renamed or retyped, or a required set is narrowed | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake, or a retired element returns | A contract test fails | In review |

This baseline declares no case state machine and no document state machine of its own. The intake item states PENDING, MATCHED, NO_MATCH, MULTIPLE, CONFLICT, CASE_CLOSED and NO_TYPE are field values of `matchStatus`, and the transitions between them belong to RWB-P5-E1032-APP. The seven values are the whole of LOV-INTAKE-MATCH and the baseline declares all of them, including PENDING and MATCHED, so a consumer can read the field in every state (`ASM-1754`).

| Field value in the baseline | Meaning declared by this document |
|---|---|
| `matchStatus` = "PENDING" | An item the matcher has not decided yet; the selected value of the next run |
| `matchStatus` = "MATCHED" | An item attached to exactly one case, automatically or by a person |
| `matchStatus` = "NO_MATCH" | No case and no account number resolved, or the case number does not exist |
| `matchStatus` = "MULTIPLE" | Two or more open cases for the account number |
| `matchStatus` = "CONFLICT" | The case number and the account number point to different cases |
| `matchStatus` = "CASE_CLOSED" | The only candidate is closed |
| `matchStatus` = "NO_TYPE" | Classification named no agreed type, or the model was unavailable |
| `reviewStatus` = "PENDING" | A stored document whose type a person must confirm; `write_once` is false |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Tech lead of rwb-document | Owns the OpenAPI document, the AsyncAPI fragment and the seven fakes; tags the baseline |
| Solution architect | Approves a breaking change, a new major version and the resolution of `GAP-0991` |
| Consuming teams (RWB-P5-E1032-APP, the review screen, the store owner, the wave 1 harness) | Review and sign off the parts they consume |
| RW-LITOFF and RW-CASEOWN, the reviewer roles | Confirm that the list, the item read and the resolve answer carry what the review queue needs (Documents C on the chosen case) |
| Platform library owner | Owns the CloudEvents envelope, the error envelope, the `Idempotency-Key` rule and the naming rule this document reuses |
| Data steward | Confirms that no personal data field is declared in an answer, an example or a fake |

The per-service login behind the document's security scheme is not part of this baseline; the document names the scheme "the rwb-document login (DP-02)" and the name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0992; ASM-1755). The declared area and right are enforced at gateway-bff (DP-19); no `rwb-access` contract is declared here.

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| IntakeItem | intakeItemId (uuid), source (one of LOV-DOC-SOURCE), receivedAt, matchStatus (one of LOV-INTAKE-MATCH), predictedType, classificationConfidence (numeric(5,4)), typeCandidates, candidateCases (caseId, caseNo), pages (pageNo, text), reviewReason (one of LOV-INTAKE-REVIEW), version, from the `document_intake` fields DF-DOC-045 to DF-DOC-084 |
| IntakeItemPage | items (array of IntakeItem), page, size, total; the list is oldest first by receivedAt |
| Document | documentId, caseId, partyId, documentType, source, storageRef, classificationConfidence, reviewStatus, retentionClass, writeOnce, docVersion, from the `document` fields DF-DOC-001 to DF-DOC-011 and the store answer of RWB-P5-E1024-APP |
| IntakeAttachRequest | caseId (uuid, required), documentType (string, required), version (integer, required) |
| DocumentText page | pageNo (integer), text (string); read from `document_text` DF-DOC-088 and DF-DOC-089, masked by role |
| Match outcome set | MATCHED, NO_MATCH, MULTIPLE, CONFLICT, CASE_CLOSED (the legacy five) with NO_TYPE and PENDING as the additional values of LOV-INTAKE-MATCH |
| DecisionRecord | decisionCode DOCATT, finalCall, inputsRef, decidedAt and the chain fields of the library; the match method and the classifier version are inputsRef content and not a copy of the text |
| Error envelope | RFC 9457 problem details with `messageId`, `detail`, `instance` and the status of section 14 |

Every example in the document is synthetic and uses the legacy values: case "RW-2026-000123", account "TEST-ACC-0002", the confidence 0.9300 and 0.62, the threshold 0.80, the classifier version "CLS-1.0" and the decision code "DOCATT". No example carries a real customer value; the legacy values are examples only. The field-level names of `IntakeItem`, `IntakeItemPage` and `IntakeAttachRequest` beyond the legacy list are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0992; ASM-1755), and the baseline fixes them as the smallest superset of that list.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-document (P5); base `/api/recovery/document/v1`.

| Method | Path | API ID | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/intake-items` | API-P5-010 | 200 `IntakeItemPage`; query `matchStatus` default NO_MATCH, MULTIPLE, CONFLICT, CASE_CLOSED and NO_TYPE, `page`, `size` 50, oldest first, scope applied | Documents R, scope applied | None |
| GET | `/intake-items/{intakeItemId}` | API-P5-011 | 200 `IntakeItem` with the OCR pages, masked by role; each read to the access log | Documents R, scope applied | None |
| GET | `/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/content` | API-P5-012 | 200 `application/octet-stream`, the file of the held item | Documents R, scope applied | None |
| POST | `/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/resolve` | API-P5-013 | Request `IntakeAttachRequest`; answer 201 `Document` | Documents C, scope applied to the chosen case | `Idempotency-Key` header plus the `version` lock |

Error statuses 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 are those of T-A.2 and section 14. The TSD path is declared; the legacy `POST /intake-items/{intakeItemId}/attach` is recorded as the loser of the conflict `GAP-0991` with the assumption `ASM-1755`, and it is declared nowhere in the document.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/by-no/{caseNo}` | P3 rwb-case | The case, its status and its owner for the match by case number; one hop, 2 s, faked; the contract is RWB-P3-E1018-CON and the plan lists it in no C row (`ASM-1758`) |
| GET | the open-cases-by-account read of rwb-case | P3 rwb-case | The open cases of an account number for the MULTIPLE outcome; same owner document; the path is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0992; ASM-1758) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters/{paramCode}` | P3 rwb-case | `CASE_NO_PATTERN`, `ACCOUNT_NO_PATTERN` and `CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD` (C `RWB-P3-E1042-CON`) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 rwb-case | LOV-INTAKE-MATCH, LOV-INTAKE-REVIEW, LOV-DOC-TYPE, LOV-DOC-SOURCE and LOV-REVIEW (C `RWB-P3-E1043-CON`) |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retry once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (DP-11, ADR-020). A failed read maps to 503 with MSG-GEN-006 naming the system that failed and never to a held item answered as matched. The two case reads are consumed and faked and are named in no C row of the plan, so they carry `ASM-1758` and no row is added to the metadata C list.

This baseline declares the event schema and the record declaration because the service owns the topic; the event row itself is written by the attach path of RWB-P5-E1032-APP inside the store transaction, and this key publishes nothing at run time. Arch v5 slide 42 lists `DocumentStored` and `DocumentFieldsExtracted` for this service and not the name above; the difference is recorded as `GAP-0991` with `ASM-1759`, and the event catalogue owner confirms the final name before the wave 1 release. No third event exists for this key.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** The OpenAPI 3.1 document `openapi/rwb-document-v1.yaml` with the four intake operations and the four resources; the AsyncAPI 3.0 fragment for `rwb.document.DocumentAttached.v1` and the record declaration; the contract README rows for the outcome set, the error mapping, the idempotency rule and the event count; and the seven WireMock mapping sets of section 12.8.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The H, C, I and X lists of the metadata table are empty: this baseline adds no build dependency of its own (it is Day 1 by rule), and the platform and service contracts it names are the ones the app story declares. DP-01 is applied because every shape derives from a table of `rwb_document` and no other schema is declared. DP-03 is applied because the resolve operation's record is declared and faked here, although the row is written by the app story. DP-05 is applied by removal: the legacy ACE view read behind `CaseDirectory` is not part of the baseline and the account arrives inside the `rwb-case` answer. DP-06 and DP-07 are the two C rows: the three parameters and the five lists are read through the `rwb-case` contracts and never typed into the document. DP-09 fixes the topic, the envelope and the `Idempotency-Key` rule. DP-10 names the `matchStep` activity contract and the workflow that calls it, without declaring a Schedule. DP-11 fixes the four consumed rows to one hop with 2 s and a fake each. DP-15 records that the three tables behind the shapes belong to this service's own migration sequence. DP-19 records that the list and the item read are reached through the gateway-bff composite route; this baseline fixes the answer shapes only and no route specification.

**Build steps**

1. Write the four operations with their paths, queries, resources and error responses; validate the document in the pipeline.
2. Fix the required and optional sets of AC2 and AC3 and the paging default as schema constraints and README rows.
3. Declare the outcome set and the four status and list fields of AC4, with the seven values of LOV-INTAKE-MATCH as an enum.
4. Map every status and message ID of AC5 and record the RFC 9457 envelope, including the not-found placeholder.
5. Record the `Idempotency-Key` rule and the `version` lock of AC6.
6. Declare the event and the record of AC7, with the no-personal-data test and the absence test for a fourth operation and a foreign event name.
7. Publish the seven fakes and the eight contract tests, including the drift test; tag the baseline and collect the consumer sign-off of RWB-P5-E1032-APP, the review screen and the wave 1 harness.

**Done when.** The OpenAPI artefact and the AsyncAPI fragment validate in the pipeline, the eight contract tests pass, the seven fakes answer every operation and read of sections 12.1 and 12.2, the drift test is green, and RWB-P5-E1032-APP and RWB-ITG-E1032-ITG have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | HTTP status |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P5-003 | Item held for a person or document stored for review (a label, not an error) | Some fields need checking. The document is in the review queue. | 200 |
| MSG-P5-006 | Reviewer picks a type not in force | {value} is not a document type in force. Choose a type from the list. | 422 |
| MSG-GEN-001 | Case or type missing on attach, or a response body that fails validation | Enter {field}. | 422 |
| MSG-GEN-004 | Item attached by someone else, or a changed version | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. | 409 |
| MSG-P7-003 | Decision record write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | 503 |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | 403 |
| MSG-P4-003 | Chosen case outside the scope | This case is not in your scope. | 403 |
| MSG-P4-001 | No authenticated caller | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0992; ASM-1755) | 401 |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The case read failed or timed out | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. | 503 |
| not-found message | An intake item or a document that does not exist | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0992; ASM-1755) | 404 |

The message IDs and the wording are contract elements copied unchanged from RWB-E1-032 section 14; Thai text for each follows decision DL10. MSG-P4-001, MSG-GEN-006 and the not-found message are named by the target error envelope and are copied from the platform set, and their exact texts are recorded as the placeholder above.

Delivery shape: every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set to the ID above, `detail` carrying the text with its placeholders filled, and `instance` naming the request. The status mapping is the legacy one plus the two platform rows: 401 with MSG-P4-001, 403 with MSG-P4-002 or MSG-P4-003, 404 with the not-found message, 409 with MSG-GEN-004, 422 with MSG-P5-006 or MSG-GEN-001, and 503 with MSG-P7-003 or MSG-GEN-006. For MSG-GEN-006 the {system} value is fixed by the consumed row that failed, and it is "Case service" for both `rwb-case` reads.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-31 Document review queue is the screen these operations serve, reached through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), which calls the owner once and merges the answer into the screen model; the screen itself and its attach dialog are RWB-P5-E1032-APP and the case document list is RWB-P5-E1026-APP. This baseline fixes the answer shapes only and declares no screen field list and no route specification. The states its shapes imply are: an item in each of the seven match statuses, a page of OCR text masked by role, a candidate list of one or more cases, and a held item that no longer exists when a second reviewer resolves it.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the patterns, the threshold, the type list, the decision code, the review labels and the paging default stay parameters, reference rows or document defaults of the app story.
- No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: identifiers, codes, versions, confidences and dates only, and the page text of a synthetic document only.
- No OCR text and no file byte in the event or the decision record: the payload carries the item ID and the match method, and the text stays behind the read operation with masking and the access log.
- The two `rwb-case` reads are consumed and faked and never declared as provided; the parameters and the lists arrive through their client libraries (DP-06, DP-07).
- ACE data is reached only through the owner's contract or a `v_ace_*` view; this document declares no ACE view and no cross-schema join (DP-05).
- The contract names only `rwb_document` tables and only operations owned by `rwb-document`; a foreign base or a foreign table fails the review (DP-01).
- One REST base and one topic per service; a document that names another service's base or topic as its own fails the review.
- The event name carries the service short and the topic is the service's own; the difference from the catalogued DocumentStored is recorded in `GAP-0991` and never hidden (DP-14).
- Every example in the document is synthetic and the legacy values are examples only; no production payload is copied into a schema or a fake.
- The contract declares no case state and no intake state machine; a transition belongs to RWB-P5-E1032-APP.

Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **documents from the OCR intake attached to their case automatically when the case ID or the account number is read, with unmatched or ambiguous documents held for a person who sees the OCR text and the candidate cases and attaches the document**, so that **no document is filed by hand when the case is clear and none is filed on the wrong case when it is not**.

Inside `rwb-document` this is the auto-attach capability of the document hub, and the same user story holds with the target service frame:

- Service `rwb-document`, schema `rwb_document`, REST base `/api/recovery/document/v1`, topic `rwb.document.events.v1` with the retry and `.dlt` topics of the platform convention and event names `rwb.document.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document`.
- The matcher reads its three parameters `CASE_NO_PATTERN`, `ACCOUNT_NO_PATTERN` and `CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD` through the parameters contract and client library of `rwb-case` (DP-06, H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON). The rows they resolve to stay in `document_hub_parameter` in `rwb_document`, which the Ownership Map gives to P5 (ASM-1748).
- The match outcomes, the review reasons and the review states are read as reference data through the reference-data contract of `rwb-case` (DP-07, H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON): LOV-INTAKE-MATCH, LOV-INTAKE-REVIEW, LOV-DOC-TYPE, LOV-DOC-SOURCE and LOV-REVIEW. No list value is typed in code.
- The case and the account are resolved through the `rwb-case` contract (RWB-P3-E1018-CON, one hop, 2 s timeout, DP-11), never from a case table of another service and never from a `recovery_case` copy: `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/by-no/{caseNo}` for a case number and the open-cases-by-account read for an account number, whose exact path is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0991; ASM-1749).
- The document is stored through the store capability of RWB-P5-E1024-APP, which stays the only writer of the `document` table and the DOCATT decision record; this story writes `document_intake` and reads `document_text`, and calls the store in the same service.
- The decision is recorded through the local decision-record library of DP-03 (H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON; the central ledger contract is RWB-P7-E1027-CON) with decision code DOCATT and the match method. A failed record means nothing is stored and the item stays `PENDING` (MSG-P7-003, R-UNI-39).
- The attach outcome is published as `rwb.document.DocumentAttached.v1` on `rwb.document.events.v1` (the legacy DocumentStored, EV-16, carried through the store), keyed by caseId, written to the outbox in the same transaction as the store (DP-09, H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON); the difference from the event catalogue of Arch v5 slide 42 is recorded as GAP-0991 and ASM-1752.
- JOB-12 Document intake becomes a Temporal Schedule started through the workflow kit (DP-10, H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON), and `matchStep` is one activity of `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` on queue `rwb-document`, registered by RWB-P5-E1049-APP, which owns the workflow. The Schedule is deployed and monitored by RWB-P5-E1032-OPS.
- The `document_intake` and `document_text` tables are created by this service's own per-service Flyway step in `rwb_document` (DP-15, H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON), and the Unmatched list reaches SCR-31 through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19, H RWB-PLT-N001-CON).
- The database login is one per service (DP-02). Its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0991); this story uses the phrase "the rwb-document login (DP-02)" and never a shared login.
- The legacy feature flag `rwb.dochub.autoattach` is retired with the monolith and replaced by `rwb.document.intake-autoattach` (ASM-1751).

The legacy behaviour is carried unchanged in intent and values: the same user story, rationale, preconditions, flow, fourteen exception paths, seven business rules, seven messages, authority, data fields, fifteen acceptance criteria and seventeen test cases, adapted to the target service's schema, topic, API base and workflow template.

##### 2. Business rationale

Scans, partner files and emails arrive without a case link; today a person reads each one and files it. This story matches each classified intake item to one open case by the case ID or the account number in its text and stores it on that case with no person involved (FSD P5 A2.12). An item that matches no case, more than one case, a closed case or no agreed type is held as unmatched, and a person attaches it from the review queue with the OCR text and the candidates in front of them. It meets REQ-DCM-007 and writes the document attached record required from Epic 1 (REQ-DRI-004, RWB-E1-027). The measure is fields extracted without review (FSD P5 A2.12.1).

The realignment changes the mechanics, not the business rule:

1. One schema, one topic, one API base: `rwb_document`, `rwb.document.events.v1` and `/api/recovery/document/v1` (DP-01). No table of another service is read and no monolith table name survives; the legacy story names no monolith API path, so DP-13 is not in this story's pattern list.
2. The case is no longer read in process through `CaseDirectory`: it arrives through the `rwb-case` contract with a mock and a 2 s timeout (DP-11, ASM-1749), so the matcher builds against a published shape and its fake on Day 1.
3. The decision log write becomes the local decision-record library of DP-03, written in the same transaction as the `document_intake` update and the store's outbox row, and published on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; `rwb-decision` collects it into the central ledger.
4. The Quartz step of JOB-12 becomes the `matchStep` activity of the `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` template of the workflow kit, started by a Temporal Schedule on queue `rwb-document` (DP-10).
5. The account view read of the legacy flow (`v_ace_account` through `CaseDirectory`) is removed with the in-process call: the account number is matched inside the `rwb-case` answer and this service reads no ACE view (DP-05).
6. The three parameters arrive through the parameters contract and the five lists through the reference-data contract (DP-06, DP-07); the document-hub parameter rows sleep in `rwb_document`, which is P5's own store for them.
7. The attach event is written to the outbox inside the store transaction and published once per stored document by the relay (DP-09); the intake item update commits with it.
8. The intake tables are created in the per-service Flyway sequence (DP-15), and the Unmatched list and the item detail are served through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).

Business preconditions carried from RWB-E1-032, in the target wording:

- RWB-E1-050 is done: intake items carry predicted_type, classification_confidence, type_candidates, classifier_version and review_reason.
