The field-level names of the four operations and the exact path of the open-cases-by-account read are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0991; ASM-1749); the baseline RWB-P5-E1032-CON fixes the names this story is built against.

##### 4. Flow

1. JOB-12 Document intake: the intake Schedule starts `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` on queue `rwb-document` every 15 minutes in business hours; it runs `matchStep` after the extraction step, as one activity of the same workflow (DP-10).
2. `matchStep`: selects `document_intake` rows with `ocr_status` DONE, `match_status` PENDING, no `document_id` and a predicted type (`review_reason` empty or LOW_CONFIDENCE), locking each row with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`; items with `review_reason` UNKNOWN_TYPE or MODEL_UNAVAILABLE get `match_status` NO_TYPE and are held for a person.
3. `CaseMatcher`: collects case numbers from the extracted field `case_no` and from the OCR text of `document_text` with `CASE_NO_PATTERN`, and account numbers from the extracted field `account_no` and the same text with `ACCOUNT_NO_PATTERN`; both patterns arrive through the parameters contract (DP-06).
4. `CaseMatcher`: resolves each case number through the `rwb-case` contract `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/by-no/{caseNo}` and each account number through the open-cases-by-account read, and returns one of MATCHED, NO_MATCH, MULTIPLE, CONFLICT or CASE_CLOSED with the candidates. A contract error, a 2 s timeout or an open breaker fails the activity and leaves the item PENDING for the next run.
5. `matchStep`: for MATCHED, calls the store of RWB-P5-E1024-APP with the case ID, `predicted_type`, the intake source, the file of the hold container, its SHA-256 and the extracted fields; the store writes the DOCATT entry with the classifier version, the confidence and the match method, the `document` row and the attach event.
6. `matchStep`: on the stored document sets `classification_confidence`, `document_type` and `type_candidates`; for `review_reason` LOW_CONFIDENCE sets `review_status` PENDING and `write_once` false, so it is held in `rwb-docs` and listed on SCR-31 (RWB-E1-054).
7. `matchStep`: sets the `document_intake` row `match_status` MATCHED, `case_id` and `document_id`; for any other result sets `match_status` to the result and `candidate_case_ids`, and the item is held for a person. The row update, the store row and the outbox row commit in that order inside one transaction of `rwb_document`.
8. Reviewer: opens the Unmatched list on SCR-31 through the gateway-bff composite route (`GET /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items`), opens an item to see the scan, the OCR text of `document_text` and the candidates (`GET /intake-items/{intakeItemId}` and `GET /intake-items/{intakeItemId}/content`), picks the case and the type, and attaches it (`POST /intake-items/{intakeItemId}/resolve`).
9. `ManualAttachService`: checks with `rwb-case` that the case is in the reviewer's scope and with the type table that the type is in force, calls the store with the reviewer as approver on the DOCATT entry, sets the item `match_status` MATCHED, `review_outcome` ATTACHED and `resolved_by`, and returns the Document. The `version` of the item is the optimistic lock.
10. Outbox relay: publishes `rwb.document.DocumentAttached.v1` to `rwb.document.events.v1` and the decision record to `rwb.decision-record.v1`, once per committed attach, keyed by caseId, with no personal data; the store's own `DocumentStored` row for the same document is the legacy EV-16 carried through (12.3, GAP-0991).

The decision record is written before the change takes effect and inside the store transaction, so a failed record leaves the document, the intake item and the outbox unchanged, and an automatic attach stays PENDING for the next run (R-UNI-39).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | No readable case ID or account number | Item held, match_status NO_MATCH, OCR text held for the reviewer | MSG-P5-003 | AC2 |
| X2 | The account number matches two or more open cases | Item held, match_status MULTIPLE, every candidate offered | MSG-P5-003 | AC3 |
| X3 | The case ID and the account point to different cases | Item held, match_status CONFLICT, both cases offered | MSG-P5-003 | AC5 |
| X4 | A case ID is read that does not exist | No candidate; NO_MATCH | MSG-P5-003 | AC6 |
| X5 | The only candidate case is closed | Item held, match_status CASE_CLOSED | MSG-P5-003 | AC7 |
| X6 | The same file is already on the matched case | The item is linked to the existing document; no second document | None | AC8 |
| X7 | The job runs again over attached items | No second attach, entry or event | None | AC9 |
| X8 | Classification confidence below the threshold and one case matched | Stored with review_status PENDING and write_once false | MSG-P5-003 | AC10 |
| X9 | No agreed type from classification | Item held, match_status NO_TYPE | MSG-P5-003 | AC11 |
| X10 | The reviewer picks a case outside their scope | Refused with 403; item stays held | MSG-P4-003 | AC13 |
| X11 | The reviewer picks a type not in force | Refused with 422 | MSG-P5-006 | AC14 |
| X12 | Two reviewers attach the same item at the same time | The first succeeds; the second gets 409 | MSG-GEN-004 | AC15 |
| X13 | The decision log write fails during an attach | Nothing stored; an automatic attach stays PENDING for the next run; a manual attach returns 503; incident raised (R-UNI-39) | MSG-P7-003 | TC-E1-032-17 (Principle 5) |
| X14 | A role without Documents C attaches an item | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-032-16 (Access) |

Three target-service notes:

- JOB-12 is no longer a Quartz job: it is a Temporal Schedule on queue `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, registered from the values of RWB-P5-E1032-OPS, and `matchStep` is an activity of `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` on the same queue (DP-10). A run that leaves items PENDING is retried by the next run of the Schedule, exactly as the legacy restart behaviour states.
- The `rwb-case` contract answers two calls per item; a 2 s timeout, a 503 or an open breaker fails the activity, leaves the item PENDING and raises MSG-GEN-006 with {system} = "Case service"; the breaker shields `rwb-case`, and this service adds no retry of its own beyond the activity retry of the kit.
- The legacy `POST /intake-items/{intakeItemId}/attach` is published as `POST /intake-items/{intakeItemId}/resolve` (12.1, GAP-0991; ASM-1750); the refusal shapes of X10 to X14 are unchanged by the rename.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the store (RWB-P5-E1024-APP), the classification output (RWB-P5-E1050-CON), the extracted fields (RWB-P5-E1053-CON), the case contract (RWB-P3-E1018-CON), the decision-record library, the parameters and reference-data libraries, all earlier or contract work |
| Negotiable | The two patterns, the threshold, the outcomes and the reviewer action are data rows or fixed behaviour; the shapes come from the contract baseline |
| Valuable | Ends hand filing for every scan that names its case or account, and gives every other scan one place to be filed |
| Estimable | One job activity, one matcher, four endpoint operations, one list tab, one migration |
| Small | Fits within two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test case in section 16 |

Every Given, When and Then line above is the legacy line unchanged: the only added lines are the four Background mock Givens on the `rwb-case` contract and the `rwb-decision` contract Given in AC1 and AC12, and the legacy endpoints map to the target operations of 12.1 as `GET /review-items` → `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items`, `GET /intake-items/{id}` → `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}`, `POST /intake-items/{id}/attach` → `POST /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/resolve`, and `JOB-12` → the intake Schedule that starts `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` with its `matchStep` activity.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A classified document attaches to its case without a person when exactly one open case is found | REQ-DCM-007; FEAT-DCM-12 |
| BR2 | The case is found by the case ID or the account number read from the document; the account number is the join to other systems | DL21; parameters CASE_NO_PATTERN and ACCOUNT_NO_PATTERN in document_hub_parameter (New) |
| BR3 | No match, more than one candidate, disagreement, a closed case or no agreed type goes to a person | REQ-DCM-005; FSD P5 A2.12.4 |
| BR4 | A document classified below the threshold is stored for review in the standard container, not write-once, until a person confirms its type | Parameter CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD in document_hub_parameter (New); RWB-E1-054; CTL-12 |
| BR5 | Each attach is written to the decision log with the classifier version, the confidence and the person where one decided, before the document is stored | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; REQ-DRI-004 |
| BR6 | An item attached once is not attached again | R-UNI-40 |
| BR7 | A reviewer attaches only to a case in their scope | CTL-09 |

Target-service statements that make the rules hold in `rwb-document`:

- BR1 and BR3 are executed by `CaseMatcher` over the answer of the `rwb-case` contract: the five outcomes are fixed behaviour, not rule rows, and the matcher never picks one of several candidates. An item with no candidate reaches a role with scope ALL only.
- BR2 is executed by the two patterns read through the parameters contract (DP-06): the patterns are compared against the extracted fields and the `document_text` pages, and no pattern is typed in code.
- BR4 is executed by `matchStep` setting `review_status` PENDING and `write_once` false on the stored document, so the store keeps the file in `rwb-docs` and not in `rwb-docs-legal` (RWB-P5-E1024-APP); the confirmation of the type and the fields is RWB-P5-E1054-APP.
- BR5 is executed by the decision-record library of DP-03 inside the store transaction: the DOCATT record, the `document` row, the `document_intake` update and the outbox row commit together or not at all (R-UNI-39).
- BR6 is executed by the selection rule of `matchStep` (`match_status` PENDING and no `document_id`), by the store's duplicate check on case, type and hash (`uk_document_case_type_hash`) and by the optimistic lock on `document_intake.version`.
- BR7 is executed by the authorisation decision the service template's guard holds against `rwb-access`, and by the case read of the chosen case before the store call; every read of the item detail is written to the PII access log by the ACE common module, never by this package.
- DP-05 keeps ACE data out of this service: the account number is matched inside the `rwb-case` answer and no `v_ace_*` view is read. DP-09 puts the attach event in the outbox; DP-15 puts the intake migration in the per-service sequence; DP-19 puts the two screens behind the gateway-bff composite route.

##### 9. State transitions

None for the case. This story does not change a case status. It changes the intake item match_status: PENDING to MATCHED on an automatic attach; PENDING to NO_MATCH, MULTIPLE, CONFLICT, CASE_CLOSED or NO_TYPE when held for a person; a held value to MATCHED when a reviewer attaches it. It creates a document record (COPY_PENDING, then STORED, in RWB-E1-024, now RWB-P5-E1024-APP).

| From (`document_intake.match_status`) | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| PENDING | `matchStep` finds exactly one open case and the type is agreed | The store commits with the DOCATT record and the outbox row | MATCHED |
| PENDING | `matchStep` finds no case | No case number and no account number resolves | NO_MATCH |
| PENDING | `matchStep` finds two or more open cases for the account | The store is not called | MULTIPLE |
| PENDING | `matchStep` finds a case number and an account that point to different cases | The store is not called | CONFLICT |
| PENDING | `matchStep` finds only a closed case | The store is not called | CASE_CLOSED |
| PENDING | `matchStep` reads UNKNOWN_TYPE or MODEL_UNAVAILABLE from classification | The store is not called | NO_TYPE |
| NO_MATCH, MULTIPLE, CONFLICT, CASE_CLOSED, NO_TYPE | A reviewer resolves the item | Scope and type checks pass, the store commits | MATCHED |

The held values are the same on a repeat run: an item in any held state is not selected by `matchStep` again, and an item that fails on the decision record stays PENDING. The document state machine COPY_PENDING to STORED belongs to RWB-P5-E1024-APP and is not changed by this story.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| SY-OCR, OCR and extraction pipeline | Matches and attaches automatically (Documents C) |
| SY-DECLOG, decision log writer | Writes the DOCATT entry |
| Roles with Documents C and the candidate case in scope (for example RW-LITOFF, RW-CASEOWN) | See and attach unmatched items that name a candidate in their scope |
| Roles with Documents C and scope ALL (for example RW-LEGAL) | See and attach unmatched items with no candidate |
| Roles with Documents R only (for example RW-TEAMMGR) | See attached documents on cases in their scope; no attach |

In the target the authorisation decision is taken by `rwb-access` (roles as data, scope, masking and DoA in `rwb_access`) and consumed as the cached permission decision the service holds; this story adds no guard of its own and inherits the 403 shapes of MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P4-003. SY-DECLOG is the local decision-record library of DP-03 in the target, called inside the store transaction, and it publishes the DOCATT record on `rwb.decision-record.v1`. The worker runs as the rwb-document service identity (DP-02), carried by the chart as a secret reference; the login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0991).

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary and the TSD P5 T3.1 table. No `recovery_case` row is copied and no ACE view is read by this service: DF-CAS-001, DF-CAS-002, DF-CAS-005, DF-CAS-026 and DF-ACE-002 arrive inside the `rwb-case` contract answer, and DP-01 forbids a foreign-schema read. Personal data never enters the event payload, the workflow input, the decision record or the log: OCR text is read by the reviewer's screen only, and a log line carries the intake item ID, the outcome and the match method, never a text page, a file name or an account number in clear.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-document (P5); base `/api/recovery/document/v1`; the shapes are those of RWB-P5-E1032-CON.

| Method | Path | Owner | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/resolve` | P5 | Resolve a held item: attach it to a case in scope with a type in force. `IntakeAttachRequest` in, 201 `Document` out, Documents C on the chosen case, `Idempotency-Key` required, `version` as the optimistic lock. The legacy name `/attach` and the TSD right U are recorded in GAP-0991 and ASM-1750 |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items` | P5 | The Unmatched list of SCR-31 (legacy `GET /review-items`): query `matchStatus` (default the five held values NO_MATCH, MULTIPLE, CONFLICT, CASE_CLOSED and NO_TYPE), `page`, `size` (default 50); answer 200 `IntakeItemPage`, oldest first, only items whose candidates are in scope, and items with no candidate for scope ALL |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}` | P5 | One held item as `IntakeItem`: source, received time, match status, predicted type, confidence, the type candidates, the candidate cases and the OCR text pages, masked by role; each read written to the PII access log |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/content` | P5 | The file of the held item as `application/octet-stream`, read from `rwb-quarantine` through the storage product; Documents R with scope applied |

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Story | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/by-no/{caseNo}` | P3 rwb-case | RWB-P3-E1018-CON | The case exists, its status and its owner; one hop, 2 s timeout, breaker per downstream, one GET retry with jitter (DP-11) |
| GET | the open-cases-by-account read of rwb-case | P3 rwb-case | RWB-P3-E1018-CON | The open cases of an account number for the MULTIPLE outcome; one hop, 2 s timeout; the exact path is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0991; ASM-1749) |
| GET | the parameters read of DP-06 | P3 behind the client library | RWB-P3-E1042-CON | `CASE_NO_PATTERN`, `ACCOUNT_NO_PATTERN`, `CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD`, cached for 5 minutes |
| GET | the reference-data read of DP-07 | P3 behind the client library | RWB-P3-E1043-CON | LOV-INTAKE-MATCH, LOV-INTAKE-REVIEW, LOV-DOC-TYPE, LOV-DOC-SOURCE, LOV-REVIEW |

The store of RWB-P5-E1024-APP is the same service and is called through its published operation (`POST /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/store`), one hop with a 2 s budget; it is not a contract of another service and appears in 12.9 as REST consumed inside the service. A failed case read maps to 503 with MSG-GEN-006 naming "Case service" and leaves the item PENDING.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Key | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.document.DocumentAttached.v1` (the attach outcome; the legacy DocumentStored, EV-16) | `rwb.document.events.v1`, with the retry topics at 1 min, 10 min and 1 h and the `.dlt` topic | P5 | caseId | documentId, caseId, documentType, source, intakeItemId, matchMethod, attachedAt |
| decision record (DOCATT) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | PLT library, consumed by P7 | caseId | the hash-chained record with decision code DOCATT, the match method CASE_ID, ACCOUNT_NO or PERSON, the classifier version and the confidence |

CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, binary mode; no personal data and no OCR text in either payload. The attach event and the record are written to the outbox inside the store transaction, so they exist exactly when the document row and the item update exist. Arch v5 slide 42 lists DocumentStored and DocumentFieldsExtracted for this service and not the name above; the difference is recorded as GAP-0991 and ASM-1752, and the event catalogue owner confirms the final name before the wave 1 release.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document`, module `intake/attach`; front end folder `recovery/documents`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| MatchStepActivity | Temporal activity | `matchStep`: select, lock, match, store or hold, update `document_intake`; idempotent by item ID |
| CaseMatcher | Service | Reads case numbers and account numbers from the extracted fields and `document_text`; resolves them through `rwb-case`; returns the outcome and the candidates |
| MatchPatterns | Library client | Reads `CASE_NO_PATTERN`, `ACCOUNT_NO_PATTERN` and `CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD` through the parameters contract, cached for 5 minutes |
| AutoAttachService | Service | Builds the store request with the classification inputs, applies the review rule of BR4 and updates the item |
| ManualAttachService | Service | Scope and type checks, optimistic lock on the item, store call with the reviewer as approver |
| IntakeItemController | Controller | The four operations of 12.1, with the access check, the scope filter and the RFC 9457 error mapping |
| IntakeItemRepository | Repository | Reads and writes `document_intake` only, and reads `document_text`; `version` is the optimistic lock |
| UnmatchedIntakeTab | React component | The Unmatched list on SCR-31 with the scan viewer, the OCR text, the candidates, the case picker and the type picker |

**Database.**

- One migration in the per-service Flyway sequence (DP-15): `V1032_1__intake_match.sql` adds to `document_intake` `match_status` varchar(12) not null default 'PENDING', `candidate_case_ids` jsonb, `review_outcome` varchar(12), `resolved_by` uuid and `resolved_at` timestamptz; the classification columns come from the RWB-P5-E1050-CON migration and the text table from the RWB-P5-E1049-APP migration.
- Indexes: `ix_intake_held ON document_intake (match_status, received_at) WHERE match_status NOT IN ('PENDING', 'MATCHED')`; `ix_intake_pending ON document_intake (match_status, received_at) WHERE match_status = 'PENDING'`; `ix_intake_sha ON document_intake (file_sha256)`.

**Configuration and reference data.**

- Parameters `CASE_NO_PATTERN` = "RW-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{6}", `ACCOUNT_NO_PATTERN` = "[0-9]{10}" (assumed; DL21) and `CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD` = 0.80 in `document_hub_parameter`, read through the parameters contract (DP-06, ASM-1748).
- Reference lists LOV-INTAKE-MATCH, LOV-INTAKE-REVIEW, LOV-DOC-TYPE, LOV-DOC-SOURCE and LOV-REVIEW read through the reference-data contract (DP-07); no list value is typed in code.
- Decision code DOCATT, assumed, with the LOV-DECISION list loaded by the data steward; the match method is one of CASE_ID, ACCOUNT_NO or PERSON.
- Feature flag `rwb.document.intake-autoattach` (ASM-1751). Off: `matchStep` sets every classified item to `match_status` NO_MATCH and reviewers attach them by hand, exactly as the legacy flag states.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-01 moves the three tables the legacy story wrote into `rwb_document` and stops the module reaching into the recovery schema: `document_intake` and `document_text` are this service's, and the `document` row is written only through the store. DP-03 replaces `DecisionLogWriter` with the local library, so the DOCATT record, the item update and the outbox row share one transaction and the record is published on the shared topic. DP-05 is applied by removal: the legacy `AceSourceQuery` and `v_ace_account` read inside `CaseDirectory` are gone, because the account number is matched inside the `rwb-case` answer and this service reads no ACE view. DP-06 and DP-07 keep the three parameters and the five lists out of the code through the two client libraries, while the parameter rows themselves stay in `rwb_document` as the Ownership Map gives them to P5. DP-09 puts the attach event and the record in the outbox. DP-10 turns the Quartz step of JOB-12 into the `matchStep` activity of the kit's "Document intake" template, started by a Schedule that this story does not register. DP-11 is the case read: one hop, a published shape, a fake in the build and a 2 s timeout, replacing the in-process `CaseDirectory`. DP-15 puts the intake migration in the service's own sequence. DP-19 puts the Unmatched list and the item detail behind the gateway-bff composite route, so SCR-31 calls the owner once.

**Build steps**

1. Write the migration and the entities; test that the held index returns only held items and that the optimistic lock refuses a stale `version`.
2. Build `MatchPatterns` and the text scan; unit test the two patterns on synthetic Thai and English text around the numbers.
3. Build `CaseMatcher` against the case fake and unit test the five outcomes, AC2 to AC7, and the 2 s timeout path.
4. Build `AutoAttachService` with the store call, the review rule of BR4 and the item update; integration test AC1, AC4, AC8, AC10 and AC11.
5. Build `MatchStepActivity` selection and skip rules and register it with the kit on queue `rwb-document`; test AC9 and the repeat run.
6. Build `IntakeItemController` and `ManualAttachService`; API tests AC12 to AC15, the access test TC-E1-032-16 and the scope refusal of AC13.
7. Build `UnmatchedIntakeTab`; component tests for the list, the detail, the OCR text, the candidates and the attach dialog.
8. Test the decision-record failure path for the automatic and the manual attach (TC-E1-032-17) and confirm that nothing is stored and the item stays PENDING.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass and, on the 180 synthetic samples in SIT, every item with one readable case ID and a confidence at or above 0.80 is attached in the same run, with one DOCATT record and one attach event per stored document.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P5-003 | Item held for a person or document stored for review | Some fields need checking. The document is in the review queue. |
| MSG-P5-006 | Reviewer picks a type not in force | {value} is not a document type in force. Choose a type from the list. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | Case or type missing on attach | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | Item attached by someone else | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Decision log write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | Chosen case outside the scope | This case is not in your scope. |

Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

Delivery shape: every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set to the ID above, `detail` carrying the text with its placeholders filled, and `instance` naming the request. The HTTP mapping is the legacy one and is fixed by AC13 to AC15 and the baseline RWB-P5-E1032-CON: 403 for MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P4-003, 409 for MSG-GEN-004, 422 for MSG-P5-006 and MSG-GEN-001, and 503 for MSG-P7-003 and MSG-GEN-006 naming "Case service". MSG-P5-003 is not an error response: it is the label of a held item and of a document stored for review on SCR-31 and SCR-30. A held item that a reviewer opens is a 200; an item that no longer exists answers 404 with a not-found message whose ID is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0991).

##### 15. Screens and states

| Screen | State | What the user sees and does |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-31 Document review queue | Loading | Skeleton rows while the Unmatched list loads through the gateway-bff composite route |
| SCR-31 Document review queue | list | The Unmatched tab: items oldest first with source, received time, match status, proposed type and candidate cases |
| SCR-31 Document review queue | held | An item in NO_MATCH, MULTIPLE, CONFLICT, CASE_CLOSED or NO_TYPE shows MSG-P5-003, its OCR text pages by role and the candidates it has, and the attach dialog with the case picker and the type picker |
| SCR-31 Document review queue | refused | A case outside the scope answers MSG-P4-003 in the dialog and the item keeps its held status; a type not in force answers MSG-P5-006 naming the value |
| SCR-31 Document review queue | reviewed | The item is attached; it leaves the list and the document opens on SCR-30 of the chosen case |
| SCR-30 Case documents | list | An automatically attached document shows on its case; a PENDING document shows MSG-P5-003 |

The tab for documents pending type or field review on SCR-31 is built in RWB-E1-054 (now RWB-P5-E1054-APP), and the case document list is RWB-P5-E1026-APP; this story adds the Unmatched tab and the attach dialog only.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the case number and account number patterns and the threshold are parameters read through DP-06, and the five lists are reference data read through DP-07.
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts: account numbers and OCR text are never logged; logs carry the intake ID and the outcome; test accounts are synthetic.
- No read of another module's tables: cases and accounts are resolved through the `rwb-case` contract, one hop, 2 s timeout, and no `v_ace_*` view is read by this service (DP-01, DP-05).
- The matcher never picks one of several candidates; any doubt goes to a person, and an item with no candidate is visible only to a role with scope ALL.
- A document stored for type review is never put in the write-once container before its type is confirmed: `write_once` false and `rwb-docs` until RWB-P5-E1054-APP confirms the type (RWB-E1-054; CTL-12).
- The decision record is written in the same transaction as the document, the item update and the outbox row; a failure stores nothing (R-UNI-39).
- The attach is idempotent twice over: `Idempotency-Key` on the resolve POST, and the selection rule plus the store's duplicate check on case, type and hash.
- The feature flag `rwb.document.intake-autoattach` removes the automatic attach without a rollback of the schema (ASM-1751).

| Requirement ID | Requirement (short) | BRD section | Feature | L3 process | Rules | Test cases |

##### 1. Story

As a **partner portal user of an instructed firm (PT-AGENCY, PT-LAWFIRM, PT-VALUER, PT-AUCTION, PT-BUYER, PT-RAMC)**, I want **the file I submit on my instruction to reach the OCR intake carrying the case its instruction names, and to show its attach state on the instruction**, so that **no partner file is filed by hand when the firm and the instruction are clear, and none is filed on a case the firm was not instructed on**.

This is the secondary slice of legacy RWB-E1-032 (FEAT-DCM-12). The legacy story names partner files as one of the three sources that arrive without a case link. The case owner, the reviewer, the matcher and the store are the primary slice's; this story owns the partner side of the same attach, a boundary no source states and this story fixes (GAP-3138; ASM-5504), and **owns no legacy AC**: AC1 to AC15 and TC-E1-032-01 to TC-E1-032-17 stay with RWB-P5-E1032-APP, which is where the case is matched, the document is stored and the reviewer resolves a held item (GAP-3144; ASM-5510).

In the target frame the service is `rwb-partner`, schema `rwb_partner`, REST base `/api/recovery/partner/v1`, topic `rwb.partner.events.v1` with the retry and `.dlt` topics of the platform convention and event names `rwb.partner.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-partner` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.partner` (Template and Rules R4; GAP-3137; ASM-5503). It builds:

- the submission `POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/documents` on the service base (DP-13) and the read `GET /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/documents`, behind the partner gateway for partners and the gateway-bff composite route for staff (DP-19);
- the row `partner_intake` in `rwb_partner` (DP-01) with its own Flyway step (DP-15), holding the firm, the instruction, the document type, the file SHA-256, the case ID of the instruction, the state and the intake item ID;
- one local decision record per accepted file in the same transaction (DP-03), so an accepted partner file exists only with the record that proves the acceptance;
- the fact `rwb.partner.PartnerDocumentSubmitted.v1` on `rwb.partner.events.v1`, written to the outbox in that transaction and keyed on the case ID (DP-09), so the document hub's matcher receives the case the instruction names and the partner source;
- the consumption of `rwb.document.DocumentAttached.v1` and the read of `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}` of RWB-P5-E1032-CON (DP-11), so the submission closes with the document ID or carries the held match outcome back to the partner;
- the reconcile Schedule `partner-intake-reconcile` on queue `rwb-partner` in the legacy JOB-12 cadence (DP-10);
- the document type list and the intake bound as reference data and parameter, never as code (DP-06, DP-07).

The file, the OCR, the classification, the extraction, the match, the case, the account and the document row are not this service's (section 19).

##### 2. Business rationale

Scans, partner files and emails arrive without a case link; today a person reads each one and files it (legacy RWB-E1-032 section 2). A partner file is the one source whose party knows, at the moment of sending, which instruction and therefore which case it belongs to, and that knowledge is the only thing the partner service can add to the intake: the firm, the instruction and its case ID. Without it the matcher has to read the case out of the OCR text alone, and a partner file whose instruction is clear is held as if it were an anonymous scan.

Architecture v5 moves that fact once and in one direction. The partner reaches the partner gateway (FAPI 2.0) that fronts S9, so the submission is a REST operation on the service base; the case and the document live in other services, so the partner service sends the case hint as a fact on `rwb.partner.events.v1` and reads the outcome back through the published contract of the document hub, one hop with a 2 s budget. It writes no document row, no intake item, no case row and stores no file.

The one rule that must hold is that an accepted partner file exists only with its record (principle 5; R-UNI-39). The submission row, the local record and the outbox row are one `rwb_partner` transaction; if the record cannot be written nothing happens and the partner sees MSG-P7-003. The second rule is that a file is submitted once (R-UNI-40): the write key on the instruction and the file hash, with the `Idempotency-Key` on the operation, make the repeat return the first answer.

No business value is invented. The states are the legacy match states (`PENDING`, `MATCHED`, `NO_MATCH`, `MULTIPLE`, `CONFLICT`, `CASE_CLOSED`, `NO_TYPE`); the types are the legacy document types of the LOV; the hold rule is legacy BR3 and the record rule is legacy BR5. The requirement rows are REQ-DCM-007 (a classified document attaches without a person), REQ-DCM-005 (a document that cannot be matched goes to a person) and REQ-DRI-004 (the attached record), read for their partner half.

##### 3. Preconditions

- `RWB-P5-E1032-CON` is published: the IntakeItem shape, the item read `GET /intake-items/{intakeItemId}`, the five match outcomes, the error envelope and the `Idempotency-Key` rule. The contract dependency never blocks the build (§R5.4, §R5.7); the partner service builds against the published shape and its fake on Day 1.
- The document-hub operation that creates an intake item for a partner file is reachable; The exact path and shape are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3141; ASM-5507). The four operations RWB-P5-E1032-CON publishes are the resolve, the list, the item read and the content read, and the creation is outside them.
- `rwb_partner` and its login exist, and the service's own Flyway sequence is at the version that carries the library tables; this story adds one version and never edits an applied migration.
- `partner`, `partner_user`, `partner_instruction` exist with the columns of the S9 module tables (DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-016, DF-REF-212 to DF-REF-217), and the instruction carries `case_id`, `partner_id`, `instruction_type`, `due_at` and `status`.
- A partner instruction of type `COLLECT` on a case sits with the firm in status `SENT`, `ACCEPTED` or `IN_PROGRESS`, so a file may be submitted on it.
- The partner user reaches the service through the partner gateway, holds Partner portal C, and the instruction belongs to the user's own firm (NFR-050).
- The reference lists LOV-DOC-TYPE and LOV-INSTR-STATUS are in force at their version and the intake bound parameter is in force; no source names the bound or the parameter row this service reads (GAP-3142; ASM-5508).
- The decision code of the acceptance and the version in force are read as values at their version; which code and version the record names is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3142; ASM-5508).
- MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-003 and MSG-GEN-006 are unchanged from FSD and the legacy story.
- No approval stop: FSD S9 and TSD S9 are not approved in this run and the story is Draft (realignment v1) (ASM-5512).
- Wave 1 is the W-MAP wave of EP01 and is earlier than the Arch v5 wave 4 of rwb-partner; the W-MAP wave is kept as R5.6 requires and the release date is copied unchanged and marked tentative (GAP-3139; ASM-5505).

##### 4. Flow

1. The partner user submits a file with its document type on `POST /api/recovery/partner/v1/partner/instructions/{instructionId}/documents`, behind the partner gateway.
2. The guard library resolves the identity and the right; a role without Partner portal C is refused before any read (MSG-P4-002).
3. The service reads `partner_instruction`, `partner` and `partner_user` in `rwb_partner` and checks that the instruction belongs to the firm of the partner user (404 otherwise, disclosing nothing).
4. It checks the state: a file is accepted only from `SENT`, `ACCEPTED` or `IN_PROGRESS`; `DONE`, `DECLINED` and `RECALLED` answer 409 and change nothing (X1).
5. It validates the submission: a file present, a `documentType` in LOV-DOC-TYPE, the body within the intake bound; a missing or refused element answers 422 with MSG-GEN-001 and the field (X2).
6. It computes the SHA-256 of the file, takes the case ID of the instruction as the case hint, and assembles the record with the decision code and the version in force.
7. In one `rwb_partner` transaction: the `partner_intake` row is written with state `PENDING`, the firm, the instruction, the type, the hash and the case ID; the record is written through `DecisionRecordWriter.record`; the outbox row is written (DP-03, DP-09).
8. If the record write refuses, nothing at all is written and the answer is MSG-P7-003 (AC6, X3).
9. After the commit the service calls the document hub's intake creation with the file reference, the partner source and the case ID, one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker (DP-11; the path is GAP-3141); a failure leaves the row `PENDING` and the reconcile run retries it (X4).
10. The relay publishes `rwb.partner.PartnerDocumentSubmitted.v1` on `rwb.partner.events.v1` keyed on the case ID; the document hub's matcher resolves the case, stores the document and publishes `rwb.document.DocumentAttached.v1` (that journey is RWB-P5-E1032-APP's).
11. On the attach event the service matches the submission by its intake item ID and sets `MATCHED` with the document ID, and signals `documentAttached` to `PartnerInstructionWorkflow` (AC2).
12. The reconcile Schedule runs every 15 minutes in business hours over the rows still `PENDING`: it reads `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}` and copies the match state and the candidate case IDs onto the row; a held value is shown to the partner read only, and the item is resolved by a person holding Documents C in rwb-document (AC3).
13. The submission list and its states reach the partner portal and SCR-35 through the composite route, one hop; no screen writes (DP-19).
14. The same `Idempotency-Key` and the same hash under the same instruction return the first answer and write no second row and no second event (AC4).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The instruction is `DONE`, `DECLINED` or `RECALLED`, or belongs to another firm | 409 for a closed instruction, 404 for a foreign firm; nothing written, nothing called | MSG-GEN-001 for the closed case is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3141; ASM-5507) | AC5 |
| X2 | A required element is missing or the body exceeds the intake bound | The whole submission is refused; no row, no record, no event, no intake call | MSG-GEN-001 | AC5 |
| X3 | The local decision record cannot be written | Nothing is written: no row, no event, no intake call | MSG-P7-003 | AC6 |
| X4 | The intake creation misses the 2 s budget or its breaker is open | The row stays `PENDING`; the reconcile run retries with jitter; the partner is told it is queued | MSG-GEN-006 | BR6 |
| X5 | The same file and the same `Idempotency-Key` are submitted twice | The first answer returns, the repeat is counted, one row and one event exist | None | AC4 |
| X6 | The attach outcome never arrives and the item is held | The reconcile run copies the held match state and the candidates; this service attaches nothing | MSG-P5-003 to the partner, read only | AC3 |
| X7 | A component or test reaches a document, intake, case or ledger table | The grant refuses and the boundary test fails the build | None (pipeline log) | Section 17 |

X1 to X6 are this slice's paths; X7 is the inherited boundary rule. The legacy X1 to X12 (no match, two candidates, conflict, a case that does not exist, a closed case, a duplicate file, a repeat run, low confidence, no type, a reviewer outside scope, a type not in force, two reviewers at once) are the matcher's and the reviewer's and stay with RWB-P5-E1032-APP; this slice receives their outcome as a state and never decides it.

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Starts on Day 1 with no H row and one C row; the document hub is a mock and the case arrives inside the instruction |
| Negotiable | The operation path, the activity names, the intake bound and the write key are this story's design choice; the states, the types and the messages are fixed |
| Valuable | A partner file that names its instruction is attached without a person and is never filed on a case the firm was not instructed on |
| Estimable | One operation, one read, one migration, one record adapter, one event in and one out, one Schedule, one screen fragment |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests, as the secondary slice of one legacy key |
| Testable | Each of the seven criteria of section 7 is one automated test |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Automatic attach from the OCR intake — the partner file channel

  Background:
    Given partner instruction of type "COLLECT" on case "RW-2026-000123" for firm "TEST-PT-001" and account "TEST-ACC-0001", in status "ACCEPTED"
    Given the partner user holds Partner portal C and the instruction belongs to the user's own firm
    Given the lists LOV-DOC-TYPE and LOV-INSTR-STATUS are in force at their version and the intake bound parameter is in force
    Given the rwb-document contract mock returns intake item "TI-0001" with match_status "PENDING" for the submission of case "RW-2026-000123"

  Scenario: AC1 A partner file on an open instruction is recorded and announced (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the partner user submits a file of type "APPRAISAL_REPORT" with SHA-256 "H1" on the instruction
    When the submission operation validates it and writes the transaction
    Then partner_intake holds one row with state "PENDING", the firm ID, the instruction ID, type "APPRAISAL_REPORT", hash "H1" and case_id "RW-2026-000123"
    Then exactly one local decision record is written in the same transaction, naming the decision code of the acceptance and the version in force
    Then exactly one PartnerDocumentSubmitted event is written to the outbox in that transaction, keyed on the case ID
    Then the event carries the submission ID, the instruction ID, the case ID, the document type and the hash, and no personal data and no file content
    Then the document hub intake is called once with the file reference, the partner source and case "RW-2026-000123", and the row records the intake item ID it answers
    Then this service writes no document row, no intake item, no case row and stores no file

  Scenario: AC2 The attach outcome closes the submission (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the submission of AC1 holds state "PENDING" with intake item "TI-0001"
    Given the rwb-document contract mock returns the attach event for "TI-0001" on case "RW-2026-000123" with document "DOC-0001"
    When the attach event is consumed
    Then partner_intake holds state "MATCHED" and document_id "DOC-0001"
    Then PartnerInstructionWorkflow receives the documentAttached signal once
    Then a second delivery of the same event changes no column and writes no second record

  Scenario: AC3 A held file is copied to the partner side and attached by no one here (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rwb-document contract mock returns intake item "TI-0002" with match_status "MULTIPLE" and candidate cases "RW-2026-000321" and "RW-2026-000654"
    When the reconcile run reads the item
    Then partner_intake holds state "MULTIPLE" and both candidate case IDs
    Then this service attaches nothing, stores no file and writes no document row
    Then the partner portal and SCR-35 show state "MULTIPLE" with both candidate cases, read only
    Then the item is resolved by a person holding Documents C in rwb-document, and the next run copies state "MATCHED" and the document ID

  Scenario: AC4 The same file under the same instruction writes one submission (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the submission of AC1 is complete
    When the partner user submits the same file with the same SHA-256 "H1" on the same instruction with the same Idempotency-Key
    Then the first answer is returned and the repeat is counted
    Then partner_intake holds one row for hash "H1" and the instruction
    Then rwb.partner.events.v1 holds one event for it

  Scenario: AC5 A submission that cannot be accepted writes nothing (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given an instruction in status "DONE", an instruction of another firm and a submission with no document type
    When the partner user submits on each
    Then the closed instruction answers 409 and the foreign instruction 404
    Then the submission without a type answers 422 with MSG-GEN-001
    Then a role without Partner portal C answers 403 with MSG-P4-002
    Then no partner_intake row, no decision record and no event is written, and the intake is not called

  Scenario: AC6 A refused record leaves no trace (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the decision record cannot be written
    When the partner user submits a file on an open instruction
    Then the answer is 503 with MSG-P7-003
    Then no partner_intake row and no outbox row exists
    Then the document hub intake is not called

  Scenario: AC7 The submission and its attach state read on SCR-35 (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the gateway-bff composite route serves SCR-35 Placement and allocation
    Given the instruction holds two submissions, one "MATCHED" and one "MULTIPLE"
    When a case owner holding Partner portal R opens SCR-35 for the case

    Then the browser calls no owner service directly and no screen writes anything
```

AC1 to AC7 are new under D-RCV-60 and test only the rwb-partner deliverable of the title. No legacy criterion is restated: the fifteen legacy criteria of RWB-E1-032 stay word for word with RWB-P5-E1032-APP (GAP-3144; ASM-5510). Every value above is a legacy value (case, account, types, states, messages, the JOB-12 cadence) or test data.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A partner file is accepted on an instruction of the user's own firm that is not closed; a closed instruction and a foreign instruction write nothing | legacy RWB-E1-032 sections 3 and 5; NFR-050 |
| BR2 | The case hint of a partner file is the `case_id` of its instruction; this service resolves no case by itself and reads no account | legacy BR2 (the case is found by the case read); DP-01 |
| BR3 | No match, more than one candidate, a disagreement, a closed case or no agreed type goes to a person, and the person resolves it in rwb-document | legacy BR3; REQ-DCM-005 |
| BR4 | A partner file is accepted only with a document type in force and within the intake bound, both read at their version | legacy BR1 and BR4; DP-06, DP-07 |
| BR5 | Each acceptance is written to the record before the row, the event and the intake call exist; a failed record means nothing happens | legacy BR5; principle 5; R-UNI-39 |
| BR6 | A contract read or call that misses the 2 s budget changes nothing and is retried once with jitter | ADR-020; legacy X13 |
| BR7 | A file submitted once under one instruction is not submitted again: one hash, one row, one event | legacy BR6; R-UNI-40 |
| BR8 | The partner sees the state of its own submission only, and read only; the item detail and the resolve are rwb-document's | legacy BR7; CTL-09 |
| BR9 | A submission carries identifiers, codes, a hash and dates only; no personal data and no file content reach the row, the record, the event or the log | legacy guardrails; Architecture v5 slide 22 |

BR1 is the firm and state check of steps 3 and 4; BR2 is the case hint of step 6; BR3 is the held states of step 12 and X6; BR4 is the validation of step 5; BR5 is `recordPartnerDocument` and the rollback of X3; BR6 is the retry of X4; BR7 is the write key and the `Idempotency-Key` of AC4; BR8 is the access of 12.1; BR9 is the payload rule of 12.3.

##### 9. State transitions

The case status is rwb-case's and is not moved here. The document state machine is rwb-document's. The rows below are the states of a partner submission, and they are the legacy match states, copied and not extended.

| From (`partner_intake.state`) | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| (none) | Submission accepted | Validation passes, the record and the outbox row commit | `PENDING` |
| (none) | Submission refused | A closed instruction, a foreign firm, a refused element or an unrecordable acceptance | No row (`X1`, `X2`, `X3`) |
| `PENDING` | Attach event for its intake item | The document hub stored the document | `MATCHED`, `document_id` set |
| `PENDING` | Reconcile run reads the item | The item holds `NO_MATCH`, `MULTIPLE`, `CONFLICT`, `CASE_CLOSED` or `NO_TYPE` | The same value, with the candidate case IDs |
| `PENDING` | Reconcile run reads the item | The item is still `PENDING` or the read fails | `PENDING`; retried by the next run |
| `NO_MATCH`, `MULTIPLE`, `CONFLICT`, `CASE_CLOSED`, `NO_TYPE` | Reconcile run reads the item | A person holding Documents C resolved it in rwb-document | `MATCHED`, `document_id` set |

`PENDING` is the only state a submission is created in, and a submission leaves the held set only through the document hub's own resolution: this service copies the state and never sets it on a document.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Partner portal users of the instructed firm: PT-AGENCY, PT-LAWFIRM, PT-VALUER, PT-AUCTION, PT-BUYER, PT-RAMC (C on their own firm) | Submit a file on their own firm's instruction; read their own submissions |
| RW-AGENCYMG, partner and agency manager (CRUDA) | Read the submissions of any firm; submit on behalf of a firm through the portal |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner (R) | Read the submissions and their attach state on the case |
| RW-LITOFF, RW-ENFORCE, RW-SALEOFF, RW-NPAMGR, RW-DEBTSALE, RW-GUARANT (R) | Read the submissions inside their capability area |
| RW-AUDIT, RW-COE (R) | Read the submission and the record it was accepted under |
| A person holding Documents C (in rwb-document) | Resolve a held item there; this service grants no attach right and holds no document |
| SY-PARTNER, service identity (login `rwb_partner`) | Writes `partner_intake`, the record and the outbox row in its own schema; no grant elsewhere |
| Role without Partner portal C | Refused with MSG-P4-002 before any read |

No delegation of authority level applies: submitting a file decides nothing about the customer, and the record names the code in force, not a person's level. No personal name or credential appears in the story, a test or a log.

| DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007 | partner (S9, `rwb_partner`) | id, partner_code, partner_type, panel_status, contract_end, score | Read, the firm and its panel status |
| DF-REF-212 to DF-REF-217 | partner_user (S9, `rwb_partner`) | identity_ref, partner_id, role_code, valid_from, valid_to | Read, the firm and role binding |
| Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3143; ASM-5509) | partner_intake (S9, `rwb_partner`, created by this story) | id, partner_id, instruction_id, case_id, document_type, file_sha256, intake_item_id, state, candidate_case_ids, received_at | Write on acceptance; written again by the attach event and the reconcile run |
| Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3143; ASM-5509) | partner_intake (S9) | version, created_at, created_by, updated_at, updated_by | Write the audit columns; `version` is the optimistic lock |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision_record (local, `rwb_partner`) | all fields, through `DecisionRecordWriter.record` | Write, in the same transaction (DP-03) |
| DF-DOC-001 to DF-DOC-011 | document (P5, `rwb_document`) | the document and its ID | Not read and not written: they arrive in the attach event |
| DF-DOC-075, DF-DOC-076 | document_intake (P5) | match_status, candidate_case_ids | Read through the item read of RWB-P5-E1032-CON only |
| DF-CAS-001, DF-CAS-002, DF-CAS-005 | recovery_case (P3, `rwb_case`) | id, case_no, status | Not read: the case ID is the instruction's and travels as the event key |
| DF-ACE-002 | v_ace_account | account_code | Not read: this service resolves no account (DP-05) |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_partner` | the outbox row, the inbox row and the write key | Write through the library, in the transaction (DP-09) |

`partner_intake` is the only table this story creates and writes, and the fields above are its design content, not source values: no published data model carries a partner-side intake row (GAP-3143). No foreign key leaves `rwb_partner`: `partner_id`, `instruction_id` and `case_id` are identifiers. No file and no OCR text is stored here.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-partner (S9); base `/api/recovery/partner/v1` (DP-13). No source publishes these two operations (GAP-3141; ASM-5507).

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/partner/instructions/{instructionId}/documents` | Multipart: file, documentType; `PartnerSubmission` out, 201; errors 401, 403, 404, 409, 415, 422, 503 | Partner portal C, own firm, guard library | `Idempotency-Key` header |
| GET | `/partner/instructions/{instructionId}/documents` | Query: state, page, size; `SubmissionPage` out; errors 401, 403, 404, 503 | Partner portal R, own firm, scope applied | Not applicable |

Both are reached through the partner gateway (FAPI 2.0) by partners and through the composite route by staff (DP-19). Errors are RFC 9457 problem bodies; the 409 body text is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3141; ASM-5507).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Story | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | the intake creation of the document hub | P5 rwb-document | RWB-P5-E1032-CON carries the IntakeItem shape; the operation itself is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3141) | One hop, 2 s timeout, breaker, one POST retry with jitter; a failure leaves the row `PENDING` (DP-11) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}` | P5 rwb-document | RWB-P5-E1032-CON (12.1 of RWB-P5-E1032-APP) | The match state and the candidate cases of a submission not yet concluded |
| GET | the parameters read of DP-06 | P3 behind the client library | RWB-P3-E1042-CON | The intake bound, cached for 5 minutes |
| GET | the reference-data read of DP-07 | P3 behind the client library | RWB-P3-E1043-CON | LOV-DOC-TYPE and LOV-INSTR-STATUS at their version |

The two list reads and the bound arrive through the client library of the service template, so the plan's C row names the document-hub contract only (GAP-3140; ASM-5506).

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Key | Payload carries | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.partner.PartnerDocumentSubmitted.v1` | `rwb.partner.events.v1` | `caseId` | submission ID, instruction ID, case ID, document type, file SHA-256, intake item ID, submitted time | Carries the partner source and the case hint to the document hub's matcher and the state to rwb-reporting; written to the outbox in the transaction |

| Envelope element | Value |
|---|---|
| Mode | CloudEvents 1.0, binary |
| ce_type | `rwb.partner.PartnerDocumentSubmitted.v1` |
| ce_source | rwb-partner |
| ce_subject and key | The case ID of the instruction |
| ce_id and traceparent | The event identifier and the W3C trace context of the call |
| Payload | Identifiers, a type code, a hash and a time only; no file content, no OCR text, no personal data, no file name |

The event name and its catalogue ID are this story's design choice and are absent from the Arch v5 event list for this service (GAP-3141; ASM-5507). The retry and `.dlt` topics are the service template's and add no row here.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.document.DocumentAttached.v1` | `rwb.document.events.v1` | P5 rwb-document (RWB-P5-E1032-APP 12.3) | Matched to the submission by its intake item ID: sets `MATCHED` and `document_id` and signals the instruction workflow; a duplicate is discarded by the inbox row (AC2) |

The held match states do not travel as events: the reconcile run reads them through the item read of 12.2, so a held item is copied and never re-decided here.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PartnerInstructionWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per instruction, owned by the S9 instruction stories | `rwb-partner`, namespace `rwb-recovery` | Signal `documentAttached` with the submission ID and the document ID; a replay reuses the recorded outcome |
| `recordPartnerDocument` (name is this story's design choice) | Activity | `rwb-partner` | One `rwb_partner` transaction: the submission row, the record, the outbox row; then the intake call |
| `reconcilePartnerIntake` | Activity | `rwb-partner` | The item read per open submission, the state copy, the retry of a failed intake call |
| `PartnerIntakeReconcileWorkflow` | Workflow, started by the Schedule of 12.6 | `rwb-partner` | The L3 "Document intake" template applied to the partner channel: one activity over the open submissions |

The signal and activity names are fixed by no source (GAP-3141; ASM-5507).

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Schedule | Workflow | Queue | Interval | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `partner-intake-reconcile` | `PartnerIntakeReconcileWorkflow` | `rwb-partner` | Every 15 minutes in business hours (the legacy JOB-12 cadence) | Registered by this story; a run that leaves a submission `PENDING` is retried by the next run, as the legacy restart behaviour states |

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Schema | Owner | This story |
|---|---|---|---|
| `partner_intake` | `rwb_partner` | S9 | Creates it in its own Flyway step; writes the row, the state, the candidate case IDs and the intake item ID |
| `partner` | `rwb_partner` | S9 | Read only, the firm and its panel status |
| `partner_user` | `rwb_partner` | S9 | Read only, the firm and role scope |
| `partner_instruction` | `rwb_partner` | S9 | Read only, the case hint, the type and the state |
| `decision_record` | `rwb_partner` | PLT library applied here | Written through `DecisionRecordWriter.record`; the central `decision_log_entry` is P7's (DP-03) |

Not owned and never read as a table: `document`, `document_intake` (P5), `recovery_case`, `task`, `timer` (P3), `decision_log_entry`, `rule_row` (P7) and `interaction` (P1). No foreign key leaves the schema.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `RWB-P5-E1032-CON` intake fake | An intake item ID with state `PENDING`; a held item with a match state and two candidates; a `MATCHED` item with a document ID; a 409 for a closed instruction; a 404 for a foreign firm; a 422 for a refused element | AC1, AC2, AC3, AC5 |
| Attach-event fixture | One `rwb.document.DocumentAttached.v1` per item keyed on the case ID, and the same event twice | AC2, AC4 |

The fakes are test-only and are replaced by the real services in SIT; a drift is a build failure of the story that owns the fake.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 provided, 4 consumed | The submission and the list on `/api/recovery/partner/v1`; the intake creation and the item read of rwb-document; the parameters and reference-data reads behind the client library |
| Kafka | 1 published, 1 consumed | `rwb.partner.PartnerDocumentSubmitted.v1` keyed on the case ID; `rwb.document.DocumentAttached.v1` in; the record library's `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03) |
| Temporal | 2 workflows, 2 activities, 1 Schedule | `PartnerInstructionWorkflow` signal and `PartnerIntakeReconcileWorkflow` with their activities on `rwb-partner`; the 15-minute Schedule |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.partner`, module `intake`; front end `src/modules/recovery/partner/InstructionDocuments.tsx`, the fragment SCR-35 embeds, read only.

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-01 moves the partner-side intake row into `rwb_partner` and stops this service reaching into the document schema. DP-03 is the transaction the story is built on: the row, the record and the outbox row commit together or not at all. DP-05 is applied by removal: the legacy matcher read `v_ace_account` through the case directory, and here the case is the instruction's `case_id` and no account is read. DP-06 and DP-07 keep the intake bound and the two lists out of the code through the client library. DP-09 writes the fact in the outbox and discards a duplicate through the inbox. DP-10 turns the legacy JOB-12 step into a Schedule in the same cadence. DP-11 is the document-hub call and read: one hop, a published shape and a 2 s timeout. DP-15 puts the migration in the service's own sequence, and DP-19 puts SCR-35 behind the composite route. The six platform CON rows the DP table names are the shared baseline of wave 0 and add no row to this plan's H list, which the work package fixes empty (GAP-3140; ASM-5506).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `PartnerDocumentController` | REST controller | The two operations, the multipart parse, the RFC 9457 mapping (BR1, BR4, BR7) |
| `PartnerDocumentService` | Service | Firm scope, state check, validation, the case hint, the version in force, the record assembly (BR2, BR4, BR8) |
| `PartnerIntakeRepository` | Repository | Reads and writes `partner_intake`; reads `partner`, `partner_user`, `partner_instruction` in `rwb_partner` only |
| `DecisionRecordAdapter` | Library adapter | Calls `DecisionRecordWriter.record` with the code and the version (DP-03, BR5) |
| `SubmissionOutboxWriter` | Library adapter | Writes the outbox row in the transaction (DP-09) |
| `DocumentHubClient` | Client | The intake creation and the item read, one hop, 2 s budget, breaker (DP-11) |
| `AttachEventConsumer` | Consumer | Matches the attach event to the submission, sets `MATCHED`, signals the workflow, discards a duplicate |
| `ReconcileActivity` | Temporal activity | Copies the state of the open submissions and retries a failed intake call |
| `InstructionDocuments` | React component | The submission list of SCR-35, read only |

**Database.** One migration in the per-service Flyway sequence (DP-15), `V1032_1__partner_intake.sql` (the version number is this story's choice): `partner_intake` with `partner_id`, `instruction_id`, `case_id`, `document_type`, `file_sha256`, `intake_item_id`, `state`, `candidate_case_ids` jsonb, `received_at`, the standard audit columns and `version`; unique key `uk_partner_intake_instr_hash` on (`instruction_id`, `file_sha256`) for BR7; index `ix_partner_intake_open` on (`state`, `received_at`) where `state = 'PENDING'` for the reconcile run.

**Configuration and reference data.** The intake bound and the two lists read at their version through DP-06 and DP-07; no list value and no bound is typed in code. The decision code of the acceptance is a reference value in force whose name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3142; ASM-5508). No feature flag of its own: `rwb.dochub.autoattach` belongs to the document-hub slice and the partner column keeps the partner portal as documented.

**Build steps.** (1) The migration, the entity and the write key; test BR7 and the stale `version`. (2) The two operations behind the contract fake; test AC1 and AC5. (3) The record adapter and the rollback; test AC6 (X3). (4) The outbox row and the event fixture; test AC1 and AC4. (5) The consumer, the inbox row and the signal; test AC2. (6) The reconcile Schedule and its activity against the item-read fake; test AC3 (X4, X6). (7) The screen fragment and the boundary, stale-data and no-PII tests; test AC7 and section 17. **Done when** the tests of section 16 pass, one accepted file writes one row, one record and one event, one attach outcome closes one submission, a held file is copied and never attached here, and SCR-35 shows the state through the composite route in SIT.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required element is missing or refused on submission (X2, AC5) | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The identity has no Partner portal C on the submission or R on the read | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The record cannot be written and the submission is not accepted (AC6, X3) | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The intake creation or the item read misses the budget, or its breaker is open (X4) | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P5-003 | The submission is held for a person in the document hub (AC3) | Some fields need checking. The document is in the review queue. |
| Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3141; ASM-5507) | The instruction is closed (409) or belongs to another firm (404) (X1) | The 409 and 404 bodies carry no message ID in any source |

The five IDs and their texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story and the FSD; this story adds no message. Status mapping: 403 MSG-P4-002, 404 and 409 for a closed or foreign instruction, 415 for a wrong body type, 422 MSG-GEN-001, 503 MSG-GEN-006 or MSG-P7-003. Thai text follows DL10.

| SCR-35 Placement and allocation | Attached | State `MATCHED` with the document ID; the case owner opens the document on SCR-30 of rwb-document |

Both reads come through the composite route, which composes the case read of rwb-case with the submission read of this service, one hop each (DP-19). ##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the states, the types, the intake bound, the decision code and the version are read at their version; a build check fails on a list member in source or configuration (BR4).
- No personal data and no document content in the row, the record, the event, logs or spans: identifiers, codes, a hash and dates only (BR9).
- No read of another service's tables and no cross-schema join: `document`, `document_intake` (P5), `recovery_case` (P3), `decision_log_entry`, `rule_row` (P7) and `interaction` (P1) are reached only through their owners.
- The record is written in the same transaction as the acceptance, and a failed write leaves no row, no event and makes no call (AC6, X3).
- One submission per instruction and file hash, and one event per submission: the unique key and the `Idempotency-Key` carry the rule (BR7, AC4).
- The file is hashed and handed over; this service stores no file, runs no OCR and writes no document row.
- No ACE view and no ACE grant in this service: the case arrives from the instruction (DP-05).
- An applied migration is never edited: `partner_intake` is a new version of the service's own sequence.
- The portal is reached only through the partner gateway with multi-factor authentication, and a scope filter applies to every query (NFR-050).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-032 for rwb-case; the document hub keeps the intake, classification and store work in RWB-P5-E1032-APP. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)** and the **rwb-case service**, I want **the case-directory answers the document matcher calls (a case by its case number, the open cases of an ACE account number) and, when rwb-document publishes that a document was stored, one case document link on the right case with its timeline entry, its decision record and one review task when the document is held for review**, so that **a classified document lands on the right case without a person and no document lands on a wrong case**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Scans, partner files and emails arrive without a case link; today a person reads each one and files it. The legacy story matched each classified intake item to one open case by the case ID or the account number in its text and stored it on that case with no person involved (FSD P5 A2.12), and wrote the document attached record required from Epic 1 (REQ-DRI-004, RWB-E1-027). An item that matched no case, more than one case, a closed case or no agreed type was held for a person.

This story is one half of that legacy story. The intake (`POST /documents`), the OCR, the classification and extraction, the matching decision itself and the store stay in the document hub, rwb-document (P5), in RWB-P5-E1032-APP. rwb-case owns only what belongs to the case: the case identity that the matcher asks for, the case-side link to the stored document, the timeline record on the case, the review task when a document is held for review, and the decision record of that link (DP-03). rwb-case reads no document table and rwb-document reads no case table (DP-01); the only cross-service paths are one-hop REST with a 2 s timeout (DP-11) and the events `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` (EV-16) and `rwb.document.DocumentFieldsExtracted.v1` (EV-17) on the document hub's topic (DP-09).

The split keeps the case the system of record for its own documents list: SCR-30 Case documents and the case timeline read one owner, and a document stored for a case that rwb-case does not hold is never silently attached.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P5-E1032-CON is published: the document metadata, intake-item and review-item resources, the `rwb.document.events.v1` schemas for DocumentStored (EV-16) and DocumentFieldsExtracted (EV-17) with the CloudEvents envelope, the error envelope, the Idempotency-Key rule and the contract fakes.
- Build dependencies: none. The story has no same-service story to wait for and no H dependency; it builds Day 1 against the published P5 contract and its fake.
- RWB-P3-E1042-CON is published: the parameters contract of rwb-case with the client library (DP-06). RWB-P3-E1043-CON is published: the reference-data contract of rwb-case (DP-07), holding LOV-CASE-STATUS, LOV-TASK-STATUS and the task codes.
- The platform libraries are consumed as published interfaces and are not build dependencies of this story: the outbox and inbox library (RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, DP-09), the Temporal workflow kit in namespace `rwb-recovery` (RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, DP-10), the per-service Flyway sequence (RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, DP-15) and the local decision-record library with the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the gateway-bff composite route that serves SCR-30, SCR-03 and SCR-04 (DP-19).
- The rwb_case tables `recovery_case`, `case_account`, `task` and the case interaction projection exist before this story runs its own migration.
- The rwb-case login (DP-02) is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0748; ASM-1369).

##### 4. Flow

1. rwb-document (P5): the DocumentIntakeWorkflow classifies a stored intake item and the matcher needs the case. It calls the rwb-case case-directory answers, one hop with a 2 s timeout (DP-11).
2. rwb-case: `CaseLookupService` answers by case number on `GET /cases?caseNo=...` with the case id, the case number and the status, and the outcome MATCHED, or NO_MATCH when no case holds that number.
3. rwb-case: for an account number the matcher passes the ACE account number. `AccountKeyResolver` calls the rwb-source-data contract once for the `account_key` of that account number (DP-05), then reads `case_account` in schema `rwb_case` for the open cases on that key.
4. rwb-case: the answer carries the outcome MATCHED, NO_MATCH, MULTIPLE or CASE_CLOSED with the candidates as case id, case number and status. rwb-case never chooses among candidates and never resolves a doubt.
5. rwb-document (P5): the matcher stores the document on the case it chose and publishes DocumentStored (EV-16) to its outbox in the same transaction as its own rows (DP-09).
6. rwb-case: the case router consumes EV-16 from `rwb.document.events.v1` through its inbox (one action per event id) and calls `signalWithStart` on CaseWorkflow with the workflow ID equal to the case ID, on task queue `rwb-case`.
7. rwb-case: the `LinkDocument` activity writes one `case_document_link` row for the case and the document with the checklist state LINKED, and one timeline entry of type DOCUMENT in the case interaction projection.
8. rwb-case: when the event carries a `review_status` of PENDING, `ReviewTaskRaiser` raises exactly one case review task in the review queue, status OPEN, owned by the case role.
9. rwb-case: the `RecordAndApply` activity writes the decision record (DP-03) and the outbox row in the same transaction as the link and the timeline entry; a failed write rolls the link back, so no partial record exists.
10. rwb-document (P5): when the extracted fields are ready it publishes DocumentFieldsExtracted (EV-17). rwb-case updates the extracted field count on the same link; it never creates a second link.
11. rwb-case: the daily reconcile Schedule (DP-10) compares the documents that rwb-document holds for a case with the links in `rwb_case` and writes the links that a timeout left uncreated.
12. rwb-case: the review queue entry raised in step 8 is worked in RWB-P3-E1054-APP; the reviewer confirms or corrects the document type and the link moves to CONFIRMED or CORRECTED.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | No case holds the case number, or no open case is on the account | The answer carries NO_MATCH and no candidate; rwb-case writes nothing; the matcher holds the item for a person | MSG-P5-003 | AC1, AC2 |
| X2 | The account number carries two or more open cases | The answer carries MULTIPLE with every candidate as case id, case number and status; rwb-case chooses neither and writes no link | MSG-P5-003 | AC3 |
| X3 | The only case on the account is closed | The answer carries CASE_CLOSED with that case and its status; rwb-case writes no link | MSG-P5-003 | AC4 |
| X4 | rwb-source-data does not answer inside the REST budget | One hop, 2 s timeout (DP-11); the answer is 503 and no candidate is invented; the caller holds the item and calls again | MSG-P1-001 | AC2 |
| X5 | The document metadata read times out, or the decision record write fails | Nothing is written: no link, no timeline entry and no decision record; the event is retried, so no partial record exists | MSG-P7-003 | AC5, TC-E1-032-17 |
| X6 | The same event id is delivered again, or two deliveries run at once | The inbox drops the duplicate and the unique key on the link keeps one row; nothing changes | None | AC6 |
| X7 | An event names a case that rwb-case does not hold | No link, no timeline entry and no decision record; the event is retried and then parked for the operations team | None | AC8 |
| X8 | The case is outside the reader's scope | The read is refused with 404 and MSG-P4-003; no document link shows | MSG-P4-003 | AC8 |
| X9 | A role without Case record R calls a case-directory answer | The call is refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002; no case and no document link are returned | MSG-P4-002 | AC9 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds Day 1 against the RWB-P5-E1032-CON contract fake and the rwb-source-data fake; it has no same-service story to wait for |
| Negotiable | The switch, the review task code and the link field names are data or contract values; the outcomes and the one-link rule are fixed |
| Valuable | Puts every OCR-read document on the right case with no person, and gives every document held for review one task on the case |
| Estimable | One controller with three reads, two event handlers, one workflow with three activities, one Schedule and one migration |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Every criterion in section 7 has a test case in section 16; every cross-service answer is stubbed in a contract fake |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin

    Given case "RW-2026-000123" is open, owned by "U-CO-01" and linked to account key "A-5001"
    Given case "RW-2026-000456" is open and linked to account key "A-5002"

  Scenario: AC3 Two open cases on one account (new, D-RCV-60)

    When the matcher calls GET /cases?accountNo=TEST-ACC-0003

  Scenario: AC4 A closed case only (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rwb-source-data contract mock returns account_key "A-5009" for the ACE account number "TEST-ACC-0009"
    When the matcher calls GET /cases?accountNo=TEST-ACC-0009
    Then the answer holds case "RW-2026-000789" with its closed status and the outcome is CASE_CLOSED

  Scenario: AC5 DocumentStored links the document once (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rwb-document contract mock raises rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1 (EV-16) with event id "EVT-0001", document "DOC-0001", case "RW-2026-000123" and review_status "NOT_NEEDED"
    When rwb-case consumes the event

  Scenario: AC6 A repeated event and a later field extraction change no rows twice (new, D-RCV-60)

    When a further EV-17 arrives for document "DOC-0001" with extracted field count 5

    When rwb-case consumes the event
```
