
These nine criteria are new for the `rwb-decision` slice of RWB-E1-032 and are the record and read criteria of the key. `acs` is empty for this story: no legacy criterion is owned verbatim here, because every legacy criterion of the key matches, stores, holds or refuses a document, and those changes belong to RWB-P5-E1032-APP, RWB-P4-E1032-APP and RWB-P3-E1032-APP. The values are the legacy values of RWB-E1-032 — cases `RW-2026-000123`, `RW-2026-000456`, `RW-2026-000789`, `RW-2026-000321`, `RW-2026-000654`, accounts `TEST-ACC-0001`, `TEST-ACC-0002`, `TEST-ACC-0003`, classifier version `CLS-1.0`, confidences 0.93, 0.88 and 0.62, threshold 0.80, reviewer `TEST-LIT-01` with role `RW-LITOFF`, item version 3, the 15 `MATCHED` items, the types `COURT_NOTICE`, `DEMAND_LETTER`, `APPRAISAL_REPORT`, `TITLE_DEED`, `GUARANTOR_NOTICE` and `PAYSLIP`, and the messages MSG-P7-003, MSG-P7-009, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003, MSG-P5-003, MSG-P5-006 and MSG-GEN-004 — and no new business value is introduced.

The decision code `DOCATT` and the match methods `CASE_ID`, `ACCOUNT_NO` and `PERSON` are the legacy values; whether the code list in force carries `DOCATT` has no source and is carried in GAP-2445 with ASM-4053. The final call `ATTACHED`, the payload field set of the fact and of the entry, the read shape, the parameter names and the login name have no source and are carried in GAP-2444, GAP-2447 and GAP-2449 with ASM-4052, ASM-4055 and ASM-4057.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every document the OCR intake attaches, automatically or by a reviewer, leaves exactly one decision record; no attach stands without it | Legacy BR1 and BR5; R-UNI-39; FSD P7 v3 A2.2; FEAT-DRI-02 |
| BR2 | The record is written on the decision-record path of DP-03: it is appended to the chain, it names the rule and the rule version in force, and the entry, its chain position and its outbox row commit together or not at all | FSD P7 v3 A2.1 and A2.3; TSD P7 v2 T5.3; DP-03 |
| BR3 | The entry names the case, the decision code `DOCATT`, the document reference, the intake item, the classifier model version, the confidence, the match method, the approver where a person decided, the inputs reference, the final call and the decided time | Legacy AC1, AC10 and AC12; TSD P7 v2 T3.1; ASM-4052 and ASM-4055 |
| BR4 | A record that cannot be written refuses the attach: the library raises `DecisionLogUnavailableException`, the store's transaction rolls back, the automatic item stays `PENDING`, the manual attach answers MSG-P7-003 and an incident is raised | Legacy X13 and TC-E1-032-17; FSD P7 v3 VR-P7-001-2 and AC-EXC-P7-002-02; principle 5 |
| BR5 | The entry is append only and hash chained: an UPDATE and a DELETE are refused, a correction is a new entry naming the one it corrects in `corrects_entry_id`, and every `entry_hash` is the SHA-256 of the entry's canonical form | FEAT-DRI-01; FSD P7 v3 AC-P7-001-01 and AC-ALT-P7-001-01; NFR-035 |
| BR6 | An item that is held as no match, multiple, conflict, a closed case or no agreed type, and an attach refused for its type, its scope or its version, leaves no record, because no document was stored and no attach decision was taken | Legacy BR3 and section 9; the reading is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2446; ASM-4054) |
| BR7 | The service applies no match rule: the patterns, the threshold, the outcomes and the store's review rule are `rwb-document`'s, and the entry copies their outcome | Legacy BR2 and BR4; FSD P4 v3 A2.4; DP-01 |
| BR8 | One entry per stored document under a repeated fact, a repeated file or two reviewers: the inbox dedupe, the idempotency key and the partial unique key on the document reference make a second entry impossible, and the repeat is counted | Legacy BR6, AC8 and AC9; R-UNI-40; FEAT-DRI-02 |
| BR9 | The record is written before the document stands, in one transaction with its chain position and its outbox row; a failed append leaves nothing and the fact is redelivered | Legacy BR5; R-UNI-39; DP-03 |
| BR10 | The story records and exposes; it writes no document, no intake item, no review item and no case status, and it reads no table of another service | Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41; DP-01 |
| BR11 | The two reads declare the `DECISION_LOG` capability area and the right `R` with the scope applied; a role without the right is refused with MSG-P4-002 and a case out of scope with MSG-P4-003 | TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 and T6.1; legacy section 10 and AC13 |
| BR12 | The ledger is reconciled: the documents of a case are compared with the `DOCATT` entries of the case inside the ingest window, and a document with no entry is reported as a gap and alerted; no entry is invented for it | Architecture v5 slide 28; NFR-035; ASM-4058 |

Target-service statements that make the rules hold in `rwb_decision`:

- BR1 and BR2 are one append on the `DecisionRecorded` fact of the owning service through the library of DP-03; the store's transaction is `rwb-document`'s and this story supplies the path, its fail-closed contract and its exception.
- BR3 is the entry composition: the columns of TSD P7 v2 T3.1 plus the document reference, the intake item, the match method and the confidence of the assumed shape of ASM-4055; `model_version` carries the classifier version and `recommendation` carries the type candidates.
- BR4 is the exception mapping: `DecisionLogUnavailableException` becomes MSG-P7-003 for the attach and an incident for the platform administrator queue.
- BR5 is the table's trigger `tr_declog_append_only` and the missing `UPDATE` and `DELETE` grant on the service login, inherited from the decision-log baseline of RWB-P7-E1008-APP.
- BR6 is the absence: the listener has no path that writes an entry without a stored document reference, and a fact with no document reference is refused as X6.
- BR8 is the partial unique key on the document reference and the inbox dedupe by event ID and idempotency key.
- BR11 is the guard inherited from the decision-log baseline's authorise path; the Java code holds no role, no scope and no delegation row.
- BR12 is the checker of flow step 10: one read of the document contract per case per window, one comparison, one gap alert.

##### 9. State transitions

None for a document, an intake item, a review item, a task or a case; the intake item's `match_status` moves PENDING to MATCHED, or to a held value, in `rwb-document` and under RWB-P5-E1032-APP (legacy section 9). The states below are the states of an entry of this story, and an entry has no state column of its own: it is appended and then immutable.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Absent | A `DecisionRecorded` attach fact arrives with a document reference | The decision code, the rule version and the match method are readable at the version in force | Appended, with the next `chain_seq`, its `prev_hash` and its `entry_hash`, in one transaction with its outbox row |
| Absent | A `DecisionRecorded` attach fact arrives | The decision code is unknown, or the match method or the document reference is absent | Absent: refused with MSG-P7-009 or MSG-GEN-006, and nothing is written |
| Absent | A `DecisionRecorded` attach fact arrives | The library is unavailable or the chain cannot be taken | Absent: the attach is refused with MSG-P7-003, nothing is stored, and the fact stays for redelivery |
| Absent | No attach fact arrives, because the item is held or the attach was refused | The store wrote no document | Absent: no entry and no chain position (BR6) |
| Appended | The same fact arrives again with the same idempotency key | The inbox or the idempotency key holds the entry | Unchanged: the first entry's ID is returned and the repeat is counted |
| Appended | A correction of the record is taken | The correction names the entry it corrects | A new entry is appended with `corrects_entry_id`, and the corrected entry stays unchanged |
| Appended | An UPDATE or a DELETE is attempted | Any caller, including the schema owner | Unchanged: the statement is refused by the append-only rule |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| SY-OCR, the OCR and extraction pipeline | Its attach is recorded: the entry names it as the actor of an automatic attach |
| SY-DECLOG, the decision log writer | Appends the entry through the library; writes no document |
| RW-LITOFF and RW-CASEOWN, reviewers with Documents `C` | Their attach is recorded with them as approver and the match method `PERSON`; they read the entries of the cases in their scope |
| RW-LEGAL, role with scope `ALL` | Reads the entries of any case, including the items that no candidate named |
| RW-AUDIT and RW-COMPLY | Read the `DOCATT` entries of a case and one entry with its versions and its chain position (`DECISION_LOG` R) |
| RW-TEAMMGR and the other roles of TSD P7 v2 T6.1 | Hold `R` on the decision log and read the entries of the cases in their scope; no attach |
| A role holding Documents R only, or a role outside the matrix | Refused with MSG-P4-002; a case out of scope is refused with MSG-P4-003 |
| The `rwb-decision` service identity | Consumes the fact, reads its own `rwb_decision` rows, and appends the entry and its outbox row (DP-02) |
| `rwb-document` | Owns the match, the store, the review queue and the reviewer's `resolve`; this story holds no authority over any of them |
| `rwb-access` | Owns the Documents right, the scope answer and the masking; this story consumes the answer for its reads |
| `rwb-case` | Owns the case, the open cases of an account and the reference and parameter rows this story reads through DP-06 and DP-07 |
| No approval level from the delegation of authority applies to an automatic attach | It is a system decision and carries no approver; a reviewer's attach names the reviewer and no level, and whether a level is recorded is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2444; ASM-4052) |

The authorisation decision behind the two reads is `rwb-access`'s role, scope and right data, taken through the authorise contract of DP-11 and the guard the decision-log baseline already carries; this story adds no guard of its own. The database login is per service (DP-02) and its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2449; ASM-4057).

| (reference lists) | reference data (P3) | the decision code list with `DOCATT` and the approval level list, at the version in force | Read through the reference-data contract of DP-07, never a table |
| (parameters) | `parameter_value` (P3) | the ledger ingest target and the chain-check time, at the version in force | Read through the parameters contract of DP-06, never a table |
| (inbox) | `processed_event` | event_id, consumer, processed_at | Write |
| (outbox) | outbox library table in `rwb_decision` | the append row | Write |

No row of `document`, `document_intake`, `document_text`, `document_type`, `document_hub_parameter`, `recovery_case`, `case_account`, `role`, `permission` or `masking_rule` is copied into `rwb_decision`: the attach facts arrive on the document contract and on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and no other service's table is queried (DP-01). Field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8; the document reference, the intake item, the match method, the confidence and the message id have no field ID in TSD P7 v2 T3.1 and are written from the assumed shape of section 12.1.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner `rwb-decision` (P7); base `/api/recovery/decision/v1`. Both paths are the ones TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 carries (API-P7-006 and API-P7-007); this story fills them with the `DOCATT` entries of an attach and adds no third path. The request and response field set of an attach entry is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2444; ASM-4052).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/decision-log` | API-P7-006: search the decision log by `caseId`, `decision`, `ruleId`, `approver`, `from`, `to`, `page` and `size`, and by the document or intake item reference of an attach; 200 with the DecisionLogPage | `DECISION_LOG`, right `R`, scope applied through the authorise contract | Not applicable, read only |
| GET | `/decision-log/{entryId}` | API-P7-007: read one entry with its inputs reference, its versions, its document reference, its match method, its final call and its hash chain; 200 with the DecisionLogEntry | `DECISION_LOG`, right `R`, scope applied | Not applicable, read only |

The `DecisionLogEntry` body carries `entryId`, `chainSeq`, `caseId`, `decisionCode`, `ruleId`, `ruleVersion`, `modelVersion`, `agentVersion`, `inputsRef`, `recommendation`, `approverUserId`, `approvalLevel`, `finalCall`, `objectRef`, `intakeItemId`, `matchMethod`, `confidence`, `messageId`, `decidedAt`, `prevHash`, `entryHash`, `correctsEntryId` and `actorUserId`. The `DecisionLogPage` body carries `items`, `page`, `size` and `total`.

Errors: 401 no session; 403 the role lacks the right (MSG-P4-002) or the case is out of scope (MSG-P4-003); 404 the entry is absent; 422 a query value is outside its list (MSG-GEN-001); 503 the log is unavailable (MSG-GEN-006) or the append could not be made (MSG-P7-003). Every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents` | P5 rwb-document, on RWB-P5-E1032-CON | The documents a case holds with their type and review state, for the completeness check of the ledger (BR12, X9); faked, one hop and 2 s (DP-11) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access, on RWB-P4-E1037-CON | The role, scope and right decision behind the two reads: area `DECISION_LOG`, right `R` (BR11); faked. The contract is added by the DP table and is not in the metadata rows (GAP-2448; ASM-4056) |

The reference lists and the parameters of `rwb-case` (DP-07, RWB-P3-E1043-CON; DP-06, RWB-P3-E1042-CON) are read in process through their client libraries with their fakes and are not cross-service REST rows; the attach facts arrive on `rwb.decision-record.v1` and not over REST.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. This story publishes no event of its own: the attach fact is `rwb-document`'s and the entries of the central ledger are read through the operations of 12.1. `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` is published by the owning service of each decision, and `rwb-decision` is its consumer. The `ApprovalRequested`, `ApprovalDecided` and the rule-registry events of `rwb.decision.events.v1` belong to the approval and rule stories of this service and are not touched here.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Handler |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 ledger library, published by `rwb-document` for this key | `IntakeAttachDecisionListener`: inbox dedupe by event ID, then `IntakeAttachDecisionRecorder` and `DecisionLogAppender` for the case, the document reference, the intake item, the match method, the classifier version, the confidence, the approver, the final call and the message id |

The fact carries IDs, codes, versions, a confidence, a message id and a time only; no OCR text, no file and no account number travels on the topic (AC9, section 17). Which fields of the fact this service requires, and whether the document reference travels on the fact or is read through the document contract, is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2447; ASM-4055).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None of this story's own. The append is a transactional write on the consumer path and not a workflow step: the handler is a Kafka consumer with the inbox of DP-09, and the store's `matchStep` and `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` on queue `rwb-document` are `rwb-document`'s (RWB-P5-E1032-CON section 12.5). This story registers no workflow and no activity on the `rwb-decision` queue and adds none to the workflow kit of DP-10.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The intake of a scan is JOB-12's, every 15 minutes in business hours, and after DP-10 it is a Temporal Schedule of `rwb-document`; this story neither owns that Schedule nor creates one. The daily hash-chain check JOB-14 at 02:00 is the decision-log baseline of this service and covers the entries of this story like any other. Whether the completeness check of flow step 10 runs on its own timer or on the ingest window is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2450; ASM-4058); the reading applied is that of ASM-4058 and it creates no Schedule.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|
| `decision_log_entry` | P7 (`rwb_decision`) | The attach entry, its document and intake item references, its versions, its chain position, its hashes and its final call; append only |
| decision record (local library) | P7 rows in `rwb_decision`, written through the decision-record library | The append of DP-03 and its hash chain |
| `outbox_event`, `processed_event`, `idempotency_key` | PLT library, created in `rwb_decision` | Outbox, inbox and idempotency objects (DP-09) |

Not owned and never read: `document`, `document_intake`, `document_text`, `document_type` and `document_hub_parameter` (P5), `recovery_case`, `case_account`, `task`, `timer` and `parameter_value` (P3), and `role`, `permission` and `masking_rule` (P4). The other P7 tables — `approval`, `rule_package`, `rule_package_version`, `rule_row` and `rule_test_case` — are not touched by this story. No foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01).

Each fake is replaced by the real service as RWB-P5-E1032-APP, RWB-P4-E1032-APP and RWB-P3-E1032-APP land, without a change to the scenarios.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count in this story | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | Provided 2, consumed 2 | `GET /decision-log` and `GET /decision-log/{entryId}` provided; the document list and the authorise decision consumed, one hop and 2 s with a breaker per downstream |
| Kafka | Published 0, consumed 1 | `rwb.decision-record.v1` consumed; no event published and no new topic |
| Temporal | None | No workflow, no activity and no Schedule; the intake Schedule and the intake workflow are `rwb-document`'s |
| File | None | No file input and no file output; a scan never leaves `rwb-document` |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision`, module `log/intakeattach`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision.intakeattach`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

Which patterns have an instance in this slice: DP-01 is the boundary — the entry lives in `rwb_decision` and the attach facts arrive on the document contract and on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, never as a read of `rwb_document`; DP-03 is the append path with its chain, its append-only rule and its fail-closed exception; DP-05 is applied by removal — the legacy `CaseDirectory` read of `v_ace_account` is gone, and the case and the account number arrive as facts on the fact and on the document contract; DP-06 is the ingest target and the chain-check time read as parameters; DP-07 is the decision code list and the approval level list read as reference data; DP-09 is the outbox, the inbox and the idempotency key; DP-10 is named because the intake trigger becomes a Temporal Schedule of `rwb-document` and this slice is event-started, holding no workflow of its own; DP-11 is the document read of the completeness checker and the authorise decision behind the reads, each with a mock and a 2 s timeout; DP-15 is the one migration; DP-19 is the composite route the reads are reached through, not built here.

The platform H dependencies in the table — H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and H RWB-PLT-N001-CON — and the C dependencies of the published contracts of other services — C RWB-P3-E1042-CON, C RWB-P3-E1043-CON and the authorise contract RWB-P4-E1037-CON that DP-11 consumes — are not in the metadata rows of this story, which name `Depends on (build)` = None and `Contract dependencies` = RWB-P5-E1032-CON. They are the dependencies the DP table adds and they are recorded in GAP-2448 and ASM-4056. None of them blocks the build beyond Day 1: they are platform contracts of waves 0 and 1 and published contracts of `rwb-case`, `rwb-access` and `rwb-document`, built against their fakes.

The work of the legacy key that sits with other slices: the `matchStep` of JOB-12, the `CaseMatcher` with its five outcomes, the store and the duplicate check on the file hash, the `review_status` and `write_once` rule, the `rwb-docs` container, the four intake operations, the `resolve` of a reviewer, the `DocumentAttached` event and the SCR-31 Unmatched list are `rwb-document`'s (RWB-P5-E1032-APP, RWB-P5-E1032-CON). The Documents right, the scope answer and the masking are `rwb-access`'s (RWB-P4-E1032-APP). The case, the open cases of an account number, the reference lists and the parameters are `rwb-case`'s (RWB-P3-E1032-APP). This story builds the record of the attach and nothing beside it.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| IntakeAttachDecisionListener | Kafka consumer with the inbox | Reads `DecisionRecorded` for an attach, deduplicates by event ID and idempotency key, and hands the decision facts to the recorder |
| IntakeAttachDecisionRecorder | Service | Composes the entry from the attach facts, reads the decision code list and the ledger parameters at the version in force, and decides nothing about the match (BR3, BR7) |
| DecisionLogAppender | Service | Takes the next `chain_seq`, computes `prev_hash` and `entry_hash`, and writes the entry and its outbox row in one transaction (DP-03, BR2, BR9) |
| DecisionRecordFailClosedHandler | Service | Maps the library's `DecisionLogUnavailableException` to MSG-P7-003 for the attach and to an incident, so the store's transaction rolls back and nothing is stored (BR4) |
| IntakeAttachCompletenessChecker | Service | Compares the documents of a case from the document contract with the `DOCATT` entries of the case inside the ingest window and reports a document with no entry as a gap (BR12) |
| DecisionLogQueryController | Controller | `GET /decision-log` and `GET /decision-log/{entryId}` with the declared area and right, the scope, the paging and the problem mapping for 401, 403, 404, 422 and 503 |
| DecisionLogRepository | Repository | `decision_log_entry` in `rwb_decision`, with the append-only rule, the chain columns, the document reference and the idempotency key |
| DocumentFactClient | Adapter | The document list of RWB-P5-E1032-CON for the completeness check, one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker |
| AccessCheckClient | Client | The cached authorise decision behind the two reads (DP-11) |
| ReferenceAndParameterClient | Client | The decision code list, the approval level list, the ingest target and the chain-check time at the version in force (DP-06, DP-07) |

**Database and migrations**

- Writes `decision_log_entry`, the local decision record of the append and the library objects, all in schema `rwb_decision`; reads no other schema (DP-01).
- Migration in this story, in the per-service Flyway sequence of `rwb_decision`: `V1032_1__decision_intake_attach_entry.sql` adds the attach columns of section 11 that the decision-log store baseline does not hold — the document reference, the intake item, the match method, the confidence and the message id — plus the partial unique key `ux_declog_intake_attach ON decision_log_entry (object_ref) WHERE decision_code = 'DOCATT' AND object_ref IS NOT NULL`, so one entry per stored document is a constraint and not only a check (BR8), and the search index for the case-and-decision read of 12.1. The column names and types are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2444; ASM-4052).
- The append-only rule is the table's, with the trigger `tr_declog_append_only` that refuses an UPDATE and a DELETE from the schema owner and the missing grant for the service login, as FSD P7 v3 AC-P7-001-01 fixes it.
- No row of `document`, `document_intake`, `document_type` or `parameter_value` is written here: the document hub's tables and the case's parameters are their owners'.

**Configuration and reference data**

- The decision code list with `DOCATT` and the approval level list are reference data of `rwb-case` read through DP-07 at the version in force; the value `DOCATT` and the final call `ATTACHED` are the reading of ASM-4052 and ASM-4053 and are held as reference rows, not as constants (GAP-2444; GAP-2445).
- The ledger ingest target of 5 minutes and the daily chain-check time of 02:00 are parameter rows of `rwb-case` read through DP-06 with the version in force; the parameter names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2449; ASM-4057).
- The match parameters `CASE_NO_PATTERN`, `ACCOUNT_NO_PATTERN` and `CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD` are the store's rows; this story reads none of them (BR7).
- The outbox retry policy, the inbox retention and the chain-check alert route are the platform's (RWB-PLT-TE006-CON).

**Build steps**

1. `DecisionLogRepository` and the migration, with the partial unique key on the document reference and the append-only trigger; test that a second entry for the same document and an UPDATE are both refused (AC4, AC8).
2. `IntakeAttachDecisionListener` with the inbox and the dedupe by event ID and idempotency key; test the replay of the same fact (AC4).
3. `IntakeAttachDecisionRecorder` and `ReferenceAndParameterClient`: the entry composed from the attach facts with the versions in force, and the refusal of an unknown decision code and of a rule id with no version (X5; AC1 to AC3).
4. `DecisionLogAppender` and the chain: `chain_seq`, `prev_hash`, `entry_hash` over the canonical form, the first `prev_hash` of 64 zeros, and the one-transaction append (AC1, AC8).
5. `DecisionRecordFailClosedHandler`: the `DecisionLogUnavailableException` path to MSG-P7-003 with the store's rollback and the incident; test the three items of AC5 with the library fake forced to fail (AC5, TC-E1-032-17).
6. The absence path of AC6: a fact with no document reference, and a held item that produces no fact, leave no entry and no chain position.
7. `DecisionLogQueryController` with the two operations, the declared area and right, the scope, the paging and the problem mapping; tests for AC7 and the refusals of TC-E1-032-16.
8. `IntakeAttachCompletenessChecker` over the document list of a case, with the gap report of X9 and the ingest window of DP-06.
9. The contract-fake run of the whole slice: the document fake, the access fake, the reference-data and parameters fakes, the decision-record fake and the outbox fake, green from Day 1 (AC1 to AC9).
10. The boundary test: no write to `rwb_document`, `rwb_case` or `rwb_access`, and no OCR text, file or account number in any entry, fact, outbox row or log line (AC9).

**Feature switch.** None of its own, and the record path must have no off state: an attach that cannot be recorded must not be stored, so a switch that silenced the record would break BR4. The legacy flag `rwb.dochub.autoattach` stays `rwb-document`'s; with it off every classified item is held, no automatic attach fact arrives, and a reviewer's attach still leaves its record (GAP-2444; ASM-4052).

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the contract tests of RWB-P5-E1032-CON stay green, and a SIT day shows one `DOCATT` entry per attached document with its classifier version, its confidence, its match method and its approver where a person decided; no entry for a held item or a refused attach; a chain with no break and no entry changed or deleted; an attach refused with MSG-P7-003 when the record cannot be written; both reads answering by case and by entry; and not one document, intake item, review item or case status changed by this story.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Where it is produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-003 | The record of the attach cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | This story, on the fail-closed handler; the legacy text is copied unchanged |
| MSG-P7-009 | An entry has an unknown decision code, or a rule id with no version | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2444; ASM-4052) | This story, on the append, naming `decisionCode` or `ruleVersion` |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role holds no right in the `DECISION_LOG` area | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | This story, through the authorise answer of the read |
| MSG-P4-003 | The entry or the case is outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. | This story, through the authorise answer of the read |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A query value is outside its list, or a required field of the entry is absent | Enter {field}. | This story, on the read and on the append |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The log, the reference list or the parameters are unavailable, or the fact names no document | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2444; ASM-4052) | This story, on the read, on the retried fact and on the gap report |
| MSG-P5-003, MSG-P5-006, MSG-GEN-004 | An item is held, a type is not in force, or the item changed under a second reviewer | The legacy texts of RWB-E1-032 section 14 | `rwb-document`, on the item; this story records the message id only where the fact names one |

MSG-P7-003, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P4-003 are copied unchanged from the FSD P7 v3 message set and the platform messages the authorise contract carries; MSG-P5-003, MSG-P5-006 and MSG-GEN-004 are the legacy texts and are produced by `rwb-document`, not here. The texts of MSG-P7-009 and MSG-GEN-006 are named by the FSD P7 v3 exception flows but are not written out in a source this story may read, so the placeholders stand. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen is built in this story. The two reads are consumed by the decision-log view of a case and by the decision screen SCR-11 of this service, which are served through the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19 and are another story's; SCR-30 Case documents and SCR-31 Document review queue stay `rwb-document`'s, and the Unmatched list with its scan viewer, OCR text, candidates and pickers belongs to RWB-P5-E1032-APP.

| Where | State | What the reader sees |
|---|---|---|
| The decision-log read (P7) | List | The `DOCATT` entries of the case in chain order, with the document reference, the type, the classifier version, the confidence, the match method, the approver where one decided and the final call |
| The entry read | One entry | The same row with its inputs reference, its `decidedAt`, its `prevHash` and its `entryHash` |
| The entry read | An entry of a reviewer's attach | `matchMethod` `PERSON`, the reviewer as approver and the document reference |
| The read | A held item | No row: the hold is shown by the Unmatched list on SCR-31, not here |
| The read | 403 or 404 | MSG-P4-002 for a role without the right, MSG-P4-003 for a case out of scope, and the not-found answer for an absent entry; no row is returned |

The `-ITG` copies of these cases belong to RWB-ITG-E1032-ITG and are not written here.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the decision code, the final call, the match methods, the approval levels, the ingest target and the message ids are reference rows, parameter rows or facts of another service; nothing of them is a constant here.
- No personal data in the entry, the fact, the outbox, the tests or the logs: the case reference, the document reference, the intake item, the decision code, the classifier version, the confidence, the match method, the approver reference, the final call and dates only. OCR page text, file bytes and account numbers stay in `rwb_document`, and a test scans the entry, the fact and the log line for the account numbers of the scenarios.
- No read of another service's tables (DP-01): the attach facts arrive on the document contract and on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, the authorise answer on its contract, the reference lists and parameters in process; no `document`, `document_intake`, `document_text`, `recovery_case`, `case_account`, `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule` or `parameter_value` row is copied into `rwb_decision`.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `v_ace_*` views (DP-05): this story reads no ACE data at all, and the account number arrives as a fact of the intake.
- One recorder and no mover: this story changes no document, intake item, review item or case status, so a decision record can never move a case (BR10).
- No attach without its record and no record without a stored document: the entry, its chain position and its outbox row commit in one transaction, and a store transaction that cannot record its decision refuses the attach (BR4, BR9).
- Append only and hash chained: no UPDATE and no DELETE on `decision_log_entry`, and the chain is verifiable from `chain_seq` 1 (BR5).
- One entry per stored document: the partial unique key on the document reference, the inbox dedupe and the idempotency key make a second entry impossible (BR8).
- One base, one topic, one queue: `/api/recovery/decision/v1`, `rwb.decision.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1` with `rwb-decision` in namespace `rwb-recovery`; no story in this key declares another service's base or topic as its own.
- One hop and 2 s on every call with a breaker per downstream; a missing document fact, reference list or parameter never produces an entry from a guessed type, code or version (DP-11).
- The record path has no off switch, because an attach that cannot be recorded must not stand.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-032 for rwb-document. The legacy story assumed a Quartz job on a shared scheduler, a shared schema and a review queue an operator could open in the database; on the infrastructure side this story provisions the compute of the intake workers and the 15-minute Schedule they serve, the OCR text storage and its index, the hold container `rwb-quarantine`, the topic with its retry and `.dlt` topics and the least-privilege ACLs, the managed identity and secret layout, the private network path and the scanning capacity. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As an **infrastructure engineer**, I want **the intake-match path of `rwb-document` provisioned as infrastructure — the container and compute sizing of the workers that run `matchStep` for the 15-minute JOB-12 Schedule in business hours, the `document_text` storage and its index sized for the OCR estate, the hold container `rwb-quarantine` with its rule and its clearing, the topic `rwb.document.events.v1` with its three retry topics and its `.dlt` topic and the least-privilege ACLs of the consumers, the managed identity and the secret layout of the service, the private network path to `rwb-case`, `rwb-decision` and Blob, and the scanning capacity of the intake path**, so that **the matcher, the reviewer's queue and the store run on Day 1 against provisioned capacity with no secret in a values file, no public route to a dependency and no file left in a container whose rule nobody wrote down**.

The legacy story had one line for this work: "JOB-12 Document intake: runs matchStep after the extraction step" inside a shared Quartz scheduler, a shared recovery schema and a review queue opened from the same database. Under D-RCV-60 each of those three is gone. The scheduler is a Temporal Schedule on queue `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery` (DP-10, Arch v5 slide 44); the tables are `document_intake`, `document_text` and `document` in `rwb_document`, reached with the rwb-document login only (DP-01, DP-02); and the review queue is the service's own list operation behind the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). What is left for this story is capacity, storage, a container rule, a topic, ACLs, an identity, a route and the scan.

The path has one property that shapes the provisioning: the OCR text is the only personal-data-bearing artefact this service holds at scale. The text of a scanned notice sits in `document_text` until the document is attached or discarded, and the file sits in `rwb-quarantine` until the same moment. The provisioning therefore fixes three rules alongside the capacity: the text is never copied to a container or a topic, the hold container answers one claim-check read at a time through the storage product, and both are cleared by a stated rule rather than by an operator's memory.

##### 2. Business rationale

About 860,000 documents arrive in 2027 (NFR-004) and the hub holds about 5.8 million documents and 2.8 TB by the end of 2031, including every version and every held document (NFR-069). The intake path is the door every one of them comes through: a scan, a partner file or an email becomes a row in `document_intake`, a page set in `document_text`, and then a document on a case or an item in the review queue. If the compute is sized for a demonstration, the 15-minute run falls behind and the queue grows; if the text has no index budget, the matcher's pattern scan and the reviewer's page read slow to a crawl at the 500-page sample of the module; if the hold container has no rule, a held file stays in a container for years and a copy of a customer document outlives its case.

The private path matters as much. Zero trust requires the service to reach `rwb-case`, `rwb-decision`, the Kafka brokers, the Temporal frontend and Blob over private endpoints with a workload identity (Arch v5 slide 35; NFR-052, NFR-053). A public endpoint added for a test is a security finding that survives to production, and a connection string pasted into a values file turns a rotation into a rebuild.

The scanning capacity is the one new element the legacy story did not have in its own words: every inbound file is scanned before it is stored (FSD P5 A2.18; RWB-P5-E1041-APP), so the intake rate is bounded by the scan rate and not by the OCR or the matcher. This story provisions that capacity and states the rule that an item waits in the hold container rather than entering the matcher unscanned.

The 15-minute cadence is the legacy one and the architecture one: JOB-12 runs every 15 minutes, owned by `rwb-document` (Arch v5 slide 44; FSD P5 AC-BG-P5-012-01). The legacy story says "every 15 minutes in business hours"; the architecture slide gives no business-hours qualifier, so the Schedule and the compute are sized for the business-hours cadence and the difference is recorded as `ASM-1762`.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The platform subscription, the resource group and the network (virtual network, subnets, private DNS zones) of the environment are available, and the AKS cluster of the ACE platform is reachable from the `rwb-recovery` namespace.
- The workload identity of rwb-document is registered in each environment, so every access is bound to an identity and not to a shared credential (DP-02).
- RWB-PLT-N012-INF provisions the standard Blob account, the key store and the MFT/SFTP resources; this story consumes the Blob account and the key store for the three document containers.
- RWB-PLT-N002-INF provisions the 20 event topics with their 60 retry topics and their 20 dead-letter topics, so `rwb.document.events.v1`, its three retry topics and its `.dlt` topic exist before this story binds the ACLs.
- RWB-PLT-N003-INF provisions the namespace `rwb-recovery`, its certificates and the payload codec, so queue `rwb-document` can be polled.
- RWB-PLT-DB provisions the `rwb_document` schema and the rwb-document login; this story creates no schema, no table and no grant, and the migration is RWB-PLT-E1044-CON's sequence applied by the release of RWB-P5-E1032-OPS.
- The scanning product of RWB-P5-E1041-APP exists as a service call, so the capacity provisioned here is the cluster and network capacity around it and not a scanner binary.
- The baseline RWB-P5-E1032-CON is published, so the four operations of the app story and their status codes are known to the network and the identity work.
- No build dependency and no contract dependency in the plan of this key; this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).
- The release date 30 November 2026 is the legacy one and is tentative (ASM-1760), and the story carries Status Draft (realignment v1) because no approval of the realigned story is recorded (ASM-1761).

##### 4. Flow

1. List what the path needs: the worker compute for `matchStep`, the database storage and index for `document_text`, the three containers with their policies, the topic and its four derived topics, the six service principals it talks to, the four secret classes, the network routes and the scan rate.
2. Size the worker pool for the 15-minute business-hours cadence: the `matchStep` activity runs on queue `rwb-document`, the pool scales on the queue backlog through KEDA, and the request and limit set of the activity is fixed as values per environment.
3. Size the storage: `document_text` holds one row per page with its quality, `document_intake` holds the item, and both are measured against the 860,000 documents a year of NFR-004 and the 2.8 TB estate of NFR-069; the index budget is set for the matcher's pattern scan and the reviewer's page read.
4. Provision the container `rwb-quarantine` for held intake files with its access rule (managed identity only), its one-file-per-link claim-check read through the storage product and its clearing rule on attach, discard or age.
5. Bind the three containers `rwb-docs`, `rwb-docs-legal` and `rwb-quarantine` to the storage account, with `rwb-docs-legal` under the immutability policy the storage product owns; this story takes the policy as given and states that no blob is overwritten.
6. Verify the topic `rwb.document.events.v1` with its 12 partitions, replication factor 3, 7-day retention, key caseId, the three retry topics at 1 min, 10 min and 1 h and the `.dlt` topic; provision nothing new if RWB-PLT-N002-INF already did it.
7. Bind the ACLs: the rwb-document principal writes `rwb.document.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1` and reads nothing else; the consumer groups of `rwb-case` and `rwb-agent` read `rwb.document.events.v1`; no Recovery principal reads an ACE PII logging topic.
8. Put the login, the Kafka credential, the Temporal mTLS material and the storage identity in the key store behind the workload identity, and write the rotation entry for each of the four classes.
9. Apply the private route: private DNS for `rwb-case`, `rwb-decision`, the brokers, the Temporal frontend and Blob; no public inbound rule on the service; egress limited to the named endpoints.
10. Provision the scan capacity and the hold rule that makes an item wait unscanned, and run the six tests of section 16 against the provisioned state.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The worker pool is saturated and the queue backlog grows past its threshold | The pool scales out on the backlog; if the ceiling is reached the run takes longer and the run book names the ceiling as the cause | MSG-P5-E1032-INF-02 | AC1, AC5 |
| X2 | A page of OCR text pushes the `document_text` storage past its budget | The alert fires on the storage series; the run book names the retention and archiving step and the capacity request | MSG-P5-E1032-INF-03 | AC2 |
| X3 | The hold container is unreachable or refuses the write of a new item | The item stays `ocr_status` PENDING and no match runs; the scan alert fires and the run book names the container | MSG-P5-E1032-INF-04 | AC3 |
| X4 | A held file is older than the clearing rule allows | The clearing job records the item for the owner role and does not delete a file whose item is still open | MSG-P5-E1032-INF-04 | AC3 |
| X5 | A principal writes to a topic it does not own, or reads a topic where the event catalogue lists no consumer | The broker refuses the operation and the attempt is audited | MSG-P5-E1032-INF-01 | AC4 |
| X6 | A credential, certificate or identity binding expires or is rotated out | The dependency fails closed, the service health reports not ready and the rotation entry restores the version; no clear-text fallback exists | MSG-P5-E1032-INF-02 | AC5 |
| X7 | A network rule admits public egress, or a public inbound rule appears on the service | The network scan fails the change and the release is blocked | None | AC6 |
| X8 | The scan rate falls below the intake rate | Items wait in the hold container and the queue age rises; the alert fires and the run book names the scan capacity | MSG-P5-E1032-INF-03 | AC6 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Provisions compute, storage, containers, topic bindings, ACLs, identity, route and scan capacity; no application code is built here and no service build blocks it |
| Negotiable | Replica counts, request and limit sets, storage budgets, the clearing age, the backlog threshold and the scan rate are environment values settled with the platform and network teams |
| Valuable | Gives the app and operations stories provisioned capacity, a ruled hold container and a private path on Day 1, with no secret in a values file |
| Estimable | One worker pool, one storage and index budget, three containers with rules, one topic binding, one ACL set, one identity layout, one route set and one scan capacity |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the runbook entries and the six tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against provisioned state, a refused operation, a container rule or a scan, never against a business outcome |

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One worker pool polls one task queue: queue `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, and no other queue | Arch v5 slides 20, 41 and 44; DP-02 |
| BR2 | The intake cadence is 15 minutes in business hours (JOB-12), served by a Temporal Schedule and not by a Quartz job or a shared scheduler | Arch v5 slide 44; FSD P5 AC-BG-P5-012-01; DP-10 |
| BR3 | The OCR text lives in `document_text` in `rwb_document` only; it is never copied to a container, a topic or a workflow payload | DP-01; Arch v5 slide 11 |
| BR4 | Three containers exist with one rule each: `rwb-docs` standard, `rwb-docs-legal` write-once, `rwb-quarantine` hold; no blob is overwritten and a held file is read through one claim-check link at a time | RWB-P5-E1024-APP; Arch v5 slide 11 |
| BR5 | Every event topic has three retry topics and one dead-letter topic, and the ACLs are least privilege and separate from the ACE PII logging topics | Arch v5 slides 11 and 21; DP-09 |
| BR6 | No secret in code, configuration, a values file or a script; the four secret classes live in the key store behind the workload identity and rotate under a written entry | NFR-052; Arch v5 slide 35 |
| BR7 | Every dependency is reached over a private endpoint resolved by private DNS, with no public inbound rule on the service | Arch v5 slide 35 |
| BR8 | Every inbound file is scanned before it enters the matcher; the scan rate bounds the intake rate and an unscanned item waits in the hold container | FSD P5 A2.18; RWB-P5-E1041-APP |
| BR9 | Capacity is provisioned for the volume the sources state: about 860,000 documents a year (NFR-004) and 5.8 million documents and 2.8 TB by 2031 (NFR-069), including every held document | NFR-004; NFR-069 |
| BR10 | This story provisions capacity, storage, a container rule, a topic binding, an identity, a route and a scan: it registers no Schedule, builds no matcher and writes no business rule | Arch v5 slides 16, 38 and 44; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |

##### 9. State transitions

Container lifecycle.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Requested | Provisioning approved | The identity, the private endpoint and the policy are known | Provisioned |
| Provisioned | Identity bound | The workload identity resolves to read and write on the container | In use |
| In use | Policy changed | The storage product changes the immutability policy of `rwb-docs-legal` | Changing |
| Changing | Policy in force | No blob write is in flight and no version depends on the earlier policy | In use |
| In use | Container retired | No item refers to a file of the container and the retention has elapsed | Retired |

Held file.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Received | Scan clean | The file passed the scan and the item row exists | In the hold container |
| In the hold container | Match runs | The item is selected by `matchStep` | Read by the matcher |
| In the hold container | Item attached | The store wrote the document | Cleared from the hold container |
| In the hold container | Item discarded | A reviewer discards it with a reason | Cleared from the hold container |
| In the hold container | Age rule reached | The item is still open and the age rule of the container is met | Reported to the owner role, not deleted |

Worker pool.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Provisioned | Backlog rises | The queue backlog passes the threshold value | Scaling out |
| Scaling out | Backlog clears | The backlog falls below the threshold | At floor |
| At floor | Ceiling reached | The backlog keeps rising at the ceiling | Saturated |
| Saturated | Capacity raised | The ceiling value is raised and applied | Scaling out |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** `infra/compute/workers.yaml` (the pool, the KEDA rule, the floor and the ceiling, the request and limit set, the queue and the namespace), `infra/storage/database.yaml` (the storage and index budget of `document_intake` and `document_text`), `infra/storage/containers.yaml` (the three containers, their access rule, the hold rule and the clearing rule), `infra/kafka/bindings.yaml` (the topic settings, the retry and `.dlt` verification, the producer and consumer ACLs), `infra/security/identity.yaml` (the workload identity bindings, the four secret classes and the rotation entries), `infra/network/rules.yaml` (the private endpoints, the private DNS records, the egress allow-list and the absence of a public inbound rule), `infra/scan/capacity.yaml` (the scan rate and the queue-age alert) and `runbooks/hold-and-scan.md` (the hold rule, the clearing step, the scan capacity check and the escalation).

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON (of the app story) |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON (of the app story) |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON (of the app story) |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON (of the app story) |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON (of the app story) |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON (of the app story) |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON (of the app story) |

DP-01 is applied by sizing one schema and one login: `document_intake` and `document_text` live in `rwb_document`, no cross-schema read is provisioned and no ACE view is granted. DP-03, DP-06, DP-07 and DP-09 appear because the capacity this story provisions carries the paths those patterns run on: the decision record, the parameters, the lists and the attach event all need the private routes, the identity and the topic binding that are provisioned here; their H dependencies are the app story's and are not carried by this story. DP-05 is applied by absence: no grant, no route and no view for this service, because only rwb-source-data reads ACE data. DP-10 is the substantive change: the Quartz job on a shared scheduler becomes a Temporal Schedule on queue `rwb-document`, so this story sizes a worker pool against a queue and a backlog rather than a scheduler table, and it registers no Schedule of its own. DP-11 fixes the four internal routes to private endpoints with a 2 s client budget. DP-15 keeps the migration with the service sequence, so this story creates no table and no grant. DP-19 records that the reviewer's list is reached through the gateway-bff composite route, and the only network consequence here is that the service answers the edge privately.

**Build steps**

1. Write the compute inventory: the queue, the namespace, the KEDA rule, the floor and the ceiling, and the request and limit set of `matchStep`.
2. Size the storage: the page rows, the item rows, the three indexes and the growth budget against NFR-004 and NFR-069.
3. Provision the three containers, the private endpoint of each and the access rule that names the workload identity only.
4. Write the hold rule: one claim-check read at a time, the clearing events, the age rule and the rule that an open item is reported and never deleted.
5. Verify the topic settings and the retry and `.dlt` topics against RWB-PLT-N002-INF, and bind the producer and consumer ACLs.
6. Place the four secret classes in the key store, bind them to the workload identity and write the four rotation entries.
7. Apply the private endpoints, the private DNS records and the egress allow-list, and run the public-access scan that proves no inbound rule answers.
8. Set the scan rate as a value, wire the queue-age alert and add the hold-and-scan runbook entry that names the scan capacity as the cause of a rising queue.
9. Hand the queue, the storage budget, the container references, the identity and the scan rate to the app and operations stories, and run the six tests of section 16.

**Done when.** The pool scales on the queue backlog and keeps the 15-minute cadence in a replayed business-hour window, the storage and index budgets are measured and alerting, the three containers exist with their rule and the clearing rule is exercised, the topic and its four derived topics carry the ACLs of BR5, no secret appears in a values file or a script, the public-access scan finds no inbound rule, the scan capacity bounds the intake, and the six tests of section 16 pass against the provisioned state.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a resource file: the patterns, the threshold, the type list, the paging default and the clearing policy of a business rule stay parameters or reference rows, never a literal in the infrastructure.
- No personal data in a file name, a manifest, a log, a trace attribute or an alert: identifiers, counts, page counts, sizes and hashes only.
- No second copy of OCR text: `document_text` is the only store, no container and no topic receives the text, and the hold container keeps the file and not the text (BR3).
- No secret in code, configuration, a values file or a script; the four secret classes are read with the workload identity (BR6, NFR-052).
- No public inbound rule and no open egress: every dependency is reached over a private endpoint resolved by private DNS (BR7).
- No ACE grant and no ACE view for this service; only rwb-source-data reads the views (DP-05).
- No data-lake endpoint, route or landing container is provisioned, because the data lake is removed (DP-17).
- A held file is never deleted while its item is open: it is reported to the owner role by the clearing job (BR4).
- An item is never matched unscanned: the scan is a condition of entering the matcher (BR8).
- No Schedule, no workflow and no activity is registered by this story; the queue is sized and the Schedule is the deployment story's (BR10).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-032 for rwb-document. The legacy story ran JOB-12 on a shared Quartz scheduler behind a shared schema and expected an operator to read the review queue in the database. This story deploys the intake-match capability of `rwb-document`: one chart and its values, the `rwb_document` migration step, the topic and the queue, the 15-minute intake Schedule registered in Temporal on queue `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, the flag that replaces `rwb.dochub.autoattach`, the dashboards for match outcomes and held items, the alerts on a failed run and on a decision-record failure, the runbook and the rollback. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform engineer**, I want **the intake-match capability of `rwb-document` deployed as one Helm release with its values files, its per-service Flyway step in `rwb_document`, its topic and its task queue with retry and `.dlt`, the 15-minute intake Schedule registered in Temporal on queue `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, the feature flag that turns the automatic attach on and off, the dashboards that show match outcomes and held items, the alerts on a failed run and on a decision-record failure, and a runbook with its rollback**, so that **an operator can see a run that failed, an item that was held, a decision record that could not be written and a queue that stopped moving, restart it from the run book alone, and prove that no document was filed twice or lost when the flag was switched or the release was rolled back**.

The legacy story ran the intake behind a shared Quartz scheduler and a shared schema: JOB-12 fired on the scheduler table, `matchStep` wrote the recovery schema, and the Unmatched list was a query somebody ran. In the target that picture splits in four. JOB-12 is a Temporal Schedule in the service that owns it, so the release registers the Schedule and the worker that serves it (DP-10). The migration is one step of the service's own Flyway sequence in `rwb_document` (DP-15). The topic is `rwb.document.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics and its ACLs (DP-09, DP-14). The review queue is SCR-31 served through the gateway-bff composite route by the app story (DP-19). What is left for this story is a chart, a migration gate, a Schedule, a flag, six dashboard series, four alert rules, five runbook entries and a rollback.

Deployment is also where the split is enforced operationally. The release carries the rwb-document login only, migrates `rwb_document` only, publishes on its own topic and on the shared decision-record topic only, and polls `rwb-document` only. It provisions no ACE grant, no view and no data-lake route (DP-01, DP-05, DP-17), and no inbound consumer on this path, because the trigger is the Schedule. The observability follows ADR-023 per service: six series, four alerts and five runbook entries, each alert carrying a message identifier and one runbook entry.

##### 2. Business rationale

The business measure of this legacy key is fields extracted without review (FSD P5 A2.12.1), and the operational measure behind it is simple: an item that is held must be visible to the reviewer, and an item that failed must be visible to the operator. Neither is a unit test. A run that fails at 10:15, a decision record that refuses every write for ten minutes, a queue that stops moving because the worker lost its identity, and a set of held items that nobody counted are all silent unless the release emits them and the run book says what to do.

The split changes what an operator does. In the legacy story the operator restarted a Quartz job and opened the review queue in the same database. In the target the operator reads the Schedule's run history, the match-outcome counters and the held-item panel, restarts through the Schedule itself, and confirms three things: that the worker polled `rwb-document`, that the hole in the decision records is closed by the retry of the run, and that the items the failed run touched are back in PENDING so the next run selects them. The runbook is written for that sequence, because the difference between a busy morning and an incident is whether the operator has to guess which of the three failed.

The story also carries the retirement explicitly. No Quartz job, no scheduler table and no shared schema is deployed; the Schedule is the only timer, and a release that registers a second one or a job on a foreign queue fails its own checks (BR1, BR2, BR3). The flag keeps the automatic attach reversible without a schema change, and the rollback keeps the previous build serving open runs.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template, the chart skeleton and the pipeline are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-LIB).
- The Kafka event platform provides `rwb.document.events.v1` with its three retry topics and its `.dlt` topic and the shared `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and the ACLs of this service's principals (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON; DP-09).
- The Temporal workflow kit and the namespace `rwb-recovery` exist, with worker versioning, the build ID provider and the payload codec (RWB-PLT-WF, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON; DP-10).
- The per-service Flyway sequence and the migration conventions of `rwb_document` are published (RWB-PLT-E1044-CON; DP-15).
- The platform error envelope and the message catalogue are in force, so an alert can carry a message identifier.
- The three environments DEV, SIT and UAT exist and the production namespace exists for the release date; the feature flag library is available.
- The worker compute, the storage, the hold container, the topic binding, the ACLs, the identity and the route exist in each environment (RWB-P5-E1032-INF).
- The gateway-bff composite route for SCR-31 is published (RWB-PLT-N001-CON; DP-19).
- The store and the intake workflow are declared (RWB-P5-E1024-APP, RWB-P5-E1049-APP), so the release deploys a capability that exists and not a shell.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7). The baseline it deploys is RWB-P5-E1032-APP's and the values it injects are RWB-P5-E1032-INF's; both are declared before the release and neither blocks the chart work.
- The release date 30 November 2026 is the legacy one and is tentative (ASM-1764), and the story carries Status Draft (realignment v1) because no approval of the realigned story is recorded (ASM-1765).

##### 4. Flow

1. The pipeline builds the service image and the contract jar, runs the unit, component and contract tests, scans the image and the dependencies, and publishes one chart version.
2. The chart deploys the API deployment and the worker deployment with the rwb-document login, the namespace `rwb-recovery`, the task queue `rwb-document`, the codec, the build ID of the release and the values of RWB-P5-E1032-INF.
3. The worker scaling step enables KEDA on the queue backlog of `rwb-document`, so the pool grows with the 15-minute run and the front stays at its fixed replica count.
4. The migration step applies the `rwb_document` sequence of the release and refuses to run when the target schema is not `rwb_document`; the intake migration `V1032_1__intake_match.sql` is one step of it.
5. The topic step creates or verifies `rwb.document.events.v1` with its partitions, its replication factor, its retention, the three retry topics at 1 minute, 10 minutes and 1 hour and its `.dlt` topic, and records the ACL of the producer and of the consumer groups.
6. The Schedule step registers the intake Schedule: workflow `DocumentIntakeWorkflow`, queue `rwb-document`, namespace `rwb-recovery`, every 15 minutes in business hours, overlap policy skip and a catch-up window of one run, its ID fixed by the release so a second apply changes nothing.
7. The flag step sets `rwb.document.intake-autoattach` from the values of the environment; the legacy name `rwb.dochub.autoattach` is recorded as retired and is not deployed (ASM-1766).
8. The dashboards are published with the six series and the environment, release and build ID as dimensions.
9. The four alerts are wired to their message identifiers and to their runbook entries: MSG-P2-004 for a failed run, MSG-P7-003 for failed decision records, MSG-P5-003 for held items and MSG-GEN-006 for a dependency that is not available.
10. A smoke step in DEV drops one synthetic notice in the hold container with the case ID "RW-2026-000123", waits for one Schedule run, confirms one document, one DOCATT record and one attach event, forces one decision-record failure to see the alert, and confirms that the item returned to PENDING and the environment is restored.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The chart render or the migration job fails | The deployment stays unready and the pipeline stops; no traffic, no offset and no migration is left half applied | None | AC1 |
| X2 | The migration step is pointed at a schema other than `rwb_document` | The step refuses and the release stops | None | AC1 |
| X3 | A run of the intake Schedule fails, or runs past its threshold | The run-failure alert fires with MSG-P2-004 naming the run, the time and the runbook path; the Schedule retries on its next interval | MSG-P2-004 | AC4 |
| X4 | The decision-record write fails during a run | The run stops at the failing item, MSG-P7-003 is raised, the item stays PENDING and the decision-record alert fires with the count of failed records | MSG-P7-003 | AC4, AC6 |
| X5 | The feature flag is off in an environment | No automatic attach runs: `matchStep` sets every classified item to NO_MATCH and the items reach the reviewer; the flag is not a way to stop a run in progress | None | AC1, AC6 |
| X6 | A dependency is not available, or its credential has expired | The run fails closed, the item stays PENDING, the dependency alert fires with MSG-GEN-006 naming the system and the runbook entry names the rotation | MSG-GEN-006 | AC4, AC6 |
| X7 | The Schedule is registered twice, or a foreign job is registered on the queue | The Schedule check fails the release: one Schedule ID, one workflow, one queue | None | AC3 |
| X8 | A dashboard series is missing, or an alert carries no message identifier or no runbook link | The observability check fails the release | None | AC5, AC6 |
| X9 | A new build is promoted while runs are open | The open runs replay on the new build from their history; the dashboards show both build IDs | None | AC1, AC5 |
| X10 | The lag of the attach-event consumer group passes its threshold | The lag alert fires; the runbook entry names the group, the topic and the partition | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0994; ASM-1768) | AC5, AC6 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the chart skeleton, the workflow kit, the topic provisioning, the migration conventions and the flag library; no application code is built here |
| Negotiable | Replica counts, resource sizes, lag and age thresholds, intervals and quotas are environment values |
| Valuable | Makes the intake path observable, restartable and provable before the release date, and keeps the automatic attach reversible |
| Estimable | One chart, one migration gate, one Schedule, one flag, six series, four alerts and five runbook entries |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the runbook |
| Testable | Every criterion tests an artefact: the chart renders, the migration refuses a foreign schema, the Schedule exists once, an alert fires on a synthetic metric, the smoke run passes |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin

  Background:

    Given the target environment is SIT

    When the chart is rendered for DEV, SIT and UAT

    Then the API and the worker deployments carry the rwb-document login and no other service's credential

    Then the migration step applies the rwb_document sequence and refuses a target schema other than rwb_document
    Then worker versioning is enabled and a new run goes to the new build while the old build drains
    Then the deployment registers no Quartz job and no scheduler table

  Scenario: AC2 The topic and its retry and dead-letter topics are provisioned with their ACLs (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the release of this story and the platform event epic
    When the topic step runs
    Then rwb.document.events.v1 exists with its partitions, its replication factor and its retention
    Then the retry topics at 1 minute, 10 minutes and 1 hour and the .dlt topic exist for it
    Then the producer ACL is granted to the rwb-document principal only
    Then the consumer ACLs of rwb-case and rwb-agent are granted on the topic
    Then a topic outside rwb.document.events.v1 and rwb.decision-record.v1 is refused by the release
    Then the deployment subscribes to no topic of this service, because the path is started by the Schedule

  Scenario: AC3 The 15-minute intake Schedule is registered in Temporal and in no other scheduler (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the deployed release and the namespace rwb-recovery
    When the Schedule step runs and is applied a second time
    Then one Schedule exists with the ID fixed by the release, the workflow DocumentIntakeWorkflow and the queue rwb-document
    Then its interval is every 15 minutes in business hours and its overlap policy is skip with a catch-up window of one run
    Then the second apply creates no second Schedule and changes nothing
    Then no Quartz job, no scheduler table and no cron entry exists in the release
    Then a run that fails is retried on the next interval and the items it touched are back in PENDING
    Then the exact business-hours window and the catch-up policy are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0994; ASM-1767)

  Scenario: AC4 The failed-run and decision-record alerts fire with their identifiers (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published alert rules of the deployment
    When a synthetic run fails and a synthetic decision-record write is forced to fail
    Then the run-failure alert fires with MSG-P2-004 naming the run, the time, the business date and the runbook path
    Then the decision-record alert fires with MSG-P7-003 and the count of failed records of the run
    Then each alert names the Schedule ID, the build ID and the environment
    Then each alert carries a message identifier and one runbook link
    Then no alert payload carries OCR text, a file name, an account number or a customer identifier

  Scenario: AC5 The dashboards show the six series for match outcomes and held items (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published dashboards of the deployment
    When a synthetic run produces matched items, held items of each status and one failure
    Then the dashboards show items by match status, the age of the oldest held item, documents attached per run, the count of files stored for review, decision-record failures per run, and the queue backlog and age of the task queue
    Then each series carries the environment, the release and the build ID as dimensions
    Then a held item, a failed run and a decision-record failure are visible on the dashboards before any alert is read
    Then no panel shows OCR text or a customer identifier

  Scenario: AC6 The flag, the runbook and the rollback are exercised (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published runbook, the flag and the rollback of the release
    When the flag rwb.document.intake-autoattach is turned off in SIT and one Schedule run is waited for
    Then every classified item of that run is held with match_status NO_MATCH and no document is stored
    Then the legacy flag rwb.dochub.autoattach appears in no values file, chart or runbook
    When a failed run, a held item, a stuck retry, an unavailable dependency and a lagging group are simulated
    Then each condition maps to one runbook entry with the check, the owner role and the recovery step
    Then the rollback redeploys the previous chart with its own build ID and the open runs finish on the old build
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One login, one task queue and one schema per service: the release carries the rwb-document login, polls `rwb-document` only and migrates `rwb_document` only | Arch v5 slide 41; DP-02; DP-15 |
| BR2 | The release publishes on `rwb.document.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1` only and subscribes to no topic of this service | Arch v5 slides 16, 42 and 43; DP-09; DP-14 |
| BR3 | One Schedule and one scheduler: the intake Schedule is the only timer for JOB-12, registered in Temporal on queue `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery`; no Quartz job, no scheduler table and no cron entry exists | Arch v5 slide 44; DP-10; `ASM-1767` |
| BR4 | The automatic attach is reversible by one flag, `rwb.document.intake-autoattach`, which replaces the legacy `rwb.dochub.autoattach` | legacy section 13; DP-14; `ASM-1766` |
| BR5 | Every alert carries a message identifier and the agreed text and links one runbook entry | Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR6 | No environment value is hard-coded: replicas, resources, thresholds, intervals, quotas and the flag come from values files and parameters | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR7 | Dashboard series, alert payloads and the runbook carry counts, identifiers, statuses, business dates and build IDs only, never OCR text, a file name or a customer identifier | ADR-023; CTL-11 |
| BR8 | The release exposes the four intake operations through the chart and its ingress and declares no path of its own; SCR-31 is reached through the gateway-bff composite route | DP-19; RWB-P5-E1032-CON 12.1 |
| BR9 | A failing release never replaces a working one: the previous build stays in force until the new build passes its tests and its smoke run | DP-10 |
| BR10 | An item a failed run touched is never deleted and never left matched on a guess: it stays PENDING for the next run, and a decision-record failure leaves nothing stored | R-UNI-39; legacy X13 |
| BR11 | The release provisions no ACE grant, no view, no data-lake route and no inbound consumer of this path | D-RCV-35 U1; ADR-010; DP-05; DP-17 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | Chart published | The image, the chart and the contract tests pass | Deploying |
| Deploying | Migration applied and worker registered | The `rwb_document` sequence applied and the worker polls `rwb-document` | Ready |
| Ready | Schedule registered | One Schedule with the release ID, the workflow and the queue | Scheduled |
| Scheduled | First run completes | The run finishes and its counters reach the dashboards | In use |
| In use | Release superseded | A new chart version passes its tests | Rolling |
| Rolling | All workers on the new build | The old build drains its open runs | In use |
| In use | Flag off | `rwb.document.intake-autoattach` is turned off in the environment | Held |
| Held | Flag on | The flag is turned on again and the next run matches | In use |
| In use | Smoke run failed | The Schedule check, the alert check or the smoke step fails | Blocked |
| Blocked | Previous build restored | The previous chart is redeployed or a later build passes the smoke run | In use |

The item states PENDING, MATCHED, NO_MATCH, MULTIPLE, CONFLICT, CASE_CLOSED and NO_TYPE are the app story's runtime and are not states of this deployment.

| Who | What they may do in this story |

| DevOps engineer | Owns the chart, the values files, the pipeline stages, the migration gate, the Schedule step, the dashboards and the runbook |
| Platform administrator | Owns the `rwb-recovery` namespace, the Schedule, the topic ACLs, the consumer quotas, the flag library and the restart of a run |
| Platform event owner | Owns `rwb.document.events.v1`, its retry and `.dlt` topics, its schema subject and its retention |
| Release manager | Approves the promotion of one artefact and may block it on a failing smoke run |

| rwb-document owner | Owns the matcher, the store and the migration the release applies |
| Data steward | Confirms that no dashboard, alert or runbook carries OCR text or a customer identifier |
| RW-AUDIT | Reads the run history, the alert trail and the runbook |

The worker runs as the rwb-document service identity (DP-02), carried by the chart as a secret reference and never as a literal. The login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0994; ASM-1768).
