| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Deployment values | Image digest, chart version, replica counts for the API and the worker, resource requests and limits, probe paths and timings, log level, namespace, task queue, build ID, feature switch, KEDA backlog threshold, Schedule ID and interval |
| Task queue | `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, polled by the worker of this service only |
| Topic | `rwb.document.events.v1` with its partitions, replication factor, retention and key, its three retry topics and its `.dlt` topic; `rwb.decision-record.v1` published by the library; no subscription of this service |
| Schema | `rwb_document`, migrated by its own per-service Flyway sequence; the intake migration `V1032_1__intake_match.sql` is one step of it |
| Schedule | The intake Schedule: `DocumentIntakeWorkflow`, queue `rwb-document`, namespace `rwb-recovery`, every 15 minutes in business hours (JOB-12), overlap policy skip, catch-up window one run, ID fixed by the release |
| Flag | `rwb.document.intake-autoattach`, on in DEV and SIT for the tests, from the values of each environment; the legacy `rwb.dochub.autoattach` is retired |
| Dashboard series | Items by match status, age of the oldest held item, documents attached per run, files stored for review, decision-record failures per run, queue backlog and age; dimensions environment, release, build ID |
| Runbook entries | Failed run, held item, stuck retry, unavailable dependency, lagging group; each with the check, the owner role and the recovery step |
| Alerts | Four rules and one runbook entry each: MSG-P2-004 for a failed run, MSG-P7-003 for failed decision records, MSG-P5-003 for held items, MSG-GEN-006 for an unavailable dependency; the lag alert carries the identifier placeholder of GAP-0994 |
| Secrets | The rwb-document login secret, the Kafka client credential, the Temporal mTLS material and the storage identity reference, all from the platform secret store |
| Test data | One synthetic notice for case "RW-2026-000123", one forced decision-record failure and one flag-off run; synthetic identifiers only |

The deployment topology (cluster names, node pools, replica counts, resource sizes, zone spread, ingress class and probe timings) belongs to each environment and is set by the platform team in its values file; the chart exposes every one of them as a value and this story fixes only their names and the rule that they are never hard-coded.

**Probes.** Readiness answers healthy only after the worker has polled `rwb-document` once and the API has answered its health path; liveness answers healthy when the process is up and its internal loop is responsive. Neither probe writes to the database or commits an offset, and a failing dependency is reported as not ready, never as live-and-broken.

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

| None | — | — | The four intake operations — `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items`, `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}`, `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/content` and `POST /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/resolve` — are declared by RWB-P5-E1032-CON and implemented by RWB-P5-E1032-APP; this deployment exposes them through the chart and its ingress and declares no path of its own. The probes are cluster-internal and are not part of the API surface |

| Method | Path | Owner | Story | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| None | — | — | — | The deployment carries no REST client of its own. At run time the app story's clients reach `rwb-case` and `rwb-decision` over the private routes of RWB-P5-E1032-INF; the chart's only start-up calls are the Temporal frontend, the Kafka brokers and the health paths of its own dependencies |

| Event | Topic | Owner | Key | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| None | — | — | — | `rwb.document.DocumentAttached.v1` on `rwb.document.events.v1` is published by the app story, and `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` by the local decision-record library through the relay (DP-03, DP-09); the deployment publishes nothing of its own |

| Event | Topic | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | — | — | This path consumes no event: the trigger is the intake Schedule. The consumer groups of `rwb-case` and `rwb-agent` on `rwb.document.events.v1` are theirs and not deployed here |

| Name | Type | Task queue | Deployment element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` | Workflow, from the L3 "Document intake" template | `rwb-document` | Registered by the worker of this release with the build ID and worker versioning; owned by RWB-P5-E1049-APP |
| `matchStep` | Activity | `rwb-document` | Registered by the same worker with the kit's retry policy; owned by RWB-P5-E1032-APP |
| Outbox relay | Platform relay | not a worker | Deployed with the library; publishes `rwb.document.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1` on its one-minute interval (JOB-11) |

**Build ID and versioning.** The build ID is the one supplied by the workflow kit for the release commit; worker versioning is enabled and a new build takes new runs while the old build drains. The build ID format and the versioning policy are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0994; ASM-1768).

| Schedule | Workflow | Queue | Interval | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| The intake Schedule (JOB-12 Document intake) | `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` | `rwb-document` | Every 15 minutes in business hours | Registered by this release from its values, with the ID fixed by the release, overlap policy skip and a catch-up window of one run; a run that fails is retried on the next interval and the items it touched stay PENDING. The exact business-hours window and the catch-up policy are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0994; ASM-1767) |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | The release migrates `rwb_document` only and reads no other schema | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | The local record library is deployed with the relay and publishes to `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | No ACE grant, no view and no route in this release | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | The three parameters stay rows read through the client library; no chart value carries them | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | The five lists stay reference rows; no chart value carries them | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | The topic with its retry and `.dlt` topics, the inbox and the relay | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | The worker, the task queue, worker versioning and the intake Schedule from the kit; no Quartz job | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | The release declares no REST path and no client of its own; the private routes are RWB-P5-E1032-INF's | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | The `rwb_document` sequence with its intake step and a foreign-schema refusal | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | The ingress registers the service base for the gateway-bff edge; no screen is deployed | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-10 is the substantive row of this story: JOB-12 stops being a Quartz job on a shared scheduler and becomes a Temporal Schedule on the service's own queue, so the release registers the Schedule, the worker and the build ID, and the operator restarts a run through the Schedule rather than a scheduler table. DP-01 and DP-15 keep the migration inside `rwb_document` and make the step refuse a foreign schema. DP-02 is not in the pattern list of the key and is applied by the chart anyway: one login, carried as a secret reference. DP-03 and DP-09 deploy the library, the relay, the topic and the retry and `.dlt` topics the attach event needs. DP-06 and DP-07 keep the parameters and the five lists out of the values files. DP-11 and DP-05 are applied by absence: the release declares no REST path of its own, no client and no ACE grant. DP-19 registers the ingress path the edge calls and deploys no screen.

**Artefacts**

| Artefact | Content |
|---|---|
| `helm/rwb-document/` overlay | API deployment, worker deployment, config map, secret references, probes, task queue, namespace, build ID, KEDA rule, Schedule definition and flag |
| `helm/rwb-document/values-dev.yaml`, `values-sit.yaml`, `values-uat.yaml` | Image digest, replicas, resources, probe timings, log level, flag value, build ID, Schedule ID and interval, KEDA threshold, container references (ASM-1768) |
| Pipeline stage | Build, unit and contract tests, image and dependency scan, chart publish, migration gate, topic step, Schedule step, smoke run, promotion |
| Migration step | The `rwb_document` sequence with `V1032_1__intake_match.sql`; a target schema other than `rwb_document` is refused |
| Topic step | `rwb.document.events.v1` with its three retry topics and its `.dlt`, the producer ACL and the consumer ACLs of rwb-case and rwb-agent |
| Schedule step | The intake Schedule with its release ID, the workflow, the queue, the interval, the overlap policy and the catch-up window, idempotent on the ID |
| Dashboards | The six series of section 11 with the three dimensions |
| Alerts | Four rules, each with a message identifier or its placeholder and one runbook entry |
| Runbook | Five entries: failed run, held item, stuck retry, unavailable dependency, lagging group |

**Alert mapping**

| Message ID | Condition | Alert | Route |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P2-004 | A run of the intake Schedule failed or ran past its threshold | Run-failure alert naming the Schedule ID, the run, the time, the business date and the runbook path | Platform on-call, page in business hours, else ticket |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision-record write failed during a run | Decision-record alert naming the run, the count of failed records and the retry state of the items | Platform on-call and the rwb-decision owner, page |
| MSG-P5-003 | Items are held for a person, or a document is stored for review | Held-items alert on the age of the oldest held item and the count per status | Reviewer lead and the data steward, ticket |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A dependency is not available or its credential has expired | Dependency alert naming the system and the health state | Platform on-call, page |
| Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0994; ASM-1768) | The attach-event consumer group lags past its threshold | Lag alert naming the group, the topic, the partition and the lag | Platform on-call, ticket |

**Retry and offsets.** The Schedule retries a failed run on its next interval and never runs two runs at once, because the overlap policy is skip. The activity retry is the kit's three attempts with back-off; the deployment adds no retry of its own. The relay commits its offset after the outbox row is marked sent, so a restart republishes nothing twice, and the consumer inbox of rwb-case makes a replay harmless (DP-09).

**Rollback.** A release that fails the smoke run is not promoted. A release already promoted is rolled back by redeploying the previous chart version with its own build ID, which keeps the old build serving its open runs until they finish; the Schedule keeps its ID and points at the workflow, so a rollback changes the build under it and not the timer. Items a failed run touched are PENDING and are selected again; no data repair is needed, because the release writes no business row of its own and the migration is additive.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.document.intake-autoattach`. On: `matchStep` matches, stores or holds. Off: every classified item is set to NO_MATCH and reaches the reviewer, and the flag is not a way to stop a run in progress, which is what the Schedule and the runbook are for. The legacy name `rwb.dochub.autoattach` appears in no value, chart or runbook (ASM-1766).

**Done when.** The chart renders for DEV, SIT and UAT with a pinned digest and the build ID, the migration step refuses a foreign schema, the topic and its retry and `.dlt` topics exist with their ACLs, one Schedule exists with the release ID and the queue `rwb-document` and a second apply changes nothing, the flag-off run holds every classified item, the six series and the four alerts are published with their identifiers or placeholders and their runbook links, the smoke run produces one document, one record and one event with no duplicate, and the five runbook entries are reviewed by the on-call rota. The alert thresholds, the intervals and the catch-up window are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0994; ASM-1768).

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P2-004 | A run of the intake Schedule failed or ran past its threshold | {job} failed at {time} for business date {date}. Follow run book {runbook}. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision-record write failed during a run | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P5-003 | Items held for a person, or a document stored for review | Some fields need checking. The document is in the review queue. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A dependency is not available or its credential has expired | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| Identifier pending | The attach-event consumer group lags past its threshold | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0994; ASM-1768) |

MSG-P5-003 and MSG-P7-003 are the legacy texts of section 14 of RWB-E1-032 and are unchanged. MSG-P2-004 is the job-failure text of the observability epic and MSG-GEN-006 the platform text for an unavailable system; both are used here with their agreed wording. The lag alert has no identifier in the source set, so it carries the placeholder until the Error and Message Standard names it. An alert payload names counts, statuses, business dates, the Schedule ID, the build ID and group names only, never OCR text, a file name, an account number or a customer identifier.

##### 15. Screens and states

The deployment has no screen of its own. Its operator-facing surfaces are the pipeline run view, the release view, the Temporal Web UI, the dashboards, SCR-31 Document review queue through the gateway-bff composite route, and the runbook. SCR-31 is served by the app story and the route of RWB-PLT-N001-CON; the deployment only registers the ingress path. The Temporal Web UI stays behind Entra ID: RW-PLATADM operates and RW-AUDIT reads, and payloads are decoded only through the codec server under break-glass. SCR-44 Interface and job monitor belongs to Epic 2 and shows the same run data from there; this release publishes the run records the monitor reads.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a values file: the patterns, the threshold, the type list, the owner role and the alert role are parameters and reference rows, never a deployment value.
- No personal data in logs, dashboard series, alert payloads, the runbook or the workflow history: counts, statuses, identifiers, business dates and build IDs only, and payloads stay encrypted.
- One login, one task queue and one schema per service: the release carries the rwb-document login, polls `rwb-document` and migrates `rwb_document` only (DP-02, DP-15).
- The release deploys no ACE grant, no view, no data-lake route and no inbound consumer of this path (DP-05, DP-17, BR11).
- One Schedule and one scheduler: no Quartz job, no scheduler table and no cron entry besides the intake Schedule (BR3).
- The topic and its retry and `.dlt` topics exist with their ACLs before the worker starts (DP-09, BR2).
- An item a failed run touched is never deleted and never left matched on a guess; a decision-record failure leaves nothing stored (BR10, R-UNI-39).
- The release pins the image digest, the chart version and the build ID; a rebuild between environments is not allowed, and a failing smoke run never replaces a working build.
- No secret is written into a values file, a chart template, a dashboard or the runbook; all secrets come from the platform secret store (NFR-052).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: integration slice of RWB-E1-032 for RWB-ITG-W1. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **QA integration engineer**, I want **the end-to-end proof of the RWB-E1-032 automatic attach across P5 rwb-document (intake, match, store, held items), P3 rwb-case (the case directory and case status), P6 rwb-comms (the letter copy), S9 rwb-partner (the partner result file) and P7 rwb-decision (the DOCATT decision records)**, so that **every document that names its case or account is attached without a person and every doubtful one is held, proved on the real wave 1 services**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story runs the match step inside the Quartz job JOB-12 every 15 minutes in business hours. The step selects the intake items that hold OCR text, no document and a predicted type, reads the case numbers and account numbers from the extracted fields and from the text, resolves them through the P3 `CaseDirectory` published interface, stores the matched file through the P5 `DocumentStore` and writes the `DOCATT` entry through the P7 `DecisionLogWriter`. A person attaches everything the matcher holds.

In the 19-service target JOB-12 becomes an event-started `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` in P5 rwb-document, started from the document event and scaled on KEDA workers (DP-10; Architecture v5 slide 44). The case lookup is the P3 rwb-case case contract rather than an in-process interface (DP-11), and ACE account data is read through the P1 rwb-source-data views or the owning service's own ACE views (DP-05). The intake parameters stay data rows (DP-06) and the document type and intake status lists are reference data read through the P3 reference-data contract (DP-07). The document events travel on `rwb.document.events.v1` through outbox and inbox with CloudEvents (DP-09); the topic carries the service name of the naming rule, and the legacy `rwb.p<n>.` names disappear with it. Each attach writes its `DOCATT` record locally in rwb_document and P7 rwb-decision collects it within five minutes (DP-03). The held-item list and the reviewer's attach use the P5 operations of the Ownership Map, `GET /review-items` and `POST /intake-items/{intakeItemId}/resolve`, and not the legacy `/attach` path. The screen is reached through gateway-bff (DP-19) but is not built or tested here.

This ITG story owns no legacy acceptance criterion. Legacy AC1 to AC15 sit at component level with RWB-P5-E1032-APP, and the access and the resilience criteria sit with the sibling APP stories RWB-P3-E1032-APP, RWB-P6-E1032-APP, RWB-S9-E1032-APP and RWB-P7-E1032-APP. The seventeen scenarios of section 7 are the integration proof across the five owners, and every value in them is a legacy value.

Two of the three intake sources are contracts of services that only exist in the target: the letter copy that P6 rwb-comms generates in `NoticeDispatchWorkflow` and the partner result file that S9 rwb-partner records from the partner gateway. They are why RWB-P6-E1032-APP and RWB-S9-E1032-APP sit in the chain. Without them only the scan path of P5 would be proved, AC4 would have no partner result to arrive on, and the letter copy would never become an intake item in the evidence.

Where the sources do not name the event that starts the workflow, the operation and version field that resolve a held item, the home of the three intake parameters in the target, or the exact P6 and S9 paths that feed the hub, the suite asserts through the owners' contracts and records the open point as `Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0356; ASM-0454)`.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P5-E1032-APP is done: intake, match, store, the held-item list and the resolve operation are in SIT on P5 rwb-document.
- RWB-S9-E1032-APP is done: the partner result file reaches the document hub from the partner gateway.
- RWB-P3-E1032-APP is done: the case directory contract returns a case by case number, the open cases of an account number, and the case read of the suite.
- RWB-P6-E1032-APP is done: the letter copy generated by P6 rwb-comms reaches the document hub as an intake item.
- RWB-P7-E1032-APP is done: the DOCATT records written locally in rwb_document are collected into the central ledger of P7 rwb-decision.
- The published contracts of P5, P3, P6, S9 and P7 are deployed under their own per-service bases behind gateway-bff.
- The harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG is available with its synthetic cases RW-2026-000123, RW-2026-000456 and RW-2026-000789, its accounts TEST-ACC-0001, TEST-ACC-0002 and TEST-ACC-0003, its synthetic users and its synthetic files.
- The parameters CASE_NO_PATTERN = "RW-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{6}", ACCOUNT_NO_PATTERN = "[0-9]{10}" (assumed; DL21) and CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD = 0.80 are loaded as data rows and read through the parameters contract of P3 rwb-case.
- The feature flag `rwb.dochub.autoattach` is on.
- The synthetic users, roles and scopes of section 10 are loaded: TEST-CO-01, TEST-LIT-01, TEST-LIT-02 and TEST-TM-01.
- No production data is used and no production connection is opened, and the release date 30 November 2026 is tentative; a date is not a precondition of this story.
- The story has no build dependency, so it is ready on Day 1 and waits only on its five integration dependencies.

##### 4. Flow

1. QA integration engineer: seeds the synthetic cases, accounts, users and files of the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG; no production data is used. Case RW-2026-000123 is open, owned by TEST-CO-01 and linked to TEST-ACC-0001; RW-2026-000456 is open and linked to TEST-ACC-0002; RW-2026-000789 is closed.
2. Harness: signs in as the synthetic users of section 10 through gateway-bff and holds their roles and scopes for the run.
3. Harness: stores the three intake sources — a scanned notice through POST /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents on P5 rwb-document, a partner result file through POST /api/recovery/partner/v1/partner/instructions/{instructionId}/results on the S9 partner gateway path, and a letter copy through POST /api/recovery/comms/v1/cases/{caseId}/notices on P6 rwb-comms — and reads the returned upload link, the instruction result and the notice.
4. Harness: waits on `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1`, `rwb.document.DocumentFieldsExtracted.v1` and `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` before it asserts any item, and records the elapsed time of each wait.
5. Harness: reads the documents of the case through GET /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents and asserts the type, source, confidence, review status and write-once flag of each, then reads the `DOCATT` entries through GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log and asserts the model version, the confidence, the match method, the approver where a person decided, and the five-minute collection.
6. Harness: reads the held items through GET /api/recovery/document/v1/review-items and each one through GET /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}, with the OCR text pages from the content path.
7. Harness: resolves the held items through POST /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/resolve as TEST-LIT-01 and TEST-LIT-02, at the item version read in the previous step, and asserts the stored document and the approver on the `DOCATT` entry.
8. Harness: runs the repeats and the negative cases — the same file twice, the repeat run over matched items, the closed case, the conflict, the unknown type, the case outside the scope, the type not in force, two reviewers at one version and the role without Documents C.
9. Harness: proves the decision-record failure path with the agreed test-only fault switch, restores the switch and the feature flag, writes the evidence report and removes the synthetic fixtures.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | No readable case ID or account number | The item is held with match_status NO_MATCH and the OCR text stays for a person | MSG-P5-003 | AC2 |
| X2 | The account number matches two or more open cases | The item is held with match_status MULTIPLE and every candidate is offered by GET /review-items | MSG-P5-003 | AC3 |
| X3 | The case ID and the account point to different cases | The item is held with match_status CONFLICT and both cases are offered | MSG-P5-003 | AC5 |
| X4 | A case ID is read that does not exist | No candidate is returned and the item has match_status NO_MATCH | MSG-P5-003 | AC6 |
| X5 | The only candidate case is closed | The item is held with match_status CASE_CLOSED; no document row is written | MSG-P5-003 | AC7 |
| X6 | The same file is already on the matched case | The item is linked to the existing document; no second document and no second entry | None | AC8 |
| X7 | The workflow runs again over the attached items | No second attach, entry or event is written | None | AC9 |
| X8 | The classification confidence is below the threshold and one case is matched | The document is stored with review_status PENDING and write_once false | MSG-P5-003 | AC10 |
| X9 | Classification returns no agreed type | The item is held with match_status NO_TYPE | MSG-P5-003 | AC11 |
| X10 | The reviewer picks a case outside the scope | Refused with status 403 and the item stays held | MSG-P4-003 | AC13 |
| X11 | The reviewer picks a type not in force | Refused with status 422 naming the type | MSG-P5-006 | AC14 |
| X12 | Two reviewers resolve the same item at the same version | The first call returns 201 and the second 409 | MSG-GEN-004 | AC15 |
| X13 | The decision record cannot be written during an attach | Nothing is stored; an automatic item stays PENDING for the next run; a manual call returns 503; an incident is raised (R-UNI-39) | MSG-P7-003 | AC17 |
| X14 | A role without Documents C resolves a held item | Refused with status 403 and the item stays held | MSG-P4-002 | AC16 |
| X15 | A consumed call exceeds the 2 s timeout or returns a server error | The call is retried once under the suite policy; the evidence report records the call and the response; no assertion is made on unverified data | None | AC1, AC12 |
| X16 | The fixture set does not match the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG expectations, or the classifier returns no fixture answer | The suite fails as a harness fault and names the element; no service defect is raised | None | AC1, AC4 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | The suite is its own module and reuses the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG; it needs the five APP stories and the published contracts of P5, P3, P6, S9 and P7, not their source code |
| Negotiable | The patterns, the threshold, the fixture sizes and the fault-switch mechanism are data rows or properties of the harness; the story fixes the assertions and the call set |
| Valuable | Attach without a person and the four held outcomes are proved on real services across five owners before wave 1 exits, not assumed from a unit test |
| Estimable | One suite module, one fixture pack of scans, a partner result and a letter copy, one item-version control, one decision-record assertion and one evidence report |
| Small | Seventeen scenarios over five services and one shared ledger topic; no service code and no schema change |
| Testable | Every scenario asserts a contract response, a stored document, a `DOCATT` entry, an event, a status or a message; all data is synthetic |

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A classified document attaches to its case without a person when exactly one open case is found | RWB-E1-032 BR1; REQ-DCM-007; FEAT-DCM-12 |
| BR2 | The case is found by the case ID or the account number read from the document; the account number is the join to other systems | RWB-E1-032 BR2; DL21; parameters CASE_NO_PATTERN and ACCOUNT_NO_PATTERN |
| BR3 | No match, more than one candidate, disagreement, a closed case or no agreed type goes to a person | RWB-E1-032 BR3; REQ-DCM-005; FSD P5 A2.12.4 |
| BR4 | A document classified below the threshold is stored for review in the standard container, not write-once, until a person confirms its type | RWB-E1-032 BR4; parameter CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD; RWB-E1-054; CTL-12 |
| BR5 | Each attach is written to the decision log with the classifier version, the confidence and the person where one decided, before the document is stored | RWB-E1-032 BR5; Principle 5; R-UNI-39; REQ-DRI-004 |
| BR6 | An item attached once is not attached again | RWB-E1-032 BR6; R-UNI-40 |
| BR7 | A reviewer attaches only to a case in their scope | RWB-E1-032 BR7; CTL-09 |
| BR8 | JOB-12 is an event-started DocumentIntakeWorkflow in P5 rwb-document with KEDA workers, not a Quartz job, and it runs no Schedule | DP-10; Architecture v5 slide 44; ASM-0454 |
| BR9 | Each attach writes its DOCATT decision record in rwb_document in the same transaction as the document and publishes it on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; P7 rwb-decision collects it within five minutes | DP-03; ADR-022; Architecture v5 slide 28 |
| BR10 | The intake parameters stay data rows read through the P3 parameters contract, and every cross-service call is one hop with a 2 s timeout | DP-06; DP-11; ADR-020; ASM-0456 |

##### 9. State transitions

None for the case status. This story changes no case status and reads the status only to prove the closed case of AC7. It changes the intake item match_status and creates the document record, both in P5 rwb_document. A held value becomes MATCHED when a reviewer resolves the item through the P5 resolve operation, and the suite reads every state through that contract and writes none of them itself.

| Object | State | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| document_intake | PENDING | The item holds OCR text, no document and a predicted type; the match step may pick it up |
| document_intake | MATCHED | The item is attached to one case and holds the document ID; a repeat run skips it |
| document_intake | NO_MATCH | No readable case ID and no readable account number, or a case ID that does not exist; the OCR text is held for a person |
| document_intake | MULTIPLE, CONFLICT | More than one open case was found for the account number, or the case ID and the account number point to different cases; every candidate is held |
| document_intake | CASE_CLOSED, NO_TYPE | The only candidate case is closed and no document row is written, or classification returned no agreed type; the item is held for a person |
| document | COPY_PENDING, STORED | The file is written to its container and the metadata is committed with the DOCATT record in one transaction; the file is then in its final place |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| QA integration engineer | Runs the suite, seeds the synthetic fixtures, reads the evidence report |
| SY-OCR, OCR and extraction pipeline | Matches and attaches automatically (Documents C) |
| SY-DECLOG, decision log writer | Writes the DOCATT record locally in rwb_document; P7 rwb-decision collects it |
| Roles with Documents C and the candidate case in scope (for example RW-LITOFF, RW-CASEOWN) | See and attach held items that name a candidate in their scope |
| Roles with Documents C and scope ALL (for example RW-LEGAL) | See and attach held items with no candidate |
| Roles with Documents R only (for example RW-TEAMMGR) | See attached documents on cases in their scope; no attach |

The synthetic users of the run are TEST-CO-01, TEST-LIT-01, TEST-LIT-02 and TEST-TM-01; no other role is in scope for this story.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The suite provides no REST operation. The names reserved for P2 rwb-integration — /api/recovery/integration/v1, rwb.integration.events.v1, rwb-integration and rwb_integration — are not used, and no rwb_integration table is written.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method and path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|
| POST /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents | P5 rwb-document | Store a synthetic scan on a case and read the returned upload link |
| GET /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents | P5 rwb-document | Read the documents of a case and the type, source, confidence, review status and write-once flag of each |
| GET /api/recovery/document/v1/review-items | P5 rwb-document | Read the held items and their candidates, oldest first |
| GET /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId} | P5 rwb-document | Read match_status, the candidates, the predicted type, the confidence and the version of the item |
| GET /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/content | P5 rwb-document | Read the file and the OCR text pages of a held item |
| POST /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/resolve | P5 rwb-document | Attach a held item to a case with a type and the item version, as the reviewer |
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId} | P3 rwb-case | Read the case, its status, its owner and its account |
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters | P3 rwb-case | Read CASE_NO_PATTERN, ACCOUNT_NO_PATTERN and CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD as data rows |
| POST /api/recovery/comms/v1/cases/{caseId}/notices | P6 rwb-comms | Request the letter copy that becomes an intake item |
| POST /api/recovery/partner/v1/partner/instructions/{instructionId}/results | S9 rwb-partner | Submit the partner result file on the partner gateway path |
| GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log | P7 rwb-decision | Read the DOCATT entries and the collection time against the five-minute target |

The resolve call carries the case, the type and the item version in its request; the exact version field and the held-item semantics are the open point recorded as `Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0356; ASM-0455)`. Every call is one hop with a 2 s timeout (ADR-020, DP-11).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The suite publishes no event; every event of the chain is published by its owning service through its own outbox.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Producer | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1 | rwb.document.events.v1 | P5 rwb-document | The document is stored; the suite waits for it before it asserts the item and the DOCATT entry |
| rwb.document.DocumentFieldsExtracted.v1 | rwb.document.events.v1 | P5 rwb-document | The case number and account number fields are extracted; the match step and the suite wait for it |
| rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1 | rwb.agent.events.v1 | P10 rwb-agent | The classify run behind the intake returned its answer; the suite asserts the type and confidence from the fixture |
| rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1 | rwb.comms.events.v1 | P6 rwb-comms | The letter copy is generated and becomes an intake item |
| rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1 | rwb.decision-record.v1 | P5 rwb-document, with the central ledger in P7 rwb-decision | The DOCATT record is collected into the ledger inside the five-minute target |

The suite consumes no other event and produces none. The P6 letter copy and the S9 partner result are the two intake sources that make RWB-P6-E1032-APP and RWB-S9-E1032-APP part of the chain (ASM-0457).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Workflow or activity | Owner | Task queue | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| DocumentIntakeWorkflow | P5 rwb-document | rwb-document | Holds the OCR step, the classify step, the extract step and the match step under test; started by the document event, not by a Schedule |
| AgentRunWorkflow | P10 rwb-agent | rwb-agent | Serves the classify run of the item: 60 seconds, then the rule result |
| NoticeDispatchWorkflow | P6 rwb-comms | rwb-comms | Generates the letter copy that becomes an intake item |

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. JOB-12 has no Schedule in the target: the workflow starts from `DocumentStored` and scales on KEDA workers (DP-10; Architecture v5 slide 44). The suite waits on no Schedule and moves no clock.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None (DP-01). document, document_intake, document_text, document_type and document_hub_parameter are P5 tables, decision_log_entry is written locally by P5 and held centrally by P7, and the suite owns no table and never reads another service's schema.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

None. Every call of section 12.2 goes to the real SIT service on its published wave 1 contract. The files are synthetic, and the classifier returns the fixture answers of the harness. AC17 uses the agreed test-only fault switch on the P5 decision-record write, agreed with the service owner, and it is the only intervention in a running service.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Provided by the suite | Consumed by the suite |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 | 11 |
| Kafka | 0 | 5 |
| Temporal | 0 | 3 observed |
| File | 0 | 0 |

##### 13. Solution plan

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Suite module for RWB-ITG-W1, reusing harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG | Integration suite | Runs the seventeen scenarios against SIT and holds no service code |
| Fixture pack | Test data | Synthetic scans, the partner result file and the P6 letter copy, with the three cases, the three accounts and the four synthetic users |
| Item-version control | Harness control | Reads the item version before a resolve and sends the same version twice for AC15, then restores the item |
| Decision-record assertion | Assertion | Reads the DOCATT entry of each attach, compares the model version, the confidence and the match method, and measures the collection time against the five-minute target |
| Evidence report | Report | Records per scenario the item ids, the document ids, the DOCATT entries, the events and their times, the statuses and the messages |

Decoupling patterns applied (Template and Rules v1 §R5.5):

|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | recovery.<table>, "recovery schema" | Owner's schema rwb_<name>; never read another service's tables | none | document, document_intake, document_text, document_type and document_hub_parameter stay in rwb_document under P5; the suite asserts through the P5, P3, P6, S9 and P7 contracts only |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic rwb.decision-record.v1 | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON | On RWB-P5-E1032-APP and RWB-P7-E1032-APP; this suite only waits for the collected record and measures the five minutes |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, v_ace_*, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none | On RWB-P3-E1032-APP and RWB-P5-E1032-APP for the account read; the suite never reads an ACE table |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON | On the APP stories; the three intake values stay data rows and are read through the P3 parameters contract (ASM-0456) |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON | On the APP stories for the document types and the intake status list; the suite sends the codes as data |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON | On RWB-P5-E1032-APP for DocumentStored and DocumentFieldsExtracted, on RWB-P6-E1032-APP for NoticeGenerated, and on every owner for DecisionRecorded; the suite consumes them |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON | JOB-12 becomes DocumentIntakeWorkflow on queue rwb-document, started from the document event and scaled on KEDA workers; the suite observes the run |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) | The eleven consumed REST operations of section 12.2 |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON | On RWB-P5-E1032-APP and RWB-P7-E1032-APP for the match columns and the local record; the suite changes no schema |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The suite enters through gateway-bff; SCR-31 and SCR-30 are not built or tested here |

The dependency-added column records the build dependency of the owning story. Those H and C dependencies belong to the owning APP stories, not to this suite; this story's H, C and X lists are exactly those of the metadata table — no H, no C and no X — and its I list is the five integration dependencies RWB-P5-E1032-APP, RWB-S9-E1032-APP, RWB-P3-E1032-APP, RWB-P6-E1032-APP and RWB-P7-E1032-APP. An ITG story waits on no build of its own.

Build steps:

1. Create the suite module next to harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG and wire it to the SIT endpoints of P5, P3, P6, S9 and P7 through gateway-bff.
2. Build the fixture pack: the three synthetic cases, the three accounts, the four synthetic users, the scans, the partner result file and the P6 letter copy, with the three parameters read as data rows through the P3 parameters contract.
3. Add the three intake sources: the scan through the P5 upload, the partner result through the S9 partner gateway path and the letter copy through the P6 notice request; assert that each becomes one intake item.
4. Implement AC1 to AC4 with the event waits on DocumentStored, DocumentFieldsExtracted and AgentRunCompleted and the contract reads of section 12.2.
5. Implement AC5 to AC9 and AC11: the two held outcomes with their candidates, the closed case, the unknown type, the duplicate file and the repeat run, and assert that no document row is written where the story says so.
6. Implement AC10 with the low-confidence fixture, the standard container and write_once false, and assert both candidates on the document for the review queue.
7. Implement AC12 to AC16 with the item-version control, the resolve operation, the two scopes, the type not in force and the role holding Documents R only.
8. Implement AC17 through the agreed test-only fault switch on the P5 decision-record write, assert the PENDING item, the 503 and the incident, restore the switch and the flag, then write the evidence report and run the suite in SIT against the wave 1 release candidate.

Done when: all seventeen test cases pass in SIT against the published wave 1 contracts of P5, P3, P6, S9 and P7, the evidence report shows for each item the document row, the DOCATT entry and the event that prove it, every DOCATT entry is collected into the ledger inside the five-minute target, and no service code or schema was changed by this story apart from the agreed test-only fault switch.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the case number and account number patterns and the classification threshold are data rows read through the parameters contract.
- No personal data in logs, events, evidence or fixtures: account numbers and OCR text are never logged; logs carry the intake item ID and the outcome; every test account and file is synthetic.
- No cross-service table read: cases, accounts, documents, notice copies, partner results and decision records are read through the owner's contract, and the suite owns no table.
- One hop and a 2 s timeout on every consumed call (ADR-020).
- The matcher never picks one of several candidates; any doubt goes to a person.
- A document stored for type review is never put in the write-once container before its type is confirmed (RWB-E1-054).
- The decision-record fault switch is test-only, agreed with the service owner, and restored at the end of the run.
- Synthetic data only, loaded by the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG; no production access of any kind from the suite or its configuration.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: search across cases moved into `rwb-document` with the schema `rwb_document`, the REST base `/api/recovery/document/v1`, the topic `rwb.document.events.v1` and the gateway-bff composite route; the case scope, the masking decision, the parameters, the reference lists, the access record and the migration are rebased on the target contracts and libraries. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **litigation officer (RW-LITOFF)**, I want **a search across all cases in my scope by document type, date range, extracted field and free text, with every search written to the access log**, so that **I find a document in seconds without opening cases one by one, and every look at personal data can be audited**.

Inside `rwb-document` this is the cross-case search capability of the document service:

- Service `rwb-document`, schema `rwb_document`, REST base `/api/recovery/document/v1`, topic `rwb.document.events.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document`. No Kafka event and no workflow is used by a search.
- One operation is provided, `GET /documents`, the cross-case search of TSD P5 API-P5-009 (12.1). It reads `document`, `document_field`, `document_text` and `document_type` in `rwb_document` and nothing outside it (DP01). `document_text` rows carry `document_id` once the intake item that produced them is attached, which RWB-P5-E1032-APP and RWB-P5-E1049-APP make true; a page of text that is still held in intake is not searchable across cases.
- The case scope (legacy `CaseDirectory.caseIdsInScope`) is one REST hop to `rwb-case`, and the masking decision (legacy `mayReadUnmasked`) is one REST hop to `rwb-access`; both are called with a fake and a 2 s timeout (DP11) and no case, account or role table of another service is read. Neither contract is in the Work Package contract rows, which are copied as they stand (GAP-2335; ASM-3884, ASM-3885).
- The four search parameters `SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS`, `SEARCH_PAGE_SIZE`, `FREE_TEXT_MIN_CHARS` and `FREE_TEXT_MAX_CHARS` arrive through the parameters contract and client library of `rwb-case` (DP06, H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, C RWB-P3-E1042-CON); the rows they resolve to are in `document_hub_parameter` in `rwb_document`, which the Ownership Map gives to P5. The document-type list and the other LOV lists arrive through the reference-data contract (DP07, H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, C RWB-P3-E1043-CON); the type table `document_type` itself is P5's own table and is read locally in the version in force (RWB-P5-E1025-APP).
- Each search is one append to the service's local decision-record chain through the DP03 library and one record on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, which `rwb-decision` collects into the central ledger; the free text term is carried as its SHA-256 hash. The record code of a search access event and the acknowledgement the request waits for are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2334; ASM-3882).
- The page is published by gateway-bff through the composite route of DP19 (H RWB-PLT-N001-CON), which asks this service one hop for what is on screen; the search indexes are one step in the per-service Flyway sequence (DP15, H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON).
- The database login is one per service (DP02) and its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2334; ASM-3882); this story uses the phrase "the rwb-document login" and never a shared login.

The legacy behaviour is carried unchanged: the same user story, rationale, preconditions, flow, exception paths, business rules, authority, data fields, ten acceptance criteria with their values, six messages and eleven test cases, rebased on the target service's schema, parameters, reference data and two contract hops.

##### 2. Business rationale

Legal, audit and recovery questions span many cases: every appraisal above a value, every notice from one court, every document naming a guarantor. Today each case folder is opened by hand (FSD P5 A2.6). This story searches the document index, the extracted fields and the OCR text across the cases the user may see, masks personal data the role may not see, and records each search. It meets REQ-DCM-001 (documents found by their type, date and extracted fields) and REQ-ACA-006 (every read of the document store written to the access log), under control CTL-09 and CTL-11, and it is the read that makes an audit population answerable at all (REQ-DCM-017, whose export is Epic 2).

The realignment changes the mechanics, not the business rule:

1. One schema, one base: the query runs in `rwb_document` over the four P5 tables and never over a `recovery.*` table or another service's schema (DP01). The legacy join to `recovery_case` for the scope and the case number becomes an answer on the `rwb-case` contract (DP11).
2. The in-process scope call `CaseDirectory.caseIdsInScope` becomes the case-list read of `rwb-case`, one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker, and the in-process masking call `mayReadUnmasked` becomes the authorise decision of `rwb-access` (DP11). Both are faked from Day 1, so the search builds before either service is ready.
3. The PII access log write becomes the local decision-record append of DP03 with the record published on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; the access log is held in the append-only decision log in the target (FEAT-ACA-08), the record is written in the request, and a search whose record is not acknowledged returns no row (AC9).
4. The parameters leave the code path and arrive through the parameters contract and client library of `rwb-case` (DP06). The rows stay in `document_hub_parameter` in this schema; the values are unchanged from the legacy story.
5. The LOV lists arrive through the reference-data contract (DP07); the type table and its field definitions are read locally in the version in force, so a field condition is always checked against the fields of the type table in force.
6. The legacy `V1_5_033__document_search_indexes.sql` becomes one step in the per-service Flyway sequence of `rwb_document` (DP15), with no baseline and no shared migration file.
7. The page is published to the browser by the gateway-bff composite route (DP19), which calls this service one hop; no screen chains calls to the case service or the access service, and the row opens the DocumentDetailPanel of RWB-P5-E1024-APP.

| Precondition | What it gives this story |

| RWB-PLT-E1042-CON | The parameters client library, so the four `SEARCH_*` values are read and never typed in code (DP06) |
| RWB-PLT-E1043-CON | The reference-data client library for LOV-DOC-TYPE and the other lists the criteria use (DP07) |

| RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The gateway-bff composite route that publishes the Document search page and asks this service one hop (DP19) |
| RWB-P5-E1024-APP | The store and index: `document` and `document_field` populated, active and versioned, with the case number on the row |
| RWB-P5-E1049-APP | The OCR pipeline: `document_text` populated for every read page and linked to the document once the intake item is attached |
| RWB-P5-E1053-CON | The extraction contract: the field names and values in `document_field` are the agreed ones, with their confidence |
| RWB-P3-E1042-CON | The parameters contract of `rwb-case`, read through the client library of DP06 |
| RWB-P3-E1043-CON | The reference-data contract of `rwb-case`, read through the client library of DP07 |

Business preconditions carried from RWB-E1-033, unchanged in value:

- Documents and extracted fields are in the index (RWB-P5-E1024-APP), OCR text is in `document_text` (RWB-P5-E1049-APP), and extracted fields carry names from the type table and a confidence (RWB-P5-E1053-CON).
- Masking rules loaded (DL26). Assumed until Compliance provides them: RW-LITOFF, RW-LEGAL and RW-AUDIT see party names in document text unmasked; every other role sees them masked.
- Parameters loaded in `document_hub_parameter`: SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS = 1000, SEARCH_PAGE_SIZE = 50, FREE_TEXT_MIN_CHARS = 3, FREE_TEXT_MAX_CHARS = 100 (assumed; DL11), read through the parameters contract of DP06.
- Every search is recorded in the append-only decision log and the append is acknowledged before a row is returned (FEAT-ACA-08; ASM-3882).
- The user holds Documents R and the case IDs of the search are in their scope. Feature flag `rwb.document.search` is on; the legacy flag `rwb.dochub.search` is retired with the monolith.

##### 4. Flow

1. Litigation officer: opens Document search from the Documents menu and enters a type, a stored date range, a field condition (field, operator, value) and or a free text term. The page is published by gateway-bff through the composite route of DP19; the browser calls `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents` once.
2. `DocumentSearchController`: accepts the criteria, applies the guard the service template holds, and passes the caller, the role codes and the criteria to the service.
3. `DocumentSearchService`: validates the criteria: at least one criterion, date order, free text length, field in the type's field list, operator in the allowed set (BR4, BR5).
4. `DocumentSearchService`: asks `rwb-access` through the authorise contract whether the role may search a personal field or free text (legacy `mayReadUnmasked`, field classes PARTY_NAME, ACCOUNT_NO, ID_NO); a refusal ends the request with 422 and MSG-P5-020, and no query runs. One hop, 2 s timeout, breaker (DP11).
5. `DocumentSearchService`: gets the case IDs in the caller's scope from the case-list read of `rwb-case` (legacy `caseIdsInScope`; the filter is empty for scope ALL), one hop, 2 s timeout, breaker (DP11). An empty answer returns the empty state and still records the search.
6. `DocumentSearchRepository`: one query over active `document` rows joined to `document_field` for the field condition and to `document_text` for the free text, newest stored date first, capped at SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS; the page is served at SEARCH_PAGE_SIZE. The case number is taken from the case answer of step 5, not from a case table.
7. `DocumentSearchService`: builds each row: case number, document type, stored date, source, the matched field or a text snippet of 60 characters with the term highlighted and other personal identifiers masked (BR2).
8. `DocumentSearchService`: appends the access record for the search through the decision-record library of DP03 (user, role, criteria with the free text term as a SHA-256 hash, result count, case IDs returned), waits for the acknowledgement, and only then returns the page; the record is published on `rwb.decision-record.v1` for the central ledger in `rwb-decision`.
9. Front end: shows the first page of 50 rows; the user opens a row in DocumentDetailPanel (RWB-P5-E1024-APP). A row is a metadata read of that document, recorded by the same rule.

The record is written before the rows are released, so no search is answered without its record (REQ-ACA-006; FEAT-ACA-08).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The role's masking rule hides party names and the user searches free text or a personal field | Refused with 422; nothing searched | MSG-P5-020 | AC4 |
| X2 | No criterion entered | Refused with 422 | MSG-GEN-001 | AC5 |
| X3 | Date from after date to | Refused with 422 | MSG-GEN-003 | AC6 |
| X4 | Free text shorter than 3 or longer than 100 characters | Refused with 422 | MSG-GEN-002 | AC7 |
| X5 | More than SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS documents match | The first 1000 by date are returned with a capped flag | MSG-P5-021 | AC8 |
| X6 | The access record is not confirmed | Results are not returned; 503 | MSG-P5-019 | AC9 |
| X7 | Nothing matches | Empty state | None | AC10 |
| X8 | A role without Documents R searches | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-033-11 (Access) |
| X9 | The `rwb-case` case-list read does not answer within 2 s or its breaker is open | Refused with 503; nothing searched and no record; the breaker shields the case service | MSG-GEN-006 (system "Case service") | TC-E1-033-02 (target path) |
| X10 | The `rwb-access` authorise read does not answer within 2 s or its breaker is open | Refused with 503; nothing searched; the masking decision is never assumed | MSG-GEN-006 (system "Access service") | TC-E1-033-04 (target path) |

Three target-service notes:

- A 503 on X9 or X10 is a refusal, not a partial answer: no criterion is evaluated in part, no row is returned and no access record is written, because nothing was read.
- A search refused at X1, X2, X3, X4 or X8 writes no access record: the append of step 8 happens only for a search that runs. The refusal itself stays in the request log of the shared edge, which is not this service's control.
- The access record of step 8 replaces the legacy PII access log call: the ACE common module still logs the request at the edge, but the search record is the append of DP03, which is what AC9 waits for (ASM-3882).

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the index (RWB-P5-E1024-APP), the OCR text (RWB-P5-E1049-APP), the extraction contract (RWB-P5-E1053-CON) and the two faked contract reads, all earlier or contract work |
| Negotiable | Limits, page size, text length and the masking rules are data; the criteria set can grow |
| Valuable | A cross-case question takes one search instead of opening each case |
| Estimable | One operation, one service, one query with three indexes, one page |
| Small | Fits within two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test case in section 16 |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Search across cases

  Background:
    Given 500 synthetic documents indexed across 120 cases
    Given 60 of them are "APPRAISAL_REPORT", 14 with appraised_value above 5,000,000, 9 of those stored in October 2026
    Given user "TEST-LIT-01" holds RW-LITOFF with scope ALL
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the 120 case IDs in the scope of "TEST-LIT-01" for scope ALL, with their case numbers
    Given the rwb-access contract mock returns that "RW-LITOFF" may read "PARTY_NAME" unmasked

  Scenario: AC1 Search by field (legacy RWB-E1-033 AC1)
    Given "TEST-LIT-01" is on the Document search page
    When "TEST-LIT-01" searches type "APPRAISAL_REPORT", field appraised_value greater than 5,000,000, stored from 1 October 2026 to 31 October 2026
    Then exactly the 9 matching documents list with case number, type, stored date and the field value
    Then the response arrives within 2 seconds

  Scenario: AC2 Role limit (legacy RWB-E1-033 AC2)
    Given user "TEST-LIT-02" holds RW-LITOFF with scope TEAM on team "MTG-BKK-LIT", whose cases are all product group "MORTGAGE"
    Given 40 of the 500 documents are on "HIRE_PURCHASE" cases
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case IDs in the scope of "TEST-LIT-02" for team "MTG-BKK-LIT" with product group "MORTGAGE"
    When "TEST-LIT-02" searches type "COURT_NOTICE" with no date
    Then no document on a "HIRE_PURCHASE" case appears
    Then the system writes one access event "DOCUMENT_SEARCH" with the user, the criteria, the result count and the case IDs returned

  Scenario: AC3 Free text (legacy RWB-E1-033 AC3)
    Given the OCR text of 3 documents holds the synthetic guarantor name "SYN GUARANTOR ONE"
    When "TEST-LIT-01" searches the free text "SYN GUARANTOR ONE"
    Then the 3 documents list with a snippet in which the name is highlighted
    Then the access event holds the SHA-256 hash of the term and not the term

  Scenario: AC4 Free text refused for a masked role (legacy RWB-E1-033 AC4)
    Given user "TEST-CO-01" holds RW-CASEOWN, whose masking rule hides party names
    Given the rwb-access contract mock returns that "RW-CASEOWN" may not read "PARTY_NAME" unmasked
    When "TEST-CO-01" searches the free text "SYN GUARANTOR"
    Then the system refuses the request with 422 and MSG-P5-020 naming "document text"
    Then no query runs

  Scenario: AC5 No criterion (legacy RWB-E1-033 AC5)
    Given "TEST-LIT-01" is on the Document search page
    When "TEST-LIT-01" searches with every criterion empty
    Then the system refuses the request with 422 and MSG-GEN-001 naming "a search criterion"

  Scenario: AC6 Date range in the wrong order (legacy RWB-E1-033 AC6)
    Given "TEST-LIT-01" is on the Document search page
    When "TEST-LIT-01" searches stored from 31 October 2026 to 1 October 2026
    Then the system refuses the request with 422 and MSG-GEN-003

  Scenario: AC7 Free text length boundary (legacy RWB-E1-033 AC7)
    Given "TEST-LIT-01" is on the Document search page
    When "TEST-LIT-01" searches the free text "ab" and then the free text "abc"
    Then the system refuses "ab" with 422 and MSG-GEN-002 showing 3 and 100
    Then "abc" runs

  Scenario: AC8 More results than the limit (legacy RWB-E1-033 AC8)
    Given 1,250 documents of type "DEMAND_LETTER" in the user's scope
    When "TEST-LIT-01" searches type "DEMAND_LETTER"
    Then the first page of 50 rows returns with total 1000 and capped true
    Then MSG-P5-021 shows with the count 1000

  Scenario: AC9 Access log not confirmed (legacy RWB-E1-033 AC9)
    Given the PII access log does not confirm writes
    When "TEST-LIT-01" searches type "COURT_NOTICE"
    Then the request returns 503 with MSG-P5-019
    Then the system returns no result row

  Scenario: AC10 Nothing matches (legacy RWB-E1-033 AC10)
    Given no document holds the free text "NO SUCH TEXT"
    When "TEST-LIT-01" searches it
    Then the page shows the empty state "No documents match this search." and the action "Clear the search"
    Then the access event records a result count of 0
```

Every Given, When and Then line above is the legacy line unchanged. The cross-service parts are mocked by the two added Background Givens on the `rwb-case` and `rwb-access` contracts and by the per-scenario Givens in AC2 and AC4. In AC9 the "PII access log" is the append of DP03 into the local decision-record chain: the request waits for the library's acknowledgement, and an unacknowledged append is the 503 the criterion fixes (ASM-3882).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Results hold only active documents on cases in the user's scope | CTL-09; FEAT-DCM-20 |
| BR2 | Personal fields and free text are searchable only by roles that see them unmasked; snippets mask other personal identifiers | CTL-11; DL26; masking rules reference table |
| BR3 | Every search is written to the access log before results are returned; a free text term is logged as a hash | REQ-ACA-006; CTL-11 |
| BR4 | Field conditions use the field names and data types of the type table in force | RWB-P5-E1025-APP; DL19 |
| BR5 | Result limit, page size and free text length are parameters | Document hub parameter table (New); DL11 |
| BR6 | The date criterion is the stored date of the document | FSD P5 A2.6 |

Target-service statements that make the rules hold in `rwb-document`:

- BR1 is executed in `rwb_document` by the `is_active` predicate on `document` and by the case-ID set of the case-list read; no case row is copied and no `rwb_case` table is read (DP01, DP11). A case that leaves the caller's scope stops matching on the next search, because the set is fetched per request and never cached across requests.
- BR2 is executed by the authorise decision of `rwb-access` before the query (DP11) and by `SnippetBuilder`, which masks every other identifier in the 60-character snippet; the masking rule set is versioned data, not code.
- BR3 is executed by the decision-record append of DP03 in the request path: the record is acknowledged before the page is released, the free text term is stored as its SHA-256 hash, and the record is published on `rwb.decision-record.v1` for the central ledger.
- BR4 is executed by reading `document_type` in the version in force (`valid_from`, `valid_to`) and by comparing the field condition with `field_definitions` (DF-REF-224) before any SQL is built; an unknown field is refused as a criterion error, not ignored.
- BR5 is executed by the parameters contract of DP06: the four `SEARCH_*` rows resolve in `document_hub_parameter`, and no limit, page size or length is a constant in the code.
- BR6 is executed on `document.created_at`, the stored date, with the range predicate on the `(case_id, document_type, created_at)` index that RWB-P5-E1024-APP created.
- DP07 keeps the type and other lists in reference data; DP15 puts the three search indexes in one step of the service's sequence; DP19 puts the page behind the composite route, so the screen never calls `rwb-case` or `rwb-access` itself.

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status and writes no document record. In the target it performs one append to the local decision-record chain:

| From | Event | To |
|---|---|---|
| (no entry) | a search runs and the append is acknowledged | one access record on the chain, replicated to `rwb.decision-record.v1` |
| (no entry) | the append is not acknowledged | no record; 503 with MSG-P5-019 and no row |
| (no entry) | the search is refused before the query (X1 to X4, X8) | no record; the refusal is a validation answer |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer | Searches by type, date, field and free text in their scope |
| RW-LEGAL, legal counsel; RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Search across all cases (scope ALL); free text allowed under the assumed masking rule |
| RW-COMPLY, compliance and PDPA officer | Searches by type, date and non-personal fields; reads the access log |
| Other roles with Documents R | Search by type, date and non-personal fields in their scope |
| RW-CAPACITY and other roles without Documents R | No search |
| SY-DOCUMENT, the service identity | Runs the query and appends the access record; it searches no case outside the set the case-list read returns |

The authorisation decision is taken by `rwb-access` (roles, scope, masking and DoA as data) and consumed as the authorise answer of DP11; the command-level guard of the service template checks the Documents right R before the criteria are read, and a scope answer that omits a case is the only thing that keeps the case out of the result. The recovery access guard is not built here: the story inherits the guard library the service template carries. The database login is one per service (DP02) and its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2334; ASM-3882).
