No `rwb_case` row is copied, no ACE view is read and no foreign schema is queried (DP01): DF-CAS-001 and DF-CAS-002 arrive inside the case-list answer. Personal data never enters the record payload, the log or the event; the free text term is a SHA-256 hash and a snippet in a response is masked for every identifier but the matched term.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

| Operation | Path | Owner | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents` | P5 | The cross-case search of TSD P5 API-P5-009. Query: `type` (doc type code), `dateFrom`, `dateTo` (date), `field`, `op` (eq, gt, lt, between), `value`, `value2`, `q` (free text, 3 to 100 characters), `page`, `size` (default 50, maximum 50). Response 200 DocumentSearchPage: items [documentId, caseId, caseNo, documentType, storedAt, source, matchedField, matchedValue, snippet], page, size, total, capped. Errors 401; 403 no Documents R (MSG-P4-002); 422 no criterion (MSG-GEN-001), date order (MSG-GEN-003), text length (MSG-GEN-002), personal field or free text not allowed (MSG-P5-020); 503 record not acknowledged (MSG-P5-019) or a contract downstream unavailable (MSG-GEN-006). Authorisation: Documents, right R, scope applied. No `Idempotency-Key`: each call writes its own access record |

The parameter names above are the legacy Request row of RWB-E1-033 section 12; the page bounds beyond `size` maximum 50 and the behaviour of `page` beyond the cap are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2334; ASM-3882). The operation is carried into the service's contract document; this story builds it.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Path | Owner | Story | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases` | P3 rwb-case | RWB-P3-E1018-CON | The case IDs in the caller's scope with their case numbers (legacy `caseIdsInScope` and `caseNumbers`); one hop, 2 s timeout, breaker per downstream (DP11). Consumed and faked although it is in no C row of this Work Package (GAP-2335; ASM-3884) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | RWB-P4-E1037-CON | The masking decision for a role and a field class (legacy `mayReadUnmasked`); one hop, 2 s timeout, breaker (DP11). Consumed and faked although it is in no C row of this Work Package (GAP-2335; ASM-3885) |

The scope filter parameter names of the case-list read are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2334; ASM-3884). The four parameters and the LOV lists are not REST operations of this story: they are read through the parameters and reference-data client libraries of DP06 and DP07, which wrap RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON. The document type table is a P5 table read locally.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Key | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| access record of a search | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | PLT library, consumed by P7 | the caller reference (a search spans cases) | record code, role codes, criteria with the free text term as its SHA-256 hash, result count, case IDs returned, decidedAt |

CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, binary mode; no personal data in the payload. The record is appended in the request path and published by the DP03 library, so it exists exactly when a search is answered; a failed append answers 503 and releases no row.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. This story consumes no Kafka event. `DocumentStored` (EV-16) and the intake events (EV-17) are consumed by other paths of this service and by `rwb-case`; the search reads committed rows only, in its own schema.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. A search is a synchronous read and starts no workflow and no activity. `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` on queue `rwb-document` is RWB-P5-E1049-APP's and is untouched here; `document_text` reaches the search through that workflow's output, which is why this story depends on it.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Schedule is owned or started by this story; the indexes are created by a migration, not by a job.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|
| `document` | P5 | Read only: active rows with type, source, stored date and case |
| `document_field` | P5 | Read only: the field condition and the matched value |
| `document_text` | P5 | Read only: the free text and the snippet |
| `document_type` | P5 | Read only: the field definitions and the version in force |
| `document_hub_parameter` | P5 | Read only: the four `SEARCH_*` rows behind the parameters contract |
| decision-record library table | PLT library, created in `rwb_document` | The access record appended per search |

No table of another service is read (DP01) and no ACE view is read by this service. No table is created by this story, only indexes (section 13).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Story | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-case case-list fake | RWB-P3-E1018-CON | The scope set for AC1, AC2, AC7, AC8 and AC10, the empty set, the 2 s timeout and the open breaker (X9) |
| rwb-access authorise fake | RWB-P4-E1037-CON | The masking answer of AC3 and AC4, the refusal, the timeout and the open breaker (X10) |
| reference-data fake | RWB-P3-E1043-CON (through RWB-PLT-E1043-CON) | LOV-DOC-TYPE and the lists the criteria use |
| parameters fake | RWB-P3-E1042-CON (through RWB-PLT-E1042-CON) | SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS, SEARCH_PAGE_SIZE, FREE_TEXT_MIN_CHARS, FREE_TEXT_MAX_CHARS |
| decision-record fake | RWB-PLT-E1027-CON | The acknowledged and the unacknowledged append (AC9) and the record content of AC2 and AC3 |
| gateway-bff composite route fake | RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The page states of section 15 and the one-hop call |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count in this story | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | Provided 1, consumed 2 | The search; the `rwb-case` case-list read and the `rwb-access` authorise decision |
| Kafka | Published 1 decision record; consumed 0 | `rwb.decision-record.v1`; no business topic of this service is published or consumed |
| Temporal | 0 | No workflow, no Schedule, no activity |
| File | 0 | A snippet and metadata travel in the response body; no file is opened by a search |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document`, module `document/search`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| DocumentSearchController | Controller | The one operation of 12.1; criteria binding, the Documents right R, RFC 9457 problems with the message ID |
| DocumentSearchService | Service | Validation, masking check, scope, query orchestration, row building, access record and its acknowledgement |
| DocumentSearchRepository | Repository | One query over `document`, `document_field` and `document_text` in `rwb_document`, with paging and the cap |
| SnippetBuilder | Service | 60-character snippet, term highlight and the masking of every other identifier through the authorise answer |
| CaseScopeClient | Client | The case-list read of `rwb-case`: the case IDs in scope and their numbers, on the request, 2 s timeout, breaker |
| AccessDecisionClient | Client | The authorise read of `rwb-access` for a role and a field class, cached per request, 2 s timeout, breaker |
| SearchParameters | Library client | Reads the four `SEARCH_*` values through the parameters contract of `rwb-case`, cached 5 minutes |
| DocumentSearchPage | React component | Criteria form, result table with paging, the capped banner, the empty and error states |

**Database.** One step in the per-service Flyway sequence (DP15), `V1033_1__document_search_indexes.sql`:

- `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;` and `ix_document_text_trgm` on `document_text` using gin (`text_content` `gin_trgm_ops`).
- `dochub_to_numeric(text)` returning numeric or null, and `ix_document_field_name_num` on `document_field` (`field_name`, `dochub_to_numeric(field_value))`.
- `ix_document_field_name_value` on `document_field` (`field_name`, `field_value`).
- No table and no column is added; the case/type/date index `ix_document_case_type_created` comes from RWB-P5-E1024-APP and is reused. No extension or index is created in another schema.

**Configuration and reference data.**

- SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS = 1000, SEARCH_PAGE_SIZE = 50, FREE_TEXT_MIN_CHARS = 3, FREE_TEXT_MAX_CHARS = 100 in `document_hub_parameter`, assumed (DL11), read through the parameters contract of DP06.
- Masking rules (DL26), assumed as the legacy story states them, held as versioned data of the access service; this service holds no masking rule.
- Document type table version in force with the field definitions of the six types (RWB-P5-E1025-APP); LOV-DOC-TYPE through the reference-data contract of DP07.
- Feature flag `rwb.document.search`. Off: the operation returns 404 with a feature-off problem and the menu item is hidden.

**Build steps**

1. Write the migration and test that Thai free text is found through the trigram index on the legacy 500-document set.
2. Build criteria validation: at least one criterion, date order, text length, field in the type's field list, operator set; unit test AC5, AC6, AC7.
3. Build `AccessDecisionClient` against its fake and the masking check; test AC4 and the timeout path X10.
4. Build `CaseScopeClient` against its fake, the scope ALL path and the empty set; test X9 and the empty-scope state.
5. Build the query with scope, paging, cap and newest-first order; integration test AC1, AC2 and AC8 on the 500-document set with the two fakes.
6. Build `SnippetBuilder`; test AC3 with the synthetic Thai and Latin names.
7. Add the access record with the SHA-256 hash and the acknowledgement wait; test AC9 and the record content of AC2 and AC3.
8. Build DocumentSearchPage on the composite route with the states of section 15; component tests, AC10, and the SIT performance run of AC1.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-01 moves the four tables the legacy query joined into `rwb_document` and removes the `recovery_case` join: the scope and the case number now arrive on the case-list read, which is DP-11's REST-with-mock shape. DP-03 replaces the write to the ACE common PII access log with the local append and the shared decision-record topic, so the record, the query answer and the 503 of AC9 have one source. DP-06 and DP-07 keep four parameters and the lists out of the code, while `document_hub_parameter` and `document_type` stay P5's own tables. DP-11 covers both legacy in-process calls, each with a fake and a 2 s timeout, and adds the two C rows the Work Package does not list. DP-15 puts the three indexes in one step of the service's own sequence. DP-19 puts the page behind the composite route, so the browser makes one call and the screen chains nothing.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, AC1 answers within 2 seconds at the 95th percentile over 50 runs in SIT, a Thai free text term is found through the trigram index, and every answered search has exactly one access record on `rwb.decision-record.v1` with no term and no personal data in it.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | No criterion | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-002 | Free text length outside 3 to 100 | {field} must be between {min} and {max}. |
| MSG-GEN-003 | Date from after date to | {field} cannot be before {other}. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A contract downstream does not answer or its breaker is open | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P5-019 | Access record not acknowledged | The search was not run because it could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P5-020 | Role may not search personal data | Your role cannot search on {field} because it holds personal data. |
| MSG-P5-021 | Results above the limit | More than {count} documents match. Narrow the search to see them all. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

HTTP mapping unchanged from the legacy contract: 422 for MSG-GEN-001, MSG-GEN-002, MSG-GEN-003 and MSG-P5-020; 403 for MSG-P4-002; 503 for MSG-P5-019 and MSG-GEN-006. For MSG-GEN-006 the {system} value is "Case service" for X9 and "Access service" for X10. Every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId`, `detail` with the placeholders filled and `instance`; MSG-P5-021 is a banner on a 200 answer, not an error. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

The screen ID of "search across cases" is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2334; ASM-3882); `screens.txt` holds none and the legacy story records the same absence. The page Document search under the Documents menu is published through the gateway-bff composite route of DP19 (RWB-PLT-N001-CON), which asks `rwb-document` one hop for what is on screen.

| State | What the user sees |
|---|---|
| Loading | Skeleton rows while the search runs; the criteria stay enabled |
| Result list | Case number, document type, stored date, source and the matched field or the 60-character snippet with the term highlighted |
| Capped | The first SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS rows with the MSG-P5-021 banner and the count 1000, plus the paging control |
| Empty | "No documents match this search." with the action "Clear the search" (labels.txt) |
| Error | The section 14 message at the top of the form, with the criterion preserved so it can be corrected |
| Refused | 403 with MSG-P4-002 when Documents R is missing; 422 on the criteria when the role may not search a personal field |

A row opens DocumentDetailPanel (RWB-P5-E1024-APP), which is a second one-hop call from the same composite route.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: result limit, page size, free text length, the masking rule set, the LOV lists and the type fields are data rows or parameters.
- No personal data in logs, events, records or tests: the free text term is stored as a SHA-256 hash, snippets mask every identifier but the match, and every test name is synthetic.
- No read of another service's tables (DP01). The scope and case numbers come from the `rwb-case` case-list read and the masking decision from `rwb-access`, each one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker; this service reads no ACE view.
- A result is never returned before its access record is acknowledged, and an unacknowledged record answers 503 with no row (REQ-ACA-006).
- The query is built from the type table in force and from bound parameters only; no criterion string is concatenated into SQL, and the field name is checked against `field_definitions` first.
- Scope is fetched per request and never cached across callers; a page is capped at SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS so a wide search cannot drain the service.
- The feature flag `rwb.document.search` removes the capability without a schema rollback; the three indexes stay valid and harmless when it is off.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: moved from RWB-E1-034 to rwb-comms, with the five template administration operations on base `/api/recovery/comms/v1` and the screen behind gateway-bff. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **litigation officer (RW-LITOFF)**, I want **a screen to upload a template version, have Legal counsel record the approval and set it current**, so that **templates are managed without a developer**.

##### 2. Business rationale

A template change today needs a person outside Legal to edit a file and send it round, and nothing records which wording was approved. This story gives the litigation officer an upload and Legal counsel an approve and withdraw action on SCR-33 Template approval, with the approver and date held on the version. It serves REQ-OCC-002 and control CTL-14 (every notice from the current Legal-approved version), and removes the developer from template changes.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-046 is done: the template and merge_field tables, the load checks and the TemplateCatalog interface exist.
- RWB-E1-015 is done: the freshness stamp shows on screens that read data products.
- The merge field catalog is loaded, with codes "CASE_NO", "CUSTOMER_NAME", "POSTAL_ADDRESS", "TOTAL_OUTSTANDING" and "NOTICE_DATE" in the synthetic set.
- The uploader holds RW-LITOFF or RW-LEGAL (Documents C); the approver holds RW-LEGAL (Documents A).
- The ACE storage pattern with a write-once container is available for template bodies (DL27).

##### 4. Flow

1. Litigation officer: opens SCR-33 Template approval and chooses the template code and language, or a new code.
2. Litigation officer: uploads the DOCX body and enters product group, channel, notice type, signature basis and the merge codes used.
3. System: checks the role (Documents C), the required fields, the file type and size, and every merge code against the catalog (MergeCodeScanner from RWB-E1-046).
4. System: stores the body write-once, creates the next version number in state Draft and shows it in the list.
5. Legal counsel: opens the Draft version, reads the body and the merge codes, enters the valid from date and approves.
6. System: checks the role (Documents A), that the approver is not the uploader (CTL-05), that the version is Draft and that valid from is not before today; sets state Approved with approver and approval time.
7. System: from valid from, TemplateCatalog returns this version as current; earlier Approved versions stay readable on SCR-33.
8. Legal counsel: may withdraw an Approved version with a reason; the system sets state Withdrawn and generation for that code and language holds (R-LIT-04).
9. System: writes every upload, approval and withdrawal to the ACE audit log with the user, the version and the time.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Set current is chosen on a version with no approver | Refused; the version stays Draft | MSG-P6-005 | AC2 |
| X2 | The uploader of a version tries to approve it | Refused; the version stays Draft | MSG-P7-002 | AC3 |
| X3 | The body uses a merge code not in the catalog | Upload refused; nothing stored | MSG-P6-006 | AC4 |
| X4 | Template code or language is empty | Upload refused | MSG-GEN-001 | AC5 |
| X5 | The file is not a DOCX file | Upload refused | MSG-P6-010 | AC6 |
| X6 | Valid from is before today | Approval refused | MSG-GEN-003 | AC7 |
| X7 | Legal withdraws the current version | Version Withdrawn; generation holds | MSG-P6-003 | AC8 |
| X8 | Two approvers act on the same version at once | The first wins; the second is refused | MSG-GEN-004 | AC9 |
| X9 | Approve is sent twice with the same Idempotency-Key | The second returns the first result; nothing changes | None | AC10 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the catalog (RWB-E1-046) only; generation (RWB-E1-052) is separate |
| Negotiable | Layout of SCR-33 follows the ACE components (DL08, DL31); the behavior is fixed here |
| Valuable | Legal approves wording in the Workbench, and the approval is on the version |
| Estimable | Five endpoints, one screen with three states |
| Small | Fits in two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion is an API or screen test with synthetic templates |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

  Scenario: AC10 Repeated approval request (legacy RWB-E1-034 AC10)
    Given "LEG-0001" approved version 3 with Idempotency-Key "7f1c0d2e-0001"
    When the same request is sent again with Idempotency-Key "7f1c0d2e-0001"
    Then the response is the first response with status 200
    Then the audit log holds one approval for version 3
```

The ten criteria are the legacy scenarios AC1 to AC10 of RWB-E1-034, copied word for word with their values, IDs, statuses and messages, and each carries its origin tag. No Given line is added and no legacy line is changed. `TemplateCatalog` is the legacy name of the current-version read that this story serves behind the five operations of section 12.1, and the exception name `TemplateWithdrawnException` is carried on MSG-P6-003.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Only an Approved version with an approver and approval time can become current | REQ-OCC-002; CTL-14 |
| BR2 | The person who uploaded a version cannot approve it | CTL-05; roles.txt separation of duty |
| BR3 | Approval needs Documents A, held by Legal counsel | roles.txt permission matrix; DL28 |
| BR4 | Every merge code in the body is in the merge field catalog in force | RWB-E1-046 BR4; Principle 1 |
| BR5 | Valid from is today or later | MSG-GEN-003 rule; refdata.txt change process, step 5 |
| BR6 | A withdrawn version holds generation until a new version is approved; no fallback to an earlier version | R-LIT-04, R-LIT-06 |
| BR7 | Template bodies are stored write-once; a change is a new version | CTL-12; DL27 |
| BR8 | Allowed body file types are a configuration list, DOCX in Epic 1 | Principle 1 |

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-comms (P6); base `/api/recovery/comms/v1` (DP-13). The five operations are the TSD P6 appendix T-A.1 rows API-P6-003 to API-P6-007 re-based on the per-service base, with the purpose, request and answer, errors, authorization and idempotency of the T-A.2 rows.

| Method | Path | API ID | Purpose | Request and answer | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/admin/templates` | API-P6-003 | List template versions by code, language and state | Query: code, language, state, page, size; answer 200 `TemplatePage` of `Template` | Documents, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| POST | `/admin/templates` | API-P6-004 | Upload a new template version in state Draft | Multipart: file, templateCode, language, productGroup, channel, noticeType, signatureBasis, mergeCodes; answer 201 `Template` in state DRAFT | Documents, right C, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header |
| GET | `/admin/templates/{templateId}/content` | API-P6-005 | Download a template body | None; answer 200 `application/octet-stream` | Documents, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| POST | `/admin/templates/{templateId}/approve` | API-P6-006 | Record the Legal approval of a Draft version with its valid-from date | `TemplateApproval`: validFrom; answer 200 `Template` in state APPROVED | Documents, right A, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header |
| POST | `/admin/templates/{templateId}/withdraw` | API-P6-007 | Withdraw an Approved version with a reason | `TemplateWithdrawal`: reason; answer 200 `Template` in state WITHDRAWN | Documents, right A, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header |

The error statuses per operation are the legacy ones and agree with T-A.2: 401, 403, 503 on the list; 401, 403 (MSG-P4-002), 413, 415 (MSG-P6-010), 422 (MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P6-006), 503 (MSG-GEN-006) on the upload; 401, 403, 404, 503 on the content read; 401, 403 (MSG-P4-002), 404, 409 not Draft (MSG-P3-005), changed (MSG-GEN-004), own upload (MSG-P7-002), 422 (MSG-GEN-003), 503 on the approve; 401, 403, 404, 409 not Approved (MSG-P3-005), 422 reason empty (MSG-GEN-001), 503 on the withdraw. Every error uses the platform error envelope with the `Problem` schema and one message ID of section 14.

`Template` schema: id, templateCode, templateVersion, language, productGroup, channel, noticeType, signatureBasis, mergeCodes, state, approvedBy, approvedAt, validFrom, createdBy, createdAt, version. 409 MSG-GEN-004 is raised from the optimistic lock on the standard column `version`.

**Legacy names.** The legacy story declares the same five operations on the legacy base path (DP-13) as `GET /templates`, `POST /templates`, `GET /templates/{templateId}/content`, `POST /templates/{templateId}/approve` and `POST /templates/{templateId}/withdraw`. The target names them `/admin/templates`, `/admin/templates/{templateId}/content`, `/admin/templates/{templateId}/approve` and `/admin/templates/{templateId}/withdraw` on `/api/recovery/comms/v1`, as TSD P6 T-A.1 gives them. The disagreement between the legacy story and the TSD is carried as a gap and an assumption; the TSD name wins on source precedence and the legacy names are kept only as a record `Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1137; ASM-2084)`.

**Set current.** Legacy AC2 names an action "set current", and the target has no such operation: none of the five operations sets a version current. The current version of a template code and language on a date is the Approved version with the latest valid from on or before that date, and the rule that makes it current is `Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1138; ASM-2085)`. AC2 is kept word for word and its refusal is served by the approve operation on a Draft version with no Legal approval, which answers 422 with MSG-P6-005 and leaves the version Draft.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 rwb-case | Read LOV-LANG, LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-NOTICE, LOV-CHANNEL and LOV-SIGNATURE-BASIS of TSD P6 T3.2 at the version in force (DP-07, RWB-P3-E1043-CON) |
| GET | the freshness read of RWB-P1-E1015-CON | P1 rwb-source-data | The freshness stamp SCR-33 shows beside the template rows; its path and its answer are fixed by that contract and are not restated here |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (DP-07). A read that does not answer refuses the upload or the approval with MSG-GEN-006 naming the system that failed; no version is created or approved on a partial answer. No list value and no stamp is written in code.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The event catalogue names no template event on `rwb.comms.events.v1`, so this story publishes none and invents none: `rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1`, `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1` and `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1` belong to the generation and dispatch stories of this service. An upload, an approval and a withdrawal are synchronous answers, written to the service log and the ACE audit entry.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. No topic is subscribed by this story; the reference-data read and the freshness read of section 12.2 are synchronous answers. A change to a list reaches the screen on its next read.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The five operations are synchronous REST calls in the caller's thread; this story starts no workflow, registers no activity and holds nothing on task queue `rwb-comms` in namespace `rwb-recovery`.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Schedule and no cron entry is registered by this story; JOB-10 WIN notices belongs to the dispatch stories and JOB-11 is the platform outbox relay.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| template | P6 (`rwb_comms`) | The template versions, their state and their Legal approval record; written by the upload, approve and withdraw operations and read by the list and content operations |
| merge_field | P6 (`rwb_comms`) | The merge codes of the catalog version in force; read only by the upload check (BR4) |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_comms` | The `idempotency_key` row of each POST and the envelope objects of the service; this story writes the idempotency row only and no outbox event |

`lov_value`, `reference_row` and `reference_version` are P3 rwb-case's and are read only through the reference-data contract of 12.2 (DP-07). `document`, `document_custody`, `document_text`, `document_type` and `document_checklist_item` are P5 rwb-document's, `recovery_case`, `task` and `timer` are P3's, `decision_log_entry` is P7's and `interaction` is P1's; they are named as consumed answers only and never read or written here (DP-01).

The template body is the claim-check file named by `body_ref` (DF-REF-050). Whether the object behind that reference is held by P5 rwb-document or by this service's own Blob container is `Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1140; ASM-2087)`; either way only the reference is a row of this service and the body is never a row and never a log line.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-case reference-data fake (RWB-P3-E1043-CON) | `GET /admin/lists/{listCode}` answers LOV-LANG "TH" and "EN"; LOV-PRODUCT "MORTGAGE", "HIRE_PURCHASE", "SSME" and "UNSECURED"; LOV-NOTICE "DEMAND", "RECALL", "STATUTORY_SALE_NOTICE" and "GUARANTOR_NOTICE"; LOV-CHANNEL "MOBILE", "HOME_PHONE", "WORK_PHONE", "LINE", "EMAIL", "POSTAL_ADDRESS", "CALL", "VISIT", "SMS", "LETTER", "PORTAL" and "BRANCH"; LOV-SIGNATURE-BASIS "E_SIGNATURE_ALLOWED" and "WET_INK_REQUIRED" | App story, contract tests |
| rwb-source-data freshness fake (RWB-P1-E1015-CON) | A fresh stamp for the business date and a stale stamp beyond it | App story, contract tests |
| template fixture pack | DEMAND-MTG "TH" version 2 Approved by "LEG-0001" with valid from 2026-11-01; the DEMAND-MTG "TH" version 3 body `demand-mtg-th-v3.docx`; RECALL-SSME "TH" version 4 uploaded by "LEG-0001"; a DEMAND-HP "TH" body using "LINE_ID"; `demand.pdf`; an upload with no template code | App story, contract tests |
| merge-field catalog fixture, version "MF-2026.11" | Rows for merge codes "CASE_NO", "CUSTOMER_NAME", "POSTAL_ADDRESS", "TOTAL_OUTSTANDING" and "NOTICE_DATE", with catalog version "MF-2026.11" and its valid-from date | App story, contract tests |

The two consumed fakes answer the paths of section 12.2 with the values above, so the story builds and its tests run before rwb-case and rwb-source-data are live. The template fixture pack is the synthetic material of section 7 and of section 16; it carries synthetic wording only.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 5 provided, 2 consumed | The five template administration operations of 12.1 provided; the reference-data read and the freshness read of 12.2 consumed; one hop, 2 s |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.comms`, module `template`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.comms.template`; the front end module sits in the ACE front end behind the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The legacy folders `recovery/comms/templates` of the monolith are replaced by this package.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/comms/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| TemplateAdminController | Controller | The five operations of 12.1; maps every error to the `Problem` answer and the message ID of section 14 |
| TemplateAdminService | Service | Upload, approve and withdraw; applies BR1 to BR8; writes the ACE audit entry |
| TemplateRepository | Repository | From RWB-P6-E1046-APP; reads and writes `template` in `rwb_comms`; carries the optimistic lock on `version` |
| TemplateBodyStore | Service | Stores the body write-once and returns `body_ref`; the container is the open point of 12.7 (GAP-1140) |
| MergeCodeScanner | Service | From RWB-P6-E1046-APP; reads every `{{CODE}}` of the body and checks it against the catalog version in force (BR4) |
| ReferenceCatalog | Service | Reads the five LOV lists of 12.2 through the reference-data client (DP-07) |
| TemplateApprovalScreen | React component | SCR-33: list by code and language, version detail, upload form, approve and withdraw dialogs, the Loading and Error states |

**Database and migrations.** `template` and `merge_field` live in schema `rwb_comms` with the rwb-comms login (DP-01). This story adds no table and no migration: it reads and writes `template` with the columns of section 11 and reads `merge_field`, both created by RWB-P6-E1046-APP in the per-service Flyway sequence of `rwb_comms`. The unique constraint `uk_template_version` on `template_code`, `language` and `template_version` stops a duplicate version number; version numbers are assigned inside a transaction with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the highest version of the code and language.

**Configuration and reference data.** The property `rwb.comms.template.allowed-types` = DOCX and the property `rwb.comms.template.max-size-mb` = 10 are marked assumed in the legacy text, and no source fixes the list or the limit: the two values are `Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1139; ASM-2086)`. Both are read as configuration, never written in Java (BR8); the allowed list drives MSG-P6-010. The merge field catalog is loaded by the reference data administrator through RWB-P6-E1046-APP (DL11). The five lists of 12.2 arrive on the reference-data contract at the version in force (DP-07). The feature switch is `rwb.comms.template-admin` (legacy name kept): off means the five operations answer 503 with MSG-GEN-006 and nothing is stored.

**Platform rows**

| Platform element | What this story uses it for |
|---|---|
| Error envelope and `Problem` schema | Every error answer of 12.1, one message ID per condition |
| `idempotency_key` store in `rwb_comms` | The `Idempotency-Key` of the three POSTs and the stored first answer (AC10) |
| gateway-bff composite route (RWB-PLT-N001-CON) | SCR-33 and its Draft, Approved and Withdrawn states, read and acted on through one route (DP-19) |
| Reference-data client (RWB-PLT-E1043-CON) | The five LOV lists of 12.2, with one hop and a 2 s budget (DP-07) |
| Freshness read of RWB-P1-E1015-CON | The freshness stamp SCR-33 shows beside the rows that read data products |
| ACE audit entry | The upload, approval and withdrawal entry with the user, the version and the time; never a body and never a merge value |

**Build steps**

1. Add the `Template`, `TemplatePage`, `TemplateApproval` and `TemplateWithdrawal` schemas to the OpenAPI file of `/api/recovery/comms/v1` and generate the controller interface.
2. Build the upload path with the type, size, required field and merge code checks; test AC1 (upload part), AC4, AC5, AC6.
3. Build TemplateBodyStore with write-once storage; test that a second write to the same ref is refused.
4. Build approve with the role, self-approval, state and valid from checks; test AC1, AC2, AC3, AC7.
5. Add the optimistic lock and the Idempotency-Key store; test AC9 and AC10.
6. Build withdraw; test AC8.
7. Build SCR-33 with states Draft, Approved and Withdrawn, the common Loading and Error states, and the MSG texts in English and Thai; browser test of the upload and approve path through the gateway-bff route.
8. Run the contract test of section 16 over the five operations and their error answers.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.comms.template-admin`.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, SCR-33 shows only the actions the signed-in role holds, and no template body and no merge value appears in a log of the run.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P6-005 | Set current on a version with no Legal approval | {template} version {version} has no Legal approval. It cannot be used. |
| MSG-P7-002 | The uploader approves their own version | You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it. |
| MSG-P6-006 | A merge code is not in the catalog | {template} uses the merge field {field}, which is not in the merge field catalog. The load was refused. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field is empty | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P6-010 | The body file type is not allowed | This template file type cannot be loaded. Use {types}. |
| MSG-GEN-003 | Valid from is before today | {field} cannot be before {other}. |
| MSG-P6-003 | A withdrawn template is asked for | The {template} template has been withdrawn. The notice is on hold until Legal approves a new version. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | Another person changed the version first | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P3-005 | Approve on a version that is not Draft, or withdraw on one that is not Approved | This case cannot move to {state} from {current}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-33 Template approval (module P6, capability area Documents). screens.txt lists it as first in E2; this story builds it in Epic 1 behind its flag.

| State | What the user sees and does |
|---|---|
| Draft | The litigation officer sees the uploaded version, its merge codes and the body preview. Legal counsel sees Approve with a valid from date |
| Approved | Everyone with Documents R sees the version, approver, approval time and valid from. Legal counsel sees Withdraw |
| Withdrawn | The version shows its withdrawal reason; no action is offered |

The common states Loading and Error apply (screens.txt, common states).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: file types, size limit, merge codes and the template list are data or configuration.
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts. Template bodies in tests carry synthetic wording; the audit entry holds user IDs, template code and version only.
- No read of another module's tables. Roles come from the ACE access check; storage through the ACE storage pattern.
- A stored body is never overwritten; a correction is a new version.
- The screen hides actions the role does not hold, and the server checks the right on every call.

##### 1. Story

As a **QA integration engineer**, I want **the end-to-end proof of the RWB-E1-034 letter template management on P6 rwb-comms — upload, approve, set current, withdraw and the merge-code, file-type and self-approval refusals — with the freshness stamp of the reference data product read from P1 rwb-source-data**, so that **Legal approval of letter wording and its effect are proved on the real wave 1 services with no change to the built behaviour**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story is recorded as Moved (no impact). Its five operations, its three version states and its ten messages are unchanged in the target, and they change owner and base only. The template and merge_field tables belong to P6 rwb-comms (Ownership Map rows template and merge_field, both P6), the five operations are served under `/api/recovery/comms/v1` instead of the monolith base (DP-13), and SCR-33 Template approval is reached through gateway-bff (DP-19). Nothing in the built behaviour moves, so this story is proof and not rework.

One element of the story crosses a service boundary. The reference data behind the screen is shown with the freshness stamp that P1 rwb-source-data keeps for its data products (RWB-E1-015; RWB-P1-E1015-APP), and that stamp is read through the P1 data product contract. The merge field catalog itself is P6's own table set (DP-07), and the template body stays in the P6 schema with a write-once store (DP-01), so no other service reads a comms table.

The split is as follows. This ITG story owns no legacy acceptance criterion. Legacy AC1 to AC10 sit at component level with RWB-P6-E1034-APP, which builds the upload, the approval, the set-current rule, the withdrawal and the four refusals inside P6 rwb-comms. This story proves the same behaviour through the published P6 contract, adds AC11 for the role refusal at the contract edge and AC12 for the freshness stamp of the reference data product, and adds nothing to the built behaviour.

No service contract is faked. Every call goes to the real SIT service under its published wave 1 contract. Where the sources do not name the moved base and the route of the five operations, the suite asserts through the P6 contract and records the open point as Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0357; ASM-0458). The same holds for the composite route of SCR-33 through gateway-bff (GAP-0357; ASM-0459), for the data product whose stamp the catalog shows (GAP-0357; ASM-0460) and for the point at which a withdrawal holds generation (GAP-0357; ASM-0461).

The measure is unchanged from the legacy story: it serves REQ-OCC-002 and control CTL-14, because every notice is produced from the current Legal-approved version. It removes the developer from template changes and keeps the approver and the approval date on the version.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P6-E1034-APP is done: the five operations, the three version states and the ten messages run on P6 rwb-comms and are in SIT.
- RWB-P1-E1015-APP is done: the freshness stamp per data product is published and deployed on P1 rwb-source-data.
- The P6 and P1 contracts are deployed under their per-service bases behind gateway-bff.
- The harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG is available with its synthetic templates and its synthetic users.
- The merge field catalog is loaded with codes "CASE_NO", "CUSTOMER_NAME", "POSTAL_ADDRESS", "TOTAL_OUTSTANDING" and "NOTICE_DATE".
- Synthetic users hold RW-LITOFF and RW-LEGAL; the approver of a version holds RW-LEGAL with Documents A.
- The write-once storage for template bodies is available in SIT (DL27), and the allowed file-type list carries DOCX.
- The template DEMAND-MTG in language TH has version 2 Approved by "LEG-0001" with valid from 2026-11-01, and the suite clock reads 2026-11-20.
- No production data is used, no production copy is loaded and no production connection is opened.
- The release date 30 November 2026 is tentative; a date is not a condition of this story.
- This story has no build dependency, so it is ready on Day 1.

##### 4. Flow

1. QA integration engineer: seeds the synthetic templates and users of the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG; no production data is used.
2. Harness: signs in as "LIT-0101" holding RW-LITOFF and as "LEG-0001" holding RW-LEGAL through gateway-bff.
3. Harness: reads the template list with GET /api/recovery/comms/v1/admin/templates and asserts version 2 of "DEMAND-MTG" "TH" as current with approver "LEG-0001".
4. Harness: uploads "demand-mtg-th-v3.docx" with POST /api/recovery/comms/v1/admin/templates using merge codes "CASE_NO" and "TOTAL_OUTSTANDING", and reads the new version in state Draft.
5. Harness: reads the body with GET /api/recovery/comms/v1/admin/templates/{templateId}/content and asserts the stored body and its merge codes.
6. Harness: approves version 3 with POST /api/recovery/comms/v1/admin/templates/{templateId}/approve and valid from 2026-11-20, then reads the list and asserts version 3 as current and version 2 still readable.
7. Harness: withdraws version 3 with POST /api/recovery/comms/v1/admin/templates/{templateId}/withdraw and reason "Wording under review", and reads the list again.
8. Harness: runs the negative cases — set current with no approver, self-approval, an unknown merge code, an empty code, a PDF, valid from in the past, two approvals within the same second and a repeated approval.
9. Harness: reads GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness and checks the stamp shown for the reference product of the template catalog against the value the template list carries.
10. Harness: writes the evidence report with each status, message, version number and state.
11. Harness: removes the synthetic fixtures and restores the clock.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Set current is chosen on a version with no approver | Refused; the version stays Draft and the earlier version stays current | MSG-P6-005 | AC2 |
| X2 | The uploader of a version tries to approve it | Refused with 409; the version stays Draft | MSG-P7-002 | AC3 |
| X3 | The body uses a merge code not in the catalog | Upload refused with 422; no version is created and no file is stored | MSG-P6-006 | AC4 |
| X4 | The template code is empty | Upload refused with 422; nothing is created | MSG-GEN-001 | AC5 |
| X5 | The file is not a DOCX file | Upload refused with 415; nothing is stored | MSG-P6-010 | AC6 |
| X6 | Valid from is before today | Approval refused with 422; the version stays Draft | MSG-GEN-003 | AC7 |
| X7 | Legal counsel withdraws the current version | The version moves to Withdrawn, the code and language have no current version and generation holds | MSG-P6-003 | AC8 |
| X8 | Two approvers act on the same version at once | The first wins; the second is refused with 409 and the version keeps one approval | MSG-GEN-004 | AC9 |
| X9 | Approve is sent twice with the same Idempotency-Key | The first response returns with 200 and one approval stays on the record | None | AC10 |
| X10 | A consumed call exceeds the 2 s timeout or returns a server error | The call is retried once under the suite policy; the evidence report records the call and the response; no assertion is made on unverified data | None | AC1, AC8, AC12 |
| X11 | The fixture set does not match the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG expectations, or the clock control cannot move the date | The suite fails as a harness fault and names the element; no service defect is raised | None | AC1, AC9 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | The suite is its own module and reuses the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG; it needs the two APP stories and the published contracts of P6 and P1, not their source code |
| Negotiable | The template codes, languages, merge codes, file names and dates are fixture data; the story fixes the assertions and the call set |
| Valuable | Legal approval of letter wording and the freshness of the reference data are proved on the real services before wave 1 exits, with no change to the built behaviour |
| Estimable | One suite module, one template fixture pack, one state and version reader, one freshness reader and one evidence report |
| Small | Twelve scenarios over two services; no service code and no schema change |
| Testable | Every scenario asserts a contract response, a version number, a version state or a message; all data is synthetic |

  Scenario: AC4 An unknown merge code is refused at upload (new, D-RCV-60)

```

**Target reading.** No scenario of this story is new behaviour. AC1 to AC10 repeat the legacy wording through the P6 contract, which is why every one of them carries the origin tag of this run and no legacy tag. AC11 reads the role check at the contract edge, and AC12 is the only cross-service line: the stamp comes from the P1 contract and the template list carries the same value. The data product whose stamp the catalog shows is not named in the source documents (GAP-0357; ASM-0460).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Only an Approved version with an approver and approval time can become current | RWB-E1-034 BR1; REQ-OCC-002; CTL-14 |
| BR2 | The person who uploaded a version cannot approve it | RWB-E1-034 BR2; CTL-05; roles.txt separation of duty |
| BR3 | Approval needs Documents A, held by Legal counsel | RWB-E1-034 BR3; roles.txt permission matrix; DL28 |
| BR4 | Every merge code in the body is in the merge field catalog in force | RWB-E1-034 BR4; RWB-E1-046 BR4; Principle 1 |
| BR5 | Valid from is today or later | RWB-E1-034 BR5; MSG-GEN-003 rule; refdata.txt change process, step 5 |
| BR6 | A withdrawn version holds generation until a new version is approved, with no fallback to an earlier version | RWB-E1-034 BR6; R-LIT-04, R-LIT-06 |
| BR7 | Template bodies are stored write-once; a change is a new version | RWB-E1-034 BR7; CTL-12; DL27 |
| BR8 | Allowed body file types are a configuration list, DOCX in Epic 1 | RWB-E1-034 BR8; Principle 1 |
| BR9 | The five operations keep their request, response and message shapes on P6 rwb-comms under `/api/recovery/comms/v1`, and no monolith path is called | DP-13; ASM-0458 |
| BR10 | The freshness stamp is read from the P1 data product contract and shown with the reference data on SCR-33 | RWB-E1-015; DP-07; ASM-0460 |

The behaviour of BR1 to BR8 is built by RWB-P6-E1034-APP. This story asserts it through the contract and changes none of it.

##### 9. State transitions

None for the case status. This story does not change a case status. It observes the template version state moving through the legacy table:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | Upload | Checks pass | Draft |
| Draft | Approve | Approver is Legal counsel and not the uploader; valid from today or later | Approved |
| Approved | Withdraw | Reason entered | Withdrawn |

A withdrawn version leaves no current version for its code and language, and generation for that code and language holds until a new version is approved (R-LIT-04, R-LIT-06). The point at which the hold is enforced is not named in the source documents (GAP-0357; ASM-0461); the suite asserts the state through the P6 contract and leaves the hold to RWB-P6-E1034-APP and RWB-E1-052.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| QA integration engineer | Runs the suite, seeds the synthetic templates and users, reads the evidence report |
| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer | Uploads a version (Documents C) and reads templates (Documents R); is refused set current and approve |
| RW-LEGAL, Legal counsel | Uploads, approves and withdraws a version (Documents CRUA); cannot approve an own upload |
| Other roles with Documents R, for example the case owner and the team manager | Read templates and the current version |
| RW-COMPLY, Compliance and PDPA officer | Reads templates (Documents R) |

No approval level from the delegation of authority applies; Legal approval of wording is a Documents A right. No other role is in scope for this story.

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |

| DF-REF-045 to DF-REF-051 | template (P6 rwb-comms) | id, template_code, template_version, language, product_group, body_ref, approved_by_legal | Read through the P6 contract |
| DF-REF-063 to DF-REF-069 | template (P6 rwb-comms) | approved_by, approved_at, valid_from, channel, notice_type, signature_basis, merge_codes | Read through the P6 contract |

The legacy story writes every template field from the upload path. In the target the write happens inside P6 rwb-comms, and the suite reads the same fields back through the five P6 operations; it never reads a schema and it never writes a template row. Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary, taken from the field list of the legacy story. Every body in the suite carries synthetic wording and no personal data.

The data product whose stamp the catalog carries is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0357; ASM-0460); the fixture names one product of the P1 set and the assertion compares the contract value with the value the template list shows.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The suite provides no REST operation. The names reserved for P2 rwb-integration — `/api/recovery/integration/v1`, `rwb.integration.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-integration` and schema `rwb_integration` — are not used, and no `rwb_integration` table is written.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method and path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|
| GET /api/recovery/comms/v1/admin/templates | P6 rwb-comms | Read the template versions, their state and the current version for a code and language |
| POST /api/recovery/comms/v1/admin/templates | P6 rwb-comms | Upload a body with its template code, language, product group, channel, notice type, signature basis and merge codes |
| GET /api/recovery/comms/v1/admin/templates/{templateId}/content | P6 rwb-comms | Read the stored body and its merge codes |
| POST /api/recovery/comms/v1/admin/templates/{templateId}/approve | P6 rwb-comms | Approve a version with valid from, and repeat the call with Idempotency-Key "7f1c0d2e-0001" |
| POST /api/recovery/comms/v1/admin/templates/{templateId}/withdraw | P6 rwb-comms | Withdraw a version with a reason |
| GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness | P1 rwb-source-data | Read the freshness stamp of the reference data product |

Every call is one hop on the owner's base with a 2 s timeout (ADR-020, DP-11). No monolith path is called (DP-13). The exact base and route of the five operations are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0357; ASM-0458); the suite reads them from the P6 contract in the registry.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The suite publishes no event.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. No event is produced or consumed by this story. Notice generation and its `NoticeGenerated` event belong to RWB-E1-052, and this story neither triggers nor waits for one.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. No workflow, activity or Nexus operation is started or awaited; the five operations and the freshness read are synchronous REST calls.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Schedule is started, moved or waited for, and no shared scheduler table is read.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The suite owns no table. template and merge_field belong to P6 rwb-comms and data_product and data_product_load belong to P1 rwb-source-data; the suite never reads either schema (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

None. Every call in section 12.2 goes to the real SIT service under its published wave 1 contract. The write-once body store and the pattern of the template file are P6's and are not stubbed. The freshness value is a synthetic P1 load of the harness data set, read back through the P1 contract; it is not a stub of the P1 contract.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Provided by the suite | Consumed by the suite |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 | 6 |
| Kafka | 0 | 0 |
| Temporal | 0 | 0 |
| File | 0 | 0 |

##### 13. Solution plan

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Suite module for RWB-ITG-W1, reusing harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG | Integration suite | Runs the twelve scenarios against SIT and holds no service code |
| Template fixture pack | Test data | The synthetic bodies for "DEMAND-MTG", "DEMAND-HP" and "RECALL-SSME" in language "TH", "demand-mtg-th-v3.docx", "demand.pdf" and the body with no template code |
| State and version reader | Assertion | Reads the list, the body, the approval and the withdrawal through the P6 contract and compares state, approver, approval time and current version |
| Freshness reader | Assertion | Reads GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness and compares the stamp with the value the template list carries |
| Evidence report | Report | Records per scenario the status, the message, the version number, the state and the stamp of the run |

Decoupling patterns applied (Template and Rules v1 §R5.5):

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added | Where it sits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | recovery.<table>, "recovery schema" | Owner's schema rwb_<name>; never read another service's tables | none | template, merge_field and the body reference sit in rwb_comms; data_product and data_product_load sit in rwb_source_data; the suite asserts through contracts only |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case; reference data held as rows, not code | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON | The merge field catalog is P6's own row set read through the P6 contract; the lists a role sees come from P3; on the APP stories, not a build dependency of the suite |
| DP-13 | /api/recovery/v1 | /api/recovery/<short>/v1 | none | The five comms paths of section 12.2 |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The suite enters through gateway-bff and reads the same template list and stamp the screen shows; no screen is built here |

The dependency-added column records the build dependency of the owning story. The H and C dependencies in the table belong to the owning APP stories and to the platform contract stories, not to this suite. The H, C, I and X lists of this story are exactly the metadata rows: no H, no C, no X, and the two I dependencies RWB-P1-E1015-APP and RWB-P6-E1034-APP. An ITG story waits on no build of its own.

Build steps:

1. Create the suite module next to harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG and wire it to the SIT bases of P6 rwb-comms and P1 rwb-source-data through gateway-bff.
2. Build the template fixture pack with synthetic wording, and assert that no fixture holds a personal value.
3. Implement the state and version reader over the five P6 operations, with the current-version rule read on 2026-11-20.
4. Implement AC1 to AC10 in TC order: the upload, the body read, the approval, the list, the withdrawal and the eight refusals, and assert every status and every message.
5. Implement AC11 through the contract edge and AC12 through the freshness read, then compare the stamp with the value the template list carries.
6. Write the evidence report, remove the fixtures and run the suite in SIT against the wave 1 release candidate.

Done when: all twelve test cases pass in SIT against the published wave 1 contracts of P6 rwb-comms and P1 rwb-source-data, the five operations answer with their legacy request, response and message shapes, no monolith path is called, and no service code or schema was changed by this story.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P6-005 | Set current on a version with no Legal approval | {template} version {version} has no Legal approval. It cannot be used. |
| MSG-P7-002 | The uploader approves their own version | You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it. |
| MSG-P6-006 | A merge code is not in the catalog | {template} uses the merge field {field}, which is not in the merge field catalog. The load was refused. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field is empty | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P6-010 | The body file type is not allowed | This template file type cannot be loaded. Use {types}. |
| MSG-GEN-003 | Valid from is before today | {field} cannot be before {other}. |
| MSG-P6-003 | A withdrawn template is asked for | The {template} template has been withdrawn. The notice is on hold until Legal approves a new version. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | Another person changed the version first | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P3-005 | Approve on a version that is not Draft, or withdraw on one that is not Approved | This case cannot move to {state} from {current}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The message IDs and wording are copied from RWB-E1-034. No new message ID is added by this story. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-33 Template approval, capability area Documents, is read in this story and not built or tested. The suite reads the same state through the P6 contract.

| State | What the user sees and does |
|---|---|
| Draft | The litigation officer sees the uploaded version, its merge codes and the body preview; Legal counsel sees Approve with a valid from date |
| Approved | Everyone with Documents R sees the version, approver, approval time and valid from; Legal counsel sees Withdraw |
| Withdrawn | The version shows its withdrawal reason; no action is offered |

The common states Loading and Error apply. The freshness stamp is shown above the list, and the suite compares the value it reads from the P1 contract with the value the template list carries on that path. The composite route of SCR-33 through gateway-bff is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0357; ASM-0459); the suite reads the list and the stamp through gateway-bff and takes no screenshot.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the file types, the size limit, the merge codes, the template list and the case names are data or configuration, read through the owner's contract.
- No personal data in logs, evidence or fixtures: the synthetic bodies carry no customer name, account number or address value, and the evidence report holds user IDs, template codes and version numbers only.
- No cross-service table read: every assertion goes through the owner's contract, and the suite owns no table (DP-01).
- One hop and a 2 s timeout on every call (ADR-020).
- A stored body is never overwritten; a correction is a new version, and the suite asserts that the earlier version stays readable.
- The screen hides actions the role does not hold, and the server checks the right on every call; AC11 reads that check at the contract edge.
- Synthetic data only, loaded by the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG.
- No production access of any kind from the suite or its configuration.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-035 for rwb-case. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As **TechX (any team may pick up this story)**, I want **the v1.1 timeline contract of rwb-case: the item shape with its type, summary, actor and reference plus the transfer detail fields, the paged envelope with the total, the per-section state that lets one failed source degrade one section, and the nine contract tables**, so that **rwb-case, gateway-bff and the three owner services build the timeline panel against one published document on Day 1**.

The document is an additive minor version of the timeline operation first published by RWB-P3-E1023-CON: same path, same query parameters, same status codes, one new item shape, one new section state, one new page field. Nothing in the baseline is removed or renamed, so no consumer has to change (ASM-3636).

This story fixes the shape the APP story builds against and generates its fakes. It carries no build dependency and is Day-1 work.

##### 2. Business rationale

The timeline is the only screen of the case record that merges four owners at once: rwb-case for the assignments, transfers and state, rwb-decision for the decision records, rwb-source-data for the contact ledger, rwb-document for the documents. Unless the merge shape, the order rule inputs, the actor field, the transfer detail and the partial-failure behaviour are fixed before the panel work starts, each caller invents a different item and the merge in gateway-bff breaks at every change.

The legacy contract carried the whole timeline in one class with a `by` string and no section state, because one module read four of its own tables. In the target three of the four sources are another service's contract, so the item must say what it could not read and the page must say which section failed. That is the whole change: a section state on the page, and the transfer detail fields the legacy story added for RWB-E2-016.

The document fixes no business value: the type order, the section timeout and the labels are named as parameters and reference data of rwb-case, so a change is data, not a new version.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service naming of Template and Rules §R4 is fixed for rwb-case: schema `rwb_case`, REST base `/api/recovery/case/v1`, topic `rwb.case.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`.
- The baseline of RWB-P3-E1023-CON is published: the timeline path, the query parameters `type`, `from`, `to`, `page` and `size`, the status codes and the shared error envelope.
- The legacy contract of RWB-E1-035 §12 and endpoint API-P3-003 of TSD P3 v3 Appendix T-A are the source of the operation and the item fields.
- The decision-record query of C RWB-P7-E1027-CON is named as the hook that fills the decision items. Its path and its field list are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2211; ASM-3635).
- The interaction read and the paging of the ledger are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0695; ASM-1242).
- The rwb-case login (DP-02) will exist with SELECT on schema `rwb_case`. The login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0692; ASM-1239).
- No build dependency. Day 1.

##### 4. Flow

1. TechX: takes the operation, the item fields and the detail fields from §12.1 and the legacy contract, and names the operation `getCaseTimeline`.
2. TechX: writes the `TimelineItem`, `TimelinePage` and `TimelineSection` schemas and keeps every baseline field name unchanged.
3. TechX: fixes the actor rule: `by` carries either a person reference or a rule ID with its version, and `actorType` says which.
4. TechX: fixes the section state: one entry per section with its state and, when failed, the MSG code; the page stays 200.
5. TechX: names the parameter and reference sources for the type order, the timeout, the page size and the labels, and fixes none of their values.
6. TechX: runs the OpenAPI 3.1 validator, the compatibility check against the baseline checksum and the contract linter.
7. TechX: generates the fakes of 12.8 and publishes them with the checksum to RWB-P3-E1035-APP and gateway-bff.
8. TechX: records the acknowledgements of gateway-bff, rwb-decision, rwb-source-data and rwb-document against the checksum.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A field of the item has no source value | The document carries the placeholder Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2211; ASM-3635) for the decision-record query and (GAP-0695; ASM-1242) for the ledger read; no value is invented | None | AC2, AC4 |
| X2 | The document removes or renames a baseline field | The compatibility check against the RWB-P3-E1023-CON checksum fails and the document is not published | None | AC5 |
| X3 | The document declares a write operation on the timeline path | The linter fails and the document is not published | None | AC5 |
| X4 | The section state is modelled as an error response | The linter fails: a failed section is a 200 with a section state, never a 4xx or 5xx for one source | None | AC3 |
| X5 | A consumer builds against a superseded checksum | The consumer fails the compatibility check against the published checksum | None | AC5 |
| X6 | The rwb-document or rwb-decision contract changes shape after publication | A new minor version is raised and the hook is re-pointed; the APP story is not changed in place | None | AC2, AC6 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency and no table; it fixes the shape the panel and the edge build against |
| Negotiable | Schema names and field order are design choices; no business value is fixed here |
| Valuable | One published item and section shape removes the guesswork from the panel, the edge and the three clients |
| Estimable | One document, one operation, three schemas, one section state, five fakes |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its contract tests |
| Testable | The document is the test object; every criterion is checked by a linter or a contract test |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Case timeline contract v1.1

  Background:
    Given the baseline timeline contract of rwb-case published by RWB-P3-E1023-CON with its checksum

  Scenario: AC1 The v1.1 document for the timeline operation (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the OpenAPI 3.1 document is generated from the timeline baseline
    When the document is validated with an OpenAPI 3.1 validator and the contract linter
    Then it validates with no error
    Then it declares GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timeline with operationId getCaseTimeline
    Then the operation carries the query parameters type, from, to, page and size, the 200 response, the error responses and the Case record R security requirement

  Scenario: AC2 The item and page schemas (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the document is published with version v1.1
    When a consumer resolves TimelineItem
    Then it holds at, type, summary, by, actorType, reference and the transfer detail fields reasonCode, fromQueueCode, toQueueCode and ruleId
    Then actorType distinguishes a person from a rule, and a rule item carries its ruleId and the rule version in by
    Then TimelinePage holds the items, the page, the size and the total of the merged set
    Then every baseline field of RWB-P3-E1023-CON is present with the same name and type

  Scenario: AC3 The partial-result section state (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the document is published

    Then no field of a failed section carries an invented value

    Then the timeline path carries GET only and no POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE appears

  Scenario: AC6 The nine contract tables and the consumed hooks (new, D-RCV-60)

```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| CB1 | The document follows OpenAPI 3.1 and the naming of Template and Rules §R4: base `/api/recovery/case/v1`, schema `rwb_case`, topic `rwb.case.events.v1`, queue `rwb-case`, package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case` | R4; ADR-020 |
| CB2 | The document is additive over the RWB-P3-E1023-CON baseline: no field is removed or renamed, and the version 1.1 is a minor version inside major version 1 | ADR-020; §R8.2 |
| CB3 | One item shape serves every type; the type is a coded value and the order between types is a parameter, never a field of the schema | BR1 of RWB-P3-E1035-APP; DP-06 |
| CB4 | A failed section is data in a 200 response, never an error status; the section entry names the section and the MSG code | MSG-P3-023; §R7.2 s14 |
| CB5 | Every personal field of a contact item names its masking hook, and the operation states Case record R and the scope filter | CTL-09; the authorise guard of the service template |
| CB6 | The document fixes no business value: the order, the timeout, the page size and the labels are named as parameters and reference data of rwb-case | DP-06; DP-07 |
| CB7 | Every value a source does not give is a placeholder with its gap and assumption, never an invented value | Template and Rules §R9; GAP-2211 |

##### 11. Data

The document fixes shapes, not values. The schemas carry these fields, with the field IDs of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v7:

| Block | Fields | Table or contract behind it | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| item | at, type, summary, by, actorType, reference, reasonCode, fromQueueCode, toQueueCode, ruleId | assignment and decision record, or the ledger, document and decision hooks | P3, P1, P5, P7 |
| item, assignment and transfer | assignee, assignedAt, endedAt, reason, ruleId, queueCode, transferReasonCode (DF-WRK-012 to DF-WRK-016, DF-WRK-039, DF-WRK-040) | assignment, queue | P3 |
| item, decision | decisionCode, ruleId, ruleVersion, approverUserId, finalCall, decidedAt (DF-DEC-003 to DF-DEC-005, DF-DEC-010, DF-DEC-012, DF-DEC-016) | the rwb-decision decision-record query | P7 |
| item, contact | occurredAt, channel, direction, contactResult, summary (DF-INT-004 to DF-INT-011) | the rwb-source-data interaction read | P1 |
| item, document | documentId, documentType, source (DF-DOC-001, DF-DOC-004, DF-DOC-005) | the rwb-document documents-by-case operation | P5 |
| page | items, page, size, total, sections | composed in rwb-case | P3 |
| section | name, state, messageCode | composed in rwb-case from the section outcomes | P3 |

No row is read or written by this story. The item field names of the legacy contract of RWB-E1-035 §12 (`at`, `type`, `summary`, `by`, `reference` and the added `reasonCode`, `fromQueueCode`, `toQueueCode`, `ruleId`) are kept unchanged.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

| Operation | operationId | Request | Response | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timeline | getCaseTimeline | Path caseId; query type, from, to, page, size | TimelinePage: items[], page, size, total, sections[] | 400, 401, 403, 404, 503 |

`TimelineItem` holds `at`, `type`, `summary`, `by`, `actorType`, `reference`, `reasonCode`, `fromQueueCode`, `toQueueCode` and `ruleId`; `TimelineSection` holds `name`, `state` (ok, failed, empty) and `messageCode`. The type order, the section timeout and the page size are parameters of rwb-case and the document fixes none of their values (AC4). Every operation states Case record R and scope applied.

| The interaction read of the rwb-source-data contract (DP-18) | rwb-source-data (P1) | The contact items. Path and paging Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0695; ASM-1242) |

| POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise | rwb-access (P4) | The scope hook of the operation |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** The document is held with the service contract of rwb-case, under Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`; it is the input to the code generator of the platform contract library.

**Deliverables**

| Deliverable | Content |
|---|---|
| OpenAPI 3.1 document v1.1 | The timeline operation, the three schemas, the security scheme and the shared error envelope |
| Compatibility baseline | The RWB-P3-E1023-CON checksum and the additive-diff report |
| Contract linter rules | Read-only rule, additive-only fields, the section state as a 200, the nine tables present |
| Fakes | The rwb-case timeline fake plus the four fakes of 12.8 |
| Checksum register | The published document with its checksum and the four consumer acknowledgements |

**Pattern application**

| DP code | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-18 | Interaction ledger | Ledger owned by rwb-source-data (default ruling) | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

As a CON story it carries no build dependency: the H rows above are the pattern rows of the vehicle, recorded here for the trace, and they are taken by the APP story that builds.

**Build steps**

1. Fix the operation and the operationId from 12.1; diff every field against the baseline document.
2. Write `TimelineItem`, `TimelinePage` and `TimelineSection`; check every field name against section 11 and the legacy contract.
3. Add the actor rule, the transfer detail fields and the section state; add the masking hook to every contact item field.
4. Name the parameter and reference sources and fix no value.
5. Fix version v1.1, the media type, the identifier format and the read-only rule.
6. Run the validator, the linter and the additive compatibility check; a removed baseline field or a write operation fails the build.
7. Generate the fakes of 12.8 and publish them with the checksum.
8. Collect the gateway-bff, rwb-decision, rwb-source-data and rwb-document acknowledgements.

**Done when.** The document validates, the linter and the additive check pass, the fakes are published with the checksum and the four acknowledgements are recorded.

**Contract tests.** Schema validity, the additive diff against the baseline checksum, the section state on a 200, the error envelope on every status code, the masking flag on every contact field and the completeness of the nine tables.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | No session or an expired session | You are not signed in. Sign in to continue. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | Case outside the scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P3-023 | One source does not answer | {section} cannot be shown now. The rest of the case is shown. |
| MSG-P3-024 | The panel has nothing to show | Nothing is recorded in {section} yet. |

Validation rules the document must satisfy: OpenAPI 3.1 valid; the operation has an operationId in the service namespace; the path is under `/api/recovery/case/v1` and carries GET only; every contact field carries a personal-data flag and a masked source; every error response carries the shared envelope with a code, a message and a trace identifier; `page` is 0 or more and `size` 1 to 100, and a value outside the range is 400; a failed section is a section state on a 200 and never an error status.

##### 15. Screens and states

None. This story delivers no screen. It fixes the data the SCR-03 timeline panel shows in each state: Loading (the page shape with empty item and section arrays), Read only (items in time order with actor and reference; a new case shows its creation item), Empty (a section with no item and MSG-P3-024), Error (the section entry with state failed and MSG-P3-023 while the page stays 200, MSG-P4-003 out of scope, MSG-P4-002 without the right). The screen is built by RWB-P3-E1035-APP as the gateway-bff composite route.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the document: the type order, the timeout, the page size and the labels are named as sources, never fixed here.
- No personal data in the examples: every example party is synthetic and no example carries a clear contact value.
- No PII in events, workflow inputs or logs, and none in the contract examples.
- The document declares no foreign table and no cross-schema read; ACE data behind the contact items is named only through the rwb-source-data contract (DP-01, DP-18).
- The ledger is declared through its owner's read, never as a table (DP-18).
- The operation states Case record R and the scope; a hook that hides the scope fails the linter.
- A failed section is data on a 200 response, never an error status that would hide the rest of the page.
