**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-035 for rwb-case. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **a timeline on the case record view with contacts, documents, assignments, transfers and status changes in time order, each with who or which rule caused it**, so that **I see what happened to the case without asking anyone**.

In the target the panel is one operation of rwb-case, `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timeline`, served to SCR-03 as the gateway-bff composite route of RWB-PLT-N001-CON (DP-19). It merges four sources one hop each, never a table read: the assignments, transfers and case state of schema `rwb_case` (DP-01); the decision records of the case through the rwb-decision decision-record query (DP-03, C RWB-P7-E1027-CON); the contact ledger through the interaction read owned by rwb-source-data (DP-18); the documents through rwb-document (DP-11). This story delivers the full four-source timeline, the transfer item detail, the paged total, the fixed type order and the per-section degradation; the read-only case header and the contact history behind the same screen are RWB-P3-E1023-APP.

The type order, the section timeout and every label are data read through the parameters and reference-data contracts of rwb-case (DP-06, DP-07); no business value sits in code. The right and the scope are checked by the authorise guard that the service template provides and RWB-P3-E1023-APP wires (ASM-3637), so this story adds no access decoupling row.

##### 2. Business rationale

A case that changes owner today arrives with no history except what the last owner remembers. The legacy story added a timeline panel to SCR-03 that merged the interaction ledger, the documents, the assignments and the decision log entries in time order and showed the person or the rule and version behind each event, including the coded reason of a manual transfer. It met REQ-CWC-016 (every workflow event carries its rule ID and version, now visible) and REQ-OCC-007 (contact history and documents on the case view).

The split changes where each record comes from, not what the case owner sees. The interaction ledger now belongs to rwb-source-data, the decision record is written locally and sealed in the ledger of rwb-decision, the documents belong to rwb-document, and rwb-case keeps only what it owns: the case, its assignments and its queue. The panel therefore becomes one contract operation with three mocked calls behind it, and the timeline reads in under 2 seconds against a ledger at its 2031 size (NFR-070, BR6).

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P3-E1023-APP is done: SCR-03 shows the read-only case record; the timeline operation is published with its page and size parameters and the panel mounts behind the flag.
- RWB-P3-E1035-CON is done: the v1.1 timeline item shape, the partial-result envelope and its fakes, through which this story builds.
- RWB-P3-E1021-CON is done: the transfer rules write `assignment.transfer_reason_code`, `assignment.rule_id` and the closed assignment row this story reads.
- RWB-P3-E1023-APP already applies the authorise guard of the service template: Case record R and the scope are checked by it, and this story adds no access decoupling row (ASM-3637).
- C RWB-P7-E1027-CON is published with its fake: the decision-record query by case. Its path, its time filter and its field list are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2210; ASM-3635).
- The rwb-document documents-by-case operation is published with its fake, and rwb-source-data publishes the interaction read the ledger part needs. The path and the paging of the interaction read are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0695; ASM-1242).
- RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1042-CON (parameters), RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON (reference data), RWB-PLT-E1047-CON (event and topic naming), RWB-PLT-E1044-CON (Flyway sequence), RWB-PLT-E1027-CON (decision record) and RWB-PLT-N001-CON (gateway-bff composite route) are done.
- The rwb-case login (DP-02) holds SELECT on schema `rwb_case` and no privilege on another schema. The login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0692; ASM-1239).
- The user holds a role with Case record R and the case is in the user's scope.

##### 4. Flow

1. Case owner: opens SCR-03 for case RW-2026-000801 and selects the Timeline panel.
2. gateway-bff: checks the session in Redis, takes the short-lived JWT through ACE Common sign-in and checks the coarse permission, then calls rwb-case.
3. rwb-case TimelineController: checks Case record R and the scope through the authorise guard; a case outside the scope returns 404 and never 403.
4. rwb-case TimelineQueryService: calls, in parallel and one hop each, the assignment read in `rwb_case`, the rwb-decision decision-record query, the rwb-source-data interaction read and the rwb-document documents-by-case operation; each has a 2 s budget and a GET retry once with jitter.
5. rwb-case TimelineMapper: maps every record to a TimelineItem with at, type, summary, by, reference and, for a transfer, reasonCode, fromQueueCode, toQueueCode and ruleId; "by" holds the person, or the rule ID with its version.
6. rwb-case TimelineQueryService: sorts by time, then by the type order of parameter `timeline.type.order`, then by record ID, and returns the page with the total of the merged set.
7. rwb-case SectionGuard: a source that fails or exceeds its budget sets that section to a failed state with MSG-P3-023 and leaves the other items in the page; the response stays 200.
8. TimelinePanel: shows each item with an icon for its type and the time; a new case shows one "Case created" item with the entry rule version.
9. Case owner: opens a transfer item; the panel shows the reason label, the from and to queue and owner, and the rule version.
10. TimelinePanel: pages by 50 with the total, and shows MSG-P3-023 in place of the section that failed.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The decision-record query does not answer | The other items show; the panel shows the section message for "Decisions" | MSG-P3-023 | AC3 |
| X2 | The case has only its creation record | One item "Case created" shows with the entry rule and version | None | AC4 |
| X3 | Two events have the same time | Fixed order by type, then record ID; the order is stable on every opening | None | AC5 |
| X4 | The case has more than 50 events | Paged by 50; the total of the merged set shows | None | AC6 |
| X5 | The case is outside the user's scope | 404; no item shows | MSG-P4-003 | AC7 |
| X6 | A role without Case record R opens the timeline | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-E1-035-08 |
| X7 | The document hub does not answer | The items show without documents; the section message names "Documents" | MSG-P3-023 | AC3 pattern |
| X8 | The interaction read does not answer | The items show without contacts; the section message names "Contacts" | MSG-P3-023 | AC3 pattern |
| X9 | A transfer record has no closed previous assignment | The from queue and the from owner show as empty; the item and its reason still show | None | AC2 pattern |

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Events show in time order; equal times follow the type order decision, status change, assignment, transfer, contact, document, then record ID | FSD A2.45; FEAT-ACA-12 |
| BR2 | An event caused by a rule shows the rule ID and version; an event by a person shows the person | REQ-CWC-016 |
| BR3 | A manual transfer shows its transfer reason | REQ-WKM-003; RWB-E1-021 |
| BR4 | Only cases in the caller's scope open | CTL-09 |
| BR5 | Personal fields in a contact summary follow the masking rules | REQ-ACA-005; DL26 |
| BR6 | The timeline reads in under 2 seconds at the ledger's 2031 size | NFR-070 |
| BR7 | The type order and the section timeout are parameters, never constants in code; the values in force are read on every request through the parameters contract | DP-06; legacy §13 |
| BR8 | A transfer item takes its to-queue from `assignment.queue_id` and its from-queue and from-owner from the closed previous assignment row of the same case; its rule version comes from the decision record of the transfer, never from a column | TSD P3 v3 assignment (DF-WRK-013, DF-WRK-016, DF-WRK-039, DF-WRK-040); ASM-3633 |
| BR9 | A case state change and the creation item are read as the decision records of the case; rwb-case adds no status-history table and keeps no second copy of the history | ASM-3632; GAP-2210 |
| BR10 | One failed source degrades one section and never the page: the response stays 200 with the section state, and the MSG-P3-023 text names the section | §5 X1, X7, X8; MSG-P3-023 |
| BR11 | The panel reads only what the caller may see: the scope filter is applied before the merge, and an out-of-scope case is 404 with no item | CTL-09; REQ-ACA-009 |

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It reads the records of past changes: the assignment rows of `rwb_case` and the decision records of the case. The events that move a case are published by other rwb-case stories on topic `rwb.case.events.v1`; this story publishes and consumes none of them.

##### 12. Contract

This is the v1.1 behaviour of the operation first published by RWB-P3-E1023-CON: the path, the query parameters `type`, `from`, `to`, `page` and `size` and the status codes are unchanged, and the item gains the detail fields and the section state (ASM-3636). None. The panel publishes no case event. The AC-READ access record goes to the rwb-access access log through its contract, not to topic `rwb.case.events.v1` (DP-14 keeps the service topic name for the stories that publish).

None. The panel reads on open and subscribes to no topic in this story.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The read is synchronous REST and starts, signals and queries no workflow. CaseWorkflow (parent, one per case, task queue `rwb-case`) owns the case state the timeline shows; this story only reads the decision records it leaves.

None.

| parameter_catalog | rwb_case | P3 | `timeline.type.order`, `caserecord.section.timeout.ms`, the page size |
| parameter_value | rwb_case | P3 | The values in force on the read date |

The interaction ledger, the documents and the decision records are read through their owners' contracts, never through a table (DP-01, DP-18). The service also owns case_account, case_party, case_entry_exclusion, task, queue_member and queue_measure; this story touches none of them.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Operations | Owner | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| rwb-decision fake | The decision-record query by case | P7 (C RWB-P7-E1027-CON) | AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6 |
| rwb-document fake | Documents by case | P5 | AC1, AC6, X7 |
| rwb-source-data fake | The interaction read | P1 (DP-18) | AC1 pattern, AC3, X8 |
| rwb-access fake | Authorise and the masking policy | P4 | AC7, TC-E1-035-08 |
| gateway-bff composite route stub | The SCR-03 route | edge (RWB-PLT-N001-CON) | AC1 to AC7 on the screen path |
| rwb-case read fake | The timeline operation of RWB-P3-E1035-CON | P3 | The contract tests of the sibling story |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | In this story |
|---|---|
| REST | Yes. One read operation provided under `/api/recovery/case/v1`; three contracts consumed one hop each, 2 s timeout, GET retried once with jitter, breaker per downstream |
| Kafka | None. The panel publishes and consumes no event |
| Temporal | None. No workflow is started, signalled or queried |
| File | None. Documents arrive through the rwb-document contract, not as a file read |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`, module `timeline`; the screen module is served by the gateway-bff composite route of RWB-PLT-N001-CON and holds no server code of its own.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| TimelineController | Controller | GET /cases/{caseId}/timeline with the guard, the query parameters and the problem response |
| TimelineQueryService | Service | Fans out to the three contracts and the assignment read, merges, sorts by BR1 and pages with the total |
| TimelineMapper | Service | One mapper per source; rule ID and version, or the person, into "by"; the transfer detail fields |
| AssignmentRepository | Repository | The assignments of a case ordered by assigned_at, with the closed previous row for the from queue and owner (DF-WRK-013, DF-WRK-039) |
| DecisionRecordClient | Client | The decision-record query of rwb-decision; 2 s budget, gets the case state changes and the creation item |
| LedgerClient | Client | The interaction read of rwb-source-data (DP-18) |
| DocumentClient | Client | The documents-by-case operation of rwb-document |
| SectionGuard | Component | Per-source budget, failure capture and the section state with MSG-P3-023 |
| ParameterReader | Component | `timeline.type.order`, `caserecord.section.timeout.ms` and the page size through the parameters contract (DP-06) |
| TimelinePanel, TimelineItemDetail, SectionMessage | Screen component | SCR-03 timeline panel, item detail for a transfer, section message |

**Pattern application**

| DP code | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-18 | Interaction ledger | Ledger owned by rwb-source-data (default ruling) | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Database**

- Reads assignment, recovery_case, queue, lov_value, reference_row, reference_version, parameter_catalog and parameter_value in schema `rwb_case` only, through the rwb-case login (DP-02).
- No migration. The tables and the Flyway sequence come from RWB-P3-E1018-CON and RWB-PLT-E1044-CON; the assignment read uses the index on `assignment(case_id, assigned_at)` that the DB story creates.
- No index and no read outside `rwb_case`; the ledger read is a contract call.

**Configuration and reference data**

- Parameter `timeline.type.order` (legacy §13) with the BR1 order as its value; `caserecord.section.timeout.ms` = 3000 (legacy assumed; DL11); the page size with the legacy default of 50.
- Reference data LOV-TRANSFER-REASON (R01 to R06), LOV-DOC-TYPE and LOV-CHANNEL through the reference-data contract (DP-07).

**Build steps**

1. AssignmentRepository and the transfer item detail from the closed previous row; tests AC1, AC2.
2. Mappers for the decision record, the ledger row and the document; tests AC1, AC4.
3. Merge, type order from the parameter and the record-ID tie break; tests AC1, AC5.
4. Paging with the total of the merged set; test AC6.
5. SectionGuard with the per-source budget and the partial page; tests AC3, X7, X8.
6. Scope check through the guard and the 404 path; test AC7.
7. TimelinePanel, item icons and the transfer detail; test AC2.
8. Performance test with 500 events; BR6; and the access test.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.timeline` (legacy). Off: SCR-03 hides the Timeline panel and the operation returns 404.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass and the timeline of a case with 500 events reads in under 2 seconds in SIT (NFR-070).

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | No session or an expired session | You are not signed in. Sign in to continue. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | Case outside the scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P3-023 | One source does not answer | {section} cannot be shown now. The rest of the case is shown. |
| MSG-P3-024 | The panel has nothing to show | Nothing is recorded in {section} yet. |

Validation: `caseId` must be a case identifier; `page` is 0 or more and `size` 1 to 100, and a value outside the range is 400 with no data; `from` and `to` are optional date-times and `from` after `to` is 400. A case that is unknown, out of scope or behind the flag returns 404, never 403, so the panel leaks nothing about the case. Every error is the service problem response of TSD P3 v3 T2.1 carrying the MSG code and the trace ID.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-03 Case record gains the Timeline panel, served as the gateway-bff composite route of RWB-PLT-N001-CON (DP-19). Loading: skeleton rows with the section headings. Read only: items in time order with type icon, summary, by and time; a new case shows its creation item; a transfer opens its detail with reason, from and to queue and owner, and the rule version. Empty: a case with no item shows MSG-P3-024 for the panel. Error: MSG-P3-023 for the section that failed, MSG-P4-003 out of scope and MSG-P4-002 without the right; the panel never blocks the rest of the screen. The full timeline screen with filters, SCR-04, comes in Epic 2 (RWB-P3-E2016-APP).

The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the type order, the timeout, the page size and every label are data, read through the parameters and reference-data contracts.
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts; contact summaries follow masking by role and test parties are synthetic. No PII in events, workflow inputs or logs.
- No read of another service's tables: documents through rwb-document, decision records through rwb-decision, ledger rows through rwb-source-data (DP-01, DP-18).
- No call chains: the panel asks each owner one hop, in parallel, with a 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream.
- The timeline never writes; it shows records as they were written, and the AC-READ access record is the only record the read produces.
- A failed source degrades one section and never the page.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform contract owner**, I want **the published contract of the guard and masker library — the `AccessGuard`, `ScopeGuard` and `MaskApplier` interfaces, the `@PersonalData` annotation, the scope descriptor, the error vocabulary with its message ids, the fail-closed rule, the statement that the library owns no table and no token, and the fakes — instead of the monolith's `recovery.access.matrix` package that read the permission and masking tables in the same database**, so that **every service can be built and tested against one frozen authorisation and masking contract while the data stays with P4**.

The contract is a contract before it is code. The three interfaces fix what a service may call and what it may never pass; the annotation fixes how a response field is declared as personal data; the scope descriptor fixes what the owning service receives and applies; the error vocabulary fixes the two statuses and the message ids a caller sees; the fail-closed rule fixes the behaviour of every failure; and the fakes let a service build on Day 1 while the access owner and the data owner are still being built.

The contract also fixes the negative space, which is the part that keeps the split honest: the library owns no table, holds no login and no token, can never receive the clear identity number, publishes no event of its own and takes no delegation decision. A service that wants a table, a cache store or a user list of its own is outside this contract by design.

**The division is fixed and is the same in both stories of this legacy key.** The permission matrix as data, the masking rules, the scope rule, the access log and the matrix load and approve operations stay with **RWB-P4-E1037-APP**, which owns the legacy acceptance criteria; the end-to-end proof across the wave 1 services is **RWB-ITG-E1037-ITG**; this story and its app story RWB-PLT-E1037-APP deliver the **shared guard library and masker library** that every service binds, so that the right check and the masking are one mechanism and not nineteen copies. Neither story copies a legacy acceptance criterion: every criterion in section 7 is tagged (new, D-RCV-60) and tests only the contract deliverable in the title, and the fifteen legacy test cases are executed by RWB-P4-E1037-APP and RWB-ITG-E1037-ITG (section 18).

##### 2. Business rationale

In the monolith the permission matrix, the masking rules, the scope rule and the guard sat in one database and one package: `recovery.access.matrix` read `permission`, `masking_rule`, `role` and `delegation_limit` in the same connection, built a `ScopeFilter`, filled annotated DTOs and answered `isUnmasked`. There was one implementation because there was one process. In the 19-service target those tables stay with one owner (DP-01): P4 rwb-access owns `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule`, `role_conflict` and `delegation_limit`, P3 rwb-case owns `lov_value`, and P1 rwb-source-data owns the ACE view fields. Every service still has to check a right, bound a query and mask a field.

Without a published contract that check becomes nineteen implementations of the same four things, drifting apart at the first policy change. With it, a service compiles against one frozen interface from Day 1, tests against fakes before the access owner exists, and cannot quietly read a P4 table because the contract gives it no connection to do so. Each service authorises the object itself, using cached permission data from rwb-access (Architecture v5 slide 10); the access owner publishes `POST /authorise` for role, scope and DoA, `GET /me/permissions`, `GET /doa-limits` and `/masking-policies`, and writes `AccessPolicyChanged` and `DoaLimitChanged` on `rwb.access.events.v1` (slide 14); the masking rules of the access owner are enforced in each service and the clear identity number never leaves ACE (slide 35; ADR-010).

The values the criteria use are the legacy values unchanged — matrix version `PM-2026.11`, masking version `MASK-SIT-01`, cases `RW-2026-000123` and `RW-2026-000456`, team `MTG-NE`, the role codes RW-CASEOWN, RW-LEGAL, RW-PHONECOL, RW-SECADM, RW-REFADM, RW-COE and RW-AUDIT, the field ids DF-ACE-073 `id_no_masked`, DF-ACE-074 `id_no_last4`, DF-ACE-078 `contact_value`, DF-ACE-079 `contact_value_masked` and DF-ACE-059 `date_of_birth`, the area `QUEUE_AND_ALLOCATION`, the letters C, R, U, D and A, the scopes OWN, TEAM, REGION and ALL, and the messages MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003, MSG-P4-001 and MSG-GEN-004. It supports REQ-ACA-003, REQ-ACA-005, REQ-ACA-006, REQ-ACA-007, REQ-ACA-009 and REQ-ACA-011.

Where the sources do not fix the contract shapes — what the authorise request and answer carry, what the `/masking-policies` answer holds, what the audit record carries and how a failure maps to a status — the contract states the shape in force and records the open point as Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1405; ASM-2448) and (GAP-1405; ASM-2449).

##### 3. Preconditions

- Wave 0 is the platform wave: the shared libraries are published once and every later epic binds them (Architecture v5 slide 38).
- Architecture v5 slide 10 fixes the authorisation model the contract publishes: each service authorises the object itself with cached permission data from rwb-access, 2 s timeouts and a circuit breaker per downstream, deny by default.
- Architecture v5 slide 14 names the access operations and the two events the contract refers to: `POST /authorise` (role, scope, DoA), `GET /me/permissions`, `GET /doa-limits`, `/masking-policies`, and `AccessPolicyChanged` and `DoaLimitChanged` on `rwb.access.events.v1`.
- Architecture v5 slides 20 and 35 fix the cache-refresh rule, the deny-by-default rule and the rule that personal data never travels in events, workflow payloads or logs.
- ADR-010 fixes the identity boundary the contract restates: the clear identity number never leaves ACE, there is no token store, and `id_no_last4` is the clearest identity value any role can receive.
- The Ownership Map keeps `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule`, `role_conflict` and `delegation_limit` with P4 rwb-access and `lov_value` with P3 rwb-case; the contract names those tables and owns none of them (DP-01, DP-07).
- The paths of the three consumed operations are reached at `/api/recovery/access/v1/…` under the per-service base rule of §R4, because slide 14 names the operations and the Ownership Map has no path row for them (GAP-1405; ASM-2448).
- The library is published as one versioned artefact with major version 1, its contract shapes and its fakes, pinned by the service template; the coordinates themselves are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1405; ASM-2449).
- No build dependency: the contract is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Fix the three interfaces: `AccessGuard.check`, `ScopeGuard.describe` and `MaskApplier.fill`, with their input and output types and their exceptions, and the rule that each is synchronous and one hop at most.
2. Fix the fail-closed rule in the interface documentation: a 2 s timeout, a circuit breaker per downstream, deny by default, 503 on an unreachable, timed-out or malformed access owner, and no caching of a failed or malformed answer.
3. Fix the scope descriptor: the type OWN, TEAM, REGION or ALL with the user, team and region codes; the contract states that the owning service applies it in its own query and that the library returns no record.
4. Fix the annotation: `@PersonalData("DF-…")` on a response field, and the masked-versus-clear source rule — masked column or last-four value where the policy does not allow the clear value, the clear value where it does, and masked where no rule covers the field.
5. Fix the error vocabulary: 403 `MSG-P4-002` for a denied right, 404 `MSG-P4-003` for a record outside the descriptor, 503 with no business data for a failure of the access owner, and the audit record shape with the case id, the field id and the flag `clear` or `masked`, never the value.
6. Fix the negative statements: the library owns no table, holds no login and no token, and no method, parameter, cache entry or fake accepts a clear identity number.
7. Fix the consumed surface: the three access operations and the two access events, with their owner, their base and their call type.
8. Publish the fakes: an authorise fake with allow, deny, unreachable and malformed answers, a masking-policy fake, a scope fake and an audit fake.
9. Wire the contract test and the drift test into the build of every consuming service, and publish the contract document with the nine tables of section 12.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A service implements its own guard instead of calling `AccessGuard` | The contract test fails and the build is refused | None | AC1, AC6 |
| X2 | A service passes a clear identity number to the masker | The signature does not compile; no overload accepts it | None | AC5 |
| X3 | The access owner is unreachable, times out or answers malformed | 503, fail closed, nothing cached, no business data in the answer | None | AC1 |
| X4 | A service applies the descriptor to another service's table or query | The boundary test fails on the cross-schema reference and the build is refused | None | AC2 |
| X5 | A field is annotated but no rule covers it | The contract states that the field is masked | None | AC3 |
| X6 | A rule names the clear identity number | The access owner refuses the rule at load; the contract states the clearest value it can receive is `id_no_last4` | MSG-P1-002 (raised by P4) | AC5 |
| X7 | A service resolves another version of the library | The drift test fails the build with the pinned and the resolved version named | None | AC6 |
| X8 | An audit record is written with a value instead of a flag | The audit fake refuses the record and the contract test fails | None | AC4 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; the contract refers to the access owner, the data owner and the platform contracts by name only |
| Negotiable | The artefact coordinates and the payload details are agreed at the contract freeze; the interfaces, the annotation, the descriptor, the vocabulary and the fail-closed rule are fixed by the target architecture |
| Valuable | Unblocks every service CON and APP story that checks a right or masks a field, from Day 1, against one frozen contract and its fakes |
| Estimable | Three interfaces, one annotation, one value type, one error vocabulary, one audit shape and four fakes |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion below is a contract test that the build of a consuming service runs |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Access guard and masker library contract

  Background:
    Given the platform library contract document is published with major version 1
    Given permission matrix version "PM-2026.11" is in force and masking version "MASK-SIT-01" is in force
    Given RW-CASEOWN holds "R" in Queue and allocation and RW-LEGAL holds "-" in Queue and allocation in "PM-2026.11"

  Scenario: AC1 The interfaces and the fail-closed rule are published (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the contract jar of the platform library is published
    When a service compiles against it
    Then AccessGuard.check(ActionRef action, SessionRef session) returns a Decision of ALLOWED or REFUSED, with the area "QUEUE_AND_ALLOCATION" and the right "U" taken from the caller
    Then ScopeGuard.describe(SessionRef session) returns a ScopeDescriptor with type OWN, TEAM, REGION or ALL and the user, team and region codes
    Then MaskApplier.fill(Object dto, SessionRef session) returns the same dto with every annotated field filled, masked or left clear, and no method accepts a clear identity number
    Then every method is synchronous, is one hop at most, has a 2 s timeout and a circuit breaker per downstream
    Then an unreachable, timed-out or malformed access owner answers 503 and nothing is cached, so deny by default holds

  Scenario: AC2 The scope descriptor contract and the rule that the owning service applies it (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published ScopeDescriptor of type "OWN" with user "U-2105" and the team and region codes
    When a consuming service receives it for a case read
    Then the descriptor carries no record and no query and the library runs no query of another service
    Then the owning service applies the descriptor in its own query and returns 12 records for 12 owned cases
    Then a record outside the descriptor, case "RW-2026-000456" in team "MTG-NE", is refused by the owner with 404 and message MSG-P4-003
    Then the descriptor of each type OWN, TEAM, REGION and ALL is the same shape, and the library states that it never returns a record

  Scenario: AC3 The annotation contract and the masked-versus-clear source rule (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a response field annotated @PersonalData("DF-ACE-079") and a field annotated @PersonalData("DF-ACE-059")
    When the masker fills them for a session in "MASK-SIT-01"
    Then DF-ACE-079 is filled from the masked value the data owner supplies, and the clear contact value is requested only where the rule allows it for one of the session's roles
    Then DF-ACE-074 is filled from the last-four value and DF-ACE-078 from the clear value only where the rule allows it
    Then the field for DF-ACE-059, which no rule covers, is masked
    Then the contract states that a field with no rule is masked and that the masker holds no value of its own

  Scenario: AC4 The error vocabulary and the audit record shape are fixed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a denied right, a record outside the descriptor and a failing access owner
    When a consuming service raises each of the three through the contract
    Then the denied right is 403 with MSG-P4-002 and the handler does not run
    Then the out-of-descriptor record is 404 with MSG-P4-003 and the record is not returned
    Then the failing access owner is 503 with no business data in the body, the log or the trace
    Then every masked or clear read writes one audit record with the case id, the field id and the flag "clear" or "masked", and the audit fake refuses a record that carries a value

  Scenario: AC5 The library owns no table, holds no token and never receives the clear identity number (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published contract and its declared inputs
    When a service tries to give the library a schema, a table, a login or a token
    Then the contract has no parameter, no configuration key and no method for any of them
    Then role, permission, masking_rule, role_conflict, delegation_limit and lov_value are named only, as the tables of P4 rwb-access and P3 rwb-case
    Then the clearest identity value the contract carries is id_no_last4 and a clear identity number cannot be expressed
    Then the contract states that there is no token store (ADR-010)

  Scenario: AC6 The fakes and the drift test of every consuming service (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the four published fakes: authorise with allow, deny, unreachable and malformed answers, masking policy, scope and audit
    When the contract test of a consuming service runs against the published jar
    Then the fake answers each of the four authorise variants and the service behaves as section 7 states for each
    Then a service that pins another version, overrides a class or re-implements a guard fails the drift test with the pinned and the resolved version named
    Then the fake set is the same for every consuming service and needs no access owner to be running
```

These criteria are new and test only the contract deliverable. No legacy acceptance criterion is copied: legacy AC1 to AC13 belong to RWB-P4-E1037-APP, and their end-to-end form belongs to RWB-ITG-E1037-ITG.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The capability area and the right are checked before the handler runs, and a denied action changes nothing | permission.letters (DF-REF-043); REQ-ACA-007; CTL-09 |
| BR2 | Deny by default and fail closed: an unreachable, timed-out or malformed access owner is a 503 refusal, never an allow, and no failed answer is cached | Architecture v5 slides 10, 29 and 35; REQ-ACA-007 |
| BR3 | The library produces the scope descriptor and the owning service applies it in its own query; the library runs no query and returns no record | role.default_scope (DF-REF-038); LOV-SCOPE; REQ-ACA-009 |
| BR4 | A personal data field is masked unless the masking policy in force lets one of the session's roles see it; a masked field is filled from the masked column or the last-four value, and a field with no rule is masked | Masking rules reference table; DL26; CTL-11; REQ-ACA-005; DF-ACE-073, DF-ACE-079 |
| BR5 | Every masked or clear read writes one audit record with the case id, the field id and the flag, never the value | REQ-ACA-006; RWB-E1-039 BR3; NFR-040 |
| BR6 | The library owns no table, no login and no token: the matrix, masking, role, conflict and delegation data are P4 rwb-access's and the reference values are P3 rwb-case's | DP-01; DP-02; Ownership Map |
| BR7 | No clear identity number is expressible in the contract: no parameter, cache entry or fake accepts it, and `id_no_last4` is the clearest value | ADR-010; Data Tier Map section 7; D-RCV-35 U1 |
| BR8 | The policy is refreshed on `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` and `rwb.access.DoALimitChanged.v1` through the inbox, and a change takes effect within the time to live with no deployment | Arch v5 slide 20; RWB-E1-037 AC1; REQ-ACA-003 |
| BR9 | One version of the contract is pinned by the service template; a service that resolves another version, overrides a class or re-implements a guard fails its build | Arch v5 slides 20 and 38; RWB-PLT-NF02-APP |
| BR10 | No personal data in a log record, a span attribute, a metric label, an error body, a cache key or a fixture | Architecture v5 slides 11 and 35 |
| BR11 | The contract takes no business decision: it relays the access owner's decision and the data owner's value, and holds no delegation limit or approver role | Arch v5 slide 10; slide 35 note on attribute-based access control |
| BR12 | The two events the contract refers to are consumed by the consuming service through the library, under that service's own consumer group and inbox | Arch v5 slide 20 (cache refresh); RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |

##### 9. State transitions

The contract fixes the states of a guard decision and of an annotated field; it holds no case status and no stored object of its own.

| Object | From | Event | To | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Contract version | 1 | A backward-compatible change to a payload, an attribute or a fake | Version 1, minor change | The pinned services build unchanged |
| Contract version | 1 | A breaking change to an interface, the annotation, the descriptor or the vocabulary | Version 2 with a migration note | A service moves only by changing the pin and passing the drift test |
| Guard decision | UNCHECKED | Allow, deny or failure of the access owner | ALLOWED, REFUSED or FAIL_CLOSED | The handler runs, is refused with 403, or is refused with 503 |
| Annotated field | UNFILLED | A rule allows the role a clear or a last-four view, or no rule covers the field | CLEAR or MASKED | The value is filled from the source the rule names, or masked, and the audit flag records which |

A published version is never edited in place; a breaking change is a new major version with a migration note.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The platform library team (any team, per U3) | Owns the interfaces, the annotation, the descriptor, the vocabulary, the fail-closed rule and the fakes; publishes version 1 and later versions |
| The service template owner | Pins exactly one version of the contract in the template and moves the pin with the build as the gate |
| The consuming squads of the 19 services | Compile and test against the published jar and its fakes, and raise a change request instead of a local override |
| The access owner (P4 rwb-access) | Owns the data and the authorise, permission and masking-policy operations the contract calls; the contract only names them |
| The data owner (P1 rwb-source-data) | Owns the ACE views and the masked and last-four columns the masker fills from |
| RW-COMPLY Compliance and PDPA officer | Sets the masking values behind the rules the contract refers to (DL26); the contract holds none |
| The security architecture reviewer | Confirms that the fail-closed rule, the annotation and the audit shape meet the architecture standards |
| No approval level from the delegation of authority applies | The contract takes no business decision |

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-REF-035, DF-REF-037, DF-REF-038 | role (P4 rwb-access) | role_code, role_class, default_scope | Named only: carried in the authorise and permission answers |
| DF-REF-040 to DF-REF-044 | permission (P4 rwb-access) | letters, matrix_version and the other fields | Named only: carried in the permission answer |
| DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204 | masking_rule (P4 rwb-access) | id, role_code, field_id, unmasked, masking_version, valid_from, valid_to | Named only: carried in the masking-policy answer |
| DF-ACE-073 | v_ace_customer (P1 rwb-source-data) | id_no_masked | Named only: the masked identity value a consuming service supplies |
| DF-ACE-074 | v_ace_customer (P1 rwb-source-data) | id_no_last4 | Named only: the clearest identity value the contract can carry |
| DF-ACE-059 | v_ace_customer (P1 rwb-source-data) | date_of_birth | Named only: masked where no rule covers it |
| DF-ACE-078 | v_ace_contact (P1 rwb-source-data) | contact_value | Named only: clear only where the rule allows it, and audited |
| DF-ACE-079 | v_ace_contact (P1 rwb-source-data) | contact_value_masked | Named only: the masked contact value |
| No data of its own | Library | None | The contract stores nothing, caches nothing on disk, holds no table and owns no schema |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary. Every row is named and none is written by the library: the contract states the field id it annotates and the owner it comes from (DP-01). A contract that carried a value, a table or a token would break the identity boundary of ADR-010, so the shapes are published without one.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The library provides no REST operation and publishes no API document: it is a versioned artefact inside the consuming service. The authorise, permission and masking-policy operations belong to P4 rwb-access and the access-log operation to P4 rwb-access through RWB-P4-E1039-CON.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method and path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|
| POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise | P4 rwb-access | The role, scope and delegation decision the guard asks for on a cache miss, a stale entry or a policy event |
| GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/permissions | P4 rwb-access | The letters and the default scope in force, used to refill the cache after `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` |
| GET /api/recovery/access/v1/masking-policies | P4 rwb-access | The masking rules in force for the fields and roles of the session |

The contract fixes the call shape, not the service: each is one hop, 2 s timeout, breaker per downstream, deny by default, at the owner's `/api/recovery/access/v1` base (DP-11, DP-13, ADR-020). The paths are the base rule of §R4 applied to the operations slide 14 names, because the Ownership Map has no path row for them (GAP-1405; ASM-2448).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The library publishes no event and owns no topic. `AccessPolicyChanged` and `DoaLimitChanged` are published by P4 rwb-access on `rwb.access.events.v1`.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Producer | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1 | rwb.access.events.v1 | P4 rwb-access | Consumed by the consuming service through the library, to drop the cached permissions and masking policy |
| rwb.access.DoALimitChanged.v1 | rwb.access.events.v1 | P4 rwb-access | Consumed by the consuming service through the library, to drop the cached delegation band |

Both are consumed under the consuming service's own consumer group and recorded in its own `processed_event` inbox (RWB-PLT-TE006-CON); the library supplies the listener and not the consumer group, and a repeated delivery changes nothing.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The contract defines no workflow and no activity; the guard and the masker are synchronous calls inside the caller's handler or activity, and the contract states that no workflow code may call them with a personal value in the payload.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The contract owns no Schedule. The six-monthly access review list (JOB-18) is a P4 rwb-access Schedule and is not this story.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The contract owns no table and no schema: `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule`, `role_conflict` and `delegation_limit` are P4 rwb-access's tables and `lov_value` is P3 rwb-case's, named here only so that no consuming service reads them or copies them into a local store (DP-01, DP-07).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| Authorise fake | `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | Allow, deny, unreachable and malformed answers for area "QUEUE_AND_ALLOCATION" and right "U" (AC1, AC6) |
| Masking-policy fake | `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/masking-policies` | One rule that lets RW-CASEOWN see DF-ACE-078 in clear, and no rule for DF-ACE-059 (AC3) |
| Scope fake | The scope part of the authorise answer | Type OWN with user "U-2105" and the team and region codes, and type ALL for the comparison (AC2) |
| Audit fake | The access-log contract of P4 rwb-access | A recorder of the case id, the field id and the flag, and a refusal of a record that carries a value (AC4) |

The four fakes are published with the contract jar so that a consuming service needs no access owner to build or test (AC6).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Provided | Consumed | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 | 3 | The authorise, permission and masking-policy operations of P4; the audit record goes through the access-log contract and adds no path |
| Kafka | 0 | 2 | `AccessPolicyChanged` and `DoaLimitChanged` on `rwb.access.events.v1`, consumed by the consuming service through the library |
| Temporal | 0 | 0 | No workflow, activity or Schedule; the calls run inside the caller |
| File | 0 | 0 | No file is read or written |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** A versioned shared-library contract artefact of the platform: the three interfaces and the exceptions in `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.platform.api`, the annotation and the scope descriptor with them, the contract document and the fakes as resources of the same artefact. The implementation is the APP story of this legacy key, in `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.platform.access`. The artefact coordinates are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1405; ASM-2449).

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables. The contract states that the library owns no table and names the P4 and P3 tables only | none |
| DP-02 | `recovery_svc` login | One login per service. The contract states that the library holds no login and borrows none | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`. Referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views. The contract fills from the value the data owner supplies and reads no view | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library. The time to live and the breaker settings are read through it | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case. The scope codes and the letter set are reference values, named and not owned | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library. This story is the contract of that guard library | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit. Referred to for the activity context the guard is proven in | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout. The contract fixes the three consumed calls and their timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1`. Every consumed path uses the base of its owner and the library adds none | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema. The contract adds no migration and states that each service migrates its own | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting. The contract names no lake endpoint and no export | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route. The contract fixes the 403 and 404 answers the route renders; SCR-43 and SCR-47 are not built here | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |

The H and C dependencies named in the last column belong to the consuming stories and to RWB-PLT-E1037-APP; this contract story has no build dependency of its own, which is why its `H` and `C` rows in the metadata table read `None`.

**Hardware and software change.** The contract replaces the `recovery.access.matrix` package with a versioned artefact: the permission matrix and the masking rules are no longer read from the same database by the same process, but asked of their owner over three one-hop operations and cached per service against a published policy version. The ACE values reach the masker already masked or cut to the last four, through the data owner's contract. The contract adds no schema, no topic, no queue, no Schedule and no bucket, so no new hardware is implied: the artefact is published to the package registry and runs inside each service's existing pods on the existing AKS cluster.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `AccessGuard` | Published interface | One method returning ALLOWED or REFUSED for an action and a session, with the pre-handler rule and the 403 `MSG-P4-002` (AC1, AC4) |
| `ScopeGuard` | Published interface | One method returning the `ScopeDescriptor`, with the statement that the owning service applies it (AC2) |
| `MaskApplier` | Published interface | One method filling the annotated fields from the masked, last-four or clear value the policy allows (AC3) |
| `@PersonalData` | Annotation | The field-id marker on a response field; the only way a field becomes maskable and auditable (AC3, AC4) |
| ScopeDescriptor | Value type | Type OWN, TEAM, REGION or ALL with the user, team and region codes, and no record (AC2) |
| Error vocabulary | Document | 403 `MSG-P4-002`, 404 `MSG-P4-003`, 503 with no business data, and the audit record shape (AC4) |
| Contract document | Document | The fail-closed rule, the timeout and breaker settings, the ownership and token statements, and the versioning rule (AC1, AC5) |
| Fakes and fixtures | Test asset | The four fakes of section 12.8 and the fixture set used by every consuming service (AC6) |

**Build steps**

1. Write the three interfaces, the annotation, the scope descriptor and the exception types; run the compile and drift test of a sample service (AC1, AC2, AC3).
2. Write the fail-closed rule into the interface documentation and prove it with the authorise fake: unreachable, timeout and malformed each answer 503 and cache nothing (AC1).
3. Write the error vocabulary and the audit record shape; prove the 403, the 404, the 503 and the refusal of a record that carries a value (AC4).
4. Write the ownership and identity statements and check that the contract has no parameter, key or method for a schema, a table, a login, a token or a clear identity number (AC5).
5. Publish the four fakes and wire the contract and drift tests into the build of a consuming service; test all four authorise variants and a service that pins another version (AC6).
6. Publish the contract document with the nine tables of section 12 and record the version and the compatibility rule.

**Done when.** The six criteria pass as contract tests, the four fakes are published with the jar, the nine tables of section 12 name their owner from the Ownership Map, and RWB-PLT-E1037-APP builds and passes its tests against the published jar.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | The access owner reports that the session has ended; the contract relays it unchanged and does not retry | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A denied right, refused before the handler runs | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | A record outside the scope descriptor, refused by the owning service | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | A consumed access operation answers 409; the contract relays it unchanged and the caller re-reads its permissions | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |

The message ids and the wording are copied unchanged from RWB-E1-037; the contract adds no message of its own, and the Thai text of each follows DL10. The 503 fail-closed answer carries no message id and no business data: it is one RFC 9457 problem detail with the trace identifier and the operation.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen of its own. The contract has no user interface: what it fixes for the screens of the 19 services is the status and the message id a screen receives (403 `MSG-P4-002`, 404 `MSG-P4-003`, 503 with no business data), the masked value a field carries, and the rule that no screen error reveals a token, an internal path or a personal value. SCR-43 Roles and access and SCR-47 Personal data are Epic 8 and out of scope (DP-19).

##### 16. Test cases

| TC ID | Covers | Level | Data |
|---|---|---|---|
| TC-PLT-E1037-CON-01 | AC1 | Contract | A sample service compiles against the jar; area "QUEUE_AND_ALLOCATION" and right "U"; the four authorise fake variants, with 503 and no cache on the last two |
| TC-PLT-E1037-CON-02 | AC2 | Contract | A `ScopeDescriptor` of each type OWN, TEAM, REGION and ALL; the assertion that the descriptor holds no record and the library runs no query |
| TC-PLT-E1037-CON-03 | AC3 | Component | Annotated DF-ACE-079, DF-ACE-074, DF-ACE-078 and DF-ACE-059; values "XXXXXX5678", "0123" and "XXXXXXXXX1234"; the no-rule field masked |
| TC-PLT-E1037-CON-04 | AC4 | Contract | A denied right, an out-of-descriptor record, a failing access owner, one clear audit record and one audit record carrying a value that the fake refuses |
| TC-PLT-E1037-CON-05 | AC5, AC6 | Contract | A search of the published jar for a schema, a table, a login, a token or a clear identity number parameter; the four fakes and the drift test of a service that pins another version |

No test in this story is an integration copy: the contract is exercised against its own fakes, never against a live service, and no `-ITG` variant belongs to it.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: letters, scopes, masking positions, approver roles and the time to live are data or parameters behind the interfaces.
- No personal data in a payload, a fixture or a log; the interfaces carry field ids and IDs only.
- No schema, table, login or token in the contract: the library owns none, and the P4 and P3 tables are named only.
- A clear identity number cannot be expressed: `id_no_last4` is the clearest value the contract can carry, and there is no token store (ADR-010).
- Deny by default and fail closed on every failure of the access owner, with no business data in the 503 answer.
- A published version is never edited in place; a breaking change is a new major version with a migration note and a new pin.

##### 1. Story

As a **service developer**, I want **one guard library that checks the capability area and the right before the handler runs and one masker library that fills every field annotated as personal data from the masked or last-four value the data owner supplies, with a cache of the permission and masking policy that refreshes on the access owner's policy events and fails closed**, so that **every service refuses an action the matrix does not allow and no service ever holds or prints a clear personal value**.

This is the platform-library slice of legacy key RWB-E1-037 under epic RWB-PLT-LIB. The library is not one of the 19 services: it has no service short name, no schema, no topic, no task queue and no REST base of its own. It is a versioned artefact that a service binds, and it holds no data of its own — the permission matrix, the masking rules, the roles, the scope and the delegation limits stay with P4 rwb-access, the ACE fields it masks stay with P1 rwb-source-data, and the access log store stays with P4 rwb-access through RWB-P4-E1039.

The story covers:

- The `AccessGuard`: the capability area and the right of the action are checked before the handler runs, against the access owner's answer, and a refusal returns 403 `MSG-P4-002` with the handler never invoked.
- The `ScopeGuard`: the library produces a scope descriptor (OWN, TEAM, REGION, ALL plus the user, team and region codes) and the owning service applies it in its own query. The library never runs another service's query and never returns a record.
- The `MaskApplier`: a `@PersonalData("DF-…")` annotation on a response field, filled from the masked column or the last-four value the data owner supplies; with no rule in force the field is masked; the clearest identity value the library may hold is `id_no_last4`.
- The policy cache: the permission and masking policy is cached per service with the time to live read through the parameters client, and refreshed on `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` and `rwb.access.DoALimitChanged.v1` through the inbox.
- The fail-closed rule: an unreachable, timed-out or malformed access owner means refusal with 503 and no business data anywhere in the response or the log.
- The audit record: every masked or clear read writes one record with the case id, the field id and the flag `clear` or `masked`, never the value, through the access-log contract of P4 rwb-access.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story holds the role-to-permission matrix (54 roles against 14 capability areas), the masking rules and the scope rule as versioned tables that every screen and API applies, with `ScopeFilter`, `FieldMasker` and `AccessCheck` published from one package, `recovery.access.matrix`, inside one process and one database.

**The division is fixed and is the same in both stories of this legacy key.** The permission matrix as data, the masking rules, the scope rule, the access log and the matrix load and approve operations stay with **RWB-P4-E1037-APP**, which owns the legacy acceptance criteria; the end-to-end proof across the wave 1 services is **RWB-ITG-E1037-ITG**; this story and its contract story RWB-PLT-E1037-CON deliver the **shared guard library and masker library** that every service binds, so that the right check and the masking are one mechanism and not nineteen copies. Neither story copies a legacy acceptance criterion: every criterion in section 7 is tagged (new, D-RCV-60) and tests only the library deliverable in the title, and the fifteen legacy test cases are executed by RWB-P4-E1037-APP and RWB-ITG-E1037-ITG (section 18).

The split follows the architecture and not a preference. Each service authorises the object itself, using cached permission data from rwb-access, with a 2 s timeout and a circuit breaker per downstream (Architecture v5 slide 10); the access owner publishes `POST /authorise` for role, scope and DoA, `GET /me/permissions`, `GET /doa-limits` and `/masking-policies`, and writes `AccessPolicyChanged` and `DoaLimitChanged` on `rwb.access.events.v1` (slide 14); personal data stays in the owning service and the masking rules of the access owner are enforced in each service (slide 35). A shared library is the only shape that makes those three sentences true at nineteen services: without it, nineteen services each write their own guard against the same contract, nineteen cache implementations expire at nineteen different moments, and the masking rule is re-implemented wherever a DTO is mapped.

The negative side is fixed as tightly as the positive one. Deny by default and fail closed (slides 35 and 29), no personal data in logs, payloads or events, no token store (ADR-010; slide 35), and no cross-schema read: the library holds no table, so it cannot read a P4 or a P1 table even by accident. The values the criteria use are the legacy values unchanged — matrix version `PM-2026.11`, masking version `MASK-SIT-01`, cases `RW-2026-000123` and `RW-2026-000456`, team `MTG-NE`, the role codes RW-CASEOWN, RW-LEGAL, RW-PHONECOL, RW-SECADM, RW-REFADM, RW-COE, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, the field ids DF-ACE-073 `id_no_masked`, DF-ACE-074 `id_no_last4`, DF-ACE-078 `contact_value`, DF-ACE-079 `contact_value_masked`, DF-ACE-059 `date_of_birth`, the area `QUEUE_AND_ALLOCATION`, the letters C, R, U, D and A, the scopes OWN, TEAM, REGION and ALL, and the messages MSG-P4-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003 and MSG-GEN-004.

It supports REQ-ACA-003, REQ-ACA-005, REQ-ACA-006, REQ-ACA-007, REQ-ACA-009 and REQ-ACA-011 and keeps controls CTL-09, CTL-10 and CTL-11 in place. Where the sources do not fix the library artefact coordinates, the cache time to live, the authorise payload, or the split of the masking read between the policy of P4 and the record of P1, the story builds to the assumption in force and records the open point as Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1404; ASM-2445), (GAP-1404; ASM-2446) and (GAP-1404; ASM-2447). The measure is unchanged from the legacy story: rule and limit changes made without a code release, target 100 percent (FSD P4 A2.4).

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-PLT-E1037-CON is published (this story's contract deliverable): the `AccessGuard`, `ScopeGuard` and `MaskApplier` interfaces, the `@PersonalData` annotation, the scope descriptor, the error vocabulary, the fail-closed rule and the fakes.
- RWB-P4-E1037-CON and RWB-P4-E1039-CON are published: the authorise, permission and masking-policy operations of P4 rwb-access, and the access-log contract that the audit record is written through (DP-08, DP-11).
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published: the local decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`, which the library refers to and does not write (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and RWB-PLT-E1043-CON are published: the parameters client library and the reference-data client library (DP-06, DP-07); RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON publish the rwb-case contracts behind them.
- RWB-PLT-TE006-CON is published: the inbox contract through which the two access policy events are consumed and deduplicated (the library consumes no event without an inbox row in the consuming service's own schema).
- RWB-PLT-E1071-CON is published: the workflow kit, so the guard is proven to run inside a workflow activity as well as inside a REST handler (DP-10).
- RWB-PLT-E1044-CON is published: the per-service Flyway sequence. The library itself adds no migration; a service that wants a local cache table applies its own (DP-15).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the gateway-bff composite route, so the 403 and 404 answers of the guard reach the screen in the route's problem-detail shape (DP-19).
- Permission matrix version `PM-2026.11` is in force. In it RW-LEGAL holds `-` in Queue and allocation and RW-CASEOWN holds `R` in Queue and allocation.
- Masking version `MASK-SIT-01` is in force, in which only RW-CASEOWN may see `v_ace_contact.contact_value` in clear for DF-ACE-078; no unmasked rows go to PROD until Compliance supplies the rules (DL26).
- The access owner answers `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise`, `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/permissions` and `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/masking-policies` under its own per-service base, one hop, 2 s timeout and breaker per downstream (DP-11, DP-13, ADR-020).
- No table is read by the library: the role, permission, masking_rule, role_conflict and delegation_limit tables are P4 rwb-access's and `lov_value` is P3 rwb-case's (DP-01, DP-07).
- The library artefact coordinates, the cache time to live and the authorise request and answer payload are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1404; ASM-2445), (GAP-1404; ASM-2446) and (GAP-1404; ASM-2447).
- No build dependency blocks the start: every dependency in the metadata table is a CON story, so the story is ready on Day 1 against the published contracts and their fakes.

##### 4. Flow

1. A service binds the published library. The service template pins exactly one version of it, and the consuming service writes no guard, no cache and no masker of its own.
2. A request arrives at the consuming service. The `AccessGuard` reads the action's capability area and right from the service's own annotation or route declaration, and asks the policy cache for the answer of the signed-in role.
3. On a cache miss, the guard calls `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` with the role, the scope and the delegation band of the action, one hop, 2 s timeout, with the breaker of that downstream.
4. The guard stores the answer in the cache with the time to live read through the parameters client, and answers the request from the cached policy while it is fresh. The time to live and the parameter key are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1404; ASM-2446).
5. A denied action is refused with 403 `MSG-P4-002` before the handler runs; the handler is never invoked, nothing changes, and the refusal is written to the log with the area and the right and no business data.
6. A permitted action runs. Where the action reads a set of records, `ScopeGuard` produces a scope descriptor with the type (OWN, TEAM, REGION or ALL) and the user, team and region codes, and hands it to the owning service, which applies it in its own query. The library returns no record and runs no query of another service.
7. The owning service writes its own answer. A record outside the descriptor is refused by the owner with 404 `MSG-P4-003`; the library supplies the message id and the status only.
8. The answer passes through `MaskApplier` before it leaves the service. Every field annotated `@PersonalData("DF-…")` is filled from the masked column or the last-four value that the data owner supplies, or from the clear value only where the masking policy of the access owner allows it for one of the session's roles.
9. Where no rule in force covers an annotated field, the field is masked. The masker never asks for the clear identity number, never receives it, never caches it and never logs it; `id_no_last4` is the clearest identity value the library may hold.
10. Every masked or clear read writes one audit record through the access-log contract of P4 rwb-access (RWB-P4-E1039-CON): the case id, the field id and the flag `clear` or `masked`, and never the value.
11. `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` and `rwb.access.DoALimitChanged.v1` are consumed from `rwb.access.events.v1` through the inbox of the consuming service. Each one drops the stale cache entries before the next guard call, so a policy change takes effect within the time to live and with no deployment.
12. The access owner is unreachable, times out, or answers outside its contract: the guard refuses with 503, the handler does not run, the failure is logged with the operation and the trace identifier and with no business data, and the decision is counted as a fail-closed decision.
13. The library reports its own counters on the platform observability path: guard decisions by outcome, cache hits and misses, fail-closed decisions, masker fills by flag, and audit writes refused.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A role without the right calls an action, for example a transfer | Refused with 403 before the handler runs; nothing changes; the refusal is logged | MSG-P4-002 | AC1 |
| X2 | The access owner is unreachable or answers after the 2 s timeout | Refused with 503, fail closed; the handler does not run; no business data in the log or the error body | None | AC2 |
| X3 | The access owner answers a malformed or partial policy answer | Refused with 503, fail closed; the malformed answer is discarded and never cached | None | AC2 |
| X4 | A policy event arrives while a request is in flight | The in-flight request keeps the answer it was given; the next request reads the refreshed entry | None | AC3 |
| X5 | The same policy event is delivered twice | The inbox drops the second delivery; one refresh happens | None | AC3 |
| X6 | A record outside the scope descriptor is requested | Refused with 404; the record is not returned and the excluded count is never shown | MSG-P4-003 | AC4 |
| X7 | A consuming service builds its own query result instead of applying the descriptor | The contract and drift test fails the build; the library returns no record by design | None | AC4, AC8 |
| X8 | An annotated field has no rule in force | The field is masked | None | AC5 |
| X9 | A masking rule names the clear identity number | The rule is refused at load by the access owner; the clearest value the library can receive is `id_no_last4` | MSG-P1-002 (raised by P4) | AC6 |
| X10 | The audit write fails | The read is refused, not served, because an unaudited personal read is not allowed | None | AC7 |
| X11 | A consuming service pins another library version or overrides a class | The drift test fails the build and names the pinned and the resolved version | None | AC8 |
| X12 | A log record, a span attribute or an error body is found to carry a personal value | The redaction test fails the build; the record is purged under the owning service's retention and a defect is raised | None | AC8 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against the library CON story and the platform contract stories; the access owner and the data owner are reached through their contract fakes, so no service has to be finished first |
| Negotiable | The artefact coordinates, the cache time to live and the payload shapes are open until the contract freeze; the interfaces, the fail-closed rule, the annotation and the audit shape are fixed by the target architecture |
| Valuable | Gives every service one guard and one masker instead of nineteen copies, and makes fail-closed and no-clear-personal-data the default rather than a review finding |
| Estimable | Three interfaces, one annotation, one cache, one audit writer and the fakes |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is a component, contract or NFR test in section 16, against the fakes of section 12.8 |

```gherkin

  Background:
    Given the guard and masker library is published with major version 1 and pinned by the service template
```

These criteria are new and test only the library deliverable. No legacy acceptance criterion is copied: legacy AC1 to AC13 belong to RWB-P4-E1037-APP, and their end-to-end form belongs to RWB-ITG-E1037-ITG.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The capability area and the right are checked before the handler runs; a denied action changes nothing and is logged with the area and the right | permission.letters (DF-REF-043); REQ-ACA-007; CTL-09 |
| BR2 | Deny by default: an action with no matching permission entry, an unreachable access owner, a timeout or a malformed answer is refused, never allowed | Architecture v5 slides 10, 29 and 35; REQ-ACA-007 |
| BR3 | Scope filters records first and the permission is checked second; the library produces the descriptor and the owning service applies it in its own query, and the excluded count is never shown | role.default_scope (DF-REF-038); LOV-SCOPE; REQ-ACA-009 |
| BR4 | OWN means cases the person owns or has a task on; TEAM means cases in the person's team queues; REGION means cases in the regions of the person's teams; ALL means every case | Key sheet, roles.txt |
| BR5 | A personal data field is masked unless the masking policy in force lets one of the session's roles see it; a masked field is filled from the masked column or the last-four value the data owner supplies; with no rule it is masked | Masking rules reference table; DL26; CTL-11; REQ-ACA-005; DF-ACE-073, DF-ACE-079 |
| BR6 | Masking is applied inside the owning service before data reaches a screen, an agent or an event | NFR-039; NFR-040 |
| BR7 | The policy cache is refreshed on `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` and `rwb.access.DoALimitChanged.v1` through the inbox, and a change takes effect within the time to live with no deployment | Arch v5 slide 20 (cache refresh); RWB-E1-037 AC1; REQ-ACA-003 |
| BR8 | There is no tokenization and no token store. The clear `customer.identification_number` never leaves ACE; the library never receives it, and `id_no_last4` is the clearest identity value it may hold | ADR-010; Data Tier Map section 7; D-RCV-35 U1 |
| BR9 | Every masked or clear read of a personal data field writes one audit record with the case id, the field id and the flag, never the value; an unaudited personal read is refused | REQ-ACA-006; RWB-E1-039 BR3; NFR-040 |
| BR10 | The library owns no table and reads no service's schema: the matrix, masking, role, conflict and delegation data are P4 rwb-access's and the reference values are P3 rwb-case's | DP-01; Ownership Map; REQ-ACA-003 |
| BR11 | No personal data in a log record, a span attribute, a metric label, an error body or a cache key: identifiers, codes and flags only | Architecture v5 slides 11 and 35 |
| BR12 | A joiner, mover or leaver change reaches the service through the access owner's policy and session state, never through a library-held user list | DL38; CTL-10; REQ-ACA-011 |
| BR13 | One version of the library is pinned by the service template, and a service that resolves another version or overrides a class fails its build | Arch v5 slides 20 and 38; RWB-PLT-NF02-APP |
| BR14 | The library takes no business decision of its own: it relays the access owner's decision and the data owner's value, and it holds no delegation limit | Arch v5 slide 10; slide 35 note on attribute-based access control |

##### 9. State transitions

No case status changes in this story. The library holds three small states of its own, all in memory or in the consuming service's own cache:

| Object | From | Event | To | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Guard decision | UNCHECKED | The access owner answers allow for the role, the area and the right | ALLOWED | The handler runs; the answer is cached with the time to live |
| Guard decision | UNCHECKED | The access owner answers deny, or holds no entry for the area | REFUSED | 403 `MSG-P4-002`, the handler does not run, the refusal is logged |
| Guard decision | UNCHECKED | The access owner is unreachable, times out, or answers malformed | FAIL_CLOSED | 503, the handler does not run, the decision is counted and nothing is cached |
| Cache entry | EMPTY | A guard call fills it from the authorise or permission answer | FRESH | The answer is served from the cache until the time to live ends |
| Cache entry | FRESH | The time to live ends | STALE | The next call asks the access owner again |
| Cache entry | FRESH or STALE | `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` or `rwb.access.DoALimitChanged.v1` arrives through the inbox | EMPTY | The entry is dropped before the next guard call |
| Annotated field | UNFILLED | A rule in force allows the role a clear or a last-four view | CLEAR | The field is filled from the value the data owner supplies, and the audit flag is `clear` |
| Annotated field | UNFILLED | No rule allows the role a clear view, or no rule covers the field | MASKED | The masked value is filled, or the value is masked, and the audit flag is `masked` |

A `FAIL_CLOSED` decision is never cached: the next request tries the access owner again, so a recovered access owner restores service without a restart.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The platform library team (any team, per U3) | Builds, tests and publishes the guard and masker library, owns its versioning and its changelog |
| The service template owner | Pins exactly one library version in the template and moves the pin with the build as the gate |
| The consuming squads of the 19 services | Bind the library, annotate their response fields, supply the scope descriptor to their own query, and raise a change request against the library instead of a local override |
| The access owner (P4 rwb-access) | Owns the role, permission, masking_rule, role_conflict and delegation_limit data, the authorise, permission and masking-policy operations and the access log; the library only calls them |
| The data owner (P1 rwb-source-data) | Owns the ACE views and the masked and last-four columns the masker fills from; the library never reads a view |
| RW-CASEOWN, RW-LEGAL, RW-PHONECOL, RW-SECADM, RW-REFADM, RW-COE, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY | Hold the roles whose answers the criteria exercise; each sees only what the matrix and the masking policy allow |
| RW-COMPLY Compliance and PDPA officer | Sets the masking rules and approves each masking version outside this story (DL26) |
| The security architecture reviewer | Confirms that the fail-closed rule, the annotation and the audit shape of a library version meet the architecture standards |
| No delegation of authority decision is made in the library | A delegation band is the access owner's data and the owning service's decision, never a value in a shared library |
