| DF-CAS-009, DF-CAS-011, DF-CAS-012 | recovery_case (P3 rwb-case) | owner_user_id, team_code, region_code | Named only: the fields the owning service applies the descriptor to, in its own query |
| DF-ACE-055, DF-ACE-057, DF-ACE-058 | v_ace_customer (P1 rwb-source-data) | cif_no, first_name, last_name | Read as masked values where an annotated field names them |
| Cache entry (no field ID) | Library cache, in the consuming service's memory | role code, area, right, scope type, policy version, expiry | Write and read, in memory only; no table and no schema |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary. The library holds no table, no schema and no login of its own (DP-01, DP-02): every value above arrives in an answer of the access owner or of the data owner, and the cache entry has no field ID in the source because no source defines a library cache (GAP-1404; ASM-2446). No clear identity number is read, cached, logged or accepted by any method of the library (BR8).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The library provides no REST surface of its own: it has no service short name, no `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` base and no OpenAPI document. The authorise, permission and masking-policy operations are provided by P4 rwb-access, and the access-log operation by P4 rwb-access through RWB-P4-E1039-CON; this story consumes them and never republishes them.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method and path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|
| POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise | P4 rwb-access | The guard check for the role, the scope and the delegation band of the action, cached with the time to live and called again on a miss, a stale entry or a policy event |
| GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/permissions | P4 rwb-access | The letters and the default scope in force for the signed-in role, used to refill the cache after `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` |
| GET /api/recovery/access/v1/masking-policies | P4 rwb-access | The masking rules in force for the fields and roles of the session, used to decide clear, masked or last-four and refilled after `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` |

Every call is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a circuit breaker per downstream and a deny-by-default answer on failure (DP-11, ADR-020). The audit record is written through the access-log contract of P4 rwb-access (RWB-P4-E1039-CON), not through a path of this story.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The library publishes no event of its own. The policy changes it reacts to are published by P4 rwb-access, and the refusal and audit facts it writes go to the access log through the P4 contract.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Producer | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1 | rwb.access.events.v1 | P4 rwb-access | Drops the cached permissions and masking policy of the consuming service before its next guard call |
| rwb.access.DoALimitChanged.v1 | rwb.access.events.v1 | P4 rwb-access | Drops the cached delegation band before the next guard call, so the next authorise call carries the band in force |

Both are consumed through the inbox of the consuming service, under that service's own consumer group and in that service's own `processed_event` table (RWB-PLT-TE006-CON); a repeated delivery changes nothing.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None of its own. The guard and the masker are synchronous code inside the caller: the guard runs in a REST handler before the handler body, and inside a workflow activity when a service calls it from one. The library starts no workflow, starts no activity and holds no task queue.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The library owns no Schedule. The six-monthly access review list (JOB-18) is a P4 rwb-access Schedule and is not this story.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The library owns no `rwb_*` schema, no table and no login: `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule`, `role_conflict` and `delegation_limit` are P4 rwb-access's tables, `lov_value` is P3 rwb-case's, and the ACE view fields are P1 rwb-source-data's. They are named here only, so that no reader mistakes a shared cache for a stored copy (DP-01, DP-02).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| Authorise fake | `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | Allow, deny, unreachable, timeout and malformed answers for the same role, area and right (AC1, AC2) |
| Permission fake | `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/permissions` | The letters of `PM-2026.11` and, after the policy event, of `PM-2026.12` (AC3) |
| Masking-policy fake | `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/masking-policies` | One rule that lets RW-CASEOWN see DF-ACE-078 in clear, and no rule for DF-ACE-059 (AC5, AC6) |
| Scope fake | The scope part of the authorise answer | Type OWN with the user, team and region codes, and type ALL for the comparison (AC4) |
| Audit fake | The access-log contract of P4 rwb-access | A recorder that captures the case id, the field id and the flag, and a switch that fails the write (AC7) |
| Policy-event fake | `rwb.access.events.v1` with the inbox | `AccessPolicyChanged` and `DoaLimitChanged`, each delivered twice (AC3) |
| Data-owner value fake | The masked and last-four values P1 rwb-source-data supplies | `id_no_masked` "XXXXXXXXX1234", `id_no_last4` "0123" and `contact_value_masked` "XXXXXX5678" for case RW-2026-000123 (AC5, AC6) |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Provided | Consumed | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 | 3 | The authorise, permission and masking-policy operations of P4; the audit record goes through the access-log contract of P4 and adds no path of its own |
| Kafka | 0 | 2 | `AccessPolicyChanged` and `DoaLimitChanged` on `rwb.access.events.v1`, through the inbox of the consuming service |
| Temporal | 0 | 0 | No workflow, activity or Schedule; the guard runs inside the caller's handler or activity |
| File | 0 | 0 | No file is read or written |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** A versioned shared-library artefact of the platform, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.platform.access` for the implementation, with the published interfaces in `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.platform.api`. The artefact coordinates, the repository and the publication channel are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1404; ASM-2445).

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables. The library holds no table, so the matrix and the masking rows are read only through the P4 operations | none |
| DP-02 | `recovery_svc` login | One login per service. The library has no login of its own and borrows none: every value arrives over a contract | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`. A policy approval and its consequences are recorded by P4, not by the guard | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views. The masker fills from the masked or last-four value the data owner supplies and reads no view itself | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library. The cache time to live and the breaker settings are read through it | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case. The scope codes OWN, TEAM, REGION and ALL and the letter set are reference values, never library constants | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library. This story is that guard library | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit. The guard is proven inside an activity context as well as inside a REST handler | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout. Each of the three consumed operations is one hop with its own breaker | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1`. The library adds no base of its own; every consumed path uses the base of its owner | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema. The library adds no migration; a service that wants a local cache table migrates it itself | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting. The access log and the refusal facts stay in the P4 access log, and no library path writes a lake copy | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route. The 403 and 404 answers reach the screen through the route, and SCR-43 and SCR-47 are not built here | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Hardware and software change.** The `recovery.access.matrix` package of the monolith is replaced by a versioned library that every service binds. The permission and masking rows leave the monolith's single schema and stay in the P4 schema, read through the access owner's operations; the ACE values stay behind the P1 contract and reach the masker already masked or cut to the last four. The guard caches its answers per service with the time to live from the parameters client and refreshes them from the two access policy events through the inbox, instead of reading a shared table on every request. No new hardware is implied: the library runs inside each service's existing pods on the existing AKS cluster, the cache is per-process memory, and no database, topic, queue or bucket is added. The two libraries RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-TE006-CON are used unchanged for the decision record and the inbox.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `AccessGuard` | Published interface | Decides the area and the right before the handler runs, from the cache or from the authorise call, and refuses with 403 `MSG-P4-002` or 503 on failure (BR1, BR2) |
| `ScopeGuard` | Published interface | Produces the scope descriptor with its type and the user, team and region codes; returns no record and runs no query (BR3, BR4) |
| `MaskApplier` | Published interface | Fills the annotated fields from the masked, last-four or clear value the policy allows, masks a field with no rule, and never accepts a clear identity number (BR5, BR8) |
| `@PersonalData` | Annotation | Names the DF field id of a response field so the masker and the audit writer can act without a per-DTO list (BR5, BR9) |
| ScopeDescriptor | Value type | The type OWN, TEAM, REGION or ALL with the user, team and region codes; the owning service applies it (BR3) |
| PolicyCache | Service | Per-process cache of permissions, masking policy and delegation band, with the time to live from the parameters client and the drop on the two policy events (BR7) |
| PolicyEventInboxListener | Service | Consumes `AccessPolicyChanged` and `DoaLimitChanged` through the inbox and drops the matching cache entries (BR7) |
| AccessAuditWriter | Service | Writes one audit record per masked or clear read through the access-log contract of P4, with the field id and the flag and never the value (BR9) |
| FailClosedPolicy | Component | The timeout, the breaker and the deny-by-default mapping of every failure to 503 (BR2) |
| Library fake and fixtures | Test asset | The fakes of section 12.8, used by the contract test of every consuming service (BR13) |

**Configuration.** The cache time to live and the parameter key that holds it, the 2 s timeout and the breaker thresholds are configuration read through the parameters client (DP-06). The time to live and its key are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1404; ASM-2446). Letters, scopes and masking positions are never library constants: they arrive in the access owner's answers and the reference data of P3 (DP-07).

**Build steps**

1. Publish the three interfaces, the annotation, the scope descriptor and the exception types from RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; prove that a sample service compiles against the jar and that no method of the library accepts a clear identity number (AC6, AC8).
2. Build the policy cache with the time to live from the parameters client and the refusal to cache a failed or malformed answer; test a fresh entry, a stale entry and a fail-closed answer (AC2, AC3).
3. Build the `PolicyEventInboxListener` over the inbox contract of RWB-PLT-TE006-CON; test both events, a repeated delivery and the drop of the exposed entry (AC3).
4. Build `AccessGuard` with the pre-handler check, the 403 `MSG-P4-002` and the 503 fail-closed path; test the allow, the deny, the unreachable, the timeout and the malformed answer with the probe handler (AC1, AC2).
5. Build `ScopeGuard` and the descriptor; give the owning service a repository test that applies OWN, TEAM, REGION and ALL in its own query and returns 404 `MSG-P4-003` for a record outside it (AC4).
6. Build `MaskApplier` over the annotation, the masking-policy answer and the values the data owner supplies; test the masked fill, the last-four fill, the clear fill and the no-rule field (AC5, AC6).
7. Build `AccessAuditWriter` over the access-log contract of P4; test one `clear` record, one `masked` record and the refusal of the read when the write fails (AC7).
8. Wire the redaction and drift checks: a log, a span or an error body that carries a personal value fails the build, and a service that pins another version fails the drift test (AC8).
9. Run the contract test of a second service of another epic against the same fakes and prove the identical status, message id, audit shape and masked value (AC8).

**Feature flag.** One flag per service, read as a parameter: off, the guard answers from the last known policy and refuses every action whose policy is unknown, so a switch-off never opens an unchecked path.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the contract tests of section 12.8 pass against the fakes, two services of different epics produce the same refusal, audit and masking behaviour against the same version of the library, and no log record, trace, metric label or error body carries a personal value.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | The access owner reports that the session has ended after a leaver's group was removed; the guard relays it unchanged and does not retry | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-P4-002 | An action outside the role's permission, refused before the handler runs | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | A record outside the scope descriptor, refused by the owning service | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | A consumed access operation answers 409; the library relays it unchanged and the caller re-reads its permissions | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |

The message ids and the wording are copied unchanged from RWB-E1-037; the library adds no message of its own, and the Thai text of each follows DL10. The 503 fail-closed answer carries no message id and no business data: it is one RFC 9457 problem detail with the trace identifier and the operation, per Architecture v5 slide 11.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen of this story. The library has no route and no state of its own. A person sees only the effect: a menu entry absent where the role has no right (RWB-E1-022), a masked field on the case record view (RWB-E1-023), a 403 with `MSG-P4-002` and a 404 with `MSG-P4-003` rendered by gateway-bff. SCR-43 Roles and access and SCR-47 Personal data arrive in Epic 8 and are out of scope (DP-19).

| TC-PLT-E1037-APP-02 | AC2, BR2, BR11 | NFR | The authorise fake unreachable, timing out at 2 s and malformed; 503 on each; the log, the trace and the error body searched for a case id, a personal value and a token |
| TC-PLT-E1037-APP-03 | AC3, BR7 | Component | A fresh cache entry, `AccessPolicyChanged` for `PM-2026.12`, `DoaLimitChanged`, each delivered twice through the inbox; the entry dropped and refilled within the time to live |

No test in this story is an integration copy: the library is exercised against the fakes of section 12.8, never against a live service, and no `-ITG` variant belongs to it.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: letters, scopes, masking positions, approver roles, the time to live and the breaker settings are data or parameters read through their contracts.
- No personal data in a log record, a span attribute, a metric label, an error body, a cache key or a fixture: field ids and the masked flag only, never values.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or a `v_ace_*` view read by the data owner; the library reads no database at all.
- No tokenization and no token store: the library never receives the clear identity number, and `id_no_last4` is the clearest identity value it may hold (ADR-010).
- A field with no masking rule is masked, and a clear read happens only where the rule allows it and is audited.
- Deny by default and fail closed on every failure of the access owner, with no business data in the 503 answer.
- The library owns no table, publishes no event, starts no workflow and takes no delegation decision of its own.
- The library is pinned at one version by the service template, and a local override fails the build.

##### 1. Story

As a **contract owner of rwb-access**, I want **the published access and masking contract of this service — the two load operations, the approve operation, the matrix and masking-policy reads, the approver rule, the five data objects, the error vocabulary, `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` and the fakes**, so that **its app stories and every service that authorises or masks build and test against one frozen contract from Day 1, while the policy rows stay in `rwb_access` and no consumer invents a shape of its own**.

The document is fixed before it is code. It fixes what a caller sends and what it receives on four operations, which fields of `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule`, `role_conflict` and `delegation_limit` appear in an answer, which status and message id each failure returns, when the policy event is published and what it may not carry, and which fakes let a consumer build while the access owner is still being built.

**The division of this legacy key is fixed.** The guard, the masker and the `@PersonalData` annotation that every service binds are the platform library contract **RWB-PLT-E1037-CON** and its app story **RWB-PLT-E1037-APP**; this story publishes the **data-side contract** of `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule`, `role_conflict` and `delegation_limit` — the objects, their versions, the two loads and their approval, the two reads and the policy event — and implements none of the guard. RWB-P4-E1022-APP owns the sign-in and the session, RWB-P4-E1039-APP owns the access log and break-glass, and RWB-ITG-E1037-ITG owns the end-to-end proof. The permission matrix as data, the masking rules and the load and approve path are the deliverable of **RWB-P4-E1037-APP**, which also owns the thirteen legacy criteria; this story owns no legacy criterion, publishes new criteria only, and names the owner of the legacy criteria and of the fifteen legacy test cases of its key in section 18.

##### 2. Business rationale

In the monolith the matrix, the masking rules, the scope rule and the guard sat in one package over one database: `recovery.access.matrix` read `permission`, `masking_rule`, `role` and `delegation_limit` in the same connection and answered a scope filter, a masked DTO and an `isUnmasked` call. There was one shape because there was one process. In the 19-service target the policy rows stay with one owner (DP-01) and the enforcement moves into a platform library that every service binds, so a consumer now depends on two published artefacts and must find in each exactly what it needs: the library gives it the guard, the masker and the annotation; the access owner gives it the policy data, the versions and the approval trail.

That is the gap this story closes. Without a published data-side contract a consumer guesses what `GET /masking-policies` returns, whether a permission answer carries letters or a set of booleans, which approver approves a masking version, and what a 403 means on the load path — and the guesses drift at the first policy change. With it, a consumer compiles and tests from Day 1 against fakes, and cannot quietly read a P4 table because the contract gives it no connection to do so. Architecture v5 slide 14 fixes the operations the contract publishes — `POST /authorise`, `GET /me/permissions`, `GET /doa-limits` and `/masking-policies` — and the two events `AccessPolicyChanged` and `DoaLimitChanged` on `rwb.access.events.v1`; slide 41 keeps Recovery roles as data, scope, masking policy, the DoA table and the access log in `rwb_access`; and ADR-010 keeps the clear identity number inside ACE with no token store.

**The division, in one paragraph.** The guard, the masker and the `@PersonalData` annotation, with the scope descriptor and the fakes that every service binds, are the artefact of **RWB-PLT-E1037-CON**; this story publishes the data-side contract of **`role`, `permission`, `masking_rule`, `role_conflict` and `delegation_limit`** — the two loads and their approval with the approver role from the parameter, the matrix read, the masking-policy read, the versions in force and the policy event — and the two artefacts meet at one point only: the masker reads the rules this contract publishes, and the guard reads the letters of the permission rows it publishes.

The values the criteria use are the legacy values unchanged: matrix version `PM-2026.11`, the next version `PM-2026.12` with 756 permission rows, masking versions `MASK-SIT-01` and `MASK-2026.11`, the role codes RW-REFADM, RW-SECADM, RW-COMPLY, RW-LEGAL, RW-CASEOWN, RW-PHONECOL and RW-COE, the field ids DF-ACE-073 `id_no_masked`, DF-ACE-074 `id_no_last4`, DF-ACE-059 `date_of_birth`, DF-ACE-078 `contact_value` and DF-ACE-079 `contact_value_masked`, the area `QUEUE_AND_ALLOCATION`, the letters C, R, U, D and A, the scopes OWN, TEAM, REGION and ALL, and the messages MSG-P4-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003, MSG-P1-002, MSG-P7-002, MSG-P7-003, MSG-GEN-004 and MSG-GEN-006. It supports REQ-ACA-003, REQ-ACA-005, REQ-ACA-006, REQ-ACA-007, REQ-ACA-009 and REQ-ACA-011.

Two open points are carried as placeholders and register rows: the path and the right of the masking-policy operation, which Arch v5 slide 14 names without a path in the API Specification v4 or TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A — Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0779; ASM-1416) — and the payload of `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1`, which no source fixes — Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0779; ASM-1417).

##### 3. Preconditions

- Wave 1 and lane `CG-W1`: the contract is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7) and has no build dependency. `H`, `C`, `I` and `X` read None.
- Architecture v5 slide 14 fixes the access operations and the two events: `POST /authorise`, `GET /me/permissions`, `GET /doa-limits`, `/masking-policies`, and `AccessPolicyChanged` and `DoaLimitChanged` on `rwb.access.events.v1`.
- Architecture v5 slide 41 keeps `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule`, `role_conflict` and `delegation_limit` with P4 rwb-access; the Ownership Map gives P4 the paths `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/roles` and `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log` and no path for the load, approve or masking-policy operation.
- API Specification v4 declares `x-module: P4` for `/admin/reference-loads`, `/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve` and `/admin/roles`, and TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A names the same operations as API-P4-005, API-P4-006 and API-P4-007.
- ADR-010 and D-RCV-35 U1 fix the identity boundary the contract restates: the clear identity number never leaves ACE, there is no token store, and `id_no_last4` is the clearest identity value any role can receive.
- Parameters `rwb.refload.approver.permission=RW-SECADM` and `rwb.refload.approver.masking_rule=RW-COMPLY` are in the catalog of rwb-case (RWB-E1-042, DP-06), and `LOV-CAPABILITY`, `LOV-SCOPE` and `LOV-ROLE-CLASS` are in the reference data of rwb-case (DP-07).
- The decision record is written through the local decision-record library of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON with decision code `AC-VERS` for a version approval (DP-03).
- The `rwb_access` baseline of RWB-PLT-E1044-CON holds the five tables and their dictionary rows; the baseline migration is the service template's, because WP B-P4-01 carries no DB story for this legacy key (DP-15, ASM-1418).
- The masking-shape function `recovery.ace_mask_value` and the `recovery.v_ace_*` columns are the ACE team's and RWB-P1-E1069-APP's; the contract names their field ids and owns no value.
- No approval stops the build: the contract is Draft (realignment v1) and is frozen when the consumers pass their contract tests (R-UNI-38 applies to the version, not to the document).

##### 4. Flow

1. Fix the four operations on the base `/api/recovery/access/v1`: the matrix load, the approve, the matrix read and the masking-policy read, each with its method, path, purpose, access right, request, answer and idempotency.
2. Fix the load shape: a multipart body with the file, the `table` value ("permission" or "masking_rule") and `validFrom`, answered 201 with the load id, the table, the `validFrom`, the status "Loaded" and the row count.
3. Fix the approve shape: no body, answered 200 with the version Approved; the approver role is the one the parameter names for the table, the caller may not be the loader, and the decision code is `AC-VERS`.
4. Fix the matrix read: for each role in force, its role code, its permission rows with the capability area and the letters, its default scope, the matrix version and the conflict version of its pairs, and no person.
5. Fix the masking-policy read: for each rule in force, the field id, the role code, `unmasked`, the masking version, `valid_from` and `valid_to`, and the statement that a field with no rule is masked and that a rule may not name the clear identity number.
6. Fix the error vocabulary: 401 with MSG-P4-001, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404 with MSG-P4-003, 409 with MSG-GEN-004 and MSG-P7-002, 422 with MSG-P1-002 and the failed check in the detail, 503 with MSG-GEN-006 and MSG-P7-003, all as RFC 9457 problem responses.
7. Fix the event: `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` on `rwb.access.events.v1`, published on the approval of a matrix or a masking version, carrying the version label, the change kind and the effective date, and no personal value.
8. Fix the negative statements: the contract owns no guard and no masker (those are RWB-PLT-E1037-CON), holds no session and no password (RWB-P4-E1022-APP), keeps no token (ADR-010) and owns no partner table (S9).
9. Publish the fakes of section 12.8 and wire the contract test into the build of the app stories of this service and of the consumers.
10. Publish the contract document with the nine tables of section 12 and record its version and its compatibility rule.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A consumer asks for a path the contract does not publish | The answer is 404 with MSG-P4-003 and no shape is guessed | MSG-P4-003 | AC1 |
| X2 | A matrix file misses a role, repeats a role and area, or holds a letter outside C, R, U, D, A and "-" | The load is refused in full with the failed check named and the version in force stays | MSG-P1-002 | AC2 |
| X3 | The caller of approve is not the role the parameter names for the table | Refused with 403 before the change | MSG-P4-002 | AC2 |
| X4 | The caller of approve is the person who loaded the version | Refused as a conflict and the version stays Loaded | MSG-P7-002 | AC2 |
| X5 | The decision record cannot be written | The approval does not take effect and nothing is published | MSG-P7-003 | AC2, AC4 |
| X6 | A masking rule names the clear identity number, or a field id that is not personal, or an unknown role code | The whole masking version is refused and the rule is named | MSG-P1-002 | AC3 |
| X7 | A consumer reads the matrix with no Platform administration R, or the masking rules with no Reference data R | Refused with 403 and the right named; a caller with no Workbench role gets 401 | MSG-P4-002; MSG-P4-001 | AC3, AC6 |
| X8 | A consumer treats the contract as the guard or the masker | The contract test fails: the guard, the masker and the annotation are RWB-PLT-E1037-CON's | None | AC5 |
| X9 | A consumer waits for a payload field the contract does not fix | The build fails the contract test rather than inventing the field | None | AC1, AC6 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; the contract refers to the parameter, reference-data, decision-record and library artefacts by name only |
| Negotiable | The payload details of the policy event and the right of the masking-policy read are agreed at the contract freeze; the four operations, the five objects, the approver rule and the vocabulary are fixed by the sources |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app stories of this service and every consumer that authorises or masks, from Day 1, against one frozen contract and its fakes |
| Estimable | Four operations, two load shapes, one approve shape, two reads, one event, one error vocabulary and six fakes |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion below is a contract test that the build of this service and of a consumer runs |

No legacy criterion is copied: legacy AC1 to AC13 of RWB-E1-037 belong to RWB-P4-E1037-APP, where they are carried verbatim with their origin tag, and the end-to-end form of the same outcome belongs to RWB-ITG-E1037-ITG (section 18).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The permission matrix version in force is the only source of what a role may do, and a capability area with "-" refuses every action in it | permission.letters (DF-REF-043), matrix_version (DF-REF-044); REQ-ACA-003; CTL-09 |
| BR2 | A matrix load is checked whole — every active role once for each of the 14 capability areas, letters from C, R, U, D, A or "-", known role codes — and a file with any error is refused in full | LOV-CAPABILITY; FSD P4 BR-P4-004; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 |
| BR3 | A version is approved by the role the parameter names for its table and never by the person who loaded it; the decision record is written before the change takes effect | Parameters rwb.refload.approver.*; Admin and access model section 3.3; CTL-05; CTL-06 |
| BR4 | The matrix answer carries role code, capability area, letters, matrix version, default scope and conflict version, and no person | TSD P4 v3 API-P4-007; FSD P4 A2.4 field catalog; NFR-039 |
| BR5 | A personal data field is masked unless the masking rule in force lets one of the session's roles see it; a masked field is filled from the masked view column or the last-four value, and a field with no rule is masked | Masking rules reference table; DL26; CTL-11; REQ-ACA-005; DF-ACE-073, DF-ACE-079 |
| BR6 | A masking rule names a field id that is personal and belongs to a `recovery.v_ace_*` view or a Workbench table, and a rule that names the clear identity number is refused | RWB-E1-069; Data Tier Map section 7; BR10 |
| BR7 | There is no tokenization and no token store; the clear identity number never leaves ACE and `id_no_last4` is the clearest value a rule or an answer may carry | ADR-010; Data Tier Map section 7; D-RCV-35 U1 |
| BR8 | A matrix or a masking version that reaches Approved is published as `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` with the version, the change kind and the effective date, and no personal value | Arch v5 slide 14 and slide 20; ASM-1417 |
| BR9 | Every operation declares the right it needs and a failure is a refusal, never an allow: 401 with no role, 403 without the letter, 503 when a dependency fails | TSD P4 v3 T-A; DP-08; ADR-020 |
| BR10 | The guard, the masker, the scope descriptor and the annotation are RWB-PLT-E1037-CON's and are not restated or re-implemented here | Arch v5 slide 10 and slide 35; RWB-PLT-E1037-CON |
| BR11 | This contract owns no session, no password, no token and no partner table, and it writes no table of P3 or P7 | DP-01; DP-02; Ownership Map; ADR-010 |
| BR12 | No business value is a constant in the contract or in its fakes: letters, scopes, masking positions, approver roles, versions and effective dates are data or parameters | FSD P4 BR-P4-004; BR-P4-005; DP-06; DP-07 |
| BR13 | A published version of the document is never edited in place: a breaking change is a new major version with a migration note and a new pin | Arch v5 slides 20 and 38; RWB-PLT-NF02-APP |

##### 9. State transitions

The contract holds no case status and no stored object; it fixes the states of a version and the shape of the answer a state produces. The version states are LOV-VERSION-STATUS (LOADED, VALIDATED, APPROVED, IN_FORCE, SUPERSEDED, ROLLED_BACK, REFUSED) in TSD P4 v3 T3.2, and the `state` column of the standard record columns holds them.

| Object | From | Event | To | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Contract document | Version 1 | A backward-compatible addition to an answer or a fake | Version 1, minor | Consumers build unchanged against the pinned version |
| Contract document | Version 1 | A breaking change to a path, an answer or the event payload | Version 2 with a migration note | A consumer moves only by changing the pin and passing the contract test |
| Matrix or masking version | No version | A load passes every check | LOADED | The load answer is 201 with the row count and the version label; no version is in force |
| Matrix or masking version | LOADED | The table's approver role approves it and the decision record is written | APPROVED | 200 with the effective date and one published policy event |
| Matrix or masking version | LOADED | A failed approval | LOADED or REFUSED | 403, 409, 422 or 503 with its message id; nothing published and the version in force unchanged |
| Matrix or masking version | APPROVED | The effective date arrives | IN_FORCE | Every new session resolves it and the answer names it |
| Matrix or masking version | IN_FORCE | A later version is approved | SUPERSEDED | The later version answers from its date and the older rows stay readable for audit |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The rwb-access contract owner (any team, per U3) | Publishes the document, the four operations, the five objects, the vocabulary, the event and the fakes; owns version 1 and every later version |
| The app stories of this service (RWB-P4-E1037-APP and the contract dependencies of its consumers) | Implement the contract and pass the contract test; raise a change request instead of a local override |
| RW-REFADM Reference data administrator | Loads a matrix or a masking version (Reference data C); approves none |
| RW-COE Center of excellence analyst | Holds Reference data C and may load; may not approve |
| RW-SECADM Security administrator | Approves a permission version, as the approver role the parameter names for the `permission` table |
| RW-COMPLY Compliance and PDPA officer | Sets the masking values and approves a masking version, as the approver role the parameter names for the `masking_rule` table (DL26) |
| RW-AUDIT Internal audit | Reads every version and the approval entries; changes nothing |
| RW-PLATADM Platform administrator | Reads the matrix through the administration view (Platform administration R) |
| Every service that authorises or masks | Builds against this contract and RWB-PLT-E1037-CON and passes both contract tests; reads no P4 table |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A permission, a masking rule and a version are not a credit decision |

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |

| DF-REF-034, DF-REF-035, DF-REF-036, DF-REF-037, DF-REF-038, DF-REF-039 | `role` (P4 rwb-access) | id, role_code, role_name, role_class, default_scope, entra_group | Named only: carried in the matrix answer as role code, class and default scope |
| DF-REF-040, DF-REF-041, DF-REF-042, DF-REF-043, DF-REF-044 | `permission` (P4 rwb-access) | id, role_id, capability_area, letters, matrix_version | Named only: the matrix answer and the matrix load shape |
| DF-REF-198, DF-REF-199, DF-REF-200, DF-REF-201, DF-REF-202, DF-REF-203, DF-REF-204 | `masking_rule` (P4 rwb-access) | id, role_code, field_id, unmasked, masking_version, valid_from, valid_to | Named only: the masking load shape and the masking-policy answer |
| DF-REF-205, DF-REF-206, DF-REF-207, DF-REF-208, DF-REF-209, DF-REF-210, DF-REF-211 | `role_conflict` (P4 rwb-access) | id, role_code, conflicts_with, reason, conflict_version, valid_from, valid_to | Named only: the conflict version travels in the matrix answer |
| DF-REF-016 to DF-REF-062 | `delegation_limit` (P4 rwb-access) | the DoA fields | Named only: the DoA table this contract lists as a P4 object; its rows are written and read by RWB-P4-E1038-APP and RWB-P4-E2013-APP |
| DF-ACE-073, DF-ACE-074, DF-ACE-059, DF-ACE-078, DF-ACE-079 | `recovery.v_ace_customer` and `recovery.v_ace_contact` (P1 rwb-source-data) | id_no_masked, id_no_last4, date_of_birth, contact_value, contact_value_masked | Named only: the field ids a masking rule may name; no value is carried by the contract |
| No data of its own | the contract | None | The document stores nothing and the fakes hold only synthetic values |

Field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8, and the ACE fields are those of Physical Schema v6. Every row is named and none is written by the contract: the document fixes which field appears in which answer and which owner it comes from (DP-01), and a rule that names the clear identity number has no place in it (BR6, BR7).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/reference-loads` | Load a matrix file (table "permission") or a masking file (table "masking_rule") with `validFrom`; the body is multipart with the file, the table and the date; the answer is 201 with id, table, validFrom, status "Loaded" and rows | Reference data C (TSD P4 v3 API-P4-005; API Specification v4 `x-module: P4`) | `Idempotency-Key`; the same key returns the first answer |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve` | Approve a loaded version with the approver role the parameter names for its table, after maker and checker and the decision record; the answer is 200 with the version Approved and its effective date | Reference data A as declared; the approver role in force (TSD P4 v3 API-P4-006) | `Idempotency-Key`; a repeat approve of an Approved version answers 409 and writes nothing |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/roles` | The matrix in force: for each role, its role code, its permission rows with capability area and letters, its default scope, its conflict version and the matrix version | Platform administration R (TSD P4 v3 API-P4-007; the Ownership Map path) | Not applicable, read only |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/masking-policies` | The masking rules in force for the fields and roles of the session: field id, role code, `unmasked`, masking version, `validFrom`, `validTo` | Reference data R (Arch v5 slide 14 names the operation; the right is assumed, GAP-0779; ASM-1416) | Not applicable, read only |

All four paths sit on `/api/recovery/access/v1` (DP-13). The two load and approve operations keep the legacy shape of RWB-E1-037 section 12 and the path that API Specification v4 (`x-module: P4`) and TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A name; the R-PREC default ruling gives generic reference data to P3, so the contract states that these two operations carry **this service's own two tables only** and that lists, queues, timers, templates and parameters load through rwb-case (GAP-0779; ASM-1414). `GET /admin/roles` is one operation with one contract answered by two slices of this service: the role, class, scope and conflict fields by RWB-P4-E1019-APP and the permission rows and matrix version by RWB-P4-E1037-APP (ASM-1419). `GET /masking-policies` is the operation Arch v5 slide 14 names; neither the API Specification v4 nor TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A gives it a path, so the base rule of §R4 is applied and the gap is recorded.

Answers carry the dictionary field names DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-044, DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204 and DF-REF-205 to DF-REF-211, and the conflict version travels with each conflict pair. Errors: 401 MSG-P4-001; 403 MSG-P4-002; 404 MSG-P4-003; 409 MSG-GEN-004 or MSG-P7-002; 422 MSG-P1-002 with the failed check in the detail; 503 MSG-GEN-006 or MSG-P7-003. Both loads accept `Idempotency-Key`; the two reads are read only.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. This service consumes no REST operation to answer the four operations: the parameters and the lists reach it through the client libraries of DP-06 and DP-07, the decision record is written through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, and the session arrives in the caller's token. A consumer's call to this contract is one hop with a 2 s budget and a breaker, under DP-11.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` | `rwb.access.events.v1` | The change kind (`matrix` or `masking`), the version label, the effective date and the approver reference; no field value, no person, no case id and no letter of a role | On the commit of an approval of a matrix or a masking version, in the same transaction as the decision record (BR8) |

The payload shape is not fixed by any source — Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0779; ASM-1417) — and the contract forbids a personal value in it (BR7, NFR-040). The contract also states that the publish uses the outbox of the service baseline and that DP-09 and RWB-PLT-TE006-CON are not part of this slice (ASM-1420). `rwb.access.DoALimitChanged.v1` is published by RWB-P4-E1038-APP and is not published here.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. rwb-access is a reference-data owner in Arch v5 slide 14 (events: none) and reads the version in force from its own schema; this contract opens no subscription and writes no inbox row.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The four operations are synchronous REST in the caller's thread and the approval is one transaction. The six-monthly access review is a Temporal Schedule on the `rwb-access` queue owned by RWB-P4-AD008-APP; DP-10 is referred to by this contract and no workflow, activity or Schedule is registered here (ASM-1421).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Temporal Schedule and no quartz job belongs to the contract: a version takes effect on a date that the answer resolves, and the review Schedule of JOB-18 is RWB-P4-AD008-APP's.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Schema | Owner (ownership map) | This contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| `role` | `rwb_access` | P4 | Named; the matrix answer carries role code, class and default scope |
| `permission` | `rwb_access` | P4 | Named; the matrix load and the matrix answer |
| `masking_rule` | `rwb_access` | P4 | Named; the masking load and the masking-policy answer |
| `role_conflict` | `rwb_access` | P4 | Named; the conflict version of a role pair |
| `delegation_limit` | `rwb_access` | P4 | Named; its own contract is RWB-P4-E1038-CON |
| `outbox_event`, `processed_event`, `idempotency_key` | `rwb_access` | PLT library | Created by the service baseline; the policy event writes one outbox row |
| `decision_log_entry`, `approval` | `rwb_decision` | P7 | **Never written**; the approval entry goes through the decision-record library (DP-03) |
| `lov_value`, `reference_row`, `reference_version`, `parameter_catalog`, `parameter_value` | `rwb_case` | P3 | **Never read by SQL**; reached through DP-06 and DP-07 |
| `partner`, `partner_user`, `partner_instruction` | `rwb_partner` | S9 | **Never read and never written** (Ownership Map) |

The contract names the five P4 tables and owns none of another service's; no foreign key crosses a schema and no answer carries a row of a table outside `rwb_access`.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this contract |
|---|---|---|
| Matrix file fake | The multipart body of the matrix load | The version "PM-2026.12" with 756 rows that gives RW-LEGAL "R" in Queue and allocation, the refused file "PM-2026.13" with a duplicate row and the letters "RX" (AC2) |
| Masking file fake | The multipart body of the masking load | "MASK-SIT-01", in which only RW-CASEOWN sees DF-ACE-078 in clear, no rule for DF-ACE-059, and a refused rule naming the clear identity number (AC3) |
| Decision-record fake | RWB-PLT-E1027-CON | The written entry with code `AC-VERS`, the unavailable store, and the assertion that no value and no case reach it (AC2, AC4) |
| Parameters fake | RWB-P3-E1042-CON | "rwb.refload.approver.permission" = "RW-SECADM", "rwb.refload.approver.masking_rule" = "RW-COMPLY", "rwb.access.membership-refresh-minutes" = 5 (AC2, AC6) |
| Reference-data fake | RWB-P3-E1043-CON | `LOV-CAPABILITY` with 14 areas, `LOV-SCOPE` with OWN, TEAM, REGION and ALL, `LOV-ROLE-CLASS`, each with a version (AC2, AC3) |
| Approver fake | The approver rule of the approve operation | The table's approver, the loader who may not approve, a caller with no approver role, and the unavailable decision record (AC2, AC6) |

The six fakes are published with the contract document so that the app stories of this service and every consumer build and test with no running rwb-access, rwb-case or rwb-decision (AC6).

| Kafka | 1 event on `rwb.access.events.v1` | 0 | `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` on approval, through the baseline outbox |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** The contract lives with the service: `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access.matrix`, module `matrix`, with the OpenAPI 3.1 document, the request and answer records of the four operations, the error vocabulary, the event schema and the six fakes as resources of the module. Service base `/api/recovery/access/v1`, schema `rwb_access`, topic `rwb.access.events.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-access` (not used here). The implementation is RWB-P4-E1037-APP's.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables. The contract names the five P4 tables and no table of another service | none |
| DP-02 | `recovery_svc` login | One login per service: the contract states that the per-service rwb-access login serves the four operations | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`. Referred to; the app story of this key carries the dependency | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views. The contract names the view field ids a rule may use and reads no view | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library, for the two approver roles and the refresh interval | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case, for `LOV-CAPABILITY`, `LOV-SCOPE` and `LOV-ROLE-CLASS` | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library. This contract declares the rights the guard enforces and restates neither the guard nor its decision | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit. Referred to for the sibling six-monthly access review (JOB-18, RWB-P4-AD008-APP); no Schedule is registered here | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout: the four operations fix the one-hop shape and the fakes | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1`: every path is on `/api/recovery/access/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema. The contract adds no migration and states that the two unique indexes are the app story's | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting. The contract has no export and no lake endpoint | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route: the route renders the 403, the 404 and the masked field the contract fixes; SCR-43 and SCR-47 are not built here | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |

The H and C dependencies named in the last column belong to RWB-P4-E1037-APP and to the consumers; this contract story has no build dependency of its own, which is why its `H`, `C`, `I` and `X` rows read None.

**Hardware and software change.** The contract replaces the in-process call of the monolith's `recovery.access.matrix` package with four REST operations and one Kafka event: the matrix and the masking rules are asked of their owner instead of being read from the same connection, and the policy change reaches consumers as an event rather than as a restart. It adds no schema, no topic, no queue, no Schedule and no bucket beyond what the service and the platform already have, so no new hardware is implied.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| OpenAPI document | Document | The four operations of section 12.1, their requests, answers, errors and idempotency (AC1, AC2, AC3) |
| Load and approve shapes | Record set | The multipart load, the table value, the validFrom, the 201 answer and the 200 approve answer with the effective date (AC2) |
| Matrix answer | Record set | The role code, permission rows with area and letters, default scope, conflict version and matrix version, with no person (AC1, AC4 of the app story) |
| Masking-policy answer | Record set | The field id, role code, unmasked flag, masking version and validity of each rule in force (AC3) |
| Error vocabulary | Document | The six statuses with their message ids and the RFC 9457 problem shape (AC6) |
| Event schema | Schema | `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` with the change kind, the version and the effective date, and the prohibition on a personal value (AC4) |
| Division statement | Document | The one paragraph of section 2 and the negative statements of AC5 |
| Fakes and fixtures | Test asset | The six fakes of section 12.8 (AC6) |

**Build steps**

1. Write the OpenAPI document with the four operations, their access rights, requests, answers and statuses; run the contract test of a consumer against it (AC1, AC2, AC3).
2. Write the load and approve shapes and prove the 201, the 422 with the failed check, the 403 of the approver role, the 409 of the loader and the 503 of the decision record (AC2).
3. Write the matrix and masking-policy answers and prove that every policy row carries a version and that no answer carries a person (AC1, AC3).
4. Write the error vocabulary and the RFC 9457 shape; prove the six statuses and that no body, log or trace carries a personal value (AC6).
5. Write the event schema and prove that an approval publishes one event and that a failed decision record publishes none (AC4).
6. Write the division paragraph and the negative statements, and prove that the guard and masker are absent here and the policy rows absent from the library contract (AC5).
7. Publish the six fakes with their allow, refuse, unavailable and malformed cases, and wire the contract test into the build of RWB-P4-E1037-APP and of a consumer (AC6).

**Done when.** The six criteria pass as contract tests; the four operations and the nine tables of section 12 name their owner from the Ownership Map; the six fakes are published with the document; and RWB-P4-E1037-APP and one consumer build and pass their contract tests against the published version.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | The caller holds no Recovery Workbench role | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A caller without the letter an operation declares, or approve by a role that is not the table's approver | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | A path the contract does not publish, or a record outside the role's scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P1-002 | A matrix or masking file fails a check | The {source} load for {date} was refused: {check}. The previous load is still in use. |
| MSG-P7-002 | The loader calls approve on their own load | You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The approval cannot be recorded | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | A second approve of an Approved load, or a load that is not Loaded | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The store is unavailable | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |

The message ids and their wording are copied unchanged from RWB-E1-037; the contract adds no message of its own, and the Thai text of each follows DL10. Every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set; for MSG-P4-002 the `{action}` value names the action and never a case fact or a field value, and for MSG-P1-002 the `{check}` value names the failed check.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen of its own. What the contract fixes for the screens of the 19 services is the status and the message id a screen receives (401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404 with MSG-P4-003, 503 with no business data), the masked value a field carries, and the rule that no screen error reveals a token, an internal path or a personal value. SCR-43 Roles and access and SCR-47 Personal data are Epic 8 and out of scope (DP-19), and the route that renders them is RWB-PLT-N001-CON's.

The states an administrator sees through the contract are the states of a version: Loaded with its row count, Approved with its approver and effective date, in force from that date, superseded by a later version, or refused with the failed check named.

No test of this story is an integration copy: the contract is exercised against its own fakes, never against a live service, and no `-ITG` id belongs to it. The five contract test cases are new and carry no legacy cover.

The fifteen legacy test cases of RWB-E1-037 are `TC-E1-037-01`, `TC-E1-037-02`, `TC-E1-037-03`, `TC-E1-037-04`, `TC-E1-037-05`, `TC-E1-037-06`, `TC-E1-037-07`, `TC-E1-037-08`, `TC-E1-037-09`, `TC-E1-037-10`, `TC-E1-037-11`, `TC-E1-037-12`, `TC-E1-037-13`, `TC-E1-037-14` and `TC-E1-037-15`; they are owned and executed by RWB-P4-E1037-APP, with their end-to-end copies in RWB-ITG-E1037-ITG, and none of them is restated here.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract or in a fake: letters, scopes, masking positions, approver roles, versions and effective dates are data or parameters (BR12).
- No personal data in a payload, a fixture, an example or a log: the answers carry field ids and version labels, and the policy event carries no value (BR7, BR8).
- The contract owns no guard and no masker: the guard, the masker, the scope descriptor and the annotation are RWB-PLT-E1037-CON's and are not restated here (BR10).
- No session, no password, no token and no partner table: the session is RWB-P4-E1022-APP's, the token store does not exist and partners are S9's (BR11, BR7).
- Every failure is a refusal: 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 with their message id, never an allow (BR9).
- A published version is never edited in place; a breaking change is a new major version with a migration note and a new pin (BR13).
- No statement names a table outside `rwb_access` and no answer carries a row of another service's table (DP-01).

##### 1. Story

As a **product owner**, I want **the mapping of roles to capability areas, the scope of each role and the masking of each personal data field held as versioned rows in `rwb_access` that this service publishes and every screen and API applies, with the identity number masked inside the ACE view and contact values masked at the API**, so that **a change of rights is a data load with an approver, a person is scoped to the cases their role allows, and personal data shows unmasked only to the roles that need it**.

This is the rwb-access slice of legacy RWB-E1-037, and it is the data half of that legacy key. The legacy story held the matrix, the masking rules, the scope rule, the loader, the approver, the masker and the identity boundary in one package over one database. D-RCV-60 keeps the behaviour and separates who answers what:

- **This story, rwb-access (P4), schema `rwb_access`:** `permission` (DF-REF-040 to DF-REF-044) and `masking_rule` (DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204) written and read, `role` (DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-039) and `role_conflict` (DF-REF-205 to DF-REF-211) read, the whole-file checks of a matrix and a masking version, the approver check with maker and checker, the version in force on its date, the permission rows on `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/roles`, the rules in force on `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/masking-policies`, the load and approve operations on `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/reference-loads` and `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve`, and the publication of `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` when a matrix or a masking version is approved (DP-01, DP-13).
- **Not this story, the platform library (RWB-PLT-E1037-APP and RWB-PLT-E1037-CON):** the guard, the masker, the `@PersonalData` annotation, the scope descriptor and the fakes that every service binds. This story publishes the data the guard and the masker read; it implements neither, and it holds no copy of a library class.
- **Not this story, sign-in and session (RWB-P4-E1022-APP):** the Entra ID sign-in, the multi-factor check, the group-to-role answer, the session in the Redis store of gateway-bff, and the ending of a session when a group is removed. Criterion AC8 is carried here verbatim and is proven at the session boundary against the session contract; the session itself is E1022's.
- **Not this story, the access log and break-glass (RWB-P4-E1039-APP):** the access event stream, the refusal entry, the search and export of the access log and every break-glass grant. Criteria AC2, AC3 and AC12 name an access event; this story supplies the decision and the field ids, and the access-entry writer of E1039 writes the record through the local decision-record library (DP-03).
- **Not this story, the end-to-end proof (RWB-ITG-E1037-ITG):** the same business outcome across P4, P1, P3 and the library, including the ACE grant check of AC11 and the three-role masking test in SIT.
- **Not this story, P3 and P7:** `lov_value`, `reference_row`, `reference_version`, `parameter_catalog` and `parameter_value` are rwb-case's (DP-07, DP-06); `decision_log_entry` and `approval` are rwb-decision's (DP-03). This story writes no row of any of them.
- **Not this story, the six-monthly access review:** JOB-18 and its access review list are RWB-P4-AD008-APP's Temporal Schedule on the `rwb-access` queue. DP-10 appears in the pattern table as referred to; this story registers no Schedule, and the workflow-kit dependency is carried for that sibling.
- **Service naming:** base `/api/recovery/access/v1`, schema `rwb_access`, topic `rwb.access.events.v1` with the event `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-access` in namespace `rwb-recovery` (not used here), Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`.
- **Criteria and tests:** the thirteen legacy criteria are carried verbatim with their origin tag, and the part of a criterion that calls another service is exercised through that service's contract mock — `Given the rwb-case contract mock returns …`, `Given the rwb-decision contract mock returns …`, `Given the rwb-source-data contract mock returns …` — with every value, id and code of the legacy line kept. The fifteen legacy test cases are kept with their legacy cover in section 16.

##### 2. Business rationale

Audit findings record unsuitable user access to EFS and staff sending debtor data outside the bank, and today rights are set inside each system and cannot be shown for a past date. The legacy answer was one package that held the permission matrix (54 roles against 14 capability areas), the masking rules and the scope rule as versioned data, applied scope before permission on every request, and ended access at the next request when a person left. That answer is still the right one, and the realignment makes it a narrower and a stronger one: the policy is data with an owner and an approver, the enforcement is one library every service binds, and the personal value never leaves ACE.

This story is the policy owner. A matrix load is one file, checked whole, approved by a second person and in force from its date with no deployment; a masking load is the same path with Compliance as its approver. The rules the service publishes are what every screen, every API and every agent call applies, so a change of rights is a row and not a release: the measure is rule and limit changes made without a code release, target 100 percent (FSD P4 A2.4). Under D-RCV-35 there is no load of a token and no tokenization: ACE ingests the source row once, `v_ace_customer` exposes the identity number as `id_no_masked` and `id_no_last4` only, and `v_ace_contact` exposes the full phone, e-mail and address because notices and calls need them. Masking is therefore a rule over view columns, not a token stored at load, and `id_no_last4` is the clearest identity value any role can receive (ADR-010).

**The division of this legacy key is fixed.** The guard, the masker and the `@PersonalData` annotation that every service binds are the platform library contract **RWB-PLT-E1037-CON** and its app story **RWB-PLT-E1037-APP**. This story publishes the **data-side contract** of `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule`, `role_conflict` and `delegation_limit`: the five objects, their versions, the two loads and their approval, the two read operations and the policy event. RWB-P4-E1022-APP owns sign-in and the session, RWB-P4-E1039-APP owns the access log and break-glass, and RWB-ITG-E1037-ITG owns the end-to-end proof. Neither this story nor its contract copies a legacy section wholesale, and neither claims the other's deliverable.

The values the criteria use are the legacy values unchanged: matrix version `PM-2026.11`, the new version `PM-2026.12` with 756 rows, the rejected file `PM-2026.13`, masking version `MASK-SIT-01`, the production version `MASK-2026.11`, cases `RW-2026-000123` and `RW-2026-000456`, team `MTG-NE`, the role codes RW-REFADM, RW-SECADM, RW-LEGAL, RW-PHONECOL, RW-CASEOWN, RW-COE and RW-AUDIT, the group `RWB-SIT-RW-TEAMMGR`, the field ids DF-ACE-073 `id_no_masked`, DF-ACE-074 `id_no_last4`, DF-ACE-059 `date_of_birth`, DF-ACE-078 `contact_value` and DF-ACE-079 `contact_value_masked`, the area `QUEUE_AND_ALLOCATION`, the letters C, R, U, D and A, the scopes OWN, TEAM, REGION and ALL, and the messages MSG-P4-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003, MSG-P1-002, MSG-P7-002, MSG-P7-003, MSG-GEN-004 and MSG-GEN-006. It meets REQ-ACA-003, REQ-ACA-005, REQ-ACA-006, REQ-ACA-007, REQ-ACA-009 and REQ-ACA-011, and puts controls CTL-09, CTL-10 and CTL-11 in place.

Three assumptions fix the behaviour the sources leave to the run, and each is a register row: a matrix version and a masking version resolve at sign-in and stay until the session ends, so open work keeps the version it was decided under (ASM-1408); a person whose roles include both halves of a `role_conflict` row at the conflict version in force is refused the session (ASM-1409); and an unmapped or inactive group gives no role at all (ASM-1410). Values no source fixes are carried as placeholders: the path and the right of the masking-policy operation of Arch v5 slide 14, and the payload of the policy event — Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0778; ASM-1416) and (GAP-0778; ASM-1417).

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P4-E1022-APP is done (H, same lane): sessions resolve roles from Entra ID groups, the guard runs on every endpoint, and a session names the matrix version and the masking version it signed in under.
- RWB-P4-E1037-CON is published (H): the nine contract tables of this service, the four operations of section 12.1, the load and approve shapes, the approver rule, the error vocabulary and the fakes. This story implements it and adds no path.
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-E1037-CON and RWB-PLT-E1044-CON are in place: the decision-record library, the parameter and reference-data client libraries, the guard and masker library, and the migration baseline (DP-03, DP-06, DP-07, DP-08, DP-15).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is in place: the gateway-bff composite route that renders the 403 and the 404 and the masked field on the case record view (DP-19).
- RWB-PLT-E1071-CON is in place for the sibling six-monthly access review Schedule (JOB-18, RWB-P4-AD008-APP); this story registers no Schedule (DP-10, ASM-1421).
- RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON are published (C): the parameters `rwb.refload.approver.permission=RW-SECADM`, `rwb.refload.approver.masking_rule=RW-COMPLY` and `rwb.access.membership-refresh-minutes=5`, and the lists `LOV-CAPABILITY` (14 areas), `LOV-SCOPE` (OWN, TEAM, REGION, ALL) and `LOV-ROLE-CLASS`. This story builds against their fakes from Day 1 and never against the rwb-case build (DP-11). The five-minute refresh is the legacy assumption (DL38) and is carried as ASM-1413.
- RWB-P7-E1027-CON is published (C): the decision-record write contract, so the approval entry of decision code `AC-VERS` is written through it and no P7 table is touched (DP-03).
- The `rwb_access` baseline exists: `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule`, `role_conflict` and `delegation_limit` with their dictionary rows, created by the service baseline migration `V0001` of RWB-PLT-E1044-CON; WP B-P4-01 carries no DB story for this legacy key, so this story adds only its two unique indexes (DP-15, ASM-1418).
- Permission matrix version `PM-2026.11` is the version in force; `PM-2026.12` is the next version and carries 756 permission rows.
- Masking version `MASK-2026.11` is loaded with no unmasked rows in production until Compliance supplies the rules (DL26), so every personal field is masked for every role; SIT carries the test version `MASK-SIT-01`, in which only RW-CASEOWN may see `v_ace_contact.contact_value` in clear for DF-ACE-078.
- The masking rules name the view field ids of Physical Schema v6: DF-ACE-073 `id_no_masked`, DF-ACE-074 `id_no_last4`, DF-ACE-059 `date_of_birth`, DF-ACE-078 `contact_value` and DF-ACE-079 `contact_value_masked`, plus the customer number and name fields. `is_personal` on those rows of `sys_fields` is P1 rwb-source-data's registry, read through its contract and never copied here (DP-05).
- The matrix file covers the role roster of TSD P4 v3 T6.1 (42 role codes) and grows to the 54 roles the legacy criteria count; the number of roles and the 756 rows are carried as ASM-1415 with the register row.
- Every user, case, file and value in the tests is synthetic; no production role, entitlement or personal value is read, and no name is stored in a row, a log or a prompt.

##### 4. Flow

1. RW-REFADM prepares the matrix file from the approved workbook, with the application owner's approval reference in the file header, and calls `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/reference-loads` with table "permission" and the `validFrom` date.
2. PermissionMatrixLoader validates the file whole: every active role once against all 14 capability areas of `LOV-CAPABILITY`, letters only from C, R, U, D and A in that order or "-", known role codes of `role` at the version in force, and no required value empty. It stores the rows with state Loaded and the new `matrix_version`, and produces the difference report against the version in force (BR2).
3. RW-SECADM reviews the difference report and calls `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve`.
4. ReferenceLoadApprovalService checks that the approver holds the role the parameter names for the table and is not the person who loaded it, writes one decision-record entry with decision code `AC-VERS` and no case through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, and marks the version Approved with its valid-from date in one transaction (BR3, BR9).
5. On approval the service publishes `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` on `rwb.access.events.v1` with the version label, the change kind and the effective date, through the outbox of the service baseline and with no personal value (BR13).
6. From the valid-from date every new session resolves the new version, and a session already open keeps the version it signed in under (RWB-P4-E1022-APP; ASM-1408). The screens and endpoints that the new letters open need no deployment.
7. A person requests a list or a record; the session answer carries the scope descriptor built from the role's `default_scope` and the person's teams and regions, and the owning service applies it in its own query (BR4, BR5). This service answers the descriptor; it runs no query over a case.
8. The guard of RWB-PLT-E1037-CON tests the right in the capability area on the records inside the scope, with the letters of the permission rows this service publishes (BR1).
9. A consuming service reads `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/masking-policies` for the fields and roles of the session. For each field tagged as personal data, when no rule lets a role see it in clear the value comes from the masked view column (`v_ace_customer.id_no_masked`, `v_ace_contact.contact_value_masked`) or is masked where the view holds no masked column; when a rule allows it, the value comes from `v_ace_contact.contact_value` where ACE exposes it, or from `id_no_last4` for the identity number. There is no token and no detokenization call (BR6, BR10).
10. The clear `customer.identification_number` never leaves ACE: no Workbench column, token store or service returns it, and `id_no_last4` is the clearest identity value any role receives.
11. Criterion AC2, AC3 and AC12 name an access event; the decision and the field ids are this story's, and the access-entry writer of RWB-P4-E1039-APP writes one event with the field ids and their masked flags and never a value (BR11, ASM-1412).
12. On each request, the session compares the groups the session holds with the group answer of ACE common, refreshed at most every five minutes; where a group has been removed, the session ends and the request is refused with status 401 and MSG-P4-001 (BR8, ASM-1413). The session lifecycle is RWB-P4-E1022-APP's.
13. The version in force is read from `rwb_access` on each call, with no cache of another service's data and no cache of a peer's answer (ASM-1411).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A role without the right calls an action, for example a transfer | Refused with 403 before the handler runs; nothing changes; the refusal is passed to the access-entry writer of RWB-P4-E1039-APP | MSG-P4-002 | AC3 |
| X2 | A record outside the person's scope is requested | Refused with 404; the record is not returned and the count of excluded records is never shown | MSG-P4-003 | AC4 |
| X3 | A matrix file misses a role, repeats a role and area, or holds a letter outside C, R, U, D, A and "-" | The load is refused in full and the version in force stays | MSG-P1-002 | AC5 |
| X4 | The person who loaded a version tries to approve it | Refused; the version stays Loaded | MSG-P7-002 | AC6 |
| X5 | A role other than the table's approver role calls approve | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | AC6, AC13 |
| X6 | The decision-record write for an approval fails | The version is not approved and stays Loaded; nothing is published | MSG-P7-003 | AC7 |
| X7 | A leaver's group is removed while a session is open | The next request after the membership refresh ends the session | MSG-P4-001 | AC8 |
| X8 | No masking rule exists for a personal field and role | The field shows from the masked view column, or is masked where the view holds no masked column | None | AC9 |
| X9 | Two approve calls for the same load arrive at once | One approves and one decision-record entry is written; the second returns 409 and writes nothing | MSG-GEN-004 | AC10 |
| X10 | A rule asks for the clear identity number | The rule is refused at load; the clearest value a rule can name is `id_no_last4` | MSG-P1-002 | TC-E1-037-13 |
| X11 | A masking file names a role code the `role` table does not hold, or a field id that is not `is_personal` | The whole masking version is refused and the field is named | MSG-P1-002 | TC-E1-037-13 |
| X12 | The masking store or the matrix store is unavailable | The call answers 503 and no version changes | MSG-GEN-006 | AC7 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds on the session (RWB-P4-E1022-APP), the four contract fakes and the published contracts of this WP, all earlier in wave 1 |
| Negotiable | Letters, scopes, masking positions, approver roles and the refresh interval are data or parameters; Compliance sets the masking values under DL26 |
| Valuable | A change of rights takes effect by an approved load, and personal data is masked by default at the view and at the API |
| Estimable | One loader, one masking loader, one approval service, one catalogue read, one policy read and one event |
| Small | Fits a sprint with its tests as one slice of a legacy key whose criteria are already written |
| Testable | Each of the thirteen criteria below is one test in section 16, and the boundary parts are proven against the named contract mocks |
