The thirteen criteria above are the legacy criteria of RWB-E1-037, copied verbatim and tagged with their origin, with the cross-service part of a criterion expressed by the contract mock it runs against: `rwb-case` for GET /queues, GET /cases, GET /cases/{caseId} and POST /cases/{caseId}/transfer, `rwb-decision` for the decision-record entry and the access event stream, and `rwb-source-data` for the ACE view columns. Every value, id, code, field id, message id and version of the legacy line is kept. Where a criterion names the case record view (AC2, AC9, AC12) or the session (AC8), the value the user sees is produced by the policy this story publishes applied by the guard and masker library in the owning service; the end-to-end form of the same criterion is RWB-ITG-E1037-ITG, and the access record it writes is RWB-P4-E1039-APP's.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The permission matrix version in force is the only source of what a role may do; a capability area with "-" refuses every action in it | permission.letters (DF-REF-043), matrix_version (DF-REF-044); REQ-ACA-003; CTL-09 |
| BR2 | A matrix file holds every active role once for each of the 14 capability areas, with letters from C, R, U, D, A in that order or "-"; a file with any error is refused in full | LOV-CAPABILITY; reference data change process, step 3; FSD P4 BR-P4-004 |
| BR3 | A version is approved by the role the parameter names for the table, and never by the person who loaded it | Parameters rwb.refload.approver.*; Admin and access model, section 3.3; CTL-05 |
| BR4 | Scope filters records first and the permission is checked second; an out-of-scope record is never returned and the excluded count is never shown | role.default_scope (DF-REF-038); LOV-SCOPE; REQ-ACA-009 |
| BR5 | OWN means the cases the person owns or has a task on; TEAM means the cases in the person's team queues; REGION means the cases in the regions of the person's teams; ALL means every case | Key sheet, roles.txt |
| BR6 | A personal data field is masked unless the masking rule in force lets one of the session's roles see it; a masked field is filled from the masked view column (`id_no_masked`, `contact_value_masked`), or masked where the view holds no masked column; with no rule it is masked | Masking rules reference table; DL26; CTL-11; REQ-ACA-005; DF-ACE-073, DF-ACE-079 |
| BR7 | Masking is applied before data reaches a screen or an agent, by the masker of RWB-PLT-E1037-CON reading the rules this service publishes | NFR-039; NFR-040 |
| BR8 | A leaver's removal from a group ends the open session at the next request after the membership refresh; leaver removal is within the same working day | DL38; CTL-10; REQ-ACA-011 |
| BR9 | A version approval that cannot be written to the decision record does not take effect, and nothing is published | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; CTL-06 |
| BR10 | There is no tokenization and no token store; the clear `customer.identification_number` never leaves ACE, `v_ace_customer` exposes `id_no_masked` and `id_no_last4` only, and `id_no_last4` is the clearest identity value any role can receive | ADR-010; Data Tier Map section 7; D-RCV-35 U1 |
| BR11 | Every read of a personal data field is written to the access log with the field id and its masked flag, never the value; the writer is RWB-P4-E1039-APP's | REQ-ACA-006; RWB-E1-039 BR3; NFR-040 |
| BR12 | A masking rule names a field id that exists in `sys_fields` with `is_personal` true and belongs to a `recovery.v_ace_*` view or a Workbench table; a rule that names the clear identity number is refused | RWB-E1-069; Data Tier Map section 7 |
| BR13 | A matrix or a masking version that reaches Approved is published as `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` on `rwb.access.events.v1` with the version, the change kind and the effective date, and no personal value | Arch v5 slide 14; slide 20; ASM-1417 |
| BR14 | Every operation of this story demands the right it declares, through the guard of RWB-PLT-E1037-CON: Reference data C to load, the parameter's approver role to approve, Platform administration R to read the matrix, Reference data R to read the masking rules | TSD P4 v3 T-A; DP-08; TSD P4 v3 API-P4-006 |
| BR15 | No value a business person may change is written in code: the letters, the scopes, the approver roles, the refresh interval, the versions and the effective dates are rows and parameters | FSD P4 BR-P4-004; BR-P4-005; DP-06; DP-07 |

Where each rule sits in the target: BR1 and BR2 are answered from `permission` in `rwb_access` and the whole-file checks before any row is written. BR3 and BR9 are the approve path with the parameter's approver role, the maker and checker check, the decision-record write and the optimistic lock in one transaction. BR4 and BR5 are the scope descriptor in the session answer, applied by the owning service. BR6, BR7 and BR12 are the masking rules this service publishes and the masker that reads them. BR8 is the group comparison on each request, and the session lifecycle is RWB-P4-E1022-APP's. BR10 and BR11 are the identity boundary and the access record. BR13 is the policy event. BR14 and BR15 are the guard and the data rows.

##### 9. State transitions

None for a case; this story changes no case status (TSD P4 v3 T4). It moves a matrix or a masking version from Loaded to Approved and into force, or refuses it at validation, and it ends a session when a group is removed. The version status vocabulary is LOV-VERSION-STATUS (LOADED, VALIDATED, APPROVED, IN_FORCE, SUPERSEDED, ROLLED_BACK, REFUSED) in TSD P4 v3 T3.2, and the `state` column of the standard record columns holds it.

| Object | From | Event | To | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Matrix or masking version | No version of the table | A file passes every check | LOADED | The rows are stored with the version label and no version is in force yet |
| Matrix or masking version | LOADED | A second person holding the table's approver role approves it | APPROVED | One decision-record entry with code `AC-VERS`, the valid-from date, and `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` published |
| Matrix or masking version | LOADED | Any check fails, or the loader tries to approve, or the approver role is not held | REFUSED for a failed check; LOADED for a refused approval | No row of a refused version is stored; a refused approval changes nothing |
| Matrix or masking version | LOADED | The decision record cannot be written | LOADED | The version is not approved, nothing is published, and the call answers 503 with MSG-P7-003 |
| Matrix or masking version | APPROVED | The valid-from date arrives | IN_FORCE | Every new session resolves it; the version before stays readable with its end date |
| Matrix or masking version | IN_FORCE | A later version is approved with a later date | SUPERSEDED | The later version answers from its date; the rows of this one stay for audit |
| Session | RESOLVED | The person's group is removed and the membership refresh has run | ENDED | The next request answers 401 with MSG-P4-001; the session lifecycle is RWB-P4-E1022-APP's |

A version is never edited in place: a change is a new version with its own label and effective date, and a refused version leaves the version in force untouched.

| Role owners (level 2) | Request matrix changes for the roles they own |
| RW-REFADM Reference data administrator | Loads a matrix or a masking version (Reference data C); approves none |
| RW-COE Center of excellence analyst | Holds Reference data C and may load; may not approve |
| RW-SECADM Security administrator | Approves a permission version: the approver role for the `permission` table, from the parameter `rwb.refload.approver.permission=RW-SECADM` |
| RW-COMPLY Compliance and PDPA officer | Sets the masking rules and approves each masking version: the approver role for the `masking_rule` table, from the parameter `rwb.refload.approver.masking_rule=RW-COMPLY` |
| RW-AUDIT Internal audit | Reads every version and the approval entries; changes nothing |
| RW-PLATADM Platform administrator | Reads the matrix and the masking rules through the administration view; changes no row here |
| Access administrator (level 3, bank IAM) | Removes leavers and movers from Entra ID groups |

| Every bank role | Sees cases inside the default scope of its roles, with fields masked per the masking rules |
| ACE team lead | Owns the ACE tables and columns behind `v_ace_customer` and `v_ace_contact` |
| rwb-access service identity (the per-service login, DP-02) | Validates and stores a version, answers the two reads, writes the approval entry and publishes the policy event; holds no grant outside `rwb_access` |

Two values the sources do not fix are carried as placeholders. The path and the right of the masking-policy operation are named by Arch v5 slide 14 without a path in the API Specification v4 or TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A, so the base rule of §R4 is applied — Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0778; ASM-1416). The role count is a conflict between the legacy criteria, which count 54 roles against 14 areas for the 756 rows of AC1, and the roster of TSD P4 v3 T6.1, which lists 42 role codes — Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0778; ASM-1415); the story seeds and counts exactly the rows of the approved file and never a constant.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/reference-loads` | Load a matrix file with table "permission" or a masking file with table "masking_rule", with `validFrom`; validate whole and store the version as Loaded | Reference data C (TSD P4 v3 API-P4-005) | `Idempotency-Key`; the same key returns the first response |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve` | Approve a loaded version with the approver role the parameter names, after the maker and checker check, and write the decision record | Reference data A as declared; the approver role of the table in force (TSD P4 v3 API-P4-006) | `Idempotency-Key`; a repeat approve of an Approved load returns 409 and writes nothing |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/roles` | The permission rows of each role at the matrix version in force: role code, capability area, letters and matrix version, with the scope descriptor of the role | Platform administration R (TSD P4 v3 API-P4-007; Ownership Map path) | Not applicable, read only |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/masking-policies` | The masking rules in force for the fields and roles of the session: field id, role code, `unmasked`, masking version and validity | Reference data R (Arch v5 slide 14 names the operation; the right is assumed — GAP-0778; ASM-1416) | Not applicable, read only |

All four paths sit on the base `/api/recovery/access/v1` of DP-13. The two load and approve operations keep the legacy shape of RWB-E1-037 section 12 and the path of API Specification v4 `x-module: P4` and TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A (API-P4-005, API-P4-006), and they are the load and approve of **this service's own two tables**; the generic reference-load path for lists, queues, timers, templates and parameters stays with rwb-case (GAP-0778; ASM-1414). `GET /admin/roles` is the Ownership Map path and is one operation with one contract: RWB-P4-E1019-APP answers the role, class, default scope and conflict fields, and this story answers the permission rows and the matrix version of the same answer (ASM-1419). `GET /masking-policies` is the operation Arch v5 slide 14 names; neither the API Specification v4 nor TSD P4 v3 T-A gives it a path, so the base rule is applied and the gap is recorded.

Request and answer field names are the dictionary names DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-044, DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204 and DF-REF-205 to DF-REF-211; the answer envelope and the problem response are those of RWB-P4-E1037-CON. Errors: 401 no Workbench role (MSG-P4-001); 403 no letter or not the table's approver (MSG-P4-002); 404 no such load (MSG-P4-003); 409 a version of the same label exists, the load is not Loaded, or the caller loaded it (MSG-GEN-004, MSG-P7-002); 422 a failed check with the failed check in the detail (MSG-P1-002); 503 the store or the decision record is unavailable (MSG-GEN-006, MSG-P7-003).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None at run time. This service answers and calls no service on a request: the caller's identity and the group answer arrive in the session of RWB-P4-E1022-APP, the lists and the parameters arrive through the client libraries of DP-06 and DP-07, and the decision record is written through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON. The case, decision and source-data contracts of the criteria exist in this story only as test fakes (section 12.8), each one hop with a 2 s budget under DP-11.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` | `rwb.access.events.v1` | The change kind (`matrix` or `masking`), the version label, the effective date and the approver reference; no field value, no person and no case | On the approval of a matrix or a masking version, in the same transaction as the approval, through the outbox of the service baseline (BR13) |

The topic name and the event name are those Arch v5 slide 14 fixes. The payload shape is not specified by any source — Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0778; ASM-1417) — and the payload carries no personal data by BR13 and NFR-040. The publish uses the outbox of the service baseline; DP-09 and RWB-PLT-TE006-CON are not in this slice's pattern set, and the delivery guarantee is the platform event platform's (ASM-1420). `rwb.access.DoALimitChanged.v1` belongs to RWB-P4-E1038-APP and is not published here.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. rwb-access is a reference-data owner in Arch v5 slide 14, and the version in force is read from `rwb_access` on each call, so this story subscribes to no topic and writes no inbox row.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The load, the approve, the two reads and the publish are synchronous work in the caller's thread. The six-monthly access review (JOB-18) is a Temporal Schedule on the `rwb-access` queue owned by RWB-P4-AD008-APP; DP-10 is referred to here and this story registers no workflow, no activity and no Schedule (ASM-1421).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Temporal Schedule and no quartz job sits in this story: a version takes effect on its date, which is a value the read resolves, and the review Schedule of JOB-18 is RWB-P4-AD008-APP's.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access.matrix`, module `matrix`, in the service root `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`. Service base `/api/recovery/access/v1`, schema `rwb_access`, topic `rwb.access.events.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-access` (not used here).

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables. The five policy tables are `rwb_access`'s, the lists are P3's and the views are P1's | none |
| DP-02 | `recovery_svc` login | One login per service: the per-service rwb-access login; the ACE grant the identity test names is RWB-P1-E1069-APP's | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`; the approval entry of code `AC-VERS` is written through it | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views. This service reads no view: it holds the field ids the rules name, and the values stay with the owner | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library, for the two approver roles and the refresh interval | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case, for `LOV-CAPABILITY`, `LOV-SCOPE` and `LOV-ROLE-CLASS` with the version in force | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library: every operation demands the letter it declares before its handler runs | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit. Referred to: JOB-18 and its six-monthly access review are RWB-P4-AD008-APP's, and this story registers no Schedule | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, carried for that sibling |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout: the four operations of this story and the fakes of section 12.8 | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1`: every path of this story is on `/api/recovery/access/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema: `V1037_1__permission_version_index.sql` adds the two unique indexes | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting. The legacy lake copy of the decision log (RWB-E1-014) is retired and nothing here reads or writes a lake | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route: the route renders the masked field, the 403 and the 404 this story produces | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

All nine build dependencies and three contract dependencies of the metadata table are carried by this story except RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, which is carried for the sibling Schedule of JOB-18; no dependency is added beyond that row.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| AccessAndAdministrationController | Controller | The four operations of section 12.1; validation; problem responses with their message ids |
| PermissionMatrixLoader | Service | Validates a matrix file whole — 54 roles, 14 areas, letters CRUDA or "-", known role codes, no empty value — stores the rows as Loaded and builds the difference report (AC1, AC5) |
| MaskingRuleLoader | Service | Validates a masking file: known role codes, field ids present with `is_personal` true, and no rule naming the clear identity number; stores the rows as Loaded (TC-E1-037-13) |
| ReferenceLoadApprovalService | Service | The approver role from the parameter, the maker and checker check, the decision-record write, the status change and the publish, in one transaction on an optimistic lock (AC1, AC6, AC7, AC10, AC13) |
| MatrixCatalogueService | Service | Answers the permission rows, letters and matrix version of `GET /admin/roles` at the version in force, with the scope descriptor of each role |
| MaskingPolicyService | Service | Answers the rules in force of `GET /masking-policies` for the fields and roles of the session |
| ScopeService | Published interface | Builds the scope descriptor from `role.default_scope` and the teams and regions the session holds; the owning service applies it (AC4) |
| AccessPolicyEventPublisher | Service | Writes the outbox row of `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` in the approval transaction; no personal value (BR13) |
| AccessAndAdministrationRepository | Repository | Reads and writes `permission`, `masking_rule`, `role` and `role_conflict` in `rwb_access`; no statement names another schema |
| MaskingRule | Entity | Maps the `masking_rule` table |

**Database and migrations**

- Writes `permission` (role_id, capability_area, letters, matrix_version) and `masking_rule` (role_code, field_id, unmasked, masking_version, valid_from, valid_to) in `rwb_access`, each row carrying the `state` and `version` of the standard record columns.
- Migration `V1037_1__permission_version_index.sql` adds `uk_permission_version` on `permission (matrix_version, role_id, capability_area)`; `uk_masking_rule` on `masking_rule (role_code, field_id, masking_version)` comes from the baseline V0001. It adds no other object, and the baseline objects are the service template's (DP-15, ASM-1418).
- The approve path locks the load row (`version`), so two approvals of one load cannot both write: one commits and one answers 409 (AC10).
- DB access uses the per-service rwb-access login (DP-02). No grant on `rwb_case`, on `recovery` or on `public` is added by this story.
- The decision record is written only through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, never by SQL against a P7 table (DP-03).

**Configuration and reference data**

- Matrix versions `PM-2026.11` (RW-REFADM loads, RW-SECADM approves) and `PM-2026.12` with 756 permission rows; masking versions `MASK-2026.11` (values DL26, RW-COMPLY approves) and `MASK-SIT-01` for SIT.
- Parameters `rwb.refload.approver.permission=RW-SECADM`, `rwb.refload.approver.masking_rule=RW-COMPLY` and `rwb.access.membership-refresh-minutes=5`, read through RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1042-CON; the five-minute value is the legacy assumption and is carried as ASM-1413.
- `LOV-CAPABILITY`, `LOV-SCOPE` and `LOV-ROLE-CLASS` are read with the version in force through DP-07; no list value is a Java constant.
- The masking shape — the last four characters, or the first character and the domain of an e-mail address — is the view function `recovery.ace_mask_value`, owned by the ACE team, so no Workbench parameter sets it.

**Build steps**

1. `V1037_1__permission_version_index.sql` and the two unique indexes, proven by a second apply that reports the version as already applied (DP-15).
2. PermissionMatrixLoader with whole-file validation, the difference report and a failing fixture for each check; tests AC1 and AC5.
3. MaskingRuleLoader with the personal-field check and the refusal of a rule naming the clear identity number; the clear identity rule case of TC-E1-037-13.
4. ReferenceLoadApprovalService with the parameter's approver role, the maker and checker check, the decision-record write, the optimistic lock and the publish in one transaction; tests AC1, AC6, AC7, AC10 and AC13.
5. MatrixCatalogueService and MaskingPolicyService over the version in force, with the guard and the two rights; tests AC1, AC9 and the masking-policy contract cases.
6. ScopeService and the scope descriptor in the session answer, given to P3 as a repository test over `GET /cases` and `GET /cases/{caseId}` through the rwb-case mock; test AC4.
7. AccessPolicyEventPublisher with its outbox row and the no-personal-data assertion on the payload; the contract test of RWB-P4-E1037-CON AC4.
8. The boundary checks: the identity statement of AC11 against the source-data mock, the ACE grant half being RWB-P1-E1069-APP's; the session boundary of AC8 against the session contract, the session being RWB-P4-E1022-APP's; and AC2, AC3 and AC12 against the access-entry writer of RWB-P4-E1039-APP.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.access.permission-matrix`, read through the platform feature-flag library: off returns the version in force to the baseline file and refuses a load with MSG-P4-002. The switch changes no letter, scope, masking position or approver role.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass; the thirteen criteria are proven against the named contract mocks; the masker in SIT shows the same case to three roles with the expected masked and clear fields and Compliance signs that test; the two unique indexes are applied; a second version takes effect on its date with no deployment; and no statement in the package names a table outside `rwb_access`.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | Session ended after a leaver's group was removed | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-P4-002 | An action outside the role's permission, or approve by a role that is not the table's approver | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | A record outside the role's scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P1-002 | A matrix or masking file fails validation | The {source} load for {date} was refused: {check}. The previous load is still in use. |
| MSG-P7-002 | The loader tries to approve their own load | You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The approval cannot be written to the decision log | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | A second approve of a load already approved | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The reference data store is unavailable | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |

The message ids and their wording are copied unchanged from RWB-E1-037. Every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set and `detail` carrying the text with its placeholders filled; for MSG-P4-002 the `{action}` value names the action the caller tried and never a case fact or a field value, and for MSG-P1-002 the `{check}` value names the failed check and `{source}` and `{date}` name the version and its effective date. Thai text for each message follows DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen is built by this story. The matrix and masking versions arrive by file load until SCR-43 Roles and access and SCR-47 Personal data come in Epic 8 (FEAT-ADM-01, FEAT-ADM-14); the gateway-bff composite route renders the matrices from the two read operations in one hop (DP-19). A person sees the effect in the menu of RWB-P4-E1022-APP, in the masked fields of the case record view of RWB-E1-023, and in 404 responses for out-of-scope cases.

The states an administrator sees are the states of a version: Loaded with its difference report, Approved with its approver and effective date, in force from that date, superseded by a later version, or refused with the failed check named. A refused approval leaves the version Loaded and shows MSG-P7-002 or MSG-P4-002.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: letters, scopes, masking positions, approver roles, versions and the refresh interval are rows or parameters, and a new area or letter is accepted as data (BR15).
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts: tests use synthetic values, the access event lists field ids and their masked flag and never a value, and the policy event carries no value (BR11, BR13).
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or the service's own `v_ace_*` views, and this service reads neither: the field ids are named in the rules and the values stay in ACE (DP-05, BR10).
- No tokenization and no token store: the clear identity number never leaves ACE, no Workbench column, service or rule returns it, and a rule that names it is refused (BR10, BR12).
- A field with no masking rule is masked, and an unmasked contact value is read only where a rule allows it and every such read is audited (BR6, BR11).
- Default deny on every operation: a missing role answers 401 with MSG-P4-001 and a missing letter 403 with MSG-P4-002, never allow (BR14).
- One writer for a version: only the load and approve path of this story writes `permission` and `masking_rule`, the loading person never approves, and the decision record is written before the change takes effect (BR3, BR9).
- No statement names a table outside `rwb_access`, and no grant on another schema is added (BR1, DP-01).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: integration slice of RWB-E1-037 for RWB-ITG-W1. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **QA integration engineer**, I want **the end-to-end proof of the RWB-E1-037 permission matrix as data, the scope rule and the PDPA field masking across P4 rwb-access (matrix, roles, masking rules, the guard and the access log), P1 rwb-source-data (the ACE view boundary and the masked read) and the platform guard and masker library, with the decision records collected by P7**, so that **a rights change is a load with an approver, an out-of-scope record never returns, and the clear identity number never leaves ACE, proved on the real wave 1 services**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story holds the permission matrix (54 roles against 14 capability areas), the scope rule and the masking rules as versioned tables that every screen and API applies, with the `ScopeFilter`, `FieldMasker` and `AccessCheck` published interfaces inside one monolith. In the 19-service target the tables stay with one owner each (DP-01): the role, permission, masking_rule, role_conflict and delegation_limit tables sit with P4 rwb-access, and the entity and field registry with P1 rwb-source-data. The matrix is data in P4's schema and the fields it masks are data in P1's schema; no service reads the other's tables, and the suite reads both through the published contracts only.

The legacy published interfaces split three ways. The right check and the scope rule become the authorise contract of P4 rwb-access behind the platform guard library (DP-08), with one login per service (DP-02). The masking is applied by rwb-source-data at the data read, against the masking policy that P4 owns and publishes on `rwb.access.events.v1` (Arch v5 slide 46; D-RCV-35 U1), so the clear identity number never leaves ACE and the clear contact value is read only where the rule allows it. Parameters and reference data are read as data through the contracts of P3 rwb-case (DP-06, DP-07), and the legacy `recovery.access.matrix` package disappears with no replacement library of its own.

Every approval writes its local decision record in `rwb_access` in the same transaction and publishes `DecisionRecorded` to `rwb.decision-record.v1`, collected by P7 rwb-decision within five minutes (DP-03; ADR-022). Access policy changes travel as `AccessPolicyChanged` on `rwb.access.events.v1` (DP-10 is the Schedule only, and the legacy event marker belongs to the owner; DP-14 is not in the pattern list of this story and is not claimed). Every call in the suite is one hop with a 2 s timeout (DP-11) under the per-service REST bases (DP-13), each service keeps its own schema and its own Flyway sequence (DP-15), the data lake copy is removed and reporting comes from events (DP-17), and SCR-43 and SCR-47 are reached through gateway-bff but are not built here (DP-19).

The split is stated plainly. This ITG story owns no legacy acceptance criterion. Legacy AC1 to AC13 sit at component level with RWB-P4-E1037-APP and the platform library story RWB-PLT-E1037-APP, and the fifteen scenarios of section 7 are the integration proof across the two services and the shared topic. The I list of this story names P1, the platform library and P4 only, so the suite proves the scope and masking outcomes through P4's guard and P1's masked read, not through a P3 case read. The measure is unchanged from the legacy story: rule and limit changes made without a code release, target 100 percent (FSD P4 A2.4). The story meets REQ-ACA-003, REQ-ACA-005, REQ-ACA-006, REQ-ACA-007, REQ-ACA-009 and REQ-ACA-011 and supports controls CTL-09, CTL-10 and CTL-11.

Where the sources do not name who owns the matrix load operation at integration level, the exact masking read path between P4's policy and P1's read, the boundary of the platform guard and masker library, or how the scope is proved without a P3 case read, the suite asserts through the owners' contracts and records the open point as Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0358; ASM-0462), (GAP-0358; ASM-0463), (GAP-0358; ASM-0464) and (GAP-0358; ASM-0465).

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P4-E1037-APP is done: the permission matrix as data, the masking rules, the scope rule, the guard and the access log are in SIT on P4 rwb-access.
- RWB-PLT-E1037-APP is done: the guard library and the masker library are published and versioned for the wave 1 services.
- RWB-P1-E1069-APP is done: `v_ace_customer` and `v_ace_contact` exist, `recovery_svc` holds SELECT on them and no privilege on `public`, and the boundary rule is enforced.
- The published contracts of P4 rwb-access and P1 rwb-source-data are deployed under their own per-service bases behind gateway-bff, and permission matrix version PM-2026.11 is in force.
- A test version PM-2026.12 differs from PM-2026.11 in one letter, and a refused file PM-2026.13 carries a duplicate row and an invalid letter.
- Masking version MASK-SIT-01 is in force, in which only RW-CASEOWN may see `v_ace_contact.contact_value` in clear for DF-ACE-078. No unmasked rows go to PROD until Compliance supplies the rules (DL26).
- The synthetic users U-2101 to U-2109, U-2111 and the group RWB-SIT-RW-TEAMMGR exist in SIT, and the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG is available with its synthetic users and cases.
- The parameters rwb.refload.approver.permission=RW-SECADM, rwb.refload.approver.masking_rule=RW-COMPLY and rwb.access.membership-refresh-minutes=5 are loaded, read as data rows through the parameters contract of P3 rwb-case.
- No production data is used, and no production connection is opened.
- The release date 30 November 2026 is tentative; a date is not a condition of this story.
- This story has no build dependency, so it is ready on Day 1.

##### 4. Flow

1. QA integration engineer: seeds the synthetic users U-2101 to U-2111, the group RWB-SIT-RW-TEAMMGR, the 12 owned cases of U-2105 and case RW-2026-000456 of team MTG-NE from harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG, and signs the users in through gateway-bff as RW-REFADM, RW-SECADM, RW-LEGAL, RW-PHONECOL, RW-CASEOWN, RW-COE and RW-TEAMMGR; no production data is used.
2. Harness: loads matrix file PM-2026.12 as U-2101 with table "permission" and validFrom "2026-12-01" through POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/reference-loads, and asserts 756 rows with status "Loaded".
3. Harness: approves PM-2026.12 as U-2102 through POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve, then reads GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/roles and GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log and asserts one approval entry with final call "APPROVED", the load ID, version "PM-2026.12", 756 rows and approver "U-2102".
4. Harness: with the clock at 1 December 2026 signs in U-2103 as RW-LEGAL and calls POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise for Queue and allocation U; asserts the call is allowed, where under PM-2026.11 it was refused, with no deployment; reads the letters through GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/permissions.
5. Harness: signs in U-2104 as RW-PHONECOL, reads the data product record of case RW-2026-000123 through GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/{productCode}/records, and asserts id_no_masked "XXXXXXXXX1234" and contact_value_masked "XXXXXX5678" with no clear contact value read.
6. Harness: runs the refusals (U-2105 holding RW-CASEOWN for Queue and allocation U, the out-of-scope read of case RW-2026-000456, U-2101 approving its own load, U-2111 and U-2106 holding RW-COE approving) and records every status and message.
7. Harness: removes U-2107 from group RWB-SIT-RW-TEAMMGR at 10:00 and calls GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session at 10:06, after the 5 minute membership refresh; asserts 401 with MSG-P4-001 and a refused new sign-in.
8. Harness: loads the refused file PM-2026.13 as U-2101, reads the record of U-2105 as RW-CASEOWN where no masking rule covers `v_ace_customer.date_of_birth` (DF-ACE-059), and runs the two approval calls of AC10 for one load.
9. Harness: reads GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/data-dictionary/fields and GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness, runs the identity test with `recovery_svc` on `public.customer` and `recovery.v_ace_customer`, and with U-2109 reads the borrower's phone number on case RW-2026-000123.
10. Harness: writes the evidence report, removes the synthetic fixtures and restores the clock.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A role without the right calls an action, for example a transfer | Refused with 403 before the handler runs; nothing changes; the refusal is logged | MSG-P4-002 | AC3 |
| X2 | A record outside the person's scope is requested | Refused with 404; the record is not returned and the count of excluded records is never shown | MSG-P4-003 | AC4 |
| X3 | A matrix file misses a role, repeats a role and area, or holds a letter outside C, R, U, D, A and "-" | The load is refused in full; the version in force stays | MSG-P1-002 | AC5 |
| X4 | The person who loaded a version tries to approve it | Refused; the version stays Loaded | MSG-P7-002 | AC6 |
| X5 | A role other than the table's approver role calls approve | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | AC6, AC15 |
| X6 | The decision record write for an approval fails | The version is not approved and stays Loaded | MSG-P7-003 | AC7, AC12 |
| X7 | A leaver's group is removed while a session is open | The next request after the membership refresh ends the session | MSG-P4-001 | AC8 |
| X8 | No masking rule exists for a personal field and role | The field comes from the masked view column, or is masked by the masker where the view holds no masked column | None | AC9 |
| X9 | Two approve calls for the same load arrive at once | One approves; the second returns 409 and writes nothing | MSG-GEN-004 | AC10 |
| X10 | A rule asks for the clear identity number | The rule is refused at load; the clearest value a rule can name is `id_no_last4` | MSG-P1-002 | AC13 |
| X11 | A consumed call exceeds the 2 s timeout or returns a server error | The call is retried once under the suite policy; the evidence report records the call and the response; no assertion is made on unverified data | None | AC1, AC12 |
| X12 | The fixture set does not match the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG expectations, or the clock control cannot move the time | The suite fails as a harness fault and names the element; no service defect is raised | None | AC4, AC8 |

X1 to X10 are the legacy exception paths with their messages; X11 and X12 are added for the integration run.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | The suite is its own module and reuses the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG; it needs the three APP stories and the published contracts of P4 and P1, not their source code |
| Negotiable | The matrix files, the masking version, the letters, the scopes, the fixture sizes and the exact fault-switch mechanism are data or properties of the harness; the story fixes the assertions and the call set |
| Valuable | A rights change by load, a scope boundary and the masking of personal data are proved on the real wave 1 services, and the clear identity number is shown absent from every response, before wave 1 exits |
| Estimable | One suite module, one matrix file pack, one identity and grant test, one session control and one evidence report |
| Small | Fifteen scenarios over two services and two events; no service code and no schema change |
| Testable | Every scenario asserts a contract response, an access event, a status or a message; all data is synthetic |

```gherkin
    When the user reads the data product records for the case set
    Then 12 cases return and the total is 12
    Then the read of "RW-2026-000456" returns 404 with MSG-P4-003

  Scenario: AC5 A matrix file with an error is refused in full (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given matrix file "PM-2026.13" lists RW-CASEOWN twice for Case record and gives RW-AUDIT the letters "RX" in Reporting
    When U-2101 loads it
    Then the load is refused with MSG-P1-002 naming the duplicate row and the invalid letters
    Then no row of "PM-2026.13" is stored and "PM-2026.11" stays in force

  Scenario: AC6 The loader cannot approve (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given load "PM-2026.12" was loaded by U-2101
    When U-2101 calls approve on it
    Then the call is refused with MSG-P7-002 and the load stays "Loaded"

  Scenario: AC7 An approval that cannot be recorded does not take effect (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the local decision record write is switched to fail by the agreed test-only fault switch
    When U-2102 holding RW-SECADM approves load "PM-2026.12"
    Then the call returns 503 with MSG-P7-003
    Then the load stays "Loaded" and "PM-2026.11" stays in force

  Scenario: AC8 A leaver loses access at the next request (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given U-2107 holds RW-TEAMMGR and has an open session since 08:00
    And the access administrator removes U-2107 from group "RWB-SIT-RW-TEAMMGR" at 10:00
    When the user calls GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session at 10:06, after the 5 minute membership refresh
    Then the call returns 401 with MSG-P4-001
    Then the session ends and a new sign-in is refused

  Scenario: AC9 A personal field with no masking rule is masked (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given no masking rule in "MASK-SIT-01" covers `v_ace_customer.date_of_birth` (DF-ACE-059) for any role
    When U-2105 holding RW-CASEOWN reads the record through the P1 data product
    Then the date of birth shows masked as "XXXX-XX-XX"

  Scenario: AC10 Two approvals of the same load at once (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given load "PM-2026.12" is "Loaded"
    When two approve calls arrive at the same time from U-2102 and U-2108 holding RW-SECADM
    Then one call approves and one decision record is written
    Then the other returns 409 with MSG-GEN-004 and writes nothing

  Scenario: AC11 A role without the right is refused (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given test user "U-2111" holds RW-COE
    When the user calls the approve operation
    Then the call returns 403 with MSG-P4-002

  Scenario: AC12 A decision record that cannot be written blocks the approval (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the local record write is switched to fail for every call by the agreed test-only fault switch
    When an approved load and a refused right are attempted
    Then nothing is approved and no refusal is recorded as complete
    Then MSG-P7-003 is returned and the version in force is unchanged

  Scenario: AC13 The clear identity number never leaves ACE (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the recovery service identity `recovery_svc` in SIT
    And `v_ace_customer` holds the identity number "1234567890123" for person_key "P-0001"
    When the identity test runs
    Then SELECT on public.customer is refused with permission denied
    Then SELECT on recovery.v_ace_customer returns id_no_masked "XXXXXXXXX0123" and id_no_last4 "0123" and no column holds the clear value
    Then GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/data-dictionary/fields shows DF-ACE-073 and DF-ACE-074 and no field for the clear value
    Then no Workbench table, token store or service returns the clear identity number for any role

  Scenario: AC14 A read of a personal field is audited (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given U-2109 holds RW-CASEOWN, which may see DF-ACE-078 in clear
    When U-2109 reads the borrower's phone number on case "RW-2026-000123"
    Then one access event holds the case ID, field ID DF-ACE-078 and the flag "clear"
    Then the event holds no field value

  Scenario: AC15 Only the table's approver role may approve (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given load "PM-2026.12" is "Loaded"
    When U-2106 holding RW-COE calls approve on it
    Then the call returns 403 with MSG-P4-002
    Then the load stays "Loaded"
```

**Target reading.** Every scenario is new at integration level, because each one is re-expressed against the P4 and P1 contracts behind gateway-bff; the business values, the matrix versions, the masking version, the message IDs, the user IDs, the case IDs, the team code and the row count are the legacy values unchanged. AC11 is the legacy access test at integration level. AC4 proves the scope through the records of the P1 data product, because the I list of this story names P1, the platform library and P4 only and not P3 rwb-case (GAP-0358; ASM-0465). The guard and masker library is exercised through the P4 and P1 operations and is never called by the suite (GAP-0358; ASM-0464).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The permission matrix version in force is the only source of what a role may do; a capability area with "-" refuses every action in it | permission.letters (DF-REF-043), matrix_version (DF-REF-044); REQ-ACA-003; CTL-09 |
| BR2 | A matrix file holds every active role once for each of the 14 capability areas, with letters from C, R, U, D, A in that order or "-"; a file with any error is refused in full | LOV-CAPABILITY; reference data change process, step 3 |
| BR3 | A version is approved by the role the parameter names for the table, and never by the person who loaded it | Parameters rwb.refload.approver.*; Admin and access model, section 3.3; CTL-05 |
| BR4 | Scope filters records first and the permission is checked second; an out-of-scope record is never returned and the excluded count is never shown | role.default_scope (DF-REF-038); LOV-SCOPE; REQ-ACA-009 |
| BR5 | OWN means cases the person owns or has a task on; TEAM means cases in the person's team queues; REGION means cases in the regions of the person's teams; ALL means every case | Key sheet, roles.txt |
| BR6 | A personal data field is masked unless the masking rule in force lets one of the session's roles see it. A masked field is filled from the masked view column (`id_no_masked`, `contact_value_masked`), or masked by the masker where the view holds no masked column; with no rule it is masked | Masking rules reference table; DL26; CTL-11; REQ-ACA-005; DF-ACE-073, DF-ACE-079 |
| BR7 | Masking is applied before data reaches a screen or an agent | NFR-039; NFR-040 |
| BR8 | A leaver's removal from a group ends the open session at the next request after the membership refresh; leaver removal is within the same working day | DL38; CTL-10; REQ-ACA-011 |
| BR9 | A version approval that cannot be written to the decision record does not take effect | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; CTL-06 |
| BR10 | There is no tokenization and no token store. The clear `customer.identification_number` never leaves ACE; `v_ace_customer` exposes `id_no_masked` and `id_no_last4` only, and `id_no_last4` is the clearest identity value any role can receive | ADR-010; Data Tier Map section 7; D-RCV-35 U1 |
| BR11 | Every read of a personal data field is written to the access log with the field ID and its masked flag, never the value | REQ-ACA-006; RWB-E1-039 BR3; NFR-040 |
| BR12 | A masking rule names a field ID that exists in `sys_fields` with `is_personal` true and belongs to a `recovery.v_ace_*` view or a Workbench table; a rule that names the clear identity number is refused | RWB-E1-069; Data Tier Map section 7 |
| BR13 | The matrix, role, role_conflict, delegation_limit and masking_rule tables are P4 rwb-access's, and the entity and field registry and the ACE boundary are P1 rwb-source-data's; no service reads another's tables | DP-01, DP-05; Ownership Map |
| BR14 | An approval writes its local decision record in `rwb_access` in the same transaction and publishes `DecisionRecorded`, collected by P7 within five minutes; every call in the suite is one hop with a 2 s timeout | DP-03; ADR-022; ADR-020; DP-11 |

##### 9. State transitions

None for the case status. This story does not change a case status. It moves a reference load from Loaded to Approved, or to Refused at validation, and a session from Resolved to Ended when a group is removed.

| Object | State | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Reference load | Loaded, or Refused at validation | The rows of the version are stored with the new version name and no right changes yet; the loader may not approve it, no other role may approve it, and a file that fails validation stores no row |
| Reference load | Approved | The approver role named for the table approved the load, one local decision record is written in `rwb_access` and the version takes effect from its valid from date |
| Session | Resolved, then Ended | The session holds the roles and the scope of the version in force and the guard resolves the letters at each request; when a group is removed and the membership refresh has run, the session returns 401 with MSG-P4-001 and a new sign-in is refused |

The suite reads these states through the owners' contracts; it changes none of them directly, apart from the agreed test-only fault switch and the group removal in the ACE test double.

| QA integration engineer | Runs the suite, seeds the synthetic fixtures, reads the evidence report |
| Application owner (level 1, assumed DL02); role owners (level 2) | Approves each permission matrix version outside the Workbench, with the approval reference carried in the load file; requests matrix changes for the roles they own |
| RW-REFADM Reference data administrator | Loads a matrix or masking version (Reference data C). Approves none |
| RW-COE Center of excellence analyst | Holds Reference data C and may load; may not approve |

| RW-AUDIT Internal audit | Reads every version and the approval entries; changes nothing |

| Every bank role | Sees cases inside the default scope of its roles, with fields masked per the masking rules |
| ACE team lead | Owns the ACE tables and columns behind `v_ace_customer` and `v_ace_contact` |

No other role is in scope for this story.

Every value in the suite is synthetic.

None. The suite provides no REST operation. The names reserved for P2 rwb-integration — `/api/recovery/integration/v1`, `rwb.integration.events.v1`, `rwb-integration` and `rwb_integration` — are not used, and no rwb_integration table is written.

| Method and path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|
| POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise | P4 rwb-access | The guard check for Queue and allocation U by RW-LEGAL and by RW-CASEOWN |
| GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/permissions | P4 rwb-access | The letters in force for the signed-in role |
| GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/roles | P4 rwb-access | The roles and their default scope as data |

| POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve | P4 rwb-access | The approval, the loader refusal, the wrong approver role and the two approvals |

Every call is one hop with a 2 s timeout (ADR-020, DP-11). The paths use the per-service bases of DP-13.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The suite publishes no event.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Producer | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1 | rwb.access.events.v1 | P4 rwb-access | The suite waits for the policy change before it asserts the new letters and the new masking rule |
| rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1 | rwb.decision-record.v1 | every service, with the ledger owned by P7 rwb-decision | The suite waits for the ledger entry of the approval before it asserts the access log |

The suite consumes no other event, and it produces none.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. No workflow, activity or Nexus operation is started or awaited by this story; the guard and the masking are synchronous, and every call is a REST read or write.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Schedule is started, moved or waited for. The six-monthly access review list (JOB-18) is a P4 rwb-access Schedule and is not this story. The clock control moves the request time only.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The suite owns no table and never reads another service's schema (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

No service contract is faked: every call in section 12.2 goes to the real SIT service. AC7 and AC12 use the agreed test-only fault switch on the P4 decision-record write, and it is the only intervention in a running service. The subgroup membership change of AC8 is the ACE test double, which is an outside system and not a service contract. The platform guard and masker library is exercised through the P4 and P1 operations and is never called by the suite (GAP-0358; ASM-0464).

The dependency-added column records the build dependency of the owning story. The H and C dependencies in the table belong to the owning APP stories. The H, C and X lists of this story are exactly those of the metadata table: no H, no C, no X, and the three I dependencies RWB-P1-E1069-APP, RWB-PLT-E1037-APP and RWB-P4-E1037-APP. An ITG story waits on no build of its own.

Build steps:

1. Create the suite module next to harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG and wire the SIT endpoints of P4 rwb-access and P1 rwb-source-data through gateway-bff.
2. Prepare the matrix files PM-2026.11, PM-2026.12 and PM-2026.13 as data, with the 756 rows of PM-2026.12, and the masking file MASK-SIT-01 with the rule that lets RW-CASEOWN see DF-ACE-078 in clear and no rule for DF-ACE-059.
3. Implement AC1, AC5, AC6, AC10 and AC15: the load, the approval, the refused file, the loader refusal, the wrong approver role and the two approvals, with the exact messages and one writer per entry.
4. Implement AC2, AC9, AC13 and AC14: the masked identity and contact values, the no-rule field, the field registry, the view boundary and the audited clear read.
5. Implement AC3, AC4, AC11 and AC8: the guard refusal, the scope boundary through the P1 records, the role without the right and the session revalidation control (GAP-0358; ASM-0465).
6. Implement AC7 and AC12 through the agreed test-only fault switch on the P4 decision-record write, and assert that the version in force is unchanged.
7. Run the suite in SIT against the wave 1 release candidate, write the evidence report, remove the synthetic fixtures and restore the clock. The masking read path is asserted through the P1 record and the P4 policy response, because its internal wiring is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0358; ASM-0463).

Done when: all fifteen test cases pass in SIT against the published wave 1 contracts of P4 rwb-access and P1 rwb-source-data, the evidence report shows every masked value and no clear identity number in any response, log or event, and no service code or schema was changed by this story apart from the agreed test-only fault switch.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | Session ended after a leaver's group was removed | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-P4-002 | An action outside the role's permission, or approve by a role that is not the table's approver | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | A record outside the role's scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P1-002 | A matrix or masking file fails validation | The {source} load for {date} was refused: {check}. The previous load is still in use. |
| MSG-P7-002 | The loader tries to approve their own load | You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The approval cannot be written to the decision record | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | A second approve of a load already approved | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The reference data store is unavailable | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |

The message IDs and wording are copied from RWB-E1-037. No new message ID is added by this story. Thai text for each message follows DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story. A person sees the effect in the menu (RWB-E1-022), in masked fields on the case record view (RWB-E1-023) and in 404 responses for out-of-scope cases. SCR-43 Roles and access and SCR-47 Personal data are Epic 8. The suite reads through the P4 and P1 contracts only, and no screen is built or tested here.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: letters, scopes, masking positions, approver roles and the refresh interval are data rows read through the contracts.
- No personal data in logs, events, evidence or fixtures: field IDs and the masked flag only, never values.
- No cross-service table read: every assertion goes through the owner's contract, and the suite owns no table.
- ACE data only through the P1 contract or `recovery.v_ace_*`; the suite holds no grant on a `public` table and reads no ACE view directly outside the identity test of AC13. There is no tokenization and no token store: the clear identity number never leaves ACE, and no Workbench column, service or rule returns it.
- A field with no masking rule is masked, and an unmasked contact value is read only where the masking rule allows it; every such read is audited.
- One hop and a 2 s timeout on every call (ADR-020).
- The session end is enforced on the next request after the membership refresh and never by a job; the suite moves only its own clock.
- Synthetic data only, loaded by the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG, and no production access of any kind from the suite or its configuration.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: realigned from RWB-E1-038 for `rwb-access`, which becomes the only writer of the delegation of authority table. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **Risk and model risk officer (RW-RISK)**, I want **the delegation of authority (which approval level may approve which decision, by product, principal amount and second condition) held as a versioned table that the approval router reads**, so that **approval limits change by an approved data load and every approval can be checked against the limit that applied on its date**.

Inside `rwb-access` this is the delegation-of-authority reference-data capability of the legacy story RWB-E1-038, and it is the **only writer** of the table:

- Service `rwb-access`, schema `rwb_access`, REST base `/api/recovery/access/v1`, topic `rwb.access.events.v1` with event names `rwb.access.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-access` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`.
- **What this story owns.** The `delegation_limit` table and its per-service Flyway migration in `rwb_access` (DP-01, DP-15); the load of a delegation version and its whole-file validation; the approval of a version with the four-eyes control and the approver role read from a parameter; the version window `valid_from`/`valid_to`; the rollback of a version; the parameter and reference-data reads the load needs (DP-06, DP-07); the authority check behind the load and the approval (DP-08); one access-log entry per approval or refusal (DP-03); and the `rwb.access.DoaLimitChanged.v1` event that tells the other services a version moved.
- **What this story does not own.** The lookup that the approval router calls — level, row and version for one decision and one date — is RWB-P4-E2013-APP's `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/doa-limits`, and it only reads the rows this story writes. The approval record, `ApprovalWorkflow`, the approval endpoints, the case status, the decision task, the escalation and the central decision log entry are `rwb-decision`'s (P7). The rule-package governance of the same authorise-and-date discipline is RWB-P4-E2041-APP and RWB-P4-E2042-APP.
- **The legacy story is moved, not reworked.** Its nine acceptance criteria are carried word for word with the legacy story's numbering; what changes is the transport (four REST operations of this service in place of the monolith reference-load endpoints and the in-process `DelegationOfAuthority` interface) and the schema (one table owned by one service in `rwb_access`). No business value of the legacy story changes.
- **Reference data, not code.** Levels L1 to L6, products, decision codes and regulation items are rows of `delegation_limit` and values of reference lists read through DP-07; the approver role is a parameter read through DP-06. No limit, level, product or role is written in code.

##### 2. Business rationale

Approval and authority governance is an audit finding, and limits today sit in the bank regulation and in people's heads. The legacy story loads the 95 limits of Regulation 540031 as amended by Regulation 690070 (chapter 2 for problem loans, chapter 3 for assets held for sale) as versioned rows and gives the approval router one lookup that returns the lowest approval level whose limit covers a decision, with the version used. In the target the table is still the same regulation in rows, but it belongs to one service: `rwb-access` writes it, `rwb-decision` and every approver read it through the contract, and no service keeps a copy of a limit or reads another service's table (DP-01, DP-11).

The target change is therefore a change of custody, not of policy. In the monolith the DoA matrix was a table of the recovery schema, loaded through a generic reference-load endpoint and read in process by `DelegationOfAuthority`. In the target the table is `rwb_access.delegation_limit`, loaded and approved through this service's own operations, and read only through RWB-P4-E2013-APP's lookup or the `rwb-access` authorise operation. The version window, the approve-and-date discipline and the four-eyes rule are kept exactly as the legacy story states them, and the same discipline is what the Drools rule packages follow (DP-04): a version is approved by a second person and takes effect on a date, not on the day it was approved.

This story meets REQ-ACA-004 (the delegation of authority table as reference data, setting every limit) and REQ-APD-010 (delegation changes versioned, approved and dated, and open items keep their version). It is the data behind control CTL-04 and supports the measure decisions within the delegation of authority: target 100 percent.

##### 3. Preconditions

| Precondition | What it gives this story |
|---|---|
| RWB-PLT-E1044-CON | The per-service Flyway sequence and migration conventions (DP-15) that carry `delegation_limit` into `rwb_access` |
| RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-P7-E1027-CON | The local decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03): the `AC-VERS` entry of an approved version and the `AC-DENY` entry of a refusal |
| RWB-PLT-E1072-CON | The embedded Drools kit (DP-04). This story evaluates no rule; the kit is the build dependency the legacy key carries, because the DoA table follows the approve-and-date discipline of the rule packages and the router that reads it evaluates rules in its own service |
| RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-P3-E1042-CON | The parameters client library and the `rwb-case` parameters contract (DP-06): the approver-role parameter `rwb.refload.approver.delegation_limit` |
| RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-P3-E1043-CON | The reference-data client library and the reference-data contract of `rwb-case` (DP-07): LOV-DECISION, LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL and LOV-PRODUCT with the version in force |
| RWB-PLT-E1037-CON, RWB-P4-E1037-CON | The guard library and this service's own authorise contract (DP-08): the role and permission rows behind the Reference data right, with the RFC 9457 refusal shape and MSG-P4-002 |
| RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). No screen of this story is served through it; it is carried because the delegation version read will be shown in the Epic 8 administration console (SCR-41) |

Business preconditions carried from RWB-E1-038:

- The reference-data load and rollback of the monolith are now this service's own operations, because the Ownership Map gives the generic reference-load path to `rwb-case` and `delegation_limit` to `rwb-access` (GAP-0970; ASM-1704).
- LOV-DECISION holds D5, D6.4, D6.5, D6.6, D7.1, D7.4, D7.5, D8.2, D8.3, D8.4, D9.2 and D9.3; LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL holds L1 to L6; LOV-PRODUCT holds MORTGAGE, HIRE_PURCHASE, SSME and UNSECURED. Under the R-PREC default ruling these are reference-data rows of `rwb-case`, read through DP-07, not rows of `rwb_access`.
- The parameter `rwb.refload.approver.delegation_limit=RW-RISK` exists in the parameter catalog of `rwb-case`, read through DP-06.
- The holder and substitute of each level are not yet named (DL18); rows load with `holder_user_id` and `substitute_user_id` empty in PROD and with named test users in SIT and UAT.
- The version in force in SIT is DOA-2026.11: 218 rows, 109 for MORTGAGE and 109 for SSME, with item 2.1.1 at L4 as two rows and item 2.1.10 at L1 on the related-party flag.
- The rollback of a version is in this story's scope, and no legacy acceptance criterion covers it (GAP-0971; ASM-1705).

##### 4. Flow

1. Reference data administrator (RW-REFADM) converts the Delegation of authority matrix to the load file: one row per limit and decision code, for MORTGAGE and SSME, amounts converted from THB million to baht, "No limit" to an empty value, "Up to X%" to `loss_pct_limit`, "At least X%" against fair market value to `min_price_pct_fmv`, "Once" and "Twice" to `max_delay_count`.
2. RW-REFADM calls `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/doa-loads` with the file, `table` = `delegation_limit`, `validFrom` and the version name, for example DOA-2026.11, and an `Idempotency-Key`. The path is this service's own, because the generic reference-load path of the monolith is `rwb-case`'s under the Ownership Map (GAP-0970; ASM-1704).
3. `DoaLoadController` validates the call: `table` must be `delegation_limit`, which is the only table this path accepts; `validFrom` and the version name are required, and an empty one is 422 with MSG-GEN-001 naming the field; a version name already loaded is 409 with MSG-GEN-004; a missing `Idempotency-Key` is 422. A repeated key answers the stored answer of the first call and writes no second row.
4. `DoaLimitLoader` validates the file whole, never row by row: every decision code, approval level and product must be a value of the reference lists in force (LOV-DECISION, LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL, LOV-PRODUCT, read through DP-07 and never written in code); every required field must be present; no two rows may repeat the same decision, regulation item, product, level and limits; and no level's highest principal limit may fall from L6 up to L1. Any failure refuses the load in full with 422 and MSG-P1-002 naming the check and the row, and stores no row.
5. On pass, `DoaLimitLoader` inserts all rows of the version in one transaction with the same `limit_version`, `valid_from` and status Loaded, and answers 201 with the load, the row count (218 for DOA-2026.11) and the difference report against the version in force: rows added, rows removed and rows changed, by decision, regulation item, product, level and limit.
6. Risk and model risk officer (RW-RISK) reviews the difference report and calls `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/doa-loads/{loadId}/approve`.
7. `FourEyesRule` and `ApproverRoleReader` check the approval: the approver reference of the caller must differ from the load's author reference, or the call is refused with MSG-P7-002; and the caller must hold the role the parameter `rwb.refload.approver.delegation_limit` names, or the call is refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002. The authority is the parameter role, not the Reference data A letter that the legacy contract document declares and no role holds.
8. On pass, `DoaVersionService` approves in one transaction: the rows of the new version move from Loaded to Approved; `valid_to` of the rows of the previous version is set to the day before the new `valid_from`; one decision-record entry of the DP-03 library is appended with decision code `AC-VERS`, the version, `valid_from`, the approver reference and no case; and the outbox row is written. An approval that cannot be recorded does not take effect: the transaction rolls back, the call returns 503 with MSG-P7-003 and the version stays Loaded.
9. After the commit, the outbox relay publishes `rwb.access.DoaLimitChanged.v1` on `rwb.access.events.v1`, keyed on the delegation version, so the other services refresh their cached reference view. The event carries the version, the table, the change kind and the two dates, and no personal data (GAP-0972; ASM-1706). The outbox row is written through the library created in `rwb_access`; the library's own contract is a service-baseline dependency rather than a row of this story's metadata (GAP-0973; ASM-1707).
10. `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/doa-loads/{loadId}/rollback` is the inverse of the approval, one call: the caller must hold the same approver role, the same four-eyes rule applies, the window of the rolled-back version and of the version before it is reversed, one `AC-VERS` entry records the rollback and the event is published. Only a version inside its own window may be rolled back; an approved version whose `valid_to` has passed is history and is never reopened (GAP-0971; ASM-1705).
11. `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/doa-versions` reads the versions with their state, `valid_from`, `valid_to`, row count, author and approver reference for RW-AUDIT and for the administration console. It is read only and carries the Reference data R right.
12. Every refusal of an approval or a rollback appends one decision-record entry with decision code `AC-DENY`, the version, the caller reference and the reason refused, and no personal data. A refusal of a load file at validation writes no record, because no row of that version was ever accepted and the legacy story stores nothing.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A file repeats a decision, regulation item, product, level and condition, or a level's highest principal limit falls below a lower level's | The load is refused in full; the version in force stays | MSG-P1-002 | AC4 |
| X2 | A file holds an unknown decision code, level or product, or a required field is empty | The load is refused in full | MSG-P1-002 | AC4 |
| X3 | The person who loaded the version approves it | Refused; the version stays Loaded; one AC-DENY entry with both references | MSG-P7-002 | AC5 |
| X4 | A role other than the parameter's approver role approves | Refused with 403; one AC-DENY entry with the area and the right | MSG-P4-002 | AC5 |
| X5 | The decision-record write for the approval fails | The version is not approved and stays Loaded; the transaction rolls back | MSG-P7-003 | AC6 |
| X6 | A lookup finds no row for the decision and product, for example hire purchase before the chapter 8 limits arrive | The lookup answers `NOT_COVERED` (RWB-P4-E2013-APP) and `rwb-decision` raises the incident to RW-RISK; this story supplies the rows and no incident path of its own | MSG-P7-010 (produced by `rwb-decision`) | AC7 |
| X7 | A lookup date falls on the last day of the old version or the first day of the new one | The version valid on that date is used, because `valid_to` of the old version is the day before `valid_from` of the new one | None | AC8 |
| X8 | A write-off is for a director, senior executive, major shareholder or related party | The L1 row of item 2.1.10 is stored with the related-party condition, so the lookup answers L1 whatever the amount | None | AC9 |
| X9 | The version name already exists | 409, nothing stored | MSG-GEN-004 | AC1 |
| X10 | A rollback is called on a version whose window has already closed | 409, nothing changed; an approved version that has expired is never reopened | MSG-GEN-004 | None |
| X11 | A rollback is called by a caller other than the approver role, or by the version's loader | 403 with MSG-P4-002, or MSG-P7-002 for the loader; one AC-DENY entry | MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-002 | None |
| X12 | The reference-data or parameter read is unavailable when a load arrives | 503, nothing stored; the load is retried under the same `Idempotency-Key` | MSG-GEN-006 | AC1 |

No exception path of this story changes a case, a task or an approval: this service writes the delegation table and the versions, and the state machine of an approval is `rwb-decision`'s.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against the platform contract stories, the parameter and reference-data contracts and its own authorise operation; the lookup that consumes the table is RWB-P4-E2013-APP's and the two stories share only the table |
| Negotiable | Limits, levels, products, regulation items, conditions, holders, substitutes and versions are rows; the approver role is a parameter; no value is fixed in code |
| Valuable | One approved, dated, four-eyes version of the regulation replaces a table that every module copied and a limit that lived in a document |
| Estimable | One migration, one loader, one approval gate, one rollback, one version read, one record appender, one event |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests; there is no screen, no workflow and no case state |
| Testable | Each of the nine owned criteria has a test case in section 16, and the lookup half of AC2, AC7, AC8 and AC9 is exercised against the published lookup contract and its fake |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Delegation of authority table as reference data

  Background:
    Given the environment is SIT
    Given test user "U-3101" holds RW-REFADM and test user "U-3102" holds RW-RISK

  Scenario: AC1 Table loaded (legacy RWB-E1-038 AC1)

    When "U-3101" loads it with table "delegation_limit" and validFrom "2026-11-30" and "U-3102" approves it

    Then every row has a decision code, an approval level and a product, and no two rows repeat the same decision, regulation item, product, level and limits

  Scenario: AC2 Lookup (legacy RWB-E1-038 AC2)
```
