These ten criteria are the legacy criteria of RWB-E1-039, copied with their values unchanged and tagged with their origin. Two things are read in the target shape and not in the monolith's: the path `POST /admin/break-glass` of AC2, AC5 and AC6 is the published operation `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/break-glass-grants` (the criterion keeps the legacy spelling), and the decision log of AC1, AC3, AC4, AC7, AC8 and AC9 is the local decision record of DP-03 in the serving service's own schema, with the central ledger of P7 behind `GET /decision-log` for the workbench-wide query of AC8 (GAP-0780; ASM-1425).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every sign-in, refusal, read of the case store or the document store, and export writes one access event to the decision record: one entry, in the same transaction as the response, hash-linked to the previous record of that chain | REQ-ACA-006; NFR-042; FEAT-ACA-08 |
| BR2 | A read or export whose access event cannot be written returns no data; the answer is 503 with MSG-P7-003 and an incident to the platform administrator queue | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; RB1 |
| BR3 | An access event lists field ids and their masking position, never field values; the clearest fact an entry may carry is the case id, the document id, the field id and the flag `clear` or `masked` | NFR-040; guardrail on personal data; RB7 |
| BR4 | Break-glass needs a grant approved by the security administrator in the bank IAM, an open incident reference and a reason of at least 20 characters; the requester and the approver are never the same person | Admin and access model, section 5.3; Access flow sheet, roles.txt; REQ-ACA-008 |
| BR5 | A grant ends at the earlier of the window (4 hours, assumed) and the IAM group end, with no action by anyone, and the end is enforced on every request rather than by a job | rwb.access.breakglass.window-hours; DL38; RB5 |
| BR6 | Every action under break-glass is marked with the grant id and the incident reference, in the `actions` element of the entry | Admin and access model, section 5.3; RB10 |
| BR7 | The security administrator reviews each use inside the review window (one working day, assumed); an unreviewed use goes to the head of SCB IT security and to Compliance | DL38; Access flow sheet, roles.txt |
| BR8 | A platform administrator holds only the letters of RW-PLATADM in the matrix version in force; any right beyond them comes only from an active break-glass grant | Admin and access model, section 3.2; permission matrix |
| BR9 | A person may not review their own break-glass use, and the reviewer is not the requester and not the approver | Admin and access model, section 6.2 |
| BR10 | The entry is written in the schema of the service that served the read and published to `rwb.decision-record.v1` from that service's outbox; P4 reads and writes no table of rwb-decision | DP-01; DP-03; Architecture v5 slide 28 |
| BR11 | The event codes, the areas, the scopes and the roles are reference data with a version, and the window, the incident pattern, the reason bounds and the review window are parameters; neither is a constant in code | DP-06; DP-07; BR-P4-007 |

##### 9. State transitions

No case status changes in this story. A break-glass grant and a decision-record entry have states of their own:

| Object | From | Event | To | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Break-glass grant | NONE | `POST /admin/break-glass-grants` with a verified group membership, a valid incident and a valid reason | ACTIVE | The AC-BGON entry is written; `startsAt` and `endsAt` are set to the earlier of the window and the group end |
| Break-glass grant | ACTIVE | The end time is reached | ENDED | The guard ignores the grant on every request with no action by anyone; the role's own letters apply |
| Break-glass grant | ACTIVE | An explicit end request from the requester or the security administrator | ENDED | Closed before the end time; the close is written as an entry and the grant is never reopened |
| Break-glass grant | ACTIVE | A second activation with the same Idempotency-Key | ACTIVE | The first answer returns and no second entry is written |
| Break-glass grant | ACTIVE | A second activation with a new Idempotency-Key | ACTIVE | Refused with 409 and MSG-GEN-004 |
| Access entry | NONE | An access event of the service | APPENDED | One entry, hash-linked; an entry is never updated or deleted |
| Access entry | APPENDED | The event is a refused call | APPENDED | An AC-DENY entry with the area, the right and the reason code |
| Access entry | APPENDED | The outbox relay publishes it | PUBLISHED | `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; the local entry is unchanged |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-PLATADM Platform administrator | Requests break-glass in the bank IAM and activates an approved grant with the grant operation (Platform administration C) |
| RW-SECADM Security administrator | Approves break-glass in the bank IAM, reviews each use and reads the access log (Platform administration R) |
| RW-COMPLY Compliance and PDPA officer | Reads the access log and receives the unreviewed uses |
| RW-AUDIT Internal audit | Reads the access log and queries access to a case through the central ledger; changes nothing |
| RW-COE, RW-DATASTEW | Read the access log (Platform administration R) |
| Every bank role | Generates access events by signing in, reading and exporting |
| The serving services of the workbench | Call the published writer through the guard and masker library; each writes in its own schema |
| SY-DECLOG Decision record writer | The DP-03 library identity that writes the entry and the outbox row in the caller's transaction |
| Head of SCB IT security | Receives a break-glass use that is not reviewed inside the window |

No person is named in this story; every actor is a role code or a test user reference.

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | the local decision record of DP-03, in `rwb_access` | all fields | Write (one entry per access event) |
| DF-DEC-002 | the local decision record of DP-03 | case_id | Write; empty for sign-in, refusal, export and break-glass events (change recorded in the additions file) |
| DF-DEC-030 | the local decision record of DP-03 | actor_user_id | Write, read |
| DF-DEC-003 | the local decision record of DP-03 | decision_code | Read (query by access event code) |
| DF-DEC-014 | the local decision record of DP-03 | actions | Read (area, right, fields, filter, row count, grant, incident) |
| DF-DEC-016 | the local decision record of DP-03 | decided_at | Read; the partition key of the log |
| DF-REF-035 | role (P4 rwb_access) | role_code | Read (the role whose letters the grant extends) |
| DF-REF-043 | permission (P4 rwb_access) | letters | Read (the letters of RW-PLATADM that the grant adds to) |

Field ids are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary. The entry is the decision record of the DP-03 library: it carries the field ids above, its `prev_hash` and `entry_hash`, and no personal value — the case id, the document id, the field id and the mask flag are the clearest facts it holds (BR3). **The access log is written through the local decision-record library of DP-03 to the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`**: the library commits the entry in the serving service's own schema and in the same transaction as the read, and publishes it from that service's outbox as `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1`. `decision_log_entry` in `rwb_decision` and the central ledger are P7 rwb-decision's and are not written, read or named as this service's table; `GET /decision-log` is P7's operation. The local decision-record table of the DP-03 library has no table name in the Ownership Map, so it is named by its contract and never by an invented table name (GAP-0780; ASM-1423). The break-glass grant is a row of `break_glass_grant` in `rwb_access`, created by RWB-P4-E1039-DB; this story reads the grant through the contract of RWB-P4-E1039-CON, whose seven legacy fields — the grant id, the incident reference, the IAM request id, the capability area, the right, the scope and the reason with its start and end — are the only grant values it names, and it adds no column of its own.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-access (P4); base `/api/recovery/access/v1`. The shapes are fixed by RWB-P4-E1039-CON; this story implements them.

| Method | Path | Shape | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log` | AccessLogPage over the entries of `rwb_access`: query `user`, `from`, `to`, `event`, `capabilityArea`, `page`, `size`; items with `at`, `user`, `event`, `capability`, `result`, `grantId`, `incidentReference`, `matrixVersion`, `maskingVersion` | Platform administration R, scope applied |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/break-glass-grants` | BreakGlassActivation in, BreakGlassGrant out: `grantId`, `incidentReference`, `capabilityArea`, `right`, `scope`, `startsAt`, `endsAt`; `Idempotency-Key` required | Platform administration C, plus membership of the break-glass group |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/break-glass-grants/{grantId}/end` | Closes an active grant before its end time and writes the close as an entry; `Idempotency-Key` required | Platform administration C, or the requester of the grant |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/break-glass-grants/{grantId}` | BreakGlassGrant with its state ACTIVE or ENDED, `startsAt`, `endsAt` and the IAM request id | Platform administration R |

Errors for the four: 401 the gateway-bff session envelope; 403 no right (MSG-P4-002), or no membership of the break-glass group on the grant operation (MSG-P4-007); 409 a grant is already active (MSG-GEN-004); 422 a field missing or invalid (MSG-GEN-001, MSG-GEN-002) or a period that ends before it starts (MSG-GEN-003); 503 the entry could not be written (MSG-P7-003). The end and read paths follow the base rule of DP-13 and the assumption in force, because no source names them (GAP-0780; ASM-1425).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

One hop per call, 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream (DP-11).

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` | P4 rwb-access (RWB-P4-E1022-APP) | The caller's roles, matrix and masking versions, and the break-glass state with the end time that the MSG-P4-004 banner shows |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | P3 rwb-case | The window of 4 hours, the incident pattern, the reason minimum of 20 and the review window of one working day (DP-06) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 rwb-case | LOV-DECISION with AC-SIGN, AC-DENY, AC-READ, AC-EXPT, AC-BGON and AC-VERS, and LOV-CAPABILITY, LOV-SCOPE and LOV-ROLE, each with its version (DP-07) |

No operation of rwb-decision, rwb-document or rwb-case's case read appears here: the caller of the writer already holds the case id, the document id and the field ids it passes, so P4 calls no service to build an entry.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | The DP-03 library of PLT, in this service's outbox | One message per access entry, with the entry id, the case id, the decision code, the actor reference, the grant id, the incident reference, `prev_hash` and `entry_hash`, in the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope |

This story publishes no business event on `rwb.access.events.v1`: the two policy events of the service, `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` and `rwb.access.DoALimitChanged.v1`, belong to RWB-P4-E1037-APP and the delegation story, and an access entry is not a policy change.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. P4 rwb-access is the reference-data owner of Architecture v5 slide 14, whose contract line records no consumed event; the access entry needs no subscription, and the break-glass state is read from the session, not from a topic.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The writer, the grant and the read are synchronous code in a REST handler; no workflow is started and no activity is registered for this key.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The six-monthly access review list (JOB-18) is a Schedule of rwb-access but belongs to RWB-P4-AD008-APP; this story registers none.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|
| `role` | P4 (rwb_access) | Read: the role code of the actor and the letters the grant extends (DF-REF-035) |
| `permission` | P4 (rwb_access) | Read: the Platform administration R letter and the matrix version (DF-REF-043) |
| `masking_rule` | P4 (rwb_access) | Read: the masking version an entry states |
| the local decision-record table of the DP-03 library | P4, in `rwb_access` | Written through the library; the access entries and their chain |
| `break_glass_grant` | P4, in `rwb_access` | Written and read; created by RWB-P4-E1039-DB, whose name for it is an assumption (GAP-0780; ASM-1423) |
| `outbox_event`, `processed_event`, `idempotency_key` | PLT library objects, created in `rwb_access` | The outbox row of each entry, the inbox the service does not use for this key, and the stored answer of the two POST operations |

**`decision_log_entry` and the central ledger are P7 rwb-decision's, and P4 writes no P7 table.** The ledger consumes `rwb.decision-record.v1` and answers `GET /decision-log`; this service publishes to the topic and never reads the ledger's tables, and it holds no copy of them. The grant table is a P4 table of this key: no source names it, so its name is the assumption in force and not a copied value.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access` for the implementation, with the writer interface published in `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access.api` so that the guard and masker library of RWB-PLT-E1037 binds one implementation rather than nineteen copies.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables. The entry is written in the serving service's own chain, and `decision_log_entry` is never read here | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library. The window, the incident pattern, the reason bounds and the review window are parameter rows | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case. The event codes, the areas, the scopes and the roles arrive with their version | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout. The writer call of the monolith becomes a contract call of the serving service to its own library, and the two P3 reads are one hop each | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/access/v1`; every path of this story sits under the service base | none |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting. The lake copy of the access log and its read logging leave with the lake, and P9 reads `DecisionRecorded` | none; no lake data is needed |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route. The access-log read and the banner reach the screen through the route, and SCR-43 is not built here | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Hardware and software change.** The `recovery.access.accesslog` package of the monolith is replaced by a writer that every service binds and a grant service in `rwb-access`. The entry leaves the monolith's single `decision_log_entry` and is written in each service's own schema through the DP-03 library; the central ledger of P7 collects it from `rwb.decision-record.v1` and answers the workbench-wide query. The ACE audit and PII path to the SOC is unchanged: every service still sends the audit fact through ACE Common (Architecture v5 slide 30), and the decision record is the second, durable copy. No new hardware is implied: the writer runs inside each service's existing pods, the grant service inside the `rwb-access` pods, and the only new objects are the four tables of RWB-P4-E1039-DB in `rwb_access`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `AccessEventWriter` | Published interface | Turns an access event into one decision-record entry and appends it through the DP-03 library in the caller's transaction (BR1, BR10) |
| `AccessEventPublisher` | Service | Builds the event from the request context — code, actor, case, area, right, result, field ids with the flag, filter, row count, document id, grant and incident — and raises the fail-closed error when the write fails (BR2) |
| `BreakGlassService` | Service | Verifies the group membership, the incident pattern, the reason bounds and the absence of an active grant; writes the AC-BGON entry; records the grant with `startsAt` and `endsAt` (BR4, BR5) |
| `BreakGlassGrantCheck` | Service | Adds the grant's right in its area and scope to the guard answer until `endsAt`, marks every entry with the grant and the incident, and ignores an ended grant on every request (BR5, BR6) |
| `GrantEndService` | Service | Ends a grant early, writes the close as an entry and refuses to reopen it (BR5) |
| `AccessLogQueryService` | Service | Maps the access-log read onto the entries of `rwb_access`, with the subject scope and the two version fields |
| `RefusalRecorder` | Service | Writes an AC-DENY entry for an admin call the matrix refuses, with the area, the right and no case id (BR1, AC9) |
| `BreakGlassBanner` contract element | Screen element | Shows MSG-P4-004 with the end time from the session answer, through the gateway-bff route (DP-19) |

**Configuration.** The four break-glass parameters come from the rwb-case catalogue through the parameters client (DP-06). The event codes, the areas, the scopes and the roles come from the reference lists with their version (DP-07). Nothing of either is a constant in code, and no environment value is read outside the parameter contract.

**Build steps**

1. Bind the DP-03 library and implement `AccessEventWriter` over it; prove one entry committed in the caller's transaction and one outbox row, with the `prev_hash` chain intact (AC1).
2. Extend `AccessEventPublisher` with the field ids and the mask flag, the filter and the row count, the document id, the grant id and the incident reference; test the case read, the export and the document read (AC1, AC3, AC4).
3. Make the read fail closed when the write fails, with 503, MSG-P7-003, no business data and the incident to the platform administrator queue (AC7).
4. Build `BreakGlassService` and the grant operation with the group check, the incident pattern, the reason bounds, the time box and the idempotency rule; test the granted case, the missing membership and the two validation refusals (AC2, AC5, AC6, AC10).
5. Build `BreakGlassGrantCheck` with the end time enforced on every request, a clock fixed at 10:30 and moved to 14:20 and 14:31, and the marking of every entry (AC2).
6. Build `AccessLogQueryService` and the read, with the subject scope, the period validation and the two version fields (AC8).
7. Build `RefusalRecorder` on the admin surface, so a refused admin call writes its AC-DENY entry with the area and the right (AC9).
8. Extend the session answer with the break-glass state and the end time, and hand the banner element to the gateway-bff route (AC2).
9. Run the ten criteria against the fakes of section 12.8 and hand the shapes to RWB-ITG-E1039-ITG for the cross-service proof.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.access.access-log`, read as a parameter per environment. Off, the writer still refuses a read it cannot record, so a switch-off never opens an unaudited path; it only stops the grant operation and leaves the matrix letters in force.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the entry of every access event is committed in the serving service's transaction and appears once on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, the grant ends at the earlier of the window and the group end with no action by anyone, a refused admin call writes its AC-DENY entry, the fail-closed path returns no data, and the break-glass test of the access test set (one request with an open incident, one without) passes in SIT and is signed by the security administrator.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-004 | Break-glass access is active; the banner shows the end time | Emergency access is on until {time}. Every action is recorded. |
| MSG-P4-007 | Break-glass requested with no approved IAM grant, or with no verified group membership | Emergency access needs an approved break-glass request in the bank IAM with an open incident. |
| MSG-P4-002 | An action after the grant has ended, or an access log query without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | Incident reference empty, or a required field empty | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-002 | Reason shorter than 20 characters or longer than 1000, or page size outside 1 to 500 | {field} must be between {min} and {max}. |
| MSG-GEN-003 | Query from date after to date | {field} cannot be before {other}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | A second activation while a grant is active | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The access event cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The ids and the texts are copied unchanged from RWB-E1-039; the story adds no message of its own. Thai text for each follows DL10, and the proposed Thai for MSG-P4-007 is the one recorded in the additions file. The 503 of the fail-closed path carries MSG-P7-003 and no personal data; the 401 of an expired session carries the gateway-bff session envelope, whose business message id is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0780; ASM-1425).

##### 15. Screens and states

| Screen | State | What the story supplies |
|---|---|---|
| The ACE front-end shell | Break-glass active | The MSG-P4-004 banner with the end time from the session answer, over every screen while the grant is active |
| SCR-43 Roles and access | Access log, list | The access-log read with the entries, `matrixVersion` and `maskingVersion`, paged at 50 and at most 200 |
| SCR-43 Roles and access | Access log, filtered | The same read narrowed by `user`, `from`, `to`, `event` and `capabilityArea` |
| SCR-43 Roles and access | Refused | The 403 with MSG-P4-002 and no list, plus the AC-DENY entry the refusal writes |
| SCR-38 Decision log query | Case access | The workbench-wide answer of P7's `GET /decision-log`, which is out of scope here and named for the audit journey only |

No screen is built in this story. SCR-43 belongs to Epic 8 and SCR-38 to Epic 2 (RWB-E2-005); the gateway-bff composite route of RWB-PLT-N001-CON merges the access-log read and the session read, one hop each, and renders the problem-detail shape of a refusal (DP-19).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the window, the incident pattern, the reason bounds, the review window, the event codes, the areas, the scopes and the roles are parameters and reference data with a version.
- No personal data in an entry, a log, an event, a test or a prompt: an entry carries the case id, the document id, the field id and the mask flag, never a value; the reason text is free text written by the administrator and must not hold customer data.
- No read of another module's tables: the entry is written in the serving service's own schema through the DP-03 library, `decision_log_entry` is P7's, and the access log is read through the owner's operation (DP-01).
- No right beyond the letters of RW-PLATADM without an active grant, and the grant end is enforced on every request rather than by a job.
- The read fails closed: an access event that cannot be written returns no data, with MSG-P7-003 and no business payload.
- No token store and no session table: the session is gateway-bff's, and P4 holds the roles, the policy and the access log only (ADR-010).
- The chain is append only: an entry is never updated or deleted, and its hash link is written in the same transaction as the entry.
- The central ledger is consumed by P7 and P9 and never by P4; a P4 path that reads `rwb_decision` fails the review.
- Every example and fixture is synthetic; no production payload is copied into a test or a fake.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the document half of RWB-E1-039 becomes the recorder of one `AC-READ` access entry per served document content read in `rwb_document`, written through the DP-03 library before the first byte of the file, marked with the grant and the incident while a break-glass grant is active, and failing closed when it cannot be written; the writer, the grant, the access-log read and the central ledger stay with rwb-access and rwb-decision. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **security administrator (RW-SECADM)**, I want **every read of a document's content through the Workbench to be written into the access log as one `AC-READ` entry before the file is returned, with the case, the document, the actor and — while emergency access is on — the grant and the incident, and to return nothing when that entry cannot be written**, so that **no document leaves the Workbench unrecorded and a document read can be audited from the same log as the decisions and the emergency access**.

This story is the `rwb-document` part of legacy RWB-E1-039 — the recorder of a document content read:

- Service `rwb-document`, schema `rwb_document`, REST base `/api/recovery/document/v1`, topic `rwb.document.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document`.
- What this story owns is one act, done once per served read: a local decision record with decision code `AC-READ`, the actor, the case id, the document id, the area and the right, and the grant id and incident reference when the caller holds an active break-glass grant — committed through the DP-03 library in `rwb_document` before the first byte of the file is streamed, and collected into the central ledger from `rwb.decision-record.v1`.
- What this story does not own, and must not build, is the access log, the writer of the access event, the break-glass grant, the two-person rule, the time box and the access-log read: they are rwb-access's in RWB-P4-E1039-CON and RWB-P4-E1039-APP. The central ledger, the `GET /decision-log` query and the chain verification are rwb-decision's in RWB-P7-E1039-APP. This service holds no access-log table and evaluates no grant (DP-01).
- Neighbours of the same legacy key: RWB-P4-E1039-APP (all ten legacy criteria), RWB-P4-E1039-CON (the shapes this story builds to), RWB-P4-E1039-DB and RWB-P4-E1039-OPS, RWB-P7-E1039-APP (the ledger and the query) and RWB-ITG-E1039-ITG (the end-to-end journey).
- The row the entry describes is written by RWB-P5-E1024-APP; the store's own decision record on a store is decision code `DOCATT` and is not this story; the content read is reached from SCR-30 Case documents (RWB-P5-E1026-APP) through the gateway-bff route.
- The entry carries references and codes only: the user id, the case id, the document id, the document type code and — while a grant is active — its id and incident reference. No person name, no account number, no identity number, no extracted field value and no file content is in the entry or in a log line.

##### 2. Business rationale

The bank cannot answer today who read a debtor's document on a given date, and an administrator with emergency access leaves no trace of what was opened. RWB-E1-039 answered both with one in-process publisher and one `decision_log_entry` table inside one module. In the target the entry is a decision record of the service that served the read (DP-03), the central ledger collects it from `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and the access-log read and the grant belong to rwb-access. For rwb-document the debt is exact: one correct entry, in the right transaction, before the bytes leave.

The architecture fixes each part: every service writes its decisions to its own chain through the library and publishes on the shared topic; the ledger collects them and answers the workbench-wide query (Architecture v5 slides 28 and 42; ADR-022); the write-once Blob copy is read only through this service (slide 9). The functional source states the same fact for the document hub: the module writes the decision log entry before any change and records each document read (FSD P5 A1, and the read rules of A2.1 and A2.6); the technical source gives the content read `Documents` right `R` with scope applied and the error set 401, 403, 404, 503 (TSD P5 API-P5-004, T6.1).

The value is trust in one category the case service cannot produce: the document read. It meets REQ-ACA-006 for the content read and REQ-ACA-008 for the marking of a break-glass read, and it supports controls CTL-09 and CTL-11. The measure is reads of the document store written to the access log: target 100 percent (NFR-042).

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P4-E1039-CON is published: the record shape of one access-log entry, the six decision codes `AC-SIGN`, `AC-DENY`, `AC-READ`, `AC-EXPT`, `AC-BGON` and `AC-VERS`, the optional `grantId` and `incidentReference`, the session answer with the break-glass state and its end time, the fail-closed rule and the refusal vocabulary. This story consumes those shapes and calls none of the four grant and log operations.
- The DP-03 library is part of the `rwb_document` baseline (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON): the local decision-record table, the chain and the publish of `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1`. This story writes rows, not DDL, and adds no build dependency of its own — the Work Package fixes "Depends on (build)" as None for this secondary slice.
- RWB-P5-E1024-APP is done: the `document` row exists with its case id, type, version, content hash and storage reference, and the file is in the write-once container. A content read of a missing or pending copy is the store's path, not this story's.
- LOV-DECISION holds `AC-READ` with the other access event codes, read through the reference-data contract of rwb-case at the version in force (DP-07, C RWB-P3-E1043-CON); no decision code is written in code.
- The caller's identity and break-glass state reach the service in the forwarded session envelope of gateway-bff, and the session answer of rwb-access is the authority for the grant (DP-19, DP-11). The mechanism that carries the grant id and the incident is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2339; ASM-3893).
- The tunables of this story — the name of the platform administrator incident queue, the lifetime of the cached session answer and the 2 s client budget — are parameter rows behind the parameters contract of rwb-case (DP-06, C RWB-P3-E1042-CON), never constants. The break-glass window and the review window are rwb-access's parameter rows and are not restated here.
- The exact capability-area code and result code of a document read in an entry are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2340; ASM-3894). Which P5 reads other than the content read write an entry is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2341; ASM-3895).
- No approval is required for a Draft story in this run; the story builds against the published contract and its fake (R5.4 class C).

##### 4. Flow

1. Caller: a user with `Documents` right `R` opens a document on SCR-30 Case documents and asks for its content; the browser calls `GET /api/recovery/documents/{documentId}/content` through gateway-bff, one hop.
2. `DocumentReadAuthoriser` takes the caller identity, the rights and the break-glass state from the forwarded session envelope, refuses a caller without `Documents` right `R` (403, MSG-P4-002) and a document outside the caller's scope (403) before any row is read for streaming.
3. `DocumentReadService` resolves the `document` row in `rwb_document` — case id, type, version, storage reference, content hash — and confirms the copy is present. A missing row answers 404 and a pending copy 503 with MSG-GEN-006; neither writes an entry.
4. `AccessEntryFactory` builds the entry from the row and the session, not from the request: decision code `AC-READ` from LOV-DECISION, actor user id, case id, document id, capability area and right of the operation, result, and the grant id and incident reference when the session carries an active grant.
5. `AccessEntryRecorder` writes the entry through the DP-03 library in the read's transaction, with the occurred time and the actor, and the library publishes `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` from the outbox. The entry carries no file content, no hash, no storage reference and no field value.
6. The write commits. Only now does `DocumentContentStreamer` open the blob and stream the bytes to the caller; the response carries no entry id and no ledger reference.
7. The central ledger of rwb-decision collects the record and answers the workbench-wide query; RW-AUDIT reads the reads of a case from that query with decision `AC-READ` (RWB-P7-E1039-APP, not this story).
8. RW-SECADM reads the same entries from `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log` of rwb-access, which is the access log the legacy story built (RWB-P4-E1039-APP).
9. While a grant is active: every entry this service writes carries the grant id and the incident reference, so the review of the use finds the document reads of the incident; at the end time the session stops marking and the grant stops applying, with no action by anyone.
10. A second read of the same document is a second read and writes a second entry: the log answers who read what and when, and a repeat by the same person on the same day is two facts, not one.
11. The entry is never written after the bytes: a read that cannot be recorded returns 503 with MSG-P7-003, no bytes and no partial file, and raises one incident to the platform administrator queue (AC2).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The entry cannot be written (library unavailable, chain refused, timeout) | The read returns nothing: 503, no bytes, no partial file, no retry that serves the file | MSG-P7-003 | AC2 |
| X2 | The session envelope carries no break-glass state, or an expired one | The grant is not applied and nothing is marked; the role's own letters decide the read, and the check runs on every request | MSG-P4-002 when the right is missing | AC3 |
| X3 | A caller without `Documents` right `R` asks for the content | Refused before the row is read and before any entry; the denial entry is rwb-access's | MSG-P4-002 | AC5 |
| X4 | The document is outside the caller's scope | Refused with 403 before any entry; no bytes and no case fact in the answer | None (the API's 403) | AC5 |
| X5 | The document id does not exist | 404 with no entry, no incident and no decision record — no read happened | None (the API's 404) | AC5 |
| X6 | The copy of the document is still pending | 503 with MSG-GEN-006 and no entry; the read is refused, not served empty | MSG-GEN-006 | AC5 |
| X7 | The reference-data read of LOV-DECISION fails | The cached version in force is used; if no version is cached the read fails closed with MSG-P7-003, because an entry without a listed code is not written | MSG-P7-003 | AC1, AC2 |
| X8 | The session answer does not arrive inside 2 s | The read fails closed with MSG-GEN-006 and no entry; the breaker opens and the next request is refused until it closes | MSG-GEN-006 | AC3, AC5 |
| X9 | The blob read fails after the entry is committed | The caller gets 503 and no bytes; the entry stands, because a read was attempted and refused, and the store's own path reports the storage fault | MSG-GEN-006 | AC2 |
| X10 | A caller asks for the content of an earlier version of a document | The row served is the version's own row; the entry names the document id of that version, so the log distinguishes the versions | None | AC6 |

X9 is the one path where an entry stands for a read that returned nothing. That is deliberate: the entry records the attempt to read the content and its refusal, and a log that lost it would hide the attempt.

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against RWB-P4-E1039-CON and its fake, the DP-03 library of the baseline and the store of RWB-P5-E1024-APP; no build dependency of its own |
| Negotiable | The grant-carrying mechanism, the cache lifetime and the queue name are open; the entry shape, the fail-closed rule and the order of entry and bytes are fixed |
| Valuable | Every document content read is auditable from one log, and an unauditable read is refused |
| Estimable | One authoriser, one entry factory, one recorder, one streamer and one contract test |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests, as a secondary slice of the legacy key |
| Testable | Each criterion of section 7 runs over the committed record and the response bytes, with the access contract and the library stubbed |

```gherkin
    Then the call is refused with status 403 before any record and no byte is returned
    And a document id that does not exist answers 404 with no record, no incident and no decision record
    And a caller without the Documents right is refused with MSG-P4-002 and no record

  Scenario: AC6 The record names the version that was served (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given document "DOC-2026-0009981" of case "RW-2026-000123" is at version 2 of type "COURT_NOTICE"
    When the content of version 2 is read

```

The six criteria are new and test only this deliverable: the record, its ordering against the bytes, the fail-closed path, the grant marking, the prohibition of a second access log, the refusals and the version. No legacy criterion of RWB-E1-039 is copied into this section: AC1 to AC10 belong to RWB-P4-E1039-APP, and their end-to-end form belongs to RWB-ITG-E1039-ITG. The values reused here are the legacy ones: case "RW-2026-000123", document "DOC-2026-0009981", the read time 10:15 on 3 December 2026, users "U-4101" and "U-4102", incident "INC0004521", the end time 14:30 with the read at 14:20 and the refusal at 14:31, and the messages MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-004, MSG-GEN-006 and MSG-P7-003.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every read of a document's content writes one access entry as it happens; here one record per served read, committed before the bytes (legacy BR1) | REQ-ACA-006; FEAT-ACA-08; NFR-042; legacy BR1 |
| BR2 | A read whose access entry cannot be written returns no data (legacy BR2) | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; legacy BR2 |
| BR3 | An access entry lists field IDs and their masking position, never field values; a content read names the case and the document and no extracted value (legacy BR3) | NFR-040; legacy BR3 |
| BR4 | Break-glass needs an approval in the bank IAM against an open incident and a reason of at least 20 characters; this service verifies nothing and accepts the rwb-access answer (legacy BR4) | Admin and access model, section 5.3; REQ-ACA-008; legacy BR4 |
| BR5 | A grant ends at the earlier of the window and the IAM group end, enforced on every request rather than by a job (legacy BR5) | rwb.access.breakglass.window-hours; DL38; legacy BR5 |
| BR6 | Every action under break-glass is marked with the grant and the incident reference; here every record written while the grant is active (legacy BR6) | Admin and access model, section 5.3; legacy BR6 |
| BR7 | A platform administrator holds only the letters of RW-PLATADM, which include Documents R; a right beyond them comes only from an active grant (legacy BR8) | Admin and access model, section 3.2; TSD P5 T6.1; legacy BR8 |
| BR8 | The entry is the serving service's own decision record and the ledger collects it; no service holds a second access-log table (DP-03, DP-01) | ADR-022; Architecture v5 slides 28 and 42 |
| BR9 | No personal data in the record, the log lines, the metrics or the tests: the actor is a user id, the document a reference, the case a reference (legacy guardrail) | NFR-040; legacy section 17 |

Target-service statements that make the rules hold in `rwb-document`:

- BR1 is executed by `AccessEntryRecorder` being the only path that writes the record, by the record being committed before `DocumentContentStreamer` opens the blob, and by the absence of any cached-serve path that returns a file without the record. A second read is a second record.
- BR2 is executed by the read's transaction: the record and the open of the blob are in one unit of work, so a failed record raises MSG-P7-003 and no byte is written to the response. There is no asynchronous after-commit log and no "log it later" queue on this side.
- BR3 is executed by the entry factory reading five columns of the row — case, document, type, version and the actor from the session — and by no field of `document_field` being read for the entry at all.
- BR4 and BR5 are executed by this service not evaluating a grant: `DocumentReadAuthoriser` takes the state from the session answer, which rwb-access has already bounded by its window and the group end, and re-reads it on every request, so a grant that ended one second ago cannot mark a record.
- BR6 is executed by the entry factory copying the grant id and the incident reference from the session answer onto the record, and by the refusal to derive either from the request: a caller cannot name a grant.
- BR7 is executed by the matrix of TSD P5 T6.1, where RW-PLATADM already holds Documents R, and by nothing in this service extending a right: the grant marks the record, it does not open a document the role could not read.
- BR8 is a prohibition with an owner elsewhere: the access log is rwb-access's and the ledger is rwb-decision's, so this service may write its own record and nothing else. A class that appends to a shared access-log table fails the build.
- BR9 is executed by the record's field list and by the test fixtures: no fixture carries a name, an identity number or a file body, and a personal-data pattern in the record or a log line fails the build.

##### 9. State transitions

No case transition: this story changes no case status and moves no stage. It adds the lifecycle of one access record and reads the lifecycle of the grant as rwb-access states it.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| (no record) | a content read is authorised and the row resolves | The caller holds Documents R, the document is in scope and the copy is present | record written, bytes not yet sent |
| record written | the record commits | The DP-03 library accepts the entry | `committed`; the library outbox publishes it on `rwb.decision-record.v1` |
| record written | the write fails | Library unavailable, chain refused, timeout | `none`; the read answers 503 with MSG-P7-003 and one incident |
| committed | the central ledger collects the record | rwb-decision's consumer group reads the topic | `collected`, and the ledger query answers it |

Read-only, for the reader of the record:

| Grant state (rwb-access answer) | What the record says |
|---|---|
| `ACTIVE` with end time 14:30 | The grant id and incident `INC0004521` are on every record written before 14:30 |
| `ENDED` | No grant on the record; a read the role cannot make is refused 403 with MSG-P4-002 and no record |
| No grant | The record carries the role's own right only |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-SECADM, security administrator | Reads the entries of document reads from the access log of rwb-access and reviews each break-glass use in the review window; Platform administration R |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Reads the document reads of a case from the ledger query of rwb-decision; changes nothing |
| RW-COMPLY, compliance and PDPA officer | Reads the same entries; receives an unreviewed use from the access side |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Holds Documents R and reads a document content; a read under an active grant marks the record, and the role gains no document right from it |
| Every bank role with Documents R | Generates the entry by reading a document content; the entry names the user id |
| SY-OCR and SY-AGENT | Read a document through the store and the extraction path, not through the content read; their reads are their own stories' |
| The rwb-document service identity (the rwb_document login, DP-02) | Writes the record in `rwb_document` through the DP-03 library and runs the outbox relay |
| Nobody | Holds an access-log table, appends to the access log of rwb-access, reads `rwb_access` or grants a break-glass right from this service |

The refusals are the operation's and are quoted, not built, here: MSG-P4-002 for a missing Documents right or a read after the grant has ended, MSG-GEN-006 for a document storage that cannot answer, MSG-P7-003 for a record that cannot be written.

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Table in `rwb_document` | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-DOC-001 | `document` | id | Read into the record as the document reference |
| DF-DOC-002 | `document` | case_id | Read into the record as the case reference |
| DF-DOC-004 | `document` | document_type (LOV-DOC-TYPE) | Read into the record as the type code |
| DF-DOC-011 | `document` | doc_version | Read to name the version that was served |
| DF-DOC-006 | `document` | storage_ref | Read to open the blob only; never carried in the record |
| DF-DOC-026 | `document` | content_sha256 | Read by the store's own check only; never carried in the record |
| DF-DEC-002 | the DP-03 local record in `rwb_document` | case_id | Write; empty for a sign-in, a refusal and an export, never empty for this read |
| DF-DEC-003 | the DP-03 local record | decision_code | Write `AC-READ` from LOV-DECISION |
| DF-DEC-014 | the DP-03 local record | actions | Write the area, the right, the result, the document id and, while a grant is active, the grant id and the incident |
| DF-DEC-016 | the DP-03 local record | decided_at | Write the occurred time of the read |
| DF-DEC-030 | the DP-03 local record | actor_user_id | Write the caller's user id |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | the DP-03 local record | all fields | Write (one record per read) as the library shapes them |

The row and the record carry different things on purpose. The `document` row holds the storage reference, the hash, the retention class and the party reference; the record holds references and codes. DF-DOC-003, DF-DOC-006, DF-DOC-009 and DF-DOC-026 stay in `rwb_document` and never travel, because the log needs to know *that* the content was read, of which document, by whom and when, and not what is in it. The legacy field IDs of the decision record are kept unchanged (DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018, with DF-DEC-002, -003, -014, -016 and -030 the ones this story writes); `decision_log_entry` and its index belong to rwb-decision, and no record of this service is written into `rwb_decision`. The legacy `decision_log_id` reference that the retention rows carry (DF-DOC-095) stays with the retention stories.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

One operation of the `rwb-document` contract changes behaviour; its path, request, response and error set stay those of the API Specification.

| ID | Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| API-P5-004 | GET | `/documents/{documentId}/content` | Download the document content; one `AC-READ` record is committed before the first byte; response Binary; errors 401, 403, 404, 503, with 503 and MSG-P7-003 when the record cannot be written and 503 with MSG-GEN-006 when the copy is not available | Documents, right R, scope applied | Not applicable, read only |

No field, header or path parameter is added, so a caller learns nothing new: no record id and no ledger reference is returned. A read that is refused for want of a record answers the same 503 envelope as a read the store cannot serve, and no caller can ask for "unlogged" content.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

One hop, 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream (DP-11). One operation at run time and two contract facts:

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` | P4 rwb-access | The caller identity, the roles and the break-glass state with the grant id, the incident reference and the end time; the state is re-read for the request, never cached across a request |
| — | the entry shape and the code list of RWB-P4-E1039-CON | P4 rwb-access | A fact and a fixture: `decisionCode`, `actorReference`, `caseReference`, `documentReference`, `capabilityArea`, `right`, `result`, `grantId`, `incidentReference` and `decidedAt`. This story writes its own record to that shape and calls no access-log operation |
| — | the parameters and reference-data contracts | P3 rwb-case | A fact: LOV-DECISION at the version in force and the tunables of section 13 (DP-06, DP-07) |

The access-log read `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log`, the two grant writes and the grant read are declared by RWB-P4-E1039-CON and are never called from this service. The ledger query `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` is rwb-decision's and is not called here either.

###### 12.3 Events published

None of its own. The access record leaves the service as the DP-03 library's message, named here so that the reader of the ledger recognises it and never declared as this story's contract:

| Message | Topic | Owner of the schema | Carries |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` (shared) | RWB-PLT-E1027-CON | The local record of this service, envelope and payload as the library defines them; key caseId, so the records of a case travel in order |

The service's own topic `rwb.document.events.v1` carries `DocumentStored` and `DocumentFieldsExtracted` only, and this story adds no message to it (DP-14): an access record is a decision record, not a document event.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. This story subscribes to no topic and creates no consumer group in `rwb_document`; the grant state is read from the session answer, not from an event.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The read is synchronous in the caller's thread, the record is written in that transaction, and no activity or child workflow is started. The `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` and its activities belong to RWB-P5-E1049-APP and RWB-P5-E1024-APP; queue `rwb-document` gains no task from this story.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The grant end is enforced on every request rather than by a job (BR5), the review window is rwb-access's parameter and its review list is RWB-P4-AD008-APP, and the outbox relay of JOB-11 is the platform's one-minute Schedule, not this story's.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |

| `document` | P5 (`rwb_document`) | Read for the case id, the type, the version and the reference; written by RWB-P5-E1024-APP |
| the DP-03 local decision-record table | PLT library, created in `rwb_document` | The `AC-READ` record, written in the read's transaction (DP-03) |
| `outbox_event` | PLT library, created in `rwb_document` | The record's outbox row, written by the library; the relay publishes it |
| `document_field` | P5 (`rwb_document`) | Not read by this story: the record carries no field value (BR3) |

No foreign-schema table is read (DP-01). `decision_log_entry` and its index are rwb-decision's, `break_glass_grant` is rwb-access's, and the case is a value taken from the `document` row, not a foreign key into `rwb_case`.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document`, module `accesslog`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document.accesslog`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| DocumentReadAuthoriser | Service | Takes the identity, the rights and the break-glass state from the forwarded session envelope; refuses a missing Document R and an out-of-scope document before the row is read for streaming |
| AccessEntryFactory | Service | Builds the `AC-READ` entry from the `document` row and the session: code, actor, case, document, type, area, right, result, grant id and incident; refuses a code outside LOV-DECISION and derives nothing from the request body |
| AccessEntryRecorder | Service | Writes the entry through the DP-03 library in the read's transaction and returns only when the record is committed; the single path that writes an access record in this service |
| DocumentContentStreamer | Service | Opens the blob and streams the bytes after the record commits; renders 503 with MSG-P7-003 when the record fails and 404 or 503 before any record when the row or the copy is missing |
| AccessRecordContractTest | Test component | Asserts the record against the shape of RWB-P4-E1039-CON and the library's message: fields, code list, grant marking, key caseId and the absence of a personal value |

**Database and migrations.** None, and that is the DP-15 statement for this story: the per-service Flyway sequence of `rwb_document` is not extended. The local record table and the outbox table arrive with the DP-03 library at the baseline; the `document` table is unchanged and no index is added, because the ledger query runs on rwb-decision's side.

**Configuration.**

- `rwb.document.access-log.queue` is the platform administrator incident queue, read as a parameter (DP-06); its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2342; ASM-3896).
- `rwb.document.access-log.session-cache` bounds the reuse of the session answer within one request only; a grant is re-checked for every read (BR5).
- `rwb.document.access.client.timeout` is the 2 s budget of the session read, with a breaker per downstream.
- `rwb.access.access-log` is rwb-access's flag and is not read here; this story adds no switch that can turn the entry off, because a switch that serves content unlogged is the fault the story prevents.
- The exact capability-area code and the result code of a document read are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2340; ASM-3894), and the mechanism that carries the grant id and the incident reference is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2339; ASM-3893).

**Build steps**

1. `DocumentReadAuthoriser` over the session envelope, with the missing-right refusal (MSG-P4-002) and the scope refusal before any record (AC5).
2. `AccessEntryFactory` over five columns of the row and the session, with a negative test per forbidden field (no hash, no storage reference, no field value, no person name) and the code check against LOV-DECISION (AC1, AC6).
3. `AccessEntryRecorder` inside the read's transaction, with the record-before-bytes assertion, the forced failure of AC2 and the one-record-per-read test.
4. `DocumentContentStreamer` after the commit, with the 404, the pending copy, the scope refusal and the blob fault of X9; no partial file on any path.
5. The grant marking from the session answer, with the 14:20 read marked and the 14:31 read refused before any record (AC3).
6. The negative tests of DP-01 and DP-03: no access-log table, no `rwb_access` read, no call of the access-log read or the grant operations, and no second writer of an access record (AC4).
7. The contract test against RWB-P4-E1039-CON and RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, then the same run against the real session and ledger in SIT.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables. The record is written in `rwb_document`, and `break_glass_grant` and `decision_log_entry` are only named | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`. This is the pattern that carries the story: one local record per read, published on the shared topic | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, satisfied by the baseline of `rwb_document`; the Work Package fixes this slice as a secondary story with no build dependency of its own |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library: the queue name, the cache bound and the timeout are rows, not code | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON (baseline) |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case: the `AC-READ` code and the other five codes arrive with the version in force | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON (baseline) |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout. The content read answers the caller and the session read is the only outbound call | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/document/v1`; the content read sits under the service base and no other base appears | none |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake). The legacy key knew a lake copy of the log and a lake read to be logged; neither exists, and no access record travels to a lake — the ledger of rwb-decision is the reporting path | none; no lake data is needed |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route: SCR-30 asks the document owner for the content and the session, one hop each; the route passes the identity and the grant claim | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON, satisfied by the platform baseline |

DP-03 is the pattern that carries the story, and DP-01 and DP-17 are the two prohibitions that shape it: no second access-log table inside this service, and no lake copy of the entry. DP-11 and DP-13 keep the read a one-hop REST call under the service base; DP-19 is the route it is reached through; DP-06 and DP-07 keep the values in rows and lists rather than in code. This is a secondary slice: it adds no new build dependency of its own. Metadata "Depends on (build)" stays `None` and "Contract dependencies" stays `RWB-P4-E1039-CON` exactly as the Work Package fixes them, and the platform libraries arrive with the baseline of `rwb_document`.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the contract tests of RWB-P4-E1039-CON and RWB-PLT-E1027-CON stay green, one document content read in SIT produces exactly one `AC-READ` record before the first byte with the case, the document, the actor and no personal data, a read under an active grant carries the grant and the incident, a forced record failure returns 503 with MSG-P7-003 and no bytes, and no class of the service writes an access-log row or reads `rwb_access`.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-003 | The access record of the read cannot be written, so no byte is served | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller lacks Documents right R, or reads after the grant has ended | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-004 | A break-glass grant is active for the caller; the banner shows the end time | Emergency access is on until {time}. Every action is recorded. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The document storage does not answer inside 2 s, or the copy is still pending | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |

The texts are the legacy texts, copied unchanged; this story adds no message id of its own. For MSG-P4-002 the {action} value names the action, for example "read a document", and never a case fact, a document type or a role name. For MSG-GEN-006 the {system} value is "Document storage". Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story, and no state on a screen. The read is reached from SCR-30 Case documents (RWB-P5-E1026-APP) through the gateway-bff route; the entries are read elsewhere — the access log on SCR-43 Roles and access (Epic 8) and the reads of a case on SCR-38 Decision log query (RWB-E2-005, RWB-P7-E1039-APP). The ACE front-end shell shows the MSG-P4-004 banner while a grant is active, from the session answer, and this story adds no field to that route.

The user-visible consequence is indirect and worth one sentence in the test pack: a document that will not be recorded does not open, and the user sees MSG-P7-003 instead of a file; the successful read looks exactly as it does today.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the decision codes come from LOV-DECISION through the reference-data contract, and the queue name, the cache bound and the timeout are parameter rows. No window, pattern or bound of the break-glass rule is restated in this service.
- No personal data in the record, the log lines, the metrics, the tests or the prompts. The actor is a user id, the document and the case are references, and the type is a code; no name, account number, identity number, extracted value or file body appears anywhere.
- The record is committed before the first byte and in the read's transaction. No after-commit log, no "log it later" queue and no cached serve that skips the record — a read that cannot be recorded is refused.
- No access log of its own (DP-01, BR8): no access-log table in `rwb_document`, no read of `rwb_access`, no call of `GET /admin/access-log`, of the grant operations or of the ledger query. A class that adds one fails the build.
- The grant is accepted, never evaluated or granted here. The grant id and the incident come from the session answer and never from a request field, and the end is re-checked on every request.
- No cross-schema read: the case and the document are values in the `document` row, and the copy is read through the write-once Blob reference, not through another service's table.
- One record per read and one read per record: no batching of reads into one entry, no sampling and no suppression for a service identity or a bulk reader.
- The record carries the reference of the version that was served, so two versions of one document are two facts in the log.

##### 1. Story

As **internal audit, and as the security administrator who reviews emergency access**, I want **every sign-in, refusal, read of a case or a document and export recorded as one entry in the central append-only, hash-chained decision ledger of rwb-decision, with the field IDs and their masking position and never a field value, and every entry written while a break-glass grant is active carrying the grant and the open incident**, so that **"who read this case, and under which emergency grant" is answered from one ledger, and each grant can be reviewed from the record it left**.

**The division of legacy RWB-E1-039 is fixed by this run.** The legacy story was one story in one process: it wrote an access event into the same `decision_log_entry` in the single `recovery` schema through a writer called in process, and it also owned the break-glass grant and the access-log read.

| Story | Owns |
|---|---|
| RWB-P4-E1039-CON | The published contract of the access log and of the grant: the entry shape, the operations, the refusal vocabulary and the fail-closed rule |
| RWB-P4-E1039-APP | The writer in the serving service, the break-glass grant with its time box, the access-log read of `rwb_access`, and the ten legacy acceptance criteria |
| RWB-P4-E1039-DB, RWB-P4-E1039-OPS | The schema of `rwb_access` and the deployment, alerts and run book |
| RWB-P5-E1039-APP | The access event of a document content read, where the document is served |
| **RWB-P7-E1039-APP (this story)** | The ledger's side: the ingest of the six access event codes into `decision_log_entry` in `rwb_decision`, the grant and incident marking, the review due time, and the access answer of the decision-log read |
| RWB-ITG-E1039-ITG | The end-to-end proof of the key across the services that serve the reads and the ledger |

This slice owns no legacy acceptance criterion: the ten criteria of the legacy story belong to RWB-P4-E1039-APP and are kept there word for word and tagged with their origin. The criteria of this story are new (`new, D-RCV-60`) and test only the ledger side named in the title. The store, the writer and the two reads are the other stories of this service and are named where they are relied on, never rebuilt here.

##### 2. Business rationale

The bank cannot answer today who read a debtor's record on a given date, and administrators hold standing access to production data. Legacy RWB-E1-039 answered both with one append-only, hash-chained decision log and a break-glass grant that names an incident, ends on its own and marks every action. In the target the log is still one ledger, but it is no longer one table written by one process: every service writes its own decision record in its own schema and publishes it, and rwb-decision keeps the central ledger that audit reads (Architecture v5 slides 28 and 42; ADR-022; DP-03).

That move puts three things on this story. First, the ingest: the ledger has to recognise the six access event codes, keep the shape of an access entry, and apply the rule that an access entry is not a decision about a customer — so the case ID is empty for a sign-in, a refusal, an export and a grant, and no field value is ever carried (legacy section 11, DF-DEC-002; NFR-040). Second, the break-glass record: an activation is an `AC-BGON` entry, a refused activation leaves no `AC-BGON` behind and a refused admin call is an `AC-DENY` entry, and every entry written while a grant is active carries the grant and the incident, so the review of a use reads one entry and sees both (legacy BR4 to BR8; FEAT-ACA-09, FEAT-ACA-10). Third, the answer: the legacy criterion "who read this case over a period" is a query of the ledger with the case, the access code and a period, and its third line is that the entry under a grant names the incident — that query is what makes the whole slice auditable.

The negative side is fixed as tightly as the positive one. No service writes or reads another's tables, so the grant, its time box and the permission matrix stay with rwb-access and the ledger records only what the event carries (DP-01). No personal value in an entry, a log or an event: the field ID and the flag are the clearest facts an entry holds (NFR-040; §17). And the data-lake copy of the log is gone with the lake, so reporting builds its read model from the same events (DP-17; ADR-018).

It meets REQ-ACA-006 and REQ-ACA-008 and supports controls CTL-09 and CTL-11; the measure is unchanged, reads of the case store and the document store written to the access log at 100 percent (NFR-042). Every legacy value used by a criterion is carried unchanged into sections 7, 12.8 and 16, so the fixtures of this slice and of RWB-P4-E1039-APP read the same numbers and identifiers.

The element names the ledger adds to an access entry — the grant, the incident and the review due time — are named by no published schema, the use of the code AC-VERS is described nowhere, and the payload names inside `actions` beyond the legacy list are open; this story builds to the assumption in force and records it as Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2452; ASM-4061).

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P4-E1039-CON is published (the one contract dependency of this story, class C, never blocking the build): the `AccessLogEntry` shape, the six access event codes, the grant vocabulary, the refusal reason codes and the fail-closed rule, as an OpenAPI 3.1 document plus its fake.
- The `rwb_decision` schema and login are in place from the service-template work (DP-02), with the base `/api/recovery/decision/v1`, the topics `rwb.decision.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1`, the task queue `rwb-decision` and the inbox table `processed_event` (DP-09).
- RWB-P7-E1008-APP is in place: `decision_log_entry` in `rwb_decision` with its legacy field identifiers, `chain_seq`, `prev_hash`, `entry_hash`, the append-only trigger, the unique key on the idempotency key and the chain verifier behind the nightly check at 02:00. This story appends and reads those entries and adds no column of its own.
- RWB-P7-E1027-APP is in place: the writer and the `DecisionRecorded` contract of the service, so the payload this story consumes has one shape and no second record type exists.
- The decision-record library of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is the published baseline, and the producer side of `rwb.decision-record.v1` is each serving service's own writer (RWB-P4-E1039-APP, RWB-P5-E1039-APP): DP-03 and DP-09 are the platform baseline of this slice, and the story record carries no build-order dependency of its own (metadata "Depends on (build)" = None, Template and Rules §R5.7 rules 2 and 3).
- The parameters client of RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and the reference-data client of RWB-PLT-E1043-CON are published, and RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON answer behind them (DP-06, DP-07). The value this story reads is `rwb.access.breakglass.review-days=1`, the legacy assumed value, kept as a parameter (DL38); the review due time is computed from it on the read and never stored (GAP-2452; ASM-4062).
- LOV-DECISION in the rwb-case reference lists holds AC-SIGN, AC-DENY, AC-READ, AC-EXPT, AC-BGON and AC-VERS with their version; the six codes are data and never a constant in code (DP-07).
- The gateway-bff composite route of RWB-PLT-N001-CON carries the decision-log read to the auditor's screen and renders a refusal in the route's problem-detail shape (DP-19).
- The readers hold Decision log R and the producing services hold Decision log C in the capability area; the authorisation decision is the cached permission decision the service template holds from rwb-access, and this story adds no guard of its own.
- Every fixture is synthetic: no production entry, case or grant is copied into a test or a fake.

##### 4. Flow

1. A person signs in, or reads a case record, a document or a list, or exports a list. The service that serves the read builds the access event and writes its own decision record in its own schema, in the same transaction as the read answer (RWB-P4-E1039-APP, RWB-P5-E1039-APP).
2. The serving service's outbox relay publishes `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1`. The event carries the access event code, the actor reference, the case ID where there is one, the area, the right, the result, the field IDs with their flag, the filter and the row count of a list or export, the document ID, the reason code of a refusal, the grant ID and the incident reference where a grant is active.
3. rwb-decision: `AccessEntryListener` reads the message in the inbox and keeps it only when its decision code is one of the six access codes; every other record is left to the consumer of RWB-P7-E1027-APP. A record already processed is answered with the first entry's ID and counted as a repeat; nothing is appended.
4. `AccessEntryMapper` maps the record to the access shape: the case ID only where the event has a case, an empty case ID for a sign-in, a refusal, an export and a grant; the `actions` element with the area, the right, the result, the field IDs and their flag, the filter and the row count, the document ID, the reason code, the grant ID and the incident reference.
5. `EntryFieldGuard` refuses a record whose `actions` carries a value instead of a field ID, with `MSG-P7-009` naming the element, and nothing is appended; an unauditable read is never recorded as clear data.
6. `AccessEntryWriter` appends one row to `decision_log_entry` in `rwb_decision` through the store of RWB-P7-E1008-APP, with `decision_code`, `actor_user_id`, `case_id`, `decided_at`, `actions`, the idempotency key of the event and the chain link. An entry is never updated and never deleted.
7. For an `AC-BGON` entry, `BreakGlassReviewDue` adds the review due time: `decided_at` plus the parameter `rwb.access.breakglass.review-days`, one working day at the legacy assumed value. For an `AC-DENY` entry the reason code, the area and the right are carried, with no case ID.
8. Internal audit asks `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` with the case ID, decision "AC-READ", `from` and `to`. The read returns the entries in time order with the actor, the time, the field IDs and their flags, and, where the entry was written under a grant, the grant ID and the incident reference.
9. A read of the ledger that cannot be served answers nothing: 503 with `MSG-P7-003`, no item, and an incident to the platform administrator queue. A partial page is never returned.
10. The ingest break is alerted and the message stays on the topic: the retry cadence and the dead-letter topic are the platform's, so an entry either exists in full with its chain link or does not exist at all.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The `actions` of a record carries a field value instead of a field ID | Refused with `MSG-P7-009` naming the element; nothing is appended | MSG-P7-009 | AC1, AC7 |
| X2 | A record carries a decision code outside the six access codes | Not an access entry: it is left to the record consumer and no access entry is appended | None | AC1, AC5 |
| X3 | The same event arrives twice with the same idempotency key | One entry; the first entry ID is answered and the repeat is counted | None | AC7 |
| X4 | The ledger cannot be appended | The message is retried and then parked on the dead-letter topic with its headers; no partial row and no half-written chain link exists | None | AC8 |
| X5 | The ledger cannot be read | 503 with `MSG-P7-003`, no item, no partial page, and an incident to the platform administrator queue | MSG-P7-003 | AC8 |
| X6 | A caller without the Decision log right asks the read | Refused before the query, with no item | MSG-P4-002 | AC6 |
| X7 | A grant activation is refused for a missing field or a short reason | No `AC-BGON` entry exists; the access service owns the 422 and the field name | MSG-GEN-001, MSG-GEN-002 | AC5 |
| X8 | An `AC-BGON` record arrives with no incident reference | Refused with `MSG-P7-009` naming `incidentReference`; a grant entry without an incident is not auditable | MSG-P7-009 | AC4 |
| X9 | The reference list answers late or not at all | The record is retried; the code is never accepted on a guess, and no entry is appended from a failed list read | None | AC1 |

X8 and X9 are the paths this slice adds: the incident reference is the one element a grant entry cannot do without, and the six codes are data, so a list that cannot answer cannot validate a code.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against RWB-P4-E1039-CON, the store of RWB-P7-E1008-APP, the writer of RWB-P7-E1027-APP and the platform contracts of the baseline |
| Negotiable | The element names inside `actions`, the grant and incident elements of the answer and the review due time are the open points of the assumption; the shape of the entry and the prohibition on values are fixed |
| Valuable | One ledger answers who saw what and when and names the emergency use, and each grant is reviewed from the entry it left |
| Estimable | One listener, one mapper, one guard, one review calculation, one query and one index |
| Small | Fits one week with its tests, as the ledger slice of the legacy key |
| Testable | Each criterion of section 7 is one test of section 16, run against the fakes of section 12.8 |
