The eight criteria are new: no line of them is a legacy criterion, and each one tests only the ledger side of the key. Where a criterion names a fact another owner holds — the read, the export, the document, the grant and its end time, the refusal — the line states the answer of that owner's contract mock and the legacy values are carried unchanged. The ten legacy criteria of RWB-E1-039 are delivered by RWB-P4-E1039-APP and the cross-service journey by RWB-ITG-E1039-ITG.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every access event of the six codes is one entry in the ledger, appended once, never updated and never deleted | REQ-ACA-006; NFR-042; FEAT-ACA-08; legacy BR1 |
| BR2 | The case ID is present only where the event has a case: it is empty for a sign-in, a refusal, an export and a grant activation | Legacy section 11, DF-DEC-002 |
| BR3 | An entry lists field IDs and their masking flag, never a field value; the clearest facts it may hold are the case ID, the document ID, the field ID, the flag, the filter, the row count, the grant ID and the incident | NFR-040; legacy BR3 |
| BR4 | Every entry written while a grant is active carries the grant ID and the incident reference in its `actions` | Admin and access model 5.3; legacy BR6; FEAT-ACA-09 |
| BR5 | An `AC-BGON` entry carries the incident, the grant, the area, the right, the scope and a review due time computed from the review-window parameter; the ledger records the grant and does not enforce it | Legacy BR4, BR5, BR7; FEAT-ACA-10 |
| BR6 | A refused admin call is an `AC-DENY` entry with the area, the right and the reason code, and no case ID | Legacy BR1, BR8; FEAT-ACA-07 |
| BR7 | The same event with the same idempotency key gives one entry, and the repeat is counted | R-UNI-40; DP-09 |
| BR8 | The ledger is append only and hash chained, and the chain is verified nightly at 02:00 by the store story | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; FEAT-DRI-01 |
| BR9 | An entry that cannot be appended is not partially stored: the message is retried and then parked with its headers | Principle 5; DP-09 |
| BR10 | An access entry arrives on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; no service writes `decision_log_entry` from outside rwb-decision and no field value crosses the topic | DP-01; DP-03; ADR-022 |
| BR11 | The six codes, the areas, the scopes and the roles are reference data with a version, and the review window is a parameter; neither is a constant in code | DP-06; DP-07; legacy section 17 |

##### 9. State transitions

No case status changes in this story, and the ledger holds no grant state: the grant lives in rwb-access and the ledger records what each event says about it. The entry has the states below and no other.

| Object | From | Event | To | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Access entry | NONE | A `DecisionRecorded` of the period arrives | MAPPED | The code, the case, the actor and the `actions` are mapped; nothing is stored yet |
| Access entry | MAPPED | The `actions` carries a field ID and a flag | VALIDATED | The chain link is read and the append is prepared |
| Access entry | VALIDATED | The append commits | APPENDED | One row with `chain_seq`, `prev_hash` and `entry_hash`; never updated, never deleted |
| Access entry | MAPPED | The `actions` carries a value | REFUSED | `MSG-P7-009` names the element and nothing is appended |
| Access entry | APPENDED | The same event arrives again | REPEATED | The first entry ID is answered and the repeat is counted |
| Access entry | VALIDATED | The store cannot append | RETRIED | The message is retried and then parked on the dead-letter topic; no partial row exists |
| Grant entry | APPENDED | The review window after `decided_at` passes | DUE FOR REVIEW | The read answers the review due time; no state is written by the ledger |
| Read answer | REQUESTED | The store answers | RETURNED | Items in time order with the grant and the incident where the entry carries them |
| Read answer | REQUESTED | The store does not answer | REFUSED | 503 with `MSG-P7-003`, no item, one incident |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-AUDIT Internal audit | Reads the ledger for a case, an access code and a period; changes nothing |
| RW-SECADM Security administrator | Reads the ledger and reviews each break-glass use from the `AC-BGON` entry and the entries it marks |
| RW-COMPLY Compliance and PDPA officer | Reads the ledger; receives an unreviewed use through the channel of Epic 8 |
| RW-COE, RW-DATASTEW | Read the access entries with the Decision log R right |
| The producing services of the workbench | Publish their own access records on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; they never read or write `decision_log_entry` (DP-01) |
| The rwb-decision service identity | Appends and reads the entries of `rwb_decision` (DP-02) |
| RW-PLATADM Platform administrator | Receives the incident of a failed ingest or a failed read; operates the run from the alerts of the OPS story |
| No delegation of authority level applies | An access entry records an access, not a credit decision; the ledger applies no limit |

No personal name, e-mail address or credential appears in this story, its examples or its fixtures; every actor is a role code or a test user reference.

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity in `rwb_decision` | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision_log_entry | all fields | Write, one entry per access event |
| DF-DEC-002 | decision_log_entry | case_id | Write; empty for a sign-in, a refusal, an export and a grant |
| DF-DEC-003 | decision_log_entry | decision_code | Write, read: the access code of the entry and the query filter |
| DF-DEC-014 | decision_log_entry | actions | Write, read: area, right, result, field IDs with the flag, filter, row count, document ID, reason code, grant ID, incident reference |
| DF-DEC-016 | decision_log_entry | decided_at | Write, read: the time order of the answer and the base of the review due time |
| DF-DEC-030 | decision_log_entry | actor_user_id | Write, read |
| DF-REF-028, DF-REF-029 | lov_value, through the rwb-case contract | lov_code, value_code | Read: the six access codes of LOV-DECISION |
| Standard column | decision_log_entry | chain_seq, prev_hash, entry_hash | Write, through the store of RWB-P7-E1008-APP |
| Standard column | processed_event, idempotency_key | processed id, stored answer | Write, read, through the outbox and inbox library (DP-09) |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary. The migration is one per-service Flyway step in the `rwb_decision` sequence (DP-15): `V1039_1__access_ledger.sql` adds the index on `(decision_code, decided_at)` and the index on `(case_id, decision_code, decided_at)` where the store does not already carry them, and it creates no table and no column.

The ledger holds no personal data: the actor is a role code or a user identifier, the subject is a case, document or entry identifier, and `actions` holds field IDs, flags, filters and counts. The review due time is computed and never stored, so the review window changes for tomorrow's entries without a data migration. The retention of the entries is the store story's and the access entries are not carved out of it.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

| Method | Path | Status | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` | Declared by API-P7-006; owner P7 | The access answer: `caseId`, `decision` "AC-READ", `from` and `to`, with `page` and `size` of the standard query, items in time order with actor, time, field IDs and flags, and the grant ID and incident reference where the entry carries them |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log/{entryId}` | Declared by API-P7-007; owner P7 | One access entry as it was appended, for the review of a single use |

This slice adds no path and no query parameter. It fixes what an access entry means on the read, and it answers three elements the published document does not name — `grantId`, `incidentReference` and the review due time of an `AC-BGON` item — which are taken from the assumption in force (GAP-2452; ASM-4061). Both paths answer 401 through the gateway-bff session envelope, 403 without Decision log R with `MSG-P4-002`, 422 for a period that ends before it starts and 503 when the store cannot be read.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method and path | Owner | Use in this story | Contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters/{code}` | P3 rwb-case | `rwb.access.breakglass.review-days` for the review due time of a grant entry | RWB-P3-E1042-CON (C) |
| GET `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 rwb-case | LOV-DECISION for the six access codes and their version | RWB-P3-E1043-CON (C) |

No operation of rwb-access, rwb-document or rwb-case's case read is consumed: the access facts arrive on the topic, and the grant, the matrix and the masking policy stay with their owners. RWB-P4-E1039-CON is consumed as the published record shape and its fake and not as a call. Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (DP-11, ADR-020). A missing list answer refuses the record rather than accepting a code on a guess (BR11). The parameter path and the element names inside the `actions` element are Not specified in the source documents beyond the legacy names (GAP-2452; ASM-4060).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The ledger is the consumer of the record topic and does not republish what it stores. The service's own topic `rwb.decision.events.v1` carries the approval and rule events of RWB-P7-E2013-APP and RWB-P7-E1073-CON and nothing of this story, and nothing is forwarded to a lake or a file (DP-17).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Producer | Handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| DecisionRecorded (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | All 19 services, through the decision-record library (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, DP-03) | The six access codes are mapped and appended; every other record is left to the record consumer; idempotent on the event's key; a record that fails the access schema is retried and then parked on the dead-letter topic with its headers |

The envelope and the key are the library's (DP-09). The retry cadence and the dead-letter policy are the event platform's and this story configures no policy of its own.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The ingest is a message consumer and the read is synchronous code in a REST handler. This story starts no workflow, registers no activity and holds no Quartz job; the task queue `rwb-decision` serves the other stories of the service (DP-10).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The nightly chain check at 02:00 is the store story's, and the review of a break-glass use is a person's act measured by a computed due time, not a scheduled job. The legacy Quartz rows are retired for this service (DP-10; Template and Rules §R6), so this story declares no cron entry and no shared scheduler row.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| `decision_log_entry` | P7, in `rwb_decision` | The entry of every access event: the legacy field identifiers, the `actions` element, the chain columns and the decided-at time. Appended and read only |
| `processed_event` | PLT library, created in `rwb_decision` | The inbox that makes the ingest idempotent (DP-09) |
| `idempotency_key` | PLT library, created in `rwb_decision` | The stored answer of the event key and of a repeated read |
| `outbox_event` | PLT library, created in `rwb_decision` | Created with the schema; this story writes no row to it, because it publishes nothing |

No `rwb_access`, `rwb_case`, `rwb_document` or `rwb_reporting` table is read and no `v_ace_*` view is read (DP-01, DP-05). `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule` and `break_glass_grant` are P4's and this story holds no grant on them.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-access contract fake (RWB-P4-E1039-CON) | The shape of an access event and its refusal vocabulary | One read of case `RW-2026-000123` at 10:15 by `U-4101` with DF-PTY-007 and DF-PTY-016 masked; an export of 37 rows by `U-4103`; a document read of `DOC-2026-0009981`; an activation by `U-4102` with incident `INC0004521`, IAM request `IAM-778812`, area `CASE_RECORD`, right `U`, scope `ALL`, ending 14:30; two reads under the grant at 14:20 and 14:25; a refusal of `U-4104` with reason `NO_BREAKGLASS_GRANT`; a refusal of `U-4106` with area `PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION` and right `R`; a field value in `actions`; a missing `incidentReference` |
| decision-record fixture (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON) | The `DecisionRecorded` payload and the key | The same events as records, one repeated with its key, one with a decision code outside the six codes, one with a slow delivery past the retry budget |
| Parameters fake (RWB-P3-E1042-CON) | The parameter read | `rwb.access.breakglass.review-days` = 1 with its version; an absent key; a slow answer past 2 s |
| Reference-data fake (RWB-P3-E1043-CON) | The list read | LOV-DECISION at version REF-2026.11 with the six codes and one code outside the list; a slow answer past 2 s |
| Ledger fixture (RWB-P7-E1008-APP) | `decision_log_entry` and its chain | Three entries of case `RW-2026-000123` on 3 December 2026 at 10:15, 11:02 and 16:40, the middle one carrying the grant and the incident; an entry at chain_seq 412 for the repeat; a store closed for the failed read |

The values are the legacy values of RWB-E1-039, kept unchanged so that the component, contract and integration assertions read the same fixtures; the fixtures carry no personal data. The element names inside the `actions` element and the three read elements of 12.1 are stubbed from the assumption and are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2452; ASM-4061).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 provided, 2 consumed | The decision-log read and the entry read on base `/api/recovery/decision/v1`; the parameter and list reads of rwb-case, one hop each within 2 s |
| Kafka | 0 published, 1 consumed | DecisionRecorded (EV-08) on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; nothing on `rwb.decision.events.v1` from this story |
| Temporal | None | No workflow, activity or Schedule; queue `rwb-decision` serves the other stories |
| File | None | No file is read or written, and the lake copy of the access log is removed (DP-17) |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision`, module `accessledger`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision.accessledger`; the artefact is the `rwb-decision` api deployment of the service template.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_decision`; never read another service's tables. The grant, the matrix and the masking policy stay with rwb-access and the document with rwb-document | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`; the ledger consumes what the serving services write | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library; the review window is a parameter row | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case; the six access codes arrive with their version | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout. The monolith's in-process call to the writer becomes the event on the topic, and the two data reads are one hop each | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/decision/v1`; every path of this story sits under the service base | none |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting. The lake copy of the access log and its read logging leave with the lake | none; no lake data is needed |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route for the decision-log read and the refusal shape | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

No pattern is claimed for DP-02, DP-04, DP-05, DP-08, DP-09, DP-10, DP-12, DP-14, DP-15, DP-16, DP-18 or DP-20: this story creates no login and no migration, evaluates no Drools package, reads no ACE view, declares no authorise call of its own, configures no topic name and no Schedule, runs no per-case workflow, calls no adapter, writes no ledger entry of the interaction ledger and calls no agent. The four H rows are platform contracts consumed as the published baseline: the story record carries no build-order dependency of its own (metadata "Depends on (build)" = None, §R5.7 rules 2 and 3).

**Hardware and software change.** The access log leaves one shared table in the single `recovery` schema, written in process by every module through one writer. Each serving service now writes its own record and publishes it, and the central ledger of rwb-decision keeps the auditable copy of every access event in `rwb_decision` with its chain. No new hardware is implied: the ingest runs in the existing `rwb-decision` pods, the entries live in the ACE PostgreSQL server under the `rwb_decision` schema and login, and the topic is the Kafka platform ACE already runs. The data-lake copy disappears with the lake.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `AccessEntryListener` | Inbox consumer | Consumes `DecisionRecorded`, keeps the six access codes, recognises a repeat by the event key and parks a record that fails the access schema |
| `AccessEntryMapper` | Service | The case-ID rule of BR2, the `actions` element of BR3, and the grant and incident marking of BR4 |
| `EntryFieldGuard` | Service | Refuses an `actions` element that carries a value instead of a field ID, with `MSG-P7-009` |
| `AccessEntryWriter` | Service | Appends one entry with its chain link through the store of RWB-P7-E1008-APP; never updates and never deletes |
| `BreakGlassReviewDue` | Service | Computes the review due time of a grant entry from `decided_at` and the review-window parameter (BR5) |
| `AccessLedgerQuery` | Service | The query behind the decision-log read for an access code and a period, with the grant and incident elements and the time order |
| `AccessCodeCatalog` | Service | Reads the six codes from LOV-DECISION with their version and refuses an unknown code (BR11) |

**Database and migrations.** One Flyway step in the `rwb_decision` sequence (DP-15), `V1039_1__access_ledger.sql`: the index on `(decision_code, decided_at)` for the period query and the index on `(case_id, decision_code, decided_at)` for the case answer, where the store does not already carry them. No column, no table and no seed: the six codes are reference data of rwb-case and the review window is a parameter.

**Configuration and reference data.** `rwb.access.breakglass.review-days=1` through the parameters client (DP-06), and LOV-DECISION through the reference client (DP-07), each with its version. Nothing else is configured: no retention value, no page size and no tolerance is set here.

**Build steps**

1. `AccessEntryListener` against the record fixture, with the six codes, one record outside them and one repeated key; tests for AC1 and AC7.
2. `AccessEntryMapper` with the case-ID rule and the `actions` element of a read, an export, a document read and a grant; tests for AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC4.
3. `EntryFieldGuard` and the refusal of a value in `actions`, with `MSG-P7-009` and nothing appended (X1).
4. `AccessEntryWriter` over the store of RWB-P7-E1008-APP, asserting the chain link on two consecutive entries and no update path.
5. `BreakGlassReviewDue` with a clock fixed at 10:30 and the parameter fake; test for AC4.
6. `AccessLedgerQuery` with the period validation, the time order and the grant and incident elements; tests for AC6.
7. The refused paths: no `AC-BGON` on a refused activation, the `AC-DENY` entry of a refusal, and the 422 case that writes nothing (AC5).
8. The failed store: the retry, the parked message and the 503 read with `MSG-P7-003` and no partial page (AC8).

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, every access event of the period is in the ledger once with its chain link, the grant and the incident are on every entry written under a grant, the review due time is answered for a grant entry, the audit answer of a case names the emergency use, and the access entries of a business date reconcile one for one with the `DecisionRecorded` messages of the topic.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Raised as |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-003 | The ledger cannot be read, or an entry cannot be appended | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | The read answer 503, and the incident of the ingest |
| MSG-P7-009 | A record is refused for a missing or invalid element (written to the service log and the incident, never shown to a customer) | The decision record was refused: {field} is missing or not valid. | `DecisionRecordInvalidException`, with `field` |
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller lacks Decision log R on the read | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | The service guard, before the query |
| MSG-GEN-002 | Page size outside 1 to 500 on the read | {field} must be between {min} and {max}. | The read validation |

The ids and the texts are copied unchanged from legacy RWB-E1-039 and this story adds no message of its own. The field names of the refusals are `actions`, `incidentReference` and `decisionCode`. MSG-P4-004 and MSG-P4-007 belong to rwb-access and are named here only as the answers the fake returns. The published catalogue entry format of MSG-P7-009 is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2452; ASM-4063). Thai text for each follows DL10.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the six access codes, the areas, the scopes and the roles are list values with a version, and the review window is a parameter.
- No personal data in an entry, a log, an event, a test or a prompt: an entry carries the case ID, the document ID, the field ID and the flag, never a value, and the `actions` element is refused if a value appears in it.
- No read of another service's tables: the access facts arrive on the topic, the codes and the parameter arrive through the rwb-case contract, and a boundary test fails the build on a cross-schema reference.
- No write path to `decision_log_entry` other than the writer of this service, checked by an architecture test; the ledger has no update and no delete at all.
- No enforcement of the grant in the ledger: the time box, the group membership and the matrix are rwb-access's, and the ledger records what the event states.
- No personal data in the incident of a failed ingest: the incident carries the entry id, the message key and the field name only.
- No data-lake sink and no reporting copy: the legacy lake copy is retired and reporting follows the events (DP-17).
- The ingest is idempotent on the event key: a build that appends before checking the key fails the repeat test.
- Every example and fixture is synthetic; no production payload is copied into a test or a fake.

##### 1. Story

As an **ACE database engineer**, I want **the four tables this legacy key needs created on the per-service Flyway sequence in schema `rwb_access` — the outbox, the inbox and the idempotency store of the decision-record library and the break-glass grant table with its two-person constraint — with the grants to the `rwb-access` login, the log partitioned by month and retained as data, and an explicit guarantee that no entry holds a personal value**, so that **the writer, the grant and the read of the app story run on a schema that is correct, granted, reversible and confined to this service's own schema**.

This is the database story of legacy key RWB-E1-039 under epic RWB-SVC-P4. It delivers, in schema `rwb_access`:

- the migration that applies the decision-record library DDL of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and creates the three library objects this key writes through — `outbox_event`, `processed_event` and `idempotency_key` — on the per-service sequence after the V0001 baseline (DP-03, DP-15);
- the migration that creates `break_glass_grant`, the table behind the grant, the end and the read operations of the contract, with its keys and the two-person constraint;
- the grant script for the `rwb-access` login (DP-02), whose name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0782; ASM-1427);
- the retention and partitioning of the access log **as data**: the month partition on `decided_at`, the retention class and the archive rule, held as parameter rows and never as a job in this story;
- the rollback of each migration, in reverse order, with the appended chain preserved;
- the explicit assertion that **no entry holds a personal value** — only the case id, the field id and the flag, with the actor as a staff user reference and never a name.

**The division of this legacy key is fixed and is the same in all four stories.** **RWB-P4-E1039-APP** owns the ten legacy acceptance criteria and implements the writer, the grant and the read. **RWB-P4-E1039-CON** owns the published contract of the four operations, the entry shape, the two-person rule, the time box, the refusal vocabulary and the fail-closed rule. **This story** owns the schema, the four tables, the grants, the retention and the partitioning, and it changes no business rule. **RWB-P4-E1039-OPS** owns the deployment: the Helm values, the Kafka ACLs, the secrets, the alerting and the run book, and it provisions no database object. **The end-to-end proof is RWB-ITG-E1039-ITG**, and the two neighbours of the same legacy key are **RWB-P5-E1039-APP** on the document side and **RWB-P7-E1039-APP** on the ledger side.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story added one index (`ix_declog_actor_time`) to a single `decision_log_entry` table in one recovery schema with one shared login, and wrote the access events of every module into the P7 writer inside the same process. After the split there is no shared table to index: every service owns a schema, a login and a Flyway sequence, and the access entry is written in the schema of the service that served the read (DP-01, DP-03, DP-15).

**The division is fixed and is the same in all four stories.** The entry shape is **RWB-P4-E1039-CON**'s, the writer and the grant are **RWB-P4-E1039-APP**'s, the deployment and the alerts are **RWB-P4-E1039-OPS**'s, and **RWB-ITG-E1039-ITG** proves the key end to end; **RWB-P5-E1039-APP** records the document side and **RWB-P7-E1039-APP** owns the central ledger. **RWB-P4-E1039-DB** owns only what the database must enforce so that the other three can be true: the four tables exist and nothing else is created, the login is the only writer, the log is partitioned and retained as data rather than by an application job, and no entry can hold a personal value because there is nowhere to put one.

The four tables matter for four different reasons. The `outbox_event` row is written in the same transaction as the access entry, so the record and its publication can never disagree; without it the fail-closed rule of the app story would have nothing to fail on. The `idempotency_key` row is what makes AC10 true — the same `k-001` returns the first grant answer and writes no second entry, while `k-002` is refused with 409 — so the table is a correctness requirement of the story and not a library formality. The `processed_event` table is created by the library DDL so that every service schema has the same shape; this key subscribes to no event, so no row is written to it and the inbox stays empty, which is stated rather than left to be discovered. And `break_glass_grant` is the one table this key adds of its own: it holds the grant, its start and its end, the IAM request and the incident, and the constraint that a person has at most one active grant.

The negative side is the reason the retention is a story and not a footnote. An access log that keeps a personal value would become the largest personal-data store in the workbench, so **the schema holds no personal value at all**: the case id, the document id, the field id and the flag are the clearest facts an entry can carry, the actor is a staff user reference, and the reason text of a grant is free text that the application checks and the run book tells the operator never to fill with customer data (NFR-040, BR7 of the app story). Partitioning by month keeps the retention rule enforceable by a partition drop instead of a mass delete, and the retention period itself is a parameter, because no source fixes it (DL26).

The values copied from the sources are the table names of the library and of the key, the service schema `rwb_access`, the login `rwb_access`, and the field ids of the decision record: DF-DEC-002 for the case id, DF-DEC-003 for the decision code, DF-DEC-014 for the actions, DF-DEC-016 for the decided at and DF-DEC-030 for the actor. Where no source names the break-glass grant table, its constraint, the retention period or the partition granularity, the migration carries the placeholder and the assumption in force (GAP-0782; ASM-1428) and (GAP-0782; ASM-1429).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The V0001 baseline of `rwb_access` exists on the per-service Flyway sequence, from RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and RWB-PLT-NF06-DB: the schema, the `flyway_schema_history` table and the standard record columns (`is_active`, `state`, `version`, `created_at`, `created_by`, `updated_at`, `updated_by`).
- The ACE database and the per-service login policy are in place; the login of rwb-access is created by the platform DB work and its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0782; ASM-1427).
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published: the DDL template of the decision-record library, with its local table, its outbox, its inbox and its idempotency store, and the `prev_hash` and `entry_hash` columns of the chain.
- The ownership map is the only source of table ownership: `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule`, `role_conflict` and `delegation_limit` are P4 and in `rwb_access`; `outbox_event`, `processed_event` and `idempotency_key` are PLT library objects created in each service schema by that service's own DB story; `decision_log_entry` and `approval` are P7's and `lov_value` is P3's.
- The parameter contract is available for the retention and partition rows (DP-06), and the retention decision DL26 is still open, so the retention period is carried as a parameter with the placeholder of this story.
- The field ids are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary, and the library DDL fixes the column names of its three objects; the grant table has no field id in any source and its columns are named after the legacy request and response fields.
- No approval is required to run a Draft migration on a development database; the migration is released to SIT only after the tests in section 16 pass.

##### 4. Flow

1. The ACE database engineer checks out the rwb-access migration folder and confirms the highest applied version on the sequence (the V0001 baseline).
2. The engineer adds three migrations after that version, in this order: the library DDL application with its three objects, the `break_glass_grant` table with its constraint, and the grants with the partition and retention rows.
3. The engineer proves on an empty schema that each migration applies once, records its version and checksum, and that a second run reports no pending migration.
4. The engineer writes the grant script for the `rwb-access` login, scoped to schema `rwb_access` and to the four tables, plus the sequence usage the idempotency store needs.
5. The engineer creates the month partition of the access log on `decided_at`, with a default partition for a late-arriving entry and the retention class read from the parameter.
6. The migration pipeline applies the baseline and this story's migrations to an empty schema, then to a copy of the SIT schema, and runs the schema checks: keys, the two-person constraint, partitioning, grants, and a scan for any foreign key that names another schema.
7. The pipeline scans the chain's columns and a fixture of entries for a personal field: only the case id, the document id, the field id, the flag, the codes, the references, the versions and the times may appear.
8. The rollback is exercised on a copy: the four objects drop in reverse order, the appended chain keeps its rows, and a sequence re-apply returns the same shape.
9. The migrations are recorded in the release notes of the sequence, with their version numbers and their checksums, and the retention row is handed to the parameter load of RWB-P3-E1042-CON.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message |
|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A migration runs before the V0001 baseline | Flyway refuses with an unresolved baseline and nothing is applied | Pipeline error, no message id |
| X2 | An object of this story already exists in the sequence | The repeatable check refuses to re-create it and the migration is marked as already applied | Pipeline error, no message id |
| X3 | A foreign key names `rwb_decision` or another schema | The catalogue check fails the build; the key is removed and the reference is kept as a value | Check finding, no message id |
| X4 | The grant script runs before the login exists | The script fails on the missing role; the platform DB story creates the login first | Database error, no message id |
| X5 | The grant script grants to a shared or legacy login | The review rejects the script: one login per service (DP-02) | Review finding, no message id |
| X6 | A second active grant row is inserted for the same person | The two-person constraint refuses it; the application maps it to 409 with MSG-GEN-004 | MSG-GEN-004 through the application |
| X7 | The chain table is written with a column that could hold a personal value | The personal-data scan fails the build and the column is removed | Check finding, no message id |
| X8 | The rollback would drop the chain and lose committed entries | The rollback of this story drops only the objects it created; the chain's rows are never deleted | Review finding, no message id |
| X9 | The retention period is still open at release | The retention row carries the placeholder and the gap; the partition still exists with the default class | GAP-0782 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Three migrations, one grant script, one rollback and the partition rows on the service's own sequence; nothing to build against |
| Negotiable | Constraint and index names follow the platform naming library; the column set of the grant table is fixed by the legacy request and response fields |
| Valuable | The writer, the grant and the read have a schema that is granted, partitioned, retained and free of personal values |
| Estimable | Four tables, one constraint, two indexes, one partition scheme, one grant script and one rollback |
| Small | Days, not weeks, with the schema checks |
| Testable | Every criterion is a catalogue query or a pipeline run in section 16 |

```gherkin

    Given the grantee is the rwb-access login (DP-02), whose name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0782; ASM-1427)

  Scenario: AC1 The migrations apply in sequence on an empty schema (new, D-RCV-60)

  Scenario: AC2 The three library objects exist as the library DDL declares them (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the library DDL of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON applied by this story
    When the catalogue is read

    Then outbox_event holds the message id, the topic, the payload, the created time and the published time of each access entry
    Then idempotency_key holds the key, the request hash and the stored answer of the grant and end operations
    Then processed_event exists and holds no row, because this key consumes no event

  Scenario: AC3 break_glass_grant is created with its keys and the two-person constraint (new, D-RCV-60)

    Then the primary key is on grant_id and an index on actor_user_id and starts_at exists
    Then a constraint refuses a second row in state ACTIVE for the same actor_user_id
    Then ends_at is NOT NULL and state is limited to ACTIVE and ENDED
    Then no column of the table can hold a personal value, and reason is free text checked by the application

  Scenario: AC4 The grants belong to the rwb-access login and to no other (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the grant script of this story
    When it runs
    Then the rwb-access login has usage on schema rwb_access and select, insert, update and delete on the four tables of this key
    Then no other login holds a grant on those tables and no grant on rwb_decision or on any other schema is present
    Then the login holds no right to alter the chain beyond insert, and no right to delete an appended entry

  Scenario: AC5 The access log is partitioned by month and retained as data (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the decision-record table of the library applied by this story
    When the catalogue is read
    Then the table is partitioned by range on decided_at with one partition per month and a default partition
    Then the retention class and the retention period are parameter rows, and the period is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0782; ASM-1429)
    Then the index on actor_user_id and decided_at exists, so the access read of a user and a period is indexed
    Then a partition drop is the only retention action and no row is deleted individually

  Scenario: AC6 No entry holds a personal value (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the chain table and a fixture of access entries
    When the column list and the fixture are scanned
    Then no column of the chain holds a name, an identity number, a contact value or an address
    Then the clearest facts an entry carries are the case id, the document id, the field id and the flag clear or masked
    Then the actor is a staff user reference and the reason text of a grant is the only free text in the four tables
    Then the scan fails the build if a column or a fixture value of another kind appears

  Scenario: AC7 The rollback is complete and preserves the chain (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the grant script and the rollback of this story
    When the rollback runs on a copy of the SIT schema

    Then the appended entries of the chain keep their rows, their hashes and their times

```

These criteria are new and test the database artefacts only: no legacy acceptance criterion is repeated, and every physical value (table, column, field id, constraint) is the legacy or library value, copied character for character.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Each service's objects live in its own schema under its own login; one login per service | DP-01, DP-02, DP-15 |
| BR2 | The access entry and its outbox row are committed in one transaction, so the record and its publication can never disagree | DP-03; Architecture v5 slide 28 |
| BR3 | The grant and the end operation are idempotent by key, and a repeated key returns the stored answer without a second entry | RWB-E1-039 AC10; DP-09 |
| BR4 | A person holds at most one active grant, and the database refuses a second active row for the same actor | Admin and access model, section 5.3; RWB-E1-039 BR5 |
| BR5 | An entry is append only: it is never updated and never deleted, and the retention action is a partition drop | RWB-E1-039 BR1; Architecture v5 slide 28 |
| BR6 | An access entry holds no personal value: the case id, the document id, the field id and the flag are its clearest facts | NFR-040; RWB-E1-039 BR3 |
| BR7 | The retention period and the partition granularity are parameter rows, never literals in a migration | DP-06; DL26 |
| BR8 | The tables of rwb-decision and of rwb-case are never referenced by a key here; the incident, the case and the document are values | DP-01; Ownership Map v1 |
| BR9 | The inbox table exists in every service schema and holds no row where the service consumes no event | DP-09; RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |

##### 9. State transitions

None in the runtime sense: a table has no state machine. The states this story moves through are the migration states of the service's Flyway history (pending, applied, failed, undone), and the row states the schema exposes are the standard record columns plus the grant state ACTIVE and ENDED, which the application moves at `endsAt` or on an explicit end. A partition has the states ATTACHED, DETACHED and DROPPED, and the retention rule moves a month partition from ATTACHED to DROPPED after the period in force.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The ACE database engineer (any team, per U3) | Writes and runs the migrations, the grant script, the partition scheme and the rollback |
| The service owner of rwb-access | Approves a destructive change; none is planned here |
| The platform DB owner (RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, RWB-PLT-NF06-DB) | Owns the sequence, the baseline and the login policy |
| The owner of the retention rule (P5 rwb-document, per the ownership map) | Confirms the retention class and the period used by the parameter row |
| rwb-decision (P7) | Owns `decision_log_entry` and the central ledger; this schema holds no key to them |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A schema change is not a credit decision |

The grantee is named only as the rwb-access login (DP-02); its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0782; ASM-1427). No personal name and no credential appears in a migration, a script or a runbook.

**No entry holds a personal value.** The chain table has no column for a name, an identity number, a contact value or an address; it carries the case id, the document id, the field id and the flag, the codes, the references, the versions and the times, and the actor as a staff user reference. The only free text in the four tables is the reason of a grant, which the application bounds and the run book tells the operator never to fill with customer data.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Sequencing.** The service's Flyway sequence is owned by RWB-PLT-E1044-CON. The V0001 baseline creates the schema, the history table and the standard columns. This story adds the next versions after the baseline:

| Version | File | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| V0001 | baseline, from the platform DB story | Schema `rwb_access`, history table, standard columns |
| next after the baseline | `..._decision_record_library.sql` | Applies the DP-03 library DDL: the chain table, `outbox_event`, `processed_event` and `idempotency_key` |
| next after that | `..._break_glass_grant.sql` | Creates `break_glass_grant`, its index and the two-person constraint |
| next after that | `..._access_log_partitions_grants.sql` | The month partition scheme, the parameter rows of the retention class and the grants to the rwb-access login |

The legacy index `ix_declog_actor_time` on `decision_log_entry` is the source of the actor and time index of this story; the monolith name and number are not reused on the service sequence, and the index is created on the chain table of `rwb_access` instead. The exact version numbers are assigned by the sequence owner at build time; the order above is fixed by this story.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`. This story applies the library DDL and creates the outbox, inbox and idempotency objects | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library. The retention class and the retention period are parameter rows | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case. The event codes and the areas the entry carries are reference values and no copy is created here | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout. No call is made by this story; the keys it creates support the app story's one-hop calls | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1`. No path is served here, and the schema serves the base of the app story only | none |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting. No lake copy table, no lake watermark and no lake export object is created | none; no lake data is retained |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route. The screen reads the entries through the access-log operation and never through SQL | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Table definitions**

`break_glass_grant` — `grant_id` uuid NOT NULL, `actor_user_id` uuid NOT NULL, `incident_reference` varchar(20) NOT NULL, `iam_request_id` varchar(40) NOT NULL, `capability_area` varchar(30) NOT NULL, `right_code` varchar(5) NOT NULL, `scope_code` varchar(8) NOT NULL, `reason` varchar(1000) NOT NULL, `state` varchar(10) NOT NULL, `starts_at` timestamptz NOT NULL, `ends_at` timestamptz NOT NULL, plus the standard record columns of the V0001 baseline. Primary key `(grant_id)`; index on `(actor_user_id, starts_at)`; a unique partial constraint on `(actor_user_id)` where `state = 'ACTIVE'`, so that a person holds at most one active grant and a second activation is refused by the database; check `state IN ('ACTIVE','ENDED')`; `ends_at` NOT NULL, because a grant without an end is not a grant (BR4, BR7).

The chain table, `outbox_event`, `processed_event` and `idempotency_key` take the column names, types and keys of the RWB-PLT-E1027-CON DDL template and are not restated here; the only addition this story makes to the chain is the month range partition on `decided_at` and the index on `(actor_user_id, decided_at)` that the legacy `ix_declog_actor_time` stands for.

**Retention and partitioning as data.**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Partition key | `decided_at`, range, one partition per calendar month, with a default partition for a late entry |
| Index | `(actor_user_id, decided_at)`, so the access read of a user and a period is indexed and the ledger's five-minute collection is a range scan |
| Retention class | A parameter row of the rwb-case catalogue, read by the retention job of the platform and never by a literal |
| Retention period | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0782; ASM-1429); DL26 is open |
| Retention action | Detach and drop a month partition older than the period in force; no row is deleted individually, so the append-only rule survives |
| Archive | The partition is archived under the decision log's rule before it is dropped; the archive target is the platform's and not this schema's |

**Grants.** `GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA rwb_access TO <the rwb-access login>`; `GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON break_glass_grant, outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key TO <the rwb-access login>`; `GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON` the chain table, with no `UPDATE` and no `DELETE`, so that an appended entry cannot be rewritten from the service (BR5); usage on the sequences those tables own. No grant to a shared login, no grant to another service's login, and no grant on `rwb_decision` or `rwb_case`. The grantee name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0782; ASM-1427).

**Rollback.** Per migration, in reverse order: the partition and grant migration is reversed by revoking the grants it made and dropping the parameter rows it added; the grant-table migration is reversed by dropping the constraint, the index and `break_glass_grant`; the library migration is reversed by dropping the three library objects, while the chain table keeps its rows and is never dropped by this story's rollback because it holds the appended entries (BR5, AC7). The rollback is exercised on a copy of the SIT schema and recorded in the runbook.

**Done when.** The migrations apply twice without a change, the catalogue checks pass, the two-person constraint refuses a second active grant, the personal-data scan finds no personal field, the grants are exactly as above, the rollback returns the schema to its pre-migration shape with the chain intact, and the tests in section 16 pass.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-004 | A second active grant row is inserted for the same actor; the application maps the constraint to 409 | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-GEN-002 | A grant reason reaches the database outside the 20 to 1000 bound | {field} must be between {min} and {max}. Raised by the application, not by a database constraint |
| Database error, no message id | A migration runs before the baseline or finds an object already present | The migration fails and nothing is applied; the pipeline stops |
| Database error, no message id | A grant script runs before the login exists | The script fails on the missing role; the platform DB story creates the login first |
| Check finding, no message id | A foreign key names another schema, or a column could hold a personal value | The pipeline check fails the build; the key or the column is removed |

The reason bound is deliberately in the application: it comes from the parameter `rwb.access.breakglass.reason-min` and its 1000 maximum, so a business person can change it without a migration (BR7). The database enforces what does not change: the keys, the two-person constraint, the partition, the append-only grant set and the schema boundary. Every message and its id is the legacy one and is raised by the app story.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen. The result of a migration is visible in the release pipeline and in the service's Flyway history: pending, applied, failed, undone, each with a version and a checksum. The partition list and the retention class are visible on the platform database dashboard. Nothing here is shown to a user directly, and SCR-43 Roles and access reads the entries through the access-log operation, never through SQL.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a constraint: the reason bounds and the retention period are parameter data, read through the parameter contract (DP-06, BR7).
- No personal data in a migration, a script, a fixture or a runbook: the case id, the document id, the field id and the flag only, and the actor as a staff user reference (BR6).
- No read of another schema and no key into another schema: `rwb_access` objects reference `rwb_access` objects only (DP-01, BR8).
- One login per service: the rwb-access login is the only grantee, and its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0782; ASM-1427).
- No destructive change: an appended entry is never updated or deleted, the chain is never dropped by a rollback of this story, and the retention action is a partition drop (BR5).
- The sequence is per service and linear: no monolith migration name is reused and no object is created twice (DP-15).
- No table of rwb-decision or rwb-case is created, granted or referenced from here (BR8).
- The obligations of the bank IAM, the SOC logging path and the alerts are not database objects and are not created here.

The legacy test cases of this key — TC-E1-039-01, TC-E1-039-02, TC-E1-039-03, TC-E1-039-04, TC-E1-039-05, TC-E1-039-06, TC-E1-039-07, TC-E1-039-08, TC-E1-039-09, TC-E1-039-10, TC-E1-039-11 and TC-E1-039-12 — are executed by RWB-P4-E1039-APP and, as the cross-service copy, by RWB-ITG-E1039-ITG; this story proves the schema beneath them.

##### 19. Out of scope

- The application code of the writer, the grant and the read: RWB-P4-E1039-APP.
- The published contract of the four operations and its fakes: RWB-P4-E1039-CON.
- The Helm chart, the migration job, the Kafka ACLs, the secrets, the alerts and the run book: RWB-P4-E1039-OPS.
- The chain table's own DDL, its hash columns and its library behaviour: RWB-PLT-E1027-CON; this story applies it and does not redefine it.
- `decision_log_entry`, `approval`, the central ledger, the five-minute collection and the chain verification: P7 rwb-decision and RWB-P7-E1039-APP.
- `lov_value`, `reference_row`, `reference_version`, `parameter_catalog` and `parameter_value`: P3 rwb-case; the retention and partition rows are loaded over that contract.
- The role, permission, masking and delegation tables and their migrations: the other stories of RWB-SVC-P4.
- The retention job implementation and the archive target of the platform: the platform DB and retention work.
- Data migration from the monolith's `decision_log_entry` and its reconciliation: the migration work of the programme, not this story.
- Performance tuning beyond the index on actor and time and the month partition: the non-functional work.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform engineer**, I want **the access-log and break-glass capability of `rwb-access` deployed as one service from the service template, with its Helm chart and values, its migration job invocation, its probes, the Kafka ACLs on `rwb.access.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1` with their retry and `.dlt` topics, the three secret references, the alerting of a failed or refused access-log write and of break-glass use routed to the security administrator queue, and the run book**, so that **the capability runs predictably in every environment and an operator can see and act on a failure of the log or of the grant without reading code**.

This is the DevOps slice of legacy key RWB-E1-039 under epic RWB-SVC-P4. It delivers no application code, **provisions no database object** — the four tables, the grants and the partitions are RWB-P4-E1039-DB's — and **changes no business rule**: every threshold, window and message id it uses is the one the contract and the app story already fix.

**The division of this legacy key is fixed and is the same in all four stories.** **RWB-P4-E1039-APP** owns the ten legacy acceptance criteria and implements the writer, the grant and the read. **RWB-P4-E1039-CON** owns the published contract of the four operations, the entry shape, the two-person rule, the time box, the refusal vocabulary and the fail-closed rule. **RWB-P4-E1039-DB** owns the ACE DB slice in `rwb_access`, provisions every table of the key and runs the migration. **RWB-P4-E1039-OPS** owns the deployment, the topics and their ACLs, the secrets, the alerts and the run book. **The end-to-end proof is RWB-ITG-E1039-ITG**, and the two neighbours of the same legacy key are **RWB-P5-E1039-APP** on the document side and **RWB-P7-E1039-APP** on the ledger side.

The story covers:

- the chart and its values for three environments, with the image digest and the chart version pinned, no replica count, resource size, threshold or cadence in a template;
- the pre-deploy invocation of the per-service Flyway migration job, which is owned and written by RWB-P4-E1039-DB and only invoked here;
- the readiness and liveness probes, neither of which writes to the database;
- the topic ACLs of the service identity, the topic provisioning of the retry and `.dlt` paths, and the shared decision topic that is reused and never recreated;
- the three secret references from the platform secret store;
- the alert rules of a failed or refused access-log write, of a break-glass activation, of a refused break-glass request and of a lagging outbox, each with its message id and one runbook entry;
- the run book of six entries.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story depended on one shared log table, an in-process publisher and a set of standing alert conditions that lived in an operations note. In the target a service is a Helm release built by one pipeline, with its own schema, login, topic, queue and secret references (DP-02, DP-09, DP-15), and two of its behaviours are security controls rather than features: an access log that silently stops recording, and a break-glass grant that nobody sees. Neither can be caught by a stack trace, so both have to be made observable at deployment time.

**The division is fixed and is the same in all four stories.** The app slice is **RWB-P4-E1039-APP**, the contract is **RWB-P4-E1039-CON**, the schema and the tables are **RWB-P4-E1039-DB**, and **RWB-ITG-E1039-ITG** proves the key end to end; **RWB-P5-E1039-APP** records the document side and **RWB-P7-E1039-APP** owns the central ledger. **RWB-P4-E1039-OPS** adds no behaviour to any of them: it deploys what they build, grants the service identity exactly the topics it writes, and turns two silent failures into paged or queued alerts.

The ACLs are the tightest statement of the split the workbench makes about the log. `rwb-access` **writes** `rwb.decision-record.v1` because every service publishes its own decision records (Architecture v5 slides 28 and 42), and it **writes** `rwb.access.events.v1` because that is the service's own topic for `AccessPolicyChanged` and `DoaLimitChanged`. It **reads** neither of another service's business topics, because P4 consumes no event (slide 14), and it has no ACL on `rwb.decision.events.v1`: the central ledger of P7 consumes the decision topic and answers the query, and the access owner never reads the ledger's topic or its tables. A deployment that granted a read on `rwb.decision-record.v1` would let the access owner keep a second copy of the ledger, which is exactly what DP-01 and DP-03 forbid.

The alert routes follow from who can act. A **failed access-log write** is a fail-closed condition: the read was refused, so a caller is blocked and the platform on-call queue is paged with MSG-P7-003 and the operation, route and trace id. A **refused access-log write** — a 403 on an admin read — is counted on the dashboard and never pages anyone, because a refusal is the control working. A **break-glass activation** and a **refused break-glass request** are security events: they go to the security administrator queue with MSG-P4-004 and MSG-P4-007, so the reviewer sees the use inside the review window of one working day rather than finding it in a monthly report. The thresholds and the review window are parameter values and not deployment values, so a business person changes them without a release (DP-06).

The values copied from the sources are the service, the base, the two topic names, the retry and `.dlt` suffixes, the message ids of the legacy story and the parameter names of the break-glass window and the review window. Where no source names the alert thresholds, the Kubernetes topology or the secret names, the story carries the placeholder and the assumption in force (GAP-0783; ASM-1430).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template, chart skeleton and pipeline are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-LIB).
- The Kafka event platform provisions topics with a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic, and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` exists as a platform asset (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON).
- The three environments DEV, SIT and UAT exist with the parameter scope of LOV-ENVIRONMENT, and the parameter rows of the break-glass window, the incident pattern, the reason bounds and the review window are loaded through RWB-P3-E1042-CON.
- RWB-P4-E1039-DB has published the migration folder of the service, so the pre-deploy job has a sequence to run; this story invokes it and owns no statement of it.
- The platform error envelope and the message catalogue are in force, so an alert can carry a message id and the agreed text.
- The platform secret store and the ACE Common PII and SOC logging path are available; the second copy of an access event still leaves the service through ACE Common (Architecture v5 slide 30).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7), and the per-service login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0783; ASM-1427).

##### 4. Flow

1. The pipeline builds the service image, runs the unit, component and contract tests, scans the image and the dependencies, and publishes the Helm chart version; the image digest and the chart version come from the same commit.
2. The chart deploys the service with its own login reference, the pre-deploy migration job of RWB-P4-E1039-DB and the two probes; the migration job runs before the deployment is marked ready.
3. The provisioning step creates `rwb.access.events.v1` with its retry topic and its `.dlt` topic, joins `rwb.decision-record.v1` as a producer, and creates the retry and `.dlt` topics of the shared topic where the platform has not already created them; the shared topic itself is reused and never recreated.
4. The ACL step applies the service identity's rights: WRITE on `rwb.access.events.v1`, WRITE on `rwb.decision-record.v1` and on the retry topics, DESCRIBE on both, and READ on a `.dlt` topic for the operator replay identity only.
5. The secret references are mounted from the platform secret store: the rwb-access login, the Kafka client credential and the Temporal mTLS material. No value of any of them is written in a values file, a chart template, a dashboard or the run book.
6. The dashboards are published: entries written, entries refused, entries failed, grant activations by environment, grants ended, the active grant count, and the outbox and ledger lag.
7. The alert rules are wired to the message ids of section 14 and to the run book entries, with the platform on-call queue for a failed write and the security administrator queue for break-glass.
8. A smoke step writes one synthetic access entry and one synthetic grant in a test namespace, checks that both appear once on the topic and on the dashboard, and checks that both alerts fire on a forced failure.
9. The run book is published with the six entries and is reviewed by the on-call rota before the SIT release.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The migration job fails | The deployment stays unready and the pipeline stops; no traffic to the new version | None | AC1 |
| X2 | The readiness probe fails after the start-up window | The pod is removed from the service and the pipeline marks the release failed | None | AC1 |
| X3 | The topic is missing its retry or `.dlt` topic | The provisioning step fails the release; the relay refuses to start | None | AC3 |
| X4 | The service identity is granted READ on `rwb.decision-record.v1` or on another service's business topic | The ACL review fails the release: a read right would let the service keep a second copy of the ledger | None | AC3 |
| X5 | A secret value is found in a values file, a chart template or the run book | The pipeline scan fails the release | None | AC4 |
| X6 | Access-log entries fail to be written | The alert carries MSG-P7-003, the operation and the trace id, and pages the platform on-call queue | MSG-P7-003 | AC5 |
| X7 | Access-log entries are refused for want of a right | The refused count rises on the dashboard and nothing pages; a refusal is the control working | MSG-P4-002 | AC5 |
| X8 | A break-glass grant is activated | The alert carries MSG-P4-004, the grant id and the end time, and routes to the security administrator queue | MSG-P4-004 | AC5 |
| X9 | A break-glass request is refused | The alert carries MSG-P4-007 and the reason code NO_BREAKGLASS_GRANT and routes to the security administrator queue | MSG-P4-007 | AC5 |
| X10 | The outbox relay lags beyond the alert threshold | The lag alert names the topic and the delay; the entries are already committed and the ledger catches up | None | AC5 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the chart skeleton, the platform topic provisioning and the secret store; no application code and no database object is built here |
| Negotiable | Replica counts, resource sizes, alert thresholds and the lag window are environment values, not story decisions |
| Valuable | Makes a silent failure of the log and an unseen break-glass use visible and actionable in every environment |
| Estimable | One chart, one pipeline stage, one migration job invocation, two probes, one provisioning and ACL step, four dashboard series and six alert rules |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the run book |
| Testable | Every criterion tests an artefact: the chart renders, the probes answer, the ACLs are exact, the secrets are references, the alerts fire on a synthetic metric |

These six criteria are new and test the deployment artefacts only. No legacy acceptance criterion is copied: AC1 to AC10 of RWB-E1-039 belong to RWB-P4-E1039-APP, and the legacy test cases are named in section 18.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One service, one schema, one login: the release uses the rwb-access login reference and no other service's credential | DP-02; Architecture v5 slide 41 notes |
| BR2 | The migration is the per-service Flyway sequence of RWB-P4-E1039-DB and runs before the deployment is ready; this story invokes it and provisions no database object | DP-15; RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| BR3 | Every topic the service uses has a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic, and the shared decision topic is reused and never recreated | DP-09; Architecture v5 slide 42 notes |
| BR4 | The service identity writes the decision topic and its own topic and reads neither of another service's business topics, because P4 consumes no event | DP-01, DP-09; Architecture v5 slide 14 |
| BR5 | No environment value is hard-coded: replica counts, resource sizes, thresholds, the lag window and the cadences come from values files and parameters | DP-06; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR6 | An alert carries a message id and the agreed text, and links one runbook entry | Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR7 | A failed access-log write pages the platform on-call queue; a refused write is counted and never pages | RWB-E1-039 BR2; MSG-P7-003, MSG-P4-002 |
| BR8 | A break-glass activation and a refused break-glass request route to the security administrator queue, so the review inside the window is possible | RWB-E1-039 BR7; MSG-P4-004, MSG-P4-007 |
| BR9 | No secret is written in a values file, a chart template, a dashboard, an alert payload or the run book | NFR-052 |
| BR10 | The deployment changes no business rule: the window, the incident pattern, the reason bounds and the review window stay parameter rows | DP-06; RWB-P4-E1039-CON BR11 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | Chart published | The image, the chart and the migration job pass the pipeline | Deploying |
| Deploying | Migration job complete and probes healthy | The schema is at the expected version and both probes answer | Ready |
| Ready | Release superseded | A new chart version is promoted | Rolling |
| Rolling | All pods on the new version | The old ReplicaSet drains | Ready |
| Ready | Migration job failed | The schema is not at the expected version | Failed |
| Failed | Rollback | The previous chart version is redeployed and the migration is reversed by its own script | Ready |

The grant and entry states of the capability belong to the app story; this story shows them only as dashboard and alert facts.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

The deployment exposes the four operations of RWB-P4-E1039-CON behind gateway-bff: `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log`, `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/break-glass-grants`, `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/break-glass-grants/{grantId}/end` and `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/break-glass-grants/{grantId}`. Owner rwb-access (P4). The probes are cluster-internal and are not part of the API surface.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Deployment need |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` | P4 rwb-access | The session and the break-glass state, at the readiness smoke and at each request |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | P3 rwb-case | The window of 4 hours, the incident pattern, the reason bounds and the review window; 2 s client budget with a breaker (DP-11) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 rwb-case | LOV-DECISION, LOV-CAPABILITY, LOV-SCOPE and LOV-ROLE with the version in force (DP-07) |

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Provisioning | Producing story |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | Shared topic reused with its retry and `.dlt` path; WRITE for the service identity through the outbox relay | RWB-P4-E1039-APP |
| `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` | `rwb.access.events.v1` | Topic with retry and `.dlt`; WRITE for the service identity | RWB-P4-E1037-APP |
| `rwb.access.DoALimitChanged.v1` | `rwb.access.events.v1` | Same topic, same retry and `.dlt` path | The delegation story of RWB-SVC-P4 |

The chart grants the write rights of all three because they share one service identity; the two policy events are not produced by this legacy key and are listed so that the ACL set is complete and reviewed once.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. `rwb-access` is the reference-data owner of Architecture v5 slide 14, whose contract line records no consumed event; the deployment creates no consumer group and subscribes to no topic, which is why the inbox of the service stays empty.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The capability starts no workflow and registers no activity; the `rwb-access` task queue carries the access review Schedule of RWB-P4-AD008-APP and this story does not register it.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The six-monthly access review list (JOB-18) is a Schedule of rwb-access but belongs to RWB-P4-AD008-APP, and the retention action of the access log is a partition drop owned by RWB-P4-E1039-DB and the platform retention job, not a Temporal Schedule.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None provisioned here. The four tables of this key — the local decision-record table of the DP-03 library, `outbox_event`, `processed_event` and `idempotency_key`, plus `break_glass_grant` — are created by RWB-P4-E1039-DB in `rwb_access`, and **this story creates no database object and no grant**. It invokes that migration job, and it provisions only Kafka topics and ACLs, secret references, dashboards and alerts. `decision_log_entry` and the central ledger are P7's and appear in no chart, no ACL and no dashboard of this service.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Deployment use |
|---|---|
| rwb-case WireMock | Runs in the pipeline and in the SIT smoke profile, so the release can start without the parameters and reference-data service |
| rwb-decision WireMock | Same, for the `GET /decision-log` answer the audit smoke reads |
| rwb-access contract fake | The seven fakes of RWB-P4-E1039-CON run as the SIT smoke profile of this service |
| IAM group fake | The member and non-member answers of the break-glass group for the smoke of AC5 |

The fakes are test-only workloads; they are not deployed into UAT or production.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 4 provided, 3 consumed in the deployment path | The four operations; the session, parameters and reference-data reads; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 3 published, 0 consumed | `rwb.decision-record.v1` and `rwb.access.events.v1` with their retry and `.dlt` topics; no consumer group |
| Temporal | 0 | No workflow, activity or Schedule is registered by this story |
| File | None | The release reads no runtime file; values files are build inputs |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables. The chart references one schema and one login | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`. The deployment grants the write right on the shared topic and its retry path | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library. The thresholds, the window and the review window are parameter rows and values, never chart literals | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case. The event codes and areas the smoke uses come from the list with its version | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout. The three consumed calls are configured with their budget and breaker | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/access/v1`. The route and the probes sit under the service base; the route is registered on gateway-bff | none |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting. The deployment provisions no lake sink and no lake export for the log | none; no lake data is deployed |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route. The route target, the banner state and the health check of the two reads are registered here | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Artefacts**

| Artefact | Content |
|---|---|
| `helm/rwb-access/` | Chart with deployment, service, pre-deploy migration job invocation, config map, secret references, probes and the route registration |
| `helm/rwb-access/values-dev.yaml`, `values-sit.yaml`, `values-uat.yaml` | Image digest, replicas, resources, probe timings, log level, the `rwb.access.access-log` switch, alert thresholds, environment name |
| Pipeline stage | Build, unit and contract tests, image and dependency scan, chart publish, promote the same artefact |
| Provisioning and ACL step | `rwb.access.events.v1` with retry and `.dlt`, producer rights on `rwb.decision-record.v1` and its retry path, no consumer group |
| Dashboards | Entries written, refused and failed; grant activations, ends and the active count; outbox lag; ledger lag |
| Alerts | Six rules, each with a message id, a route and one runbook entry |
| Runbook | Six entries, each with the check, the owner role, the recovery step and the message id |

**Probes.** Readiness answers healthy only when the migration is at the expected schema version, the outbox relay is running and the worker has polled; liveness answers healthy when the process is up and its internal loop is responsive. Neither probe writes to the database or to the log. Exact paths and timings are values.

**Migration job.** Invokes the per-service Flyway sequence of RWB-P4-E1039-DB with the rwb-access login as a pre-deploy job with a backoff limit; a failed job blocks the rollout and the release, and this story owns no statement of the migration.

**Alert mapping carried from the legacy story.**

| Message ID | Condition | Alert | Route |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-003 | An access-log entry cannot be written; the read was refused | Failed-write alert with the operation and the trace id, page | Platform on-call queue |
| MSG-P4-002 | An admin read is refused for want of a right | Refused-write count on the dashboard, no page | No route |
| MSG-P4-004 | A break-glass grant is activated | Activation alert with the grant id, the incident and the end time, ticket | Security administrator queue |
| MSG-P4-007 | A break-glass request is refused for want of an approval or a membership | Refused-grant alert with the reason code NO_BREAKGLASS_GRANT, ticket | Security administrator queue |
| None | The outbox relay or the ledger falls behind the lag window | Lag alert naming the topic and the delay | Platform on-call queue, no page below the window |
| None | The migration job or a probe fails | Release-failure alert naming the version | Platform on-call queue, page |

**Done when.** The chart renders in all three environments, the pipeline promotes one artefact, the probes answer without a write, the two topics and their retry and `.dlt` paths are verified by a test, the ACL set is exactly WRITE and DESCRIBE on the two topics with no READ on the decision topic, the six alerts fire on synthetic conditions with their message ids, the runbook entries are reviewed by the on-call rota, and the security administrator has accepted the break-glass route.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-003 | An access-log entry cannot be written and the read is refused | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | An admin read or write is refused for want of a right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-004 | A break-glass grant is activated; the banner and the activation alert | Emergency access is on until {time}. Every action is recorded. |
| MSG-P4-007 | A break-glass request is refused | Emergency access needs an approved break-glass request in the bank IAM with an open incident. |

The texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story; the deployment adds the alert routing and the runbook link, never a new wording and never a new message id. An alert payload carries the message id, the operation, the grant or incident id and the trace id, and **no personal value**: the case id of an entry is an identifier and the actor is a staff user reference.

##### 15. Screens and states

The deployment serves the banner of the ACE front-end shell (break-glass active, with the end time) and the access-log and grant panels of SCR-43 Roles and access, behind the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The operator-facing surfaces of this story are the pipeline run view, the release view, the dashboards, the alert queue and the run book. The composite route specification and the screen field list belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON and to the Epic 8 screen work; the deployment registers the route target and the health check of the two reads only.
