##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a values file: the window, the incident pattern, the reason bounds, the review window and the event codes are parameters and reference data, never a deployment value (BR5, BR10).
- No personal data in logs, dashboard series, alert payloads or the run book: identifiers, references, codes, counts and durations only.
- One login per service; the chart carries the rwb-access login reference and no other service's credential (DP-02, BR1).
- The service writes only `rwb_access`; the migration job is invoked, never edited, and this story provisions no database object (BR2).
- Every topic has a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic, and the shared decision topic is reused and never recreated (BR3).
- The service identity has no read on the decision topic and no ACL on another service's business topic (BR4).
- No secret is written into a values file, a chart template, a dashboard, an alert payload or the run book; all secrets come from the platform secret store (BR9).
- An alert never changes a rule: it points at the parameter row and at the runbook entry, and a business person changes the value without a release.
- The release pins the image digest and the chart version; a rebuild between environments is not allowed.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: integration slice of RWB-E1-039 for RWB-ITG-W1. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **QA integration engineer**, I want **the end-to-end proof of the RWB-E1-039 access-log and break-glass behaviour across P4 rwb-access (the grant and the access log), P3 rwb-case (the case read and the task action), P5 rwb-document (the document read), P7 rwb-decision (the central ledger and the audit query) and the P7 rwb-decision log store story**, so that **access and emergency access are proved on the real services before wave 1 exits**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story writes one append-only, hash-chained decision log entry inside the caller's transaction for every sign-in, refusal, read or export, and holds the break-glass grant on the session. In the 19-service target that single write is replaced by the decoupling pattern DP-03: each owning service writes a local decision record in its own schema in the same transaction as the change, and publishes `DecisionRecorded` to the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`; P7 rwb-decision collects the records idempotently into the central ledger with a completeness target of five minutes, gap alerts and daily chain verification (DP-03, Arch v5 slide 28). Auditors keep one place to search every decision, and no service takes a synchronous dependency on the ledger for an ordinary read. Only the points of no return wait for the ledger acknowledgement, and none of them is in this story.

The target split for the legacy key is therefore: P4 rwb-access owns the break-glass grant, the grant end it shows on the session, the access log query and the masking policy; P3 rwb-case owns the case read, the task action and the local decision record written for each; P5 rwb-document owns the document content read and its local decision record; P7 rwb-decision owns the central ledger, the consumer of `rwb.decision-record.v1` and the audit query over it, and its own log store is the product of the legacy RWB-E1-008 work. This story is the integration proof across those four owners and the log store.

No service contract is faked. The suite exercises the published wave 1 contracts of the four services through gateway-bff and reads the bank IAM only as an outside system. Where the sources do not name the cross-service split of the grant and ledger operations, the exact fault point for the fail-closed case or the location of the SIT evidence, the suite asserts through the owners' contracts and records the open point as Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0359; ASM-0466).

The measure is unchanged from the legacy story: reads of the case store and the document store written to the access log, target 100 percent (NFR-042). The story meets REQ-ACA-006 and REQ-ACA-008 and supports controls CTL-09 and CTL-11. It ends standing administrator access, because a platform administrator holds only the letters of RW-PLATADM except while an approved grant is active.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P7-E1008-APP is done: the P7 rwb-decision decision log store is append only and hash chained, and it receives the central ledger records.
- RWB-P4-E1039-APP is done: the break-glass grant, the grant check, the access event writer and the access log query are in SIT on P4 rwb-access.
- RWB-P5-E1039-APP is done: the document content read writes its local decision record before the file is returned.
- RWB-P7-E1039-APP is done: the audit query over the central ledger, the ledger completeness alert and the chain check are in SIT.
- The published contracts of P3 rwb-case, P4 rwb-access, P5 rwb-document and P7 rwb-decision are deployed under their own per-service bases behind gateway-bff.
- The harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG is available with its synthetic cases, users and documents.
- The SIT decision log store is available.
- The break-glass group RWB-SIT-BREAKGLASS exists in SIT (name per DL40, assumed).
- The four parameters rwb.access.breakglass.window-hours, rwb.access.breakglass.incident-pattern, rwb.access.breakglass.reason-min and rwb.access.breakglass.review-days are loaded, read as data rows through the parameters contract of P3 rwb-case.
- No production data is used, and no production connection is opened.
- The release date 30 November 2026 is tentative; a date is not a condition of this story.
- This story has no build dependency, so it is ready on Day 1.

##### 4. Flow

1. QA integration engineer: seeds the synthetic cases, users and documents of the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG and the RWB-SIT-BREAKGLASS membership of the platform administrator; no production data is used.
2. Harness: opens case RW-2026-000123 through gateway-bff with GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId} as U-4101 holding RW-CASEOWN at 10:15 on 3 December 2026.
3. Harness: reads the local decision record of P3 rwb-case and asserts the entry through GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log is present within five minutes.
4. Harness: activates the grant with POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/break-glass-grants at 10:30, with incident INC0004521, IAM request IAM-778812, area CASE_RECORD, right U, scope ALL and a reason of 46 characters, and asserts the banner MSG-P4-004 with time 14:30 read through GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session.
5. Harness: allows PATCH /api/recovery/case/v1/tasks/{taskId} at 14:20 and asserts the action carries the grant and the incident; refuses the same call at 14:31 with MSG-P4-002.
6. Harness: reads the document DOC-2026-0009981 of case RW-2026-000123 through GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/content under the grant and asserts one entry written before the file is returned.
7. Harness: runs the access audit query through GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log with caseId, decision AC-READ, from 2026-12-03 and to 2026-12-03 and asserts three entries in time order.
8. Harness: reads the access events of the day through GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log and compares them with the ledger entries of the same case and time window.
9. Harness: posts the negative cases — no grant, missing incident, a reason of 12 characters, a repeated key and a local decision record failure — and records every status, message and entry.
10. Harness: writes the evidence report, removes the synthetic fixtures and restores the clock.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The access log entry cannot be written | The read returns no data; status 503; an incident is raised to the platform administrator queue | MSG-P7-003 | AC5 |
| X2 | Break-glass is activated with no IAM grant for the caller | Refused with 403; the refusal is written as an AC-DENY entry with reason NO_BREAKGLASS_GRANT | MSG-P4-007 | AC4 |
| X3 | Break-glass is activated with no incident reference, a reference that fails the pattern, or a reason under the minimum | Refused with 422 naming the field; no grant is opened | MSG-GEN-001, MSG-GEN-002 | AC2 |
| X4 | An action is attempted after the grant has ended | The grant is ignored; the role's own letters apply; a refusal is written | MSG-P4-002 | AC2 |
| X5 | A second activation is sent while a grant is active | With the same Idempotency-Key the first response returns and no entry is written; with a new key the call returns 409 | MSG-GEN-004 | AC7 |
| X6 | A role without Platform administration R calls the access log or another admin endpoint | Refused with 403; an AC-DENY entry is written | MSG-P4-002 | AC6 |
| X7 | The central ledger lags the local record beyond five minutes | The read is never blocked; the lag is reported against the five-minute target and the ledger completeness alert is raised | None | AC1, AC5 |
| X8 | A consumed call exceeds the 2 s timeout or returns a server error | The GET is retried once under the suite policy; the evidence report records the call and the response; no assertion is made on unverified data | None | AC1, AC6 |
| X9 | The fixture set does not match the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG expectations, or the clock control cannot move the time | The suite fails as a harness fault and names the element; no service defect is raised | None | AC1, AC3 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | The suite is its own module and reuses the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG; it needs the four APP stories and the published contracts of P3, P4, P5 and P7, not their source code |
| Negotiable | The window, the incident pattern, the reason length, the review window, the fixture sizes and the exact fault-switch mechanism are data rows or properties of the harness; the story fixes the assertions and the call set |
| Valuable | Every access and every emergency access is proved on real services, and the ledger completeness of five minutes is measured rather than assumed, before wave 1 exits |
| Estimable | One suite module, one fixture pack, one grant clock control, one ledger completeness assertion and one evidence report |
| Small | Eight scenarios over four services and one shared topic; no service code and no schema change |
| Testable | Every scenario asserts a contract response, an entry, a status or a message; all data is synthetic |

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every sign-in, refusal, read of the case store or the document store, and export writes one access event to the decision log; in the target the record is local to the owning service and reaches the central ledger within five minutes | RWB-E1-039 BR1; REQ-ACA-006; NFR-042; DP-03 |
| BR2 | A read or export whose access event cannot be written returns no data; the fail-closed point is the local record write of the owning service | RWB-E1-039 BR2; Principle 5; ASM-0467 |
| BR3 | An access event lists field IDs and their masking position, never field values | RWB-E1-039 BR3; NFR-040 |
| BR4 | Break-glass needs a grant approved by the security administrator in the bank IAM, an open incident reference and a reason of at least the minimum length; the activation is served by P4 rwb-access | RWB-E1-039 BR4; REQ-ACA-008 |
| BR5 | A grant ends at the earlier of the window (4 hours, assumed) and the IAM group end, with no action by anyone, and the end is enforced on every request | RWB-E1-039 BR5; rwb.access.breakglass.window-hours; DL38 |
| BR6 | Every action under break-glass is marked with the grant and the incident reference, in the local record and in the ledger entry | RWB-E1-039 BR6 |
| BR7 | The security administrator reviews each use inside the review window (one working day, assumed); an unreviewed use goes to the role that heads SCB IT security and to Compliance | RWB-E1-039 BR7; DL38 |
| BR8 | A platform administrator holds only the letters of RW-PLATADM in the matrix version in force; any right beyond them comes only from an active break-glass grant | RWB-E1-039 BR8 |
| BR9 | A person may not review their own break-glass use | RWB-E1-039 BR9 |
| BR10 | Each owning service writes its own decision record in its own schema in the same transaction as the change and publishes `DecisionRecorded` to `rwb.decision-record.v1`; P7 rwb-decision owns the central ledger and collects the records within five minutes; no service writes another service's ledger table | DP-03; ADR-022; Arch v5 slide 28 |
| BR11 | Every cross-service call in the suite is one hop with a 2 s timeout | ADR-020; DP-11 |

##### 9. State transitions

None for the case status. This story does not change a case status. It observes the break-glass grant moving from Active to Ended at its end time, and the decision record moving from Local to collected centrally within five minutes.

| Object | State | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Break-glass grant | Active | The grant adds its right in its area and scope to the access check until the end time read through GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session; every entry carries the grant and the incident |
| Break-glass grant | Ended | The end time has passed; the grant is ignored with no action by anyone and an action beyond the role's own letters is refused with MSG-P4-002 |
| Decision record | Local | The owning service holds the record in its own schema, chained to its previous record, written in the same transaction as the read or action |
| Decision record | Collected centrally within five minutes | P7 rwb-decision holds the record in the central ledger, visible through GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log inside the completeness target |

The suite reads these states through the owners' contracts; it changes none of them directly.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| QA integration engineer | Runs the suite, seeds the synthetic fixtures, reads the evidence report |
| RW-SECADM Security administrator | Approves break-glass in the bank IAM and reviews each use; reads the access log |
| RW-PLATADM Platform administrator | Requests break-glass in the bank IAM and activates an approved grant; holds only the role's own letters when no grant is active |
| RW-AUDIT Internal audit | Queries access to a case through the decision log; changes nothing |
| RW-COMPLY Compliance and PDPA officer | Reads the access log; receives an unreviewed use |
| RW-COE, RW-DATASTEW | Read the access log |
| Every bank role | Generates access events by signing in, reading and exporting |
| SY-DECLOG Decision log writer | Writes the local decision record and the central ledger entry |

No other role is in scope for this story.

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |

| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision_log_entry (central ledger in P7 rwb-decision; local decision record in P3, P4 and P5) | all fields | Write (one entry per access event) |
| DF-DEC-002 | decision_log_entry | case_id | Write; empty for sign-in, refusal, export and break-glass events |

The legacy story writes decision_log_entry in the monolith. In the target the entry is written locally by the owning service and collected into the central ledger of P7 rwb-decision; the suite asserts both through contracts and never reads a schema. Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary. Every row in the suite is synthetic.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The suite provides no REST operation. The names reserved for P2 rwb-integration — `/api/recovery/integration/v1`, `rwb.integration.events.v1`, `rwb-integration` and `rwb_integration` — are not used, and no rwb_integration table is written.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method and path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|
| POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/break-glass-grants | P4 rwb-access | Activate the grant with the incident, the IAM request, area CASE_RECORD, right U and scope ALL |
| GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log | P4 rwb-access | Read the access events and the break-glass entries by user and date |
| GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session | P4 rwb-access | Read the grant end time shown in the banner |
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId} | P3 rwb-case | Open the case record that produces the AC-READ entry |
| PATCH /api/recovery/case/v1/tasks/{taskId} | P3 rwb-case | The action allowed at 14:20 and refused at 14:31 |
| GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/content | P5 rwb-document | The document read under the grant |
| GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log | P7 rwb-decision | The audit query and the ledger confirmation |

Every call is one hop with a 2 s timeout (ADR-020, DP-11).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The suite publishes no event.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Producer | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1 | rwb.decision-record.v1 | every service, with the ledger owned by P7 rwb-decision | The suite waits for the ledger entry of the owning service before it asserts the read |

The suite consumes no other event, and it produces none.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. No workflow, activity or Nexus operation is started or awaited by this story; the reads and the actions are synchronous REST calls.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Schedule is started, moved or waited for. The clock control moves the request time only.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The suite owns no table and never reads another service's schema (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

The bank IAM break-glass group membership is an outside system, read through the P4 session and grant responses; it is not a service contract. No service contract is faked: every call in section 12.2 goes to the real SIT service. The AC5 fault point is a test-only switch on the owning service's decision-record library, agreed with the service owner, and it is the only intervention in a running service.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Provided by the suite | Consumed by the suite |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 | 7 |
| Kafka | 0 | 1 |
| Temporal | 0 | 0 |
| File | 0 | 0 |

##### 13. Solution plan

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Suite module for RWB-ITG-W1, reusing harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG | Integration suite | Runs the eight scenarios against SIT and holds no service code |
| Fixture pack | Test data | Synthetic cases, users, documents and the RWB-SIT-BREAKGLASS membership of the platform administrator |
| Grant clock control | Harness control | Sets the grant start at 10:30 and moves the request time to 14:20, 14:31 and 18:00, then restores it |
| Ledger completeness assertion | Assertion | Polls GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log until the entry of the owning service appears and measures the elapsed time against the five-minute target |
| Evidence report | Report | Records per scenario the grant id, the entry ids of each service, the statuses, the messages and the elapsed ledger time |

Decoupling patterns applied (Template and Rules v1 §R5.5):

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added | Where it sits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | recovery.<table>, "recovery schema" | Owner's schema rwb_<name>; never read another service's tables | none | Each of P3, P4, P5 and P7 writes its own schema; the suite asserts through contracts only |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic rwb.decision-record.v1 | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON | On RWB-P4-E1039-APP, RWB-P5-E1039-APP and RWB-P7-E1039-APP; not a build dependency of this suite, which only waits for the ledger entry |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON | On RWB-P4-E1039-APP for the four rwb.access.breakglass.* values; the suite reads the same rows as data |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON | On the APP stories for the access event codes and the capability and scope lists; the suite sends the codes as data |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) | The seven consumed REST operations of section 12.2 |
| DP-13 | /api/recovery/v1 | /api/recovery/<short>/v1 | none | Every consumed path in section 12.2 |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting | none | The legacy E1-014 copy path is absent; AC8 asserts that the call set holds no lake endpoint |

The dependency-added column records the build dependency of the owning story. The H, C, I and X lists of this story are exactly those of the metadata table: no H, no C, no X, and the four I dependencies RWB-P7-E1008-APP, RWB-P4-E1039-APP, RWB-P5-E1039-APP and RWB-P7-E1039-APP. An ITG story waits on no build of its own.

Build steps:

1. Create the suite module next to harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG and wire it to the SIT endpoints of P3, P4, P5 and P7 through gateway-bff.
2. Build the fixture pack: synthetic cases, users, documents and the RWB-SIT-BREAKGLASS membership, with the four rwb.access.breakglass.* values read as data rows through the P3 parameters contract.
3. Add the grant clock control and the restore step.
4. Implement AC1 and AC6: the recorded case read, the ledger entry within five minutes and the audit query in time order.
5. Implement AC2, AC3 and AC7 with the clock at 10:30, 14:20, 14:31 and 18:00: the grant, the banner, the marked case action, the document read and the repeated activation.
6. Implement AC4 and the negative activation cases — no grant, missing incident and a reason of 12 characters — and assert the exact statuses and messages.
7. Implement AC5 through the agreed test-only fault switch on the owning service's decision-record library, and add the ledger lag report.
8. Prove AC8 over the call set of the run, write the evidence report and run the suite in SIT against the wave 1 release candidate.

Done when: all eight test cases pass in SIT against the published wave 1 contracts of P3, P4, P5 and P7, the ledger completeness report shows every entry collected inside the five-minute target, and no service code or schema was changed by this story apart from the agreed test-only fault switch.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-004 | Break-glass access is active | Emergency access is on until {time}. Every action is recorded. |
| MSG-P4-007 | Break-glass requested with no approved IAM grant | Emergency access needs an approved break-glass request in the bank IAM with an open incident. |
| MSG-P4-002 | An action after the grant has ended, or an access log query without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | Incident reference empty | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-002 | Reason shorter than the minimum, or page size outside 1 to 500 | {field} must be between {min} and {max}. |
| MSG-GEN-003 | Query from date after to date | {field} cannot be before {other}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | A second activation while a grant is active | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The access event cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The ledger completeness check is reported as one line of the evidence report and carries no message ID: {collected} of {expected} access entries of case {caseId} were collected into the central ledger of rwb-decision, the slowest in {seconds} seconds against the five-minute target of 300 seconds.

The message IDs and wording are copied from RWB-E1-039. No new message ID is added by this story. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story. The ACE front-end shell shows the MSG-P4-004 banner while a grant is active, and the suite reads the same end time through GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session. The access log is read through the P4 contract until SCR-43 Roles and access, and access to a case is read through the decision log query SCR-38 (RWB-E2-005). Neither screen is built or tested here.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the window, the incident pattern, the reason length and the review window are data rows read through the parameters contract.
- No personal data in logs, events, evidence or fixtures: field IDs and the masking position only, never values. The break-glass reason is free text written by the administrator and carries no customer data.
- No cross-service table read: every assertion goes through the owner's contract, and the suite owns no table.
- One hop and a 2 s timeout on every call (ADR-020).
- The grant end is enforced on every request and never by a job; the suite moves only its own clock.
- Synthetic data only, loaded by the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG.
- No production access of any kind from the suite or its configuration.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: moved RWB-E1-040 into `rwb-document` unchanged in behaviour; the checklist rows and the completeness flag now sit in `rwb_document`, the case stage and route are read through the rwb-case contract instead of an in-process call, the load goes through the rwb-case reference-data contract, and the refresh step of JOB-12 becomes a Temporal activity on queue `rwb-document`. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **litigation officer (RW-LITOFF)**, I want **the required documents per case type and route held as a versioned reference table that the case documents screen, the case list and the review queue read**, so that **a missing document shows on the case without a person checking a list**.

Inside `rwb-document` this is the checklist capability of the document hub:

- Service `rwb-document`, schema `rwb_document`, REST base `/api/recovery/document/v1` (DP-13), topic `rwb.document.events.v1` with event names `rwb.document.<Event>.v1` (DP-09), Temporal task queue `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document`.
- The story owns two tables in its own schema, `document_checklist_item` and `case_document_check` (DP-01, DP-15), and reads `document` and `document_type` of the same schema. It reads nothing of another service: the stage, the route and the owner of a case arrive from `rwb-case` over one REST hop with a mock (DP-11).
- The checklist table version, its rows and their valid-from dates come through the reference-data contract of rwb-case (DP-07, C RWB-P3-E1043-CON); the load is submitted and approved through that contract, so the reference data has one owner and one change process.
- The recompute is event driven: `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` from the store of RWB-P5-E1024-APP and `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` from `rwb-case`, both through the outbox and inbox library (DP-09). The refresh of a version that has just taken effect is one activity of the JOB-12 document-intake Schedule on queue `rwb-document` (DP-10).
- The screens are published by gateway-bff through the composite route (DP-19): the checklist panel of SCR-30 is RWB-P5-E1026-APP's tab, this story fills its required items, and the missing count of SCR-02 is read by `rwb-case` through this service.

The legacy behaviour is unchanged: the same rules, messages, required types, acceptance criteria and test cases with their values, the same authority letters and the same fields.

##### 2. Business rationale

Litigation packs and guarantee claims fail when a required document is missing, and today the gap is found by a person reading a paper list, often at filing (CTL-19, R-LIT-17). This story holds the checklist per case stage and route as data and keeps a completeness flag per case, recomputed whenever a document is stored or the case changes stage. It meets REQ-DCM-011 and gives the pack checks of Epics 4 and 5 (R-LIT-16, R-GUA-07) one checklist source. The measure is fields extracted without review (FSD P5 A2.16.1).

In the target the same intent needs three decoupling moves and no new behaviour: the two tables become `rwb_document` tables (DP-01), the case facts become the rwb-case contract with a mock and a 2 s budget (DP-11), and the flag becomes an operation the case list reads one hop away (DP-07, DP-19). A change to the items is still a data change with a valid-from date and no deployment (BR3).

##### 3. Preconditions

| Precondition | What it gives this story |
|---|---|
| RWB-PLT-E1043-CON | The reference-data client library, so the checklist version, its rows and their dates arrive as versioned data and never as code (DP-07) |
| RWB-PLT-TE006-CON | The outbox and inbox library and the CloudEvents envelope for the two consumed events (DP-09) |
| RWB-PLT-E1071-CON | The workflow kit and Schedules, so the refresh step of JOB-12 runs as a Temporal activity on queue `rwb-document` (DP-10) |
| RWB-PLT-E1044-CON | The per-service Flyway sequence, so the migration that creates the two tables belongs to `rwb_document` (DP-15) |
| RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The gateway-bff composite route that publishes the Documents tab and the case list (DP-19) |
| RWB-P5-E1024-APP | The document store and `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1`, so documents are stored and the event exists to listen to |
| RWB-P5-E1025-APP | Document type table version "DOCTYPE-2026.11" in force with the six agreed types |
| RWB-P5-E1026-APP | The `GET /cases/{caseId}/document-checklist` placeholder and the SCR-30 panel this story fills |
| RWB-P3-E1043-CON | The reference-data contract of rwb-case; a contract dependency, so it never blocks the build |

Business preconditions carried from RWB-E1-040:

- Checklist version "CHK-2026.11" loaded and approved with valid from 30 November 2026, assumed until the bank list is signed (DL19): stage LITIGATION requires DEMAND_LETTER, COURT_NOTICE, TITLE_DEED and APPRAISAL_REPORT; stage DEED_IN_LIEU requires TITLE_DEED, APPRAISAL_REPORT and SETTLEMENT_AGREEMENT.
- The rwb-case contract returns stage_code, route_code and owner of a case, and `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` (EV-05) is published by `rwb-case`. The operation ID and the field names of that read are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2337; ASM-3889).
- The reference-load and approval operations of table "DOCUMENT_CHECKLIST" are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2337; ASM-3889); the load is submitted and approved through the rwb-case reference-data contract (DP-07 default ruling).
- Feature flag `rwb.document.checklist` is on, the service-scoped name of the legacy flag `rwb.dochub.checklist`. Off: the endpoint returns the RWB-P5-E1026-APP placeholder and no flag is written.

##### 4. Flow

1. Reference data administrator: loads the checklist file through the rwb-case reference-data contract, table "DOCUMENT_CHECKLIST", with its valid-from date; the approver with Reference data A approves it, and the load is handed to this service for validation.
2. ChecklistLoader: validates every row: stage in LOV-STAGE, route in LOV-ROUTE or empty, document type in the type table in force, no duplicate row; it refuses the load whole on any error and answers the row error to the contract.
3. ChecklistEvaluator: on `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` (EV-16), on `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` (EV-05) and when a checklist version takes effect, takes the stage and the route of the case through the rwb-case contract, one hop, 2 s timeout, circuit breaker and one GET retry with jitter.
4. ChecklistEvaluator: picks the rows of the version in force for that stage, using the rows of the route where they exist and the rows with no route otherwise.
5. ChecklistEvaluator: counts the active documents of each required type on the case and writes `case_document_check`: checklist version, required count, present count, missing types and complete.
6. Litigation officer: opens the Documents tab (SCR-30) through gateway-bff; `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/document-checklist` returns each required item marked present or missing.
7. Case owner: sees the number of missing documents for each case on the case list (SCR-02); `rwb-case` reads it from this service, at most 500 case IDs per call.
8. ChecklistRefreshActivity: on the JOB-12 document-intake Schedule (every 15 minutes) finds checklist versions whose valid-from date has been reached since the last run and recomputes the cases of the stages they change.

The evaluation is read-only for the case: it writes `case_document_check` and never moves a case. A failure between step 3 and step 5 leaves the previous flag in place and the event is retried (section 5, X3 and X6).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The case stage has no checklist rows | The checklist shows "No checklist for this case type"; complete is empty | None | AC6 |
| X2 | A checklist load names a document type not in the type table, or a stage not in LOV-STAGE | Load refused in full; the version in force is unchanged | MSG-P3-027 | AC7 |
| X3 | The same `DocumentStored` event arrives twice | One recompute result; the second is ignored and counted as a repeat in the inbox | None | AC8 |
| X4 | A document type is present only as an inactive earlier version | Counted once, through its active version | None | AC9 |
| X5 | A role without Documents R opens the checklist | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-040-10 (Access) |
| X6 | The rwb-case contract does not answer inside the 2 s budget, or answers with an error | No flag is written; the event is retried; after the retry limit it goes to `rwb.document.events.v1.dlt` with the platform administrator as owner | None | Section 13, build step 4 |
| X7 | The case is outside the user's scope | Refused with 403; no item list is returned | MSG-P4-003 | TC-E1-040-10 (Access) |

X6 is the only new path: it replaces the in-process call of the legacy story with a contract call, and it changes nothing in the case.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the store, the type table and the placeholder endpoint (RWB-P5-E1024-APP, RWB-P5-E1025-APP, RWB-P5-E1026-APP) and the five platform contracts, all earlier in the wave or Day 1 |
| Negotiable | The items per stage and route are data under DL19; the story fixes only how they are applied |
| Valuable | Missing documents show on the case and on the case list before a pack is built |
| Estimable | Two tables, one loader, one evaluator, two listeners, one activity, one operation and two screen parts |
| Small | Fits within one week with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test case in section 16 |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Document checklist per case type as reference data

  Background:
    Given checklist version "CHK-2026.11" is in force
    Given stage "LITIGATION" requires DEMAND_LETTER, COURT_NOTICE, TITLE_DEED and APPRAISAL_REPORT
    Given stage "DEED_IN_LIEU" requires TITLE_DEED, APPRAISAL_REPORT and SETTLEMENT_AGREEMENT
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the stage, the route and the owner of the case under test

  Scenario: AC1 Checklist by type (legacy RWB-E1-040 AC1)
    Given case "RW-2026-000123" at stage "LITIGATION" holds a demand letter and a court notice
    When the litigation officer opens the Documents tab
    Then the checklist shows the 4 items from version "CHK-2026.11" for "LITIGATION"
    Then DEMAND_LETTER and COURT_NOTICE are marked present
    Then TITLE_DEED and APPRAISAL_REPORT are marked missing

  Scenario: AC2 Change as data (legacy RWB-E1-040 AC2)
    Given version "CHK-2026.12" adds GUARANTOR_NOTICE for "DEED_IN_LIEU" and is approved with valid from 1 December 2026
    Given the rwb-case reference-data contract mock returns version "CHK-2026.12" in force from 1 December 2026
    When case "RW-2026-000456" at stage "DEED_IN_LIEU" is opened on 1 December 2026
    Then the checklist shows 4 items including GUARANTOR_NOTICE
    Then no code was deployed between 30 November and 1 December 2026

  Scenario: AC3 Completeness flag (legacy RWB-E1-040 AC3)
    Given case "RW-2026-000456" at stage "DEED_IN_LIEU" holds a title deed and an appraisal report
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case list read for the case owner's cases
    When the pack check runs after the appraisal report is stored
    Then case_document_check for the case has complete false, missing count 1 and missing type SETTLEMENT_AGREEMENT
    Then the case owner sees "1 missing" for the case on the case list

  Scenario: AC4 The missing document arrives (legacy RWB-E1-040 AC4)
    Given the case from AC3 with SETTLEMENT_AGREEMENT missing
    When a settlement agreement is stored on the case
    Then case_document_check has complete true and missing count 0
    Then the case list shows no missing documents for the case

  Scenario: AC5 Stage change (legacy RWB-E1-040 AC5)
    Given case "RW-2026-000789" at stage "DEED_IN_LIEU" with complete true
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns CaseStateChanged moving the case to stage "LITIGATION"
    When CaseStateChanged moves it to stage "LITIGATION"
    Then the pack check uses the "LITIGATION" rows
    Then case_document_check has complete false with the missing litigation types

  Scenario: AC6 No checklist for the stage (legacy RWB-E1-040 AC6)
    Given case "RW-2026-000321" at stage "DEBT_SALE" and no rows for "DEBT_SALE"
    When the Documents tab opens
    Then the checklist shows "No checklist for this case type"
    Then case_document_check has complete empty and missing count 0

  Scenario: AC7 Load with an unknown type (legacy RWB-E1-040 AC7)
    Given a load file for table "DOCUMENT_CHECKLIST" with a row for stage "LITIGATION" and type "POWER_OF_ATTORNEY"
    Given the rwb-case reference-data contract mock returns the "DOCUMENT_CHECKLIST" load for validation
    When the reference data administrator loads it
    Then the system refuses the load in full with MSG-P3-027 naming the row and "document type not in the type table"
    Then version "CHK-2026.11" stays in force

  Scenario: AC8 The same event twice (legacy RWB-E1-040 AC8)
    Given DocumentStored for one document on case "RW-2026-000123" is delivered twice with the same event ID
    When the evaluator handles both
    Then the system writes case_document_check once for that event
    Then the system counts the second delivery as a repeat

  Scenario: AC9 Earlier version of a document (legacy RWB-E1-040 AC9)
    Given case "RW-2026-000123" holds an appraisal report at version 2 with version 1 inactive
    When the pack check runs
    Then APPRAISAL_REPORT counts as present once
```

The four extra Givens mock the rwb-case contract, the CaseStateChanged message and the rwb-case reference-data load; every value of the legacy criteria is kept unchanged, and no business value is added.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The checklist per case type is held as reference data so a missing document is visible | REQ-DCM-011; FEAT-DCM-16 |
| BR2 | The case type is the case stage, with route rows taking precedence over rows with no route | LOV-STAGE; LOV-ROUTE; checklist table (New) |
| BR3 | A checklist version takes effect on its valid from date, without a deployment | refdata.txt change process; R-UNI-38; DT02 |
| BR4 | Only active documents count, once per type | FEAT-DCM-20 |
| BR5 | The completeness flag is recomputed on every document stored and every stage change | EV-16; EV-05 |
| BR6 | A repeated event changes nothing | R-UNI-40 |
| BR7 | The checklist is the source the pack checks read in later epics | R-LIT-16, R-LIT-17, R-GUA-07, R-GUA-08 |

Target-service statements that make the rules hold in `rwb-document`:

- BR1 and BR3 are held by DP-07: the rows carry `table_version`, `valid_from` and `valid_to`, the service reads the version in force with the business date, and a new version is a new load, never a code change.
- BR2 is executed by the query on `document_checklist_item`: rows of the route where they exist, rows with no route otherwise, ordered by `sort_order`.
- BR4 counts `document` rows of the case with `is_active` true and the required type, once per type.
- BR5 and BR6 are held by the inbox: both listeners run inside the inbox transaction, `processed_event` holds the event ID, and a repeat returns without a write.
- BR7 is held by the operation, which the pack checks of Epics 4 and 5 and the case list of `rwb-case` read; DP-01 keeps every read and write in `rwb_document`.

##### 9. State transitions

None for the case. This story does not change a case status. It writes the completeness flag of the case in `case_document_check`: complete false while a required type is missing, true when every required type is present, empty when the stage has no checklist. The record is upserted once per case, with `checked_at` and the ID of the event that caused it in `last_event_id`.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | Loads the checklist (Reference data C) |
| Approver with Reference data A | Approves the load; no role holds Reference data A in the permission matrix today, assumed granted to the legal counsel as co-owner of the checklist (DL01; GAP-2338; ASM-3890) |
| RW-LITOFF, RW-CASEOWN and roles with Documents R | Read the checklist and the flag for cases in their scope |
| RW-LEGAL, legal counsel | Agrees the items per stage (DL19) |
| SY-CASEWF | Publishes CaseStateChanged that triggers the recompute |

The authorisation decision is taken by `rwb-access` (Recovery roles as data, scope and masking in `rwb_access`) and consumed as the cached permission decision the service holds; the refusal shapes stay 403 with MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P4-003. The guard itself is inherited from the service template (DP-08) and this story adds no guard. The loader acts for `rwb-case` on the reference-data contract and takes its identity from the per-service login (DP-02).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/document/v1`, owned by P5, path and authorization taken from TSD P5 T-A.2 (API-P5-008).

**GET /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/document-checklist** (API-P5-008)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Path caseId; the placeholder of RWB-P5-E1026-APP is extended with the repeatable query `caseId` for the batch count of up to 500 cases |
| Response | 200 DocumentChecklist: caseId, checklistVersion, stageCode, items [documentType, label, required, presentCount], missingCount, complete; for a batch call, one entry per case ID |
| Errors | 401; 403 no Documents R (MSG-P4-002) or out of scope (MSG-P4-003); 404; 422 more than 500 IDs; 503 |
| Authorization | Documents, right R, scope applied |
| Idempotency | Not applicable |
| Field names | The response field names above are the legacy item names; the published names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2337; ASM-3889) |

The batch form exists because the legacy published interface `DocumentChecklistService.missingCounts(Collection<UUID>)`, at most 500 IDs per call, is an in-process call that the rwb-case case list now has to make over REST; no operation for it appears in the TSD P5 inventory. Its operation ID and query name are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2337; ASM-3889).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| GET `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 | The CaseDirectory read: stage_code, route_code and owner_user_id; one hop, 2 s timeout, breaker, one GET retry with jitter. Its operation ID is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2337; ASM-3889) |
| The reference-load and approval of table "DOCUMENT_CHECKLIST" | P3 behind the reference-data client of DP-07 | The file, its valid-from date, the approval and the version register; this service validates the rows and answers the row error. Path and operation ID are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2337; ASM-3889) |
| The reference-data read of DP-07 | P3 behind the client library | The checklist version in force for the business date and its rows; cached, read through RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON |

###### 12.3 Events published

None. This story publishes no event: it writes `case_document_check` inside the inbox transaction of the event that caused the recompute, and the case list reads the count through the operation of 12.1.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Producer | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` (EV-16) | `rwb.document.events.v1` | The store of RWB-P5-E1024-APP | Recompute the checklist of the case |
| `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` (EV-05) | `rwb.case.events.v1` | rwb-case | Recompute with the new stage and route |

Idempotency key is the CloudEvents event ID: a repeat is ignored and counted (BR6, R-UNI-40). A failed handling retries on the topic policy (1 min, 10 min, 1 h) and then goes to `rwb.document.events.v1.dlt` with the platform administrator as owner. No personal data travels in either payload: case ID, document ID, document type and stage code only.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Item | Name | Queue | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|---|
| Activity | `checklistRefresh` | `rwb-document` | Finds the checklist versions whose valid-from date has been reached since the last run and recomputes the cases of the stages they change |
| Workflow | `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` (owned by RWB-P5-E1026-APP's intake story, RWB-P5-E1049-APP) | `rwb-document` | Hosts the activity as the refresh step of JOB-12; this story adds no workflow |

###### 12.6 Schedules

The JOB-12 document-intake Schedule every 15 minutes (FSD P5 AC-BG-P5-016-01) runs `checklistRefresh` as one of its steps; the Schedule replaces Quartz (DP-10) and this story adds no Schedule of its own. The Schedule ID and the retention of its history are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2337; ASM-3889).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|
| `document_checklist_item` | P5 (`rwb_document`) | Write: the validated rows of a checklist version, their stage, route, type, order and dates |
| `case_document_check` | P5 (`rwb_document`) | Write: version, required count, present count, missing types, complete, checked_at, last_event_id; upsert by case |
| `document` | P5 (`rwb_document`) | Read: case_id, document_type, is_active |
| `document_type` | P5 (`rwb_document`) | Read: the types in force for the load validation |
| `processed_event` | PLT library in `rwb_document` | Write: the consumed event IDs of the inbox |

No table of another service is read, written or joined.

| rwb-case reference-data fake | RWB-PLT-E1043-CON with RWB-P3-E1043-CON | Version "CHK-2026.11" and "CHK-2026.12" with their rows and valid-from dates; the load of table "DOCUMENT_CHECKLIST" |
| document store fake | RWB-P5-E1024-APP | `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` for AC3, AC4, AC8 and AC9, with the same event ID twice for AC8 |

| REST | Provided 1, consumed 2 | The checklist read and its batch form provided; the case read and the reference-data read consumed through the contract and the client library |
| Kafka | Published 0, consumed 2 | `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` and `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1`, through the inbox |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document`, module `checklist`; front end folder `recovery/documents`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| ChecklistLoader | Service | Implements the reference-table loader for table "DOCUMENT_CHECKLIST" and validates rows against LOV-STAGE, LOV-ROUTE and the type table |
| ChecklistEvaluator | Service | Picks the rows for the stage and route, counts the active documents and writes `case_document_check` |
| DocumentStoredChecklistListener, CaseStateChangedChecklistListener | Listener | Inbox listeners that call the evaluator and keep the event ID for repeats |
| ChecklistRefreshActivity | Temporal activity | The refresh step of JOB-12: versions whose valid-from date has been reached since the last run |
| DocumentChecklistController | Controller | `GET /cases/{caseId}/document-checklist`, single and batch, with the access check |
| ChecklistRepository, CaseDocumentCheckRepository | Repository | Read and write the two tables of `rwb_document` only |
| DocumentChecklistPanel | React component | Replaces the placeholder on SCR-30 with required items present or missing |
| MissingDocumentsBadge | React component | The count shown on the SCR-02 case list rows, read through gateway-bff |

**Database**

- Flyway migration in the per-service sequence of DP-15 (legacy name `V1_5_040__document_checklist.sql`; the sequence number is the service's own) creates `document_checklist_item` (id, stage_code varchar(20), route_code varchar(4), document_type varchar(30), required boolean, sort_order integer, table_version varchar(20), valid_from date, valid_to date, load_id uuid, standard columns) with unique (stage_code, route_code, document_type, table_version); and `case_document_check` (id, case_id uuid, checklist_version varchar(20), required_count integer, present_count integer, missing_types jsonb, complete boolean, checked_at timestamptz, last_event_id uuid, standard columns) with unique (case_id).
- Index `ix_checklist_stage` on `document_checklist_item` (stage_code, valid_from).

**Configuration and reference data**

- Checklist "CHK-2026.11", prepared by the reference data administrator, agreed with the legal counsel and the litigation officers (DL19), loaded through the rwb-case reference-data contract.
- No property beyond the feature flag `rwb.document.checklist`.

**Build steps**

1. Write the migration; test the unique keys on `document_checklist_item` and on `case_document_check`.
2. Build ChecklistLoader with the validation against LOV-STAGE, LOV-ROUTE and the type table; test AC7.
3. Build ChecklistEvaluator with the route precedence and the active-version rule; unit test AC1, AC6 and AC9.
4. Build the two inbox listeners with the repeat check and the 503 path of X6; test AC3, AC4, AC5 and AC8.
5. Build ChecklistRefreshActivity and wire it into the JOB-12 Schedule; test AC2 on 30 November and 1 December 2026.
6. Extend the checklist operation with the batch form and build DocumentChecklistPanel and MissingDocumentsBadge; component tests and the access test.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-01 and DP-15 move the two legacy tables into `rwb_document` with the service's own migration. DP-07 replaces the shared reference-data service with the rwb-case contract, so the checklist version and its rows are versioned data. DP-09 is the event path: both events arrive through the inbox with the event ID as the key. DP-10 replaces the Quartz step of JOB-12 with the `checklistRefresh` activity on the `rwb-document` queue. DP-11 is the change to the case facts: the published interface `CaseDirectory` becomes a REST call with a mock, one hop and a 2 s budget. DP-13 and DP-19 put the two screens on the service base and the gateway-bff composite route.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, and the case list shows the missing count for the synthetic litigation cases in SIT.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P5-023 | Required documents are missing on the case | {count} required documents are missing for this case: {types}. |
| MSG-P3-027 | Checklist load fails a check | The {table} load was refused: {error} at row {row}. The version in force is unchanged. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | Case outside the scope | This case is not in your scope. |

Thai text for each message follows decision DL10. MSG-P3-027 is owned by the rwb-case reference-load operation: this service raises the row error and rwb-case answers the message, so the text and the ID stay unchanged. Every error is an RFC 9457 problem response carrying `messageId`.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-30 Case documents and SCR-02 Case list are reached through gateway-bff and the composite route of DP-19 (H RWB-PLT-N001-CON); the browser never calls `rwb-document` directly.

| Screen | State | What the user sees and does |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-30 Case documents | list | The checklist panel with each required type present or missing, and MSG-P5-023 above it when a type is missing |
| SCR-30 Case documents | Loading | Skeleton rows while the checklist loads |
| SCR-02 Case list | list | A "Documents missing" count per case; 0 shows as empty |
| SCR-02 Case list | filtered | The user can filter cases with one or more missing documents |

The panel is RWB-P5-E1026-APP's tab with the required items filled by this story; when the stage has no checklist the panel shows the text of AC6 and no count. The route path and the fields gateway-bff merges are RWB-PLT-N001-CON's.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: stages, routes and required types are rows in `document_checklist_item` (BR-P5-016, DP-07).
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts: the flag holds type codes and counts only.
- No read of another service's tables (DP-01): stage, route and owner come through the rwb-case contract, and `rwb-case` reads the flag through the operation of 12.1.
- The evaluator never blocks a case move; it reports only.
- The migration runs in `rwb_document` on the per-service Flyway sequence; no shared baseline is edited (DP-15).
- The feature flag `rwb.document.checklist` returns the placeholder without a rollback of the schema.

##### 18. Traceability

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the retention classes, the monthly retention run and the virus scan on intake moved into `rwb-document` with the schema `rwb_document`, the topic `rwb.document.events.v1`, the REST base `/api/recovery/document/v1`, the Temporal task queue `rwb-document` and the monthly retention Schedule of the workflow kit. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **compliance and PDPA officer (RW-COMPLY)**, I want **every uploaded or scanned file checked for malware before it is stored, and a retention class per document type that the store applies and a monthly job acts on**, so that **the store holds only safe files and keeps each document for the time the policy sets, never removing one silently or while a legal hold is in place**.

Inside `rwb-document` this is the retention and intake-safety capability of the document service:

- Service `rwb-document`, schema `rwb_document`, REST base `/api/recovery/document/v1`, topic `rwb.document.events.v1` with event names `rwb.document.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document`.
- Retention is this service's own: `retention_rule` and `retention_action` are P5's in `rwb_document` (the Ownership Map ruling moves the retention tables to the document hub, on Architecture v5 slides 16, 41 and 44 where JOB-17 runs in `rwb-document`), and the legacy monthly job JOB-17 becomes the `retention-monthly` Temporal Schedule on queue `rwb-document` through the workflow kit (DP-10, H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON).
- The scan result is a document attribute written by this service: `document_intake.scan_result` and `document_intake.scanned_at` (DF-DOC-058, DF-DOC-059) on the intake path, and the same two attributes on the `document` row for an upload that creates no intake item. The scanning engine's own capacity, licences, queue and throughput are not this story's table and not this service's data (ASM-1771).
- The file itself is never written or moved by this story's own code: the store RWB-P5-E1024-APP owns the Blob containers and the platform storage product, and this story calls the store to move an infected file to `rwb-quarantine`, to move a due blob to the archive tier and to write the review-list file to the standard container.
- The legal hold is `recovery_case.legal_hold` (DF-CAS-020) in `rwb-case`, read through the case contract `GET /cases/{caseId}` (DP-11, one hop, 2 s timeout, breaker per downstream) and never from a case table and never from a `rwb_case` copy. The plan lists no C row for that read; it is consumed and faked (ASM-1769).
- The class of a type is `document_type.retention_class` (DF-REF-223) read locally; the class rows with the period, the age basis, the end action and the rule version are `retention_rule` (DF-REF-116 to DF-REF-127); the list values of LOV-RETENTION, LOV-SCAN-RESULT, LOV-RETENTION-ACTION and LOV-RETENTION-END are read through the reference-data contract of `rwb-case` (DP-07, H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, C RWB-P3-E1043-CON) and no list value is typed in code.
- Every archive and every listed disposal writes its decision record through the local decision-record library of DP-03, in the same transaction as the `retention_action` row and the event row, with decision code DOCRET; a failed record means nothing is archived (MSG-P7-003, R-UNI-39).
- The interaction ledger is `rwb-source-data`'s (DP-18): this service owns no ledger table, reads no ledger row and writes no ledger row. The audit event `MALWARE_BLOCKED` of the legacy story is an audit entry in the service audit log, and where the monolith also recorded the scan in the ledger, the target keeps the audit entry and reaches the ledger only through the P1 contract, never through a local table.
- The database login is one per service (DP-02). Its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0995; ASM-1772); this story uses the phrase "the rwb-document login (DP-02)" and never a shared login.

The legacy behaviour is carried unchanged in intent and values: the same user story, rationale, preconditions, flow, exception paths, business rules, messages, authority, data fields, ten acceptance criteria and twelve test cases, adapted to the target service's schema, topic, API base, workflow template and Schedule.

##### 2. Business rationale

Files reach the bank from branches, partners and email; one infected file in the store reaches every user who opens it. Documents also have no retention rule today, so nothing shows when a document may be archived (FSD P5 A2.17, A2.18). This story scans every file before storage and quarantines a failed file, holds the retention classes as data, and runs the monthly retention run to archive documents past their class or list them for the Compliance review. It meets REQ-DCM-010 and REQ-DCM-016 (legal hold overrides retention), with NFR-028, NFR-072 and NFR-074.

The realignment changes the mechanics, not the business rule:

1. One schema, one topic, one API base: `rwb_document`, `rwb.document.events.v1` and `/api/recovery/document/v1` (DP-01, DP-13). No table of another service is read, the legacy recovery-schema names do not survive, and the retention tables sit in the document hub's own schema.
2. The legal hold arrives through the `rwb-case` contract `GET /cases/{caseId}` with a mock and a 2 s timeout (DP-11, C from the legacy dependency), so the run builds against a published shape and never against a case table.
3. The class list is reference data of `rwb-case` behind the reference-data contract and client library (DP-07), while the class rows themselves are this service's `retention_rule` data, loaded and approved through its own admin operation. That split is the reason the legacy reference-load step becomes a document-hub operation and the list values stay with the reference-data owner.
4. The legacy decision-log write becomes the local decision-record library of DP-03, written in the same transaction as the `retention_action` row and the event row and published on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; `rwb-decision` collects it into the central ledger, so an archive without its record does not proceed.
5. JOB-17 becomes the `retention-monthly` Schedule of the workflow kit on queue `rwb-document` (DP-10): a Schedule, a workflow and activities, not a Quartz row and not a shared job table. The scan step becomes an activity of the intake workflow owned by RWB-P5-E1049-APP, which is why the scan runs first without this story owning the 15-minute Schedule.
6. The interaction ledger leaves this story altogether (DP-18): the ledger is P1's, the audit event is an audit entry, and the job counts live on the run record of this service rather than in a ledger row.
7. The retention and scan reads reach the screens through the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19 (RWB-PLT-N001-CON); the migration is one step in the per-service Flyway sequence (DP-15) in `rwb_document`.
8. The retention periods and the end actions stay data of the class version in force (the legacy assumed DL26), and the scan engine stays behind a client and a stub, so neither the period of a class nor the provider of the scanner is a value of this code.

The database login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0995; ASM-1772). The name of the scanning service and its provider is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0995; ASM-1771).

The status and the release are the run defaults of D-RCV-60: the story is Draft (realignment v1) and the release is 30 November 2026 (tentative), with no approval and no build go-ahead recorded in the sources read (ASM-1773).

##### 4. Flow

1. The 15-minute document-intake Schedule (legacy JOB-12, owned by RWB-P5-E1049-APP) starts `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` and runs the scan step first, before the OCR step (12.5).
2. `scanIntakeItem` activity: selects intake items with no `scan_result` and sends each file to the scan client, which calls the bank scanning service through `POST /scans` of this service's own contract (12.1, 12.2); the item's `intake_ref` is the only identifier sent, never the file name or its content.
3. `scanIntakeItem`: on `CLEAN`, sets `document_intake.scan_result` = CLEAN and `scanned_at`, so the OCR step may read the item; on `INFECTED`, calls the store to move the file to `rwb-quarantine`, sets `scan_result` = INFECTED, writes the audit event `MALWARE_BLOCKED` with the intake ID and the source to the service audit log, and alerts the platform administrator; no `document` row is ever written and the file is never stored.
4. Upload (RWB-P5-E1026-APP): calls `POST /scans` before the store call; an `INFECTED` answer returns 422 MSG-P5-016 on the upload and nothing is stored; if the scanning service does not answer inside the declared budget the call returns 503 MSG-P5-022 and nothing is kept.
5. The store (RWB-P5-E1024-APP): stores clean files with the retention class of the type; legal types go to the write-once container. This story writes no document row and no blob.
6. `retention-monthly` Schedule starts `RetentionWorkflow` on the first Sunday of each month at 02:30 Asia/Bangkok; for each active document the run computes expiry date = stored date (`document.created_at`) plus `retention_months` of its class row in the version in force.
7. `checkLegalHold` activity: skips a document whose case has `legal_hold` true, read through the `rwb-case` contract, and counts it as held (`retention_action.action` = HELD).
8. `archiveDocument` / `listForReview` activities: for a due document with end action ARCHIVE, writes the decision record DOCRET through the library of DP-03, calls the store to move the blob to the archive tier, sets the document state ARCHIVED and inserts the `retention_action` row (action ARCHIVED) in the same transaction as the record; for end action REVIEW, adds it to the review list for Compliance, inserts the action row (action LISTED) and changes nothing else.
9. `writeReviewList` activity: writes the review list to `retention/review/{runDate}.csv` in the standard container through the store, and the counts (due, archived, listed, held, exceptions) to the run record; `Exception` rows carry RETENTION_CLASS_MISSING where a class is not in force.
10. Event and record relay: the retention_action row, its decision record and the `rwb.document.RetentionApplied.v1` row are committed together; the platform relay publishes the record on `rwb.decision-record.v1` and the event on `rwb.document.events.v1`, once per committed action, keyed by caseId, with no personal data.
11. Compliance reads the review list file and the run counts; the platform administrator sees the scan alerts and the run results through the composite route of DP-19.

The decision record is written before the change takes effect and in the same transaction as the `retention_action` row and the event row, so a failure leaves all three unchanged (R-UNI-39).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The scan finds malware on an intake file | File quarantined, not stored, audit event written, platform administrator alerted | MSG-P5-016 | AC1 |
| X2 | The scanning service does not answer | Intake item stays unscanned and is not read by OCR; retried in the next run; alert after two failed runs; an upload returns 503 and nothing is stored | MSG-P5-022 | AC6 |
| X3 | A due document is on a case with a legal hold | Not archived, not listed; counted as held | None | AC5 |
| X4 | A document carries a class not in the retention table | Listed as an exception RETENTION_CLASS_MISSING; nothing changes | None | AC7 |
| X5 | The retention run runs again in the same month | Documents already archived or listed for that month are not acted on again | None | AC8 |
| X6 | A retention class load holds an end action other than ARCHIVE or REVIEW, or a period of 0 months | Load refused in full | MSG-P3-027 | AC9 |
| X7 | The decision record write fails for an archive | The document stays as it is; picked up by the next run; incident raised (R-UNI-39) | MSG-P7-003 | TC-E1-041-12 (Principle 5) |
| X8 | A role without Reference data C loads retention classes | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-041-11 (Access) |
| X9 | The `rwb-case` contract does not answer within 2 s, or the breaker is open | The document is counted as an exception of the run and is not archived; the next run picks it up; the failure names the case service | MSG-GEN-006 | TC-E1-041-05 (target path) |
| X10 | The Schedule does not fire, or the workflow is stopped mid-run | The run resumes from the last committed chunk of 500 documents; the month key on `retention_action` keeps every decided document from being acted on twice | None | AC8 (target path) |
| X11 | The relay is down when an action commits | The action row, the decision record and the event row are committed; the relay publishes both when it recovers, once, with no duplicate action | None | TC-E1-041-03 (target path) |
| X12 | A store call for the quarantine move or the archive move fails | The item or document keeps its state; the activity retries under the workflow kit's retry policy; an item scanned CLEAN is never stored without its scan result | MSG-GEN-006 | AC1, AC3 (target path) |

Two target-service notes:

- A repeated scan of the same item is refused by the item's own `scan_result` and by the `Idempotency-Key` of `POST /scans` (the pair `storageRef` and `sha256`), so a retried activity writes one result and one audit entry.
- The legacy rerun operation is not a REST operation of this story: a rerun is the same Schedule started for the same run month, and the unique key (`document_id`, `run_month`) on `retention_action` makes the second start act on nothing that was already decided (AC8). The run resource and its read belong to RWB-P5-E1017-APP.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the store (RWB-P5-E1024-APP) and the intake (RWB-P5-E1049-APP); the upload (RWB-P5-E1026-APP) calls this scan; all three are earlier or in-lane work |
| Negotiable | Retention periods and end actions are data of the class version under DL26; the scanning service is reached through a client, a stub and a timeout property |
| Valuable | No infected file reaches a user; every document has a retention rule from day one and no document leaves the store silently |
| Estimable | One scan activity, one Schedule, one workflow with six activities, two tables and one client |
| Small | Fits within one week with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test case in section 16 |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin

  Background:
    Given retention class table version "RET-2026.11" is in force
```

Every Given, When and Then line above is the legacy line unchanged; the target-service part is the three added mock Givens (`rwb-case` for the case and its hold, `rwb-case` for the two lists, `rwb-decision` for the DOCRET record), and the legacy endpoints of the story map to the target operations of 12.1: `MalwareScanService.scanNow` is `POST /scans`, the item scan state is `GET /intake-items/{intakeItemId}/scan-status`, the retention class read is `GET /retention-rules` and `GET /retention-rules/{classCode}`, and the legacy class load is `POST /admin/retention-loads` with `POST /admin/retention-loads/{loadId}/approve`.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every file is scanned for malware before it is stored; an infected file is quarantined and never stored | REQ-DCM-010; FEAT-DCM-18 |
| BR2 | Every document carries a retention class from its type | REQ-DCM-010; NFR-028 |
| BR3 | Retention periods and end actions are data owned by Compliance | Retention classes reference table; DL26 |
| BR4 | A legal hold stops archive and expiry for as long as it is in place | REQ-DCM-016; NFR-072; recovery_case.legal_hold |
| BR5 | No document is removed by the retention run; an end action REVIEW lists it for a recorded decision | NFR-074; REQ-DCM-019 (Epic 2) |
| BR6 | A document with a class missing from the table is listed as an exception | R-WO-48 |
| BR7 | An archive that cannot be written to the decision log does not proceed | Principle 5; R-UNI-39 |
| BR8 | A document is due when its expiry date is on or before the run date | Retention classes reference table; JOB-17 |

Target-service statements that make the rules hold in `rwb-document`:

- BR1 is executed by the scan step running first inside `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` and by the upload calling `POST /scans` before its store call; a CLEAN answer is the only path to a document row, and an INFECTED answer leaves the file in `rwb-quarantine` and the item unread. The engine is behind the scan client, its provider is not named in the sources, and the timeout is the property `rwb.document.scan.timeout-seconds` = 30 carried from the legacy story (ASM-1771).
- BR2 and BR3 read the class of the type from `document_type` and the class row from `retention_rule` in the version in force (`valid_from`, `valid_to`, `rule_version`); the period, the age basis and the end action are never written in code, and the load refuses an invalid row in full (AC9). The list values come from the `rwb-case` reference-data contract (DP-07).
- BR4 is executed by `checkLegalHold` reading `recovery_case.legal_hold` through the case contract on every run, never from a case table and never from a local copy, and by the run counting a held document as HELD in `retention_action` (AC5).
- BR5 is executed by the run never deleting a blob: an end action REVIEW writes a LISTED row and the review-list file, and the disposal or the extension of the document is a later recorded decision (Epic 2).
- BR6 is executed by the exception path of the run: a class that is not in the rule version in force writes an EXCEPTION row with RETENTION_CLASS_MISSING, is listed in the review file and changes nothing.
- BR7 is executed by the decision-record library of DP-03 inside the archive transaction: the record, the `retention_action` row and the event row commit together or not at all (R-UNI-39).
- BR8 is executed by the due selection `expiry_date <= run_date`, computed from `document.created_at` as the stored date and `retention_months` of the class row; AC10 fixes the boundary as an inclusion.
- DP-01 keeps every table in `rwb_document`; DP-07 keeps the four lists in reference data; DP-11 makes the hold one hop with a 2 s timeout; DP-15 puts the two-table migration in the per-service Flyway sequence; DP-18 keeps the ledger with P1; DP-19 puts the two screen reads behind the composite route.

##### 9. State transitions

No case state machine in this story: it changes no case status. It changes the intake item scan result and the document state:

| From | Event | To |
|---|---|---|
| `document_intake.scan_result` (none) | `scanIntakeItem` receives CLEAN | `scan_result` = CLEAN, `scanned_at` set, the OCR step may read the item |
| `document_intake.scan_result` (none) | `scanIntakeItem` receives INFECTED | `scan_result` = INFECTED, the file is in `rwb-quarantine`, no document row exists |
| `document_intake.scan_result` (none) | the scanning service does not answer | unchanged; retried by the next intake run; alert after two failed runs |
| `document.state` = STORED | the run archives with end action ARCHIVE and the DOCRET record commits | ARCHIVED, the blob is in the archive tier |
| `document.state` = STORED | the run meets end action REVIEW | unchanged; `retention_action.action` = LISTED |
| `document.state` = STORED | the run meets `legal_hold` true | unchanged; `retention_action.action` = HELD |
| `document.state` = STORED | the class is not in force | unchanged; `retention_action.action` = EXCEPTION |

A document that is out on custody is not moved to the archive tier while a custody row with a `due_back` date is open; it is counted as an exception of the run and its review-list row names the location and the due-back date (DF-DOC-021, DF-DOC-024, read only; no custody row is written by this story).

| Who | What they may do in this story |

| SY-OCR, OCR and extraction pipeline | Runs the scan step (Documents CRU) |
| RW-COMPLY, compliance and PDPA officer | Owns the retention classes; reads the review list and the run counts |
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | Loads the retention class table (Reference data C) |
| Approver with Reference data A | Approves the load; no role holds Reference data A in the permission matrix today; assumed granted to the compliance and PDPA officer as table owner (DL01; ASM-1770) |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Receives scan alerts; reruns the intake and the retention run |
| SY-DECLOG, decision record writer | Writes the DOCRET record |
| SY-DOCUMENT, the rwb-document service identity | Runs the Schedule, the activities, the quarantine move and the archive move |

The authorisation decision is taken by `rwb-access` (roles as data, scope, masking and DoA in `rwb_access`) and consumed as the cached permission decision the service holds; this story adds no guard of its own and inherits the 403 shape with MSG-P4-002. The database login is per service (DP-02) and its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0995; ASM-1772).

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary and the TSD P5 T3.1 table. Two scan columns on `document` are added by the migration of this story because the sources hold the two attributes on `document_intake` only and an upload creates no intake item; the addition is design and is recorded with the class-load and scan-surface gap (GAP-0995; ASM-1771).
