##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

| Operation | Path | Owner | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/document/v1/scans` | P5 | Scans one file and answers `ScanResult` synchronously: `storageRef`, `sha256`, `intakeId` (optional), `source`; 200 with CLEAN or INFECTED, 503 MSG-P5-022 when the engine does not answer. `Idempotency-Key` required; internal operation, service identity only |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/scan-status` | P5 | `ScanStatus` of a stored document: scanResult, scannedAt, threatFound, quarantineRef |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/scan-status` | P5 | `ScanStatus` of an intake item, read from `document_intake` (DF-DOC-058, DF-DOC-059) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/retention-rules` | P5 | Query ruleVersion, docTypeCode, productCode, page, size; answers `RetentionRulePage` in the version in force |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/retention-rules/{classCode}` | P5 | Answers `RetentionRule` in the version in force; 404 when the class is not in force |
| POST | `/api/recovery/document/v1/admin/retention-loads` | P5 | The class load: multipart file and `validFrom`, table RETENTION_CLASS; 201 `RetentionLoad`. Reference data right C; `Idempotency-Key` required (table code and table version) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/document/v1/admin/retention-loads/{loadId}/approve` | P5 | Approves a loaded version; Reference data right A; 200 `RetentionLoad`; 409 when the version is already loaded or already in force |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/admin/retention-loads/{loadId}` | P5 | `RetentionLoad` with the accepted and refused rows and their reasons |

The paths and the field names of the eight operations are fixed by RWB-P5-E1041-CON, because no source names them (GAP-0995; ASM-1769). The class list used by the SCR-31 and SCR-32 panels is declared by RWB-P5-AD021-CON on the same base and is a projection of the same `retention_rule` rows; this story does not re-declare it. The run resource and its read belong to RWB-P5-E1017-APP. Errors follow RFC 9457 with `messageId`.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Path | Owner | Story | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 | RWB-P3-E1018-CON | The case and its `legal_hold`, one hop, 2 s timeout, breaker per downstream (DP-11); consumed and faked although the plan lists it in no C row (ASM-1769) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 | RWB-P3-E1043-CON | LOV-RETENTION, LOV-SCAN-RESULT, LOV-RETENTION-ACTION and LOV-RETENTION-END in the version in force (DP-07) |

The two lists and the hold are read through the client libraries of DP-07 and DP-11, which wrap the two contracts. No interaction-ledger operation is consumed: the ledger is `rwb-source-data`'s and this story writes no ledger row (DP-18). The blobs are moved through the store RWB-P5-E1024-APP, which is a same-service H dependency and not a REST contract of another service; the file move appears in 12.9 as File.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Key | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.document.RetentionApplied.v1` | `rwb.document.events.v1` | P5 | caseId | documentId, caseId, runMonth, action, retentionClass, ruleVersion, expiredAt, decisionLogRef |
| decision record | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | PLT library, consumed by P7 | caseId | the hash-chained record with decision code DOCRET and final call ARCHIVED, LISTED, HELD or EXCEPTION |

CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, binary mode; no personal data in either payload, and no file byte, no document name and no customer value. The event row is written inside the transaction of the `retention_action` row and the decision record, so it exists exactly when the action exists; the envelope, the outbox and the relay are the platform library's, and the schema is fixed by RWB-P5-E1041-CON. `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` and `rwb.document.DocumentFieldsExtracted.v1` are the service's other two events and belong to other stories; the retention event is added by this key and recorded in the Kafka Topic and Event Catalog (GAP-0995; ASM-1774).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. This story consumes no Kafka event: the intake Schedule starts the workflow, the case hold and the two lists are synchronous reads, and the storage moves are same-service calls.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Kind | Queue | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` | Workflow, from the L3 workflow kit template "Document intake" | `rwb-document` | Owned by RWB-P5-E1049-APP; the scan step runs first, before the OCR step |
| `scanIntakeItem` | Activity, contributed by this story | `rwb-document` | Scans one intake item, moves an infected file to `rwb-quarantine`, writes `scan_result` and `scanned_at`, writes the `MALWARE_BLOCKED` audit entry and the two-failure alert counter |
| `RetentionWorkflow` | Workflow, from the L3 workflow kit template "Scheduled job" | `rwb-document` | Owned by this story: the monthly retention run (legacy JOB-17), started by the `retention-monthly` Schedule |
| `selectDueDocuments` | Activity | `rwb-document` | Selects the active documents whose expiry date is on or before the run date, in chunks of 500 |
| `checkLegalHold` | Activity | `rwb-document` | Reads `legal_hold` through the `rwb-case` contract and marks the held documents HELD |
| `archiveDocument` | Activity | `rwb-document` | Writes the DOCRET record, calls the store to move the blob to the archive tier, sets state ARCHIVED, writes the retention_action row and the event row |
| `listForReview` | Activity | `rwb-document` | Writes a LISTED or EXCEPTION row and changes no document |
| `writeReviewList` | Activity | `rwb-document` | Writes `retention/review/{runDate}.csv` through the store and the run counts to the run record |

The workflow kit fixes the retry policy, the continue-as-new boundary and the Schedule registration (DP-10, H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON); this story contributes the template configuration and the activities, not a scheduler.

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Schedule | Job | Owner | Detail |

| `retention-monthly` | JOB-17 Retention | P5, this story | Temporal Schedule on queue `rwb-document`: monthly on the first Sunday at 02:30 Asia/Bangkok, starting `RetentionWorkflow` with the run month as its input; the run month is the idempotency key of the run |
| document intake, every 15 minutes in business hours | JOB-12 Document intake | RWB-P5-E1049-APP | Named because the scan step rides inside it; this story registers no Schedule for it and only contributes the `scanIntakeItem` activity the started workflow calls |

Both legacy schedules become Temporal Schedules of the workflow kit (DP-10); no Quartz row and no shared job table survives. The rerun of a month is a second start of the same Schedule with the same run month, and the unique key (`document_id`, `run_month`) on `retention_action` makes it act on nothing already decided.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document`, modules `document/retention` and `document/scan`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| RetentionAdminController | Controller | The three class-load operations and the two rule reads of 12.1; Reference data rights C and A; refuses an invalid load in full |
| ScanController | Controller | `POST /scans` and the two scan-status reads; maps the engine answer, the timeout and the alert counter |
| ScanClient | Client | Calls the bank scanning service; maps CLEAN, INFECTED and the timeout to the answers of 14; the provider is a property, not a constant |
| ScanActivity | Temporal activity | `scanIntakeItem`: the scan, the quarantine move, the two intake columns, the audit entry |
| RetentionWorkflowImpl | Temporal workflow | `RetentionWorkflow` on queue `rwb-document`, from the workflow kit's "Scheduled job" template |
| RetentionActivities | Temporal activities | `selectDueDocuments`, `checkLegalHold`, `archiveDocument`, `listForReview`, `writeReviewList` |
| RetentionRuleLoader | Service | The class load of table RETENTION_CLASS: row checks, version uniqueness, approve and its separation of duty |
| RetentionRuleRepository | Repository | Reads and writes `retention_rule` only, in the version in force by `valid_from` and `valid_to` |
| RetentionActionRepository | Repository | Writes `retention_action` only; the unique (`document_id`, `run_month`) key is the run's idempotency |
| RetentionReviewWriter | Service | Builds `retention/review/{runDate}.csv` and the run counts |
| RetentionStatePanel | React component | Reads the scan and retention states through the gateway-bff composite route for SCR-44 and SCR-47 |

**Database.**

- One migration in the per-service Flyway sequence (DP-15): `V1041_1__retention_and_scan.sql` creates `retention_rule` (id, product_code varchar(25), table_name varchar(60), record_class varchar(20), retention_months integer, age_basis_field varchar(60), end_action varchar(12), rule_version varchar(20), valid_from date, valid_to date, approved_by uuid, load_id uuid, standard columns) with unique (`table_name`, `record_class`, `rule_version`), check `retention_months between 1 and 600` and check `end_action in ('ARCHIVE','REVIEW')`.
- The same migration creates `retention_action` (id, document_id, run_month char(7), action varchar(12), retention_class varchar(10), rule_version varchar(20), decided_entry_id uuid, standard columns) with unique (`document_id`, `run_month`) and adds `document.scan_result` varchar(10) null and `document.scanned_at` timestamptz null.
- Indexes: `ix_document_retention ON document (retention_class, created_at) WHERE is_active`; `ix_retention_action_run_month ON retention_action (run_month)`; `ix_document_scan_result ON document (scan_result)`.

**Configuration and reference data.**

- Retention classes RET-2026.11, loaded through the class load and approved, owned by Compliance (DL26; the periods are not set by any source and the legacy values are carried as the Compliance default, ASM-1770).
- Properties `rwb.document.container.quarantine` and `rwb.document.scan.timeout-seconds` = 30.
- Decision code DOCRET, assumed; the LOV-DECISION list is loaded by the data steward.
- Feature flags `rwb.document.malware-scan` and `rwb.document.retention`. With the scan flag off, intake items stay unscanned and are not read, and uploads are refused with 503 and MSG-P5-022. With the retention flag off, the run lists due documents and archives none.

**Build steps**

1. Write the migration and the entities; test the two check constraints, the unique version key and the unique run key.
2. Build the scan client against a stub that flags the EICAR signature; test AC1, the timeout and the upload call.
3. Build `scanIntakeItem` with the quarantine move, the audit entry and the two-failure alert; test AC6.
4. Build the class loader with validation and the approve step; test AC9 and the separation of duty.
5. Build the rule reads and the class-in-force rule; unit test the boundary of a valid-from and valid-to date.
6. Build the run selection, the expiry computation and the hold check; unit test AC5, AC7 and AC10 on fixed dates.
7. Add archive with the DOCRET record, the review list and the event row; integration test AC3, AC4 and AC8.
8. Test the access refusal (TC-E1-041-11) and the failed decision record (TC-E1-041-12).
9. Register the `retention-monthly` Schedule through the workflow kit and test one start, one restart and one rerun of the same month.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-18 | Interaction ledger | Ledger owned by rwb-source-data (default ruling) | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-01 moves the two legacy retention tables into `rwb_document` and stops every cross-module read: the hold is no longer read from a case table but from the `rwb-case` contract, which is DP-11 and the C dependency of the legacy story. DP-03 replaces the in-process decision-log writer with the local library, so the DOCRET record, the action row and the event row share one transaction and the record is published on the shared topic. DP-07 keeps the four lists out of the code while the class rows stay in this service's own `retention_rule`, which the Ownership Map gives to P5. DP-10 replaces the Quartz schedule of JOB-17 and the job-step trigger of the scan with a Schedule, a workflow and activities of the workflow kit. DP-13 gives the service its own base. DP-15 puts the two-table migration in the service's own sequence. DP-18 keeps the interaction ledger with `rwb-source-data`: the legacy audit write is an audit entry here and the legacy interaction-ledger position is a call to the P1 owner, never a local table and never a local row. DP-19 puts the two screen reads behind the gateway-bff composite route. The platform event library is not DP-09 in this story: the envelope and the relay are the library's and the schema is RWB-P5-E1041-CON's, so this story only writes the event row inside the DP-03 transaction.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the boundary test on `rwb_document` passes, the EICAR file is quarantined in SIT on every intake path, one run of `retention-monthly` archives and lists the expected documents and writes `retention/review/{runDate}.csv`, and `rwb.document.RetentionApplied.v1` is on the topic once per action with no personal data.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P5-016 | Malware found | This file was not stored because the malware scan found a threat. It is held in quarantine. |
| MSG-P3-027 | Retention class load fails a check | The {table} load was refused: {error} at row {row}. The version in force is unchanged. |
| MSG-P5-022 | Scanning service unavailable on upload | The malware scan is not available, so the file was not stored. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Decision record write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The case contract or a store call does not answer | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |

The HTTP mapping is fixed by RWB-P5-E1041-CON: 422 for MSG-P5-016, 422 and 409 for MSG-P3-027, 503 for MSG-P5-022, MSG-P7-003 and MSG-GEN-006, 403 for MSG-P4-002. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

Delivery shape: every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set to the ID above, `detail` carrying the text with its placeholders filled, and `instance` naming the request. For MSG-P3-027 the {table} value is RETENTION_CLASS, {error} names the failing check and {row} the row number. For MSG-GEN-006 the {system} value is "Case service" for a case-contract timeout and "Document storage" for a store call.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen of its own in this story. The compliance and PDPA officer reads the review-list file and the run counts; SCR-47 Personal data, which shows retention classes, comes in Epic 8. The platform administrator sees the scan alerts and the run results on SCR-44 Interface and job monitor through the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19 (RWB-PLT-N001-CON):

| State | What the user sees |
|---|---|
| Running | The run of the month in progress with the counts so far |
| Failed | The run stopped with MSG-GEN-006 or MSG-P7-003 and the document that stopped it |
| Complete | The counts of due, archived, listed, held and exceptions, and the review-list file of the month |
| Scan alert | The `MALWARE_BLOCKED` alert of a branch or mailroom item, with the intake ID and the source and no file name |

An uploader sees MSG-P5-016 or MSG-P5-022 in the upload dialog of SCR-30, which belongs to RWB-P5-E1026-APP; this story fixes the two answers, not the dialog.

| TC ID | Covers | Level | Data |
|---|---|---|---|

The legacy level System maps to End to end, Access to Component and Resilience to NFR. No integration harness story exists for this key, so no test case is copied with the `-ITG` suffix; the cross-service proof of the hold and the two lists sits in the wave-1 harness of RWB-E1-049 and in the contract tests of RWB-P5-E1041-CON. The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the periods, the end actions, the rule version, the four lists, the scan timeout and the container names are data rows, list values or properties.
- No personal data in the event, the workflow input, the decision record, the audit entry or the log: the `MALWARE_BLOCKED` entry carries the intake ID and the source only, never a file name and never a customer value; `document_custody.held_by` is never read; the review-list file carries IDs, classes and dates only; test files are synthetic.
- No read of another service's tables (DP-01). The hold is read through the `rwb-case` contract, one hop, 2 s timeout, with a mock and a breaker.
- No ledger row (DP-18): the interaction ledger is `rwb-source-data`'s and is reached only through the P1 contract if a ledger entry is ever required.
- The scanning engine's own state, capacity and queue are never stored or queried: the result, the time and the quarantine reference are the only three values this service keeps.
- No document is deleted and no blob is overwritten: the run changes a state and moves a blob to the archive tier; a write-once blob is never touched.
- The run is idempotent twice over: the unique (`document_id`, `run_month`) key, and the run month as the Schedule input.
- The decision record is written in the same transaction as the action row and the event row; a failure archives nothing (R-UNI-39).
- The feature flags `rwb.document.malware-scan` and `rwb.document.retention` remove either capability without a rollback of the schema.

- The document store, its containers and the storage product (RWB-P5-E1024-APP), and the OCR, classification and extraction steps after the scan (RWB-P5-E1049-APP, RWB-P5-E1050-APP, RWB-P5-E1053-APP).
- The scanning engine itself, its licences, its capacity and its own console: only the result, the time and the quarantine reference are this service's.
- Retention of the decision record and of the interaction ledger (RWB-E1-014, RWB-E2-034; the ledger is P1's, DP-18).
- The published contract documents of this service, their fakes and their versioning, and the Helm chart, the retry policy values, the topic and DLT provisioning, the metrics, the alerts and the runbook: the contract is RWB-P5-E1041-CON.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the contract baseline of the retention and virus-scan API of `rwb-document` is split out of legacy RWB-E1-041 and published on base `/api/recovery/document/v1` with the topic `rwb.document.events.v1`, the class load, the rule and scan reads, the event schema and the fakes. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the retention and virus-scan API of `rwb-document` — the retention rule read and the class load and approve operations, the scan request and the two scan-status reads on base `/api/recovery/document/v1`, the `RetentionRule`, `RetentionLoad`, `RetentionAction` and `ScanStatus` shapes, the retention classes as reference data, the error envelope with every message ID and its HTTP status, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the `rwb.document.RetentionApplied.v1` event schema with no personal data, and the fakes with their drift test**, so that **the app story of this legacy key, the upload path that scans before it stores, the intake pipeline, the screens SCR-44 and SCR-47 and the wave-1 harness build against a fixed, testable contract on Day 1, and a class code, a period, an end action, a scan value or an event field can never drift between the service that writes it and the callers that read it without a failing build**.

The service is `rwb-document` (P5): schema `rwb_document`, REST base `/api/recovery/document/v1`, topic `rwb.document.events.v1` with event names `rwb.document.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document`. The legacy key is RWB-E1-041 and its ten acceptance criteria belong to `RWB-P5-E1041-APP`; this story owns no legacy criterion and writes eight new ones that test the artefact only.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). In the monolith the retention class of a type, the period and the end action of a class, the scan result of a file and the record of what the monthly job did were values passed in process between the store, the upload, the intake and the job, and the retention class table was loaded through a reference-data surface that no document contract described. Under the target architecture the store, the upload and the intake are three stories of the same service and a period, a scan value or an event field that changes without its consumers is a silent break. The shapes most likely to drift silently are exactly these:

- a class code or an end action renamed in the class load, so the run archives what Compliance meant to review;
- a period read differently by the load and the run, so the same class expires on two dates;
- a scan answer that says 200 with an empty body instead of CLEAN or INFECTED, so an uploader cannot tell "safe" from "not scanned";
- an `Idempotency-Key` honoured by the scan but not by the class load, so a repeated load creates a second version in force;
- an event payload that carries a customer value or a document name, so the retention decision leaks personal data to every consumer;
- an error returned with the wrong status or without a `messageId`, so a caller cannot tell a refused load from a missing class.

The baseline fixes the names the checks require and records what the sources leave open: no source names the paths or the field sets of the class load, the rule read or the scan operation (GAP-0996; ASM-1776); the legacy class table code RETENTION_CLASS and its columns are not the `retention_rule` shape the Ownership Map gives to P5 (GAP-0996; ASM-1778); the event `rwb.document.RetentionApplied.v1` is new, because the service catalogue names only two events (GAP-0996; ASM-1777); and the plan gives this story an empty Contract dependencies list while two P3 reads are consumed (GAP-0996; ASM-1776). Nothing else is guessed and no business value is fixed.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the base, the topic, the event and the queue names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- The platform error envelope, the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, the `Idempotency-Key` rule and the retry and `.dlt` topic convention are the platform baseline (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON); where this document narrows them it does so explicitly.
- TSD P5 T3.1 and T3.2 are in force for `retention_rule` (DF-REF-116 to DF-REF-127), `retention_action` (DF-DOC-091 to DF-DOC-095), the scan fields of `document_intake` (DF-DOC-058, DF-DOC-059) and the lists LOV-RETENTION, LOV-SCAN-RESULT (CLEAN, INFECTED), LOV-RETENTION-ACTION (ARCHIVED, LISTED, HELD, EXCEPTION) and LOV-RETENTION-END (ARCHIVE, REVIEW).
- The Ownership Map is the only source of owners: `retention_rule`, `retention_action`, `document`, `document_intake` and `document_type` are P5's in `rwb_document`; `recovery_case`, `lov_value` and `reference_row` are P3's; `decision_log_entry` is P7's; `interaction` is P1's.
- The `rwb-case` case contract and reference-data contract are published with their fakes, so the two consumed rows of 12.2 have one owner document each.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

The status and the release are the run defaults of D-RCV-60: the story is Draft (realignment v1) and the release is 30 November 2026 (tentative), with no approval recorded in the sources read (ASM-1775).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 document `openapi/rwb-document-retention-v1.yaml` with the eight operations of 12.1, the five resources of section 11 and the error responses of section 14, on the single base `/api/recovery/document/v1`.
2. Fix the `RetentionRule` shape and the class-in-force rule: one row per `record_class` in a `rule_version`, exactly one version in force on a business date, and a class that is not in force refused with 422 rather than answered with an invented class.
3. Fix the class load: the multipart request with `validFrom` and the table code RETENTION_CLASS, the `RetentionLoad` answer with the accepted and refused rows, the two rights (C to load, A to approve), the row checks of the legacy story and the whole-load refusal.
4. Fix the scan resource: the synchronous `POST /scans` request and its `ScanResult` answer, the declared budget, the 503 of an unavailable engine, and the two `ScanStatus` reads that answer a stored document and an intake item.
5. Fix `RetentionAction` and the action values, with the decision-record reference of a decided action and the empty-page rule.
6. Fix the `rwb.document.RetentionApplied.v1` schema: the topic, the key, the nine payload fields, the CloudEvents envelope, the no-personal-data rule and the count of the service's events.
7. Map every failure to the error envelope and a message ID, status by status, and record the two consumed P3 rows with their owner, their use, the 2 s budget and the missing C entries.
8. Record the `Idempotency-Key` rule on the three POSTs and the natural keys behind it, then publish the six fakes, the contract tests and the drift test, tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-P5-E1041-APP, RWB-P5-E1026-CON, RWB-P5-E1049-APP and the wave-1 harness.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A response body fails schema validation | The build fails on the schema lint; a deployed service answers 500 with the error envelope | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1, AC2 |
| X2 | A property is renamed, removed or retyped within major version 1 | The contract test fails; the change needs a corrected document or a new major version | None | AC2, AC3 |
| X3 | The scan answer is a 200 with an empty or partial body | The contract test fails: `scanResult` is required and is CLEAN or INFECTED, never absent | MSG-GEN-001 | AC3, AC6 |
| X4 | The class load accepts a row it should refuse, or refuses one it should accept | The contract test fails on the row checks of AC4; the version in force is unchanged | MSG-P3-027 | AC4 |
| X5 | The event carries a personal value, a document name, a file byte or a tenth field | The AsyncAPI schema test and the no-personal-data test fail | None | AC5 |
| X6 | An operation returns a status or a `messageId` outside the mapping of AC6 | The contract test fails; the document states one status per condition | None | AC6 |
| X7 | A class load or a scan repeats a request with the same key and creates a second version or a second result | The contract test fails on the stored-answer rule of AC7 | MSG-GEN-004 | AC7 |
| X8 | A fake drifts from the document, or a scan event is declared besides the retention event | The drift test and the absence test fail the build | None | AC8 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Criterion | Verdict | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Independent | Pass | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, TSD P5 T3, the Ownership Map and the two `rwb-case` contracts only |
| Negotiable | Pass | The field-level names are settled with the consumers; the base, the eight operations, the two natural keys, the event schema and the error mapping are fixed by the target architecture and the legacy section 12 |
| Valuable | Pass | Unblocks the app story, the upload path, the intake pipeline and the harness on Day 1 |
| Estimable | Pass | One document, five resources, eight operations, two consumed rows, nine contract tables and six fakes |
| Small | Pass | Fits one sprint with its contract tests |
| Testable | Pass | Every criterion in section 7 is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

The eight criteria are new for the contract baseline and test the artefact only; they restate no business outcome owned by `RWB-P5-E1041-APP`, whose AC1 to AC10 are the legacy criteria of RWB-E1-041. No criterion fixes a business value beyond the legacy examples: the class codes, the periods, the rule version, the run month and the decision code are fixtures and data rows, not constants of the contract.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One REST base per service: `/api/recovery/document/v1` on every declared operation | DP-13; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR2 | One topic per service: `rwb.document.events.v1`, with the retry and `.dlt` topics of the platform convention | DP-09; Architecture v5 slides 16 and 42 |
| BR3 | A change inside major version 1 is additive; a removed, renamed or retyped property and a narrowed required set are a new major version | Architecture v5 slide 42 notes (BACKWARD compatibility) |
| BR4 | The document declares only tables of `rwb_document` and only operations owned by `rwb-document`; a consumed operation is described as consumed and faked, never as provided | Ownership Map; DP-01 |
| BR5 | The class of a type is answered only from the rule version in force on the business date, and a class not in force is refused, never invented | NFR-028; FSD P5 AC-EXC-P5-017-02; DL26 |
| BR6 | The scan answer is CLEAN or INFECTED and nothing else; an unavailable engine is a refusal and never a safe answer | REQ-DCM-010; FEAT-DCM-18; legacy section 5 X2 |
| BR7 | No business value is fixed in the contract: the class codes, the periods, the age bases, the end actions, the rule version, the run month, the scan timeout and the decision code stay data rows, parameters or properties | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17; RWB-E1-041 section 17 |
| BR8 | No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: identifiers, codes, versions, dates and counts only, and no customer name, national identifier, document name or custody holder | PDPA minimisation; RWB-E1-041 section 17 |
| BR9 | The interaction ledger is `rwb-source-data`'s: the contract declares no ledger row, no ledger read and no ledger table, and the audit entry of a blocked file stays an audit entry | DP-18; default ruling of R-PREC |
| BR10 | Every consumed row states one hop, a 2 s timeout, a GET retry once with jitter and a breaker per downstream, and a failed read maps to MSG-GEN-006 naming the system that failed | DP-11, ADR-020; Architecture v5 slide 11 |
| BR11 | A POST requires `Idempotency-Key` and stores its answer, and its natural key makes the second answer the same as the first; a GET declares none | Architecture v5 slide 11 |
| BR12 | This key publishes one event, `rwb.document.RetentionApplied.v1`, and declares no scan event: the scan result is an attribute of the document and of the intake item | TSD P5 T5.3; WP B-P5-01; ASM-1777 |

##### 9. State transitions

| Baseline state | Event | Condition | Next state |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The eight operations, the five resources and the two consumed rows are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | RWB-P5-E1041-APP, RWB-P5-E1026-CON, RWB-P5-E1049-APP and the wave-1 harness accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A property is added within major version 1, for example an optional label on `RetentionRule` | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A property is removed, renamed or retyped, a status changes or the event payload gains a field | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake, or a retired element returns | A contract test fails | In review |

This baseline declares no document state machine and no case state machine. The four values it does fix as answers, not as transitions:

| Field value in the baseline | Meaning declared by this document |
|---|---|
| `scanResult` = "CLEAN" | The file may be stored; the value is written by the scan activity, never by a caller |
| `scanResult` = "INFECTED" | The file is in quarantine and no document row exists; a caller never overrides it |
| `status` = "APPROVED" | The rows of a load are the rule version in force from their `validFrom`; the earlier rows stay readable |
| `action` = "LISTED" | The run listed a due document for a recorded decision and changed nothing else |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Tech lead of `rwb-document` | Owns the OpenAPI document, the AsyncAPI fragment and the six fakes; tags the baseline |
| Solution architect | Approves a breaking change, a new major version, the naming of the new retention event and the correction of the plan's Contract dependencies list for the two P3 reads |
| Consuming teams (RWB-P5-E1041-APP, RWB-P5-E1026-CON, RWB-P5-E1049-APP, the SCR-44 and SCR-47 route, the wave-1 harness) | Review and sign off the parts they consume |
| RW-COMPLY, Compliance and PDPA officer | Confirms that the class, the period and the end action answer is the retention authority the legacy story gives the role, and that the load needs the second right |
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | Confirms the load template of table RETENTION_CLASS and the row checks that refuse a load in full |
| P3 owner (`rwb-case`) | Confirms the case, the hold and the reference-list rows: the owner of `recovery_case`, `lov_value` and `reference_row` |
| Platform library owner | Owns the CloudEvents envelope, the error envelope, the `Idempotency-Key` rule and the naming rule this document reuses |
| Data steward | Confirms that no personal value is declared in an answer, an example or a fake |

The per-service login behind the document's security scheme is not part of this baseline: the document names the scheme "the rwb-document login (DP-02)" and the name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0996; ASM-1776). The declared area and right of each operation are enforced at gateway-bff (DP-19); no `rwb-access` contract is declared here.

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| RetentionRule | classCode, docTypeCode, productCode, tableName, retentionMonths, ageBasisField, endAction, ruleVersion, validFrom, validTo, approvedByRole; from `retention_rule` DF-REF-116 to DF-REF-127 and `document_type` DF-REF-223 |
| RetentionRulePage | The page items as `RetentionRule` with page, size and total; the page field names are the platform convention, and the legacy source fixes none (GAP-0996; ASM-1776) |
| RetentionLoad | loadId, table, ruleVersion, validFrom, rowCount, acceptedCount, refusedCount, refusedRows (row, error), status (LOADED, APPROVED, REFUSED) |
| RetentionAction | documentId, runMonth, action, retentionClass, ruleVersion, decisionLogId, decidedAt; from `retention_action` DF-DOC-091 to DF-DOC-095 and the standard columns |
| ScanRequest | storageRef (required), sha256 (required), intakeId (optional), source (optional); no file name, no file byte |
| ScanResult | scanResult (CLEAN or INFECTED, required), scannedAt, threatFound, quarantineRef |
| ScanStatus | documentId or intakeItemId, scanResult, scannedAt, threatFound, quarantineRef; from `document_intake` DF-DOC-058 and DF-DOC-059 and the two scan columns of `document` |
| RetentionApplied | documentId, caseId, runMonth, action, retentionClass, ruleVersion, expiredAt, decisionLogRef; the CloudEvents envelope carries the rest |
| DecisionRecord | decisionCode, finalCall, inputsRef, decidedAt and the chain fields of the library; decision code DOCRET, final call ARCHIVED, LISTED, HELD or EXCEPTION |
| Error envelope | RFC 9457 problem details with `messageId`, `detail`, `instance` and the status of section 14 |
| List values | LOV-RETENTION, LOV-SCAN-RESULT (CLEAN, INFECTED), LOV-RETENTION-ACTION (ARCHIVED, LISTED, HELD, EXCEPTION) and LOV-RETENTION-END (ARCHIVE, REVIEW), read through the `rwb-case` reference-data contract and never copied |

Every example in the document is synthetic and uses the legacy values: class "LEGAL10Y" at 120 months with end action "REVIEW", class "GENERAL05Y" at 60 months with end action "ARCHIVE", rule version "RET-2026.11", run month "2026-12", the stored date 1 November 2021, the expiry date 1 November 2026, the run date 2026-12-06 and the decision code "DOCRET". No example carries a real customer value and none carries a document name. The set of LOV-RETENTION values is not enumerated in the source documents; the two class codes above are the ones the legacy criteria use, and the periods are the legacy fixtures under DL26 (GAP-0996; ASM-1778).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner `rwb-document` (P5); base `/api/recovery/document/v1`.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/retention-rules` | Query ruleVersion, docTypeCode, productCode, page, size; answer `RetentionRulePage` | Documents R | Not applicable |
| GET | `/retention-rules/{classCode}` | Answer `RetentionRule` in the rule version in force; 404 when the class is not in force | Documents R | Not applicable |
| POST | `/admin/retention-loads` | multipart file and `validFrom`, table RETENTION_CLASS; 201 `RetentionLoad` | Reference data C | `Idempotency-Key` header, keyed by table and ruleVersion |
| POST | `/admin/retention-loads/{loadId}/approve` | 200 `RetentionLoad` with status APPROVED; 409 when already approved or in force | Reference data A | `Idempotency-Key` header, keyed by loadId |
| GET | `/admin/retention-loads/{loadId}` | Answer `RetentionLoad` with the accepted and refused rows and their reasons | Reference data R | Not applicable |
| POST | `/scans` | Request `ScanRequest`; answer `ScanResult` with CLEAN or INFECTED; 503 when the engine does not answer | Documents C, service identity for the intake and the upload | `Idempotency-Key` header, keyed by storageRef and sha256 |
| GET | `/documents/{documentId}/scan-status` | Answer `ScanStatus` of a stored document | Documents R | Not applicable |
| GET | `/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/scan-status` | Answer `ScanStatus` of an intake item | Documents R | Not applicable |

The eight paths and their field names are this baseline's design: no source names them (GAP-0996; ASM-1776). The class panel reads of SCR-31 and SCR-32 are declared by RWB-P5-AD021-CON on the same base as a projection of the same `retention_rule` rows, so exactly one baseline owns each path; the run resource, its read and the rerun are RWB-P5-E1017-APP's and are named nowhere here. Error statuses are those of section 14.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 `rwb-case` | The case and `legal_hold` (DF-CAS-020), faked (RWB-P3-E1018-CON); the plan lists no C row for it (ASM-1776) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 `rwb-case` | LOV-RETENTION, LOV-SCAN-RESULT, LOV-RETENTION-ACTION and LOV-RETENTION-END at the version in force, faked (RWB-P3-E1043-CON) |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retry once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (DP-11, ADR-020). A failed read maps to 503 with MSG-GEN-006 naming the system that failed and never to an accepted class or a safe scan answer. No P1 ledger operation is consumed: the ledger is `rwb-source-data`'s and this contract declares no ledger row (DP-18).

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Declared schema |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.document.RetentionApplied.v1` | `rwb.document.events.v1` | P5 `rwb-document` | Key caseId; payload documentId, caseId, runMonth, action, retentionClass, ruleVersion, expiredAt, decisionLogRef; CloudEvents 1.0 binary mode; no personal data, no document name, no file byte |
| decision record | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | PLT library, consumed by P7 | The hash-chained record with decision code DOCRET and final call ARCHIVED, LISTED, HELD or EXCEPTION, with `inputsRef` naming the class row and the run |

This baseline declares the event schema and the record declaration because the service owns the topic; the row itself is written by the run of RWB-P5-E1041-APP in its own transaction, and this key publishes nothing at run time. The event is new: the service catalogue names `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` and `rwb.document.DocumentFieldsExtracted.v1` only, and this baseline adds the third event of the service and records it in the Kafka Topic and Event Catalog (GAP-0996; ASM-1777). No scan event is declared: the scan result is an attribute of the document and of the intake item, and the `MALWARE_BLOCKED` audit entry is an audit-log entry.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The retention and scan paths subscribe to no topic: the hold and the four lists are synchronous reads and the trigger is the Schedule or the HTTP request. A hold placed a minute ago is visible on the next run.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Kind | Queue | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `RetentionWorkflow` | Workflow contract, from the L3 workflow kit template "Scheduled job" | `rwb-document` | One typed workflow with the run month in and the run counts out, started by the `retention-monthly` Schedule; owned by RWB-P5-E1041-APP |
| `scanIntakeItem` | Activity contract | `rwb-document` | One typed activity with the intake item ID in and `ScanStatus` out, idempotent by the item and its scan result; contributed to `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` of RWB-P5-E1049-APP |

This baseline declares the two contracts and the queue, not their implementation: the workflow body, the six activities of the run and the retry values are RWB-P5-E1041-APP's, and the intake workflow is RWB-P5-E1049-APP's.

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Schedule | Job | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `retention-monthly` | JOB-17 Retention | RWB-P5-E1041-APP | Temporal Schedule on queue `rwb-document`, monthly on the first Sunday at 02:30 Asia/Bangkok, with the run month as its input; the baseline fixes the Schedule name, the queue and the input, not the cron of an environment |
| document intake, every 15 minutes in business hours | JOB-12 Document intake | RWB-P5-E1049-APP | Named because the scan answer exists only after this Schedule runs; this baseline creates no Schedule for it |

No Quartz row and no shared job table survives either Schedule (DP-10); both are Schedules of the workflow kit, and this baseline registers neither.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| `retention_rule` | P5 (`rwb_document`) | The class rows behind `RetentionRule` and the class load: record class, period, age basis, end action, rule version, validity, approver |
| `retention_action` | P5 (`rwb_document`) | The action of a month behind `RetentionAction`, with the decision-record reference |
| `document` | P5 (`rwb_document`) | The class, the stored date and the two scan attributes the `ScanStatus` read answers |
| `document_intake` | P5 (`rwb_document`) | `scan_result` (DF-DOC-058) and `scanned_at` (DF-DOC-059) behind `ScanStatus` |
| `document_type` | P5 (`rwb_document`) | The class of a type, read to resolve the rule of a document |
| decision-record library table | PLT library, created in `rwb_document` | The DOCRET record the run writes |
| outbox and idempotency library tables | PLT library, created in `rwb_document` | The RetentionApplied row and the idempotency rows of the three POSTs |

`recovery_case`, `lov_value` and `reference_row` are P3's, `decision_log_entry` is P7's and `interaction` is P1's; they are named only as consumed answers and never declared as this service's tables (DP-01, DP-18). No ACE view is read.

A drifted fake fails the drift test of AC8. The exact response field names of the page metadata of `RetentionRulePage` and of the refused rows of `RetentionLoad` beyond what section 11 names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0996; ASM-1776).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 8 provided, 2 consumed | The two rule reads, the three class-load operations, the scan request and the two scan-status reads; the case read and the list read of P3; one hop and 2 s on every consumed call, and the declared 30 s budget of the scan |
| Kafka | 1 event schema and 1 record declared, 0 consumed | `rwb.document.RetentionApplied.v1` on `rwb.document.events.v1` and the record on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; no scan event |
| Temporal | 1 workflow contract, 1 activity contract, 1 Schedule named | `RetentionWorkflow` and `scanIntakeItem` on queue `rwb-document`, and the `retention-monthly` Schedule |
| File | 1 reference | `storageRef` points at the blob the store owns; the review-list file of the run is a File call of the app story; this baseline carries no byte and no body |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** The OpenAPI 3.1 document `openapi/rwb-document-retention-v1.yaml` with the eight operations and the five resources; the AsyncAPI 3.0 fragment for `rwb.document.RetentionApplied.v1` and the record declaration; the contract README rows for the class-in-force rule, the load checks, the scan budget, the idempotency keys and the event count; and the seven WireMock mapping sets of section 12.8.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-18 | Interaction ledger | Ledger owned by rwb-source-data (default ruling) | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The H, C, I and X lists of the metadata table are empty: this baseline adds no build dependency of its own (it is Day 1 by rule), and the platform and service contracts it names are the ones the app story declares. DP-01 appears because the contract names only `rwb_document` tables and consumes the case and the lists through their owners; DP-03 because the DOCRET record is a declared part of the retention answer; DP-07 because the four lists are the reference data of the class and the scan values; DP-10 because the retention Schedule and the scan activity are the Temporal surface the contract declares; DP-11 because both consumed rows are one hop with a fake; DP-13 because the base is the service's own; DP-15 because the migration position is recorded here for the app story; DP-18 because the ledger is P1's and no ledger row is declared; DP-19 because the two screen reads reach SCR-44 and SCR-47 through the composite route.

**Build steps**

1. Write the eight operations with their paths, parameters, resources and error responses; validate the document in the pipeline.
2. Fix the required and optional sets of AC2 to AC5 as schema constraints and README rows, with the class-in-force rule as a written rule.
3. Declare the class load with its multipart request, the row checks, the whole-load refusal and the two rights of AC4.
4. Declare the scan resource with the synchronous answer, the declared budget and the 503 of an unavailable engine, and the two scan-status reads of AC3.
5. Map every status and message ID of AC6 and record the RFC 9457 envelope.
6. Declare the `RetentionApplied` schema and the record of AC5, with the no-personal-data test and the absence test for a scan event.
7. Record the `Idempotency-Key` rule and the three natural keys of AC7.
8. Publish the seven fakes and the eight contract tests, including the drift test; tag the baseline and collect the consumer sign-off of RWB-P5-E1041-APP, RWB-P5-E1026-CON, RWB-P5-E1049-APP and the wave-1 harness.

**Done when.** The OpenAPI artefact and the AsyncAPI fragment validate in the pipeline, the eight contract tests pass, the seven fakes answer every operation of 12.1 and both consumed rows of 12.2, the drift test is green, and RWB-P5-E1041-APP and the upload and intake stories have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P5-016 | Malware found | This file was not stored because the malware scan found a threat. It is held in quarantine. |
| MSG-P3-027 | Retention class load fails a check | The {table} load was refused: {error} at row {row}. The version in force is unchanged. |
| MSG-P5-022 | The scanning service is unavailable | The malware scan is not available, so the file was not stored. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Decision record write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field is empty, or a body fails its schema | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | A concurrent request for the same load or the same scan | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A consumed P3 read does not answer, or the breaker is open | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |

The message IDs and the wording are contract elements copied unchanged from RWB-E1-041 section 14; MSG-GEN-001, MSG-GEN-004 and MSG-GEN-006 are the platform messages the envelope adds, and their text is the platform baseline text. Thai text for each follows decision DL10.

Delivery shape: every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set to the ID above, `detail` carrying the text with its placeholders filled, and `instance` naming the request. The status mapping is fixed by AC6: 401 unauthenticated, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404 for a document, an intake item, a class or a load that does not exist, 409 with MSG-P3-027 or MSG-GEN-004, 422 with MSG-P5-016, MSG-P3-027 or MSG-GEN-001, and 503 with MSG-P5-022, MSG-P7-003 or MSG-GEN-006. A refusal returns no partial page, no partial load and no partial scan result. For MSG-P3-027 the {table} value is RETENTION_CLASS. For MSG-GEN-006 the {system} value is fixed by the consumed row that failed.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-44 Interface and job monitor and SCR-47 Personal data are the two screens the legacy story names, and the states they render are the scan and run states of `RWB-P5-E1041-APP`. The contract serves them through the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19 (`RWB-PLT-N001-CON`), which calls this service once for the scan status, the rule of a class and the last action of a document and merges the answers into the screen model. This baseline fixes the answer shapes only: the screen field list, the route specification, the merge order and the read-only projection belong to `RWB-PLT-N001-CON`.

The three answers the screens depend on are fixed here: `ScanStatus` with `scanResult` CLEAN or INFECTED and `scannedAt`, `RetentionRule` with the period and the end action in the version in force, and `RetentionAction` with the action of the month. A screen that shows an unscanned item as safe is a drift of the answer, and the drift test of AC8 fails it.

The twelve legacy test cases of RWB-E1-041 are listed in the order of the WP and the legacy story; each is answered here at contract level against the artefact and the fakes, and its business outcome is proved by `RWB-P5-E1041-APP`. The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the class codes, the periods, the age bases, the end actions, the rule version, the run month and the scan timeout stay data rows, fixtures or properties of the app story.
- No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: identifiers, codes, versions, dates and counts only; no customer name, national identifier, document name and no custody holder.
- No file byte, no file body and no document content in any payload, example or fake; `storageRef` and `sha256` are the only file identifiers declared.
- No ledger row, no ledger read and no ledger table (DP-18): the interaction ledger is `rwb-source-data`'s.
- No decision-log row: the contract answers a `decisionLogRef` or a `decisionLogId` reference and never a decision-log row.
- The contract names only `rwb_document` tables and only operations owned by `rwb-document`; the two P3 reads are consumed and faked, never declared as provided (DP-01).
- One REST base and one topic per service; a document that names another service's base or topic as its own fails the review (DP-13).
- One event is added by this baseline and no scan event exists; the absence test of AC8 fails a build that declares one.
- The scanning engine, its provider and its capacity are named nowhere in the contract.
- Every example is synthetic and the legacy values are examples only; no production payload is copied into a schema or a fake.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform contract owner**, I want **the published contract of the parameters client — the client interface and its types, the catalog and value data contract with the field ids of the logical data model, the four operations it consumes with their owner and their errors, the cache and refresh rule, the start-up rule, the two build-check contracts and the fakes** — instead of **the monolith's `recovery.casewf.config` package that read two tables in the same database**, so that **all 19 services read parameters through one client and one frozen data contract while the catalog and the endpoints stay with P3** (Template and Rules §R6, DP-06).

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story published a Java interface and one read endpoint inside one application, and it left the loader, the cache and the two build checks to the same module (legacy sections 12 and 13). Nineteen services cannot share that shape: each has its own schema, its own login and its own image, none may read another service's tables, and a client written nineteen times drifts in its types, in its cache and in its build rule (Arch v5 slides 11, 20 and 29; DP-01, DP-06, DP-11). The contract is therefore the deliverable that lets the other eighteen services, and the owner's own service, build and test on Day 1 against a frozen interface and a fake.

**The division is fixed.** The catalog rows, the value versions, the owning service rwb-case, that service's own decision of which version is in force and its server-side cache, and the five REST operations of the legacy story stay with **RWB-P3-E1042-APP** and **RWB-P3-E1042-CON**, under the REST base `/api/recovery/case/v1`. That story owns the legacy acceptance criteria and executes the legacy test cases `TC-E1-042-01` to `TC-E1-042-12`. This contract publishes the **parameters client library** that all 19 services bind, and the two build-check contracts that make "no business value in code" true; it copies no legacy acceptance criterion.

What the contract freezes is the behaviour, not the storage (ASM-2451): a typed read by key, business date and product group that reports the environment and the version; a cache whose time to live is itself a catalog entry; a refresh on the owner's approval event, consumed through the inbox; a start-up rule that refuses to let a service serve traffic without a required value; a generated key set; and two build checks with one finding shape. What it deliberately does not freeze is anything the owner owns: the catalog columns beyond the contract members, the load validation, the approval separation of duty and the authorisation of the five paths.

The contract also fixes the one boundary that keeps the split honest. A service may read a parameter only through the interface and a generated key; it may not call the owner's read path itself, may not read the catalog table, may not cache a secret and may not hold a default in its own code. Held to that, a value changes as data without a release and the same rule holds in all 19 services.

It supports REQ-DRI-010 and REQ-ACA-005: a value changes without a code release, every parameter has an owner and a default, and a secret is listed and never served.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The catalog and the values belong to rwb-case under the Ownership Map and the §R3 default ruling: `parameter_catalog` and `parameter_value` are P3 tables, and the five operations are P3 operations.
- The client has no service short: it is library code inside each service, so it declares no REST base, no topic, no consumer group and no Temporal task queue of its own.
- The field identifiers DF-REF-132 to DF-REF-146 (`parameter_catalog`) and DF-REF-147 to DF-REF-158 (`parameter_value`) are taken from the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary, character for character.
- The legacy members of the published types are taken from legacy section 12: `ParameterValue<T>(String key, T value, int versionNo, LocalDate validFrom, String environment)`, `get(ParameterKey<T>, LocalDate)`, `get(ParameterKey<T>, String productGroup, LocalDate)` and `CatalogEntry entry(String key)`.
- The message ids MSG-P3-032, MSG-GEN-002, MSG-P1-002, MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P7-002, MSG-P3-015 and MSG-P4-002 are used unchanged; the contract invents none.
- The event name `rwb.case.ParameterVersionApproved.v1` on the owner's topic `rwb.case.events.v1` follows §R4 naming on the legacy event "ParameterVersionApproved"; the mapping is recorded in ASM-2453 because no source states the name.
- The artifact coordinates of the library — the group, the artefact name, the version scheme and the publication channel — are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1407; ASM-2454).
- The published status codes of the consumed operations beyond the legacy story's — 200, 201, 401, 403, 409, 422 and 503 — are carried from legacy section 12 and from the message rows; a status that the legacy story does not state for an operation is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1407; ASM-2454).
- No build dependency: the contract is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7), and no approval is needed to publish a draft baseline, which is frozen when the consuming stories pass their contract tests.

##### 4. Flow

1. The contract author writes the client interface and its four types: `Parameters`, `ParameterKey<T>`, `ParameterValue<T>` and `CatalogEntry`.
2. The author writes the generated key contract: `ParameterKeys`, generated from `config/parameter-catalog.csv`, one constant per key with its type, for example `ParameterKeys.CASE_ENTRY_DPD : ParameterKey<Integer>`; a key that the file does not list has no constant.
3. The author writes the catalog and value data contract from the legacy members and the field identifiers of section 11, so the interface, the generated keys, the fakes and the owner's schemas agree.
4. The author writes the four consumed operations exactly as the Ownership Map and the legacy story name them, with the owner, the request, the responses, the status codes and the message ids, and states that the library provides no path of its own.
5. The author writes the cache and refresh rule: one line per key, product group, business date and environment; the time to live read from the catalog entry `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds`; the eviction on `rwb.case.ParameterVersionApproved.v1` through the inbox; approved versions only.
6. The author writes the start-up rule: every required key of a service must have a value for its deployment's environment, and a missing one fails the start with MSG-P3-032 and keeps the pod out of traffic.
7. The author writes the two build-check contracts: what `RwbMagicNumberCheck` and `CatalogCompletenessCheck` accept, what they refuse, and the finding shape — file, line and key.
8. The author publishes the fake and the fixture set, and wires one drift test into the build of every consuming service.
9. The contract is validated: the four paths compared with the Ownership Map, every message id compared with the legacy message table, every type member compared with the field identifiers, and every value taken from the legacy story.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A service declares a read path of its own or calls the owner's path directly | The drift test fails the build: the only read is through `Parameters` | None | AC1, AC6 |
| X2 | A published type gains, loses or renames a member | The contract test of every consuming service fails until the version is raised with a migration note | None | AC1, AC6 |
| X3 | A consumed operation is published with a path that the Ownership Map does not own | The lint step fails and the document is not published | None | AC2 |
| X4 | An operation is published without its status codes or its message id | The lint step fails the build | None | AC2 |
| X5 | A caller reads a key with a string literal | The interface refuses it, so the read does not compile; the completeness check has nothing to compare | None (build output) | AC3 |
| X6 | A service caches a value without a version or reads a value that is not approved | The contract test fails and the review rejects the change | None | AC5 |
| X7 | A consuming service's build drifts from section 12 | The drift test fails naming the member or the operation that moved | None | AC6 |
| X8 | A consumer needs a member that no source defines | The member is not invented; the contract carries the placeholder and the gap stays open | None | AC3 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Publishes documents, a jar and a fake; builds nothing and depends on nothing |
| Negotiable | The member order, the example values and the finding layout are open until the version is frozen |
| Valuable | Every service and the owner's own service start on Day 1 against one interface and one fake |
| Estimable | One interface, four types, one generated key set, four consumed operations, two build-check contracts and the fake |
| Small | One sprint for the contract and the fake, with the lint and contract tests |
| Testable | Each criterion is a schema, lint or drift assertion in section 16 |

Every criterion above is new and tests only the contract artefact. No legacy acceptance criterion is copied: the eleven criteria of RWB-E1-042 stay with RWB-P3-E1042-APP, and the legacy test cases `TC-E1-042-01` to `TC-E1-042-12` execute there.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A service reads a parameter only through the interface and a generated key; it never reads the catalog table and never calls the owner's path itself | Legacy guardrails; DP-01; DP-06 |
| BR2 | Every key a service reads is in the catalog file with an owner and a default; the contract publishes the generated key set and the completeness rule | Legacy BR2; REQ-DRI-010 |
| BR3 | The client is not authoritative: the contract fixes the value line, the version, the environment and the read time, and states that the owner's approved version is the only truth | Legacy section 4 steps 8 and 9 |
| BR4 | A value version that is not APPROVED is never served; the approval event follows §R4 naming on the owner's topic | Legacy BR5; ASM-2453 |
| BR5 | A secret is listed and never served: the value member is absent from a secret line, and no example carries a secret value | Legacy BR6; DL26; REQ-ACA-005 |
| BR6 | A service does not start without every required value for its environment, and MSG-P3-032 names the key and the environment | Legacy BR7 |
| BR7 | The contract publishes platform resources only: the catalog, the values and the five operations stay with P3 rwb-case | Template and Rules §R3 default ruling; Ownership Map |
| BR8 | A published version is never edited in place; a breaking change is a new major version with a migration note | Legacy section 12 versioning; ASM-2454 |

##### 9. State transitions

None in this story: a contract has no runtime state. The states it describes are the value version states of the owner — VALIDATED, APPROVED, ROLLED_BACK — and the client cache line states the APP story implements: absent, loaded, stale and evicted. Each is described with the call or the event that produces it, and the behaviour itself is specified in RWB-PLT-E1042-APP section 9.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The contract author (any team, per U3) | Writes and versions the interface, the data contract, the operation list, the message table and the fake |
| The platform library owner | Approves a breaking change and the version freeze |
| The consuming teams of all 19 services | Read the contract, pin a version, raise a change request |
| rwb-case (P3) | Owns the catalog, the values, the five operations and their authorisation model |
| rwb-access (P4) | Owns the Reference data and Rules and parameters rights that the operations check |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A contract is a technical artefact, not a credit decision |

Role names appear as role codes only, resolved by rwb-access at run time (DP-08). No name of a person, no email address and no credential appears in the contract or in an example.

##### 11. Data

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Field identifiers published | DF-REF-132 to DF-REF-146 (`parameter_catalog`); DF-REF-147 to DF-REF-158 (`parameter_value`) |
| Members published from the legacy contract | key, kind, type, unit, min, max, default, scope, required, owner, environments, usedBy, secret, versionNo, validFrom; the value, its version and its valid-from date; the environment and the product group |
| Members with no field identifier | The client cache line and the event payload members (`paramKeys`, `versionNo`, `validFrom`); the working read of this run |
| Tables owned by the contract | None. `parameter_catalog` and `parameter_value` are P3 tables, named only |
| Personal data in examples | None. Users appear as user ids such as `U-2101`, roles as role codes, values as numbers and dates |

The contract carries no value that no source holds. The catalog members and their order are the legacy section 12 response, the field identifiers are the Logical Data Model's, and the event members are the legacy section 12 event. A member that a consumer needs and no source defines is not invented: the contract carries the placeholder and the gap stays open (GAP-1407; ASM-2454).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None — the client declares no REST operation. The catalog read and the four reference-load operations are provided by P3 rwb-case under `/api/recovery/case/v1` and are consumed, never provided or republished by the library.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Owner | Request | Responses and messages | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | P3 rwb-case | Query: key prefix, kind, owner, environment | 200 array of the catalog line with the value in force, its version and its valid-from date; 401 without a session; 403 without Rules and parameters R (MSG-P4-002); 503 | `get`, `entry` and the start-up check |
| POST `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads` | P3 rwb-case | multipart/form-data: file of key, environment and value; table = "PARAMETER"; validFrom | 201 load with id, table, validFrom, status and rows; 401; 403 without Reference data C (MSG-P4-002); 422 range (MSG-GEN-002), type or unknown key (MSG-P1-002), empty file (MSG-GEN-001); 503 | The contract test and the operator rehearsal; the client never loads |
| POST `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve` | P3 rwb-case | None | 200 approved; 401; 403; 409 when the approver is the author (MSG-P7-002); 503 | The approval whose event refreshes the cache |
| POST `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/rollback` | P3 rwb-case | None | 200 with the previous version in force; 401; 403; 409 when no earlier version exists (MSG-P3-015); 503 | The rollback whose event returns the previous value |

These are exactly the four operations of the Ownership Map rows, at v1, and the owner of all four is P3 rwb-case. The contract states that the library declares no path, no base and no service short, and that a service calls the read only through `Parameters` (DP-11, DP-13). The status codes and message ids are the legacy story's, character for character.

###### 12.3 Events published

None — the library publishes no event. The approval event that refreshes the cache is published by P3 rwb-case through its own outbox.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Producer | Members | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.case.ParameterVersionApproved.v1` | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 rwb-case | `paramKeys`, `versionNo`, `validFrom` | The client evicts the named keys before the next read, through the inbox, with one consumer group per service |

The name follows §R4 on the legacy event "ParameterVersionApproved", which the legacy story calls a new internal event without a topic; the mapping is recorded in ASM-2453. A repeated CloudEvents id has no second effect, and an older `versionNo` never replaces a newer one (DP-09).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None — the client is library code inside each service; the contract declares no workflow, no activity and no task queue of its own.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None — the refresh is event-driven and otherwise lazy by the time to live, which is the catalog entry `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds`; no Schedule and no Quartz job (GAP-1407; ASM-2454).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None — `parameter_catalog` and `parameter_value` are P3 tables in the rwb_case schema under the Ownership Map, and the contract names them only. The client creates no table, holds no copy and writes no row; the one row the listener writes is the inbox row of the outbox and inbox library in the consuming service's own schema (DP-01, DP-15).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| Parameters fake (this story) | The read, the catalog entry, the start-up check and the three interface cases | Every consuming service's drift test and RWB-PLT-E1042-APP |
| Reference-load fake | The three load operations with their success and refusal examples | The contract test of this story and the operator rehearsal of the deployment story |
| Approval-event fake | `rwb.case.ParameterVersionApproved.v1` with one new id, one repeat and one rollback | The cache and refresh tests of RWB-PLT-E1042-APP |
| Build-check fixture set | The two build checks | `RwbMagicNumberCheck` and `CatalogCompletenessCheck` tests: the literal 90, `allocation.retry.limit`, 0, 1, -1 and test code |
| rwb-case reference-data fake | The product-group codes behind RWB-P3-E1043-CON | The typed read examples that carry a product group |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | None provided, 4 consumed | Four operations of P3 rwb-case, at v1; the read at run time, the three load operations in the contract test and the operator rehearsal |
| Kafka | None published, 1 consumed | `rwb.case.ParameterVersionApproved.v1` on `rwb.case.events.v1`, through the inbox |
| Temporal | None | No workflow, no activity and no Schedule |
| File | None | `config/parameter-catalog.csv` is a build input of the generator and the completeness check |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Contract artefact of the platform, the interface and types in `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.platform.params.api`, the data contract and the fake as resources; the implementation is RWB-PLT-E1042-APP.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables. The contract reads the catalog through the owner and holds no copy | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`; the contract supplies the version and the owning service writes the record | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library. This story is the client's contract and names the rwb-case contract it consumes | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case; the product-group codes are reference rows of the owner | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents. The contract fixes the inbox rule for the approval event | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout. The contract replaces the in-process `ParameterService` call with one documented read and a fake | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1`; every consumed path is a `/api/recovery/case/v1` path and the library declares no base | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library. The event name and the topic are fixed on the owner's naming | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema; the inbox table the contract refers to is created by that sequence | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route; the contract adds no route and no screen | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |

**Hardware and software change.** The contract replaces a two-table read in one database with four documented operations of rwb-case and one interface compiled into nineteen deployments; it fixes a per-service cache with a time to live that is itself a catalog entry, an approval event on the owner's topic and a start-up rule that keeps a pod out of traffic. No new hardware is implied; the contract is a jar and a document, and the owner's service and its two tables stay where they are.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `Parameters` | Published interface | Three methods: two typed reads and one catalog entry |
| `ParameterKey<T>`, `ParameterValue<T>`, `CatalogEntry` | Published types | The key with its type; the value with its version, date and environment; the catalog line with its members |
| `ParameterKeys` | Generated source, contract | One constant per catalog key, generated from the catalog file |
| Catalog and value data contract | Document | The members of section 11 with their field identifiers and the secret rule |
| Operation list and message table | Document | The four operations, their owner, their status codes and the seven legacy message ids |
| Cache, refresh and start-up rule | Document | The line, the time to live from the catalog, the eviction on the event and the refusal at start-up |
| Build-check contract | Document | The two checks, their allowed and refused inputs and the finding shape |
| Contract fake and fixtures | Test asset | The four operations, the event, the three interface cases and the build-check fixtures |

**Build steps**

1. Write the interface and the two record types with their members and types; run a compile test of a sample service (AC1).
2. Write the generated key contract and the generator's input rule; prove that a key outside the catalog file has no constant (AC1, AC3).
3. Write the catalog and value data contract from section 11 and cross-check every member with the field identifiers (AC3).
4. Write the operation list from section 12.2 and lint it against the Ownership Map rows; check every status code and message id (AC2).
5. Write the message table from section 14 and compare it with the legacy table, character for character (AC4).
6. Write the cache, refresh and start-up rules as testable sentences, with the time to live as the catalog entry (AC5).
7. Write the two build-check contracts with the finding shape and the allowed literals (AC6).
8. Generate the fake and the fixtures, and wire the drift test into a sample service build (AC6).
9. Publish v1 to the contract registry and hand it to RWB-PLT-E1042-APP and to every consuming service.

**Done when.** The five test cases of section 16 pass, the four operations match the Ownership Map rows, every message id matches the legacy table, and the drift test fails on a changed member and passes on the published jar.
