| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-032 | A required parameter has no value at start-up, published as the start-up refusal | Parameter {name} has no value for {environment}. The service did not start. |
| MSG-GEN-002 | A loaded value is outside its range, published on the load operation | {field} must be between {min} and {max}. |
| MSG-P1-002 | A loaded value has the wrong type or an unknown key, published on the load operation | The {source} load for {date} was refused: {check}. The previous load is still in use. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | The load file is empty, published on the load operation | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P7-002 | The approver is the author, published on the approval operation | You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it. |
| MSG-P3-015 | A rollback has no earlier version, published on the rollback operation | There is no earlier version of {table} to return to. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right, published on all four operations | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The ids and the texts are the legacy story's, character for character, and the status code beside each one in section 12.2 is the legacy status. The two build checks raise no message id: their finding is the build output, with the file, the line and the key. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story. The contract is read by the teams that build the client and by the services that consume it; the catalog screen SCR-39 Rules and parameters belongs to Epic 8 and reads the owner's operation, and the client adds no route and no state to any screen (DP-19). The states the contract describes are the value version states of the owner and the client cache line states of the APP story.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the members are typed, the values are data, and the time to live is the catalog entry `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds`.
- No member that no source defines; a needed member carries the placeholder and the gap stays open.
- No personal data and no secret value in an example, a fixture or a log; only user ids, role codes, numbers and dates.
- No cross-schema reference: the two tables are named as P3 tables and the client holds no copy.
- The four consumed operations stay exactly as the Ownership Map owns them, with owner P3 rwb-case and no path of the library's own.
- A published version is never edited in place; a breaking change raises a new major version with a migration note.
- Every consuming service runs the drift test; a service that skips it has not met the contract.

##### 1. Story

As a **squad member**, I want **the parameters client implemented in the platform library — the typed read by key, business date, product group and environment with the version in the answer, the cache whose time to live is itself a catalog entry, the refresh on the owner's approval event, the start-up check that stops a service whose required parameter has no value, the generated key constants and the two build checks that fail a literal business value and an unknown key**, so that **every service reads its values at run time from the catalog and no team writes the same loader or the same lint rule again** (Template and Rules §R6, DP-06).

##### 2. Business rationale

In the monolith one package, `recovery.casewf.config`, held the published `ParameterService` interface and read two tables, `parameter_catalog` and `parameter_value`, in the same `recovery` schema as every caller (legacy section 13). Under Arch v5 there are 19 services, 19 schemas and 19 logins, no service reads another service's tables, and the parameters belong to rwb-case (Arch v5 slides 14, 20 and 29; Template and Rules §R3 default ruling). A loader that reads two tables is therefore no longer possible for 18 of the 19 services, and a loader written 19 times is the same defect the legacy story was written to remove.

**The division is fixed.** The catalog rows, the value versions, the owning service rwb-case, that service's own decision of which version is in force and its server-side cache, and the five REST operations of the legacy story — `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters`, `POST /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads`, `POST /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve`, `POST /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/verify` and `POST /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/rollback` — stay with **RWB-P3-E1042-APP** and **RWB-P3-E1042-CON**. That story owns the legacy acceptance criteria, and the legacy test cases `TC-E1-042-01` to `TC-E1-042-12` execute there. This story delivers the **parameters client library** that all 19 services bind, plus the **two build checks** that make "no business value in code" true; it copies no legacy acceptance criterion and claims none of the legacy test cases.

What the client keeps from the legacy story is its behaviour, unchanged (ASM-2451): a typed read that answers the value with its version number, resolves the business date and the product group, reports the environment, refreshes on the owner's approval, falls back to its time to live, and refuses to let a service start when a required value has no value for that environment. What it adds is the shape the split forces: the values arrive over the rwb-case contract instead of a second table read, the environment comes from the deployment, the cache is per service and never authoritative, and the time to live is itself a catalog entry rather than a property in a file.

The two build checks are the part of the legacy story that cannot live with the service owner, because they fail a service's build, not a request. `RwbMagicNumberCheck` fails on a numeric or string business literal in the recovery packages and names the catalog key whose default equals the literal; `CatalogCompletenessCheck` compares the keys a service reads with `config/parameter-catalog.csv` and fails on a key with no entry, no owner or no default (legacy section 13; ASM-2452). Held once in the library and applied by the service template, they are written once and enforced everywhere; copied per service they drift, and a check that drifts is worse than none.

It meets REQ-DRI-010 and REQ-ACA-005: a value changes as data without a release, every parameter has an owner and a default, and a secret is listed in the catalog and never served, cached, logged or exported by the client. The measure is the legacy one: zero business values found in code by the build checks, on every service, in every build.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-PLT-E1042-CON is published (this story's contract deliverable): the client interface and its types, the generated key set, the catalog and value data contract, the four consumed operations, the cache and refresh rule, the start-up rule, the two build-check contracts and the fakes.
- RWB-P3-E1042-CON is published: the rwb-case contract behind the operations, with the catalog entry members, the value-in-force members and the approval event (C dependency; DP-06).
- RWB-P3-E1043-CON is published: the reference-data contract of rwb-case, which carries the product-group codes the typed read resolves (C dependency; DP-07).
- RWB-PLT-TE006-CON is published: the outbox and inbox library, so the approval event is consumed through an inbox row in the consuming service's own schema instead of a second consumer loop (DP-09).
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published: the local decision-record library that the owning service writes the parameter version into; the client only supplies the version (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-E1047-CON is published: the naming library that fixes `rwb.case.ParameterVersionApproved.v1` and the topic `rwb.case.events.v1` (DP-14).
- RWB-PLT-E1044-CON is published: the per-service Flyway sequence, which creates the inbox table the listener uses in each service's own schema (DP-15).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the gateway-bff composite route; the library adds no route of its own (DP-19).
- The catalog file `config/parameter-catalog.csv` is in the repository, owned by RW-COE, and lists at least `case.entry.dpd` (INTEGER, range 1 to 365, default 90, scope GLOBAL, required, owner RW-COE, used by `recovery.casewf.casecreation`), `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds` (default 300; 30 in SIT) and `ace.db.password` (kind ENVIRONMENT, secret true).
- The ACE secret store holds the secret values per environment; the catalog lists the secret entries and never their values.
- The artifact coordinates of the platform library — the group, the artefact name, the version scheme and the publication channel — are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1406; ASM-2450).
- The environment name of each deployment (DEV, SIT, UAT, PROD) is a deployment value, not a code constant.
- No build dependency blocks the start of the work: every H dependency above is a platform contract story, so the story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. The build generates `ParameterKeys` from `config/parameter-catalog.csv`, one constant per catalog key with its Java type, for example `ParameterKeys.CASE_ENTRY_DPD : ParameterKey<Integer>`.
2. A service reads a value only through `Parameters.get(ParameterKeys.CASE_ENTRY_DPD, businessDate)`, optionally with a product group; it never passes a string literal and never reads a configuration file for a business value.
3. `ParameterClient` resolves the environment from the deployment, applies the business date and the product group, and asks `ParameterCache` for the key.
4. On a miss, a stale entry or a forced refresh, the client calls `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` over one hop with a 2 s budget and the breaker of the caller, and takes the entry with its value in force, its version number and its valid-from date.
5. `ParameterCache` stores the value per key, product group and business date, with the time to live taken from the catalog entry `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds` — 30 in SIT and 300 in PROD — never from a constant.
6. `ParameterVersionApprovedListener` consumes `rwb.case.ParameterVersionApproved.v1` from `rwb.case.events.v1` through the inbox of the outbox and inbox library, records the CloudEvents id in `processed_event` in the consuming service's own schema, and evicts the named `paramKeys` before the next read.
7. A read on a date before the valid-from date of an approved version keeps the earlier version; on the valid-from date the next read answers the new version, with no restart and no deployment.
8. A rollback approved by the owner is announced on the same event; the cache evicts the key and the next read answers the previous value and its version.
9. At start-up `ParameterStartupCheck` reads every required key of the service's own list for the deployment's environment; when one has no value and no default, the check fails with MSG-P3-032, names the key and the environment, and the probe keeps the pod out of traffic.
10. `CatalogEntry entry(String key)` answers the catalog line — kind, type, unit, minimum, maximum, default, scope, required, owner, environments, used by, secret, version and valid-from — and never a value for a line marked secret.
11. The build runs `RwbMagicNumberCheck` over the recovery packages and `CatalogCompletenessCheck` over the keys read; each reports the file, the line and the key, and fails the build.
12. The owning service records the version in its decision record through the local decision-record library; the client writes no decision record of its own.
13. The client publishes its own counters and timers on the platform observability path: reads, cache hits, cache age per key, refreshes, failed refreshes and start-up refusals.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The catalog entry for a required key has no value and no default for the deployment's environment | The start-up check fails for that key and environment; the probe stays unready and the pod takes no traffic | MSG-P3-032 | AC5 |
| X2 | The rwb-case read fails, times out at 2 s or the breaker is open | The read fails with the client's own exception; a cached value inside its time to live is served with its own version and a stale marker; nothing is invented | None | AC8 |
| X3 | A cached value is older than `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds` | The next read re-reads the owner; a failed re-read returns the exception and never a guessed value | None | AC8 |
| X4 | The approval event arrives twice or out of order | The inbox drops the repeat; an older `versionNo` never replaces a newer one in the cache | None | AC8 |
| X5 | A secret entry is asked for as a value | The catalog line is answered without a value; the client never calls the secret store and never logs the line as a value | None | AC4 |
| X6 | Code holds a numeric or string business literal | The build fails and names the file, the line and the catalog key whose default equals the literal | None (build output) | AC6 |
| X7 | Code reads a key that the catalog file does not list | The build fails and names the key | None (build output) | AC7 |
| X8 | A caller passes a string literal instead of a generated key | The interface rejects it, so the read does not compile, and the catalog completeness check has nothing to compare | None (build output) | AC7 |
| X9 | The product-group override has no value for the group | The read answers the GLOBAL value of the same key with its version, never a default written in the service | None | AC1 |
| X10 | The refresh event names a key the service does not read | The event is recorded in the inbox and no cache line is evicted | None | AC8 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against the library and platform contracts and the rwb-case fake; no other service has to exist first |
| Negotiable | The cache time to live, the read timeout and the key list are configuration; the types, the operations and the two checks are the published contract |
| Valuable | Gives all 19 services one loader and one build check on Day 1 and removes the two-table read from every service plan |
| Estimable | One interface, four types, one generated key set, one cache, one listener, one start-up check and two build checks |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion uses the rwb-case fake, a fixture module and the two build checks of section 12.8 |

```gherkin
    When rwb.case.ParameterVersionApproved.v1 for versionNo 2 arrives on rwb.case.events.v1
    Then the client evicts the key before the next read and the inbox drops a repeat of the same CloudEvents id
    When the event is lost and the time to live passes
    Then the client re-reads GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters and still serves only the approved version
    Then a version whose load status is VALIDATED and not APPROVED is never served, read from the cache or from the owner
```

No legacy acceptance criterion is copied into this story. The eleven legacy criteria `AC1` to `AC11` of RWB-E1-042 stay with RWB-P3-E1042-APP, which owns the catalog, the value versions and the five operations; the eight criteria above are new and test only the client library and its two build checks. The values they use — `case.entry.dpd`, the range 1 to 365, the default 90, the scope GLOBAL, the owner RW-COE, the used-by `recovery.casewf.casecreation`, `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds` 30 in SIT and 300 in PROD, `allocation.retry.limit`, `ace.db.password`, versions 1 and 2, the dates 2026-12-05, 2026-12-09 and 2026-12-10 and the message ids — are the legacy story's, character for character.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | No business value in code: every limit, threshold, name and timer is read at run time through a generated key, and the build fails on a literal business value | Legacy BR1; Principle 1; DT02; BR-P3-022; DP-06 |
| BR2 | Every key a service reads is in the catalog file with an owner and a default, and the build fails naming the key that is not | Legacy BR2; REQ-DRI-010 |
| BR3 | A value changes only through the owner's checked, approved, dated load; the client shows the new value on its valid-from date and the previous one before it | Legacy BR3; CTL-08; AC2 |
| BR4 | A client never serves a value version that is not APPROVED, and an open decision keeps the version it was taken under because the owning service records the version it read | Legacy BR5; R-UNI-38 |
| BR5 | A secret entry is listed in the catalog and held only in the secret store: the client returns no value for it and never asks for one | Legacy BR6; DL26; REQ-ACA-005 |
| BR6 | A service does not start without every required value for its environment; the probe keeps the pod out of traffic | Legacy BR7; AC5 |
| BR7 | The client is not authoritative: it caches a value it has read, with a time to live that is itself a catalog entry, and re-reads the owner when the event arrives or the time to live passes | Legacy section 4 step 8; ASM-2451 |
| BR8 | The environment is a deployment value and the product group is a request value; neither is a constant of the code | Legacy AC8; ASM-2451 |
| BR9 | The two build checks are held once in the library and applied by the service template: a literal business value and an unknown key fail the build with the file, the line and the key | Legacy section 13; ASM-2452 |

##### 9. State transitions

The client holds no case status and changes none. It holds one cache line per key, product group, business date and environment, and the owner holds the version states the legacy story fixed (VALIDATED, APPROVED, ROLLED_BACK).

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| No line | First read | The owner answers an approved version | Loaded with that version and its valid-from date |
| Loaded | Read before the valid-from date of a newer approved version | The newer version is not yet in force | Loaded, still the earlier version |
| Loaded | The valid-from date arrives | The newer version is approved and in force | Loaded with the newer version, no restart |
| Loaded | `rwb.case.ParameterVersionApproved.v1` | The CloudEvents id is new to the inbox | Evicted, then loaded on the next read |
| Loaded | The time to live passes | None | Stale; re-read on the next read |
| Stale | The owner answers | None | Loaded with the version in force |
| Stale | The owner fails | A value inside the last known state exists | An exception to the caller; never a guessed value |
| Loaded | Owner rollback to an earlier version | The earlier version is APPROVED | Loaded with the earlier version |
| Any | A required key has no value at start-up | The deployment's environment | Start refused with MSG-P3-032 |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-COE | Owns the catalog file and the values; the client reads what the owner approved |
| RW-RISK | Approves a value version where a threshold or a limit moves, on the owner's service; the client has no approval path |
| RW-PLATADM | Owns the environment settings and reads the client's counters and start-up refusals |
| RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY | Read the client's version trace and the build reports |
| The owning service of each caller | Chooses the keys it reads, lists the required ones and records the version it read in its decision record |
| Platform library team, owning the template | Publishes the interface, the generated keys, the cache rule and the two build checks; changes them only through the contract story |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A parameter is not a credit decision |

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-REF-132 to DF-REF-146 | parameter_catalog | all fields | Read only, through the rwb-case contract |
| DF-REF-147 to DF-REF-158 | parameter_value | all fields | Read only, through the rwb-case contract |
| The outbox and inbox library tables | processed_event | ce_id, consumer_group, processed_at | Write, in the consuming service's own schema, through RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary. `parameter_catalog` and `parameter_value` are P3 tables in the rwb_case schema under the Ownership Map; this story names them and never creates, reads or writes a copy of either (DP-01). The client holds no business table: its cache is in memory and its only row is the inbox row it already has through the outbox and inbox library. The cache line members — key, product group, business date, environment, value, version number, valid-from date and read time — are the working read of this run and have no field identifier of their own (GAP-1406; ASM-2451).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None — the library has no REST surface. The five operations of the legacy story belong to P3 rwb-case under the REST base `/api/recovery/case/v1`, and RWB-P3-E1042-APP provides them.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | P3 rwb-case | The typed read, the catalog entry and the start-up check; one hop, 2 s budget, breaker and bulkhead of the caller |
| POST | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads` | P3 rwb-case | Drives a new value version in the contract test of this story; the client never loads a value |
| POST | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve` | P3 rwb-case | The approval whose event refreshes the cache, driven by the contract test |
| POST | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/rollback` | P3 rwb-case | The rollback whose event returns the previous value, driven by the contract test |

Only the read is called at run time; the three load operations are the owner's and are driven by the contract test and the operator rehearsal of the deployment story, so that the client is proved against a new version, an approval and a rollback on the owner's own paths and never against a value of its own.

###### 12.3 Events published

None — the client publishes no event. A cache refresh is local to the service that received the owner's event.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Producer | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.case.ParameterVersionApproved.v1` | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 rwb-case | Carries `paramKeys`, `versionNo` and `validFrom`; the listener evicts those keys through the inbox, in the consuming service's own consumer group |

The event name follows the §R4 naming of the owner's topic and is recorded in ASM-2453; the payload members are the legacy story's. The client subscribes once per service and adds no second consumer group.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None — the client is library code inside each service; it starts no workflow and no activity, and a service that needs a workflow for its own step uses the workflow kit.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None — the refresh is event-driven and otherwise lazy by the time to live; no Temporal Schedule and no Quartz job is created (GAP-1406; ASM-2451).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None — `parameter_catalog` and `parameter_value` are P3 tables, named only. The client creates no table, owns no table and writes no row except the inbox row that the outbox and inbox library already owns in the consuming service's own schema.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-case parameters fake | `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | `case.entry.dpd` version 1 = 90 and version 2 = 91 from 2026-12-10 for PROD; `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds` 30 for SIT and 300 for PROD; `ace.db.password` listed with no value; a required key with no value for UAT |
| rwb-case reference-load fake | The three load operations | A load answered 201, an approval answered 200, a rollback answered 200 with status ROLLED_BACK, and one refusal of each kind |
| rwb-case approval-event fake | `rwb.case.ParameterVersionApproved.v1` on `rwb.case.events.v1` | One event for `case.entry.dpd` version 2, one repeat of the same CloudEvents id and one rollback event for version 1 |
| Inbox fake | The outbox and inbox library | A repeated CloudEvents id that is dropped, and a new id that is recorded |
| Fixture modules | The two build checks | A module with the literal 90, a module reading `allocation.retry.limit`, a module with 0, 1 and -1, and a module with the literal 90 in test code |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | None provided, 4 consumed | The read at run time; the three load operations in the contract test and the operator rehearsal |
| Kafka | None published, 1 consumed | `rwb.case.ParameterVersionApproved.v1` on `rwb.case.events.v1`, through the inbox |
| Temporal | None | No workflow, no activity and no Schedule |
| File | None | `config/parameter-catalog.csv` is a build input of the key generator and the completeness check, never a run-time read |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Shared library artefact of the platform, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.platform.params`; the published interface and types in `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.platform.params.api`; the two build checks in `build-tools/rwb-checks`. The legacy package `recovery.casewf.config` is the monolith's and is not carried.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables. The client reads the catalog through the rwb-case contract and holds no copy | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`; the client supplies the version and the owning service writes the record | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library. This story is that client library, and the rwb-case contract is what it reads | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case; the product-group codes the typed read resolves are reference rows | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents. The approval event is consumed through the inbox | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout. The old in-process `ParameterService` call becomes one REST read with a mock and a breaker | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1`; the client calls `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` and adds no base of its own | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library. The refresh event is `rwb.case.ParameterVersionApproved.v1` on `rwb.case.events.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema; the inbox row the listener writes arrives through that sequence | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route; the client adds no screen, no route and no state of its own | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Hardware and software change.** The two-table read in one database becomes one REST read of the rwb-case contract from each of the 19 services, with a per-service cache and a breaker; the time to live moves from a property to a catalog entry read through the same client; the approval event arrives on the owner's Kafka topic and is consumed through the library inbox; and the two build checks move from the monolith's build to the platform library, where the service template applies them to every service. No new hardware is implied: the client runs inside the existing service pods on the AKS cluster, and the catalog and the values stay on the ACE PostgreSQL server in the rwb_case schema under the owner's login.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `Parameters` | Published interface | `get(ParameterKey<T>, LocalDate)`, `get(ParameterKey<T>, String productGroup, LocalDate)` and `CatalogEntry entry(String key)` (BR1, BR7) |
| `ParameterKey<T>`, `ParameterValue<T>`, `CatalogEntry` | Published types | The key with its type; the value with `key`, `value`, `versionNo`, `validFrom` and `environment`; the catalog line with its thirteen members |
| `ParameterKeys` and `ParameterKeysGenerator` | Generated source and build tool | One constant per catalog key, generated from `config/parameter-catalog.csv`; a key that is not in the file is not generated (BR2) |
| `ParameterClient` | Service | Environment, business date and product-group resolution; one hop, 2 s budget, breaker and bulkhead; the version in the answer (BR3, BR8) |
| `ParameterCache` | Service | One line per key, product group, business date and environment; time to live from `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds`; approved versions only (BR4, BR7) |
| `ParameterVersionApprovedListener` | Service | Consumes the approval event through the inbox, drops a repeat and evicts the named keys (BR7) |
| `ParameterCatalogReadClient` | Client | Calls the read operation and leaves the value out of a secret line (BR5) |
| `ParameterStartupCheck` | Service | Reads the service's required keys for its environment and fails the start with MSG-P3-032 (BR6) |
| `RwbMagicNumberCheck` | Build tool | Fails on a numeric or string business literal in the recovery packages; allowed: 0, 1, -1, test code; names the catalog key whose default equals the literal (BR9) |
| `CatalogCompletenessCheck` | Build tool | Compares the keys read through `ParameterKeys` with the catalog file; fails on a missing key, owner or default (BR2, BR9) |
| `ParameterMetrics` | Service | Counters and timers for reads, cache age, refreshes, failed refreshes and start-up refusals |

**Configuration and reference data.** The environment name, the location of `config/parameter-catalog.csv` and the bootstrap of the cache time to live are deployment values; from the first successful read the time to live is the catalog entry `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds`, 30 in SIT and 300 in PROD (ASM-2451; ASM-2455). The required key list of each service is a short list in that service's own configuration, and the build check proves every key on it exists in the catalog file. The legacy feature flag `rwb.p3.configservice` stays with the owner's service (RWB-P3-E1042-APP); the library has no flag of its own.

**Build steps**

1. Publish the interface and the four types from the CON story; test that a string literal does not compile (AC1, AC7).
2. Write `ParameterKeysGenerator` and generate `ParameterKeys` from the catalog file; test a key that the file does not list (AC7).
3. Write `ParameterClient` with the environment, date and product-group resolution and the 2 s budget; test the read, the pre-valid-from date and the valid-from date (AC1, AC2).
4. Write `ParameterCache` with the time to live read from the catalog and the approved-only rule; test the stale line and the failed re-read (AC2, AC8).
5. Write `ParameterVersionApprovedListener` against the inbox; test the eviction, the repeat drop and the out-of-order event (AC8).
6. Write `ParameterCatalogReadClient` with the secret line left out; test the listed entry with no value and the owner not asked (AC4).
7. Write `ParameterStartupCheck` and the readiness probe wiring; test the missing value for UAT (AC5).
8. Write `RwbMagicNumberCheck` and `CatalogCompletenessCheck` with the file, line and key in the report; test both on the fixture modules (AC6, AC7).
9. Run the contract test against the fakes of section 12.8 for a rollback and for a load, with the owner's three operations driven from the test (AC3).
10. Wire the metrics and hand the version to the owning service's decision record as a contract test (AC1, AC8).

**Done when.** The seven test cases of section 16 pass, the contract test of the CON story passes against the fakes, the two build checks run green on main over the 19 services with the file, line and key in every finding, and one service in SIT reads `case.entry.dpd` through the client with no value in its own image or chart.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-032 | A required parameter has no value at start-up | Parameter {name} has no value for {environment}. The service did not start. |
| MSG-GEN-002 | A loaded value is outside its range, on the owner's operation | {field} must be between {min} and {max}. |
| MSG-P1-002 | A loaded value has the wrong type or an unknown key, on the owner's operation | The {source} load for {date} was refused: {check}. The previous load is still in use. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | The load file is empty, on the owner's operation | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P7-002 | The approver is the author, on the owner's operation | You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it. |
| MSG-P3-015 | A rollback has no earlier version, on the owner's operation | There is no earlier version of {table} to return to. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right calls the owner's operation | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

MSG-P3-032 is the only message the library raises; the other six are the owner's, carried here unchanged because the contract test of this story drives the operations that raise them. The two build checks raise no user-facing message: their finding is the build output, with the file, the line and the key. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen of its own. A squad member sees the two build findings in the pipeline output, with the file, the line and the key, and a cache or start-up event in the service's own log and on SCR-44 Interface and job monitor. SCR-39 Rules and parameters belongs to Epic 8 and reads the owner's operation; the client adds no screen, no route and no state to any screen (DP-19).

The levels are the target shape: the legacy `System` level becomes Component, and the cache, the time to live and the start-up refusal are measured as NFR. The legacy test case ids are not reused here — they stay with RWB-P3-E1042-APP, which executes them.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: every limit, threshold, name and timer is a catalog entry read through a generated key, and `RwbMagicNumberCheck` fails the build on a literal.
- No key outside the catalog: `CatalogCompletenessCheck` fails the build naming a key that the catalog file does not list, and the generator cannot create a constant for it.
- No personal data in the cache, a log, a test or a prompt; a parameter is a threshold, a name or a timer, never a person.
- No secret value in the cache, a response, a log or a build report: a secret line is listed and its value is never asked for.
- No read of another service's tables: the catalog and the values arrive over the rwb-case contract only, and the client holds no copy (DP-01).
- No value change needs a deployment and no parameter needs a code change: a new value is the owner's load, and a new parameter is a reviewed catalog entry.
- The client is never authoritative: a cached value carries its version and its read time, and a stale value is marked rather than presented as current.
- The library adds no REST base, no topic and no task queue of its own; it is not one of the 19 services.

##### 1. Story

As a **DevOps engineer of the platform**, I want **the parameters client released as one pinned library version in the service template, its environment name, cache time to live and catalog file held as chart values, the catalog seed and the start-up probe deployed in the right order in each environment, the secret references kept out of the catalog values, the dashboards and alerts for a missing value, a stale cache and a failed refresh, and the runbook for a value load, an approval and a rollback**, so that **a value change needs no release and a missing value stops a deployment instead of a service** (Template and Rules §R6, DP-06).

##### 2. Business rationale

A client that is correct in code is not yet safe in a deployment. The legacy story put the catalog seed in a Flyway migration of the same application that read it, so the loader and the values always started together (legacy section 13). In the target the values are served by rwb-case and read by 19 services, each in its own image and its own chart, so three new failure modes appear that no line of client code can close: a service deployed with a library version that drifted from the published contract, a service started before the values it needs exist, and a cache that goes stale without anyone noticing because the refresh event never arrived.

**The division is fixed.** The catalog rows, the value versions, the owning service rwb-case, that service's own decision of which version is in force and its server-side cache, and the five REST operations of the legacy story stay with **RWB-P3-E1042-APP** and **RWB-P3-E1042-CON**, under the REST base `/api/recovery/case/v1`; that story owns the legacy acceptance criteria and executes the legacy test cases `TC-E1-042-01` to `TC-E1-042-12`. This story delivers the **deployment of the parameters client library** — the pinned version, the chart values, the seed order, the probe, the secret references, the alerts and the runbook — for the client that RWB-PLT-E1042-APP builds and RWB-PLT-E1042-CON publishes. It copies no legacy acceptance criterion.

What the deployment adds is the order that the split forces. The catalog must exist before a pod starts, so the chart runs a seed check in front of the rollout and the pod carries a readiness probe on the same check as its start-up; the library version must be one version for all 19 services, so the template pins it and the build fails on a drift; the environment name and the catalog file must be deployment data, so they are chart values and a change needs no rebuild; and a stale cache must be visible, so the library's own metrics feed three alerts rather than a log line nobody reads.

The secrets rule is the one place where the deployment carries a security control rather than a convenience. The catalog lists `ace.db.password` as a secret entry and never holds its value; the chart, the pipeline and the image therefore hold a reference to the key store and never a credential, and a scan of the three finds none. That is the deployment half of REQ-ACA-005; the value itself never leaves the key store.

It supports REQ-DRI-010 and REQ-ACA-005, and it makes the legacy measure observable: zero business values in code, and zero services serving traffic without the values they require.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-PLT-E1042-APP is delivered: the client, its cache, its listener, its start-up check and its two build checks.
- RWB-PLT-E1042-CON is published and frozen: the pinned major version, the four consumed operations, the event, the cache and start-up rules and the two build-check contracts.
- RWB-PLT-N004-OPS provides the pipeline template and the Helm chart of every service, into which this story adds the library version, the chart values, the seed job and the probe.
- RWB-PLT-NF04-OPS provides the secrets baseline: the key-store reference shape and the scan that proves no credential sits in a pipeline file, a chart value or an image layer.
- RWB-PLT-N005-OPS provides the dashboards and alerts baseline, into which this story adds the three alerts and the client's panel.
- RWB-PLT-E1044-OPS provides the migration run at service start in each environment, which is the sequence that carries the owner's catalog seed and the inbox table the listener writes.
- RWB-P3-E1042-APP serves the catalog and the values in every environment, with the seed of the catalog in its own Flyway sequence in `rwb_case` (DP-01, DP-15).
- The catalog file `config/parameter-catalog.csv` is in the repository, owned by RW-COE, and lists `case.entry.dpd`, `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds` (30 in SIT, 300 in PROD) and `ace.db.password` as a secret entry.
- The chart value names, the seed-job weight, the probe period and thresholds and the alert thresholds of the library are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1408; ASM-2455; ASM-2456).
- No build dependency: the story has no build dependency and is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Pipeline: the template pins one library version for every service, for example `parameterClientVersion` with major version 1, and the build compares the version in the chart with the version the service compiles against.
2. Pipeline: the build fails when the two versions differ, naming the service, the chart value and the compiled version.
3. Chart: `RWB_ENV` carries the environment name (DEV, SIT, UAT or PROD), `RWB_PARAMETER_CATALOG` carries the catalog file the service ships, and `RWB_PARAMETER_TTL_KEY` carries the name of the catalog entry that bounds the cache, `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds`.
4. Chart: a bootstrap time to live is set for the window before the first catalog answer, and it is compared with the catalog entry at deployment; once the catalog answers, the catalog entry is the time to live and the chart value is ignored (ASM-2455).
5. Deployment: the `parameter-catalog-seed` job runs as a Helm hook before the rollout (`pre-install,pre-upgrade`, weight -5). It reads the chart's catalog file and calls `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` to confirm that every key of the file exists in the catalog with an owner and a default for that environment; a missing key fails the release before any pod starts.
6. Deployment: the owner's own Flyway sequence in `rwb_case` carries the authoritative row load; the hook never writes the owner's tables (DP-01).
7. Deployment: the pod starts and the readiness probe reads `/health/parameters`, which is the same check as the start-up check; a required value with no value for the environment fails with MSG-P3-032 and the pod stays out of traffic.
8. Chart: the secret entries, `ace.db.password` among them, are key-store references in the chart and the pipeline; no credential appears in a chart value, a pipeline file, an image layer, a log or a prompt.
9. Observability: the client's own metrics feed one panel and three alerts — a required value missing at start-up (page), a cache line older than its time to live (warning, per key and environment), and a failed refresh or a failed read (warning with the breaker state).
10. Operator: a value change is the runbook — load a version, get it approved, verify it in force, roll back if needed — and every step is a call of the owner's operations, never a change of a chart value or of a database row.
11. Release: a library version is rolled forward and back by the pipeline, and a value version is rolled forward and back by the runbook; both are rehearsed in SIT with the evidence attached to the story.
12. The version in the chart and the version in the client's published contract are compared on every build, and a drift is a failed build rather than a discovery in production.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The chart pins a library version other than the one the service compiles against | The build fails, naming the service, the chart value and the compiled version | None (build output) | AC1 |
| X2 | A required key has no value for the environment at deployment | The seed hook fails the release before the rollout, or the probe keeps the pod out of traffic; the key and the environment are named | MSG-P3-032 | AC4 |
| X3 | The owner's read is unreachable at deploy time | The seed hook fails the release; a running pod keeps its last known state and raises the failed-read alert | None | AC4, AC5 |
| X4 | A credential is found in a pipeline file, a chart value or an image layer | The scan fails the build and the release is not promoted | None (build output) | AC3 |
| X5 | A cache line is older than its time to live | The stale-cache alert fires for the key and the environment; the next read re-reads the owner | None | AC5 |
| X6 | The approval event is never consumed | The failed-refresh alert fires; the time to live closes the gap at the next read and the version served is still an approved one | None | AC5 |
| X7 | A library rollback leaves a pod on the previous version | The pipeline rolls the deployment back and the drift check proves chart and contract agree again | None | AC6 |
| X8 | A value rollback leaves no earlier version | The owner refuses the rollback and the runbook stops; the value in force does not change | MSG-P3-015 | AC6, AC7 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the client, its contract and the three platform baselines; no service has to be built first |
| Negotiable | The chart value names, the seed weight, the probe period and the alert thresholds are settled with the platform team; the order and the rules are fixed |
| Valuable | A value change needs no release, and a missing value stops a deployment instead of a service |
| Estimable | One pinned version, three chart values, one seed hook, one probe, one panel, three alerts and one runbook |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its rehearsals |
| Testable | Each criterion runs in the pipeline and in SIT against the chart and the fake of section 12.8 |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Deployment of the parameters client

  Background:
    Given the parameters client library is published at major version 1
    Given the catalog and the values are served by rwb-case under /api/recovery/case/v1
    Given every service is deployed from the service template and its Helm chart

  Scenario: AC1 The library version is pinned and a drift fails the build (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the template pins parameterClientVersion 1.0.0 for every service
    When a service chart pins 1.1.0 while the service compiles against 1.0.0
    Then the build fails naming the service, the chart value and the compiled version
    When the chart and the compiled version agree
    Then the build passes and the deployed image carries the pinned version

  Scenario: AC2 The environment, the time to live and the catalog file are chart values (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the chart values RWB_ENV, RWB_PARAMETER_CATALOG and RWB_PARAMETER_TTL_KEY
    When SIT is deployed with RWB_ENV SIT and PROD with RWB_ENV PROD
    Then the client reads the environment name from the chart and reports it in every answer
    Then the time to live is the catalog entry refdata.cache.ttl-seconds, 30 in SIT and 300 in PROD, and the chart value is the bootstrap only
    Then a change of the environment name or of the catalog file needs no rebuild of the image

  Scenario: AC3 The secret references are kept out of the catalog values (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the catalog lists "ace.db.password" as kind ENVIRONMENT with secret = true
    When the chart, the pipeline and the image are scanned
    Then every secret is a key-store reference and no credential appears in a chart value, a pipeline file, an image layer, a log or a prompt
    Then the catalog carries the entry and no value for it, and the scan reports no secret value in any catalogue row

  Scenario: AC4 The catalog seed runs before the start and the probe holds the pod out of traffic (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the parameter-catalog-seed job runs as a Helm hook before the rollout
    When a key of the chart's catalog file has no entry, no owner or no default in the catalog for that environment
    Then the hook fails the release before any pod starts
    Given "refdata.cache.ttl-seconds" is required and has no value for UAT
    When the rollout runs in UAT
    Then the readiness probe answers DOWN with MSG-P3-032 naming the key and the environment and the pod takes no traffic
    Then the deployment reports a failed rollout instead of a serving service

  Scenario: AC5 The dashboards and the alerts cover the three failures (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the client's own metrics on the platform observability path
    When a required value is missing at start-up, a cache line passes its time to live, or a refresh fails
    Then each case raises its own alert with the service, the key and the environment
    Then the panel shows cache age per key, refreshes, failed refreshes and start-up refusals for each environment
    Then the missing-value alert is the only one that pages

  Scenario: AC6 The rollout and the rollback are rehearsed with evidence (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the library at version 1.0.0 in SIT
    When the pipeline rolls version 1.1.0 out and then rolls it back
    Then each step is recorded with the image, the chart value, the time and the result
    Given a value version 2 of "case.entry.dpd" and a later rollback to version 1
    When the runbook runs in SIT
    Then the client serves 91 with version 2 and then 90 with version 1, and each step is recorded with the load id, the approver role and the time

  Scenario: AC7 The runbook is published and one rehearsal is recorded (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the runbook for a value load, an approval, a verify and a rollback
    When an operator follows it for a value of "case.entry.dpd"
    Then every step names the owner's operation, the role that may run it and the message of a refusal
    Then the rehearsal of the six-step path is recorded with its evidence and no step changes a chart value or a database row by hand
```

Every criterion above is new and tests only the deployment of the client. No legacy acceptance criterion is copied: the eleven criteria of RWB-E1-042 stay with RWB-P3-E1042-APP, and the legacy test cases `TC-E1-042-01` to `TC-E1-042-12` execute there.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One library version for all 19 services, pinned in the template; a chart that disagrees with the compiled version fails the build | Legacy section 4 step 2; DP-06 |
| BR2 | The environment name, the catalog file and the time-to-live entry are deployment values, so a value change needs no release and no rebuild | Legacy BR3; REQ-DRI-010; ASM-2455 |
| BR3 | The time to live is itself a catalog entry; the chart value is the bootstrap and the catalog entry governs once the owner answers | Legacy section 13; ASM-2455 |
| BR4 | The catalog seed runs before the service starts, and a service without its required values takes no traffic | Legacy BR7; Principle 1 |
| BR5 | Secrets are key-store references: the catalog lists them and the chart, the pipeline and the image hold no value for them | Legacy BR6; DL26; REQ-ACA-005; NFR-052 |
| BR6 | A value change is the operator's load, approval, verify and rollback, never a chart change and never a manual row update | Legacy BR3, BR4; CTL-08 |
| BR7 | A cache older than its time to live, a failed refresh and a missing required value are visible on the platform dashboards and raise their own alert | Legacy section 5 X3; ASM-2456 |
| BR8 | The deployment never writes the owner's tables: the row load is the owner's Flyway sequence in `rwb_case` | DP-01; DP-15 |

##### 9. State transitions

The deployment has release states, not case states.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | Seed hook passes | Every key of the catalog file exists with an owner and a default | Rollout started |
| Not deployed | Seed hook fails | A key is missing, has no owner or has no default | Release failed, no pod started |
| Rollout started | Probe ready | Every required value is present for the environment | Serving |
| Rollout started | Probe unready with MSG-P3-032 | A required value has no value for the environment | Rollout failed, the pod takes no traffic |
| Serving | Library roll-forward | The chart and the compiled version agree | Serving on the new version |
| Serving | Library rollback | The pipeline restores the previous chart value | Serving on the previous version |
| Serving | Value load approved and in force | The valid-from date is reached | Serving the new value with no restart |
| Serving | Value rollback approved | An earlier approved version exists | Serving the previous value |
| Serving | Cache older than the time to live, or a failed refresh | None | Alert raised; the value served is still an approved one |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| DevOps engineer of the platform | Owns the pinned version, the chart values, the seed hook, the probe, the alerts and the runbook |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Reads the client's panel and the failed rollout on SCR-44; reruns a release |
| RW-COE | Owns the catalog file and runs a value load |
| RW-RISK | Approves a value version where a threshold or a limit moves |
| RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY | Read the release record, the value history and the alert history |
| Key store administrator | Owns the secret entries and their rotation; not a Workbench role |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A parameter is not a credit decision |

##### 11. Data

No business field is written by this story. The deployment reads the catalog file from the chart, reads the catalog through the owner's operation and writes a release record with the service, the environment, the image, the chart values, the library version, `startedAt`, `endedAt` and a status of PASSED or FAILED. It reads the secret references from the key store and never their values.

The chart value names, the seed-job weight, the probe period and thresholds, the alert thresholds and the retention of the release record are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1408; ASM-2455; ASM-2456); the working read of this run is used until the register closes the point. The catalog file holds keys, types, ranges, defaults, owners and environments and no personal data and no secret value.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None — the deployment provides no REST operation. The client's only HTTP surface inside a pod is the service's own health endpoint, which the probe reads.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the deployment |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | P3 rwb-case | The seed hook confirms every key of the chart's catalog file, with its owner and its default, for the environment; a running client reads it for its values |
| POST | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads` | P3 rwb-case | The runbook's load step and the SIT rehearsal of a value version |
| POST | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve` | P3 rwb-case | The approval whose event refreshes the caches; driven by the runbook and the rehearsal |
| POST | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/rollback` | P3 rwb-case | The rollback of a value version in the runbook and the rehearsal |

The deployment calls the read; the three load operations are called by an operator following the runbook. The pipeline holds no credential of its own for them: every call is an operator session with a right from the P4 matrix, and the deployment only records that the step happened.

###### 12.3 Events published

None — the deployment publishes no event.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Producer | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.case.ParameterVersionApproved.v1` | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 rwb-case | The pods of every service subscribe through the client's inbox; the deployment's part is the consumer group per service, the topic ACL, the retry topics and the dead-letter alert of the event platform |

The event name follows §R4 naming on the owner's topic and is recorded in ASM-2453; the topic, its ACLs and its retry and dead-letter topics are the event platform's (RWB-PLT-EVT).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None — the seed hook is a Helm hook, the probe is a readiness probe and the refresh is library code; the deployment starts no workflow and no activity.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None — a value load is operator-initiated and the refresh is event-driven; no Schedule is created for the catalog, for the seed or for the alerts.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None — the deployment owns no table. The catalog and the values are P3 tables in `rwb_case`, and the inbox row the listener writes is the outbox and inbox library object in each service's own schema.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-case parameters fake | `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` answering the catalog line with the value in force, the version and the valid-from date, and an entry with no value for `ace.db.password`; a missing required value for UAT | The seed hook test, the probe test and the alert tests |
| rwb-case reference-load fake | The three load operations answering 201, 200 and 200 with status ROLLED_BACK, and 409 for a rollback with no earlier version | The runbook rehearsal and the SIT value-version test |
| Approval-event stub | `rwb.case.ParameterVersionApproved.v1` on `rwb.case.events.v1`, one new id and one repeat | The failed-refresh alert test and the library rollback test |
| Key-store stub | The secret references of the chart | The credential scan test |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | None provided, 4 consumed | The seed hook reads the catalog; the runbook and the rehearsal call the three load operations |
| Kafka | None published, 1 consumed | The pods subscribe to `rwb.case.ParameterVersionApproved.v1` on `rwb.case.events.v1` |
| Temporal | None | No workflow, no activity and no Schedule |
| File | 1, the catalog file | `config/parameter-catalog.csv` travels in the image and the chart and is read by the client's generator and the seed hook, never by a running request |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** The pinned library version in the pipeline template, the three chart values with their bootstrap and drift check, the `parameter-catalog-seed` Helm hook, the readiness probe on the client's health check, the key-store references for the secret entries, the panel and the three alerts, the runbook and its rehearsal record.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables. The seed hook reads the catalog through the owner and writes no row | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`. The version a service records is the one the client answered | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library. This story deploys that client into every chart | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case. The product-group codes the client resolves are reference rows of the owner | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents. The deployment fixes the consumer group and the topic ACL for the refresh event | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout. The read is one hop from the pod with the caller's breaker, and the seed hook uses the same path | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1`. Every path the chart and the runbook use is a `/api/recovery/case/v1` path | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library. The deployment subscribes to `rwb.case.events.v1` and creates no topic name of its own | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema. The run at service start carries the owner's catalog seed and each service's inbox table | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route. The panel and SCR-44 are read through the gateway; a value change has no screen of its own | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |

**Hardware and software change.** The deployment adds one pinned library to every service image, three chart values per environment, one pre-rollout hook and one readiness probe, and one panel with three alerts on the existing observability path. The catalog row load stays with the owner's Flyway sequence in `rwb_case`, so the deployment creates no table, no seed of its own and no database row. No new hardware is implied: the hook and the probes run in the existing AKS namespaces, and the metrics go to the platform the observability baseline already provides.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Pinned library version | Pipeline template value | One version for all 19 services, compared with the compiled version on every build (BR1) |
| `RWB_ENV`, `RWB_PARAMETER_CATALOG`, `RWB_PARAMETER_TTL_KEY` | Chart values | The environment name, the catalog file and the catalog entry that bounds the cache (BR2, BR3) |
| Bootstrap time to live and its drift check | Chart value and pipeline step | The value used before the first catalog answer, compared with `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds` at deployment (BR3) |
| `parameter-catalog-seed` hook | Helm hook, `pre-install,pre-upgrade`, weight -5 | Confirms every key of the catalog file with an owner and a default before the rollout (BR4) |
| Readiness probe | Chart probe | Reads the client's health check; a missing required value keeps the pod out of traffic with MSG-P3-032 (BR4) |
| Secret references | Chart values and pipeline variables | The key-store reference for each secret entry, and the scan that proves no credential (BR5) |
| Panel and three alerts | Observability assets | Cache age per key, refreshes, failed refreshes, start-up refusals; one page and two warnings (BR7) |
| Runbook and rehearsal record | Document | Load, approve, verify and rollback with the owner's operations, the role and the refusal message (BR6) |

**Build steps**

1. Add the pinned version to the pipeline template and the drift check against the compiled version; prove a mismatch fails the build (AC1).
2. Add the three chart values per environment and the bootstrap of the time to live with its comparison against the catalog entry (AC2).
3. Replace every secret value in the chart and the pipeline with a key-store reference and wire the scan (AC3).
4. Write the seed hook and run it before the rollout in SIT; prove that a missing key, owner or default fails the release (AC4).
5. Wire the readiness probe to the client's health check and prove the UAT case with MSG-P3-032 (AC4).
6. Add the panel and the three alerts and prove each one fires once, with the missing-value alert as the only page (AC5).
7. Write the runbook for load, approve, verify and rollback, with the owner's operations, the roles and the refusal messages (AC7).
8. Rehearse the library roll-forward and rollback, then the value version and its rollback in SIT, and record both (AC6).
9. Hand the release record and the alert routes to the platform administrator and the platform team.

**Done when.** The six test cases of section 16 pass in SIT, a drifted chart fails the build, a release with a missing required value fails before it serves, the three alerts fire in the rehearsal, and the runbook and its evidence are published.

The exact chart value names, the seed-job weight, the probe period and the alert thresholds are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1408; ASM-2455; ASM-2456); the names and the order above are the working read of this run.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-032 | A required parameter has no value at start-up, in the log and on the probe answer | Parameter {name} has no value for {environment}. The service did not start. |
| MSG-GEN-002 | A loaded value is outside its range, on the owner's load operation | {field} must be between {min} and {max}. |
| MSG-P1-002 | A loaded value has the wrong type or an unknown key, on the owner's load operation | The {source} load for {date} was refused: {check}. The previous load is still in use. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | The load file is empty, on the owner's load operation | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P7-002 | The approver is the author, on the owner's approval operation | You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it. |
| MSG-P3-015 | A rollback has no earlier version, on the owner's rollback operation | There is no earlier version of {table} to return to. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right calls an operation in the runbook | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

MSG-P3-032 is shown in the pod's log and on the probe answer, never to a business user; the other six are the owner's and appear in the runbook unchanged. The build findings of the pinned version and of the credential scan carry no message id: they name the service, the chart value and the compiled version, or the file and the line of the finding. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

No new screen. SCR-44 Interface and job monitor shows the release in state Running, Failed or Complete, with the service, the environment, the image, the chart values and the library version, and the platform administrator reruns a failed release from there. The client's panel shows cache age per key, refreshes, failed refreshes and start-up refusals per environment, and the three alerts route to the platform administrator and the platform team. A value change has no screen of its own in this story: SCR-39 Rules and parameters belongs to Epic 8, and until it exists the operator uses the owner's operations through the runbook (DP-19).

| TC-PLT-E1042-OPS-04 | AC4 | Component | A catalog file key with no owner fails the hook; UAT with no value for `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds` fails the probe with MSG-P3-032 and serves no traffic |
| TC-PLT-E1042-OPS-05 | AC5 | NFR | One missing value, one cache line past its time to live and one failed refresh; three alerts, one page, the panel shows each case |
| TC-PLT-E1042-OPS-06 | AC6, AC7 | Component | The library roll-forward and rollback; the value version 2 to 91 and its rollback to 90 for `case.entry.dpd`; the six-step runbook rehearsal recorded |

The levels are the deployment-side shape: the pipeline pieces are Contract, the chart and hook behaviour is Component, and the scan, the alerts and the cache age are NFR. The legacy test case ids are not reused here; they stay with RWB-P3-E1042-APP.

##### 17. Guardrails

- One library version for all 19 services, pinned in the template; a drift is a failed build and never a production discovery.
- No business value and no credential in a chart value, a pipeline file, an image layer, a log or a prompt; every secret is a key-store reference.
- No value in the catalog tables is written by the deployment: the row load is the owner's Flyway sequence in `rwb_case` (DP-01).
- No manual row update and no chart change to move a parameter value: a value changes through the runbook's load, approve, verify and rollback.
- No pod serves traffic without its required values for the environment; the probe reads the same check as the start-up.
- No alert without an owner: the missing-value alert pages the platform administrator, and the two cache alerts go to the platform team.
- No personal data in a release record, an alert or a log; the record holds the service, the environment, the versions and the times only.
- The library adds no REST base, no topic and no task queue of its own, and the deployment invents none for it.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: preserved from RWB-E1-042 word for word (sections 1 to 11, 14 to 16, 18 and 19), with the as-built contract and solution plan kept unchanged under "As built (monolith)" and sections 12, 13 and 17 written for rwb-case; the delta of this legacy key is the contract slice RWB-P3-E1042-CON. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **squad member (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **every environment setting and business parameter read from one configuration service and listed in a parameter catalog with name, type, default, owner, environment and where it is used**, so that **no value is hard-coded and every parameter has an owner**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Thresholds such as the 90-day entry point are written into code and spreadsheets today, so a change needs a release and nobody can say who owns a value. This story holds every parameter definition in a catalog with an owner and a default, holds business values as approved, dated versions per environment, serves them to every engine at run time, and fails the build when code carries a literal business value or reads a parameter the catalog does not list. It meets REQ-DRI-010 and puts Principle 1 (DT02) into the build pipeline.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-044 is done: the recovery schema exists in each environment.
- The catalog seed file `config/parameter-catalog.csv` is in the repository, owned by RW-COE, with the Epic 1 entries, including `case.entry.dpd` (default 90; DL16), `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds` (default 300; DL11) and `caselist.export.maxrows` (default 10000; DL11).
- The ACE secret store holds secrets per environment; the catalog lists them and never holds their values.
- Loaders hold Reference data C (RW-COE, RW-REFADM). Approvers hold Reference data A: the parameter owner, and RW-RISK where a threshold or a limit moves (assumed grant; DL01).
- The build pipeline runs the checks of this story on every pull request (DL37 code owners).

##### 4. Flow

1. Squad member: adds a parameter to `config/parameter-catalog.csv` with key, kind, type, unit, range, default, scope, required, owner role, environments and used by; the pull request is reviewed by the owner.
2. Build: generates the `ParameterKeys` class from the catalog file; code reads a value only through ParameterService with a generated key.
3. Build: runs the magic number check over the recovery packages and the catalog completeness check.
4. Flyway: loads the catalog rows and the default values into parameter_catalog and parameter_value at deployment.
5. RW-COE: loads a new value version through POST /admin/reference-loads with table "PARAMETER", for example `case.entry.dpd` = 91 in PROD valid from 2026-12-10.
6. ParameterLoadChecks: checks key in catalog, type, range, environment and required values; refuses the load whole on any failure.
7. Owner: approves through POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve; refused if the approver is the author.
8. ParameterService: from the valid from date returns the new value; every instance refreshes its cache on ParameterVersionApproved and at the latest after the cache time to live.
9. Engines: read values at run time with the version number, and record the version in their decision log inputs.
10. Any role with Rules and parameters R: reads the catalog and the values in force through GET /admin/parameters.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Code holds a literal business value | Build fails naming the file, the line and the parameter with that default | None (build output) | AC2 |
| X2 | Code reads a key that the catalog does not list | Build fails naming the key | None (build output) | AC3 |
| X3 | A required parameter has no value for the environment at start-up | The service does not start; the health check names the key | MSG-P3-032 | AC4 |
| X4 | A loaded value is outside its range | Load refused in full | MSG-GEN-002 | AC5 |
| X5 | A loaded value has the wrong type | Load refused in full | MSG-P1-002 | AC6 |
| X6 | The approver is the author | Approval refused | MSG-P7-002 | AC7 |
| X7 | A secret is asked for through the catalog read | The value is not returned | None | AC9 |
| X8 | Rollback of a value version | The previous version is in force | MSG-P3-015 when none exists | AC10 |
| X10 | A new version is approved before its valid from date | The current value stays until that date; no restart is needed | None | AC11 |
| X9 | A role without Rules and parameters R reads the catalog | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-E1-042-12 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs only the schema and migrations (RWB-E1-044); every later engine reads through it |
| Negotiable | The catalog columns and the build check rules can be tuned; the values are data |
| Valuable | No business value in code, and every parameter has an owner |
| Estimable | Two tables, one service, one load check, two build checks, one read endpoint |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Every criterion has a test case in section 16 |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Central configuration service and parameter catalog

  Background:
    Given the catalog lists "case.entry.dpd" as INTEGER, range 1 to 365, default 90, scope GLOBAL, required, owner RW-COE, used by "recovery.casewf.casecreation"

  Scenario: AC1 Parameter read at run time (legacy RWB-E1-042 AC1)
    Given the parameter "case.entry.dpd" set to 90 in PROD, version 1
    When the case service evaluates entry on 2026-12-01
    Then it uses 90 from the service, not a constant in code
    Then the entry decision records parameter version 1

  Scenario: AC2 Hard-coded value caught (legacy RWB-E1-042 AC2)
    Given code in package "recovery.casewf.casecreation" with a literal 90 in the entry rule
    When the lint rule for magic numbers runs in the build
    Then the build fails
    Then the output names the file, the line and the parameter "case.entry.dpd"

  Scenario: AC3 Catalog complete (legacy RWB-E1-042 AC3)
    Given the parameter catalog
    Given code that reads the key "allocation.retry.limit" which the catalog does not list
    When the pipeline compares the catalog with the parameters read by the services
    Then the build fails naming "allocation.retry.limit"
    Then every other parameter in use is in the catalog with an owner and a default

  Scenario: AC4 Required value missing at start-up (legacy RWB-E1-042 AC4)
    Given "refdata.cache.ttl-seconds" is required and has no value and no default for UAT
    When the service starts in UAT
    Then the health check fails with MSG-P3-032 for "refdata.cache.ttl-seconds" and "UAT"
    Then the service takes no traffic

  Scenario: AC5 Value outside its range (legacy RWB-E1-042 AC5)
    When RW-COE loads "case.entry.dpd" = 400 for PROD
    Then the system refuses the load with MSG-GEN-002 with minimum 1 and maximum 365

  Scenario: AC6 Wrong type (legacy RWB-E1-042 AC6)
    When RW-COE loads "case.entry.dpd" = "ninety" for PROD
    Then the system refuses the load with MSG-P1-002 and check "value is not INTEGER"

  Scenario: AC7 Author cannot approve (legacy RWB-E1-042 AC7)
    Given RW-COE user U-41 loaded value version 3
    When U-41 approves version 3
    Then the system refuses the approval with MSG-P7-002

  Scenario: AC8 Values per environment (legacy RWB-E1-042 AC8)
    Given "refdata.cache.ttl-seconds" is 30 in SIT and 300 in PROD
    When the reference data service reads it in SIT and in PROD
    Then SIT uses 30 and PROD uses 300

  Scenario: AC9 Secrets are listed, never served (legacy RWB-E1-042 AC9)
    Given the catalog lists "ace.db.password" as kind ENVIRONMENT with secret = true
    When GET /admin/parameters is called by RW-COE
    Then the entry shows owner, environments and used by
    Then the system returns no value for "ace.db.password"

  Scenario: AC10 Rollback of a value version (legacy RWB-E1-042 AC10)
    Given value version 2 of "case.entry.dpd" is in force and version 1 was in force before it
    When RW-COE calls rollback for version 2
    Then version 1 is in force and the service returns 90

  Scenario: AC11 A new value takes effect on its valid from date (legacy RWB-E1-042 AC11)
    Given version 2 sets "case.entry.dpd" to 91 for PROD with valid from 2026-12-10 and is approved on 2026-12-05
    When the case service evaluates entry on 2026-12-09 and on 2026-12-10
    Then it uses 90 on 2026-12-09 and 91 on 2026-12-10
    Then the system restarts no instance
```

These eleven criteria stay as written and every value in them is kept: no criterion carries a cross-service leg, because in the target the catalog, the value versions, the case engine and the reference-data reader all live in rwb-case, so no scenario needs a contract mock; where the legacy text says "the service" or "the reference data service" it is rwb-case itself. The two build checks of AC2 and AC3 run against the target packages of section 13, and the `used by` value "recovery.casewf.casecreation" is the legacy package name (GAP-2214; ASM-3641).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every value a business person may change is a parameter row with a version, never a constant in code | Principle 1; DT02; BR-P3-022 |
| BR2 | Every parameter in use has a catalog entry with owner, type, default, environments and used by | REQ-DRI-010 |
| BR3 | A business value changes only through a checked, approved, dated load | CTL-08; reference data change process |
| BR4 | The author of a load cannot approve it; Risk approves where a threshold or a limit moves | Separation of duty table; reference data change process, step 4 |
| BR5 | Open decisions keep the version they were taken under; new decisions use the version in force | R-UNI-38 |
| BR6 | Secrets are listed in the catalog and held only in the secret store | DL26; REQ-ACA-005 |
| BR7 | A service does not start without every required parameter for its environment | Principle 1 |

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It changes the status of a parameter value version: VALIDATED, APPROVED, ROLLED_BACK.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | Load | Every check passes | VALIDATED |
| VALIDATED | Approve | Approver is not the author | APPROVED; in force from valid from |
| APPROVED | Rollback | An earlier approved version exists | ROLLED_BACK |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-COE | Owns the catalog; loads value versions (Reference data C; Rules and parameters CRUD) |
| RW-RISK | Approves a value version where a threshold or a limit moves (Reference data A, assumed grant; DL01) |
| RW-PLATADM | Owns environment settings; reads the catalog (Rules and parameters R) |
| RW-TRIBE | Adds catalog entries through reviewed pull requests |
| Every role with Rules and parameters R | Reads the catalog |
| RW-PHONECOL | No Rules and parameters right; refused |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A parameter is not a credit decision |

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |
