These criteria are new and test only the contract deliverable: no legacy acceptance criterion is repeated here — AC1 to AC10 of RWB-E1-043 belong to RWB-P3-E1043-APP — and every number and identifier comes from the legacy story, the Ownership Map or Architecture v5, character for character.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The contract publishes three read methods and two records, and nothing else: `ReferenceDataClient`, `ReferenceVersion` and `VersionedRows` | RWB-E1-043 section 12; RWB-PLT-E1043-APP section 1 |
| BR2 | No repository, table, schema or connection type crosses a published signature: the client reads the owner's contract and holds no table | DP-01; Architecture v5 slide 29 |
| BR3 | The version in force is chosen from the caller's business date and the valid from and valid to dates, and the chosen version number travels in the answer | RWB-E1-043 section 8 BR3 (R-UNI-38) |
| BR4 | A missing approved version is the refusal `NoVersionInForceException` with MSG-P3-027, non-retryable, and never a default value | RWB-E1-043 section 8 BR9; Principle 5; NFR-033 |
| BR5 | The code set is the twelve LOV-REF-TABLE codes; a rule package code is not a reference table code and is refused | RWB-E1-043 section 8 BR1 and section 12; DP-04 |
| BR6 | The holiday calendar is not served: it is ACE data under `v_ace_holiday`, read by rwb-source-data (P1) | RWB-E1-043 section 2 and section 12; DP-05 |
| BR7 | The cache time to live is a catalog entry read through the parameters operation, never a code constant; the legacy value is 300 (assumed; DL11) | DP-06; RWB-E1-043 section 13 |
| BR8 | A version change reaches a consumer by cache expiry, because the legacy design publishes no event and this contract declares none | RWB-E1-043 section 12 |
| BR9 | The status vocabulary is VALIDATED, APPROVED and ROLLED_BACK, and only an APPROVED version is served | RWB-E1-043 section 9 and section 17 |
| BR10 | A breaking change raises a new version and deprecates v1; a published signature is never edited in place | Template and Rules §R7.2; §R5.4 class C |
| BR11 | The message identifier MSG-P3-027 is kept unchanged although the tables now sit with rwb-case | RWB-E1-043 section 14; ASM-2460 |

##### 9. State transitions

None in this story: a document has no runtime state. Two vocabularies are fixed here so that the two documents agree; the runtime behind them is specified in RWB-PLT-E1043-APP section 9.

| Object | State | Meaning in the contract |
|---|---|---|
| Cache entry of a read | ABSENT | No entry is held for that table code and business date |
| Cache entry of a read | CACHED | The approved version in force and its rows are held for the time to live |
| Cache entry of a read | EXPIRED | The time to live elapsed and the next read reloads |
| Cache entry of a read | EVICTED | The version was rolled back or the code was refused; the entry never serves a read |
| Reference version, owner states | VALIDATED, APPROVED, ROLLED_BACK | rwb-case's states; this contract reads only the one in force for a date |

The owner states are named here only so that the contract and the store agree on the vocabulary; the transitions among them and the effective dating are the business of RWB-P3-E1043-APP section 9.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The contract author (any team, per U3) | Writes and versions the interface document, the data contract, the code set, the refusal, the cache rule and the fakes |
| The platform owner of the library | Approves a breaking change and freezes a version |
| The service teams of the 19 services | Consume the contract, pin the version and raise a change request rather than a private variant |
| The rwb-case owner (P3) | Confirms the two operations, the version and row projection, the twelve codes and the status vocabulary |
| The rwb-decision owner (P7) | Confirms that rule packages and the registry are outside this contract |
| The rwb-source-data owner (P1) | Confirms the holiday-calendar exclusion and the `v_ace_holiday` read |
| RW-REFADM, RW-RISK, RW-COE | Load and approve values in rwb-case; have no right in the contract |
| RW-PLATADM | Receives the incident a caller raises when no version is in force |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A library contract is a technical artefact, not a credit decision |

No personal name, no email address and no credential appears in a document, a schema, an example or the fake. Where a caller must be named, the example uses the user identifier `U-REF-01` or a role code only.

##### 11. Data

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Business data published | None. The document publishes signatures, field identifiers, codes, status values and one message identifier; no customer, account, case or document value appears |
| Version projection | Table code, version number, valid from, valid to, status, author, approver, approved at, row count, content hash, load identifier |
| Row projection | Row key and row data, as the two row fields DF-REF-183 and DF-REF-184 carry them |
| Example values | EXPOSURE_BAND versions 3 and 4 with bands "E1" to "E5", QUEUE version 7, the content hash "a1b2" and the user identifiers "U-REF-01" and "U-RSK-01", all from the legacy story |
| Personal data | None. No name, no email address, no account number and no national identifier in a schema, an example or the fake |
| Tables published | None. The two reference tables stay with rwb-case (P3) and the rule tables with rwb-decision (P7); the contract declares no table and no migration |
| Field identifiers | DF-REF-159 to DF-REF-171 and DF-REF-181 to DF-REF-184, from the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary |
| Retention | None at the contract: a document keeps no data, and the fake holds only the examples it publishes |

The version projection is the one place where a value could leak into the contract, so the document fixes that the rows travel as row key and row data and that no rule content and no holiday row is part of the projection (Architecture v5 slides 27 and 29).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided
None. The library is a Java artefact: it publishes an interface and two records, not an OpenAPI document, and it has no REST base of its own. The reference read, the list read, the parameters read, the reference-load and the approve operations belong to rwb-case (P3); the reference data screens reach them through the gateway-bff composite route of RWB-PLT-N001-CON, which this contract names and does not declare (DP-19).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed
| Operation | Provider | Why the contract needs it | Pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode} | rwb-case (P3) | The list read with its versions: the twelve LOV-REF-TABLE codes, and for a table code the approved version in force with its rows | DP-07, DP-11 |
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters | rwb-case (P3) | The cache time to live as a catalog entry, so the bound is data and not a code constant | DP-06, DP-11 |

Two consumption rows, both one hop, with a 2 s timeout and a breaker per provider (Architecture v5 slide 11). The list operation reads a list with its versions, which is the legacy contract's own wording, so the version and rows of a table code arrive in that answer and no third call is needed. The cache-time-to-live catalog entry is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1410; ASM-2461); the legacy value 300 (assumed; DL11) is the default the document publishes and is read through this operation, never hard-coded.

###### 12.3 Events published
None. The library publishes no event and the legacy design publishes no event for a version change; the contract states it so that no consumer waits for one.

###### 12.4 Events consumed
None. The legacy design publishes no event for a version change and this contract declares none: a new approved version reaches a consumer at its next cache expiry. A later owner event would be consumed through the inbox library of RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, and the contract would then be raised to a new version.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities
None. The contract declares no workflow, no activity and no task queue: the client is called inside the caller's own activity or start-up hook on that service's queue `rwb-<short>`, and never from workflow code.

###### 12.6 Schedules
None. The contract declares no Schedule and no job; the refresh is the cache expiry of section 9, and no job of the legacy design belongs to the library.

###### 12.7 Tables owned
None. `reference_version`, `reference_row` and `lov_value` stay with rwb-case (P3) under the Ownership Map default ruling and are named here only as the source of the read; `rule_package`, `rule_package_version`, `rule_row` and `rule_test_case` stay with rwb-decision (P7) and are not named as a source at all. The document declares no table, no column and no migration, and no consumer of it may read a reference table or a rule table (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes
| Fake | Serves | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| Client fake (this story) | `ReferenceDataClient.rows`, `versionInForce` and `versions`, answered from the owner fakes below | RWB-PLT-E1043-APP, every service's read test and the integration harness |
| rwb-case reference-data fake (RWB-P3-E1043-CON) | The version and rows of the list operation | The version-in-force answer with EXPOSURE_BAND versions 3 and 4 and QUEUE version 7, and the no-version answer for TEAM on 2026-11-30 (AC1, AC3, AC6) |
| rwb-case list fake (RWB-P3-E1043-CON) | `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | The twelve codes, a rule package code that is absent from the list, and a 403 for a role without Reference data R (AC2, AC5) |
| rwb-case parameter fake (RWB-P3-E1042-CON) | `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | The cache time to live at 300, raised and missing (AC2, AC6) |
| Rules kit boundary fake (RWB-PLT-E1072-CON) | The kit's evaluator boundary | A call proving that no rule package code and no rule row reaches the client (AC5, AC6) |

The client fake answers from the owner fakes rather than from copied payloads, so a change in rwb-case shows up as a contract-test failure in every consuming service rather than as a surprise at run time.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary (REST, Kafka, Temporal, File)
| Call type | Provided | Consumed | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| REST | 0: the contract publishes interfaces, not operations | 2 operations over 1 provider | OpenAPI 3.1 at rwb-case, one hop, 2 s timeout, breaker per provider, GET only |
| Kafka | 0 published | 0 consumed | No event exists for a version change; the refresh is the cache expiry |
| Temporal | 0 | 0 | The client runs inside the caller's activity and owns no queue |
| File | 0 | 0 | A reference load file belongs to the reference data administrator and rwb-case; no file crosses this contract |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Shared library contract artefact of the platform, the interface and the records in `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.platform.refdata.api`, the document, the fakes and the drift test; the implementation is RWB-PLT-E1043-APP. The library is not one of the 19 services and declares no schema, topic, queue or REST base.

**Hardware and software change.** The contract records the move of the reference read from an in-process service call against a shared schema to a published library interface compiled into 19 services (Architecture v5 slides 20 and 29): the two tables stay in the existing ACE PostgreSQL server under the rwb_case login, the client keeps a small heap cache and one log line per table read, and no new hardware is implied. The software change is that a service no longer needs a grant on a reference table, and that the version number of every value an engine used is visible in its logs.

**Deliverables.** The interface document; the version and row data contract with the field identifiers; the operation rows; the code set with the two exclusions; the refusal section; the cache and TTL section; the client fake and the owner fakes it composes; the drift test and the lint rules.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables. The contract fixes that the client reads the owner's two tables through the rwb-case contract only | none; referred to, and the consuming story RWB-PLT-E1043-APP carries the dependency |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision. The registry stays with rwb-decision (P7) and the contract fixes that this client serves no rule table | referred to; the consuming story RWB-PLT-E1043-APP carries the dependency H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON and C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views. The contract fixes that the ACE views are read by rwb-source-data (P1) and never by this library | none; referred to, and the consuming story RWB-PLT-E1043-APP carries the dependency |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library. The cache time to live is a catalog entry of that contract | referred to; the consuming story RWB-PLT-E1043-APP carries the dependency H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case. This contract is that dependency for every other story, and it is built against the owner contract it documents | referred to; the consuming story RWB-PLT-E1043-APP carries the dependency H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Interface document | Document | The three methods, the two records, the checked refusal and the no-repository rule (AC1) |
| Version and row data contract | Document | The field identifiers, the status vocabulary and the projections (AC3) |
| Operation rows | Document | The two consumed operations, their owner, their projection and the timeout (AC2) |
| Code set | Document | The twelve LOV-REF-TABLE codes, the rule-package exclusion and the holiday exclusion (AC5) |
| Refusal section | Document | MSG-P3-027, the exception fields, the non-retryable rule and the caller's no-run rule (AC4) |
| Cache and TTL section | Document | One entry per read, the time to live from the catalog, the refresh by expiry (BR7, BR8) |
| Client fake and owner fakes | Test asset | The answers every consuming service builds and tests against (AC6) |
| Drift test and lint rules | Test asset | The assertions that fail a build on any difference from section 12 (AC1 to AC6) |

**Build steps**

1. Write the interface document with the three methods, the two records and the checked refusal, taken from the legacy published interface character for character (AC1).
2. Write the version and row data contract from DF-REF-159 to DF-REF-171 and DF-REF-181 to DF-REF-184, with the status vocabulary (AC3).
3. Write the operation rows for the list operation and the parameters operation, with their owner, their projection and the 2 s timeout (AC2).
4. Write the code set with the twelve codes, the rule-package exclusion and the holiday exclusion, each as a testable sentence (AC5).
5. Write the refusal section with MSG-P3-027, the exception fields and the no-run rule (AC4).
6. Write the cache and TTL section, with the time to live as a catalog entry and the refresh by expiry (BR7, BR8).
7. Add the lint rules: no repository or table type in a signature, a mandatory message identifier, the twelve codes asserted, the two exclusions asserted, and a personal-data scan over every example.
8. Generate the client fake over the three owner fakes and write the drift test that pins the signatures, the fields, the refusal and the message identifier.
9. Publish v1 to the contract registry, notify RWB-PLT-E1043-APP and the consuming services, and record the version each one pins.

**Done when.** The document validates, every lint rule passes, the fake answers the version-in-force and no-version cases and the two consumed operations, the drift test is green on the build of this story and in at least one consuming service, and v1 is recorded as the pinned version.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Published as |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-027 | No approved version of the table is in force for the caller's business date, or the code is not a reference table code | The {table} load was refused: {check}. Version {version} stays in force. | `NoVersionInForceException`, messageId MSG-P3-027, non-retryable in the caller |
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller holds no Reference data R right for the consumed list or parameters read | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | The caller's own 403; the contract requires the client to fail closed |

The two texts are the legacy ones, character for character, and Thai text for each follows decision DL10. The refusal keeps the message identifier MSG-P3-027 unchanged although the tables now sit with rwb-case; no source renumbers it, and renumbering would break every log line, data quality report and decision record that cites it (ASM-2460).

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story, and the contract declares none. The library has no user interface: it answers inside an activity or a start-up hook and the screens read the result through the owning service. The reference data screens SCR-39, SCR-40 and SCR-42 come in Epic 8 and read the tables through the gateway-bff composite route against the rwb-case contract; the screen is out of scope here. This story fixes the four cache-entry states of section 9 so that the app story's operability view has one vocabulary.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: table codes, versions, bands, limits and periods are rows of rwb-case, and the only number this document fixes is the documented default 300 of the cache time to live.
- No personal data in a schema, an example, a fake or a log: codes, user identifiers and role codes only, and the scan fails the build otherwise.
- No table and no migration in this contract: the reference tables are rwb-case's and the rule tables are rwb-decision's, and a consumer that reads either breaks DP-01.
- No repository, table, schema or connection type in a published signature; the interface is the whole surface.
- A missing version is a refusal with MSG-P3-027 and never a default value or a silent fallback.
- Only an APPROVED version is served; VALIDATED and ROLLED_BACK are named so that a consumer can never serve them.
- No rule package code is accepted and no holiday row is served; the rules kit and rwb-source-data are named as the owners of those reads.
- The contract is versioned: a breaking change raises v2 and deprecates v1 in place of editing v1.
- No event is invented for a version change; the refresh is the cache expiry, and an owner event would arrive through the inbox library and a new contract version.

##### 1. Story

As a **service developer**, I want **the reference-data client implemented in the platform library — the typed read of a table code for a business date that returns the approved version in force with its rows, a cache whose time to live is a catalog entry, one log line per table read with the table code and the version, a typed exception when no approved version applies so that an engine never runs on a missing or stale value, and the exclusions proved in code (no rule table is served, the holiday calendar is not served)** — so that **every engine reads a dated, approved value through one contract and can say which version it used, with no service reading another service's tables** (Template and Rules §R6, DP-07, DP-01).

This is the delta slice of legacy RWB-E1-043 for the platform shared libraries. The legacy story built the two versioned tables, the registry, the read service and the load and approve operations inside one module; this story keeps none of that and delivers only the client library that every service binds against the rwb-case owner contract. The conformance points of the legacy story are kept unchanged: the approved version with the latest valid from on or before the business date, the one log line per table read, no run on a missing or stale value, and no rule table in the reference set.

##### 2. Business rationale

Today the values that drive allocation, timers and approval limits live in team spreadsheets and in procedure documents, so nobody can say which value applied to a case on a given day. The reference data service answers that question, and after the realignment the answer has to cross a service boundary: the tables, the registry, the read service, the load and approve operations and the cache stay with rwb-case (P3), and each of the 19 services reads a value through a library instead of a shared schema.

**The division is fixed.** The two versioned tables `reference_version` and `reference_row`, the `ReferenceVersionRegistry` and its load and approve operations, the reference read service and its cache stay with **RWB-P3-E1043-APP** and **RWB-P3-E1043-CON**, and the legacy acceptance criteria AC1 to AC10 of RWB-E1-043 stay with RWB-P3-E1043-APP. This story and its contract **RWB-PLT-E1043-CON** deliver the reference-data client library that every service binds, so that a service reads a dated, approved version through one published contract and never reads another service's table (DP-01, DP-07; Architecture v5 slides 14, 20, 27 and 29).

That split is what makes the reference promise auditable across 19 services. "Every engine can say which version it used" only holds if the value arrives with its version number attached, if the version in force is derived from a business date the caller passes rather than from the system clock, and if a missing version is a refusal rather than a default. Writing that down once, in the client, is cheaper and safer than 19 readings of the same table.

The client also carries the two exclusions the target architecture depends on. Rule packages are Drools packages governed in rwb-decision (P7, DP-04) and are not reference tables, so the client refuses a rule package code; the Bank of Thailand holiday calendar is ACE data read through `v_ace_holiday` by rwb-source-data (P1, DP-05) and is not served here at all. The acceptance criteria below are new, tagged `(new, D-RCV-60)`, and test only this library deliverable: no legacy acceptance criterion is copied into this story.

It supports REQ-DRI-011 and REQ-CWC-006, and the logging rule REQ-CWC-016 that the legacy story cites: every engine logs the table code and the version of every table it reads.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-PLT-E1043-CON is published: the `ReferenceDataClient` interface, the `ReferenceVersion`, `VersionedRows` and `NoVersionInForceException` types, the two consumed operations, the twelve-code set and the fakes.
- RWB-PLT-E1042-CON is published: the parameters client library that reads the cache time to live from the catalog (DP-06).
- RWB-PLT-E1072-CON is published: the embedded rules kit contract, so the boundary between this client and the kit is a published contract and not a verbal agreement (DP-04).
- RWB-PLT-E1037-CON is published: the access guard library, so a permission failure on the consumed read is surfaced by the caller's guard and not by this client (DP-08).
- RWB-PLT-TE006-CON is published: the outbox and inbox library, which carries no reference event because the legacy design publishes none (DP-09).
- RWB-PLT-E1047-CON and RWB-PLT-E1044-CON are published: the naming library and the per-service Flyway baseline the library artefact follows (DP-14, DP-15).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the gateway-bff composite route under which the reference data screens read the tables; no screen is built here (DP-19).
- RWB-P3-E1043-CON is published: the rwb-case reference-data contract behind the read operation; RWB-P3-E1042-CON publishes the parameters operation behind the time to live.
- The list LOV-REF-TABLE is loaded with the twelve reference table codes of section 8 BR1. No rule table has a code in it, and the holiday calendar has no code in it.
- The business date of the calling service is set from the ACE batch record for the day (`v_ace_batch_status`) through the P1 contract; the client never reads the system clock for the business date.
- The cache time to live is the value the legacy story carries, `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds` = 300 (assumed; DL11). The catalog entry that now carries it is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1409; ASM-2458).
- The artefact coordinates of the library — the group and the artefact name it is published under — are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1409; ASM-2458) and come from the platform library baseline, not from this story.
- The three tests build against the contract fakes of section 12.8; no rwb-case instance has to be running.

##### 4. Flow

1. A service adds the library dependency and calls `ReferenceDataClient.rows(tableCode, businessDate)` in its engine start-up hook, passing the business date it received from `v_ace_batch_status` through the P1 contract.
2. The client checks the table code against the twelve codes the LOV-REF-TABLE list carries, read through `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` on rwb-case. A code outside the twelve is refused and never reaches the owner.
3. The client resolves the version in force: the APPROVED version of that table with the latest `valid_from` on or before the business date, taken from the version projection of the same list operation on rwb-case. The client reads no `reference_version` and no `reference_row` row of its own.
4. The client looks up its cache by table code and business date. A hit inside the time to live answers without a call to rwb-case.
5. On a miss the client reads the version with its rows, stores the entry with the time to live read from the parameters catalog through `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters`, and answers.
6. The client writes one `ReferenceVersionLogger` line per table read: the table code, the version number and the business date. The line carries no customer identifier and no row content.
7. If no approved version applies, the client throws `NoVersionInForceException(tableCode, businessDate)` carrying MSG-P3-027. The calling engine does not start its run and raises its own alert through its own story.
8. The caller receives rows only: a rule package code is refused as not a reference table (the kit owns rule packages), and the holiday calendar is not served at all — the working-day calculator reads `v_ace_holiday` through the P1 query.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The table code is not one of the twelve reference table codes | The client refuses the read before any call to rwb-case; nothing is cached and nothing is logged as a table read | MSG-P3-027 | AC6 |
| X2 | The code is a rule package code | The client refuses it as not a reference table and names the kit as the owner of rule packages; no rule table is read | MSG-P3-027 | AC6 |
| X3 | No approved version applies to the business date | `NoVersionInForceException` is thrown with the table code, the business date and MSG-P3-027; the caller's engine does not run | MSG-P3-027 | AC4 |
| X4 | Only a VALIDATED or a ROLLED_BACK version exists for the date | It is never served; the read resolves to the previous APPROVED version or refuses with the exception | MSG-P3-027 | AC8 |
| X5 | The cache entry passes its time to live while a new version is approved | The next read reloads from rwb-case and serves the new approved version; the stale entry is dropped | None | AC3 |
| X6 | A caller asks the client for the holiday calendar | The read is refused: the calendar is ACE data and is read from `v_ace_holiday` through the P1 query | MSG-P3-027 | AC7 |
| X7 | The consumed list or parameters read answers 403 for the caller | The read fails closed with the caller's own permission refusal; no cached value is served in place of the answer | MSG-P4-002 | AC3 |
| X8 | A version is rolled back after the cache was filled | The rolled-back version is never returned; the entry is dropped and the previous approved version is served | MSG-P3-027 | AC8 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against the library contract story and the platform contract stories; rwb-case is reached through its contract fake, so no other service has to be built first |
| Negotiable | The cache size, the log format around the three fixed fields and the fixture set are open; the read rule, the refusal, the code set and the log fields are fixed by the contract |
| Valuable | Gives all 19 services one dated, approved read of reference data on Day 1 and removes every private copy of a reference table from the service plans |
| Estimable | One published interface, three types, one cache, one logger, one code catalog, one fake |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test against the contract fakes of section 12.8 |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Reference-data client library

  Background:
    Given the business date is 2026-11-25
    Given the table "EXPOSURE_BAND" has version 3 approved with valid from 2026-11-30 and bands "E1" to "E4"
    Given user "U-REF-01" holds RW-REFADM and user "U-RSK-01" holds the approve right in Reference data

  Scenario: AC1 The read answers the version in force for the business date (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given "EXPOSURE_BAND" version 4 with bands "E1" to "E5" is approved with valid from 2026-12-01
    When the client reads rows("EXPOSURE_BAND", 2026-11-30)
    Then it returns version 3 with its 4 rows and version 4 is not served
    When the client reads rows("EXPOSURE_BAND", 2026-12-01)
    Then it returns version 4 with its 5 rows

  Scenario: AC2 A superseded version stays readable with its valid to (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given version 4 of "EXPOSURE_BAND" is approved with valid from 2026-12-01
    When the client reads versionInForce("EXPOSURE_BAND", 2026-11-30)
    Then the version 3 record carries its 4 rows, status APPROVED and valid to 2026-11-30
    When the client reads versions("EXPOSURE_BAND")
    Then both version 3 and version 4 are listed with their own valid from and valid to

  Scenario: AC3 The cache serves the approved version for its time to live (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given approved "QUEUE" version 7 is in force on the business date and the cache time to live is 300 seconds
    When the client reads "QUEUE" for 2026-11-30, again inside the time to live, and once more after it
    Then the second read answers from the cache with no call to rwb-case
    Then the third read reloads from rwb-case and serves the approved version in force at that moment
    Then a further approved version is picked up at the next expiry and not before

  Scenario: AC4 No version in force refuses the read and the caller does not run (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the table "TEAM" has no approved version with valid from on or before 2026-11-30
    When the client reads rows("TEAM", 2026-11-30)
    Then it throws NoVersionInForceException naming table "TEAM" and business date 2026-11-30
    Then the exception carries MSG-P3-027
    Then the calling engine does not start its run and raises its own alert

  Scenario: AC5 One log line per table read with the table code and the version (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given approved "QUEUE" version 7 is in force for business date 2026-11-30
    When the client reads "QUEUE" for 2026-11-30 twice inside the time to live
    Then exactly one ReferenceVersionLogger line is written for that table read
    Then the line carries the table code "QUEUE", the version number 7 and the business date 2026-11-30
    Then the line carries no customer identifier and no row content

  Scenario: AC6 A rule package code is refused as not a reference table (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a code that is a rule package code and not one of the twelve reference table codes
    When the client is asked to read it for 2026-11-30
    Then the read is refused with MSG-P3-027 and the code is named as a rule package code
    Then the client states that rule packages are governed by rwb-decision and served by the rules kit
    Then no rule table is read and no reference table is cached

  Scenario: AC7 The holiday calendar is not served by the client (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the working-day calculator needs the Bank of Thailand holiday calendar for business date 2026-11-30
    When the client is asked for the holiday calendar
    Then it is refused as not a reference table, because the calendar is ACE data
    Then the working-day calculator reads v_ace_holiday through the P1 query instead
    Then no holiday row is cached and no holiday table code exists in LOV-REF-TABLE

  Scenario: AC8 Only a version that is APPROVED is ever served (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a "LEGAL_PERIOD" version with status "VALIDATED" and valid from 2026-12-01
    And a "REGION" version 5 with status "ROLLED_BACK"
    When the client reads "LEGAL_PERIOD" for 2026-12-01 and "REGION" for 2026-11-30
    Then the VALIDATED version is not served and the approved version in force is returned
    Then the ROLLED_BACK version 5 is never returned and the previous approved version is served
    Then the cache holds no entry for a version that is not APPROVED
```

These criteria are new and test only the library deliverable in the title. No legacy acceptance criterion is repeated here: AC1 to AC10 of RWB-E1-043 stay with RWB-P3-E1043-APP, which owns the two tables, the registry, the read service and the load and approve operations. Every number and identifier in the criteria above is the one the legacy story carries, character for character.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The client serves the twelve reference table codes only: PRODUCT, REGION, EXPOSURE_BAND, ROLE, TEAM, QUEUE, SERVICE_LEVEL, DOCUMENT_TYPE, TEMPLATE, DELEGATION_LIMIT, LEGAL_PERIOD and PRODUCT_PARAMETER. The list is data and changes by a load of LOV-REF-TABLE | RWB-E1-043 section 8 BR1; REQ-DRI-011 |
| BR2 | The version in force on a business date is the APPROVED version with the latest valid from on or before that date, and the business date comes from the caller, never from the system clock | RWB-E1-043 section 8 BR3 (R-UNI-38) |
| BR3 | A version that is not APPROVED is never served, and a version that is ROLLED_BACK is never returned | RWB-E1-043 section 17 (the cache never serves a version that is not APPROVED) |
| BR4 | Every engine logs the table code and the version of every table it reads, one line per table read, with the business date and no customer identifier | RWB-E1-043 section 8 BR7; REQ-CWC-016 |
| BR5 | An engine that finds no version in force for a table it needs does not run on stale or missing values: the client throws and the caller stops | RWB-E1-043 section 8 BR9; Principle 5; NFR-033 |
| BR6 | The cache time to live is a catalog entry read through the parameters client, never a code constant; the value the legacy story carries is 300 (assumed; DL11) | DP-06; RWB-E1-043 section 13 |
| BR7 | A rule package is not a reference table: the client refuses a rule package code, and rule packages are governed in rwb-decision and evaluated through the rules kit | RWB-E1-043 section 12 and section 17; DP-04 |
| BR8 | The holiday calendar is not reference data: it is ACE data read from `v_ace_holiday` through the P1 query, and the client serves none of it | RWB-E1-043 section 2 and section 12; DP-05 |
| BR9 | The client reads only the rwb-case contract: it holds no table, writes no row and reads no other service's schema | DP-01; Ownership Map (`reference_version`, `reference_row` and `lov_value` are P3) |
| BR10 | The codes, the status vocabulary and the messages are those of the owner contract: the client adds no code, no status and no message of its own | RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; RWB-E1-043 sections 9 and 14 |

##### 9. State transitions

No reference version changes its status in this story: VALIDATED, APPROVED and ROLLED_BACK are the owner's states and move only through the load and approve operations of RWB-P3-E1043-APP. The client holds one state per cache entry.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| ABSENT | A read for a table code and business date | The owner answers an APPROVED version | CACHED |
| ABSENT | A read for a table code and business date | The owner answers no approved version | ABSENT; `NoVersionInForceException` thrown |
| CACHED | A read inside the time to live | None | CACHED, answered without a call |
| CACHED | The time to live elapses | None | EXPIRED |
| EXPIRED | The next read | The owner answers an APPROVED version | CACHED, replaced in place |
| CACHED or EXPIRED | The owner reports the version rolled back | None | EVICTED; the previous approved version is resolved |
| ANY | A code outside the twelve | None | ABSENT; the read is refused before any call |

The statuses of the reference version itself — VALIDATED, APPROVED, ROLLED_BACK — are named here so that the two documents agree on the vocabulary; the transitions among them are the business of RWB-P3-E1043-APP section 9.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The service developer of any of the 19 services | Binds the library, calls the read with its own business date and its own table codes, and reads the version it was given |
| The platform library team, owning the artefact | Publishes the interface and the types, changes them only through RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, and owns the cache, the logger and the code catalog |
| The rwb-case owner (P3) | Owns the two tables, the registry, the read service and the load and approve operations behind the consumed operations |
| The rwb-decision owner (P7) | Owns the rule packages and the registry the client refuses to serve |
| RW-COE, RW-REFADM | Load and approve the values in rwb-case; have no right in the library |
| RW-PLATADM | Receives the incident a caller raises when no version is in force |
| No delegation of authority level applies | The library takes no business decision and approves nothing |

No personal name, no email address and no credential appears in a document, a fixture or a log line. Where a caller must be named, the example uses the user identifier `U-REF-01` or a role code only.

| DF-REF-160 | reference_version | table_code | Read, through the rwb-case contract |
| DF-REF-161 | reference_version | version_no | Read, through the rwb-case contract |
| DF-REF-163 | reference_version | valid_from | Read, through the rwb-case contract |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary. The client writes no reference field and holds no table: `reference_version`, `reference_row` and `lov_value` are rwb-case's under the Ownership Map, and the load and approve fields DF-REF-159, DF-REF-166, DF-REF-167, DF-REF-168, DF-REF-170, DF-REF-171, DF-REF-181 and DF-REF-182 are written by RWB-P3-E1043-APP and not read here beyond the projection above. This story reads and writes no rule table and no rule field: `rule_package`, `rule_package_version`, `rule_row` and `rule_test_case` are rwb-decision's and belong to RWB-P7-E1073 and the kit contract RWB-PLT-E1072-CON.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None — the library publishes Java types, not operations. The reference read, the list read, the parameters read, the reference-load and the approve operations belong to rwb-case (P3) in the Ownership Map, and the library adds no path, no topic and no task queue of its own.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Provider | Why the client needs it | Pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode} | rwb-case (P3) | The LOV-REF-TABLE code set, so the twelve table codes are data and a rule package code is never in the set | DP-07, DP-11 |
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters | rwb-case (P3) | The cache time to live as a catalog entry, so the bound is data and not a code constant | DP-06, DP-11 |

Two consumption rows, both one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker per provider (Architecture v5 slide 11). The list operation reads a list with its versions, as the legacy contract states, so the approved version in force and its rows arrive in that answer and the client makes no third call. The catalog key that carries the time to live is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1409; ASM-2458); the legacy value 300 (assumed; DL11) is read through this operation and never hard-coded.

###### 12.3 Events published

None — the legacy design publishes no event for a version change and this story adds none. No message is written to the outbox by the client, and the outbox library of RWB-PLT-TE006-CON carries no reference event.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None — no event is published for a version change, so none is consumed. A new approved version reaches a consumer at its next cache expiry, which is the read behaviour the legacy story carried; a later owner event would be consumed through the inbox library of RWB-PLT-TE006-CON.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None — the client runs inside the caller's own activity or start-up hook, on the caller's own queue `rwb-<short>`. It starts no workflow, owns no task queue and is never called from workflow code, so a replay reuses the recorded answer.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None — the client owns no Schedule and no job. The refresh is the cache expiry of section 9, not a Temporal Schedule, and no job of the legacy design belongs to the library.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. `reference_version`, `reference_row` and `lov_value` stay with rwb-case (P3) under the Ownership Map default ruling and are named here only as the source of the read; `rule_package`, `rule_package_version`, `rule_row` and `rule_test_case` stay with rwb-decision (P7) and are not read at all. The library holds no table, no migration and no schema of its own, and the boundary test of section 13 fails the build on any read of those tables from the library (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| Reference-data client fake (RWB-PLT-E1043-CON) | `ReferenceDataClient.rows`, `versionInForce` and `versions` | A version-in-force answer with EXPOSURE_BAND version 3 and version 4, and a no-version answer for TEAM on 2026-11-30 (AC1, AC2, AC4, AC8) |
| rwb-case reference-data fake (RWB-P3-E1043-CON) | The version-and-rows read behind the client | QUEUE version 7 in force, a clock the test moves past the time to live, and a rollback of REGION version 5 (AC3, AC5, AC8) |
| rwb-case list fake (RWB-P3-E1043-CON) | `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | The twelve LOV-REF-TABLE codes, a rule package code that is absent from the list, and a 403 for a role without Reference data R (AC6, X7) |
| rwb-case parameter fake (RWB-P3-E1042-CON) | `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | The cache time to live at 300, raised and missing (AC3) |
| Rules kit boundary fake (RWB-PLT-E1072-CON) | The kit's `RuleEvaluator` boundary | A call proving that no rule package code and no rule row reaches the client (AC6) |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | None provided; two consumed operations over one provider | OpenAPI 3.1 at rwb-case, one hop, 2 s timeout, breaker per provider, GET only |
| Kafka | None published and none consumed | No event exists for a version change; the refresh is the cache expiry |
| Temporal | None | The client runs inside the caller's activity; it owns no queue, no workflow and no Schedule |
| File | None | A reference load file is handled by rwb-case and the reference data administrator; the library reads no file |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Shared library artefact of the platform, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.platform.refdata`, with the published interface and the three types in `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.platform.refdata.api`. The library is not one of the 19 services: it has no schema, no topic, no task queue and no REST base.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables. The client reads the two reference tables only through the rwb-case contract and holds none of them | none |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision. The rule registry stays with rwb-decision (P7) and this client serves no rule table, so a rule package code is refused | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views. The ACE views are read by rwb-source-data (P1) and never by this library, so the holiday calendar reaches a caller through the P1 query and not through the client | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library. The cache time to live is a catalog entry read through the parameters client | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case. This story is that client library, so the row adds no dependency beyond the owner contract it is built against | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library. A permission failure on the consumed read is surfaced by the caller's guard, and the client fails closed | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents. The client publishes no event for a version change and uses the library for nothing | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout. The legacy in-process `ReferenceDataService` becomes the rwb-case REST contract and its fake | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1`. The library adds no path; the two consumed paths are rwb-case's under `/api/recovery/case/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library. The library has no topic of its own and follows the naming rule for the caller's queue name only | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema. The library carries no migration; the consuming service applies its own baseline through the sequence | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route. The reference data screens read the tables through gateway-bff and Epic 8; the client adds no route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Hardware and software change.** The client moves the reference read from an in-process service call against a shared schema to a library call against the rwb-case contract, compiled into 19 services on the existing AKS cluster. No new hardware is implied: the tables stay in the existing ACE PostgreSQL server under the rwb_case login and the cache lives in each service's own heap. The software change is the loss of every private copy of a reference table from the service plans, the loss of any read of `reference_version` or `reference_row` outside rwb-case, and one log line per table read in place of an untraceable value.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `ReferenceDataClient` | Published interface | `rows`, `versionInForce` and `versions`; the only way a service reads a reference table (BR2) |
| ReferenceDataClientImpl | Service | Checks the table code, resolves the version in force through the owner contract, answers from the cache, throws the refusal (BR1, BR2, BR5) |
| ReferenceVersionCache | Service | Cache keyed by table code and business date; the time to live is read through the parameters client (BR6) |
| ReferenceVersionLogger | Service | One line per table read with the table code, the version number and the business date, and no customer identifier (BR4) |
| ReferenceTableCatalog | Service | The twelve reference table codes from LOV-REF-TABLE; refuses any other code, including a rule package code (BR1, BR7) |
| `ReferenceVersion`, `VersionedRows`, `NoVersionInForceException` | Published type | The records and the typed refusal the contract publishes; the exception carries MSG-P3-027 |
| Client fake and fixtures | Test asset | Version-in-force, no-version, cache-expiry and rollback answers used by every consuming service's tests (AC1 to AC8) |

**Configuration and reference data.** The cache time to live is the catalog entry the legacy story names, `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds`, with 300 as the legacy value (assumed; DL11); the catalogue entry identifier itself is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1409; ASM-2458). LOV-REF-TABLE carries the twelve codes and is loaded by the reference data administrator through RWB-P3-E1043-APP. The first approved version of each of the twelve tables is loaded by the reference data administrator and approved by RW-RISK before SIT, as legacy section 13 states. The library itself is configured with no business value.

**Build steps**

1. Publish the interface and the three types from RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and compile a sample service against them; assert that no method opens a transaction and no method writes a row.
2. Write `ReferenceTableCatalog` over the list operation; assert the twelve codes, the absence of a rule package code and the refusal (AC6).
3. Write the version-resolution read through the owner contract with a fixed business date parameter; assert version 3 for 2026-11-30 and version 4 for 2026-12-01 (AC1, AC2).
4. Write `ReferenceVersionCache` with the time to live read through the parameters client; assert the hit, the expiry and the refresh (AC3).
5. Write the refusal path: `NoVersionInForceException` with the table code, the business date and MSG-P3-027, and the caller's contract test proving the engine does not start (AC4).
6. Write `ReferenceVersionLogger` and call it once per table read; assert the three fields and the absence of a customer identifier (AC5).
7. Prove the two exclusions in code: the holiday calendar is refused and read from `v_ace_holiday` through the P1 query, and the kit boundary shows no rule row reaching the client (AC6, AC7).
8. Prove the status filter: a VALIDATED version is not served and a ROLLED_BACK version is never returned (AC8).
9. Wire the fakes into a contract test and run it in the build of every consuming service, failing on any drift from RWB-PLT-E1043-CON.

**Feature flag.** One flag per consuming service, read as a parameter; off, the engine reads the value the service used before the library existed, and the library itself is always built.

**Done when.** The seven criteria pass, the contract tests of RWB-PLT-E1043-CON pass against the fakes, the boundary test shows no read of `reference_version`, `reference_row` or `lov_value` from outside rwb-case, a smoke run shows one log line for each of the twelve table codes, and no rule table and no holiday row is served. The artefact is published under the coordinates of the platform library baseline (GAP-1409; ASM-2458).

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Published as |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-027 | No approved version applies to the table and the business date, or the code is not a reference table | The {table} load was refused: {check}. Version {version} stays in force. | `NoVersionInForceException`, messageId MSG-P3-027, non-retryable in the caller |
| MSG-P4-002 | A caller without Reference data R reads the list or the parameters catalog | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | The caller's own 403; the client fails closed and serves no cached value |

The two texts are the legacy ones, character for character, and Thai text for each follows decision DL10. The refusal keeps the message identifier MSG-P3-027 although the tables now sit with rwb-case and the governance of a value is the owner's; no source renumbers it, and renumbering would break every log line and every decision record that cites it. In MSG-P3-027 the {table} placeholder carries the table code and, for the refusal this client raises, {check} names the check that failed and {version} names the version that stays in force.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story, and the client adds no route to any screen (DP-19). The reference data screens SCR-39, SCR-40 and SCR-42 come in Epic 8 and read the tables through gateway-bff against the rwb-case contract; the loader holds RW-REFADM and the approver holds the approve right in Reference data, unchanged from legacy section 10. The client shows nothing to a user: it either answers the version in force with its rows, or refuses with MSG-P3-027 and leaves the caller to raise its own alert.

| TC ID | Covers | Level | Data |
|---|---|---|---|
| TC-PLT-E1043-APP-01 | AC1 | Component | EXPOSURE_BAND versions 3 and 4; reads for 2026-11-30 and 2026-12-01 against the client fake and the rwb-case reference-data fake |
| TC-PLT-E1043-APP-02 | AC2 | Component | versionInForce and versions for EXPOSURE_BAND after version 4 is approved; version 3 keeps its 4 rows and valid to 2026-11-30 |
| TC-PLT-E1043-APP-03 | AC3 | Component | QUEUE version 7, time to live 300 from the parameters fake, a moved clock and a second approved version |
| TC-PLT-E1043-APP-04 | AC4 | Component | TEAM with no approved version on 2026-11-30; the exception fields and MSG-P3-027; the caller's engine does not start |
| TC-PLT-E1043-APP-05 | AC5 | NFR | Two reads of QUEUE version 7 inside the time to live; the captured log line holds the table code, the version and the date and no customer identifier |

The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is carried into the next Test Cases version under the same id. The legacy set TC-E1-043-01 to TC-E1-043-11 is executed by RWB-P3-E1043-APP and is not copied here.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: table codes, versions, bands, limits and periods are rows, and the code holds only the versioning and read behaviour.
- No personal data in logs, fixtures, tests or prompts: a log line carries the table code, the version number and the business date, and nothing else.
- No read of another service's tables: `reference_version`, `reference_row` and `lov_value` are read through the rwb-case contract only, and the boundary test fails the build otherwise (DP-01).
- The cache never serves a version that is not APPROVED, and a rolled-back version is never returned.
- A missing version is a refusal with MSG-P3-027, never a default value and never a silent fallback to an older version.
- No rule table is read, loaded or versioned by the library, and no rule package code is accepted; rule packages are Drools packages of rwb-decision and the rules kit (DP-04).
- No holiday row is read or cached by the library: the calendar is ACE data under `v_ace_holiday` and reaches a caller through rwb-source-data (DP-05).
- The time to live is a catalog entry read through the parameters client, never a constant in the code.
- The library writes no row, opens no transaction and starts no workflow; a replay of the caller's activity reuses the recorded answer.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: preserved from RWB-E1-043 word for word, with sections 1 to 11, 14 to 16, 18 and 19 verbatim (only the heading level and the test-case level vocabulary of section 16 in the target form) and the as-built contract and solution plan unchanged under "As built (monolith)", the target reading of sections 3, 8 and 11 and the target traceability additions for REQ-CWC-016 and ADR-012 carried in section 13, sections 12, 13 and 17 written for the target, and the microservice delta in RWB-P3-E1043-CON. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **reference data administrator (RW-REFADM)**, I want **products, regions, exposure bands, roles, teams, queues, service levels, document types, templates, delegation of authority and legal periods held as versioned reference data with valid from, valid to, author and approver**, so that **business values change by a data release and not by code, and every engine can say which version it used**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Today the values that drive allocation, timers and approval limits live in team spreadsheets and in procedure documents, so nobody can say which value applied to a case on a given day. This story gives every reference table a version with a valid from date, an author and a different approver, and serves the version in force to the engines. The holiday calendar is not one of them: ACE holds the Bank of Thailand calendar in `bot_holiday`, and the timer engine reads it through `v_ace_holiday`, so no Workbench list holds holidays and no holiday load is needed. It meets REQ-DRI-011 and REQ-CWC-006 and supports control CTL-08 (a rule, limit or list changes only through a validated load approved by its owner). The measure is that every value an engine reads carries a table code and a version number in its log line.

Rule tables are not reference tables any more. The reference data service holds reference tables only, and the rule packages are Drools packages that RWB-E1-072 evaluates and RWB-E1-073 loads, approves and rolls back (D-RCV-36 T3, T4, T8; ADR-012).

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-E1-044 is done: Flyway migrations run with the schema name taken from a parameter.
- RWB-E1-042 is done: the configuration service serves `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds` (assumed 300; DL11) and the list of reference table codes.
- The list LOV-REF-TABLE (new, see Additions) is loaded with the 12 reference table codes in section 8, BR1. No rule table has a code in it.
- The reference load endpoint `POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads` (P4) is deployed and calls this story's published interface.
- The loader holds RW-REFADM (Reference data C). The approver holds the approve right in Reference data (assumed RW-RISK; see section 10).
- The business date of the ACE service is set from the ACE batch record for the day (v_ace_batch_status).

##### 4. Flow

1. Reference data administrator: uploads a load file for one table code with a valid from date through `POST /admin/reference-loads`.
2. P4 load handler: passes the file rows, the table code, the valid from date and the caller's user ID to `ReferenceVersionRegistry.recordVersion(...)`.
3. Reference data service: checks the table code, the row schema for that table, the row keys, the valid from date and the author; computes the content hash and the next version number.
4. Reference data service: writes one `reference_version` row with status VALIDATED and one `reference_row` row per file row, in one transaction.
5. Approver: approves the load through `POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve`.
6. Reference data service: checks that the approver is present, is not the author and holds the approve right; sets status APPROVED, `approver_user_id` and `approved_at`.
7. Reference data service: sets `valid_to` of the version it replaces to the day before the new valid from date.
8. Case service, allocation engine and timer engine: on start and on each cache expiry, call `ReferenceDataService.rows(tableCode, businessDate)` and receive the approved version whose valid from is the latest on or before the business date.
9. Each engine: writes one log line per table read, with the table code, the version number and the business date.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Approval attempted with no approver, or by the author | The version stays VALIDATED and is never served | MSG-P7-002 | AC2, AC5 |
| X2 | A row fails the schema or key check for its table | The load is refused in full; no version is written | MSG-P3-027 | AC4 |
| X3 | The valid from date is before the business date | The load is refused in full | MSG-P3-027 | AC6 |
| X4 | The same file is loaded twice for the same table and valid from date | No second version; the first load is returned | None | AC7 |
| X5 | Two approvals of the same load arrive at the same time | One succeeds; the other is refused | MSG-GEN-004 | AC8 |
| X6 | No approved version is in force for a table on the business date | The engine does not start its run and raises an alert to the platform administrator | MSG-P3-027 | AC9 |
| X7 | The load file is empty | The load is refused in full | MSG-GEN-001 | AC10 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs only the migration tool (RWB-E1-044) and the configuration service (RWB-E1-042). The P4 load endpoint calls this story's interface |
| Negotiable | The list of table codes is data (LOV-REF-TABLE). The story fixes the versioning behavior, not the tables |
| Valuable | Every later timer and approval reads a dated, approved value instead of a spreadsheet |
| Estimable | Two tables, one registry service, one read service, one cache |
| Small | Fits in two weeks with its tests; no screen |
| Testable | Every criterion below is one automated test against a PostgreSQL test container |

The ten criteria are the legacy ones, copied with their values unchanged. Four of them name a cross-service answer that the story cannot obtain on its own; those criteria carry one added `Given` line for the rwb-access contract mock (the approve right) or the rwb-source-data contract mock (the holiday calendar of `v_ace_holiday`), and no value already in the criterion is changed (DP-05, DP-08, DP-11).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The reference tables served are PRODUCT, REGION, EXPOSURE_BAND, ROLE, TEAM, QUEUE, SERVICE_LEVEL, DOCUMENT_TYPE, TEMPLATE, DELEGATION_LIMIT, LEGAL_PERIOD and PRODUCT_PARAMETER. The list is data and changes by a load of LOV-REF-TABLE. Rule tables are not reference tables and have no code in LOV-REF-TABLE. The holiday calendar is not among them; it is read from v_ace_holiday | Principle 1; REQ-DRI-011; refdata.txt Reference tables; RWB-E1-069 |
| BR2 | Each load creates one version, numbered one above the highest version of that table. A version is never changed after it is written | ADR-012; refdata.txt Change process step 5 |
| BR3 | The version in force on a business date is the approved version with the latest valid from on or before that date | R-UNI-38 |
| BR4 | A version takes effect only after an approver who is not the author approves it | CTL-08; roles.txt Separation of duty (Reference data administrator and Risk and model risk officer) |
| BR5 | A load with any failed check is refused in full | refdata.txt Change process step 3; CTL-02 |
| BR6 | A valid from date before the current business date is refused. Open cases keep the version they were decided under | R-UNI-38 |
| BR7 | Every engine logs the table code and version of every table it reads | REQ-CWC-016; ADR-012 |
| BR8 | Approving a new version sets the valid to of the version it replaces to the day before the new valid from | refdata.txt Key (Valid from) |
| BR9 | An engine that finds no version in force for a table it needs does not run on stale or missing values | Principle 5; NFR-033 |

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It moves a reference version through these statuses (field `reference_version.status`, new):

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | Load received | Every check passes | VALIDATED |
| None | Load received | Any check fails | Not written; load refused |
| VALIDATED | Approval | Approver present, not the author, holds the approve right | APPROVED |
| APPROVED | Rollback of a reference table by the same call; rule packages roll back through RWB-E1-073 | A later version is rolled back | ROLLED_BACK |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | Loads a version (Reference data C). Reads versions (R) |
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Loads a version of the tables it owns (Reference data C) |
| RW-RISK, risk and model risk officer | Approves a version. Assumed: RW-RISK holds the approve right in Reference data, because no role holds it in the permission matrix today. The permission matrix change is loaded through RWB-E1-037; holders by name follow DL18 |
| SY-CASEWF, case workflow module | Reads the version in force (Reference data R) |
| SY-RULES, Drools evaluator | Reads reference values as Drools facts during an evaluation (Reference data R) |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Reads versions and their author and approver (Reference data R) |

The same person may not hold RW-REFADM and RW-RISK (separation of duty table). Approval of DELEGATION_LIMIT follows doa.txt How it applies, rule 11: a change is a data load approved by Risk.

##### 12. Contract

The shapes below are the contract of record of RWB-P3-E1043-CON. This story implements them under the rwb-case base `/api/recovery/case/v1` with the schema `rwb_case` (DP-13, DP-15), and the as-built form of the three endpoints is kept under "As built (monolith)" section 12.

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

| Operation | Request | Answer | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}?asOf=YYYY-MM-DD` | Path list code, for example LOV-REF-TABLE; optional `asOf` business date | The list with its versions; for a reference table code the approved version in force on the date with its rows | P3 |
| `POST /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads` | `multipart/form-data`: `file`, `table`, `validFrom`; `Idempotency-Key` | 201 with the load id, table, valid from, status VALIDATED and row count | P3 |
| `POST /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/verify` | Path load id; verifier and note | The check result per row and column of the validated load | P3 |
| `POST /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve` | Path load id | 200 with the approved load and its approver and approval time | P3 |
| `POST /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/rollback` | Path load id; reason | The version returned to ROLLED_BACK and the version in force for the business date | P3 |

A read with no approved version in force for the requested date is refused rather than answered from the latest version: the refusal names the table code and the business date and carries MSG-P3-027 (GAP-0698; ASM-1245).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Provider | Use in this story | Pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | The Reference data C, U and A right of a load, a verify, an approval and a rollback | DP-08, DP-11 |
| `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/doa-limits` | P4 rwb-access | The delegation limit a caller needs; this service holds no DoA table | DP-08, DP-11 |
| `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | P3 rwb-case (RWB-P3-E1042-CON) | `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds` and the list of reference table codes | DP-06, DP-11 |

Every call is one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker per provider (DP-11, ADR-020).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The Arch v5 catalogue gives rwb-case the topic `rwb.case.events.v1` with CaseCreated, CaseAllocated, CaseAllocationFailed, CaseTransferred, CaseStateChanged and TimerBreached, and a reference version carries no event of its own (Architecture v5 slide 14); a consumer sees a new version at its next cache expiry.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. No source declares an event for a version change, and the cache refresh is the expiry of `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds`. An owner event, were one added later, would arrive through the inbox library of RWB-PLT-TE006-CON (DP-09) and would raise a new contract version.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. A load, a verify, an approval and a rollback are one synchronous transaction each, and a read is a cached read; neither runs in a Temporal workflow or activity on the `rwb-case` queue, and no engine start-up hook is a workflow.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. There is no Schedule and no job: the refresh is the cache expiry and the loads are operator actions. The 00:01 rule promotion and the six-monthly access review belong to other owners.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Schema | Key and indexes | Owner | Rows exposed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| reference_version | rwb_case | PK id; unique on table_code and version_no; unique on table_code, valid_from and content_hash; partial unique index on table_code, valid_from where status is APPROVED | P3 | The load, verify, approve and rollback answers; the version list of the list read |
| reference_row | rwb_case | PK id; version_id to reference_version; unique on version_id and row_key | P3 | The rows of the version in force in the list read |
| lov_value | rwb_case | PK id; unique on lov_code and value_code | P3 | The list read of a LOV code |

`delegation_limit` is not in this list and not in this schema: it is the P4 rwb-access DoA table (ASM-0070). No rule table is held here (DP-01, DP-04).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-access contract fake | `POST /authorise` granting Reference data C, U and A to RW-REFADM and RW-RISK and refusing RW-CASEOWN with MSG-P4-002; `GET /doa-limits` with the DoA rows | This story's right checks and the approval refusal of AC2 and AC8 |
| rwb-case parameters fake (RWB-P3-E1042-CON) | `GET /admin/parameters` with `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds` at 300 and the twelve table codes | The cache and the code check |
| rwb-source-data contract fake | The `v_ace_holiday` answer for a business date | AC3 |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary (REST, Kafka, Temporal, File)

| Call type | Provided | Consumed | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| REST | 5 operations under `/api/recovery/case/v1` | 3 operations over 2 providers | OpenAPI 3.1, one hop, 2 s timeout, `Idempotency-Key` on every POST |
| Kafka | 0 | 0 | No event exists for a version change; the topic of the service is the case life cycle |
| Temporal | 0 | 0 | The load and the read are synchronous; no activity is registered |
| File | 0 | 1 | The load file (CSV or XLSX, one sheet) arrives on the load operation; no runtime file exchange |

##### 13. Solution plan

**As-built component set unchanged.** The eight components of the as-built plan stay as built: `ReferenceVersionRegistryImpl`, `ReferenceDataServiceImpl`, `ReferenceRowCache`, `ReferenceVersionRepository`, `ReferenceRowRepository`, `ReferenceVersionEntity`, `ReferenceRowEntity` and `ReferenceVersionLogger`, with the published interfaces `ReferenceVersionRegistry` and `ReferenceDataService`. This story changes none of them, and the as-built contract and solution plan are kept word for word under "As built (monolith)".

**Target reading of the preserved sections 3, 8 and 11.**

**Section 3.** In the target the two tables `reference_version` and `reference_row` and the list `lov_value` are tables of `rwb_case` owned by P3 rwb-case, and the load, verify, approve and rollback operations are operations of this service (Ownership Map ruling ASM-0041, which moves the reference-load paths from rwb-access to rwb-case); their base path is the rwb-case base of the paragraph above and their shapes are the contract of RWB-P3-E1043-CON. One table of the legacy list, `DELEGATION_LIMIT`, is not held here: the Ownership Map keeps `delegation_limit` with P4 rwb-access (ASM-0070), so the DoA table is read from the rwb-access DoA operation and the legacy wording of section 8 BR1 stays as written (GAP-0696; ASM-1243).

**Section 8.** BR1 is the legacy list and stays as written. In the target the twelve codes remain the codes of LOV-REF-TABLE, and eleven of them are served from `rwb_case`; `DELEGATION_LIMIT` is not, because the Ownership Map keeps `delegation_limit` with P4 rwb-access as the DoA table (ASM-0070), so a caller that needs a delegation limit reads it through the rwb-access DoA operation and not through this service (GAP-0696; ASM-1243). The approve right of BR4 is checked on the rwb-access authorise contract (DP-08), and the author check stays local.

**Section 11.** The three tables are created and read in the schema `rwb_case`: `reference_version` and `reference_row` as the rows above carry them, and `lov_value` as a P3 table of the same schema, read through the reference-data contract of this service and not through a P4 interface (Ownership Map ruling ASM-0071; DP-01; DP-07). The `delegation_limit` table is not in this schema and this story reads no column of it (ASM-0070; GAP-0696; ASM-1243). The eleven remaining table codes are rows in `reference_row` and carry no column of their own in this schema. The column definitions of each reference table code — the required columns, their types and their key columns — are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0697; ASM-1244); they are held as data beside LOV-REF-TABLE and are read by the row check of section 13.

**Target traceability additions.**

| Requirement ID | Requirement (short) | BRD section | Feature | L3 process | Rules | Test cases |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| REQ-CWC-016 | Every engine logs the table code and version of every table it reads | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 4; Program, section 5.7 | FEAT-CWC-23 | 14 Set strategy, policy and decision rules | R-UNI-38 | TC-E1-043-03 |
| ADR-012 | Versioned reference data with valid from, author and approver; rule packages separate from reference tables | Business Requirements Epic 1, section 4 | FEAT-CWC-23 | 14 Set strategy, policy and decision rules | CTL-08 | TC-E1-043-01, TC-E1-043-07 |

The two legacy rows of section 18 stay unchanged; these two rows are added for the target because section 8 BR7 and section 2 cite REQ-CWC-016 and ADR-012 and the legacy section 18 table named neither.

**Target form of the plan.** The package moves to `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case.refdata` inside the rwb-case repository, with the published part of the reference-data contract in `...case.refdata.api` (DP-13, DP-02). The five operations of section 12 are served under the rwb-case base `/api/recovery/case/v1` and not under the monolith base `/api/recovery/v1` on which the as-built endpoints sat, and their shapes are the contract of RWB-P3-E1043-CON (DP-13). The migration is a step of the rwb-case Flyway sequence in the schema `rwb_case` and takes the schema name from the parameter of RWB-PLT-E1044-CON (DP-15; RWB-E1-044). The approve right and the load right are checked on the rwb-access authorise contract and the guard library (DP-08), the cache time to live is read through the parameters contract of this service (DP-06), and the topic and event naming of the service follow RWB-PLT-E1047-CON (DP-14). The read side that the other 18 services and the Drools evaluator compile against is the client contract of RWB-PLT-E1043-CON. The holiday calendar stays ACE data read through `v_ace_holiday` and is served by no part of this story (DP-05).

**Build steps for the target**

1. Move the eight components and the two published interfaces into the rwb-case package and keep the behaviour of sections 4 and 5 unchanged.
2. Add the reference-data migration to the rwb-case Flyway sequence in `rwb_case`, with the three tables and the constraints of the as-built plan, and no `delegation_limit` table (DP-15; ASM-0070).
3. Wire the five operations of section 12.1 to the registry and the read service, with the `asOf` effective-dated read and the refusal of section 12.1.
4. Replace the in-process approve-right check with the rwb-access authorise check and the guard library (DP-08), and read the cache time to live through the parameters contract (DP-06).
5. Build the column definitions per reference table code beside LOV-REF-TABLE and run the row check of section 4 step 3 from them (GAP-0697; ASM-1244).
6. Write the tests of section 16 against the contract baseline of RWB-P3-E1043-CON and its fakes.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.refdata-versions`. Off: the engines read the reference values loaded before this story.

**Done when.** The eleven test cases of section 16 pass, the eleven table codes served here each have version 1 approved in SIT, the holiday calendar is read from `v_ace_holiday` in SIT, the delegation limit is read from the rwb-access DoA operation and not from this service, and the boundary test (RWB-TE-001) shows no read of `reference_version` or `reference_row` from outside the reference-data package.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-027 | A load check fails, the valid from is in the past, or no version is in force for a table an engine needs | The {table} load was refused: {check}. Version {version} stays in force. |
| MSG-P7-002 | The author approves their own load | You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | The load file has no data rows | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | Two approvals of one version at once | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right loads or approves | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

MSG-P3-027 is new (see Additions). Thai text follows DL10.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: table codes, columns, bands, periods and limits are rows; the code holds only the versioning behaviour.
- No personal data in logs, events, workflow inputs, tests or prompts: log lines carry table codes and version numbers only, and test files use synthetic codes and user identifiers.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or the `v_ace_*` views: the holiday calendar is read through the P1 contract of `v_ace_holiday`, and no reference class opens a connection to an ACE table.
- One schema and one login per service: the three tables are read and written in `rwb_case` and no class reads a table of another schema, `delegation_limit` included (DP-01).
- A version row is never updated in place except for its status, approver and valid to; a correction is a new version.
- The cache never serves a version that is not APPROVED, and a missing version is a refusal with MSG-P3-027, never a default value.
- No rule table is held, loaded or versioned here: rule packages are Drools packages of RWB-E1-072 and RWB-E1-073, and LOV-REF-TABLE carries no rule table code.
- The load, verify, approve and rollback rights come from the rwb-access authorise contract and never from a local role list; the separation of duty of section 10 is enforced on every approval.
