#### As built (monolith)

###### 12. Contract

**POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads** (P4 endpoint; calls this story's interface)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | multipart/form-data: `file` (CSV or XLSX, one sheet), `table` (a LOV-REF-TABLE code), `validFrom` (date) |
| Response | 201 `ReferenceLoad`: `id`, `table`, `validFrom`, `status` (VALIDATED), `rows` |
| Errors | 401 no session (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Reference data C (MSG-P4-002); 409 an approved version of the table already has this valid from (MSG-P3-027); 422 a check failed (MSG-P3-027) or the file has no rows (MSG-GEN-001); 503 the store is unavailable |
| Authorization | Reference data, right C |
| Idempotency | Table code, valid from and content hash. A repeat returns the existing load and writes nothing |

**POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve** (P4 endpoint)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Path `loadId` (uuid). No body |
| Response | 200 `ReferenceLoad` with `status` APPROVED |
| Errors | 401; 403 no Reference data A (MSG-P4-002); 404 unknown load (MSG-P4-003); 409 the approver is the author (MSG-P7-002) or the version changed since it was read (MSG-GEN-004); 503 |
| Authorization | Reference data, right A |
| Idempotency | A second approval of an APPROVED version returns 200 with the same body and changes nothing |

**GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}** (P4 endpoint) reads a list with its versions (`ListOfValues`). Reference data R. Used by AC1 to read version 3.

**Published interfaces** (package `recovery.casewf.refdata.api`):

```java
public interface ReferenceVersionRegistry {
    ReferenceVersion recordVersion(String tableCode, LocalDate validFrom, UUID authorUserId,
                              UUID loadId, List<Map<String, Object>> rows);
    ReferenceVersion approve(UUID loadId, UUID approverUserId);
}

public interface ReferenceDataService {
    VersionedRows rows(String tableCode, LocalDate businessDate);
    ReferenceVersion versionInForce(String tableCode, LocalDate businessDate);
    List<ReferenceVersion> versions(String tableCode);
}

public record ReferenceVersion(UUID id, String tableCode, int versionNo, LocalDate validFrom,
                               LocalDate validTo, String status, UUID authorUserId,
                               UUID approverUserId, Instant approvedAt, int rowCount, String contentHash) {}

public record VersionedRows(String tableCode, int versionNo, LocalDate validFrom,
                            List<Map<String, Object>> rows) {}
```

`rows(...)` throws `NoVersionInForceException(tableCode, businessDate)` when no approved version applies. The holiday calendar is not served by this interface: the working-day calculator reads `v_ace_holiday` through the P1 query of RWB-E1-028, because ACE owns the Bank of Thailand calendar. No events are published; the outbox carries none for this story.

Rule packages are out of scope for these endpoints. A rule package is not a reference table: it is loaded, approved and rolled back through the endpoints of RWB-E1-073 and evaluated through RuleEvaluator (RWB-E1-072), so no reference load accepts a rule package code.

###### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `recovery.casewf.refdata` in the recovery module; folder `recovery/casewf/refdata`. Published types in `recovery.casewf.refdata.api`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| ReferenceVersionRegistryImpl | Service | Runs the load checks, numbers the version, writes the version and its rows, approves |
| ReferenceDataServiceImpl | Service | Resolves the version in force for a date; serves rows from the cache |
| ReferenceRowCache | Service | In-memory cache keyed by table code and business date; entry time to live from `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds` |
| ReferenceVersionRepository | Repository | Reads and writes `reference_version` |
| ReferenceRowRepository | Repository | Reads and writes `reference_row` |
| ReferenceVersionEntity, ReferenceRowEntity | Entity | JPA mappings of the two tables, with the standard columns |
| ReferenceVersionRegistry, ReferenceDataService | Published interface | The Java interfaces in section 12 |
| ReferenceVersionLogger | Service | Writes the one log line per table read (table code, version, business date) |

**Database.** Flyway migration `V<next>__rwb_e1_043_reference_versions.sql` (this story creates both tables; schema from the `${schema}` placeholder):

- `reference_version`: `id uuid PK`, `table_code varchar(30) NOT NULL`, `version_no integer NOT NULL`, `valid_from date NOT NULL`, `valid_to date`, `status varchar(15) NOT NULL`, `author_user_id uuid NOT NULL`, `approver_user_id uuid`, `approved_at timestamptz`, `row_count integer NOT NULL`, `content_hash char(64) NOT NULL`, `load_id uuid NOT NULL`, plus the seven standard columns. Constraints: `UNIQUE (table_code, version_no)`; `UNIQUE (table_code, valid_from, content_hash)`; `CHECK (approver_user_id IS NULL OR approver_user_id <> author_user_id)`; partial unique index on `(table_code, valid_from) WHERE status = 'APPROVED'`.
- `reference_row`: `id uuid PK`, `version_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES reference_version (id)`, `row_key varchar(200) NOT NULL`, `row_data jsonb NOT NULL`, plus the standard columns. `UNIQUE (version_id, row_key)`; index on `version_id`.
- Both tables append only: an update trigger refuses changes to `reference_row`, and to `reference_version` except `status`, `approver_user_id`, `approved_at`, `valid_to` and the standard columns.
- No rule table exists in this schema, and this story creates none.

**Configuration and reference data.** `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds` = 300 (assumed; DL11), loaded by the platform administrator in the configuration service. LOV-REF-TABLE values and the column definitions per reference table code, loaded by the reference data administrator. The first version of each of the 12 reference tables is loaded by the reference data administrator before SIT and approved by Risk. The holiday calendar is ACE data read through `v_ace_holiday` and has no version row of its own.

**Build steps**

1. Write the migration and the two entities and repositories; test the constraints in a PostgreSQL test container.
2. Build the column definitions per reference table code and the row check (type, required, key uniqueness) from the parameter catalog of RWB-E1-042, with a check result per row and column. The definitions cover the reference table codes only.
3. Build `recordVersion(...)`: table code check, empty file check, valid from check against the business date, content hash (SHA-256 over the rows sorted by key), idempotent return on the same hash, version numbering, one transaction.
4. Build `approve(...)`: approver present and different from the author, approve right checked through the ACE access check, optimistic lock on `version`, set `valid_to` of the replaced version.
5. Build `versionInForce` and `rows` with `NoVersionInForceException`, and the cache.
6. Build `ReferenceVersionLogger` and call it from the case service, the allocation engine and the timer engine start-up hooks (one line per table; no row content).
7. Wire the P4 load and approve handlers to the published interface; map exceptions to the problem responses in section 12.
8. Write the tests in section 16.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.refdata-versions`. Off: the engines read the reference values loaded before this story.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the 12 reference tables each have version 1 approved in SIT, the holiday calendar is read from `v_ace_holiday` in SIT, and the boundary test (RWB-TE-001) shows no read of `reference_version` or `reference_row` from outside `recovery.casewf.refdata`.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: delta slice split from RWB-E1-043 for rwb-case — the reference-data contract of record that the preserved story RWB-P3-E1043-APP implements. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **consumer of the rwb-case reference data**, I want **the contract of record for the versioned reference tables in `rwb_case` — the effective-dated read with `asOf`, the version-in-force rule, the list-of-values read, the load, verify, approve and rollback operations, the rwb-access authorise and DoA reads it consumes, the parameters reuse, the Flyway step and the fakes**, so that **the app story, the case, allocation and timer engines, the Drools evaluator and the other services build and test a dated, approved reference read on Day 1 without any of them reading `reference_version`, `reference_row` or `lov_value`**.

This is the contract slice of the delta of legacy RWB-E1-043, and it is the counterpart of the preserved story RWB-P3-E1043-APP, which keeps the legacy acceptance criteria AC1 to AC10 and the runtime behind them. The contract publishes, under the rwb-case base `/api/recovery/case/v1` (DP-13):

- The five operations of the reference-data surface, with their request shape, their answer, their error answers and their rights: the list read with the `asOf` business date, the load, the verify, the approve and the rollback (Ownership Map; ASM-0041).
- The version-in-force rule: the approved version with the latest valid from on or before the requested date, and nothing else (legacy section 8 BR3 and BR4).
- The three tables of the surface — `reference_row`, `reference_version` and `lov_value` — as P3 tables of `rwb_case`, and the sentence that the DoA table is not one of them (Ownership Map; ASM-0070; ASM-0071).
- The two consumed rwb-access operations of DP-08, the one consumed parameters operation of DP-06, and the Flyway step of DP-15.
- The fakes that the app story, the allocation and timer engines, the evaluator, the platform client of RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and the integration harness build against.

The contract serves no rule table and no holiday row. Rule packages are governed in rwb-decision (P7) through RWB-P7-E1073-CON and the embedded kit of DP-04, and the holiday calendar stays ACE data read through the P1 contract of `v_ace_holiday` (DP-05). The story has no build dependency, is Day 1 by rule and sits in the contract group CG-W1 (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy module published `ReferenceVersionRegistry` and `ReferenceDataService` inside one application, so the shape of a reference read was never a contract: the version and its rows were in the same database and the caller was in the same process. After the split the tables sit in `rwb_case` (Ownership Map) and nineteen services read them across a service boundary, which means the effective-dated read, the refusal, the rights and the payload have to be agreed before any engine writes its start-up hook. Without that agreement each service invents its own projection or — worse — reads `reference_version` directly, which the schema-per-service rule forbids (DP-01).

**What this contract fixes, and what it leaves.** It fixes the operations and their answers, the version-in-force rule, the four admin operations and their rights, the three tables and their owners, and the fakes. It leaves the business values to the rows: the twelve table codes, their columns, bands, service levels, periods and limits stay data of a load, and no value appears in this document except the ones the legacy story and the technical specification carry.

**The DoA conflict, stated once.** Legacy AC2 and legacy section 8 BR1 load `DELEGATION_LIMIT` through the reference-data service. The Ownership Map ruling keeps `delegation_limit` with P4 rwb-access as the DoA table (ASM-0070) because Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41 give rwb-access the DoA table. The legacy acceptance criterion stays verbatim in RWB-P3-E1043-APP, and the target reading is this contract's: the reference surface of rwb-case serves eleven of the twelve codes, and a caller that needs a delegation limit reads the rwb-access DoA operation (GAP-0696; ASM-1243). Writing the ruling down here is cheaper than discovering it as a missing table in wave 1.

**The fakes are the Day-1 unblocker.** The first approved version of each table is loaded in SIT later in wave 1. With this document and its fakes, the app story, the engines, the evaluator and the platform client build and test the dated read on Day 1, and a drift test fails a build when an operation, a field or the refusal changes (Template and Rules §R5.4 class C). Every criterion below is new, tagged `(new, D-RCV-60)`, and tests only the contract deliverable.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service naming rules of Template and Rules §R4 are used unchanged: schema `rwb_case`, REST base `/api/recovery/case/v1`, topic `rwb.case.events.v1`, event names `rwb.case.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-case` (namespace `rwb-recovery`), Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`.
- The Ownership Map stands: `reference_row`, `reference_version` and `lov_value` are P3 tables of `rwb_case` (ASM-0071), and `delegation_limit` is a P4 table of `rwb_access` (ASM-0070).
- The five operations are the Ownership Map rows `GET /admin/lists/{listCode}`, `POST /admin/reference-loads`, `POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/verify`, `POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve` and `POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/rollback`, all owner P3 (ASM-0041), read under the rwb-case base.
- The field identifiers DF-REF-159 to DF-REF-171, DF-REF-181 to DF-REF-184, DF-REF-028 and DF-REF-029 are taken from the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary, character for character.
- The legacy message identifiers MSG-P3-027, MSG-P7-002, MSG-GEN-001, MSG-GEN-004 and MSG-P4-002 are used unchanged in the answers and the examples.
- The list LOV-REF-TABLE carries the twelve table codes of legacy section 8 BR1 and no rule table code; the non-DoA part of that list is served here (ASM-0070).
- The holiday calendar is ACE data under `v_ace_holiday`, read through the P1 contract and by no operation of this document (DP-05).
- The cache time to live is the legacy value `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds` = 300 (assumed; DL11), read as a catalog entry of the parameters contract RWB-P3-E1042-CON (DP-06).
- The platform client contract RWB-PLT-E1043-CON consumes the list read and the parameters read of this document; this document is their provider, and the platform library declares no operation of its own.
- No approval is required to publish a Draft contract: the surface is published at status Draft (realignment v1) and is frozen when the consuming stories pass their contract tests.

##### 4. Flow

1. The contract author writes the OpenAPI 3.1 document of the five operations, one tag per resource: Lists, Reference loads, Reference load approval, Reference load verification, Reference load rollback.
2. The author writes the effective-dated read: the `asOf` parameter, its default, the version-in-force rule of legacy section 8 BR3 and the refusal when no version applies.
3. The author writes the four admin operations with the legacy request, answer and error rows, with `Idempotency-Key` on every POST and with the rights resolved on the rwb-access authorise operation.
4. The author writes the table section: the three P3 tables of `rwb_case`, their keys and indexes, and the sentence that `delegation_limit` is a P4 table that this contract never names as its own.
5. The author writes the difference from the legacy contract: the authorise and DoA reads consumed, the parameters reuse, the Flyway step and the absence of a reference-data event.
6. The lint and schema steps run: OpenAPI 3.1 validation, the sibling-file rule, the operation-id rule, the error-envelope rule, `Idempotency-Key` on every POST, the base-path rule and the table-owner rule.
7. The fakes are generated from the document: the version in force, the no-version refusal, the four admin answers and the two rwb-access answers.
8. The document and the fakes are published, the app story and the platform client pin the version, and a drift test in this story refuses any difference between a fake and section 12.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message |
|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | An operation is published without a 4xx error envelope, or a POST without `Idempotency-Key` | The lint step fails the build and the document is not published | Lint finding, no message id |
| X2 | A path is published outside `/api/recovery/case/v1`, or another service's operation is declared as provided | The lint step fails the build | Lint finding, no message id |
| X3 | A read asks for a table code with no approved version in force for the requested date | The read is refused; no older version, no default row and no empty list is returned | MSG-P3-027 |
| X4 | The author of a load approves it | The approval is refused and the version stays VALIDATED | MSG-P7-002 |
| X5 | A role without the right calls a load, a verify, an approval or a rollback | The call is refused and nothing changes | MSG-P4-002 |
| X6 | `delegation_limit`, a rule table or a holiday row appears in the document as a table of this service | The table-owner lint fails the build; the DoA table stays with P4 and the holiday calendar with ACE | Lint finding, no message id |
| X7 | A field-level detail of the reference resources is missing from the source material | The element carries the placeholder, one gap row and one assumption row, and the fake is written to the assumed shape | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0697; ASM-1244) |
| X8 | A fake drifts from the document | The drift test fails the build | Lint finding, no message id |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Publishes documents and fakes; builds against the platform naming and error baselines only and starts on Day 1 |
| Negotiable | The element order inside an answer, the example values and the fake fixture set are open until the version is frozen; the operations, the version rule, the refusal and the rights are fixed |
| Valuable | The app story, three engines, the evaluator, the platform client and the harness build and test the dated read before an approved version exists |
| Estimable | Five provided operations, three consumed operations, three tables, nine sub-tables and four fakes |
| Small | One sprint for the documents, the fakes and the drift test |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one schema, lint or fake assertion in section 16, never a business outcome |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: rwb-case reference-data contract of record

  Background:
    Given the rwb-case base path is /api/recovery/case/v1, the schema is rwb_case and the contract version is v1
    Given reference_row, reference_version and lov_value are P3 tables of rwb_case and delegation_limit is a P4 table of rwb_access

  Scenario: AC1 The three tables and the twelve codes are fixed with their owners (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the table section of the contract
    When it is checked against the Ownership Map
    Then reference_row, reference_version and lov_value are named as P3 tables of rwb_case and no other table is named as this service's
    Then delegation_limit is named as a P4 rwb-access table and no operation of the contract reads or writes it
    Then no rule table, no rule package and no holiday row appears as an element of the contract
    Then the twelve LOV-REF-TABLE codes of legacy section 8 BR1 are listed, eleven of them are served here and DELEGATION_LIMIT is answered by the rwb-access DoA operation

  Scenario: AC2 The effective-dated read and the version-in-force rule are fixed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode} with the optional asOf business date
    When the document is validated
    Then the read answers the approved version with the latest valid from on or before asOf, with its version number, valid from, valid to and rows
    Then asOf defaults to the business date of the service and never to the latest version
    Then a read whose date has no approved version in force answers 404 naming the table code and the date and carrying MSG-P3-027, and never an older version, a default row or an empty list
    Then the same refusal is answered for a date before the first approved valid from and for a table code with no version at all
    Then no answer carries a customer identifier and no answer carries a rule row

  Scenario: AC3 One operation serves the list of values and the reference table (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode} for a LOV code and for a reference table code
    When the document is validated
    Then a LOV code answers its values in force with the list code, the value code and the version applied, matching DF-REF-028 and DF-REF-029
    Then a reference table code answers the version in force with its row key and row data, matching DF-REF-183 and DF-REF-184
    Then one operation serves both, so the platform client of RWB-PLT-E1043-CON reads a list with its versions in one hop
    Then an unknown list code answers 404 and a role without Reference data R answers 403 with MSG-P4-002

  Scenario: AC4 The four admin operations are the contract of record (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given POST /admin/reference-loads, POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/verify, POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve and POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/rollback
    When the document is validated
    Then the load takes multipart/form-data with file, table and validFrom, requires Idempotency-Key and answers 201 with the load id, table, valid from, status VALIDATED and row count
    Then the verify answers the check result per row and column of the validated load and changes no version number and no row
    Then the approve answers 200 with the approver and the approval time, and answers 409 with MSG-P7-002 when the approver is the author
    Then the rollback answers the version set to ROLLED_BACK with its reason and names the version in force for the business date
    Then every operation answers 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404, 409, 422 with MSG-P3-027 or MSG-GEN-001 and 503
    Then a repeat load with the same table, valid from and content hash returns the first load and writes nothing

  Scenario: AC5 The authorise check and the DoA read are consumed, not provided (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the two rwb-access operations of section 12.2 and the contract dependency RWB-P4-E1037-CON
    When the rights of the five operations are reviewed
    Then Reference data C, U, A and R are resolved on POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise for every operation and never from a local role list
    Then the delegation limit an approval needs is read from GET /api/recovery/access/v1/doa-limits and no column of delegation_limit is named as this service's
    Then a role without the right is refused with MSG-P4-002 and nothing changes
    Then each call is one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker, and this contract publishes no role, scope or DoA operation

  Scenario: AC6 The parameters reuse, the Flyway step and the topic rule are fixed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the parameters contract RWB-P3-E1042-CON, the Flyway baseline RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and the naming library RWB-PLT-E1047-CON
    When the document is validated
    Then refdata.cache.ttl-seconds and the list of reference table codes are read as catalog entries of GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters and never as code constants
    Then the three tables arrive on the rwb-case Flyway sequence in rwb_case, and the contract declares no baseline and no migration of another schema
    Then the contract declares no event on rwb.case.events.v1, because the Arch v5 catalogue carries no reference-data event and no consumer waits for one
    Then the topic rwb.case.events.v1 and the event-name form rwb.case.<Event>.v1 are quoted from the naming library and no topic outside that form appears

  Scenario: AC7 The nine contract tables are complete and the fakes match them (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the contract section and the fakes of section 12.8
    When the nine sub-tables are reviewed and the contract test runs
    Then each of 12.1 to 12.9 is present, and an empty one says None with one sentence
    Then every operation sits under /api/recovery/case/v1 and every table and every operation names its owner from the Ownership Map
    Then the fakes answer the version in force, the no-version refusal, the 403 with MSG-P4-002, the author-approves refusal and the cache time to live
    Then a drift between a fake and this document fails the contract test
```

These criteria are new and test only the contract deliverable: no legacy acceptance criterion is copied here — AC1 to AC10 of RWB-E1-043 stay with RWB-P3-E1043-APP — and every number, identifier, message and code comes from the legacy story, the Ownership Map or Architecture v5, character for character.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The contract serves the reference tables of rwb-case only: `reference_row`, `reference_version` and `lov_value` in `rwb_case`, and no table of another service | Ownership Map; DP-01 |
| BR2 | The version in force on a requested date is the approved version with the latest valid from on or before that date, and the chosen version number travels in the answer | Legacy section 8 BR3 (R-UNI-38) |
| BR3 | Only an APPROVED version is served; VALIDATED and ROLLED_BACK are never served, and a missing version is a refusal with MSG-P3-027 and never a default | Legacy section 8 BR9, section 17; Principle 5; NFR-033 |
| BR4 | A version takes effect only after an approver who is not the author approves it; the approve right is resolved on the rwb-access authorise operation | Legacy section 8 BR4 (CTL-08); DP-08 |
| BR5 | A load with any failed check is refused in full, and a repeat load of the same table, valid from and content hash writes nothing | Legacy section 8 BR5, AC7 |
| BR6 | A valid from date before the business date is refused, and an open case keeps the version it was decided under | Legacy section 8 BR6 (R-UNI-38) |
| BR7 | The DoA table is not served here: `delegation_limit` is a P4 rwb-access table and a delegation limit is read from the rwb-access DoA operation | ASM-0070; Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41 |
| BR8 | The holiday calendar is not served: it is ACE data under `v_ace_holiday`, read through the P1 contract | Legacy section 2 and section 12; DP-05 |
| BR9 | The cache time to live and the table-code list are catalog entries of the parameters contract, never code constants; the legacy value is 300 (assumed; DL11) | DP-06; legacy section 13 |
| BR10 | No event reaches a consumer for a version change: the legacy design publishes none, the Arch v5 catalogue gives rwb-case no reference-data event, and the refresh is the cache expiry | Architecture v5 slide 14; legacy section 12 |
| BR11 | One REST base and one topic per service: this contract declares `/api/recovery/case/v1` as provided and quotes `rwb.case.events.v1` without publishing an event on it | DP-13; DP-14 |
| BR12 | A breaking change raises a new contract version and deprecates the old one; an operation or a field is never edited in place | Template and Rules §R7.2; §R5.4 class C |

##### 9. State transitions

None in this story: a document has no runtime state. The states the document describes are the reference-version states of RWB-P3-E1043-APP section 9 (VALIDATED, APPROVED, ROLLED_BACK, with a refused load never written), and this story fixes the answer that accompanies each one.

| From | Event | Answer of the contract | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | Load received, every check passes | 201 with status VALIDATED and the row count | VALIDATED |
| None | Load received, any check fails | 422 with MSG-P3-027 naming the row and the column, or MSG-GEN-001 for an empty file; nothing written | Refused |
| VALIDATED | Verification recorded | 200 with the check result per row and column; no state change | VALIDATED |
| VALIDATED | Approval by someone other than the author | 200 with the approver and the approval time | APPROVED |
| VALIDATED | Approval by the author | 409 with MSG-P7-002; the version stays VALIDATED | VALIDATED |
| APPROVED | Approval of the same version again | 200 with the same body and no change | APPROVED |
| APPROVED | Rollback with a reason | 200 with the version set to ROLLED_BACK and the version in force for the date | ROLLED_BACK |

The legacy `status` vocabulary of three values is what the read returns. The list LOV-VERSION-STATUS of the technical specification carries the wider set LOADED, VALIDATED, APPROVED, IN_FORCE, SUPERSEDED, ROLLED_BACK and REFUSED (TSD P3 v3 T3.2), and the values outside the legacy three are never returned by the reference read of this contract.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The contract author (any team, per U3) | Writes and versions the document and the fakes |
| The service owner of rwb-case (P3) | Approves a breaking change and freezes a version |
| The app story RWB-P3-E1043-APP and the platform client RWB-PLT-E1043-CON | Consume the document, pin the version and raise a change request rather than a private variant |
| The allocation, timer and case engines and the Drools evaluator (SY-RULES) | Read the version in force through the document; they have no right in it |
| The rwb-access owner (P4) | Owns the authorise and DoA operations this document consumes, and confirms the rights of the five operations |
| The rwb-decision owner (P7) | Confirms that rule packages and the registry are outside this contract |
| RW-REFADM, RW-COE, RW-RISK, RW-AUDIT | Load, verify, approve, roll back and read through the operations; their rights are resolved by rwb-access |
| RW-PLATADM | Receives the alert an engine raises when no version is in force |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A contract is a technical artefact, not a credit decision |

No personal name, no e-mail address and no credential appears in a document, a schema, an example or a fake; where a caller must be named, the example uses a user identifier such as `U-REF-01` or a role code only.

##### 11. Data

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Field identifiers published | DF-REF-159 to DF-REF-171 (reference_version), DF-REF-181 to DF-REF-184 (reference_row), DF-REF-028 and DF-REF-029 (lov_value) |
| Field identifiers not published | The `delegation_limit` columns of rwb-access: reached over the rwb-access DoA operation, never in this document (ASM-0070) |
| Version projection | Table code, version number, valid from, valid to, status, author, approver, approved at, row count, content hash, load identifier |
| Row projection | Row key and row data, as DF-REF-183 and DF-REF-184 carry them |
| Example values | EXPOSURE_BAND versions 3 and 4 with bands "E1" to "E5", QUEUE version 7, SERVICE_LEVEL version 2, LEGAL_PERIOD versions 1 and 2, REGION with content hash "a1b2", the user identifiers "U-REF-01", "U-RSK-01" and "U-RSK-02", all from the legacy story |
| Personal data | None. No name, no e-mail address, no account number and no national identifier in an example or a fake |
| Load file | CSV or XLSX with one sheet, sent as multipart on the load operation; the column definitions per reference table code are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0697; ASM-1244) |
| Cache | One entry per table code and business date; the time to live is the catalog entry `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds` at 300 (assumed; DL11) |

The contract carries no business value of its own: the twelve codes, the bands, the service levels, the legal periods and the original date are the values the legacy story names, and every other value is a row of a load. The column definitions each table code needs — the required columns, their types and their key columns — have no source field by field, so the load operation carries them as data beside LOV-REF-TABLE and this document names the behaviour, not the columns (GAP-0697; ASM-1244).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

| Operation | Request | Answers | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | Path list code, for example LOV-REF-TABLE; optional `asOf` business date | 200 with the list values, or for a reference table code the approved version in force with its rows; 401; 403 MSG-P4-002; 404 MSG-P3-027 when no version is in force; 503 | P3 |
| `POST /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads` | `multipart/form-data`: `file`, `table`, `validFrom`; `Idempotency-Key` | 201 with the load id, table, valid from, status VALIDATED and row count; 401; 403 MSG-P4-002; 409 when an approved version has this valid from; 413; 422 MSG-P3-027 or MSG-GEN-001; 503 | P3 |
| `POST /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/verify` | Path load id; verifier and note | 200 with the check result per row and column of the validated load; 401; 403 MSG-P4-002; 404 unknown load with MSG-P4-003; 409 when the version changed since it was read with MSG-GEN-004; 503 | P3 |
| `POST /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve` | Path load id | 200 with the approved load, its approver and the approval time; 401; 403 MSG-P4-002; 404 MSG-P4-003; 409 MSG-P7-002 when the approver is the author, or MSG-GEN-004 when the version changed; 503 | P3 |
| `POST /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/rollback` | Path load id; reason | 200 with the version set to ROLLED_BACK and the version in force for the business date; 401; 403 MSG-P4-002; 404 MSG-P4-003; 409 when the version is not APPROVED; 422 an empty reason; 503 | P3 |

The four admin operations are the legacy load and approve operations moved to this service (ASM-0041), with the verify operation of the same ruling and the rollback of legacy section 9. The refusal of a dated read carries the status 404 because the requested dated representation does not exist; the legacy story fixes the message but not the status (GAP-0698; ASM-1245). The rights of the verify and of the rollback are not stated by any source and are taken as Reference data A, the right the legacy story gives the approval (GAP-0698; ASM-1245).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Provider | Use in the contract | Pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access (RWB-P4-E1037-CON) | The Reference data C, U, A and R right of the five operations | DP-08, DP-11 |
| `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/doa-limits` | P4 rwb-access (RWB-P4-E1037-CON) | The delegation limit an approval needs; this service holds no DoA table | DP-08, DP-11 |
| `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | P3 rwb-case (RWB-P3-E1042-CON) | `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds` and the list of reference table codes | DP-06, DP-11 |

Every call is one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker per provider (DP-11, ADR-020). The DoA operation is the target reading of legacy AC2: the reference surface of rwb-case does not hold `delegation_limit` (ASM-0070; GAP-0696; ASM-1243).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The Arch v5 catalogue gives rwb-case the topic `rwb.case.events.v1` with CaseCreated, CaseAllocated, CaseAllocationFailed, CaseTransferred, CaseStateChanged and TimerBreached (Architecture v5 slide 14), and no reference-data event exists in that catalogue; this contract therefore declares none and adds none, so the topic name and the event-name form are quoted and not extended (DP-14).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. A new approved version reaches a consumer at its next cache expiry, and no source declares an event for a version change; an owner event added later would arrive through the inbox library of RWB-PLT-TE006-CON (DP-09) and would raise a new contract version.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. A load, a verify, an approval and a rollback are one synchronous transaction each on the `rwb-case` task queue's service and not in a workflow, and a read is a cached read; the contract declares no workflow, no activity and no task queue of its own.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Temporal Schedule and no job is declared: the refresh is the cache expiry, the loads are operator actions, and the 00:01 rule promotion and the six-monthly access review belong to other owners.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Schema | Key and indexes | Owner | Exposed by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| reference_version | rwb_case | PK id; unique on table_code and version_no; unique on table_code, valid_from and content_hash; partial unique index on table_code, valid_from where status is APPROVED | P3 | The load, verify, approve and rollback answers; the version list of the list read |
| reference_row | rwb_case | PK id; version_id to reference_version; unique on version_id and row_key; index on version_id | P3 | The rows of the version in force in the list read |
| lov_value | rwb_case | PK id; unique on lov_code and value_code | P3 | The list read of a LOV code |

`delegation_limit` is not in this list: it is the P4 rwb-access DoA table (ASM-0070), read through the operation of section 12.2. `rule_package`, `rule_package_version`, `rule_row` and `rule_test_case` are P7 rwb-decision tables and appear nowhere in this document (DP-04). The three tables arrive on the rwb-case Flyway sequence after the V0001 baseline (DP-15; RWB-PLT-E1044-CON), and this contract declares no migration.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-case reference-data fake (this story) | The five provided operations: the version in force for a date, the rows of that version, the no-version refusal with MSG-P3-027, and the load, verify, approve and rollback answers with their error codes | RWB-P3-E1043-APP, the engines, the evaluator, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and the integration harness |
| rwb-access WireMock | `POST /authorise` granting Reference data C, U, A and R to RW-REFADM, RW-COE and RW-RISK and refusing with MSG-P4-002; `GET /doa-limits` with the DoA rows | The rights of the five operations and the DoA reading of AC5 |
| rwb-case parameters fake (RWB-P3-E1042-CON) | `GET /admin/parameters` with `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds` at 300 and the twelve table codes | The cache and the code check of AC6 |
| Drift and lint test assets (this story) | The assertions that compare each fake, each path and each table owner with section 12 | The contract test of section 16 and every consuming build |

The reference-data fake answers from fixtures and not from copied production payloads, and it carries user identifiers and role codes only. A consumer that needs a delegation limit is answered by the rwb-access fake, not by this one.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary (REST, Kafka, Temporal, File)

| Call type | Provided | Consumed | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| REST | 5 operations under `/api/recovery/case/v1` | 3 operations over 2 providers | OpenAPI 3.1, one hop, 2 s timeout and a breaker, `Idempotency-Key` on every POST |
| Kafka | 0 | 0 | No reference-data event exists; the topic of the service is quoted, not extended |
| Temporal | 0 | 0 | The operations are synchronous and no activity is declared |
| File | 0 | 1 | The load file of the load operation (CSV or XLSX, one sheet); no runtime file exchange |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** `openapi/lists.yaml` (the effective-dated list read, its `asOf` parameter and its refusal), `openapi/reference-loads.yaml` (the four admin operations with their error codes and the `Idempotency-Key` rule), `reference-data-tables.md` (the three tables, their keys and indexes and the DoA exclusion), `reference-data-consumed.md` (the three consumed operations and the 2 s budget), and the four fake assets of section 12.8 with the drift and lint test.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| lists.yaml | Document | The list read, the `asOf` parameter, the version-in-force answer and the 404 refusal (AC2, AC3) |
| reference-loads.yaml | Document | The load, verify, approve and rollback operations with their answers and rights (AC4) |
| reference-data-tables.md | Document | The three P3 tables, their keys and the DoA exclusion (AC1, AC7) |
| reference-data-consumed.md | Document | The two rwb-access operations and the parameters operation, with the 2 s budget (AC5, AC6) |
| Fake assets | Test asset | The version in force, the refusal, the admin answers and the two owner answers (AC7) |
| Drift and lint rules | Test asset | Base-path, operation-id, `Idempotency-Key`, table-owner, error-envelope and drift assertions (AC1 to AC7) |

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables. The contract names the three tables of `rwb_case` and no table of `rwb_access` | none |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision. The contract serves no rule package and no rule row | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views. The holiday calendar is excluded and read through the P1 contract | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library. The cache time to live and the table-code list are catalog entries | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case. This document is that contract, and it is what the other services and the platform client consume | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; this key's own contract |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library. The four rights are resolved there, and the DoA limit is read there | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents. No event is declared, and an owner event added later arrives through the inbox library | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout. The legacy in-process interface becomes the published read, and its fake is Day-1 work | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1`. The five operations sit under `/api/recovery/case/v1` and the lint refuses any other base | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library. The contract quotes `rwb.case.events.v1` and `rwb.case.<Event>.v1` and publishes no event | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema. The three tables arrive on the rwb-case sequence, and the contract declares no migration | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route. The reference data screens of Epic 8 reach the read through gateway-bff; the contract declares no route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Build steps**

1. Write `lists.yaml` with the `asOf` parameter, the version-in-force answer and the 404 refusal with MSG-P3-027 (AC2, AC3).
2. Write `reference-loads.yaml` with the four admin operations, their answers, the `Idempotency-Key` rule and the rights of section 12.1 (AC4).
3. Write `reference-data-tables.md` with the three tables, their keys and the two exclusions — the DoA table and the rule tables (AC1, AC7).
4. Write `reference-data-consumed.md` with the two rwb-access operations and the parameters operation, each with the 2 s budget (AC5, AC6).
5. Add the lint rules: base path, operation id, `Idempotency-Key` on every POST, error envelope, table owner and no path of another service (AC1 to AC7).
6. Generate the four fake assets from the documents and write the drift test that compares each fake with section 12 (AC7).
7. Publish v1, notify RWB-P3-E1043-APP and RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, and record the pinned version.
8. Agree the column definitions per table code with the reference data administrator and hand them to the app story as data, not as schema (GAP-0697; ASM-1244).

**Done when.** Both documents validate and pass every lint rule, the four fake assets answer every operation, the drift test is green here and in the app story, and the app story and the platform client have pinned version 1.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-027 | A load check fails, the valid from is before the business date, or no approved version is in force for the requested date | The {table} load was refused: {check}. Version {version} stays in force. |
| MSG-P7-002 | The author of a load approves it | You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | The load file has no data rows | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | Two approvals of one version at once, or the version changed since it was read | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right calls a load, a verify, an approval, a rollback or the list read | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The texts are the legacy ones, character for character, and Thai text for each follows DL10. MSG-P4-001 and MSG-P4-003 are named as error codes by section 12.1 exactly as the as-built contract of RWB-P3-E1043-APP names them; their texts are not in the source material and this contract adds no text of its own.

##### 15. Screens and states

None in this story. The contract serves the version list and the load result that SCR-39, SCR-40 and SCR-42 show in Epic 8, and those screens reach the operations through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). Until those screens exist the reference data administrator loads files through the operation, and the load result is returned in the answer and listed in the daily data quality report (RWB-E1-011).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: codes, columns, bands, service levels, periods and limits are rows of a load, and the only number this document fixes is the documented default 300 of the cache time to live.
- No personal data in an example, a fake or a log: user identifiers and role codes only, and no customer identifier in any answer.
- The contract names rwb-case tables and rwb-case operations as provided, and the three consumed operations as consumed; it never restates another service's operation as its own (DP-01, DP-13).
- `delegation_limit` is a P4 rwb-access table and appears here only as a consumed read; a document that declares it as this service's table fails the table-owner lint (ASM-0070).
- No rule table, no rule package and no holiday row appears as an element of the contract (DP-04, DP-05).
- Only an APPROVED version is served, and a missing version is a refusal with MSG-P3-027, never a default value, an older version or an empty list.
- Every POST carries `Idempotency-Key`, and a repeat load with the same hash writes nothing.
- No event is invented for a version change; the topic of the service is quoted and not extended, and an owner event added later arrives through the inbox library and a new contract version.
- The contract is versioned: a breaking change raises a new version and deprecates the old one in place of editing it.

##### 18. Traceability

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: preserved from RWB-E1-044 word for word and re-pointed at the platform template; the microservice delta is RWB-PLT-E1044-APP-2 with the contract in RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and the deployment in RWB-PLT-E1044-OPS. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform administrator (RW-PLATADM)**, I want **every schema change applied by a versioned Flyway migration, one migration per story, forward-only in PROD, with the schema name taken from a parameter**, so that **the database in every environment is the sum of known migrations and nothing else**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The recovery tables share the ACE database with the collection module, and two squads change it from one repository (DT07, DT08). A column added by hand in one environment makes SIT and UAT test a database that PROD does not have. This story makes every change a numbered, checksummed migration with no schema name written in the file, and fails the pipeline on drift. It supports REQ-RDF-001 (the 14 data products held in the ACE database) and REQ-RDF-014 (stage 2 tables exist before the first treatment goes live). The measure is zero schema differences between a clean build and each environment at every release.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The recovery tables are defined in the Logical Data Model and Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v6.sql.
- The recovery module folder and boundary test exist (RWB-TE-001).
- Each environment has a database account for migrations and a read-only account for the drift check, held in the key store (NFR-052).
- The schema parameter `RWB_SCHEMA` is set per environment (DEV, SIT, UAT, PROD). Assumed value `recovery` in every environment, as in Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v6.sql.
- Deployment slots are booked (DL35).

##### 4. Flow

1. Developer: adds one migration file for the story under `recovery/src/main/resources/db/migration/recovery/`, named `V<number>__<description>.sql`, with the header line `-- Story: <story key>`.
2. Pipeline: runs the migration lint: no literal schema name, no foreign key into `public`, exactly one story key per file, no story key in two files, no undo file.
3. Pipeline: starts a clean PostgreSQL container and applies all migrations with `RWB_SCHEMA` set.
4. Pipeline: runs the drift check: dumps the schema object list of the clean database and of the target environment, and compares them.
5. Deployment: on service start, Flyway applies each pending migration once, in version order, and writes its checksum to the history table.
6. Deployment: Flyway validates the checksums of applied migrations; a changed file stops the start.
7. Platform administrator: reads the migration run on SCR-44 Interface and job monitor.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | An object in the target environment is not produced by the migrations | The pipeline fails and names each extra or missing object | MSG-P3-016 | AC2 |
| X2 | An applied migration file was edited after it ran | Flyway validation fails and the service does not start | MSG-P3-016 | AC4 |
| X3 | A migration contains a literal schema name | The lint fails the build and names the file and line | MSG-P3-016 | AC5 |
| X4 | Two migration files carry the same story key, or one carries none | The lint fails the build | MSG-P3-016 | AC6 |
| X5 | An undo migration or a clean command is used against PROD | Refused; PROD runs forward only | MSG-P3-016 | AC7 |
| X6 | A migration fails part way | The transaction rolls back; the history records the failure; the service does not start | MSG-P3-016 | AC8 |
| X7 | Two service instances start at the same time | One applies the migrations; the other waits for the lock and finds nothing pending | None | AC9 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs only the table definitions in the Logical Data Model; it comes first so every later table is a migration |
| Negotiable | The schema name and the history table name are parameters; the story fixes the process |
| Valuable | Every later story changes the database the same way, and environments stay equal |
| Estimable | Flyway configuration, two pipeline checks and a lint |
| Small | Fits in one week with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion runs in the pipeline against PostgreSQL containers |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Database migrations versioned with parameterized schema names

  Background:
    Given the schema parameter RWB_SCHEMA is "rwb_case"
    Given the Flyway history table is "flyway_schema_history_recovery"

  Scenario: AC1 Migration applied (legacy RWB-E1-044 AC1)
    Given migration V12__add_queue_to_case.sql with the header "-- Story: RWB-E1-020"
    When the deployment runs
    Then the migration applies once
    Then its version 12 and its checksum are recorded in "flyway_schema_history_recovery"
    Then a second deployment run applies nothing and changes no object

  Scenario: AC2 Drift detected (legacy RWB-E1-044 AC2)

    When the migration check runs
    Then the pipeline fails with MSG-P3-016 naming "rwb_case.queue.note_x"
    Then no deployment to SIT starts

  Scenario: AC3 Schema name as parameter (legacy RWB-E1-044 AC3)
    Given RWB_SCHEMA set to "rwb_case" in DEV and in SIT
    When the migration V13__create_timer.sql runs in DEV and in SIT
    Then the table "timer" exists in schema "rwb_case" in both environments
    Then the file V13__create_timer.sql is byte for byte the same in both runs

  Scenario: AC4 Applied migration edited (legacy RWB-E1-044 AC4)
    Given V12__add_queue_to_case.sql applied in SIT with checksum 104553219
    Given the file changed in the repository so its checksum is 88120477
    When the service starts in SIT
    Then Flyway validation fails with MSG-P3-016 naming version 12
    Then the service does not start

  Scenario: AC5 Literal schema name (legacy RWB-E1-044 AC5)
    Given V14__add_index.sql contains the text "CREATE INDEX ix_a ON recovery.queue (team_code)"
    When the migration lint runs
    Then the build fails with MSG-P3-016 naming V14__add_index.sql line 1

  Scenario: AC6 One migration per story (legacy RWB-E1-044 AC6)
    Given V15__a.sql and V16__b.sql both carry the header "-- Story: RWB-E1-028"
    When the migration lint runs
    Then the build fails with MSG-P3-016 naming both files and RWB-E1-028

  Scenario: AC7 Forward only in PROD (legacy RWB-E1-044 AC7)
    Given the PROD configuration
    When a pipeline step calls Flyway clean or an undo migration U12__add_queue_to_case.sql is present
    Then the system refuses the step with MSG-P3-016
    Then no object in PROD changes

  Scenario: AC8 Migration fails part way (legacy RWB-E1-044 AC8)
    Given V17__add_two_columns.sql whose second statement refers to a table that does not exist
    When the deployment runs in DEV
    Then the system rolls the first statement back
    Then the history records version 17 as failed
    Then the service does not start and the run shows "failed" on the job monitor

  Scenario: AC9 Two instances start together (legacy RWB-E1-044 AC9)
    Given two service instances in SIT with migration V18__add_column.sql pending

```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every schema change is a versioned migration in the repository; no change is made by hand in any environment | ADR-002; DT08 |
| BR2 | No migration file contains a literal schema name; the schema comes from `RWB_SCHEMA` through the Flyway `${schema}` placeholder and the default schema | Principle 1 |
| BR3 | One migration file per story that changes the database, carrying the story key in its header | DL04 (merge owner per module) |
| BR4 | PROD runs forward only: clean is disabled, undo files are refused, a fix is a new compensating migration | DT11; NFR-027 |
| BR5 | An applied migration is never edited; checksums are validated on every start | DT11 (untested code is not merged) |
| BR6 | The recovery module keeps its own Flyway history table so its versions do not collide with the ACE and collection modules | DT07; DT08 |
| BR7 | The drift check runs before every deployment to SIT, UAT and PROD | CTL-02 (checks before use) |
| BR8 | No migration in the recovery schema declares a foreign key into `public`; an ACE row is held by its business key and ACE cascades deletes on `account`. The lint fails the build and names the file | ADR-010; D-RCV-35 U4 |

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It changes the migration state of each environment: a migration moves from pending to applied (or failed) in `flyway_schema_history_recovery`.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Runs deployments and reruns a failed migration job (Platform administration CRUD); reads migration runs on SCR-44 |
| RW-DATASTEW, data steward | Reads migration runs (Platform administration R) |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Reads migration runs (Platform administration R) |
| Pipeline migration account | Applies migrations with the migration database account from the key store; not a Workbench role |

##### 11. Data

No business field. The story writes the Flyway history table `flyway_schema_history_recovery`, which is a tool table and is not in the Logical Data Model. It reads the schema object list (`information_schema`) in each environment for the drift check.

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. This preserved story provides no REST operation: the governing migration contract is published by RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, the deployment behaviour is RWB-PLT-E1044-OPS, and the as-built contract is kept in the "As built (monolith)" section below.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. The only consumed operation of the as-built story is the P1 job view `GET /admin/jobs?type=MIGRATION`, which keeps its as-built description below and moves to RWB-PLT-E1044-APP-2 and RWB-PLT-E1044-OPS in the target.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. A migration publishes no event.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. A migration consumes no event.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. Migrations run at service start, not inside a Temporal workflow or activity.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. There is no schedule: the run is triggered by service start and by the pipeline step.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The only table the as-built story writes is the Flyway tool table `flyway_schema_history_recovery`, which is not a business table; the per-service history table is named in RWB-PLT-E1044-APP-2 and RWB-PLT-E1044-CON.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

None. The migration fixture and the P1 job view fake are published by RWB-PLT-E1044-CON.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary (REST, Kafka, Temporal, File)

None. This preserved story makes no REST, Kafka, Temporal or file call; the consumed job view keeps its as-built description below.

**As-built component set unchanged.** The five components of the as-built plan stay as built: `RecoveryFlywayConfig`, `MigrationRunRecorder`, `MigrationLint`, `SchemaDriftCheck` and the `V0001__rwb_e1_001_recovery_schema.sql` baseline. This story changes none of them. The microservice delta starts in RWB-PLT-E1044-APP-2 (one sequence, one schema and one history table per service), is published as a contract by RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and is deployed through RWB-PLT-E1044-OPS.

**Done when.** The ten test cases of section 16 still pass against the platform template, and the delta is delivered by RWB-PLT-E1044-APP-2, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and RWB-PLT-E1044-OPS. The legacy level `System` in section 16 maps to Component or End to end in the target; the delta test cases are in RWB-PLT-E1044-APP-2 and RWB-PLT-E1044-OPS.

The per-service history table name and the fields of the migration-run record are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1420; ASM-2488); this story keeps `flyway_schema_history_recovery` exactly as built.

The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID.

##### 17. Guardrails

- One schema and one login per service: a migration writes only `rwb_<name>` and runs under that service's own login (DP-01, DP-02).
- No literal schema name in a migration or in a repository query; the schema is `${schema}` fed by `RWB_SCHEMA`, and the file stays byte for byte the same in every environment.
- No cross-schema join, view or foreign key; a service holds another service's ID and asks the owner through its contract.
- No business value in a migration; seed values are reference loads (RWB-PLT-E1043-CON), never migration inserts.
- No personal data in a migration, a test or a log; no migration copies production rows.
- ACE data only through the P1 rwb-source-data contract or the `v_ace_*` views; a service never reads an ACE table directly.
- Forward only: no clean, no undo file and no edit of an applied migration; a fix is a new version.
- No manual change in any environment; a hotfix is a new migration through the pipeline.

| REQ-RDF-014 | Stage 2 data products exist before the first treatment goes live | Business Requirements Epic 2, section 4; Program, section 5.1 | FEAT-CWC-24 | All recovery processes | DT11 | TC-E1-044-01, TC-E1-044-03 |

#### As built (monolith)

###### 12. Contract

**GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/jobs** (P1 endpoint) lists migration runs with `type=MIGRATION`.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | Query `type` = MIGRATION, `status`, `from`, `to` |
| Response | 200 `Job[]`: `id`, `type`, `businessDate`, `status` (APPLIED, FAILED), `startedAt`, `endedAt`, `checks` (version, checksum, drift result) |
| Errors | 401 (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Platform administration R (MSG-P4-002); 503 |
| Authorization | Platform administration, right R |
| Idempotency | Not applicable |

**Migration job**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Service start in each environment, and the pipeline step `migrate` |
| Job name | Not a scheduled job in batch.txt; it runs at deployment |
| Input | The files in `db/migration/recovery`, `RWB_SCHEMA`, the migration account |
| Output | Applied objects in schema `RWB_SCHEMA`; rows in `flyway_schema_history_recovery`; one `Job` record per run through the P1 job monitor |
| Events published | None |
| Idempotency key | Migration version. An applied version is never applied again |
| Restart behavior | A failed migration rolls back; after a fix is merged as a new version, the next start applies it |

**Configuration** (Spring Boot properties, values from the configuration service):

```properties
spring.flyway.enabled=true
spring.flyway.locations=classpath:db/migration/recovery
spring.flyway.schemas=${RWB_SCHEMA}
spring.flyway.default-schema=${RWB_SCHEMA}
spring.flyway.table=flyway_schema_history_recovery
spring.flyway.placeholders.schema=${RWB_SCHEMA}
spring.flyway.validate-on-migrate=true
spring.flyway.out-of-order=false
spring.flyway.clean-disabled=true
```

###### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `recovery.casewf.migration` (configuration and checks); migration files in `recovery/src/main/resources/db/migration/recovery`; pipeline scripts in `recovery/build/migration-checks`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| RecoveryFlywayConfig | Service | Builds the recovery Flyway instance from the properties above; refuses clean in every profile |
| MigrationRunRecorder | Service | Writes one job record per migration run through the P1 job monitor interface |
| MigrationLint | Job | Build step: refuses literal schema names (pattern on `<identifier>.` before a table name for every name in `sys_objects`), a foreign key into `public`, missing or repeated story keys, and `U*.sql` files |
| SchemaDriftCheck | Job | Pipeline step: applies all migrations to a clean container, lists tables, columns, types, constraints and indexes of `RWB_SCHEMA`, compares with the target environment through the read-only account, reports each difference |
| V0001__rwb_e1_001_recovery_schema.sql | RWB-E1-001 baseline | Built from Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v6.sql with the `${recoverySchema}` placeholder and `SET search_path` removed; applied by RWB-E1-001 (D-RCV-28) |

**Database.** No business table changes. Flyway creates `flyway_schema_history_recovery` in `RWB_SCHEMA`. The baseline migration creates the 92 tables of Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v6.sql; the 4 extension tables ship inside it as ordinary tables of the recovery schema, and the 30 `v_ace_*` views ship in two later migrations (Section A with RWB-E1-069, Section B after RWB-ACE-001). No migration in the recovery schema declares a foreign key into `public`: an ACE row is held by its business key. The initial seed rows (`lov_value`, `role`, `permission`, `delegation_limit`, `sys_objects`, `sys_fields`, `data_product`) ship with the RWB-E1-001 baseline `V0001__rwb_e1_001_recovery_schema.sql` (D-RCV-28, D-RCV-29); later dictionary changes are reference loads through RWB-E1-043, not migrations.

**Configuration and reference data.** The schema value is the placeholder `${recoverySchema}`, fixed to `recovery` in every environment (D-RCV-28); no per-environment override. Migration and read-only database accounts in the key store, set by the platform administrator.

**Build steps**

Ruled 2026-11-05 as D-RCV-28: recovery Flyway files are named `V<seq>__<story>_<name>.sql` with a four-digit sequence taken in merge order; line 1 is `-- Story: <story key>`; the schema is referenced only as `${recoverySchema}` and is `recovery` in every environment. The RWB-E1-001 baseline is `V0001__rwb_e1_001_recovery_schema.sql`; RWB-E1-044 ships no production migration file. Former open point: The rule in this story is a single rising number with the placeholder ${schema} fed by RWB_SCHEMA. The other 51 stories that name a migration file use four other rules, 30 of them V<epic>_<story>__<name>.sql with the placeholder ${recoverySchema} as in RWB-E1-001. The lint rule reports and fails the build for a name that breaks the rule.

1. Add Flyway to the recovery module and `RecoveryFlywayConfig` with the properties in section 12; prove start-up applies and records a test migration.
2. Convert Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v6.sql into the RWB-E1-001 baseline `V0001__rwb_e1_001_recovery_schema.sql` with the `${recoverySchema}` placeholder; prove it creates every table in the recovery schema.
3. Build `MigrationLint` and add it to the build; test each refusal with fixture files.
4. Build `SchemaDriftCheck` and add it before each deployment stage; test with a hand-added column.
5. Build `MigrationRunRecorder` and show runs on the job monitor.
6. Prove forward only: clean refused, undo files refused, failed migration rolls back.
7. Prove the lock with two instances starting together.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.migration-drift-gate`. On in SIT, UAT and PROD: drift fails the deployment. Off in DEV: drift is reported and the deployment continues.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, and DEV and SIT show no drift against the baseline.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: migration contract published for the 19 services (ADR-021; DP-15; Arch v5 slides 29 and 41). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **one published migration contract that every service follows: the file name `V<seq>__<story>_<name>.sql`, the line `-- Story: <story key>` on line 1, exactly one story key per file, the schema only as `${schema}` fed by `RWB_SCHEMA`, the default `flyway_schema_history` inside each service's own schema, one `V0001` baseline per service, forward-only in PROD, no foreign key into `public`, no cross-schema reference, one migration account per service and the migration-run record**, so that **19 teams migrate in one way and a contract test refuses a file that breaks the rule before any environment receives it**.

##### 2. Business rationale

With one Flyway sequence per service (DP-15, ADR-021), the naming, the story header, the placeholder, the history table, the baseline and the forward-only rule become 19 local choices unless they are published once. Arch v5 slide 29 fixes the physical rule: one schema and one login per service, no cross-schema joins or keys, Flyway per service in its own pipeline, a boundary test in every build. This contract turns that slide into a testable artefact: a service team writes a migration against the contract and its fixture, and the contract test refuses a literal schema name, a foreign key into `public`, a missing or repeated story key, an undo file and a cross-schema reference, naming the file and the line. It is the Day-1 baseline that RWB-PLT-E1044-APP-2 builds and RWB-PLT-E1044-OPS deploys.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The platform template supplies the Flyway module and the golden pipeline in which the contract test runs (RWB-PLT-TPL).
- Each of the 19 services has its own schema `rwb_<name>` and its own login in the ACE database (Arch v5 slides 29 and 41); creating them is database work outside this story.
- ADR-021 (per-service Flyway and migration ownership) is the decision in force and DP-15 is the pattern.
- The legacy build rule of RWB-E1-044 (D-RCV-28) is the starting text: `V<seq>__<story>_<name>.sql`, four-digit sequence in merge order, `-- Story: <story key>` on line 1.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule and sits in contract group CG-W0 (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the contract document around the nine elements: the file name, the story header, one story key per file, the placeholder, the history table, the baseline, the forward-only rule, the no-cross-schema rule and the account rule.
2. Fix the 19 parameter sets, one per service, from the schema table of section 11.
3. Publish the migration-run record shape with the P1 job view as the owner.
4. Publish the fixture set: one valid file per service and the six forbidden fixtures.
5. Publish the contract test: each fixture is run through the lint and the boundary test and the expected refusal names the file and the line.
6. State the versioning rule: an additive clarifying change keeps the version, a rule that refuses a file which passed before raises v2 and deprecates v1.
7. Review with the service teams and tag the baseline.
8. Hand the baseline to RWB-PLT-E1044-APP-2, RWB-PLT-E1044-OPS and every service pipeline.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A fixture carries a literal schema name | The contract test refuses it and names the file and the line | MSG-P3-016 | AC2 |
| X2 | A fixture declares a foreign key into `public` | The contract test refuses it and names the file and the line | MSG-P3-016 | AC2 |
| X3 | A fixture carries no story header, or two files carry the same story key | The contract test refuses it and names both files | MSG-P3-016 | AC2 |
| X4 | A fixture is an undo file `U*.sql` | The contract test refuses it and names the file | MSG-P3-016 | AC2 |
| X5 | A fixture references another service's schema | The contract test refuses it and names the file and the line | MSG-P3-016 | AC2 |
| X6 | A parameter set resolves to a schema outside the 19 values | The contract test refuses the set | MSG-P3-016 | AC3 |
| X7 | A rule change would refuse a file that passed the published version | The new rule is published as v2 and v1 is deprecated | None | AC5 |
| X8 | A contract element or a fixture value is missing from every source | The element is marked with the placeholder and one gap row is carried | None | AC1 |

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A migration file is named `V<seq>__<story>_<name>.sql`, with a four-digit sequence taken in merge order inside the service | RWB-E1-044 build rule (D-RCV-28); ADR-021 |
| BR2 | Line 1 of a migration file is `-- Story: <story key>`, and exactly one story key appears in the file | RWB-E1-044 BR3 |
| BR3 | A story key appears in the files of exactly one service; a key repeated across services is refused | ADR-021; DP-15 |
| BR4 | The schema is referenced only as `${schema}` and is fed by `RWB_SCHEMA`; a literal schema name is refused | RWB-E1-044 BR2; DP-01 |
| BR5 | The history table is the default `flyway_schema_history` inside the service's own schema; no shared history table | ADR-021; Arch v5 slide 29 |
| BR6 | Each service has one `V0001` baseline that creates its own objects and is applied once per environment | DP-15 |
| BR7 | PROD runs forward only: no clean, no undo file; a fix is a new version; an applied file is never edited | RWB-E1-044 BR4, BR5 |
| BR8 | No foreign key into `public` and no cross-schema reference in any migration; the boundary test fails the build | RWB-E1-044 BR8; Arch v5 slide 29 |
| BR9 | Each service migrates with its own account from the key store; the account is a secret reference, never a value in the contract | Arch v5 slide 29; NFR-052 |
| BR10 | A rule change that would refuse a file which passed the published version raises the contract to the next major version | Arch v5 slide 42 notes (BACKWARD compatibility) |

**Build steps**

1. Write the contract with the nine elements of section 4 and the 19 parameter sets of section 11.
2. Write the 19 valid fixtures, one per service, each naming the schema only as `${schema}`.
3. Write the 6 forbidden fixtures, one per refusal, each with its expected message, file and line.

6. State the versioning rule and the deprecation window.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract or its fixtures: no threshold, code list or seed row.
- No personal data in a fixture, an example or a test: synthetic identifiers only.
- The contract names the 19 schema values and no other schema; it never documents another service's tables.
- The schema is `${schema}` everywhere in a migration; a literal schema name is a defect, not a style choice.
- No foreign key into `public` and no cross-schema reference, in the rule or in a fixture.
- The contract never carries a credential: the migration account is a secret reference in the key store.
- The contract is additive within a major version; a rule that refuses a file which passed before raises a new major version.
