**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: delta copy of RWB-E1-044 for the platform template, one Flyway sequence, schema, login and history table per service (Arch v5 slide 29; ADR-021; DP-15). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform administrator (RW-PLATADM)**, I want **one Flyway sequence per service in that service's own `rwb_<name>` schema, under its own login and its own `flyway_schema_history`, with the schema named only as `${schema}` fed by `RWB_SCHEMA` and one `V0001` baseline per service**, so that **the 19 services migrate independently and a change in one service can never reach another service's schema**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The as-built story runs one Flyway sequence for the whole recovery schema: one `recovery` schema, one `V0001` baseline and one `flyway_schema_history_recovery` table shared by every module. Arch v5 slide 29 replaces that with 19 schemas, one login each, Flyway per service in its own pipeline, no cross-schema joins or keys, and a boundary test in every build that fails on a cross-schema reference. ADR-021 makes per-service Flyway and migration ownership the decision of record and DP-15 is the pattern. One shared history table serialises 19 pipelines on one lock and lets one bad file stop every service; one sequence per service keeps "the database in every environment is the sum of known migrations and nothing else" true for each service and keeps the blast radius inside one schema. It supports REQ-RDF-001 (the 14 data products held in the ACE database) and REQ-RDF-014 (stage 2 tables exist before the first treatment goes live).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template of RWB-PLT-TPL provides the Flyway module and the migration lint, the drift gate and the boundary test.
- Each of the 19 services has its own schema `rwb_<name>` and its own login in the ACE database (Arch v5 slides 29 and 41); creating them is database work outside this story.
- ADR-021 (per-service Flyway and migration ownership) is the decision in force.
- Each service pipeline has a clean PostgreSQL container and a read-only account for the drift check.
- `RWB_SCHEMA` is set per environment (DEV, SIT, UAT, PROD) to the schema of the service that is being deployed.
- No build dependency: the story has no build dependency and is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Take the Flyway module from the platform template into the service and set `spring.flyway.locations=classpath:db/migration/<service>`, `spring.flyway.schemas=${schema}`, `spring.flyway.default-schema=${schema}`, `spring.flyway.placeholders.schema=${schema}`, `spring.flyway.table=flyway_schema_history`, `spring.flyway.validate-on-migrate=true`, `spring.flyway.out-of-order=false` and `spring.flyway.clean-disabled=true`.
2. Add the service's `V0001` baseline from that service's part of the physical schema; the other services' tables are not in it.
3. Set `RWB_SCHEMA` per environment to the schema of the service; no migration file carries a schema literal.
4. Run the lint: file name `V<seq>__<story>_<name>.sql`, line 1 `-- Story: <story key>`, exactly one story key per file, a story key never in two services' files, no literal schema name, no foreign key into `public`, no `U*.sql` file.
5. Run the boundary test: a cross-schema join, view or foreign key fails the build.
6. Run the drift gate with the service's read-only account before the deployment.
7. Start two services at the same time in SIT and prove each migrates through its own login and its own history table, within the PgBouncer cap of that login.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A migration file contains a literal schema name | The lint fails the build and names the file and the line | MSG-P3-016 | AC3 |
| X2 | A migration references another service's schema in a join, a view or a foreign key | The boundary test fails the build and names the file and the line | MSG-P3-016 | AC2 |
| X3 | One story key appears in the files of two services, or a file carries none | The lint fails the build and names both files and the story key | MSG-P3-016 | AC4 |
| X4 | An applied file was edited after it ran | Flyway validation fails and the service does not start | MSG-P3-016 | AC5 |
| X5 | An object in the service's schema is not produced by its migrations | The drift gate fails and no deployment starts | MSG-P3-016 | AC5 |
| X6 | Two instances of one service start together | One applies the pending migrations; the other waits for the lock and finds nothing pending | None | AC6 |
| X7 | Two services migrate at the same time | Each uses its own login and history table; no shared lock is taken and both finish inside the connection cap | None | AC6 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the platform template and the 19 schemas and logins; it reads no other story's code |
| Negotiable | The migration folder name and the baseline content per service are settled per service; the rule is fixed |
| Valuable | Each service owns its migrations and no pipeline can block another |
| Estimable | Flyway module wiring, one baseline per service and the three gates |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its tests, one service at a time |
| Testable | Each criterion runs in a pipeline against PostgreSQL containers |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: One Flyway sequence per service in its own schema

  Background:
    Given the platform template supplies the Flyway module with the schema placeholder ${schema} fed by RWB_SCHEMA
    Given each service has its own schema rwb_<name> and its own login

  Scenario: AC1 Each service has its own sequence, schema and history table (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the service rwb-case with schema rwb_case and its own login
    When the service starts with RWB_SCHEMA set to rwb_case
    Then Flyway applies the service's V0001 baseline from db/migration/case
    Then the history rows are written to the default flyway_schema_history inside schema rwb_case
    Then no object is created in another schema and no other history table is written

  Scenario: AC2 A run against rwb_case creates nothing in rwb_payment (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a migration file for rwb-case that references schema rwb_payment
    When the lint and the boundary test run in the build
    Then the boundary test fails on the cross-schema reference and names the file and the line
    Then the build stops and no deployment runs
    When a build runs only the migrations of rwb-case
    Then the object list of schema rwb_payment is unchanged

  Scenario: AC3 The same file applies in DEV and SIT (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given one migration file that names the schema only as ${schema}
    When it runs in DEV and in SIT with RWB_SCHEMA set to rwb_case
    Then the object is created in schema rwb_case in both environments
    Then the file is byte for byte the same in both runs
    Then no literal schema name is present in the file

  Scenario: AC4 One migration file per story per service (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a story that changes the database of rwb-case
    When it adds two files for the same story, or a file whose story key is already in a file of rwb-payment
    Then the lint fails with MSG-P3-016 naming both files and the story key
    Then a story key appears in the files of exactly one service

  Scenario: AC5 Forward-only and drift guards carry over per service (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the service rwb-case in SIT with its migrations applied
    When an undo file is added, or a column is added to rwb_case by hand
    Then the build or the drift gate fails with MSG-P3-016 naming the file or the object
    Then PROD refuses clean and undo and no object in PROD changes

  Scenario: AC6 Two services migrate concurrently through their own logins (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given rwb-case and rwb-payment both have pending migrations in SIT
    When both services start at the same moment with their own logins and history tables
    Then both apply their own migrations and neither waits for the other's lock
    Then each set of history rows is in its own schema
    Then the connections of the two logins stay within their PgBouncer caps
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One Flyway sequence per service, in the service's own schema; the files live in the service's own folder `db/migration/<service>` and run in its own pipeline | ADR-021; DP-15; Arch v5 slide 29 |
| BR2 | Each service has one login that owns `rwb_<name>` and holds no grant on another schema; the migration account is that service's login | Arch v5 slide 29; DP-02 |
| BR3 | The schema is referenced only as `${schema}` and fed by `RWB_SCHEMA`; no migration file carries a literal schema name | DP-01; Arch v5 slide 29 |
| BR4 | The history table is Flyway's default `flyway_schema_history` inside the service's own schema; no shared history table across services | ADR-021; Arch v5 slide 29 |
| BR5 | Each service has one `V0001` baseline that creates its own objects and is applied once per environment | DP-15 |
| BR6 | No cross-schema join, view or foreign key; a cross-schema reference fails the boundary test in every build | Arch v5 slide 29 notes |
| BR7 | One migration file per story per service, named `V<seq>__<story>_<name>.sql` with line 1 `-- Story: <story key>` | RWB-E1-044 build rule (D-RCV-28); RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| BR8 | Forward only in PROD and no edit of an applied file; the drift gate runs before SIT, UAT and PROD | RWB-E1-044 BR4, BR5, BR7; RWB-PLT-E1044-OPS |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pending | Service start | The version is next in the service's own sequence | Applied |
| Pending | Migration fails | A statement fails, or the checksum differs | Failed (rolled back, the service does not start) |
| Applied | Validation on start | The file and its checksum are unchanged | Applied |
| Applied | A fix is merged | A new version is added; the applied version is never edited | Pending (new version) |
| Applied | Drift found in the environment | An object is not produced by the migrations | Drift reported, deployment stopped |

The state of one service's sequence has no effect on the state of another service's sequence.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Configures `RWB_SCHEMA`, runs and reruns the migration of a service, reads the run on SCR-44 |
| RW-DATASTEW, data steward | Reads the migration runs (Platform administration R) |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Reads the migration runs (Platform administration R) |
| Pipeline migration account of the service | Applies the migrations of that service with that service's login from the key store |
| ACE database administrator | Creates and grants the per-service login; not a Workbench role |

##### 11. Data

No business field. The story writes the Flyway tool table `flyway_schema_history` inside each service's own schema; that table is not in the Logical Data Model. It reads the object list of the service's own schema from `information_schema` for the drift gate, and it reads nothing from another schema.

The fields of the migration-run record that each service reports are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1421; ASM-2489); the legacy `Job` response of RWB-E1-044 is the shape used until the register closes the point. The order of the baselines and the sequence start across the 19 services are part of the same open point.

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** The Flyway module wiring in the platform template for one service, the per-service `V0001` baseline and migration folder, the lint, drift and boundary gates wired into the golden pipeline, and the run-record call to the P1 job view.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Build steps**

1. Wire the Flyway module in the platform template with the properties of section 4 and the `${schema}` placeholder; prove a start applies one test migration in the service's own schema.
2. Add the per-service `V0001` baseline and the `db/migration/<service>` folder; prove the service's objects are created and no other schema receives an object.
3. Wire the lint with the six refusals of section 5 and test each refusal with a fixture.
4. Wire the boundary test and prove it fails on a cross-schema join, view or foreign key.
5. Wire the drift gate before SIT, UAT and PROD with the read-only account of the service.
6. Write the migration-run record through the P1 job view and show one record per service.
7. Prove two services migrate at the same time through their own logins and history tables, inside the connection cap.

**Done when.** The six test cases of section 16 pass for two services (rwb-case and rwb-payment), every service in the template applies its own `V0001` baseline in a clean container, and no build produces a cross-schema reference.

The order of the baselines and the sequence start across the 19 services, and the fields of the migration-run record, are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1421; ASM-2489); the template takes `V0001` in each service and the legacy `Job` shape until the point is closed.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-016 | Drift found, checksum mismatch, lint failure, a cross-schema reference, or a failed migration | Schema check failed in {schema}: {object}. The deployment was stopped. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without Platform administration R reads the migration runs | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

MSG-P3-016 is the message of RWB-E1-044, carried unchanged; the schema and the object in the text are those of the service that owns the migration.

No new screen. SCR-44 Interface and job monitor shows one migration run per service through the P1 job view, in state Running, Failed or Complete, with the service, the schema, the version and the drift result. A run of one service never changes the state of another service's run.

##### 17. Guardrails

- One schema and one login per service: a migration writes only `rwb_<name>` and runs under that service's own login (DP-01, DP-02).
- No literal schema name in a migration or in a repository query; the schema is `${schema}` fed by `RWB_SCHEMA`.
- No cross-schema join, view or foreign key; a service holds another service's ID and asks the owner through its contract.
- No business value in a migration; seed values are reference loads (RWB-PLT-E1043-CON), never migration inserts.
- No personal data in a migration, a test or a log; no migration copies production rows.
- ACE data only through the P1 rwb-source-data contract or the `v_ace_*` views.
- Forward only: no clean, no undo file and no edit of an applied migration.
- No manual change in any environment; a hotfix is a new migration through the pipeline.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: deployment side of RWB-E1-044 for the 19 services: Flyway on service start, the drift gate, the forward-only PROD rule, the key-store account, the job-run record and the two-instance lock (ADR-021; DP-15). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **DevOps engineer of the platform**, I want **Flyway to run on service start in every environment, one migration run per service, the drift gate before SIT, UAT and PROD, forward-only PROD, the migration account read from the key store as a secret reference, one job-run record per service to the P1 job view and a two-instance lock**, so that **a deployment applies exactly the pending migrations of that service and stops before an environment whose schema has drifted**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The migration rule is only as good as the deployment that runs it. Arch v5 slide 29 puts Flyway in each service's own pipeline; slide 33 deploys every service as two parts (an API deployment and a worker deployment on the same task queue), so two instances of one service can start at the same moment and both would try to migrate. This story fixes the deployment side: the run at start, one run per service, the drift gate before each environment, the forward-only rule in PROD, the account from the key store, the job-run record that the platform administrator reads on SCR-44 and the lock that lets two instances start safely. The legacy feature flag `rwb.p3.migration-drift-gate` keeps its name and its values across the split: on in SIT, UAT and PROD, off in DEV. It supports REQ-RDF-001, REQ-RDF-014 and NFR-052 (the key store).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The platform template and the Helm chart deploy a service as an API deployment and a worker deployment (RWB-PLT-TPL; Arch v5 slide 33).
- Each service has its own schema `rwb_<name>`, its own login and its own history table (RWB-PLT-E1044-APP-2; Arch v5 slide 29).
- The migration account of each service and its read-only drift account are entries in the key store (NFR-052).
- The P1 job view operations are published with their fakes by their owner, P1 rwb-source-data.
- The feature flag library of the platform is available to the pipeline and the chart.
- No build dependency: the story has no build dependency and is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Pipeline: build and test the service image; the migration files are inside the image.
2. Pipeline: run the drift gate before the deployment to SIT, UAT and PROD: apply the migrations to a clean container and compare the object list with the target schema through the read-only account.
3. Pipeline: stop the deployment when the gate finds a difference and the flag is on; report only in DEV where the flag is off.
4. Deployment: on service start, Flyway reads its account from the key store, applies each pending migration of that service once in version order and writes the checksum to the service's own history table.
5. Deployment: the second instance that starts at the same moment waits for the Flyway lock, finds nothing pending and starts.
6. Deployment: the service writes one job-run record for the run to the P1 job view, with the status APPLIED or FAILED.
7. Platform administrator: reads the run on SCR-44 Interface and job monitor, with the service, the schema, the version, the checksum and the drift result.
8. Platform administrator: reruns a failed migration job through the P1 job view after the fix is merged as a new version.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The drift gate finds an object that the migrations do not produce | The deployment stops before it starts and the object is named | MSG-P3-016 | AC2 |
| X2 | An applied migration file was edited | Flyway validation fails, the pod does not become ready and the deployment stops | MSG-P3-016 | AC1 |
| X3 | A pipeline step calls Flyway clean or an undo file is present in PROD | The step is refused and no object changes | MSG-P3-016 | AC3 |
| X4 | The migration account cannot be read from the key store | The pod does not start; the failure is logged without the secret | None | AC4 |
| X5 | The job-run record cannot be written | The run is logged locally with the same fields and the next run reports the gap | None | AC5 |
| X6 | A migration fails part way | The transaction rolls back, the history records the failure, the pod does not become ready and the run shows FAILED | MSG-P3-016 | AC1, AC5 |
| X7 | Two instances of one service start together | One applies the migrations, the other waits for the lock and finds nothing pending | None | AC6 |

| Independent | Needs the template, the chart, the per-service schema and login and the P1 job view contract |
| Negotiable | The gate wiring and the alert threshold are settled with the platform team; the rules are fixed |
| Valuable | A deployment can never change a schema by hand or leave an environment drifted |
| Estimable | The gate stage, the start configuration, the run record and the lock test |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion runs in a pipeline against containers and a two-instance environment |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Deployment of per-service migrations

  Background:
    Given each service has its own schema rwb_<name>, its own login and its own history table
    Given the migration account of each service is a secret reference in the key store

  Scenario: AC1 Start applies pending migrations once (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a service with two pending migrations in SIT
    When the service starts
    Then both migrate in version order and the history records them with their checksums
    When the service starts a second time
    Then no migration runs and no object changes

  Scenario: AC2 The drift gate runs before each deployment (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the feature flag rwb.p3.migration-drift-gate is on in SIT, UAT and PROD and off in DEV
    When a column has been added by hand to the service's schema
    Then the gate fails with MSG-P3-016, names the object and stops the deployment in SIT, UAT and PROD
    Then in DEV the gate reports the same difference and the deployment continues

  Scenario: AC3 PROD refuses clean and undo (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the PROD profile
    When a pipeline step calls Flyway clean or an undo file is present
    Then the step is refused with MSG-P3-016
    Then no object in PROD changes

  Scenario: AC4 The migration account is a secret reference (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the migration account of each service in the key store
    When the pipeline and the pod read it
    Then the account is a secret reference and never a value in a pipeline file, an image, a log or a prompt
    Then a scan of the pipeline files, the chart and the image finds no credential

  Scenario: AC5 Each run writes one job-run record per service (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a service start in SIT
    When the migrations finish
    Then one job-run record for that service is written to the P1 job view with type MIGRATION and status APPLIED
    When a migration fails
    Then the record shows FAILED with the version and the message

  Scenario: AC6 Two instances start together (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given two instances of one service starting at the same moment with one migration pending
    When both start
    Then one applies the migration and the other waits for the lock and finds nothing pending
    Then both instances start and the connections of the login stay within its PgBouncer cap
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Flyway runs on service start in every environment and applies each pending migration of that service once | RWB-E1-044 flow step 5; DP-15 |
| BR2 | One migration run per service; a run of one service never applies the migrations of another service | ADR-021; Arch v5 slide 29 |
| BR3 | The drift gate runs before every deployment to SIT, UAT and PROD and stops it on a difference | RWB-E1-044 BR7 |
| BR4 | PROD runs forward only: clean is disabled and an undo file is refused; a fix is a new version | RWB-E1-044 BR4 |
| BR5 | The migration account and the read-only drift account are secret references from the key store; no credential appears in a pipeline file, an image, a log or a prompt | NFR-052; RWB-E1-044 precondition 3 |
| BR6 | Each run writes one job-run record per service to the P1 job view, with status APPLIED or FAILED | RWB-E1-044 contract (migration job) |
| BR7 | Two instances of one service may start together: the Flyway lock lets one apply and the other wait and start | RWB-E1-044 AC9 |
| BR8 | The feature flag `rwb.p3.migration-drift-gate` keeps its name and values: on in SIT, UAT and PROD, off in DEV, where drift is reported and the deployment continues | RWB-E1-044 feature flag |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | Deployment starts | The drift gate passes, or the flag is off in DEV | Migrating |
| Migrating | All pending versions applied | The history records every checksum | Complete |
| Migrating | A version fails | A statement fails, or validation fails | Failed (rolled back, the pod does not become ready) |
| Failed | Fix merged and the job is rerun | The fix is a new version | Migrating |
| Complete | Second instance starts | The lock is released and nothing is pending | Complete |
| Complete | Drift gate fails before the next deployment | An object is not produced by the migrations | Deployment stopped |

##### 11. Data

No business field. The deployment writes one job-run record per service run; the record carries the service, the schema, the version, the checksum, the drift result, `startedAt`, `endedAt` and a status of APPLIED or FAILED, and it is the legacy `Job` shape. It reads the migration account from the key store and the object list of the service's own schema from `information_schema`.

The job-run record fields, the alert threshold and the owner of the feature flag after the split are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1423; ASM-2491); the legacy `Job` response of RWB-E1-044 is used until the register closes the point.

| REST | 2 consumed | The P1 job view: read the runs and rerun a failed job |
| Kafka | None | No event is published or consumed |
| Temporal | None | The run is not a workflow |
| File | None | The migration files are read from the image of the service |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** The golden pipeline stage that runs the drift gate before SIT, UAT and PROD, the chart values that read the migration account from the key store and set `RWB_SCHEMA` per environment, the start configuration with `spring.flyway.clean-disabled=true` and the lock, the run-record call to the P1 job view and the flag entry of `rwb.p3.migration-drift-gate`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Build steps**

1. Add the drift gate stage to the golden pipeline before SIT, UAT and PROD; wire the flag so a difference stops the deployment when the flag is on.
2. Set the chart values for `RWB_SCHEMA` per environment and point the migration account and the read-only account at their key-store references.
3. Set the start configuration: validation on start, out-of-order off, clean disabled in every profile and the lock on.
4. Add the run-record call to the P1 job view and the rerun path.
5. Prove two instances start together: one applies, the other waits and both become ready.
6. Prove the DEV behaviour: the flag is off and a difference is reported while the deployment continues.
7. Prove the scan: no credential in a pipeline file, the chart, the image or a log.

**Done when.** The six test cases of section 16 pass in SIT, the gate stops a drifted SIT/UAT/PROD deployment and passes it in DEV, PROD refuses clean and undo, and two instances start together inside the connection cap.

The job-run record fields, the alert threshold and the owner of the feature flag after the split are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1423; ASM-2491); the legacy `Job` shape, a single failed-run alert and the platform library as the flag owner are used until the point is closed.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-016 | Drift found, checksum mismatch, a refused clean or undo, or a failed migration | Schema check failed in {schema}: {object}. The deployment was stopped. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without Platform administration R reads the migration runs | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

MSG-P3-016 is the message of RWB-E1-044, carried unchanged; it is shown in the pipeline log and on SCR-44, not to business users.

##### 15. Screens and states

No new screen. SCR-44 Interface and job monitor shows one migration run per service, in state Running, Failed or Complete, with the service, the schema, the version, the checksum and the drift result; the administrator reruns a failed job from the same screen. The flag `rwb.p3.migration-drift-gate` has two states per environment: blocking in SIT, UAT and PROD, report only in DEV.

##### 16. Test cases

| TC ID | Covers | Level | Data |
|---|---|---|---|
| TC-PLT-E1044-OPS-01 | AC1 | Component | A service with two pending migrations; start applies once, the second start changes nothing |
| TC-PLT-E1044-OPS-02 | AC2 | End to end | A hand-added column in SIT, UAT and PROD stops the deployment; the same in DEV only reports |
| TC-PLT-E1044-OPS-03 | AC3 | Component | PROD profile with a clean call and an undo file; both refused, no object changes |
| TC-PLT-E1044-OPS-04 | AC4 | NFR | Scan of the pipeline files, the chart, the image and the logs; no credential, account is a secret reference |
| TC-PLT-E1044-OPS-05 | AC5 | End to end | One job-run record per service run, APPLIED and FAILED cases, read through the P1 job view |
| TC-PLT-E1044-OPS-06 | AC6 | NFR | Two instances starting together, inside the PgBouncer cap of the login, both ready |

##### 17. Guardrails

- One schema and one login per service: the run uses the login of the service and touches no other schema (DP-01, DP-02).
- No credential in a pipeline file, a chart value, an image layer, a log or a prompt; every account is a secret reference from the key store.
- No drift gate bypass in PROD: the flag is on in SIT, UAT and PROD and only DEV reports instead of blocking.
- Forward only in PROD: no clean, no undo file, no manual change; a fix is a new version through the pipeline.
- No business value in a migration and no personal data in a migration, a test or a log.
- ACE data only through the P1 rwb-source-data contract or the `v_ace_*` views.
- One migration run per service; a run never applies the migrations of another service.
- The two-instance lock stays on in every environment; a lock bypass is a defect.

##### 18. Traceability

| Requirement ID | Requirement (short) | Deployment element | Test cases |
|---|---|---|---|
| REQ-RDF-001 | Recovery data held in 14 data products in the ACE database | The run at service start writes the objects of the service's own schema | TC-PLT-E1044-OPS-01, TC-PLT-E1044-OPS-05 |
| REQ-RDF-014 | Stage 2 data products exist before the first treatment goes live | The gate and the run order guarantee the schema before the service serves traffic | TC-PLT-E1044-OPS-01, TC-PLT-E1044-OPS-02 |
| NFR-052 | Database and drift accounts held in the key store | The chart reads the accounts as secret references; the scan proves no credential | TC-PLT-E1044-OPS-04 |
| ADR-021 | Per-service Flyway and migration ownership | One run per service, forward only in PROD, the lock and the run record | TC-PLT-E1044-OPS-03, TC-PLT-E1044-OPS-06 |

##### 19. Out of scope

- The migration contract document and its fixtures (RWB-PLT-E1044-CON).
- The Flyway module wiring and the per-service baselines (RWB-PLT-E1044-APP-2).
- The as-built monolith behaviour, kept word for word in RWB-PLT-E1044-APP.
- The creation of the 19 schemas and logins and the grants (RWB-PLT-NF06-DB).
- The platform dashboards and alerts beyond the one failed-run alert (RWB-PLT-OBS).
- Deployment slots and release windows (DL34, DL35).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: moved from RWB-E1-045 to rwb-case with behaviour unchanged. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **every product-specific value (entry rule, exclusion list, service levels, notice and cure periods, exposure bands) keyed by product group in the versioned parameter and reference data of rwb-case, read only through the parameters contract of rwb-case (DP-06) and the reference-data contract of rwb-case (DP-07), with the notice and cure clocks running as durable Temporal timers inside CaseWorkflow on task queue `rwb-case` and their due dates computed by the CalculateDueDate activity from those values**, so that **a new product or a product change needs no code change**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Mortgage, hire purchase and SSME follow different notice periods, service levels and bands, and today each difference is held in a team procedure. If the engines carry these values as constants, every product change waits for a release. This story keys each value by product group in the versioned reference tables of RWB-E1-043 and refuses a load that leaves a product without a required value. It meets REQ-DRI-010 and REQ-CWC-011. The measure is that a product is added or changed by a reference load with no deployment.

In the target, PRODUCT, PRODUCT_PARAMETER and SERVICE_LEVEL are versions in the reference-data service of rwb-case: the catalog and its dated values in `parameter_catalog` and `parameter_value` (DF-REF-132 to DF-REF-158), the table versions and their rows in `reference_version` and `reference_row` (DF-REF-159 to DF-REF-184), and the lists in `lov_value`, all in schema `rwb_case`, owned by P3 under the R-PREC default ruling that gives parameters and reference data (E1-042, E1-043) to rwb-case (Template and Rules §R3; Ownership Map). The load and the completeness check now run inside the reference-data service of rwb-case, and every engine reads a value through the contract and its client library, never from a table of another service (DP-06, DP-07; DP-01). No service holds a product value, a product name or a period in code.

The clock changes shape as well. What the legacy story wrote as a `timer` row from a five-minute check is now a durable Temporal timer inside CaseWorkflow on task queue `rwb-case`: JOB-05 Timer check and the TimerDue event are retired, and the `timer` row is kept only as the screen projection behind `GET /cases/{caseId}/timers` (Architecture v5 slides 42 and 44; Ownership Map ruling ASM-0078). The due date is computed in the CalculateDueDate activity, which is where the value in force, its unit and the holiday calendar meet, and the reference version the calculation used is written to the local decision record through the decision-record library and published as DecisionRecorded on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03).

The holiday calendar moves behind the rwb-source-data contract (DP-05): rwb-case no longer reads the `v_ace_holiday` view itself, so a change in the ACE public-holiday list is absorbed in one service (Architecture v5 slide 45, "Who reads ACE's data?").

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1042-CON are published: the parameters contract of rwb-case with the client library, the catalog fields `scope` (DF-REF-140) and `required` (DF-REF-141), the dated value row `parameter_value`, and the build rule that fails on a parameter read that the catalog does not list (DP-06; FSD P3 A2.22).
- RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON are published: the reference-data contract of rwb-case with the client library, the version and row shapes of `reference_version` and `reference_row`, the load, approve and rollback operations of the reference-data service, and its table checks (DP-07; FSD P3 A2.23).
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published: the local decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`, so the reference version a due date was computed from is recorded and published in the same transaction as the timer projection (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-E1072-CON is published: the embedded Drools kit, so the engines that consume these values (entry, allocation, transfer) evaluate their packages with the rule version in force beside the parameter version in force (DP-04).
- RWB-PLT-E1047-CON is published: the topic and event naming library, so the one published event carries its agreed name and envelope (DP-14).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the gateway-bff composite route that serves the case record and the exception queue, so the timer projection and the refusal messages reach a person without a second screen model in this service (DP-19).
- Tables PRODUCT, PRODUCT_PARAMETER and SERVICE_LEVEL have an approved version in force, and the catalog marks each parameter with scope PRODUCT or GLOBAL, required yes or no, type, unit and allowed range.
- The loader holds RW-COE or RW-REFADM (Reference data C); the approver holds the approve right in Reference data, and an author never approves the same version.
- The `timer` and `task` rows and the CaseWorkflow wiring exist in schema `rwb_case` from their own stories: CaseWorkflow runs on task queue `rwb-case`, the CalculateDueDate, EvaluateRules and RecordAndApply activities are registered on that queue, and the notice timer is started on a task that carries the owner role. This story adds no column to either table.
- The engines that consume a product value (case creation, allocation, the stage clocks) are switchable, so the value can be moved behind the client library without a second release.
- The login is the rwb-case login (DP-02): one login and one connection pool for the service, with grants on schema `rwb_case` only.

##### 4. Flow

1. Center of excellence analyst: prepares a PRODUCT_PARAMETER load with one row per product group and parameter code, and a SERVICE_LEVEL load with one row per product group and case status; the values are the business's, never the code's.
2. Reference data administrator: loads each file through the load operation of the reference-data service of rwb-case (`POST /admin/reference-loads`, owner P3, carried by RWB-P3-E1043-APP), with the table code and the valid-from date; the call stays inside rwb-case, so no contract of another service is called.
3. Reference-data service: runs the RWB-E1-043 checks (content hash, row count, dry-run counts, valid-from discipline), then the product completeness check: every product in the PRODUCT version in force on the valid-from date has a row for every catalog parameter with scope PRODUCT and required yes, and a SERVICE_LEVEL row for every status in the parameter `servicelevel.required-statuses`.
4. Reference-data service: checks each value against the catalog type and range, and refuses a second row for the same product group and parameter code inside one version.
5. Approver: approves the version; it takes effect on its valid-from date and the version before it stays readable up to the day before, so a decision can always name the version in force on its business date.
6. CaseWorkflow: when a notice or a cure clock starts on a case, the CalculateDueDate activity reads the period through the parameters contract of rwb-case, `ProductParameterService.get(productGroup, "NOTICE_PERIOD_DAYS", businessDate)`, takes the unit from the same answer, and adds calendar days or working days; for working days it reads the holiday calendar through the rwb-source-data contract, never from an ACE view (DP-05). The activity writes `timer.expires_at` and `timer.warn_at` in the `timer` projection of schema `rwb_case` and returns the expiry to the workflow, which waits on a durable Temporal timer until that date.
7. Case creation and allocation: read the entry threshold, the exclusion list and the exposure bands for the case's product group the same way, through the parameters contract; a product group that has no value in force is never guessed from a default.
8. Each engine: writes the PRODUCT_PARAMETER version it used, with the table code and the version number, into its decision record through the decision-record library, and publishes DecisionRecorded on `rwb.decision-record.v1` in the same transaction as its own change, so an auditor can name the version behind every deadline and every entry decision.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A product has no SERVICE_LEVEL row for a required status | The load is refused in full and the missing product and status are named | MSG-P3-034 | AC3 |
| X2 | A parameter value is outside the catalog range or of the wrong type | The load is refused in full | MSG-GEN-002 | AC4 |
| X3 | Two rows for the same product and parameter | The load is refused in full | MSG-P3-027 | AC5 |
| X4 | A PRODUCT version removes a product that still has open cases | The load is refused in full; the open case count is read from `recovery_case` in rwb_case, not from another service | MSG-P3-027 | AC6 |
| X5 | At run time a case's product has no parameter row in force | The CalculateDueDate activity throws `MissingProductParameterException`; no timer is set and no durable timer starts; the case goes to the exception queue; the gap is named | MSG-P3-034 | AC7 |
| X6 | A parameter changes while a timer is running | The running timer keeps its expiry; new timers use the new value from its valid-from date | None | AC8 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against the P3 contract stories and their fakes only: the parameters and reference-data contracts of rwb-case, the decision-record and Drools platform contracts and the composite route. The rwb-source-data holiday answer comes from its contract fake, so neither the source-data service nor an ACE view is needed in the development environment |
| Negotiable | The parameter list and every value are data; the story fixes the lookup, the completeness check and the point where the due date is computed |
| Valuable | A product change becomes a reference load approved by its owner, and every deadline names the value version behind it |
| Estimable | Two read clients, one completeness check, one due-date calculation in one activity, one projection repository, two read operations |
| Small | Fits in one week with its tests |
| Testable | Every owned criterion has a test case in section 16; each cross-service answer is stubbed in a contract fake and real in SIT |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin

  Background:
    Given the business date is 2026-12-01
    Given PRODUCT_PARAMETER version 2 is in force with NOTICE_PERIOD_DAYS 30 calendar days for "MORTGAGE" and 60 calendar days for "HIRE_PURCHASE"
    Given PRODUCT version 1 is in force with "MORTGAGE", "HIRE_PURCHASE", "SSME" and "UNSECURED"

  Scenario: AC1 Product value differs (legacy RWB-E1-045 AC1)
    Given case "RW-2026-000101" with product group "MORTGAGE" and case "RW-2026-000102" with product group "HIRE_PURCHASE"
    When the timer engine sets the notice timer on both cases on 2026-12-01
    Then the notice timer of "RW-2026-000101" expires on 2026-12-31
    Then the notice timer of "RW-2026-000102" expires on 2027-01-30
    Then each timer start records PRODUCT_PARAMETER version 2

  Scenario: AC2 New product added (legacy RWB-E1-045 AC2)
    Given PRODUCT version 2 adds product group "AUTO_LEASE" with valid from 2026-12-05
    Given PRODUCT_PARAMETER version 3 and SERVICE_LEVEL version 3 add every required row for "AUTO_LEASE" with valid from 2026-12-05

  Scenario: AC4 Value outside its range (legacy RWB-E1-045 AC4)

```

**Note.** The eight criteria are the ones this story owns, copied word for word from RWB-E1-045 with one added Given in AC2: the "rwb-source-data contract mock returns an AUTO_LEASE account at 90 days past due on 2026-12-05" line stands in for the rwb-source-data answer that the ACE data would carry, so the criterion proves the product parameter load and not the source-data service. In the target the notice timer is a durable Temporal timer inside CaseWorkflow and `timer` is its projection, so AC1, AC7 and AC8 read the result through `GET /cases/{caseId}/timers`, and AC2 proves that a new product group gets its case and its timers from the new rows; AC3 to AC6 prove the completeness check inside the reference-data service of rwb-case. No value in any criterion is new.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every product-specific value is a PRODUCT_PARAMETER or SERVICE_LEVEL row keyed by product group and read through the parameters contract of rwb-case; no engine holds a product value or a product name in code | Principle 1; DT02; DP-06 |
| BR2 | The parameters required per product are those the catalog marks with scope PRODUCT and required yes: ENTRY_DPD, EXCLUSION_LIST, NOTICE_PERIOD_DAYS, CURE_PERIOD_DAYS and EXPOSURE_BAND_SET. Values per product are the business's (entry 90 days, DL16; service levels DL22; caps DL23) | RWB-E1-042 catalog; DL16; DL22 |
| BR3 | Every product in force has one SERVICE_LEVEL row per status in `servicelevel.required-statuses` (assumed NEW, ASSIGNED, IN_PROGRESS, WAITING_CUSTOMER, WAITING_PARTNER, WAITING_APPROVAL; DL22; the list itself is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0760; ASM-1382)) | REQ-CWC-011; casemodel.txt Case status |
| BR4 | A load that leaves a required row missing, a value out of range or a duplicate key is refused in full; the check runs inside the reference-data service of rwb-case | CTL-08; refdata.txt Change process step 3; DP-07 |
| BR5 | A product with open cases cannot be removed from PRODUCT; the count is taken from `recovery_case` in schema rwb_case | R-UNI-38 |
| BR6 | A timer takes the value in force on the date it starts and keeps it; new values apply from their valid-from date, and the version used is named on the decision record | R-UNI-38; DP-03 |
| BR7 | A value in unit WORKING_DAYS skips the public holidays returned by the rwb-source-data contract; a value in CALENDAR_DAYS does not. rwb-case reads no ACE view for the calendar | refdata.txt Reference tables; DP-05 |
| BR8 | A case whose product has no required value in force is not timed and goes to the exception queue; R-UNI-41 handles the case once a person decides | Principle 5; R-UNI-41 |

##### 9. State transitions

None on the case. This story does not change a case status. It changes how the notice and cure clocks set `timer.expires_at` and adds the completeness check to reference version validation (status VALIDATED or refused, RWB-P3-E1043-APP). A case sent to the exception queue under X5 keeps status New or its current status.

| Object | From | Event | Condition | To | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| timer (projection) | None | A notice or cure clock starts and the CalculateDueDate activity computes the due date | A PRODUCT_PARAMETER row is in force for the product group on the business date | RUNNING | The row is the screen projection of the durable Temporal timer and carries `started_at`, `expires_at` and `warn_at` |
| timer (projection) | RUNNING | The durable Temporal timer inside CaseWorkflow reaches `expires_at` | No payment and no cure clears the clock first | EXPIRED | The clock is a durable Temporal timer and not a five-minute job; the case status does not change |
| recovery_case | Any status | X5 — no PRODUCT_PARAMETER row is in force | The CalculateDueDate activity throws `MissingProductParameterException` | Same status, queue set to the exception queue | No timer row is written and no durable timer starts; MSG-P3-034 names the gap |

No row above moves a case status: the clock is now a durable Temporal timer inside CaseWorkflow, its expiry no longer moves the case by itself, and the stage clock behaviour belongs to RWB-P3-E1028-APP.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Prepares and loads PRODUCT_PARAMETER and SERVICE_LEVEL versions (Reference data C) |
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | Loads PRODUCT, PRODUCT_PARAMETER and SERVICE_LEVEL versions (Reference data C); has no Case record right and is refused on the timer read |
| RW-PRODHEAD, product head | Owns the values for the product (LOV-PRODUCT owner in refdata.txt); reads versions (Reference data R) |
| RW-RISK, risk and model risk officer | Approves a version where a limit or threshold moves, and never approves a version they authored (refdata.txt Change process step 4; assumed approve right as in RWB-E1-043) |
| rwb-case service identity (the rwb-case login, DP-02) | Runs the completeness check inside the reference-data service, reads the parameter and reference answers, computes the due date in the CalculateDueDate activity and writes the timer projection |
| Drools evaluator (SY-RULES identity) | Reads product values for allocation and entry through the parameters contract, never from a copy (Rules and parameters R; DP-04) |
| Decision-record library identity | Writes the local decision record of a timer start and publishes DecisionRecorded on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (Decision log C; DP-03) |

##### 11. Data

|---|---|---|---|
| DF-CAS-001 | recovery_case | id | Read |
| DF-CAS-003 | recovery_case | product_group | Read |

The timer rows are the screen projection behind `GET /cases/{caseId}/timers`; they are written by the CalculateDueDate activity together with the decision record of that timer start, and the clock that fires is the durable Temporal timer inside CaseWorkflow (Ownership Map ruling ASM-0078). The holiday calendar is read only through the rwb-source-data contract inside the same activity: rwb-case holds no copy of a holiday row and reads no ACE view (DP-05, DP-01). Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/case/v1`; owner rwb-case (P3).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/admin/parameters` | Read the parameter catalog with the value in force per environment and product group, so a person can see the value behind a due date; a secret parameter is listed without its value | Rules and parameters R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}/timers` | Read the clocks of a case: stage, service level, prescription and notice, as the projection the durable timer writes; used by AC1, AC2, AC8 | Case record R, scope applied | Not applicable |

The timers answer is `Timer[]` (`timerType`, `startedAt`, `expiresAt`, `warnAt`, `status`) ordered by `expiresAt` ascending, with the reference version behind a due date on the decision record and not on the timer. Errors for both: 401 no session (MSG-P4-001), 403 no right (MSG-P4-002), 404 unknown case or out of scope (MSG-P4-003), 503 store down. Idempotency is not applicable to a read. The load, approve, verify and rollback operations of the reference-data service are its own surface, carried by RWB-P3-E1043-APP, and this story adds no operation to them.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Service | Used for | Timeout |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Activity read inside the CalculateDueDate activity | Holiday calendar read on the rwb-source-data contract; operation name and path: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0759; ASM-1380) | rwb-source-data (P1) | The public holidays of a date range, so a value in unit WORKING_DAYS can be added without reading an ACE view (DP-05) | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |

One call, no chain: the holiday answer is read inside the activity that computes the due date, so CaseWorkflow never calls a service from workflow code. The parameters and reference-data answers are not REST calls of this story: they arrive through the published client libraries of rwb-case (DP-06, DP-07).

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Key | Payload (IDs and facts only) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 | caseId | decision code, the table code and the version number in force, the product group, the business date and the record reference |

The event is written to the outbox in the same transaction as the timer projection and the decision record and relayed with the CloudEvents envelope; it carries IDs, codes and dates only, never a customer key and never a product value (DP-03).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The load and the completeness check are synchronous; the rule version in force reaches the evaluating services through their own RulePackageInForce consumption and this story consumes nothing.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| CaseWorkflow | Workflow (parent, one per case, workflow ID = case ID) | `rwb-case` | Waits on the durable notice and cure timers this story's calculation produces; adds no workflow of its own |
| CalculateDueDate | Activity | `rwb-case` | Reads the period and its unit through the parameters contract, adds calendar or working days with the holiday calendar from the rwb-source-data contract, writes the `timer` projection and the decision record in one transaction |
| EvaluateRules | Activity (workflow kit) | `rwb-case` | Evaluates the entry, allocation and transfer packages with the embedded Drools kit, using the product values this story publishes (DP-04) |
| RecordAndApply | Activity (workflow kit) | `rwb-case` | Writes the decision record, the state change and the outbox rows in one transaction, including the reference version in force |

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. A notice or cure clock is a durable Temporal timer inside CaseWorkflow and not a Schedule; JOB-05 Timer check is retired (Architecture v5 slide 44; Ownership Map ruling ASM-0078). This story registers no Schedule and carries no daily parameter check.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| parameter_catalog | P3 (rwb_case) | The definition of every parameter: key, kind, type, unit, range, default, scope, required, owner role (DF-REF-132 to DF-REF-146) |
| parameter_value | P3 (rwb_case) | The approved, dated value per environment and product group (DF-REF-147 to DF-REF-158) |
| reference_version | P3 (rwb_case) | One version of PRODUCT, PRODUCT_PARAMETER or SERVICE_LEVEL with author, approver, row count and content hash (DF-REF-159 to DF-REF-180) |
| reference_row | P3 (rwb_case) | One row of a version, keyed by `row_key` with its `row_data` (DF-REF-181 to DF-REF-184) |
| lov_value | P3 (rwb_case) | The list values, including LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-PARAM-SCOPE and LOV-CASE-STATUS, read with their version (DP-07) |
| timer | P3 (rwb_case) | The screen projection of the durable timer: type, start, expiry, warning point, paused flag, status (DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-044) |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in rwb_case | Outbox, inbox and idempotency objects of the platform library |

rwb-case reads no table of another service and holds no foreign key across services (DP-01). The holiday calendar is not a table of this schema: it is read through the rwb-source-data contract.

|---|---|---|
| rwb-source-data WireMock | The P1 contract | The holiday calendar answer for the 2026-12-31 year end and for 2027-01-30, and a delayed answer beyond 2 s (operation name and path Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0759; ASM-1380)) |
| Parameters contract fake of rwb-case | The DP-06 client library of RWB-P3-E1042-CON | `parameter_catalog` and `parameter_value` answers for NOTICE_PERIOD_DAYS 30 and 60, 45 from 2026-12-03, CURE_PERIOD_DAYS, and `servicelevel.required-statuses` |
| Reference-data contract fake of rwb-case | The DP-07 client library of RWB-P3-E1043-CON | PRODUCT versions 1 and 2, PRODUCT_PARAMETER versions 2, 3 and 4 and SERVICE_LEVEL version 3 with their valid-from dates, the version in force per business date, and the refusal answers MSG-P3-034, MSG-P3-027 and MSG-GEN-002 |

| Call type | Count | Detail |

| REST | 2 provided, 1 consumed | Parameters and timers provided; the holiday calendar consumed inside the activity; one hop, 2 s timeout |
| Kafka | 1 published, none consumed | DecisionRecorded on `rwb.decision-record.v1` |
| Temporal | 1 workflow, 3 activities | CaseWorkflow holds the durable timer; CalculateDueDate computes the date, EvaluateRules reads the values, RecordAndApply writes the record and the outbox row |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`, module `refdata`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case.refdata`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | The monolith base path of the legacy API (Template and Rules §R5.5, DP-13) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.case.events.v1` and the shared `rwb.decision-record.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The same-service contracts RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON and the platform contracts RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1072-CON, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON are class H dependencies and are not DP rows. The C dependency of DP-04 belongs to the packages that consume these values and is carried where they are governed; this story's own contract dependencies are None (Template and Rules §R5.4).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| ProductParameterServiceClient | Client | Reads `parameter_catalog` and `parameter_value` through the parameters contract of rwb-case with the version in force; throws `MissingProductParameterException` when no row is in force (DP-06) |
| ReferenceDataClient | Client | Reads `reference_version`, `reference_row` and `lov_value` through the reference-data contract of rwb-case; resolves PRODUCT, PRODUCT_PARAMETER and SERVICE_LEVEL for a business date (DP-07) |
| ParameterVersionResolver | Service | Resolves the version in force for a product group, parameter code and business date, and returns the value, its unit and the table code and version number so the caller can record them |
| ProductCompletenessCheck | Service | The load check for PRODUCT, PRODUCT_PARAMETER and SERVICE_LEVEL: required rows, catalog type and range, duplicate key, products with open cases |
| OpenCaseCounter | Repository | Counts open cases by product group in `recovery_case` (status not CLOSED) inside schema rwb_case |
| DueDateCalculator | Service | Adds calendar days or working days, reading the holiday calendar through the rwb-source-data contract (DP-05); called by the CalculateDueDate activity |
| TimerProjectionRepository | Repository | Writes and reads the `timer` projection rows of a case in schema rwb_case; no write to any other schema |
| ProductParameterController | Controller | `GET /admin/parameters` and `GET /cases/{caseId}/timers`, with the right and the scope check behind each |
| DecisionRecordWriter | Library client | Writes the local decision record of a timer start or a refusal and its outbox row in the same transaction (DP-03) |

**Database and migrations**

- No new table. This story reads `parameter_catalog`, `parameter_value`, `reference_version`, `reference_row`, `lov_value` and `recovery_case`, and writes `timer`, `recovery_case.queue_id` and the outbox, all in schema `rwb_case`.
- Migration `V1045_1__product_parameter_projection.sql` in the per-service Flyway sequence of rwb-case adds three indexes and no column: `ix_case_status_queue ON recovery_case (status, queue_id)` for the open-case count, `ix_timer_case_expiry ON timer (case_id, expires_at)` for the timers answer, and `ix_parameter_value_lookup ON parameter_value (param_key, product_group, valid_from DESC)` for the version-in-force lookup.
- Uniqueness of a version and of a row is enforced by the reference-data service baseline of RWB-P3-E1043-APP and is not re-created here; the duplicate-row refusal of AC5 is that constraint plus the completeness check.

**Configuration and reference data**

- PRODUCT, PRODUCT_PARAMETER and SERVICE_LEVEL versions, loaded by the reference data administrator and owned by the product heads (values per DL16, DL22, DL23).
- Catalog entries for the five parameters of BR2 with scope, required, type, unit and allowed range, loaded by the center of excellence analyst through RWB-P3-E1042-APP.
- Parameter `servicelevel.required-statuses`, whose list is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0760; ASM-1382); the legacy assumed list is carried until it is confirmed.
- The holiday calendar is read through the rwb-source-data contract and is not a version of this service (DP-05).
- The 2 s timeout and the retry policy of the holiday read are service configuration values fixed by DP-11 and held outside code.

**Build steps**

1. `ProductParameterServiceClient` and `ParameterVersionResolver` over the parameters contract of rwb-case, with `MissingProductParameterException` and the version number returned beside the value; tests for AC1 and AC7.
2. `ReferenceDataClient` over the reference-data contract: version in force per business date, the row of a product group and the list values; tests for AC2 and AC8.
3. `ProductCompletenessCheck` and `OpenCaseCounter`, added as the table check of the three table codes in the reference-data service; tests for AC3, AC4, AC5 and AC6.
4. `DueDateCalculator` with the calendar and working-day rules and the holiday read through the rwb-source-data contract; test across the 2026-12-31 year end and a holiday row.
5. `CalculateDueDate` activity: the value in force, the unit, the projection write of `timer.started_at`, `expires_at` and `warn_at`, and the decision record with the table code and version number, in one transaction; tests for AC1, AC7 and AC8.
6. Move every product group name and period out of the case creation, allocation and stage-clock code so that each reads through the client; the catalog-versus-code build rule of RWB-P3-E1042-APP fails the build on a leftover literal.
7. `ProductParameterController` with the two read operations, the right and scope check, and the 401, 403, 404 and 503 answers; tests for AC1, AC2 and AC8 and the refusal of TC-E1-045-09.
8. Contract-fake run of every cross-service answer in isolation, so the story builds before rwb-source-data exists in the environment.

**Feature switch.** The legacy flag name `rwb.p3.product-parameters` is kept as the legacy reference. In the target the switch is a parameter read through the parameters contract: off, the engines use the values they read before this story and the CalculateDueDate activity falls back to the projection only; on, every value and every due date comes from the parameter and reference answers.

**Done when.** Every test in section 16 passes, `GET /cases/{caseId}/timers` returns the projection of a case with a notice timer and its expiry inside the 2 s budget, every decision record of a timer start names the table code and the version number in force, and a search of the rwb-case code finds no product group code literal outside test fixtures and the generated API types.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-034 | A product has no required parameter or service level row, at load or at run time | {product} has no {parameter} row. Add it before the load. |
| MSG-P3-027 | Duplicate row, or a product with open cases removed | The {table} load was refused: {check}. Version {version} stays in force. |
| MSG-GEN-002 | A value is outside its catalog range | {field} must be between {min} and {max}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without Reference data C loads a file, or a role without the read right calls either operation | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-001 | A call arrives with no valid session, or the person holds no Workbench role | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The case is outside the person's scope, or its ID is unknown | This case is not in your scope. |

MSG-P3-027 and MSG-P3-034 are new (see Additions). Thai text follows DL10. For MSG-P3-027 the {check} value names the failed check only; for MSG-P3-034 the {parameter} value is the parameter code or the case status that has no row.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story. A person sees the result on SCR-03 Case record, read only: the notice timer and its due date for each case, returned by `GET /cases/{caseId}/timers` and rendered by the case record view. A case sent to the exception queue under X5 shows on SCR-09 Exception queue (Loading; list) with MSG-P3-034. Both screens are served by the gateway-bff composite route, which calls rwb-case for the case and its timers and rwb-source-data for the account and customer facts in parallel, one hop each, and merges the answers into the screen model (DP-19; RWB-PLT-N001-CON). The screen fields, the mask of customer fields and the route specification are owned by that platform contract; this story fixes only the content of the timers answer.

| TC-E1-045-01 | AC1, BR1, BR6 | End to end | One Mortgage and one HP case; NOTICE_PERIOD_DAYS 30 and 60 |
| TC-E1-045-02 | AC2, BR1, BR2 | End to end | New product group AUTO_LEASE with all required rows; one synthetic account |

The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID. Legacy levels map System to End to end, Access to Component and Resilience to NFR; no case of this story carries a Resilience level, so no NFR row is created and no `-ITG` copy exists for an APP story.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: no product group code, period, threshold or band is written in Java or TypeScript; the generated API types treat a product group as a string checked against LOV-PRODUCT, not as a closed enum, and every value arrives through the parameters or reference-data contract (DP-06, DP-07).
- No personal data in logs, tests, workflow history, events or prompts: test cases use synthetic case numbers and synthetic account and customer keys, no customer name, address or identity number is read into a timer calculation, and the one published event carries IDs, codes and dates only.
- ACE data is read only through the owner's contract or the `v_ace_*` views of rwb-source-data: the holiday calendar comes through the rwb-source-data contract inside the CalculateDueDate activity, and rwb-case reads no ACE view at all (DP-05, DP-01).
- No read of another service's table: `rwb_case` holds no foreign key and no join into another schema, and the parameters and reference answers arrive only through their published client libraries.
- One evaluator: the product values feed the embedded Drools kit in the owning service, and no code reads a workbook, a DRL source or a rule row directly (DP-04).
- A running timer is never recalculated when a parameter changes, and its expiry keeps the value in force on the day it started (BR6).
- Every write of a timer projection goes with its decision record and its outbox row in one transaction, so a record never exists without the clock it explains (DP-03).
- The load is refused in full on any failed check, so no half-approved product version ever reaches an engine.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-046 for rwb-comms. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the template and merge field catalog of `rwb-comms` — the five admin template operations on base `/api/recovery/comms/v1` with their `Template`, `TemplatePage`, `TemplateApproval` and `TemplateWithdrawal` shapes, the template and merge-field state rules, the merge-field catalog version in force, the error envelope with its message IDs, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the two consumed reads with their owner and the contract fakes**, so that **the app, test and integration stories of this legacy key build against a fixed, testable contract on Day 1 and a version state, an approval field or a catalog version can never drift between rwb-comms, rwb-case and rwb-source-data without a failing build**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). Legacy RWB-E1-046 exposes its catalog as an in-process `TemplateCatalog` interface inside one module, with the load path owned by another module, and its state, its approval columns and its catalog version are read by the letter engine of RWB-P6-E1052, by the dispatch stories of wave 2 and by the integration harness of wave 1. Those are exactly the values most likely to drift silently: an approval field renamed, a state spelled differently in an answer than in a check, a catalog version that a load silently replaces, or a refusal that returns 200 with an empty page.

The baseline fixes the names the checks require: schema `rwb_comms`, REST base `/api/recovery/comms/v1`, topic `rwb.comms.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-comms` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.comms`. It records that this key publishes none of the service's three notice events, because a template load, an approval or a withdrawal is a synchronous answer and never a notice. It also records what the sources leave open: the exact request and answer field names of the five operations, the approver identity type on the file, where the body object lives, and the data-dictionary read of rwb-source-data, which has no contract dependency in the plan. Each of those is a placeholder and a gap row, never a guess `Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1067; ASM-2015)`.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the document, topic, event and queue names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- The platform error envelope, the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, the `Idempotency-Key` rule and the retry and `.dlt` topic convention are the platform baseline (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON); where this document narrows them it does so explicitly.
- The rwb-case reference-data contract RWB-P3-E1043-CON is published, so the LOV read this catalog consumes has one owner document and one fake.
- The TSD P6 appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2 are in force for API-P6-003 to API-P6-007, and the template and merge_field definitions of TSD P6 T3.1 and the lists of T3.2 are in force for the shapes and the values.
- The Ownership Map is the only source of owners: `template` and `merge_field` are P6's in `rwb_comms`, `lov_value` is P3's, `sys_fields` is P1's, `signature_request` and `document` are P5's and `decision_log_entry` is P7's.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 document of `rwb-comms` with the five admin template operations, the four resources of section 11 and the error responses of T-A.2.
2. Fix the state spelling and the state rules: Draft is created by upload, Approved and Withdrawn are reached only through the approve and the withdraw operation, and a version is current only when it is Approved and its valid-from date has arrived.
3. Fix the merge-field catalog shape and the meaning of the version in force, so two consumers never read a different catalog for the same business date.
4. Record the two consumed reads with their owner, their use and the 2 s budget, and map every failure to the error envelope and a message ID; carry the missing contract dependency of the data-dictionary read as a gap row.
5. Record the `Idempotency-Key` rule on the three POSTs and state the stored-answer behaviour of a repeat.
6. Record the event position: this key publishes none of `rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1`, `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1` and `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1`, and consumes no topic.
7. Publish the nine contract tables of section 12 and the contract fakes of section 12.8.
8. Add the contract tests: schema validation, the state values, the catalog version, the error mapping, the idempotency rule, the drift between a fake and the document, and the absence of a notice event in this key.
9. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-P6-E1046-APP, the dispatch stories of wave 2 and the wave 1 harness RWB-ITG-E1046-ITG.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A response body fails schema validation | The build fails on the schema lint; a deployed service answers 500 with the error envelope | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |
| X2 | A state value is spelled differently in the document and in a check | The contract test fails; the change needs a corrected document, not a new spelling | None | AC2, AC7 |
| X3 | A field is renamed or removed within major version 1 | The contract test fails; the change needs a new major version | None | AC1 |
| X4 | A contract fake drifts from the document | The drift test fails the build and the merge is blocked | None | AC8 |
| X5 | The data-dictionary read path has no contract dependency in the plan | The row carries the gap and the assumption, and the fake is derived from the published data-dictionary document | None | AC6 |
| X6 | A notice event is declared as published by this key | The absence test fails: no `rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1`, `NoticeDispatched.v1` or `NoticeDelivered.v1` on a template load or an approval | None | AC8 |
| X7 | A field-level definition is missing from the source material | The field is marked with the placeholder and one gap row is carried | None | AC2, AC3, AC5 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Criterion | Verdict | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Independent | Pass | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the TSD P6 appendix, the Ownership Map and the rwb-case reference-data contract only |
| Negotiable | Pass | The field-level names are settled with the consumers; the five operations, the state values, the catalog version and the two consumed reads are fixed by the target architecture |
| Valuable | Pass | Unblocks the app story of this legacy key, the notice story of wave 1 and the wave 1 harness on Day 1 |
| Estimable | Pass | One document, four resources, five operations, two consumed reads, nine contract tables and four fakes |
| Small | Pass | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Pass | Every criterion in section 7 is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |
