The eight criteria are new, test only the record side of the legacy key and copy no legacy criterion: RWB-E1-046 AC1 to AC8 are owned by RWB-P6-E1046-APP, and the cross-service proof of the same values is RWB-ITG-E1046-ITG. Every value used is the legacy value of RWB-E1-046 or of FSD P7 A2.10, A2.11 and A2.22 (GAP-2453; ASM-4064). `Given the rwb-comms catalog mock returns …` and `Given the rwb-case reference-data mock returns …` name the contract through which each cross-service value is stubbed, so no test reads another service's schema.

##### 8. Business rules

| BR | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Only a version in state Approved, carrying the Legal approver and the approval date, may be recorded; the row keeps the approver and the valid-from date it was given | RWB-E1-046 BR1; REQ-OCC-002; CTL-14 |
| BR2 | The version in force on a business date is the Approved version with the highest version number whose valid from is on or before that date, and the catalog version in force is chosen on the same date | RWB-E1-046 BR2; R-LIT-03 (template_status = current) |
| BR3 | A withdrawn version has no current version, so an answer that would need one is refused and nothing is recorded | RWB-E1-046 BR3; R-LIT-04, R-LIT-06 |
| BR4 | Every merge code an answer uses exists in the catalog version in force; the BR Field ID behind a code is the catalog owner's check and is not repeated here | RWB-E1-046 BR4; REQ-OCC-001; Principle 1 |
| BR5 | A refused answer is refused in whole: no row, no partial row, and the rows already written stay as they are | RWB-E1-046 BR5; refdata change process, step 3 |
| BR6 | A row is never updated or deleted, and an answer keeps the version it was decided under even after a later version or a withdrawal | RWB-E1-046 BR6; refdata change process, step 6; R-UNI-38 |
| BR7 | Templates are Legal counsel's reference data and the approver named on a version is that authority; this service records the authority but grants none | RWB-E1-046 BR7; DL28 |
| BR8 | `template` and `merge_field` are P6's in `rwb_comms`; rwb-decision holds no catalog table, copies no catalog row and reaches the catalog only through RWB-P6-E1046-CON (DP-01, DP-11) | Ownership Map; Architecture v5 slides 17 and 41; DP-01 |
| BR9 | The notice type and the product group are validated against LOV-NOTICE and LOV-PRODUCT read from the rwb-case reference-data contract at the version in force; no list value is written in code (DP-07) | TSD P7 T3.2; DP-07 |
| BR10 | No business value in code: template codes, merge codes, languages, notice types, product groups, catalog versions and dates are data of the catalog or the lists | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17; RWB-E1-046 section 17 |
| BR11 | Every catalog and list read is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retry once with jitter and a breaker per downstream; a failed read refuses the answer and never accepts a partial version | DP-11; ADR-020 |
| BR12 | The row carries codes, versions, identifiers and dates only: no merge value, no template body and no personal data; a merge field marked personal_data is resolved at generation time by its owner | RWB-E1-046 section 17; section 17 of this story |
| BR13 | The row and the answer are one unit of work: a row that cannot be written refuses the answer, so no answer is recorded without the version that explains it | R-UNI-39; DP-03 principle applied locally to this row |

##### 9. State transitions

None for a case status: this story moves no case, no notice and no template version. It sets the state of its own row only.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| (none) | An answer is recorded | The catalog answers an Approved version, every merge code is in the catalog version in force and the lists hold the values | Stored, with the version, the catalog version and the valid-from date |
| (none) | An answer is recorded | The version is unapproved, withdrawn or unknown, a merge code is unknown, or a read fails | Refused; no row; the refusal names the check and the message ID |
| Stored | A later version takes effect on its valid-from date | A new answer is recorded after that date | A new row for the new answer; the earlier row is unchanged |
| Stored | A version is withdrawn at the owner | Nothing | The earlier row is unchanged; a later answer is refused under BR3 |
| Stored | An update or a delete is attempted | Never | Refused; the row stays as written |

The catalog states this story reads are the owner's: Draft, Approved and Withdrawn, with Draft never usable and Withdrawn never current (RWB-P6-E1046-CON). The state word of a `template_use` row is this story's own and is stored on the standard `state` column; the column names of the row are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2453; ASM-4065).

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The rwb-decision service identity (the rwb-decision login, DP-02) | Reads the catalog and the lists; writes `template_use` in `rwb_decision` |
| The caller of an answer (the approval path of the service, the notice decision path) | Supplies the template code, language, version, notice type and merge codes; receives the refusal and its message ID |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit lead | Reads the values of an entry through the decision-log read of RWB-P7-E2005-APP (Decision log R) |
| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer | Reads the values of the entries on their cases (Decision log R) |
| RW-LEGAL, Legal counsel | Owns the approval of a version at rwb-comms (Documents A); grants nothing here and approves nothing here |
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | Loads the catalog and the template versions at rwb-comms (Reference data C); has no path into this story |
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Reads the catalog and the rows (Decision log R, Reference data R) |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A version and a catalog version are not a credit decision; the authority on the record is the approver named by the catalog |

No personal name, no e-mail address and no credential appears in this story, its examples or its fixtures. Where an actor must be named, the story uses a role code or a staff identifier only.

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity (owner) | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | template_use (P7, `rwb_decision`) | id, entry_ref, template_code, language, template_version, catalog_version, merge_codes, notice_type, product_group, approver_ref, valid_from, business_date, state | Write; the row name and the column names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2453; ASM-4065) |
| DF-REF-045 to DF-REF-051, DF-REF-063 to DF-REF-069 | template (P6 `rwb_comms`) | the version, its state, the approver, the approval date, the valid from, the channel, the notice type, the signature basis and the merge codes | Read through the catalog contract only |
| DF-REF-252 to DF-REF-260 | merge_field (P6 `rwb_comms`) | the merge code, its BR Field ID, the catalog version and the valid from | Read through the catalog contract only; the BR Field ID check stays the owner's |
| DF-REF-028, DF-REF-029 | lov_value (P3 `rwb_case`) | lov_code, value_code | Read through the reference-data contract (DP-07) |
| DF-DEC-001, DF-DEC-003, DF-DEC-008 | decision_log_entry (P7) | id, decision_code, inputs_ref | Read as the entry reference the row explains; the entry is written by RWB-P7-E1027-APP |
| Standard column | template_use | state, created_at, created_by | Write |
| None | outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key (PLT library in `rwb_decision`) | — | Created with the schema; not written by this story |

Keys and rules in `rwb_decision`:

- `template_use`: primary key `id`; unique `uk_template_use_entry (entry_ref, template_code, language)` so one entry names one version of one template; index `(template_code, language, business_date)` for the audit read; check that `template_code`, `language`, `template_version`, `catalog_version` and `business_date` are present.
- The migration is one per-service Flyway step in the `rwb_decision` sequence (DP-15, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON): `V_E1046__template_use.sql` creates `template_use` and alters no existing table. Its name and its position in the sequence are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2453; ASM-4065).
- No row is seeded by the migration: the catalog and the lists are the owners' data, reached through their contracts, and the fixtures of section 12.8 live in the test environment only.
- The row holds no foreign key into another schema and no copy of a catalog row; `template_code` and `language` are values, not references (DP-01).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The base of this service is `/api/recovery/decision/v1` (DP-13), and this story adds no operation to it: the row is written inside the answer the caller already asked for, and the values are read back through the decision-log read of RWB-P7-E2005-APP, which is named here and not declared as provided. A template-catalog read on this base would be a second catalogue and is refused by BR8.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

Every row is one hop on the owner's base with a 2 s timeout, a breaker per downstream and a single GET retry with jitter (DP-11, ADR-020).

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/comms/v1/admin/templates` | P6 rwb-comms | The current version of a template code and language on the business date, with its state, approver, approval date, valid from, notice type, channel and signature basis. The query parameter names and the answer field names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2453; ASM-4067); contract RWB-P6-E1046-CON (C) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/comms/v1/admin/templates/{templateId}/content` | P6 rwb-comms | Named and not called: the body is the owner's claim-check file and this story stores the reference, never the body. The merge-field set of a version is reached through the catalog contract and its path is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2453; ASM-4068) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 rwb-case | LOV-NOTICE and LOV-PRODUCT in force on the business date (DP-07, RWB-P3-E1043-CON) |

The catalog-version-in-force read of the same contract is the value matched in AC1 and AC6; its path and its field names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2453; ASM-4069). A failed read of any row refuses the answer with MSG-GEN-006 naming the system that did not answer; no answer is ever accepted on a partial answer (BR11).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. A recorded row is not an event of this story: the `DecisionRecorded` event of the entry is published by RWB-P7-E1027-APP on the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03), and the service's own topic `rwb.decision.events.v1` carries `ApprovalRequested`, `ApprovalDecided` (RWB-P7-E2013-APP) and `RulePackageInForce` (RWB-P7-E1073-CON), never a template reference. If the template values must travel, they travel inside the record of the entry, not as a new event type.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The values are read on demand at the moment of the answer, so a catalog change reaches this service on the next answer and needs no subscription; a cached copy would be the second catalogue BR8 forbids.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The recording is synchronous inside the caller's step, in the caller's thread and transaction: this story registers no workflow, adds no activity and holds nothing on task queue `rwb-decision` in namespace `rwb-recovery`. `ApprovalWorkflow` belongs to RWB-P7-E2013-APP and the record activity `RecordAndApply` to RWB-P7-E1027-APP.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Schedule, no cron entry and no job name is registered; the nightly chain check JOB-14 at 02:00 is RWB-P7-E1008-APP's Schedule, the promote run JOB-20 at 00:01 is rwb-decision's rule Schedule, and this story reads no scheduler row.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| template_use | P7 (`rwb_decision`) | One row per accepted answer: the entry reference, the template code, the language, the version, the catalog version in force, the merge codes, the notice type, the product group, the approver reference, the valid from, the business date and the state. Appended, never updated. Row and column names Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2453; ASM-4065) |
| decision_log_entry | P7 (`rwb_decision`) | Contracted use only: the entry id that `entry_ref` names; the entry is written by RWB-P7-E1027-APP and this story writes no entry |
| approval | P7 (`rwb_decision`) | Contracted use only: `source_ref` may name the template version of an approval; the approval row is RWB-P7-E2013-APP's and this story writes none |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_decision` | Created with the schema; this story writes no row of any of them |

`template` and `merge_field` are P6 rwb-comms's in `rwb_comms`; `lov_value` is P3 rwb-case's; `sys_fields` and the data dictionary are P1 rwb-source-data's; `document` is P5 rwb-document's. None of them is declared as owned here, read directly or copied (DP-01, BR8).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision`, module `templateuse`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision.templateuse`; the artefact is the `rwb-decision` api deployment of the service template.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

Six patterns are applied and every one is a row above. Two readings matter and are stated rather than silently resolved. First, the DP rows add `H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON`, `H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON` and `H RWB-PLT-N001-CON` while the plan's build list is empty; the three are read as wave-0 platform prerequisites of the service template, so the lane L-P7-M and the Day-1 start do not change (GAP-2453; ASM-4066). Second, DP-11 carries the legacy in-process catalog call across the service boundary and the only dependency it adds is the plan's C row RWB-P6-E1046-CON, which is built against and faked. DP-05 is not claimed because this story reads no ACE view and no data dictionary; DP-03, DP-08 and DP-16 are not claimed because this story writes no decision entry, declares no authorise call and reaches no integration adapter.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| TemplateUseRecorder | Service | The one entry point: takes the answer facts, calls the catalog and the lists, applies BR1 to BR5 and BR9, and writes the row in the caller's unit of work |
| CatalogClient | Client | The current-version read, the merge-field read and the catalog-version read on RWB-P6-E1046-CON, with the 2 s budget, the GET retry and the breaker |
| MergeCodeChecker | Service | Compares the merge codes of the answer with the set of the version and the catalog version in force |
| CatalogRefusalMapper | Service | Maps each refusal of the owner and each local check to its message ID of section 14, never to an accepted row |
| TemplateUseEntity, TemplateUseRepository | Entity, Repository | Map and write `template_use`; the append-only guard; the audit read by template and business date |
| ReferenceListReader | Service | Reads LOV-NOTICE and LOV-PRODUCT through the reference-data client (DP-07) |

**Database and migration.** `template_use` in `rwb_decision` with the keys and checks of section 11, created by `V_E1046__template_use.sql` in the per-service sequence (DP-15). The table is written by insert only; a trigger or a missing grant refuses UPDATE and DELETE, following the append-only pattern of the ledger.

**Configuration and reference data.**

- The catalog base URL, the list base URL and the timeouts are configuration, never a value in code.
- The feature switch is `rwb.decision.template-use`; off means the recording is refused with MSG-GEN-006 and no answer is recorded without its version, never a silent accept.
- The login is the rwb-decision login (DP-02); its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2453; ASM-4070).

**Build steps**

1. The migration, the entity and the repository with the unique key and the append-only refusal; test them on Testcontainers.
2. `CatalogClient` on the catalog fake with the 2 s budget and the retry, and the refusal mapping of MSG-P6-005, MSG-P6-003 and MSG-P6-006; test AC2, AC3 and AC5.
3. `MergeCodeChecker` against the merge-field read and the catalog version in force; test AC4.
4. `ReferenceListReader` and the MSG-GEN-001 refusal for an unknown notice type; test AC8.
5. `TemplateUseRecorder` with the business-date rule and the one-unit-of-work rule; test AC1 and AC6.
6. The append-only and no-catalog-table assertions of AC7, including a schema scan and a dependency scan.
7. A contract-fake run in isolation, so the story builds before rwb-comms and rwb-case are live.

**Done when.** The nine test cases of section 16 pass, the migration runs clean on an empty schema and on the SIT schema, the contract tests of RWB-P6-E1046-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON stay green, and no merge value, template body or personal value appears in a log or an evidence line.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P6-005 | The catalog answers no Approved version for the template code and language | {template} version {version} has no Legal approval. It cannot be used. |
| MSG-P6-006 | An answer uses a merge code not in the catalog version in force | {template} uses the merge field {field}, which is not in the merge field catalog. The load was refused. |
| MSG-P6-003 | The only version in force is withdrawn | The {template} template has been withdrawn. The notice is on hold until Legal approves a new version. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required value is missing on the answer, or the notice type or product group is not in the list in force | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A catalog or list read does not answer inside the 2 s budget, or the feature switch is off | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |

The texts of MSG-P6-005, MSG-P6-006 and MSG-P6-003 are copied character for character from RWB-E1-046 section 14 and keep their legacy meanings; MSG-GEN-001 and MSG-GEN-006 are the platform messages of the same legacy section. The word "load" in MSG-P6-006 is the legacy wording and is kept unchanged even though this story refuses an answer and loads nothing. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10; no new message ID is introduced by this story.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen is built here. The values of a row are read back on the decision-log view that RWB-P7-E2005-APP serves and that the gateway-bff composite route projects (DP-19): a reader with the Decision log right asks for an entry and sees the template code, the version, the catalog version, the notice type, the product group and the valid-from date of the answer. The screen field list and the route specification belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON, and the read itself to RWB-P7-E2005-APP.

SCR-33 Template catalog admin and SCR-40 Reference data are the legacy screens of the catalogue and stay P6's (RWB-P6-E1046-APP, RWB-P6-E1034); their states — Loading, Read only, Draft, Approved and Withdrawn — describe the catalog, not this row. The row's own states are the three of section 9, and a refused answer leaves no state behind because no row is written.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: template codes, merge codes, languages, notice types, product groups, catalog versions and dates come from the catalog contract, the list contract or the caller; no such value appears in Java, a resource file or a migration.
- No personal data in rows, events, workflow inputs, logs, tests or prompts. The row holds codes, versions, identifiers and dates; a merge value is resolved at generation time by the owner and never stored here.
- No template body and no merge value in a row, a payload, a log or an evidence line; the body stays the owner's claim-check file behind `body_ref`.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or the `v_ace_*` views: this story reads no ACE table and no ACE view, and reads no `sys_fields` and no data dictionary.
- No cross-schema read and no copy: `rwb_decision` holds no foreign key into another schema and no catalog row; `template` and `merge_field` stay P6's (DP-01, BR8).
- One REST base and one topic per service; this story declares neither a new operation nor a new event (DP-13).
- The row is append only: an update and a delete are refused, and an answer keeps the version it was decided under (BR6, R-UNI-38).
- One hop, a 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream; a failed read refuses the answer and never accepts a partial version (BR11).
- Every fixture is synthetic and uses the legacy identifiers only; no production payload is copied into a test or a fake.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the secondary P5 slice of RWB-E1-046. It binds a document generated by `rwb-document` to one Legal-approved template version and to the merge field catalog in force, with schema `rwb_document`, REST base `/api/recovery/document/v1` and the contract of `rwb-comms`. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **litigation officer (RW-LITOFF)**, I want **every document `rwb-document` generates or regenerates to be stamped with the one Legal-approved template version it came from and to carry only merge values the catalog in force knows**, so that **a letter on a case can always be traced to the approved wording it used, and a template change never silently alters a document already issued**.

Inside `rwb-document` this is the document-side binding of the catalog, not the catalog itself:

- Service `rwb-document`, schema `rwb_document`, REST base `/api/recovery/document/v1`, topic `rwb.document.events.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document`.
- **This is the secondary P5 slice of RWB-E1-046 and it owns no legacy acceptance criterion.** Legacy AC1 to AC8 stay where the split puts them: RWB-P6-E1046-APP carries the version numbering, the approval columns, the merge code check, the field-ID check, the repeat load and the current-version selection, and RWB-ITG-E1046-ITG carries the composed proof. The nine criteria of section 7 are new under D-RCV-60 and test only the P5 binding.
- **The catalog stays with its owner.** `template` and `merge_field` are P6's tables in `rwb_comms` (ownership map; RWB-P6-E1046-CON 12.7). This service creates neither, copies neither and never reads `rwb_comms` by SQL: it asks the catalog contract for the version in force and for its merge field list, one hop, 2 s timeout (DP01, DP11).
- **The local facts are `document.template_id` and `document_field`.** `document.template_id` (DF-DOC-032) holds the identifier of the catalog version the document was generated under, and each merge value is written as a `document_field` row whose `field_name` (DF-DOC-014) is a merge code of that catalog version. The legacy relationship "`document.template_id` many to 0 or 1 `template`" (TSD P5 v2 T3.3) becomes a soft reference across services with no foreign key and no cross-schema join.
- **Three operations of the service run the binding step** — `POST /cases/{caseId}/generated-documents` (API-P5-016), `POST /documents/{documentId}/regenerate` (API-P5-017) and `PATCH /documents/{documentId}/fields/{fieldId}` (API-P5-006). This story adds no endpoint; it supplies `TemplateVersionBinder`, `MergeValueBinder` and `CatalogCurrentVersionClient`, which those operations call (12.1).
- **No event is published and none is consumed.** The service's two events, `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` and `rwb.document.DocumentFieldsExtracted.v1`, belong to RWB-P5-E1024-APP and RWB-P5-E1053-APP; DP-09 is not a pattern of this story and the stamp is not announced.
- The reference lists are read as data through the rwb-case reference-data contract (DP07); the base is the owner's base (DP13); the index the binding needs is one step in the per-service Flyway sequence (DP15); the screen path is the gateway-bff composite route (DP19).
- The database login is one per service (DP02) and its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2343; ASM-3897); this story says "the rwb-document login".

##### 2. Business rationale

Legacy RWB-E1-046 makes the wording of a notice a data release: Legal approves a template version, and generation may use only a version that is Approved and may fill only fields the catalog knows. The P6 slice builds that catalog. This slice answers the other half of the same control: the document that was actually produced must carry the version it used, and the values inside it must be values the catalog allowed (CTL-14; REQ-OCC-002). Without it, an approved version could be replaced after a letter was issued and nothing on the case would show which wording was sent.

The realignment changes the mechanics, not the rule:

1. **One schema, one base.** `rwb_document` replaces the recovery schema and `/api/recovery/document/v1` replaces the monolith base (DP01, DP13). No `recovery.*` table and no `rwb_comms` table is named by a statement of this service.
2. **The catalog is a contract, not a table.** The in-process `TemplateCatalog` interface becomes the `rwb-comms` catalog contract (DP11), with a fake from Day 1, so the P5 binding builds before P6 is ready. A refusal from the catalog is carried to the caller unchanged: MSG-P6-005 for a version with no Legal approval, MSG-P6-003 for a withdrawn version, MSG-P6-006 for a merge code outside the catalog.
3. **The stamp is an identifier, not a copy.** The document holds `template_id` only. The code, language, approval user, approval date, body and valid-from of the version stay with their owner and are read when they are needed; no denormalized template attribute is written into `rwb_document` (BR3).
4. **Merge values become document fields.** A merge value is a `document_field` row with the merge code as its name, so the document index, the PATCH of one field and the extraction index answer the same rows (RWB-P5-E1024-APP, RWB-P5-E1053-APP). A code marked `personalData` is masked by role on every read and never logged (Guardrails).
5. **A regenerate is a new version under a new stamp.** The earlier version keeps the stamp it was issued under; the new one carries `previous_version_id`, the catalog version in force at the regenerate and its reason (API-P5-017; BR4).

It serves REQ-OCC-001 by holding the merge values of a notice as catalog-checked fields and REQ-OCC-002 by making the approved version an identifier on the document the officer signed (FSD P5 measure "notices with proof of delivery, 100 percent" is the P6 side of CTL-14).

##### 3. Preconditions

| Precondition | What it gives this story |

| RWB-P6-E1046-CON, published | The catalog contract and its fake: the template resource, the merge field resource, the catalog version in force, the state values, the message IDs and the error envelope (DP11, C) |
| Catalog fixture "MF-2026.11" and the template fixture pack | The five merge codes of the legacy Background, template "DEMAND-MTG" "TH" versions 1, 2 and 3, "RECALL-HP" "TH" with one Draft version, and a withdrawn version 2 (12.8) |
| rwb-case reference-data contract (RWB-P3-E1043-CON) | LOV-LANG, LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-NOTICE, LOV-CHANNEL and LOV-SIGNATURE-BASIS at the version in force, so no list value is typed in code (DP07, DP11) |
| Per-service Flyway sequence (RWB-PLT-E1044-CON) | The one migration step of this story, after the V0001 baseline in `rwb_document` (DP15) |
| gateway-bff composite route (RWB-PLT-N001-CON) | The route that publishes the generation screen and asks this service one hop; the route is not built here (DP19) |
| `document` and `document_field` in `rwb_document` | The two P5 tables of the binding, with DF-DOC-032 and DF-DOC-012 to DF-DOC-017 and DF-DOC-034 and DF-DOC-035 (TSD P5 v2 T3.1) |
| Document generation and field capture | `POST /cases/{caseId}/generated-documents`, `POST /documents/{documentId}/regenerate` and `PATCH /documents/{documentId}/fields/{fieldId}` exist in the service contract; the generation engine, the body rendering and the template content read are RWB-P5-E2026-APP's |

Business preconditions carried from RWB-E1-046, unchanged in value:

- Case `RW-2026-000102` exists with an approved treatment, so a document may be generated for it; the case is read through the rwb-case contract, not through a case table.
- Catalog version "MF-2026.11" is in force from 2026-11-01 with merge codes "CASE_NO", "CUSTOMER_NAME", "POSTAL_ADDRESS", "TOTAL_OUTSTANDING" and "NOTICE_DATE"; template "DEMAND-MTG" "TH" version 1 was Approved by "LEG-0001" on 2026-10-01.
- The user holds Documents U for a regenerate and Documents C for a generation (TSD P5 v2 T6.1: RW-LITOFF is CRU, RW-LEGAL is CRUA).
- No masking rule from Compliance is loaded (DL26). Until the rules load, a merge field marked `personalData` is masked for every role but RW-LEGAL.
- Feature flag `rwb.document.template-binding` is on (ASM-3900).

The build-dependency row is None and the contract-dependency row carries one entry, both copied as the Work Package fixes them. The three platform contracts named above (DP07, DP15, DP19) are the service template's baseline, and the rwb-case reference-data contract is not in the C row; both facts are recorded rather than edited into the rows (GAP-2344; ASM-3897, ASM-3898).

The database login is one per service (DP02); its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2343; ASM-3897).

##### 4. Flow

1. Caller: generates documents for an approved treatment, or corrects the merge values of one generated draft with a reason, and so reaches API-P5-016, API-P5-017 or the one-field PATCH API-P5-006. The generation engine, the body and the content read are RWB-P5-E2026-APP's.
2. `CatalogCurrentVersionClient`: asks the catalog contract for the version in force for the template code and language on the business date, with the merge field list of that version. One hop, 2 s timeout, breaker per downstream, GET retried once with jitter (DP11).
3. `TemplateVersionBinder`: refuses when the catalog answers no Approved version (MSG-P6-005, naming template and version) or a withdrawn version (MSG-P6-003). Nothing is rendered and no row is written.
4. `MergeValueBinder`: reads every merge code of the body and of the request and compares it with the catalog list of the version in force. An unknown code refuses the whole document (MSG-P6-006, naming the code) and writes no row; a required code with no value refuses it in full (MSG-GEN-001, naming the merge code).
5. `TemplateVersionBinder`: stamps `document.template_id` with the catalog version identifier the contract returned, and writes nothing else of the version.
6. `MergeValueBinder`: writes one `document_field` row per merge value of the version, with `field_name` set to the merge code, the value, its confidence when the engine supplies one and the extractor version. A code marked `personalData` is stored and masked on read; it is never written to a log.
7. `DocumentVersionService` (API-P5-017): on a regenerate, re-reads the catalog (step 2), requires a reason, writes the next `doc_version` with `previous_version_id` set to the earlier document and `template_id` set to the version now in force; the earlier row keeps its own stamp unchanged.
8. `DocumentHubController`: answers the document or the page. No outbox row is written by this slice: the stamp and the fields travel with the `DocumentStored` event that RWB-P5-E1024-APP publishes, and that event carries identifiers and counts only.
9. A refused step writes nothing at all — no document row, no field row, no version — so a half-stamped document cannot exist.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The catalog answers a version that is not Approved | Refused before rendering; nothing written | MSG-P6-005 | AC4 |
| X2 | The catalog answers a withdrawn version | Refused; nothing written; the earlier document version keeps its stamp | MSG-P6-003 | AC5 |
| X3 | The body or the request uses a merge code not in the catalog version in force | Refused in full; the code is named; no document row and no field row | MSG-P6-006 | AC3 |
| X4 | A required merge code has no value | Refused in full; the merge code is named | MSG-GEN-001 | AC6 |
| X5 | A regenerate carries no reason | Refused with 422; the version chain is unchanged | MSG-GEN-001 ("reason") | AC7 |
| X6 | The catalog contract does not answer inside 2 s, or its breaker is open | Refused with 503; nothing written; no cached version past its time-to-live is used | MSG-GEN-006 ("Template catalog service") | AC8 |
| X7 | A statement names `rwb_comms`, `template` or `merge_field`, or the schema holds a key into another schema | The build fails and names the statement or the constraint; at the database the statement fails with SQLSTATE 42501 | None (build log) | AC9, TC-E1-046-10 |
| X8 | A role without Documents U regenerates, or without Documents C generates | Refused with 403 before any row is read | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-046-09 |
| X9 | A merge value of a code marked `personalData` reaches a log line or an event payload | The guard test fails the build; the value is replaced by the field name in a trace | None (build log) | AC9 |

Two target-service notes:

- A refusal is a refusal of the whole document, never a partial write: the validation of steps 3 and 4 runs before the first insert, and a failed catalog read writes nothing.
- The message texts are the catalog contract's and the legacy story's, unchanged; this service produces them with the placeholders filled and never invents a wording of its own.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against the catalog contract and its fake, the reference-data fake, the two P5 tables and the service template; it creates no other story's work and needs no other story's build |
| Negotiable | The template codes, merge codes, languages, dates and catalog version are data; the story fixes only the binding, the checks and the version-chain rule |
| Valuable | Every generated document is traceable to the approved version it used, and no document carries a value the catalog does not know |
| Estimable | Three components, one index step, no endpoint and no event |
| Small | Under one week with its tests and its contract fake |
| Testable | Each criterion in section 7 is one test case in section 16, on the fixture pack of 12.8 |

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A document is generated or regenerated only from a template version the catalog returns as current, and a current version is Approved with its Legal approver and approval date | RWB-E1-046 BR1, BR2; REQ-OCC-002; CTL-14 |
| BR2 | Every merge value of a generated document is a code of the catalog version that stamped it, and no other field name is written by the binding | RWB-E1-046 BR4; REQ-OCC-001 |
| BR3 | The document holds the catalog version identifier only: no template attribute, no approval field and no body is copied into `rwb_document` | RWB-E1-046 BR6; DP01; ASM-3898 |
| BR4 | A regenerate writes a new document version with `previous_version_id` and a reason, and leaves the stamp of every earlier version unchanged | RWB-E1-046 BR6; API-P5-017; R-UNI-38 |
| BR5 | A document with a refused version, a refused code or a missing required value is refused in full and writes nothing | RWB-E1-046 BR5; refdata change process, step 3 |
| BR6 | A withdrawn version stops generation until Legal approves a new one, and the refusal names the template | RWB-E1-046 BR3; R-LIT-04, R-LIT-06 |
| BR7 | Templates are owned by Legal counsel as reference data, and the approval on a version is that authority | RWB-E1-046 BR7; DL28 |
| BR8 | A merge field marked `personalData` is masked by role on every read and is never written to a log, an event payload, a workflow input or a test prompt | RWB-E1-046 section 17; PDPA; DL26 |
| BR9 | The declared Documents right of the operation is enforced before any row: C to generate, U to regenerate or correct a field | TSD P5 v2 T6.1 |
| BR10 | The catalog is read as a contract, one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker; a failed read is a refusal and never a cached or assumed version | DP11; ADR-020 |

Where each rule lives in the target: no rule changes, and three change their mechanism. BR1, BR2, BR3 and BR6 are answered by the catalog contract: the current version, its state and its merge field list arrive in one answer, the identifier is what the document stores, and a refused answer refuses the document. BR4 is a row in `rwb_document`: the version chain is `previous_version_id` plus `doc_version`, and a regenerate never updates an earlier row. BR5 is enforced on this service's own rows: validation runs before the first insert. BR7 is an authority statement and stays with P6's approve operation. BR8 is a guardrail plus a masking call; BR9 is the guard of the service template; BR10 is the client and the fake. No template code, merge code, language or date is a constant in Java.

##### 9. State transitions

None for the case. This story changes no case status and no template version state; it writes the state of a document version only, on the standard record columns of TSD P5 v2 T3.0.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | Generate (API-P5-016) | The catalog answers a current Approved version and every merge code of the body is in its list with a value | A document row with `template_id` set and its `document_field` rows written |
| None | Generate or regenerate | The version is Draft, is Withdrawn, a code is outside the catalog, a required value is missing or the catalog does not answer | No row written; the previous document and its stamp are unchanged |
| A generated version | Regenerate (API-P5-017) | A reason is given and the catalog answers a current version, which may be a later one | The next `doc_version`, with `previous_version_id` and the new `template_id` |
| A generated version | PATCH of one field (API-P5-006) | The field name is a merge code of the version stamped on that document and the caller holds Documents U | The same document version with the corrected field value and its `confirmed_by` |

The version in force can change between two generations of the same template code; that moves nothing on a document already written, and the next generation takes the version current on its own business date (BR4).

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer | Generates a document and corrects one field (Documents CRU) |
| RW-LEGAL, legal counsel | Generates and regenerates, and reads a personal merge value unmasked (Documents CRUA) |
| RW-CREDITAD, Credit Administration officer | Generates the contract and CA documents (Documents CRU) |
| RW-CREDITAD or RW-LITOFF, on an approved treatment | Starts the generation of a document set for the case |
| SY-CASEWF, case workflow module | Calls the generation for a case transition (Documents R, generation through the case flow) |
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Reads the documents and their stamps (Documents R) |
| The rwb-comms catalog | Owns the template version, its approval and the merge field catalog; this service reads it and writes none of it |
| The rwb-document service identity | Writes `document` and `document_field` only, under the rwb-document login |

Every "who" is a role code. The rights are the legacy ones and are enforced by the platform guard library the service template carries; this story's pattern set does not include the access pattern, so it adds no dependency for the guard and holds no role table. The role codes, their rights and their separation of duty stay with rwb-access (P4) and are not read here. No approval level from the delegation of authority applies to this slice: the approval is the Legal approval recorded on the catalog version.

`document` and `document_field` are P5's in `rwb_document` (ownership map). `template` and `merge_field` are P6's in `rwb_comms`: they are never read by SQL from this service, only through the catalog contract (DP01, DP11), and the version identifier that comes back is the value written to `DF-DOC-032`. The standard record columns of TSD P5 v2 T3.0 are written by the platform persistence layer. `document_type` is read for the type code of the document and is not written here.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None new. This slice adds no endpoint, no path and no resource to `/api/recovery/document/v1`; it supplies the binding step of three operations of the service, each provided by its own story:

| Operation | Provided by | What this story adds to it |
|---|---|---|
| POST /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/generated-documents (API-P5-016) | RWB-P5-E2026-APP | Steps 2 to 6 of section 4: the current-version read, the version stamp and the merge value rows; the engine, the body and the content read stay there |
| POST /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/regenerate (API-P5-017) | RWB-P5-E2026-APP | The re-read of the catalog, the reason requirement and the new stamp on the next `doc_version` |
| PATCH /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/fields/{fieldId} (API-P5-006) | RWB-P5-E1024-APP | The check that the field name is a merge code of the version stamped on that document, before the value is updated |

A consumer of those three operations sees no change to their declared shape. The exact request field names of `GenerateRequest` and `RegenerateRequest`, the reason field of the regenerate and the error body of a refused document are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2344; ASM-3899). Every response remains an OpenAPI 3.1 contract published before code, with `Idempotency-Key` on the two POSTs.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Provider | Why | Pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET /api/recovery/comms/v1/admin/templates (API-P6-003), with the current-version answer | rwb-comms (P6), contract RWB-P6-E1046-CON | The version in force for a template code and language on a business date, with its state, its Legal approval and its merge field list; one hop, 2 s timeout, breaker, cached for the life of the request | DP11, C |
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode} | rwb-case (P3), reference-data contract | LOV-LANG, LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-NOTICE, LOV-CHANNEL and LOV-SIGNATURE-BASIS in force, so a list value is data and never a constant | DP07, DP11 |

The catalog baseline declares the list operation and the content operation but **no operation that answers the current version for a code, language and date**: the current-version rule is RWB-P6-E1046-APP's, and this consumer has no operation to call for it. The story builds against the fake's current-version answer and records the missing operation as one gap (GAP-2345; ASM-3898). The rwb-case list read is not in the contract-dependency row, which the Work Package fixes as one entry (GAP-2344; ASM-3898). No parameter is read: nothing of this story is tunable by parameter.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The service's two events, `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` and `rwb.document.DocumentFieldsExtracted.v1`, are declared and published by RWB-P5-E1024-APP and RWB-P5-E1053-APP; this slice writes no outbox row and DP-09 is not in its pattern set. The stamp travels inside the `DocumentStored` payload that the store publishes, as an identifier only.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. No event starts a generation or a regenerate: both are synchronous calls from the case flow or the officer, and the catalog is read on demand.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` is the intake workflow of the service and belongs to RWB-P5-E1032-APP and RWB-P5-E1057-APP; the binding runs inside the caller's request, in one transaction per document version, and DP-10 is not in this pattern set.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Schedule, no cron entry and no job of this story: JOB-12 and JOB-17 of the service are other stories' work, and the version in force is resolved by the read, not by a job that moves it.

| Table | Schema | Owner (ownership map) | This story |
|---|---|---|---|
| document | rwb_document | P5 | Writes `template_id` (DF-DOC-032), `doc_version` and `previous_version_id`; reads the case reference and the type |
| document_field | rwb_document | P5 | Writes one row per merge value, DF-DOC-012 to DF-DOC-017 and DF-DOC-034 and DF-DOC-035 |
| template, merge_field | rwb_comms | P6 | **Never read.** Reached over the catalog contract only (DP01, DP11) |

Database access uses the rwb-document login (DP02); its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2343; ASM-3897). No statement in this story names a table in another schema, and `rwb_document` holds no key into another schema: the catalog version identifier is a value, not a foreign key.

| File | 0 | 0 | The template body is a claim-check file read from the catalog by RWB-P5-E2026-APP, not by this slice |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document`, module `templates`. Service base `/api/recovery/document/v1`, schema `rwb_document`, topic `rwb.document.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-document` (not used by this story).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| CatalogCurrentVersionClient | Client | Calls the catalog contract for the version in force and its merge field list; one hop, 2 s timeout, breaker, GET retried once with jitter; caches for the life of the request only |
| TemplateVersionBinder | Service | Refuses a version that is not Approved or is withdrawn; stamps `document.template_id` with the catalog version identifier and copies nothing else |
| MergeValueBinder | Service | Compares every merge code of the body and the request with the list in force; refuses an unknown code or a missing required value whole; writes one `document_field` row per value |
| DocumentVersionLinker | Service | Writes the next `doc_version` with `previous_version_id` on a regenerate and requires a reason |
| TemplateBindingRepository | Repository | Reads and writes `document` and `document_field` in `rwb_document` only; no cross-schema SQL |
| TemplateBindingConfig | Configuration | Feature flag `rwb.document.template-binding`, the catalog client base URL and the timeouts |

**Database**

- No column is added: `document.template_id` (DF-DOC-032), `document.doc_version`, `document.previous_version_id` and the `document_field` columns already exist in TSD P5 v2 T3.1.
- One index, `ix_document_template` on `document` (`template_id`, `doc_version`), so the version chain of a document is one index range.
- One Flyway step `V1046_1__document_template_binding.sql` in the per-service sequence, after the V0001 baseline (DP15, H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON). The index name and the step name are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2344; ASM-3899).
- No constraint into another schema: `template_id` carries no foreign key, because `template` is P6's table in `rwb_comms` (DP01).

**Configuration and reference data**

- The catalog is data: template codes, merge codes, languages, channels, notice types, signature bases, approval users and valid-from dates are rows in `rwb_comms` and rows of the fake; none is a constant.
- The five reference lists arrive through the rwb-case reference-data contract (DP07).
- Feature flag `rwb.document.template-binding`. Off: a generation refuses with 503 and the feature-off error of the service template, and no document is stamped (ASM-3900).

**Build steps**

1. Write the catalog client against the OpenAPI document of RWB-P6-E1046-CON and point it at the WireMock of 12.8; test the 2 s timeout, the breaker and the delayed answer (AC8).
2. Build `TemplateVersionBinder` with the Approved and Withdrawn refusals and the identifier-only stamp; test AC1, AC4 and AC5.
3. Build `MergeValueBinder`: code comparison, required-value check and one row per value; test AC2, AC3 and AC6.
4. Build `DocumentVersionLinker`: reason requirement, `previous_version_id` and the untouched earlier row; test AC7.
5. Write the migration step and the index; run the boundary test on `rwb_document` that no statement names `rwb_comms` and no key leaves the schema (AC9).
6. Wire the three components into the three operations of 12.1 behind the flag, and run the guard and guard log tests; add TC-E1-046-10 to the build.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

Each row in place. DP-01 puts the stamp and the merge values in `rwb_document` and is why the catalog is a contract and not a table: `template` and `merge_field` stay in `rwb_comms`, the document holds an identifier, and no statement here names another schema. DP-07 supplies the five reference lists as data. DP-11 makes the catalog read one hop with a mock and a 2 s timeout, so the build starts on the fake before P6 publishes and the in-process `TemplateCatalog` call becomes a testable contract. DP-13 moves the base to `/api/recovery/document/v1`. DP-15 is the Flyway step `V1046_1__document_template_binding.sql`, with no baseline and no monolith name reused. DP-19 is the gateway-bff route to the generation screen; this story builds no screen.

The H, C, I and X rows are the Work Package's: the build row is None and the contract row is one entry. The platform contracts named by DP-07, DP-15 and DP-19 are the service template's baseline and the rwb-case list read is consumed against its fake; neither is added to a row (GAP-2344; ASM-3897, ASM-3898).

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, a generated document in SIT carries the identifier of the version in force, no `document_field` row holds a code outside it, the boundary test of AC9 is green, and the catalog fake drifts from RWB-P6-E1046-CON in no field this service reads.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P6-005 | The version in force has no Legal approval | {template} version {version} has no Legal approval. It cannot be used. |
| MSG-P6-006 | The body or the request uses a merge code outside the catalog | {template} uses the merge field {field}, which is not in the merge field catalog. The load was refused. |
| MSG-P6-003 | The version in force is withdrawn | The {template} template has been withdrawn. The notice is on hold until Legal approves a new version. |
| MSG-P1-002 | The catalog refuses the version or the catalog version in force | The {source} load for {date} was refused: {check}. The previous load is still in use. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required merge value is missing, or a regenerate carries no reason | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The catalog contract does not answer inside 2 s | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller holds no Documents right for the operation | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The message IDs and texts are the legacy ones and the catalog baseline's, unchanged; Thai text for each message follows decision DL10. For MSG-GEN-001 the {field} value is the merge code or the word "reason"; for MSG-GEN-006 it is "Template catalog service"; for MSG-P6-005 and MSG-P6-003 the template code and version come from the catalog answer.

Delivery shape: every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set to the ID above, `detail` carrying the text with its placeholders filled, and `instance` naming the request. A refused generation answers 403, 422 or 503 and writes nothing; a refused regenerate answers 403, 404, 409, 422 or 503 and leaves the version chain unchanged.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story. The generation screen is RWB-P5-E2017-APP's (Epic 2) and reaches this service through the gateway-bff composite route (DP19); SCR-33 Template catalog admin is P6's and is never served by this service. What the officer sees of the binding is one line on the generated document: the template code and version of the stamped catalog version, read from the catalog by identifier, and its Legal approval date. The only state this story writes is the document version state of section 9.

The nine legacy test cases are carried because the Work Package lists them for this slice, in the legacy order, with the P5 part of each named in the Covers column; their legacy acceptance criteria are owned by RWB-P6-E1046-APP and the composed cross-service proof is RWB-ITG-E1046-ITG, whose copies carry the `-ITG` suffix and are not listed here. TC-E1-046-10 is new under D-RCV-60 for the timeout and the boundary build check. Every level is Component or Contract because the fixture drives the three components directly; an End to end copy belongs to RWB-ITG-E1046-ITG. The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID where one exists.

##### 17. Guardrails

- **No business value in code.** Template codes, merge codes, languages, channels, notice types, signature bases, approval users and dates are rows of the catalog or of the fake; the merge codes of the fixture appear in tests only.
- **No personal data in logs, events, workflow inputs, tests or prompts.** A merge value of a code marked `personalData` is replaced by its field name in a trace, never written to a log line, and never put in an event payload; the fixtures of sections 7 and 16 are synthetic.
- **No cross-schema read and no cross-schema key** (DP01): every statement names `rwb_document` only, `template_id` carries no foreign key into `rwb_comms`, and the catalog arrives over its contract.
- **ACE data only through the owner's contract or the `v_ace_*` views.** This module reads no ACE view and holds no grant on the recovery schema; the case is read through the case contract.
- **The stamp is an identifier only** (BR3): a template attribute, an approval field or a body copied into `rwb_document` fails the boundary test of AC9.
- **A refusal writes nothing.** The version check and the merge code check run before the first insert, and a failed catalog read writes no row and creates no version.
- **One catalog answer per request.** No version is cached beyond the request, so a version withdrawn or replaced between two calls is never reused.
- **The guard is the service template's.** This story configures the Documents right of three operations and builds no guard, no role table and no access row.
- **No event and no workflow is added.** The two service events and `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` stay with their own stories.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: integration slice of RWB-E1-046 for RWB-ITG-W1. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **QA integration engineer**, I want **the end-to-end proof of the RWB-E1-046 template and merge field catalog across P3 rwb-case (the reference-load path), P1 rwb-source-data (the field registry), P6 rwb-comms (template and merge_field), P5 rwb-document (the body and the generated letter) and P7 rwb-decision (the approval decision)**, so that **a template change is proved as a data release before wave 1 exits**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story keeps the catalog and the templates in the recovery schema with a P4 load path, checks every catalog row against sys_fields in the same module and lets the letter engine read the current version through an in-process published interface. The target puts the reference-load operations on P3 rwb-case (DP-07, Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41), the field registry on P1 rwb-source-data (the data dictionary contract of the data engine), the catalog rows on P6 rwb-comms (Architecture v5 slide 17: notices, templates, merge fields, proof of delivery), the template body on P5 rwb-document (the document hub and its Blob custody) and the Legal approval of a version as a decision record that reaches the rwb-decision ledger (DP-03, ADR-022). The split keeps every legacy check and changes only the owner of each artifact and the call type between them.

The legacy measures stand unchanged. A notice may only be produced from a Legal-approved template version whose merge fields the catalog knows, which serves REQ-OCC-001 and REQ-OCC-002 and the FSD P6 measure "notices with proof of delivery, 100 percent" under control CTL-14: every notice traces to one known template version and one catalog version in force. A template change is a data release approved by Legal and never a code release, so the same catalogue build proves the change without a deployment.

No service contract is faked. The suite exercises the published wave 1 contracts of the five services under their own per-service bases behind gateway-bff, and every call is one hop with a 2 s timeout (ADR-020, DP-11). Where the sources do not name the service that performs the field-ID check across the split, the container that holds the template body, or the point at which the approval of a version becomes a decision record, the suite asserts through the owners' contracts and records the open point as `Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0360; ASM-0469)`.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P1-E1001-APP is done: the entity and field registry of rwb-source-data answers the data dictionary contract for every BR Field ID.
- RWB-P1-E1069-APP is done: the data dictionary and freshness surfaces of rwb-source-data are published and deployed in SIT.
- RWB-P6-E1046-APP is done: the template and merge_field tables live in rwb_comms, version numbering assigns the next version per template code and language, and the state is set from the approval columns.
- RWB-P5-E1046-APP is done: the body reference resolves through the document hub and a letter can be generated for a case.
- RWB-P7-E1046-APP is done: the central ledger collects rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1 and answers the decision-log query.
- The published contracts of P1 rwb-source-data, P3 rwb-case, P5 rwb-document, P6 rwb-comms and P7 rwb-decision are deployed under their own per-service bases behind gateway-bff.
- Lists LOV-LANG, LOV-PRODUCT and LOV-NOTICE are loaded and in force on the business date.
- The merge field catalog file and the template files are prepared by the reference data administrator (RW-REFADM), one row per merge field with its BR Field ID, and the template files carry the Legal approval columns where Legal has signed.
- The catalog version MF-2026.11 is in force on the business date.
- The Blob container for the template body is available (Azurite in the lower environment) and body_ref names an object in it.
- The harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG is available with its synthetic cases and its clock control.
- No production data is used and no production connection is opened.
- The release date 30 November 2026 is tentative; a date is not a condition of this story, and there is no build dependency, so the story is ready on Day 1.

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: loads the 12-row merge field catalog file through the P3 reference-load path with table `merge_field` and the valid-from date; the P3 operation stores the load and the P6 handler answers for the rows.
2. Harness: verifies the load through the P3 verify operation and reads the refused rows; a refused load names the failing row check and stores no row.
3. Harness: loads the DEMAND-MTG TH version 2 file with the Legal approval columns, then reads the template versions and their state through the P6 contract.
4. Harness: reads version 2 and version 1 through the P6 content operation and asserts that version 1 is unchanged, with its own approver and approval date, and that both point at a body in the container.
5. Harness: loads the GUARANTOR-SSME file whose body uses the merge code GUARANTOR_EMAIL, which no catalog row defines, and reads the refusal.
6. Harness: repeats the first successful load with the same file hash and asserts that no new version is created and that DEMAND-MTG still has two versions.
7. Harness: generates one letter through the P5 generated-documents operation on the case, reading the template through the P6 catalog at generation time, and repeats the generation with the clock control on 2026-11-10, on 2026-11-30 and on 2026-12-01.
8. Harness: reads the approval decision of template DEMAND-MTG version 2 through the P7 decision log and compares the approver, the template code and the version.
9. Harness: posts the negative cases — a catalog row with no body_ref, a Draft-only template, a withdrawn version and a role without the reference-data right — and records every message and status.
10. Harness: writes the evidence report with the load results, the version numbers, the generated documents, the decision-log entry, the messages and the counts, and removes the synthetic fixtures.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Generation asks for a template whose versions are all Draft | The current version is refused; nothing is generated; the missing approval is named | MSG-P6-005 | AC7 |
| X2 | A template uses a merge code that is not in the catalog in force | The whole load is refused; the unknown merge code is named; no version is created | MSG-P6-006 | AC3 |
| X3 | A catalog row names a BR Field ID that is not in the data dictionary | The whole catalog load is refused in full; the check is named; no row is stored and the catalog version in force stays in force | MSG-P1-002 | AC1 |
| X4 | A template row has no template code, language or body reference | The whole load is refused; the field is named | MSG-GEN-001 | AC4 |
| X5 | The same template file is loaded twice | The second load creates no new version; the repeat is named | MSG-P1-002 | AC5 |
| X6 | The only Approved version is withdrawn | No current version is returned and generation holds | MSG-P6-003 | AC7 |
| X7 | A version has valid from in the future | The earlier Approved version stays current until that date | None | AC6 |
| X8 | A role without the reference-data right posts a load | Status 403; nothing is loaded and no version is created | MSG-P4-002 | AC8 |
| X9 | A consumed contract call exceeds the 2 s timeout or returns a server error | The step is retried under the pack policy; the evidence report records the call and the response; no load, version or generation result is asserted on unverified data | None | AC1, AC2, AC6 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | The suite is its own module and reuses the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG; it needs the five APP stories and the published contracts of P1, P3, P5, P6 and P7, not their source code |
| Negotiable | The merge codes, the template codes, the languages, the field mappings and the valid-from dates are data rows of the load files; the story fixes the checks, the current-version rule and the call set |
| Valuable | A template change is proved as a data release approved by Legal before wave 1 exits, and every check the legacy story held is proved across the five owners |
| Estimable | One suite module, one load-file fixture pack with its file hash, one clock control, one generation assertion and one evidence report |
| Small | Ten scenarios over five services; no service code and no schema change |
| Testable | Every scenario asserts a contract response, a version number, a version state, a generation result, a decision-log entry or a message; all data is synthetic |

```gherkin
    Given a template load file whose row has no body reference
    When it is loaded
    Then the system refuses the load in full with MSG-GEN-001 naming "body_ref"

  Scenario: AC5 A repeated load of the same file hash creates no new version (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the load file of AC2 has been loaded once and version 2 exists
    When the same file with the same file hash is loaded again
    Then the system refuses the load with MSG-P1-002 naming the check "repeat of load"
    Then "DEMAND-MTG" still has 2 versions

  Scenario: AC6 The current version is chosen at generation time across the two services (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given version 3 of "DEMAND-MTG" "TH" is Approved with valid from 2026-12-01
    When a letter is generated for a synthetic case through the P5 generated-documents operation on 2026-11-10, on 2026-11-30 and on 2026-12-01
    Then the P6 catalog returns version 2 as current on 2026-11-10 and on 2026-11-30
    Then the P6 catalog returns version 3 as current on 2026-12-01
    Then the generated document is confirmed by rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1 and records the version it used

  Scenario: AC7 A Draft-only template and a withdrawn version leave no usable current version (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given template "RECALL-HP" in language "TH" has only version 1 in state "Draft"
    When the pack asks the P6 catalog for the current version of "RECALL-HP", "TH"
    Then the catalog refuses with MSG-P6-005 naming "RECALL-HP" version 1
    Given version 2 of "DEMAND-MTG" "TH" was Approved and current and is now in state "Withdrawn"
    When a letter is generated for a synthetic case on 2026-11-20
    Then the catalog returns no current version and refuses with MSG-P6-003 naming "DEMAND-MTG"
    Then generation holds and no document is stored

  Scenario: AC8 A role without the reference-data right is refused at the load path (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a user holds RW-LITOFF, a role without the reference-data right
    When the user posts a catalog load through the P3 reference-load path
    Then the service refuses the call with status 403 and MSG-P4-002
    Then nothing is loaded and no version is created

  Scenario: AC9 The approval of a template version reaches the decision ledger (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the load of "DEMAND-MTG" "TH" version 2 approved by "LEG-0001" on 2026-11-10 completed
    When the pack reads GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log
    Then one entry names approver "LEG-0001", template "DEMAND-MTG" and version 2
    Then the entry is visible within five minutes of the load

  Scenario: AC10 No template body or merge value leaves the service in an event or a log (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the events of the run on rwb.decision-record.v1 and rwb.document.events.v1 and the service logs of the run are collected
    When the pack searches them for the template body and for the resolved merge values
    Then they carry template codes, catalog versions, template versions and counts only
    Then a merge field marked personal_data carries no value in any event, log or evidence line
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A template version is used only when its state is Approved and it carries the Legal approver and approval date | RWB-E1-046 BR1; REQ-OCC-002; CTL-14 |
| BR2 | The current version for a template code and language on a date is the Approved version with the highest version number whose valid from is on or before that date | RWB-E1-046 BR2; R-LIT-03 (template_status = current) |
| BR3 | A withdrawn template has no current version, and generation holds until Legal approves a new one | RWB-E1-046 BR3; R-LIT-04, R-LIT-06 |
| BR4 | Every merge code a template uses exists in the catalog in force, and every catalog row names a BR Field ID in the data dictionary | RWB-E1-046 BR4; REQ-OCC-001; Principle 1 |
| BR5 | A load with any refused row is refused in full and the previous catalog version stays in force | RWB-E1-046 BR5; refdata change process, step 3 |
| BR6 | Earlier versions are never changed or deleted; open cases keep the version they were generated under | RWB-E1-046 BR6; refdata change process, step 6; R-UNI-38 |
| BR7 | Templates are owned by Legal counsel as reference data | RWB-E1-046 BR7; DL28 |
| BR8 | P6 rwb-comms owns the template and merge_field rows, P1 rwb-source-data owns the field registry, P3 rwb-case owns the reference-load path and P5 rwb-document owns the body; no service holds a copy of another service's table and the pack reads each through its owner's contract | Architecture v5 slide 17 and slide 41; DP-01; ASM-0469; ASM-0470 |
| BR9 | The approval of a version is written as one local decision record by the owning service in its own schema and is collected into the P7 central ledger within five minutes; the pack reads the approval only through the ledger | DP-03; ADR-022; ASM-0472 |

##### 9. State transitions

None for the case status. This story does not change a case status. It reads and asserts the template version state, the reference load state and the current-version selection.

| Object | State | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Template version | Draft | Loaded without an approver or an approval date; it is never a current version |
| Template version | Approved | Loaded with the Legal approver and approval date; it may be current from its valid-from date |
| Template version | Withdrawn | Withdrawn by Legal; it is no longer current and generation holds until a new version is Approved |
| Reference load | Loaded | Every row passed its checks and the rows are stored |
| Reference load | Refused | At least one row failed a check; no row of the file is stored and the catalog version in force stays in force |
| Reference load | In force | The loaded catalog version that every later load and every generation is checked against |

The pack moves a load from Loaded to Refused and a version to Withdrawn through the owners' contracts; it never writes a state directly.

| Service owner of rwb-document | Owns the body, the container and the generated document |
| Service owner of rwb-decision | Owns the central ledger and the decision-log query |

No other role is in scope for this story. No delegation-of-authority level applies.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The pack provides no REST operation. The names reserved for P2 rwb-integration — /api/recovery/integration/v1, rwb.integration.events.v1, rwb-integration and rwb_integration — are not used, and no rwb_integration table is written.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method and path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|
| POST /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads | P3 rwb-case | Load the merge field catalog file and the template file with the table and the valid from date |
| POST /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/verify | P3 rwb-case | Verify a load and read the refused rows |
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode} | P3 rwb-case | Read LOV-LANG, LOV-PRODUCT and LOV-NOTICE in force |
| GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/data-dictionary/fields | P1 rwb-source-data | Check every BR Field ID named by the catalog |
| GET /api/recovery/comms/v1/admin/templates | P6 rwb-comms | Read the template versions and their state |
| GET /api/recovery/comms/v1/admin/templates/{templateId}/content | P6 rwb-comms | Read the body reference and the merge codes of a version |
| POST /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/generated-documents | P5 rwb-document | Generate one letter so the catalog is read at generation time |
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId} | P3 rwb-case | Read the case the letter is generated for |
| GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log | P7 rwb-decision | Read the approval decision record |

Every call is one hop with a 2 s timeout (ADR-020, DP-11).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The pack publishes no event.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Producer | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1 | rwb.decision-record.v1 | Every service; the ledger is owned by P7 rwb-decision | Follow the approval decision from the owning service into the central ledger |
| rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1 | rwb.document.events.v1 | P5 rwb-document | Confirm that the generated letter was stored and read the version it used |

No event is produced by the pack. The ledger is complete within five minutes of the decision (ADR-022, DP-03).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The letter is generated by the P5 generated-documents operation; no workflow is started by the pack, and the pack reads no workflow history.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The pack fires no Schedule and reads no Schedule state; the loads and the generations are triggered by the pack itself on the dates named in section 7.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The pack owns no table and never reads another service's schema (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

External stubs only:

| Stub | Use |
|---|---|
| Legal approval identity recorded on the load file | The approver named in the load file is the approval identity; no directory call is made |
| Azurite Blob container for the template body and the generated letter | The lower environment stands in for the managed container; the object layout is the production layout |
| Synthetic case and clock control (harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG) | Supplies the case and moves the business date so the current-version rule can be read on three dates |

No service contract is faked: every call in section 12.2 goes to the real SIT service under its published wave 1 contract.

|---|---|---|

##### 13. Solution plan

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Suite module for RWB-ITG-W1, reusing harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG | Integration suite | Runs the ten scenarios against SIT and holds no service code |
| Load-file fixture pack | Test data | The 12-row catalog file, the DEMAND-MTG TH version 1 and version 2 files, the DEMAND-MTG TH version 3 file, the GUARANTOR-SSME file, the RECALL-HP file, the file with no body_ref, and the SHA-256 file hash of each |
| Current-version clock control | Harness control | Moves the business date to 2026-11-10, 2026-11-30 and 2026-12-01 and restores it after each assertion |
| Generation assertion | Assertion | Calls the P5 generated-documents operation and reads the template version recorded on the stored document |
| Evidence report | Report | Records per scenario the load id, the refused rows, the version numbers and states, the generated documents, the decision-log entry, the messages and the counts |

Decoupling patterns applied (Template and Rules v1 §R5.5):

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added | Where it sits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | recovery.<table>, "recovery schema" | Owner's schema rwb_<name>; never read another service's tables | none | template and merge_field sit in rwb_comms, the body in P5, the field registry in P1; the pack asserts through contracts only |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON | The reference-load path and the three lists of section 12.2; on the APP stories, not a build dependency of the pack |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) | The nine consumed REST operations of section 12.2 |
| DP-13 | /api/recovery/v1 | /api/recovery/<short>/v1 | none | Every consumed path in section 12.2 |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON | The history of template and merge_field in rwb_comms; on the APP stories, the pack changes no schema |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The reference load record is read through gateway-bff; no screen is built by this story |

The H, C, I and X lists are exactly those of the metadata table: no build dependency, no contract dependency, the five integration dependencies RWB-P1-E1001-APP, RWB-P1-E1069-APP, RWB-P6-E1046-APP, RWB-P7-E1046-APP and RWB-P5-E1046-APP, and no external dependency.

Build steps:

1. Create the suite module next to harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG and wire it to the SIT endpoints of P1, P3, P5, P6 and P7.
2. Build the load-file fixture pack and record the SHA-256 file hash of every file as a data row.
3. Add the current-version clock control and the restore step for the three business dates.
4. Implement the ten scenarios of section 7 in TC order and assert only through the contracts of section 12.2 and the events of section 12.4.
5. Add the load-result assertions: refused rows per load, the catalog version in force, the version number and state created, and the catalog version that stays in force on a refusal.
6. Add the generation assertion at the three business dates and compare the version used with the version the catalog reports as current.
7. Add the decision-log assertion and the log and event scan for template bodies and merge values, including the merge field marked personal_data.
8. Run the pack in SIT against the wave 1 release candidate and keep the evidence report with the wave exit evidence.

Done when: all eleven test cases pass in SIT against the published wave 1 contracts, the evidence report is attached to the wave exit pack, and no service code or schema was changed by this story.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P6-005 | Generation asks for a template with no Approved version | {template} version {version} has no Legal approval. It cannot be used. |
| MSG-P6-006 | A template uses a merge code not in the catalog | {template} uses the merge field {field}, which is not in the merge field catalog. The load was refused. |
| MSG-P6-003 | The current version is withdrawn | The {template} template has been withdrawn. The notice is on hold until Legal approves a new version. |
| MSG-P1-002 | A catalog load fails a check, or repeats a load | The {source} load for {date} was refused: {check}. The previous load is still in use. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field is empty in a load row | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the reference-data right posts a load | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| RPT-E1046-GEN | Generation check report, one line per generated letter | Case {case} used template {template} language {language} version {version} on {date}; {count} merge codes resolved at generation time; no merge value recorded. |

The message IDs and wording are copied from RWB-E1-046. No new message ID is added by this story; RPT-E1046-GEN is an evidence report line, not a service message. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.
