##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One service, one schema, one login: the release uses the rwb-document login and no other service's credential | DP-02; Architecture v5 slide 29 |
| BR2 | The migration is a per-service Flyway sequence in schema `rwb_document` and runs before the deployment is ready | DP-15; RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| BR3 | Every subscription has a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic, and a consumer never acknowledges an event it could not process | DP-09; Architecture v5 slide 22 notes |
| BR4 | The outbox relay runs every minute and is the platform standard of JOB-11; it is not rebuilt per story | Architecture v5 slide 44; DP-09 |
| BR5 | JOB-12 is a Temporal Schedule of this service; no Quartz row, no shared job table entry and no Control-M job is registered | DP-10; Architecture v5 slide 44 |
| BR6 | No environment value is hard-coded: replica counts, resource sizes, the business-hours window, thresholds and the flag state come from values files | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR7 | An alert carries a message ID and the agreed text where one maps, and links exactly one runbook entry | Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR8 | A refused read is counted and never pages the on-call rota | MSG-P4-002 |
| BR9 | A re-run of a business date never reads a DONE item twice and never writes a second text row for a page | legacy AC8, AC9; R-UNI-40 |
| BR10 | No dashboard series, log line or alert payload carries page text or personal data; intake IDs, document IDs, statuses, counts and durations only | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR11 | The pipeline's time promise is operational: every scan becomes text the same day and an unreadable page is sent back for rescan the same day | RWB-E1-049 story intent; FSD P5 A2.7.1 |

##### 9. State transitions

The release and the Schedule move through these states; no business object moves.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | Chart published | The image, the chart and the migration job pass the pipeline | Deploying |
| Deploying | Migration complete and probes healthy | The schema is at the expected version, the relay runs and the worker polls `rwb-document` | Ready |
| Ready | Schedule registered | Exactly one Schedule exists and the retirement of the Quartz job is recorded | Armed |
| Armed | Release superseded | A new chart version is promoted | Rolling |
| Rolling | All pods on the new version | The old ReplicaSet drains and the worker build ID is the new one | Armed |
| Armed | Alert on a failed run, held items or a queue with no poller | The condition passes its value | Alerted; the runbook entry opens |
| Alerted | Re-run of the business date, or the owner's repair | The items move and the status is what the run wrote | Armed |
| Armed | Flag turned off | The `ocr` activity is skipped and the reads still answer | Armed, capability off |
| Armed | Rollback | The previous chart version and the previous flag state are restored | Armed on the previous version |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| DevOps engineer | Owns the chart, the values files, the pipeline stages, the Schedule registration, the dashboards, the alerts and the runbook |
| Platform administrator | Owns the `rwb-recovery` namespace, the topic set, the visibility queries behind JOB-21 and the re-run of a job on SCR-44 |
| ACE database administrator | Owns schema `rwb_document`, the login and its grants, and approves the migration job |
| OCR provider owner | Owns the engine endpoint, its quota and its availability window; is paged by the engine alert and owns the repair beyond the pipeline's client |
| Release manager | Approves the promotion of one artefact through the environments and the rollback |
| On-call operator | Runs the runbook entries and opens an incident when a failed run or a held-item spike persists |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Sees the run counts and the alerts on SCR-44 in the running service, not in the cluster |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Receives the rescan notice of MSG-P5-018 for a held item of their case, through the running service |

The per-service login used by the chart is a secret reference resolved at deploy time; the chart references "the rwb-document login (DP-02)" and never a literal name. The deployment slot and the exact business-hours window are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1001; ASM-1783).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The deployment exposes the four operations of RWB-P5-E1049-CON behind gateway-bff: the intake submit, the intake item read, the text read and the OCR status read. The probes are cluster-internal and are not part of the API surface, and this story adds no path.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. The deployment configures the client timeouts and the breakers of the consumed rows declared in RWB-P5-E1049-CON and adds no call of its own.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. `rwb.document.OcrCompleted.v1` is RWB-P5-E1049-APP's; the deployment reuses `rwb.document.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics as provisioned by its owner and creates no topic.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None declared. The subscription of the `ingest` activity to `rwb.document.events.v1` is provisioned in the step of section 13 and described in AC1 and AC2, and its shape belongs to RWB-P5-E1049-CON.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Deployment element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` | Workflow, one run per Schedule tick and business date | `rwb-document` | Worker deployment with the build ID of the release; holds the five activities in order |
| `ingest` | Activity, P5 | `rwb-document` | Registered by the same worker; creates the intake item from `DocumentStored` |
| `ocr` | Activity, P5 | `rwb-document` | Registered by the same worker; selects and locks the pending items, calls the engine and writes the status and the text |
| `classify` | Activity, P5 | `rwb-document` | Registered by the same worker; owned by RWB-P5-E1050-APP |
| `extract` | Activity, P5 | `rwb-document` | Registered by the same worker; owned by RWB-P5-E1053-APP |
| `matchStep` | Activity, P5 | `rwb-document` | Registered by the same worker; owned by RWB-P5-E1032-APP |

Exactly one worker build serves the workflow and all five activities; a release that leaves one of them unregistered fails the readiness check of AC2.

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Schedule | Cron | Overlap | What it starts |
|---|---|---|---|
| Document intake (legacy JOB-12) | Every 15 minutes in business hours, Asia/Bangkok, from the environment values | SKIP, with the catch-up window of the kit | `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` on `rwb-document` |

Exactly one Schedule is registered per environment, and no Quartz row, shared job table entry or Control-M job is created. The exact business-hours window is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1001; ASM-1783).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The migration job creates and migrates the tables of RWB-P5-E1049-APP in schema `rwb_document`; this story owns no table and adds no column. `document`, `document_type` and `document_hub_parameter` belong to their P5 stories and the migration job touches schema `rwb_document` only (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

None. The fakes are test-only workloads of RWB-P5-E1049-CON; the SIT smoke profile of section 13 runs against them and they are not deployed into UAT or production.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | None | No operation is provided or consumed by the deployment itself |
| Kafka | None | No topic is created; the event and the consumed event ride `rwb.document.events.v1` with retry and `.dlt` |
| Temporal | 1 workflow, 5 activities, 1 Schedule | `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` with `ingest`, `ocr`, `classify`, `extract` and `matchStep` on `rwb-document`, and the 15-minute business-hours Schedule registered once per environment |
| File | 1 dotted grey path | The intake file read and the OCR JSON written at `ocr/{intakeId}.json`, through the storage product; the smoke profile asserts the path against the stub |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Artefacts**

| Artefact | Content |
|---|---|
| `helm/rwb-document/` | Chart with api and worker deployments, service, migration job, config map, secret references, probes and the Schedule registration hook |
| `helm/rwb-document/values-dev.yaml`, `values-sit.yaml`, `values-uat.yaml` | Image digest, replicas, resources, probe timings, log level, `rwb.document.ocr`, the Schedule state and its business-hours window, the client timeouts, the alert thresholds |
| Pipeline stage | Build, unit, component and contract tests, the retired-element check, image and dependency scan, chart publish, one artefact promoted through the environments |
| Schedule registration step | Exactly one document-intake Schedule, its cadence, its window, its overlap and its catch-up, plus the recorded retirement of the Quartz job |
| Provisioning step | The consumer subscription on `rwb.document.events.v1` with retry and `.dlt`; reuse of `rwb.document.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1`; task queue `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery` with all five activities registered |
| Outbox relay | The platform standard of JOB-11, one relay per service, with lag and dead-letter series |
| Dashboards | Six panels: intake volume, OCR failure rate, held items, queue depth and scale events, outbox lag, workflow health |
| Alerts | Five rules, each with a message ID where one maps, and one runbook entry |
| Runbook | Five entries: failed run, held item, re-run of a business date, stuck workflow, outbox relay stopped |
| Smoke profile | The SIT run of section 13's step 10 against the four fakes |

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The platform H rows are delivered by the platform waves and are not repeated in the metadata H field, which stays empty. DP-10 is the pattern this story serves: the Schedule registration and the worker deployment are the operational form of "no shared Quartz", and the retired-element check proves that no Quartz row survives the release. DP-09 is the failure path of the event, DP-15 the migration the release runs, and DP-19 the route the four operations are read through. DP-01, DP-06, DP-07, DP-11 and DP-13 add no work here: they are the shapes the deployment carries.

**Probes.** Readiness answers healthy only when the migration is at the expected schema version, the outbox relay is running, the Temporal worker on `rwb-document` has polled and all five activities are registered; liveness answers healthy when the process is up and its internal loop is responsive. Neither probe writes to the database and neither calls another service or the OCR engine.

**Alert mapping**

| Message ID | Condition | Alert | Route |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-006 | A run fails twice on the engine, or the engine error rate passes its value | Failed-run alert with the run, the business date, the failed count and the engine endpoint reference | Platform on-call, page; ticket to the OCR provider owner and the rwb-document owner |
| MSG-P4-002 | A read without the Documents right is refused | Refusal count on the dashboard | No page |
| None | Held items past their age value, or their count rising while the runs complete | Held-item alert with the reason, the count and the oldest item | Platform on-call, page; the held-item runbook entry |
| None | No worker polls `rwb-document`, or the queue depth rises while the runs complete | No-poller or queue-depth alert with the backlog and the scale events | Platform on-call, page |
| None | The outbox lag passes its value, or the dead-letter count rises | Relay alert with the lag and the oldest row | Platform on-call, page |
| None | The stuck-workflow scan of JOB-21 raises a `rwb-document` workflow | Stuck-workflow alert with the workflow ID, the business date and the last event | Platform on-call, page |

Every alert carries its message ID where the condition maps to one, and the conditions without one carry the series or the workflow name instead. The thresholds and the held-item age are deployment values with provisional defaults; the missing source is carried by the gap and the assumption of section 14 (GAP-1001; ASM-1783).

**Done when.** The chart renders for the three environments and the migration job runs before the pods are ready; the worker serves `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` with all five activities; exactly one Schedule exists and no Quartz row survives; the flag is off and on in the expected environments and the off state is safe; the six panels and five alerts answer a synthetic day, including a failed run with MSG-GEN-006 and a held-item spike; the five runbook entries resolve and each alert links exactly one; the smoke profile passes against the four fakes; the rollback has been rehearsed once in UAT after a business-hours run that read 180 items and held one for rescan.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-006 | The engine did not answer, a run failed twice, or a consumed call failed | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P5-018 | A held item of a known case is notified again after a re-run | Page {page} of {document} on case {case} could not be read. Scan it again and send it to the document hub. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the Documents right reads an item | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

MSG-P5-018 and MSG-P4-002 are the legacy messages copied unchanged; MSG-GEN-006 is the unavailability shape the alert of a failed run uses, naming "OCR service". Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

Delivery shape: the alert payload carries the message ID where one maps, the environment, the business date, the run identifier, the counts and the runbook path; it never carries a page text, a file name with a customer value or a personal value.

##### 15. Screens and states

No Workbench screen in this story. The operator surfaces are the workbook "Document intake" (six panels and the alert list) and SCR-44 Interface and job monitor, which shows the same run counts in the running service. The four states the operator reads are Running, Complete, Failed and Waiting, as defined by the app story; the deployment adds the flag state and the Schedule state per environment, which are configuration and not a screen state.

|---|---|---|---|
| TC-P5-E1049-OPS-01 | AC1 | Component | The chart rendered for DEV, SIT and UAT with the login reference, the migration job and the api and worker probes |
| TC-P5-E1049-OPS-02 | AC2 | Integration | One business date run with all five activities registered; one release with `extract` unregistered, which fails readiness |

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: thresholds, the held-item age, the business-hours window, the replica counts and the flag state are values-file entries.
- No personal data in logs, metrics, alerts, tests or prompts; the run record and the dashboards hold intake IDs, document IDs, statuses, counts, durations and role names only, and never a page text.
- No read of another service's tables and no read of a table in schema `public`; the case owner comes through the owner's contract and no ACE view is read by this service.
- A runbook names roles and service identities, never a person.
- No runbook describes a hand-registered Schedule, a Quartz row or a Control-M job; the Schedule is registered from configuration only.
- No secret, credential or connection string appears in a runbook, a dashboard panel or an alert payload; each is a secret reference.
- The re-run path never reads a DONE item twice and never writes a second text row for a page; the guard is the status predicate and the unique page index of the app story.
- The flag removes the capability without a rollback of the schema, and the rollback restores the previous flag state with the previous chart version.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: integration slice of RWB-E1-049 for RWB-ITG-W1. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **QA integration engineer**, I want **the end-to-end proof of the RWB-E1-049 OCR step across P5 rwb-document (the intake item, the text and layout, the OCR step of DocumentIntakeWorkflow), P3 rwb-case (the case owner the rescan notice goes to) and P6 rwb-comms (the notice)**, so that **every inbound file becomes searchable text and an unreadable page is sent back the same day, proved on the real services before wave 1 exits**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story runs JOB-12 as a Quartz job inside the document module with document_intake and document_text in the recovery schema. The target keeps both tables in rwb_document (Owner P5, Architecture v5 slides 16 and 41), starts the OCR step inside DocumentIntakeWorkflow from the DocumentStored event plus the JOB-12 trigger with KEDA workers (Architecture v5 slide 44), dedupes the duplicate event through the inbox (DP-09), reads its four parameters as data rows and returns the rescan notice to the case owner through P6 rwb-comms. The trigger, the meaning of the worker cap and the home of the four parameters are not fixed by the sources: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0362; ASM-0476).

The legacy measures stay as they are: REQ-DCM-006 (fields extracted in Thai and English, which needs Thai and English text first), REQ-DCM-009 (every path ends in the same intake item), REQ-DCM-010 (a file is read only after its malware scan is CLEAN) and FSD P5 A2.7, whose measure is fields extracted without review (FSD P5 A2.7.1).

No service contract is faked. The suite exercises the published wave 1 contracts of P3, P5 and P6, the shared Temporal namespace and the standard container; the only stubs are the external ones named in section 12.8. Where the sources do not name the trigger, the worker cap or the evidence location, the suite asserts through the owners' contracts and the open point is recorded as GAP-0362 and ASM-0476.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P5-E1049-APP is done: document_intake and document_text, the OCR step of DocumentIntakeWorkflow, the OcrClient adapter and the rescan notifier are in SIT.
- RWB-P3-E1045-APP is done: the case and its owner are readable through the rwb-case contract.
- RWB-P6-E1049-APP is done: MSG-P5-018 is sent through the ACE notification path and the notice is readable through the rwb-comms contract.
- The published contracts of P3 rwb-case, P5 rwb-document and P6 rwb-comms are deployed under their own per-service bases behind gateway-bff: /api/recovery/case/v1, /api/recovery/document/v1 and /api/recovery/comms/v1.
- Temporal namespace rwb-recovery with task queue rwb-document is available.
- The OCR service is reachable in SIT through the OcrClient adapter under the identity SY-OCR, and its stub is available for the unavailable-service scenario.
- The standard container is available (Azurite in the lower environment).
- The document hub parameters OCR_MIN_QUALITY 0.70, OCR_WORKERS 4, OCR_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 120 and OCR_MAX_ATTEMPTS 3 are loaded (legacy values, all assumed; ASM-0477).
- The 180 synthetic sample documents, 30 of each of the six agreed types, and the 500-page set in 125 items are in the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG.
- The feature flag rwb.dochub.ocr is on.
- No production data is used, and no production connection is opened.
- The release date 30 November 2026 is tentative; a date is not a condition of this story.
- No build dependency: the story is Day 1 and waits on no build of its own.

##### 4. Flow

1. QA integration engineer: loads the synthetic fixtures of harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG; no production data is used.
2. Harness: stores a synthetic upload through POST /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents and waits for rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1 on rwb.document.events.v1.
3. Harness: reads the intake item through GET /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId} and asserts one intake item for the stored file; it delivers the same event twice with the same event id and asserts one intake item and one inbox record (AC1).
4. Harness: replaces the stub with the real OCR service, which answers under the identity SY-OCR, and runs the 180-sample set; the item states, the ocr_ref, the page rows, the languages and the Thai and English text are asserted (AC2).
5. Harness: runs the 500-page set in 125 items with OCR_WORKERS 4 and times the window from the first item starting (AC3).
6. Harness: reads the intake item and the document with its text pages through GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId} (AC2, AC3).
7. Harness: posts the threshold cases — page 3 at quality 0.41 on case RW-2026-000123 owned by TEST-CO-01, a 2-page mailroom scan with no case and page 1 at 0.30, and one page at exactly 0.70; it reads the case owner through GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId} and the notice through GET /api/recovery/comms/v1/notices/{noticeId} (AC4, AC5, AC6).
8. Harness: makes the stub return HTTP 503 for two JOB-12 runs, records the job monitor state and the alert, restores the service and lets the next run finish the items (AC7); it posts the password-protected PDF and asserts the unreadable outcome with no text row (AC8).
9. Harness: reruns over 10 items already DONE, starts four workers on one CLEAN pending item, changes OCR_MIN_QUALITY as a data row and reruns one scenario (AC9, AC10).
10. Harness: asserts the refusal of a role without the Documents right (AC11), writes the evidence report and removes the synthetic fixtures.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A page has quality below OCR_MIN_QUALITY | The item is set RESCAN with the page numbers; the case owner is told, or the item goes to the review queue with review_reason RESCAN | MSG-P5-018 | AC4, AC5 |
| X2 | Page quality exactly at OCR_MIN_QUALITY | The page is accepted and the item can end DONE | None | AC6 |
| X3 | The OCR service does not answer within OCR_TIMEOUT_SECONDS or returns an error | ocr_attempts increases; the item stays PENDING for the next run; after two failed runs the job monitor shows the step failed and an alert is raised to the platform administrator | None | AC7 |
| X4 | The item reaches OCR_MAX_ATTEMPTS or the file cannot be opened | ocr_status FAILED and review_reason UNREADABLE_FILE; no text row is written | None | AC8 |
| X5 | The run covers items already DONE | Those items are not read again and no second set of text rows appears | None | AC9 |
| X6 | Two workers start on the same item | The row lock lets one worker take the item; the other skips it and one call is made | None | AC9 |
| X7 | A user holds a role without the Documents right and reads a document holding OCR text | Refused with 403 and no text returned | MSG-P4-002 | AC11 |
| X8 | A consumed contract call exceeds the 2 s timeout or returns a server error | The step is retried under the run policy; the evidence report records the call and the response; no assertion is made on unverified data | None | AC1, AC2 |
| X9 | The stub cannot be replaced by the real OCR service, or a fixture of the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG does not match | The suite fails as a harness fault and names the element; no service defect is raised | None | AC2, AC3 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | The suite is its own module and reuses the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG; it needs the three APP stories and the published contracts of P3, P5 and P6, not their source code |
| Negotiable | The quality threshold, the worker cap, the timeout, the attempt limit and the fixture sizes are data rows of the harness; the story fixes the assertions and the call set |
| Valuable | The OCR text, the quality rule, the rescan notice and the throughput target are proved on real services before wave 1 exits |
| Estimable | One suite module, one fixture pack, one OCR stub, one worker control and one evidence report |
| Small | Eleven scenarios over three services and one workflow; no service code and no schema change |
| Testable | Every scenario asserts a contract response, an item state, a text row, a notice or a message; all data is synthetic |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: OCR pipeline on the Workbench document hub, end-to-end across wave 1 services

  Background:

    Then the text holds Thai and English words, and the languages th and en are recorded where both appear

  Scenario: AC3 500 pages in 125 items finish within 60 minutes with the worker cap (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given 500 pages in 125 CLEAN intake items in SIT
    When they are processed with OCR_WORKERS 4
    Then all 125 items reach DONE or RESCAN within 60 minutes of the first item starting

  Scenario: AC4 An unreadable page on a known case is sent for rescan and the case owner is told (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given an uploaded court notice of 4 pages on case RW-2026-000123 owned by TEST-CO-01
    Given page 3 has quality 0.41 and the other pages are above 0.70
    When the OCR step runs
    Then the intake item has ocr_status RESCAN and rescan_pages 3
    Then TEST-CO-01 receives MSG-P5-018 naming page 3, the document and case RW-2026-000123 through P6

  Scenario: AC5 An unreadable page with no case goes to the review queue with no notification (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a mailroom scan of 2 pages with no case and page 1 at quality 0.30
    When the OCR step runs
    Then the intake item has ocr_status RESCAN, rescan_pages 1 and review_reason RESCAN
    Then no notification is sent

  Scenario: AC6 A page exactly at the quality threshold is accepted (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a scan of 1 page at quality 0.70
    When the OCR step runs
    Then the item has ocr_status DONE and no rescan pages

  Scenario: AC7 An OCR service that does not answer is retried and alerted (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the OCR stub returns HTTP 503 for every call
    When JOB-12 runs twice
    Then each pending item has ocr_status PENDING and ocr_attempts 2
    Then the job monitor shows the OCR step failed in both runs and an alert is raised to the platform administrator
    Then when the service answers again the next run sets the items DONE

  Scenario: AC8 A file that cannot be read ends FAILED with the unreadable reason (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a password-protected PDF as a CLEAN intake item
    When the OCR step runs
    Then the item has ocr_status FAILED and review_reason UNREADABLE_FILE
    Then no document_text row exists for it

  Scenario: AC9 A repeat run reads nothing twice and two workers read one item once (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given 10 intake items already DONE with 25 document_text rows
    When JOB-12 runs again
    Then the OCR service receives no call for those items
    Then they still hold 25 document_text rows
    Given one CLEAN pending item and four workers starting at the same time
    When the OCR step runs
    Then the OCR service receives exactly one call for the item
    Then the item has one set of document_text rows

  Scenario: AC10 The four OCR parameters are read as data and a change needs no deployment (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given OCR_MIN_QUALITY is changed in the document hub parameter table and one scenario is rerun
    When the run completes
    Then the outcome changes with no code change and no deployment
    Then the four values are read from the document hub parameter table whose owner the Ownership Map names

  Scenario: AC11 A role without the Documents right is refused (new, D-RCV-60)

```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every inbound file is read in Thai and English | RWB-E1-049 BR1; REQ-DCM-006; FEAT-DCM-07 |
| BR2 | Scans, partner files, emails and uploads go through the same intake item and OCR step | RWB-E1-049 BR2; REQ-DCM-009 |
| BR3 | A file is read only after its malware scan is CLEAN | RWB-E1-049 BR3; REQ-DCM-010; FEAT-DCM-18 |
| BR4 | A page below OCR_MIN_QUALITY is sent for rescan; the threshold is inclusive | RWB-E1-049 BR4; document hub parameter OCR_MIN_QUALITY; DL11 |
| BR5 | A system that does not answer is retried on the next run and alerted after two failed runs | RWB-E1-049 BR5; R-UNI-33; JOB-12 |
| BR6 | An item read once is not read again | RWB-E1-049 BR6; R-UNI-40 |
| BR7 | Worker count, timeout and attempts are parameters | RWB-E1-049 BR7; Principle 1; DT02 |
| BR8 | P5 rwb-document owns document_intake and document_text; no other service holds a copy and the suite reads them only through the P5 contract | Ownership Map (document_intake and document_text owner P5); Architecture v5 slides 16 and 41; DP-01 |
| BR9 | One intake item exists per stored file; a duplicate DocumentStored event creates no second item because the inbox dedupes it | DP-09; ASM-0476 |

##### 9. State transitions

None for the case status: this story changes no case status. It observes the intake item OCR state inside rwb_document through the P5 contract.

| Object | State | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Intake item | PENDING | The item is CLEAN and waiting for the OCR step |
| Intake item | PENDING (after a failed call) | The call failed below the attempt limit; ocr_attempts increased and the next run takes the item again |
| Intake item | DONE | Every page is at or above OCR_MIN_QUALITY and the text rows are written |
| Intake item | RESCAN | At least one page is below OCR_MIN_QUALITY; rescan_pages holds the page numbers, and review_reason RESCAN is set when no case is known |
| Intake item | FAILED | The attempt limit was reached or the file cannot be opened; review_reason UNREADABLE_FILE |

The suite reads these states and never writes them.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| QA integration engineer | Runs the suite, seeds the synthetic fixtures, reads the evidence report |
| SY-OCR, OCR and extraction pipeline | Reads intake files, writes OCR output and text rows (Documents CRU) |
| RW-CASEOWN | Receives the rescan notice for their case |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Sees the job counts and alerts in the job monitor; reruns JOB-12 |
| Roles with Documents R | Read the OCR text of documents in their scope |

No other role is in scope for this story. The suite acts as the QA integration engineer and asserts the other roles only through the contracts.

The case owner comes through the P3 contract and the notice through the P6 contract. Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary. Every row in the suite is synthetic.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The suite provides no REST operation. The names reserved for P2 rwb-integration — /api/recovery/integration/v1, rwb.integration.events.v1, rwb-integration and rwb_integration — are not used.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method and path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|
| POST /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents | P5 rwb-document | Store the synthetic uploads that raise DocumentStored |

Build steps:

1. Create the suite module next to harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG and wire it to the SIT endpoints of P3, P5 and P6.
2. Build the fixture pack: the 180 synthetic documents, 30 of each of the six agreed types in Thai and English, and the 500-page set in 125 items.
3. Add the OCR stub with fixed pages per file and the HTTP 503 mode, and the switch to the real OCR service under the identity SY-OCR.
4. Implement AC1 to AC3 — the intake dedupe, the 180-sample run and the 500-page window — and assert only through the contracts of section 12.2, the event of section 12.4 and Temporal visibility.
5. Implement the threshold cases AC4 to AC6, reading the case owner through the P3 contract and the notice through the P6 contract.
6. Implement AC7 to AC9: the two failed runs and the alert, the unreadable file, the repeat run and the four workers on one item.
7. Implement AC10 and AC11: change OCR_MIN_QUALITY as a data row, rerun one scenario, and post the read by a role without the Documents right.
8. Write the evidence report with the throughput line, the item state counts and the message ids, and keep it with the wave exit evidence.

Done when: all twelve test cases pass in SIT against the published wave 1 contracts, the 500-page set finishes within 60 minutes with OCR_WORKERS 4, the evidence report is attached to the wave exit pack, and no service code or schema was changed by this story.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the threshold, the workers, the timeout and the attempts are parameters, changed as data rows.
- No personal data in logs, events, evidence or fixtures. OCR text is never written to application logs; logs carry the intake id and counts only; test documents are synthetic.
- No cross-service table read: the case owner comes through the P3 contract, the notice through the P6 contract and the intake item through the P5 contract.
- One hop and a 2 s timeout on every call (ADR-020).
- OCR text stays in document_text and the standard container; it is not sent to any service other than the OCR service.
- Synthetic data only; the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG loads the fixtures.
- No production access of any kind from the suite or its configuration.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the classification step moved into `rwb-document` as the `classifyStep` activity of the intake workflow over the schema `rwb_document`, the topic `rwb.document.events.v1`, the REST base `/api/recovery/document/v1` and the queue `rwb-document`; the legacy thresholds, type codes, review reasons, evaluation sample and messages are kept character for character. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **each scanned document classified into one of the six agreed types with a confidence score, and any document below the threshold sent to the review queue with its top two candidate types**, so that **each document is filed under the right type and checklist item without a person typing it**.

Inside `rwb-document` this is the classification capability of the document service:

- Service `rwb-document`, schema `rwb_document`, REST base `/api/recovery/document/v1`, topic `rwb.document.events.v1` with event names `rwb.document.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document`.
- Classification is a service-internal capability fed by the intake workflow: the `classifyStep` activity of `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` selects `document_intake` rows, masks the text, calls the internal `ClassifierClient` through `ModelGatewayClassifier`, ranks the scores and writes the classification columns on the intake row. The model provider, the endpoint route and the model version behind `ClassifierClient` are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1002; ASM-1789): the legacy story reaches a model through the P10 model gateway set under DL33 and Architecture v5 slide 16 draws the classify run as a child of `rwb-agent`, so the satellite is tracked as external work and the plan's C list is not extended with an invented dependency id.
- The type codes and their labels come from `document_type` in the version in force (`valid_from` and `valid_to`, table version DOCTYPE-2026.11), a P5 table read locally with no contract hop (DP-01). The review reasons come from LOV-INTAKE-REVIEW through the reference-data contract of `rwb-case` (DP-07, H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, C RWB-P3-E1043-CON); the type list LOV-DOC-TYPE is faked with the same six codes so the two agree at build time and no list value is typed in code.
- `CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD` (0.80), `CLASSIFY_MAX_PAGES` (3) and `CLASSIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (60, R-UNI-32) are read through the parameters contract and client library of `rwb-case` (DP-06, H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, C RWB-P3-E1042-CON). The rows they resolve to live in `document_hub_parameter` in `rwb_document`, which the Ownership Map gives to P5; the legacy table name `document_hub_parameter` is kept.
- The OCR text is masked before the model call by the ACE PII masking service of the ACE common module (CTL-11, DL26, DL33); national ID numbers, account numbers and phone numbers are replaced by tokens, and neither the prompt nor the response is logged.
- The classify step is one step of the 15-minute document-intake Schedule (legacy JOB-12) that RWB-P5-E1049-APP owns; this story contributes the step, the service-internal classifier and the on-demand evaluation runner (DP-10, H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON).
- The classification state is read by attach (RWB-P5-E1032-APP) and by the review queue (RWB-P5-E1054-APP) through the operations of 12.1; the stored document carries `classification_confidence` and `type_candidates` on the `document` row that the store RWB-P5-E1024-APP writes on attach.
- The migration is one step of the per-service Flyway sequence in `rwb_document` (DP-15, H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON): the legacy `V1_5_050__intake_classification.sql` becomes `V1050_1__intake_classification.sql`. The review queue reads reach SCR-31 through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19, H RWB-PLT-N001-CON).
- The deployment of the capability, the model artefact pinning and promotion, the configuration reads, the feature flag, the dashboards and the alerts are RWB-P5-E1050-OPS, the X dependency of this story.

The legacy behaviour is carried unchanged in intent and values: the same user story, rationale, preconditions, flow, eight exception paths, seven business rules, two messages, authority, twelve data fields, ten acceptance criteria and eleven test cases, adapted to the target service's schema, topic, API base, workflow template and internal classifier.

##### 2. Business rationale

A scan arrives with no type; today a person reads it and files it by hand. Classification reads the OCR text and names the type with a confidence, so the document can be attached, extracted and counted against the case checklist (FSD P5 A2.8). A document the model is unsure of goes to a person, so no document is filed under the wrong type. It meets REQ-DCM-005 and serves the measure fields extracted without review (FSD P5 A2.8.1).

The realignment changes the mechanics, not the business rule:

1. One schema, one topic, one API base: `rwb_document`, `rwb.document.events.v1` and `/api/recovery/document/v1` by the service naming rule of §R4 and DP-01. No table of another service is read and no monolith table name survives except the module's own `document_intake`, `document_text`, `document_type` and `document_hub_parameter`.
2. The three thresholds and page bound leave the legacy `document_hub_parameter` read inside the module and arrive through the parameters contract and client library of `rwb-case` (DP-06), while the parameter rows themselves stay in `rwb_document`, which is P5's own store for them.
3. The review reason value set arrives through the reference-data contract (DP-07); the type codes stay in the P5 type table, so a type the business adds is a new table version and never a code change.
4. The Quartz job step becomes the `classifyStep` activity of the `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` template of the workflow kit (DP-10), registered on queue `rwb-document`, so the 15-minute Schedule that starts it belongs to RWB-P5-E1049-APP and this story only contributes one step.
5. The classifier itself is inside the service behind `ClassifierClient`, so the model can change without a contract change, and the evaluation runner is a second activity on the same queue; the legacy P10 model-gateway call is tracked as external work rather than declared as a C dependency the plan does not carry (GAP-1002; ASM-1789).
6. The migration is one step of the per-service Flyway sequence in `rwb_document` (DP-15), and the review queue reads reach SCR-31 through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).
7. The stored document's type and confidence are written on attach by RWB-P5-E1024-APP, so the classification result has one owner and one write path; this story never writes the `document` row.

##### 4. Flow

1. The 15-minute Schedule of RWB-P5-E1049-APP starts `DocumentIntakeWorkflow`; the `ocrStep` activity of the same workflow leaves items with `ocr_status` DONE, and the workflow then calls `classifyStep`.
2. `ClassifyStep`: selects `document_intake` rows with `ocr_status` DONE, no `predicted_type` and no document type given (uploads carry their type and are skipped), locking each row with `version` as the optimistic lock.
3. `TextMasker`: takes the text of the first `CLASSIFY_MAX_PAGES` pages from `document_text` and replaces national ID numbers, account numbers and phone numbers with tokens through the ACE PII masking service.
4. `ClassifierClient`: sends the masked text and the six type codes with their labels from `document_type` in the version in force; receives a score per type and the model version, within `CLASSIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`.
5. `ClassifyStep`: ranks the scores; writes `predicted_type`, `classification_confidence`, the top two candidates in `type_candidates` and `classifier_version` on the intake row.
6. `ClassifyStep`: if the top score is at or above `CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD` and the type is in the table in force, marks the item classified with no `review_reason`; attach (RWB-P5-E1032-APP) stores it with `review_status` NOT_NEEDED.
7. `ClassifyStep`: below the threshold, sets `review_reason` LOW_CONFIDENCE; attach stores the document with `review_status` PENDING and `write_once` false, so it shows on SCR-31 with MSG-P5-003 and its two candidates (RWB-P5-E1054-APP). A type outside the table sets `review_reason` UNKNOWN_TYPE with no predicted type, and attach holds the item for a person.
8. `ClassifyStep`: a model that does not answer inside `CLASSIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` sets `review_reason` MODEL_UNAVAILABLE with no `predicted_type` and `classify_fallback` true, and the fallback is recorded on the item.
9. `ClassifyStep`, one transaction in `rwb_document`: writes the classification columns on the `document_intake` row and, through the event library, the `rwb.document.DocumentClassified` row to the outbox; the event carries the intake ID, the case ID, the predicted type, the confidence band and the review reason, and no text, no candidate list and no personal data.
10. `ClassificationEvaluationRunner`: on demand, runs the labeled sample through the same masked path, writes the accuracy and the 6 by 6 confusion matrix to `evaluation/classification/{runDate}.json` and to the job record, and reports the model version it used. The on-demand trigger is an operator-started workflow on queue `rwb-document`; a named admin operation is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1002; ASM-1790).

The classification result is written once per item: the selection of step 2 excludes every row that already carries `predicted_type` or `review_reason`, so a repeat run of the workflow makes no second model call (R-UNI-40, BR7).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Top score below the threshold | Item marked LOW_CONFIDENCE with the two candidates; stored for review at attach | MSG-P5-003 | AC2 |
| X2 | Top score exactly at the threshold | Item classified | None | AC3 |
| X3 | Classifier does not answer within CLASSIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS | Fallback: item to review with reason MODEL_UNAVAILABLE; the fallback is recorded on the item | MSG-P5-003 | AC4 |
| X4 | The model returns a type code not in the table in force | Item to review with reason UNKNOWN_TYPE | MSG-P5-003 | AC5 |
| X5 | The item already carries a type (upload) | Not classified | None | AC6 |
| X6 | The item is in RESCAN or FAILED | Not classified | None | AC7 |
| X7 | The job runs again over classified items | Not classified again; no second model call | None | AC8 |
| X8 | A user without Documents R reads the classification of a document | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-050-11 (Access) |

Two target-service notes:

- The threshold is read once per run from the parameters contract and cached for five minutes; a value changed in `document_hub_parameter` is therefore in force on the next run without a deployment (AC9). A parameters read that fails leaves the step unstarted and the items unclassified rather than classified on a guessed threshold, and the run is recorded FAILED for the job monitor of RWB-P5-E1050-OPS.
- The masking call is inside the step and not a separate hop: a masking failure stops the item before the model call and the item keeps `ocr_status` DONE with no `predicted_type`, so the next run retries it and no unmasked text is ever sent (X3 is not used for a masking failure, because no model call was made).

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs OCR output (RWB-P5-E1049-APP) and the type table (RWB-P5-E1025-APP); attach (RWB-P5-E1032-APP) reads its result; the classifier is inside the service |
| Negotiable | Thresholds and pages read are data; the model behind `ClassifierClient` can change under DL33 without a contract change |
| Valuable | Removes hand filing for every document the model is sure of |
| Estimable | One workflow step, one internal classifier, one masking client, one evaluation runner, one migration step |
| Small | Fits within two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test case in section 16 |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Document classification

  Background:
    Given document type table version "DOCTYPE-2026.11" is in force
    Given parameter CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD is 0.80
    Given CLASSIFY_MAX_PAGES is 3 and CLASSIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS is 60
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the reference-data list "LOV-DOC-TYPE" with the six agreed types of version "DOCTYPE-2026.11"
    Given the rwb-case parameters contract mock returns CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD 0.80, CLASSIFY_MAX_PAGES 3 and CLASSIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 60

  Scenario: AC1 Accuracy (legacy RWB-E1-050 AC1)
    Given the labeled sample of 180 synthetic documents, 30 of each type, with ocr_status "DONE"
    When ClassificationEvaluationRunner runs on the sample
    Then at least 162 of the 180 documents get the labeled type as predicted_type
    Then the report "evaluation/classification/2026-11-20.json" holds the accuracy, the 6 by 6 confusion matrix and the model version

  Scenario: AC2 Low confidence routed (legacy RWB-E1-050 AC2)
    Given a scanned intake item whose scores are COURT_NOTICE 0.62, DEMAND_LETTER 0.21 and the rest below 0.10
    When classification runs
    Then the item has predicted_type "COURT_NOTICE", classification_confidence 0.6200 and review_reason "LOW_CONFIDENCE"
    Then type_candidates holds COURT_NOTICE 0.62 and DEMAND_LETTER 0.21
    Then the system passes the item to attach marked for type review, with write_once to be set false on the stored document

  Scenario: AC3 Score at the threshold (legacy RWB-E1-050 AC3)
    Given a scanned intake item whose top score is APPRAISAL_REPORT 0.80
    When classification runs
    Then the system classifies the item as "APPRAISAL_REPORT" with no review_reason

  Scenario: AC4 Classifier does not answer (legacy RWB-E1-050 AC4)
    Given the classifier stub does not answer within 60 seconds
    When classification runs for one item
    Then the item has review_reason "MODEL_UNAVAILABLE" and no predicted_type
    Then the item records that the fallback was used

  Scenario: AC5 Type not in the table (legacy RWB-E1-050 AC5)
    Given the classifier returns "LOAN_CONTRACT" 0.91 for an item
    When classification runs
    Then the item has review_reason "UNKNOWN_TYPE"
    Then type_candidates holds the two highest agreed types

  Scenario: AC6 Upload with a type given (legacy RWB-E1-050 AC6)
    Given an intake item created from an upload of type "TITLE_DEED"
    When classification runs
    Then the classifier receives no call for it and its type stays "TITLE_DEED"

  Scenario: AC7 Item waiting for rescan (legacy RWB-E1-050 AC7)
    Given an intake item with ocr_status "RESCAN"
    When classification runs
    Then the classifier receives no call for it

  Scenario: AC8 Repeat run (legacy RWB-E1-050 AC8)
    Given 20 items already classified
    When JOB-12 runs again
    Then the classifier receives no call for those 20 items and their results are unchanged

  Scenario: AC9 Threshold changed as data (legacy RWB-E1-050 AC9)
    Given parameter CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD is changed to 0.90 in document_hub_parameter
    Given a scanned item whose top score is COURT_NOTICE 0.85
    When classification runs
    Then the item has review_reason "LOW_CONFIDENCE"
    Then no code or deployment changed between the two values

  Scenario: AC10 Personal identifiers masked before the model call (legacy RWB-E1-050 AC10)
    Given a scanned page holding the synthetic national ID number "0000000000000" and account number "TEST-ACC-0001"
    When classification runs
    Then the text received by the classifier stub holds tokens in place of both values
```

Every Given, When and Then line above is the legacy line unchanged, with every legacy value kept character for character; the only added lines are the two Background Givens that mock the `rwb-case` reference-data and parameters contracts (DP-07, DP-06), and the legacy endpoints of the shell map to the target operations of 12.1: the classification state read is `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/classification` (API-P5-011 read of the same item), `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/review-items` (API-P5-010) lists the held candidates, and the access case TC-E1-050-11 is `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}` (API-P5-003).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A document is classified into one of the agreed types with a confidence score | REQ-DCM-005; FEAT-DCM-08 |
| BR2 | Below the threshold the document goes to the review queue; the threshold is inclusive | REQ-DCM-005; parameter CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD in document_hub_parameter (New); DL11 |
| BR3 | The types come from the type table in force and the threshold from document_hub_parameter | DL19; principle 1 |
| BR4 | A model that does not answer within the timeout falls back to review and the fallback is recorded | R-UNI-32 |
| BR5 | Accuracy on the labeled sample is at least 90 percent before the step runs in production | Story acceptance; FEAT-AGT-04 |
| BR6 | Personal identifiers are masked before text leaves the document hub | CTL-11; DL26; DL33 |
| BR7 | An item classified once is not classified again | R-UNI-40 |

Target-service statements that make the rules hold in `rwb-document`:

- BR1, BR2 and BR3 are executed on `document_intake` only: the selected row is locked, the scores are ranked in the step, and the four result columns (`predicted_type`, `classification_confidence`, `type_candidates`, `classifier_version`) plus `review_reason` are written in one transaction. No foreign schema is read (DP-01).
- BR2 keeps the threshold inclusive: the comparison is "top score at or above `CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD`", so AC3 at exactly 0.80 classifies and AC9 at 0.85 under 0.90 routes to review. The value comes from the parameters contract (DP-06) and is never written in code, so the two settings of AC9 differ by one data row.
- BR3 reads `document_type` in the version in force by `valid_from` and `valid_to`, with `table_version` DOCTYPE-2026.11; a type code that is absent from that version is UNKNOWN_TYPE and never a new code (AC5). The review reasons come from LOV-INTAKE-REVIEW through the reference-data contract (DP-07).
- BR4 is executed by the activity timeout and by `classify_fallback`; a timeout is recorded on the item and is not retried for a second model call inside the same run, so AC4 sees one fallback and no predicted type.
- BR5 is executed by the evaluation runner and its 6 by 6 confusion matrix; the report is the evidence the risk and model risk officer reads before production use, and the threshold of 162 of 180 is the story acceptance value.
- BR6 is executed before the call: the masked text is the only text that leaves the step, and the prompt, the response and the candidate list are never logged. The masking service is the ACE common module's, called and never reimplemented.
- BR7 is executed by the selection predicate and by the `ix_intake_classify` partial index on `document_intake (ocr_status) where predicted_type is null and review_reason is null`, so a repeat run finds nothing to do (AC8).
- DP-10 puts the step inside the workflow kit template, DP-15 puts the migration in the per-service sequence, DP-19 puts the review queue reads behind gateway-bff, and DP-11 fixes the 2 s timeout of the reference-data and parameters reads.

##### 9. State transitions

No case state machine in this story: classification changes no case status. It moves the intake item:

| From | Event | To |
|---|---|---|
| `ocr_status` DONE, no type given | top score at or above `CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD` and the type is in the table in force | classified, no `review_reason` |
| `ocr_status` DONE, no type given | top score below `CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD` | review with `review_reason` LOW_CONFIDENCE and two candidates |
| `ocr_status` DONE, no type given | the model names a type outside the table in force | review with `review_reason` UNKNOWN_TYPE, no predicted type |
| `ocr_status` DONE, no type given | no answer inside `CLASSIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | review with `review_reason` MODEL_UNAVAILABLE, no predicted type, `classify_fallback` true |
| `ocr_status` RESCAN, FAILED or PENDING | the classify step selects | unchanged, not classified |
| any item with `predicted_type` or `review_reason` set | a repeat run selects | unchanged, no second model call |

The stored `document` row follows the store's own state machine (RWB-P5-E1024-APP): COPY_PENDING then STORED, with `review_status` NOT_NEEDED for a confident classification and PENDING for a routed one.

The authorisation decision is taken by `rwb-access` (Recovery roles as data, scope and masking in `rwb_access`) and consumed as the cached permission decision the service holds; this story adds no operation and no guard of its own. The refusal shape of X8 is 403 with MSG-P4-002, as in the legacy endpoint, and it is raised by the document read of RWB-P5-E1024-APP. The per-service login is DP-02; this story refers to "the rwb-document login (DP-02)" and never to a shared login.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

| Operation | Path | Owner | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/classify` | P5 | The classify command: the item, the pages bound, the type codes of the version in force and the timeout; answers the `ClassificationResult`. Service identity only; `Idempotency-Key` required. An item that already carries `predicted_type` or `review_reason` answers the stored result with no second model call. The path is the CON baseline's, because no source names a classification path (GAP-1003; ASM-1792) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/classification` | P5 | The classification-state read: predicted type, confidence, the top two candidates, `classifier_version`, `review_reason` and `classify_fallback`, masked by role; Documents right R with scope applied |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/review-items` | P5 | The review queue list (API-P5-010), which shows the two candidates and the reason next to each held item; declared by RWB-P5-E1054-APP and referenced here |

`GET /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}`, `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/content`, `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}` and `POST /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/resolve` are this service's operations built by RWB-P5-E1049-APP, RWB-P5-E1024-APP and RWB-P5-E1054-APP; this story reads their shapes and adds no field to them beyond the classification properties of the `IntakeItem` answer.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Path | Owner | Story | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters/{paramCode}` | P3 | RWB-P3-E1042-CON | `CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD`, `CLASSIFY_MAX_PAGES` and `CLASSIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, read through the client library; one hop, 2 s timeout (DP-06, DP-11) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 | RWB-P3-E1043-CON | LOV-INTAKE-REVIEW and LOV-DOC-TYPE, read through the client library; one hop, 2 s timeout (DP-07, DP-11) |

The model call is not a REST operation of another service in this story: the classifier is service-internal, and where the deployed model is reached through the `rwb-agent` platform the call is external work tracked by ASM-1789 rather than a declared contract row.

The event is written to the outbox in the classification transaction, so it exists exactly when the classification columns exist. CloudEvents 1.0 envelope in binary mode; consumers dedupe through their inbox. The schema is declared by RWB-P5-E1050-CON, and the third-event position of `rwb-document` is recorded there (ASM-1794).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document`, module `document/classify`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| ClassificationController | Controller | The three operations of 12.1; maps exceptions to RFC 9457 problem responses with the message ID; access check and scope |
| ClassifyStep | Temporal activity | Select, mask, call, rank, apply the threshold, write, outbox |
| ClassifierClient, ModelGatewayClassifier | Service | Calls the classifier inside the service boundary with `CLASSIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`; parses the score per type and the model version |
| TextMasker | Service | Calls the ACE PII masking service for national ID, account and phone numbers |
| ClassificationReader | Service | The published read the classification-state operation and attach use; predicted type, confidence, candidates, classifier version, review reason |
| ClassificationEvaluationRunner | Service | The labeled sample, the accuracy, the 6 by 6 confusion matrix, the report and the job record |
| DocumentIntakeRepository | Repository | The intake row, its classification columns and the selection predicate of step 2 |
| DocumentTypeReader | Repository | `document_type` in the version in force by `valid_from` and `valid_to` |
| ClassificationParameters | Library client | The three parameters through the parameters contract of `rwb-case`, cached for 5 minutes |
| ClassifyThresholdPolicy | Service | The inclusive comparison and the three review decisions, as one unit-testable class |

**Database.**

- One migration step in the per-service Flyway sequence (DP-15): `V1050_1__intake_classification.sql` adds to `document_intake` the legacy columns `predicted_type` varchar(30), `classification_confidence` numeric(5,4), `type_candidates` jsonb, `classifier_version` varchar(40), `classify_fallback` boolean default false; the legacy migration `V1_5_050__intake_classification.sql` is not replayed against a foreign schema. `review_reason` varchar(20) is created by the intake migration of RWB-P5-E1049-APP and reused here.
- Index `ix_intake_classify ON document_intake (ocr_status) WHERE predicted_type IS NULL AND review_reason IS NULL`.
- `document.document_type` varchar(30) and `document.type_candidates` jsonb are written by attach (RWB-P5-E1032-APP) through the store and read here; this story adds no column to `document`.

**Configuration and reference data.**

- `CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD` = 0.80, `CLASSIFY_MAX_PAGES` = 3 and `CLASSIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` = 60 in `document_hub_parameter`, loaded by the reference data administrator, read through the parameters contract (DP-06).
- Document type table version DOCTYPE-2026.11 in force, loaded and approved through RWB-P5-E1025-APP.
- LOV-INTAKE-REVIEW and LOV-DOC-TYPE through the reference-data contract (DP-07).
- Property `classify.model-route` naming the internal route; the legacy `rwb.dochub.classify.model-route` key is retired with the monolith (ASM-103).
- Feature flag `rwb.document.classify`. Off: `classifyStep` is skipped, no item is classified, and every scanned item goes to review with reason LOW_CONFIDENCE at attach.

**Build steps**

1. Write the migration step and the index; test the five columns and the partial index on a boundary date.
2. Build `TextMasker` against the masking stub; test AC10 that no national ID number and no account number reaches the client.
3. Build `ClassifierClient` against the stub with fixed scores; contract test the response mapping, the model version and the timeout.
4. Build the selection and skip rules of `ClassifyStep`; test AC6, AC7 and AC8.
5. Add `ClassifyThresholdPolicy` with the inclusive comparison and the three review decisions; test AC2, AC3, AC5 and AC9.
6. Add the timeout fallback and `classify_fallback`; test AC4.
7. Build the outbox write of `DocumentClassified` inside the same transaction; test that a failed write leaves no classification.
8. Build `ClassificationEvaluationRunner` with the 6 by 6 confusion matrix; run the labeled sample in SIT for AC1 and give the report to the risk and model risk officer.
9. Build the three operations with the access check and scope; API test TC-E1-050-11.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-01 keeps the four document tables in `rwb_document` and removes the module-internal cross-read: the scores are written on `document_intake`, the types are read from the P5 type table, and no other service's table is touched. DP-06 keeps the threshold, the page bound and the timeout out of the code: the client library wraps the `rwb-case` parameters contract while the parameter rows stay in this schema, as the Ownership Map gives them to P5, and the 5-minute cache is what makes AC9 a data change. DP-07 keeps the review-reason set out of the code and fakes LOV-DOC-TYPE with the same six codes as the type table, so a code added to a table version is a data change on both sides. DP-10 replaces the Quartz step with an activity of the workflow kit template, which is what makes the step restartable and observable per run. DP-11 fixes the two consumed reads to one hop with a 2 s timeout and a fake, so the step builds before `rwb-case` is live. DP-15 puts the migration in the service's own sequence and DP-19 puts the review queue reads behind the composite route, so the screen calls the owner once. The model satellite is not a DP row: the legacy `ClassifierClient` behind the P10 gateway is carried as an internal capability with an external satellite, which is the reason the plan's C list stays as it is.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the SIT evaluation report shows at least 162 of 180 correct with the model version named, `rwb.document.DocumentClassified.v1` is on the topic once per classified item with no text and no personal data, and the threshold is proven to change by data alone.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P5-003 | Item sent to the review queue | Some fields need checking. The document is in the review queue. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

Delivery shape: every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set to the ID above, `detail` carrying the text with its placeholders filled, and `instance` naming the request. MSG-P5-003 is not an error of the classify command: it is the text SCR-31 shows for a held item, and the command answers 200 with the `review_reason` and the two candidates that put the item there. A refusal without the Documents right answers 403 with MSG-P4-002, as in the legacy endpoint. The not-found message of the classification-state read and the message of a malformed request are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1003; ASM-1792).

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story. Items sent to review are listed on SCR-31 Document review queue (states Loading; list; reviewed), built in RWB-P5-E1054-APP, with the two candidate types and MSG-P5-003; the reads reach it through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The evaluation report is read from the standard container by the center of excellence analyst.

| State | What the operator or reader sees |
|---|---|
| Classified | The intake item and, after attach, the document carry the type and the confidence of 0 to 1 with four decimals; no review reason |
| Held for type review | The review queue row shows the reason, the predicted type and the two candidates, with MSG-P5-003 |
| Fallback recorded | The item shows MODEL_UNAVAILABLE and the fallback flag, and the reader knows the model did not answer |
| Unknown type | The item shows UNKNOWN_TYPE, no predicted type and the two highest agreed types as candidates |
| Report | The evaluation report of the run date with the accuracy, the 6 by 6 confusion matrix and the model version |

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: types, thresholds, pages read, the timeout and the review reasons are data rows or parameters.
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts: text is masked before the model call; prompts and responses are not logged; test documents are synthetic and the national ID number and account number of AC10 are the synthetic values of the legacy story.
- No read of another service's tables (DP-01). The parameters and lists arrive through the `rwb-case` contracts, one hop, 2 s timeout.
- ACE data is reached only through the owner's contract or a `v_ace_*` view; this service reads no view.
- The model stays inside the SCB tenant (DL33): no document text leaves the bank, and the masked text is the only text that reaches the model.
- The classification is written once per item: the selection predicate and the partial index are the guard, not a caller's promise.
- The event carries identifiers, a type code, a confidence band and a reason; no text, no candidate list and no personal value.
- The classifier is inside the service behind one interface, so a model change is a configuration change and not a contract change.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-050 for rwb-case; the OCR text, the classifier and the type table stay with rwb-document (P5). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **the document type code, the classifier version and the confidence that rwb-document returns for a scanned document applied to exactly one item of the document checklist of the case, one case review task raised when the document hub marks the result for review, and one decision record behind the result**, so that **the type and confidence of a classified document land on the right checklist item and only doubtful documents cost a person's time**.

##### 2. Business rationale

A scan arrives with no type, and a document filed under the wrong type is filed against the wrong checklist item, so the stage gate, the pack check and the timers that follow the checklist all follow the wrong type (FSD P5 A2.8; legacy section 2). The legacy story read the OCR text, called the classifier, ranked the scores and applied the threshold inside the document hub, and then let attach store the document on the case. In the target the document hub owns the file, the OCR text, the classifier, the threshold and the type table (P5, RWB-P5-E1050-APP), and rwb-case owns what happens to a case when the answer arrives: the checklist item, the review task, the timeline record, the decision record and the queue the review task sits on.

rwb-case classifies nothing and computes nothing: it reads the answer the document hub published or served, keeps the type code, the classifier version and the confidence as they were given, maps the code to one checklist item of the checklist the document hub returns for the case, and raises one review task when the answer carries a review reason. No document table is read (DP-01): `document`, `document_intake`, `document_type`, `document_checklist_item` and `case_document_check` stay with rwb-document and are reached only through its contract, one hop with a 2 s timeout (DP-11). A low-confidence or unknown-type document then costs one person one task, and every other document costs nobody.

It meets REQ-DCM-005 (a document is classified into an agreed type with a confidence and a doubtful one goes to review) from the case side only, and it serves the measure of fields extracted without review (FSD P5 A2.8.1) by keeping the answer traceable on the case.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The parameters contract and the reference-data contract of rwb-case are published and in force, with the client library (DP-06, DP-07): the review reasons of LOV-INTAKE-REVIEW (`LOW_CONFIDENCE`, `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE`, `UNKNOWN_TYPE`, `RESCAN`, `UNREADABLE_FILE`), the task codes of the review task, the case document checklist states and the switch parameter of section 13 are read through them, never from code.
- The rwb-document published contract is available for the document metadata, the case checklist and the field answers: `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/document-checklist` and `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}`, with its WireMock fake. No contract story for it is listed for this story, so the build starts against the published contract and its fake, and the contract is taken as carrying the document type, the review status, the review reason, the classifier version and the two candidate types with their confidence: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0761; ASM-1384).
- The Temporal workflow kit is in namespace `rwb-recovery` (DP-10) and CaseWorkflow runs on task queue `rwb-case`, started by the case router from the events of section 12.4.
- `case_document_link` exists in schema `rwb_case` from the attach story RWB-P3-E1032-APP; this story adds the classification columns to it and creates no second link table.
- The review queue, the task model and the task completion are the ones of RWB-P3-E1054-APP: its queue codes, task codes and outcome codes are read through the reference-data contract, and the review screen and the correction of a type are that story's.
- The gateway-bff composite route that serves the case documents screen is published (DP-19).
- The login is the rwb-case login (DP-02): Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0762; ASM-1385).

##### 4. Flow

1. rwb-document (P5): the document hub classifies a scanned document, stores it against the case and publishes DocumentStored (EV-16) with `documentId`, `caseId`, `type` and `source` on `rwb.document.events.v1`; it publishes DocumentFieldsExtracted (EV-17) when the fields of the document are ready.
2. rwb-case: the case router consumes EV-16 through the inbox row it writes in `processed_event` in schema `rwb_case` (one action per event id), and calls `signalWithStart` on CaseWorkflow with the workflow ID equal to the case ID on task queue `rwb-case`.
3. CaseWorkflow: the `ApplyClassification` activity reads the checklist of the case through the rwb-document contract, one hop with a 2 s timeout (DP-11), and reads the classification answer of the document through the same contract.
4. ApplyClassification: holds the `documentType`, the `classificationConfidence`, the `classifierVersion`, the `reviewStatus`, the `reviewReason` and the two candidate types with their confidence exactly as the answer carries them. rwb-case reads no threshold, calls no model and holds no type table.
5. ApplyClassification: maps the type code to exactly one checklist item of the checklist answer. A type code with a matching item satisfies that item; a type code with no matching item adds no item, and the result is treated as the contract carried it, reason code `UNKNOWN_TYPE`.
6. ApplyClassification: a result with no `reviewReason` writes the classification columns on the case document link, sets the checklist item state to SATISFIED and the classification state to CLASSIFIED. A result with a `reviewReason` keeps the link UNCLASSIFIED, records the reason, the two candidates and the confidence, and adds no satisfied item.
7. `RaiseReviewTask`: a result marked for review — `LOW_CONFIDENCE`, `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` or `UNKNOWN_TYPE` — raises exactly one case review task in the review queue of the case, `element_type` HUMAN_TASK, status OPEN, carrying the document reference, the review reason, the two candidate types and the confidence. An OPEN task for the same document is reused, never doubled.
8. `RecordAndApply`: in one `rwb_case` transaction the activity writes the link columns, the checklist item state, the task row and the local decision record. A failed write rolls the whole result back, so no satisfied item, task or record exists from a partial answer.
9. The case router also consumes EV-17 and updates the extracted field count on the same link; it creates no second link, applies no second classification and re-classifies nothing.
10. `RedriveClassificationLinks`, started by the daily Schedule of section 12.6 (DP-10), re-drives the links whose classification answer arrived before the case document link existed: it reads the documents of the case through the rwb-document contract and applies every answer the link does not hold yet, once.
11. Case owner: opens the case documents screen through gateway-bff, which calls `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` on rwb-case and the checklist answer on rwb-document in parallel, and merges the two answers so that the type label comes from the document hub and the type code, the classifier version and the confidence come from the case.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The answer carries `LOW_CONFIDENCE` | One review task with the two candidates and the confidence; the link keeps the type code and stays UNCLASSIFIED | MSG-P5-003 | AC3 |
| X2 | The answer carries `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` | One review task, no type code on the link and no satisfied item; the link stays UNCLASSIFIED | MSG-P5-003 | AC3, AC7 |
| X3 | The answer carries `UNKNOWN_TYPE` | No checklist item is added, no type code is written, one review task carries the reason code as the contract gave it | MSG-P5-003 | AC4 |
| X4 | The same event id is delivered again, or two deliveries run at once | The inbox row in `processed_event` drops the duplicate and the unique key on the link keeps one row; no state, task or record changes | None | AC5 |
| X5 | The classification answer was produced before the case document link existed | The daily Schedule applies the answer once and writes the one link, the one decision record and, if the reason says so, the one task | None | AC6 |
| X6 | rwb-document does not answer inside the REST budget | One hop, 2 s timeout (DP-11); the link stays unchanged, no candidate is invented, the result is counted as failed and the next Schedule run retries | MSG-GEN-006 | AC7 |
| X7 | A role without Case record R reads the tasks or the case | The call is refused with 403 before any read; the review task and the link are unchanged | MSG-P4-002 | AC8 |
| X8 | A document of a case outside the reader's scope is read | The read is refused with 404 and no document, type code or confidence is returned | MSG-P4-003 | AC8 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Day 1 against the rwb-document contract fake and the platform libraries' published contracts; it has no same-service story to wait for and no build dependency |
| Negotiable | The switch, the task codes, the checklist item states and the review reasons are data or contract values; the one-item, one-task and stored-as-received rules are fixed |
| Valuable | Puts the type and confidence of every classified document on the right checklist item and sends only doubtful documents to a person |
| Estimable | One event handler, one workflow with two activities, one Schedule, three endpoints and one migration |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Every criterion of section 7 has a test case in section 16; every cross-service answer is stubbed in the contract fake |
