##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | rwb-case never classifies a document and never calls a model: it applies only the type code, the review reason and the confidence that the rwb-document answer carries | Legacy AC1 to AC10; FSD P5 A2.8; DP-01 |
| BR2 | A type code is applied to exactly one checklist item of the checklist the document hub returns for the case, or to none; rwb-case adds no item the checklist answer does not hold | Legacy AC5; FSD P5 A2.8; FEAT-DCM-08 |
| BR3 | A review reason always raises exactly one case review task; a result with no review reason satisfies its checklist item, and an OPEN task for the same document is reused | Legacy AC2, AC4, AC5; RWB-E1-054 BR1 |
| BR4 | The confidence and the classifier version are stored as received and never recomputed, rounded or compared with a threshold in rwb-case | Legacy AC3, AC9; DF-DOC-007, DF-DOC-073 |
| BR5 | An event acts once: the event id is recorded in `processed_event`, a duplicate changes nothing, and the unique key on the case document link keeps one row per case and document | R-UNI-40; Architecture v5 slide 11 |
| BR6 | The decision record, the link columns, the checklist item state and the task row commit in one transaction; a failed write leaves none of them | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; REQ-DRI-004 |
| BR7 | No `rwb_document` table is read and no foreign key crosses the service boundary: the document is held by its id from the document hub, and no OCR text, field value or file reference is copied into `rwb_case` | DP-01; ADR-010; D-RCV-35 U4; CTL-11 |
| BR8 | The type label shown to a person is read from the document hub answer at read time; the case holds the code and the classifier version only | DP-01; FSD P3 A2.45 (documents on the case record) |
| BR9 | The review reasons, the task codes and the checklist item states are read from the reference lists of rwb-case with their version in force, never from a Java constant | DP-07; BR-P3-003; LOV-INTAKE-REVIEW |

##### 9. State transitions

No case status change: this story writes no value of `recovery_case.status` and moves no LOV-CASE-STATUS value. It moves the case document link and the review task.

| Object | From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| case document link (classification state) | UNCLASSIFIED | A classification answer is applied | The type code maps to one checklist item and the answer carries no review reason | CLASSIFIED |
| case document link (classification state) | UNCLASSIFIED | A classification answer is applied | The answer carries LOW_CONFIDENCE, MODEL_UNAVAILABLE or UNKNOWN_TYPE | UNCLASSIFIED, with the reason, the two candidates and the confidence recorded |
| case document link (type state) | CLASSIFIED | A reviewer confirms or corrects the type | Worked in RWB-P3-E1054-APP | CONFIRMED or CORRECTED |
| case review task | None | A classification answer with a review reason, and no OPEN task for the document | — | OPEN |
| case review task | OPEN | The reviewer completes the review | Worked in RWB-P3-E1054-APP | DONE |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| rwb-case service identity (the rwb-case login, DP-02) | Consumes EV-16 and EV-17; reads the checklist and the document answer through the rwb-document contract; writes the link columns, the checklist item state, the review task and the decision record; runs the daily re-drive Schedule |
| rwb-document service identity (the document hub) | Owns the document, the OCR text, the classifier, the threshold and the type table; publishes EV-16 and EV-17 and serves the checklist and document answers; reads no case table |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Reads the case documents screen in scope; works the review tasks of own cases |
| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer | Reads the case documents screen in scope; works the review tasks of litigation cases |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | Reads the case documents screen and the review tasks of the team in scope; completes no review task |
| Roles with Documents R only | See the documents of a case in their scope on the case documents screen; apply no classification and work no task |
| RW-REFADM | Has no Case record right; refused on the task and case reads |

The rwb-case login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0762; ASM-1385); the story names it "the rwb-case login (DP-02)" until it is agreed.

| DF-CAS-005 | recovery_case | status | Read |
| DF-CAS-026 | case_account | account_key (physical column account_id) | Read |
| DF-WRK-017 to DF-WRK-026 | task | all fields | Write |

| Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0765; ASM-1388) | case_document_link | `document_type_code`, `classifier_version`, `classification_confidence`, `review_reason`, `candidate_one_type`, `candidate_one_confidence`, `candidate_two_type`, `candidate_two_confidence`, `classification_state`, `checklist_item_state`, `classified_at`, `source_event_id` | Write |

The classification columns are added to the case-side link that RWB-P3-E1032-APP created; the table is not an Owner row of the Ownership Map and its field IDs are not in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0765; ASM-1388).

The decision record is a local row in the rwb_case table created by the service baseline, because DP-03 is not among this story's patterns and the central ledger belongs to rwb-decision: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0767; ASM-1390).

Document side, read only through the rwb-document contract and never stored: the document id, the case id, the document type code, the review status, the review reason, the classifier version, the confidence, the two candidate types with their confidence, the type label, the checklist version of the case and the checklist items with their present counts. The classifier version is stored as an opaque string of up to 40 characters as received (the shape of DF-DOC-073); no source names a version label, so every version value in this story is a synthetic test fixture: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0764; ASM-1387).

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8. No OCR text, no field value, no file reference and no personal data is written into `rwb_case`.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/case/v1`; owner rwb-case (P3).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}` | Read one case with its status and the classification state of its document links (type code, classifier version, confidence, checklist item state) for the case screen | Case record R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/me/tasks` | List the caller's open review tasks with the case, the document reference, the review reason, the two candidate types and the confidence | Case record R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| PATCH | `/tasks/{taskId}` | Complete or reassign a task; for a review task the outcome codes and the correction rules are those of RWB-P3-E1054-APP | Case record U, scope applied | Task version in the body; a stale version answers 409 MSG-GEN-004 |

Response fields per the case contract story: case `id`, `caseNo`, `productGroup`, `status`, `entryDate`, `totalOutstandingAtEntry`, `deviationOpen`, `legalHold`, and per document link `documentId`, `documentTypeCode`, `classifierVersion`, `classificationConfidence`, `classificationState`, `checklistItemState`, `reviewReason`, `classifiedAt`; task `id`, `caseId`, `documentRef`, `taskCode`, `status`, `ownerRole`, `reviewReason`, `candidateTypes`, `confidence`, `dueAt`, `outcomeCode`, `completedAt`. The type `label` is not part of the case answer: it is read from the rwb-document contract at read time (BR8). Errors: 401 no session (MSG-P4-001), 403 no Case record R (MSG-P4-002), 404 not found or out of scope (MSG-P4-003), 409 stale task version (MSG-GEN-004), 503 a dependency down (MSG-GEN-006).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Service | Used for | Timeout |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/document-checklist` | rwb-document (P5) | The checklist in force for the case: the checklist version, the items, the type of each item, the label and the present count | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}` | rwb-document (P5) | The classification answer of the document: type code, review status, review reason, classifier version, confidence and the two candidates | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |

The checklist answer matches the published `DocumentChecklist` schema: `checklistVersion`, `stageCode`, `items` with `documentType`, `label`, `required` and `presentCount`, `missingCount` and `complete`. The document answer is taken as carrying `classifierVersion`, `reviewReason` and the two candidate types with their confidence in addition to the fields the published schema names, and those three additions are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0761; ASM-1384).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. No case status changes in this story, so no `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` is published; DP-03 is not among the patterns applied, so no `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` is published either, and the decision record of section 11 is a local write only.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Handler |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` (EV-16) | `rwb.document.events.v1` | P5 | Case router, inbox row in `processed_event`, `signalWithStart` of CaseWorkflow; `ApplyClassification` then `RaiseReviewTask` |
| `rwb.document.DocumentFieldsExtracted.v1` (EV-17) | `rwb.document.events.v1` | P5 | Case router; updates the extracted field count on the same link, applies no classification |

The published payloads are `documentId`, `caseId`, `type`, `source` for EV-16 and `documentId`, `fields`, `confidence` for EV-17, so the review reason, the classifier version and the two candidates are read from the contract answer of section 12.2 and never from the event (GAP-0761; ASM-1384).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| CaseWorkflow | Workflow (parent, one per case, workflow ID = case ID) | `rwb-case` | Receives the signal from the case router and runs the classification step of the case |
| ApplyClassification | Activity | `rwb-case` | Reads the checklist and the document answer, maps the type code to one item, writes the link columns, the item state and the decision record |
| RaiseReviewTask | Activity | `rwb-case` | Raises exactly one case review task for a result marked for review, reusing an OPEN task for the same document |
| RedriveClassificationLinks | Workflow started by the daily Schedule | `rwb-case` | Applies the answers of documents that were classified before their case document link existed |

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Schedule | Cadence | Trigger | Legacy reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| RedriveClassificationLinks | Daily; the time of day is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0766; ASM-1389) | Temporal Schedule in namespace `rwb-recovery`, overlap policy SKIP and a catch-up window (DP-10) | Legacy RWB-E1-050 section 12 restart behaviour: "unfinished items stay unclassified and are taken by the next run"; the case side of that rule is new |

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| case_document_link | P3 (rwb_case) | The case-side link per case and document; this story adds the classification columns and the two states of section 11 |
| task | P3 (rwb_case) | The review task row, with `task_code`, `status`, `owner_role` and the case-side review columns |
| recovery_case | P3 (rwb_case) | Read only: the case header for the screen |
| case_account | P3 (rwb_case) | Read only: the accounts the checklist is keyed on |
| interaction (case timeline projection) | P3 (rwb_case) | One DOCUMENT entry per applied result |
| processed_event | PLT library object created in `rwb_case` | The inbox row that makes an event act once; this story publishes nothing, so `outbox_event` is not used |

rwb-case reads no table of another service and holds no foreign key across services (DP-01); `document`, `document_intake`, `document_type`, `document_checklist_item` and `case_document_check` stay with rwb-document (P5) and are reached only through the contract of section 12.2.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-document WireMock | The P5 contract | `GET /cases/{caseId}/document-checklist` for checklist version 3 and the six agreed types; `GET /documents/{documentId}` for a satisfied type at 0.8000, a `LOW_CONFIDENCE` answer `COURT_NOTICE` 0.6200 and `DEMAND_LETTER` 0.2100, a `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` answer, an `UNKNOWN_TYPE` answer with `TITLE_DEED` 0.4100 and `SETTLEMENT_AGREEMENT` 0.3300, and a no-answer stub for the 2 s timeout |
| rwb-access permission fixture | The P4 cached permission answer used by the guard | Case record R granted, granted with a scope that excludes case "RW-2026-000456", and refused for RW-REFADM; the fixture serves the 403 and 404 paths only and adds no build dependency |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 3 provided, 2 consumed | Case, task and task-write provided; the checklist and the document answer consumed, one hop with a 2 s timeout |
| Kafka | None published, 2 consumed | `rwb.document.events.v1` for EV-16 and EV-17 only |
| Temporal | 2 workflows, 2 activities | CaseWorkflow and RedriveClassificationLinks; ApplyClassification and RaiseReviewTask |
| File | None | This story reads and writes no file and holds no document blob |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`, module `classification`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case.classification`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The DP-06, DP-07, DP-10, DP-15 and DP-19 rows name the dependency the pattern adds in the DP table of Template and Rules v1 §R5.5; WP B-P3-09 records Depends on (build) None and Contract dependencies None for this story, which therefore starts Day 1 against the platform libraries' published contracts and their fakes. DP-03, DP-09 and DP-14 are not applied: this story publishes no event and writes no outbox row, so it claims neither the decision-record topic nor the event naming library.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| ClassificationRouter | Consumer | Consumes EV-16 and EV-17, writes the inbox row in `processed_event` and signals CaseWorkflow with the case ID |
| DocumentAnswerClient | Client | Calls the rwb-document contract for the case checklist and the document answer, one hop with a 2 s timeout; masks nothing and stores no answer payload beyond the fields of section 11 |
| ApplyClassification | Activity | Maps the type code to one checklist item, holds the values as received, writes the link columns, the item state and the decision record in one transaction |
| ChecklistItemMapper | Service | Reads the checklist answer and returns the one item of the type code, or none; adds no item |
| ReviewTaskRaiser | Service | Raises one case review task for a result marked for review on the review queue of the case, reusing an OPEN task for the same document |
| ClassificationStateCatalog | Service | Reads the review reasons, the task codes and the checklist item states through the reference-data contract; no Java enum of reasons |
| CaseDocumentLinkRepository | Repository | `case_document_link`, `task` and the interaction projection in schema `rwb_case` only |
| RedriveClassificationLinks | Workflow | Daily Schedule that applies the answers whose link did not exist when the event arrived |
| CaseController | Controller | `GET /cases/{caseId}`, `GET /me/tasks`, `PATCH /tasks/{taskId}`; declares capability area Case record and the right, and applies the caller's scope |

**Database and migrations**

- `V1050_1__case_document_classification.sql` adds to `rwb_case.case_document_link`: `document_type_code varchar(30)`, `classifier_version varchar(40)`, `classification_confidence numeric(5,4)`, `review_reason varchar(20)`, `candidate_one_type varchar(30)`, `candidate_one_confidence numeric(5,4)`, `candidate_two_type varchar(30)`, `candidate_two_confidence numeric(5,4)`, `classification_state varchar(15) not null default 'UNCLASSIFIED'`, `checklist_item_state varchar(15)`, `classified_at timestamptz`, `source_event_id uuid`.
- Constraint: the unique key `ux_case_document_link ON case_document_link (case_id, document_id)` from V1032_1 keeps one link per case and document, so a duplicate event and a re-drive apply once.
- Constraint: a partial index `ix_case_document_link_unclassified ON case_document_link (linked_at) WHERE classification_state = 'UNCLASSIFIED'` serves the re-drive run.
- The scale of `classification_confidence` matches the document side (DF-DOC-007, numeric(5,4)), so 0.8000 is stored as received and never rounded (BR4).
- No column carries OCR text, a field value, a file reference or a candidate label; the candidates are stored as type codes and confidences only (BR7).

**Configuration and reference data**

- The switch of this capability is a boolean parameter read through the parameters contract of rwb-case (DP-06); its key is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0766; ASM-1389). Off means no classification answer is applied and the re-drive Schedule does not run.
- LOV-INTAKE-REVIEW with its five values, the task codes of the review task and the checklist item states are loaded through the reference-data contract (DP-07), not written in code.
- The classifier threshold, the pages read, the timeout and the type table are rwb-document's and are read by nobody in this story.

**Build steps**

1. `V1050_1` with the classification columns, the indexes and the state default; unit test on the columns and the unique key.
2. DocumentAnswerClient against the rwb-document WireMock, one hop with the 2 s timeout and no retry inside the call; test for AC7.
3. ChecklistItemMapper and the map of a type code to one item, with the no-item case; tests for AC1 and AC4.
4. ApplyClassification holding the values as received and writing the link, the item state and the decision record in one transaction; tests for AC1, AC2 and AC7.
5. ReviewTaskRaiser with the one-task-per-document rule and the reuse of an OPEN task; tests for AC3, AC4 and AC5.
6. ClassificationRouter with the inbox row, the duplicate rule and the second-event rule; test for AC5.
7. RedriveClassificationLinks on the daily Schedule with overlap policy SKIP; test for AC6.
8. Controller endpoints with the declared right, the scope and the 409 on a stale task version; test for AC8.
9. Contract-fake run of both answers in isolation, so the story builds before the document hub is on the environment.

**Feature switch.** The legacy flag `rwb.dochub.classify` stays with rwb-document (P5) and is not read here. The rwb-case switch is a parameter read through the parameters contract (DP-06): off means the router applies no answer and the re-drive Schedule is idle, and the links stay UNCLASSIFIED with no review task.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, every applied result names the document, the type code, the classifier version and the confidence it was given, no test writes an OCR text or a field value into `rwb_case`, and the contract tests of the rwb-document fake stay green.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P5-003 | A document is marked for review on the case and the review task is raised | Some fields need checking. The document is in the review queue. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A read or a task write without Case record R or U | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | A case or a document outside the reader's scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | A task write with a task version other than the one in force | Text from the message catalogue: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0763; ASM-1386) |
| MSG-GEN-006 | rwb-document does not answer inside the 2 s budget | Text from the message catalogue, naming the document hub: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0763; ASM-1386) |

Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-30 Case documents (Loading; empty; list; filtered) shows the documents of the case with the type label read from the rwb-document answer, the received date, the checklist item state and, for a document held for review, MSG-P5-003 with its two candidates. SCR-03 Case record (Loading; read only) shows the case and its documents on the same screen model. Both are served by the gateway-bff composite route, which calls rwb-case and rwb-document in parallel, one hop each, and merges the two answers so the label comes from the document hub and the code and the version come from the case (DP-19, BR8).

The review queue screen, the queue filters and the correction of a type are RWB-P3-E1054-APP's. The field-level masking of the document list and the composite route specification are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0761; ASM-1384).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the review reasons, the task codes, the checklist item states and the switch are data read through the parameters and reference-data contracts; the type codes and the labels belong to rwb-document.
- rwb-case never calls a model and never holds the classifier, the prompt, the OCR text or a threshold: it applies what the document hub answers, and the type table stays in `rwb_document`.
- No OCR text, no extracted field value and no document blob is copied into `rwb_case`; the link holds the document id, the type code, the classifier version, the confidence, the review reason and the two candidates with their confidences only.
- No personal data in logs, workflow inputs or events: the case router writes the document id, the case id and the event id, never a name, an address or an identity number, and workflow payloads pass the payload codec.
- No read of another service's tables and no foreign key across services: the checklist, the document and the type label come only through the rwb-document contract (DP-01).
- The confidence and the classifier version are stored as received; no rounding, no re-ranking and no comparison with a threshold happens in rwb-case (BR4).
- The review task carries IDs and codes only; MSG-P5-003 is shown on the screen, never written into the task row.

- The attach of the document to the case, the case-directory answers and the link itself (RWB-P3-E1032-APP).
- The review queue screen, the queue filters, the correction of a type and the outcome codes of a review task (RWB-P3-E1054-APP).
- Any change to `recovery_case.status` or to a stage, the timers that follow a checklist item and the case-list measures.
- The deployment of this capability: topic and queue provisioning, the Schedule registration, dashboards and the runbook (the OPS stories of the epic).

##### 1. Story

As a **DevOps engineer**, I want **rwb-document's classification capability deployed from the service template with its own login and migration job, the classifier and its model artefact pinned, promoted and rollback-able by version, the three parameters and the type table read from data, a feature flag that can switch the capability off, its participation in the 15-minute intake Schedule, dashboards for the confidence distribution and the review reasons, the alerts of the legacy story and a runbook that names each entry**, so that **every environment classifies on the same artefact version, an operator can see a model that has drifted or stopped answering before a reviewer drowns in the queue, and one person can roll the model or the release back without a build**.

##### 2. Business rationale

In the legacy story classification is a Quartz step and an in-process adapter inside one deployable: the model version is a string in a column, the threshold is a row an administrator edits, and the only signal that the model has drifted is a review queue that grows. In the target the step runs in the `rwb-document` worker on the Temporal queue, the model is one artefact among the release's artefacts, and the 15-minute intake Schedule that starts it belongs to RWB-P5-E1049-APP (DP-10). Deployment is therefore part of the capability: an unpinned model means two environments classify differently on the same document, a missing parameter read means the step either guesses a threshold or stops the whole intake, and a dashboard without the confidence distribution means nobody sees a model that has started answering the same low score to everything until the review queue is the size of the day's scans.

The story also carries the guard that has to be visible in operations. BR5 of the app story makes 162 of 180 the release gate of the model, and BR6 keeps the PII masking in front of every call; both are only real if the pipeline refuses a promotion without an evaluation report and the runbook says what to do when the masking service, the parameters contract or the model does not answer. This story makes those two guards deployable and observable, so the app story can be proven in SIT and the on-call rota can operate it.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template, chart skeleton and pipeline are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-LIB, RWB-PLT-N004-OPS).
- The Temporal workflow kit and the `rwb-recovery` namespace are available (RWB-PLT-WF, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON), and the intake workflow and its 15-minute Schedule are registered by RWB-P5-E1049-APP.
- The Kafka event platform provisions topics with a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON), and `rwb.document.events.v1` already exists for the store and extraction events.
- The observability platform provides the dashboard, the alert rules and the runbook link convention (RWB-PLT-OBS, RWB-PLT-N005-OPS, ADR-023).
- The storage product behind the evaluation report is available through the service's configured storage client (the platform storage product, reached by managed identity); the container and account are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1004; ASM-1791).
- RWB-P5-E1050-CON and RWB-P5-E1050-APP are baselined and buildable, so the chart, the values and the dashboards render from published names rather than from a local choice.
- The three parameters `CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD` 0.80, `CLASSIFY_MAX_PAGES` 3 and `CLASSIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` 60 are reference rows of the environment, loaded through the rwb-case parameters contract (DP-06).
- The type table version DOCTYPE-2026.11 is loaded and approved through RWB-P5-E1025-APP.
- The classifier provider and its model version, and the way a model artefact is produced, are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1002; ASM-1795).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).
- No approval of this deployment story was available in this run, so it is carried as Status Draft (realignment v1) with the release 30 November 2026 unchanged and marked tentative (ASM-1788).

##### 4. Flow

1. The pipeline builds the service image, runs the unit and contract tests, scans the image and the dependencies, and publishes one Helm chart version and one classifier artefact version from the same commit.
2. The chart deploys an api workload and a worker workload with the `rwb_document` login, the migration job on the service's own Flyway sequence and the probes; the migration job runs before the deployment is marked ready.
3. The release pins the classifier artefact by digest and records the pair (chart version, classifier artefact version) in the release record; the artefact identifier is what the step writes into `classifier_version`.
4. The evaluation gate reads the report of `evaluation/classification/{runDate}.json`; a report below 162 of the 180 labeled documents, or a report whose model version differs from the pinned artefact, blocks the promotion.
5. The configuration step confirms the three parameter rows, the type table version in force, the property `classify.model-route` and the feature flag `rwb.document.classify`.
6. The worker joins the intake Schedule: it polls queue `rwb-document`, and its `classifyStep` runs as one step of `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` started by the 15-minute Schedule that RWB-P5-E1049-APP registers; this story registers no Schedule of its own.
7. KEDA scales the worker on the depth of the intake queue and on the running workflow count, so a morning scan burst does not age the review queue.
8. The dashboards are published: classified items, the confidence distribution, the review reasons, the fallback count, the masking failures, the evaluation accuracy and the artefact version in force.
9. The alerts are wired to the message IDs of section 14 and to the runbook entries, and the threshold values behind them are values entries, not code.
10. The runbook is published with its entries: a model that stops answering, a review queue that grows, a masking failure, a parameter read failure, a migration failure, a probe failure and a rollback to the previous model version.
11. A smoke step classifies one synthetic intake item in SIT, checks the answer against the classifier stub, and confirms that the artefact version of the answer equals the version the release pinned.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The migration job fails | The deployment stays unready and the pipeline stops; no traffic to the new version | None | AC1 |
| X2 | The readiness probe fails after the start-up window | The pod leaves the service and the pipeline marks the release failed | None | AC1 |
| X3 | The chart is rendered without a pinned classifier artefact or image digest | The pipeline fails the release before the deployment step | None | AC1, AC2 |
| X4 | The evaluation report is missing, below 162 of 180, or names another model version | The promotion is blocked and the previous artefact stays in force | None | AC2 |
| X5 | The parameters contract does not answer, or a parameter row is absent | The step writes no classification; the item stays unclassified for the next run and the alert fires | MSG-GEN-006 | AC3, AC5 |
| X6 | The feature flag is off | `classifyStep` is skipped, no classification is written and every scanned item goes to review at attach | MSG-P5-003 | AC3, AC5 |
| X7 | The intake Schedule fires while the previous run is still open | The run is skipped by the overlap policy; the skip is counted on the dashboard and never alerted | None | AC4 |
| X8 | The review share or the unknown-type share crosses its threshold | The drift alert fires with the window, the share and the artefact version, and the runbook entry is opened | MSG-P5-003 | AC5 |
| X9 | The masking service fails before a model call | No call is made, the item stays with `ocr_status` DONE, and the masking-failure alert fires | MSG-GEN-006 | AC5, AC6 |
| X10 | A rollback is requested | The previous (chart, classifier artefact) pair is redeployed, the flag stays on and the version in force is shown on the dashboard | None | AC2, AC6 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the chart skeleton, the platform topic provisioned for the service, the workflow kit and the observability platform; the step itself is the app story's |
| Negotiable | Replica counts, resource sizes, KEDA thresholds, alert shares and windows are environment values, not story decisions |
| Valuable | Makes the classification capability deployable, observable and repeatable, and makes a drifted or silent model impossible to miss |
| Estimable | One chart with two workloads, one pipeline stage, one migration job, two probes, one artefact pinning and promotion step, one configuration step, two dashboards, five alert rules and one runbook set |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the runbook |
| Testable | Every criterion tests an artefact: the chart renders, the probes answer, the artefact pair is pinned, the parameters are read, the flag is proven off and on, the worker joins the Schedule, the alerts fire on a synthetic series |

```gherkin

  Scenario: AC3 The configuration, the parameter reads and the feature flag are in force (new, D-RCV-60)

    Then the type codes come from document_type in the version in force and no code list appears in a values file
    Then with the feature flag on a synthetic item is classified
    Then with the feature flag off no classification is written, the item is left unclassified, and the review guard of the app story routes it to review with review_reason LOW_CONFIDENCE

    Then a second run for the same business date and the same open workflow is skipped by the overlap policy and the skip is counted
    Then KEDA scales the worker out on the intake queue depth and back in when the queue is empty
    Then a run that ends with unclassified items leaves them for the next run and the queue age is on the dashboard

  Scenario: AC5 The dashboards and the alerts cover the confidence distribution and the review reasons (new, D-RCV-60)

    Then the review-reason series shows LOW_CONFIDENCE, MODEL_UNAVAILABLE and UNKNOWN_TYPE separately, and the fallback count matches classify_fallback true
    Then the review-share and unknown-type-share alerts fire above their values with the window, the share and the artefact version, and carry MSG-P5-003
    Then the model-unavailable and masking-failure alerts fire with MSG-GEN-006 naming the dependency
    Then the evaluation series shows the accuracy of the last run against the 162 of 180 gate and names the model version it measured
    Then every alert links one runbook entry and no alert payload carries OCR text, a candidate list or a personal value

  Scenario: AC6 The runbook and the rollback cover the legacy signals (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published runbook for the classification capability
    When an operator follows it for a model that stops answering, a review queue that grows, a masking failure, a parameter read failure, a migration failure and a probe failure
    Then each entry names the check, the role, the recovery step and the message ID the screen shows
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One service, one schema, one login: the release uses the `rwb_document` login and no other service's credential | DP-02; Architecture v5 slide 29 |
| BR2 | The migration is a per-service Flyway sequence in schema `rwb_document` and runs before the deployment is ready | DP-15; RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| BR3 | The topic `rwb.document.events.v1` carries a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic, and the release never recreates the topic the store and extraction events already use | DP-09; Architecture v5 slide 11 |
| BR4 | The classify step is a step of the intake Schedule that RWB-P5-E1049-APP registers: this release adds no Schedule, no cron entry and no job name | DP-10; Architecture v5 slide 44 JOB-12 |
| BR5 | No environment value is hard-coded: replica counts, resource sizes, KEDA thresholds, alert shares and windows come from values files and parameters | DP-06; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR6 | The classifier artefact is pinned by digest, promoted as one (chart, artefact) pair and rolled back as one pair; a rebuild between environments is not allowed | Architecture v5 slide 11 notes; Template and Rules §R5.7 |
| BR7 | A promotion requires an evaluation report of at least 162 of 180 correct that names the pinned model version | Legacy BR5; FEAT-AGT-04 |
| BR8 | The three parameters and the type table are data: the threshold 0.80, the page bound 3, the timeout 60 and the six type codes are rows, never values | DP-06, DP-07; legacy BR3 and AC9 |
| BR9 | The feature flag `rwb.document.classify` removes the capability without a schema rollback; with the flag off every scanned item routes to review | Legacy section 13; ASM-1790 |
| BR10 | No personal data in a log, a dashboard series, an alert payload or the runbook: type codes, reasons, scores, counts, versions and durations only | CTL-11; DL26; ADR-023 |
| BR11 | An alert carries a message ID and the agreed text, and links one runbook entry | Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | Chart and artefact published | The image, the chart, the classifier artefact and the migration job pass the pipeline | Deploying |
| Deploying | Migration job complete and probes healthy | The schema is at the expected version and both probes answer | Ready |
| Ready | Evaluation gate passed and promotion approved | The report is at least 162 of 180 and names the pinned version | Promoting |
| Promoting | Previous ReplicaSet drained | The new pair serves and the Schedules are unchanged | Ready, pair in force |
| Ready | Flag off | An operator takes the capability out of service | Ready, capability dark |
| Ready, capability dark | Flag on | The cause is cleared and the smoke item classifies | Ready, capability live |
| Ready | Model drift or model unavailable | The review share or the fallback alert fires | Degraded |
| Degraded | Rollback | The previous (chart, artefact) pair is redeployed and the smoke item classifies on it | Ready, previous pair in force |
| Ready or Degraded | Migration job failed | The schema is not at the expected version | Failed |
| Failed | Rollback | The previous chart version is redeployed and the migration is reversed by its own script | Ready |

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

The deployment exposes the two operations of RWB-P5-E1050-CON behind gateway-bff: `POST /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/classify` and `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/classification`, owner rwb-document (P5). It also serves the review list of API-P5-010 and the document read of API-P5-003, which RWB-P5-E1049-APP and RWB-P5-E1024-APP declare. The probes are cluster-internal and are not part of the API surface.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The seven rows are the patterns the legacy RWB-E1-050 carries. DP-10 is the substantive one for a deployment: the legacy Quartz step is now a step of a workflow that another story's Schedule starts, so this release must deploy a worker that polls the same queue and registers the two activities, and must register no Schedule of its own or the intake would run twice. DP-06 and DP-07 keep the threshold, the page bound, the timeout and the reason set out of the values files: the environment provisions rows, and AC3 proves that a value change needs no release. DP-01 and DP-15 keep the release inside `rwb_document` and its own sequence, so the migration job needs no grant elsewhere. DP-11 fixes the three consumed reads to one hop with a 2 s client budget and a fake, and DP-19 is the route the classification-state read answers through. The platform H dependencies are wave 0 contracts published before this story starts under the Day-1 rule (§R5.7) and are therefore not repeated in the metadata row, which stays None.

**Artefacts**

| Artefact | Content |
|---|---|
| `helm/rwb-document/` | Chart with the api and worker deployments, service, migration job, config map, secret references, probes, KEDA scaler and the artefact-pinning values |
| `helm/rwb-document/values-dev.yaml`, `values-sit.yaml`, `values-uat.yaml` | Image digest, classifier artefact version and digest, replicas, resources, KEDA thresholds, probe timings, log level, alert shares and windows, feature switches, environment name |
| Pipeline stage | Build, unit and contract tests, image and dependency scan, chart publish, classifier artefact publish, evaluation gate, promote the same pair |
| Evaluation gate | Reads `evaluation/classification/{runDate}.json`, refuses below 162 of 180 or a report naming another version, and records the pair in the release record |
| Provisioning step | The schema subject and the outbox relay configuration for `rwb.document.DocumentClassified.v1` on the existing topic with its retry and `.dlt` topics; the queue `rwb-document` is asserted, not created |
| Configuration step | The three parameter rows, the type table version in force, the property `classify.model-route` and the flag `rwb.document.classify` |
| Dashboards | Classified items, confidence distribution, review reasons, fallback count, masking failures, queue age, evaluation accuracy, artefact version, flag state, skips, workflow failures |
| Alerts | Five rules, each with a message ID and one runbook entry |
| Runbook | Nine entries: model unavailable, model drift, review queue growth, masking failure, parameter read failure, migration failure, probe failure, flag left off, rollback to the previous model version |

**Probes.** Readiness answers healthy only when the migration is at the expected schema version, the outbox relay is running and the Temporal worker has polled; liveness answers healthy when the process is up and its internal loop is responsive. Neither probe writes to the database and neither calls the model. Exact paths and timings are values.

**Migration job.** Runs the per-service Flyway sequence for schema `rwb_document` with the `rwb_document` login, as a pre-deploy job with a backoff limit; a failed job blocks the rollout and the release. The classification step is `V1050_1__intake_classification.sql`, one step of that sequence; the job replays no legacy monolith script.

**Model artefact policy.** The classifier artefact is versioned with the release, pinned by digest in the values, and promoted as one (chart, artefact) pair; the version string it reports is what the step writes into `classifier_version`, so the column, the dashboard and the release record agree. A rollback redeploys the previous pair and needs no schema change, because the six classification columns are unchanged between model versions. How the artefact is produced, and who produces it, is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1002; ASM-1795).

**Alert mapping carried over from the legacy story.**

| Message ID | Condition | Alert | Route |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P5-003 | The review share crosses its value, or the unknown-type share crosses its value | Drift alert with the window, the share, the reason and the artefact version | Data steward queue, ticket |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The model does not answer, or the masking service or the parameters read fails | Dependency alert naming the failing system and the trace identifier | Platform on-call, page |
| None (evaluation gate) | The evaluation report is below 162 of 180 or names another model version | Gate alert in the pipeline and in the dashboard | Release manager, ticket |
| None (fallback count) | The fallback count rises above its value in one window | Fallback alert with the artefact version | Platform on-call, ticket |

The legacy message texts are copied unchanged; the deployment adds the routing and the runbook link, never a new wording. The legacy story's own signal to the reviewer is carried by SCR-31 and MSG-P5-003, not by a second alert.

**Capacity.** The worker is sized on the intake volume and the page bound, not on the case volume: one `classifyStep` per selected intake item, one model call per item and one evaluation run on demand, with the extraction and attach steps of the neighbouring stories sharing the same queue. The per-environment capacity (replica counts, KEDA thresholds, resource requests and limits, alert shares and windows) is a values entry, and its numbers are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1004; ASM-1796).

**Done when.** The chart renders in all three environments, the pipeline promotes one (chart, artefact) pair, the probes answer, the topic and its dead-letter path are verified by a test, the worker joins the 15-minute Schedule with no Schedule of its own, the flag is proven off and on, the five alerts fire on synthetic series, the model rollback is proven in SIT, and the runbook entries are reviewed by the on-call rota.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |

| MSG-P5-003 | Items are held for type review, or the review share alert fires | Some fields need checking. The document is in the review queue. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The model, the masking service or the parameters read does not answer | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The classification-state read is called without the Documents right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story; the deployment adds the alert routing and the runbook link, never a new wording. Thai text for each follows decision DL10. For MSG-GEN-006 the {system} value is "Classification model", "PII masking" or "Classification parameters", fixed by the dependency that failed.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a values file: the threshold, the page bound, the timeout, the type codes and the reason set are reference rows and parameters, never a deployment value.
- No personal data in logs, dashboard series, alert payloads, workflow inputs or the runbook: type codes, reasons, scores, counts, versions, dates and durations only.
- No OCR text and no candidate list on a dashboard, in an alert or in a runbook: the evidence is a count, a share and a version.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or the `v_ace_*` views; this capability reads no ACE view.
- No cross-schema read and no cross-schema key: the release writes only `rwb_document`, holds no grant elsewhere and creates no constraint into another schema (DP-01, DP-02).
- One login per service; the chart carries the `rwb_document` login reference and no other service's credential.
- The topic keeps its retry topic and its `.dlt` topic, and the release never recreates a topic that other keys' events already use (DP-09).
- The release pins the image digest, the chart version and the classifier artefact digest; a rebuild between environments is not allowed.
- No secret is written into a values file, a chart template, a dashboard or the runbook; all secrets come from the platform secret store, including the model endpoint credential.
- The flag is the first step of every recovery, and a rollback changes no schema: the release is designed so the previous model version can run against the same columns.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: integration slice of RWB-E1-050 for RWB-ITG-W1. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **QA integration engineer**, I want **the end-to-end proof of the RWB-E1-050 classification step across P5 rwb-document (the intake item, the classification fields, the text) and P3 rwb-case (the case of the item and the access check), with the model call served by the P10 agent run on its own queue**, so that **each document is filed under the right type and a document below the threshold reaches a person, proved on the real services before wave 1 exits**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story runs classifyStep inside JOB-12 and calls the classifier through the P10 model gateway. The target keeps document_intake and document_text in rwb_document under P5 rwb-document as their owner (Architecture v5 slides 16 and 41), runs the classify step inside DocumentIntakeWorkflow on the rwb-document task queue, and calls the classifier as a child run of P10 rwb-agent: AgentRunWorkflow runs on the rwb-agent task queue for 60 seconds and then returns the rule result (Architecture v5 slide 16). P5 reads its three parameters as data — CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD, CLASSIFY_MAX_PAGES and CLASSIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS — and stores the model version returned by the run on the intake item in classifier_version.

The legacy split for this key is therefore: P5 rwb-document owns the intake item, its classification fields, the text and the type table; P3 rwb-case owns the case of the item and the access decision that guards the read. This story is the integration proof across both owners and the agent run. The types, the threshold, the pages read and the timeout stay data and are never compiled in (DP-06, DP-07).

Where the sources do not name the route that serves the model call, the home of the three parameters in the target or the agent run evidence the pack may read, the suite asserts through the owners' contracts and records the open point as `Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0363; ASM-0479)`.

The legacy measures are kept unchanged: REQ-DCM-005 for the classified type and the confidence, FSD P5 A2.8 and A2.8.1 for the step and the fields extracted without review, and the 90 percent accuracy target on the labelled sample before the step is used in production (FEAT-AGT-04).

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P5-E1050-APP is done: the classification columns on document_intake, the classify step inside DocumentIntakeWorkflow and the evaluation runner are in SIT.
- RWB-P3-E1050-APP is done: the case of the item and the Documents right check are in SIT.
- The published contracts of P5 rwb-document and P3 rwb-case are deployed under their own per-service bases behind gateway-bff, and P10 rwb-agent publishes its own.
- P10 rwb-agent serves AgentRunWorkflow on task queue rwb-agent in namespace rwb-recovery, with the 60-second budget then the rule result (Architecture v5 slide 16).
- The document type table DOCTYPE-2026.11 is in force.
- CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD 0.80, CLASSIFY_MAX_PAGES 3 and CLASSIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 60 are loaded as rows in the document hub parameter table; the three values are the legacy values and all three are assumed (GAP-0363; ASM-0480).
- The labelled sample of 180 synthetic documents, 30 per type, is in the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG, with the true type of each document.
- The classifier stub behind the agent run is available, returns fixed scores per file, and its model version is known.
- The feature flag `rwb.dochub.classify` is on.
- No production data is used and no production connection is opened.
- The release date 30 November 2026 is tentative; a date is not a precondition of this story.
- The story has no build dependency: it is ready on Day 1 and waits only on its two integration dependencies.

##### 4. Flow

1. QA integration engineer: seeds the labelled sample of 180 synthetic documents, 30 per type, through DocumentIntakeWorkflow on queue rwb-document, and waits until ocr_status is DONE and rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1 arrives for each stored file.
2. Harness: posts the five classifier cases — the low-confidence case, the at-threshold case, the silence case, the unknown-type case and the upload case — as fixed scores per file in the classifier stub behind the agent run.
3. Harness: lets the classify step of DocumentIntakeWorkflow run for each case, and waits for the child run of AgentRunWorkflow on queue rwb-agent and for rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1.
4. Harness: reads each intake item through GET /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId} and asserts predicted_type, classification_confidence, type_candidates, review_reason, classify_fallback and classifier_version; reads the text sent for classification through the content path of the same item.
5. Harness: reads the type stored at attach through GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}, and reads the document type table in force to prove the type returned by the run is one of the agreed types.
6. Harness: reads the agent runs of the sample through GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-runs and asserts one run per classification, the fixed model version and the 60-second budget of the run.
7. Harness: runs the labelled sample through the classify step and reads the evaluation report from the standard container: the accuracy, the 6 by 6 confusion matrix and the model version; asserts at least 162 of the 180 documents carry the labelled type.
8. Harness: reruns the step over the 20 classified items and asserts no new agent run is started and no result changed.
9. Harness: changes CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD to 0.90 as a data row and reruns one case; asserts review_reason LOW_CONFIDENCE and that no code or deployment changed between the two values.
10. Harness: reads the masked text received by the classifier stub, posts the access refusal by a role without the Documents right, reads the case of the item through GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}, writes the evidence report and removes the synthetic fixtures.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The top score is below CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD | The item is marked LOW_CONFIDENCE with its two candidates and is passed to attach marked for type review | MSG-P5-003 | AC2 |
| X2 | The top score is exactly at CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD | The item is classified with no review_reason | None | AC3 |
| X3 | The classifier does not answer within CLASSIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS | The item goes to review with reason MODEL_UNAVAILABLE, holds no predicted_type and records the fallback | MSG-P5-003 | AC4 |
| X4 | The run returns a type code outside the type table in force | The item goes to review with reason UNKNOWN_TYPE and the two highest agreed types as its candidates | MSG-P5-003 | AC5 |
| X5 | The item already carries a type (an upload) | The classifier receives no call and the given type is kept | None | AC6 |
| X6 | The item is in RESCAN or FAILED | The classifier receives no call; the item stays as it is | None | AC7 |
| X7 | The step runs again over an item that already carries a classification | No second model call and no change of the result | None | AC8 |
| X8 | A role without the Documents right reads the classification | Refused with status 403 and the message; the case read is unchanged | MSG-P4-002 | AC11 |
| X9 | A consumed contract call exceeds the 2 s timeout or returns a server error | The step is retried under the run policy; the evidence report records the call and the response; no classification assertion is made on unverified data | None | AC1, AC5 |
| X10 | The synthetic fixture set does not match the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG expectations, or the classifier stub returns no fixed score for a file | The suite fails as a fixture or stub fault and names the file; no service defect is raised | None | AC1, AC10 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | The suite is its own module and reuses the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG; it needs the two APP stories and the published contracts of P5, P3 and P10, not their source code |
| Negotiable | The threshold, the pages read, the timeout and the fixed stub scores are data rows of the harness; the story fixes the assertions and the call set |
| Valuable | The classified type, the review routing and the agent run are proved on real services before wave 1 exits |
| Estimable | One suite module, one labelled fixture pack, one classifier stub with its silence control, one threshold clock and one evidence report |
| Small | Eleven scenarios over two services and one agent run; no service code and no schema change |
| Testable | Every scenario asserts a contract response, an agent run, a stored file in the standard container or a message; all data is synthetic |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Document classification, end-to-end across the P5, P3 and P10 wave 1 services

  Background:
    Given the wave 1 services rwb-document, rwb-case and rwb-agent are deployed in SIT with their published contracts
    Given the RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG synthetic data set is loaded and no production data is used
    Given document type table version "DOCTYPE-2026.11" is in force
    Given parameter CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD is 0.80
    Given CLASSIFY_MAX_PAGES is 3 and CLASSIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS is 60

  Scenario: AC1 Accuracy on the labelled sample through the agent run (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the labelled sample of 180 synthetic documents, 30 of each type, with ocr_status "DONE"
    When the classify step runs on the sample and the model call is served by AgentRunWorkflow on queue rwb-agent
    Then at least 162 of the 180 documents get the labelled type as predicted_type on the intake item
    Then the report "evaluation/classification/2026-11-20.json" in the standard container holds the accuracy, the 6 by 6 confusion matrix and the model version

  Scenario: AC2 A low-confidence document is routed to review with its two candidates (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a scanned intake item whose scores are COURT_NOTICE 0.62, DEMAND_LETTER 0.21 and the rest below 0.10
    When classification runs
    Then the item has predicted_type "COURT_NOTICE", classification_confidence 0.6200 and review_reason "LOW_CONFIDENCE"
    Then type_candidates holds COURT_NOTICE 0.62 and DEMAND_LETTER 0.21
    Then the system passes the item to attach marked for type review, with write_once to be set false on the stored document

  Scenario: AC3 A score exactly at the threshold is classified (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a scanned intake item whose top score is APPRAISAL_REPORT 0.80
    When classification runs
    Then the system classifies the item as "APPRAISAL_REPORT" with no review_reason

  Scenario: AC4 A classifier that does not answer within 60 seconds falls back to review (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the classifier stub behind the agent run does not answer within 60 seconds
    When classification runs for one item
    Then the item has review_reason "MODEL_UNAVAILABLE" and no predicted_type
    Then the item records that the fallback was used

  Scenario: AC5 A type outside the table in force goes to review (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the classifier returns "LOAN_CONTRACT" 0.91 for an item
    When classification runs
    Then the item has review_reason "UNKNOWN_TYPE"
    Then type_candidates holds the two highest agreed types

  Scenario: AC6 An upload that already carries a type is not classified (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given an intake item created from an upload of type "TITLE_DEED"
    When classification runs
    Then the classifier receives no call for it and its type stays "TITLE_DEED"

  Scenario: AC7 An item waiting for rescan is not classified (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given an intake item with ocr_status "RESCAN"
    When classification runs
    Then the classifier receives no call for it

  Scenario: AC8 A repeat run over classified items calls nothing (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given 20 items already classified
    When the classify step runs again
    Then the classifier receives no call for those 20 items and their results are unchanged

  Scenario: AC9 The threshold is data and a change needs no deployment (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given parameter CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD is changed to 0.90 in the document hub parameter table
    Given a scanned item whose top score is COURT_NOTICE 0.85
    When classification runs
    Then the item has review_reason "LOW_CONFIDENCE"
    Then no code or deployment changed between the two values

  Scenario: AC10 Personal identifiers are masked before the model call (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a scanned page holding the synthetic national ID number "0000000000000" and account number "TEST-ACC-0001"
    When classification runs
    Then the text received by the classifier stub holds tokens in place of both values

  Scenario: AC11 A role without the Documents right is refused (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a user holds role RW-CAPACITY without the Documents right
    When the user reads the classification of a document of a case
    Then the service refuses the call with status 403 and MSG-P4-002
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A document is classified into one of the agreed types with a confidence score | REQ-DCM-005; FEAT-DCM-08; RWB-E1-050 BR1 |
| BR2 | Below the threshold the document goes to the review queue; the threshold is inclusive | REQ-DCM-005; CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD as a data row; DL11; RWB-E1-050 BR2 |
| BR3 | The types come from the type table in force and the threshold from the document hub parameter table | DL19; RWB-E1-050 BR3 |
| BR4 | A model that does not answer within the timeout falls back to review and the fallback is recorded | R-UNI-32; RWB-E1-050 BR4 |
| BR5 | Accuracy on the labelled sample is at least 90 percent before the step runs in production | FEAT-AGT-04; RWB-E1-050 BR5 |
| BR6 | Personal identifiers are masked before text leaves the document hub | CTL-11; DL26; DL33; RWB-E1-050 BR6 |
| BR7 | An item classified once is not classified again | R-UNI-40; RWB-E1-050 BR7 |
| BR8 | P5 rwb-document owns document_intake, document_text, document_type and document_hub_parameter, and the model call runs as a child run of P10 rwb-agent on queue rwb-agent with the 60-second budget then the rule result | Architecture v5 slide 16; Ownership Map; ASM-0479 |

##### 9. State transitions

None for the case status: this story reads the case of the item and never changes it. It changes the classification state of the intake item, which belongs to P5 rwb-document.

| Object | State | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| document_intake | OCR DONE | The item holds OCR text and no classification; the classify step may pick it up |
| document_intake | CLASSIFIED | The top score met the threshold, the type is in the table in force, and predicted_type, classification_confidence and classifier_version are set |
| document_intake | Review, LOW_CONFIDENCE | The top score was below the threshold; the two candidates are held and the item goes to a person |
| document_intake | Review, MODEL_UNAVAILABLE | The run did not answer within CLASSIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS; no predicted_type, and the fallback is recorded |
| document_intake | Review, UNKNOWN_TYPE | The run returned a type outside the table in force; the two highest agreed types are held as candidates |

The suite reads these states through the P5 contract and writes none of them itself.

| SY-AGENT, agent runtime | Serves the model call as a run on queue rwb-agent |

No other role is in scope for this story.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The suite provides no REST operation. The names reserved for P2 rwb-integration — /api/recovery/integration/v1, rwb.integration.events.v1, rwb-integration and rwb_integration — are not used, and no rwb_integration table is written.

| Method and path | Owner | Use |

| GET /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId} | P5 rwb-document | Read the predicted type, the confidence, the candidates, the review reason, the fallback and the classifier version |

| GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId} | P5 rwb-document | Read the document type stored at attach |

Every call is one hop with a 2 s timeout (ADR-020, DP-11).

None. The suite publishes no event.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

|---|---|---|---|

None. JOB-12 Document intake is described as an event-started workflow with workers scaled by KEDA (Architecture v5 slide 44) and is owned by RWB-P5-E1049-APP; this suite starts the step through the published workflow interface and waits for no Schedule.

The dependency-added column records the build dependency of the owning story. This story has no build dependency: an ITG story waits on no build of its own, and its I dependencies are the APP stories listed in the metadata table.

Build steps:

1. Create the suite module next to harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG and wire it to the SIT endpoints of P5, P3 and P10.
2. Build the labelled sample fixture pack: 180 synthetic documents, 30 per type, with the true type as a data row.
3. Add the classifier stub behind the agent run with fixed scores per file, one 60-second silence and one fixed model version.
4. Implement the eleven scenarios of section 7 in TC order and assert only through the contracts of section 12.2, the events of section 12.4 and Temporal visibility.
5. Add the skip cases — the upload with a given type, the item in RESCAN and the repeat run — and assert that no agent run is started.
6. Add the threshold clock control and the change to 0.90, and assert that no code and no deployment changed.
7. Add the masking assertion on the text the classifier stub receives, the evaluation report assertion and the access refusal with its status and message.
8. Write the evidence report with the item ids, the agent run ids, the accuracy, the confusion matrix, the model version and the messages; run the suite in SIT against the wave 1 release candidate and keep the report with the wave exit evidence.

Done when: all eleven test cases pass in SIT against the published wave 1 contracts, the evaluation report shows at least 162 of 180 correct, the evidence report is attached to the wave exit pack, and no service code or schema was changed by this story.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the types, the threshold, the pages read and the timeout are data rows, not constants.
- No personal data in logs, events, evidence or fixtures: text is masked before the model call, prompts and responses are not logged, and every test document is synthetic.
- No cross-service table read: every assertion goes through the owner's contract and the suite owns no table.
- One hop and a 2 s timeout on every consumed call (ADR-020).
- The model endpoint is inside the SCB tenant and no document text leaves the bank (DL33).
- Synthetic data only; the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG loads the fixtures and no production data is read, copied or connected to.
- No production access of any kind from the suite or its configuration.
