Each `v_ace_*` Given line stands as the value fixture of the legacy story and is kept unchanged; the `contract mock` line beside it names the contract through which the target service reads the same value, so the assertion is unchanged and the reader moves from the view to its owner (DP-05). AC9's legacy When line reads the notice through `GET /cases/{caseId}/notices`; in the target that read is `GET /api/recovery/comms/v1/notices/{noticeId}` of API-P6-002, and the legacy line and its values are kept as written.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A notice is generated only from the current Approved template for its notice type, product group and language | RWB-E1-052 BR1; R-LIT-03; CTL-14 |
| BR2 | A withdrawn template holds generation and raises a task to the litigation officer team | RWB-E1-052 BR2; R-LIT-04 |
| BR3 | A required merge value that is empty holds the notice, names the field and raises a task to the case owner | RWB-E1-052 BR3; merge_field.is_required; pattern of R-RES-36 |
| BR4 | The footer carries the case number, template code, template version and generation date | RWB-E1-052 BR4; REQ-OCC-001; CTL-14 evidence |
| BR5 | The generated PDF is a write-once document on the case, held by rwb-document | RWB-E1-052 BR5; CTL-12; DT06 |
| BR6 | A notice whose local decision record cannot be written is not generated; the record, the notice row and the outbox row commit together or not at all | RWB-E1-052 BR6; Principle 5; R-UNI-39; CTL-06; DP-03 |
| BR7 | Sent type is NPL for a case at 90 days past due or more; the mapping is reference data | RWB-E1-052 BR7; LOV-SENT-TYPE; DL16 |
| BR8 | One notice per case, notice type, `person_key` and business date | RWB-E1-052 BR8; R-UNI-40; notice key of the service |
| BR9 | The party, the customer name and the notice address are read by `person_key` and the composite `contact_key` (`contact_type:key`) through rwb-source-data; no service holds a party or contact copy and no service reads an ACE view except rwb-source-data | RWB-E1-052 BR9; D-RCV-35 U4; ADR-010; DP-01; DP-05 |
| BR10 | A merge code resolves to a case field, a source-data field or a template field. The clear `identification_number` is never a merge source; `id_no_masked` and `id_no_last4` only | RWB-E1-052 BR10; ADR-010; DF-ACE-073 |
| BR11 | Proof of delivery is read through rwb-source-data by `notice_ref`; the Workbench writes no WIN delivery fact | RWB-E1-052 BR11; RWB-E1-055; DP-05 |
| BR12 | The merge snapshot holds the merge code, the source column, the business key and the field ID of each value used, never the value | RWB-E1-052 BR12; NFR-040; guardrail on personal data |
| BR13 | The litigation route rule decides when a notice is asked for; this story answers a request and evaluates no route rule, so R-LIT-01 stays with rwb-decision | R-LIT-01; RWB-E1-052 section 19 |
| BR14 | A document store that fails after the record write rolls the notice back and a correcting decision record follows | R-UNI-24; RWB-E1-052 section 12 (order of writes) |
| BR15 | The notice rule set is R-LIT-03 for generation and R-LIT-04 for a withdrawn template; a variant of either is a new rule version in rwb-decision, never a code change | R-LIT-03; R-LIT-04; DP-01 |

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It sets the notice state (standard column `state`), and the template check runs before any state is written:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | Generate through POST /cases/{caseId}/notices | The current template version is Approved and every required merge value is present | Generated |
| None | Generate | A required merge value is empty, for example POSTAL_ADDRESS | Held, hold_reason "POSTAL_ADDRESS" |
| None | Generate | The current template version is Withdrawn and no later version is Approved | Held, hold_reason "TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN" |
| None | Generate | The template has no Approved version at all | No row; the call is refused with MSG-P6-005 |
| Held | Generate | The missing value arrives or a new version is Approved | Generated, in a new request |
| Generated | Dispatch through WIN, owned by RWB-P6-E2021-APP | The notice is written to the WIN file | Sent |
| Sent | Proof of delivery read, owned by RWB-P6-E2021-APP | The delivery status is DELIVERED | Delivered |
| Sent | Proof of delivery read, owned by RWB-P6-E2021-APP | The delivery status is UNDELIVERABLE or REFUSED | Unserved |
| Any | A read of the notice | Never | The same state; a read changes no row |

The template check is part of generation and not a state of its own: it decides between Generated, the two hold reasons and the MSG-P6-005 refusal before any row is written. The state `APPROVED` of the legacy check constraint belongs to the notice approval story RWB-E2-014 and is not set here. `Sent`, `Delivered` and `Unserved` are set by the dispatch and proof-of-delivery stories; this story only reads and returns the state it finds.

##### 10. Authority

The letters below are taken from the rwb-comms RBAC matrix of the module specification and from no other table.

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| rwb-comms service identity (the rwb-comms login, DP-02) | Serves the two notice operations, reads the five contracts, writes `rwb_comms` only |
| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer | Documents CRU and Litigation CRUA: reads the notice and the document for a case in scope, and requests generation; receives the withdrawn-template task |
| RW-LEGAL, Legal counsel | Documents CRUA and Litigation RA: reads the notice; approves the template version this story reads |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Documents CRU and Litigation R: reads the notice and receives the "Complete notice data" task |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | Documents R and Litigation R: reads the notice for a case in scope |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Documents R only: reads the notice for a case in scope; no Litigation right, so the notice read is not granted by the matrix and is refused at the edge |

No delegation-of-authority level applies to notice generation: the two rights that matter are the Documents right and the Litigation right, and the authorisation itself is enforced at gateway-bff and not in this story (GAP-1083; ASM-2031). No role in this story grants itself a right.

The merge snapshot is an artefact of this service and not one of its three business tables: no source read here names the table or the store it lives in, so the reference is carried on the decision record and the location is a gap (GAP-1081; ASM-2029). Its content is fixed by BR12: merge code, source column, business key and field ID, never the value. No `document`, `recovery_case`, `task`, `timer`, `interaction`, `signature_request` or `decision_log_entry` row is read or written directly. The schema is `rwb_comms`, its migration runs in the per-service Flyway sequence (DP-15), and the service holds no foreign key into another schema (DP-01).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-comms (P6); base `/api/recovery/comms/v1`; naming per the service catalog.

| ID | Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| API-P6-001 | POST | `/cases/{caseId}/notices` | Generate a notice from the approved template for a case, notice type, `person_key`, language and business date; answer 201 with the Notice | Litigation, right C, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header |
| API-P6-002 | GET | `/notices/{noticeId}` | Read one notice with its state, hold reason, template version, document ID and its dispatch and proof-of-delivery facts; answer 200 with the Notice | Litigation, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |

Errors for API-P6-001: 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 503. Errors for API-P6-002: 401, 403, 404, 503. The request and answer shapes, the field list of the Notice resource and the error codes are fixed by RWB-P6-E1052-CON; the response field names are Not specified in the source documents beyond the type name (GAP-1082; ASM-2030).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

Every row is one hop on the owner's base with a 2 s timeout, a breaker per downstream, a single GET retry with jitter and a POST retried only with the same `Idempotency-Key` (DP-11, ADR-020).

| Method and path | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|
| GET `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/{productCode}/records` | P1 rwb-source-data | The customer name, the contact address and phone, the account balance and `data_as_of`, and the proof-of-delivery facts, for DP01 Account and arrears and DP07 Legal; contract RWB-P1-E1015-CON |
| GET `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness` | P1 rwb-source-data | The data date and freshness stamp of each data product the notice merges, carried onto the decision record |
| GET `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The case number, product group, status and owner; contract RWB-P3-E1018-CON |
| GET `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/parties` | P3 rwb-case | The party links and roles, and the AC8 check that `person_key` is a party on the case; contract RWB-P3-E1018-CON |
| POST `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/tasks` | P3 rwb-case | Raise "Complete notice data" to the case owner and the withdrawn-template task to the litigation officer team; the raise path is Not specified in the source documents as an operation of the Ownership Map (GAP-1085; ASM-2033) |
| GET `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 rwb-case | LOV-NOTICE, LOV-SENT-TYPE and LOV-PRODUCT, so no notice type or sent type is written in code; contract RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| GET `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId={caseId}` | P7 rwb-decision | Read back the D7.1 entry of a notice in the component tests and on the failure path; the write itself is local (DP-03) |
| POST `/api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/generated-documents` | P5 rwb-document | Store the rendered PDF write-once on the case and receive the document ID with `source` "GENERATED" and `write_once` true; no contract dependency row exists for P5 (GAP-1079; ASM-2027) |

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Key | Schema element (IDs and facts only) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1` (EV-13) | `rwb.comms.events.v1` | P6 rwb-comms | caseId | noticeId, caseId, templateId, templateVersion, noticeType, generatedAt; one event for every stored notice, written to the outbox in the same transaction as the notice row |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 rwb-decision | caseId | decision code D7.1, rule "R-LIT-03", rule version, template code and version, data date, record reference; published by the local decision-record library (DP-03) |

`generatedAt` is the outbox write time of the notice; the element list of the event is not enumerated beyond the legacy payload, so the field is carried with the placeholder of GAP-1082 and ASM-2030. The event carries no name, no address, no account number and no account key, and no notice body.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Declared shape | Handler in this story |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` (EV-05) | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 rwb-case | caseId, caseNo, fromState, toState, changedAt | None for generation; declared so the hold rules of the later stories have one owner for the case state |
| `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1` (EV-06) | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` | S8 rwb-deviation | caseId, deviationCode, raisedAt, contactStop | None here; the contact-stop and conduct rules are applied before an outbound contact in RWB-P6-E2021-APP and RWB-P6-E2022-APP |
| `rwb.deviation.DeviationCleared.v1` (EV-07) | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` | S8 rwb-deviation | caseId, deviationCode, clearedAt, outcome | None here, as above |

The three rows are declared for the hold rules this capability depends on; this story subscribes to none of them and each is consumed inside rwb-comms by the dispatch stories. The inbox table is in place so those stories consume idempotently (DP-09).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. Generation is synchronous inside rwb-comms: the POST answers with the notice and its document reference. No workflow, activity or Nexus operation is started here, and no workflow input carries a personal value. `NoticeDispatchWorkflow` exists in the service (Architecture v5 slide 17) and belongs to the dispatch loop, which is RWB-P6-E2021-APP; its contract reference is fixed there and not here.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. JOB-10 WIN notices at 16:00 is the dispatch job and belongs to RWB-P6-E2021-APP and rwb-integration (Architecture v5 slide 44). This story registers no Schedule, no cron entry and no job name, and reads no shared scheduler table (DP-10).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| notice | P6 (rwb_comms) | The notice row: case, document, notice type, sent type, `person_key`, template, hold reason and state |
| template | P6 (rwb_comms) | The template catalog this story reads; written by RWB-P6-E1046-APP |
| merge_field | P6 (rwb_comms) | The merge code catalog and `is_required`; written by RWB-P6-E1046-APP |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_comms` | The outbox of the two published events, the inbox of the three declared events and the `Idempotency-Key` answer store (DP-09) |
| local decision record | P6 rows in `rwb_comms`, written through the decision-record library | The D7.1 entry of every notice (DP-03) |

Not owned and never read directly: `document` and `signature_request` (P5 rwb-document), `interaction` (P1 rwb-source-data), `recovery_case`, `case_party`, `task` and `timer` (P3 rwb-case), `decision_log_entry` (P7 rwb-decision).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.comms`, module `notices`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.comms.notices`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_comms`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-02 | `recovery_svc` login | One login per service | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views; this service reads no view | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/comms/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

No pattern is claimed for DP-04, DP-06, DP-08, DP-10, DP-14 or DP-18: this story evaluates no rule package, reads no parameter, calls no authorise operation, starts no job, keeps the platform topic name and writes no interaction ledger.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| NoticeController | Controller | `POST /cases/{caseId}/notices` and `GET /notices/{noticeId}`, with validation and the problem mapping of the error envelope |
| NoticeGenerationService | Service | Steps 2 to 10 of the flow: the idempotency answer, the template check, the hold paths, the record write, the render and the store |
| TemplateCatalog | Service | The current Approved version for a notice type, product group and language, from `template` |
| MergeValueResolver | Service | Resolves each merge code through the owner named by `merge_field.source_entity` and the column named by `merge_field.source_field`, and builds the merge snapshot |
| LetterRenderer | Service | Fills the approved body and renders the PDF with the footer: case number, template code, template version and generation date |
| NoticeRepository | Repository | Reads and writes `notice`; finds by case, notice type, `person_key` and business date |
| SourceDataClient | Client | The two rwb-source-data reads of 12.2, one hop with the 2 s budget |
| CaseClient | Client | The case, the parties, the task raise and the reference-data reads of rwb-case |
| DocumentClient | Client | Stores the generated PDF through rwb-document and returns the document ID |
| LocalDecisionRecordWriter | Service | Writes the D7.1 entry through the decision-record library, first in the transaction, and its outbox row |
| NoticeGeneratedPublisher | Service | Writes `NoticeGenerated` to the outbox in the same transaction as the notice row |

**Database and migrations**

- Writes `notice`, `template` (read only here) and `merge_field` (read only here) in schema `rwb_comms`; writes the local decision record and the outbox, inbox and idempotency rows of the platform library.
- Migration `V1052_1__notice_generation.sql` in the rwb-comms Flyway sequence: the unique index on `(case_id, notice_type, person_key, created_at::date)` and the check constraint on `state` in ('GENERATED','HELD','APPROVED','SENT','DELIVERED','UNSERVED'). No party or contact column is added (BR9).
- The merge snapshot reference is stored on the local decision record; where the snapshot itself is persisted is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1081; ASM-2029).

**Configuration and reference data**

- LOV-NOTICE, LOV-SENT-TYPE, LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-LANG and LOV-DELIVERY are reference rows read through the rwb-case contract; no notice type, product group, sent type or language is written in code.
- The task code "Complete notice data" and the task owner roles are reference rows of the case model, read through the rwb-case contract.
- The feature switch is `rwb.comms.notice-generation`. Proof of delivery reads a data product the source marks as behind a flag, so the delivery read of API-P6-002 is switched on only when that data product is published, and the notice answer stays complete without it.
- The login is the rwb-comms login (DP-02); its name is allocated by the platform database story and is not fixed here.

**Build steps**

1. Migration and `NoticeEntity`: the unique index, the state check and a test for each.
2. `TemplateCatalog` over `template` and `merge_field`, with the Draft-only and Withdrawn cases of AC2 and AC4; no template value in code.
3. `SourceDataClient`, `CaseClient` and the reference read, each against its WireMock fake, with the missing-row, the timeout and the delayed-answer tests.
4. `MergeValueResolver` with every merge code of the synthetic catalog and the empty required value of AC3; assert that the snapshot holds the column, the business key and the field ID and no value.
5. `LetterRenderer` with the merged text and the footer string of AC1 from a synthetic body.
6. `NoticeGenerationService` with the template check, the two hold paths and the two task raises; tests for AC2, AC3, AC4 and AC8.
7. `LocalDecisionRecordWriter` before `DocumentClient`, with the rollback path; tests for AC5 and the file-store failure of X10.
8. The `Idempotency-Key` answer store and the repeat test of AC6.
9. `NoticeGeneratedPublisher` and the outbox, with the key and the payload asserted; the proof-of-delivery read of AC9.
10. The contract-fake run of the five fakes, so the story builds before rwb-case, rwb-source-data, rwb-document and rwb-decision are live.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, a generated PDF from the synthetic set opens in a standard PDF reader with Thai text rendered, one `NoticeGenerated` and one `DecisionRecorded` leave the outbox per notice, and no personal value appears in an event, a log or the merge snapshot.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P6-005 | The template has no Approved version | {template} version {version} has no Legal approval. It cannot be used. |
| MSG-P6-007 | A required merge value is empty | {notice} for case {case} is on hold. {field} has no value on the case. |
| MSG-P6-003 | The template is withdrawn | The {template} template has been withdrawn. The notice is on hold until Legal approves a new version. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The local decision record could not be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The ACE account batch is stale | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |
| MSG-P1-002 | A reference or data-product load behind a merged value is refused by its owner | The {source} load for {date} was refused: {check}. The previous load is still in use. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The person is not on the case, or the case is outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller holds no Litigation right for the operation | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required request field is missing | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A consumed call does not answer inside 2 s | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |

The message IDs and wording are copied from RWB-E1-052 section 14, with MSG-P1-002 from the message catalog of rwb-source-data and MSG-P4-002, MSG-GEN-001 and MSG-GEN-006 from the platform message catalog. MSG-P1-001 is raised by rwb-source-data on the freshness read and is carried unchanged; its outcome in generation is asserted by legacy AC7, which belongs to RWB-ITG-E1052-ITG. MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P4-003 are raised at the gateway-bff edge and by the case contract, not by this service. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: notice types, product groups, languages, templates, merge codes, task codes, the sent type mapping and the delivery status list are data or reference rows read through the owner's contract.
- No personal data in events, logs, workflow inputs or tests. The name and the address reach the PDF only; the notice event carries IDs and the template version only; there is no merge value, no notice body and no addressee in an event, a workflow input or a log line.
- The merge snapshot holds the merge code, the source column, the business key and the field ID of each value, never the value, and the decision record holds only a reference to it.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: the customer, the contact point, the account balance, the freshness stamp and the delivery facts come from rwb-source-data, and this service reads no ACE view and holds no foreign key into another schema (DP-01, DP-05).
- The clear identity number never leaves ACE and is never merged into a notice; only `id_no_masked` and `id_no_last4` exist for a merge code.
- One hop and a 2 s timeout on every consumed call, with a breaker and a single GET retry; a POST is retried only with the same `Idempotency-Key` (DP-11, ADR-020).
- The generated PDF is write-once and is never overwritten; a correction is a new notice.
- The local decision record, the notice row and the outbox row commit together or not at all, and a failed record means no notice (R-UNI-39, DP-03).
- No production data, no production copy and no production connection in any test or fixture.
- No screen is built here and no route is declared here: the three screens are read through gateway-bff (DP-19).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the secondary P5 slice of RWB-E1-052. A notice produced by `rwb-comms` becomes a write-once generated document on the case in schema `rwb_document`, through `/api/recovery/document/v1` and against the contract `RWB-P6-E1052-CON`. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **litigation officer (RW-LITOFF)**, I want **every demand, recall and guarantor notice that `rwb-comms` produces for a case to be stored by `rwb-document` as one write-once generated document on that case, with its document type and retention class taken from the type in force, its template version identifier and its merge values carried as document facts, and its SHA-256 recorded**, so that **the letter that was issued is the letter that is kept, unchanged, and every reader can name its type, its template version and the values it carried**.

- Service `rwb-document`, schema `rwb_document`, REST base `/api/recovery/document/v1`, topic `rwb.document.events.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document`.
- **This is the secondary P5 slice of RWB-E1-052 and it owns no legacy acceptance criterion.** Legacy AC1 to AC9 and the eleven legacy test cases stay with `rwb-comms` in RWB-P6-E1052-APP and RWB-P6-E1052-CON; the end-to-end journey of legacy AC7 is RWB-ITG-E1052-ITG's. The nine criteria of section 7 are new under D-RCV-60 and test only the document side.
- **What stays with `rwb-comms`:** the template approval check, the merge value resolution, the two hold paths (MSG-P6-005, MSG-P6-003, MSG-P6-007), the rendering of the template body and the footer (case number, template code, template version, generation date), the `notice` row with its state and sent type, the D7.1 decision record, `rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1`, the WIN dispatch and the proof of delivery read.
- **What this story owns:** the notice path of `POST /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/generated-documents` (API-P5-016) — the notice type to document type mapping, the retention class and the write-once flag from the type row in force, the file receipt and its SHA-256, the `document` row with `source` `GENERATED`, the `document_field` rows, the `DocumentStored` outbox row, the idempotent repeat, the correction by a new version, and the answer `rwb-comms` needs to name the notice.
- **What other stories of the service own:** the store path, the containers and the upload path are RWB-P5-E1024-APP's; the document type table is RWB-P5-E1025-APP's; the catalog binding that stamps `template_id` and writes the merge values as catalog-checked fields is RWB-P5-E1046-APP's; the generation engine for contract, CA and mortgage templates is RWB-P5-E2026-APP's. This story calls those and re-tests none of them.
- **No ACE read** (DP-05 as a prohibition): the customer name, the notice address, the phone and the outstanding are inside the PDF that `rwb-comms` renders; they reach the notice through `rwb-source-data`, the only reader of the `recovery.v_ace_*` views. This service opens no `v_ace_*` view, holds no grant on `public` and stores no party, contact or account copy.
- **DP-03 is a boundary, not a writer.** The D7.1 record is `rwb-comms`' and the `DOCATT` record of a store is the store path's (RWB-P5-E1024-APP); this path writes no decision record of its own and `rwb_document` holds no decision table.
- The call is inbound and synchronous: one hop from `rwb-comms`, 2 s budget, `Idempotency-Key` (DP-11). The database login is one per service (DP-02); its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2348; ASM-3903), so the story says "the rwb-document login".

##### 2. Business rationale

Legacy RWB-E1-052 ends with a letter on the case. The rule behind step 8 is CTL-14 and NFR-029 — a legal document that cannot be altered or deleted inside its retention period — and DT06, the document hub as the system of record for documents. If the notice were only a `rwb-comms` fact with a file reference, nothing would guard the file, name its type or show which wording and which values were sent, and the dispatch and its proof of delivery would rest on a document that can move under them.

The realignment changes the mechanics, not the rule:

1. **One schema, one base.** `rwb_document` replaces the recovery schema and `/api/recovery/document/v1` replaces the monolith base (DP01, DP13). No `recovery.*` table is named by a statement of this service, and the `notice` table remains `rwb_comms`'.
2. **The type decides the holding, not the code.** A generated notice is write-once and carries a retention class because its document type says so in the type table in force (NFR-028, NFR-029); a type code, a class, a flag and a container name are never constants.
3. **The notice type is data too.** Which document type a `DEMAND`, `RECALL` or `GUARANTOR_NOTICE` produces is a row, so Legal can add a notice type without a release (DL28).
4. **A repeat is answered, not re-stored.** The `Idempotency-Key` and the notice key answer the second request with the first document, so the legacy "one notice per case, notice type, person and business date" (R-UNI-40) holds on the document side as well.
5. **A correction is a new version.** The generated PDF is never overwritten; a correction writes `doc_version` n+1 with `previous_version_id` and a reason, and the earlier version keeps its bytes and its stamp.

##### 3. Preconditions

| Precondition | What it gives this story |
|---|---|
| RWB-P6-E1052-CON, published | The caller's shape of the generation request and answer: case, notice type, `person_key`, language, business date, template code and version, merge values, the claim-check file reference, the two event envelopes, the message IDs and the error envelope (DP11, C) |
| RWB-P6-E1052-APP | The caller itself: it renders the PDF, adds the footer and posts the request after its own template check and value resolution. Built against the fake of 12.8 |
| RWB-P5-E1024-APP, store path | The document identity, the container write, the `COPY_PENDING` → `STORED` step, the `DOCATT` record and the copy retry |
| RWB-P5-E1025-APP, type table | `document_type` in the version in force from 30 November 2026 with its retention class and write-once flag |
| RWB-P5-E1046-APP, binding step | `template_id` set to the catalog version identifier and one `document_field` row per merge code of that version |
| Reference-data contract (DP07) | LOV-DOC-TYPE, LOV-DOC-SOURCE, LOV-RETENTION in force, so no list value is typed in code |
| Outbox library (DP09) | `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` written in the same transaction as the row |
| Per-service Flyway sequence (DP15) and gateway-bff route (DP19) | The one migration step in `rwb_document`, and the documents tab of the case |

The platform contracts behind DP-03, DP-07, DP-09, DP-15 and DP-19 are the service template's baseline, and the generation contract RWB-P5-E2026-CON and the rwb-case reference-data contract are consumed against their fakes; none of them is in the rows this Work Package fixes. Both facts are recorded rather than edited into the rows (GAP-2350; ASM-3905).

Business preconditions carried from RWB-E1-052, unchanged in value: template "DEMAND-MTG" "TH" version 2 is Approved and current with id "TPL-0002"; case "RW-2026-000123" is in product group "MORTGAGE" with borrower `person_key` "P-0001"; the rendered PDF of the notice is in the claim-check file store; the business date is 2026-11-25; the release date 30 November 2026 is tentative and is not a condition.

##### 4. Flow

1. `rwb-comms` posts `POST /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/generated-documents` with the notice type, the template code and the catalog version identifier, the language, the business date, the merge code and value list, the rendered PDF as a claim-check file reference, and an `Idempotency-Key`. One hop, 2 s budget (DP11).
2. `GeneratedDocumentController`: validates the case ID, the file type (PDF) and the size, resolves the document type of the notice type from the mapping row in force, and refuses an unmapped notice type with 422 and MSG-P5-006 naming it.
3. `GenerationIdempotencyGuard`: answers a key already answered from the stored answer (document ID, `doc_version`, `source`, `write_once`); no second row, no second object and no second event.
4. `NoticeDocumentTypeResolver`: reads the `document_type` row in force and takes its `retention_class` and `write_once` flag; a notice is write-once because its type is, never because a constant says so.
5. `TemplateBindingClient`: the binding step of RWB-P5-E1046-APP stamps `template_id` with the version identifier the caller supplies from the catalog answer and writes one `document_field` row per merge code. A refused version, a code outside the catalog or a missing required value writes nothing and returns that story's message unchanged.
6. Store path: the document identity is created and the row is written with `case_id`, `document_type`, `source` `GENERATED`, `doc_version` 1, `template_id`, state `COPY_PENDING`.
7. `StorageWriter`: writes the file to the write-once legal container at `{container}/{caseId}/{documentId}/v1`, computes `content_sha256`, and sets the row `STORED`. A refused container leaves the row `COPY_PENDING`, answers 503 with MSG-GEN-006 naming "Document storage", and writes no outbox row; the copy retry stores it once.
8. `DocumentStoredPublisher`: writes the `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` outbox row in the same transaction as the `STORED` state, with the document ID, the case ID, the type and the source, and no field value (DP09).
9. Answer 201 with the document ID, `source` `GENERATED`, `write_once` true, `doc_version` 1 and the template version, which is what `rwb-comms` needs to write its `notice` row.
10. A correction posts `POST /documents/{documentId}/regenerate` (API-P5-017) with a reason: a new `doc_version` with `previous_version_id`, never a replace of version 1.
11. Reads: `GET /documents/{documentId}` and `/content` on the case documents tab through the gateway-bff route (DP19); the content returned hashes to the `content_sha256` of the row, and the read changes nothing.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The notice type has no mapping row in force | Refused with 422; no row, no file and no event | MSG-P5-006 | AC2 |
| X2 | The binding refuses the version, a merge code or a required value | Refused whole by the binding; nothing stored; the binding's message returned unchanged | MSG-P6-005, MSG-P6-006, MSG-GEN-001 | AC2 (the refusal itself is RWB-P5-E1046-APP's) |
| X3 | The same request arrives twice with the same `Idempotency-Key` | The first answer is replayed; one document, one object, one event | None | AC3 |
| X4 | The container refuses the write | Row `COPY_PENDING`; 503; no outbox row; the retry stores it once | MSG-GEN-006 ("Document storage") | AC4 |
| X5 | A replace or a delete is attempted on a stored notice version | Refused; the row and the file are unchanged; an audit event is written | MSG-P5-002 | AC5 |
| X6 | A statement names `rwb_comms`, `notice` or another schema, or the schema holds a cross-schema key | The build fails and names the statement or the constraint; at the database the statement fails with SQLSTATE 42501 | None (build log) | AC6, AC9 |
| X7 | A role without Documents C posts a generation, or without Documents U corrects one | Refused with 403 before any row is read | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-052-09 |
| X8 | A personal value reaches a log line, an event payload, a storage path or a test | The guard test fails the build; the value is replaced by the field name in a trace | None (build log) | AC7 |

Two target notes: the hold paths (a missing ADDRESS row, a withdrawn template) are `rwb-comms`' and never reach this operation — a request for a held notice is not posted, and one that is posted stores nothing. The message texts are the caller's and the store's, unchanged.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against the `rwb_document` baseline, the type table, the store path, the binding step and the fake of RWB-P6-E1052-CON; it needs no P6 build and no ACE view |
| Negotiable | The notice type mapping, the type codes, the retention classes, the container name and the flag are data or placeholders; the repeat rule, the write-once rule and the version rule are fixed |
| Valuable | The notice that was issued is the document that is kept, write-once, with its type, its template version and its hash |
| Estimable | One operation path, one resolver, one guard, one storage write and one outbox row |
| Small | Under one week with its tests and its fake |
| Testable | Each criterion of section 7 is one test case of section 16, on the fixtures of 12.8 |

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A notice document is stored with `source` `GENERATED` and `write_once` true, and both the flag and its retention class come from the document type row in force | RWB-E1-052 BR5; CTL-12; DT06; NFR-028, NFR-029 |
| BR2 | One document per case, notice type, `person_key` and business date: the `Idempotency-Key` answers a repeat with the first document | RWB-E1-052 BR8; R-UNI-40 |
| BR3 | The generated PDF is never overwritten; a correction writes a new `doc_version` with `previous_version_id` and a reason, and the earlier version keeps its bytes and its stamp | RWB-E1-052 section 17; CTL-12 |
| BR4 | Which document type a notice type produces is a data row, and no type code, class, flag or container name is a Java constant | RWB-E1-052 section 17; DL28 |
| BR5 | The name, the address and the amounts reach the PDF and its masked field rows only: never the document row, the event, the storage path, the decision record or a log | NFR-040; PDPA; RWB-E1-052 section 17 |
| BR6 | The template version identifier and the merge values are the binding step's, written on the document by RWB-P5-E1046-APP; this path never checks the catalog itself | RWB-E1-052 BR1, BR10; DP-11 |
| BR7 | The row, the file and the event agree: a `COPY_PENDING` document publishes no `DocumentStored` until its file is stored, and a retried copy creates no second document | R-UNI-24; FSD P5 AC-EXC-P5-001-03 |
| BR8 | `rwb-document` writes no notice fact: the state, the hold reason, the sent type, the delivery facts and the D7.1 record are `rwb-comms`' | RWB-E1-052 flow step 9, BR11; DP-01; D-RCV-35 |

Where each rule lives in the target: BR1 is a read of `document_type` plus the row columns `retention_class` and `write_once`; BR2 is the platform idempotency row keyed by the notice key; BR3 is the version chain of `document`; BR4 is the mapping and type tables; BR5 is a masking call and a guard test; BR6 is a call into the binding step; BR7 is the state change that gates the outbox row; BR8 is the absence of any `rwb_comms` statement. No business value is a constant in Java.

##### 9. State transitions

None for the case. This story moves the document state only, on the standard record columns of TSD P5 T3.0.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | Generation request (API-P5-016) | The type mapping resolves, the binding accepts the version and the values | A `document` row, `source` `GENERATED`, `doc_version` 1, `COPY_PENDING` |
| `COPY_PENDING` | The file is written and hashed | The container accepts the write | `STORED`, and the `DocumentStored` row is written |
| `COPY_PENDING` | The container refuses the write | The write fails | Stays `COPY_PENDING`; 503; the copy retry runs |
| `STORED` | A correction with a reason (API-P5-017) | The caller holds Documents U | A new `doc_version` with `previous_version_id`; the earlier row is unchanged |
| `STORED` | A replace or a delete on the same version | Any caller | Refused with MSG-P5-002; nothing moves |

The notice state (Generated, Held, Sent, Delivered) is `rwb-comms`' and is not a transition of any `rwb_document` row.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer | Opens the notice document on the case documents tab (Documents R) |
| RW-LEGAL, legal counsel | Reads the document and its merge values unmasked (Documents CRUA) |
| RW-COE, centre of excellence analyst | Reads the generated notice and its hash (Documents R) |
| SY-CASEWF, case workflow module | Reads the document reference the notice carries (Documents R) |
| `rwb-comms` service identity | Posts the generation request and the correction with an `Idempotency-Key` (Documents C and U) |
| The rwb-document service identity (the rwb-document login, DP-02) | Writes `document` and `document_field`, writes the file and the outbox row, and refuses a change to a stored notice |
| The decision-record library identity | Writes the store's `DOCATT` record as RWB-P5-E1024-APP invokes it; this story writes no record and no new decision code |

Every "who" is a role code; the rights are the legacy ones and are enforced by the guard library the service template carries, with the decision held in `rwb-access`. The pattern set carries no access pattern, so this story adds no guard and no role table. No delegation of authority applies: the approval behind a notice is the Legal approval on the catalog version, and it is `rwb-comms`' check.

Field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary and the TSD P5 T3.1 tables. `document`, `document_field` and `document_type` are P5's in `rwb_document` (ownership map). The merge values arrive in the request and are written as `document_field` rows by the binding step; the decision record reference the caller writes names the field IDs and never a value; the `DOCATT` record of the store carries inputs references only. No field value, no file byte and no personal value enters an event payload or a log line.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

| Operation | Path | Right | This story |
|---|---|---|---|
| API-P5-016 | POST `/api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/generated-documents` | Documents C | The notice path of the operation: steps 2 to 9 of section 4. The generation engine for contract, CA and mortgage templates is RWB-P5-E2026-APP's |
| API-P5-003 | GET `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}` | Documents R | Answers the metadata, the version list and the fields of the stored notice |
| API-P5-004 | GET `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/content` | Documents R | Answers the file whose SHA-256 is `content_sha256` |
| API-P5-017 | POST `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/regenerate` | Documents U | The correction path: a new version with a reason, never a replace |

No new path is added. The request field names of the generation request, the reason field of the correction and the field names of the answer are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2348; ASM-3903); they are fixed by RWB-P5-E2026-CON and matched to the caller's published shape of RWB-P6-E1052-CON. Every operation is published as OpenAPI 3.1 before code, with `Idempotency-Key` on the two POSTs.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Provider | Why | Pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | rwb-case (P3), reference-data contract | LOV-DOC-TYPE, LOV-DOC-SOURCE and LOV-RETENTION in force, so no list value is a constant | DP07 |
| The store command of RWB-P5-E1024-APP (in service) | rwb-document | Identity, container write, `COPY_PENDING` → `STORED` and the copy retry | DP01 |

The rwb-case list read is consumed against its fake and is in no C row of this Work Package, which fixes one entry (GAP-2350; ASM-3905). No parameter is read: nothing of this story is tunable by parameter. The caller's request shape is the document part of RWB-P6-E1052-CON's flow and is the contract-test oracle of 12.8.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Key | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` (EV-16) | `rwb.document.events.v1` | caseId | documentId, caseId, documentType, source, storedAt |

CloudEvents 1.0 binary mode, outbox row in the same transaction as the `STORED` state, published once per committed store by the relay, with retry and `.dlt` topics (DP09). The payload carries no file byte, no field value and no personal data; the envelope is the platform library's and the schema is `rwb_document_stored`. EV-17 `DocumentFieldsExtracted` is the extraction path's and is not published here.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The generation is a synchronous call from `rwb-comms`, not an event, and the notice-derived events (`NoticeGenerated`, `NoticeDispatched`, `NoticeDelivered`) are `rwb-comms`'.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` is the intake workflow of the service (RWB-P5-E1049-APP); this path runs in the caller's thread and waits for the store's answer. DP-10 is not a pattern of this story.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. JOB-12 document intake (every 15 minutes) belongs to RWB-P5-E1049-APP and JOB-17 retention (monthly, first Sunday, 02:30 Asia/Bangkok) to RWB-P5-E1017-APP. Two other service story files attribute JOB-17 to this key; the mapping is recorded as a conflict and this story claims no Schedule (GAP-2351; ASM-3906).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document`, module `notices`. Base `/api/recovery/document/v1`, schema `rwb_document`, topic `rwb.document.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-document` (not used).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| GeneratedDocumentController | Controller | The notice path of API-P5-016: validation, the type resolution, the answer and the problem response |
| NoticeDocumentTypeResolver | Service | Maps the notice type to a document type row and takes its `retention_class` and `write_once`; refuses an unmapped type with MSG-P5-006 |
| NoticeDocumentService | Service | The store transaction: the binding call, the row with `source` `GENERATED`, the field rows, the state change and the outbox row |
| GenerationIdempotencyGuard | Service | Replays the first answer for a repeated `Idempotency-Key`; writes no second row, object or event |
| StorageWriter | Client of the store path | Writes the file once to the legal container, computes `content_sha256`, sets `STORED`, and leaves `COPY_PENDING` on a refused write |
| DocumentStoredPublisher | Service | Writes the `DocumentStored` outbox row when the row becomes `STORED` |
| NoticeDocumentConfig | Configuration | Feature flag, the container name from `document_hub_parameter`, the timeouts |

**Database.** No column is added: `document` and `document_field` already carry every field of section 11 (TSD P5 T3.1). One index, `ix_document_generated_notice` on `document` (`case_id`, `document_type`, `created_at`), so the one-document rule of a case and a type is one index range. One Flyway step in the per-service sequence after the V0001 baseline (DP15). The index name and the step name are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2348; ASM-3903). No key into another schema: `template_id` is a value.

**Configuration and reference data.** The notice-type mapping, the type codes, the retention classes, the write-once flags, the container name and the source value are rows; none is a constant. The three lists arrive through the reference-data contract (DP07). Feature flag `rwb.document.notice-generation` (ASM-3903): off, a generation answers 503 with the feature-off error and stores nothing.

**Build steps**

1. Write the type resolver and the mapping fixture; test AC2 and the unmapped refusal.
2. Build the notice path of the controller over the store path; test AC1 and AC8.
3. Add the idempotency guard; test AC3 and the repeat of AC4.
4. Wire the `COPY_PENDING` → `STORED` step and the copy retry; test AC4.
5. Add the correction path and the write-once refusals; test AC5.
6. Run the boundary, guard and masking tests of AC6, AC7 and AC9 with the migration step and the index.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-02 | `recovery_svc` login | One login per service | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | none here: the D7.1 record is `rwb-comms`' and the store's `DOCATT` record is RWB-P5-E1024-APP's (H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON arrives through the store path) |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*` | ACE data through rwb-source-data's contract | none, as a prohibition: this service reads no view |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; owner topic; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

Each row in place. DP-01 keeps the notice row in `rwb_comms` and the document in `rwb_document`, so the two agree by contract and by the stored reference, not by a key. DP-02 gives the service its own login. DP-03 stops a third record: the caller records the decision, the store records the store, this path records nothing. DP-05 is why no ACE read appears in the story. DP-07 makes the lists data, DP-09 puts the event in the store transaction, DP-11 makes the inbound call one hop with a fake, DP-13 rebases the path, DP-15 is the one migration step and DP-19 is the documents tab.

The H, C, I and X rows are the Work Package's: the build row is empty and the contract row is one entry, although DP-03, DP-07, DP-09, DP-15 and DP-19 name platform contracts and DP-07 names the rwb-case contract. The platform contracts are the service template's baseline, the rwb-case list read is consumed against its fake, and neither is added to a row (GAP-2350; ASM-3905).

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, a generated notice in SIT sits `STORED` in the legal container with a hash that matches its row, a replace is refused with MSG-P5-002, a repeat stores nothing, and the boundary test of AC9 is green.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P5-002 | A change to a write-once legal document | Legal documents cannot be changed. Add a new version instead. |
| MSG-P5-006 | The notice type has no document type in force | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2348; ASM-3903); the FSD names the code and the refused type only |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The storage copy does not complete inside the budget | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller holds no Documents right for the operation | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P6-005, MSG-P6-006, MSG-P6-003, MSG-GEN-001 | Raised by the binding step of RWB-P5-E1046-APP | Returned unchanged, with the binding's placeholders filled |

MSG-P5-002 is quoted from FSD P5 VR-P5-001-2 word for word; for MSG-GEN-006 the {system} value is "Document storage". Delivery shape: an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set to the ID above, `detail` carrying the text with its placeholders filled and `instance` naming the request; a refused generation answers 403, 415, 422 or 503 and stores nothing.

No screen in this story. The generated notice appears on SCR-30 Case documents as a document of type "DEMAND_LETTER" with its template version, its state and its hash, read through the gateway-bff route (DP19). SCR-01 My work and SCR-18 Notice approval are `rwb-comms`' and `rwb-case`'s. The only state this story writes is the document state of section 9.

##### 17. Guardrails

- **No business value in code.** The notice-type mapping, the type codes, the retention classes, the write-once flags, the source value, the container name and the merge codes are rows or fixtures; none is a Java constant.
- **No personal data in logs, events, workflow inputs, tests or prompts.** The name, the address and the amounts sit inside the PDF and its masked field rows only; a value is replaced by its field name in a trace, and the fixtures of sections 7 and 16 are synthetic.
- **No cross-schema read and no cross-schema key** (DP01): no statement names `notice`, `template`, `rwb_comms` or any `v_ace_*` view, and `template_id` carries no foreign key.
- **ACE data only through the owner's contract or `v_ace_*` views.** This module reads no ACE view and holds no grant on `public`; the customer, contact and account facts reach the notice through `rwb-comms` and `rwb-source-data`.
- **The notice is write-once because its type is** (BR1): a class or a flag typed in code fails AC2.
- **A correction is a new version** (BR3): the stored bytes and the stamp of an earlier version are never touched.
- **The row, the file and the event agree** (BR7): no `DocumentStored` for a `COPY_PENDING` document, and no second document from a retried copy.
- **The guard is the service template's.** This story configures the Documents right of four operations and builds no guard, no role table and no access row.
- **No event, workflow or Schedule is added.** `DocumentFieldsExtracted` and `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` are other stories', and the two jobs belong to the intake and retention stories.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-052 for rwb-case; templates, merge fields, rendering and dispatch stay with rwb-comms (P6). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **litigation officer (RW-LITOFF)**, and as the **rwb-case service** behind the case task, I want **a notice requested from the case task in one step — rwb-case sending the case ID, the notice type, the case party key and the language to the rwb-comms contract, and then writing the answer back onto the case as one notice reference, one timeline entry and one decision record, with a held notice opening one case task for the case owner and a delivered notice recorded from the event**, so that **a letter is requested without re-keying the case facts and the case shows exactly what was generated or held, while the template, the merge, the PDF, the dispatch and the proof of delivery stay with the services that own them**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Notices are typed by hand from the core bank screens, so a wrong amount or address on a notice can void the notice period and delay litigation. The legacy story answers that by generating the letter from the Legal-approved template with the case data merged, and it serves REQ-OCC-001 and control CTL-14. The need does not change in the target: a demand, a recall and a guarantor notice still have to be produced from an approved template, and the case still has to show which notice went out, on which template version and on what decision.

What changes is where each part of that capability lives. The **template catalog, the Approved check, the merge of every merge code, the party name and address, the PDF render, the footer, the write-once document, the dispatch to the field and the proof of delivery are rwb-comms' (P6) and rwb-document's (P5)**: the Ownership Map gives `notice`, `template` and `merge_field` to P6 and `document` to P5, and Architecture v5 slide 41 names notices, templates, merge fields and proof of delivery as P6's own. **rwb-case owns the case-side half**: the case fact set it sends, the case task that raises the request, the notice reference the case keeps, the timeline entry, the decision record and the delivery fact the case records from the event. rwb-case holds no template, merges no value, stores no PDF and reads no ACE view (DP-01, DP-05). The legacy in-process `NoticeApi.generate` call from the case module becomes **one hop on the rwb-comms contract inside a CaseWorkflow activity, with a 2 s timeout (DP-11)**, and the two event ends become **the outbox and inbox of the service (DP-09)**.

The split is what keeps the two services independent and it is why this story is a secondary slice of a split legacy key: a template change, a renderer change or a dispatch change reaches the case through one answer and one event, and never through a template table, a merge value or a document row. It also keeps the promise the notice relies on — that the case shows what was generated or held — without the case holding a second copy of the letter or of the address.

The legacy test cases of this key are kept in section 16 with their identifiers unchanged, and the end-to-end proof across rwb-case, rwb-comms, rwb-document, rwb-source-data and rwb-decision sits with RWB-ITG-E1052-ITG of the same legacy key.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P6-E1052-CON is published: the notice resources `POST /cases/{caseId}/notices` and `GET /notices/{noticeId}` on base `/api/recovery/comms/v1`, the Notice answer with `noticeId`, `documentId`, `noticeType`, `personKey`, `templateId`, `templateVersion`, `state`, `holdReason` and `messageCodes`, the state values and the hold reasons as data, the `rwb.comms.events.v1` schemas of NoticeGenerated, NoticeDispatched and NoticeDelivered (EV-13, EV-14, EV-15), the error envelope, the `Idempotency-Key` rule with its stored answer and the contract fake. This story builds against that contract and its fake and never against a notice table (DP-01, DP-11).
- The `rwb_case` schema baseline and the case of record exist from the Epic 1 case story (RWB-P3-E1018-APP): `recovery_case`, `case_party`, `task`, `interaction` and the outbox, inbox and idempotency objects.
- The parameters contract and the reference-data contract of rwb-case are published, with the client library, so the notice types, the task code and the case-side switch are read as data and never written in code (DP-07).
- The case task model carries the request task and the hold task as task rows, with their task codes, element type, discretion and status values held as reference data (DP-07).
- The platform contract stories that the pattern table of section 13 names — the decision-record library of DP-03, the reference-data library of DP-07, the outbox and inbox library of DP-09, the migration conventions of DP-15 and the gateway-bff route of DP-19 — are held by the platform stories and are not repeated in the metadata rows, which carry only the contract dependency of this legacy key (GAP-0754; ASM-1375).
- The gateway-bff composite route is published for the case record, the case documents screen and the task list (DP-19).
- The business date is the service business date of rwb-case; the legacy calendar values are not carried over.
- No other CON story is required: the metadata row "Depends on (build)" is None and the lane is Day 1 against the P6 contract fake.
- The login is the rwb-case login (DP-02): Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0753; ASM-1374).

##### 4. Flow

1. rwb-case: the litigation officer, or the case owner, opens the request task of the case on SCR-01 My work through the gateway-bff composite route, which calls `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/me/tasks` on rwb-case (DP-19).
2. rwb-case: the officer completes the task through `PATCH /api/recovery/case/v1/tasks/{taskId}` with the notice type and the party key of the case; the endpoint checks the caller's right, the scope of the case and that the notice type is in the notice-type list read through the reference-data contract (DP-07).
3. rwb-case: reads the party links of the case from `case_party`. A party key that is not on the case is refused before any call, with MSG-P4-003 (AC5).
4. rwb-case: builds the request from the case facts it already holds — the case ID, the notice type, the case party key, the language and the business date — and builds the `Idempotency-Key` from the case ID, the notice type, the party key and the business date. No name, address, identity number, balance or any other merge value is read or sent: the merge is P6's.
5. rwb-case: the `RequestNotice` activity calls `POST /api/recovery/comms/v1/cases/{caseId}/notices` on the rwb-comms contract with the request and the key, one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker; the call sits inside the workflow activity, so the answer is in the workflow history and a replay reuses it (DP-11).
6. rwb-comms: answers the notice — `noticeId`, `state` Generated or Held, `documentId`, `holdReason` and `templateVersion`. rwb-comms and rwb-document do the Approved check, the merge, the render, the footer and the write-once PDF; rwb-case receives a reference and a state, never a merged value and never a document body.
7. rwb-case: the `RecordAndApply` activity applies the answer in one `rwb_case` transaction — the notice reference, the notice state as a notice fact, the template code and the template version, the document reference and the hold reason on the case row; one timeline entry for the request and its answer; one decision record with decision code "D7.1", the template code and version and the business date; and the task moves to DONE (DP-03).
8. rwb-case: a Held answer — `holdReason` POSTAL_ADDRESS or TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN, as the source carries them — additionally opens exactly one case task with the task code "Complete notice data" for the case owner, and leaves the case status and the case route state unchanged (AC2).
9. rwb-case: a repeated request on the same business date sends the same `Idempotency-Key`, returns the first notice and writes nothing a second time: no second notice reference, no second timeline entry, no second decision record and no second task (AC3).
10. rwb-comms: publishes `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1` (EV-15) on `rwb.comms.events.v1` when the proof of delivery is in; the case inbox consumes it once and records the delivery fact on the case timeline (AC4, DP-09).
11. rwb-case: a time-out or a refusal from rwb-comms writes nothing at all — no notice reference, no timeline entry, no decision record and no task — and the request task stays OPEN for a retry under the same key (AC6).
12. Case officer: SCR-03 Case record, SCR-30 Case documents and SCR-01 My work show the notice reference, its state, the template version, the delivery fact and the hold task, all read through the gateway-bff composite route; the notice itself, its PDF and its dispatch stay on the rwb-comms and rwb-document screens' own answers.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | rwb-comms does not answer inside 2 seconds, or is unavailable | No notice reference, no timeline entry, no decision record and no task; the request task stays OPEN and the activity is retried under the same `Idempotency-Key` | MSG-GEN-006 | AC6 |
| X2 | rwb-comms refuses because the template has no Approved version | Nothing is written on the case; the request task stays OPEN with the message of the answer and the officer re-requests when Legal approves a version | MSG-P6-005 | AC1, AC6 |
| X3 | rwb-comms answers a held notice, POSTAL_ADDRESS or TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN | The notice reference and its held state are recorded; exactly one case task "Complete notice data" is opened; the case status and route state are unchanged | MSG-P6-007 for POSTAL_ADDRESS, MSG-P6-003 for TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN | AC2 |
| X4 | The same request arrives a second time on the same business date | The first notice is returned from the stored answer and the case keeps one notice reference, one timeline entry, one decision record and one task | None | AC3 |
| X5 | The party key is not a party on the case | Refused before any call; nothing is written and rwb-comms is not called | MSG-P4-003 | AC5 |
| X6 | The caller's role has no Litigation C right | Refused at the endpoint with 403 before any write and before any call | MSG-P4-002 | AC7 |
| X7 | The local decision-record write fails | The transaction rolls back: no notice reference, no timeline entry and no task; the request task stays OPEN | MSG-P7-003 | AC8 |
| X8 | A duplicate `NoticeDelivered` event arrives | The inbox drops it: no second timeline entry and no other write | None | AC4 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Day 1 against the RWB-P6-E1052-CON fake: the notice answer, the held answers and the delivered event are stubbed, so no P6 build is waited for; the platform kits are held by their platform stories |
| Negotiable | The notice types, the task codes, the hold reasons and the case-side switch are data; the story fixes the case-side behaviour, not the values |
| Valuable | The litigation officer reaches a notice from the case task without re-keying, and the case shows exactly what was generated or held and on which template version |
| Estimable | One client, one step with two activities, one repository set, one migration and three read endpoints |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each of the eight criteria of section 7 is one automated test; every cross-service value is stubbed in the P6 fake |

AC1 to AC8 are new for the rwb-case slice. This story owns no legacy criterion of RWB-E1-052: the legacy AC1 to AC6, AC8 and AC9 are owned by RWB-P6-E1052-APP, the legacy AC7 by RWB-ITG-E1052-ITG, and the end-to-end proof of the generated notice, its PDF and its delivery sits with the harness of the same legacy key. The legacy criteria are not copied here; the eight above test only the case-side deliverable of this title.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One notice request per case, notice type, case party key and business date; the key of the request is built from those four values and the answer of the first call is returned for the rest of the business date | R-UNI-40; legacy AC6; the `Idempotency-Key` rule of RWB-P6-E1052-CON |
| BR2 | rwb-case sends facts only — case ID, notice type, party key, language and business date — and never a value it merged. No name, address, identity number, balance or other merge value is sent, stored or logged | DP-01, DP-05; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17; legacy BR10 |
| BR3 | A held notice always opens exactly one case task with the task code "Complete notice data" for the case owner, and it never blocks the case: the case status and the case route state are unchanged | legacy AC3 and AC4; MSG-P6-007, MSG-P6-003 |
| BR4 | The notice state is read from the rwb-comms answer and kept as a notice fact of the case; it is never a case status and never a case route state, so no case state transition is created by this story | DF-CAS-005 status; DF-CAS-007 route_state; RWB-P6-E1052-CON state values |
| BR5 | The notice reference and the decision record commit together in one transaction; a failed decision-record write leaves no notice reference and no timeline entry | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; DP-03; legacy AC5 |
| BR6 | The delivery fact is recorded from the event only, through the inbox of the case, once per notice; rwb-case writes no delivery fact of its own and reads no delivery table and no ACE view | EV-15; DP-09; legacy BR11 |
| BR7 | rwb_case stores no template, no PDF and no address, and reads no template, merge-field or document table: rwb-case holds no foreign key into `rwb_comms` and no copy of a notice row | DP-01; Ownership Map (notice, template, merge_field P6; document P5) |
| BR8 | A party key that is not on the case is refused before any call with MSG-P4-003, and a role without the Litigation C right is refused at the endpoint with MSG-P4-002; neither path writes anything | legacy AC8 and the legacy permission block; DP-19 route |

##### 9. State transitions

No case status and no case route state changes in this story. The two small machines below are the notice request and the request task.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | Notice requested from the request task | The party key is on the case and rwb-comms answers Generated | REQUESTED, then GENERATED |
| None | Notice requested from the request task | rwb-comms answers Held with POSTAL_ADDRESS or TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN | REQUESTED, then HELD |
| REQUESTED | Time-out or refusal from rwb-comms | No answer, or an error answer, inside the 2 s budget | REQUESTED; nothing is written and the request is retried under the same key |
| GENERATED or HELD | The same request on the same business date | The stored answer of the first call exists | unchanged |

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | A held notice is applied | The answer carries POSTAL_ADDRESS or TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN and no open task of that code exists for the case | OPEN |
| OPEN | The case owner completes the task | The missing data is supplied and a new request is answered Generated | DONE |
| OPEN | The request is answered Generated on a retry | The first answer had been held | CANCELED |

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Any case status | A notice reference, a notice state or a delivery fact is written | The notice facts are case facts, not states | unchanged |
| Any case route state | A notice reference, a notice state or a delivery fact is written | The route state belongs to the routing rules of the case | unchanged |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| rwb-case service identity (the rwb-case login, DP-02) | Runs the notice step; reads the case and its parties; calls the rwb-comms contract; writes the notice facts, the timeline entry, the decision record and the case tasks |
| rwb-comms (P6) service identity, the comms identity | Owns the notice, the template, the merge fields, the PDF request to rwb-document and the proof of delivery; answers the request and publishes the events |
| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer | Holds Litigation C and Litigation R; completes the notice request task and reads the notice facts of the case in scope |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Holds Litigation R and Case record CRU; receives the task "Complete notice data" and supplies the missing data |
| RW-LEGAL, Legal counsel | Holds Litigation RA and Documents CRUA; approves and withdraws the template versions the answer depends on, in the P6 stories |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | Holds Litigation R; reads the notice facts and the hold tasks of the team in scope |
| RW-REFADM | Holds no Litigation C right; refused on the task completion with MSG-P4-002 |
| rwb-access guard behind the endpoint (RWB-PLT-E1037-CON, RWB-P4-E1037-CON) | Answers the right and the scope of every call; the story reads no access table |
| Decision-record library identity | Writes the local decision record and its outbox row (Decision log C) |

The per-service login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0753; ASM-1374); the story names it "the rwb-case login (DP-02)" until it is agreed, and names the counterpart "the comms identity" from the legacy authority block.

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8. The seven notice columns of `recovery_case` have no field ID in that version, so the row carries the placeholder and one combined gap row: the story needs the reference, the state, the hold reason, the template code and version, the document reference and the delivery date on the case so that the case shows what was generated or held. No copy of a notice row, no merged value, no PDF and no address is written into `rwb_case`, and no foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01). `interaction` is the case timeline projection behind the timeline read; the ledger itself is rwb-source-data's under the Ownership Map ruling.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/case/v1`; owner rwb-case (P3). No new path is added by this story: the request task, the case facts and the next action are served by the existing operations and this story writes the rows behind them.

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/me/tasks` (API-P3-008) | The caller's open tasks, including the notice request task and the hold task | Case record R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| PATCH | `/tasks/{taskId}` (API-P3-009) | Complete the notice request task with the notice type and the party key; the path that raises the request | Case record U, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}` (API-P3-002) | The case facts the request is built from: the case number, the product group, the status and the notice facts of the answer | Case record R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}/next-action` (API-P3-016) | The next action and its due date after the request is answered or held | Case record R, scope applied | Not applicable |

Response fields follow the case CON story: the task `id`, `taskCode`, `status`, `ownerRole`, `dueAt`, `completedAt`, `outcomeCode`; the case `id`, `caseNo`, `productGroup`, `status`, `routeState`, `noticeRef`, `noticeState`, `noticeTemplateVersion`, `noticeDeliveredAt`. The notice fields are an additive change to the case answer within major version 1: the field list of the case CON story stays valid, the new properties are optional, and a consumer of the previous version keeps working (GAP-0749; ASM-1370). Errors: 401 no session (MSG-P4-001), 403 no Case record right (MSG-P4-002), 404 not found or out of scope (MSG-P4-003), 409 the task is not in a state that may be completed, 422 an invalid request field (MSG-GEN-001), 503 a store that does not answer.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Service | Used for | Timeout |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/comms/v1/cases/{caseId}/notices` (API-P6-001) | rwb-comms (P6) | The notice request of AC1: the case ID, the notice type, the party key, the language and the business date, with the `Idempotency-Key`; built against RWB-P6-E1052-CON and its fake | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/comms/v1/notices/{noticeId}` (API-P6-002) | rwb-comms (P6) | The re-read of the notice answer for a retry of a request that wrote nothing, and the answer the case shows when the first call left no stored answer | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |

Both rows are consumed only, never provided, and the answer fields are those of the Notice resource of RWB-P6-E1052-CON. The request field names beyond the legacy generation request are Not specified in the source documents apart from the contract baseline (GAP-0750; ASM-1371); rwb-case sends exactly the case ID, the notice type, the party key, the language and the business date and nothing else.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Key | Payload (IDs and facts only) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 owns the type and the central ledger; every service writes its own record | caseId | decision record reference, decision code "D7.1", template code and template version, notice reference, business date |

The record is written by the local decision-record library in the same transaction as the notice reference, the timeline entry and the task state, and is relayed with the CloudEvents envelope (DP-03, DP-09). `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` is not published, because no case state changes in this story. The decision code is the one the source carries for generation; the final call and the outcome value that the case-side record should name are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0750; ASM-1371).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Handler |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1` (EV-15) | `rwb.comms.events.v1` | P6 rwb-comms | The case inbox: one table hit on `processed_event`, one timeline entry per notice, and no write on a duplicate (AC4) |

The consumer is rwb-case, as the event catalogue records for EV-15. The payload carries the notice reference, the delivered date and the channel only; no name, address or identity number is in the event and none is written by the case.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| CaseWorkflow | Workflow (parent, one per case, workflow ID = case ID) | `rwb-case` | Carries the notice step of the case from the task to the answer, and the delivery fact from the event |
| Notify (workflow kit template) | Workflow template of the kit | `rwb-case` | The notice step: raises the request, waits for the answer within the 2 s budget, keeps the request task open on a hold, a refusal or a time-out, and holds the delivery wait |
| RequestNotice | Activity | `rwb-case` | Builds the request and the `Idempotency-Key` and calls the rwb-comms operation with one hop, a 2 s timeout and a breaker; records the answer in the workflow history |
| RecordAndApply | Activity | `rwb-case` | Writes the notice facts, the timeline entry, the decision record and the task state in one transaction, and opens the hold task on a held answer |

The step runs inside the workflow, not in a request thread, so a retry reuses the recorded answer and never sends a second notice. That the request is a REST call from a `rwb-case` activity rather than an event-only exchange is the reading of the contract; Architecture v5 slide 13 lists P3 as a listener of P6 and slide 17 gives rwb-comms `POST /notices` as an accepted REST operation, so the direction is recorded as a conflict and assumed here (GAP-0752; ASM-1373).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The notice request is raised from a case task and the delivery fact arrives on an event; no Schedule, no cron entry and no polling job is registered by this story (DP-10).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| recovery_case | P3 (rwb_case) | The story adds the seven notice columns and writes them with the case row; the status and the route state are read only |
| case_party | P3 (rwb_case) | The party links the request is validated against; read only |
| task | P3 (rwb_case) | The request task and the hold task "Complete notice data" |
| interaction | P3 (rwb_case) as the case timeline projection | The timeline entries of the request and the delivery; the ledger itself is rwb-source-data's under the Ownership Map ruling |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_case` | Outbox, inbox and idempotency objects of the published record and the consumed event (DP-09) |
| decision_record | PLT library, created in `rwb_case` | The local hash-linked decision record of every notice request (DP-03) |

`notice`, `template` and `merge_field` are P6's tables in `rwb_comms`, and `document` is P5's in `rwb_document`; none of them is read or written here, no foreign key crosses a schema and no view over them is created (DP-01). `decision_log_entry` is a rwb-decision table and is reached only through its topic and its contract.

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-comms WireMock | The P6 contract of RWB-P6-E1052-CON | notice "N-0001" in state "Generated" with template version 2 and document "DOC-0001"; notice "N-0002" in state "Held" with hold reason "POSTAL_ADDRESS" and no document; notice "N-0003" in state "Held" with hold reason "TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN"; a 422 refusal with MSG-P6-005 for a template with no Approved version; a replayed answer for the same `Idempotency-Key`; a delayed answer beyond 2 s; the `NoticeDelivered` fixture for notice "N-0001" with delivered_at 2026-11-27 |
| rwb-access WireMock | The platform guard contract behind the endpoint | `POST /authorise` granting Litigation C and Case record U, and refusing them for RW-REFADM (AC7) |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 4 provided, 2 consumed | The task, case and next-action reads and the task completion provided; the two rwb-comms notice operations consumed; one hop, 2 s |
