##### 4. Flow

1. Litigation officer: opens SCR-31 Document review queue through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).
2. System: lists, oldest first, the intake items with a review_reason and no case that belong to the officer's review team, the intake items whose candidate cases are in the officer's scope, and the stored documents with review_status PENDING on cases in scope; each row shows the reason, the proposed type, the two candidates, confidence and age. The queue read is `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/review-items`; the team of an item with no case comes from the REVIEW_TEAM_UNATTACHED row of `document_hub_parameter`, and the scope of an item with candidates comes from the `rwb-case` answer of the candidate cases and the officer's cached permission decision.
3. Litigation officer: opens an item (`GET /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}`); the system shows the file (`GET /intake-items/{intakeItemId}/content`), the OCR text of `document_text`, the type with its candidates, the candidate cases and the fields of `document_field`, with fields in state REVIEW marked and values masked by role.
4. Litigation officer: keeps the type or chooses another type from the list in force — the versioned `document_type` of this service, whose values are checked against LOV-DOC-TYPE; a new type re-runs extraction for that type through the published extraction operation of RWB-P5-E1053-APP and shows the new fields, each in state REVIEW (ASM-1814). The action travels as `POST /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/resolve` with action SET_TYPE.
5. Litigation officer: chooses the case from the candidates, or enters a case number that the system looks up through the `rwb-case` case record contract, one hop with a 2 s timeout and a mock in the build (DP-11).
6. Litigation officer: confirms each marked field with Confirm, or enters the value with Correct (`PATCH /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/fields/{fieldId}`); the system checks it against the field data type and the range REVIEW_DATE_MIN to REVIEW_DATE_MAX and keeps the extracted value beside the corrected one.
7. Litigation officer: chooses Attach; the system calls the store of RWB-P5-E1024-APP with the case, the type and the fields, which writes the document, its fields and the DOCATT decision record, and stores a legal type in the write-once container `rwb-docs-legal`. The action travels as the resolve operation with action ATTACH.
8. System: sets the intake item review_outcome ATTACHED and the document review_status CONFIRMED (nothing changed) or CORRECTED (type, case or a value changed), and writes `rwb.document.DocumentFieldsExtracted.v1` to the outbox (EV-17). The item update, the store row, the decision record and the outbox row commit together or not at all.
9. Litigation officer: for a stored document with a field in REVIEW, confirms or corrects the field and completes the review with `POST /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/review` and action COMPLETE; the document review_status moves to CONFIRMED or CORRECTED.
10. Center of excellence analyst: the model evaluations (RWB-E1-060) read the resolved items as labeled examples through the item read of this service — predicted type, confirmed type, extracted value and corrected value — instead of the retired `LabeledSetReader` interface (ASM-1811).

The decision record is written before the document exists and inside the store transaction, so a failed record leaves the item, the document and the outbox unchanged and answers MSG-P7-003 (R-UNI-39; X13). The queue read itself is a GET with no side effect and no `Idempotency-Key`; the resolve and the review completion are POSTs with `Idempotency-Key`, and a repeat returns the first answer.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Correct is chosen with an empty value | 422; nothing saved | MSG-GEN-001 | AC4 |
| X2 | The chosen type is not in the type list in force | 422; nothing saved | MSG-P5-006 | AC5 |
| X3 | A corrected date is outside the allowed range | 422; nothing saved | MSG-GEN-002 | AC6 |
| X4 | Attach or complete with a field still in REVIEW | 422; nothing stored | MSG-GEN-001 | AC7 |
| X5 | The chosen case is closed | 422; nothing stored | MSG-P5-005 | AC8 |
| X6 | Another officer saved the same item first | 409; the officer reloads | MSG-GEN-004 | AC9 |
| X7 | The same file is already on the chosen case | The item is linked to the existing document; no second document | MSG-P5-024 | AC11 |
| X8 | Discard without a reason | 422 | MSG-GEN-001 | AC13 |
| X9 | No item in the officer's queue | Empty state on SCR-31 | None | AC15 |
| X10 | A document outside the officer's scope | 404 | MSG-P4-003 | AC16 |
| X11 | The same confirmation is sent twice | Second call returns the saved field; nothing changes | None | AC17 |
| X12 | The user holds Documents R only | 403 | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-E1-054-18 |
| X13 | The decision log write fails on attach | Nothing stored; item unchanged; incident raised | MSG-P7-003 | Principle 5 test TC-E1-054-19 |

Four target-service notes:

- X1 to X9 and X11 are refusals of a body or of a version and keep their legacy statuses and message IDs unchanged; the RFC 9457 problem response carries `messageId`, `detail` and `instance`, and the status mapping is the legacy one (14).
- X10 is a 404 and not a 403 because a document outside the scope must not be distinguishable from a document that does not exist; the scope comes from the candidate cases of the `rwb-case` answer and the officer's cached permission decision, and MSG-P4-003 is returned by the document read of RWB-P5-E1024-APP, which this story calls and does not change (ASM-1815).
- X12 is enforced before the body is read, at the resolve and the review POST and at the field patch, with MSG-P4-002 naming the action; the officer's role and its rights are data in `rwb-access` and this story inherits the shape (ASM-1815).
- X13 is the store's local decision record of DP-03 inside one transaction: the record, the `document` row, the `document_field` rows, the `document_intake` update and the outbox row commit together or not at all, and a failure answers 503 with MSG-P7-003 and raises the incident of R-UNI-39 (ASM-1812).

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the intake item and its text (RWB-P5-E1049-APP), the match hold (RWB-P5-E1032-APP), the classification output (RWB-P5-E1050-CON), the extracted fields (RWB-P5-E1053-CON), the case contract (RWB-P3-E1035-CON), the reference-data library and contract, the decision-record library, the outbox library, the Flyway sequence and the gateway route, all earlier or contract work |
| Negotiable | The review team, the date limits and the page size are data rows; the type list is the versioned `document_type`; the layout follows the ACE components (DL31); the shapes come from the contract baseline |
| Valuable | No low-confidence or unmatched document reaches a case without a person checking it, and every correction becomes a labeled example |
| Estimable | Six operations, three services, one queue service, one review service, one migration, one screen with two components |
| Small | Fits in two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one test case in section 16 |

Every Given, When and Then line above is the legacy line unchanged. The only added lines are the six Background mocks on the `rwb-access` and `rwb-case` contracts and the `rwb-decision` contract, the extraction mock of AC10 and the case mock of AC16, and the one rebased path: AC16's legacy document read under the base `/api/recovery/v1` is published as `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/DOC-0111` by DP-13, with the same operation, the same 404 and the same MSG-P4-003. The legacy interfaces and paths map to the target as `GET /review-items` → `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/review-items`, `GET /intake-items/{id}` → `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}`, `POST /intake-items/{id}/resolve` → `POST /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/resolve`, the legacy field patch under the base `/api/recovery/v1` → `PATCH /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/fields/{fieldId}`, `POST /documents/{documentId}/review` → `POST /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/review`, and `LabeledSetReader` → the item read, which answers the labeled example of AC2 with the predicted type, the confirmed type, the extracted value and the corrected value (ASM-1811).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The queue holds intake items with a review_reason and no outcome, and documents with review_status PENDING | RWB-E1-049, RWB-E1-050, RWB-E1-053, RWB-E1-032; LOV-REVIEW |
| BR2 | An item with no case is shown to the review team named in REVIEW_TEAM_UNATTACHED and to roles with scope All; an item with candidate cases and a document are shown by case scope | Permission matrix scope; CTL-09; REVIEW_TEAM_UNATTACHED (DOC-SVC assumed) |
| BR3 | Attach and complete are allowed only when no field is in REVIEW, the type is in force and the case is open | LOV-REVIEW; DocumentTypeCatalog; DF-CAS-005 |
| BR4 | review_status becomes CONFIRMED when type, case and values are kept, CORRECTED when any changes | LOV-REVIEW |
| BR5 | A corrected value keeps the extracted value in extracted_value and the corrector in confirmed_by | DF-DOC-017; FEAT-DCM-11 |
| BR6 | Attach stores through DocumentStore, which writes the DOCATT decision log entry first and places a legal type in the write-once container | RWB-E1-024; Principle 5; CTL-12 |
| BR7 | Each resolved item is a labeled example for the model evaluations | FEAT-AGT-04; FEAT-DCM-11 |
| BR8 | A change saved against an old version is refused | Optimistic lock column version; MSG-GEN-004 |
| BR9 | A discarded item keeps its file in the intake container and records the reason and the person | REQ-DCM-019 (never removed silently) |
| BR10 | Field values are masked unless the role may see them | DF-DOC-015; CTL-11; DL26 |

Target-service statements that make the rules hold in `rwb-document`:

- BR1 is executed by the queue query over `document_intake` and `document` in `rwb_document`: `review_reason IS NOT NULL AND review_outcome IS NULL` for the item half, and `review_status = 'PENDING'` for the document half, both oldest first by `received_at` and `created_at` and both filtered by BR2 before the page is cut (index `ix_intake_review`, index `ix_document_review`).
- BR2 is executed in two steps. The scope of an item with candidates and of a stored document comes from the `rwb-case` answer of the case and the officer's cached permission decision, which this story reads and does not build (ASM-1815); the review team of an item with no case comes from the REVIEW_TEAM_UNATTACHED row, and a role with scope All sees every item with no candidate. The parameter is a row of `document_hub_parameter` in `rwb_document` and no team code is typed in code (ASM-1807).
- BR3 is executed before the store is called: the resolve operation rejects a type outside the versioned `document_type` (MSG-P5-006), a field still in state REVIEW (MSG-GEN-001), and a closed case read through the `rwb-case` case record contract (MSG-P5-005).
- BR4 is executed by comparing the submitted type, case and field values with the stored ones at the moment of the store call, and by writing CORRECTED when any of the three differs and CONFIRMED when none does.
- BR5 is executed by the field patch: the corrected value goes to `field_value`, the extracted value stays in `extracted_value`, the caller goes to `confirmed_by` and the row increments `version`.
- BR6 is executed by the store operation of RWB-P5-E1024-APP: the DOCATT record of DP-03 is written inside the same transaction as the `document` row, the `document_field` rows, the write-once placement in `rwb-docs-legal` and the outbox row, so a failed record leaves nothing behind (R-UNI-39; ASM-1812).
- BR7 is executed by answering the labeled example on the item read and by publishing `rwb.document.DocumentFieldsExtracted.v1` for the resolved item; the evaluation path of RWB-E1-060 is P10's and this story only exposes the shape.
- BR8 is executed by the optimistic lock on `document_intake.version` for the resolve and on `document_field.version` and the `If-Match` document version for the field patch; a stale version answers 409 with MSG-GEN-004.
- BR9 is executed by the discard action: `review_outcome` DISCARDED, `discard_reason`, `resolved_by` and `resolved_at` are written, the file stays in `rwb-quarantine` and the content read still returns it; nothing is deleted.
- BR10 is executed by the masking the service applies to a `document_field` value and to a page of `document_text` before the answer leaves the service, by role; the masking rule is `rwb-access` data (DF-DOC-015, DL26) and every read of the item is written to the PII access log by the ACE common module, never by this package.
- DP-01 keeps every read in `rwb_document`; DP-07 keeps the four lists out of the code; DP-09 puts the event in the outbox inside the transaction; DP-15 puts the migration in the per-service sequence; DP-19 puts the two screens behind the gateway-bff composite route.

##### 9. State transitions

None for the case. This story does not change a case status. It sets document_intake.review_outcome (ATTACHED or DISCARDED), document.review_status (PENDING to CONFIRMED or CORRECTED) and document_field.state (REVIEW to CONFIRMED or CORRECTED).

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Intake item with review_reason | Attach | BR3 passes; store succeeds | review_outcome ATTACHED |
| Intake item with review_reason | Discard | Reason given | review_outcome DISCARDED |
| document.review_status PENDING | Review completed | Nothing changed | CONFIRMED |
| document.review_status PENDING | Review completed | A value changed | CORRECTED |

| From (`document_field.state`) | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| REVIEW | Confirm | The value is kept and the row version matches | CONFIRMED |
| REVIEW | Correct | A new value passes the type and range check and the row version matches | CORRECTED |
| CONFIRMED or CORRECTED | The same confirmation arrives again | Same value, same flag, same version | CONFIRMED or CORRECTED, unchanged with 200 |

The intake states are the field values of `review_outcome` and of `review_status` and not a workflow: an item that is attached or discarded leaves the queue for good, and a document whose review is completed stops being PENDING. An item in any held state is not selected by the queue query of BR1 again, and an item whose store call failed on the decision record stays in the queue untouched (X13). The document state machine COPY_PENDING to STORED belongs to RWB-P5-E1024-APP and is not changed by this story.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer | Lists, reads, corrects, attaches and discards review items in scope (Documents CRU) |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Lists, reads, corrects and attaches review items of own cases (Documents CRU) |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | Reads the queue for the team (Documents R); cannot correct or attach |
| SY-OCR, OCR and extraction pipeline | Re-runs extraction on a type change (Documents CRU) |
| SY-DECLOG, decision log writer | Writes the DOCATT entry through DocumentStore |
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Reads the labeled examples through the model evaluations (Documents R) |

Every "who" in this table is a **role code** held as data in `rwb-access` (P4): roles as data, scope and masking policy are P4's and reach this service as the cached permission decision of the service template. This story adds no guard of its own and inherits the 403 shapes of MSG-P4-002 and the 404 shape of MSG-P4-003; its C list carries no `rwb-access` row, which is recorded in ASM-1815. SY-DECLOG is the local decision-record library of DP-03 in the target, called by the store inside the caller's transaction, and it publishes the DOCATT record on `rwb.decision-record.v1`. SY-OCR is the extraction operation of RWB-P5-E1053-APP in the same service. The worker runs as the rwb-document service identity (DP-02), carried by the chart as a secret reference; the login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1010).

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary and the TSD P5 T3.1 table. No `recovery_case` row is copied and no ACE view is read by this service: DF-CAS-002 and DF-CAS-005 arrive inside the `rwb-case` case record answer, and DP-01 forbids a foreign-schema read. The intake columns DF-DOC-070 to DF-DOC-084 come from RWB-P5-E1050-CON, RWB-P5-E1053-CON and RWB-P5-E1032-APP, and this story adds no new intake column except the four it writes. Personal data never enters the event payload, the outbox row or the log: field values and OCR text are masked by role on the screen and are never logged; a log line carries the intake item ID or the document ID, the action, the outcome and the version, never a value, a text page, a file name or an account number in clear.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-document (P5); base `/api/recovery/document/v1`; the shapes are those of RWB-P5-E1054-CON.

| Method | Path | Owner | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/review-items` | P5 | The review queue of SCR-31 (legacy `GET /review-items`, API-P5-010): query `kind` (INTAKE, DOCUMENT or ALL, default ALL), `reason`, `page`, `size` (default the REVIEW_PAGE_SIZE row, 50); answer 200 `ReviewItemPage`, oldest first, filtered by BR2 before the page is cut; Documents R, scope applied; no `Idempotency-Key` |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}` | P5 | One held item as `IntakeItem` (API-P5-011): source, received time, review reason, predicted type, the type candidates, the candidate cases with their status, the OCR text pages, the extracted fields masked by role, the review outcome and the version; each read written to the PII access log |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/content` | P5 | The file of the held item as `application/octet-stream` (API-P5-012), read from `rwb-quarantine` through the storage product; a discarded item still answers with its file (BR9) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/resolve` | P5 | Set the type, attach the item to a case in scope with confirmed fields, or discard it with a reason (API-P5-013): request `IntakeResolveRequest` with action SET_TYPE, ATTACH or DISCARD; answer 200 `IntakeResolution` carrying the item and, for ATTACH, the stored `Document`; Documents U, scope applied; `Idempotency-Key` required; `version` in the body is the optimistic lock |
| PATCH | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/fields/{fieldId}` | P5 | Confirm or correct one field of a stored document (the legacy field patch under the base `/api/recovery/v1`, rebased by DP-13; API-P5-006): request `FieldReview` with `value` (required when `confirmed` is false) and `confirmed`, header `If-Match` with the document version; answer 200 `DocumentField`; a repeat with the same value and flag answers 200 and changes nothing (AC17) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/review` | P5 | Complete the review of a stored document with action COMPLETE (API-P5-014): request `DocumentReviewRequest` with `action` and `version`; answer 200 `Document` with the final review_status; 422 with MSG-GEN-001 when a field is still in REVIEW; Documents U |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}` | P5, owned by the document read of RWB-P5-E1024-APP | The document, its type, its fields with state and values, its review_status and its version, behind AC16's 404 with MSG-P4-003 and the drill-down after an attach; this story declares it for the baseline and changes none of its fields |

The seven operations are the ones RWB-ITG-E1054-ITG consumes, and the six of this key's own are declared in RWB-P5-E1054-CON. The legacy `/review-queue` name of the controller and the `DocumentHubController` split of the legacy section 13 are not published: one controller serves the queue and one the item, and the field patch keeps its own operation (ASM-1808). The 404 of X10 belongs to the document read and is inherited, not reimplemented.

The other calls are inside the service and are not contracts of another service: the store operation of RWB-P5-E1024-APP writes the `document` and `document_field` rows, the write-once placement and the DOCATT record of one attach; the extraction operation of RWB-P5-E1053-APP re-runs the extraction of a new type in AC10; and the document read of RWB-P5-E1024-APP answers the drill-down and AC16. They appear in 12.9 as REST consumed inside the service. A failed case read maps to 503 with MSG-GEN-006 naming the system that failed and leaves the item untouched; it never becomes a 404 and never a silent pass.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document`, module `review`; front end folder `recovery/documents`. The legacy Java package `recovery.dochub.review` is retired.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| ReviewQueueController | Controller | `GET /review-items`, the item read and the content read, with the scope filter, the masking and the RFC 9457 error mapping |
| ReviewQueueService | Service | Builds the queue and the item answer with the scope rule of BR2 and the oldest-first order of BR1 |
| ReviewResolutionService | Service | SET_TYPE, ATTACH and DISCARD on an item: BR3 to BR9, the type check against `document_type`, the case check through the contract, the store call and the item update |
| FieldReviewService | Service | Confirm and correct one field: the empty-value check, the type and range check of `REVIEW_DATE_MIN` to `REVIEW_DATE_MAX`, the `If-Match` document version and the idempotent repeat of AC17 |
| DocumentReviewService | Service | Completes the review with action COMPLETE and sets `review_status` CONFIRMED or CORRECTED |
| LabeledExampleProjection | Read model | Answers the labeled example on the item read — predicted type, confirmed type, extracted value and corrected value — in place of the retired `LabeledSetReader` |
| ReviewQueueRepository | Repository | Reads and writes `document_intake` and `document_field`, reads `document`, `document_text`, `document_type` and `document_hub_parameter`; `version` is the optimistic lock |
| ReviewQueuePage | React component | The SCR-31 list, the filters, the paging and the empty state |
| ReviewItemPanel | React component | The file and OCR text viewer, the type chooser with candidates, the case chooser, the fields with Confirm and Correct, Attach and Discard |

**Database.**

- One migration in the per-service Flyway sequence (DP-15): `V1054_1__review_outcome.sql` adds to `document_intake` `review_outcome` varchar(12), `resolved_by` uuid, `resolved_at` timestamptz and `discard_reason` varchar(400); the classification, extraction and match columns come from the migrations of RWB-P5-E1050-CON, RWB-P5-E1053-CON and RWB-P5-E1032-APP.
- Index `ix_intake_review ON document_intake (received_at) WHERE review_reason IS NOT NULL AND review_outcome IS NULL`; index `ix_document_review ON document (review_status, created_at) WHERE review_status = 'PENDING'`. Both are partial, so the queue query of BR1 never scans a resolved row.

**Configuration and reference data.**

- `document_hub_parameter` rows REVIEW_TEAM_UNATTACHED "DOC-SVC" (assumed), REVIEW_DATE_MIN 2000-01-01, REVIEW_DATE_MAX 2100-12-31 and REVIEW_PAGE_SIZE 50, loaded by the reference data administrator and read from this service's own table (ASM-1807); the production value of the review team is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1010).
- DOCTYPE version in force through the versioned `document_type` of this service (RWB-E1-025; DL19), and the type codes checked against LOV-DOC-TYPE (DP-07). No type code is typed in code.
- Reference lists LOV-INTAKE-REVIEW, LOV-INTAKE-OUTCOME, LOV-REVIEW and LOV-DOC-TYPE read through the reference-data contract (DP-07, ASM-1809).
- Decision code DOCATT, assumed, with the LOV-DECISION list loaded by the data steward.
- Feature flag `rwb.document.review` (ASM-1813). Off: SCR-31 is hidden and review items stay in the queue untouched, exactly as the legacy flag states.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-01 moves the six tables the legacy story reads and writes into `rwb_document` and stops the module reaching into the recovery schema: `document_intake`, `document_text`, `document`, `document_field`, `document_type` and `document_hub_parameter` are all P5's, and the case is never a local copy. DP-03 replaces `DecisionLogWriter` and the `DocumentStore`-internal write with the local decision-record library, so the DOCATT record, the document row, the field rows, the item update and the outbox row share one transaction and the record is published on the shared topic. DP-07 keeps the review reasons, the two outcome values, the four review statuses and the type codes out of the code through the client library and the `rwb-case` contract. DP-09 puts `rwb.document.DocumentFieldsExtracted.v1` in the outbox inside the same transaction and fixes the CloudEvents envelope and the retry and `.dlt` topics. DP-11 is the two case reads: in-process `CaseDirectory` becomes one hop on a published shape with a fake in the build and a 2 s timeout; the same-service calls to the store, the extraction and the document read keep the one-hop rule without a contract of another service. DP-13 rebases the two legacy paths that carried `/api/recovery/v1` — the field patch of legacy section 12 and the document read of AC16 — onto `/api/recovery/document/v1`, with no change of verb, shape or message. DP-15 puts the four review columns and the two partial indexes in the service's own Flyway sequence. DP-19 puts the queue and the item panel behind the gateway-bff composite route, so SCR-31 calls the owner once and the screen model merges the case and reference answers.

**Build steps**

1. Write the migration and the indexes; test that the held index returns only unresolved items, that the document index returns only PENDING documents and that the optimistic lock refuses a stale `version`.
2. Build `ReviewQueueService` with the scope rule of BR2 and the oldest-first order; test AC14 and AC15 and the two scope halves of AC1 and AC14.
3. Build the item read and the content read with masking and the PII access log; test AC1, AC16 and the access test TC-E1-054-18.
4. Build SET_TYPE with the type check and the extraction re-run through RWB-P5-E1053-APP; test AC5 and AC10.
5. Build the field confirm and correct with the empty-value check, the range check and the `If-Match` version; test AC3, AC4, AC6, AC9 and AC17.
6. Build ATTACH through the store with BR3, the duplicate link and the outcome; test AC2, AC7, AC8, AC11 and the decision-record failure TC-E1-054-19.
7. Build DISCARD and `LabeledExampleProjection`; test AC12, AC13 and the labeled example of AC2.
8. Build `ReviewQueuePage` and `ReviewItemPanel` on SCR-31 with the Loading, List, Reviewed and Empty states; browser tests (RWB-TE-010).

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the seventeen legacy criteria hold on synthetic data, SCR-31 passes the browser and accessibility tests of RWB-TE-010, and no review item leaves the queue without one of the two outcome values, one store row and — for an attach — one DOCATT record and one `DocumentFieldsExtracted` event.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P5-003 | An item or document is in the review queue | Some fields need checking. The document is in the review queue. |
| MSG-P5-005 | The chosen case is closed (new) | Case {case} is closed. Choose an open case. |
| MSG-P5-006 | The chosen type is not in force (new) | {value} is not a document type in force. Choose a type from the list. |
| MSG-P5-024 | The file is already on the case | This file is already on the case as {document}. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | Empty value, empty reason, or field still in review | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-002 | Date outside the allowed range | {field} must be between {min} and {max}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | Saved against an old version | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-GEN-005 | Field, attach or discard saved | Saved. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Decision log write failed on attach | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Caller lacks Documents U | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | Item or document outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P4-001 | No authenticated caller | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1010; ASM-1816) |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A consumed read failed or timed out | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1010; ASM-1816) |
| not-found message | An intake item or a document that does not exist | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1010; ASM-1816) |

Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

Delivery shape: every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set to the ID above, `detail` carrying the text with its placeholders filled, and `instance` naming the request. The HTTP mapping is the legacy one and is fixed by AC4 to AC13 and the baseline RWB-P5-E1054-CON: 401 for MSG-P4-001, 403 for MSG-P4-002, 404 for MSG-P4-003 and for an item or a document that does not exist, 409 for MSG-GEN-004, 422 for MSG-GEN-001, MSG-GEN-002, MSG-P5-005 and MSG-P5-006, and 503 for MSG-P7-003 and MSG-GEN-006. MSG-P5-003 is not an error response: it is the label of a held item on SCR-31. MSG-GEN-005 is the confirmation of a saved action and not an error. The three platform rows — MSG-P4-001, MSG-GEN-006 and the not-found message — are named by the target error envelope and their exact texts are Not specified in this key's source documents, so they carry the placeholder above.

| Screen | State | What the user does |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-31 Document review queue | Loading | Skeleton rows while the queue loads through the gateway-bff composite route |
| SCR-31 Document review queue | List | Sees review items oldest first with reason, candidates, confidence and age; opens one; sets type and case, confirms or corrects fields, attaches or discards |

| SCR-31 Document review queue | Refused | An empty correction answers MSG-GEN-001, a type outside the list MSG-P5-006, a date outside the range MSG-GEN-002, a field still in REVIEW MSG-GEN-001, a closed case MSG-P5-005, a stale version MSG-GEN-004 and a role without Documents U MSG-P4-002; nothing is saved and the item keeps its state |
| SCR-31 Document review queue | Reviewed | After attach, discard or complete the item leaves the list and MSG-GEN-005 shows |
| SCR-31 Document review queue | Empty (common state) | Sees "No documents are waiting for review." |
| SCR-30 Case documents | List | Sees the attached document with its confirmed or corrected type and fields |

The queue and the item panel are reached through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), which calls this service once for the queue and once for the item and merges the case answer for the drill-down. The case document list on SCR-30 is RWB-P5-E1026-APP and the release work that hides SCR-31 behind the flag is this story's. The route specification and the screen field list beyond the legacy section 15 are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1010; ASM-1808).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the review team, the date limits and the page size are rows of `document_hub_parameter`; the reasons, outcomes, statuses and types are reference data read through DP-07 and the versioned `document_type` of this service.
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts: field values and OCR text are masked by role and never logged; a log line carries the item or document ID, the action, the outcome and the version; test data is synthetic.
- No read of another module's tables: the case is resolved through the `rwb-case` contract, one hop with a 2 s timeout, and no `v_ace_*` view and no `recovery.*` table is read by this service (DP-01, DP-11).
- Attach goes only through the store of RWB-P5-E1024-APP, so a document never exists without its DOCATT record and a legal type never reaches the write-once container without the record first.
- The decision record is written in the same transaction as the document, the fields, the item update and the outbox row; a failure stores nothing and raises the incident of R-UNI-39.
- A discarded item is never removed: the file stays in `rwb-quarantine`, the reason and the person are kept, and the content read still answers (REQ-DCM-019).
- The queue and the item read are GETs with no side effect and no `Idempotency-Key`; the resolve and the review completion are POSTs with the header, and the field patch is idempotent on the same value and flag.
- No field value and no OCR text enters the event payload or the decision record; the payload carries the item ID, the document ID, the type, the field count and the review status.
- The feature flag `rwb.document.review` removes the queue from the screen without a rollback of the schema.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-054 for rwb-access. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **litigation officer, a case owner, a team manager, a compliance and PDPA officer or an internal auditor who works the document review queue**, I want **the access service to answer, for one review item or one stored document in front of me, whether my role may read it, which scope admits it, whether my role may resolve it, and which of the fields it carries come back masked**, so that **a low-confidence document is shown only to the people entitled to work it, a correction is offered only to the role that may make it, and no OCR text and no extracted value ever leaves the document service on the strength of this answer**.

Inside `rwb-access` this is the access-side capability of legacy RWB-E1-054:

- Service `rwb-access`, schema `rwb_access`, REST base `/api/recovery/access/v1`, topic `rwb.access.events.v1` with event names `rwb.access.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-access` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`.
- The capability answers four questions behind the three operations the service already publishes, `POST /authorise`, `GET /me/permissions` and `GET /masking-policies`, and it adds no operation: does the caller hold Documents right R for the item, document, its content and the queue; does the caller hold Documents right U for resolve (`SET_TYPE`, `ATTACH`, `DISCARD`), for the field confirm and correct and for the review completion; does the scope in force admit this item or this document; and which of the field IDs the caller asks about are returned masked. The queue endpoints, SCR-31 Document review queue, the intake rows, the documents, the fields, the candidates, the review outcome, the labeled set, DocumentStore and the DOCATT entry stay in `rwb-document` (P5) and are RWB-P5-E1054-APP's; this story builds no screen, stores no document and starts no job.
- The item and document facts the decision needs — the item reference, its review reason, its predicted type, its candidates, its review team and its candidate cases, and for a stored document its case, the case's team and owner and the field IDs in `REVIEW` — arrive in the authorise request, built by `rwb-document` from its own rows. The attribute set of an authorise request for a review item, including the review team of an unattached item, is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0988; ASM-1736).
- The policy the answers come from is data in `rwb_access`: the role list, the role-to-permission matrix version in force (`PM-2026.12`), the scope rule with LOV-SCOPE, and the masking rows (`MASK-SIT-01`). The parameter `REVIEW_TEAM_UNATTACHED` belongs to `rwb-document` and is read as a value in the request: this service compares the caller's team with it and writes no copy of it. Loading and approving a policy pack is the load path of RWB-P4-AD002-APP and RWB-P4-AD004-APP and is out of scope here.
- The access log is a decision-record entry on `rwb.decision-record.v1` written through the local library of DP-03: `AC-READ` for a granted read of an item or its content with the item reference, the field IDs and their masked markers, `AC-DENY` for a refusal with the area DOCUMENTS and the right and no item fact (FEAT-ACA-07, FEAT-ACA-08).

The legacy behaviour carried into the access service is unchanged: the same scope rule of RWB-E1-054 `BR2` (an item with no case goes to the review team named by `REVIEW_TEAM_UNATTACHED` and to roles whose default scope is ALL; an item with candidate cases and a stored document go by case scope), the same refusal of a role that holds Documents R only when it tries to resolve (legacy X12, access test TC-E1-054-18), the same "not in your scope" answer with no fact for an item or a document outside the scope (legacy AC16), and the same masking of extracted values with no covering row meaning masked (legacy BR10, AC-EXC-P4-004-05).

##### 2. Business rationale

A wrong type or a wrong hearing date on a court notice puts the wrong date on a case and the litigation timers run from it, which is why RWB-E1-054 routes every item the pipeline could not type, read or match to a person. That person reads OCR text and extracted values of documents that belong to customers, so the queue is a PDPA surface before it is a work list: CTL-09 and CTL-11 sit on the scope of the queue and on the masking of field values, NFR-039 and NFR-040 require masking by role at rest and in use, NFR-042 requires every read of the document store to be logged, and REQ-DCM-019 forbids any document leaving the hub silently. A queue that is readable by every role that can sign in, or that answers with a value instead of a marker, defeats all four controls at once.

This story supplies the authority slice of that queue: the two rights (Documents R for reading, Documents U for resolving), the scope rule of the queue, and the masked markers for the fields it shows, behind the three operations `rwb-access` already publishes. It meets REQ-DCM-005 and REQ-DCM-019 on the access side, and supports the measure "rule and limit changes made without a code release" at 100 percent, because the matrix, the scope values, the masking rows and their versions are data. The measure of success is that every read of a review item or a stored document is granted or refused by the policy in force, that a role holding Documents R is never granted a resolve, that a field with no masking row comes back masked, and that every granted read leaves one `AC-READ` entry naming the field IDs and their markers and nothing else.

This story implements the decision behind those operations for the review queue; it adds no operation |

Which attributes of them an authorise request carries is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0988; ASM-1736) |

Business preconditions carried from RWB-E1-054, owned by other services where they say so:

That these are the letters of the matrix version at the release date is assumed (GAP-0988; ASM-1737).

The parameter row and its value are RWB-P5-E1054-APP's; this story names the value and writes none of it (legacy section 3; ASM-1736).

##### 4. Flow

1. Caller: a review user opens SCR-31. gateway-bff resolves the session; `rwb-document` reads the item or the stored document from its own rows and builds the authorise request.
2. Caller: the request names the area `DOCUMENTS`, the right — `R` for the queue read, the item read, the content read and the document read, `U` for resolve, for the field confirm and correct and for the review completion — the item reference or the document reference, the scope attributes the policy reads (the owning user reference, the review team of an unattached item, the candidate cases with their team and region, the case of a stored document with its team, region and owner) and the field IDs the screen is about to show. The full attribute set is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0988; ASM-1736).
3. `rwb-access`: resolves the caller's roles from the session the ACE common module resolved at sign-in, and the rights from `permission` for the matrix version in force, `PM-2026.12`. `role`, `permission`, `matrix_version` and their versions are read from `rwb_access` only.
4. `rwb-access`, right check: no DOCUMENTS R for any role the caller holds gives a refusal, 403 with MSG-P4-002 naming the action, and no item fact (BR1). The refusal is written as an `AC-DENY` entry (BR7).
5. `rwb-access`, resolve check: for right `U` the caller must hold the letter `U`; a caller holding Documents R only is refused 403 with MSG-P4-002 naming the action, before any item or candidate is read (BR1; legacy X12). The refusal is an `AC-DENY` entry and the item is untouched.
6. `rwb-access`, scope check: an item with no case and no candidate case is in scope when the caller's team is the review team the request names — the `REVIEW_TEAM_UNATTACHED` value of the document hub — or when the caller's `default_scope` in force is `ALL`; an item with candidate cases and a stored document are in scope when the candidate case or the document's case satisfies the caller's `default_scope` read from LOV-SCOPE: OWN for a case the caller owns, TEAM for a case of the caller's team, REGION for a case of the caller's region, ALL for any case (BR2; legacy BR2).
7. `rwb-access`: an item or a document outside the scope is answered 404 with MSG-P4-003 and no fact, so the answer never confirms that an item or a document exists, and the refusal is written as an `AC-DENY` entry (BR3).
8. `rwb-access`, masking: for each field ID the request names, the marker is read from `masking_rule` for the roles the caller holds and the masking version in force, `MASK-SIT-01`. A field with no covering row is masked (BR5). The answer marks each field `masked` or `clear`; it never carries the value, the extracted value or the OCR text (BR5).
9. `rwb-access`: writes one `AC-READ` decision record through the library of DP-03, with the item reference or the document reference, the field IDs and their masked markers, and returns the answer to the caller inside the 2 s timeout of DP-11 (BR6; AC-READ).
10. `rwb-access`: caches the policy answer for the versions in force. A caller that asks again under the same versions is answered from the cache and reads no matrix row twice; the `AC-READ` entry is still written for that read (BR9).
11. Policy change: a new matrix version (`PM-2026.13`) or a new masking version (`MASK-SIT-02`) is approved through the load path, `rwb-access` writes the rows and publishes `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` on `rwb.access.events.v1`; every caller drops its cached answer and the next request is answered under the new version, with no deployment (BR9).
12. Document service: performs the resolve, the field confirm or correct and the review completion on its own rows and renders SCR-31 with the granted fields and their masked markers, or the "not in your scope" page for a 404 (RWB-P5-E1054-APP).

Every answer, granted or refused, is written before it is returned; when the record cannot be written nothing is returned, the call answers 503 with MSG-P7-003 and an incident is raised, so no read of a review item is ever unlogged (BR6, BR7, BR8).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The item or the document is outside the caller's scope | Not found: 404 with no item fact; one `AC-DENY` entry, no item fact | MSG-P4-003 | AC5, AC3 |
| X2 | The caller holds Documents R only and calls resolve, corrects a field or completes a review | Refused before any item fact is read: 403, no item and no candidate | MSG-P4-002 | AC4, AC7 |
| X3 | No masking rule covers a review field | The field is marked `masked` with the default marker; the read is otherwise granted | None | AC6 |
| X4 | The token carries no Recovery role, or no second factor | No answer is given: 401 before the policy is read; one refusal entry with the reason | MSG-P4-001 | BR4 |
| X5 | The decision record cannot be written | Nothing is shown: 503 with no item fact, and an incident is raised to the platform administrator queue | MSG-P7-003 | AC7, TC-E1-054-19 |
| X6 | Two roles of the caller conflict (for example RW-SECADM with a business role) | The sign-in access check refuses the session from the `role_conflict` rows this service holds; no authorise request is made | MSG-P4-006 | BR4 |
| X7 | The caller is an agent or a service identity, not a person | The same checks run under the service identity's roles; a service identity with no role is refused 401 | MSG-P4-001 | BR4, section 10 |
| X8 | The reference list of scope is not available | No answer is given rather than a guessed one: 503; the refusal is recorded | MSG-GEN-006 | BR2 |
| X9 | A new type is set on the item and extraction runs again for it | Not this story's: the re-run and its fields are P5's; the access answer is recomputed on the next read with the new field IDs | None | Out of scope |

An answer that spans two masking versions in force on the same day is not specified in the source documents (GAP-0988; ASM-1737); until it is, the version whose `valid_from` is the latest on or before the business date is used, and the answer names the version it used. The legacy attach case X13 / TC-E1-054-19 is the document side of the record-before-the-answer rule: the attach transaction, its document and its DOCATT entry are P5's, and this story's record is the read and the refusal.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds and tests against RWB-P5-E1054-CON and the contract fake of the item and document facts; reads its own schema only and calls no other service at run time |
| Negotiable | The policy pack — roles, letters, scope values, masking rows and their versions — is data; the story fixes the shape of the answer, the scope rule and the refusal behaviour only |
| Valuable | The queue reaches the people entitled to work it, a correction is offered only to the role that may make it, and no value or OCR text crosses the boundary on this answer |
| Estimable | Four answers behind three existing operations, one cache, one decision-record path and two indexes |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests; no screen, no document, no job and no workflow |
| Testable | Every owned criterion has a test case in section 16; the document side is a published fake |

```gherkin
    Then the second answer is served from the cached decision without a second read of the permission matrix
    Then each answer is returned inside the 2 s timeout and each granted read writes its own AC-READ entry
    Then when policy version "PM-2026.13" and masking version "MASK-SIT-02" are approved and rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1 is published for both
    Then the next ask is answered under matrix version "PM-2026.13" and masking version "MASK-SIT-02" with no deployment
    Then the earlier change from "PM-2026.11" to "PM-2026.12" reached the answer the same way
```

AC1 to AC8 are the criteria this story owns; the document-side criteria AC1 to AC17 of the legacy key are owned by RWB-P5-E1054-APP/CON and are proved against this story's answers. In AC1 the two assertions that belong to this service are the scope it names and the masked markers on the field IDs; the queue list, its order and its content are P5's. In AC2 the two callers prove that an unattached item is admitted by the review team and by scope ALL, and that a caller whose team is another team is answered 404 rather than a list. In AC3 the same document follows its case and not its reader, so a document of another team is not found. In AC4 and AC7 the refusal is proved twice for the same legacy case: as the answer the caller gets, with no item fact, and as the refusal entry the audit reads; the second half of AC7 is the record-before-the-answer rule of X13 applied to a read. In AC5 the 404 carries no review reason, no candidate and no case number, so the answer never confirms that the item exists. In AC6 the default is masked when no row covers the field, which is AC-EXC-P4-004-05 of the FSD and BR10 of the legacy key. In AC8 the cached answer is proved to change on the policy event, for both the matrix and the masking version, with no deployment.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Documents right R gates the queue read, the intake item read, its content read and the document read; Documents right U gates resolve (`SET_TYPE`, `ATTACH`, `DISCARD`), the field confirm and correct and the review completion; a caller whose roles hold no such right is refused with MSG-P4-002 naming the action and no item fact | FSD P4 A2.4 VR-P4-004-1; legacy RWB-E1-054 X12, TC-E1-054-18 and section 12 authorization rows; FEAT-ACA-04 |
| BR2 | An intake item with no case and no candidate case is in scope when the caller's team is the review team named by `REVIEW_TEAM_UNATTACHED` in the request, or when the caller's `default_scope` in force is ALL; an item with candidate cases and a stored document are in scope when the candidate case or the document's case satisfies the caller's `default_scope`: OWN, TEAM, REGION or ALL | legacy RWB-E1-054 BR2, AC14; FSD P4 A2.14 VR-P4-014-1; LOV-SCOPE; CTL-09 |
| BR3 | An item or a document outside the scope is answered 404 with MSG-P4-003 and no fact, so the answer never confirms that it exists | FSD P4 A2.14 VR-P4-014-1; legacy RWB-E1-054 X10, AC16 |
| BR4 | No Recovery role, or no second factor, is answered 401 with MSG-P4-001 before the policy is read, and one refusal entry is written with the reason | FSD P4 A2.1 VR-P4-001-1, AC-EXC-P4-001-01; TSD P4 T6.2 |
| BR5 | A review field is marked `masked` unless a `masking_rule` row for a role the caller holds and that field says unmasked true for the masking version in force; with no covering row the field is masked; the answer carries markers only, never a value, an extracted value or OCR text | FSD P4 A2.5; AC-EXC-P4-004-05; NFR-039; NFR-040; legacy RWB-E1-054 BR10 |
| BR6 | Every granted read of an intake item, its content or a stored document writes one `AC-READ` decision record with the item or document reference and the field IDs with their masked markers, before the answer is returned | FSD P4 A2.7 AC-P4-007-01, A2.8; FEAT-ACA-07; FEAT-ACA-08; NFR-042 |
| BR7 | Every refusal writes one `AC-DENY` decision record with the area DOCUMENTS and the right, and carries no item reference and no case fact | FSD P4 A2.7 AC-EXC-P4-007-04; FEAT-ACA-07 |
| BR8 | The record is written before the answer; when it cannot be written nothing is shown, the call answers 503 with MSG-P7-003 and an incident is raised | FSD P4 AC-EXC-P4-007-03; legacy RWB-E1-054 X13, TC-E1-054-19; DP-03 |
| BR9 | An answer is cached for the matrix and masking versions in force and dropped when `AccessPolicyChanged` arrives, so a policy change takes effect with no deployment | Architecture v5 slide 43; FSD P4 AC-P4-004-01; DP-11 |
| BR10 | The intake rows, the documents, the fields, the comments, the review outcome, the labeled set, DocumentStore and the DOCATT entry are `rwb-document`'s; this service holds no item, no document and no field and reads no foreign table | DP-01; ownership map (document, document_intake, document_field, document_text, document_checklist_item to P5) |

Target-service statements that make the rules hold in `rwb-access`:

- BR1 is a read of `permission` for the caller's roles and the `matrix_version` in force; the letters C, R, U, D and A are held as the five-character field of TSD P4 T3.1, and the answer names the version it used. Documents R and Documents U are two letters of one row, so the resolve refusal of AC4 costs one read and no join.
- BR2 is the scope rule of `ScopeRule` comparing the attributes of the request with the `default_scope` value read through DP-07. The unattached-item rule is one branch of it: it compares the caller's team with the review team value the request carries, which is `REVIEW_TEAM_UNATTACHED` of the document hub, and it reads the parameter from no table of this service. The scope names OWN, TEAM, REGION and ALL are list values, never Java constants, and the attribute names of a request are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0988; ASM-1736).
- BR3 is the same rule answering not found rather than forbidden, because a 403 on an out-of-scope item would confirm that the item exists; the refusal entry is the only place the attempt is recorded.
- BR4 is the sign-in check this service already holds the rows for; it runs before any policy read, so a caller with no role costs no query.
- BR5 is a read of `masking_rule` by `field_id`, `role_code` and `masking_version`; the answer carries markers, never values, so no personal data crosses the boundary in either direction (NFR-039, NFR-040). The OCR text and the extracted values never enter this service at all: they are P5's and are not part of any request or answer.
- BR6, BR7 and BR8 are the same `RecordAndApply` transaction as the answer: the record is written first, the answer is returned after it commits, and a failure answers 503 with MSG-P7-003 and shows nothing.
- BR9 is a cache keyed by the pair of versions in force; the `AccessPolicyChanged` entry that drops it is published by the same transaction that writes the new policy rows.
- BR10 is the reason there is no repository for an item or a document: the service holds `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule`, `role_conflict`, the decision record, the outbox and the inbox, and nothing else.

##### 9. State transitions

None for a case or a document. This story changes no case status, no intake item, no document review status, no field state and no review outcome: `document_intake.review_outcome`, `document.review_status` and `document_field.state` are P5's and move on P5's calls (legacy section 9). This story runs no workflow of its own and owns no Schedule.

The only states this story has are the states of its answer and of its record, which it does not persist beyond the record:

| Answer state | When | What the caller gets | Record written |
|---|---|---|---|
| Granted | The caller holds the right and the item or the document is in scope, by the review-team rule or by case scope | The granted answer with the scope it used, the item or document reference, and the masked or clear marker per field ID | `AC-READ` |
| Refused, no right | No role of the caller holds Documents R, or the caller holds R only and asks for U | 403 MSG-P4-002 naming the action, no item fact | `AC-DENY` |
| Not found | The caller holds the right and the item or the document is outside the scope | 404 MSG-P4-003, no item fact | `AC-DENY` |
| Not answered | The record cannot be written, or the scope list cannot be read | 503 with MSG-P7-003 or MSG-GEN-006, nothing shown | None; the failure is raised as an incident |

The review-team rule of BR2 has no stored state: it is computed per request from the review team the request carries and the caller's team and default scope, so an item that acquires a candidate case moves from the review-team rule to the case-scope rule on the next request with no call between the services.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer | Documents CRU with default scope TEAM: reads the queue, an item of its review team and a document of its team's cases, and is granted resolve; the resolve itself is P5's |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Documents CRU with default scope OWN: reads an item or a document of its own cases and is granted resolve on them |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | Documents R with default scope TEAM: reads the queue for the team; refused 403 MSG-P4-002 on resolve, on a field correction and on a review completion |
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Documents R: reads the queue and the labeled examples through the model evaluations; no resolve and no correction |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Documents CRUA with default scope ALL: reads any item and any document; the field markers stay `masked` |
| RW-COMPLY, Compliance and PDPA officer | Reads which masking version is in force and which fields it covers through `GET /masking-policies`; this story writes no value on their behalf and grants no item on that basis |
| RW-REFADM and every role with no Documents right | Refused with MSG-P4-002 on every read of the queue, an item, its content or a document |
| SY-OCR, OCR and extraction pipeline | Documents CRU as a service identity: asks the same question before re-running extraction on a type change, and its roles are checked as a person's are |

No delegation-of-authority level applies to a review: a review is a read with a correction, not an approval with a limit, so the DoA table and its lookup are RWB-P4-E2013-APP's and RWB-P4-E2014-APP's and this story reads no `delegation_limit` row.

This story grants or refuses a read and, for the resolve, the right to make one; it changes no item, no document, no field and no policy row. A policy row changes only through the load path of RWB-P4-AD002-APP and RWB-P4-AD004-APP, and a break-glass grant, its incident reference and its four-hour ceiling stay with the wave-1 stories of the access service.

The database login is per service (DP-02). Its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0988; ASM-1736); the story refers to "the rwb-access login (DP-02)".

| DF-REF-040 to DF-REF-044 | `permission` | id, role_id, capability_area, letters, matrix_version | Read |

| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision record (local library, DP-03) | the `AC-READ` and `AC-DENY` entries: code, actor, area, right, item or document reference, actions, decided at | Write |

The document field IDs the answer marks are identifiers only, taken from the request and never from a query:

| Field ID | Name in the document hub | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|
| DF-DOC-015 | `document_field.field_value` | Identifier only; never read by SQL |
| DF-DOC-017 | `document_field.confirmed_by` | Identifier only; never read by SQL |
| DF-DOC-034 | `document_field.extracted_value` | Identifier only; never read by SQL |

| DF-DOC-081 | `document_intake.review_outcome` | Identifier only; never read by SQL |

The field IDs the answer marks appear in `masking_rule.field_id` and in the answer as identifiers only. Which review-field IDs the masking pack of `MASK-SIT-01` must cover is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0988; ASM-1740), so the story answers markers for whatever field IDs a request names and writes no roster in code. No field value, no extracted value and no OCR text enters `rwb_access`, the answer, the record or the event: masking markers are the whole payload (NFR-039, NFR-040). Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8.

The item and document facts of a request — the item reference, its review reason, its predicted type, its candidates, its review team, its candidate cases, the stored document's case with its team, region and owner, and the field IDs in state `REVIEW` — are read from the request and never from a table: `document`, `document_intake`, `document_field`, `document_text` and `document_checklist_item` are P5's, `recovery_case` is P3's and the `v_ace_*` views are P1's, and no foreign key and no query crosses a schema (DP-01). Which attributes a request must carry is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0988; ASM-1736).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None new in this story. The operations are those of the service contract already in force from wave 1 (RWB-P4-E1037-CON), on base `/api/recovery/access/v1`, owner rwb-access (P4), unchanged in path, request, response and error shape:

| Operation | Path | What this story decides behind it |
|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | The Documents right, the scope of the item or the document, and the masked or clear marker per field ID for one request. Errors 401 (MSG-P4-001), 403 (MSG-P4-002), 404 (MSG-P4-003), 503 (MSG-P7-003) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/me/permissions` | The roles, the matrix version and the default scope of the caller, as the session resolved them |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/masking-policies` | The masking version in force and the fields it covers for the caller's roles |

`GET /doa-limits` is the same service's operation and is not used here: the delegation of authority table and its routing lookup are RWB-P4-E2013-APP's.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. The item and document facts arrive in the authorise request, built by `rwb-document` from its own rows; this story calls no service at run time. The shape it expects is the one RWB-P5-E1054-CON publishes, and that contract is used as a fake in the tests (12.8) and as the alignment reference in the build.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Key | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` | `rwb.access.events.v1` | P4 | policy kind and version | the policy kind (permission matrix, masking), the version label, the valid-from date and the change reference |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | PLT library; consumed by P7 | item or document reference where there is one, else the actor reference | the hash-chained `AC-READ` or `AC-DENY` record |

CloudEvents 1.0 envelope. Neither payload carries a personal value: the `AC-READ` record carries identifiers, field IDs and markers, the `AC-DENY` record carries the area and the right only, and the policy event carries version labels. `rwb.access.DoALimitChanged.v1` belongs to the delegation slice and is not published here.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. A policy change is written and published by the same service, so the cache is dropped on the commit that publishes `AccessPolicyChanged` rather than on a consumed event; the topic exists for the other services' caches (Architecture v5 slide 43: all consume it for cache refresh).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. This story runs no Temporal workflow and registers no activity on `rwb-access`. The review queue has no workflow: an item is created by the document intake job of P5 (JOB-12) and resolved by a person through P5's operations (Architecture v5 slide 44; Temporal and Drools design).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The document intake job (JOB-12, every 15 minutes) and the retention job (JOB-17, monthly on the first Sunday) are `rwb-document`'s under Architecture v5 slide 44; this story starts no Schedule and reads no job row. The only Schedule of this service is the six-monthly access review list (JOB-18), which is RWB-P4-AD008-APP's.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|
| `role` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | The caller's roles and their `default_scope` |
| `permission` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | The DOCUMENTS letters and the `matrix_version` in force |
| `masking_rule` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | The masked or clear marker per role, field and masking version |
| `role_conflict` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | The conflicting role pairs the sign-in check reads |
| `outbox_event`, `processed_event`, `idempotency_key` | PLT library, created in `rwb_access` | Outbox, inbox and idempotency objects (DP-09) |
| `lov_value`, `reference_row`, `reference_version` | P3 (`rwb_case`) | LOV-SCOPE, read through the contract; not owned here |
| `delegation_limit` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | Not read in this story; it is the delegation slice's |

No table of `rwb_document`, `rwb_case`, `rwb_decision` or `rwb_source_data` is read: the item, the document, the fields, the OCR text, the candidates, the review outcome and the case stay with their owners, and the only facts of them that enter this service are identifiers carried by a request (DP-01).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`, module `access/review-authority`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access.review`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-01 is the reason the service answers from the attributes it is given: `document`, `document_intake`, `document_field`, `document_text` and `document_checklist_item` are P5's and `recovery_case` is P3's, so the answer is built from identifiers and never from a joined query, and the OCR text and the field values never enter the service. DP-03 is the access log: an `AC-READ` and an `AC-DENY` are decision records on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, so an access question and a review decision are answered from one log. DP-07 supplies LOV-SCOPE with the version in force, because `lov_value` stays with P3 under the ownership map; the review team of an unattached item is not a list value of this service either — it is `REVIEW_TEAM_UNATTACHED` of the document hub, carried by the request, so no scope string and no team string is a Java constant. DP-09 is the outbox: the only rows this story writes to a topic are the decision record and the policy-change event, both from the transaction that answers. DP-11 is the caller-facing boundary: one hop, 2 s timeout, cached, and the answer must hold inside it. DP-13 and DP-15 are the naming and migration conventions of the service. DP-19 is the route that renders the answer: SCR-31, its list, its reviewed state and its empty state are RWB-P5-E1054-APP's, and this story supplies only the grant, the refusal and the markers.

The platform contracts the DP rows name are preconditions of the service lane already in place behind RWB-P4-E1037-CON in wave 1; this secondary slice adds no new build dependency of its own (metadata H = None; ASM-1736), and the only contract it builds against is RWB-P5-E1054-CON, which never blocks.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| AuthoriseController | Controller | The three operations of the existing contract on `/api/recovery/access/v1`; validation and problem responses |
| ReviewAuthorityService | Service | Right, scope and masking profile for one review request, in that order; one answer, one record |
| PermissionResolver | Service | Reads `permission` for the caller's roles and the `matrix_version` in force; resolves the five letters |
| ScopeRule | Service | Compares the request attributes with the `default_scope` value in force |
| ReviewTeamRule | Service | The unattached-item branch of BR2: the caller's team against the review team the request carries |
| FieldMarkerService | Service | The masked or clear marker per field ID for the caller's roles and the masking version in force; default masked |
| AccessRecordWriter | Service | The `AC-READ` and `AC-DENY` entries through the library of DP-03, and the `AccessPolicyChanged` outbox row |
| PolicyCache | Service | The cached answer per matrix and masking version, dropped on the policy change |
| PolicyChangeListener | Service | Applies a new policy version and publishes `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` in the same transaction |
| AccessRepository | Repository | `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule`, `role_conflict`, inbox and outbox in `rwb_access`; no foreign table |

**Database and migrations**

- No new table: `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule` and `role_conflict` exist from the wave-1 stories of this service behind RWB-P4-E1037-CON, and the policy rows are loaded by the load path stories.
- One migration in the per-service Flyway sequence of DP-15: `V1054_1__review_authority_read_path.sql` adds `ix_masking_rule_role_field` on `masking_rule (role_code, field_id, masking_version)` and `ix_permission_role_area` on `permission (role_id, capability_area, matrix_version)`. These are the only two objects the migration creates, so the two reads of an answer are index reads inside the 2 s budget of DP-11. No index is created on an item, a document or a case, because no such table is read.
- The policy rows are versioned by `matrix_version`, `masking_version` and the roles' `valid_from` and `valid_to`; this story writes none of them, and a version is never edited in place (a new version is loaded, approved and published).

**Configuration and reference data**

- The matrix version and the masking version in force are data: the latest `valid_from` on or before the business date, read from `permission.matrix_version` and `masking_rule.masking_version`. The label of the matrix and masking versions in force at the release date of 30 November 2026 is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0988; ASM-1737); the tests use `PM-2026.12` and `MASK-SIT-01` and the answer always names the version it used.
- LOV-SCOPE (OWN, TEAM, REGION, ALL) through the reference-data contract of DP-07 (RWB-P3-E1043-CON). No other list is read.
- `REVIEW_TEAM_UNATTACHED` is a parameter of `rwb-document`, not of this service: the story names its assumed value `DOC-SVC` and compares the caller's team with the value carried by the request. No copy of it is written here, and no parameter row is read (DP-01, DP-06 not applied).
- The roster of review-field IDs that the masking pack must cover is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0988; ASM-1740); the pack is loaded by the load path stories with the masking rows, and this story marks whatever field IDs a request names.
- No timeout constant and no role code in code: the 2 s is the platform standard of RWB-PLT-E1037-CON's client, and the cache lives for the versions in force (BR9).
- The database login is the rwb-access login (DP-02): Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0988; ASM-1736).

**Build steps**

1. `PermissionResolver` and `ScopeRule` over `permission`, `role` and the reference list, with the matrix version named in the answer; tests for AC3 and AC5, and a test that a new scope value is accepted as data.
2. `ReviewTeamRule` with the review team and the scope ALL alternative; tests for AC2 with the review team, with scope ALL and with another team.
3. The resolve branch of BR1: Documents U required for resolve, field correction and completion; tests for AC4 with RW-TEAMMGR and with RW-LITOFF.
4. `FieldMarkerService` with the covering-row lookup and the default; tests for AC1 and AC6.
5. `AccessRecordWriter` with the `AC-READ` and `AC-DENY` entries written before the answer, and the forced failure of X5; tests for AC1, AC7 and TC-E1-054-19.
6. `PolicyCache` and `PolicyChangeListener` with the publish and the drop; test AC8 against the PM-2026.13 and MASK-SIT-02 fixture.
7. The migration of the two indexes, and a timing test that one answer stays inside the 2 s budget on a policy pack of the loaded size, with a contract-fake run of the whole capability against RWB-P5-E1054-CON and the decision-record fake.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.p4.doc-review-authority`, read from the platform feature-flag library under the R-PREC default ruling. Off: the review-team branch of BR2 is not applied, so an unattached item is admitted only by scope ALL and by case scope, while the right check, the masking profile and the access log are unchanged — an item that no case covers stays out of every team's queue, and nothing else in the service changes. The switch needs no schema rollback and blocks no read that the policy allows.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass; a review officer's read of an item is granted with the scope it used and markers on every field ID; an unattached item is admitted by the review team and by scope ALL and refused to another team; a stored document follows its case; a team manager holding Documents R is refused on resolve with no item fact; an item outside the scope is answered 404 with no fact; a field with no masking row comes back masked; a refusal leaves an `AC-DENY` entry with no item and no case; a failed record answers 503 and shows nothing; and an approved matrix or masking version changes the answer with no deployment.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Where it is produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | The token carries no Recovery role, or no second factor | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. | The access check before this story's answer (X4, X7) |
| MSG-P4-002 | No role of the caller holds the right in the capability area, including a caller holding Documents R only who asks for U | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | This story, on the refusal of BR1 |
| MSG-P4-003 | The item or the document is outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. | This story, on the refusal of BR3 |
| MSG-P4-006 | Two roles of the caller conflict | {role} may not be held together with {role}. | The access check, from this service's `role_conflict` rows (X6) |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | This story, on every answer (X5) |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The scope list the answer needs is not available | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. | This story, on a reference-list failure (X8) |

For MSG-P4-002 the {action} value is the action the caller attempted, for example "resolve the item" or "correct the field"; for MSG-P4-003 no item fact, no candidate and no case number is echoed, because the message must not confirm that an item or a document exists. Every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId`, the text with its placeholders filled and the instance of the request; the Thai text follows DL10, and MSG-P4-003 keeps its wording even where the object is a review item rather than a case, so the screen and the audit read one message.

##### 15. Screens and states

This story builds no screen. SCR-31 Document review queue, its file and OCR text viewer, the type chooser with candidates, the case chooser, the fields with Confirm and Correct, the Attach and Discard actions and the reviewed and empty states are RWB-P5-E1054-APP/CON through the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19 (RWB-PLT-N001-CON). The route, the page and the copy of the "not in your scope" page are P5's; the refusal text it shows is the one this story produces.

What this story decides for SCR-31 is what each state may show:

| Screen | State | What the answer decides |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-31 Document review queue | Loading | The skeleton rows load with no item fact; the first answer arrives inside the 2 s budget and names the scope and the versions it used |
| SCR-31 Document review queue | List | Only the items and documents this story grants are rendered; a row's reason, candidates and age come from P5, and a field the answer marks masked is rendered masked even where the OCR text shows the value |
| SCR-31 Document review queue | Reviewed | After a resolve the item leaves the list; the resolve itself was granted by the U answer and performed by P5, and the read that followed it writes its own `AC-READ` entry |
| SCR-31 Document review queue | Empty (common state) | An empty list may mean no item in the team's queue or no grant for the caller; the screen shows the same empty state, and one `AC-DENY` entry exists for every refusal that produced it |

A screen that renders a field clear because a client cached it is a defect of the screen, not of the answer: the answer always names the masking version it used, and a field is clear only where a row of that version says so. A screen that renders OCR text on the strength of a read grant is P5's defect and this story's control: the grant names the field IDs, never the text.
