| DF-DOC-008 | document | review_status | Read, through the P5 contract, never stored |
| DF-DOC-081, DF-DOC-084 | document_intake | review_outcome, discard_reason | Read, through the P5 contract, never stored |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary. Nothing of the review item is copied into `rwb_decision` beyond the identifiers and the codes that the record carries, and the field names inside `actions` and `outcome` are a convention of the contract, not columns (GAP-2456; ASM-4080). The ledger holds no OCR text, no document body and no personal datum.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The Ownership Map gives P7 the two decision-log reads under `/api/recovery/decision/v1` and no append operation; those reads belong to the audit query story RWB-P7-E2005-APP, and this story declares nothing on them. The write path of the ledger is the consumer of section 12.4 and the service-local `DecisionLogStore.append` of RWB-P7-E1008-APP. A REST append is absent from the Ownership Map and is therefore not invented here (DP-01, DP-13).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Service | Used for | Timeout |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}` | rwb-document (P5) | The review item: it exists, its review reason, its review outcome and its version, checked against the record before the append | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}` | rwb-document (P5) | The `review_status` of the stored document the record names, checked against the `actions` of the record | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | rwb-case (P3) | LOV-DECISION and the outcome list in force, referred to and never copied into code | One hop, 2 s (DP-07) |

The first two rows are the review contract of RWB-P5-E1054-CON, the recorded contract dependency. The third is the reference-data contract of DP-07 (RWB-P3-E1043-CON through RWB-PLT-E1043-CON) and is carried in the pattern table of section 13 rather than in the metadata row. No other service is called at run time.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The service topic `rwb.decision.events.v1` with event names `rwb.decision.<Event>.v1` (DP-14) carries `ApprovalRequested`, `ApprovalDecided` and `RulePackageInForce` — EV-08, EV-09 and EV-30 — and every one of them belongs to the approval and rule-registry stories of this service. An append seals an entry and publishes nothing; the sealed-entry announcement on `rwb.decision-record.v1` is the store story's (RWB-P7-E1008-APP).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Handler |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` (shared topic of DP-03), with its retry topic and `.dlt` | P7 ledger library of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON; published here by `rwb-document` (the DOCATT and review-completion records) | `DecisionRecordIngestListener`: validate, dedupe on `ce_id` and `idempotencyKey`, `ReviewRecordValidator`, `DecisionChainAppender` |

The envelope is CloudEvents 1.0 in binary mode with `ce_specversion` 1.0, `ce_type`, `ce_source`, `ce_subject` (the case ID where there is one, the entry id where there is not), `ce_id`, `ce_time` and the trace header, keyed by the case or the entry id. The platform library writes the same type as `rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1` in one of its baseline documents; the run convention here is the shared-topic spelling above, and the difference between the two documents is recorded as a conflict of the platform contracts, not of this story.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The ingest is event driven and has no workflow, no activity and no timer; the append is the store's own transaction, so a redelivery and a replay are absorbed by the inbox and the chain rather than by a retry loop in workflow code.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. JOB-13 of the legacy design is continuous Kafka ingest in the target and JOB-14 at 02:00 is the chain check of RWB-P7-E1008-APP; JOB-20 belongs to that story as well. This story adds no Temporal Schedule and moves no clock.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Schema | Owner (ownership map) | This story |
|---|---|---|---|
| decision_log_entry | rwb_decision | P7 | Appends the review entry with its chain link, its codes, its actor and its dedupe key |
| processed_event | PLT library, created in `rwb_decision` | PLT | The inbox of the consumer: one row per `ce_id` |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_decision` | PLT | The stored `idempotencyKey` of the record and its repeat count |
| outbox_event | PLT library, created in `rwb_decision` | PLT | Not written here; named because the table exists in the schema |

`approval` is P7's but belongs to RWB-P7-E2013-APP; `rule_package`, `rule_package_version`, `rule_row` and `rule_test_case` are P7's but belong to RWB-P7-E1073-CON and its app story. The document hub's `document`, `document_field`, `document_intake`, `document_text`, `document_type` and `document_hub_parameter` are P5's in `rwb_document` and are never read; the reference rows are P3's in `rwb_case` and are reached over the contract only. No statement in this story names a table in another schema.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-document WireMock | The P5 review contract of RWB-P5-E1054-CON | `GET /intake-items/{intakeItemId}` with an item in each review outcome and a 404 MSG-P4-003; `GET /documents/{documentId}` with `review_status` PENDING, CONFIRMED and CORRECTED, a 404 and a 2 s timeout |
| rwb-case reference-data fake | The lists row of DP-07 | LOV-DECISION with DOCATT and without D99; the outcome list with ATTACHED, DISCARDED, CONFIRMED and CORRECTED |
| DecisionRecorded topic fixture | The shared topic of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON | One valid DOCATT envelope; one repeated `ce_id`; one envelope with no `inputsRef`; one with an unknown code; one whose final call disagrees with the item; one with no case |
| Chain fixture | The chain rule of BR5 | The genesis hash of 64 zeros; a second entry linked to the first; the recomputed digests; a refused update and a refused delete |
| Store fake | `DecisionLogStore.append` of RWB-P7-E1008-APP | An append that answers the entry reference; an append refused because the store is unavailable, raising `DecisionLogUnavailableException` with MSG-P7-003 |
| Outbox and inbox fake | `OutboxWriter` and `ProcessedEventStore` of RWB-PLT-TE006-CON | The row present after a commit and absent after a rollback; the repeat count of a duplicated `ce_id` |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 3 consumed | The review item and the document read on RWB-P5-E1054-CON and the two lists on DP-07; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 1 consumed, 0 published | `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` with the retry topic and `.dlt` |
| Temporal | None | No workflow, no activity and no Schedule |
| File | None | No file is read or written; the document body never reaches this service |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision`, module `reviewrecord`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision.reviewrecord`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_decision`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency: RWB-P5-E1054-CON) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The dependency-added column records the platform contract stories this story builds on; they arrive as platform CON work, so Depends on (build) stays None and the story is ready on Day 1. DP-19 adds nothing at run time here because this story serves no screen: the review queue screen of legacy SCR-31 is P5's and the decision log screen SCR-38 is RWB-P7-E2005-APP's.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| DecisionRecordIngestListener | Consumer | Reads `rwb.decision-record.v1`, validates the envelope, dedupes in `processed_event`, drives the validator and the appender, and routes the refusals |
| EnvelopeValidator | Service | The CloudEvents attributes, the required record fields and the decision code against LOV-DECISION |
| ReviewRecordValidator | Service | Reads the review item and the document through the P5 contract and compares the outcome and the review status with the record |
| DecisionChainAppender | Service | Takes the next `chain_seq`, computes `prev_hash` and `entry_hash`, appends the entry and writes the inbox row in one transaction |
| ReferenceDataClient | Client | LOV-DECISION and the outcome list in force (DP-07) |
| ExceptionRouter | Service | Writes the exception-queue row with its reason and owner, raises incident `LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED`, and routes to the retry topic or `.dlt` |

**Database and migrations**

- Migration `V1054_1__review_decisions.sql`, on the per-service Flyway sequence after the V0001 baseline (DP-15), adds no table and no column: it adds `ix_declog_inputs ON decision_log_entry (inputs_ref)` for the review correlation and `ix_declog_decision_time ON decision_log_entry (decision_code, decided_at)` for the decision filter of the audit reads. The chain columns and the append-only grant are RWB-P7-E1008-APP's and are not redefined.
- No review column is added: the review facts sit in `actions` and `outcome`, whose key names are a contract convention (GAP-2456; ASM-4080).

**Configuration.** The consumer group `rwb-decision-ledger`, the maximum of four delivery attempts, the retry topic and the `.dlt` topic of the naming library (DP-14), the exception-queue owner `RW-PLATADM`, the incident name `LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED`, the genesis hash of 64 zeros and the 5-minute collection target of Architecture v5 slide 28. Everything but the target, the owner and the incident name is the platform standard of DP-09 and the store's own configuration.

**Build steps**

1. Write the migration and the two indexes; assert that no review column exists and that the append-only grant is in force.
2. Build `EnvelopeValidator` and `ReferenceDataClient` over the reference-data fake and the topic fixture; tests for AC5.
3. Build `DecisionRecordIngestListener` with the inbox dedupe and the repeat count; tests for AC2 and AC9.
4. Build `ReviewRecordValidator` over the P5 fake: item found, item absent, outcome match, outcome mismatch, document status match, and the 2 s timeout; tests for AC1, AC3, AC4, AC6 and AC8.
5. Build `DecisionChainAppender` with the genesis hash, the link to the entry before, the correction through `corrects_entry_id` and the store refusal; tests for AC1, AC3, AC7 and the store-unavailable path.
6. Build `ExceptionRouter`: the reason, the owner, the incident and the `.dlt` route, and the replay path from `.dlt` and from the exception queue; tests for AC4, AC6 and AC8.
7. Run the full ingest against the topic fixture with the P5 fake in place, so the story builds before the document hub publishes anything.

**Feature switch.** None is added. Skipping a decision record breaks NFR-033, NFR-034 and NFR-035, so the ingest has no off state; the store's own flag `rwb.decision.log-store` of RWB-P7-E1008-APP pauses collection and is not this story's.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, every review outcome of the fixture has exactly one chained entry, a repeated delivery adds no entry and no chain position, no entry exists for an item that does not exist or an outcome the item does not carry, the ledger holds no field value and no OCR text, and the contract tests of RWB-P5-E1054-CON stay green.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-009 | A record is refused at validation: a field missing, a decision code outside LOV-DECISION, or an item or an outcome that does not answer | The record cannot be accepted: {field}. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The ledger store is unavailable at the append | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The review item or the document does not answer inside the budget, or answers 503 | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The review item the record names is not returned by the P5 contract | This case is not in your scope. |

The checks of section 4 raise these four; the refusals of X2, X3 and X6 to X9 also carry a reason value of the exception queue — "review item not found", "outcome mismatch", "no answer in the budget" and "store unavailable" — which is data of the platform standard and not a message ID. MSG-P7-003, MSG-P7-009 and MSG-P4-003 keep the wording of the P7 module of the source documents and the legacy story; MSG-GEN-006 is the shared platform message. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

This story serves no screen of its own. The review queue screen SCR-31 and its Loading, list, reviewed and empty states are RWB-P5-E1054-APP's, reached through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19); the decision log screen SCR-38 is RWB-P7-E2005-APP's. What this story adds is what those screens can then show.

| Screen | State | What the user sees and does |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-31 Document review queue | Reviewed | The item has left the queue and its review decision has one chained entry, so the case record can point at it |
| SCR-38 Decision log query | List | The review entries appear with their decision code, actor, decided time and `chainVerified` on each row, answered by RWB-P7-E2005-APP from this service's ledger |
| SCR-38 Decision log query | Chain warning | An entry that does not verify is returned flagged and one incident is raised per entry; nothing is hidden and nothing is corrected |
| Operator console | Exception queue | The refused or dead-lettered envelope with its reason and owner RW-PLATADM, and the replay action once the cause is cleared |

No layout, no field-level masking and no screen text is fixed here; the entries carry identifiers and codes only, so no screen of this story shows a field value, an OCR page or a personal datum.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the decision codes, the outcome values and the reasons are reference rows read through DP-07, and the retry count, the exception owner and the incident name are the platform standard of DP-09.
- No field value, no OCR text, no document body and no personal datum in `rwb_decision`, in the topic or in the logs. The entry carries identifiers, codes, an actor reference and a timestamp; test data uses synthetic items, documents, cases and users only.
- No read of another service's table (DP-01): the review item and the document come through the P5 contract, the lists through the reference-data contract, and no foreign schema appears in a statement.
- One hop and a 2 s timeout on every consumed call, with the fake in place from Day 1, so a P5 outage sends the envelope to the retry and `.dlt` path instead of holding a topic partition (DP-11).
- The ledger is append only: no update, no delete, no REST write path and no writer other than the consumer; a correction is a new entry that names the entry it corrects (DP-01, DP-03).
- Every append commits with its inbox row in one transaction, so a redelivery and a replay add no entry and consume no chain position (DP-09).
- The record is never written on behalf of another service: the acting service writes its own record in its own transaction, and this service only collects it (BR7; DP-03).
- Nothing is removed silently: a refused or dead-lettered record is kept with its reason and its owner until it is replayed, and a discarded review item keeps its reason in the document hub and in its entry (REQ-DCM-019).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: integration slice of RWB-E1-054 for RWB-ITG-W1. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **QA integration engineer**, I want **the end-to-end proof of the RWB-E1-054 review queue across P5 rwb-document (the queue, intake items, the field patch, the review completion and the document read), P3 rwb-case (the case status behind the closed case), P4 rwb-access (the session scope and the role rights) and P7 rwb-decision (the DOCATT ledger entry collected within five minutes)**, so that **no low-confidence or unmatched document reaches a case without a person checking it, and every correction is kept as a labeled example, proved on the real wave 1 services before wave 1 exits**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story runs the review queue inside the document hub of the monolith. One screen, SCR-31, lists every intake item the pipeline could not type, read or match and every stored document with a field below its threshold; one officer keeps or changes the type, chooses the case, confirms or corrects each marked field, then attaches the item or discards it with a reason. A stored document with a field in review is confirmed or corrected on the same screen and completed with the review operation. Each resolution leaves a labeled example behind for the model evaluations.

In the 19-service target the queue, the items, the field patch and the review completion are P5 rwb-document behaviour inside its own schema and its own service (DP-01). The case is read through the P3 rwb-case case contract instead of the in-process `CaseDirectory` (DP-11), and the officer's team and rights are read through the P4 rwb-access session contract instead of the shared ACE access check (DP-08 dependency on the access owner). The document type list in force and the review reasons are reference data read through the P3 reference-data contract (DP-07), and the attach writes its `DOCATT` record locally in rwb_document with the change in one transaction, then P7 rwb-decision collects it into the central ledger within five minutes (DP-03; Architecture v5 slide 28). The document events travel on `rwb.document.events.v1` through the outbox and inbox library with CloudEvents (DP-09). Every path moves to the per-service base of DP-13, and the screen is reached through gateway-bff (DP-19) but is not built or tested here.

This ITG story owns no legacy acceptance criterion. Legacy AC1 to AC17 sit at component level with RWB-P5-E1054-APP, which is why the `acs` list of the work package is empty for this slice; the sixteen scenarios of section 7 are the integration proof of the same legacy behaviour across the four owners, and every business value in them is a legacy value. The suite provides no REST operation, publishes no event and owns no table; it consumes the ten operations of section 12.2 and the three events of section 12.4 and nothing else.

Two of the five integration dependencies exist only because the target separates concerns the monolith held in one call: RWB-P3-E1035-APP carries the case status that decides the closed case of AC8, and RWB-P4-E1054-APP carries the right and the scope that decide the refusals of AC11 and AC15. Without them the closed case and the out-of-scope refusals would be proved against a fixture and not against the services that own the facts.

The resolve call carries the item version returned by the read, and the labeled example is read through the resolved item and its fields on the P5 review contract (ASM-0487; ASM-0490); neither value is invented by the suite.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P5-E1054-APP is done: the review queue, the intake item reads and content, the resolve operation, the field patch, the review completion and the document read are in SIT on P5 rwb-document.
- RWB-P3-E1054-APP is done: the case read of the suite returns the case, its status and its owner through GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}.
- RWB-P3-E1035-APP is done: the case status returned by the P3 case contract is the status the closed-case rule reads.
- RWB-P4-E1054-APP is done: the session contract returns the officer's role, team and scope, and the role-rights check of Documents R and Documents U is enforced on the P5 operations.
- RWB-P7-E1054-APP is done: the `DOCATT` records written locally in rwb_document are collected into the central ledger of P7 rwb-decision within five minutes and are readable through the decision-log operation.
- The published contracts of P5, P3, P4 and P7 are deployed in SIT under their own per-service bases behind gateway-bff.
- The harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG is available with its synthetic cases RW-2026-000201, RW-2026-000202, RW-2026-000203 and RW-2026-000150, its synthetic users, teams LIT-BKK and HP-NE and its synthetic files.
- DOCTYPE-2026.11 is in force and the classify_threshold of every type is 0.8000, loaded as reference data and read through the P3 reference-data contract.
- REVIEW_TEAM_UNATTACHED is "LIT-BKK" for the test, REVIEW_DATE_MIN is 2000-01-01, REVIEW_DATE_MAX is 2100-12-31 and REVIEW_PAGE_SIZE is 50, loaded as data rows of the document hub.
- The synthetic users, roles and scopes of section 10 are loaded: the litigation officer with RW-LITOFF in team LIT-BKK, a case owner with RW-CASEOWN, a team manager with RW-TEAMMGR holding Documents R only, and a center of excellence analyst with RW-COE holding Documents R.
- The feature flag `rwb.dochub.review` is on.
- No production data is used and no production connection is opened, and the release date 30 November 2026 is tentative; a date is not a precondition of this story.
- The story has no build dependency, so it is ready on Day 1 and waits only on its five integration dependencies.

##### 4. Flow

1. QA integration engineer: seeds the synthetic cases, users, teams and files of the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG; no production data is used. Case RW-2026-000201 is open and owned by the case owner, RW-2026-000202 and RW-2026-000203 are open, and RW-2026-000150 is closed.
2. Harness: signs in as the synthetic litigation officer of section 10 through gateway-bff, holds the RW-LITOFF role with team LIT-BKK and reads the session through GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session.
3. Harness: waits on `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` and `rwb.document.DocumentFieldsExtracted.v1` before it asserts any item or document, and records the elapsed time of each wait.
4. Harness: reads the queue through GET /api/recovery/document/v1/review-items and asserts, for each row, the kind, the item or document ID, the case number, the review reason, the predicted type, the two candidates, the confidence, the received time and the version; it asserts the order and the scope against the session of step 2.
5. Harness: opens one item through GET /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId} and its file and OCR text pages through GET /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/content, and asserts the masked fields, the fields in REVIEW and the version.
6. Harness: resolves the items through POST /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/resolve with action SET_TYPE, ATTACH or DISCARD at the version read in the previous step, and asserts the stored document through GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId} and its case status through GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}.
7. Harness: confirms and corrects a stored document's fields through PATCH /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/fields/{fieldId} and completes the review through POST /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/review, then repeats the same patch to prove it changes nothing.
8. Harness: reads the `DOCATT` entries through GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId={caseId}, asserts one entry per attach with the confirmed type and the approver, and measures the collection time against the five-minute target.
9. Harness: runs the refusals and the conflicts — the empty correction, the type not in force, the date outside the allowed range, the field still in review, the closed case, the stale version, the duplicate file, the item and document outside the scope, the discard without a reason and the role holding Documents R only.
10. Harness: proves the failed local record with the agreed test-only fault switch on the P5 local-record write, restores the switch and the flag, writes the evidence report and removes the synthetic fixtures.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Correct is chosen with an empty value | 422; nothing saved; the field keeps its value | MSG-GEN-001 | AC4 |
| X2 | The chosen type is not in the type list in force | 422; nothing saved; the item keeps its predicted type | MSG-P5-006 | AC5 |
| X3 | A corrected date is outside the allowed range | 422; nothing saved; the field keeps its extracted value | MSG-GEN-002 | AC6 |
| X4 | Attach or complete with a field still in REVIEW | 422; nothing stored; the item keeps its outcome | MSG-GEN-001 | AC7 |
| X5 | The chosen case is closed, as read through the P3 case contract | 422; nothing stored; the item stays in the queue | MSG-P5-005 | AC8 |
| X6 | Another officer saved the same item first | 409; the officer reloads and resends at the new version | MSG-GEN-004 | AC9 |
| X7 | The same file is already on the chosen case | The item is linked to the existing document; no second document | MSG-P5-024 | AC10 |
| X8 | Discard without a reason | 422; the item stays in the queue | MSG-GEN-001 | AC13 |
| X9 | No item in the officer's queue | The queue answers with an empty page and the empty message | None | AC14 |
| X10 | An item or document outside the officer's scope | 404; nothing is returned | MSG-P4-003 | AC11 |
| X11 | The same confirmation is sent twice | The second call returns the saved field; nothing changes | None | AC3 |
| X12 | The user holds Documents R only and resolves an item | 403; the item stays in the queue | MSG-P4-002 | AC15 |
| X13 | The local DOCATT record cannot be written on attach | Nothing stored; the item unchanged; 503; an incident is raised; no ledger entry | MSG-P7-003 | AC16 |
| X14 | A consumed call exceeds the 2 s timeout or returns a server error | The call is retried once under the suite policy; the evidence report records the call and the response; no assertion is made on unverified data | None | AC1, AC12 |
| X15 | The fixture set does not match the harness expectations, or a service returns no fixture answer | The suite fails as a harness fault and names the element; no service defect is raised | None | AC1, AC14 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | The suite is its own module and reuses the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG; it needs the five APP stories and the published contracts of P5, P3, P4 and P7, not their source code |
| Negotiable | The review team, the date limits, the page size and the type list are data rows or harness properties; the story fixes the assertions and the call set |
| Valuable | The one screen that keeps a wrong type or a wrong hearing date off a case is proved against the real owners of the queue, the case status, the scope and the ledger before wave 1 exits |
| Estimable | One suite module, one fixture pack of synthetic items and documents, one item-version control, one fault switch and one evidence report |
| Small | Sixteen scenarios over four services and one shared ledger topic; no service code and no schema change |
| Testable | Every scenario asserts a contract response, a stored field, a document, an outcome, an event, a message or the ledger; all data is synthetic |

```gherkin
    Then the response is 409 with MSG-GEN-004
    Then one document exists for "IN-0107"

  Scenario: AC10 The same file already on the chosen case (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given document "DOC-0109" on case "RW-2026-000203" holds a file with hash "H109"
    Given intake item "IN-0109" holds the same file
    When the officer attaches "IN-0109" to "RW-2026-000203" through POST /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/resolve with action ATTACH
    Then the system stores no second document and "IN-0109" is linked to "DOC-0109"
    Then the response carries MSG-P5-024 naming "DOC-0109"

  Scenario: AC11 An item or document outside the officer's scope is refused through the P4 scope (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given document "DOC-0111" belongs to a case of team "HP-NE"
    Given the session read of GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session returns team "LIT-BKK" with team scope for the officer
    When the officer calls GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId} for "DOC-0111"
    Then the response is 404 with MSG-P4-003
    Then the same 404 with MSG-P4-003 is returned when the officer reads an intake item whose candidate cases are all of team "HP-NE" through GET /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}

  Scenario: AC12 An unreadable item is discarded with a reason and the file is retained (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given intake item "IN-0110" with review_reason "UNREADABLE_FILE"
    When the officer calls POST /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/resolve with action DISCARD and reason "Blank page from the branch scanner"
    Then "IN-0110" has review_outcome "DISCARDED" with the reason, the officer's user ID and the time
    Then the file of "IN-0110" is still returned by GET /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/content
    Then "IN-0110" leaves the queue and no document is stored

  Scenario: AC13 Discard without a reason is refused (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given intake item "IN-0112" with review_reason "RESCAN"
    When the officer calls POST /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/resolve with action DISCARD and an empty reason
    Then the response is 422 with MSG-GEN-001 naming "Reason"
    Then "IN-0112" stays in the queue

  Scenario: AC14 The queue lists items in scope oldest first and shows the empty state (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given 3 review items for team "LIT-BKK" received on 2 November, 4 November and 3 November
    Given 2 review items of team "HP-NE"
    When the officer reads GET /api/recovery/document/v1/review-items
    Then 3 items show, in the order 2 November, 3 November, 4 November
    Then no item of team "HP-NE" shows
    When no review item is left for team "LIT-BKK"
    Then the page holds no row and the empty message "No documents are waiting for review."

  Scenario: AC15 A role with Documents R only is refused (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a user in team "LIT-BKK" holding role RW-TEAMMGR with Documents R only
    When the user calls POST /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/resolve with action ATTACH
    Then the response is 403 with MSG-P4-002
    Then the item stays in the queue

  Scenario: AC16 A failed local DOCATT record stops the attach (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the local DOCATT record write of P5 rwb-document is switched to fail by the agreed test-only fault switch
    When the officer calls POST /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/resolve with action ATTACH
    Then no document is stored and the item keeps its review_outcome
    Then the response is 503 with MSG-P7-003
    Then an incident is raised
    Then GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId={caseId} returns no DOCATT entry for the item
    And the fault switch is restored
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The queue holds intake items with a review_reason and no review_outcome, and documents with review_status PENDING; both are P5 rwb-document rows read through the P5 contract | RWB-E1-054 BR1; RWB-E1-049, RWB-E1-050, RWB-E1-053, RWB-E1-032; LOV-REVIEW |
| BR2 | An item with no case is shown to the review team named in REVIEW_TEAM_UNATTACHED and to roles with scope All; an item with candidate cases and a document are shown by the case scope, and the scope comes from the P4 rwb-access session | RWB-E1-054 BR2; permission matrix scope; CTL-09; REVIEW_TEAM_UNATTACHED |
| BR3 | Attach and complete are allowed only when no field is in REVIEW, the type is in force and the case is open, the last read through the P3 case status | RWB-E1-054 BR3; LOV-REVIEW; DocumentTypeCatalog; DF-CAS-005 |
| BR4 | review_status becomes CONFIRMED when the type, the case and the values are kept, and CORRECTED when any of them changes | RWB-E1-054 BR4; LOV-REVIEW |
| BR5 | A corrected value keeps the extracted value in extracted_value and the corrector in confirmed_by | RWB-E1-054 BR5; DF-DOC-017; FEAT-DCM-11 |
| BR6 | The attach is stored by P5 rwb-document in one transaction with its local DOCATT record and the file in the write-once container; P7 rwb-decision collects the record into the central ledger within five minutes | RWB-E1-054 BR6; DP-03; ADR-022; Architecture v5 slide 28 |
| BR7 | Each resolved item is a labeled example that holds the predicted type, the confirmed type, the extracted value and the corrected value | RWB-E1-054 BR7; FEAT-AGT-04; FEAT-DCM-11 |
| BR8 | A change saved against an old version is refused with 409, and a repeat of the same confirmation changes nothing | RWB-E1-054 BR8; MSG-GEN-004 |
| BR9 | A discarded item keeps its file in the intake container and records the reason and the person | RWB-E1-054 BR9; REQ-DCM-019 |
| BR10 | Field values are masked unless the role may see them, by the masking policy of P4 rwb-access | RWB-E1-054 BR10; DF-DOC-015; CTL-11; DL26 |
| BR11 | No service reads another service's tables: the suite reads the queue, the items, the documents, the case, the session and the ledger only through the owner's contract, one hop with a 2 s timeout | DP-01; DP-11; ADR-020 (new, D-RCV-60) |

##### 9. State transitions

None for the case status. This story changes no case status and reads it only to prove the closed case of AC8. The transitions below are the ones the suite proves; every one of them is written by its owner, never by the suite.

| Object | From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| document_intake | item with a review_reason and no outcome | Attach | BR3 passes and the local record is written | review_outcome ATTACHED |
| document_intake | item with a review_reason and no outcome | Discard | A reason is given | review_outcome DISCARDED |
| document | review_status PENDING | Review completed | Type, case and values kept | review_status CONFIRMED |
| document | review_status PENDING | Review completed | The type, the case or a value changed | review_status CORRECTED |
| document_field | state REVIEW | Confirm or Correct | The value passes the type and range check | state CONFIRMED or CORRECTED |
| decision_log_entry | no record | Attach | The local write succeeds | One DOCATT record, collected by P7 within five minutes |

A discarded item leaves the queue and keeps its file. A refused call of section 5 leaves every state unchanged.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| QA integration engineer | Runs the suite, seeds the synthetic fixtures, reads the evidence report; no service right of its own |
| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer | Lists, reads, corrects, attaches and discards review items in scope (Documents CRU) |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Lists, reads, corrects and attaches review items of own cases (Documents CRU) |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | Reads the queue for the team (Documents R) and cannot correct, attach or discard |
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Reads the resolved items as labeled examples (Documents R) |
| P5 rwb-document owner | Owns the queue, the intake items, the documents, the fields and the local DOCATT record |
| P3 rwb-case owner | Owns the case, its status and its owner, served by the case contract |
| P4 rwb-access owner | Owns the roles, the team scope, the masking policy and the session contract |
| P7 rwb-decision owner | Owns the central decision ledger and the collection of the DOCATT records |

The synthetic users of the run are the litigation officer of team LIT-BKK, a case owner, a team manager holding Documents R only and a center of excellence analyst. No other role and no person is in scope for this story.

The legacy story writes these fields in one module; in the target they are written by P5 rwb-document inside its own schema, the case status is owned by P3 rwb-case and the ledger entry by P7 rwb-decision, and the suite only reads them through the four contracts (DP-01). Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary. Every row in the suite is synthetic.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The suite provides no REST operation. The names reserved for P2 rwb-integration — /api/recovery/integration/v1, rwb.integration.events.v1, rwb-integration and rwb_integration — are not used, and no rwb_integration table is written.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method and path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|
| GET /api/recovery/document/v1/review-items | P5 rwb-document | Read the queue with the reason, the predicted type, the two candidates, the confidence, the age and the version of each row, oldest first |
| GET /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId} | P5 rwb-document | Read one item with its candidates, candidate cases, masked fields, review_outcome, resolved_by, resolved_at and version |
| GET /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/content | P5 rwb-document | Read the file and the OCR text pages of an item, including a discarded one |
| POST /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/resolve | P5 rwb-document | Set the type, attach the item to a case or discard it with a reason, at the item version |
| PATCH /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/fields/{fieldId} | P5 rwb-document | Confirm or correct one field of a stored document, and repeat the same confirmation |
| POST /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/review | P5 rwb-document | Complete the review of a stored document with action COMPLETE |
| GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId} | P5 rwb-document | Read the document, its type, its fields with state and values, and its review_status |
| GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId} | P3 rwb-case | Read the case, its status and its owner, to prove the closed case of AC8 |
| GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session | P4 rwb-access | Read the officer's role, team, scope and rights, and prove the refusals of AC11 and AC15 |
| GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId={caseId} | P7 rwb-decision | Read the DOCATT entries of the case and measure the five-minute collection |

Every call is one hop from gateway-bff with a 2 s timeout and a retry of GET only (ADR-020, DP-11). The resolve call carries the action, the type, the case, the fields, the reason and the item version returned by the read (ASM-0487).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The suite publishes no event; every event of the chain is published by its owning service through its own outbox.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Producer | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1 | rwb.document.events.v1 | P5 rwb-document | The document is stored; the suite waits for it before it asserts the document, its fields and the DOCATT entry |
| rwb.document.DocumentFieldsExtracted.v1 | rwb.document.events.v1 | P5 rwb-document | The fields of the item or the document were extracted or re-extracted; the suite waits for it before it asserts a field state |
| DecisionRecorded | rwb.decision-record.v1 | P5 rwb-document, with the central ledger in P7 rwb-decision | The DOCATT record is collected into the ledger inside the five-minute target |

The suite consumes no other event and produces none. A duplicate delivery is absorbed by the inbox of the consumer and changes no assertion.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Workflow or activity | Owner | Task queue | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| DocumentIntakeWorkflow | P5 rwb-document | rwb-document | Carries the intake of each item under test and the re-extraction of a changed type; the suite observes its run and asserts nothing about its history |

The suite starts no workflow of its own and reads no workflow history through an owner's schema. It waits on the two document events and observes the workflow through its published interface only.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The review queue has no Schedule in the target: the queue is a read of the P5 rows and the re-extraction of a changed type is part of the intake workflow. The suite waits on no Schedule and moves no clock.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None (DP-01). document, document_field, document_intake, document_text, document_type and document_hub_parameter are P5 tables, recovery_case is a P3 table, role and permission data are P4 tables, and decision_log_entry is written locally by P5 and held centrally by P7. The suite owns no table and never reads another service's schema.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

External controls and synthetic SIT fixtures only; no service contract is faked.

| Element | Kind | Use |
|---|---|---|
| P5 local-record fault switch | Agreed test-only switch in the P5 configuration | Forces the local DOCATT record write to fail for AC16, and is restored at the end of the run |
| P3 closed case | Synthetic SIT row seeded through the P3 case contract | Case RW-2026-000150 with status Closed for AC8; the real P3 contract answers |
| P4 scoped users | Synthetic SIT users and roles seeded through the P4 access contract | The HP-NE scope of AC11 and the RW-TEAMMGR rights of AC15; the real P4 session answers |
| Clock | Harness control | Measures the age column and the five-minute collection target |

No service contract is faked: every call of section 12.2 goes to the real SIT service on its published wave 1 contract, and the queue, the items, the documents, the fields and the ledger are always the real P5 and P7 answers.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Provided by the suite | Consumed by the suite |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 | 10 |
| Kafka | 0 | 3 |
| Temporal | 0 | 1 observed |
| File | 0 | 1 as needed |

The only file read is the item content through the P5 content call; the suite opens no file share and no container of its own, and writes no file except its evidence report.

##### 13. Solution plan

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Suite module for RWB-ITG-W1, reusing harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG | Integration suite | Runs the sixteen scenarios against SIT and holds no service code |
| Fixture pack | Test data | Synthetic intake items, stored documents, cases, teams, users and files with the legacy values of section 7 |
| Item-version control | Harness control | Reads the item version before a resolve and sends a stale and a repeated version for AC9 and AC3, then restores the item |
| Scope and rights control | Harness control | Holds the LIT-BKK session, the HP-NE document and the RW-TEAMMGR rights of AC11 and AC15 |
| Ledger assertion | Assertion | Reads the DOCATT entry of each attach and measures the collection time against the five-minute target of 300 seconds |
| Evidence report | Report | Records per scenario the item and document IDs, the field states and values, the outcome, the DOCATT entry, the events and their times, the statuses and the messages |

Decoupling patterns applied (Template and Rules v1 §R5.5):

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added | Where it sits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | recovery.<table>, "recovery schema" | Owner's schema rwb_<name>; never read another service's tables | none | document, document_field, document_intake, document_text, document_type and document_hub_parameter stay in rwb_document under P5, recovery_case in rwb_case under P3 and the ledger in rwb_decision under P7; the suite asserts through the four contracts only |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic rwb.decision-record.v1 | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON | On RWB-P5-E1054-APP and RWB-P7-E1054-APP; the suite only waits for the collected record and measures the five minutes |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON | On RWB-P5-E1054-APP for the type list in force and the review reasons; the suite sends the codes as data |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON | On RWB-P5-E1054-APP for DocumentStored and DocumentFieldsExtracted and on every owner for DecisionRecorded; the suite consumes them |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) | The ten consumed REST operations of section 12.2, one hop from gateway-bff |
| DP-13 | /api/recovery/v1 | /api/recovery/<short>/v1 | none | Every path sits under /api/recovery/document/v1 for P5, /api/recovery/case/v1 for P3, /api/recovery/access/v1 for P4 and /api/recovery/decision/v1 for P7 |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON | On RWB-P5-E1054-APP for the review outcome columns and the two review indexes; the suite changes no schema |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The suite enters through gateway-bff; SCR-31 and SCR-30 are not built or tested here |

The dependency-added column records the build dependency of the owning story. Those H and C dependencies belong to the owning APP stories, not to this suite. This story's H, C and X lists are exactly those of the metadata table — no H, no C and no X — and its I list is the five integration dependencies RWB-P3-E1035-APP, RWB-P5-E1054-APP, RWB-P4-E1054-APP, RWB-P3-E1054-APP and RWB-P7-E1054-APP. An ITG story waits on no build of its own.

Build steps:

1. Create the suite module next to harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG and wire it to the SIT endpoints of P5, P3, P4 and P7 through gateway-bff.
2. Build the fixture pack: the four synthetic cases, the two teams, the four synthetic users, the intake items IN-0101 to IN-0112, the documents DOC-0103, DOC-0109 and DOC-0111, the file with hash H109 and the OCR text and field values of section 7, all with the legacy values.
3. Implement AC1 and AC14 with the queue read, the row assertions and the order and scope assertions against the session read.
4. Implement AC2 with the attach at the item version, the document read, the DOCATT entry, the five-minute collection and the labeled example through the item read.
5. Implement AC3 and AC17's behaviour in one scenario with the field patch, the review completion and the repeated patch, and assert that confirmed_by and updated_at do not move.
6. Implement AC4 to AC8 with the four refusals of the queue and the document path: the empty correction, the type not in force, the date outside the allowed range, the field still in review and the closed case read through the P3 status.
7. Implement AC9 to AC13 with the item-version control, the duplicate file link, the two scope refusals and the discard with and without a reason, and assert that no document is stored where the story says so.
8. Implement AC15 with the RW-TEAMMGR rights from the P4 session, then AC16 through the agreed test-only fault switch on the P5 local-record write; assert the 503, the unchanged item, the incident and the empty ledger, restore the switch and the flag, and write the evidence report.

Done when: all twenty test cases pass in SIT against the published wave 1 contracts of P5, P3, P4 and P7, the evidence report shows for each scenario the response, the field state, the document, the outcome and the ledger entry that prove it, every DOCATT entry is collected into the ledger inside the five-minute target, and no service code or schema was changed by this story apart from the agreed test-only fault switch.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P5-003 | An item or document is in the review queue | Some fields need checking. The document is in the review queue. |
| MSG-P5-005 | The chosen case is closed | Case {case} is closed. Choose an open case. |
| MSG-P5-006 | The chosen type is not in force | {value} is not a document type in force. Choose a type from the list. |
| MSG-P5-024 | The file is already on the case | This file is already on the case as {document}. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | Empty value, empty reason, or field still in review | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-002 | Date outside the allowed range | {field} must be between {min} and {max}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | Saved against an old version | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-GEN-005 | Field, attach or discard saved | Saved. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Decision log write failed on attach | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Caller lacks Documents U | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | Item or document outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. |

The message IDs and the wording are copied from RWB-E1-054. No new message ID is added by this story. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

The ledger line of the evidence report carries no message ID: {stored} of {expected} attachments of case {caseId} were stored with their DOCATT entry, and the slowest entry was collected into the central ledger of rwb-decision in {seconds} seconds against the five-minute target of 300 seconds.

No screen is built or tested in this story. The suite reaches the services through gateway-bff (DP-19) and reads the same states the screens render.

The four states of SCR-31 and the one state of SCR-30 are the only screens of the legacy story and no screen is added by this story.

Every test uses synthetic data and runs against the real services on the wave 1 contracts. The legacy full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same legacy test case id.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the review team, the date limits, the page size and the type list come from data rows and from the reference-data contract, never from the suite source.
- No personal data in logs, events, evidence or fixtures: the OCR text and the field values are masked by role and never logged, and every case, item, document, file and user of the suite is synthetic.
- No cross-service table read: the queue, the items, the documents, the fields, the case, the session and the ledger are read through the owner's contract, and the suite owns no table.
- One hop and a 2 s timeout on every consumed call, with a retry of GET only (ADR-020, DP-11).
- The type list in force and the closed case are never assumed by the suite: the first comes from the reference data and the second from the P3 case status.
- A discarded item keeps its file; nothing is ever removed silently (REQ-DCM-019).
- The local-record fault switch is test-only, agreed with the service owner, and restored at the end of the run.
- The P3 closed case and the P4 scoped users are synthetic SIT rows seeded through the published P3 and P4 contracts, and no real contract is replaced in the normal path.
- Synthetic data only, loaded by the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG; no production access of any kind from the suite or its configuration.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-055 for rwb-comms (CON). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the proof-of-delivery loop of rwb-comms — `GET /api/recovery/comms/v1/notices/{noticeId}` with its dispatch and proof-of-delivery fields, the internal digest write, the INT-14 and INT-15 file elements (record layout, feed version, business date and batch status), the LOV-DELIVERY and LOV-SENT-TYPE contract elements, the idempotent digest of a repeated proof-of-delivery row, the `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1` and `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1` envelopes, the `outbound_item` reference of `dispatch_file_id`, the four consumed contracts and the four fakes**, so that **the app, infrastructure, deployment and test stories of this legacy key build against a fixed, testable contract on Day 1 and a field named differently in the P1, P3 or P5 contract can never empty a notice panel or a delivery fact at run time without failing a build**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). The capability of RWB-E1-055 reads one notice and one proof of delivery, and it writes two facts that other services act on: the dispatch, which rwb-reporting consumes, and the delivery, which rwb-case turns into a `NOTICE_PERIOD` timer and rwb-litigation and rwb-guarantee read (Architecture v5 slide 42, events 14 and 15). Both are composed from answers that are no longer local: the proof-of-delivery row and the freshness stamp come from rwb-source-data, the letter behind the notice comes from rwb-document, the timer is rwb-case's, and the file item is rwb-integration's. A field renamed on any of those four edges is exactly the failure that no single-service suite sees.

The baseline also fixes the naming the checks require: schema `rwb_comms`, REST base `/api/recovery/comms/v1`, topic `rwb.comms.events.v1`, event names `rwb.comms.<Event>.v1`, task queue `rwb-comms` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.comms`. It records that JOB-10 is the bank Airflow file window plus the dispatch Schedule and workers of this service (Architecture v5 slide 44), so no contract in this story declares a Quartz row, a shared job table or a Control-M job.

This document is the rwb-comms contract slice of legacy RWB-E1-055 and it owns no legacy acceptance criterion; the criteria of the key are owned by RWB-P6-E1055-APP (AC2 to AC8 and AC10 to AC11) and by `RWB-ITG-E1055-ITG` (AC1 and AC9). It restates no business outcome and makes no runtime claim: it fixes shapes, envelopes, list values and fakes.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the topic, event, queue and package names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- The platform error envelope, the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope and the retry and `.dlt` topic convention are the platform baseline (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON); where this document narrows them it does so explicitly.
- RWB-P6-E1055-APP and RWB-P6-E1052-APP define the fields the baseline declares; this document fixes their shape and never their computation.
- RWB-P1-E1066-CON, RWB-P3-E1043-CON, RWB-P3-E1028-CON and RWB-P5-E1054-CON are the consumed contracts of section 12.2. The exact element names behind RWB-P1-E1066-CON and RWB-P5-E1054-CON are not in the source documents (GAP-1097; ASM-2045; GAP-1099; ASM-2047).
- The fixed layouts and the transport of INT-14 and INT-15 are the WIN owner's documents, which are not in the source material (GAP-1100; ASM-2048).
- The operations and their owners are taken from the Ownership Map only; this document never declares another service's operation as provided.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the rwb-comms OpenAPI 3.1 document fragment for `GET /notices/{noticeId}` and the internal digest write, and the AsyncAPI fragment for the two `rwb.comms.events.v1` events.
2. Fix the notice shape: the identity, the two dates of the dispatch, the barcode, the two list values, the callback date, the dispatch file reference, the attempts and the hold reason, with the optionality rule of AC1.
3. Fix the file contract element: the INT-14 record set and its trailer, the feed version, the business date and the batch status the read is gated on, and record that the fixed layout is the WIN owner's (AC2).
4. Fix the delivery list: LOV-DELIVERY and LOV-SENT-TYPE as versioned reference data, with the state that each value drives, and no literal value in the document's examples beyond the ones the sources name (AC3).
5. Fix the idempotent digest of a repeated proof-of-delivery row: the key, the answer and the counter (AC4).
6. Fix the two event envelopes and their key, with the no-personal-data rule (AC5).
7. Fix the `dispatch_file_id` reference to `outbound_item` of rwb-integration, its cardinality and the fact that it is an identifier and not a foreign key (AC6).
8. Fix the four consumed rows with their owner, the 2 s budget and the degraded shape, and the four fakes with documented answers (AC7, AC8).
9. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-P6-E1055-APP, RWB-P6-E1055-INF, RWB-P6-E1055-OPS and RWB-ITG-E1055-ITG.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A response body fails schema validation | The build fails on the schema lint; a deployed service answers 500 with the error envelope | None | AC1 |
| X2 | A field is renamed or removed within major version 1 | The contract test fails; the change needs a new major version | None | AC1 |
| X3 | A list value is written into the document as an enumeration instead of a versioned reference | The list test fails the build | None | AC3 |
| X4 | A contract fake drifts from the document | The drift test fails the build and the merge is blocked | None | AC7 |
| X5 | The consumed row of P1 or P5 names no element the sources fix | The row carries the placeholder, its gap and its assumption, and the fake is derived from the owner's published document | None | AC8 |
| X6 | The WIN fixed layout is not available | The INT-14 element is declared as a shape only, with the gap and the assumption, and no field order is invented | None | AC2 |
| X7 | An event carries a personal field or loses its key | The envelope test fails the build | None | AC5 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the four consumed contracts and the Ownership Map only |
| Negotiable | Field-level detail is settled with the consumers; the two events, the two list values and the four consumed rows are fixed by the target architecture |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app, infrastructure, deployment and test stories on Day 1 and every consumer of the two dispatch facts |
| Estimable | Two documents, eight contract tests, four consumed rows and four fakes |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion tests the artefact, not a business outcome |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Contract baseline of the proof-of-delivery loop of rwb-comms

  Background:
    Given the service naming rule of the platform library is in force
    Given the base path of rwb-comms is /api/recovery/comms/v1 and its topic is rwb.comms.events.v1

  Scenario: AC1 The notice read declares the dispatch and proof-of-delivery fields (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the OpenAPI 3.1 fragment of GET /notices/{noticeId} is published with this change
    When it is validated against the OpenAPI 3.1 schema
    Then it validates with no error and is owned by rwb-comms on base /api/recovery/comms/v1
    Then the Notice resource carries noticeId, caseId, noticeType, state, sentDate, barcode, sentType, callbackDate, deliveryStatus, dispatchFileId, dispatchAttempts, holdReason and templateVersion
    Then sentDate, barcode, sentType, callbackDate and deliveryStatus are optional, so a notice that is not yet dispatched is a valid answer
    Then the operation names its Litigation R right, its 2 s budget and its error responses 401, 403, 404 and 503, and takes no Idempotency-Key
    Then the internal digest write POST /internal/pod-digests declares the Idempotency-Key header as required and the service identity as its only caller
    Then no answer field carries a name, an address, an identity number or a contact value

  Scenario: AC2 The INT-14 file element fixes the record set, the feed version, the business date and the batch status (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the file element of the document
    When it is reviewed against the legacy job description and the ACE batch record
    Then the INT-14 element names one record per notice with the contract number of the case's primary account, the addressee, the address, the notice type, the template version and the document reference, and a trailer with the record count
    Then it names the business date, the file ID, the feed version and the attempt number of the file
    Then it names the INT-15 side as barcode, sent date, callback date, delivery status and sent type, read only when the batch status of source WIN is COMPLETE for the business date
    Then the fixed field order, the lengths, the delimiters, the encoding and the transport are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1100; ASM-2048)
    Then the document states that the layout is the WIN owner's and that a change of layout is a new file version, never an edit in place

  Scenario: AC3 LOV-DELIVERY and LOV-SENT-TYPE are the only delivery list elements (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the list element of the document
    When it is compared with the TSD P6 list of values and the reference-data contract
    Then LOV-DELIVERY is DELIVERED, REFUSED, UNDELIVERABLE and PENDING, and no other value is valid on deliveryStatus
    Then LOV-SENT-TYPE is BEFORE_NPL and NPL, and no other value is valid on sentType
    Then both lists are read with their version through the rwb-case reference-data contract and are never enumerated in a schema
    Then the document states which notice state each delivery value leads to, and that the queue transfer on a refusal is RWB-E2-021 and not this service
    Then the hold reason list is carried as a reference element with TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN as its only named value (GAP-1105; ASM-2053)

  Scenario: AC4 The digest of a repeated proof-of-delivery row is idempotent (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the internal digest element of the document
    When the same business date, feed version and digest are posted twice with the same Idempotency-Key
    Then the second call returns the first answer with status 200 and writes no second row
    Then the document states the digest key as the business date with the feed version and the digest of the batch
    Then the document states that a second delivery for the same barcode and callback date changes no notice, writes no second NoticeDelivered and is counted under R-UNI-40
    Then the document names the counter and the collection that holds it, without a personal field

  Scenario: AC5 The two event envelopes carry IDs and facts only (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the AsyncAPI fragment of rwb.comms.events.v1
    When the two events are validated against the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope and the registry
    Then rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1 declares noticeId, caseId, sentDate, barcode and sentType, keyed by caseId
    Then rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1 declares noticeId, caseId, deliveredDate, callbackDate and deliveryStatus, keyed by caseId
    Then neither payload declares a name, an address, an identity number or a contact value
    Then each has its retry topic and its .dlt topic and is versioned with BACKWARD compatibility
    Then the document states that each is written to the outbox in the same transaction as the notice change

  Scenario: AC6 dispatch_file_id is a reference to outbound_item of rwb-integration (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the data element of the document
    When the dispatch file reference is reviewed
    Then dispatchFileId is declared as an identifier of the outbound item of rwb-integration, many to 0 or 1 from the notice
    Then the document states that it is stored as an identifier and never as a foreign key across schemas, and that the file itself is read through the owner's contract
    Then dispatchAttempts is declared as an integer with a default of 0 and is incremented once per file the notice enters
    Then the document names no path of rwb-integration as provided by this service

  Scenario: AC7 The four consumed rows carry their owner, the budget and the degraded shape (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the consumed element of the document
    When it is compared with the Ownership Map
    Then the DP07 records read and the freshness read name P1 rwb-source-data and the ledger write names P1 rwb-source-data
    Then the stored letter read names P5 rwb-document, the timer read names P3 rwb-case and the list read names P3 rwb-case
    Then every row states one hop, the 2 s timeout, one GET retry with jitter and a breaker per downstream
    Then the document states the degraded shape of a failed pod read, a failed freshness read and a failed document read, and that a failed pod read never sets a notice Delivered
    Then the pod and document elements carry their gap and assumption where no source names them (GAP-1097; GAP-1099)

  Scenario: AC8 The four fakes answer the document and the drift test fails the build (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the fakes of section 12.8
    When each one is compared with the shapes of 12.1 to 12.4
    Then the rwb-source-data fake answers 25 of 25 records with 0 refused, the 30-row batch with one held row, the repeat row, the three batch states and the stale marker
    Then the rwb-document fake answers one stored letter per notice, the rwb-case fake answers a running NOTICE_PERIOD timer started on 2026-11-28, and the rwb-integration fake answers one outbound item and the acknowledgment record
    Then every fake value is the legacy value of RWB-E1-055 and no business value is added
    Then a fake that drifts from the document fails the build
```

These eight criteria are new for the contract baseline and test the artefact only. The legacy criteria of RWB-E1-055 are owned by RWB-P6-E1055-APP (AC2 to AC8 and AC10 to AC11) and by RWB-ITG-E1055-ITG (AC1 and AC9), and none of them is restated here.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One REST base per service: `/api/recovery/comms/v1`; the document never declares another service's path as provided | DP-13; Architecture v5 slide 41 notes |
| BR2 | Event names are `rwb.<short>.<Event>.v1` on `rwb.<short>.events.v1`, with retry and `.dlt` topics | DP-14; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR3 | Every event carries the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, is keyed by caseId and carries no personal data | Architecture v5 slides 42 and 43 notes; DP-09 |
| BR4 | A read declares no Idempotency-Key; a POST declares it, stores its response and returns the first answer on a repeat | Architecture v5 slide 11; DP-09 |
| BR5 | Error responses use one envelope and one message ID per condition, and the business message texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story | Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR6 | A schema change is additive within a major version; a breaking change is a new major version | Architecture v5 slide 42 notes (BACKWARD compatibility) |
| BR7 | The document lists only operations owned by rwb-comms; a consumed operation is described as consumed, never as provided | Ownership Map v1 |
| BR8 | The list values are versioned reference data, read through the rwb-case contract, and are never an enumeration in a schema or a constant in code | DP-07; TSD P6 T3.2 |
| BR9 | The proof of delivery is read by rwb-source-data, not by this service: the contract declares a consumed answer and no `v_ace_*` view | DP-05; legacy BR4 |
| BR10 | The notice period is started by rwb-case from the delivered date on the event, and no contract element of this story declares a timer | R-LIT-07; DP-09 |
| R-LIT-07 | A notice period starts only from the delivery date, so the event carries the delivered date and the callback date beside it | Temporal and Drools design slide 20 notes; legacy BR2 |
| R-LIT-08 | The proof window is 7 days from dispatch and belongs to RWB-E2-021; this baseline declares no window field | Temporal and Drools design slide 20 notes; RWB-E2-021 |
| R-LIT-09 | An undeliverable result moves the notice to Unserved in RWB-E2-021; this baseline only fixes the list value that carries it | FSD P6 A2.2 AC-ALT-P6-002-02 |
| R-UNI-33 | A downstream system that fails is retried, and the record state does not advance until the retry succeeds | INT-14 error handling |
| R-UNI-34 | A retried call that passes its limit leaves the record in the exception queue with its reason | INT-14 error handling |
| R-UNI-40 | The same event, the same digest and the same proof-of-delivery row produce one effect, and the repeat is counted | legacy BR6; FSD P6 A2.2 AC7 |

##### 9. State transitions

The baseline declares the notice states as contract elements; it writes none of them.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Generated | The file of the business date holds the notice | The notice is in the dispatch-eligible state and has no sent date | Generated, with the file reference and the attempt count |
| Generated | `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1` content | A barcode is present in the acknowledgment | Sent |
| Sent | `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1` content | A callback date is present on the row | Delivered |
| Sent | A delivery value of REFUSED or UNDELIVERABLE | The row carries that value | Unserved; the queue transfer is RWB-E2-021 |
| Generated or Sent | A hold | The holding condition applies | Held, with the hold reason |
| Held | The hold is released | The condition is cleared | The previous state, and the notice is eligible again |

The lifecycle column and the four delivery values are declared here so a consumer never invents a state. The `NOTICE_PERIOD` timer is rwb-case's state: the `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1` envelope carries the delivered date, and rwb-case starts the timer from it. No contract element of this story declares a timer, a case status or a queue.

| Consuming teams (app, infrastructure, deployment, test and the P1, P3 and P5 owners) | Review and sign off the parts they consume |

The rights of the capability itself are the rows of TSD P6 T6.1 — RW-LITOFF Litigation CRUA, RW-LEGAL Litigation RA, RW-CASEOWN Documents CRU and Litigation R, RW-PLATADM Documents R — and they are declared on the operations by name only. DP-08 is not in the patterns of this story: the operation declares its capability area and right, and the enforcement point of the declared right is gateway-bff; where a local guard is required the guard is not specified in the source documents (GAP-1098; ASM-2046). The per-service login name behind the security scheme is not part of this baseline; the document names the scheme "the rwb-comms login (DP-02)".

##### 11. Data

The baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Notice resource | `noticeId`, `caseId`, `noticeType`, `state`, `sentDate`, `barcode`, `sentType`, `callbackDate`, `deliveryStatus`, `dispatchFileId`, `dispatchAttempts`, `holdReason`, `templateVersion`, from DF-LEG-015 to DF-LEG-023, DF-LEG-032 to DF-LEG-034 and DF-REF-047 |
| Dispatch and proof dates | `sentDate` and `callbackDate` are dates in the ISO form on the wire and DDMMYYYY in the WIN file only; the conversion is the app story's |

The field-level types, lengths and required flags of the added properties are settled in the baseline review; this story fixes the names, the optionality rule of AC1 and the list rule of AC3.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-comms (P6); base `/api/recovery/comms/v1`.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/notices/{noticeId}` | The Notice resource of AC1 with the dispatch and proof fields, all optional except the identity, the case, the notice type and the state | Litigation R, scope applied |
| POST | `/internal/pod-digests` | The business date, the feed version, the row count and the digest of the batch; the answer is the digest record; Idempotency-Key required, service identity only | Service identity |

Both answer with the platform error envelope; the read answers 401, 403, 404 and 503, the internal write answers 401, 409, 422 and 503.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Shape the baseline fixes |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/DP07/records` | P1 rwb-source-data (RWB-P1-E1066-CON) | The proof-of-delivery records of a business date, with the fields of DF-ACE-253 to DF-ACE-258; the element names are not in the source documents (GAP-1097) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness` | P1 rwb-source-data (RWB-P1-E1066-CON) | The batch status of source WIN, the feed version and the stale marker |
| POST | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions` | P1 rwb-source-data (DP-18) | The outbound LETTER entry; ids, dates, direction, channel and a summary with no personal field |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}` | P5 rwb-document (RWB-P5-E1054-CON) | The stored letter of a notice; the element is not named in the source documents (GAP-1099) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers` | P3 rwb-case (RWB-P3-E1028-CON) | The `NOTICE_PERIOD` timer, observed only to assert the start date |
| The LOV read of the reference-data contract | P3 rwb-case (RWB-P3-E1043-CON) | LOV-NOTICE, LOV-DELIVERY, LOV-SENT-TYPE and the hold reason reference, by version |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, one GET retry with jitter and a breaker per downstream. The baseline fixes the shapes and the failure mapping only; it makes no runtime claim.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |

The platform H rows of the table are delivered by the platform waves and are not repeated in the metadata H field of this story, which stays empty by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7). DP-05 applies as a prohibition and DP-18 as "the ledger is a consumed operation of rwb-source-data".

**Build steps**

1. Add the Notice resource and the internal digest write; validate the optionality rule of AC1 and the additive rule of BR6 in the pipeline.
2. Write the file element of AC2, with the gap and the assumption where the fixed layout is the WIN owner's.
3. Write the list element of AC3 and the state that each delivery value leads to.
4. Write the digest element of AC4 and the repeat counter.
5. Write the two event envelopes of AC5 and the no-personal-data check.
6. Record the `dispatchFileId` reference and its cardinality (AC6).
7. Record the six consumed rows with their owner, the budget and the degraded shape, with the two gap rows where no source names the element (AC7).
8. Publish the four fakes and the eight contract tests; a drift between a fake and the document fails the build (AC8).
9. Baseline tag and the consumer sign-off note, including the P1, P3, P5 and P2 owners and the wave 1 harness.

**Done when.** The OpenAPI and AsyncAPI fragments validate in the pipeline, the eight contract tests pass, the four fakes answer every consumed path and the drift test is green, and the app, infrastructure, deployment and test stories have accepted the baseline.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the eligible state, the attempt limit, the break days, the stale period, the hold reasons and the retry intervals stay data, reference data or service configuration.
- No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: IDs, codes, dates, a barcode and list values only; no name, address, identity number or contact value.
- The contract names only rwb-comms tables and only operations owned by rwb-comms; the P1, P3 and P5 operations are consumed and faked, never declared as provided (DP-01).
- ACE data is reached only through the owner's contract or the owner's `v_ace_*` views; this document declares no ACE view and no cross-schema join (DP-05).
- One REST base and one topic per service; a document that names another service's base or topic as its own fails the review (DP-13, DP-14).
- Every event is keyed by case ID, carries the CloudEvents envelope and no personal field, and its repeat is deduped through the inbox (DP-09, R-UNI-40).
- No timer, no case status and no queue element is declared: the notice period is started by rwb-case from the event (BR10).
- Every example in the document is synthetic; no production payload is copied into a schema or a fake.
