The seven criteria above are new and test only this deliverable: the two documents on the case, the delivery facts as document fields, the write-once refusal, the read, the event, the idempotent store and the prohibitions that keep the ledger and the timer with their owners. This story owns no legacy acceptance criterion: legacy AC1 to AC11 of RWB-E1-055 are held by the primary slice rwb-comms in RWB-P6-E1055-CON and RWB-P6-E1055-APP, by the timer slice in RWB-P3-E1055-APP and by the ACE data slice in RWB-P1-E1055-APP, and legacy test case TC-E1-055-12 belongs to RWB-P6-E1055-APP. No legacy criterion text is copied into this section.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR2 | A notice period starts only from the delivery date on the proof of delivery; in this slice the delivered date is a document field of the receipt and the timer is rwb-case's (legacy BR2) | CTL-15; R-LIT-07; legacy BR2 |
| BR4 | A `v_ace_pod` row is read only when the ACE batch for source WIN is COMPLETE for its business date, and a row with an unknown reference is held; the check and the read are rwb-comms' in RWB-P6-E1055-APP, the data product freshness is RWB-P1-E1055-APP's, and this slice stores only the receipt that answer names (legacy BR4) | ACE batch record; INT-15 error handling; legacy BR4 |
| BR6 | The same receipt twice produces one effect and the repeat is counted (legacy BR6) | R-UNI-40; legacy BR6 |
| BR7 | A write-once document is never changed or deleted inside its retention period; a change is a new version | NFR-029; FSD P5 A2.1 and AC-ALT-P5-001-01; DT06 |
| BR8 | A document reaching the end of its retention period is disposed of or extended by a recorded decision and is never removed silently, and every document type carries a retention class that sets how long the document is kept | NFR-074; NFR-028; FSD P5 A2.17 |
| BR9 | The write-once flag, the retention class and the field list of a type come from the document type table version in force, never from the caller; no value a business person may change is written in code | BR-P5-004; FSD P5 A2.4.3.1; TSD P5 T3.1 (document_type) |
| BR10 | The document reference the INT-14 dispatch file carries is the document ID of the stored notice PDF; the reference is data read through the rwb-comms contract and is never derived from a case number, a notice number or a file name | Legacy RWB-E1-055 section 4 step 2; DF-LEG-017 |
| BR11 | rwb-document writes only its own schema: no `v_ace_*` view, no `public` table and no other service's table is read, and the case, the notice and the ledger arrive through their owners' contracts | DP-01; DP-05; Architecture v5 slides 20 and 41 |
| BR12 | rwb-document writes no interaction-ledger entry and starts no timer; the ledger belongs to rwb-source-data and the notice-period timer to rwb-case | DP-18; DP-10; Architecture v5 slide 20 |
| BR13 | The receipt carries the delivery facts as document fields so that the case shows what was delivered and when, and a fact the type's field list does not hold is refused rather than stored | FSD P5 A2.9; TSD P5 T3.1 (document_field); legacy section 4 steps 4 to 7 |

Target statements that make these rules hold in `rwb-document`:

- BR7 is executed by `WriteOnceGuard` on every change request and by the blob path being immutable per version, with the container's own WORM policy behind it; the row, the `content_sha256` and the file stay as stored, and the attempt is recorded as the audit event `DOCUMENT_CHANGE_REFUSED` (FSD P5 AC-ALT-P5-001-01, NFR-029).
- BR8 is executed by carrying the retention class on the document row from the type in force and by leaving every expiry action to the monthly retention job of RWB-P5-E1052-APP; this slice stores, it never archives, extends or disposes.
- BR9 is executed by reading `document_type` in the version in force (`valid_from` and `valid_to`) inside the same service, by the three lists arriving through the reference-data contract (DP-07), and by a boundary test that fails the build when a type code, a retention class or a source value appears in Java.
- BR10 is executed by returning the document ID of the stored notice PDF as the document reference, so the dispatch file, the notice and the case screen all name the same document; the reference is a value, not a formula.
- BR11 is executed by the schema and login per service and by the boundary test that fails on any cross-schema read; the notice facts arrive in the contract answer and no `v_ace_*` view is opened by this service (DP-01, DP-05).
- BR12 is executed by the absence of a ledger call and of a Schedule in this story: the `LETTER` entry is written by rwb-source-data from `DocumentStored` or from `NoticeDispatched`, and the `NOTICE_PERIOD` timer by rwb-case from `NoticeDelivered` (DP-18, DP-10).
- BR13 is executed by `DocumentFieldWriter`, which writes one `document_field` row per fact of the type's field list and refuses a fact outside it, so the index of the case is never wider than the type in force.

##### 9. State transitions

No case state machine in this story: the slice changes no case status and starts no timer (TSD P5 T4). It uses the document lifecycle of the store path — COPY_PENDING to STORED, as RWB-P5-E1024-APP defines it and as RWB-P5-E1026-APP reads it — and reads the notice states of rwb-comms as facts:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| (no document row) | the store transaction commits with the outbox row | The type is in force and the caller holds the Documents right | `document.state` = COPY_PENDING, `doc_version` 1 |
| COPY_PENDING | the `copyPending` activity of the workflow kit stores the file and sets `storage_ref` | The container accepts the write and the SHA-256 matches `content_sha256` | STORED |
| COPY_PENDING | the copy fails | The container refuses the write or the storage product does not answer | COPY_PENDING, retried by the next run of the activity |
| STORED, `is_active` = true | a new version is added with `POST /documents/{documentId}/versions` on the latest version | The new file passes the type and signature checks | the earlier row becomes the superseded version with `is_active` = false and `previous_version_id` on the new row, which is COPY_PENDING then STORED; both versions stay readable |
| STORED, `write_once` = true | a content replace or a delete inside the retention period | The retention period has not ended and no legal hold release exists | no transition: refused with MSG-P5-002, the row and the file unchanged |

The notice states Generated, Sent and Delivered are read-only facts of rwb-comms in this slice: this story never writes them, and the `NOTICE_PERIOD` timer that rwb-case starts from `NoticeDelivered` is not a transition of any `rwb_document` row. The end-of-retention states — ARCHIVED, LISTED, HELD and EXCEPTION of LOV-RETENTION-ACTION — belong to the monthly retention job of RWB-P5-E1052-APP, which writes `retention_action`; this slice writes no such row.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| rwb-document service identity (the rwb-document login, DP-02) | Stores the notice PDF and the receipt, writes the field rows, writes the outbox row, serves the reads and refuses a change to a write-once document |
| rwb-comms service identity, through RWB-P6-E1055-CON | Asks for the document evidence of a notice and receives the document reference; reads no `rwb_document` table directly |
| Decision-record library identity | Writes the DOCATT record of the store path as RWB-P5-E1024-APP invokes it; this slice writes no second record and no new decision code (DP-03 is not a pattern of this story) |
| SY-DATALOAD, data load | Runs the receipt load that hands the partner file to this slice; the WIN outbound file itself is rwb-comms' and rwb-integration's (legacy authority table) |
| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer | Reads the notice document, the receipt, its delivery facts and its versions inside the scope (Documents R, Litigation R) |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Reads the documents of the case inside the scope (Documents R) |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Reads the document and its state on SCR-30, including a COPY_PENDING document; reruns nothing, because this slice runs no job or Schedule |
| RW-DATASTEW, data steward | Reads the document index and the receipt facts for a case in scope; writes nothing |
| Nobody | Changes or deletes a write-once document inside its retention period, or writes a notice state, a ledger entry or a timer from this service |

The authorisation decision is taken by rwb-access (DP-08, roles, scope and masking held as data in `rwb_access`) and reaches this slice as the permission decision the service template's guard holds; this story adds no guard of its own and no operation of its own, and the refusal shapes are MSG-P4-002 for a role without the right and MSG-P4-003 for a case outside the scope. TC-E1-055-12, in which RW-PHONECOL is refused the notice dispatch detail, is not a case of this slice: the dispatch detail is rwb-comms' and that test case belongs to RWB-P6-E1055-APP. SY-OCR, the OCR and extraction pipeline, is not used here: the OCR text and the extracted fields of a scanned receipt belong to the intake path of RWB-P5-E1049-APP, and this slice writes the receipt facts it is given.

The two documents of this slice write `document` and `document_field` only, plus their outbox rows. No custody row, no `retention_action` row, no `document_intake` row and no `document_text` row is written here, because custody belongs to the originals path, the retention action to RWB-P5-E1052-APP and the intake, OCR text and extraction to RWB-P5-E1049-APP and its extraction stories. Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary and the TSD P5 T3.1 tables. No `rwb_case` row is copied, no ACE view is read and no personal data enters the event payload, the fields of the event, a log line or a test: the addressee of the notice stays inside the PDF, and the receipt carries a barcode and dates, not a person.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None new. The four operations this slice uses are the ones of the store and read contract on base `/api/recovery/document/v1`, owner rwb-document (P5), built by RWB-P5-E1024-APP. This story adds no path, no query parameter and no response field, and answers behind them:

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents` | Store a notice PDF or a receipt on the case: the document row in COPY_PENDING with its metadata, the field rows, the outbox row, and the upload link of the storage product for the file (API-P5-001) | Documents right C, scope applied; rwb-comms for the notice, the receipt intake for the partner file | `Idempotency-Key` header, plus the unique partial index on case, type and active hash |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}` | Read the metadata, the version list and the extracted fields of a document (API-P5-003) | Documents right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/content` | Download the file of a document; 503 while the state is COPY_PENDING (API-P5-004) | Documents right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| POST | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/versions` | Add a new version to the latest version of a document; the change of a write-once document is a new version and never a replace (API-P5-005) | Documents right U, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header |

The request of the store operation carries the case ID, the document type, the source (`GENERATED` or `PARTNER`), the file reference in the intake container with its SHA-256, and any extracted field the type defines; the answer carries the document ID, the state, the retention class, the write-once flag and the version, and the document ID is the value rwb-comms takes as the document reference of the dispatch file. Errors follow RFC 9457 with `messageId`: 401, 403 (MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003), 404, 409 on a version race, 413, 415, 422 (MSG-P5-006, MSG-P5-016), 503 (MSG-GEN-006, MSG-P7-003). The exact request and response field names of the four operations are those of the store contract; the field name by which rwb-comms names the document reference in its own answer is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1043; ASM-1991).

The rest of the P5 surface — the case document list `GET /cases/{caseId}/documents` (API-P5-002), the checklist read (API-P5-008), the cross-case search (API-P5-009), the review queue and the intake reads (API-P5-010 to API-P5-013), the field review (API-P5-014), the field captures (API-P5-015), the generation and regeneration operations (API-P5-016, API-P5-017) and the custody operation (API-P5-007) — belongs to the other P5 stories; this slice adds none of them and changes the shape of none of them.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Owner | Contract | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| The notice read and the dispatch reference — the operation of RWB-P6-E1055-CON whose field names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1043; ASM-1991) | rwb-comms (P6) | RWB-P6-E1055-CON | Called once per notice, one hop, 2 s timeout, circuit breaker per downstream (DP-11); returns the notice type, the case ID, the generated PDF reference, the sent date, the barcode, the sent type, the callback date, the delivery status and the document reference |

That contract is the only C dependency of this story. The case read and the duplicate check of the store path are RWB-P5-E1024-APP's, and its rwb-case contract (RWB-P3-E1018-CON) remains that story's dependency and not this one's; the rwb-case answer in the Background is the fake of that store path. The interaction-ledger write is not consumed here: rwb-source-data writes it from the event (DP-18).

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Key | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` (event 16) | `rwb.document.events.v1` | P5 | caseId | documentId, caseId, documentType, source, storedAt |

CloudEvents 1.0 envelope in binary mode, JSON Schema registry with BACKWARD compatibility, retry topics and a dead-letter topic (Architecture v5 slides 11 and 42). The event row is written to the outbox in the same transaction as the document row and its field rows, so the event exists exactly when the document exists; the relay publishes it once per committed store. The payload carries no personal data, no field value and no file content: the case, the type and the source are the facts others react to, and a consumer that needs a facet of the notice asks rwb-comms for it. Its consumers are rwb-agent and rwb-case by the catalogue, and the letter ledger entry is written by rwb-source-data from it. The DOCATT decision record on `rwb.decision-record.v1` is published by the store path of RWB-P5-E1024-APP, not by this story: DP-03 is not a pattern of this slice.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. This slice consumes no Kafka event. The document states and facts that change are written through the store path and read through the contract; `DocumentFieldsExtracted` is published by the extraction path and consumed by rwb-case, and `NoticeDispatched` and `NoticeDelivered` are rwb-comms' events consumed by rwb-source-data, rwb-case, rwb-litigation, rwb-guarantee and rwb-reporting, not by this service (Architecture v5 slide 42).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. This story starts no workflow and contributes no activity. The `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` template — OCR, classify, extract — is registered and owned by RWB-P5-E1049-APP, and the `copyPending` activity that sets a stored document from COPY_PENDING to STORED is contributed by RWB-P5-E1024-APP; this slice calls the store path and waits for its answer in the caller's thread. DP-10 applies as a prohibition here: this service's dispatch-evidence module holds no Schedule and no event-started workflow.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The 15-minute document intake (JOB-12) belongs to RWB-P5-E1049-APP, the monthly retention run (JOB-17, monthly on the first Sunday) to RWB-P5-E1052-APP, and the daily WIN outbound file (JOB-10, 16:00) to rwb-comms with the integration adapters (Architecture v5 slide 44). This slice runs on the call of rwb-comms and on the receipt intake, never on a timer of its own.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|
| `document` | P5 (`rwb_document`) | The evidence row: metadata, type, source, storage reference, retention class, write-once flag, version, hash |
| `document_field` | P5 (`rwb_document`) | The delivery facts of the receipt as index rows |
| `document_type` | P5 (`rwb_document`) | Read only: the type row in force with its flag, class and field list; the load is RWB-P5-E1025-APP's |
| `document_custody`, `retention_action`, `document_intake`, `document_text` | P5 (`rwb_document`) | Not written by this story: custody, the retention action and the intake path belong to their own stories |
| outbox, inbox and idempotency library tables | PLT library, created in `rwb_document` | The `DocumentStored` row and the `Idempotency-Key` of the store (DP-09) |

rwb-document reads no table of another service and holds no foreign key across services (DP-01): `recovery_case` is rwb-case's, the notice is rwb-comms' and the ledger is rwb-source-data's, and each reaches this story through its owner's contract or its owner's event. No `v_ace_*` view and no `public` table is read by this service.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 4 provided, 1 consumed | The store, the document read, the content read and the version add on `/api/recovery/document/v1`; the notice read and dispatch reference of RWB-P6-E1055-CON, one hop, 2 s timeout, breaker per downstream |
| Kafka | 1 published, 0 consumed | `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` on `rwb.document.events.v1`, keyed by caseId, written to the outbox in the store transaction |
| Temporal | None | No workflow, no activity and no Schedule in this slice (DP-10 as a prohibition) |
| File | 2 blobs per case | The notice PDF and the receipt in `rwb-docs-legal` at `rwb-docs-legal/{caseId}/{documentId}/v1` through the storage product the store path already depends on; this slice adds no new external dependency |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document`, module `dispatchevidence`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| DispatchEvidenceService | Service | Reads the notice answer of RWB-P6-E1055-CON, stores the notice PDF with source `GENERATED` and the type of the notice, and returns the document ID as the document reference the dispatch file carries |
| ProofOfDeliveryDocumentService | Service | Stores the receipt file of a business date with source `PARTNER` and the type the table in force holds for a proof-of-delivery receipt, and hands the delivery facts to the field writer |
| DocumentFieldWriter | Service | Writes one `document_field` row per delivery fact in the same transaction as the receipt row, checks each fact against the field list of the type in force, and refuses a fact outside it |
| WriteOnceGuard | Service | Refuses a content replace and a delete inside the retention period with MSG-P5-002, leaves the row and the hash unchanged, and writes the audit event `DOCUMENT_CHANGE_REFUSED` with the document ID and the caller |
| DocumentEventPublisher | Service | Writes `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` to the outbox inside the store transaction through the DP-09 library, with the case key and no personal data |

**Database and migrations**

- Writes `document` and `document_field`, and the outbox row, in schema `rwb_document`; reads `document_type` in the same schema. No other schema is read (DP-01).
- No new table and no new column in this slice; the type rows are RWB-P5-E1025-APP's. The migration this slice relies on is the one RWB-P5-E1024-APP contributes to the per-service Flyway sequence — `V1024_1__document_store.sql`, which adds `document.previous_version_id`, `document.content_sha256`, `document_hub_parameter` and the unique partial index `uk_document_case_type_hash` on `(case_id, document_type, content_sha256)` where the row is active — and the type load of RWB-P5-E1025-APP. This slice adds no migration step of its own, so DP-15 is the ordering rule that keeps its two dependencies before the code (DP-15).
- The duplicate rule of AC6 rests on that unique partial index plus the pre-insert read; no separate key is introduced for the business date, because the receipt is a document like any other and its facts are fields.

**Configuration and reference data**

- `rwb.document.dispatch-evidence.notice-source` = `GENERATED` and `rwb.document.dispatch-evidence.receipt-source` = `PARTNER`, both values of LOV-DOC-SOURCE read through the reference-data contract and set as properties per environment.
- `rwb.document.dispatch-evidence.receipt-type` names the type code the type table in force holds for a proof-of-delivery receipt; its value is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1044; ASM-1992), and the code is resolved against `document_type` at start-up, so an unknown code stops the module rather than storing a receipt of no type.
- `rwb.document.dispatch-evidence.notice-type-map` maps a notice type to a document type and holds `DEMAND` to `DEMAND_LETTER`; the mapping between a notice type and a document type is Not specified in the source documents beyond that pair (GAP-1044; ASM-1992).
- `rwb.document.dispatch-evidence.receipt-fields` lists the delivery facts written as document fields, by field name; the names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1045; ASM-1993).
- `rwb.document.dispatch-evidence.write-once-container` = `rwb-docs-legal` and `rwb.document.dispatch-evidence.path-template` = `{container}/{caseId}/{documentId}/v1`; the account and its immutability policy belong to the storage product the store path already depends on.
- The feature switch is `rwb.document.dispatch-evidence`: on in wave 1; off means the slice stores no dispatch evidence and rwb-comms receives the store path's refusal, never a silent success.

**Build steps**

1. `DispatchEvidenceService` over the RWB-P6-E1055-CON fake, with the notice answer, the type resolution and the document reference returned; test AC1 and the not-found and timeout paths of X8 and X4.
2. `ProofOfDeliveryDocumentService` over the receipt answer, with the type from the table in force and source `PARTNER`; test AC2 and the unknown-type path of X2.
3. `DocumentFieldWriter` with one row per delivery fact, the field list check of the type and the refusal of a fact outside it; test AC2 and X3.
4. `WriteOnceGuard` with the content replace and the delete on the store path and on the container, the unchanged hash and the `DOCUMENT_CHANGE_REFUSED` audit event; test AC3 against the write-once container of SIT.
5. `DocumentEventPublisher` inside the store transaction, with the forced-failure test that leaves no row, no field and no event, and the relay-recovery test of X6; test AC5.
6. The reads of AC4 with the permission decision of the guard, the scope check, the 2 s budget through the gateway-bff route and the content read compared against `content_sha256`; test AC4 and the refusals of X9.
7. The duplicate path of AC6 on the same receipt and business date, and the prohibition test of AC7: no ledger call and no timer registration in the module, with the two listener fakes asserting who writes what.
8. The boundary test over the module: no `v_ace_*` view, no `public` table and no foreign schema in any SQL or entity of `dispatchevidence`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-18 | Interaction ledger | Ledger owned by rwb-source-data (default ruling) | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-01 puts both documents in `rwb_document` and removes every cross-module read: the notice arrives through RWB-P6-E1055-CON, the case through the store path, and no `recovery` table name survives.

DP-05 applies as a prohibition: this service opens no `v_ace_*` view and no `public` table. The legacy `v_ace_pod` read belongs to the rwb-comms slice with the data product of RWB-P1-E1055-APP, and the delivery facts reach the receipt inside the contract answer (DF-ACE-253 to DF-ACE-258).

DP-07 keeps LOV-DOC-SOURCE, LOV-RETENTION and LOV-SCAN-RESULT in reference data through the contract and the client library, so `GENERATED`, `PARTNER`, `LEGAL10Y` and `GENERAL05Y` are values and never code.

DP-09 is the outbox: `DocumentStored` is written in the store transaction with the document row and its fields, keyed by caseId, and the relay publishes it once with no personal data; an inbox is wired by the template and nothing is consumed in this slice.

DP-10 applies as a prohibition: no Quartz job, no Schedule and no event-started workflow is created here. The intake and the retention Schedules stay with RWB-P5-E1049-APP and RWB-P5-E1052-APP, and the notice-period timer with rwb-case.

DP-11 is the one-hop contract to rwb-comms: REST, a mock and a 2 s timeout with a breaker per downstream, and no call chain from rwb-document onward while the caller waits.

DP-15 is the per-service Flyway sequence: this slice contributes no migration step, and it builds only after the store migration of RWB-P5-E1024-APP and the type load of RWB-P5-E1025-APP are in the sequence, in their own schema and never in the shared baseline.

DP-18 makes the interaction ledger rwb-source-data's: this slice publishes the event and writes no `LETTER` entry, and the ledger listener of rwb-source-data records the interaction from the event (REQ-ILG-004).

DP-19 is the gateway-bff composite route: the documents tab of SCR-30 reaches rwb-document in one hop, in parallel with the other tabs, and the answer is composed at the edge, so no service is asked to call another on behalf of a screen.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, a notice PDF and a WIN receipt are stored on case `RC-2026-000123` with the type, the write-once flag and the retention class of the type in force, a content replace and a delete inside the retention period are refused with MSG-P5-002 and the hash is unchanged, `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` is on `rwb.document.events.v1` once per store with no personal data, the document is read with its metadata, versions and fields within 2 s through the gateway-bff route, the same receipt stored twice leaves one document and counts the repeat, and the boundary test shows no cross-schema read, no ledger entry and no timer in this module.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P6-004 | The notice is acknowledged by WIN and the case record shows the dispatch | {notice} was sent for registered mail on {date}. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The rwb-comms contract does not answer within 2 s, or the storage copy has not completed | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The WIN batch is late or not COMPLETE for the business date of a receipt | {product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived. |
| MSG-P5-002 | A content replace or a delete of a write-once document inside its retention period | Legal documents cannot be changed. Add a new version instead. |
| MSG-P5-016 | The virus scan finds malware in the receipt or the notice file on intake | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1046; ASM-1994) |
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller's role holds no Documents right for the action | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The case is absent or outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The store path cannot write its decision record, so nothing is stored | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

MSG-P6-004 is raised by rwb-comms, not by this slice: the case record line is quoted here because the document reference this slice returns is what makes the line nameable, and the wording is the legacy wording unchanged. MSG-P5-016 is named by the FSD P5 upload exception flow with the ID and the meaning "malware found" only, so its text is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1046; ASM-1994) and the story does not invent one. MSG-P7-003 belongs to the store path of RWB-P5-E1024-APP, which writes the DOCATT record; this slice inherits the refusal and writes no record of its own. For MSG-P4-002 in this story {action} names the action the caller tried — for example "attach the proof of delivery" — and never a case fact or a role name.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen is built in this story. The evidence is read on two screens that other stories own, both read only for this slice:

| Screen | What this slice makes visible |
|---|---|
| SCR-03 Case record | The notice and its proof of delivery as documents of the case, with the type, the stored date and the write-once label |
| SCR-30 Case documents | The two documents in the case document list with their type, source, stored date and version, the delivery facts of the receipt as document fields, and the download of the file through the content read |

| State | What the user sees |
|---|---|
| Loading | The tab skeleton while the document list or the document detail arrives through the gateway-bff composite route |
| List | The documents of the case with type, source, stored date, version and the write-once label; a COPY_PENDING document shows its state and its download disabled with MSG-GEN-006 |
| Error | The message of section 14 when a read is refused (MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003, MSG-GEN-006) with a retry action, and a document reference the service does not hold shown as unresolved to the owner |

The tab is reached only through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), which asks rwb-document once for the documents of the case and never asks this service to call another; the full tab, its search and its upload form are RWB-P5-E1026-APP's.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the document type, the write-once flag, the retention class, the source, the container, the path template and the delivery field names are rows of the type table, values of a reference list or properties read at start-up. The boundary test fails a build in which a type code, a retention class or a source value appears in Java.
- No personal data in events, workflow inputs, payloads, logs, tests or prompts. The event carries IDs and business facts only (`documentId`, `caseId`, `documentType`, `source`, `storedAt`); the addressee of a notice stays inside the PDF; the receipt carries a barcode, a delivery status and dates; no person name, no address, no identity number and no account number is written by this slice, and a field value is replaced by its field name in a log line.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or the owner's `v_ace_*` views — and this story reads neither: DP-05 applies as a prohibition, the ACE proof of delivery reaches the receipt inside the rwb-comms answer, and no `v_ace_pod` row is opened by this service.
- No cross-schema read: `rwb_document` holds no foreign key into another schema and no copy of a case, a notice or a ledger entry (DP-01); the case, the notice and the ledger arrive through their owners' contracts or events.
- Write once: a legal document is stored in `rwb-docs-legal` with `write_once` true, is never overwritten, replaced or deleted inside its retention period, and every change is a new version at a new blob path with the earlier version still readable (NFR-029, FSD P5 AC-ALT-P5-001-01).
- Retention class from the type in force: the class and the flag come from `document_type` in the version in force, are carried on the row for the life of the document, and no end-of-retention action is taken by this slice (NFR-028, NFR-074, RWB-P5-E1052-APP).
- No ledger entry and no timer from this service: the interaction ledger is rwb-source-data's (DP-18) and the notice-period timer is rwb-case's (DP-10); the module registers no ledger call, no Schedule and no timer, and the test of AC7 fails if one appears.
- The document reference is data: it is the document ID returned by the store and read through the contract, never a value computed from a case number, a notice number, a barcode or a file name, so the dispatch file, the notice and the case screen name the same document or name none.
- One event per committed store, written in the store transaction: a failed transaction leaves no document row, no field row and no outbox row, and a repeated receipt leaves one row and a counted repeat (R-UNI-40).

##### 19. Out of scope

- The whole dispatch and acknowledgment path: the notice state machine, the barcode, the INT-14 file, the acknowledgment, the retry after three failures, the REC-05 reconciliation and the NoticeDispatched and NoticeDelivered events — RWB-P6-E1055-CON and RWB-P6-E1055-APP.
- The `v_ace_pod` read, the ACE batch check and the data product freshness of the notice — RWB-P1-E1055-APP, with the data product of the notice.
- The notice-period timer and the case history item that shows the dispatch and the delivery — RWB-P3-E1055-APP.
- The WIN file interface, its SFTP and MFT path, the PGP handling and its infrastructure — RWB-P6-E1055-INF and RWB-P6-E1055-OPS.
- The document intake, the OCR, the classification and the field extraction of a scanned receipt, and the review queue of a low-confidence extraction — RWB-P5-E1049-APP and the extraction stories of P5.
- The monthly retention run, the retention action rows and the end-of-retention dispositions — RWB-P5-E1052-APP.
- The document type table load, its Legal and NPA sign-offs and its version — RWB-P5-E1025-APP.
- The store path itself, the upload form, the case document list, the search and the generation of a document from a template — RWB-P5-E1024-APP, RWB-P5-E1026-APP and the generation story of P5.
- Custody of originals and electronic discovery — the Epic 2 stories of P5.
- The end-to-end proof of these values across rwb-comms, rwb-document, rwb-source-data and rwb-case — RWB-ITG-E1055-ITG.
- The `rwb_document` schema baseline, the platform migration role, the topic and DLT provisioning, the container provisioning and its WORM policy, the observability and the runbook of this service.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-055 for rwb-source-data. The proof of delivery that ACE ingests from WIN is read from `v_ace_pod` on this service's own base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` as one named read, `GET /proof-of-delivery?businessDate=` (DP-05, DP-11, DP-13), gated on the WIN batch row of `v_ace_batch_status` so that no row of a date whose batch is not COMPLETE is ever returned (the gate of FSD P1 A2.14 and BR9 of this story); the delivery is recorded once on this service's own interaction ledger `interaction` in schema `rwb_source_data` through the ledger writer, keyed on the pod key and the notice with its callback date (DP-01, DP-18), with the lookup index on the per-service Flyway sequence (DP-15); the read stays behind its flag until `v_ace_pod` and `v_ace_batch_status` arrive with RWB-ACE-001 (DL43; TSD P1 T3.2 and T3.7). The WIN file, the acknowledgment, the notice, the row-to-notice matching and the notice period timer are rwb-comms, rwb-integration and rwb-case and are not in this story. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **litigation officer (RW-LITOFF)**, I want **the proof of delivery that ACE ingests from WIN to be read from the Workbench source-data service for a business date whose WIN batch is COMPLETE, with the delivery recorded once on the interaction ledger of the case**, so that **the delivery date a notice period is counted from is the one the bank's own record holds, stated with its age, and a second look at the same row never writes a second entry**.

This is the rwb-source-data slice of legacy RWB-E1-055, and it owns no legacy criterion: the criteria of the key are owned by the rwb-comms slice (RWB-P6-E1055-APP: AC2 to AC8 and AC10 to AC11), by the rwb-case, rwb-document and rwb-comms slices between them, and by the cross-service proof RWB-ITG-E1055-ITG (AC1 and AC9). What this story delivers is the source side of that loop, and it is worth a story of its own because it is the only door in the Workbench to the proof of a delivery:

- **the read** — `GET /proof-of-delivery?businessDate=` on base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`, one row per `v_ace_pod` row of the business date, in pod-key order, carrying `pod_key`, `account_key`, `notice_ref`, `sent_date`, `barcode`, `callback_date`, `delivery_status`, `sent_type`, `source_system` and `data_as_of`;
- **the WIN batch gate** — a row of the date is returned only when the WIN row in `v_ace_batch_status` is COMPLETE for that date; otherwise no row of that date is returned, nothing of an earlier date is served in its place, DP07 is STALE and MSG-P1-001 is answered;
- **the delivery entry** — one outbound `LETTER` entry per delivery on this service's interaction ledger, through the ledger writer, carrying the delivery date and the notice reference and keyed on the pod key with the notice and its callback date, so a repeat read writes no second entry and the repeat is counted under R-UNI-40;
- **the Section B discipline** — `v_ace_pod` is a Section B view over the ACE table `pod_receipt`, so the read stays behind its flag until RWB-ACE-001 lands and answers "not available" until then (DL43).

It does **not** match a row to a notice by barcode or by `notice_ref`, does not change a notice state, does not start the `NOTICE_PERIOD` timer, does not hold a row with an unknown reference, opens no WIN connection and sends or acknowledges no file. Those are RWB-P6-E1055-APP, RWB-P3-E1055-APP, RWB-P5-E1055-APP and the integration slice of this key.

##### 2. Business rationale

Proof of delivery is chased by phone today, and a notice period counted from a print date can be challenged in court. The Workbench writes no WIN delivery fact of its own: ACE ingests the WIN proof-of-delivery file (INT-15) into `pod_receipt`, and the Workbench reads the result through the view `recovery.v_ace_pod` (D-RCV-35 U1; Architecture v5 slide 41; TSD P1 T5.1). One reader of ACE's views is the whole point of ADR-010: rwb-source-data holds the grant, and every other service asks it (REQ-DRI-006). So the delivery fact a notice period rests on must leave this service in a shape that says how old it is and never in a shape that silently serves yesterday's rows.

The batch gate is the part that has to survive the move. In the monolith the read ran inside one job beside the ACE batch record; in the target the read is on demand and may be asked at any hour, so the date's completeness is checked at the door. A WIN batch that is late, failed at its record count check or absent yields no row of that date, no earlier date in its place, DP07 STALE and MSG-P1-001: a notice period that starts one day early is a legal defect, and a period that starts from an earlier delivery is worse than a period that starts late and says so (FSD P1 A2.14 BR-P1-014-2 and BR-P1-014-3; TSD P1 T3.7).

The ledger entry is the second half. REQ-ILG-004 asks that what happens in an interaction is recorded against that interaction, and R-UNI-40 asks that the same fact twice produces one effect and a counted repeat. A delivery is a fact with a natural key that ACE already holds — the pod key, the notice reference and the callback date — so the entry is written under exactly that key, and the repeat is a no-op that is counted rather than a second line in the history of a case. Serves REQ-OCC-003, REQ-ILG-004 and REQ-DRI-006.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The wave-1 service baseline of rwb-source-data is in place: schema `rwb_source_data`, the `interaction` table with its ledger columns, the running per-service Flyway sequence with its own history table, the REST base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`, the task queue name `rwb-source-data` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and the login `rwb_source_data` with SELECT on the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views and no privilege on any ACE table (DP-01, DP-02, DP-13, DP-15).
- **No build dependency of its own.** The metadata row *Depends on (build)* is None and the story starts on Day 1: it is a read over a view plus one entry on a table this service already owns, and the pipeline baseline it builds on is the service template, the schema, the sequence, the reference-data client library and the ledger writer interface of this service. The H rows the pattern table names (DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-15, DP-19) are the wave-0 platform libraries and are not repeated in the metadata row (Template and Rules §R5.7 rules 1 and 2; §13).
- RWB-P6-E1055-CON is published with its fake: the proof-of-delivery record shape of this key, the delivery fact and the answers of the consumer's fake. This story is the provider side of that shape and builds against the fake from Day 1; it calls no operation of rwb-comms.
- The ledger writer of this service is delivered by RWB-P1-E1066-APP and published in RWB-P1-E1066-CON: the append operation `POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/interactions`, its `InteractionRequest` schema, its `Idempotency-Key` rule, the `LETTER` event code of the list **LOV-LEDGER-EVENT**, the `case_seq` allocator and the unique key on the idempotency key. This story writes its delivery entry through that writer and never inserts into `interaction` directly; the build order of the two same-service stories is settled at sprint planning and is not a build dependency of this one (GAP-0578; ASM-0820).
- The freshness stamp and the DP07 status are delivered by RWB-P1-E1015-APP: `data_product_load` with one row per product and business date, the status list **LOV-FRESHNESS** and the repeat counter `duplicate_count`. This story reads the stamp and adds one to the counter of a repeat; it writes no stamp of its own.
- The feature flag of this read is a data row of the platform library and is closed until RWB-ACE-001 has created `v_ace_pod` and `v_ace_batch_status` (DL43; TSD P1 T3.2 and T3.7; GAP-0579; ASM-0821).
- The caller is the service identity of rwb-comms, holding a workload identity token, and never a person: a person reaches the delivery through the notice panel of rwb-comms and the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).
- The read's page parameters, its error statuses and the per-field "not available" answer are not fixed by any source document (GAP-0577; ASM-0819; GAP-0579; ASM-0821), and neither is the home of the repeat counter (GAP-0580; ASM-0822) nor the exact wording render of MSG-P1-001 (GAP-0581; ASM-0823).

##### 4. Flow

1. rwb-comms calls `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/proof-of-delivery?businessDate=2026-11-30` once per business date, after the WIN file window, as the service identity of rwb-comms; one hop, 2 s budget, one GET retry with jitter and a breaker (DP-11).
2. `SectionBGuard` reads the flag `rwb.dataengine.pod-read`: closed, the read answers with no row and the ten field names marked *not available* with the reason "Section B view not deployed" (AC5, X3).
3. `WinBatchGate` reads `v_ace_batch_status` for source WIN and the requested business date. The row is unique on `(source_system, business_date)`; when it is absent, or `is_complete` is false, or the status is FAILED, no `v_ace_pod` row of that date is read, nothing of an earlier date is served in its place, DP07 is STALE and MSG-P1-001 is answered (AC2, X1, X2).
4. `ProofOfDeliveryRepository` reads `v_ace_pod` for that business date. A Section B view carries `source_system` and `data_as_of` from the Tier 2 `business_date`, so the filter is the business date and `data_as_of` travels on the row as the age of the fact (TSD P1 T3.3).
5. The rows are mapped to the ten fields of the record and returned in ascending `pod_key` order; `sent_date` and `callback_date` arrive as dates through `recovery.ace_to_date`, so a dirty ACE text date is a null and never an error (TSD P1 T3.2, BR-P1-001-7).
6. Nothing is matched and nothing is resolved: a `notice_ref` that names no notice is returned like any other row, because the notice is rwb-comms' and the hold on an unknown reference is its check (RWB-P6-E1055-APP).
7. When the caller names the case of the notice the rows belong to, `DeliveryLedgerWriter` appends one delivery entry per row through the ledger writer, with the delivery date as the occurred time, the `LETTER` event code and outbound direction, the notice reference in the summary and `pod_key` as the source reference (AC3, DP-18).
8. The writer derives the idempotency key from the pod key, the notice reference and the callback date, so a second read of the same row finds the stored entry and writes no second one; `DuplicateCounter` adds one to `duplicate_count` of the DP07 stamp of that business date and writes nothing else (AC4, R-UNI-40).
9. The answer carries the rows and the freshness stamp of DP07 for the business date — its status, its source business date and the time the stamp was written — because every source-data answer states the age of what it carries (TSD P1 T3.7 Display).
10. A view or database failure answers 503 with MSG-GEN-006 and writes nothing; a ledger failure rolls the entry back, the read answers 503 with MSG-P1-022 and no row of the answer is presented as recorded (X6).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The WIN batch for the business date is not COMPLETE in `v_ace_batch_status` | No `v_ace_pod` row of that date is read; no earlier date is served in its place; DP07 is STALE; the answer carries no row | MSG-P1-001 | AC2 |
| X2 | The WIN batch for the business date is FAILED at its record count check | As X1, and the stale flag is set at once; the stamp of the last complete business date stays the one in use | MSG-P1-001 | AC2 |
| X3 | `v_ace_pod` or `v_ace_batch_status` does not exist yet, or the flag is closed | No row is invented and no date is guessed: the answer names the ten fields as not available with the reason, and nothing else | None | AC5 |
| X4 | The same `v_ace_pod` row is read twice | One delivery entry exists; the repeat is counted; no notice and no entry changes | None | AC4 |
| X5 | A row names a notice reference that resolves to no notice | The row is returned unchanged; it is neither held nor dropped here; the hold is the consumer's check | None | AC6 (the hold is RWB-P6-E1055-APP) |
| X6 | The view, the database or the ledger does not answer | 503 with the platform problem envelope; no entry is written and no partial answer is presented | MSG-GEN-006; MSG-P1-022 | 12.2 |
| X7 | The request names no business date | 422 with the field name; nothing is read | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |

X1 and X2 are the legacy exception paths of RWB-E1-055 this slice owns (X2 of the legacy story, and the failed batch of AC5); X4 is the repeated read of the legacy story (X4, AC7 and AC10) carried as one counted repeat. X3 is the path DL43 and TSD P1 T3.7 add: a Section B view that is not there yet must answer "not available" rather than an empty list that reads as "no delivery". X5 and X6 keep their legacy shape but cross no boundary: the unknown reference is no longer held here, and a failure of the view is now a failure of a service call.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency: one view, one table this service owns and one published shape of RWB-P6-E1055-CON with its fake |
| Negotiable | The class split, the page size and the exact envelope members are the squad's choice behind the contract; the ten fields, the gate and the delivery key are fixed |
| Valuable | One door to ACE's proof of delivery, stated with its age, and one recorded delivery per row |
| Estimable | One controller, one gate, one repository, one writer client, one counter, one index |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests, as the source slice of the legacy key |
| Testable | Every criterion is one read against a fixture of `v_ace_pod`, `v_ace_batch_status` and the ledger |

```gherkin
    Given v_ace_pod holds one row for 2026-11-30 with pod_key "POD-0001", account_key "ACC-0001", notice_ref "N-0001", sent_date 2026-11-26, barcode "RR123456789TH", callback_date 2026-11-28, delivery_status "DELIVERED", sent_type "NPL", source_system "WIN" and data_as_of 2026-11-30
    Given case "RC-2026-000123" holds the delivery of notice "N-0001" on contract "CT-77001"

    When rwb-comms calls the proof-of-delivery read for business date 2026-11-30
    Then the answer holds no row and no business date is guessed

    Then DP07 is STALE and MSG-P1-001 is answered, and no default, no placeholder date and no earlier row is written

  Scenario: AC6 The row carries the ten view fields and nothing else (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rows of business date 2026-11-30 are returned

```

**Target reading.** Every value above is the legacy synthetic value of RWB-E1-055 and none of it is new: notice `N-0001`, case `RC-2026-000123`, contract `CT-77001`, barcode `RR123456789TH`, the sent date `26112026` read as 2026-11-26, the callback date 2026-11-28, the business dates 2026-11-25 and 2026-11-30 and the product "DP07 Legal". What changes is where each step runs. The read is a named operation of this service, `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/proof-of-delivery?businessDate=`, on base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` (DP-11, DP-13; the address, the envelope members and the page parameters are not fixed by any source and are recorded as target choices — GAP-0577; ASM-0819). The rows come from `v_ace_pod`, a Section B view over ACE's `pod_receipt` (TSD P1 T3.3 row 24), read behind the flag until RWB-ACE-001 lands (DL43). The gate is `v_ace_batch_status`, one row per source and business date, and its `is_complete` (TSD P1 T3.7; FSD P1 A2.14 BR-P1-014-2: freshness is read from the batch record only and never inferred from `data_as_of`, a row count or a file). The delivery entry is written through the ledger writer of this service, on `interaction` in `rwb_source_data`, which the R-PREC default ruling makes P1's ledger (DP-01, DP-18; Ownership Map, `interaction` owner P1); the case of the entry is the case the caller names, and the reading that the caller does that rather than this service is recorded with GAP-0578 and ASM-0820. The repeat counter is `data_product_load.duplicate_count` of DP07 for the business date (TSD P1 T3.6; T3.7 Repeat), which is the counter the sources name for a repeated read; the choice is recorded with GAP-0580 and ASM-0822. The "not available" answer of AC5 is the shape DL43 and TSD P1 T3.7 ask for and no source spells out; it is recorded with GAP-0579 and ASM-0821. The message render of AC2 is recorded with GAP-0581 and ASM-0823. Legacy AC1 to AC11 are not claimed here: the matching, the notice state, the events, the timer and the file are RWB-P6-E1055-APP, RWB-P3-E1055-APP, RWB-P5-E1055-APP and RWB-ITG-E1055-ITG.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A `v_ace_pod` row is read only when the ACE batch for source WIN is COMPLETE for its business date | Legacy RWB-E1-055 BR4; ACE batch record; INT-15 error handling |
| BR2 | The proof of delivery is read from ACE through `recovery.v_ace_pod`; the Workbench writes no WIN delivery fact and opens no WIN connection | REQ-DRI-006; D-RCV-35 U1; FSD P1 A2.1 BR-P1-001-2 |
| BR3 | Freshness is read from `v_ace_batch_status` only and never inferred from `data_as_of`, a row count or a file | FSD P1 A2.14 BR-P1-014-2 |
| BR4 | A product fed by more than one source carries the oldest business date among its sources and is STALE while any of them is late; DP07 is fed by LIT and WIN | FSD P1 A2.14 BR-P1-014-3; FSD P1 A2.2 DP07 row |
| BR5 | A notice period starts only from the delivery date on the proof of delivery, so the delivery date is carried unchanged and never derived | CTL-15; R-LIT-07; legacy BR2 |
| BR6 | The same proof-of-delivery fact twice produces one effect and the repeat is counted | R-UNI-40; legacy BR6 |
| BR7 | The notice data product is stale one business day after the WIN batch was due | v_ace_batch_status; MSG-P1-001; legacy BR7 |
| BR8 | One ledger holds every interaction on a case, and the delivery is recorded there once, on the case the delivery belongs to | REQ-ILG-001; REQ-ILG-004; DP-18 |

**Where each rule lives in the target.** BR1 and BR3 are one statement in this story and one in the freshness story: the gate is read from `v_ace_batch_status` at the door of the read, and the stamp is written by RWB-P1-E1015-APP; this story never computes a business date from a row and never trusts `data_as_of` as a completeness signal (BR3). BR2 is the schema boundary: `rwb_source_data` holds the grant on the view and no privilege on `public`, and the WIN file moves through rwb-integration only (DP-01, DP-02, DP-05; REQ-DRI-006). BR4 is why a DP07 stamp can be STALE because LIT is late while WIN is complete, and the read states the stamp it found rather than a status of its own. BR5 is why the entry's occurred time is the callback date of the row and never the time the read ran. BR6 becomes the delivery key plus the repeat counter, both inside this service. BR7 is the stale flag and the message of AC2. BR8 is the ledger's ownership: the entry is written through the writer of this service and no other service holds a copy of the ledger (DP-18).

##### 9. State transitions

This story changes no notice state and starts no timer; both are rwb-comms and rwb-case. It writes a ledger entry, and it moves the DP07 freshness stamp by reading it.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP07 with no stamp for the business date | a COMPLETE WIN row is read | `is_complete` is true for the requested date | A DP07 stamp for the business date, LOADED, as the freshness story writes it |
| DP07 at an earlier business date | the WIN batch of the requested date is late, failed or absent | The gate finds no complete row | DP07 STALE with the earlier business date still in use |
| A case at case_seq n | the delivery of a pod row is recorded | The WIN batch is COMPLETE and the caller names the case | The case is at case_seq n+1 and one outbound LETTER entry exists |
| A delivery already on the ledger | the same row is read again | The same pod key, notice reference and callback date | No change to the ledger; the repeat is counted |
| An applied migration version | a correction of the delivery lookup index | The index needs a fix | A new version on the service sequence; the applied version is never edited |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The service identity of rwb-comms | The only caller of the read: the DP07 rows of one business date and the delivery entries of the case it names (Case record R on that case) |
| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer | Reads the delivery date, the barcode and the delivery status on the notice panel of rwb-comms; calls nothing of this service directly (Litigation R) |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Reads the delivery on the case record view; calls nothing of this service directly (Litigation R) |
| RW-DATASTEW, data steward and data product owner | Reads the DP07 freshness stamp, the stale flag and the repeat count |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Opens and closes the flag of the read and reads the series of the deployment |
| rwb-source-data | Runs as its own login, holds SELECT on the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views and no privilege on any ACE table (DP-02; Architecture v5 slides 11 and 29) |
| rwb-comms (P6) | Owns the notice, the row-to-notice matching, the unknown-reference hold, the two events and the displayed message; answers the case of the delivery it names (C RWB-P6-E1055-CON) |

The read carries the caller's token and the case it names, and the ledger entry is written for that case. This service decides no right of its own on a notice: it answers source data to an authenticated service identity, and the right on the notice is enforced where the notice lives.

| DF-INT-019 | interaction | case_seq | Allocated and written by the ledger writer |

| DF-OPS-009 | data_product_load | duplicate_count | Write (plus one on a repeat read) |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary.

**Which side is this story's.** `DF-ACE-251` to `DF-ACE-260` are ACE's own columns, read through `v_ace_pod` and never written; the ten of them are the whole row this story answers, and the view carries no name, address or contact value, so no personal field of ACE enters the answer (TSD P1 T3.3). `DF-ACE-178` to `DF-ACE-186` are ACE's batch record, read through `v_ace_batch_status` for the gate only. `DF-INT-002` to `DF-INT-019` are this service's own ledger rows: this story supplies the values and the writer allocates `case_seq` and stores the idempotency key; no field is inserted directly. `DF-OPS-007` is read and `DF-OPS-009` is incremented on the stamp of RWB-P1-E1015-APP, which owns the row and its keys.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` (DP-13). One operation, the proof-of-delivery read of the DP07 product.

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/proof-of-delivery?businessDate=` | Reads the WIN proof-of-delivery rows of one business date from `v_ace_pod`, one row per ACE row in ascending `pod_key` order, only when the WIN row in `v_ace_batch_status` is COMPLETE for that date; with `caseId` it also records the delivery entries of that case through the ledger writer | Service identity of rwb-comms, Case record R on the named case; one hop, 2 s budget | Idempotent: a repeat returns the same rows, and with the same `caseId` it writes no second ledger entry (R-UNI-40) |

The answer is `ProofOfDeliveryPage` of RWB-P6-E1055-CON: the business date, the product code `DP07`, the freshness stamp of DP07 (status, source business date and the time the stamp was written) and the rows. Each row is the ten-field record of AC6, mapped one to one from `v_ace_pod` with `sent_date` and `callback_date` in the ISO form on the wire. Errors are 401 without a session, 403 for a case outside the caller's scope (MSG-P4-002), 422 for a missing or invalid field (MSG-GEN-001), and 503 when the views or the ledger do not answer (MSG-GEN-006, MSG-P1-022). The page parameters, the element types, the exact error set and the second query parameter `caseId` are a target choice and are not specified in the source documents (GAP-0577; ASM-0819; GAP-0578; ASM-0820).

The ledger entry is not a second operation of this story: it is written through the append operation of the interaction ledger, `POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/interactions`, inside this service and in the same transaction as the read, so the writer's rule on the time, the actor, the list and the allocator is applied once, in one place (DP-18; RWB-P1-E1066-CON).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None at run time. This story is the provider side of the shape RWB-P6-E1055-CON publishes: rwb-comms calls this read, and this story calls nothing of rwb-comms. The only calls it makes are inside its own service — the ledger writer of RWB-P1-E1066-CON and the DP07 stamp of RWB-P1-E1015-APP — and neither is a hop of the 2 s budget that DP-11 governs. No table of another service is read and no foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01).

###### 12.3 Events published

None of its own. The topic of the service is `rwb.source-data.events.v1` with event names `rwb.source-data.<Event>.v1` (DP-14), and its two events `AceDataReady` and `AceDataLate` belong to RWB-P1-E1015-APP (Architecture v5 slides 15 and 43). The delivery entry is a same-service write on this service's own ledger and no event announces it; the business event a notice period rests on, `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1`, is rwb-comms' and is published by RWB-P6-E1055-APP (DP-09). This story adds no message schema.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. No event starts this read: rwb-comms calls it after the WIN file window, and Architecture v5 slide 15 gives this service no consumed event. `AceDataReady` and `AceDataLate` are on this service's producing side, and the batch completeness the gate needs is read from `v_ace_batch_status` and not waited for as a message.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The read is a synchronous step and writes one row per delivery in one transaction. The task queue of this service is `rwb-source-data` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, and this story registers no workflow and no activity on it: the activities `listEligibleAccounts` and `snapshot(page)` and the workflows `AceIngestCheck` and `reconciliation` of Architecture v5 slide 15 are RWB-P1-E1015-APP's and the case-list stories'.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The 06:00 daily read of the legacy story (`v_ace_pod` read path, RWB-E1-055 section 12) is not a Schedule of this story. In the target the pod read is started by the slice that owns the run: the DP07 cut-off Schedule of RWB-P1-E1015-APP marks the product and the pod step of RWB-P6-E1055-APP calls this read after the WIN file window; this operation answers on demand and holds no state, so no Temporal Schedule is registered here and DP-10 applies as a statement only — no Quartz trigger and no row of a shared job table survives the move (Architecture v5 slide 44).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Object | Schema | Owner | This story |
|---|---|---|---|
| `v_ace_pod` | `recovery` | ACE team (Tier 2 Section B view over ACE `pod_receipt`); SELECT to `rwb_source_data` only | Read only, the ten fields of AC6; a view and not a table, and the table behind it is ACE's and outside the 19 schemas; it exists only after RWB-ACE-001 |
| `v_ace_batch_status` | `recovery` | ACE team (Tier 2 Section B view over ACE `ace_batch_run`); SELECT to `rwb_source_data` only | Read only: `source_system`, `business_date`, `status` and `is_complete`, the gate of AC2 |
| `interaction` | `rwb_source_data` | P1 rwb-source-data (Ownership Map) | The ledger of the delivery: inserted through the writer only, with the lookup index of section 13; this story updates and deletes nothing |
| `data_product_load` | `rwb_source_data` | P1 rwb-source-data (Ownership Map) | The DP07 stamp of the business date: status read, `duplicate_count` incremented by one on a repeat; the stamp itself is RWB-P1-E1015-APP's write |
| `outbox_event`, `processed_event`, `idempotency_key` | `rwb_source_data` | PLT library objects, created in this service's schema | The writer's stored response and the idempotency key of the delivery; read and written by the library, not by this story |

`v_ace_pod` and `v_ace_batch_status` are views, not tables: the Ownership Map names tables of the 19 schemas, and an ACE table is ACE's, so no ownership row is invented for `pod_receipt` or `ace_batch_run`. The notice is `rwb_comms`' and the case is `rwb_case`'; both are reached through rwb-comms' own answer and never read here. No table of another service is read and no foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01, DP-05).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| RWB-P6-E1055-CON fake | The proof-of-delivery record and page shape, and the delivery fact of the key | The ten-field record of AC6 for business date 2026-11-30, the empty answer of AC2, the "not available" answer of AC5, and the repeat answer of AC4 |
| View fixture | `recovery.v_ace_pod` and `recovery.v_ace_batch_status` in a container | One pod row of 2026-11-30 with `RR123456789TH`, notice `N-0001` and callback date 2026-11-28; a second row of 2026-11-25; batch rows for WIN COMPLETE, FAILED at its record count check and absent; LIT not COMPLETE beside a complete WIN |
| Ledger fixture | `rwb_source_data` | A container at the baseline plus the ledger columns, the unique key on the idempotency key and this story's index, so the repeat of AC4 runs on the real key and the real allocator |
| Flag-closed fixture | The service with `rwb.dataengine.pod-read` closed | The AC5 answer, with no view present in the schema |

No WIN connection is opened and no production payload is copied into a fake: the pod values are the legacy synthetic values of RWB-E1-055.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Provided | Consumed | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| REST | 1 operation on `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` | None | One hop, 2 s budget for the caller; the ledger write and the stamp read are same-service calls (DP-11) |
| Kafka | None | None | The topic belongs to RWB-P1-E1015-APP; `NoticeDelivered` is rwb-comms' and belongs to RWB-P6-E1055-APP |
| Temporal | None | None | No workflow, activity or Schedule in this story (DP-10 as a statement) |
| File | None | None | INT-15 is ACE's inbound file and INT-14 is rwb-integration's outbound file; this service opens neither |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.sourcedata`, module `pod`, with the published types in `...sourcedata.api`. Base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`, schema `rwb_source_data`, topic `rwb.source-data.events.v1` (not published here), task queue `rwb-source-data` in namespace `rwb-recovery` (not used here).

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-18 | Interaction ledger | Ledger owned by rwb-source-data (default ruling) | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**How each pattern applies here.**

- **DP-01.** `interaction`, `data_product_load` and the library tables live in `rwb_source_data`; the notice, the case and the calendar are not copied and not joined. A delivery row holds ACE business keys — `pod_key`, `account_key`, `notice_ref` — as references and never as foreign keys, so nothing crosses a schema.
- **DP-05.** This is one of the two views DP-05 is about: `v_ace_pod` is read here and nowhere else in the Workbench, and `v_ace_batch_status` beside it. The read is the service's own `v_ace_*` read, which is why the pattern adds no dependency; the consumer answers of RWB-P6-E1055-CON exist so that no other service needs the grant.
- **DP-07.** This story enumerates no list value of its own: the product code `DP07`, the freshness status and the threshold of a late batch are read as data — the stamp and its status from RWB-P1-E1015-APP, and any run-time list through the reference-data client library of the platform baseline, which is the wave-0 side of the DP-07 row. The `LETTER` event code and the channel of the ledger entry are values of the lists the ledger writer reads, never constants in this story.
- **DP-09.** No event is published and none is consumed: the delivery entry is a same-service ledger write and `NoticeDelivered` is rwb-comms'. The pattern applies as the prohibition that keeps this read out of the event path — the outbox and inbox library of the ledger writer is the only event-adjacent machinery this story touches, and it touches it through the writer.
- **DP-10.** Applies as a statement: the 06:00 job of the legacy story is gone with Quartz, and no Schedule, no workflow and no activity of this read is registered here (12.6). The cut-off that decides when the pod read may run is RWB-P1-E1015-APP's Schedule and the run itself is rwb-comms'.
- **DP-11.** Applies from the caller's side: the read is a REST contract with one hop and a 2 s budget, and the two things this story calls are inside its own service, so the read adds no hop to the chain. Its 503 answers carry the platform problem envelope so that a caller's breaker sees a plain failure.
- **DP-15.** This story adds one version to the service's own Flyway sequence, in schema `rwb_source_data`, for the delivery lookup index, and it reuses the ledger columns the ledger story created rather than re-creating them (see Migrations below).
- **DP-18.** The ledger is this service's own (R-PREC default ruling; Ownership Map, `interaction` owner P1), and this story is a consumer of its own writer: the delivery entry is written there and read back from there, and no other service holds or writes a delivery line.
- **DP-19.** Applies as a statement for the person: the litigation officer and the case owner see the delivery on the notice panel and the case record view, which arrive through the gateway-bff composite route, and never call this operation. The only caller of this operation is a service identity.

The platform H rows of the pattern table are delivered by the wave-0 platform and are not repeated in the metadata H field of this story, which stays empty by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7 rule 2): the story is Day 1 on the pipeline baseline, and the one contract it builds against as a dependency is RWB-P6-E1055-CON with its fake.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `ProofOfDeliveryController` | Controller | The operation of 12.1 on `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`; parameter validation; RFC 9457 problem details |
| `SectionBGuard` | Guard | Reads the flag `rwb.dataengine.pod-read` and answers the ten fields as not available when the Section B views are not deployed (AC5) |
| `WinBatchGate` | Service | Reads `v_ace_batch_status` for source WIN and the business date and decides whether a row of that date may be read; marks DP07 STALE and renders MSG-P1-001 (AC2) |
| `ProofOfDeliveryRepository` | Repository | Reads `v_ace_pod` for the business date in ascending `pod_key` order; no write method exists |
| `PodReceipt` | Record | Immutable mapping of the ten view fields |
| `ProofOfDeliveryPage` | Record | The answer: business date, product code, freshness stamp and rows |
| `DeliveryLedgerWriter` | Client, in-service | Appends the delivery entry through the ledger writer of RWB-P1-E1066-CON, with the delivery key as the idempotency key (AC3, AC4) |
| `DuplicateCounter` | Service | Adds one to `duplicate_count` of the DP07 stamp when the delivery key is already stored (AC4) |
| `V<next>__rwb_e1_055_pod_delivery_index.sql` | Migration | The delivery lookup index on `interaction`, on the service's own sequence |

**Migrations and sequence (DP-15).** One version on rwb-source-data's own Flyway sequence, after the ledger version and after the freshness version it depends on at run time: the index `ix_interaction_pod_delivery` on `(event_code, source_ref)` of `interaction` in `rwb_source_data`, so that the read can tell a recorded delivery from a new one without a second key. The columns the entry needs — `event_code`, `direction`, `source_ref`, `idempotency_key` and `case_seq` — are created by the ledger version of RWB-P1-E1066-APP and are not re-created here; this story adds no table and no column. The exact version number is assigned by the sequence owner at build time, no monolith version number is reused, and an applied version is never edited.

**Database.** This story owns no table shape: it inserts into `interaction` through the writer and increments one column of `data_product_load`. It creates no table of another service, adds no foreign key across a schema, and reads ACE only through the two Section B views (DP-01, DP-05).

**Configuration and reference data**

- The flag `rwb.dataengine.pod-read` is a data row of the platform library and gates the read until RWB-ACE-001 lands (DL43; GAP-0579; ASM-0821).
- The product code `DP07` and the freshness status values come from the catalog and the stamp, not from the code; the product name rendered in MSG-P1-001 ("DP07 Legal") is the catalog value and the date is the last complete business date of the stamp (GAP-0581; ASM-0823).
- The ledger `LETTER` event code, the channel and the direction are values of the lists the ledger writer reads, and no list value is written in this story's code (DP-07).
- The 2 s budget, the single GET retry and the breaker of the caller are configuration of the edge; the page size and the maximum page of this read are configuration of this service (GAP-0577; ASM-0819).
- The delivery key of the ledger entry — pod key, notice reference and callback date — is a rule of this story and not a configuration value; a change of it is a new version of the writer's contract.

**Build steps**

1. The read operation on the base, with the parameter validation of X7 and the problem envelope of 12.1.
2. `SectionBGuard` and the "not available" answer, with the flag fixture of 12.8 (AC5).
3. `WinBatchGate`: the batch row of source WIN and the business date, the FAILED path, the absent row and the no-earlier-date rule (AC2).
4. `ProofOfDeliveryRepository` and the ten-field mapping, with `ace_to_date` on the two dates and the null-on-dirty rule (AC1, AC6).
5. The ordering and the paging of the rows, and the page element of the answer.
6. `DeliveryLedgerWriter`: one entry per row for the named case, the delivery key as the idempotency key, and the read-back that proves one entry (AC3).
7. `DuplicateCounter` and the repeat path, on the real unique key of the ledger fixture (AC4).
8. The migration of the lookup index on the service sequence, with a repeated run that changes nothing.
9. Tests for AC1 to AC6 with the fakes of 12.8, and the regression rows of section 16 where the fixture of the owning slice is available.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.dataengine.pod-read`. Off, the read answers the ten fields as not available and no row, no stamp and no entry are written.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, the read answers the ten fields for a COMPLETE WIN business date against the view fixture, a FAILED or absent batch answers no row with DP07 STALE and MSG-P1-001, one delivery yields one outbound `LETTER` entry with the delivery date and the notice reference, a second read yields no second entry and counts the repeat, the flag-closed answer invents nothing, and the index is applied on the service sequence.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-001 | The WIN batch is late, failed or not COMPLETE for the business date | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The source views or the database do not answer | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P1-022 | The delivery entry could not be written | The entry was not saved because the interaction ledger could not be written. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | The request names no business date, or names an invalid one | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller names a case outside its scope | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The wording of MSG-P1-001 is the FSD P1 v3 rendering, which names the ACE batch rather than a load (FSD P1 OQ-P1-07), and its values are the legacy ones: {product} is the catalog product name ("DP07 Legal" in the fixture) and {date} is the last complete business date of the DP07 stamp (2026-11-23 in the fixture). The exact render of the product name and of the date is not fixed by any source document (GAP-0581; ASM-0823). MSG-GEN-006 takes the name of what failed; MSG-P1-022, MSG-GEN-001 and MSG-P4-002 are passed on unchanged from the ledger writer and from the case check, and the field name of MSG-GEN-001 is filled from the validation failure and is never a data value. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story. The litigation officer and the case owner see the delivery date, the barcode and the delivery status on the notice panel and on SCR-03 Case record, both served by rwb-comms and reached through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19; RWB-PLT-N001-CON), and the data steward sees the DP07 freshness stamp, the stale flag and the repeat count on SCR-45 Data quality (RWB-P1-E1015-APP). This operation has no screen: it is called by a service. When the read answers "not available" or no row, the notice panel shows MSG-P1-001 with the age of the product, and the delivery state of the notice is left as it was; this story renders none of it.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the product code, the product name, the freshness status values, the `LETTER` event code and the channel come from the catalog, the stamp and the lists; the page size, the retry, the 2 s budget and the flag are configuration.
- No personal data in an answer, a log, a test or a prompt: the ten view fields carry no name, address, contact value or identity number, the log holds the business date, the pod count, the case ID and the error class, and no field of `v_ace_customer` or `v_ace_contact` is touched by this story.
- No read of another service's tables and no `public.*` read: ACE data is reached only through the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views, which is why this read exists at all (DP-01, DP-05; FSD P1 A2.1 BR-P1-001-2).
- No WIN connection and no file: INT-14 and INT-15 are rwb-integration's and ACE's, and this service opens neither (REQ-DRI-006; legacy guardrail 4).
- No second delivery line: the entry is written through the writer with the delivery key, and the ledger's unique key on the idempotency key is what makes the repeat a no-op rather than a hope (R-UNI-40).
- No invented date and no earlier date: a date whose WIN batch is not COMPLETE answers no row, and a Section B view that is not there answers "not available" — never an empty list that reads as "no delivery" and never a fallback to `data_as_of` (BR3; DL43).
- One login, one schema and one sequence: the release carries the `rwb_source_data` login, migrates `rwb_source_data` only, and an applied migration version is never edited (DP-02, DP-15).
- The platform library objects stay the library's: `outbox_event`, `processed_event` and `idempotency_key` are created in this schema and are never redefined by this story (DP-09).
