##### 19. Out of scope

- The outbound WIN file, the trailer and the dispatch (INT-14, JOB-10) and the acknowledgment that sets the sent date, the barcode and the sent type (RWB-P6-E1055-APP and RWB-ITG-E1055-ITG).
- The row-to-notice matching by barcode and then by `notice_ref`, the notice state, and the hold of a row whose reference names no notice (RWB-P6-E1055-APP).
- `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1` and `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1`, and the `NOTICE_PERIOD` timer that rwb-case starts from the delivered date (RWB-P6-E1055-APP, RWB-P3-E1055-APP; R-LIT-07).
- The WIN inbound interface INT-15, its file layout, its ingestion checks and its batch row: ACE's and the ACE team's (RWB-ACE-001; INT-15 owner ACE team).
- The freshness stamp itself, the cut-off Schedule, the stale flag and `AceDataReady` and `AceDataLate` (RWB-P1-E1015-APP).
- The ledger read interface and its filters, and the case timeline built on the ledger (RWB-P1-E1068-APP and rwb-case).
- The refused and undeliverable letters, the proof window and the queue transfer (RWB-E2-021, R-LIT-08, R-LIT-09).
- The gateway-bff composite route, the notice panel and the case record view (RWB-PLT-N001-CON and the screen owners).
- The deployment, the flag row, the dashboards, the alerts and the runbook of this read (the P1 deployment story of this wave).

##### 1. Story

As an **infrastructure engineer**, I want **the runtime for the WIN file exchange — the one-hop egress path from the rwb-comms and rwb-integration pods to the WIN SFTP endpoint, the client certificate and key that authenticate it, the file landing and staging area with its retention and its private access, the worker and KEDA scaling that carries the 16:00 dispatch burst and the proof-of-delivery ingest, the key-store entries for every credential, the storage that holds the dispatch files of the business date, and the observability signals with the freshness alert for a late WIN batch**, so that **the loop of RWB-E1-055 can run against an outside system under the bank's network and key rules, a late or failed WIN batch is visible to an operator within the business day, and no certificate, key or file ever sits in a values file, a log or a public location**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story leaned on integration adapters that an ACE operator configured once, and the only production trace of a broken WIN edge was an operator noticing that notices stayed Generated. In the target the same edge is a service-to-service chain: rwb-comms builds the file, rwb-integration executes `deliverFile`, and the proof of delivery returns through the ACE ingestion that rwb-source-data reads (Architecture v5 slides 17, 41 and 44, JOB-10 "Airflow file window + workers"). Every one of those steps needs something the pod does not have by default: an egress path that reaches one host and nothing else, a certificate the WIN owner accepts, a staging area where a file waits without being world-readable, and enough workers to finish the 16:00 batch without stretching into the next business date.

Two of the failure modes are pure infrastructure. A certificate that expires silently stops every dispatch, and the only symptom is a notice that never goes Sent. A staging area that fills or is misclassified as a log destination leaks the one artefact of this loop that carries an addressee and an address, so the area has to be private, sized and swept. Neither is visible from the application metrics alone, which is why the freshness signal of the WIN batch and the file-age signal are part of this story rather than a dashboard line in the deployment story.

This story creates no `rwb_*` table, no topic, no queue, no Schedule and no business value. It provisions and configures the runtime, the identity, the storage and the signals; the app story builds the workflow and the read, and the deployment story registers the Schedule, the consumer groups, the dashboards and the runbook.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template, the chart skeleton and the pipeline are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-LIB).
- The platform Blob account or object store, the platform key store and the workload identity mechanism of the platform are available (RWB-PLT-LIB), so no credential sits in a file, a chart or a repository.
- The Temporal workflow kit and the `rwb-recovery` namespace are available (RWB-PLT-WF, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON), and the KEDA scaler of the platform is available for the worker pools.
- The Kafka event platform, the schema registry and the observability stack are available (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-OBS, ADR-023).
- rwb-integration owns the file transport and its `outbound_item`; this story opens the path and provides the identity, and never builds the file.
- The WIN SFTP endpoint, the certificate subject, the certificate owner, the network zone, the storage container name and every size are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1102; ASM-2050).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Provision the workload identity of rwb-comms and the workload identity of rwb-integration for this exchange, each with the least grant it needs: read and write on the staging area for the exchange, read on the file store of the business date, and nothing else.
2. Open the egress path from the pods of both services to the WIN SFTP endpoint, on the reviewed port, one hop, with no broader internet egress, and record the allowed destinations as a reviewed list.
3. Provision the key-store entries: the SFTP client certificate and its private key reference, the host key of the WIN endpoint, the storage reference of the staging area and the Kafka and Temporal client material. No literal value reaches a values file, a chart template, a log or a ticket.
4. Provision the file landing and staging area for each environment: a private container with no anonymous access, the object layout by business date and interface, an immutability or versioning policy for the delivered copy, a retention period and a sweep that runs after the retention.
5. Size the staging area and the file store from the measured file size of the INT-14 batch and the INT-15 proof file, and record the figure as a reviewed value per environment.
6. Size the worker pools: a dispatch pool that carries the 16:00 burst of `NoticeDispatchWorkflow`, an ingest pool that carries the proof-of-delivery read and its retries, and a KEDA scaler that follows the queue depth of each pool, with the Temporal worker build ID pinned per release.
7. Expose the signals: the age of the newest delivered file per interface, the size and count of files in the staging area, the SFTP handshake result and its latency, the certificate expiry in days, the worker queue depth and the pod restarts of each pool.
8. Wire the freshness alert: the WIN batch is late when the freshness answer of the pod data product is not COMPLETE for the business date by the reviewed time, and the alert names the product, the business date, the last load date and the interface.
9. Hand the identity, the storage references and the signal names to RWB-P6-E1055-APP and RWB-P6-E1055-OPS; the app story builds the flow, the deployment story registers the Schedule, the consumer groups and the runbook.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The egress allow list is broader than one hop, or a destination outside it is reachable | The provisioning check fails the environment and the release is blocked | None | AC1 |
| X2 | The client certificate is missing, expired or not issued by the agreed authority | The handshake fails, the file is not delivered and the expiry alert fires before the expiry, not after | None | AC1, AC4 |
| X3 | The staging area allows anonymous access or is granted to a wider identity | The provisioning check fails and the environment is not marked ready | None | AC2 |
| X4 | The staging area passes its size or its object count | The staging alert fires and the sweep runs; the run is not blocked by a full area | None | AC2, AC6 |
| X5 | The dispatch burst outruns the worker pool | The queue depth alert fires and KEDA adds workers up to its cap; the run finishes inside the window or the cap is reviewed | None | AC3 |
| X6 | The WIN batch is not COMPLETE by the reviewed time | The freshness alert fires with the product, the business date and the last load date, and the runbook entry opens | MSG-P1-001 | AC6 |
| X7 | A secret, key or certificate body appears in a values file, a log or a ticket | The pipeline check fails the build and the credential is rotated | None | AC4 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Provisions network, identity, storage, scaling, secrets and signals; builds no application code and creates no business object |
| Negotiable | The host name, the port, the sizes, the retention and the alert time are environment values settled with the platform team |
| Valuable | Makes the WIN edge reachable and watchable at all, and unblocks the app and deployment stories on Day 1 |
| Estimable | One egress list, two identities, four key-store entries, one staging area, two worker pools, six signals and one alert |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the provisioning checks |
| Testable | Every criterion tests an artefact: a reachable host, a refused destination, a private container, an expiry alert, a scaled pool and a fired alert |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Infrastructure for the proof-of-delivery loop of rwb-comms

  Background:
    Given the platform object store, key store and service mesh are in force
    Given the target environment is SIT

  Scenario: AC1 The WIN file exchange reaches one host through one egress path (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the egress policy of the rwb-comms and rwb-integration pods
    When the allowed destinations and the handshake are inspected
    Then the WIN SFTP endpoint is allowed on the reviewed port and no other outside destination is reachable
    Then the handshake uses the client certificate from the key store and accepts only the host key recorded for the endpoint
    Then a destination outside the reviewed list is dropped, counted and alerted
    Then the host name, the port, the network zone and the certificate owner are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1102; ASM-2050)
    Then the provisioning check fails the environment when the path is broader than one hop

  Scenario: AC2 The file landing and staging area is private, sized and swept (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the staging area of the environment and the delivered-file store of the business date
    When their access level, layout, retention and size are inspected
    Then neither has anonymous or public access, and each is reachable only by the two workload identities of this exchange
    Then the object layout is by business date and by interface, so the file of a date is found without a search
    Then the delivered copy is kept under an immutability or versioning policy for the reviewed retention period, and the sweep runs after it
    Then the size and the object count are reviewed values per environment and are not a template constant
    Then the container name, the retention period and the sizes are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1102; ASM-2050)

  Scenario: AC3 The dispatch and ingest worker pools scale on their queue depth (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the two worker pools and their KEDA scalers
    When the 16:00 burst of NoticeDispatchWorkflow and a proof-of-delivery ingest are replayed
    Then the dispatch pool scales out on the queue depth of rwb-comms up to its reviewed cap and finishes inside the file window
    Then the ingest pool scales on its own queue depth and does not consume the dispatch capacity
    Then each worker polls its own task queue in namespace rwb-recovery with the build ID of the release
    Then no replica count, resource size or scaler threshold is hard-coded in a template
    Then the pool sizes and the scaler caps are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1102; ASM-2050)

  Scenario: AC4 Every credential comes from the key store and is rotated without a rebuild (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the key-store entries of the environment
    When the service reads them at run time
    Then the SFTP client certificate and key, the host key, the storage reference, the Kafka credential and the Temporal mTLS material are read by the workload identity and never from a file or a chart value
    Then no secret, key or certificate body appears in a values file, a log, a dashboard or a ticket
    Then the certificate expiry is a monitored signal in days, with an alert before the expiry
    Then rotating the certificate or the key is a key-store operation with no rebuild of the service and no chart change

  Scenario: AC5 The dispatch files of a business date are stored and addressable (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the file store of the service and the outbound item of rwb-integration
    When the files of a business date are listed
    Then the INT-14 file of the date is addressable by its file ID and its business date, and the address is what the outbound item carries
    Then the stored file is private, encrypted at rest and in transit, and no copy is written to a log or to a temporary public path
    Then the retention of the stored file follows the reviewed retention and the sweep does not delete a file that is under review
    Then the storage names, the retention and the encryption mechanism are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1102; ASM-2050)

  Scenario: AC6 A late WIN batch is visible on the freshness signal (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the six signals of this story and the freshness alert
    When the batch of source WIN is not COMPLETE for the business date by the reviewed time
    Then the freshness alert fires with the product, the business date, the last load date and the interface, using MSG-P1-001 as its message
    Then the file-age signal, the staging signal, the handshake signal, the expiry signal and the queue-depth signal are each published with the environment and the business date
    Then no signal or alert payload carries a name, an address, an identity number or a contact value
    Then the alert time and its threshold are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1102; ASM-2050)
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One service, one login: the runtime uses the rwb-comms login for the service and the rwb-integration identity for the file transport, and no other service's credential | DP-02; Architecture v5 slide 29 |
| BR2 | The WIN endpoint is reached one hop from the pods, on the reviewed port, and nothing outside the reviewed list is reachable | DP-11; ADR-020 |
| BR3 | Every secret and every certificate comes from the key store through the workload identity; none appears in a file, a chart, a log or a ticket | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17; NFR-052 |
| BR4 | The staging area is private, laid out by business date and interface, and swept after its retention; a file that carries an addressee and an address never sits in a public or shared location | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17; legacy section 17 |
| BR5 | No replica count, resource size, scaler threshold or alert value is hard-coded; all come from values files or the key store | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR6 | The file store carries the delivered file of the business date and its identifier, and the identifier is the one `outbound_item` records | DP-01; TSD P6 T3.3 (`dispatch_file_id` to `outbound_item`) |
| BR7 | The batch of source WIN is read only when it is COMPLETE for its business date, and a late batch is signalled with MSG-P1-001 | legacy BR4 and BR7; MSG-P1-001 |
| BR8 | This story creates no `rwb_*` table, no topic, no queue, no Schedule and no business object; identity, storage, network and signals are the whole deliverable | Template and Rules §R7.2 s12 |
| R-LIT-07 | The delivery date drives the notice period, so a late WIN batch delays a legal clock; the freshness signal is therefore an operational control and not a report | Temporal and Drools design slide 20 notes |
| R-UNI-33 | A downstream endpoint that fails is retried, and the state does not advance until the retry succeeds; the retry policy is a values entry, not code | INT-14 error handling |
| R-UNI-34 | A retried delivery that passes its limit leaves the file in the exception path with its reason, and the operator sees it on the file-age and staging signals | INT-14 error handling |
| REQ-DRI-006 | No direct call to a system of record from a business component; the file moves only through rwb-integration, and this story opens the path it uses | REQ-DRI-006; DP-16 |

##### 9. State transitions

The infrastructure of one environment moves through these states; no business object moves.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not provisioned | Identity, key-store entries and egress path created | The two identities hold their least grant and one host is reachable | Provisioned |
| Provisioned | Staging area and file store created | Private access, layout, retention and sweep in place | Active |
| Active | Provisioning check fails after a platform change | A grant widens, a destination opens or the access level drifts | Degraded; the environment is not marked ready |
| Active | Certificate rotated | The key-store entry is updated and the pod reloads it | Active with the new certificate |
| Active | Certificate nears its expiry | The expiry signal passes its value | Alerted; rotation is due |
| Active | Staging area passes its size or count | The sweep runs and the alert fires | Active after the sweep |
| Degraded | Rollback of the platform change | The reviewed grant, destination and access level are restored | Active |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| SCB IT infrastructure | Owns the egress path, the identities and their grants, the staging area, the file store, the sizing and the signals |
| ACE platform team | Owns the object store, the key store, the certificate authority, the KEDA scaler and the service mesh this story configures against |
| Security | Approves the identity grant, the certificate subject, the key-store entries and the network allow list |
| The rwb-comms and rwb-integration owner teams | Confirm the sizing and the file window after the burst test and consume the identity and the storage |
| Platform administrator | Rotates the certificate, extends the retention when the audit requirement changes, and acts on the freshness alert |
| ACE database administrator | Confirms that no database object is created by this story, since it creates none |

The identity names, the key-store entry names, the certificate subject and the host name are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1102; ASM-2050); this story fixes their shape and leaves the names to the environment configuration.

##### 11. Data

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Identities | The rwb-comms workload identity and the rwb-integration identity for the exchange, each with read and write on the staging area and read on the file store, and nothing else |
| Key-store entries | The SFTP client certificate and its key reference, the WIN host key, the storage reference, the Kafka credential and the Temporal mTLS material |
| Staging area | Private container, layout by business date and interface, retention and sweep, reviewed size and object count |
| File store | The delivered file of the business date, addressable by file ID and business date, private and encrypted |
| Egress list | The WIN SFTP endpoint on the reviewed port; no other outside destination |
| Worker pools | A dispatch pool and an ingest pool, each with its KEDA scaler, its queue and its reviewed cap |
| Signals | File age per interface, staging size and count, handshake result and latency, certificate expiry in days, queue depth, pod restarts of each pool |
| Alert | The freshness alert of the WIN batch, with MSG-P1-001 as its message |

The host, the port, the zone, the container names, the retention, the sizes and the alert time are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1102; ASM-2050); they are reviewed values per environment and are recorded here as assumptions, not as business values. The staging area and the file store hold letter files, which are business documents and may carry an addressee and an address: they are private, encrypted and never copied into a log, a ticket or a test fixture, and every test file is synthetic.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. This story exposes no API, no operator endpoint and no cache read. The readiness and liveness endpoints are cluster-internal and are owned by RWB-P6-E1055-OPS.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. The one-hop path that carries the rwb-comms calls to rwb-source-data and rwb-document is a platform route it sits on; the operations themselves are consumed by RWB-P6-E1055-APP and declared in RWB-P6-E1055-CON. This story adds no call of its own.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The story provisions no topic and publishes no event; the two events of the loop are RWB-P6-E1055-APP's and their envelopes are RWB-P6-E1055-CON's.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The three consumer groups of the service are provisioned by RWB-P6-E1055-OPS; this story only ensures the platform routes and the signals that their failure would show.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. No workflow, activity or task queue is created here. The worker pools this story sizes poll `rwb-comms` and the queue of the integration activity, and the workflow definition itself belongs to RWB-P6-E1055-APP.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The 16:00 dispatch Schedule is registered by RWB-P6-E1055-OPS against the workflow kit, and the cross-system edge is the bank Airflow file window (Architecture v5 slide 44). This story opens the network and the storage that the Schedule's workers need and registers no Schedule.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. This story creates no `rwb_*` table, no column and no index; the objects it provisions are a container, key-store entries, a network policy and a scaler, none of which is an ACE DB table. The `notice` columns of this loop arrive in the service's own Flyway sequence through RWB-P6-E1055-APP (DP-15).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

None. The fakes run in the pipeline and in SIT and belong to RWB-P6-E1055-CON and RWB-P6-E1055-OPS; no fake is deployed or configured here. The WIN edge stub of SIT is a test folder and a test acknowledgment record on a synthetic fixture, and this story provisions it as a test-only destination outside the production allow list.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | None | No operation is provided or consumed by this story |
| Kafka | None | No topic, no producer, no consumer |
| Temporal | None | No workflow, activity or Schedule; the worker pools it sizes serve the app story's workflow |
| File | 1 dotted grey path | P6 builds the INT-14 file, P2 delivers it to the WIN edge, the INT-15 proof file returns through ACE and rwb-source-data; this story provides the staging area, the file store, the identity and the egress for that path |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** `infra/network/win-egress.yaml` (the one-hop allow list and the drop rule), `infra/identity/rwb-comms-workload.json` (the two identities and their least grants), `infra/keyvault/entries.md` (the certificate, the host key and the storage references), `infra/storage/staging.json` (the staging area, its layout, retention, sweep and sizes), `infra/storage/file-store.json` (the delivered-file store of the business date), `infra/sizing/workers.yaml` (the two pools and their scalers) and `infra/observability/signals.md` (the six signals and the freshness alert).

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-18 | Interaction ledger | Ledger owned by rwb-source-data | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-11 is served by the one-hop egress list: the pods of the two services reach the WIN endpoint, the owners' contracts and their own storage endpoint, and nothing else. DP-05 is a prohibition here and DP-18 and DP-19 add no work. The platform H rows are delivered by the platform waves and are not repeated in the metadata H field, which stays empty.

**Build steps**

1. Create the egress allow list and the drop rule; test an allowed handshake and a dropped destination (AC1, X1).
2. Create the two identities and their least grants; test that a write outside the staging area and a read outside the file store are refused (AC2, X3).
3. Create the key-store entries; test the handshake with a valid, an expired and an unissued certificate, and the expiry signal (AC4, X2).
4. Create the staging area and the file store with their layout, retention and sweep; test privacy, the address of a file and the sweep (AC2, AC5).
5. Run the burst test of the dispatch pool and the ingest test of the second pool; record the sizes and the caps per environment (AC3, X5).
6. Publish the six signals and the freshness alert; replay a late WIN batch and a failed handshake and confirm each fires (AC6, X6).
7. Hand the identity, the storage references and the signal names to the app and deployment stories.

**Done when.** The egress list is one hop in all three environments, a destination outside it is dropped, the staging area and the file store are private and swept, the handshake succeeds only with the issued certificate, the burst test finishes inside the file window with the reviewed caps, and the freshness alert fires on a late batch with MSG-P1-001.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-001 | The WIN batch is late or not COMPLETE for the business date | {product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived. |
| None | A policy, identity, certificate or sizing check fails | No business message is produced. The provisioning check fails the environment with the resource name and the violated rule, and the platform administrator acts on it. |

This story adds no message ID. The freshness alert carries MSG-P1-001 with the text of the legacy story, unchanged, and the product and date values the freshness answer holds. Every other condition is reported to the operator as a provisioning or signal condition, never to a Workbench user, and the platform administrator is the owner of the action in each case.

##### 15. Screens and states

None. There is no screen in this story. The operator-facing surfaces are the provisioning check, the container and key-store policy views, the burst-test report and the six signals; SCR-44 Interface and job monitor and SCR-45 Data quality show the effects on the screens the deployment story serves (DP-19), and no screen is built or changed here.

The twelve are the legacy test cases of RWB-E1-055 in their legacy order, with the Level column added; System maps to End to end and Access to Component. The provisioning checks of this story are named in section 13 and carry their own identifiers, because they test an environment and not a business case.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a policy or a values file: the eligible state, the attempt limit, the break days, the stale period and the list values stay reference data of their owner, never a deployment value.
- No personal data in a container name, an object path, a signal or a log: the file store addresses a file by interface and business date, and no name, address, identity number or contact value is written there.
- One login per service; the runtime carries the rwb-comms login reference and the rwb-integration identity for the exchange, and no other service's credential (DP-02).
- The staging area and the file store are private and encrypted; no file that carries an addressee or an address is copied into a log, a ticket or a shared location.
- Every secret and every certificate comes from the key store through the workload identity; no value sits in a chart, a values file or a repository (NFR-052).
- The egress list is one hop and is reviewed; a destination outside it is dropped, counted and alerted (DP-11).
- The service writes only its own schema; this story writes none, and no signal query reads another service's schema or an ACE view (DP-01, DP-05).
- Files move only through rwb-integration: no component of this story calls WIN, and the test folder of SIT is outside the production allow list (REQ-DRI-006).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-055 for rwb-comms (OPS). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform engineer**, I want **the proof-of-delivery loop of rwb-comms deployed from the service template with its chart, its values files and its own login, the Temporal worker deployment that polls `rwb-comms` for `NoticeDispatchWorkflow`, the 16:00 Schedule registered against the workflow kit with the JOB-10 Airflow file-window handoff, the JOB-11 outbox relay, the dashboards and alerts for a missing proof-of-delivery batch and a failed file, a runbook for a re-run of the dispatch and of the pod read, a smoke profile against the four contract fakes, and the feature flags with their rollback**, so that **an operator can see within minutes that a notice will not be dispatched or that a delivery will not land, and repair it inside the business day without reading code or waiting for a business report**.

This story deploys an existing capability. It adds no topic, builds no endpoint, table or workflow and writes no notice: the run is `NoticeDispatchWorkflow` on queue `rwb-comms`, the file moves through rwb-integration, the pod is rwb-source-data's and the timer is rwb-case's.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy capability leaned on a Quartz job whose only failure signal was a job exception, so a file that was never delivered and a pod batch that was never ingested looked the same as a quiet night. In the target the run is a workflow with a Schedule (DP-10), the cross-system edge is the bank Airflow file window (Architecture v5 slide 44, JOB-10 "Airflow file window + workers"), and the delivery facts arrive as events (DP-09). There is no scheduler row to be late and no job record to inspect, so the operational signal has to move from "did the job run" to "is the file of the day delivered, is the pod of the date COMPLETE, is the outbox moving, and is the workflow stuck".

Two properties of this loop make deployment part of the capability. First, its failure is silent for the officer: a notice stays Generated and looks like a notice that nobody dispatched, so the missing-file and missing-batch alerts have to be built here or nobody will raise them. Second, its clock is legal: a delivered notice starts the notice period (R-LIT-07), so a pod batch that is one business day late delays a legal clock, and the freshness signal with MSG-P1-001 is a control rather than a report.

Deployment is otherwise the standard shape: the chart carries the rwb-comms login and no other credential (DP-02), the migration job runs the per-service Flyway sequence in schema `rwb_comms` (DP-15), the consumer groups of the three consumed events are provisioned with retry and `.dlt` paths (DP-09), the outbox relay runs every minute (JOB-11), and the runbook names the four failures an operator will actually see.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template, the chart skeleton and the pipeline are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-LIB).
- The Temporal workflow kit and the `rwb-recovery` namespace are available (RWB-PLT-WF, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON), so the worker polls `rwb-comms` and the Schedule runs in every environment.
- The Kafka event platform provisions topics with a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON), and `rwb.comms.events.v1`, `rwb.case.events.v1` and `rwb.deviation.events.v1` are provisioned by their owners.
- The observability stack of the platform is available (RWB-PLT-OBS, ADR-023): metrics, traces and logs with one trace across REST, Kafka, Temporal and the file step.
- The three environments DEV, SIT and UAT exist with their parameter scope and their Kafka, Temporal and object-store endpoints.
- RWB-P6-E1055-CON is published, so the smoke profile runs against the two operations and the four fakes of that baseline.
- RWB-P6-E1055-INF has provisioned the egress path, the identities, the key-store entries, the staging area, the file store and the worker sizing.
- The dispatch Schedule expression and the deployment slot of the service are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1103; ASM-2051), and the alert values are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1104; ASM-2052).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. The pipeline builds one image and one chart version from the same commit, runs the unit, component and contract tests, scans the image and the dependencies, and publishes the chart.
2. The chart deploys rwb-comms with the rwb-comms login, the pre-deploy migration job for schema `rwb_comms`, the readiness and liveness probes, the api deployment and the worker deployment that polls `rwb-comms`.
3. The Schedule registration step registers the 16:00 dispatch Schedule against the workflow kit, with overlap SKIP and the catch-up window of the kit, and asserts that `NoticeDispatchWorkflow` is what it starts.
4. The same step records the JOB-10 handoff: the bank Airflow file window opens the edge for the business date and the in-service Schedule starts the workflow, with no Quartz row, no shared job table entry and no Control-M job anywhere in the release.
5. The provisioning step declares the consumer group `rwb-comms` for `rwb.case.events.v1` and `rwb.deviation.events.v1`, each with its retry topic and its `.dlt` topic, and reuses `rwb.comms.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1` as their owners provision them.
6. The outbox relay is deployed as the platform standard of JOB-11: every minute, one relay per service, with its lag and its dead-letter count exposed.
7. The dashboards are published: the file of the business date by state, the age of the newest delivered file, the pod batch state of the date, the dispatch and delivery counts, the outbox lag, the workflow open, stuck and failed count, the refusal rate and the SFTP handshake result.
8. The alerts are wired to MSG-P1-001, MSG-GEN-006, MSG-P6-004 and MSG-P4-002 where the condition maps to one, and each alert links exactly one runbook entry.
9. A smoke step runs the loop against the four fakes in SIT: one file for 2026-11-25, one acknowledgment, one Sent notice, one pod batch, one Delivered notice and one unacknowledged run that raises the task.
10. The runbook is published and reviewed with the on-call rota: a missing proof-of-delivery batch, a failed file, a dispatch run that must be re-run, a stuck workflow and an outbox relay that stopped.
11. The feature flags are set per environment and the rollback path is rehearsed once in UAT.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The migration job fails | The deployment stays unready and the pipeline stops; no traffic reaches the new version | None | AC1 |
| X2 | The worker is deployed with the wrong build ID | The Schedule starts a workflow no worker serves; the stuck-workflow alert fires and the release is rolled back | None | AC1, AC7 |
| X3 | The Schedule is registered twice, or with overlap ALLOW | The registration check fails the release; the duplicate is removed before promotion | None | AC2 |
| X4 | The file of the business date is not delivered by the reviewed time | The missing-file alert fires with MSG-GEN-006 and the failed-file runbook entry opens | MSG-GEN-006 | AC4, AC5 |
| X5 | The pod batch of the date is not COMPLETE | The freshness alert fires with MSG-P1-001 and the missing-batch runbook entry opens | MSG-P1-001 | AC4, AC5 |
| X6 | The outbox relay stops or its lag passes its value | The relay alert fires and the relay runbook entry restarts the relay and replays the topic | None | AC3, AC4 |
| X7 | A workflow stops on a non-retryable failure | The stuck workflow scan of JOB-21 raises the case and the stuck-workflow runbook entry starts from the history | None | AC4, AC5 |
| X8 | A role without the Litigation right is refused | The refusal is counted on the dashboard and no page is sent | MSG-P4-002 | AC4 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the chart skeleton, the Schedule registration, the topic provisioning and the observability stack; builds no application code |
| Negotiable | Replica counts, resource sizes, alert thresholds, the Schedule slot and the retention are environment values, not story decisions |
| Valuable | Makes a loop with no job record observable: the file, the batch, the relay and the workflow each have a signal, an owner and a runbook entry |
| Estimable | One chart, one Schedule registration, one provisioning step, one relay, eight panels, six alerts, five runbook entries and one smoke profile |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the runbook and the smoke profile |
| Testable | Every criterion tests an artefact: the chart renders, the Schedule exists once, an alert fires on a synthetic metric, a runbook entry resolves, the smoke profile passes |

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One service, one schema, one login: the release uses the rwb-comms login and no other service's credential | DP-02; Architecture v5 slide 29 |
| BR2 | The migration is a per-service Flyway sequence in schema `rwb_comms` and runs before the deployment is ready | DP-15; RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| BR3 | Every subscription has a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic, and a consumer never acknowledges an event it could not process | DP-09; Architecture v5 slide 22 notes |
| BR4 | The outbox relay runs every minute and is the platform standard of JOB-11; it is not rebuilt per story | Architecture v5 slide 44; DP-09 |
| BR5 | JOB-10 is the bank Airflow file window plus the dispatch Schedule and workers of this service; no Quartz row and no Control-M job is registered | DP-10; Architecture v5 slide 44 |
| BR6 | No environment value is hard-coded: replica counts, resource sizes, timeouts, thresholds and the Schedule state come from values files | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR7 | An alert carries a message ID and the agreed text, and links exactly one runbook entry | Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR8 | A refused read is counted and never pages the on-call rota | MSG-P4-002 |
| BR9 | A re-run of a business date never writes a notice into a second file and never re-sends an acknowledged notice | legacy AC8; DP-10 |
| BR10 | No dashboard series, log line or alert payload carries personal data; notice IDs, case IDs, the barcode, counts and durations only | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| R-LIT-07 | The delivery date starts the notice period, so a missing pod batch delays a legal clock and is an alert, not a report | Temporal and Drools design slide 20 notes |
| R-UNI-33 | A failed delivery is retried and the notice does not advance until the retry succeeds; the retry interval is a values entry | INT-14 error handling |
| R-UNI-34 | A delivery that passes its retry limit leaves the file in the exception path with its reason, and the operator sees it on the file-age and file-state panels | INT-14 error handling |
| R-UNI-40 | A repeated event or a repeated pod row produces one effect, and the repeat is counted; the re-run entry is written so it cannot break this | legacy BR6 |

##### 9. State transitions

The release and the Schedule move through these states; no business object moves.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | Chart published | The image, the chart and the migration job pass the pipeline | Deploying |
| Deploying | Migration complete and probes healthy | The schema is at the expected version, the relay runs and the worker polls `rwb-comms` | Ready |
| Ready | Schedule registered | Exactly one Schedule exists and the window handoff is recorded | Armed |
| Armed | Release superseded | A new chart version is promoted | Rolling |
| Rolling | All pods on the new version | The old ReplicaSet drains and the worker build ID is the new one | Armed |
| Armed | Alert on a missing file, a missing batch or a stuck workflow | The condition passes its value | Alerted; the runbook entry opens |
| Alerted | Re-run of the business date, or the owner's repair | The file or the batch is delivered and the notice state is what the run wrote | Armed |
| Armed | Rollback | The previous chart version and the previous flag state are restored | Armed on the previous version |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| DevOps engineer | Owns the chart, the values files, the pipeline stages, the Schedule registration, the dashboards, the alerts and the runbook |
| Platform administrator | Owns the `rwb-recovery` namespace, the topic provisioning, the visibility queries behind JOB-21 and the re-run of a job on SCR-44 |
| ACE database administrator | Owns schema `rwb_comms`, the login and its grants, and approves the migration job |
| Release manager | Approves the promotion of one artefact through the environments and the rollback |
| On-call operator | Runs the runbook entries and opens an incident when a missing batch or a failed file persists |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Reruns the dispatch run from SCR-44 and reads the REC-05 break on SCR-45 in the running service, not in the cluster |
| Service owners of rwb-integration, rwb-source-data and rwb-case | Are paged by the file, batch and workflow alerts and own the repair beyond the rwb-comms breaker |

The per-service login used by the chart is a secret reference resolved at deploy time; the chart references "the rwb-comms login (DP-02)" and never a literal name. The deployment slot and the namespace assignment of the service are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1103; ASM-2051).

| Topics | `rwb.comms.events.v1` carries the two events with retry and `.dlt`; `rwb.case.events.v1` and `rwb.deviation.events.v1` are consumed with retry and `.dlt`; `rwb.decision-record.v1` is reused as its owner provisions it |
| Queue | Temporal task queue `rwb-comms` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, and the `rwb-integration` queue of the `deliverFile` activity |
| Schedule | One dispatch Schedule at 16:00 Asia/Bangkok, overlap SKIP, with the catch-up window of the kit |
| Dashboard series | File of the date by state, age of the newest delivered file, pod batch state of the date, dispatch count, delivery count, outbox lag, workflow open, stuck and failed, refusal rate, SFTP handshake result |
| Runbook entries | Missing batch, failed file, dispatch re-run, stuck workflow, outbox relay stopped |
| Secrets | The rwb-comms login secret, the SFTP client certificate reference, the Kafka client credential and the Temporal mTLS material, all from the platform key store |

The alert thresholds and the reviewed time of the late batch are deployment values; their provisional values are carried by the gap and the assumption of section 14 (GAP-1104; ASM-2052). The exact cluster topology, node pools, replica counts and probe timings are deployment values of the platform chart and are not fixed here.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The deployment exposes the operations of RWB-P6-E1055-CON behind gateway-bff: `GET /api/recovery/comms/v1/notices/{noticeId}` and the internal digest write. The probes are cluster-internal and are not part of the API surface, and this story adds no path.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. The deployment configures the client timeouts and the breakers of the consumed rows declared in RWB-P6-E1055-CON and adds no call of its own.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The two events are RWB-P6-E1055-APP's; the deployment reuses `rwb.comms.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics as provisioned by its owner and creates no topic.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None declared. The consumer groups of the three consumed events are provisioned in the step of section 13 and described in AC3, and their shapes belong to RWB-P6-E1055-CON.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Deployment element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NoticeDispatchWorkflow` | Workflow, one per business date and dispatch run | `rwb-comms` | Worker deployment with the build ID of the release; holds the dispatch run, the acknowledgment wait and the two events |
| `generateLetter` | Activity, P6 | `rwb-comms` | Registered by the same worker |
| `approveNotice` | Child workflow in rwb-decision | `rwb-decision` | Reached through the platform namespace; no worker of this release serves it |
| `deliverFile` | Activity, P2 | `rwb-integration` | Served by the rwb-integration worker; the deployment asserts the queue exists and is served |

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Schedule | Cron | Overlap | Handoff |
|---|---|---|---|
| The dispatch Schedule of rwb-comms (RWB-PLT-E1071-CON) | 16:00 Asia/Bangkok, daily | SKIP, with the catch-up window of the kit | The bank Airflow file window opens the WIN edge for the business date (JOB-10); the Schedule starts `NoticeDispatchWorkflow`, which requests the file through rwb-integration |

Exactly one Schedule is registered per environment, and no Quartz row, shared job table entry or Control-M job is created. The deployment slot and the namespace assignment are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1103; ASM-2051).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The migration job creates and migrates the tables of RWB-P6-E1052-APP and RWB-P6-E1046-APP in schema `rwb_comms` and the dispatch columns of RWB-P6-E1055-APP; this story owns no table and adds no column. `document`, `interaction`, `recovery_case`, `timer` and `outbound_item` belong to their services and the migration job touches schema `rwb_comms` only (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

None. The fakes are test-only workloads of RWB-P6-E1055-CON; the SIT smoke profile of AC6 runs against them and they are not deployed into UAT or production.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | None | No operation is provided or consumed by the deployment itself |
| Kafka | None | No topic is created; the two events and the three consumed events ride their owners' topics with retry and `.dlt` |
| Temporal | 1 workflow, 1 Schedule | `NoticeDispatchWorkflow` on `rwb-comms`, with the `generateLetter` activity registered by the same worker and the 16:00 Schedule registered once per environment |
| File | 1 dotted grey path | The INT-14 file of the business date through rwb-integration to the WIN edge, and the INT-15 proof file back through ACE and rwb-source-data; the smoke profile asserts the outbound path against the fake |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Artefacts**

| Artefact | Content |
|---|---|
| `helm/rwb-comms/` | Chart with api and worker deployments, service, migration job, config map, secret references, probes and the Schedule registration hook |
| `helm/rwb-comms/values-dev.yaml`, `values-sit.yaml`, `values-uat.yaml` | Image digest, replicas, resources, probe timings, log level, `rwb.comms.win-dispatch-v1`, the Schedule state, the two client timeouts, the alert thresholds |
| Pipeline stage | Build, unit, component and contract tests, the retired-element check, image and dependency scan, chart publish, one artefact promoted through the environments |
| Schedule registration step | Exactly one dispatch Schedule, its cron, its overlap and its catch-up, plus the recorded JOB-10 window handoff |
| Provisioning step | Consumer group `rwb-comms` on `rwb.case.events.v1` and `rwb.deviation.events.v1` with retry and `.dlt`; reuse of `rwb.comms.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1`; task queue `rwb-comms` in namespace `rwb-recovery` |
| Outbox relay | The platform standard of JOB-11, one relay per service, with lag and dead-letter series |
| Dashboards | Eight panels: file by state, file age, batch state, dispatch count, delivery count, outbox lag, workflow health, refusal rate |
| Alerts | Six rules, each with a message ID where one maps, and one runbook entry |
| Runbook | Five entries: missing batch, failed file, dispatch re-run, stuck workflow, outbox relay stopped |
| Smoke profile | The SIT run of AC6 against the four fakes |

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-18 | Interaction ledger | Ledger owned by rwb-source-data | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The platform H rows are delivered by the platform waves and are not repeated in the metadata H field, which stays empty. DP-10 is the pattern this story serves: the Schedule registration and the worker deployment are the operational form of "no shared Quartz". DP-05 and DP-18 add no work here.

**Probes.** Readiness answers healthy only when the migration is at the expected schema version, the outbox relay is running and the Temporal worker on `rwb-comms` has polled; liveness answers healthy when the process is up and its internal loop is responsive. Neither probe writes to the database and neither calls another service.

**Alert mapping.**

| Message ID | Condition | Alert | Route |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-006 | The file of the business date is not delivered by the reviewed time, or the SFTP handshake fails | Missing-file alert with the interface, the business date and the attempt count | Platform on-call, page; ticket to the rwb-integration owner |
| MSG-P1-001 | The pod batch of the date is not COMPLETE by the reviewed time, or is FAILED at its record count check | Missing-batch or failed-batch alert with the product, the business date and the last load date | Platform on-call, page; ticket to the rwb-source-data owner |
| MSG-P6-004 | The dispatch count of the date is zero inside the window while notices are eligible | Dispatch-count alert with the eligible count and the workflow state | Platform on-call, page |
| MSG-P4-002 | A read without the Litigation right is refused | Refusal count on the dashboard | No page |
| None | The outbox lag passes its value, or the dead-letter count rises | Relay alert with the lag and the oldest row | Platform on-call, page |
| None | The stuck workflow scan of JOB-21 raises a `rwb-comms` workflow | Stuck-workflow alert with the workflow ID, the business date and the last event | Platform on-call, page |

Every alert carries its message ID where the condition maps to one, and the two conditions without one carry the series or the workflow name instead. The thresholds and the reviewed time are deployment values with provisional defaults; the missing source is carried by the gap and the assumption of section 14 (GAP-1104; ASM-2052).

**Done when.** The chart renders in all three environments, the pipeline promotes one artefact and fails on a fake drift, exactly one Schedule exists in each environment, the consumer groups exist with their retry and `.dlt` paths, the eight panels carry the synthetic day, the six alert conditions fire on synthetic metrics, the five runbook entries are reviewed by the on-call rota and the smoke profile of AC6 passes in SIT.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P6-004 | A notice is acknowledged by WIN | {notice} was sent for registered mail on {date}. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | WIN has not acknowledged after the third attempt, or the file of the date is not delivered | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The WIN batch is late or not COMPLETE | {product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A read without the Litigation right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The message texts are the legacy wording of RWB-E1-055, copied unchanged, and the deployment adds the routing, the threshold and the runbook link, never a new wording. The alert values and the reviewed time of the late batch are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1104; ASM-2052).

##### 15. Screens and states

The deployment serves SCR-44 Interface and job monitor and SCR-45 Data quality for this capability behind the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19): SCR-44 shows the dispatch run and the pod read in the states Running; failed; complete, with the file ID and the attempt count, and SCR-45 shows the held row with check `References` and the REC-05 break in state breaks. The operator-facing surfaces of this story are the pipeline run view, the release view, the Schedule view, the eight panels and the runbook; the smoke step opens the notice of a synthetic case in SIT and asserts that the dispatch and proof fields answer inside the 2 s budget.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a values file: the eligible state, the attempt limit, the break days, the stale period and the list values stay reference data held by their owner, never a deployment value.
- No personal data in logs, dashboard series, alert payloads or the runbook: notice IDs, case IDs, the barcode, counts, durations and file IDs only.
- One login per service; the chart carries the rwb-comms login reference and no other service's credential (DP-02).
- The service writes only schema `rwb_comms`; the migration job never touches another schema and no dashboard query reads one (DP-01).
- Every subscription has a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic, and the consumer dedupes through the inbox (DP-09).
- No new topic and no Quartz row: the capability reuses its owner's topics and the run is a Temporal Schedule with the Airflow window as the edge (DP-10, DP-14).
- ACE data is read only through the owner's contract; no dashboard reads an ACE view or another service's schema (DP-05).
- The release pins the image digest and the chart version, and no secret is written into a values file, a chart template, a dashboard or the runbook.
- A refused read is not an incident: it is counted and it never pages the on-call rota (BR8).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: integration slice of RWB-E1-055 for RWB-ITG-W1. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **QA integration engineer on the wave 1 release**, I want **JOB-10 WIN dispatch and the whole proof-of-delivery capture proved end to end on the real wave-1 SIT services before wave 1 exits — the 16:00 file through rwb-integration to the stubbed WIN edge, the acknowledgment that makes the notice Sent, the INT-15 proof file that ACE ingests and rwb-source-data serves, the Delivered notice and its ledger entry, and the NOTICE_PERIOD timer that rwb-case starts from the delivery date**, so that **a notice period is never counted from the print date, no notice is sent twice into a second file, and every freshness, held-row and reconciliation break of the loop is evidenced on the owners' published contracts rather than found in production**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Proof of delivery is chased by phone today, and a notice period counted from the print date can be challenged in court. The legacy story fixed one loop for that: a daily 16:00 file to WIN, an acknowledgment that sets the notice Sent, a weekly proof file that ACE ingests and the Workbench reads back, a delivery fact on the notice, a ledger entry, and a notice period that starts on the delivery date. In the target that loop is no longer one process over one schema. rwb-comms owns the notice and the dispatch workflow, rwb-integration owns the file and executes `deliverFile` on queue `rwb-integration`, rwb-document holds the letter behind a document ID, rwb-source-data is the single reader of the `recovery.v_ace_*` views and the single owner of the pod, freshness and interaction facts, and rwb-case owns the NOTICE_PERIOD timer that starts on the event (DP-01, DP-05, DP-09, DP-10, DP-15, DP-18).

Every one of those edges fails in a way no single-service suite can see: a notice that stays Sent because the acknowledgment landed on the wrong base, a second file built for one rerun, a pod row read while the ACE batch for the date is not COMPLETE, two deliveries for one pod row, a timer started on the sent date, or a held row that nobody lists. This story is the end-to-end proof of the loop on the wave-1 services, and it is the evidence the wave 1 exit check reads.

It serves REQ-OCC-003, REQ-ILG-004 and REQ-DRI-006, it carries CTL-15 and the reconciliation rule REC-05 into evidence, and it holds the FSD P6 measure "notices with proof of delivery, 100 percent". It exercises the loop the way the services are built: every read is one hop on the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget (DP-11, DP-13), the dispatch and delivery facts are consumed as Kafka events from the owner's topic and deduped through the inbox (DP-09), reference data such as the notice type and template version is read through the owning contract (DP-07), the ledger is rwb-source-data's and never a table (DP-18), the 16:00 run is the Airflow file window plus the P6 workflow rather than a Quartz row (DP-10), and the job and data-quality surfaces are reached through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The suite provides no REST operation, publishes no event and owns no table.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P6-E1055-APP is done in SIT: rwb-comms holds the notice state, dispatch_file_id, dispatch_attempts and the WIN acknowledgment handling, publishes `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1` and `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1` on `rwb.comms.events.v1`, and serves `GET /api/recovery/comms/v1/notices/{noticeId}`.
- RWB-P3-E1055-APP is done: rwb-case consumes `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1` through its inbox and starts the NOTICE_PERIOD timer from the delivered date, and serves `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers`.
- RWB-P1-E1055-APP is done: rwb-source-data serves the pod records and the freshness stamp of the WIN proof-of-delivery data product, and holds the pod read behind the ACE batch completeness check.
- RWB-P1-E1066-APP is done: the interaction ledger is written and read on `POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions`, and the data-quality exceptions are listed on `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/data-quality/exceptions`.
- RWB-P3-E1028-APP is done: the NOTICE_PERIOD timer type exists in rwb-case and is visible through the timers read.
- RWB-P5-E1054-APP and RWB-P5-E1055-APP are done: rwb-document stores the WIN letter generated for the notice and returns the document ID, readable with `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}`.
- The P6 contract is published, and the seven integration dependencies above are the real services in SIT; this story builds against no contract and waits for none.
- The dispatch-eligible notice states are set to GENERATED and the attempt limit to 3 in the owning configuration; both are data in the P6 configuration and are read, never set, by this story.
- The external boundary is the stubbed WIN folder and acknowledgment at the P2 edge. The folder layout, the acknowledgment file naming and its record keys are harness configuration; they follow the WIN INT-14 and INT-15 contract and are named in the run report.
- The SIT fixture set of section 13 is loaded: case `RC-2026-000123`, notices `N-0001` and `N-0002` in state Generated with notice type DEMAND and primary account contract CT-77001, the WIN owner's sample file `WIN-POD-SAMPLE-v1` of 25 records, the 30-row pod batch of 2026-11-30 with one unknown row, and the second pod row of 2026-11-28.
- The run uses the per-service logins of the wave-1 services (DP-15); no service login is shared and the suite holds no grant on any `rwb_*` schema.
- No build dependency and no contract dependency: Day 1, against the real services as soon as the seven APP stories are live in SIT.

##### 4. Flow

1. The harness resets the wave-1 SIT fixtures and loads the fixture set of section 13: the case `RC-2026-000123`, notices `N-0001` and `N-0002` in state Generated with notice type DEMAND and contract CT-77001, the WIN sample file `WIN-POD-SAMPLE-v1`, the 30-row pod batch of 2026-11-30 and the repeat pod row of 2026-11-28, all seeded through the owners' published operations only.
2. The harness opens the WIN file window at 16:00 on 2026-11-25 the way the Airflow window opens it and lets rwb-comms ask rwb-integration for the INT-14 file for that business date.
3. rwb-comms builds the file from its own notice rows for the dispatch-eligible state, sets `dispatch_file_id` and increments `dispatch_attempts`, and asks rwb-integration to deliver it.
4. rwb-integration executes the `deliverFile` activity on queue `rwb-integration`, stores the letter behind a document ID in rwb-document, and records one `outbound_item` for INT-14 and 2026-11-25.
5. The harness reads the item on `GET /api/recovery/integration/v1/admin/outbound-items` and the file on `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}`, and asserts `N-0001` and `N-0002` each appear once in the file of 2026-11-25.
6. The harness drops the acknowledgment for contract CT-77001 — sent date 26112026, barcode `RR123456789TH`, sent type NPL — at the stubbed P2 edge, the way the WIN acknowledgment arrives.
7. The harness asserts `GET /api/recovery/comms/v1/notices/N-0001` returns state Sent, sent date 2026-11-26 and barcode `RR123456789TH`, and that the ledger call to `POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/RC-2026-000123/interactions` arrives once with direction OUT, channel LETTER and the date 2026-11-26 (AC1).
8. The harness consumes `rwb.comms.events.v1` and asserts one `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1` for `N-0001` with the barcode and the sent date, keyed by the case ID, with no personal data in the payload (AC1).
9. The harness reruns JOB-10 on 2026-11-25 from the job monitor, and asserts the second file does not hold `N-0001` and no second `outbound_item` exists for the date (AC8).
10. The harness withholds the acknowledgment on the runs of 2026-11-26, 2026-11-27 and 2026-11-28, and asserts `N-0001` stays Generated, three files are recorded for it, and after the third failure one open task carries MSG-GEN-006 naming WIN (AC4).
11. The harness sets the ACE batch for source WIN of 2026-11-30 COMPLETE, loads the sample file `WIN-POD-SAMPLE-v1` through ACE ingestion, reads it on `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/DP07/records`, and reads `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness` for the feed version (AC3).
12. The harness loads the 30-row pod batch of 2026-11-30 with one row of barcode `RR000000000TH` and notice_ref `WIN-99999`, lets the pod read run, and asserts 29 notices update, 1 row is held with check References on the data-quality exceptions read, one delivery per notice, and the repeat counted (AC6, AC7).
13. The harness asserts the delivery outcome for `N-0001`: state Delivered with delivery status DELIVERED and callback date 2026-11-28, one ledger entry with the delivered date 2026-11-28, one `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1` on `rwb.comms.events.v1`, and a running NOTICE_PERIOD timer on `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/RC-2026-000123/timers` started on 2026-11-28 (AC2).
14. The harness loads the second pod row of 2026-11-28 for barcode `RR123456789TH` and asserts the notice is unchanged, no second `NoticeDelivered` is consumed, and the repeat is counted under R-UNI-40 (AC10).
15. The harness sets the ACE batch of 2026-11-30 FAILED at its record count check (AC5) and then leaves the batch due on 2026-11-30 not COMPLETE on 2026-12-01 (AC11); it asserts no pod row of the date is read, no notice changes state, and the freshness answer carries MSG-P1-001 naming DP07 Legal and 2026-11-23.
16. The harness runs REC-05 on 2026-11-28 with `N-0002` still carrying no barcode, and asserts the break is listed and visible on SCR-45 through the data-quality exceptions read (AC9).
17. The harness repeats the dispatch with rwb-integration returning `rwb.integration.FileFailed.v1` on the first attempt, waits for the retry at the interval in force, and asserts the retry succeeds, one item is ACKNOWLEDGED, one `rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1` is consumed, and the file carries `N-0001` once (AC13).
18. The harness repeats the reads as a caller in role RW-PHONECOL, asserts status 403 with MSG-P4-002 and no state change (AC12), then runs the boundary check of section 13 and publishes the run report with the counts, the fixture versions and the contract versions.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The stubbed WIN folder does not pick the file up inside the run window | The run fails and the report names the window, the business date and the file ID; no criterion is marked passed | None | AC1 |
| X2 | The acknowledgment fixture is dropped twice for one file | The owner's inbox dedupes it; the harness asserts one Sent state and one `NoticeDispatched`, and fails the run on a second effect | None | AC7 |
| X3 | A pod row names an unknown barcode and notice_ref | The row is held on the data-quality exception list with check References and the rest of the batch is read | None | AC6 |
| X4 | The ACE batch for source WIN is not COMPLETE for the business date | No pod row of that date is read, earlier delivery data stays, and the notice data product answers with the stale marker | MSG-P1-001 | AC5, AC11 |
| X5 | rwb-source-data does not answer inside the 2 s budget | One GET retry with jitter, then the step fails and the run fails; the harness never asserts on a partial answer | None | AC3 |
| X6 | A caller in a role without the Litigation R right | The owner refuses with 403 and MSG-P4-002; nothing changes | MSG-P4-002 | AC12 |
| X7 | The same pod rows are read twice | One delivery is recorded per notice and the repeat is counted; no notice changes state a second time | None | AC7, AC10 |
| X8 | rwb-integration raises FileFailed or the acknowledgment times out | The retry runs at the interval in force; one outbound item and one letter exist at the end | MSG-GEN-006 | AC13, AC4 |
| X9 | A service answers outside `/api/recovery/<short>/v1`, or a cross-schema read appears in the run | The boundary check fails the run before the report is written | None | BR9 |
| X10 | The clock is not held for a date-dependent criterion | The run fails before the assertion and names the date and the criterion; the harness never waits on the wall clock | None | AC9, AC11 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Runs against the real wave-1 services already in SIT; the suite builds no operation, publishes no event and owns no table. The seven integration dependencies are the services it exercises |
| Negotiable | The fixture set, the window call, the stub shape and the expected counts are harness configuration; the business values are the legacy ones and are not changed |
| Valuable | The loop that decides when a notice period starts is proved on the real services before wave 1 exits, including the freshness gate, the held row and the reconciliation break |
| Estimable | One harness, one fixture set, one boundary check and one run report; no production code and no schema |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the fixture set and the two external stubs |
| Testable | Each owned criterion has a test case in section 16, and every assertion is made on a REST answer, an event or a job artefact |

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Only notices in a dispatch-eligible state are written to the WIN file: Generated in Epic 1, Approved from RWB-E2-014. In the target the eligible state is configuration in rwb-comms and the suite reads it as data, never assumes it | INT-14; JOB-10; legacy RWB-E1-055 BR1; `rwb.comms.dispatch.eligible-states` |
| BR2 | A notice period starts only from the delivery date on the proof of delivery. The date travels on `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1` and rwb-case starts the NOTICE_PERIOD timer from the event, so the event date and the timer start date are the same | CTL-15; R-LIT-07; legacy RWB-E1-055 BR2; DP-09 |
| BR3 | An unacknowledged file is sent again by rwb-integration and the notice stays in its dispatch-eligible state; after the third failure a task goes to the owning team | INT-14 error handling; R-UNI-33, R-UNI-34; legacy RWB-E1-055 BR3; DP-10 |
| BR4 | A pod row is read only when the ACE batch for source WIN is COMPLETE for its business date, and the read is made by rwb-source-data, the only service with a grant on `recovery.v_ace_*`; a row with an unknown reference is held | ACE batch record; INT-15 error handling; legacy RWB-E1-055 BR4; DP-05 |
| BR5 | A notice sent with no barcode after three days is a reconciliation break, listed by rwb-source-data and shown on SCR-45 | REC-05; legacy RWB-E1-055 BR5 |
| BR6 | The same event twice, and the same pod row twice, produce one effect and the repeat is counted | R-UNI-40; legacy RWB-E1-055 BR6; DP-09 |
| BR7 | The notice data product is stale one business day after the WIN batch was due, and MSG-P1-001 names the product and the last load date | `v_ace_batch_status`; MSG-P1-001; legacy RWB-E1-055 BR7 |
| BR8 | One hop and a 2 s budget: every call in the run goes from the harness to the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1`, with one GET retry with jitter, a circuit breaker per downstream and no call chain | Architecture v5 slides 10, 11 and 12; DP-11; ADR-020 |
| BR9 | No service reads another service's tables: the notice is read on `/api/recovery/comms/v1`, the letter and its document ID on `/api/recovery/document/v1`, the outbound item on `/api/recovery/integration/v1`, the pod, the freshness, the ledger and the held rows on `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`, and the timer on `/api/recovery/case/v1`. A cross-schema read or a cross-schema join fails the boundary check of the run | DP-01; Architecture v5 slide 29; ADR-014 |

##### 9. State transitions

The notice state, as the suite observes it on the owner's contract:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | JOB-10 file written | The notice is Generated and not already in a file of the date | Generated, with `dispatch_file_id` set and `dispatch_attempts` incremented |
| Generated | WIN acknowledgment | A barcode returns for contract CT-77001 | Sent |
| Sent | `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1` content | A callback date is present on the pod row | Delivered |
| Sent | A second acknowledgment or a repeated pod row | The repeat is counted under R-UNI-40 | Sent, unchanged |
| Delivered | A repeated pod row for the same barcode and callback date | The repeat is counted under R-UNI-40 | Delivered, unchanged |

The move to Delivered is made by rwb-comms on its own row, not by this story. rwb-case starts the NOTICE_PERIOD timer when it consumes `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1` through its inbox, and the timer starts on the delivered date the event carries, 2026-11-28, never on the sent date 2026-11-26. No case status changes in this story: the case stays in the status rwb-case holds for it, and the suite asserts that status before and after the run and fails on any move. The suite sets no state by hand; a state it set itself would prove nothing, so the run report names the owner and the operation that made each move.
