##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. This story is a test suite: it proves the dispatch and the proof-of-delivery loop and provides no REST operation. The operations of the loop belong to the P6, P3, P5 and P1 APP stories.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

Every call is one hop on the owner's per-service base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1`, with a 2 s timeout, one GET retry with jitter and a circuit breaker per downstream (DP-11, DP-13).

| Method | Path | Owner | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/comms/v1/notices/{noticeId}` | P6 rwb-comms | Notice state, sent date, barcode, callback date, delivery status and dispatch counters (AC1, AC2, AC4, AC5, AC10, AC12) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}` | P5 rwb-document | The stored letter behind the notice document ID, to prove one letter per notice (AC8, AC13) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/integration/v1/admin/outbound-items` | P2 rwb-integration | The INT-14 items of the business date, their state and attempt count (AC4, AC8, AC13) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/{productCode}/records` | P1 rwb-source-data | The pod records of DP07 for the business date, as rwb-source-data serves them (AC3, AC5, AC6) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness` | P1 rwb-source-data | The freshness stamp, the feed version and the stale marker of DP07 (AC3, AC5, AC11) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions` | P1 rwb-source-data | The ledger operation the dispatch and the delivery write through; the harness asserts exactly one call per fact, with its direction, channel, date and summary (AC1, AC2) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/data-quality/exceptions` | P1 rwb-source-data | The held pod row with check References and the REC-05 breaks (AC6, AC9) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers` | P3 rwb-case | The running NOTICE_PERIOD timer and its start date (AC2, AC12) |

The harness writes nothing through these operations: the POST is the ledger operation rwb-comms calls, and the harness observes that exactly one call arrives per dispatched or delivered fact and reads back what the call carried. The suite composes no call: no operation of this table is used to reach another service.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The suite publishes no Kafka event and writes no outbox row; it consumes the owners' events and puts its result in the run report.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Handler in the run |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1` | `rwb.integration.events.v1` | P2 rwb-integration | The file was delivered to WIN; asserted once per item, per business date (AC13) |
| `rwb.integration.FileFailed.v1` | `rwb.integration.events.v1` | P2 rwb-integration | The attempt failed and the retry path is open; asserted on the first attempt (AC13, AC4) |
| `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1` | `rwb.comms.events.v1` | P6 rwb-comms | The notice is Sent with barcode and sent date; asserted once per acknowledged notice (AC1, AC8) |
| `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1` | `rwb.comms.events.v1` | P6 rwb-comms | The notice is Delivered with the delivered date; asserted once per newly delivered notice and never twice (AC2, AC7, AC10) |

All four are CloudEvents on the owner's topic, keyed by case ID, carrying IDs and facts only; the harness asserts the key and the absence of personal data (DP-09).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

Observed only. This story creates, changes and owns no workflow and no activity.

| Name | Type | Task queue | What the run observes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NoticeDispatchWorkflow` | Workflow, owned by P6 | `rwb-comms` | The dispatch of the notice set for the business date: the file request, the acknowledgment handling and the two events (AC1, AC4, AC8) |
| `deliverFile` | Activity, owned by P2 | `rwb-integration` | The one file delivery for INT-14 and 2026-11-25, its retry on failure and the `FileDelivered` or `FileFailed` fact (AC13) |

The harness never starts, signals or terminates either one. It opens the 16:00 window the way the Airflow task does, drops the acknowledgment and the pod batch at the stubbed edge, and asserts the effects through the contracts and the topic.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. JOB-10 is not a Temporal Schedule in this design: it is the bank Airflow 16:00 file window that opens the file run, plus the P6 `NoticeDispatchWorkflow` that executes it, as Architecture v5 slide 44 records ("Airflow file window + workers"). The harness creates, moves and owns no Schedule and no cron; it opens the window for the business date under test through the fixture of section 12.8 and records the call in the run report.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The tables of the loop belong to their owners: `notice` and `template` to P6 in `rwb_comms`, `outbound_item` to P2 in `rwb_integration`, `document` to P5 in `rwb_document`, `case_account` and `timer` to P3 in `rwb_case`, and the pod, freshness and interaction facts to P1 in `rwb_source_data`. The suite reads them through the operations of section 12.2 only (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

The run uses the real wave-1 services. The only fakes are the external boundary and the fixtures, and none of them replaces a service:

| Fake or fixture | Boundary | Use in the run |
|---|---|---|
| WIN SFTP folder stub | The P2 edge, outside the bank | Receives the INT-14 file and answers the acknowledgment record (AC1, AC4, AC13) |
| WIN acknowledgment stub | The P2 edge, outside the bank | Emits the acknowledgment with sent date 26112026, barcode `RR123456789TH` and sent type NPL for CT-77001; silent for the unacknowledged runs, and a `FileFailed` answer for the retry criterion (AC1, AC4, AC13) |
| Pod and freshness fixture | Behind rwb-source-data, loaded through ACE ingestion | The `WIN-POD-SAMPLE-v1` sample of 25 records, the 30-row batch of 2026-11-30 with one unknown row, the second row of 2026-11-28, and the batch states COMPLETE, FAILED and not COMPLETE (AC3, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC10, AC11) |
| Clock control | The environment clock | Holds 2026-11-25 to 2026-12-01 so the three-day REC-05 window and the one-business-day stale window are deterministic (AC9, AC11) |

No real WIN connection is opened, no production data is touched, and the fixture contents, the stub file naming and the acknowledgment record keys are harness configuration named in the run report.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 8 consumed | Notice read on rwb-comms; document read on rwb-document; outbound items on rwb-integration; pod records, freshness, ledger operation and data-quality exceptions on rwb-source-data; timers on rwb-case; one hop and 2 s each |
| Kafka | 0 published, 4 consumed | `FileDelivered` and `FileFailed` on `rwb.integration.events.v1`; `NoticeDispatched` and `NoticeDelivered` on `rwb.comms.events.v1` |
| Temporal | 1 observed | `NoticeDispatchWorkflow` on queue `rwb-comms`, with the `deliverFile` activity asserted through its effects on queue `rwb-integration` |
| File | 2 | INT-14 outbound WIN letters file, and INT-15 inbound proof-of-delivery file read back through rwb-source-data; no file content in any message or workflow payload |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `itg/recovery`, package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.itg.win`, test scope only; it is not part of any deployed service and holds no production code.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-18 | Interaction ledger | Ledger owned by rwb-source-data (default ruling) | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The platform H rows of the table above are delivered by the platform waves and are not repeated in the metadata H field of this story, which stays empty. The blocking work is the seven integration dependencies: RWB-P6-E1055-APP for the notice state, the dispatch workflow and the two events; RWB-P3-E1055-APP for the timer; RWB-P3-E1028-APP for the timer type; RWB-P1-E1055-APP for the pod read and the freshness stamp; RWB-P1-E1066-APP for the ledger and the held rows; RWB-P5-E1054-APP and RWB-P5-E1055-APP for the stored letter. DP-07 resolves to "the notice type and template version are read as data through the P6 contract", DP-15 to "each service migrates its own schema and the suite holds no grant", DP-18 to "the ledger is read and asserted through rwb-source-data's interaction operation" and DP-19 to "SCR-03, SCR-30, SCR-44 and SCR-45 are reached through the gateway-bff composite route".

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| WinDispatchRun | Test suite | The ordered end-to-end run of section 4 for one business date, with one run lock per environment |
| WindowDriver | Fixture | Opens the 16:00 WIN file window the way the Airflow task does and records the call |
| WinEdgeStub | Fake | The WIN folder and the acknowledgment record at the P2 edge, with the silent and failed variants |
| PodBatchFixture | Fixture | The `WIN-POD-SAMPLE-v1` sample, the 30-row batch, the unknown row and the repeat row, loaded through ACE ingestion and never in a view the suite reads |
| NoticeAssertions | Assertions | State, sent date, barcode, callback date, delivery status and the dispatch counters on the P6 contract |
| TimerAssertions | Assertions | The NOTICE_PERIOD timer and its start date on the P3 contract |
| LedgerAssertions | Assertions | One ledger call per dispatched or delivered fact, with direction, channel, date and summary |
| ExceptionAssertions | Assertions | The held row with check References and the REC-05 break on the P1 data-quality read |
| BoundaryCheck | Check | Fails the run on any read outside `/api/recovery/<short>/v1`, any cross-schema read, any call chain and any path outside the published contract |
| RunReport | Publisher | Publishes the run report with the counts, the contract versions and the fixture versions |

**Fixtures**

- Case `RC-2026-000123` with primary account contract CT-77001, and notices `N-0001` and `N-0002` in state Generated with notice type DEMAND.
- The WIN owner's sample file `WIN-POD-SAMPLE-v1` of 25 records for 2026-11-30, and the 30-row batch of the same date with 29 matchable rows and one row of barcode `RR000000000TH` and notice_ref `WIN-99999`.
- The repeat pod row of 2026-11-28 for barcode `RR123456789TH`, and the second pod row of 2026-11-28 used by AC10.
- Batch states of source WIN: COMPLETE for 2026-11-30, FAILED at the record count check for AC5, and not COMPLETE on 2026-12-01 for AC11.
- Business dates 2026-11-25, 2026-11-26, 2026-11-27, 2026-11-28, 2026-11-30 and 2026-12-01, held by the clock control.
- Synthetic keys only: no name, address, identity number or real barcode anywhere in the fixtures.

**Real-service topology of the run**

| Node | Part in the run |
|---|---|
| rwb-comms (P6) | Owns the notice, runs `NoticeDispatchWorkflow`, handles the acknowledgment and publishes `NoticeDispatched` and `NoticeDelivered` |
| rwb-integration (P2) | Owns the outbound item and executes `deliverFile` to the stubbed WIN edge; publishes `FileDelivered` and `FileFailed` |
| rwb-source-data (P1) | Serves the pod records, the freshness stamp and the ledger operation; the only reader of `recovery.v_ace_*` |
| rwb-document (P5) | Holds the stored letter behind the document ID |
| rwb-case (P3) | Owns the NOTICE_PERIOD timer and the task after the third failure |
| rwb-access (P4) | Answers the cached permission data the owners check when a role without the Litigation R right calls; the harness calls no access operation of its own and asserts the owner's 403 |
| Kafka, Temporal and the Airflow frame | Shared platform parts; the Airflow frame opens the 16:00 window and calls the services through their APIs only |
| WIN folder and acknowledgment stub | The external party at the SFTP edge; the only stub in the run, on a synthetic fixture |

**Run order**

1. Reset the wave-1 SIT fixtures, load the fixture set of this section and hold the clock on 2026-11-25.
2. Run AC1 and AC8 on 2026-11-25: one file, `N-0001` and `N-0002` once each, the acknowledgment, Sent with barcode `RR123456789TH`, one ledger call, one `NoticeDispatched`, then the rerun with no second file and no second item.
3. Run AC4: three runs with no acknowledgment on 2026-11-26, 2026-11-27 and 2026-11-28, the notice still Generated, three files and the task with MSG-GEN-006 naming WIN.
4. Run AC3 on 2026-11-30: the 25-record sample ingested by ACE and read on the pod records and the freshness stamp, 25 of 25 and 0 refused, with the feed version.
5. Run AC2, AC6 and AC7 on 2026-11-30: 29 notices delivered, 1 row held with check References, one delivery per notice, the repeat counted, one `NoticeDelivered` and the timer started on 2026-11-28.
6. Run AC10 with the second pod row of 2026-11-28: the notice unchanged, no second `NoticeDelivered`, the repeat counted.
7. Run AC5 and AC11: the batch FAILED at the record count check and then not COMPLETE on 2026-12-01, no pod row read, no state change, and MSG-P1-001 naming DP07 Legal and 2026-11-23.
8. Run AC9 on 2026-11-28 with `N-0002` still without a barcode, and assert the REC-05 break on the data-quality read.
9. Run AC13: the `FileFailed` answer on the first attempt, the retry at the interval in force, one ACKNOWLEDGED item, one `FileDelivered`, one letter.
10. Run AC12 as RW-PHONECOL, assert 403 with MSG-P4-002 and no change, then run the boundary check, publish the run report and restore the environment.

**Configuration.** The fixture set, the window call, the stub file naming and the expected counts sit in `itg/recovery/config`; the eligible notice state, the attempt limit and the retry intervals are data in the owning services and are read, never set, by the harness. No business value is compiled into the suite.

**Done when.** The thirteen test cases of section 16 pass in one run; the boundary check finds no read outside `/api/recovery/<short>/v1`, no cross-schema read and no call chain; the run report shows one file per business date, one delivery per pod row, one `NoticeDelivered` per newly delivered notice and the timer started on 2026-11-28; and the run is repeated once green on the same build to prove it is repeatable.

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P6-004 | A notice is acknowledged by WIN | {notice} was sent for registered mail on {date}. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | WIN has not acknowledged after the third attempt | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The WIN batch is late or not COMPLETE | {product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right calls the notice or the proof-of-delivery read | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The message text is the legacy wording of RWB-E1-055, unchanged. The run asserts the message the owning service returns, with the values of section 7 — "DEMAND was sent for registered mail on 26 November 2026." for MSG-P6-004, "{system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried." with WIN named for MSG-GEN-006, "DP07 Legal is from 2026-11-23. Today's load has not arrived." for MSG-P1-001 — and names the message ID in the report. The run adds no message of its own, and the report text is for the wave entry check and not part of the message standard.

| SCR-45 Data quality | The held pod row with check References in state breaks, and the REC-05 break on `N-0002` in state breaks, after the loading state of the date |

The harness reads the same facts from the owners' contracts and not from the rendered screen, because the screens are the edge's own stories; a passed run therefore means the data behind each surface is right. The composite route itself is RWB-PLT-N001-CON and the screen field lists are the edge's own stories; this suite stops at the owners' contracts.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the eligible notice states, the attempt limit, the retry intervals, the break days, the stale days, the fixture set and every expected count are configuration or data.
- No personal data in logs, events, fixtures, workflow inputs or the run report: the address is read from the source-data contract into the outbound file stream only and is never logged, and the report holds notice IDs, counts and hashes.
- ACE data only through rwb-source-data: the pod, the account contract number and the contact value leave through its contract, and the suite holds no grant on `recovery.v_ace_*`.
- Files only through rwb-integration: the INT-14 file is built and sent by the owner activity, no component calls WIN directly, and the WIN edge is the synthetic stub.
- No read of another service's tables and no cross-schema join: every assertion is made through `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` or on the topic, and a cross-schema read fails the boundary check.
- One hop and a 2 s budget, one GET retry with jitter and a circuit breaker per downstream; a call chain or an unbounded timeout fails the run.
- No PII in events: the four consumed events are asserted for IDs and facts only, keyed by case ID.
- Synthetic data only: no real WIN connection, no production or UAT data, and the environment is restored after the run.
- A failing criterion is fixed in the service that owns it or raised as a gap; it is never waived in the suite.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-056 for the platform observability epic; the 16 job rows, the eight run book sections, the message IDs and the guards are kept. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform administrator (RW-PLATADM)**, I want **the platform to hold one run book for every Epic 1 Workbench job, a pipeline gate that proves the run books and the catalogue rows exist, one monitoring workbook that shows each job's last run, status and duration beside the last complete ACE business date per source, and alert and rerun guards that route to the owning role**, so that **the operations team can restart any Epic 1 job without the developer and can tell a late ACE batch from a failed Workbench job**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The Workbench loads no source data (D-RCV-35 U1; ADR-010). Its scheduled work is the case list chain, the daily rebalancing, payment matching and booking confirmation, the WIN notice file, the outbox relay, document intake, the decision-record ingest and its hash-chain check, the reporting extract, retention, the agent runtime and the view conformance test. A failed job that only its developer can restart holds the case list and the morning allocation; a late ACE batch looks exactly like a failed Workbench job unless the monitor shows the ACE business date beside it.

In the target the 16 Epic 1 jobs no longer run in one scheduler: each runs as a Temporal Schedule or as an event-started workflow in the service that owns it (DP-10, Arch v5 slide 44), and JOB-05 and JOB-11 have no Schedule of their own, because timers live inside each workflow and the outbox relay runs in every service, while JOB-13 is continuous Kafka ingest. The catalogue row, the run book gate and the workbook therefore become the one platform place that spans the 16 jobs: they name the owning service and the mechanism, hold the owner role and the threshold, and prove in the pipeline that neither the row nor the run book is missing. No inbound load job is catalogued: ACE ingests every source, ACE monitors its own ingestion, and the Workbench watches only the business date it receives. This meets REQ-DRI-007 (a named owner for every failure), NFR-067 and NFR-068.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The owning service workflows exist: DailyCaseRun and its steps in rwb-case, the reconciliation workflow in rwb-source-data, the matching and booking workflows in rwb-payment, the notice, document, decision and reporting work (RWB-PLT-WF and RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, DP-10).
- The Kafka platform and the outbox relay are in force, so JOB-11 and the event-started jobs have a transport (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, DP-09).
- The per-service Flyway sequence is in force, so no migration of this story writes into an owning service's schema (RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, DP-15).
- The parameters and reference-data contracts are in force, so the owner role of a job is a reference-data value and not a literal (DP-06, DP-07).
- RWB-P1-E1015 is done: `v_ace_batch_status`, the stale marker on `data_product_load` and EV-27 `rwb.source-data.AceDataLate.v1` exist in rwb-source-data.
- `job_catalog` is owned by P2 rwb-integration and its admin operation exists, so the 16 Epic 1 rows are loaded as data (ownership map; DP-01).
- The Log Analytics workspace and the OpenTelemetry baseline receive the application logs, the spans and the job-run records (RWB-PLT-N005-OPS).
- The person holds RW-PLATADM through RWB-<env>-RW-PLATADM.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. The platform administrator confirms one `job_catalog` row per job with job ID, name, owner role, schedule, run book path, expected duration and alert threshold. The 16 Epic 1 rows are JOB-02, JOB-03, JOB-04, JOB-05, JOB-06, JOB-07, JOB-08, JOB-10, JOB-11, JOB-12, JOB-13, JOB-14, JOB-15, JOB-17, AGT-01 and CHK-01; they are loaded as data through the P2 rwb-integration admin operation, not by code.
2. A squad member (RW-TRIBE) writes the run book at `docs/operations/runbooks/<job ID>.md` with the eight sections: purpose, schedule, owner, dependencies, failure signs, checks, restart steps and escalation.
3. The squad member names the ACE sources the job reads through `recovery.v_ace_*` and the upstream Workbench job in Dependencies; names the stale marker on `data_product_load` and EV-27 `rwb.source-data.AceDataLate.v1` in Failure signs when the job reads ACE; and the CHK-01 run book names the view conformance test with the dictionary load through RWB-E1-043 in Checks and Restart steps.
4. The pipeline runs `RunbookCompletenessTest`: it checks every Temporal Schedule and every event-started job of the owning services and every catalogue row, checks the eight headings, and fails on the forbidden names (an inbound load job, a file arrival, a load rerun, a data quality exception console, a table in schema `public`).
5. Each job writes a structured job-run record at start and end with job ID, business date, status and duration: OpenTelemetry span attributes on the workflow or activity span, plus the P1 job run log.
6. The platform administrator opens the workbook "Recovery jobs" or calls the P1 job view and sees last run, status and duration per job, and the last complete ACE business date per source from `v_ace_batch_status`.
7. An alert rule emails the owner role and RW-PLATADM with MSG-P2-004 when a job is FAILED or runs past its threshold.
8. When an ACE batch is late or failed, the freshness step marks the product STALE, publishes EV-27 and holds the dependent job; the run book says to wait for the batch and not to rerun the job.
9. The platform administrator follows the restart steps in the run book and calls the P1 rerun operation.
10. The job restarts from its failed step and the dependent jobs run in the order of the daily timeline.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A job has a Temporal Schedule registration or an event trigger but no catalogue row, or a catalogue row with no run book, or a run book lacks a section | The pipeline fails and names the job and the missing section | MSG-P2-005 | AC1 |
| X2 | A run book names an inbound load job, a file arrival, a load rerun, a data quality exception console or a table in schema `public` | The pipeline fails and names the run book and the forbidden line | Build log: JOB-02.md names public.account; a run book may name only the Workbench jobs and recovery.v_ace_* | AC1, AC7 |
| X3 | A rerun is requested while the job runs | Refused; the running job continues | MSG-P2-006 | AC5 |
| X4 | A job runs past its alert threshold | The owner role and RW-PLATADM are alerted; the job is not stopped | MSG-P2-004 | AC4 |
| X5 | A rerun of a job that already completed for the business date | Refused with 409; the job runs nothing and no business row changes | MSG-GEN-004 | AC5 |
| X6 | An ACE batch is late or failed | The product is marked STALE, EV-27 is published, the dependent job is recorded WAITING and is not rerun | MSG-P1-001 | AC6 |
| X7 | The view conformance test CHK-01 fails | The merge is blocked; the CHK-01 run book gives the dictionary load through RWB-E1-043 as the fix | v_ace_account.legacy_bucket has no data dictionary entry | AC1, AC7 |
| X8 | A role without the right reruns a job | Refused; nothing changes | MSG-P4-002 | AC8 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the owning services' Schedules and event triggers (RWB-PLT-WF, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON), the batch view and stale marker of RWB-P1-E1015 and the telemetry baseline of RWB-PLT-N005-OPS; each job's own story supplies the job body |
| Negotiable | Owners, thresholds and paths are catalogue rows; the story fixes the eight run book sections and the gate |
| Valuable | Any Epic 1 job can be restarted by operations on the day it fails, and a late ACE batch is not mistaken for a Workbench failure |
| Estimable | 16 run books, one pipeline gate, one workbook, three alert rules, one business-date panel, the guard definitions and one catalogue baseline |
| Small | Within one week with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion is one automated test, one pipeline check or one workbook query |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Run books and monitoring for every Epic 1 Workbench job

  Background:
    Given job_catalog holds 16 rows with first release "E1": JOB-02, JOB-03, JOB-04, JOB-05, JOB-06, JOB-07, JOB-08, JOB-10, JOB-11, JOB-12, JOB-13, JOB-14, JOB-15, JOB-17, AGT-01 and CHK-01
    Given the daily case list chain is JOB-02, then JOB-03, JOB-04, JOB-07 and JOB-08, with JOB-05 carried by durable timers inside each workflow and JOB-13 continuous on Kafka

    Then each file has the sections purpose, schedule, owner, dependencies, failure signs, checks, restart steps and escalation

    Then a Schedule or an event trigger with no catalogue row, and a catalogue row with no run book or a run book without a section, fail the gate with MSG-P2-005 naming the job and the missing section

    Then no file names an inbound load job, a file arrival, a load rerun, a data quality exception console or a table in schema public

    When the baseline is applied through the admin operation of rwb-integration
    Then each row carries the job ID, the job name, the owner role, the schedule, the run book path, the expected duration and the alert threshold
    Then applying the same baseline a second time changes nothing, because the load is idempotent by job ID
    Then no migration of this story inserts a catalogue row into a schema, and no job ID, owner role, schedule, path or threshold is hard-coded in a class, a test or a dashboard
    Then GET /api/recovery/integration/v1/admin/scheduled-jobs returns 16 entries

  Scenario: AC3 The workbook and the P1 job view agree on last run, status, duration and the last complete ACE business date per source (new, D-RCV-60)

    Given JOB-02 has an alert threshold of 45 minutes (assumed; DL11)
    When JOB-02 fails at 05:40 on business date 2026-11-30
    Then the data steward group and the platform administrator group receive message MSG-P2-004 with the job, the time, the date and the run book path
    When JOB-02 has run for 46 minutes on business date 2026-12-01
    Then the data steward group and the platform administrator group receive message MSG-P2-004 and the system does not stop JOB-02
    When a job is held for a late ACE batch
    Then the held run raises MSG-P1-001 and the alert reaches the named owner role within the 15-minute target of NFR-068

  Scenario: AC5 A rerun is refused while the job runs and refused for a completed business date (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given JOB-04 started at 06:40 and is running

    Then the response is 409 with message MSG-P2-006
    Then JOB-04 continues its run
    Given JOB-04 completed for business date 2026-12-01
    When a platform administrator reruns it for the same date
    Then the response is 409 with message MSG-GEN-004
    Then case_list_row still holds one row per case account for 2026-12-01
    Then reconciliation_result still holds one row per product group for 2026-12-01

    Given RW-CASEOWN holds no rerun right

  Scenario: AC9 The view conformance test has a run book (legacy RWB-E1-056 AC9)

    When the pipeline runs CHK-01
    Then CHK-01 fails with "v_ace_account.legacy_bucket has no data dictionary entry"
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every Epic 1 Workbench job, the agent runtime and the view conformance test have a run book, an alert and an owner, held as one `job_catalog` row and one file under `docs/operations/runbooks/`. No inbound load job is catalogued; ACE ingestion is ACE's and is not monitored here | FEAT-DRI-18; D-RCV-35 U1 |
| BR2 | A run book has eight sections: purpose, schedule, owner, dependencies, failure signs, checks, restart steps and escalation | Story intent |
| BR3 | The owner of each job is the role in `job_catalog`: JOB-02 and JOB-04 data steward; JOB-03 and JOB-06 team managers; JOB-07 and JOB-08 credit administration; JOB-10, JOB-11, JOB-12 and CHK-01 platform administrator; JOB-13 data steward; JOB-14 and JOB-17 compliance; JOB-15 reporting and BI analyst; AGT-01 center of excellence | batch.txt; roles.txt |
| BR4 | Daily jobs restart in the order of the daily timeline: JOB-02, then JOB-03, JOB-04, JOB-07 and JOB-08; JOB-05 is carried by durable timers inside each workflow and has no Schedule of its own; JOB-06 runs at 06:30 as a Temporal Schedule; JOB-13 is continuous Kafka ingest and has no Schedule | batch.txt Daily timeline; Arch v5 slide 44; ownership map jobs |
| BR5 | A rerun of a completed job and business date is refused; the job body is idempotent for its business date | R-UNI-40; events.txt Rules sheet, Delivery |
| BR6 | A job reads ACE only through `recovery.v_ace_*` and never loads source data. A run book that names a public table, an inbound load job or a file arrival fails the build | D-RCV-35 U1, U4; ADR-010; RWB-TE-001 |
| BR7 | When an ACE batch is late or failed, the product is STALE, EV-27 is published and the dependent job waits; the monitor shows the ACE business date beside the job run | RWB-E1-015; BR-P1-014 |
| BR8 | Owners, thresholds and paths are data rows in `job_catalog`, never code, and are written only through the P2 rwb-integration admin operation | Principle 1; DP-01; ownership map |

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It reads and records job run status: STARTED, COMPLETED, FAILED, WAITING and SKIPPED. A rerun of a completed job for its business date is refused.

| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Maintains the catalogue rows through the P2 admin operation; reruns a job (Platform administration, U); owns JOB-10, JOB-11, JOB-12 and CHK-01 |
| RW-DATASTEW, data steward | Reads job runs; owns JOB-02, JOB-04 and JOB-13; receives their alerts (Platform administration, R) |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | Owns JOB-03 and JOB-06; receives their alerts by email; no endpoint right |
| RW-CREDITAD, credit administration | Owns JOB-07 and JOB-08; receives their alerts by email |
| RW-BIANAL, reporting and BI analyst | Owns JOB-15; receives its alerts by email |

| RW-COMPLY, compliance | Owns JOB-14 and JOB-17; receives their alerts by email |
| RW-TRIBE, squad member | Writes and maintains the run books and RunbookCompletenessTest; reads job runs (Platform administration, R) |
| RW-AUDIT and RW-SECADM | Read job runs (Platform administration, R) |

The service identity that runs the platform jobs and writes the job-run record is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1419; ASM-2483).

One job-run record is added for each run: its fields are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1419; ASM-2483); the story fixes that it carries the job ID, the business date, the status, the started and ended time and the duration, and no other business content. The run book path is the catalogue row's `runbook_path`, `docs/operations/runbooks/<job ID>.md`. This story owns no table: `job_catalog` stays with P2 rwb-integration and is written only through its admin operation, and the ACE fields are read through the P1 contract or the P1 view. No business data and no personal data are held by this story; the job-run record and the run books carry job IDs, dates, statuses, durations and role names only.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. This story provides no REST operation. The job view and the rerun stay with P1 rwb-source-data (`GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs` and `POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun`) and the catalogue stays with P2 rwb-integration (`GET /api/recovery/integration/v1/admin/scheduled-jobs`, per the ownership map).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Deployment need |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs` | P1 rwb-source-data | The workbook "Recovery jobs" and the job view read last run, status, startedAt and endedAt; one hop, 2 s client budget (DP-11) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun` | P1 rwb-source-data | The restart steps of every run book call the rerun; the running guard returns 409 MSG-P2-006 and the completed-date guard returns 409 MSG-GEN-004 |
| GET | `/api/recovery/integration/v1/admin/scheduled-jobs` | P2 rwb-integration | The catalogue baseline load, the gate and the workbook read the 16 rows; the owner role, the schedule, the run book path and the alert threshold come from here |

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The job-run signal is a structured telemetry record (OpenTelemetry span attributes) plus the P1 job run log, not a business event; the v5 event catalogue carries no job-run event, so this story adds no topic and no event name.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` (EV-26) | `rwb.source-data.events.v1` | The business-date panel of the workbook and the alert list show the date the batch completed |
| `rwb.source-data.AceDataLate.v1` (EV-27) | `rwb.source-data.events.v1` | The held-run alert and the STALE marker beside the job that is waiting |

Both topics and both events are owned by P1 rwb-source-data; this story consumes them and republishes nothing.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None owned. The workbook and the gate observe the Schedules and the workflows of the owning services: DailyCaseRun in rwb-case, the reconciliation workflow of rwb-source-data, and the matching and booking workflows of rwb-payment are observed through their run records and the job view; this story starts none of them and claims none of them.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None registered. The Schedules and event triggers observed, with the legacy job references: the JOB-06 rebalancing Schedule in rwb-case, the JOB-14 hash-chain check Schedule in rwb-decision, the JOB-17 retention Schedule in rwb-document, and the event-started JOB-02 (case creation), JOB-04 (reconciliation), JOB-07 (payment matching) and JOB-08 (booking confirmation). JOB-05 has no Schedule (durable timers inside each workflow), JOB-11 has no Schedule (outbox relay in every service) and JOB-13 has no Schedule (continuous Kafka ingest); each still has a catalogue row and a run book.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. `job_catalog` is owned by P2 rwb-integration (ownership map) and this story writes it only through the P2 admin operation; the ACE fields are read through the P1 contract or the P1 view; this story creates no table and runs no migration.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Use |
|---|---|
| rwb-source-data WireMock | Runs in the pipeline so the gate and the workbook tests can read a job view without the service, including the 409 answers of MSG-P2-006 and MSG-GEN-004 and the ACE batch status |
| rwb-integration WireMock | Runs in the pipeline so the catalogue baseline load and the gate can read 16 rows without the service |

The fakes are test-only workloads; they are not deployed into SIT, UAT or production.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 3 consumed | The job view, the rerun and the catalogue; one hop, 2 s (DP-11) |
| Kafka | 2 consumed, 0 published | EV-26 AceDataReady and EV-27 AceDataLate; the job-run signal is telemetry, not an event |
| Temporal | 0 owned; the observed Schedules and workflows are named in 12.5 and 12.6 | The story reads run records, it does not start or claim a workflow |
| File | None | The run books are repository content and the catalogue baseline is applied through the admin operation |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The nine rows are the patterns the legacy RWB-E1-056 carries after the split. DP-10 is the substantive one: the 16 jobs are Temporal Schedules or event-started workflows in their owning services, so a catalogue row and a run book name a mechanism the platform does not own and cannot schedule. DP-01, DP-05 and DP-07 keep the story off another service's tables and off schema `public`: the catalogue is written through the P2 admin operation, the ACE batch status is read through the P1 contract or `recovery.v_ace_*`, and an owner role is resolved from reference data. DP-03 and DP-09 stay on the story because the job set it monitors includes the outbox relay (JOB-11) and the decision-record jobs (JOB-13 and JOB-14), whose run signals the story reads from the owning services and from the telemetry baseline, never from a topic of its own. DP-11 fixes the three consumed operations to one hop with a 2 s client budget, and DP-15 keeps the migration with the owning service, so this story seeds no Flyway migration. DP-19 is the gateway-bff route the workbook does not need and the P1 job view uses.

**Artefacts**

| Artefact | Content |
|---|---|
| Run book set | 16 files under `docs/operations/runbooks/<job ID>.md`, each with the eight sections purpose, schedule, owner, dependencies, failure signs, checks, restart steps and escalation |
| `RunbookCompletenessTest` | Pipeline gate: every Temporal Schedule, every event-started job and every catalogue row has a run book with the eight headings; the forbidden names fail the build with MSG-P2-005 |
| Workbook "Recovery jobs" | Panels for last run, status and duration per job, the alert list, and the last complete ACE business date per source from `v_ace_batch_status` |
| Alert rules | One rule for a FAILED job, one for a run past its threshold, one for a held run; each emails the owner role and RW-PLATADM with MSG-P2-004 or MSG-P1-001 |
| ACE business-date panel | The last complete business date per source beside the job panels, fed by EV-26 and EV-27 and by `v_ace_batch_status` |
| Catalogue baseline | The 16 Epic 1 rows as a data set applied through the P2 admin operation, idempotent by job ID; no migration and no code |
| Guard definitions | The running guard (409, MSG-P2-006), the completed-date guard (409, MSG-GEN-004) and the right check (MSG-P4-002), defined here and implemented by P1 rwb-source-data in its rerun operation |

**Platform contract policy.** The DP table's platform H dependencies (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, RWB-PLT-N001-CON) are wave 0 platform contracts, published before this story starts under the Day-1 rule (§R5.7). They are therefore not repeated in the metadata `Depends on (build)` row, which stays None, and the story builds against their published contracts and fakes (DP-11).

**Done when.** The gate passes on 16 run books and 16 catalogue rows and fails on a missing section and on a public table name; the catalogue baseline loads twice with one result; the workbook and the job view agree on last run, status and duration for all 16 jobs and show the last complete ACE business date per source; the three alert rules fire with MSG-P2-004 and MSG-P1-001 inside the 15-minute target; and a platform administrator restarts JOB-02 in SIT from the run book alone after a late ACE batch. The join key between the P1 job run log, the P2 catalogue row and the telemetry record, and the default expected duration and alert threshold of each job, are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1419; ASM-2483).

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P2-004 | A job failed or runs past its threshold | {job} failed at {time} for business date {date}. Follow run book {runbook}. |
| MSG-P2-005 | Pipeline finds a job without a complete run book | Job {job} has no run book with the eight sections. Missing: {section}. |
| MSG-P2-006 | Rerun of a running job | {job} is already running. Wait until it ends before you run it again. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | A rerun of a run that already completed, or a change from an old version | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P1-001 | A late or failed ACE batch holds a job | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right reruns a job | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

No Workbench screen in this story. The operator surfaces are the workbook "Recovery jobs" (job panels, the alert list and the ACE business-date panel), the P1 job view and the alert list. SCR-44 Interface and job monitor (states running, failed, complete) belongs to Epic 2, with the full monitor in Epic 8, and shows the same data from there. The workbook layout and its panel set are fixed at the wave 0 entry check (GAP-1419); the story fixes only the four things each panel must show: the last run, the status, the duration and the last complete ACE business date per source.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: owners, thresholds and paths are catalogue rows.
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts; the job-run record and the run books hold job IDs, dates, statuses, counts, durations and role names only.
- No read of another service's tables and no read of a table in schema `public`: ACE data comes through the P1 contract or `recovery.v_ace_*` only, and the catalogue through the P2 admin operation.
- ACE data is read only through the owner's contract or `recovery.v_ace_*` views (DP-05); no run book describes a direct read of an ACE table.
- A run book names roles and service identities, never a person.
- No run book describes an inbound load, a file arrival or a load rerun; the Workbench has none.
- No secret, credential or connection string appears in a run book, a workbook panel or an alert payload; each is a secret reference.

| NFR-067 | Every scheduled job has a run book, monitoring and an alert to the operations channel | Program 6.12 | FEAT-DRI-18 | All recovery processes | D-RCV-35 U1 | TC-E1-056-01, TC-E1-056-04 |

| ADR-023 | Observability per service | Program 6.12 | FEAT-DRI-18 | All recovery processes | D-RCV-60 | TC-E1-056-03, TC-E1-056-06 |

##### 19. Out of scope

- The job bodies and the 19 services' workflows: their own stories.
- The implementations of the P1 job view and rerun and of the P2 catalogue admin operation.
- The SCR-44 screen (Epic 2, full monitor in Epic 8).
- Incident handling after a job failure (FEAT-ADM-12, Epic 8).
- ACE's own ingestion monitoring and alerting; the Workbench watches the business date, not the ACE job.
- The freshness stamp, the stale marker and EV-27 (new stories of RWB-E1-015).
- The 30 views and the view conformance test CHK-01 (new stories of RWB-E1-069); this story only requires that its run book names them.
- The platform jobs JOB-21 and JOB-22 (platform workflow epic); they appear only on the baseline dashboards of RWB-PLT-N005-OPS.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the contract baseline of the channel-intake API of `rwb-document` is split out of legacy RWB-E1-057 and published on base `/api/recovery/document/v1` with the three admin operations, the two run shapes, the channel and result enumerations, the error envelope, the event position, the fakes and the drift test. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the channel-intake API of `rwb-document` — the run list, the run read and the rerun operation on base `/api/recovery/document/v1` with the `IntakeRun` and `IntakeRunPage` shapes, the channel code rule, the source, scan-result and OCR-status enumerations, the run states and the refusal reason codes, the error envelope with every message ID of section 14 and its HTTP status, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the event position of the path and the fakes with their drift test**, so that **the app story of this legacy key, the operator screen of Epic 2, the partner slice of the same key and the wave 1 integration harness build against a fixed, testable contract on Day 1, and a renamed count, a channel code that the run record cannot carry or a rerun answered with the wrong status can never drift between two builds without a failing test**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). Legacy RWB-E1-057 carries its one endpoint in a section 12 of prose, with an in-process `PartnerDirectory` and a `JobRecord` row beside it, and it leaves the consumer to infer the exact shapes of a run. Under the target architecture the parts most likely to drift silently are exactly the ones this baseline fixes:

- a count renamed in `IntakeRun` or `IntakeRunPage`, so the operator reads a channel column that carries nothing;
- a channel code widened to a free string, so a branch, a mailroom, a partner code and a mailbox code become indistinguishable in the run record and the per-channel alert of MSG-P5-008 names nothing;
- a result or a refusal reason outside the declared set, so a refused file is counted as taken in and the duplicate rule of R-UNI-40 stops being visible;
- a rerun answered 200 where the legacy contract answers a job, or a rerun of a run still in progress answered without MSG-GEN-004;
- an event invented for the path, so a consumer subscribes to a name the catalogue never publishes;
- an `Idempotency-Key` that is not the channel-code, source-reference and hash rule, so a repeat run takes the same file in twice.

The baseline fixes the names the checks require: schema `rwb_document`, REST base `/api/recovery/document/v1`, topic `rwb.document.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics, task queue `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document`. It makes the C dependencies of the app story explicit — the P3 parameters contract `RWB-P3-E1042-CON` and the P3 reference-data contract `RWB-P3-E1043-CON` — and it records that the partner-by-code read of `rwb-partner` is consumed and faked although the plan lists it in no C row (ASM-1839).

It also records the boundary the sibling baselines already occupy. `POST /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items` and the intake item read are declared by RWB-P5-E1049-CON, the review list and the resolve operation by RWB-P5-E1032-CON, and the content read by both; this baseline therefore declares the three operations of the run record and the rerun and nothing else, so no operation is declared twice for `rwb-document` (ASM-1838). Nothing else is guessed: the names this key does not settle carry the placeholder `Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1013; ASM-1837)`.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the operation, topic, event and queue names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- The platform error envelope, the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, the `Idempotency-Key` rule and the retry and `.dlt` topic convention are the platform baseline (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON); where this document narrows them it does so explicitly.
- TSD P5 appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2 are in force for the intake operations API-P5-010 to API-P5-013, and TSD P5 T3.1 and T3.2 are in force for the `document_intake` field definitions and the three lists LOV-DOC-SOURCE, LOV-SCAN-RESULT and LOV-OCR-STATUS.
- The Ownership Map is the only source of owners: `document_intake`, `document_hub_parameter` and `document` are P5's in `rwb_document`; `partner` is S9's in `rwb_partner`; `parameter_catalog`, `reference_row` and `lov_value` are P3's; the ACE views are P1's.
- The sibling baselines are published: RWB-P5-E1049-CON for the intake item submit and read, RWB-P5-E1032-CON for the review list and the resolve, and RWB-P5-E1041-CON for the scan result and the quarantine rule; none of their operations is re-declared here.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7), so its four H, C, I and X columns are empty and every dependant builds against the published baseline and its fakes.
- The release date 30 November 2026 is the legacy one and is tentative (ASM-1826), and the story carries Status Draft (realignment v1) because no approval of the realigned story is recorded (ASM-1836).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 document of `rwb-document` with the three admin operations, the two run resources of section 11 and the error responses of section 14, on the single base `/api/recovery/document/v1`.
2. Fix the run list and the run read: the paging default, the newest-first order, the per-channel counts and the per-result counts of one 15-minute window.
3. Fix the `IntakeRun`, `IntakeRunPage` and `IntakeRunChannel` shapes, so the operator reads one answer with the run, its channels and its reason counts, and the page carries its own paging fields.
4. Fix the channel code rule: a channel code is the branch code of a scanner folder, the literal MAILROOM, the partner code of an SFTP subfolder or the mailbox code, and it is a 40-character uppercase token rather than a free string.
5. Fix the enumerations: the three values of LOV-DOC-SOURCE on the run rows, the two values of LOV-SCAN-RESULT, the four values of LOV-OCR-STATUS, the three run states and the four result and refusal classes.
6. Map every failure to the error envelope and a message ID, status by status, and carry the missing names and the missing C row as a gap and an assumption.
7. Record the `Idempotency-Key` rule of the rerun operation and the channel-code, source-reference and hash key of a pickup, and declare that the two are different keys for different operations.
8. Declare the event position: this path publishes nothing, `DocumentStored` and `DocumentFieldsExtracted` are the catalogue's two events of the service, and a third name fails the absence test.
9. Publish the six fakes, the drift test and the baseline tag, then hand the baseline to RWB-P5-E1057-APP, RWB-S9-E1057-APP and the wave 1 harness.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A response body fails schema validation | The build fails on the schema lint; a deployed service answers 500 with the error envelope | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |
| X2 | A count, a channel row or a page field is renamed, removed or retyped within major version 1 | The contract test fails; the change needs a corrected document or a new major version | None | AC2 |
| X3 | A channel code is declared as a free string, or a run row carries a code the rule cannot produce | The contract test fails on the pattern and on the enum of the code | None | AC3 |
| X4 | A value outside LOV-DOC-SOURCE, LOV-SCAN-RESULT or LOV-OCR-STATUS appears on a run row, or an unknown run state is answered | The contract test fails on the enum | None | AC3, AC4 |
| X5 | A refusal is answered without its message ID, or a message ID with the wrong status | The contract test fails on the error envelope and on the status mapping of section 14 | MSG-GEN-004 | AC5 |
| X6 | A repeat of the same `Idempotency-Key` starts a second run, or a rerun of a live run is accepted | The contract test fails: one 202 and one 409 with MSG-GEN-004 | MSG-GEN-004 | AC5 |
| X7 | An event is declared for the pickup, or a fourth event name appears for the service | The absence test fails the build | None | AC6 |
| X8 | A fake drifts from the document | The drift test fails the build and the merge is blocked | None | AC7, AC8 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Criterion | Verdict | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Independent | Pass | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, TSD P5 T-A and T3, the Ownership Map and the three sibling baselines only |
| Negotiable | Pass | The field-level names are settled with the consumers; the operations, the channel code rule, the enumerations, the status mapping, the idempotency rules and the event position are fixed by the target architecture and the legacy section 12 |
| Valuable | Pass | Unblocks RWB-P5-E1057-APP, the operator screen of Epic 2, the partner slice RWB-S9-E1057-APP and the wave 1 harness on Day 1 |
| Estimable | Pass | One document, three resources, three operations, three consumed rows, nine contract tables and six fakes |
| Small | Pass | Fits one sprint with its contract tests |
| Testable | Pass | Every criterion in section 7 is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

The eight criteria are new for the contract baseline and test the artefact only; they restate no business outcome owned by RWB-P5-E1057-APP. The legacy AC1 to AC16 are owned by RWB-P5-E1057-APP (eleven) and RWB-S9-E1057-APP (five), and the wave 1 harness RWB-ITG-E1057-ITG consumes this baseline and copies none of these criteria.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One REST base per service: `/api/recovery/document/v1` on every declared operation | DP-01; Template and Rules §R4; Arch v5 slide 41 notes |
| BR2 | One topic per service: `rwb.document.events.v1`, with the retry and `.dlt` topics of the platform convention | DP-09; Arch v5 slides 16 and 42 |
| BR3 | A change inside major version 1 is additive; a removed, renamed or retyped property and a narrowed required set are a new major version | Architecture v5 slide 42 notes (BACKWARD compatibility) |
| BR4 | The document declares only tables of `rwb_document` and only operations owned by `rwb-document`; a consumed operation is described as consumed and faked, never as provided | Ownership Map; DP-01 |
| BR5 | No operation of this base is declared twice: the intake submit and the intake item read are RWB-P5-E1049-CON's and the review list and the resolve are RWB-P5-E1032-CON's | Ownership Map; the three sibling baselines |
| BR6 | No business value is fixed in the contract: the type list, the size limit, the duplicate window, the alert threshold, the channel values and the paging default are parameters, reference rows or document defaults | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17; RWB-E1-057 section 17 |
| BR7 | No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: identifiers, channel codes, counts, states and business dates only, and no sender address, no file name and no email subject in any payload | Arch v5 slide 11; RWB-E1-057 section 17 |
| BR8 | A channel code is a token of at most 40 characters and never a path, an address or a URL; the folder and the mailbox behind it stay in the property set of the deployment | RWB-E1-057 section 8 BR8; DP-15 |
| BR9 | The pickup publishes no event and the contract invents none: the two catalogued events of the service belong to the store and to extraction | Arch v5 slide 42; ASM-1841 |
| BR10 | Every error uses one envelope and one message ID per condition; the message texts are copied unchanged from legacy RWB-E1-057 section 14 | Architecture v5 platform baseline; Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR11 | A POST requires `Idempotency-Key` and stores its answer; a GET declares none; the rerun answers 202 and never 200 or 201 | Architecture v5 slide 11; DP-09; legacy section 12 |
| BR12 | The contract declares no channel and no run state machine beyond the values the fields may take; a transition belongs to the app story that performs it | RWB-E1-057 section 9; RWB-P5-E1057-APP owns the run and item transitions |

##### 9. State transitions

| Baseline state | Event | Condition | Next state |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The three operations, the three resources, the three consumed rows and the event position are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | RWB-P5-E1057-APP, RWB-S9-E1057-APP, the operator screen of Epic 2 and the wave 1 harness accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A property is added within major version 1, for example an optional `reasonCode` on a channel row | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A property is removed, renamed or retyped, or a required set is narrowed | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake, or a retired element returns | A contract test fails | In review |

This baseline declares no channel state machine and no run state machine of its own. The three run states are values of a field, and the transitions between them belong to RWB-P5-E1057-APP.

| Field value in the baseline | Meaning declared by this document |
|---|---|
| `state` = "running" | The Schedule has started the run and the channels are being read |
| `state` = "failed" | The run stopped on a channel; a rerun may start one run for the same window |
| `state` = "complete" | Every channel was read and the counts were written, whether or not any file was taken in |
| `source` = "SCAN" | A branch scanner folder or the mailroom folder |
| `source` = "PARTNER" | A partner SFTP subfolder named by the partner code |
| `source` = "EMAIL" | A recovery mailbox attachment |
| `scanResult` empty | The item was taken in and not yet scanned; the scan step sets the value |
| `ocrStatus` = "PENDING" | The item was taken in and not yet read; the OCR step moves it |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Tech lead of rwb-document | Owns the OpenAPI document, the AsyncAPI position and the six fakes; tags the baseline |
| Solution architect | Approves a breaking change, a new major version and the resolution of `GAP-1013` |
| Consuming teams (RWB-P5-E1057-APP, RWB-S9-E1057-APP, the operator screen of Epic 2, the wave 1 harness) | Review and sign off the parts they consume |
| RW-PLATADM, the platform administrator | Confirms that the run record and the rerun carry what the operator needs (Platform administration CRUD) |
| Platform library owner | Owns the CloudEvents envelope, the error envelope, the `Idempotency-Key` rule and the naming rule this document reuses |
| Data steward | Confirms that no personal data field is declared in an answer, an example or a fake |

The per-service login behind the document's security scheme is not part of this baseline; the document names the scheme "the rwb-document login (DP-02)" and the name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1013; ASM-1837). The declared area and right are enforced at gateway-bff (DP-19); no `rwb-access` contract is declared here.

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| IntakeRun | runId (uuid), businessDate, scheduleId (uuid), state (running, failed, complete), startedAt, endedAt, channels (array of IntakeRunChannel), takenIn, refused, duplicate, version, from the `document_intake` fields DF-DOC-045 to DF-DOC-063 grouped by `run_id` and `channel_code` |
| IntakeRunChannel | channelCode, takenIn, refused, duplicate, reasons (array of reasonCode and count); the channel code rule of AC3 |
| IntakeRunPage | items (array of IntakeRun), page, size, total; the list is newest first by businessDate and startedAt |
| Run state set | running, failed, complete |
| Result classes | taken in, refused, duplicate |
| Refusal reason codes | MSG-P5-001 for a type not allowed, MSG-P5-017 for a size above the limit, PARTNER_UNKNOWN and PARTNER_NOT_ACTIVE for the partner panel |
| Channel code | A token of 1 to 40 uppercase characters: a branch code, the literal MAILROOM, a partner code or a mailbox code |
| Error envelope | RFC 9457 problem details with `messageId`, `detail`, `instance` and the status of section 14 |

Every example in the document is synthetic and uses the legacy values: branch "BR-0123", branch "BR-0077", channel "MAILROOM", partner "LF-007", mailbox "MBX-RECOVERY-01", the file "scan-0001.pdf" of 1.2 MB, the 25.0 and 25.1 MB boundary and the 6 KB signature image. No example carries a real customer value, a real sender address or a real file name; the legacy values are examples only. The field-level names of `IntakeRun`, `IntakeRunChannel` and `IntakeRunPage` are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1013; ASM-1837), and the baseline fixes them as the smallest superset of the legacy job record.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-document (P5); base `/api/recovery/document/v1`.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/admin/jobs` | 200 `IntakeRunPage`; query `businessDate`, `state`, `page`, `size` 50, newest first | Platform administration R | None |
| GET | `/admin/jobs/{jobId}` | 200 `IntakeRun` with its channels and its reason counts | Platform administration R | None |
| POST | `/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun` | 202 `IntakeRun` of the started run | Platform administration U | `Idempotency-Key` header |

Error statuses 401, 403, 404, 409 and 503 are those of section 14. The legacy path `POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun` is rebased by DP-13 and the names of the three operations and of the two resources are the baseline's own (GAP-1013; ASM-1837). No intake submit, intake item read, review list, resolve or content operation is declared here, because RWB-P5-E1049-CON and RWB-P5-E1032-CON declare them (ASM-1838).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters/{paramCode}` | P3 rwb-case | `INTAKE_ALLOWED_TYPES`, `INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB`, `INTAKE_DUPLICATE_WINDOW_DAYS`, `INTAKE_MIN_IMAGE_KB` and `INTAKE_ALERT_AFTER_FAILURES` (C `RWB-P3-E1042-CON`) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 rwb-case | LOV-DOC-SOURCE, LOV-SCAN-RESULT and LOV-OCR-STATUS (C `RWB-P3-E1043-CON`) |
| GET | the partner-by-code read of rwb-partner | S9 rwb-partner | The partner ID, code and panel status behind a PARTNER channel code; one hop, 2 s, faked; the exact path is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1013; ASM-1839) and no C row of the plan carries it |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retry once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (DP-11, ADR-020). A failed read maps to 503 with MSG-GEN-006 naming the system that failed and never to a run answered as complete.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Declared position |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | — | — | This path publishes no event and holds no outbox row of its own. `rwb.document.events.v1` with its retry topics at 1 min, 10 min and 1 h and its `.dlt` topic carries `DocumentStored` and `DocumentFieldsExtracted`, published by the store of RWB-P5-E1024-APP and by the extraction of RWB-P5-E1053-APP (ASM-1841) |

The baseline declares the service topic and the two catalogue events because the service owns the topic, and it declares no third name. The absence test of AC6 and AC8 fails a build that declares a pickup event; the event catalogue owner confirms the position before the wave 1 release.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | — | — | The path is started by the intake Schedule, not by an event. `DocumentStored` with source UPLOAD is consumed by the `ingest` activity of RWB-P5-E1049-APP and not by this baseline, and `rwb.decision-record.v1` is not used by this path |

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Kind | Queue | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pickup` | Activity contract | `rwb-document` | One typed activity interface with the run slot in and the run counts out, idempotent by channel code, source reference and file hash; called by `DocumentIntakeWorkflow`; no workflow is declared here |
| `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` | Workflow, from the L3 "Document intake" template | `rwb-document` | Owned by RWB-P5-E1049-APP; this baseline names only the activity it contributes and the run record the activity writes |

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Schedule | Workflow | Queue | Interval | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| None | `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` | `rwb-document` | Every 15 minutes in business hours (JOB-12) | This baseline declares no Schedule and no cron entry; the Schedule is registered from the values of RWB-P5-E1057-OPS and its ID is the `scheduleId` of the run record |

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| `document_intake` | P5 (`rwb_document`) | The rows behind every count of the run record: `run_id`, `channel_code`, `source`, `source_ref`, `file_sha256`, `scan_result` and `ocr_status` |
| `document_hub_parameter` | P5 (`rwb_document`) | Contracted use only: the rows behind the five parameters |
| idempotency library table | PLT library, created in `rwb_document` | The `Idempotency-Key` row of the rerun and the channel-code, source-reference and hash key of a pickup |
| outbox, inbox library tables | PLT library, created in `rwb_document` | Created by the library migration; this path writes no outbox row of its own |

`partner` is S9's in `rwb_partner`, `parameter_catalog`, `reference_row` and `lov_value` are P3's, and the ACE views are P1's and are named as consumed answers and never declared as this service's tables (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| run fake | One run in each of the running, failed and complete states with the channel rows of branch "BR-0123", channel "MAILROOM", partner "LF-007" and mailbox "MBX-RECOVERY-01" | App story, operator screen, contract tests |
| refusal fake | One run per reason code, MSG-P5-001 for a DOCX, MSG-P5-017 for 25.1 MB, PARTNER_UNKNOWN and PARTNER_NOT_ACTIVE, with the 25.0 MB row taken in | App story, partner slice, contract tests |
| parameters and reference-data WireMock | The five parameters with `INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB` 25 and `INTAKE_DUPLICATE_WINDOW_DAYS` 30; the three lists with the five DOC-SOURCE, two SCAN-RESULT and four OCR-STATUS values | App story, contract tests |
| rwb-partner WireMock | Partner "LF-007" ACTIVE, a code that resolves to no partner, a partner SUSPENDED and a delayed answer beyond 2 s | App story, partner slice, contract tests |
| rerun fake | A 202 with the started run, a 409 with MSG-GEN-004 for a live run, a 404 with the not-found message and a 503 with MSG-GEN-006 | App story, operator screen, contract tests |
| error envelope fake | One answer per message ID of section 14 with its status and its `detail` text | Contract tests, operator screen |

A drifted fake fails the drift test of AC8. The exact response field names of the partner-by-code read are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1013; ASM-1839).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 3 provided, 3 consumed | The run list, the run read and the rerun; the parameters read, the lists read and the partner-by-code read; one hop and 2 s on every consumed call |
| Kafka | 0 published, 0 consumed; 1 topic position declared | `rwb.document.events.v1` carries the two catalogue events of the service and this path publishes neither; the idempotency library of RWB-PLT-TE006-CON is the only Kafka dependency |
| Temporal | 1 activity contract, 1 workflow named | `pickup` on queue `rwb-document`, called by `DocumentIntakeWorkflow`, which is owned by RWB-P5-E1049-APP; no Schedule |
| File | 0 byte carried | The run counts are counts of files the channels handed over; no file name, no path and no container reference is part of an answer |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** The OpenAPI 3.1 document `openapi/rwb-document-v1.yaml` with the three admin operations and the three resources; the contract README rows for the channel code rule, the enumerations, the state and result sets, the error mapping, the two idempotency rules, the event position and the operation-ownership boundary; and the six WireMock mapping sets of section 12.8.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/document/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The H, C, I and X lists of the metadata table are empty: this baseline adds no build dependency of its own (it is Day 1 by rule), and the platform and service contracts it names are the ones the app story declares. DP-01 is applied because every shape derives from rows of `rwb_document` and no other schema is declared. DP-06 and DP-07 are the two C rows: the five parameters and the three lists are read through the `rwb-case` contracts and never typed into the document. DP-09 fixes the topic position, the absence of a pickup event and the idempotency rules. DP-10 names the `pickup` activity contract and the workflow that calls it, without declaring a Schedule. DP-11 fixes the three consumed rows to one hop with 2 s and a fake each, including the partner read that carries no C row. DP-13 rebases the only legacy path on the service base. DP-15 records that the table behind the counts belongs to this service's own migration sequence. DP-19 records that the run record and the rerun are reached through the gateway-bff composite route; this baseline fixes the answer shapes only and no route specification.

**Build steps**

1. Write the three operations with their paths, queries, resources and error responses; validate the document in the pipeline.
2. Fix the required and optional sets of AC2 and the paging default as schema constraints and README rows.
3. Declare the channel code pattern, the three lists and the state and result sets of AC3 and AC4, with every list value named as a list and never typed.
4. Map every status and message ID of AC5 and record the RFC 9457 envelope, the 202 rerun and the two idempotency rules, including the not-found placeholder.
5. Record the event position of AC6 and the absence test for a pickup event.
6. Publish the six fakes and the eight contract tests, including the drift test; tag the baseline and collect the consumer sign-off of RWB-P5-E1057-APP, RWB-S9-E1057-APP, the operator screen of Epic 2 and the wave 1 harness.

**Done when.** The OpenAPI artefact validates in the pipeline, the eight contract tests pass, the six fakes answer every operation and read of sections 12.1 and 12.2, the drift test is green, and RWB-P5-E1057-APP, RWB-S9-E1057-APP and RWB-ITG-E1057-ITG have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | HTTP status |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P5-001 | A file type is not allowed (a refusal reason code, not an error) | This file type cannot be stored. Use PDF, JPG or PNG. | 200 |
| MSG-P5-017 | A file is above the size limit (a refusal reason code) | This file is larger than {size} MB and cannot be stored. | 200 |
| MSG-P5-007 | A file is refused at intake (a refusal text) | {source} file {file} was not taken in: {reason}. It is in the {folder} folder. | 200 |
| MSG-P5-008 | Two runs in a row fail on one channel (an alert text) | Document intake failed twice in a row for {channel}. Check the interface and job monitor. | 200 |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A dependency is not available or the storage refuses the write | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. | 503 |
| MSG-GEN-004 | The run is still in progress or the idempotency key changed the record | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. | 409 |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | 403 |
| MSG-P4-001 | No authenticated caller | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1013; ASM-1837) | 401 |
| not-found message | A run that does not exist | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1013; ASM-1840) | 404 |

The message IDs and the wording are contract elements copied unchanged from RWB-E1-057 section 14; Thai text for each follows decision DL10. MSG-P4-001 and the not-found message are named by the target error envelope and are copied from the platform set, and their exact texts are recorded as the placeholder above.

Delivery shape: every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set to the ID above, `detail` carrying the text with its placeholders filled, and `instance` naming the request. The status mapping is the legacy one plus the two platform rows: 202 for an accepted rerun, 401 with MSG-P4-001, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404 with the not-found message, 409 with MSG-GEN-004 and 503 with MSG-GEN-006. The four refusal and alert texts of the run record are never answered as an error status.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-44 Interface and job monitor of Epic 2 is the screen these operations serve, reached through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), which calls the owner once and merges the answer into the screen model; the screen itself belongs to Epic 2 and the run record is published by RWB-P5-E1057-APP. This baseline fixes the answer shapes only and declares no screen field list and no route specification. The states its shapes imply are: a run in each of the three states, a channel row per channel read, a refusal count per reason code, a duplicate count, and a rerun that is refused because the run is still in progress.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the type list, the size limit, the duplicate window, the alert threshold, the channel values and the paging default stay parameters, reference rows or document defaults of the app story.
- No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: identifiers, channel codes, counts, states and business dates only, and no sender address, no file name and no email subject.
- The channel code is a token and never a path, an address or a URL; the folder and the mailbox behind it stay in the property set of the deployment (BR8).
- No operation of this base is declared twice: the intake submit and read, the review list, the resolve and the content read belong to the sibling baselines (BR5).
- ACE data is reached only through the owner's contract or a `v_ace_*` view; this document declares no ACE view and no cross-schema join (DP-01).
- The contract names only `rwb_document` tables and only operations owned by `rwb-document`; a foreign base or a foreign table fails the review (DP-01).
- One REST base and one topic per service; a document that names another service's base or topic as its own fails the review.
- The path publishes no event and the contract invents none; a pickup event name fails the absence test (BR9).
- Every example in the document is synthetic and the legacy values are examples only; no production payload is copied into a schema or a fake.
- The contract declares no channel state and no run state machine beyond the values the fields may take; a transition belongs to RWB-P5-E1057-APP.
