**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-057 for rwb-document. The legacy story assumed four channels configured as Spring properties on a single monolith node, a shared scheduler, a shared schema and an operator who could open the job record in the database. On the infrastructure side this story provisions the branch-folder, mailroom, partner SFTP and mailbox pickup channels as environment configuration with their credentials and their folder lifecycle, the compute of the intake workers against queue `rwb-document`, the storage and the hold container `rwb-quarantine` with its clearing rule, the topic `rwb.document.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics and its least-privilege ACLs, the managed identity and the secret layout, the partner file route and the DMZ position, and the scanning capacity that bounds the intake. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As an **infrastructure engineer**, I want **the channel-intake path of `rwb-document` provisioned as infrastructure — the branch scanner folders and the mailroom folder on the bank file service, the partner SFTP inbound root with one subfolder per partner code and its PGP and key handling, the recovery mailboxes and the mailbox reader identity, the intake worker pool that serves the 15-minute business-hours run on queue `rwb-document`, the storage and the hold container `rwb-quarantine` with its clearing rule, the topic `rwb.document.events.v1` with its three retry topics, its `.dlt` topic and its least-privilege ACLs, the workload identity and the four secret classes of the path, the private route to `rwb-case`, `rwb-partner` and Blob with no public inbound rule, and the scanning capacity that bounds the rate at which files enter the matcher**, so that **the pickup activity runs on Day 1 against provisioned folders, mailboxes, queue and storage, a file that comes from a partner over the DMZ path reaches the hold container without a public endpoint anywhere, and no secret, no partner key and no mailbox credential sits in a values file or in a script**.

The legacy story had one paragraph for this work: the channels "are set per environment by the platform administrator in properties", the mailboxes "are read by the SY-OCR managed identity", the intake and quarantine containers "exist and SY-OCR writes to the intake container by managed identity", and the partner panels "are loaded". Under D-RCV-60 each of those is provisioned separately and none of them is a property of a monolith node any more:

- the four channels become four environment configuration blocks of one service deployed on AKS in the `rwb-recovery` namespace, with their own credentials (ASM-1844);
- the SFTP inbound root becomes a platform MFT/SFTP resource with one subfolder per partner code and PGP for the outside party, and it is the same file path the platform provisions for the outside file transfers of the architecture (Arch v5 slide 11; ASM-1845);
- the mailboxes become a mailbox reader identity with its own grant and its own scope, because reading a shared recovery mailbox is a permission and not a folder (ASM-1846);
- the intake compute becomes a Temporal worker pool on queue `rwb-document` scaled on the queue backlog, because the trigger is a Schedule and not a Quartz row (DP-10);
- the intake container and the quarantine container are one hold container `rwb-quarantine` with one rule and one clearing step (RWB-P5-E1032-INF);
- the partner side of the network becomes an explicit DMZ decision, because partners reach the bank only through the partner gateway, and a partner file path that is not the gateway must be shown to be private as well (Arch v5 slide 35; ASM-1847);
- the scan becomes a capacity, because the intake rate is bounded by the scan rate and not by the matcher (FSD P5 A2.18; ASM-1849).

The path has one property that shapes the provisioning: a picked-up file is personal data from the moment it is copied, and a recovery mailbox is a shared inbox nobody owns. The provisioning therefore fixes three rules alongside the capacity: a file is scanned before it is matched and the unscanned file waits in `rwb-quarantine`, the mailbox reader sees only the declared mailboxes and never the whole tenant, and the hold container is cleared by a stated rule rather than by an operator's memory.

##### 2. Business rationale

About 860,000 documents arrive in 2027 (NFR-004) and the hub holds about 5.8 million documents and 2.8 TB by the end of 2031, including every version and every held document (NFR-069). Every one of them comes through this path: a branch scan, a mailroom scan, a partner file or a mailbox attachment becomes one `document_intake` row and one file in the hold container, and then a page set in `document_text` and a document on a case. If the worker pool is sized for a demonstration, the 15-minute run falls behind and the channels accumulate; if a branch folder has no lifecycle, a processed folder fills the branch file share and the scanner stops writing; if a mailbox is read with a grant wider than the four declared mailboxes, a personal inbox is read by a machine identity; if the partner subfolder is reachable from anywhere but the private path, a partner's evidence file is one hop from the internet.

The private path matters as much. Zero trust requires the service to reach `rwb-case`, `rwb-partner`, the Kafka brokers, the Temporal frontend and Blob over private endpoints with a workload identity (Arch v5 slide 35; NFR-052, NFR-053). A public endpoint added for a test is a security finding that survives to production, and a partner SFTP key pasted into a values file turns a rotation into a rebuild.

The 15-minute cadence is the legacy one and the architecture one: JOB-12 runs every 15 minutes, owned by `rwb-document` (Arch v5 slide 44; FSD P5 AC-BG-P5-013-01). The legacy story says "every 15 minutes in business hours"; the architecture slide gives no business-hours qualifier, so the Schedule and the compute are sized for the business-hours cadence and the difference is recorded as `GAP-1014`.

The scan capacity is the one element the legacy story names only as an existing step: every inbound file is scanned before it is stored (FSD P5 A2.18; RWB-P5-E1041-APP), so the intake rate is bounded by the scan rate and not by the OCR or the matcher. This story provisions that capacity and states the rule that an item waits in the hold container rather than entering the matcher unscanned.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The platform subscription, the resource group and the network (virtual network, subnets, private DNS zones) of the environment are available, and the AKS cluster of the ACE platform is reachable from the `rwb-recovery` namespace.
- The workload identity of rwb-document is registered in each environment, so every access is bound to an identity and not to a shared credential (DP-02).
- RWB-PLT-N012-INF provisions the standard Blob account, the key store and the MFT/SFTP resources; this story consumes the Blob account, the key store and the MFT/SFTP root for the channel path.
- RWB-PLT-N002-INF provisions the 20 event topics with their 60 retry topics and their 20 dead-letter topics, so `rwb.document.events.v1`, its three retry topics and its `.dlt` topic exist before this story binds the ACLs.
- RWB-PLT-N003-INF provisions the namespace `rwb-recovery`, its certificates and the payload codec, so queue `rwb-document` can be polled.
- RWB-PLT-DB provisions the `rwb_document` schema and the rwb-document login; this story creates no schema, no table and no grant, and the migration is RWB-PLT-E1044-CON's sequence applied by the release of RWB-P5-E1057-OPS.
- The partner gateway of the edge epic is in place in its DMZ, fronting `rwb-partner` with FAPI 2.0, so a partner API call has a route and a partner file path has a boundary to be measured against (Arch v5 slide 35).
- The scanning product of RWB-P5-E1041-APP exists as a service call, so the capacity provisioned here is the cluster and network capacity around it and not a scanner binary.
- The baseline RWB-P5-E1057-CON is published, so the three admin operations of the app story and their status codes are known to the network and the identity work.
- No build dependency and no contract dependency in the plan of this key; this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).
- The release date 30 November 2026 is the legacy one and is tentative (ASM-1826), and the story carries Status Draft (realignment v1) because no approval of the realigned story is recorded (ASM-1843).

##### 4. Flow

1. List what the path needs: the four channel configurations, the file-service folders and their lifecycle, the SFTP inbound root and its partner subfolders with their key material, the mailbox reader identity and its scope, the worker pool and its queue, the storage and the hold container, the topic and its four derived topics, the six service principals it talks to, the five secret classes, the network routes with their DMZ position, and the scan rate.
2. Provision the branch-folder channel: a scanner folder per branch code, a processed folder and a rejected folder per branch, the write grant the branch scanner holds and the read, move and delete grants the rwb-document identity holds, and the age rule that clears a processed folder after the stated period.
3. Provision the mailroom channel: one mailroom folder with its processed and rejected folders and the same grant pattern.
4. Provision the partner SFTP channel: the inbound root, one subfolder per partner code, the processed and rejected subfolders, the host key and the client key of each partner in the key store, the PGP key pair for the encrypted file of an outside party, and the read-only grant the partner holds on its own subfolder only.
5. Provision the mailbox channel: the four declared mailboxes, the mailbox reader identity with its application permission scoped to those mailboxes and to no other, the archive folder per mailbox, and the rule that the reader may move a message and may not delete one.
6. Size the worker pool for the 15-minute business-hours cadence: the `pickup` activity runs on queue `rwb-document`, the pool scales on the queue backlog through KEDA, and the request and limit set of the activity is fixed as values per environment.
7. Size the storage for `document_intake` and its two indexes against the 860,000 documents a year of NFR-004 and the 2.8 TB estate of NFR-069.
8. Provision the hold container `rwb-quarantine` for a picked-up file with its access rule (managed identity only), its one-file-per-link claim-check read through the storage product and its clearing rule on scan, discard or age; verify the two containers `rwb-docs` and `rwb-docs-legal` against the store's own provisioning.
9. Verify the topic `rwb.document.events.v1` with its 12 partitions, replication factor 3, 7-day retention and key caseId and its four derived topics; provision nothing new if RWB-PLT-N002-INF already did it, and bind the ACLs: the rwb-document principal writes its own topic and the shared `rwb.decision-record.v1` and reads nothing of another service.
10. Put the login, the Kafka credential, the Temporal mTLS material, the storage identity binding and the channel credentials in the key store behind the workload identity, and write the rotation entry for each class.
11. Apply the private route: private DNS and private endpoints for `rwb-case`, `rwb-partner`, the brokers, the Temporal frontend and Blob; the partner file path documented against the DMZ position of the partner gateway; no public inbound rule on the service; egress to the named endpoints only.
12. Set the scan rate as a value, wire the queue-age alert to it, and run the six tests of section 16 against the provisioned state.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A branch or mailroom folder does not exist, or the scanner's write grant is missing | The channel is reported failed, the run names the branch code and the other channels still run | MSG-P5-E1057-INF-01 | AC1 |
| X2 | The partner SFTP host key or a partner client key does not match | The handshake is refused, the subfolder is not read, and the failure counts towards the two-run alert of the app story | MSG-P5-E1057-INF-01 | AC1, AC4 |
| X3 | The mailbox reader identity has no grant on a declared mailbox, or a grant wider than the declared mailboxes | The read is refused and audited; a wider grant fails the access review and the release | MSG-P5-E1057-INF-01 | AC1, AC4 |
| X4 | The worker pool is saturated and the queue backlog grows past its threshold | The pool scales out on the backlog; if the ceiling is reached the run takes longer and the run book names the ceiling as the cause | MSG-P5-E1057-INF-02 | AC1 |
| X5 | The hold container is unreachable or refuses the write of a new file | The file stays at its channel, the run fails and no row is committed; the storage alert fires and the run book names the container | MSG-P5-E1057-INF-03 | AC2 |
| X6 | A processed or rejected folder is past its age rule | The clearing job moves the file to the archive tier and records the count; no file of a channel is deleted while a run refers to it | MSG-P5-E1057-INF-03 | AC2 |
| X7 | A principal writes to a topic it does not own, or reads a topic where the event catalogue lists no consumer | The broker refuses the operation and the attempt is audited | MSG-P5-E1057-INF-01 | AC3 |
| X8 | A credential, certificate, partner key or identity binding expires or is rotated out | The dependency fails closed, the channel reports not ready and the rotation entry restores the version; no clear-text fallback exists | MSG-P5-E1057-INF-02 | AC4 |
| X9 | A partner subfolder is reachable from a public address, or a public inbound rule appears on the service | The network scan fails the change and the release is blocked | MSG-P5-E1057-INF-04 | AC5 |
| X10 | The scan rate falls below the intake rate | Files wait in the hold container and the queue age rises; the alert fires and the run book names the scan capacity | MSG-P5-E1057-INF-03 | AC6 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Provisions channels, folders, mailboxes, compute, storage, a container rule, a topic binding, ACLs, identity, route and scan capacity; no application code is built here and no service build blocks it |
| Negotiable | Branch codes, folder names, mailbox codes, replica counts, request and limit sets, storage budgets, the clearing age, the backlog threshold and the scan rate are environment values settled with the platform and network teams |
| Valuable | Gives the app and operations stories provisioned channels, a ruled hold container and a private path on Day 1, with no secret in a values file and no partner key in a script |
| Estimable | Four channel configurations, one worker pool, one storage and index budget, one hold container with a rule, one topic binding, one ACL set, one identity layout with five secret classes, one route set and one scan capacity |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the runbook entries and the six tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against provisioned state, a refused operation, a folder rule, a route or a scan, never against a business outcome |

```gherkin
Feature: Infrastructure of the channel-intake path for rwb-document

    Then the four declared mailboxes exist and the mailbox reader identity holds an application permission scoped to those mailboxes and to no other, with move but no delete
    Then the worker pool polls the task queue rwb-document in namespace rwb-recovery and nothing else, and the pickup activity carries its request and limit set as environment values and not in code
    Then the pool scales on the queue backlog through KEDA, with a floor that keeps one poller and a ceiling that is a value
    When a business-hour backlog is replayed
    Then every batch of the 15-minute cadence finishes before the next one starts

  Scenario: AC2 The intake storage and the hold container are provisioned with their rule and their clearing (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the storage of rwb_document and the storage account of the environment
    Then document_intake carries its unique key on channel code, source reference and file hash and its indexes on the channel, the hash and the run, and the storage budget is set against the 860,000 documents a year of NFR-004 and the 5.8 million documents and 2.8 TB of NFR-069
    Then rwb-quarantine exists with a private endpoint and access for the rwb-document workload identity only
    Then a picked-up file is readable through one claim-check link at a time and is never copied into a second container or a message
    Then rwb-docs and rwb-docs-legal exist as the store provisions them, rwb-docs-legal keeps the immutability policy of the storage product and no blob of any container is overwritten
    Then the clearing rule states the three events that clear a held file: the scan result, a discard by the owner role, or the age rule carried as GAP-1014
    Then the clearing job never deletes a file whose item is still open, and it records the item for the owner role instead
    Then the processed and rejected folders of every channel carry an age rule and a move to the archive tier

  Scenario: AC3 The topic, its retry and dead-letter topics and the ACLs are bound to the service (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the topics provisioned by the platform event epic
    Then rwb.document.events.v1 exists with 12 partitions, replication factor 3, 7-day retention and the key caseId
    Then the three retry topics at 1 min, 10 min and 1 h and the .dlt topic exist with the same partition count
    Then the rwb-document principal writes rwb.document.events.v1 and rwb.decision-record.v1 and reads no topic of another service
    Then the consumer groups of rwb-case and rwb-agent read rwb.document.events.v1 and nothing else of this service
    Then this path binds no consumer group for the pickup, because the pickup writes rows and publishes no event
    When the rwb-document principal writes another service's topic
    Then the write is refused and the attempt is audited
    Then no Recovery ACL opens an ACE PII logging topic

  Scenario: AC4 The identity, the secret layout and the channel credentials rotate under a runbook entry (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the key store of the environment and the workload identity of rwb-document
    Then the rwb-document login, the Kafka credential, the Temporal mTLS material, the storage identity binding and the channel credentials are held there and bound to the workload identity
    Then the channel credentials are the mailbox reader secret or certificate, the partner SFTP host key, one client key per partner and the PGP key pair of the outside-party file
    Then a secret scan of the values, the scripts, the runbook and the image finds no secret, no partner key and no connection string
    When a credential, a partner key or a certificate reaches its rotation point
    Then the rotation entry stages the new version, switches the channel or the principal and retires the previous version
    Then a channel with an expired credential fails closed, reports not ready and reads nothing
    Then the mailbox permission is re-reviewed at every rotation and a wider grant blocks the release

  Scenario: AC5 The partner file route is private and the DMZ position is documented (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the network rules, the partner gateway of the edge epic and the MFT/SFTP resources
    Then the service reaches rwb-case, rwb-partner, the Kafka brokers, the Temporal frontend and Blob over private endpoints resolved by private DNS
    Then the partner SFTP inbound root is reachable only over the private MFT/SFTP path and never from a public address, and the partner's own side reaches it outbound from its own network
    Then the document records the DMZ position: partner API traffic terminates at the partner gateway with FAPI 2.0 and partner file traffic terminates at the MFT/SFTP root, and neither reaches the service directly
    Then no public inbound rule answers on the service and egress is admitted to the named endpoints only
    When a connection arrives from outside the allow-list, on the SFTP root or on the service
    Then it is refused before authentication and logged
    Then an outside-party file is PGP-encrypted and its checksum is verified on receipt

  Scenario: AC6 The scanning capacity bounds the intake and the queue age is alerted (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the network rules and the scanning product of the environment
    Then every inbound file is scanned before it enters the matcher, and an unscanned item waits in rwb-quarantine
    Then the scan rate of the environment is a value and the queue-age alert of the intake is wired to it
    When the scan rate is set below a replayed intake rate
    Then the queue age rises, the alert fires with MSG-P5-E1057-INF-03 naming the scan capacity, and no file enters the matcher unscanned
    Then the capacity is sized against the 15-minute cadence and the 860,000 documents a year of NFR-004
    Then the scan product and its provider are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1014; ASM-1849)
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One worker pool polls one task queue: queue `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, and no other queue | Arch v5 slides 20, 41 and 44; DP-02 |
| BR2 | The intake cadence is 15 minutes in business hours (JOB-12), served by a Temporal Schedule and not by a Quartz job or a shared scheduler | Arch v5 slide 44; FSD P5 AC-BG-P5-013-01; DP-10 |
| BR3 | A channel is configuration and not code: a branch folder, the mailroom folder, the SFTP root and the mailboxes are environment values, and no path, address or branch code is written in a class | RWB-E1-057 section 8 BR8; DP-15 |
| BR4 | The SFTP inbound root is one subfolder per partner code and a partner holds a read-only grant on its own subfolder only | RWB-E1-057 section 8 BR4; Arch v5 slide 11 |
| BR5 | The mailbox reader identity holds a grant on the declared mailboxes only, may move a message and may never delete one | CTL-11; Arch v5 slide 35 |
| BR6 | A picked-up file lives in the hold container `rwb-quarantine` until it is scanned; it is never copied into a second container and never put in a message | Arch v5 slide 11; RWB-P5-E1041-APP |
| BR7 | Every event topic has three retry topics and one dead-letter topic, and the ACLs are least privilege and separate from the ACE PII logging topics | Arch v5 slides 11 and 21; DP-09 |
| BR8 | No secret in code, configuration, a values file or a script; the five secret classes live in the key store behind the workload identity and rotate under a written entry | NFR-052; Arch v5 slide 35 |
| BR9 | Every dependency is reached over a private endpoint resolved by private DNS, and a partner file path reaches the bank only through the private MFT/SFTP route or the partner gateway in its DMZ | Arch v5 slide 35 |
| BR10 | Capacity is provisioned for the volume the sources state: about 860,000 documents a year (NFR-004) and 5.8 million documents and 2.8 TB by 2031 (NFR-069), including every held file | NFR-004; NFR-069 |
| BR11 | Every inbound file is scanned before it enters the matcher; the scan rate bounds the intake rate and an unscanned item waits in the hold container | FSD P5 A2.18; RWB-P5-E1041-APP |
| BR12 | This story provisions channels, capacity, storage, a container rule, a topic binding, an identity, a route and a scan: it registers no Schedule, builds no reader and writes no business rule | Arch v5 slides 16, 38 and 44; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |

##### 9. State transitions

Channel lifecycle.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Requested | Provisioning approved | The grant, the endpoint and the credential are known | Provisioned |
| Provisioned | Identity bound | The workload identity resolves to read and move on the folder or the mailbox | In use |
| In use | Credential rotated | The rotation entry stages a new version | Rotating |
| Rotating | Version switched | The channel answers with the new credential | In use |
| In use | Credential expired and not rotated | The channel fails closed | Not ready |
| Not ready | Rotation entry applied | The version is restored or advanced | In use |
| In use | Channel retired | No partner subfolder or mailbox is declared and the age rule has run | Retired |

Picked-up file.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| At the channel | `pickup` accepts the file | The type, the size and the duplicate check pass | In the hold container with a row |
| In the hold container | The scan step runs | The scan answers | CLEAN and matched, or INFECTED and quarantined |
| At the channel | `pickup` refuses the file | A rule refuses it | In the rejected folder of the channel |
| In the hold container | The item is attached or discarded | The owner role resolves it | Cleared from the hold container |
| In the hold container | The age rule is reached | The item is still open | Reported to the owner role, not deleted |
| In a processed folder | The age rule is reached | The file has been moved for the stated period | Archive tier |

Worker pool.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Provisioned | Backlog rises | The queue backlog passes the threshold value | Scaling out |
| Scaling out | Backlog clears | The backlog falls below the threshold | At floor |
| At floor | Ceiling reached | The backlog keeps rising at the ceiling | Saturated |
| Saturated | Capacity raised | The ceiling value is raised and applied | Scaling out |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| SCB IT infrastructure | Owns the story, the four channels, the folders and their lifecycle, the capture compute, the storage budgets, the hold container, the identity bindings, the route and the scan capacity |
| ACE platform team | Owns the brokers, the schema subjects, the quotas and the namespace; approves every ACL change |
| Platform team | Owns the key store, the workload identity, the private DNS zones, the storage account and the MFT/SFTP resources |
| Network and security | Own the partner gateway and its DMZ, the private endpoints, the public-access scan and the PGP requirement; approve any relaxation |
| Branch operations and the mailroom | Own the scanners and the folders their scan writes into; confirm the branch codes and the mailroom folder |
| Partner and agency manager | Confirms the partner codes, the SFTP subfolders and the PGP keys of the partners (partner portal CRUDA) |
| rwb-document owner | Consumes the queue, the storage, the container references and the channel configuration; owns the pickup, the run record and the migration |
| rwb-case and rwb-agent owners | Consume `rwb.document.events.v1` through their groups; they never write it |
| Data steward | Confirms that no folder, no mailbox, no topic and no metric carries personal data beyond the ruled path |
| RW-AUDIT and RW-SECADM | Read the ACL trail, the key-rotation trail, the mailbox permission review and the public-access scan |

The branch codes, the folder names, the mailbox codes, the replica counts, the request and limit sets, the storage budgets, the clearing age, the backlog threshold and the scan rate are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1014; ASM-1848). The rwb-document login name is Not specified in the source documents either; it is held as a secret reference and never written in a values file.

| Topic binding | `rwb.document.events.v1` with 12 partitions, replication factor 3, 7-day retention, key caseId, three retry topics and one `.dlt` topic; `rwb.decision-record.v1` as the shared topic | Arch v5 slides 11 and 42; DP-09 |
| ACLs | Producer: rwb-document on its own topic and the shared topic. Consumers: rwb-case and rwb-agent on `rwb.document.events.v1`. No consumer group for the pickup. No ACL on a PII logging topic | Arch v5 slides 21, 35 and 42 |
| Secrets | The rwb-document login, the Kafka credential, the Temporal mTLS material, the storage identity binding and the channel credentials, in the key store behind the workload identity | NFR-052; Arch v5 slide 35 |
| Network | Private DNS and private endpoints for `rwb-case`, `rwb-partner`, the brokers, the Temporal frontend and Blob; the SFTP root on the private MFT path; the partner gateway in its DMZ; no public inbound rule; egress to the named endpoints only | Arch v5 slide 35; ASM-1847 |
| Scan capacity | The scanning product call of RWB-P5-E1041-APP, its throughput as a value, and the queue-age alert wired to it | FSD P5 A2.18; ASM-1849 |
| Observability hooks | Queue backlog and age, batch duration against the 15-minute cadence, channel failures per channel code, folder age, held-file age, scan rate, retry and `.dlt` counts, dependency health; no file name, no sender address and no page text | ADR-023; CTL-11 |
| Absent by design | No shared Quartz scheduler, no shared schema, no second copy of a picked-up file, no public inbound rule, no tenant-wide mailbox grant, no data-lake route, no ACE view grant | D-RCV-35 U1; ADR-010; DP-01; DP-17 |

The names, numbers and sizes of the table above are environment values of the resource files in section 13; they are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1014; ASM-1848) and this story fixes only their shape and the rule that no value is written in code.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** `infra/channels/branch.yaml` and `infra/channels/mailroom.yaml` (the folder set, the grants and the age rule of each branch and of the mailroom), `infra/channels/sftp.yaml` (the inbound root, the per-partner subfolders, the host key reference, the per-partner client key references, the PGP key pair and the grants), `infra/channels/mailbox.yaml` (the four mailboxes, the archive folder, the reader identity, its scoped grant and the move-only rule), `infra/compute/workers.yaml` (the pool, the KEDA rule, the floor and the ceiling, the request and limit set, the queue and the namespace), `infra/storage/database.yaml` (the storage and index budget of `document_intake`), `infra/storage/hold.yaml` (the hold container, its private endpoint, its rule and its clearing rule, and the two store containers verified), `infra/kafka/bindings.yaml` (the topic settings, the retry and `.dlt` verification, the producer and consumer ACLs), `infra/security/identity.yaml` (the workload identity bindings, the five secret classes and the rotation entries), `infra/network/rules.yaml` (the private endpoints, the private DNS records, the DMZ position of the partner paths, the egress allow-list and the absence of a public inbound rule), `infra/scan/capacity.yaml` (the scan rate and the queue-age alert) and `runbooks/channels-hold-and-scan.md` (the channel check, the hold rule, the clearing step, the scan capacity check and the escalation).

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON (of the app story) |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON (of the app story) |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON (of the app story) |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON (of the app story) |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/document/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON (of the app story) |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON (of the app story) |

DP-01 is applied by sizing one schema and one login: `document_intake` lives in `rwb_document`, no cross-schema read is provisioned and no ACE view is granted. DP-06, DP-07 and DP-09 appear because the capacity this story provisions carries the paths those patterns run on: the parameters, the lists and the idempotency rows all need the private routes, the identity and the topic binding that are provisioned here; their H dependencies are the app story's and are not carried by this story. DP-10 is the substantive change: the Quartz job on a shared scheduler becomes a Temporal Schedule on queue `rwb-document`, so this story sizes a worker pool against a queue and a backlog, provisions the four channels a poller reads, and registers no Schedule of its own. DP-11 fixes the partner read to a private endpoint with a 2 s client budget. DP-13 is applied by absence: this story exposes no REST path of its own, and the rebased base is the app story's. DP-15 keeps the migration with the service sequence, so this story creates no table and no grant. DP-19 records that the run record is reached through the gateway-bff composite route, and the only network consequence here is that the service answers the edge privately.

**Build steps**

1. Write the branch and mailroom channel inventory: the folder set per branch code, the grants, the age rule and the scanner write pattern.
2. Write the SFTP channel: the inbound root, one subfolder per partner code, the processed and rejected subfolders, the host key, one client key per partner, the PGP key pair and the read-only per-partner grant.
3. Write the mailbox channel: the four mailboxes, the archive folder, the reader identity, the scoped application permission and the move-only rule; run the permission review that proves no wider grant.
4. Write the compute inventory: the queue, the namespace, the KEDA rule, the floor and the ceiling, and the request and limit set of `pickup`.
5. Size the storage: the item rows, the unique key, the two indexes and the growth budget against NFR-004 and NFR-069.
6. Provision the hold container `rwb-quarantine` and verify the two store containers; write the clearing rule and the folder age rules.
7. Verify the topic settings and the retry and `.dlt` topics against RWB-PLT-N002-INF, and bind the producer and consumer ACLs.
8. Place the five secret classes in the key store, bind them to the workload identity and write the five rotation entries.
9. Apply the private endpoints, the private DNS records, the DMZ position of the two partner paths and the egress allow-list, and run the public-access scan that proves no inbound rule answers on the service or on the SFTP root.
10. Set the scan rate as a value, wire the queue-age alert and add the channels-hold-and-scan runbook entry that names the scan capacity as the cause of a rising queue.
11. Hand the queue, the channel configuration, the storage budget, the container references, the identity and the scan rate to the app and operations stories, and run the six tests of section 16.

**Done when.** The four channels exist with their grants and their lifecycle, the pool scales on the queue backlog and keeps the 15-minute cadence in a replayed business-hour window, the hold container exists with its rule and its clearing rule is exercised, the topic and its four derived topics carry the ACLs of BR7, no secret or partner key appears in a values file or a script, the public-access scan finds no inbound rule on the service or on the SFTP root, the mailbox grant is scoped to the four mailboxes, the scan capacity bounds the intake, and the six tests of section 16 pass against the provisioned state.

| MSG-P5-E1057-INF-01 | A channel is not reachable, a grant is missing, a key does not match, or a principal attempts an operation its ACL does not allow | The channel or the topic {component} refused the operation. Follow the rotation or grant entry of the runbook. |
| MSG-P5-E1057-INF-02 | The worker pool is saturated, a dependency is not ready, or a credential has expired | The intake path is not ready: {component}. Follow the rotation or capacity entry of the runbook. |

The four messages are the infrastructure texts of this story and are new; no legacy business message is renumbered or reworded by them. The business messages of section 14 of the app story are unchanged, and a refused channel is reported to the operator through the run record of AC1 and, at run time, through MSG-P5-008 of the app story naming the channel code.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a resource file: the type list, the size limit, the duplicate window, the alert threshold and the channel values stay parameters or reference rows, never a literal in the infrastructure.
- No personal data in a file name, a manifest, a log, a trace attribute or an alert: channel codes, counts, sizes, states and hashes only, and never a sender address, a partner's file name or a page text.
- No second copy of a picked-up file: the hold container is the only store until the scan, no topic and no message receives the file, and the claim-check link is one read at a time (BR6).
- No secret, no partner key and no mailbox credential in code, configuration, a values file or a script; the five secret classes are read with the workload identity (BR8, NFR-052).
- No public inbound rule and no open egress: every dependency is reached over a private endpoint resolved by private DNS, and the SFTP root is reachable only over the private MFT path (BR9).
- The mailbox reader grant is scoped to the declared mailboxes and is re-reviewed at every rotation; a wider grant blocks the release (BR5).
- A partner holds a read-only grant on its own subfolder only, never on the root and never on another partner's subfolder (BR4).
- No ACE grant and no ACE view for this service; only rwb-source-data reads the views (DP-01).
- No data-lake endpoint, route or landing container is provisioned, because the data lake is removed (DP-17).
- A file is never deleted while its item is open, and a processed folder is cleared by move to the archive tier and never by delete (BR6).
- An item is never matched unscanned: the scan is a condition of entering the matcher (BR11).
- No Schedule, no workflow and no activity is registered by this story; the queue and the channels are provisioned and the Schedule is the deployment story's (BR12).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-057 for rwb-document. The legacy story ran JOB-12 on a shared Quartz scheduler behind a shared schema, held the four channel paths as Spring properties of one monolith node, and expected an operator to read the job record in the database. This story deploys the channel-intake capability of `rwb-document`: one chart and its values, the `rwb_document` migration step, the 15-minute intake Schedule registered in Temporal on queue `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, the channel configuration and its four flags, the dashboards for the channels and the run states, the four alerts with their message identifiers, the runbook and the rollback. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform engineer**, I want **the channel-intake capability of `rwb-document` deployed as one Helm release with its values files, its per-service Flyway step in `rwb_document`, the channel configuration of each environment behind the flag `rwb.document.intake` and its four sub-flags, the 15-minute intake Schedule registered in Temporal on queue `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, the dashboards that show a channel that was read, a channel that failed and a folder that is filling, the four alerts with their message identifiers, and a runbook with its rollback**, so that **an operator can see a channel that stopped reading, a run that failed on one channel, a branch folder whose processed folder is filling and a mailbox whose grant was withdrawn, take the channel out of service with one flag without a redeploy, and prove that no file was taken in twice and none was lost when the flag was switched or the release was rolled back**.

The legacy story ran the pickup behind a shared Quartz scheduler, a shared schema and a property file: JOB-12 fired on the scheduler table, `IntakeStep` wrote the recovery schema, and the four channel paths were entries in a monolith's properties. In the target that picture splits in four. JOB-12 is a Temporal Schedule in the service that owns it, so the release registers the Schedule and the worker that serves it (DP-10). The migration is one step of the service's own Flyway sequence in `rwb_document` (DP-15). The channel configuration is one value block per environment, injected as configuration and never built into the image (BR6). The four channels have one feature switch each, so a branch, the mailroom, the SFTP root or the mailboxes can be taken out of service without a redeploy. What is left for this story is a chart, a migration gate, a Schedule, a configuration block, four switches, six dashboard series, four alert rules, five runbook entries and a rollback.

Deployment is also where the split is enforced operationally. The release carries the rwb-document login only, migrates `rwb_document` only, publishes on its own topic and on the shared decision-record topic only, polls `rwb-document` only, and reads only the channels of its own environment. It provisions no ACE grant, no view and no data-lake route (DP-01, DP-05, DP-17), and no inbound consumer of this path, because the trigger is the Schedule. The observability follows ADR-023 per service: six series, four alerts and five runbook entries, each alert carrying a message identifier and one runbook entry.

##### 2. Business rationale

The business measure of this legacy key is documents on the case the same day (FSD P5 AC-BG-P5-013-01), and the operational measure behind it is simple: a channel that stops reading must be visible before the case owner asks where a scan went. Neither is a unit test. A branch folder whose grant was withdrawn, a partner key that expired, a mailbox whose permission was removed, a run that failed at 10:15 and a processed folder that is filling the branch file share are all silent unless the release emits them and the run book says what to do.

The split changes what an operator does. In the legacy story the operator restarted a Quartz job and read the job record in the same database. In the target the operator reads the Schedule's run history and the run record of the app story, restarts through the Schedule, takes one channel out of service through its own switch, and confirms three things: that the worker polled `rwb-document`, that the channel that failed is named, and that the files it did not take in are still at the channel so the next run reads them. The runbook is written for that sequence, because the difference between a busy morning and an incident is whether the operator has to guess which of the four channels stopped.

The story also carries the retirement explicitly. No Quartz job, no scheduler table and no shared schema is deployed; the Schedule is the only timer, and a release that registers a second one or a job on a foreign queue fails its own checks (BR1, BR2, BR3). The switches keep a channel reversible without a schema change, and the rollback keeps the previous build serving open runs.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template, the chart skeleton and the pipeline are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-LIB).
- The Kafka event platform provides `rwb.document.events.v1` with its three retry topics and its `.dlt` topic and the shared `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and the ACLs of this service's principals (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON; DP-09).
- The Temporal workflow kit and the namespace `rwb-recovery` exist, with worker versioning, the build ID provider and the payload codec (RWB-PLT-WF, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON; DP-10).
- The per-service Flyway sequence and the migration conventions of `rwb_document` are published (RWB-PLT-E1044-CON; DP-15).
- The platform error envelope, the message catalogue and the feature-flag library are in force, so an alert can carry a message identifier and a channel can be switched in one environment.
- The three environments DEV, SIT and UAT exist and the production namespace exists for the release date.
- The four channels, the worker compute, the hold container, the topic binding, the ACLs, the identity and the private routes exist in each environment (RWB-P5-E1057-INF).
- The gateway-bff composite route for the run record is published (RWB-PLT-N001-CON; DP-19).
- The pickup activity and the run record are declared (RWB-P5-E1057-APP), so the release deploys a capability that exists and not a shell.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7). The baseline it deploys is RWB-P5-E1057-APP's and the values it injects are RWB-P5-E1057-INF's; both are declared before the release and neither blocks the chart work.
- The release date 30 November 2026 is the legacy one and is tentative (ASM-1826), and the story carries Status Draft (realignment v1) because no approval of the realigned story is recorded (ASM-1850).

##### 4. Flow

1. The pipeline builds the service image and the contract jar, runs the unit, component and contract tests, scans the image and the dependencies, and publishes one chart version.
2. The chart deploys the API deployment and the worker deployment with the rwb-document login, the namespace `rwb-recovery`, the task queue `rwb-document`, the codec, the build ID of the release and the values of RWB-P5-E1057-INF.
3. The worker scaling step enables KEDA on the queue backlog of `rwb-document`, so the pool grows with the 15-minute run and the front stays at its fixed replica count.
4. The migration step applies the `rwb_document` sequence of the release and refuses to run when the target schema is not `rwb_document`; the intake migration `V1057_1__intake_channels.sql` is one step of it.
5. The channel step renders the four channel blocks of the environment — the branch folders by branch code, the mailroom folder, the SFTP root and the mailboxes with their processed, rejected and archive folder names — as configuration, and the Deployment states that no path, no branch code and no mailbox address is in the image.
6. The topic step verifies `rwb.document.events.v1` with its partitions, its replication factor, its retention, the three retry topics at 1 minute, 10 minutes and 1 hour and its `.dlt` topic, and records the ACL of the producer and of the consumer groups.
7. The Schedule step registers the intake Schedule: workflow `DocumentIntakeWorkflow`, queue `rwb-document`, namespace `rwb-recovery`, every 15 minutes in business hours, overlap policy skip and a catch-up window of one run, its ID fixed by the release so a second apply changes nothing.
8. The flag step sets `rwb.document.intake` and its four sub-flags `rwb.document.intake.branch`, `.mailroom`, `.sftp` and `.email` from the values of the environment; the legacy name `rwb.dochub.intake` and its four sub-flags are recorded as retired and are not deployed (ASM-1856).
9. The dashboards are published with the six series and the environment, release and build ID as dimensions.
10. The four alerts are wired to their message identifiers and to their runbook entries: MSG-P5-E1057-OPS-01 for a channel that is not ready, MSG-P5-008 for two failed runs in a row, MSG-P2-004 for a failed run, and MSG-P5-E1057-OPS-02 for a folder or a held file past its age rule.
11. A smoke step in DEV drops one synthetic file in a SIT branch folder and one in the mailroom folder, waits for one Schedule run, confirms one intake row per file, one move to each processed folder and one refused file in a rejected folder, switches the branch flag off to see the channel skipped, and confirms that the environment is restored.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The chart render or the migration job fails | The deployment stays unready and the pipeline stops; no traffic, no offset and no migration is left half applied | None | AC1 |
| X2 | The migration step is pointed at a schema other than `rwb_document` | The step refuses and the release stops | None | AC1 |
| X3 | A channel block is missing from the values of an environment, or a branch code has no folder | The render fails with the missing key named; a channel with no configuration is not deployed | MSG-P5-E1057-OPS-01 | AC1, AC3 |
| X4 | A channel path, a branch code or a mailbox address appears in the image or in a chart template | The configuration check fails the release | None | AC1, AC3 |
| X5 | A run of the intake Schedule fails, or runs past its threshold | The run-failure alert fires with MSG-P2-004 naming the run, the time and the runbook path; the Schedule retries on its next interval | MSG-P2-004 | AC2, AC4 |
| X6 | Two runs in a row fail on one channel | The channel alert fires with MSG-P5-008 naming the channel code and the runbook entry | MSG-P5-008 | AC4, AC6 |
| X7 | A dependency is not available, or its credential has expired | The run fails closed, the file stays at its channel, the channel alert fires with MSG-P5-E1057-OPS-01 and the runbook entry names the rotation | MSG-P5-E1057-OPS-01 | AC4, AC6 |
| X8 | The Schedule is registered twice, or a foreign job is registered on the queue | The Schedule check fails the release: one Schedule ID, one workflow, one queue | None | AC2 |
| X9 | A dashboard series is missing, or an alert carries no message identifier or no runbook link | The observability check fails the release | None | AC4 |
| X10 | A new build is promoted while runs are open | The open runs replay on the new build from their history; the dashboards show both build IDs | None | AC1, AC4 |
| X11 | A channel is switched off in an environment | The channel is skipped and the run completes with zero on it; a switched-off channel is not an error and is not counted as failed | None | AC6 |
| X12 | The lag of the attach-event consumer group passes its threshold | The lag alert fires; the runbook entry names the group, the topic and the partition | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1015; ASM-1854) | AC4 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the chart skeleton, the workflow kit, the topic provisioning, the migration conventions, the flag library and the channel values; no application code is built here |
| Negotiable | Replica counts, resource sizes, lag and age thresholds, intervals and quotas are environment values |
| Valuable | Makes the four channels observable, restartable and reversible before the release date, and keeps a channel switchable without a redeploy |
| Estimable | One chart, one migration gate, one Schedule, one channel block with four switches, six series, four alerts and five runbook entries |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the runbook |
| Testable | Every criterion tests an artefact: the chart renders, the migration refuses a foreign schema, the Schedule exists once, an alert fires on a synthetic metric, a switch skips a channel, the smoke run passes |

```gherkin

    Given the target environment is SIT

    Then worker versioning is enabled and a new run goes to the new build while the old build drains

    Then the partner SFTP block carries the inbound root and the processed and rejected subfolder names, and no partner key is written in a values file
    Then the mailbox block carries the declared mailbox codes and their archive folder names, and no mailbox address is written in a values file beyond the reference the environment supplies

  Scenario: AC4 The dashboards and the four alerts fire with their identifiers (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published dashboards and alert rules of the deployment

    Then the dashboards show runs by state, files taken in per channel, refusals per reason code, duplicates per channel, the age of the oldest held file, and the queue backlog and age of the task queue

    Then the rollback redeploys the previous chart with its own build ID and the open runs finish on the old build
    Then the Schedule keeps its ID across the rollback and points at the same workflow, so only the build under it changes
    Then the smoke run ends with one intake row per synthetic file, one move to each processed folder, one refused file in a rejected folder and the environment restored

  Scenario: AC6 The feature switches take one channel out of service without a redeploy (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the feature-flag library and the deployed release

    When the switch rwb.document.intake is turned off and one Schedule run is waited for

    Then a switch change needs no rebuild, no migration and no restart of the worker
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One login, one task queue and one schema per service: the release carries the rwb-document login, polls `rwb-document` only and migrates `rwb_document` only | Arch v5 slide 41; DP-02; DP-15 |
| BR2 | The release publishes on `rwb.document.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1` only and subscribes to no topic of this service | Arch v5 slides 16, 42 and 43; DP-09; DP-14 |
| BR3 | One Schedule and one scheduler: the intake Schedule is the only timer for JOB-12, registered in Temporal on queue `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery`; no Quartz job, no scheduler table and no cron entry exists | Arch v5 slide 44; DP-10; `ASM-1851` |
| BR4 | Each of the four channels is switchable by its own flag, and the whole path by `rwb.document.intake`, which replaces the legacy `rwb.dochub.intake` | legacy section 13; DP-14; `ASM-1856` |
| BR5 | A channel is configuration and never code: the branch folders, the mailroom folder, the SFTP root and the mailboxes come from the values of the environment and never from the image | RWB-E1-057 section 8 BR8; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR6 | No partner key, no mailbox credential and no connection string is written in a values file, a chart template, a dashboard or the runbook; all of them come from the platform secret store | NFR-052 |
| BR7 | Every alert carries a message identifier and the agreed text and links one runbook entry | Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR8 | No environment value is hard-coded: replicas, resources, thresholds, intervals, quotas, channel blocks and flags come from values files and parameters | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR9 | Dashboard series, alert payloads and the runbook carry counts, channel codes, statuses, business dates and build IDs only, never a file name, a sender address or a customer identifier | ADR-023; CTL-11 |
| BR10 | A failing release never replaces a working one: the previous build stays in force until the new build passes its tests and its smoke run, and the Schedule keeps its ID across a rollback | DP-10 |
| BR11 | A file the run did not take in is never deleted and never moved by an operator: it stays at its channel for the next run, and a switched-off channel is skipped and never failed | R-UNI-40; legacy X4, X10, X11 |
| BR12 | The release provisions no ACE grant, no view, no data-lake route and no inbound consumer of this path | D-RCV-35 U1; ADR-010; DP-05; DP-17 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | Chart published | The image, the chart and the contract tests pass | Deploying |
| Deploying | Migration applied and worker registered | The `rwb_document` sequence applied and the worker polls `rwb-document` | Ready |
| Ready | Channel blocks rendered | Every channel block of the environment is present and no path is in the image | Configured |
| Configured | Schedule registered | One Schedule with the release ID, the workflow and the queue | Scheduled |
| Scheduled | First run completes | The run finishes and its counts reach the dashboards | In use |
| In use | Release superseded | A new chart version passes its tests | Rolling |
| Rolling | All workers on the new build | The old build drains its open runs | In use |
| In use | A channel switch is turned off | `rwb.document.intake.<channel>` is off in the environment | Partly in use |
| Partly in use | The switch is turned on again | The next run reads the channel | In use |
| In use | Smoke run failed | The Schedule check, the alert check or the smoke step fails | Blocked |
| Blocked | Previous build restored | The previous chart is redeployed or a later build passes the smoke run | In use |

The run states running, failed and complete and the intake item states of the app story are its runtime and are not states of this deployment.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| DevOps engineer | Owns the chart, the values files, the pipeline stages, the migration gate, the channel block, the Schedule step, the dashboards and the runbook |
| Platform administrator | Owns the `rwb-recovery` namespace, the Schedule, the topic ACLs, the consumer quotas, the flag library and the restart of a run |
| Platform event owner | Owns `rwb.document.events.v1`, its retry and `.dlt` topics, its schema subject and its retention |
| Network and security | Own the partner key material, the mailbox grant and the public-access scan; approve any relaxation |
| Release manager | Approves the promotion of one artefact and may block it on a failing smoke run |
| On-call operator | Runs the five runbook entries and opens an incident when a failed run, a channel that is not ready or a filling folder persists |
| rwb-document owner | Owns the pickup, the run record and the migration the release applies |
| Data steward | Confirms that no dashboard, alert or runbook carries a file name, a sender address or a customer identifier |
| RW-AUDIT | Reads the run history, the alert trail and the runbook |

The worker runs as the rwb-document service identity (DP-02), carried by the chart as a secret reference and never as a literal. The login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1015; ASM-1852). The partner keys and the mailbox credential are secret references, and the values file carries the reference name and never the value.

##### 11. Data

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Deployment values | Image digest, chart version, replica counts for the API and the worker, resource requests and limits, probe paths and timings, log level, namespace, task queue, build ID, feature switches, KEDA backlog threshold, Schedule ID and interval (ASM-1852) |
| Channel block | The branch entries with their scanner, processed and rejected folder names; the mailroom entry with its folder names; the SFTP root with its processed and rejected subfolder names; the mailbox entries with their codes and archive folder names; and the secret reference names of the partner keys and the mailbox credential. The values are the environment's and are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1015; ASM-1851) |
| Task queue | `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, polled by the worker of this service only |
| Topic | `rwb.document.events.v1` with its partitions, replication factor, retention and key, its three retry topics and its `.dlt` topic; `rwb.decision-record.v1` published by the library; no subscription of this service |
| Schema | `rwb_document`, migrated by its own per-service Flyway sequence; the intake migration `V1057_1__intake_channels.sql` is one step of it |
| Schedule | The intake Schedule: `DocumentIntakeWorkflow`, queue `rwb-document`, namespace `rwb-recovery`, every 15 minutes in business hours (JOB-12), overlap policy skip, catch-up window one run, ID fixed by the release |
| Flags | `rwb.document.intake` and `rwb.document.intake.branch`, `.mailroom`, `.sftp` and `.email`, on in DEV and SIT for the tests, from the values of each environment; the legacy `rwb.dochub.intake` and its four sub-flags are retired |
| Dashboard series | Runs by state, files taken in per channel, refusals per reason code, duplicates per channel, age of the oldest held file, queue backlog and age; dimensions environment, release, build ID |
| Runbook entries | Failed run, channel not ready, expired partner key or withdrawn mailbox grant, filling processed folder or held file past its age rule, lagging consumer group; each with the check, the owner role and the recovery step |
| Alerts | Four rules and one runbook entry each: MSG-P5-E1057-OPS-01 for a channel not ready, MSG-P5-008 for two failed runs in a row on a channel, MSG-P2-004 for a failed run, MSG-P5-E1057-OPS-02 for a folder or held file past its age rule; the lag alert carries the identifier placeholder of GAP-1015 |
| Secrets | The rwb-document login secret, the Kafka client credential, the Temporal mTLS material, the storage identity reference, the partner SFTP keys and the mailbox credential, all from the platform secret store |
| Test data | One synthetic file in a branch folder, one in the mailroom folder, one refused file and one flag-off run; synthetic identifiers only |

The deployment topology (cluster names, node pools, replica counts, resource sizes, zone spread, ingress class and probe timings) belongs to each environment and is set by the platform team in its values file; the chart exposes every one of them as a value and this story fixes only their names and the rule that they are never hard-coded.

**Probes.** Readiness answers healthy only after the worker has polled `rwb-document` once and the API has answered its health path; liveness answers healthy when the process is up and its internal loop is responsive. Neither probe reads a channel, writes to the database or commits an offset, and a failing dependency is reported as not ready, never as live-and-broken.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

| Method | Path | Owner | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | — | — | The three admin operations — `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/admin/jobs`, `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}` and `POST /api/recovery/document/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun` — are declared by RWB-P5-E1057-CON and implemented by RWB-P5-E1057-APP; this deployment exposes them through the chart and its ingress and declares no path of its own. The probes are cluster-internal and are not part of the API surface |

| Method | Path | Owner | Story | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| None | — | — | — | The deployment carries no REST client of its own. At run time the app story's client reaches `rwb-partner` and the shared clients reach `rwb-case` over the private routes of RWB-P5-E1057-INF; the chart's only start-up calls are the Temporal frontend, the Kafka brokers and the health paths of its own dependencies |

| Event | Topic | Owner | Key | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| None | — | — | — | This path publishes no event. `rwb.document.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1` are bound by the release and written by the store and by the local decision-record library through the relay (DP-03, DP-09); the deployment publishes nothing of its own |

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | — | — | This path consumes no event: the trigger is the intake Schedule. The consumer groups of `rwb-case` and `rwb-agent` on `rwb.document.events.v1` are theirs and not deployed here |

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Deployment element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` | Workflow, from the L3 "Document intake" template | `rwb-document` | Registered by the worker of this release with the build ID and worker versioning; owned by RWB-P5-E1049-APP |
| `pickup` | Activity | `rwb-document` | Registered by the same worker with the kit's retry policy; owned by RWB-P5-E1057-APP |

**Build ID and versioning.** The build ID is the one supplied by the workflow kit for the release commit; worker versioning is enabled and a new build takes new runs while the old build drains. The build ID format and the versioning policy are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1015; ASM-1853).

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Schedule | Workflow | Queue | Interval | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| The intake Schedule (JOB-12 Document intake) | `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` | `rwb-document` | Every 15 minutes in business hours | Registered by this release from its values, with the ID fixed by the release, overlap policy skip and a catch-up window of one run; a run that fails is retried on its next interval and the files it did not take in stay at their channels. The exact business-hours window and the catch-up policy are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1015; ASM-1851) |

No other Schedule, cron entry or Quartz job is registered by this release (BR3).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|
| `document_intake` | P5 (`rwb_document`) | Created or altered by the `rwb_document` sequence of the release; written by the app story, never by the deployment |
| `document_hub_parameter` | P5 (`rwb_document`) | Created by the store's migration; the five parameter rows are loaded as data by the reference data administrator, never as a chart value |
| idempotency library table | PLT library, created in `rwb_document` | Created by the library migrations in the same schema; written by the app story |
| outbox, inbox library tables | PLT library, created in `rwb_document` | Created by the library migrations in the same schema; this path writes no outbox row of its own |

The release applies the `rwb_document` sequence of this key and no other: no ACE view, no other service's table and no lake object is created, altered or read (DP-01, DP-05, DP-15, DP-17).

| Fake | Story | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| None | — | No fake is deployed. The contract fakes of RWB-P5-E1057-CON and the channel and storage fixtures of RWB-P5-E1057-INF are test-only workloads and are not promoted into SIT, UAT or production |

| Call type | Count | Detail |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | The release migrates `rwb_document` only and reads no other schema | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | The five parameters stay rows read through the client library; no chart value carries them | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | The three lists stay reference rows; no chart value carries them | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | The topic with its retry and `.dlt` topics and the ACLs; the path binds no consumer group | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | The worker, the task queue, worker versioning and the intake Schedule from the kit; no Quartz job | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | The release declares no REST path and no client of its own; the private routes are RWB-P5-E1057-INF's | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | The ingress registers the service base `/api/recovery/document/v1` and declares no path of its own | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | The `rwb_document` sequence with its intake step and a foreign-schema refusal | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | The ingress registers the service base for the gateway-bff edge; no screen is deployed | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-10 is the substantive row of this story: JOB-12 stops being a Quartz job on a shared scheduler and becomes a Temporal Schedule on the service's own queue, so the release registers the Schedule, the worker and the build ID, and the operator restarts a run through the Schedule rather than a scheduler table. DP-01 and DP-15 keep the migration inside `rwb_document` and make the step refuse a foreign schema. DP-02 is not in the pattern list of the key and is applied by the chart anyway: one login, carried as a secret reference. DP-06 and DP-07 keep the parameters and the three lists out of the values files. DP-09 binds the topic and its four derived topics and subscribes to nothing. DP-11 and DP-13 are applied by absence: the release declares no REST path of its own and no client. DP-19 registers the ingress path the edge calls and deploys no screen.

**Artefacts**

| Artefact | Content |
|---|---|
| `helm/rwb-document/` overlay | API deployment, worker deployment, config map, secret references, probes, task queue, namespace, build ID, KEDA rule, Schedule definition, channel block and the five switches |
| `helm/rwb-document/values-dev.yaml`, `values-sit.yaml`, `values-uat.yaml` | Image digest, replicas, resources, probe timings, log level, flag values, build ID, Schedule ID and interval, KEDA threshold, container references, the four channel blocks and the secret reference names (ASM-1852) |
| Pipeline stage | Build, unit and contract tests, image and dependency scan, chart publish, migration gate, channel configuration check, topic step, Schedule step, smoke run, promotion |
| Migration step | The `rwb_document` sequence with `V1057_1__intake_channels.sql`; a target schema other than `rwb_document` is refused |
| Channel step | The four channel blocks as configuration per environment and the check that no path, no branch code and no mailbox address is in the image or a template |
| Topic step | `rwb.document.events.v1` with its three retry topics and its `.dlt`, the producer ACL and the consumer ACLs of rwb-case and rwb-agent |
| Schedule step | The intake Schedule with its release ID, the workflow, the queue, the interval, the overlap policy and the catch-up window, idempotent on the ID |
| Dashboards | The six series of section 11 with the three dimensions |
| Alerts | Four rules, each with a message identifier or its placeholder and one runbook entry |
| Runbook | Five entries: failed run, channel not ready, expired partner key or withdrawn mailbox grant, filling processed folder or held file past its age rule, lagging consumer group |

**Alert mapping**

| Message ID | Condition | Alert | Route |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P5-E1057-OPS-01 | A channel is not reachable, its grant is missing or its key does not match | Channel-not-ready alert naming the channel code, the run and the grant or key class | Platform on-call and network security, page |
| MSG-P5-008 | Two runs in a row failed on one channel | Channel alert naming the channel code, the two runs and the runbook path | Platform on-call, page in business hours, else ticket |
| MSG-P2-004 | A run of the intake Schedule failed or ran past its threshold | Run-failure alert naming the Schedule ID, the run, the time, the business date and the runbook path | Platform on-call, page in business hours, else ticket |
| MSG-P5-E1057-OPS-02 | A processed or rejected folder, or a held file, is past its age rule | Age alert naming the folder or the item count per channel | Branch operations, the mailroom and the data steward, ticket |
| Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1015; ASM-1854) | The attach-event consumer group lags past its threshold | Lag alert naming the group, the topic, the partition and the lag | Platform on-call, ticket |

**Retry and offsets.** The Schedule retries a failed run on its next interval and never runs two runs at once, because the overlap policy is skip. The activity retry is the kit's three attempts with back-off; the deployment adds no retry of its own. A file the failed run did not take in is still at its channel and is read by the next run, so no replay tool and no offset reset is part of this runbook.

**Rollback.** A release that fails the smoke run is not promoted. A release already promoted is rolled back by redeploying the previous chart version with its own build ID, which keeps the old build serving its open runs until they finish; the Schedule keeps its ID and points at the workflow, so a rollback changes the build under it and not the timer. Files a failed run did not take in are still at their channels and are read again; no data repair is needed, because the release writes no business row of its own and the migration is additive.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.document.intake` and its four sub-flags. On: the pickup reads the channels. Off: the channel is skipped and the run completes with zero on it. A switch change is a configuration change in the flag library, needs no rebuild, no migration and no restart, and is not a way to stop a run in progress, which is what the Schedule and the runbook are for. The legacy name `rwb.dochub.intake` and its four sub-flags appear in no value, chart or runbook (ASM-1856).

**Done when.** The chart renders for DEV, SIT and UAT with a pinned digest and the build ID, the migration step refuses a foreign schema, the four channel blocks render as configuration with no path in the image, one Schedule exists with the release ID and the queue `rwb-document` and a second apply changes nothing, a switched-off channel is skipped and never failed, the six series and the four alerts are published with their identifiers or placeholders and their runbook links, the smoke run produces one row per synthetic file, one move per processed folder, one refusal and no duplicate, and the five runbook entries are reviewed by the on-call rota. The alert thresholds, the intervals, the catch-up window and the channel values are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1015; ASM-1851).

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P5-E1057-OPS-01 | A channel is not ready, its grant is missing or its key does not match | Channel {channel} of document intake is not ready. Follow run book {runbook}. |
| MSG-P5-E1057-OPS-02 | A folder or a held file is past its age rule | {resource} of document intake is past its age rule. Follow run book {runbook}. |
| MSG-P2-004 | A run of the intake Schedule failed or ran past its threshold | {job} failed at {time} for business date {date}. Follow run book {runbook}. |
| MSG-P5-008 | Two runs in a row failed on one channel | Document intake failed twice in a row for {channel}. Check the interface and job monitor. |
| Identifier pending | The attach-event consumer group lags past its threshold | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1015; ASM-1854) |

MSG-P5-008 is the legacy alert text of section 14 of RWB-E1-057 and is unchanged. MSG-P2-004 is the job-failure text of the observability epic and is used here with its agreed wording. MSG-P5-E1057-OPS-01 and MSG-P5-E1057-OPS-02 are the deployment's own two texts and are new; no legacy business message is renumbered or reworded by them. The lag alert has no identifier in the source set, so it carries the placeholder until the Error and Message Standard names it. An alert payload names counts, channel codes, statuses, business dates, the Schedule ID, the build ID and group names only, never a file name, a sender address, an account number or a customer identifier.

##### 15. Screens and states

The deployment has no screen of its own. Its operator-facing surfaces are the pipeline run view, the release view, the Temporal Web UI, the dashboards, the folder and mailbox inventories of the file service and the mail service, the run record of RWB-P5-E1057-APP through the gateway-bff composite route, and the runbook. The run record is served by the app story and the route of RWB-PLT-N001-CON; the deployment only registers the ingress path. The Temporal Web UI stays behind Entra ID: RW-PLATADM operates and RW-AUDIT reads, and payloads are decoded only through the codec server under break-glass. SCR-44 Interface and job monitor belongs to Epic 2 and shows the same run data from there; this release publishes the records the monitor reads.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a values file: the type list, the size limit, the duplicate window, the alert threshold and the channel values are parameters and reference rows, never a deployment value.
- No personal data in logs, dashboard series, alert payloads, the runbook or the workflow history: counts, channel codes, statuses, identifiers, business dates and build IDs only, and payloads stay encrypted.
- No partner key, no mailbox credential and no connection string in a values file, a chart template, a dashboard or the runbook; all of them come from the platform secret store (BR6, NFR-052).
- One login, one task queue and one schema per service: the release carries the rwb-document login, polls `rwb-document` and migrates `rwb_document` only (DP-02, DP-15).
- A channel is configuration and never code: the branch folders, the mailroom folder, the SFTP root and the mailboxes come from the values of the environment and never from the image (BR5).
- The release deploys no ACE grant, no view, no data-lake route and no inbound consumer of this path (DP-05, DP-17, BR12).
- One Schedule and one scheduler: no Quartz job, no scheduler table and no cron entry besides the intake Schedule (BR3).
- An operator never deletes a file at a channel and never resets a cursor to make a file reappear; the next run reads it (BR11).
- The release pins the image digest, the chart version and the build ID; a rebuild between environments is not allowed, and a failing smoke run never replaces a working build.
