**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: integration slice of RWB-E1-057 for RWB-ITG-W1. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **QA integration engineer**, I want **the end-to-end proof of the RWB-E1-057 intake step across P5 rwb-document (the intake item, the scan result and the JOB-12 intake step of DocumentIntakeWorkflow), S9 rwb-partner (the panel status behind the partner channel), P1 rwb-source-data (the job view and the rerun) and P4 rwb-access (the Platform administration right U)**, so that **every branch scan, mailroom scan, partner file and email attachment enters the same intake with its source recorded, proved on the real SIT services before wave 1 exits**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story adds intakeStep as the first step of the JOB-12 DocumentIntakeJob, a Spring Batch job inside the document module, and writes document_intake in the single recovery schema. The target keeps document_intake in rwb_document (Owner P5, Architecture v5 slides 16 and 41), runs JOB-12 as an event-started workflow with KEDA workers on queue rwb-document (Architecture v5 slide 44), reads the partner panel status through the S9 rwb-partner contract instead of an in-process PartnerDirectory call (DP-11), shows and reruns the run through the P1 rwb-source-data job contract on SCR-44, and reads the intake parameters as data rows of the P5 document hub parameter table. The branch scanner folders, the mailroom folder, the partner SFTP inbound folder and the recovery mailboxes stay as they are: they are properties set per environment, and the mailbox service (Exchange Online read through Microsoft Graph) is outside the 19 services. The run evidence that shows the S9 partner check is the suite's own report, JOB-12 runs and reruns are read through P1's admin job contract (ASM-0499), and a failed step is restarted by the P5 workflow's retry policy (ASM-0498).

The legacy measures stay as they are: REQ-DCM-009 (documents arrive from branches, the mailroom, partner file transfer and email through the same intake, so every document path ends in the document hub) and REQ-DCM-010 (every inbound file is virus-scanned before it is stored). CTL-11 is kept too: a customer document never moves by email hand-off, so the mailbox channel is read by the platform identity and the sender address is masked.

No service contract is faked. The suite exercises the published wave 1 contracts of P5 rwb-document, S9 rwb-partner, P1 rwb-source-data and P4 rwb-access, the Temporal namespace rwb-recovery and four external channel endpoints; the only stubs are the external ones named in section 12.8.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P5-E1057-APP is done: document_intake, the intakeStep activity of DocumentIntakeWorkflow and the four channel readers are in SIT.
- RWB-S9-E1057-APP is done: the partner panel with partner_code and panel_status is readable through the rwb-partner contract.
- The published contracts of P5 rwb-document, S9 rwb-partner, P1 rwb-source-data and P4 rwb-access are deployed under their own per-service bases behind gateway-bff: /api/recovery/document/v1, /api/recovery/partner/v1, /api/recovery/source-data/v1 and /api/recovery/access/v1.
- Temporal namespace rwb-recovery with task queue rwb-document is available.
- The partner panel rows are real synthetic SIT rows: partner "LF-007" a law firm with panel_status "ACTIVE", partner "LF-008" with panel_status "SUSPENDED", and no partner with partner_code "LF-099".
- The four external channel endpoints exist as properties of the SIT environment: the scanner folders by branch code, the mailroom folder, the partner SFTP inbound folder with one subfolder per partner_code, and the recovery mailboxes. The mailboxes are read through the mailbox stub of section 12.8.
- The document hub parameter rows are loaded: INTAKE_ALLOWED_TYPES PDF, JPG, PNG; INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB 25; INTAKE_DUPLICATE_WINDOW_DAYS 30; INTAKE_MIN_IMAGE_KB 10; INTAKE_ALERT_AFTER_FAILURES 2 (legacy values, all assumed; ASM-0497).
- The synthetic fixtures of harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG are loaded for branch, mailroom, partner SFTP and mailbox channels.
- The feature flag rwb.dochub.intake and its per-channel sub-flags are on.
- No production data is used, and no production connection is opened.
- The release date 30 November 2026 is tentative; a date is not a condition of this story.
- No build dependency: the story is Day 1 and waits on no build of its own.

##### 4. Flow

1. QA integration engineer: loads the synthetic fixtures of harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG; no production data is used.
2. Harness: writes one file to the scanner folder of branch "BR-0123", one to the mailroom folder, one to the SFTP subfolder "LF-007" and one email to mailbox "MBX-RECOVERY-01", all synthetic.
3. Harness: reads the panel status of "LF-007", "LF-008" and "LF-099" through GET /api/recovery/partner/v1/partners and records the answers as run evidence (AC2, AC5, AC7, AC16).
4. Harness: lets the 09:15 run of JOB-12 start and reads the run through GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs, with its state and its intakeStep counts per channel (AC1, AC9).
5. Harness: reads each taken-in item through GET /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId} and asserts source, channel_code, captured_at, file_sha256, an empty scan_result and ocr_status PENDING (AC1, AC2, AC3).
6. Harness: asserts the file moves — the channel file is gone and is in its processed folder, the refused file is in its rejected folder, and the email is in the archive folder (AC1, AC3, AC4, AC6).
7. Harness: posts the refused files — a DOCX, a 25.1 MB PDF next to a 25.0 MB PDF — and reads MSG-P5-001, MSG-P5-017 and MSG-P5-007 on the job record (AC4).
8. Harness: posts the partner exceptions — subfolder "LF-099" with no partner_code and subfolder "LF-008" with panel_status "SUSPENDED" — and reads MSG-P5-007 with PARTNER_UNKNOWN and PARTNER_NOT_ACTIVE (AC5, AC7).
9. Harness: repeats the same hash "H1" from "BR-0123" on 2 December after 30 November and asserts one row and a duplicate count (AC6).
10. Harness: switches the intake container fault control on, runs, then restores it and reruns through the P1 job contract (AC8, AC10, AC15).
11. Harness: makes the SFTP subfolder unreadable for two runs and reads MSG-P5-008 naming PARTNER_SFTP, then lets the 10:30 run finish (AC10).
12. Harness: starts the second rwb-document instance and waits for the 09:15 run, then observes scanStep and ocrStep on one item and the trigger window at 18:15 (AC11, AC12, AC14).
13. Harness: reads one intake item per file across the four channels and the DocumentIntakeWorkflow execution with the partner check in its evidence, writes the evidence report and removes the synthetic fixtures (AC16).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | File type not allowed | No intake row; file moved to the rejected folder; counted as refused | MSG-P5-001, MSG-P5-007 | AC4 |
| X2 | File above the size limit | No intake row; file moved to the rejected folder | MSG-P5-017, MSG-P5-007 | AC4 |
| X3 | Partner subfolder code unknown or partner not ACTIVE | No intake row; file moved to the rejected folder | MSG-P5-007 | AC5, AC7 |
| X4 | Same hash from the same channel inside the window | No new row; file moved to processed; counted as a duplicate | None | AC6 |
| X5 | No new file or email on any channel | Run logged with zero counts | None | AC9 |
| X6 | The intake container does not accept writes | Files left at the channel; run failed; next run takes them | MSG-GEN-006 | AC8 |
| X7 | Two runs in a row fail on one channel | Alert to the platform administrator | MSG-P5-008 | AC10 |
| X8 | Two service instances are due at once | The run starts once and each file has one row | None | AC11 |
| X9 | A consumed contract call exceeds the 2 s timeout or returns a server error | The scenario is retried and the evidence report records the call and the response; no assertion is made on unverified data | None | AC1, AC16 |
| X10 | A user without Platform administration U reruns the job | 403 and no run started | MSG-P4-002 | AC15 |
| X11 | An email with no attachment, or only an image under 10 KB | Email archived; no intake row | None | AC13 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | The suite is its own module and reuses the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG; it needs the two APP stories and the published contracts of P5, S9, P1 and P4, not their source code |
| Negotiable | The folders, the mailbox codes, the allowed types, the size limit, the duplicate window and the alert count are properties and data rows; the story fixes the assertions and the call set |
| Valuable | The four inbound channels and the intake step are proved on real services before wave 1 exits, with the source of every file recorded |
| Estimable | One suite module, one fixture pack, four channel controls, one container fault switch and one evidence report |
| Small | Sixteen scenarios over four services and one workflow; no service code and no schema change |
| Testable | Every scenario asserts an intake item, a run state, a folder position, a counted refusal or a message; all data is synthetic |

```gherkin
  Scenario: AC5 An unknown and a suspended partner are refused through the S9 contract (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given file "notice-0005.pdf" in the SFTP subfolder "LF-099", which is no partner_code
    Given file "notice-0006.pdf" in the SFTP subfolder "LF-008", a partner with panel_status "SUSPENDED"
    When the job runs
    Then the S9 partner contract answers no partner for "LF-099" and panel_status "SUSPENDED" for "LF-008"
    Then the system writes no document_intake row for either file
    Then the job record shows MSG-P5-007 with reasons "PARTNER_UNKNOWN" and "PARTNER_NOT_ACTIVE"

  Scenario: AC6 The same hash from the same channel is one item across two dates (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given file "scan-0001.pdf" with hash "H1" from branch "BR-0123" was taken in on 30 November
    When the same file arrives again from branch "BR-0123" on 2 December
    Then the system writes no second document_intake row for "H1" on "BR-0123"
    Then the job record counts the file as a duplicate
    Then the file is in the processed folder of branch "BR-0123"

  Scenario: AC7 An unknown or suspended partner is refused (legacy RWB-E1-057 AC7)
    Given file "notice-0005.pdf" in the SFTP subfolder "LF-099", which is no partner_code
    Given file "notice-0006.pdf" in the SFTP subfolder "LF-008", a partner with panel_status "SUSPENDED"
    When the job runs
    Then the system writes no document_intake row for either file
    Then the job record shows MSG-P5-007 with reasons "PARTNER_UNKNOWN" and "PARTNER_NOT_ACTIVE"

  Scenario: AC8 The intake container refuses writes and the file stays at the channel (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the intake container refuses writes
    When the job runs with file "scan-0007.pdf" in the folder of branch "BR-0123"
    Then the system writes no document_intake row
    Then "scan-0007.pdf" stays in the scanner folder and the run is failed with MSG-GEN-006
    Then on the next run with the container available the file is taken in

  Scenario: AC9 An empty run (legacy RWB-E1-057 AC9)
    Given no new file or email on any channel
    When the job runs
    Then the job record shows intakeStep complete with 0 items on each channel

  Scenario: AC10 Two failed partner SFTP runs raise the alert and the next run retries (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the run at 10:00 failed because the SFTP inbound folder could not be read
    When the run at 10:15 fails for the same reason
    Then MSG-P5-008 naming "PARTNER_SFTP" is raised to the platform administrator
    Then the run at 10:30 tries again and finishes

  Scenario: AC11 Two service instances produce one 09:15 run and one item per file (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given two service instances of rwb-document are running
    When the 09:15 run is due with one file on each of the four channels
    Then the system records one run for 09:15
    Then each of the four files has one document_intake row

  Scenario: AC12 scanStep completes before ocrStep reads an item (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given file "scan-0009.pdf" was taken in by intakeStep with an empty scan_result
    When the scanStep and ocrStep activities of the same run are observed on the item
    Then scanStep sets scan_result "CLEAN" on the item before ocrStep reads it
    Then no OCR call is made for the item while scan_result is empty

  Scenario: AC13 An email with no usable attachment (legacy RWB-E1-057 AC13)
    Given an email to "MBX-RECOVERY-01" with no attachment
    Given an email with only a 6 KB signature image
    When the job runs
    Then the system writes no document_intake row for either email
    Then both emails are in the archive folder

  Scenario: AC14 Outside business hours no run starts (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the time is 18:15 on a working day
    When the trigger for JOB-12 is due
    Then no run starts at 18:15
    Then the next run starts at 08:00 the next working day

  Scenario: AC15 A case owner without Platform administration U cannot rerun (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a user holds RW-CASEOWN and no Platform administration right U
    When the user posts a rerun of the failed JOB-12 run to the P1 job contract
    Then P1 refuses the call with status 403 and MSG-P4-002
    Then no run is started

  Scenario: AC16 All four channels end in one intake item and one workflow, with the partner check in evidence (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given one file on each of the four channels: "scan-0001.pdf" on "BR-0123", "mailroom-0001.pdf" on "MAILROOM", "LF-007-notice-0001.pdf" on "LF-007" and "reply-0001.pdf" on "MBX-RECOVERY-01"
    When the 09:15 run completes
    Then each file has exactly one intake item read through GET /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}
    Then one DocumentIntakeWorkflow execution holds the four items of the run
    Then the run evidence records the S9 partner check that returned panel_status "ACTIVE" for "LF-007"
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Scanner and mailroom files have source SCAN; partner SFTP files PARTNER; mailbox attachments EMAIL, and every one of them is read back through the P5 intake contract | RWB-E1-057 BR1; LOV-DOC-SOURCE; DF-DOC-046 |
| BR2 | Only the allowed types up to the size limit are taken in; the type is checked by content and extension | RWB-E1-057 BR2; INTAKE_ALLOWED_TYPES, INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB (25 MB assumed); VR-P5-001-1 |
| BR3 | Every file taken in is scanned for malware by scanStep before ocrStep reads it | RWB-E1-057 BR3; REQ-DCM-010; FEAT-DCM-18; RWB-E1-041 |
| BR4 | A partner file is taken in only from the subfolder of a partner whose panel_status is ACTIVE, read through the S9 rwb-partner contract | RWB-E1-057 BR4; DF-PRT-002, DF-PRT-005; Architecture v5 slide 41 (S9 owns the panel) |
| BR5 | A file with the same hash from the same channel inside the window is a duplicate | RWB-E1-057 BR5; INTAKE_DUPLICATE_WINDOW_DAYS (30 assumed); R-UNI-40 |
| BR6 | A source file is moved or an email archived only after the intake row is committed | RWB-E1-057 BR6; Events rule "Transactions" |
| BR7 | JOB-12 runs every 15 minutes in business hours, once across instances; two failed runs in a row on a channel raise an alert; the run and its counts are read through the P1 rwb-source-data job contract | RWB-E1-057 BR7; JOB-12; Architecture v5 slide 44 |
| BR8 | Folders and mailboxes are properties; types, sizes and windows are parameters — rows of the P5 document hub parameter table whose owner the Ownership Map names, read through the parameters contract of P3 and its client library where a value is a case-workflow parameter; none is code | RWB-E1-057 BR8; Principle 1; DP-06; DP-07 |
| BR9 | The sender address is personal data: masked by role and never logged | RWB-E1-057 BR9; CTL-11; DL26 |

Every read behind these rules is one hop with a 2 s timeout (ADR-020, DP-11). The suite reads no other service's tables: the partner panel comes through the S9 contract, the intake item through the P5 contract, the run through the P1 contract and the rights through the P4 contract.

##### 9. State transitions

None for the case status: this story changes no case status. It observes the intake row that intakeStep creates with an empty scan_result and ocr_status PENDING; scanStep and ocrStep move it on.

| Object | State | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Intake item | scan_result empty, ocr_status PENDING | intakeStep committed the row; the file is in the intake container and the source file has been moved |
| Intake item | scan_result CLEAN, ocr_status PENDING | scanStep has read the file; ocrStep may now take it |
| Intake item | scan_result INFECTED | scanStep quarantined the file; ocrStep never reads it (RWB-E1-041) |
| Intake item | ocr_status DONE or RESCAN | ocrStep has read the file (RWB-E1-049) |
| Run | running, failed, complete | The JOB-12 run state on SCR-44, with the intakeStep counts per channel |

The suite reads these states through the P5 contract and the P1 job contract and never writes them.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| QA integration engineer | Runs the suite, seeds the synthetic fixtures, reads the evidence report |
| SY-OCR, OCR and extraction pipeline | Runs intakeStep; reads the four channels; writes document_intake and the intake container (Documents CRU) |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Sees runs on SCR-44 and reruns JOB-12 (Platform administration CRUD); sets the channel properties |
| RW-AGENCYMG, partner and agency manager | Keeps the partner codes and panel status that BR4 reads (Partner portal CRUDA) |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Reads documents from intake once attached (Documents R); holds no Platform administration right U |
| P5 rwb-document owner | Owns document_intake, the intakeStep activity and the four channel readers |
| S9 rwb-partner owner | Owns the partner panel and the partner contract the intake calls |
| P1 rwb-source-data owner | Owns the job view and the rerun operation |
| P4 rwb-access owner | Owns the role and right model behind the refusal |

No other role is in scope for this story. The suite acts as the QA integration engineer and asserts the other roles only through the contracts.

The legacy story writes document_intake; in this suite P5 rwb-document writes it and the suite only reads it through the P5 contract. scan_result and ocr_status are read through the same contract and their field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary. The partner panel comes through the S9 contract, the run through the P1 contract and the rights through the P4 contract. Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary. Every row in the suite is synthetic.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The suite provides no REST operation. The names reserved for P2 rwb-integration — /api/recovery/integration/v1, rwb.integration.events.v1, rwb-integration and rwb_integration — are not used.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method and path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|
| GET /api/recovery/partner/v1/partners | S9 rwb-partner | Read partner_code and panel_status before the SFTP channel takes a file: "LF-007" ACTIVE, "LF-008" SUSPENDED and no row for "LF-099" |
| GET /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId} | P5 rwb-document | Read source, channel_code, captured_at, file_sha256, scan_result and ocr_status of every item taken in |
| GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId} | P5 rwb-document | Read the document a taken-in item becomes after matching |
| GET /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents | P5 rwb-document | Confirm a taken-in document reaches the case through the same hub |
| GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs | P1 rwb-source-data | Read the JOB-12 run, its state and the intakeStep counts per channel |
| POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun | P1 rwb-source-data | Rerun a failed run, and post the refusal for a user without the Platform administration right U |
| GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session | P4 rwb-access | Read the roles and rights of the calling user for the refusal of AC15 |

Every call is one hop with a 2 s timeout (ADR-020, DP-11).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The suite publishes no event.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The intake step publishes no event in the event catalogue: DocumentStored on rwb.document.events.v1 is raised when a document is stored after matching, not by intakeStep (Architecture v5 slide 16; Ownership Map). The suite therefore polls the P5 intake contract of section 12.2 for the item, and no event is invented for the intake step.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Workflow or activity | Owner | Task queue | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| DocumentIntakeWorkflow | P5 rwb-document | rwb-document | Observed only: the intake step takes the four channels, then scanStep and ocrStep run in the same run |

The workflow reads and writes only the rwb_document schema. No workflow, activity or the suite reads another service's schema.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. JOB-12 is event-started with KEDA workers on queue rwb-document, not a Temporal Schedule (Architecture v5 slide 44). The 15-minute cadence, the 08:00-18:00 window and the working-day rule are the trigger configuration of the P5 workflow kit; this story creates and asserts no Schedule.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None (DP-01). document_intake and document_hub_parameter are P5 tables; partner is an S9 table.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Stub | Use |
|---|---|
| Branch and mailroom folder fixture | Holds the scanner folders by branch code and the mailroom folder with the processed and rejected folders under them |
| Partner SFTP folder fixture | Holds the SFTP inbound root with one subfolder per partner_code and its processed and rejected folders |
| Mailbox stub | Stands in for the recovery mailboxes; Exchange Online read through Microsoft Graph is outside the 19 services and is not called |
| Intake-container fault switch | Makes the intake container refuse writes for the failed-run scenario and restores it |

The S9 partner rows are real synthetic SIT rows and no service contract is faked: every call in section 12.2 goes to the real SIT service.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Provided by the suite | Consumed by the suite |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 | 7 |
| Kafka | 0 | 0 |
| Temporal | 0 | 1 workflow observed (DocumentIntakeWorkflow) |
| File | 0 | 4 (branch folder, mailroom folder, partner SFTP folder, mailbox) |

##### 13. Solution plan

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Suite module for RWB-ITG-W1, reusing harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG | Integration suite | Runs the sixteen scenarios against SIT and holds no service code |
| Intake fixture pack | Test data | Synthetic files for the branch, mailroom, partner SFTP and mailbox channels, including the DOCX, the 25.1 MB and 25.0 MB PDFs and the 6 KB image |
| Channel fixtures and mailbox stub | External stubs | The four channel endpoints of section 12.8 with processed, rejected and archive folders |
| Container fault switch | Harness control | Makes the intake container refuse writes and restores it |
| Instance and clock controls | Harness controls | Starts the second rwb-document instance and moves the clock to 18:15 and to 2 December |
| Evidence report | Report | Records per scenario the run id, the counts per channel, the item fields, the contract responses and the messages |

Decoupling patterns applied (Template and Rules v1 §R5.5):

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added | Where it sits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | recovery.<table>, "recovery schema" | Owner's schema rwb_<name>; never read another service's tables | none | document_intake and document_hub_parameter stay in rwb_document (P5); the suite asserts through the P5 contract only |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON | On the APP stories; the five intake values are rows of the P5 document hub parameter table, read as data |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON | On the APP stories; the source LOV and the working-day calendar are reference data read through the contracts |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON | On the APP stories; the intake step publishes no event, so the suite consumes none and polls the P5 contract |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON | JOB-12 is the intake step inside DocumentIntakeWorkflow, event-started with KEDA workers on queue rwb-document (Architecture v5 slide 44) |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) | The seven consumed operations of section 12.2, including the PartnerDirectory call of the legacy story as the S9 partner contract |
| DP-13 | /api/recovery/v1 | /api/recovery/<short>/v1 | none | Every consumed path in section 12.2, including the P1 rerun path that was the monolith admin job rerun |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON | On the APP stories; the suite changes no schema |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The run is seen on SCR-44 and the documents on SCR-30 through gateway-bff; no screen is exercised here |

The dependency-added column records the build dependency of the owning story. This story has no build dependency: an ITG story waits on no build of its own. The H, C, I and X lists are exactly as the metadata table: no H, no C, no X, and the two I dependencies RWB-P5-E1057-APP and RWB-S9-E1057-APP.

Build steps:

1. Create the suite module next to harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG and wire it to the SIT endpoints of P5, S9, P1 and P4.
2. Build the fixture pack: the branch, mailroom, partner SFTP and mailbox files, the DOCX, the 25.1 MB and 25.0 MB PDFs, the 6 KB image and the hash "H1" pair for 30 November and 2 December.
3. Add the four channel fixtures, the mailbox stub and the container fault switch, and the instance and clock controls.
4. Implement AC1 to AC3 and AC16 — the four channels, the taken-in items and the single workflow — and assert only through the contracts of section 12.2 and Temporal visibility.
5. Implement AC4 to AC7: the type and size refusals, the partner check through the S9 contract and the unknown and suspended partner rows.
6. Implement AC6 and AC9: the duplicate across two dates and the empty run with zero counts.
7. Implement AC8, AC10, AC11 and AC12: the container fault, the two failed SFTP runs and the alert, the two instances, and the scan-before-OCR order.
8. Implement AC13 to AC15: the email with no usable attachment, the trigger at 18:15 and the refusal of a user without the Platform administration right U.
9. Write the evidence report with the counts per channel, the item fields, the partner check and the message ids, and keep it with the wave exit evidence.

Done when: all eighteen test cases pass in SIT against the published wave 1 contracts, the evidence report is attached to the wave exit pack, no sender address appears in any log or in the job record, and no service code or schema was changed by this story.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P5-001 | A file type is not allowed | This file type cannot be stored. Use PDF, JPG or PNG. |
| MSG-P5-017 | A file is above the size limit | This file is larger than {size} MB and cannot be stored. |
| MSG-P5-007 | A file is refused at intake | {source} file {file} was not taken in: {reason}. It is in the {folder} folder. |
| MSG-P5-008 | Two intake runs in a row fail on one channel | Document intake failed twice in a row for {channel}. Check the interface and job monitor. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The intake container is unavailable | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Rerun without Platform administration U | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The message IDs and wording are copied from RWB-E1-057. No new message ID is added by this story. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

The evidence report also carries the counts line of every run: {channel} took in {taken}, refused {refused} and counted {duplicates} as duplicates, with the reason of each refusal.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story. The platform administrator sees each JOB-12 run on SCR-44 Interface and job monitor in the states running, failed and complete, with the intakeStep counts per channel, and reruns a failed run there through the P1 job contract. The case owner sees intake documents on SCR-30 Case documents once RWB-E1-032 attaches them.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the folders, the mailbox codes, the allowed types, the size limit, the duplicate window and the alert count are properties and data rows.
- No personal data in logs, events, evidence or fixtures: the sender addresses and the email file names are not logged, and the sender address is masked in every response and absent from the job record; test emails use synthetic senders.
- No read of another service's tables: the partner panel comes only through the S9 contract, the intake item and the document through the P5 contract, the run through the P1 contract and the rights through the P4 contract.
- A file is never removed from a channel before its intake row is committed; the suite asserts the order commit then move.
- Storage is reached by managed identity only, never by key or shared access signature (RWB-TE-012).
- One hop and a 2 s timeout on every call (ADR-020).
- Synthetic data only; the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG loads the fixtures.
- No production access of any kind from the suite or its configuration.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: contract baseline of RWB-E1-058 for rwb-agent. This is the agent-platform contract of the key: the eleven operations of the platform on the base `/api/recovery/agent/v1` (DP-13), the schema `rwb_agent` with the eight agent tables and their keys (DP-01), the EV-28 payload on `rwb.agent.events.v1` with its envelope and registry subject (DP-09), the decision-record payload written through the local library on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03), the INT-23 model-gateway request at the boundary with the policy timeout (DP-11 as the recorded exception), the consumed contracts of rwb-case, rwb-document, rwb-access and rwb-decision (DP-06, DP-07, DP-08), and the contract fakes every build of the key uses. It builds no business behaviour and adds no business value. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead of rwb-agent**, I want **the agent-platform side of RWB-E1-058 fixed as a contract on Day 1 - the eleven operations on the base `/api/recovery/agent/v1` with their requests, answers, rights, refusals and idempotency, the schema `rwb_agent` and its eight tables with their keys, the EV-28 payload on `rwb.agent.events.v1` as a CloudEvents 1.0 message with a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic, the decision-record payload on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, the INT-23 request at the boundary with its timeout and its status mapping, and the five contract fakes with their synthetic fixtures**, so that **the app story, the infrastructure story and the deployment story of this key, and the calling services that reach an agent through the rwb-agent contract, all build against one agreed and testable shape on Day 1, without waiting for the agent runtime to be complete and without any of them inventing an answer of its own**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy key was written against a Java interface inside one process: `AgentOrchestrator.run` returned an `AgentRunResult`, `ToolGateway` called another module's interface, `RecoveryAccessGuard` and `PromptInputMasker` ran in the caller's transaction, the run row and the decision log entry were tables of one schema, and `EV-28` was an in-process event written by the same deployment (legacy section 12). In the target every one of those is a boundary:

- the published interface becomes a contract with two faces - the operations of the platform on the base `/api/recovery/agent/v1` and the run that a calling step reaches through the agent runtime client and AgentRunWorkflow on queue `rwb-agent` (DP-11, DP-13, DP-20; ASM-0850);
- the run table becomes one table of eight in schema `rwb_agent`, owned by P10, with the keys that the legacy section 13 fixed and the field list of TSD P10 v2 T3.1 (DP-01; AC4);
- the run completion becomes EV-28 on the service's own topic with a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic, and a decision of a calling step becomes a record on the shared topic through the local library (DP-09, DP-03; AC3);
- the case facts, the parameter keys, the lists, the document fields, the right and the masking decision come through their owners' contracts, because the service holds no grant on another schema (DP-06, DP-07, DP-08; ASM-0851);
- the model is reached at the Enterprise AI private endpoint INT-23, which is the only outside call of the service, and its request is small and load-bearing: the model code, the masked inputs and the output schema reference (ASM-0850; AC5).

Contract-first only works if the seam is written down once. The seam here is the platform every later agent stands on: four other agent keys of this service and the calling services of wave 1 read a run, a version or a score through it. If the shape is agreed and faked on Day 1, four teams move at once - the app story of RWB-P10-E1058-APP builds the gateway client, the store, the guardrail, the harness and the workflow against these fakes; the infrastructure story provisions the endpoint, the topic, the queue, the login and the alarms against the same names; the deployment story wires the migration job, the probes and the alerts against the same operations; and the calling services read one shape. Without it, each caller invents its own answer, the version record of a run stops matching the version in force, and the evidence of what an agent answered stops being readable by the owner.

This document owns the consumed side and the provided side of the key and never restates what another owner holds: the case, its parameters and its lists are rwb-case's, the document and its fields are rwb-document's, the right and the masking policy are rwb-access's, the central decision ledger is rwb-decision's, the case-output read as a business feature is Epic 3's, and the metrics read belongs to the monitor story (DP-01).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL), so the base, the topic, the event names, the queue and the schema follow the platform rule and not a local choice (§R4; DP-13, DP-14).
- The CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, the platform error envelope, the idempotency rule and the message-catalogue convention are the platform baseline; this document narrows them where it must and says so.
- The decision-record library of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON publishes the record shape and the topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` with its envelope (DP-03).
- The outbox and inbox library of RWB-PLT-TE006-CON publishes the outbox and inbox envelope, the relay and the `.dlt` rule (DP-09).
- The parameter and reference-data client libraries of RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and the access guard library of RWB-PLT-E1037-CON are published (DP-06, DP-07, DP-08).
- The per-service Flyway library of RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and the gateway-bff route contract of RWB-PLT-N001-CON are published (DP-15, DP-19).
- The agent runtime client of RWB-P10-TE013-CON is known: it submits to AgentRunWorkflow on queue `rwb-agent` and returns the run result or the fallback to the caller (DP-20).
- The Enterprise AI private endpoint INT-23 is named as the external system and its request elements are the legacy ones; its host, port, certificate and the Key Vault entries are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0608; ASM-0854) and are provisioned by RWB-P10-E1058-INF.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (§R5.7) and sits in contract group CG-W1.

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the eleven operations of the platform on the base `/api/recovery/agent/v1`: method, path below the base, request members, answer resource, rights, refusals, idempotency and the one-hop budget, taking the operation set from TSD P10 v2 T-A.1 and T-A.2 and the legacy section 12 (AC1).
2. Fix the error model: the status codes per operation, the business message IDs of the legacy section 14 and the platform codes, and the rule that no refusal is answered without one of them (AC2).
3. Declare the schema `rwb_agent` with the eight agent tables, their columns from TSD P10 v2 T3.1, their keys from the legacy section 13 and the ownership ruling that every one of them is P10's (AC4).
4. Declare EV-28 `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` on `rwb.agent.events.v1`: the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, the key, the payload members taken from the `agent_run` fields, the registry subject with BACKWARD compatibility, and the retry and `.dlt` route (AC3).
5. Declare the decision-record payload written through the local library on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, with the rule that the record of a case step is written by that step and never by an agent run (AC3).
6. Fix the INT-23 request at the boundary: the model code, the masked inputs and the output schema reference, the policy timeout, and the mapping of a timeout, a 4xx, a 5xx and a schema failure to a status of LOV-AGENT-RUN with fallback true (AC5).
7. Restate the consumed operations of rwb-case, rwb-document, rwb-access and rwb-decision with their rights, their answers and their 2 s budget, and mark each as the owner's and not this story's (AC1).
8. Write the contract fakes with synthetic fixtures: rwb-case, rwb-document, rwb-access, rwb-decision, the gateway-bff route, the INT-23 model gateway, the decision-record library and the outbox (AC5, AC6).
9. Publish the nine sub-tables of section 12 and the contract tests, including a drift test between each fake and this document (AC6).
10. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-P10-E1058-APP, RWB-P10-E1058-INF, RWB-P10-E1058-OPS, the other agent keys of the service and RWB-ITG-E1058-ITG.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A member of an operation drifts from this document: a renamed member, a retyped field, a dropped status | The contract test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC1 |
| X2 | A request misses a required member, or a role without the right calls an operation | Refused with 422 and MSG-GEN-001 naming the member, or with 403 and MSG-P4-002; nothing is written | MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P4-002 | AC1, AC2 |
| X3 | A prompt, policy or sample file fails a load check | Refused with 422 and MSG-P10-001; the version in force is unchanged and no version row exists | MSG-P10-001 | AC2 |
| X4 | The person who loaded a version approves it, or two approvals of one row version arrive at once | Refused with 409 and MSG-P7-002 for the loader, and with 409 and MSG-GEN-004 for the second approval | MSG-P7-002, MSG-GEN-004 | AC2 |
| X5 | An evaluation is started on an empty sample, or on a sample already RUNNING | Refused with 422 and MSG-P10-002, or with 409 and MSG-P10-003 | MSG-P10-002, MSG-P10-003 | AC2 |
| X6 | A payload gains a personal field, fails its registry subject, or the topic is unreachable | The payload is refused before the relay and routed to the `.dlt` topic with an alert; the outbox row is kept until the relay succeeds | None | AC3 |
| X7 | A name outside the family `rwb.agent.<Event>.v1` is published on the agent topic | The registry subject does not resolve and the message is refused before the relay | None | AC3 |
| X8 | The model gateway answers a 4xx or a 5xx, returns nothing inside the policy timeout, or answers outside the output schema | The run maps to MODEL_ERROR, TIMED_OUT or GUARDRAIL_FAILED with fallback true, and no status outside LOV-AGENT-RUN is written | None | AC5 |
| X9 | A fake drifts from this document, or a fixture holds a production value | The contract test fails, the merge is blocked, and the fixture is replaced with a synthetic one | None | AC6 |
| X10 | A key of an agent table is loosened, or a foreign key crosses a schema | The schema drift test fails against the declared keys and the boundary scan blocks the change | None | AC4 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes and the four owner contracts as published, and owns no running code |
| Negotiable | The media type, the paging of a list, the exact member types of a report and the fixture composition are settled with their owners; the operation set, the table keys, the event payload, the boundary mapping and the message IDs are fixed by this realignment |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app, infrastructure and deployment stories of this key and the four agent keys of the service on Day 1 |
| Estimable | Eleven operations, eight tables, two event payloads, one boundary contract, eight fakes and six contract tests |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is asserted against the artefact - a schema file, a payload, a fake, a key, a status - and never against a business outcome |

**Target reading.** The operation set, the rights, the status codes and the message texts are those of TSD P10 v2 T-A.1 and T-A.2 and of the legacy section 12 and 14, copied rather than invented; the table names, the field list and the lists of values are those of TSD P10 v2 T3.1 and T3.2; the keys are those of the legacy section 13; the event is EV-28 of Arch v5 slide 43 with the payload members of `agent_run`; and the boundary is the INT-23 request of the legacy section 12 with the policy timeout of the approved version. Where a source is silent, this document names the element and writes the §R9 placeholder with its gap and assumption rather than a value.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One base per service: every operation of this key is declared on `/api/recovery/agent/v1` and no operation is declared on the legacy monolith base or on another service's base | DP-13; §R4; Arch v5 slide 41 |
| BR2 | One topic per service with a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic, one event name pattern `rwb.agent.<Event>.v1`, and the topic and the event names of this key are rwb-agent's alone | DP-09; DP-14; §R4 |
| BR3 | Every message is a CloudEvents 1.0 message keyed by the case ID, validated against its registry subject with BACKWARD compatibility before the relay, and routed to `.dlt` on failure | DP-09; Arch v5 slide 42 |
| BR4 | EV-28 carries run facts only: the payload is the `agent_run` fields this document names, with no account number, no name and no personal field | Arch v5 slides 42 and 43; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR5 | The schema is `rwb_agent`, the eight agent tables are P10's, the primary key is `id` in each, and no foreign key crosses a schema | DP-01; Arch v5 slide 41; legacy section 13 |
| BR6 | A run status is always one of LOV-AGENT-RUN, and a timeout, an error and a schema failure map to TIMED_OUT, MODEL_ERROR and GUARDRAIL_FAILED and never to an invented value | TSD P10 v2 T3.2; legacy section 5 |
| BR7 | No business value in the contract: the model code and version, the timeout, the floor, the tool list, the price and the list values are rows of the policy version and of the owner contracts, and the contract only names them | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17; legacy BR11 |
| BR8 | The decision-record type and the central ledger are rwb-decision's, and the record itself is written by the step that took the decision through the local library; no agent run writes one | DP-03; ADR-022; legacy section 19 |
| BR9 | The two admin reads of this key, the metrics read and the case-output read are declared once and read by their consumers; a consumer never redefines a shape it does not own | DP-13; TSD P10 v2 T-A.1 |
| BR10 | Every payload and every fixture is synthetic: no production account, document, prompt, model answer or record is copied into a schema, a payload or a fake | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The operations, the schema, the payloads, the boundary contract and the fakes are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | The app, infrastructure and deployment stories of this key and its calling services accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A member, a query parameter, a payload field or an operation is added without removing one | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A member, a status, a key or a payload field is removed, renamed or retyped | In review, with the owner of the affected contract |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |
| Baselined | An owner publishes a new version of a consumed contract | rwb-case, rwb-document, rwb-access or rwb-decision changes a shape | In review, aligned to the owner |

These are the states of this document, not of a case or a run. The run states themselves are those of LOV-AGENT-RUN and belong to RWB-P10-E1058-APP.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Tech lead of rwb-agent | Owns the operations, the schema, the two payloads, the boundary contract, the document and the fakes; tags the baseline |
| Solution architect | Approves a breaking change to an operation, a key or a payload, and the recorded exception of the 60 second boundary budget |
| The rwb-case, rwb-document and rwb-access owners | Own the consumed operations and sign off the shapes taken from their documents |
| The rwb-decision owner | Owns the record shape, the shared topic and the ledger, and signs off the record mapping |
| The rwb-agent app, infrastructure and deployment stories | Review and accept the parts they consume |
| Platform library owner | Owns the CloudEvents envelope, the error envelope, the naming rule, the decision-record library, the outbox library and the guard library this document reuses |
| Data steward | Confirms that no personal data field is declared in a payload, a boundary request or a fixture |

The identity that calls INT-23 is the rwb-agent service identity (DP-02); its name, the Key Vault entries it uses and the certificate it presents are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0606, GAP-0608; ASM-0848, ASM-0854) and are fixed by RWB-P10-E1058-INF.

##### 11. Data

The contract declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Provided operations | the eleven operations of 12.1: run listing, config listing, config load, config approve, sample load, evaluation start, evaluation listing, evaluation report, metrics read, case-output read, run feedback |
| Request shapes | the query of a listing; the multipart body of a load (file, kind, agent, validFrom) and of a sample (file, agent, sampleCode); AgentEvaluationRequest with agent, sampleCode, sampleVersion and approaches; AgentFeedbackRequest; path identifiers as uuid |
| Answer shapes | AgentRun[] (id, agent, agentVersion, caseId, outcome, fallback, latencyMs), AgentConfigVersion[] (versionId, agent, kind, version, status, validFrom, validTo, loadedBy, approvedBy, bodyHash), AgentSample, AgentEvaluationRun with its AgentEvaluation score rows, AgentEvaluationReport, AgentMetric[], AgentOutput[] |
| Refusal | the platform problem response: status, code, detail, the message ID where a business message applies |
| EV-28 payload | run ID, agent_code, agent_version, model_version, case_id, autonomy_mode, trigger_event, status, fallback, confidence, latency_ms, run_at |
| Record payload | record reference, decision code, agent version, model version, inputs reference, final call, actions {caseId, agentRunId} |
| Boundary request | model code, masked inputs, output schema reference, timeout; the boundary answer is the answer of the model owner checked against that schema |
| Table keys | primary key `id` on each of the eight tables; unique (agent_code, policy_version), (agent_code, prompt_version), (idempotency_key), the sample key, and the partial unique index of agent_evaluation_run on (agent_code, sample_code, sample_version) where status = 'RUNNING' |

The sample key of this document is (agent_code, sample_code, sample_version, subject_id, label_key), taken from the legacy section 13; the physical schema of today states (sample_code, sample_version, label_key) and the difference is carried as GAP-0606 and settled in ASM-0858. The member types of AgentEvaluationReport and AgentMetric[] beyond the members named here, the type and length of the inputs reference, and the boundary answer shape are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0607; ASM-0849, ASM-0850); this document fixes the element names and leaves the types to the review with their owners. `agent_run_daily`, named by FSD P10 v3 A2.6, is not in the Ownership Map, the logical model or the physical schema and is out of this baseline (ASM-0859).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/agent/v1`; owner rwb-agent (P10). Every path below is relative to that base.

| Method | Path | Purpose | Rights |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/admin/agent-runs` | List agent runs with fallbacks: query agent, from, to; 200 AgentRun[] | Platform administration R, scope applied |
| GET | `/admin/agent-configs` | List prompt and policy versions per agent: query agent, kind, status; 200 AgentConfigVersion[] | Rules and parameters R |
| POST | `/admin/agent-configs` | Load a new prompt or policy version from a checked file; 201 AgentConfigVersion in status LOADED | Rules and parameters C |
| POST | `/admin/agent-configs/{versionId}/approve` | Approve a loaded version with If-Match on the row version; 200 AgentConfigVersion in status APPROVED | Rules and parameters A |
| POST | `/admin/agent-samples` | Load a labeled evaluation sample; 201 AgentSample with the sample version and the row count | Rules and parameters C |
| POST | `/admin/agent-evaluations` | Start the evaluation harness for an agent on a labeled sample; 202 AgentEvaluationRun in status RUNNING | Rules and parameters C |
| GET | `/admin/agent-evaluations` | List evaluation runs with their score rows; query agent, from, to; 200 AgentEvaluationRun[] | Rules and parameters R |
| GET | `/admin/agent-evaluations/{evaluationId}/report` | Read the report of one evaluation run; 200 AgentEvaluationReport | Rules and parameters R |
| GET | `/admin/agent-metrics` | Read agent measures per agent, version, segment and day for the monitor; query agent, segment, version, from, to; 200 AgentMetric[] | Rules and parameters R |
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs` | Read the recorded agent outputs of a case; 200 AgentOutput[] | Case record R, scope applied |
| POST | `/agent-runs/{runId}/feedback` | Record a person's verdict on an item of an L1 agent output; 200 AgentOutput | Case record U, scope applied |

Errors: 401 no session, 403 a role without the right (MSG-P4-002), 404 an unknown version, evaluation, run or case, 409 a version number that exists, an approver who is the loader (MSG-P7-002), a version not in LOADED, a row changed since it was read (MSG-GEN-004), an evaluation already RUNNING (MSG-P10-003) or a feedback already recorded, 422 a file that fails a check (MSG-P10-001), an empty sample (MSG-P10-002) or a missing required member (MSG-GEN-001), 503 the store or a consumed contract unavailable. Idempotency: the two loads and the approve carry an Idempotency-Key header; the sample load creates the next sample version; one RUNNING evaluation is allowed per agent, sample and sample version; the feedback operation is idempotent on its key; the four reads write nothing.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in this contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The case facts the tool gateway returns as SY-AGENT; one hop, 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/parameters/{key}` | P3 rwb-case | The parameter keys a run reads, with the version in force (DP-06) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/reference-data/{lovCode}` | P3 rwb-case | LOV-AGENT, LOV-AUTONOMY, LOV-CONFIG-STATUS, LOV-EVAL-STATUS, LOV-SUBJECT-TYPE and LOV-FEEDBACK with their version (DP-07) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}` | P5 rwb-document | The document and its extracted fields, read as SY-AGENT by the document tool |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | The right, the scope and the masking decision of the caller, through the guard library (DP-08) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/masking-policies` | P4 rwb-access | The masking policy in force for the agent identity, read once per run (DP-08) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` | P4 rwb-access | The session and rights of a caller, for the session answer of 12.1 |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log/{entryId}` | P7 rwb-decision | The sealed record of a step, read back to prove the record reference of EV-28 and of the record event |

Every operation is one hop with the 2 s client budget (DP-11, ADR-020). The call to INT-23 is external and is declared in 12.8 and 12.9, not here. The paths of the parameter, reference-data and session reads are the owner's and are fixed by their own contract documents; a drift is corrected there and never here.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Key | Payload (IDs and facts only) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` (EV-28) | `rwb.agent.events.v1` | P10 | the case ID | run ID, agent_code, agent_version, model_version, case_id, autonomy_mode, trigger_event, status, fallback, confidence, latency_ms, run_at |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 owns the type and the central ledger; every service writes its own record | the record reference | record reference, decision code, agent version, model version, inputs reference, final call, actions {caseId, agentRunId} |

Both are CloudEvents 1.0 messages inserted in the outbox in the same transaction as the row they describe and relayed by the outbox library; a payload is validated against its registry subject before the relay (DP-09; BR3). The family name pattern is `rwb.agent.<Event>.v1`: EV-28 is the only member the sources name, and a run-started or run-failed member is a new version of this contract agreed with its consumers, never an invented name (ASM-0849). The consumers of EV-28 are rwb-decision, rwb-document and rwb-deviation (Arch v5 slide 43); the consumers of the record event are rwb-decision's ledger and rwb-reporting.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None in this contract. The service consumes no topic for this key: CaseCreated and DocumentStored are the intake and screening consumers and are declared by RWB-P10-E1059-CON and RWB-P10-E1062-CON. The inbox of the outbox library is installed with the schema of 12.7 and dedupes on the event ID where a consumer is added.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| AgentRunWorkflow | Workflow (Arch v5 slide 16) | `rwb-agent` | Input: agent code, case ID, subject ID, trigger event, idempotency key, inputs. One execution per idempotency key, with the policy timeout of up to 60 seconds and then the rule result |
| ResolveAgentConfig | Activity | `rwb-agent` | Output: the approved policy and prompt versions in force on the run date and the parameter and list values read through the owner contracts |
| GatherInputs | Activity | `rwb-agent` | Output: the tool results of the allow-list, read through the owner contracts as the agent identity |
| MaskInputs | Activity | `rwb-agent` | Output: the masked inputs and the masking decision; no personal value leaves the activity |
| CallModelGateway | Activity | `rwb-agent` | Input: model code, masked inputs, output schema reference, timeout. Output: the answer or the mapped status TIMED_OUT, MODEL_ERROR |
| CheckGuardrail | Activity | `rwb-agent` | Input: the answer and its schema reference. Output: the check codes SCHEMA, TOOL_NOT_ALLOWED and BELOW_FLOOR, or a clean answer |
| RecordAgentRun | Activity (workflow kit) | `rwb-agent` | Input: the run row and the outbox row; one transaction, no partial write |

The workflow name, the queue and the 60 second budget are those of Arch v5 slide 16 and the workflow kit of the Temporal and Drools design ("Agent run with rule fallback", slide 12); the activity names and their inputs and outputs are this document's and are accepted by RWB-P10-E1058-APP. A calling step submits through the agent runtime client of RWB-P10-TE013-CON and never starts the workflow itself (DP-20).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Temporal Schedule belongs to this key: the Arch v5 job map names no job for the agent platform (slide 44), a run is started by a calling step and an evaluation by RW-COE through `POST /admin/agent-evaluations`. No quota, retention job or Schedule is invented here.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Key and contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| agent_policy | P10 (rwb_agent) | Primary key `id`; unique (agent_code, policy_version). A version of an agent's policy: model code and version, output schema reference, allowed tools, autonomy mode, segment, confidence floor, timeout, daily cap, price, alert role, review date, status and validity |
| agent_prompt | P10 (rwb_agent) | Primary key `id`; unique (agent_code, prompt_version). A version of an agent's prompt text with its hash, status and validity; the body is never returned by a read |
| agent_run | P10 (rwb_agent) | Primary key `id`; unique (idempotency_key). One call of an agent with agent_version, prompt_version, model_version, case_id, subject_id, autonomy_mode, trigger_event, status, fallback, guardrail_result, output, confidence, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_thb, data_as_of, run_at, evaluation_run_id and decision_log_id; index on (agent_code, run_at) |
| agent_sample | P10 (rwb_agent) | Primary key `id`; unique (agent_code, sample_code, sample_version, subject_id, label_key). One labeled subject in a versioned evaluation sample |
| agent_evaluation_run | P10 (rwb_agent) | Primary key `id`; partial unique index on (agent_code, sample_code, sample_version) where status = 'RUNNING'. One evaluation of an agent version against a sample, with its versions, status, timestamps, cost, p95 latency and failure counts |
| agent_evaluation | P10 (rwb_agent) | Primary key `id`; evaluation_run_id. The score of one approach on one label key: sample size, TP, FP, FN, agreement, precision and recall |
| agent_feedback | P10 (rwb_agent) | Primary key `id`; agent_run_id. A person's verdict on an item of a run, with its reason and its record reference |
| agent_alert | P10 (rwb_agent) | Primary key `id`; agent_code, alert_type and business_date. A cost-cap or drift alert of an agent with its measured and threshold values and its recipient role |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in rwb_agent | The outbox, inbox and idempotency envelope of the service (DP-09) |

The eight agent tables are created in `rwb_agent` by the rwb-agent Flyway sequence; agent_feedback and agent_alert are created by the stories that own their behaviour (RWB-P10-E2032-APP and RWB-P10-E1063-APP) and are declared here because every build of the key needs their shape. `decision_log_entry` is a rwb-decision table and is reached only through its contract (DP-01, DP-03). No foreign key crosses a schema; `case_id`, `subject_id`, `evaluation_run_id` and `decision_log_id` are cross-service references by ID only. The migration numbering is the service's own and only `V10_001__agent_runtime.sql` is named by a source (ASM-0856).

| Call type | Count | Detail |

| REST | 11 provided, 8 consumed | The eleven operations of 12.1 on `/api/recovery/agent/v1`; the case, parameter, reference-data, document, authorise, masking-policy, session and record read-back operations of 12.2; one hop, 2 s each; the INT-23 call is HTTPS at the boundary with the policy timeout of up to 60 seconds |
| Kafka | 2 published, 0 consumed | EV-28 on `rwb.agent.events.v1` with its retry topic and its `.dlt` topic, and the record event on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; both through the outbox, both CloudEvents 1.0 |
| Temporal | 1 workflow, 6 activities | AgentRunWorkflow and ResolveAgentConfig, GatherInputs, MaskInputs, CallModelGateway, CheckGuardrail and RecordAgentRun on queue `rwb-agent` in namespace `rwb-recovery` |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** `contract/agent-operations.yaml` (the eleven operations, their queries, requests, answers, rights, refusals and idempotency), `contract/agent-schema.sql` and `contract/agent-schema.md` (the eight tables, their columns and keys, and the library objects they rely on), `contract/agent-run-completed.asyncapi.yaml` (EV-28 on `rwb.agent.events.v1` with its registry subject and its `.dlt` route), `contract/agent-decision-record.md` (the record payload and the rule that the calling step writes it), `contract/model-gateway-boundary.yaml` (the INT-23 request, the schema reference and the status mapping) and the eight WireMock mappings with their synthetic fixtures.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON for the app story; the payload and topic are declared here |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and C RWB-P3-E1042-CON for the app story; the paths are restated here |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and C RWB-P3-E1043-CON for the app story; the lists are restated here |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON and C RWB-P4-E1037-CON for the app story; the rights are declared here |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON for the app story; the topic, the envelope and the subject are declared here |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none here; the budget is declared for every operation |
| DP-13 | the monolith API base | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON for the app story; the keys are declared here |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON for the app story; the route stub is declared here |
| DP-20 | Agent client | rwb-agent contract | H RWB-P10-TE013-CON for the app story; the workflow and the run result are declared here |

This story is Day 1 and holds no build dependency of its own (§R5.7): the platform contracts and RWB-P10-TE013-CON are the build dependencies its consumers add, and no C or I dependency is claimed. DP-11 is the pattern of every operation and of the eight consumed reads; the model boundary keeps the policy timeout of up to 60 seconds as the recorded exception to the 2 s budget, and no other hop is allowed to inherit it (ASM-0850).

**Build steps**

1. Write the operation contract from TSD P10 v2 T-A.1 and T-A.2 and the legacy section 12, with the rights, the status codes, the message IDs and the idempotency of each; add a lint to the pipeline (AC1, AC2).
2. Write the schema file with the eight tables, their columns from TSD P10 v2 T3.1 and their keys from the legacy section 13, and the boundary note on cross-service references (AC4).
3. Write the EV-28 AsyncAPI document: the envelope, the key, the payload members, the registry subject and the `.dlt` route (AC3).
4. Write the record payload and the rule that the calling step writes it through the library in its own transaction (AC3).
5. Write the boundary contract: the request, the schema reference, the policy timeout and the mapping to LOV-AGENT-RUN (AC5).
6. Build the eight fakes and their synthetic fixtures, including the 61 second silence and the payload that fails its subject (AC5, AC6).
7. Add the six contract tests of section 16, including the drift test between each fake and this document (AC6).
8. Tag the baseline and collect the sign-off of the app, infrastructure and deployment stories of this key and of the calling services.

**Done when.** The six contract artefacts validate in the pipeline, the six contract tests pass, the eight fakes answer every consumed path and payload, the nine sub-tables are complete with `None` where empty, and the app, infrastructure and deployment stories of this key and its calling services have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P10-001 | A prompt, policy or sample file fails a check | The {kind} file for {agent} was refused: {check}. The version in force is unchanged. |
| MSG-P10-002 | Evaluation started on a sample with no labeled rows | Sample {sample} has no labeled rows for {agent}. Load the labels before you run the evaluation. |
| MSG-P10-003 | Evaluation started while the same one is running | An evaluation of {agent} on sample {sample} is already running. Wait for it to finish. |
| MSG-P7-002 | Loader tries to approve their own version | You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | Approval of a version that changed since it was read | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required member of a request is empty | Enter {field}. |

The seven texts are the legacy messages of RWB-E1-058 and MSG-GEN-001 of the platform, copied character for character; this contract adds no message ID. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10. In MSG-P4-002 the {action} value is the operation the caller attempted, for example "read the agent runs", "load a configuration" or "record feedback".

##### 15. Screens and states

None in this story. The contract serves the admin reads that the agent monitor screen SCR-46 of RWB-E2-031 and RWB-P10-E1063-APP will compose, the case-output read of the Epic 3 case record, and the future feedback area of a case; it fixes no screen field, no order and no masking rule. The admin reads are reached through the gateway-bff route (DP-19), and the exact route name and path are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0607; ASM-0857).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the model code and version, the timeout, the floor, the tool list, the price and the list values stay rows of the policy version and of the owner contracts, and the contract only names them (BR7).
- No personal data in a payload, an example or a fixture: identifiers and facts only, the inputs reference holds the masked snapshot, and every fixture is synthetic (BR4, BR10).
- The contract names the agent base, the agent topic and the agent queue as rwb-agent's and consumes every other operation and topic; a document that declares another service's path or topic as provided fails the review (BR1, BR2).
- The eight agent tables are P10's and no foreign key crosses a schema; the record table of rwb-decision is read only through its contract (BR5, BR8).
- Every payload is validated against its registry subject before the relay and a refusal is routed to `.dlt` and alerted (BR3).
- The model boundary carries the model code, the masked inputs and the schema reference only; nothing else of the case leaves the service (BR6).
- The two admin reads, the metrics read, the case-output read and the feedback operation are declared once and never redefined by a consumer (BR9).

##### 19. Out of scope

- The implementation of the operations, the gateway client, the store, the guardrail, the harness and the workflow (RWB-P10-E1058-APP).
- The network path to INT-23, the login, the Key Vault entries, the topic with its retry and `.dlt` topics, the queue, the sizing, the budgets and the pipeline gates (RWB-P10-E1058-INF).

- The four other agent keys of the service (RWB-P10-E1059, E1060, E1062 and E1063) and the TDR offer-suggestion key of Epic 2, whose payloads are declared where their behaviour is built.
- The member types of AgentEvaluationReport and AgentMetric[] beyond the elements named here, the type of the inputs reference, the INT-23 host and certificate, the route name in front of the admin reads and the `agent_run_daily` table named by FSD P10 v3, which are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0607, GAP-0608; ASM-0849, ASM-0850, ASM-0854, ASM-0857, ASM-0859).
