##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code or in the suite: the agent, the model version, the prompt and policy versions, the timeout, the confidence floor, the tool list, the price and the daily cap are the approved P10 rows, read through the contract at run time (BR11).
- No personal data in logs, events, prompts, workflow inputs, fixtures or the report: the run carries case IDs, agent codes, version labels, check codes, token counts, costs and dates only, and every national ID number, mobile number and account number is synthetic.
- Masking before the prompt: no value reaches INT-23 before rwb-access has returned its masking token for SY-AGENT, and the recorded request is scanned for personal patterns on every run.
- The model endpoint is reached only through the gateway client of rwb-agent and only on its private endpoint; the suite reaches it only through the recorded stub of its OpenAPI 3.1 contract, and a caller that reaches the agent by direct REST fails the run.
- Prompt text and model answers never appear in a response of section 12.2, in `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1`, in `DecisionRecorded`, in a workflow history or in the application log; the listing returns ids and measures only (BR15).
- No cross-service table read and no schema client in the suite: every fact is read through a contract of section 12.2, 12.4 or 12.5, and a pipeline scan fails any change that adds a schema connection (DP-01).
- One hop and a 2 s client budget on every REST call, and the 60 s model budget only inside AgentRunWorkflow; the suite calls no service through another service (ADR-020, DP-11).
- No production access and no production namespace: the run is pinned to SIT with the synthetic set and refuses to start against any other environment.
- Clean-up in the same run: the synthetic cases, the sample and the evaluation run, the loaded versions and the stub deployment are removed or retired, and the report records what was cleaned.

##### 19. Out of scope

- The application builds this run depends on: RWB-P1-E1001-APP, RWB-P1-E1069-APP and RWB-P10-E1058-APP.
- The contract, database, operations and infrastructure stories of the legacy key.
- The rule fallback inside a case step and the decision record entry of that step, which belong to RWB-TE-013; this story asserts only the rule result that comes back and the record the calling step writes.
- The case intake agent, the extraction evaluation and the deviation screening agent.
- The monitoring dashboard and the cost alert (RWB-E1-063, RWB-E2-031), and the agent monitor screen SCR-46.

- The choice of model endpoint (DL33): the run reads the model version of the policy and never selects an endpoint.
- The build of the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG itself and the non-functional epic RWB-ITG-NFR.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-059 for rwb-agent. This is the contract slice of the legacy key: the two run operations the intake flow uses on `/api/recovery/agent/v1` - one to start a run and one to read it (DP-11, DP-13, DP-20) - the intake answer shape "intake-summary-v1" with its four gap types and its no-personal-data rule, the `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` payload as a CloudEvents 1.0 message on `rwb.agent.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics (DP-09), the event-driven interface that replaces the legacy in-process listener and any job-style trigger, the rwb-source-data read contract the intake inputs are built from (DP-05), the cases, parameters and lists read from rwb-case (DP-06, DP-07), and the six fakes every consumer builds against. It does not restate the whole rwb-agent contract, whose baseline is RWB-P10-E1058-CON and RWB-P10-TE013-CON, and it builds no business behaviour. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the rwb-agent side of the intake run fixed as a contract on Day 1: the start operation and the read operation on `/api/recovery/agent/v1` that the intake flow uses, with the run key, the mode and the run status of LOV-AGENT-RUN; the intake answer shape "intake-summary-v1" with its four gap types, the summary of at most 1,500 characters of masked tokens, the gap array and the confidence, and no personal data in it; the `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` payload on `rwb.agent.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics; the event-driven interface that replaces the in-process listener and any job-style trigger; the rwb-source-data read contract the inputs are built from; and the six fakes**, so that **the app story of this key, the operations story and every story that reads an agent run build against one agreed, testable shape without waiting for the intake agent to be complete**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy key RWB-E1-059 was written against a monolith: an `IntakeShadowListener` inside the same module received the case creation event from the same schema, `read_case`, `read_accounts`, `read_documents`, `read_valuations` and `read_contact_points` were in-process query services of the same deployment, the ACE facts came from `v_ace_*` views of the same database, the answer was validated against a schema file beside the code, and the run completion was an application event written by the same transaction. In the target every one of those is a boundary. The in-process call becomes one REST operation under `/api/recovery/agent/v1` with one hop and a client budget (DP-11, DP-13; ADR-020); the case, its parties and its accounts are read through the rwb-case contracts (DP-06, DP-07); the ACE facts are read through rwb-source-data (DP-05); the documents through rwb-document; the run completion becomes EV-28 on the service's own topic (DP-09; Arch v5 slide 43 row 28); and the run is started from the event by the runtime that owns it, not by a listener that shares a schema with the case store (DP-20; Arch v5 slide 16).

Contract-first only works if the seam is written down once. The seam here is small and load-bearing: one operation whose answer carries the run the intake flow needs, one read whose answer in SHADOW carries no content, one answer shape whose three members and four gap types are the legacy ones, one event payload that carries the run facts and no personal data, and one consumed read side whose four tool operations and freshness stamp are named.

If the shape is agreed and faked on Day 1, three teams move at once. RWB-P10-E1059-APP builds the listener, the assembler, the guardrail and the scorer against these fakes; the operations story of the service provisions the topic with its retry and `.dlt` topics, the queue and the indexes against the same names; and RWB-P10-E1061-APP, which reads a run of this agent for its report and its L1 proposal, reads one shape. Without it, each caller invents its own answer, the run key drifts, and the score that decides autonomy level 1 stops matching the run it was computed from.

This story defines the provided side and the consumed side of this key and never restates what another owner holds: the agent runtime baseline is RWB-P10-E1058-CON and RWB-P10-TE013-CON, the case is rwb-case's, the ACE facts are rwb-source-data's, the documents are rwb-document's and the rights are rwb-access's (DP-01).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL), so the REST base `/api/recovery/agent/v1`, the topic `rwb.agent.events.v1` and the event names `rwb.agent.<Event>.v1` follow the platform rule and not a local choice (§R4; DP-13, DP-14).
- The CloudEvents 1.0 envelope and the platform error envelope are the platform baseline; this document narrows them where it must and says so.
- The agent runtime baseline contract of RWB-P10-E1058-CON is in force: the policy and prompt resources, the admin configuration and run reads, the run resource, the error taxonomy and the evaluation operations are its elements, and this story reuses them rather than redefining them. Its task queue is `rwb-agent` and its namespace `rwb-recovery` (§R4; ASM-0865).
- The agent runtime client contract of RWB-P10-TE013-CON is the consumer of the two operations of this document for every caller inside the platform; this document fixes the members the intake flow reads and leaves the rest to that baseline.
- The outbox and retry library of RWB-PLT-TE006-CON publishes the outbox and inbox envelope, the relay, the retry topics (1 min, 10 min, 1 h) and the `.dlt` rule (DP-09).
- The decision-record library of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is in force; a shadow run writes no decision record with it (BR7).
- The parameter and reference-data contracts of rwb-case are published by RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and RWB-PLT-E1043-CON with their client libraries (DP-06, DP-07).
- The rwb-source-data tool reads and the freshness read are named by the platform contract and their paths are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0611; ASM-0866); the P1 fake is written to the assumed shape.
- The document read of RWB-P5-E1053-CON is published with its fake (ASM-0864).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (§R5.7) and sits in contract group CG-W1.

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the start operation: its method, its path below the base `/api/recovery/agent/v1`, its request members - agent code "INTAKE", case ID, business date, trigger "CaseCreated", idempotency key `INTAKE:<caseId>:<businessDate>` - its answer, its refusal codes and its one-hop budget (DP-11, DP-13, DP-20).
2. Draft the read operation: its path, its answer, the run facts it returns, the rule that in mode SHADOW the answer carries neither the summary nor the gap flags, and its refusal codes.
3. Fix the intake answer shape "intake-summary-v1": summary at most 1,500 characters of masked tokens only, gaps as an array of gapType from the enum, reason and sourceRef, confidence from 0 to 1, and the rule that no personal field appears in the answer, the run row or the event payload.
4. Declare `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` on `rwb.agent.events.v1`: the envelope, the key, the payload members taken from the `agent_run` fields of TSD P10 v2 T3.1, the registry subject, the retry topics and the `.dlt` route (DP-09).
5. Fix the event-driven interface: `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1` on `rwb.case.events.v1`, consumed through the inbox, starts one AgentRunWorkflow on queue `rwb-agent` for the run key, and the document states that no job table, no Quartz entry and no shared schedule table is used (DP-09, DP-20; ASM-0863).
6. Fix the consumed read side: the four rwb-source-data reads, the freshness stamp written to data_as_of, the rwb-case reads of the case, the accounts, the parties, the parameters and the lists, the rwb-document read and the rwb-access authorise call, each one hop with 2 s (DP-05, DP-06, DP-07, DP-11).
7. Write the six contract fakes: rwb-case, rwb-source-data, rwb-document, rwb-access, the model stub of the agent platform and the gateway-bff route stub, each with the answers, the errors and the timings this key's tests need.
8. Publish the nine sub-tables of section 12 and the contract tests: the operation shapes, the answer shape, the event envelope and its registry subject, the event-driven start, the consumed read side and a drift test between each fake and this document.
9. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-P10-E1059-APP, RWB-P10-E1061-APP and the test cases of this key.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A field of the start or the read operation drifts from this document: a renamed member, a retyped business date, a dropped refusal | The contract test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC1, AC2 |
| X2 | A caller sends a request without the case ID, the business date or the idempotency key | The operation refuses the request with 422 and names the field; nothing is written | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |
| X3 | The answer or the event payload gains a personal field | The data-steward review and the contract test refuse the payload; nothing is published | None | AC3, AC4 |
| X4 | A produced payload fails its registry subject, or the relay cannot reach the topic | The message is refused before the relay and routed to the `.dlt` topic of `rwb.agent.events.v1` with an alert | None | AC4 |
| X5 | A member of the run resource or of an admin read drifts from the baselines RWB-P10-E1058-CON and RWB-P10-TE013-CON | The contract test fails on the baseline and this document is aligned, because the baseline is the owner | None | AC2 |
| X6 | A consumed read answers beyond 2 s or refuses | The answer maps to TOOL_UNAVAILABLE with fallback true; no partial input set is used and no invented default is applied | None | AC6 |
| X7 | A field-level detail of a consumed operation, a member of the answer or the path of a consumed read is missing from the source material | The element is marked with the placeholder, one gap row and one assumption row are carried, and the fake is written to the assumed shape | None | AC1, AC3, AC6 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the agent runtime baselines, the outbox library, the decision-record library and the rwb-case contracts as published |
| Negotiable | The field-level detail of the consumed operations is settled with their owners; the two operation shapes, the answer shape, the event payload and the start interface are fixed by this realignment |
| Valuable | Unblocks the two app stories of this key on Day 1 and gives every reader of an intake run one shape |
| Estimable | Two provided operations, ten consumed reads, one answer shape, one event, one start interface and six fakes |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact - the schema file, the payload, the fake, the contract test - and never against a business outcome |

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The intake run is one start operation and one read operation under `/api/recovery/agent/v1`; no caller embeds the agent runtime and no in-process listener interface survives | DP-11; DP-13; DP-20; legacy section 12 |
| BR2 | The run key is `INTAKE:<caseId>:<businessDate>`, one run per key, and a repeat returns the stored run with 409 | Legacy section 12; R-UNI-40; AC3, AC6 |
| BR3 | In mode SHADOW the read returns run metadata only: the summary and the gap flags are stored and never returned by a user-facing operation | Legacy section 7 AC1, section 12 and section 15; BR1 of the legacy story; AC2 |
| BR4 | The answer carries summary, gaps and confidence only, with masked tokens in the summary and no personal field anywhere in the answer, the run row or the payload | Legacy section 12; REQ-ACA-005; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR5 | The four gap types are the enum of the output schema version in force, are data and are never a constant of the source | Legacy BR3; agent_policy.output_schema_ref (DF-AGT-006); DP-06 |
| BR6 | Every message is a CloudEvents 1.0 message on `rwb.agent.events.v1`, keyed by the case ID, validated against its registry subject before the relay, retried on the three retry topics and routed to `.dlt` on failure | DP-09; Arch v5 slides 42 and 43 |
| BR7 | A shadow run writes no decision record: the record that proves a decision is written when a person acts on the answer, and this contract promises none | DP-03; legacy BR1; AC2 |
| BR8 | A run status is always one of LOV-AGENT-RUN and an evaluation status one of LOV-EVAL-STATUS; a timeout, an error, a tool failure, a schema failure and a disabled agent map to TIMED_OUT, MODEL_ERROR, TOOL_UNAVAILABLE, GUARDRAIL_FAILED and DISABLED and never to an invented value | TSD P10 v2 T3.2 |
| BR9 | One base and one topic per service: this contract declares `/api/recovery/agent/v1` and `rwb.agent.events.v1` for rwb-agent and never another service's path or topic as its own | DP-13; DP-14; Arch v5 slide 41 |

| From | Event | Condition | To |

| Baselined | Additive change | A member, a query parameter or a payload field is added without removing one | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change to an operation or a payload | A member, a refusal code or an event member is removed, renamed or retyped | In review, with the owner of the affected contract |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |
| Baselined | The agent runtime baseline changes the run resource | RWB-P10-E1058-CON or RWB-P10-TE013-CON publishes a new shape | Baselined, aligned to the baseline |

These are the states of this document, not of a case or a run. The run states themselves are those of LOV-AGENT-RUN and belong to RWB-P10-E1059-APP.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |

| Tech lead of rwb-agent | Owns the two operations, the answer shape, the event payload, the start interface, the document and the six fakes; tags the baseline |
| Solution architect | Approves a breaking change to an operation, the answer shape or the event, and any change to the 60 second budget |
| The rwb-source-data owner | Owns the tool reads and the freshness read and signs off the shapes taken from its document |
| The rwb-case, rwb-document and rwb-access owners | Own the consumed operations and sign off the shapes taken from their documents |

| Platform library owner | Owns the CloudEvents envelope, the error envelope, the naming rule, the outbox library and the decision-record library this document reuses |
| Data steward | Confirms that no personal data field is declared in the answer, the event or the consumed read |

The identity that starts and reads a run is the rwb-agent service identity (DP-02); its name, the entries it uses and the credentials it presents are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0610; ASM-0861) and are fixed by the operations story of the service.

##### 11. Data

The contract declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Start request | agent code "INTAKE", case ID, business date, trigger "CaseCreated", idempotency key `INTAKE:<caseId>:<businessDate>` |
| Start answer | the run resource: run ID, mode "SHADOW", a status of LOV-AGENT-RUN, the run key |
| Read answer | run ID, agent_code, agent_version, prompt_version, model_version, case_id, autonomy_mode, trigger_event, status, fallback, guardrail_result, confidence, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_thb, data_as_of, run_at; no summary and no gap flags in SHADOW |
| Intake answer | summary (at most 1,500 characters, masked tokens only), gaps (array of gapType, reason, sourceRef), confidence (0 to 1) |
| Refusal | the platform problem response: status, code, detail, the message ID when a business message applies |
| EV-28 payload | run ID, agent_code, agent_version, model_version, case_id, autonomy_mode, trigger_event, status, fallback, confidence, latency_ms, run_at |
| Consumed read inputs | the case ID and the business date; the answers are the owners' shapes, of which this document names only the members the intake flow reads |

The field-level detail of the start request beyond the five members named above, the type and length of sourceRef, the exact member set of the rwb-source-data tool answers and the paths of the four reads are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0611; ASM-0862, ASM-0866); this document fixes the element names and leaves the types to the review with their owners.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/agent/v1`; owner rwb-agent (P10).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/agent-runs` - the path is fixed by this document; no source names it (GAP-0611; ASM-0862) | Start one run of an agent for a case and a business date: request agent "INTAKE", caseId, businessDate, trigger "CaseCreated" and the idempotency key; 202 AgentRun with the run ID and a status of LOV-AGENT-RUN | the service identity of the caller; Rules and parameters C, scope applied | Idempotency-Key header and the run key; a repeat answers 409 with the stored run |
| GET | `/agent-runs/{runId}` | Read one run: the run facts of 12.3 and of the `agent_run` fields; in mode "SHADOW" the answer carries neither the summary nor the gap flags (Arch v5 slides 16 and 41) | Platform administration R, scope applied; the caller's own run always | Not applicable: the call writes nothing |

Errors: 401 no session, 403 no right (MSG-P4-002), 404 no run for the identifier, 409 a repeat of the run key (R-UNI-40), 422 a missing or malformed request member (MSG-GEN-001), 503 the store or a consumed contract unavailable. The full run resource, the admin configuration and run reads and the evaluation operations are baselined in RWB-P10-E1058-CON and RWB-P10-TE013-CON; this document fixes the two operations the intake flow uses and redefines neither (ASM-0865). No operation of this document is served on the legacy monolith base (DP-13).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in this contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The case facts the input set is built from, and the proof that the case read returns no agent output |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/accounts` and `/parties` | P3 rwb-case | The accounts and parties of the case, masked before the model call |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 rwb-case | The reference lists the answer is validated against, in force at run time (DP-07) |
| POST | the parameters resolve operation of the rwb-case contract - path Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0611; ASM-0865) | P3 rwb-case | The values of the policy and prompt versions in force (DP-06) |
| POST | the `read_accounts`, `read_valuations` and `read_contact_points` tool reads of rwb-source-data - paths Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0611; ASM-0866) | P1 rwb-source-data | The ACE account facts, the appraisals and the contact points of the case (DP-05) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness` | P1 rwb-source-data | The last complete business date, written to data_as_of (DP-05) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents` | P5 rwb-document | The documents of the case with their type and review status (ASM-0864) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | The right and the scope before a start or a read |

Every operation is one hop with a 2 s client budget (DP-11, ADR-020); the model call to INT-23 is the agent platform's boundary with the policy timeout and is declared in 12.9, not here. This contract declares no contract dependency of its own: it is Day 1, and each consumer adds the contract dependencies of the operations it builds against (§R5.7).

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Key | Payload (IDs and facts only) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` (EV-28) | `rwb.agent.events.v1` | P10 | the case ID | run ID, agent_code, agent_version, model_version, case_id, autonomy_mode, trigger_event, status, fallback, confidence, latency_ms, run_at |

One CloudEvents 1.0 message, inserted in the outbox in the same transaction as the run row and relayed by the outbox library; it is validated against its registry subject before the relay, retried on the topics of 1 min, 10 min and 1 h and routed to `rwb.agent.events.v1.dlt` with an alert on failure (DP-09; BR6). No decision record is published for a shadow run (BR7), and no personal data is carried (BR4).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Key | Dedupe |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1` (EV-01) | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 | the case ID | Inbox on the event ID, then the run key `INTAKE:<caseId>:<businessDate>` |

This is the event-driven interface that replaces the legacy in-process listener and any job-style trigger: the event starts one AgentRunWorkflow for the run key and nothing else starts an intake run (AC5; BR2).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| AgentRunWorkflow | Workflow (Arch v5 slide 16) | `rwb-agent` | Input: agent code "INTAKE", case ID, business date, trigger "CaseCreated", idempotency key. One execution per key, with the 60 second budget and then the run status |
| BuildIntakeInputs | Activity | `rwb-agent` | Output: the masked input set, the inputs reference and data_as_of; no personal field leaves the activity |
| CallModelGateway | Activity | `rwb-agent` | Input: model code, masked inputs, output schema "intake-summary-v1", timeout. Output: the answer or the mapped status TIMED_OUT, MODEL_ERROR, TOOL_UNAVAILABLE |
| CheckGuardrail | Activity | `rwb-agent` | Input: the answer and the output schema reference. Output: the check code and the outcome, SCHEMA_RULE included |
| RecordShadowRun | Activity (workflow kit) | `rwb-agent` | Input: the run row and the outbox row; one `rwb_agent` transaction, no partial write |

The workflow name, the queue and the 60 second budget are those of Arch v5 slide 16; the activity names and their inputs and outputs are this story's and are accepted by RWB-P10-E1059-APP. The workflow is started by the agent runtime contract of RWB-P10-TE013-CON, which is why the workflow platform contract is not a build dependency here (ASM-0863).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The intake run is event-started and never on a cadence, and the Arch v5 job map names no job for an agent run (slide 44). No Temporal Schedule is declared, changed or owned by this contract.

`recovery_case`, `case_account` and `case_party` are rwb-case tables, `document` is a rwb-document table and the account, appraisal and contact-point rows are rwb-source-data's; all of them are reached only through their owners' operations, and `decision_log_entry` is rwb-decision's and is not written here. No foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** `contract/agent-run-operations.yaml` (the start and the read operation, their members, their refusals and their budget), `contract/intake-summary-v1.json` (the answer shape with the four gap types and the 1,500 character limit), `contract/agent-run-completed.asyncapi.yaml` (EV-28 on `rwb.agent.events.v1`, its registry subject, its retry and `.dlt` topics), `contract/intake-run-start.md` (the event-driven interface and the run key, aligned to RWB-P10-TE013-CON), `contract/intake-consumed-reads.md` (the ten consumed operations with their owners and budgets) and the six WireMock and stub mappings with their synthetic fixtures.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON for the app story; none here |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | C RWB-P3-E1042-CON for the app story; none here |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | C RWB-P3-E1043-CON for the app story; none here |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON for the app story; none here |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none here; the consumer adds RWB-P10-E1059-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON for the app story; none here |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON for the app story; none here |
| DP-20 | Agent client | rwb-agent contract | C RWB-P10-TE013-CON for the app story; none here |

This story is Day 1 and holds no build dependency of its own (§R5.7): the platform contracts and the P3, P5 and P4 contracts it names are those its consumers add, and each C dependency of the key sits on the app story and not here. DP-03 is named because the run record of the platform uses the library; a shadow run writes no record with it (BR7).

**Build steps**

1. Write the two operation contracts: method, path below the base, the request members, the answer members, the refusal codes with MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P4-002 and the 409 of a repeat; add a lint to the pipeline.
2. Write the answer shape `intake-summary-v1.json` with the 1,500 character limit, the three members and the four gap types, and a check that it carries no personal field.
3. Write the EV-28 AsyncAPI document: the envelope, the key, the payload members, the registry subject, the three retry topics and the `.dlt` route.
4. Write the start interface document: the CaseCreated consumption, the run key, the one workflow per key, and the statement that no job table is used.
5. Write the consumed read side with the ten operations, their owners and their budgets, and mark the paths the sources do not name.
6. Build the six fakes and their synthetic fixtures, including the silent model answer and the slow read.
7. Add the contract tests of section 16, including the drift test between each fake and this document.
8. Tag the baseline and collect the sign-off of the app stories of this key.

**Done when.** The six contract files validate in the pipeline, the eight contract tests pass, the six fakes answer every consumed path and payload, and RWB-P10-E1059-APP and RWB-P10-E1061-APP have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required member of the request is empty | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right calls an operation | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P1-001 | A consumed data product is stale | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |

The two business messages MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P1-001 are the legacy messages reachable from RWB-E1-059 and keep their wording character for character; MSG-GEN-001 is the platform message of an empty required field. This contract adds no message. In AC1 the {action} value is "start a run of this agent" and in AC2 "read a run".

None in this story. The contract serves the admin reads through the gateway-bff route indirectly: the route in front of `/api/recovery/agent/v1` is a pass-through of one hop and belongs to RWB-PLT-N001-CON (DP-19), the run monitor screen SCR-46 belongs to RWB-E2-031 and is not changed, and the case screens are not touched because a shadow run shows nothing to a case owner. The contract fixes no screen field, no order and no masking rule; the route name and path are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0610; ASM-0868).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the agent code, the policy and prompt versions, the 60 second timeout, the confidence floor 0.80, the 1,500 character limit and the four gap types are rows and schema values in force, and the contract only names them (BR5).
- No personal data in an answer, an event, an example or a fake: identifiers and facts only, the summary holds masked tokens only, and no fixture carries a real account number, name or national ID (BR4).
- The contract names the two run operations and the agent topic as rwb-agent's and consumes every other operation and topic; a document that declares another service's path or topic as provided fails the review (DP-13, DP-14).
- The run resource and the admin reads are restated, never redefined: RWB-P10-E1058-CON and RWB-P10-TE013-CON own them and a drift is corrected there (BR1).
- Every payload is validated against its registry subject before the relay, retried on the three retry topics and routed to `.dlt` with an alert on failure (BR6, DP-09).
- A shadow run promises no decision record, so no consumer waits for one before acting (BR7).
- Every fixture is synthetic; no production account, document, model answer or run is copied into a schema, a payload or a fake.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: app slice of RWB-E1-059 for rwb-agent. The behaviour of the legacy story is unchanged - the intake agent still builds a case file summary and the gap flags for every new Epic 1 case in shadow and is still scored against the business analysts' review of the same 200 cases - and what changes is service placement only: the run tables move into schema `rwb_agent` (DP-01), the run is started through the agent runtime contract of RWB-P10-TE013 (DP-20) from the CaseCreated event instead of an in-process listener, the ACE account, appraisal, contact and freshness facts are read through the rwb-source-data contract instead of `v_ace_*` (DP-05), the case and party facts, the parameters and the reference lists are read through the rwb-case contracts (DP-06, DP-07), the run completion is published as `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` on `rwb.agent.events.v1` through the outbox and consumed through the inbox (DP-09), the parameters that decide the run are read through the client library (DP-06), the two evaluation operations stay on the base `/api/recovery/agent/v1` (DP-13) and are baselined in the platform contract of RWB-P10-E1058-CON, the run key index arrives with the service's own migration `V10_004__intake_run_key.sql` (DP-15), and the reads reach the service through the gateway-bff route (DP-19). The legacy decision log write is dropped in shadow mode, so no decision record is written by a shadow run (DP-03 applies to the run record only through the platform library). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **the case intake agent to build a case file summary and flag gaps for every new Epic 1 case in shadow mode inside rwb-agent - the shadow run started from the CaseCreated event through the agent runtime contract, its summary and gap flags stored in agent_run in schema `rwb_agent`, its inputs read through the rwb-source-data, rwb-case and rwb-document contracts as SY-AGENT, and its completion published as `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` on `rwb.agent.events.v1`**, so that **the agent is scored against the business analysts' review before any case owner sees its output**.

##### 2. Business rationale

A case owner who takes over a case at day 90 reads every account, document and appraisal to find what is missing before deciding the next step. The intake agent prepares that summary and the list of gaps. In Epic 1 it runs in shadow only: its output is stored, compared with the business analysts' review of the same 200 cases and shown to nobody, so the step to autonomy level 1 in RWB-E2-028 is decided on a measured agreement rate. Inputs are masked before the model call (REQ-ACA-005) and the agent reads data as SY-AGENT (REQ-ACA-010).

In the legacy delivery the listener, the assembler, the scorer, the output schema and the run rows sat in one module and one schema, the case, the accounts, the valuations and the contact points were read through in-process query services, the case creation event was a row of the same schema, the run completion was an application event written by the same deployment, and the evaluation was started on a path of the monolith. The behaviour is unchanged, so the disposition is Split (rework): the legacy story is not preserved word for word, and its behaviour is carried onto the service. What changes is where each fact lives and how it is reached:

- The case, the parties, its accounts and the queues are P3 rwb-case, schema `rwb_case`, and are read only through the P3 contracts; the legacy in-process `CaseQueryService` becomes the two reads of the case contract and the case creation event (DP-01, DP-11; BR9).
- The ACE account facts, the appraisals, the contact points and the business-date completeness that sets `data_as_of` are P1 rwb-source-data and are read through its contract, never through `recovery.v_ace_*` views of the service (DP-05; BR9).
- The documents and their stored fields are P5 rwb-document and are read through its contract as SY-AGENT (DP-01; BR9).
- The run rows - agent_run, agent_sample, agent_evaluation_run and agent_evaluation - are P10 rwb-agent, schema `rwb_agent`, and this story writes them and no others (DP-01; BR10).
- The approved policy and prompt versions, the gap types of the output schema, the timeout, the confidence floor and the allowed tools stay rows of agent_policy and agent_prompt, read at run time through the parameters contract and the configuration read and never written in code (DP-06; BR8).
- The run is started through the agent runtime contract of RWB-P10-TE013 on the CaseCreated event, with the 60 second policy budget, instead of a listener inside the monolith (DP-20; BR7).
- The run completion is one CloudEvents 1.0 message on the service's own topic, inserted in the outbox in the same transaction as the run row and deduplicated by the consumers' inbox (DP-09; BR7).
- The evaluation operations are served on the base `/api/recovery/agent/v1`, and the legacy monolith base is retired for them (DP-13).
- The run key index arrives with the service's own Flyway sequence, in its own schema (DP-15; AC3, AC6).
- RW-COE and RW-RISK reach the reads through the gateway-bff route, which is the only route a screen will use (DP-19).

The cross-service behaviour of this key - that a case created by rwb-case, with its ACE facts and its documents, produces one shadow run and no change in force, and that the same 200 cases produce one complete evaluation - is proved by the integration copy of this key and by the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG, which is why this story carries no integration dependency (I = None) and claims none. This story builds and unit-tests its own deliverables against the published contracts and their fakes, and it owns seven of the eight legacy acceptance criteria, AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC6, AC7 and AC8. The legacy criterion AC5 belongs to the integration slice of this key, RWB-ITG-E1059-ITG, and is not reconstructed here; the gap GAP-0610 records it.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P10-E1058-APP is done: the agent platform, the orchestrator, the model gateway client, the prompt and policy store, the guardrail and the admin configuration operations exist in rwb-agent, agent "INTAKE" exists, and a run can be made in mode SHADOW.
- RWB-P10-TE013-APP is done: the agent runtime client with fallback exists in rwb-agent, so a run is started, read and given its 60 second budget through one contract.
- RWB-P10-E1059-CON is published: the two run operations this key needs on `/api/recovery/agent/v1`, the intake answer shape "intake-summary-v1", the `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` payload and the five contract fakes, so this story builds against a fixed shape and its fakes from Day 1.
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON are published: the decision-record library (used by the platform's run record and not by a shadow run), the parameters client library, the reference-data client library, the outbox and inbox library with its retry and `.dlt` rule, the per-service Flyway sequence with parameterized schema names, and the gateway-bff route contract with its stub.
- The `rwb_agent` schema baseline exists with the standard record columns and the Flyway history table of the service, and the four run tables of this story are created by the P10 migrations of RWB-P10-E1058-APP; this story adds one index migration only.
- The rwb-case contracts of RWB-P3-E1030-CON, RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON are published: the case creation event `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1` on `rwb.case.events.v1` with its case, party and account reads; the parameters contract; and `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` for the reference lists the agent needs. This story builds against those contracts and their fakes and never reads `rwb_case`.
- The rwb-source-data contract is available for the ACE reads (`POST`/`GET` tool operations of section 12.2, one hop, 2 s) and returns the account facts, the appraisals, the contact points and the business-date completeness stamp, so `data_as_of` comes from the owner and not from a view (DP-05).
- The rwb-document contract of RWB-P5-E1053-CON is published: `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents` returns the documents of a case with their type and review status. This story builds against that contract and its fake (ASM-0864).
- The rwb-access contract is available for the right check: `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` granting Rules and parameters C to RW-COE and R to RW-RISK and refusing a role without the right.
- Approved agent_policy "INTAKE" version "P1" with autonomy_mode SHADOW, timeout 60 seconds, confidence floor 0.80, allowed tools read_case, read_accounts, read_documents, read_valuations, read_contact_points, and output schema "intake-summary-v1".
- Approved agent_prompt "INTAKE" version "PR1".
- The output schema lists the gap types as data: MISSING_DOCUMENT, NO_VALID_APPRAISAL, NO_CONTACT_POINT, STALE_INPUT.
- Labeled sample "INTAKE-S1" version 1 is loaded by RW-COE: the business analysts' review of 200 Epic 1 cases, one row per case and gap type with expected value Y or N.
- The login of this service is the rwb-agent login: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0610; ASM-0861).
- The release date 30 November 2026 is tentative and is copied unchanged.

##### 4. Flow

1. rwb-case creates case "RW-2026-000301", writes the row in `rwb_case` and inserts `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1` in its outbox in the same transaction; the relay publishes it to `rwb.case.events.v1` (P3; RWB-P3-E1030-CON).
2. IntakeShadowListener in rwb-agent consumes the event through its inbox, so a duplicate event ID is dropped before any work, and calls the agent runtime of RWB-P10-TE013 for agent "INTAKE" with the run key "INTAKE:<caseId>:<businessDate>" (DP-09, DP-20; AC3, AC6).
3. The runtime starts one run: it reads the case through `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}`, the accounts and parties through their case reads, the documents through the rwb-document contract, the appraisals and contact points through the rwb-source-data contract, all as SY-AGENT, and marks `data_as_of` from the freshness stamp the owner returns (DP-01, DP-05, DP-11; BR4, BR7).
4. IntakeInputAssembler masks personal fields with the tokens of the mask in force and builds the request of the model gateway; no unmasked value leaves rwb-agent (BR7; REQ-ACA-005).
5. The model is called through the gateway on the private endpoint INT-23 with the output schema "intake-summary-v1" and is bounded by timeout_seconds of the policy version in force, 60 seconds (BR8; NFR-010).
6. IntakeOutputGuardrail checks the answer against the schema, the allowed tools and the confidence floor 0.80, and stores the summary and the gap flags on the agent run with mode SHADOW together with the policy version "P1", the prompt version "PR1" and the model version (AC1, AC2, AC4).
7. The run row and the `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` outbox row are written in one `rwb_agent` transaction and the relay publishes the event to `rwb.agent.events.v1` with the case ID as its key; no screen, no case field, no task, no queue and no decision log entry changes (AC1; BR1, BR2).
8. RW-COE starts the evaluation of "INTAKE" on sample "INTAKE-S1" through `POST /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-evaluations`, whose contract is baselined in RWB-P10-E1058-CON and is not re-declared here (AC8; ASM-0865).
9. The evaluator runs the agent in shadow on each of the 200 sample cases and compares each gap flag with the label, using only the labeled cases, and writes one agent_evaluation row per gap type with the agreement rate, precision, recall and sample size at four decimals (AC2, AC7; BR5).
10. RW-COE reads the scores through `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-evaluations`, one hop through the gateway-bff route, and the response carries run metadata only: no summary and no gap flags reach a user-facing path in shadow mode (AC1; DP-19; section 15).
11. The run writes only the four tables of `rwb_agent`; the case, the accounts, the documents and the valuations are read through their owners' contracts and no value in force changes (BR9, BR10; section 17).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The agent times out or fails a guardrail on a case | Run stored with status TIMED_OUT or GUARDRAIL_FAILED; counted as a failure type; no retry for that event | None to a user | AC4 |
| X2 | The ACE batch for the day is not COMPLETE | Run proceeds; data_as_of holds the last complete business date and the agent must return gap STALE_INPUT; a run without it fails check SCHEMA_RULE | None to a user | None of this story's criteria: the legacy AC5 sits with RWB-ITG-E1059-ITG (GAP-0610) |
| X3 | The same CaseCreated event arrives twice | One run for the case and business date (R-UNI-40) | None to a user | AC6 |
| X4 | Labels cover fewer cases than the sample | Agreement is computed on labeled cases only; sample size shows the labeled count | None to a user | AC7 |
| X5 | A user endpoint is asked for shadow output | No endpoint returns the output content; GET /admin/agent-runs returns metadata only | None to a user | AC1 |
| X6 | Evaluation started on an empty sample | Refused with 422 | MSG-P10-002 | AC8 |
| X7 | A role without the right starts or reads evaluations | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-059-09 |
| X8 | The rwb-source-data, rwb-case or rwb-document contract does not answer inside the 2 s budget | The run stops before the model call, holds status TOOL_UNAVAILABLE with fallback true, the failure is counted, and no partial answer is stored | None to a user | BR9; section 13 |
| X9 | The policy version in force holds no value for the timeout, the floor or the allowed tools | No model call is made, the run holds status DISABLED or fails closed before the call, and the missing policy value is named on the run; no value in code is used as a default | None to a user | BR8 |
| X10 | The outbox relay cannot reach `rwb.agent.events.v1` | The run row stands and the event waits in the outbox; it is published when the topic returns, and a payload that fails its registry subject goes to the `.dlt` topic with an alert | None to a user | BR7 |
| X11 | The migration `V10_004__intake_run_key.sql` fails in the service's Flyway sequence | The new version does not start and the version in force keeps serving; no run row is written by the new build | None | BR10 |

X1 to X7 are the legacy exception paths of RWB-E1-059 carried onto the service; X8 to X11 are the failures that appear when the reads leave the service and when the schema, the policy row and the topic become the service's own responsibility. X7 is not reached by a criterion of this story: it is proved by the access test case TC-E1-059-09, and the message is kept so a reader finds the legacy set complete.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the platform contract, the agent runtime contract, the published P1, P3, P4 and P5 contracts with their fakes and its own schema objects; it waits only for the in-lane stories RWB-P10-E1058-APP and RWB-P10-TE013-APP |
| Negotiable | The package layout, the component names and the poll of the read are design; the gap types, the agent, the policy and prompt versions, the timeout, the floor, the sample, the counts and the message IDs are fixed by the legacy story and by the policy rows |
| Valuable | Gives the measured agreement rate that decides whether the case owner gets the summary in Epic 3 |
| Estimable | One listener, one prompt, one output schema, one sample, one scorer, one migration and five contract clients; no screen |
| Small | One developer and one analyst for two weeks, as in the legacy estimate |
| Testable | Each of the seven criteria of section 7 is one automated test on an observable: a stored row, a REST answer, a failure count, an agreement rate, a schema refusal or a scan of the source |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Case intake agent in shadow [E1b]

  Background:
    Given agent "INTAKE" has approved policy "P1" with mode "SHADOW" and prompt "PR1"
    Given the gap types in output schema "intake-summary-v1" are MISSING_DOCUMENT, NO_VALID_APPRAISAL, NO_CONTACT_POINT and STALE_INPUT

  Scenario: AC1 Shadow run (legacy RWB-E1-059 AC1)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the 200 Epic 1 cases, their CaseCreated events created between 2026-11-30 and 2026-12-04, and no agent output on GET /cases/{caseId} and GET /cases/{caseId}/timeline
    Given 200 Epic 1 cases created between 2026-11-30 and 2026-12-04
    When the agent runs on each CaseCreated event
    Then 200 agent runs with mode "SHADOW" store a summary and gap flags
    Then no case field, task, queue or decision log entry changes
    Then GET /cases/{caseId} and GET /cases/{caseId}/timeline return no agent output
    Then GET /admin/agent-runs returns the 200 runs without the summary or the gap flags

  Scenario: AC2 Agreement rate (legacy RWB-E1-059 AC2)
    Given the business analysts' review of the same 200 cases in sample "INTAKE-S1" version 1
    When the comparison runs
    Then one score row per gap type holds the agreement rate, precision, recall and sample size 200
    Then for MISSING_DOCUMENT with 182 agreeing cases the agreement rate is 0.9100
    Then each score row holds policy "P1", prompt "PR1" and the model version

  Scenario: AC3 A new case starts one shadow run (legacy RWB-E1-059 AC3)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns case "RW-2026-000301" created on 2026-11-30 and its CaseCreated event
    Given case "RW-2026-000301" is created on 2026-11-30
    When EV-01 CaseCreated is processed
    Then one agent run exists with key "INTAKE:<caseId>:2026-11-30", trigger "CaseCreated" and mode "SHADOW"

  Scenario: AC4 A failed run is counted and not retried (legacy RWB-E1-059 AC4)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns case "RW-2026-000302" and its CaseCreated event
    Given the model stub does not answer for case "RW-2026-000302"
    When the agent runs
    Then the run holds status "TIMED_OUT" and fallback true
    Then the system makes no second run for that event
    Then the failure count for type "TIMED_OUT" on 2026-11-30 is 1

  Scenario: AC6 A repeated event has no further effect (legacy RWB-E1-059 AC6)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the CaseCreated event of case "RW-2026-000301" for 2026-11-30 with one event ID
    Given EV-01 CaseCreated for case "RW-2026-000301" was processed on 2026-11-30
    When the same event arrives again with the same event ID
    Then one agent run exists for the case and date and the repeat is counted (R-UNI-40)

  Scenario: AC7 Partly labeled sample (legacy RWB-E1-059 AC7)
    Given sample "INTAKE-S1" version 2 has labels for 180 of 200 cases
    When the comparison runs
    Then each score row holds sample size 180
    Then the system lists the 20 unlabeled cases as unlabeled on the evaluation run

  Scenario: AC8 Empty sample (legacy RWB-E1-059 AC8)
    Given sample "INTAKE-S3" has no labeled rows for "INTAKE"
    When RW-COE starts the evaluation
    Then the system refuses the request with 422 and MSG-P10-002
```

**Target reading.** The agent, its policy and prompt versions, the gap type enum, the sample, the 200 cases and their dates 2026-11-30 to 2026-12-04, the agreement rate 0.9100 with 182 agreeing cases, the sample sizes 200 and 180, the failure type TIMED_OUT, the message IDs and the run key are the legacy values of RWB-E1-059, copied character for character. The scenario lines keep their legacy titles and every legacy Given, When and Then, and each one carries the origin tag of its legacy criterion. Four criteria carry one inserted line as their first Given, `Given the rwb-case contract mock returns ...`, because the legacy criterion reads a case, its event or its absence across the P3 boundary: AC1 reads the case and the silence of the case reads, AC3 and AC6 read the case and its event, and AC4 reads the case of the silent model. AC2, AC7 and AC8 need none: they assert the comparison, the labeled count and the refusal of an empty sample, all inside rwb-agent. The in-process `CaseQueryService`, `DocumentQueryService` and `CollateralQueryService` of the legacy section 12 become one-hop operations of their owners behind the 2 s budget (DP-11, DP-05, DP-01), so a run row of this story is built from a value the owner served and not from a table read. The seven criteria are the legacy AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC6, AC7 and AC8; the legacy AC5 is owned by the integration slice RWB-ITG-E1059-ITG and is not reconstructed here (GAP-0610).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | In SHADOW mode the output is stored and never shown, and nothing on the case changes | agent_policy.autonomy_mode (DF-AGT-008) = SHADOW; legacy BR1 |
| BR2 | The agent runs once per case per business date on EV-01 CaseCreated | R-UNI-40; agent_run.idempotency_key (DF-AGT-045); legacy BR2 |
| BR3 | Gap types are the enum in the approved output schema, not code | Principle 1; agent_policy.output_schema_ref (DF-AGT-006); legacy BR3 |
| BR4 | When an input is older than the business date, the answer must include STALE_INPUT | VR-P10-003-1; MSG-P1-001 rule of the data products; legacy BR4 |
| BR5 | Agreement rate per gap type = cases where agent flag equals label / labeled cases, 4 decimals | agent_evaluation.agreement_rate (DF-AGT-094); legacy BR5 |
| BR6 | A run that times out or fails a check is not retried for the same event | R-UNI-32; agent_run.fallback (DF-AGT-047); legacy BR6 |
| BR7 | Personal fields are masked before the model call, and no personal value reaches a log, an event or a prompt | CTL-11; REQ-ACA-005; legacy BR7 |
| BR8 | The timeout 60 seconds, the confidence floor 0.80, the allowed tools and the gap types are values of the approved policy version and the output schema, read at run time; a code default is a defect and a missing value stops the call | DP-06; Principle 1; FSD P10 v3 BR-P10-003 |
| BR9 | rwb-agent reads no table of another service: the case, the parties and the accounts come through the rwb-case contracts, the ACE facts and the freshness stamp through rwb-source-data, the documents through rwb-document, and no foreign key crosses a schema | DP-01; DP-05; DP-11; Arch v5 slides 15 and 16 |
| BR10 | The story writes four tables only - agent_run, agent_sample, agent_evaluation_run and agent_evaluation - all in `rwb_agent`, and adds the run key index by its own migration in its own Flyway sequence | DP-01; DP-15; Ownership Map (P10 owns the four tables) |
| BR11 | A shadow run writes no decision record: nothing in force changes, so the record that proves a decision is not written for an answer nobody acts on | Legacy section 7 AC1 and section 12; DP-03; legacy BR1 |

##### 9. State transitions

None to a case: this story does not change a case status. The state of one run of agent "INTAKE":

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | CaseCreated consumed and the run key is new | The policy version in force has mode SHADOW and its values are complete | Run row with mode SHADOW, status ANSWERED, fallback false (DF-AGT-046, DF-AGT-047) |
| None | CaseCreated consumed | A run exists for the same case and business date | No row; the repeat is counted (R-UNI-40) |
| None | CaseCreated consumed | The policy values are missing | No model call; the run is refused before the call and the missing value is named (X9) |
| ANSWERED | The guardrail passes and the floor is met | None | ANSWERED with the summary, the gap flags and the confidence stored (DF-AGT-049, DF-AGT-050) |
| None | The model does not answer inside 60 seconds | None | TIMED_OUT with fallback true, no retry for that event (AC4) |
| None | The guardrail refuses the answer | A schema, tool or floor check fails | GUARDRAIL_FAILED with fallback true and the check code in guardrail_result (DF-AGT-048) |
| None | The answer is under the confidence floor 0.80 | None | BELOW_FLOOR with fallback true |
| None | A consumed read fails inside the 2 s budget | None | TOOL_UNAVAILABLE with fallback true (X8) |

The state of one evaluation run: RUNNING to DONE, or FAILED when a sample row cannot be scored (DF-AGT-077). No state outside LOV-AGENT-RUN and LOV-EVAL-STATUS is written (TSD P10 v2 T3.2).

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| SY-AGENT, agent platform | Reads the case, the accounts, the parties, the documents, the appraisals and the contact points through the owner contracts (Documents R, Case record R) |
| SY-CASEWF, case and workflow in rwb-case | Publishes CaseCreated; not called by this story |
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Loads the labeled sample, starts the evaluation, reads the scores (Rules and parameters C) |
| RW-RISK, risk and model risk officer | Approves the policy and prompt versions and reads the scores (Rules and parameters A and R) |
| rwb-agent service identity (the rwb-agent login, DP-02) | Consumes the event, writes the four tables in `rwb_agent`, reads the P1, P3, P5 and P4 contracts, publishes the run completion |
| RW-PLATADM, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-DATASTEW, RW-SECADM | Read run metadata (Platform administration R) |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Sees nothing from this story |
| rwb-access (P4) | Answers the right check `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` and refuses a role without the right with MSG-P4-002 |
| No role | Reads `rwb_case`, `rwb_source_data`, `rwb_document` or any other service's schema, reads the shadow output of a case, or changes a value in force |

The login of the service is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0610; ASM-0861); the story names it "the rwb-agent login (DP-02)" until it is agreed. No delegation of authority level applies: the approval of the policy and prompt versions is the Rules and parameters A right, as in the legacy story.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. This story provides no operation of its own: the run is started by the CaseCreated event through the agent runtime contract of RWB-P10-TE013, the run read is `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/agent-runs/{runId}` as fixed by RWB-P10-E1059-CON and baselined in RWB-P10-E1058-CON, and the sample and evaluation operations are baselined in RWB-P10-E1058-CON (ASM-0865). The base `/api/recovery/agent/v1` is the service's own and the legacy monolith base is retired for these paths (DP-13).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use | Budget |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | AC1, AC3 and AC4: the case facts the summary is built from, and the proof that no agent output is returned on the case read | One hop, 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/accounts` and `/parties` | P3 rwb-case | AC1: the accounts and parties of the case, masked before the model call | One hop, 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 rwb-case | The reference lists the answer is validated against, in force at run time (DP-07) | One hop, 2 s |
| POST | the parameters resolve operation of the rwb-case contract — path Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0610; ASM-0865) | P3 rwb-case | The values of the policy and prompt versions in force, read at run time and never coded (DP-06) | One hop, 2 s |
| POST | the `read_accounts` tool read of the rwb-source-data contract — path Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0610; ASM-0866) | P1 rwb-source-data | AC1: the ACE account facts of the case (DP-05) | One hop, 2 s |
| POST | the `read_valuations` tool read of the rwb-source-data contract — path Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0610; ASM-0866) | P1 rwb-source-data | AC1: the appraisals and their dates (DP-05) | One hop, 2 s |
| POST | the `read_contact_points` tool read of the rwb-source-data contract — path Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0610; ASM-0866) | P1 rwb-source-data | AC1: the contact points and their usage codes (DP-05) | One hop, 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness` | P1 rwb-source-data | The last complete business date, written to data_as_of (DP-05; ASM-0866) | One hop, 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents` | P5 rwb-document | AC1: the documents of the case with their type and review status, for the MISSING_DOCUMENT flag | One hop, 2 s |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | The Rules and parameters right and the scope before a read, cached by the guard library | One hop, 2 s |

Every call is one hop to the owning service on its own base (DP-13) with the 2 s client budget (DP-11); rwb-agent calls no service through another service and holds no schema client of another service. The three P3 contracts are the contract dependencies of the metadata row; the P1 reads add no dependency by DP-05, and the P5 read is a C-class contract built against its fake (ASM-0864). The model call is not a REST budget of this story: it is the INT-23 boundary of the agent platform of RWB-P10-E1058-APP with the 60 second policy timeout.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Key | Payload (IDs and facts only) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` (EV-28) | `rwb.agent.events.v1` | P10 | the case ID | run ID, agent_code "INTAKE", agent_version, model_version, case_id, autonomy_mode "SHADOW", trigger_event "CaseCreated", status, fallback, confidence, latency_ms, run_at |

One CloudEvents 1.0 message, inserted in the outbox in the same transaction as the run row and relayed by the outbox library; a payload is validated against its registry subject before the relay and a refusal goes to the `.dlt` topic with an alert (DP-09). No decision record is published by a shadow run (BR11). No personal value is carried: the payload holds IDs and facts only.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Use | Dedupe |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1` (EV-01) | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 | AC1, AC3, AC4 and AC6: one shadow run per new case, keyed by the case ID and the business date | Inbox on the event ID, then the run key "INTAKE:<caseId>:<businessDate>" |

The listener is idempotent on the event ID and on the run key, so a repeated event is counted and produces no second run (R-UNI-40; AC6). No other topic is consumed by this story.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| AgentRunWorkflow | Workflow (Arch v5 slide 16) | `rwb-agent` | Input: agent code "INTAKE", case ID, business date, trigger "CaseCreated", idempotency key. One execution per key, with the 60 second policy budget and then the run status |
| BuildIntakeInputs | Activity | `rwb-agent` | Output: the masked input set, the inputs reference and data_as_of; no personal field leaves the activity |
| CallModelGateway | Activity | `rwb-agent` | Input: model code, masked inputs, output schema "intake-summary-v1", timeout. Output: the answer or the mapped status TIMED_OUT, MODEL_ERROR, TOOL_UNAVAILABLE |
| CheckGuardrail | Activity | `rwb-agent` | Input: the answer and the output schema reference. Output: the check code and the outcome, SCHEMA_RULE included |
| RecordShadowRun | Activity (workflow kit) | `rwb-agent` | Input: the run row and the outbox row; one `rwb_agent` transaction, no partial write |

The workflow name, the queue and the 60 second budget are those of Arch v5 slide 16; the activity names and their inputs and outputs are this story's and are accepted by RWB-P10-TE013-APP.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The intake run is started by the CaseCreated event and the evaluation is started by RW-COE on request; the legacy Quartz entry of the evaluation does not exist in the target, and no Temporal Schedule is declared, changed or owned here.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| agent_run | P10 (rwb_agent) | One run of agent "INTAKE" per case and business date, with mode SHADOW, the summary and the gap flags in output, data_as_of and the status of LOV-AGENT-RUN |
| agent_sample | P10 (rwb_agent) | The labels of sample "INTAKE-S1", read at the comparison; loaded through the platform's sample operation |
| agent_evaluation_run | P10 (rwb_agent) | One evaluation of "INTAKE" against a sample version, RUNNING to DONE or FAILED, with the failure counts |
| agent_evaluation | P10 (rwb_agent) | One score row per gap type: sample_size, true_positive, false_positive, false_negative, agreement_rate, precision, recall |

rwb-agent reads no table of another service and holds no foreign key across services (DP-01). `recovery_case` is P3's, `document` is P5's and the account, appraisal, contact-point and freshness rows are P1's; all of them are read through their owners' operations. `V10_004__intake_run_key.sql` runs in the rwb-agent Flyway sequence of `rwb_agent` and touches no other schema (DP-15; ASM-0867).

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-case WireMock | The P3 contracts of RWB-P3-E1030-CON, RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON | The 200 Epic 1 cases created 2026-11-30 to 2026-12-04 with their CaseCreated events; case "RW-2026-000301" and case "RW-2026-000302"; the same event ID twice; the case reads that return no agent output; the lists and the policy values in force |
| rwb-source-data WireMock | The P1 tool and freshness contract | The account facts, the appraisals and their dates, the contact points and their usage codes of every case; the freshness stamp of the last complete business date; a delay beyond 2 s |

| Model stub | The agent platform of RWB-P10-E1058-APP on the INT-23 boundary | A valid answer of "intake-summary-v1" with the four gap types; silence for 61 seconds for case "RW-2026-000302"; an answer with a missing member; an answer with a confidence under 0.80 |
| gateway-bff route stub | The DP-19 route of RWB-PLT-N001-CON | A pass-through route in front of the admin reads, one hop, with the query parameters preserved |

The agent model endpoint INT-23 is never called live by a test of this story: the answer is the stub of the agent platform owned by RWB-P10-E1058-APP, and no test calls a live model endpoint with real prompts. Every fixture is synthetic.

| Kafka | 1 published, 1 consumed | `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` on `rwb.agent.events.v1` through the outbox, and `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1` on `rwb.case.events.v1` through the inbox |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.agent.intake`, module `intake`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.agent.intake` inside the rwb-agent service (DP-13, §R4).

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |
| DP-20 | Agent client | rwb-agent contract | C RWB-P10-TE013-CON |

The H and C dependencies of this table are the ones in the metadata rows: the five platform contracts, RWB-PLT-N001-CON, RWB-P10-E1059-CON, RWB-P10-TE013-CON, RWB-P10-E1058-APP and RWB-P10-TE013-APP are build dependencies; the three P3 contracts and RWB-P10-TE013-CON are contract dependencies built against their fakes. DP-05 adds no dependency of its own, DP-11 sits behind DP-01 on every read (one hop, 2 s), and DP-03 is carried by the platform's run record only: a shadow run writes no decision record (BR11).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| IntakeShadowListener | Listener | Consumes `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1` through the inbox, applies the run key and calls the agent runtime of RWB-P10-TE013 (DP-09, DP-20) |
| IntakeInputAssembler | Service | Builds the masked input set from the case, account, document, appraisal and contact-point reads and records data_as_of from the owner's freshness stamp |
| IntakeOutputGuardrail | Service | Applies the schema, the allowed tools and the floor of the policy version in force, writes guardrail_result and maps a failure to GUARDRAIL_FAILED or BELOW_FLOOR |
| IntakeOutputScorer | Service | Compares each gap flag with the label per gap type for the evaluation harness and writes the score rows (BR5) |
| intake-summary-v1.json | Rule table | The output schema with the gap type enum, versioned with the policy and read as a version, never coded |
| prompt INTAKE PR1 | Rule table | The prompt text, loaded through the configuration operation of RWB-P10-E1058-APP and approved by RW-RISK |
| CaseContractClient | Client | Calls the rwb-case reads and the parameter and list reads with one hop and the 2 s budget (DP-06, DP-07, DP-11) |
| SourceDataToolClient | Client | Calls the three tool reads and the freshness read of rwb-source-data as SY-AGENT (DP-05) |
| DocumentContractClient | Client | Calls the document read of rwb-document as SY-AGENT (DP-11) |
| AgentRunRepository | Repository | Writes and reads agent_run, agent_sample, agent_evaluation_run and agent_evaluation in `rwb_agent` only (DP-01) |

**Database and migrations**

- `V10_004__intake_run_key.sql` adds the index `ux_agent_run_intake_key ON agent_run (agent_code, idempotency_key)` in `rwb_agent`, so the repeat check of AC3 and AC6 is answered without a scan; it runs in the rwb-agent Flyway sequence after the earlier P10 migrations and touches no other schema (DP-15; ASM-0867).
- The four run tables are created in `rwb_agent` by the P10 migrations of RWB-P10-E1058-APP; this story creates no table outside its four and no foreign key across services (DP-01; BR10).

**Configuration and reference data**

- Policy version "P1" of agent "INTAKE" (mode SHADOW, timeout 60 seconds, confidence floor 0.80, allowed tools read_case, read_accounts, read_documents, read_valuations, read_contact_points, output schema "intake-summary-v1") and prompt version "PR1": loaded by RW-COE, approved by RW-RISK, read at run time through the parameters contract and the configuration read (DP-06).
- The gap type enum MISSING_DOCUMENT, NO_VALID_APPRAISAL, NO_CONTACT_POINT and STALE_INPUT is a value of the output schema version, not a constant of the source (BR3).
- Sample "INTAKE-S1" version 1 and version 2, loaded by RW-COE from the business analysts' review file through the platform's sample operation.
- The list codes read through the reference-data contract, the 2 s client budget and the token set of the mask as service configuration.
- The legacy feature flag `rwb.agent.intake-shadow` is kept as the legacy reference: off, the listener ignores CaseCreated and no run row is written.

**Build steps**

1. `V10_004__intake_run_key.sql` and the four repositories in `rwb_agent` (BR10).
2. CaseContractClient, SourceDataToolClient and DocumentContractClient against their fakes, with the 2 s budget, the SY-AGENT identity and the tool-unavailable path (AC1; X8).
3. IntakeShadowListener with the inbox dedupe and the run key, then the call to the agent runtime contract (AC3, AC6).
4. IntakeInputAssembler with the mask and a scan proving that no personal field reaches the request (AC1; BR7).
5. IntakeOutputGuardrail with the schema, tool and floor checks and the failure counts (AC4).
6. IntakeOutputScorer with a 10-case fixture of known counts, then the full 200-case sample (AC2, AC7).
7. The empty-sample refusal on the evaluation start (AC8).
8. Pipeline scans for another service's table name, for a cross-schema foreign key and for the values 60, 0.80 and the gap type names in the source (BR8, BR9).
9. gateway-bff route contract test in front of the admin reads (DP-19).

**Done when.** The nine test cases of section 16 pass, a DEV run over the 200 synthetic cases produces 200 runs in mode SHADOW and one complete evaluation with sample size 200, the migration applies cleanly on an empty `rwb_agent` schema, no policy value appears in the source, and no case field, task, queue or decision log entry has changed.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P10-002 | Evaluation started on an empty sample | Sample {sample} has no labeled rows for {agent}. Load the labels before you run the evaluation. |
| MSG-P10-003 | Same evaluation already running | An evaluation of {agent} on sample {sample} is already running. Wait for it to finish. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P1-001 | A data product the run reads is stale | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |

The three business messages MSG-P10-002, MSG-P10-003 and MSG-P4-002 are copied unchanged from RWB-E1-059; MSG-P1-001 is the freshness message of the data products, named by the legacy rule BR4 and carried by rwb-source-data (VR-P10-003-1). This story adds no message ID. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10. In AC8 the {sample} value is "INTAKE-S3" and the {agent} value is "INTAKE"; in the access test the {action} value is "load a sample, start an evaluation or read the scores".

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story. No case owner sees the output. RW-COE reads scores through `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-evaluations` and run metadata shows through `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-runs`, both reached through the gateway-bff route in front of the admin path, so a screen never calls rwb-agent directly (DP-19). The agent monitor screen SCR-46 - the screen that shows runs, fallback, latency and cost per agent and comes with RWB-E2-031 - is not changed by this story, and the case screens, the review queue and the document screens belong to other stories and are out of scope. The exact path of the gateway-bff route in front of the admin reads is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0610; ASM-0868).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the gap types, the prompt, the timeout 60 seconds, the confidence floor 0.80, the allowed tools and the output schema are versioned rows read at run time, and a missing value stops the call instead of falling back to a default (BR8).
- No personal data in logs, tests, prompts or events: the inputs are masked with tokens before the model call, the summary holds masking tokens only, the event payload holds IDs and facts, and no test uses a real account number, name or national ID (BR7, legacy section 17).
- No read of another service's tables and no schema client: the case, the parties and the accounts come through the rwb-case contracts, the ACE facts and the freshness stamp through rwb-source-data, the documents through rwb-document and the right through rwb-access (DP-01, DP-05, DP-11).
- The four tables agent_run, agent_sample, agent_evaluation_run and agent_evaluation are the only tables this story writes, all in `rwb_agent`, and the run key index arrives only by `V10_004__intake_run_key.sql` (BR10, DP-15).
- The run is in shadow and changes nothing in force: it writes no case field, no task, no queue, no threshold and no decision record, and no user-facing endpoint returns its output (BR1, BR11).
- One hop and a 2 s client budget on every consumed REST call; the model budget belongs to the agent platform and is never a REST budget of this story (DP-11, ADR-020).
- The admin reads are reached through the gateway-bff route and never from a screen to the service (DP-19).
- Every payload is validated against its registry subject before the relay and a refusal is routed to `.dlt` with an alert (DP-09).
