**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: app slice of RWB-E1-061 for rwb-agent. The behaviour of the legacy story is unchanged, so the disposition is Moved (no impact) and the content is carried onto the service rather than rewritten: the evaluation tables the report reads and the policy row the L1 proposal writes are P10's own in schema `rwb_agent` (DP-01), the four promotion columns arrive with the service's own migration `V10_004__policy_promotion.sql` in the P10 Flyway sequence (DP-15), the report operation is served on the base `/api/recovery/agent/v1` and the legacy monolith base is retired for it (DP-13), the minimum sample and the check list of an autonomy step are read through the rwb-case parameters contract instead of the local policy schema (DP-06), LOV-AUTONOMY, LOV-CONFIG-STATUS and LOV-EVAL-STATUS are read through the rwb-case reference-data contract instead of being code enumerations (DP-07), and the reads are reached through the gateway-bff route (DP-19). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **the evaluation report of the case intake agent and the proposal to run it at autonomy level 1, built inside rwb-agent from the stored shadow results - the four `rwb_agent` tables of the evaluation harness, the report operation on the base `/api/recovery/agent/v1` with its JSON, CSV and PDF answers, the L1 promotion checks inside the policy load, and the four promotion columns added by the service's own migration - reading the minimum sample and the check list through the rwb-case parameters contract and the three lists through the rwb-case reference-data contract**, so that **the risk and model risk officer approves the step to L1 on measured results, on the same values the legacy story fixed, before wave 1 exits**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The step from shadow to L1 puts agent output in front of case owners, so the approver needs the agreement rate, the failure types, the cost and the latency on a stated sample before deciding. The legacy story produced that report from the evaluation run of RWB-E1-059 and held the L1 proposal as a versioned policy row with its conditions, fallback and measures to watch (REQ-DRI-010), approved and dated like any other reference row (REQ-DRI-011). Nothing goes to L1 until RW-RISK approves the row. That behaviour is unchanged and is copied here value for value: the evaluation run "EV-INTAKE-001", the 200 shadow runs with 188 ANSWERED, 7 TIMED_OUT, 3 GUARDRAIL_FAILED and 2 BELOW_FLOOR, the total cost 412.6000 baht, the cost per case 2.0630 baht, the median latency 4,100 ms, the 95th percentile 9,800 ms, the policy "INTAKE" versions "P1" and "P2", the prompt "PR1", the condition "agreement at least 0.85 for every gap type", the NO_CONTACT_POINT agreement 0.8150 and the sample size 150 of "EV-INTAKE-003" are the legacy values and every criterion of section 7 keeps them character for character.

In the legacy delivery the report, the score rows, the shadow runs and the policy row sat in one module and one `recovery` schema, the minimum sample was a value of the local policy JSON schema, the mode and status values were code enumerations, and the report was served by the monolith on the legacy monolith base. The disposition is Moved (no impact), so what changes is only where each fact lives and how it is reached:

- The evaluation run, the score rows and the shadow runs the report aggregates are P10 rwb-agent, schema `rwb_agent`: agent_evaluation_run, agent_evaluation and agent_run (DP-01; BR7).
- The policy row the proposal writes is P10 rwb-agent too: agent_policy in `rwb_agent`, extended with the four promotion columns by the service's own migration (DP-01, DP-15; BR8).
- The minimum sample of an autonomy step and the promotion check list in force are values of the rwb-case parameters contract, read at load time and never written in code; the legacy wording "set in the policy loader schema" is read as the versioned parameter row (DP-06; BR4; ASM-0870).
- LOV-AUTONOMY, LOV-CONFIG-STATUS and LOV-EVAL-STATUS are reference data of rwb-case, read through the reference-data contract, so mode "L1" and status "LOADED" are checked against the list in force and not against an enumeration in the service (DP-07; BR3; ASM-0873).
- The report operation is served on the base `/api/recovery/agent/v1`, and the legacy monolith base is retired for it (DP-13; AC1, AC3).
- The four promotion columns are added by `V10_004__policy_promotion.sql` in the rwb-agent Flyway sequence, in the service's own schema (DP-15). The legacy number is kept because it follows the `V10_003__evaluation_proposal.sql` of the extraction evaluation in the same P10 sequence.
- RW-COE, RW-RISK and RW-AUDIT reach the reads through the gateway-bff route, which is the only route a screen or an export will use (DP-19).

This key carries no integration dependency (I = None) and the story set holds no integration story for it: the two cross-service parts - the parameter values and the three lists - are consumed through published contracts and proved against their fakes by the contract tests of RWB-P10-E1061-CON, and this story claims no cross-service behaviour of its own. It owns the seven legacy acceptance criteria AC1 to AC7, unchanged.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P10-E1059-APP is done: the case intake agent "INTAKE" exists in rwb-agent, runs in mode SHADOW on a CaseCreated event through the agent platform, and policy version "P1" (SHADOW) with prompt version "PR1" is approved and in force.
- Evaluation run "EV-INTAKE-001" of "INTAKE" on sample "INTAKE-S1" version 1 has status DONE and holds 200 labeled cases with 188 ANSWERED, 7 TIMED_OUT, 3 GUARDRAIL_FAILED and 2 BELOW_FLOOR; the 200 runs cost 412.6000 baht in total with median latency 4,100 ms and 95th percentile 9,800 ms (legacy Background, copied unchanged).
- RWB-P10-E1058-APP is done: the agent platform, the prompt and policy store, the configuration operations `POST /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-configs` and `POST /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-configs/{versionId}/approve`, and the evaluation harness of RWB-P10-E1060-APP with `POST /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-evaluations` and `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-evaluations` exist in rwb-agent (ASM-0871).
- RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON are published: the parameters client library, the reference-data client library, the per-service Flyway sequence with parameterized schema names, and the gateway-bff route contract with its stub.
- The `rwb_agent` schema baseline exists with the standard record columns and the Flyway history table of the service; agent_evaluation_run, agent_evaluation, agent_run and agent_policy are created by the P10 migrations, and this story adds only the four promotion columns to agent_policy.
- Agent "INTAKE" has policy version "P1" approved in mode SHADOW with prompt version "PR1" and a model version; the report reads those versions from the evaluation run row and never from a constant.
- The rwb-case contracts of RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON are published: `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` for the minimum sample and the promotion check list in force, and `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` for LOV-AUTONOMY, LOV-CONFIG-STATUS and LOV-EVAL-STATUS.
- The minimum sample of an autonomy step for agent "INTAKE" is 200 in the parameters contract in force, and the L1 check list carries the three checks of BR2 to BR4: the named evaluation run is DONE, every stated condition is met by the scores, the sample size reaches the minimum, and the conditions, the fallback and the measures are present (ASM-0870).
- RW-COE holds Rules and parameters C and RW-RISK holds Rules and parameters A; RW-AUDIT holds R on the report and the versions. The refusals of MSG-P4-002 are proved by the access test case TC-E1-061-08.
- The login of this service is the rwb-agent login: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0612; ASM-0869).
- The release date 30 November 2026 is tentative and is copied unchanged.

##### 4. Flow

1. RW-COE requests the report of an evaluation run through `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-evaluations/{evaluationId}/report`, with Accept application/json, text/csv or application/pdf (AC1).
2. EvaluationReportService reads the run row and refuses the request with 409 and MSG-P10-008 when the run is not DONE, so a report exists only for a finished evaluation (AC3; legacy X1).
3. For a DONE run the service aggregates the stored rows of `rwb_agent` only: the sample size, the agreement rate per gap type and the failure counts from agent_evaluation and agent_evaluation_run, the total cost and the latency percentiles from the agent_run rows, and the policy, prompt and model versions from the run row (BR1, BR4; AC1).
4. The service computes cost per case as total cost divided by the number of runs at four decimals, and the median and the 95th percentile over all runs including timeouts at 60,000 ms (BR1; AC1).
5. The report object carries counts, rates, versions and durations only; no personal field and no customer, party or account identifier is read into it (BR5; AC1).
6. EvaluationReportExporter writes the CSV and the PDF from the same report object, so the three answers of the operation cannot disagree (AC1; section 15).
7. RW-COE loads policy "INTAKE" version "P2" with mode "L1", evaluation run "EV-INTAKE-001", the conditions "agreement at least 0.85 for every gap type", the fallback "rule result per R-UNI-32" and the measures "acceptance, correction rate, fallback rate below 0.10" through `POST /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-configs` (AC2).
8. PromotionProposalValidator runs inside the policy load for mode "L1": it checks that the named run is DONE, that the conditions, the fallback and the measures to watch are present, that every stated condition is met by the scores of that run, and that the sample size reaches the minimum read through the parameters contract (BR2, BR3, BR6; AC4, AC5, AC6).
9. Mode "L1" and the status values are checked against LOV-AUTONOMY and LOV-CONFIG-STATUS read through the reference-data contract; a mode or a status outside the list in force is refused by the same check (BR3).
10. A load that passes is stored as a new agent_policy version in `rwb_agent` with status LOADED, the four promotion columns filled and the loader recorded as loaded_by (AC2).
11. Version "P1" stays in force until RW-RISK approves "P2": the load alone changes no mode in flight (BR6; AC2).
12. RW-RISK approves version "P2" with a valid from date through `POST /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-configs/{versionId}/approve`; the approval moves the row to APPROVED and records approved_by and valid_from (AC2).
13. The approval is refused with 409 and MSG-P7-002 when the user who approves is the user who loaded the version (BR6; AC7).
14. The report and the version reads are reached through the gateway-bff route in front of the admin path, one hop each, so a screen never calls rwb-agent directly (DP-19).
15. The story writes agent_policy rows and reads agent_evaluation_run, agent_evaluation and agent_run; it writes nothing else and changes no case, no document and no threshold in force (BR7, BR8; section 17).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The report is requested for an evaluation that is still running | Refused with 409 | MSG-P10-008 | AC3 |
| X2 | The L1 proposal has no conditions, no fallback or no measures | Load refused in full | MSG-P10-001 | AC4 |
| X3 | The evaluation scores do not meet a stated condition | Load refused, naming the gap type and the score | MSG-P10-001 | AC5 |
| X4 | The sample size is below the minimum of 200 cases | Load refused | MSG-P10-001 | AC6 |
| X5 | The loader tries to approve the proposal | Refused with 409 | MSG-P7-002 | AC7 |
| X6 | A role without the right | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-061-08 |
| X7 | The parameters contract does not answer inside the 2 s budget, or answers without the minimum sample or without the check list for agent "INTAKE" | The load is refused with 422 and MSG-P10-001 naming the missing parameter; no default and no value in code is used, and no version row is written | MSG-P10-001 | AC2, AC6 |
| X8 | LOV-AUTONOMY, LOV-CONFIG-STATUS or LOV-EVAL-STATUS does not answer inside the 2 s budget, or the mode or status offered is not in the list in force | The load or the approval is refused with 422 and MSG-P10-001 naming the list and the value, and the version in force keeps serving | MSG-P10-001 | AC2, AC7 |
| X9 | The migration `V10_004__policy_promotion.sql` fails in the service's Flyway sequence | The new version does not start and the version in force keeps serving; no version row is created and no report is served | None | AC1, AC2 |
| X10 | The report is requested for a run of an agent the caller may not read, or through a route that is not the gateway-bff route | Refused with 403 with MSG-P4-002, or 404 at the edge; nothing is read | MSG-P4-002 | AC1, TC-E1-061-08 |

X1 to X6 are the legacy exception paths of RWB-E1-061 carried onto the service; X7 to X10 are the failures that appear when the parameter and list reads leave the service and when the schema and the route become the service's own responsibility. X6 is not reached by a criterion of this story: it is proved by the access test case TC-E1-061-08, and the message is kept so a reader finds the legacy set complete.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Reads only the stored results of RWB-P10-E1059-APP and the agent platform of RWB-P10-E1058-APP; it waits only for the in-lane story RWB-P10-E1059-APP and owns its own schema objects |
| Negotiable | The package layout, the component names, the export column order and the PDF rendering are design; the run, the sample, the counts, the cost, the latencies, the policy and prompt versions, the conditions, the measures, the minimum sample and the message IDs are fixed by the legacy story |
| Valuable | Gives the approver one report and one row to approve for the first autonomy step, on measured results |
| Estimable | One report operation with three media types, one validator inside the existing policy load, four columns in one migration, two contract clients and one route |
| Small | Three to four days, as in the legacy estimate |
| Testable | Each of the seven criteria of section 7 is one automated test on an observable: a REST answer, a stored row, a report field, a migration record or a scan of the source |

**Target reading.** The agent "INTAKE", its policy versions "P1" and "P2", the prompt "PR1", the evaluation runs "EV-INTAKE-001", "EV-INTAKE-002" and "EV-INTAKE-003", the sample "INTAKE-S1" version 1, the 200 runs with 188 ANSWERED, 7 TIMED_OUT, 3 GUARDRAIL_FAILED and 2 BELOW_FLOOR, the total cost 412.6000 baht, the cost per case 2.0630 baht, the median 4,100 ms, the 95th percentile 9,800 ms, the gap type NO_CONTACT_POINT with agreement 0.8150, the sample size 150, the conditions, the fallback, the measures and the message IDs are the legacy values of RWB-E1-061, copied character for character, and the Background keeps its three lines. Each Scenario line keeps its legacy number and title and carries the origin tag of its criterion; every legacy Given, When and Then is kept word for word.

Five of the seven criteria carry one inserted line, `Given the rwb-case contract mock returns ...`, as their first Given, because the criterion crosses into rwb-case: AC2 and AC7 name a mode and a status whose lists are reference data of rwb-case (DP-07; ASM-0873), and AC4, AC5 and AC6 run through a load that reads the minimum sample of an autonomy step from the parameters contract (DP-06; ASM-0870). AC1 and AC3 need none: AC1 aggregates only the run, score and shadow rows of `rwb_agent` - the cost 412.6000 baht and the two latencies are the agent_run rows of this service and are not a figure of another service - and AC3 asserts only the refusal of a report for a run that is not DONE. The report object is the legacy one of section 12: sampleSize, agreementByLabel[], failureCounts, totalCostThb, costPerCaseThb, latencyP50Ms, latencyP95Ms, agent, sampleSize and the three versions (ASM-0877 in RWB-P10-E1061-CON). The in-process monolith call of the legacy section 13 becomes one operation on the base `/api/recovery/agent/v1` (DP-13); the four promotion columns arrive by P10's own migration `V10_004__policy_promotion.sql` (DP-15); the minimum sample and the check list come from the parameters contract instead of the local policy schema (DP-06); the three lists come from the reference-data contract instead of the service's enumerations (DP-07); and the reads are reached through the gateway-bff route (DP-19). The behaviour is unchanged, which is why the disposition is Moved (no impact) and no legacy criterion is added to or dropped from this story.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The report holds the sample size, the agreement rate per gap type, the failure counts by type, the total and per-case cost, the median and 95th percentile latency, and the policy, prompt and model versions; cost per case = total cost / runs at 4 decimals, and the percentiles are computed over all runs including timeouts at 60,000 ms | agent_evaluation_run (DF-AGT-070 to DF-AGT-083); agent_run (DF-AGT-051, DF-AGT-054); legacy BR4 |
| BR2 | Every stated condition of an L1 proposal is checked against the scores of the named run before the version is stored | Principle 1; CTL-08; legacy BR2 |
| BR3 | The mode and the status of a version are always values of LOV-AUTONOMY and LOV-CONFIG-STATUS in force, read through the rwb-case reference-data contract | TSD P10 v2 T3.2; DP-07; ASM-0873 |
| BR4 | The minimum sample for an autonomy step is a parameter value of rwb-case read at load time - 200 for agent "INTAKE" - and never a value in code | FEAT-AGT-03; DP-06; ASM-0870 |
| BR5 | No personal field is read into the report, the CSV or the PDF: the report holds counts, rates, versions and durations only | Legacy section 17; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR6 | The fallback of an L1 agent is the rule result, the loader and the approver are different people, and a load changes no mode in force before the approval and its valid from date | R-UNI-32; legacy BR5, BR6 |
| BR7 | rwb-agent reads no table of another service and holds no foreign key across services: the parameter values and the lists come through the rwb-case contracts | DP-01; DP-06; DP-07 |
| BR8 | The story writes agent_policy only, in `rwb_agent`, and adds the four promotion columns by `V10_004__policy_promotion.sql` in its own Flyway sequence | DP-01; DP-15; Ownership Map (P10 owns agent_policy) |

##### 9. State transitions

No case state transition: this story does not change a case status and touches no case of record. The transitions of the policy version are these:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | An L1 proposal loaded through `POST /admin/agent-configs` | The named run is DONE, the conditions, the fallback and the measures are present, every condition is met and the sample reaches the minimum | LOADED (agent_policy.status, DF-AGT-021) with loaded_by (DF-AGT-024) |
| None | An L1 proposal loaded | A condition, the fallback or the measures is missing | No row; 422 MSG-P10-001 |
| None | An L1 proposal loaded | A stated condition is not met by the scores, or the sample is under the minimum | No row; 422 MSG-P10-001 |
| None | An L1 proposal loaded | The parameters or reference-data contract does not answer, or a value is outside its list | No row; 422 MSG-P10-001 |
| LOADED | RW-RISK approves through `POST /admin/agent-configs/{versionId}/approve` | The approver is not the loader and the valid from date is given | APPROVED with approved_by (DF-AGT-025) and valid_from (DF-AGT-022) |
| LOADED | The loader approves their own version | The user who loaded the version is the user who approves it | LOADED; 409 MSG-P7-002 |
| LOADED | A later version is loaded and approved | None | The earlier version keeps its status and its dates; RETIRED is reached by the configuration story of Epic 3, not here |

The evaluation run states RUNNING, DONE and FAILED are read by this story and are set by the evaluation harness of RWB-P10-E1060-APP; the report is refused for anything but DONE (AC3). The state of a version in force changes no case, no document and no threshold; the mode takes effect only on a business run after the approval and its valid from date (BR6).

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Requests and exports the report; loads the proposal (Rules and parameters C) |
| RW-RISK, risk and model risk officer | Reads the report; approves the proposal (Rules and parameters A) |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Reads the report and the versions (Rules and parameters R) |
| rwb-agent service identity (the rwb-agent login, DP-02) | Builds the report, runs the promotion checks inside the load, writes agent_policy in `rwb_agent`, reads the agent_run and agent_evaluation rows of its own schema, and reads the rwb-case contracts |
| rwb-access (P4) | Answers the right check and refuses a role without the right with MSG-P4-002 |
| No role | Reads `rwb_case`, `rwb_agent` of another deployment or any other service's schema, changes a version in force, changes a case, or reads production data |
| Approval levels | No delegation of authority level applies; the approval of the L1 proposal is the Rules and parameters A right, as in the legacy story |

The login of the service is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0612; ASM-0869); the story names it "the rwb-agent login (DP-02)" until it is agreed.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/agent/v1`; owner rwb-agent (P10).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/admin/agent-evaluations/{evaluationId}/report` | The report of one evaluation run: sample size, agreement per gap type, failure counts, total and per-case cost, median and 95th percentile latency and the three versions; Accept application/json, text/csv or application/pdf; 200 AgentEvaluationReport; 409 when the run is not DONE (MSG-P10-008) | Rules and parameters R, scope applied | Not applicable: the call writes nothing and the same run gives the same report |

`POST /admin/agent-configs` and `POST /admin/agent-configs/{versionId}/approve` are provided by the agent platform of RWB-P10-E1058-APP and are not re-declared here: this story adds the L1 promotion checks inside the load (the 422 answers of AC4, AC5, AC6 and X7) and reuses the approval check for an L1 version (AC7). The shape of the version resource, the status values and the error taxonomy are the baseline's (ASM-0871). `POST /admin/agent-evaluations` and `GET /admin/agent-evaluations`, which start and read the run this report aggregates, are the evaluation harness of RWB-P10-E1060-APP.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use | Budget |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | P3 rwb-case | AC4, AC5, AC6 and X7: the minimum sample of an autonomy step for agent "INTAKE" and the promotion check list in force, read before a version is stored | One hop, 2 s, cached by the client library for the life of the request |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 rwb-case | AC2, AC7 and X8: LOV-AUTONOMY, LOV-CONFIG-STATUS and LOV-EVAL-STATUS in force, read before a version is stored or approved and before a run status is reported | One hop, 2 s, cached by the client library for the life of the request |

Every call is one hop to the owning service on its own base (DP-13) with the 2 s client budget (DP-11 behind DP-06 and DP-07); rwb-agent calls no service through another service and holds no schema client of another service.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The report is built on the admin request path and the promotion changes a configuration row: neither publishes a business event of this key, and the evaluation completion is read through `GET /admin/agent-evaluations` and the report operation. `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` on `rwb.agent.events.v1` is published by a business run of an agent and belongs to RWB-P10-E1058-APP, not here.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The report is started by RW-COE on request and the load is started by RW-COE through the configuration operations; the events the agent runtime consumes belong to the business runs of RWB-P10-E1058-APP.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The report and the promotion checks run inside rwb-agent on the admin request path and start no workflow. `AgentRunWorkflow` on the queue `rwb-agent` in the namespace `rwb-recovery` belongs to the agent platform of RWB-P10-E1058-APP and to RWB-ITG-TE013-ITG; the shadow runs this report aggregates were made by it.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Temporal Schedule belongs to this story: the report is requested by a person and the proposal is loaded by a person, never on a cadence, and the legacy Quartz entry of the evaluation does not exist in the target (JOB-05 is retired and JOB-21 only scans stuck workflows).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| agent_evaluation_run | P10 (rwb_agent) | The run the report is built from; read only here, written by the evaluation harness of RWB-P10-E1060-APP |
| agent_evaluation | P10 (rwb_agent) | The score of one label key in a run: sample_size, agreement_rate, precision and recall, read only here |
| agent_run | P10 (rwb_agent) | The shadow runs: status, latency_ms and cost_thb, from which the total cost, the cost per case and the two latencies are computed |
| agent_policy | P10 (rwb_agent) | The versioned policy row the L1 proposal writes; this story adds evaluation_run_id, promotion_conditions, watch_measures and fallback_rule by `V10_004__policy_promotion.sql` |

rwb-agent reads no table of another service and holds no foreign key across services (DP-01, BR7). The parameter and reference rows of schema `rwb_case` are P3's and are read through its two contracts; a pipeline scan finds no `rwb_case`, no `recovery.` and no other service's table name in the rwb-agent sources. `V10_004__policy_promotion.sql` runs in the rwb-agent Flyway sequence of `rwb_agent` and touches no other schema (DP-15).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-case parameters WireMock | The P3 parameters contract of RWB-P3-E1042-CON | The minimum sample 200 for agent "INTAKE" and the promotion check list with its version; a version that raises the minimum above 200; an answer without the minimum; a delay beyond 2 s |
| rwb-case reference-data WireMock | The P3 reference-data contract of RWB-P3-E1043-CON | LOV-AUTONOMY with OFF, SHADOW and L1, LOV-CONFIG-STATUS with LOADED, APPROVED and RETIRED, and LOV-EVAL-STATUS with RUNNING, DONE and FAILED; a list version that lacks L1; a delay beyond 2 s |
| gateway-bff route stub | The DP-19 route of RWB-PLT-N001-CON | A pass-through route in front of the report read and the two configuration operations, one hop, with the JSON, CSV and PDF media types preserved |
| agent-run fixture | The event rows of RWB-P10-E1059-APP and RWB-P10-E1060-APP | The 200 stored runs of "EV-INTAKE-001" with 188 ANSWERED, 7 TIMED_OUT, 3 GUARDRAIL_FAILED and 2 BELOW_FLOOR, 412.6000 baht in total, median 4,100 ms and 95th percentile 9,800 ms; and "EV-INTAKE-003" with sample size 150 |

The access stub and the configuration store stub are the platform's and are used but not declared here. Every fixture is synthetic: no production run, no customer identifier and no personal value appears in one, and the agent model endpoint INT-23 is never called by a test of this story.

| Kafka | None | The report and the promotion publish no event and consume no topic |
| Temporal | None | No workflow and no schedule in this story |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.agent.eval.report`, module `eval-report`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.agent.eval.report` inside the rwb-agent service; the promotion checks sit in `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.agent.config` beside the policy loader of RWB-P10-E1058-APP.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The H and C dependencies of this table are the ones in the metadata rows: the three platform contract stories and RWB-PLT-N001-CON are build dependencies, RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON are contract dependencies built against their fakes, and RWB-P10-E1059-APP is the in-lane story that produced the shadow runs. DP-11 sits behind DP-06 and DP-07 on the two reads (one hop, 2 s) and adds no dependency of its own.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| AgentEvaluationController | Controller | Adds `GET /admin/agent-evaluations/{evaluationId}/report` on the agent base, the access check and the three media types (DP-13) |
| EvaluationReportService | Service | Aggregates the stored run, score and shadow rows into the report object: sample size, agreement per gap type, failure counts, total cost, cost per case and the two latencies (BR1) |
| EvaluationReportExporter | Service | Writes the CSV and the PDF from the same report object, so the three answers cannot disagree |
| PromotionProposalValidator | Service | BR2 to BR4 and BR6 inside the policy load for mode "L1": the run is DONE, the three parts are present, every condition is met and the sample reaches the minimum |
| PolicyParameterReader | Client | Reads the minimum sample and the promotion check list through the parameters contract, caches them for the request and fails closed when a value is missing (DP-06) |
| ReferenceListReader | Client | Reads LOV-AUTONOMY, LOV-CONFIG-STATUS and LOV-EVAL-STATUS through the reference-data contract (DP-07) |
| AgentPromotionRepository | Repository | Reads agent_evaluation_run, agent_evaluation and agent_run and writes agent_policy in `rwb_agent` only (DP-01) |

**Database and migrations**

- `V10_004__policy_promotion.sql` adds `evaluation_run_id` uuid, `promotion_conditions` jsonb, `watch_measures` jsonb and `fallback_rule` varchar(20) to `agent_policy` in `rwb_agent`, runs after `V10_003__evaluation_proposal.sql` in the rwb-agent Flyway sequence and touches no other schema (DP-15; AC2, AC6).
- The four tables are created by the P10 migrations of RWB-P10-E1058-APP and RWB-P10-E1060-APP; this story adds no table of its own, no column outside the four and no foreign key across services (DP-01; BR8).
- One index for the read: `ix_agent_policy_l1 ON agent_policy (agent_code, status, valid_from)`, so the version in force for an agent is found without a scan.

**Configuration and reference data**

- The minimum sample of an autonomy step for "INTAKE" - 200 - and the promotion check list: values of the rwb-case parameters contract, loaded and versioned by RWB-P3-E1042-CON, read at load time and never written in code (DP-06; ASM-0870).
- LOV-AUTONOMY (OFF, SHADOW, L1), LOV-CONFIG-STATUS (LOADED, APPROVED, RETIRED) and LOV-EVAL-STATUS (RUNNING, DONE, FAILED): reference data of rwb-case read through its contract (DP-07; ASM-0873).
- Policy version "P1" of agent "INTAKE" in force with prompt version "PR1", and the run "EV-INTAKE-001" with its 200 labelled runs, loaded through the evaluation harness of RWB-P10-E1060-APP.
- The list codes, the 2 s client budget and the CSV column order as service configuration.
- The legacy feature flag `rwb.agent.promotion` is kept as the legacy reference and is held by the platform library, not by this service: off, a policy with mode L1 is refused with 422 (ASM-0874).

**Build steps**

1. Flyway migration `V10_004__policy_promotion.sql` and the repository over `rwb_agent` (AC2, AC6).
2. EvaluationReportService over the 200-run fixture with the counts of the Background: 188, 7, 3, 2, 412.6000 baht, 2.0630 baht, 4,100 ms, 9,800 ms (AC1).
3. EvaluationReportExporter and the three media types of the report operation, from the same object (AC1).
4. The 409 of a run that is not DONE, with MSG-P10-008 (AC3).
5. PolicyParameterReader and ReferenceListReader against the two rwb-case fakes, with the missing-value and the delay paths (X7, X8; AC4, AC6).
6. PromotionProposalValidator inside the load: the three checks of AC4, AC5 and AC6 and the condition comparison against the scores of "EV-INTAKE-001" (AC2, AC4, AC5, AC6).
7. The loader-versus-approver 409 with MSG-P7-002 for an L1 version (AC7).
8. Pipeline scans for another service's table name, for a cross-schema foreign key and for the value 200 and the three lists in the source (BR4, BR7, BR8).
9. gateway-bff route contract test in front of the report read and the two configuration operations.

**Done when.** The eight test cases of section 16 pass, the report operation answers on `/api/recovery/agent/v1` in JSON, CSV and PDF, the report of "EV-INTAKE-001" carries the legacy counts and the legacy cost and latencies, the migration applies cleanly on an empty `rwb_agent` schema, no value of the minimum sample and no list value appears in the source, and no version in force and no case has changed.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P10-008 | Report requested before the evaluation is done | The evaluation of {agent} on sample {sample} has not finished. The report is ready when it is done. |
| MSG-P10-001 | The proposal fails a check | The {kind} file for {agent} was refused: {check}. The version in force is unchanged. |
| MSG-P7-002 | Loader approves own proposal | You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The four texts are copied unchanged from RWB-E1-061 and this story adds no message ID. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10. In AC3 the {agent} value is "INTAKE" and the {sample} value is "INTAKE-S1" version 1. In AC4, AC5, AC6, X7 and X8 the {kind} value is "policy" and the {check} value is the check name - "measures to watch present", "NO_CONTACT_POINT 0.8150 below 0.85", "sample size at least 200", the missing parameter name, or the list and the value outside it. In the access test the {action} value is "read the report or approve the proposal".

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story. RW-COE requests and exports the report through the report operation and RW-RISK reads it, with Accept text/csv or application/pdf for the steering committee pack; the reads are reached through the gateway-bff route in front of the admin path, so a screen never calls rwb-agent directly (DP-19). The report holds counts, rates, versions and durations only, so there is no personal field to mask on it. The agent monitor screen SCR-46 - the screen that shows runs, fallback, latency and cost per agent and comes with RWB-E2-031 - and the autonomy screen of Epic 3 are not changed by this story, and the exact path of the gateway-bff route in front of the reads is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0612; ASM-0872).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the minimum sample 200, the promotion check list, the three lists, the check names and the message IDs are parameter and reference values read at run time, and a missing value refuses the load instead of falling back to a default (BR3, BR4).
- No personal data in logs, tests or the report: the report holds counts, rates, versions and durations only, the fixtures are synthetic, and no account number, national ID number or name appears in a log, a CSV or a PDF (BR5).
- No read of another service's tables and no schema client: the parameter values and the lists come through the rwb-case contracts, the right through rwb-access, and no foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01, DP-06, DP-07).
- The only table this story writes is agent_policy, in `rwb_agent`, and the four promotion columns arrive only by `V10_004__policy_promotion.sql` (BR8, DP-15).
- A proposal never changes the mode in force before it is approved and its valid from date is reached, and the loader and the approver are different people (BR6, R-UNI-32).
- One hop and a 2 s client budget on every consumed REST call; the model budget belongs to the agent platform and is never a REST budget of this story (DP-11, ADR-020).
- The reads are reached through the gateway-bff route and never from a screen to the service (DP-19).
- The report publishes no event and writes no decision record: the run, the score and the version rows are internal to rwb-agent and are read through its own contract.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: contract slice of RWB-E1-061 for rwb-agent, written on Day 1 because a contract story carries no build dependency (§R5.7). The behaviour of the legacy key is unchanged - the disposition is Moved (no impact) - and only its seams are written down: the three evaluation operations on the base `/api/recovery/agent/v1` (DP-13), the L1 proposal payload with its policy-version binding and the approval operation used here, the agent topic `rwb.agent.events.v1` with the rule that an evaluation completes into a status and publishes no business message of its own, the parameter and reference-data operations of rwb-case this key consumes (DP-06, DP-07), and the four fakes the app story builds against. It does not restate the whole rwb-agent contract, whose baseline is RWB-P10-E1058-CON, and it fixes no table of its own beyond the four `rwb_agent` tables of the key (DP-01) and no migration beyond `V10_004__policy_promotion.sql` (DP-15). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the rwb-agent side of the intake agent evaluation and the L1 proposal fixed as a contract on Day 1: the three evaluation operations on `/api/recovery/agent/v1` with their query, their answer resources and their refusals, the L1 proposal payload with the four promotion members and its policy-version binding, the approval operation used here with its separation-of-duty refusal, the declaration of `rwb.agent.events.v1` with the rule that an evaluation publishes no message of its own, the parameter and reference-data operations of rwb-case that the promotion checks read, and the four contract fakes**, so that **the app story RWB-P10-E1061-APP, the operations story of the key and every story that reads an evaluation or a policy version build against one agreed, testable shape on Day 1 without waiting for the service to be complete**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy key RWB-E1-061 was written against in-process calls inside the monolith: the report was a service method behind the admin controller, the four promotion members were columns of the same `recovery` schema, the minimum sample was a value of the local policy JSON schema, the mode and status values were code enumerations, and the approval was the in-process maker-checker of the same deployment (legacy sections 12 and 13). In the target each of those is a boundary or an owner:

- The report is one REST operation on the base `/api/recovery/agent/v1`, with one hop and a 2 s client budget (DP-13; ADR-020).
- The four promotion members are columns of `agent_policy` in `rwb_agent`, added by the service's own migration in its own Flyway sequence (DP-01, DP-15).
- The minimum sample and the promotion check list are parameter values of rwb-case, reached through its contract (DP-06); the three lists are reference data of rwb-case (DP-07).
- The version in force is reached through the gateway-bff route by every screen and every export (DP-19).
- The completion of an evaluation is a row state, not a business event: the one business event of the service, `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` (EV-28), belongs to a business run of an agent and is declared here only so that the topic is complete.

Contract-first only works if the seam is written down once and faked on Day 1. The seam here is small and load-bearing: one report operation whose answer carries the legacy report members so that the approver's pack needs no change of shape, one payload for the L1 proposal that binds exactly one evaluation run and one policy version, one approval operation whose refusal is the separation of duty, and one honest statement that an evaluation completion is read and not published. Without it the app story invents its own answer, the report members drift from the legacy ones, and the row that proves what was measured stops matching the report the committee approved.

This story defines the provided side of this key and consumes the two rwb-case contracts. It restates nothing that another owner holds: the configuration operations and the policy resource are baselined in RWB-P10-E1058-CON, the evaluation harness that produces the runs is RWB-P10-E1060-APP, and the parameter rows and reference rows are rwb-case's (DP-01).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL), so the REST base, the topic and the event names follow the platform rule and not a local choice (§R4; DP-13).
- The CloudEvents 1.0 envelope and the platform error envelope are the platform baseline; this document narrows them where it must and says so.
- The agent runtime baseline contract of RWB-P10-E1058-CON is in force: the policy and prompt resources, the configuration operations `POST /admin/agent-configs` and `POST /admin/agent-configs/{versionId}/approve`, the error taxonomy and the queue `rwb-agent` in the namespace `rwb-recovery` are its elements, and this story reuses them rather than redefining them.
- The evaluation harness of RWB-P10-E1060-APP is known and produces the run resource this contract reads: it is the `POST /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-evaluations` operation of that story, and this contract fixes the shape once for both keys (ASM-0871).
- The parameter and reference-data contracts of rwb-case are published by RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and RWB-PLT-E1043-CON with their client libraries, and the operations are `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` and `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` owned by P3 (DP-06, DP-07).
- The four `rwb_agent` tables of the key - agent_evaluation_run, agent_evaluation, agent_run and agent_policy - are the P10 objects of the Ownership Map, and the four promotion columns are added by `V10_004__policy_promotion.sql` (DP-01, DP-15).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (§R5.7) and sits in contract group CG-W1.

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the three evaluation operations below the base `/api/recovery/agent/v1`: the start, the read and the report, with their query, their answer resource, their rights, their errors and their one-hop budget (AC1).
2. Fix the L1 proposal payload on the configuration load: the kind, the agent, the policy version, the autonomy mode, the four promotion members and the binding to exactly one evaluation run (AC2).
3. Fix the approval operation used here: its request, its answer, the separation-of-duty refusal and the dates it writes (AC3).
4. Declare the agent topic: `rwb.agent.events.v1` with `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` (EV-28), its envelope, its key, its registry subject and its retry and `.dlt` topics, and the rule that an evaluation completion publishes no message of its own (AC4).
5. Write the parameter and reference-data operations this key consumes, as owned by rwb-case, with the values the promotion checks read and the two lists (AC5).
6. Write the four fakes: the parameters fake, the reference-data fake, the gateway-bff route stub and the evaluation-run fixture, each with the answers and the failures this key's tests need (AC5; 12.8).
7. Publish the nine sub-tables of section 12 and the contract tests of section 16, and mark every shape that another document owns as baselined there (AC6).
8. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-P10-E1061-APP and to the test cases of this key.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A member of an answer or of a payload drifts from this document: a renamed member, a retyped amount, a dropped one of the four promotion members | The contract test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC1, AC2 |
| X2 | A caller asks for the report of a run that is not DONE | The operation refuses with 409 and names the run | MSG-P10-008 | AC1 |
| X3 | A payload carries a personal field, a customer identifier or an account number | The data-steward review and the contract test refuse the payload; nothing is written | None | AC2 |
| X4 | The payload names a run that does not belong to the agent or to the policy version it binds | The load is refused with 422 before the row is stored | MSG-P10-001 | AC2 |
| X5 | A produced message fails its registry subject, or the relay cannot reach the topic | The message is refused before the relay and routed to the `.dlt` topic of the agent topic with an alert | None | AC4 |
| X6 | A shape owned by another document is restated here and drifts from it | The contract test fails on the owner's document and this document is aligned, because the owner is the baseline | None | AC3, AC6 |
| X7 | A member, a query parameter, a type or a route path is missing from the source material | The element is marked with the placeholder, one gap row and one assumption row are carried, and the fake is written to the assumed shape | None | AC1, AC2, AC5 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the agent runtime baseline contract and the two rwb-case contracts as published |
| Negotiable | The member names and their types are fixed here; the values stay rows of the parameter, reference and policy tables, and the review with the owners settles any type detail |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app story of this key on Day 1 and gives every reader of an evaluation, a report or a policy version one shape |
| Estimable | Three provided evaluation operations, two restated configuration operations, two consumed reads, one topic declaration and four fakes |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact - the schema file, the payload, the fake, the document - and never against a business outcome |

**Target reading.** This contract adds no behaviour and no business value: the run, the sample, the 200 runs with 188 ANSWERED, 7 TIMED_OUT, 3 GUARDRAIL_FAILED and 2 BELOW_FLOOR, the 412.6000 baht, the condition "agreement at least 0.85 for every gap type", the fallback "rule result per R-UNI-32", the measures "acceptance, correction rate, fallback rate below 0.10", the minimum sample 200, the sample size 150 of "EV-INTAKE-003", the user "coe.user01" and the message IDs are the legacy values of RWB-E1-061, copied character for character, and the keys of the promotion payload are the field names of TSD P10 v2 T3.1 (DF-AGT-017 to DF-AGT-020). The disposition of the key is Moved (no impact): the contract states the seams of an unchanged behaviour. Three values are not named by any source and are marked where they appear: the route path and route name of the gateway-bff route in front of the reads - Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0613; ASM-0872) - the name of an event for the completion of an evaluation, which no source names and which this contract therefore does not declare (GAP-0613; ASM-0875), and the type and length of the members beyond the names the legacy report and TSD T3.1 give (GAP-0613; ASM-0876, ASM-0877).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The evaluation is three operations on one base - start, read and report - and no caller embeds the evaluation harness or reads `rwb_agent` | DP-11 behind DP-01; DP-13; legacy section 12 |
| BR2 | The report exists only for a run in status DONE, and its members are the legacy report members; the same run gives the same report | Legacy AC1, AC3; MSG-P10-008 |
| BR3 | An L1 proposal binds exactly one DONE evaluation run of the same agent and one policy version, and the four promotion members are columns of agent_policy | Legacy BR1; TSD P10 v2 T3.1 DF-AGT-017 to DF-AGT-020 |
| BR4 | The loader and the approver are different people, and the approval writes approved_by and valid_from | Legacy BR6; R-UNI-39; MSG-P7-002 |
| BR5 | The minimum sample and the promotion check list are parameter values of rwb-case read at load time, and the three lists are reference data of rwb-case: no such value is written in the contract | DP-06; DP-07; ASM-0873 |
| BR6 | `rwb.agent.events.v1` carries `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` (EV-28) and nothing else; an evaluation completion is a row state and publishes no message | Arch v5 slide 43 row 28; DP-14; ASM-0875 |
| BR7 | Every message is a CloudEvents 1.0 message on the owner's topic, keyed by the case ID, validated against its registry subject before the relay and routed to `.dlt` on failure, with retry topics | DP-09; DP-14; Arch v5 slide 42 |
| BR8 | One base and one topic per service: this contract declares `/api/recovery/agent/v1` and `rwb.agent.events.v1` for rwb-agent and never another service's path or topic as its own | DP-13; DP-14; Arch v5 slide 41 |
| BR9 | No personal data in a payload, an example or a fake: the report and the proposal carry identifiers, facts and rates only | Legacy section 17; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |

##### 9. State transitions

These are the states of this document, not of a case or a policy version:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The three evaluation operations, the L1 payload, the approval, the topic and the four fakes are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | The app story of this key and the test cases accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A member, a query parameter or a payload field is added without removing one | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change to an operation or to the payload | A member of the report, of the L1 payload or of the topic declaration is removed, renamed or retyped | In review, with the owner of the affected contract |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |
| Baselined | A baseline changes a restated shape | RWB-P10-E1058-CON publishes a new policy resource | Baselined, aligned to the baseline |

The run states RUNNING, DONE and FAILED are those of LOV-EVAL-STATUS and are set by the evaluation harness; the version states LOADED, APPROVED and RETIRED are those of LOV-CONFIG-STATUS and belong to RWB-P10-E1061-APP and RWB-P10-E1058-APP. This document fixes neither table of values; it names them as reference data read through the rwb-case contract.

##### 11. Data

The contract declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Start request | agent, sampleCode, sampleVersion, approaches; 202 AgentEvaluationRun; 409 a same evaluation already RUNNING; 422 an empty sample |
| Read answer | AgentEvaluationRun[] with the run row members of TSD P10 v2 T3.1 (DF-AGT-070 to DF-AGT-085), with Accept text/csv for the score and proposal rows |
| Report answer | agent, sampleSize, agreementByLabel[], failureCounts, totalCostThb, costPerCaseThb, latencyP50Ms, latencyP95Ms, policyVersion, promptVersion, modelVersion (the legacy report members) |
| L1 payload | kind "POLICY", agent "INTAKE", policyVersion, autonomyMode, evaluationRunId, promotionConditions, watchMeasures, fallbackRule, validFrom |
| Approval request and answer | the version ID in the path, the valid from date in the body; the AgentConfigVersion answer with status APPROVED, approved_by and valid_from |
| Error | the platform problem response: status, code, detail, the business message ID when one applies |
| Topic | `rwb.agent.events.v1`, `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` (EV-28), CloudEvents 1.0, key the case ID, subject the run ID |
| Consumed values | the minimum sample 200 for agent "INTAKE" and the promotion check list; LOV-AUTONOMY, LOV-CONFIG-STATUS and LOV-EVAL-STATUS with their versions |

The type and length of the members beyond the names the legacy report and TSD P10 v2 T3.1 give, and the internal member names of `promotionConditions` and `watchMeasures` beyond the three legacy texts, are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0613; ASM-0876, ASM-0877); this document fixes the member names and leaves the nested types to the review with the owners. The route name and path of the gateway-bff route are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0613; ASM-0872), and no event name for the completion of an evaluation is specified (GAP-0613; ASM-0875).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/agent/v1`; owner rwb-agent (P10).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Rights | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/admin/agent-evaluations` | Start the evaluation of an agent on a labelled sample: agent "INTAKE", sampleCode "INTAKE-S1", sampleVersion 1; 202 AgentEvaluationRun in status RUNNING; 409 a same evaluation already RUNNING (MSG-P10-003); 422 a sample with no labelled rows (MSG-P10-002) | Rules and parameters C, scope applied | Idempotency-Key header |
| GET | `/admin/agent-evaluations` | List evaluation runs with their scores and proposals: query agent, from, to; 200 AgentEvaluationRun[]; with Accept text/csv the score and proposal rows | Rules and parameters R, scope applied | Not applicable: the call writes nothing |
| GET | `/admin/agent-evaluations/{evaluationId}/report` | The report of one run: agent, sampleSize, agreementByLabel[], failureCounts, totalCostThb, costPerCaseThb, latencyP50Ms, latencyP95Ms and the three versions; 200 AgentEvaluationReport in application/json, text/csv or application/pdf; 409 the run is not DONE (MSG-P10-008); 404 unknown run | Rules and parameters R, scope applied | Not applicable: the same run gives the same report |

`POST /admin/agent-configs` and `POST /admin/agent-configs/{versionId}/approve` are provided by rwb-agent and baselined in RWB-P10-E1058-CON, which owns their full shape. This contract restates only the members this key writes or reads and declares no configuration operation of its own: the four promotion members of the L1 payload (AC2) and the separation-of-duty refusal of the approval (AC3). Errors of the three operations above: 401 no session, 403 no right (MSG-P4-002), 404 unknown run, 409 the business refusal named per operation, 422 a payload or a sample that fails a check (MSG-P10-001), 503 the store or a consumed contract unavailable.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in this contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | P3 rwb-case | The minimum sample of an autonomy step for agent "INTAKE" - 200 - and the promotion check list in force, with their version (DP-06) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 rwb-case | LOV-AUTONOMY, LOV-CONFIG-STATUS and LOV-EVAL-STATUS in force, against which the mode "L1" and the status values of every answer are checked (DP-07) |

Every operation is one hop with a 2 s client budget and is cached by the client library for the life of the request (DP-11 behind DP-06 and DP-07). No other service's data is read, and no schema client of another service exists in rwb-agent. The right check is the guard library's and is not a REST operation of this key.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Key | Payload (IDs and facts only) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` (EV-28) | `rwb.agent.events.v1` | P10 | the case ID | run ID, agent_code, agent_version, model_version, case_id, autonomy_mode, trigger_event, status, fallback, confidence, latency_ms, run_at |

`rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` is the one business event of the service and is published by a business run of an agent, through the outbox in the same transaction as the run row and validated against its registry subject before the relay. The topic carries its retry topics and its `.dlt` topic as the platform naming rule sets them (DP-09, DP-14).

No message is published when an evaluation run completes. An evaluation ends in `agent_evaluation_run.status` DONE and is read through `GET /admin/agent-evaluations`, the report operation and the CSV answer of the read. No source names an event for the completion of an evaluation, so this contract declares none, and a `rwb.agent.<Something>.v1` message invented for that state would be an unowned event type (ASM-0875). If the programme later wants one, its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0613; ASM-0875) and it is added here first, never in a service.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. This key reads no topic: the evaluation is started by RW-COE on request through `POST /admin/agent-evaluations` and reads its inputs through the two contracts of 12.2. The consumers of EV-28 are rwb-decision, rwb-document and rwb-deviation (Arch v5 slide 43), not this service.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The evaluation, the report and the promotion checks run inside rwb-agent on the admin request path and start no workflow of their own. `AgentRunWorkflow` on the task queue `rwb-agent` in the namespace `rwb-recovery` belongs to the agent platform of RWB-P10-E1058-CON and RWB-ITG-TE013-ITG, and the shadow runs this report aggregates were made by it; this contract declares neither its input nor its activities.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The evaluation is started by a person, the report is requested by a person and the proposal is loaded by a person; the Arch v5 job map names no job for an agent evaluation (slide 44). No Temporal Schedule is declared, changed or owned by this contract.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| agent_evaluation_run | P10 (rwb_agent) | The run resource of the start and the read, and the source of the report; status is one of LOV-EVAL-STATUS; no column added |
| agent_evaluation | P10 (rwb_agent) | The score rows the report aggregates by label key: sample_size, agreement_rate, precision and recall; no column added |
| agent_run | P10 (rwb_agent) | The shadow runs the report costs and times: status, latency_ms, cost_thb, evaluation_run_id; no column added |
| agent_policy | P10 (rwb_agent) | The L1 proposal row and its four promotion members evaluation_run_id, promotion_conditions, watch_measures and fallback_rule, added by `V10_004__policy_promotion.sql` (DP-15) |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in rwb_agent | The outbox, inbox and idempotency envelope of the one declared event (DP-09) |

`parameter_catalog`, `parameter_value`, `reference_version` and `reference_row` are P3's tables of schema `rwb_case` and are reached only through the two contracts of 12.2 (DP-01, DP-06, DP-07). No foreign key crosses a schema.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-case parameters fake (WireMock) | `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters`: the minimum sample 200 for agent "INTAKE" and the promotion check list with its version; a version that raises the minimum above 200; an answer without the minimum; a delay beyond 2 s | Contract tests, app story |
| rwb-case reference-data fake (WireMock) | `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}`: LOV-AUTONOMY with OFF, SHADOW and L1; LOV-CONFIG-STATUS with LOADED, APPROVED and RETIRED; LOV-EVAL-STATUS with RUNNING, DONE and FAILED; a list version that lacks L1; a delay beyond 2 s | Contract tests, app story |
| gateway-bff route stub | A pass-through route of one hop in front of the three provided operations, preserving application/json, text/csv and application/pdf and returning the 403 of MSG-P4-002 unchanged; its route name and path are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0613; ASM-0872) | Contract tests, app story |
| Evaluation-run fixture (in-service, not WireMock) | The 200 stored runs of "EV-INTAKE-001" with 188 ANSWERED, 7 TIMED_OUT, 3 GUARDRAIL_FAILED and 2 BELOW_FLOOR, 412.6000 baht, median 4,100 ms and 95th percentile 9,800 ms; the run "EV-INTAKE-003" with sample size 150; a run in status RUNNING | Contract tests, app story |

The configuration store stub, the outbox stub and the access stub are the platform's and are used but not declared here. Every fixture is synthetic: no production run, no customer identifier and no personal value appears in one, and the agent model endpoint INT-23 is never called by a test of this contract.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 3 provided, 2 consumed, 2 restated | The start, the read and the report on `/api/recovery/agent/v1`; the rwb-case parameters read and list read; the configuration load and approve restated from RWB-P10-E1058-CON; one hop, 2 s each |
| Kafka | 1 declared, 0 consumed | `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` (EV-28) on `rwb.agent.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics; no message for the completion of an evaluation |
| Temporal | None | No workflow and no schedule in this contract; `AgentRunWorkflow` on the queue `rwb-agent` is the agent platform's |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** `contract/agent-evaluation-operations.yaml` (the start, the read and the report with their query, answers, rights, errors and budget), `contract/agent-l1-proposal.yaml` (the payload with the four promotion members and the run binding), `contract/agent-config-approval.md` (the approval operation as restated from the baseline, with the separation-of-duty refusal), `contract/agent-evaluation-topic.asyncapi.yaml` (`rwb.agent.events.v1` with EV-28, the retry and `.dlt` topics and the rule that an evaluation publishes none), `contract/agent-promotion-parameters.md` (the two consumed operations and the values the promotion reads) and the four fake mappings with their synthetic fixtures.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON for the app story; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON for the app story; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON for the app story |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON for the app story |

This story is Day 1 and holds no build dependency of its own (§R5.7): the platform contracts it names are those its consumer adds, and the two C dependencies, RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON, are the rwb-case side of the parameter and list reads, built against their fakes. DP-11 is the pattern of the three provided and the two consumed reads; DP-09 and DP-14 sit behind the one declared event and add no dependency here.

**Build steps**

1. Write the three evaluation operations with their query, answer resources, rights, errors and one-hop budget, and add a lint to the pipeline (AC1).
2. Write the L1 payload with the four promotion member names, the run binding and the no-personal-data rule (AC2).
3. Restate the approval operation from the baseline with the separation-of-duty refusal and mark the baseline as owner (AC3).
4. Write the AsyncAPI document for `rwb.agent.events.v1`: EV-28, its envelope, key, subject, registry subject, retry and `.dlt` topics, and the statement that an evaluation publishes no message (AC4).
5. Write the two consumed operations and the values the promotion reads, with the parameter and reference-data owners named (AC5).
6. Build the four fake mappings and their synthetic fixtures, including the missing parameter, the list without L1 and the two delays (AC5).
7. Add the six contract tests of section 16, including the drift test between each fake and this document (AC6).
8. Tag the baseline and collect the sign-off of the app story of this key and of the rwb-case owner on the two restated consumed shapes.

**Done when.** The six contract files validate in the pipeline, the six contract tests pass, the four fakes answer every consumed path and payload, and RWB-P10-E1061-APP has accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P10-008 | Report requested before the evaluation is done | The evaluation of {agent} on sample {sample} has not finished. The report is ready when it is done. |
| MSG-P10-001 | The proposal fails a check | The {kind} file for {agent} was refused: {check}. The version in force is unchanged. |
| MSG-P10-002 | The sample has no labelled rows | Sample {sample} has no labeled rows for {agent}. Load the labels before you run the evaluation. |
| MSG-P10-003 | Same evaluation already running | An evaluation of {agent} on sample {sample} is already running. Wait for it to finish. |
| MSG-P7-002 | Loader approves own proposal | You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | The version is already approved | This version is already approved. |

The five business messages of the evaluation and the promotion are the legacy messages of RWB-E1-061 and RWB-E1-058 and keep their wording character for character; MSG-P4-002 and MSG-GEN-004 are the platform messages of a right and of a state already reached. This contract adds no message. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

None in this story. The contract serves the report export for the steering committee pack and the version reads of the configuration operations: both are reached through the gateway-bff route (DP-19) and belong to RWB-P10-E1061-APP and RWB-P10-E1058-CON. The contract fixes no screen field, no order and no masking rule, and the agent monitor screen SCR-46 and the autonomy screen of Epic 3 are untouched. The route name and path of the gateway-bff route are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0613; ASM-0872).

TC-P10-E1061-CON-01 to TC-P10-E1061-CON-06 are new (D-RCV-60) and test only the deliverables of this story: the three operation shapes, the L1 payload and its binding, the approval, the topic declaration, the four fakes and the completeness of section 12. They add no `-ITG` copy, because this key carries no integration dependency and the story set holds no integration story for it; the cross-service behaviour is proved against the fakes.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the minimum sample 200, the check list, the three lists, the conditions, the measures and the run identifiers stay rows of the parameter, reference and policy tables, and the contract only names them (BR5).
- No personal data in a payload, an example or a fake: identifiers, facts and rates only, and the report body is never copied into the L1 payload (BR9).
- The contract names the agent base and the agent topic as rwb-agent's and consumes every other operation and topic; a document that declares another service's path or topic as provided fails the review (BR8, DP-13, DP-14).
- The configuration operations and the policy resource are restated, never redefined: the baseline RWB-P10-E1058-CON owns them and a drift is corrected there (BR3, X6).
- Every payload is validated against its registry subject before the relay, and a refusal is routed to `.dlt` and alerted with the retry topics in between (BR7).
- An event is declared only where a source names it: the completion of an evaluation publishes no message, and no unowned event type is invented (BR6, ASM-0875).
- Every fixture is synthetic; no production run, report, policy version or customer value is copied into a schema, a payload or a fake.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-062 for rwb-agent. This is the contract slice of the legacy key: the screening run-start and run-read operations that replace the in-process orchestrator call and the legacy admin paths on the base `/api/recovery/agent/v1` (DP-13, DP-20), the screening proposal payload that replaces the `screening-v1` object of the legacy section 12, the three event payloads that turn EV-28 and the two new run facts into CloudEvents on `rwb.agent.events.v1` (DP-09), the four consumed contracts of rwb-case, rwb-deviation, rwb-source-data and rwb-document plus the rule-model read of the embedded kit (DP-04, DP-18), the tables of schema `rwb_agent` the shapes sit on (DP-01), the Flyway ownership of the review count (DP-15), the gateway-bff route in front of the reads (DP-19), and the fakes. It does not restate the whole rwb-agent contract, whose baseline is RWB-P10-E1058-CON, and it builds no business behaviour. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the rwb-agent side of the deviation screening agent fixed as a contract on Day 1: the run-start and run-read operations on the base `/api/recovery/agent/v1`, the screening proposal payload with its code, confidence, reason, source reference and owner role, the three event payloads on `rwb.agent.events.v1` for a run started, a run completed and a proposal raised, the consumed shapes of rwb-case, rwb-deviation, rwb-source-data and rwb-document and the rule-model read of the embedded kit, with the fakes that answer each of them**, so that **RWB-P10-E1062-APP, RWB-S8-E1062-APP, RWB-P5-E1062-APP, RWB-P4-E1062-APP and RWB-ITG-E1062-ITG build against one agreed, testable shape without waiting for the screening runtime to be complete**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy key RWB-E1-062 was written against a single deployment: the screening listener called an in-process orchestrator, the case, the interaction ledger, the documents and the rule catalog were read through in-process interfaces (`CaseQueryService`, `InteractionLedgerReader.list`, `DocumentQueryService.listByCase` and `getFields`, `RuleEvaluator.ownerFor`), the agent tables, the run and the evaluation lived in the same schema, and the two admin paths were served on the legacy monolith base (legacy section 12). In the target every one of those is a boundary: the orchestrator becomes a run-start operation on the service's own base (DP-20, DP-13; ADR-020), the ledger becomes rwb-source-data's contract (DP-18), the deviation read becomes S8's contract, the rule rows become a package the embedded kit fetches from the rwb-decision registry (DP-04; ADR-017), the run facts become events on the service's own topic (DP-09; ADR-015), and the run and its proposals become rows of schema `rwb_agent` (DP-01; ADR-014).

Contract-first only works if the seam is written down once. The seam here is small and load-bearing: two operations whose answer carries the run and its proposals so that the app story, the integration story and the screens of the deviation module need no change of shape; one proposal payload that keeps every legacy member — code, reasons, source references, the preceding contact of X1, the owner role and the confidence — and carries no personal data; three event payloads that carry facts only; and one fetched package shape that keeps the owner role a data value of rwb-decision.

If the shape is agreed and faked on Day 1, four teams move at once. The app story of this key builds the listener, the input assembler, the rule adapter, the guardrail and the scorer against these fakes; the S8 and P5 sibling stories build the deviation record and the document read against the same names; the integration story proves the same values across the real services; and every reader of a screening run reads one shape. Without it, each caller invents its own answer, the legacy members drift, and the score that decides the L1 segment stops matching the run that produced it.

This story defines the provided side of the key and the consumed side it needs, and never restates what another owner holds: the agent runtime baseline and the evaluation operations belong to RWB-P10-E1058-CON and RWB-P10-E1060-CON, the deviation record is S8's, the ledger is P1's, the case, the parameters and the lists are P3's, the documents are P5's and the rule registry is P7's (DP-01).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL), so the REST base, the topic and the event names follow the platform rule and not a local choice (§R4; DP-13).
- The CloudEvents 1.0 envelope and the platform error envelope are the platform baseline; this document narrows them where it must and says so.
- The agent runtime baseline contract of RWB-P10-E1058-CON is in force: the run resource, the policy and prompt resources, the admin run read and the error taxonomy are its elements, and this story reuses them rather than redefining them. Its task queue is `rwb-agent` and its namespace `rwb-recovery` (§R4).
- The evaluation contract of RWB-P10-E1060-CON is in force: the sample load, the evaluation start and the evaluation read carry the score rows and the review count this key's AC2 depends on, and this story restates none of them (ASM-0886).
- The embedded Drools kit of RWB-PLT-E1072-CON publishes the KieBase registry, the first-match semantics and the `RuleResult` with `packageCode`, `packageVersion`, `ruleId` and the outputs, and the rule-model read `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-models/{n}/{v}` belongs to it (DP-04).
- The outbox and retry library of RWB-PLT-TE006-CON publishes the outbox and inbox envelope, the relay and the `.dlt` rule (DP-09).
- The parameter and reference-data client libraries of RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and RWB-PLT-E1043-CON are published, and the rwb-case contracts they wrap are the ones of RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON (DP-06, DP-07).
- The rwb-deviation contract of S8, the rwb-source-data ledger contract of P1 and the rwb-document contract of P5 are named by their owners; the operation paths this document fixes where no source names them are marked with the gap and the assumption (GAP-0615; ASM-0880, ASM-0883).
- The per-service Flyway sequence of RWB-PLT-E1044-CON is in force and `V10_005__evaluation_review_count.sql` is owned by RWB-P10-E1062-APP in the rwb-agent sequence (DP-15).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (§R5.7) and sits in contract group CG-W1.
- The release date 30 November 2026 is tentative and is copied unchanged.

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the run-start operation that replaces the in-process orchestrator call: its method, its path below the base `/api/recovery/agent/v1`, its request members, its answer resource and its refusal codes (AC1).
2. Draft the run-read operation: its path from Arch v5 slide 16, its query, its answer with the proposals, its rights, its errors and its one-hop budget (AC2).
3. Fix the screening proposal payload: the code from LOV-DEVIATION, the confidence, the reasons, the source references, the preceding contact of X1, the owner role and the marker, with no personal value in any member (AC3).
4. Declare the three events on `rwb.agent.events.v1`: the envelope, the key, the payload members taken from the `agent_run` and the proposal fields of TSD P10 v2 T3.1, the registry subject and the `.dlt` route (AC4).
5. Fix the consumed shapes: the case read, the parameter and list reads, the deviation read, the ledger read, the document read and the rule-model read, each with its owner, its use in the legacy criteria, its one-hop budget and the ones whose path no source names (AC5).
6. Write the seven contract fakes with the answers, the errors and the timings this key's tests need (AC6).
7. Publish the nine sub-tables of section 12 and the contract tests: the operation shapes, the proposal payload, the event envelopes, the consumed shapes, the fakes and a drift test between each fake and this document (AC7).
8. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-P10-E1062-APP, the S8, P5 and P4 sibling stories and RWB-ITG-E1062-ITG.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A member of the run-start request or of the answer drifts from this document: a renamed member, a retyped confidence, a dropped one of the proposal members | The contract test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC1, AC3 |
| X2 | A run-start request arrives without the case ID, the trigger event or the idempotency key | The operation refuses the request with 422 and names the field; nothing is written | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |
| X3 | The proposal payload or an event payload gains a personal field | The data-steward review and the contract test refuse the payload; nothing is published | None | AC3, AC4 |
| X4 | A produced payload fails its registry subject, or the relay cannot reach the topic | The message is refused before the relay and routed to the `.dlt` topic of the agent topic with an alert | None | AC4 |
| X5 | A consumed shape drifts from its owner's published contract | The fake is corrected against the owner's document and the drift test of this document fails until they agree | None | AC5, AC6 |
| X6 | A field-level detail of a consumed operation or a payload member is missing from the source material | The element is marked with the placeholder, one gap row and one assumption row are carried, and the fake is written to the assumed shape | None | AC1, AC5, AC6 |
| X7 | The run read is asked for an unknown run, or a role without the right reads it | The operation answers 404, or 403 with MSG-P4-002, and no member of the answer leaks | MSG-P4-002 | AC2 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the agent runtime baseline, the evaluation contract, the rule kit and the rwb-case, rwb-deviation, rwb-source-data and rwb-document contracts as published |
| Negotiable | Field-level detail of the consumed operations is settled with their owners; the operation shape, the proposal payload, the event payloads and the budgets are fixed by this realignment |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app story and the three sibling stories of this key on Day 1 and gives every reader of a screening run one shape |
| Estimable | Two provided operations, six consumed reads, one proposal payload, three events, seven fakes |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact — the schema file, the payload, the fake, the document — and never against a business outcome |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

