**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-062 for rwb-deviation, carrying the deviation estate the shadow screening run reads (the open codes of the case and the owner role each code would route to) and the gate that keeps a screening raise out of the service while the policy in force is SHADOW. Applied: the plan's H row is None and the platform libraries of DP-04, DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-15 and DP-19 arrive with the baseline; the Ownership Map gives S8 two write operations and no read, so the read is declared here with a gap (GAP-3085; ASM-5252); and legacy AC1 to AC9 stay with RWB-P10-E1062-APP. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **rwb-deviation to serve the screening agent the open deviations of a case and the owner role each code in force would route to, and to refuse any raise that names the screening agent while the policy in force is SHADOW**, so that **the shadow run reads the deviation estate of the case from its owner and changes nothing in force — no deviation record, no contact stop, no clock**.

This story is the rwb-deviation part of legacy RWB-E1-062. The legacy story has the agent read "the case, the interaction ledger, the documents and their fields" and store proposals in shadow (legacy sections 2 and 4), and its Data table reads `deviation.deviation_code` "so a code already open is not proposed again" and `recovery_case.deviation_open` (DF-CAS-038, DF-CAS-019). Two of those facts are this service's: the open deviations of the case, and the routing truth of each code.

Inside `rwb-deviation` this is the screening-input capability of the deviation service:

- Service `rwb-deviation`, schema `rwb_deviation`, REST base `/api/recovery/deviation/v1`, topic `rwb.deviation.events.v1` with event names `rwb.deviation.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-deviation` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.deviation` (context pack, service row).
- `GET /deviations` with the case as query answers the deviation estate of one case in one hop: the open deviations with their code, state, raised date, contact stop, paused state and outcome, and beside them the owner role that each code of LOV-DEVIATION routes to at the package version in force (DP-13, DP-04, DP-07).
- The answer is built from `deviation` in `rwb_deviation` only; no `recovery_case` row, no `v_ace_*` view and no another service's table is read (DP-01).
- `ScreeningRaiseGate` refuses a raise that names `raised_by` "SCREENING_AGENT" while the autonomy mode of policy "SCREENING" in force is "SHADOW", read on the rwb-agent contract of RWB-P10-E1062-CON (DP-20); a refused raise writes no row, publishes no event and moves no clock.
- No event is published by this slice: in shadow nothing is raised, so `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1` (EV-06) stays with the raise story (DP-09 as a prohibition).

What this story does not own: the agent runtime, the policy "SCREENING" and its versions, the prompt "PR1", the output schema "screening-v1", the guardrail checks, the per-proposal owner resolution, the evaluation on sample "SCREEN-S1" and the run states, which are rwb-agent's in RWB-P10-E1062-APP against the contract RWB-P10-E1062-CON, and which own legacy AC1 to AC9; the documents and extracted fields the agent reads, which are rwb-document's in RWB-P5-E1062-APP; the masking policy itself, which is rwb-access's in RWB-P4-E1062-APP; the raise, pause, routing, contact stop and clear of a deviation, which are the Epic 2 stories of this service; and the end-to-end proof across the five services, which is RWB-ITG-E1062-ITG.

##### 2. Business rationale

A dispute, a death, a fraud sign or a lost contact found late means contact that should have stopped, or a case worked on the wrong route. The screening agent reads the case, the ledger and the documents at entry and again when a document arrives, and proposes deviations with reasons (legacy section 2); in Epic 1 the proposals are stored only, scored against the business analysts' review and shown to nobody. The measurement is only worth something if a proposal is measured against the deviation estate the case actually carries, and if nothing in that estate moves while the agent is in shadow.

Three target facts shape this slice.

1. **The deviation estate is this service's.** `deviation` is S8's single table in `rwb_deviation` (context pack ownership rows; TSD S8 T3.1), so an open code, its state, its contact stop and its paused state are answered here and nowhere else. The agent cannot read another service's table (DP-01), and under DP-18 the ledger it also reads is rwb-source-data's, not this service's answer.
2. **The owner role of a code is data, and its owner is the service that routes it.** R-DEV-02 to R-DEV-06 are rows of the DEV route set, 22 rules over 9 states in TSD S8 T4, and they are what assigns each deviation to the complaint officer, the specialist, the fraud investigator or Legal (FSD S8 A2.4). Serving the projection here means the agent's proposal names the role the case would really route to, which is REQ-DVH-003, and the value is read with the package version and never typed in code (DP-04, DP-07).
3. **Shadow means nothing in force moves.** Legacy BR1 and AC1 fix it: no deviation record, `deviation_open` false on every case, no contact stop, no user-facing proposal. In the target the agent cannot write here at all (no operation of this service is a write the agent may call), and the gate of this story refuses a screening raise on the service side as well, so a change in the agent cannot leak into a deviation row, a contact stop or a clock (R-DEV-01 is never fired from a shadow run).

The slice therefore supports REQ-DVH-001 (the codes of the estate the detection is measured on), REQ-DVH-003 (each code routes to its named owner, an unmapped code to the team manager) and REQ-DVH-007 (a complaint is matched to the contact before it — the ledger window is rwb-source-data's and this answer carries no interaction). It changes no rule of the DEV route set and no policy of the agent.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The `rwb_deviation` baseline is in place: `deviation` exists with the columns of DF-CAS-036 to DF-CAS-045 and the standard record columns of TSD S8 T3.0, loaded by the DB story of this service, and the outbox, inbox and idempotency tables of the platform event library exist in the schema.
- The service runs as its own login on `rwb_deviation` (DP-02) and holds no grant on another `rwb_*` schema and no `v_ace_*` grant, so a statement on `recovery_case` or `rwb_case` is refused by the database and fails the boundary test.
- RWB-P10-E1062-CON is published: the rwb-agent contract of this legacy key, which fixes the policy read (agent "SCREENING", its version in force, its autonomy mode, the confidence floor and the prompt) and the run key "SCREENING:<caseId>:<eventId>" the agent uses. The operation name and the field names of the policy read are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3085; ASM-5253), and the story builds against its fake.
- The DEV route set is in force in the rwb-decision registry with R-DEV-02 to R-DEV-06 among its 22 rules, reachable on the registry read with its package version; its operation name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3085; ASM-5254).
- The embedded Drools kit of RWB-PLT-E1072-CON is on the service template, so the projection is evaluated in the service and not in the caller (DP-04).
- The parameters contract and client library of rwb-case are on the service template (DP-06), and the maximum number of deviations one answer carries is a parameter value; its value is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3085; ASM-5256).
- The reference-data contract of rwb-case is on the service template (DP-07), with LOV-DEVIATION (X1 to X7) and LOV-RAISED-BY (SCREENING_AGENT, RULE, OFFICER, CUSTOMER_CONTACT) at the version in force (TSD S8 T3.2).
- The authorisation decision of rwb-access is consumed as the cached permission of the service (DP-08, which arrives with the baseline and is not added to the H row): the read needs Case record right R and the two write operations need right U (TSD S8 T-A.1, T-A.2).
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft contract baseline; the contract is tagged by RWB-P10-E1062-CON when its tests pass.

##### 4. Flow

1. The screening run of RWB-P10-E1062-APP assembles its inputs and asks this service for the deviation estate of the case: `GET /api/recovery/deviation/v1/deviations?caseId=<caseId>` with the identity SY-AGENT, one hop, inside a 2 s budget (legacy section 4 step 3; DP-13).
2. `DeviationGuard` authorises the call from the cached decision of rwb-access (Case record right R, scope applied) and refuses with 403 and MSG-P4-002 before a row is read (legacy X7, TC-E1-062-10).
3. `OpenDeviationReader` reads the `deviation` rows of the case in `rwb_deviation` whose `cleared_at` is null and whose `state` is not a cleared state, with the code, state, raised date and actor, contact stop, paused state and outcome (DF-CAS-036 to DF-CAS-045).
4. `DeviationOwnerProjection` takes the codes of LOV-DEVIATION at the version in force from the reference-data contract (DP-07), fetches the DEV package at its version in force on the registry read (DP-04), evaluates R-DEV-02 to R-DEV-06 in the embedded kit for each code, and pairs each code with the owner role the rule assigns; a code with no owner row is paired with "RW-TEAMMGR" and the marker "unmapped" (legacy BR3, AC4).
5. `ScreeningInputAssembler` builds the answer: the open deviations of the case and the owner projection of the codes in force, with no person name, no contact value, no handler identity and no free-text note (legacy section 11; BR2).
6. The answer is returned inside the 2 s budget, one hop, with no call to another service on the read path beyond the reference-data and package reads of steps 4, and the read is repeated on the same inputs with the same answer (a read is idempotent and writes nothing).
7. On the write path, `ScreeningRaiseGate` checks each raise request that names `raised_by` "SCREENING_AGENT": it reads the autonomy mode of policy "SCREENING" at its version in force on the rwb-agent contract (DP-20). Where the mode is "SHADOW" the request is refused with 409 and no message to a user, nothing is written, no outbox row is created, no contact stop is set and no clock moves (legacy BR1; AC1).
8. Where the mode is not "SHADOW" the gate lets the request through to the raise path of the Epic 2 story of this service, and this story changes nothing of that path (legacy section 19; RWB-E2-029).
9. A read of a case that this service holds no deviation for answers an empty list with 200: the case is rwb-case's row and this service does not confirm its existence, so no 404 is invented for a case it does not own (ASM-5252).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The calling identity holds no Case record right R | Refused with 403 before any row is read; nothing is returned | MSG-P4-002 | AC5, TC-E1-062-10 |
| X2 | The `caseId` query is absent or is not a case reference | 422 and no read; nothing is written | MSG-GEN-001 | Section 14 |
| X3 | The reference-data or the package read does not answer inside the budget, or the registry has no package version in force | 503 with the platform envelope and the name of the system; no partial answer is built | MSG-GEN-006 | Section 14 |
| X4 | A code of the version in force has no owner row in R-DEV-02 to R-DEV-06 | The projection names "RW-TEAMMGR" and the marker "unmapped" for that code; the rest of the answer stands | None | AC3 |
| X5 | A raise request names `raised_by` "SCREENING_AGENT" while the policy in force is "SHADOW" | Refused with 409; no `deviation` row, no `deviation_open` change, no contact stop, no clock and no outbox row | None to a user | AC4 |
| X6 | The rwb-agent policy read does not answer, so the mode in force is unknown | The raise is refused with 503 and the reason names the agent contract; the shadow side never falls back to "raise" | MSG-GEN-006 | Section 14 |
| X7 | A component, a statement or a test reaches a `recovery_case` row, a `rwb_case` table, a `v_ace_*` view or another service's schema | The grant refuses the statement and the boundary test fails the build; nothing is released | None (pipeline log) | Section 17, BR1, BR6 |

X1 and X5 to X7 are the legacy exception paths carried onto the slice (the role case X7 of the legacy story is TC-E1-062-10, the shadow case is BR1); X2 to X4 are the paths the two owner reads and the projection add. The agent's own paths — a code outside X1 to X7, a low-confidence proposal, a repeated event on the run side and a timeout — are RWB-P10-E1062-APP's and are not restated here.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Answers from `rwb_deviation` only and builds on Day 1 against the RWB-P10-E1062-CON fake, the registry and reference-data fakes and the platform libraries of the baseline; it waits for no in-lane story |
| Negotiable | The view name, the answer's field order, the parameter values of the limit and the wording of the projection are this story's; the codes, the owner roles, the states and the lists are rows |
| Valuable | The shadow run is measured against the real deviation estate of each case, a proposal names the role the case would route to, and no shadow run can create a deviation, a stop or a clock |
| Estimable | One module, one read operation, one projection, one gate, one view and one Flyway step |
| Small | Fits one sprint as a secondary slice of the legacy key, beside RWB-P10-E1062-APP and RWB-P5-E1062-APP |
| Testable | Every criterion runs on synthetic deviations and synthetic packages through the contract fakes, plus the access, refusal and boundary cases |

The five criteria are new and test only this slice: the deviation estate the screening run reads and the gate that keeps a screening raise out of the service in shadow. The legacy criteria AC1 to AC9 of RWB-E1-062 are owned word for word by RWB-P10-E1062-APP (the shadow flags, the comparison, the document trigger, the owner role, the preceding contact, the review marker, the repeated event, the code outside the list and the timeout), and no legacy criterion text is copied here. Two legacy values are reused because the sources publish them: the owner role "RW-FRAUD" from R-DEV-04 for X4 and the mapping of a code with no row to "RW-TEAMMGR" with the marker "unmapped" (legacy AC4, BR3); they are asserted on this service's projection, not on the agent's proposal. Two points are recorded rather than smoothed over: the read is not in the Ownership Map (GAP-3085; ASM-5252), and the reference of a case this service holds no deviation for is answered as an empty list rather than a 404 (ASM-5252).

The two text rows of R-DEV-02 and R-DEV-03 are those of the FSD, copied character for character; R-DEV-04 to R-DEV-06 are rows of the same DEV route set (22 rules over 9 states, TSD S8 T4) whose owner-role values are published only for X4 and are otherwise read from the package with its version. The codes of R-DEV-05 and R-DEV-06 are not printed by any source read for this slice, so they are not guessed.

| BR2 | The answer carries references, codes, states, dates and the owner projection, and no person name, contact value, handler identity, free-text note or document field value | Template and Rules §R7.2 (s17); TSD S8 T6.2; legacy section 11 |
| BR3 | The owner role of each code is read from the rule rows R-DEV-02 to R-DEV-06 at the package version in force; a code with no row maps to "RW-TEAMMGR" and carries the marker "unmapped" | Legacy BR3, AC4, X5; REQ-DVH-003; DP-04 |
| BR4 | In shadow the service raises nothing: no deviation record, no `deviation_open` change, no contact stop, no clock and no event, and the gate refuses a raise that names the screening agent while the mode in force is SHADOW | Legacy BR1, AC1; agent_policy.autonomy_mode is rwb-agent's (DF-AGT-008) |
| BR5 | The codes, the actor values and the owner roles are reference data and rule rows read with their version; none of them is a constant, a default or a branch in the module | FSD S8 BR-S8-001, BR-S8-004; TSD S8 T3.2; DP-07 |
| BR6 | The interaction ledger is rwb-source-data's and the ledger of the agent's reads is written by its listener from the event: this service writes no ledger row and reads none (DP-18) | DP-18; context pack default ruling; Architecture v5 slide 13 |
| BR7 | This service publishes no event of this slice: `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1` and `rwb.deviation.DeviationCleared.v1` stay with the raise and clear steps (DP-09 as a prohibition) | DP-09; TSD S8 T5.3; legacy BR7 |
| BR8 | A read is idempotent: the same request on the same rows and the same package version answers the same values and writes nothing; the two write operations of the service are not called by the agent | Legacy AC7; TSD S8 T-A.1 |

BR1 and BR2 are property tests over the serialised answer: a synthetic personal value placed in `handler_user_id` or in a free-text column must not appear in the JSON, the log or the span attributes. BR3 is executed by `DeviationOwnerProjection`, which asks the kit for the rules and never for a table of owner roles; a build check fails on a code or an owner role in the source. BR4 is executed by `ScreeningRaiseGate` before the raise path, with the mode read on the agent contract. BR6 and BR7 are prohibitions checked by the same build: no ledger table, no Drools event, no outbox write on this slice, and no outbound call to rwb-source-data.

##### 9. State transitions

None for the case and none for a deviation. This story changes no case status, raises no deviation and clears none: it reads the state of the `deviation` rows of the case and refuses a screening raise in shadow, so the state machine of the DEV route set is not entered (TSD S8 T4). `DEV_FLAGGED` and every state after it stay with the raise, routing, handling and clear steps of the Epic 2 stories of this service, and `deviation_open` is a rwb-case field that this slice never writes (ASM-5253).

| Read or step | Event | Condition | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| The read request | The caller's identity and the case | The Case record right R is granted | The estate of the case is answered; nothing is written |
| The read request | A case this service holds no open deviation for | The right is granted | An empty list is answered; the case row is not confirmed here |
| The raise request | `raised_by` is "SCREENING_AGENT" | The mode in force is "SHADOW" | Refused with 409; no row, no event, no clock, no contact stop |
| The raise request | `raised_by` is "SCREENING_AGENT" | The mode in force is not "SHADOW" | Passed to the raise path of the Epic 2 story; this slice changes nothing of it |
| The projection | The package read answers | R-DEV-02 to R-DEV-06 are in force | Each code pairs with its owner role; a code with no row pairs with "RW-TEAMMGR" and "unmapped" |
| The projection | The package or the reference-data read does not answer | X3 | Held; 503 with MSG-GEN-006; no partial projection is served |

The run states of the screening agent — PENDING, RUNNING, TIMED_OUT, GUARDRAIL_FAILED and the review marker of a low-confidence proposal — are rwb-agent's rows and rwb-agent's transitions (RWB-P10-E1062-APP), and no state of them is written or read here.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| SY-AGENT, agent platform | Case record right R (TSD S8 T6.1): reads the deviation estate of a case and the owner projection, masked, in scope; holds no write right and calls no write operation |
| SY-RULES, the embedded rule kit | Evaluates R-DEV-02 to R-DEV-06 for the projection from the package in force; subject to the same checks as a person |
| rwb-deviation service identity (the service login, DP-02) | Serves the read, reads `deviation` in `rwb_deviation` and the two owner contracts of DP-04 and DP-07, and runs the raise gate; holds no grant on another schema and no `v_ace_*` grant |
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Owns the sample and the evaluation (RWB-P10-E1062-APP); this story serves that work the estate it is measured on and grants it nothing of its own |
| RW-COMPLAIN, RW-SPECIAL, RW-FRAUD, RW-LEGAL, RW-TEAMMGR | The roles the projection names: they hold Case record RU or R as TSD S8 T6.1 gives it and read the same estate on their own screens; nothing is granted by this story beyond the matrix |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Case record CRU: raises and clears a deviation in the Epic 2 stories, through the two write operations the Ownership Map gives the service; the screening gate never widens that right |
| RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-PLATADM, RW-DATASTEW | Read run metadata or platform administration of the service, as the matrix gives it; no deviation content of their own |

The rights are the rows of TSD S8 T6.1 and the declared right of each operation in TSD S8 T-A.1 and T-A.2. DP-08 is not in this story's pattern set: the authorisation decision is rwb-access's and is consumed as the cached permission the service template already carries, so the check is stated here and not built here. The agent's identity is read only: no shared identity exists for its reads, and every read is authorised with the caller's own identity.

No personal data. The answer carries identifiers, codes, states, dates, a boolean and a rule version. No name, address, contact value or identity number enters the answer, a log, a trace or a workflow input, and every fixture is synthetic.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-deviation (S8); base `/api/recovery/deviation/v1` (DP-13).

| Method | Path | Query | Answer | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/deviations` | `caseId` (required) | The open deviations of the case and the owner projection of the codes in force | Case record right R, scope applied | Idempotent read; no `Idempotency-Key` needed |

The answer is one object with two arrays. `openDeviations` carries, per row, `deviationId`, `caseId`, `deviationCode`, `state`, `raisedAt`, `raisedBy`, `contactStop`, `pausedState`, `outcome` and `clearedAt` (null while open), which are the TSD S8 T3.1 columns of `deviation` and nothing else. `ownerRoles` carries, per code of LOV-DEVIATION at the version in force, `deviationCode`, `ownerRole` and `mapped`, the outcome of R-DEV-02 to R-DEV-06 at the package version in force. Errors: 401 no Workbench identity, 403 Case record right R absent (MSG-P4-002) or case outside the scope, 422 `caseId` absent or malformed (MSG-GEN-001), 503 a downstream of steps 4 and 5 is unavailable (MSG-GEN-006). A case with no open deviation answers both arrays, `openDeviations` empty, with 200.

The Ownership Map gives S8 two operations, `POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations` and `PATCH /deviations/{deviationId}` (API-S8-001, API-S8-002), and no read, while the screening run needs the open codes of the case and rwb-agent's contract names this read as its source for them. The read is therefore declared here with a gap and an assumption (GAP-3085; ASM-5252), and the two write operations stay with the Epic 2 stories of this service.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| The agent policy read of RWB-P10-E1062-CON (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3085; ASM-5253)) | `/api/recovery/agent/v1` | P10 rwb-agent | The autonomy mode of policy "SCREENING" at its version in force, for the raise gate; faked |
| The rule-package read in force (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3085; ASM-5254)) | `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | P7 rwb-decision | The DEV route set at its version, for R-DEV-02 to R-DEV-06 and the owner roles; faked, through the kit |
| The parameters read (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3085; ASM-5256)) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The maximum number of deviations one answer carries; faked, cached |
| The reference-data read (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3085; ASM-5257)) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | LOV-DEVIATION and LOV-RAISED-BY at the version in force; faked, cached |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). The four rows are class C dependencies in fact that the plan does not hold, because this story's C row is `RWB-P10-E1062-CON` and its H row is None; the first is the contract of the key and the other three arrive with the platform libraries of DP-04, DP-06 and DP-07 (GAP-3085; ASM-5254).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. In shadow nothing is raised, so this slice writes no outbox row and publishes nothing: `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1` (EV-06) and `rwb.deviation.DeviationCleared.v1` (EV-07) on `rwb.deviation.events.v1` belong to the raise and clear steps of this service (DP-09 as a prohibition; ASM-5258). A gate that refused a raise leaves no event behind, which is the producer-side half of legacy AC1 "no deviation record exists".

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. This story subscribes to no topic, holds no consumer group and writes no inbox row: the estate is read on request, not on an event, and the trigger of the screening run is the agent's own. The inbox table of DP-09 is present in `rwb_deviation` for the consumers other stories of this service add.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The read and the gate are synchronous, in the caller's thread, one hop and 2 s. `DeviationWorkflow` on queue `rwb-deviation` is the service's and belongs to the raise, pause, handling and clear steps; this slice contributes no activity to it and starts no workflow. The agent's own `AgentRunWorkflow` is rwb-agent's on queue `rwb-agent`.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The estate is read on request, the gate runs on the request, and the service owns no job in the ownership rows (Jobs 0). The deviation service level of R-DEV-20 is a workflow timer of the handling step, not a Temporal Schedule of this slice.

| Table | Owner | Use in this story |

| deviation | S8 (`rwb_deviation`) | Read only: the open rows of the case and the family of codes |
| v_open_deviation | S8 (`rwb_deviation`) | Read only view over `deviation`, created by this story's migration for the read of an open estate and its index (DP-15) |
| outbox_event | PLT library, created in `rwb_deviation` | Present for the raise and clear steps; this slice writes none of its rows |
| processed_event | PLT library, created in `rwb_deviation` | Present for the consumers of other stories; this slice writes none of its rows |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_deviation` | Present for the write operations; this slice writes none of its rows |

Not owned and never read as a table: `recovery_case` and `deviation_open` (P3), the `v_ace_*` views and the interaction ledger (P1), `document` and `document_field` (P5), `agent_policy` and the agent run (P10 `rwb_agent`), `rule_row` and `decision_log_entry` (P7). No foreign key leaves `rwb_deviation`; `case_id` and `raised_by` are references, not keys across schemas (DP-01).

| File | None | No file is read, built or delivered here |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.deviation`, module `screening-input`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `DeviationGuard` | Guard | The Case record right of `GET /deviations` from the cached decision of rwb-access, the scope check and the problem mapping of section 14 |
| `OpenDeviationReader` | Repository | Reads the open rows of `deviation` for the case in `rwb_deviation`, with the columns of §11 and no other table |
| `DeviationOwnerProjection` | Service | Reads the codes of LOV-DEVIATION at the version in force, fetches the DEV package at its version, evaluates R-DEV-02 to R-DEV-06 in the embedded kit and pairs each code with its owner role and the "unmapped" marker |
| `ScreeningInputAssembler` | Service | Builds the answer of 12.1: the open estate, the projection, the limit and the absence of personal data |
| `ScreeningRaiseGate` | Service | Reads the autonomy mode of policy "SCREENING" on the rwb-agent contract and refuses a screening raise with 409 while the mode is SHADOW, before the raise path |
| `AgentPolicyClient` | Client | The policy read of RWB-P10-E1062-CON, one hop, 2 s, breaker, cached for the request |
| `RulePackageClient` | Client | The package read of rwb-decision at its version in force, through the kit |
| `ReferenceDataClient`, `ParameterClient` | Client | LOV-DEVIATION, LOV-RAISED-BY and the answer limit, from the rwb-case contracts, cached |

**Database and migrations.** One step in the per-service Flyway sequence of `rwb_deviation` (DP-15): `V1062_1__screening_deviation_read.sql`, which creates the read-only view `v_open_deviation` over `deviation` (the open rows with their code, state, raised date, actor, contact stop, paused state, outcome and cleared date) and one index on the columns the read filters by. No business table, no column and no constraint is added, and no migration of this service touches another schema or the shared baseline. The view name is a design choice fixed by no source document (ASM-5259).

**Configuration and reference data.**

- The codes, the actor values and the owner roles are rows of LOV-DEVIATION, LOV-RAISED-BY and the DEV package at their version in force; none is a constant of the module (DP-07, DP-04).
- The maximum number of deviations one answer carries is a parameter value of rwb-case; its value is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3085; ASM-5256).
- The policy "SCREENING", its version and its autonomy mode are rwb-agent's data and are read on its contract; this service holds no copy of them (DP-20).
- The 2 s budget, the single hop and the breaker are the platform rule of ADR-020, and the flag `rwb.deviation.screening-input` is a flag of the platform library: off means the read answers 404 to every caller and the gate refuses every screening raise with 409, while the estate of the service itself is unchanged.

**Build steps**

1. The view and its index in the service's Flyway sequence, applied on an empty `rwb_deviation` and on a loaded one (AC1, AC2, DP-15).
2. `OpenDeviationReader` with the open-row filter and the columns of §11; unit tests for AC1 and AC2.
3. `DeviationOwnerProjection` over the reference-data and package fakes, with R-DEV-02 to R-DEV-06, "RW-FRAUD" for X4 and the unmapped path; unit tests for AC3 and X4.
4. `ScreeningInputAssembler` and the operation with the guard and the scope check, the empty case and the refusal path; API tests for AC1, AC2, AC5 and X1.
5. `ScreeningRaiseGate` with the agent-policy fake, the 409 path, the not-refused path and the no-answer path; tests for AC4, X5 and X6.
6. The property test that places a synthetic personal value in `handler_user_id` and in a free-text fixture and asserts that it appears in no answer, no log line and no span attribute (BR2).
7. The build check that fails on a code, an actor value, an owner role or the marker in the source, and on any statement outside `rwb_deviation` (BR5, BR1, X7).
8. A contract-fake run of RWB-P10-E1062-CON, the registry, the parameters and the reference data, so the slice proves every criterion before the agent is live in DEV.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-18 | Interaction ledger | Ledger owned by rwb-source-data (default ruling) | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |
| DP-20 | Agent client | rwb-agent contract | C RWB-P10-TE013-CON |

This is a secondary slice: the metadata "Depends on (build)" stays `None` and "Contract dependencies" stays `RWB-P10-E1062-CON` exactly as the Work Package fixes them, so the platform contracts that DP-04, DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-15 and DP-19 name arrive with the service template and are not written into the H row (GAP-3085; ASM-5254).

- **DP-01** keeps the whole answer inside `rwb_deviation`; a statement on `rwb_case` or on a `v_ace_*` view fails the boundary test. **DP-15** puts the view and its index in the per-service Flyway sequence, never in the shared baseline.
- **DP-04** is the owner projection: the DEV package is fetched at its version in force and R-DEV-02 to R-DEV-06 are evaluated in the embedded kit, so no owner role is duplicated in a table of this service (legacy BR3). **DP-07** is the two lists, resolved at the version in force, which is what makes the projection cover exactly the codes in force. **DP-06** is the parameter read of the answer limit; no limit is a constant of the module.
- **DP-09** and **DP-18** apply as prohibitions: the library and the topic exist for the service and in shadow the read publishes nothing because nothing is raised, and the ledger stays rwb-source-data's, so the answer carries no interaction and this service writes no ledger row.
- **DP-13** gives the read its base `/api/recovery/deviation/v1`, and **DP-19** is the route a screen reads the same estate through; the agent reaches the operation through the edge, one hop, and no route calls a service that calls another.
- **DP-20** is the policy read of the gate: this service is a client of the rwb-agent contract for the autonomy mode in force and never embeds the agent runtime; the platform agent contract of DP-20 (`RWB-P10-TE013-CON`) is not in the plan's C row, which holds the contract of this legacy key instead (GAP-3085; ASM-5253).

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, the read answers the estate of `RW-2026-000403` and `RW-2026-000502` on the fakes with their codes and states, the projection names "RW-FRAUD" for X4 and "RW-TEAMMGR" with "unmapped" for a code without a row, a screening raise in shadow is refused with 409 and leaves no row, no event, no contact stop and no clock, an identity without the right is refused with MSG-P4-002, the migration applies cleanly on an empty `rwb_deviation`, and no statement outside the schema exists in the build.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller's identity holds no Case record right R (X1, AC5) | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | The `caseId` query is absent or malformed (X2) | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The package, the reference data or the agent policy does not answer inside the budget (X3, X6) | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| None | A screening raise in shadow (X5, AC4) | No message: no user is in the loop, and the agent receives 409 with the platform error envelope |

The three IDs and their text are those of the legacy and FSD message sets, copied unchanged. For MSG-P4-002, {action} names the action the caller tried — "read the deviations of this case" — and never a case fact. For MSG-GEN-006, {system} is "Rule package", "Reference data" or "Agent policy" on the three paths. Errors are RFC 9457 problem responses with `messageId`, `detail` with the placeholders filled and `instance` naming the request; the HTTP mapping is 403 for MSG-P4-002, 409 on the shadow refusal, 422 for MSG-GEN-001 and 503 for MSG-GEN-006. MSG-P10-002 and MSG-P10-003 (the empty sample and the evaluation already running) are RWB-P10-E1062-APP's and are not restated here.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story. The read is a service-to-service call: the agent's tool gateway calls rwb-deviation, one hop, and no person is in the loop. No screen of the case record, the deviation queue or the review queue changes because of this slice, and the deviation screens of this service belong to its other stories (SCR-06 Raise deviation and SCR-08 Deviation queue).

A screen that shows the same estate reaches it through the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19, which merges the deviation answer of this service with the case state of rwb-case; the route specification and the field-level masking of the composite route belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON. The agent run metadata screen — the runs, their mode, their status and the evaluation scores — is rwb-agent's on `/api/recovery/agent/v1`, and this story serves it nothing.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the codes, the actor values, the owner roles, the "unmapped" marker and the answer limit are rows, parameters or configuration, read with their version. A build check fails on a code, an owner role or the marker in the source.
- No personal data in the answer, an event, a workflow input or a log: identifiers, codes, states, dates, a boolean and a rule version only. `handler_user_id` is not returned, and a property test asserts that a synthetic personal value never reaches the JSON, a log line or a span attribute.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or a `v_ace_*` view: this service holds no `v_ace_*` grant and reads no ACE table, and the answer needs no ACE product at all.
- No cross-schema read and no cross-schema key: `rwb_deviation` holds the row, `case_id` is a reference, and a statement on `rwb_case`, `rwb_agent` or `rwb_decision` fails the boundary test (DP-01).
- The ledger is not this service's: no interaction row is read, written or copied, and no ledger listener of this slice exists (DP-18).
- One event owner per fact: this slice publishes nothing, and a build that writes an outbox row for a shadow run fails the acceptance test (DP-09, BR4).
- One base, one topic, one queue, one schema and one login per service; no document names another service's base or topic as its own (DP-13, DP-14).
- The agent runtime is never embedded and never called back: this service consumes the policy read of RWB-P10-E1062-CON and calls nothing else of rwb-agent (DP-20).
- Any migration is a step in the per-service Flyway sequence of `rwb_deviation`, versioned and repeatable, and touches no other schema (DP-15).
- No retired element is reintroduced: no Quartz row, no shared job table, no monolith base and no data-lake export.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-062 for rwb-document, carrying the masked document and extracted-field read the screening agent makes and the `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` event whose event ID keys one run per case and event. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **rwb-document to serve the documents and their extracted fields of a case to the screening agent, masked, and to publish one DocumentStored event per stored document with a stable event ID**, so that **the agent's shadow run reads the same evidence every time and one run exists per case and event**.

This story is the rwb-document part of legacy RWB-E1-062. The legacy story asks for a deviation screening agent that reads "case data, call notes and documents" and proposes X1 to X7 in shadow (legacy sections 1 and 2), and its flow step 2 consumes "EV-16 DocumentStored for a document on an open case" while step 3 reads "the documents and their fields as SY-AGENT, masks personal fields and calls the model" (legacy section 4). Two of those facts are rwb-document's: the document and field read the agent makes, and the event that starts one run for that document.

Inside `rwb-document` this is the agent input capability of the document service:

- Service `rwb-document`, schema `rwb_document`, REST base `/api/recovery/document/v1`, topic `rwb.document.events.v1` with event names `rwb.document.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document` (Architecture v5 slides 13, 16 and 41).
- The read answers from `document` and `document_field` in `rwb_document` only. The rows are written by the store of RWB-P5-E1024-APP; this story adds no write to them and copies no row of another service (DP-01).
- The event is `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` on `rwb.document.events.v1`, written to the outbox in the same transaction as the `document` row, keyed by caseId, and carrying references and codes only (DP-09; Architecture v5 slides 16, 20 and 42).
- The agent is never called by this service. It is the caller of the read and the consumer of the event, which is why the only contract dependency of the story is RWB-P10-E1062-CON.

The rest of legacy RWB-E1-062 is owned elsewhere and is not answered here:

- The agent runtime, the policy "SCREENING" version "P1", the prompt "PR1", the output schema "screening-v1", the guardrail checks, the owner-role resolution from R-DEV-02 to R-DEV-06, the evaluation on sample "SCREEN-S1" and the run states are rwb-agent's, in RWB-P10-E1062-APP against the contract RWB-P10-E1062-CON. Legacy AC1 to AC9 belong there.
- The deviation itself — registration, pause, handling and return — is rwb-deviation's, in RWB-S8-E1062-APP.

What remains here is the input the model is given and the fact that announces it: the documents of a case, their extracted fields with a confidence, the masking of every personal value before the answer leaves the service, and one event per stored document whose event ID and idempotency key never change, so that the agent's run key "SCREENING:<caseId>:<eventId>" is stable.

##### 2. Business rationale

A dispute, a death, a fraud sign or a lost contact found late means contact that should have stopped, or a case worked on the wrong route. The screening agent reads the case, the interaction ledger and the documents at entry and again when a document arrives, and proposes deviations with reasons (legacy section 2). In Epic 1 the proposals are stored only and scored against the business analysts' review, and shown to nobody. None of that can be measured unless the agent reads the same document estate the officers read, and unless every new document announces itself once with an identity the agent can key on.

rwb-document is the system of record for those documents (FSD P5 A2.19, DT06), indexes them by case, type, date and extracted field (A2.2, FEAT-DCM-02), writes each extracted field with its confidence (A2.9, FEAT-DCM-09) and keeps every version with its date and source (A2.20, FEAT-DCM-20). The three read operations of this slice are the published form of that index: API-P5-002 lists the documents of a case, API-P5-003 reads one document's metadata, versions and extracted fields, and API-P5-009 searches the index in the caller's scope with an extracted-field filter. The event of this slice is EV-16 DocumentStored, which lists rwb-agent as one of its consumers (Architecture v5 slide 42).

Four target facts shape this slice:

1. **One identity, one answer.** The agent reads as the service identity SY-AGENT, which holds Documents right R in the document hub RBAC matrix (TSD P5 T6.1: "SY-AGENT Agent platform | R"). The authorisation decision is rwb-access's and is consumed as the cached permission of the service (DP-08); a read by an identity without the right is refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002 before any row is touched. Masking applies to every field the policy of the version in force marks personal, so the agent's input carries references, codes and confidences and no clear personal value (CTL-11, DL26).
2. **One hop, two seconds.** The read is a synchronous call on the caller's thread, one hop, with a 2 s budget and a breaker per downstream (Architecture v5 slide 10 and slide 11). The gateway-bff composite route of DP-19 is what a screen would use; for the agent the hop is its tool gateway, which calls this service directly and never chains.
3. **One event, one row.** The store of RWB-P5-E1024-APP writes the outbox row inside the transaction that writes the `document` row, and the relay publishes it on `rwb.document.events.v1` once per committed row, so the event exists exactly when the document exists (FSD P5 A2.1 and A2.2: "DocumentStored is written to the outbox with the document ID, the case ID, the type and the source"; DP-09; Architecture v5 slide 20 and the slide 42 note).
4. **One run per case and event.** The agent keys its run on the event ID, with the run key "SCREENING:<caseId>:<eventId>" of legacy AC3 and BR7 (R-UNI-40). That key is only stable if the event ID and the idempotency key of a redelivery are the same, which is what this slice guarantees on the producer side.

The slice therefore answers REQ-DVH-001 for the document part of its detection sources, and supports REQ-DVH-003 and REQ-DVH-007 with the document and interaction references the agent's proposal quotes (legacy section 18). It changes no business rule of the document hub and no rule of the agent.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The `rwb_document` baseline is in place: `document`, `document_field` and `document_type` exist at the platform migration version, and the outbox, inbox and idempotency tables of DP-09 are created in the schema by the event library.
- RWB-P5-E1024-APP is done: the store writes `document` and `document_field`, sets `doc_version`, `content_sha256`, `stored` state COPY_PENDING then STORED, and writes the `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` outbox row in the store transaction.
- RWB-P10-E1062-CON is published: the rwb-agent contract of this legacy key, which fixes the run key "SCREENING:<caseId>:<eventId>", the tool call the agent makes to read documents and fields, and the event header fields the agent reads. The field names of that contract are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1047; ASM-1995), and the story builds against its fake.
- The authorisation and masking decision is served by rwb-access (DP-08, H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON and C RWB-P4-E1037-CON, which arrive with the baseline). The mask format and the list of fields the policy marks personal for SY-AGENT are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1049; ASM-1997).
- The document type table is loaded at a version in force in `rwb_document.document_type`, with the six Epic 1 types and their field definitions (RWB-P5-E1025-APP); the version in force is resolved through the reference-data route of rwb-case (DP-07, C RWB-P3-E1043-CON). The type "DEATH_CERTIFICATE" used in the criteria is a stored row of that table version.
- LOV-DOC-SOURCE holds "SCAN", "UPLOAD", "GENERATED", "PARTNER" and "EMAIL", and LOV-DOC-TYPE holds the type codes of the version in force (TSD P5 T3.2), read through the reference-data contract and never typed in code.
- The case "RW-2026-000401" and its open state are rwb-case's; this story reads no case row and needs only the case ID carried on the document row and in the event.
- The service identity SY-AGENT exists in the identity provider and holds Documents right R; SY-OCR holds CRU and stores through RWB-P5-E1049-APP, and neither identity is shared with another purpose.
- The page size and the read timeout of the list operations are configuration values resolved through the parameters contract and client library of rwb-case (DP-06, H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and C RWB-P3-E1042-CON); no page size and no timeout is written in code.
- The relay of `rwb.document.events.v1` is running with its retry topics and its dead-letter topic, as the platform event library provides them (DP-09, H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON).

##### 4. Flow

1. SY-OCR or the intake path of RWB-P5-E1049-APP stores a document on an open case through the store of RWB-P5-E1024-APP, with its case ID, type, source, file hash and extracted fields.
2. The store commits one transaction in `rwb_document`: the `document` row with `doc_version` and state COPY_PENDING, the `document_field` rows with `field_name`, `field_value`, `confidence` and `extractor_version`, and the `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` outbox row. Nothing is committed if any of the three fails (DP-09).
3. The relay of `rwb.document.events.v1` publishes the outbox row in CloudEvents 1.0 binary mode, keyed by caseId, with the event ID, the idempotency key, schema version 1, the occurred time and the actor "SY-OCR"; the event carries documentId, caseId, documentType, source and storedAt and no personal value.
4. rwb-agent consumes the event, derives the run key "SCREENING:<caseId>:<eventId>" and starts one shadow run for that case and event; a redelivery of the same event carries the same event ID and the same idempotency key, so no second run is keyed and the repeat is counted (R-UNI-40).
5. The agent's tool gateway calls `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents` with the identity of SY-AGENT to list the documents of the case, or `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}` to read one document with its versions and extracted fields, or `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents` with an extracted-field filter when the screening question is field-driven.
6. `AgentDocumentReader` authorises the call through the cached decision of rwb-access (DP-08, Documents right R, scope applied) and refuses with 403 and MSG-P4-002 before reading a row when the right is absent.
7. `AgentDocumentReader` reads the rows of `rwb_document` only: the document with id, case, type, source, stored date and `doc_version`, the type row at the version in force, and the extracted fields with their name, value, confidence and extractor version.
8. `DocumentFieldMasker` masks every field the masking policy marks personal before the answer is built, and the answer carries the masked value only; no clear value of a masked field is serialised, logged or put in a trace.
9. `rwb-document` answers the caller inside the 2 s budget, one hop, with no call to another service on the read path.
10. When the read is repeated for the same document and the same case, the same evidence is returned: the masking is deterministic on the policy version, the type is resolved at the version in force, and the version returned is the stored one, so the agent's input does not drift between two runs of the same event.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The caller's identity holds no Documents right R | Refused by the guard before any row is read; nothing is returned | MSG-P4-002 | AC5 |
| X2 | The case ID on the request names no document and no case in the caller's scope | The list is empty, or the single read answers 404; nothing else changes | None | AC1 |
| X3 | A field the policy marks personal is read | The value is masked in the answer; the clear value never leaves the service | None | AC1 |
| X4 | The outbox write fails inside the store transaction | The `document` row, the `document_field` rows and the event are all rolled back; the store answers 503 with MSG-P7-003 through its decision record | MSG-P7-003 | AC3 |
| X5 | The relay cannot publish a committed outbox row | The event stays in the outbox and is published when the relay recovers, once, with the same event ID | None | AC3, AC4 |
| X6 | The same event is delivered twice to the agent | The event ID and the idempotency key are the same, so the run key is the same; the repeat is counted (R-UNI-40) | None | AC4 |
| X7 | The stored type of a document has left the version in force | The document is served with the type stored on its row and is never re-typed by this story | None | AC6 |
| X8 | The reference-data read of the type version does not answer | The read answers 503 with MSG-GEN-006 naming "Reference data" and returns no document | MSG-GEN-006 | AC6 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Answers from `rwb_document` only, builds against the rwb-agent contract fake RWB-P10-E1062-CON, the authorisation and masking decision of rwb-access and the reference-data route of rwb-case; no build dependency of its own |
| Negotiable | The type, the field list, the mask policy version, the page size and the timeout are rows, parameters or configuration; the story fixes only the behaviour |
| Valuable | The screening agent reads the same masked evidence on every run, and the event that starts a run has one stable identity |
| Estimable | One module, three operations already on the P5 contract, one event already on the P5 topic, one masker and one stability guard |
| Small | Fits one sprint as a secondary slice of the legacy key, with the store of RWB-P5-E1024-APP already in place |
| Testable | Every criterion in section 7 is one automated test over synthetic documents, with every cross-service answer stubbed |

The seven criteria above are new and test only this slice: the masked document and extracted-field read the screening agent makes, and the one event per stored document with its stable identity. The legacy criteria AC1 to AC9 of RWB-E1-062 are owned by RWB-P10-E1062-APP (the shadow run, the shadow flags, the precision and recall, the owner role, the preceding contact, the review marker, the repeated event on the run side, the code outside the list and the timeout) and by RWB-S8-E1062-APP (raising, pausing and handling the deviation). No legacy criterion text is copied into this section, and this story owns no legacy AC.

The cross-service facts are read from the contract mocks named in the Background: the rwb-agent contract of RWB-P10-E1062-CON returns the run key and the tool call, the rwb-access contract returns the authorisation and masking decision, and the rwb-case reference-data contract returns the type version in force. The idempotency-key format of `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` and the event field names the agent's contract expects are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1048; ASM-1996); the payload names used above are the ones the FSD P5 A2.1, A2.2 and A2.19 fix in prose (the document ID, the case ID, the type and the source) and the stored date of the row.

The read behaviour of a document whose stored type has left the version in force is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1050; ASM-1998): the FSD P5 A2.1, A2.2 and A2.19 fix only the refusal of an unknown type at store time, with 422 and MSG-P5-006, and say nothing of a document already stored. AC6 keeps the type stored on the row, serves the document, and leaves both the refusal path and any re-typing to the store stories of P5.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every read is authorised with the caller's own identity, and every field the masking policy marks personal is masked before the answer leaves the service; no clear personal value is returned, logged or traced | CTL-11; DL26; FSD P5 A2.6 AC-ALT-P5-006-01; TSD P5 T6.2 |
| BR2 | In the document sense, a read carries codes, references and a confidence and no clear personal value: the document ID, the case ID, the type code, the source code, the stored date, `doc_version` and per field the name, the masked value and the confidence (legacy BR2) | FSD P5 A2.9 AC-P5-009-01; legacy BR2 |
| BR3 | The event payload carries references and codes only — document ID, case ID, type, source and stored date — and never a personal value, an extracted field value or a document's text | Architecture v5 slide 42 note; FSD P5 A2.1, A2.2, A2.19; legacy section 8 BR7 |
| BR4 | One `DocumentStored` event per `document` row, written to the outbox in the same transaction as the row, and never a second event for the same row, also when the store is retried (legacy BR7 on the producer side) | R-UNI-40; DP-09; FSD P5 A2.2 AC-P5-002-01; legacy BR7 |
| BR5 | The event ID and the idempotency key of one stored document never change across a redelivery, so the agent's run key "SCREENING:<caseId>:<eventId>" is stable and the repeat is counted (R-UNI-40) | Legacy AC3, AC7, BR7; R-UNI-40 |
| BR6 | The type and its field list are read from the type table at the version in force; no type code, field name, mask value or page size is written in code | FSD P5 A2.3 BR-P5-003; TSD P5 T3.1, T3.2; DP-07 |
| BR7 | rwb-document evaluates no rule for this story: no decision table, no DRL, no workbook and no rule package is loaded to serve the agent its input (DP-04 as a prohibition) | DP-04; Architecture v5 slide 16 |
| BR8 | rwb-document stores no agent output, no agent run and no deviation: the proposal, the guardrail result and the run state are rwb-agent's rows, and the ledger is rwb-source-data's (DP-18 and DP-20 as prohibitions) | DP-18, DP-20; Architecture v5 slides 13 and 16 |

The rules hold in `rwb_document` as follows. BR1 is executed by the guard of the service template holding the cached decision of rwb-access and by `DocumentFieldMasker` on the answer path; the access log entry for a read is written by the ACE common module, not by this package. BR2 and BR3 are property tests over the serialised answer and over the event payload: a synthetic personal value placed in a masked field must not appear in the JSON, in the log or in the span attributes. BR4 is executed by the outbox row being written inside the store transaction of RWB-P5-E1024-APP and by the relay publishing per outbox row, so a rolled-back store leaves no event and a retried store finds the existing document and writes no second row. BR5 is executed by `EventIdStabilityGuard`, which takes the event ID from the outbox row and derives the idempotency key from it, so a redelivery of the same row carries the same pair. BR6 is executed by reading `document_type` at the version the reference-data route reports in force, and by a build check that fails on a type code or a field name in the source. BR7 and BR8 are prohibitions checked by the same build: no Drools dependency in the module, no write to an agent, deviation or ledger table, and no outbound call to rwb-agent.

##### 9. State transitions

None for the case. This story changes no case status, raises no deviation and creates no agent run. Two lifecycles are read or written here, and both belong to other parts of the service:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| (no row) | the store of RWB-P5-E1024-APP commits | The document row, its fields and the outbox row are written in one transaction | `document.state` = COPY_PENDING, and the outbox row exists |
| COPY_PENDING | the copy to the container succeeds | The file is stored and `storage_ref` is set | STORED (read only in this story; written by RWB-P5-E1024-APP) |
| outbox row written | the relay picks the row | The relay is running and the topic accepts the record | relayed: the event is on `rwb.document.events.v1` with its event ID and idempotency key |
| relayed | the agent's consumer records the event in its inbox | The event is new to that consumer | delivered at most once to the handler; a redelivery of the same event ID is counted and discarded (R-UNI-40) |

The agent run states — PENDING, RUNNING, TIMED_OUT, GUARDRAIL_FAILED, COMPLETED and the review marker of a low-confidence proposal — are rwb-agent's rows and rwb-agent's transitions (RWB-P10-E1062-APP), and no state of them is written here. The document lifecycle beyond COPY_PENDING and STORED, including retention and custody, belongs to the store, retention and custody stories of P5.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| SY-AGENT, agent platform | Reads documents, their versions and their extracted fields with Documents right R, masked, inside the scope the decision grants (TSD P5 T6.1) |
| SY-OCR, OCR and extraction pipeline | Stores documents with Documents right CRU; the store itself is RWB-P5-E1049-APP and RWB-P5-E1024-APP, and this story reads the rows it writes |
| rwb-document service identity (the rwb-document login, DP-02) | Serves the three read operations and writes the outbox row inside the store transaction; reads `document`, `document_field` and `document_type` in `rwb_document` only |
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Reads run metadata only; the run metadata screen is rwb-agent's, and this story serves it no document content of its own |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Platform administration right R: reads the service's operational views, no document content |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Platform administration right R: reads the access entries of the document estate written by the ACE common module |

The authorisation decision is not taken here. It comes from rwb-access, which owns Recovery roles as data, scope and masking policy (Architecture v5 slide 41), consumed as the cached permission of the service (DP-08); the refusal shape is 403 with MSG-P4-002, and a case outside the caller's scope is refused with MSG-P4-003. Each read uses the caller's own identity: the agent's tool gateway presents SY-AGENT, and no shared identity exists for the agent's reads.

The legacy access case TC-E1-062-10 (a role without the right is refused with MSG-P4-002) is answered here only for the document read of AC5. The rest of that legacy case — RW-CASEOWN calling the agent evaluation read — belongs to RWB-P10-E1062-APP, because the evaluation is the agent's.

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary and the TSD P5 T3.1 table. The outbox row of the event is written by RWB-P5-E1024-APP inside its store transaction; this story owns the event's shape and its stability, and 12.3 fixes what it carries.

Nothing else is read or written here. The case, the interaction ledger, the type version and the rules arrive only through contracts: the case ID arrives on the document row and in the event, the ledger entries are rwb-source-data's and rwb-agent reads them itself, the type version comes from the reference-data route of rwb-case (DP-07), and no rule row is read at all (DP-04 as a prohibition). No `v_ace_*` view and no `public` table is read by this story, and no row of another service's schema is copied (DP-01).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

The three operations of the document hub contract on base `/api/recovery/document/v1`, owner rwb-document (P5). This story adds no path, no query parameter and no response field; it answers these three for the agent, masked, under the caller's identity.

| ID | Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| API-P5-002 | GET | `/cases/{caseId}/documents` | List the documents on a case | Documents right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| API-P5-003 | GET | `/documents/{documentId}` | Read a document's metadata, versions and extracted fields | Documents right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| API-P5-009 | GET | `/documents` | Search active documents across the cases in the caller's scope by type, stored date, extracted field and free text | Documents right R, scope applied; each search written to the access log | Not applicable |

**API-P5-002.** Request: query `type`, `page`, `size`. Response: DocumentPage — the documents of the case with id, caseId, documentType, source, stored date, docVersion, retentionClass and writeOnce, and for each document its extracted fields with name, masked value, confidence and extractorVersion. Errors: 401 no Workbench identity, 403 Documents right R absent (MSG-P4-002) or case outside the scope (MSG-P4-003), 404 no such case, 503 the reference data or the store is unavailable (MSG-GEN-006).

**API-P5-003.** Request: none. Response: Document — the metadata of API-P5-002 for one document, its version list (docVersion, stored date, source, previousVersionId) and its extracted fields. Errors: 401, 403 (MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003), 404 no such document, 503 (MSG-GEN-006).

**API-P5-009.** Request: query `type`, `dateFrom`, `dateTo`, `field`, `op`, `value`, `value2`, `q`, `page`, `size`. Response: DocumentSearchPage — the matching documents with case number, type, stored date and the matched field value (masked), inside the caller's scope. Errors: 401, 403 (MSG-P4-002), 422 a criterion outside its list or an empty criterion set (MSG-GEN-001), 503 (MSG-GEN-006). The access-log entry of each search is written by the ACE common module.

The operation the agent's own contract names as its tool call is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1047; ASM-1995): whether the agent reads through one operation per document or one per case, and the field names of that call, are fixed by RWB-P10-E1062-CON, and this story serves it through the three operations above. Its responses are the TSD P5 T-A.2 shapes named here; no new shape is introduced.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None at run time. This story calls no other service on the read path and no other service on the event path: the answer is built from `rwb_document`, and the event is written to the outbox and published by the relay, not by a call.

Two contracts are consumed as shapes and fixtures:

| Contract | What is consumed | Note |
|---|---|---|
| RWB-P10-E1062-CON | The run key "SCREENING:<caseId>:<eventId>", the agent's tool call and the event header fields the agent reads | The agent is the caller of 12.1 and the consumer of 12.3; the contract fixes the shape this service must satisfy. Its field names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1047; ASM-1995) and its idempotency-key expectation is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1048; ASM-1996) |
| DP-07 reference data of rwb-case (C RWB-P3-E1043-CON) | The document type version in force and the two lists LOV-DOC-TYPE and LOV-DOC-SOURCE | Read through the reference-data client library; no list value is copied into `rwb_document` |

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Key | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` (EV-16) | `rwb.document.events.v1` | caseId | documentId, caseId, documentType, source, storedAt |

CloudEvents 1.0 envelope in binary mode, with the event ID, the idempotency key, the schema version 1, the occurred time, the actor "SY-OCR" and the source of the event; no personal data and no extracted field value in the envelope or the payload. rwb-agent and rwb-case are the consumers (Architecture v5 slide 42, event 16). The event is written to the outbox in the store transaction of RWB-P5-E1024-APP, so it exists exactly when the `document` row exists, and the relay publishes it once per outbox row, with the retry topics and the dead-letter topic of the platform event library.

The idempotency key is the event's own identity in this slice: the key is derived from the outbox row's event ID, so a redelivery of the same row carries the same pair. The exact idempotency-key format the rwb-agent contract expects is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1048; ASM-1996). `rwb.document.DocumentFieldsExtracted.v1` is on the same topic but is published by the extraction path of RWB-P5-E1053-APP, not by this story.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. This service is the producer of the event that starts the agent's run, not a consumer of it: the agent triggers on the event it receives, and this story subscribes to no topic, holds no consumer group and writes no inbox row. The inbox table of DP-09 is present in `rwb_document` for the consumers that other P5 stories add, and this story writes none of its rows.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The read is a synchronous REST call in the caller's thread, one hop, inside the 2 s budget. `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` and its activities belong to RWB-P5-E1049-APP, and the agent's `AgentRunWorkflow` is rwb-agent's on queue `rwb-agent` (Architecture v5 slide 16); this story starts neither and contributes no activity.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The 15-minute document intake Schedule (legacy JOB-12) belongs to RWB-P5-E1049-APP and the retention Schedule to the retention story; this slice adds no Schedule and no timer.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|
| `document` | P5 (`rwb_document`) | Read only: the metadata of the answer and the row the event announces |
| `document_field` | P5 (`rwb_document`) | Read only: the extracted fields with their confidence, masked in the answer |
| `document_type` | P5 (`rwb_document`) | Read only: the type row at the version in force, for the code and the field list (loaded by RWB-P5-E1025-APP) |
| `outbox_event` | PLT library, created in `rwb_document` | The `DocumentStored` row, written by the store of RWB-P5-E1024-APP in its transaction and published by the relay (DP-09) |
| `processed_event` | PLT library, created in `rwb_document` | Present for the consumers of other P5 stories; not written by this story |
| `idempotency_key` | PLT library, created in `rwb_document` | The store's request key; read by this story only to assert that a retried store writes one row and one event |

rwb-document reads no table of another service and holds no foreign key across services (DP-01). The case is not copied: its ID arrives on the document row and in the event. The type version, the lists and the page size arrive through the contracts of 12.2.

| rwb-access authorise and masking fake (RWB-P4-E1037-CON) | DP-08 | A granted decision for SY-AGENT with Documents right R, a refused decision for an identity without it, and a masking decision that marks two fields of "DEATH_CERTIFICATE" personal |
| rwb-case reference-data fake (RWB-P3-E1043-CON) | DP-07 | The document type version in force with "DEATH_CERTIFICATE" and its field list, LOV-DOC-TYPE and LOV-DOC-SOURCE, and a version in force in which one stored type is absent (AC6) |

| Kafka | 1 event published, 0 consumed | `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` on `rwb.document.events.v1`, keyed by caseId, through the outbox and the relay; no consumer group in this story |
