**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-065 for rwb-source-data. The sandbox becomes a build tool of this service rather than a step of a monolith pipeline: `tools/sandbox-generator` in package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.sourcedata.sandbox`, a separate build module that is never packaged into the service, creates `rwb_sandbox` on the one ACE PostgreSQL server with schema `public` as the ACE test double, schema `recovery` holding the 30 read-only views and schema `rwb_source_data` holding this service's own tables and the four extension tables (DP-01, DP-02, DP-05; Architecture v5 slides 8, 15, 29 and 41). The nine legacy acceptance criteria are copied here word for word and the generator, verifier, export tool and pipeline stage move with them; the login, the grants and the extension tables are RWB-P1-E1065-DB, the contract baseline is RWB-P1-E1065-CON. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **recovery developer (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **a sandbox build tool of rwb-source-data that stands up `rwb_sandbox` on the one ACE PostgreSQL server from the same DDL as SIT, with schema `public` as the ACE test double, schema `recovery` holding the 30 read-only `v_ace_*` views and schema `rwb_source_data` holding this service's own tables and the four extension tables, all filled with synthetic rows**, so that **I can build and test every read before the ACE interfaces are available and without production data, in DEV only and with no second copy of source data**.

This is the application slice of legacy RWB-E1-065, and it owns all nine legacy acceptance criteria. It delivers:

- `tools/sandbox-generator`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.sourcedata.sandbox`, a separate build module that is never packaged into the service artefact;
- `AceSchemaLoader`, `SandboxGenerator`, `ValueFactory`, `ExceptionShapeBuilder`, `SandboxVerifier`, `AccessSeedLoader` and `SandboxExport`, and the sandbox build stage that runs them (DP-15);
- the seed profile as data: seed 20261128, 1,226 Mortgage, 1,296 Hire purchase and 290 SSME cases, 10 cases per exception shape, every value overridable;
- the dictionary-driven fill, so that a schema change reaches the sandbox with no generator change (DP-01, DP-15);
- the lists of values read through the rwb-case reference-data contract (DP-07), and the embedded Drools kit that evaluates the seeded rule packages in the sandbox smoke check (DP-04).

It does not create the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views, which are RWB-P1-E1069-APP's; it does not create the `rwb_source_data` login, the grants or the read-only role `rwb_sandbox_read`, which are RWB-P1-E1065-DB's (external dependency X), nor the four extension tables, which are RWB-P1-E1069-DB's; and it writes no table of another service (DP-01). It asserts the views, the tables and the grants those two stories deliver and re-creates none of them.

##### 2. Business rationale

SIT reads the real ACE database; DEV has none. Without an ACE-shaped schema the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views cannot compile, so no squad can test a source read, the case list, a notice or a report before SIT is connected. Since the realignment, that schema has to stand up inside a single service: rwb-source-data is the one service that holds the views and the ACE read path (Architecture v5 slides 8, 15 and 41), so the sandbox belongs to rwb-source-data and serves the other 18 services through the read contract rather than through a shared database object they each read.

The sandbox applies the ACE schema for the Tier 1 tables, the RWB-ACE-001 DDL for the 14 Tier 2 tables as a fixture, the per-service Flyway baseline and view migrations for this service's tables and the 30 views, and it fills the ACE-shaped tables with synthetic source rows and the service's own tables with synthetic cases across Mortgage, Hire Purchase and SSME, plus the exception shapes the rules must handle (DP-01, DP-02, DP-15).

There is no copy and no load table: `loan_account`, `account_payment`, `party`, `contact_point`, `collateral`, `account_collateral`, `collections_history`, `party_product`, `valuation`, `score`, `asset`, `load_run`, `dq_exception`, `dq_rule`, `source_field_map`, `source_code_map`, `interface_run`, `interface_signoff`, `tracker_inventory` and `tracker_row` do not exist. The generator reads the data dictionary, so a schema change reaches the sandbox with no manual rebuild, and the verifier allows a clear identity number only in the ACE-shaped tables, where ACE itself holds it; schema `recovery` and schema `rwb_source_data` see `id_no_masked` and `id_no_last4` only. Serves REQ-RDF-001 (the 14 data products with one system of record and one owner) and REQ-RDF-010 (no personal data outside its permitted use).

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P1-E1001-APP is done: the per-service Flyway baseline creates this service's 13 tables, `data_product`, the 122 `sys_objects` rows, the 1,366 `sys_fields` rows and the four extension tables on rwb-source-data's own sequence (legacy RWB-E1-001 in the target; DP-15).
- RWB-P1-E1069-APP is done: the per-service sequence holds the two view migrations that create the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views, their three helper functions and their dictionary rows, and the `ViewConformanceTest` that compares them with the dictionary.
- The ACE schema DDL `15 ACE DB Alignment/ACE Schema PostgreSQL v1.sql` is in the repository. It holds the Tier 1 tables, among them `account`, `payment`, `customer`, `efs_action` and `iam_user`.
- The RWB-ACE-001 DDL for the 14 Tier 2 tables is available in DEV as a fixture (DL43); until it lands, the 14 Section B views and the features that read them stay behind their flags.
- The one ACE PostgreSQL server is reachable from the pipeline, and the DEV instance holds the database `rwb_sandbox`, or the stage creates it as `rwb_sandbox_next` and renames it (RWB-P1-E1065-DB; Architecture v5 slides 8, 9 and 29).
- The read-only database role `rwb_sandbox_read` is delivered by RWB-P1-E1065-DB, and the Entra ID group RWB-DEV-RW-TRIBE maps to it.
- The role to permission matrix rows (roles.txt, Permissions) are available as a seed file for the sandbox.
- A consuming service, starting with rwb-case, can be deployed in DEV against the sandbox database through the rwb-source-data read contract; this story neither deploys it nor changes it.
- RWB-P3-E1043-CON is published with its client library, so a list of values is read as data and never as a constant (DP-07).
- RWB-P1-E1065-CON is published, so the stage contract, the seed profile and the failure contract are fixed before the generator is written.
- Whether the 19-service target keeps one sandbox database per service or one shared sandbox across the 19 services, and where the generator's build module sits relative to the service artefact, are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0501; ASM-0693). This story is read as one DEV sandbox database per service release, `rwb_sandbox` for rwb-source-data, with the generator as a separate build module of the rwb-source-data repository that the service artefact does not contain.

##### 4. Flow

1. Pipeline: on a merge to main that changes the ACE schema DDL, a file under the rwb-source-data migration folder, the dictionary or the seed profile, or on a manual start, runs the sandbox build stage in DEV.
2. Pipeline: creates the database `rwb_sandbox_next` and its three empty schemas, `public`, `recovery` and `rwb_source_data` (RWB-P1-E1065-DB).
3. Pipeline: applies `ACE Schema PostgreSQL v1.sql` (the Tier 1 tables) and the RWB-ACE-001 DDL fixture (the 14 Tier 2 tables) into schema `public`, then the per-service Flyway baseline (this service's 13 tables, the four extension tables and the dictionary) and the two view migrations of RWB-P1-E1069-APP into schema `recovery` (DP-15; RWB-PLT-E1044-CON).
4. SandboxGenerator: reads `sys_objects`, `sys_fields` and the lists of values to learn every table, column, type and list, and reads every list of values through the rwb-case reference-data contract rather than from a constant (DP-07).
5. SandboxGenerator: seeds the Tier 1 and Tier 2 ACE-shaped tables with synthetic rows, including one `ace_batch_run` row per source and business date.
6. SandboxGenerator: creates synthetic cases with seed 20261128: 1,226 Mortgage, 1,296 Hire purchase and 290 SSME (10 percent of the 30 June 2026 inventory; DL15), with their accounts, parties, contact points, collateral, valuations, payments and interactions, linked by business key to the ACE-shaped rows.
7. SandboxGenerator: adds 10 cases for each exception shape in section 8, BR4.
8. SandboxGenerator: seeds the role and permission rows and one synthetic test user reference per role; the roles themselves are reference data of rwb-case (DP-07).
9. SandboxVerifier: checks that the 30 views compile and each returns a row, that every seeded table has rows, that every list-backed column holds list values, that every foreign key resolves, that no clear personal value sits outside schema `public`, and that the boundary accounts exist.
10. Smoke check: the embedded Drools kit evaluates the seeded rule packages against the generated cases and records one decision record per evaluation through the decision-record library (DP-03, DP-04).
11. Pipeline: renames `rwb_sandbox_next` to `rwb_sandbox` under the advisory lock, applies the grants of RWB-P1-E1065-DB, and publishes the build result with the row count per table.
12. Developer or analyst: queries the sandbox with SQL or the export script, or calls the DEV service, without a request to another team.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A table column has no `sys_fields` row | Build fails naming the table and column; previous sandbox kept | None (pipeline result) | AC4 |
| X2 | The reset runs twice for the same commit and seed | The schemas are dropped and recreated; the same seed gives the same rows and counts | None | AC5 |
| X3 | A generated value breaks a constraint | Build fails naming the table and constraint; previous sandbox kept | None (pipeline result) | AC6 |
| X4 | A generated value outside schema `public` matches a personal data pattern | Build fails naming the table and column | None (pipeline result) | AC7 |
| X5 | Accounts sit at the 90 days past due boundary | Accounts at 89 and at 90 days past due are both generated | None | AC8 |
| X6 | A second build starts while one runs | The second build waits on the PostgreSQL advisory lock and runs after the first | None | AC9 |
| X7 | The RWB-ACE-001 DDL fixture is not yet available in DEV | The build stops before the Section B view migration; the Section A views and the service's own tables are still built and published | None (pipeline result) | AC1 |
| X8 | The reference-data read of rwb-case does not answer | The build fails closed before any row is written, names the missing list and keeps the previous sandbox | None (pipeline result) | AC6, section 12.2 |
| X9 | The verifier finds a table, view or grant that RWB-P1-E1065-DB or RWB-P1-E1069-APP delivers and the sandbox does not hold | The build fails on the delivered-objects check and publishes nothing, because the sandbox asserts those objects and never re-creates them | None (pipeline result) | AC1 |

X1 to X7 are the exception paths of RWB-E1-065 carried onto the split; X8 and X9 are the two paths the target adds, one for the reference-data contract and one for the two stories that deliver the views, the grants and the extension tables.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the baseline and the view migrations of two sibling stories and, for Section B, the Tier 2 DDL fixture; it publishes the environment every squad tests in |
| Negotiable | Volumes, seed and exception shapes are properties; the story fixes the generator, the checks and the access |
| Valuable | Every squad builds and tests every view read from the first day with no production data |
| Estimable | One generator tool, one verifier, one pipeline stage, one read-only role |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests, as the primary slice of the legacy key |
| Testable | Each criterion is a pipeline test or a query against the built sandbox |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Sandbox database with synthetic recovery data

  Background:
    Given the sandbox build uses seed 20261128
    Given volumes of 1,226 Mortgage, 1,296 Hire purchase and 290 SSME cases

  Scenario: AC1 The sandbox exists (legacy RWB-E1-065 AC1)
    Given the ACE schema DDL with 22 Tier 1 tables, the RWB-ACE-001 DDL with 14 Tier 2 tables, V0001, V0002 and V0003
    When the sandbox is provisioned
    Then schema public holds the ACE schema, including the 22 Tier 1 tables and the 14 Tier 2 tables
    Then schema recovery holds 92 tables, including party_ext, contact_point_ext, account_ext and valuation_ext
    Then schema recovery holds 30 v_ace_* views and 30 of 30 compile
    Then each of the 30 views returns at least one row
    Then the dictionary holds 122 objects and 1,366 fields
    Then the sandbox holds 2,812 synthetic cases plus 10 cases for each exception shape, across Mortgage, Hire Purchase and SSME
    Then case "RW-2026-000001" has its accounts, parties, interactions and documents linked
    Then none of the 20 tables that left the schema exists in schema recovery: loan_account, account_payment, party, contact_point, collateral, account_collateral, collections_history, party_product, valuation, score, asset, load_run, dq_exception, dq_rule, source_field_map, source_code_map, interface_run, interface_signoff, tracker_inventory and tracker_row

    Then the result shows MORTGAGE, HIRE_PURCHASE and SSME with their counts

    Then the system refuses an UPDATE by the same database role

  Scenario: AC3 It scales with the schema (legacy RWB-E1-065 AC3)

    When it is applied

  Scenario: AC4 A column with no dictionary entry (legacy RWB-E1-065 AC4)

    When the sandbox build runs

  Scenario: AC5 The reset is idempotent (legacy RWB-E1-065 AC5)

    When the build runs again for commit "a1b2c3d" and seed 20261128
    Then a fresh schema public and a fresh schema recovery are built in rwb_sandbox_next and swapped in

  Scenario: AC6 A generated value breaks a constraint (legacy RWB-E1-065 AC6)

    Then the previous sandbox stays in use

  Scenario: AC7 No clear personal value outside the ACE tables (legacy RWB-E1-065 AC7)

    Then the build fails naming recovery.document_field.extracted_value

  Scenario: AC8 Accounts at the entry boundary (legacy RWB-E1-065 AC8)
    Given the exception shapes include the entry boundary
    When the sandbox is provisioned
    Then 10 accounts in v_ace_account have days_past_due 89 and no case
    Then 10 accounts in v_ace_account have days_past_due 90 and one open case each

  Scenario: AC9 Two builds at once (legacy RWB-E1-065 AC9)
    Given a sandbox build is running for commit "a1b2c3d"

```

**Target reading.** Every assertion above keeps its legacy wording; what changes is where it runs and who delivers the objects. The sandbox becomes a build tool of rwb-source-data: `tools/sandbox-generator`, package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.sourcedata.sandbox`, a separate build module that is never packaged into the service artefact, because a build tool must not read or write another service's tables at run time (DP-01; Architecture v5 slides 8, 15 and 41). It creates `rwb_sandbox` on the one ACE PostgreSQL server in three schemas: schema `public` as the ACE test double (the Tier 1 tables and the RWB-ACE-001 Tier 2 tables), schema `recovery` holding the 30 read-only `v_ace_*` views, and schema `rwb_source_data` holding this service's 13 tables and the four extension tables `party_ext`, `contact_point_ext`, `account_ext` and `valuation_ext` (DP-01, DP-02, DP-05). The legacy line "schema recovery holds 92 tables" keeps its wording as the criterion of RWB-E1-065; in the target those tables sit in schema `rwb_source_data` on the sandbox database, and the criterion is executed against the objects the baseline delivers, not against a second copy.

The DDL the stage applies is the ACE schema file `15 ACE DB Alignment/ACE Schema PostgreSQL v1.sql` and the RWB-ACE-001 Tier 2 DDL held as a fixture, then the per-service Flyway baseline and the two view migrations of RWB-P1-E1069-APP on rwb-source-data's own sequence (DP-15; RWB-PLT-E1044-CON). The lists of values are read through the rwb-case reference-data contract on base `/api/recovery/case/v1` and never from a constant (DP-07; section 12.2). The embedded Drools kit (DP-04) evaluates the seeded rule packages in the sandbox smoke check, so a case that meets an exception shape is also a case the rules can decide. The sandbox is DEV only and is never deployed to SIT, UAT or PROD.

The four extension tables and the 30 views are delivered by RWB-P1-E1069-DB and RWB-P1-E1069-APP; the sandbox asserts them in its verifier and never re-creates them, so the criteria that name those objects are executed once, where they are delivered (X9). No criterion here reaches another service over a contract at run time, so no contract-mock Given line is added, and no legacy line is dropped or reworded.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | No production data in DEV; the sandbox holds synthetic data only | NFR-045; CTL-11 |
| BR2 | The sandbox is built from the same DDL as SIT: the ACE schema for the Tier 1 tables, the RWB-ACE-001 DDL for the 14 Tier 2 tables, and the per-service baseline and view migrations for this service's tables and the 30 views | RWB-E1-001; RWB-E1-069; ADR-001 |
| BR3 | Generated values come from the data dictionary and the lists of values, not from code | sys_fields; lov_value; Principle 1 |
| BR4 | Exception shapes generated: duplicate case for one customer and product (R-UNI-17), deceased customer (R-UNI-05), bankruptcy (R-UNI-07), open deviation, legal hold (R-UNI-20), unmapped product code, collateral with no account, case with three accounts, accounts at 89 and 90 days past due (DL16), withdrawn consent (R-UNI-10) | rules.txt; DL16 |
| BR5 | Case volumes follow the product split of the 30 June 2026 inventory at 10 percent | DL15 |
| BR6 | Every role has a named test user before it has real users | DL39 |
| BR7 | The ACE-shaped tables are a DEV test double for ACE, not a copy of source data: they hold synthetic rows only, they are never deployed to SIT, UAT or production, and no service table is loaded from them by a batch job | D-RCV-35 U1; NFR-045 |
| BR8 | No copy and no load table exists in the sandbox; the 20 tables that left the schema are absent, and every service reads source data only through this service's contract or its own `v_ace_*` views | D-RCV-35; ADR-010 |
| BR9 | A clear identity number is allowed only in the ACE-shaped tables; schema `recovery` and schema `rwb_source_data` hold masked or synthetic values only | D-RCV-35 U4; CTL-11 |

**Where each rule lives in the target.** BR1, BR4, BR5 and BR6 are the seed profile and the verifier of this story and stay as data, not as code. BR2 is the DDL set the stage applies, and it now names the per-service baseline and the two view migrations instead of the monolith's V0001 to V0003 (DP-15). BR3 and BR7 are enforced by the generator and the verifier here; BR7's deployment gate is a check of RWB-P1-E1065-DB, which refuses any target other than DEV. BR8 is asserted here over the built sandbox: the 20 absent tables are absent in every schema of the database, and the service reads source data only through the 30 views (DP-01, DP-05). BR9 is the personal-data pattern check of the verifier, which scans every column tagged `is_personal` outside schema `public`. BR2, BR3, BR8 and BR9 are also proven across the other 18 logins by the integration slice; this story proves them inside rwb-source-data.

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It changes the sandbox build state in the pipeline: Building, Published or Failed.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| no sandbox for the commit | the stage starts | A trigger fires and the advisory lock is free | Building, in `rwb_sandbox_next` |
| Building | the verifier passes | Every check of section 4 step 9 passes | Published: `rwb_sandbox_next` is renamed to `rwb_sandbox` |
| Building | the verifier fails | X1, X3, X4, X6, X8 or X9 | Failed: the previous `rwb_sandbox` stays in use |
| Building | a second build starts | The advisory lock is held | Waiting, then Building after the first ends |
| Published | a schema, dictionary or seed change | A merge to main or a manual start | Building again |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-TRIBE, tribe lead and squad members | Read and extract the sandbox through the read-only role `rwb_sandbox_read`; start a manual build |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Owns the sandbox database, the pipeline stage and the build result |
| Test users per role | Call the DEV service against the sandbox with their role's rights |
| ACE team lead and ACE DBA | Own the ACE schema DDL used as the test double and the Tier 2 DDL of RWB-ACE-001; approve a change to either |
| Recovery tech lead | Owns the seed profile, the seed value and the schema file properties |
| No approval level from the delegation of authority applies | The story takes no business decision |

The generator's build module and the service artefact are separated on purpose: the module runs in the pipeline under a build identity, the service runs in the cluster under the `rwb_source_data` login, and no credential of either appears in a migration, a script or a runbook.

The 30 views are `v_ace_account`, `v_ace_payment`, `v_ace_customer`, `v_ace_contact`, `v_ace_ca_relation`, `v_ace_aa_relation`, `v_ace_collateral`, `v_ace_asset`, `v_ace_efs_action`, `v_ace_efs_action_code`, `v_ace_efs_assignment`, `v_ace_bucket_log`, `v_ace_product`, `v_ace_branch`, `v_ace_holiday`, `v_ace_plan`, `v_ace_batch_status`, `v_ace_valuation`, `v_ace_collateral_detail`, `v_ace_npa_asset`, `v_ace_npa_sale`, `v_ace_lawsuit`, `v_ace_hearing`, `v_ace_pod`, `v_ace_write_off`, `v_ace_score`, `v_ace_party_product`, `v_ace_credit_decision`, `v_ace_esign` and `v_ace_iam_group`. The other tables of this service are filled the same way from their `sys_fields` rows; `delegation_limit` stays empty until version DOA-2026.11 is loaded, and `decision_log_entry` and `interaction` receive their rows from running the Workbench jobs against the sandbox. Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary.

**Which side is this story's.** The 22 `DF-` families above are this story's seed: the generator writes those rows into the sandbox and the verifier reads them back. The four `DF-EXT-` families are seeded here into tables that RWB-P1-E1065-DB creates, and the 30 `DF-ACE-` families are seeded here into views that RWB-P1-E1069-APP creates; neither table nor view is created by this story. The dictionary rows `DF-REF-` are this service's own metadata, delivered by the baseline of RWB-P1-E1001-APP.

**Where the case rows live.** The field list above is the legacy list and is kept as it stands, because it is what the sandbox has to produce. The tables it names are not this service's in the target: `recovery_case`, `case_account`, `case_party` and `deviation` belong to rwb-case and rwb-deviation, and `document` and `document_field` to rwb-document (Ownership Map v1). The sandbox database holds three schemas only — `public`, `recovery` and `rwb_source_data` — so the synthetic case is held where this service owns the row: the `case_list_row` projection (case number, product group, status, entry date, days past due and total outstanding), `interaction`, `dp_treatment`, `dp_guarantee_claim` and `efs_ledger_outcome`, with the account, party, collateral and valuation keys carried as business keys. That keeps the generator inside its own schema (DP-01), keeps the sandbox to one service's release, and leaves the case record of rwb-case, the document store of rwb-document and the deviation record of rwb-deviation to their own stories and their own sandbox slices. The SQL text of AC2 and AC5 that names `recovery.recovery_case` is the legacy text and is executed against the sandbox's case projection; the meaning of the criterion, the three product groups with their counts and the one case with its linked rows, is unchanged.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. This story delivers a build tool and a pipeline stage; it publishes no operation. The read contract of the service is RWB-P1-E1069-APP's, on base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` (DP-13), and this story neither adds a path to it nor documents one as provided.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

One read, at build time only.

| Method | Path | Owner | Use | Pattern |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0501; ASM-0693); read as `/api/recovery/case/v1/reference-data/{tableCode}` | P3 rwb-case | Every list of values the generator needs, read as data per `tableCode` instead of being written in code, once per build and cached for the run | DP-07; one hop, 2 s timeout, no retry beyond the client default |

The reference-data path of rwb-case is not named in the source set of this run, so the row carries the placeholder and the reading fixed above: the family is read through the published RWB-P3-E1043-CON client library on base `/api/recovery/case/v1`, and the exact path is settled in that contract's review. A read that does not answer fails the build closed before any row is written (X8), and the generator never falls back to a constant or to a copy of a list.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The topic of the service is `rwb.source-data.events.v1` with event names `rwb.source-data.<Event>.v1` (DP-14), and its two events `AceDataReady` and `AceDataLate` belong to RWB-P1-E1013-APP. A sandbox build is a pipeline run, not a business fact, so it writes no outbox row and publishes nothing.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The service consumes no event in Architecture v5 slide 15 ("none: Airflow call; fallback polls ACE batch record"), and a build tool subscribes to nothing.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The sandbox build stage calls no Temporal workflow and no activity, because it runs in the pipeline and not in the cluster; the task queue of the service is `rwb-source-data` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, and the workflows `AceIngestCheck` and `reconciliation` and the activities `listEligibleAccounts` and `snapshot(page)` of Architecture v5 slide 15 are other P1 stories. The only process this story starts is the pipeline job of 12.6.

###### 12.6 Schedules

**Pipeline stage**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Merge to main that changes the ACE schema DDL, a file under the rwb-source-data Flyway migration folder, the dictionary or the seed profile; manual start by RW-TRIBE or RW-PLATADM |
| Job name | Sandbox build, a DEV pipeline stage of the rwb-source-data repository; not a scheduled job, not a Temporal Schedule and not in `job_catalog` |
| Schedule | On trigger only |
| Input | `ACE Schema PostgreSQL v1.sql`; the RWB-ACE-001 Tier 2 DDL as a fixture; the per-service Flyway baseline and the two view migrations of RWB-P1-E1069-APP; `sys_objects`, `sys_fields` and the lists of values after migration; the role and permission seed file; the seed profile properties of section 13 |
| Output | Database `rwb_sandbox` with schema `public` (the ACE test double, the Tier 1 and Tier 2 tables), schema `recovery` (the 30 views) and schema `rwb_source_data` (this service's 13 tables and the four extension tables) holding synthetic rows; the build report with the row count per table and the verifier result |
| Events published | None |
| Idempotency key | Commit hash and seed. The same pair produces the same rows |
| Restart behavior | The build works on `rwb_sandbox_next` and renames it to `rwb_sandbox` only after the verifier passes, under one PostgreSQL advisory lock; a failed build leaves the previous sandbox and no partial database |

The stage is the only "schedule" this story has, and it is deliberately not a Temporal Schedule: it is a release activity, not a business timer. The contract of the stage itself — its inputs, outputs, seed profile, failure contract and fixtures — is the deliverable of RWB-P1-E1065-CON.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None created in schema `rwb_source_data` by this story. The objects the stage stands up in the sandbox database are these, and each keeps its own owner:

| Object in `rwb_sandbox` | Schema | Owner (ownership map) | This story |
|---|---|---|---|
| the ACE-shaped test double: the Tier 1 tables and the 14 Tier 2 tables | `public` | ACE team (schema `public` is ACE's) | Created as a test double from the ACE schema file and the Tier 2 DDL fixture and filled with synthetic rows; never deployed outside DEV |
| the 30 `v_ace_*` views and the three helper functions | `recovery` | View owner `ace_view_owner`; contract owner P1 | **Not created here**: RWB-P1-E1069-APP creates them; the verifier asserts 30 of 30 compile and return a row |
| `party_ext`, `contact_point_ext`, `account_ext`, `valuation_ext` | `rwb_source_data` | P1 | **Not created here**: RWB-P1-E1069-DB creates them; the verifier asserts their columns and keys |
| `case_list_row`, `data_contract`, `data_product`, `data_product_access`, `data_product_load`, `dp_guarantee_claim`, `dp_treatment`, `efs_ledger_outcome`, `interaction`, `reconciliation_result`, `sys_field_version`, `sys_fields`, `sys_objects` — the 13 tables of P1 in the ownership map | `rwb_source_data` | P1 | Created by the per-service baseline that the stage applies; the baseline itself is RWB-P1-E1001-APP's and this story writes no row of it |
| the read-only role `rwb_sandbox_read` and its grants | database | P1 (sandbox), credential by the platform DB owner | **Not created here**: RWB-P1-E1065-DB creates the role and issues the grants |

`lake_copy_watermark` is in the ownership map but has no target, because the data lake is removed (DP-17), so it is not in the 13 and the generator does not seed it. No table of another service is created, altered or read, and no foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fixture | Serves | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| ACE head fixture | `ACE Schema PostgreSQL v1.sql` | The Tier 1 tables of the test double on every build |
| Tier 2 DDL fixture | The RWB-ACE-001 DDL (DL43) | The 14 Tier 2 tables while RWB-ACE-001 is not deployed in DEV (X7) |
| Reference-data fake | RWB-P3-E1043-CON | Every list of values, answered per `tableCode` with a granted answer, an empty list and a timeout (X8) |
| Delivered-tables fixture | RWB-P1-E1001-APP, RWB-P1-E1069-APP and RWB-P1-E1065-DB | A container with the baseline, the 30 views and the four extension tables, so the verifier asserts the real objects instead of a second definition (X9) |
| Seed profile fixture | RWB-P1-E1065-CON | Seed 20261128, the three volumes, the shape count and the LOV source, so a changed volume is a diff and not a code change |

| Call type | Provided | Consumed | Notes |

| REST | None | 1 operation at build time (`/api/recovery/case/v1` reference data, DP-07) | One hop, 2 s timeout; the exact path is settled in RWB-P3-E1043-CON |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `tools/sandbox-generator`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.sourcedata.sandbox`, built as a separate build module of the rwb-source-data repository and never packaged into the service artefact. Service base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` (not used here), schema `rwb_source_data`, views in schema `recovery`, sandbox database `rwb_sandbox`, build database `rwb_sandbox_next`, topic `rwb.source-data.events.v1` (not published here), Temporal task queue `rwb-source-data` in namespace `rwb-recovery` (not used here).

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-01, DP-05 and DP-15 are the subject of this story: one schema, one read path and one sequence, all exercised by a build tool that runs outside the service. DP-07 is used for every list of values, through the published contract and its fake. DP-03 applies as one decision record per seeded rule evaluation in the smoke check, and DP-04 as the embedded kit that evaluates the seeded packages; the C row of DP-04 (`RWB-P7-E1073-CON`) is not taken by this story, because the smoke check evaluates the packages held in its own fixture and calls no rwb-decision operation, and the contract list of this story is fixed at `RWB-P3-E1043-CON`. DP-13 and DP-19 are named for completeness of the pattern set: this story serves no path and no screen, and their build dependencies stay with the application stories that do.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `AceSchemaLoader` | Service | Applies the Tier 1 tables, the Tier 2 DDL fixture, the per-service baseline and the two view migrations to `rwb_sandbox_next` |
| `SandboxGenerator` | Service | Reads the metadata and writes synthetic rows table by table in foreign key order, in schema `public` first and then in schema `rwb_source_data` |
| `ValueFactory` | Service | Produces a value per data type and list, seeded; synthetic names as "SYN-FIRST-000123"; tokens as random 64-character hex |
| `ExceptionShapeBuilder` | Service | Adds the shapes in BR4, 10 cases each |
| `SandboxVerifier` | Service | View compile and row checks, list, key, personal data pattern, boundary and delivered-objects checks |
| `AccessSeedLoader` | Service | Seeds the role and permission rows and one synthetic test user reference per role, from the reference-data contract |
| `SandboxExport` | Service | Writes a table to CSV for the read-only role |
| `Sandbox build stage` | Job | Pipeline stage: create the database and its three schemas, apply the DDL and the baseline, generate, verify, rename, grant |

**Database.** The stage creates `rwb_sandbox_next` with schema `public`, schema `recovery` and schema `rwb_source_data`, applies the DDL set of section 4 step 3, fills all three schemas, verifies, then renames the database to `rwb_sandbox` from the maintenance connection; RWB-P1-E1065-DB owns the role `rwb_sandbox_read` and the grants, and the pipeline holds one PostgreSQL advisory lock for the whole build. The stage creates no table of the service schema that the baseline does not already create, and it edits no applied migration (DP-15).

**Configuration and reference data.** Properties `rwb.sandbox.seed=20261128`, `rwb.sandbox.cases.mortgage=1226`, `rwb.sandbox.cases.hire-purchase=1296`, `rwb.sandbox.cases.ssme=290`, `rwb.sandbox.shape-count=10`, `rwb.sandbox.ace-schema=15 ACE DB Alignment/ACE Schema PostgreSQL v1.sql`, owned by the recovery tech lead; the lists of values through the reference-data contract (DP-07); the role and permission rows from the seed file of rwb-case. Every value is overridable, and the seed profile document is RWB-P1-E1065-CON's.

**Build steps**

1. `AceSchemaLoader` for the Tier 1 tables and the Tier 2 fixture; stop before the Section B view migration when the Tier 2 DDL is absent.
2. Metadata reader over `sys_objects`, `sys_fields` and the reference-data read, with foreign key order from the relationships.
3. `ValueFactory` per data type and list, seeded; a column with no `sys_fields` row fails the build.
4. `SandboxGenerator` for the ACE-shaped tables, then the case volumes with linked accounts, parties, contact points, collateral, valuations, payments and interactions.
5. `ExceptionShapeBuilder` for the shapes in BR4.
6. `AccessSeedLoader` with a synthetic test user reference per role.
7. `SandboxVerifier`: 30 views compile and return rows, rows per table, list values, foreign keys, personal data patterns outside schema `public` (national ID with check digit, mobile number, email), the 89 and 90 days past due boundary, and the delivered objects of the two sibling stories.
8. The Drools smoke check over the seeded packages, with one decision record per evaluation.
9. The pipeline stage with `rwb_sandbox_next`, the advisory lock, the rename and the grant.
10. Tests for AC1 to AC9 and the access test in the pipeline.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.source-data.sandbox` (enables the DEV profile that points the service at `rwb_sandbox`).

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, `rwb_sandbox` holds the three schemas with the seeded rows, the build report is published with the row count per table, and squads use the sandbox in DEV.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the volumes, the seed, the shape count and the schema file are properties, and every list of values is read through the reference-data contract; values come from the dictionary and the lists.
- No personal data in logs, tests, events or prompts: every name, identifier and contact value is synthetic, and the verifier blocks a value that looks real outside schema `public`.
- No read of another service's tables at run time: the generator is a build tool outside the service artefact and is never deployed to SIT, UAT or production (DP-01).
- The sandbox is in DEV only; no copy goes to another environment. The ACE-shaped tables are a test double, not a data copy, and the deployment gate of RWB-P1-E1065-DB refuses any other target.
- No copy and no load table is created: every service reads source data only through this service's contract or its own `v_ace_*` views.
- The 30 views, the four extension tables, the login and the grants are one story's delivery each and one story's test each: this story asserts them and never re-creates them.
- An applied migration is never edited: a correction is a new version on the service sequence (DP-15).
- The embedded Drools kit evaluates packages held in its own fixture: no rule package is downloaded from rwb-decision during a build.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-065 for rwb-access. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **security administrator (RW-SECADM), a reference data administrator (RW-REFADM) and a squad member with a Workbench role (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **the DEV sandbox to stand up the Recovery role list and the role to permission matrix in `rwb_access` from the same seed file on every rebuild, one synthetic test identity per role with no person name, the authorise answer and the resolved permission view those identities receive, and one local access entry per decision**, so that **every squad can build and test a role's read and action in DEV from the first day, before any role has a real user and with no production data**.

##### 2. Business rationale

SIT reads the real ACE database and the real IAM groups; DEV has neither. Without a seeded role list and matrix, no squad can test a case read, a queue action or a refusal before a real user is mapped to a role, and every squad would ask the security administrator to create an identity by hand. The legacy story builds a sandbox database in DEV from the same DDL as SIT, fills both schemas with synthetic rows and, in step 8 of its flow, "loads the 54 roles, the permission matrix and one named test user per role"; legacy BR6 fixes the rule behind it (every role has a test user before it has real users, DL39) and legacy AC1 names the role and permission seeding in the same breath as the schema build.

This story is the rwb-access part of legacy RWB-E1-065. It carries the access seed and the access answers, not the database, the generator or the views: the DEV database `rwb_sandbox`, the ACE-shaped tables, the 92 recovery tables, the 30 `v_ace_*` views, the case volumes, the exception shapes, the dictionary-driven value factory, the verifier, the rename and the read-only grant on the sandbox belong to the rwb-source-data contract of this legacy key (RWB-P1-E1065-CON), the P1 and DB app stories of the same key, and the integration story RWB-ITG-E1065-ITG. What this slice owns is the part that answers for rwb-access: the `role` and `permission` rows the sandbox loads into `rwb_access`, one synthetic identity per role, and the two answers every other service and every screen gets from those rows at the matrix version in force.

rwb-access owns Recovery roles as data, scope, masking policy, the DoA table and the access log (Architecture v5 slide 41), and every other service asks it before a read or an action (slide 14: `POST /authorise`, cached). The seed is therefore the difference between a DEV environment where a role's rights exist only in a document and one where the authorise answer of every service is computed from rows. The seed writes role codes, capability areas, letters, a version label and synthetic identity keys only; it carries no person name, no account number and no identity number, so the sandbox keeps BR1 (no production data) and BR9 (no clear personal value outside the ACE-shaped tables) while giving DEV a usable policy pack.

The matrix this slice seeds is the access slice of the pack version in force: capability areas from LOV-CAPABILITY, letters C, R, U, D and A or a dash, scope from LOV-SCOPE, all rows at one matrix version. Loading and approving a pack in a running environment is the matrix story (RWB-P4-E1037-APP) and the pack load story (RWB-P4-AD002-APP); here the same file is written by a per-service migration so a fresh sandbox has the pack without a screen, and it meets REQ-RDF-001 (one owner per data product) and REQ-RDF-010 (access per data product by role, with personal data masked).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The `rwb_access` baseline is in place: `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule`, `role_conflict` and `delegation_limit` exist at the platform migration version, and the local decision-record table is created by the decision-record library (DP-03).
- RWB-P4-E1037-CON is published — the authorise contract of rwb-access with `POST /authorise`, `GET /me/permissions` and the masking read — so this story answers an identity's rights behind a published shape. The request and answer field lists are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0898; ASM-1619).
- RWB-P1-E1065-CON is published: the rwb-source-data contract of this legacy key, which fixes the DEV sandbox build, the database name `rwb_sandbox`, the seed value `20261128`, the order in which the per-service migrations run after the sandbox build, and the fixture the application tests run against (DP-11, C dependency).
- The access seed file — the legacy `roles.txt` and `Permissions` file of this key — is in the rwb-access repository as a migration resource. Its location, format, version label and row count are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0895; ASM-1616).
- The matrix letters for the capability areas this seed fills are read from that file; the TSD P4 RBAC matrix tabulates only three of the 14 capability areas, so the letters of the other areas are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0900; ASM-1621).
- The role count is the legacy 54; the TSD P4 RBAC matrix tabulates 42 role rows. The difference is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0899; ASM-1620).
- The capability areas and scopes of the seed are the values of LOV-CAPABILITY (14 areas: CASE_RECORD, QUEUE_AND_ALLOCATION, TREATMENT_AND_OFFER, LITIGATION, ASSET_AND_DISPOSAL, DEBT_SALE, WRITE_OFF_AND_POSTING, DOCUMENTS, RULES_AND_PARAMETERS, REFERENCE_DATA, DECISION_LOG, PARTNER_PORTAL, REPORTING, PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION) and LOV-SCOPE (OWN, TEAM, REGION, ALL), read through the reference-data contract of rwb-case (DP-07, C RWB-P3-E1043-CON).
- The DEV groups named in `role.entra_group` and one synthetic test identity per role are provisioned in the DEV directory by the sandbox build; who owns that list and when an identity is retired is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0896; ASM-1617).
- The login is the rwb-access login (DP-02). The per-service login name and the DEV-only read-only role are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0897; ASM-1618).
- The sign-in path that resolves directory groups to `role.entra_group` rows is RWB-P4-E1022-APP and RWB-P4-AD001-APP; this story neither serves nor changes it, and it reads no `v_ace_*` view and no `public` table (DP-05 applies here as a prohibition).

##### 4. Flow

1. The sandbox build of RWB-P1-E1065-CON creates the DEV database `rwb_sandbox`, applies the ACE-shaped test double and the per-service migrations in order, and reaches the `rwb_access` migration step with an empty `role` and `permission`.
2. The rwb-access migration `V1065_1__access_seed.sql` applies the access seed file in one transaction: the 54 `role` rows with role code, role name, role class, default scope and the DEV group name, then the `permission` rows with the role, the capability area, the letters and matrix version `PM-2026.12`.
3. The migration writes the same file on every rebuild, so the same seed value `20261128` and the same file give the same rows and the same counts; a row of the seed is never merged with a row of a different matrix version.
4. AccessSeedVerifier reads the written rows back: the role count, one matrix version on every permission row, every capability area against LOV-CAPABILITY and every scope against LOV-SCOPE through the reference-data contract, every letter in C, R, U, D, A or a dash, and every role with at least one permission row or an explicit dash.
5. TestIdentitySeeder records the DEV group of each role in `role.entra_group` and the sandbox build provisions one synthetic identity per role as a member of that group; the identity key carries the role code and a sequence and no person name.
6. A squad member signs in with the synthetic identity of the role being tested; the sign-in path of RWB-P4-E1022-APP resolves the directory groups to `role.entra_group` rows and holds the role set on the session.
7. rwb-access serves `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/permissions` for that identity: the role, its default scope, the matrix version in force and the letters per capability area, all read from `role` and `permission`.
8. rwb-access serves `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` for the read or the action the identity attempts: the letters of the area are unioned across the identity's roles, the scope test runs on the facts carried in the request, and the answer is `AC-READ` with matrix version `PM-2026.12` or a refusal with MSG-P4-002.
9. rwb-access writes one local access entry for the decision — decision code, actor, case ID when the decision is on a case, area, right, field IDs and the time — through the decision-record library, first in the transaction, and answers the caller.
10. The DEV sandbox has no Kafka, so no relay runs and no event leaves the sandbox; the entry stays in `rwb_access` and the DEV access-log read serves it. A squad that needs the entry in the central ledger uses the SIT environment built by RWB-ITG-E1065-ITG.
11. When the seed file changes, the next build writes the new rows at the new matrix version; the read-back of step 4 is the gate, and a role whose area has no row is refused by default, never allowed.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A seeded permission row names an area that is not in LOV-CAPABILITY, or a scope that is not in LOV-SCOPE | The sandbox build fails naming the row and the value; the previous sandbox stays in use | None (pipeline result) | AC1 |
| X2 | The same seed and the same file run twice | The same role rows and the same permission rows are written, with no duplicate and no row of another version | None | AC2 |
| X3 | A role has no permission row for an area, or the area holds a dash | The identity's action in that area is refused by default; nothing is allowed | MSG-P4-002 | AC5 |
| X4 | A test identity holds RW-REFADM and calls the case list | Refused before the case read, with one `AC-DENY` entry naming the area, the right and the result | MSG-P4-002 | AC5 |
| X5 | A seeded value matches a personal data pattern | The sandbox build fails naming the table and column; no sandbox is published from that build | None (pipeline result) | AC6 |
| X6 | The identity carries no Workbench role at all | Refused at the door of every endpoint; no case, queue or reference data is returned | MSG-P4-001 | AC3 |
| X7 | The local access entry cannot be written | The answer is 503 and no case data is returned; the decision is not taken on an unrecorded basis | MSG-P7-003 | AC7 |
| X8 | A reader holds the DEV read-only role and tries to change a seed row | The write is refused by the database; the row is unchanged | None (database error) | AC8 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against the `rwb_access` baseline, the published authorise contract RWB-P4-E1037-CON and the RWB-P1-E1065-CON fixture. rwb-case's case list and reference data are contract fakes |
| Negotiable | Roles, areas, letters, scope, the matrix version and the seed file content are rows; the story fixes the migration, the verifier and the two answers, and names no role or letter in code |
| Valuable | Every role can be exercised in DEV from Day 1, with no person name and no production data, and every squad hears the same answer from rwb-access |
| Estimable | One migration, one seed file, one verifier, one identity seeder and two answers already on the contract |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests, as a secondary slice of the legacy key |
| Testable | Every criterion in section 7 is one automated test over the seeded schema, with every cross-service answer stubbed |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Sandbox database with synthetic recovery data — the rwb-access seed and the access answers

  Background:
    Given the sandbox build uses seed 20261128
    Given the rwb-source-data contract mock returns the DEV sandbox build result for seed 20261128 with database "rwb_sandbox", schema "rwb_access" and the access seed file in the repository
    Given the rwb-case reference-data contract mock returns LOV-CAPABILITY with the 14 capability areas and LOV-SCOPE with "OWN", "TEAM", "REGION" and "ALL"

  Scenario: AC1 The access seed loads at one version (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the access seed file holds 54 role rows and the role to permission matrix rows
    When the rwb-access migration runs in schema "rwb_access" after the baseline
    Then 54 rows are in "role", each with a role code, a role name, a role class from LOV-ROLE-CLASS, a default scope from LOV-SCOPE and a DEV group name
    And every permission row names a role of the seed, a capability area of LOV-CAPABILITY, its letters and matrix version "PM-2026.12"
    And every letter is "C", "R", "U", "D", "A" or a dash
    And the seed writes no person name, no account number and no identity number

  Scenario: AC2 The seed rebuild is idempotent (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given schema "rwb_access" holds the seed for seed 20261128 at matrix version "PM-2026.12"
    When the same migration and the same seed file run again in a rebuilt database
    Then the same 54 role rows and the same permission rows are present at "PM-2026.12"
    And no row is duplicated and no row of another matrix version is left in the schema
    And each role code, capability area and letter reads back character for character as in the seed file

  Scenario: AC3 One synthetic test identity per role (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the sign-in path of RWB-P4-E1022-APP has resolved the groups of a synthetic identity to "role.entra_group" rows of "rwb_access"
    Given the seed names one DEV group per role in "role.entra_group" and the build provisions one synthetic identity per group
    When the identity "SYN-ID-RW-CASEOWN-01" calls GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/permissions
    Then the answer names role "RW-CASEOWN", its default scope "OWN" and matrix version "PM-2026.12"
    And the same holds for each of the 54 roles, with one identity each and no role without an identity
    And no identity key carries a person name, an e-mail address or an identity number

  Scenario: AC4 The case list is granted to a role that holds the letter (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the sandbox case list with case "RW-2026-000001"
    Given the identity "SYN-ID-RW-CASEOWN-01" holds role "RW-CASEOWN" with default scope "OWN" and owns case "RW-2026-000001"
    And the seed gives "RW-CASEOWN" the letter "R" in capability area "CASE_RECORD"
    When the caller asks POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise for area "CASE_RECORD", right "R" and case "RW-2026-000001"
    Then the answer grants the read with decision code "AC-READ" and matrix version "PM-2026.12"
    And the case list is returned through the rwb-case contract
    And one local access entry is written with decision code "AC-READ", the actor, case "RW-2026-000001", area "CASE_RECORD", right "R" and the time

  Scenario: AC5 RW-REFADM is refused the case list (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the sandbox case list
    Given the identity "SYN-ID-RW-REFADM-01" holds role "RW-REFADM" and matrix version "PM-2026.12" holds no CASE_RECORD row for it
    When the caller asks POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise for area "CASE_RECORD" and right "R"
    Then the call is refused with status 403 and message MSG-P4-002 for action "open the case list"
    And no case row is returned and no account, party or document is read
    And one local access entry is written with decision code "AC-DENY", area "CASE_RECORD", right "R" and result "REFUSED"

  Scenario: AC6 No clear personal value in rwb_access (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the seeded tables "role", "permission" and the local access entries
    When the verifier scans every column of schema "rwb_access" tagged is_personal, and every seeded text column, for the national ID, mobile number and e-mail patterns
    Then the build passes with no match, because the seed writes role codes, capability areas, letters, the matrix version, DEV group names and synthetic identity keys only
    And a clear identity number in the ACE-shaped tables is not a failure of this slice, because those tables are the ACE test double and belong to RWB-P1-E1065-CON
    And no sandbox is published from a build in which a seeded access value matches a personal data pattern

  Scenario: AC7 One local access entry per decision, with no relay (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the DEV sandbox runs with no Kafka broker and no relay
    When two decisions are served for one identity, an "AC-READ" and an "AC-DENY"
    Then two entries are written through the decision-record library, each with its sequence number, its previous hash and its entry hash
    And the entry is written before the answer, and a failed write answers 503 with MSG-P7-003 and returns no case data
    And no topic is produced to and no consumer group is created by this schema in the sandbox

  Scenario: AC8 The DEV read-only role reads the seed and cannot change it (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the DEV-only read-only role over the sandbox
    When a member of that role runs "SELECT role_code, default_scope FROM rwb_access.role" and then an UPDATE on the same row
    Then the read returns the 54 role rows
    And the UPDATE is refused by the database and the row is unchanged
    And the role holds no SELECT on the local access-entry table, so the access log cannot be read with it
```

The eight criteria above are new and test only this deliverable: the access seed, the synthetic identities and the two answers rwb-access gives from the seeded rows, including the legacy access case TC-E1-065-10 (a test identity holding RW-REFADM is refused the case list with MSG-P4-002). The legacy criteria AC1 to AC9 of RWB-E1-065 are owned elsewhere: the schema, the dictionary, the case volumes, the exception shapes and the verifier by the rwb-source-data and DB stories of the same key (RWB-P1-E1065-CON and RWB-P1-E1065-APP); only legacy AC1's role and permission seeding sentence, legacy BR6 and legacy BR9 are answered here. No legacy criterion text is copied into this section.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | No production data in DEV: the DEV sandbox holds synthetic rows only, and the access seed holds role codes, letters and synthetic identity keys (legacy BR1) | NFR-045; CTL-11; legacy BR1 |
| BR2 | Every role has a test identity before it has real users, and the identity carries no person name (legacy BR6) | DL39; legacy BR6 |
| BR3 | A clear identity number is allowed only in the ACE-shaped tables; `rwb_access` holds no clear personal value at all (legacy BR9) | D-RCV-35 U4; CTL-11; legacy BR9 |
| BR4 | Roles, capability areas, letters, scope and the matrix version are data rows with a version; no role code, area, letter or scope value is written in code | FSD P4 A2.3, A2.4; BR-P4-003, BR-P4-004; TSD P4 T3.2 |
| BR5 | The same seed and the same seed file give the same rows on every rebuild, and a rebuild never mixes two matrix versions | Legacy RWB-E1-065 AC5; TSD P4 T3.1 (matrix_version) |
| BR6 | The authorise answer is served only from `role` and `permission` at the matrix version in force; a capability area with no letter, and a role with no permission row, are refused (default deny) | FSD P4 A2.4; VR-P4-004-1; legacy TC-E1-065-10 |
| BR7 | rwb-access writes only its own schema: no `v_ace_*` view, no `public` table and no other service's table is read by this story, and the DEV groups reach it from the sign-in path of RWB-P4-E1022-APP | Architecture v5 slides 13, 14 and 41; DP-01, DP-05 |
| BR8 | The sandbox has no Kafka: the access entry is a local decision record written through the decision-record library, with no relay and no topic in the DEV profile (DP-09 is not a pattern of this story) | FSD P4 A2.8; DP-03; Architecture v5 slide 20 |
| BR9 | The DEV-only read-only role reads the seed and never changes it, and holds no read on the local access-entry table | Legacy RWB-E1-065 AC2, section 10; TSD P4 T6.2 |
| BR10 | The DEV matrix version is one label on every permission row of the seed; a row of a previous version is not carried into the sandbox | TSD P4 T3.1 (permission.matrix_version); FSD P4 A2.4 AC-P4-004-01 (version "PM-2026.12") |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| no `role` or `permission` row in `rwb_access` | the rwb-access migration runs | The sandbox build reaches the access step with the seed file present | 54 role rows and their permission rows at matrix version `PM-2026.12` |
| rows at `PM-2026.12` | the same migration and the same seed file run again | A rebuilt database with seed `20261128` | the same rows at `PM-2026.12`, no duplicate and no row of another version |
| a role with a letter in the area | an authorise request | The area and right are covered and the scope test passes | `AC-READ`, and one local entry written |
| a role with no letter in the area, or with a dash | an authorise request | The area or right is asked for | refused by default with MSG-P4-002, and one `AC-DENY` entry written |
| a synthetic identity of a role | the role receives its first real user | The release that gives the role a screen (DL39) | the identity is retired from the DEV group by its owner; the seeded role and permission rows do not change |

A `role` and a `permission` row have no lifecycle of their own: rwb-access holds no case state machine, and the module acts on events from rwb-case and writes through the decision log (TSD P4 T4). The pack version states LOADED, VALIDATED, APPROVED, IN_FORCE, SUPERSEDED and ROLLED_BACK belong to the load path (TSD P4 T3.2 LOV-VERSION-STATUS, T4) and to the pack load story RWB-P4-AD002-APP; this story writes one label and reads it back, and never promotes a version.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| rwb-access service identity (the rwb-access login, DP-02) | Runs the seed migration, reads `role` and `permission`, serves the authorise answer and the resolved permission view, and writes the local access entry |
| Decision-record library identity | Writes the local access entry with its sequence and hash link; no relay runs in the sandbox (DP-03) |
| RW-SECADM, security administrator | Owns the role list and the matrix as data: approves a new version of the seed file, and reads the seeded rows and the access entries of the sandbox |
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | Prepares the seed file and the change checklist; no approval, and in the sandbox an identity holding RW-REFADM holds no CASE_RECORD letter, so the case list is refused with MSG-P4-002 |
| RW-TRIBE, tribe lead and squad members | Sign in with the synthetic identity of a role and exercise a read or an action in DEV against the seeded rows |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Owns the DEV identity list behind `role.entra_group` and the retirement of an identity when the role receives its first real user |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Reads the local access entries of the sandbox with scope ALL; the read-only DEV role holds no access to them |

The per-service login name and the DEV-only read-only role are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0897; ASM-1618); the story keeps the legacy name `rwb_sandbox_read` for the read-only role and "the rwb-access login (DP-02)" for the service. The roles, areas and letters above are rows of the seed and are not fixed in code; no role in this story may grant itself a letter.

| DF-REF-035 | role | role_code | Write (seed), then Read |
| DF-REF-038 | role | default_scope | Write (seed), then Read |
| DF-REF-039 | role | entra_group (the DEV group of the synthetic identity) | Write (seed), then Read |

The seed writes the 54 roles and their permission rows and nothing else: no case row, no ACE row, no `lov_value` row, no `masking_rule` row, no `delegation_limit` row and no `role_conflict` row is loaded by this story. The synthetic identities are not a `rwb_access` table — the seed records the DEV group of each role in `role.entra_group` (DF-REF-039) and the directory holds the identity, so no identity, person name or credential is stored in the schema. `delegation_limit` stays empty until its own load story runs (legacy section 11). Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None new. The two answers are served through the operations of RWB-P4-E1037-CON on base `/api/recovery/access/v1`; owner rwb-access (P4). This slice adds no path, no query parameter and no response field, and answers the following behind them:

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/authorise` | Decide a role's read or action for a capability area, a case and a field list, from the seeded matrix, with one local access entry | Any authenticated caller with a Workbench role | Idempotent by identity, area, right, case reference and field list within the cache window |
| GET | `/me/permissions` | The identity's resolved roles, default scope, matrix version and the letters per capability area | Authenticated caller, own record only | Not applicable |

Request for `/authorise`: the caller identity from the session, the capability area, the right, the case reference and the field IDs. Answer: the decision code (`AC-READ` or `AC-DENY`), the matrix version, the scope result and the access-entry reference. Errors: 401 no Workbench role (MSG-P4-001), 403 no letter for the area or right (MSG-P4-002), 404 a case outside the caller's scope (MSG-P4-003), 503 the access entry cannot be written (MSG-P7-003). The field names of the request and the answer are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0898; ASM-1619).

The masking read, the DoA read, the role read `GET /admin/roles`, the access-log search `GET /admin/access-log`, the session read `GET /me/session` and the reference loads are P4 surface delivered by other P4 stories (RWB-P4-E1037-APP, RWB-P4-E1038-APP, RWB-P4-E1039-APP, RWB-P4-E1022-APP, RWB-P4-AD002-APP, RWB-P4-AD011-APP); this story adds none of them and changes no shape of any of them.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None at run time. This story answers from its own seeded rows, calls no service and reads no ACE view or ACE table (DP-01, DP-05 as a prohibition).

Two contracts are consumed as fixtures only. RWB-P1-E1065-CON fixes the DEV sandbox build this seed runs inside: database `rwb_sandbox`, seed `20261128`, the migration order and the fixture the application tests run against. The rwb-case case list and the rwb-case reference data are the mocks of AC4 and AC5 and of AC1, so the story builds and proves the grant and the refusal before rwb-case is live in DEV.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The DEV sandbox has no Kafka broker, so nothing is produced and no outbox relay runs: the access entry of this story is a local decision record written through the decision-record library, and DP-09 is not a pattern of this story. In a running environment the access entry is relayed as `DecisionRecorded` (EV-08) on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, which is the behaviour of the authorise story RWB-P4-E2007-APP and of the P7 ledger story; here the entry stops in `rwb_access`. `AccessPolicyChanged` on `rwb.access.events.v1` is raised by the load path (RWB-P4-AD002-APP) when a pack version goes in force, not by this seed.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. A migration consumes no topic; the seed is the file, not a subscription, and the sandbox profile wires no consumer group into `rwb_access`.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The seed is a migration and the two answers are synchronous REST calls in the caller's thread; this story runs no workflow, starts no activity and holds no Temporal worker of its own (Temporal and Drools design, this story runs no workflow).

DP-04 applies as a prohibition here: rwb-access evaluates no decision table for this story, the letters of a capability area are rows, and no DRL, workbook or rule package is written by the seed.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The only Schedule of rwb-access is the six-monthly access review list (JOB-18), which belongs to RWB-P4-AD008-APP (Architecture v5 slide 44). The sandbox build stage that calls this migration is a pipeline stage owned by RWB-P1-E1065-CON, not a Schedule of this service.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| role | P4 (`rwb_access`) | Recovery roles as data, with role class, default scope and the DEV group name |
| permission | P4 (`rwb_access`) | Capability area, letters and matrix version per role; the seeded matrix |
| local access entry (decision record) | P4 rows in `rwb_access`, written through the P7 decision-record library | One entry per decision in the DEV sandbox, with no relay |
| masking_rule, role_conflict, delegation_limit | P4 (`rwb_access`) | Same service, not written by this story; their load stories own the rows |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_access` | Present in the schema but not written by this story, because no event leaves the sandbox (DP-09 is not a pattern here) |

rwb-access reads no table of another service and holds no foreign key across services (DP-01); `lov_value` and the reference tables belong to rwb-case (P3) and reach this story only through the reference-data contract (DP-07); the central ledger copy of the access entries is written in `rwb_decision` from the topic by RWB-P7-E1027-CON and is out of this slice.

| RWB-P1-E1065-CON fixture | The P1 contract of this legacy key | The DEV sandbox build result for seed `20261128`: database `rwb_sandbox`, schema `rwb_access` after the baseline, the migration order and the access seed file in the repository |
| rwb-case case-list mock | AC4 and AC5 | The sandbox case list with case `RW-2026-000001`, and a refusal path that returns no case row |
| reference-data fake (RWB-P3-E1043-CON) | DP-07 | LOV-CAPABILITY with the 14 areas, LOV-SCOPE with OWN, TEAM, REGION and ALL, LOV-ROLE-CLASS with BANK_USER, PARTNER_USER and NON_HUMAN_ACTOR |
| RWB-P4-E1037-CON fake | The P4 authorise and permission contract | `/authorise` and `/me/permissions`, with a granted identity and a refused identity |
| decision-record library stub | DP-03 | A local chain that accepts the entry, and a stopped chain for the 503 path (AC7) |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |

| REST | 2 provided, 0 consumed | Both operations are the published contract of RWB-P4-E1037-CON on `/api/recovery/access/v1`; no outbound call and one hop within 2 s on the inbound call |
| Kafka | None | No topic produced and none consumed in the DEV sandbox; the access entry is a local decision record with no relay (DP-03, and DP-09 is not a pattern of this story) |
| Temporal | None | No workflow, no activity and no Schedule in this story |
| File | None | The seed file is a migration resource of the repository, not a file interface; no claim-check file is read or written |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`, module `seed`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access.seed`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

This is a secondary slice: it adds no new build dependency of its own. Metadata "Depends on (build)" stays `None` and "Contract dependencies" stays `RWB-P1-E1065-CON` exactly as the Work Package fixes them, and the platform contract libraries of DP-03, DP-04, DP-07, DP-15 and DP-19 arrive with the baseline, not with this story. DP-05 applies as a prohibition (the seed reads no ACE view and no `public` table, and no ACE-shaped row is written), DP-04 as a prohibition (no decision table and no DRL in this service), DP-15 as the per-service Flyway sequence that carries the seed, DP-13 as the base of the two answers, and DP-19 as the route on which SCR-43 Roles and access will show the seeded rows when it arrives.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| AccessSeedLoader | Service | Applies the seed file in one transaction: the 54 `role` rows and their `permission` rows at one matrix version; refuses a row whose area, scope, class or letters are outside their list |
| SeedFileReader | Service | Parses the access seed file (the legacy `roles.txt` and `Permissions` file); holds no role code, area or letter of its own |
| AccessSeedVerifier | Service | Reads the written rows back: role count, one version per permission row, area against LOV-CAPABILITY, scope against LOV-SCOPE, letters format, and the personal-data pattern scan of the seeded columns |
| TestIdentitySeeder | Service | Records the DEV group of each role in `role.entra_group` and asserts one synthetic identity per group, with an identity key that carries the role code and no person name |
| MePermissionReader | Service | Answers `GET /me/permissions` from `role` and `permission`: the role set, the default scope, the matrix version and the letters per area |
| AuthoriseAnswerReader | Service | Answers `POST /authorise` from the seeded rows: union of the letters across the identity's roles, the scope test on the request facts, and `AC-READ` or `AC-DENY` |
| AccessEntryWriter | Service | Writes the local access entry through the decision-record library, first in the transaction, with no relay |

**Database and migrations**

- Writes `role`, `permission` and the local access entry in schema `rwb_access`; writes no other table and reads no other schema (DP-01).
- Migration in this story: `V1065_1__access_seed.sql`, the versioned per-service Flyway migration that carries the seed file's rows into `role` and `permission`, run after the `rwb_access` baseline. Its companion `R__access_seed_rebuild.sql` is the repeatable migration that re-applies the same file, so a rebuild of the sandbox writes the same rows (AC2). No column, index or constraint is added for case, ACE or identity data; the synthetic identities live in the directory, not in the schema.
- The seed is idempotent by construction: the repeatable migration writes the rows of the file it is given, deletes nothing outside the matrix version it writes, and refuses a row that belongs to two versions of the same role and area.
- No row of `masking_rule`, `role_conflict` or `delegation_limit` is written by this story, and no `lov_value` row is written at all.

**Configuration and reference data**

- `rwb.access.seed-file` names the migration resource that holds the seed file; its path and format are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0895; ASM-1616).
- `rwb.access.matrix-version` is the label written on every permission row; the value the sandbox loads is `PM-2026.12`, the version the access examples of FSD P4 A2.4 load, and whether the DEV seed must carry the same label as SIT is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0895; ASM-1616).
- `rwb.access.seed.identity-prefix` is the prefix of the synthetic identity key; the key format follows the legacy synthetic convention `SYN-` and is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0896; ASM-1617).
- The roles, areas, letters and scopes are rows of the seed file; the area and scope values are compared with LOV-CAPABILITY and LOV-SCOPE read through the reference-data contract of rwb-case (DP-07), and a `rwb_access` copy of a list is never kept.
- The login is the rwb-access login (DP-02), and the DEV-only read-only role keeps the legacy name `rwb_sandbox_read`; both names are Not specified in the source documents for the target schema (GAP-0897; ASM-1618).
- The feature switch is `rwb.access.sandbox-access-seed`, read as a parameter: on in the DEV profile only; off means the seed does not apply and every authorise request is refused closed with MSG-P4-002, never allowed by default.

**Build steps**

1. SeedFileReader and AccessSeedLoader over the seed file, with a test per list violation (an unknown area, an unknown scope, an invalid letter) and a test that no role code, area or letter appears in the Java source.
2. `V1065_1__access_seed.sql` and `R__access_seed_rebuild.sql`, with the read-back of AC1 and the same-seed test of AC2.
3. AccessSeedVerifier with the role count, the single matrix version, the area and scope comparison through the reference-data fake, and the personal-data pattern scan; tests for AC1 and AC6.
4. TestIdentitySeeder over `role.entra_group`, with one identity per role and the no-person-name check; tests for AC3.
5. MePermissionReader and AuthoriseAnswerReader over the seeded rows, with the granted path, the default-deny path and the missing-role path; tests for AC3, AC4 and AC5.
6. AccessEntryWriter with the entry before the answer, the `AC-READ` and `AC-DENY` codes, the local chain and the 503 when the record cannot be written; tests for AC4, AC5 and AC7.
7. The DEV grant script for the read-only role: SELECT on `role` and `permission` only, no UPDATE, no SELECT on the access-entry table; test for AC8.
8. Contract-fake run of RWB-P1-E1065-CON, the rwb-case case list and the reference data, so the story builds and proves every answer before rwb-case and rwb-source-data are live in DEV.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.access.sandbox-access-seed`, read as a parameter; off refuses closed and seeds nothing.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the contract tests of RWB-P4-E1037-CON and RWB-P1-E1065-CON stay green, a rebuilt DEV sandbox carries the same 54 role rows and permission rows at one matrix version, every role has one synthetic identity that carries no person name, an identity holding RW-REFADM is refused the case list with MSG-P4-002, and no column of `rwb_access` holds a clear personal value.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | No Workbench role on the token | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The area or the right is absent for the identity's roles | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The case is absent or outside the identity's scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The local access entry cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

Seed failures are reported in the pipeline result with the table, the row and the value named; no user message applies. For MSG-P4-002 in this story, {action} names the action the identity tried — for example "open the case list" — and never a case fact or a role name.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story. SCR-43 Roles and access — roles, permissions, scope and the group mapping, with the access log, first in E8 and by file load before (FSD P4 Screens) — will show the rows this seed writes, and the seeded identities make that screen demonstrable in DEV before a real user exists; the screen itself belongs to the administration stories and to RWB-P4-E1022-APP.

Both answers reach a screen only through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), which calls rwb-access for the decision and each owner service for its own data, one hop each. The route specification and the field-level masking of the composite route are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0898; ASM-1619).
