##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the seed, the volumes, the shape count and the fixture are properties of the stage contract, and every code, actor value, outcome and state is a row of the dictionary and the lists. A build check fails on a code, a list value or a state in the source.
- No personal data in logs, tests, events or prompts: every case reference, user reference and value is synthetic, and the verifier blocks a value that looks real in `rwb_deviation`.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or a `v_ace_*` view: this service holds no `v_ace_*` grant, reads no ACE table and needs no ACE product, so the seed writes nothing in schema `public`.
- No cross-schema read and no cross-schema key: `deviation` is the whole estate, `case_id` is a reference to the fixture, and a statement on `rwb_case`, `rwb_document` or a `v_ace_*` view fails the boundary test (DP-01).
- No copy and no load table: the 20 tables that left the schema are absent from `rwb_deviation`, and no row of it is loaded from `public` or from another service's table (DP-05, DP-17).
- One event owner per fact: the seed publishes nothing, and a build that writes an outbox row fails the acceptance test (DP-09 as a prohibition).
- The sandbox is in DEV only and never reaches SIT, UAT or production; the stage contract's deployment gate refuses any other target.
- An applied migration is never edited, and the dictionary changes by a new version on the service sequence (DP-15).
- No retired element is reintroduced: no Quartz row, no shared job table, no monolith base and no data-lake export.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-065 for rwb-document, carrying the DEV sandbox document estate. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tribe lead and squad member (RW-TRIBE)** I want **the DEV sandbox to stand up `rwb_document` from the same per-service migration as SIT, with the six document types at the version in force, one synthetic document per agreed type on every synthetic case with its extracted fields and no clear personal value**, so that **every squad can build and test the document screens, the OCR and extraction paths and the retention checks from the first day, before any ACE interface is available and with no production data**.

This story is the rwb-document part of legacy RWB-E1-065: the document estate of the DEV sandbox. The DEV database `rwb_sandbox`, the ACE-shaped test double, the 92 recovery tables, the 30 `v_ace_*` views, the dictionary-driven generator, the case volumes, the exception shapes, the verifier of the whole sandbox, the pipeline stage, the rename and the read-only grant on schema `recovery` belong to RWB-P1-E1065-CON, RWB-P1-E1065-APP and RWB-P1-E1065-DB. What this slice owns is what answers for `rwb_document`: the six document types at version "DOCTYPE-2026.11" with their fields and retention classes, one synthetic document per agreed type on every synthetic case with its extracted fields, the held intake items and their OCR text, the checklist and completeness rows, the custody and retention rows the sandbox needs to be demonstrable, the personal-data gate on `document_field.extracted_value` (legacy AC7 names exactly that column), and the DEV read-only role's read of the schema.

rwb-document owns metadata, custody, OCR text and fields, signatures and retention (Architecture v5 slide 41), and every document file is in Blob with WORM (slides 8 and 16). Every service runs from the service template, reads and writes only its own schema and holds its outbox and inbox there (slide 20), so the document estate is only usable for the squads if it exists in `rwb_document` and in the DEV container, not in a shared fixture. The type table version this slice seeds is the one in force from 30 November 2026: FSD P5 AC-ALT-P5-003-01 gives version "DOCTYPE-2026.11" with the six types, COURT_NOTICE with retention class "LEGAL10Y" and write_once true, and APPRAISAL_REPORT with "GENERAL05Y", write_once false and 4 fields. The checklist the sandbox carries is checklist version "CHK-2026.11" (FSD P5 A2.16) and the retention action the sandbox carries names retention version "RET-2026.11" (FSD P5 A2.17).

##### 2. Business rationale

SIT reads the real ACE database and the real document store; DEV has neither. Without a seeded document estate, no squad can test the case documents screen, the OCR and extraction review queue or a retention or custody check before a real scan arrives: the tables are empty, the review list is empty and every document story would ask another team for a fixture. The legacy story builds a sandbox database in DEV from the same DDL as SIT, fills it with synthetic rows, and its AC1 fixes the document part of the outcome — the case "RW-2026-000001" has its accounts, parties, interactions and documents linked — while legacy BR3 requires the values to come from the data dictionary and the lists and legacy AC7 names `recovery.document_field.extracted_value` as the one column the personal-data gate scans.

This story is the rwb-document part of legacy RWB-E1-065; the primary slice is the rwb-source-data contract of the same key. The DEV database `rwb_sandbox`, the ACE-shaped test double, the 92 recovery tables, the 30 `v_ace_*` views, the dictionary-driven value factory, the case volumes, the exception shapes, the verifier of the whole sandbox, the pipeline stage, the rename and the read-only grant on schema `recovery` are not here. What is here is the estate that answers for this service: the six types at the version in force, one document per agreed type on every synthetic case with its fields, confidence and extracted value, the held intake items and their page text, the checklist items and the completeness row, one custody movement and one retention action, and the DEV read-only role's read of the tables the screens read.

The seed is the difference between a DEV environment where a document screen shows an empty list and one where it shows six types, their confidence and their retention class. It keeps BR1 (no production data in DEV) and BR9 (a clear identity number only in the ACE-shaped tables) because the seed writes synthetic type codes, synthetic file references, synthetic field values and a masked or synthetic national ID only, and it serves REQ-RDF-001 (one owner per data product, reachable in DEV without a request to another team) and REQ-RDF-010 (access per data product by role, with personal data masked). The type codes, the fields, the write-once flags, the retention classes and the checklist rows are data with a version, not code, so the same estate follows a new type table version without a release (FSD P5 A2.3, BR-P5-003; DP-07).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The `rwb_document` baseline is in place: `document`, `document_field`, `document_custody`, `document_type`, `document_checklist_item`, `case_document_check`, `document_hub_parameter`, `document_intake`, `document_text` and `retention_action` exist with the standard record columns of TSD P5 T3.0 (`is_active`, `state`, `version`, `created_at`, `created_by`, `updated_at`, `updated_by`), at the platform migration version of DP-15.
- RWB-P1-E1065-CON is published: the rwb-source-data contract of this legacy key, which fixes the DEV sandbox build, the database name `rwb_sandbox`, the seed value `20261128`, the order in which the per-service migrations run after the sandbox build, the case list of the seed and the fixture the application tests run against (DP-11, C dependency). Its operation names and payload field lists are those it publishes and are not restated here.
- The type table version in force from 30 November 2026 is "DOCTYPE-2026.11" (FSD P5 AC-ALT-P5-003-01), loaded and approved by RWB-P5-E1025-APP in a running environment; in the sandbox the same version is written by the migration of this story, so no screen and no approval step is needed to build it.
- LOV-RETENTION holds the codes "LEGAL10Y" and "GENERAL05Y", assumed until the bank retention schedule arrives (DL26), and LOV-STAGE, LOV-DOC-SOURCE, LOV-REVIEW, LOV-CUSTODY, LOV-OCR-STATUS, LOV-INTAKE-REVIEW, LOV-INTAKE-MATCH, LOV-SCAN-RESULT and LOV-EXTRACT-STATUS hold the values of TSD P5 T3.2. They are read through the reference-data contract of rwb-case (DP-07, C RWB-P3-E1043-CON) and never copied into `rwb_document`.
- The DEV storage account and the DEV Blob containers of the sandbox exist and accept writes from the build. Their names and the location of the container holding the write-once legal types are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1053; ASM-2001); the running containers named in FSD P5 A2.1 are "rwb-docs" and "rwb-docs-legal".
- The number of documents a synthetic case holds beyond the one per agreed type, and the number of versions a seeded document carries, are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1051; ASM-1999); this story fixes one document per agreed type at doc_version 1 on every synthetic case and treats any further document as a parameter.
- The file name pattern of the synthetic PDFs the estate seeder writes to Blob is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1052; ASM-2000).
- The count of held intake items per exception shape, and the pages each held item carries, are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1054; ASM-2002); FSD P5 AC-P5-007-01 fixes only the 180-document OCR sample, 30 of each type, which is the sample of the OCR story and not the case estate.
- The login is the rwb-document login (DP-02), and the DEV-only read-only role keeps the legacy name `rwb_sandbox_read`; both names are Not specified in the source documents for the target schema (GAP-1053; ASM-2001).
- The seed reads no `v_ace_*` view, no `public` table and no table of another service (DP-05 applies here as a prohibition), and it evaluates no rule (DP-04 as a prohibition): the personal-data pattern test of legacy AC7 is a value test on a seeded column, not a Drools decision.
- The document store, the upload, the OCR, the classification, the extraction, the review queue and the retention job are other stories of this service (RWB-P5-E1024-APP, RWB-P5-E1049-APP, RWB-P5-E1052-APP and their siblings); this story seeds the rows they read and changes none of them.

##### 4. Flow

1. The sandbox build of RWB-P1-E1065-CON creates the DEV database `rwb_sandbox`, applies the ACE-shaped test double and the per-service migrations in order, and reaches the `rwb_document` step with empty document tables and the `rwb_document` baseline in place.
2. The rwb-document migration `V1065_1__document_estate_seed.sql` applies the type table in one transaction: 6 `document_type` rows at table version "DOCTYPE-2026.11" with valid_from 30 November 2026, each with its label, its write-once flag, its retention class, its field definitions and its classification threshold.
3. DocumentTypeSeeder checks the written rows against the lists read through the reference-data contract: every retention class is in LOV-RETENTION, every field definition names a field of the type, and exactly one table version is in force.
4. DocumentEstateSeeder reads the case list from the rwb-source-data contract fixture and writes one `document` row per agreed type on every synthetic case with case_id, document_type, source, doc_version 1, review_status, retention_class and write_once taken from its type row, content_sha256 over the synthetic file, and a storage_ref pointing at the file it writes to the DEV Blob container.
5. The seed writes the same file content for the same case, seed value and type, so the content_sha256 of a seeded document is stable across rebuilds.
6. DocumentFieldSeeder writes one `document_field` row per field definition of the stored document with field_name, extracted_value, confidence and extractor_version; the value comes from the deterministic value factory with the seed, and the seeder masks an identity number and then runs the national ID check before it commits.
7. HeldIntakeSeeder writes at least one `document_intake` row per held shape with source, file_name, received_at, file_sha256, scan_result, ocr_status, ocr_attempts, page_count, predicted_type, classification_confidence, match_status, extract_status and review_reason, and one `document_text` row per page with page_no, text_content and quality.
8. ChecklistSeeder writes the `document_checklist_item` rows of checklist version "CHK-2026.11" for the stages and their required types with required and sort_order, then one `case_document_check` row for case "RW-2026-000001" with checklist_version, required_count, present_count, missing_types, complete and checked_at.
9. DocumentEstateSeeder writes one `document_custody` movement for an original document (from_location and to_location from LOV-CUSTODY, the holder and the due back date) and one `retention_action` row for the appraisal report stored on 1 November 2021 (run_month "2026-12", action "ARCHIVED", the decision record of FSD P5 AC-ALT-P5-017-02).
10. The retention action carries one local decision record written through the decision-record library, first in the transaction, with the decision code "DOCRET", the document, the class "GENERAL05Y", the retention version "RET-2026.11" and the expiry date 1 November 2026; the entry stays in `rwb_document`.
11. DocumentSeedVerifier reads the whole estate back: the six types at one table version, one document per agreed type per case of the fixture, one field row per field definition with a confidence, no extracted value matching the national ID pattern, the held items with their pages, the custody and retention rows, every storage_ref present in the container, and the row count per table; a failure fails the build and the previous sandbox stays in use.
12. The build grants the DEV-only read-only role `rwb_sandbox_read` SELECT on the schema and publishes the build result with the row count per table; the DEV service serves the seeded estate through the P5 reads of section 12.1.
13. The DEV sandbox has no Kafka, so no relay runs and no event leaves it; the document rows and the seeded retention action stay in `rwb_document`, and a squad that needs a document event uses the SIT environment built by RWB-ITG-E1065-ITG.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A seeded type row has no `valid_from`, no `table_version`, or a retention class that is not in LOV-RETENTION | The sandbox build fails naming the row and the value; the previous sandbox stays in use | None (pipeline result) | AC1 |
| X2 | The same seed value and the same case list run twice on a rebuilt database | The same types, the same document rows per type and the same content_sha256 are written, with no row of the previous build left | None | AC5 |
| X3 | A seeded document row names a storage_ref that does not exist in the DEV container | The build fails naming the table, the row and the storage_ref; the document is not published | None (pipeline result) | AC2 |
| X4 | A seeded extracted value matches the 13-digit national ID pattern with a valid check digit | The build fails naming `document_field.extracted_value` and the document; no sandbox is published from that build | None (pipeline result) | AC3 |
| X5 | A held intake item has no review_reason, or no page text | The build fails naming the intake item and the review_reason column; the held shape is not published | None (pipeline result) | AC4 |
| X6 | A reader holding `rwb_sandbox_read` tries to change a seeded row | The write is refused by the database; the row is unchanged | None (database error) | AC6 |
| X7 | The seed writes a row into `public`, into a `v_ace_*` view or into another service's schema | The build fails naming the object; the seed writes only schema `rwb_document` | None (pipeline result) | AC7 |
| X8 | A case ID used by the seed is absent from the case list of the fixture | The build fails naming the case and the table; no document is written for a case the sandbox does not hold | None (pipeline result) | AC2, AC7 |
| X9 | A write-once document is changed through the DEV service or directly in the container | The change is refused; the file hash and the document row are unchanged | MSG-P5-002 | AC2 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against the `rwb_document` baseline and the published RWB-P1-E1065-CON fixture. It reads no ACE view, calls no other service at run time and adds no dependency of its own |
| Negotiable | The number of documents per case beyond one per type, the synthetic file pattern, the container names and the held item count are parameters and rows; the story fixes the migration, the seeders, the verifier and the gate, and writes no type code, class or list value in code |
| Valuable | Every squad can open a seeded case, see its documents with their fields and confidence, open a held item and read a retention action in DEV from Day 1, with no production data |
| Estimable | One migration, one repeatable companion, six seeders, one verifier and one grant script |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests, as a secondary slice of the legacy key |
| Testable | Every criterion in section 7 is one automated test over the seeded schema, with the case list and the lists stubbed |

The eight criteria above are new and test only this deliverable: the document estate of the DEV sandbox — the six types at the version in force, one document per agreed type per case, their fields and extracted values, the held intake items with their text, the checklist and completeness rows, the custody and retention rows, the personal-data gate on `document_field.extracted_value` and the DEV read-only role's read. No legacy criterion text is copied into this section. The legacy criteria AC1 to AC9 of RWB-E1-065 are owned elsewhere: the schema, the dictionary, the case volumes, the exception shapes and the verifier of the whole sandbox by RWB-P1-E1065-CON and RWB-P1-E1065-APP; legacy AC1's document sentence, legacy AC7's `document_field.extracted_value` gate and legacy BR3 are the three lines answered here.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | No production data in DEV: the sandbox holds synthetic documents, synthetic field values and synthetic file references only (legacy BR1) | NFR-045; CTL-11; legacy BR1 |
| BR2 | The sandbox is built from the same DDL as SIT: here that means the per-service migration applied after the `rwb_document` baseline, at the table version in force (legacy BR2) | Legacy RWB-E1-065 BR2; DP-15; TSD P5 T3.1 |
| BR3 | Values come from the data dictionary and the lists of values, never from code: the six type codes, their fields, the write-once flags, the retention classes and the checklist rows are rows or list values (legacy BR3) | sys_fields; lov_value; Principle 1; FSD P5 A2.3; TSD P5 T3.1, T3.2 |
| BR4 | Every seeded document carries the write-once flag and the retention class of its type at the version in force, so the DEV sandbox can show the write-once refusal and the retention class of a document | FSD P5 A2.1, A2.17 (AC-ALT-P5-001-01, AC-ALT-P5-017-01); TSD P5 T3.1 (DF-DOC-009, DF-DOC-010); NFR-028, NFR-029 |
| BR5 | The seeded estate is written in the owner's schema `rwb_document` only: no `v_ace_*` view, no `public` table and no table of another service is read or written by this seed (DP-01) | Architecture v5 slides 16, 20 and 41; DP-01 |
| BR6 | Every role has a test identity before it has real users: here the DEV read-only role `rwb_sandbox_read` over the seeded schema, with no role and no person name written in `rwb_document` (legacy BR6) | DL39; legacy BR6 |
| BR7 | The seeded estate is applied by the per-service Flyway sequence, versioned and repeatable, and it writes the one table version in force rather than a version chosen in code (DP-15, DP-07) | DP-15; DP-07; FSD P5 AC-ALT-P5-003-01 |
| BR8 | There is no copy and no load table: the Workbench reads source data only through the source-data contract, and this slice reads the case IDs from that contract's fixture (legacy BR8) | D-RCV-35; ADR-010; DP-05; legacy BR8 |
| BR9 | A clear identity number is allowed only in the ACE-shaped tables; schema `rwb_document` holds masked or synthetic values only (legacy BR9) | D-RCV-35 U4; CTL-11; legacy BR9 |

The four document-specific statements are BR4, BR5, BR7 and the retention part of BR1. BR4 turns the type table into behaviour on every seeded row: `document.write_once` and `document.retention_class` (DF-DOC-009, DF-DOC-010) are copied from `document_type` when the row is written, so a squad sees "LEGAL10Y" and true on a court notice and "GENERAL05Y" and false on an appraisal report without any rule running in DEV. BR5 keeps the estate inside the one schema the service owns, so no squad's test depends on another service's rows and no seeded row can be mistaken for an ACE row. BR7 is what makes a rebuild comparable with SIT: the same migration family, applied in the same order, writing the table version that the type table says is in force. The retention rows of the estate — the class on each document and the one `retention_action` row with its decision record — make the retention check demonstrable before JOB-17 runs anywhere.

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| no sandbox in DEV | the sandbox build of RWB-P1-E1065-CON starts | A merge to main that changes the ACE DDL, a recovery migration or the dictionary, or a manual start | Building |
| Building | the migrations and the seeders finish and the verifier passes | Every check of section 4 step 11 passes | Published |
| Building | a seeder or the verifier fails | A type row, a storage_ref, an extracted value, a held item or a case ID fails its check | Failed, and the previous sandbox stays in use |
| Published | the next build is published | The same database is renamed for the new build | Published with the rows of the new build only |

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| a document written by the seed | the estate seeder commits the file and the row | The file is in the DEV container and its `content_sha256` is on the row | state "STORED", doc_version 1 |
| a held intake item written by the seed | the seeder commits the item and its pages | The item carries a review_reason of LOV-INTAKE-REVIEW | ocr_status "DONE" (or "RESCAN" where the synthetic page quality is below the threshold) and match_status of LOV-INTAKE-MATCH |
| a document of class "GENERAL05Y" stored on 1 November 2021 | the seeded retention action is written | No legal hold covers the document | one `retention_action` row with action "ARCHIVED", run_month "2026-12" and its decision record |

The document states and the held item states above are data the seed writes, not a state machine of this story: the document life (COPY_PENDING, STORED, ARCHIVED), the OCR status and the match status are moved by the store, the OCR pipeline and the retention job of this service (RWB-P5-E1024-APP, RWB-P5-E1049-APP, RWB-P5-E1052-APP). The sandbox build state is the only state this story moves, and it moves it through the pipeline of RWB-P1-E1065-CON, never through the service.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| rwb-document service identity (the rwb-document login, DP-02) | Runs the migration and the seeders, reads and writes the ten tables of `rwb_document`, writes the one local decision record and serves the seeded rows through the P5 reads |
| RW-TRIBE, tribe lead and squad members | Read and extract the sandbox through `rwb_sandbox_read`, and open a seeded case, its documents, a held item and its checklist through the DEV service |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Owns the sandbox database and the pipeline stage that calls this migration; owns the DEV container grant and the retirement of the read-only role |
| Test identities per role | Call the DEV service against the seeded estate with their role's rights, as RWB-P4-E1065-APP seeds them |
| ACE team lead and ACE DBA | Own the DDL of the ACE-shaped test double and the 14 Tier 2 tables; that DDL is used by RWB-P1-E1065-CON and is not written, read or changed here |
| Decision-record library identity | Writes the one local decision record of the seeded retention action, with its sequence and hash link; no relay runs in the sandbox (DP-03) |
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | Prepares and approves the type table version that the sandbox mirrors; in the sandbox the same rows are written by the migration, and no approval is taken in DEV |

The per-service login name and the DEV-only read-only role are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1053; ASM-2001); the story keeps the legacy name `rwb_sandbox_read` for the read-only role and "the rwb-document login (DP-02)" for the service. The refusal shapes a role meets are MSG-P4-002 when the role holds no right in the Documents capability area and MSG-P4-003 when the case is outside the caller's scope; both are answered by rwb-access and the guard, not by the seed. No identity of this story may change a seeded row, and the role list, the capability letters and the scope values are rows of RWB-P4-E1065-APP, not of `rwb_document`.

The seed writes the ten tables of `rwb_document` and the one local decision record, and nothing else: no case row, no ACE row, no role row, no `lov_value` row and no reference row of another service is written here. `document_hub_parameter` keeps its schema but its rows arrive with their own load stories. The ACE-shaped tables (the 22 Tier 1 and the 14 Tier 2 tables) and the 30 `v_ace_*` views belong to RWB-P1-E1065-CON and are never written by this slice; the seed reads no view and no `public` table, and it takes the case IDs from the contract fixture instead of from a case table. `document.party_id` (DF-DOC-003) is the ACE customer business key and no foreign key backs it; FSD P5 A2.3 calls the same field `document.person_key`. Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 and the TSD P5 field ranges above.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None at run time. The seed is a migration and the estate is read with SQL; the reads the squads use are SQL through `rwb_sandbox_read` and the DEV service. The DEV service serves the seeded estate through the P5 operations of appendix T-A on the normal base `/api/recovery/document/v1`, and this slice adds no path, no query parameter and no response field:

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}/documents` | List the documents on a seeded case, with type, source, version and retention class | Documents R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/documents/{documentId}` | Read a seeded document's metadata, versions and extracted fields | Documents R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/documents/{documentId}/content` | Download the synthetic file the row points at | Documents R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}/document-checklist` | Read the required types of the case with present counts, from the seeded checklist items and the check row | Documents R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/documents` | Search the seeded documents by type, date, extracted field and free text | Documents R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/review-items` | List the held intake items and the documents with fields in review | Documents R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/intake-items/{intakeItemId}` | Read one held item with its OCR text, candidates and extracted fields | Documents R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/content` | Download the file of a held item | Documents R, scope applied | Not applicable |

The write operations of appendix T-A (API-P5-001, API-P5-005, API-P5-006, API-P5-007, API-P5-013, API-P5-014, API-P5-015, API-P5-016, API-P5-017) are the surface of the store, the review, the custody and the generation stories of this service; this story seeds the rows they act on and changes none of them. Every endpoint declares the Documents capability area and its right (TSD P5 T6.1, T6.2), which is why a role without the right is refused before any seeded row is read.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None at run time. This story answers from its own schema and calls no service: the case list it needs arrives as a fixture of RWB-P1-E1065-CON, and the lists it validates against arrive as a fixture of the rwb-case reference-data contract (DP-07).

Two contracts are consumed as fixtures only. RWB-P1-E1065-CON fixes the DEV sandbox build this migration runs inside: database `rwb_sandbox`, seed `20261128`, the migration order after the baseline, the case list of the seed and the build result the pipeline publishes. The rwb-case reference-data contract returns LOV-RETENTION, LOV-STAGE, LOV-DOC-SOURCE, LOV-REVIEW, LOV-CUSTODY, LOV-OCR-STATUS, LOV-INTAKE-REVIEW, LOV-INTAKE-MATCH, LOV-SCAN-RESULT and LOV-EXTRACT-STATUS, so the story builds and proves every criterion before either service is live in DEV.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The DEV sandbox has no Kafka broker, so nothing is produced and no outbox relay runs: DP-09 is not a pattern of this story and the seed writes no `outbox_event` row. In a running environment the store publishes `DocumentStored` (event 16) and the extraction publishes `DocumentFieldsExtracted` (event 17) on `rwb.document.events.v1`, which is the behaviour of RWB-P5-E1024-APP and RWB-P5-E1053-APP; here the seeded documents announce nothing.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. A migration consumes no topic, the seed is the file and the fixture, and the DEV profile wires no consumer group into `rwb_document`.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The seed is a migration and its seeders run in the build thread; this story starts no `DocumentIntakeWorkflow`, no activity and holds no Temporal worker of its own (Architecture v5 slide 16). The sandbox build stage that calls this migration is a pipeline stage of RWB-P1-E1065-CON, not a workflow of this service.

DP-04 applies as a prohibition here: this story evaluates no decision table. The national ID check of the personal-data gate is a value test on `document_field.extracted_value`, not a DRL rule, and the seed writes no rule package, no workbook and no decision table.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The two jobs of rwb-document are JOB-12 Document intake (every 15 minutes) and JOB-17 Retention (monthly, first Sunday), and they belong to RWB-P5-E1049-APP and RWB-P5-E1052-APP (Architecture v5 slide 44). The build stage that calls this migration is a pipeline stage of RWB-P1-E1065-CON, not a Schedule of this service.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| document | P5 (`rwb_document`) | One row per synthetic document, each row synthetic |
| document_field | P5 (`rwb_document`) | One row per field definition per document, with a synthetic extracted value |
| document_custody | P5 (`rwb_document`) | One synthetic movement so the custody read is demonstrable |
| document_type | P5 (`rwb_document`) | The six rows at "DOCTYPE-2026.11", written by this seed and by RWB-P5-E1025-APP in a running environment |
| document_checklist_item | P5 (`rwb_document`) | The checklist rows of "CHK-2026.11", synthetic but the same shape as the loaded version |
| case_document_check | P5 (`rwb_document`) | One synthetic completeness row for case "RW-2026-000001" |
| document_intake | P5 (`rwb_document`) | The held synthetic items and their pages |
| document_text | P5 (`rwb_document`) | The OCR text of the held items' pages |
| retention_action | P5 (`rwb_document`) | One synthetic action of the seeded appraisal report, with its decision record |
| document_hub_parameter | P5 (`rwb_document`) | Present in the schema and not written by this story |
| local decision record | P5 rows in `rwb_document`, written through the P7 decision-record library | One entry for the seeded retention action, with no relay |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_document` | Present in the schema and not written by this story, because no event leaves the sandbox |

rwb-document reads no table of another service and holds no foreign key across services (DP-01); `recovery_case` is reached only as a case ID value from the fixture, and `lov_value` and the reference tables belong to rwb-case (P3) and reach this story only through the reference-data contract (DP-07). Every row in this table, in this sandbox, is synthetic: no row of a running environment is copied into `rwb_document` and no row of `rwb_document` is promoted out of DEV.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| RWB-P1-E1065-CON fixture | The P1 contract of this legacy key | The DEV sandbox build result for seed `20261128`: database `rwb_sandbox`, schema `rwb_document` after the baseline, the migration order, the case list with case `RW-2026-000001` and the held shapes |
| reference-data fake (RWB-P3-E1043-CON) | DP-07 | LOV-RETENTION with LEGAL10Y and GENERAL05Y, LOV-STAGE, LOV-DOC-SOURCE, LOV-REVIEW, LOV-CUSTODY, LOV-SCAN-RESULT, LOV-OCR-STATUS, LOV-INTAKE-MATCH, LOV-INTAKE-REVIEW and LOV-EXTRACT-STATUS of TSD P5 T3.2 |
| Blob container stub | The DEV file store | A container that accepts the synthetic files and returns their hash, and a container that refuses a write for the storage_ref path (X3) |
| decision-record library stub | DP-03 | A local chain that accepts the seeded entry, and a stopped chain that fails the build before a row is published |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | None outbound; the DEV service serves the eight reads of section 12.1 on `/api/recovery/document/v1` | The seed calls no service; the case list and the lists arrive as fixtures; one hop and 2 s timeout on the inbound read |
| Kafka | None | No topic produced and none consumed in the DEV sandbox; DP-09 is not a pattern of this story |
| Temporal | None | No workflow, no activity and no Schedule in this story |
| File | The synthetic documents of the estate | One file per seeded document in the DEV Blob container, plus the files of the held intake items; the write-once legal types go to the legal container |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document`, module `sandboxseed`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document.sandboxseed`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

This is a secondary slice: it adds no new build dependency of its own. Metadata "Depends on (build)" stays `None` and "Contract dependencies" stays `RWB-P1-E1065-CON` exactly as the Work Package fixes them, and the platform contract libraries of DP-03, DP-04, DP-07, DP-15 and DP-19 arrive with the baseline, not with this story.

DP-01 is the first rule of the seed: every row lands in `rwb_document`, the type table is read from there, and the case ID is a value from the fixture, never a row read from another schema.

DP-03 applies as the local decision record written for the seeded retention action: the one `retention_action` row of the appraisal report carries one entry written through the decision-record library, with the decision code "DOCRET", the class "GENERAL05Y", the retention version "RET-2026.11" and the expiry date of FSD P5 AC-ALT-P5-017-02; the entry stays in `rwb_document` because no relay runs.

DP-04 applies as a prohibition: this seed evaluates no rule. The personal-data gate is a value test on `document_field.extracted_value`, and no DRL, workbook or rule package is written or read by the seed.

DP-05 applies as a prohibition: the seed reads no `v_ace_*` view and no `public` table. The case list, the held shapes and the build result arrive from the RWB-P1-E1065-CON fixture, so the estate can be built before the ACE views exist in DEV.

DP-07 is the type and list read: the six type codes are rows of `document_type`, the retention classes of those rows are checked against LOV-RETENTION, and the checklist, source, review, custody, scan, OCR, match and extract values are checked against their lists, all read once per build through the rwb-case reference-data contract and never copied into `rwb_document`.

DP-15 is the per-service Flyway sequence that carries the seed: `V1065_1__document_estate_seed.sql` runs after the `rwb_document` baseline and before the build is renamed, and `R__document_estate_seed_rebuild.sql` re-applies the same rows on a rebuild.

DP-13 is the base of the DEV service: the seeded estate is served at `/api/recovery/document/v1`, and the legacy `/api/recovery/v1` shape is not used by this story.

DP-19 is the route the screens use in DEV: SCR-30 Case documents and SCR-31 Document review queue reach the seeded rows through the gateway-bff composite route, one hop to rwb-document.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| DocumentTypeSeeder | Service | Writes the six `document_type` rows at "DOCTYPE-2026.11" with their field definitions, write-once flags, retention classes, valid_from and table_version; refuses a row outside LOV-RETENTION or without a version |
| DocumentEstateSeeder | Service | Writes one `document` row per agreed type on every case of the fixture with its storage_ref, content_sha256 and the write_once and retention_class of its type; writes the synthetic files to Blob; writes the custody movement and the one retention action |
| DocumentFieldSeeder | Service | Writes one `document_field` row per field definition with a deterministic extracted_value and a confidence, masks an identity number, and runs the national ID check before commit |
| HeldIntakeSeeder | Service | Writes the held `document_intake` items with their review reason, status and file hash, and their `document_text` pages |
| ChecklistSeeder | Service | Writes the `document_checklist_item` rows of "CHK-2026.11" and the `case_document_check` row of case "RW-2026-000001" |
| DocumentSeedVerifier | Service | Reads the whole estate back: one table version, one document per agreed type per case, one field row per field definition, the pattern scan, the held items and pages, the custody, retention and checklist rows, every storage_ref present, and the row count per table |
| DevGrantScript | Script | Grants SELECT on schema `rwb_document` to `rwb_sandbox_read`, with no UPDATE, no DELETE and no access to the local decision-record table |

**Database and migrations**

- Writes the ten tables of `rwb_document` and the one local decision record; writes no other table and reads no other schema (DP-01).
- Migration in this story: `V1065_1__document_estate_seed.sql`, the versioned per-service migration that carries the type rows and the estate, run after the `rwb_document` baseline and inside the build order of RWB-P1-E1065-CON.
- Its companion `R__document_estate_seed_rebuild.sql` is the repeatable migration that writes the same rows again from the same seed value and the same fixture, so a rebuilt sandbox holds the same counts and the same `content_sha256` values (AC5).
- The seed is idempotent by construction: the repeatable migration clears the estate tables it writes and writes them again from the seed value, deletes nothing outside those tables, and refuses a type row that belongs to two table versions.
- No column, index or constraint is added for a case, an ACE value or an identity; the case ID is a value and the customer key is a business key with no foreign key.

**Configuration and reference data**

- `rwb.document.sandbox.seed=20261128` is the seed value of the deterministic value factory.
- `rwb.document.sandbox.type-table-version=DOCTYPE-2026.11` is the table version the seed writes, the version in force from 30 November 2026 (FSD P5 AC-ALT-P5-003-01).
- `rwb.document.sandbox.documents-per-case` is the number of documents beyond the one per agreed type; the value is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1051; ASM-1999) and the story fixes one per type when it is unset.
- `rwb.document.sandbox.synthetic-file-pattern` is the file name pattern of the synthetic PDFs; the value is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1052; ASM-2000).
- `rwb.document.sandbox.container` and `rwb.document.sandbox.legal-container` name the DEV containers; their names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1053; ASM-2001) and the running names of FSD P5 A2.1 are "rwb-docs" and "rwb-docs-legal".
- `rwb.document.sandbox.held-intake-per-shape` is the count of held items per shape; the value is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1054; ASM-2002) and the story fixes at least one per shape.
- The type codes, fields, write-once flags, retention classes and checklist rows are rows of the seed file and the type table; the retention, stage, source, review, custody, scan, OCR, match and extract values are compared with the lists read through the rwb-case reference-data contract (DP-07), and no list is kept in `rwb_document`.
- The login is the rwb-document login (DP-02) and the DEV-only read-only role keeps the legacy name `rwb_sandbox_read`; both are Not specified in the source documents for the target schema (GAP-1053; ASM-2001).
- The feature switch is `rwb.document.sandbox-estate`, read as a parameter: on in the DEV profile only; off means the seed does not apply and the document tables stay empty, never half filled.

**Build steps**

1. Value factory and `DocumentTypeSeeder` over the six types, with a test per list violation (an unknown retention class, a missing valid_from, a second table version) and a test that no type code, class or field name appears in the Java source.
2. `V1065_1__document_estate_seed.sql` and `R__document_estate_seed_rebuild.sql`, with the read-back of AC1 and the same-seed test of AC5.
3. `DocumentEstateSeeder` over the case list of the fixture, with the per-type loop, the Blob write, the storage_ref check and the write_once and retention_class copy; tests for AC2.
4. `DocumentFieldSeeder` with the field definitions of each type, the deterministic value per field, the confidence, the identity mask and the national ID check; tests for AC3.
5. `HeldIntakeSeeder` over the held shapes with the review reason, the status, the file hash and the page text; test for AC4.
6. `ChecklistSeeder` over "CHK-2026.11" and the completeness row of case "RW-2026-000001"; tests for AC4.
7. `DocumentSeedVerifier` with every check of its row above, including the pattern scan and the storage_ref check, and the decision record of the one retention action; tests for AC3, AC5 and AC8.
8. `DevGrantScript` for `rwb_sandbox_read`: SELECT on the schema and no UPDATE, no DELETE and no SELECT on the decision-record table; test for AC6.
9. Contract-fake run of RWB-P1-E1065-CON and the reference data, so the story builds and proves every criterion before rwb-source-data and rwb-case are live in DEV; test for AC7.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.document.sandbox-estate`, read as a parameter; off leaves the tables empty and publishes nothing.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the contract tests of RWB-P1-E1065-CON stay green, a rebuilt DEV sandbox holds the six types at "DOCTYPE-2026.11", one document per agreed type on every synthetic case with its fields and no clear national ID in `document_field.extracted_value`, the held items, the checklist and completeness rows, one custody movement and one retention action with its local decision record, and `rwb_sandbox_read` reads the schema without being able to change it.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller's role holds no right in the Documents capability area | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The case of the read is absent or outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P5-002 | A write-once document is changed through the DEV service or the container | Legal documents cannot be changed. Add a new version instead. |
| MSG-P5-003 | A document with fields below the confidence threshold is opened | Some fields need checking. The document is in the review queue. |

Seed failures are reported in the pipeline result with the table and the column named: a type row outside LOV-RETENTION, a missing valid_from or table_version, a storage_ref absent from the container, an extracted value that matches the national ID pattern, a held item without a review reason and a case ID absent from the fixture each fail the build with the row and the column, and no user message applies. For MSG-P4-002 in this story, {action} names the action the caller tried — for example "open the case documents" — and never a case fact, a field value or a role name.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story. SCR-30 Case documents — documents on a case by type, with the extracted fields and versions (FSD P5 Screens; first in E1) — will show the six types, their confidence and their retention class that this seed writes, and SCR-31 Document review queue will show the held intake items and their pages, so both screens are demonstrable in DEV before a real scan and before SCR-31 is built. The screens themselves belong to RWB-P5-E1026-APP and the store, OCR and review stories of this service.

Both screens reach the estate only through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), which calls rwb-document for the documents and rwb-access for the decision, one hop each. The route specification and the field-level masking of the composite route are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1053; ASM-2001).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the type codes, the fields, the write-once flags, the retention classes, the checklist rows, the seed value, the table version, the per-case count, the file pattern and the container names are rows, list values, parameters or the fixture. No type code, class or list value appears in Java, and the verifier fails a build whose seed names a retention class outside LOV-RETENTION.
- Synthetic only, and no clear personal value in `rwb_document`: every name, identifier and extracted value is synthetic, an identity number is masked, and the pattern scan blocks a value that looks real in `document_field.extracted_value`, in every other seeded text column and in the OCR text of a held item. A clear identity number in the ACE-shaped tables is allowed there and is not this slice's data.
- The verifier gate stands between the seed and the squads: a build that fails any check of section 4 step 11 publishes no sandbox, and the previous sandbox stays in use, so no squad ever reads a half-seeded estate.
- No cross-schema write and no cross-schema read: `rwb_document` holds no foreign key into another schema and no copy of a case, a list value or an ACE row (DP-01); the case IDs come from the RWB-P1-E1065-CON fixture and the lists from the reference-data contract (DP-07), and the ACE-shaped tables and the 30 views belong to RWB-P1-E1065-CON.
- No event leaves the sandbox: the seeded retention action carries one local decision record and no relay, and no `outbox_event` row is written (DP-03, and DP-09 is not a pattern of this story).
- One owner for retention and write-once: the seed copies the class and the flag from the type table and never decides a retention period or a hold; the retention job of RWB-P5-E1052-APP acts on the rows and the store of RWB-P5-E1024-APP enforces the write-once refusal.
- The seed is a per-service Flyway migration in `rwb_document`, versioned and repeatable, and no migration of this service touches another service's schema or the shared baseline (DP-15).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-065 for the ACE database work of rwb-source-data. The single `recovery` schema of the monolith becomes three schemas of one DEV database on the one ACE PostgreSQL server — `public` as the ACE test double, `recovery` for the 30 read-only `v_ace_*` views and `rwb_source_data` for this service's own tables and the four extension tables — with one read-only role `rwb_sandbox_read` and a deployment gate that refuses any target other than DEV (DP-01, DP-02; Architecture v5 slides 8, 9, 29 and 41). The legacy build's database create, DDL apply, verifier, rename and advisory lock move here as database objects and checks. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As an **ACE database engineer**, I want **the sandbox database `rwb_sandbox` of rwb-source-data created from the same DDL as SIT with its three schemas and its read-only role, the ACE-shaped tables held in schema `public` as a test double with synthetic rows only, the grants that give `rwb_sandbox_read` SELECT on schema `recovery` and schema `rwb_source_data` and nothing else, a deployment gate that refuses any target other than DEV, a data-pattern check that refuses a clear identity number outside `public`, and a build that runs in `rwb_sandbox_next`, verifies, then renames under an advisory lock**, so that **the sandbox is one DEV database per service release, a breach is refused by the database and the pipeline instead of by a review, and a failed build never leaves a half-built sandbox behind**.

This is the database slice of legacy RWB-E1-065. It delivers:

- the database `rwb_sandbox` and the build database `rwb_sandbox_next`, with schema `public`, schema `recovery` and schema `rwb_source_data`;
- the read-only role `rwb_sandbox_read` and its grant set: SELECT on schema `recovery` and schema `rwb_source_data`, no INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE, no grant on schema `public`, PUBLIC empty;
- the DEV-only deployment gate and the synthetic-rows-only rule for the ACE-shaped test double;
- the data-pattern check over every column tagged `is_personal` outside schema `public`, and the check that the 20 absent tables exist in no schema of the database;
- the build sequence: create `rwb_sandbox_next`, apply the DDL set, seed, verify, rename, grant, under one PostgreSQL advisory lock;
- the assertion of the four extension tables, the 30 views and the 122 object and 1,366 field dictionary rows that three sibling stories deliver, and no re-creation of any of them.

It builds no generator, no verifier logic and no export tool: those are RWB-P1-E1065-APP. It creates no view, no extension table and no service table: RWB-P1-E1069-APP, RWB-P1-E1069-DB and RWB-P1-E1001-APP deliver them. It writes no application code and no REST operation.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story asked one pipeline to stand up one schema of one database and prove it with a verifier and a rename. In the target the sandbox is one service's, on the one ACE PostgreSQL server, beside 19 service schemas, and the ownership rule is enforced by grants and not by separate servers (Architecture v5 slide 29). That changes the work from "build a schema" to "build a database whose three schemas each have one owner and one audience": schema `public` belongs to ACE and is only ever a test double, schema `recovery` holds the 30 views that only rwb-source-data may read, and schema `rwb_source_data` holds this service's own tables and the four extension tables.

The grant and gate half is what makes the sandbox safe to exist at all. A database that could be deployed to SIT would put synthetic ACE-shaped rows next to real ones, so the gate refuses any target but DEV. A role that could write would let a test corrupt the fixture it is testing, so the role is read only. A clear identity number anywhere but the test double would breach BR9 before anyone noticed, so the pattern check fails the build. And a build without the rename step could publish a half-built sandbox, so the verifier and the rename are one step under an advisory lock. Serves REQ-RDF-001 (the 14 data products with one system of record and one owner) and REQ-RDF-010 (no personal data outside its permitted use). The measure is the legacy one: 100 percent of pipeline runs in which the built sandbox passes every check (FSD P1 A2.1.1).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The one ACE PostgreSQL server is reachable from the pipeline, and the migration account holds the ACE DBA role for the release window, so it can create a database, create a role, and grant on schema `public` (RWB-E1-044 in the legacy set; legacy RWB-E1-065 §3).
- The per-service Flyway sequence of rwb-source-data exists with its own history table in schema `rwb_source_data`, and the baseline version has been applied on it (DP-15; RWB-PLT-E1044-CON).
- The ACE schema DDL `15 ACE DB Alignment/ACE Schema PostgreSQL v1.sql` is in the repository, and the RWB-ACE-001 DDL for the 14 Tier 2 tables is available as a fixture (DL43).
- Schema `recovery` and the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views with their three helper functions are created by RWB-P1-E1069-APP on the same sequence; this story's checks run after them.
- The four extension tables `party_ext`, `contact_point_ext`, `account_ext` and `valuation_ext` are created by RWB-P1-E1069-DB, and the 122 `sys_objects` rows and 1,366 `sys_fields` rows with them.
- The read-only role name and the database scope of the sandbox are not fixed by any source document for the 19-service target: they are read as one DEV database per service release, `rwb_sandbox` for rwb-source-data with the build database `rwb_sandbox_next`, and the role `rwb_sandbox_read`. That reading is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0503; ASM-0695).
- The credential of the role and its rotation are held by the platform DB owner, and no credential appears in a migration, a script or a runbook.
- No approval is required to run a Draft migration on a development database; the setup is released to the pipeline only after the tests of section 16 pass.

##### 4. Flow

1. The ACE database engineer confirms the highest applied version on the service sequence (the baseline) and checks that the DEV target is named in the pipeline parameters.
2. The engineer writes the deployment gate: the stage refuses any environment other than DEV and any host other than the DEV instance, before a database is created.
3. The engineer writes the database build step: create `rwb_sandbox_next` with schema `public`, schema `recovery` and schema `rwb_source_data`, owned as the ownership rule says.
4. The engineer writes the DDL apply step: the ACE schema file and the Tier 2 fixture into schema `public`, then the per-service baseline and the two view migrations into their schemas in the fixed order (DP-15).
5. The engineer writes the role step: create `rwb_sandbox_read`, grant USAGE and SELECT on schema `recovery` and schema `rwb_source_data`, grant nothing on schema `public`, revoke PUBLIC, and grant no INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE.
6. The engineer writes the two checks: the data-pattern check over every column tagged `is_personal` outside schema `public`, and the absence check over the 20 tables that left the schema.
7. The engineer writes the delivered-objects check: the 30 views compile, the four extension tables hold their 49 columns and the dictionary holds 122 objects and 1,366 fields — asserted, never re-created.
8. The pipeline runs the verifier on `rwb_sandbox_next`, then renames the database to `rwb_sandbox` under one advisory lock and re-applies the grants.
9. A failed verifier leaves `rwb_sandbox` as it was and drops `rwb_sandbox_next`; the pipeline reports the failure with the object it named.
10. The engineer records the build step, the role and the gates in the release notes of the sequence.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message |
|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The stage is pointed at a target that is not DEV | The gate stops the stage before a database is created and names the target | Pipeline error, no message id |
| X2 | A clear identity number appears outside schema `public` in a column tagged `is_personal` | The data-pattern check fails and names the schema, the table and the column | Pipeline error, no message id |
| X3 | One of the 20 absent tables exists in any schema of the database | The absence check fails and names the table and the schema | Pipeline error, no message id |
| X4 | The verifier fails on a delivered object — a view that does not compile, a missing extension table, a dictionary count that is not 122 and 1,366 | The rename does not run, the previous sandbox stays in use and `rwb_sandbox_next` is dropped | Pipeline error, no message id |
| X5 | A second build starts while one runs | The second build waits on the advisory lock and runs after the first | None |
| X6 | The role `rwb_sandbox_read` already exists | The create is skipped, the grants are re-applied and nothing changes | None |
| X7 | A session as `rwb_sandbox_read` runs an INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE | The statement is refused | SQLSTATE 42501 permission denied for schema rwb_source_data (or for the object named) |
| X8 | A session as `rwb_sandbox_read` selects from a table in schema `public` | The statement is refused | SQLSTATE 42501 permission denied for schema public |
| X9 | The rename runs while a session still holds a connection to `rwb_sandbox` | The rename waits for the connection cap and then fails cleanly; the previous sandbox stays | Pipeline error, no message id |

X1, X2, X3, X5, X7 and X8 are the legacy paths X1, X4, X6 and the access rule of RWB-E1-065 carried onto the three-schema database; X4, X6 and X9 are the paths the delivered objects, the reusable role and the rename add.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | One build step, one role step and three checks, on the service's own sequence; nothing to build against and no application code |
| Negotiable | The order of the grants and the check harness are the engineer's choice; the three schemas, the role, the gate and the two checks are fixed by this story and the contract |
| Valuable | The sandbox exists once, in DEV only, and a breach is refused by the database and the pipeline |
| Estimable | One build step, one role step, one gate, three checks and the rename under the lock |
| Small | Days, not weeks, with the catalogue checks |
| Testable | Every criterion in section 7 is one catalogue query, one refused statement with its SQLSTATE, or one pipeline run |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: The sandbox database, its three schemas and its read-only role

  Background:
    Given the one ACE PostgreSQL server and the DEV instance of it
    Given the per-service Flyway baseline of rwb-source-data has been applied on its own sequence

  Scenario: AC1 rwb_sandbox is built from the same DDL as SIT into three schemas (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the ACE schema DDL, the RWB-ACE-001 Tier 2 DDL fixture, the baseline and the two view migrations
    When the build step runs in DEV
    Then the database "rwb_sandbox_next" exists with schema "public", schema "recovery" and schema "rwb_source_data"
    Then schema "public" holds the Tier 1 tables and the 14 Tier 2 tables of the fixture
    Then schema "recovery" holds the 30 v_ace_* views and the three helper functions
    Then schema "rwb_source_data" holds this service's 13 tables and the four extension tables
    Then the login "rwb_source_data" of the service has USAGE on its own schema and SELECT on schema "recovery"
    Then no schema other than the three exists in the database

  Scenario: AC2 The ACE-shaped tables are a test double in schema public only (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the Tier 1 tables and the 14 Tier 2 tables in schema "public"
    When the catalogue is queried for their rows and for the target of the build
    Then every row in schema "public" is synthetic and no production row is loaded
    Then no table of schema "public" exists in schema "recovery" or in schema "rwb_source_data"
    Then the deployment gate refuses a target other than DEV before a database is created
    Then the pipeline records the target environment in the build report
    Then no batch job of any service loads a service table from schema "public"

  Scenario: AC3 The read-only role holds SELECT and nothing else (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the role "rwb_sandbox_read"
    When the catalogue is queried for its grants
    Then it holds USAGE and SELECT on schema "recovery" and on schema "rwb_source_data"
    Then it holds no INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE on any object of either schema
    Then it holds no privilege of any kind on schema "public"
    Then PUBLIC holds nothing on any object of the three schemas
    Then the role is mapped to the DEV group RWB-DEV-RW-TRIBE and to no other group

  Scenario: AC4 The data-pattern and absence checks refuse a breach (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given every column of the database tagged is_personal outside schema "public"
    When a generated value matches the 13-digit national ID pattern with a valid check digit
    Then the data-pattern check fails and names the schema, the table and the column
    Then a clear identity number in schema "public" is not a failure, because ACE holds it there
    When the catalogue is queried for the 20 tables that left the schema
    Then none of them exists in schema "public", schema "recovery" or schema "rwb_source_data"
    Then the build publishes no sandbox when either check fails

  Scenario: AC5 The delivered objects are present and asserted, never re-created (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the four extension tables, the 30 views and the dictionary rows delivered by their own stories
    When the verifier runs on "rwb_sandbox_next"
    Then the 30 v_ace_* views compile and each returns at least one row
    Then party_ext, contact_point_ext, account_ext and valuation_ext hold their 49 columns and their primary keys
    Then the dictionary holds 122 objects and 1,366 fields, and 49 of those fields sit on the four extension tables
    Then the build creates no view, no extension table and no dictionary row of its own
    Then a missing delivered object fails the build and no object is created to replace it

  Scenario: AC6 The build is verified, renamed and locked, and a failure leaves the previous sandbox (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a sandbox "rwb_sandbox" in use and a build of "rwb_sandbox_next"
    When the verifier passes
    Then the database is renamed to "rwb_sandbox" and the grants are re-applied in the same step
    Then the previous database is gone and no partial database remains
    When the verifier fails
    Then no rename happens, "rwb_sandbox" still answers, and "rwb_sandbox_next" is dropped
    When a second build starts while one runs
    Then the second waits on the PostgreSQL advisory lock and runs after the first
```

These six criteria are new and prove only the database artefacts in the story title: the database with its three schemas, the test double, the role and its grants, the two checks, the delivered objects and the build sequence. No legacy acceptance criterion text is repeated here. The legacy criteria these objects answer are AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC7 of RWB-E1-065 and they are owned by RWB-P1-E1065-APP; AC4, AC5, AC6, AC8 and AC9 are the verifier, the idempotency, the constraint, the boundary and the lock, and they are proven by RWB-P1-E1065-APP against these objects.

| BR1 | No production data in DEV; the sandbox holds synthetic data only and the ACE-shaped tables are a test double | legacy BR1, BR7; NFR-045; CTL-11 |
| BR2 | The sandbox is built from the same DDL as SIT: the ACE schema, the RWB-ACE-001 Tier 2 DDL fixture, the per-service baseline and the two view migrations | legacy BR2; ADR-001; DP-15 |
| BR3 | Three schemas and no more: `public` as the ACE test double, `recovery` for the 30 read-only views, `rwb_source_data` for this service's tables and the four extension tables | DP-01, DP-02, DP-05; Architecture v5 slides 15 and 29 |
| BR4 | One read-only role, `rwb_sandbox_read`: SELECT on `recovery` and on `rwb_source_data`, nothing on `public`, no write on any object, PUBLIC empty | legacy BR9; DP-02 |

**Where each rule lives in the target.** BR1, BR6 and BR9 are this story's gates and checks: the target gate, the absence check and the synthetic-only rule. BR2 is the DDL set the build applies. BR3 and BR4 are the schemas and the role this story creates, and their names come from the platform naming rule and the ownership map. BR5 is the data-pattern check. BR7 is the rename and the lock. BR8 is the delivered-objects check, which names the three sibling stories and creates nothing of theirs. The seed values, the exception shapes and the volumes are the app story's profile and do not live here; this story only gives them a database to be written into.

##### 9. State transitions

None in the runtime sense: a database has no case state machine and this story changes no business row. The states this story moves through are the build states of the sandbox and the grant states of the role.

| Item | States |
|---|---|
| the sandbox | Absent, Building in `rwb_sandbox_next`, Verified, Published as `rwb_sandbox`, Failed with the previous sandbox kept |
| the role | Absent, present and granted, present and refused with SQLSTATE 42501; never a member of another service's login role |
| a grant | Held on a schema or an object, refused with SQLSTATE 42501, or held by PUBLIC, which is a failure |
| a personal column outside `public` | Clean, or matching a pattern, which fails the build |
| one of the 20 absent tables | Absent, or present, which fails the build |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Sequencing.** rwb-source-data's Flyway sequence is owned by the platform; the V0001 baseline creates the schema, the history table and the standard record columns (DP-15). This story adds no migration of its own: it adds the build step, the role step and the checks that run around the sequence.

| Position in the build | Step | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | deployment gate | Refuse any target other than DEV and any host other than the DEV instance; record the target in the build report |
| 1 | create | Database `rwb_sandbox_next` with schema `public`, schema `recovery` and schema `rwb_source_data` |
| 2 | DDL apply | The ACE schema file and the Tier 2 fixture into `public`; the baseline and the two view migrations into their schemas in the fixed order |
| 3 | seed | The generator of RWB-P1-E1065-APP, under the seed profile of RWB-P1-E1065-CON |
| 4 | role and grants | Create `rwb_sandbox_read`, grant USAGE and SELECT on `recovery` and `rwb_source_data`, grant nothing on `public`, revoke PUBLIC, grant no write |
| 5 | checks | The personal-data pattern check, the 20-table absence check and the delivered-objects check |
| 6 | verify and publish | The verifier of RWB-P1-E1065-APP, then the rename to `rwb_sandbox` and the re-application of the grants under one advisory lock |
| 7 | failure | No rename, the previous `rwb_sandbox` kept, `rwb_sandbox_next` dropped |

The exact version numbers of the migrations this story applies are assigned by the sequence owner at build time, and no monolith version number is reused. The platform dependency of the sequence is `RWB-PLT-E1044-CON`: it is not in this story's "Depends on (build)" list, which the Work Package fixes as None, so it is recorded here as a note and not as a metadata dependency.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-02 | `recovery_svc` login | One login per service | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-01, DP-02, DP-05 and DP-15 are the subject of this story: three schemas with one owner each, one login per service, one read path and one sequence. DP-03, DP-04, DP-07, DP-13 and DP-19 are named for completeness of the pattern set: this story writes no decision record, evaluates no rule, calls no contract, serves no path and serves no screen, and their build dependencies stay with the application story.

**Grant block**

```sql
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA recovery TO rwb_sandbox_read;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA rwb_source_data TO rwb_sandbox_read;
GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA recovery TO rwb_sandbox_read;
GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA rwb_source_data TO rwb_sandbox_read;
REVOKE ALL ON SCHEMA public FROM rwb_sandbox_read;
REVOKE ALL ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC;
REVOKE ALL ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA recovery FROM PUBLIC;
REVOKE ALL ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA rwb_source_data FROM PUBLIC;
```

The `ALL TABLES` form is used here on purpose and only for the two read-only schemas: the sandbox role is a reader of the whole sandbox and holds no write, and a table added later must be readable without a second grant. The write revocation is explicit, so a later grant of `ALL` on the same schema cannot silently add a write:

```sql
REVOKE INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA recovery FROM rwb_sandbox_read;
REVOKE INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA rwb_source_data FROM rwb_sandbox_read;
```

No grantee other than `rwb_sandbox_read` appears in this block, `rwb_source_data` keeps its own DML on its own schema through the baseline, and PUBLIC receives nothing in any of the three schemas. The schema-wide SELECT is not a migration on the service sequence and grants no write, so the rule that the service login is granted one view at a time, in RWB-P1-E1069-DB, is unaffected: the sandbox reader is a DEV reader of a whole schema, the service login is the production reader of 30 named views.

**Checks**

| Check | Rule | Failure |
|---|---|---|
| `SandboxTargetGate` | The target is DEV and the host is the DEV instance | The stage stops before a database is created |
| `PersonalPatternCheck` | No column tagged `is_personal` outside `public` holds a value matching the national ID, mobile or email pattern | The build fails and names the schema, the table and the column |
| `AbsentTableCheck` | None of the 20 tables that left the schema exists in any schema | The build fails and names the table and the schema |
| `DeliveredObjectsCheck` | The 30 views compile and return a row; the four extension tables hold 49 columns; the dictionary holds 122 objects and 1,366 fields | The build fails and names the missing object |
| `SandboxGrantCheck` | `rwb_sandbox_read` holds SELECT on the two schemas and no write; PUBLIC empty; `rwb_no_grant` refused | The build fails and names the privilege |
| `SandboxBuildLock` | One advisory lock for create, verify and rename | The second build waits, then runs |

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `sandbox_build.sql` | Build script | Creates the database and the three schemas, applies the DDL and the migrations, renames and drops |
| `sandbox_role.sql` | Build script | Creates `rwb_sandbox_read`, issues the grants and the revokes, re-applied after the rename |
| `SandboxTargetGate` | Pipeline check | Refuses any target other than DEV before a database is created |
| `PersonalPatternCheck` | Pipeline check | The personal-data pattern rule over every column tagged `is_personal` outside `public` |
| `AbsentTableCheck` | Pipeline check | The 20 tables that left the schema are absent in every schema |
| `DeliveredObjectsCheck` | Pipeline check | The 30 views, the four extension tables and the dictionary counts, asserted and not created |
| `SandboxGrantCheck` | Pipeline check | The role's grants, the two refusals with SQLSTATE 42501 and PUBLIC empty |

**Build steps**

1. The `SandboxTargetGate` with a fixture pointed at a non-DEV target (AC2, AC6).
2. `sandbox_build.sql` with the create, the DDL apply, the verify, the rename and the drop-on-failure, and a failing fixture for each branch (AC1, AC6).
3. `sandbox_role.sql` with the grants, the revokes and the re-application after the rename, and a fixture that asserts no write and no privilege in `public` (AC3).
4. `PersonalPatternCheck` with an injected 13-digit value outside `public` and a clear value in `public.customer` (AC4).
5. `AbsentTableCheck` with a fixture that creates one of the 20 tables (AC4).
6. `DeliveredObjectsCheck` against the delivered-views and delivered-tables fixtures, with a missing object in each (AC5).
7. `SandboxGrantCheck` with sessions as `rwb_sandbox_read`, `rwb_source_data` and `rwb_no_grant` (AC3).
8. The repeated build on a second run for the same commit and seed, and the advisory-lock test with two builds (AC6).

**Done when.** The build applies twice without a change, the three schemas exist with their owners, `rwb_sandbox_read` holds SELECT on `recovery` and `rwb_source_data` and nothing else, the gate refuses a non-DEV target, the pattern and absence checks fail on their fixtures, a failed verifier leaves the previous sandbox and drops `rwb_sandbox_next`, and the tests in section 16 pass.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| SQLSTATE 42501 | A session as `rwb_sandbox_read` selects from schema `public` | permission denied for schema public |
| SQLSTATE 42501 | A session as `rwb_sandbox_read` runs INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE on a sandbox object | permission denied for schema rwb_source_data |
| Pipeline error, no message id | The target is not DEV | The gate names the target and the host refused |
| Pipeline error, no message id | A personal column outside `public` matches a pattern | The check names the schema, the table and the column |
| Pipeline error, no message id | One of the 20 absent tables exists | The check names the table and the schema |
| Pipeline error, no message id | A delivered object is missing | The check names the object and the story that delivers it |

These are pipeline and database texts for developers and are not part of the message standard. No `MSG-` ID of this story is new: the two texts of the access test are the legacy texts MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P4-003 raised by the guard library on the DEV service, and they are tested in RWB-P1-E1065-APP. A build failure returns no body from this story, because it has no service.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen. The result of a build is visible in the pipeline run and in the service's Flyway history (pending, applied, failed, undone, each with a version and a checksum). The platform administrator reads the build result under Platform administration R and on SCR-44 Interface and job monitor, and the data steward reads the dictionary counts of the sandbox. Nothing in this story is shown to a user directly: the sandbox is read with SQL and the export script of the app story, never through a screen.

The full legacy test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a script: the seed, the volumes, the shape count and the pattern rule are the profile of the app story and the contract; this story's scripts hold names, grants and checks only.
- No personal data in a migration, a script, a test fixture or a runbook: the test double holds synthetic rows, the pattern check blocks a real-looking value outside `public`, and the test values are synthetic.
- No read of another schema and no key into another schema: no foreign key of the sandbox crosses a schema, and no statement of this story reads another service's table (DP-01).
- One read-only role: `rwb_sandbox_read` is the only grantee of the sandbox, it holds no write, and it is mapped to one DEV group (DP-02).
- No privilege for PUBLIC anywhere, and no write granted on any object of the three schemas.
- DEV only: the gate refuses any other target before a database is created, and no copy of the sandbox is promoted.
- The delivered objects are asserted and never re-created: a missing view, extension table or dictionary row fails the build instead of being created here.
- An applied migration is never edited: a correction is a new version on the service sequence (DP-15), and a wrong grant is revoked by a later step, never by an edit.
