**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-066 for rwb-source-data. The single deployment of the monolith becomes the release of the ledger writer on its own chart, with the `rwb_source_data` sequence applied by its own migration step (DP-15), the ledger table, its two unique keys and its append-only trigger verified after the migration, the flag `rwb.dataengine.ledger-writer` gating the writer, five series and three alerts with one runbook entry each (ADR-023), and a smoke run that appends one synthetic entry and replays the same key. The ledger itself stays P1's table in `rwb_source_data` (DP-01, DP-18; the R-PREC default ruling) and no other service's schema is migrated or read. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform engineer**, I want **the ledger writer of rwb-source-data deployed from one chart on DEV, SIT and UAT with a pinned image digest and build ID, the `rwb_source_data` migration applied by its own step, the ledger table verified with its columns, its two unique keys, its append-only trigger and its index, the flag `rwb.dataengine.ledger-writer` to turn the writer on and off, five dashboard series, three alerts each with one runbook entry, and a smoke run that appends one synthetic entry and replays the same key without writing a second row**, so that **an operator can see the append rate and its failures, prove that a repeated key writes nothing, and roll back to the previous build without losing or duplicating an entry**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story assumed one process in one module: the ledger table, the writer and the incident hook were in the same deployment, so a failed append was a row in the log of the same application that took the call. In the target the writer is a service of its own, its table lives in its own schema, and the callers are a screen through gateway-bff and an event path of rwb-integration (DP-01, DP-11, DP-19; Architecture v5 slides 11, 29 and 41).

That separation is what this story makes operable. A table that is created by the wrong schema, an append-only trigger that is missing after a migration, a `case_seq` sequence with a gap because a second pod allocated the same number, or an append that fails silently in one environment are all conditions that no unit test of the writer can see, and each of them breaks the one promise of the ledger: the history has no gap. The release therefore verifies four things on every environment instead of trusting the migration once: that the ledger columns and both unique keys exist, that the append-only trigger is present and refuses an update, that a repeated `Idempotency-Key` returns the same entry and the same `caseSeq`, and that an append failure is visible on a series and raises its alert with MSG-P1-022.

Observability follows ADR-023 per service and keeps the personal-data rule of the platform: five series and three alerts carry counts, classes, codes and build IDs only, never a summary and never a contact point (Architecture v5 slide 11). The deployment also enforces the ownership boundary operationally: the release carries the `rwb_source_data` login only, applies the `rwb_source_data` migration only, and refuses any other target schema (DP-01, DP-02, DP-15).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template, the chart skeleton and the pipeline are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-LIB).
- The `rwb_source_data` schema, its login and the per-service Flyway sequence exist, delivered by RWB-PLT-NF06-DB and the baseline of RWB-P1-E1001-APP (DP-02, DP-15).
- The chart of rwb-source-data and its values files exist from the earlier P1 releases, with base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` and the ingress served by gateway-bff (DP-13, DP-19).
- The ledger migration of RWB-P1-E1066-APP is merged on the service sequence, and its version is the one this release applies; the writer and the migration ship together.
- The contract of RWB-P1-E1066-CON is published, so the smoke run can call `POST /interactions` and `GET /interactions/{entryId}` with a known shape.
- The case fake and the decision-log fake of the contract are available in the service environment, so a smoke run appends a synthetic entry without calling a live rwb-case or rwb-decision.
- The flag library is in force and the flag `rwb.dataengine.ledger-writer` is registered for the three environments.
- The platform secret store holds the `rwb_source_data` credential, and no secret appears in a values file, a chart template, a dashboard or the runbook.
- The observability platform of ADR-023 is in force, so a series can carry the environment, the release and the build ID as dimensions.
- The deployment values, the alert thresholds, the probe timings and the incident route are not given by any source: no values file, threshold, timing or routing rule for the ledger writer exists in the source set (GAP-0506; ASM-0698).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. The pipeline builds the service image and the contract jar, runs the unit, component and contract tests, scans the image and the dependencies, and publishes one chart version with one image digest.
2. The chart deploys the API deployment of rwb-source-data with the `rwb_source_data` login, the namespace `rwb-recovery`, the base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` behind gateway-bff, the build ID of the release and the flag value of the environment.
3. The migration step applies the `rwb_source_data` sequence of this release, ledger version included, and refuses to run when the target schema is not `rwb_source_data`.
4. The verification step reads the catalogue and asserts the ledger objects of 13: the eight ledger columns, the nullable `channel` and `direction`, the unique key `(case_id, case_seq)`, the unique key `(idempotency_key)`, the append-only trigger `tr_interaction_append_only` and the index `ix_interaction_case_time`.
5. The trigger step attempts one `UPDATE` and one `DELETE` on a synthetic row inside a transaction it rolls back, and fails the release when either statement succeeds.
6. The flag step sets `rwb.dataengine.ledger-writer` from the values of the environment.
7. The dashboards are published with the five series of section 11 and the environment, release and build ID as dimensions.
8. The three alerts are wired to their message identifiers and to their runbook entries: the append failure alert carries MSG-P1-022, the incident alert carries the incident code `LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED`, and the trigger alert names the missing object.
9. The smoke run appends one synthetic entry for a synthetic case against the case fake in DEV, reads it back, re-sends the same `Idempotency-Key` and confirms the same entry and the same `caseSeq`, then rolls the transaction of the update attempt back and records the result.
10. The release is promoted only when the smoke run passes; a failing smoke run leaves the previous build in force.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The chart render or the migration job fails | The deployment stays unready and the pipeline stops; no traffic is served | None | AC1 |
| X2 | The migration step is pointed at a schema other than `rwb_source_data` | The step refuses and records the refused target; no object is created | Pipeline error, no message id | AC1 |
| X3 | The migration ran but a ledger column, a unique key, the trigger or the index is missing | The verification step fails the release and names the missing object | Pipeline error, no message id | AC3 |
| X4 | The append-only trigger is missing, or an `UPDATE` or `DELETE` succeeds on a ledger row | The trigger step fails the release and the trigger alert fires | MSG-P1-022 is not used here; the alert carries no message ID and names the object (GAP-0506; ASM-0698) | AC5 |
| X5 | The append fails, or its rate passes the threshold | The failure series rises by class and the append failure alert fires with MSG-P1-022 and the build ID | MSG-P1-022 | AC4, AC5 |
| X6 | The flag is off in an environment | The writer is not deployed, the append answers as refused at the edge and no entry is written | None | AC2 |
| X7 | The smoke run replays the same key and a second row appears | The smoke run fails the release and names the case, the key and the two `caseSeq` values | Pipeline error, no message id | AC6 |
| X8 | A new build is promoted while entries are being appended | The previous build drains and the new build takes new requests; both build IDs appear on the series | None | AC1, AC4 |

X1 and X2 are the deployment paths; X3 and X4 are the four facts the release verifies instead of assuming; X5 and X8 are the observability paths of ADR-023; X6 is the flag; X7 is the one assertion that proves the idempotency of the append in a live environment.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the chart skeleton, the flag library and the observability platform; no application code is built here |
| Negotiable | Replica counts, resource sizes, probe timings, alert thresholds and the incident route are environment values |
| Valuable | Makes the append rate, its failures, its duplicates and its sequence gaps visible, and makes a rollback safe |
| Estimable | One chart, one migration step, one verification step, one trigger step, five series, three alerts and three runbook entries |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the runbook |
| Testable | Every criterion tests an artefact: the chart renders, the catalogue shows the objects, an alert fires on a synthetic metric, the smoke run replays a key |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Deployment of the interaction ledger writer for rwb-source-data

  Background:
    Given the service template chart and the platform pipeline are in force
    Given the namespace is rwb-recovery and the schema of this service is rwb_source_data
    Given the target environment is SIT

  Scenario: AC1 The writer is deployed from one chart with one digest and one build ID (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rwb-source-data chart and its values files
    When the chart is rendered for DEV, SIT and UAT
    Then each render succeeds with the chart version and the image digest pinned
    Then the deployment carries the build ID of the release and serves the base /api/recovery/source-data/v1 behind gateway-bff
    Then the release declares the rwb_source_data login and no other service's credential
    Then the migration step applies the rwb_source_data sequence and refuses a target schema other than rwb_source_data
    Then the migration carries the ledger columns, the append-only trigger and the two unique keys of the interaction table

  Scenario: AC2 The flag turns the writer on and off (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the flag rwb.dataengine.ledger-writer and its values for the three environments
    When the flag is on
    Then the writer is deployed and the append operation answers
    When the flag is off in an environment
    Then the writer is not deployed in that environment, no entry is written and no append series is emitted
    Then the flag value comes from the values file of the environment and is never hard-coded in a template

  Scenario: AC3 The ledger objects exist after the migration and a repeated run changes nothing (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the migration of this release has been applied in SIT
    When the catalogue is read for the interaction table
    Then the columns event_code, actor_type, actor_ref, source_ref, idempotency_key, case_seq, decision_log_id and corrects_entry_id exist
    Then channel and direction are nullable
    Then the unique key on (case_id, case_seq) and the unique key on (idempotency_key) exist
    Then the trigger tr_interaction_append_only exists and is enabled
    Then the index ix_interaction_case_time on (case_id, occurred_at) exists
    When the migration is applied a second time
    Then Flyway reports the version as already applied and no object, column, key or trigger changes

  Scenario: AC4 The five series carry the environment, the release and the build ID (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published dashboard of the deployment
    When a synthetic run, a set of failed appends and a duplicate key are produced
    Then the dashboard shows the append rate, the append failures by error class, the duplicate hits, the p95 latency of the append and the case_seq gaps
    Then each series carries the environment, the release and the build ID as dimensions
    Then a failed append and a case_seq gap are both visible on the dashboard before any alert is read
    Then no series carries a summary, a contact point or a case identifier beyond the case ID

  Scenario: AC5 The three alerts each link one runbook entry (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published alert rules and the runbook
    When a failing append, a raised incident and a dropped trigger are simulated
    Then the append failure alert fires with MSG-P1-022 and the build ID
    Then the incident alert fires on the incident code LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED with the case ID and the error class and no summary
    Then the trigger alert fires when tr_interaction_append_only is missing or disabled, and names the object
    Then every alert links one runbook entry with the check, the owner role and the recovery step
    Then no alert threshold, window or route is hard-coded in a chart template

  Scenario: AC6 The smoke run appends, replays and rolls back cleanly (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the deployed writer in DEV and the case fake of the contract
    When the smoke run appends one synthetic entry for a synthetic case with a fresh Idempotency-Key
    Then the answer is 201 with the stored entry and its caseSeq
    When the same key is sent again with the same body
    Then the answer carries the same entry ID and the same caseSeq and the table still holds one row
    When the release is rolled back to the previous chart version
    Then the previous build serves the append with its own build ID and no entry is lost or duplicated
```

**Target reading.** The six criteria are new, because the legacy story had no deployment section: it assumed the table, the writer and the incident hook sat in one monolith release. What they assert is the split. The migration is the ledger version of RWB-P1-E1066-APP on this service's own sequence, applied by a step that refuses any schema but `rwb_source_data` (DP-15; Architecture v5 slides 11 and 29). The table is P1's and no other service's schema is migrated or read (DP-01, DP-18). The append is reached over REST through gateway-bff and one hop, so the deployment registers a route and no direct call (DP-11, DP-19). The values, thresholds, timings and the incident route below are not given by any source and are carried as the placeholder (GAP-0506; ASM-0698).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One login, one schema and one sequence per service: the release carries the `rwb_source_data` login and migrates `rwb_source_data` only | Architecture v5 slides 11 and 29; DP-02, DP-15 |
| BR2 | The ledger table, its two unique keys and its append-only trigger are verified after every migration, on every environment, and a missing object fails the release | REQ-ILG-001; R-UNI-24; legacy RWB-E1-066 BR4 |
| BR3 | A repeated `Idempotency-Key` writes no second row and returns the same entry and the same `caseSeq` | REQ-ILG-007; DP-09; Architecture v5 slide 11 |
| BR4 | Every alert carries a message ID or a named incident code and links one runbook entry | Template and Rules §R7.2 s14; ADR-023 |
| BR5 | No environment value is hard-coded: replicas, resources, probe timings, thresholds, windows and the flag come from the values files of the environment | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR6 | Series and alert payloads carry counts, classes, codes, case IDs and build IDs only, never a summary, a contact point or an amount | Architecture v5 slide 11 (PDPA); ADR-023 |
| BR7 | The release writes no entry of its own and reads no other service's table: the smoke entry is synthetic and goes through the append with the case fake | DP-01; DP-18 |
| BR8 | A failing release never replaces a working one: the previous build stays in force until the new build passes its tests and its smoke run | DP-15 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | Chart published | The image, the chart and the contract tests pass | Deploying |
| Deploying | Migration applied and the ledger objects verified | The eight columns, the two keys, the trigger and the index are present | Ready |
| Deploying | Verification failed | A column, a key, the trigger or the index is missing | Blocked |
| Ready | Release superseded | A new chart version passes its tests and its smoke run | Rolling |
| Rolling | All pods on the new build | The previous build drains | Ready |
| Ready | Flag off | `rwb.dataengine.ledger-writer` is turned off in the environment | Not deployed |
| Ready | Smoke run failed | The append, the replay or the rollback step fails | Blocked |
| Blocked | Previous build restored | The previous chart is redeployed with its own build ID | Ready |

The ledger entry has no status and is never changed; the states above are states of the deployment and not of a row.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| DevOps engineer | Owns the chart, the values files, the pipeline stages, the dashboards and the runbook |
| Platform administrator | Owns the `rwb-recovery` namespace, the secret store, the flag library and the ingress route |
| ACE database administrator | Grants the ledger objects to the `rwb_source_data` login and confirms the migration ran on the right schema |
| Release manager | Approves the promotion of one artefact and may block it on a failing smoke run |
| On-call operator | Runs the three runbook entries and opens an incident when the append failure rate or a `case_seq` gap persists |
| RW-AUDIT | Reads the append history and the release record |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator role | Reads the series, the alerts and the runbook and receives the incident |

The release runs as the `rwb_source_data` service identity (DP-02), carried by the chart as a secret reference and never as a literal credential.

##### 11. Data

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Deployment values | Image digest, chart version, replica counts, resource requests and limits, probe paths and timings, log level, namespace, build ID, flag value, alert thresholds, windows and route (GAP-0506; ASM-0698) |
| Schema | `rwb_source_data`, migrated by its own per-service Flyway sequence; this release applies the ledger version |
| Ledger objects | The `interaction` table with `event_code`, `actor_type`, `actor_ref`, `source_ref`, `idempotency_key`, `case_seq`, `decision_log_id` and `corrects_entry_id`, a nullable `channel` and `direction`, the unique keys `(case_id, case_seq)` and `(idempotency_key)`, the trigger `tr_interaction_append_only` and the index `ix_interaction_case_time` |
| Platform library objects | `processed_event`, `idempotency_key` and `outbox_event`, created in `rwb_source_data` by the library (DP-09) |
| Series | Append rate, append failures by error class, duplicate hits, p95 latency of the append, `case_seq` gaps; dimensions environment, release, build ID |
| Alerts | Append failure rate with MSG-P1-022; the incident `LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED` with the case ID and the error class; a missing or disabled `tr_interaction_append_only` |
| Runbook entries | Append failure, ledger incident, missing trigger; each with the check, the owner role and the recovery step |
| Secrets | The `rwb_source_data` credential, from the platform secret store; no other credential is carried |
| Test data | One synthetic entry for a synthetic case in DEV, appended against the case fake with a fresh `Idempotency-Key`, and the same key replayed; no production payload is used |

The deployment topology (cluster names, node pools, replica counts, resource sizes, zone spread, ingress class and the exact probe timings) belongs to each environment and is set by the platform team in its values file; the chart exposes every one of them as a value and this story fixes only their names and the rule that they are never hard-coded (GAP-0506; ASM-0698).

**Probes.** Readiness answers healthy only after the migration has been applied on `rwb_source_data` and the API has served one request; liveness answers healthy when the process is up and its loop is responsive. Neither probe writes a ledger row and neither commits a transaction. A failing dependency is reported as not ready, never as live-and-broken.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None from this story. `POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/interactions` and `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/interactions/{entryId}` are declared by RWB-P1-E1066-CON and implemented by RWB-P1-E1066-APP, and the list read `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/interactions` is implemented by RWB-P1-E1068-APP; this deployment exposes them through the chart and the ingress and declares no path of its own. The probes are cluster-internal and are not part of the API surface.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None from the deployment. The migration step, the verification step, the trigger step and the smoke run read the catalogue and call the service under test; the chart carries no REST client of its own, no composite route and no outbound call at start-up.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The topic `rwb.source-data.events.v1` carries `AceDataReady` and `AceDataLate`, published by RWB-P1-E1013-APP, and this release publishes neither. `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` is published by the local decision-record library through the outbox when an entry is appended (DP-03, DP-09); the deployment only provides the relay the library already has.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. No consumer group is created by this release; the ledger writer is called over REST and consumes no topic (Architecture v5 slide 15).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The writer is a synchronous REST service and this release registers no workflow, activity or worker on the task queue `rwb-source-data` of namespace `rwb-recovery`.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The deployment registers no Temporal Schedule and no Quartz job.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Deployment element |
|---|---|---|
| `interaction` | P1 (rwb_source_data) | The ledger table: migrated by this release, verified after the migration, and exercised by the smoke run |
| `processed_event` | PLT library, created in rwb_source_data | The inbox; created and used by the library, not by this release |
| `idempotency_key` | PLT library, created in rwb_source_data | The stored response of the append; the smoke run relies on it for the replay |
| `outbox_event` | PLT library, created in rwb_source_data | The outbox of the decision-record library |

No other schema is migrated, created, altered or read by this release (DP-01, DP-15, DP-18).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

None is deployed. The case fake and the decision-log fake of the contract run in the service environment and the smoke run appends against them; the real cross-service proof belongs to RWB-ITG-E1066-ITG.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 0 consumed by the deployment | The three ledger operations are the app story's; the probes are cluster-internal |
| Kafka | 0 published, 0 consumed | No topic of this service and no consumer group in this release |
| Temporal | 0 workflows, 0 activities, 0 Schedules | No worker on `rwb-source-data` |
| File | None | No file is read or written by the deployment |
| SQL | One schema migrated, one table verified | `rwb_source_data`; the ledger objects of section 11 |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | The release migrates `rwb_source_data` only and reads no other schema | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | The local decision-record library is deployed with the service and publishes to `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | No ACE read in this release; the smoke entry names no ACE object | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | The rwb-case reference-data contract is a run-time dependency of the append; the deployment configures nothing of it | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | The library objects in `rwb_source_data` and the outbox relay of the service | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | The append is reached over REST through gateway-bff; the smoke run uses the same path | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | The ingress serves `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` and no other base | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | The per-service Flyway sequence of `rwb_source_data`; the migration step refuses another schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-18 | Interaction ledger | The ledger table is P1's and is deployed here; no other service's ledger object exists | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff serves the recording screens; the deployment registers the route and no screen of its own | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Artefacts**

| Artefact | Content |
|---|---|
| `helm/rwb-source-data/` overlay | API deployment, config map, secret references, probes, ingress route for the ledger operations, namespace and build ID |
| `helm/rwb-source-data/values-dev.yaml`, `values-sit.yaml`, `values-uat.yaml` | Image digest, replicas, resources, probe timings, log level, flag value, build ID, alert thresholds and windows (GAP-0506; ASM-0698) |
| Pipeline stage | Build, unit and contract tests, image and dependency scan, chart publish, migration step, verification step, trigger step, smoke run, promotion |
| Migration step | The `rwb_source_data` migration of this release, ledger version included; a target schema other than `rwb_source_data` is refused |
| Verification step | The catalogue check of the eight columns, the two unique keys, the trigger and the index, and the repeated-run check |
| Trigger step | One `UPDATE` and one `DELETE` on a synthetic row inside a rolled-back transaction; either statement succeeding fails the release |
| Dashboards | The five series of section 11 with the three dimensions |
| Alerts | Three rules, each with its message identifier or incident code and one runbook entry |
| Runbook | Three entries: append failure, ledger incident, missing trigger |

**Alert mapping**

| Identifier | Condition | Alert | Route |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-022 | The append failure rate is past its threshold, or one append fails with 503 | Append failure alert naming the error class, the release and the build ID, with the rate and the window | Platform on-call, page (route and window are environment values: GAP-0506; ASM-0698) |
| LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED | The writer raised the incident `LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED` for a case | Ledger incident alert naming the case ID, the error class and the build ID, with no summary and no contact point | Platform on-call and the recovery on-call, ticket (route is an environment value: GAP-0506; ASM-0698) |
| Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0506; ASM-0698) | `tr_interaction_append_only` is missing or disabled after a migration | Trigger alert naming the table and the object, and failing the release when it is raised in a pipeline | DevOps on-call, page |

**Rollback.** A release that fails the smoke run is not promoted. A release already promoted is rolled back by redeploying the previous chart version with its own image digest and build ID; the ledger rows written by the new build stay, because an entry is never deleted and never updated, and the previous build serves the append against the same table. The migration is forward only: a wrong ledger version is corrected by a new version and never by editing an applied one (DP-15). The series show both build IDs while the two builds overlap, so a duplicate hit or a `case_seq` gap is attributable to one of them.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.dataengine.ledger-writer`. On: the writer is deployed and the append answers through gateway-bff. Off: the writer is not deployed in that environment, the append is refused at the edge, no entry is written and no append series is emitted; the rest of the service is unchanged.

**Done when.** The chart renders for DEV, SIT and UAT with a pinned digest and the build ID, the migration step refuses a foreign schema, the verification step finds the eight columns, the two keys, the trigger and the index in each environment, a repeated migration changes nothing, the five series and the three alerts are published with their identifiers or placeholders and their runbook links, the smoke run appends one synthetic entry and replays its key with one row in the table, and the three runbook entries are reviewed by the on-call rota.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-022 | An append fails, or its failure rate is past its threshold | The entry was not saved because the interaction ledger could not be written. Try again in a few minutes. |
| LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED | The writer raised the ledger incident for a case | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0506; ASM-0698) |
| Identifier pending | `tr_interaction_append_only` is missing or disabled | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0506; ASM-0698) |

MSG-P1-022 keeps its legacy text unchanged and is the message of the append failure alert. The ledger incident and the trigger alert have no agreed text in the source set, and the threshold, the window and the route of each alert are not given either, so both are carried as the placeholder until the Error and Message Standard names them (GAP-0506; ASM-0698). An alert payload names counts, error classes, case IDs and build IDs only, never a summary, a contact point or an amount.

##### 15. Screens and states

The deployment has no screen of its own. Its operator-facing surfaces are the pipeline run view, the release view, the dashboard, the alert route and the runbook. The recording screens and the case timeline that reach the append are served by rwb-case and by the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19; RWB-PLT-N001-CON), and this deployment only registers the route. The platform administrator reads the release result and the ledger series under Platform administration R, and internal audit reads the append history and the release record under the same right.

The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a values file: the event codes, the channels, the directions and the case states are reference data and application behaviour, never a deployment value.
- No personal data in logs, series, alert payloads, the runbook or the smoke data: counts, error classes, case IDs and build IDs only; the smoke summary is synthetic, and no production payload is copied into a fixture.
- One login, one schema and one sequence: the release carries the `rwb_source_data` login and migrates `rwb_source_data` only (DP-02, DP-15).
- The release migrates, verifies and exercises the ledger table and no other service's schema; the ledger is P1's (DP-01, DP-18).
- The append-only trigger is verified on every environment and never assumed; a missing trigger blocks the release (BR2).
- No secret is written into a values file, a chart template, a dashboard or the runbook; the credential comes from the platform secret store.
- An applied migration is never edited: a wrong ledger version is corrected by a new version (DP-15).
- A failing smoke run never replaces a working build, and a rollback keeps the previous digest and build ID (BR8).

| RWB-P1-E1067-APP | App development | Sibling of the same legacy key: the outbox path whose appends the failure series also shows |
| RWB-ITG-E1066-ITG | Integration | Proves the append, the duplicate rule and the trigger against the live rwb-case and rwb-decision contracts |
| RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, RWB-PLT-N001-CON | Contract | H: the libraries and the sequence the release is built on |
| RWB-PLT-NF06-DB, RWB-P1-E1001-APP | ACE DB and App development | Prerequisites: the schema, the login and the baseline the ledger migration sits on |

##### 19. Out of scope

- The writer, the controller, the repository and the migration as code (RWB-P1-E1066-APP).
- The contract documents, the schemas, the error envelope and the fakes (RWB-P1-E1066-CON); this story only deploys, verifies and gates them.
- The outbox path from a business event to an entry (RWB-P1-E1067-APP).
- The ledger read interface and its filters (RWB-P1-E1068-APP).
- The recording screens and the case timeline of rwb-case (RWB-P3-E1018-APP and the screen owners).
- The real cross-service proof of the append, the duplicate rule and the append-only behaviour against the live rwb-case and rwb-decision contracts (RWB-ITG-E1066-ITG).
- The platform components: the Kafka topics and the schema registry, the Temporal cluster and its namespace, the flag library, the secret store and the observability platform (the platform epics).
- The exact deployment topology, resource sizes, replica counts, probe timings, alert thresholds, windows and the incident route; they are set per environment by the platform team (GAP-0506; ASM-0698).
- The Error and Message Standard texts of the ledger incident and of the trigger alert (the standard owner); both are carried as placeholders.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: RWB-E1-066 is split and reworked as the wave-1 integration story RWB-ITG-E1066-ITG. In the monolith the ledger, the `InteractionLedgerWriter` and the `POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions` endpoint sat in one deployable, with the P3 handler calling a published interface in the caller's transaction. Under the R-PREC default ruling and DP-18 the ledger and both interaction operations belong to P1 rwb-source-data in schema `rwb_source_data`, and P3 rwb-case keeps the case record, the case scope and the timeline and reads the ledger through P1's contract. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **QA integration engineer**, I want **the interaction ledger proved end to end on the real wave-1 services — P3 rwb-case committing the case action and serving the case timeline `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timeline`, P1 rwb-source-data appending the entry through `POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions` and reading it back through `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions`, and P7 rwb-decision holding the central decision log entry that a decision entry links to**, so that **the history of a case is written where it is owned and read by every other service through a contract, and the crossing between the two services is proved before wave 1 exits rather than assumed**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Today the history of a recovery case is spread across EFS, LIT, letters and team spreadsheets, and an officer rebuilds it by hand before each decision. One append-only ledger per case, written in the same transaction as the action it records, gives one ordered history with no gap. The ledger records what happened with the customer; the decision log records why the system acted; each ledger entry for a decision points to its decision log entry. A ledger write that fails stops the action and raises an incident, so the history never has a silent gap. Serves REQ-ILG-001, REQ-ILG-002, REQ-ILG-004 and REQ-ILG-008; NFR-070 and NFR-077.

The target moves the store and the writer out of the monolith. The interaction ledger and both interaction operations belong to P1 rwb-source-data (R-PREC default ruling, DP-18; the Ownership Map ruling on `interaction` and on `POST` and `GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions`), in schema `rwb_source_data`, on base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` (DP-01, DP-13). The write is one hop from gateway-bff to P1 with a 2 s timeout (DP-11, DP-19); the schema arrives through P1's own Flyway sequence (DP-15); the local decision record and the outbox and inbox library carry the decision link to the central ledger in P7 rwb-decision (DP-03, DP-09); the LOV-LEDGER-EVENT values are read through the reference-data contract of rwb-case (DP-07); and no service but P1 reads an ACE view, so the EFS history entries on the ledger come through P1 alone (DP-05).

P3 rwb-case keeps the case record, the case scope and the case timeline. The timeline `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timeline` is composed from P1's interaction contract and P3's own case fields; schema `rwb_case` holds no interaction table and no copy of an entry. That leaves one behaviour that no single service story can prove: a P3 case action and a P1 ledger entry form one business transaction, and a P1 failure must not leave the P3 action committed. The sources do not name the mechanism that closes the gap, so this story asserts the outcome — the action is rolled back or compensated and the case shows its previous state — and records the open point as Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0375; ASM-0539).

The measure is unchanged from the legacy story: every contact, letter, promise, payment and hand-over on a case is on the ledger when it is recorded, and a failed write stops the action and raises incident LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED (REQ-ILG-008; CTL-06). The story meets REQ-ILG-001, REQ-ILG-002, REQ-ILG-004 and REQ-ILG-008 and supports NFR-070 and NFR-077. It ends the history that is assembled after the fact, because the ledger of a case is one owned, ordered and append-only sequence that every other service reads through its owner.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P3-E1018-APP is done: `recovery_case` exists in schema `rwb_case` with case numbers RW-YYYY-NNNNNN, the case scope is applied, and `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` answers from it.
- RWB-P1-E1066-APP is done: `interaction` is written and read in schema `rwb_source_data`, `POST` and `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions` are published on base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`, the case lock and the case_seq assignment work, the required-value validation answers MSG-GEN-001, and a failed write raises incident LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED with MSG-P1-022.
- RWB-P3-E1066-APP is done: `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timeline` composes the case timeline from P1's interaction contract and P3's case fields, and schema `rwb_case` holds no interaction table and no stored copy of an entry.
- Schema `rwb_source_data` is migrated by the P1 Flyway sequence (DP-15) with the columns of DF-INT-001 to DF-INT-021, the unique keys on (case_id, case_seq) and on (idempotency_key), the append-only trigger `tr_interaction_append_only`, and the P1 login holding INSERT and SELECT with no UPDATE or DELETE grant (DP-01, DP-02).
- The DP-03 and DP-09 library objects `decision_record`, `outbox_event` and `processed_event` exist in schema `rwb_source_data`, and the outbox relay publishes `DecisionRecorded` on the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON).
- P7 rwb-decision holds `decision_log_entry`, ingests the shared topic idempotently through its inbox, and answers `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log/{entryId}` (RWB-P7-E1008-APP).
- The list LOV-LEDGER-EVENT is in force with the values CONTACT, LETTER, PROMISE, PAYMENT, HANDOVER, CASE_CREATED, CASE_ALLOCATED, CASE_TRANSFERRED, CASE_ESCALATED, DOCUMENT_ATTACHED, DECISION_TAKEN and CORRECTION, read as data rows through the reference-data contract of rwb-case (DP-07).
- The gateway-bff route for the case screens is deployed in SIT, with the 2 s per-call budget and no call chain deeper than one (DP-19, RWB-PLT-N001-CON).
- The harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG is available with its synthetic data set: case "RW-2026-000201" with its six ledger entries, user "u-owner-02" as its owner, approver "u-teammgr-01", rule "R-UNI-18" version "2026.11", and the four EFS history entries, the CASE_CREATED and the CASE_ALLOCATED entry.
- The mechanism that keeps the P3 case action and the P1 ledger entry in one business transaction — and the record of a compensated action — is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0375; ASM-0539). The suite therefore asserts the committed or compensated state of the case, not the mechanism.
- Every service called by the suite is the real SIT service behind its own login; no contract fake stands in for a service.
- No production data is used and no production connection is opened. The release date 30 November 2026 is tentative; a date is not a condition of this story.
- This story has no build dependency, so it is ready on Day 1 (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. QA integration engineer: runs the preflight of section 13 — the two P1 interaction operations on base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`, the P3 case read and timeline path, the P3 statement log, the append-only trigger, the local record objects, the shared topic and the P7 decision-log read. A missing element stops the run before any test.
2. Harness: seeds the synthetic data set of RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG — case "RW-2026-000201" with its six entries, "u-owner-02" as the owner, "u-teammgr-01" as the approver, and the LOV-LEDGER-EVENT values read as data rows through the reference-data contract of rwb-case (DP-07).
3. Case owner: records an outbound call on 2026-12-02 at 10:15 with result RIGHT_PARTY and a promise of 25,000.00 baht for 2026-12-15, through `POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions` on the gateway-bff route, with an Idempotency-Key, channel CALL, direction OUTBOUND and source system WORKBENCH.
4. P3 rwb-case: commits the case action the call belongs to — the promise and the last contact of case "RW-2026-000201" — as the case side of the same business transaction, and calls no table of schema `rwb_source_data` (DP-01, DP-18).
5. P1 rwb-source-data: validates the command against LOV-LEDGER-EVENT, takes the transaction-level advisory lock on the case ID, assigns case_seq 7 as the case's highest case_seq plus 1, and inserts the entry with event code, actor "u-owner-02", source system "WORKBENCH", channel "CALL", direction "OUTBOUND" and the promise fields, and answers 201 with the entry.
6. P1 rwb-source-data: writes one local `decision_record` row naming the entry and one `outbox_event` row in the same transaction (DP-03, DP-09); the relay publishes `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and P7 rwb-decision records the event id in its inbox and appends one `decision_log_entry`.
7. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions` and asserts the sequence of case_seq 1 to 7 with no gap and the fields of the call; reads `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` and asserts the case action is committed on the case.
8. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timeline` and compares the timeline entry with the ledger entry on entry ID, case_seq 7, occurred time 2026-12-02T10:15+07:00, event "CONTACT" and actor "u-owner-02"; then reads the P3 statement log and asserts no statement of the timeline read touches schema `rwb_source_data`.
9. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log/{entryId}` and asserts that the decision entry of the reassignment holds decision code "D6", rule "R-UNI-18", version "2026.11", the inputs reference and the approver "u-teammgr-01", while the ledger entry holds event "DECISION_TAKEN", the time, the actor and the decision log entry ID with no rule, version or inputs.
10. Harness: asserts the ordered history — the four EFS history entries from 2026-08-03 to 2026-11-28, the CASE_CREATED entry and the CASE_ALLOCATED entry of 2026-12-01 — read through P1 only, in one sequence by occurred time with case_seq 1 to 6 (DP-05).
11. Harness: forces the ledger insert to fail with a database error through the agreed test-only fault hook, repeats a call with an Idempotency-Key, records the 503 with MSG-P1-022, the unchanged entries, the absent contact in P1 and the absent timeline entry, the incident LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED, and the compensated case action of that call read through `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}`; it restores the hook and sends the same call again with the same key, and asserts exactly one entry.
12. Harness: issues an UPDATE and a DELETE on entry case_seq 3 and asserts both are refused, then writes a correction as a new entry with event "CORRECTION" naming entry case_seq 3.
13. Harness: writes the evidence report — per scenario the entry ID, the case_seq, the timeline entry, the statuses, the messages, the incident and the call latencies — restores every fixture, and confirms the fault hook and the append-only trigger are back in place.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The ledger cannot be written inside P1's transaction | The P1 transaction rolls back, no entry and no contact are saved, the caller receives 503, incident LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED is raised, and the P3 timeline holds no entry for the call | MSG-P1-022 | AC4, AC9 |
| X2 | A required value is missing (event code, occurred time, actor) | 422; nothing written | MSG-GEN-001 | AC5, owned by RWB-P1-E1066-APP |
| X3 | Two entries for one case at the same moment | Both written with consecutive case_seq under the case lock; no gap and no repeat | None | AC6, owned by RWB-P1-E1066-APP |
| X4 | A call names a case that does not exist or is out of scope, for example case ID "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000999" | 404; nothing written | MSG-P4-003 | AC7, owned by RWB-P1-E1066-APP |
| X5 | Any change or delete of an entry | Refused by the append-only trigger; a correction is a new entry naming the original | None | AC8 |
| X6 | P1 answers 503 after P3 has prepared the case action of the call | P3 rolls the action back or compensates it, the case read shows the state before the call, and no timeline entry appears | MSG-P1-022 | AC9 |
| X7 | The timeline disagrees with the ledger, or P3 reads schema `rwb_source_data` directly | The run fails and names the entry ID, the two values and the offending statement | None | AC10 |
| X8 | A call is a chain rather than one hop, or exceeds the 2 s budget | The run fails and names the call, the services on the path and the latency | None | AC1, AC4, AC10 |
| X9 | The fixture set does not match the harness expectations, or the fault hook cannot be reached | The suite fails as a harness fault and names the element; no service defect is raised | None | AC1, AC2 |

X1 and X5 are the legacy exception paths carried onto the real services; X2 to X4 are carried with their owners; X6 to X9 are the cross-service paths that appear only once the ledger lives in P1 and the timeline reads it through the contract.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | The suite is its own module and reuses the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG; it needs the three APP stories and the published contracts of P1, P3 and P7, not their source code |
| Negotiable | The fixture size, the retry count, the wait intervals and the report layout are configuration; the case, the users, the rule, the values and the messages are fixed by the legacy story |
| Valuable | Proves across services what no single service story can prove: one owned entry, one order, one timeline agreement, one entry after a retry and no committed action without its entry |
| Estimable | One suite module, one fixture pack, one fault hook, one statement-log assertion and one evidence report |
| Small | Seven scenarios over three services and one shared topic; no service code and no schema change |
| Testable | Every criterion asserts a row, a response, a timeline entry, a status, a message, an incident or a recorded statement |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Interaction ledger store and writer, end-to-end across the wave 1 services

  Background:
    Given case "RW-2026-000201" exists with 6 ledger entries, case_seq 1 to 6
    Given user "u-owner-02" holds RW-CASEOWN and owns case "RW-2026-000201"
    Given the wave 1 services rwb-source-data, rwb-case and rwb-decision are deployed in SIT with their published contracts behind gateway-bff and no production data is used

  Scenario: AC1 The ledger exists and is written to (legacy RWB-E1-066 AC1)
    Given the case owner records an outbound call through POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions on 2026-12-02 at 10:15 with result RIGHT_PARTY and a promise of 25,000.00 baht for 2026-12-15
    When the action completes
    Then the ledger holds entry case_seq 7 for case "RW-2026-000201" with event "CONTACT", occurred at 2026-12-02T10:15+07:00, actor "u-owner-02", channel "CALL" and direction "OUTBOUND"
    Then the entry carries promise amount 25,000.00 and promise date 2026-12-15
    Then the entry names source system "WORKBENCH"

  Scenario: AC2 It is ordered and complete (legacy RWB-E1-066 AC2)
    Given case "RW-2026-000201" has 4 EFS history entries from 2026-08-03 to 2026-11-28, a CASE_CREATED entry on 2026-12-01 and a CASE_ALLOCATED entry on 2026-12-01
    When the ledger is read
    Then the 6 entries are in one sequence ordered by occurred time
    Then case_seq runs 1 to 6 with no gap

  Scenario: AC3 It is distinct from the decision log (legacy RWB-E1-066 AC3)
    Given owner reassignment of case "RW-2026-000201" was decided under rule "R-UNI-18" version "2026.11" by approver "u-teammgr-01"
    When both are read
    Then the decision log entry holds decision code "D6", rule "R-UNI-18", version "2026.11", the inputs reference and the approver
    Then the ledger entry holds event "DECISION_TAKEN", the time, the actor and the decision log entry ID, with no rule, version or inputs

  Scenario: AC4 A write failure is visible (legacy RWB-E1-066 AC4)
    Given the ledger insert fails with a database error
    When the case owner records a call on case "RW-2026-000201"
    Then the system refuses the call with status 503 and MSG-P1-022
    Then the ledger still holds 6 entries and no contact is saved
    Then the system raises an incident "LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED" with case "RW-2026-000201"

  Scenario: AC8 An entry cannot be changed (legacy RWB-E1-066 AC8)
    Given ledger entry case_seq 3 of case "RW-2026-000201"
    When any process issues an UPDATE or DELETE on it
    Then the database refuses the statement
    Then the system writes a correction as a new entry with event "CORRECTION" naming entry case_seq 3

  Scenario: AC9 The P3 case action and the P1 ledger entry are one business transaction, and a P1 failure leaves no committed action (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given case "RW-2026-000201" is owned by "u-owner-02" and holds 6 ledger entries, case_seq 1 to 6
    Given P3 rwb-case commits the case action of a call as the case side of the same business transaction as the ledger entry
    When the case owner records an outbound call through POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions and P1 rwb-source-data answers 201
    Then the ledger holds entry case_seq 7 for the call
    Then GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId} shows the promise of 25,000.00 for 2026-12-15 on case "RW-2026-000201"
    When the ledger insert of a second call fails with a database error and P1 answers 503 with MSG-P1-022
    Then the ledger still holds 7 entries and no contact of the second call is saved
    Then the case action of the second call is rolled back or compensated, and GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId} shows the case as it stood after the first call, with no promise of the second
    Then the timeline of case "RW-2026-000201" holds no entry for the second call
    Then the system raises an incident "LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED" with case "RW-2026-000201"

  Scenario: AC10 The P3 timeline shows the same entry through the P1 contract and rwb-case holds no copy (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given case "RW-2026-000201" holds entry case_seq 7 appended by P1 rwb-source-data for the outbound call of 2026-12-02 at 10:15
    When the case owner reads GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timeline through gateway-bff
    Then the timeline shows the entry with the same entry ID and case_seq 7, occurred 2026-12-02T10:15+07:00, event "CONTACT" and actor "u-owner-02"
    Then P3 answers the timeline through GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions, one hop with a 2 s timeout
    Then the statement log of the timeline read holds no statement on schema rwb_source_data
    Then schema rwb_case holds no interaction table and no column that stores a copy of an entry
```

The two new criteria carry the cross-service part the monolith never had: the one business transaction across P3 and P1 with its compensation, and the timeline that reads the ledger through the owner's contract without holding a copy. The five legacy criteria are carried verbatim in substance, with only the monolith names adapted to the target operation, schema and owner.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One ledger holds every interaction on a case; no other record is the authoritative history | REQ-ILG-001; case file item "Interaction ledger" (casemodel.txt) |
| BR2 | Every entry carries case, event, time, actor and source | REQ-ILG-002 |
| BR3 | An offer, promise, payment or hand-over is recorded on the interaction it was made in | REQ-ILG-004; interaction.promise_amount |
| BR4 | Entries are append only; a correction is a new entry naming the original | tr_interaction_append_only (Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v6.sql); R-UNI-24 |
| BR5 | A ledger write that fails stops the action and raises an incident; no entry is discarded | REQ-ILG-008; CTL-06 |
| BR6 | The ledger records what happened; the decision log records why; a decision entry links the two | FEAT-ILG-02; ADR-009 |
| BR7 | Entries of one case carry a gap-free sequence | REQ-ILG-001; interaction.case_seq |
| BR8 | The ledger and both interaction operations belong to P1 rwb-source-data in schema `rwb_source_data`; P3 rwb-case keeps the case record, the case scope and the timeline and holds no copy of an entry | DP-18; DP-01; R-PREC default ruling; Ownership Map v1 |
| BR9 | The P3 case action and the P1 ledger entry are one business transaction: a P1 503 never leaves the P3 action committed, and no distributed transaction is used to achieve it | RWB-E1-066 AC4; Arch v5 slide 11 (Idempotency-Key on every POST); ASM-0539 |
| BR10 | The write is one REST hop from gateway-bff to the owner within a 2 s budget, every POST carries an Idempotency-Key, and a repeat returns the first entry | ADR-020; DP-11; DP-19; Arch v5 slide 11 |
| BR11 | Each append writes one local decision record and one outbox row in the same transaction in `rwb_source_data`, and the consumer inbox makes the central effect exactly one entry | DP-03; DP-09; Arch v5 slides 20 and 28 |
| BR12 | The event and LOV values are reference data read through the contract of rwb-case; no service but P1 reads an ACE view, and the EFS history entries reach the ledger through P1 alone | DP-07; DP-05; R-PREC default ruling |

##### 9. State transitions

None for a case status: the story changes no case status of its own and asserts the states below.

| Object | State | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `interaction` entry in `rwb_source_data` | Appended | Written by P1 in the caller's transaction; it has no status, is never updated and is never deleted |
| Correction | Correction of an entry | A new entry with `corrects_entry_id` naming the corrected entry; the corrected entry keeps its own record |
| P3 case action | Committed | The case side of the business transaction is on the case record, for example the promise and the last contact of the call |
| P3 case action | Rolled back or compensated | The P1 append answered 503; the case read shows the state before the call and no timeline entry exists |
| Local decision record | Committed with the entry | Present only with the entry, chained to the previous record, never alone |
| Central `decision_log_entry` | Ingested once | Appended to the central chain in P7, deduplicated by the P7 inbox |
| P3 timeline | Derived | Composed by P3 from its own case fields and P1's interaction contract; it holds no state of its own in `rwb_case` |
| Suite run | Not started, running, passed, failed | A failed run names the criterion, the service, the entry ID and the evidence |

The compensation state of the case action is read through `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}`; the suite changes none of these states directly.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| QA integration engineer | Runs the suite, seeds the synthetic fixtures, reads the evidence report |
| rwb-source-data service identity (the P1 login, DP-02) | Validates and appends entries, assigns case_seq, writes the local decision record and the outbox row, owns schema `rwb_source_data` |
| rwb-case service identity (the P3 login, DP-02) | Commits or compensates the case action, serves the case read and the timeline, calls P1's interaction contract, holds no copy of an entry |
| rwb-decision service identity (the P7 login, DP-02) | Ingests `DecisionRecorded` into the central ledger and serves the decision-log read |
| gateway-bff, platform edge | Owns the route, the 2 s per-call budget and the session check |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Records contacts and promises on own cases (Case record C, scope Own) and reads the timeline of own cases |
| RW-TEAMMGR, RW-PHONECOL and other case roles | Read entries and the timeline in this story (Case record R); they record nothing here |
| RW-AUDIT Internal audit | Reads entries and the timeline only; may not record |
| RW-PLATADM Platform administrator | Receives the LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED incident |
| No role | May update or delete an entry; no role may read schema `rwb_source_data` through another service |

No approval level from the delegation of authority applies: the story takes no business decision of its own.

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DF-INT-001 to DF-INT-013 | `interaction` | all fields | Write by P1; read through P1 | rwb_source_data |
| DF-INT-014 | `interaction` | event_code | Write by P1; read through P1 | rwb_source_data |
| DF-INT-015, DF-INT-016 | `interaction` | actor_type, actor_ref | Write by P1; read through P1 | rwb_source_data |
| DF-INT-017 | `interaction` | source_ref | Write by P1; read through P1 | rwb_source_data |
| DF-INT-018 | `interaction` | idempotency_key | Write by P1; read through P1 | rwb_source_data |
| DF-INT-019 | `interaction` | case_seq | Write by P1; read through P1 | rwb_source_data |
| DF-INT-020 | `interaction` | decision_log_id | Write by P1; read through P7 | rwb_source_data |
| DF-INT-021 | `interaction` | corrects_entry_id | Write by P1; read through P1 | rwb_source_data |
| DF-CAS-001 | `recovery_case` | id | Read through P3 | rwb_case |
| DF-CAS-009 | `recovery_case` | owner_user_id | Read through P3 (the committed or compensated case action) | rwb_case |
| DF-DEC-001 | `decision_log_entry` | id | Read through P7 | rwb_decision |
| DF-DEC-003 | `decision_log_entry` | decision_code | Read through P7 | rwb_decision |
| DF-DEC-004 | `decision_log_entry` | rule_id | Read through P7 | rwb_decision |
| DF-DEC-005 | `decision_log_entry` | rule_version | Read through P7 | rwb_decision |
| DF-DEC-008 | `decision_log_entry` | inputs_ref | Read through P7 | rwb_decision |
| DF-DEC-010 | `decision_log_entry` | approver_user_id | Read through P7 | rwb_decision |
| Compensation record of the P3 case action | `rwb_case` | the field or record that marks an action as compensated | Read through P3 | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0375; ASM-0539) |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary and are copied from RWB-E1-066. The legacy story writes `interaction` in the monolith and reads `decision_log_entry` in process; in the target the entry is written and read by P1 in schema `rwb_source_data`, the case state is P3's, and the central entry is P7's. The suite owns no schema, no table and no field: it writes only through P1's contract and reads the three owners through their contracts.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The suite provides no REST operation. The names reserved for P2 rwb-integration — `/api/recovery/integration/v1`, `rwb.integration.events.v1`, `rwb-integration` and `rwb_integration` — are not used, and no `rwb_integration` table is written.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Base | Use in the suite |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions` | P1 rwb-source-data | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` | The one-hop ledger write of the call, with an Idempotency-Key (AC1, AC4, AC9) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions` | P1 rwb-source-data | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` | The entries of one case in case_seq order (AC1, AC2) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | The case record and the committed or compensated case action (AC9) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timeline` | P3 rwb-case | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | The timeline that shows the entry without holding a copy (AC10) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log/{entryId}` | P7 rwb-decision | `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | The central decision entry the ledger entry links to (AC3, AC9) |

Every call is one hop to the owning service on its own base with a 2 s budget (DP-11, DP-13); the browser reaches the services only through gateway-bff (DP-19). The request and response fields of the interaction write, the Idempotency-Key rule, the failure mapping and the compensation mechanism are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0375; ASM-0538), so the suite asserts the outcomes named in section 7 and not a wire shape it would have to invent.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The suite publishes no business event. The `DecisionRecorded` event asserted in AC9 and AC3 is produced by P1 rwb-source-data through its outbox relay and is named in 12.4.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None by the suite. DP-09, the outbox and inbox library, sits on the owning APP stories — RWB-P1-E1066-APP produces `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and RWB-P7-E1008-APP consumes it into the central ledger; this story asserts the effect through the decision-log read of 12.2 and consumes no event itself.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. No workflow, activity or Nexus operation is started or awaited by this story; the write and the reads are synchronous REST calls (Arch v5 slide 12, question 1).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Schedule is started, moved or waited for. The outbox relay of P1 is the every-minute sender JOB-11 of the owning service (Arch v5 slide 44), and this story only observes its effect.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The suite owns no table and writes no schema of its own (DP-01). The tables it exercises are `interaction`, `decision_record`, `outbox_event` and `processed_event` in schema `rwb_source_data` (P1); `recovery_case` in schema `rwb_case` (P3); and `decision_log_entry` with its inbox in schema `rwb_decision` (P7). It reads and writes them only through their owners.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

None. The suite runs against the deployed SIT services and their published contracts. The bank systems behind the ACE views are outside the bank's service contracts and are read by P1 alone through the `recovery.v_ace_*` views (DP-05); no service contract is faked, because the point of the story is that the real cross-service behaviour is proved (Template and Rules §R5.4 class I). The only intervention in a running service is the agreed test-only fault hook of AC4 and AC9 on the P1 insert, and it is switched off in UAT and production.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Provided by the suite | Consumed by the suite |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 | 5: the two P1 interaction operations, the P3 case read, the P3 timeline read and the P7 decision-log read, each one hop with a 2 s budget |
| Kafka | 0 | 0; the `DecisionRecorded` effect is asserted through the decision-log read |
| Temporal | 0 | 0 |
| File | 0 | 0 |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** One suite module `integration/recovery-w1/interaction-ledger`, next to the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG, with the test classes `LedgerWriteIT`, `LedgerOrderIT`, `DecisionDistinctionIT`, `TimelineAgreementIT` and `CaseTransactionIT`, the fixture files and the evidence report writer. The module holds no service code and is not part of a deployed service.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| SuiteRunner | Runner | Preflight, run order, evidence report and exit code |
| PreflightProbe | Service | Checks the two P1 interaction operations, the P3 case read and timeline path, the P3 statement log, the append-only trigger, the local record objects, the shared topic and the P7 decision-log read before any test |
| LedgerWriter | Service | Calls the P1 write with an Idempotency-Key, channel CALL, direction OUTBOUND, result RIGHT_PARTY and the promise of 25,000.00 for 2026-12-15, and asserts 201 and the entry |
| LedgerReader | Service | Reads the case entries through P1 and asserts the order, case_seq 1 to 7 and the gap-free sequence |
| CaseReader | Service | Reads the case through P3 and asserts the committed or the compensated case action (AC9) |
| TimelineReader | Service | Reads the P3 timeline and compares entry ID, case_seq, occurred time, event code and actor with the ledger |
| SchemaBoundaryProbe | Service | Reads the P3 statement log and asserts no statement on schema `rwb_source_data`, and no interaction table or copy column in `rwb_case` |
| DecisionReader | Service | Reads the central entry through P7 and asserts decision code "D6", rule "R-UNI-18", version "2026.11", the inputs reference and the approver |
| FailureInjector | Service | Forces the P1 insert to fail through the agreed test-only fault hook, restores it in the same run, and repeats the call with the same Idempotency-Key |
| AppendOnlyProbe | Service | Issues the UPDATE and the DELETE on entry case_seq 3 and writes the CORRECTION entry naming it |
| EvidenceReport | Report | Per scenario the entry ID, the case_seq, the timeline entry, the statuses, the messages, the incident and the call latencies |

**Decoupling patterns applied (Template and Rules v1 §R5.5)**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added | Where it sits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none | `interaction` and the library objects in `rwb_source_data`; the suite asserts through contracts only |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON | On RWB-P1-E1066-APP and RWB-P3-E1066-APP; the suite only reads the central entry through P7 |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none | The four EFS history entries of AC2 come from the ACE EFS action view and are read by P1 alone; the suite asserts them through P1's contract |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON | LOV-LEDGER-EVENT rows read as data through the P3 contract by P1 and by the fixtures |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON | On RWB-P1-E1066-APP for the local record and the outbox row; the suite asserts the central effect, not the envelope |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) | The interaction write and read and the timeline read of section 12.2; the legacy `append()` in the caller's transaction becomes a one-hop command |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none | Every consumed path of section 12.2 |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON | On RWB-P1-E1066-APP for `rwb_source_data` and its append-only trigger; the suite owns no schema |
| DP-18 | Interaction ledger | Ledger owned by rwb-source-data (default ruling) | none | The ledger and both interaction operations in P1; the P3 timeline reads them through P1's contract (AC9, AC10) |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The browser reaches the interaction write and the case and timeline screens through gateway-bff only |

The dependency-added column records the build dependency of the owning story, exactly as §R5.5 states it. The H, C and X lists of this story are empty — the H dependencies of DP-03, DP-07, DP-09, DP-15 and DP-19 sit on the APP and platform stories that implement them, and the C dependency of DP-07 is published by P3 rwb-case. The three integration dependencies RWB-P3-E1018-APP, RWB-P1-E1066-APP and RWB-P3-E1066-APP are the only dependencies of this story, they are of class I, and an integration dependency never blocks a build (Template and Rules §R5.4).

**Build steps**

1. Create the suite module next to the harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG and wire it to the SIT bases of P1, P3 and P7 through gateway-bff; the preflight fails the run when a fake endpoint is configured.
2. Build the fixture pack from the legacy values: case "RW-2026-000201", "u-owner-02", "u-teammgr-01", rule "R-UNI-18" version "2026.11", the promise of 25,000.00 for 2026-12-15, the four EFS entries, CASE_CREATED and CASE_ALLOCATED, and the LOV values read as data rows.
3. Implement AC1 and AC2: the one-hop write on `POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions`, the entry of case_seq 7, and the ordered sequence 1 to 6 read through P1.
4. Implement AC3: the decision entry through `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log/{entryId}` against the ledger entry of event "DECISION_TAKEN".
5. Implement AC8: the refused UPDATE and DELETE on entry case_seq 3 and the CORRECTION entry naming it.
6. Implement AC4 and AC9: the forced insert failure, the 503 with MSG-P1-022, the incident LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED, the compensated case action read through P3, and the retry with the same Idempotency-Key.
7. Implement AC10: the timeline read, the comparison with the ledger entry, and the statement-log and `rwb_case` boundary assertions.
8. Run the suite in SIT against the wave 1 release candidate, write the evidence report, and restore the fixtures, the fault hook and the trigger.

**Done when.** The seven test cases of section 16 pass in SIT against the published wave 1 contracts of P1, P3 and P7; a P1 503 leaves no committed case action and no timeline entry; the timeline agrees with the ledger and `rwb_case` holds no copy; and no service code or schema was changed by this story apart from the agreed test-only fault hook.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-022 | The ledger write failed | The entry was not saved because the interaction ledger could not be written. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required value is missing, for example the field "event code" | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without Case record C | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | Case missing or out of scope, for example 404 for case ID "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000999" | This case is not in your scope. |

The four message IDs and their texts are copied unchanged from RWB-E1-066, and this story adds no message ID. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10. The suite's own report lines — the entry ID, the case_seq, the timeline values and the latencies — are for the integration record and are not part of the message standard.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen is built in this story. The screen the behaviour serves is the case record view SCR-03 with its ledger and timeline part, and it is not in scope here: the suite calls the interaction write, the case read, the timeline read and the decision-log read directly, and the browser reaches them through gateway-bff with the 2 s budget (DP-19). A failed write shows MSG-P1-022 in the error state of the screen; the timeline shows an entry only after P1 has appended it, and after a compensated action it shows nothing of the failed call. The screen build and its states belong to RWB-P3-E1066-APP and RWB-E1-068 (the ledger read view).

The five legacy test cases are kept as ITG copies with the suffix `-ITG`, and the two new criteria carry `TC-ITG-E1066-01` and `TC-ITG-E1066-02`. The legacy criteria not owned here — AC5, AC6 and AC7 — and the access test TC-E1-066-09 are owned by RWB-P1-E1066-APP and are re-exercised only inside the end-to-end run where they appear as exception paths X2 to X4. The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the legacy test case id.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the case, the users, the rule, the promise and the dates are fixture configuration; the event codes are LOV-LEDGER-EVENT values read through the rwb-case reference-data contract (DP-07).
- No personal data in logs, events, evidence or fixtures: IDs, codes and case_seq values only; the summary of a call is never logged and every fixture is synthetic.
- No cross-service table read: the case is read through P3, the entries through P1 and the decision entry through P7, and the suite owns no table (DP-01, DP-05, DP-18).
- One hop and one timeout: every call is a contract call with a 2 s budget and no chain deeper than one; the browser reaches nothing directly (DP-11, DP-19).
- No update and no delete path: no repository method, no grant and no endpoint exists for either, and AC8 asserts the refusal instead of relying on review.
- The ledger is owned by P1 and P3 holds no copy (DP-18); a timeline that answers from its own interaction table fails AC10, and it fails the statement-log assertion the same way.
- A P1 failure leaves no committed case action: the suite asserts the compensated state of AC9 and not only the error status.
- The forced insert failure runs only in DEV and SIT through the agreed test-only fault hook, is refused in UAT and production, and is restored in the same run with the append-only trigger.
- No production access of any kind from the suite or its configuration.
