##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the page-size default and maximum are parameters of rwb-case, the channels are list values of LOV-CHANNEL, the masking rule is policy of rwb-access, and the 2 s budgets are configuration.
- No personal data in logs, tests, events or prompts: a summary is never logged and never written to a trace; the PII access log records the user, the product, the case and the time of the read and never the value; test summaries are synthetic.
- No read of another service's tables: the case is answered by the case contract, the masking and the authorise answers by the access contract, the parameters and the lists by their contracts, and `interaction` is read only in this service (DP-01, DP-06, DP-07, DP-08, DP-11).
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `v_ace_*` views: this story reads no ACE data at all; the ledger holds what the writer recorded and the read adds nothing.
- The read changes nothing: no insert, no update and no delete on the ledger, no advisory lock, and the repository has no write method.
- The scope answer and the masking answer are never cached; a scope call that does not answer inside 2 s refuses the read, and a masking call that does not answer masks the summary (DP-08, DP-11).
- A personal field with no unmasking rule is never returned; a personal field is not returned unmasked when the PII access log cannot be written (BR-P1-015-2, BR-P1-015-4).
- One login, one schema and one sequence: the release carries the `rwb_source_data` login, migrates `rwb_source_data` only, and an applied migration version is never edited (DP-02, DP-15).
- No screen is served here: SCR-03 and SCR-04 arrive through the gateway-bff composite route and are the screen owners' (DP-19).

- The gateway-bff composite route and the rendering of a masked summary (RWB-PLT-N001-CON and the screen owners).
- The retention class resolution and the archive of ledger rows (RWB-E1-017 in the legacy set); this read returns live rows only and resolves nothing.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-069 for rwb-source-data. The 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views stay in schema `recovery` with `ace_view_owner` as their owner and are read by the `rwb_source_data` login only (DP-02, DP-05; Architecture v5 slides 11 and 29); the view SQL, the conformance test and the ACE read contract move to this story, the login, the grant block and the four extension tables to RWB-P1-E1069-DB, and the proof across the 19 logins to RWB-ITG-E1069-ITG. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **recovery developer (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **the 30 SELECT-only `recovery.v_ace_*` views created on rwb-source-data's own migration sequence, the view conformance test that fails the build on a compile error, a constraint into `public`, a missing dictionary row or a grant outside the views, the ACE read contract that every other service and every agent calls, and the authorise-and-mask hop that every read takes before it returns an ACE-sourced field**, so that **there is one copy of source data, the Workbench cannot alter or copy it, and a direct read of an ACE table fails in the database and in the build**.

This is the application slice of legacy RWB-E1-069. It owns:

- the view SQL of the 16 Section A and 14 Section B views, taken from `recovery_views.sql` of the Physical Schema folder, and the two migrations that apply them on rwb-source-data's per-service Flyway sequence (DP-15);
- the view conformance test of the legacy story, with its four checks and its named failures;
- the ACE read contract served over the views on base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` (DP-05, DP-11, DP-13): `GET /customers/{id}`, `GET /accounts/{id}` and `GET /collateral/{id}`;
- the authorise-and-mask hop of DP-08 to rwb-access (P4) that every read takes once, one hop, 2 s timeout, before a field is returned;
- the read path that every other service and every agent calls, and boundary rule BND-6 over this service's own package, with the 30 view names as the only allowed source objects.

It does not create the `rwb_source_data` login, the `GRANT` statements, the view owner `ace_view_owner` or the four extension tables: they are RWB-P1-E1069-DB (external dependency X). It does not prove the grant matrix across the 19 logins, or the second half of boundary rule BND-6 outside this service: that is RWB-ITG-E1069-ITG. It creates no table of its own, and it reads no table of another service (DP-01).

##### 2. Business rationale

The Workbench takes no inbound source data. ACE ingests every source, and the recovery module reads it through 30 SELECT-only views: 16 over the ACE tables that exist today, 177 fields, and 14 over the tables RWB-ACE-001 adds, 127 fields, 304 in all. The views are owned by a dedicated role that holds SELECT on the ACE tables; the service login holds SELECT on the views and no privilege on anything in `public`. PUBLIC holds no privilege, and no write is granted on a view. The Workbench keeps its own decisions about an ACE record in four extension tables keyed by the ACE business key, never in a copy of an ACE column (legacy RWB-E1-069 §2).

In the target the boundary is enforced in three places instead of two. The catalog refuses a direct `public` read, because only the `rwb_source_data` login holds SELECT on the views and no login holds anything in `public` (Architecture v5 slides 8, 9, 11 and 29; ADR-010). Boundary rule BND-6 fails this service's build when a class of `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.sourcedata` names a `public` table. And every other service reaches ACE data only through this story's read contract, because only rwb-source-data reads the views at all (Architecture v5 slides 8, 9, 13, 41 and 45; DP-05, DP-11), so a change in ACE is absorbed in one place instead of nineteen.

Serves REQ-RDF-002 (account balance, arrears, payments and classification read from ACE through `v_ace_account` and `v_ace_payment`) and REQ-DRI-006 (no component calls a system of record directly); applies DP-01, DP-02, DP-05, DP-08 and DP-11 and ADR-010. The measure is 100 percent of pipeline runs in which every view compiles and the conformance test passes (FSD P1 A2.1.1).

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P1-E1001-APP is done: the `rwb_source_data` baseline holds P1's tables, the dictionary rows in `sys_objects` and `sys_fields`, the view `v_data_dictionary` and the data product rows (legacy RWB-E1-069 §3, RWB-E1-001 in the target).
- The per-service Flyway sequence of rwb-source-data exists with its own history table in schema `rwb_source_data`, and the baseline version has been applied on it (DP-15; RWB-PLT-E1044-CON).
- The ACE schema in DEV and SIT is at the head that holds the 21 Tier 1 tables of section 11, among them `account`, `payment`, `customer` and `efs_action` (ACE Schema PostgreSQL v1.sql; legacy RWB-E1-069 §3).
- The recovery migration account holds the ACE DBA role for the release window, so it can create a view in schema `recovery` and set a view owner (RWB-E1-044; legacy RWB-E1-069 §3).
- The roles `ace_view_owner` and the login `rwb_source_data` exist in DEV and SIT, with the grant block delivered by RWB-P1-E1069-DB (DP-02; Architecture v5 slides 11 and 29).
- The view definitions are available in `recovery_views.sql` of the Physical Schema folder; a view definition is copied from there and never rewritten by hand (legacy RWB-E1-069 §13).
- The module map of the service template is in the repository, and `recovery-modules.yaml` holds `sourceViews`, the 30 view names that BND-6 allows (legacy RWB-E1-069 §4 step 5; RWB-TE-001 in the target).
- RWB-P4-E1037-CON is published and the rwb-access guard library is on the classpath, so the authorise hop of DP-08 runs against the published contract and its fake from Day 1 (`POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise`, one hop, 2 s).
- RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON are published with their client libraries, so a parameter and a list of values are read as data and never as a constant (DP-06, DP-07).
- For the 14 Section B views only: RWB-ACE-001 is deployed in DEV and SIT and its 14 Tier 2 tables exist (DL43; the build dependency RWB-P1-ACE001-DB). Until then the features that read a Section B view stay behind their flags.
- The split of this legacy key across three stories, and the position of the two view migrations on the service sequence, are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0566; ASM-0807); the maker of every view definition and its checksum come from `recovery_views.sql`.

##### 4. Flow

1. Recovery developer: takes the 16 Section A view definitions and the three helper functions `recovery.ace_to_date`, `recovery.ace_to_boolean` and `recovery.ace_mask_value` from `recovery_views.sql` into the Section A migration of the service sequence, and writes no environment name in the file: the schema is the fixed `recovery` and the two role names come from the Environment and Deployment Design (TSD P1 T3.2; legacy RWB-E1-069 §4 steps 1 and 2).
2. Recovery developer: adds the second view migration for the 14 Section B views, and one SELECT grant per view is issued by RWB-P1-E1069-DB, not here (legacy RWB-E1-069 §4 step 7).
3. Pipeline: applies the baseline, then the Section A migration in DEV and then in SIT, on the service's own sequence (DP-15).
4. Pipeline: runs `ViewConformanceTest`: every view compiles, no constraint in schema `recovery` references `public`, every view has one `sys_objects` row and one `sys_fields` row per column, and the service login holds no privilege in `public` and no write on a view (legacy RWB-E1-069 §4 step 4).
5. Recovery developer: writes boundary rule BND-6 over the package of this service and adds the 30 view names to `recovery-modules.yaml` as the only allowed source objects (legacy RWB-E1-069 §4 step 5).
6. ACE team: applies RWB-ACE-001 with the 14 Tier 2 tables, and its migration grants SELECT on those tables to `ace_view_owner` (DL43; tracked in RWB-P1-E1069-DB).
7. Pipeline: applies the Section B migration in DEV and SIT after RWB-ACE-001 is reported deployed; 30 of 30 views compile and the features that read a Section B view come out from behind their flags (legacy RWB-E1-069 §4 step 8).
8. Recovery developer: serves the three read operations on `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` from `AceSourceReadRepository`, each one a SELECT on a view and nothing else; every read calls `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` once with the caller identity, the area, the right and the field IDs it is about to return, and returns the field clear or masked as answered (DP-08, DP-11).
9. Every other service and every agent reaches ACE data in step 8 and never in a view of its own (Architecture v5 slides 13, 41 and 45); a service that names a view fails its own boundary rule in RWB-ITG-E1069-ITG.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A Section A view does not compile | The Section A stage of the service sequence rolls back; no view from that run exists; the step names the view and the ACE column | Pipeline log: v_ace_account does not compile: column a.core_banking_system_date does not exist | AC1 |
| X2 | The Section B migration is applied before RWB-ACE-001 | The stage fails; no Section B view is created; the 16 Section A views and their features are unchanged | Pipeline log: relation public.valuation does not exist | AC3 |
| X3 | A recovery constraint references a table in `public` | The conformance test fails and the merge is blocked | fk_case_account_account_key references public.account; no constraint in recovery may reference another schema | AC4 |
| X4 | A view has no `sys_objects` row or a column has no `sys_fields` row | The conformance test fails and names the view and the column | v_ace_account.legacy_bucket has no data dictionary entry | AC5 |
| X5 | The service login holds a privilege in `public`, or a write on a view | The conformance test fails and names the privilege and the object | recovery_svc holds SELECT on public.account; the recovery role reads the views only | AC2 |
| X6 | A class of this service names a table in `public` | The build fails with boundary rule BND-6 and the class is named | Boundary rule BND-6 broken: AccountReader reads public.account. Read recovery.v_ace_account instead. | AC8 |
| X7 | A read asks for a field ID that the authorise answer does not cover | The field is returned masked; the read itself succeeds and no value is returned clear | None; the answer carries a marker per field ID, never text | Section 12.2 |
| X8 | The authorise call does not answer inside 2 s | The read is refused with 503 and no field is returned; no answer is guessed from a stale cache | MSG-P4-002 from the guard library; no body from this service | Section 12.2 |

X1 to X6 are the exception paths of RWB-E1-069 carried onto the split; X7 and X8 are the two paths the authorise hop of DP-08 adds. A second row for one ACE key in an extension table (legacy X7, SQLSTATE 23505) is RWB-P1-E1069-DB's path and is tested there.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against the published rwb-access, parameters and reference-data contracts and their fakes from Day 1; needs the `rwb_source_data` baseline and, for Section B, the ACE tables RWB-ACE-001 adds; it publishes the read path every later story uses |
| Negotiable | The view names and fields are frozen in the ACE Data Tier Map v1 and `recovery_views.sql`; the migration order, the test harness and the response shape are the squad's choice behind the contract |
| Valuable | One copy of source data, a boundary the database and the build enforce, one read path for 18 other services, and no load estate to build |
| Estimable | Two view migrations, three helper functions, one conformance test class, one boundary rule, one repository, three read operations and one authorise client |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests, as the primary slice of the legacy key |
| Testable | Every criterion in section 7 is one pipeline run, one catalog query or one refused statement with its SQLSTATE |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

**Target reading.** Every assertion above keeps its legacy wording; what changes is where it runs. `V0002__rwb_e1_069_ace_source_views.sql` (the 16 Section A views and the three helper functions, per TSD P1 T3.2) and `V0003__rwb_e1_069_ace_tier2_views.sql` (the 14 Section B views) become the next two versions of rwb-source-data's per-service Flyway sequence (DP-15), and the views they create stay in schema `recovery`, owned by `ace_view_owner`, because that is where the 30 views live and who owns them (DP-05, ADR-010); the role named `recovery_svc` in the legacy criteria is the `rwb_source_data` login of the target (DP-02; Architecture v5 slides 11 and 29). The grant block, the schema privileges, the `ace_view_owner` ownership and the four extension tables that AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC7 assert are delivered by RWB-P1-E1069-DB (external dependency X), so those assertions are executed against the objects and grants that story ships, not against a second copy; the dictionary counts and the field mapping of AC5 and AC6 are rwb-source-data's own rows in `sys_objects`, `sys_fields` and `data_product`, delivered with RWB-P1-E1001-APP; and boundary rule BND-6 of AC8 runs in this service's build and again across the other 18 logins in RWB-ITG-E1069-ITG. No criterion here reaches another service over a contract, so no contract-mock Given line is added, and no legacy line is dropped or reworded.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The recovery module reads ACE source data only through the 30 SELECT-only `recovery.v_ace_*` views: 16 now over tables ACE holds, 14 when RWB-ACE-001 lands. It loads, copies and transforms nothing | D-RCV-35 U1, U4; ADR-010 |
| BR2 | A view is owned by `ace_view_owner`, which holds SELECT on the ACE tables it reads and writes nothing. It holds no right in schema `recovery` other than the views it owns | D-RCV-35 U4; CTL-02 |
| BR3 | On ACE source data `recovery_svc` holds SELECT on the views and no privilege of any kind in `public`; PUBLIC holds nothing; no INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE is granted on a view. Its DML on the Workbench's own tables is granted by V0001 and is outside this story | D-RCV-35 U4; BR-P1-001-4; CTL-02 |
| BR4 | No constraint in schema `recovery` references a table or a type outside it. A link to an ACE record is a `varchar(255)` business-key column with no foreign key, because ACE cascades deletes on `account` | D-RCV-35 U4; BR-P1-001-3; ADR-010 |
| BR5 | Every view carries one `sys_objects` row and one `sys_fields` row per column, with the ACE source field and the data product | BR-P1-001; RWB-E1-064 |
| BR6 | A text date in ACE becomes a date through `recovery.ace_to_date`, and a Y/N flag becomes a boolean through `recovery.ace_to_boolean`; both return NULL rather than fail a read | BR-P1-001-7 |
| BR7 | An extension table holds a Workbench decision about an ACE record and never a copy of an ACE column. It is 1:1 with the ACE record on the ACE business key and carries the seven standard record columns | BR-P1-001-5 |
| BR8 | Boundary rule BND-6: no recovery class names a table in schema `public`; the only source objects it may name are the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views, read from the module map | REQ-DRI-006; RWB-TE-001 |
| BR9 | A Section B view is created only after its ACE table exists. Until then the feature that reads it stays behind its flag, and the Section B migration is a later Flyway version | ADR-010; DL43 |

**Where each rule lives in the target.** BR1, BR2, BR3 and BR7 are the grant and ownership rules, and the objects and statements that enforce them are RWB-P1-E1069-DB's; this story only asserts them through the conformance test and its own read path, and the role named `recovery_svc` in BR2 and BR3 is the `rwb_source_data` login of the target (DP-02; Architecture v5 slides 11 and 29). BR4 is a rule about schema `recovery`, so its constraint scan runs here, over the views' own schema, and repeats over the 19 `rwb_*` schemas in RWB-ITG-E1069-ITG. BR5 and BR6 are answered inside this service: the dictionary rows are rwb-source-data's own, and the three helper functions `ace_to_date`, `ace_to_boolean` and `ace_mask_value` ship with the Section A migration (TSD P1 T3.2). BR7 is RWB-P1-E1069-DB's tables. BR8 is this service's build rule, with the 30 view names in `recovery-modules.yaml`; the second half of the boundary, no `v_ace_*` view named outside rwb-source-data and no other service's schema named anywhere, is proven in RWB-ITG-E1069-ITG. BR9 is the deployment order of the Section B migration, and the flag on each Section B feature stays with its own story.

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It moves the service's Flyway sequence through two versions (Section A now, Section B with RWB-ACE-001) and changes no business row.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| a view absent from schema `recovery` | the Section A or Section B migration | Every statement compiles against the ACE head | The view exists, compiles and answers a select of one row |
| a Section B view absent | the Section B migration | RWB-ACE-001 is reported deployed | The 14 Section B views exist; the feature flags of their readers may be switched on |
| a branch that names `public` in a class | the build | Boundary rule BND-6 sees the reference | The build fails and no artifact is produced |
| an applied view version | a correction | A fix is needed | A new version is merged; the applied version is never edited |

##### 12. Contract

**12.1 REST operations provided**

The three read operations of the ACE read path on base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` (DP-13), one per read family of the views. Each returns the columns of its view for one business key, with the personal fields masked or clear as the authorise answer says (12.2).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/customers/{id}` | The customer behind `v_ace_customer`, with `id_no_masked` and `id_no_last4` only and never the clear identity number | Any authenticated caller with a Workbench role and a right on the data product of the customer, over the authorise contract | Idempotent by id and business date |
| GET | `/accounts/{id}` | The account behind `v_ace_account`, with its arrears, balance and classification fields | As above, on the data product of the account | Idempotent by id and business date |
| GET | `/collateral/{id}` | The collateral and asset behind `v_ace_collateral`, with `v_ace_collateral_detail` once the Section B view is deployed | As above, on the data product of the collateral | Idempotent by id and business date |

`GET /payments?accountId=`, `GET /business-days/{date}/ready`, `GET /business-days/{date}/status` and `GET /data-products/freshness` are not in this story: they are RWB-P1-E1013-APP (Architecture v5 slide 15, OUT and IN lines). The admin operations of the module (`/admin/jobs`, `/admin/reconciliation/results`, `/admin/data-products`, `/admin/data-dictionary/fields`, `/admin/data-contracts`, `/admin/lists` and the freshness read) belong to the other P1 stories; this story adds none of them and changes no path of theirs.

The response field names and the problem body of the three operations are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0566; ASM-0807); the story fixes the rule, one row per business key with the view's columns, and leaves the names to the contract in RWB-P1-E1069-CON.

**12.2 REST operations consumed**

| Method | Path | Owner | Use | Pattern |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | Once per read: the caller identity from the session, the capability area, the right, the case reference and the field IDs about to be returned; the answer names the decision code, the matrix version and the masking version, with a marker per field ID | DP-08, DP-11; one hop, 2 s timeout, cached per call only |

The answer carries no value, and this service returns the value clear or masked as answered. A refusal is passed on with the rwb-access message; a call that does not answer inside 2 s refuses the read with 503 and returns no field (X8). No other service is called at run time: the parameters and the lists of values reach this service through the client libraries of rwb-case (DP-06, DP-07), and the ACE data is read in this service's own view (DP-01, DP-05).

**12.3 Events published**

None. The topic of the service is `rwb.source-data.events.v1` with event names `rwb.source-data.<Event>.v1` (DP-14), and its two events `AceDataReady` and `AceDataLate` belong to RWB-P1-E1013-APP (Architecture v5 slides 15 and 41). This story publishes no event and writes no outbox row of its own.

**12.4 Events consumed**

None. A view migration is a deployment step, not a reaction to an event, and Architecture v5 slide 15 gives the service no consumed event ("none: Airflow call; fallback polls ACE batch record").

**12.5 Workflows and activities**

None. The two migrations, the conformance test and the three reads are synchronous steps. The Temporal activities `listEligibleAccounts` and `snapshot(page)` and the workflows `AceIngestCheck` and `reconciliation` of Architecture v5 slide 15 are other P1 stories; the task queue of this service is `rwb-source-data` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, and this story starts no workflow and no activity on it.

**12.6 Schedules**

None. No Temporal Schedule and no Quartz job sits in this story.

**12.7 Tables owned**

| Object | Schema | Owner | This story |
|---|---|---|---|
| the 30 `v_ace_*` views | `recovery` | View owner `ace_view_owner`; contract owner P1 rwb-source-data | Created by this story's two migrations; the view itself is a SELECT-only projection with no primary key and no foreign key |
| `sys_objects`, `sys_fields`, `data_product`, `v_data_dictionary` | `rwb_source_data` | P1 | Read by the conformance test and by AC5 and AC6; the rows are delivered with RWB-P1-E1001-APP and no row is written here |
| `party_ext`, `contact_point_ext`, `account_ext`, `valuation_ext` | `rwb_source_data` | P1 | **Not created here**: RWB-P1-E1069-DB creates them; this story asserts their columns and their dictionary fields only |

No table of another service is read and no foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01). No service table sits in schema `recovery`, which holds the 30 views and the three helper functions and nothing else.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.sourcedata`, modules `views` and `read`, with the published types in `...sourcedata.api`. Service base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`, schema `rwb_source_data`, views in schema `recovery`, topic `rwb.source-data.events.v1` (not published here), Temporal task queue `rwb-source-data` in namespace `rwb-recovery` (not used here).

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-02 | `recovery_svc` login | One login per service | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-05 is this story's own pattern: rwb-source-data is the one service that reads the `v_ace_*` views, and it publishes them onward as a contract. DP-02 is used, not delivered: the login and the grants are RWB-P1-E1069-DB's. DP-03 applies as one decision record per refused or masked read answered through the guard library, and this story adds no event of its own. DP-19 applies to the composite route of the screens that read a customer or an account, which this story serves and does not build.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `V0002__rwb_e1_069_ace_source_views.sql` (legacy name; the next version on the service sequence) | Migration | The three helper functions and the 16 Section A views, copied from `recovery_views.sql` |
| `V0003__rwb_e1_069_ace_tier2_views.sql` (legacy name; the version after it) | Migration | The 14 Section B views, copied from `recovery_views.sql` |
| `ViewConformanceTest` | Test | Four checks: every view compiles, no constraint references `public`, every view has dictionary rows, the service login has no privilege in `public` and no write on a view |
| `AceSourceReadRepository` | Repository | SELECT only on `recovery.v_ace_*`, one read method per view; names no `public` table and no other schema |
| `SourceReadService` | Service | Resolves the business key, reads the view, takes the authorise answer, applies the marker per field and returns the row |
| `AccessGuardClient` | Client | The rwb-access authorise contract through the guard library: one hop, 2 s timeout, no stale cache (DP-08, DP-11) |
| `SourceReadController` | Controller | The three read operations on `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`; RFC 9457 problem details |
| `SourceViewBoundaryRule` | ArchUnit rule in `RecoveryBoundaryTest` | Boundary rule BND-6 over this service's package: no class names a table in schema `public` |
| `recovery-modules.yaml` | Rule table | Gains `sourceViews`, the 30 view names that BND-6 allows |

**Migrations and sequence (DP-15).** The two view migrations sit on rwb-source-data's own Flyway sequence, after the baseline, in this order: Section A (helper functions and 16 views), then Section B (14 views). The legacy file names are kept as the source of the objects; the exact version numbers are assigned by the sequence owner at build time, and no monolith version number is reused. The statements create objects in schema `recovery` and are run under the ACE DBA role for the release window; the schema name is written as the fixed `recovery`, and no environment name appears in a file. The grant statements of the legacy migration are **not** in these files: they are RWB-P1-E1069-DB's migration, applied on the same sequence.

**Database.** This story creates 30 views and three helper functions in schema `recovery` and no table. It adds no foreign key, no index and no column to any table. The four extension tables are created by RWB-P1-E1069-DB, and the dictionary rows of the views come with RWB-P1-E1001-APP.

**Configuration and reference data**

- The 30-view list is frozen in the ACE Data Tier Map v1 and copied into `recovery-modules.yaml`; a change needs the data architect and the recovery tech lead.
- The view definitions are taken verbatim from `recovery_views.sql`; a rewritten view is a diff and fails its fixture.
- The three helper functions are `recovery.ace_to_date`, `recovery.ace_to_boolean` and `recovery.ace_mask_value`, with the rules of TSD P1 T3.2.
- The authorise contract, its 2 s budget and the masking answer are configuration of the guard library, not constants in this service (DP-08).
- The read path is a REST contract on `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` and not a shared Java interface, so the other 18 services and the agents reach ACE data through it and never through a view of their own (Architecture v5 slides 11, 13 and 45; DP-05, DP-11; GAP-0567; ASM-0808).
- The Section B read path stays behind the flag of the feature that reads it until the Section B migration is applied (BR9).
- The boundary rule is written once, in this service's build, and the module map it reads is the only place the 30 view names are listed; the proof over the other 18 logins is the integration slice (GAP-0566; ASM-0812).

**Build steps**

1. The Section A migration with the three helper functions and the 16 views, copied from `recovery_views.sql`, and its fixture against the ACE head (AC1).
2. `ViewConformanceTest` with its four checks and a failing fixture for each: a view that does not compile, a foreign key into `public`, a view column with no `sys_fields` row, and a privilege or a write found on the login (AC1 to AC5).
3. The Section B migration with the 14 views, and a pipeline stage that runs only after RWB-ACE-001 is reported deployed (AC3).
4. `AceSourceReadRepository` with one read method per view; a test that the service names no `public` table and no other schema (AC4, AC8).
5. `SourceReadService` with the authorise hop, the marker per field, the masked default and the 503 on a timeout (12.2, X7, X8).
6. The three read operations on the contract, with RFC 9457 problem details and the cache key of the read (12.1).
7. Boundary rule BND-6 and `recovery-modules.yaml`, with a fixture class on `public.account`, the same class on `recovery.v_ace_account`, and the module map read at run time (AC8).
8. The delivered-grants fixture that runs AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC7 against the objects and grants of RWB-P1-E1069-DB, so the criteria are tested once, where they are delivered.

**Feature flag.** None for the views: they are the read path, not a feature. Each Section B feature keeps the flag it already has until the Section B migration is applied (BR9); this story adds no flag of its own.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, SIT holds 30 compiling views and the three helper functions in schema `recovery`, the conformance test and boundary rule BND-6 appear in the pipeline report of main, and the three read operations answer against the grants delivered by RWB-P1-E1069-DB with the authorise answer of rwb-access.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| Conformance check 1 | A view does not compile | v_ace_account does not compile: column a.core_banking_system_date does not exist |
| Conformance check 2 | A constraint references `public` | fk_case_account_account_key references public.account; no constraint in recovery may reference another schema |
| Conformance check 3 | A view has no dictionary row | v_ace_account.legacy_bucket has no data dictionary entry |
| Conformance check 4 | The service login holds a privilege in `public` or can write a view | recovery_svc holds SELECT on public.account; the recovery role reads the views only |
| Build log | A class names a `public` table | Boundary rule BND-6 broken: AccountReader reads public.account. Read recovery.v_ace_account instead. |
| SQLSTATE 42501 | The service login selects a public table or writes a view | permission denied for schema public |
| SQLSTATE 23505 | A second row for one ACE key in an extension table | duplicate key value violates unique constraint party_ext_pkey |
| MSG-P4-002 | The authorise answer refuses the read | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The access entry of the read cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The five conformance, build-log and SQLSTATE texts are the legacy ones, unchanged, and are for developers; they are not part of the message standard. No `MSG-` ID of this story is new: MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P7-003 are raised by the rwb-access guard library on the authorise hop (DP-08), and a read refused because the authorise call timed out returns 503 with no body from this service (X8).

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story. The platform administrator reads the deployment result in the pipeline run and on SCR-44 Interface and job monitor, which shows the two view versions with their status and the conformance result under Platform administration R. A developer reads the conformance test and boundary rule BND-6 in the pull request checks. The customer and account panels of the case screen reach this service through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), which calls rwb-case and rwb-source-data in parallel, one hop each; the rendering of a masked field belongs to the screen owner.

TC-E1-069-02 and TC-E1-069-07 run against the grants and the four extension tables that RWB-P1-E1069-DB delivers, and the authorise hop of every read is tested at Component level inside the read operations of section 12.1. The `-ITG` copies of these cases belong to RWB-ITG-E1069-ITG and are not listed here.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the view list, the role names and the schema name are configuration and data, not constants in a service; `recovery-modules.yaml` carries the 30 view names and the boundary rule reads them.
- No personal data in logs, tests, events or prompts: test rows are synthetic; the customer view returns `id_no_masked` and `id_no_last4` only and never the clear identity number; the authorise answer carries a marker and a version, never a value.
- No read of a `public` table and no write to an ACE table: the database grants and boundary rule BND-6 enforce it, and a breach is a defect.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `v_ace_*` views: this service reads the views and no other schema, and every other service reads this service's contract (DP-01, DP-05).
- One hop and 2 s on the authorise call; a slow answer refuses the read and returns no field (DP-11).
- The views are forward only in PROD; a wrong view is corrected by a new migration, never by editing an applied one (DP-15).
- The grants, the login and the four extension tables are one story's delivery and one story's test: this story asserts them and never re-creates them.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-069 for rwb-access. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **security administrator (RW-SECADM), a reference data administrator (RW-REFADM) and a compliance and PDPA officer (RW-COMPLY)**, I want **the masking rows for the ACE-sourced personal fields held as data at the masking version in force, the masking answer served on the authorise decision that a source-data read takes before it returns an ACE-sourced field, and boundary rule BND-6 applied to the rwb-access package so that no class of this service names a `v_ace_*` view or a `public` table**, so that **rwb-access enforces the read-only ACE boundary on itself and answers the masking question for every caller while it reads no ACE data at all**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Only rwb-source-data reads the 30 read-only `recovery.v_ace_*` views (Architecture v5 slides 8, 9 and 41; ADR-010). Every other service, and every agent, asks for source data through rwb-source-data's contract, so the boundary is enforced in two places: the catalog, where the other 18 logins hold no privilege on the views and nothing in `public`, and the build, where boundary rule BND-6 fails a class that names a `public` table (legacy RWB-E1-069 BR1, BR3 and BR8). rwb-access owns the third piece: Recovery roles as data, scope, the masking policy and the DoA table (Architecture v5 slide 41), and it serves `POST /authorise`, `GET /me/permissions`, `GET /doa-limits` and `/masking-policies` (slide 14). It therefore holds the policy that masks the ACE-sourced personal fields and never the fields themselves: the `masking_rule` rows are keyed by the field IDs of the views, which is metadata about a field, not a read of it. This story is the rwb-access slice of legacy RWB-E1-069.

The legacy story enforces the boundary on one module with two grants and one build rule. In the target, that legacy key splits across five stories. RWB-P1-E1069-DB creates the per-service login, the grants and the four extension tables in the owner's schema; RWB-P1-E1069-APP writes the per-service Flyway sequence that creates the views in rwb-source-data's read path and runs the conformance test; RWB-ITG-E1069-ITG proves the grant model across the 19 logins end to end; and this story carries the policy side plus the boundary applied to rwb-access's own package. This slice re-specifies no view definition, no grant statement and no extension-table column: it keys the masking rows on the field IDs the dictionary publishes, answers the masking question on the authorise contract, and fails its own build on a view read or a `public` read. It meets REQ-RDF-002 (account, arrears and payment facts read from ACE through the views) by making the personal fields of those reads maskable by role, and REQ-DRI-006 (no component calls a system of record directly) by making a direct read in this service impossible to merge.

The policy pack this slice writes is the ACE-sourced slice of the masking version: one `masking_rule` row per field ID and role, `unmasked` true only where a role may see the field, and the last-four answer for every other role. The field IDs the pack must cover, the masking version label and the roster of roles that see a field unmasked are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0901; ASM-1622), (GAP-0902; ASM-1623) and (GAP-0903; ASM-1624); the story covers `DF-ACE-055` to `DF-ACE-074`, the 20 fields of `v_ace_customer`, at masking version `MASK-2026.12`, and treats an `unmasked` true row as the only allow.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P4-E1037-APP delivered the `rwb_access` baseline: the tables `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule`, `role_conflict` and `delegation_limit` exist with their dictionary rows (DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-044, DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204, DF-REF-205 to DF-REF-211, DF-REF-016 to DF-REF-026 and DF-REF-055 to DF-REF-062), and RWB-P4-E1037-CON published the authorise and masking operations this story answers behind.
- The local decision-record library and the topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` are live (DP-03, EV-08), so the masking answer of an authorised read can be recorded before it is returned.
- The build-rule harness of the service template is in the repository: the target form of legacy RWB-TE-001's `RecoveryBoundaryTest`, which reads its allowed source objects from a module map in the service and runs on every merge.
- The field catalogue exists in P1's dictionary: `sys_objects` and `sys_fields` hold `DF-ACE-055` to `DF-ACE-074` for `v_ace_customer`, with `DF-ACE-073` as `id_no_masked` and `DF-ACE-074` as `id_no_last4`. rwb-access reads neither table and holds no dictionary row of its own (GAP-0905; ASM-1626).
- The masking pack file for version `MASK-2026.12` is prepared by RW-REFADM and approved by RW-SECADM through the load path, and this story's migration applies the rows of its ACE-sourced slice. That the version label is `MASK-2026.12` is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0902; ASM-1623).
- The roster of roles that see a given field unmasked is not held by any source document; the pack file fixes it as data, and the story treats every role without an `unmasked` true row as masked (GAP-0903; ASM-1624).
- The parameters contract of rwb-case and its client library are live (DP-06), for the feature switch of the masking answer; the reference-data contract of rwb-case is live for LOV-CAPABILITY, LOV-ROLE and LOV-SCOPE (DP-07).
- The login is the rwb-access login (DP-02). The per-service login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0904; ASM-1625).
- The 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views exist in schema `recovery` and are owned and granted by RWB-P1-E1069-DB; this story neither creates, alters nor grants on them, and it asserts only that its own login holds nothing there.

##### 4. Flow

1. RW-REFADM prepares the masking pack file for version `MASK-2026.12` and RW-SECADM approves it on the load path: one row per field ID and role, `unmasked` true only where a role may see the field, and every other role absent (BR1, BR2).
2. rwb-access: the migration `V1069_1__ace_masking_pack.sql` writes the rows for the field IDs `DF-ACE-055` to `DF-ACE-074` into `masking_rule` in schema `rwb_access`, each with `masking_version` `MASK-2026.12` and a `valid_from` date; it copies no value of any field and no ACE row (BR3).
3. rwb-access: the version becomes visible to the read that resolves the version in force; a later version is loaded, approved and dated, and the previous rows stay readable with their `valid_to` (BR4). This slice runs no relay: DP-09 is not a pattern of this story (section 12.3).
4. rwb-source-data holds an ACE-sourced field for a caller and calls `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` with the caller identity from the session, the capability area, the right, the case reference and the field IDs it is about to return (DP-08, DP-11).
5. rwb-access: reads the caller's roles and the letters of the area from `role` and `permission` at the matrix version in force, and applies the scope and default-deny rules of RWB-P4-E1037-APP; no role code, area or letter is written in code (BR5).
6. rwb-access: resolves the masking answer per field ID from `masking_rule` at the masking version in force — `clear` only where a row for a role the caller holds, that field ID and that version says `unmasked` true, `masked` otherwise, including where no row exists (BR6, BR7).
7. rwb-access: the answer names the decision code, the matrix version, the masking version and a marker per field ID; it carries no value, clear or masked, and no last four digits (BR8).
8. rwb-access: the access entry is written through the decision-record library first, in the same transaction as the answer, with the field IDs and the markers only; a write that fails returns 503 MSG-P7-003 and no masking answer (BR9).
9. rwb-source-data returns the field masked or clear as answered; rwb-access has read no view, no `public` table and no other schema at any step of the flow (BR10).
10. Build: boundary rule BND-6 runs over the module map of the service on every merge, and a class of `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access` that names a `v_ace_*` view or a `public` table fails the build (BR11).
11. Deploy: the rwb-access login holds no SELECT on any of the 30 views and no privilege of any kind in `public`; the proof across all 19 logins is RWB-ITG-E1069-ITG, and this story asserts the two facts for its own login in its own test (BR12).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A requested field ID has no `masking_rule` row at the version in force | The field is answered masked; the decision itself is unchanged and no value is returned | None | AC4 |
| X2 | The caller holds no Workbench role at all | The call is refused before any masking answer is resolved | MSG-P4-001 | AC6 |
| X3 | The area or the right is absent for the caller's roles | The call is refused and no field ID is answered clear, so no masking version is named | MSG-P4-002 | AC6 |
| X4 | A class of the package names `recovery.v_ace_customer` | The build fails with boundary rule BND-6 and the class is named; nothing merges | Build log | AC7 |
| X5 | A class of the package names `public.customer` | The build fails with boundary rule BND-6 and the class is named; the fix is rwb-source-data's contract | Build log | AC7 |
| X6 | The masking version in force holds a gap for a personal field ID | The field stays masked and the gap is raised to RW-COMPLY naming the field ID and the version | None | AC4 |
| X7 | The access entry cannot be written | The answer is 503 and no masking answer is returned; an incident is raised | MSG-P7-003 | AC5, AC9 |
| X8 | The migration is applied a second time | Flyway reports the version as already applied; no row is written twice and no version is edited in place | None | AC1 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against the `rwb_access` baseline and the RWB-P4-E1037-CON fake; the views, the grants and the dictionary belong to the P1 stories and are not prerequisites of this build |
| Negotiable | The field-ID range, the masking version, the roster of unmasked roles and the feature switch are data rows and parameters; the story fixes the answer rule and the build rule only |
| Valuable | The personal fields of every ACE read are maskable by role from one place, and a direct view read inside this service cannot be merged |
| Estimable | One migration, one masking resolver, one build rule, one module map and one contract-fake path |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests, as a secondary slice of the legacy key |
| Testable | Every criterion in section 7 is one automated test with a synthetic fixture; no ACE data is needed |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

The nine criteria above are new and test only this deliverable: the masking rows of the ACE-sourced fields, the masking answer on the authorise decision, and the boundary of this service. The legacy criteria of RWB-E1-069 are owned elsewhere: AC1 to AC3 (the 16 and 14 view sets and their compilation) by RWB-P1-E1069-DB and RWB-P1-E1069-APP, AC4 and AC7 (the constraint rule and the four extension tables) by RWB-P1-E1069-DB, AC5 and AC6 (the dictionary rows and the delay-day mapping) by RWB-P1-E1069-APP, and AC8 (the boundary test) here and in RWB-ITG-E1069-ITG. No legacy criterion text is copied into this story.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The masking rows are data with a version: one row per field ID and role, `unmasked` true only where a role may see the field. No role code, field ID or masking version is written in Java | FSD P4 A2.5; BR-P4-005; TSD P4 T3.1 (`masking_rule`) |
| BR2 | Which roles see a given field unmasked is set by the pack owner, not by this story; the rows arrive by load and by this story's migration of the approved file | FSD P4 A2.5; TSD P4 T3.1 |
| BR3 | A `masking_rule` row names a field ID and the masking version; it never carries a value, a rendering of a value or a copy of an ACE row | TSD P4 T3.1 (DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204); FSD P1 BR-P1-001-6 |
| BR4 | A version is never edited in place: a change is a new masking version with its `valid_from`, and the previous rows stay readable with their `valid_to` | FSD P4 A2.4 AC-EXC-P4-004-02; TSD P4 T3.2 (LOV-VERSION-STATUS) |
| BR5 | The decision is refused before any masking answer where the caller holds no role, or where the area or the right is absent (default deny) | FSD P4 A2.4; VR-P4-004-1; MSG-P4-001 and MSG-P4-002 |
| BR6 | A field is `clear` only where a `masking_rule` row for a role the caller holds, that field ID and the masking version in force says `unmasked` true; the union of the caller's roles applies | FSD P4 A2.5; TSD P4 T3.1 |
| BR7 | A personal field with no covering row is `masked`, never `clear`; a gap in the pack masks and is alerted, and never opens a field | FSD P4 AC-EXC-P4-004-05; NFR-039 |
| BR8 | The answer carries a marker, the matrix version and the masking version; it never carries a value, a masked rendering or the last four digits of a field | FSD P4 A2.5; NFR-039; NFR-040 |
| BR9 | The access entry is written first, in the same transaction as the answer, through the local decision-record library; a failed write means 503 and no answer | FSD P4 A2.7 AC-EXC-P4-007-03; R-UNI-39; DP-03 |
| BR10 | rwb-access reads no ACE table, no `v_ace_*` view and no other service's schema: the field IDs are keys into its own policy, and the values are returned by rwb-source-data | Architecture v5 slides 8, 9 and 41; DP-01; DP-05 |
| BR11 | Boundary rule BND-6 fails the build when a class of `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access` names a `v_ace_*` view or a table in schema `public`; the allowed object list is read from the module map, and it is empty for this service | Legacy RWB-E1-069 BR8 and AC8; REQ-DRI-006; RWB-TE-001 |
| BR12 | The rwb-access login holds no SELECT on any of the 30 views and no privilege of any kind in `public`; PUBLIC holds nothing on the views | Legacy RWB-E1-069 BR3; ADR-010; DP-02 |
| BR13 | The clear identity number never leaves ACE: the customer view returns `id_no_masked` (`DF-ACE-073`) and `id_no_last4` (`DF-ACE-074`), so no masking row of this pack can open it | FSD P1 BR-P1-001-6; TSD P1 T3.1 (DF-ACE-073, DF-ACE-074) |
| BR14 | The feature switch is read as a parameter; off means every ACE-sourced field is answered masked, never clear | FSD P4 A2.5; DP-06 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| masking rows of a version in force | a new masking version is loaded, approved and in force | The pack is approved and carries a later `valid_from` | The new version is in force; the previous rows stay readable with their `valid_to` |
| a personal field ID with no covering row | an authorise request | Any role, any masking version | The field stays `masked`; the pack gap is alerted |
| a class of the service naming a `v_ace_*` view or a `public` table | the build | The rule sees the reference | The build fails with BND-6; no artifact is produced |

rwb-access holds no case state machine of its own (TSD P4 T4): the case, the treatment and the task states move in rwb-case and rwb-treatment, and this story neither reads nor writes them. The masking version moves from LOADED to APPROVED to IN_FORCE to SUPERSEDED or ROLLED_BACK on the load path (TSD P4 T3.2 LOV-VERSION-STATUS); this story reads the version in force and writes the rows of its own approved slice.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| rwb-access service identity (the rwb-access login, DP-02) | Serves the masking answer, writes the pack rows by migration, runs the boundary rule and writes the access entry |
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | Prepares the masking pack file for a version; no approval, no upload into another service and no rollback |
| RW-SECADM, security administrator | Approves a masking version; holds CRUDA in Platform administration (TSD P4 T6.1) |
| RW-COMPLY, Compliance and PDPA officer | Reads which masking version is in force and which field IDs it covers, through `GET /masking-policies`; receives the pack-gap alert |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Reads the masking version, the rows and the access entries |
| RW-CASEOWN, RW-PHONECOL and every other business role | Reads the masked or clear marker of a field they are entitled to ask about; may not change a row, a version or the roster |
| ACE view owner and ACE DBA | Not this story: the views and the grants stay with RWB-P1-E1069-DB and RWB-ACE-001 |
| No approval level from the delegation of authority applies | The story takes no business decision |

The per-service login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0904; ASM-1625); the story names it "the rwb-access login (DP-02)" until the platform DB story fixes it. The roles above are rows of the pack and of `role`; no role grants itself a row, and no role code is fixed in code.

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204 | `masking_rule` | id, role_code, field_id, unmasked, masking_version, valid_from, valid_to | Write (the rows of this story's migration); Read |
| DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-039 | `role` | role_code, role_name, role_class, default_scope | Read |
| DF-REF-040 to DF-REF-044 | `permission` | role_id, capability_area, letters, matrix_version | Read |
| DF-REF-205 to DF-REF-211 | `role_conflict` | role_code, conflicts_with, conflict_version | Read; no row changes here |
| DF-REF-016 to DF-REF-026 and DF-REF-055 to DF-REF-062 | `delegation_limit` | decision_code, approval_level, limit_version | Read; no row changes here |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 and DF-DEC-028 to DF-DEC-031 | access entry (local decision record) | decision code, actor, case ID, actions, decided at, hash chain, idempotency key | Write |
| DF-DEC-014 | access entry (local decision record) | actions (area, right, field IDs, marker, masking version) | Write |
| DF-ACE-055 to DF-ACE-074 | `v_ace_customer` (keyed by field ID, never read) | `cif_no` to `id_no_last4`, 20 fields | Not read and not written; named as `field_id` keys only |
| DF-ACE-073 and DF-ACE-074 | `v_ace_customer` (keyed by field ID, never read) | `id_no_masked`, `id_no_last4` | Not read and not written; the pair that means the clear identity number is unreachable |
| DF-ACE-059 | `v_ace_customer` (keyed by field ID, never read) | `date_of_birth` | Not read and not written; the no-row case of AC4 |

No ACE row, no view column and no other service's row is copied into `rwb_access`: a `masking_rule` row names a field ID and a version, and nothing else. The clear identity number never leaves ACE, because the view returns `id_no_masked` and `id_no_last4` and no masking row of this pack can open it (BR13). The field-ID range the pack must cover, and whether rwb-access may hold rows that reference the P1 field catalogue at all, are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0901; ASM-1622) and (GAP-0905; ASM-1626); the story keys its rows on the field IDs and holds no dictionary row. Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None new. The three operations of RWB-P4-E1037-CON on base `/api/recovery/access/v1` are served by this service, and this slice delivers the masking resolution behind two of them. It adds no path, no query parameter and no response field:

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/authorise` | Decide a role's read or action for a capability area, a case and a field list, and answer the mask of each field ID with the masking version | Any authenticated caller with a Workbench role | Idempotent by identity, area, right, case reference and field list within the cache window |
| GET | `/me/permissions` | The caller's resolved roles, scope, matrix version and masking version | Authenticated caller, own record only | Not applicable |
| GET | `/masking-policies` | The masking rows in force for a role and a field list: the marker per field ID and the version | Authenticated caller | Not applicable |

Request for `/authorise`: the caller identity from the session, the capability area, the right, the case reference and the field IDs. Answer: the decision code (`AC-READ` or `AC-DENY`), the matrix version, the masking version and a marker per field ID (`masked` or `clear`); the response field names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0901; ASM-1622). Errors: 401 no Workbench role (MSG-P4-001), 403 no letter for the area or right (MSG-P4-002), 404 case absent or out of scope, 503 access entry unwritable (MSG-P7-003).

The role read, the session read, the access-log search, the DoA read and the load paths are P4 surface delivered by other P4 stories (RWB-P4-E1037-APP, RWB-P4-E1039-APP, RWB-P4-E2013-APP, RWB-P4-AD002-APP); this story adds none of them.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. At run time rwb-access calls no service: the caller's identity arrives in the session, the case attributes for the scope test arrive in the request, and the parameters and reference-data values reach it through the client libraries of rwb-case (DP-06, DP-07). The one hop and the 2 s budget of DP-11 apply to the inbound call.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. This slice applies no DP-09 pattern and holds no relay of its own: the masking answer of an authorised read is a decision-record entry written through the local decision-record library (DP-03), whose payload is EV-08 on `rwb.decision-record.v1` and which the library publishes. This story adds no event, no topic and no outbox row of its own, and the access log is never a Kafka event of this service.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The masking version in force is read from `rwb_access` on each call; no topic is consumed here.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The masking answer is a synchronous REST answer in the caller's thread. The six-monthly access review list (JOB-18) belongs to RWB-P4-AD008-APP (Architecture v5 slide 44), and this story starts no workflow and no activity.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Temporal Schedule and no Quartz job sits in this story.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `role` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | Recovery roles as data; read here, no row written |
| `permission` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | Capability area, letters and matrix version; read here, no row written |
| `masking_rule` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | Which role sees which personal field unmasked, by masking version; the rows of the ACE-sourced slice are written by this story's migration |
| `role_conflict` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | Conflicting role pairs; read, no row written |
| `delegation_limit` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | DoA limits; read, no row written |
| access entry (local decision record) | P4 rows in `rwb_access`, written through the P7 decision-record library | The `AC-READ` and `AC-DENY` entries with the field IDs and the markers (DP-03) |
| `outbox_event`, `processed_event`, `idempotency_key` | PLT library, created in `rwb_access` | Outbox, inbox and idempotency objects (DP-09); this slice writes none of them |

No table of another service and no `v_ace_*` view is read and no foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01). The dictionary rows (`sys_objects`, `sys_fields`) stay with P1, and no `v_ace_*` object is created, altered or granted here.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| RWB-P4-E1037-CON fake | The authorise and masking operations | A granted read, a refused read and a no-row field, each with the masking answer |
| field-ID catalogue fixture | The P1 dictionary (`DF-ACE-055` to `DF-ACE-074`) | The 20 field IDs of `v_ace_customer` with `DF-ACE-073` as `id_no_masked` and `DF-ACE-074` as `id_no_last4`; no value and no row of ACE data |
| decision-record library stub | DP-03 | A healthy chain and a stopped chain for the 503 path |
| parameters and reference-data fakes | DP-06, DP-07 | The feature switch and LOV-CAPABILITY, LOV-ROLE and LOV-SCOPE |

The request and answer field names of `/authorise` are stubbed from the published fixture of RWB-P4-E1037-CON; their list is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0901; ASM-1622).

| Kafka | 0 published, 0 consumed | DP-09 is not applied; the access entry is a decision-record library write (EV-08) and no topic is added or consumed here |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access.policy`, module `policy`, in the service root `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`. The boundary rule lives in the test source tree of the same service, beside the template harness.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-02 | `recovery_svc` login | One login per service | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

This is a secondary slice: it adds no new build dependency of its own, and the metadata rows "Depends on (build)" and "Contract dependencies" stay exactly as this Work Package fixes them, with the platform contract libraries and DP-08's `RWB-PLT-E1037-CON` and `RWB-P4-E1037-CON` arriving with the baseline and its contract story. DP-05 applies as a prohibition for this service (no ACE view is read here, and the boundary rule enforces it), DP-11 as the inbound budget of the authorise call, and DP-19 as the screen route behind SCR-43 and SCR-47, which this story does not build.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `V1069_1__ace_masking_pack.sql` | Migration | Writes the `masking_rule` rows of the ACE-sourced field IDs at `MASK-2026.12`; copies no value |
| MaskingRepository | Repository | Reads `masking_rule` by `field_id`, `role_code` and `masking_version`; reads no other schema |
| MaskingAnswerResolver | Service | Unions the caller's roles, answers `clear` only on an `unmasked` true row and `masked` otherwise, and names the version |
| MaskingControllerPart | Controller contribution | Wires the resolver behind `POST /authorise`, `GET /me/permissions` and `GET /masking-policies` of RWB-P4-E1037-CON; adds no path |
| PackGapAlerter | Service | Raises the gap alert to RW-COMPLY for a personal field ID with no covering row |
| AccessEntryWriter | Service | Writes the access entry with the field IDs and the markers, first in the transaction, through the decision-record library |
| AceBoundaryRule | ArchUnit rule in the test source | BND-6 over the module map: a class of the package names no `v_ace_*` view and no `public` table |
| `access-modules.yaml` | Rule table | The package name and the allowed source object list, which is empty for this service |

**Database and migrations**

- Reads `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule`, `role_conflict` and `delegation_limit` in schema `rwb_access`; writes the access entry of the decision-record library.
- Migration in this story: `V1069_1__ace_masking_pack.sql` writes the rows for `DF-ACE-055` to `DF-ACE-074` at masking version `MASK-2026.12`. It adds no index: the read is covered by the baseline index on `masking_rule (role_code, field_id, masking_version)`, and this story repeats it in no table.
- The tables arrive with the `rwb_access` baseline, and no column is added. No row of `role`, `permission`, `role_conflict` or `delegation_limit` is written by this story; the matrix is loaded by RWB-P4-AD002-APP and the DoA rows by RWB-P4-E2013-APP.
- No `v_ace_*` object and no `public` object is created, altered or granted: the tables and grants of the legacy key belong to RWB-P1-E1069-DB, and the migration text belongs to RWB-P1-E1069-APP.

**Configuration and reference data**

- The masking version in force: `MASK-2026.12`, the label this Work Package fixes. That no source names the label is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0902; ASM-1623).
- The covered field IDs: `DF-ACE-055` to `DF-ACE-074`. Which ACE view fields the pack must cover is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0901; ASM-1622).
- The roster of unmasked roles: set by the pack owner in the pack file, with no row meaning masked. That no source holds the roster is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0903; ASM-1624).
- The allowed source object list of `access-modules.yaml` is empty for this service, and the 30 view names are not copied into it. A class may name rwb-source-data's contract only.
- The feature switch is `rwb.access.ace-masking-answer`, read as a parameter through the parameters contract (DP-06): off answers every ACE-sourced field masked and allows nothing clear.
- The login is the rwb-access login (DP-02): Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0904; ASM-1625).

**Build steps**

1. Migration `V1069_1__ace_masking_pack.sql` with the rows of the ACE-sourced slice and a failing fixture for a duplicated field ID and role; tests for AC1.
2. MaskingRepository and MaskingAnswerResolver with the union of the caller's roles and the no-row default; tests for AC2 and AC3.
3. The no-row path with the gap alert, and the refusal paths (no role, no letter) ordered before any masking answer; tests for AC4 and AC6.
4. The answer shape with the version and the marker only, and the 503 when the entry cannot be written; tests for AC5.
5. AccessEntryWriter with the field IDs and the markers on the entry, and no value; tests for AC9.
6. AceBoundaryRule and `access-modules.yaml` with a fixture class on `recovery.v_ace_customer`, the same class on `public.customer`, and the same class on the rwb-source-data contract; tests for AC7.
7. The privilege test of AC8 as a container test with a session as the rwb-access login against the 30 view names.
8. A contract-fake run of the whole path, so the story builds before rwb-source-data and the load path are live.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.access.ace-masking-answer`, read as a parameter; off answers every ACE-sourced field masked and still fails the build on a view or `public` read.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, `masking_rule` holds the rows of `MASK-2026.12`, the authorise answer names the masking version for every field ID, the build is green and red on the two fixtures of the boundary rule, and a session as the rwb-access login holds no privilege on any of the 30 views and none in `public`.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | The token holds no Workbench role | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The area or the right is absent for the caller's roles | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The access entry cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| Build log | A class names a `v_ace_*` view or a `public` table | Boundary rule BND-6 broken: {class} names {object}. A recovery class names no ACE view and no public table. |
| Privacy Kafka | A pack fails its scope check; no value and no identity number is carried | ACE PII logging path (INT-22) |

For MSG-P4-002 in this story, {action} names the action the caller tried — for example "read the customer identity number" — and never a case fact or a field value. The build-log wording is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0906; ASM-1627); the rule fails the build on the class and the object either way. No `MSG-` ID applies to the masking answer itself: it returns a marker and a version, never text.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen is built by this story. SCR-47 Personal data shows the masking versions and the field IDs they cover, and the Compliance and PDPA officer and the security administrator read it there; SCR-43 Roles and access shows the roles, the permissions and the scope. Both screens are served by the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), which calls rwb-access for the policy and rwb-source-data for any value, one hop each. The rendering of a masked field on a screen belongs to the screen owner, not here: this story returns the marker and the version, and no rendering. The screen fields and the field-level masking of the composite route are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0901; ASM-1622).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the roles, capability areas, letters, field IDs, masking rows and masking version are data rows read with the version in force. No role code, area, letter or field-ID list appears in Java, and the boundary rule reads its allowed object list from the module map.
- No personal data in events, logs, workflow inputs, tests or prompts: the answer carries a marker and a version only, the access entry carries IDs and field IDs only, and every test row is synthetic (`DF-ACE-073` and `DF-ACE-074` are named, never rendered).
- The clear identity number stays in ACE: the customer view returns `id_no_masked` and `id_no_last4`, this service never reads them and no pack row can open them.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `v_ace_*` views — and this service reads neither: a class that names a view fails the build, and the pointer to the value is rwb-source-data's contract.
- No cross-schema read and no cross-schema key: `rwb_access` holds no foreign key into another schema and no copy of a case, customer or ACE row (DP-01). The dictionary stays with P1.
- The access entry is written first, in the same transaction as the answer, through the decision-record library; a failed write means 503 and no answer (BR9).
- A missing row, a missing permission row and a missing role all resolve to masked or refused, never to clear and never to allow (BR5, BR7, BR14).
- One migration per story in the service's own Flyway sequence (DP-15); an applied version is never edited, and a change is a new version with a later `valid_from`.
