**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-069 for the ACE database work of rwb-source-data. The single `recovery` schema of the monolith is replaced by one schema and one login per service (DP-01, DP-02; Architecture v5 slides 8, 9 and 29): the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views stay in schema `recovery`, owned by `ace_view_owner`, and only the `rwb_source_data` login holds SELECT on them; the four extension tables `party_ext`, `contact_point_ext`, `account_ext` and `valuation_ext` move with the service into schema `rwb_source_data`. The grant block of legacy section 12 is reused with the schema fixed to `recovery` and the service role renamed `rwb_source_data`. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As an **ACE database engineer**, I want **the `rwb_source_data` login of this service and the grants it holds, the view owner `ace_view_owner` with SELECT on the 21 Tier 1 and 14 Tier 2 ACE tables, SELECT on each of the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views and nothing of any kind in `public`, the four extension tables `party_ext`, `contact_point_ext`, `account_ext` and `valuation_ext` in schema `rwb_source_data` with their primary keys, their standard record columns, the `ck_contact_point_ext_type` check and their 49 field IDs, and a schema in which no constraint names `public` and every link to an ACE record is a `varchar(255)` business key with no foreign key**, so that **one copy of ACE source data serves the Workbench without a second copy, without a write path into ACE data, and with a catalog that refuses a breach instead of a review that hopes**.

This is the database slice of legacy RWB-E1-069. It delivers:

- the `rwb_source_data` login of this service, and the grant set it holds: USAGE on schema `recovery`, SELECT on each of the 30 views, one GRANT and one ALTER VIEW OWNER per view, no privilege in `public` and no write on a view (DP-02, DP-05);
- the view owner `ace_view_owner`: USAGE on schema `public` and SELECT on the 21 Tier 1 tables of section 11, SELECT on the 14 Tier 2 tables once RWB-ACE-001 lands, the ownership of the 30 views, and no DML;
- the four extension tables in schema `rwb_source_data`, with their columns, their primary keys, the `ck_contact_point_ext_type` check and the 49 field IDs `DF-EXT-001` to `DF-EXT-049`;
- the schema privileges and the PUBLIC revokes;
- the schema checks: no constraint in `rwb_source_data` names `public`, and every ACE link is a `varchar(255)` business key with no foreign key;
- the migration set on rwb-source-data's per-service Flyway sequence (DP-15), with a repeated run that changes nothing.

It does not create, alter or own the view SQL, the conformance test or the read contract: those are RWB-P1-E1069-APP. It does not prove the grant matrix across the 19 logins: that is RWB-ITG-E1069-ITG. It writes no application code and no REST operation.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story proved the boundary against one schema: 30 SELECT-only views over the ACE tables, one view owner, one service role, boundary rule BND-6 and a conformance test in the pipeline. In the target the same objects must work across 19 schemas and 19 logins, where the ownership rule is enforced by grants and not by separate servers (Architecture v5 slide 29: "Ownership is enforced by grants, not by separate servers").

This story is the grant and ownership half of that proof. It fixes who may read the views (the `rwb_source_data` login of this service and no other), who owns them (`ace_view_owner`, which holds SELECT on the ACE tables they read and nothing else), and where the Workbench's own decisions about an ACE record live (the four extension tables, in the service's own schema, keyed by the ACE business key and holding no copy of an ACE column). Everything else follows from those three facts: a direct read of a `public` table fails at the database, a write on a view fails at the database, a second row for one ACE key fails on the primary key, and no service can reach another service's rows because each login is granted on its own schema only (DP-01, DP-02; Architecture v5 slides 8, 11, 29 and 45).

Serves REQ-RDF-002 (ACE source data read only through the views) and REQ-DRI-006 (no component calls a system of record directly). The measure is the one the legacy story set: 100 percent of pipeline runs in which every view compiles, every grant is as specified and the conformance test passes (FSD P1 A2.1.1). The business value is not restated here: this story adds no new one.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The per-service Flyway sequence of rwb-source-data exists with its own history table in schema `rwb_source_data`, and the baseline version has been applied on it (DP-15; RWB-PLT-E1044-CON).
- The 19 `rwb_*` schemas and their logins are created in DEV and SIT by the platform DB story RWB-PLT-NF06-DB, with the names fixed in the Environment and Deployment Design; the login of this service is `rwb_source_data` (Architecture v5 slides 11 and 29). Where the login already exists, this story asserts it and issues the grants; where it does not, it is created once for this service and never a second time.
- The credential of the login and its rotation are held by the platform, and no credential appears in a migration, a script or a runbook. That the platform DB story rather than this story issues the credential is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0568; ASM-0809).
- Schema `recovery` exists and holds the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views and the three helper functions `recovery.ace_to_date`, `recovery.ace_to_boolean` and `recovery.ace_mask_value`, created by RWB-P1-E1069-APP on the same sequence; the grant migrations of this story are applied after the views they grant on.
- The ACE schema in DEV and SIT is at the head that holds the 21 Tier 1 tables of section 11, among them `account`, `payment`, `customer` and `efs_action` (ACE Schema PostgreSQL v1.sql; legacy RWB-E1-069 §3).
- The recovery migration account holds the ACE DBA role for the release window, so it can grant on schema `public`, create a role and set a view owner (RWB-E1-044; legacy RWB-E1-069 §3).
- The four extension tables are taken verbatim from Physical Schema v6 (legacy RWB-E1-069 §13) with the field IDs of TSD P1 T3.5: `DF-EXT-001` to `DF-EXT-012` on `party_ext`, `DF-EXT-013` to `DF-EXT-026` on `contact_point_ext`, `DF-EXT-027` to `DF-EXT-035` on `account_ext` and `DF-EXT-036` to `DF-EXT-049` on `valuation_ext`.
- The 30-view list is frozen in the ACE Data Tier Map v1 and in `recovery_views.sql`; this story grants on those 30 names and on no other object (legacy RWB-E1-069 §13).
- For the 14 Tier 2 tables only: RWB-ACE-001 is deployed in DEV and SIT (DL43), and its migration grants SELECT on those tables to `ace_view_owner`; until then the Tier 2 grant of this story is not applied and the Section B views stay behind their flags.
- No approval is required to run a Draft migration on a development database; the migration is released to SIT only after the tests in section 16 pass.

##### 4. Flow

1. The ACE database engineer checks out the rwb-source-data migration folder and confirms the highest applied version on the service sequence (the baseline).
2. The engineer writes the first migration: the four extension tables, copied from Physical Schema v6 with their primary keys, their standard record columns and the `ck_contact_point_ext_type` check (BR7).
3. The engineer writes the Section A grant migration, run as the ACE schema owner: USAGE on schema `public` and SELECT on the 21 Tier 1 tables for `ace_view_owner`, one ALTER VIEW OWNER statement per view, USAGE on schema `recovery` and one SELECT grant per view for `rwb_source_data`, and the PUBLIC revoke (legacy RWB-E1-069 §12).
4. The engineer writes the Section B grant migration: SELECT on the 14 Tier 2 tables for `ace_view_owner`, one ALTER VIEW OWNER statement per Section B view, one SELECT grant per view for `rwb_source_data`; it is applied only after RWB-ACE-001 is reported deployed (BR9).
5. The engineer writes the schema checks of the pipeline: no constraint in `rwb_source_data` names `public`, every ACE link column is a `varchar(255)` business key with no foreign key, and the login holds no privilege outside its own schema and schema `recovery`.
6. The migration pipeline applies the baseline, this story's migrations and the two view migrations of RWB-P1-E1069-APP in the fixed order on the sequence, first to an empty schema and then to a copy of the SIT schema.
7. The pipeline runs the grant checks: a session as `rwb_source_data` selects one row from each of the 30 views, is refused on `public.account` with SQLSTATE 42501, and is refused on insert, update and delete on a view; a session as `ace_view_owner` is checked for ownership and for SELECT only; the test role `rwb_no_grant` is refused on a view.
8. The pipeline runs the duplicate-key test in a transaction it rolls back, and records the result; a repeated run of any migration changes nothing.
9. The engineer records each migration in the release notes of the sequence, with its version number and its checksum.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message |
|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A grant migration runs before the view migration it grants on | The statement fails on the missing relation and the stage stops; no grant is recorded | Pipeline error, no message id |
| X2 | The login `rwb_source_data` does not exist when the grant runs | The statement fails on the missing role; the login is created once for this service, by this story's migration or by the platform DB story, and the grant is re-run | Database error, no message id |
| X3 | The login holds a privilege in `public`, or a write on a view | The grant check fails the build and names the privilege and the object | recovery_svc holds SELECT on public.account; the recovery role reads the views only |
| X4 | A constraint in `rwb_source_data` names a table in `public` | The schema check fails the build and names the constraint | fk_case_account_account_key references public.account; no constraint in recovery may reference another schema |
| X5 | An ACE link column is not `varchar(255)`, or carries a foreign key | The schema check fails the build and names the column | Check finding, no message id |
| X6 | A second row is written for an ACE key already in an extension table | The write is refused; the first row is unchanged | SQLSTATE 23505 duplicate key value violates unique constraint party_ext_pkey |
| X7 | An extension table already exists in the sequence | The repeatable check refuses to create it twice and the migration is marked as already applied | Pipeline error, no message id |
| X8 | A migration is applied a second time | Flyway reports the version as already applied; no object, row or grant changes | None |

X3, X4 and X6 are the legacy exception paths X5, X3 and X7 of RWB-E1-069 carried onto the split, with the role renamed and the schema named `rwb_source_data`; X1, X2, X5, X7 and X8 are the paths the per-service sequence and the 19-login split add.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | One migration for the four tables and two grant migrations, on the service's own sequence; nothing to build against and no application code |
| Negotiable | Constraint and index names follow the platform naming library; the column set, the primary keys, the check and the grant list are fixed by the legacy story and the TSD |
| Valuable | The read path of 19 services is granted from one place, and the Workbench's own decisions about an ACE record have a schema that cannot write to ACE |
| Estimable | Four tables, one check, two grant migrations, one PUBLIC revoke and five schema checks |
| Small | Days, not weeks, with the catalogue checks |
| Testable | Every criterion in section 7 is one catalogue query, one refused statement with its SQLSTATE, or one pipeline run |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin

  Background:
    Given the ACE schema in DEV holds the 21 Tier 1 tables of section 11, among them public.account, public.payment, public.customer and public.efs_action

  Scenario: AC2 The login reads each of the 30 views and is refused on public.account (new, D-RCV-60)

  Scenario: AC3 The login holds no write on any view (new, D-RCV-60)

    Then no INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE privilege appears for the login on any of the 30 views
    Then the migration grants one view at a time and holds no "GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA recovery"
    Then "REVOKE ALL ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA recovery FROM PUBLIC" is in the migration and PUBLIC holds nothing on any of the 30 views

  Scenario: AC4 ace_view_owner owns the views and holds SELECT on the ACE tables only (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the 21 Tier 1 tables of section 11 and, after RWB-ACE-001, the 14 Tier 2 tables

    Then "ace_view_owner" owns each of the 30 views, through one ALTER VIEW OWNER statement per view

    Then it holds SELECT on the 14 Tier 2 tables once RWB-ACE-001 is applied

    Then it holds no right in schema recovery other than the views it owns

  Scenario: AC5 The four extension tables exist with their keys, the contact-type check and 49 columns (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given schema rwb_source_data at the migration that creates the four extension tables

    Then party_ext holds 12 columns with person_key as its primary key
    Then contact_point_ext holds 14 columns with contact_key as its primary key and the check ck_contact_point_ext_type that contact_type is PHONE, EMAIL or ADDRESS
    Then account_ext holds 9 columns with account_key as its primary key
    Then valuation_ext holds 14 columns with valuation_key as its primary key
    Then the four tables hold 49 columns in all and 49 dictionary fields, DF-EXT-001 to DF-EXT-049

  Scenario: AC6 A duplicate ACE business key is refused with SQLSTATE 23505 (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given one row in party_ext for person_key "P0000123" and one row in account_ext for account_key "ACC0000017"
    When a second party_ext row is written for person_key "P0000123" inside a transaction
    Then the write fails with SQLSTATE 23505 and the message names party_ext_pkey
    Then party_ext holds one row for "P0000123"
    When a second row is written for the same contact_key and the same valuation_key
    Then each write fails with SQLSTATE 23505 and each table holds one row for that key
    Then the transaction is rolled back and no row of the test survives

  Scenario: AC7 No constraint names public and every ACE link is a business key (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the applied schema rwb_source_data
```

These eight criteria are new and prove only the database artefacts in the story title: the login, the grants, the view owner, the four extension tables and the schema boundary. No legacy acceptance criterion text is repeated here. The legacy criteria these grants and tables answer are AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4 and AC7 of RWB-E1-069 — the view sets and their compilation, the read-only role, the constraint rule and the four extension tables — and they are proven end to end across the 19 real logins in RWB-ITG-E1069-ITG; AC5, AC6 and AC8 of the legacy story are the dictionary, the delay-day mapping and the build rule, and they belong to RWB-P1-E1069-APP.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The recovery module reads ACE source data only through the 30 SELECT-only `recovery.v_ace_*` views: 16 now over tables ACE holds, 14 when RWB-ACE-001 lands. It loads, copies and transforms nothing | D-RCV-35 U1, U4; ADR-010 |
| BR2 | A view is owned by `ace_view_owner`, which holds SELECT on the ACE tables it reads and writes nothing. It holds no right in schema `recovery` other than the views it owns | D-RCV-35 U4; CTL-02 |
| BR3 | On ACE source data `recovery_svc` holds SELECT on the views and no privilege of any kind in `public`; PUBLIC holds nothing; no INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE is granted on a view. Its DML on the Workbench's own tables is granted by V0001 and is outside this story | D-RCV-35 U4; BR-P1-001-4; CTL-02 |
| BR4 | No constraint in schema `rwb_source_data` or schema `recovery` references a table or a type outside it. A link to an ACE record is a `varchar(255)` business-key column with no foreign key, because ACE cascades deletes on `account` | D-RCV-35 U4; BR-P1-001-3; ADR-010 |
| BR5 | Every view carries one `sys_objects` row and one `sys_fields` row per column, with the ACE source field and the data product | BR-P1-001; RWB-E1-064 |
| BR6 | A text date in ACE becomes a date through `recovery.ace_to_date`, and a Y/N flag becomes a boolean through `recovery.ace_to_boolean`; both return NULL rather than fail a read | BR-P1-001-7 |
| BR7 | An extension table holds a Workbench decision about an ACE record and never a copy of an ACE column. It is 1:1 with the ACE record on the ACE business key and carries the seven standard record columns | BR-P1-001-5 |
| BR8 | Boundary rule BND-6: no recovery class names a table in schema `public`; the only source objects it may name are the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views, read from the module map | REQ-DRI-006; RWB-TE-001 |
| BR9 | A Section B object is created only after its ACE table exists. Until then the feature that reads it stays behind its flag, and the Section B grant is a later Flyway version | ADR-010; DL43 |

**Where each rule lives in the target.** BR2, BR3 and BR7 are this story's: the ownership, the grant set and the four tables are the objects it creates and the statements it runs, and the role named `recovery_svc` in BR2 and BR3 is the `rwb_source_data` login of the target (DP-02; Architecture v5 slides 11 and 29). BR4 is split by schema — the constraint scan over `rwb_source_data` runs here, the scan over schema `recovery` and over the 19 `rwb_*` schemas runs in RWB-P1-E1069-APP and RWB-ITG-E1069-ITG. BR1 and BR5 are asserted here and delivered elsewhere: the view SQL is RWB-P1-E1069-APP's and the dictionary rows are RWB-P1-E1001-APP's. BR6 is delivered by the helper functions of the Section A migration, in RWB-P1-E1069-APP. BR8 is a build rule and lives in that story's build, not in the database. BR9 is the order in which the Section B grants are applied, and this story is the one that applies them.

##### 9. State transitions

None in the runtime sense: a table has no state machine and this story changes no business row. The states this story moves through are the migration states of the service's Flyway history (pending, applied, failed, undone), one per version of this story's set.

| Item | States |
|---|---|
| a migration of this story | Pending, applied, failed, undone; an applied version is never edited |
| the login | Present and granted, or absent and named by the preflight; never a member of another service's login role |
| a grant | Held on a view or a table, refused with SQLSTATE 42501, or granted to PUBLIC, which is a failure in every schema |
| an extension row | One row per ACE key, or the second row refused with SQLSTATE 23505 |
| a constraint | Inside `rwb_source_data`, or naming `public`, which is a failure that blocks the merge |

The login is named `rwb_source_data` (Architecture v5 slides 11 and 29; DP-02). Its credential and the rotation policy are held by the platform DB owner, and no personal name and no credential appears in a migration, a script or a runbook.

|---|---|---|---|
| party_ext | rwb_source_data | P1 | Created: 12 columns, primary key `person_key` varchar(255) |
| contact_point_ext | rwb_source_data | P1 | Created: 14 columns, primary key `contact_key` varchar(255), check `ck_contact_point_ext_type` |
| account_ext | rwb_source_data | P1 | Created: 9 columns, primary key `account_key` varchar(255) |
| valuation_ext | rwb_source_data | P1 | Created: 14 columns, primary key `valuation_key` varchar(255) |

No table of another service and no `v_ace_*` view is created, altered or dropped here, and no service table other than these four is in this story. The 30 views are objects of schema `recovery`, created by RWB-P1-E1069-APP and owned by `ace_view_owner`; this story grants on them and writes no view definition. The dictionary tables `sys_objects`, `sys_fields` and `data_product` are rwb-source-data's own and are delivered with RWB-P1-E1001-APP; this story writes no row of them.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Sequencing.** rwb-source-data's Flyway sequence is owned by the platform; the V0001 baseline creates the schema, the history table and the standard record columns (DP-15). This story adds the extension-table migration and the two grant migrations, and the two view migrations of RWB-P1-E1069-APP sit between them:

| Position on the sequence | File | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| baseline | from the platform DB story | Schema `rwb_source_data`, history table, standard record columns |
| next | `..._rwb_e1_069_extension_tables.sql` | The four extension tables, their primary keys and the `ck_contact_point_ext_type` check |
| next | `V0002__rwb_e1_069_ace_source_views.sql` (RWB-P1-E1069-APP) | The three helper functions and the 16 Section A views in schema `recovery` |
| next | `..._rwb_e1_069_ace_source_views_grant.sql` | The Section A grant block: `ace_view_owner`, the 21 Tier 1 tables, the view ownership, the login's SELECT on the 16 views and the PUBLIC revoke |
| next | `V0003__rwb_e1_069_ace_tier2_views.sql` (RWB-P1-E1069-APP) | The 14 Section B views |
| next | `..._rwb_e1_069_ace_tier2_views_grant.sql` | The Section B grant: SELECT on the 14 Tier 2 tables for `ace_view_owner`, the view ownership and the login's SELECT on the 14 views |

The legacy migration names `V0002__rwb_e1_069_ace_source_views.sql` and `V0003__rwb_e1_069_ace_tier2_views.sql` are recorded as the source of the objects they hold; the exact version numbers of this story's three migrations are assigned by the sequence owner at build time, and no monolith version number is reused. Until RWB-ACE-001 is reported deployed, the last two positions are not applied and the features that read a Section B view stay behind their flags (BR9).

The platform dependency of the sequence is `RWB-PLT-E1044-CON`: it is not in this story's "Depends on (build)" list, which the Work Package fixes as None, so it is recorded here as a note and not as a metadata dependency (GAP-0568; ASM-0811).

DP-01, DP-02, DP-05 and DP-15 are the subject of this story: one schema, one login, one read path and one sequence. DP-03, DP-06, DP-07, DP-08, DP-11 and DP-19 are named for completeness of the pattern set: this story writes no decision record, calls no contract, starts no workflow and serves no screen, and their build dependencies stay with the application story.

**Grant block (the legacy section 12 block, with the schema fixed and the login renamed)**

```sql
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO ace_view_owner;
GRANT SELECT ON public.account, public.payment, public.customer, public.phone, public.email,
     public.address, public.ca_relation, public.aa_relation, public.collateral, public.asset,
     public.efs_action, public.efs_action_code, public.efs_assignment,
     public.bucket_log_snapshot, public.product, public.branch, public.bot_holiday,
     public.ace_case, public.cfsc_mg_ssme_tdr_case, public.tdr_calculation,
     public.ai_recommended_plan
     TO ace_view_owner;

ALTER VIEW recovery.v_ace_account OWNER TO ace_view_owner;
-- one ALTER VIEW OWNER statement for each of the 16 views

GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA recovery TO rwb_source_data;
GRANT SELECT ON recovery.v_ace_account TO rwb_source_data;
-- one GRANT per view, 16 in the Section A grant and 30 in all; never GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA recovery

REVOKE ALL ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA recovery FROM PUBLIC;
```

The Section B grant adds, once RWB-ACE-001 is deployed:

```sql
GRANT SELECT ON public.ace_batch_run, public.valuation, public.collateral_detail,
     public.npa_asset, public.npa_sale, public.lawsuit, public.hearing, public.pod_receipt,
     public.gl_write_off, public.collins_score, public.party_product,
     public.credit_decision, public.esign_request, public.iam_group
     TO ace_view_owner;

ALTER VIEW recovery.v_ace_batch_status OWNER TO ace_view_owner;
-- one ALTER VIEW OWNER statement for each of the 14 views

GRANT SELECT ON recovery.v_ace_batch_status TO rwb_source_data;
-- one GRANT per view for the 14 Section B views
```

No `GRANT ... ON ALL TABLES` appears in any migration that touches the views, PUBLIC receives nothing, and the login receives no write privilege on a view and no privilege at all in `public`.

**Table definitions** (verbatim from Physical Schema v6, legacy RWB-E1-069 §13)

- `party_ext`: `person_key` varchar(255) primary key, `vulnerable`, `deceased_override`, `bankruptcy`, `fraud_flag` boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false, `is_active` boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true, `state` varchar(40), `version` integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, `created_at` and `updated_at` timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), `created_by` and `updated_by` uuid.
- `contact_point_ext`: `contact_key` varchar(255) primary key, `contact_type` varchar(10) NOT NULL, `consent_given` boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false, `consent_at` and `verified_at` timestamptz, `failed_count` integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, `source` varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'WORKBENCH', `is_active`, `state`, `version`, `created_at`, `created_by`, `updated_at`, `updated_by`, and the check `ck_contact_point_ext_type` that `contact_type` is PHONE, EMAIL or ADDRESS.
- `account_ext`: `account_key` varchar(255) primary key, `dispute_open` boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false, `is_active`, `state`, `version`, `created_at`, `created_by`, `updated_at`, `updated_by`.
- `valuation_ext`: `valuation_key` varchar(255) primary key, `accepted` boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false, `accepted_at` timestamptz, `accepted_by` and `valuer_partner_id` uuid, `stale_flag` boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false, `age_days` integer, `is_active`, `state`, `version`, `created_at`, `created_by`, `updated_at`, `updated_by`.

The four tables hold 49 columns in all, which are the 49 fields `DF-EXT-001` to `DF-EXT-049`. The primary key of each is the ACE business key: there is no `id` column and there is no foreign key into `public`, and `valuer_partner_id` carries no foreign key (TSD P1 T3.5).

**Schema privileges and revokes.** The login owns schema `rwb_source_data`, which carries USAGE and the table privileges the application story needs. On the ACE side it holds USAGE on schema `recovery` and SELECT on each of the 30 views, and nothing else: no USAGE on `public`, no privilege on a `public` table, no write on a view, and no grant on another service's schema. PUBLIC is revoked on all tables of schema `recovery`, and no grant to PUBLIC is written in any migration of this story.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `..._rwb_e1_069_extension_tables.sql` | Migration | The four extension tables, their primary keys, their standard record columns and the `ck_contact_point_ext_type` check |
| `..._rwb_e1_069_ace_source_views_grant.sql` | Migration | The Section A grant: `ace_view_owner`, the 21 Tier 1 tables, the 16 view owners, the login's SELECT on the 16 views, the PUBLIC revoke |
| `..._rwb_e1_069_ace_tier2_views_grant.sql` | Migration | The Section B grant: the 14 Tier 2 tables, the 14 view owners and the login's SELECT on the 14 views |
| `SchemaBoundaryCheck` | Pipeline check | No constraint in `rwb_source_data` names a schema outside it; every ACE link is `varchar(255)` with no foreign key |
| `GrantCheck` | Pipeline check | The login's grants, the view owner's ownership and privileges, the refusals with SQLSTATE 42501 and PUBLIC empty |
| `ExtensionKeyCheck` | Pipeline check | The four tables' columns, primary keys, the check, the 49 field IDs and the duplicate-key refusal |

**Build steps**

1. The extension-table migration with the four tables, their primary keys and the check, and a failing fixture for a duplicate name (AC5, AC7).
2. The Section A grant migration with the 21 Tier 1 table names, the 16 view owners, the 16 SELECT grants and the PUBLIC revoke; a fixture that asserts no `ALL TABLES` grant and no grant in `public` (AC2, AC3, AC4).
3. The Section B grant migration, wired to run only after RWB-ACE-001 is reported deployed (AC2, AC4, BR9).
4. The `SchemaBoundaryCheck` over the catalogue, with a fixture that adds a foreign key to `public.account` (AC7).
5. The `GrantCheck` as a container test with sessions as the login, `ace_view_owner` and `rwb_no_grant` (AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4).
6. The `ExtensionKeyCheck` with the duplicate-key fixtures, rolled back in the same transaction (AC5, AC6).
7. A repeated-run test of the whole set on a copy of the SIT schema (AC8).
8. The release note of the sequence, with the version numbers and the checksums of the three migrations.

**Done when.** The migration set applies twice without a change, the catalogue checks pass, the login holds SELECT on the 30 views and nothing else, `ace_view_owner` owns the 30 views and holds SELECT on the 21 Tier 1 and 14 Tier 2 ACE tables with no DML, the four extension tables hold their 49 columns and refuse a second row for one ACE key, no constraint in `rwb_source_data` names `public`, and the tests in section 16 pass.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| Conformance check 1 | A view does not compile | v_ace_account does not compile: column a.core_banking_system_date does not exist |
| Conformance check 2 | A constraint references `public` | fk_case_account_account_key references public.account; no constraint in recovery may reference another schema |
| Conformance check 3 | A view has no dictionary row | v_ace_account.legacy_bucket has no data dictionary entry |
| Conformance check 4 | The service login holds a privilege in `public` or can write a view | recovery_svc holds SELECT on public.account; the recovery role reads the views only |
| Build log | A recovery class names a `public` table | Boundary rule BND-6 broken: AccountReader reads public.account. Read recovery.v_ace_account instead. |
| SQLSTATE 42501 | The service login selects a public table or writes a view | permission denied for schema public |
| SQLSTATE 23505 | A second row for one ACE key in an extension table | duplicate key value violates unique constraint party_ext_pkey |
| Check finding, no message id | A constraint of `rwb_source_data` names a schema outside it | The pipeline check names the constraint and the referenced object; the key is removed |

The five conformance, build-log and SQLSTATE texts are copied from RWB-E1-069, character for character, including the role name `recovery_svc` they carry, which is the `rwb_source_data` login of the target (DP-02). They are pipeline and build log texts for developers and are not part of the message standard. No `MSG-` ID applies to this story: it has no user-facing message, and the messages of the application layer are raised by RWB-P1-E1069-APP and by the guard library.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen. The result of a migration is visible in the release pipeline and in the service's Flyway history (pending, applied, failed, undone, each with a version and a checksum). The platform administrator reads the deployment result under Platform administration R and on SCR-44 Interface and job monitor, and the data steward reads the dictionary rows of the four extension tables. Nothing in this story is shown to a user directly: the four tables are read through the application and its contract, never through SQL on a screen.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a constraint: the check `ck_contact_point_ext_type` is business-neutral and comes from the legacy physical schema; every other business value, the masking answer and the authorise decision are data read by the application, not constants in a migration.
- No personal data in a migration, a script, a test fixture or a runbook: the four tables hold business keys and flags only, `person_key` is a business key and never a name, and the test values `P0000123` and `ACC0000017` are synthetic.
- No read of another schema and no key into another schema: `rwb_source_data` objects reference `rwb_source_data` objects only, and a key to `public.account` is forbidden because ACE cascades deletes on `account` (DP-01, BR4).
- One login per service: `rwb_source_data` is the only grantee on the 30 views, and no other login is granted on them (DP-02; Architecture v5 slide 29).
- No write path into ACE data: no INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE is granted on a view, and the four extension tables hold Workbench decisions only.
- No privilege for PUBLIC anywhere, and no `GRANT ... ON ALL TABLES` in any migration that touches the views.
- The schema is the fixed `recovery`: no `${recoverySchema}` token and no environment name survives in a migration (DP-15).
- An applied migration is never edited: a correction is a new version, and a wrong grant is revoked by a later version, never by an edit.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-069 for the wave-1 integration epic. The single `recovery` schema of the monolith is split: the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views stay in schema `recovery` with `ace_view_owner` as their owner, the 92 tables move to the 19 `rwb_*` schemas with one login each (DP-01, DP-02, DP-15), only `rwb_source_data` holds SELECT on the views (DP-05) and the four extension tables move to `rwb_source_data`. The boundary becomes two-part (BND-6 halves A and B): no class names a `public` table, and no class outside rwb-source-data names a `v_ace_*` view or another service's schema (DP-11 for every other service). This story builds the harness that proves the grant matrix and both halves of the boundary on the real 19 logins in SIT, and it owns no schema. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the read-only ACE source views, the grant matrix and the boundary rule of the monolith proven on the real split in SIT: the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views in schema `recovery` read only through the `rwb_source_data` login, each of the other 18 service logins confined to its own schema and holding nothing on the views or in `public`, no constraint or table name crossing a schema, the four extension tables in `rwb_source_data` 1:1 on the ACE key, and boundary rule BND-6 refusing both a `public` table and a `v_ace_*` view named outside rwb-source-data**, so that **one copy of ACE source data serves 19 services without a second copy, without a write path into ACE data, and with a build that fails on a breach instead of a review that hopes**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The Workbench takes no inbound source data and keeps no copy of it. RWB-E1-069 proved that against one schema: 30 SELECT-only views over the ACE tables, one view owner, one service role and boundary rule BND-6 in RWB-TE-001. In the target the schema is split 19 ways, and every property that story proved is now a property of the split rather than of one schema: the views stay in `recovery` because they read ACE's own tables (Arch v5 slides 8 and 9, "ACE schemas + 30 recovery.v_ace_* views · 19 rwb_* schemas"), the 92 tables move to the 19 `rwb_*` schemas with one login each (DP-01, DP-02, DP-15; Arch v5 slides 8 and 41), only `rwb_source_data` holds SELECT on the views (Arch v5 slides 8, 9, 11 and 45; DP-05), and the four extension tables sit in `rwb_source_data` (Ownership Map; Arch v5 slide 41).

The boundary now has two halves. Half A is the legacy rule: no class in the Workbench names a table in schema `public`. Half B is new: no class outside rwb-source-data names a `v_ace_*` view or another service's schema, and every other service reaches ACE data through the source-data contract or a Temporal activity (DP-11; Arch v5 slides 11, 12, 13 and 45). A single service story cannot prove either half for 19 services, and no service story may read the other 18 schemas to find out — which is exactly why this story exists. It is the one place allowed to hold 19 logins, connect as each of them and assert the catalog.

Serves REQ-RDF-002 (ACE source data read only through the views) and REQ-DRI-006 (no component calls a system of record directly). The measure is every one of the 19 logins passing its row of the grant matrix and both halves of BND-6 in one SIT run, with zero cross-schema reads found.

##### 3. Preconditions

- SIT holds the ACE head with the 21 Tier 1 tables of RWB-E1-069 and the 14 Tier 2 tables that RWB-ACE-001 adds, among them `public.account`, `public.payment`, `public.customer` and `public.efs_action`.
- Schema `recovery` holds the 30 `v_ace_*` views and the three helper functions `recovery.ace_to_date`, `recovery.ace_to_boolean` and `recovery.ace_mask_value`, owned by `ace_view_owner` (RWB-P1-E1069-APP, RWB-P4-E1069-APP).
- The 92 tables of the legacy schema sit in the 19 `rwb_*` schemas: `rwb_source_data`, `rwb_case`, `rwb_access`, `rwb_document`, `rwb_comms`, `rwb_decision`, `rwb_reporting`, `rwb_agent`, `rwb_integration`, `rwb_payment`, `rwb_treatment`, `rwb_asset`, `rwb_deviation`, `rwb_valuation`, `rwb_guarantee`, `rwb_litigation`, `rwb_debtsale`, `rwb_writeoff` and `rwb_partner`, and the four extension tables `party_ext`, `contact_point_ext`, `account_ext` and `valuation_ext` sit in `rwb_source_data`.
- The 19 schemas and their logins are created in SIT by the platform DB story RWB-PLT-NF06-DB, with names fixed in the Environment and Deployment Design (Arch v5 slide 8, "19 rwb_* schemas, one login each").
- The module map of RWB-TE-001 is in the repository, with `recovery-modules.yaml` read by `RecoveryBoundaryTest`, and it holds `sourceViews`, the 30 view names the rule allows.
- The two integration services are deployed in SIT on their published wave 1 contracts: P1 `rwb-source-data` with `GET /accounts/{id}` and `GET /customers/{id}`, and P4 `rwb-access` with `POST /authorise` (RWB-P1-E1069-APP, RWB-P4-E1069-APP).
- The module map, the 30-view list and the schema names are configuration; the harness writes no business value into its code.
- The 19 login names (one per `rwb_*` schema), the grant matrix on the 30 views after the split and the two-part boundary rule (BND-6 halves A and B) are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0377; ASM-0543).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7). The harness is written on Day 1 and is run in SIT once the logins exist; a fake is never used in place of a real login, and the harness never points at a production database.

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: reads its run file — the SIT connection strings of the 19 logins, the 30-view list from the module map and the schema names. The 19 login names, the grant matrix on the 30 views after the split and the two-part boundary rule are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0377; ASM-0543); the run file carries them once and every probe reads the file, never a constant.
2. Harness: runs the preflight of section 13 — 19 logins reachable, 30 views present in schema `recovery`, `sourceViews` present in the module map, the four extension tables present in `rwb_source_data`. One missing item stops the run before the first test.
3. Grant-matrix probe: connects as `rwb_source_data` and selects one row from each of the 30 views, then from `public.account`, then runs insert, update and delete on `recovery.v_ace_account`.
4. Grant-matrix probe: connects as `ace_view_owner` and reads the catalog for the ownership of the 30 views and for SELECT on the ACE tables the views read.
5. Grant-matrix probe: connects as each of the other 18 logins in turn, reads a table in its own schema, then attempts the 30 views, `public.account` and a table of another service's schema.
6. Schema-boundary probe: scans every constraint in the 19 `rwb_*` schemas for a referenced table, type or schema outside its own, lists every table name across the 19 schemas and schema `recovery` for a duplicate, and confirms that schema `recovery` holds no service table.
7. Extension-key probe: lists the columns, the primary keys and the check of the four extension tables in `rwb_source_data`, counts their dictionary fields, and attempts a second `party_ext` row for person_key "P0000123" inside a transaction it rolls back.
8. Boundary-test runner: runs `RecoveryBoundaryTest` in the split tree with the fixture class on `public.account`, the same class on `recovery.v_ace_account` from a module outside rwb-source-data, a class of rwb-case on a table of `rwb_source_data`, and the same class against the source-data contract, with the allowed view list read from the module map.
9. Dictionary probe: connects as `rwb_source_data` and counts one `sys_objects` row per view and one `sys_fields` row per column of the 30 views.
10. Harness: reads the two source-data operations and the authorise check the boundary runner needs, so that the pass of half B is proven on the contract and not on a mock.
11. Harness: reconciles the findings — 19 logins, 30 views, four extension tables, zero cross-schema constraints, zero duplicate table names, zero grants to PUBLIC — and writes the run report naming every login, view, table and class it touched.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | One of the 19 logins is missing in SIT | The preflight stops the run and names the login and its schema; no test is reported as passed | Run report: login rwb_case is not reachable in SIT | AC3 |
| X2 | A view does not compile after the split | The owning migration fails, names the view and the ACE column, and no view of that run exists | Pipeline log: v_ace_account does not compile: column a.core_banking_system_date does not exist | AC1 |
| X3 | `rwb_source_data` holds a privilege in `public`, or any DML on a view | The probe fails and names the login, the privilege and the object | rwb_source_data holds SELECT on public.account; only SELECT on the 30 views is granted | AC2 |
| X4 | One of the other 18 logins reads a view, `public` or another service's schema | The probe fails and names the login, the object and the grant that allowed it | rwb_case reads recovery.v_ace_account; only rwb_source_data reads the views | AC3 |
| X5 | A constraint references another schema, or a table name sits in two schemas | The scan fails and names the constraint or the doubled table | fk_case_account_account_key references public.account; no constraint in an rwb_* schema may reference another schema | AC4 |
| X6 | A second row is written for an ACE key already in an extension table | The write is refused, the first row is unchanged and the transaction is rolled back | SQLSTATE 23505 duplicate key value violates unique constraint party_ext_pkey | AC5 |
| X7 | A class names a `public` table, a `v_ace_*` view outside rwb-source-data, or another service's table | The build fails with BND-6 and names the class and the object | Boundary rule BND-6 broken: AccountReader names recovery.v_ace_account outside rwb-source-data. Call the source-data contract instead. | AC6 |

X1 to X7 are the exception paths of RWB-E1-069 carried onto the split, with X1 and X4 added for the 18 logins that did not exist in the monolith and X7 widened to the second half of the boundary.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | A test project of its own; it needs the 19 logins, the 30 views and the module map, and it owns no schema, no table and no grant |
| Negotiable | Probe layout, report layout, run-file format and the order inside one AC are the harness's choice; the 30 view names, the helper functions, the four extension tables and the two message texts are fixed by RWB-E1-069 |
| Valuable | Proves for 19 services what no single service can: one read path, no privilege in `public`, no cross-schema constraint, no second copy and a build that fails on both halves of the boundary |
| Estimable | One harness project, six probes, five fixtures, one run file and one report |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the report |
| Testable | Every criterion is one catalog query, one refused statement with its SQLSTATE, one scan result or one build verdict |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Read-only ACE source views, grants and boundary rule, proven on the 19 logins of the split

  Background:
    Given the environment is SIT with synthetic data
    Given the ACE schemas hold the 21 Tier 1 tables and the 14 Tier 2 tables of RWB-E1-069, among them public.account, public.payment and public.customer
    Given schema recovery holds the 30 v_ace_* views, owned by ace_view_owner, and the three helper functions
    Given the 19 rwb_* schemas exist with one login each and the 92 tables sit in them

  Scenario: AC1 The 30 views stay in schema recovery, compile and answer through the rwb_source_data login (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the 92 tables have left schema recovery for the 19 rwb_* schemas and the 30 views did not move
    When the harness counts the views in schema recovery whose name starts with v_ace_
    Then the count is 30, all 30 compile, and no v_ace_* view exists in any rwb_* schema
    When the harness selects one row from each of the 30 views on the rwb_source_data login
    Then each of the 30 statements returns a row and no statement exceeds the 5 s statement timeout
    Then no view carries a primary key or a foreign key into an rwb_* schema
    Then schema recovery holds the 30 views and the three helper functions and no service table

  Scenario: AC2 rwb_source_data holds SELECT on the views and no privilege in public (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the grant matrix on the 30 views after the split is loaded from the run file
    Then has_schema_privilege('rwb_source_data', 'recovery', 'USAGE') is true
    Then has_table_privilege('rwb_source_data', 'recovery.v_ace_account', 'SELECT') is true, and the same holds for each of the 30 views
    Then has_schema_privilege('rwb_source_data', 'public', 'USAGE') is false
    Then has_table_privilege('rwb_source_data', 'public.account', 'SELECT') is false
    When the same login runs insert, update and delete on recovery.v_ace_account
    Then each statement fails with SQLSTATE 42501 and no row of any view changes
    Then ace_view_owner owns the 30 views, holds SELECT on the ACE tables the views read and holds no INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE on any of them
    Then the test role "rwb_no_grant" cannot select recovery.v_ace_account, because PUBLIC holds no privilege on it

  Scenario: AC3 The other 18 logins reach neither the views nor public and read only their own schema (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the 18 logins other than rwb_source_data: rwb_case, rwb_access, rwb_document, rwb_comms, rwb_decision, rwb_reporting, rwb_agent, rwb_integration, rwb_payment, rwb_treatment, rwb_asset, rwb_deviation, rwb_valuation, rwb_guarantee, rwb_litigation, rwb_debtsale, rwb_writeoff and rwb_partner
    Then each login is reachable in SIT and each one's own schema is named in the run file
    When each login selects from recovery.v_ace_account and from public.account
    Then each statement fails with SQLSTATE 42501
    When each login selects from a table in its own schema
    Then the statement returns without error
    When each login selects from a table in another service's schema
    Then the statement fails with SQLSTATE 42501
    Then has_schema_privilege(<login>, 'recovery', 'USAGE') is false and has_schema_privilege(<login>, 'public', 'USAGE') is false for all 18
    Then PUBLIC holds no privilege of any kind on the 30 views, on schema recovery or on schema public

  Scenario: AC4 No constraint leaves its own schema and no table name sits in two schemas (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the 19 rwb_* schemas are at the head of their Flyway sequences
    When the harness lists every constraint in the 19 rwb_* schemas
    Then no foreign key, check, unique or exclusion constraint names a table, a type or a schema outside its own
    Then the scan returns 0 rows for a constraint whose referenced object sits in another rwb_* schema or in schema public
    When the harness lists every table name of the 19 rwb_* schemas and of schema recovery
    Then no table name sits in two schemas
    Then schema recovery holds no service table
    When a branch adds a foreign key from rwb_case.case_account.account_key to public.account
    Then the scan fails with "fk_case_account_account_key references public.account; no constraint in an rwb_* schema may reference another schema"
    Then the merge is blocked

  Scenario: AC5 The four extension tables sit in rwb_source_data and stay 1:1 on the ACE key (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the four extension tables party_ext, contact_point_ext, account_ext and valuation_ext are in rwb_source_data
    When the harness lists their columns, primary keys and constraints
    Then party_ext holds 12 columns with person_key as its primary key
    Then contact_point_ext holds 14 columns with contact_key as its primary key and the check ck_contact_point_ext_type
    Then account_ext holds 9 columns with account_key as its primary key
    Then valuation_ext holds 14 columns with valuation_key as its primary key
    Then the four tables hold 49 columns in all and 49 dictionary fields, DF-EXT-001 to DF-EXT-049
    Then no constraint on any of the four tables references a table outside rwb_source_data
    When the Workbench writes a second party_ext row for person_key "P0000123"
    Then the write fails with SQLSTATE 23505 and party_ext holds one row for "P0000123"

  Scenario: AC6 Boundary rule BND-6 refuses public and refuses the views outside rwb-source-data (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the module map recovery-modules.yaml holds sourceViews, the 30 view names the rule allows
    Given the fixture class "recovery.dataengine.internal.AccountReader" holds a query on "public.account"
    When the pipeline runs the boundary-test runner
    Then the build fails with boundary rule BND-6, "AccountReader" and "public.account"
    When the same class queries "recovery.v_ace_account" from a module outside rwb-source-data
    Then the build fails with boundary rule BND-6, because only rwb-source-data may name a v_ace_* view
    When a class of rwb-case names a table of rwb_source_data
    Then the build fails with boundary rule BND-6, because no service names another service's schema
    When the same class names no table and calls GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/accounts/{id} instead
    Then the build passes, with the scope check of POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise for the reader's data-product scope
    Then the view names the rule allows are read from the module map, not written in the runner
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views stay in schema `recovery` after the split, owned by `ace_view_owner`, and they are the only read path to ACE source data | Arch v5 slides 8 and 9; ADR-010; DP-05 |
| BR2 | The 92 tables of the legacy schema sit in the 19 `rwb_*` schemas with one login each, and four of them — the extension tables — in `rwb_source_data` | Arch v5 slides 8 and 41; DP-01, DP-02, DP-15; Ownership Map |
| BR3 | `rwb_source_data` holds USAGE on schema `recovery` and SELECT on the 30 views, no privilege of any kind in schema `public`, and no INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE on a view | Arch v5 slide 11 (SQL view: read-only login); DP-05 |
| BR4 | Each of the other 18 service logins holds USAGE on its own schema only: no privilege on the 30 views, none in `public`, none in another service's schema, and PUBLIC holds nothing anywhere | Arch v5 slides 8, 11 and 45; DP-01, DP-02 |
| BR5 | Every view carries one `sys_objects` row and one `sys_fields` row per column, held in `rwb_source_data` | RWB-E1-069 BR5; RWB-E1-064 |
| BR6 | No constraint in an `rwb_*` schema references a table, a type or a schema outside it; no table name sits in two schemas; schema `recovery` holds no service table | RWB-E1-069 BR4; ADR-010; DP-01 |
| BR7 | The four extension tables sit in `rwb_source_data`, hold a Workbench decision about an ACE record and never a copy of an ACE column, and are 1:1 with the ACE record on the ACE business key | RWB-E1-069 BR7; Ownership Map; DF-EXT-001 to DF-EXT-049 |
| BR8 | Boundary rule BND-6 has two halves. Half A: no class names a table in schema `public`. Half B: no class outside rwb-source-data names a `v_ace_*` view or another service's schema. The allowed view list is read from the module map | REQ-DRI-006; RWB-TE-001; Arch v5 slides 11, 12, 13 and 45 |
| BR9 | A service other than rwb-source-data reaches ACE data through the source-data REST contract or a Temporal activity, one hop, 2 s client budget, never through the views and never through another service's tables | DP-05, DP-11; Arch v5 slides 11 to 13 and 45 |
| BR10 | A change to the 30-view list, to the grant matrix or to either half of BND-6 is a migration plus a rule change, approved by the recovery tech lead and the data architect; an applied grant is never edited | RWB-E1-069 BR9; DP-15 |

##### 9. State transitions

None for a case status. This story reads, attempts and asserts; it changes no business row.

The schema, grant and run states the harness observes:

| Item | States |
|---|---|
| `recovery.v_ace_*` | Present and compiling, or absent and named; owned by `ace_view_owner` throughout |
| `rwb_*` schema | Created and on its Flyway head, or not created and named by the preflight |
| Grant | Held, refused with SQLSTATE 42501, or granted to PUBLIC — which is a failure in every schema |
| Constraint | Inside its own schema, or crossing a schema — which is a failure and blocks the merge |
| Extension row | One row per ACE key, or the second row refused with SQLSTATE 23505 |
| Boundary verdict | Pass, or fail with the class and the object named |
| Harness run | Not started, running, passed, or failed with the criterion, the login and the object named |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Tech lead of the integration harness | Owns the harness, the run file, the fixtures and the run report |
| ACE DBA and ACE schema owner | Own schema `public`, the 30 views and the grants; approve nothing in this story, supply the grants |
| rwb-source-data owner (RWB-P1-E1069-APP, RWB-P4-E1069-APP) | Owns the views' contract, the extension tables in `rwb_source_data` and the source-data operations the harness calls |
| rwb-access owner (RWB-P4-E1069-APP) | Owns the authorise check the boundary pass relies on |
| Platform DB owner (RWB-PLT-NF06-DB) | Owns the 19 schemas and the 19 logins the harness connects as |
| Recovery tech lead and data architect | Approve a change to the 30-view list, the grant matrix or either half of BND-6 |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Reads the grant matrix, the view list and the run report |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Reads the deployment result and the run report; may not change a grant |
| RW-DATASTEW, data steward | Reads the dictionary rows for the 30 views |
| No role | May write a view, copy ACE data or grant a privilege to PUBLIC |

The harness holds no schema and no grant of its own: it connects as the 19 existing logins, and the only write it attempts is the duplicate extension row of AC5, which is rolled back in the same transaction.

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-ACE-001 to DF-ACE-304 | the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views | all 304 fields, one row per view | Read |
| DF-EXT-001 to DF-EXT-012 | `rwb_source_data.party_ext` | all 12 fields | Read; the duplicate write is refused |
| DF-EXT-013 to DF-EXT-026 | `rwb_source_data.contact_point_ext` | all 14 fields | Read |
| DF-EXT-027 to DF-EXT-035 | `rwb_source_data.account_ext` | all 9 fields | Read |
| DF-EXT-036 to DF-EXT-049 | `rwb_source_data.valuation_ext` | all 14 fields | Read |
| DF-REF-097, DF-REF-098, DF-REF-105 | reference values carried on the source-data response | the three reference fields | Read |
| None | schema `recovery` | no service table | None |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary and are copied from RWB-E1-069. The harness owns no schema, no table and no field: `v_data_dictionary` and the `sys_objects` and `sys_fields` rows are read on the `rwb_source_data` login, and the four extension tables are read on that login too. The 30 views keep the field split of the legacy story: 177 fields in Section A over the ACE tables that exist and 127 in Section B over the tables RWB-ACE-001 adds, 304 in all. The three reference values are the codes the source-data response already carries; the harness asserts the code and never resolves a list itself (DP-07).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness is a test project and provides no REST operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/accounts/{id}` | P1 rwb-source-data | The account "ACC0000017" behind `v_ace_account`, read on the contract rather than the view, so that half B of AC6 passes on the real response |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/customers/{id}` | P1 rwb-source-data | The customer behind the party of person_key "P0000123", read on the same contract for the same pass |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | The scope check of AC6 for the reader that calls the two source-data operations |

Every call is one hop to the owning service on its own base (DP-11) with the 2 s client budget; the harness calls no service through another service and calls no path outside the three above.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness publishes no business event and the grant matrix publishes nothing.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. No event carries a grant or a schema fact; the run reads the catalog and the contracts only.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The harness starts no workflow. A service that reads ACE data inside a workflow does it in an activity on the source-data contract (DP-11); this story asserts the rule and adds no workflow.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The run is started by hand or by the wave 1 integration pipeline; no Schedule is registered and no job of the job map is touched.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The harness owns no table. The objects it reads and the login it reads them on:

| Data | Owner | Reached through |
|---|---|---|
| the 30 `v_ace_*` views | schema `recovery`; view owner `ace_view_owner`; contract owner P1 rwb-source-data | the `rwb_source_data` login and the P1 source-data contract |
| `party_ext`, `contact_point_ext`, `account_ext`, `valuation_ext` | P1 rwb-source-data | the `rwb_source_data` login |
| `sys_objects`, `sys_fields`, `v_data_dictionary` | P1 rwb-source-data | the `rwb_source_data` login |
| the 88 other tables of the 19 schemas | each service's own owner, per the Ownership Map | the catalog only; no row is read |
| scope and role data behind the authorise check | P4 rwb-access | the P4 authorise contract |

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

None. This is the integration level: the 19 real logins, the real 30 views and the real contracts replace the fakes of the app stories. The ACE tables of SIT are the only stand-in for an outside system, and they are the schema the ACE team owns.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Provided | Consumed | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 | 3 | Two source-data reads and the authorise check; one hop, 2 s (DP-11) |
| Kafka | None | None | No topic in this story |
| Temporal | None | None | No workflow, activity or Schedule in this story |
| File | None | None | No file in this story |
| SQL view | None | 30 views | Read only by the `rwb_source_data` login, 5 s statement timeout (Arch v5 slide 11) |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** One test project `integration/recovery-w1/source-views`, with the grant-matrix probe, the boundary-test runner, the dictionary probe, the schema-boundary probe, the extension-key probe and the report writer, its run file and its fixtures.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| HarnessRunner | Runner | Preflight, run order, report, exit code |
| GrantMatrixProbe | Service | Connects as the 19 logins; reads the catalog and asserts SELECT on the 30 views for `rwb_source_data`, denial for the other 18, no privilege in `public`, own-schema-only reads, PUBLIC empty and DML refused with SQLSTATE 42501 |
| ViewOwnerProbe | Service | Asserts that `ace_view_owner` owns the 30 views and holds SELECT only on the ACE tables they read |
| SchemaBoundaryProbe | Service | Scans every constraint in the 19 `rwb_*` schemas and the table names across the 19 schemas and `recovery` |
| ExtensionKeyProbe | Service | Asserts the columns, keys and check of the four extension tables in `rwb_source_data` and the duplicate person_key refusal |
| BoundaryRunner | Service | Runs `RecoveryBoundaryTest` with the three fixtures of AC6 and reads `sourceViews` from the module map |
| DictionaryProbe | Service | Counts one `sys_objects` row per view and one `sys_fields` row per column on the `rwb_source_data` login |
| ReportWriter | Service | One row per test case, with the login, the object and the verdict, and no row data |

**Database.** None of its own. The harness creates no schema, no table and no grant; it connects as the 19 logins that already exist, and its one write attempt is refused by the primary key and rolled back.

**Configuration and reference data**

- SIT, the 19 login names (from the Environment and Deployment Design), the 19 schema names and the 30-view list (from the module map).
- The 19 login names, the grant matrix on the 30 views after the split and the two-part boundary rule: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0377; ASM-0543).
- The 5 s statement timeout, the 2 s client budget, the report layout and the run-file format.
- The synthetic values the fixtures reuse: account "ACC0000017" with delay_days 95, person_key "P0000123", the test role "rwb_no_grant" and the fixture class "AccountReader".

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-02 | `recovery_svc` login | One login per service | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The ten rows above are the pattern rows of §R5.5 with their wording. The story carries no H, C or X dependency: the build dependencies of DP-03, DP-06, DP-07, DP-08, DP-15 and DP-19 stay with the service, platform and operations stories this harness proves. DP-01, DP-02 and DP-15 are the subject of the run — the 19 schemas and their logins; DP-05 is what the grant matrix enforces — one login on the views; DP-08 is the authorise check of AC6; DP-07 is the reference code the source-data response carries, which the harness asserts and never resolves; DP-03, DP-06 and DP-19 are named for completeness and are exercised by no criterion here. The I list names the two services whose behaviour it exercises, and an integration dependency never blocks a build (Template and Rules §R5.4).

| Account fixture | Account "ACC0000017" with delay_days 95 | AC1, TC-E1-069-06-ITG |
| Extension fixture | `party_ext` with one row for person_key "P0000123", and the duplicate insert | AC5, TC-E1-069-07-ITG, TC-ITG-E1069-05 |
| Boundary classes | "AccountReader" on `public.account`, on `recovery.v_ace_account` outside rwb-source-data, on the source-data contract; a rwb-case class on an `rwb_source_data` table | AC6, TC-E1-069-08-ITG, TC-ITG-E1069-06 |

**Run order.** Preflight on the 19 logins, the 30 views, the module map and the four extension tables; AC1 on the view count and the 30 reads; AC2 as `rwb_source_data` and as `ace_view_owner`; AC3 across the other 18 logins; AC4 on the constraint scan and the table-name scan; AC5 on the four extension tables and the duplicate; AC6 on the boundary runner with its four fixtures; the dictionary probe; the report. A failing step stops the run and the report names the criterion, the login, the object and the evidence. The duplicate insert is rolled back before the report is written.

**Done when.** The 14 test cases of section 16 pass in SIT on the real 19 logins, every one of the 19 logins passes its row of the grant matrix, both halves of BND-6 fail on their fixtures and pass on the source-data contract, no constraint and no table name crosses a schema, the four extension tables sit in `rwb_source_data` and refuse a second row for one ACE key, and the report names all 19 logins, 30 views and four extension tables with no grant to PUBLIC.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the 30 view names, the 19 logins, the schema names, the report layout and the timeouts are configuration; the run file carries them once.
- No personal data in the run file, the report, the logs or the fixtures: the fixtures reuse account "ACC0000017", person_key "P0000123" and the test role, and the report carries login names, object names and verdicts, never a row value.
- The harness owns no schema, no table and no grant; it connects as the 19 existing logins and writes nothing that survives the run.
- No service reads another service's schema and no service but rwb-source-data names a `v_ace_*` view (DP-01, DP-05); both halves of BND-6 fail the build, and the check is a regression test, not a review.
- No write path into ACE data: INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE on a view are refused by the database and asserted in every run.
- No privilege for PUBLIC anywhere, and no `GRANT ... ON ALL TABLES` in any migration that touches the views.
- The 30-view list is read from the module map, never from the runner; a change to it is a rule change, not a test change.
- The harness never uses production data, never points at a production database and never connects as a production schema owner.
