**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-070 for the workflow platform epic; the platform now publishes the namespace, client-identity, frontend API subset, OIDC role mapping and metrics and health contract of namespace rwb-recovery with a fake frontend, so the 19 services build against a frozen platform contract on Day 1. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **consumer of the Temporal platform contract, a service team or the platform team**, I want **the namespace, client identity and frontend API contract, the Web UI role mapping, the metrics and health contract and a fake frontend published on Day 1**, so that **the 19 services build and test against one frozen platform contract before the cluster exists**.

This is the contract story of legacy key RWB-E1-070 under epic RWB-PLT-WF. A shared cluster cannot wait for 19 teams to agree names, so the contract fixes, in one versioned document, the namespace `rwb-recovery` and its retention and search attributes, the client certificate profile that identifies a service's workload, the subset of the frontend gRPC API the services may call and the typed errors it may return, the Entra ID role mapping of the Web UI, the metrics and health endpoints the ACE monitoring namespace scrapes, and a fake frontend that answers every one of those declarations without a cluster.

The platform is shared platform, not one of the 19 services: it owns no `rwb_*` schema, no `rwb.<short>.events.v1` topic and no `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` base, so this document publishes names and shapes only and never a business model (Template and Rules §R4, §R5.5 DP-13, DP-14). The namespace `rwb-recovery`, its 30-day retention and its four Keyword search attributes are fixed by R4 and Architecture v5. The contract is published at status Draft (realignment v1) and is frozen when the consuming stories pass their contract tests.

##### 2. Business rationale

In the monolith one process held the workflow state, so the namespace and the certificate were an operational detail nobody had to publish. In the target the engine is shared platform in namespace `rwb-recovery`, one cluster per environment, with the workers living inside each of the 19 services (Architecture v5 slides 23 and 24; Temporal and Drools Design slides 11 and 12). Nineteen teams, four environments and one platform team then have to agree the namespace, the certificate profile, the API subset, the errors, the OIDC roles and the metrics endpoints before the first worker is written, or each team invents its own reading and the cluster is reconfigured per team.

Publishing the contract on Day 1 also protects the two boundaries the design depends on. First, a service reaches Temporal only as a client with its own certificate and its own namespace claim: no shared certificate, no anonymous client, and no cross-namespace call, which is what keeps AC3 of the legacy story meaningful after the split. Second, the platform publishes no business data and no personal-data attribute, so the search attributes stay case codes and queue codes and the payload encryption work stays with the codec-server story. The fake frontend is the instrument that makes this testable before the cluster exists: every service's worker test, every contract test and the integration harness run against the same declarations.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The namespace `rwb-recovery`, retention 30 days and the four Keyword search attributes CaseId, Stage, ProductGroup and QueueCode are fixed by Template and Rules §R4 and Architecture v5 (slides 23, 24 and 41); the contract records them and changes none of them.
- The five-layer design fixes L1 and L2 as platform-owned: one cluster per environment, one namespace per workbench, the workflow kit above them (Architecture v5 slide 23; Temporal and Drools Design slide 12).
- The Release is 30 November 2026 (tentative) and is copied unchanged; the contract carries no date of its own.
- The contract is Draft (realignment v1) until the consuming stories pass their contract tests; no approval is required to publish a Draft contract.
- The frontend gRPC port 7233 is reachable only from the cluster network and the worker subnets, and the Web UI only on its internal ingress.
- The ACE internal certificate authority issues the client and server certificates, and the certificates are held in Key Vault.
- The ACE monitoring namespace exists and is the only network source allowed to scrape the platform endpoints.
- The RW-PLATADM and RW-AUDIT roles exist through the environment group (RWB-P4-E1022-CON), and every other Workbench role code is known to the mapping so it can be refused.
- The approved Temporal server and SDK release is not in the read sources: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1440; ASM-2535).

##### 4. Flow

1. The contract author writes the namespace contract: the namespace name, retention in hours and days, the four Keyword search attributes, the refusal of any personal-data attribute, and the rule that a second bootstrap run changes nothing.
2. The author writes the client identity and certificate profile: one client certificate per service workload identity, issued by the ACE internal CA, carrying the namespace claim, with the validity window and the renewal rule.
3. The author writes the frontend API subset and the typed errors: which gRPC calls a service may make, the request and response shapes at the level of names, and the error codes with the condition that produces each.
4. The author writes the Web UI role mapping: RW-PLATADM operates, RW-AUDIT reads, every other Workbench role is refused, and the refusal carries MSG-P4-002.
5. The author writes the metrics and health contract: the two endpoints, their schemes, ports, paths and result codes, and the network source allowed to call them.
6. The author writes the Helm values contract: the value names each environment supplies, with no value of its own beyond the pinned release family, so the app story and the environments fill the same keys.
7. The fake frontend is generated or assembled from the declarations: a Temporal dev server carrying the namespace, the search attributes, test CA certificates and one seeded smoke workflow.
8. The contract test runs the fake against the documents on every change: every declaration answered, every error produced, every refusal proved.
9. The contract is published as v1 to the contract registry; the app story, the worker and SDK story and the 19 services' worker tests pin the version.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message |
|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A client connects with no certificate, an expired certificate or a certificate issued for another namespace, or it names a foreign namespace in the request | The TLS handshake fails for the first two cases and the call is refused with PERMISSION_DENIED for the last two; no workflow is started and the event is in the frontend log with the client identity only | None (TLS); PERMISSION_DENIED |
| X2 | A caller presents a Workbench role other than RW-PLATADM or RW-AUDIT to the Web UI mapping | The mapping refuses the role, no namespace is listed and no workflow is shown | MSG-P4-002 |
| X3 | The namespace bootstrap runs a second time | Nothing changes: the namespace, the retention and the four search attributes stay as declared, and the run is recorded as a no-op | None (idempotent) |
| X4 | A change to the contract breaks a consumer: a renamed namespace, a renamed search attribute, a removed API call or a changed error code | The change raises a new version, marks the current version deprecated, and no consumer sees an edited document | Lint finding, no message id |
| X5 | A value the consumers need is named by no read source (the platform login, the platform admin base, the approved release number) | The value is published as the working read of the assumption, with the placeholder where it is still open, and the gap stays open | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1440; ASM-2535) |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Publishes documents and a fake; builds no cluster, reads no business data and depends on no other story |
| Negotiable | Document format, example workflow identifiers and the internal layout of the fake are open until the version is frozen; the namespace, the retention, the four search attributes, the API subset and the error codes are fixed |
| Valuable | The 19 services, the worker and SDK story and the platform app story start on Day 1 against one frozen platform contract |
| Estimable | One namespace contract, one client-identity profile, one API subset, one OIDC mapping, one metrics and health contract, one values schema, one fake and one contract test |
| Small | One sprint for the documents, the fake and the contract test |
| Testable | Each criterion in section 7 is a schema, lint or fake assertion in section 16 |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Temporal platform contract for namespace rwb-recovery and the fake frontend

  Background:
    Given the platform is shared platform and owns no schema, no topic and no Workbench REST base
    Given the namespace rwb-recovery is the unit of isolation on one cluster per environment

  Scenario: AC1 The namespace contract is published and a second bootstrap run changes nothing (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the namespace contract document
    When it is validated against the platform schema
    Then it declares the namespace rwb-recovery
    Then it declares retention 720 hours, 30 days
    Then it declares the search attributes CaseId, Stage, ProductGroup and QueueCode as Keyword
    Then it declares that no search attribute holds a name, a national ID or another personal data field
    When the namespace bootstrap runs a second time
    Then the namespace, the retention and the four search attributes are unchanged

  Scenario: AC2 The frontend API subset and its typed errors are declared (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the frontend API document
    When it is validated
    Then the allowed calls are StartWorkflowExecution, SignalWorkflowExecution, DescribeWorkflowExecution, ListWorkflowExecutions and GetWorkflowExecutionHistory
    Then every other frontend call is declared out of the subset for a service client
    Then the typed errors are TLS handshake failure, NOT_FOUND, PERMISSION_DENIED, FAILED_PRECONDITION and UNAVAILABLE
    Then each error names the condition that produces it and carries no business value and no personal data

  Scenario: AC3 One client certificate per service workload identity (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the client identity and certificate profile
    When it is validated
    Then it declares one client certificate per service workload identity, issued by the ACE internal CA, carrying the namespace claim rwb-recovery
    Then it declares the validity window and the renewal rule, and that a certificate is never shared between two services
    When a client connects with no certificate
    Then the TLS handshake fails and no workflow call is served
    When a client connects with an expired certificate
    Then the TLS handshake fails with certificate expired
    When a client connects with a certificate issued for another namespace
    Then the call is refused with PERMISSION_DENIED and no workflow is started

  Scenario: AC4 The Web UI role mapping is published (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the OIDC role mapping in the contract
    When it is reviewed
    Then RW-PLATADM maps to operate and RW-AUDIT maps to read
    Then every other Workbench role is refused with MSG-P4-002 and no namespace is listed
    Then the mapping names roles only and never a person, an account or an email address

  Scenario: AC5 The metrics and health contract is published (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the metrics and health contract
    When it is validated
    Then it declares HTTPS GET /metrics on port 9090
    Then it declares HTTP GET /health on port 8080, answering 200 when the service is ready and 503 when it is not
    Then it declares that both endpoints are scraped and probed only from the ACE monitoring namespace and the cluster probe
    Then neither endpoint carries a business value or a personal data field

  Scenario: AC6 The fake frontend answers every declaration and a breaking change raises v2 (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the fake frontend, a Temporal dev server with the namespace rwb-recovery, test CA certificates and the seeded smoke workflow
    When the contract test runs
    Then every declaration of sections 12 and 14 is answered or refused as declared, including the no-certificate, expired-certificate and foreign-namespace cases
    Then the fake is declared test-only and is never deployed to SIT, UAT or PROD
    Then a breaking change raises v2, marks v1 deprecated, and no consumer sees an edited v1
```

These six criteria are new and test only the contract baseline: no legacy acceptance criterion is repeated here; the values they assert are the namespace, retention, search attributes, API calls and error codes the read sources fix, character for character.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The namespace is the unit of isolation: one namespace per environment is `rwb-recovery`, with its own retention, certificates and codec keys; a new workbench takes a namespace, not a cluster | Architecture v5 slides 23, 24 and 46; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR2 | The server release is 1.30 or later, for Nexus and Worker Versioning; the approved release number is recorded in the environment design | Temporal and Drools Design slide 32 item 6; Architecture v5 slide 23 |
| BR3 | The frontend accepts mTLS only: every client presents a certificate from the ACE internal CA that names the namespace, and no anonymous or shared certificate is accepted | Architecture v5 slide 35; Temporal and Drools Design slide 11 |
| BR4 | The Web UI is OIDC only: RW-PLATADM operates, RW-AUDIT reads, every other Workbench role is refused with MSG-P4-002 | Architecture v5 slide 35; RWB-P4-E1022-CON |
| BR5 | The contract carries no service short, no schema name, no topic name and no Workbench REST base; the platform owns none of them | Template and Rules §R4 and §R5.5 DP-13, DP-14 |
| BR6 | The fake is test-only and is never deployed to SIT, UAT or PROD; no environment value points at it | Template and Rules §R7.2 section 12.8 |
| BR7 | A breaking change raises a new version and deprecates the current one; a published version is never edited in place | Template and Rules §R7.2 |
| BR8 | Every value the consumer supplies is configuration: replica counts, node sizes, retention and releases are declared keys with no value baked into the document | REQ-DRI-010; Architecture v5 slide 20 |

##### 9. State transitions

The contract has its own lifecycle; the objects it describes have the states below. This story changes no case status.

| Object | From | Event | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Contract | Draft | The consuming stories pass their contract tests | Published |
| Contract | Published | A consumer pins the version and the change window closes | Frozen |
| Contract | Published or Frozen | A breaking change is accepted | A new version, and the old version is Deprecated |
| Namespace | None | The namespace bootstrap runs once | REGISTERED |
| Namespace | REGISTERED | The bootstrap runs again | REGISTERED, unchanged |
| Client certificate | None | The ACE internal CA issues the certificate | VALID |
| Client certificate | VALID | The validity window ends | EXPIRED, and the handshake fails |
| Client certificate | VALID | The certificate is renewed before expiry | ROTATED, and the new certificate is VALID |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The contract author (any team, per U3) | Writes and versions the documents, the mapping, the fake and the contract test |
| The platform owner of the Temporal layer | Approves a breaking change and a version freeze |
| Security architecture | Reviews the client certificate profile, the namespace claim and the refusal rules |
| The service teams of the 19 services | Read the contract, confirm the calls they need, raise a change request |
| The ACE Common team | Owns the Entra ID sign-in and the app roles the mapping references, and never republishes them |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A platform contract is a technical artefact, not a credit decision |

No personal name, no email address and no credential appears in the contract or in an example. Where a caller must be named, the example uses a service workload identity or a role code only.

##### 11. Data

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Business data published | None. The contract publishes names, shapes, codes and result codes only; no case, customer, account or document value appears |
| Personal data | None, and no search attribute may hold one: CaseId, Stage, ProductGroup and QueueCode are codes |
| Data held by the platform | The two Temporal persistence stores of the app story; their contents are workflow histories and visibility records, not business records |
| Data held by the fake | Synthetic workflow identifiers only: the seeded smoke workflow `platform-smoke-20261116` and the identifiers its test starts; no business data and no personal data |
| Field identifiers | None owned. The platform owns no `rwb_*` field and no ACE field |
| Retention | The namespace retains closed workflows for 30 days, as declared; the contract document itself keeps no data |

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The platform has no service short (Template and Rules §R4 has no platform row), so it publishes no path under `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` and no Workbench endpoint. The document declares the gRPC subset of section 12.5 as the interface, not a REST path.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. The platform consumes no Workbench REST operation. The Web UI calls the frontend and the OIDC provider only, and the cluster reads its configuration through the platform parameters contract.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The platform publishes no `rwb.<short>.events.v1` topic and no event schema; the decision-record, case and access events keep their owners (DP-14).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The platform consumes no Kafka topic.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The contract publishes the task-queue and activity-contract convention rather than a workflow: a service's worker polls only its own task queue `rwb-<short>` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, publishes its typed activity interfaces in a contract jar, and calls another service only through that interface or a child workflow on the owner's queue (Architecture v5 slides 23 and 24; Architecture v5 slide 11). The platform task queue is task queue `rwb-platform`; the document records it as the platform queue and owns no workflow on it in this story.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The contract declares no Schedule and no batch window; the platform jobs JOB-21 and JOB-22 belong to the observability and smoke stories.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The platform owns no `rwb_*` schema and no table in the ACE database; its two persistence stores belong to the app story and are Temporal persistence, not ACE tables.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| Temporal platform fake frontend (this story) | A Temporal dev server with the namespace `rwb-recovery`, its retention and four Keyword search attributes, test CA certificates, the declared frontend API subset with its typed errors, the declared metrics and health endpoints, and the seeded smoke workflow `platform-smoke-20261116` | The app story (RWB-PLT-E1070-APP), the worker and SDK story (RWB-PLT-E1071), the 19 services' worker tests and the Wave 1 integration harness |

The fake answers from the declarations of this document, so a change to a declaration shows up as a contract-test failure rather than as a difference between environments. It is test-only and is never deployed to SIT, UAT or PROD.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary (REST, Kafka, Temporal, File)

| Call type | Provided | Consumed | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 | 0 | The platform publishes no Workbench REST base; the metrics and health endpoints are operational, not Workbench routes |
| Kafka | 0 | 0 | The platform owns no topic and consumes none |
| Temporal | The contract of the frontend gRPC subset, the client identity, the namespace, the task-queue convention, the metrics and health endpoints | 0 | Temporal only: the document describes the platform interface and the fake stands in for it |
| File | 0 | 0 | No file is read or written by the contract or the fake |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables**

| Deliverable | Form | Content |
|---|---|---|
| Namespace contract | Versioned document plus schema | Namespace name, retention in hours and days, the four Keyword search attributes, the personal-data refusal, the idempotent bootstrap rule |
| Client-identity and certificate profile | Document plus profile file | One certificate per service workload identity, the ACE internal CA, the namespace claim, the validity window and the renewal rule |
| Frontend API document | Document plus interface stub | The five allowed calls, the calls outside the subset, the request and response names, the five typed errors |
| OIDC role mapping | Table in the document and in configuration | RW-PLATADM operates, RW-AUDIT reads, every other role refused with MSG-P4-002 |
| Metrics and health contract | Table in the document | HTTPS GET /metrics on 9090, HTTP GET /health on 8080 with 200 and 503, the allowed network source |
| Helm values schema | Schema file | The keys each environment supplies, with the release family pinned and no business value |
| Fake frontend | Runnable test double | Temporal dev server with the namespace, the search attributes, test CA certificates and the seeded smoke workflow |
| Contract test | Test suite in the build | Every declaration, every error and every refusal asserted against the fake |

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-02 | `recovery_svc` login | One login per service | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |

These are the Template and Rules §R5.5 rows that bear on a platform contract. DP-01 and DP-02 are declared, not implemented: the contract states that the platform owns no `rwb_*` schema and that every client is one service workload identity, so the separation the app story proves in AC2 is already fixed here. DP-13 and DP-14 are declared as absences: the platform has no `/api/recovery` base and no topic, so a consumer that expects one finds the rule in the contract rather than in a review. DP-04, DP-05, DP-06, DP-07, DP-15 and DP-19 are recorded in the metadata because the platform sits under all of them; the document repeats none of their content, because the parameters, the Drools kit, the views, the migrations and the screens keep their owners. This story adds no dependency of its own: it is a CON story and starts on Day 1.

**Build steps**

1. Write the namespace contract and its schema: the name, retention 720 hours and 30 days, the four Keyword search attributes, the personal-data refusal and the idempotent second run.
2. Write the client-identity and certificate profile: one certificate per service workload identity, the ACE internal CA, the namespace claim, the validity window and the renewal rule.
3. Write the frontend API document and the interface stub: the five allowed calls, the calls outside the subset, and the five typed errors with their conditions.
4. Write the OIDC role mapping, the metrics and health contract and the Helm values schema, and generate the tables of sections 12 and 14 from them so the document, the mapping and the fake cannot drift.
5. Assemble the fake frontend: the dev server, the namespace with its retention and search attributes, the test CA certificates, the seeded smoke workflow and the declared error answers.
6. Write the contract test: every declaration answered, the no-certificate, expired-certificate and foreign-namespace cases refused, and the metrics and health codes produced.
7. Publish v1 to the contract registry, notify the app story, the worker and SDK story and the 19 services, and record the version each one pins.

**Done when.** Every document validates, the mapping and the tables match the documents, the fake answers every declaration of sections 12 and 14 including the three certificate cases, and the contract test is green on the build of this story.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Published as |
|---|---|---|---|
| PLT-TLS-NOCERT | A client connects with no certificate | The TLS handshake fails; the frontend log records the client identity only | TLS alert |
| PLT-TLS-EXPIRED | A client connects with an expired certificate | The TLS handshake fails with certificate expired | TLS alert |
| PLT-403 | A call presents a certificate issued for another namespace, or names a foreign namespace | The call is refused; no workflow is started | PERMISSION_DENIED |
| PLT-404 | The namespace named in the request is not registered on the cluster | The call is refused; no workflow is started | NOT_FOUND |
| PLT-412 | The request is well formed but the platform state does not allow it, for example a workflow start against a closing namespace | The call is refused with the condition named | FAILED_PRECONDITION |
| PLT-503 | The frontend or the persistence layer is unavailable | The call is refused; the client retries under its own policy | UNAVAILABLE |
| MSG-P4-002 | A Workbench role other than RW-PLATADM or RW-AUDIT is presented to the Web UI mapping | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | 403 on the Web UI |

The contract's own error identifiers are reserved for the implementation; the message catalogue's identifiers for edge and platform entries replace them when they exist and no other value changes.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story, and the document declares none: the Web UI is an operational console behind Entra ID, not a Workbench screen, and no screen is composed by gateway-bff for the platform (DP-19). The mapping fixes the two states the console exposes, operate for RW-PLATADM and read-only for RW-AUDIT, and the refusal state for every other Workbench role. The screens of the Workbench are the gateway-bff surface and the front end, and the platform adds nothing to them.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value and no personal data in the contract, in an example or in the fake: namespace names, role codes, result codes and synthetic workflow identifiers only.
- No service short, no schema name, no topic name and no Workbench REST base in the document: the platform owns none of them (DP-13, DP-14).
- The four search attributes stay CaseId, Stage, ProductGroup and QueueCode; a new attribute is a breaking change and is never added quietly.
- One certificate per service workload identity, from the ACE internal CA, with the namespace claim; no shared certificate and no anonymous client.
- The Web UI maps two roles only; every other Workbench role is refused, and no shared operator account exists.
- The fake is test-only, holds synthetic data and is never deployed to SIT, UAT or PROD; the values schema of no environment points at it.
- The contract is versioned: a breaking change raises v2 and deprecates v1 in place of editing v1.
- Every environment value is a declared key; the document bakes in no replica count, node size, retention value or release number beyond the namespace settings and the release family.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-070 for the workflow platform epic; the cluster is now the shared L1 and L2 platform in namespace rwb-recovery, the monolith schema and login in AC2 are expressed as the P3 rwb-case login and schema rwb_case, and the platform is recorded as owning no schema, no topic and no Workbench REST base. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform administrator (RW-PLATADM)**, I want **one Temporal cluster per environment on the ACE AKS clusters, with its own persistence databases, the rwb-recovery namespace, mTLS and the Web UI behind Entra ID OIDC**, so that **Epic 3 workflows have a durable engine that SCB IT runs like the rest of ACE**.

This is the app story of legacy key RWB-E1-070 under epic RWB-PLT-WF, the Temporal workflow platform of the realignment. The platform is L1 and L2 of the five-layer Temporal design (Architecture v5 slides 23 and 24; Temporal and Drools Design slides 11 and 12): **L1** is the cluster, one per environment on the ACE AKS clusters, with its own persistence database and no grant on the ACE database; **L2** is the namespace `rwb-recovery`, carrying its own retention, certificates and codec keys. The cluster is shared, one per environment, and the next workbench takes a namespace on it rather than a second cluster (Architecture v5 slide 46).

The platform is **not one of the 19 services**. Template and Rules §R4 has no platform row, so the platform owns no `rwb_*` schema, no `rwb.<short>.events.v1` topic, no `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` base and no service short; Architecture v5 slides 4 and 41 keep the shared platform pieces outside the service catalogue, and the platform owns no schema of the ACE database. The server and Java SDK release is Temporal 1.30 or later, for Nexus and Worker Versioning (Temporal and Drools Design slide 32 item 6). The platform identity, meaning its database login, its admin base and the approved release line item, is not in the read sources: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1440; ASM-2535). The platform task queue is task queue `rwb-platform`, which the Ownership Map gives to JOB-22, and the Workbench gives the platform one operation, `POST /admin/workflows/smoke`, both outside this story.

##### 2. Business rationale

Case workflow begins in Epic 3, and a durable engine must exist before the first case workflow is written. The realignment keeps the decision that Temporal runs the case lifecycle while case data stays the system of record in each owner service's `rwb_*` schema; the engine therefore needs its own persistence database, its own identity, its own certificates and its own run book, or Epic 3 builds on a shared service that nobody owns and a restart becomes a developer task.

The split changes three things. First, the cluster is the shared platform layer: one cluster per environment for Recovery and for ACE, namespaces as the unit of isolation, one task queue per service, and workers that stay inside each of the 19 services (Architecture v5 slides 23, 24 and 46). Second, the monolith's single `recovery_svc` login and single `recovery` schema no longer exist, so the separation of databases is proved against one named service: the P3 rwb-case login and schema `rwb_case` (DP-01, DP-02). Third, the platform publishes nothing into the Workbench: no `rwb_*` schema, no topic, no `/api/recovery` base, and no screen, because the Web UI is an operational console behind Entra ID rather than a Workbench screen (DP-13, DP-14, DP-19).

This story provides the platform only: the cluster, the two persistence databases owned by `temporal_svc`, the namespace with 30-day retention and four search attributes, mTLS between the services and the frontend, the Web UI behind Entra ID OIDC, metrics to the ACE monitoring stack and a run book with the eight sections of the run book catalog. It meets REQ-DRI-007 (a named owner and a tested way back for every failure) and REQ-DRI-010 (environment values come from parameters, not code). The measure is that DEV and SIT pass every check in section 16 and that operations restarts a stopped frontend in SIT from the run book alone.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-PLT-E1070-CON is published: the namespace and client contract (namespace `rwb-recovery`, retention, the four search attributes, the client certificate profile, the frontend API subset and its typed errors, the OIDC role mapping, the metrics and health contract) and the fake frontend.
- RWB-PLT-E1072-CON is published: the embedded Drools kit the services' workers run inside their activities (DP-04). The platform hosts those workers and never calls the kit itself.
- RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and RWB-PLT-E1043-CON are published: the platform parameters contract and the reference-data contract, with the client library (DP-06, DP-07).
- RWB-PLT-E1047-CON is published: the topic and event naming library (DP-14). The platform owns no topic and reads it only to prove that no platform topic exists.
- RWB-PLT-E1044-CON is published: the per-service Flyway sequence and migration conventions (DP-15). The Temporal persistence stores are created by the schema job, not by a Flyway migration.
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the gateway-bff composite route surface (DP-19). The Web UI is not a Workbench screen and is not served through it.
- RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON are built against their published contracts and fakes: the parameters and reference data owned by rwb-case, read by the cluster configuration through the platform parameters contract.
- RWB-P4-E1022-CON is built against its published contract and fake: the roles RW-PLATADM and RW-AUDIT that the Web UI maps, and every other Workbench role that it refuses.
- The ACE AKS clusters for DEV, SIT, UAT and PROD exist with the ACE namespace, a zone-redundant PostgreSQL flexible server, Azure Key Vault and the ACE monitoring namespace.
- The SCB IT approved Temporal server and Java SDK release is recorded in Environment and Deployment Design v4, approved 16 November 2026; the approved release is not selected by the build. The release number itself is not in the read sources: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1440; ASM-2535).
- An internal DNS name and ingress exist for the Web UI; the frontend gRPC port 7233 is reachable only from the cluster network and the worker subnets.
- The ACE internal certificate authority issues the mTLS certificates, and the platform administrator may read the certificate from Key Vault.
- The platform administrator holds RW-PLATADM through the environment group; RW-AUDIT holds RW-AUDIT through the environment group.

##### 4. Flow

1. Platform administrator: deploys the Helm release `rwb-temporal` into the ACE namespace of DEV, then SIT, from `rwb-temporal-values.yaml`; the chart runs the frontend, history, matching, internal-worker and web deployments, pinned to the SCB IT approved release.
2. TemporalSchemaJob: creates the databases `temporal` and `temporal_visibility` owned by `temporal_svc` on the zone-redundant PostgreSQL flexible server, then runs the Temporal schema tool at the pinned release; a second run changes nothing and no Flyway migration touches the two stores.
3. NamespaceBootstrapJob: registers the namespace `rwb-recovery` with retention 30 days and the Keyword search attributes CaseId, Stage, ProductGroup and QueueCode; a second run changes nothing.
4. Platform administrator: binds the mTLS certificate and key from Key Vault to the frontend and to each service's worker through the CSI driver; the certificate is issued by the ACE internal CA and names the namespace, and the profile is the one RWB-PLT-E1070-CON publishes.
5. Platform administrator: configures the Web UI with Entra ID OIDC; the app roles map RW-PLATADM to operate and RW-AUDIT to read, and any other Workbench role is refused.
6. Platform administrator: turns on the metrics scrape to the ACE monitoring namespace on the contract endpoints and imports the platform dashboard.
7. Platform administrator: runs every check in section 16 and records the pinned server and SDK release in Environment and Deployment Design v4.
8. Platform administrator: writes the run book with the eight sections and asks operations to restart the frontend in SIT from the run book alone; RWB-PLT-E1056-OPS registers it in the run book catalog and runs RunbookCompletenessTest.
9. System: a frontend pod restart or reschedule keeps every workflow; history and visibility are durable in PostgreSQL, and the workers of the five services in scope reconnect to the replacement pod through the frontend without a replay error.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A client connects to the frontend with no certificate, an expired certificate or a certificate for another namespace | The TLS handshake fails or the call is refused; no workflow call is served and the event is in the frontend log with the client identity only | None (TLS) | AC3 |
| X2 | A user with a Workbench role other than RW-PLATADM or RW-AUDIT signs in to the Web UI | The sign-in is refused; no namespace is listed and no workflow is shown | MSG-P4-002 | AC4 |
| X3 | A grant joins the two databases, for example `temporal_svc` on schema `rwb_case` or the P3 rwb-case login on `temporal` | The access review check fails, the release is held and the grant is removed before the next environment | None (access review) | AC2 |
| X4 | A value the build needs is named by no read source (the platform login, the platform admin base, the approved release number) | The value is used as the working read of the assumption, the placeholder is written where the value is still open, and the gap stays open | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1440; ASM-2535) | AC1, AC7 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Stands alone as platform infrastructure; it needs the ACE cluster, the persistence database server, the Entra app roles, the Key Vault certificate and the run book catalog |
| Negotiable | Pod sizes, storage class, replica count, certificate life and dashboard panels are Helm values; the separation of databases, the namespace settings and the certificate profile are fixed by the contract |
| Valuable | Epic 3 starts on an engine that SCB IT can run, restart and review like the rest of ACE, with one cluster per environment instead of one per workbench |
| Estimable | One Helm release, two persistence databases, one namespace bootstrap, one OIDC app, one certificate binding, one dashboard and one run book |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its checks |
| Testable | Each criterion in section 7 is one check in section 16 |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Temporal platform on the ACE AKS clusters

  Background:
    Given the ACE AKS clusters for DEV and SIT with the ACE namespace
    Given the platform administrator U-70 holds RW-PLATADM through the environment group

    Then the frontend, history, matching and internal-worker deployments each show 2 of 2 pods ready
    Then the web deployment answers on its internal ingress
    Then the namespace rwb-recovery is listed with status REGISTERED
    Then no pod of the release restarted in the last 24 hours

  Scenario: AC2 Separate database grants (legacy RWB-E1-070 AC2)
    Given temporal_svc owns the databases temporal and temporal_visibility
    Given the P3 rwb-case service login owns schema rwb_case in the ACE database
    When a session as temporal_svc runs SELECT on rwb_case.recovery_case
    Then PostgreSQL refuses the statement with SQLSTATE 42501 and returns no row
    When a session as the P3 rwb-case service login runs SELECT on temporal.executions
    Then PostgreSQL refuses the statement with SQLSTATE 42501 and returns no row
    Then the access review report shows no grant between the two roles and the two databases

  Scenario: AC3 mTLS enforced (legacy RWB-E1-070 AC3)
    Given the frontend requires a client certificate signed by the ACE internal CA

    Then the TLS handshake fails and no workflow call is served
    When a worker connects with an expired certificate
    Then the TLS handshake fails with certificate expired
    When a worker connects with a certificate issued for another namespace
    Then the call is refused with PERMISSION_DENIED and no workflow is started

  Scenario: AC4 Web UI roles (legacy RWB-E1-070 AC4)
    Given the Temporal Web UI uses the Entra ID OIDC application with the Workbench app roles
    When U-62 holds RW-CASEOWN only and signs in to the Web UI
    Then the sign-in is refused with MSG-P4-002 and no namespace is listed

  Scenario: AC5 Namespace settings (legacy RWB-E1-070 AC5)
    Given the namespace rwb-recovery in SIT
    When U-70 describes the namespace
    Then retention is 720 hours, 30 days
    Then the search attributes CaseId, Stage, ProductGroup and QueueCode are registered as Keyword
    Then no search attribute holds a name, a national ID or another personal data field

  Scenario: AC6 Frontend restart loses no workflow (legacy RWB-E1-070 AC6)
    Given the smoke workflow platform-smoke-20261116 is RUNNING and waits on its timer
    When the frontend pod is deleted and a replacement pod becomes ready
    Then the workflow is still RUNNING with the same workflow ID and run ID
    When the timer fires and the activity completes
    Then the workflow status is COMPLETED
    Then the history holds every event once, with no gap and no duplicate start

  Scenario: AC7 Run book with the eight headings (legacy RWB-E1-070 AC7)
    Given the run book docs/operations/runbooks/RWB-E1-070.md
    When RunbookCompletenessTest reads the run book
    Then the run book has the sections purpose, schedule, owner, dependencies, failure signs, checks, restart steps and escalation
    Then it names the five Temporal services, the two databases, the namespace, the certificate renewal step and the parameter temporal.target
    Then it names roles and service identities, never a person and never a personal data field
```

The seven criteria are copied from RWB-E1-070 and keep every value; the monolith schema and login names are expressed in target terms (DP-01, DP-02, DP-13).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One Temporal cluster per environment, on the ACE AKS clusters, deployed by the official Temporal Helm chart; the server and Java SDK release are pinned to the SCB IT approved release recorded in Environment and Deployment Design v4, and the release is 1.30 or later for Nexus and Worker Versioning | Template and Rules §R5.5 DP table; ADR-016; Architecture v5 slide 23; Temporal and Drools Design slide 32 item 6 |
| BR2 | Temporal persistence is separate from the ACE database: the databases `temporal` and `temporal_visibility` are owned by `temporal_svc`; `temporal_svc` has no grant on the ACE database and no service login has a grant on the Temporal databases | Architecture v5 slides 8 and 9; Temporal and Drools Design slide 11 |
| BR3 | The frontend requires mTLS from every client; certificates come from the ACE internal CA through Key Vault, name the namespace, and are renewed before expiry | Architecture v5 slide 35; RWB-PLT-E1070-CON |
| BR4 | The Web UI is behind Entra ID OIDC: RW-PLATADM operates, RW-AUDIT reads, every other Workbench role is refused; decode is not in this story | Architecture v5 slide 35; RWB-PLT-E1070-CON; RWB-P4-E1022-CON |
| BR5 | One namespace per environment, `rwb-recovery`; retention is 30 days and the only search attributes are CaseId, Stage, ProductGroup and QueueCode as Keyword | Architecture v5 slides 23 and 24; Temporal and Drools Design slide 27 |
| BR6 | A frontend pod restart loses no workflow; history and visibility are durable in PostgreSQL and a worker reconnects without a replay error | Temporal and Drools Design slide 28; AC6 |
| BR7 | The run book has the eight sections of the run book catalog and is tested by RunbookCompletenessTest | RWB-PLT-E1056-OPS |
| BR8 | Server and SDK releases, replica counts, retention and node sizes are Helm values or parameters, never code | REQ-DRI-010; Architecture v5 slide 20 |

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story changes no case status. It establishes the namespace and the cluster; a workflow created in Epic 3 moves through its own states.

| Object | State | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Namespace | REGISTERED | `rwb-recovery` is registered on the cluster with retention 720 hours and the four Keyword search attributes |
| Server | RUNNING | The five deployments are ready and the frontend serves gRPC on 7233 and the Web UI on its ingress |
| Server | RUNNING (after upgrade) | An upgrade keeps the server RUNNING; AC1 is re-run after the change and no workflow is lost |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-PLATADM | Installs and upgrades the release, runs the namespace bootstrap, reads the database grants, operates the Web UI and restarts a service (Platform administration, U) |
| RW-AUDIT | Reads the namespace and workflow history in the Web UI (Platform administration, R) |
| RW-SECADM | Reads the certificate and OIDC configuration; decode through the codec server is RWB-E2-038, not this story |
| SY-CASEWF | Connects to the frontend as a worker with its own client certificate; no Web UI account |
| SY-RULES | Runs the embedded Drools kit inside its own service's activities and does not connect to Temporal directly |
| RW-TRIBE | Maintains the Helm values and the run book through the change process; may not deploy to PROD |
| RW-CASEOWN and every other Workbench role | No Web UI access; a sign-in is refused with MSG-P4-002 |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A platform deployment is not a credit decision |

##### 11. Data

Temporal persistence is outside the ACE database. This story reads and writes no table in any `rwb_*` schema and no ACE view, and no DF-REF, DF-CAS or DF-DEC field is added or changed.

| Store | What it holds | Owner | In the Physical Schema |
|---|---|---|---|
| temporal | Workflow histories, mutable state, timers, tasks | temporal_svc | No |
| temporal_visibility | Workflow visibility records and search attributes | temporal_svc | No |
| ACE database schemas of the 19 services | Each service's own `rwb_*` schema, the system of record for its data | the 19 services, one login each (DP-02) | Yes, unchanged by this story, no table read or written |

The Physical Schema does not include the Temporal tables. The two stores are created by TemporalSchemaJob at the pinned release; no Flyway migration in any service touches them (DP-15). No field identifier is added by this story.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The platform owns no service short (Template and Rules §R4 has no platform row), so it provides no path under `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` and no Workbench endpoint. The one Workbench operation the Ownership Map gives the platform, `POST /admin/workflows/smoke`, belongs to the platform smoke story (JOB-22) and is out of scope here.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. The platform calls no Workbench service over REST. The cluster reads its configuration through the platform parameters contract of section 13, and the Web UI calls only the frontend and the OIDC provider.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The platform is shared platform and publishes no `rwb.<short>.events.v1` topic and no event schema (DP-14). The decision-record events, the case events and the audit events keep their owners; the ledger seal is out of scope.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The platform consumes no Kafka topic. The events that reach a workflow reach it through the owning service's worker and its own consumer, never through the platform.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None owned. The cluster hosts the workers of the 19 services: each service runs its own worker, polls only its own task queue `rwb-<short>` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, and KEDA scales it on backlog (Architecture v5 slide 24). The platform task queue is task queue `rwb-platform`; it carries the platform smoke workflow and the stuck-workflow scan (JOB-21 and JOB-22 in the Ownership Map), both outside this story.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The platform owns no Schedule in this story. The two platform jobs, the stuck-workflow scan and the smoke workflow, are the observability story's work and are owned there.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Store | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| temporal | temporal_svc | Workflow histories, mutable state, timers and tasks; a Temporal persistence store, not an ACE table and not an `rwb_*` table |
| temporal_visibility | temporal_svc | Workflow visibility records and the four Keyword search attributes; a Temporal persistence store, not an ACE table and not an `rwb_*` table |

The two stores are Temporal persistence and sit outside the Physical Schema of the ACE database. The platform owns no `rwb_*` schema and no table in the ACE database.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| Temporal platform fake frontend (RWB-PLT-E1070-CON) | A Temporal dev server with the namespace `rwb-recovery`, test CA certificates, the declared frontend API subset and a seeded smoke workflow | This story's checks before the cluster exists, the five services' worker tests, the integration harness |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary (REST, Kafka, Temporal, File)

| Call type | Provided | Consumed | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 | 0 | The platform has no `/api/recovery` base and no service short; the Web UI is an operational console, not a Workbench route |
| Kafka | 0 | 0 | The platform owns no topic and consumes none (DP-14) |
| Temporal | The cluster itself: frontend gRPC over mTLS on port 7233, Web UI over HTTPS, metrics on 9090 and health on 8080 | 0 workflows and 0 activities of its own | The 19 services' workers run on this cluster; namespace `rwb-recovery`; task queue `rwb-platform` is the platform queue |
| File | 0 | 0 | No file is read or written; the ledger seal file is out of scope |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** No Java package. The deployment assets live in `deploy/temporal/`; the run book lives in `docs/operations/runbooks/RWB-E1-070.md`; the dashboard lives in `ops/monitoring/`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-temporal-values.yaml | Helm values | Images, replica counts, resources, persistence, mTLS, metrics and ingress per environment |
| TemporalSchemaJob | Pipeline job | Creates `temporal` and `temporal_visibility` and runs the Temporal schema tool at the pinned release; idempotent |
| NamespaceBootstrapJob | Pipeline job | Registers `rwb-recovery` with retention 30 days and the four Keyword search attributes; idempotent |
| OidcConfig | Configuration | Entra ID app registration, redirect URI, role claims and the mapping to RW-PLATADM and RW-AUDIT |
| KeyVaultCertificateBinding | Configuration | CSI driver binding of the mTLS certificate and key; renewal before expiry |
| TemporalPlatformDashboard | Dashboard | Grafana JSON for service readiness, request rate, errors and persistence latency |
| TemporalPlatformRunBook | Document | The eight sections of the run book catalog, with the restart steps for each service |

**Database and namespace**

- Create the databases `temporal` and `temporal_visibility` with owner `temporal_svc` on the zone-redundant PostgreSQL flexible server.
- Create the role `temporal_svc` with no membership in any service login, and no service login with a grant on the two Temporal databases; revoke PUBLIC on both databases.
- Register `rwb-recovery` with retention 720 hours and the search attributes CaseId, Stage, ProductGroup and QueueCode as Keyword.
- Keep the ACE namespace `ace-collection` unregistered by this story; it belongs to the ACE team and is reached through Nexus.

**Configuration and reference data**

- Parameters through RWB-E1-042, published as the platform parameters contract RWB-PLT-E1042-CON (DP-06): `temporal.target`, `temporal.namespace`, `temporal.taskqueue.platform`, `temporal.retention.days` = 30.
- Helm values per environment: replica counts, resources, storage class, ingress host, certificate secret name, metrics scrape and log level.
- No business parameter and no reference table in this story; reference data is read through RWB-PLT-E1043-CON (DP-07) and no value is copied into a values file.
- The platform login and the platform admin base are not in the read sources: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1440; ASM-2535).

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-02 | `recovery_svc` login | One login per service | none |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**DP-01.** The cluster writes no ACE schema. It owns the two persistence stores and nothing else, and AC2 proves that `temporal_svc` cannot read `rwb_case.recovery_case`, so the split of the old `recovery` schema into per-service schemas is not quietly undone by a platform grant.

**DP-02.** One login per service, and `temporal_svc` is separate. The monolith's single `recovery_svc` login is replaced by one login per service; this story creates only `temporal_svc` and uses the P3 rwb-case login as the named counterparty in AC2, because rwb-case is the first owner of case data the engine serves.

**DP-04.** The Drools kit runs in each service's worker inside an activity and never in workflow code (Temporal and Drools Design slide 12). The platform hosts those workers; it installs no rule engine, holds no KieBase and makes no Drools call, and the kit contract is a precondition only.

**DP-05.** No service reads the ACE views except rwb-source-data, and the platform reads no ACE view at all. The workflows the cluster runs get their ACE data through the owning service's activity, so the cluster needs no view grant and no ACE login.

**DP-06.** Parameters arrive through the platform parameters contract rather than a values file: `temporal.target`, `temporal.namespace`, `temporal.taskqueue.platform` and `temporal.retention.days` = 30 are read at deploy time, and a change of environment value is a parameter change, not a rebuild.

**DP-07.** Reference data is read through RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and never copied into the chart. The only list this story touches is the environment list, which is a Helm value, and the role codes the Web UI maps, which come from RWB-P4-E1022-CON.

**DP-13.** There is no monolith API base and no `/api/recovery` base on the platform. The platform has no service short, so no path is published; the Web UI is reached on its own ingress and the frontend on gRPC 7233, both internal to the ACE network.

**DP-14.** The platform has no topic and events keep the owners' names. The decision-record topic, the case topic and the audit events stay with their owners, and the platform's Helm values carry no topic name at all.

**DP-15.** The Temporal schema job is not a Flyway migration. The two persistence stores are created and upgraded by the Temporal schema tool at the pinned release, outside the per-service Flyway sequence, so no service migration history records a Temporal object.

**DP-19.** The Web UI is not a Workbench screen, and screens go through gateway-bff. The console is an operational view with Entra ID sign-in behind it; no case screen is served by the platform, and the platform adds no route to the gateway.

**Build steps**

1. Write the values file for DEV and SIT and run helm lint and helm template in the pipeline, against the pinned release.
2. Build TemporalSchemaJob with the schema tool; prove a second run changes nothing and that no Flyway migration touches the two stores.
3. Build NamespaceBootstrapJob with retention and the four search attributes; prove a second run changes nothing.
4. Bind the certificate from Key Vault; test AC3 with no certificate, an expired certificate and a foreign certificate, using the profile the contract publishes.
5. Configure the OIDC app roles; test AC4 with RW-CASEOWN, RW-AUDIT and RW-PLATADM.
6. Add the metrics scrape on the contract endpoints and import the dashboard; check that every service reports.
7. Run the database grant checks for AC2 and add them to the access review.
8. Write the run book, hand it to RWB-PLT-E1056-OPS for the catalog and RunbookCompletenessTest, and run the frontend restart in SIT for AC6.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.p3.temporal`, read through the platform parameters contract. The flag controls the worker of RWB-PLT-E1071, not the cluster. With the flag off, the cluster and namespace stay in place and nothing else changes.

**Done when.** The checks in section 16 pass in DEV and SIT, the database grants are in the access review, the contract test of RWB-PLT-E1070-CON stays green, and operations restarts the frontend in SIT from the run book alone.

No Workbench screen in this story. The operational view is the Temporal Web UI behind Entra ID, with two states: operate for RW-PLATADM and read-only for RW-AUDIT. A refused sign-in shows MSG-P4-002. The Grafana dashboard "Temporal platform" shows the five deployments, request rate, errors and persistence latency. The Web UI is not a Workbench screen and is not composed by gateway-bff (DP-19); the Workbench admin screens for platform settings come in Epic 8.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: replica counts, retention, node sizes and releases are Helm values or parameters (BR8, DP-06).
- No personal data in logs, tests, workflow history or prompts: search attributes hold case codes and queue codes only; the smoke payload is synthetic.
- No read of another service's tables and no ACE view: the platform reads no `rwb_*` table and no `recovery.v_ace_*` view (DP-01, DP-05).
- Temporal persistence is never placed in the ACE database, and no service login is granted on the two Temporal stores (BR2).
- No Workbench account for a role other than RW-PLATADM and RW-AUDIT; no shared operator account (BR4).
- No clear personal data in a Temporal payload; the codec is the codec-server story's work.
- No mTLS bypass in DEV or SIT; a test that needs a certificate uses a certificate from the test CA, as the contract's fake declares.
- No platform topic, no platform `/api/recovery` base and no `rwb_*` schema: the platform is not one of the 19 services (DP-13, DP-14).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: RWB-E1-070 is split and reworked. The cluster, the two Temporal databases, the namespace bootstrap, the mTLS certificates, the Entra ID configuration, the dashboard and the run book become the wave-0 platform deliverable RWB-PLT-E1070-APP, and the Workbench roles the Web UI maps come from RWB-P4-E1022-APP; the legacy criteria AC1 to AC7 stay at component level there. This wave-1 integration story keeps only what no component story can prove: one namespace `rwb-recovery` per environment, one task queue `rwb-<short>` and one worker identity per service on the real wave-1 services, a step in another service executed as a Temporal call on that service's queue and not as a REST chain, the two Temporal databases refused to every `rwb_*` login and back, a smoke run that survives a frontend pod restart with the same workflow ID and run ID, no personal data in payloads or search attributes, and 30-day retention with no Quartz table behind a workflow timer. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **QA integration engineer**, I want **the shared Temporal platform of the programme proved on the real wave-1 services — one namespace `rwb-recovery` per environment, one task queue `rwb-<short>` and one worker identity per service, each worker presenting its own certificate, the two Temporal databases refused to every `rwb_*` login and back, a step in another service executed as a Temporal call on that service's queue with no REST hop, the smoke workflow `platform-smoke-20261116` still RUNNING with the same workflow ID and run ID after a frontend pod restart, no personal data in workflow payloads or search attributes, and 720 hours of retention with no Quartz table or shared job table behind a workflow timer**, so that **the engine every case workflow of Epic 3 depends on is proved on the services that will run it, before wave 1 exits**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story installs one Temporal cluster per environment on the ACE AKS clusters as a single-module platform enabler: the databases `temporal` and `temporal_visibility` owned by `temporal_svc`, the namespace `rwb-recovery` with 30-day retention and four Keyword search attributes, mTLS from the ACE internal CA, the Web UI behind Entra ID OIDC, metrics and a run book. That work does not disappear, but it is no longer Epic 1 module work: Arch v5 slides 23 and 24 keep the cluster, the namespaces and the workflow kit owned once by the platform team and reused by every workbench (DP, platform epic RWB-PLT-WF), so the release, the schema jobs, the namespace bootstrap, the certificates, the OIDC application, the dashboard and the run book become RWB-PLT-E1070-APP in wave 0, and the Workbench roles the Web UI maps come from rwb-access in RWB-P4-E1022-APP. The seven legacy criteria stay where they are built.

What no component story can prove is the shape the platform has to hold once 19 services use it. In the target every service has its own task queue `rwb-<short>` in the one namespace (Arch v5 slide 41), its own login and its own schema `rwb_<name>` with its own Flyway sequence (DP-02, DP-01, DP-15), its own topic `rwb.<short>.events.v1` through the naming library (DP-14), its own embedded Drools kit taking rule packages from rwb-decision (DP-04), parameters and reference data through the contracts of rwb-case (DP-06, DP-07), ACE data only through rwb-source-data (DP-05), REST only at `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` (DP-13) and only behind gateway-bff (DP-19). On that shape four properties are load-bearing and none of them is visible from one module:

- A service that polls another service's queue takes work it may not execute; two registrations of one service quietly double the pollers of a queue. Both break the release boundary that makes a service reusable.
- A shared or foreign certificate makes the frontend log useless and lets one service signal another service's workflows.
- A REST chain between two services inside a business step puts a synchronous dependency inside a durable process, which is exactly what Arch v5 slide 11 forbids; the step has to be a Temporal call on the owner's queue with the workflow ID as the idempotency key.
- One grant between `temporal_svc` and a `rwb_*` schema puts case data in the workflow store or workflow history in the case schema, and a workflow timer parked in a Quartz table puts the durability of a case on the scheduler that Arch v5 slide 44 retires.

This story builds the harness that proves those properties together, on the nine wave-1 services, against the deployed platform of RWB-PLT-E1070-APP and the roles of RWB-P4-E1022-APP. It meets REQ-DRI-007 (a named owner and a tested way back for every failure) and REQ-DRI-010 (environment values come from configuration, not code): the namespace, the retention, the four search attributes, the queue list, the probe queue and the endpoints are configuration, and the harness edits no platform value to make a test pass.

The legacy measure — DEV and SIT pass every check, and operations restart a stopped frontend in SIT from the run book alone — stays with RWB-PLT-E1070-APP, which owns the run book. The measure of this story is the platform-wide one: the seven checks of section 16 pass on the deployed wave-1 services in SIT, each of the nine services shows exactly one poller on its own queue, the smoke run keeps its workflow ID and run ID across a frontend pod delete and completes once, the cross-service step is a Temporal call with no REST hop, and both grant directions are refused with SQLSTATE 42501.

The worker registration, the per-service certificate and the smoke-queue element of the platform contract, and the exact way the suite selects the cross-service step and the access review evidence, are not named in the sources: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0378; ASM-0544). The suite asserts the properties that are named and records the three defaults it reads from configuration, so a change of registration path or probe queue is one configuration edit and one test edit.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-PLT-E1070-APP is done in wave 0: the release, TemporalSchemaJob, NamespaceBootstrapJob, the OIDC configuration, the certificate binding, the dashboard and the run book are in place (Template and Rules §R5.6: platform is wave 0).
- The namespace `rwb-recovery` exists once in SIT with retention 720 hours and the Keyword search attributes CaseId, Stage, ProductGroup and QueueCode.
- RWB-P4-E1022-APP is done: rwb-access holds the Workbench roles RW-PLATADM, RW-AUDIT and RW-CASEOWN with their letters, and the synthetic SIT sign-in identities U-70, U-53 and U-62 are mapped to them.
- The nine wave-1 services are deployed in SIT with their own worker deployment, login and schema: rwb-source-data (P1), rwb-integration (P2), rwb-case (P3), rwb-access (P4), rwb-document (P5), rwb-comms (P6), rwb-decision (P7), rwb-reporting (P9) and rwb-agent (P10), each on its own task queue `rwb-<short>`.
- Each of the nine worker deployments runs in the ACE namespace of SIT with a workload identity and a client certificate issued by the ACE internal CA that names the namespace; the certificate and key are readable through the CSI driver binding of RWB-PLT-E1070-APP.
- The published activity contract jar of each service is in the artefact repository, so the smoke run can call a step on another service's queue without importing that service's code.
- The ACE AKS SIT cluster runs the ACE namespace, the zone-redundant PostgreSQL flexible server, Key Vault, the ACE monitoring namespace and the internal ingress of the Web UI; the frontend gRPC port 7233 is reachable only from the cluster network and the worker subnets.
- The access review report of the platform is produced in SIT and lists the grants of `temporal_svc` and of every `rwb_*` login.
- The harness reads the namespace, the retention, the four search attributes, the nine queues, the probe queue, the workflow ID `platform-smoke-20261116`, the endpoints and the three test identities from configuration, and refuses a UAT or production target.
- The worker registration, the per-service certificate and the smoke-queue element of the platform contract, and the selection of the cross-service step, are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0378; ASM-0544).
- The run is SIT only, on synthetic data; no run of this harness points at UAT or production, and no production connection is opened.
- The release date 30 November 2026 is tentative; a date is not a condition of this story.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7). The harness is written on Day 1 against the platform contract and is run when the wave-1 services are in SIT; a fake worker is never used in place of a service worker.

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: loads the configuration — the namespace, the retention, the four search attributes, the nine queues, the probe queue, the workflow ID `platform-smoke-20261116`, the endpoints, the three test identities — and runs the preflight; a missing namespace, deployment, queue, role or certificate, or a UAT or production target, stops the run before any test.
2. Harness: describes the namespace of the environment and asserts that it is the single namespace `rwb-recovery` in which a wave-1 service runs (AC1, AC7).
3. Harness: describes the nine task queues and records the poller identity of each, then compares it with the workload identity of the owning service and with the queue declaration of that service's worker deployment (AC1).
4. Harness: connects to the frontend with no certificate, with an expired certificate and with a certificate issued for another namespace, and attempts to start a workflow each time; then connects each of the nine service certificates and records the result (AC2).
5. Harness: runs the grant probes — a session as `temporal_svc` against a table of each `rwb_*` schema, and a session as each `rwb_*` login against `temporal` and `temporal_visibility` — and records SQLSTATE 42501 each time, then reads the access review report (AC3).
6. Harness: starts the smoke workflow `platform-smoke-20261116` on the queue of the service named in configuration, with the workflow ID `platform-smoke-20261116` as the idempotency key, and waits until it is RUNNING on its timer (AC4, AC5).
7. Harness: asserts the two steps the run executes — the read step through the published activity contract on task queue `rwb-decision` and the write step on task queue `rwb-case` — and asserts that the call chain of the run holds no REST call between two services (AC4).
8. Harness: starts the same workflow ID a second time and asserts that the running execution is returned with no second run and no second write (AC4).
9. Harness: deletes the frontend pod, waits for the replacement pod to be ready, and re-reads the workflow — same workflow ID, same run ID, still RUNNING; the timer then fires and the smoke activity completes the run (AC5).
10. Harness: reads the search attributes of the namespace and of the run and the payload of the run and of its two activity calls, and asserts the four Keyword attributes only and no personal data field (AC6).
11. Harness: reads the timer of the run from the workflow history of the database `temporal` and asserts that no Quartz table and no ACE shared job table holds it (AC7).
12. Harness: reconciles the counts — one namespace, nine queues, nine pollers, one smoke run, zero grants across the boundary, zero REST calls in the chain — and writes the run report.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A client connects to the frontend with no certificate, an expired certificate or a certificate for another namespace | The TLS handshake fails or the call is refused with PERMISSION_DENIED; no workflow is started or signalled, and the frontend log records the client identity only | None (TLS) | AC2 |
| X2 | A service registers two workers, a worker declares two queues, or a queue lists a poller of another service | The run fails and the report names the service, the queue and the identity; no test after it runs | None | AC1 |
| X3 | A grant exists between `temporal_svc` and a `rwb_*` schema, or between a `rwb_*` login and the Temporal databases, in either direction | The run fails, the access review check fails and the grant is removed before the next environment | None (access review) | AC3 |
| X4 | A step in another service is executed as a REST call, or a workflow of the run calls a service base | The run fails and the report names the step, the workflow ID and the path called | None | AC4 |
| X5 | The frontend pod delete loses, restarts or duplicates the smoke run | The run fails and names the workflow ID, the run ID and the status observed after the restart | None | AC5 |
| X6 | A search attribute, a workflow input or a payload carries a name, a national ID or another personal data field | The run fails and the field is named in the report; the platform value is corrected in RWB-PLT-E1070-APP, never in the harness | None | AC6 |
| X7 | Retention differs from 720 hours, or a workflow timer is found in a Quartz table or a shared job table | The run fails and names the store that holds the timer | None | AC7 |
| X8 | The configuration points at UAT or production, a service has no worker deployment, or a fake worker or fake frontend is configured | The preflight stops the run with the offending element named; no test data is written anywhere | None | AC1 |

X1 is the legacy exception path X1 of RWB-E1-070 carried onto the real services; X3 is the legacy X3 carried onto the 19 schemas; X2 and X4 are the registration and call-shape regressions that Arch v5 slides 11, 24 and 41 need; X5 to X7 are the durability, boundary and retention guardrails in testable form.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | A harness of its own that owns no schema, no migration and no workflow; it needs the platform contract of RWB-PLT-E1070-APP, the roles of RWB-P4-E1022-APP and the nine wave-1 workers |
| Negotiable | Probe queue, wait intervals, retry counts, the certificate names and the report layout are configuration; the namespace, the retention, the four search attributes, the queue list and the two message IDs are fixed |
| Valuable | Proves across services what no single story proves: nine registrations on nine queues, no cross-polling, one certificate per service, a step in another service as a Temporal call, a restart that loses nothing, a boundary with no grant and no timer in a scheduler table |
| Estimable | One harness module, six probes, one restart window and one report |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the report |
| Testable | Every criterion is asserted on an observable: a namespace describe, a queue describe, a poller identity, a TLS result, an activity call, a workflow ID and run ID, SQLSTATE 42501, a search attribute, a retention value and a history event count |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin

  Background:
    Given the environment is SIT with synthetic data

    Given the nine wave-1 services rwb-source-data, rwb-integration, rwb-case, rwb-access, rwb-document, rwb-comms, rwb-decision, rwb-reporting and rwb-agent each run their own worker deployment behind their own login and schema
    Given no contract fake stands in for a service in this suite

  Scenario: AC1 One namespace per environment, one queue per service and each worker polls only its own queue (new, D-RCV-60)

    When the harness describes the namespaces of SIT

    When the harness describes every task queue of the namespace
    Then the nine queues rwb-source-data, rwb-integration, rwb-case, rwb-access, rwb-document, rwb-comms, rwb-decision, rwb-reporting and rwb-agent are registered
    Then each of the nine queues lists exactly one poller and that poller is the workload identity of the service that owns the queue
    Then no queue lists a poller of another service and no worker identity appears on two queues

  Scenario: AC2 Each worker presents its own certificate and a missing, expired or foreign certificate is refused (new, D-RCV-60)

    When a client connects with no certificate and tries to start the smoke workflow

    When a client connects with a certificate issued for another namespace

    Then every connection is accepted and no two services present the same certificate

  Scenario: AC3 The Temporal databases and the rwb_* schemas are separated in both directions (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given temporal_svc owns the databases temporal and temporal_visibility
    Given each wave-1 service reads and writes the ACE database through its own rwb_* login
    When a session as temporal_svc runs SELECT on a table of each rwb_* schema of the nine services
    Then PostgreSQL refuses every statement with SQLSTATE 42501 and returns no row
    When a session as each of the nine rwb_* logins runs SELECT on temporal.executions and on a table of temporal_visibility
    Then PostgreSQL refuses every statement with SQLSTATE 42501 and returns no row
    Then the access review report shows no grant between temporal_svc and any rwb_* schema and no grant from a rwb_* login to the two Temporal databases

  Scenario: AC4 A step in another service is a Temporal call on that service's queue and the chain makes no REST call (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the platform workflow kit of RWB-PLT-WF and the published activity contract of each wave-1 service are deployed

    When the run reaches the write step that belongs to rwb-case
    Then the step is executed as the activity RecordAndApply on task queue rwb-case
```
