All seven criteria are new: the legacy criteria AC1 to AC7 of RWB-E1-070 assert the cluster, the two databases, mTLS, the Web UI roles, the namespace settings, the frontend restart and the run book at component level, and they are owned by RWB-PLT-E1070-APP (with the roles of AC4 taken from RWB-P4-E1022-APP). Nothing of that is re-copied here; this story asserts the same platform across services, on the queues, the identities, the call shape, the retention and the boundary that only exist once more than one service uses it.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One Temporal cluster per environment on the ACE AKS clusters and one namespace per workbench; the platform is owned once by the platform team and each service only runs a worker in it | Arch v5 slides 23 and 24; RWB-PLT-E1070-APP |
| BR2 | The namespace is `rwb-recovery` in every environment; retention is 30 days (720 hours) and the only search attributes are CaseId, Stage, ProductGroup and QueueCode as Keyword, holding case codes and queue codes only | RWB-E1-070 BR5; Arch v5 slide 23; Temporal design slide 27 |
| BR3 | Each service registers exactly one worker on the task queue `rwb-<short>` of its own service in namespace `rwb-recovery`, and no worker polls another service's queue | Arch v5 slides 23, 24 and 41; Temporal design slide 11 |
| BR4 | Every worker connects to the frontend over mTLS with its own certificate from the ACE internal CA naming the namespace; a missing, expired or foreign-namespace certificate starts and signals nothing | RWB-E1-070 BR3; Arch v5 slide 11 |
| BR5 | Temporal persistence is separate from the ACE database: `temporal_svc` has no grant on any `rwb_*` schema and no `rwb_*` login has a grant on `temporal` or `temporal_visibility` | RWB-E1-070 BR2; Arch v5 slide 11 |
| BR6 | A step in another service is a Temporal call on the owner's task queue; the workflow ID is the business key and therefore the idempotency key, and a REST call between two services inside a business step is not allowed | Arch v5 slide 11 (never: call chains, depth greater than one); Temporal design slide 12 |
| BR7 | A frontend pod restart loses no workflow: the run keeps its workflow ID and run ID, completes on its timer, and its history holds every event once | RWB-E1-070 BR6 |
| BR8 | No personal data in a search attribute, a workflow payload, a workflow input, a workflow history or a log; the smoke payload is synthetic and the codec is out of scope here | RWB-E1-070 §17; Arch v5 slide 11 (never: PII in workflow code or payloads); Temporal design slide 27 |
| BR9 | A workflow timer lives in the Temporal history and never in a Quartz table or a shared job table; every scheduled job is a Temporal Schedule in its owning service | Arch v5 slide 44; Template and Rules §R5.5 DP-10 |
| BR10 | Namespace, retention, search attributes, queue list, endpoints, probe queue and workflow ID are configuration read at run time, never code (REQ-DRI-010); the harness never points at UAT or production | RWB-E1-070 BR8; REQ-DRI-010 |

##### 9. State transitions

None for a case status. This story changes no case status and starts no business workflow; it observes the platform states below.

| Item | States |
|---|---|
| Namespace | REGISTERED (the only state of a namespace in this story); a missing namespace or a second namespace holding a wave-1 run stops the run |
| Worker registration | Registered on its own queue `rwb-<short>` and polling it, or unregistered; a second registration, a second queue or a foreign poller fails the run |
| Certificate | Valid and accepted, or absent, expired or issued for another namespace and refused |
| Workflow run | RUNNING on its timer, then COMPLETED; a lost, restarted or duplicated run fails the run |
| Activity step | Executed on the owner's queue, or refused; a REST hop in its place fails the run |
| Grant | Absent across the boundary (`temporal_svc` against `rwb_*`, `rwb_*` against the Temporal databases) and refused with SQLSTATE 42501; present fails the run |
| Timer | Held in the workflow history of the database `temporal`; held in a Quartz table or a shared job table fails the run |
| Harness run | Not started, running, passed, or failed with the criterion, the service and the observable named |

The suite reads these states through the platform interfaces and the access review report; it changes none of them directly.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| QA integration engineer | Owns the harness, the fixtures, the restart window and the report; runs the suite in SIT |
| RW-PLATADM Platform administrator | Reads the namespace, the queues and the deployments; owns the platform values the suite only reads |
| RW-AUDIT Internal audit | Reads the namespace and the workflow history in the Web UI; changes nothing |
| RW-SECADM Security administrator | Reads the certificate and OIDC configuration; decode through the codec server is RWB-E2-038, not this story |
| RW-CASEOWN and every other Workbench role | No Web UI access on the platform surface; the role mapping is RWB-P4-E1022-APP |
| The nine service worker identities | Connect with their own certificate and poll only their own queue `rwb-<short>`; no Web UI account |
| RWB-PLT-E1070-APP owner | Owns the cluster, the namespace, the registration contract, the certificates, the Schedule and the run book that this story exercises |
| RWB-P4-E1022-APP owner | Owns the Workbench roles and their letters that the Web UI maps |
| No role | May register a second worker, poll another service's queue, share a certificate between services or hold a grant across the database boundary |

No delegation of authority level applies: a platform proof is not a credit decision.

##### 11. Data

Temporal persistence is outside the recovery schema. This story reads and writes no table in the recovery schema, adds no DF-REF, DF-CAS or DF-DEC field, and owns no schema of its own.

| Store | What it holds | Owner | In the Physical Schema |
|---|---|---|---|
| `temporal` | Workflow histories, mutable state, timers, tasks | `temporal_svc` | No |
| `temporal_visibility` | Workflow visibility records and search attributes | `temporal_svc` | No |
| ACE database, the `rwb_*` schemas | Case and module data, the system of record | each service login | Yes, unchanged by this story |

The Physical Schema counts 93 tables and does not include the Temporal tables. The two Temporal databases are created by TemporalSchemaJob of RWB-PLT-E1070-APP; no Flyway migration of any service touches them. The only data the suite handles is the synthetic smoke payload, which carries CaseId, Stage, ProductGroup and QueueCode and no personal data; every other observable is a namespace describe, a queue describe, a Web UI page, a gRPC start or signal, a SQL SELECT that must be refused, or a read of the access review report. Where the suite stores its evidence is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0378; ASM-0546).

##### 12. Contract

The platform is reached over Temporal gRPC on port 7233 with mTLS, and over the Temporal Web UI on its internal ingress behind Entra ID OIDC. It is not reached through a Workbench REST operation: this story adds no path under `/api/recovery/<short>/v1`, no service base and no service route, and no service proxies a workflow call.

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness is a test project and provides no REST operation. No path is added under `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` for any service, and the names of P2 rwb-integration are not used: no `/api/recovery/integration/v1` operation, no `rwb.integration.events.v1` topic and no `rwb_integration` table is written by this story.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. The platform interfaces are Temporal gRPC (start, signal, describe) and the Web UI; neither is a Workbench REST operation. No service base is called by the harness and none is called by a workflow of the run, because a step in another service is a Temporal call on that service's queue (AC4). The Workbench roles the Web UI maps are held in rwb-access and reach the Web UI as Entra ID app-role claims (RWB-P4-E1022-APP), so the harness makes no authorise call.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness publishes no business event, and no workflow payload is published to Kafka.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. This story consumes no Kafka topic: the smoke run is started by the harness on a task queue, not by an event, and no consumer group is created for the suite.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Owner | Use in the suite |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PlatformSmokeWorkflow` with workflow ID `platform-smoke-20261116` | Workflow, one of the templates of the platform workflow kit | the queue of the one wave-1 service named in configuration | RWB-PLT-E1070-APP (platform workflow kit) | Started once with the workflow ID as the idempotency key, survives a frontend pod delete and completes on its timer (AC4, AC5) |
| `EvaluateRules` | Activity of the published activity contract | `rwb-decision` | P7 rwb-decision | The decision step that belongs to another service, executed as a Temporal call on the owner's queue and not as a REST call (AC4) |
| `RecordAndApply` | Activity of the published activity contract | `rwb-case` | P3 rwb-case | The write step executed on the owner's queue; repeated under the same workflow ID to prove no second write (AC4) |
| the remaining templates of the platform workflow kit (`Approval`, `Human task with SLA`, `Saga runner`, `Scheduled job`, `Notify`, `Partner instruction`) | Versioned workflow and activity library | the queue of the service that uses the template | RWB-PLT-WF | Not started by this story; named so the suite asserts that the smoke run uses a kit template and starts no business workflow |

The workflow ID is the business key of the run and therefore the idempotency key: a second start with `platform-smoke-20261116` returns the running execution and starts nothing. No case workflow, no stage workflow and no child workflow of any service is started by this story.

The worker registration, task-queue and namespace contract between the services and the platform — worker identity, certificate per service, queue registration, the selection of the step that belongs to another service and the smoke endpoint target — is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0378; ASM-0544); ASM-0545 fixes the call shape the suite asserts: one activity call on the owner's queue per cross-service step, under the workflow ID of the run.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Temporal Schedule belongs to this story: the smoke run is started once by the harness, and the Schedule JOB-22 of Arch v5 slide 44 — the same workflow type at 06:00 — is owned and registered by RWB-PLT-E1070-APP. The suite reads that JOB-22 exists and changes nothing about it.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. Temporal persistence is outside the recovery schema and the harness owns no table in the ACE database, in `temporal` or in `temporal_visibility`. The stores it touches are listed in section 11 with their owners, and every statement the harness runs is a SELECT that must be refused.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

None, and no service contract is faked: this is the integration level, so the real platform, the real nine service workers, the real certificates and the real access review replace the fakes of the app stories. A run configured with a fake worker or a fake frontend fails the preflight. The payload codec of the platform is out of scope and is neither exercised nor faked here.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Provided by the suite | Consumed by the suite |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 | 0 |
| Kafka | 0 | 0 |
| Temporal | 0 | 14 calls: one namespace describe, nine queue describes, two starts of the same workflow ID, the `EvaluateRules` call on `rwb-decision` and the `RecordAndApply` call on `rwb-case` |
| File | 0 | 0 |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `integration/recovery/wave1/temporal` in the ACE repository, package `<ACE base package>.recovery.itg.wave1.temporal`. Not part of a deployed service.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| HarnessRunner | Runner | Preflight against the platform contract and the nine worker deployments, run order, report and exit code |
| ConfigLoader | Service | Reads the namespace, the retention, the four search attributes, the nine queues, the probe queue, the workflow ID, the endpoints and the three test identities, and refuses a UAT or production target |
| QueuePollerProbe | Service | Describes the namespace and the nine queues, records the poller identity of each, and fails on a second namespace, a second registration of one service, a worker identity on two queues or a poller of another service (AC1) |
| TlsProbe | Service | Connects with no certificate, an expired certificate, a certificate for another namespace and each of the nine service certificates; starts a workflow on each attempt and records the TLS result and the frontend log line (AC2) |
| GrantProbe | Service | Runs the SELECT set as `temporal_svc` against each `rwb_*` schema and as each `rwb_*` login against the two Temporal databases, records SQLSTATE 42501 and reads the access review report (AC3) |
| CallShapeProbe | Service | Starts the smoke run, asserts the `EvaluateRules` call on `rwb-decision` and the `RecordAndApply` call on `rwb-case`, asserts no REST call in the chain, and repeats the start under the same workflow ID (AC4) |
| RestartProbe | Service | Deletes the frontend pod, waits for the replacement pod, re-reads the workflow ID, the run ID, the status and the history event count, and lets the timer complete the run (AC5) |
| PayloadProbe | Service | Reads the search attributes of the namespace and of the run and the payload of the run and of its two activity calls, and asserts the four Keyword attributes and no personal data field (AC6) |
| TimerProbe | Service | Reads the retention of the namespace, the timer of the run from the history of `temporal`, and the absence of the timer in a Quartz table and in the ACE shared job table (AC7) |
| ReportWriter | Service | One row per test case with the observable, the evidence and the elapsed time |

**Real-service topology.** The nine wave-1 services are reached as the real SIT services behind their own logins (DP-02): rwb-source-data (P1, schema `rwb_source_data`, queue `rwb-source-data`), rwb-integration (P2, schema `rwb_integration`, queue `rwb-integration`), rwb-case (P3, schema `rwb_case`, queue `rwb-case`), rwb-access (P4, schema `rwb_access`, queue `rwb-access`), rwb-document (P5, schema `rwb_document`, queue `rwb-document`), rwb-comms (P6, schema `rwb_comms`, queue `rwb-comms`), rwb-decision (P7, schema `rwb_decision`, queue `rwb-decision`), rwb-reporting (P9, schema `rwb_reporting`, queue `rwb-reporting`) and rwb-agent (P10, schema `rwb_agent`, queue `rwb-agent`). Each service keeps its own base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` (DP-13) behind gateway-bff (DP-19) and its own topic `rwb.<short>.events.v1` (DP-14); none of those bases is called by this suite.

**Fixtures**

| Fixture | Content | Used by |
|---|---|---|

| Namespace baseline | The namespace describe, retention 720 hours, the four Keyword search attributes and the Schedule JOB-22 | AC1, AC6, AC7 |

The dependency-added column records the build dependency of the owning story: DP-04, DP-06, DP-07, DP-14, DP-15 and DP-19 resolve to platform contract stories and stay with the service and platform builds that apply them; DP-01, DP-02, DP-05 and DP-13 add none. The H, C, I and X lists of this story are exactly those of the metadata table: no H, no C, no X, and the two I dependencies RWB-P4-E1022-APP and RWB-PLT-E1070-APP. An ITG story waits on no build of its own (§R5.4, §R5.7).

**Build steps**

1. Create the harness module next to the wave-1 harness RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG and wire it to the SIT gRPC endpoint, the Web UI ingress and the platform contract of RWB-PLT-E1070-APP.
2. Build the ConfigLoader with the namespace, the retention, the four search attributes, the nine queues, the probe queue, the workflow ID and the three test identities; prove that a UAT or production target stops the run.
3. Implement AC1 with the namespace describe and the nine queue describes, and fail on a second namespace, a second registration or a foreign poller.
4. Implement AC2 with the three refusal certificates and the nine accepted service certificates, and record the frontend log line of each refusal.
5. Implement AC3 with the two grant directions and the access review report read.
6. Implement AC4: start the smoke run with the workflow ID `platform-smoke-20261116`, assert the `EvaluateRules` call on `rwb-decision` and the `RecordAndApply` call on `rwb-case`, assert no REST call in the chain, and repeat the start.
7. Implement AC5 with the frontend pod delete, the readiness wait, the workflow ID, the run ID, the status and the history event count, and implement AC6 and AC7 on the payload, the search attributes, the retention and the timer store.
8. Run the suite in SIT against the wave-1 release candidate, write the report and attach it to the wave-1 integration record.

**Configuration.** The namespace, the retention, the four search attributes, the nine queues, the probe queue, the workflow ID, the endpoints, the certificate names and the three test identities sit in configuration files; no platform value and no business value is coded in a test method.

**Done when.** The seven test cases of section 16 pass in SIT on the nine deployed wave-1 services, each of the nine shows exactly one poller on its own queue, the cross-service step is a Temporal call on the owner's queue with no REST hop, the smoke run keeps its workflow ID and run ID across the frontend delete and completes once, both grant directions are refused with SQLSTATE 42501, the retention is 720 hours with no timer in a Quartz or shared job table, no payload or search attribute holds personal data, and the report names every criterion with its observable.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | A user with no Workbench role opens the platform surface | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A Workbench role other than RW-PLATADM or RW-AUDIT opens the platform surface | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

A certificate failure shows in the frontend log and the TLS alert only, with the client identity and no personal data; no Workbench message is shown because no Workbench screen is involved. The same holds for a missing namespace, a foreign poller, a REST hop in the chain, a lost run, a grant across the boundary and a timer in a scheduler table: each is a harness report line and an alert for the platform owner, with the service, the queue and the observable, and none of them is user-facing text. The two message IDs and their texts are copied unchanged from RWB-E1-070 and the platform surface; this story adds no message ID.

##### 15. Screens and states

No Workbench screen is built in this story and the harness renders nothing of its own. The operational view is the Temporal Web UI behind Entra ID with two states — operate for RW-PLATADM and read-only for RW-AUDIT — and a refused sign-in showing MSG-P4-001 or MSG-P4-002 with no namespace listed; those states and the role mapping belong to RWB-PLT-E1070-APP and RWB-P4-E1022-APP. The Grafana dashboard "Temporal platform" of the platform story shows the five services, request rate, errors and persistence latency and is referenced, not built, here. The Workbench admin screens for platform settings come in Epic 8.

The seven legacy test cases are kept as ITG copies with the `-ITG` suffix and re-scoped to the platform-wide proof: the cluster and namespace checks of TC-E1-070-01 and TC-E1-070-05 and the Web UI role check of TC-E1-070-04 are owned at component level by RWB-PLT-E1070-APP and RWB-P4-E1022-APP, so their ITG copies assert the registered queues (AC1), the retention and the timer store (AC7) and what the platform exposes to an operator and an auditor (AC6); the run book of TC-E1-070-07 stays with RWB-PLT-E1070-APP, so its ITG copy asserts the call path the run book documents (AC4). No legacy test is re-run against the monolith and no new business value is added; the full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the namespace, the retention, the search attributes, the queue list, the probe queue, the workflow ID, the endpoints and the wait intervals are configuration (REQ-DRI-010).
- No personal data in search attributes, workflow payloads, workflow inputs, workflow history, fixtures, logs or the report: CaseId, Stage, ProductGroup and QueueCode only; the smoke payload is synthetic and the codec is out of scope here.
- One namespace and one worker per service on its own queue (BR2, BR3): a second namespace, a second registration, a worker on two queues or a poller of another service fails the run rather than being reported as a warning.
- One certificate per service (BR4): a shared certificate, a certificate for another namespace or an mTLS bypass fails the run; there is no bypass in SIT.
- A step in another service is a Temporal call on the owner's queue (BR6): a REST hop between two services, or a workflow calling a service base, fails the run.
- Temporal persistence never sits in the ACE database and no `rwb_*` schema is granted to `temporal_svc` (BR5); both directions are asserted, not only the one the platform story checks.
- No workflow timer in a Quartz table or a shared job table (BR9); the timer is read from the history of `temporal`.
- The harness owns no schema, no migration and no workflow of its own: every write is made by a service or by the platform, every statement the harness runs is a SELECT that must be refused, and its only workflow is the synthetic smoke run.
- The suite never starts a case workflow, never signals a case workflow, never edits a platform value and never uses production data or a production namespace.
- Synthetic data only, and the SIT data set is restored after the run.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-071 for the workflow platform epic; the contract freezes the WorkflowGateway, the workflow-ID and task-queue conventions, the payload-codec metadata and the smoke workflow and admin operation, published on Day 1 with a fake, and every value is kept from the legacy story. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **consumer of the workflow worker contract (any service team)**, I want **the WorkflowGateway interface, the workflow-ID and task-queue convention, the payload codec contract, the smoke workflow contract and the admin operation published on Day 1 with a fake**, so that **every service builds and tests its workflows without a cluster**.

This is the contract story of legacy key RWB-E1-071 under epic RWB-PLT-WF. It publishes the worker surface of the shared platform — the interface, the conventions, the codec metadata, the smoke workflow and its admin operation — as a contract document with a fake and a contract test. It owns no schema, no topic and no service base: the platform is shared platform, its namespace is the specified `rwb-recovery`, and every business value behind the surface stays with the owning service.

##### 2. Business rationale

Without one published worker contract each squad invents its own queue, workflow ID, codec and start-up checks, and the first clear payload in a history is found in production. The legacy story fixed the worker inside one deployable module, where a convention held because one team wrote all the workflows. In the target there are 19 services, each running its own worker on its own queue, so the conventions have to be published before the first service builds: one gateway, one codec, one set of IDs, one smoke path.

The contract is what makes DP-11 and DP-13 real for the workflow surface. A caller starts or signals a workflow through the published WorkflowGateway and never imports a Temporal type, so a change of SDK, of cluster endpoint or of codec never reaches a business module. The payload contract is what makes NFR-045 defensible after the split: the codec metadata is declared, the key reference is declared, and a payload without metadata is refused rather than stored in clear. The contract does not decide any business value; it freezes only the shapes and the names that the app story and Epic 3 build against.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-PLT-E1070-CON is published: the cluster contract of namespace `rwb-recovery`, with the frontend endpoint, the mTLS certificate, the Web UI and the codec server. This contract references it and never republishes it.
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published: the DecisionLogApi of the local decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03). The smoke workflow's one activity is specified against that interface, not against a schema.
- RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and RWB-PLT-E1047-CON are published: the parameters, reference-data and naming contracts the conventions are expressed in (DP-06, DP-07, DP-14).
- The parameter names are fixed by the legacy story and kept: temporal.target, temporal.namespace, temporal.taskqueue.platform and temporal.retention.days, with the flag `rwb.p3.temporal`.
- The contract is Draft (realignment v1) and is frozen only when every consuming story passes its contract test. No approval is required to publish a Draft.
- The platform login, the platform queue row in the Ownership Map and the admin base are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1443; ASM-2538). The contract publishes the working read of ASM-2538 and is corrected by a new version when the Wave 0 Service Catalog fixes them.

##### 4. Flow

1. The contract author writes the WorkflowGateway interface: start(workflowType, workflowId, input) returning the run ID, and signal(workflowId, signal, payload), with one typed exception and no Temporal type in either signature.
2. The author writes the workflow-ID and task-queue conventions: platform-smoke-{yyyymmdd} for the platform smoke, case-{caseId} from Epic 3, `rwb-platform` for the platform smoke and health, and `rwb-<short>` per service.
3. The author writes the payload-codec contract: the AES-GCM algorithm, the Key Vault key reference, the key version in the payload metadata, and the refusal of a payload without metadata.
4. The author writes the smoke workflow contract: one activity, the decision code PLATFORM_SMOKE, the 60-second completion and the statement that no case row and no ACE row is read.
5. The author writes the admin operation contract: `POST /admin/workflows/smoke` with its request, response, errors and idempotency, and the observation that its owner is PLT in the Ownership Map.
6. The fake gateway and the fake worker are generated from the same source as the document, so the document, the tables and the fake cannot drift.
7. The contract test runs against the fake: the interfaces, the conventions, the codec refusal, the smoke workflow shape, the admin operation and the versioning rule.
8. The document and the fake are published as v1 to the contract registry, and RWB-PLT-E1071-APP, RWB-PLT-E2037-APP, RWB-PLT-E2038-APP and the Epic 3 services pin the version.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message |
|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The contract is read without the cluster contract it references | The review stops: the endpoint, the namespace and the mTLS identity are declared as references to RWB-PLT-E1070-CON and are never restated here | Review finding, no message id |
| X2 | A consumer starts a workflow with a workflow ID that is already RUNNING | The published rule returns the running execution; no second run and no second activity | None |
| X3 | A payload is handed to the codec without codec metadata | The codec refuses the payload; nothing is written to a history | Review finding, no message id |
| X4 | The admin operation is called while the flag `rwb.p3.temporal` is off | The operation is not registered and the answer is 404, as published | None |
| X5 | A consumer asks for a breaking change to an interface or a convention | The change raises v2 and deprecates v1 in place of editing v1 | None |
| X6 | A value the consumers need is named by no source: the platform login, the queue row, the admin base, the build-ID format and the codec key name | The value is published as the working read of the assumption, with the placeholder where it stays open, and the gap stays open | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1443; ASM-2538) |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Publishes a document and a fake; builds nothing, starts no workflow, reads no business data, depends on nothing |
| Negotiable | The codec metadata field names, the exception type name and the fake's transport are open until the version is frozen; the conventions and the interface are fixed |
| Valuable | RWB-PLT-E1071-APP, the platform successors and every Epic 3 service start on Day 1 against the fake, without a cluster |
| Estimable | One interface, two conventions, one codec metadata block, one smoke workflow, one admin operation, one fake and one contract test |
| Small | One sprint for the document, the fake and the contract test |
| Testable | Each criterion is a schema, lint or fake assertion in section 16 |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Temporal worker and SDK in the recovery module - contract

  Background:
    Given the platform worker contract is published as v1 at status Draft
    Given the platform is shared platform and owns no schema, no topic and no service base

  Scenario: AC1 The WorkflowGateway interface is published and leaks no Temporal type (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the WorkflowGateway interface in the package recovery.casewf.workflow
    When the interface is validated
    Then it declares start(workflowType, workflowId, input) returning the run ID and signal(workflowId, signal, payload)
    Then neither signature, nor the WorkflowRun record, imports or returns a Temporal type
    Then an unreachable frontend is published as one typed exception carrying MSG-P3-036

  Scenario: AC2 The workflow-ID and task-queue conventions are published (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the convention section of the document
    When it is read against the platform and the services
    Then the workflow ID is platform-smoke-{yyyymmdd} for the platform smoke and case-{caseId} from Epic 3
    Then the task queue is `rwb-platform` for the platform smoke and health and `rwb-<short>` per service
    Then a repeated start with the same workflow ID returns the running execution and never starts a second run

  Scenario: AC3 The codec contract declares the algorithm, the key reference and the key version, and refuses a payload without metadata (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the payload-codec section of the document
    When a payload is encoded and then decoded through the published contract
    Then the metadata declares AES-GCM, the Key Vault key reference and the key version
    Then a payload without codec metadata is refused and no clear value reaches a history
    Then no key, no key name in clear and no personal data appears in the document, the examples or the fake

  Scenario: AC4 The smoke workflow contract declares one activity, the decision code and the completion bound (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the smoke workflow section of the document
    When it is compared with the app story and the fake
    Then PlatformSmokeWorkflow declares exactly one activity, PlatformSmokeActivity
    Then the activity writes decision code PLATFORM_SMOKE through the DecisionLogApi before the workflow completes
    Then the workflow completes within 60 seconds, reads no case row, no ACE row and no business table, and carries workflow ID platform-smoke-{yyyymmdd}

  Scenario: AC5 The admin operation contract is published (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the admin operation section of the document
    When it is validated
    Then it declares POST /admin/workflows/smoke with the optional request { workflowId }, the WorkflowRun response of workflowId, runId, workflowType, status, taskQueue and startedAt, and errors 401, 403, 404, 409 and 503 with MSG-P4-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-GEN-004 and MSG-P3-036
    Then it declares Platform administration U as the authority and the workflow ID as the idempotency key
    Then the operation names PLT as its owner in the Ownership Map

  Scenario: AC6 The fake answers every contract test and a breaking change raises v2 (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the fake gateway and the fake worker
    When the contract test is run
    Then the fake answers a start, a duplicate start, a signal, an unreachable frontend, a payload without metadata and the flag-off 404
    Then the interfaces, the conventions, the codec declaration and the admin operation in the tables equal those in the document and in the fake
    Then a breaking change raises v2 and marks v1 deprecated, and no consumer sees an edited v1
```

These six criteria are new and test only the contract baseline: no legacy acceptance criterion is repeated here, every value is taken from the legacy story, Architecture v5, the Temporal and Drools design or the Ownership Map character for character, and the platform values that no source names are published as the working read of ASM-2538.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The WorkflowGateway is the only way a module starts or signals a workflow; no caller imports a Temporal type or builds a stub of its own | DP-11; Architecture v5 slide 11 (typed activity and workflow interface in a contract jar) |
| BR2 | The codec is the only payload path: every payload carries AES-GCM, the key reference and the key version in its metadata, and a payload without metadata is refused | NFR-045; Architecture v5 slides 23 and 35 |
| BR3 | The conventions are fixed and versioned: platform-smoke-{yyyymmdd}, case-{caseId} from Epic 3, `rwb-platform` and `rwb-<short>` | DP-10; Architecture v5 slides 20, 23 and 24 |
| BR4 | The contract carries no business value: no threshold, band, limit, reason code or decision outcome appears in an interface, a convention or an example | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR5 | The fake is test-only: it is published with the contract, is pinned by the consumers, and never ships in a runtime artefact | Architecture v5 slide 11 (contract tests run in every build) |
| BR6 | Versioning: a breaking change raises a new version and deprecates the old one; a published version is never edited in place | Template and Rules §R7.2; Architecture v5 slide 11 |
| BR7 | The contract names no service shard and no schema: it names the platform, the queue and the interface, and every business table stays with its owner | DP-01; Architecture v5 slides 20 and 29 |
| BR8 | The platform queue is the working read of the assumption: `rwb-platform` is published because JOB-22 places PlatformSmokeWorkflow there and Template and Rules §R4 has no platform row, and the Wave 0 Service Catalog and the Ownership Map replace it when they name it | JOB-22; Architecture v5 slide 44; ASM-2538 |

##### 9. State transitions

The contract itself has three states, and it publishes one runtime transition for a caller:

| Object | From | Event | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Contract version | Draft | The consuming stories pass their contract tests | Published |
| Contract version | Published | The consumers pin the version and no change is open | Frozen |
| Contract version | Published or Frozen | A breaking change is needed | A new version; the old one is deprecated, never edited |
| Workflow start | None | A start with an unknown workflow ID | RUNNING, and the run ID is returned |
| Workflow start | RUNNING | A start with the same workflow ID | RUNNING, and the same running execution is returned with no second run |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The contract author (any team, per U3) | Writes and versions the document, the conventions, the codec declaration and the fake |
| The platform owner of the workflow layer | Approves a version freeze and a breaking change |
| The service teams of the 19 services | Read the contract, confirm the queue and the ID their service will use, raise a change request |
| The ACE Common team | Owns the identity and the key path the codec references and never republishes them here |
| RWB-PLT-E1071-APP and the platform successors | Consume the interface, the conventions and the fake; pin the version |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A worker contract is a technical artefact, not a credit decision |

No personal name, no email address and no credential appears in the document, an example or the fake. Where a caller must be named, the example uses a user identifier or a role code only.

##### 11. Data

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Business data published | None. The document publishes names, shapes, conventions, codes and status values only |
| Payload fields declared | The codec metadata only: the algorithm, the key reference and the key version; the payload body stays opaque to the contract |
| WorkflowRun fields | workflowId, runId, workflowType, status, taskQueue, startedAt |
| Personal data in examples | None. The workflow IDs are synthetic and carry a date, a case identifier or a counter; no name, no national identifier and no account number |
| Tables named | None. The contract names no `rwb_*` table and no schema, and the smoke writes no table of its own |
| Retention | The retention value stays the parameter temporal.retention.days; the contract states that a closed workflow leaves visibility after that value and holds no data of its own |

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner PLT, taken from the Ownership Map. The operation is published on the platform and not inside a service base.

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Errors | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/admin/workflows/smoke` | Run PlatformSmokeWorkflow on demand and return its run | Platform administration, right U | 401 (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Platform administration U (MSG-P4-002); 404 flag off; 409 the workflow ID already completed (MSG-GEN-004); 503 Temporal unreachable (MSG-P3-036) | Workflow ID |

Request: body optional, { workflowId: string }, default platform-smoke-{yyyymmdd} in the server time zone. Response: 200 WorkflowRun with workflowId, runId, workflowType, status, taskQueue and startedAt. The host, the admin base and the platform login of the operation are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1443; ASM-2538); the path and the owner are taken from the Ownership Map.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. This contract consumes no operation: it publishes the interface, the conventions, the codec declaration and the admin operation, and it names the contracts it references without calling them.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The platform publishes no topic of its own. The decision record that the smoke activity writes travels on `rwb.decision-record.v1` through the library of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, whose type owner is P7; this contract declares the code PLATFORM_SMOKE and no event schema.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The worker consumes no topic and the smoke workflow waits on its one activity.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract declares |
|---|---|---|---|
| WorkflowGateway | Published interface | `rwb-platform` | start(workflowType, workflowId, input) returning the run ID; signal(workflowId, signal, payload); one typed exception carrying MSG-P3-036 |
| PlatformSmokeWorkflow | Workflow | `rwb-platform` | One activity, then complete within 60 seconds; workflow ID platform-smoke-{yyyymmdd}; no case row and no ACE row |
| PlatformSmokeActivity | Activity | `rwb-platform` | Writes decision code PLATFORM_SMOKE through the DecisionLogApi before the workflow completes, and returns the build ID |

The contract publishes the two Temporal interfaces as a contract jar and nothing else: a consumer imports the interface, never a workflow implementation, and never a Temporal type.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The JOB-22 Schedule is declared by RWB-PLT-E1071-APP section 12.6; the contract states only that a platform Schedule starts PlatformSmokeWorkflow at 06:00 on `rwb-platform` with overlap SKIP and a catch-up window, and creates none.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The contract owns no `rwb_*` schema and no table, and it names no table of another owner.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| Fake gateway (this story) | start, a duplicate start that returns the running execution, a signal, and the unreachable frontend exception with MSG-P3-036 | RWB-PLT-E1071-APP, RWB-PLT-E2037-APP, RWB-PLT-E2038-APP |
| Fake worker (this story) | The PlatformSmokeWorkflow and PlatformSmokeActivity shapes, the PLATFORM_SMOKE decision code and the 60-second completion, with the flag-off 404 | RWB-PLT-E1071-APP and the Epic 3 workflow tests |

The fakes answer from the published document rather than from copied payloads, so a change of interface or convention shows up as a contract-test failure in every consumer.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary (REST, Kafka, Temporal, File)

| Call type | Provided | Consumed | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| REST | 1 operation (`POST /admin/workflows/smoke`, owner PLT) | 0 | OpenAPI 3.1, one problem envelope, `Idempotency-Key` carried as the workflow ID |
| Kafka | 0 | 0 | The contract declares no topic and no event schema; the decision record belongs to the P7 library and `rwb.decision-record.v1` |
| Temporal | 1 interface (WorkflowGateway) and 1 workflow (PlatformSmokeWorkflow) with its activity | 0 | Published as a contract jar in namespace `rwb-recovery`, on task queue `rwb-platform` |
| File | 0 | 0 | No file is declared |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** `workflow-gateway.yaml` (the interface and the WorkflowRun record), the convention section (workflow IDs and task queues), the codec metadata declaration, `platform-smoke.yaml` (the workflow and its activity, the decision code and the completion bound), `admin-workflows.yaml` (the admin operation), the fake gateway, the fake worker and the contract test.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; the contract names no table and no schema | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`; the smoke activity is specified against the DecisionLogApi | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON (of the app story) |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | The parameter names the conventions read are published, and their values stay with the parameters contract | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON (of the app story) |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | The decision code PLATFORM_SMOKE is a LOV-DECISION value; the list is referenced, never copied | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON (of the app story) |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit; the Schedule row is named here and declared by the app story | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout; the gateway is the one published interface of the workflow surface | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` for the services; the platform operation sits on its own path with no service base | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library, referenced and not republished | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON (of the app story) |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema; the contract owns no migration | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON (of the app story) |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route; the contract exposes no screen path | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON (of the app story) |

The pattern that matters most for a contract is DP-11: the gateway is the one published interface of the workflow surface, so an in-process call becomes a typed call across the platform boundary with a 2 s budget and one hop, and every Temporal detail stays behind it. DP-10 is applied by naming the platform Schedule and its queue instead of a Quartz job, and DP-13 by publishing the admin operation on its own path with no service base and no repetition of the monolith path.

**Build steps**

1. Write `workflow-gateway.yaml` with the two operations, the WorkflowRun record and the one typed exception; prove no Temporal type appears in either signature.
2. Write the convention section: the two workflow-ID patterns, the platform queue, the per-service queue pattern, the duplicate-start rule and the build-ID rule.
3. Write the codec declaration: AES-GCM, the key reference, the key version in the metadata, the refusal rule and the statement that no key appears in the document or a test.
4. Write `platform-smoke.yaml` with the workflow, its one activity, the decision code, the 60-second completion and the no-case-row and no-ACE-row rule.
5. Write `admin-workflows.yaml` with the request, the response, the five error answers, the authority and the idempotency key, and record PLT as the owner.
6. Generate the fake gateway and the fake worker from the same source as the tables, so document, tables and fakes cannot drift, plus the personal-data scan over every example.
7. Publish v1 to the contract registry, notify RWB-PLT-E1071-APP, RWB-PLT-E2037-APP, RWB-PLT-E2038-APP and the Epic 3 services, and record the version they pin.

**Done when.** The document validates, every convention and every interface matches the tables and the fakes, the codec refusal and the duplicate-start rule are asserted, and the contract test of this story is green in the build.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Published as |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-036 | The workflow service is unreachable or refuses a start | The workflow service is not available. Try again in a few minutes. | 503 of the admin operation, and the one typed exception of the gateway |
| MSG-P3-032 | A required parameter has no value at start-up | Parameter {name} has no value for {environment}. The service did not start. | Start-up failure, published and not raised by the contract itself |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without Platform administration U calls the admin operation | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | 403 |
| MSG-P4-001 | No session, or the session has expired | Existing message catalogue entry; its text is not restated in the source documents | 401 |
| MSG-GEN-004 | The same workflow ID has already completed | Existing message catalogue entry; its text is not restated in the source documents | 409 |

No identifier is renumbered by the realignment. The refusal of a payload without codec metadata is a contract rule and not a user message: it fails the encoder or the decoder and writes nothing, so it carries no message identifier.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story, and the contract declares none. The admin operation is the surface a platform administration screen would call; the smoke run states it publishes are Not run, Running, Completed and Failed, and the screen itself, if one is built, belongs to the platform observability work and not to this contract.

##### 17. Guardrails

- One published interface for the workflow surface: no caller imports a Temporal type, builds its own stub or starts a workflow outside the gateway.
- The codec is the only payload path: the metadata carries the algorithm, the key reference and the key version, and a payload without metadata is refused; no key, no key name in clear and no personal data appears in the document, the examples or the fakes.
- No business value in the contract: thresholds, bands, limits, reason codes and decision outcomes stay with the owner or the parameters.
- No personal data in examples: workflow IDs are synthetic and carry a date, a case identifier or a counter only.
- No schema and no table in the contract: the platform owns no `rwb_*` schema, and every business table stays with its owner (DP-01).
- The fake is test-only and is pinned by the consumers; it never ships in a runtime artefact.
- The monolith base is never republished: the admin operation sits on its own platform path (DP-13).
- The contract is versioned: a breaking change raises v2 and deprecates v1 in place of editing v1.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E1-071 for the workflow platform epic; the smoke job is now the JOB-22 Temporal Schedule on `rwb-platform` and the smoke operation is the PLT-owned `POST /admin/workflows/smoke`, while the worker, the codec, the gateway and every value are kept. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform administrator**, I want **the recovery module to run one Temporal worker through the Spring Boot starter with fixed task-queue and workflow-ID conventions, the payload codec, the published WorkflowGateway and a smoke workflow on a Temporal Schedule**, so that **Epic 3 workflows plug into a worker that is already secure and observable**.

This is the app story of legacy key RWB-E1-071, split from the monolith Epic 1 story of the same name for epic RWB-PLT-WF. The platform is shared platform and not one of the 19 services: it has no `rwb_*` schema, no `rwb.<short>.events.v1` topic and no `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` REST base of its own, and its namespace is the specified `rwb-recovery`. The story delivers one worker pattern, one codec, one published gateway and one smoke workflow, and it proves the whole path before the first case workflow exists.

##### 2. Business rationale

The cluster of RWB-PLT-E1070-APP is only useful when a worker connects to it from the recovery module. Without one worker pattern, each Epic 3 squad would choose its own task queue, workflow ID, payload handling and start-up checks, and the first clear personal data in a workflow history would be found in production. This story gives the module one worker, one codec, one gateway and one smoke workflow, and it proves the path end to end before the first case workflow exists.

It meets REQ-DRI-005 (an action does not proceed when its decision record cannot be written), REQ-DRI-007 (a failed start reaches a named owner) and REQ-DRI-010 (the target, namespace and task queue are parameters, not code). It keeps the codec rule of NFR-045: every payload is a ciphertext with codec metadata, and the history, the worker log and the test data hold no clear personal data. The measure is a daily smoke workflow that completes with one decision-record entry and a history that holds no clear personal data.

**Two realignment deltas.** First, the smoke job is **JOB-22**: a Temporal Schedule at 06:00 on the platform task queue (Architecture v5 slide 44; Temporal and Drools design slide 32 item 6; ADR-016, DP-10). The legacy story relied on the clustered ACE Quartz scheduler under exception T2 and on the retired RWB-TE-007 Quartz scheduler; both no longer apply, this story creates no Quartz job and no job-catalog row, and the Schedule is owned by the platform. Second, the monolith API base is retired (DP-13): the smoke operation is published as `POST /admin/workflows/smoke`, whose owner is PLT in the Ownership Map, so it no longer sits in a service base and does not repeat the monolith path.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-PLT-E1071-CON is published: the WorkflowGateway interface, the workflow-ID and task-queue conventions, the payload-codec metadata contract, the smoke workflow contract and the admin operation, with its fake.
- RWB-PLT-E1070-CON is published: the cluster contract of namespace `rwb-recovery` with the frontend endpoint, the mTLS certificates, the Web UI and the codec server, at server version 1.30 or later.
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published: the DecisionLogApi of the local decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03). RWB-P7-E1027-CON publishes the central ledger contract behind it.
- RWB-PLT-E1072-CON is published: the embedded Drools kit (DP-04). The worker registers the kit activity classes so that Epic 3 workflows find them; the smoke workflow evaluates no rule package.
- RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and RWB-PLT-E1043-CON are published: the parameters contract and the reference-data contract with the client library (DP-06, DP-07), with RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON behind them as the C dependencies that never block this build.
- RWB-PLT-E1047-CON is published: the topic and event naming library (DP-14). RWB-PLT-E1044-CON is published: the per-service Flyway conventions (DP-15); this story adds no migration.
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the gateway-bff route contract (DP-19). This story exposes no screen, and the contract is cited because the platform administration surface reaches its operations through the edge.
- The Temporal Java SDK version is pinned with the server version approved for RWB-PLT-E1070-APP, and the build reads the version from the dependency lock and not from a property. The release is the SCB IT approved release recorded in Environment and Deployment Design v4, Temporal 1.30 or later (ASM-2537).
- A Key Vault key for the payload codec exists, and the SY-CASEWF managed identity has wrap and unwrap rights on that key only. The key is one AES-GCM key per environment and is never in a values file or a test (ASM-2537); the key name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1442; ASM-2537).
- LOV-DECISION carries PLATFORM_SMOKE as a system event code with no case, loaded by the data steward through the versioned reference load of the rwb-case reference-data contract. The decision-record library accepts it under the system event exception, as it accepts the access event codes.
- No Quartz scheduler is needed and none is a dependency: the smoke job is the JOB-22 Temporal Schedule with overlap policy SKIP and a catch-up window, and the retired RWB-TE-007 Quartz scheduler is not referenced.
- The platform login, the queue row in the Ownership Map and the admin base of the platform are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1442; ASM-2537). The story uses the working read of ASM-2537 until the Wave 0 Service Catalog fixes them.

##### 4. Flow

1. Application start: TemporalConfig reads temporal.target, temporal.namespace and temporal.taskqueue.platform through the parameters contract; a missing value stops start-up with MSG-P3-032.
2. Application start: TemporalWorkerLifecycle reads the flag `rwb.p3.temporal`; when it is on, it creates one worker on `rwb-platform` with the workflow and activity classes and the build ID from the pipeline.
3. Worker: connects to the frontend with its mTLS certificate and polls `rwb-platform`; when the flag is off, no worker and no poller are created.
4. PdpaPayloadCodec: registers as the data converter on the client and the worker; it encrypts every payload with AES-GCM and the Key Vault key, and it decrypts only inside the worker.
5. WorkflowGateway: starts and signals workflows by workflow ID; a start with an existing workflow ID returns the running execution and does not start a second run.
6. The platform smoke Schedule (JOB-22) fires daily at 06:00, with overlap policy SKIP and a catch-up window, and calls WorkflowGateway.start("PlatformSmokeWorkflow", "platform-smoke-{yyyymmdd}", input) through the worker.
7. PlatformSmokeWorkflow: runs one activity; PlatformSmokeActivity writes the decision record with decision code PLATFORM_SMOKE through the DecisionLogApi, then returns the worker build ID.
8. Workflow: completes when the activity commits; a failed decision-record write fails the activity and the workflow, and the incident reaches RW-PLATADM.
9. Platform administrator: may call `POST /admin/workflows/smoke` to run the same workflow on demand; the response gives the workflow ID, run ID and status.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The Temporal frontend is unreachable or refuses the connection | WorkflowGateway.start fails; `POST /admin/workflows/smoke` returns 503; no workflow, no history and no decision record are written | MSG-P3-036 | AC3 |
| X2 | A start uses a workflow ID that is already RUNNING | The running execution is returned; no second run and no second activity | None | AC4 |
| X3 | The flag `rwb.p3.temporal` is off | No worker is registered and the admin smoke operation is not registered; the call returns 404 | None | AC5 |
| X4 | A required parameter has no value for the environment at start-up (temporal.target, temporal.namespace or temporal.taskqueue.platform) | The service does not start; the missing parameter and environment are named | MSG-P3-032 | AC6 |
| X5 | A workflow class is placed outside recovery.casewf.workflow | The build fails naming the class and the package rule; the merge is blocked | Build log | AC7 |
| X6 | A role without Platform administration U calls `POST /admin/workflows/smoke` | The call is refused with 403; nothing starts | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E1-071-08 |

The missing-parameter row is X4: the legacy exception covered temporal.target only, and the platform binds the namespace and the task queue under the same start-up rule because all three are parameters and none may take a default (REQ-DRI-010).

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the cluster contract, the parameters, the reference data, the decision-record library, the Drools kit, the naming library, the Flyway conventions, the edge contract and the module rules; the smoke workflow is self-contained |
| Negotiable | The Schedule cadence, the build-ID format, the retry policy and the actor identity are configuration or platform values; the codec, the package boundary, the queue and the ID conventions are fixed by the contract |
| Valuable | Epic 3 starts from a worker that already encrypts payloads, records a decision and survives a restart |
| Estimable | One worker, one codec, one gateway, one smoke workflow, one Schedule and one admin operation |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion in section 7 is one test in section 16 |

```gherkin
    Then the workflow runs one activity and ends COMPLETED within 60 seconds
    Then one decision_log_entry exists with decision code PLATFORM_SMOKE, actor SY-CASEWF and inputsRef "platform-smoke-20261116"
    Then no recovery_case row is created or changed

  Scenario: AC2 History holds encrypted payloads only (legacy RWB-E1-071 AC2)
    Given the smoke activity input carries the synthetic national ID "1101700203456"
    When the workflow completes
    Then the raw history from the Temporal CLI shows the payload as binary ciphertext with codec metadata
    Then the string "1101700203456" appears nowhere in the history or the worker log
    Then decoding through PdpaPayloadCodec with the Key Vault key returns the input
    Then the worker log holds the workflow ID and no payload

  Scenario: AC3 Temporal unreachable (legacy RWB-E1-071 AC3)
    Given the Temporal frontend is unreachable on port 7233
    When U-70 calls POST /admin/workflows/smoke
    Then the response is 503 with MSG-P3-036
    Then no workflow execution exists and no decision_log_entry is written
    Then the metric workflow_start_failures_total increases by one

  Scenario: AC4 Duplicate workflow ID (legacy RWB-E1-071 AC4)
    Given platform-smoke-20261116 is RUNNING
    When U-70 calls the smoke endpoint again with workflow ID platform-smoke-20261116
    Then the response is 200 with the same run ID and status RUNNING
    Then the history holds one WorkflowExecutionStarted event
    Then the activity runs once

  Scenario: AC5 Flag off (legacy RWB-E1-071 AC5)
    Given rwb.p3.temporal is off in DEV
    When the application starts
    Then no worker is registered on `rwb-platform` and no poller connection is opened
    When U-70 calls POST /admin/workflows/smoke
    Then the response is 404 and no workflow starts

  Scenario: AC6 Missing parameter at start-up (legacy RWB-E1-071 AC6)
    Given temporal.target has no value for SIT
    When the application starts in SIT
    Then start-up fails with MSG-P3-032 naming temporal.target and SIT
    Then no worker polls and the health endpoint stays 503

  Scenario: AC7 Workflow class outside the package (legacy RWB-E1-071 AC7)
    Given a branch adds the class recovery.casewf.smoke.SmokeWorkflowImpl outside recovery.casewf.workflow
    When the build runs WorkflowBoundaryTest
    Then the build fails naming the class and the package rule
    Then the merge is blocked
```

Two substitutions are made and no other change: the Quartz smoke job becomes the platform smoke Schedule (JOB-22), which is DP-10 and ADR-016, and the monolith admin path becomes the PLT-owned `POST /admin/workflows/smoke`, which is DP-13. Every value of the seven legacy criteria is kept character for character — the workflow ID "platform-smoke-20261116", the namespace `rwb-recovery`, the 60-second completion, the decision code PLATFORM_SMOKE, the actor SY-CASEWF, the synthetic national ID "1101700203456", the message identifiers MSG-P3-036, MSG-P3-032 and MSG-P4-002, the metric workflow_start_failures_total, the flag `rwb.p3.temporal`, the package `recovery.casewf.workflow` and the port 7233 — and the scenario titles stay as the legacy titles with their origin tag.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Workflow code lives only in recovery.casewf.workflow; activities, gateways and I/O live in recovery.casewf.activities or the owning module, and WorkflowBoundaryTest enforces the boundary in every build | D-RCV-36 T7; ADR-011; DP-01 |
| BR2 | Workflow code is deterministic: no clock, random, I/O, parameter read or direct Drools call; time comes from Workflow.currentTimeMillis or a timer, and all I/O is an activity | D-RCV-36 T7; DP-10 |
| BR3 | Every payload passes through PdpaPayloadCodec (AES-GCM, one key per environment in Key Vault); no clear personal data in history, logs, tests or prompts | D-RCV-36 T1; NFR-045 |
| BR4 | Task queues are `rwb-platform` for the platform smoke and health, and `rwb-<short>` per service from Epic 3; no Epic 1 workflow uses a service queue | D-RCV-36 T1; Architecture v5 slide 24; JOB-22 |
| BR5 | Workflow IDs are platform-smoke-{yyyymmdd} and, from Epic 3, case-{caseId}; a repeated start with the same ID returns the running execution and never starts a second run | D-RCV-36 T1; R-UNI-40 |
| BR6 | Every worker carries the build ID from the pipeline manifest; a worker with no build ID or an unknown build ID starts no new workflow | D-RCV-36 T1; Architecture v5 slide 23 (Worker Versioning) |
| BR7 | With `rwb.p3.temporal` off, no worker is registered, no poller is opened and `POST /admin/workflows/smoke` returns 404; nothing else changes | D-RCV-36 T1; RWB-E1-047 |
| BR8 | A required parameter with no value stops start-up with MSG-P3-032; the service never substitutes a default for temporal.target, temporal.namespace or temporal.taskqueue.platform | REQ-DRI-010; MSG-P3-032; DP-06 |
| BR9 | The smoke activity writes its decision record through the DecisionLogApi before the workflow completes; a failed write fails the workflow | REQ-DRI-005; DP-03 |
| BR10 | The smoke workflow reads no case row, no ACE view and no business table | D-RCV-35 U1; Architecture v5 slide 20; DP-01, DP-05 |
| BR11 | A start that cannot reach the frontend fails with MSG-P3-036 and writes no workflow, no history and no decision record | D-RCV-36 T1; REQ-DRI-007; DP-11 |

The task queue name is the working read of ASM-2537: Template and Rules §R4 has no platform row, and JOB-22 on Architecture v5 slide 44 puts PlatformSmokeWorkflow on the platform queue, so `rwb-platform` is published as the platform queue until the Wave 0 Service Catalog and the Ownership Map name it (GAP-1442).

##### 9. State transitions

None for a case. This story changes the status of the platform smoke workflow only.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | Start (Schedule or admin operation) | Workflow ID not known | RUNNING |
| RUNNING | Activity completes | The decision record is committed | COMPLETED |
| RUNNING | Activity fails after its retry policy | No decision record is written | FAILED |
| COMPLETED or FAILED | Retention 30 days (parameter temporal.retention.days) | The workflow is closed | Removed from visibility; archive is RWB-PLT-E2039-APP |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-PLATADM | Runs the smoke workflow on demand, reads the worker health and the history (Platform administration, U) |
| RW-AUDIT | Reads the history and the decision record (Platform administration and Decision log, R) |
| RW-SECADM | Reads the codec configuration; decode through the codec server is RWB-PLT-E2038-APP, not this story |
| SY-CASEWF | The worker identity; connects with mTLS, polls `rwb-platform` and writes the PLATFORM_SMOKE entry (Decision log C) |
| RW-COE | Reads the smoke result as a platform check (Platform administration, R) |
| RW-TRIBE | Builds and deploys the worker through the pipeline; has no PROD endpoint right |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A smoke run is not a credit decision |

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision_log_entry | all fields | Write | P7 (rwb_decision) |
| DF-DEC-030 | decision_log_entry | actor_user_id | Write | P7 (rwb_decision) |
| DF-DEC-031 | decision_log_entry | idempotency_key | Write, read | P7 (rwb_decision) |
| DF-REF-028 | lov_value | lov_code | Read | P3 (rwb_case) |
| DF-REF-029 | lov_value | value_code | Read | P3 (rwb_case) |

The PLATFORM_SMOKE entry has no case, no rule ID and no version group; it is a system event under the same exception that the access event codes use. Its idempotency key is the workflow ID, so a repeated run of the same day cannot write a second entry. The decision record is written through the DecisionLogApi into the rwb-decision schema and this story writes no table of its own; the level of detail (lov_code, value_code) is read through the reference-data contract of rwb-case. The parameters temporal.target, temporal.namespace, temporal.taskqueue.platform and temporal.retention.days are read through the parameters contract and add no field. No field is added by this story.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner PLT. The operation is published on the platform, not inside a service base.

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Errors | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/admin/workflows/smoke` | Run PlatformSmokeWorkflow on demand and return its run | Platform administration, right U | 401 (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Platform administration U (MSG-P4-002); 404 flag off; 409 the workflow ID already completed (MSG-GEN-004); 503 Temporal unreachable (MSG-P3-036) | Workflow ID: a repeat while RUNNING returns the running execution; a repeat after COMPLETED returns 409 with no second run |

Request body optional: { workflowId: string }, default platform-smoke-{yyyymmdd} in the server time zone. Response 200 WorkflowRun: workflowId, runId, workflowType, status, taskQueue, startedAt. The host, the admin base and the platform login of the operation are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1442; ASM-2537); the path is taken from the Ownership Map row, whose owner is PLT, and is kept character for character.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Provider | Used for | Transport |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | rwb-case (P3) | temporal.target, temporal.namespace, temporal.taskqueue.platform and temporal.retention.days, with the flags | One hop, 2 s, GET retried once with jitter (DP-06, DP-11) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | rwb-case (P3) | LOV-DECISION, to confirm PLATFORM_SMOKE is a loaded system event code | One hop, 2 s, GET retried once with jitter (DP-07, DP-11) |
| POST (library call, not REST) | DecisionLogApi.record | RWB-PLT-E1027-CON library | The PLATFORM_SMOKE decision record in the activity's transaction | In-process library call; the library writes the row and the outbox row |

Both REST reads are built against the RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON contracts and their fakes, so the C dependencies never block this build. The decision record does not travel over REST: the DecisionLogApi of the platform library is the only path, and it is not a second writer of the schema.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Key | Payload (IDs and facts only) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 | workflow ID | decision code PLATFORM_SMOKE, actor SY-CASEWF, workflow ID, build ID, recorded at |

The event is written to the outbox by the library in the same transaction as the decision record, and relayed with the CloudEvents envelope (DP-03). The platform publishes no topic of its own and no platform event name.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The smoke workflow waits on its activity and on no event, and the worker consumes no topic of its own.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| PlatformSmokeWorkflow | Workflow | `rwb-platform` | Runs one activity and completes; deterministic and free of I/O (JOB-22) |
| PlatformSmokeActivity | Activity | `rwb-platform` | Writes the PLATFORM_SMOKE decision record through the DecisionLogApi and returns the build ID |
| WorkflowGateway | Published interface | `rwb-platform` | start(workflowType, workflowId, input) and signal(workflowId, signal, payload), implemented by WorkflowGatewayImpl; the only way a module starts or signals a workflow |

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Schedule | Cadence | Task queue | Overlap | Legacy reference |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Platform smoke (JOB-22) | Daily at 06:00 | `rwb-platform` | SKIP, with a catch-up window | JOB-22 Smoke workflow; Architecture v5 slide 44; Temporal and Drools design slide 32 item 6; ADR-016; DP-10 |

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The platform owns no `rwb_*` schema of its own: the decision record is written through the library into the rwb-decision schema (P7), the reference data is read through the rwb-case contract (P3), and the smoke writes no table of its own and no migration.

| Fake | Serves | Used by this story |

| WorkflowGateway fake and platform worker fake (RWB-PLT-E1071-CON) | The gateway interface, the ID and queue conventions, the codec metadata and the smoke workflow contract | The unit and component tests of the gateway, the worker lifecycle and the boundary test |
| Decision-log fake (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON) | DecisionLogApi.record | AC1 and the failed-write path of BR9 |
| rwb-case parameter fake (RWB-P3-E1042-CON) | `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | AC6, and the temporal.retention.days read |
| rwb-case reference-data fake (RWB-P3-E1043-CON) | `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | The LOV-DECISION check that PLATFORM_SMOKE is loaded |
| Temporal frontend fake (RWB-PLT-E1070-CON) | The frontend endpoint, the namespace and the mTLS identity | AC3, AC4 and AC5 without a cluster |

| Call type | Provided | Consumed | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| REST | 1 operation (`POST /admin/workflows/smoke`, owner PLT) | 3 consumption rows: 2 REST reads on rwb-case and 1 library call (DecisionLogApi) | OpenAPI 3.1, one hop, 2 s timeout, GET retried once with jitter, `Idempotency-Key` carried as the workflow ID |
| Kafka | 1 published (`rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1`) | 0 | CloudEvents 1.0 through the outbox of the decision-record library; the platform publishes no topic of its own |
